title: Lightweight Accounts — Slice A: account store + name reservation + Login handshake
body:
Slice A of the Lightweight Accounts PRD (#60). Establishes the substrate everything else hangs off: the first durable server-side store in britbank, name reservation, and the connect-handshake change that lets a connection be rejected.

## Scope

1. **Account store module.** Single atomic JSON file (`name → {displayName, salt, passcodeHash, totalOnlineMs, createdAt, lastSeen}`).
   - Versioned (`version: 1`); malformed/old-schema file fails loud (mirror the world-snapshot version guard in `src/sim/persistence.ts`), never silently resumes wrong.
   - Load whole map into memory on boot (empty if absent); write atomically (`write tmp + rename`).
   - Location: env `ACCOUNT_STORE_PATH`, default a gitignored `./data/accounts.json` for local dev. Add `data/` to `.gitignore`. Wire `StateDirectory=uo-homage` + `ReadWritePaths` in `deploy/uo-homage.service` so the store survives `git pull` in deploy.
   - **Passcode fields are written by Slice B** — Slice A may leave them empty/absent for reservation-only records; design the schema so B slots in without migration.
2. **`normalizeName()`** — lowercase + collapse whitespace (+ minimal NFKC / zero-width strip) to produce the store key; keep `sanitizeName()` for display. First-claimed display casing is canonical.
3. **Reserve-on-first-use.** A name with a (Slice-A interim) reservation marker is owned; another connection using a reserved name is **rejected**. Anonymous unreserved names still work as today.
4. **Spawn-gate handshake change.** Move the spawn gate behind a first `Login`-style WS message (PRD §2.2 option A) so the connect path can reject *before* `spawnPlayerFor` (`server/gameServer.ts:481-482`). On failure send a new `Rejected {reason}` message and close the socket; no entity is ever created for a failed login. (This is the natural home for the passcode privacy move in Slice B.)
5. **Default character name** changes from `Stranger` to **`Generic Player`** (`DEFAULT_NAME`, `server/identity.ts`).
6. **New ADR** documenting that ADR-0004's never-reject identity contract now has one explicit exception (reserved-name rejection) and that identity moves from the connect URL to a first `Login` message.

## Captain's resolved decisions (apply across the feature)
- Taken reserved name with wrong/blank passcode → **reject with a clear message**, let the user edit the name and retry. No auto-suggest.

## Acceptance
- Two browsers, same name: the second is refused and never spawns an entity.
- Anonymous (unreserved) names still drop straight in (today's behavior preserved).
- Store survives a server restart and a simulated `git pull` (lives outside the working tree).
- Default name shows as "Generic Player".
- ADR added; `CONTEXT.md` updated per DoD.

PRD: https://github.com/modfreq/britbank/issues/60 (§2.1, §2.5, slice A). Depends on nothing; B/C/D build on this.

title: Lightweight Accounts — Slice B: passcode set/verify (salted scrypt)
body:
Slice B of the Lightweight Accounts PRD (#60). Adds the passcode lock on top of Slice A's store and `Login` handshake. Builds on Slice A — depends on it.

## Scope

1. **Splash passcode field** (`src/splash.ts` + `index.html`). Add a passcode input to the identity form. Blank passcode = "I don't want to reserve this name" (anonymous, today's behavior; refused only if the name is already reserved).
2. **Set-on-claim.** First claim (name not reserved, passcode non-blank): generate a random salt, `passcodeHash = scrypt(passcode, salt, 64)`, write the record. No confirm-passcode double-entry in v1.
3. **Verify on re-login.** Reserved name + correct passcode → log in as owner (resume their record). Reserved name + wrong/blank passcode → **reject** via the Slice-A `Rejected` path, never spawns.
4. **Passcode off the wire/logs.** Carry the passcode in the first `Login` WS message body, NOT the connect URL — query strings land in access/proxy logs and browser history. Verify the passcode never appears in the URL, server access logs, or history.
5. **Wrong-passcode UX.** Splash shows an inline error ("Name taken — wrong passcode"), keeps the form populated, allows retry or name change.

## Captain's resolved decisions
- **Passcode storage: salted scrypt** (Node built-in `crypto.scrypt`, no new dependency; verify with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`). Never plaintext.
- Taken name + bad passcode → reject with clear message + retry (no auto-suggest).

## Acceptance
- Claim a name with a passcode → record stored with salt + scrypt hash, never plaintext.
- Reconnect with the correct passcode → logs in, same identity. Wrong passcode → inline splash error, no spawn.
- Passcode verified absent from the connect URL, access logs, and browser history.
- Docs/ADR updated per DoD.

PRD: https://github.com/modfreq/britbank/issues/60 (§2.1, §2.2, slice B). Depends on Slice A.

title: Lightweight Accounts — Slice C: persistent per-name online time
body:
Slice C of the Lightweight Accounts PRD (#60). The core feature: persistent per-name online time. Builds on Slice A's store. Depends on Slice A (and naturally pairs with B for reserved-name identity).

## Scope

1. **Server-authoritative accrual.** On connect, stamp `connectedAt = Date.now()` into the session (`server/sessions.ts` `Session` extended to carry resolved account name + connect timestamp). On disconnect (`server/gameServer.ts:495-499`), `delta = Date.now() - connectedAt`, add to the account's `totalOnlineMs`, persist. All timing server-side — the client never reports its own time.
2. **Architectural boundary.** Wall-clock reads (`Date.now()`) live ONLY in the server/account layer, **never in `sim/`**, so the simulation stays clock-free and deterministic (`server/gameServer.ts:459-461`).
3. **Periodic checkpoint.** Every ~60s, flush each live session's in-progress delta to the store (advance `totalOnlineMs`, reset the session checkpoint stamp). A crash loses at most one interval, not hours.
4. **Real SIGTERM flush.** Wire a genuine SIGTERM handler in `server/index.ts:17-22` that flushes all live sessions before exit. **Fix the stale deploy docs** that already falsely claim a SIGTERM world-snapshot save (`deploy/uo-homage.service:50-52`, `deploy/deploy.sh:7`).
5. **WS ping/pong liveness.** Ping ~every 30s; terminate sockets that miss two pongs. Without it, a dropped connection that never fires `close` accrues time forever (cheat + memory leak).
6. **Only reserved names accrue.** Anonymous sessions accrue nothing (answers "whose time is it" for duplicate anonymous names).

## Captain's resolved decisions
- **AFK counts** — all connected time accrues, including idle banksitting. No activity gating.
- **Concurrent sessions: refuse the second login** under one reserved name ("already online"). This is the simpler rule the captain chose, so the count-once machinery is NOT needed — at most one live session per reserved name means accrual is unambiguous.

## Acceptance
- A name's `totalOnlineMs` increases by ~the wall-clock connected duration, server-measured, **persisted across a full server restart**.
- `kill -9` mid-session loses at most the checkpoint interval (~60s), not the whole session.
- A second concurrent login under a reserved name is refused with "already online."
- AFK time counts.
- Deploy docs corrected; ADR/CONTEXT.md updated per DoD.

PRD: https://github.com/modfreq/britbank/issues/60 (§2.3, slice C). Depends on Slice A.

title: Lightweight Accounts — Slice D: online-time leaderboard
body:
Slice D of the Lightweight Accounts PRD (#60). The leaderboard that surfaces Slice C's totals. Depends on Slice C (needs `totalOnlineMs`).

## Scope

1. **`GET /leaderboard` HTTP route.** The bare HTTP server currently 404s everything (`server/gameServer.ts:465-468`); add one route returning top-N JSON read from the in-memory account map (authoritative, current to the last checkpoint).
2. **Splash "Top Banksitters" panel** (`src/splash.ts` + `index.html`). Fetch `/leaderboard` before the WS connects and render a ranked list — the natural place to advertise the game and motivate claiming a name. Pure DOM.
3. **`/top` chat command.** Intercept a `/top` line server-side in the chat path (`Say` → `handleSay`, `server/gameServer.ts:425-430`) and reply with a system/`Speech` message listing the top N. No new client UI.

## Ranking rules
- Rank by total cumulative online time per **reserved** name; anonymous sessions excluded.
- Tiebreak by `createdAt` (older claim wins) for stable ordering.
- No push/live-updating leaderboard in v1 (splash fetch is on-demand; `/top` computes on call).

## Acceptance
- Splash shows top-N by total online time, current to the last checkpoint.
- `/top` in chat returns the same ranking.
- Anonymous sessions never appear.
- Docs/CONTEXT.md updated per DoD.

PRD: https://github.com/modfreq/britbank/issues/60 (§2.4, slice D). Depends on Slice C.

PRIMARY: wire firstmate to use the relay's new POST /connector/dismiss endpoint, which acknowledges a pending X mention WITHOUT replying (drops the request, posts nothing, stops re-offering it). Previously firstmate only cleared the local inbox file when it chose not to reply, leaving the relay re-offering every poll until it timed out to a polite 'offline' auto-reply (observed live). (1) New client bin/fm-x-dismiss.sh modeled on bin/fm-x-reply.sh: reuses fm-x-lib.sh fmx_load_config for FMX_PAIRING_TOKEN/FMX_RELAY_URL (default https://myfirstmate.io), POSTs {request_id} with no text body to RELAY/connector/dismiss with Authorization: Bearer , echoes request_id on 2xx, exits non-zero on non-2xx/transport failure, honors FMX_DRY_RUN (records would-be POST to state/x-outbox/.json with an endpoint:dismiss marker, posts nothing), validates request_id is path-safe since it becomes a filename. Deliberate: payload built with jq like fm-x-reply (jq required before dry-run, matching fm-x-reply); dry-run runs before token/network checks so previews need no token; on failure the inbox file is left for retry, mirroring fm-x-reply. (2) fmx-respond skill skip path now calls bin/fm-x-dismiss.sh before removing the inbox file; answer and follow-up paths unchanged. (3) AGENTS.md section 14 documents dismiss-on-skip; CLAUDE.md is a symlink. (4) Tests mirror fm-x-reply style in tests/fm-x-mode.test.sh (dismiss case in fake curl plus seven focused tests). The repo previously had no test command, so the test step delegated to an agent, and that agent-driven run crashed the no-mistakes daemon mid-step on two prior runs; running the suite deterministically removes the agent from the test step and makes the gate's test baseline match CI. This permanently fixes the repo's gating, not just this branch. ## What Changed - Adds `bin/fm-x-dismiss.sh` so X mention skips can call the relay dismiss endpoint, with dry-run output, request id validation, and failure behavior matching the existing reply client. - Updates the X response playbook and docs so pure acknowledgments dismiss relay requests instead of only deleting local inbox files. - Configures no-mistakes to run the firstmate bash test suite directly with a tmux preflight, matching CI more closely. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, this is a narrow additive client plus docs and focused tests, reusing the existing X reply-client patterns with no material review findings. ## Testing I inspected the branch intent and touched files, ran the focused X-mode behavior suite, ran the full bash test loop that the new no-mistakes test command uses, produced reviewer-visible fake-relay transcripts and dry-run JSON evidence under the requested evidence directory, and confirmed the worktree stayed clean.

title: fix(fm-brief): bash 3.2 here-doc parse error breaks default brief scaffolding
body:
## Problem

On stock macOS Bash (GNU bash **3.2.57**, i.e. `/bin/bash`), `bin/fm-brief.sh` fails to parse:

```
$ /bin/bash -n bin/fm-brief.sh
bin/fm-brief.sh: line 211: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `''
bin/fm-brief.sh: line 263: syntax error: unexpected end of file
```

This breaks the **default** task path: no-mistakes-mode briefs cannot be scaffolded at all on a stock-bash machine. It went unnoticed because modern bash (5.x) parses the file fine.

## Root cause

The no-mistakes (default-mode) Definition-of-done block was assigned via command substitution wrapping a here-doc:

```sh
DOD=$(cat <<EOF
...
Follow no-mistakes' own guidance for the mechanics: ...
...
EOF
)
```

That here-doc body contains an apostrophe (`no-mistakes'`). Bash 3.2's command-substitution parser mis-tokenizes the apostrophe inside `$(...)` as an opening single-quote and scans to EOF looking for its match. The `--scout`, `direct-PR`, and `local-only` here-docs happen to contain no apostrophe, so only the default path errored.

A quoted delimiter (`<<'EOF'`) does **not** fix it — the bug is in the `$(...)` command-substitution parser itself, not heredoc quoting (verified: an apostrophe in a `<<'EOF'` body inside `$(...)` still breaks bash 3.2). The same here-doc body parses fine at statement level.

## Fix

Move every mode's Definition-of-done out of `$(...)` and append it directly to the brief with `cat >> "$BRIEF" <<EOF`. The here-doc bodies are byte-identical to before — this is a parser-compatibility fix, not a content change. The assembled brief output is unchanged for all modes: same single blank line at the Project-memory → Definition-of-done join, and `$ID` interpolation plus escaped backticks preserved.

## Validation (stock Bash 3.2.57, `/bin/bash`)

`bash -n` before vs after:

```
# before
bin/fm-brief.sh: line 211: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `''
bin/fm-brief.sh: line 263: syntax error: unexpected end of file   (exit 2)
# after
$ /bin/bash -n bin/fm-brief.sh ; echo $?
0
```

Functionally scaffolded a complete, correct brief under `/bin/bash` for **every** mode and inspected the output:

- **no-mistakes** (default), **direct-PR**, **local-only**, **scout**, and a **--secondmate** charter all scaffold successfully.
- direct-PR / local-only driven via a temp registry (`data/projects.md`); unknown-project fallback (→ no-mistakes) also exercised.
- Confirmed the default-mode brief still contains the unchanged no-mistakes DoD text: the `/no-mistakes` invocation, `no-mistakes axi run --help`, the ask-user / `--yes` rules, and the `done: PR {url} checks green` line.
- Confirmed exactly one blank line at the Project-memory → Definition-of-done join, backticks rendered (not literal `` \` ``), and `$ID` interpolated correctly in Setup, Rule 1, and the local-only/direct-PR DoD.

Diff is limited to `bin/fm-brief.sh`.

title: feat(cognee): add local lookup manifest checker
body:
## Summary

Firstmate can now rehearse Cognee lookup locally without touching Cognee, MCP config, env files, or remote datasets. A dry-run wrapper treats answer text as `hint_only` by default, then upgrades only locally verified references to `verified_local_source` or `stale_warning` after manifest, checksum, path-risk, and source reopen checks pass.

The checker fails closed for missing citations, unknown manifest references, unsafe redaction status, risky source paths, bad size/checksum, and high/live stale-risk labels. Even verified local matches keep `external_action_authorized=false`, so memory output cannot become merge, deploy, cleanup, vendor, or customer authority.

## Notes

- Manifest support is TSV-only in this first wrapper; JSONL can be added later if a real importer needs it.
- No Cognee API path is implemented. Running without `--dry-run` exits before any network or config access.
- Code review was a manual staged-diff review. The multi-agent CE review path was not used because this harness exposes sub-agents only when the user explicitly requests delegation.

## Tests

- `bash -n bin/*.sh tests/*.sh`
- `tests/fm-cognee-lookup.test.sh`
- `for t in tests/*.test.sh; do bash "$t"; done`

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

No additional production monitoring is required. This is local CLI plumbing only, with no daemon, network call, config mutation, or remote dataset mutation. Healthy validation is continued passing shell tests and local dry-run output that keeps unverified Cognee text labeled as `hint_only`.

title: fix(spawn): make tmux window handling robust under non-default config
body:
## Intent The developer was working on the firstmate codebase as an ordinary software project, tasking a coding agent with applying a small robustness fix to bin/fm-spawn.sh's tmux window handling to address two empirically-reproduced bugs that surface under a non-default tmux config (base-index 1 and automatic-rename on): a window-creation collision (fixed by targeting the session with a trailing colon so tmux appends at the next free index) and a dangerous lost-window-name issue where a renamed window caused the wait-loop to misread firstmate's own primary checkout as the worktree (fixed by capturing the stable window id, disabling automatic-rename/allow-rename, and targeting by id). They required the change be confined to that one script plus an optional deterministic test, that bash -n and shellcheck pass, and that the behavior test suite (especially the spawn/tangle tests) pass, with the work shipping through the no-mistakes contribution pipeline. After the code was committed and verified locally, the pipeline was blocked by a no-mistakes gate transport error (invalid gate path: '.'); the developer fixed gate infrastructure on their end (restarting the daemon and clearing the stale ref), and when that did not resolve it, told the agent to stand by while they worked the deeper no-mistakes transport/path issue from the firstmate side, instructing it not to retry the gate or change anything. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-spawn.sh`: create the task window by targeting the session with a trailing colon so tmux appends at the next free index instead of colliding when `base-index` is non-zero, and capture the resulting stable window id from `new-window -P`. - `bin/fm-spawn.sh`: disable `automatic-rename`/`allow-rename` on the new window and target the worktree wait loop and `treehouse get` send-keys by the captured window id, so a window rename can no longer make the wait loop misread firstmate's own primary checkout as the worktree. - Added `test_spawn_tmux_window_construction` to `tests/fm-tangle-guard.test.sh` covering the window-construction behavior, and listed it in the `CONTRIBUTING.md` coverage list. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A small, well-bounded robustness fix confined to one script's tmux handling plus a hermetic deterministic test; the only finding is a low-practical-risk consistency gap where the launch and persisted meta target still use name-based addressing the fix otherwise hardened against. ## Testing `Baseline (the full tmux-gated e2e suite) already passed; on top of that I confirmed the change's added deterministic test passes and then demonstrated the intent end-to-end on a real tmux server configured with the exact bug-triggering options (base-index 1, automatic-rename on, allow-rename on). Running the real fm-spawn.sh there, it spawns successfully, resolves the correct isolated worktree, and the window retains its fm- name despite the rename config; a side-by-side run against the actual pre-fix base script shows that code deterministically failing under the same conditions, and an instrumented copy proves the most dangerous mode — the old name-based query silently returning firstmate's own primary checkout as the worktree and slipping past the isolation guard. Bug 1's hard collision does not surface as an error on the installed tmux 3.6b for a bare session name (it does for an explicitly occupied index), but the colon-append form the fix adopts is the canonical version-independent append and is pinned by the new test — non-actionable. This is a shell/CLI/tmux change with no rendered UI surface, so evidence is CLI transcripts rather than screenshots. Overall: all tests pass and the user intent is demonstrated working end-to-end.`
Evidence: Focused real-tmux mechanism demo (annotated before/after for both bugs) BUG 1 — old form 'new-window -t firstmate:1' => create window failed: index 1 in use; new form 'new-window -t firstmate:' => created @1 at next free index, and CAPTURED the id BUG 2 (name lost to allow-rename): >>> OLD code by NAME (firstmate:fm-job) -> /private/tmp/.../primary *** DANGER: firstmate's PRIMARY checkout, NOT the worktree *** >>> NEW code by id (@1) -> /private/tmp/.../worktree CORRECT: the real worktree BUG 2 fix (a) — pinned window after same rename trigger: name stayed 'fm-pinned'; firstmate:fm-pinned -> /private/tmp/.../worktree ```text ================================================================ BUG 1 — window creation under base-index 1 ================================================================ session 'firstmate' created; first window sits at index 1 (base-index 1): 1: home OLD form targets an explicit occupied index -> tmux refuses (collision): new-window -t firstmate:1 => create window failed: index 1 in use (rc=1, refused) NEW form targets the session with a trailing colon -> tmux appends at next free index: new-window -t 'firstmate:' => created @1 at next free index, and CAPTURED the id 1: home (@0) 2: fm-job (@1) ================================================================ BUG 2 — window name lost to automatic-rename/allow-rename ================================================================ PRIMARY (firstmate's own checkout) = /private/tmp/fm-mech.tDnmqD/primary WORKTREE (crewmate's isolated wt) = /private/tmp/fm-mech.tDnmqD/worktree The worktree subshell cd's in and its prompt emits a title escape; with allow-rename on, tmux renames the window away from 'fm-job' instantly: 1: ..DnmqD/primary (@0) cwd=/private/tmp/fm-mech.tDnmqD/primary 2: ..nmqD/worktree (@1) cwd=/private/tmp/fm-mech.tDnmqD/worktree >>> OLD code queried the window by NAME (firstmate:fm-job): -> returns: /private/tmp/fm-mech.tDnmqD/primary -> *** DANGER: that is firstmate's PRIMARY checkout, NOT the worktree *** >>> NEW code queries the window by stable id (@1): -> returns: /private/tmp/fm-mech.tDnmqD/worktree -> CORRECT: the real worktree ================================================================ BUG 2 fix part (a) — pinning the name blocks the rename entirely ================================================================ created+pinned @2 (name fm-pinned); now hit it with the SAME rename trigger: name after the rename attempt: fm-pinned (stayed fm-pinned) name-based target now still resolves correctly: firstmate:fm-pinned -> /private/tmp/fm-mech.tDnmqD/worktree ```
Evidence: End-to-end: real fm-spawn.sh under bug config (PASS) spawned e2e-fix-zz9 harness=codex kind=ship mode=no-mistakes yolo=off window=firstmate:fm-e2e-fix-zz9 worktree=/private/tmp/fm-e2e.../wt meta: window=firstmate:fm-e2e-fix-zz9 / worktree=/private/tmp/fm-e2e.../wt live windows: 2: fm-e2e-fix-zz9 (@1) cwd=/private/tmp/fm-e2e.../wt PASS: resolved the WORKTREE, not the primary checkout PASS: window kept its name 'fm-e2e-fix-zz9' (automatic-rename pinned off) === END-TO-END RESULT: PASS === ```text === inputs === project (primary checkout) = /private/tmp/fm-e2e.6bENaQ/proj worktree (isolated) = /private/tmp/fm-e2e.6bENaQ/wt tmux config: base-index 1, automatic-rename on, allow-rename on === running REAL bin/fm-spawn.sh (TMUX unset -> creates 'firstmate' session on private socket) === warn: no registry at /tmp/fm-e2e.6bENaQ/home/data/projects.md; defaulting proj to no-mistakes off spawned e2e-fix-zz9 harness=codex kind=ship mode=no-mistakes yolo=off window=firstmate:fm-e2e-fix-zz9 worktree=/private/tmp/fm-e2e.6bENaQ/wt fm-spawn exit code = 0 === state/e2e-fix-zz9.meta written by fm-spawn === window=firstmate:fm-e2e-fix-zz9 worktree=/private/tmp/fm-e2e.6bENaQ/wt project=/private/tmp/fm-e2e.6bENaQ/proj harness=codex kind=ship mode=no-mistakes yolo=off === live tmux windows on the private server (name pinned despite automatic-rename) === 1: bash (@0) cwd=/Users/pierre/.no-mistakes/worktrees/115f5e328d0c/01KW98ENA4KVE77QNFD2YZKQS9 2: fm-e2e-fix-zz9 (@1) cwd=/private/tmp/fm-e2e.6bENaQ/wt PASS: fm-spawn resolved the WORKTREE (/private/tmp/fm-e2e.6bENaQ/wt), not the primary checkout PASS: spawned window kept its name 'fm-e2e-fix-zz9' (automatic-rename pinned off) === END-TO-END RESULT: PASS === ```
Evidence: Before/after vs pre-fix base script (base fails 3/3, fix correct 3/3) BEFORE (base 81c94db): BASE#1 exit=1 aborted; BASE#2 exit=1 aborted; BASE#3 exit=1 aborted AFTER (target e00cc40): FIXED#1 CORRECT (real worktree); FIXED#2 CORRECT; FIXED#3 CORRECT ```text ############ BEFORE — base 81c94db (name-based targeting), allow-rename trigger ############ [BASE#1] exit=1 [BASE#1] aborted before recording a worktree. message: (real worktree=/private/tmp/fm-ba.sbm165/wt ; primary=/private/tmp/fm-ba.sbm165/primary ; project=/private/tmp/fm-ba.sbm165/proj) [BASE#2] exit=1 [BASE#2] aborted before recording a worktree. message: (real worktree=/private/tmp/fm-ba.bqqBYu/wt ; primary=/private/tmp/fm-ba.bqqBYu/primary ; project=/private/tmp/fm-ba.bqqBYu/proj) [BASE#3] exit=1 [BASE#3] aborted before recording a worktree. message: (real worktree=/private/tmp/fm-ba.fSoH8f/wt ; primary=/private/tmp/fm-ba.fSoH8f/primary ; project=/private/tmp/fm-ba.fSoH8f/proj) ############ AFTER — target e00cc40 (window-id + name pinned) ############ [FIXED#1] exit=0 [FIXED#1] CORRECT: resolved the real worktree (/private/tmp/fm-ba.LLcFFN/wt) (real worktree=/private/tmp/fm-ba.LLcFFN/wt ; primary=/private/tmp/fm-ba.LLcFFN/primary ; project=/private/tmp/fm-ba.LLcFFN/proj) [FIXED#2] exit=0 [FIXED#2] CORRECT: resolved the real worktree (/private/tmp/fm-ba.VjTgOo/wt) (real worktree=/private/tmp/fm-ba.VjTgOo/wt ; primary=/private/tmp/fm-ba.VjTgOo/primary ; project=/private/tmp/fm-ba.VjTgOo/proj) [FIXED#3] exit=0 [FIXED#3] CORRECT: resolved the real worktree (/private/tmp/fm-ba.1NZBC8/wt) (real worktree=/private/tmp/fm-ba.1NZBC8/wt ; primary=/private/tmp/fm-ba.1NZBC8/primary ; project=/private/tmp/fm-ba.1NZBC8/proj) ```
Evidence: Instrumented base proves primary-checkout misread DEBUG[base]: wait-loop resolved WT=/private/tmp/.../primary (PROJ_ABS=/private/tmp/.../proj) spawned ba-task-qq1 ... worktree=/private/tmp/.../primary <-- pre-fix records firstmate's OWN checkout as the worktree; isolation guard did not catch it ```text Captures: the PRE-FIX (base) fm-spawn under base-index 1 + automatic-rename/allow-rename. The wait-loop misreads firstmate's OWN primary checkout as the worktree and the isolation guard does NOT catch it (the primary is a distinct repo). Result: meta records worktree=. (Launch send-keys short-circuited in this analysis copy so the misread is visible; in the unmodified base the final launch then errors on the lost name.) ================================================================ PRIMARY=/private/tmp/fm-ba.8XLVDL/primary WT=/private/tmp/fm-ba.8XLVDL/wt PROJ=/private/tmp/fm-ba.8XLVDL/proj ---- fm-spawn output ---- DEBUG[base]: wait-loop resolved WT=/private/tmp/fm-ba.8XLVDL/primary (PROJ_ABS=/private/tmp/fm-ba.8XLVDL/proj) warn: no registry at /tmp/fm-ba.8XLVDL/home/data/projects.md; defaulting proj to no-mistakes off DEBUG[base]: would launch into window firstmate:fm-ba-task-qq1 (name-based) spawned ba-task-qq1 harness=codex kind=ship mode=no-mistakes yolo=off window=firstmate:fm-ba-task-qq1 worktree=/private/tmp/fm-ba.8XLVDL/primary ---- exit=0 ---- ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 warning - ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:502` - The fix hardens the worktree wait loop and the `treehouse get` send-keys to use the stable `$WID`, with a comment warning that a lost window name makes `display-message -t <bad-name>` fall back to the active client's window. But the two highest-stakes operations still use the name-based `$T` (`$SES:$W`): the agent launch at lines 502/504 (`tmux send-keys -t "$T" -l "$LAUNCH"` then `Enter`) and the persisted supervision target at line 479 (`window=$T` in meta, consumed by fm-peek/fm-send/fm-teardown/fm-watch/fm-ff-lib as a tmux target for the whole task lifetime). In the exact scenario the fix defends against — the name lost before the rename-disable settles (e.g. an `allow-rename` escape sequence in the create→disable gap) — the launch keys could be sent to the wrong/active pane (potentially firstmate's own session) and the recorded `window=` target would be broken for all later supervision. In practice the risk is low: `new-window -n` auto-disables automatic-rename for the window, `allow-rename off` is set before treehouse/agent run, so by launch time the name is well-pinned and the residual race is a microsecond window with a bare shell. Recommend using `$WID` for the launch send-keys and the persisted meta target for full consistency with the fix's own rationale; note this changes the documented `window=<session:window>` meta/output format (line 30) to a `@id`, which is a valid tmux target everywhere but is the reason this warrants author sign-off rather than a blind change.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` - `bash tests/fm-tangle-guard.test.sh` — full file incl. the new `test_spawn_tmux_window_construction`; all 6 cases ok - Full behavior suite spot-checked: ran each `tests/*.test.sh`; every file that completed reported its final `ok`/`all ... passed` line (matches the green baseline run) - Real-tmux mechanism demo on an isolated server with `base-index 1; automatic-rename on; allow-rename on`: old form `new-window -t firstmate:1` collides (`index 1 in use`); new form `new-window -dP -F '#{window_id}' -t 'firstmate:'` appends and captures the id - Real-tmux Bug-2 reproduction: after a worktree subshell emits a window-rename escape, `display-message -p -t firstmate:fm-job` silently returns firstmate's PRIMARY checkout, while `display-message -p -t @<id>` returns the real worktree; `set-window-option automatic-rename/allow-rename off` keeps the name pinned - End-to-end with the REAL `bin/fm-spawn.sh` under the bug config (fake `treehouse get` cd'ing into a genuine git worktree, fake `codex`): exit 0, `worktree=` resolves to the worktree, meta correct, window keeps name `fm-<id>` (`e2e-spawn-nondefault-tmux.sh`) - Before/after: base `fm-spawn.sh` from `81c94db` (staged with current libs) vs the fixed worktree script, 3 runs each — base fails 3/3, fixed resolves the real worktree 3/3 (`e2e-before-after.sh`) - Instrumented analysis copy of the base script: proves the pre-fix wait-loop resolves `WT=<primary checkout>` and records `worktree=<primary>`, with the isolation guard not catching it
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: cs-backend: migrate crewmate execution from local worktrees to leased GitHub Codespaces
body:
## Summary

Migrates the crewmate execution backend for **project ship/scout tasks** from local treehouse git worktrees to **leased GitHub Codespaces**. Each project crewmate now runs its Copilot CLI harness *inside* a leased codespace, driven from a local tmux pane over `gh codespace ssh`, with a relay bridging remote status back to local state. **Secondmates remain local treehouse worktrees** — unchanged.

## What changed

**New backend infrastructure (prior commits):**
- `bin/fm-cs-lib.sh` — lease registry, repo/pool helpers, dual-auth `gh` wrapper, token/harness config, headless copilot driver-loop spawn helpers (`cs_push_brief`, `cs_push_driver`, `cs_send_steer`, `cs_pull_report`, …).
- `bin/fm-cs-setup.sh` — codespace cold-setup (installs user-local `gh` when the image lacks it).
- `bin/fm-cs-relay.sh` — remote→local status / turn-end bridge over a persistent SSH `tail -F`.
- `bin/fm-cs-pool.sh` — pool acquire/release (reuse FREE pooled lease, else cold-create).
- Offline test suites: `cs-lib` (35), `cs-pool` (13), `cs-relay` (8) — all green.

**Rewired existing scripts to the codespace backend:**
- `fm-spawn.sh` — ship/scout lease a codespace, push brief+driver, create SSH pane, detached relay supervisor; **refuses `local-only`** (no GitHub repo ⇒ no codespace).
- `fm-teardown.sh` — codespace teardown branch with a **fail-closed** landed-work check (requires a positive `__FM_OK__` SSH sentinel; an SSH failure no longer reads as "landed").
- `fm-send.sh` — steers codespace crewmates via the remote inbox file (the headless driver loop can't be reached by `tmux send-keys`).
- `fm-review-diff.sh`, `fm-pr-check.sh` — run their diff / HEAD / PR checks over SSH inside the lease.
- `fm-brief.sh` — ship/scout briefs rewritten for the codespace model (remote events/report paths; ship resets to a clean default branch before branching).
- Retired the worktree-tangle guard (`fm-tangle-lib.sh` deleted; refs removed from `fm-guard.sh`, `fm-bootstrap.sh`) — project crewmates no longer touch local worktrees.
- `AGENTS.md` rewritten for the codespace-lease model (CLAUDE.md symlink unchanged).

## Notes for the reviewer
- **`local-only` projects are now unsupported** on this backend (they have no GitHub repo to lease a codespace from); `fm-spawn` refuses them with a clear message.
- **no-mistakes gate was not run** — the tool isn't installed in this environment (installing needs captain consent). A thorough `code-review` pass was used as the substitute; it found one high-severity fail-open bug in the teardown landed-check, now fixed (`__FM_OK__` sentinel, fail-closed).
- Live end-to-end verification against a real codespace lease was done in prior sessions; it was **not** re-run after these final rewires.

🤖 Generated with GitHub Copilot CLI

title: feat: add grok crewmate harness support
body:
## Intent Add grok (the Grok Build CLI from xAI) as a fully supported, empirically verified crewmate harness adapter in firstmate, so crewmates can run on grok. Follows the harness-adapters 'verify a new adapter' flow. Encoded across the machinery: (1) fm-harness.sh detects grok via the GROK_AGENT=1 env marker (grok does NOT set CLAUDECODE despite Claude-Code compatibility) plus 'grok' command-name ancestry; (2) fm-spawn.sh adds grok's launch template 'grok --always-approve "$(cat BRIEF)"' (verified fully autonomous, no permission gate) and installs grok's turn-end Stop hook; (3) fm-watch.sh and fm-tmux-lib.sh add grok's busy signature 'Ctrl+c:cancel'; (4) the harness-adapters skill gains a grok facts section and the /no-mistakes invocation form; the bare-adapter-name allowlists are extended with grok. KEY DESIGN DECISION (turn-end hook): grok only loads PROJECT-scoped hooks after a manual folder-trust grant, which is not automatic and which firstmate must not establish by editing grok's own managed trust store (high blast radius). So instead of a worktree-local hook, the turn-end hook is installed as ONE firstmate-owned, always-trusted GLOBAL hook at $GROK_HOME/.grok/hooks/fm-turn-end.json that is a deliberate guarded no-op for every non-firstmate grok session: its Stop command fires only when the current workspace holds a per-task .fm-grok-turnend pointer file, then touches the absolute path that pointer names. fm-spawn writes that gitignored pointer (excluded via git info/exclude exactly like the other harnesses' worktree hook files) naming state/.turn-ended, and the hook reads $GROK_WORKSPACE_ROOT (always set for hooks, equal to the worktree). This keeps the hook outside the worktree, needs no trust grant, and writes only firstmate-owned files. The global hook is overwritten idempotently with identical content on every grok spawn (self-healing, no duplicate-table risk). OTHER DELIBERATE CHOICES: the busy signature matches the ASCII 'Ctrl+c:cancel' mid-turn cancel hint rather than grok's braille spinner glyph, to avoid grep locale fragility; it is present iff a turn is running and absent when idle. No FM_COMPOSER_IDLE_RE override is added because grok's idle composer is a bare prompt glyph already classified empty by the generic reader. Two facts from the original task notes were empirically corrected: grok's interrupt is Ctrl+C (cancels the turn) and exit is Ctrl+Q double-press (the notes incorrectly had Ctrl+C as exit; Esc only refocuses scrollback). The gating question was verified positively: grok invokes /no-mistakes and drives a real 'no-mistakes axi run', so grok is usable for no-mistakes-mode tasks, not just direct-PR/local-only/scout. The whole adapter was verified end-to-end through the real fm-spawn (autonomous launch past the project-dir picker into an isolated worktree, brief processed, busy->idle and the turn-end signal both detected, fm-send steer landed, clean Ctrl+Q exit and teardown). config/crew-harness is intentionally left UNCHANGED - this only makes grok available as a verified option; choosing the active crew harness stays the captain's switch. ## What Changed - Added `grok` as a verified crewmate harness adapter, including harness detection, spawn launch support, busy-state detection, turn-end signaling, teardown cleanup, and allowlist coverage. - Documented Grok support across firstmate docs and the harness adapter skill, including the verified autonomy and `/no-mistakes` invocation behavior. - Added and hardened shell tests for the Grok harness path plus related crew-state and watcher-lock timing behavior. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the Grok adapter changes are scoped and the prior hook, lock, teardown, and test-executable issues appear addressed without leaving a material merge blocker. ## Testing The configured full shell sweep had already passed as baseline; I reran focused grok and adjacent supervision tests, produced an isolated CLI transcript that exercises the user-facing spawn, hook, busy-detection, and cleanup path, then reran the full configured suite to exit 0. title: feat(notify): native out-of-band notifier for captain escalations
body:
## Summary A native out-of-band notifier for captain-relevant escalations (the first backend of the pluggable notifier requested in #106). It fires a native OS notification so the captain is pinged off the tmux pane the moment captain-relevant work needs them, in **both** supervision modes - the always-on watcher (`bin/fm-watch.sh`) and the away-mode sub-supervisor daemon (`bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh`).
> firstmate notifications are more detailed in practice ## Behavior - **Persistent, sounding, click-to-focus - never auto-focus.** The toast pops, sounds, and stays up by default. Stealing the foreground was deliberately rejected as invasive; instead, clicking **Go to firstmate** raises the host terminal and selects the firstmate tmux window+pane, resolved *dynamically at click time* with nothing hardcoded. The resolution is shared between the notifier and the click handler via `bin/fm-focus-lib.sh` so they cannot drift. - **Open PR button**, gated to review/done-state notifications. `fm-notify.sh --open ` adds a second action that opens the PR. It rides only when a captain-relevant `done:` status carries a PR/MR URL and the task is not `local-only`; a mixed wake that pairs a `needs-decision`/`blocked`/`failed` item with a `done:` line stays a decision notification and gets no Open-PR button. The URL rides only the flag, so the id-free summary text is unchanged. - **`FM_NOTIFY` kill switch.** `FM_NOTIFY=off` (and the aliases `0`/`false`/`no`/`disabled`/`disable`) silences everything. The gate is enforced *before any command runs*, so a custom `FM_NOTIFY_CMD` override can never become a bypass. ## Platform backends Each backend mirrors the behavior as closely as it robustly allows: - **WSL / Windows:** a raw WinRT toast via `powershell.exe` (no PowerShell modules), `scenario="reminder"` so it persists, an explicit `

title: feat(dispatch): add dynamic crew profiles

## Intent Implement dynamic dispatch profiles for firstmate. The captain wants optional local config/crew-dispatch.json containing natural-language rules that firstmate reads and matches with its own judgment at intake, while shell scripts only validate the JSON and receive concrete --harness/--model/--effort flags. The change must preserve backward compatibility when the config file and profile flags are absent, inherit the dispatch JSON into secondmate homes, add low-cost bootstrap validation, document the behavior in AGENTS/docs, and supersede PR #151 by covering model meta/batch support plus broader harness support. Per the captain's follow-up, every supported harness flag must be empirically verified and effort values must be passed only when accepted by that harness: Claude supports model plus low/medium/high/xhigh/max effort, Codex uses --model plus -c model_reasoning_effort for low/medium/high/xhigh only, Grok uses --model plus --reasoning-effort for low/medium/high/xhigh only, Pi uses --model plus --thinking for low/medium/high/xhigh only, and Opencode supports model only for firstmate's interactive launch. Unsupported effort values are recorded in meta for traceability but omitted from launch flags so spawns do not break. ## What Changed - Adds optional `config/crew-dispatch.json` profiles so firstmate can choose per-task harness, model, and effort from validated local rules while `fm-spawn` receives concrete launch flags. - Expands spawn support and metadata handling for model and effort across verified crewmate harnesses, omitting unsupported effort flags while preserving traceability. - Documents dispatch profile configuration and inheritance, propagates the dispatch config into secondmate homes safely, and adds bootstrap/spawn/secondmate harness tests for the new behavior. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the change is well-bounded around dispatch profile validation, spawn flag construction, and inherited config propagation, with no material correctness issues found in the reviewed diff. ## Testing The pre-run full-suite baseline was already green; I reran the smallest changed-area tests for spawn profile flags, bootstrap dispatch validation, and secondmate config inheritance, then produced an E2E transcript showing fake tmux captured launches, meta persistence, valid/invalid crew-dispatch bootstrap behavior, and secondmate inheritance; no worktree changes or leftover transient `/tmp/fm-demo-*` artifacts remained.

title: fix(fm-brief): unbalanced apostrophe breaks ship-brief scaffolding
body:
## Bug

Scaffolding a **ship** brief with `bin/fm-brief.sh` fails outright:

```
bin/fm-brief.sh: line 211: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `''
```

The script does not parse, so `fm-brief.sh <id> <repo>` (ship path) errors and writes nothing. Scout briefs use a different code path and are unaffected.

## Root cause

In the no-mistakes ship-brief branch (the `*)` default of the `case`), the definition-of-done text is built inside a command-substitution heredoc:

```sh
DOD=$(cat <<EOF
...
Follow no-mistakes' own guidance for the mechanics: ...
...
EOF
)
```

The lone apostrophe in `no-mistakes'` is read by bash's command-substitution parser as an opening single quote that is never closed, so the whole `$( ... )` — and the rest of the script — fails to tokenize.

## Fix

Reword `no-mistakes' own guidance` -> `the no-mistakes guidance` so no unbalanced single quote remains in that heredoc. Minimal one-line change; no restructuring. Grepped the file for other lone/unbalanced single quotes inside `$( ... )` heredocs — line 211 was the only one (other apostrophes are in comments, in single-quoted assignments, or in the plain `cat > "$BRIEF"` redirect heredoc, which is not parsed the same way).

## Verification

- `bash -n bin/fm-brief.sh` now exits 0.
- `bin/fm-brief.sh <throwaway-id> grafana-recommender` (ship, no-mistakes mode — the previously-broken path) prints `scaffolded: ...` and writes a valid brief; throwaway data dir removed afterward.
- `--scout` path still scaffolds correctly.
- Generated ship-brief text reads sensibly after the reword.

Note: related to #166 and overlaps with #173 (which also touches this apostrophe among other changes).

title: fix(spawn): wrap launch command in bash -c for non-bash pane shells
body:
## Summary
- Every harness's launch command in `launch_template()` used bash-only `"$(cat __BRIEF__)"` command substitution, which fails outright when the treehouse worktree's interactive pane shell is fish instead of bash/zsh.
- Wraps the fully assembled launch string in `shell_quote()`'d `bash -c` right before the final `tmux send-keys`, so the pane's own shell only ever needs to parse `bash -c '<string>'` regardless of whether it's fish, zsh, or bash.
- Also fixes a portability bug the pipeline caught along the way in the same area (Darwin `stat -f` vs `stat -c` detection).

title: fix(spawn): pin tmux session targets with exact-match form
body:
## Intent Fix a tmux target-ambiguity bug: a numeric tmux session name (e.g. a session literally named 7) passed as a bare -t target resolves as a window index of the current session, landing the crewmate window in an unrelated session or colliding with an occupied index. Pin session targets with tmux's exact-match form (=SES: / =firstmate) in the tmux backend, and add an end-to-end regression test with a numeric session so spawns land in the intended session with no collision. ## What Changed - Pin tmux session targets to the exact-match form (`=firstmate` in container-ensure, `=:` in create-task's `list-windows`/`new-window`) in `bin/backends/tmux.sh`, so a numeric session name (a session literally named `7`) is no longer misread by `-t` as a window index of the current session — which previously landed the crewmate window in an unrelated session or failed on an occupied index. - Add explanatory comments in `bin/fm-spawn.sh` and the tmux backend documenting the exact-match targeting rationale. - Add an end-to-end regression test (`tests/fm-spawn-tmux-target.test.sh`) covering a spawn into a session named `7` with an occupied index 7 and no leak into a decoy session, plus the outside-tmux path still targeting `firstmate`; extend `tests/fm-backend.test.sh`, pin an rc-free bash and pane `PATH` for CI, and list the new test in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A tightly-scoped, correct fix that pins only the two bare session-target tmux calls that were misparsing numeric session names, backed by an end-to-end regression test and documentation, with no other unpinned session targets and no functional risk to the safe colon-qualified pane targets. ## Testing The configured baseline suite already ran green; I ran the smallest relevant set for this change — the new e2e regression test `tests/fm-spawn-tmux-target.test.sh` and the two touched backend suites — all pass. I also captured a manual before/after transcript on a live tmux server showing the bare numeric target failing with `index 7 in use` while the exact-match `=7:` form correctly lands the window in the session named `7`. The full 25-test e2e suite exceeded the 2-minute tool timeout but is unrelated to this change and covered by the baseline. This is a CLI/tooling change with no UI surface, so CLI transcripts are the appropriate reviewer-visible evidence.
Evidence: tmux target ambiguity: before/after demo on live tmux server Current session: 7 (indices 0-7 in use) OLD: bare '-t 7' -> FAILED: create window failed: index 7 in use NEW: exact '=7:' -> SUCCESS: window created in session 7, 0 leak into decoy 'other' ```text ### Reproducing the tmux target-ambiguity bug and the exact-match fix ### tmux 3.4 Current session on server: 7 (window indices in use: 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 ) --- OLD behavior: bare '-t 7' (session name misread as window index of current session) --- FAILED as expected: create window failed: index 7 in use --- NEW behavior: exact-match '=7:' pins the session named 7 --- SUCCESS: window 'newexact' created in session 7 session 7 windows now: bash bash bash bash bash bash bash bash newexact did it leak into decoy 'other'? -> 0 matches ```
Evidence: end-to-end regression test transcript ok - raw tmux: bare numeric -t collides with a window index; exact form '=7:' pins the session ok - fm-spawn in a session named '7' lands its window in session 7 despite occupied index 7 ok - fm-spawn outside tmux still creates and targets the dedicated 'firstmate' session all fm-spawn tmux target tests passed ```text ### End-to-end regression test: tests/fm-spawn-tmux-target.test.sh ### (fm-spawn run against a real tmux server whose current session is literally named '7' with index 7 occupied) ok - raw tmux: bare numeric -t collides with a window index; exact form '=7:' pins the session ok - fm-spawn in a session named '7' lands its window in session 7 despite occupied index 7 ok - fm-spawn outside tmux still creates and targets the dedicated 'firstmate' session all fm-spawn tmux target tests passed EXIT=0 ```
- Outcome: 🔧 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ across 2 runs (16m28s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

title: feat(bin): add experimental Herdr runtime backend
body:
## Intent

Implement P2 of firstmate's runtime-backend abstraction: an experimental herdr session-provider backend (bin/backends/herdr.sh), on top of the P1 tmux-extraction dispatcher already on main. Herdr is a session provider only - treehouse stays the worktree provider (locked decision D3). The container shape (tab-per-task in one 'firstmate' workspace vs workspace-per-task) was an open decision (D4) I resolved empirically against the real herdr v0.7.1 binary: tab-per-task wins because both shapes expose identical per-item agent_status rollups via their list calls, but tab-per-task gives a materially better single-attach human-watching story (one tab bar shows the whole fleet) matching tmux's model. Busy-state detection uses herdr's native agent.get semantic state (working/idle/done/blocked) as the primary signal in fm-watch.sh and fm-crew-state.sh, falling back to the existing tmux pane-regex detector only when herdr reports unknown - this is intentional layering, not a regression risk to tmux, since tmux's own busy-state dispatch call always returns unknown and its regex path is unchanged. fm-spawn.sh's tmux-specific calls were refactored into small backend-dispatching wrapper functions (spawn_send_text_line etc.) that just delegate to the existing tmux adapter functions for backend=tmux, specifically to keep the tmux command sequence byte-identical - I verified this against the existing old-vs-new conformance test suite (tests/fm-backend.test.sh), which I also had to fix: it had a PRE-EXISTING bug on main (missing bin/fm-backend.sh and bin/backends/ from its old-bin fixture, causing a source failure) unrelated to my change but blocking the 'entire existing suite must stay green' requirement, so I fixed the test fixture itself. During empirical verification against the real herdr binary I found and fixed two real herdr v0.7.1 CLI bugs that were not documented anywhere: (1) 'pane read --lines N' returns completely empty output when N is smaller than the pane's viewport height (~23 rows) instead of clamping to the last N lines - worked around by always requesting >=200 lines from herdr and trimming to the caller's actual bound locally with tail; this was critical because my own composer-verification code requested only 6 lines and was silently getting nothing back, which I caught via a flaky real smoke-test run. (2) 'pane get' JSON's .result.pane.cwd field is frozen at pane-creation time and never updates when the shell cd's or enters a subshell; I originally read that field for fm-spawn.sh's worktree-discovery poll (mirroring tmux's pane_current_path poll after 'treehouse get'), which would have made the isolation guard never see the pane leave the project directory - fixed by reading .result.pane.foreground_cwd instead, which tracks the live running process; caught this by actually running the mandatory end-to-end test against a real claude crewmate, not just unit tests. I ran a full, real, end-to-end lifecycle by hand as a captain-mandated bar for this task (not something no-mistakes itself needs to re-run): spawned a real claude crewmate through bin/fm-spawn.sh with FM_BACKEND=herdr against an isolated, throwaway HERDR_SESSION and a scratch FM_HOME/local-only project (never the captain's default herdr session or the live tmux fleet), steered it with bin/fm-send.sh, peeked it with bin/fm-peek.sh, confirmed its done status, confirmed bin/fm-teardown.sh correctly REFUSES before the branch is merged (the unlanded-work safety gate), merged it locally with bin/fm-merge-local.sh, then confirmed teardown succeeds and fully cleans up (worktree returned, herdr pane closed, state files removed) - then tore down all the isolated herdr test infrastructure and scratch state afterward. I also deliberately made a mistake mid-task that I want called out for my own accountability, not hidden: I briefly wrote a findings file to data/fm-backend-design-d7/ under the PRIMARY firstmate checkout (a different git worktree than the one I'm committing from) instead of my own worktree - data/ is gitignored so it created no git-visible change and I deleted the stray file immediately upon noticing, but it was still a real violation of 'never write outside your own worktree' that I want on the record. Added two new test files (tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh with 20 fake-CLI unit tests covering every adapter function including both discovered bugs, and tests/fm-backend-herdr-smoke.test.sh with 11 real-binary assertions gated on herdr actually being installed, run against an isolated session and cleaned up afterward) plus docs/herdr-backend.md recording the full verification findings, the D4 decision evidence, and the end-to-end run evidence, with small pointer updates in docs/architecture.md, docs/configuration.md, and AGENTS.md. bin/fm-bootstrap.sh's tool-detection list was deliberately left unchanged (still unconditionally requires tmux only) - herdr's version/tool gate happens at spawn time instead (fm_backend_herdr_version_check refuses loudly on missing/incompatible herdr or jq) - this was a scope call to keep the diff focused on the adapter and its wiring rather than bootstrap detection polish; I documented it explicitly as a known gap in docs/herdr-backend.md rather than silently leaving it undone.

## What Changed

- Adds an experimental Herdr runtime backend with backend-dispatched spawn, send, peek, watcher, crew-state, daemon, and teardown support while keeping tmux as the default backend.
- Uses Herdr native agent state for busy detection, adds backend-aware stale recovery paths, and documents the Herdr backend behavior and known gaps.
- Adds Herdr unit and smoke coverage plus updates existing backend, crew-state, daemon, and watcher tests for the new runtime path.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: Captain, the remaining risk is mostly integration risk from an opt-in experimental backend and external Herdr CLI semantics, but I did not find a merge-blocking issue in this review pass.

## Testing

The configured full baseline was already successful; I then exercised the herdr adapter through targeted automated tests, a real herdr CLI lifecycle, and a scratch `fm-spawn.sh --backend herdr` flow that showed spawn metadata, peek routing, pane output, tab listing, and cleanup all working.

title: fix(spawn): reject FM_ROOT unconditionally in worktree detection
body:
## Intent

Fix two failing CI checks on the already-open cross-fork PR #187 (fm/fm-spawn-race-fix -> kunchenguid:main), which fixes a race in fm-spawn.sh worktree detection (unconditionally rejecting FM_ROOT as the resolved worktree instead of gating on a timing-sensitive seen-project flag) plus its regression test tests/fm-spawn-worktree-wait.test.sh. That worktree-detection fix itself is already validated and correct and must not change. The two CI failures being fixed here are process issues, not logic bugs: (1) the new test file was committed as mode 100644 instead of 100755, and CI invokes tests/*.test.sh directly rather than through bash, so the non-executable file aborted with exit 126 - fixed by chmod +x and recording the bit in git; (2) PR #187 was originally raised manually via gh pr create instead of through no-mistakes, so the PR body is missing the deterministic no-mistakes signature the 'Require no-mistakes' check greps for - this run re-raises it through the pipeline via a fork remote (atqamz/firstmate) since the PR author has no push access to the upstream repo, so the pipeline pushes to the fork and updates the existing cross-fork PR #187 against kunchenguid/firstmate. No other code changes are intended or wanted on this branch.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` and `bin/backends/orca.sh`: drop the timing-sensitive `seen_proj` gate and unconditionally reject `FM_ROOT` as a resolved spawn worktree, closing a race where a crewmate could be launched against the primary checkout instead of an isolated worktree.
- `tests/fm-spawn-worktree-wait.test.sh`: add regression coverage for the worktree-wait/detection race, and fix its file mode to executable (100755) so the test harness, which invokes `tests/*.test.sh` directly, can run it.
- Update related backend/dispatch/harness test fakes (`fm-backend*.test.sh`, `fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh`, `fm-secondmate-sync.test.sh`, `fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh`, `fm-tangle-guard.test.sh`, `fm-grok-harness.test.sh`, `fm-bootstrap.test.sh`, `fm-session-start.test.sh`, `fm-x-mode.test.sh`) to model a project-first pane flow consistent with the new detection logic.
- Document the configurable spawn worktree timeout and unconditional `FM_ROOT` rejection in `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/zellij-backend.md`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Diff = chmod fix (verified 100755 on new test file) + already-landed prior commits (FM_ROOT unconditional rejection, configurable timeout, orca JSON-parse guard, PATH portability in tests). Logic reviewed end to end: FM_ROOT_REAL/PROJ_ABS_REAL comparison is correct and order-independent, all make_spawn_fakebin call sites updated consistently for the new proj param, orca.sh JSON parse failure now exits 1 and every caller already treats nonzero as generic failure. No functional or behavioral changes beyond what intent describes.

title: fix(spawn): re-export PWD after worktree entry to prevent gate path failures
body:
## Intent The developer directed a crewmate agent to fix a firstmate bug where crewmate shells inherited a broken $PWD="." environment variable from treehouse's worktree-entry chain, causing the no-mistakes gate's post-receive hook to fail with "invalid gate path: .". Requirements: confirm the bug empirically, add a minimal, targeted re-export of PWD (via pwd -P) in bin/fm-spawn.sh right after worktree entry for ship/scout launches (not necessarily secondmates), add a matching bash-style test following existing test conventions, and document the diagnosis/rationale in AGENTS.md, without touching the external no-mistakes tool or treehouse binary. After discovering mid-session PWD corruption could recur beyond spawn time, the developer explicitly asked for the fix to be strengthened by also having bin/fm-brief.sh instruct crewmates to re-export PWD immediately before any git push to a no-mistakes gate, with that limitation likewise noted in AGENTS.md. The developer also gave explicit unblocking instructions for a wedged no-mistakes run (re-export PWD, delete-and-repush the branch) and, once genuinely confirmed by a 403 error, directed the agent to push to the captain's own fork (briceparrott1/firstmate) and open the PR from there since the agent lacked direct write access to the upstream template repo (kunchenguid/firstmate). ## What Changed - `bin/fm-spawn.sh` re-exports `PWD="$(pwd -P)"` right after the isolation guard passes for ship/scout launches, fixing a stale `$PWD="."` inherited from treehouse's worktree-entry chain that broke the no-mistakes gate's `post-receive` hook with `invalid gate path: .`. - `bin/fm-brief.sh` adds mid-session guidance instructing crewmates to re-run `export PWD="$(pwd -P)"` immediately before any push to the no-mistakes gate, since the corruption can recur later in a long-lived session, not just at spawn time. - `bin/backends/tmux.sh` and `bin/backends/herdr.sh` are updated to route the PWD re-export command through each backend's own send/exec abstraction rather than a raw call. - `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, and `docs/herdr-backend.md` document the diagnosis and the PWD re-export as a fixed spawn-time (and pre-push) command. - `tests/fm-spawn-pwd-export.test.sh` (new) and `tests/fm-backend.test.sh` cover the re-export behavior against the backend abstraction. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a small, well-scoped defensive re-export of PWD mirroring the existing GOTMPDIR pattern, correctly guarded to non-secondmate launches and routed through the existing backend abstraction (tmux/herdr) rather than raw send-keys; the brief/AGENTS.md/docs updates and the incidental empty-array quoting fix in fm-pr-merge.sh/fm-spawn.sh (needed for bash 3.2 compatibility under set -u) are all consistent and verified, and the accompanying test, while structural rather than behavioral, matches the repo's established test conventions (e.g. fm-gotmp.test.sh). ## Testing Ran the full baseline test suite (all tests/*.test.sh, tmux 3.7 present) which passed cleanly, then specifically re-ran tests/fm-spawn-pwd-export.test.sh (new structural test asserting the PWD re-export is present, correctly ordered between GOTMPDIR and launch, and scoped to non-secondmate) and tests/fm-backend.test.sh (updated conformance test verifying the real tmux command log fm-spawn.sh produces now includes the PWD re-export send at the right point) — both passed. Because the structural tests only assert the source contains the right lines, I additionally drove a real tmux session (the actual mechanism fm-spawn.sh uses) reproducing the documented bug: simulated a pane whose real cwd is correct but whose $PWD env var is stale (\"PWD=.\", matching the \"invalid gate path: .\" failure), confirming a child process inherits the broken value, then sent the exact line bin/fm-spawn.sh now sends (`export PWD=\"$(pwd -P)\"`) and confirmed the pane's PWD env var and any child process's inherited PWD are corrected to the real absolute path. This end-to-end tmux transcript is stronger evidence than the unit tests alone since it exercises the real send-keys mechanism and the real bug/fix behavior. Overall result: fix behaves as intended, no issues found.
Evidence: tmux transcript reproducing the stale-$PWD bug and confirming the fix BEFORE_FIX_ENV: PWD=. child-inherited-PWD=. title: fix(fm-brief): scaffold ship briefs under bash 3.2
body:
## Problem

`bin/fm-brief.sh` fails to run under macOS's stock bash 3.2 (`/usr/bin/env bash` resolves to `/bin/bash`, GNU bash 3.2.57) whenever it scaffolds a ship brief. Because the failure is at **parse time**, the script cannot scaffold *any* ship brief on a stock macOS box:

```
$ /bin/bash -n bin/fm-brief.sh
bin/fm-brief.sh: line 211: unexpected EOF while looking for matching quote
bin/fm-brief.sh: line 263: syntax error: unexpected end of file
```

## Root cause

The ship-mode section built each mode's "Definition of done" with a heredoc wrapped in command substitution:

```sh
DOD=$(cat <<EOF
...
Follow no-mistakes' own guidance ...
... no-mistakes axi respond ...
EOF
)
```

The no-mistakes DOD body contains apostrophes (`no-mistakes'`). Bash 3.2 has a well-known parser bug where a single quote inside a heredoc body that is itself nested in `$(...)` command substitution is treated as an *opening* quote, so the parser runs to EOF looking for its match and aborts. Modern bash (5.x) parses it fine, which is why it was never caught. The scout path was unaffected because it uses a plain `cat > "$BRIEF" <<EOF` (no command substitution).

## Fix

Fix the structural pattern, not the wording (the apostrophes are intentional and future DOD/Setup bodies could gain more): drop the `DOD` variable and the command substitution, and append each mode's Definition of done directly into the brief with a plain `cat >> "$BRIEF" <<EOF` - the same non-nested heredoc form the scout path already uses. The pre-write `case` now only prepares the mode-specific Setup/Rule-1 text. Any future apostrophe in a DOD/Setup body is now safe.

The shebang is untouched (`#!/usr/bin/env bash`); no hard-coded bash path.

## Byte-for-byte identical output

The generated brief is unchanged from the previous intended output on modern bash. Command substitution stripped the heredoc's single trailing newline before `$DOD` expanded; the common body now ends at the "Project memory" blank line and each DOD is appended exactly where `$DOD` used to expand, reproducing the same join and the same single trailing newline. DOD body text diffs identical to `HEAD` for all three ship modes.

## Verification

Before (on macOS, `/bin/bash` = 3.2.57):

```
$ /bin/bash -n bin/fm-brief.sh
bin/fm-brief.sh: line 211: unexpected EOF while looking for matching quote
```

After:

```
$ /bin/bash -n bin/fm-brief.sh   # exits 0, no output
```

Generated real briefs under bash 3.2.57 for **no-mistakes**, **direct-PR**, **local-only**, and **scout**, plus the secondmate charter - all scaffold with no syntax error and correct content (apostrophes render intact). Confirmed the join point keeps a single blank-line separator and the file ends in exactly one trailing newline (no double newline).

## Scope

Tightly scoped to `fm-brief.sh`. `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` has the same `$(cat <<EOF)` shape, but its heredoc bodies carry no lone apostrophes, so it parses cleanly under bash 3.2 (`/bin/bash -n bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` -> OK) and is left unchanged.

title: fix(tests): protect herdr smoke cleanup from default sessions
body:
## Intent Fix a safety bug in the real-herdr smoke tests: their cleanup used a bare/inline-prefixed 'herdr server stop', which is unscoped and silently falls back to whatever herdr server is already running on the machine instead of the test's own isolated throwaway HERDR_SESSION. This killed the captain's live default herdr server twice in production on 2026-07-02 (once from each of tests/fm-backend-herdr-smoke.test.sh and tests/fm-backend-autodetect-smoke.test.sh). Fix: add tests/herdr-test-safety.sh with herdr_safe_stop_and_delete, which (1) uses the explicit-by-name 'herdr session stop/delete ' form instead of the ambient 'server stop', appending --session too, and (2) runs a read-only hard guard (herdr_refuse_if_default) immediately before any stop/delete that re-queries 'herdr session list --json' and refuses if the target is literally default, not found, or flagged default:true - fails closed on any ambiguity. Both smoke test files' cleanup_all now call only this helper. This is a standalone fix, split out from a larger in-progress feature branch (workspace-per-home herdr labeling) specifically so it can merge fast and unblock a separate dependent task; the feature branch will rebase onto this once merged. Verified empirically against a real isolated herdr session (not the fake-CLI mocks): the guard refuses on default/nonexistent/empty session names without ever invoking a destructive command, and correctly tears down a genuinely isolated session while leaving the default session's real workspace state (labels, tab counts) byte-identical before and after. ## What Changed - Hardened real-herdr smoke test cleanup by routing stop/delete through guarded session-name helpers instead of ambient server shutdown. - Added a shared test safety helper that refuses destructive cleanup for empty, missing, default, or ambiguous herdr sessions and re-checks immediately before delete. - Updated herdr smoke test docs and contributor guidance to document the default-session protection. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the change is narrowly scoped to real-herdr smoke-test cleanup and adds a fail-closed guard before destructive session operations. ## Testing The already-successful full baseline was complemented with real-herdr end-to-end evidence: the guard failed closed for empty/default/missing targets, safely stopped and deleted an isolated non-default session, both real smoke tests passed, the normalized default herdr workspace/tab labels and counts were byte-identical before and after, and no working-tree artifacts were left behind.

title: feat(bin): route herdr secondmates into per-home workspaces
body:
## Intent Give each secondmate its own labeled herdr workspace ('space') instead of every firstmate home (the primary and all secondmates) sharing one 'firstmate' workspace, and make crewmates spawned from a secondmate home land in that secondmate's own space. This is a refinement of the P2 herdr backend design (docs/herdr-backend.md), not a reversal: workspace-per-TASK was explicitly rejected there for bad human-watching ergonomics, and stays rejected here - the change is workspace-per-HOME (one space per firstmate home) with tabs-per-task inside it, unchanged from P2's tab-per-task shape within each home. Key decisions: (1) label derivation - the primary (no .fm-secondmate-home marker) resolves to the constant 'firstmate', byte-identical to every pre-existing task's recorded label so there is no forced migration; a secondmate home (marker written by bin/fm-home-seed.sh) resolves to 'firstmate-', read fresh from FM_HOME on every call rather than cached, so it is automatically stable across every respawn without extra bookkeeping. (2) A --secondmate spawn is launched BY THE PRIMARY's own fm-spawn.sh process, whose FM_HOME still names the primary at that point, so fm-spawn.sh's herdr case arm shadows FM_HOME to the secondmate's own home for exactly the two calls that resolve/create the workspace and tab, using bash's temporary-assignment-before-a-command form (verified this restores automatically and works for shell functions, not just external commands) - every other spawn kind (including a crewmate spawned FROM a secondmate's own fm-spawn.sh process) needs no such glue, since that process's own FM_HOME already names the right home; this was proven end to end in a new mandatory E2E test, not merely by code inspection, because this exact path had never run before. (3) Along the way, verifying focus behavior empirically against the real binary uncovered that workspace/tab create do NOT focus by default once a workspace already exists (matching the pre-existing flagless calls) except for the very first workspace ever created in a brand-new session, which focuses regardless - --no-focus is now passed unconditionally on both calls as defense in depth against that one edge case, not a behavior change in the already-safe steady state. (4) Also verifying this empirically surfaced and fixed a real, separate session-targeting bug: HERDR_SESSION (env var, exported or inline-prefixed) is not reliably honored by herdr 0.7.1 CLI subcommands once another herdr server is already running - it silently falls back to whatever server IS running instead of the requested session. A new fm_backend_herdr_cli helper wraps every herdr invocation in the adapter with both HERDR_SESSION and a trailing --session flag (verified to route correctly in both leading and trailing position for every subcommand tried), fixing this for the whole adapter, not just the new label-scoped calls; this same underlying bug is what caused a SEPARATE incident during this work (real herdr smoke-test cleanup killed the captain's live default herdr server twice in production), which was split out and already shipped as its own fast-tracked PR (#199, merged) specifically so it could unblock a concurrent dependent task; this branch is based on top of that merged fix. (5) Label-collision semantics are deliberately NOT disambiguated beyond adopt-the-first-match-by-list-order, mirroring the pre-existing tab duplicate-label behavior - documented as a known, accepted characteristic (a user-created herdr workspace sharing a firstmate home's label would be silently adopted), not something this change newly introduces or needed to solve. Tests: extended the fake-CLI unit tests for per-home label resolution, --no-focus, the --session flag, and workspace-find/list-live scoping; extended the real-CLI smoke test with a secondmate-shaped home's workspace/label, list-live scoping, and restart-stability verification in the MULTI-workspace shape (P2 only verified single-workspace restart stability); added a new mandatory isolated end-to-end test that drives the real bin/fm-spawn.sh and bin/fm-teardown.sh (not just adapter primitives) covering all five required scenarios - primary-shaped home into 'firstmate', a --secondmate spawn into its own labeled space, a crewmate spawned FROM that secondmate-shaped home landing in the same space, teardown closing only the right tab, and list-live recovery seeing only each home's own tabs - all ten assertions passed against the real herdr binary, with the default herdr session's own workspace state confirmed byte-identical immediately before and after every real-herdr test run in this change (an isolated HERDR_SESSION was used throughout, never the captain's default). The tmux backend is completely untouched - this change is entirely contained to the herdr adapter (still marked EXPERIMENTAL), fm-spawn.sh's herdr-only case arm, tests, and docs; no watcher changes. ## What Changed - Adds Herdr workspace-per-home routing so the primary keeps `firstmate`, each secondmate gets `firstmate-`, and secondmate-owned crewmates spawn into that home’s workspace. - Updates the Herdr adapter to resolve workspace labels from `FM_HOME`, pass explicit `--session` targeting, and use `--no-focus` when creating workspaces and tabs. - Expands Herdr unit, smoke, and end-to-end coverage for per-home workspace scoping, secondmate spawning, list-live recovery, teardown behavior, and restart stability. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the change is scoped to the experimental herdr backend, herdr-only spawn behavior, docs, and targeted tests, with existing task operations still routed through recorded pane targets. ## Testing Baseline full-suite testing was already green; I reran the focused herdr unit, real-herdr smoke, and workspace-per-home E2E suites, gathered a real CLI transcript proving workspace-per-home behavior through `fm-spawn.sh`, verified the default herdr session JSON was unchanged before and after, and confirmed no working-tree changes or isolated herdr sessions remained.

title: feat(bin): add unified session start digest
body:
## Intent

Collapse firstmate's multi-turn session start (AGENTS.md sections 3 and 5) into one command, bin/fm-session-start.sh, so a session starts in one or two agent turns instead of six-plus. It composes the existing fm-lock.sh, fm-bootstrap.sh, and fm-wake-drain.sh as real subprocesses (never reimplementing their logic) and prints one ordered digest: lock acquisition, bootstrap's detect-only diagnostics plus its three mutating sweeps (fleet sync, local secondmate fast-forward, X-mode artifacts), the drained wake queue, a context digest (data/projects.md, data/secondmates.md, data/captain.md, data/learnings.md with explicit ABSENT markers when a file is missing, never confused with an empty-but-present file), and a fleet-state digest (data/backlog.md, every state/*.meta, a bounded configurable tail of each state/*.status labeled as wake-event history, the state/.afk flag, and one cheap read-only alive/dead endpoint-liveness check per task reusing a new fm_backend_target_exists primitive added to fm-backend.sh for both the tmux and herdr backends - deliberately NOT the deeper fm-crew-state.sh run-step read, to keep the digest fast and bounded).

Deliberate design decision on ordering: the OLD documented AGENTS.md order was bootstrap-then-lock, which let a second concurrent firstmate session run bootstrap's mutating sweeps before ever discovering another session already held the lock - a real race hazard. I changed the order to lock-first: fm-session-start.sh acquires the lock before any mutating step, and on a lock refusal it prints a loud bordered read-only banner, skips every mutating step (secondmate sync, X-mode artifacts, fleet sync, and the wake-queue drain itself), but still runs bootstrap's read-only detect-only diagnostics (tool/version checks, gh auth, the worktree-tangle check, harness override, crew-dispatch validation, tasks-axi availability) so a refused session is not left completely dark. This required one small additive change to bin/fm-bootstrap.sh: a new opt-in FM_BOOTSTRAP_DETECT_ONLY=1 environment flag that skips only its three mutating sweep calls (secondmate_sync, x_mode_setup, fleet_sync) at the very end of the script, while every existing detect-only diagnostic line runs and prints exactly as before. Default/unset behavior is completely unchanged, so fm-bootstrap.sh, fm-lock.sh, and fm-wake-drain.sh all remain fully working standalone for their other callers (fm-bootstrap.sh install <tools> after consent, /updatefirstmate, the afk daemon, and existing tests) - this is composition via subprocess invocation, not a fork of their logic.

I rewrote AGENTS.md sections 3 and 5 to describe the single command, explicitly instruct the agent NOT to separately re-run fm-bootstrap.sh/fm-lock.sh/fm-wake-drain.sh or re-read any of the digest-printed files afterward (re-reading defeats the entire point of collapsing session start), and to re-read a file only if the digest flagged it ABSENT or unparseable. I grepped AGENTS.md, .agents/skills/, bin/, and docs/ for stale references to the old multi-step flow and found none that needed changing beyond docs/scripts.md (added a row for the new script and noted the new flag/primitive) and CONTRIBUTING.md (added the new test file to the test-file list).

Added tests/fm-session-start.test.sh (8 tests): ABSENT vs empty-but-present vs populated context files, the lock-refusal read-only path (banner leads, every mutating step verifiably skipped - proven by seeding a secondmate meta that WOULD produce a SECONDMATE_SYNC line if the mutating sweep ran, and asserting its absence - detect-only diagnostics still present, digest still completes), output section ordering (diagnostics lead, bulk file dumps follow, verified with line-number comparisons), status-tail bounding (default 5 lines and the FM_SESSION_START_STATUS_TAIL override), per-task endpoint-liveness for both a live and a dead recorded target on both the tmux and herdr backends, and composition (asserting the real fm-lock.sh success text, fm-bootstrap.sh MISSING-tool line, and fm-wake-drain.sh's real drained tab-separated queue record all appear verbatim in the digest, proving the real scripts ran rather than being reimplemented). I manually ran real end-to-end scenarios in throwaway scratch homes (never touching the live fleet's own lock or state): a fresh scratch home, a home seeded with fake in-flight tasks including one live and one dead tmux endpoint plus a real wake-queue record, and a concurrent-lock scenario using a real backgrounded process plus a faked PID TTY TIME CMD
