✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 3 issues found → auto-fixed (6) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/backends/cmux.sh:336` - cmux workspace IDs are documented as unstable across app relaunch, but target_ready only validates the stored workspace_uuid:surface_uuid and fails when that old UUID disappears. After cmux restores a workspace under the same fm-<id> title, fm-send, fm-peek, watcher liveness, and teardown cannot recover the live target; teardown can then remove metadata after a best-effort kill of the stale ID, leaving the workspace unmanaged. Re-resolve by expected label and surface before failing, or refresh meta during recovery. - ⚠️ `bin/backends/cmux.sh:535` - list_live enumerates every fm-* workspace in the shared cmux app with no FM_HOME or session discriminator. Unlike herdr's workspace scope or zellij's session scope, this can expose another firstmate home's tasks if recovery ever consumes it, which conflicts with the documented invariant not to sweep every cmux workspace across homes. Either add a home-specific namespace or keep cmux list-live out of recovery until that design exists. - ⚠️ `bin/backends/cmux.sh:143` - The password file parser removes all whitespace from the first non-empty line, so a cmux socket password containing a space or tab works via CMUX_SOCKET_PASSWORD but is silently changed when stored in config/cmux-socket-password. Preserve the line value except the newline, or reject whitespace with a clear error. 🔧 Fix: Harden cmux recovery and password parsing 3 warnings still open: - ⚠️ `bin/backends/cmux.sh:454` - The `read-screen | jq` pipeline does not propagate a `cmux read-screen` failure when the command emits no stdout, because `jq` exits successfully on empty input. That means `fm-peek`, watcher captures, and submit verification can treat an unreadable surface as a successful blank capture. Capture the raw `read-screen` output first or enable `pipefail` for this command so CLI failures return non-zero. - ⚠️ `bin/backends/cmux.sh:547` - `kill` returns immediately when `close-surface` succeeds, leaving the `fm-<id>` workspace behind if it ever contains a second surface. Since teardown then removes metadata, that task workspace becomes an unmanaged orphan. If firstmate owns the whole task workspace, close the workspace even after a surface close succeeds, or explicitly document and guard the multi-surface case. - ⚠️ `bin/backends/cmux.sh:556` - `list_live` enumerates every `fm-*` workspace in the shared cmux app without an FM_HOME or session discriminator. If recovery/orphan handling starts consuming this helper, one firstmate home can see another home’s cmux tasks, which conflicts with the invariant not to sweep other homes' endpoints. Add a home-specific namespace before wiring it into recovery, or keep it test-only. 🔧 Fix: Harden cmux capture failure handling 4 issues (3 errors, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `bin/backends/cmux.sh:350` - When a stored cmux UUID goes stale, target_ready recovers by the bare `fm-<id>` title in the global cmux app. Because cmux has no per-home namespace, a label collision after app relaunch can make fm-send, fm-peek, or fm-teardown operate on another home's workspace, including closing it during teardown. Add a home-scoped discriminator or avoid global label recovery unless the match is unambiguous. - 🚨 `tests/fm-backend-cmux.test.sh:1` - Git records this new `tests/*.test.sh` file as non-executable, but GitHub CI runs each test script directly with `"$test_script"`. This will fail with permission denied before the test body runs. Mark the file executable. - 🚨 `tests/fm-backend-cmux-smoke.test.sh:1` - Git records this new `tests/*.test.sh` file as non-executable, but GitHub CI runs each test script directly with `"$test_script"`. This will fail with permission denied before the smoke test can skip or run. Mark the file executable. - ⚠️ `bin/backends/cmux.sh:548` - `kill` returns immediately when `close-surface` succeeds, so if a task workspace ever has another surface, teardown removes metadata but leaves the `fm-<id>` workspace open and unmanaged. Since the backend docs say firstmate owns one workspace per task, either close the workspace after a successful surface close or explicitly preserve and document user-added surfaces. 🔧 Fix: Mark cmux test scripts executable 2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `bin/backends/cmux.sh:350` - When the stored cmux UUID is stale, recovery falls back to the first global workspace titled `fm-<id>`. cmux has no per-home namespace and titles are not unique, so another firstmate home with the same task id can receive sends/peeks or be closed during teardown. Add a home-scoped discriminator or recover only from an unambiguous in-home match. - ⚠️ `bin/backends/cmux.sh:548` - `kill` returns as soon as `close-surface` succeeds. If a task workspace ever has a second surface, teardown removes metadata but leaves the `fm-<id>` workspace open and unmanaged. Since the backend owns one workspace per task, either close the workspace too or explicitly preserve and track the multi-surface case. 🔧 Fix: Scope cmux workspaces and teardown 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `bin/backends/cmux.sh:138` - `fm_backend_cmux_password` hard-codes `$FM_HOME/config/cmux-socket-password`, while backend selection honors `FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE`. A run using an overridden config dir can select cmux there and place the socket password there, but cmux auth still fails because the adapter reads the default home config instead. Read `${FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE:-$FM_HOME/config}/cmux-socket-password` here. 🔧 Fix: Captain, honor cmux password config override 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/backends/cmux.sh:269` - The primary-home fallback is the literal `firstmate`, so every primary firstmate home/install in the shared cmux app still creates and recovers titles like `fm-firstmate-<id>`. A stale UUID can still send/peek/teardown another primary home's task when task ids collide, and `list_live` still enumerates other primary homes. Either document that remaining primary-primary collision limit, or add a stable per-primary-home discriminator. 🔧 Fix: Captain, hash cmux home labels ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: fix(afk): support herdr away-mode injection
body:
## Intent

Make the away-mode supervise-daemon (bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh) work on the herdr runtime backend, not just tmux. Live failure: on a herdr-based fleet (firstmate itself running with HERDR_ENV=1, no TMUX_PANE), /afk's daemon errored out at startup because supervisor-pane discovery and every injection primitive (busy-guard, composer-guard, verified submit) were tmux-only raw calls.

Scope, deliberately kept to a transport-layer fix (classification policy, batching, max-defer, the FM_INJECT_MARK contract, locks, and wake-queue handling are explicitly NOT touched):
- Extended supervisor-target/backend discovery: FM_SUPERVISOR_TARGET stays the explicit override (now also accepting a herdr '<session>:<pane-id>' target), and a NEW FM_SUPERVISOR_BACKEND override resolves independently, mirroring bin/fm-backend.sh's own fm_backend_detect precedence (TMUX_PANE wins over HERDR_ENV=1, matching the innermost-first tmux-nested-in-herdr rule; falls back to tmux/firstmate:0 byte-identical to before when nothing is configured or detected).
- zellij and orca are explicitly out of scope for this daemon and refuse loudly at startup with a clear message (FM_SUPERVISOR_SUPPORTED_BACKENDS) rather than being silently misapplied to tmux primitives - this is a deliberate scope decision, not an oversight.
- inject_msg's pane-exists probe, busy-guard (pane_is_busy), composer-guard (pane_input_pending), and verified submit now take an optional backend argument (default tmux, so every existing caller/test is unaffected) and dispatch through bin/fm-backend.sh's generic primitives (fm_backend_target_exists, fm_backend_busy_state, fm_backend_capture, fm_backend_send_text_submit) instead of raw tmux calls. Added a new generic fm_backend_composer_state dispatcher to bin/fm-backend.sh (tmux/herdr/orca arms; zellij/unknown fall back to 'unknown') since no such generic dispatcher existed before, mirroring the existing fm_backend_busy_state pattern.
- For backend=tmux every dispatch resolves to the EXACT same underlying call as before (verified: the full pre-existing test suite, including a real-tmux private-socket e2e test, passes unchanged) - this is intentionally byte-identical, not a behavior change.
- Found and fixed a PRE-EXISTING, unrelated bug while doing empirical real-herdr verification: fm_backend_target_exists's herdr arm called WITHOUT the required --session flag, which docs/herdr-backend.md already documented as unreliable once more than one herdr server is running (it silently falls back to whichever server IS running). This is a real bug affecting bin/fm-session-start.sh's endpoint-liveness digest too, not something I introduced, but it directly blocked the daemon's own herdr startup validation and I fixed it in passing (route through fm_backend_herdr_cli, which appends --session). This is a deliberate fix, not scope creep - it was empirically reproduced (an isolated test session was misrouted to the ambient default session) before being fixed.
- Empirical verification against THIS machine's real herdr, in strict isolation (never the live default session or any live pane): read-only discovery check against my own real pane first (confirmed target/backend resolution), then a full new e2e test file tests/fm-afk-inject-herdr-e2e.test.sh (mirroring tests/fm-afk-inject-e2e.test.sh's tmux e2e) on a throwaway, never-default HERDR_SESSION with guarded teardown (herdr_safe_stop_and_delete), covering: partial-input deferral, swallowed-Enter retry (via a thin herdr CLI shim that swallows exactly one Enter, since herdr's real CLI has no built-in way to drop a keystroke), a normal single digest, and a NEW max-defer scenario (a persistently pending composer must alarm via state/.subsuper-inject-wedged, preserve the buffer, and never crash the daemon).
- Along the way, discovered and documented (docs/herdr-backend.md) that 80 is unreliable when called from within a script launched into a herdr pane (reports a stale default width instead of the pane's real width) - worked around in the test's own composer-drawing script with a hardcoded conservative width; this is a test-harness-only finding, not a change to the herdr adapter itself.
- Also added an FM_SUPERVISOR_BACKEND=tmux pin to the existing tests/fm-afk-inject-e2e.test.sh's daemon-subprocess launch, because that e2e spawns the real daemon process and, without an explicit pin, would inherit whatever HERDR_ENV the invoking shell happens to carry (e.g. running this validation itself from inside a herdr pane) and misdetect backend=herdr against what is actually a tmux pane on a private socket - this is a necessary correctness fix given the new auto-detection behavior, not incidental to the task.
- Documentation: docs/herdr-backend.md gets a new 'Away-mode daemon: herdr supervisor-pane support' section; .agents/skills/afk/SKILL.md's tmux-specific mechanics (busy-guard/composer-guard, submit model, auto-discovered supervisor pane) are updated to describe both backends. AGENTS.md's own afk stub was deliberately NOT touched - its inline facts (marker contract, watcher ownership, approval semantics) are backend-independent and did not change.
- Out of scope, left alone: multi-harness (codex/opencode/pi) pane-mechanics verification, the primary turn-end guard, and any watcher-policy change.

Full local test suite (tests/*.test.sh) and shellcheck both pass clean.

## What Changed

- Captain, made `fm-supervise-daemon.sh` backend-aware so away-mode injection can discover tmux or Herdr supervisor targets, refuse unsupported supervisor backends, and route target, busy, composer, and submit checks through backend primitives.
- Fixed Herdr backend helpers used by daemon startup and session liveness by adding generic composer-state dispatch and using session-scoped Herdr target existence checks.
- Updated AFK/Herdr documentation and added tmux/Herdr daemon coverage for startup, pending input deferral, swallowed-submit retry, and wedged max-defer behavior.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: Captain, the review found no material defects, but the change touches the daemon's live injection transport and backend discovery path, so residual integration risk is moderate.

## Testing

Captain, the already-successful baseline was accounted for; I reran focused daemon, herdr backend, tmux E2E, and real-herdr E2E coverage, then performed a preserved manual real-herdr run showing pending-input deferral, sentinel-prefixed injection after idle, max-defer wedge alarm with buffer preservation, and loud unsupported-backend refusal. No tests failed, no source files were modified, and no UI surface changed, so no screenshot was applicable.

title: fix(bin): tmux next-free window index, symlink-safe spawn wait, crew-state lookup retries
body:
## What Changed

- `bin/backends/tmux.sh` now creates task windows with the `$ses:` (trailing colon) target, the documented "next free window index" form, instead of a bare session target that could resolve to the current window and fail with "index in use" under `renumber-windows on`; this replaces the previous external PATH shim.
- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` canonicalizes both sides (`pwd -P`) when waiting for the pane's cwd to move from the project to the treehouse worktree, so a symlinked project path (e.g. macOS `/tmp` -> `/private/tmp`) no longer reads as "already moved" and trips the worktree-isolation check.
- `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` retries the no-mistakes run lookup (configurable `FM_CREW_STATE_RETRIES` / `FM_CREW_STATE_RETRY_DELAY` knobs) when a busy CLI returns an empty `axi status` answer or a timed-out coarse `runs` listing, instead of surfacing a false `stale`; answered-but-no-matching-run responses remain authoritative and are not retried. New tests cover the tmux target, the symlinked spawn path, and the retry paths, and the pipeline's review round hardened the timed-out-coarse-lookup case.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Well-bounded shell fixes with dedicated regression tests for each; the prior round's retry-gate finding was fixed exactly per the given instructions (NM_RUNS_RESPONDED timeout signature, authoritative no-run fast path preserved) and no new issues surfaced on a full re-pass.

It is bounded, documented, and configurable (and replaces an equivalent production shim), so no action needed; just noting the tradeoff.

title: fix(spawn): isolate docker-compose project names per worktree
body:
## Intent

Firstmate's own bin/fm-spawn.sh and bin/fm-brief.sh needed a fix for a near-miss: two treehouse worktrees of the same project (e.g. two wealthsync worktrees) run docker compose from directories that share the same leaf basename, so Compose's default project-naming (derived from cwd basename) collides across worktrees on container/volume/network names. One crewmate this session briefly touched another worktree's Docker volume before catching it, and another had resorted to an ad-hoc non-standard host port (5439) for the same underlying reason. Confirmed via grep that no project's docker-compose.yml sets an explicit top-level name: or COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, so an externally-supplied project name is viable.

Fix: fm-spawn.sh derives a stable, Docker-Compose-safe project name from a ship/scout worktree's own pool-slot path once $WT is resolved (e.g. .../wealthsync-323ec0/2/wealthsync -> wealthsync-323ec0-2), writes it to <worktree>/.treehouse-compose-project, excludes that marker from git via .git/info/exclude (reusing the same exclude_path helper already used for the grok turn-end pointer file), and records compose_project=<name> in state/<id>.meta. Stable per pool slot (not per task id) so a stale docker compose stack left by a prior task in that slot is superseded rather than orphaned under a new name. Secondmates are excluded since they run in their own firstmate home, not a per-task pool worktree.

fm-brief.sh tells ship/scout crewmates, next to the existing worktree-isolation-check step, to read .treehouse-compose-project and pass it explicitly on every docker compose invocation (env vars don't reliably persist across separate tool-call invocations in this harness, so restate per command), and to avoid fixed host ports as a second collision vector.

This is purely additive - non-docker tasks see zero behavior change. My own review/test/document/lint pass already completed clean in a prior run on this same commit (7eef86e): the test step auto-fixed 3 pre-existing, unrelated issues the full suite surfaced on this box's older git (2.34.1) - fm-teardown.sh's content_in_default() no longer requires git>=2.38's merge-tree --write-tree, a cmux.sh error-propagation bug in fm_backend_cmux_surface_exists, and two flaky-test fixes (a herdr fake-CLI race, and a test that assumed no real 'node' binary was on PATH) - and the document step added a 'Docker Compose project isolation' section to docs/configuration.md plus matching AGENTS.md/docs/architecture.md/docs/scripts.md/docs/orca-backend.md updates. I reviewed all of that and it's correct. That prior run's only failure was the push step: the authenticated GitHub account only had read access to kunchenguid/firstmate. The captain has now decided to fork kunchenguid/firstmate under that account and push there instead, opening the PR fork->upstream; I forked it and re-ran no-mistakes init --fork-url to register the fork as the push target while origin stays kunchenguid/firstmate for the PR. Re-running now purely to get past that push step; no code has changed since the last clean pass.

## What Changed

- `fm-spawn.sh` derives a stable, Docker-Compose-safe project name from a ship/scout worktree's own pool-slot path, writes it to `<worktree>/.treehouse-compose-project` (git-excluded via `.git/info/exclude`), and records `compose_project=<name>` in `state/<id>.meta`; secondmate spawns are excluded since they run in their own firstmate home rather than a per-task pool worktree. `fm-brief.sh` tells ship/scout crewmates to read that marker and pass the project name explicitly on every `docker compose` invocation, and to avoid fixed host ports.
- `fm-teardown.sh`'s `content_in_default()` is rewritten to check per-path diffs against the merge-base instead of `git merge-tree --write-tree`, so the landed-work check works on git older than 2.38; `bin/backends/cmux.sh` fixes `fm_backend_cmux_surface_exists` to propagate a failed `list-panes` call instead of letting `jq -e` silently treat empty stdin as "not found".
- Adds `tests/fm-spawn-compose-isolation.test.sh`, extends the herdr backend and secondmate lifecycle e2e tests, fixes a race in the herdr fake-CLI counter, and documents per-worktree Docker Compose project isolation in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, and `docs/orca-backend.md`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The core feature (per-worktree Docker Compose project naming) is additive, gated off for secondmates, only writes into an already-validated isolated worktree, and is documented consistently everywhere; the bundled fm-teardown.sh content_in_default() rewrite (dropping the git>=2.38 merge-tree dependency) is a careful, behavior-preserving rewrite that traces correctly through squash-merge, fast-forward, and conflicting-change cases and matches existing test coverage (a dedicated positive fallback test plus several negative refuse tests); the cmux.sh fix corrects a genuine pre-existing bug (empty jq input silently reporting success) rather than introducing new risk.

## Testing

`The baseline full-suite run had already passed on the target commit, but no test anywhere exercised the actual new behavior (docker-compose project-name isolation per worktree), so I wrote a new end-to-end test that drives the real fm-spawn.sh and proves two same-project worktrees at different treehouse pool slots get distinct, stable compose_project names and a git-excluded marker file, verified it fails without the fix and passes with it, added two assertions to an existing secondmate e2e test confirming secondmates never get the marker, verified the three other unrelated auto-fixed issues (git<2.38 teardown compat, a cmux error-propagation bug, two flaky-test fixes) already have adequate pre-existing regression coverage that is genuinely exercised on this box, and reran the entire tests/*.test.sh suite (real tmux) to a clean 0-failure completion.`

title: feat: add campaign task dispatch
body:
## Intent

Add campaign task support to firstmate: a third dispatch shape alongside ship and scout for one long-lived crewmate driving a committed roadmap/spec. Include --campaign brief scaffolding, kind=campaign spawn metadata, ship-like teardown protection, campaign-aware validation state, docs, and tests without changing existing ship/scout behavior. Campaign crewmates must never merge: PR-based campaigns stop at PR ready/checks green so firstmate can merge through bin/fm-pr-merge.sh, including yolo repos; local-only campaigns are supported and use the fixed fm/<id> task branch, stopping at ready in branch for firstmate's local merge path. Existing no-mistakes review/test fixes through 3c92fe1 are intentional and should be validated; the prior run reached document before a captain-approved daemon restart cancelled it, then a retry hit a Claude session limit.

## What Changed

- Introduces `campaign` as a third dispatch shape alongside `ship` and `scout`: `bin/fm-brief.sh --campaign` scaffolds a long-lived roadmap-driven crewmate brief, and `bin/fm-spawn.sh --campaign` records `kind=campaign` metadata, including model/effort/harness dispatch-profile support consistent with ship/scout launches.
- Gives campaigns ship-like teardown protection in `bin/fm-teardown.sh`: every `fm/<id>`-prefixed local branch (the fixed branch for local-only projects, per-batch branches for PR-based projects) must be verified as landed and is pruned at teardown, with each campaign batch branch checked against its own PR rather than the task's last-recorded PR.
- Makes campaign crewmates never merge on their own: PR-based campaigns stop at PR-ready/checks-green for firstmate to merge via `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` (including yolo repos), and local-only campaigns stop at "ready in branch" on the fixed `fm/<id>` branch for firstmate's local merge path; `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` and `bin/fm-send.sh` gain campaign-aware state handling.
- Updates `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `docs/` (architecture, configuration, scripts, herdr/orca/zellij backends, turnend-guard) to document the campaign lifecycle end to end, alongside `harness-adapters` and `secondmate-provisioning` skill updates.
- Adds/updates tests covering campaign brief scaffolding, spawn dispatch profiles, teardown branch protection, and crew-state handling, and fixes a treehouse worktree-discovery race plus test env isolation (hermetic `FM_HOME` in the turnend-guard test, isolated gotmp env) uncovered while validating this branch.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The campaign feature is additive (new --campaign kind alongside ship/scout), the multi-branch teardown protection and per-branch PR verification logic is subtle but thoroughly covered by new targeted tests (unpushed refusal, unlanded batch branch refusal even with HEAD parked elsewhere, all-batches-landed pruning, per-branch PR lookup, local-only detached-HEAD refusal), and existing ship/scout/secondmate code paths are left behavior-unchanged (kind defaults and gating conditions were extended, not altered). No security, data-loss, or breaking-change risks found.

## Testing

The configured baseline test command passed, and I independently reran the full 44-file suite (0 failures) plus the four campaign-specific suites in isolation; I additionally exercised bin/fm-brief.sh --campaign directly to produce a real generated brief showing the roadmap contract, fm/<id>/<batch> branch naming, "never merge" rule, and mode-specific stop conditions (PR ready/checks green vs. ready in branch) — end-to-end evidence that campaign scaffolding, spawn metadata, and teardown protection work as intended without regressing ship/scout behavior. Working tree is clean; no stray artifacts left behind.

You work in ONE persistent worktree for the whole roadmap. Do not ask for teardown, respawn, or a fresh worktree between slices or batch PRs.
Teardown happens only after the roadmap is closed and firstmate confirms the final campaign work has landed.

The execution artifact is already finished before you start: either a committed roadmap at `docs/plans/<feature>.md` with `- [ ]` slices and optional `[gate]` / `[risk:high]` markers, or a single upstream-produced spec.
Planning is out of scope. If the artifact is missing, unfinished, or asks you to plan the feature, append `blocked: missing finished campaign artifact` to the status file and stop.

Project delivery mode: ``
Project yolo flag: ``

# Setup
You are in a persistent, isolated git worktree of demo-repo, at a detached HEAD on a clean default-branch commit. It stays yours for the whole roadmap; firstmate tears it down only after the campaign closes.

**Verify isolation before anything else.** Run `pwd -P` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; both must resolve to the isolated task worktree you were launched in, such as a treehouse pool path or an Orca-managed worktree, not the primary checkout firstmate operates from.
The path check is authoritative: `git rev-parse --git-dir` and `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` can help inspect the repo, but they do not prove you are outside the primary checkout.
If the top-level path is the primary checkout or not the worktree you were launched in, STOP - do not branch or commit here - append `blocked: launched in primary checkout, not an isolated worktree` to the status file and stop.

1. Record the launch commit: `git rev-parse HEAD`. Treat this commit as the roadmap base.
2. Do not attempt to check out the default branch. The pooled clone holds it, so this worktree starts detached by design. Create the first slice or batch branch directly from the launch commit with `git switch -c fm/demo-campaign-x1/<batch-slug>`; when the execution skill preflight expects a named default branch, the current detached base commit stands in for it. Name EVERY campaign branch under the `fm/demo-campaign-x1/` prefix - firstmate's teardown protection and ref cleanup track that prefix, and a branch outside it can strand work.

# Execution loop
Drive the captain-provided execution skill in roadmap mode. Invoke `/autopilot`; if the harness needs plain language instead, ask it to run the captain-provided execution skill against the committed roadmap/spec in roadmap mode.

This campaign contract overrides any normal landing behavior inside the execution skill. The execution skill may help open or update the batch PR, but if it would run `land-pr`, call `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh`, call `gh-axi pr merge`, merge directly, or treat `yolo=` as permission for you to merge, do not do that step. Stop before landing at `done: PR {url} checks green` so firstmate can run `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` after the captain's word or firstmate's yolo decision.

Use this loop:
1. Pick the next unchecked slice from the roadmap/spec.
2. Implement only that slice.
3. Verify the slice.
4. Review the slice.
5. Commit it with a message containing `[S<N>]`, where `<N>` is the slice number.
6. Open or update the batch PR when the batch is ready.
7. Run roadmap-tick after the batch PR state changes as required by the execution artifact.
8. After firstmate reports a batch PR merged, start the next batch branch from the updated default branch, not the launch commit: `git fetch origin` then `git switch -c fm/demo-campaign-x1/<next-batch-slug> origin/<default-branch>`, so each batch PR contains only its own batch's diff.

For `no-mistakes` projects, keep the execution skill's normal inner verify/review loop per slice, then run the no-mistakes pipeline as the final batch-PR gate before reporting the PR ready. The no-mistakes evidence trail is part of the fleet contract.

# Escalation mapping
Every stop raised by the execution skill maps to the status file:

- `[gate]` slice: append `needs-decision: [gate] <exact stop reason + options>`, then wait.
- `[risk:high]` slice: append `needs-decision: [risk:high] <exact stop reason + options>`, then wait.
- Off-spec or off-blueprint UI stop: append `needs-decision: off-spec UI <exact stop reason + options>`, then wait.
- Structured clarification question: append `needs-decision: clarification <exact question + options>`, then wait.
- Visual approval: append `needs-decision: visual approval <artifact/link + options>`, then wait.

Never push past a stop. Firstmate relays the decision to the captain and replies with the answer.

# Rules
1. Never push to the default branch. Never merge a PR.
2. Stay inside this worktree; modify nothing outside it.
3. Use gh-axi for GitHub operations and chrome-devtools-axi for browser operations.
4. Report status by appending one line:
   `echo "{state}: {one short line}" >> '/var/folders/l1/t2yfcls14bs7vfn5yjyc66wr0000gn/T/tmp.qWtOsCbsYN/state/demo-campaign-x1.status'`
   States: working, needs-decision, blocked, done, failed.
   Each append wakes firstmate, so report sparingly: setup complete, each stop that needs a decision, batch ready, roadmap close, blocked, or failed.
5. If you hit the same obstacle twice, append `blocked: {why}` and stop; firstmate will help.
6. If a decision belongs to a human, append `needs-decision: {exact stop reason + options}` and stop. Firstmate will reply with the decision.

# Merge authority
Stop at "PR ready, checks green" for each batch PR and append `done: PR {url} checks green`. Wait for firstmate to relay the captain's merge word or, when `yolo=` is `on`, firstmate's yolo merge decision and continuation instruction. Firstmate performs every PR merge through `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` so task metadata records the landed PR. Never merge a red PR.

If `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` already exists, or if this campaign produced durable project-intrinsic knowledge, run `/var/folders/l1/t2yfcls14bs7vfn5yjyc66wr0000gn/T/tmp.qWtOsCbsYN/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh .` in the worktree.
If this campaign produced durable project-intrinsic knowledge, record it in `AGENTS.md` as part of your change.

The campaign is complete only when the roadmap/spec is fully closed, every batch has passed its required gates, and the final work has landed or is waiting at the mode-specific merge stop above.

title: fix: dedup herdr stale wakes for settled panes
body:
## Intent Fix the herdr-backend watcher stale-echo churn: idle and done crews' herdr panes re-wake the supervisor every few minutes because bin/fm-watch.sh hashes a volatile bounded pane capture and claude's idle UI repaints timer-driven rows (the recap line toggling, rotating tips, the animated 'for Xm Ys' summary, transient slash-completion menus), so each repaint mints a fresh stable hash. Decision: dedup the stale signal on the native SEMANTIC agent state (herdr idle/done/blocked map to a constant 'agentstate:idle') instead of the pane content, because content line-stripping cannot converge - those volatile rows also shift a variable-length prefix through the tail-N hash window (measured). Constraints held: the tmux path stays byte-identical (busy state is always unknown there, so it keeps the pane-content hash); the resolved backend busy state is shared between this new stale signal and the existing busy-suppression check so herdr's agent.get is read once per pane per poll, not twice; the now-unused window_is_busy wrapper is removed in favor of the extracted busy_state_is_busy. Verified live against real herdr 0.7.1 on 2026-07-05 (a done pane churned 4 distinct hashes and an idle pane 8 over ~7 minutes, both collapsing to 1 under the semantic signal; a plain post-exit shell pane stayed at 1 and is intentionally left on the pane-hash fallback). The related herdr away-mode injection wedge is already fixed upstream by PR #251, so this change is deliberately scoped to only the watcher stale-echo churn #251 did not touch. Adds a colocated behavioral test in tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh and a backend-verification section in docs/herdr-backend.md. ## What Changed - Captain, `bin/fm-watch.sh` now deduplicates settled herdr stale panes using the semantic agent state instead of volatile pane hashes, while keeping tmux and busy-looking herdr panes on the existing content-hash path. - Resets stale suppression when the signal changes and reuses the resolved backend busy state for both stale signaling and busy suppression. - Adds herdr stale-dedup regression coverage, stabilizes the session-start missing-tool fixture, and documents the live herdr verification notes. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the change is narrow, the semantic herdr stale signal matches the documented backend contract, and the added tests cover the prior regressions without introducing a material merge risk. ## Testing The configured full baseline had already passed; I reran the targeted watcher triage and session-start regression suites, then exercised a fake herdr idle pane through the real watcher and drain path, confirming semantic stale dedup wakes once, stores `agentstate:idle`, and does not re-wake after volatile pane repaint.
Evidence: fm-watch-triage transcript ```text ok - signal_reason_is_actionable: benign absorbed, captain verbs and coalesced batches surfaced ok - stale_is_terminal: terminal status surfaces, non-terminal and no-status are benign ok - scan_captain_relevant_statuses lists only captain-relevant statuses ok - classifier primitives: last line, captain-relevance, window->task, FM_CAPTAIN_RE override ok - crew_is_provably_working: only working+run-step/pane is provable; idle/finished/parked/failed/unknown surface ok - signal_crew_provably_working: benign only when every referenced crew is provably working ok - a no-verb signal whose crew is provably working is absorbed (no exit, no queue, suppressor advanced, beacon present) ok - a bare turn-end whose crew is provably working (busy pane) is absorbed ok - a bare turn-end whose crew is not provably working is surfaced (the swallowed-finish fix) ok - a no-verb working: note whose crew is idle with no running pipeline is surfaced ok - captain-relevant signal is surfaced (queue + exit) and marked surfaced ok - a stale pane sitting on a terminal status is surfaced (queue + exit) ok - herdr settled pane: stale-dedup signal is the semantic agent state, not the volatile pane hash ok - herdr idle pane: busy banner keeps stale signal on pane-content hash ok - herdr settled pane: stale suppressor resets after intervening work ok - a stale terminal-looking status is overridden and absorbed while a run is actively working, then wedge-escalated ok - provably-working non-terminal stale is absorbed on first sight, then wedge-escalated past the threshold ok - a not-provably-working non-terminal stale is surfaced immediately (never left to wait out the timer) ok - matching non-terminal stale suppressors repair missing or corrupt stale-since timers ok - triage log capping handles wc byte counts with leading spaces ok - a heartbeat with no captain-relevant change is absorbed and backs off the cadence ok - heartbeat backstop fail-safe surfaces a captain-relevant status the per-wake path missed ok - the liveness beacon stays fresh while the watcher absorbs benign wakes (fm-guard never false-alarms) ok - with .afk present the watcher reverts to one-shot so the daemon owns triage (no double-triage) ```
Evidence: fm-session-start transcript ```text ok - context digest distinguishes ABSENT, empty-but-present, and populated files ok - a lock refusal prints a loud read-only banner, skips every mutating step, and still completes the digest ok - digest sections are ordered diagnostics-first, bulk-context-last ok - status tail is bounded to the configured line count, with the full log path always printed ok - orphan status logs are printed once with bounded tails ok - tmux endpoint liveness is reported per task: alive for a live window, dead for a gone one ok - herdr endpoint liveness is reported per task: alive for a live pane, dead for a gone one ok - fm-session-start.sh composes the real fm-lock.sh, fm-bootstrap.sh, and fm-wake-drain.sh output verbatim ok - an empty fleet reports (none) for in-flight tasks and an absent AFK flag ok - next step sources the X-mode cadence before arming the watcher ok - next step delegates watcher ownership to the AFK daemon ```
Evidence: Manual fake-herdr semantic stale evidence Shows first watcher poll emitted `stale: default:w1:p2`, recorded `hash=agentstate:idle`, drained one stale wake, then stayed running with empty stdout and empty wake queue after volatile pane repaint. ```text ## Manual fake-herdr stale-dedup evidence Scenario: a settled herdr pane reports native idle while its visible pane text repaints. # first watcher poll: pre-seeded semantic signal reaches n>=2 and wakes once stale: default:w1:p2 hash=agentstate:idle stale_suppressor=agentstate:idle # drained durable wake drain: 1783243072 1 stale default:w1:p2 stale: default:w1:p2 # repaint pane text but keep native agent state idle; watcher should stay quiet second_poll=still-running-no-duplicate-wake second_stdout= wake_queue_after_repaint= # herdr command calls observed status --json --session default pane read w1:p2 --source recent --lines 200 --session default status --json --session default agent get w1:p2 --session default status --json --session default pane read w1:p2 --source recent --lines 200 --session default status --json --session default agent get w1:p2 --session default status --json --session default pane read w1:p2 --source recent --lines 200 --session default status --json --session default agent get w1:p2 --session default status --json --session default pane read w1:p2 --source recent --lines 200 --session default status --json --session default agent get w1:p2 --session default ```
- Outcome: 🔧 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ across 2 runs (19m19s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:195` - Using one constant stale key for every settled herdr period means `.stale-$key` remains `agentstate:idle` after the first surfaced stale pane. If the same pane later does more work and returns to idle/done without a status/turn-ended signal, the stale path treats it as already surfaced and can suppress or delay the new completion wake. Clear the stale suppressor when the signal leaves settled-idle, or include a transition/generation component in the semantic key. 🔧 Fix: Captain, reset stale suppressor on signal change 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:195` - Captain, `idle` is not always a settled herdr pane: the existing docs note that long foreground tool calls can report `agent_status=idle` while the pane still shows the busy banner. Collapsing every `idle` verdict to `agentstate:idle` means changing tool output no longer resets the stale generation; in afk mode it can queue a stale wake after two polls, and in normal mode it can keep or suppress the stale marker across real intervening work. Corroborate `idle` with the pane busy regex before using the semantic settled signal, or keep the pane-content hash while the idle pane still looks busy. 🔧 Fix: Captain, corroborate idle stale signal ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
🔧 **Test** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 tests failed with exit code 1 - `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` 🔧 Fix: Captain, stabilize session-start missing-tool fixture ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain. - `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` - Baseline already ran successfully before this validation: `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` - `bash tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh | tee /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KWRQ2K32MZPGK20MYN5K2X1D/fm-watch-triage.out` - `bash tests/fm-session-start.test.sh | tee /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KWRQ2K32MZPGK20MYN5K2X1D/fm-session-start.out` - Manual fake-herdr watcher/drain scenario saved with `tee /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KWRQ2K32MZPGK20MYN5K2X1D/herdr-semantic-stale-manual.out`

title: fix brief no-mistakes pooled setup
body:
## Summary
- remove the standard ship-brief setup instruction that told crewmates to run `no-mistakes doctor` and possibly `no-mistakes init` inside pooled worktrees
- replace it with a read-only `command -v no-mistakes` availability check and an explicit prohibition on `doctor`/`init` in pooled worktrees
- document the recurring gate symptom and mitigation in `CONTRIBUTING.md`

## Root Cause
Firstmate's generated no-mistakes ship brief was our-side trigger: it instructed each crewmate to run `no-mistakes doctor`, then `no-mistakes init` if the repo looked uninitialized from inside the disposable pooled worktree. Those commands can rewrite/reinitialize the shared no-mistakes hook and gate state for the repo, which re-breaks the fleet's shared hook patch and leads to first-run failures such as `no previous run for branch <branch>`.

The underlying first-run-on-pooled-worktree behavior is in the closed no-mistakes v1.31.2 binary, so this PR does not try to patch it. The mitigation here is to keep no-mistakes initialization at the shared repo level and prevent crewmates from re-running init/doctor in task worktrees.

## Validation
- generated a pre-patch sample ship brief and confirmed Setup emitted `no-mistakes doctor` / `no-mistakes init`
- generated a post-patch sample ship brief and confirmed Setup emits only the read-only CLI check plus the pooled-worktree prohibition
- `bash -n bin/fm-brief.sh`
- `tests/fm-brief.test.sh`
- `for script in bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh; do bash -n "$script" || exit 1; done`
- `git diff --check`

Not run: `shellcheck bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh tests/*.sh` because `shellcheck` is not installed in this worktree environment. Per task instruction, I did not run `no-mistakes init`, `no-mistakes doctor`, or any `no-mistakes axi ...` command.

title: feat(spawn): name claude crewmate sessions fm-<id> for agent-view readability
body:
## What

Name fm-spawned claude crewmate sessions `fm-<id>` so they are readable in Claude Code's agent view (`claude agents`), instead of all sharing one auto-generated name.

- `bin/fm-spawn.sh`: the claude launch template gains `-n __TASKID__`, wired through a new `__TASKID__` placeholder substituted next to `__BRIEF__`/`__TURNEND__`. The value is `fm-<task-id>`, matching the tmux window name, so agent view and tmux agree on identity. Claude template only; codex/opencode/pi/grok are untouched.
- The template also prefixes `CLAUDE_JOB_DIR=`: verified empirically (claude 2.1.201) that when firstmate's tmux server was started from inside a `claude --bg` job, that job's `CLAUDE_JOB_DIR` leaks into every pane via the tmux server environment and the nested claude silently adopts the parent job's name, defeating `-n`. Bisected to that single variable; an empty value behaves as unset. This is why every session previously showed the same leaked name.
- `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md`: two lines in the claude section documenting the naming and the leak.

## Verification

- `-n` + `CLAUDE_JOB_DIR=` produces a session named `fm-<id>` in `claude agents --json` and the prompt box (verified live in a scratch tmux pane, cleaned up after).
- Busy-pane spinner rendering is identical with and without `-n` (sampled 10x each during live tool runs). The `esc to interrupt` hint not rendering on 2.1.201 is pre-existing version drift, present in the baseline too.
- `fm_tmux_composer_state` reads an idle `-n`-labeled pane as `empty` (the name renders on the border row, not the cursor row).
- zellij/cmux tab naming is unaffected: both match titles they set themselves at creation, never the live terminal title.

## Tests

Five assertion sites pinning the exact claude launch string updated to the new form. The old-vs-new spawn conformance test in `tests/fm-backend.test.sh` rewrites the baseline log's launch line to the new form before diffing - a targeted tolerance for this one intentional delta (a no-op once merged, since the merge-base then contains the new template) that keeps the diff sensitive to unintended drift. All 19 fm-spawn-touching test files pass locally; the full suite passed in the no-mistakes pipeline (review, test, document, lint all green).

title: fix: canonicalize spawn worktree path checks
body:
## Intent Fix bin/fm-spawn.sh's worktree-isolation guard false-refusal bug for projects reached through a symlinked path prefix (e.g. macOS's /tmp -> /private/tmp), per backlog item fm-spawn-symlink-guard-s8. The guard's worktree-discovery poll compared a LOGICAL PROJ_ABS (plain cd && pwd, symlinks preserved) against every backend's PHYSICALLY-resolved pane-cwd read (tmux's pane_current_path, herdr's foreground_cwd, etc.), so when the project itself sat under a symlinked directory, the very first poll already saw two different strings for the identical starting directory and the guard mistook an unmoved pane for one that had already left the project - handing validate_spawn_worktree the project's own directory as 'the worktree' and tripping a false isolation refusal before treehouse ever moved the pane. This was previously discovered and documented (but left unfixed) in docs/herdr-backend.md's Known gaps section, from building the fm-backend-autodetect-a4 smoke test, which had to work around it by pre-resolving its own scratch TMP_ROOT via pwd -P. Fix: canonicalize PROJ_ABS into a new PROJ_ABS_REAL (cd "$PROJ_ABS" && pwd -P) once, immediately after PROJ_ABS is resolved in bin/fm-spawn.sh, and compare against that physical form in both the worktree-discovery poll loop and validate_spawn_worktree's own primary-vs-worktree comparison (which now reuses PROJ_ABS_REAL instead of recomputing it) instead of the still-symlinked PROJ_ABS. This removes both failure directions: a symlinked prefix can no longer false-refuse an isolated spawn, and a genuinely tangled spawn (worktree resolving to the same physical directory as the project) still correctly refuses, since PROJ_ABS_REAL is always the OS-level resolved form regardless of how the caller's path was spelled. I audited every other caller/comparison for the same class of bug: the secondmate-home path (validate_firstmate_home_for_spawn/resolved_existing_dir) already canonicalizes via pwd -P, and bin/fm-teardown.sh's removal-target and worktree-registration comparisons already canonicalize via pwd -P consistently, so only the one PROJ_ABS comparison needed the fix. Added a new regression test, tests/fm-backend.test.sh:test_spawn_symlinked_project_prefix_avoids_false_refusal, which builds a synthetic symlinked-prefix project (a real directory plus a symlink pointing at it, project passed through the symlinked path) and a fake tmux backend whose pane_current_path stub returns the project's true pwd -P-resolved physical path on the FIRST poll (reproducing the unmoved-but-physically-differing read) and the real worktree path from the second poll onward (reproducing treehouse actually moving the pane). I verified this test reproduces the exact original bug against the pre-fix script (git-stash the bin/fm-spawn.sh change and rerun: it fails with the exact same 'did not yield an isolated worktree' error the bug report describes) and passes cleanly against the fix. Updated docs/herdr-backend.md's Known gaps entry from an open gap to RESOLVED, with the date, tool versions (GNU bash 5.3.9(1)-release, git 2.53.0, macOS Darwin 25.5.0), the exact verification method, and the confirmed pre-fix/post-fix test behavior, per this repo's backend-verification-doc evidence convention (docs record empirical facts with exact commands/output, not just narrative). Scope is strictly limited to these three files: bin/fm-spawn.sh (the fix), tests/fm-backend.test.sh (the new regression test), and docs/herdr-backend.md (the Known gaps update) - no other behavior was touched. Before committing I ran shellcheck bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh tests/*.sh clean, and directly ran (not just relied on file greps) every test file that actually invokes bin/fm-spawn.sh - fm-backend.test.sh, fm-backend-autodetect-smoke, fm-backend-cmux(-smoke), fm-backend-herdr(.smoke/-respawn-idem-e2e/-workspace-per-home-e2e), fm-backend-orca, fm-backend-tmux-smoke, fm-backend-zellij(-smoke), fm-gotmp, fm-secondmate-sync/-lifecycle-e2e/-harness/-safety, fm-grok-harness, fm-spawn-batch, fm-spawn-dispatch-profile, fm-tangle-guard (which directly exercises 'fm-spawn: aborts unless the resolved worktree is a genuine, isolated worktree'), and fm-turnend-guard - plus fm-teardown.test.sh for its own worktree-path comparisons - and all passed with zero failures. ## What Changed - Canonicalizes `fm-spawn` project and backend cwd comparisons to physical paths so symlinked project prefixes no longer trigger false worktree-isolation refusals. - Keeps genuinely tangled spawns rejected by validating the resolved worktree path against the canonical project checkout path. - Adds regression coverage for symlinked-prefix spawn discovery and refreshes backend docs to mark the previously documented herdr gap as resolved. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the change is narrowly scoped to canonicalizing spawn path comparisons and adds a targeted regression test without touching broader spawn behavior. ## Testing The configured full-suite baseline had already passed; I then ran the focused backend regression, captured a CLI-level `fm-spawn.sh` symlinked-prefix transcript showing success after a physical first cwd poll, ran the tangle-guard safety test, and confirmed the working tree remained clean.

title: fix(teardown): recover provably stale git index locks
body:
## Intent Fix bin/fm-teardown.sh's stale git index.lock failure (backlog item teardown-lock-race-l2). A crew process killed mid-git-operation can leave a stale .git/worktrees//index.lock behind, which makes treehouse return --force fail closed and aborts teardown. Two real occurrences were logged on 2026-07-04. Implemented a new teardown_treehouse_return wrapper around every treehouse return --force call site (main worktree return, secondmate home removal, and the child-worktree removal fallback): on failure it waits FM_STALE_WORKTREE_LOCK_RETRY_WAIT_SECS (default 2s) and retries once, since the owning process may simply be exiting mid-shutdown. If the lock is still present after that retry, it is removed and the return retried exactly one more time, but ONLY when the lock is provably stale by a documented three-part proof: (1) it still exists after the retry wait, (2) its mtime age is at least FM_STALE_WORKTREE_LOCK_AGE_SECS (default 30s, since a freshly created lock might belong to a process lsof has not yet reflected), and (3) lsof reports no live process holding the lock file open AND no process has the worktree directory itself open as cwd or an fd (a live git process keeps its own lock file open for the operation's full duration, so an empty lsof result means the file was abandoned by a now-exited process). A missing lsof, or failing any one of the three checks, is deliberately treated as NOT provably stale (fail safe): the lock is left untouched and the original failure surfaces exactly as before this fix - we intentionally never remove a lock that could belong to a live process. Every wait, retry, and removal is echoed to teardown's stderr output so the outcome is visible. Documented the exact staleness proof in the script's own header comment per this repo's coding-guidelines skill (mechanics belong in the script header, not AGENTS.md). Added two new tests to tests/fm-teardown.test.sh: one where the lock is provably stale (old mtime, fakebin/lsof mocked to report no holder) and teardown succeeds after clearing it, and one where the lock has a live holder (fakebin/lsof mocked to report a holder) even with an old mtime, where teardown must refuse and the lock file must be left untouched - proving age alone is never sufficient. Also fixed tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh's minimal fake-FM_ROOT fixture, which symlinks specific real bin/ scripts into an isolated directory: it needed a new fm-wake-lib.sh symlink added (in two places) because fm-teardown.sh now sources that library for the fm_path_age helper reused for the lock-staleness age check, reusing existing shared infrastructure rather than duplicating a stat/mtime helper. Updated CONTRIBUTING.md's one-line description of tests/fm-teardown.test.sh and added the two new FM_STALE_WORKTREE_LOCK_AGE_SECS / FM_STALE_WORKTREE_LOCK_RETRY_WAIT_SECS environment-variable knobs to docs/configuration.md's reference list, matching the documentation conventions already used for every other FM_* runtime-tuning knob in that file. All changes are scoped to bin/fm-teardown.sh, its two test files, and these two doc/config-reference files - no other behavior was touched. shellcheck (bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh tests/*.sh) is clean, and I ran fm-teardown.test.sh, fm-gotmp.test.sh, fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh, fm-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh, fm-pr-merge.test.sh, fm-backend.test.sh, fm-backend-orca.test.sh, fm-backend-zellij.test.sh, fm-backend-herdr-workspace-per-home-e2e.test.sh, fm-backend-autodetect-smoke.test.sh, and fm-grok-harness.test.sh directly (every suite that invokes fm-teardown.sh as a subprocess) and all passed with zero failures before committing. ## What Changed - Captain, added stale `index.lock` recovery around forced teardown returns, with one retry, fail-closed staleness proof checks, and visible stderr reporting for waits, retries, removals, and refusals. - Hardened teardown safety paths so unproven or live-held locks preserve worktrees instead of falling through to raw cleanup, and safety checks are re-run after stale-lock cleanup. - Expanded teardown, secondmate safety, and gotmp tests, and documented the stale-lock behavior plus related `FM_STALE_WORKTREE_LOCK_*` tuning knobs. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: Captain, the change is safety-sensitive teardown code with stale-lock deletion and multiple destructive call sites, but I did not find any substantiated merge-blocking or follow-up issues in the final diff. ## Testing Baseline full test command was already green before this run; I then inspected the teardown lock-recovery diff, reran the focused teardown, secondmate safety, and gotmp suites, captured manual CLI evidence for stale-lock success and live-lock refusal, pruned the temporary evidence sandbox, and confirmed the worktree stayed clean.

title: feat(skills): add captain-invocable bearings status-report skill
body:
## Intent Create captain-invocable firstmate skill bearings (.agents/skills/bearings/SKILL.md) that generates a pick-up-where-I-left-off status report from live fleet state; the reusable version of data/status-report-2026-07-06.md. Procedure reads backlog, state/*.meta plus bin/fm-crew-state.sh per task (never a raw status-log tail), open PRs via gh-axi, scout reports, pending decisions and date-gated queued work; composes exemplar sections (TL;DR, Check first, Landed, In flight, Plans, Decisions pending, Date-gated/queued); writes data/status-report-DATE.md plus a concise chat summary, optional Lavish board. Deliberate constraints: create ONLY the skill file; do NOT edit AGENTS.md (captain-invocable skills are auto-discovered by the harness; concurrent crewmates edit AGENTS.md so a pointer would conflict and is not needed); no helper script - the report is agent composition work, not a deterministic script; renamed from morning-brief to bearings per captain. title: fix(bin): make scripts parse and run under macOS system bash 3.2
body:
## What Changed

- Guarded empty-array `"${arr[@]}"` expansions in `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` and `bin/fm-spawn.sh` with the `${arr[@]+...}` pattern, since macOS system bash 3.2 treats an empty array's `[@]` expansion as unbound under `set -u` (fixed upstream in bash 4.4), which broke default squash merges and batch spawns without shared profile flags on a stock Mac.
- Added `tests/fm-bash32-compat.test.sh`, which syntax-checks every `bin/` script under `/bin/bash`, runs a self-tested lexer that catches unmatched quotes inside `$( )` heredoc bodies so the parse-level regression is also caught on Linux CI, and scaffolds `fm-brief.sh` briefs end-to-end for every ship delivery mode plus scout.
- Hardened existing tests along the way (`fm-backend.test.sh` now picks the newest merge-base across candidate default-branch refs instead of a possibly stale local `main`; the tmux smoke test polls for loop output instead of a fixed sleep, which the pipeline's Test step flagged and auto-fixed) and documented the two bash 3.2 sharp edges in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The bin/ changes are comment-only (the empty-array guards already existed at the base commit); everything else is documentation and new or hardened tests with no runtime behavior change, and the new compat test's design is sound with self-tests guarding its own checker.

Use a discriminating substring, e.g. 'instruct you to run /no-mistakes', or additionally assert absence of 'ships **direct-PR**'.

title: feat: add fleet freeze and stale task-state reconciliation
body:
## Intent

Build a safe dry-run-first stale state reconciler for firstmate: report stale tracked records without writes, clean exactly one dead and landed state record only with --clean <id> --yes, refuse live endpoints, unlanded work, and frozen fleets, reuse fleet-map matching and teardown-style landed-work semantics, add focused tests, and keep shellcheck clean. PRs target the fork origin now; the guardrails commit e2e0da7 is present on origin/main and should not be treated as bundled unrelated work.

## What Changed

- Added `bin/fm-freeze.sh` (+ `bin/fm-freeze-lib.sh`) for a manual fleet park/unpark switch; while frozen, `fm-spawn.sh`, `fm-send.sh`, `fm-watch.sh`, `fm-watch-arm.sh`, and the away-mode daemon refuse to spawn, steer, or wake anything.
- Added `bin/fm-fleet-map.sh` (+ `bin/fm-fleet-map-lib.sh`) as a read-only diagnostic that matches tracked `state/*.meta` records against live backend endpoints and flags stale-tracked or operator-untracked agents.
- Added `bin/fm-reconcile-stale.sh` (+ `bin/fm-landed-work-lib.sh`) for stale-tracked-state reconciliation: a dry-run-first report reusing fleet-map matching and teardown-style landed-work semantics (with secondmate/scout carve-outs), and a `--clean <id> --yes` path that re-verifies the endpoint is dead, the work is landed, and the fleet isn't frozen before removing only that task's volatile state files.
- Wired the freeze check into `fm-spawn.sh`, `fm-send.sh`, `fm-watch.sh`, `fm-watch-arm.sh`, and `fm-supervise-daemon.sh`, and surfaced freeze/reconcile state in `fm-session-start.sh`.
- Added test coverage (`fm-freeze.test.sh`, `fm-fleet-map.test.sh`, `fm-reconcile-stale.test.sh`, plus updates to `fm-session-start.test.sh`, `fm-daemon.test.sh`, `fm-watcher-lock.test.sh`, `fm-gotmp.test.sh`, `fm-turnend-guard.test.sh`) and documented both features across `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, `README.md`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Both prior findings (secondmate carve-out, scout carve-out) are correctly fixed in bin/fm-landed-work-lib.sh with matching call-site updates in bin/fm-reconcile-stale.sh, backed by targeted regression tests that reproduce the exact previously-unsafe scenarios; shellcheck is clean and no new issues were introduced.

## Testing

Ran the dedicated fm-reconcile-stale test suite (9/9 pass), covering dry-run reporting with no writes, --clean requiring --yes, refusals for live endpoints, unlanded work, frozen fleet, and secondmate-kind records, plus the scout report carve-out; also ran every other test file touched by this change (fleet-map, freeze, session-start, daemon, watcher-lock, gotmp, turnend-guard) and all passed with no regressions. Tree left clean with no leftover artifacts.

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

<details>
<summary>✅ **intent** - passed</summary>

✅ No issues found.

</details>

<details>
<summary>⚠️ **Rebase** - 1 warning</summary>

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-map.sh` - branch carries 1 commit(s) that exist on your local main branch but were never pushed to origin/main; rebasing would bundle this unrelated work (16 file(s)) into the PR:
- e2e0da7 feat: fleet freeze and fleet-map incident guardrails (#1)

Push main to origin, or rebase your branch onto origin/main, before gating.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 **Review** - 4 issues found → auto-fixed ✅</summary>

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-reconcile-stale.sh:122` - fm-reconcile-stale.sh's --clean path (and the shared fm_landed_assess_worktree it calls) never branches on task kind. It treats a stale-tracked kind=secondmate record exactly like an ordinary ship/scout task: if the recorded backend endpoint looks dead and the secondmate home's git worktree is clean (its normal steady state, since secondmate homes are kept fast-forwarded), the landed assessment reports landed and --clean --yes deletes the primary's state/<id>.meta, .status, .turn-ended, etc. for that secondmate. AGENTS.md section 7 treats secondmate teardown as an explicit, captain/firstmate-gated decision checked against the secondmate's own in-flight work, and fm-teardown.sh hard-codes a secondmate/scout carve-out (skips the ordinary dirty/unpushed safety checks entirely and separately removes the registered home/registry entry). fm-reconcile-stale.sh has no equivalent carve-out, so a transiently-dead endpoint (e.g. right after a host restart, before recovery has run) is enough to silently wipe a persistent secondmate's firstmate-side tracking record with no check of whether it still has in-flight crewmates depending on it.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-landed-work-lib.sh:45` - fm_landed_assess_worktree also ignores kind for scout tasks. A scout worktree is deliberately left dirty/scratch, and fm-teardown.sh explicitly skips its dirty/unpushed checks for kind=scout. The new shared assessor has no such carve-out, so a stale-tracked scout task's normal uncommitted scratch state is reported as unlanded and --clean is refused. This fails closed (over-cautious, not unsafe) but likely makes --clean a no-op for the common scout case, contrary to the header comment's claim that the assessor mirrors fm-teardown.sh.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-landed-work-lib.sh:93` - fm_landed_assess_worktree only reimplements teardown's content-in-default fallback; it omits teardown's other landed path (pr_is_merged / unpushed_patches_are_in_pr_head) which uses gh to confirm a merged PR head contains the local work via patch-id matching, covering the case where no-mistakes pushed fix-round commits directly to the PR so the local branch tree no longer matches origin default exactly after a squash merge. Missing it just makes reconcile-stale over-conservative (refuses --clean on some genuinely-landed tasks) rather than unsafe.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-reconcile-stale.sh:188` - remove_grok_turnend_auth is copy-pasted verbatim from fm-teardown.sh rather than shared, and the tasktmp-removal logic is a second, independently-written implementation (with an extra basename safety check teardown itself lacks). Worth eventually consolidating into a shared lib so the two cleanup tools cannot drift apart further.

title: feat(supervision): add fleet-freeze, fleet-map, and usage-tripwire guardrails
body:
## Intent The developer (Mielye) was recovering from an incident where a prior Fable/Herdr session caused excessive token burn ("token burn") by spawning uncontrolled subagents/workers. They asked the assistant to prepare a handoff prompt for a new Fable chat to take over firstmate fleet recovery, with strict constraints: do not auto-resume the old fleet, do not spawn hidden subagents, do not create raw Herdr workers without explicit approval, keep the firstmate chat orchestration-only, limit current Herdr to only two chats (firstmate and a separate manually-run Nemesis payroll review chat), and treat prior screenshots as weak/unverified context to be reconciled against actual firstmate and Herdr state. The new agent was instructed to first load a checkpoint (fable-incident-guardrails) plus an older referenced checkpoint, read stowed captain/learnings/backlog files, and report back on what happened, current fleet state, guardrails added, and remaining work — explicitly not to code or unfreeze/run any agents until the developer approves the plan. ## What Changed - Add `bin/fm-freeze.sh`/`bin/fm-freeze-lib.sh` to pause fleet spawn/send/watch during an incident, and make `bin/fm-guard.sh`, `bin/fm-spawn.sh`, `bin/fm-send.sh`, `bin/fm-watch.sh`, `bin/fm-watch-arm.sh`, and `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh` freeze-aware so they refuse or pause cleanly instead of crash-looping while frozen - Add `bin/fm-fleet-map.sh` to inventory tracked task/meta state against the live Herdr/tmux surface for diagnosing drift - Add `bin/fm-usage-tripwire.sh`, a read-only token/session usage burst check for arming as a per-task check, with a fix to scope its sums to per-entry timestamps within the sliding window instead of re-summing a whole transcript file's lifetime total - Wire freeze status into `bin/fm-session-start.sh`, document all three guardrails across `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `docs/`, and add regression tests covering freeze, fleet-map, daemon, session-start, watcher-lock, and usage-tripwire behavior ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: All three round-1 findings (tripwire window scoping, freeze-unaware guard banner, daemon crash-loop on freeze) are correctly fixed with sound logic, the tripwire fix has solid new tests verifying the exact scenario reported, and the AGENTS.md additions are minimal one-line pointers as the captain directed - the only gap is missing regression tests for two of the three fixes, which is a low-severity follow-up. ## Testing Captain, the configured suite (all tests/*.test.sh) passed as baseline, and I re-ran the six test files touched by this change plus hand-drove the actual CLI end-to-end: freezing the fleet correctly blocked spawn/send with a clear error and bypass path, the usage tripwire correctly flagged a simulated 341-session-style burst while correctly excluding stale history from a long-lived session's token sum (the exact bug this review commit fixes), and fm-guard.sh now shows a distinct "fleet frozen" banner instead of a false watcher-crash alarm when the fleet is intentionally parked. No issues found. ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Rebase** - 1 warning - ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-map.sh` - branch carries 1 commit(s) that exist on your local main branch but were never pushed to origin/main; rebasing would bundle this unrelated work (16 file(s)) into the PR: - e2e0da7 feat: fleet freeze and fleet-map incident guardrails (#1) Push main to origin, or rebase your branch onto origin/main, before gating.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ⚠️ `bin/fm-usage-tripwire.sh:100` - sum_claude_file/sum_codex_file sum ALL usage entries in a transcript file, not just entries generated within the sliding window. Files are selected by mtime (-mmin -$WINDOW_MINUTES), but a long-lived, actively-appended session file always has a 'recent' mtime, so its ENTIRE historical output-token total gets re-summed on every poll. Verified: writing one file with 50 lines of 5000 output_tokens each (250k total) and a fresh mtime triggers 'breach=output_tokens' even though none of that usage happened in the current window. Once a long session's lifetime total crosses FM_USAGE_OUTPUT_THRESHOLD, this signal will alarm on every check cycle for the rest of that session's life, defeating the sliding-window burst-detection purpose the script's own header describes and making the operator likely to ignore/disable the tripwire (alarm fatigue) right before a real burst. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-guard.sh:71` - fm-guard.sh's watcher-liveness check has no knowledge of the new state/.fleet-freeze file. While the fleet is frozen and any state/*.meta task is in flight, fm-watch.sh/fm-watch-arm.sh will always refuse to (re)arm (by design), so the watcher beacon can never go fresh — meaning every guarded command (fm-send, fm-spawn, fm-teardown, fm-pr-check, etc.) will perpetually print the bordered 'WATCHER DOWN - SUPERVISION IS OFF' alarm and tell the operator to run bin/fm-watch-arm.sh, which will just fail again with 'fleet frozen: watch-arm refused'. This produces confusing, self-contradicting guidance during exactly the incident-review window the freeze feature exists for. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:856` - fm_fleet_freeze_refuse is only checked once, before fm_super_main's `while true` loop starts. If the away-mode daemon is already running when the fleet is frozen, its loop keeps calling start_watcher, which forks fm-watch.sh — and fm-watch.sh now refuses immediately with 'fleet frozen: watch refused' (exit 1, empty stdout). The daemon's crash-handling path (record_crash/backoff) treats this as a genuine watcher crash: it logs 'watcher exited rc=1 reason=' repeatedly every CRASH_NORMAL_SLEEP (5s) until CRASH_THRESHOLD (10) trips within CRASH_WINDOW (60s), then backs off 60s and repeats forever. The daemon never cleanly recognizes the freeze and pauses; it crash-loops indefinitely with misleading 'watcher crashed' error logs for as long as both the daemon and the freeze remain active. - ℹ️ `AGENTS.md` - Three new operator-facing scripts (bin/fm-freeze.sh, bin/fm-fleet-map.sh, bin/fm-usage-tripwire.sh) ship with tests but are not referenced anywhere in AGENTS.md (e.g. section 8 supervision protocol, or a new subsection). AGENTS.md is described in this repo as firstmate's 'entire job description', so without an entry here firstmate has no durable way to learn these tools exist or when to reach for them (e.g. arming the tripwire check, using fleet-map to diagnose Herdr drift, or freezing the fleet during an incident). 🔧 Fix: Fix tripwire window scoping, freeze-aware guard/daemon, add AGENTS.md pointers 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:1048` - The tripwire window-scoping fix shipped with two new regression tests (tests/fm-usage-tripwire.test.sh), but the other two round-1 fixes - fm-guard.sh's freeze-aware banner text and fm-supervise-daemon.sh's deferred-restart-without-crash-count logic - shipped with no new test coverage. Both are meaningful control-flow changes (a new branch in the banner logic, and a new early-continue path in the daemon's crash/restart loop) that would benefit from a regression test asserting the daemon does not log 'watcher exited rc=1' / trip record_crash while state/.fleet-freeze is present, and that fm-guard.sh prints 'FLEET FROZEN' instead of 'WATCHER DOWN' when frozen.
