title: feat(bin): encode project AGENTS.md authoring bar with canonical self-governance section
body:
## Intent Encode the captain's 2026-07-06 AGENTS.md authoring bar into firstmate's shared tracked surfaces so every firstmate user inherits it. The intended contract is that project AGENTS.md files are only for knowledge useful to almost every future session, should not repeat details already discoverable from the codebase except as pointers to authoritative files or commands, should prefer rewriting or pruning over appending, and should instruct all agents how to maintain that bar. Keep the canonical short self-governance wording in bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh as the one owner, update bin/fm-brief.sh so ship briefs tell crewmates to apply the bar and add the self-governance section when touching project AGENTS.md files that lack it, and add only a concise principle plus pointer in shared AGENTS.md section 6. Extend colocated tests for fm-ensure-agents-md.sh and fm-brief.sh, keep additions tight, preserve one-sentence-per-line tracked Markdown and plain dashes, and ensure bin/*.sh, bin/backends/*.sh, and tests/*.sh pass shellcheck. This run includes the no-mistakes review fix that promotes existing CLAUDE.md files with the same canonical maintenance section instead of limiting the wording to newly created AGENTS.md files. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh` now owns the canonical `## Maintaining this file` self-governance wording for project `AGENTS.md` files, appending it when creating the skeleton and when promoting an existing `CLAUDE.md`; the append is idempotent (already-present sections succeed as a no-op) and inserts a blank-line separator even when the promoted file lacks a trailing newline. - `bin/fm-brief.sh` ship briefs' Project memory section now states the authoring bar - record only knowledge useful to almost every future session, prefer pointers to authoritative files or commands over copied detail - and instructs crewmates to add the self-governance section from `fm-ensure-agents-md.sh` when a touched project `AGENTS.md` lacks it. - Shared `AGENTS.md` section 6, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/scripts.md` record the principle and point to the script as the one owner of the wording; new colocated tests cover skeleton creation, CLAUDE.md promotion, the newline-less separator case (asserting the heading is actually present), and the new ship-brief wording. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Well-bounded additive change (docs, one idempotent newline-safe script function, brief wording, colocated tests) already hardened through three review-fix rounds, with no remaining correctness, security, or behavioral risks found. ## Testing Baseline full test suite passed before this run; I re-ran the two colocated test files for the changed scripts (7 tests, all green) and then exercised the change the way a crewmate would experience it, capturing CLI transcripts: fm-ensure-agents-md.sh creates AGENTS.md with the canonical "## Maintaining this file" section, promotes an existing CLAUDE.md with the section appended (including the newline-less edge case with a proper blank-line separator), and is idempotent on re-run; a freshly scaffolded ship brief carries the authoring-bar and add-the-section-if-lacking wording; and shared AGENTS.md section 6 contains the principle plus pointer. No visual artifact applies since this is a CLI/markdown-contract change with no rendered UI surface; transcripts are the product-level evidence. No failures found.
Evidence: fm-ensure-agents-md.sh E2E transcript (create, promote, newline-less separator, idempotency) ```text === E2E demo: bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh AGENTS.md authoring bar === --- Case 1: empty project (no AGENTS.md, no CLAUDE.md) --- $ fm-ensure-agents-md.sh /tmp/fm-agents-bar-demo.P4wMh4/new-project created: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md in /private/tmp/fm-agents-bar-demo.P4wMh4/new-project $ ls -l new-project total 8 -rw-r--r--@ 1 kunchen wheel 651 Jul 6 19:20 AGENTS.md lrwxr-xr-x@ 1 kunchen wheel 9 Jul 6 19:20 CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md $ cat new-project/AGENTS.md # Project agent memory This file is the project's committed home for project-intrinsic agent knowledge: build, test, release, architecture, and sharp-edge notes that should travel with the code. - Add durable project-specific notes here as they are discovered through real work. ## Maintaining this file Keep this file for knowledge useful to almost every future agent session in this project. Do not repeat what the codebase already shows; point to the authoritative file or command instead. Prefer rewriting or pruning existing entries over appending new ones. When updating this file, preserve this bar for all agents and keep entries concise. --- Case 2: existing hand-written CLAUDE.md gets promoted WITH the maintenance section --- $ cat claude-project/CLAUDE.md (before) # Existing agent memory Run tests with `make test`. $ fm-ensure-agents-md.sh /tmp/fm-agents-bar-demo.P4wMh4/claude-project promoted: moved CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md and symlinked CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md in /private/claude-project $ ls -l claude-project total 8 -rw-r--r--@ 1 kunchen wheel 423 Jul 6 19:20 AGENTS.md lrwxr-xr-x@ 1 kunchen wheel 9 Jul 6 19:20 CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md $ cat claude-project/AGENTS.md (after promotion) # Existing agent memory Run tests with `make test`. ## Maintaining this file Keep this file for knowledge useful to almost every future agent session in this project. Do not repeat what the codebase already shows; point to the authoritative file or command instead. Prefer rewriting or pruning existing entries over appending new ones. When updating this file, preserve this bar for all agents and keep entries concise. --- Case 3: CLAUDE.md WITHOUT trailing newline still gets a clean blank-line separator --- $ fm-ensure-agents-md.sh /tmp/fm-agents-bar-demo.P4wMh4/no-newline-project promoted: moved CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md and symlinked CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md in /private/no-newline-project $ cat no-newline-project/AGENTS.md # Existing agent memory Run tests with make test. ## Maintaining this file Keep this file for knowledge useful to almost every future agent session in this project. Do not repeat what the codebase already shows; point to the authoritative file or command instead. Prefer rewriting or pruning existing entries over appending new ones. When updating this file, preserve this bar for all agents and keep entries concise. --- Case 4: idempotency - re-running on an already-promoted project keeps exactly one section --- $ fm-ensure-agents-md.sh /tmp/fm-agents-bar-demo.P4wMh4/claude-project (second run) unchanged: AGENTS.md with CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md in /private/claude-project $ grep -c '## Maintaining this file' claude-project/AGENTS.md 1 ```
Evidence: fm-brief.sh generated ship brief Project-memory section + shared AGENTS.md section 6 wording ```text === E2E demo: bin/fm-brief.sh ship brief carries the AGENTS.md authoring bar === $ FM_HOME=/fmhome fm-brief.sh demo-task-x1 some-proj warn: no registry at /fmhome/data/projects.md; defaulting some-proj to no-mistakes off scaffolded: /fmhome/data/demo-task-x1/brief.md (ship, mode=no-mistakes; replace {TASK}) $ sed -n '/# Project memory/,/^$/p' /fmhome/data/demo-task-x1/brief.md # Project memory If `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` already exists, or if this task produced durable project-intrinsic knowledge, run `/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh .` in the worktree. Record only project knowledge useful to almost every future session. For anything the codebase already shows, prefer a pointer to the authoritative file, command, or doc over copying the detail. If you touch a project `AGENTS.md` that lacks `## Maintaining this file`, add that short self-governance section from `/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh` in the same pass. Keep it proportionate: skip `AGENTS.md` edits for trivial tasks that produced no durable project knowledge. === Shared AGENTS.md section 6 principle + pointer (added lines in context) === $ grep -n -A2 'only for knowledge useful to almost every future session' AGENTS.md 357:A project's `AGENTS.md` is only for knowledge useful to almost every future session in that repo. 358-Prefer a pointer to the authoritative file, command, or doc over repeating what the codebase already shows, and rewrite or prune stale entries instead of appending by default. 359-The canonical self-governance wording for project `AGENTS.md` files lives in `bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh`; this section states the principle and points there. ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed (3) ✅ - ℹ️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:259` - The canonical self-governance section is auto-appended only on AGENTS.md creation and CLAUDE.md promotion; for an existing AGENTS.md that lacks it (the most common fleet case), the ship brief tells crewmates to hand-transcribe the wording from the script's heredoc. There is no script-side append or --print-section accessor for that path, so each manual transcription is a drift vector against the stated one-owner goal. Consider a flag that prints or appends the canonical section so crewmates never copy prose by hand. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh:45` - ensure_maintenance_section returns 1 when the section already exists, but no caller consumes that value - both call sites must add '|| true' to survive set -eu, and a future unguarded call would silently abort the script mid-flow on the benign already-present case. Returning 0 unconditionally removes the set -e trap and the '|| true' noise. 🔧 Fix: make ensure_maintenance_section idempotent-success, drop || true guards 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh:48` - When a promoted CLAUDE.md lacks a trailing newline, the appended section's `printf '\n'` only terminates the dangling last line, so the `## Maintaining this file` heading is glued directly to the previous content line with no blank separator (verified by running the script on such a file). Still parses as an ATX heading, but produces a malformed-looking committed file. Fix mechanically: if the file is non-empty and its last byte is not a newline, emit two newlines before the section instead of one. 🔧 Fix: separate appended maintenance section on newline-less CLAUDE.md promotion 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `tests/fm-ensure-agents-md.test.sh:62` - The newline-less-promotion separator test passes vacuously if the maintenance section is never appended: when the heading is absent, `grep -B1 -Fx` produces no output, `before` is empty, and `[ -z "$before" ]` succeeds. Assert the heading is present (e.g. `assert_grep '## Maintaining this file' "$agents" ...`) before the blank-separator check so a section-not-appended regression on this path fails the test instead of slipping through. 🔧 Fix: assert maintenance heading present before separator check in test ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: fix(afk): stop herdr escalation redelivery loop
body:
## Intent Fix the away-mode supervise daemon's escalation-redelivery loop on the herdr backend. Symptom: while state/.afk is set and the fleet runs on herdr, bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh re-injected the SAME buffered escalation digest every cycle instead of clearing state/.subsuper-escalations once delivery landed, waking firstmate's LLM repeatedly for an already-handled escalation. Reproduced live against a real, isolated herdr session running a real claude process as the supervisor pane and the real fm-supervise-daemon.sh (not a synthetic script): observed 5+ identical digest deliveries in 40 seconds. Root cause confirmed empirically (not assumed): fm_backend_herdr_composer_state's structural composer-row classifier only recognized BORDERED composer rows (the grok shape it was originally built for). Real claude's and codex's live input rows are UNBORDERED - claude's is a bare '❯' with no surrounding border characters at all, flanked by plain horizontal-rule separators, and codex's is a bare '›'. Both harnesses' own startup banners ARE bordered, so immediately after launch the 'last bordered row wins' scan locks onto the banner's own blank interior row (a coincidental false 'empty'), and once that banner scrolls out of the 20-line capture window (true of any real, in-use supervisor pane) NO bordered row exists anywhere in view, so the classifier reports 'unknown' for a genuinely idle composer, forever. fm_backend_herdr_send_text_submit only treats 'empty' as a confirmed submit, so escalate_flush never clears the buffer even though the real Enter key actually submitted the digest - and because the pre-type pending-guard only defers on 'pending' (never 'unknown'), the next housekeeping tick retypes and resubmits the identical buffered digest, which is the redelivery loop. Fix: fm_backend_herdr_composer_state (bin/backends/herdr.sh) now recognizes TWO composer-row shapes in one forward scan - the existing bordered shape and a new bare/unbordered shape (a trimmed line starting with a known prompt glyph: claude's ❯, codex's ›, plus the existing >/$/%/# set) - keeping whichever match is bottom-most, since a decorative bordered box is always rendered above the live composer, never below it, in every harness observed. This is a deliberate decision to prefer 'last match of either shape' over 'bordered-only with a bare fallback', because the earlier design was empirically proven wrong (a bordered decorative banner coexisting with a live bare prompt caused a false-empty misread). Also empirically discovered but explicitly NOT fixed in this change (documented as a known, separate follow-up in docs/herdr-backend.md): codex's idle composer shows dynamic/rotating tip text rather than a blank row or a fixed placeholder string, so it cannot be told apart from real pending text by regex; this makes an idle codex composer classify as 'pending' rather than 'empty', which is a strictly SAFER failure mode (defer forever, buffer preserved, max-defer wedge alarm still fires) than the redelivery loop, so it was deliberately left as a documented gap rather than folded into this fix. Similarly, the task's suggested secondary scope item - a 'paused/awaiting-external' crew state so an intentional rate-limit wait isn't flagged as a wedge - was deliberately deferred and documented as a separate backlog-style follow-up note in docs/herdr-backend.md rather than implemented, per explicit instruction to keep this PR scoped to the redelivery-loop fix if the secondary item would balloon the change. Verification performed: re-ran the exact same real-herdr+real-claude E2E repro after the fix and confirmed the composer now reads 'empty' correctly, zero 'inject failed' log lines, the escalation buffer clears, and the digest is delivered exactly once (was unknown/redelivered before). ## Intent

Fix Firstmate watcher so no-mistakes gates that appear after an initially absorbed turn-end are reliably surfaced.

## What Changed
- Captain, watcher triage now records targeted run-step follow-up markers when a provably working signal is absorbed, then rechecks those tasks so later parked or terminal no-mistakes gates surface as signal wakes.
- Real status and turn-ended signals are prioritized over due follow-up markers, and stale follow-up markers are cleared when a task is gone or a newer signal has surfaced.
- Shared classifier logic now exposes the provably-working line parser for follow-up scans, with watcher triage tests covering parked follow-ups, marker cleanup, and signal precedence.

title: fix(backends): confirm Herdr submits with native agent state
body:
## Intent Fix the herdr backend's message-submit confirmation so it no longer false-reads codex's dynamic idle-tip composer text as pending and blocks/mis-confirms a send (the fm-afk-herdr-loop-a4 codex idle-read gap, captain-flagged 2026-07-07). Changed fm_backend_herdr_send_text_submit in bin/backends/herdr.sh to confirm a landed submit via herdr's NATIVE semantic agent-state (agent get idle->working transition), via a new fm_backend_herdr_wait_for_working helper that polls FM_BACKEND_HERDR_SUBMIT_POLLS (default 6) times spread across the existing per-Enter-attempt budget, rather than a single check-at-the-end - this deliberately guards against BOTH a slow transition (samples spread across the whole window, not just the end) and an instant round-trip (empirically measured real claude/codex first-working latency at 90-490ms across 20 real trials, comfortably inside the sampling window). Composer-content reading (fm_backend_herdr_composer_state) is intentionally UNCHANGED and kept, but only for the pre-injection empty-box guard (bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh's pane_input_pending) - it is deliberately no longer used for post-submit confirmation, since that composer-based approach is exactly what let codex's dynamic idle-composer hint text misread as 'pending' forever. Verified empirically against a real, isolated herdr 0.7.1 session with real claude 2.1.203 and codex 0.142.1 agents: timing distribution, a genuinely swallowed Enter, an unreadable target, and an already-busy target (message queued while working). Also discovered and fixed a real incompatibility in tests/fm-afk-inject-herdr-e2e.test.sh: its synthetic supervisor-pane fixture only drew composer text without being a registered herdr agent, so under the new agent-state confirmation it would read agent_not_found forever and cause the daemon to retype/resubmit the same escalation every housekeeping tick (the exact duplicate-send bug this whole change exists to prevent) - fixed by having the fixture register itself as a real herdr agent via herdr's own documented 'herdr pane report-agent' integration primitive and report a real idle->working->idle cycle around each submission. Extended tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh with new direct unit coverage for fm_backend_herdr_wait_for_working (busy-on-first-poll, slow-transition-caught-mid-window, idle-when-never-busy, unknown-when-never-readable) and rewrote the send_text_submit tests to use agent-state responses instead of composer-text fixtures, including the core regression test proving send_text_submit confirms correctly and never calls 'pane read' even when composer_state on the same target would misread as pending (using a real captured codex idle-tip fixture), plus a regression guard confirming the pre-injection guard still refuses genuine pending composer text unaffected by this change. Documented the empirical timing/design rationale as backend-verification evidence in docs/herdr-backend.md (new 'Native agent-state submit confirmation' section) and added the new FM_BACKEND_HERDR_SUBMIT_POLLS tunable to docs/configuration.md. title: fix(watcher): never surface orphaned .status/.turn-ended/.check.sh signals
body:
## Intent

Fix orphan-signal watcher marker guard so watcher supervision correctly detects and guards against orphaned signal state

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-watch.sh` now detects `.status`/`.turn-ended`/`.check.sh` files with no matching `state/<id>.meta` (leftovers from a torn-down task, or a leaked turn-end hook writer) and absorbs/removes them before classification instead of surfacing them as actionable wakes.

title: fix(session-start): respawn dead secondmate agents conservatively
body:
## Intent Fix a fleet-reliability gap: a secondmate agent (persistent domain supervisor) that exits leaves its backend pane alive as a bare shell, which the session-start endpoint check reports as 'alive' since it only checks pane presence. Recovery never respawns it and the watcher deliberately exempts secondmates from stale-pane detection, so a dead secondmate sits dead indefinitely and invisibly (evidence 2026-07-07: all four secondmates in one fleet were found as dead zsh shells). This must be fixed deterministically at the SCRIPT level, not via agent judgment, and must be conservative in one specific direction: a false-dead reading would spin up a DUPLICATE agent (two supervisors sharing one home), which is worse than leaving the original bug unfixed for one more sweep, so any ambiguous/unknown probe result must never trigger a respawn. Implementation, in two parts: 1. A new deeper per-backend liveness PROBE (fm_backend_agent_alive in bin/fm-backend.sh, dispatching to fm_backend_tmux_agent_alive in bin/backends/tmux.sh and fm_backend_herdr_agent_alive in bin/backends/herdr.sh) that answers 'is a real harness-agent PROCESS running here', distinct from the existing fm_backend_target_exists pane-presence-only check. For tmux this reads tmux's own #{pane_current_command} (empirically verified with real tmux 3.6a, evidence recorded in docs/tmux-backend.md) and classifies known harness names (claude/codex/opencode/grok) as alive, bare shell names as dead, and anything ambiguous - including a bare 'node'/'python' interpreter name, which is a real, deliberate, documented gap because the pi harness runs under a generic node process name that cannot be confidently attributed from outside the pane - as unknown, never dead. For herdr it's a thin wrapper reusing the ALREADY-VERIFIED fm_backend_herdr_pane_agent_state husk classifier (dead/no-agent -> dead, live -> alive, unknown -> unknown), so no new empirical herdr verification was needed. Backends with no verified classifier (zellij/orca/cmux) deliberately report unknown rather than guessing. 2. An idempotent session-start respawn sweep (secondmate_liveness_sweep in bin/fm-bootstrap.sh) added alongside the existing locked-and-primary-only mutating sweeps (secondmate fast-forward sync, X-mode setup, fleet sync). For every live secondmate meta it runs the probe and acts ONLY on a confident 'dead' verdict: kill the stale endpoint first (a deliberate design choice - the tmux adapter's create_task refuses to create a same-named window over a live one, so the sweep must remove the dead pane before respawning) then respawn via the existing documented recovery path (bin/fm-spawn.sh --secondmate). 'alive' is a no-op; 'unknown' is reported (SECONDMATE_LIVENESS: ... skipped: liveness probe inconclusive) but never acted on. The sweep is skipped under FM_BOOTSTRAP_DETECT_ONLY=1 (the read-only session path) exactly like the other mutating sweeps, and is naturally scoped to the primary since a secondmate's own state/ never holds kind=secondmate metas (secondmates never spawn secondmates) - no explicit primary-check was needed for that scoping. Explicitly out of scope, called out in code comments and docs/herdr-backend.md 'Known gaps': a secondmate dying MID-session (only session-start/reboot is covered here) - that needs a periodic liveness beacon since the watcher exempts secondmates from stale detection by design, and is a harder follow-on not attempted in this change. Added tests/fm-secondmate-liveness.test.sh with 9 tests covering: tmux classifier alive/dead/unknown cases including the login-shell-dash defensive strip and the node-is-unknown-not-dead case, the herdr wrapper's state mapping (via function-override unit tests, mirroring the existing convention in tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh), the generic dispatcher's routing and unverified-backend fallback, and five sweep-level end-to-end tests against the real bin/fm-bootstrap.sh (dead->respawn with kill-then-new-window verified via a call log, alive->untouched, unknown->never-acted-on, idempotent convergence across two runs, skipped under detect-only, and silent no-op with no secondmate meta present). All new and existing related tests pass (fm-secondmate-sync, fm-bootstrap, fm-backend, fm-session-start, fm-backend-herdr, fm-backend-herdr-respawn-idem-e2e, tmux/herdr smoke tests, fm-crew-state) and shellcheck is clean across bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh tests/*.sh. Documentation: docs/tmux-backend.md and docs/herdr-backend.md each got an 'Agent liveness probe' section with the empirical evidence (exact tmux commands/output, real binary types for claude/codex/opencode/pi checked via file/ps), plus AGENTS.md section 3 got a two-sentence pointer (no mechanics duplicated there per this repo's coding-guidelines skill). ## What Changed - Add a session-start secondmate liveness sweep that uses backend-level agent probes and respawns only on confident dead-agent verdicts, leaving alive or inconclusive endpoints untouched. - Introduce tmux and herdr agent-process liveness classifiers, with unsupported or ambiguous backends returning unknown instead of guessing. - Document the new liveness behavior and backend-specific gaps, and add focused coverage for classifier routing, conservative sweep behavior, detect-only mode, and idempotent respawn convergence. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: Captain, the change has no substantiated blocking findings, but it adds a locked session-start path that can kill and respawn persistent supervisors, so the operational blast radius is higher than a low-risk script-only change. ## Testing The pre-existing full baseline had already passed; I reran the focused liveness test in a marker-stripped shell, ran adjacent bootstrap/session-start/backend coverage, and captured isolated CLI transcripts showing dead-shell respawn, ambiguous-node no-op, and detect-only skip behavior; all checks passed and the worktree remained clean.

title: secondmate clone gate and docs omit cross-model-review mode
body:
## Context

The `cross-model-review` delivery mode was added as plumbing (PR for `fm/cross-model-mode-p4`). A cross-model-review reviewer flagged a consistency gap that was deliberately left out of that plumbing-only PR and deferred here.

## The gap

`bin/fm-home-seed.sh` (around lines 540-543 and 567-570) gates secondmate project clones by rejecting only `mode=local-only`. Its error message, and the `secondmate-provisioning` skill (SKILL.md:80), both state that secondmates "support only no-mistakes and direct-PR projects".

Now that a fourth mode (`cross-model-review`) exists, a cross-model-review project silently passes that gate into a secondmate home, contradicting the stated restriction.

## Severity

Not a correctness bug. It is harmless in practice (cross-model-review is remote-backed, so the clone works) and the review orchestration itself is a separate deferred follow-up. But the code and its documented restriction no longer agree.

## Suggested fix

Decide the intended policy for `cross-model-review` in secondmate homes, then make the gate, its error message, and the `secondmate-provisioning` skill wording agree:
- if cross-model-review IS allowed in secondmate homes, update the error message and SKILL.md:80 to list it alongside no-mistakes and direct-PR; or
- if it is NOT allowed, add it to the rejected set in `fm-home-seed.sh` alongside `local-only`.

## Related

Follow-up to the cross-model-review delivery-mode plumbing. Pairs with the deferred reviewer-panel orchestration work (convergence check + F5 escalation), which is also not yet implemented.

title: fix(backends): target all-digit tmux sessions by name and harden bash 3.2 compatibility
body:
## Intent Fix two firstmate tooling bugs plus one same-class bug found along the way, all around macOS system bash 3.2 compatibility and tmux session targeting. (1) The fm-brief.sh bash-3.2 parse bug (issue #166): the core apostrophe fix already landed on main in PR #173 before this branch, so this branch closes the remaining asked-for gaps: a repo-wide regression guard that runs bash -n over bin/, bin/backends/, and tests/ (tests/fm-bash32-parse.test.sh, preferring /bin/bash when it is a 3.x bash so macOS machines get the true 3.2 parse check), a new bash32 CI job that parses every script under the official bash:3.2.57 docker image because the Ubuntu runner's own bash 5.2 parser accepts the 3.2-breaking heredoc-in-command-substitution constructs and cannot catch this class natively, and extending tests/fm-brief.test.sh with the previously uncovered --scout and --secondmate scaffold variants. (2) Ship the stashed fm-spawn numeric-session fix: the stash targeted tmux new-window -t "$SES" in bin/fm-spawn.sh, but that code was since refactored into bin/backends/tmux.sh fm_backend_tmux_create_task, so per firstmate's explicit approval the equivalent one-character fix (-t "$ses:") was ported there instead of applying the conflicting stash, and the stash itself is deliberately left in place for firstmate to clean up. The trailing colon forces an all-digit session name (tmux reuses the current session name, which can be numeric) to parse as a session name instead of a window index; verified empirically on a private tmux socket that the bare form lands the window in the wrong session or forces a wrong index, and a regression case was added to the real-tmux smoke test that fails with the bare form. The byte-exact old-vs-new backend conformance test still passes because both old and new paths route through the shared backends dir. (3) Bonus fix per the captain's standing fix-failures-you-find rule: tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh extra-args was failing under /bin/bash 3.2 before this branch, because fm-pr-merge.sh expands an empty merge_args array under set -u, an unbound-variable error until bash 4.4 that Linux CI masks; guarded with the repo's established "${arr[@]+...}" idiom from fm-spawn, and the rest of bin/ was swept for the class (all other array expansions are length-guarded, :-guarded, or provably non-empty). CONTRIBUTING.md documents the bash 3.2 compatibility contract, both trap classes, and which guard catches which. Deliberate choices a diff-only reviewer might flag: the CI docker job is intentionally a separate small job rather than part of lint; the new parse test includes tests/*.sh not just bin/ because the test suite also runs on macOS dev machines; the comment in bin/backends/tmux.sh create_task explains why list-windows keeps the bare form (it takes a target-session, unaffected); commit messages intentionally carry the empirical repro details. Later pipeline commits on the branch (exec bit on the new test, CONTRIBUTING syncs, SC2016 directive) were applied by the no-mistakes pipeline itself in earlier runs. Full behavior suite verified green under /bin/bash 3.2.57 locally. ADDENDUM: one more same-theme fix on the branch: tests/fm-tangle-guard.test.sh ran bin/fm-bootstrap.sh with the inherited host PATH - the only real-host-CLI call in the suite - and its real 'no-mistakes --version' probe deadlocks when the suite executes inside a no-mistakes pipeline test step (observed wedged probe processes up to 17h old; this is what made earlier pipeline runs die at the test step as 'daemon crashed during execution'). Both bootstrap invocations are now pinned to a stub toolchain plus system dirs, matching every other bootstrap-invoking suite and the file's own hermeticity contract. ## What Changed - Fixed `fm_backend_tmux_create_task` in `bin/backends/tmux.sh` to target the session explicitly with `-t "$ses:"`, so an all-digit (numeric) session name is parsed as a session rather than a window index that lands the new window in the wrong place; added a regression case to the real-tmux smoke test. - Corrected bash 3.2 UTF-8 handling in the `composer_state` glyph classification for `bin/backends/cmux.sh` and `bin/backends/herdr.sh`, and restored the canonical `merge_args` guard idiom in `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh`. - Added a repo-wide bash 3.2 parse guard (`tests/fm-bash32-parse.test.sh`) plus a `bash:3.2.57` Docker CI job that the Ubuntu runner's bash 5.2 parser cannot substitute for, and extended `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` with `--scout`/`--secondmate` coverage and `tests/fm-tangle-guard.test.sh` to stub the toolchain instead of invoking the host `no-mistakes`. - Documented the bash 3.2 compatibility contract and its guards in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and synced `docs/configuration.md` and the coding-guidelines skill. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The branch is almost entirely additive test and CI coverage plus one verified one-character tmux targeting fix with its own regression test, and the round-1 review fix restored bin/fm-pr-merge.sh to match origin/main exactly. ## Testing The configured e2e suite already passed as baseline. I additionally exercised each part of this multi-fix change on its true end-user surface — the genuine macOS /bin/bash 3.2.57 — since that is exactly the environment these fixes target and where Linux CI's newer bash cannot catch the bug class. The repo-wide parse sweep (tests/fm-bash32-parse.test.sh) confirmed it selects and runs under /bin/bash 3.2.57; the tmux smoke test's new all-digit-session regression, the fm-pr-merge empty-array guard, the cmux/herdr UTF-8 glyph composer classification, the new scout/secondmate brief variants, and the tangle-guard hermeticity fix all pass. I also empirically reproduced the core tmux bug on a private socket: the pre-fix `-t \"204\"` form mis-parses the numeric session name as a window index (forcing index 204), while the shipped `-t \"204:\"` form correctly lands the window at the next free index — evidence saved to tmux-numeric-session-repro.txt. No product or test failures; the full suite was already confirmed green and only exceeds a 2-minute foreground window due to real-tmux/backend timing, not failures.
Evidence: tmux numeric-session bug/fix repro (bare form forces index 204, fixed form lands at next free index) === BARE FORM (buggy): tmux new-window -t "204" === session=204 index=1 name=zsh session=204 index=204 name=fm-bare <- forced to INDEX 204 === FIXED FORM: tmux new-window -t "204:" === session=204 index=2 name=fm-fixed <- lands at next free index ```text Repro: fm-spawn numeric-session tmux targeting bug (bin/backends/tmux.sh create_task) Simulating firstmate running inside an all-digit tmux session named '204'. === BARE FORM (buggy): tmux new-window -t "204" === session=204 index=1 name=zsh session=204 index=204 name=fm-bare ^ window forced to INDEX 204 (numeric name mis-parsed as window index) === FIXED FORM: tmux new-window -t "204:" === session=204 index=1 name=zsh session=204 index=2 name=fm-fixed session=204 index=204 name=fm-bare ^ window lands at next free index 2 (204: parses as session name) ```
Evidence: bash 3.2 parse sweep + composer tests running under genuine /bin/bash 3.2.57 ```text $ /bin/bash --version -> GNU bash, version 3.2.57(1)-release (arm64-apple-darwin24) ok - all bin/, bin/backends/, and tests/ scripts parse under /bin/bash (3.2.57(1)-release) ok - real tmux: fm_backend_tmux_create_task targets an all-digit session by name, not window index ok - fm_backend_cmux_composer_state: a bare '❯' composer row reads empty ok - fm_backend_herdr_composer_state: a real-claude unbordered '❯' prompt row reads empty ```
- Outcome: 🔧 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ across 2 runs (1h0m9s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Rebase** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `CONTRIBUTING.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main 🔧 Fix applied. ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ℹ️ `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh:93` - Post-rebase, this commit (05aff90) no longer adds the set -u guard its message describes - main already got that guard via PR #209 (51f7186), so the remaining delta only rewrites the canonical unquoted idiom ${merge_args[@]+"${merge_args[@]}"} (the exact form used at bin/fm-spawn.sh:257, which the commit message claims to match) into a fully-quoted variant. Verified empirically: the base-commit script runs clean under /bin/bash 3.2.57 with an empty merge_args, and the new quoted form expands to zero words on 3.2, so behavior is identical - but the change is redundant, diverges from the repo's established idiom, and CONTRIBUTING now documents the quoted variant. Consider reverting to the unquoted form (and fixing the CONTRIBUTING example) for consistency, or dropping the delta. - ℹ️ `.github/workflows/ci.yml:34` - The new bash32 job pulls bash:3.2.57 anonymously from Docker Hub on every run; shared GitHub runners occasionally hit Docker Hub rate limits, so this job can flake independently of the code. title: fix: detect degraded Codex watcher supervision
body:
## Summary

This makes Firstmate honest on Codex surfaces where a tracked background watcher can exit without automatically waking the assistant turn.

The watcher still runs normally, but Codex sessions whose background-completion wake channel has not been empirically verified now surface a `DEGRADED` diagnostic instead of claiming full one-shot supervision reliability.

## Example failure mode

A concrete local case that motivated this patch:

1. Firstmate arms `bin/fm-watch-arm.sh` as a long-running tracked Codex exec session.
2. A secondmate appends a real update, for example `done: Project #16 no-status triage inspected 56 rows...`, to `state/minekube-secondmate.status`.
3. `fm-watch.sh` detects the status write correctly and exits with a wake reason such as:

   ```text
   signal: /Users/robin/Developer/robinbraemer/firstmate/state/minekube-secondmate.status
   ```

4. On this Codex surface, that background exec completion does not reliably start a new assistant turn. The signal is present, but the operator only sees it after manually polling the exec session.
5. Without this patch, Firstmate could treat the watcher as normally supervised and end the turn, leaving the watcher down after it fired.
6. With this patch, the arm/guard/turn-end paths say `DEGRADED` and warn that a fresh one-shot watcher is not proof of an automatic Codex wake path. The operator must keep the exec session polled, use a verified wake channel, or explicitly set `FM_CODEX_BACKGROUND_WAKE=verified` only after a local smoke proves it.

So the bug is not that `fm-watch.sh` misses the event. It catches the event. The unsafe assumption is that Codex will reliably wake Firstmate when that background watcher exits.

## Changes

- Add shared supervision helpers for detecting an unverified Codex background wake channel.
- Show a loud guard warning when in-flight work has only a fresh watcher on that degraded Codex path.
- Add the degraded suffix to `fm-watch-arm.sh` `started` / `healthy` output.
- Block primary turn end in Codex when in-flight work depends on an unverified watcher wake path, while preserving the AFK/sub-supervisor exemption.
- Add focused watcher and turn-end guard tests.
- Document the Codex caveat in `docs/turnend-guard.md`.

## Validation

- `bash tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh`
- `bash tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh`
- Full `tests/*.test.sh` suite via no-mistakes test step
- Manual smoke in this fleet: primary watcher exited on a disposable status signal, was drained, and re-armed; Akua and Minekube secondmate homes were fast-forwarded to this fix and re-armed with the degraded Codex diagnostic.

No CI checks are configured on this repository; no-mistakes reported `checks-passed` after review, tests, lint fallback, push, PR creation, and CI monitoring.

title: feat(self-fix): worktree-based self-fix flow for firstmate's own tracked code
body:
## Intent Bootstrap firstmate's self-fix capability. Problem: firstmate could not ship fixes to its OWN tracked code (bin/, AGENTS.md) because the repo is not treehouse-pooled (so fm-spawn cannot get an isolated worktree for it) and the primary checkout must stay on its default branch (the tangle guard alarms otherwise). This change adds a worktree-based self-fix flow so it can. New bin/fm-self-fix.sh creates an isolated plain 'git worktree' of this repo on a fix/ branch rooted OUTSIDE any FM_HOME, then dispatches a crewmate into it via a new fm-spawn --worktree mode. Deliberate decisions a diff-only reader would not know: (1) plain git worktree rather than treehouse-pooling the firstmate repo - intentionally lighter, no pool setup; (2) scoped to the tmux backend ONLY for this bootstrap (herdr/zellij/orca/cmux are a deliberate later follow-up), which is why only the tmux window-cwd path is wired via SPAWN_CWD; (3) every change is gated behind the new --worktree flag / selffix=1 meta marker, so ALL existing spawn and teardown paths are byte-identical when the flag is absent - zero behavior change for normal tasks is intended; (4) fm-teardown reuses the existing landed-work safety check UNCHANGED and only swaps the cleanup verb to 'git worktree remove --force' for selffix tasks - the --force is safe by construction because it runs only AFTER that safety check has already passed (or --force was given), so it never bypasses the unlanded-work protection. The primary checkout never leaves its default branch throughout. This is the one-time human-bootstrap commit for keystone task fm-self-fixable-k1. ## What Changed - Add `bin/fm-self-fix.sh`, which creates an isolated plain `git worktree` of this repo on a `fix/` branch rooted outside any `FM_HOME` and dispatches a crewmate into it via `fm-spawn.sh --worktree`, so firstmate can ship fixes to its own tracked material while the primary checkout stays on its default branch. - Extend `bin/fm-spawn.sh` with a `--worktree` mode that wires the passed-in worktree as the task cwd (via `SPAWN_CWD` on the tmux create-task path) and records a `selffix=1` meta marker; the mode is gated to the tmux backend only and refuses other backends. All existing spawn paths are unchanged when the flag is absent. - Update `bin/fm-teardown.sh` to reuse the existing landed-work safety check unchanged for `selffix=1` tasks, swapping only the cleanup verb to `git worktree remove --force` (plus `fix/` branch delete) and skipping the post-teardown fleet-sync; document the flow in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, and add coverage in `tests/lib.sh`, `tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh`, and `tests/fm-session-start.test.sh`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is fully gated behind a new `--worktree` flag / `selffix=1` meta marker so all existing spawn and teardown paths are unchanged, both prior-round findings are resolved, and the `--force` cleanup runs only after the unchanged landed-work safety gate. ## Testing Baseline configured command plus the full tests/*.test.sh suite pass (including the diff-touched fm-gotmp and fm-session-start suites and the teardown/tangle/turnend guards). Since no committed test covers the new self-fix flow, I drove it end-to-end against a hermetic copy of the firstmate repo on a private tmux socket, capturing a labelled transcript that demonstrates every deliberate decision in the intent: isolated fix/<id> worktree outside FM_HOME, a real crewmate launched in that worktree, the primary checkout staying on its default branch throughout, the gated selffix=1 meta marker with an otherwise byte-identical default meta, the unchanged landed-work safety check (refuses unlanded, passes once landed) with only the cleanup verb swapped to `git worktree remove`, and the tmux-only backend guard. No product or setup issues found; working tree left clean and transient tmux/scratch artifacts removed.
Evidence: Self-fix end-to-end transcript (dispatch → verify isolation → safety refusal → landed teardown → tmux-only guard) ```text ========== 0. SETUP: hermetic firstmate repo + private tmux socket ========== primary checkout: /tmp/selffix-e2e.1pSv4q/firstmate (branch main) ========== 1. DISPATCH: fm-self-fix.sh creates an isolated worktree + spawns a crewmate ========== authored brief at data/demo-fix-a1/brief.md running: bin/fm-self-fix.sh demo-fix-a1 '' Preparing worktree (new branch 'fix/demo-fix-a1') HEAD is now at cc94570 initial firstmate snapshot self-fix worktree: /tmp/selffix-e2e.1pSv4q/scratch/demo-fix-a1 (branch fix/demo-fix-a1 off main) warn: no registry at /tmp/selffix-e2e.1pSv4q/firstmate/data/projects.md; defaulting firstmate to no-mistakes off spawned demo-fix-a1 harness=bash kind=ship mode=no-mistakes yolo=off window=firstmate:fm-demo-fix-a1 worktree=/tmp/selffix-e2e.1pSv4q/scratch/demo-fix-a1 fm-self-fix exit code: 0 ========== 2. VERIFY: isolated worktree on fix/, primary still on default branch ========== worktree path: /tmp/selffix-e2e.1pSv4q/scratch/demo-fix-a1 worktree exists: YES worktree branch: fix/demo-fix-a1 worktree rooted OUTSIDE the firstmate home (/tmp/selffix-e2e.1pSv4q/firstmate)?: YES PRIMARY checkout branch (must stay default): main git worktree list: /tmp/selffix-e2e.1pSv4q/firstmate cc94570 [main] /tmp/selffix-e2e.1pSv4q/scratch/demo-fix-a1 cc94570 [fix/demo-fix-a1] ========== 3. VERIFY: crewmate launched inside the worktree (live tmux pane) ========== bash -lc "echo FM_SELFFIX_CREWMATE_ON_DECK; echo cwd=$(pwd); exec sleep 600" CK; echo cwd=$(pwd); exec sleep 600" FM_SELFFIX_CREWMATE_ON_DECK cwd=/tmp/selffix-e2e.1pSv4q/scratch/demo-fix-a1 pane cwd matches worktree?: YES ========== 4. VERIFY: state meta records selffix=1 (the gated marker) ========== state/demo-fix-a1.meta: window=firstmate:fm-demo-fix-a1 worktree=/tmp/selffix-e2e.1pSv4q/scratch/demo-fix-a1 project=/tmp/selffix-e2e.1pSv4q/firstmate harness=bash kind=ship mode=no-mistakes yolo=off tasktmp=/tmp/fm-demo-fix-a1 model=default effort=default selffix=1 selffix marker present?: YES backend= absent (tmux default, byte-identical meta)?: YES ========== 5. SAFETY: teardown REFUSES a self-fix worktree with unlanded work ========== unlanded commit on fix/demo-fix-a1: 06a3dfb wip self-fix change (unlanded) teardown exit code: 1 (nonzero = refused, safety check UNCHANGED) REFUSED: worktree /tmp/selffix-e2e.1pSv4q/scratch/demo-fix-a1 has work not on any remote and not landed. 06a3dfb wip self-fix change (unlanded) worktree preserved after refusal?: YES ========== 6. LANDED: merge the fix into the default branch, then teardown succeeds ========== default branch now contains the fix: 5623a07 land self-fix demo-fix-a1 running: bin/fm-teardown.sh demo-fix-a1 (no --force; safety check must PASS) teardown exit code: 0 teardown demo-fix-a1 complete (window firstmate:fm-demo-fix-a1, worktree /tmp/selffix-e2e.1pSv4q/scratch/demo-fix-a1) worktree removed via 'git worktree remove'?: YES fix branch deleted?: YES scratch parent dir cleaned?: YES meta removed?: YES PRIMARY still on default branch after full lifecycle: main git worktree list (worktree admin entry gone): /tmp/selffix-e2e.1pSv4q/firstmate 5623a07 [main] ========== 7. TMUX-ONLY: fm-spawn --worktree refuses a non-tmux backend ========== running: bin/fm-spawn.sh x proj --worktree /tmp/x --backend herdr exit code: 1 (nonzero expected) error: self-fix (--worktree) is only supported on the tmux backend ========== DONE ========== ```
Evidence: End-to-end demonstration harness (reproducible against any repo copy) ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # End-to-end demonstration of the worktree-based self-fix flow. # # Exercises the REAL bin/fm-self-fix.sh -> bin/fm-spawn.sh --worktree -> the # crewmate running in an isolated git worktree -> bin/fm-teardown.sh (selffix=1), # against a hermetic COPY of the firstmate repo (never the gate). A private tmux # socket keeps the host's sessions untouched. Produces a labelled transcript. set -u SRC_REPO=${1:?usage: selffix-e2e.sh } WORK=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/selffix-e2e.XXXXXX") SOCKET="selffix-e2e-$$" REAL_TMUX=$(command -v tmux) SHIM="$WORK/shim" hr() { printf '\n========== %s ==========\n' "$1"; } note() { printf ' %s\n' "$*"; } cleanup() { "$REAL_TMUX" -L "$SOCKET" kill-server >/dev/null 2>&1 || true rm -rf "$WORK" } trap cleanup EXIT # --- 0. hermetic fake firstmate repo + private tmux shim --------------------- hr "0. SETUP: hermetic firstmate repo + private tmux socket" FAKE="$WORK/firstmate" mkdir -p "$FAKE" # Copy only what the scripts need; skip .git so the copy is its own fresh repo. ( cd "$SRC_REPO" && tar cf - bin docs .agents AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md 2>/dev/null ) | ( cd "$FAKE" && tar xf - ) export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=selffix GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=selffix@example.invalid export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=selffix GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=selffix@example.invalid git -C "$FAKE" init -q -b main git -C "$FAKE" add -A git -C "$FAKE" commit -qm "initial firstmate snapshot" note "primary checkout: $FAKE (branch $(git -C "$FAKE" symbolic-ref --short HEAD))" mkdir -p "$SHIM" cat > "$SHIM/tmux" < "$FAKE/data/$ID/brief.md" <<'BRIEF' # Self-fix task demo-fix-a1 Fix a typo in bin/. Ship through the gate like any project change. BRIEF note "authored brief at data/$ID/brief.md" note "running: bin/fm-self-fix.sh $ID ''" bash "$FAKE/bin/fm-self-fix.sh" "$ID" "$STUB" rc=$? note "fm-self-fix exit code: $rc" WT="$FM_SELFFIX_ROOT/$ID" hr "2. VERIFY: isolated worktree on fix/, primary still on default branch" note "worktree path: $WT" note "worktree exists: $( [ -d "$WT" ] && echo YES || echo NO )" note "worktree branch: $(git -C "$WT" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null)" note "worktree rooted OUTSIDE the firstmate home ($FAKE)?: $(case "$WT" in "$FAKE"/*) echo NO;; *) echo YES;; esac)" note "PRIMARY checkout branch (must stay default): $(git -C "$FAKE" symbolic-ref --short HEAD)" note "git worktree list:" git -C "$FAKE" worktree list | sed 's/^/ /' hr "3. VERIFY: crewmate launched inside the worktree (live tmux pane)" sleep 2 pane=$("$REAL_TMUX" -L "$SOCKET" capture-pane -p -t "firstmate:fm-$ID" 2>/dev/null) printf '%s\n' "$pane" | grep -E 'FM_SELFFIX_CREWMATE_ON_DECK|cwd=' | sed 's/^/ /' note "pane cwd matches worktree?: $(printf '%s\n' "$pane" | grep -qF "cwd=$WT" && echo YES || echo 'NO (see pane)')" hr "4. VERIFY: state meta records selffix=1 (the gated marker)" note "state/$ID.meta:" sed 's/^/ /' "$FAKE/state/$ID.meta" note "selffix marker present?: $(grep -q '^selffix=1$' "$FAKE/state/$ID.meta" && echo YES || echo NO)" note "backend= absent (tmux default, byte-identical meta)?: $(grep -q '^backend=' "$FAKE/state/$ID.meta" && echo 'NO' || echo YES)" # ============================================================================ hr "5. SAFETY: teardown REFUSES a self-fix worktree with unlanded work" # Crewmate makes a real commit on fix/ that is NOT merged anywhere. echo "// self-fix change" >> "$WT/bin/fm-self-fix.sh" git -C "$WT" add -A git -C "$WT" commit -qm "wip self-fix change (unlanded)" note "unlanded commit on $(git -C "$WT" symbolic-ref --short HEAD): $(git -C "$WT" log --oneline -1)" set +e out=$(bash "$FAKE/bin/fm-teardown.sh" "$ID" 2>&1) rc=$? set -e 2>/dev/null || true note "teardown exit code: $rc (nonzero = refused, safety check UNCHANGED)" printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -iE 'REFUSED|unlanded|not on any remote' | sed 's/^/ /' note "worktree preserved after refusal?: $( [ -d "$WT" ] && echo YES || echo NO )" # ============================================================================ hr "6. LANDED: merge the fix into the default branch, then teardown succeeds" git -C "$FAKE" merge -q --no-ff -m "land self-fix demo-fix-a1" "fix/$ID" note "default branch now contains the fix: $(git -C "$FAKE" log --oneline -1)" note "running: bin/fm-teardown.sh $ID (no --force; safety check must PASS)" set +e out=$(bash "$FAKE/bin/fm-teardown.sh" "$ID" 2>&1) rc=$? set -e 2>/dev/null || true note "teardown exit code: $rc" printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -iE 'teardown .* complete' | sed 's/^/ /' note "worktree removed via 'git worktree remove'?: $( [ -d "$WT" ] && echo 'NO' || echo YES )" note "fix branch deleted?: $(git -C "$FAKE" show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/fix/$ID" && echo NO || echo YES)" note "scratch parent dir cleaned?: $( [ -d "$FM_SELFFIX_ROOT" ] && echo 'still present' || echo YES )" note "meta removed?: $( [ -e "$FAKE/state/$ID.meta" ] && echo NO || echo YES )" note "PRIMARY still on default branch after full lifecycle: $(git -C "$FAKE" symbolic-ref --short HEAD)" note "git worktree list (worktree admin entry gone):" git -C "$FAKE" worktree list | sed 's/^/ /' # ============================================================================ hr "7. title: docs(agents): trim section 7 spawn duplication to its owners
body:
## Trim section 7 Spawn duplication to its owners

Continues the AGENTS.md diet (after #253/#255/#258) with one surgical one-owner consolidation, in the same style as those PRs.
Section 7's Spawn subsection had grown to restate mechanics that already have canonical owners; this replaces each restatement with a pointer, per the one-owner rule in `firstmate-coding-guidelines`.

### Measured size delta

Always-loaded `AGENTS.md` is paid by every session of every fleet member, every turn, whether or not that session hits the situation the lines describe.

| Surface | Before | After | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AGENTS.md (o200k_base tokens) | 26,759 | 26,397 | **-362 (-1.35%)** |
| AGENTS.md (lines) | 939 | 936 | -3 |

### What changed (all in section 7 Spawn)

- **Runtime backend resolution** - the selection order, the innermost-first auto-detection nesting, and the per-backend refusals (including `codex-app` as unknown) were restated nearly verbatim from `docs/configuration.md` "Runtime backend".
  Replaced with a pointer.
  Firstmate never computes backend resolution at spawn - the script does - and the actionable "a backend refusal is a blocker, never silently retry another backend" rule already sits on the very next line, so nothing firstmate acts on was lost.
- **Per-backend workspace scoping** (herdr per-home workspaces, zellij single shared session) was likewise owned in full by that doc.
  Replaced with a pointer.
- **The `<id>.meta` field enumeration** (`harness=`/`model=`/`effort=`/`kind=`/`mode=`/`yolo=`, secondmate `home=`/`projects=`, and the non-default `backend=` note) duplicated section 2's canonical `<id>.meta` line.
  Replaced with a section 2 pointer.
- **The grok per-task turn-end hook mechanics** duplicated `docs/configuration.md` (the `$GROK_HOME/hooks/` install plus `.fm-grok-turnend` pointer, teardown removal) and section 2's `grok-turnend-token` line.
  Removed: `harness-adapters` already delegates per-task turn-end hook mechanics to `bin/fm-spawn.sh`, and the hook is installed by spawn and removed by teardown with no firstmate action in between, so there is no wake-time trigger to preserve inline.
- **A redundant "`backend=codex-app` is unknown" line** already stated in the spawn command block, section 2, and the runtime-backend pointer.

### Safety

- No hard rule, no section 8 always-on supervision core-loop content, and no wake-time trigger was touched.
- Every distinctive token removed (env vars, flags, thresholds, paths) was programmatically confirmed to survive in its owner (`docs/configuration.md` or AGENTS.md section 2).
- All 14 section numbers and titles are unchanged; `CLAUDE.md` -> `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/skills` -> `.agents/skills` symlinks untouched.
- Validated locally through the no-mistakes pipeline: review, test, document, and lint each returned zero findings.

### Scope note

This is deliberately one surgical theme kept independently reviewable, not a whole-file diet.
Judgment-heavy extractions that need a maintainer decision on shape (the section 14 X-mode cadence block, and the section 7 `no-mistakes axi status` validation state table) were intentionally left out of this PR.

fix(backends): pass provider API keys through to cmux crewmate spawns
body:
## Intent Fix the cmux backend so provider API keys reach spawned crewmate processes: opencode spawns need FIREWORKS_API_KEY so opencode's Fireworks-backed models (e.g. GLM 5.2) work. fm_backend_cmux_create_task now builds --env FIREWORKS_API_KEY= for cmux new-workspace by fetching the key at spawn time from AWS Secrets Manager (secret opencode/fireworks-api-key, region us-east-1) using ambient AWS credentials - no hardcoded profile; a missing key fails the spawn loudly rather than silently continuing. Deliberate decisions already made and binding: the harness-to-secret pairing lives in local gitignored config/cmux-env-secrets so shipped code stays provider-neutral (captain decision); the fetched secret value is never printed, logged, or committed, and is redacted from cmux new-workspace failure output (captain decision); the SC2015 and-or chain in the empty-value check was rewritten as a proper if/then to satisfy shellcheck CI. Unit tests stub the aws CLI so no real AWS calls happen in tests. Push goes through the fork Kadriya89/firstmate per CONTRIBUTING.md since contributors lack upstream push access; PR targets kunchenguid/firstmate. An earlier hand-raised PR #360 exists and should be updated or superseded by the pipeline-raised PR. ## What Changed - `bin/backends/cmux.sh` gains a provider-credential passthrough for workspace creation: a new local, gitignored `config/cmux-env-secrets` file pairs a harness with `ENV_VAR / secret-name / optional region` lines, and `fm_backend_cmux_create_task` (now taking an optional harness argument, which `bin/fm-spawn.sh` passes on every cmux spawn) fetches each paired secret from AWS Secrets Manager at spawn time using ambient AWS credentials and injects it via cmux's `new-workspace --env KEY=VALUE`. This fixes opencode spawns on the cmux backend, whose scrubbed surface environment never received `FIREWORKS_API_KEY`, breaking Fireworks-backed models. - The fetch fails the spawn loudly (missing `aws` CLI, failed call with AWS stderr surfaced, or empty secret) instead of silently launching without a configured key; the fetched value is never printed or logged and is redacted from echoed-back `new-workspace` failure output; malformed pairing lines are skipped with a stderr warning; an absent file or unpaired harness triggers no AWS call at all. title: Move the X-mode cadence block out of always-loaded AGENTS.md
body:
Section 14's `**Cadence.**` block only matters to an instance that has opted into X mode, but it sits inline in `AGENTS.md`, so every session pays for it whether or not X mode is on.
It's 14 lines, about 337 tokens (o200k_base), roughly 1.3% of the file.
The earlier X-mode cleanup (#253) moved the Answering and Mechanism procedures out to `fmx-respond` and `docs/configuration.md` but left this block inline.

There's a real reason it was left, which is why I'm filing an issue instead of a PR: the cadence procedure fires at watcher-arm time, not mention time.
`fmx-respond` loads on an `x-mention` wake, but sourcing `config/x-mode.env` before arming and the restart on an opt-in or opt-out transition happen when firstmate arms the watcher, with no X skill loaded.
So some arm-time facts have to survive inline, and a full move into `fmx-respond` would risk a missed trigger.

I think the right shape is the same inline-stub split section 8 uses for away mode: keep the arm-time stub inline (source `config/x-mode.env` before arming, restart the watcher on a cadence transition, keep the watcher armed for an X-only user even with no fleet work) and move the explanatory prose (why non-X instances keep 300s, the `FM_CHECK_INTERVAL` read-at-process-start mechanism, the note that bootstrap deliberately doesn't restart the watcher, the away-mode out-of-scope note) into `docs/configuration.md` "X mode (.env)", which already owns the wire protocol.
That leaves maybe 120 to 150 tokens inline and saves around 200.
The judgment call that's yours: which of the cadence facts count as arm-time safety-critical.

Draft PR #313 lists this as its unapplied proposal #3.
Filing it standalone so the decision survives whatever happens to that PR.

title: fix(composer): make composer-state classification locale-invariant
body:
## Intent

Make firstmate's composer-state classification locale-invariant, so the away-mode supervisor cannot misread a pane's composer under the C/POSIX locale its daemon actually runs with.

Two separate faults, one root cause - a multibyte glyph treated as bytes under a C locale:

1. bin/fm-composer-lib.sh stripped a leading prompt glyph by CHARACTER COUNT (${content#?}). Under C/POSIX that removes a single BYTE, orphaning two bytes of the three-byte U+276F glyph. The backends' idle-placeholder regexes are anchored, so the stray byte defeats the anchor and an idle composer reads 'pending' instead of 'empty' - which makes the away-mode injector defer every escalation indefinitely (the overnight wedge).

2. bin/backends/herdr.sh matched the bare agent prompt with a grep bracket class ('^[❯›]'). Under C/POSIX that degenerates into a BYTE class, and every box-drawing glyph leads with the same byte, so the composer box's own bottom border row falsely matches as a bare prompt row. herdr keeps the bottom-most match, so the border row outranks the real composer, strips to empty, and the composer reads 'empty' while the human's unsubmitted text sits right above it - the false-EMPTY direction, where the injector would type over real input.

The fix replaces both byte-fragile forms with literal glyph sets matched by bash 'case', so no locale-sensitive grep or byte arithmetic remains anywhere in the glyph path. The glyph set becomes configurable - fleet-wide, and per-herdr layered on top of the fleet-wide default - and is threaded through the shared classifier so an operator-added harness glyph is honored for classification, not just for structural row detection (previously it was honored for detection only, so an overridden harness's idle composer wedged on 'pending' forever).

Deliberate decisions a reviewer should know about:

- Shell prompt glyphs are refused from the configurable agent set at three layers, and the hardcoded shell rule is evaluated before the configurable set, so no operator configuration can make a bare dead-shell prompt classify as an empty, injectable composer. That safety rule is the reason bin/fm-composer-lib.sh exists and it is preserved absolutely.
- A supplied set that sanitizes down to nothing falls back to the built-in default rather than to an empty set, so agent-glyph recognition can never be switched off fleet-wide.
- FM_BACKEND_HERDR_BARE_PROMPT_RE is retired in favour of a literal glyph-set knob. This is a real cost and is stated plainly: it changes the accepted FORMAT of a documented environment override. It is unavoidable, because any regex spelling must reach grep, and grep under a C locale is the hazard itself. Mitigating: the knob is set nowhere but its own default and one doc example; setting it now warns loudly on stderr instead of being silently ignored; and the code already contradicted its own documentation, since the knob was documented as controlling the recognized prompt glyphs but was honored only for row detection.
- Default behavior with no knob set is byte-identical to before, for every backend.
- Every locale regression test pins the locale in a child process, because an 'LC_ALL=C <shell function>' prefix does not re-run setlocale on bash 3.2 and would guard nothing.
- The test step also repaired two pre-existing fixture faults unrelated to this change (a missing composer-lib sibling in the gotmp fixture, and two Pi tests that did not tolerate node 23's experimental type-stripping warning), which were failing the suite locally before this branch.

## What Changed

- Replaced the two byte-fragile glyph forms in the composer path with literal glyph sets matched by bash `case`: `bin/fm-composer-lib.sh` no longer strips a leading prompt glyph by character count (`${content#?}`, which removes a single byte under C/POSIX and orphans two bytes of a three-byte glyph), and `bin/backends/herdr.sh` no longer matches bare prompts with a grep bracket class (`^[❯›]`, which degenerates into a byte class where every box-drawing glyph shares the leading byte, so a composer border row outranks the real composer). The only remaining regex — the per-harness idle placeholder — is now matched under a pinned `LC_ALL=C` so a hand-tested pattern behaves the same inside the C-locale supervise daemon.
- Made the agent glyph set configurable and threaded it through the shared classifier: `FM_COMPOSER_AGENT_GLYPHS` fleet-wide, with herdr's `FM_BACKEND_HERDR_BARE_PROMPT_GLYPHS` layering on that default and handed to `fm_composer_classify_content` as well as to structural row detection, so a configured glyph is honored for classification rather than detection only. Shell prompt glyphs (`>`, `$`, `%`, `#`) are refused at three layers, including the shared match chokepoint, and a set that sanitizes down to nothing falls back to the built-in `❯ ›` instead of emptying. `FM_BACKEND_HERDR_BARE_PROMPT_RE` is retired: it now warns loudly on stderr instead of being silently ignored. With no knob set, behavior is byte-identical to before for every backend.
- Added locale regression coverage in `tests/fm-composer-lib.test.sh` and `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh`, each pinning the locale in a child process because an `LC_ALL=C <shell function>` prefix does not re-run `setlocale` on bash 3.2. Along the way, repaired two pre-existing fixture faults that were failing the suite locally (a missing composer-lib sibling in the gotmp fixture, and two Pi tests that did not tolerate node's experimental type-stripping warning), and updated the herdr, configuration, and harness-adapter docs to the new knobs.

title: feat: add omp (Oh My Pi) harness adapter
body:
## What

Adds `omp` (Oh My Pi) as a sixth verified firstmate harness adapter, alongside claude, codex, opencode, pi, and grok. Firstmate can now detect when it is itself running on omp (previously mis-detected as claude), and can spawn / supervise / steer / recover / tear down omp crewmates and secondmates, hold its session lock under omp, and run its own primary turn-end guard + watcher supervision under omp.

## Why omp is distinct (not just "pi")

omp is Pi-derived but differs in ways that matter to the adapter:

- Sets both `OMPCODE=1` and `CLAUDECODE=1`, so detection must check OMPCODE first or omp mis-detects as claude.
- Runs as process `omp`, so it supports confident secondmate liveness (pi's bare `node` does not).
- Has a real approval system, so unattended crewmates need `--auto-approve`.
- `.omp/extensions/*.ts` is a native auto-discovery root, so the primary turn-end guard is a tracked, auto-discovered extension (no `-e` wiring, no generated bridge like pi needs).
- Exposes an active `session_stop` hook that forces a continuation by returning `{continue:true}`, making omp a **direct-blocking** turn-end harness (class with claude/codex) - a third mechanism distinct from the passive follow-up used by pi/grok/opencode.

## Surface

- Detection (`fm-harness.sh`), lock (`fm-lock.sh`), spawn mechanics + crewmate turn-end signal extension (`fm-spawn.sh`).
- Busy detection (`fm-watch.sh`, `fm-tmux-lib.sh`), liveness (`bin/backends/tmux.sh`).
- Bootstrap dispatch/effort/secondmate-liveness (`fm-bootstrap.sh`), session-start guard load-health (`fm-session-start.sh`), teardown cleanup (`fm-teardown.sh`).
- Primary turn-end guard: new tracked `.omp/extensions/fm-primary-turnend-guard.ts` (session_stop); classification comment + `repair_line` arm; new `docs/supervision-protocols/omp.md`; `docs/turnend-guard.md`.
- Knowledge: `harness-adapters` skill omp section + an expanded new-adapter wiring checklist so future adapters are fully wired; verified-set enumerations across `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, docs, and the afk skill.
- Tests: new `tests/fm-omp-harness.test.sh` and `tests/fm-lock.test.sh`, plus coverage in bootstrap/teardown/turnend-guard/supervision/liveness; `tests/lib.sh` now clears ambient harness markers so detection is hermetic across dev machines.

## How it was built

Spec-first: a frozen spec was authored, then reviewed from four angles in parallel (adapter-integration consistency, version-resilience, correctness/security, test coverage). The review caught real gaps the first draft missed - a `fm-lock.sh` blocker (an omp primary could not hold its session lock), three separate adapter enumerations in `fm-bootstrap.sh`, and the `repair_line()` arm - which were folded into the spec before the parallel implementation.

## Verification

- Every omp runtime fact verified live on **omp 16.3.12**: detection markers, process name, busy signature (`⟦esc⟧`), `/quit` exit + resume line, `.omp/extensions` auto-discovery of a committed file, and `session_stop` forced continuation (with both a static return and a realistic async handler that awaits a spawned subprocess).
- `shellcheck bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh tests/*.sh` is clean.
- ~25 test files pass locally covering every touched surface plus a regression sweep; 0 failures.

Interrupt (Escape) is inferred from omp's own `⟦esc⟧` hint rather than cleanly observed; a re-confirm item is recorded in the skill's re-verification checklist.

title: fix(watcher): wait when arm attaches to a healthy watcher
body:
## Intent Fix empty/false Grok (and Claude) supervision wakes caused by bin/fm-watch-arm.sh exiting immediately when a live watcher already holds the lock. On Grok's background-notify protocol, firstmate re-arms with bin/fm-watch-arm.sh after every turn that ends with work still in flight. When a watcher was already healthy, the arm printed watcher: healthy and exited 0 in ~0.1s, which completed the harness background task and injected a synthetic task_completed wake with no real signal/stale/check/heartbeat and no queued wake - an empty false wake. The same early-exit shape existed on the peer-startup-race path. The captain chose attach-and-wait (not "error if already armed"): when mode=arm and a healthy watcher already holds the lock, do not exit; print watcher: attached pid= (beacon s) and poll/wait until that identity-matched holder is no longer healthy, then exit 0 so the harness notify fires for a real cycle end. Do not start a second watcher (singleton preserved). Peer-startup-race after a stood-down child uses the same attach-and-wait contract. --restart and the started (fork+wait child) path stay unchanged. Optional re-attach if a different healthy watcher appears mid-attach. Tests rewritten for attach-and-wait (do not exit while seed lives; exit 0 after seed dies; peer race same). Protocol docs for Grok and Claude updated to remove "healthy no-op" as an exit that ends the turn; architecture/scripts/AGENTS one-line cross-refs updated. No watcher/wake-queue/harness redesign. ## What Changed - Updated `fm-watch-arm.sh` so normal arm mode attaches to an already-healthy watcher and waits for that watcher cycle to end instead of exiting immediately, while preserving the existing restart and child-start behavior. - Added watcher lock coverage for attach-and-wait and peer startup race behavior so the arm process stays alive while the seed watcher owns the lock and exits cleanly after it is gone. - Synced the watcher arm contract across AGENTS and supervision docs, including Claude and Grok protocol guidance, to describe attached watcher waits instead of a healthy no-op exit. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the change is narrowly scoped to watcher arm/attach handling plus matching docs and tests, and I did not find any substantiated merge-blocking or follow-up findings. ## Testing Captain, the pre-run full baseline was already green, the focused watcher-lock regression test passed, and the manual CLI transcript shows `fm-watch-arm.sh` attaching to an existing healthy watcher, staying live until that watcher exits, preserving the singleton lock, and exiting cleanly afterward.

title: fix(fm-spawn): capture only a project-repo worktree
body:
## Intent Fix intermittent fm-spawn.sh worktree-capture bug where a task's meta sometimes recorded worktree=~/.oh-my-zsh (or another transient dir) though the crew launched in the correct treehouse worktree, breaking teardown and defeating isolation. Root cause: the capture loop accepted the first polled pane cwd that merely differed from the primary checkout; treehouse's fresh shell sources ~/.zshrc and oh-my-zsh's update check momentarily runs cd $ZSH (=~/.oh-my-zsh), and a poll sampling that instant recorded it. validate_spawn_worktree missed it because ~/.oh-my-zsh is a real git repo distinct from the project. Fix (robust for any transient cwd): the capture loop now accepts a candidate only if it shares the project repository's git common-dir (all treehouse worktrees share one object store with the primary; unrelated repos do not), and validate_spawn_worktree gained the same assertion as defense-in-depth, scoped to the treehouse path (orca owns its own worktree handling, untouched). Physical paths (pwd -P) preserve symlink handling. Added defaulted poll knobs FM_SPAWN_WT_POLL_TRIES/SLEEP purely so tests exercise the timeout path fast; default 60x1s behavior unchanged. New tests/fm-spawn-worktree-capture.test.sh reproduces the bug end-to-end: a transient unrelated repo sampled first is skipped and the real worktree captured, a cwd that never becomes a project worktree is refused, and a genuine worktree is accepted. A non-git or unrelated-repo cwd now aborts via the capture-loop timeout instead of validate_spawn_worktree - same safe outcome (exit 1, no meta recorded); the existing tangle-guard test was aligned to that. firstmate's own shared/tracked material; shellcheck clean across bin and tests. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now accepts a polled pane cwd as the task worktree only when it shares the project repository's git common-dir, so a transient cwd (e.g. oh-my-zsh's `cd $ZSH` during `~/.zshrc` sourcing) is skipped instead of being recorded as `worktree=`; `validate_spawn_worktree` gained the same common-dir assertion as defense-in-depth, scoped to the treehouse path and leaving Orca's own worktree handling untouched. - Added defaulted poll knobs `FM_SPAWN_WT_POLL_TRIES`/`FM_SPAWN_WT_POLL_SLEEP` (default 60x1s, behavior unchanged) so tests can exercise the capture-timeout path quickly; a cwd that never becomes a project worktree now aborts via the capture-loop timeout rather than `validate_spawn_worktree`, same safe outcome (exit 1, no meta recorded). - Added `tests/fm-spawn-worktree-capture.test.sh` covering transient-skip, persistent-unrelated refusal via timeout, and genuine-worktree accept; realigned `tests/fm-tangle-guard.test.sh` to the timeout path; documented the common-dir check and poll knobs in `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/configuration.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A well-bounded defense-in-depth fix that only tightens worktree acceptance, rests on a confirmed repo invariant (treehouse worktrees share the project's git common-dir), leaves the happy path and orca/secondmate paths untouched, and ships with end-to-end regression tests; the only concerns are a minor consistency/robustness nit and a documented error-path latency tradeoff. ## Testing `Baseline configured suite had already run green. I ran the two directly-affected test files (the new fm-spawn-worktree-capture.test.sh and the realigned fm-tangle-guard.test.sh), both pass. On the target commit fm-spawn skips the transient repo and records the correct worktree= in the task meta (exit 0); the base commit's capture loop accepts the first differing cwd and does not cleanly produce the correct spawn on the same input, confirming the fix changes behavior. UI evidence is not applicable - this is a shell/CLI worktree-capture change whose end-user surface is the recorded state/.meta worktree= line, captured in the transcript artifact.`
