title: feat(scm): add first-party Azure DevOps support via provider abstraction
body:
## Intent Add first-party Azure DevOps (ADO) support to firstmate's own tracked material (Stream A: firstmate-core only), per an approved design blueprint and binding captain decisions. Introduce bin/fm-scm-lib.sh as a single sourced+CLI provider abstraction that detects the SCM host from the origin URL (github.com -> github; dev.azure.com/ssh.dev.azure.com/*.visualstudio.com -> ado; else unknown) and provides normalized PR helpers (state MERGED/OPEN/CLOSED, head sha, merged-PR-for-branch, ensure/resolve PR head commit) via gh for GitHub and az for ADO. Deliberate design decision: github AND unknown both take the exact pre-existing gh/git path so GitHub behavior is byte-for-byte preserved and non-github/non-ado remotes keep today's fallthrough - this is intentional, not a missed case. Rewire fm-pr-check, fm-review-diff, fm-teardown, and widen fm-fleet-snapshot's PR-URL extraction to also match ADO /_git//pullrequest/; teardown keeps the provider-agnostic content_in_default fallback and ALL refusal semantics intact. Captain decision #1: firstmate must NEVER merge/complete an ADO PR, so fm-pr-merge.sh refuses an ADO PR URL before any recording or host call and points the captain at the ADO UI (squash to match GitHub, never delete source branch); GitHub merge behavior is unchanged (--squash default). Captain decision #4: bootstrap adds az (+azure-devops extension) as a dependency for ADO-origin projects and emits NEEDS_AZ_AUTH prompting az login when unauthenticated, analogous to NEEDS_GH_AUTH, following detect->consent (never auto-install). Provider-aware crewmate brief wording (gh-axi for GitHub, az repos for ADO). AGENTS.md prose is reworded GitHub-specific contract lines to provider-neutral pointing at fm-scm-lib.sh/docs/ado-backend.md, deliberately NOT restating az command shapes inline (AGENTS.md size discipline / one-owner rule). docs/ado-backend.md is the human reference, and now also codifies which ADO gates firstmate gates on: firstmate judges content-readiness using only content-influenced automation gates (build/test/e2e, coverage, Component Governance) and ignores human review/sign-off/attestation gates even when blocking/rejected, re-queuing expired content build gates via PR-native policy evaluation rather than treating them as vacuously green. Scope is intentionally firstmate-core only (captain decision #5): no Python ado-pr CLI vendored, no new delivery mode, no explicit provider registry tag (provider auto-detected from origin, decision #2); fork-based ADO contribution is intentionally out of scope and firstmate refuses+escalates it (decision #6). Live end-to-end ADO run against a real repo is intentionally left as documented manual verification in docs/ado-backend.md (out of scope for automated CI). Tests: new tests/fm-scm-lib.test.sh (hermetic URL->provider table) plus extended pr-merge/review-diff/teardown/bootstrap/fleet-snapshot tests with an az mock alongside the gh-axi mock; the entire existing GitHub regression suite must stay green unchanged as proof the abstraction did not alter GitHub behavior. Prior pipeline rounds already added kept fix commits: a test fix trapping watcher signals so a checkpoint SIGTERM releases the singleton lock, and document-sync commits updating README/docs; all are intentionally on the branch. Follows firstmate coding guidelines: one sentence per line, plain dash, shellcheck-clean, colocated tests. NOTE: some existing watcher/timeout tests are timing-sensitive and can flake under load, and the fork push can hit transient network drops; treat a flaky-timing or transient-network failure as infra, not a code defect. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-scm-lib.sh`, a sourced+CLI provider abstraction that detects the SCM host from the origin URL (github.com → github, dev.azure.com/ssh.dev.azure.com/*.visualstudio.com → ado, else unknown) and exposes normalized PR helpers (state, head sha, merged-PR-for-branch, resolve/ensure PR head) backed by `gh` for GitHub and `az` for Azure DevOps; github and unknown both keep the exact pre-existing gh/git path so GitHub behavior is byte-for-byte preserved. - Rewired `fm-pr-check`, `fm-review-diff`, and `fm-teardown` through the abstraction, widened `fm-fleet-snapshot` PR-URL extraction to also match ADO `/_git//pullrequest/`, made `fm-pr-merge` refuse ADO PR URLs before any recording or host call (pointing the captain at the ADO UI), added `NEEDS_AZ_AUTH` bootstrap detection for ADO-origin projects, and made crewmate brief wording provider-aware; teardown keeps its content-in-default fallback and all refusal semantics intact. - Reworded GitHub-specific AGENTS.md contract lines to provider-neutral pointers, added `docs/ado-backend.md` (including which ADO gates firstmate gates on) plus doc/index updates, and added hermetic `fm-scm-lib` tests alongside extended pr-merge/review-diff/teardown/bootstrap/fleet-snapshot coverage with an `az` mock; a kept fix disarms terminating-signal traps during watcher lock release so a checkpoint SIGTERM releases the singleton lock. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change introduces a well-isolated provider abstraction that preserves the exact prior GitHub/git paths for github and unknown providers, keeps all teardown refusal semantics and the provider-agnostic content fallback intact, refuses ADO merges per captain policy, and is backed by hermetic tests plus the unchanged GitHub regression suite. ## Testing The configured baseline e2e suite already passed. I ran the smallest relevant set — every ADO-touched test plus the timing-sensitive watcher-lock and watch-checkpoint tests the final commit fixed — and all passed; the earlier full-suite failure is consistent with the author's flagged flaky timing/network tests rather than a code defect. I then exercised the two core captain decisions end-to-end as an operator would: provider auto-detection from origin URLs correctly maps GitHub/ADO/unknown, and fm-pr-merge refuses an Azure DevOps PR URL (exits non-zero, records no pr=, never invokes gh-axi, and points the captain to the ADO UI with squash/no-delete guidance) while the GitHub path stays byte-for-byte the same squash merge. Evidence captured as CLI transcripts.
Evidence: Provider detection from origin URLs `github.com -> github; dev.azure.com/ssh.dev.azure.com/*.visualstudio.com -> ado; gitlab.com -> unknown` ```text ### Provider detection from origin URL (fm-scm-lib.sh provider-of-url) https://github.com/owner/repo.git -> github git@github.com:owner/repo.git -> github https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/repo -> ado git@ssh.dev.azure.com:v3/org/project/repo -> ado https://org.visualstudio.com/project/_git/repo -> ado https://gitlab.com/owner/repo.git -> unknown ```
Evidence: ADO PR merge refusal (captain decision #1) `error: firstmate does not merge Azure DevOps PRs. Complete this PR yourself in the Azure DevOps UI ... Use squash to match GitHub, and do NOT delete the source branch. exit=1, pr= not recorded, gh-axi never called` ```text === fm-pr-merge against an Azure DevOps PR URL === error: firstmate does not merge Azure DevOps PRs. The gates are verified green; complete this PR yourself in the Azure DevOps UI: https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/repo/pullrequest/42 Use squash to match GitHub, and do NOT delete the source branch. --- exit code: 1 --- meta after attempt (pr= must NOT be recorded): pr= line count: 0 ```
Evidence: GitHub merge path preserved `gh-axi invoked with: pr merge 7 --repo owner/repo --squash ; pr=https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/7 recorded` ```text === GitHub merge path preserved: fm-pr-merge parses GH URL into gh-axi call === ●━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ● WATCHER DOWN - SUPERVISION IS OFF ● 1 task(s) in flight, but no watcher has a fresh beacon (last beat: never, grace 300s). ● Trust the emitted supervision protocol for this harness; do not use shell & for watcher repair. ● This is a supervision warning only; the guarded operation WILL still run. ● resume supervision with bin/fm-watch-arm.sh as its own Claude Code background task, never shell &. ●━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ armed: state/gh-demo.check.sh polls https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/7 gh-axi invoked with: pr merge 7 --repo owner/repo --squash --- exit: 0 ; pr recorded: pr=https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/7 ```

title: fix: enforce LF line endings via .gitattributes
body:
## Summary
- `core.autocrlf=true` in an operator's git config converts checked-out shell scripts to CRLF on checkout, which breaks their `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang (`env` looks for a `bash\r` executable and fails).
- This surfaced as a `Stop` hook failure running `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh`.
- Added `.gitattributes` (`* text=auto eol=lf`) so the repo enforces LF regardless of the operator's `core.autocrlf` setting, and renormalized the working tree accordingly (no blob content changed - only the checkout representation).

## Test plan
- [x] Verified `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh` no longer has a CRLF shebang after re-checkout.
- [x] Confirmed no tracked file remains with CRLF line endings (`file` scan across all `git ls-files`).
- [ ] `shellcheck` not available locally; relying on repo CI (`no-mistakes-required.yml`) to verify.

title: feat(supervision): prevent unsafe watcher-arm commands
body:
## Intent Prevent primary firstmate agents from arming the watcher the wrong way (shell background operator, piped-into-head, or bundled multi-command arms), which reaps the arm process when the tool call ends and silently leaves supervision blind - this exact failure took a Grok primary's supervision down for real. Captain's explicit order: implement a PreToolUse pattern-deny seatbelt now (not a delayed post-turn beacon recheck), and audit all five verified harnesses (claude, codex, opencode, pi, grok) for the same gap, closing what can be closed with one shared checker. Implementation: added bin/fm-arm-pretool-check.sh as the single owner of the anti-pattern detection (background operator, truncating pipe, multi-statement bundling, broad pkill against the watcher), with a documented 'blessed shape' allow-list matching the existing documented arm recipe. Wired it into all five harnesses' real PreToolUse-equivalent hooks, and every single one was validated empirically live (not just from docs) in a scratch project/home per harness, including capturing real hook debug logs and confirming both the deny and allow paths actually executed as expected. Along the way I discovered two things that changed the output-shape design and are intentional, not accidental complexity: (1) Claude Code only honors a PreToolUse deny when stdout is completely empty - any content there, even a differently-shaped decision JSON, makes it silently allow the tool instead of falling back to stderr - so the checker gained a --claude flag used only by the Claude adapter to suppress its default Grok-shaped stdout JSON. (2) Grok's own hook command string does its own ${VAR}/$VAR pre-substitution and rejects any bare local variable (like the pre-existing turnend-guard hook's root=${GROK_WORKSPACE_ROOT:-} pattern followed by a bare $root reference) unless every reference carries an inline :-default - this is a real regression in grok 0.2.93 (last validated at 0.2.91) that was silently making the EXISTING, already-shipped turnend-guard Stop hook no-op. I fixed both the new pretool hook and the pre-existing turnend-guard hook to reference the workspace-root variable directly everywhere instead of a bare local variable, and documented this as a dated regression note in docs/turnend-guard.md pointing to the fuller writeup in the new docs/arm-pretool-check.md. Deliberately out of scope, per the captain's instructions: no delayed post-turn beacon recheck, no change to Codex's foreground-checkpoint supervision model, no change to OpenCode/Pi's plugin/extension ownership of the actual arm mechanism (this checker is a residual-risk backstop for those two, since their arm is a real child process, not a model tool call). Added tests/fm-arm-pretool-check.test.sh (40 cases: the required acceptance table, additional pattern coverage, stdin JSON schema handling for both Grok and Claude/Codex shapes, fail-open behavior, the --claude output-shaping contract, and assertions that every harness wiring file actually invokes the shared checker plus a regression test for the grok local-variable bug) and docs/arm-pretool-check.md (full contract, per-harness audit table, the grok regression writeup, and the empirical validation transcript for all five harnesses). Cross-referenced from docs/turnend-guard.md, the harness-adapters skill, the arm script's own header, and a one-line note in each docs/supervision-protocols/*.md file, while deliberately not adding anything to AGENTS.md itself to avoid bloating it per the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill. ## What Changed - Add a shared pre-tool watcher-arm guard that blocks unsafe shell patterns while allowing the documented arm command shape. - Wire the guard into Claude, Codex, Grok, OpenCode, and Pi hooks, with harness-specific input and denial handling. - Add regression coverage and documentation for arm validation, including the Grok turn-end hook variable-expansion correction. ## Risk Assessment 🚨 High: Captain, I could not complete the required read-only review because the execution host failed to start (`/opt/homebrew/bin/codex-code-mode-host` is missing), so the commit history and diff could not be inspected. ## Testing The provided baseline passed, but targeted and end-to-end validation could not run because the local command-execution host is unavailable; no files or evidence artifacts were created. - Outcome: ⚠️ 1 warning across 1 run (10m59s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

title: feat(bootstrap): report available tool and firstmate updates
body:
## Intent Add an update-availability check to firstmate's session-start bootstrap so a captain never silently runs months-old tooling. Today bin/fm-bootstrap.sh only enforces MINIMUM versions (a floor: is the tool present, is it new enough to work); it never asks whether a newer version exists. Motivating incident (2026-07-09): the fleet sat on no-mistakes v1.33.0 for days while stable v1.34.0 shipped a fix (#411, single-daemon ownership) for a bug actively producing FALSE pipeline failures; tasks-axi was a minor version behind too. Bootstrap said nothing because both cleared the floor. The deliverable is a new report-only bootstrap diagnostic line, in the existing report style: 'UPDATE_AVAILABLE: -> (update: )', covering no-mistakes and treehouse (GitHub releases), tasks-axi (npm registry), and firstmate itself (commits behind origin/main, whose suggested action is /updatefirstmate rather than a raw git command). Deliberate decisions and constraints the user set, which a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: 1. Bootstrap must NEVER block or fail because of this. Every network call is best-effort with a hard bounded timeout, following the existing FM_FLEET_SYNC_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT precedent via an analogous overridable FM_UPDATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT (small default, 5s). Offline, rate-limited, or unauthenticated must degrade to SILENCE, never to an error or a hang. A failed check is not a failed bootstrap, so uc_report always returns 0 and swallows every probe error. Probes therefore run as background children whose stdout is redirected to result FILES rather than inherited from bootstrap's stdout: fm-session-start.sh reads bootstrap through a $(...) capture, and a straggling grandchild holding that pipe open would hang the session long after bootstrap exited. This is why the code looks indirect there; it is deliberate, not accidental. 2. Never nag onto a prerelease. Compare against the latest STABLE release only. This is not hypothetical: v1.33.0, the very version we were pinned to, is itself flagged prerelease:true, while the then-newest stable was the OLDER v1.31.2, so a naive 'latest release' check would have recommended a DOWNGRADE and reintroduced a known gate bug. Draft and prerelease releases are explicitly filtered, only bare vX.Y.Z tags are accepted, and the newest stable is selected by semver comparison rather than by GitHub's newest-first ordering (which interleaves prereleases). A test pins this exact case. 3. Cache the result. Do not hit GitHub and npm on every session start. The cache holds the REMOTE answers (not the rendered report) in state/.update-check with a checked_at epoch and a TTL (24h default, overridable via FM_UPDATE_CHECK_TTL). A cache hit involves zero network calls while local current-version reads still run so the report stays accurate. Respect the existing locked-vs-read-only split: a read-only session (FM_BOOTSTRAP_DETECT_ONLY=1, i.e. it could not acquire the fleet lock) must not write cache files. A probe round that learned nothing also writes no cache, so one transient outage does not blind the next 24h. 4. Report only, never auto-update. Installing is consent-gated exactly like the existing MISSING: flow: the captain approves, then it installs. Never update a tool as a side effect of a session starting. 5. Warn about in-flight runs: 'no-mistakes update' restarts its daemon and kills any active pipeline run, so the no-mistakes suggestion says so inline. We deliberately do NOT defeat 'no-mistakes update''s own refusal-without--y behavior. 6. Silence when everything is current. Bootstrap's contract is that silence means all good, so there is no 'everything up to date' chatter. Also required and done: AGENTS.md section 3 documents the new UPDATE_AVAILABLE: line alongside the existing MISSING:/FLEET_SYNC:/TASKS_AXI: lines and how firstmate handles it (surface to the captain with the update command, get consent, never auto-update, never update while a pipeline run is in flight). docs/configuration.md documents the mechanism and the three new env vars, per the repo's knowledge-placement rule that reference detail lives in docs rather than AGENTS.md. Tests are colocated in tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh (the repo convention is to extend the existing suite, not invent a runner) and cover: the prerelease-filter case, offline/timeout degrade-to-silence, cache-hit-makes-no-network-call, read-only-session-writes-no-cache, silence-when-current, one-line-per-stale-tool including firstmate's own staleness, and a corrupted-cache guard. Fakes are a canned-payload curl and a git wrapper that logs ls-remote, so 'zero network calls' is actually asserted rather than assumed. A deliberate choice worth calling out: tests/lib.sh now exports FM_UPDATE_CHECK=0 by default. Every suite sources that lib, so this keeps all existing tests hermetic and offline-safe; the new update-check cases opt back in explicitly per case. FM_UPDATE_CHECK=0 doubles as the documented user-facing kill switch, analogous to FM_FLEET_PRUNE=0. Scope discipline the user explicitly imposed: do not refactor the bootstrap report format, the fleet-sync sweep, or the lock logic; add the check alongside them. bin/fm-watch.sh, bin/fm-spawn.sh, and the wake queue are untouched by design. HISTORY OF THIS BRANCH so already-resolved findings do not re-surface: an earlier run of this pipeline passed intent, rebase, review, test, document, and lint, and failed only at push (a GitHub 403: the author has no write access to the upstream repo). That is now resolved by pushing to an authorized fork and opening the PR against upstream. That earlier run produced two commits that are already on this branch and must not be redone. First, a document-step fix commit filling three doc gaps: the fm-update-check-lib.sh entry in docs/scripts.md, the new test cases in CONTRIBUTING.md's suite listing, and a staleness-detection pointer in docs/architecture.md's self-update section. Second, a commit fixing the one review finding that run surfaced, which was correct: git's http.lowSpeedLimit/lowSpeedTime only bound an HTTPS origin, and GIT_SSH_COMMAND set no ConnectTimeout, so an SSH origin on a black-holed connection was not bounded by the timeout, and killing only the probe subshell orphaned its curl or git/ssh grandchild. Bootstrap itself never hung either way, because uc_wait_probes returns at the deadline and probe stdout goes to a file rather than the caller's capture, but the straggler was real. Both transports are now bounded (ssh ConnectTimeout/ServerAlive alongside the http low-speed settings) and probes are spawned under monitor mode so a timed-out probe is signalled as a process group and takes its grandchild with it, mirroring fleet_sync's existing set -m / kill -TERM -$pid precedent; the header comment was corrected to describe the process-group kill as the guard and the per-transport bounds as narrowing the window rather than overstating them. This was verified empirically: a probe with a deliberately hung grandchild leaves it running before the fix and reports Terminated: 15 after. Repo conventions followed: one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never an em dash, shellcheck-clean bin/ scripts (verified with shellcheck 0.11.0 across bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh tests/*.sh), no agent co-author trailer. Verified empirically: live probes resolve no-mistakes v1.34.0, treehouse v2.0.0, tasks-axi 0.2.0; a real bootstrap run on current tooling prints nothing new in about 1 second; with no curl/jq it prints nothing in 0 seconds; bash 3.2 compatibility confirmed since that is what 'env bash' resolves to on macOS. Known pre-existing and unrelated: tests/fm-session-start.test.sh fails when the suite is run from inside a Claude harness because detect_own() short-circuits on ambient CLAUDECODE=1 so the test's fake ps is never consulted. It fails identically on the clean base commit and passes with that variable unset, so it was deliberately left alone rather than folding a harness-detection fix into this change. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-update-check-lib.sh`, which checks no-mistakes and treehouse against latest-stable GitHub releases (prerelease/draft filtered, semver-compared), tasks-axi against the npm registry, and firstmate itself against `origin/main` commit count, caching results in `state/.update-check` with a TTL and skipping cache writes on read-only sessions. - Wired the new checks into `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` to emit `UPDATE_AVAILABLE: -> (update: )` lines alongside the existing `MISSING:`/`FLEET_SYNC:` diagnostics, bounded by an overridable timeout so a slow or offline probe degrades to silence instead of blocking bootstrap. - Hardened the update-check probes to bound both HTTPS and SSH origins (git SSH `ConnectTimeout`/`ServerAlive` alongside the existing HTTP low-speed settings) and to kill each probe's full process group on timeout, preventing an orphaned grandchild process from stranding a hung probe. - Added six new test cases plus a corrupted-cache guard to `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh`, defaulted `FM_UPDATE_CHECK=0` in `tests/lib.sh` for hermetic test runs, and documented the feature across `AGENTS.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a well-isolated, report-only diagnostic addition (new lib file plus a single call site in bootstrap) with strong empirically-verified safety invariants: bounded/backgrounded network probes with process-group kill on timeout, prerelease filtering verified against the exact incident that motivated it, cache TTL/read-only-write behavior, and a comprehensive colocated test suite (all 16 tests pass, shellcheck clean, bash 3.2 compatible). I independently verified the riskiest-looking mechanism (toggling `set -m` mid-script for process-group probe control) does not leak job-control notification text into bootstrap's captured stdout/stderr in the real invocation path, and confirmed no unbounded/blocking call was introduced beyond the pre-existing pattern already used elsewhere in fm-bootstrap.sh. ## Testing Baseline full suite passed; I additionally ran live, real-network end-to-end verification of the update-check mechanism (cache miss, cache hit, stale-tool report, and the prerelease-safety property) and empirically reproduced both the bug and the fix for the process-group-kill change in the second commit, with all results matching the author's claimed behavior and no discrepancies found.
Evidence: Manual end-to-end verification log (live probe run, cache-hit timing, motivating-incident reproduction, before/after process-group-kill fix) ```text # Manual end-to-end verification: update-availability bootstrap check ## 1. Live probe run against the real network (no cache) Sourced `bin/fm-update-check-lib.sh` and called `uc_report` directly against this repo's real `no-mistakes`/`treehouse`/`tasks-axi` installs and GitHub/npm. `` ` elapsed: 1s, exit code: 0 stdout (silence contract, everything current): [] cache written: checked_at=1783629551 no-mistakes=v1.34.0 treehouse=v2.0.0 tasks-axi=0.2.0 `` ` Confirms: real GitHub release API resolves no-mistakes latest STABLE as v1.34.0 (correctly skipping the v1.33.0 prerelease), treehouse as v2.0.0, and npm resolves tasks-axi as 0.2.0 — matching the versions actually installed, so bootstrap stayed silent per the "silence means all good" contract. ## 2. Cache-hit path (no second network round-trip) Re-ran `uc_report` against the same state dir within the TTL: `` ` elapsed: 154ms (vs 1s+ for the network round) output: [] cache checked_at unchanged -> served from cache, not re-probed `` ` ## 3. Captain-facing UPDATE_AVAILABLE line, reproducing the motivating incident Faked a local `no-mistakes --version` reporting v1.33.0 (the real prerelease version the fleet was pinned to during the incident) while letting the probe hit the real GitHub API for the latest stable release: `` ` UPDATE_AVAILABLE: no-mistakes 1.33.0 -> 1.34.0 (update: no-mistakes update - restarts the daemon and aborts any in-flight validation run) `` ` This is exactly the line a captain would see, and it correctly recommends the newer STABLE release rather than downgrading to v1.31.2 (which a naive "latest release" check would have suggested, since v1.33.0 itself is GitHub-flagged prerelease:true). ## 4. Process-group kill fix (target commit 0bf2061 vs parent bf18222) Reproduced the author's claimed empirical verification with a probe whose grandchild process outlives the timeout: - On `bf18222` (pre-fix): grandchild `sleep 30` process was **still running** after the timeout kill — orphaned, confirming the bug existed. - On `0bf2061` (target/fixed): grandchild process was **terminated** at timeout via `kill -TERM -$pid` (process-group signal), logged as `Terminated: 15`. ## 5. Automated suite `bash tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` — all cases pass, including the 6 new update-check cases (stale-tool reporting, prerelease filtering, silence when current, offline degrade-to-silence, cache-hit no-network-call, read-only session writes no cache) plus the corrupted-cache guard assertion embedded in the cache-hit case. ```
Evidence: Real captain-facing UPDATE_AVAILABLE line reproducing the v1.33.0-prerelease incident ```text UPDATE_AVAILABLE: no-mistakes 1.33.0 -> 1.34.0 (update: no-mistakes update - restarts the daemon and aborts any in-flight validation run) ```
Evidence: Process-group-kill fix: hung grandchild survives on pre-fix commit bf18222, is terminated on target commit 0bf2061 ```text bf18222 (before): GRANDCHILD 64207 STILL RUNNING after timeout -- ORPHANED 0bf2061 (after): GRANDCHILD 63794 TERMINATED after timeout -- process-group kill worked (Terminated: 15) ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Review** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` - `bash tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` (all cases pass, including 6 new update-check cases and the embedded corrupted-cache guard) - Manual live-network run of `uc_report` against this repo's real no-mistakes/treehouse/tasks-axi installs — verified real GitHub/npm resolution and silence-when-current - `Manual cache-hit run within TTL — confirmed 154ms (vs 1s+ network round) and unchanged checked_at, proving zero network calls on cache hit` - Manual simulated-stale scenario (faked local no-mistakes v1.33.0 against live GitHub API) — reproduced the exact captain-facing `UPDATE_AVAILABLE: no-mistakes 1.33.0 -> 1.34.0 (update: ...)` line and confirmed it does not suggest a downgrade to v1.31.2 - Manual before/after comparison of the process-group-kill fix using a probe with a deliberately hung grandchild process on commit bf18222 (orphaned) vs target commit 0bf2061 (terminated via `kill -TERM -$pid`, logged `Terminated: 15`) - `git status --short` and process check after testing to confirm no leftover artifacts or stray processes

title: fm-ensure-agents-md.sh creates a case-fragile CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md symlink when the project's real file is lowercase agents.md
body:
## Summary

`bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh` hardcodes the memory filename as uppercase `AGENTS.md`. In a project whose real, committed memory file is lowercase `agents.md`, the script does not detect the mismatch. On a case-insensitive filesystem (default macOS) it silently creates `CLAUDE.md` as a symlink whose literal target is `AGENTS.md` - a link that resolves locally but points at a name that does not exist on a case-sensitive filesystem (Linux, CI checkouts, case-sensitive APFS/HFS+ volumes). The result is a symlink that is committed and works on the author's Mac but is dangling for anyone who checks the repo out on a case-sensitive filesystem.

## Environment

- Silent-and-fine host: macOS, case-insensitive filesystem.
- Broken host: any case-sensitive filesystem (typical Linux CI runner, case-sensitive APFS/HFS+ volume).

## Root cause

The script fixes both names to uppercase and never reconciles against an existing lowercase real file:

- `AGENTS=AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE=CLAUDE.md` are hardcoded uppercase.
- `if [ -e "$AGENTS" ]` matches an existing lowercase `agents.md` on a case-insensitive filesystem, so the script takes the "AGENTS.md already exists" branch even though the real file is lowercase.
- With no `CLAUDE.md` present, it runs `ln -s "$AGENTS" "$CLAUDE"`, i.e. `ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md`. The stored target is the uppercase literal `AGENTS.md`, which does not name the real lowercase `agents.md` on a case-sensitive filesystem.

So the produced `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md` is correct only by the accident of case-insensitive path resolution.

## Reproduction

Reproduced end-to-end on a disposable case-sensitive disk image. The script was first run on a normal case-insensitive macOS directory (where the lowercase-match illusion actually happens and the symlink is created), then that directory was copied - preserving the symlink literally, not dereferencing it - onto a disposable case-sensitive APFS volume, exactly modeling a git commit/checkout onto a case-sensitive filesystem. The final `cat` failing to read `CLAUDE.md` on the case-sensitive volume is the dangling-symlink proof:

```sh
$ rm -f /tmp/lc-repro.sparseimage
$ hdiutil create -size 20m -fs 'Case-sensitive APFS' -volname LCREPRO -type SPARSE /tmp/lc-repro.sparseimage
created: /tmp/lc-repro.sparseimage

$ hdiutil attach /tmp/lc-repro.sparseimage
/dev/disk14         	GUID_partition_scheme
/dev/disk14s1       	Apple_APFS
/dev/disk15         	EF57347C-0000-11AA-AA11-0030654
/dev/disk15s1       	41504653-0000-11AA-AA11-0030654	/Volumes/LCREPRO

# Prove the volume is actually case-sensitive before relying on it
$ cd /Volumes/LCREPRO && touch Foo foo && ls -1
foo
Foo
$ rm -f /Volumes/LCREPRO/Foo /Volumes/LCREPRO/foo

# Step 1: build the repro project with only a lowercase agents.md, on macOS's
# normal case-insensitive filesystem (/tmp), and run the script under test there.
$ rm -rf /tmp/lc-src && mkdir -p /tmp/lc-src
$ printf '# project memory\n' > /tmp/lc-src/agents.md
$ ls -la /tmp/lc-src
total 8
drwxr-xr-x@   3 bnguyen  wheel     96 Jul  9 16:50 .
drwxrwxrwt  584 root     wheel  18688 Jul  9 16:50 ..
-rw-r--r--@   1 bnguyen  wheel     17 Jul  9 16:50 agents.md

# confirm /tmp is case-insensitive
$ cd /tmp/lc-src && touch TESTCASE testcase && ls -1 | grep -i testcase
TESTCASE
$ rm -f TESTCASE testcase

$ bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh /tmp/lc-src
symlinked: CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md in /private/tmp/lc-src

$ ls -la /tmp/lc-src
total 8
drwxr-xr-x@   4 bnguyen  wheel    128 Jul  9 16:50 .
drwxrwxrwt  584 root     wheel  18688 Jul  9 16:50 ..
-rw-r--r--@   1 bnguyen  wheel     17 Jul  9 16:50 agents.md
lrwxr-xr-x@   1 bnguyen  wheel      9 Jul  9 16:50 CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md

$ readlink /tmp/lc-src/CLAUDE.md
AGENTS.md

$ cat /tmp/lc-src/CLAUDE.md    # resolves fine here only because /tmp is case-insensitive
# project memory

# Step 2: carry the project (symlink preserved literally, not dereferenced) onto
# the case-sensitive volume - modeling a git commit/checkout elsewhere.
$ rm -rf /Volumes/LCREPRO/lc
$ cp -R -P /tmp/lc-src /Volumes/LCREPRO/lc
$ ls -la /Volumes/LCREPRO/lc
total 8
drwxr-xr-x@ 4 bnguyen  staff  128 Jul  9 16:50 .
drwxr-xr-x  4 bnguyen  staff  128 Jul  9 16:50 ..
-rw-r--r--@ 1 bnguyen  staff   17 Jul  9 16:50 agents.md
lrwxr-xr-x@ 1 bnguyen  staff    9 Jul  9 16:50 CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md

# Step 3: capture the failure on the case-sensitive volume
$ readlink /Volumes/LCREPRO/lc/CLAUDE.md
AGENTS.md

$ cat /Volumes/LCREPRO/lc/CLAUDE.md
cat: /Volumes/LCREPRO/lc/CLAUDE.md: No such file or directory

# Cleanup
$ cd /tmp
$ hdiutil detach /Volumes/LCREPRO
"disk14" ejected.
$ rm -f /tmp/lc-repro.sparseimage
$ rm -rf /tmp/lc-src
$ ls /Volumes/ | grep -i LCREPRO   # confirm gone
(no output)
$ ls -la /tmp/lc-repro.sparseimage   # confirm deleted
ls: /tmp/lc-repro.sparseimage: No such file or directory
```

## Observed vs. expected

- Observed: a `CLAUDE.md` symlink with literal target `AGENTS.md`, created without warning, resolving only on case-insensitive filesystems and dangling on case-sensitive ones.
- Expected: the script either recognizes the existing lowercase `agents.md` as the real file and creates `CLAUDE.md` pointing at the real file's actual name, or refuses and reports the case mismatch so the operator can reconcile it, instead of silently emitting a case-fragile link.

## Impact

Any consuming repo whose committed memory file is lowercase `agents.md` ends up with a `CLAUDE.md` that is broken for every collaborator or CI job on a case-sensitive filesystem, while looking fine to the macOS author who ran the script. It is a silent, portability-only failure that passes local checks and only surfaces on another machine.

## Suggested direction (non-prescriptive)

Detect the actual on-disk case of the real memory file before choosing the symlink target and point `CLAUDE.md` at its true name; if the real file's case cannot be reconciled with the hardcoded `AGENTS.md`, report a conflict instead of creating a link.

title: feat(supervision): add resting vs active state for secondmate in-flight counting
body:
## Intent

Add a 'resting vs active' supervision state for persistent secondmates, so a resting secondmate does not count as in-flight work for stop-hook/turnend-guard supervision, while an active one still does. Background: state/<id>.meta records kind=secondmate for persistent secondmates; previously ANY secondmate meta counted as in-flight for supervision purposes exactly like an ordinary crewmate/scout task, so a secondmate that is deliberately idle-but-alive still blocked the primary's turn-end whenever there was no fresh watcher beacon. This is purely a supervision-COUNTING change, not a lifecycle change: persistent secondmates/bosuns stay alive regardless of this field. Implementation: bin/fm-supervision-lib.sh's fm_supervision_status (the shared predicate used by both fm-guard.sh and fm-turnend-guard.sh) now reads kind= and supervision= from each state/*.meta file via a new fm_sup_resting_secondmate helper, and skips a meta file only when it is BOTH kind=secondmate AND supervision=resting when computing FM_SUP_IN_FLIGHT. supervision=active and legacy meta with no supervision= field at all (the pre-existing case) still count exactly as before - this is a deliberate safe default so pre-existing secondmates are never silently dropped from supervision. Ordinary crewmate/scout meta (kind=ship, kind=scout, or no kind field) is completely unaffected. dormant is a distinct, pre-existing, unrelated concept (a registry-only entry in data/secondmates.md with no live state/<id>.meta at all) and this change does not touch or conflate it. Deliberately out of scope (per explicit instruction from the task brief): no command or plumbing was added to actually set/toggle supervision=resting on a live secondmate - that lifecycle mechanism is left for a future task; this change only wires the counting predicate and documents the field. bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh itself was deliberately NOT modified: the predicate change in fm-supervision-lib.sh alone was sufficient to fix its behavior (verified by a new passing test), so per the brief's explicit guidance the hook script was left untouched to keep the change minimal. Secondmate liveness probing and respawn behavior in bin/fm-bootstrap.sh (SECONDMATE_LIVENESS sweep) is unrelated to this predicate and was verified unaffected by supervision=resting via a new test. Tests were written first (TDD), confirmed failing against the old predicate, then the implementation was added and confirmed passing. Added tests to the existing tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh (predicate-level: resting excluded, active counts, legacy counts, ordinary crewmate/scout unaffected, a resting secondmate plus real co-located in-flight work still counts; hook-level: turn-end guard silent with only a resting secondmate in flight, still blocks with an active one) and one new test in tests/fm-secondmate-liveness.test.sh proving the liveness/respawn sweep is unaffected by supervision=resting. Documentation: one clause added to AGENTS.md's existing state/<id>.meta field-list line (section 2) describing the new optional supervision= field, one new sentence in AGENTS.md section 8 cross-referencing it, and docs/turnend-guard.md's 'Shared Predicate' and 'Tests' sections updated to describe the exception and the new test coverage - all one-line pointers per this repo's one-owner/inline-stub documentation conventions (loaded the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill before making these changes, per this repo's own CONTRIBUTING.md). No yolo: this is the core firstmate-core template repo, and PR merge decisions belong to the upstream maintainer (the captain), never auto-merged by me.

## What Changed
- `bin/fm-supervision-lib.sh`'s `fm_supervision_status` (shared by `fm-guard.sh` and `fm-turnend-guard.sh`) now reads `kind=`/`supervision=` from each `state/*.meta` via a new `fm_sup_resting_secondmate` helper, excluding a meta only when it is both `kind=secondmate` and `supervision=resting` from `FM_SUP_IN_FLIGHT`; `supervision=active`, legacy meta with no `supervision=` field, and ordinary crewmate/scout meta all still count exactly as before.
- Added predicate- and hook-level test coverage to `tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` (resting excluded, active/legacy counts, ordinary crewmate/scout unaffected, resting-secondmate-plus-real-in-flight-work still counts, silent-vs-blocking hook behavior) and a new test in `tests/fm-secondmate-liveness.test.sh` proving the liveness/respawn sweep is unaffected by `supervision=resting`; also fixed portable test assertions in `tests/fm-session-start.test.sh` (mkdir wording, leaked `CLAUDECODE` env var) and a shellcheck SC1007 warning in the same file.
- Documented the new optional `state/<id>.meta` `supervision=` field and the resting/active exception in `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, and `docs/turnend-guard.md`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Small, well-scoped change to a single shared predicate function with a safe default (absent/non-"resting" values still count as in-flight), backed by thorough new tests covering the predicate, the hook-level behavior, and non-interference with the unrelated liveness/respawn sweep; docs and AGENTS.md are updated consistently with the code.

## Testing

Ran the full portable test suite (51 files via tests/*.test.sh) with tmux 3.6, and it passed end-to-end with a clean worktree afterward; targeted runs of tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh and tests/fm-secondmate-liveness.test.sh confirm the new fm_sup_resting_secondmate behavior end-to-end: a kind=secondmate meta with supervision=resting is excluded from FM_SUP_IN_FLIGHT (predicate) and does not block the turn-end hook when it's the only in-flight entry, while supervision=active or legacy meta with no field still counts and still blocks the hook exactly as before; a separate test confirms the secondmate liveness/respawn sweep in fm-bootstrap.sh is unaffected by supervision=resting (a dead resting secondmate is still killed and respawned). Ordinary crewmate/scout meta (kind=ship/kind=scout) is unaffected in all cases.

title: feat: first-party Azure DevOps support with provider-agnostic SCM layer
body:
## Intent Repoint the davidkydd/firstmate fork's no-mistakes installer reference from upstream kunchenguid/no-mistakes to the davidkydd/no-mistakes fork, so a fresh davidkydd/firstmate user installs the ADO-capable fork rather than upstream (which lacks the ADO fix). Surgical two-line change: bin/fm-bootstrap.sh install_cmd case for no-mistakes now emits the davidkydd/no-mistakes raw install.sh URL, and the matching assertion string in tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh was updated to keep the suite green. Deliberately left untouched: CONTRIBUTING.md's canonical project link and the .github/workflows/no-mistakes-required.yml CI marker string, since neither is an install/download source. Only the no-mistakes install source was changed; firstmate's own repo identity and CI references were left alone. Delivery target: PR must be into davidkydd/firstmate (the fork), not kunchenguid. ## What Changed - Added a new `bin/fm-scm-lib.sh` provider abstraction plus `docs/ado-backend.md`, and reworked `fm-pr-check.sh`, `fm-pr-merge.sh`, `fm-review-diff.sh`, and `fm-teardown.sh` to detect GitHub vs Azure DevOps from the origin remote and route PR/merge/diff/teardown operations accordingly (with `NEEDS_AZ_AUTH` bootstrap detection for ADO-origin projects). - Replaced `bin/fm-pi-watch-extension.sh` with a `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts` extension and simplified the pi primary session launch and supervision instructions. - Pointed the bootstrap `no-mistakes` installer at the davidkydd fork's raw `install.sh` URL and updated the matching bootstrap test assertion, leaving the CONTRIBUTING canonical link and CI marker untouched. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The branch's new work is a single self-consistent two-line URL swap (bootstrap install command plus its matching test assertion), with deliberately-untouched non-install references correctly left alone. ## Testing The configured baseline suite already passed; I ran the change-relevant `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` in a single clean run (all 11 tests green) and additionally exercised the real `fm-bootstrap.sh` script end-to-end in a hermetic sandbox to capture the install line a fresh davidkydd/firstmate user is actually shown, which now points at the davidkydd/no-mistakes fork. The Round 1 failure was the timing-sensitive fleet-sync timeout tests flaking under 3x concurrent load (timeout=7s elapsed=8s), not a product defect — they pass reliably in a non-concurrent run. title: fix(backlog-handoff): move full item blocks including indented bodies
body:
## Intent

Fix bin/fm-backlog-handoff.sh so secondmate backlog handoffs move the full item block, not just the checklist header line.

Bug (confirmed live 2026-07-09): handing ha-codex-fast-default-4e to a secondmate only moved the `- [ ] <id> ...` header; the item's indented multi-line body stayed in the source data/backlog.md and visually attached to the preceding item. The secondmate worked from the title alone and the spec had to be re-delivered by hand.

Required behavior:
1. Move header plus every following indented body line up to the next item line or section heading, atomically and byte-exact, preserving existing destination section placement.
2. Idempotence for body-carrying items: re-run skips when already in destination (no duplicate body, no partial moves).
3. Keep existing safety: ## In flight refusal, destination validation (seeded secondmate home with .fm-secondmate-home), byte-exact preservation of untouched lines.
4. Body membership is by indentation, not content - indented lines beginning with ## (e.g. ## Intent) must NOT be treated as section boundaries (the tokenizer trap that caused the incident).
5. Update the script header comment; add regression tests covering body followed by another item, by a section heading, as last lines of file, indented ## headings inside body, and idempotent re-run.

Prior pipeline run completed intent/rebase/review/test; review auto-fixed EOF terminator preservation (commit 8c9276c on this branch). Document step failed only because of a Codex usage limit; the gate daemon now runs Claude. Re-validate the full branch including that review fix through to a green PR.

Deliberate scope: only bin/fm-backlog-handoff.sh and tests/fm-backlog-handoff.test.sh. Sibling crews own other files; do not expand scope.

## What Changed

- Rewrote the move logic in `bin/fm-backlog-handoff.sh` so a handoff carries the `- [ ] <id>` header plus every following indented body line - including internal blank lines and indented `##` lines - up to the next item line or section heading, atomically and byte-exact, instead of moving only the header and orphaning the body in the source.
- Determined body membership strictly by indentation rather than content, so indented `##` markers (e.g. `## Intent`) are no longer misread as section boundaries, and preserved existing safeguards (`## In flight` refusal, seeded-secondmate-home destination validation, idempotent re-run, untouched-line preservation) plus EOF handoff terminators.
- Added `tests/fm-backlog-handoff.test.sh` covering body-followed-by-item, body-followed-by-section-heading, multi-paragraph internal blanks, EOF last lines, indented `##` tokenizer trap, and idempotent re-run; updated the script header comment, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and the secondmate-provisioning skill to describe the full-block move behavior.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is well-bounded to two files, correctly fixes the prior round's body-orphaning finding, carefully preserves byte-exact EOF terminators, and is backed by thorough regression tests covering item/section/EOF boundaries, indented headings, internal blanks, and idempotence; I found no correctness bugs.

## Testing

Baseline test command had already passed; I additionally ran the colocated tests/fm-backlog-handoff.test.sh (8 passing regression cases covering all five required scenarios) plus the two related secondmate suites (safety and lifecycle-e2e), all green. To demonstrate the intent as an end user experiences it, I built an E2E reproduction of the exact 2026-07-09 incident: the base-commit script moved only the `- [ ]` header and orphaned the indented body (## Intent / spec / ## Acceptance) onto the preceding item, while the fixed branch moved the entire block atomically to the secondmate backlog with neighbors untouched and the source clean. I also confirmed the retained safety behavior (in-flight refusal, unseeded-destination refusal) and idempotent re-run. This is a CLI/data-file change with no rendered UI surface, so evidence is the before/after backlog transcripts rather than screenshots. Working tree left clean.

<summary>Evidence: Base-commit (pre-fix) copy of fm-backlog-handoff.sh used for the buggy-vs-fixed contrast</summary>

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Hand already-identified, in-scope backlog items off from the main firstmate
# backlog to a secondmate's own home backlog. Use this when a secondmate is
# created (or whenever an existing queued item should become its domain's work)
# so the secondmate owns its queue from day one instead of the item staying
# stranded in the main backlog.
#
# Scope-matching is firstmate's JUDGMENT: you pass the task-id keys you have
# already judged in-scope for the secondmate. This script performs only the
# mechanical move - it removes each matched line from data/backlog.md under the
# active firstmate home and appends it, under the same section heading, to the
# secondmate home's data/backlog.md (home resolved from data/secondmates.md). It
# never changes a line's text, never writes into a project (it refuses a home
# that is not a firstmate home), and is idempotent: a key already present in the
# secondmate backlog is reported and skipped, so re-running converges. If any key
# matches neither backlog, nothing is moved. See AGENTS.md project management
# and task lifecycle.
# Usage: fm-backlog-handoff.sh <secondmate-id> <item-key>...
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
FM_ROOT="${FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE:-$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)}"
FM_HOME="${FM_HOME:-${FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE:-$FM_ROOT}}"
DATA="${FM_DATA_OVERRIDE:-$FM_HOME/data}"
REG="$DATA/secondmates.md"
MAIN_BACKLOG="$DATA/backlog.md"

[ $# -ge 2 ] || { echo "usage: fm-backlog-handoff.sh <secondmate-id> <item-key>..." >&2; exit 1; }
ID=$1
shift

secondmate_home() {
  local id=$1 line
  [ -f "$REG" ] || { echo "error: no secondmate registry at $REG" >&2; return 1; }
  line=$(grep -E "^- $id( |$)" "$REG" | tail -1 || true)
  [ -n "$line" ] || { echo "error: secondmate $id is not registered in $REG" >&2; return 1; }
  printf '%s\n' "$line" | sed -n 's/^[^(]*(home: \([^;)]*\);.*/\1/p'
}

path_is_ancestor_of() {
  local ancestor=$1 path=$2
  [ -n "$ancestor" ] || return 1
  [ -n "$path" ] || return 1
  [ "$ancestor" != "$path" ] || return 1
  case "$path" in
    "$ancestor"/*) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}

resolved_existing_dir() {
  local path=$1
  [ -d "$path" ] || { echo "error: firstmate home does not exist or is not a directory: $path" >&2; return 1; }
  cd "$path" && pwd -P
}

validate_operational_dirs() {
  local abs_home=$1 abs_active_home=$2 abs_root=$3 name dir abs_dir
  for name in data state config projects; do
    dir="$abs_home/$name"
    if [ -L "$dir" ] && [ ! -e "$dir" ]; then
      echo "error: secondmate $name directory must resolve inside the secondmate home: $dir" >&2
      return 1
    fi
    if [ -d "$dir" ]; then
      abs_dir=$(cd "$dir" && pwd -P)
    elif [ -e "$dir" ]; then
      echo "error: secondmate $name path is not a directory: $dir" >&2
      return 1
    else
      abs_dir="$abs_home/$name"
    fi
    if ! path_is_ancestor_of "$abs_home" "$abs_dir"; then
      echo "error: secondmate $name directory must resolve inside the secondmate home: $dir" >&2
      return 1
    fi
    if [ "$abs_dir" = "$abs_active_home" ] || path_is_ancestor_of "$abs_active_home" "$abs_dir"; then
      echo "error: secondmate $name directory cannot be inside the active firstmate home: $dir" >&2
      return 1
    fi
    if [ "$abs_dir" = "$abs_root" ] || path_is_ancestor_of "$abs_root" "$abs_dir"; then
      echo "error: secondmate $name directory cannot be inside the firstmate repo: $dir" >&2
      return 1
    fi
  done
}

validate_secondmate_home() {
  local id=$1 home=$2 abs_home abs_active_home abs_root marker_id
  abs_home=$(resolved_existing_dir "$home") || return 1
  abs_active_home=$(resolved_existing_dir "$FM_HOME")
  abs_root=$(resolved_existing_dir "$FM_ROOT")
  if [ "$abs_home" = "/" ]; then
    echo "error: secondmate home cannot be the filesystem root: $home" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if [ "$abs_home" = "$abs_active_home" ]; then
    echo "error: secondmate home cannot be the active firstmate home: $home" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if [ "$abs_home" = "$abs_root" ]; then
    echo "error: secondmate home cannot be the firstmate repo: $home" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if path_is_ancestor_of "$abs_active_home" "$abs_home"; then
    echo "error: secondmate home cannot be inside the active firstmate home: $home" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if path_is_ancestor_of "$abs_root" "$abs_home"; then
    echo "error: secondmate home cannot be inside the firstmate repo: $home" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if path_is_ancestor_of "$abs_home" "$abs_active_home"; then
    echo "error: secondmate home cannot be an ancestor of the active firstmate home: $home" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if path_is_ancestor_of "$abs_home" "$abs_root"; then
    echo "error: secondmate home cannot be an ancestor of the firstmate repo: $home" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  validate_operational_dirs "$abs_home" "$abs_active_home" "$abs_root" || return 1
  if [ ! -f "$abs_home/.fm-secondmate-home" ]; then
    echo "error: firstmate home $home is not a seeded secondmate home" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  marker_id=$(cat "$abs_home/.fm-secondmate-home" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ "$marker_id" != "$id" ]; then
    echo "error: firstmate home $home is marked for secondmate ${marker_id:-unknown}, expected $id" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -f "$abs_home/AGENTS.md" ]; then
    echo "error: $home is not a firstmate home (missing AGENTS.md)" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -d "$abs_home/bin" ]; then
    echo "error: $home is not a firstmate home (missing bin/)" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$abs_home"
}

validate_backlog_file() {
  local label=$1 path=$2
  if [ -L "$path" ]; then
    echo "error: $label must not be a symlink: $path" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -e "$path" ] && [ ! -f "$path" ]; then
    echo "error: $label is not a regular file: $path" >&2
    return 1
  fi
}

backlog_key_section() {
  local file=$1 key=$2
  [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
  awk -v key="$key" '
    BEGIN { section = "## Queued" }
    /^## / { section = $0; next }
    /^- \[[ x]\] / {
      rest = $0
      sub(/^- \[[ x]\] +/, "", rest)
      id = rest
      sub(/[ \t].*/, "", id)
      if (id == key) { print section; found = 1; exit }
    }
    END { exit found ? 0 : 1 }
  ' "$file"
}

RAW_HOME=$(secondmate_home "$ID") || exit 1
[ -n "$RAW_HOME" ] || { echo "error: secondmate $ID has no home in $REG" >&2; exit 1; }
SUB_HOME=$(validate_secondmate_home "$ID" "$RAW_HOME") || exit 1
SUB_BACKLOG="$SUB_HOME/data/backlog.md"
validate_backlog_file "main backlog" "$MAIN_BACKLOG" || exit 1
validate_backlog_file "secondmate backlog" "$SUB_BACKLOG" || exit 1

# Classify every key before changing anything: move-from-main, already-in-sub, or
# missing. Abort with no changes if any key matches neither backlog.
TO_MOVE=()
ALREADY=()
MISSING=()
IN_FLIGHT=()
for key in "$@"; do
  if backlog_key_section "$SUB_BACKLOG" "$key" >/dev/null; then
    ALREADY+=("$key")
  elif section=$(backlog_key_section "$MAIN_BACKLOG" "$key"); then
    if [ "$section" = "## In flight" ]; then
      IN_FLIGHT+=("$key")
    else
      TO_MOVE+=("$key")
    fi
  else
    MISSING+=("$key")
  fi
done

FAILED=0
if [ "${#IN_FLIGHT[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "error: refusing to hand off in-flight backlog items: ${IN_FLIGHT[*]}" >&2
  FAILED=1
fi
if [ "${#MISSING[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "error: no backlog item matched these keys in $MAIN_BACKLOG: ${MISSING[*]}" >&2
  FAILED=1
fi
if [ "$FAILED" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "       nothing was moved." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "${#TO_MOVE[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "nothing to move: ${ALREADY[*]:-no keys} already present in $SUB_BACKLOG"
  exit 0
fi

mkdir -p "$SUB_HOME/data"
SUB_EXISTED=0
if [ ! -f "$SUB_BACKLOG" ]; then
  printf '## In flight\n\n## Queued\n\n## Done\n' > "$SUB_BACKLOG"
else
  SUB_EXISTED=1
fi

MAIN_DIR=$(dirname "$MAIN_BACKLOG")
SUB_DIR=$(dirname "$SUB_BACKLOG")
KEYS_FILE=$(mktemp "$MAIN_DIR/.fm-handoff-keys.XXXXXX")
MOVED_FILE=$(mktemp "$MAIN_DIR/.fm-handoff-moved.XXXXXX")
KEPT_FILE=$(mktemp "$MAIN_DIR/.fm-handoff-kept.XXXXXX")
SUB_TMP=$(mktemp "$SUB_DIR/.fm-handoff-sub.XXXXXX")
MAIN_BAK=$(mktemp "$MAIN_DIR/.fm-handoff-main-bak.XXXXXX")
SUB_BAK=$(mktemp "$SUB_DIR/.fm-handoff-sub-bak.XXXXXX")
CHANGES_STARTED=0
COMMITTED=0
cleanup() {
  if [ "$CHANGES_STARTED" -eq 1 ] && [ "$COMMITTED" -eq 0 ]; then
    cp "$MAIN_BAK" "$MAIN_BACKLOG" 2>/dev/null || true
    if [ "$SUB_EXISTED" -eq 1 ]; then
      cp "$SUB_BAK" "$SUB_BACKLOG" 2>/dev/null || true
    else
      rm -f "$SUB_BACKLOG"
    fi
  fi
  rm -f "$KEYS_FILE" "$MOVED_FILE" "$KEPT_FILE" "$SUB_TMP" "$MAIN_BAK" "$SUB_BAK"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
printf '%s\n' "${TO_MOVE[@]}" > "$KEYS_FILE"
cp "$MAIN_BACKLOG" "$MAIN_BAK"
if [ "$SUB_EXISTED" -eq 1 ]; then
  cp "$SUB_BACKLOG" "$SUB_BAK"
fi

# Pass 1: drop the matched lines from the main backlog, capturing each removed
# line tagged with the "## " section heading it lived under.
: > "$MOVED_FILE"
awk -v keysfile="$KEYS_FILE" -v movedfile="$MOVED_FILE" '
  BEGIN {
    while ((getline k < keysfile) > 0) { if (k != "") want[k] = 1 }
    section = "## Queued"
  }
  /^## / { section = $0; print; next }
  /^- \[[ x]\] / {
    rest = $0
    sub(/^- \[[ x]\] +/, "", rest)
    id = rest
    sub(/[ \t].*/, "", id)
    if (id in want) { print section "\t" $0 > movedfile; next }
  }
  { print }
' "$MAIN_BACKLOG" > "$KEPT_FILE"

# Pass 2: insert each moved line at the end of its section in the sub backlog,
# creating the section heading if the sub backlog lacks it.
awk -v movedfile="$MOVED_FILE" '
  function flush(sec) {
    if (sec != "" && (sec in items) && !(sec in flushed)) {
      printf "%s", items[sec]
      flushed[sec] = 1
    }
  }
  BEGIN {
    nsec = 0
    while ((getline rec < movedfile) > 0) {
      tab = index(rec, "\t")
      if (tab == 0) continue
      sec = substr(rec, 1, tab - 1)
      line = substr(rec, tab + 1)
      if (!(sec in items)) { order[++nsec] = sec }
      items[sec] = items[sec] line "\n"
    }
    cur = ""
  }
  /^## / { flush(cur); cur = $0; print; next }
  { print }
  END {
    flush(cur)
    for (i = 1; i <= nsec; i++) {
      s = order[i]
      if (!(s in flushed)) {
        print ""
        print s
        printf "%s", items[s]
        flushed[s] = 1
      }
    }
  }
' "$SUB_BACKLOG" > "$SUB_TMP"

CHANGES_STARTED=1
mv "$SUB_TMP" "$SUB_BACKLOG"
mv "$KEPT_FILE" "$MAIN_BACKLOG"
COMMITTED=1

echo "handed off ${#TO_MOVE[@]} item(s) to $ID: ${TO_MOVE[*]}"
echo "  into $SUB_BACKLOG"
if [ "${#ALREADY[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "  already present (skipped): ${ALREADY[*]}"
fi
```

title: feat(herdr): make Herdr lab lifecycle safety deterministic for briefs
body:
## Intent

Make Herdr safety deterministic for every future firstmate brief, closing a class of fleet-kill incidents where an ambient 'herdr server stop' or HERDR_SESSION-only cleanup in a crew's teardown hit the running server's live 'default' session. Three deliverables: (1) A first-class helper bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh that provisions an isolated, never-'default' named lab session, runs task commands through it with a mandatory trailing '--session <name>' appended on every call, and tears down through a guard that re-checks refuse-default immediately before each destructive stop/delete and records+verifies the live default session as a before/after tripwire. It is now the single owner of the guard logic previously living inline in tests/herdr-test-safety.sh; that test file was refactored to source the helper (hence its large line reduction) rather than keep a duplicate copy - one owner for the guard, per the brief. (2) bin/fm-brief.sh gained a --herdr-lab flag that emits the full Herdr-isolation HARD SAFETY CONTRACT into the scaffolded brief (isolated never-default lab session via the helper, trailing --session on every call, teardown only via the guarded helper, an explicit forbidden-command list including any server-global operation, and a before/after fleet-state tripwire). Design decision, stated deliberately: the trigger is an EXPLICIT flag rather than auto-detection, because the {TASK} text is filled in after scaffolding and the caller-supplied repo string cannot reliably identify the firstmate repo, so reliable auto-detection is impossible. To ensure the contract cannot silently fail to fire, every brief scaffolded WITHOUT the flag carries a loud NOT-ENABLED hard-safety gate declaration instructing the agent to stop and regenerate with --herdr-lab if the task will drive Herdr lifecycle behavior. --herdr-lab is rejected for secondmate briefs. (3) Colocated shellcheck-clean tests in tests/ (tests/fm-herdr-lab.test.sh and additions to tests/fm-brief.test.sh). Verified constraint preserved throughout: on Herdr 0.7.3 the API socket is NOT env-relocatable (HERDR_CONFIG_PATH, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, HOME all leave the client on ~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock), so a named non-'default' session with per-call --session scoping is the only viable local isolation. All firstmate repo-style conventions apply (one sentence per line in prose, plain dash not em-dash, shellcheck-clean bin scripts, colocated tests).

## What Changed

- Added `bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh`, a first-class helper that provisions an isolated, never-`default` named lab session, runs task commands through it with a mandatory trailing `--session <name>` appended on every call, and tears down through a guard that re-checks refuse-default before each destructive stop/delete and records/verifies the live `default` session as a before/after tripwire; `tests/herdr-test-safety.sh` was refactored to source this single owner of the guard logic instead of keeping a duplicate copy.
- Added a `--herdr-lab` flag to `bin/fm-brief.sh` that emits the full Herdr-isolation HARD SAFETY CONTRACT into the scaffolded brief; briefs scaffolded without the flag carry a loud NOT-ENABLED gate instructing regeneration, and the flag is rejected for secondmate briefs.
- Added colocated tests (`tests/fm-herdr-lab.test.sh` plus new `--herdr-lab` cases in `tests/fm-brief.test.sh`) and documented the helper and flag across `AGENTS.md`, `docs/herdr-backend.md`, and `docs/scripts.md`; several herdr e2e/smoke suites were updated to call the shared prepare helper.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: A well-bounded, additive safety helper with defensive fail-closed guards and thorough colocated tests; the material issues were already found and fixed across prior review rounds, and this fresh full pass surfaced no new substantiated defect.

## Testing

The configured full e2e suite already passed as baseline; I additionally ran the two directly-relevant suites (tests/fm-herdr-lab.test.sh and tests/fm-brief.test.sh, all green), rendered the actual scaffolded briefs showing the HARD SAFETY CONTRACT with --herdr-lab and the loud NOT-ENABLED gate without it plus the secondmate rejection, and drove the new helper against the real running herdr 0.7.3 where a complete provision/scoped-run/guarded-teardown cycle on an isolated fm-lab- session left the live default session byte-identical before and after while every fleet-kill vector refused, confirming the deterministic Herdr isolation the change set out to deliver; cleanup left no stray sessions, no tripwire state, and a clean working tree. I did not run shellcheck because static-analysis tools are out of scope for this testing step.

title: fix: reconcile existing AGENTS.md safely
body:
## Intent

Make bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh idempotently inject its canonical '## Maintaining this file' self-governance section into an EXISTING AGENTS.md that lacks it. Before, the script only appended that section on skeleton create or CLAUDE.md promotion, so a project that already had an AGENTS.md exited 'unchanged' without the section, forcing hand-copying during a rollout across existing projects (found during the 2026-07-09 preamble rollout).

Key decisions/tradeoffs: (1) Reused the script's already-idempotent ensure_maintenance_section helper rather than forking a second copy of the wording - the canonical section text stays defined exactly once in write_maintenance_section (firstmate 'one-owner rule'). (2) Called ensure_maintenance_section on the two existing-AGENTS.md success paths and added a MAINT_INJECTED global so the report distinguishes 'updated' (section added) from 'unchanged'; a re-run and an already-complete file stay byte-identical. (3) Skeleton-create and CLAUDE.md-promotion output/behavior are intentionally unchanged (regression-covered).

Also fixes GitHub issue #389 in the same PR (small and coherent): the script used to emit a CLAUDE.md symlink with the uppercase literal target 'AGENTS.md' even when the real on-disk file was lowercase agents.md, which dangles on a case-sensitive filesystem. I added an early guard that reads the real directory entries (works on both case-insensitive and case-sensitive filesystems) and refuses with a 'conflict:' message + non-zero exit, creating no symlink, when the real memory file is a case-variant of AGENTS.md. I deliberately chose conflict-and-refuse over auto-renaming, matching the script's existing conflict-detection style and firstmate's never-silently-do-something-fragile safety philosophy; the issue is referenced as 'fixes #389' so it closes on merge.

Tests are colocated by extending tests/fm-ensure-agents-md.test.sh (4 new cases + 3 preserved regressions), shellcheck is clean across bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh tests/*.sh, and docs/architecture.md and docs/scripts.md were updated to match. This is a firstmate-repo change made under the firstmate-coding-guidelines (one-sentence-per-line Markdown, plain dash, no agent co-author).

## What Changed

- Idempotently inject the canonical `## Maintaining this file` section into existing `AGENTS.md` files, preserve LF or CRLF formatting, and report when the file was updated.
- Refuse case-variant agent-memory filenames before creating a `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md` symlink that would break on case-sensitive filesystems.
- Document the reconciliation behavior and add regression coverage for injection, idempotency, CRLF preservation, and case-variant conflicts.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Captain, the change is tightly scoped and the previously identified CRLF and dangling-symlink risks are addressed without introducing a substantiated material regression.

## Testing

The supplied full-suite baseline had already succeeded; focused regression testing and a manual CLI transcript confirmed existing-file injection and updated reporting, byte-identical reruns, fail-closed lowercase `agents.md` handling without a symlink, and unchanged skeleton/promotion behavior versus the base commit. The worktree remained clean.

title: fix(tmux): disambiguate numeric session names when creating task windows
body:
## Intent Fix a live-hit bug in firstmate's own tmux backend adapter (bin/backends/tmux.sh): fm_backend_tmux_create_task passed a bare session name to tmux's -t target in both its duplicate-check (list-windows) and its new-window create call. When the session name is purely numeric (e.g. "0", tmux's own session-name default), tmux's target-window resolution for new-window prefers a window-INDEX match in the current session over a session-NAME match, and index 0 is always occupied by that session's initial window - so a spawn against a numeric-named session failed with the exact live error "create window failed: index 0 in use" even though the session name itself was free. This blocked a real secondmate launch on 2026-07-09 and forced a manual session-rename workaround. Empirically confirmed live (real tmux 3.4, private socket) that appending a trailing colon ("$ses:") forces session-name interpretation and fixes it; a leading "=$ses" was also tried and still collided, so the colon form is the deliberate, verified fix - not a guess. Scope, per the task brief: (1) apply the trailing-colon fix at fm_backend_tmux_create_task's tmux calls, (2) audit the rest of bin/backends/tmux.sh and other backend files for the same bare-session-name ambiguity (audited; no other call site passes a bare session name to -t), (3) add a regression test extending the existing real-tmux smoke suite (tests/fm-backend-tmux-smoke.test.sh) reproducing the exact bug with a session literally named "0" whose window index 0 is occupied, verified empirically to fail on the pre-fix code and pass on the fix, (4) shellcheck-clean. This is firstmate's own shared template repo, so the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill's repo style rules apply. The change is deliberately minimal and surgical: 2 tmux -t targets changed in bin/backends/tmux.sh plus one new self-contained test block, plus doc updates (CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/tmux-backend.md) - no refactor of unrelated code. Captain-authorized scope note: an earlier run of this same intent had its test step auto-fix an UNRELATED pre-existing flaky test in bin/fm-wake-lib.sh (PID-identity derivation broken by WSL2 clock drift) - that fix duplicates already-open upstream PR #392 by a different author and is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this PR; the captain decided to drop it and keep this PR minimal, and this branch has been corrected to exclude it (only the tmux fix commit plus its docs commit remain). If the test step hits that same unrelated flake again, do not re-patch fm-wake-lib.sh into this branch - treat it as a known pre-existing environment flake with an already-open upstream fix (PR #392) and respond to the gate accordingly to keep this PR scoped to the tmux fix only. Push target: the gate is now configured with --fork-url so it pushes fm/fm-spawn-numeric-session to the fork remote (mikaellinares87-code/firstmate, captain-authorized, shared with a sibling task) and opens the PR cross-repo against kunchenguid/firstmate automatically. ## What Changed - `fm_backend_tmux_create_task` in `bin/backends/tmux.sh` now appends a trailing colon to its `-t` targets (`"$ses:"`) in both the duplicate-check `list-windows` call and the `new-window` call, forcing tmux to resolve the target as a session name. Previously a purely numeric session name (e.g. `"0"`, tmux's own default) was resolved as a window index — which is always occupied by the session's initial window — so spawning a task failed with `create window failed: index 0 in use` even though the session name was valid. The trailing-colon form was verified live on tmux 3.4; a leading `=$ses` was also tried and still collided. - Adds a regression check to the real-tmux smoke suite (`tests/fm-backend-tmux-smoke.test.sh`) that reproduces the exact collision — a session literally named `"0"` whose window index 0 is occupied — confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code and pass with the fix. - Documents the root cause, the verified fix, and the audit result (no other call site in the tmux backend passes a bare session name to `-t` for task creation) in `docs/tmux-backend.md`, and updates the test-index line in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A two-line, empirically verified fix using the standard tmux session-disambiguation idiom, with a self-contained leak-safe regression test, accurate docs, no impact on the old-vs-new conformance byte-diff (both builds share the current backends dir), and a substantiated audit that no other call site is affected. ## Testing Ran the real-tmux smoke suite on the fixed code (all 8 checks pass, including the new numeric-session regression check), replayed the live bug end-to-end on real tmux 3.4 showing the pre-fix backend failing with the exact `create window failed: index 0 in use` error and the fixed backend succeeding, and confirmed the new regression test fails on pre-fix code and passes on the fix; the only failure encountered was a pre-existing, unrelated capture-bounds timing flake that passed on retry and in the baseline full-suite run.

title: feat(herdr): opt-in pane-split layout for crewmate spawns
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in pane-split layout mode to the herdr runtime backend: crewmate/scout agents can spawn as split panes beside the spawning firstmate instead of each getting its own tab.

- **Toggle:** local, gitignored `config/herdr-layout` (`split` on; absent or `tabs` keeps today's tab-per-task behavior byte-for-byte), with an `FM_HERDR_LAYOUT` env override. Herdr-only; tmux/zellij/orca/cmux untouched.
- **Layout:** the first crewmate splits the spawner's pane left/right (spawner keeps the left half); each subsequent crewmate stacks in the right column with `--direction down`, newest at the bottom, `--ratio 0.5`.
- **Cap/overflow:** `FM_HERDR_SPLIT_MAX` (default 3) caps the right-column stack; beyond it spawns overflow to the existing tab path. A layout constraint never refuses a spawn.
- **No anchor:** when firstmate is not itself running in a herdr pane of the target session (`HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID`), the spawn falls back to tab mode with a one-line stderr notice.
- **Identity/husk at pane granularity:** split panes are labeled `fm-<id>` via `pane rename`; duplicate/husk detection runs on pane labels with the same conservative dead/no-agent classification and create-before-close ordering as the tab husk path. Detection is cross-layout: each spawn path also scans the other scope for the same `fm-<id>` label, so a task respawned in the other layout (cap overflow, no-anchor fallback, or a config toggle) still finds its earlier incarnation's live duplicate or husk.
- **Scope:** crewmate/scout only; `--secondmate` spawns keep their own workspace in tab mode. All supervision already addresses `session:pane_id` targets from meta, so no supervision path assumed one-tab-per-agent.

## Verification

- Empirically verified against real herdr 0.7.2 / protocol 16 (NixOS Linux x86_64) in an isolated `fm-lab-*` session via `bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh`; evidence recorded in `docs/herdr-backend.md` "Pane-split layout mode" (split placement/geometry, labeling, cap overflow + override, both no-anchor paths, husk close-and-replace, live-duplicate refusal, middle-pane re-tile, spawner-tab survival).
- New fake-CLI unit tests in `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh` (`make_herdr_splitfake` + `test_layout_*`/`test_split_*`) covering layout resolution, cap overflow at the cap and via override, no-anchor fallback, cross-scope duplicate/husk handling, and create-before-close ordering.
- `shellcheck bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh tests/*.sh` clean.
- Also fixes a NixOS portability bug in the pre-existing herdr and zellij missing-binary version-check tests (their restricted `PATH` lacked `bash`); the fix links the real `bash` into the private fakebin so the restricted `PATH` stays free of the binary under test on any host layout.

Validated through the no-mistakes pipeline (review with fix round, tests, docs, lint all green); pushed via fork because this account has no upstream push access.
