title: fix(supervision): close the watcher arm/guard identity-check race
body:
## Intent Fix a watcher-arm/guard identity-check race that made the primary turn-end guard (and the pull-based fm-guard) false-alarm 'no live watcher holds this home lock' seconds to tens of seconds after a healthy arm, costing a verification round-trip almost every turn end. Root cause 1: the watcher process claims the singleton lock's pid, then writes its home/watcher-path/identity trio as three separate non-atomic steps before its first liveness-beacon touch, so a guard sampled in that window sees a live pid but an incomplete identity and reports unhealthy even though the watcher is genuinely, successfully starting. Two prior fixes on other branches were tried and discarded before this one - deliberately not ported: one only self-heals a wedged incumbent watcher (a different problem); the other added a single fixed 2-second sleep-and-recheck in the guard, which failed because real observed race gaps ran 6-29 seconds, well past a fixed short window. Fix for root cause 1: the shared wake library gained a second, independent liveness signal - a live, identity-matched marker that the arm helper writes the instant it starts and refreshes on every polling-loop iteration, always cleared on exit via a trap. It has its own bounded grace window (default 30s) so a wedged or dead arm still alarms - this is liveness-driven via continuous refresh, not a fixed sleep. Both guard scripts now accept that in-progress-arm signal as a fallback when the identity-matched watcher-healthy check fails. Root cause 2, found via fresh live evidence and a deeper investigation mid-session: the guard also false-fired on a watcher that had been healthy for about 15 minutes with no arm involved at all. My first hypothesis (a transient subprocess fork failure in the identity check, addressed with a bounded retry) was superseded by a deeper, confirmed measurement: on this host, /proc's own boot-time reference (btime) measurably drifts forward under continuous wall-clock sampling (about 1 second per 20 seconds of wall time, confirmed via two direct /proc samples and a same-pid lstart shift over the same window), even though the system clock itself reports as synchronized. Since the previous identity check compared ps's lstart wall-clock string, this silently walked a live, never-restarted process's own recorded identity forward until it stopped matching a fresh read - a persistent, monotonically-growing mismatch, not a transient hiccup a retry can fix. Fix for root cause 2: the identity comparison now reads /proc//stat's starttime field (clock ticks since boot, set once at process creation by the kernel and never recomputed from wall time on a later read) when /proc is available, falling back to the original lstart+command form only on hosts without /proc (macOS). Audited every start-time/lstart read across the codebase and confirmed this was the sole hazard - no other process-identity comparison in the repo depends on wall-clock time. Kept the bounded empty-read retry as a narrower, still-valid guard against a generic subprocess-fork hiccup (distinct from the drift bug), since it never masks a genuine identity mismatch, only a failed/empty subprocess invocation. Regression tests added and passing: hermetic marker tests in the turn-end-guard suite (silent during a healthy in-progress arm with no watch lock yet; blocks on a dead arm-marker pid; blocks on a stale/wedged arm marker past grace); watcher-lock suite tests for guard arm-in-progress suppression and wedged-arm warning, identity-retry-recovers and identity-retry-still-fails-when-persistent, a real end-to-end repro spawning the actual arm helper against a deliberately slow watcher stub sampling the turn-end guard mid-startup (the literal reproduction recipe from the original bug report), a direct stability proof that the new /proc-based starttime primitive does not drift across reads of the same live pid, and a simulated-shifted-btime-read test using a fake ps whose lstart output deliberately drifts a full minute per call, confirming the fix ignores it once /proc is available. Both full suites (36 and 29 assertions respectively) are green; 7 other adjacent test suites were also verified green with no regressions both before and after the rework. One unrelated pre-existing test failure in the session-start suite was confirmed present on the unmodified baseline before any of these changes, so it is out of scope here. shellcheck -x is clean on every changed script. Also updated the turn-end-guard doc to document both the new arm-in-progress fallback and the /proc-based identity mechanism, since it previously stated the lstart-based watcher-healthy check as the sole and unconditional predicate. ## What Changed - Added a second, independent liveness signal to the shared wake library (`bin/fm-wake-lib.sh`): the arm helper (`bin/fm-watch-arm.sh`) now writes an identity-matched in-progress marker the instant it starts, refreshes it on every polling-loop iteration, and clears it on exit via a trap, with its own bounded grace window (default 30s) so a wedged or dead arm still alarms; both `bin/fm-guard.sh` and `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh` accept this arm-in-progress marker as a fallback when the identity-matched watcher-healthy check fails. - Switched process-identity comparison from `ps` lstart wall-clock strings to `/proc//stat` starttime ticks when `/proc` is available, falling back to lstart+command only on hosts without `/proc`; this eliminates a persistent, monotonically-growing false-mismatch caused by btime drift walking a live process's recorded identity forward, and keeps the bounded empty-read retry as a narrower guard against subprocess-fork hiccups. - Added regression coverage (`tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh`, `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh`) for arm-in-progress suppression, dead/wedged arm-marker alarms, an end-to-end slow-watcher startup-race repro, starttime stability across reads, and a simulated btime-drift case; hardened the dispatch-select and session-start suites against jq path, system node, and harness env leaks; and documented the new arm-in-progress fallback and `/proc`-based identity mechanism (`docs/turnend-guard.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `AGENTS.md`). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A well-bounded, heavily-commented and test-backed supervision-race fix whose writers/readers stay consistent and whose new signal is best-effort with a bounded grace window; the only observations are cosmetic or a self-healing one-time rollout artifact. ## Testing Baseline ran the full e2e suite green; on top of that I exercised the two core regression suites and the two hardened suites for this change, plus seven adjacent supervision suites, all green with no regressions. The assertions are behavioral, not just unit checks: the turn-end-guard repro spawns the real fm-watch-arm.sh against a deliberately slow watcher stub and samples the guard mid-startup, proving the guard no longer false-alarms during a healthy arm (root cause 1), while dead/wedged arm markers still alarm past their grace window; and dedicated tests prove the new /proc-starttime identity primitive is stable across reads while ignoring a simulated btime-drifting ps lstart (root cause 2). This is a supervision/CLI change with no UI surface, so evidence is CLI test transcripts rather than screenshots.
Evidence: Core regression suite transcript (fm-turnend-guard + fm-watcher-lock, all assertions green) ```text ======== tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh ======== ok - fm_supervision_unhealthy: false with no state/*.meta at all ok - fm_supervision_unhealthy: true with in-flight task and no beacon ever ok - fm_supervision_unhealthy: true with in-flight task and a beacon far outside the grace window ok - fm_supervision_unhealthy: false with in-flight task and a fresh beacon ok - fm_supervision_status: FM_SUP_QUEUE_PENDING tracks state/.wake-queue ok - fm-turnend-guard: silent no-op with nothing in flight ok - fm-turnend-guard: blocks when a fresh beacon has no live watcher lock ok - fm-turnend-guard: blocks on a dead watcher lock even when the beacon is fresh ok - fm-turnend-guard: silent no-op with a live watcher lock and fresh beacon ok - fm-turnend-guard: silent no-op during a healthy in-progress arm with no watch lock yet ok - fm-turnend-guard: blocks when the arm marker's pid is dead (no fail-open on a dead arm) ok - fm-turnend-guard: blocks on a wedged arm (live pid, marker stale past grace) ok - fm-turnend-guard: blocks on a live watcher lock with an ancient beacon ok - fm-turnend-guard: blocks with the exact required reason in the primary when unhealthy ok - fm-turnend-guard: blocks from active FM_HOME state, not only repo-root state ok - fm-turnend-guard: X-mode repair reason sources the cadence config ok - fm-turnend-guard: ignores stale repo-root state when FM_HOME is set ok - fm-turnend-guard: uses FM_STATE_OVERRIDE ahead of FM_HOME/state ok - fm-turnend-guard: stop_hook_active=true always allows the stop (never blocks twice in one turn) ok - fm-turnend-guard: inert in a secondmate home (.fm-secondmate-home marker present) even when unhealthy ok - fm-turnend-guard: inert in a crewmate/scout task worktree (linked git worktree) even when unhealthy ok - fm-turnend-guard: fails open (never blocks) when jq is missing ok - fm-turnend-guard: silent no-op on empty stdin ok - fm-turnend-guard: runs well under the generous timing margin (0s) ok - fm-turnend-guard-grok: forces one same-session resume when the shared predicate blocks ok - .codex/hooks.json: Stop hook uses hook process root when payload cwd is outside ok - .codex/hooks.json: Stop hook ignores nested git root guard scripts ok - .opencode primary plugin: session.idle forces one follow-up through the shared guard ok - .opencode primary plugin: guard path is anchored to worktree, not directory ok - .pi primary extension: agent_settled forces one follow-up through the shared guard ok - .pi primary extension: no-tool and multi-tool runs each inject exactly one guard follow-up ok - .pi primary extension: delivery failure resets the logical-run latch ok - .grok primary hook: Stop hook invokes the grok adapter -- exit 0 -- ======== tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh ======== ok - simultaneous watcher starts leave exactly one live process ok - fm_pid_identity is locale-invariant across LC_ALL/LC_TIME ok - fm_pid_starttime_ticks is stable across reads of an unchanged live pid ok - fm_pid_identity ignores a drifting ps lstart once /proc is available (simulated btime-drift regression) ok - killed watcher stale lock is reclaimed ok - live watcher lock with stale heartbeat is actionable ok - guard banner leads when down with pending wakes (re-arm-after-drain) and stays silent when fresh ok - guard: silent with no fresh watcher beacon while a live in-progress arm marker exists ok - guard: still warns when the arm marker names a dead pid ok - fm_watcher_lock_matches_pid retries a transient ps failure and still confirms identity ok - fm_watcher_lock_matches_pid still fails (bounded retry) when ps never recovers ok - fm-turnend-guard: silent during a real fm-watch-arm.sh startup race (repro: sampled before the watch lock exists) ok - concurrent fm_lock_try_acquire yields exactly one winner ok - dead-pid stale lock is reclaimed by a single acquirer ok - concurrent stale-lock steal yields exactly one winner ok - live steal mutex is not reclaimed ok - live-held lock is not stolen ok - empty mid-acquire lock keeps a minimum grace ok - late original claimant cannot claim a recreated lock ok - paused mid-acquire claimant backs off to active stealer ok - watch restart refuses to signal a reused pid ok - watch restart reports a healthy peer without attaching to it ok - watcher self-evicts when the lock pid no longer names it ok - arm attaches to a live fresh watcher and exits only when that cycle ends ok - arm starts+confirms a fresh watcher on a clean lock and self-heals a dead-pid lock (never healthy off a dead pid) ok - arm cleans child watcher and temp output on HUP ok - arm propagates an immediate watcher wake before confirmation ok - arm attaches to a peer watcher after child stands down and exits when peer dies watcher: lock held by live pid 2857528 but heartbeat is stale for 837007503s (>300s); inspect or stop that watcher before re-arming. ok - arm reports FAILED and exits non-zero when no fresh watcher can be confirmed -- exit 0 -- ```
Evidence: Race-fix highlight assertions (arm-in-progress silence, dead/wedged arm alarm, /proc starttime stability vs lstart drift) ok - fm-turnend-guard: blocks on a wedged arm (live pid, marker stale past grace) ok - fm_pid_starttime_ticks is stable across reads of an unchanged live pid ok - fm_pid_identity ignores a drifting ps lstart once /proc is available (simulated btime-drift regression) ok - guard: silent with no fresh watcher beacon while a live in-progress arm marker exists ok - guard: still warns when the arm marker names a dead pid ok - fm_watcher_lock_matches_pid retries a transient ps failure and still confirms identity ok - fm_watcher_lock_matches_pid still fails (bounded retry) when ps never recovers ok - fm-turnend-guard: silent during a real fm-watch-arm.sh startup race (repro: sampled before the watch lock exists) ```text ok - fm-turnend-guard: blocks on a wedged arm (live pid, marker stale past grace) ok - fm_pid_starttime_ticks is stable across reads of an unchanged live pid ok - fm_pid_identity ignores a drifting ps lstart once /proc is available (simulated btime-drift regression) ok - guard: silent with no fresh watcher beacon while a live in-progress arm marker exists ok - guard: still warns when the arm marker names a dead pid ok - fm_watcher_lock_matches_pid retries a transient ps failure and still confirms identity ok - fm_watcher_lock_matches_pid still fails (bounded retry) when ps never recovers ok - fm-turnend-guard: silent during a real fm-watch-arm.sh startup race (repro: sampled before the watch lock exists) ok - arm starts+confirms a fresh watcher on a clean lock and self-heals a dead-pid lock (never healthy off a dead pid) ```

title: feat: support project-less secondmate homes

## Intent The developer wanted firstmate to support deliberately project-less secondmate homes, using a clear explicit signal such as `--no-projects`, so firstmate-repo domains need no placeholder clone. title: feat(harness): add verified GitHub Copilot CLI adapter
body:
## Summary

Adds GitHub Copilot CLI (`copilot`) as a verified crewmate/secondmate harness adapter, validated end-to-end through the no-mistakes gate.

## Changes

- New `copilot` harness adapter: launch, autonomy flag, busy-pane signature, exit/interrupt, resume, folder-trust dialog handling, and `agentStop` turn-end hook, documented in `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md`.
- `bin/fm-spawn.sh`: copilot launch template and worktree-resident turn-end hook install (`.github/hooks/fm-turn-end.<task-id>.json`, per-task filename to avoid clobber, `shell_quote`/`json_escape`-safe command).
- `bin/fm-lock.sh`: fixed `INTERP_RE` interpreter-scan regex to include `MainThread` (copilot's child process reports `comm=MainThread`, not `node`/`python`), restoring correct lock detection for copilot-backed tasks.
- `bin/fm-harness.sh`: `COPILOT_CLI=1` env-marker detection.
- New tests in `tests/fm-copilot-harness.test.sh` covering hook install/preservation, quoting safety, model/effort meta threading, harness detection, and lock-detection regressions.
- Docs updated across `AGENTS.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/orca-backend.md`, `docs/tmux-backend.md`, `README.md`.

## Validation

Passed the full no-mistakes gate (review, test, document, lint) across two runs, including:
- A pipeline-surfaced and pipeline-fixed args-scan regression (harness-scan narrowed to interpreter processes only), which itself broke copilot lock detection and was corrected.
- A pipeline-surfaced and pipeline-fixed hook-safety review round (per-task hook filename instead of a shared fixed name, safe shell/JSON quoting) — empirically verified against the installed copilot CLI's native hook loader (confirmed it scans all files under `.github/hooks/`, not a fixed name).
- Test-flakiness fixes for pre-existing PATH-shadowing and timing issues, unrelated to this feature but surfaced by the same test run.

## Testing

```sh
bash tests/fm-copilot-harness.test.sh
shellcheck bin/fm-spawn.sh bin/fm-lock.sh
```

title: feat(daemon): add liveness beacon and down-detection for the afk daemon
body:
## Intent

Management-audit finding B4/L2 ("nothing owns the daemon"): while state/.afk is set, the away-mode supervise daemon owns supervision, but nothing verified it was alive, so a silent daemon death was classified benign without any check. Goal: give the daemon its own liveness beacon and a down-detection check, mirroring the existing watcher idiom (the watcher touches state/.last-watcher-beat every poll and fm-guard.sh alarms when it goes stale) rather than inventing a new mechanism.

Decisions and tradeoffs made: (1) New shared bin/fm-daemon-lib.sh owns the daemon lock/beacon liveness contract in one place (one-owner rule) - it absorbed the lock-owner/pid-match helpers that were previously duplicated inline in fm-afk-start.sh, so fm-afk-start.sh now sources them instead of redefining them. (2) The daemon touches state/.last-daemon-beat at startup (before the first backoff sleep, so a just-started daemon reads alive immediately) and at the top of every main-loop cycle (so it stays fresh through the pane-gone and crash-backoff branches), and clears it on clean shutdown so a stopped daemon reads gone at once instead of aging out of grace. (3) fm_daemon_down is deliberately NOT gated on in-flight task count: away mode keeps the daemon armed for X mode and late crew reports even with an empty queue, so a dead daemon under afk is a fault regardless. (4) Grace defaults to FM_GUARD_GRACE then 300, matching fm-guard.sh. (5) Two alarm points added, both using the shared predicate: fm-guard.sh prints a bordered banner on the next fleet action, and the session-start AFK digest reports daemon-down - covering both the guard path and the recovery path the brief named, and distinguishing "process gone" from "beacon stale/wedged". Read-only sessions are told to report the lapse, not repair it.

Doc changes are minimal and respect one-owner: two lines added to the afk skill's reliability-properties section and one line to AGENTS.md's state-file index for the new beacon; the detection contract itself lives in the library and skill, not duplicated into AGENTS.md. Regression test: six new tests in tests/fm-daemon.test.sh, including one that proves fm-guard.sh (which was silent on base) now alarms when .afk is set and the daemon is dead.

## What Changed

- Added `bin/fm-daemon-lib.sh` as the single owner of the away-mode daemon's lock/beacon liveness contract, absorbing the lock-owner and pid-match helpers previously duplicated inline in `bin/fm-afk-start.sh` (which now sources them). The daemon touches `state/.last-daemon-beat` at startup and at the top of every main-loop cycle, and clears it on clean shutdown so a stopped daemon reads gone immediately rather than aging out of grace.
- Wired the shared `fm_daemon_down` predicate into two alarm points: `bin/fm-guard.sh` prints a bordered banner on the next fleet action, and the `bin/fm-session-start.sh` AFK digest reports daemon-down, distinguishing "process gone" from a stale/wedged beacon; the session-start repair line is gated so read-only sessions are told to report the lapse rather than repair it. Down-detection is intentionally not gated on in-flight task count, since away mode keeps the daemon armed for X mode and late crew reports even with an empty queue.
- Added `tests/fm-daemon.test.sh` covering the beacon and down-detection, including a regression proving `fm-guard.sh` now alarms when `state/.afk` is set and the daemon is dead. Updated the afk skill, AGENTS.md state-file index, and supporting docs to reference the new beacon.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Well-bounded change that mirrors the existing, proven watcher-beacon idiom, faithfully extracts previously-inline helpers, is covered by six new tests, and has both prior-round findings already resolved.

## Testing

Completed 1 recorded test check.

- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 error across 4 runs (1h23m22s)

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

✅ No issues found.

</details>

</details>

<details>
<summary>⚠️ **Review** - 1 info</summary>

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-session-start.sh:292` - The session-start AFK subsection prints the repair instruction 'Load /afk and restart the daemon (bin/fm-afk-start.sh)' unconditionally when the daemon is down, without checking READ_ONLY. This contradicts the stated design ('read-only sessions are told to report the lapse, not repair it') that the author correctly implemented in fm-guard.sh (which gates the equivalent line on READ_ONLY), and it directly conflicts with the very next 'NEXT STEP' block that tells a read-only session 'do not arm, drain, spawn, steer, merge, or repair fleet state from here.' A read-only session-start with .afk set and a dead daemon emits contradictory guidance. Gate the repair line on READ_ONLY, mirroring fm-guard.sh's read-only banner text.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-daemon-lib.sh:112` - FM_DAEMON_PID is computed in fm_daemon_status and carries a shellcheck-disable comment claiming it is 'read by callers (fm-guard.sh) after this returns', but no caller (fm-guard.sh, fm-session-start.sh, or the tests) actually reads it. If any fleet action runs fm-guard.sh (or session start reads the AFK digest) in that sub-second-to-seconds window, fm_daemon_down returns true with FM_DAEMON_ALIVE=false and the banner false-alarms 'its process is gone'. title: feat(pr-check): make the per-PR poll comment-aware
body:
## What

The per-PR poll generated by `bin/fm-pr-check.sh` (`state/<id>.check.sh`) woke firstmate only when the PR merged. New review activity - an AI or human review, a PR issue comment, an inline review comment - sat unnoticed until someone happened to look.

This extends the poll so new review activity also wakes firstmate, within one poll cycle, while preserving the check contract (one line of stdout only when firstmate should wake, silence otherwise, bounded runtime).

## Behavior

- Each poll counts reviews + comments via `gh pr view --json reviews,comments` (gh's built-in jq), consistent with the existing `gh pr view --json` usage in the script family.
- The last-seen total is persisted in a firstmate-owned marker `state/<id>.pr-activity`, following the naming/lifecycle of sibling per-task state files.
- **First poll** initializes the baseline silently - activity predating the arm never wakes firstmate.
- **Increase** prints exactly one line, `new-review-activity: +<n> on <url>`, and advances the marker.
- **No change** stays silent.
- **Merge wins**: a merged PR echoes only `merged` and skips the activity check, so each fire prints exactly one line.
- **API error**: a `gh` failure (or any non-integer reading) stays silent and never touches the marker - retries next cycle.
- **No bot classification**: any new activity wakes firstmate to triage - cheaper than getting bot-detection wrong. Noted in the script header.

`bin/fm-teardown.sh` removes `state/<id>.pr-activity` alongside its sibling state files (both the main-task and secondmate-child cleanup paths).

## Notes

- `AGENTS.md` untouched: the check-contract sentence ("print one line only when firstmate should wake, print nothing otherwise") still accurately describes the new behavior.
- Mechanics documented in the script header per the coding-guidelines decision tree.

## Tests

New colocated `tests/fm-pr-check.test.sh` covers baseline init, wake-on-increase, silence-on-no-change, merged-beats-activity, API-error silence (existing marker and first poll), and the fallen-count resync. `shellcheck bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh tests/*.sh` is clean; `fm-teardown` and `fm-pr-merge` suites still green.

title: fix(composer): prevent dead-shell message injection
body:
## Intent Fleet-wide composer-empty safety: stop treating bare shell prompt glyphs (>, $, %, #) as an empty AGENT composer, and consolidate composer empty/pending/unknown detection into one shared source of truth across all four session-provider backends (tmux via bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh, herdr, orca, cmux). Problem solved: a pane whose agent has exited to a plain login shell shows a bare shell prompt, which the old per-backend classifiers read as an empty, ready-to-inject agent composer. The away-mode escalation injector (bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh's inject_msg) reads composer-emptiness to decide whether a supervisor pane is a safe injection target, so a dead-shell pane could false-deliver an escalation typed into (worst case executed by) that shell. Deliberate decisions and tradeoffs (things a reviewer reading only the diff would not know were intentional): - The ONE glyph/idle/pending classification decision now lives in a new shared library bin/fm-composer-lib.sh (fm_composer_classify_content); all four adapters delegate to it. Each adapter deliberately KEEPS its own capture and structural row-finding because those use genuinely different primitives (tmux cursor-row read, herdr ANSI tail scan, orca/cmux plain read-screen). Only the driftable classification decision is single-owned - this is intentional, not partial consolidation. - Safety rule: a bare shell glyph (> $ % #) is empty ONLY inside a bordered composer box (the harness's own prompt, e.g. claude's older bordered composer); on a bare unstructured row it is a dead shell and classifies as unknown (unsafe), never empty. The agent prompt glyphs claude's and codex's read empty either way, bordered or bare. - The chosen verdict for a dead shell is unknown (not pending), deliberately, to stay consistent with what herdr/orca/cmux already returned structurally when no composer row is found. - Hardened inject_msg to require an affirmatively-empty composer, deferring on both pending and unknown (previously only pending). This is what actually closes the false-deliver hole, because a boolean pending-check cannot distinguish an empty agent composer from a dead shell or an unreadable pane. - The daemon's pane_input_pending helper is deliberately retained (still a tested predicate and the vehicle for the composer-classifier dispatch regression tests) even though inject_msg no longer routes through it; inject_msg now reads the full tri-state verdict directly. - herdr's faint-tail override (Codex idle ghost-suggestion handling) is deliberately kept inside the herdr adapter, applied after the shared classifier returns, because it needs herdr's raw ANSI row that the shared classifier does not see. - Added the new shared lib to the differential test's OLD_BIN_UNCHANGED_SIBLINGS (tests/fm-backend.test.sh) so the old-vs-new conformance test provides fm-composer-lib.sh to both comparison roots, which both pull in transitively via the current fm-tmux-lib.sh and backends. Constraints respected: this is a firstmate-repo change following the firstmate-coding-guidelines (one-owner rule, size discipline, shellcheck-clean, one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash not em dash, no agent commit co-author). The herdr incident regression tests in tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh stay green, and shellcheck over bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh tests/*.sh is clean. New and changed tests: new tests/fm-composer-lib.test.sh unit-tests the shared owner directly; per-backend dead-shell tests were added to fm-daemon (tmux classifier plus the injector defer-on-dead-shell) and orca; the existing herdr and cmux dead-shell tests are preserved. Reviewer note: one pre-existing, unrelated failure exists in tests/fm-session-start.test.sh (a pi harness supervision-block assertion) that fails identically on the base branch with these changes stashed; it is out of scope for this change and flagged separately for triage, not introduced here. ## What Changed - Centralized empty, pending, and unknown composer classification across tmux, Herdr, Orca, and cmux, treating unstructured shell prompt glyphs as unsafe rather than empty. - Require an affirmatively empty agent composer before the supervision daemon injects an AFK escalation, deferring pending and unreadable or dead-shell panes. - Added shared and backend regression coverage, plus documentation for the composer-injection safety model. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the change is a bounded fail-closed safety hardening with consistent backend delegation and no substantiated regression found in the reviewed diff. ## Testing The supplied full baseline had already passed; focused shared-classifier, daemon, and all four backend suites passed, and a real tmux pane proved a bare `$` shell prompt becomes `unknown`, receives no injected escalation, and leaves the pane unchanged while `❯` and `›` agent glyph controls remain `empty`.
Evidence: Real tmux shell-glyph safety transcript ```text End-to-end shell-glyph injection safety check Target: isolated real tmux pane running bash with PS1="$ " Before inject_msg (visible pane): bash-5.3$ PS1='$ ' $ Composer verdict for bare shell prompt: unknown inject_msg result: deferred (non-zero): no escalation was sent After inject_msg (visible pane): bash-5.3$ PS1='$ ' $ Real tmux Claude glyph control (❯): empty Real tmux Codex glyph control (›): empty ```
- Outcome: 🔧 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ across 2 runs (36m47s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh:146` - `bordered` becomes true when any border glyph appears anywhere in the cursor row, not when the row has a composer-box shape. A dead shell with a decorative prompt such as `| $ ` or `$ |` is stripped to `$`, classified as a bordered empty composer, and passes `inject_msg`'s safety guard. Require actual leading and trailing matching box borders before setting this flag. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-composer-lib.sh:61` - The shared helper now evaluates idle regexes case-insensitively, whereas herdr, Orca, and cmux previously used case-sensitive matching. A typed case-variant of an idle placeholder can therefore be classified as empty, allowing an AFK injection to append to user input or a submit to be falsely confirmed. Preserve each backend's previous regex case semantics. 🔧 Fix: Captain: harden composer safety checks ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
🔧 **Test** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 tests failed with exit code 1 - `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` 🔧 Fix: Stabilize Herdr prune safety setup ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain. - `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` - Previously successful baseline: `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` - Focused coverage: `rc=0; for t in tests/fm-composer-lib.test.sh tests/fm-daemon.test.sh tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh tests/fm-backend-cmux.test.sh tests/fm-backend.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` - End-to-end real tmux check: `bash /var/folders/5x/4nqprlbx0518k3ybcb1sz6gr0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KX5Q43GGV3Q9FPZJH0H4KXDH/e2e-shellglyph-safety.sh "$PWD"`

title: fix: ignore secondmate home marker during sync
body:
## Intent Make the .fm-secondmate-home marker stop reading as a dirty secondmate home to firstmate's sync machinery. bin/fm-home-seed.sh writes an untracked, unignored .fm-secondmate-home marker into every seeded home; because a home is a worktree/clone of the firstmate repo, any plain 'git status --porcelain' dirtiness check counted it, so a home read as dirty forever (fleet-sync reported STUCK). Fix: add .fm-secondmate-home to the tracked .gitignore - the uniform root-cause fix that makes the marker invisible to every dirtiness check at once, WITHOUT broadening fleet-sync's deliberate untracked-counting for project clones and WITHOUT switching the ff-skip to a blanket --untracked-files=no (which would weaken the leave-a-home's-genuine-untracked-in-flight-work-untouched guarantee); the pre-existing marker-specific ignore_seed_marker tolerance stays as the convergence bridge. Convergence of existing pre-fix homes is SCOPED BY HOME TYPE and this scope is INTENDED and already documented on this branch (the no-mistakes(review) commit 'document standalone-clone update path' narrowed the T13 test comment; this resolves the earlier standalone-clone-migration review finding, which the captain approved): a linked-worktree home - the canonical treehouse-lease case that shares the primary's object store - advances past the fix commit on its next bootstrap or spawn sweep via the marker-tolerant local-HEAD fast-forward, after which .gitignore takes over with no hand intervention; a standalone-clone home instead receives the fix commit via /updatefirstmate's origin fetch, since the local-HEAD sweep deliberately never fetches a commit absent from a clone - and origin fetch via /updatefirstmate is a standalone clone's only firstmate-update path anyway - so no home is left permanently marker-dirty. title: fix(watch): detect and handle crewmates parked at permission dialogs
body:
## What Changed

- `bin/fm-watch.sh` and `bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh` add compound-signature detection for panes parked at interactive permission-confirmation dialogs, surfacing a distinct `stale: permission-dialog` wake reason instead of generic staleness.

- `bin/backends/cmux.sh` fixes `surface_exists` to check the CLI call's own exit status rather than a stale prior status.
- `.agents/skills/stuck-crewmate-recovery/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md`, plus `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, and `docs/scripts.md`, document the new detection env vars and response behavior; test suite updates resolve stale-baseline and env-leak false failures uncovered while adding coverage for the new detection path.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The branch adds a well-tested, narrowly-scoped permission-dialog detection feature (compound signature to avoid false positives, correctly placed in the fallback path so it never overrides run-step or busy-pane precedence), fixes a genuine bug in cmux's surface_exists (previously swallowed the CLI's own exit status via a pipe, now checked explicitly), cleanly reverts an abandoned approach with no leftover artifacts, and includes matching regression tests and documentation updates; no correctness, security, or behavioral risks were found.

title: feat(watcher): add paused external-wait supervision
body:
## Intent Add a paused/awaiting-external crew state so an in-flight crewmate intentionally idling on a KNOWN external wait (an upstream tool release, a vendor rate-limit reset, a scheduled window) does not trip the possible-wedge stale escalation like a genuine wedge. This was a deferred item from the 2026-07-07 herdr incident (docs/herdr-backend.md), reproduced live on 2026-07-09/10 in this home when a crew held parked awaiting an upstream release and its idle pane tripped repeated 'stale ... possible wedge' escalations all day. Design decisions and tradeoffs a diff-only reviewer would not know: - New verb 'paused: ' that a crew (or firstmate steering it) appends. It is DELIBERATELY NOT added to the captain-relevant verb set (FM_CLASSIFY_CAPTAIN_RE_DEFAULT): a pause is a 'stop wedge-nagging this idle pane' signal, not work to keep surfacing. The initial pause still surfaces once via the existing not-provably-working signal path in always-on mode, and is self-handled (routine) in away/afk mode - the intended present-vs-away split. - One-owner vocabulary in bin/fm-classify-lib.sh: added FM_CLASSIFY_PAUSED_VERB_DEFAULT, FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS_DEFAULT (3600s, chosen far longer than the 240s wedge threshold but finite so a forgotten pause cannot rot invisibly), status_is_paused, and crew_absorb_class. I intentionally REFACTORED crew_is_provably_working to delegate to the new crew_absorb_class (which returns working|paused|none from ONE fm-crew-state.sh read) so both the watcher and daemon share the classification and there is no duplicated logic; crew_is_paused is a sibling delegating wrapper. This refactor is behavior-preserving for crew_is_provably_working (covered by the existing classifier test). - Watcher (bin/fm-watch.sh): a declared pause is absorbed like a working crew but on the long PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS re-surface cadence instead of the wedge timer. The re-surface age is anchored on the pause's own STATUS-FILE mtime (not a per-hash marker) deliberately, so a churny idle pane - a ticking clock or token counter - cannot keep resetting the cadence the way the hash-tied wedge timer would; a .paused-resurfaced- throttle marker makes it fire once per window. This asymmetry with the wedge timer (which does reset on churn) is intentional: a wedge is about a FROZEN pane, a pause is about a DECLARED wait regardless of pane animation. The afk one-shot branch is untouched (daemon owns triage there). - Daemon (bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh): classify_stale returns a distinct 'pause' action; handle_wake records a .subsuper-paused- marker and drops any wedge marker (and vice versa) so the two are mutually exclusive; housekeeping adds a pause re-surface recheck on the long cadence that re-surfaces a recheck or clears the marker on resume/unpause. The daemon uses the cheap status_is_paused verb read plus a busy recheck (mirroring its existing wedge path), not an fm-crew-state call, to stay cheap. - fm-crew-state.sh reports 'state: paused' distinctly (map_log_state) so a supervisor sees a declared pause and its reason rather than a wedge-suspect idle. - Safety preserved: a crew that goes idle WITHOUT declaring a pause classifies exactly as before (crew_absorb_class returns none -> surfaces); covered by the existing not-working and wedge regression tests, which still pass. - FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS_DEFAULT carries a '# shellcheck disable=SC2034' because it is read by the two consumer scripts, not the library itself - matching the repo's existing convention for externally-consumed constants. - Docs updated consistently: AGENTS.md sections 8 and 11, the three brief-scaffold status state lists in bin/fm-brief.sh (distinguishing paused: from blocked:), and the docs/herdr-backend.md deferral item marked RESOLVED. Tests colocated in tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh, tests/fm-daemon.test.sh, and tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh. shellcheck bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh tests/*.sh is clean. This is a firstmate-repo change; per its no-mistakes contract .no-mistakes/ stays gitignored and CI rejects tracked .no-mistakes paths. ## What Changed - Add a configurable `paused:` crew status for declared external waits, including distinct paused reporting in crew-state output and generated briefs. - Update the watcher and AFK supervision daemon to suppress wedge escalation during declared waits, recheck them on a bounded long cadence, and restore normal tracking when work resumes or terminates. - Document paused-wait behavior and configuration, with regression coverage for watcher, daemon, crew-state, and brief transitions. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The implementation is a broad, stateful coordination change across normal and AFK supervisors, but the final marker transitions and added regressions cover the material risks identified in prior rounds. ## Testing The supplied baseline full suite had already passed; focused daemon and crew-state suites passed, and controlled production watcher/daemon/tmux scenarios demonstrated that declared pauses suppress wedge escalation, re-surface as awaiting-external checks, and retain actionable AFK daemon handoff. Reviewer-visible transcripts are recorded above.
Evidence: AFK paused-state end-to-end transcript AFK daemon self-handled `stale: crew:fm-external-wait` as paused, injected bounded awaiting-external rechecks, and emitted no wedge marker or possible-wedge escalation. ```text Paused external-wait AFK end-to-end transcript Input status: paused: awaiting the upstream release Observed daemon handoff and triage: [2026-07-10T06:21:12-0700] wake: stale: crew:fm-external-wait [2026-07-10T06:21:12-0700] self-handle (paused): stale: crew:fm-external-wait -> paused (awaiting external), rechecked on a long cadence: paused: awaiting the upstream release Supervisor-visible recheck injected after the bounded 3s cadence: tmux send-keys -t supervisor -l ^_Supervisor escalate ( 1 event(s)): paused 3s (awaiting external, recheck whether the wait still holds): crew:fm-external-wait (pre-read; re-arm not needed — watcher daemon-managed) tmux send-keys -t supervisor Enter tmux send-keys -t supervisor -l ^_Supervisor escalate ( 1 event(s)): paused 3s (awaiting external, recheck whether the wait still holds): crew:fm-external-wait (pre-read; re-arm not needed — watcher daemon-managed) tmux send-keys -t supervisor Enter tmux send-keys -t supervisor -l ^_Supervisor escalate ( 1 event(s)): paused 3s (awaiting external, recheck whether the wait still holds): crew:fm-external-wait (pre-read; re-arm not needed — watcher daemon-managed) tmux send-keys -t supervisor Enter Persisted tracking after recheck: pause marker: present (window reset for future rechecks) wedge marker: absent wedge wording: absent Result: PASS - daemon received a plain stale window, classified paused, and surfaced an awaiting-external recheck without a wedge escalation. ```
Evidence: Watcher pause re-surface transcript `A fresh declared pause was absorbed, then re-surfaced after the shortened pause cadence as awaiting external, never as a wedge.` ```text Paused external-wait normal watcher end-to-end transcript Input status: paused: holding for the upstream tool release Fresh declared pause: watcher remained running=1; queued wake=0; wedge timer present=0 Bounded re-surface after status age exceeded the 3s test cadence: stale: crew:fm-normal-external-wait (paused 10s, awaiting external - declared pause, rechecked on a long cadence not a wedge; confirm the wait still holds) wedge wording: absent Result: PASS - a fresh pause is absorbed without wedge timing and later re-surfaces as an awaiting-external recheck. ```
Evidence: Crew-state paused output transcript `Crew-state output reports the declared paused state and reason distinctly.` ```text Paused crew-state end-to-end transcript Input status: paused: awaiting the vendor rate-limit reset Supervisor read: state: paused · source: status-log · awaiting the vendor rate-limit reset Result: PASS - the production current-state reader exposes the declared external wait as paused. ```
- Outcome: 🔧 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ across 2 runs (1h0m39s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed (7) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:601` - Pause mode is decided only for a new pane hash. If firstmate appends `paused:` to an already-stale, unchanged pane, `sf == h` bypasses `crew_absorb_class` and retains the wedge timer, producing a `possible wedge`; AFK similarly retains its existing stale marker because no new stale wake is emitted. Reclassify or reset stale state when status enters or leaves pause. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:129` - The configurable pause verb is not honored here. `status_is_paused` accepts `FM_CLASSIFY_PAUSED_VERB`, but this fallback maps only literal `paused`, so a custom verb is paused in the daemon but becomes `state: unknown` for the always-on watcher. Use the shared configured verb or helper. 🔧 Fix: Captain: fix paused-state transitions 3 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:657` - A paused pane whose output changes every poll never reaches `handle_paused_stale`: this branch clears the pause flag and resets the stale hash. A ticking clock or token counter, explicitly meant not to reset pause cadence, can therefore prevent any bounded re-surface. - 🚨 `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:906` - AFK mode records a pause marker only for a `stale:` wake. A new `paused:` append arrives as a routine `signal:`, and if the watcher already has the same stale hash from before AFK it emits no later stale wake. The daemon then never performs the promised long-cadence recheck. - 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:629` - Once a pause flag exists, this path trusts the append-only `paused:` tail without consulting `crew_absorb_class`. If the crew starts a validation run without another status append and later becomes idle, the active run is hidden on the hour-long pause cadence instead of returning to wedge tracking, despite `fm-crew-state.sh` treating run state as authoritative. 🔧 Fix: Captain: fix paused-state supervision transitions 3 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:479` - When a paused task appends a non-paused status such as `working:`, this removes `.subsuper-paused-*` without restoring normal stale tracking. title: feat: add bounded stop conditions to crewmate briefs
body:
## Intent Add explicit stop conditions and bounded work caps to firstmate's standard ship and scout crewmate brief scaffolds, closing the gap where new obstacles can consume unbounded time without a supervisor-actionable update. Include a default of roughly two hours or 50 significant actions with no supervisor-actionable phase change, while making clear that expected waiting on validation or long test suites is not exhaustion. Add an optional --budget '' task-specific hard cap that renders in the same block. Report early and stop if the task is clearly larger than briefed. Preserve the existing status protocol, isolation assertion, Herdr-lab gate, delivery-mode definitions of done, and shared scaffold structure. Keep the change focused, extend the existing fm-brief tests for ship and scout defaults, the budget override, and unregressed sections, and keep shell scripts shellcheck-clean. Document --budget in AGENTS.md section 11 and docs/scripts.md as an optional per-task control for unattended or long-running task shapes, and fix the fm-brief.sh usage() range so --help includes its entire script contract. ## What Changed Captain, this covers the full branch delta. - Add bounded stop conditions to generated ship and scout briefs, including default progress caps, early scope-expansion stops, and an exception for expected validation waits. - Add and document `--budget ''` for task-specific hard caps, with argument validation and expanded brief-rendering coverage. - Stabilize worktree readiness and locale-sensitive composer handling, along with related test fixtures and compatibility skips. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the change is well-bounded, preserves existing brief invariants, validates ambiguous budget arguments, and includes focused regression coverage. ## Testing The supplied full tmux-backed baseline and focused brief tests passed; manual CLI generation demonstrated default and custom budget caps, preserved ship/scout contracts, complete help and documentation, with reviewer-visible transcript evidence and no worktree residue.
Evidence: End-user fm-brief CLI transcript ```text $ bin/fm-brief.sh --help Scaffold a crewmate brief or persistent secondmate charter at data//brief.md under the active firstmate home. For ordinary tasks, the standard Setup/Rules/Definition-of-done contract is filled in. Firstmate then replaces the {TASK} placeholder with the task description, acceptance criteria, and context, and may adjust other sections when the task genuinely deviates (e.g. working an existing external PR instead of shipping a new one). Usage: fm-brief.sh [--scout] [--herdr-lab] [--budget ''] fm-brief.sh --secondmate {...|--no-projects} --scout writes the scout contract instead: the deliverable is a report at data//report.md (no branch, no push, no PR) and the worktree is scratch. --secondmate writes a persistent secondmate charter. The project list is cloned into the secondmate home, while the natural-language scope tells the main firstmate when to route work there; routine churn stays in its own home; captain-relevant escalations and marked from-firstmate replies append to this home's status file. --no-projects writes a project-less charter for a domain whose subject is the firstmate repo itself (its home is a firstmate worktree, its crews take pooled worktrees of the same repo). It is mutually exclusive with a project list, and omitting both still fails loudly so an accidental omission is never silent. Set FM_SECONDMATE_CHARTER='' to fill the charter text. Set FM_SECONDMATE_SCOPE='' to write a routing scope distinct from the charter text. --herdr-lab is mandatory when the task will issue Herdr lifecycle commands. Scout tasks ignore mode - their deliverable is a report, not a merge. Ship tasks include a project-memory section so durable project-intrinsic learnings can be committed to AGENTS.md through the project's delivery path; it carries the AGENTS.md authoring bar (widely useful knowledge only, pointers over copied detail) and has the crewmate add the fm-ensure-agents-md.sh self-governance section when a touched project AGENTS.md lacks it. title: fix: preserve X-mode follow-up platform limits
body:
## Intent Fix a publicly-visible bug: X-mode completion follow-ups posted to Discord were splitting at X's ~280-char tweet length, mangling a ~470-char reply into a (1/2)(2/2) thread when Discord's real limit is ~2000 and no split was needed. Root cause: fm-x-link only learned the reply platform from the local inbox payload or carry flags, but the fmx-respond ack path can drain the inbox file before the task is spawned and linked, so a link recorded after cleanup silently lost the platform and the splitter defaulted to the X budget. Make platform resolution immune to procedure ordering. Design decisions: (1) fm-x-link now resolves the platform AUTHORITATIVELY by request_id via a new fmx_request_relay_context helper in fm-x-lib.sh that POSTs {request_id} to the relay's /connector/request-context endpoint; the request_id survives the inbox drain so a post-cleanup link still learns the right budget. This is best-effort by design: no token/curl/jq or a non-2xx relay response degrades gracefully. (2) fm-x-link emits a loud WARNING when no platform source resolves, so platform context is never SILENTLY lost - it never falls back to the X 280-char budget without a visible reason. (3) The fmx-respond skill procedure is reordered to link BEFORE inbox cleanup so the fast local path stays correct without needing a relay round-trip. The relay /connector/request-context endpoint does not exist yet (verified against the relay router) and is the companion durable change to ship separately in the myfirstmate repo; until it ships, the link-before-cleanup reorder keeps the normal path correct and the pathological post-cleanup path warns loudly rather than failing silently. Splitting ownership intentionally stays with firstmate's mature fence-aware splitter; the relay only supplies platform context. Added two colocated regression tests in tests/fm-x-mode.test.sh (a Discord follow-up >280 <2000 posts as ONE message even when linked after inbox cleanup, and an unresolvable-platform case warns loudly instead of splitting silently), extended the test's fake-curl relay mock with the new endpoint, and updated docs/configuration.md. This is a firstmate-repo change following the firstmate-coding-guidelines (one-owner rule, shellcheck-clean, one sentence per line in Markdown, plain dash, no agent co-author). ## What Changed - Recover missing reply-platform context for newly linked X-mode tasks through a request-ID relay lookup, preserving platform-specific follow-up split limits after inbox cleanup. - Emit a warning when the follow-up platform cannot be resolved instead of silently using the default split limit. - Link X-mode tasks before inbox cleanup and document the recovery behavior. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: Captain, the normal inbox-before-cleanup path is bounded and corrected, but the advertised ordering-independent fallback relies on an unshipped relay API. ## Testing The provided full-suite baseline had passed; focused X-mode regression coverage and a hermetic CLI flow then confirmed post-cleanup Discord follow-ups stay unsplit while unresolved context warns visibly before the intentional X-budget fallback. This is a CLI integration change, so the recorded CLI transcript is the reviewer-visible end-user evidence.
Evidence: Post-cleanup Discord resolution and unresolved-context warning transcript ```text SCENARIO 1: post-cleanup link resolves Discord context from the relay fm-x-link stdout: linked fix-after-cleanup to X request req-after-cleanup recorded meta: window=w worktree=/wt kind=ship mode=no-mistakes yolo=off x_request=req-after-cleanup x_request_ts=1700000000 x_followups=0 x_platform=discord x_reply_max_chars=1900 relay request-context trace: url=https://relay.test/connector/request-context data={"request_id":"req-after-cleanup"} fm-x-followup stdout: req-after-cleanup reply length: 555 characters recorded follow-up payload summary: {"endpoint":"followup","request_id":"req-after-cleanup","payload_text_characters":554,"threaded":false,"message_count":1} RESULT: one Discord follow-up payload was recorded after inbox cleanup. SCENARIO 2: unresolved platform is visibly warned before X fallback splitting fm-x-link stdout: linked fix-unresolvable to X request req-unresolvable fm-x-link stderr: fm-x-link: WARNING: no reply-platform context for request req-unresolvable (inbox payload absent and the relay did not resolve it by request_id); completion follow-ups will use the default X 280-char split budget and may wrongly split a longer Discord reply into a numbered thread. Link the task before the inbox file is drained, or ensure the relay request-context lookup is available. recorded meta: window=w kind=ship x_request=req-unresolvable x_request_ts=1700000000 x_followups=0 fm-x-followup stdout: req-unresolvable reply length: 442 characters recorded fallback payload summary: {"endpoint":"followup","request_id":"req-unresolvable","payload_text_characters":276,"threaded":true,"message_count":2,"first_chunk_characters":276,"last_chunk_characters":176} RESULT: the X-budget fallback was visibly preceded by a WARNING. ```

title: feat(spawn): auto-compact claude crewmates around 200k tokens
body:
## Intent

Give firstmate's claude-harness crewmates and secondmates automatic context compaction at roughly 200k tokens, matching the primary. Adds CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=200000 (single-var form, no percentage override) to the claude) launch prefix in bin/fm-spawn.sh, so min(200000, window) lands near ~193k whether the model window is 200K or 1M. codex/opencode/pi templates deliberately do NOT carry the var since only claude's launch shape was verified to honor it; grok was left out because its honoring of the var is unverified. A colocated test asserts the claude template carries the var and the others do not. Rationale is recorded in the bin/fm-spawn.sh header comment and the harness-adapters claude section.

## What Changed

- Add `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=200000` to the `claude` launch template in `bin/fm-spawn.sh` so separately-launched claude crewmates, scouts, and secondmates auto-compact near 200k tokens like the primary session does (they never inherit its `.claude/settings.local.json`); the value is capped at the model's real window so `min(200000, window)` stays correct whether the window is 200k or ~1M, and the codex/opencode/pi/grok templates deliberately omit the var. Rationale is recorded in the `fm-spawn.sh` header, the launch-case comment, and the harness-adapters skill; a colocated test asserts the claude template carries the var and the others do not.
- Fix the cmux backend surface-presence check in `bin/backends/cmux.sh` to capture `list-panes` and gate on its own exit and output before piping to `jq`, since `jq -e` on empty input exits 0 on jq 1.6 and would false-positive an absent surface as present.
- Harden environment-fragile tests (jq, git, and harness detection) and skip the backlog-handoff tests when the installed `tasks-axi` is incompatible, matching the auto-fix applied during the Test stage.

## Risk Assessment

title: feat(spawn): auto-provision run-ready worktrees
body:
## Intent

Make every newly spawned crewmate and scout worktree run-ready automatically through opt-in per-project provisioning. Add a generic gitignored personal config format under config/provision with absolute env_source_dir, repo-relative env_files, setup_cmd, and an optional setup_timeout. Add bin/fm-provision-worktree.sh to copy configured environment files without reading or printing contents, preserve relative paths, warn on missing files, run setup idempotently, and fail cleanly on real errors. Bound setup_cmd portably with timeout precedence FM_PROVISION_SETUP_TIMEOUT over setup_timeout over a 600-second default; timeout failure remains best-effort because fm-spawn must warn with PROVISION and continue. Integrate provisioning after the existing worktree isolation guard and before agent launch for ship and scout tasks, with FM_SPAWN_NO_PROVISION=1 to skip. Keep worktree acquisition and isolation unchanged, commit only a generic example and documentation, never real captain environment data or project config. The exact pipeline head already passed review, the complete repository test suite, documentation, and lint. Resume at push through the configured fork, open the upstream PR, and validate CI.

## What Changed
- Add `bin/fm-provision-worktree.sh`, which copies configured env/credential files (preserving relative paths) and runs an optional `setup_cmd` in a freshly spawned worktree, driven by a per-project, gitignored `config/provision/<project>.toml` (`env_source_dir`, `env_files`, `setup_cmd`, optional `setup_timeout`); a project with no config file is a no-op.
- Wire provisioning into `bin/fm-spawn.sh` for ship/scout worktree spawns, running after the worktree-isolation guard and before agent launch, best-effort (a `PROVISION:` warning never aborts the spawn), skippable per-spawn via `FM_SPAWN_NO_PROVISION=1`.
- Bound `setup_cmd` with a portable timeout (precedence `FM_PROVISION_SETUP_TIMEOUT` > per-project `setup_timeout` > 600s default); on expiry the setup process group is killed and treated as a non-aborting failure.

title: fix(composer): handle ANSI ghost text safely
body:
## Intent Fix a fleet-critical bug: away-mode escalation injection wedged all night on the primary claude-on-herdr pane because the composer classifier false-read de-emphasised ghost/placeholder text as real pending input (6524 defers; empirically reproduced read-only from the live primary pane - claude's rotating prompt-suggestion ghost is a bare '❯' then SGR-2 dim text, which herdr's ANSI pane read preserves; the tmux path already stripped dim but the herdr path only had a narrow codex bold-wrapped byte-pattern check that claude's non-bold prompt never matched). Per explicit captain direction, consolidate ghost-text stripping into ONE ANSI-aware classification owner that both ANSI-capable backends route through, instead of per-harness one-offs. Key decisions and deliberate tradeoffs a diff reader would not know: - fm_composer_strip_ghost (bin/fm-composer-lib.sh) is the single owner. It drops every de-emphasised run: SGR-2 dim/faint (claude/codex) AND a dark/muted TRUECOLOR foreground (grok's placeholder) whose perceived luminance is below FM_COMPOSER_GHOST_LUMA_MAX (default 128, new tunable). This closes the previously-documented grok TRUECOLOR gap by the SAME mechanism, per acceptance criteria. - The dark-truecolor rule deliberately assumes a dark terminal theme (the fleet reality; empirically grok real input is bright 38;2;224;222;244 lum ~225 kept, muted UI is 38;2;50;47;70..110;106;134 lum ~51..110 dropped). SGR-2 stays theme-independent. Bias is conservative: under-stripping merely defers (surfaced by the max-defer alarm), so 256-color (38;5) is deliberately NOT luminance-tested (palette-dependent, not empirically needed) and only truecolor 38;2 is. - fm_tmux_strip_ghost and fm_backend_herdr_strip_ansi are reduced to thin adapters over the shared owner; the herdr-only faint byte-pattern check (fm_backend_herdr_prompt_tail_is_faint) is removed because the generic dim strip subsumes it (codex faint regressions stay green through the shared path). - Bordered-composer detection now reads the PLAIN row (not the ghost-stripped one) because in a dark theme the box border is itself dark truecolor and drops with the ghost; reading shape from the plain row keeps that correct. - Two pre-existing ghost-test fixtures that used a near-black 38;2;1;2;3 as 'real' colored text were intentionally corrected to a bright 38;2;224;222;244: near-black was never a realistic real-input color (invisible on a dark bg) and only existed to exercise the truecolor payload-skip parser, which the bright value still exercises. This is a deliberate fixture correction, not a weakened assertion. - Scope was deliberately kept to the composer classification layer only (fm-composer-lib.sh, fm-tmux-lib.sh, backends/herdr.sh) and did NOT touch fm-supervise-daemon.sh / fm-watch.sh / fm-classify-lib.sh, to avoid conflict with a concurrently-landing paused-state supervision PR (#421). - The observed 'wedge alarm alarmed into the void' secondary concern (inject_wedge_alarm only actively signals via the tmux status line, skipped on herdr) is deliberately deferred to its own filed task (fm-wedge-alarm-oob-w3), not in this diff. Evidence and the incident write-up (exact ANSI bytes, dates, versions, commands) are in docs/herdr-backend.md; deterministic regressions feed the exact captured bytes through the real classifiers (tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh, tests/fm-composer-ghost.test.sh); the harness-adapters skill's grok gap note and docs/configuration.md are updated. ## What Changed - Centralized ANSI ghost extraction in `fm-composer-lib.sh` so tmux and Herdr ignore dim/faint suggestions and dark truecolor placeholders while retaining real typed input. - Kept composer-shape detection separate from ghost stripping and classify erased unbordered shell prompts as `unknown`, preventing away-mode injection into an exited shell. - Added regressions for dim ghosts, Grok truecolor placeholders, and dark shell prompts, and updated AFK, backend, configuration, and harness guidance. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: Captain, the change is internally consistent but modifies a safety-critical ANSI-based injection guard shared by two backends. ## Testing The supplied baseline full suite had passed. Focused classifier regressions and a controlled end-to-end ANSI transcript confirm SGR-2 and dark truecolor ghost text classify as empty on tmux and Herdr, while bright bordered input remains pending; the transcript also verifies the configured luminance threshold behavior.
Evidence: ANSI composer classifier end-to-end transcript ```text shared/default-luma-128 dark-placeholder-output=<❯ > expected=<❯ > shared/luma-50 dark-placeholder-output=<❯ Type a message...> expected=<❯ Type a message...> tmux/claude_dim_ghost cursor_row=0 captured_ansi=\342\235\257 \033[2mwhat did the wheelhouse verification fi\|nd?\033[0m$| verdict=empty expected=empty tmux/grok_dark_bordered_placeholder cursor_row=0 captured_ansi=\033[38;2;86;82;110m\342\224\202\033[38;2;224;222;244m \342\|\235\257 \033[38;2;50;47;70mType a message...\033[38;2;86;8\|2;110m \342\224\202\033[39m$| verdict=empty expected=empty tmux/grok_bright_bordered_input cursor_row=0 captured_ansi=\033[38;2;86;82;110m\342\224\202\033[38;2;224;222;244m \342\|\235\257 land the queued patch \033[38;2;86;82;110m\342\224\|\202\033[39m$| verdict=pending expected=pending herdr/claude_dim_ghost capture=controlled-ansi-fixture verdict=empty expected=empty herdr/grok_dark_bordered_placeholder capture=controlled-ansi-fixture verdict=empty expected=empty herdr/grok_bright_bordered_input capture=controlled-ansi-fixture verdict=pending expected=pending cleanup=all temporary tmux sessions removed ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Rebase** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `docs/herdr-backend.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main 🔧 Fix applied. ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh:101` - Captain, a dark truecolor dead-shell prompt such as `$` is stripped before classification, turning the safety result from `unknown` into `empty`. AFK escalation may then type and submit into an exited shell. Preserve or re-check unbordered shell-prompt shape from the plain row before classifying stripped content. 🔧 Fix: Preserve dark shell prompt safety 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-composer-lib.sh:185` - Captain, the new safety backstop recognizes only an exact plain `$`, `>`, `%`, or `#`. A dead tmux shell prompt such as `user@host $` rendered entirely in a dark truecolor is stripped to empty, does not match this check, and then falls through as `empty`; away-mode can inject and execute its digest in that exited shell. Preserve `unknown` for any nonempty unbordered plain row that ghost stripping erased, except verified agent-composer shapes. 🔧 Fix: Harden erased shell prompt classification ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: fix: make watcher pid identity clock-independent on procfs platforms
body:
Closes #433

## What

- `fm_pid_identity` now fingerprints a process with `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 (starttime in clock ticks since boot - constant for the life of a process, immune to wall-clock changes) plus the command line, on procfs platforms.
- Platforms without procfs (macOS) keep the previous `ps -o lstart=` form as a portable fallback, documented as drift-sensitive there.
- Compat path: a lock recorded in the old lstart format still matches its live watcher, so this change landing mid-flight does not declare a running watcher dead.
- Test infrastructure fixes picked up along the way: probe node `.ts` import support so the Pi extension suites run across node versions, and skip the tasks-axi handoff suites when the installed version is incompatible.

## Why

See #433: on WSL2 the wall clock slews after host sleep/resume and `ps` recomputes lstart from the current clock, so the SAME live watcher's rendered start time changes over time (observed live: lock recorded `11:54:03`, later reads `11:54:29` then `11:54:36`). `fm_watcher_lock_matches_pid` then treats a healthy watcher as a recycled pid, producing false "TURN WOULD END BLIND" alarms, `fm-watch-arm.sh` reporting FAILED beside a live watcher, and `--restart` degrading to lock-clearing instead of a clean kill.

## Validation

- New regression coverage in `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh`: identity is byte-stable for a live process (no wall-clock component), distinct same-command processes yield distinct identities (recycled-pid guard intact), and an old-format lock still matches its live watcher.
- `shellcheck` clean on changed scripts.
- Full validation pipeline green on the branch head (review, tests, docs, lint).

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

Note for the maintainer: the no-mistakes pipeline validated this branch fully green locally (review, tests, document, lint - and the complete test suite was re-run after each rebase onto advancing main). The final push and PR-open steps were performed manually from a fork, because a fork contributor lacks the upstream push access the pipeline's own push step requires; everything else followed the standard gate.

title: fix(teardown): retry transient index locks during worktree return
body:
## Intent Fix the fm-teardown.sh lock race where treehouse return races a just-killed crew process's in-flight git operation and aborts on a transient index.lock. Observed failure: teardown kills the crew's lingering processes, then treehouse return's git reset --hard fails with Unable to create '.git/worktrees//index.lock': File exists, and teardown aborts. The lock is transient (self-clears within seconds); an immediate manual retry succeeds. Required approach: bounded wait-or-retry around the worktree-return step, only on the transient lock error signature; never delete the lock file itself during the patience window (a live git process may own it); if retries exhaust, fail as loudly as today mentioning the lock persisted across the retry window; keep retry count and wait as small named env-overridable constants. Existing provably-stale lock cleanup remains as a last-resort path after the patience window. Existing landed-work refusal logic must stay untouched. Tests must cover transient lock clearing after first attempt (retry succeeds) and persistent lock (still fails loudly), and shellcheck must stay clean. ## What Changed - Retry `treehouse return` only for Git's transient `index.lock` error signature, preserving locks until optional provably-stale cleanup and failing loudly when the lock persists. - Add bounded retry count and wait configuration, retain the legacy wait alias, and safely handle blank, invalid, and fractional wait values. - Document the retry behavior and expand teardown coverage for self-clearing and persistent locks plus retry configuration edge cases. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the bounded retry change is well-contained and preserves the existing fail-closed teardown behavior. ## Testing The supplied full-suite baseline had passed; the focused teardown suite and isolated real-Git CLI scenarios confirmed retry-on-self-clearing lock, persistent-lock refusal with retained metadata and lock, stale-lock safety coverage, and unchanged landed-work protections. No worktree changes remain.

title: feat(dispatch): add model/effort tiers and mechanical quality guardrails
body:
## Intent Add firstmate model/effort dispatch tiers and mechanical quality guardrails (fm-tier-guard.sh, fm-risk-tripwire.sh, fm-ultracode-guard.sh), wired into fm-teardown.sh, with colocated tests and updated docs. ## What Changed - Add three read-only guardrail scripts under `bin/`: `fm-risk-tripwire.sh` word-bounded-greps a task's `# Task` brief section (excluding scaffold/Herdr boilerplate and fenced code) and, once code exists, its changed file paths for migration/auth/schema/security/payment signals, exiting `0` clean / `1` on a RISK hit / `2` when the diff is uncheckable (never a silent clean pass); `fm-tier-guard.sh` escalates a task in place when its diff size, file count, or elapsed time outgrows its model/effort tier; and `fm-ultracode-guard.sh` flags tasks needing an independent second pass via a `state/.ultracode` marker and refuses PR-ready until a distinct, separately-dispatched reviewer is recorded. - Wire dispatch and teardown to the guardrails: `fm-dispatch-select.sh` now threads `ultracode`/`ultracode_role` through both first-profile and quota-balanced selection so a matched rule's flags survive into the chosen profile, and `fm-teardown.sh` removes the per-task `.ultracode` marker on teardown plus rewrites `content_in_default()` to a portable `read-tree`/`write-tree` 3-way merge instead of the git-2.38-only `merge-tree --write-tree`. - Add colocated test suites for the three guardrails and teardown cleanup, document the tiering scheme across `AGENTS.md`, `docs/` (architecture, configuration `FM_TIER_*` knobs, scripts), and `docs/examples/crew-dispatch.json`, and land incidental portability fixes (jq/git-version and test-env robustness, a handoff-test skip on incompatible tasks-axi, a herdr backend server-race fix, and a `bin/backends/cmux.sh` probe that no longer masks a failed CLI call through `jq -e`). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Well-bounded addition of three read-only guardrail scripts plus narrow wiring, already hardened across four prior review rounds; independent analysis and multi-agent verification confirm the core scripts fail safe in the dangerous (under-trigger / discard-work) direction, leaving only one info-level defense-in-depth hardening. ## Testing Baseline suite command had already passed; I re-ran the full tests/*.test.sh suite (all green except one flaky, unrelated OpenCode watcher assertion in fm-pi-watch-extension, which passed 3/3 in isolation and touches nothing in this diff), confirmed the four change-relevant tests (fm-tier-guard, fm-risk-tripwire, fm-ultracode-guard, fm-teardown) pass, and then produced a reviewer-visible CLI transcript demonstrating all three guardrails and the teardown .ultracode cleanup working end-to-end as firstmate invokes them. Overall result: the user intent is satisfied and verified.

GUARDRAIL 2 fm-risk-tripwire: cosmetic copy brief -> exit 0; login/auth/migration brief -> 'RISK: brief for risky-task mentions risk-adjacent term(s): authentication,migration,password,schema,session,token' exit 1. GUARDRAIL 3 fm-ultracode-guard: flag -> check REFUSES exit 1 -> self-review rejected -> separate reviewer recorded -> check PASSES exit 0. TEARDOWN: state/<id>.ultracode marker present, and fm-teardown.sh rm -f line now includes "$STATE/$ID.ultracode". ```text ============================================================ GUARDRAIL 1: fm-tier-guard.sh (trivial haiku/low tier outgrows its envelope) ============================================================ Scenario A - a genuinely trivial 1-line fix on haiku/low (should stay SILENT, exit 0): $ /home/orangepi/.no-mistakes/worktrees/7c3b260dcf5f/01KX6G4N3YF0V7QS0WVQSZVF66/bin/fm-tier-guard.sh tiny -> exit 0 Scenario B - a task cannot independently review itself -> exit 1 Record a genuinely separate reviewer task (needs its own recorded meta): $ /home/orangepi/.no-mistakes/worktrees/7c3b260dcf5f/01KX6G4N3YF0V7QS0WVQSZVF66/bin/fm-ultracode-guard.sh reviewed payments-refactor review-pass recorded review-pass as the independent review of payments-refactor -> exit 0 Now the PR-ready check PASSES (exit 0): $ /home/orangepi/.no-mistakes/worktrees/7c3b260dcf5f/01KX6G4N3YF0V7QS0WVQSZVF66/bin/fm-ultracode-guard.sh check payments-refactor -> exit 0 ============================================================ TEARDOWN WIRING: fm-teardown removes the state/.ultracode marker ============================================================ Marker present after flag/reviewed: /tmp/tmp.JcBHLxIXHK/state/payments-refactor.ultracode grep the teardown rm line that now includes the marker: 1058:rm -f "$STATE/$ID.status" "$STATE/$ID.turn-ended" "$STATE/$ID.check.sh" "$STATE/$ID.meta" "$STATE/$ID.pi-ext.ts" "$STATE/$ID.grok-turnend-token" "$STATE/$ID.ultracode" ============================================================ DEMO COMPLETE ============================================================ ```
Evidence: fm-tier-guard test log ```text ok - fm-tier-guard passes a trivial task within its size and age envelope ok - fm-tier-guard escalates a trivial task once its diff exceeds the line ceiling ok - fm-tier-guard escalates a trivial task once its diff exceeds the file ceiling ok - fm-tier-guard escalates a trivial task that has run past its age ceiling ok - fm-tier-guard does not apply the trivial-tier ceiling to a non-trivial task ok - fm-tier-guard escalates any tier once its diff crosses the general heavy-scale ceiling ok - fm-tier-guard surfaces a degraded (PR-head-unavailable) diff measurement instead of swallowing it ok - fm-tier-guard errors distinctly (exit 2) when the task has no recorded meta ok - fm-tier-guard uses a distinct exit code for malformed invocations # all fm-tier-guard tests passed ```

fm-risk-tripwire reports could-not-check when the diff base is unresolvable, not a clean pass ok - fm-risk-tripwire still reports a brief hit (1) when the diff base is unresolvable ok - fm-risk-tripwire still trips on multi-word risk phrases ok - fm-risk-tripwire trips on authorizer paths # all fm-risk-tripwire tests passed ```

Evidence: fm-teardown test log (asserts .ultracode marker removal) ```text ok - local-only worktree with HEAD on a fork remote is torn down (fix holds) ok - teardown prompts tasks-axi backlog refresh when compatible ok - local-only worktree with unpushed work is torn down under --force (escape hatch) ok - squash-merged + deleted-branch worktree (PR merged) is torn down (the fix) ok - squash-merged PR accepts a local HEAD that is an ancestor of the final PR head ok -
