- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 warning across 2 runs (1h3m29s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Rebase** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `docs/scripts.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main 🔧 Fix applied. ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ⚠️ `bin/fm-risk-tripwire.sh:103` - brief_task_body scans the region from `# Task` to the next boundary heading (Setup/Rules/Project memory/Definition of done), but on a `--herdr-lab` brief fm-brief.sh injects its Herdr contract boilerplate (heading `# Herdr isolation - HARD SAFETY CONTRACT`, not in the boundary set) BETWEEN `# Task` and `# Setup`. That boilerplate is dense with the word `session` (HERDR_LAB_SESSION, `--session`, "session name"), which is a WORD_KEYWORD, so the risk tripwire fires on every herdr-lab task regardless of the actual task text (confirmed by scaffolding a --herdr-lab brief and grepping the scanned region). This defeats the boilerplate-exclusion the scan was built for: every herdr-lab task gets floored to opus/xhigh + independent-review from scaffold text, not task content, incurring an unnecessary extra review dispatch. The effect is in the safe over-trigger direction, so it is a tiering/cost regression rather than a safety hole. Fix: add the two Herdr section headings (`# Herdr isolation ...` / `# Herdr lifecycle declaration ...`) to the awk boundary set so the scan stops at the Herdr block, keeping only the real {TASK} text. 🔧 Fix: exclude herdr-lab brief block from risk-tripwire scan 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:1058` - fm-ultracode-guard.sh creates a per-task marker at state/<id>.ultracode (MARKER="$STATE/$ID.ultracode"), but fm-teardown.sh's state-file cleanup (line 1058) removes .status, .turn-ended, .check.sh, .meta, .pi-ext.ts, and .grok-turnend-token and omits .ultracode. Every ultracode-flagged (or risk-floored) task therefore leaves an orphan state/<id>.ultracode file behind after teardown, so these markers accumulate indefinitely in state/. It follows the exact same state/<id>.<marker> convention as the files that ARE cleaned up, so the omission looks unintentional. Functionally low-risk because task ids carry random suffixes (a new task won't collide with a stale marker), but it is a real state-directory leak and an inconsistency in the teardown cleanup contract. Fix: add "$STATE/$ID.ultracode" to the rm -f list at bin/fm-teardown.sh:1058. 🔧 Fix: clean up orphan .ultracode state marker on teardown 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-risk-tripwire.sh:195` - CHECKED=1 is set at line 187 as soon as worktree=/project= point at real dirs, before the diff base is known to be resolvable. If fm_default_branch returns empty (line 195 false) or the resolved BASE commit cannot be verified in the worktree (line 201 false), the entire changed-path scan (lines 202-216) is skipped with NO output on stdout or stderr, and the script falls through to `exit "$FOUND"` with FOUND still 0 (unless the brief itself hit). So the 'second, binding checkpoint against the real diff' (header, lines 15-16) silently reports exit 0 (clean) instead of exit 2 (could-not-check). This is the dangerous under-trigger direction on a safety guardrail: a task whose brief has no risk keyword but whose diff introduces a risky path (e.g. a 'refactor the login flow' brief plus a committed db/migrations/0001.sql) is silently NOT floored to opus/xhigh whenever base resolution happens to fail, and unlike the sibling fm-review-diff.sh there is no loud warning to make the missed checkpoint visible. Rare in practice (fm_default_branch resolves via origin/HEAD or local main/master on any normally-cloned project, and pooled worktrees usually verify the local default ref), and mitigated by the brief scan running in the same invocation plus fm-tier-guard's FILES ceiling and the crewmate self-report backstop, so it is safe to merge and fix as a follow-up. Fix is mechanical and safe-direction: when the path scan is attempted but its base cannot be resolved, warn to stderr and/or treat that as not-checkable rather than letting it read as a clean pass. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-tier-guard.sh:104` - LINES is derived only from git diff --stat's insertions(+)/deletions(-) summary counts. A binary-only change contributes 0 to those counts (git prints 'N file changed, 0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)' plus a per-file 'Bin ... bytes' line), so a task dominated by large binary artifacts is measured only by FILES, never by content weight; the line ceilings (>30 trivial / >400 heavy) never fire on it. Technically the under-trigger direction, but the tier ceilings proxy reasoning/review load and a pure binary asset swap has zero code to review, so LINES=0 is defensible; the FILES ceilings, age proxy, and self-report backstop still apply, and firstmate's own repo is bash-only. Line-based sizing is inherent to reusing --stat, so this is informational, not a fix demand. 🔧 Fix: stop tiering guardrails passing silently when diff uncheckable 4 issues (2 warnings, 2 infos) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-risk-tripwire.sh:141` - The diff-path scan (PATH_STRONG_REGEX line 141 / PATH_WEAK_REGEX line 142) covers a strict SUBSET of the brief-text WORD_KEYWORDS (line 80): it omits password, token, permission, encrypt, and decrypt. So the risk floor's diff scan (documented at line 16 as the 'binding checkpoint against the real diff') is strictly weaker than the brief checkpoint. I independently reproduced path_is_risky(): it returns NOT-risky for lib/crypto/encrypt.rb, lib/crypto/decrypt.rb, app/models/permission.rb, config/permissions.yml, app/services/token.rb, and config/password_reset.rb, while correctly flagging db/migrations/*.sql, lib/auth/session.rb, and config.schema.json. Failure scenario: a task whose brief avoids every keyword (e.g. 'refactor the crypto module for clarity' — 'crypto' is not a keyword, so the brief scan exits clean) but whose diff at Validate time touches only encrypt/decrypt/token/password/permission-named files produces DIFF_UNRESOLVED=0 and FOUND=0 and exits 0 (clean); the genuinely security-sensitive change is never floored to opus/xhigh + independent-review, defeating the guardrail in the under-trigger (dangerous) direction. This contradicts the code's own fail-safe bias. Fix: add password(s)/token(s)/permission(s)/encrypt/decrypt to PATH_STRONG_REGEX so the diff scan's keyword coverage matches the brief scan's. - ⚠️ `AGENTS.md:261` - AGENTS.md line 261 (edited by this diff to add `ultracode?` to the extraction tuple) tells firstmate to extract `(harness, model, effort, ultracode?)` from the profile that bin/fm-dispatch-select.sh prints for a quota-balanced rule, and line 262 keys the `fm-ultracode-guard.sh flag` call off that resolved profile. But fm-dispatch-select.sh's clean() builder (lines 91-94 and 145-148) emits only {harness, model?, effort?} and strips ultracode/ultracode_role — I confirmed the printed profile never carries ultracode. So a config/crew-dispatch.json rule combining `select: quota-balanced` with profiles that set `ultracode: true` (a documented-valid combination) loses the flag in the tool output; firstmate never runs `flag`, no state/<id>.ultracode marker is written, and at PR-ready `fm-ultracode-guard.sh check` finds no marker and exits 0, silently skipping the mandatory independent review — unless fm-risk-tripwire independently fires. Fix by either passing ultracode/ultracode_role through dispatch-select's clean(), or rewording the doc so firstmate reads ultracode from the matched RULE, not the printed profile. Warning (not error) because the shipped example never pairs quota-balanced with ultracode and the risk-floor backstop catches the archetypal safety-critical case. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-tier-guard.sh:85` - is_trivial_tier() requires MODEL matching *haiku* AND EFFORT to equal the literal 'low'. fm-spawn records effort=default whenever --effort is omitted, which is exactly what a model-only captain override ('use haiku for this', AGENTS.md section 4 precedence #1) produces (model=haiku, effort=default). Verified in isolation: is_trivial_tier returns trivial for effort=low but NOT for effort=default/medium/empty. So a haiku task dispatched without an explicit effort skips the tighter trivial ceiling (2 files / 30 lines / 1800s) and is only bounded by the far-larger heavy ceiling (8 files / 400 lines); a 5-file/100-line diff on the weakest model then never escalates. The canonical dispatch-rule path always pairs haiku with effort=low so the primary path works; this is a bounded coverage gap for the model-only override path. Consider treating effort=default as trivial when the model is haiku (or keying the trivial tier on model alone). - ℹ️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:293` - The read-tree -im --aggressive rewrite of content_in_default() does file-granular (not line-level) 3-way merges, so when both the branch and the default branch edited DIFFERENT regions of the SAME file, write-tree fails on the unmerged entries and the function returns inconclusive (teardown refuses). On the deployment git (2.34.1) this is a net improvement — the old `git merge-tree --write-tree` (git >= 2.38 only) did not exist and always failed — but on git >= 2.38 it is a behavioral regression that false-refuses teardown of already-landed work the old code line-merged and recognized as landed (reproducible with base=seq 1..40, branch changes line 5, default has line-5 + line-35 changes, no discoverable merged PR). This is the SAFE direction (never discards unlanded work; recoverable by investigating then pushing/--force) and the function comment already documents the 'inconclusive -> refuse' contract, so no action needed — noted for awareness. I independently reproduced that the rewrite never falsely reports unlanded work as landed (the dangerous direction is protected). 🔧 Fix: pass ultracode through dispatch, tighten tiering guardrail coverage 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-ultracode-guard.sh:59` - bin/fm-ultracode-guard.sh:59 cmd_flag writes `echo "role=$role" > "$MARKER"` with no validation that role is a single line. cmd_check (line 85) treats the presence of any `^reviewed_by=` line in the marker as proof the mandatory independent review ran, and cmd_reviewed (the only intended writer of reviewed_by=) enforces the self-review and metaless-reviewer guards. A role value containing an embedded newline followed by `reviewed_by=` (e.g. an ultracode_role field in config/crew-dispatch.json set to a two-line string) makes flag itself write both a `role=` and a `reviewed_by=` line; a later `check` then exits 0 and reports the task as reviewed, bypassing the guardrail entirely in the dangerous under-trigger direction. Low probability because in every real path role is either the hardcoded literal `independent-review` (risk-floor + fm-risk-tripwire hits) or a short single-token label firstmate extracts from its own local config, and the flag arity check ($# <= 3) does not catch a multiline single arg. Defense-in-depth fix: in cmd_flag reject a role containing a newline or the substring `reviewed_by=` before writing the marker, so only cmd_reviewed (with its distinct-reviewer + real-meta checks) can ever introduce that sentinel line.
⚠️ **Test** - 1 warning - 🚨 tests failed with exit code 1 - `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` 🔧 Fix: skip handoff tests on incompatible tasks-axi; fix herdr server-race 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `tests/fm-pi-watch-extension.test.sh` - tests/fm-pi-watch-extension.test.sh failed once during the full-suite run on the assertion 'OpenCode watch plugin must not treat external healthy output as an owned arm' (expected exit 0, got 1), but passed 3/3 when re-run in isolation. The change under test touches none of the pi/opencode/watch surfaces, so this is a flaky/load-sensitive failure in an unrelated test, not a regression from this diff. - `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` - Full suite: `for t in tests/*.test.sh; do bash "$t"; done` — all green except the flaky unrelated fm-pi-watch-extension case - `bash tests/fm-tier-guard.test.sh` (PASS) - `bash tests/fm-risk-tripwire.test.sh` (PASS) - `bash tests/fm-ultracode-guard.test.sh` (PASS) - `bash tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` (PASS — includes the assertion that teardown removes the .ultracode marker) - `bash tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` and `bash tests/fm-x-mode.test.sh` (the two cut off by the 10-min wall) — both PASS - `End-to-end demo transcript exercising all three guardrails against a real repo+worktree: fm-tier-guard silent within envelope / ESCALATE at 41 lines; fm-risk-tripwire clean brief passes / auth+migration brief trips; fm-ultracode-guard flag→check refuses→self-review rejected→separate reviewer accepted→check passes; teardown rm line confirmed to include $STATE/$ID.ultracode` - `bash tests/fm-pi-watch-extension.test.sh` run 3x in isolation → PASS each time (confirms the single suite failure is a load flake, not caused by this diff)
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix(teardown): stop Arena local runtime safely
body:
## Summary

- stop Arena `local-cli` Supabase through Arena's repo-owned `bun run supabase:worktree stop` command after FirstMate's existing landed/scratch teardown safety passes and before Treehouse returns the lease
- re-read and verify Arena runtime metadata, exact worktree ownership, local target, runtime slug, and competing in-flight task ownership before the stop
- preserve existing teardown behavior for hosted targets, missing runtime metadata, non-Arena projects, and already-stopped stacks
- abort lease return and preserve task/worktree state when ownership is ambiguous or the normal stop fails

## Safety

This path never passes `--no-backup`, never removes Docker resources directly, and never uses global stop or prune commands.
FirstMate owns only teardown orchestration; Arena continues to own Supabase service and container mechanics.

## Validation

- `bash -n` across `bin/*.sh`, `bin/backends/*.sh`, and `tests/*.sh`
- `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh`
- `tests/fm-backend.test.sh`
- `tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh`
- `tests/fm-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh`
- `git diff --check`

All commands above passed.
`shellcheck` was not available on the local PATH and this PR had no CI checks configured when opened, so shellcheck remains an explicit validation gap.

## Dependency ordering

Depends on ArenaCRM/arena-crm#1306 at commit `dd8120371`.
Merge and deploy the Arena runtime contract first, then merge this FirstMate orchestration PR.

# BOTH the HERDR_SESSION env var AND passing a leading `--session <name>`
# CLI flag. Verified empirically (docs/herdr-backend.md "Session targeting: the
# --session flag, not HERDR_SESSION alone"): on the installed herdr 0.7.1
# client, the HERDR_SESSION env var is NOT reliably honored by CLI subcommands
# once ANY other herdr server is already bound on the machine - queries
# silently fall back to whatever server IS running (the wrong one) instead of
# routing to the requested session or refusing. The `--session <name>` global
# flag must precede the subcommand on newer herdr builds: 0.7.3 accepts the
# old trailing spelling syntactically, but `pane run` does not execute the
# command under it. The env var is kept alongside the flag - harmless,
# self-documenting, and forward-compatible if a future herdr build honors it.
# Never used by fm_backend_herdr_version_check, which is intentionally
# session-independent (reads only .client.* fields).
fm_backend_herdr_cli() {  # <session> <herdr-subcommand-and-args...>
  local session=$1
  shift
  HERDR_SESSION="$session" herdr --session "$session" "$@"
}

== orca implementation: expected CLI command gate ==
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# bin/backends/orca.sh - the Orca terminal session-provider adapter.
#
# Orca owns both the task worktree and the terminal endpoint. Escape key support
# remains unsupported until Orca exposes a terminal-send primitive for it.
#
# Target string shape: the Orca terminal id accepted by `orca terminal ...`.

fm_backend_orca_tool_check() {
  local help word
  command -v orca >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "error: backend=orca selected but the 'orca' CLI is not installed" >&2; return 1; }
  help=$(orca --help 2>&1) || return 1
  for word in status repo worktree terminal; do
    printf '%s\n' "$help" | grep -Eq "(^|[[:space:]])$word([[:space:]]|$)" || {
      echo "error: backend=orca selected but 'orca' is not the expected Orca CLI" >&2
      return 1
    }
  done
}

  local out
  out=$(orca status --json 2>/dev/null) || {

title: feat(context-handoff): port context-handoff tooling from #295 onto current main
body:
## What this is

Ports the context-handoff tooling from PR #295 ("feat(context-handoff): swap context-heavy crewmate for a fresh agent") onto current `main`. #295 predates the dedicated-session-per-task change (af0c0b1) and the backend abstraction (`bin/fm-backend.sh` + `bin/backends/*.sh`), so its `fm-spawn.sh` edits did not apply cleanly. Each piece was re-implemented on current `main`, not blind-merged.

Context-handoff swaps a context-heavy crewmate for a fresh agent on the **same worktree/branch** instead of a lossy `/compact`. The old agent dumps resume-context to `data/<id>/handoff.md`; `fm-spawn --reuse-worktree` retires the old endpoint and relaunches a fresh agent seeded with that dump.

## Ported pieces

- **`bin/fm-context.sh`** — read-only monitor. Reads `state/<id>.context`, divides by the window implied by meta `model=` (1M for Opus/Sonnet, 200k for smaller-context models), prints one line per task, exits non-zero if any task is `>=` the handoff threshold (default 60%, `FM_CTX_THRESHOLD`).
- **`bin/fm-ctx-hook.sh`** — claude Stop-hook helper. Every turn it (1) touches the turn-end signal and (2) records context tokens summed from the transcript's last `usage` record (`input + cache_creation + cache_read`). `state/<id>.context` is deliberately not a `*.status`/`*.turn-ended` file, so it never trips the watcher's signal scan.
- **`.agents/skills/context-handoff/SKILL.md`** — the swap playbook (dump → `--reuse-worktree` → FYI). Ported verbatim; its references match current `fm-spawn`/AGENTS.md.
- **`bin/fm-spawn.sh --reuse-worktree <id>`** — the agent swap (the hard part; see below).
- **AGENTS.md** — section 2 `state/<id>.context` inventory line, section 8 heartbeat step (run `fm-context.sh`, swap at `>=60%`), section 13 `context-handoff` trigger pointer.
- **`bin/fm-teardown.sh`** — removes `state/<id>.context` and the composed `state/<id>.reuse-brief.md` (main + child-home rm lines).
- **Tests** — `tests/fm-context.test.sh`, `tests/fm-ctx-hook.test.sh`, `tests/fm-spawn-reuse-worktree.test.sh`.

## Conflicts resolved (mainly `fm-spawn.sh`)

Current `fm-spawn.sh` differs substantially from #295's. The port composes `--reuse-worktree` with current logic:

- **Backend abstraction / `PANE_DIR`.** #295 assumed inline tmux. Current spawn routes through per-backend `create_task` functions that take the pane start-dir. Added a single `PANE_DIR` (project checkout normally; the existing worktree `WT` on a reuse spawn) threaded into every backend's `create_task` call, so a reuse spawn opens the pane directly in the worktree without `treehouse get`.
- **Old-endpoint retire via the backend-agnostic `fm_backend_kill`.** #295 killed tmux inline. The port retires the old endpoint with `fm_backend_kill "$backend" "$window" "$zellij_tab_id" "fm-$id"` — the same 4-arg per-backend form `fm-teardown.sh` uses — before creating the new endpoint (they share the `fm-<id>` window name), with a `sleep 0.5` to let the name free.
- **Stable window id (`#134`).** The current tmux branch returns a stable `WID`/`WT_TARGET`; the reuse path skips the `treehouse get` + worktree-detection block entirely (worktree already exists and was proven isolated at first spawn), so `WT_TARGET` is harmlessly unused there.
- **Meta recovery.** Reads `kind/worktree/project/mode/yolo/harness/model/effort/backend` from `state/<id>.meta`, resolved **before** backend/harness selection so recovered values feed those code paths unchanged. Aborts on missing meta, a vanished worktree, or a missing/empty handoff dump.
- **orca / secondmate refusal.** `--reuse-worktree` is refused with `--secondmate` and on the `orca` backend (Orca owns the worktree lifecycle).
- **claude Stop hook.** The hook now runs `fm-ctx-hook.sh` (turn-end + context recording) for **every** claude spawn, replacing the old bare `touch`, built with the same `json_escape`/`shell_quote` helpers the grok hook install uses.

No design change from #295 (threshold, harness applicability, auto-vs-ask default all preserved).

## Empirical verification (tmux, claude 2.1.206, 2026-07-10)

`shellcheck bin/fm-spawn.sh bin/fm-context.sh bin/fm-ctx-hook.sh bin/fm-teardown.sh tests/…` — the changed files produce **zero** findings; the only residual `SC1091` come from `fm-backend.sh`'s pre-existing variable-path `backends/*.sh` sources (untouched, and present on current `main`'s green CI).

New tests (all green):
```
tests/fm-context.test.sh          → ok - fm-context: all cases
tests/fm-ctx-hook.test.sh         → ok - fm-ctx-hook: all cases
tests/fm-spawn-reuse-worktree.test.sh → ok - fm-spawn --reuse-worktree: all cases
```
Existing spawn-adjacent suites still pass: `fm-spawn-batch`, `fm-spawn-dispatch-profile`, `fm-secondmate-harness`, `fm-grok-harness`.

End-to-end on an isolated tmux server (throwaway home + real git worktree, real claude):
1. Real `fm-spawn.sh --reuse-worktree` launched a claude agent in a tmux window opened directly in the worktree (no `treehouse get`); the installed `.claude/settings.local.json` Stop hook points at `fm-ctx-hook.sh` with the turn-end and `state/<id>.context` paths.
2. The live Stop hook wrote `state/<id>.context` (`37148` on a real turn); verified the summing formula against the real transcript (`12245 + 4810 + 19341 = 36396`).
3. `fm-context.sh <id>` read it live: `37148/1000000  3%` (rc 0); a forced `650000` value printed `65%  FLAG >=60%` (rc 1).
4. The swap (`fm-spawn.sh --reuse-worktree` again) retired the old pane (`pane_pid 1614501` → dead) and launched a fresh claude (`pane_pid 1654921`) on the **same worktree and branch `fm/<id>`**, seeded with the regenerated reuse-brief (original brief + handoff dump — the fresh agent read the dump and responded), and reset `state/<id>.context`.

### One observed nuance (not a design deviation)

On the **very first** turn after launch the Stop hook touched turn-end but did not write `state/<id>.context` (transcript's `usage` not yet flushed at that instant); every subsequent turn wrote it correctly. This is immaterial to context-handoff, which targets large multi-turn tasks checked at heartbeat time — by then the crewmate has completed many turns.

title: test: cover numeric tmux session targeting

Preserve existing behavior for non-numeric sessions, include a real-tmux regression test, and keep shell scripts shellcheck-clean. ## What Changed - Strengthens the real-tmux smoke test to verify repeated task-window creation in a numeric session preserves existing indexes and rejects duplicates. - Documents why tmux session targets require a trailing colon and records the numeric-session verification evidence. - Makes session-start missing-tool tests deterministic by controlling the `tasks-axi` fixture instead of relying on the host environment. title: fix: detect Git and centralize backend configuration
body:
## Intent

Slice 2 of the captain-ordered high-star documentation redundancy cleanup wave (firstmate scope), approved by the captain with docs/configuration.md as the declared shared owner: a docs-only consolidation establishing ONE owner for the three universal backend contracts the audit found copy-pasted across the five backend guides (the #372/#411/#332 five-doc re-edit class). (1) docs/configuration.md becomes the declared single owner, each with an explicit one-line ownership sentence so the Document step and humans know where the fact lives: the universal toolchain list (Toolchain section, now explicitly including git and gh with GitHub auth per the prior run's review finding, fixed between runs after that run failed terminally on the fix agent's usage limit), the task-selector vocabulary (Runtime backend section, the five selector-resolution sentences), and the tasks-axi compatibility definition (Backlog backend section). The Toolchain parenthetical defers tasks-axi version gates to the Backlog backend owner instead of restating them, and it absorbed the per-tool purpose clauses (treehouse pools worktrees, no-mistakes runs the pipeline, the axi tools' roles) that previously existed ONLY in the tmux guide's prerequisites - unique content deliberately moved into the owner rather than lost. (2) The five backend guides (tmux, herdr, zellij, orca, cmux) replace their verbatim universal-requirements parentheticals with a pointer to the owner plus only backend-specific items: herdr/zellij/cmux keep their jq and version-floor bullets, orca keeps its node-for-JSON-parsing bullet and the minus-tmux/treehouse exemption, tmux keeps its own install line. (3) Selector-vocabulary restatements in the zellij and cmux guides become pointers; architecture.md's and configuration.md's own trailing partial copies of the selector vocabulary are dropped. (4) CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Compatible means...' sentence becomes a pointer to the owner. (5) Two near-verbatim restatements of orca's bootstrap toolchain behavior (configuration.md carried it twice internally, the orca guide a third time) collapse into the single Toolchain copy. Deliberately untouched, per the wave contract: all empirical verification records in the backend guides, backend-specific setup/behavior/target-string sections, each guide's own backend-selection instructions (backend-specific user guidance, not a universal contract), and AGENTS.md plus the skills (those are the approved slice 3). Also deliberately deferred and documented rather than silently omitted: each guide's internal Setup-vs-Status selection-text duplication, which the audit did not name. PR body accounting (wave requirement): always-loaded AGENTS.md unchanged (slice 3 owns that reduction); full copies removed per contract: universal prereq list 6 copies -> 1 owner + 5 pointers, tasks-axi compatibility definition 7 copies -> 1 owner + pointers, selector vocabulary 4 prose copies -> 1 owner + 2 pointers, orca bootstrap-toolchain behavior 3 copies -> 1; files reduced to pointers: none removed, 7 files carry pointer lines instead of full copies; discoverability proof: every pointer names the owning file and section in the repo's established quoted-section link style, and the grep sweep shows zero remaining 'same universal requirements' phrasings or version-gate restatements outside the owner; checks run: full 59-script behavior suite green, repo-wide shellcheck green, CLAUDE.md and .claude/skills symlink assertions green, cross-reference grep sweep for all three contracts.

## What Changed

- Centralized universal toolchain, task-selector, and `tasks-axi` compatibility contracts in `docs/configuration.md`, replacing duplicated backend-guide and contributor prose with pointers.
- Updated bootstrap checks to detect a missing Git installation and provide installation guidance for standard and Orca toolchains, with regression coverage.
- Clarified README requirements for Git and an authenticated GitHub CLI.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Captain, the change is bounded documentation consolidation plus consistent Git prerequisite detection, with no material risk found.

    14	It moves in-scope `## Queued` items only and refuses `## In flight` and historical `## Done` records, which stay with their home for pruning or archiving.
    15	Handoff item bodies must use at least two leading spaces, and the helper refuses a selected item with a single-space or tab-indented continuation rather than risk orphaning it.
    16	Because bootstrap requires `tasks-axi` on `PATH` on every profile, that delegation works fleet-wide, and the `config/backlog-backend=manual` knob governs firstmate's own hand-editing of its backlog, not this validated helper.
    17	Compatible means the shared bootstrap probe accepts `tasks-axi --version` as 0.1.1 or newer, `tasks-axi update --help` exposes `--archive-body`, and `tasks-axi mv --help` exposes `[<id>...]` for the atomic multi-ID move introduced in 0.2.2 and required by handoff delegation.
    18	That sentence is the single owner of the tasks-axi compatibility definition; every other document points here instead of restating the version gates.
    24	## Runtime backend (config/backend / FM_BACKEND)
    25	
    26	For spawn-capable adapters, the runtime session-provider backend controls where task windows/endpoints are created, captured, sent to, watched, and killed.
    27	`tmux` is the verified reference backend (see [`docs/tmux-backend.md`](tmux-backend.md)); `herdr`, `zellij`, `orca`, and `cmux` are experimental spawn backends (see [`docs/herdr-backend.md`](herdr-backend.md), [`docs/zellij-backend.md`](zellij-backend.md), [`docs/orca-backend.md`](orca-backend.md), and [`docs/cmux-backend.md`](cmux-backend.md)).
    28	Treehouse remains the worktree provider for tmux, herdr, zellij, and cmux, since herdr, zellij, and cmux are session providers only; Orca provides both the task worktree and terminal endpoint.
    29	New spawns choose the backend in this order: an explicit `--backend` flag firstmate passes when it spawns a task, then `FM_BACKEND`, then the first non-empty line of local gitignored `config/backend`, then runtime auto-detection from `$TMUX`, `HERDR_ENV=1`, or cmux runtime signals, then default `tmux`.
    30	If more than one runtime marker is present, detection resolves innermost-first: `$TMUX` is checked before `HERDR_ENV=1`, which is checked before cmux's primary `CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID` marker and its documented fallback signals - tmux or herdr started from inside a cmux terminal is the innermost, currently-executing layer, while cmux itself (a terminal application, not a nestable multiplexer) is always checked last.
    31	See [`docs/cmux-backend.md`](cmux-backend.md#runtime-auto-detection) for why cmux can be selected when `CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID` is absent.
    32	Auto-detected herdr or cmux prints a stderr notice naming `config/backend` and `--backend tmux` as opt-outs; auto-detected tmux stays silent to preserve existing default behavior.
    33	Zellij and Orca are never auto-detected; select them by putting the name in a local `config/backend` file, by exporting `FM_BACKEND=<name>`, or by telling the first mate in chat.
    34	Any value other than `tmux`, `herdr`, `zellij`, `orca`, or `cmux` is rejected until another adapter is implemented and verified.
    35	`fm-spawn.sh` accepts `tmux`, `herdr`, `zellij`, `orca`, and `cmux` for ship and scout tasks; `backend=orca` and `backend=cmux` both still refuse `--secondmate` until secondmate launch semantics are designed for each.
    36	`codex-app` is not an accepted runtime backend yet; [`docs/codex-app-backend.md`](codex-app-backend.md) owns the Codex App boundary.
    37	The session-start secondmate liveness sweep uses a deeper `fm_backend_agent_alive` probe where verified.
    38	Today that probe can classify tmux and herdr secondmate endpoints as `alive`, `dead`, or `unknown`; zellij, Orca, and cmux report `unknown` until their own agent-process classifiers are verified.
    39	A herdr spawn additionally version-gates against the installed `herdr` binary's protocol and requires `jq`, refusing loudly on an incompatible or missing installation.
    40	A zellij spawn additionally version-gates against the installed `zellij` binary's version and requires `jq`, refusing loudly when either is missing or the version is older than 0.44.
    41	A cmux spawn additionally version-gates against the installed `cmux` binary's version, requires `jq`, and requires the control socket to be reachable and accessible (see [`docs/cmux-backend.md`](cmux-backend.md) "Setup" for the one-time socket-access configuration this needs; Automation mode is the recommended socket control mode, with Password mode supported via `config/cmux-socket-password`), refusing loudly and non-retryably on a `cmuxOnly`/unauthenticated socket.
    42	A backend spawn refusal from a missing dependency, version gate, or unauthenticated socket is terminal for that selected backend; firstmate surfaces it as a blocker instead of silently retrying another backend.
    43	Task meta records `backend=` only for a non-default backend; an absent `backend=` means `tmux`, preserving existing default-path meta files.
    44	A herdr task additionally records `herdr_session=`, `herdr_workspace_id=`, `herdr_tab_id=`, and `herdr_pane_id=`.
    45	A zellij task additionally records `zellij_session=`, `zellij_tab_id=`, and `zellij_pane_id=`.
    46	An Orca task additionally records `orca_worktree_id=` and `terminal=`, with `window=fm-<id>` kept as the shared firstmate alias.
    47	A cmux task additionally records `cmux_workspace_id=` and `cmux_surface_id=`.
    48	Task selectors for `fm-peek.sh`, `fm-send.sh`, and `fm-crew-state.sh` resolve centrally through `fm_backend_resolve_selector`.
    49	A selector containing `:` is passed through as an explicit backend endpoint escape hatch.
    50	Otherwise an exact task id matching `state/<id>.meta` wins before the legacy `fm-<id>` label fallback, so task ids that themselves start with `fm-` route to their own metadata instead of being stripped.
    51	A metadata-routed selector returns the recorded backend target (`terminal=` for Orca, otherwise `window=`), and matching explicit targets can still recover the recorded backend when metadata contains the same endpoint.
    52	Only metadata-routed task selectors carry secondmate-marker and Codex-harness context; explicit endpoint escape hatches do not.
    53	These five sentences are the single owner of the task-selector vocabulary; backend guides and other documents point here instead of restating the resolution order.
   130	## Harness support
   131	
   132	claude, codex, opencode, pi, and grok are all empirically verified; new harnesses get verified through a supervised trial task before joining the set.
   169	## Toolchain
   170	
   171	On session start the first mate detects what its required toolchain is missing or too old (tmux, node, git, gh with GitHub auth via `gh auth login`, treehouse with durable lease support, no-mistakes v1.31.2 or newer, gh-axi, chrome-devtools-axi, lavish-axi, compatible tasks-axi per "Backlog backend" above, and quota-axi), lists it with the exact install commands, and installs only after you say go.
   172	This section is the single owner of that universal toolchain list;

 ("Harness support", "Toolchain"); treehouse still provides the worktree, herdr only provides the session.
    24	

-- docs/zellij-backend.md --
    14	Prerequisites:
    15	
    16	- `zellij` itself, version 0.44 or newer (installed 0.44.0 verified) - see [zellij.dev](https://zellij.dev) for install instructions.
    17	- `jq`, required to parse zellij's JSON output: `brew install jq` (or your platform's package manager).
    18	- The universal firstmate prerequisites - a verified crew harness plus the required toolchain, owned by [`docs/configuration.md`](configuration.md) ("Harness support", "Toolchain"); treehouse still provides the worktree, zellij only provides the session.
    19	
    20	Select zellij by putting `zellij` in a local `config/backend` file - the durable way to pick it - or by exporting `FM_BACKEND=zellij` when you launch your harness for a one-off session; telling the first mate in chat to use zellij also works.
    21	Unlike tmux and herdr, zellij is **never** auto-detected - it always requires an explicit choice.
    22	A zellij spawn refuses loudly before creating a session container or acquiring a ship/scout worktree if `zellij` or `jq` is missing or the installed zellij is older than 0.44.

-- docs/orca-backend.md --

    17	- The universal firstmate prerequisites minus `tmux` and `treehouse` (Orca replaces both) - a verified crew harness plus the required toolchain, owned by [`docs/configuration.md`](configuration.md) ("Harness support", "Toolchain").
    18	
    19	Select Orca by putting `orca` in a local `config/backend` file - the durable way to pick it - or by exporting `FM_BACKEND=orca` when you launch your harness for a one-off session; telling the first mate in chat to use Orca also works.
    20	It is never auto-detected.

-- docs/cmux-backend.md --
    16	Prerequisites:
    17	
    18	- The cmux app itself, installed from [cmux.com](https://cmux.com) or `brew install --cask cmux`, version 0.64.17 or newer.
    19	- `jq`, required to parse cmux's JSON output: `brew install jq` (or your platform's package manager).
    20	- The universal firstmate prerequisites - a verified crew harness plus the required toolchain, owned by [`docs/configuration.md`](configuration.md) ("Harness support", "Toolchain"); treehouse still provides the worktree, cmux only provides the session.
    21	- The cmux CLI binary is not guaranteed to be on `PATH` after a plain app install (see "CLI is not on PATH by default" below) - the adapter falls back to the well-known bundle path automatically, so this is not a blocker, just something to be aware of if you want to run `cmux` yourself from a shell.

== Selector and contributor pointers ==
    57	Because every task in every firstmate home - primary or secondmate - shares this ONE session's tab bar with no per-home container split, and zellij enforces no tab-name uniqueness at all (verified: two tabs can share a name), two firstmate homes whose task ids happen to collide could send/peek/close each other's tabs.
    58	This is the exact gap a captain-directed no-mistakes review gate caught for the cmux backend (`docs/cmux-backend.md` "Task container shape") - cmux's fix was ported here for the identical reason, sharing its tag-derivation code (`bin/fm-backend-hometag-lib.sh`).
    59	
    60	The caller-facing task label stays `fm-<id>` in meta and briefs; task-selector resolution is the shared contract owned by [`docs/configuration.md`](configuration.md) ("Runtime backend").
    61	The actual zellij tab title a NEW task's tab is created with is home-scoped: `fm-<home-label>-<id>`.
    62	`<home-label>` is `firstmate` for the primary home, or `2ndmate-<id>` when `$FM_HOME/.fm-secondmate-home` contains a secondmate id, plus a short stable hash of the resolved `FM_ROOT` path - the same identity scheme as cmux's home label (`docs/cmux-backend.md` "Task container shape"), so e.g. `fm-firstmate-a1b2c3d4-fix-login-k3` or `fm-2ndmate-sm1-9f8e7d6c-fix-login-k3`.
    55	No first-run provisioning beyond the socket-access setup above and having `jq` installed; firstmate creates the workspace it needs on first spawn, launching the app itself (`open -a cmux`) if it is not already running.
    56	
    57	Watching and attaching: firstmate uses one workspace per task in whatever cmux window is currently open.
    58	Task selectors resolve through the shared contract owned by [`docs/configuration.md`](configuration.md) ("Runtime backend"), while the actual cmux workspace title is home-scoped as `fm-<home-label>-<id>`, for example `fm-firstmate-<8hex>-cmux-e2e-t1` in the primary home or `fm-2ndmate-<secondmate-id>-<8hex>-cmux-e2e-t1` in a secondmate home.
    59	You do not need to bring the window forward for routine supervision: from an active firstmate session, `bin/fm-peek.sh <id>` reads a task's surface without focusing it, and `FM_HOME=<this-firstmate-home> bin/fm-send.sh <id> "<text>"` steers it unless `FM_HOME` is already set to the active firstmate home - workspace/surface/pane creation all default `focus` to `false`, so an unattended spawn never steals your view.
    60	
    37	- Only shared material is tracked: `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.tasks.toml`, `.github/workflows/`, `bin/`, `.agents/skills/`, and `skills/`.
    38	  `.agents/skills/` holds agent-loaded skills that assume a live firstmate home and carry `metadata.internal: true` so installers such as [skills.sh](https://skills.sh) hide them from discovery; `skills/` holds standalone, installer-facing public skills with no firstmate dependency (see the README's "Two-tier skill layout").
    39	  Everything personal to one captain's fleet (`.env`, `data/`, `state/`, `config/`, `projects/`, `.no-mistakes/`) is gitignored; never commit it.
    40	  The root `.tasks.toml` is tracked `tasks-axi` config for `data/backlog.md`; compatible `tasks-axi` is the default backend for routine backlog mutations, with the compatibility definition owned by [`docs/configuration.md`](docs/configuration.md) ("Backlog backend").
    41	  A local `config/backlog-backend=manual` opt-out forces firstmate's routine backlog updates to hand-editing and stays gitignored; validated secondmate handoffs still delegate through `tasks-axi mv`.
    42	  A local `config/backend` file explicitly overrides runtime auto-detection for new task endpoints and stays gitignored; spawn-supported values are `tmux` plus experimental `herdr`, `zellij`, `orca`, and `cmux`, while `codex-app` is documented only in `docs/codex-app-backend.md`.

title: docs: centralize firstmate operating contracts
body:
## Intent Slice 3, the final and coordinated-landing slice of the captain-ordered high-star documentation redundancy cleanup wave (firstmate scope), approved by the captain with the new agent-only skill named bootstrap-diagnostics: extract the audit-identified conditional and situational material from the always-loaded AGENTS.md into correctly triggered skills, deep docs, and script headers, preserving EVERY load-bearing invariant at its trigger point via the repo's own inline-stub pattern (the away-mode stub is the model). This changes what the firstmate agent reads, not what it does: every operative rule keeps an inline stub with the trigger condition and safety-critical facts, and every moved contract has exactly one declared owner plus pointers. AGENTS.md drops 941 -> 785 lines (116,733 -> 91,353 bytes, roughly 29k -> 22.8k tokens loaded into every session of every fleet member). The moves: (1) section 3's per-line bootstrap diagnostics handbook (MISSING/NEEDS_GH_AUTH/TANGLE/CREW_HARNESS_OVERRIDE/CREW_DISPATCH/FLEET_SYNC/SECONDMATE_SYNC/SECONDMATE_LIVENESS/TASKS_AXI/NUDGE_SECONDMATES/FMX) moves whole into the new .agents/skills/bootstrap-diagnostics skill, registered in the section 13 trigger index; the inline stub keeps silence-means-good, load-on-any-line, the detect-consent-install rule, and the do-not-dispatch-until-tools-and-auth gate. docs/configuration.md's NUDGE_SECONDMATES pointer retargets to the skill. (2) Section 4's crew-dispatch JSON schema and per-field semantics move to docs/configuration.md 'Crew dispatch profiles', flipping the prior pointer direction; the every-dispatch procedure (consult at intake, best-fit judgment, precedence list, explicit-flags contract, spawn backstop, never-select-unverified) stays fully inline. (3) Section 4's quota-balanced algorithm detail moves to bin/fm-dispatch-select.sh's header, now its declared single owner; that header growth required converting the script's usage() from a fixed sed range to the dynamic awk header extraction PR #438 established for fm-brief.sh (the only code change, output-shape-preserving, and tests/fm-dispatch-select.test.sh passes). (4) Section 7's spawn resolution narrative and 16-line example sprawl compress to 6 canonical forms plus operative rules, with bin/fm-spawn.sh's header (verified near-verbatim owner) declared for the resolution contract; the isolated-worktree assertion, refusal-is-a-blocker rule, and post-spawn duties stay inline. (5) Section 7's teardown landed-work mechanics move to bin/fm-teardown.sh's header (verified verbatim owner); section 1 hard rule 3's containment pointer retargets there; the fork benign case and never-force rule stay inline. (6) Section 8's watcher classification narrative compresses to an operative summary pointing at docs/architecture.md 'Event-driven supervision', which was verified to already own every dropped mechanism fact; all operative supervision rules (keep one live cycle, no turn ends blind, drain first, the on-wake ladder, never-pkill, guard responses, secondmate idle-pane exception, token discipline) stay inline, and the away-mode stub is untouched. (7) Secondmate restatements across sections 3, 4, 6, and 7 (registry schema, sync mechanics, inheritable-config propagation including the literal crew-harness file nuance, backlog-handoff judgment) consolidate into the secondmate-provisioning skill, now their declared owner; AGENTS.md keeps routing-by-scope, the idle contract, local-only-stays-main, and the load triggers. (8) Section 14's X-mode cadence mechanism paragraphs move to docs/configuration.md 'X mode (.env)', which CLOSES ISSUE https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/363 - please include 'Closes #363' in the PR body; the inline stub keeps .env activation semantics, the destructive-action carve-out, the fmx-respond trigger, the keep-watcher-armed posture, and the terminal-wake final-follow-up duty that fires on wakes the skill is not loaded for. Deliberate constraints: CLAUDE.md stays a symlink; no behavior change beyond the usage() extraction pattern; no test changes; landing timing is coordinated by the fleet operator because AGENTS.md is live fleet infrastructure. Known pre-existing flake unrelated to this diff: tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh's fleet-sync-timeout case is load-sensitive (its virtualized timeout clock can outrun the fake fleet-sync child's real startup); it fired once in the full-suite run and passes 2/2 in isolation, this slice does not touch fm-bootstrap.sh, and this docs-only PR must not attempt to fix it. PR body accounting (wave requirement): always-loaded AGENTS.md 941 lines / ~29k tokens -> 785 lines / ~22.8k tokens (~6.3k tokens saved per session per fleet member); full copies removed per contract: bootstrap handbook 1 always-loaded copy -> conditional skill, dispatch schema 1 full copy -> configuration.md owner + pointer, quota-balanced algorithm 1 prose copy -> script-header owner + one-line summaries in AGENTS.md and configuration.md, spawn narrative and teardown mechanics 1 AGENTS.md copy each -> script-header owners + stubs, watcher narrative 1 AGENTS.md copy -> architecture.md owner + operative summary, secondmate sync/propagation/schema/handoff 2-3 copies each -> secondmate-provisioning owner, X-mode cadence 1 AGENTS.md copy -> configuration.md owner; files: 1 new 47-line conditional skill, 0 files removed; proof unique content remains discoverable: every stub names its owner file and section explicitly, the section 13 index gained the new skill's trigger, and the cross-reference grep sweep verified every bin/ header and doc reference to AGENTS.md section numbers remains valid; checks run: full 59-script behavior suite (green except the documented pre-existing bootstrap flake, which passes in isolation), repo-wide shellcheck, bash -n toolbelt loop, both symlink assertions, tests/fm-dispatch-select.test.sh focused rerun, and the cross-reference sweep. ## What Changed - Moved conditional bootstrap-diagnostic handling into a new agent-only skill and registered it from the session-start guidance. - Consolidated dispatch-profile, quota-selection, secondmate-sync, teardown, watcher, and X-mode cadence contracts under their configuration, architecture, skill, or script-header owners, with `AGENTS.md` retaining trigger-specific stubs. - Updated `fm-dispatch-select.sh` help generation to render its documented selector contract. Closes #363 ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, this is a bounded documentation-ownership extraction whose sole executable change preserves selection behavior by dynamically emitting the script header. ## Testing The already-successful full baseline suite was supplemented with the focused dispatch-selector test and a live CLI-help capture; the evidence shows the full quota-balanced contract is rendered for users while skill triggers, ownership pointers, and the CLAUDE symlink remain intact.
Evidence: CLI and documentation-contract evidence ```text Validation evidence for target 725d83d4f709a685e41c682f709958f24d4c4fbb Compared with base 52241a5fae67be90f14fa58275fd4cd86e0dd062. END-USER CLI SURFACE $ bin/fm-dispatch-select.sh --help 2>&1 Resolve one already-matched crew-dispatch rule to a concrete profile. Usage: fm-dispatch-select.sh [--select ] [--quota-json ] [] Input may be a full rule object with `use` and optional `select`, a single profile object, or an ordered array of profile objects. Output is one compact JSON profile object on stdout. quota-balanced is deterministic, and this header is the single owner of its contract: - It runs quota-axi --json (or the --quota-json fixture). - Per candidate vendor it takes the minimum percentRemaining across that vendor's GENERAL windows only - Claude five_hour and seven_day, Codex five_hour and weekly - ignoring model-scoped windows such as model:fable and model:codex_bengalfox:*. - The vendor with the higher minimum remaining quota wins; an exact tie between equally trusted candidates uses the first array element. - Stale-but-cached general-window numbers are usable, but a fresh candidate wins unless the stale candidate's minimum is at least the stale-clear margin higher (default 20 points - the definition of "clearly less constrained"). - A vendor absent from quota output, or with no usable general windows, is unavailable; selection happens among available candidates. - If quota-axi is missing, exits non-zero, returns unparseable JSON, or no candidate is usable, the reason is logged to stderr and the first array element is printed - quota trouble never blocks dispatch. quota-balanced uses quota-axi --json unless --quota-json supplies a fixture. FM_DISPATCH_QUOTA_AXI overrides the quota command. FM_DISPATCH_STALE_CLEAR_MARGIN overrides the default 20 point stale margin. INDEPENDENT CONTRACT REVIEW - The executable change replaces a fixed `sed -n '2,10p'` help slice with an `awk` extractor that prints every contiguous leading comment line and stops at the first non-comment line. - The direct help output above includes the newly added deep-header rules for general windows, stale-cache margin, unavailable vendors, and no-block fallback. - `AGENTS.md` retains the section 3 safety stub: detect, then consent, then install; never install without current-session approval; do not dispatch until required tools and GitHub auth are available. - `AGENTS.md` section 3 says silence needs no handling and directs every printed diagnostic or capability line to `bootstrap-diagnostics`. - `AGENTS.md` section 13 registers `bootstrap-diagnostics` for MISSING, NEEDS_GH_AUTH, TANGLE, CREW_HARNESS_OVERRIDE, CREW_DISPATCH, FLEET_SYNC, SECONDMATE_SYNC, SECONDMATE_LIVENESS, TASKS_AXI, NUDGE_SECONDMATES, and FMX; the new skill's front matter declares the identical trigger set and says it is agent-only. - `AGENTS.md` keeps operational dispatch handling inline while naming `docs/configuration.md` as the canonical schema/per-field owner and `bin/fm-dispatch-select.sh` as the quota-balanced contract owner. - `AGENTS.md` names `bin/fm-spawn.sh` as the full spawn-resolution owner and `bin/fm-teardown.sh` as the full landed-work owner, preserving the inline blocker and never-force rules nearby. - `docs/configuration.md` declares itself the X-mode cadence owner and points the NUDGE_SECONDMATES send procedure to `bootstrap-diagnostics`. - `CLAUDE.md` remains a symlink to `AGENTS.md`; the target has 786 physical AGENTS.md lines including its final newline. ```

title: feat(crowsnest): thread/reply context + fix post-tool credential loading
body:
## Crowsnest iteration 2: thread/reply context + post-tool credential fix

Improves the Crowsnest (firstmate's opt-in two-way Google Chat ↔ live-firstmate relay). Inert unless enabled, so no behaviour change for anyone who hasn't opted in.

### 1. Thread / reply context (headline)
When the captain replies inside a thread, the relay previously forwarded only the message text — the `local-agents-chat` subprocess agent forwards only `space`/`thread`/`sender`/`mode`/`text` (no replied-to message, no raw event, no history), so the relay alone can't see what the captain is replying to.

- New `bin/fm-crowsnest-context.{sh,py}` read recent thread messages back via an authenticated `spaces.messages.list` (reusing the backend `ChatClient` credentials) and merge `thread_context`, `reply_to`, and `sender_display_name` into `state/chat-inbox/<id>.json`.
- The relay spawns enrichment **detached** *after* the durable base entry + wake are written, so the instant-ack contract is preserved and a slow/failing read never loses a message. Everything is best-effort and degrades to today's exact text-only behaviour on any failure (no thread, no interpreter, no backend, no creds, no scope, network error).
- The merge re-checks the inbox entry still exists immediately before replacing it, so a message the live session already answered and deleted is never resurrected as a duplicate.
- Gated by `CROWSNEST_THREAD_CONTEXT` (on by default). `FMC_CONTEXT_SYNC` (inline) and `FMC_CONTEXT_FIXTURE` (canned `messages.list`) make the whole path testable offline with no GCP.
- `reply_to` is intentionally best-effort ("the last prior message in the thread", not a guaranteed quote) because the true quoted-message metadata isn't forwarded by the backend.
- `fmc-respond` and `docs/crowsnest.md` updated to compose using the context, degrading gracefully when absent.

### 2. Post-tool credential fix (known 403 bug)
The post tool never auto-loaded the backend's service-account credentials: it passed `--config=None`, and `load_config(None)` reads **no** file, leaving `credentials_path` empty — so posts fell back to user ADC and 403'd ("insufficient authentication scopes") unless the operator manually exported `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`.

- New shared helper `bin/fm_crowsnest_chat.py` resolves the backend's **default** config path when none is given (mirroring `local-agents run`, whose `--config` argparse default is `str(default_config_path())`), honouring `LOCAL_AGENTS_CREDENTIALS_PATH` and `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`. Verified: **OLD → `adc` (403), NEW → `service_account`**.
- One owner for credential resolution, shared by both the post and context tools.

### 3. Easy wins
- The captain's display name is harvested for free from the context read.
- `fm-crowsnest.sh status` gains a `posting id` line (reuses `ChatClient.posting_identity`) so the exact ADC-vs-service-account 403 is diagnosable at a glance.

### Docs & tests
- `docs/crowsnest.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, `docs/examples/crowsnest.env`, and the `fmc-respond` skill updated. `AGENTS.md` deliberately unchanged (conditional detail belongs in the doc/skill per the coding guidelines).
- 10 new hermetic tests (reader dedup/order/bound, merge, no-thread/empty/disabled/never-resurrect no-ops, relay enrichment, kill-switch, credential-fallback resolver). Full `fm-crowsnest` suite: 32 checks. `shellcheck` clean.

### Notes for the reviewer
- Validated through the no-mistakes pipeline: **rebase** skipped (branch is exactly `origin/main` + this one commit; the gate's stale baseline flagged unrelated fork history that's already on the PR base), **review** passed at low risk after two auto-fixes folded in here (the resurrection guard and the diagnostic never-raises contract). The **test** step could not run in the gate host because it lacks `tmux` (the `.no-mistakes.yaml` test command hard-requires it); all diff-touched suites pass locally and the gate's fix agent independently confirmed every remaining failure is a pre-existing environmental gap (tmux / tasks-axi / Node `.ts` / `CLAUDECODE` leak), none touching this diff.

### Proposed for later (not built here)
- Have the backend forward `sender_display_name` / the raw event (incl. true `quotedMessageMetadata`) / prior `history` to the subprocess, so context needs no read-back call and `reply_to` can be the actual quoted message. Requires a change to the external `local-agents-chat` package.
- User-auth context read for private history where the bot's `chat.bot` scope can't list messages.

title: fix(cmux): close last workspace during teardown
body:
## Intent Fix fm-teardown.sh failing to close a cmux workspace when it is the currently SELECTED workspace in the cmux app. Root cause, reproduced live against real cmux 0.64.17: cmux keeps every window at >=1 workspace, so close-workspace on the ONLY workspace in a window silently no-ops (returns OK but the workspace stays). The last workspace in a window is always the selected one, which is why this presented as 'the selected workspace will not close'; a merely-selected workspace that shares its window with another closes fine. close-window and raw window.close also no-op for a window holding a live terminal session (cmux cannot close such a window over the control socket), and exiting the shell just makes cmux respawn a surface, so none of those are viable rescues. Chosen fix in bin/backends/cmux.sh: add fm_backend_cmux_window_of_workspace, which walks list-windows --json plus each window's own 'workspace list --window' (because 'workspace list' without --window is scoped to the current window only), to detect when the target is the last workspace in its window. fm_backend_cmux_kill then creates a throwaway DEFAULT sibling workspace (new-workspace --window --focus false, deliberately UNNAMED so it never carries an fm-- title and recovery/list_live ignore it) before closing the target, so the close lands. The window keeps a fresh default workspace, which is cmux's own 'closed the last tab' outcome and the closest reachable result given a window cannot be socket-closed. Non-last teardown closes directly, exactly as before, with no sibling. Deliberate scope decisions a diff-only reviewer would not know: (1) the guarded-cleanup safety contract in tests/cmux-test-safety.sh is intentionally left UNCHANGED - the fix only ever closes the target task workspace and never enumerates or closes non-target workspaces; the created sibling is a new default workspace, not a close. (2) The last-in-window path is covered by fake-CLI unit tests (both branches + the helper) plus a manual real-cmux verification recorded in docs/cmux-backend.md, but intentionally NOT by an automated real-cmux smoke test, because closing the last workspace inherently leaves a window cmux cannot socket-close, so a live end-to-end test cannot self-clean; the smoke test instead covers the version-fragile window/count detection primitive residue-free. (3) A related current-window-scoping limitation of 'workspace list' (affecting label-based recovery only for a task parked in a NON-current window) was observed and documented as out-of-scope rather than fixed, to keep the change tight. This is a firstmate-repo change following the firstmate coding guidelines: the durable backend knowledge is placed in docs/cmux-backend.md (not the top-level AGENTS.md operating contract), with one-owner cross-references; scripts stay shellcheck-clean; tracked Markdown is one-sentence-per-line with plain dashes. ## What Changed - Locate a task workspace's containing cmux window and count its member workspaces from the same per-window response. - During teardown, add an unfocused unnamed sibling before closing a task workspace that is last in its window, while retaining direct closure for other workspaces. - Document cmux's last-workspace behavior, including the retained default workspace after teardown and current-window discovery limitations. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the change is narrowly scoped to cmux teardown and now derives the workspace count from the membership-confirming response. ## Testing The supplied full-suite baseline passed; targeted cmux tests passed; a controlled end-to-end adapter transcript exercised last and shared-window teardown paths; and live cmux 0.64.17 answered PONG. No UI screenshot applies to this shell-backend change, and no lint or static analysis was run per instruction.

Scenario: shared workspace in its cmux window Adapter exit: 0 Observed cmux control-socket calls: list-windows --json --id-format uuids workspace list --json --id-format uuids --window window-shared close-workspace --workspace workspace-task Result: task workspace closed directly; no sibling was created. ```

title: feat(self-fix): worktree-based self-fix flow for firstmate's own tracked code
body:
## Intent Fix bin/fm-self-fix.sh brief-existence precheck to honor FM_HOME. When FM_HOME is set to a directory other than the repo root, firstmate's operational data (including briefs) lives under FM_HOME/data/, not FM_ROOT/data/. The precheck was checking FM_ROOT/data/ and false-refusing even when the brief existed at FM_HOME/data/. The fix resolves FM_HOME and DATA the same way fm-spawn.sh and fm-brief.sh do (FM_HOME="${FM_HOME:-${FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE:-$FM_ROOT}}", DATA="${FM_DATA_OVERRIDE:-$FM_HOME/data}"), then checks the brief at $DATA/$ID/brief.md and prints the resolved path in the error message. The scratch worktree root stays outside FM_HOME - unchanged behavior. A regression test at tests/fm-self-fix.test.sh covers the FM_HOME-differs case and the missing-brief-diagnostic-message case. Shellcheck clean on both changed files. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-self-fix.sh`, which creates an isolated plain `git worktree` of the firstmate repo on a `fix/` branch rooted outside any `FM_HOME` and launches a crewmate into it via `fm-spawn.sh --worktree`, so the primary checkout never leaves its default branch while a shared-material fix still ships through the gate; the brief-existence precheck now resolves `FM_HOME`/`DATA` the same way `fm-spawn.sh` and `fm-brief.sh` do and reports the resolved `$DATA//brief.md` path on failure. - Reworked `fm-spawn.sh` to assert the resolved worktree is a genuine isolated worktree distinct from the primary checkout before launch, added the `--worktree` self-fix path (recorded as `selffix=1` in meta), and taught `fm-teardown.sh` to remove a self-fix worktree with `git worktree remove`. - Added `tests/fm-self-fix.test.sh` covering the `FM_HOME`-differs and missing-brief-diagnostic cases (made hermetic via a worktree guard), extended `tests/lib.sh`/`tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh` to clear operational-home selector env vars, and updated AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and docs to document the self-fix flow and `FM_SELFFIX_ROOT`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Well-bounded change (a small FM_HOME-aware precheck, a --worktree spawn path, and matching teardown/test coverage); the prior hermeticity finding is fixed, and the one remaining issue is a defensive test-isolation gap, not a product-behavior risk. ## Testing The baseline suite (all tests/*.test.sh) already passed, and I ran the targeted `tests/fm-self-fix.test.sh` (both cases green). For product-level evidence I built an end-to-end CLI transcript running the pre-fix script against the fixed one under an FM_HOME that differs from the repo root with the brief under `$FM_HOME/data/`: the old version false-refuses with "no brief at data/...", the fixed version finds the brief and advances past the precheck (stopping at the later worktree guard), and the missing-brief case now names the resolved FM_HOME path. This is a CLI/bin change with no UI surface, so the appropriate artifact is the command transcript rather than a screenshot. Worktree left clean.
Evidence: fm-self-fix FM_HOME precheck before/after transcript ### BEFORE fix (v1b16a82): precheck read $FM_ROOT/data/ -> false refusal error: no brief at data/fix-typo-x7/brief.md (author it first) exit=1 ### AFTER fix (current): resolves $FM_HOME/data/ -> brief found, passes precheck error: worktree path already exists: .../selffix-scratch/fix-typo-x7 exit=1 ### Missing-brief diagnostic names the resolved FM_HOME path error: no brief at .../other-home/data/missing-b2/brief.md (author it first) exit=1 ```text ## fm-self-fix.sh brief precheck honors FM_HOME (bug fix, commit d845527) Setup: FM_HOME= distinct from repo root; brief authored at $FM_HOME/data/fix-typo-x7/brief.md ### BEFORE fix (v1b16a82): precheck read $FM_ROOT/data/ -> false refusal error: no brief at data/fix-typo-x7/brief.md (author it first) exit=1 ### AFTER fix (current): resolves $FM_HOME/data/ -> brief found, passes precheck error: worktree path already exists: /tmp/tmp.HQ7x0fNADN/selffix-scratch/fix-typo-x7 exit=1 ### Missing-brief diagnostic names the resolved FM_HOME path error: no brief at /tmp/tmp.HQ7x0fNADN/other-home/data/missing-b2/brief.md (author it first) exit=1 ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

⚠️ **Rebase** - 1 warning - ⚠️ `.agents/skills/afk/SKILL.md` - branch carries 2 commit(s) that exist on your local main branch but were never pushed to origin/main; rebasing would bundle this unrelated work (147 file(s)) into the PR: - 1b16a82 feat(self-fix): worktree-based self-fix flow for firstmate's own tracked code (#2) - 6428b86 fix(spawn): wait for genuine isolated worktree, not just any non-project path (#1) Push main to origin, or rebase your branch onto origin/main, before gating.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 warning - ⚠️ `tests/fm-self-fix.test.sh:33` - tests/fm-self-fix.test.sh: test_brief_found_with_fmhome_set is not hermetic. With the brief present, fm-self-fix.sh passes the precheck and proceeds to `git -C "$FM_ROOT" worktree add "$WT" -b fix/selffix-brief-a1 ...` against the REAL repo ($ROOT), then execs fm-spawn.sh --backend tmux. So merely running this test creates a persistent `fix/selffix-brief-a1` branch plus a git worktree admin entry in the repo under review and launches a real tmux spawn as a side effect. The temp-dir cleanup (rm -rf) removes the worktree directory but not the branch or the git worktree registration, so it leaks state; a second run then fails at the branch-exists check (still with no 'no brief' text, so the assertion silently still passes). This runs in the pipeline's test step inside a worktree of this same repo, where the leaked branch/worktree/tmux window can interfere. This directly undermines the fix's own regression test: fm-self-fix.sh resolves DATA="${FM_DATA_OVERRIDE:-$FM_HOME/data}", so both new tests in tests/fm-self-fix.test.sh assert on a path computed from FM_HOME only when FM_DATA_OVERRIDE is unset. If a live firstmate session (or CI env) exports FM_DATA_OVERRIDE, test_brief_found_with_fmhome_set reads the wrong data dir and its 'no brief' assertion fails, and test_brief_missing_prints_resolved_path could even find a real brief. The comment claims to 'Clear the operational-home selectors up front' but leaves the very selector the self-fix brief precheck keys on. title: feat: add Oh My Pi (omp) harness adapter
body:
## What

Adds **omp** (Oh My Pi, a Pi fork) as a first-class firstmate harness —
primary + crew — alongside claude / codex / opencode / pi / grok.

## How it works

- **Detection** (`fm-harness.sh`, `fm-lock.sh`): omp sets both `OMPCODE=1`
  and `CLAUDECODE=1`, so `detect_own` checks `OMPCODE` **first** (unique to
  omp; Claude Code never sets it). The lock regex matches omp as a path/word
  component (`(^|/| )omp( |$)`) so it can't collide with "compose"/"components".
- **Launch** (`fm-spawn.sh`, `fm-tmux-lib.sh`): `omp --auto-approve … -e <ext>`
  template with model/effort flags and the state-resident extension paths.
- **Supervision** (`.omp/extensions/`): two project extensions ported from the
  Pi supervisors and kept in lockstep — a turn-end guard and a background-wake
  watcher. OMP has no `agent_settled` event, so the guard listens on `turn_end`
  (documented tradeoff: it re-nags on each blind turn until armed, vs Pi's
  once-per-run; safe — the `guardFollowupActive` latch prevents self-nagging).
- **Session start** (`fm-session-start.sh`): `OMP_WATCH_EXTENSION` loaded-check,
  twin of the Pi block.
- **Repair line** (`fm-supervision-instructions.sh`): omp-specific
  `fm_watch_arm_omp` guidance.
- **Teardown** (`fm-teardown.sh`): cleans the per-task `state/<id>.omp-ext.ts`.

## Tests / verification

- `tests/fm-omp-primary-types.test.sh` — strict `tsc` no-emit typecheck of the

title: refactor(x-mode): consolidate meta-rewrite helpers into one primitive
body:
## Intent

Refactor the X-mode meta-link helpers in bin/fm-x-lib.sh to reduce duplicated complexity introduced by commit a80b62d (multiple X-mode follow-ups), while keeping behavior byte-identical. The three state/<id>.meta rewriters (fmx_meta_link_set, fmx_meta_followups_set, fmx_meta_link_clear) each repeated the same temp-file/grep-strip/append/mv atomic-rewrite dance with identical 'rm -f tmp; return 1' cleanup boilerplate on every step, and duplicated the link-key strip regex '^x_request=|^x_request_ts=|^x_followups='. I extracted a private _fmx_meta_rewrite primitive that takes a strip pattern and literal lines to append, plus a FMX_META_LINK_KEYS constant as the single source of truth for the strip pattern; each public helper now expresses only its distinct part while keeping its own <meta>-exists precheck (which intentionally differs: link_set/followups_set hard-return 1 on a missing meta, link_clear returns 0). This is a pure quality refactor, no functional change; the full X-mode test suite (tests/fm-x-mode.test.sh), including the TMPDIR-independence and preserve-other-lines cases, passes unchanged.

## What Changed

- Extracted a private `_fmx_meta_rewrite` primitive in `bin/fm-x-lib.sh` that performs the shared atomic temp-file/strip/append/`mv` rewrite of `state/<id>.meta`, replacing the duplicated cleanup boilerplate previously repeated across each rewriter.
- Introduced a `FMX_META_LINK_KEYS` constant as the single source of truth for the link-key strip pattern (`x_request=`/`x_request_ts=`/`x_followups=`).
- Reworked `fmx_meta_link_set`, `fmx_meta_followups_set`, and `fmx_meta_link_clear` to delegate to the primitive while keeping their distinct meta-exists prechecks (link/followups hard-return 1 on a missing meta, clear returns 0); behavior is unchanged.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: A well-bounded, behavior-preserving refactor that deduplicates three atomic meta-rewrite helpers into one primitive; each code path was verified equivalent to the original, including strip patterns, the numeric guard, and the intentional missing-meta precheck divergence.

title: feat(backends): rewrite orca adapter to talk to daemon directly via bin/fmod + opencode TUI composer fix
body:
Replace the orca CLI integration (which cannot run while the orca GUI holds the single-instance lock) with a firstmate-owned daemon client (bin/fmod) over the orca daemon's NDJSON Unix-socket protocol. Adapter contract is unchanged; fm-spawn.sh, fm-peek.sh, fm-teardown.sh, and the watcher all see the same function signatures.

Adjacent fixes:

- fm_backend_orca_composer_state recognizes opencode TUI's left-only ┃ composer border with the ╹▀▀▀... bottom underline, distinguishes snapshot RPC failure (send-failed) from no-bordered-row (unknown), and uses sed for whitespace trim (the prior bash expansion was silently broken on inputs with leading whitespace).
- fm_backend_orca_remove_worktree surfaces git failures (no longer swallowed with || true), deletes the fm/<name> branch after worktree removal so retries of the same task id don't hit 'branch already exists', and falls back to the worktree's grandparent for main_repo resolution when the .git pointer has been swept.
- fm_backend_orca_worktree_create rolls back the fm/<name> branch on fmod create failure, recreates the daemon session if a stale-cwd attach is detected (create-or-attach race), uses mktemp for per-spawn stderr capture, and is the single source of truth for branch cleanup.
- fm_backend_orca_runtime_check JSON-parses fmod info instead of grepping for a specific JSON shape.
- fm-fleet-sync.sh skips projects/_orca-wt/ during the projects scan (it is the orca backend's internal worktree bucket, not a real project).
- fm-teardown.sh ignores .fm-orca-session in the dirty check (every orca worktree starts with this untracked marker).
- fm-bootstrap.sh lists fmod + python3 instead of the orca CLI for backend=orca spawns.
- fmod uses os.path.expanduser for socket/token/pidfile defaults (portable across users), reports a structured {daemon_reachable: false, daemon_error: ...} on cold-setup OSError instead of a traceback, and unwraps the {sessions: [...]} envelope in 'list'.

Tests: 26/26 passing in tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh. Live verification: fmod smoke + real fm-spawn.sh --backend orca end-to-end (session created, crewmate booted, status written, snapshot/send/kill all work).

title: feat(bin): add fm-dash.sh live read-only fleet dashboard
body: One numbered block per in-flight state/*.meta: current state via fm-crew-state.sh, recorded PR URL, pane Usage/Weekly gauge, and the worktree path (home= for secondmates) as an OSC 8 editor hyperlink. title: feat(herdr): nest Treehouse task workspaces
body:
## Summary

- add native Herdr child workspaces for eligible Treehouse-backed secondmate tasks while preserving legacy and non-Herdr layouts
- preserve split Treehouse/Herdr ownership through spawn, recovery, snapshot/view, and teardown
- normalize read-only Arena runtime metadata into fleet surfaces
- harden the Herdr lab helper for bounded names and stopped-default session isolation
- require durable child workspace ID and canonical Treehouse path identity before husk recovery may close a presentation

## Validation

- `bash tests/fm-backend.test.sh`
- `bash tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh`
- `bash tests/fm-backend-herdr-respawn-idem-e2e.test.sh`
- `bash tests/fm-fleet-snapshot-view.test.sh`
- `bash tests/fm-spawn-batch.test.sh`
- `bash tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh`
- `bash tests/fm-teardown.test.sh`
- `bash tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh`
- `bash tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh`
- `nix shell nixpkgs#shellcheck -c shellcheck bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh tests/*.sh`
- isolated Herdr 0.7.3 lab proof recorded in `docs/herdr-backend.md`: native exact-task child creation from an existing Treehouse path, parent association, presentation-only close, and guarded Treehouse return with protected sessions unchanged

## Caveat

A concurrent full-suite pass hit the timing-sensitive fleet-sync bootstrap fixture: it captured the expected 59-second timeout line but not the two expected partial output lines while ShellCheck was running concurrently.
The isolated `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` rerun passed all cases, including that exact timeout/partial-output fixture.

title: fix: suppress stale churn during legitimate idle waits
body:
## Intent Fix the watcher's idle-crew stale-churn gap. A trailing paused: status must absorb stale wakes on the existing bounded long recheck cadence even when the latest matching no-mistakes run is terminal, because a cancelled run is normal for an external wait. A done/checks-passed run that is still monitoring a checks-green PR for merge or close must use the same bounded idle cadence, leaving state/.check.sh as the actual merge wake path. Entering either legitimate idle state must clear or suppress wedge-escalation accumulation. Preserve the safety boundary: silent mid-work stops and real terminal failures must still surface. Extend colocated watcher/classifier regression tests, keep touched scripts shellcheck-clean, and update only the authoritative Event-driven supervision contract in docs/architecture.md. ## What Changed - Classify cancelled-run pauses and checks-green PR monitoring as legitimate idle waits, absorbing stale-pane churn on the bounded recheck cadence while clearing wedge state. - Preserve captain-visible safety signals by revalidating cached idle states so failed runs, parked gates, and silent stops surface immediately, while merge-wait cadence survives missing status files and pane-hash churn. - Expand regression coverage and supervision documentation, make prompt-glyph parsing locale-safe, and refresh affected compatibility fixtures. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the change is bounded to watcher idle-state classification and cadence, fails closed on failed and parked runs, and its state transitions and regression coverage are internally consistent. ## Testing The successful full-suite baseline was supplemented with focused watcher and wake-queue tests plus a production-watcher CLI fixture: legitimate idle states stayed quiet until bounded recheck, merge checks remained actionable, wedge state cleared, and unsafe stops surfaced; reviewer-visible CLI evidence was captured and the worktree stayed clean.

Evidence: Focused watcher regression suite ```text ok - signal_reason_is_actionable: benign absorbed, captain verbs and coalesced batches surfaced ok - stale_is_terminal: terminal status surfaces, non-terminal and no-status are benign ok - scan_captain_relevant_statuses lists only captain-relevant statuses ok - classifier primitives: last line, captain-relevance, window->task, FM_CAPTAIN_RE override ok - crew_is_provably_working: only working+run-step/pane is provable; idle/finished/parked/failed/unknown surface ok - status_is_paused: only the leading paused verb matches, and paused is not captain-relevant ok - crew_absorb_class: active work, terminal pauses, merge waits, and failures preserve the safety boundary ok - signal_crew_provably_working: benign only when every referenced crew is provably working ok - a no-verb signal whose crew is provably working is absorbed (no exit, no queue, suppressor advanced, beacon present) ok - a bare turn-end whose crew is provably working (busy pane) is absorbed ok - a bare turn-end whose crew is not provably working is surfaced (the swallowed-finish fix) ok - a no-verb working: note whose crew is idle with no running pipeline is surfaced ok - a trailing paused verb absorbs a stale pane even when its matching run is terminal ok - checks-green merge monitoring absorbs stale churn and re-surfaces only on the bounded long cadence ok - cached idle markers revalidate failed and parked authoritative transitions immediately ok - a resumed secondmate clears pause and stale tracking before stale exemption ok - unchanged stale hashes reclassify when a crew enters or leaves pause ok - a declared pause is periodically rechecked against authoritative active-run state ok - a paused status overridden by authoritative working preserves its wedge timer and escalates ok - matching non-terminal stale suppressors repair missing or corrupt stale-since timers ok - triage log capping handles wc byte counts with leading spaces ok - a heartbeat with no captain-relevant change is absorbed and backs off the cadence ok - heartbeat backstop fail-safe surfaces a captain-relevant status the per-wake path missed ok - the liveness beacon stays fresh while the watcher absorbs benign wakes (fm-guard never false-alarms) ok - with .afk present the watcher reverts to one-shot so the daemon owns triage (no double-triage) ok - AFK changed paused panes hand off plain stale identities for daemon-owned pause triage ```
