<summary>✅ **Rebase** - passed</summary>

✅ No issues found.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 **Review** - 4 issues found → auto-fixed ✅</summary>

- 🚨 `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:363` - The compare head is built as `$parent:$default`, but `$parent` is `parent.full_name` (e.g. `kunchenguid/firstmate`), so the head is `owner/repo:branch`. The embedded `/` splits the compare path segment, so GitHub returns 404. Verified against the exact fork from the intent: `GET /repos/e-jung/firstmate/compare/main...kunchenguid/firstmate:main` -> 404 Not Found, while the correct `owner:branch` form `main...kunchenguid:main` -> 200. Because the compare always fails, `sync_fork_default` always emits "fork-sync: skipped: cannot compare ..." and never reaches merge-upstream — the feature fast-forwards nothing. This contradicts the REQUIRED intent: "(1) fast-forwards the fork's default branch from its upstream parent via the GitHub merge-upstream API" / "fast-forward the fork's default branch from its upstream parent". Fix: use the parent owner only, e.g. `${parent%%/*}:$default` (or the parent's own default branch, see finding 3).
- 🚨 `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:368` - Even with the URL fixed, the fast-forward decision is inverted. The compare is base=fork (`$default`) ... head=parent (`$parent:...`), and GitHub's `status` is head-relative — proven on git/git: `compare/v2.43.0...v2.44.0` returns status="ahead" with ahead_by=761/behind_by=0 when the head is ahead. So a fork that is BEHIND its parent returns status="ahead" (parent ahead of fork), yet the `case` at line 369 proceeds only on `behind)` and routes `ahead` to the catch-all `*)` branch that reports "skipped: diverged ... (ahead)". The forks this change targets are therefore always skipped. This contradicts the REQUIRED intent: "the compare API confirms the fork is strictly 'behind' before calling merge-upstream". Correct fix is one of: act on `ahead)` (keeping base=fork/head=parent), or swap base/head (parent as base, fork as head) and keep `behind)`. Note: fixing finding 1 alone is NOT sufficient — this must be fixed too. The mock-gh tests pass only because they hardcode `GH_COMPARE=behind`, a value real GitHub never returns for this compare construction.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:350` - `$default` is the fork's default branch but is reused as the parent's branch name in both the compare and merge-upstream. The parent's actual default branch (`parent.default_branch`, already present in the same `/repos` response) could differ; if it does, the wrong branch is compared/merged. Benign in the common inherited-name case (e.g. both `main`), but it is the one piece the intent's "resolved from the API dynamically, not hardcoded" does not actually resolve dynamically.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:428` - `sync_fork_default` makes up to three sequential `gh api` calls plus a `git fetch` per GitHub-fork project, inline before the clone's own fetch, inside the time-bounded fleet-sync/bootstrap sweep. Non-fatal (best-effort; partial output is relayed on timeout), but on large fleets the extra round-trips can push `FM_FLEET_SYNC_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT` to truncate the primary clone syncs.

🔧 Fix: fix fork-sync compare form/direction; harden mock gh
✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: feat(spawn): make claude crew permission mode configurable, default to auto
body:
## Intent

Implement kunchenguid/firstmate issue #559: make the claude crewmate permission mode configurable and default to the safer auto mode instead of the hardcoded --dangerously-skip-permissions in bin/fm-spawn.sh's claude launch template. Design decisions, all deliberate: (1) a new local gitignored config/crew-permission-mode file resolves the flag - absent or 'auto' gives --permission-mode auto (the new default), 'bypass' or 'bypassPermissions' restores the prior --dangerously-skip-permissions as an explicit opt-in, any other valid claude --permission-mode choice (acceptEdits, plan, manual, dontAsk) passes through, and any unrecognized value aborts the spawn loudly - never silently launching a crew in the wrong mode. (2) Validation and placeholder splice happen right after harness resolution, before any fleet mutation (meta/worktree/window), so an invalid value fails while nothing has been created. (3) The knob is claude-only by design: codex/opencode/pi/grok autonomy flags are explicitly out of scope per the issue, and raw launch commands skip the knob. (4) Because claude has a single launch template shared by ship/scout/secondmate kinds, claude secondmate launches follow the knob too - deliberate, and pinned by the updated secondmate-harness tests. (5) The knob is deliberately NOT added to the secondmate inherit list (FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG) to keep the diff minimal; docs state it is not inherited, and inheritance parity with crew-harness is left as a possible follow-up. (6) CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=false and the __MODELFLAG__/__EFFORTFLAG__ placeholders are intentionally unchanged; only the permission flag changed. (7) .gitignore lists config files per-file, so config/crew-permission-mode was added there; no docs/examples entry on purpose because only complex config files (crew-dispatch.json, wedge-alarm) have examples while single-token knobs do not. (8) Docs: a new 'Crew permission mode' section in docs/configuration.md in the sibling-entry style, exactly one pointer line added to AGENTS.md's section 2 layout block per the repo's size discipline, and fm-spawn.sh's usage header documents the knob with the usage() sed range re-aligned; historical evidence docs (docs/turnend-guard.md, docs/cd-guard.md, docs/arm-pretool-check.md) intentionally still show --dangerously-skip-permissions because they record commands that were actually run. (9) Tests: existing pinned claude launch strings in fm-spawn-dispatch-profile, fm-secondmate-harness, and fm-backend-orca tests were updated to the new default, and five new cases pin default auto, bypass, bypassPermissions, valid passthrough, invalid-value loud failure before meta creation, and that the knob never touches other harnesses. Empirical evidence: claude --help (v2.1.202) lists auto among --permission-mode choices, and crews have run fully unattended with --permission-mode auto through real multi-step work and a validation pipeline on both tmux and cmux backends with denied actions failing fast instead of hanging. Known local-environment test caveat: six pre-existing environmental test failures on this macOS machine (fm-fleet-snapshot.sh's bash-3.2-incompatible case pattern from the base commit, node v23 ExperimentalWarning pollution in Pi tests, live-tmux capture sensitivity) are disjoint from this diff and pass on CI's ubuntu environment. The PR must reference the issue as 'Refs #559' (not Closes - the merge decision belongs to the maintainer) and ships through the fork workflow to karthikk191994/firstmate.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now resolves a new local, gitignored `config/crew-permission-mode` file into the claude launch template through a `__PERMFLAG__` placeholder: absent or `auto` launches crews with `--permission-mode auto` (the new default, replacing the hardcoded `--dangerously-skip-permissions`), `bypass`/`bypassPermissions` restores the old flag as an explicit opt-in, any other valid `claude --permission-mode` choice (`acceptEdits`, `plan`, `manual`, `dontAsk`) passes through, and an unrecognized value aborts the spawn loudly before any fleet mutation (meta/worktree/window). The knob is claude-only: raw launch commands and the other adapters' autonomy flags are untouched, and because claude's single template is shared by ship/scout/secondmate kinds, claude secondmate launches follow the knob too (it is deliberately not added to the secondmate inherit list).
- Documented the knob in a new "Crew permission mode" section of `docs/configuration.md`, a pointer line in `AGENTS.md`'s layout block, and `fm-spawn.sh`'s usage header (with the `usage()` sed range re-aligned); `config/crew-permission-mode` was added to `.gitignore`.
- Updated the pinned claude launch strings in `tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh`, `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh`, and `tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh` to the new default, and added five dispatch-profile cases pinning the auto default, the bypass/bypassPermissions opt-in, valid-value passthrough, loud failure before meta creation on an invalid value, and that other harnesses are unaffected. The pipeline's Test stage failure comes from pre-existing environment-specific failures on this macOS machine (bash 3.2 case-pattern in `fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` from the base commit, node v23 warning pollution in Pi tests, live-tmux capture sensitivity) that are disjoint from this diff.

Refs #559

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: A well-bounded, claude-only launch-flag change with validation that fails loudly before any fleet mutation, five new tests pinning every knob path, all existing pinned launch strings updated, docs aligned, and the passthrough whitelist verified against the installed claude CLI's actual --permission-mode choices; the default-behavior change from bypass to auto is the deliberate, empirically validated point of the change with an explicit opt-out.</risk_rationale>

## Testing

Completed 1 recorded test check.

- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 error across 1 run (18m40s)

为 Firstmate 增加一条简洁、持久且可执行的生命周期规则，解决 project crewmate 无法读取 private `data/captain.md` 而产生的偏好传播缺口。

title: feat(brief): add opt-in --goal-loop completion bar for ship tasks
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in `--goal-loop` completion bar to firstmate's ship-task briefs, giving the captain a stronger done-condition than the default `no-mistakes` pipeline alone for larger, more ambiguous, or first-time-trust work. Routine ship tasks are unchanged and stay as lightweight as before.

## What changed

- **`bin/fm-brief.sh`**: new `--goal-loop` flag (mirrors the `--scout`/`--herdr-lab` flag-handling pattern). When passed, the generated ship brief adds a concise `[DONE CONDITION]` section instructing the crewmate to write, before implementing, a short block naming its reward signal (one measurable metric), mechanical gate (fast, binary, no LLM judgment), qualitative gate, and done threshold — and updates the Definition of done to require that block be satisfied on top of (not instead of) the `no-mistakes` gate. The flag is rejected for scout and secondmate briefs.
- **`.agents/skills/firstmate-goal-loop/`** (new skill): owns the fuller mechanics — when to reach for `--goal-loop`, the fresh independent-checker spawn (a second crewmate, no access to the original's context, opens by stating it did not write the code under review), scoring the diff against the crewmate's done-condition block, the bounded fix loop (default 3 rounds), and escalation to the captain on repeated failure.
- **`AGENTS.md`**: one-line triggers in section 11 (Crewmate briefs) and section 13 (agent-only reference skills) pointing at the new skill; no duplication of the done-condition/checker contract.
- **`docs/scripts.md`**: lists the goal-loop variant in the `fm-brief.sh` summary.
- **`tests/fm-brief.test.sh`**: extended to cover the `--goal-loop` flag behavior.

## Validation

Validated through the `no-mistakes` pipeline: review, test, and lint all passed with 0 findings.

title: feat(catalog): optional LLM provider fallback when the primary matcher/vision provider fails
body:
## Context

The catalog LLM layer (`app/providers/llm.py`) is a single-provider-per-task design: `complete(messages, schema, model_ref)` where the provider is chosen by a config model-ref (`LLM_MATCHER_MODEL`, `LLM_VISION_MODEL`). The catalog agent design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-05-catalog-agent-design.md`, § "LLM layer") **deliberately deferred** fallback chains from v1: *"Explicitly NOT in v1: fallback chains, load balancing, per-request routing. Swapping providers = edit env var, redeploy."*

When the configured matcher/vision provider fails (outage or misconfiguration), the ask cannot be resolved. As of #94, such failures are recorded in `catalog_resolutions` with a dedicated `ERROR` outcome (distinct from `NO_MATCH` and `ABANDONED`), so failure rate is now measurable.

## Proposal

Add an optional provider fallback: if the primary matcher/vision provider fails, retry the same request against a configured secondary provider before giving up and recording `ERROR`.

## Why this is low-risk mechanically

The architecture already supports it — provider selection is a config model-ref behind one `complete()` interface, so a fallback chain is an additive wrapper, not a rewrite.

## Open design questions (resolve before building)

- **Which provider is the backup**, and is fallback opt-in per task (matcher vs vision) or global?
- **Latency budget:** a fallback attempt adds a full round-trip. The resolution flow must stay within the sub-3s ack pattern (ack first, heavy work after) and the ~≤10s worst-case total (resolution + existing lookup). Confirm a fallback retry still fits, or bound it with a tight timeout on the primary.
- **Audit semantics:** a fallback that *succeeds* must record the real success outcome (resolved/no-match/etc.), NOT `ERROR`. `ERROR` should be reserved for the case where every configured provider failed. Optionally record which provider served the result and whether fallback was used.
- **Cost/observability:** structlog event on fallback activation so silent primary degradation is visible.

## Recommendation

Do NOT build until the `ERROR` metric from #94 shows the real provider-failure rate in production. Let data justify the added latency/cost/complexity.

## Out of scope

- Load balancing / per-request routing across providers (still deferred per the v1 decision).
- Automatic provider health-checking or circuit-breaking beyond a single fallback attempt.

## Related

- Follows #94 (which added the `ERROR` outcome that motivates measuring this).
- Part of the broader Catalog Agent epic #91 (hardening, not core resolution flow).

title: Give each secondmate its own tmux session instead of sharing the main firstmate's session
body:
## Problem

On the default `tmux` backend, a `--secondmate` spawn does not get its own tmux session. In `bin/fm-spawn.sh` the tmux branch resolves the session the same way for every kind:

```sh
W="fm-$ID"
case "$BACKEND" in
  tmux)
    SES=$(fm_backend_tmux_container_ensure)
    T="$SES:$W"
```

`fm_backend_tmux_container_ensure` (in `bin/backends/tmux.sh`) reuses the **current** tmux session when firstmate is already running inside one, and only falls back to creating a session literally named `firstmate` when it is not:

```sh
fm_backend_tmux_container_ensure() {
  if [ -n "${TMUX:-}" ]; then
    tmux display-message -p '#S'
  else
    tmux has-session -t firstmate 2>/dev/null || tmux new-session -d -s firstmate
    printf 'firstmate'
  fi
}
```

Because a secondmate is launched by the main firstmate from inside the firstmate session, `container_ensure` returns that same session. So the secondmate agent (`kind=secondmate`) is created as just another window (`fm-<id>`) inside the **main firstmate's** session. Worse, the secondmate's own crewmates then inherit that same session through the default current-session path.

The net result is that a single tmux session ends up mixing four different things:

- the main firstmate
- the main firstmate's crewmates
- the secondmate (which is itself a firstmate)
- the secondmate's crewmates

A secondmate is architecturally a firstmate in its own isolated home, so having its runtime windows interleaved into the parent's session is a leaky abstraction. It makes the session hard to read, hard to attach to selectively, and blurs the ownership boundary the secondmate design otherwise keeps clean.

## Proposed fix

For `KIND=secondmate` on the tmux backend, give the secondmate its **own** tmux session named by its id, creating it if it does not exist. The secondmate's own crewmates then inherit that session through the normal current-session path, so each layer of the fleet stays partitioned by session:

- session `firstmate` (or the operator's booted firstmate session): main firstmate + its crewmates
- session `<secondmate-id>`: that secondmate + its crewmates

The name is derived from the id, so it is stable and durable across every respawn (recovery, restart, config-driven relaunch) with no extra per-task state.

## Patch

```diff
--- a/bin/fm-spawn.sh
+++ b/bin/fm-spawn.sh
@@ -695,7 +695,17 @@ validate_spawn_worktree() {  # <source> <inspect-target>
 W="fm-$ID"
 case "$BACKEND" in
   tmux)
-    SES=$(fm_backend_tmux_container_ensure)
+    if [ "$KIND" = secondmate ]; then
+      # A secondmate gets its OWN tmux session named by its id, isolated from the
+      # main firstmate's session (which container_ensure would otherwise return).
+      # Its own crewmates then inherit that session via the default current-session
+      # path, so a single session never mixes firstmate + its crewmates + a
+      # secondmate + the secondmate's crewmates. Durable across every respawn.
+      SES=$ID
+      tmux has-session -t "$SES" 2>/dev/null || tmux new-session -d -s "$SES"
+    else
+      SES=$(fm_backend_tmux_container_ensure)
+    fi
     T="$SES:$W"
```

## Notes and scope

- The change is scoped to the `tmux` backend (the verified default). The `herdr`, `zellij`, `orca`, and `cmux` backends already scope workspaces differently; whether they need an analogous per-secondmate isolation is worth a follow-up, but is out of scope here.
- No change to recovery/reconciliation is required: `state/<id>.meta` records `window=<session>:fm-<id>`, so the recorded backend target already round-trips through the new session name.
- This pairs naturally with keeping the main firstmate always in a session named `firstmate` (the fallback name `container_ensure` already assumes), which keeps the top-level session name stable rather than timestamped.

title: fix(afk): gate away-mode injection on a confirmed live agent
body:
## Intent Fix a verified safety hole: the away-mode supervise daemon could type an escalation digest (plus Enter) into a live shell, executing arbitrary commands when nobody is watching. Root cause: inject_msg (bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh) gated injection ONLY on composer-emptiness, but the default starship/pure/spaceship shell prompt glyph U+276F (the heavy right-angle quotation mark) is byte-identical to the glyph claude draws for its own empty composer, so a supervisor pane whose agent had exited to a login shell read as an empty agent composer and was injected into. Fix: after the composer-empty check, inject_msg now also calls the pre-existing fm_backend_agent_alive probe (bin/fm-backend.sh; already used by the session-start secondmate-liveness sweep) and injects ONLY on a confident 'alive'. Deliberate decisions a diff-only reviewer would not know: (1) This FAILS CLOSED on purpose - both 'dead' (a bare shell) and 'unknown' (an unreadable pane, or a harness whose liveness is unverifiable for the backend, e.g. pi's generic node interpreter) defer, on the stated principle that a missed escalation is an inconvenience but a command typed into the captain's shell is not; deferred escalations are not lost (buffer + max-defer wedge alarm + afk-exit catch-up flush). A pi-based supervisor in away mode therefore stops receiving injected escalations - this is an accepted, documented consequence, not a regression to fix here. (2) I intentionally did NOT remove the glyph from any character class - that is a band-aid because an empty shell prompt and an empty agent composer are indistinguishable by content; the guard asks what process is running instead. (3) fm-send.sh shares the same content-blindness but is deliberate/firstmate-initiated (not autonomous) and a strict alive-gate there would break steering for every unknown-liveness backend (pi, zellij, orca, cmux); I analyzed and documented it with a recommended separate dead-only guard but deliberately did NOT change fm-send in this PR to keep the safety fix focused. Tests: three deterministic inject_msg units in tests/fm-daemon.test.sh plus a real-shell end-to-end Scenario D in tests/fm-afk-inject-e2e.test.sh, each of which fails against the pre-fix daemon (verified by neutering the gate: the suite exits non-zero with an explicit 'typed into a dead shell' / 'SHELL INJECTION' failure). Test-helper changes in tests/wake-helpers.sh add a pane_current_command reply to the fake tmux so the fake supervisor panes (which stand in for a live agent) report as alive. Docs: amended the one-owner composer-emptiness safety policy in docs/herdr-backend.md (new dated subsection) and corrected the now-inaccurate claim in docs/architecture.md that a bare dead-shell prompt cannot receive an escalation. This is a generic bug affecting every firstmate user with a default shell prompt, intended to go upstream. ## What Changed - `inject_msg` in `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh` now probes `fm_backend_agent_alive` after the composer-empty check and injects only on a confident `alive`. An empty starship/pure prompt glyph (U+276F) is byte-identical to claude's empty-composer glyph, so a supervisor pane whose agent had exited to a login shell previously read as an empty composer and got the escalation digest typed in and submitted as shell commands. The guard fails closed: both `dead` and `unknown` (an unreadable pane, or a harness whose liveness the backend cannot attribute, e.g. pi's generic `node`) defer instead of injecting, so a pi-backed supervisor stops receiving injections in away mode - deferred escalations still survive via the buffer, the wedge alarm, and the afk-exit catch-up flush. - Because the guard can leave away mode permanently unable to deliver, new `bin/fm-afk-canary-lib.sh` derives and words that verdict in one place, and surfaces it on both the arm path (`bin/fm-afk-launch.sh`) and session start (`bin/fm-bootstrap.sh`, as an `AFK_INJECTION_DISABLED:` diagnostic). It probes the running daemon's own recorded target rather than the current pane, so a firstmate restarted into a new pane learns the daemon is still injecting elsewhere, and reports a vanished target instead of staying quiet. - The wedge alarm now records why the last inject deferred and reports that cause rather than always blaming a busy pane, and gains a separate debounced, latched pane-gone alarm (its own `.subsuper-pane-gone` marker, one alert per absence episode) that declares supervision DOWN when the supervisor pane vanishes. Captain-facing wording keys off the alarm kind, not the last recorded cause, so a buffer wedge can never render as "away mode is dead". Covered by three deterministic `inject_msg` units in `tests/fm-daemon.test.sh` and a real-shell Scenario D in `tests/fm-afk-inject-e2e.test.sh`, each of which fails against the pre-fix daemon; `bin/fm-send.sh` shares the same content-blindness and is documented in `docs/herdr-backend.md` but deliberately left unchanged here. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: A large, safety-critical change to the autonomous away-mode injection path that is well-tested and strictly improves on the pre-existing behavior, but it adds a fail-closed gate that fully disables away-mode escalation delivery for any supervisor whose harness a backend cannot attribute (pi, and any node-wrapped harness) — an accepted, documented regression — and ships with three deliberately deferred robustness gaps in the new alarm and canary paths. ## Testing Baseline test command had already passed; I re-ran the full suite (68 files, 0 failures) and then produced product-level before/after evidence for the safety fix. Using a real login shell displaying the default starship ❯ glyph, the end-to-end Scenario D shows the fixed daemon refuses to inject and defers the escalation, while a neutered (pre-fix) daemon typed the digest into and executed it in the live shell — the test caught this with an explicit SHELL INJECTION failure. The deterministic inject_msg units confirm the same at the function level, including fail-closed-on-unknown and the alive+empty positive path. I restored the daemon file and verified a clean working tree afterward. This is a CLI/daemon behavior change with no rendered UI surface, so evidence is CLI transcripts rather than screenshots.
Evidence: Evidence summary: before/after shell-injection guard ### A. Real-shell end-to-end (Scenario D) PRE-FIX (guard neutered): not ok - Scenario D: the escalation digest was typed into the live shell (found 'Supervisor escalate' in the pane) — SHELL INJECTION [e2e exit 1] WITH FIX: ok - Scenario D: a dead shell showing a bare starship ❯ prompt is refused — the escalation defers, nothing is typed into the shell [e2e exit 0] ### B. Impact is bounded - the buffer survives and housekeeping re-raises on the next tick - but for that window firstmate's afk-exit catch-up has no wedge report, and the re-raise is silent (the latched alarm set WEDGE_ALARM_LAST_EPOCH, so line 947 suppresses both the ERROR log and the active alert for up to max_defer). Suggest not rewriting an existing marker whose recorded cause is something else (leave it, or give the pane-gone alarm its own marker file) so recovery can only ever retire what it wrote. 🔧 Fix: give the pane-gone alarm its own marker file 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:941` - inject_wedge_alarm selects its marker file and its throttle from $kind (line 928) but selects the captain-facing summary, the Notification Center banner title (WEDGE_ALARM_TITLE), and the ERROR log from $cause (line 941). Those two disagree on a reachable path, and the result is a false 'away mode is dead' alert to an away captain. Concrete failure: the main loop's fm_backend_target_exists check passes, the watcher runs for a poll interval, and the supervisor pane dies in that window; housekeeping's max-defer escape (line 1121) then calls escalate_flush -> inject_msg, whose own target-exists check fails and records cause=pane-gone (line 1247 via _inject_defer). escalate_flush returns non-zero, so housekeeping calls inject_wedge_alarm "$state" "$oldest" with the DEFAULT kind=buffer. Inside, the cause=pane-gone branch fires: WEDGE_ALARM_TITLE becomes 'firstmate: away-mode supervision DOWN', the active alert reads 'away-mode supervision DOWN Ns (pane-gone): supervisor pane gone, nothing can be delivered', and that text is written into .subsuper-inject-wedged (the BUFFER marker). This entirely bypasses the debounce pane_gone_wedge_alarm was built around - it requires a full max-defer window of CONTINUOUS absence before declaring supervision down, precisely because 'a pane that blinks out for one poll is a backend hiccup' (line 1003) - so one flaky tmux/herdr existence probe at flush time now produces the loudest verdict in the design. Per the new .agents/skills/afk/SKILL.md guidance ('The one verdict that is never an accepted degradation is a vanished pane... report it and fix it rather than continuing away mode'), firstmate would tear down a healthy away session on that alert. This is the same misattribution class the wedge-alarm and canary work spent four rounds eliminating. Fix: branch the summary/header/detail/err/title on $kind instead of $cause (line 941 -> `if [ "$kind" = pane-gone ]`). Nothing is lost: with kind=buffer and cause=pane-gone the buffer wording still names the tag - 'away-mode escalations WEDGED Ns undelivered (pane-gone)' - which is accurate, because the buffer IS stuck and IS still being retried, while the debounced, latched supervision-DOWN declaration stays where it belongs. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-afk-launch.sh:353` - FM_AFK_LAUNCH_ARTIFACTS (line 64) was introduced this commit with the comment 'One list, so a new artifact cannot be added to the daemon and forgotten by the rollback that has to put it back' - but fm_afk_launch_restore_backup's `rm -f` at lines 353-358 still hardcodes the same four artifact names immediately above the loop that iterates the array. The drift the array exists to prevent is therefore only half-closed: a future fifth artifact added to FM_AFK_LAUNCH_ARTIFACTS but not to that rm -f would survive a rolled-back arm (the loop only restores what was in the backup, so an artifact the failed arm created fresh is never cleared). Iterate the array in the rm -f too, keeping .afk as the one explicit extra. (bin/fm-afk-start.sh's fm_afk_clear_stale_artifacts is a third hardcoded copy of the same list, in a different file - worth noting, but the launcher's internal duplication is the one that contradicts its own comment.) 🔧 Fix: key wedge alarm wording to alarm kind, not last cause 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `docs/wedge-alarm.md:12` - The alarm-semantics section (lines 12-16) still attributes the supervision-DOWN wording, the fire-once latch, and the empty-buffer firing to the CAUSE `pane-gone` ("`pane-gone` is the one cause whose captain-facing wording is not about the buffer", "It also fires on an EMPTY buffer", "Every channel therefore says supervision is down"). This commit changed all three to key on the alarm KIND instead. On the reachable pane-died-mid-flush path - the main loop's fm_backend_target_exists check passes, the pane dies during housekeeping's max-defer escalate_flush, and inject_msg records cause=pane-gone (bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:1298) while the alarm housekeeping raises is kind=buffer - the channels say "away-mode escalations WEDGED 900s undelivered (pane-gone)", the alarm IS throttled once per max-defer window, and it IS gated on a non-empty buffer. That is the exact opposite of what these lines promise, and it is the behavior the new test test_buffer_wedge_alarm_never_declares_supervision_down pins. Line 109 of the same file, added in this commit, states the correct rule ("Which alarm fired is what the captain is told, never the last recorded cause"), so the file now contradicts itself: a maintainer reading top-down would reintroduce the false 'away mode is dead' alert this commit fixed. Line 6 carries a smaller version of the slip - it claims `pane-gone` comes only from the daemon's main loop rather than an inject attempt, but inject_msg's own target-exists check records it too. Rewrite lines 6 and 12-16 so the supervision-DOWN wording, the latch, and the empty-buffer firing are described as properties of the pane-gone ALARM (the debounced, latched one raised from the backoff path), with `pane-gone` named only as a cause tag that can also appear on a buffer wedge. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-afk-start.sh:63` - FM_AFK_LAUNCH_ARTIFACTS (bin/fm-afk-launch.sh:64) was introduced this commit with the comment "One list, so a new artifact cannot be added to the daemon and forgotten by the rollback that has to put it back", and the rollback rm now iterates it. But fm_afk_clear_stale_artifacts - the fresh-arm clear that drops the PRIOR away session's delivery artifacts - still hardcodes the same four names, and it lives in bin/fm-afk-start.sh, which the launcher SOURCES, so it cannot reference the launcher's array. The two agree today (both gained .subsuper-pane-gone in this PR), but a fifth artifact added to FM_AFK_LAUNCH_ARTIFACTS alone would be backed up and rolled back correctly while surviving a fresh arm - resurfacing a prior session's buffered escalation or wedge marker under a new away session, which is the failure fm_afk_clear_stale_artifacts exists to prevent. Defining the list once in bin/fm-afk-start.sh (where the clear lives) and having bin/fm-afk-launch.sh iterate that same array would close the drift and shrink the footprint rather than grow it. Flagged as an aside in round 9 and deliberately scoped out of that fix; noting the residual, not re-litigating. 🔧 Fix: key wedge-alarm doc to alarm kind and unify afk artifact list 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:200` - The WEDGE_ALARM_TITLE declaration comment still states the captain-facing banner title "follows the CAUSE" ("so it follows the CAUSE: a vanished supervisor pane means away-mode supervision is down"), but commit 1496b85 changed inject_wedge_alarm to select the summary, WEDGE_ALARM_TITLE, and the ERROR log from $kind instead — the same discriminator that picks the marker file and the throttle — specifically so a cause=pane-gone recorded by inject_msg during housekeeping's max-defer flush cannot render the supervision-DOWN verdict from what is actually a buffer wedge. docs/wedge-alarm.md was rewritten for this (lines 201-209: "WHICH one fired - its kind - is what every captain-facing surface says") and tests/fm-daemon.test.sh's test_buffer_wedge_alarm_never_declares_supervision_down pins it, so the code comment is now the only place in the repo asserting the superseded rule. inject_wedge_alarm's own header (line ~892) carries a milder version: it opens with "the ERROR log, the durable marker, and the active alert all report the recorded cause" before the next paragraph corrects it to the kind. Concrete failure: a maintainer reads the declaration comment, re-keys the branch at line 946 on $cause, and the reachable pane-died-mid-flush path (main-loop target-exists passes, pane dies during escalate_flush -> inject_msg records pane-gone at line 1298, housekeeping raises kind=buffer at line 1137) again titles an away captain's Notification Center banner "firstmate: away-mode supervision DOWN" for a buffer that is still stuck behind a pane the daemon keeps retrying — which per .agents/skills/afk/SKILL.md means tearing down a healthy away session. Rewrite lines 198-204 (and the opening sentence of the inject_wedge_alarm header) to say the title follows the alarm KIND, with the cause carried only as a diagnostic tag. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:609` - Noting the boundary of the new session-start diagnostic, not requesting a change. afk_injection_check gates on state/.afk, then fm_afk_canary_resolve falls back to discover_supervisor_target whenever no LIVE daemon owns the lock — so when away mode is armed but the daemon has died, bootstrap probes its own pane, finds firstmate obviously alive, and prints nothing. That is the right answer for what the canary measures (can the resolved supervisor be injected into), and AGENTS.md section 5 step 8 already covers the dead-daemon case by having /afk ensure the daemon is running on recovery, so nothing is actually missed. But docs/herdr-backend.md's "a cold or restarted session that re-enters afk from the flag alone still learns injection is off" reads broader than the check guarantees: the one away-mode failure a restarted session cannot learn from this line is the daemon simply not being there. 🔧 Fix: key wedge-alarm title comment to alarm kind, not cause 2 infos still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-afk-start.sh:79` - fm_afk_clear_stale_artifacts changed from a single best-effort `rm -f` (which returns 0 essentially always) to a loop that returns 1 if ANY rm fails. In bin/fm-afk-launch.sh both call sites already test the return value and log "failed to clear stale away-mode artifacts", so there the new failure signal is an improvement. But fm_afk_start_main calls it bare inside an `if` body (bin/fm-afk-start.sh:159) and that file runs under `set -eu` with no `set +e`, so a non-zero return is not a caught error — errexit fires and the daemon start aborts before `exec "$FM_AFK_DAEMON"`, with no message at all (the rm's stderr goes to /dev/null and errexit is silent). Failure scenario: a direct, non-prepared `bin/fm-afk-start.sh` on a state dir holding an undeletable artifact (root-owned leftover from a prior run under a different user, or a read-only mount) previously logged nothing and started away mode anyway; now it exits 1 with no output and away mode silently does not arm. Reachability is narrow — the /afk skill always goes through the launcher with FM_AFK_STATE_PREPARED=1, so only a manual/legacy direct invocation takes this branch — but the silence is the problem, not the abort. Either echo the failure before returning non-zero, or guard the call site the way the launcher does. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:1081` - When the supervisor target resolves again, pane_gone_recovered deletes state/.subsuper-pane-gone and logs the recovery only to the daemon log. But the captain has, by then, already received the pane-gone active alert — a Notification Center banner titled "firstmate: away-mode supervision DOWN", and a push through any configured `command:` channel, telling them to stop away mode and arm it again. Nothing retracts it, and the marker (the one surface the afk-exit catch-up actually reads) is gone. Per .agents/skills/afk/SKILL.md:144, an absent .subsuper-pane-gone marker means "no live absence", so firstmate's catch-up reports all-clear for an alarm the captain demonstrably received. Failure scenario: the supervisor window is a session:window name (the FM_SUPERVISOR_TARGET_DEFAULT `firstmate:0` fallback, or an explicit named target — the exact case pane_gone_recovered was written for), it is killed and recreated during a >300s gap overnight; the captain gets a 2am "supervision DOWN" push, comes back to a clean catch-up, and neither they nor firstmate can explain the alert without grepping state/.supervise-daemon.log, which no catch-up instruction points at. A one-line resolved note left behind on the recovery edge, or having the /afk catch-up read the daemon log's ERROR/recovery pair, would close it. Flagging for the record rather than requesting a change: this is the same best-effort-alert reach you already scoped out (docs/wedge-alarm.md "Known follow-ups"), and it belongs with the bounded-re-fire item there.
🔧 **Test** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 tests failed with exit code 1 - `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` 🔧 Fix: provide mkdir to x-mode fakebin, silence node ExperimentalWarning ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain. - `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` - `bash tests/*.test.sh` full suite: 68 files, 0 failures, exit 0 - `bash tests/fm-afk-inject-e2e.test.sh` — real-shell Scenario D (genuine login shell with a bare starship ❯ prompt) passes: escalation defers, nothing typed into the shell - `bash tests/fm-daemon.test.sh` — the three safety-critical inject_msg units pass: defers on empty-composer dead shell (agent_alive=dead), defers on unknown liveness (fail closed), injects on alive+empty (positive path) - Pre-fix regression proof: neutered the liveness gate to `liveness=alive` (simulating gate-on-composer-only) and re-ran both files — Scenario D failed with 'SHELL INJECTION' (digest typed into and run by the live shell) and the starship-glyph unit failed with 'send_text_submit ran despite agent_alive=dead'; restored the file (git checkout) and confirmed clean tree + tests green again
⚠️ **Document** - 1 info - ℹ️ `docs/scripts.md:47` - docs/scripts.md (the bin/ toolbelt inventory) is missing five scripts that pre-date this change: fm-lint.sh, fm-install-shellcheck.sh (added in #481), fm-cd-pretool-check.sh, fm-cd-command-policy.mjs (added in #483), and fm-transition-lib.sh (added in #472). I added the row for fm-afk-canary-lib.sh, which this change introduced, but deliberately left the pre-existing five alone: backfilling unrelated scripts would expand a focused away-mode safety fix's documentation diff with work from three other PRs. Needs a human call on whether to fix them here or in a separate docs cleanup.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: OpenCode secondmate never arms its own supervision watcher (isPrimaryRoot excludes secondmate homes)
body:
## Problem
On the OpenCode harness, a secondmate (a firstmate running in its own `FM_HOME`) never arms its own supervision watcher. Its `.opencode/plugins/fm-primary-watch-arm.js` shows `WATCHER DOWN - SUPERVISION IS OFF` (last beat: never) while a crewmate is in flight, so it receives no proactive wakes and has to hand-supervise.

Reproduced 2026-07-15 (OpenCode 1.18.0, GLM 5.2): a secondmate spawned a crewmate; `state/.last-watcher-beat` in the secondmate home was absent and no `fm-watch.sh` process existed for that home for the entire session.

## Root cause
`isPrimaryRoot(root, home)` in `.opencode/plugins/fm-primary-watch-arm.js` returns `false` for any root that carries a `.fm-secondmate-home` marker:

```js
if (existsSync(`${root}/.fm-secondmate-home`)) return false;
```

A secondmate home always has that marker, so `ensureArm()` returns `"not-primary"` on every `session.idle` and the watcher never arms. But a secondmate IS the primary of its own home and must arm its own watcher to supervise its own crewmates - consistent with the turn-end guard, which already "guards both the main primary and a secondmate's own primary session".

## Proposed patch
Drop the blanket exclusion; keep only the home/root MISMATCH guard, which already prevents arming a foreign secondmate home. `sessionOwnsLock()` continues to gate arming to the lock-owning session, so this can never arm a foreign home's watcher.

```diff
-  if (existsSync(`${root}/.fm-secondmate-home`)) return false;
-  if (home && home !== root && existsSync(`${home}/.fm-secondmate-home`)) return false;
+  // A secondmate home carries a .fm-secondmate-home marker but IS the primary of its own
+  // home and must arm its own watcher to supervise its own crewmates. Only a home/root
+  // MISMATCH is disqualifying; a secondmate's own session has root === home.
+  // sessionOwnsLock() still gates arming to the session that owns this home's lock.
+  if (home && home !== root && existsSync(`${home}/.fm-secondmate-home`)) return false;
```

## Offer
Happy to open a PR with this change plus a regression test if that is welcome.

title: fm-send reports a false "Enter swallowed / text not submitted" for OpenCode targets
body:
## Problem
Sending a steer to an OpenCode target via `fm-send` frequently prints:

```
error: text not submitted to <target> (Enter swallowed; text left in composer; ...)
```

even though the message DID land and the agent processed it (the pane goes busy immediately after). Observed repeatedly 2026-07-15 (OpenCode 1.18.0, GLM 5.2) both when a main firstmate steered a secondmate and when a secondmate steered its own OpenCode crewmate.

## Root cause
`fm_tmux_submit_enter_core` (`bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh`) verifies submission via `fm_tmux_composer_state`, which reads ONLY the single cursor row and returns `pending` if real content remains. Its busy-footer allowance only matches a busy footer that lands ON the cursor row:

```sh
# A busy footer landing on the cursor line is not pending input ...
if [ -n "$stripped" ] && printf '%s' "$stripped" | grep -qiE "$BUSY_REGEX"; then ...
```

OpenCode renders its busy footer (`esc interrupt`) on a SEPARATE row from the composer cursor row, and its composer clears asynchronously (slower than the ~0.4s verify), so the verify can read the cursor row as still-pending while the agent is already busy processing the submitted message. After the retries it returns `pending` -> the false error.

## Proposed fix (needs care - shared with the away-mode daemon)
`fm_tmux_submit_core` is shared: the away-mode daemon consumes its verdict strictly (clears its escalation buffer only on `empty`), so a naive "busy => empty" in the shared core could make the daemon treat a queued-to-a-busy-pane escalation as delivered and drop it.

Safe direction: scope the busy-aware downgrade to the `fm-send` consumer (`bin/fm-send.sh`), NOT the shared core. When the verdict is `pending`, do a WHOLE-PANE busy check; if the pane is busy (a turn is running), treat the steer as delivered. This leaves the daemon's strict `empty` policy untouched. A cleaner variant guards on an idle->busy transition (capture busy state before typing) so it never false-positives when steering an already-busy pane.

## Offer
Happy to open a PR once the safe variant is picked and reproduced against live OpenCode, if welcome.

title: Windows (Git Bash/MSYS) support for spawn, supervision, adapters, and the test suite
body:
## Summary

This PR makes firstmate fully functional on Windows 11 under Git Bash (MSYS) with the herdr backend.
It is the stack we have been running in production locally since 2026-07-11; a crewmate was spawned, supervised, and shipped a merged PR end to end with these patches, and the targeted test suites now pass on Windows.

The commits fall into three groups.

### Runtime enablement (spawn and supervision path)

- **Session and wake-queue locks on Git Bash**: lock helpers gain an MSYS arm (PowerShell CIM pid walk, `MSYS=winsymlinks:sys`).
- **Worktree discovery for crewmate spawns**: herdr has no `foreground_cwd` on Windows, so pane cwd falls back to `.cwd` + `cygpath -u`; treehouse subshell detection points `COMSPEC` at PowerShell so the pane cwd updates via OSC 7.
- **Agent launch through Git Bash**: herdr panes run PowerShell on Windows, so the launch command is routed through `bash -l <launch.sh>`.
- **`fm_pid_identity` on MSYS**: BusyBox-style `ps` rejects `-o`, so the identity is parsed from the default `ps -p` columns (WINPID + STIME + COMMAND), preserving the pid-reuse guarantee the Unix `lstart+command` query gives. The Unix branch keeps the upstream `LC_ALL=C` pin.

### Node-side adapters

- **OpenCode plugin and Pi extension spawned `bin/*.sh` directly**: Windows node cannot exec a shebang script, and the spawn `error` event was swallowed as a pass, so the turn-end guard silently never ran. Scripts are now routed through bash on `win32`.
- **`fm-arm-command-policy.mjs` path matching**: `path.normalize`/`path.join` flip to backslashes on Windows node and never match the POSIX patterns, and MSYS hands `--root`/`--home` as `C:/...` while paths inside the command string stay `/c/...` - on Windows the deny policy was effectively inert. A `posixNormalize` helper folds every spelling into one forward-slash, uppercase-drive form.
- **TERM delivery to the Pi watch arm child**: native node's `child.kill()` is `TerminateProcess` on Windows, so the bash arm child died without running its TERM trap, and node's Windows pid cannot be mapped back after MSYS `exec` swaps the underlying Windows process. The launch command records the child's own MSYS pid (`$$` survives exec) in `state/.pi-watch-arm-msys-pid`, and `stopArm` delivers a real MSYS TERM via Git Bash `kill`, falling back to `child.kill` when unavailable.

### Test harness

- **TERM-resistant test peers must be MSYS processes**: MSYS `kill -TERM` to a non-MSYS binary (node) is emulated as `TerminateProcess`, which no in-process handler can ignore, so the watcher-lock healthy-peer scenario used a node peer that died and had its lock stolen. A `bash -c 'trap "" TERM; sleep 300'` peer ignores TERM identically on every platform.
- **`fm_fakebin_tool` replaces `ln -s` fakebins**: on MSYS `ln -s` copies the exe away from its DLLs (a copied `bash.exe` cannot load `msys-2.0.dll` from a bare-PATH fakebin), and bash resolves builtins like `printf` to a bare name no link can target. A `/bin/sh` wrapper execs the real path instead. Applied across the turnend-guard, cd-pretool, and arm-pretool suites.
- **Bootstrap suite**: the hermetic `BASE_PATH` (`/usr/bin:/bin`) has no git on Git-for-Windows (git lives in `/mingw64/bin`), which broke both the new `COMMON_TOOLS` git check and the fleet-sync fakes that delegate repo-state queries through `command git`; the ambient git's directory is appended on MSYS. The `add_real_jq` shim also strips the CRLF that native Windows jq builds emit, which poisoned exact-string assertions.

## Environment notes (not part of the diff)

Two host-level requirements surfaced while getting the suites green; they may be worth documenting in the Windows section of the docs:

- Native Windows jq builds (winget, even 1.8.x) open stdout in text mode and emit CRLF, which corrupts every bash `$(jq -r ...)` capture in the herdr adapter. We run an LF-stripping wrapper ahead of it on PATH.
- An empty locale (`LANG` unset) breaks multibyte glyph classification in `fm-composer-lib` (the composer `❯` row reads `pending` instead of `empty`); `LANG=C.UTF-8` fixes it.

## Test plan

On Windows 11 + Git Bash, with the environment notes above applied, all of the following pass (most failed or could not run before this stack):

`fm-bootstrap`, `fm-watcher-lock`, `fm-wake-queue`, `fm-turnend-guard`, `fm-spawn-batch`, `fm-spawn-dispatch-profile`, `fm-backend-herdr`, `fm-composer-lib`, `fm-arm-pretool-check`, `fm-cd-pretool-check`, `fm-pi-watch-extension`, `fm-pi-primary-types`, `fm-lint`.

No behavior change on macOS/Linux: every Windows arm is gated on `uname` `MINGW*|MSYS*` or `process.platform === "win32"`, and the shared-code changes (`posixNormalize`, wrapper fakebins, bash test peers) are platform-neutral.

title: SE4 natural gas missing from fuels feed — add SE4_natural_gas (history + forward) or make the capacity curve emit forward data
body:
## Summary

SE4 still has **no natural-gas data** reaching the downstream dashboards. The
correct fix is **upstream in the data-ingestion pipeline, not in the dashboard**:
the `SE4_natural_gas` series needs to exist in the **fuels feed** with both
**history and forward** coverage. Once it does, the dashboard-side migration is
trivial and **SE4 is fixed across all 6 dashboards at once**.

There are two acceptable ways to satisfy this, either of which unblocks the
dashboards:

1. **Add `SE4_natural_gas` (history + forward) to the fuels CSV feed** that the
   dashboards consume, or
2. **Make the SE4 natural-gas capacity curve emit forward data**, from which the
   fuels feed is derived — after which no dashboard change is needed.

> Reported by Bjarne Walbech, email 2026-07-12 (subject: "SE4 naturgas"). This
> is a Cloud Run / pipeline change and lives entirely on the data-ingestion
> side, outside the dashboard repo.

## What already exists

The SE4 natural-gas curve **is already registered** in `curve_meta`:

| field | value |
|---|---|
| `id` | `2047` |
| `name` | `se4_natural_gas_eq_mw_PT1H_capacity` |
| `table_name` | `capacity` |
| `zone` | `se4` |
| `measure` | `natural_gas` |
| `unit` | `mw` |
| `resolution` | `PT1H` |
| `source` | `Energy Quantified` |
| `api_adapter_id` | `eq_latest_period_instance_forecast` |
| `source_curve_key` | `SE4 @Öresundsverket-CCGT Natural Gas Power Capacity Available MW REMIT` |
| `cleaning_method` | `period_to_hourly_ffill` |

So the raw ingestion is wired; the gap is that the stored data is **backward-only**
and the fuels feed the dashboards read does not carry SE4.

## Why there is no forward data today (root cause)

The `eq_latest_period_instance_forecast` adapter
(`src/apis/eq_adapter.py::EqLatestPeriodInstanceForecastApiAdapter._load`)
fetches the latest REMIT period instance but **clamps the request window's `end`
to `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`**:

```python
kwargs = {
    "begin": from_date,
    "end": datetime.now(timezone.utc),   # forward horizon discarded here
}
period_inst = self._eq.period_instances.latest(source_curve_key, **kwargs)
```

REMIT "Available Capacity" period instances **do contain forward-dated periods**
(planned/known maintenance and capacity constraints into the future), but this
`end = now` bound throws that forward horizon away. The `capacity` fact table is
also actual-shaped (`curve_id, timestamp, value`) with no `issued_at`/forward
concept, so as things stand the curve can only ever store history.

This makes SE4 (and every other zone using this adapter) forward-blank in the
capacity store — hence the dashboards, which want a forward fuels line, get
nothing for SE4.

## Proposed work (either path is acceptable)

**Path A — capacity curve emits forward data (preferred if the fuels feed is
derived from capacity curves):**
- Extend the request window in
  `EqLatestPeriodInstanceForecastApiAdapter._load` so the forward horizon of the
  REMIT period instance is retained instead of being clipped at `now` (e.g. pass
  a forward `end`, or drop the `end` clamp for this REMIT-availability adapter).
- Confirm the `capacity` table / `period_to_hourly_ffill` cleaning method can
  store timestamps beyond `now` and that downstream reads don't silently drop
  future-dated rows.
- Verify against the paid control zones (e.g. SE3
  `se3_natural_gas_eq_mw_PT1H_capacity`, id `1047`) that forward periods appear.

**Path B — add `SE4_natural_gas` to the fuels CSV feed directly:**
- Ensure whatever job builds the fuels CSV feed the dashboards consume includes
  the `se4_natural_gas_eq_mw_PT1H_capacity` (id 2047) series with both history
  and forward, so `SE4_natural_gas` is present in the feed.

> Note: the fuels-CSV **producer** is not in this repo's `src/` — no CSV/fuels
> feed writer was found here (only `natural_gas` capacity curves in
> `curve_meta`). Confirm where the fuels feed is generated (this repo's Cloud
> Run job vs. a sibling pipeline) as the first step; the fix belongs wherever
> that feed is built, and Bjarne is clear it is on the data-ingestion / Cloud Run
> side.

## Payoff

`SE4_natural_gas` present in the fuels feed (history + forward) → the
dashboard-side change becomes a trivial migration and **all 6 dashboards get
correct SE4 natural gas at once**.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SE4_natural_gas` is available downstream in the fuels feed with **both**
      historical **and** forward coverage.
- [ ] Achieved either by the SE4 natural-gas capacity curve (id 2047) emitting
      forward data, **or** by adding the series to the fuels CSV feed.
- [ ] No change required in the dashboard repo beyond consuming the now-present
      series.

---

_Footnote (process question for the captain, not part of this fix): Bjarne also
asked whether he should start entering improvement requests like this directly
into GitHub himself. That is a workflow decision for Frederik and is out of scope
for this issue._

title: test: lock symlinked projects/ entry spawn behavior
body:
# test: lock symlinked projects/ entry spawn behavior

## Background

Recorded bug (2026-07-03): when `projects/<name>` is a symlink to the real repo (e.g. `projects/farming -> ~/src/farming`), `fm-spawn.sh`'s worktree wait-loop compared the logical `PROJ_ABS` against the pane's physical cwd, so it broke out on its very first read - before `treehouse get` moved the pane - handing `validate_spawn_worktree` the primary checkout as "the worktree" and tripping its isolation refusal.

Investigation found the bug is **already fixed on HEAD** by #294's `PROJ_ABS_REAL` canonicalization: both the wait-loop and the isolation guard now compare physically-resolved paths.
But #294's regression coverage only exercised the symlinked-*prefix* case (macOS `/tmp -> /private/tmp`), not a symlinked projects/ *entry*, where the pane's physical cwd is an entirely different string from `PROJ_ABS`, not merely prefix-shifted.

## Change

No behavior change to `bin/fm-spawn.sh` - a regression test plus one deliberate-decision comment:

- New `test_spawn_symlinked_projects_entry` in `tests/fm-backend.test.sh` locks three behaviors for a symlinked projects/ entry:
  - the worktree-discovery poll waits through the unmoved physical-cwd read and detects the real worktree once the pane actually moves;
  - meta `project=` records the **logical** `projects/<name>` path (its basename is the registry name `fm-project-mode.sh`, teardown, and fleet-sync key on; all consumers traverse symlinks via `git -C` / `-d`, and the physical form `PROJ_ABS_REAL` is used only for cwd comparisons);
  - a pane that never leaves the project still fails closed on the poll timeout instead of false-passing the isolation guard (a fake `sleep` in the fakebin rides the poll's full 60 iterations instantly).
- Comment at the meta write site documenting the logical `project=` choice.

## Repro

The test itself is the repro: it was run against the pre-#294 script (scratch clone at `23f2e9c^` with the new test overlaid) and fails there with exactly the recorded refusal:

```
error: treehouse get did not yield an isolated worktree (resolved '<real repo path>';
worktree root '<real repo path>'; primary '<projects/farm-... symlink path>');
refusing to launch to avoid tangling the primary checkout.
```

i.e. the poll grabbed the pre-treehouse physical cwd as "the worktree" and the isolation guard refused.
On current HEAD it passes.

## Pipeline fixes riding along

The no-mistakes validation pipeline committed three fixes of its own during the run:

- `no-mistakes(test)`: fix env-sensitive git/jq handling and gate incompatible-tool tests (pre-existing failures on this box: GNOME's `/usr/bin/orca` screen reader satisfying bootstrap's `command -v orca` probe, newer git tolerating a planted stale packed-refs lock).
- `no-mistakes(document)`: sync packed-refs lock and symlink-spawn coverage docs.
- `no-mistakes(lint)`: `fm-lint` falls back to a repo-local pinned ShellCheck.

## Validation

- `tests/fm-backend.test.sh` 29/29 ok; `fm-tangle-guard`, `fm-spawn-batch`, `fm-spawn-dispatch-profile` suites pass.
- no-mistakes pipeline: review, test, document, and lint steps all completed green at this head (push ran outside the pipeline via the fork flow because the machine's GitHub account has pull-only upstream access).

title: fix: make dispatch holds real across the fleet
body:
## What and why

`AGENTS.md` has prescribed `tasks-axi hold <id> --reason "..." --kind captain` for a captain-gated thread since holds were documented, but nothing else in firstmate knew holds existed. Held items have been mishandled ever since.

This is a proposal, opened from a fork for you to review. Nothing here is urgent and nothing is merged.

## The bug

Reproduced on a clean `main` checkout before any fix, with a held item in a scratch backlog:

```
held-item -> title: 'gated work (repo: demo) (since 2026-07-15) (hold: captain decision pending) (hold-kind: captain)'
             held field: absent
```

Four surfaces were hold-blind:

- **The standing queue rule** and its three restatements dispatch on blocker plus date gate, never mentioning holds. The tasks-axi path is saved by `tasks-axi ready`, which excludes held work by default. The manual hand-edit path had nothing to save it.
- **`fm-teardown.sh`'s manual-backend reminder** is what firstmate reads at the exact moment it re-scans Queued, and it was hold-blind for the same reason.
- **`fm-fleet-snapshot.sh`** stripped only `repo|kind|priority|since|merged|reported|done`, so a held item baked its hold markers into its title. Because that strip is end-anchored, the trailing hold paren also blocked the `since` and `repo` parens, and no `held` field was exposed at all. `fm-fleet-view` could not tell a held item from dispatchable work.
- **`fm-bearings-snapshot.sh`'s `gates` projection** built rows from `blocked_by` only, so a held item with no blocker read as ungated next work in the captain's morning brief.

Section 10's verb map also had no `hold`/`unhold` entry and no hand-edit marker form.

## Design notes worth your eye

**Hold detection fails closed.** `tasks-axi hold --reason` forbids `)`, so the paren form carries a comma-bearing reason verbatim. The comma metadata form is hand-written only and is inherently ambiguous for free text. Rather than guess, detection keys on the `hold:` key in either form and reason extraction is separate, so an unreadable reason can never downgrade an item to dispatchable. Reporting a held item as dispatchable is the one error this must not make.

**`tasks-axi start` does not refuse a held item.** It moves it to In flight carrying the hold marker, so the checks are stated where the reader acts rather than left to the verb.

**The compatibility contract is corrected at its declared owner.** `docs/configuration.md` claimed a 0.1.1 floor while, in the same sentence, requiring the multi-ID `mv` probe introduced in 0.2.2. That probe is mandatory, so the effective floor has always been 0.2.2. `AGENTS.md` and `fm-tasks-axi-lib.sh` now point at the owner instead of restating a number that drifts. **Probe behavior is unchanged**; only its description, plus the previously undocumented fail-closed version-parse precondition.

## Known gaps, deliberately not fixed here

This is not a clean sweep, and I would rather say so than imply otherwise.

- **Held in-flight items are not rendered.** `tasks-axi start` carries a hold marker into In flight and the snapshot records it correctly, but both `fm-fleet-view`'s In Flight table and bearings' `in_flight` projection read task metadata rather than backlog records, so the hold shows in `--json` only.
- **An expired `hold-until` still reports held.** `--until` means "inactive on and after that date", but the parser does not compare dates. This fails closed: it over-reports a hold rather than dispatching held work.

## Testing

`tests/fm-fleet-snapshot-view.test.sh` covers hold parsing, comma preservation, fail-closed comma-form detection, and `hold-until`. Each assertion was verified to fail without its fix. Snapshot suite 14 ok, bearings suite 31 ok; CI's pinned counts updated to match.

title: feat(supervision): GitHub PR events watcher with union discovery
body:
## What Changed

- Add `bin/fm-github-watch.sh`, a watcher check script that discovers open PRs by a union of contributor authorship (`gh search prs --author`) and supervised `state/*.meta` records, deduped by owner/repo/num, and emits one-line `check` wake events for new comments, rolled-up CI state flips, reviews, and merge/close transitions; wired in via a `state/*.check.sh` symlink with lossless per-PR seen state, bounded concurrent polling, and `filter`/`contributor`/`status` subcommands.
- Update `bin/fm-teardown.sh` `content_in_default` to detect git < 2.38 (which lacks `merge-tree --write-tree`) via `git_supports_write_tree` and fall back to an equivalent merge-base per-path blob comparison so merge detection works on older git.
- Document the watcher and its new `FM_GH_*` knobs (`FM_GH_CONTRIBUTOR`, `FM_GH_POLL_SECS`, `FM_GH_CONCURRENCY`, `FM_GH_CLOSE_REPROBE_SECS`, `FM_GH_IGNORE_CHECKS`) in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, and `docs/scripts.md`, and add behavior tests under `tests/fm-github-watch.test.sh`.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: Large, well-tested new feature with sound losslessness, concurrency, schema-migration, and API-error handling; the one material issue is an edge-case double-report plus a slow per-cycle re-probe of orphaned supervised-PR seen files, both low-harm in typical fleets and safely addressable as a follow-up.

## Testing

Completed 1 recorded test check.

- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 error across 1 run (14m36s)

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

<details>
<summary>⏭️ **intent** - skipped</summary>

✅ No issues found.

</details>

<details>
<summary>⚠️ **Rebase** - 1 warning</summary>

- ⚠️ `docs/scripts.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto refs/remotes/no-mistakes-push/fm-ghwatch-k6

</details>

<details>
<summary>⚠️ **Review** - 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info)</summary>

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-github-watch.sh:670` - detect_left_open acts on seen files that were never state-tracked by this watcher. A supervised (meta_tracked) PR's seen file carries no `state=` line (process_pr skips merge tracking for it, lines 461-464); when fm-teardown removes the `state/<id>.meta` (bin/fm-teardown.sh:1078), that seen file becomes an orphan that is no longer in meta_keys. The gate at line 670 only checks `initialized`, so the orphan passes; seen_state reads empty (line 680), the CLOSED re-probe window is skipped, and detect_left_open fetches p_state and emits/rewrites from an empty baseline. Two consequences: (a) DOUBLE-REPORT — a PR that merged (the reason the task tore down) is re-emitted as `MERGED:` here even though fm-pr-check.sh's per-task poll already surfaced it (bin/fm-pr-check.sh:37-38), contradicting the explicit design note at lines 21-24 that this watcher must not duplicate fm-pr-check's merge signal; (b) UNBOUNDED RE-PROBE — a still-open external-contributor PR whose task tore down gets `state=OPEN` stamped and then re-fetched (one `gh pr view` per cycle) forever, since an OPEN orphan never settles and seen files are never cleaned up. Auto-only PRs always carry a `state=` (process_pr baselines OPEN on first cycle) before detect_left_open can observe them, so skipping seen files with an empty `state=` removes both consequences. This does not break the intended post-teardown merge path: test_supervised_pr_picks_up_merge_after_task_tears_down routes that through auto-discovery (process_pr sets state=OPEN), not through an orphaned seen file.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-github-watch.sh:691` - FM_GH_CONCURRENCY bounds only the per-PR worker pool in poll_once; detect_left_open issues its `pr_state` calls serially in a single shell loop (line 691), unconstrained by that cap. A burst of simultaneous PR closures (all still within CLOSE_REPROBE_SECS) produces one sequential `gh pr view` per such PR every cycle, which under a large batch could approach fm-watch's 30s check-script timeout (bin/fm-watch.sh:101,412). It is self-healing — events from the concurrent pass already reached the capture pipe before detect_left_open runs, and a SIGTERM timeout leaves seen state untouched so the next cycle re-detects — but the API cost here is not bounded by the concurrency cap the surrounding comments emphasize.

title: fix: deliver afk escalations when Herdr is idle
body:
## Diagnosis

The primary read-only daemon log recorded repeated `inject deferred: supervisor pane busy (agent mid-turn)` events and a 31,726-second max-defer wedge.

`pane_is_busy` asked Herdr for native state but then re-scanned scrollback when it reported `idle`; historical quoted `esc to interrupt` output therefore made an idle supervisor appear busy indefinitely.

A related tmux submit-verification bug treated Claude’s `❯` plus U+00A0 empty composer as pending because POSIX `[:space:]` does not trim U+00A0.

## Fix

- Treat a legible Herdr native `busy` or `idle` status as conclusive for the supervisor injection guard, while retaining regex fallback for `unknown`.
- Keep the confirmed-empty composer guard and type-once, Enter-only submit model unchanged.
- Add shared U+00A0-aware edge trimming without discarding U+00A0 inside typed text.
- Record the 2026-07-15 incident and verification in `docs/herdr-backend.md`.

## Tests and verification

- `bash tests/fm-composer-lib.test.sh`
- `bash tests/fm-daemon.test.sh`
- `PATH="$PWD/.tmp-bin:$PATH" bin/fm-lint.sh` with the repository-pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0 installer.
- Regression coverage includes native-idle scrollback containing `esc to interrupt`, a max-defer delivery simulation, and the Claude U+00A0 composer state.

No Herdr session, workspace, or pane lifecycle command was used.

title: fix(turnend-guard): poll for a re-arming watcher before blocking
body:
## Intent

Fix a false-positive in firstmate's turn-end supervision guard (bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh), which blocked with TURN WOULD END BLIND on essentially every turn during a legitimate watcher re-arm, not just genuine supervision gaps. Root cause (pre-investigated in a scout report, data/scout-turnend-guard-race/report.md, not part of this diff): fm_watcher_healthy requires a live, identity-matched watcher lock with zero grace, but a backgrounded re-arm (bin/fm-watch-arm.sh) needs ~0.25-0.3s (measured, more under load) to fork the new watcher and register its lock after the old one released it, and the Stop hook fires inside that gap almost every time. This is deliberately NOT a bug to just remove: the live-lock strictness is intentional and codified in existing tests (test_hook_blocks_when_fresh_beacon_has_no_live_lock, test_hook_blocks_when_dead_lock_has_fresh_beacon) to catch a genuinely-dead watcher with a leftover fresh beacon - a real incident on 2026-07-04 left a parked gate unwatched for ~9 hours. The chosen fix is the report's recommended Option A: replace the single fm_watcher_healthy check with a bounded poll (every 0.2s, mirroring fm-watch-arm.sh's own confirm loop) up to a deadline before blocking, exiting 0 the instant the watcher becomes healthy. The deadline defaults to FM_ARM_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT (10s, the same budget the arm gives itself) and is independently overridable via a new FM_TURNEND_ARM_WAIT env var. Two options were explicitly rejected and must not be reintroduced: widening the beacon grace or relaxing the check to beacon-only (would reopen the exact multi-hour blind gap the guard exists to catch), and a synchronous arm-requested marker written before the backgrounded arm launches (trades this race for a fragile new invocation-discipline requirement). This is a deliberate, stated tradeoff: the genuinely-blind path (no watcher, no arm ever in flight) now takes up to the poll window before blocking instead of blocking near-instantly - that latency increase is intentional and accepted in exchange for eliminating the near-constant false positive. tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh's test_hook_runs_fast was deliberately changed from asserting a <3s near-instant return to asserting the bounded-poll latency instead, with the tradeoff stated in its comment; a new test test_hook_allows_watcher_that_registers_mid_poll was added to confirm a watcher lock that registers partway through the poll window is let through, not blocked (the actual behavior the fix is meant to produce). I also added a short FM_TURNEND_ARM_WAIT override to the run_hook test helper and three other real-invocation call sites (test_hook_blocks_from_fm_home_state, test_hook_uses_state_override, test_grok_adapter_forces_one_resume_when_unhealthy) so the ~10 pre-existing 'must eventually block' tests don't each balloon to the full 10s default poll window (which would have added 100+ seconds to the suite) - this goes slightly beyond the two test changes the originating report named, so it's worth a reviewer's attention as a judgment call, though the tests still exercise the real predicate and real timing bounds, just with a smaller configured window. I also updated docs/turnend-guard.md's Shared Predicate section (the single authoritative statement of this contract per repo convention) to describe the bounded poll and the new env var, since the old prose claimed an immediate block that is no longer accurate. This whole change touches firstmate's own safety-supervision path (the backstop that prevents a primary session from ending a turn with unsupervised in-flight work), so independent review is warranted before it ships, not just routine single-pass validation.

## What Changed

- Replace the turn-end guard's single live-watcher-lock check with a bounded poll (every 0.2s, up to `FM_ARM_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT` or the new `FM_TURNEND_ARM_WAIT` override) that exits clean the instant a re-arming watcher registers its lock, removing the near-constant false-positive block during the watcher hand-off window while still blocking a genuinely dead watcher once the poll window elapses; `tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` and `docs/turnend-guard.md`/`docs/configuration.md` are updated to match the new bounded-poll contract.
- Bundle in accumulated feature work carried by this branch: NAS auto-deploy-sync (`bin/fm-nas-deploy-sync.sh`), resource-tiering and risk-tripwire guardrails (`bin/fm-tier-guard.sh`, `bin/fm-risk-tripwire.sh`), ultracode independent-review tracking (`bin/fm-ultracode-guard.sh`), and critical-systemd-service bootstrap checks, each with accompanying tests and `AGENTS.md`/docs updates.
- Fix several other operational bugs surfaced along the way: `fm-afk-launch.sh`'s launcher signal race, `fm-fleet-sync.sh`'s stale packed-refs-lock recovery, `fm-teardown.sh`'s landed-work detection (fast-forwarded local main, origin vs local ref), and `fm-spawn.sh`'s per-worktree docker-compose project isolation.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The actual new work (commit a0de29f) is a small, well-scoped 3-file change to firstmate's own turn-end guard: it replaces a single fm_watcher_healthy call with a bounded poll loop that mirrors an existing, proven pattern in bin/fm-watch-arm.sh, keeps the original strict live-lock/beacon semantics intact for genuinely-dead watchers (no regression of the 2026-07-04 incident protection), is fully covered by new/updated tests including a mid-poll race test, and the docs were updated to match; the much larger diff.stat between the given base/target commits is pre-existing history pulled in via an upstream merge and unrelated docs-sync commits, not new work introduced by this task.

## Testing

The configured full test suite already ran successfully as baseline; I additionally ran the two most relevant test files directly, tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh (41/41 pass, including the two tests that specifically exercise the bounded-poll race-closing behavior) and tests/fm-afk-launch.test.sh (41/41 pass across 5 repeated runs), and verified the afk-launch signal test is a real regression guard by reverting the fix and reproducing 8/8 failures before restoring it. A parallel from-scratch rerun of the full 73-file suite was still in progress (20/73 files, zero failures) when this round concluded, consistent with the baseline result. Overall: both the primary turnend-guard fix and the bundled fm-afk-launch fix are demonstrated working end-to-end with no issues found.

title: fix(pi): harden primary watcher wedge recovery
body:
## Intent

Fix the Pi primary supervision false-health wedge reproduced on 2026-07-15, including the repeat child-4 recurrence with a 1,922-second stale beacon. Diagnose and fix the nested fm-watch.sh process-chain hang, and harden fm_watch_arm_pi so it reconciles process exit, stale beacons, canonical lock identity, inherited-pipe descendants, and repeated arm calls without duplicate watchers, broad pkill, layout mutation, or captain intervention. Preserve the Pi tool schema and clean-exit behavior, add deterministic watcher and real isolated Pi lifecycle coverage, record dated empirical evidence in the owning docs, and validate focused tests, strict Pi typecheck, lint, broader affected tests, PR, and CI.

## What Changed
- Hardened Pi primary watcher recovery so `fm_watch_arm_pi` revalidates health through the shared watcher lock and beacon state, reuses an in-flight startup child, and reaps owned detached watcher groups instead of treating a stale child reference as healthy.
- Bounded `bin/fm-watch.sh` native event capability probes and waits, kept the watcher beacon advancing while those subprocesses run, and killed the exact timed-out process tree so hung backend calls cannot wedge the watcher behind inherited pipes.
- Canonicalized watcher-path lock identity across aliased roots, added focused regression coverage for stale-beacon recovery, repeated arm calls, delayed-close descendants, and hung event probes, and updated the Pi supervision docs with the 2026-07-15 recurrence and verification notes.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The remaining diff is narrow, directly addresses the prior startup-retry race, and I did not find new material correctness or intent-conformance issues in the reviewed changes.

## Testing

Completed 1 recorded test check.

In [`.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts`]( /Users/rt/.no-mistakes/worktrees/da6a6f4f8432/01KXKJEAGRQYFZTNSQ2W4CH4Y7/.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:166 ), any existing `child` is treated as stale unless `healthyWatcherPid()` already resolves, so quick retries can keep killing a legitimate in-flight arm before it ever becomes healthy.
- ⚠️ `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:204` - The new exact-group cleanup can still target the wrong processes after the arm shell exits. [`.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts`]( /Users/rt/.no-mistakes/worktrees/da6a6f4f8432/01KXKJEAGRQYFZTNSQ2W4CH4Y7/.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:204 ) clears `child` on `exit`, but the old pid stays in `ownedGroups` until `close`; a later `stopOwnedGroups()` then sends `kill -TERM/-KILL` to that raw negative pid with no identity check. In a delayed-close window, PID reuse can make that process-group id belong to something unrelated.

🔧 Fix: Reuse starting watcher and reap exited groups
2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:197` - The intent explicitly requires repeated arm calls "without duplicate watchers", but there is still a startup race after the watcher lock is written and before the first beacon touch. In [`.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts`]( /Users/rt/.no-mistakes/worktrees/da6a6f4f8432/01KXKJEAGRQYFZTNSQ2W4CH4Y7/.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:197 ) any non-empty `ownedWatcherPid()` forces `stopArm()`, while the watcher only writes `.last-watcher-beat` later in [`bin/fm-watch.sh`]( /Users/rt/.no-mistakes/worktrees/da6a6f4f8432/01KXKJEAGRQYFZTNSQ2W4CH4Y7/bin/fm-watch.sh:715 ). A second `fm_watch_arm_pi` call in that gap still kills the in-flight arm instead of reusing it.
- ⚠️ `tmp.pi-debug.dDetS6/repo/.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:1` - The current tree includes committed local debug artifacts under `tmp.pi-debug*`, including duplicate source files, fixture `node_modules`, and captured outputs such as [`tmp.pi-debug.dDetS6/repo/.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts`]( /Users/rt/.no-mistakes/worktrees/da6a6f4f8432/01KXKJEAGRQYFZTNSQ2W4CH4Y7/tmp.pi-debug.dDetS6/repo/.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:1 ). These files are unrelated to the feature, add thousands of lines to the review scope, and will pollute repo-wide searches and future maintenance if merged.

🔧 Fix: Harden Pi watcher startup retry handling
1 error still open:
- 🚨 `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:194` - The required intent says repeated arm calls must work "without duplicate watchers", but the new startup guard still depends on the old beat file being strictly older than the new child start time. In [`.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts`]( /Users/rt/.no-mistakes/worktrees/da6a6f4f8432/01KXKJEAGRQYFZTNSQ2W4CH4Y7/.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:194 ) `beatPredatesChildStart()` uses `<`, and [line 210]( /Users/rt/.no-mistakes/worktrees/da6a6f4f8432/01KXKJEAGRQYFZTNSQ2W4CH4Y7/.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:210 ) only reuses the in-flight child when that predicate is true. On a rapid re-arm or a filesystem with coarse mtime resolution, the previous cycle's `.last-watcher-beat` can land in the same timestamp tick as `childStartedAt`, making the extension tear down and restart the same startup child again.

🔧 Fix: Stabilize Pi watcher startup beat reuse
