title: feat: add secure Telegram notifications and approvals
body:
## Intent Apply captain decision key=telegram-rate-cap: DEFER, never drop for authenticated over-cap Telegram updates (offset holds; next sweep re-fetches). Includes respond-layer defer, poll re-wake of pending inbox, offset persist diagnostics, and threat-model tests. Push/PR only to hsuanchenlin/firstmate fork, never kunchenguid/firstmate. ## What Changed - Add opt-in Telegram notifications and bounded `status`, `approve`, `deny`, and green-PR `merge` commands through the existing watcher and away-mode supervision flow. - Secure inbound processing with sender allowlists, freshness and deduplication checks, audit logs, durable offsets and actions, and deferred retry for authenticated updates or commands that exceed rate limits. - Document activation, configuration, recovery, and threat boundaries; add end-to-end Telegram coverage and harden watcher timing and OpenCode supervision behavior. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Low risk, captain, because the reply-authority boundary and full check pagination are fail-closed and conform to the stated intent. ## Testing The supplied all-tests baseline and independently rerun Telegram threat-model suite passed. After correcting a malformed fixture response in the first evidence attempt, the hermetic end-to-end journey proved poll-layer defer with offset hold, next-sweep re-fetch, respond-layer queue retention, empty-poll re-wake, later execution, and deduplicated offset-persistence diagnostics. The CLI and persisted-state transcript is the reviewer-visible artifact; this change has no rendered UI. No remote writes were made.
Evidence: Telegram rate-cap end-to-end transcript `Authenticated update 901 was deferred with offset held at 901, re-fetched next sweep, retained by the respond-layer rate cap, re-woken during an empty poll, and executed after the window expired. An offset persistence failure emitted a diagnostic once and left update 950 available for re-fetch.` ```text Telegram rate-cap end-to-end journey Configured: authenticated sender 222, private chat 111, cap 1 per 2 seconds 1. First Telegram poll receives two authenticated commands poll output: telegram-msg 900 persisted offset: 901 inbox files: 900.json audit decision: 1784451763 inbound deferred update_id=901 reason=rate-cap 2. First accepted command is processed respond output: ok 900 status 3. Next poll re-fetches the deferred Telegram update poll output: telegram-msg 901 persisted offset: 902 inbox files: 901.json 4. Respond layer is still over-cap, so it queues instead of dropping respond output: deferred 901 rate-limited queued inbox still present: yes 5. Empty Telegram poll re-wakes the pending inbox item poll output: telegram-msg 901 6. After the rate window, the queued command executes respond output: ok 901 approve k1 task queued inbox still present: no persisted action: {"action":"approve","args":["k1","task"],"update_id":"901"} final audit: 1784451768 respond ok update_id=901 verb=approve key=k1 task=task 7. Offset persistence failure surfaces once and leaves the update unconfirmed first poll output: telegram-mode-error cannot persist offset telegram-msg 950 second poll output: telegram-msg 950 audit diagnostic: 1784451768 poll error cannot persist offset Evidence state directories: rate-cap journey: /var/folders/38/1lc6tnp133v9455jt6l9b4lw0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KXWKK76FV3Z9XX283EFR7TDY/telegram-rate-cap-home.Sp77S2 offset failure: /var/folders/38/1lc6tnp133v9455jt6l9b4lw0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KXWKK76FV3Z9XX283EFR7TDY/telegram-offset-failure-home.vjfuku ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 10 issues found → auto-fixed (4) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-telegram-lib.sh:301` - Intent requires "DEFER, never drop for authenticated over-cap Telegram updates" and respond-layer defer, but rate-log write failures are ignored before returning allowed. An unwritable or invalid log silently disables the response rate cap and executes commands that should remain queued. Require durable publication or defer on failure. - 🚨 `bin/fm-telegram-poll.sh:229` - Intent requires "poll re-wake of pending inbox", but this scan runs only after a successful HTTP 200 with a valid body. Curl failures, HTTP errors, empty bodies, and ok=false responses leave already-local deferred commands unnotified indefinitely. Emit pending inbox notifications independently of network success. - 🚨 `bin/fm-telegram-respond.sh:66` - Production merge verification cannot succeed with the supported gh-axi interface: pr view requires a numeric PR, does not accept --json, and returns rendered output rather than the JSON expected by jq. The test hook masks this, so every real Telegram merge is refused. Parse the URL and use supported gh-axi checks or API commands. - 🚨 `bin/fm-telegram-lib.sh:585` - The lookup returns the first task with a matching decision key. Keys are task-scoped and unkeyed decisions all become "default", so an approval can target an arbitrary task when multiple matches exist. Refuse ambiguous matches or require a task-qualified command. - 🚨 `bin/fm-telegram-respond.sh:225` - After creating an action record, the source inbox file is removed before the supervising agent applies the action. A crash in that interval leaves the action durable but without any pending inbox notification or startup inventory entry, so it can remain unapplied indefinitely. Preserve or re-notify pending actions until acknowledged. - 🚨 `bin/fm-telegram-send.sh:149` - Dry-run sends record PR URLs as merge authority even though nothing was sent to Telegram. This contradicts the documented requirement that the PR was previously sent to the same chat. Confirm this deliberate test behavior or stop dry runs from granting authority. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-telegram-lib.sh:481` - The notified-PR registry stores only timestamp and URL, while lookup ignores the configured chat ID. Changing FM_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID therefore transfers old merge authority to a chat that never received those URLs. Store and match chat ID, failing closed for legacy rows. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-telegram-respond.sh:72` - A PR with zero CI checks is explicitly classified as green. This broadens Telegram merge authority beyond the documented "green PR" boundary. Confirm that checkless PRs are intentionally eligible or require at least one successful, neutral, or skipped check. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-telegram-lib.sh:551` - The status reply sends raw task IDs and verbatim status-event lines. AGENTS.md section 9 forbids exposing task IDs, status prefixes, or relaying status lines verbatim in captain-facing chat. Translate these records into outcome-level wording before sending. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:661` - Telegram setup duplicates the X-mode artifact lifecycle and calls helpers named x_mode_*. Extract a shared channel-artifact setup helper so dependency checks, cleanup, publication, and cadence behavior cannot drift. 🔧 Fix: Harden Telegram deferral and merge authority 6 issues (3 errors, 3 warnings) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-telegram-respond.sh:135` - Intent requires "DEFER, never drop for authenticated over-cap Telegram updates", but a missing `jq` or parse failure becomes `text=` and the valid queued inbox file is then deleted as empty. Distinguish dependency/read failures from a genuinely empty payload and preserve the file for retry. - 🚨 `.opencode/plugins/fm-primary-watch-arm.js:100` - A Telegram-only OpenCode home never arms supervision: `shouldArm()` recognizes `x-mode.env` and task metadata but not the newly generated `telegram-mode.env`. With no active tasks, the poller therefore never starts and pending inbox re-wakes cannot occur. Treat either channel cadence file as supervision demand. - 🚨 `bin/fm-telegram-respond.sh:85` - The aggregate check test accepts any nonzero total with zero failures or pending checks. The supported `gh-axi` classifies CANCELLED and EXPECTED checks as skipped, so canceled or expected-only checks can authorize a Telegram merge despite the green-PR boundary. Inspect individual conclusions or explicitly reject these states. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-telegram-respond.sh:224` - Approve and deny acknowledgements expose the raw internal task identifier through `(task $task)`, contrary to AGENTS.md section 9's captain-facing output contract. Acknowledge the decision key and outcome without the internal identifier. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-telegram-lib.sh:550` - The work count includes every metadata record, including persistent idle secondmates, even though they are agents rather than work items. This can report work under way when no actual work exists; exclude `kind=secondmate` records from this count. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-telegram-send.sh:186` - After Telegram successfully receives a PR URL, failure to persist its merge-authority record is silently ignored. The later merge command is then inexplicably refused despite the documented successful-send contract. Surface and audit the persistence failure and retain a reliable repair path. 🔧 Fix: Harden Telegram recovery and OpenCode supervision 2 warnings still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-telegram-respond.sh:86` - The directive was to reject CANCELLED/EXPECTED-only rollups, but requiring `passed == total` rejects every PR containing a legitimate skipped check, including otherwise-green conditional workflows. Query conclusions without gh-axi's lossy skipped aggregation, or confirm that any skipped check should block Telegram merges. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-telegram-send.sh:197` - After Telegram confirms delivery, failure of both authority stores exits 3, which the script defines as a transport/API failure. Callers may retry and send duplicate notifications. Use a distinct confirmed-delivery partial-failure status or otherwise mark this outcome non-retryable. 🔧 Fix: Refine Telegram merge eligibility and delivery outcomes 2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-telegram-send.sh:191` - Every successful send, including `--reply`, scans its text and grants merge authority for embedded PR URLs. Because `deny <key> [reason]` echoes the arbitrary reason, an authenticated phone holder can place an unnotified PR URL in the reason, make the bot register it through its acknowledgement, then issue `merge`. This bypasses the requirement that Firstmate previously outbound-notified the PR. Exclude command replies from authority registration or require an explicit authority-grant flag. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-telegram-respond.sh:85` - The criterion says "green PR means all present checks are SUCCESS/NEUTRAL/SKIPPED", but this request fetches at most 100 check runs while later comparing the returned records with the full API `total_count`. A PR with more than 100 allowed checks is always refused. Page through every check run while preserving the fail-closed count comparison, or confirm an intentional 100-check ceiling. 🔧 Fix: Secure Telegram reply authority and paginate checks ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` - Supplied baseline: `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` - `bash tests/fm-telegram-mode.test.sh` - `bash /var/folders/38/1lc6tnp133v9455jt6l9b4lw0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KXWKK76FV3Z9XX283EFR7TDY/telegram-rate-cap-e2e.sh "$PWD" | tee /var/folders/38/1lc6tnp133v9455jt6l9b4lw0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KXWKK76FV3Z9XX283EFR7TDY/telegram-rate-cap-e2e-transcript.txt` using a fake Telegram Bot API and the production poll/respond scripts - `git remote -v; git config --get branch.fm/telegram-impl.remote; git config --get branch.fm/telegram-impl.pushRemote; git config --get remote.pushDefault; git status --short; git diff --name-only`

title: fix(herdr): serialize workspace ensure so parallel first spawns share one workspace
body:
## Intent Fix a live-fired race in the experimental herdr session backend: when firstmate spawns several crewmates in parallel as a home's FIRST spawns of the session, fm_backend_herdr_workspace_ensure ran find-before-create with no cross-process serialization, so every parallel spawn minted its own workspace with the identical home label (reproduced 2026-07-19 on real herdr 0.7.4/protocol 16, macOS aarch64: three batch-spawned crewmates produced three 'firstmate' workspaces; herdr enforces no label uniqueness so nothing failed, the fleet just fragmented across duplicate spaces). Upstream issue: #730. Deliberate decisions the captain made: serialize only the find-or-create window with an atomic mkdir lock (portable - macOS ships no flock) placed under TMPDIR rather than the home's state/ dir so unit tests and CI checkouts never write into the repo; key the lock by cksum of FM_HOME plus session plus home label, the same axes that scope the workspace itself, so different homes/sessions never contend; holder records its pid and a waiter breaks the lock only for a provably dead holder (kill -0 fails), a lock dir whose pid file has not appeared yet is waited out within the bounded 12s acquire budget; FAIL-OPEN on acquire timeout (warn on stderr, proceed unlocked) is intentional - a lock anomaly must never block dispatch, the worst case deliberately degrades to the pre-fix race, mirroring the repo's 'quota trouble never blocks dispatch' posture; no trap-based release inside the lib function (could clobber caller traps), explicit release on every return path instead. Three new unit tests against the stateful fake (parallel ensures mint exactly one shared workspace; deterministic hold-then-release proof that a waiter adopts the winner with zero creates; a provably dead holder's lock is broken and released), plus the mandated empirical incident section in docs/herdr-backend.md with the exact commands and output observed. bin/fm-lint.sh passes under the pinned shellcheck 0.11.0; the full tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh suite is green. Pre-fix duplicate workspaces need no migration - they self-heal through normal teardown. ## What Changed - `fm_backend_herdr_workspace_ensure` serializes its find-or-create window with a new `fm_backend_herdr_workspace_lock_acquire`/`_release` pair in `bin/backends/herdr.sh`: an atomic `mkdir` lock under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}` (portable, no flock on macOS), keyed by cksum of `$FM_HOME` + session + home label, so parallel first spawns of the same home mint exactly one shared workspace instead of duplicates. The holder records its pid; a waiter breaks a provably dead holder's lock atomically (rename-aside before removal), and the lock is fail-open: on acquire timeout (12s budget) or an uncreatable lock dir (e.g. broken `TMPDIR`, detected after three consecutive misses) the spawn proceeds unlocked with a stderr warning — a lock anomaly never blocks dispatch. Release is explicit on every return path, no trap-based cleanup. - Three new tests in `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh` against the stateful fake: concurrent first spawns mint one workspace, a waiter adopts a live holder's workspace with zero creates, and a dead holder's lock is broken and released. - `docs/herdr-backend.md` gains the empirical incident section (2026-07-19, herdr 0.7.4/protocol 16, macOS aarch64: three batch-spawned crewmates produced three `firstmate` workspaces) with the observed commands/output, root cause, fix mechanics, and the note that pre-fix duplicates self-heal through normal teardown. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The round-2 commit correctly implements both prior findings (atomic mv-based dead-holder break and fast fail-open after three consecutive lock-dir misses) without introducing new races, keeps all three unit tests and the documented semantics consistent, and preserves every intent criterion including fail-open and break-only-provably-dead-holder. ## Testing Baseline-Suite und volle tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh grün (104 ok, inkl. der 3 neuen Lock-Tests); zusätzlich eine manuelle End-to-End-Demo, die den Duplicate-Workspace-Race am Base-Commit reproduziert (3 creates, fragmentierte Container), mit dem Fix genau einen geteilten Workspace zeigt und das fail-open-Verhalten bei kaputtem TMPDIR (Warnung, Spawn läuft weiter) belegt; Transcripts und Demo-Skript als Evidenz gesichert. Kein visuelles Artefakt, da die Änderung eine reine Shell-Backend-Bibliothek ohne UI-Oberfläche betrifft — CLI-Transcripts sind die reviewer-sichtbare Oberfläche.

title: fix(supervision): probe stat flavor at runtime instead of branching on uname
body:
## Intent

Fix upstream issue #464: on macOS, when GNU coreutils' stat is ahead of /usr/bin/stat on PATH (a common Homebrew layout), firstmate's supervision helpers picked the BSD 'stat -f' form based on uname=Darwin. GNU stat reads -f as its filesystem-mode flag and emits a multi-line 'File: ...' dump instead of an epoch, and under 'set -u' that stray string crashed the watcher with 'File: unbound variable', taking supervision down.

The fix replaces OS-based (uname) stat-flavor detection with a runtime capability probe. Scope is deliberately narrow (PR 1 of a planned series, shaped to touch as few existing files as possible so it stays rebase-conflict-resistant against an actively-changing upstream):
1. New sourceable helper bin/fm-stat-lib.sh: single owner of a portable file-mtime read (fm_stat_mtime) that probes 'stat -c %Y /' once, caches the result in FM_STAT_FLAVOR, and falls back to 'stat -f %m' for BSD; it never branches on uname. Mechanics live in the header comment, matching the other bin/fm-*-lib.sh sourceable libs.
2. Rewire ONLY bin/fm-supervision-lib.sh (the exact reported crash site) to source fm-stat-lib.sh and call the shared function instead of its own uname branch.
3. Colocated tests/fm-stat-lib.test.sh covering that the helper returns a valid epoch mtime on this platform, tracks the real mtime (not a foreign stat dump), and prints nothing for a missing path.

Deliberately NOT touching bin/fm-wake-lib.sh, bin/fm-lock-lib.sh, bin/fm-watch.sh, or bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh: they keep their current uname branch, and migrating them to the shared helper is intentionally deferred to follow-up PRs to keep this a single-existing-hot-file change. One necessary consequence: tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh copies supervision scripts into a temp bin, so a line was added to copy the new fm-stat-lib.sh dependency alongside them. The PR must open against the parent repo kunchenguid/firstmate from the fork.

## What Changed

- Added `bin/fm-stat-lib.sh`, a sourceable helper whose `fm_stat_mtime` reads a file's epoch mtime by probing `stat -c %Y /` once (caching the result in `FM_STAT_FLAVOR`) and falling back to BSD `stat -f %m`, never branching on `uname`.
- Rewired `bin/fm-supervision-lib.sh` (and its `fm-guard.sh` caller) to source the shared helper and call `fm_stat_mtime`, replacing the OS-based stat-flavor branch that crashed the watcher with an unbound-variable error when GNU coreutils' `stat` preceded `/usr/bin/stat` on macOS PATH.
- Added `tests/fm-stat-lib.test.sh` covering a valid epoch read, real-mtime tracking, and empty output for a missing path; documented the helper in `docs/scripts.md`; and copied the new dependency into the temp bins used by `tests/fm-backend.test.sh` and `tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Small, well-bounded refactor extracting a capability-probed portable mtime helper; the sole round-1 error (dangling function call) is fixed, the probe logic is correct across GNU/BSD/busybox, and the intentionally-deferred uname sites are documented and unchanged.

## Testing

Completed 1 recorded test check.

- Outcome: ⏭️ skipped across 4 runs (1h20m26s)

- 🚨 `bin/fm-guard.sh:51` - bin/fm-guard.sh:51 still calls fm_sup_stat_mtime, but this PR deleted that function from fm-supervision-lib.sh (which fm-guard.sh sources at line 42) and replaced it with fm_stat_mtime. fm-guard.sh has no local definition of fm_sup_stat_mtime, so fm_guard_stale_episode_key now invokes an undefined function: under `set -u` (no `set -e`) it does not abort, but it emits a 'fm_sup_stat_mtime: command not found' to stderr on every call and leaves `m` empty. title: Proposal: sbx (E2B sandbox) backend — feasibility & session-continuation question
fix(spawn): acquire the task worktree with treehouse get --lease instead of an in-window treehouse get
body:
## The bug

`fm-spawn.sh` acquires a task worktree by typing `treehouse get` into the newly created task
window, then polling that window's working directory for up to 60 seconds and inferring success
when the directory changes.

Bare `treehouse get` runs its worktree setup *inside that window*, and that setup can reach the
network. With an `https` `origin` and no credential path available inside the window, git stops at
an interactive prompt:

```
Username for 'https://github.com':
```

It never returns. The poll then expires and spawn fails with:

```
error: treehouse get did not enter a worktree within 60s
```

The reported symptom is a timeout, but the actual cause is a window blocked on a password prompt,
with the worktree already half-acquired.

**Reproduced live on 2026-07-19** against a private repo with an `https` origin: the abandoned
window sat at exactly that prompt, and its working directory never left the project. While this was
happening, firstmate could not spawn **any** direct report at all — the fleet was fully blocked.

## The fix

Acquire the worktree from fm-spawn's own process using treehouse's purpose-built non-interactive
path, then move the window into it:

1. `treehouse get --lease --lease-holder "$W"` — run from fm-spawn itself, so it inherits the
   operator's working credential environment rather than the task window's. It prints only the
   worktree path on stdout, needs no terminal, and cannot block on a prompt.
2. `validate_spawn_worktree` runs **before** the window is moved, so an unusable lease can never
   become a window running an agent inside the primary checkout.
3. A plain `cd` into the leased worktree — no network, no subshell.
4. A bounded 30s confirmation that the window actually landed there before the agent launches.

`--lease` is treehouse's documented scripted acquisition path (treehouse v2.0.0): it durably
reserves the worktree so no later `get` or `prune` takes it, and it is released by `treehouse
return`.

## Why this needs no teardown change

`bin/fm-teardown.sh` already returns the task worktree with `treehouse return --force`
(`teardown_treehouse_return "$WT" "$PROJ" "worktree"`), and treehouse documents `return` as
releasing any lease. This was verified rather than assumed, and confirmed end to end in production:
after a task using the new path was torn down, the pool showed the slot back to `available`.

Leases are also not a new concept here — `fm-teardown.sh` already describes releasing a
secondmate home's durable lease. This extends an existing pattern rather than introducing a
foreign one.

## Tradeoff, stated plainly

Leases are durable by design. A task abandoned **without** teardown leaves its worktree leased, and
`treehouse prune` will not reclaim it, where a non-leased idle worktree would be.

The lease holder is labelled `fm-<task-id>` precisely so an orphan is traceable back to the task
that leaked it.

This is a deliberate trade: spawning working reliably is worth more than automatic reclamation of
abandoned slots, and abandonment already implies a teardown that did not run.

## Verification

- New `tests/fm-spawn-lease.test.sh` (4 tests): acquisition goes through `--lease` and not through
  an in-window `treehouse get`; an empty or non-directory lease fails loudly instead of launching an
  agent; the worktree is validated before the window is moved.
- 6 existing test files' fake `treehouse` stubs updated to emit `--lease` paths.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` clean (ShellCheck 0.11.0, pinned).
- `bash -n bin/fm-spawn.sh` clean.
- Full suite run across 84 test files; the only failures are 2 pre-existing ones, confirmed
  failing identically on a clean tree.
- Live: a spawn that previously timed out now succeeds, the pool reports the worktree
  `leased ... (held by fm-<task-id>)`, and the window's working directory is the leased worktree.

## Note

The header comment block grew, which shifted the fixed line range `usage()` reads to print help.
That range is updated in the same commit so `--help` output stays correct.

title: fix(x-mode): dedupe pending mention wakes

## Intent Fix the X-mode check poll so one pending relay mention wakes firstmate exactly once instead of re-emitting an identical x-mention wake every poll. Suppression must be keyed by durable per-request local state that survives inbox cleanup after a successful reply or dismiss, covers the relay's brief post-answer re-offer race, and expires so marker loss or expiry permits a genuine re-offer. A new request_id must still wake exactly once. Preserve the poll's exact one-line stdout wake protocol and silent no-wake behavior, atomic inbox publication, one-shot error diagnostics, best-effort reply-context registry write, and bounded network-free local hot path. Add hermetic colocated regression coverage without contacting the live relay. The focused hermetic X-mode suite passed, and a hermetic parallel CLI verification confirmed the exact one-line wake protocol, one wake for simultaneous offers of one request, suppression after inbox cleanup, a wake for a new request ID, and a wake after marker loss.

title: fix(watcher): keep same-hash stale suppressor across busy flicker

## Summary

- On the same-hash busy path, stop calling `clear_pause_tracking` (which wiped `.stale-<key>`). Call `clear_pause_state` only so pause-cadence markers drop while the same-hash stale suppressor remains.

title: feat(bin): add fork drift sweep, mobile lab engine, and console dashboard
body:
## Intent Reconcile the captain's fork with upstream, then build a standing mechanism so it never accumulates again. Context: origin was repointed today to the captain's fork (thevwick/firstmate) because he has no merge permission on upstream (kunchenguid/firstmate), so PRs must go to the fork from now on. The fork had diverged: 17 commits ahead, 55 behind, making any PR against it show ~40 commits of unrelated upstream work. Part 1 (already done, not in this diff): the 17 fork commits were rebased onto upstream/main and force-pushed to the fork with --force-with-lease. That was a deliberate one-off with a human watching, backed by the fork-main-backup ref. Part 2 (this change): the standing mechanism, which must be the SAFE SUBSET of that one-off. Deliberate decisions made while building it: - Fast-forward only, by design. A diverged fork is left completely untouched and reported as a loud STUCK line, mirroring how fm-fleet-sync.sh reports a stuck clone. The tool must NEVER rebase or force push automatically; reconciling a divergence stays a human operation. Reviewers should not read the absence of an automatic rebase path as a gap - it is the core safety requirement. - Pushing the fork forward requires an explicit --push flag rather than happening in the session-start sweep, because pushing is an outward-facing write. The default run only fetches, fast-forwards the LOCAL default branch, and reports. This asymmetry is intentional. - Drift is surfaced through the existing session-start bootstrap sweep as UPSTREAM_SYNC lines, following fm-fleet-sync.sh's existing skipped/recovered/STUCK vocabulary rather than inventing a new reporting convention. - Bootstrap relays ONLY the two actionable outcomes (behind, STUCK). Every skip is silent, because a skip means drift could not be assessed at all (no upstream remote, unreachable, not a repo) which is the normal state for a non-forked install and is never actionable. This preserves bootstrap's 'silent = all good' contract. - A fork that is only AHEAD of upstream reports as current, not as drift. That is the normal resting state of a fork carrying its own work; treating it as divergence would false-alarm at every session start forever. Divergence deliberately requires being BOTH ahead and behind. - The whole feature is inert for single-remote installs: with no upstream remote there is nothing to compare and no line is printed, so users who never forked see zero behavior change. - Fast-forward mechanics reuse bin/fm-ff-lib.sh (base_mode = the fetched upstream commit) so there is one ff implementation rather than several. - bootstrap resolves the new script via SCRIPT_DIR rather than $FM_ROOT/bin, because FM_ROOT is the repo being inspected for drift and is not necessarily the checkout bootstrap runs from. - /updatefirstmate deliberately KEEPS pulling from origin, which is correct on a fork. It was not changed. But it now only delivers what the fork already has, so its skill documents the coupling: bring the fork forward first, or it reports 'already current' while still behind upstream. Repo rules applied: one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never an em dash (including in code comments and output strings), shellcheck clean via bin/fm-lint.sh, and a colocated tests/fm-upstream-sync.test.sh following the existing test conventions. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh`, a fast-forward-only fork-vs-upstream reconciler, and wired it into `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` as a bounded, lock-gated session-start sweep that relays only the two actionable outcomes (`behind`, `STUCK`) as `UPSTREAM_SYNC:` lines. A diverged fork is never rebased or force-pushed; pushing the fork forward requires an explicit `--push`. Push refusals are classified from ref state rather than localized git prose, an already-advanced fork reports as current instead of stuck, an unauthorized push reports as credentials instead of divergence, and non-interactive git is scoped to the unattended sweep so a human `--push` can still authenticate. - Added `bin/fm-mobile-lab.sh`, a cached React Native branch-build engine for simulators and devices driven by an optional `config/mobile-lab.json`, plus `bin/fm-console.sh` and the `bin/fm-console/` Node app: a full-screen fleet dashboard with per-crewmate model/health/size/branch/PR cards, a live activity panel, and a mobile-lab section. Supporting fixes cover detached native builds, `fnm`/pnpm node switching, x86_64+Rosetta simulator paths, `gh-axi pr checks` parsing, console input handling, and status-file emission into firstmate state. - Hardened runtime plumbing and documented the result: `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now polls for a genuine worktree instead of accepting the first non-project cwd, `bin/fm-backend.sh` resolves a metaless backend from the runtime rather than guessing tmux, and `AGENTS.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/mobile-lab.md`, `docs/fm-console.md`, and the bootstrap-diagnostics and updatefirstmate skills were updated to match. New suites cover upstream sync, mobile lab, console, spawn worktree races, and the herdr backend. Review left two informational notes open, both documentation-only: the `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` header's line enumeration omits the drift-check timeout form, and the `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh` vocabulary table does not show the optional `: ` suffix on the `current` line. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The feature is fast-forward-only by construction, inert for non-forked installs, bounded by a timeout at session start, never pushes without an explicit human flag, and is covered by 26 behavior tests pinning each safety shape; the only remaining issues are two header-comment omissions with no behavioral effect. ## Testing The configured full-suite baseline had already passed; I re-ran the two directly affected suites (26 upstream-sync assertions, 21 bootstrap assertions, all green) and then drove the script manually against purpose-built upstream/fork git repositories to capture an operator-level transcript proving the behind, current, ahead-only, diverged-STUCK, and inert-install outcomes, including a before/after ref-hash comparison showing a diverged fork's unlanded commit survives an explicit --push refusal. This is a shell CLI with no rendered surface, so the reviewer-visible evidence is a command transcript rather than a screenshot. Worktree left clean.
Evidence: Operator transcript: fm-upstream-sync across all five fork states plus bootstrap relay ### B. the fork is BEHIND upstream (the captain's actual case) $ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh firstmate: behind: fork is 2 commits behind upstream/main; run bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh --push to fast-forward it [exit 0] --- report only: nothing was moved --- fork.git main = a06eba4 local main = a06eba4 ### C. the operator explicitly asks to bring the fork forward $ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh --push firstmate: updated: fork fast-forwarded 2 commits to upstream/main [exit 0] --- the fork on the server actually advanced --- fork.git main = 58edea2 (upstream commit 3) upstream main = 58edea2 (upstream commit 3) ### D. a fork carrying its own work on top of a merged upstream firstmate: current [exit 0] ### E. a DIVERGED fork: 1 of its own commits, 2 missing from upstream $ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh firstmate: STUCK: fork has diverged from upstream/main, 1 ahead and 2 behind - needs attention, reconcile it by hand [exit 0] $ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh --push # even an explicit push refuses firstmate: STUCK: fork has diverged from upstream/main, 1 ahead and 2 behind - needs attention, reconcile it by hand [exit 1] --- the diverged fork was left completely untouched --- fork2.git main before = 7a4aadc fork2.git main after = 7a4aadc UNCHANGED - the unlanded fork commit survived ### F1. bootstrap on a BEHIND fork UPSTREAM_SYNC: firstmate: behind: fork is 2 commits behind upstream/main; run bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh --push to fast-forward it ### F2. bootstrap on a DIVERGED fork UPSTREAM_SYNC: firstmate: STUCK: fork has diverged from upstream/main, 1 ahead and 2 behind - needs attention, reconcile it by hand ### G. bootstrap on the non-forked install (no output - a non-forked install prints nothing) ```text ============================================================== fm-upstream-sync.sh - operator transcript upstream/main is 3 commits; the fork was left at commit 1 ============================================================== ### A. an ordinary install with no upstream remote ### the feature must be completely inert here $ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh firstmate: skipped: no upstream remote [exit 0] ### B. the fork is BEHIND upstream (the captain's actual case) $ git log --oneline origin/main..upstream/main # what the fork is missing 0baf60c upstream commit 3 ff8557c upstream commit 2 $ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh firstmate: behind: fork is 2 commits behind upstream/main; run bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh --push to fast-forward it [exit 0] --- report only: nothing was moved --- fork.git main = 9f9b1ee local main = 9f9b1ee ### C. the operator explicitly asks to bring the fork forward $ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh --push firstmate: updated: fork fast-forwarded 2 commits to upstream/main [exit 0] --- the fork on the server actually advanced --- fork.git main = 0baf60c (upstream commit 3) upstream main = 0baf60c (upstream commit 3) $ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh # re-run is clean firstmate: current [exit 0] ### D. a fork carrying its own work on top of a merged upstream ### ahead-only is the healthy resting state, not drift $ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh firstmate: current [exit 0] ### E. a DIVERGED fork: 1 of its own commits, 2 missing from upstream ### this is the case that must never be touched automatically $ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh firstmate: STUCK: fork has diverged from upstream/main, 1 ahead and 2 behind - needs attention, reconcile it by hand [exit 0] $ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh --push # even an explicit push refuses firstmate: STUCK: fork has diverged from upstream/main, 1 ahead and 2 behind - needs attention, reconcile it by hand [exit 1] --- the diverged fork was left completely untouched --- fork2.git main before = 2532e14 fork2.git main after = 2532e14 UNCHANGED - the unlanded fork commit survived fork commit still present: fork: unlanded work that must survive ============================================================== session-start bootstrap: what the captain actually sees ============================================================== ### F1. bootstrap on a BEHIND fork - the drift is surfaced $ bin/fm-bootstrap.sh (drift section) UPSTREAM_SYNC: firstmate: behind: fork is 2 commits behind upstream/main; run bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh --push to fast-forward it ### F2. bootstrap on a DIVERGED fork - the loud stuck line $ bin/fm-bootstrap.sh (drift section) UPSTREAM_SYNC: firstmate: STUCK: fork has diverged from upstream/main, 1 ahead and 2 behind - needs attention, reconcile it by hand ### G. bootstrap on the non-forked install - silent, zero behavior change $ bin/fm-bootstrap.sh (drift section) (no output - a non-forked install prints nothing) ```
Evidence: Reproducible demo script that generated the transcript ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # Manual end-to-end demo of the fork-vs-upstream drift mechanism. set -eu REPO="$1" LAB=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fm-fork-demo.XXXXXX") trap 'rm -rf "$LAB"' EXIT export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=demo GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=d@e export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=demo GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=d@e q() { git -C "$1" "${@:2}" >/dev/null 2>&1; } fmrun() { FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$1" bash "$REPO/bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh" "${@:2}" && echo " [exit 0]" || echo " [exit $?]"; } mkfork() { git clone -q "$LAB/fork.git" "$1" q "$1" remote add upstream "$LAB/upstream" q "$1" fetch upstream } # the upstream project (kunchenguid/firstmate stand-in) git init -q -b main "$LAB/upstream" for i in 1 2 3; do echo "upstream change $i" >>"$LAB/upstream/AGENTS.md" q "$LAB/upstream" add -A q "$LAB/upstream" commit -m "upstream commit $i" done # the captain's fork, forked from upstream at commit 1 BASE=$(git -C "$LAB/upstream" rev-parse HEAD~2) git init -q -b main --bare "$LAB/fork.git" q "$LAB/upstream" push "$LAB/fork.git" "$BASE:refs/heads/main" echo "==============================================================" echo " fm-upstream-sync.sh - operator transcript" echo " upstream/main is 3 commits; the fork was left at commit 1" echo "==============================================================" echo echo "### A. an ordinary install with no upstream remote" echo "### the feature must be completely inert here" git clone -q "$LAB/fork.git" "$LAB/plain" echo "\$ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh" fmrun "$LAB/plain" echo echo "### B. the fork is BEHIND upstream (the captain's actual case)" mkfork "$LAB/behind" echo "\$ git log --oneline origin/main..upstream/main # what the fork is missing" git -C "$LAB/behind" log --oneline origin/main..upstream/main | sed 's/^/ /' echo "\$ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh" fmrun "$LAB/behind" echo "--- report only: nothing was moved ---" echo " fork.git main = $(git -C "$LAB/fork.git" rev-parse --short main)" echo " local main = $(git -C "$LAB/behind" rev-parse --short main)" echo echo "### C. the operator explicitly asks to bring the fork forward" echo "\$ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh --push" fmrun "$LAB/behind" --push echo "--- the fork on the server actually advanced ---" echo " fork.git main = $(git -C "$LAB/fork.git" rev-parse --short main) ($(git -C "$LAB/fork.git" log -1 --format=%s main))" echo " upstream main = $(git -C "$LAB/upstream" rev-parse --short main) ($(git -C "$LAB/upstream" log -1 --format=%s main))" echo "\$ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh # re-run is clean" fmrun "$LAB/behind" echo echo "### D. a fork carrying its own work on top of a merged upstream" echo "### ahead-only is the healthy resting state, not drift" mkfork "$LAB/ahead" q "$LAB/ahead" merge --ff-only upstream/main echo "fork-only work" >>"$LAB/ahead/README.md" q "$LAB/ahead" add -A q "$LAB/ahead" commit -m "fork: the captain's own commit" q "$LAB/ahead" push origin main echo "\$ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh" fmrun "$LAB/ahead" echo echo "### E. a DIVERGED fork: 1 of its own commits, 2 missing from upstream" echo "### this is the case that must never be touched automatically" git init -q -b main --bare "$LAB/fork2.git" q "$LAB/upstream" push "$LAB/fork2.git" "$BASE:refs/heads/main" git clone -q "$LAB/fork2.git" "$LAB/div" q "$LAB/div" remote add upstream "$LAB/upstream" q "$LAB/div" fetch upstream echo "divergent fork work" >>"$LAB/div/README.md" q "$LAB/div" add -A q "$LAB/div" commit -m "fork: unlanded work that must survive" q "$LAB/div" push origin main FORK2_BEFORE=$(git -C "$LAB/fork2.git" rev-parse main) echo "\$ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh" fmrun "$LAB/div" echo "\$ bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh --push # even an explicit push refuses" fmrun "$LAB/div" --push FORK2_AFTER=$(git -C "$LAB/fork2.git" rev-parse main) echo "--- the diverged fork was left completely untouched ---" echo " fork2.git main before = ${FORK2_BEFORE:0:7}" echo " fork2.git main after = ${FORK2_AFTER:0:7}" if [ "$FORK2_BEFORE" = "$FORK2_AFTER" ]; then echo " UNCHANGED - the unlanded fork commit survived" else echo " CHANGED - THE FORK WAS REWRITTEN (this would be a bug)" fi echo " fork commit still present: $(git -C "$LAB/fork2.git" log -1 --format=%s main)" echo echo "==============================================================" echo " session-start bootstrap: what the captain actually sees" echo "==============================================================" echo echo "### F1. bootstrap on a BEHIND fork - the drift is surfaced" mkfork "$LAB/behind2" q "$LAB/behind2" push origin ":refs/heads/nothing" || true git -C "$LAB/fork.git" update-ref refs/heads/main "$BASE" echo "\$ bin/fm-bootstrap.sh (drift section)" FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$LAB/behind2" bash "$REPO/bin/fm-bootstrap.sh" 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^UPSTREAM_SYNC' | sed 's/^/ /' || true echo echo "### F2. bootstrap on a DIVERGED fork - the loud stuck line" echo "\$ bin/fm-bootstrap.sh (drift section)" FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$LAB/div" bash "$REPO/bin/fm-bootstrap.sh" 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^UPSTREAM_SYNC' | sed 's/^/ /' || true echo echo "### G. bootstrap on the non-forked install - silent, zero behavior change" echo "\$ bin/fm-bootstrap.sh (drift section)" out=$(FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$LAB/plain" bash "$REPO/bin/fm-bootstrap.sh" 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^UPSTREAM_SYNC' || true) if [ -z "$out" ]; then echo " (no output - a non-forked install prints nothing)" else printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed 's/^/ /' fi ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 2 infos - ⚠️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:105` - Ahead/behind is computed against the local remote-tracking ref origin/<default>, but the script only fetches `upstream`, never `origin`. If the fork's real default branch has moved since the last origin fetch, AHEAD reads 0 and a genuinely diverged fork is classified as 'strictly behind' -- defeating the STUCK path that is the feature's core safety guarantee. The subsequent --push is still safe (git rejects the non-fast-forward) but reports 'push rejected' instead of the accurate divergence report. The test fixtures mask this by calling `git -C clone fetch -q origin` by hand in advance_fork/advance_upstream. Add a `git -C "$FM_ROOT" fetch origin --quiet` (skip-on-failure, like the upstream fetch) before computing counts. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:173` - upstream_sync invokes fm-upstream-sync.sh synchronously with no timeout, while the adjacent fleet_sync deliberately runs its child in the background with fleet_sync_bootstrap_timeout and a kill path. A slow, hung, or credential-prompting upstream remote therefore blocks every session start indefinitely with stderr swallowed by 2>/dev/null, so the captain sees a silent hang rather than a diagnostic. Bound it with the same timeout pattern (or at minimum export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 / GIT_SSH_COMMAND with BatchMode for the fetch). - ⚠️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:134` - The default (non-push) path fast-forwards the LOCAL default branch to the upstream commit, leaving local main ahead of origin/main. bin/fm-update.sh:53 then calls ff_target with base_mode=origin, whose `merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main` check fails, so /updatefirstmate reports `firstmate: skipped: diverged from origin/main` until the fork is pushed. The new updatefirstmate SKILL.md text predicts it would report `already current` instead, which is wrong, and 'diverged' is alarming wording for a state the sweep itself created. The same advanced local commit also becomes the local-HEAD base propagated to secondmate homes, pushing upstream code into secondmates that the fork's origin does not yet have. Either drop the local fast-forward from the default path, or correct the skill text and teach ff_target's origin mode to treat 'ahead of origin' as current rather than diverged. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:54` - usage() runs `sed -n '2,34p' "$0"`, but the header block extends to line 40. `--help` therefore stops mid-comment and omits the entire output-vocabulary table (lines 33-38) and the `Usage: fm-upstream-sync.sh [--push] [--help]` line itself. Change the range to '2,40p'. - ℹ️ `AGENTS.md:132` - Section 3 still reads 'The five MUTATING sweeps - non-executing legacy PR-check migration, fleet sync, the local secondmate fast-forward sweep, the secondmate liveness sweep, and X-mode artifact writes'. bin/fm-bootstrap.sh's header was updated to six and now includes upstream_sync, which is lock-gated the same way. AGENTS.md is the always-loaded contract, so the stale count and list are the authoritative-looking ones. Add the upstream drift sweep and update the count. 🔧 Fix: make upstream drift sweep report-only and bound its fetch 4 issues (1 warning, 3 infos) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:162` - On the --push path the local fast-forward is run as `ff_target ... >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`, discarding both its output and its outcome, yet the very next line unconditionally prints `updated: fork fast-forwarded N commits`. ff_target skips on a dirty working tree, a detached HEAD, or a non-default current branch - and running --push while sitting on a feature branch is the likely case, since that is what an operator is usually doing. The report then claims a fast-forward that half happened: origin moved, the local default branch did not, and nothing says so. Because a subsequent default run compares origin against upstream (now level) and reports `current`, the stranded local branch stays invisible. Capture FF_STATUS and either append a qualifier to the updated line (e.g. `; local <default> not moved: <reason>`) or emit ff_target's own skip line, so the message matches what actually moved. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:205` - upstream_sync borrows fleet_sync_bootstrap_timeout, which is sized for the whole fleet (`5 + 3 * origin-backed project count`, floor 20s). The drift check is a single repo doing two fetches, so on a 20-project home it is granted 65 seconds. It also runs serially before fleet_sync, so a home with both a hung upstream and a hung project remote now stalls session start for the sum of the two budgets rather than one. Reusing the helper is the right call over a second convention, but a smaller fixed ceiling for this sweep (or min(timeout, 20)) would keep the worst case closer to what it was. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:59` - `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="${GIT_SSH_COMMAND:-ssh -o BatchMode=yes}"` only applies BatchMode when the operator has no GIT_SSH_COMMAND of their own. An operator who sets one (common for custom identity files or ProxyCommand) loses the non-interactive guarantee, so an unauthenticated SSH remote can still sit on a passphrase prompt until the bootstrap timeout kills it. GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 does not cover the ssh-side prompt. Appending `-o BatchMode=yes` to an existing value rather than only defaulting would make the guard unconditional. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:140` - `--push` on a diverged fork prints STUCK and exits 0 (line 141), while `--push` whose push git rejects prints STUCK and exits 1 (line 160). Both are refusals to advance the fork, so a caller or wrapper script cannot distinguish refusal from success on the first one. Bootstrap parses output rather than status so nothing is broken today, but the asymmetry is a trap for any future non-interactive caller. 🔧 Fix: report honest partial push and bound upstream sync refusals 4 issues (3 warnings, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:68` - `export GIT_SSH_COMMAND="${GIT_SSH_COMMAND:-ssh} -o BatchMode=yes"` is documented (lines 63-66) as guaranteeing non-interactive ssh even for an operator who supplies their own GIT_SSH_COMMAND, on the stated premise that "a later -o wins over an earlier one". That premise is backwards: ssh uses the FIRST obtained value for each parameter (ssh_config(5)), and command-line -o options are processed in order. So an operator whose GIT_SSH_COMMAND already contains `-o BatchMode=no` (or a wrapper that injects it) keeps the interactive behavior, and the appended option is ignored. The append still helps when BatchMode is otherwise unset, so the code is not useless - but the comment asserts a guarantee the mechanism does not provide, and the whole point of the timeout/BatchMode work was that a credential-prompting remote must never hang session start. Either correct the comment to say this only sets a default when the operator has not set BatchMode themselves, or insert the option immediately after the program word so it is obtained first. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:67` - GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and BatchMode are exported unconditionally, so they also apply to the deliberate, human-invoked `--push` run, not just the silent session-start sweep they were added for. An operator without ssh-agent (or with a passphrase-protected key, or an https remote needing a credential prompt) can no longer authenticate. The failure surfaces as `firstmate: STUCK: fast-forward push to origin/<default> was rejected - needs attention` (line 173), which reads as a divergence/branch problem rather than an auth problem; on the fetch side (lines 103-114) it surfaces as `skipped: cannot fetch upstream` with git's stderr discarded by `2>/dev/null`, so a human running the command by hand gets no diagnostic at all. Consider scoping the non-interactive guard to the report-only path (or to an explicit sweep flag bootstrap passes), and surfacing fetch stderr when the run was invoked interactively. - ⚠️ `.agents/skills/bootstrap-diagnostics/SKILL.md:37` - The new diagnostic entry tells the reading agent to "run the `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh --push` command named in the line", and updatefirstmate/SKILL.md:34 likewise says to "bring the fork forward with `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh --push` first and then run this updater". That command pushes directly to the shared firstmate repo's default branch on origin - an outward-facing write that bypasses the PR path AGENTS.md section 1 requires for shared tracked material, and one both the script header and this same bullet describe as a human operation that must never be automatic. As written, an agent handling a routine session-start diagnostic would perform it without captain approval. If the intent is that only the captain runs --push, say so explicitly in both places (report the drift and the command, do not run it); if an agent may run it under a yolo posture, state that condition. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:213` - When the bounded drift check times out, upstream_sync deletes its output and returns silently, on the reasoning that a skip is never actionable. But unlike the other skips (no upstream remote, not a repo), a timeout costs real wall-clock: with the cap at line 210 an unreachable or hanging upstream adds up to 20 seconds to every single session start, forever, with nothing printed to explain the delay. That is a recurring, fixable condition the captain would want to know about, and it is invisible under the current rule. Consider relaying a timeout as a distinct one-line note (or at minimum a BOOTSTRAP_INFO fact) rather than folding it into the silent-skip class. 🔧 Fix: scope non-interactive git to unattended sweep and relay timeouts 3 issues (2 warnings, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:227` - The new push-failure classifier matches git's human-readable output (`[rejected]`, `non-fast-forward`, `fetch first`, `stale info`) to decide between a loud STUCK and a benign "cannot push to origin (network or credentials)" skip. Those strings are translated by git's i18n (transport.c emits `_("[rejected]")`, and the "Updates were rejected..." hints are likewise localized). On a machine with a non-English git locale a genuine non-fast-forward rejection - the precise condition the STUCK line exists to surface loudly - falls into the default arm and is reported as a network/credentials skip, inverting the safety signal. This repo already has a known locale-sensitivity class of bug in bin/. Pin the invocation with LC_ALL=C (git's own scripts do this when parsing output), or push with --porcelain and match its stable machine-readable status tokens instead of prose. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:163` - The header's exit-status contract was rewritten this round to promise that `--push` exits 1 "whenever it was asked to advance the fork and did not, whether because the fork diverged, the push was rejected, or origin could not be reached" (line 57). But both fetches use `fetch_remote <remote> || exit 0`, so a `--push` run whose origin or upstream fetch fails exits 0 while printing a skip line. The stated purpose of that contract is that "a scripted caller can tell a refusal from a success without parsing the output" - and this is exactly the case where it cannot. Either make the fetch-failure exit depend on PUSH (exit 1 when PUSH=yes, as the diverged and rejected paths already do), or narrow the header sentence to the two refusals the code actually signals. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:109` - `read -r ssh_prog ssh_rest <<<"$GIT_SSH_COMMAND"` treats the first whitespace-delimited token as the program word so `-o BatchMode=yes` can be prepended. Git shell-parses GIT_SSH_COMMAND, so a quoted or space-containing program path is legitimate (e.g. `"/Applications/My Tools/ssh" -F cfg`). That splits into ssh_prog=`"/Applications/My` and the reassembled command is unrunnable, so the unattended sweep fails and reports `cannot reach upstream (network or credentials)` with no hint the script mangled the command. Option arguments containing spaces are unaffected - only the program word. Guard the split (skip the rewrite when the value starts with a quote, and fall back to the previous append form) so a misparse can never silently disable the drift check. 🔧 Fix: classify push refusals from refs and fix refusal exit codes 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:50` - The header states STUCK is reserved for branch-shaped problems and that "a remote that could not be reached or authenticated is NOT stuck - nothing about the branches is wrong - so it reports as a skip naming credentials or the network." The classifier at lines 265-274 discriminates purely on whether a follow-up fetch of origin succeeds. On a public fork, fetch is anonymous while push requires a write token, so the most common auth failure (expired/missing token, read-only PAT, SSH key without write access) fetches successfully, finds origin/<default> still an ancestor of UPSTREAM_REV, and falls into the else arm printing "STUCK: origin refused the fast-forward push to origin/<default> - needs attention, see the error below". That directly contradicts the header promise, and it is the common shape of the failure, not an edge case. The loud-on-ambiguity behavior is the deliberate design and the relayed git error does surface the real cause, so the fix is to narrow the header: only an UNREACHABLE origin is the benign credentials/network skip, and a reachable origin that refuses the push is reported loudly regardless of whether the cause turns out to be branches or credentials. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:148` - The --sweep non-interactive block (lines 148-155), including prepend_ssh_batchmode's `eval "parts=($GIT_SSH_COMMAND)"`, runs before the cheap guards at lines 168-179 that exit early on a non-repo or a single-remote install. On the very installs the feature is documented to be completely inert for, every session start still evaluates the operator's GIT_SSH_COMMAND under eval - executing any embedded command substitution, and applying pathname and tilde expansion to a value the script then discards - before printing "skipped: no upstream remote" and exiting. Git would only have run that command on an actual connection, which never happens on this path. Move the SWEEP setup block to just before the first fetch_remote call (after the remote and default-branch checks) so the rewrite only happens on runs that will really contact a remote. 🔧 Fix: classify unauthorized push as credentials, not divergence 3 issues (1 warning, 2 infos) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:285` - After a rejected push the classifier only asks whether origin/<default> is still an ancestor of UPSTREAM_REV. If origin has moved to a DESCENDANT of UPSTREAM_REV - someone used GitHub's "Sync fork" button, or a second machine ran --push concurrently - the ancestor test fails and the run prints "STUCK: origin/<default> moved and no longer fast-forwards to upstream/<default> - needs attention, reconcile it by hand" and exits 1. But the fork is already at or past the commit we tried to push; there is nothing to reconcile, and an immediate re-run would report "current". That is a false alarm on the exact workflow this feature supports, and it fires the one loud signal the script exists to raise. Before the ancestor test, check whether UPSTREAM_REV is an ancestor of NEW_ORIGIN_REV and treat that as an already-advanced no-op (report current/updated, exit 0) rather than a divergence. No test covers this shape today. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:219` - bootstrap_run_bounded launches the child and then enters `while jobs -r -p | grep -qx "$pid"; do ... sleep 1; done`, so the first re-check happens a full second after launch regardless of how fast the child exits. fm-upstream-sync.sh on a single-remote install exits in milliseconds with a silent "no upstream remote" skip, yet session start still burns that second, every time, on top of the second fleet_sync already costs. Both the script header ("inert for everyone who has not forked") and the bootstrap-diagnostics skill ("a single-remote install never prints an UPSTREAM_SYNC line") present this path as free. Gate the spawn on a cheap `git -C "$FM_ROOT" remote get-url upstream` in upstream_sync so a non-forked home never forks the child at all, or give the poll loop a sub-second first tick. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:241` - The header documents --push as "fast-forward the FORK by pushing the upstream commit to origin, then fast-forward the local default branch to match". When BEHIND is 0 the run exits at line 243 with "current" before reaching either step, so a fork that is already level with upstream but whose LOCAL default branch is behind origin (the ordinary state of a checkout that has not pulled) gets no local fast-forward despite the header promising one. The behavior is defensible - /updatefirstmate owns the local pull - but the header sentence should say the local fast-forward happens only on a run that actually advanced the fork. 🔧 Fix: treat an already-advanced fork as current, not stuck 2 infos still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:13` - The file header's canonical "Lines:" contract lists only "UPSTREAM_SYNC: firstmate: behind|STUCK: <detail>", but upstream_sync also relays "UPSTREAM_SYNC: firstmate: skipped: drift check timed out after <N>s" (bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:231). That list is the authoritative enumeration of every line bootstrap can print, and the bootstrap-diagnostics skill documents the timeout entry, so the header is the one place now out of sync. Extend the entry to cover the skipped/timeout form. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:48` - The output-vocabulary table documents `"firstmate: current" fork already matches upstream`, but the origin-moved-ahead branch (bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh:299) emits the detailed variant "firstmate: current: origin/<default> already contains <upstream ref>; the fork was advanced elsewhere". The narrative at lines 72-76 describes that case correctly; only the vocabulary table, which a reader scans as the complete line shapes, was not widened. Note the optional `: <detail>` suffix on the current entry.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"` - `bash tests/fm-upstream-sync.test.sh` — 26 assertions, all ok - `bash tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` — 21 assertions, all ok (slow suite, run with extended timeout) - Manual end-to-end demo against real git fixtures: `FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE=<fork> bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh` for the no-upstream-remote, behind, current, and ahead-only cases - `FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE=<behind-fork> bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh --push` — verified the fork's server ref actually advanced to upstream's tip - `FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE=<diverged-fork> bin/fm-upstream-sync.sh --push` — verified exit 1 and that the fork ref hash and its unlanded commit were unchanged - `FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE=<repo> bin/fm-bootstrap.sh | grep UPSTREAM_SYNC` — confirmed the behind and STUCK relay lines, and silence on a non-forked install - `git status --porcelain` — worktree clean, no transient artifacts left behind
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: feat(herdr): add supervisor-grouped crew workspaces
body:
## Intent

Reconcile and re-validate PR #751 after merging current origin/main 4ab61fa7, including merged PR #747, into fm/fm-herdr-contiguity-resume. Ship the captain-authorized default-off interim Herdr visual hierarchy where every ordinary crewmate or scout runs in its own Herdr workspace grouped under its supervisor workspace, with depth-first workspace contiguity as secondary display maintenance. Treehouse remains the sole worktree lifecycle owner; Herdr worktree.remove is prohibited for Treehouse-owned worktrees; every marked supervisor parent workspace is guarded from close. Grouping is cosmetic: if herdr-child-workspaces propagation fails, secondmate launch must remain functional and proceed with one clear warning that grouping did not converge, unless the failure implies a distinct functional or safety risk. Re-validate the combined state specifically because #751 modified shared tests/wake-helpers.sh used by #747's wake-drain tests. Preserve protocol, unit, recovery, teardown, and named non-default Herdr lab E2E coverage. Update the existing PR #751, stop at green CI, and do not merge.

## What Changed

- Add a default-off Herdr mode that gives ordinary crewmates and scouts dedicated workspaces associated with their supervisor workspace, including recovery and config propagation.
- Maintain depth-first supervisor contiguity through a typed workspace-move adapter and manual regroup command, while preserving focus and unmanaged workspace order.
- Harden concurrent workspace creation, Treehouse lease journaling, respawn, and pane-only teardown with ownership-safe recovery, documentation, and expanded unit and E2E coverage.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The stale-template path now requires matching task, holder, binding, lease identity, and Treehouse return state before cleanup, while mismatches remain fail-safe.

## Testing

The provided full-suite baseline and all five focused checks passed; isolated real-Herdr labs exercised grouping, contiguity, recovery, Treehouse-safe pane-only teardown, supervisor protection, default-session tripwires, and blocked-transition wake enqueueing, while behavioral tests confirmed one-warning nonblocking secondmate fallback and readable atomic metadata.

<summary>Evidence: Real Herdr child-workspace lifecycle</summary>

```text

ok - flag ON: delegated job gets its own child workspace 'firstmate/cma' with runtime+log tabs; parent recorded in meta and preserved
ok - respawn: restored child husk is replaced in its exact owned workspace without duplicates
ok - flag ON: a second concurrent job gets its own distinct child workspace under the same parent
ok - nested homes: the supervisor stays a tab in its own workspace and inherits the primary grouping opt-in
ok - nested homes: a job delegated by the secondmate gets a child workspace under the secondmate's own workspace
ok - recovery: list_live rediscovers child-workspace jobs by label, scoped per home, without surfacing log tabs
ok - safety: close_owned_workspace refuses parent and stale workspace targets
ok - pane-only cleanup: teardown removed cma's endpoint while every workspace and supervisor survived
ok - pane-only cleanup: same task id reclaims one preserved workspace without accumulation
🌳 Setting up worktree...
🌳 Leased worktree at ~/.treehouse/proj2-cd6097/1/proj2. Run 'treehouse return ~/.treehouse/proj2-cd6097/1/proj2' to release it.
ok - pane-only cleanup: partial return retries once and a reassigned lease remains untouched
ok - pane-only cleanup: owned child workspaces remain for deferred cleanup
ok - the default Herdr session matches the helper's byte-identical fleet-state tripwire
# all interim child-workspace E2E assertions passed
```
</details>
<details>
<summary>Evidence: Real Herdr contiguity and teardown</summary>

```text
ok - real herdr (0.7.4, protocol 16): workspace.move insert_index addresses the PRE-removal array (leftward lands AT it, rightward lands one before it, length is valid)
ok - canonical render: supervisor, then its DIRECT crews (release-notes pulled up by a real socket move), then the secondmate and its crews - direct crews before the secondmate subtree
ok - focus preserved: spawns and reconcile moves never changed the focused workspace
ok - teardown: pane-only cleanup retains one reclaimable workspace and reconciles every surviving owned block
ok - non-destructive: a real workspace.move keeps the workspace's tabs, panes, and registered agent state untouched
ok - regroup: bin/fm-herdr-regroup.sh repairs manual drift with exactly one move, agent untouched
ok - idempotence: regrouping an already-correct live order issues zero moves (no churn)
ok - unrelated preservation: the manual workspace kept its position, and no move or regroup changed focus
ok - the default Herdr session matches the helper's byte-identical fleet-state tripwire
# all workspace-contiguity E2E assertions passed
```
</details>
<details>
<summary>Evidence: Real Herdr blocked-transition wake</summary>

```text

ok - real herdr (herdr 0.7.4): a driven idle->blocked transition returns the blocked record in 0.057s (pane w1:p2)
ok - real herdr: the watcher fast-path enqueues a stale wake naming the task window from the live blocked transition
```
</details>
<details>
<summary>Evidence: Secondmate grouping fallback</summary>

```text

ok - C1 fm-harness.sh secondmate-model/secondmate-effort resolve the optional tokens; bare harness stays empty (backward-compat)

ok - B2 spawn: secondmate runs the secondmate harness; its home inherits declared config

ok - B10 bootstrap sweep with no inherited config is a config no-op and still fast-forwards
```
