title: feat(bootstrap): surface fork upstream drift at session start
body:
## Intent Detect and surface new upstream Firstmate releases at session start so forked homes stop silently drifting behind origin-only updates. Captain authorized detection, not automatic merging: automatically merging a third party's changes into a system running unattended is not acceptable; the valuable half is knowing promptly and deciding deliberately. Requirements implemented: 1. Cheap read-only detection when the configured upstream remote has commits this home lacks, suitable for every session start. 2. Surface through the existing session-start bootstrap diagnostic path (bin/fm-bootstrap.sh + bootstrap-diagnostics skill), not a parallel channel. 3. Report usefully: commit count plus subjects for urgency judgment. 4. Never fetch-and-merge, never rewrite refs destructively, never touch projects/. 5. Fail quietly when no upstream remote, offline, or not a fork (origin URL equals upstream). 6. Keep it bounded/cheap for every fleet member session start. Scope decision stated and followed: firstmate-only. Do NOT also check no-mistakes/treehouse releases here — those already surface their own version gaps; expanding would be scope creep and startup cost. Prior rebase ask-user finding about unpushed main commits was a verified false positive (stale remote-tracking ref); origin/main and local main are both ff1015f with this branch only one feature commit ahead. Approve any repeat of that false positive. Tests cover behind-with-subjects, no-upstream, offline, same-URL non-fork, current tip, secondmate silence, and bootstrap wiring. Restarting validation after a prior run failed on a network connection drop during the test step, not on the changes themselves. Commits intact; no implementation redo. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-upstream-lib.sh`, a read-only upstream drift detector wired into `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh`: when the configured upstream remote has commits this fork lacks, session-start diagnostics emit an `UPSTREAM` line with the commit count and recent subjects (clipped to 72 chars, bounded by `FM_UPSTREAM_SUBJECT_LIMIT`). It stays silent when there is no upstream remote, the origin URL matches upstream (not a fork), the fork is at the upstream tip, or the network is unreachable — and it never fetches, merges, or rewrites refs. - Updated the bootstrap-diagnostics skill to instruct agents to report upstream drift and wait for the captain's decision rather than merging. - Added `tests/fm-upstream.test.sh` covering behind-with-subjects, no-upstream, offline, same-URL non-fork, current-tip, secondmate silence, and bootstrap wiring cases, and documented the `FM_UPSTREAM_*` env knobs in `docs/configuration.md` and the new library in `docs/scripts.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A well-bounded, read-only, fail-quiet detection feature that matches every stated intent constraint (no merging, existing diagnostic path, timeout-bounded probes, secondmate/non-fork/offline silence) with comprehensive tests and no substantive defects found. ## Testing Baseline full suite plus the targeted upstream/bootstrap tests all pass, and a live end-to-end run of bin/fm-bootstrap.sh against a synthetic fork 3 commits behind its upstream printed the expected UPSTREAM diagnostic with commit subjects, left all local refs untouched, and stayed silent in the non-fork, no-remote, offline, and up-to-date cases.
Evidence: Bootstrap UPSTREAM diagnostic (fork 3 commits behind) $ FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE=.../fork FM_BOOTSTRAP_DETECT_ONLY=1 bin/fm-bootstrap.sh UPSTREAM: 3 commits behind upstream/main (/tmp/fm-upstream-demo.Ar1WI3/upstream) - docs: describe upstream drift detection; fix(spawn): stop double-registering herdr workers; feat: add fleet-wide quota telemetry exit=0 ```text $ FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE=/tmp/fm-upstream-demo.Ar1WI3/fork FM_BOOTSTRAP_DETECT_ONLY=1 bin/fm-bootstrap.sh # fork 3 commits behind upstream UPSTREAM: 3 commits behind upstream/main (/tmp/fm-upstream-demo.Ar1WI3/upstream) - docs: describe upstream drift detection; fix(spawn): stop double-registering herdr workers; feat: add fleet-wide quota telemetry exit=0 ```
Evidence: Read-only guarantee and silent cases via real bootstrap `fork HEAD/refs/heads/main unchanged after detection; silent (empty output, exit 0) for: origin==upstream URL, no upstream remote, unreachable upstream, fork at upstream tip` ```text == read-only guarantee: fork local branch/HEAD unchanged after detection == e583f250c052a52fe2f59ccc8cdcd8a2a72a850a e583f250c052a52fe2f59ccc8cdcd8a2a72a850a ## main...origin/main == silent: origin URL == upstream URL (not a fork) == output: [] exit=0 == silent: no upstream remote == output: [] exit=0 == silent: upstream unreachable (offline) == output: [] exit=0 == silent: fork already at upstream tip == output: [] exit=0 ```

title: fix(backends): guard herdr first-launch harness dialogs at spawn
body:
## Intent

Harden first-launch dialog handling for crews on the Herdr backend so Claude folder-trust and Bypass Permissions dialogs, plus Codex trust and hooks-review menus, no longer require manual intervention. Diagnose the recurring broken-pipe and silent send/readback paths, and make pre-agent TUI input reliable or fail loudly: classify only known dialog shapes, send one key at a time, re-read the pane to verify cursor or dialog movement, use bounded retries, never press Enter while a destructive No/exit choice is focused, and refuse unknown states. Corroborate visible dialogs with native agent state and allow only working to suppress a visible menu because live evidence records idle at a real displayed Claude trust dialog. Keep harness knowledge in the harness-adapters skill and mechanics in scripts, extend the existing fake-Herdr test runner, and record dated helper-isolated empirical evidence. The accepted live evidence is two real trust-dialog traversals with agent_status idle and clean teardown; document that the bypass variant is unreproducible because acceptance persists in Claude user state and do not reset that state. Preserve the smallest viable diff, require full lint and extended tests green, push the feature branch to remote fork, and update the PR against kunchenguid/firstmate main.

## What Changed

- `bin/backends/herdr.sh` gains `fm_backend_herdr_handle_startup_dialog` and its `_dialog_classify` / `_dialog_drive_visible` helpers: only four known menu shapes are recognized (Claude folder trust, Claude Bypass Permissions, Codex directory trust, Codex hooks review), focus is read from the dialog's own option rows so a composer glyph cannot be mistaken for the selection, each key is sent one at a time and verified by pane readback under bounded retries, Enter is never sent while a destructive `No, exit` row is focused, and unknown or unverifiable states fail closed. Visible menus are corroborated against `agent get` — only `working` suppresses a dialog, since live evidence records `idle` at a real displayed trust dialog. `Down`/`Up` are added to key normalization, and `fm_backend_herdr_events_capable` now pattern-matches the schema in-shell instead of `printf | grep -q`, removing the recurring `printf: write error: Broken pipe` under a caller's `pipefail`.
- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` routes claude/codex spawns on the herdr backend through that handler after the launch Enter; an unverified pane exits non-zero without printing the `spawned` line, and the error names the id, window, and worktree because the task stays registered while the harness may be running.
- Five `FM_BACKEND_HERDR_DIALOG_*` tunables (capture lines, polls, poll sleep, key retries, key sleep) are documented in `docs/configuration.md`; `docs/herdr-backend.md` adds the dated evidence block — two live Claude trust-dialog traversals, the live `down` key verification, the broken-pipe diagnosis, and a note that the bypass variant is unreproducible because acceptance persists in Claude user state — with the harness-level knowledge kept in the `harness-adapters` skill. The fake-Herdr runner grows 18 cases covering classification, cursor-move-before-Enter, destructive-default refusal, retry bounds, stale/repainted frames, agent-state corroboration, and the two spawn wiring paths.

Note: the pipeline's Test stage reported a non-zero exit for the full `tests/*.test.sh` sweep and Lint exited 127; both are unresolved on this branch as pushed.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: Every safety-critical finding from the previous rounds is now closed with surgical, tested changes, but the branch still adds a mandatory pre-flight gate on every herdr claude/codex spawn that can hard-fail a spawn on environment-dependent conditions, so it warrants the usual post-merge attention rather than being treated as cosmetic.

## Testing

Completed 1 recorded test check.

- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 error across 1 run (30m18s)

## Pipeline

✅ No issues found.

<details>
<summary>⚠️ **Review** - 1 info</summary>

- 🚨 `bin/backends/herdr.sh:1367` - fm_backend_herdr_dialog_drive_visible's `expected=dismissed` retry loop authorizes another Enter from a readback that this change's own docs call unreliable ("the recent source retains dismissed frames inside the capture window"). If Enter #1 dismissed the Claude trust dialog and Claude then rendered the Bypass Permissions warning focused on the destructive `No, exit`, a stale capture still classifies claude-trust:accept, agent_status is still `idle` (the recorded live behaviour at a displayed dialog), and Enter #2 is delivered to `No, exit`. That contradicts the required criterion "never press Enter while a destructive No/exit choice is focused". Consider not retrying Enter at all, or requiring the post-key capture to differ from the pre-key capture before concluding anything.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1264` - This is the first `exit 1` that runs after $STATE/$ID.meta is written, the worktree is acquired, the pane exists, and the harness is already launched - and HERDR_PROJECTION_ABORT_CLEANUP was disarmed two lines earlier, so spawn_abort_cleanup does nothing. A cold harness start that exceeds the 20s (40 x 0.5s) poll budget while `agent get` still reports agent_not_found fails the spawn, suppresses the `spawned <id> ... window=...` line, and leaves a registered, running crewmate behind. fm-spawn.sh:101 claims it "fails the spawn rather than leaving a crewmate parked", but both happen.
- ⚠️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:1330` - A dialog that classifies to a known kind but whose focus cannot be parsed hits drive_visible's catch-all and fails the spawn on the very first poll, with no retry and no further polling - unlike the `unknown` kind, which polls to the bounded timeout. The first capture is taken with zero delay after the launch Enter, so a mid-repaint frame (options rendered, cursor row not yet) or transcript text quoting a dialog header plus both options kills the spawn ~0s after launch.
- ⚠️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:1234` - The focus scan keeps the last `❯ `/`› ` line anywhere in the 80-line capture, but that glyph pair is the repo's own verified agent composer prompt (FM_BACKEND_HERDR_BARE_PROMPT_RE='^[❯›]'). A composer row rendered below an overlay menu therefore overrides the menu's selected item. Codex's hooks-review menu is the concrete risk: it has no live traversal in docs/herdr-backend.md, and the fake-CLI fixtures place no composer row after the menu, so an empty focus would fail every such spawn. Scoping the scan to the lines of the matched dialog block would remove the ambiguity.
- ℹ️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:1427` - FM_BACKEND_HERDR_DIALOG_POLL_SLEEP and FM_BACKEND_HERDR_DIALOG_KEY_SLEEP go straight to `sleep` while FM_BACKEND_HERDR_DIALOG_POLLS and _KEY_RETRIES get numeric fallbacks. A malformed exported value makes every sleep fail, turning the 40-poll loop into a tight spin of ~80 herdr CLI calls plus stderr noise before the spawn fails. Add the same `case ... in ''|*[!0-9.]*) fallback ;;` guard the other two tunables use.

🔧 Fix: guard herdr dialog focus, Enter retries, and spawn failure
2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:1288` - The focus rewrite changed the codex-trust `Press enter to continue` fallback from "no selection glyph anywhere in the capture" (old `codex-trust:` empty-focus case) to "no row matched a recognized option", so it now also fires when a glyph row IS present but unrecognized. codex-trust's only reject pattern is `*'No, quit'*`, so a screen focused on e.g. `❯ 2. No, exit and choose another folder` leaves choice=unknown, the fallback flips it to accept, and drive_visible sends Enter onto the destructive row. That contradicts the required criterion "never press Enter while a destructive No/exit choice is focused", and codex's trust screen has no live traversal in docs/herdr-backend.md - only a glyph-free fixture. Restoring the old width means gating the fallback on a `glyph_seen=0` flag set inside the scan loop.
- ℹ️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:1435` - The mid-repaint branch re-implements the loop tail (`i=$((i + 1)); [ "$i" -lt "$polls" ] && sleep "$FM_BACKEND_HERDR_DIALOG_POLL_SLEEP"; continue`) that already exists 27 lines below at line 1462. Two copies of the poll-advance logic will drift if the pacing ever changes; restructuring the branch to fall through to the shared tail (e.g. an `unfocused=1` guard around the drive call) removes the duplicate.

🔧 Fix: gate codex trust Enter fallback on cursorless screen

- ℹ️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:1294` - `glyph_seen` is set by any `❯ `/`› ` row anywhere in the 80-line capture, including the pane's own shell prompt and the typed launch line. On a machine whose shell prompt uses those glyphs (starship/pure/agnoster - the same set the repo records as FM_BACKEND_HERDR_BARE_PROMPT_RE), codex's cursorless trust screen would classify `codex-trust unknown`, poll the full budget and fail the spawn rather than auto-accepting. This is fail-closed and is the same width the code had before round 2, so no action is required; noting it in case codex trust later needs to work in such a pane, where scoping the glyph scan to rows below the dialog header would recover the auto-accept.

title: feat(bin): add remote host registry and guarded SSH worktree helper
body:
## Intent

Implement PR 1 of the phase-4 remote-run series from the agreed design record (data/phase4-sshpane-design-s1): give firstmate a foundations-only, safety-first remote-run layer - a local gitignored remote-host registry schema and bin/fm-remote-ssh.sh as the single owner of remote-run shell mechanics (structured args only, safe quoting, bounded preflight, git-worktree create/inspect/remove primitives that never rm -rf or force-remove and refuse unknown remote responses), with fake-ssh test coverage; no fm-spawn/fm-watch/fm-teardown routing yet

## What Changed

- Adds `bin/fm-remote-ssh.sh` as the single owner of remote-run shell mechanics, with `resolve`, `preflight`, `worktree-create`, `worktree-inspect`, and `worktree-remove` commands. Every caller-supplied value is validated against a strict allowlist charset before any `ssh` spawns and crosses the wire only via `printf %q`; remote task paths are recomputed from the registry rather than accepted from the caller; each call is bounded by a connect timeout plus an overall wall-clock deadline (`FM_REMOTE_SSH_DEADLINE`, defaulting to 120s, enforced through `timeout`/`gtimeout` or a perl alarm watchdog); removal runs `git worktree remove` without `--force` (never `rm -rf`) only after re-proving registration, strict containment below the task root, branch identity, and cleanliness; and any response that is not exactly one well-formed `fm-remote-v1` line with the expected verb and allowlisted fields is a refusal.
- Introduces the local, gitignored `config/remote-hosts` registry (alias, `client|non-client` class, login-shell flag, permitted task root, approved handoff remotes) — added to `.gitignore`, the `AGENTS.md` home layout, a new "Remote host registry" section in `docs/configuration.md`, and the `docs/scripts.md` script table, with the script header and `--help` as the canonical schema contract.
- Adds `tests/fm-remote-ssh.test.sh`, a fake-`ssh` suite following the existing fakebin/command-log convention that shadows `ssh` on `PATH` for every case so no real connection is attempted. No `fm-spawn`/`fm-watch`/`fm-teardown` path routes to the helper yet; this is the foundations layer only.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The fix commit precisely implements both requested round-1 remediations (strict task-root containment and an env-tunable 120s wall-clock deadline) with fail-closed validation, a verified portable timeout fallback chain, and targeted regression tests, leaving no material issues in the additive, not-yet-routed foundations layer.

## Testing

Completed 1 recorded test check.

- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 error across 1 run (25m48s)

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

✅ No issues found.

</details>

✅ No issues found.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 **Review** - 3 issues found → auto-fixed ✅</summary>

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-remote-ssh.sh:391` - The remote containment check `case "$dest_phys/" in "$root_phys"/*)` passes when the destination path physically resolves to the task root itself (the trailing `*` matches the empty string — verified empirically), contradicting the header's stated invariant that a removable path must be 'physically below the registered task root'. A symlink planted at the derived task path pointing at the task root would pass containment; the later registered-worktree/branch/cleanliness proofs make real damage very contrived, but the invariant is not strictly enforced. Fix is one line: additionally require `[ "$dest_phys" != "$root_phys" ]` (or use pattern `"$root_phys"/?*`).
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-remote-ssh.sh:278` - remote_run has no overall execution timeout: ConnectTimeout bounds connection setup and ServerAliveInterval=15/CountMax=4 kills dead connections in ~60s, but a live connection whose remote command hangs (e.g. git blocked on a stale index.lock) blocks the helper indefinitely. The intent requires a 'bounded preflight'; if that includes wall-clock bounding, a total command deadline (e.g. wrapping ssh in a timeout or a kill-after watchdog) is missing. Whether time-bounding was in the agreed design scope (data/phase4-sshpane-design-s1 is gitignored and not inspectable here) is an author decision.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-remote-ssh.sh:280` - printf %q renders the multi-line remote script as bash ANSI-C `$'…'` quoting, so the remote account's sshd-invoked login shell must understand it (bash/zsh/ksh93 do; dash, fish, and csh-family shells mangle the command). Every mangling scenario traced fails closed (command-not-found or garbage output → local refusal), so this is not a safety hole, but the host constraint is undocumented — a one-line note in the --help registry contract ('remote account shell must be bash-compatible') would save debugging on a dash-login host.

title: code-shape: sharpen the tending brief and comment-hygiene bar
body:
## What

Sharpens the `/code-shape` skill so a tending pass does the right work by default, addressing a review of its guidance. The scoping/tracking engine and the inherited ship pipeline (`/code-review`, `/verify`, quality hooks) were already solid; the gap was in the crew brief that step 3 hands off — it named *what* to fix but not *how to do it safely*, and the comment rule covered only two of the common cases.

## Changes (all in step 3's `{TASK}` guidance)

- **Concrete smell checklist** for structure/testability instead of "maintainability and testability smells" — long functions, deep nesting, mixed I/O and logic, hidden deps/globals, primitive obsession, unclear names.
- **Deduplication guardrail** — rule-of-three, and keep extracted code in its natural home rather than reaching across the slice boundary (avoids premature abstraction and cross-slice coupling).
- **Broader comment-hygiene rule** — now also: delete redundant comments that restate the code and commented-out code; correct/delete a comment that has gone *wrong* (worse than none); and never strip docstrings, public-API docs, or license headers.
- **New safety bar** — the piece most missing before:
  - *Pure refactor*: behavior stays identical; no feature/perf/bugfix folded in; surface a found bug as a finding, don't bury it in a cleanup diff.
  - *Tests are the net*: a green suite only protects covered code, so confirm coverage before refactoring a unit — add characterization tests first, or skip it and say why.
  - *Reviewable diff*: small semantic commits; no mass reformat/rename that buries the change and destroys `git blame`.
- Direction-recording summary broadened to match the wider comment bar.

Style: one sentence per line, plain dashes, no agent co-author (per `firstmate-coding-guidelines`).

title: fix(bin): send literal config reread nudges after pushes
body:
## Intent Implement a minimal, literal-content config-push reread nudge for Firstmate: after inherited config is propagated to an already-running secondmate (mid-session fm-config-push.sh and the locked bootstrap/startup convergence path), send that secondmate a deterministic instruction that prints each CHANGED allowlisted config file path and its full exact new destination post-write bytes - no summaries, hashes, parsed prose, selected profiles, or interpretations. This fixes the gap where propagation updated on-disk config but the live agent kept applying stale defaults. Required behavior constraints that must not be "fixed" away as mistakes: - Reuse the existing propagation report and inheritance owner; do not build a second inheritance mechanism. - Only allowlisted config/* items (crew-dispatch.json, crew-harness, backlog-backend); never inline data/captain-shared.md or secrets. - Per-home changed sets; no message when all allowlisted config is unchanged; different homes can get different sets. - ABSENT for intentional removal; construct message from validated destination state after successful push only. - Use existing routed secondmate send path; surface concrete CONFIG_REREAD retry diagnostic on send failure; do not claim reread landed when send failed. - Newly launched/relaunched secondmates need no redundant nudge unless files changed after launch. - Preserve runtime-choice flexibility: do NOT harden fm-spawn to reject deliberate runtime choices that differ from configured defaults - these are defaults/rules, not enforcement. - Keep the change small; The default tmux backend uses literal keystrokes followed by Enter, without bracketed-paste or another multiline-safe encoding, so embedded newlines can submit the prefix before the full instruction reaches the agent. The fake-tmux tests only log the command and do not validate this live transport. 🔧 Fix: Send config rereads via durable single-line pointers 2 warnings still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:446` - The fixed `state/.fm-inherited-config-reread` path is overwritten on every nudge. If a second config push occurs before the first pointer is consumed, both pointers resolve to the newer file, losing the earlier changed set and exact bytes. This conflicts with the required per-home changed-set and exact-content guarantees. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:550` - After a send failure, the instruction file remains but the report is deleted; a later `fm-config-push.sh` sees the config as unchanged and suppresses the nudge, so the emitted retry diagnostic cannot be retried through the normal command and later changes can permanently omit this reread. 🔧 Fix: Make failed config rereads retryable 2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:583` - The retry marker survives secondmate relaunch, and this branch treats it as sufficient reason to send when `changed_items` is empty. Because bootstrap calls this after liveness/respawn, a failed nudge for the old agent is resent to a newly launched agent even when no files changed after launch, contradicting the required "newly launched/relaunched secondmates need no redundant nudge unless files changed after launch" behavior. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:578` - The per-home instruction remains a single fixed path, and a later changed push rewrites it from only the current report before sending. If nudge A fails and push B occurs before A is retried, the pending marker still points to the same path but its body now contains only B; a successful B send then clears the marker, permanently losing A's exact changed set and bytes. 🔧 Fix: Make config reread retries generation-safe 3 warnings still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:702` - Publication or retry-marker failures only print a CONFIG_REREAD diagnostic. The temporary propagation report is then deleted, and unchanged future pushes have no pending generation to retry, so the live secondmate can remain stale permanently. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1261` - The required behavior is “Newly launched/relaunched secondmates need no redundant nudge unless files changed after launch.” If pending-generation cleanup fails, fm-spawn only warns but still succeeds; liveness marks the ID respawned, bootstrap skips pending delivery, and a later config push can resend the stale generation to the new agent. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-config-push.sh:150` - Mid-session pushes have no per-home serialization around propagation, generation publication, and pointer delivery. A newer push can send its generation before an older paused push resumes and sends stale bytes last; concurrent callers can also treat an already-removed marker as a delivery failure. Serialize the per-home sequence. 🔧 Fix: Make config rereads durable and ordered 4 warnings still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-config-push.sh:153` - When 16 staged generations are pending, this preflight returns before `fm_config_send_reread_nudge` can publish and deliver them. Normal `fm-config-push.sh` and bootstrap runs therefore can never drain a full retry queue; allow retry-only delivery before rejecting a new generation. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:867` - If one pending delivery fails while another generation succeeds, the early return skips `fm_config_reread_cleanup_sent`. Each later successful generation remains retained, so the promised bounded sent history can grow without limit. Run cleanup before returning failure while preserving pending files. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:98` - Sourcing `fm-wake-lib.sh` immediately runs `mkdir -p "$STATE"`, so `FM_BOOTSTRAP_DETECT_ONLY=1` can mutate the filesystem before the mutating-sweep guard. This violates the documented read-only bootstrap mode; defer initialization or separate the lock helpers. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1280` - The required behavior is "Newly launched/relaunched secondmates need no redundant nudge unless files changed after launch." If pending cleanup fails, `fm-spawn.sh` only warns but still exits successfully; liveness marks the secondmate respawned while ignoring that warning, allowing stale destination markers or retry stages to be resent by a later normal config push. 🔧 Fix: Drain retries, bound history, preserve detect-only read-only mode 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:829` - On instruction-write failure, `rm -f "$current_stage_path"` discards the only retry artifact. The command reports a CONFIG_REREAD failure, but a later unchanged push has neither changed items nor a pending generation, so the live secondmate can remain stale permanently. Retain a durable retry record for this failure path. 🔧 Fix: Retain write retries and quarantine stale respawn generations 5 issues (2 errors, 2 warnings, 1 info) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:937` - The required behavior is the full exact new destination post-write bytes. On instruction-write failure, this branch retains only the status report at lines 937-938; a later retry rebuilds the generation from the destination's then-current bytes at lines 909 and 615-617. If another push changes the file first, the failed generation no longer contains its original exact bytes. - 🚨 `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:984` - Delivery sorts generations oldest-first, but a failed pointer only sets send_failures and the loop continues. A newer generation can land while an older one remains pending, then a later retry sends the older bytes last and can restore stale defaults in the live secondmate. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:936` - Each retry stage is created as an empty file before instruction generation. When generation writing fails, the new branch saves a report but does not remove that empty stage; pending-stage accounting ignores zero-byte files, so repeated report-retention failures can accumulate unbounded orphan stages outside the retry limit. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:818` - Quarantine creates a new generation directory on every cleanup failure and never prunes old directories; the function is also called for both homes even when there are no artifacts to move. Repeated relaunch cleanup failures can therefore accumulate unbounded full-content snapshots and empty directories, conflicting with the bounded artifact lifecycle. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:634` - `fm_config_reread_new_instruction_path` has no callers in the changed code or its call sites and preserves an obsolete fixed-path publication strategy; removing it would reduce misleading dead code. 🔧 Fix: Preserve exact config reread retries and delivery order 2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:977` - If moving the preserved exact-byte temporary fails, the retry path deletes it at line 977; the fresh-generation path falls back to a report without queueing it. Later retries can rebuild from newer destination bytes, losing the original generation. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:828` - The pruner's `"$oldest"/*` glob skips hidden quarantined artifacts and `.sequence`, so real quarantine directories cannot be removed at the retention limit. Cleanup then falls back to deletion instead of bounded quarantine retention. 🔧 Fix: Preserve exact retry bytes and bounded quarantine pruning ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: fix(spawn): anchor agent launches to verified worktrees
body:
## Intent

Fix the critical Herdr 0.7.3 fm-spawn isolation failure where a transient treehouse foreground cwd could be mistaken for durable shell state and Codex could launch in the primary project checkout while spawn reported an isolated worktree. Reproduce and causally prove the race only in the mandatory named non-default Herdr lab with disposable repositories, distinguish trigger, transient masking condition, and wrong-cwd symptom, and compare the persistent-cwd counterfactual. Make the actual launch deterministically cd to the exact validated physical worktree with safe shell quoting, verify launch-side cwd and every available passive post-launch foreground agent cwd before metadata publication, and on failure stop the exact endpoint, preserve the worktree, publish no metadata, and fail loudly. Preserve tmux, Herdr, zellij, cmux, Orca, secondmates, all verified harness templates, model and effort flags, task temp export, turn-end hooks, trust prompts, supported special-character paths, metadata, and restored-layout recovery. Keep isolation mechanics in fm-spawn and backend primitives, update the precise Herdr guide and script contract without bloating AGENTS.md, add deterministic transient-cwd and fail-closed regressions, and record dated real Codex Herdr 0.7.3 named-lab evidence while leaving the default session and all captain panes unchanged. Validate with targeted tests, the full repository suite, pinned ShellCheck, fm-lint, and throwaway-home watcher checks; do not invoke the protected live primary fm-watch-arm smoke.

## What Changed

- Anchor every harness launch to the validated physical worktree, verify launch-side and available passive foreground cwd state, and publish metadata atomically only after verification succeeds.
- Fail closed with tri-state endpoint checks and exact cleanup while preserving worktrees, secondmate recovery, and restored cmux layouts across windows.
- Add deterministic regressions for transient Herdr cwd masking, launch and metadata failures, backend cleanup, and recovery, with updated Herdr, tmux, and cmux documentation.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The bounded cmux cleanup now verifies exact absence, handles the documented last-workspace case, fails safely on inconclusive inspection, and avoids closing title-based collateral targets.

## Testing

The pre-supplied full repository suite was green; focused transient-cwd, launch anchoring, passive verification, exact cleanup, recovery, and atomic metadata tests also passed, and a real guarded Herdr 0.7.3 named-lab E2E finished with the default-session tripwire intact. CLI transcripts and the tracked dated Codex race evidence were captured; no UI screenshot was applicable to this CLI-only change, and lint/static analysis was not rerun because this testing step explicitly prohibited it.

The transcript contains only harness setup, permission-approval boilerplate, skill/tool listings, and an interrupted turn, with no substantive developer request preserved; the only concrete developer-driven actions were approving command prefixes for running "wezterm cli send-text" (including one that sends a "/config" nudge to a wezterm pane). ## What Changed

- Fall back to `CODEX_THREAD_ID` ownership when process inspection or parent lookup is unavailable, while preserving live PID locks and refusing foreign Codex-thread locks.
- Add explicit lock clearing and status messaging for unrecoverable Codex-thread owners, with corresponding session-start guidance.
- Recognize a matching Codex-thread lock in the session-start nudge and add coverage for denied inspection, ownership conflicts, recovery, and nudge suppression.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The explicit operator-clear recovery is narrowly scoped and preserves the selected fail-closed behavior for automatic lock acquisition.

The acquire path then overwrites that live lock and both sessions run mutable startup work. Treat foreign thread owners as held/unknown (fail closed) unless their liveness can be independently proven.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-lock.sh:41` - The new non-numeric lock format is rejected by `fm-sessionstart-nudge.sh`'s numeric-only ownership check, so a later SessionStart in the same Codex thread re-emits the instruction to run the supposedly once-per-session mutable digest. Add matching `codex-thread:$CODEX_THREAD_ID` recognition in the nudge path.

The acquire path then overwrites a conventional live harness lock. Fail closed for a live PID whenever harness inspection is unavailable, and cover this cross-owner case.

If a sandbox permits `comm` but denies the parent lookup, this branch returns before reaching `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, so session start still fails instead of acquiring its thread lock. Treat an unavailable parent lookup as a loop break and fall back after the loop.

🔧 Fix: Reach Codex fallback after parent lookup denial

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-lock.sh:50` - Every `codex-thread:` owner is now permanently treated as alive, but there is no session-end cleanup or verifiable stale-owner recovery. ## Intent Fix Firstmate's primary Pi supervision extension so Pi's `/new` command cleanly ends the prior logical session and supervision can be armed normally in the replacement session without restarting the Pi process. Reproduce the original `Pi session is shutting down` refusal with an isolated Pi configuration and `FM_HOME`, then make the `session_shutdown`/`session_start` lifecycle robust and idempotent across repeated `/new`, `/resume`, `/fork`, and `/reload` transitions. Stop old children, cancel retries, invalidate stale timers and callbacks, reinstall exactly one process-exit cleanup listener, and never resurrect supervision during a real quit or process shutdown. Treat any non-null pending replacement as sufficient proof of a logical-session replacement while preserving generation-safe stale-callback invalidation and terminal shutdown behavior. Add deterministic regression coverage, extend the existing isolated live Pi E2E with identity-matched watcher-lock and fresh-beacon readiness checks, validate strict Pi types and related tests, and record dated verification evidence without unrelated refactors. ## What Changed eb4f28f no-mistakes(document): broaden teardown retry-class docs for git-checkout race 061f4d6 no-mistakes(test): fix orca meta-write fail-closed and treehouse return race retry 7d418e1 no-mistakes(review): gate watcher reset on pending replacement, not reason equality c3a50fc fix(pi): reset watcher across logical sessions ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a well-bounded, carefully-scoped concurrency fix that threads a session-generation guard through every async watcher callback, is type-safe against the pi SDK event contract, and is backed by documented live e2e verification, with no correctness or safety defects found. ## Testing The configured baseline suite already ran green. title: feat(bin): sandbox-safe session locking, guarded lock release, and remote SSH helper
body:
## Intent

Harden Firstmate session locking and session-start reporting against harness shell sandboxes that block process inspection, especially Codex Seatbelt. When process inspection is unavailable, acquire must fail with the truthful cause and actionable codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox remedy, status must report that liveness cannot be evaluated and never call a lock stale, and non-forced release must preserve the lock while release --force remains the explicit override. Sessions with working process inspection must behave unchanged. Session-start must relay fm-lock stderr and use the another-live-session banner only when fm-lock actually reports a live holder. Record the verified 2026-07-21 codex-cli 0.144.6 Seatbelt behavior and environment markers in the Codex harness guidance. Add colocated Bash 3.2-compatible tests using a failing ps shim for all required paths, keep bin scripts ShellCheck 0.11.0-clean, use the smallest viable diff, and do not redesign the lock with heartbeat or mtime liveness.

## What Changed

- Hardened `bin/fm-lock.sh` against harness sandboxes that block process inspection (verified against Codex Seatbelt, codex-cli 0.144.6): acquire now fails closed with the truthful cause and the `codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` remedy, status reports that liveness cannot be evaluated instead of declaring a lock stale, non-forced release preserves the lock while `release --force` remains the explicit override, and lock write/removal errors abort instead of reporting success. A new guarded manual `release` command was added, `bin/fm-spawn.sh` fails closed on macOS Bash 3.2 metadata write errors, and `bin/fm-session-start.sh` now relays fm-lock stderr and shows the another-live-session banner only when fm-lock actually reports a live holder.
- Added `bin/fm-remote-ssh.sh` with a remote host registry: an SSH worktree helper that enforces a wall-clock deadline on remote calls and strict task-root containment, documented in `docs/configuration.md` and `docs/scripts.md`.
- Hardened herdr backend startup-dialog handling in `bin/backends/herdr.sh`: guarded dialog focus and Enter retries corroborated against agent status, the codex trust Enter fallback gated on a cursorless screen, and spawn failures surfaced — with live trust-dialog evidence and tunables recorded in `docs/herdr-backend.md`. title: feat(council): add persistent multi-model council MVP with sandboxed Herdr lane
body:
## Intent

Implement the captain-approved narrow persistent council MVP for Firstmate without restoring the rejected large architecture. Provide one natural-language /council workflow backed by one authoritative CLI that creates named project-bound councils with the exact Claude Code claude-fable-5 xhigh and Codex gpt-5.6-sol xhigh profiles, preserves each participant conversation across serialized rounds, permits independent councils in parallel, fans out one fixed secret-filtered read-only view with isolated answers, handles partial availability honestly, and atomically saves the exact presented canonical decision before broadcast and catch-up. Keep accept-and-implement separate from council analysis, support reject/rerun, exact explicit close, fresh conversations with inherited accepted decisions or clean slate, restart-safe endpoint identity, interrupted-round retry, and project-specific provider consent. Enforce the first supported Linux x86_64 Herdr lane with Landlock plus terminal-socket denial, validate lifecycle with provider-free stubs in a guarded non-default Herdr lab, include deterministic contract tests and concise user documentation, and deliberately omit scorecards, judge models, budget/UI/transcript systems, global display migration, broad backend support, and complex recovery.

## What Changed

- Added a persistent council MVP: a `/council` skill and an authoritative `bin/fm-council.py` CLI (plus `bin/fm-council.sh` wrapper) that create named, project-bound councils with fixed Claude Code `claude-fable-5` xhigh and Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` xhigh participant profiles, preserve each participant's conversation across serialized rounds, allow independent councils to run in parallel, fan out one fixed secret-filtered read-only project snapshot with isolated per-participant answers, report partial availability honestly, and atomically save the canonical accepted decision before broadcast and catch-up — with reject/rerun, explicit close, fresh conversations (inheriting accepted decisions or clean slate), restart-safe endpoint identity, and interrupted-round retry.
- Added `bin/fm-council-sandbox.py` enforcing the Linux x86_64 Herdr lane (Landlock confinement plus terminal-socket and io_uring seccomp denial); follow-up review commits hardened the controller with symlink-safe answer ingest (lstat/O_NOFOLLOW/dir_fd, size caps), outbox-fd-pinned submit writes, recorded answer-refusal reasons, per-member readiness degradation instead of hard failure, snapshot directory-mode ordering, and the fixed secret-stem filter.
- Added deterministic contract tests (`tests/fm-council.test.sh`), a guarded provider-free Herdr e2e lab test (`tests/fm-council-herdr-e2e.test.sh`), and concise user docs (`docs/council.md`, Herdr lane verification record in `docs/herdr-backend.md`, configuration/scripts updates).

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: All findings accepted across prior rounds are now verifiably fixed with dedicated regression tests (fd-pinned create-exclusive submit publication and durable, deduplicated answer-refusal evidence), the branch satisfies every source-verifiable intent criterion, and this round's diff introduces no new material issues.

## Testing

Completed 1 recorded test check.

- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 error across 1 run (20m30s)

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

<details>
<summary>✅ **intent** - passed</summary>

✅ No issues found.

</details>

<details>
<summary>✅ **Rebase** - passed</summary>

✅ No issues found.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 **Review** - 6 issues found → auto-fixed (2) ✅</summary>

- 🚨 `bin/fm-council.py:1045` - Participant answer ingestion follows symlinks out of the untrusted sandbox: `command_collect` reads the roster answer path with `Path(...).is_file()`/`read_text()` (and `readiness` stats it at line 995) from the participant-writable outbox. The Landlock policy grants participants MAKE_SYM in their home, so a malicious/prompt-injected participant can plant `outbox/<round>.md -> <project>/.env` (the very file the secret filter excluded), `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, another participant's outbox, or any controller-readable file; the unsandboxed controller then reads that target as the participant's answer, surfaces it to the captain, and after acceptance broadcasts it to both model providers. This defeats the hard isolation boundary and secret-filtered-view guarantee under the change's own threat model. Fix: open answer files with O_NOFOLLOW, verify S_ISREG via lstat, and cap read size (read_text is currently unbounded).
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-council.py:377` - `build_snapshot` applies each directory's original mode immediately after mkdir (`os.chmod(target, entry["mode"])`) before copying its children. Any project directory lacking owner write permission (e.g. a 0o555 vendored or generated tree) makes the subsequent child `shutil.copyfile` raise an uncaught PermissionError — surfacing as a raw traceback instead of a CouncilError — and the round can never start until the project's permissions change. Directory modes should be applied after the subtree is populated (e.g. in the final read-only chmod pass, which already rewrites all modes anyway).
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-council.py:1000` - `readiness()` calls `probe_member` without catching CouncilError, so one corrupt or tampered member `runtime.json` mid-round makes `ready` and `wait` fail entirely (and `wait` crash on every poll) instead of degrading that member to "unavailable". This is inconsistent with the dispatch path (line 939) and the acceptance path (line 1188), which both deliberately convert the same per-member CouncilError into an honest unavailable/deferred entry. Wrap the probe in try/except CouncilError and classify the member unavailable.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-council.py:783` - Real-lane delivery passes the entire round/decision payload as one argv element to `herdr agent send`. Every round's common.md embeds all accepted decision bodies, so accumulated decisions can push a payload past Linux's ~128 KiB MAX_ARG_STRLEN, failing with E2BIG and mislabeling a live participant "unavailable"; a captain-authored decision body starting with `-` may also be parsed as a herdr flag since no `--` separator is used. The payload file is already written into the participant's inbox (write_payload), so file-referenced delivery is possible, but that changes the participant interaction contract, so the remediation choice belongs to the author.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-council.py:313` - The fixed secret filter excludes names containing "credential" and "private-key", .env variants, key suffixes, and known credential filenames, but passes through common secret-bearing names containing "secret" or "token" (e.g. secrets.yaml, secrets.json, token.txt), which then reach cloud providers in the round view. Since the filter is intentionally fixed and documented, extending it is a deliberate product decision.
- ℹ️ `tests/fm-council.test.sh:252` - The independent-council parallelism proof depends on two 0.25 s stub sleeps physically overlapping (`parallel-proved` is only created when two `active-*` markers coexist), so the assertion can flake on a heavily loaded or slow runner where the second `ask` starts after the first stub sleep ends. A longer overlap window or a rendezvous (each sender waits briefly for the peer marker) would make it deterministic.

🔧 Fix: Harden answer ingest, snapshot modes, readiness, argv delivery, secret filter
3 issues (1 warning, 2 infos) still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-council.py:1107` - Write-side TOCTOU in `command_submit`: the outbox is verified to be a private real directory via `open_outbox_dir`, but the returned fd is immediately closed and the answer is then written through the untrusted path with `atomic_bytes(destination, content)`. A participant that replaces `outbox` with a symlink between the check (line 1106) and the write can redirect the controller's `<round>.md` creation into any controller-writable directory (e.g. the source project or council data dirs). The read side already solves this pattern with dir_fd + O_NOFOLLOW; mirror it here by keeping the verified directory fd open and creating the file with os.open(f"{round_id}.md", O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, dir_fd=...) instead of a path-based atomic_bytes. Window is narrow and submit is only exercised by deterministic transports, so follow-up is acceptable.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-council.py:876` - An answer file that exists but fails the safety gate in `read_member_answer` (non-regular, hard-linked, wrong uid, group/other-writable, oversized, empty, or non-UTF-8) is silently treated as never-answered: the member shows as "pending" until wait times out, with no events.jsonl record of the refusal or its reason. Notably, a live participant that writes its answer via a plain shell redirect under a umask-002 system (Ubuntu user-private-group default) produces a 0664 file that is silently discarded even though the participant genuinely answered; only the instructed mkstemp+rename path yields a passing 0600 file. Emitting an `answer_refused_unsafe` event (with the failed check) would make the refusal observable and support the honesty contract; whether to log, mention the required mode in the pointer instruction, or relax the group-write check is a product decision.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-council.py:318` - The new secret-stem filter deliberately applies to files only (`not entry.is_dir(...)`), so a directory named `secrets/` or `tokens/` is still included in the round view and its contents leak unless individually matched by other rules. This matches the requested narrow scope (avoid broad exclusions of ordinary source identifiers like a `secrets.py` module), so no action is required; recording the tradeoff.

🔧 Fix: Pin submit writes to outbox fd, record answer refusal reasons
✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

</details>

<details>
<summary>⚠️ **Test** - 1 error</summary>

- 🚨 tests failed with exit code 1
- `command -v tmux >/dev/null || { echo "tmux is required for e2e tests" >&2; exit 1; }; tmux -V; rc=0; for t in tests/*.test.sh; do echo "== $t =="; bash "$t" || rc=1; done; exit "$rc"`

<summary>⚠️ **Document** - 1 info</summary>

- ℹ️ `docs/herdr-backend.md:1017` - The Herdr lane verification record in docs/herdr-backend.md cites source commit d0f9062c6a1c2aad189b24dc3ce461e30e2cbf68, a gate-internal commit that will dangle in the published linear history. I added a sentence documenting that the files the proof executes (bin/fm-council-sandbox.py, bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh, tests/fm-council-herdr-e2e.test.sh) are byte-identical between that commit and the shipped change, but the hash itself remains unresolvable for future readers; refreshing it honestly would require rerunning the guarded FM_COUNCIL_HERDR_E2E lab proof at the final commit, which is outside this documentation-only task.

title: fix(tmux): pin exact session-name matching in session targets
body:
## Bug

tmux resolves a bare session-name target by exact name, then prefix, then fnmatch, and parses a bare numeric target-window session name as a window INDEX in the current session.

Observed live on 2026-07-16: with firstmate running inside a tmux session literally named `1` and window index 1 occupied, the bare `new-window -d -t "$ses"` form resolved `1` as a window index, so the first concurrent spawn filled index 1 and every later one failed with `create window failed: index 1 in use`.
Serial spawn/teardown cycles never hit it, which is why it survived.

#134's trailing colon already fixed that numeric-index form for `new-window` on main.
The prefix-match half remains on main:

- with only a `firstmate2`-style session present, `fm_backend_tmux_container_ensure`'s bare `has-session -t firstmate` probe matches it, the real `firstmate` session is never created, and every task window lands in the stranger session;
- an afk daemon record naming a gone session can kill, or report alive, a prefix-sibling session via the bare `kill-session`/`has-session` targets in `bin/fm-afk-launch.sh`.

## Fix

Pin every composed session-name target with tmux's `=` exact-match prefix:

- `bin/backends/tmux.sh`: container-ensure's probe (`=firstmate`), create-task's duplicate check (`=$ses`), and the new-window target (`=$ses:`, combining the exact-name pin with the trailing-colon index pin);
- `bin/fm-afk-launch.sh`: the recorded daemon session's close, absence, and liveness probes (`=$target`).

The verified resolution semantics (tmux 3.6, private `-L` socket) are recorded in `docs/tmux-backend.md` under "Session-target resolution".

## Regression tests

- `tests/fm-backend-tmux-smoke.test.sh`: two consecutive task-window creations from a session literally named `1` with index 1 occupied must both succeed, and container-ensure must create the exact `firstmate` session next to a `firstmate2` decoy. The prefix-sibling assertion fails on main's code (`not ok - container-ensure did not create the exact 'firstmate' session (bare probe prefix-matched 'firstmate2'?)`) and passes with the fix.
- `tests/fm-afk-launch.test.sh`: a stale daemon record must neither read nor kill a prefix-sibling session. Fails on main's code (`not ok - tmux exact resolution: bare session target prefix-matched the sibling (read it as alive or killed it)`) and passes with the fix.
- `tests/fm-backend-tmux-smoke.test.sh` also gets a robustness fix found while validating on a slow WSL2 host: the shell-ready probe's `C-c` could deliver SIGINT while the pane's bash was still sourcing startup files, killing the shell (and window) before its interactive handler was armed. `C-u` clears a half-typed retry without signalling.

All of `tests/fm-backend-tmux-smoke.test.sh` (9 assertions), the tmux arm of `tests/fm-afk-launch.test.sh`, and `tests/fm-tangle-guard.test.sh` pass locally against real tmux 3.6, and the touched scripts lint clean under the pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0 (`bin/fm-install-shellcheck.sh` build).

title: 修复 watcher healthy-peer 测试夹具竞态
body:
## 问题

`test_watch_restart_attaches_to_healthy_peer` 启动 synthetic Node peer 后立即发布 PID 与 watcher identity。
Node 进程存在不代表 SIGTERM handler 已安装完成；`--restart` 若在这个窗口发送 SIGTERM，peer 会退出，生产代码随后正确启动 replacement watcher，但测试会误判为 attach 失败。
环境中继承的 `PI_CODING_AGENT` 与 `FM_HOME` 还会让 guard/X-mode 夹具走到其他路径，掩盖目标竞态。

## 修复

- watcher-lock 套件统一使用夹具自有的 `FM_HOME`，并清除会改变测试路径的 `PI_CODING_AGENT`。
- guard 与 X-mode 场景显式绑定各自 case home，避免读取调用方配置。
- synthetic peer 在安装 SIGTERM handler 后写入 readiness sentinel；夹具观察到 sentinel 后才发布 healthy lock identity。
- SIGTERM handler 另写 TERM sentinel；测试同时要求 TERM 已处理、peer 仍存活、arm 输出 `attached`，且不存在 `watcher: started` replacement。

## 确定性证明

readiness sentinel 明确建立 handler 安装完成到 healthy identity 发布之间的先后关系。
12 轮真实 `fm-watch-arm.sh --restart` 因果验证均观察到 `readiness -> identity publish -> TERM handled -> attached`，peer 在 TERM 后保持存活，replacement 启动次数为 0。

## 验证

- GitHub checks：5 passed、0 failed、1 skipped。
- `Lint shell scripts`、`PR must be raised via no-mistakes`、`Behavior tests`、`Stock macOS Bash snapshot compatibility` 与 `Repo invariants` 均通过；skipped 项为同名 required-check 的非执行记录。
- 目标 healthy-peer case 重复运行 8/8 通过。
- 完整 `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh` 在故意污染的 ambient `FM_HOME` 与 `PI_CODING_AGENT` 下 27/27 通过。
- 9 个相关 watcher/wake/guard/daemon shell 套件共 235 项断言通过。
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` 使用固定 ShellCheck 0.11.0 通过。

## 风险与限制

风险低：仅修改 `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh`，未修改 production watcher、spawn/worktree ownership、Herdr topology 或 presentation 行为。
本次验证覆盖 macOS 上的真实进程时序；Linux 专属 PID identity 用例在非 Linux 主机上按既有逻辑跳过，且不在本次变更范围内。

title: feat: guard against missed secondmate reports
body:
## Intent Implement parent-owned guards that detect and recover missed secondmate communication. Captain direction (2026-07-22): guard and detect a missed report, not pretend agent routing mistakes can be prevented. A secondmate may ignore instructions or answer only in its visible conversation. The safety property is that the parent notices the missing correlated report without scraping that conversation, requests one bounded repost, and escalates once if the repost is also missed. Design decisions: - Every marked parent-to-secondmate request gets a privacy-safe corr=<16hex> correlation id and a durable parent-owned pending-reply expectation under state/pending-replies/ before delivery (bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh). - Delivery success and reply success are separate: successful fm-send never resolves the expectation; only a correlated parent status line or status-pointed document does, idempotently. - Turn completion is proven via backend busy/idle observation (fm_backend_busy_state abstraction for Pi/Claude paths), never by reading conversation text. - After a bounded grace (FM_PENDING_REPLY_GRACE_SECS, default 120) with turn completed and no correlated report, send exactly one automatic recovery repost; track that recovery turn separately; if it also completes without a report, escalate once via blocked status + wake queue and retain the unresolved durable record forever (expiration never silently erases unresolved replies). - Wrong-home reports are counted as supporting evidence only, never acknowledgement. - Direct unmarked captain/crewmate messages create no expectation. - Optional bin/fm-secondmate-report.sh helper exists but correctness does not depend on the agent using it. - Escalation lines use pending-reply-id= (not corr=) so parent-written escalations cannot self-resolve. - Avoided overlap with concurrent test-runner work: did not edit canonical runner, CI topology, or test-family manifest. ## What Changed - Add durable parent-owned correlation records for marked secondmate requests, keeping delivery and correlated reply acknowledgement separate. - Extend the watcher to detect completed turns without reports, issue one bounded recovery repost, and escalate once while retaining unresolved records. - Add an optional correlated-report helper, operational documentation, and coverage for delivery, recovery, resolution, and escalation behavior. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The final change closes the late-report gap, and the full branch now satisfies the correlated acknowledgement, bounded recovery, one-shot escalation, and durable-state requirements without a substantiated remaining source defect. ## Testing At the requested target commit, I inspected the focused diff, ran both pending-reply behavior suites, exercised the complete missed-report recovery and escalation lifecycle through the actual send and watcher functions, verified the captured evidence assertions, and confirmed the worktree remained clean; all checks passed.
Evidence: Parent-owned pending-reply end-to-end transcript ```text PARENT-OWNED PENDING REPLY - END-TO-END TRANSCRIPT 1. Marked secondmate delivery record_exists_before_transport=yes phase_before_transport=awaiting_report marker_present=yes delivered_payload_after_marker=corr=6c79c35ed8e6c7ac audit the build corr_length=16 phase_after_transport=awaiting_report transport_resolved_expectation=no 2. Wrong-home report is evidence, not acknowledgement wrong_home_hits=1 phase_after_wrong_home_report=awaiting_report 3. Parent watcher observes request turn busy -> idle with no parent report phase_after_first_miss=recovery_sent automatic_recovery_send_count=1 recovery_payload=[fm-from-firstmate]⁣corr=6c79c35ed8e6c7ac REPOST REQUIRED: previous marked request had no correlated parent report. Reply on the parent status channel including corr=6c79c35ed8e6c7ac. Original request: audit the build 4. Parent watcher observes recovery turn busy -> idle with no report phase_after_second_miss=escalated escalation_count=1 escalation_line=blocked: pending-reply-missed: task=hibit pending-reply-id=6c79c35ed8e6c7ac request=audit the build escalation_contains_corr_token=no 5. Long-later watcher tick phase_after_long_later_tick=escalated unresolved_record_retained=yes 6. Direct unmarked crewmate message delivered_payload=captain says hello pending_record_count_before=1 pending_record_count_after=1 ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 5 issues found → auto-fixed (10) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:611` - Required behavior is absent for the default tmux backend and supported zellij path. This tick relies exclusively on `fm_backend_busy_state`, but those adapters always return `unknown`; consequently `request_turn_completed_epoch` is never set and a missed report is never recovered or escalated. This contradicts the required criteria that turn completion be observed and that a completed missed turn trigger one recovery followed by escalation. - 🚨 `bin/fm-send.sh:239` - Any message containing a correlation ID whose record exists reuses that record without checking its `task_id` or phase. Forwarding a correlated message to another secondmate therefore creates no expectation for the new target, while reusing a resolved record leaves a new send unguarded. This contradicts the requirement that every marked parent-to-secondmate request receive its own applicable durable expectation. - 🚨 `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:510` - Appending the blocked status and directly adding a `check` wake causes the same watcher cycle to detect the newly changed status and enqueue a second actionable `signal` wake. This deterministically surfaces two queue records for one miss, contradicting the required single escalation. - 🚨 `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:490` - The record is permanently transitioned to `escalated` before either escalation artifact is durably written, while both the status append and wake append discard errors. If both publications fail, later ticks refuse to retry, so the required blocked-status and wake-queue escalation is silently lost. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:525` - Every watcher tick increments `wrong_home_hits` again while the same historical correlated line remains present. Track distinct sightings or persist the last observed signature so this supporting-evidence count reflects reports rather than polling frequency. 🔧 Fix: Deduplicate wrong-home pending-reply sightings 4 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:625` - The required criterion says, "Turn completion is proven via backend busy/idle observation" and then requires recovery after a completed miss. This hunk only calls `fm_backend_busy_state`, while its existing contract returns `unknown` for tmux and every adapter except Herdr. On the default tmux backend and supported zellij path, neither completion epoch is ever set, so missed reports remain pending forever without recovery or escalation. - 🚨 `bin/fm-send.sh:239` - The required criterion says, "Every marked parent-to-secondmate request gets ... a durable parent-owned pending-reply expectation." This hunk reuses any correlation record found in message text without verifying its `task_id` or phase. Forwarding a correlated message to another secondmate creates no expectation for that target, and reusing a resolved record leaves the new send unguarded. - 🚨 `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:512` - The required criterion says to "escalate once via blocked status + wake queue." This direct `check` wake follows a newly appended `blocked:` status, but the same watcher cycle subsequently detects that changed status and appends a separate actionable `signal` wake. Wake deduplication keys by kind and key, so both records survive and one missed recovery produces two escalations. - 🚨 `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:492` - The required criterion says to "escalate once via blocked status + wake queue." The record is permanently changed to `escalated` before either artifact is published, while both the status append and wake append discard errors. If publication fails, later ticks refuse to retry and the required escalation is silently lost. 🔧 Fix: Harden pending-reply recovery and escalation guards 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:668` - Every pending-reply record is probed through the backend before `tick_one` checks its phase. Resolved records are never removed, and escalated records are retained forever, so tmux/zellij will accumulate one pane capture per historical request every watcher cycle even though those phases cannot use busy-state evidence. Skip backend observation for resolved/escalated records, and preferably reuse one probe for multiple open records targeting the same secondmate. 🔧 Fix: Bound pending-reply backend polling 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:671` - This preflight calls `fm_pending_reply_try_resolve` for every record, then each open record enters `tick_one`, which repeats the same full status-file scan before and after observation. Escalated records are retained forever and also rescan their growing parent status and wrong-home logs every cycle. Avoid the added scans by checking `phase=resolved` directly, resolving escalated records once, and relying on a cached or incremental status observation for open records. 🔧 Fix: Cache pending-reply status scans 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:381` - The required durable guard can be lost in the create-before-delivery window. A watcher may see the newly created record while `fm-send` is still delivering it and write this negative-scan signature, while `fm_pending_reply_mark_delivered` concurrently rewrites `delivered_epoch`. Because `fm_pending_reply_set` performs unlocked whole-file read/replace operations, the signature writer can move its stale copy last and erase `delivered_epoch`; that expectation then remains permanently ineligible for turn observation, recovery, or escalation. The wrong-home signature write has the same race. Skip all record mutations until delivery is marked, or serialize record rewrites with a per-record lock. 🔧 Fix: Protect undelivered pending-reply records from scans 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-send.sh:292` - The required criterion says every delivered marked request must remain guarded. After transport succeeds, this hunk discards any `fm_pending_reply_mark_delivered` error. A failed write or process exit in this window leaves the durable record permanently undelivered, and the watcher now skips such records forever, so the missing report is never recovered or escalated. Treat delivery-marker failure as a hard error and add a recoverable state for confirmed-but-uncommitted delivery. - 🚨 `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:570` - The required criterion says to "send exactly one automatic recovery repost." The recovery is delivered before `phase=recovery_sent` is persisted. If the process exits or the record rewrite fails after delivery, the record remains `awaiting_report`, and every later tick can resend the recovery. Persist an at-most-once recovery-attempt state before the external send and reconcile its outcome without reinjection. 🔧 Fix: Close pending-reply delivery durability gaps 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:347` - The required criterion separates delivery success from reply handling, but an `attempted` marker is promoted to delivered after grace without evidence that transport ran or succeeded. A sender crash before submission, a long-running send, or `FM_PENDING_REPLY_GRACE_SECS=0` can therefore manufacture delivery and trigger recovery/escalation for a request that never landed. Only reconcile `confirmed`; keep `attempted` as an unknown state until backend evidence or an explicit failure resolves it. - 🚨 `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:652` - The required criterion says to "send exactly one automatic recovery repost" and track that recovery turn separately. This path calls `fm_pending_reply_reconcile_recovery` even when transport definitively fails, and reconciliation writes `recovery_sent_epoch` and `phase=recovery_sent`. The watcher can then observe and escalate a nonexistent recovery turn. Preserve failed/unknown attempt states and escalate a delivery failure explicitly without representing it as a sent repost. 🔧 Fix: Separate pending-reply transport outcomes 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:351` - The required safety property says the parent notices a missing correlated report, but an `attempted` delivery marker is now ignored forever. If transport succeeds and `fm-send` exits before replacing that marker with `confirmed`, every watcher tick returns here, leaves `delivered_epoch` empty, and never resolves, recovers, or escalates the request. Preserve the unknown state without manufacturing delivery, but surface it once using sender/backend evidence or an explicit delivery-unknown escalation. 🔧 Fix: Escalate stalled pending-reply deliveries once 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:769` - The required criterion says "only a correlated parent status line or status-pointed document" resolves the expectation, but this delivery-unknown escalation calls `fm_pending_reply_try_resolve` while `delivered_epoch` is empty, so that function always refuses before scanning status. If transport succeeded, the sender crashed before confirmation, and the secondmate reported correctly, the watcher still publishes a false delivery-unknown escalation. Treat a correlated parent report as delivery evidence and resolve it before escalating uncertainty. 🔧 Fix: Resolve attempted deliveries from correlated reports 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:945` - The required criterion says a correlated parent status/document resolves the expectation idempotently, including late reports. After a delivery-unknown escalation, `phase=escalated` while `delivered_epoch` remains empty; this branch skips every such record before calling `fm_pending_reply_try_resolve`. A valid late report therefore never resolves automatically even though the resolver now supports attempted markers. Route undelivered escalated records through the resolver before continuing. 🔧 Fix: Resolve late reports after delivery escalation ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: fix(fm-pr-check): rebase ready-to-merge wake onto GitLab-support hardening
body:
## Intent

Re-express a local, previously-unpushed fix on top of upstream's GitLab
merge-request support (#797), which restructured `bin/fm-pr-poll.sh`'s
sidecar/argument format from `(url, owner, repo, number)` to a
provider-tagged `(provider, url, host, path, number)`.

The original fix adds a `ready-to-merge` wake (GitHub PRs, `OPEN` +
`mergeStateStatus=CLEAN`) alongside the existing `merged` wake, so the
watcher can autonomously detect a direct-PR + yolo task's PR is checks-green
and mergeable without firstmate needing to poll `gh pr view` manually. This
only applies to the `github` provider case; the `gitlab` case is untouched
from upstream, since GitLab merge-request support didn't exist when the
original fix was written and extending the ready-to-merge concept to GitLab
wasn't part of either change's original scope.

## What changed in the rebase

- `bin/fm-pr-poll.sh`: folded the `ready-to-merge` state check into the
  `github)` case of upstream's provider dispatch, preserving all of
  upstream's host/path validation and the `gitlab)` case exactly as-is.
- `tests/fm-pr-check.test.sh` (new in the original fix): updated
  `make_case`'s sidecar writer from the old 4-field format to the new
  5-field provider-tagged format so the test matrix actually exercises the
  current script instead of silently testing against a stale calling
  convention.
- `tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh`: auto-merged cleanly, no changes
  needed beyond upstream's own content.

## Verification

Both test files pass in full against the rebased script:
- `tests/fm-pr-check.test.sh`: 9/9 (ready-to-merge, merged, and every
  silent/interim case).
- `tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh`: 25/25 (arming, validation, atomic
  publish, migration, and watcher-bounded wake behavior).

title: fix(supervision): gate terminal PR read and close the watcher arm/guard race
body:
## Intent

Re-apply the three surviving local fix commits from the pre-migration fleet history (documented in data/upstream-reconcile-w7/triage.md) on top of the freshly adopted upstream main (f02eef1/14c0d5f). This is a reconciliation task, not new feature work: nine of the twelve original local commits were confirmed superseded or obsolete by reading upstream code directly and were deliberately dropped, and only the three genuinely still-needed pieces were re-applied.

1. Crew-state gh-gated terminal PR read (cherry-pick 459ef29): outcome=passed from no-mistakes was being read as a terminal PR-merged/closed state without confirmation, which could end supervision of a still-open, unlanded PR. This picked clean since the upstream region was untouched. Its documentation commit (a93bc00) could not cherry-pick cleanly because upstream had since restructured AGENTS.md (compressed from 937 to 481 lines), dropped CONTRIBUTING.md's per-test index, and rewrote the fm-crew-state row in docs/scripts.md - so the doc content was re-expressed by hand against the current wording in AGENTS.md and docs/architecture.md instead of reapplying the old patch text.

2. Watcher arm/guard identity-check race fix (cherry-pick db71adb + bec40d5): adds fm_arm_in_progress / .watch-arm.marker so bin/fm-guard.sh and bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh do not false-alarm 'WATCHER DOWN' while bin/fm-watch-arm.sh is still in the middle of establishing a fresh watcher. Six of seven files applied clean; bin/fm-guard.sh conflicted because upstream #637 had since restructured the same stale-banner block into an episode-dedup form (fm_guard_stale_episode_key / fm_guard_claim_stale_banner, one-line reminder on repeat). I manually merged the '&& ! fm_arm_in_progress ...' suppression into that dedup-restructured condition rather than reverting to the pre-dedup shape, preserving upstream's dedup semantics - the marker check only suppresses a false alarm while an arm is genuinely in progress, never a real lapse. The docs commit bec40d5 applied clean except one AGENTS.md hunk, which I merged to keep both the new .watch-arm.marker line and upstream's already-added .paused-* watcher-internals entry (dropping neither).

3. Consolidated test hardening, re-implemented once (not reapplied verbatim): two old competing draft commits (6136f6b, 8cdb24b) each fixed the same two hermeticity bugs plus an env-leak issue now superseded by upstream #432's form. I kept only the two still-needed fixes and wrote them fresh against the current test files: tests/fm-dispatch-select.test.sh now shims the real jq (which lives outside the fakebin's swapped PATH on this machine, at ~/.local/bin) into the quota-missing/quota-error/no-call fakebin cases so only the intended tool is simulated missing; tests/fm-session-start.test.sh switches its forced-missing-tool probe from node (which leaks through via /usr/bin/node and /bin/node on this machine, so the MISSING diagnostic never fired) to gh-axi, which has no system copy. I found and fixed the same node-leak in a second session-start test (test_composition_invokes_real_scripts) that the original brief didn't name but shares the identical root cause.

Beyond the three planned pieces, running bin/fm-test-run.sh --all after landing everything surfaced two additional test bugs in the just-reapplied db71adb-era tests themselves, both fixed: (a) two ps-retry tests in tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh silently stopped testing anything, because upstream a26b37c/#752 changed fm_pid_identity to read /proc directly on Linux, bypassing the ps-based fallback the tests faked - fixed by forcing the ps fallback path with an unreadable FM_PROC_ROOT_OVERRIDE so the retry logic is genuinely exercised again; (b) the isolated turnend-guard-race test harness copies a hand-picked subset of bin/ scripts into a scratch git repo, and needed fm-primary-scope-lib.sh added to that copy list since bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh now sources it (an unrelated upstream addition, not part of this reconciliation).

Final validation: bin/fm-test-run.sh --all reports total=90 failed=10 - 9 are the pre-existing Herdr-lab provisioning gap on this machine (real-herdr-gated family, environmental, unrelated to any change here) and 1 (fm-send --key old-vs-new exit code, in tests/fm-backend.test.sh) was independently confirmed via a throwaway worktree to already fail identically on the pristine upstream base at 14c0d5f before any of this work, so it was deliberately left untouched as out of scope. All three target pieces plus the two follow-up test fixes are green. Shellcheck (0.11.0, matching the pinned CI version) is clean on every script touched, with only expected info-level SC1091/SC2153 notices.

Standing captain order for this repo: origin (kunchenguid/firstmate) is pull-only, PASSIVE-CONSUMER posture - never push to origin, never open a PR on any repo from this task. Push target should be the fork (lukefork), and if the pipeline reaches a PR-opening step, it should stop there for the captain to open the PR manually rather than doing so automatically.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` now gates the terminal PR merged/closed decision on a real `gh` state instead of treating a `passed` result as landed, so a transient failure or a still-open PR no longer ends supervision of unlanded work; when the merge state cannot be verified it falls back to `done` without asserting the false "merged/closed" claim.
- Added `fm_arm_in_progress` / `.watch-arm.marker` plumbing across `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh`, `bin/fm-watch-arm.sh`, `bin/fm-guard.sh`, and `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh` so the guards no longer raise a false `WATCHER DOWN` while `fm-watch-arm.sh` is mid-establishment of a fresh watcher, while preserving upstream's stale-banner episode-dedup semantics.
- Hardened and repaired the affected tests (dispatch-select shims the real `jq`, session-start probes `gh-axi` instead of the system-leaking `node`, watcher-lock forces the `ps` fallback via `FM_PROC_ROOT_OVERRIDE`) and synced the corresponding docs in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, and `docs/turnend-guard.md`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is additive, fail-safe in the directions I traced, faithful to the authoritative reconciliation intent, and covered by thorough new hermetic tests for every branch of the new logic.

## Testing

Ran the five directly-affected test scripts (crew-state, turnend-guard, watcher-lock, dispatch-select, session-start) plus the full `bin/fm-test-run.sh --all` canonical suite. All three reconciliation pieces pass at the behavior level and I captured the specific test lines proving each (open-PR non-terminal gating, arm-marker race suppression that still catches dead/wedged arms, and the ps-retry + jq-shim + gh-axi probe fixes). I also empirically confirmed the environmental asymmetry the piece-3 fixes depend on (node leaks via /usr/bin/node while gh-axi/jq do not resolve on system paths), which shows the old probe was vacuous and the new one genuinely fires. The `--all` suite reported total=91 failed=10; I traced every failure: 9 are the pre-existing real-herdr-gated provisioning gap on this box (Herdr lab cannot provision here) and 1 is a load-induced timeout flake in fm-watcher-lock's HUP signal test (exit 124 under CPU contention from a concurrent crewmate process) that passes cleanly in isolation — none are regressions from this change. This change is script/CLI-behavior only with no rendered UI surface, so evidence is CLI test transcripts rather than screenshots.
