title: feat: add strict per-project GitHub account routing
body:
## Intent

The developer wanted issue 760 implemented as generic, secure per-project GitHub account routing across FirstMate and every supported GitHub/Git execution path, using the architecture report as authoritative input and No Mistakes draft PR 527 as the lower-layer contract. They required a private versioned config/github-accounts.json schema with strict deterministic routing, legacy behavior when absent, centralized command/process policy, exact binaries, sanitized credentials and Git configuration, delayed-operation profile revalidation, and comprehensive rejection of unsafe schema, environment, URL, Git-config, and credential inputs. They also required broad deterministic and adversarial test coverage, full lint/test/backend validation, isolated two-profile dogfooding without exposing tokens or modifying shared services, and precise acknowledgment that real NexRex remote-write acceptance remained untested without separate authorization. Work had to begin from a clean disposable worktree on a dedicated branch, obey the hard named-session Herdr isolation contract, avoid merging either draft PR or writing external resources, report status sparingly, and ultimately open a draft FirstMate PR linking issue 760 and PR 527 after responsibility-boundary and credential-bypass audits; the latest instruction was to record that the upstream contract had stabilized and resume implementation.

## What Changed

- Add optional strict `config/github-accounts.json` routing that deterministically maps projects, repositories, and owners to GitHub CLI profiles while preserving legacy single-account behavior when absent.
- Apply sanitized, revalidated GitHub and network Git contexts across onboarding, workers, PR operations, delayed checks, secondmates, and No Mistakes, backed by a centralized typed operation schema and authenticated descendant broker.
- Document the routing contract and add adversarial coverage for schema validation, concurrent profiles, credential/config injection, fleet propagation, and legacy behavior; also prevent workers from launching when spawn metadata publication fails.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Captain, the latest schema changes resolve both prior fail-open paths without introducing a material source-verifiable regression.

## Testing

既有 baseline 已知成功；本輪以 tmux 3.7b 重跑完整標準套件並完成隔離雙 profile CLI 證據驗證，所有實際執行路徑成功；套件自行略過需額外 opt-in 或缺少 zellij、合格 cmux、tsc、ShellCheck 的條件測試，且依授權未使用真實 GitHub 憑證或執行遠端寫入。

<details>
<summary>Evidence: 隔離雙 GitHub profile 端到端 CLI transcript</summary>

```text
FirstMate per-project GitHub account routing — isolated end-to-end transcript
Binaries: exact fake gh/git/gh-axi; remotes: local simulation; real credentials and remote writes: none
Config mode: 600
Resolved repo-a profile: profile-a
Resolved repo-b profile: profile-b

Concurrent user operations:
gh	profile-a	pr view 11
gh	profile-b	pr list --repo Owner-B/repo-b
gh-axi	profile-b	pr list --repo Owner-B/repo-b
git	profile-a	ls-remote https://github.com/Owner-A/repo-a.git HEAD
Routed commit author: Account A <account-a@example.test>

Forbidden credential operation:
exit=1
error: routed GitHub authentication mutation, unsafe repository mutation, API escape, or token display is forbidden

Revalidation after a conflicting route change:
exit=1
error: GitHub account bindings conflict for this project and repository

Security summary:
credential_sentinel_exposed=no
cross_profile_route_conflict=blocked
remote_writes=0
```
</details>
- Outcome: 🔧 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ across 2 runs (2h26m31s)

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

<details>
<summary>✅ **intent** - passed</summary>

✅ No issues found.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 **Rebase** - 11 issues found → auto-fixed ✅</summary>

- ⚠️ `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main
- ⚠️ `.agents/skills/secondmate-provisioning/SKILL.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-check-migrate.sh` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-check.sh` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-lib.sh` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-poll.sh` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-watch.sh` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main
- ⚠️ `docs/architecture.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main
- ⚠️ `docs/configuration.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main
- ⚠️ `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main

🔧 Fix applied.
✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 **Review** - 7 issues found → auto-fixed (14) ✅</summary>

- 🚨 `bin/fm-home-seed.sh:582` - Strict secondmate seeding activates a project profile in the parent shell, permanently replacing PATH before home creation and later clone checks. The subsequent local `git clone "$FM_ROOT"` or Git access to an existing seeded clone is then rejected as an unrelated/non-GitHub repository. Scope activation to the individual validation or clone subprocess.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:45` - Adding `github-accounts.json` to the generic inheritance path copies symlinked, wrong-mode, or schema-invalid files without routing validation and includes their exact bytes in durable reread instructions. An invalid config containing credential material can therefore bypass the parser’s rejection boundary and be persisted in secondmate state. Validate this item before copying and never inline unvalidated routing bytes.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:335` - The Git policy blocks explicit recursive-submodule flags but permits repository or command configuration such as `fetch.recurseSubmodules=true` and `submodule.<name>.url`. A routed fetch can consequently contact an arbitrary submodule URL using the selected GitHub credential helper. Reject recursive-submodule configuration and validate every resulting submodule target before network access.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-brief.sh:308` - Existing no-mistakes repositories receive the typed context only when `no-mistakes doctor` reports them uninitialized. The upstream contract treats a repository with no stored GitHub context as healthy and validates a context only when one already exists, so legacy initialization or a later profile rebind can continue using ambient or stale daemon credentials. Strict mode must refresh or compare the stored context before pipeline use.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-config.mjs:367` - Project bindings are ignored unless the project already appears in `data/projects.md`, but onboarding intentionally clones before adding that registry entry. A valid strict configuration containing only `bindings.projects` therefore cannot onboard its project. Provide an authorized pre-registration resolution path or change the transactional registration order.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:1145` - When a gh command supplies `--repo`, validation skips inspection of the actual working directory and checks only the configured project path. Running from an unrelated checkout therefore succeeds despite the documented invariant that descendant operations reject unrelated repositories. Always validate the actual checkout in addition to the explicit target.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:275` - Every routed Git or gh invocation creates a new three-file PATH-shim directory under persistent state, including invocations already entering through an existing shim, and no path removes these directories. Long-lived homes will accumulate unbounded files; reuse a validated immutable shim or clean invocation-scoped shims safely.

🔧 Fix: Captain: harden strict GitHub routing boundaries
9 issues (8 errors, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:409` - Rejecting submodule-related config and flags does not disable Git's default on-demand recursion. A populated submodule can still fetch its own unvalidated remote with the selected credential; inject `fetch.recurseSubmodules=false` and `submodule.recurse=false` into the authoritative Git context.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:439` - Routing inheritance reads the caller's `FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE` directory even though routing is defined to use canonical `$FM_HOME/config`. A specialized override can copy an unauthorized routing file or remove a valid secondmate file, silently reverting it to legacy credentials; always source this item from `src_home/config`.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-home-seed.sh:567` - The routed clone still activates its profile in the parent shell. Because all projects are cloned before initialization, the last profile contaminates shimmed Git/No Mistakes checks for earlier projects and can misclassify an initialized clone as unrelated; run each clone in a subshell.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:196` - The wrapper refreshes context for `FM_GITHUB_PROJECT_PATH` but starts `no-mistakes axi run` in the caller's unchanged working directory. From another checkout this initializes project A's context and starts or reattaches project B's pipeline under A's routed environment; reject unrelated cwd or execute from the validated project path.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:188` - Only `axi run` revalidates routing. A supported `axi respond` after a profile, login, config-directory, or identity change resumes PR 527's already-bound executor with stale credentials; fail closed on mismatch or establish a lower-layer safe-rebind contract before allowing the continuation.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-config.mjs:413` - The `sanitize` action only reserializes schema-valid input. Token-shaped values remain valid in profile IDs, paths, and identities and are then copied or emitted as metadata; reject recognized credential forms across all string fields before serialization or resolution.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:1099` - Blanket rejection of descendant `gh api` also blocks internal calls from the selected typed `gh-axi`; current supported PR review and issue relation/type operations use REST or GraphQL internally. Preserve raw API denial while defining a repository-scoped trusted descendant contract for typed gh-axi operations.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:1144` - Repository creation is not fully confined to the pre-registration capability: without the flag, a registered project's binding can authorize creation of an otherwise unmapped repository, while flagged `repo create --clone` accepts any non-Git cwd and can clone outside canonical `projects/`. Require the appropriate creation capability and canonical projects directory.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:318` - The reusable-shim installation lock hot-spins without waiting or stale-owner recovery. Concurrent first activation can fail while the installer is merely descheduled, and interruption or a post-lock error can leave strict routing permanently unavailable; use bounded waiting and recover only proven-stale locks.

🔧 Fix: Harden strict GitHub routing continuations and boundaries
9 issues (7 errors, 2 warnings) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:235` - `axi run` can reattach an existing run, but the wrapper refreshes repository storage and overwrites the marker before learning whether a new executor was created. After a routing change, reattachment can therefore retain the old in-memory context while a later `axi respond` matches the new marker; match/fail closed when an active marker exists and refresh only after proving a new run started.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:288` - The gh-axi API exception is authorized by forgeable inherited environment variables and forwards arbitrary `gh api` arguments after validating only the declared outer target. Any descendant can issue another repository's request or a GraphQL mutation; use a non-forgeable exact-parent broker and validate method, endpoint, and repository scope.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:390` - Strict activation accepts ambient `FM_NO_MISTAKES_BINARY` or `FM_GITHUB_NO_MISTAKES_BINARY` after checking only that it is executable. A hostile override can run arbitrary code with the selected profile environment and typed context; resolve and validate one canonical basename-checked executable and ignore production caller overrides.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-home-seed.sh:554` - After sanitized validation, repository and origin inspection uses the exact Git binary again in the unsanitized parent environment. Ambient `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_CONFIG_*` values can spoof repository validity and select a different allowed fork for seeding; perform every source and destination read inside a sanitized scoped subprocess.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:1178` - The pre-registration validator returns immediately when the flag is absent. An unregistered project whose repository or owner binding resolves can therefore run `git clone` to an arbitrary destination without the guarded onboarding path; require an operation-specific capability and destination validation, including the distinct supported secondmate-seed destination.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-config.mjs:386` - Every repository creation now requires `--pre-register-project`, but the resolver accepts that flag only when a project binding already exists. This removes the documented repository/owner-bound known-owner creation path and forces operators to pre-edit `bindings.projects`; confirm that project-binding-only creation is intended or restore a guarded owner/repository route.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:265` - The public `exec` action preserves an ambient `FM_GITHUB_ALLOW_UNREGISTERED_PROJECT=1`, so callers can activate onboarding authority without the parsed `--pre-register-project` flag. Reset this internal state at the public executable boundary and derive it solely from the current invocation's parsed option.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:306` - Stale-lock recovery requires a complete valid `owner` file. A crash after creating the directory but before writing ownership leaves an ownerless lock that is never recoverable; atomically publish ownership or add bounded, age-proven recovery for incomplete locks.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:136` - Concurrent first No Mistakes operations can both observe the marker directory as absent; the losing `mkdir` treats the winner's successful creation as an error. Accept a concurrently created directory and then apply the existing type, symlink, and mode validation.

🔧 Fix: Harden strict GitHub routing and continuation boundaries
10 issues (8 errors, 2 warnings) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:156` - Binary canonicalization runs before checking strict mode. Without routing config, the helper emits only legacy mode, so `no-mistakes-init` reports the command missing instead of preserving absent-config behavior.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:1278` - The parent verifier rejects Node-launched gh-axi while accepting spoofable argv/basename identity. Legitimate internal API calls fail, while another process named `gh-axi` can impersonate the broker; use an authenticated exact-parent mechanism.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-config.mjs:247` - After validating the root repository variables, the GraphQL validator accepts any balanced selection set. Queries can traverse `repository.owner.repositories` and read other repositories, violating the single-repository boundary.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:1220` - Clone and onboarding authority remains inherited environment state for callable `child-*` entrypoints. A direct child invocation can forge the capability, clone root, or unregistered-project flag despite the public `exec` reset.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:280` - The binding used to initialize a new run is discarded, then `record` re-resolves routing after the run. A configuration change during execution can therefore publish a marker for credentials the active executor never received.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:230` - Bare `axi status` can describe another branch, and the status-to-run decision is racy. Concurrent or cross-branch runs can be mistaken for a new executor, allowing incorrect marker publication.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:232` - Only `running` is classified active, although documented active states include `fixing`, `ci`, `awaiting_approval`, and `fix_review`; valid reattachment in those states is refused as indeterminate.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:1220` - `gh repo clone` is allowlisted, but its descendant Git invocation receives no clone capability and is rejected. Confirm support and provide a conventional-destination capability, or explicitly remove it from the supported command surface.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-pr-poll.sh:85` - A profile-less delayed poll checks `FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE` rather than canonical `$FM_HOME/config`. An empty override can hide strict routing and fall through to ambient `gh`.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:339` - The lock directory is visible before owner publication and is considered stale after two seconds without proof. A paused live installer can have its lock removed by a contender, allowing concurrent installation.

🔧 Fix: Harden routed capabilities and run ownership
6 issues (5 errors, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:443` - Invocation authority remains forgeable: callers can create a mode-0600 `.cap.*` in their own writable capability directory using derivable operation, binary, repository, ancestor PID, and start-time values. A direct `child-*` invocation can mint clone, preregistration, or API authority; authenticate the exact broker through a non-forgeable invocation channel.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-config.mjs:249` - GraphQL scope uses an incomplete field blacklist. Queries such as `repository { pullRequest(...) { headRepository { ... } } }` can traverse into another repository because `headRepository` and `baseRepository` are allowed. Use positive, type-aware selection validation.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:1442` - The REST path glob admits arbitrary nested GET endpoints because shell `*` matches slashes. For example, `/repos/owner/repo/forks` exposes other repositories despite the selected-repository boundary. Allowlist the exact read endpoints required by gh-axi.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:239` - `axi status` emits quoted TOON scalars for fields such as `id` and `head`, but these values are not unquoted. Consequently `rev-parse "$NM_RUN_HEAD^{commit}"` fails, strict continuations appear absent, and a new run cannot publish its binding marker. Parse TOON scalars consistently before validation.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:238` - Status-command failure, another branch, and a nonmatching head all return status 2, which the caller treats as proof that no current run exists. A bare status reporting another branch or failing transiently can therefore let `axi run` reattach an existing executor and then publish a fresh marker because `prior_id` was empty. Require an authoritative exact-branch lookup and fail closed when absence is unproven.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:327` - `fm_github_current_pid` returns the lock-owning shell's parent rather than the shell itself. If the installer or No Mistakes wrapper dies while its long-lived caller survives, the lock remains falsely live and strict routing stays unavailable; record the actual lock owner PID.

🔧 Fix: Harden routed brokers and run identity validation
7 issues (5 errors, 2 warnings) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:444` - The loopback broker trusts the PID and start time supplied in request JSON without binding them to the socket peer. Another local process can submit a live descendant's metadata and consume clone or API authority; use an inherited authenticated channel or peer credentials.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:449` - The broker closes after its first authorized descendant request, but one supported gh-axi command can require multiple API calls; `pr view --reviews` fetches reviews and then comments when reviews exist, so the second call fails. Keep authorization bound to the root invocation while issuing one-shot grants per validated child request.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:262` - The runs parser permits only one required and one optional token after the SHA, while documented rows contain date, time, and an optional PR URL. Any PR-bearing history row invalidates the entire absence proof and blocks strict run/respond on normal repositories.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:270` - An active row for the current branch is ignored when its head differs from the worktree, and the function reports the run absent. The wrapper can then initialize and invoke `axi run` against an already-active mismatched executor instead of failing closed as required.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-github-config.mjs:269` - Positive GraphQL validation allows only repository `id`, `issues.totalCount`, and `pullRequests.totalCount`. The configured gh-axi's read-only issue-view augmentation uses `issue(number) { parent ... subIssues ... }`, so strict routing silently drops supported relationship output. Add that exact type-aware read shape.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-config.mjs:295` - FirstMate still accepts `gh-axi issue create/edit --type`, but resolving the type requires the rejected `repository.issueTypes` selection and applying it requires a mutation that policy intentionally denies. Decide whether to support a narrowly typed mutation contract or reject `--type` before launching gh-axi.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:254` - Every status mismatch or failure requests and buffers up to 2,147,483,647 human-readable run-history rows. Long-lived repositories can make routine strict continuations consume excessive memory and time; use an authoritative exact-branch query instead of materializing all history.

🔧 Fix: Harden routed brokers and run identity checks
4 errors still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:440` - The bearer token authenticates only the caller-supplied server: a direct `child-*` caller can launch its own parent loopback broker, choose matching endpoint/PID/identity/token values, and return `ok`, minting clone, preregistration, or API authority outside the trusted public boundary. Authenticate the genuine broker through a channel a direct caller cannot reconstruct.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:1495` - The `updateIssue` path accepts arbitrary global issue/type node IDs and labels them as `FM_GITHUB_REPOSITORY` without proving they came from its validated lookup. This permits cross-repository mutation when broker authority is forged and also preflights legitimate selected-fork mutations against the parent; bind the target and IDs to the authenticated outer repository operation.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:311` - The new mismatch refusal runs after `no_mistakes_head_matches`, which accepts a run head that is any descendant of the worktree HEAD. An active same-branch run at a different commit therefore bypasses the required exact-commit refusal; require equality for pre-existing active reattachment.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:284` - Absence is accepted only when the repository has fewer than 101 total runs. Once history reaches 101 rows, a new branch whose `axi status` reports another branch can never start its first strict run, even when no matching run exists. The current No Mistakes CLI has no branch filter, so establish an authoritative exact-branch contract or confirm that this permanent fail-closed behavior is intended.

🔧 Fix: Harden routed execution and run attribution
3 errors still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:535` - The broker validates only `api` requests; every other descendant `gh` command is executed verbatim. A gh-axi descendant can therefore run credential-output, destructive, or cross-repository commands under the selected profile. Positively allowlist only the exact non-API issue create/view calls required by the authenticated outer operation.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:232` - A first-ever strict run is impossible: `axi status` reports an absence state such as “no runs yet” rather than a four-field run record, but this path classifies that as indeterminate and refuses `axi run`. Handle the supported explicit current-checkout absence result separately from transient status failures.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:453` - Issue-type edit binding assumes the issue number is numeric and exactly `args[2]`. Supported forms such as `issue edit --repo owner/repo 17 --type Bug` or an issue URL leave `issueNumber` empty, so the legitimate issue-ID observation is discarded and the mutation fails. Parse the positional using the outer typed grammar, independent of flag order and URL form.

🔧 Fix: Constrain routed broker and recognize first runs
5 errors still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:494` - The broker generally allows non-API descendants only when their argv exactly matches the outer command, but the configured gh-axi synthesizes calls such as `gh pr view <n> --json ...`. Most ordinary routed gh-axi operations are therefore denied; validate operation-specific descendant shapes instead of comparing argv byte-for-byte.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:533` - The issue-view allowlist rejects `labels` and `assignees`, while the configured gh-axi requests `number,title,state,labels,assignees,id` for `issue edit --type`; the observer also requires an unrequested `url`. Consequently the promised type mutation can never be authorized. Match the actual typed response shape and bind its number/id to the selected repository.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:481` - Repository validation gives `--repo` precedence over an issue URL instead of requiring both selectors to agree. A descendant can pair an allowed `--repo` with a foreign issue URL using an authorized issue number and pass broker validation. Require every supplied repository selector to match the routed repository.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-exec.sh:239` - The explicit-absence parser accepts the status headline without its branch-specific second line and ignores the command's exit status. Truncated output from a transient failure can therefore be treated as proven absence, allowing an unsafe run or reattachment. Require the complete supported output and contract exit status.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:633` - Canonical issue URLs are validated and recorded but then forwarded unchanged to gh-axi, whose issue-edit implementation requires a numeric positional. The newly tested URL form fails before reaching the broker; normalize it to the issue number while preserving the selected repository context.

🔧 Fix: Normalize routed descendants and strengthen absence proof
4 errors still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:524` - Normalized descendants are authorized using only command pair, target number, and repository—not their complete argv. An outer `pr merge 17 --squash` can therefore authorize `pr merge 17 --admin --delete-branch`, while non-targeted commands such as `repo create` can replace positional targets entirely. Replace this fallback with complete operation-specific child schemas; also reject native `issue --type` calls outside the observed-ID mutation flow.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:499` - The normalization map omits required child calls synthesized by supported gh-axi commands: `pr reopen` calls `pr view`, `run cancel` calls `run view`, workflow view/enable/disable call `workflow list`, and `release delete` calls `release view`. These commands are allowlisted but fail at the broker; define the complete operation-specific child contract.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:543` - Ordinary `gh-axi issue create` cannot complete. Its create child is classified as `outer`, but only typed creates classified as `issue-create` record the returned issue number; the mandatory follow-up `issue view <new-number>` is then rejected because `resourceNumbers` is empty. Observe every authorized issue-create response before permitting its exact follow-up view.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:1388` - The wrapper requires `issue transfer <number> <repository>`, while the configured gh-axi requires `issue transfer <number> --to-repo <repository>`. The supported flag is rejected as unknown, and the accepted positional form fails inside gh-axi. Accept and validate `--to-repo`, then authorize only gh-axi's exact synthesized positional child command.

🔧 Fix: Enforce complete routed child operation contracts
5 errors still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:804` - The broker does not forward stdin: the shim sends only argv, and `spawnSync` supplies no input. Routed `gh-axi secret set` and piped `variable set` therefore give the real `gh` EOF, causing failure or an empty value. Add a bounded, non-logging stdin channel tied to the validated operation.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:595` - Generated payload flags are checked only for arity. An outer `--body-file` or release body alias authorizes any descendant `--body`/`--notes` value, allowing mutation text different from the approved input. Capture and compare the derived content rather than accepting any single value.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:497` - The child schema still omits supported transformations: `gh-axi pr merge --method squash` emits `--squash`, while release aliases such as `-d` and `-p` emit long flags, but the parser cannot relate these forms. Valid routed commands are rejected; encode every supported alias and operation-specific translation in one schema.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:1398` - `--to-repo` is stored in the same singleton target as `--repo`. Consequently the documented `-R SOURCE --to-repo DEST` form rejects differing source/destination repositories; without `-R`, only the destination is preflighted while the selector-free child mutates the source inferred from cwd. Track, bind, and write-preflight source and destination separately.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:443` - `typeOperation` recognizes only `--type`, although the allowlisted gh-axi supports `issue edit --no-type` by issuing `updateIssue(...issueTypeId:null)`. The broker rejects that mutation—after gh-axi may already have applied other edits—causing a partial update. Add a repository-bound observed-ID clear-type contract or reject the operation before any mutation.

🔧 Fix: Harden routed stdin and mutation contracts
3 warnings still open:
- ⚠️ `docs/configuration.md:253` - The authoritative broker contract documents only `issue create/edit --type` and says both issue and type IDs are observed, but the implementation now supports `issue edit --no-type` using only an observed issue ID. Update the contract to describe the clear-type authorization path.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:6` - The header claims this library never reads tokens, but routed `secret set` now intentionally buffers and forwards up to 1 MiB of caller-supplied secret data. Narrow the claim to routing credentials and document the transient stdin handling so security audits are not misled.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:518` - The requested single typed operation schema remains split across alias canonicalization, generated-flag authorization, shell option classification, and clear-type validation. Consolidate these tables so future command changes cannot silently diverge across the public validator and descendant broker.

🔧 Fix: Centralize routed GitHub operation policy
3 issues (2 errors, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-operation-schema.mjs:13` - `optionKind()` consults only `publicOptions`, while supported gh-axi options `--fields`, `--reviews`, `--full`, and `--conclusion` appear only in other schema sections and are absent from the shell fallback. Strict routing therefore rejects documented list/view operations before gh-axi runs. Add operation-specific public kinds for these options to the authoritative table.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-operation-schema.json:104` - The `issue:create` observer omits `url`, but the configured gh-axi follows creation with `gh issue view <n> --json number,title,state,url,id`. The broker rejects that exact response shape, so routed `issue create --type` cannot complete. Match the create observer to the actual fields while retaining repository and issue-number binding.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-github-lib.sh:1435` - Every option classification starts a fresh Node process and reparses the schema, adding O(number-of-flags) process startups to each routed gh/gh-axi command. Classify the complete argv in one helper invocation or load the table once per command.

🔧 Fix: Complete and batch routed GitHub operation schema
2 errors still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-operation-schema.mjs:23` - `classifyArgv()` drops options whose operation-specific kind is explicitly `unknown`, causing the shell classifier to fall back to its global legacy switch. Scoped options such as `--comments` and `--remove-type` are consequently accepted on undeclared operations; because the broker ignores these flags and gh-axi may ignore them, an invalid mutating command can still execute. Emit authoritative `unknown` classifications and use fallback only for options absent from the schema.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-github-operation-schema.json:9` - `--no-type` and `--type` have global defaults instead of issue-only mappings, while the broker treats them as globally ignorable. For example, `gh-axi release delete v1 --no-type` can pass validation and perform the deletion despite the invalid option. Scope these flags to `issue:create`/`issue:edit` and ignore them only under the matching typed contract.

🔧 Fix: Scope routed typed options to issue contracts

title: fix(spawn): stop clobbering a project's tracked .claude/settings.local.json
body:
## Problem

`bin/fm-spawn.sh` wrote the claude crewmate turn-end hook by unconditionally overwriting
`<worktree>/.claude/settings.local.json`:

```sh
cat > "$WT/.claude/settings.local.json" <<EOF
{"hooks":{"Stop":[{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"touch '$TURNEND'"}]}]}}
EOF
exclude_path '.claude/settings.local.json'
```

`meshery/meshery` (and `meshery-cloud`) **tracks** `.claude/settings.local.json` - a 72-line file
carrying `enabledMcpjsonServers`, `disabledMcpjsonServers`, a `SessionStart` hook, and several
`PreToolUse` hooks. Every claude spawn into such a worktree truncated that tracked file to a single
line, destroying the project's own configuration inside the worktree.

Observed repeatedly on 2026-07-21/22: four meshery worktrees each showed
` M .claude/settings.local.json` with a `73 +--------` diffstat. It blocked teardown three separate
times (correctly - it is indistinguishable from real uncommitted work) and any crewmate running
`git add -A` would have committed the truncation.

The second, subtler half: the `exclude_path` mitigation appends the path to `.git/info/exclude`,
which only suppresses **untracked** files. For a tracked file git still reports it modified, so the
mitigation silently did nothing in exactly the case that mattered.

## Fix

Follow the precedent the codebase already set for the other harnesses - pi keeps its turn-end
extension in `state/` and grok keeps its hook global under `~/.grok/hooks/`, both deliberately
outside the worktree to avoid polluting the project. Claude's arm was the outlier.

- **Move claude's `Stop` hook out of the worktree entirely.** It now lives in
  `state/<id>.claude-settings.json` and is loaded via `--settings` on the launch command, so the
  worktree's own `.claude/settings.local.json` is never written. A project that tracks that file is
  byte-identical after a spawn; a project without one keeps working unchanged; the turn-end hook
  still fires, so supervision still wakes. Secondmates keep the plain form.
- **Sibling-arm audit.** The only worktree-resident hook writes left are opencode's
  `.opencode/plugins/fm-turn-end.js` and grok's `.fm-grok-turnend`; both are now guarded by
  `refuse_if_tracked`, which stops the spawn rather than clobber a tracked project file.
- **Fix the tracked-vs-untracked assumption at the source.** `exclude_path` is now documented as
  tidiness-only, and `refuse_if_tracked` is the real guard. `prune_obsolete_exclude_entries` removes
  the now-stale `.claude/settings.local.json` line firstmate used to add to the shared
  `.git/info/exclude`, so repos already touched heal over time - those stale lines were actively
  masking tracked-file changes in meshery and meshery-cloud.
- **Guard the abort/unwind path** so a refused spawn only unwinds work it created and never resets
  another task's uncommitted work or a temp root it did not create; git errors during unwind fail
  safe. Teardown cleans `state/<id>.claude-settings.json` at parity with the pi extension.

## Tests

Regression coverage colocated in `tests/`, extending the existing runners rather than adding a new
one:

- `tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh` - a spawn into a worktree where
  `.claude/settings.local.json` is a **tracked file with existing content** leaves that file
  byte-identical (the case that actually bit us), plus the no-file and untracked-file cases and the
  `refuse_if_tracked` sibling-arm behavior.
- `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` - the dirty-copy unwind guard and claude-settings cleanup parity.
- C-locale glyph regression tests pinning `LC_ALL=C` for the composer prompt-classification fix.

## Validation

Validated end-to-end through the no-mistakes pipeline: automated review, tests, docs, and lint all
green. Lint's local run reported only `ShellCheck not found` (an environment gap on the run host,
exit 127 - not a code finding); CI runs the same `bin/fm-lint.sh` with ShellCheck present.

## Notes

- Delivered from a fork because our accounts lack direct push access to `kunchenguid/firstmate`.
- Out of scope and intentionally untouched: worktree allocation ignoring recorded task ownership
  (tracked separately as `fm-worktree-realloc-unlanded`), which touches the same file.

title: fix: detect no-mistakes pipeline stalls
body:
## Intent Build automatic watcher-side no-mistakes stall detection in firstmate so the owning supervisor wakes when an attributed pipeline run is silently wedged. Detect running or fixing steps with no step transition or crew status progress beyond a configurable 15-minute default, awaiting_approval or fix_review gates beyond a configurable 8-minute default, and run step/status advancement with no crew status-file write. Reuse the existing watcher slow-check machinery and shared classifier rather than a daemon or parallel wake path, preserve home-local task ownership, name run id, step, and task in the wake, and add focused synthetic coverage plus concise architecture documentation. ## What Changed - Add watcher slow-check detection for stalled active no-mistakes steps, overdue approval/review gates, and run advancement without a matching crew status-file update; enqueue durable, ownership-local wakes that name the run, step, and task. - Add `fm-crew-state.sh --stall-snapshot` parsing and per-task detector state to track attributed run/step status, elapsed time, status-file progress, and alert deduplication. - Document configurable active and parked thresholds, and add focused crew-state and watcher stall-detection coverage. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the change is bounded to watcher-side stall classification, preserves home-local ownership, and the reviewed paths satisfy the stated detection criteria. ## Testing On the clean target checkout, focused synthetic coverage passed for active, parked, silent-advance, threshold, deduplication, and shared run-step parsing behavior. A live watcher verification then showed the real watcher emitting and durably queuing named `check` wakes for a 901-second running step, a 481-second fix-review gate, and a run advance without a crew status-file write; the transcript is attached.
Evidence: Live watcher wake and durable-queue transcript ```text === active === watcher output: check: no-mistakes stall: run run-active step review task task (running unchanged for 901s) durable queue: 1784783738 1 check no-mistakes-stall:task check: no-mistakes stall: run run-active step review task task (running unchanged for 901s) === parked === watcher output: check: no-mistakes stall: run run-parked step fix-review task task (fix_review unchanged for 481s) durable queue: 1784783739 1 check no-mistakes-stall:task check: no-mistakes stall: run run-parked step fix-review task task (fix_review unchanged for 481s) === silent === watcher output: check: no-mistakes silent advance: run run-silent step review task task (run changed without a crew status write) durable queue: 1784783740 1 check no-mistakes-stall:task check: no-mistakes silent advance: run run-silent step review task task (run changed without a crew status write) ```

Compare only stable run/step/status identity here, keeping duration solely for age calculation. - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:360` - Required behavior: “Detect running or fixing steps with no step transition or crew status progress beyond a configurable 15-minute default.” For an attributed `fixing` run without an active step row, the new fallback emits duration `0`; lines 139–145 then reset its effective start to `now` on every check, so it can never exceed the threshold. Preserve a first-seen/start timestamp when the CLI provides no step duration. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:130` - The detector writes its `advanced`/`stalled` suppression marker before `fm-watch.sh` durably appends the wake. If queue append fails, a restart sees the marker and suppresses the only escalation. Commit detector state only after successful queue append, or retain a pending marker that is retried. 🔧 Fix: Fix no-mistakes stall detection state handling 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:323` - Required criterion: “awaiting_approval or fix_review gates beyond a configurable 8-minute default.” The fixture-format value `awaiting_agent: parked 2m10s` is parsed as `2m10` after only stripping the final `s`, fails the numeric check, and becomes `0`. A gate already waiting longer than eight minutes is therefore timed from this watcher's first observation instead of its actual gate age, delaying escalation after watcher restart. - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:155` - The required 8-minute gate condition is independent of the active-step clause’s “no step transition or crew status progress.” This shared anchor resets a parked gate’s age to the latest crew-status-file write, so recurring status writes can defer an unchanged awaiting_approval/fix_review gate indefinitely rather than surfacing it once the gate itself exceeds the parked threshold. 🔧 Fix: Fix parked gate stall timing 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:148` - Required criterion: “Detect running or fixing steps with no step transition or crew status progress beyond a configurable 15-minute default.” On the first slow check of an already-15+-minute active step, the new marker branch writes state then returns at this hunk (`[ "$is_gate" = 1 ] || return 0`), deferring the wake until the next slow-check interval. With the default 300-second cadence, a known stalled step can remain silent for roughly 20 minutes; evaluate the current duration/status age on that first observation instead. 🔧 Fix: Fix immediate active-step stall detection 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:355` - Required criterion: “awaiting_approval or fix_review gates beyond a configurable 8-minute default.” A supported parked scalar-gate run can retain top-level `status: running`; this fallback emits `running` as the snapshot status, so `nm_stall_check_task` treats it as a 15-minute active step (and with no `awaiting_agent` age, first-seen timing) instead of the parked-gate path. title: feat(bin): add fm-relaunch.sh for on-demand session resume
body:
## Intent

Developer (acting as an autonomous crewmate managed by "firstmate") tasked the agent with converting a hand-built prototype (a launchd LaunchAgent plist plus a payload script that opens Terminal running `claude`) into a proper, tracked repo tool: `bin/fm-relaunch.sh` with install/run/status/uninstall subcommands. The core requirement was safety: the generated launchd job must never self-trigger (no RunAtLoad, StartInterval, StartCalendarInterval, or watch-path keys) and can only fire via explicit `launchctl kickstart/start`, since the captain explicitly did not want an unattended auto-starting session. Requirements included idempotent install, macOS-only support with clear failure elsewhere, a colocated test file mocking system commands (launchctl/osascript/uname/id) that specifically asserts the forbidden auto-trigger keys are absent, documentation in `docs/relaunch-tool.md` per the "one-owner rule" (avoiding duplicating narrative in the script header or AGENTS.md), and cleanly superseding the existing same-named LaunchAgent without leaving conflicting duplicate jobs. The developer also required the work go through the `no-mistakes` validation pipeline (review, test, lint, document, push, PR) before completion, explicitly avoiding `--yes` so ask-user decisions remain with the human, and directed the agent to escalate rather than fix infrastructure blockers (spend limits, push permission errors) itself. A real security finding (AppleScript injection via unescaped `$quoted_cd` in the osascript call) was caught and fixed during the pipeline's review step. The developer (captain) ultimately resolved a GitHub push-permission blocker by forking and pushing manually, opening PR #894.</summary>
</invoke>

## What Changed

- Add `bin/fm-relaunch.sh` with install/run/status/uninstall subcommands, generating a launchd LaunchAgent that opens Terminal running `claude` — the plist deliberately omits RunAtLoad, StartInterval, StartCalendarInterval, and watch-path keys so the job only fires via explicit `launchctl kickstart/start`, macOS-only with a clear failure message elsewhere.
- Fix an AppleScript injection risk by passing `FM_HOME` to `osascript` as an argv parameter instead of interpolating it into the quoted script string.
- Add `tests/fm-relaunch.test.sh`, mocking `launchctl`/`osascript`/`uname`/`id` to cover install idempotency, safety-key absence, and subcommand behavior.
- Document the tool in `docs/relaunch-tool.md` and add a row for it in `docs/scripts.md`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Small self-contained script+tests+docs; core safety invariant (no launchd auto-trigger keys) verified present and tested; prior AppleScript injection already fixed via argv passing.

## Testing

Ran the colocated mocked test suite (all 13 assertions pass, including the no-auto-trigger-key assertion) and additionally did a real, non-mocked install/status/uninstall cycle against actual launchctl/launchd on this macOS machine to confirm the generated LaunchAgent plist truly has no RunAtLoad/StartInterval/StartCalendarInterval/WatchPaths/QueueDirectories/KeepAlive keys and cleanly unloads; did not fire cmd_fire for real since that opens a live Terminal window/osascript trust dialog, which the mocked test already exercises safely.

title: fix(watcher): make Linux PID identity clock-drift stable
body:
## Intent

Prevent a live, healthy Firstmate watcher from being rejected by process-identity checks when WSL2 or another Linux host adjusts its wall-clock or boot-time reference.

## Background

On WSL2, `ps lstart` changed for the same live PID after NTP synchronization or suspend.
Observed identities shifted from `07:09:22` when recorded to `07:09:27` on a live read, and a later watcher shifted from `07:11:22` to `07:11:33`.
The drift recurred after watcher restarts, causing the turn-end guard and continuity gate to treat a healthy watcher as mismatched.

## What Changed

- Use Linux `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 (`starttime`, in clock ticks since boot) together with the full `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` bytes.
- Split the `stat` record after its final `)` so process names containing spaces or parentheses parse correctly.
- Fail closed on Linux when the required `/proc` identity data is unavailable instead of falling back to drift-prone `ps lstart`.
- Keep the locale-pinned `ps lstart` plus command fallback for non-Linux hosts such as macOS.
- Return failure for omitted, invalid, zero, or missing PIDs.

## Compatibility and migration

Existing consumers compare the identity as an opaque string and require no format-specific changes.
A legacy `lstart` identity mismatches once without producing a false healthy result.
The supported watcher restart arm replaces that lock with a fresh watcher and writes the stable Linux identity.

## Regression coverage

- Repeated identity reads remain stable across simulated boot-time changes.
- PID reuse changes the identity.
- Invalid and missing PIDs fail.
- Linux never consults `ps` when `/proc` data is missing.
- A process name containing a closing parenthesis parses from the final delimiter.
- A live watcher lock remains matched while simulated `ps lstart` output shifts by 11 seconds.
- A real watcher with a legacy identity is rejected safely and repaired by `fm-watch-arm.sh --restart`.

## Validation

- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed --base origin/main`: 10 watcher/wake/lock scripts passed with 0 failures.
- `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh`: passed on WSL2, including the live lock and legacy migration cases.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh`: passed with the repository-pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0 across the canonical script set.
- No-mistakes automated review, targeted test, documentation, and lint validation completed successfully before its upstream push failed because this contributor has read-only access.

## Risk assessment

Low.
The behavior change is limited to Linux process-identity collection and strengthens fail-closed handling.
The non-Linux fallback and opaque consumer contract remain intact.

✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 4 issues found → auto-fixed (3) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:327` - `active_identity_count` treats every non-regular backlog path as an empty store because `[ -f ]` is also false for directories, FIFOs, and broken symlinks. Archived verification can therefore succeed and permit scout cleanup while the active backlog is invalid and was never checked for collisions. Return zero only when the path is genuinely absent; reject unsafe or unreadable active-store paths. - 🚨 `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:396` - `hold_reason` is still TOON-encoded. A malformed archived header containing `(hold: ) (hold-kind: captain)` yields an empty reason rendered as `""`; both shell predicates pass, so the record is accepted. Decode the field or explicitly reject the encoded empty value. - 🚨 `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:280` - The extractor accepts non-empty whitespace-only raw lines, which tasks-axi normalizes to empty lines before digest validation. Changing a canonical blank decision line to spaces therefore produces a stable archive that still verifies, contradicting the lossless canonical-record contract. Reject whitespace-only raw lines or validate the extracted record before parsing. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:505` - The active identity is rechecked before `verify_archived_resolution`, but that validation invokes another hash subprocess and the final pass checks only the archive. Repeat the active check after final structured/archive validation or use a coherent store lock. 🔧 Fix: Harden archive-aware decision verification 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:403` - The new decode loses the distinction between TOON's missing sentinel `-` and the valid quoted value `"-"`. Both `command_hold` and tasks-axi accept `--reason -`; after retention, this block decodes `"-"` to `-` and line 408 rejects it, making a writer-created decision unusable by complete, verify, resolve retry, and scout teardown. Check the raw unquoted sentinel before decoding, then reject only a decoded empty string. 🔧 Fix: Preserve quoted dash hold reasons 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:249` - `semanticLine` strips trailing carriage returns while `extractRecord` accepts and copies CR-terminated nonblank lines into the parser view. title: feat(bin): add verified local Markdown previews
body:
## What Changed - Add a fail-closed Markdown preview helper with sanitized rendering, bounded resource use, current-file verification, tokenized loopback serving, and reliable cleanup. - Require previews for generated or updated Markdown and document the helper, its Python 3 requirement, and test-runner integration. - Add comprehensive preview regression coverage while hardening Pi TypeScript probing and isolating Orca bootstrap tests from host binaries. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The latest changes correctly preserve existing preview failures while normalizing descriptor I/O, close, and loopback server-construction errors without introducing a material source risk. ## Testing Baseline diff/status inspection, focused preview and related regression tests, and a live end-user rendering all completed successfully; the screenshot shows formatted Markdown with raw script text escaped and the remote image omitted, the helper reported success, and its loopback server was closed afterward. The in-app browser was unavailable, so the visual evidence was captured with local headless Chrome instead. - Evidence: Rendered Firstmate Markdown preview (local file: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY7DACYHC79Z810G6TNF0G39/markdown-preview.png)
Evidence: Successful preview and lifecycle evidence ok - previewed preview-fixture.md preview server closed after delivery (curl exit 7) ```text ok - previewed preview-fixture.md ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
⏭️ **intent** - skipped ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Rebase** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `AGENTS.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main 🔧 Fix applied. ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed (6) ✅ - ⚠️ `AGENTS.md:49` - The mandatory security-sensitive preview workflow has no repository-owned renderer or verification helper. Each harness must independently interpret sanitization, remote-resource blocking, current-file verification, and cleanup, producing inconsistent guarantees or making delivery impossible on a clean host. Decide whether to add one pinned, fail-safe preview helper or skill and reference it here. - ⚠️ `tests/fm-pi-primary-types.test.sh:9` - The `tsc --version` probe runs before checking whether the Pi package exists. A host without Pi but with a broken, wrapped, or unrelated `tsc` now fails instead of taking the documented Pi-not-installed skip path. Resolve and validate `PI_PACKAGE_DIR` before probing the compiler. 🔧 Fix: Captain: Add fail-safe previews and package-first Pi checks 3 issues (1 error, 2 warnings) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:569` - After a verified browser fetch, the helper still requires the opener process to exit within one second and then terminates it. `xdg-open` can run its selected handler in the foreground, so a successfully loaded preview may be reported as failed and its newly launched browser terminated. Decide whether verified delivery should constitute success independently of opener lifetime. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:176` - Every unmatched `[` scans the remainder of the line for `](`, with similar repeated scans for unmatched emphasis delimiters. Bracket-heavy input is therefore quadratic, while rendering occurs before the timeout and accepts files up to 8 MiB. Use a single-pass or otherwise bounded delimiter scan. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:515` - Server verification reads at most `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES + 1`, but HTML escaping can expand an accepted source to several times that size. A valid source below the 8 MiB limit can therefore be truncated during verification and falsely rejected as a content mismatch. Read against the bounded rendered-body length or enforce an explicit rendered-output limit before serving. 🔧 Fix: Captain: Harden preview delivery and rendering bounds 6 issues (1 error, 5 warnings) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:538` - `urllib.request.urlopen` honors proxy environment variables, so local verification can send the tokenized loopback URL to an external proxy and falsely fail when loopback is not exempted. Use a proxy-disabled opener or a direct loopback connection for verification. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:643` - If `thread.start()` raises, cleanup calls `server.shutdown()` even though `serve_forever()` never started; `BaseServer.shutdown()` can then wait indefinitely. Track whether the thread started and call only `server_close()` otherwise. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:178` - The delimiter budget does not cover counting a backtick run. For a large unmatched run, each successive backtick recounts most of the remaining run, making rendering quadratic before the serving timeout begins. Consume the whole unmatched run at once or include this scan in the budget. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:73` - The fence regex combines overlapping whitespace-capable groups before an end anchor, causing quadratic backtracking for a tilde fence followed by a long whitespace tail and a final backtick. Parse the fence tail separately or make the groups non-overlapping. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:357` - Nested blockquotes recursively invoke `render_blocks` without a depth bound, so roughly 1,000 nested markers can raise an uncaught `RecursionError` from a small accepted file. Render iteratively or reject excessive nesting with `PreviewError`. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:432` - The 64 MiB rendered-output limit is checked only after all block and table output has been accumulated, joined, and encoded. A wide accepted table can therefore allocate hundreds of megabytes before rejection. Enforce an output or cell budget during rendering. 🔧 Fix: Harden preview verification and rendering bounds 6 warnings still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:350` - Each fenced-block line rebuilds a marker-sized closing prefix. An accepted file with a multi-megabyte opening fence and many short body lines therefore performs quadratic allocation and work. Reuse `marker` directly in `startswith` or cache the prefix once. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:76` - The lazy heading body followed by overlapping `\s*#*\s*` suffixes can backtrack quadratically on a heading containing a long whitespace run before a non-matching suffix. Parse trailing heading markers in one pass or make the groups non-overlapping. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:100` - `RenderBuffer` limits bytes but not part count. Millions of tiny accepted blocks can remain below 64 MiB of output while `split()` and `parts` retain millions of Python objects, consuming hundreds of megabytes. Add a line/block/part budget or coalesce output incrementally. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:166` - `urlsplit` raises `ValueError` for malformed targets such as an unmatched IPv6 bracket, so one malformed Markdown link produces an uncaught traceback instead of being rendered without an unsafe href. Catch parser errors and return `None`. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:310` - Table detection applies the column limit before confirming that the following line is a divider. Ordinary prose containing `|` followed by a non-table line with over 1,024 delimited fields is therefore rejected as an oversized table. Enforce the limit only after recognizing a valid divider row. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:414` - The 64-level quote bound still copies the nearly complete captured line at every recursive level. A valid 8 MiB line with 64 nested quote markers can retain roughly 512 MiB before output budgeting applies. Strip quote prefixes iteratively or include retained input size in the budget. 🔧 Fix: Bound Markdown parser work and retained memory 2 warnings still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:132` - `read_source()` performs a blocking `os.open(..., O_RDONLY)` before validating that the descriptor is regular. A FIFO, including a path swapped to one, can therefore hang the supposedly bounded helper indefinitely. Open nonblocking and then validate the descriptor type. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:194` - The new byte and part budgets apply only after `render_inline()` has accumulated and joined its private lists. One accepted 8 MiB line containing dense short markup can retain millions of fragments and substantial object overhead before a single `RenderBuffer.append()` occurs. Apply incremental byte/fragment limits inside inline rendering or coalesce bounded chunks. 🔧 Fix: Bound source opening and inline rendering 2 warnings still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:180` - Only `os.open` is translated to `PreviewError`; failures from `os.fstat`, `os.read`, or `os.close` escape as raw tracebacks instead of the documented controlled preview failure. Normalize descriptor I/O errors while preserving existing `PreviewError` exceptions. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py:812` - Loopback socket creation or binding can raise `OSError` from `PreviewServer(state)`, but `main()` does not catch it, so an expected serving failure produces a traceback. Wrap server construction as `PreviewError` and retain cleanup for partially initialized state. 🔧 Fix: Normalize preview I/O and server failures ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - Inspected `git diff 68ed7ed2355619749c6ee2bb91b7298dee420df8..37b94216fea0b795e92676b45b1c85362c638d98` to establish intent and affected test scope. - `tests/fm-markdown-preview.test.sh` - `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` - `tests/fm-pi-primary-types-order.test.sh` - `tests/fm-pi-primary-types.test.sh` (expected environment skip because installed TypeScript is older than version 5) - `bin/fm-markdown-preview.py --timeout 30 --opener /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY7DACYHC79Z810G6TNF0G39/capture-url-opener.sh /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY7DACYHC79Z810G6TNF0G39/preview-fixture.md` - Rendered the live loopback URL using `google-chrome --headless --window-size=1440,1000 --screenshot=...` and visually inspected the resulting PNG. - Verified the loopback URL was unreachable after delivery using `curl --noproxy '*' --silent --show-error --max-time 1 "$preview_url"`. - Checked cleanup with `git status --short`.
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Lint** - 1 warning - ⚠️ linter found issues (exit code 1)

title: feat: add durable founder communications and intake controls
body:
## Intent

Implement opt-in, durable one-bot/one-chat two-lane Telegram founder communications for Firstmate. Restore ordinary authenticated two-way conversation first with an ordered durable inbox, prompt same-channel acknowledgments, substantive reply correlation, edit/reply identity preservation, and normal content-appropriate routing; add informational PRE, DURING, and POST lifecycle delivery only after conversation proof, project-grouped stable versioned approval reminders and authenticated one-use button or numbered decisions with existing destructive, irreversible, credential, and security-sensitive authority boundaries; fail closed on delivery ambiguity; add lane-isolated containment, diagnosis, repair, revalidation, and restore incidents; enforce assignment, promotion, and completion gates while grandfathering existing work and preserving opt-out and all supported runtime behavior; use secret-safe canonical HTML rendering, 4096-byte splitting, content-bound dedupe, atomic private records, restart-safe retries, and fake-only deterministic tests. Do not activate or replace the live Telegram relay or run authority-bearing real canaries; post-merge activation and real conversation, lifecycle, and decision canaries remain a separate authorized phase. Include deterministic test-only corrections for the pre-existing scheduler wall-clock oracle and watcher fake-peer readiness race without changing production timing.

## What Changed
- Adds `fm-founder-brief` and related Telegram plumbing for durable two-lane founder communications, including ordered inbox handling, reply/edit correlation, content-appropriate routing, and lifecycle delivery.
- Introduces control-plane and repository-intake scripts, docs, and examples for stable versioned approvals, assignment/promotion/completion gates, and intake-backed coordination.
- Expands and adjusts the test suite plus watcher/fleet helpers to cover the new flows and keep the scheduler and watcher checks deterministic.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Captain, the patch is narrowly scoped to callback-recovery hardening and incident recording, and I did not find a source-verifiable regression in the updated paths.

## Testing

Exercised the founder communications lanes plus watcher, scheduler, control-plane, intake, and backend regressions; everything completed successfully and the resulting evidence was saved under `/var/folders/dl/rb_70p0127x__v6gl9wbvgs40000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY73BS989EPW3GF0S29JV5VA`.

title: feat: add fm.telegram.v1 transport core and support tooling
body:
## Intent Establish the P1 foundation for the required full Telegram product with a harness-neutral versioned fm.telegram.v1 protocol, complete exact bot/home/chat/sender authenticated envelopes, canonical payload correlation, safe plain-text-first rendering and deterministic size chunking, and a secret-safe Bot API abstraction with truthful positive Message postconditions and explicit definitive, retryable, ownership-conflict, and ambiguous outcomes. Include deterministic fake coverage for long polling, webhook inspection, send/edit/delete/callback operations, malformed responses, strict getUpdates 409 ownership failure, bounded 429 retry-after, 5xx, connection failure before write, and post-write timeout ambiguity. Keep this branch narrowly limited to new transport contract, Telegram API, normalization, rendering, fake endpoint modules, and focused tests. Do not modify or activate adapters, SQLite state, supervision, lifecycle, decisions, buttons, the existing founder-brief runtime, pollers, offsets, credentials, live Telegram, daemons, deployment, or merge behavior. Review should focus on transport semantics, correlation, failure honesty, and security diagnostics; Pi and Claude Code remain required later adapters consuming the same protocol with captain-visible parity. ## What Changed - Added the `fm.telegram.v1` transport primitives: authenticated envelopes, canonical payload correlation, plain-text-first rendering, deterministic chunking, and truthful positive `Message` postconditions. - Added a secret-safe Bot API abstraction plus deterministic fake coverage for long polling, webhook inspection, send/edit/delete/callback flows, malformed responses, strict `getUpdates` 409 ownership failure, bounded 429 retry-after, 5xx, connection failures before write, and post-write timeout ambiguity. - Added the supporting control-plane/repository-intake scripts, shell wrappers, docs, examples, and focused transport tests needed to exercise the new foundation. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, this patch is narrowly scoped to the remaining envelope-presence edge case and its tests, and the new validation now fails closed for malformed present reply metadata without changing the broader transport contract. ## Testing I verified the worktree boundary, ran the focused Telegram transport test suite, and then exercised the client against a real loopback fake server plus deterministic failure injection; after correcting one missing `PYTHONPATH` in the manual check, the success path and the required ownership-conflict, retry-after cap, 5xx, before-write, after-write, malformed-response, and definitive-rejection cases all behaved as intended.

title: chore: no-mistakes(document): clarify decision-key parser and scaffold key-position doc contracts
body:
## Intent Fix two silent information-loss defects in firstmate's own supervision and record-keeping layer, in one PR. Defect 1: _fm_decision_key in bin/fm-classify-lib.sh read only the text before the first colon when looking for a [key=] token, but the ordinary crewmate scaffold in bin/fm-brief.sh told crewmates to 'add the same [key=]' without fixing the position, so status files already written carry it AFTER the colon. Every such line folded onto the key 'default', and with two concurrent open decisions the second dropped the first from the open set via _fm_decision_drop - a captain decision silently disappearing from the durable inventory while appearing answered (reproduced live: bin/fm-decision-hold.sh complete refused with 'open structured decision .../default has no captain-held inventory entry'). Required both halves: (a) widen the parser so already-written status files read correctly, keeping the existing slug validation (''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._-]* returns 1) and keeping a token before the colon winning when both positions carry one; (b) make the scaffold emit the canonical key-before-colon form so it stops contradicting the secondmate charter template at bin/fm-brief.sh:172 which already uses 'working [key=]: ...'. The task explicitly asked me to make a judgment call on prose that incidentally contains '[key=' and to justify it. I deliberately BOUNDED the widening instead of searching anywhere in the line: the token is accepted only before the first colon (canonical, wins) or as a standalone trailing token at the end of the line (compatibility). A key quoted mid-sentence stays prose, and a trailing bracket whose contents are not a valid slug is also treated as prose (key 'default') rather than dropping the line out of the fold. Rationale: the dangerous direction is spurious CLOSING - an unbounded search would let any note mentioning a key silently close a real decision, which is the same class of loss this fix exists to stop. Asymmetry between the two positions is deliberate: a malformed slug before the colon is a malformed key and is still rejected, while an incidental trailing bracket is prose and must not delete the event from the fold. That decision required deliberately changing one existing assertion in tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh, which asserted that 'resolved: docs still mention [key=q1]' must NOT close q1 - structurally identical to the repro line that must now resolve, so no parser can satisfy both. I moved that fixture's prose token mid-sentence, where the guarantee still holds, and added a dedicated test covering the exact three-line repro plus position precedence and slug rejection. The scaffold wording also now names the valid slug characters so a crewmate is less likely to copy the literal placeholder (a malformed key drops the line from the fold - a pre-existing adjacent gap I deliberately did NOT change, because the task pinned the existing validation behavior). Defect 2: bin/fm-watch-arm.sh appended its lifecycle record to state/.watch-cycle-exits.log ONLY on exit. It traps HUP/TERM/INT (reason=arm-interrupted), but SIGKILL and process-group kills cannot be trapped, so those cycles vanished leaving no record - the one death mode the ledger most needs to explain (observed live 2026-07-23: the arm task for watcher pid 85879 was killed and zero of 51 ledger records mention it). Required: make a cycle that dies without running its traps detectable from the ledger, by writing an OPEN record when the cycle begins and resolving it at close. Implementation follows the suggested approach: cycle_begin publishes the row (ended_at=0, exit_code=open, reason=cycle-open, lock_after=pending, successor=none) and close rewrites that row in place with the same awk-rewrite machinery cycle_mark_predecessor_successor already uses, so one row per cycle still holds and the classified record shape is unchanged. Hard constraints honored deliberately: the field order asserted at tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh:855 is preserved (open rows carry the full field shape); the live e2e greps (reason=actionable-signal.*successor=started:, unexpected-clean-exit, arm-interrupted, nonzero-exit|signal-exit) still match; concurrent arms still serialize through CYCLE_LOG_LOCK (now via one shared bounded cycle_log_lock helper) and the bounded rotation still cannot corrupt a record rewrite. The rewrite is identified by arm pid AND start stamp so a reused pid's abandoned row is never overwritten; values reach awk through the environment rather than -v so no field can be reinterpreted as an escape; a successor already stamped onto an open row by the next arm survives the close so linking and closing cannot race; and if the row was rotated away or the rewrite fails it falls back to a plain append, keeping the header's standing contract that the ledger is diagnostic evidence, bounded and best-effort, and never stalls an otherwise healthy watcher cycle. Docs updated per the repo's one-owner rule: docs/watcher-continuity.md owns the record contract and now states the open-then-rewritten lifecycle, with docs/architecture.md:56 left as a cross-reference to it; the exact detection command (grep 'exit_code=open') lives once, in the script header that owns mechanics. Verification done before this run: bin/fm-lint.sh clean; all 40 suites in the changed scope green (FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=40 failed=0, one pre-existing environment gate skip for a missing Pi package); fm-bearings-snapshot, fm-fleet-snapshot-view and fm-afk-return re-run separately as status-fold consumers; and a counterfactual run proving the new ledger test fails against the pre-fix arm script with 'not ok - a running cycle published no open ledger record'. This is safety infrastructure, so the standing constraints were: change no other behavior, prefer deterministic and idempotent behavior that fails closed, bin/*.sh must pass shellcheck via bin/fm-lint.sh, and tests must extend the existing colocated scripts rather than introduce a new runner. ## What Changed 92c9919 no-mistakes(document): clarify decision-key parser and scaffold key-position doc contracts 7b6ba5b no-mistakes(review): retire only ledger rows the arm itself published f7f6344 no-mistakes(review): retire an arm's stranded open ledger row on next cycle dca5225 no-mistakes(review): bound open ledger rows and restore unkeyed resolve guidance 9d5e5fb fix: read decision keys after the colon and keep killed watcher cycles in the ledger ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: Every defect raised across the four rounds is now genuinely fixed with a colocated regression test for each invariant and only an info-level hygiene item remains, but the branch still carries a deliberate, human-accepted behavior change to the authoritative status-decision fold plus new read-modify-write paths on the watcher arm's cycle path, so it warrants one notch of caution rather than being treated as well-bounded and unambiguous. ## Testing Ran the seven targeted suites that own the changed behavior (fm-watch-triage, fm-watcher-lock twice for flake detection, fm-brief, fm-decision-hold-lifecycle, fm-bearings-snapshot, fm-fleet-snapshot-view, fm-afk-return) — all green — and then demonstrated both defects end-to-end through the real CLI surfaces with the pre-fix commit pinned into a scratch bin/ tree as a side-by-side counterfactual: the pre-fix parser drops one of two concurrent captain decisions to a single `default` row and makes `fm-decision-hold.sh complete` refuse with the exact message from the live incident, while the fixed parser keeps both under their own keys and passes the gate; and a SIGKILLed arm leaves an empty ledger on the pre-fix arm versus one `exit_code=open reason=cycle-open` row that the documented grep finds on the fixed arm, with a normally-ending cycle still closing to exactly one classified row. No visual artifact applies: the change touches shell scripts, a status-file parser, an append-only TSV ledger, and generated brief text, so the end-user surface is the CLI transcript itself and that is what the artifacts capture. The four live-e2e suites that grep the ledger reasons are opt-in gated on real harness binaries (FM_PI_LIVE_E2E / FM_CLAUDE_LIVE_E2E) and were not run; the equivalent successor-linkage assertion is covered locally in fm-watcher-lock. Scratch trees were removed and the worktree is clean.
