Suggested fix: mirror the close rewrite's guard by scoping the match to start stamps this process actually published — e.g. record the first `cycle_started_at` in a `cycle_first_started_at` global and require `substr($4, 12) + 0 >= ENVIRON["FM_CYCLE_FLOOR"] + 0`, which is O(1) and sound because a recycled-PID predecessor necessarily started before this process's first cycle. Note the new fixture seeds `started_at=111` (tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh:1013), so it would need a stamp inside this process's lifetime — the test already waits for and can read the arm's first published row. While there, the pass rewrites and `mv`s the whole ledger on every cycle_begin even when nothing matched; an `exit 1`-when-no-match guard like the close rewrite's at :270 would skip that. Raising rather than fixing because it contradicts a criterion the intent marks as required. 🔧 Fix: retire only ledger rows the arm itself published 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch-arm.sh:305` - `cycle_open_stamps` is only ever reset inside `cycle_supersede_stranded_rows` (:220 and :222); `cycle_log_append` never removes a stamp when it successfully closes that cycle's row at :305. So after a normal close the stamp lingers, and the next `cycle_begin` passes the shell guard at :188 and runs the full awk pass over the ledger plus a complete temp-file write, finds nothing (the row is no longer `exit_code=open`), exits 1, and resets. Two consequences, neither a correctness bug: the variable's documented meaning at :113 ("start stamps THIS process published and has not reconciled yet") is inaccurate in the common case, and an arm that attaches across many successors pays a read + write of the ledger (up to FM_WATCH_CYCLE_LOG_MAX_BYTES, default 256KB) on every cycle_begin when the overwhelmingly common case has nothing to reconcile. The human's round-3 instruction also asked for this explicitly: "drop a stamp from it once its row is closed or superseded" - the implementation drops on superseded but not on closed. Fix: in `cycle_log_append`, when `closed=1`, strip `" $cycle_started_at "` from `cycle_open_stamps`; the guard at :188 then short-circuits and the awk only runs when a close actually failed. Do NOT drop it on the `closed=0` fallback-append path at :309 - there the original open row may still exist and must stay eligible for retirement.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` — includes the new `test_decision_key_positions` and the deliberately-moved prose-token fixture - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh` — run twice to check the new kill-timing tests for flakiness; both runs green, including `an untrappable kill leaves one unclosed cycle record...`, `open cycle rows stay inside the ledger cap...`, and `an arm retires only the open rows it published...` - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-brief.test.sh` — scaffold wording assertions for the unkeyed-blocker resolution branch - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh tests/fm-fleet-snapshot-view.test.sh tests/fm-afk-return.test.sh` — the status-fold consumers affected by the parser change - Manual e2e (defect 1): built a pinned pre-fix `bin/` tree from `git show 68ed7ed:bin/fm-classify-lib.sh` and ran the same scenario through both trees — `fm-decision-hold.sh hold` x2, `fm-fleet-snapshot.sh --json | jq '.tasks[].hints.open_decisions'`, `fm-bearings-snapshot.sh --json`, then `fm-decision-hold.sh complete sample-route-review route legacy` - Manual e2e (defect 2): built a pinned pre-fix tree from `git show 68ed7ed:bin/fm-watch-arm.sh`, armed a real watcher via `bin/fm-watch-arm.sh` in both trees, `kill -KILL <arm-pid>`, then ran the header's documented detection command `grep 'exit_code=open' state/.watch-cycle-exits.log`; also drove a normally-closing cycle and counted rows per arm pid - Manual check: generated real briefs with `bin/fm-brief.sh demo-task sample` and `bin/fm-brief.sh sm-demo --secondmate alpha` from both trees and compared the emitted decision-key instructions - Manual check: `_fm_decision_key` position matrix across canonical/trailing/precedence/mid-sentence-prose/malformed-trailing/malformed-slug inputs, sourced from both the base and fixed `fm-classify-lib.sh` - Manual check: `status_open_decisions` on a trailing-key open plus a bare `resolved:` to confirm the documented accepted consequence (decision resurfaces open rather than being lost)
⚠️ **Document** - 1 info - ℹ️ `.agents/skills/firstmate-codexapp/SKILL.md:64` - `.agents/skills/firstmate-codexapp/SKILL.md:64` carries an independent copy of the crewmate status protocol ("Use only these prefixes for status changes: working:, needs-decision:, blocked:, paused:, done:, failed:") inside a Codex Desktop prompt template. Now that the canonical scaffold in bin/fm-brief.sh emits `needs-decision [key=<slug>]:`, "use only these prefixes" reads as forbidding the key token, so the two surfaces diverge. I deliberately did not edit it: a bare `needs-decision:` still folds correctly onto the `default` key, the Desktop path is a single supervised thread where one open decision is the norm, and rewriting the block to teach key grammar would create a second full copy of a contract owned by bin/fm-classify-lib.sh rather than consolidating. The consolidating fix - reducing that line to a pointer at the fm-brief.sh scaffold contract - touches a skill surface unrelated to this change, so it is worth a separate follow-up decision.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: feat: add live task-list board

## Intent Build v1 of a live, watchable read-only board of firstmate's task and priority list, for the captain to keep open in a persistent split pane. Deliberate design decisions: it is a THIN renderer over the existing read-only data owner bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh --json (the same schema fm-fleet-view.sh renders), so it never re-parses backlog or state and cannot drift from the real task list - this reuse is intentional, not missing abstraction. New file bin/fm-tasklist-view.sh plus colocated tests/fm-tasklist-view.test.sh. The board shows four bands - IN FLIGHT (marking which run in parallel), QUEUED (ready), UPCOMING (blocked-by a dependency or a captain hold), and DONE-RECENT - in the backlog's own priority order (array order is preserved priority order). It auto-refreshes on a configurable interval (default 4s, --interval/FM_TASKLIST_INTERVAL) with a --once one-shot mode for testing. It is intentionally READ-ONLY: its only child process is fm-fleet-snapshot.sh --json; a test proves it mutates no state/ or data/ file. FM_HOME is REQUIRED and fails closed when unset, matching bin/fm-send.sh's pattern, so it never shows the wrong home - this is stricter than fm-fleet-snapshot.sh's default-to-repo-root on purpose. It degrades gracefully: a briefly absent or locked snapshot keeps the last good frame with an 'updating' footer instead of crashing the loop. Review-ready PR links and done artifacts render on their own indented sub-line so they stay clickable and full in narrow panes; those sub-lines and short decision/blocked flags are intentionally exempt from the column-width bound. Multibyte box-drawing/glyphs mean the width test measures characters (wc -m under a UTF-8 locale), not bytes. Documentation of flags and paths lives in the script header and --help per the repo one-owner rule, so AGENTS.md was intentionally not touched. shellcheck-clean under the pinned 0.11.0 and fm-lint.sh passes. ## What Changed - Adds `bin/fm-tasklist-view.sh`, a read-only live task-list board over `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh --json` with `--once`, configurable refresh interval, width handling, and required `FM_HOME` fail-closed behavior. - Renders `IN FLIGHT`, `QUEUED`, `UPCOMING`, and `DONE-RECENT` in backlog priority order, including parallel-run markers plus full-width PR/artifact sub-lines for narrow panes. - Adds task-list renderer documentation and colocated shell tests covering live/one-shot rendering, interval validation, snapshot failure handling, narrow output, and no state/data mutation. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the change is narrowly scoped to a read-only renderer and colocated tests, and the previously identified repo-precedence, interval-validation, and width-floor issues are resolved in the current diff. ## Testing Inspected the target diff, ran the focused tasklist suite plus the related snapshot/view behavior suite, captured reviewer-visible CLI transcripts for the four-band board, narrow-pane artifact sub-lines, live updating fallback, and FM_HOME fail-closed behavior, then verified the worktree stayed clean; all checks passed, and lint/static analysis was not run because the testing prompt forbids it.

title: fix(herdr): stop the events capability probe spewing Broken pipe
body:
## Intent The developer wanted to eliminate spurious `Broken pipe` stderr noise from firstmate's herdr capability probe in `bin/backends/herdr.sh`, where `fm_backend_herdr_events_capable` piped a ~220KB `herdr api schema --json` payload into short-circuiting `grep -Fq` calls, causing `printf` to take EPIPE and bury real watcher diagnostics (it fired in 28 of 33 recent watcher arms). They required a subprocess-free, pipe-free replacement (e.g. shell `case` matching) preserving the exact verdict for all inputs including empty and malformed schemas, staying portable to the script's `/bin/sh`-compatible target without new bashisms, and updating the block comment if the change made its size/memoization description stale. Scope was explicitly bounded to that one function: the other 17 `printf ... | grep -q` sites under `bin/` were to be left untouched with no sweep or shared helper, and any genuinely large-payload site found elsewhere was to be reported in the `done:` line rather than fixed silently. Verification had to go beyond a green suite — reproduce the stderr noise before the change, show it clean after, exercise both the capable and incapable branches, and put before/after evidence in the commit body, adding a regression test only if the repo had a natural home for one. Hard constraints: load the `firstmate-coding-guidelines` skill first, work only in the disposable worktree on branch `fm/fm-herdr-pipe-noise`, disturb no live watchers or `state/` files belonging to running tasks, and issue no herdr lifecycle commands (read-only introspection only). The developer then invoked `/no-mistakes` to validate the change and ship it as a PR. ## What Changed - Replaced the two `printf '%s' "$schema" | grep -Fq ...` token checks in `fm_backend_herdr_events_capable` (`bin/backends/herdr.sh`) with in-shell `case` glob matches, so probing the large `herdr api schema --json` payload no longer strands the `printf` writer mid-payload when the short-circuiting reader exits — which had been printing `printf: write error: Broken pipe` to stderr wherever SIGPIPE is ignored (the watcher's inherited disposition) and burying real diagnostics. - Refreshed the stale block comments in `bin/backends/herdr.sh` and `bin/fm-watch.sh` to describe the payload as large (248KB at herdr 0.7.5) instead of the superseded "~220KB", and to document why the checks now match in-shell rather than through a pipe. - Added `test_events_capable_verdict_and_silent_probe` to `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh`, which drives the probe against a ~250KB fixture (both tokens, each token missing, and empty) under a `trap '' PIPE` disposition to assert both the correct verdict and a clean stderr on every schema. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A two-line, verdict-identical substitution of `case` substring matching for short-circuiting `grep -Fq` pipes in a single function, with no new bashisms, matching an idiom already used three lines above, plus a targeted regression test that pins both the four-schema verdict table and the silent-probe property; the only defect found is a stale payload-size number in a sibling comment. ## Testing Ran the herdr adapter unit file and the watcher event-splice unit file (both green under a UTF-8 locale), then went past the suite to reproduce the actual defect: with a fake herdr serving the real 248KB `herdr api schema --json` payload, the base adapter prints `printf: write error: Broken pipe` under the watcher's SIGPIPE-ignored disposition while the fixed adapter is silent, and both return identical verdicts across ten payloads (real, each token missing, empty, truncated-malformed, malformed-with-tokens, glob/backslash, split-token, EOF-without-newline, single 200KB line). Driving the real `fm-watch.sh` event splice through the real backend dispatcher over an isolated scratch state dir yields 6 broken-pipe stderr lines across 3 arms before the change and completely clean stderr after — no live watcher, real herdr server, or task-owned `state/` was touched, and only read-only herdr introspection was used. I also confirmed the new regression test genuinely bites (red against the base adapter, green against the fix) and that the `case` construct is portable to /bin/sh, dash, and bash --posix. This change has no UI surface — the reviewer-visible artifact is the CLI/stderr transcript, which is exactly how an operator experiences the noise — so no screenshot applies. The one failure seen, a C-locale prompt-glyph test in the same file, reproduces identically on the base commit and is tracked as issue #883.
Evidence: Watcher arm stderr: 3 arms of the real fm-watch.sh event splice, base adapter vs fixed ===== watcher arm x3, adapter=before ===== $WORK/before/bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 1960: printf: write error: Broken pipe $WORK/before/bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 1961: printf: write error: Broken pipe $WORK/before/bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 1960: printf: write error: Broken pipe $WORK/before/bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 1961: printf: write error: Broken pipe $WORK/before/bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 1960: printf: write error: Broken pipe $WORK/before/bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 1961: printf: write error: Broken pipe -- 6 stderr line(s) ===== watcher arm x3, adapter=after ===== (watcher stderr: empty - clean arm) ```text ===== watcher arm x3, adapter=before ===== $WORK/before/bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 1960: printf: write error: Broken pipe $WORK/before/bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 1961: printf: write error: Broken pipe $WORK/before/bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 1960: printf: write error: Broken pipe $WORK/before/bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 1961: printf: write error: Broken pipe $WORK/before/bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 1960: printf: write error: Broken pipe $WORK/before/bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 1961: printf: write error: Broken pipe -- 6 stderr line(s) ===== watcher arm x3, adapter=after ===== (watcher stderr: empty - clean arm) ```
Evidence: Before/after probe: noise + verdict parity over the real 248KB schema and 9 variants herdr 0.7.5 | real `herdr api schema --json`: 248358 bytes | pipe buffer: 64KB | min events protocol: 16 PROBE UNDER SIGPIPE-IGNORED (the disposition fm-watch.sh inherits) schema payload BEFORE AFTER probe stderr -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- capable capable capable BEFORE ...herdr.sh: line 1960: printf: write error: Broken pipe (x2) AFTER clean no-subscribe incapable incapable BEFORE clean / AFTER clean no-status incapable incapable BEFORE ...line 1960: printf: write error: Broken pipe (x1) AFTER clean empty incapable incapable BEFORE clean / AFTER clean malformed-truncated incapable incapable BEFORE clean / AFTER clean malformed-with-tokens capable capable BEFORE ...Broken pipe (x2) / AFTER clean glob-and-backslashes capable capable BEFORE ...Broken pipe (x2) / AFTER clean tokens-split-across-lines incapable incapable BEFORE clean / AFTER clean tokens-at-eof-no-newline capable capable BEFORE ...Broken pipe (x2) / AFTER clean single-huge-line capable capable BEFORE clean / AFTER clean -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- verdict parity: IDENTICAL on all 10 payloads; title: fix: avoid generic secondmate start acknowledgements
body:
## Intent Reconcile the proven contradiction in Firstmate's generated persistent-secondmate charter under the captain's Option C decision, without redesigning the status protocol. A marked request must require one correlated answer after the work but no separate receipt or start acknowledgement, while keyed working reports remain available only for genuinely supervisor-actionable material changes and retain same-key later closure. Preserve correlated terse results and document pointers, declared external waits, decisions, blockers, failures, done outcomes, missing-reply recovery, wrong-home detection, unknown-state surfacing, the status vocabulary, pending-reply schema, watcher and classifier behavior, Calm, and operational-input behavior. Add focused generated-charter regression coverage that explicitly rejects the old unconditional working opener and protects those retained behaviors. ## What Changed - Update generated persistent-secondmate charters so marked requests receive one correlated result after completion without an automatic receipt or start acknowledgement. - Preserve keyed `working` reports for supervisor-actionable material changes and require same-key closure through a later state or `resolved` event. - Document the reporting behavior and add generated-charter regression coverage for both the removed acknowledgement and retained reporting contracts. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is narrowly scoped and reconciles the generated charter contradiction while preserving keyed material reporting, correlated results, closure semantics, and the existing status/recovery machinery. ## Testing Inspected the target diff, passed the focused charter, pending-reply, operational-input, watcher/classifier, and Calm tests, then generated and inspected an end-user charter artifact proving Option C behavior and retained protocol wording; no failures or residual worktree artifacts remained.
Evidence: Generated Option C persistent-secondmate charter ```text You are a persistent second mate managed by the main firstmate. Work on your own; do not wait for a human. # Charter Handle marked domain work under Option C. # Routing scope Marked requests from the main firstmate. # Project clones None. This is a project-less domain: its subject is the firstmate repo this home lives in, so it needs no separate clones under `projects/`; its crews take pooled worktrees of that firstmate repo. # Operating model You are in an isolated firstmate home. The local `AGENTS.md` is your job description, and your local `data/`, `state/`, `config/`, and `projects/` dirs are yours to operate. This domain has no separate project clones: its subject is the firstmate repo this home lives in, and its crews take pooled worktrees of that repo. Delegate project work to your own crewmates with the normal firstmate lifecycle: brief, spawn, status, watcher, steer, teardown, and recovery. Do not invent a second delegation system. You do not generate your own work. Act only on tasks the main firstmate routes to you. Never start a survey, audit, or "find improvements" sweep on your own initiative; that is not your job and it is unwanted. # Requests from the main firstmate You are a firstmate in your own home, so an incoming message reaches you in your own chat. You must distinguish who it is from, because the answer goes to a different place. A request relayed to you by the main firstmate is tagged with a leading `[fm-from-firstmate]` marker followed by an invisible system separator; this marker is untypable, so a human never produces it. When a message carries that marker, do the work, then respond via the STATUS/ESCALATION path below, never only in this chat: the main firstmate does not read your chat, so a chat-only reply is lost. Marked requests also carry a privacy-safe `corr=` token after the marker; include that exact token in your parent status reply (or in the status pointer to a detailed doc) so the parent can correlate the answer. Optional helper: `bin/fm-secondmate-report.sh` can append a correlated status line for you, but a plain `echo` that includes the same `corr=` is equally valid - do not depend on the helper being present. For a terse result, a status line is the whole answer. For a detailed answer (an investigation, a plan, an audit), write it to a doc under your home's `data/` and append a status line that points to that doc - the scout-report pattern - so the main firstmate is woken and can read it. Before treating an investigation or visual review as complete, load `decision-hold-lifecycle` from this home's `.agents/skills/` and pass its shared completion gate. A message with NO marker is the captain typing directly into your pane: treat it as authoritative captain intervention and stay conversational exactly as you would for any captain message; do not force it onto the status path. # Escalation to main firstmate Handle routine work yourself. Report only true captain-relevant outcomes or a declared external wait by appending one line: `echo "{state}: {one short line}" >> '/var/folders/5x/4nqprlbx0518k3ybcb1sz6gr0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY81NNTSDR8VDEE9KHQ9TKT7/generated-home/state/option-c-demo.status'` States: working, needs-decision, blocked, paused, done, failed. Use `paused: {why}` (distinct from `blocked:`) only when your domain is deliberately idling on a known external wait you expect to clear on its own; use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need firstmate to act. Use this only for material phase changes, a captain decision, a real blocker, a failure, or work ready for review. This is also how you return the answer to a marked from-firstmate request above. A marked request requires one correlated answer after the work; it does not require a separate receipt or start acknowledgement. Never append `working:` merely to acknowledge receipt or announce that a marked request has started. When a routed-work phase has a supervisor-actionable material change worth reporting under the rule above, give that reported phase a stable key. If its first reportable event is `working [key=]: {material phase}`, use the same key on its later `paused`, `done`, `failed`, `needs-decision`, or `blocked` event so the earlier working phase is superseded. When a keyed phase ends without another reportable state, append `resolved [key=]: {why it is no longer active}`. When a decision you escalated is answered or a blocker clears and your domain resumes, append `resolved: {how it was decided or unblocked}` (keyed with `[key=]` if you opened it with one) so it is durably closed instead of resurfacing behind later unrelated events. Routine internal supervision, heartbeats, retries, and crewmate churn stay inside your own home and must not touch that status file. # Definition of done You are persistent by default. Do not exit just because your queue is empty. On startup and restart, run normal firstmate bootstrap and recovery through `bin/fm-session-start.sh` for your own home, but only to RECONCILE work that is already yours: in-flight crewmates, tracked backlog items, and durable watches recorded in this home. When you have no assigned or in-flight work after that reconciliation, go idle and wait silently for the main firstmate to route you a task. An empty queue is a healthy resting state, not a cue to invent work: never spawn a survey, audit, or any self-directed "find work" task on your own initiative. If this charter cannot be carried out, append `blocked: {why}` or `failed: {why}` to the main status file and stop. ```

title: fix(pi): make calm mode persistent and gapless
fix(composer): byte-safe multibyte prompt-glyph matching under C locales
body:
Fixes both halves of #883: `LC_ALL=C` byte-safety in the composer classifier and in Herdr's bare-prompt-glyph regex.

## Problem

Under a C/POSIX locale on macOS Bash 3.2:

1. `fm_composer_classify_content` (`bin/fm-composer-lib.sh`) stripped a leading prompt glyph with `${content#??}`/`${content#?}` character-count patterns. Under `LC_ALL=C` those patterns strip **bytes**, not characters, so the 3-byte multibyte glyphs `❯` (claude) and `›` (codex) split mid-codepoint. An idle, empty composer (`❯ `) misclassified as `pending` instead of `empty`.
2. `FM_BACKEND_HERDR_BARE_PROMPT_RE` (`bin/backends/herdr.sh`) defaulted to the bracket expression `'^[❯›]'`. Under `LC_ALL=C`, a bracket expression decomposes into a byte-class - `[❯›]` becomes the raw UTF-8 byte set `{0xE2,0x9D,0xAF,0x80,0xBA}`. Since `0xE2` is the leading byte of *every* UTF-8 box-drawing character, not just `❯`/`›`, this wrongly matched the composer's own border rows (`╭`, `╰`, `│`, `╯`) as a bare prompt row, corrupting `fm_backend_herdr_composer_state`'s structural row scan.

Both are the same class of bug (character-count/class patterns implicitly assuming a multibyte-aware locale) against the same underlying data (the agent prompt glyphs), so both are fixed here together.

## Fix

1. Strip each prompt glyph by its literal byte sequence (`case ... in '❯'*) content=${content#'❯'} ;; ...`) instead of a character-count pattern. ASCII single-byte prompts (`>`, `$`, `%`, `#`) are handled the same way for consistency, though they were never affected by the original bug.
2. Change `FM_BACKEND_HERDR_BARE_PROMPT_RE` from the bracket expression to an alternation (`'^(❯|›)'`), which matches each glyph as a whole literal unit and is not vulnerable to byte-class decomposition.

Both fixes preserve existing behavior in a UTF-8 locale exactly (verified below) and do not touch the maintainer-selected zero-to-eight-row Pi composer classification logic.

## Testing

Reproduced and verified on macOS system Bash 3.2.57 under `LC_ALL=C`:

```
                 input=[❯ ]        input=[❯ hello]   input=[> ]
before fix        pending  (WRONG)  pending           empty
after fix         empty    (right)  pending           empty
```

- Added `test_agent_glyphs_strip_literally_under_c_locale` to `tests/fm-composer-lib.test.sh`, covering both `❯` and `›` under `LC_ALL=C` for both the empty and pending cases.
- Added `test_composer_state_bare_prompt_is_empty_under_c_locale` to `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh`, pinning the exact border-row-misclassification regression under `LC_ALL=C`.
- Full existing suites (`tests/fm-composer-lib.test.sh`, `tests/fm-composer-ghost.test.sh`, `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh`, `tests/fm-backend-cmux.test.sh`, `tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh`, `tests/fm-daemon.test.sh`) pass, including under `LC_ALL=C LANG=C`.
- `shellcheck bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh tests/*.sh` passes clean.
- One-sentence doc updates to `docs/herdr-backend.md` and `docs/configuration.md` recording both fixes and their regression coverage.

🔧 **Review** - 5 issues found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - ⚠️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:638` - The fresh-launch recovery detector never consults `config/crew-codex-mcp`, the opt-out this same change introduces. `codex_fresh_launch_candidate_elapsed` (line 473) matches on `harness=codex` + kind ship/scout only, so in a home that set `crew-codex-mcp=enabled` a Codex lane whose MCP startup legitimately exceeds FM_CODEX_MCP_STALL_SECS (15s) over two corroborating polls gets killed, its worktree removed, and respawned via `fm-spawn.sh` — which, honouring the same opt-out, relaunches it WITH MCP servers, reproducing the stall. On every poll after that, the `[ -e "$marker" ]` guard at line 638 calls `codex_fresh_launch_recover_failed`, which enqueues a stale wake and exits the watcher, repeating until the 300s fresh-launch window lapses. Unlike the ordinary stale path there is no per-hash `.stale-$key` dedupe on this branch. It also bypasses `bin/fm-continuity-pretool-check.sh`, which exists specifically to block `--force` teardown during recovery. The inline proof (`codex_fresh_launch_worktree_recyclable`, line 556: clean tree + zero commits ahead of the default ref) is stricter than teardown's, so I could not construct a case where committed or unlanded work is destroyed — the concern is that a second hand-rolled landed-work test now exists and can drift from the declared owner, and that it fires with no captain in the loop and no opt-in. Either route the removal through a shared teardown helper (`validate_worktree_teardown_safety` / `work_is_landed`) or record this as a named exception in AGENTS.md section 1. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:539` - The second corroboration branch `[ -n "$prev_hash" ] && [ "$prev_hash" = "$h" ]` is unreachable. `$h` hashes the whole pane tail, which contains the startup line including its elapsed seconds; if the hash is unchanged then both the signature and the elapsed value are unchanged, so the preceding `[ "$prev_sig" = "$sig" ] && [ "$elapsed" -ge "$prev_elapsed" ]` has already returned 0. The stored hash field and this branch can be dropped, or the intent (corroborate a frozen pane whose signature changed) needs a condition that can actually be true. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:511` - `codex_fresh_launch_call_wake() { "$@"; }` is pure indirection: its single call site at line 519 is `codex_fresh_launch_call_wake wake "$reason"`, which resolves identically to `wake "$reason"` including under the subshell function overrides the new tests use (tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh redefines `wake` directly, and bash resolves the override either way). Inline it and delete the helper. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:601` - `codex_fresh_launch_meta_sidecars` hand-maintains a duplicate of the field list `fm-spawn.sh` writes (lines 1275-1300), with nothing keeping the two in sync. It already omits the three `claude_oauth_account`, `claude_oauth_account_id`, and `claude_oauth_rotation_policy` fields, so a task rehomed from claude to codex by `fm-rehome-quota-wall.sh` would have those stale Claude-account fields re-appended onto its Codex respawn meta, misattributing the lane in account-rotation accounting. More generally, any future spawn-written field is silently treated as a preservable sidecar. Derive the owned set from a single shared list (or add an assertion test that the two agree). 🔧 Fix: remove obsolete codex MCP watcher stall detector and auto-recovery 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-rehome-quota-wall.sh:225` - This branch added the `__CODEXMCPFLAG__` placeholder to the shared codex launch template in `fm-harness-launch-lib.sh:29` (non-secondmate codex), but only `fm-spawn.sh` (line 1341) substitutes it. `fm-rehome-quota-wall.sh` is the other consumer of `fm_launch_template` (line 222) and its substitution block (lines 223-232) never replaces `__CODEXMCPFLAG__`. Rehoming a quota-walled task TO codex is a first-class supported path: `--harness codex` passes the `fm_launch_template` validity check (line 75), only `secondmate` KIND is rejected (line 94), and `fm_capacity_opposite_harness_ok` (line 86) explicitly supports claude<->codex rotation. For such a rehome the built LAUNCH string keeps the literal token glued to the next flag, i.e. `codex ... __CODEXMCPFLAG__--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox -c ...`, which codex parses as a single bogus argument — the rehomed worker fails to launch correctly (and loses the bypass flag). No test catches this: every rehome test rehomes to claude, and the only codex case (line 192) refuses before launch. Add `LAUNCH=${LAUNCH//__CODEXMCPFLAG__/...}` to the substitution block; to preserve this branch's intent (avoid the MCP startup stall), the replacement should apply the same `mcp_servers={}` strip default rather than substituting to empty, since an empty value would relaunch the rehomed codex worker WITH MCP servers and reproduce the stall the branch exists to fix. 🔧 Fix: substitute codex MCP flag in quota-wall rehome via shared helper ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

I documented them as "local, private (keep it out of version control)" instead of the project's standard "LOCAL, gitignored" wording, since claiming gitignored would be inaccurate. Resolving this (adding the three .gitignore entries so the standard wording applies) is a config change outside doc-only scope and needs a human decision. - ℹ️ `AGENTS.md` - AGENTS.md section 2's curated data/ layout does not list three durable artifacts written by the fork tools: data/dashboard.md (fleet dashboard pointer), data/efforts/ (effort board ledger + BOARD.md), and data/lindy/open-work-backlog.md (backlog pull). I deliberately left these out per AGENTS.md's stated size/curation discipline (the always-loaded contract never invokes these standalone tools, and they are documented in docs/scripts.md and each script header). Adding them for completeness is a defensible judgment call either way. 🔧 Fix: apply gitignore + standard wording for private config files ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: fix(watch): retire merged PR polls after durable notification
body:
## Intent Fix the repeated merged-PR notification bug for persistent secondmates by retiring only a canonical validated PR poll after its tracked static probe returns exactly one line 'merged' and the existing durable notification has been published successfully. Use canonical registration and full byte, hash, file-identity, mode, link, and device validation for the poll check, data, and registration artifacts, plus semantic metadata, provider, URL, and task-ID validation before and after the forge query, with a private identity-bound receipt that makes fixed-path removal crash-recoverable, safely retryable, and idempotent. Remove the runnable check first, then only its registration and data sidecars, then the receipt, while preserving pr/pr_head evidence and every unrelated task or persistent-secondmate lifecycle artifact. Keep all unmerged, error, malformed, replaced, tampered, custom-check, and X-mode behavior unchanged, and keep marker grammar, Calm policy, Ahoy, AFK, injection prefixes, turn-end messages, broad secondmate status handling, lifecycle, and merge authority out of scope. Rebase safely onto current main through the pipeline rather than by hand. ## What Changed - Retire canonical GitHub and GitLab PR polls only after an exact `merged` result is durably queued, using strict pre-query and post-query artifact validation. - Add private identity-bound receipts that recover interrupted retirements across watcher startup, migration, rearming, and teardown while preserving task metadata, secondmate lifecycle state, and replacement polls. - Expand security coverage and documentation for once-only notifications, crash recovery, template updates, tampering, nonterminal results, custom checks, and concurrent replacement races. ## Risk Assessment 🚨 High: The captain explicitly accepted the residual window in which `.meta` can be replaced by another one-link file containing the same canonical PR URL. Metadata mode, device, byte, hash, and file-identity binding is not required for this PR, and its omission is an accepted residual risk rather than an unmet required criterion. ## Testing Inspected the supplied base-to-target change and lineage, ran the focused GitHub/GitLab retirement and safety matrix, then exercised the real watcher-to-durable-wake-drain path twice; all checks passed, the transcript shows exactly one merged wake and poll-only retirement, and the worktree remained unchanged.
Evidence: Persistent secondmate merged-PR retirement transcript ```text Persistent secondmate merged-PR retirement - end-to-end evidence Initiating trigger: forge query transitions the tracked PR to MERGED. Previously visible symptom: the still-runnable poll emitted the merged wake every watcher cycle. Expected result: one durable merged wake, then poll-only retirement. ## Intent Integrate Kimi Code CLI 0.29.0 as a verified Firstmate crew harness for Kimi 3 coding and planning. Launch kimi --auto -m kimi-code/k3 without a positional prompt or unsupported effort flag, then submit a brief-file instruction after the TUI is ready; detect Kimi through process ancestry; add verified busy signatures and structural boxed-composer handling across tmux and Herdr; support Kimi slash autocomplete submission; and document the verified adapter facts and live evidence. Preserve the captain-approved tradeoff not to rewrite ~/.kimi-code/config.toml until a safe idempotent global Stop-hook merger is verified, relying on stale-pane detection in v1. Rename the verification record to docs/kimi-harness.md because Kimi is a crew harness, not a runtime backend. Extend existing tests, keep shellcheck and repository lint green, and ship through a PR with CI green. ## What Changed - Kimi Code CLI 0.29.0 als Crew-Harness angebunden: `fm-spawn.sh` startet `kimi --auto -m kimi-code/k3` ohne Positional-Prompt/Effort-Flag, wartet auf die TUI-Readiness und submittet danach die Brief-Datei-Instruktion; ## Intent Implement and ship the captain-authorized Firstmate ShellCheck source-graph speedup using the completed measured diagnosis rather than repeating profiling. Preserve every canonical shell file, ShellCheck 0.11.0, default severity, extended analysis, meaningful diagnostics, local/CI parity through bin/fm-lint.sh alone, all tests, and all five backends. Extract handle_push_transition into a narrow shared production owner used by the watcher and Herdr event-wait smoke, make every adapter an independently linted canonical boundary, fix the newly exposed SC2034 warning rather than suppressing it, and isolate imported production modules from test lint roots only where seeded parity proves dispatcher, adapter, production-owner, and test-local findings remain detectable. Add portable deterministic bounded jobs=1 and jobs=2 execution with separate outputs, stable replay, full failure propagation and cleanup, plus quiet optional telemetry for content, source graph, wall/CPU/RSS, and contention. Meet the representative-host targets of roughly <=110 seconds sequential and <=65 seconds with two workers without timing assertions in CI, and report any miss honestly. Keep CI and no-mistakes invoking only bin/fm-lint.sh; do not weaken or fork the manifest. ## What Changed - Shrink ShellCheck’s source graph while preserving canonical lint roots, source-aware analysis, all backend adapters, and the shared push-transition behavior. - Add deterministic one- and two-worker lint execution with stable diagnostics, failure propagation, cancellation cleanup, and optional quiet telemetry. - Expand lint regression coverage for source boundaries, seeded diagnostic parity, worker cleanup, and local/CI ownership through `bin/fm-lint.sh`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The follow-up now tracks both sequential and parallel workers in isolated process groups, terminates complete worker trees on cancellation, and resolves the prior required-cleanup violation without introducing another material source risk. ## Testing After baseline diff and cleanliness checks, focused lint-runner, supervision, backend, AFK, seeded CLI, telemetry, and real isolated Herdr checks passed with reviewer-visible CLI evidence; this is a CLI-only change, so no visual screenshot applies, while representative-host canonical timing remains unmeasured.

🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-lint.sh:287` - Required criterion contradicted: “jobs=1 and jobs=2 execution with ... full failure propagation and cleanup.” The jobs=1 path runs `fm_lint_run_worker` synchronously without adding its process to `ACTIVE_PIDS`, while the signal/EXIT cleanup only terminates `ACTIVE_PIDS`. title: docs(bin): add bilingual delivery-language policy and brief pointer
body:
## Intent Implement the existing bilingual-delivery-copy backlog item prospectively across Firstmate projects. Future Firstmate-authored commit subjects and pull-request titles must be concise English; authored commit and pull-request bodies must be concise Brazilian Portuguese. No-mistakes prompt-generated pull-request copy and prose reports, plus captain-facing validation summaries, must use Brazilian Portuguese wherever supported without weakening evidence, risks, decisions, fixes, or lifecycle content; keep the pull-request title in concise English. Preserve existing history and open pull requests. Use one authoritative policy owner, short references elsewhere, existing no-mistakes intent/prompt surfaces instead of translation machinery, no language-detection CI, document unsupported fixed tool surfaces honestly, and add the smallest focused check. ## What Changed - Added a `### Delivery language` section to `AGENTS.md` as the sole owner of the prospective policy: concise English commit subjects/PR titles, concise Brazilian Portuguese commit/PR bodies, Portuguese no-mistakes prompt copy and captain-facing summaries (via run intent, without dropping evidence/risks/decisions/fixes/lifecycle), and an honest note that no-mistakes' fixed tool surfaces stay English; also retargeted the section-9 captain-outcome wording to reference this owner. - Extended `bin/fm-brief.sh` so every generated ship brief points workers to the authoritative section 7 delivery-language policy (including its no-mistakes intent requirement) before they commit, open a PR, or start no-mistakes. - Added `test_ship_brief_points_to_delivery_language_owner` in `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` to assert the AGENTS.md owner copy and the brief pointer across all ship modes. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A mudança é puramente documental (política em AGENTS.md, uma referência curta no brief e um teste focado), conforma-se a todos os critérios de intenção e não altera comportamento executável. ## Testing Rodei a suíte `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` (16 testes, todos passam, incluindo o novo teste da política de idioma) e, como o intent é sobre copy/política visível ao worker, gerei um ship brief real para capturar o texto exatamente como o crewmate o vê: a regra 8 aponta para a "authoritative Delivery language policy in AGENTS.md section 7, including its no-mistakes intent requirement". Confirmei que a subseção autoritativa realmente vive na seção 7 e capturei o texto completo da política como artefato. Esta é uma mudança de docs/shell sem superfície de UI renderizada, então a evidência revisável é o markdown do brief gerado e a seção de AGENTS.md — não há screenshot aplicável. Resultado geral: verde, intent satisfeito de ponta a ponta.
Evidence: Ship brief gerado — regra 8 de delivery-language visível ao worker ```text You are a crewmate: an autonomous worker agent managed by firstmate. Work on your own; do not wait for a human. # Task {TASK} # Herdr lifecycle declaration - NOT ENABLED **HARD SAFETY GATE:** this scaffold cannot inspect the task text that replaces `{TASK}` later. If the task will start, stop, delete, restart, profile, or otherwise drive Herdr lifecycle behavior, stop and regenerate the brief with `--herdr-lab` before dispatch. Do not add Herdr lifecycle commands to this unguarded brief by hand. # Setup You are in a disposable git worktree of demo-project, at a detached HEAD on a clean default branch. **Verify isolation before anything else.** Run `pwd -P` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; both must resolve to the disposable task worktree you were launched in, such as a treehouse pool path or an Orca-managed worktree, not the primary checkout firstmate operates from. The path check is authoritative: `git rev-parse --git-dir` and `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` can help inspect the repo, but they do not prove you are outside the primary checkout. If the top-level path is the primary checkout or not the worktree you were launched in, STOP - do not branch or commit here - append `blocked: launched in primary checkout, not an isolated worktree` to the status file and stop. 1. First action: create your branch: `git checkout -b fm/demo-ticket` 2. Run `no-mistakes doctor`; if it reports the repo is not initialized here, run `no-mistakes init`. # Rules 1. Never push to the default branch. Never merge a PR. 2. Stay inside this worktree; modify nothing outside it. 3. Use gh-axi for GitHub operations and chrome-devtools-axi for browser operations. 4. Report status by appending one line: `echo "{state}: {one short line}" >> '/tmp/tmp.BxIfl19wdZ/state/demo-ticket.status'` States: working, needs-decision, blocked, paused, done, failed. Each append wakes firstmate, so report sparingly: only phase changes a supervisor would act on (setup done, bug reproduced, fix implemented, validation passed) and the needs-decision/blocked/paused/done/failed states. No step-by-step FYI progress lines; firstmate reads your pane for that. A mid-task `working:` line (including setup complete) is nonterminal: do not end the turn after it; continue the same stage until a defined `done:` gate under Definition of done. Use `paused: {why}` - distinct from `blocked:` - ONLY when you are deliberately idling on a known external wait you expect to clear on its own (an upstream release, a rate-limit reset, a scheduled window): firstmate then leaves your idle pane alone and rechecks it on a long cadence instead of treating it as a possible wedge. Use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need help. 5. If you hit the same obstacle twice, append `blocked: {why}` and stop; firstmate will help. 6. If a decision belongs to a human (product choices, destructive actions, ask-user findings), append `needs-decision: {summary of options}` and stop. Firstmate will reply with the decision. When firstmate replies or a blocker clears and you resume, append `resolved: {how it was decided or unblocked}` (add the same `[key=]` if you opened it with one) so the decision or blocker is durably closed and does not keep resurfacing. 7. Never stop, restart, or update the shared `no-mistakes` daemon - it is one instance serving every lane/home, so restarting it kills other lanes' in-flight pipeline runs. On ANY no-mistakes daemon error, append `blocked: {the daemon error}` and stop; only firstmate manages the daemon. 8. Before committing, opening a PR, or starting no-mistakes, read and follow the authoritative Delivery language policy in `/home/lucas/.no-mistakes/worktrees/2e94237bfec0/01KY8CGJE97D848GZFMNWZ6J2J/AGENTS.md` section 7, including its no-mistakes intent requirement. # Project memory If `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` already exists, or if this task produced durable project-intrinsic knowledge, run `/home/lucas/.no-mistakes/worktrees/2e94237bfec0/01KY8CGJE97D848GZFMNWZ6J2J/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh .` in the worktree. Record only project knowledge useful to almost every future session. For anything the codebase already shows, prefer a pointer to the authoritative file, command, or doc over copying the detail. If you touch a project `AGENTS.md` that lacks `## Maintaining this file`, add that short self-governance section from `/home/lucas/.no-mistakes/worktrees/2e94237bfec0/01KY8CGJE97D848GZFMNWZ6J2J/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh` in the same pass. Keep it proportionate: skip `AGENTS.md` edits for trivial tasks that produced no durable project knowledge. # Definition of done The task is complete only when committed on your branch. When you believe it is complete, append `done: {summary}` to the status file and stop. Firstmate will then instruct you to run /no-mistakes to validate and ship a PR. You drive no-mistakes by responding to its gates, not by implementing fixes. Follow the guidance no-mistakes itself provides for the mechanics: it loads when you invoke /no-mistakes, and `no-mistakes axi run --help` plus the `help` lines in each `axi` response are authoritative and version-matched to the installed binary. Do not hand-edit, commit, or fix findings yourself while a run is active - the pipeline applies every fix. Two firstmate-specific rules layer on top of that guidance: - ask-user findings are not yours to answer: escalate to firstmate (rule 6) and stop. When the decision comes back, feed it to the gate with `no-mistakes axi respond` and let the pipeline apply it - do not route the question to "the user" or implement the fix yourself. - Avoid `--yes`: the captain, not you, owns the ask-user decisions it would silently auto-resolve. After /no-mistakes reports CI green (the CI-ready return point - do not wait for it to keep monitoring in the background until merge), append `done: PR {url} checks green` and stop. You are finished. ```

Use concise English for commit subjects and pull-request titles, and concise Brazilian Portuguese for authored commit bodies and pull-request bodies. Do not rewrite existing commit history or edit existing open pull requests to apply this policy. For no-mistakes runs, include this language directive in the run intent so its prompt-generated pull-request copy and prose reports use Brazilian Portuguese while the pull-request title stays in English. Give captain-facing validation summaries in Brazilian Portuguese without dropping evidence, risks, decisions, fixes, or lifecycle content. The installed no-mistakes tool exposes no locale or language setting for its fixed AXI labels, findings, and help text, so those tool-owned surfaces remain English; never claim that they were localized. ```

title: feat(bin): split +yolo into independent autonomy grants
body:
## Intent Upstream contribution from the mattwwatson/firstmate fork: split the single +yolo autonomy flag into independent findings/merge/local-merge grants with least-permission resolution at every autonomy decision, add the --grant query contract (exit 0/1/2), and rename the per-task yolo= meta field to grants=. A caller-inventory tripwire test (tests/fm-project-mode.test.sh) guards that every resolver call site reads the field it intends. Rebased onto current upstream/main: one README.md bullet conflict from upstream drift was hand-merged (kept upstream's newer task-shapes wording, took the grants wording for project modes), and the tripwire's caller scan was tightened to count only real quoted-path invocations so upstream's fm-test-run.sh changed-file family map (which lists the script name as a path literal) is not mistaken for a caller. 14/14 project-mode tests green locally on the upstream base; touched suites (teardown, backend, fleet-snapshot-view, instruction-owners) still pass. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-project-mode.sh` now resolves three independent autonomy grants (`findings`, `merge`, `local-merge`) instead of a single on/off yolo flag, printing ` `. Registry lines accept `+yolo:[,]` (repeatable) while bare `+yolo` still means all three, and every unrecognised input — missing registry, absent project, unknown mode, unknown grant name — resolves to the least permission with a stderr warning. - Added the `--grant ` query contract: exits 0 when the grant is held, 1 when it is not, and 2 on a usage error or unknown grant name, so both non-zero exits deny. The query is answered from the same canonical grant list the resolver builds, so a name outside that list is structurally denied rather than relying on argument validation alone. - Renamed the per-task `yolo=` meta field to `grants=` across `fm-spawn.sh` (spawn line and `state/.meta`, including the abort-cleanup path) and `fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` JSON; updated call sites and prose in `fm-brief.sh`, `fm-fleet-sync.sh`, `fm-merge-local.sh`, `fm-teardown.sh`, AGENTS.md, README.md, docs, and the skills. - New `tests/fm-project-mode.test.sh` (14 cases) covers grant parsing, least-permission fallbacks, and the `--grant` exit codes, plus a caller-inventory tripwire that fails when a resolver call site in `bin/` reads the output in an unreviewed shape; the suite is classified into the `pure-contract-unit` family in `fm-test-run.sh` so `--changed` selects it. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: All three accepted findings from round 1 are correctly fixed — the grant query now answers from the single canonical grants list (verified safe against `merge`/`local-merge` substring collisions and glob injection), the new test is classified into a family without disturbing the lane coverage guard, and the last stale `yolo=` fixture is migrated — leaving a well-bounded, fail-safe change with no outstanding source risk. ## Testing I ran the new tests/fm-project-mode.test.sh (14/14 green) plus all eleven other suites the diff touches (teardown, backend, fleet-snapshot-view, instruction-owners, gotmp, pending-reply, send-secondmate-marker, x-mode, backend-orca, secondmate-safety, secondmate-lifecycle-e2e) — every suite exit 0. Because passing tests alone do not show the intent, I also drove the captain-facing path by hand: a real data/projects.md with per-grant lines, the real resolver, a real fm-spawn.sh run through the fake-Orca backend, and the real read-only fleet snapshot. That transcript shows `+yolo:findings` resolving to `no-mistakes findings`, allowing findings (exit 0) while denying merge and local-merge (exit 1), legacy bare `+yolo` still granting all three, typo'd/absent/unknown input collapsing to `none` with a warning, `--grant mrege` and `--grant ''` exiting 2 on a fully-granted project, `grants=findings` landing in the durable state/<id>.meta, and `"grants": "findings"` appearing in the snapshot JSON. I proved the caller-inventory tripwire is not vacuous by mutating a scratch copy of bin/ with an unreviewed call site (test failed as designed) and confirmed the tightened pattern matches bin/fm-test-run.sh zero times. No screenshot or rendered-HTML artifact applies: this change has no UI surface — it is a bash resolver, task metadata, JSON snapshot fields, and agent-instruction docs — so CLI transcripts and the snapshot JSON are the actual end-user surface. The worktree is clean and the stray /tmp task dir the spawn created was removed.

misspelled query on a FULLY granted project error: unknown grant "mrege"; expected findings, merge, or local-merge exit=2 (2 = usage error, never mistaken for a grant) === 6. real fm-spawn.sh (fake-Orca backend): grants reach the task metadata === spawned demotask1 harness=claude kind=ship mode=no-mistakes grants=findings window=fm-demotask1 worktree=<tmp>/scheduler-wt state/demotask1.meta: kind=ship mode=no-mistakes grants=findings === 7. read-only fleet snapshot surfaces the grants === { "tasks": [ { "id": "demotask1", "kind": "ship", "mode": "no-mistakes", "grants": "findings" } ] } ```text === 1. what the captain writes in data/projects.md === # title: docs: enforce audience-specific documentation ownership
body:
## Intent

The developer wanted a single no-mistakes validation run for the committed documentation-audience cleanup, carried through all synchronous gates, push, pull request creation, and green CI unless a genuinely new decision required escalation. They required quantified, reproducible before-and-after prompt reduction measurements and a concise preservation map tracing removed durable facts to their current authoritative owners. The evidence needed to stay current without adding historical clutter to operator documentation, while preserving the documentation audience policy and one-owner rule. They explicitly required the pipeline to make the fix, prohibited hand edits and --yes, and said not to start a second run while the current one was active.

## What Changed

- Classify maintained prose by audience and add structural enforcement for inventory coverage, ownership pointers, setup routing, and format-aware local links and anchors.
- Refocus public and operator guides on current behavior, setup, and limits while consolidating backend and supervision evidence into dedicated verification records.
- Reduce prompt-bearing supervision content, clarify documentation ownership across agent and contributor guidance, and record quantified reductions with a preservation map.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The documentation migration is well-bounded, its preservation evidence is coherent, and the final shared link extractor now closes all previously identified Markdown, reStructuredText, anchor, parsed-literal, and raw-HTML paths with focused regression coverage.

## Testing

After inspecting the base-to-target diff, I ran the focused documentation policy tests and repository checker, manually audited the preservation map, rendered actual before-and-after harness prompts, reproduced every published size reduction, confirmed unchanged harness prompts remained byte-identical, captured reviewer-visible transcript artifacts, removed snapshot scaffolding, and verified the worktree remained clean. title: fix: enforce contract boundaries for ask-user findings
body:
## Intent Implement a shared authority exception for ask-user findings whose proposed Fix would materially expand the captain's original product or engineering contract. Keep the concise always-loaded boundary in AGENTS.md and a single narrowly scoped detailed owner, with normal tracked inheritance for secondmates. Preserve autonomous yolo momentum for difficult corrections genuinely required by accepted intent and for explicitly requested complex architecture, while requiring captain escalation for unrequested new guarantees, threat models, subsystems, abstractions, compatibility surfaces, state machines, continuous monitoring, generalized frameworks, broader architecture, repeated abstraction-preserving same-theme findings, and the existing stronger destructive, irreversible, or security-sensitive boundaries. The implementation worker must never answer its own ask-user finding. Captain escalations must state the original requirement, proposed expansion, smallest compliant alternative, accept/decline consequences, and recommendation. Add scenario regressions for required defect correction, checkpoint proof expanding to continuous frame-by-frame monitoring, repeated same-theme escalation, genuine security sensitivity, and explicitly requested complex architecture. Use Hi Bit PR 148 only as motivating evidence, not a special-case rule. Validate primary and secondmate instruction generation and update conflicting authority wording without incorporating concurrent work. ## What Changed - Restrict `+yolo` ask-user decisions to the accepted contract, escalating material expansions and stronger captain-owned boundaries while preserving autonomy for required corrections and explicitly requested complexity. - Add a single authority procedure and update worker briefs, project guidance, AFK behavior, and secondmate inheritance to route decisions through firstmate without worker self-approval. - Add regression coverage for contract-expansion scenarios, repeated same-theme findings, security-sensitive choices, and primary and secondmate instruction generation. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the change cleanly centralizes the authority policy, preserves stronger escalation boundaries, updates competing instruction paths, and covers the required scenarios without a source-verifiable bypass. ## Testing Reviewed the base-to-target policy change, exercised all required authority scenarios plus away-mode wording and real secondmate tracked-file synchronization, and manually inspected generated primary and secondmate instruction artifacts; everything passed and no UI screenshot was applicable because this is a Markdown and CLI instruction-generation change.
Evidence: Generated primary worker brief ```text You are a crewmate: an autonomous worker agent managed by firstmate. Work on your own; do not wait for a human. # Task {TASK} # Herdr lifecycle declaration - NOT ENABLED **HARD SAFETY GATE:** this scaffold cannot inspect the task text that replaces `{TASK}` later. If the task will start, stop, delete, restart, profile, or otherwise drive Herdr lifecycle behavior, stop and regenerate the brief with `--herdr-lab` before dispatch. Do not add Herdr lifecycle commands to this unguarded brief by hand. # Setup You are in a disposable git worktree of sample, at a detached HEAD on a clean default branch. **Verify isolation before anything else.** Run `pwd -P` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; both must resolve to the disposable task worktree you were launched in, such as a treehouse pool path or an Orca-managed worktree, not the primary checkout firstmate operates from. The path check is authoritative: `git rev-parse --git-dir` and `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` can help inspect the repo, but they do not prove you are outside the primary checkout. If the top-level path is the primary checkout or not the worktree you were launched in, STOP - do not branch or commit here - append `blocked: launched in primary checkout, not an isolated worktree` to the status file and stop. 1. First action: create your branch: `git checkout -b fm/authority-worker` 2. Run `no-mistakes doctor`; if it reports the repo is not initialized here, run `no-mistakes init`. # Rules 1. Never push to the default branch. Never merge a PR. 2. Stay inside this worktree; modify nothing outside it. 3. Use gh-axi for GitHub operations and chrome-devtools-axi for browser operations. 4. Report status by appending one line: `echo "{state}: {one short line}" >> '/var/folders/5x/4nqprlbx0518k3ybcb1sz6gr0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY8PTHFQF15E335R0SC68763/home/state/authority-worker.status'` States: working, needs-decision, blocked, paused, done, failed. Each append wakes firstmate, so report sparingly: only phase changes a supervisor would act on (setup done, bug reproduced, fix implemented, validation passed) and the needs-decision/blocked/paused/done/failed states. No step-by-step FYI progress lines; firstmate reads your pane for that. A mid-task `working:` line (including setup complete) is nonterminal: do not end the turn after it; continue the same stage until a defined `done:` gate under Definition of done. Use `paused: {why}` - distinct from `blocked:` - ONLY when you are deliberately idling on a known external wait you expect to clear on its own (an upstream release, a rate-limit reset, a scheduled window): firstmate then leaves your idle pane alone and rechecks it on a long cadence instead of treating it as a possible wedge. Use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need help. 5. If you hit the same obstacle twice, append `blocked: {why}` and stop; firstmate will help. 6. If a decision belongs above the implementation worker (product choices, destructive actions, ask-user findings), append `needs-decision: {summary of options}` and stop. Firstmate will apply the configured authority and reply with the decision. When firstmate replies or a blocker clears and you resume, append `resolved: {how it was decided or unblocked}` (add the same `[key=]` if you opened it with one) so the decision or blocker is durably closed and does not keep resurfacing. 7. Never stop, restart, or update the shared `no-mistakes` daemon - it is one instance serving every lane/home, so restarting it kills other lanes' in-flight pipeline runs. On ANY no-mistakes daemon error, append `blocked: {the daemon error}` and stop; only firstmate manages the daemon. # Project memory If `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` already exists, or if this task produced durable project-intrinsic knowledge, run `/Users/kunchen/.no-mistakes/worktrees/016d88035d58/01KY8PTHFQF15E335R0SC68763/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh .` in the worktree. Record only project knowledge useful to almost every future session. For anything the codebase already shows, prefer a pointer to the authoritative file, command, or doc over copying the detail. If you touch a project `AGENTS.md` that lacks `## Maintaining this file`, add that short self-governance section from `/Users/kunchen/.no-mistakes/worktrees/016d88035d58/01KY8PTHFQF15E335R0SC68763/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh` in the same pass. Keep it proportionate: skip `AGENTS.md` edits for trivial tasks that produced no durable project knowledge. # Definition of done The task is complete only when committed on your branch. When you believe it is complete, append `done: {summary}` to the status file and stop. Firstmate will then instruct you to run /no-mistakes to validate and ship a PR. You drive no-mistakes by responding to its gates, not by implementing fixes. Follow the guidance no-mistakes itself provides for the mechanics: it loads when you invoke /no-mistakes, and `no-mistakes axi run --help` plus the `help` lines in each `axi` response are authoritative and version-matched to the installed binary. Do not hand-edit, commit, or fix findings yourself while a run is active - the pipeline applies every fix. Two firstmate-specific rules layer on top of that guidance: - ask-user findings are never yours to answer: escalate to firstmate (rule 6) and stop. Firstmate applies the authority contract in its `AGENTS.md` and obtains any required captain decision. When the decision comes back, feed it to the gate with `no-mistakes axi respond` and let the pipeline apply it - do not route the question to "the user" or implement the fix yourself. - Avoid `--yes`: it would silently bypass firstmate's authority check and any required captain escalation. After /no-mistakes reports CI green (the CI-ready return point - do not wait for it to keep monitoring in the background until merge), append `done: PR {url} checks green` and stop. You are finished. ```
Evidence: Generated secondmate charter ```text You are a persistent second mate managed by the main firstmate. Work on your own; do not wait for a human. # Charter Handle sample work and escalate contract expansion through firstmate. # Routing scope Handle sample work and escalate contract expansion through firstmate. # Project clones None. This is a project-less domain: its subject is the firstmate repo this home lives in, so it needs no separate clones under `projects/`; its crews take pooled worktrees of that firstmate repo. # Operating model You are in an isolated firstmate home. The local `AGENTS.md` is your job description, and your local `data/`, `state/`, `config/`, and `projects/` dirs are yours to operate. This domain has no separate project clones: its subject is the firstmate repo this home lives in, and its crews take pooled worktrees of that repo. Delegate project work to your own crewmates with the normal firstmate lifecycle: brief, spawn, status, watcher, steer, teardown, and recovery. Do not invent a second delegation system. You do not generate your own work. Act only on tasks the main firstmate routes to you. Never start a survey, audit, or "find improvements" sweep on your own initiative; that is not your job and it is unwanted. # Requests from the main firstmate You are a firstmate in your own home, so an incoming message reaches you in your own chat. You must distinguish who it is from, because the answer goes to a different place. A request relayed to you by the main firstmate is tagged with a leading `[fm-from-firstmate]` marker followed by an invisible system separator; this marker is untypable, so a human never produces it. When a message carries that marker, do the work, then respond via the STATUS/ESCALATION path below, never only in this chat: the main firstmate does not read your chat, so a chat-only reply is lost. Marked requests also carry a privacy-safe `corr=` token after the marker; include that exact token in your parent status reply (or in the status pointer to a detailed doc) so the parent can correlate the answer. Optional helper: `bin/fm-secondmate-report.sh` can append a correlated status line for you, but a plain `echo` that includes the same `corr=` is equally valid - do not depend on the helper being present. For a terse result, a status line is the whole answer. For a detailed answer (an investigation, a plan, an audit), write it to a doc under your home's `data/` and append a status line that points to that doc - the scout-report pattern - so the main firstmate is woken and can read it. Before treating an investigation or visual review as complete, load `decision-hold-lifecycle` from this home's `.agents/skills/` and pass its shared completion gate. A message with NO marker is the captain typing directly into your pane: treat it as authoritative captain intervention and stay conversational exactly as you would for any captain message; do not force it onto the status path. # Escalation to main firstmate Handle routine work yourself. Report only true captain-relevant outcomes or a declared external wait by appending one line: `echo "{state}: {one short line}" >> '/var/folders/5x/4nqprlbx0518k3ybcb1sz6gr0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY8PTHFQF15E335R0SC68763/home/state/authority-mate.status'` States: working, needs-decision, blocked, paused, done, failed. Use `paused: {why}` (distinct from `blocked:`) only when your domain is deliberately idling on a known external wait you expect to clear on its own; use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need firstmate to act. Use this only for material phase changes, a captain decision, a real blocker, a failure, or work ready for review. This is also how you return the answer to a marked from-firstmate request above. A marked request requires one correlated answer after the work; it does not require a separate receipt or start acknowledgement. Never append `working:` merely to acknowledge receipt or announce that a marked request has started. When a routed-work phase has a supervisor-actionable material change worth reporting under the rule above, give that reported phase a stable key. If its first reportable event is `working [key=]: {material phase}`, use the same key on its later `paused`, `done`, `failed`, `needs-decision`, or `blocked` event so the earlier working phase is superseded. When a keyed phase ends without another reportable state, append `resolved [key=]: {why it is no longer active}`. When a decision you escalated is answered or a blocker clears and your domain resumes, append `resolved: {how it was decided or unblocked}` (keyed with `[key=]` if you opened it with one) so it is durably closed instead of resurfacing behind later unrelated events. Routine internal supervision, heartbeats, retries, and crewmate churn stay inside your own home and must not touch that status file. # Definition of done You are persistent by default. Do not exit just because your queue is empty. On startup and restart, run normal firstmate bootstrap and recovery through `bin/fm-session-start.sh` for your own home, but only to RECONCILE work that is already yours: in-flight crewmates, tracked backlog items, and durable watches recorded in this home. When you have no assigned or in-flight work after that reconciliation, go idle and wait silently for the main firstmate to route you a task. An empty queue is a healthy resting state, not a cue to invent work: never spawn a survey, audit, or any self-directed "find work" task on your own initiative. If this charter cannot be carried out, append `blocked: {why}` or `failed: {why}` to the main status file and stop. ```

title: feat(bin): add secure Gitea forge lifecycle support
body:
## Intent

Implement the first production-quality Gitea forge foundation for FirstMate while preserving all existing GitHub and GitLab behavior. Introduce one secure provider abstraction for canonical repository and pull-request identities, private-network HTTP ports and SSH aliases/ports, strict private host/account/token configuration, and Gitea PR creation, state, head, review, checks, polling, guarded merge, and landed-work lifecycle integration. Keep tokens out of argv, environment, logs, generated checks, metadata, reports, and errors; stop on malformed, ambiguous, cross-host, auth, or unsupported responses. Update project and brief guidance so Gitea projects do not receive GitHub-only PR instructions, document mocked evidence without claiming live support, expose a typed extension point for later issue/milestone work, and comprehensively test security plus unchanged GitHub/GitLab behavior. Do not access any live Gitea server, repository, credential, or captain-private gitea-token; use deterministic mocked HTTP and git fixtures only, leaving live Brad/Test-Repo verification to a separately authorized task.

## What Changed

- Add a provider-neutral forge interface with canonical Gitea repository and pull-request identities, strict private configuration, and isolated token-authenticated HTTP requests.
- Integrate Gitea PR creation, state, head, reviews, checks, polling, guarded merge, and landed-work teardown while preserving GitHub and GitLab behavior.
- Add Gitea operator guidance and deterministic mocked coverage for security, pagination, private ports and SSH aliases, lifecycle behavior, and existing forge regressions.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The latest fix now paginates independently of server page-size caps, validates every page, aggregates only within explicit page and record bounds, and fails closed when completion cannot be proven.

## Testing

Inspected the target diff, ran the deterministic mocked Gitea lifecycle/security suite and focused existing GitHub/GitLab PR, brief, review, teardown, and poll-security regressions, then generated reviewer-visible CLI help and a real Gitea worker brief; everything passed without live network or credential access, and the worktree stayed clean.

body:
## Intent

Re-raise PR #954 through the no-mistakes pipeline so its required 'PR must be raised via no-mistakes' check passes, WITHOUT changing what the PR does. The change adds GitHub Enterprise (GHE) PR-URL support: it threads a validated host through fm_pr_url_parse() so an operator-approved GHE host listed in the local gitignored config/pr-hosts allowlist can arm the canonical merge poll and merge via fm-pr-merge.sh with a scoped GH_HOST, while github.com keeps working byte-for-byte identically with zero configuration. It is rebuilt on top of #797's provider/host/path/number identity model (GitLab MR support). Touches bin/fm-pr-lib.sh, fm-pr-merge.sh, fm-pr-poll.sh, fm-watch.sh, docs, .gitignore, AGENTS.md, and adds tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh covering the adversarial host-validation matrix. The allowlist exact-match host validation and github.com-unchanged behavior are deliberate security choices, not oversights.

## What Changed

- Accept GitHub Enterprise PR URLs only for hosts exactly allowlisted in `config/pr-hosts`, while preserving zero-config `github.com` behavior.
- Carry validated host identity through polling and scope `GH_HOST` to Enterprise merge commands; re-check the allowlist on every poll.
- Document the host requirements and add adversarial coverage for validation, polling, merging, and allowlist removal.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Captain, the change is well-bounded, preserves github.com behavior, and consistently enforces exact-match GHE host authorization.

title: fix(send): grace re-check for tmux submit races, size-aware retries
body:
## Intent Fix fm-send's tmux submit-verification false negative: an idle-lab investigation (`data/fm-send-false-negative-q4/report.md`) characterized the root cause as a fixed Enter-retry budget (~1.2-2.7s) racing variable delivery latency (a large multi-line paste can split into several separate bracketed-paste chunks; production fleet load can also slow tmux's own redraw), so a message that actually submitted successfully was misreported as a swallowed Enter (exit 1), tempting a duplicate resend. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh`: after the existing Enter-retry loop and the existing `fm_pane_is_busy` fallback in `fm_tmux_submit_enter_core` both still read `pending`, sleep one bounded grace window (`FM_SEND_GRACE`, default 1.5s), then take a single final read (composer state first, busy check second) before committing to the hard `pending` verdict. A genuinely swallowed Enter never changes on its own, so this cannot weaken real-swallow detection — it only rescues an in-flight delivery. - `bin/fm-send.sh`: scale the retry count with message size (one extra retry per ~10 lines), capped at `FM_SEND_MAX_RETRIES` (default 12, overridable) so a pathologically large paste cannot block the caller unboundedly. A single-line steer gets 0 extra retries, so the default budget is byte-identical to before. - `bin/fm-spawn.sh`: a real bug the pipeline's test step found along the way — `{ ...; } > "$STATE/$ID.meta"` did not trip `set -e` on a failed redirection (a known bash quirk), so a spawn whose metadata write failed continued silently instead of aborting. Now caught explicitly. - Docs: `docs/configuration.md` (new `FM_SEND_GRACE` / `FM_SEND_MAX_RETRIES` entries, updated `FM_SEND_RETRIES` description), `docs/tmux-backend.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and the `afk`/`harness-adapters` skills updated to describe the grace re-check. - Deliberately left the popup-settle logic for leading `/` and codex `$` messages untouched (a different, real hazard, out of scope here). ## Testing - `tests/fm-tmux-submit-grace.test.sh` (new): a composer that stays `pending` through the normal retries and busy fallback but clears only during the grace sleep returns `empty` (not `pending`); a pane that never changes still returns `pending` after the grace window, preserving genuine-swallow detection. - `tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh` updated (existing idle-swallow test now pins `FM_SEND_GRACE` small so it stays fast) and passing. - Full `tests/*.test.sh` suite passes. The only recurring failures are pre-existing Herdr-lab e2e tests that require a real Herdr backend unavailable in this environment — independently confirmed via `git stash` to fail identically on the unpatched baseline, unrelated to this change. - `bin/fm-lint.sh` (shellcheck) passes. ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ Intent - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ Rebase - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 Review - 2 issues found → 1 auto-fixed, 1 resolved by captain decision ✅ - ⚠️ `docs/configuration.md` - exhaustively lists every fm-send tunable but was not updated for the new `FM_SEND_GRACE` knob, and the `FM_SEND_RETRIES` description was inaccurate once retries scale by message size. 🔧 Fix: added `FM_SEND_GRACE` / `FM_SEND_MAX_RETRIES` entries and corrected the `FM_SEND_RETRIES` description. - 🚨 `bin/fm-send.sh` - the size-scaled retry count had no upper cap: an unusually large multi-line message could drive the retry budget (and total wait) proportionally, with no caller-side timeout. Decision: cap total retries at `FM_SEND_MAX_RETRIES` (default 12, overridable), keeping the per-~10-lines scaling below that cap. ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ Test - passed ✅ No issues found in the files this change touches. - Ran the full `tests/*.test.sh` suite, including the new `tests/fm-tmux-submit-grace.test.sh` and updated `tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh`. - Found and fixed a real pre-existing bug surfaced by `tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh` (`bin/fm-spawn.sh` metadata-write failure not aborting spawn). - Remaining failures are pre-existing Herdr-lab e2e tests requiring a real Herdr backend, confirmed present on the unpatched baseline via `git stash`.
✅ Document - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ Lint - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ Push - completed manually The pipeline's automated push failed: `git push https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate ...` was rejected with a 403 (this contributor's account does not have direct write access to the upstream repo). The already-validated commits were pushed by hand to the `pchuri/firstmate` fork and this PR was opened manually against `kunchenguid/firstmate:main`, carrying forward the exact commits produced by the Review/Test/Document steps above unmodified.
