- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 info across 1 run (8m10s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 2 infos - ⚠️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:108` - `Esc:cancel` is a generic modal-dismiss token, and verification is documented only for two Grok states (mid-turn keybind bar vs idle keybind bar). Grok renders other non-busy states that plausibly show a cancel hint - the slash-autocomplete popup that this repo already has a live incident for (.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md:293), a tool-permission dialog when a crewmate is not launched with --always-approve, or the project picker. If any of those footers reads `Esc:cancel`, the pane classifies busy while it is actually blocked on a human. That directly breaks the invariant fm-crew-state.sh:174 relies on ("A genuinely human-blocked agent (a permission dialog, not mid-tool-call) does not render the busy banner, so this corroboration does not mask that case"), and a false-busy suppresses stuck detection and the absorb-then-escalate wake path in window_is_busy (bin/fm-watch.sh:173) - i.e. a wedged crewmate is never escalated. The old `Ctrl+c:cancel` token was specific to the mid-turn cancel hint; `Esc:cancel` is not obviously so. Worth capturing a popup/permission-dialog pane on 0.2.112 and, if the token appears there, tightening the alternative (e.g. anchoring it to the mid-turn bar's neighbours such as `Ctrl+b:send to bg`). - ℹ️ `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md:289` - The harness-adapters Grok fact table still states the busy-pane signature is `Ctrl+c:cancel` with no mention of `Esc:cancel` or 0.2.112, so the adapter doc other agents read as the source of truth for this signature is now stale relative to the shipped regex. Noted only for tracking - the user intent explicitly excludes touching this skill ("Do NOT touch harness-adapters skill (in-flight elsewhere)"), so no change is expected in this change. 🔧 Fix: document Grok 0.2.112 overlay evidence, add negative footer fixtures 2 infos still open: - ℹ️ `tests/fm-grok-harness.test.sh:174` - The three negative fixtures live in a quoted heredoc (`<<'EOF'` at line 174), which performs no escape expansion, so those lines carry the literal 6-character text `│` rather than the U+2502 separator. The comment at line 142 states "Fixtures use the real U+2502 separator", and the mid-turn and permission fixtures on lines 161 and 182 do use `$'...'` and really are U+2502 - so the negative set is the odd one out and is weaker evidence than the comment claims. No assertion changes today, because no alternative in the default regex touches the separator; it only becomes a live gap if a future busy token is anchored on surrounding punctuation. Fix by pasting the literal │ characters into the heredoc lines. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-grok-harness.test.sh:183` - The new assertion pins that the Grok tool-permission footer (`1/4:select | Ctrl+o:always-approve | Ctrl+c:cancel`) MUST match the default busy regex, via the legacy token. That is the pre-existing behaviour the user explicitly ruled on, and it is honestly documented in both comment blocks, so nothing to change here. Recording only the downstream consequence: a permission dialog is a human-blocked pane, so bin/fm-crew-state.sh:174's comment ("A genuinely human-blocked agent (a permission dialog, not mid-tool-call) does not render the busy banner, so this corroboration does not mask that case") is now known to be false for Grok, and the assertion locks that behaviour against a future fix. Crewmates spawn with --always-approve, so the dialog is rare in practice.
⚠️ **Test** - 1 info - ℹ️ `tests/fm-grok-harness.test.sh:168` - tests/fm-grok-harness.test.sh: the three negative-overlay fixtures are supplied through a quoted heredoc (<<'EOF'), so their separators stay the literal 6-character string │ rather than the real U+2502 the surrounding comment claims ("Fixtures use the real U+2502 separator"). The mid-turn and permission fixtures use $'...' and do interpret it. The assertions are unaffected - none of those overlays contains a cancel token with either separator - and I verified all three negatives against real 0.2.112 panes with true separators, so this is a comment/fixture fidelity nit only. - `bash tests/fm-grok-harness.test.sh` (target commit) - all 4 tests pass including the new `test_grok_busy_regex_matches_realistic_footer_fixtures` - Ran the same new test against base sources (`git archive 3f71cdd` into a temp tree + HEAD test file) - it fails with `not ok - default busy regex missing Esc:cancel`, proving the guard is real - Launched live `grok 0.2.112` in a detached tmux pane (`grok --no-alt-screen --permission-mode plan`) and drove a real turn - Polled the shipped `fm_pane_is_busy` (sourced from bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh) against the live pane target once a second for 24s mid-turn, side by side with the base regex injected via FM_BUSY_REGEX - Replayed fm-watch.sh's own `BUSY_REGEX` default through its `window_is_busy` fallback pipeline (`grep -v blank | tail -6 | grep -qiE`) on the same live pane capture, HEAD vs base - Probed `fm_pane_is_busy` on three live non-busy 0.2.112 overlays: post-turn idle keybind bar, slash autocomplete, and the 'Run Grok Build in a project directory?' chooser - `Compared the FM_BUSY_REGEX string in bin/fm-watch.sh, bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh, and docs/configuration.md for byte equality` - `Rendered the ANSI pane captures to HTML and screenshotted the result with chrome-devtools-axi`
⚠️ **Document** - 2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) - 🚨 `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md:289` - The authoritative owner of the grok busy-pane signature is stale and the intent forbids editing it here. docs/configuration.md:178 names .agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md as the owner of verified busy signatures, but its grok table still says the busy regex is `Ctrl+c:cancel` ("the mid-turn cancel hint in grok's keybind bar, shown iff a turn is running") with no mention of `Esc:cancel`, and the section heading at line 281 still pins verification at grok 0.2.73/0.2.82/0.2.99/0.2.103 with no 0.2.112 re-verification. A reader following configuration.md's pointer now gets the exact fact this change proved wrong on the installed build. The intent explicitly says "Do NOT touch harness-adapters skill (in-flight elsewhere)", so this needs to be folded into that in-flight change: add `Esc:cancel` (0.2.112 mid-turn keybind bar) alongside the retained `Ctrl+c:cancel`, record the captured non-busy overlays, and extend the heading's re-verification list. - ⚠️ `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md:291` - Direct contradiction left unresolved by scope constraints. The Interrupt row asserts "the footer shows `Ctrl+c:cancel` mid-turn", which the empirical 0.2.112 verification behind this change contradicts: mid-turn shows `Esc:cancel` and not `Ctrl+c:cancel`. The row also states "`Esc` only moves focus to the scrollback, it does NOT interrupt", which sits awkwardly next to a mid-turn `Esc:cancel` keybind and may itself be build-dependent. The intent forbids touching both this skill and grok interrupt facts (marked unverified), so the correction needs an empirical interrupt re-check on 0.2.112 rather than a prose edit here.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: feat(bin): detect harness build drift and repair instruction-surface consistency
body:
## Intent Clear the pre-push leak-check gate that blocked the already-complete instruction-surface fix branch (fm/instr-fix at 357a778). That branch carries six instruction-surface fixes plus a detect-only harness build-drift check; that content is done and must not be redone or expanded. The only new change is a single leak-ok end-of-line marker on the one remaining HOMEPATH false positive in tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh:275 (a documentation placeholder /home/state that the scanner misreads because > is not path-blocklisted). Do not add more markers, do not change the detector, do not amend 357a778, do not merge - open a PR for the upstream maintainer. Push must succeed without --no-verify. ## What Changed - Adds `bin/fm-harness-drift.sh`, a detect-only check that parses a new machine-readable `fm-harness-builds` stamp block in `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md` and reports, per harness, whether the recorded stamp matches the installed binary, drifts in either direction, is absent, or is unreadable. It never edits or installs and always exits 0. `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` runs it as a `BOOTSTRAP_INFO: HARNESS_DRIFT:` fact only under `FM_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE_FACTS=1`, after review demoted it from an unconditional session-start probe; otherwise it is run on demand. - Repairs six consistency defects in the always-loaded instruction surfaces: the `stow` knowledge-routing pointer now names a section and list that actually exist in AGENTS.md, AGENTS.md section 9 gains an inline `bearings` trigger, the opencode busy-queued-Enter contract and afk's two self-duplicated contracts collapse to one owner each with cross-references, `firstmate-coding-guidelines` drops a stale line-count measurement from a forward instruction, and the pi adapter record carries a dated currency caveat instead of an unqualified verified header. - Adds `tests/fm-harness-drift.test.sh` covering the outcome cases, the real `--version` shapes of all five harnesses, malformed and missing stamp sources, the read-only property, and a guard that bootstrap invokes the script exactly once behind the verbose flag; adds a shared `fm_fake_stamped_harnesses` helper in `tests/lib.sh` so hermetic silence-asserting suites still exercise the check; records the mechanism in `docs/verification/harness-builds.md` and indexes it in README, `docs/scripts.md`, and `docs/documentation-audiences.json`; marks one known HOMEPATH false positive in `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh` with `leak-ok` so the pre-push leak gate passes without `--no-verify`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Both round-2 findings are fully resolved with honest documentation and a strictly stronger, less brittle regression guard that I verified extracts the correct lines, leaving only one informational note about the test also pinning the call site as mandatory. ## Testing I reproduced the end-user push experience by running the actual leak-check pre-push hook with the stdin git supplies for a new-branch push: at the pre-marker commit it prints GATE: fail with the HOMEPATH hit on tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh:275 and exits 1, and at the branch tip it prints GATE: pass over 17 scanned objects with one suppressed line and exits 0, so the push clears without --no-verify. I confirmed the branch adds exactly one leak-ok marker, that it suppresses a real hit (no stale-suppression warning), and that no scanner or detector file is modified. The behavior test owning the edited file passes, and because the two review commits after the marker also touched the bootstrap and drift-check surfaces I ran those two suites as well; all passed. Working tree left clean, with evidence written only to the evidence directory.
Evidence: Real pre-push hook transcript (blocked before marker, passes after) --- BEFORE the marker: HEAD = 617b22c --- [HOMEPATH] 絶対ホームパス ── ~ / $HOME へ相対化 (1) tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh:275 /home/s*** [SCAN-SET] 列挙 18 件 / 本文走査 18 GATE: fail (巻き込み危険 1 件 ...) leak-check(push): push を中止 ── 上の hit を処置してから再 push hook exit = 1 --- AFTER the marker: HEAD = 9f8daa6 --- [SCAN-SET] 列挙 17 件 / 本文走査 17 `leak-ok` で全検出器を通さなかった行: 1 GATE: pass (PII/secret/実データの巻き込みなし ── 17 件を全数走査) hook exit = 0 ```text $ # real leak-check pre-push hook, new-branch push of fm/instr-fix (stdin as git supplies it) --- BEFORE the marker: HEAD = 617b22c (instruction-surface fixes only) --- [HOMEPATH] 絶対ホームパス ── ~ / $HOME へ相対化 (1) tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh:275 /home/s*** [SCAN-SET] 列挙 18 件 / 本文走査 18 (読んだ中身: object 18) [DENY-INSTRUMENT] 検出器 inactive ── denylist に有効語なし(実名/顧客名は未検査。0 件は clean の意味ではない) repo 単位で張る: /.leak-denylist (gitignore 必須・`re:` で pattern も可) GATE: fail (巻き込み危険 1 件 ── 上を redact / placeholder / .gitignore で処置してから commit) .gitignore 追記案(実データ/秘密はローカル退避先を gitignore): leak-check(push): push を中止 ── 上の hit を処置してから再 push 緊急で通す時のみ: git push --no-verify hook exit = 1 --- AFTER the marker: HEAD = 9f8daa6 (branch tip being pushed) --- [SCAN-SET] 列挙 17 件 / 本文走査 17 (読んだ中身: object 17) `leak-ok` で全検出器を通さなかった行: 1 [DENY-INSTRUMENT] 検出器 inactive ── denylist に有効語なし(実名/顧客名は未検査。0 件は clean の意味ではない) repo 単位で張る: /.leak-denylist (gitignore 必須・`re:` で pattern も可) GATE: pass (PII/secret/実データの巻き込みなし ── 17 件を全数走査) hook exit = 0 ```
Evidence: leak_scan.sh --records-from before/after comparison ```text ##### pre-push simulation: pushing 617b22c (remote base 34213e6) ##### [HOMEPATH] 絶対ホームパス ── ~ / $HOME へ相対化 (1) tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh:275 /home/s*** [SCAN-SET] 列挙 18 件 / 本文走査 18 (読んだ中身: object 18) [DENY-INSTRUMENT] 検出器 inactive ── denylist に有効語なし(実名/顧客名は未検査。0 件は clean の意味ではない) repo 単位で張る: /.leak-denylist (gitignore 必須・`re:` で pattern も可) GATE: fail (巻き込み危険 1 件 ── 上を redact / placeholder / .gitignore で処置してから commit) .gitignore 追記案(実データ/秘密はローカル退避先を gitignore): EXIT=1 ##### pre-push simulation: pushing 9f8daa6 (remote base 34213e6) ##### [SCAN-SET] 列挙 17 件 / 本文走査 17 (読んだ中身: object 17) `leak-ok` で全検出器を通さなかった行: 1 [DENY-INSTRUMENT] 検出器 inactive ── denylist に有効語なし(実名/顧客名は未検査。0 件は clean の意味ではない) repo 単位で張る: /.leak-denylist (gitignore 必須・`re:` で pattern も可) GATE: pass (PII/secret/実データの巻き込みなし ── 17 件を全数走査) EXIT=0 ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ⚠️ `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md:276` - A machine-local observation is baked into a shared tracked instruction surface: "**Pi is not installed on this machine (observed 2026-07-25): `command -v pi` resolves nothing.**". Per AGENTS.md section 12, `.agents/skills/` is loaded verbatim by every running firstmate and secondmate home, so on any home where pi *is* installed this bolded lead sentence is simply false, and the following sentence ("Every fact in this section ... is therefore unverified against any currently present Pi build") inherits that falsehood. Line 279 acknowledges the drift check "self-corrects on a home where pi is present" - which is the argument for letting `fm-harness-drift.sh` report the absence at session start and *not* freezing it into the skill text. This is the same rotting-fact problem this branch deliberately removed from firstmate-coding-guidelines (the "grew from 585 to 958 lines" claim). - ⚠️ `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md:46` - All five recorded stamps ship known-drifted (docs/verification/harness-builds.md:549-554 records the check emitting a drift line for every one of claude, codex, grok, opencode, and pi on introduction). Combined with AGENTS.md:472 and bootstrap-diagnostics/SKILL.md:95, which add `HARNESS_DRIFT:` to the list of actionable lines that mandate loading the `bootstrap-diagnostics` skill, every session start of every fleet member now prints five drift lines and is required to load that skill - only to read "This never blocks work and needs no captain report on its own" (bootstrap-diagnostics/SKILL.md:104). The signal is on from day one and can only be cleared by manually re-verifying five harnesses, so the one failure mode it exists to catch (a drifted busy signature) arrives inside permanent noise, and every session pays the skill-load context cost that firstmate-coding-guidelines exists to prevent. Consider either re-stamping to the currently installed builds as part of this change, or exempting HARNESS_DRIFT from the mandatory bootstrap-diagnostics load trigger. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:874` - The drift check is invoked synchronously in the session-start bootstrap path and probes every recorded harness with `<harness> --version` on every run, with no caching. Measured on this machine: `bin/fm-harness-drift.sh` took ~0.94s wall (opencode alone ~0.45s), added to every session start. Worst case is bounded only by FM_HARNESS_DRIFT_TIMEOUT (default 10s) per harness, so five hanging or slow-starting harnesses can add ~50s to session start before the digest appears. The same cost is multiplied across the test suite - fm-x-mode.test.sh alone invokes fm-bootstrap.sh a dozen-plus times with the ambient PATH, where the probes hit real binaries. A build stamp changes at most once per harness upgrade, so a cached result (e.g. a state marker keyed on the harness binaries' mtimes, refreshed daily) would preserve the signal at near-zero recurring cost. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh:275` - leak_scan.sh's suppression is line-scoped and category-wide (`SUPPRESS = 'leak-ok'` ... "この文字列を含む行は全カテゴリで除外"): the marker `continue`s past SECRET, EMAIL, HOMEPATH, and DENY for that whole line, not just the HOMEPATH detector that false-positived. Here the suppressed line is a fixed prose comment, so the exposure is negligible, and the scanner's own STALE-SUPPRESSION audit reports the marker is actively suppressing a hit rather than sitting dead. Noting the property only so a future edit to that comment line is not assumed to be re-scanned. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh:275` - The intent says "do not amend 357a778". The branch head's parent is 617b22c, not 357a778: same author timestamp (2026-07-25 21:12:43 +0900), new committer timestamp, reparented from 3f71cdd onto 34213e6. The rewrite is a clean rebase that absorbs upstream #1039 (dropping the superseded interim quota-window rule from AGENTS.md:171 and its assertion phrase from tests/fm-instruction-owners.test.sh:118); all six instruction-surface fixes and the drift check are byte-identical. No content was redone or expanded, but the branch no longer carries the commit id named in the intent. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-harness-drift.sh:25` - The either-direction drift rationale is restated near-verbatim in four places: this header (lines 24-27), harness-adapters/SKILL.md:151, docs/verification/harness-builds.md:499, and bootstrap-diagnostics/SKILL.md:103. The owner split is otherwise clean (script owns flags and line formats, skill owns stamps, verification doc owns evidence, bootstrap-diagnostics owns the response), so a single owner for the rationale with pointers from the other three would match the single-ownership discipline the rest of this branch is enforcing. 🔧 Fix: demote harness drift check to opt-in informational fact 4 infos still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:47` - Two surfaces still assert the pre-demotion guarantee. bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:47 says the comparison runs "so a documented harness fact cannot silently expire", and docs/verification/harness-builds.md:5 says "This record supports the current guarantee that a documented harness fact cannot silently expire". After this commit nothing runs the comparison by default: on a home that never sets FM_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE_FACTS=1 and never invokes bin/fm-harness-drift.sh, a harness update expires a fact with no signal at all - precisely the state bin/fm-harness-drift.sh:7-9 describes as the defect the check was written to fix. The demotion is the right call and harness-adapters:43 states the new contract correctly ("Run it deliberately, before relying on a harness fact you have not re-verified yourself"); only these two leftover "cannot silently expire"/"guarantee" phrasings now overstate what ships. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-harness-drift.test.sh:212` - The new regression guard proves that *a* guarded invocation exists (`guarded` non-empty, containing BOOTSTRAP_INFO) but never proves that *no unguarded* invocation exists. A future edit that adds a second, unconditional `"$SCRIPT_DIR/fm-harness-drift.sh"` outside the FM_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE_FACTS block leaves this test green while reintroducing the exact per-session-start probe cost this commit removed - and tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh's silence assertions would not catch it either, because fm_fake_stamped_harnesses seeds the harnesses at their recorded stamps so the check stays silent there. Inverting the awk to collect occurrences where `guard` is 0 and failing on any would close the hole. Related brittleness: the extractor keys on the exact source shape (`^if [ "${FM_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE_FACTS:-0}" = 1 ]` at column 0, terminated by `^fi$`), so an indentation or nesting change fails the test with a misleading message even when behavior is correct. - ℹ️ `tests/lib.sh:114` - With the drift check gated behind FM_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE_FACTS=1, fm_fake_stamped_harnesses is load-bearing at only one of its four call sites. No script under bin/ ever sets that variable (it is caller-supplied only), and tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh:743 is the sole test that passes it, so the seeding at tests/fm-session-start.test.sh:86, tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh:780, and tests/fm-secondmate-sync.test.sh:353 now installs five fake harness binaries into hermetic fakebins for a check that never runs in those suites. It is inert rather than harmful - no bin/ code does `command -v <harness>` - and the helper's updated comment already narrows its stated purpose to the verbose path. Recording it only so the three redundant call sites are a known cleanup, not a lost invariant; not proposing removal in this tightly scoped round. - ℹ️ `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md:42` - The stated intent says the six instruction-surface fixes plus the drift check "is done and must not be redone or expanded" and that "The only new change is a single leak-ok end-of-line marker". Commit 0a44d94 edits eight files of that content (harness-adapters, bootstrap-diagnostics, AGENTS.md, fm-bootstrap.sh, fm-harness-drift.sh, harness-builds.md, and two test files). This is not treated as a contradiction because the round-1 review loop carries explicit user direction to make exactly these three corrections ("All three are defects this branch itself introduced, so fix them; do not expand scope beyond correcting them"), which is a later and more specific authorization from the same user. The commit stays inside that authorization: it touches only the drift-check surfaces, and bootstrap-diagnostics/SKILL.md is now byte-identical to the base commit. Recorded for traceability only. 🔧 Fix: state drift check gap honestly, harden invocation guard test 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `tests/fm-harness-drift.test.sh:220` - The hardened guard asserts the invocation count is exactly 1, which encodes two invariants: no unguarded call (the requested one) and at least one call. The second half means a future maintainer who takes the drift check fully on-demand by deleting the bootstrap call site entirely - the direction round 1 explicitly preferred ("Removing the call site is preferred over making the probe faster") - gets a test failure reading "bootstrap must invoke fm-harness-drift.sh exactly once" even though that state is strictly cheaper and still correct. It fails closed with a legible message rather than silently, and it accurately pins today's design, so this is a note rather than a defect; changing `-eq 1` to `-le 1` would keep the anti-regression half without forbidding removal.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `sh ~/.claude/skills/leak-check/hooks/pre-push` fed the real git pre-push stdin record for a new-branch push of fm/instr-fix, at 617b22c (fail, exit 1) and at 9f8daa6 (pass, exit 0) - `sh ~/.claude/skills/leak-check/leak_scan.sh --records-from <git diff --raw -z 34213e6..<sha>>` for both commits, confirming the single HOMEPATH hit disappears and one line is recorded as suppressed with no STALE-SUPPRESSION warning - `bash bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh` - `bash bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-harness-drift.test.sh tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` - `grep -rn "leak-ok"` over the tracked tree plus `git diff 34213e6..9f8daa6 -U0 | grep -c '^+.*leak-ok'` to confirm exactly one marker was added and only one exists - `git diff --name-only 34213e6..9f8daa6 | grep -iE 'leak|scan'` to confirm the detector is untouched
🔧 **Document** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md:278` - The sixth instruction-surface fix described in 617b22c's commit message - marking the pi section as unverified against any present build, kept-and-marked per an explicit captain decision - is no longer in the tree. Review commit 0a44d94 removed all four sentences of that marking because one of them ("reports this absence at session start") became false when the drift check went opt-in. The pi section now reads "## pi (VERIFIED 2026-06-11)" with no currency caveat, while docs/verification/harness-builds.md, added by this same change, records `pi: NOT INSTALLED`. I did not restore it: the user intent freezes the branch's six fixes as done and not to be redone, and there is a real placement argument for the removal - "pi is not installed on this machine" is a home-local observation, and its owner is now the dated evidence in docs/verification/harness-builds.md plus the drift check itself, not the always-shipped shared skill. The residual gap is only that the pi header claims currency the generic "Recorded build stamps" caveat softens rather than states. Maintainer call: accept the generic caveat as sufficient, or re-add a one-line pi caveat without the false session-start claim. 🔧 Fix: restore dated currency caveat on pi adapter record ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: test(watcher): cover drift-free pid identity for issue #1014

## Intent Fix kunchenguid/firstmate issue #1014 by ensuring fm-watch.sh watcher PID identity is drift-free on Linux through /proc//stat field 22, parsed after the comm field's closing parenthesis, while preserving the existing ps -o lstart fallback for macOS and hosts without usable /proc. The shared fm_pid_identity write and comparison path must remain consistent for watcher-continuity and turn-end guards across every supported primary harness and runtime backend. Add deterministic regression coverage for two immediate reads of a fresh Linux PID, proof that the Linux /proc path bypasses drifting ps output, and the macOS/no-/proc ps fallback. Do not alter PR #1015's wedge/progress subject matter. Current main already contains the requested production implementation from merged PR #752, so this branch intentionally adds the explicit #1014 regression cases that prove and preserve that behavior. The PR description must include Fixes #1014. ## What Changed - Added `test_linux_pid_identity_is_stable_across_immediate_reads` to `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh`, proving that two immediate `fm_pid_identity` reads of a fresh Linux PID return the same `/proc//stat`-derived starttime and never fall through to the drifting `ps` fallback. - Added `test_macos_pid_identity_uses_ps_fallback_without_proc`, confirming the existing `ps -o lstart=` fallback is invoked and its output preserved unchanged when `/proc` is unavailable (macOS/no-proc hosts). - Wired both new regression cases into the existing test runner sequence alongside the current locale-invariance and pid-reuse coverage; no production code (`bin/fm-wake-lib.sh`) was modified. Fixes #1014 ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is purely additive test coverage (no production code touched) that exercises the already-merged fm_pid_identity implementation: it verifies the macOS/no-proc ps fallback is preserved, and that a fresh Linux PID's /proc-based identity is stable across two immediate reads and never falls back to the drifting ps path, matching the intent's required regression cases. ## Testing Ran the full tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh suite natively on Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, WSL2): all 30 checks passed (exit 0), including the two new #1014 regression tests — one proving two immediate reads of a fresh Linux PID return a stable `linux-starttime=...` identity without ever invoking the drifting `ps` fallback, and one proving the macOS/no-/proc path still routes through and preserves the `ps -o lstart=` fallback output. Diffed base against target commit and confirmed the change is test-only; the production /proc-field-22 implementation in bin/fm-wake-lib.sh (fm_pid_identity) is unmodified, matching the stated intent that it was already merged via PR #752 and this branch only adds proving regression coverage. No related files (fm-watch.sh, fm-afk-start.sh, fm-supervise-daemon.sh, fm-afk-launch.sh) were touched. Working tree is clean after the run with no transient artifacts left behind.
Evidence: fm-watcher-lock.test.sh full run output (30/30 passing, including the two new #1014 regression tests) ```text ok - simultaneous watcher starts leave exactly one live process ok - fm_pid_identity is locale-invariant across LC_ALL/LC_TIME ok - macOS fm_pid_identity preserves the ps fallback when proc is unavailable ok - fresh Linux process identity is immediately stable and bypasses ps ok - Linux process identity ignores simulated btime changes ok - Linux process identity detects pid reuse ok - killed watcher stale lock is reclaimed ok - live watcher lock with stale heartbeat is actionable ok - guard banner leads when down with pending wakes (repair-after-drain) and stays silent when fresh ok - concurrent fm_lock_try_acquire yields exactly one winner ok - dead-pid stale lock is reclaimed by a single acquirer ok - concurrent stale-lock steal yields exactly one winner ok - live steal mutex is not reclaimed ok - live-held lock is not stolen ok - empty mid-acquire lock keeps a minimum grace ok - late original claimant cannot claim a recreated lock ok - paused mid-acquire claimant backs off to active stealer ok - watch restart refuses to signal a reused pid ok - watch restart attaches to a verified healthy peer and later surfaces a successor gap ok - watcher self-evicts when the lock pid no longer names it ok - arm turns clean self-eviction without a successor into a typed failure ok - arm attaches to a live fresh watcher and fails loudly when that cycle has no successor ok - attached arm signals record a classified lifecycle entry ok - arm starts+confirms a fresh watcher on a clean lock and self-heals a dead-pid lock (never healthy off a dead pid) ok - arm cleans child watcher and temp output on HUP ok - arm propagates an immediate watcher wake before confirmation ok - arm attaches to a peer watcher after child stands down and surfaces a missing successor watcher: lock held by live pid 487758 but heartbeat is stale for 838302525s (>300s); title: feat(bin): add verified Kimi crewmate harness adapter
body:
## Intent

Add Kimi Code CLI as a verified firstmate crewmate/scout harness adapter and ship it upstream-ready. The requested scope is passive crewmate/scout support only: do not add Kimi-hosted primary firstmate support, turn-end guard ownership, session-start nudges, or Kimi secondmate support. The adapter should launch a Kimi worker using the real local Kimi Code CLI evidence from 2026-07-25, solve launch-brief ingestion without supervisor babysitting, validate model support fail-closed through a Kimi CLI preflight before metadata writes, follow the fleet convention for Kimi effort by passing effort only for the verified k3 effort-support family and otherwise recording requested effort while omitting the hint flag, verify sends without blind double-submit on swallowed Enter, report busy/idle/exited state through the existing tmux/backend mechanisms, allow kimi in crew dispatch profile validation, and document version-stamped Kimi facts in the harness-adapters skill plus a maintainer verification record. The implementation intentionally uses prompt-mode bootstrap to seed the launch brief, parses the emitted session_id, resumes the same cwd-bound session with --auto -S, rejects Kimi secondmate launches, avoids bespoke TOML parsing, treats Kimi supervision as stale-based because no installed 0.29.1 hook-backed crew turn-end path was verified, keeps AGENTS.md to the one-line verified-harness update, preserves plain-dash and one-sentence-per-line Markdown, and pushes the branch to the jokim1 fork while opening the PR against kunchenguid/firstmate. Late review decisions require Kimi bootstrap profile validation to be model-aware: explicit k3-family models validate low/high/max, non-k3 Kimi models accept any shared effort value because spawn records it and omits the hint, and bootstrap must never reject a profile the spawn path lawfully launches.

## What Changed

- Add Kimi Code CLI crewmate and scout spawning with prompt-mode brief ingestion, same-session resume, fail-closed model preflight, and model-aware effort forwarding.
- Integrate Kimi with dispatch validation and tmux liveness and busy-state reporting while explicitly rejecting secondmate launches.

title: fix(tmux): scope busy detection and recognize current Claude turns
body:
## Intent URGENT production fix for firstmate Claude busy-pane supervision. Current Claude Code 2.1.220 no longer prints 'esc to interrupt'; detect active Claude turns using the verified structural invariant ellipsis followed by parenthesized elapsed time, while preserving the legacy Claude token and leaving Pi and Grok signatures unchanged. Also fix the existing harness-argument defect: fm_pane_is_busy must honor the supplied harness and match only that harness's verified signature, with the historical combined-pattern fallback when no harness is supplied; mirror that scoping in fm-watch. Keep Claude's signature harness-scoped because the shared pattern could false-positive ordinary output. Tests must use multiple real capture shapes with changed glyph and word, a real Worked-for idle negative, cross-harness negatives, and live end-to-end proof. The PR body must explicitly state these are two independent fixes combined because they touch the same function, and that reverting either also reverts the other. Lead the harness-scoping motivation with the concrete verified example that Kimi's idle tip can rotate through 'ctrl+c: cancel', which matches Grok's busy token, causing an idle Kimi pane to be classified busy, and state that Claude's missing signature compounded the cross-harness issue. ## What Changed - Fix harness-scoped busy detection across watchers and supervisors: Kimi's idle tip can rotate through `ctrl+c: cancel`, matching Grok's busy token and falsely classifying an idle Kimi pane as busy; Claude's missing signature compounded this cross-harness issue. Supplied harnesses now match only their verified signatures, while callers without harness metadata retain the historical combined fallback. - Detect active Claude Code 2.1.220 turns through the harness-scoped ellipsis-plus-parenthesized-elapsed-time shape, while preserving the legacy Claude token and leaving Pi and Grok signatures unchanged. Add regression coverage for real Claude capture shapes, the `Worked for` idle state, and cross-harness negatives. - These are two independent fixes combined because they touch the same busy-matching function. Reverting either also reverts the other. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The repaired dispatcher now separates exact verified signatures, the empty compatibility path, and the explicitly authorized unknown-harness fallback, with focused regression coverage and no remaining material source defect found. ## Testing Diff and call-site inspection, the focused regression test, and live isolated tmux verification all succeeded: Claude’s new and legacy signatures, the Worked-for idle negative, and Kimi/Grok/Pi cross-harness scoping produced the required direct and watcher classifications. The change is CLI-only, so a reviewer-visible transcript was captured instead of a screenshot.
Evidence: Live tmux and watcher behavior transcript ```text Claude active capture A | harness=claude | direct=busy | watcher=busy | expected=busy | capture=✢ Pollinating… (16s · ↓ 1.1k tokens · thought for 1s) Claude active capture B | harness=claude | direct=busy | watcher=busy | expected=busy | capture=✽ Proofing… (5s · thinking with high effort) Claude completed capture | harness=claude | direct=idle | watcher=idle | expected=idle | capture=✻ Worked for 31s Claude legacy capture | harness=claude | direct=busy | watcher=busy | expected=busy | capture=esc to interrupt Idle Kimi rotating tip | harness=kimi | direct=idle | watcher=idle | expected=idle | capture=Ctrl+c:cancel Active Grok capture | harness=grok | direct=busy | watcher=busy | expected=busy | capture=Ctrl+c:cancel Pi token under Claude | harness=claude | direct=idle | watcher=idle | expected=idle | capture=Working... RESULT: all live tmux and metadata-driven watcher classifications matched the required harness-scoped behavior. ```
- Outcome: 🔧 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ across 2 runs (7m52s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh:88` - The required behavior says the historical combined-pattern fallback applies "when no harness is supplied," but this `*` branch deliberately applies it to every unknown nonempty harness. A supplied harness such as `kimi` therefore still evaluates Grok/Pi/escape tokens instead of only its verified signature. Split the empty-harness compatibility case from unknown harnesses, and register each verified harness explicitly. - 🚨 `bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh:70` - The required behavior says a supplied harness must "match only that harness's verified signature," but Claude and Codex retain `esc (to )?interrupt`, which also matches OpenCode's verified `esc interrupt` footer. Thus `fm_pane_is_busy <pane> claude` or `codex` can still classify OpenCode output as busy. Use the exact legacy `esc to interrupt` token for Claude/Codex and keep `esc interrupt` exclusive to OpenCode. 🔧 Fix: Separate verified and fallback busy signatures ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
🔧 **Test** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh:89` - `fm_busy_lines_match` uses the historical combined regex for every unknown nonempty harness. This violates the required rule that the combined fallback applies only when no harness is supplied. It also preserves the motivating cross-harness failure: a real tmux pane carrying Grok's `Ctrl+c:cancel` token was classified busy with `harness=kimi`, both by `fm_pane_is_busy` and fm-watch's metadata-driven `window_is_busy`. The focused regression added at test line 182 fails on this case. - Inspected `git diff 34213e66a8c65a46098e5d7fd590987bdbfefd09..db7a502b66ac60a442994836da3bd41d0a7de8c7` to separate signature detection from harness propagation. - Ran `bash tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh` against the committed tests; existing registered-harness cases passed. - Added the missing Kimi/unknown-harness regression to `tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh` and reran `bash tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh`; it failed at `Kimi must ignore Pi's Working footer`. - Created real panes with `tmux -L nm-01KYDXJGDR6E8KZGG7ZQYBVY9M new-session`, captured their rendered output, and exercised `fm_pane_is_busy` for current Claude, idle Claude, registered cross-harness, omitted-harness, and Kimi cases. - Sourced `bin/fm-watch.sh` with task metadata and exercised `window_is_busy` against the same real tmux Claude and Kimi panes. - `Verified the temporary tmux server was terminated and the only worktree change is the intentional focused regression test.` 🔧 Fix: Scope busy signatures to supplied harnesses ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain. - Inspected `git diff 34213e66a8c65a46098e5d7fd590987bdbfefd09..a6db74419175b44b380d664a8d46ac096e5f5a42` and all busy-detection call sites - `bash tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh` - Live isolated tmux exercise of `fm_pane_is_busy` and metadata-driven `fm-watch.sh::window_is_busy` across two Claude 2.1.220 captures, Claude idle and legacy captures, Kimi/Grok shared-token cases, and a cross-harness Pi negative - `Verified the evidence transcript, clean worktree, and isolated tmux server cleanup`

title: test: shim git in test fixtures so path captures survive hook stdout
body:
## Intent Make the unsafe test-fixture shape unrepeatable: helpers that run git commit/push (hook-bearing) and return a path via stdout were silently corrupted when any hook wrote instruments to git's stdout (global core.hooksPath leak scanner on this machine exposed it; the shape was always fragile). Do not blame or change the scanner, core.hooksPath, or leak-check; do not disable hooks in fixtures as the fix. Chosen mechanism: tests/lib.sh installs a PATH shim for git (not a shell function) so hook-bearing subcommands relocate stdout to stderr by default - path capture via dir=$(helper) stays pure, while command -v git remains an absolute path so symlink toolbins and re-exec PATH mocks keep working. FM_TEST_REAL_GIT pins the real binary; shim shebang uses absolute bash for restricted PATH. Escape hatch FM_TEST_GIT_HOOK_STDOUT=keep. Regression pin in tests/fm-fixture-git-stdout.test.sh. Teardown/fleet-sync/secondmate-sync mocks use FM_TEST_REAL_GIT. Family map updated for the new test. Acceptance is durability: a new test author writing the obvious capture form must not get a silently corrupted path. Do not weaken assertions. Expect rebase later vs open PR 1043 which also touches tests/lib.sh. Open PR and stop; merge authority is upstream. ## What Changed - `tests/lib.sh` now installs a generated `git` PATH shim (not a shell function) ahead of `PATH` at library load. It re-execs the absolute real binary recorded in the new `FM_TEST_REAL_GIT` and relocates git's stdout to stderr by default, keeping stdout only for an allow-list of read-only subcommands (`rev-parse`, `status`, `diff`, `worktree list`, `remote get-url`, ...). Hook-bearing subcommands like `commit`/`push`/`clone` can therefore no longer inject hook instruments into `dir=$(helper)` captures, while `command -v git` still resolves to an absolute path so symlinked toolbins and re-exec PATH mocks keep working. `FM_TEST_GIT_HOOK_STDOUT=keep` restores the pre-fix stream layout for deliberate probes, and the shim shebang uses an absolute bash for restricted-PATH callers. - Temp-root cleanup moved to a file-mediated registry: the EXIT trap is installed at library load and `fm_test_tmproot` appends to `$FM_TEST_CLEANUP_LIST` instead of pushing to a bash array that dies with the command-substitution subshell, so fixture roots and the shim dir are actually reclaimed. `tests/wake-helpers.sh` drops its now-dead lazy trap install. - Added `tests/fm-fixture-git-stdout.test.sh` pinning the safe default, the `keep`-mode failure, and the `command -v` / re-exec safety properties, registered it in the `bin/fm-test-run.sh` family map, and switched the `fm-teardown` / `fm-fleet-sync` / `fm-secondmate-sync` git mocks to `FM_TEST_REAL_GIT`. Pipeline: review, test, lint, docs and push stages all pass; the Document stage auto-fixed an SC2317 lint hit and a shim-dir leak. Remaining review comments are informational only. One `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh` scheduler case is load-sensitive and was confirmed pre-existing at the base commit. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Both round-1 warnings are genuinely fixed - the file-mediated registry survives the command-substitution subshell that defeated the array push, and the inverted allow-list removes the unfinishable deny-list - and a static sweep of every stdout-consuming git call site in the repo (plus the leak scanner's own hooks) found each one covered by the allow-list, leaving only two info-level notes in tests-only code that carries a dedicated regression pin. ## Testing I reproduced the real defect end-to-end before validating the fix: running `tests/fm-update.test.sh` from the base commit on this machine, where a global `core.hooksPath` leak scanner writes `[SCAN-SET]` instruments to git's stdout, fails with `fatal: cannot change to '\n[SCAN-SET] ...'` because the hook output joins the fixture's path capture; the same test at the target commit passes with the scanner still running and its instruments now on stderr, so nothing was disabled. For the authoritative durability criterion I wrote a fresh helper in the obvious `w=$(new_world ...)` shape and ran it against base and target `tests/lib.sh` - base yields a 6-line corrupted path, target yields a single usable path. The new regression pin passes all six cases including the `FM_TEST_GIT_HOOK_STDOUT=keep` failure mode and the `command -v` / toolbin-symlink safety properties, and I ran the ten suites touching the changed seams (teardown, fleet-sync, secondmate-sync, lint, crew-state, wake-queue, session-start, secondmate-safety, secondmate-liveness, update) plus `--check-coverage` for the family map - all green. I additionally audited every `$(git ...)` capture site in tests/ to confirm the allow-list does not silently empty an existing assertion, and measured that the tmproot fix stops the per-run temp-dir leak the base commit still has. One sub-case in `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh` flaked under load but reproduces identically at the base commit and involves no git or lib.sh, so it is pre-existing and unrelated. No visual artifacts apply: this is a shell test-fixture library change with no rendered end-user surface.

Widening the list changes which streams tests observe, so the scope call is the author's. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh:61` - Three comments justify `FM_TEST_REAL_GIT` with a reason the PATH-shim commit made false. tests/fm-teardown.test.sh:61-62 says lib.sh "shadows `git` with a path-safe wrapper; do not use `command -v git` here - that returns the function name after lib is sourced"; tests/fm-fleet-sync.test.sh:191 and tests/fm-secondmate-sync.test.sh:250 repeat "not `command -v git` (function name)". There is no shell function any more, and tests/fm-fixture-git-stdout.test.sh:100-104 explicitly pins that `command -v git` is absolute. The real reason is that `command -v git` now resolves to the shim and these mocks want the unwrapped binary. Comment-only correction; keeps FM_TEST_REAL_GIT as the intent requires. - ℹ️ `tests/wake-helpers.sh:40` - `if [ "${#FM_TEST_CLEANUP_DIRS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then trap fm_test_cleanup EXIT; fi` can no longer fire: tests/lib.sh:179 seeds the array with the wrap dir at load, so the length is never 0 in any consumer. The identical guard at tests/fm-lint.test.sh:421-423 is dead for the same reason. Behavior is unaffected (lib.sh installs the trap), but both now document a lazy-install contract that no longer exists. - ℹ️ `tests/lib.sh:127` - In the generated shim's argument scan, the `--git-dir=*|--work-tree=*|--namespace=*|--config-env=*` arm and the `--bare|--no-replace-objects|--literal-pathspecs|--glob-pathspecs|--noglob-pathspecs|--icase-pathspecs` arm both do exactly what the later `-*)` catch-all does. Only the `-C|--git-dir|--work-tree|--namespace|--config-env|-c` arm (separate-value options needing `skip=1`) carries meaning. Collapsing lines 124-133 to a single `-*) continue ;;` drops ten lines of generated shell plus a line continuation inside the heredoc and makes the one load-bearing arm obvious. - ℹ️ `tests/lib.sh:147` - `exec "$real" "$@" 1>&2` applies after the caller's own redirections, so stdout a script deliberately discarded reappears on stderr under test. bin/fm-merge-local.sh:66 runs `git -C "$PROJ" merge --ff-only "$BRANCH" >/dev/null`; under the shim that /dev/null becomes the shim's stdout, which is then redirected into its stderr, making "Updating x..y / Fast-forward" visible in tests but not in production. Nothing trips on it today (the two capturing call sites, bin/fm-ff-lib.sh:360 and bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:400, use `2>&1`, so content is preserved), but a future `[ ! -s "$err" ]` assertion around any script that runs commit/merge/pull will fail for a suite-only reason. Worth a sentence in the lib.sh header. 🔧 Fix: invert git wrap to allow-list and fix tmproot leak 2 infos still open: - ℹ️ `tests/lib.sh:152` - Two allow-listed subcommands are not strictly hook-free: `git status` (and `git diff`) write the index when they refresh it, which fires the `post-index-change` hook whose stdout lands on git's stdout. A global core.hooksPath carrying a printing post-index-change hook would still pollute `x=$(git -C "$d" status --porcelain)` at bin/fm-ff-lib.sh:228 and bin/fm-merge-local.sh:53. Relocating them is not an option - those callers need the stdout - so the allow-list entry is the right call, but the header at tests/lib.sh:39-42 states that what is missing from the allow-list is only "a read-only subcommand" that "fails loudly", which reads as an absolute guarantee. Worth one sentence noting that allow-listed subcommands are trusted to be hook-free and that index-writing reads are the known edge. No impact today: the scanner in play installs only pre-commit and pre-push. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-fixture-git-stdout.test.sh:91` - The new allow-list assertion matches a commit id with exactly forty `?` wildcards. `build_world` runs plain `git init -q --bare`, which inherits `init.defaultObjectFormat` from the machine's global config; with sha256 set there `git rev-parse HEAD` returns 64 hex chars, the case arm misses, and the pin fails with "rev-parse must return a bare commit id on stdout" - a message pointing at the wrap rather than at the object format. That is the same class of machine-config coupling this file exists to eliminate. Asserting a non-empty all-hex string, or comparing against the seed's own rev-parse output, proves the same property without the length assumption.
⚠️ **Test** - 1 info - ℹ️ `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh:569` - `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh` case `jobs=2 must refill the first completed slot` is load-sensitive and flaked once when run 8th in a long serial batch. It is unrelated to this change: its fixture repo holds a copy of the runner plus three inline `sleep` scripts with no git and no `tests/lib.sh`, and the assertion depends on a replacement worker starting within the slow fixture's 0.5s sleep. Confirmed pre-existing - it fails 3/3 at base commit 34213e6 under artificial CPU load, and passes 3/3 standalone at the target commit. body:
## Intent Build a vetted, safe way for the firstmate fleet to run FreeLLMAPI as a local cheap bulk/research lane, with the captain condition that API keys are handled carefully. Deliver: (1) bin/fm-freellmapi.sh runner that pins FreeLLMAPI to an audited commit, generates ENCRYPTION_KEY safely, binds only to 127.0.0.1, health-checks, and stops cleanly without leaking secrets to stdout/logs/argv; (2) docs/freellmapi-lane.md for allowed/forbidden use, known risks (dependency vulns, third-party prompt egress), and removal; (3) tests for no secret leakage, localhost-only bind, and fail-closed config. Do not wire the lane into any automatic dispatch or profile path. Follow-up correction after external review: honest secret-safety claims (never on argv/not printed; live only in process env, mode-0600 files, stdin; same OS user can still inspect; warn about shell xtrace), status only alerts on non-loopback while start stops, and branch rebased cleanly onto main so the PR contains only this work. Local merge of fm-test-run.sh family list kept main's documentation-audiences entry and added fm-freellmapi.test.sh. ## What Changed - Add an opt-in FreeLLMAPI runner pinned to an audited commit, with explicit risk acceptance, localhost-only startup verification, health checks, key seeding, and clean shutdown. - Harden secret and process handling with mode-0600 files, stdin/environment transport, recorded process identity, and fail-closed behavior for unverifiable listeners or live PID records. - Document allowed use, known risks, and removal, and register behavior tests covering secret leakage, loopback binding, process identity, and configuration failures. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The latest change correctly refuses to overwrite a live but unauthenticated PID record, and the complete FreeLLMAPI lane now satisfies the reviewed safety and intent constraints without additional material source risks. ## Testing Diff and clean-worktree baselines were checked; the focused FreeLLMAPI suite exercised pinned installation, secret non-leakage, localhost-only binding, fail-closed startup, non-loopback status behavior, key seeding, and graceful/identity-safe stopping, while a reviewer-visible CLI transcript demonstrated policy help and real refusal paths. Everything passed with no actionable findings; no screenshot was produced because this is a CLI-only change, and no broad suite, lint, static analysis, push, PR, or CI phase was run.
Evidence: FreeLLMAPI end-user CLI transcript ```text $ bin/fm-freellmapi.sh --help fm-freellmapi.sh - manage the fleet's pinned, localhost-only FreeLLMAPI lane. FreeLLMAPI (https://github.com/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi, MIT) is a third-party local proxy that pools free-tier LLM provider keys behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. This script is the single owner of the fleet's vetted install: it pins one audited upstream commit, generates the mandatory ENCRYPTION_KEY without ever printing it, starts the service bound to 127.0.0.1 only, verifies that binding before declaring success, seeds provider keys from the fleet's gitignored .env without exposing their values, and stops the service cleanly. Non-sensitive bulk/scout use only - docs/freellmapi-lane.md owns the usage policy, known-risk statement, and removal procedure. Usage: fm-freellmapi.sh install --accept-risks install or repair the pinned build fm-freellmapi.sh start [--port

] [--catalog-sync] fm-freellmapi.sh status [--port

] fm-freellmapi.sh seed-keys = [= ...] fm-freellmapi.sh stop fm-freellmapi.sh --help The install lives under $FM_HOME/data/freellmapi (gitignored, chmod 0700): app/ upstream checkout at the exact pinned commit, built db/freeapi.db service state, kept outside app/ so reinstall preserves it encryption.key generated 64-hex AES-256-GCM key, mode 0600 dashboard.credentials generated local dashboard login, mode 0600 run/server.pid run/server.log runtime records Secret-safety contract (the reason this wrapper exists): - Secret values (provider keys, ENCRYPTION_KEY, dashboard password, session token) never appear in stdout, stderr, argv, this script's error messages, or files other than the mode-0600 secret files listed above. Secrets travel to child processes via environment or stdin only, never command arguments (never on argv; not printed). At runtime they live only in process env, mode-0600 files, and stdin pipes; the same OS user can still inspect those (for example /proc//environ on Linux). Do not run this script under shell xtrace (bash -x or set -o xtrace): it dumps env assignments and pipes. - This script never prints the server log; on failure it prints the log path. - start verifies every TCP listener of the server process is bound to 127.0.0.1 and stops the server if verification fails; status fails with a warning on the same condition but does not stop (use stop for that). - install refuses to run without --accept-risks and restates the known dependency-vulnerability findings every time. $ FM_HOME= bin/fm-freellmapi.sh status fm-freellmapi.sh: not running [exit: 1] $ FM_HOME= bin/fm-freellmapi.sh install KNOWN RISKS - FreeLLMAPI lane (pin 526c86349891bd336b470481ee2d732cd8e13c14, 2026-07-20): - npm ci at this pin reported 21 dependency vulnerabilities (3 critical, 7 high, 9 moderate, 2 low; npm audit 2026-07-24). - npm ci executes dependency install scripts (native modules build at install). - Every prompt sent through the lane goes to third-party free providers; some keyless providers may use prompts for training. - This service is for ISOLATED LOCAL USE ONLY: localhost binding, no tunnel, no port forwarding, no sensitive content, never a primary-model substitute. Full policy: docs/freellmapi-lane.md and data/freellmapi-koeajo/report.md. fm-freellmapi.sh: refusing to install without --accept-risks (read the risk statement above and docs/freellmapi-lane.md first) [exit: 1] $ FM_HOME= bin/fm-freellmapi.sh start (malformed mode-0600 ENCRYPTION_KEY) fm-freellmapi.sh: encryption key at /var/folders/_7/g__lbpks7bvb7_3fqhncphnm0000gp/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYDZT1RR518JMEN92DXSGN16/isolated-home/data/freellmapi/encryption.key is not 64 lowercase hex chars; refusing to start (regenerate by removing the file - existing stored provider keys become unreadable) [exit: 1] ```
