fix: harden session-lock reclaim and typed failures
body:
## Intent Fix Firstmate session-lock P0 and two P1 findings on the existing lock-hardening branch (fm/lukko-korjauskierros, built on fm/lukko-korjaus-p0 commits 41423e0/17f28b7/2446877). Goals: 1. P0: Recover from an orphaned state/.lock-reclaim mutex that previously jammed all lock ownership forever. Write owner PID + timestamp into the mutex dir; only reclaim when the owner process is proven dead (or a legacy no-pid dir ages past the mid-acquire threshold). Never override a live mutex owner. Do not use flock (unavailable/unwanted on macOS); follow the same portable "provably abandoned" pattern as other locks in this repo. Document emergency removal in the script header. 2. P1: Separate temporary reclaim-mutex contention from IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE via a new typed RECLAIM_BUSY outcome; keep main-lock status truthful (stale stays stale); session-start short-retries busy; supervision text points at retry/status rather than identity recovery. 3. P1: Every reclaim failure path must emit LOCK_RESULT= and reclassify based on the actual lock state (no bare return 1 with only English errors). Constraints: no-mistakes-level quality for firstmate's own lock machinery; extend existing tests; leave known env reds (Pi version, Orca bash 3.2) alone. Deliberate tradeoffs: mkdir-based mutex with PID proof rather than flock; RECLAIM_BUSY as its own exit 13; short busy retries in lock acquire and session-start. ## What Changed - Harden session-lock acquisition and stale-owner recovery with PID/timestamp ownership, generation fencing, retained ABA tombstones, and guarded handling of malformed reclaim state. - Add typed lock outcomes—including `RECLAIM_BUSY`—across reclaim failures, with truthful main-lock reclassification and short contention retries during acquisition and session start. - Update supervision guidance, documentation, and lock-focused tests for non-owned states, orphan recovery, live-owner protection, interrupted reclaim, and unsafe filesystem entries. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The marker-based usage extraction fixes the help regression without changing lock behavior, and the full reviewed change satisfies the stated lock-recovery and typed-outcome invariants. ## Testing Focused lock, session-start, and supervision tests pass after test-only compatibility and expectation fixes; manual CLI evidence confirms orphan recovery, protection of a live reclaim-mutex owner, typed exit 13, truthful stale main-lock status, and retry/status guidance.
Evidence: Session-lock end-to-end CLI transcript `Shows orphan recovery, live-owner preservation, exit 13 RECLAIM_BUSY, truthful STALE_RECLAIMABLE status, and retry guidance.` ```text SCENARIO 1: orphaned reclaim mutex is recovered and stale main lock is acquired LOCK_RESULT=OWNED lock acquired: harness pid 92701 persisted main lock: 92701 reclaim mutex remains: no SCENARIO 2: live reclaim mutex is never overridden and returns typed exit 13 LOCK_RESULT=RECLAIM_BUSY error: reclaim mutex busy (another reclaim operation holds state/.lock-reclaim); retry briefly and re-check bin/fm-lock.sh status exit_code=13 live mutex pid after attempt: 9818 main lock after attempt: 999999 status while mutex is busy: LOCK_RESULT=STALE_RECLAIMABLE lock: stale and reclaimable (pid 999999 is not alive) supervision guidance for RECLAIM_BUSY: Mode: non-owned lock state (RECLAIM_BUSY) - supervision withheld. The ordinary supervision protocol and every other fleet-mutating instruction are withheld: no non-owned lock state may mutate fleet state. The reclaim mutex is temporarily held; this is not an identity failure. Do not treat this as IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE and do not force the lock free. The one permitted mutation is a short retry of the atomic reclaim path: 1. Re-check with bin/fm-lock.sh status (stale owners remain STALE_RECLAIMABLE). 2. Retry bin/fm-lock.sh (or reclaim --expected ) briefly. 3. On LOCK_RESULT=OWNED, re-run bin/fm-session-start.sh; it continues as the owner into the wake-queue drain and this harness's normal supervision protocol. Every other mutation stays withheld until this session owns the lock. ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Rebase** - 3 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `AGENTS.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main - ⚠️ `bin/fm-lock.sh` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main - ⚠️ `tests/fm-session-start.test.sh` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main 🔧 Fix applied. ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
🔧 **Review** - 6 issues found → auto-fixed (11) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:376` - The durable P0 invariant remains reachable: two contenders can both prove the old mutex owner dead; after one removes and recreates the directory with its live PID, the other can execute this unconditional removal using its earlier proof. Both may then enter the critical section. This contradicts “Never override a live mutex owner.” Atomically detach/claim the exact observed mutex generation before deleting it, then retry `mkdir`. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:346` - The required timestamp is not guaranteed: failure to write `started` is ignored, and PID verification alone marks the mutex held. This contradicts “Write owner PID + timestamp into the mutex dir.” Require and verify both metadata writes before accepting ownership. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:598` - Several `reclaim` command failures—including a missing `--expected` value, unknown argument, absent expected owner, and invalid `--confirmed-closed`—still exit with only English errors and no `LOCK_RESULT=`. This contradicts “Every reclaim failure path must emit LOCK_RESULT=”. Type these exits or explicitly narrow the accepted requirement to operational reclaim failures. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:51` - Failure to create or access `$STATE` is allowed to continue; the subsequent mutex `mkdir` failure is then reported as `RECLAIM_BUSY`, although no competing owner was observed. This contradicts the requirement that `RECLAIM_BUSY` represent temporary mutex contention and directs session-start toward retries instead of storage recovery. Handle state-directory/I/O failure separately before mutex acquisition. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:333` - If `.lock-reclaim` is a symlink to a directory, these child removals follow it and can delete `pid` and `started` outside the lock directory before `rm -rf` removes the symlink itself. Reject symlink mutexes or unlink the symlink without traversing child paths. - ⚠️ `TILANNE.md:1` - This new tracked branch-status file is outside CONTRIBUTING.md’s explicit shared-material inventory and duplicates transient branch, validation, push, and PR state that will immediately become stale. Remove it from the tracked change or place durable documentation in an existing canonical owner. 🔧 Fix: Harden reclaim mutex ownership and typed failures 5 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:375` - The required legacy recovery path is still unreachable at the normal threshold: after the initial age check, creating `.reclaim-claim` updates the parent mutex directory's mtime, so the immediate second no-PID age check sees age zero and refuses reclamation. Subsequent attempts repeat the reset. This contradicts “a legacy no-pid dir ages past the mid-acquire threshold.” Validate an unchanged generation without mutating its age, preferably by atomically detaching the observed directory. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:375` - The nested claim can itself become an unrecoverable orphan: termination after this `mkdir` leaves `.reclaim-claim`, and every later reclaimer fails the same `mkdir` forever even though the outer owner is proven dead. This recreates the P0 permanent jam. Avoid introducing a second unowned mutex; atomically rename the observed outer directory to a unique quarantine path instead. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:341` - The live-owner ABA race remains reachable because cleanup is not bound to one directory generation. `rmdir` can remove the stale directory, another process can recreate it and publish a live PID, and the following existence check plus `rm -rf` can delete that new live mutex. This contradicts “Never override a live mutex owner.” Atomically detach the exact stale directory and delete only that detached path. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:395` - Acquisition still collapses non-contention failures into `RECLAIM_BUSY`: PID/timestamp publication failure, an existing but unwritable state directory, or a permanent malformed/symlink mutex all return the same failure consumed as temporary contention. This leaves the approved I/O fix partial and contradicts the typed outcome's temporary-contention meaning. Return distinct internal results and reserve `RECLAIM_BUSY` for an observed live or mid-acquire mutex. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:24` - The documented emergency command removes a mutex immediately when `pid` is missing because `kill -0 ""` fails; it does not enforce the stated no-PID age threshold and can delete a live creator's mutex during metadata publication. This contradicts the required age rule and “Never override a live mutex owner.” Document the same age and symlink checks as the implementation, or direct operators only to the guarded script. 🔧 Fix: Harden abandoned mutex recovery and error typing 3 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:324` - An existing abandonment marker is treated as proof before PID inspection. A contender can mark an aged no-PID mutex, the original creator can then publish its live PID, and a later contender will detach it solely because the marker remains and the inode matches. This contradicts “Never override a live mutex owner.” Revalidate PID/age immediately before rename; the marker must only serialize contenders, not prove abandonment. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:398` - Successful detach removes only `pid` and `started`, leaving the deterministic quarantine directory, marker, and arbitrary legacy contents permanently. A pre-existing destination also makes rename fail on every retry and is ultimately reported as temporary contention. This misses the approved requirement to delete only the detached generation and can reintroduce a permanent jam. Reserve a unique destination, remove the successfully detached tree, and classify destination/storage collisions as I/O. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:558` - When mutex publication or malformed/storage state fails during reclaim, this path emits `IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE` even though the main lock was already proven stale. That contradicts “keep main-lock status truthful (stale stays stale)” and the requirement that every reclaim failure reclassify the actual lock state. Preserve or recompute `STALE_RECLAIMABLE` while reporting the mutex I/O detail separately. 🔧 Fix: Finalize safe mutex detach and truthful failures 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:385` - The final abandonment proof is still separate from the pathname rename. After this check validates stale generation G, another contender can detach G and create/publish a new live canonical generation H; the unconditional rename at line 388 then detaches H. A delayed original creator can likewise publish its live PID between check and rename. This contradicts “Never override a live mutex owner.” Coordinate owner publication and detach through one shared claim boundary so the proven generation cannot be replaced or become live before rename. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:588` - If publishing the new main-lock owner fails after the expected owner was re-proven stale under the mutex, the stale lock remains unchanged but is reported as `IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE`. This contradicts “stale stays stale” and the requirement that every reclaim failure reclassify actual lock state. Release the mutex and emit the freshly classified main-lock result with write-failure context; the pre-mutex current-owner failure for a numeric stale lock needs the same treatment. 🔧 Fix: Coordinate mutex publication and preserve stale results 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:414` - The generation gate accepts `-d "$claimed"`/`-d "$gate"`, which follows directory symlinks, and later reads or overwrites their `pid` and `started` children. A malformed abandoned mutex can therefore redirect recovery writes outside `.lock-reclaim` instead of producing the approved malformed/storage outcome. Reject symlink gate/claimed directories and symlinked metadata before any read, write, or rename, then classify the condition as I/O rather than contention. 🔧 Fix: Reject unsafe generation gate symlinks 3 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:422` - A contender atomically renames the abandoned generation gate to `claimed`, but before it publishes its own PID at line 457, another contender can observe the inherited missing/dead PID and old mtime here, classify this new in-progress claim as abandoned, and rename it back. This leaves the required “Never override a live mutex owner” invariant reachable. Establish a fresh, exclusively created claim with its own mid-acquire grace before manipulating the abandoned gate. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:759` - The criterion “Every reclaim failure path must emit LOCK_RESULT= and reclassify based on the actual lock state” is still violated when HUP/INT/TERM interrupts an active reclaim: these traps release and exit without classification or `LOCK_RESULT=`. Route interrupted reclaim operations through the shared classification/emission boundary before exiting. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:355` - The new safety predicate rejects symlinks but accepts other non-regular metadata such as FIFOs or directories. Subsequent `cat "$claimed/pid"` can block forever on a FIFO, recreating a permanent mutex jam instead of returning the approved malformed-storage outcome. Require metadata paths to be absent or regular non-symlink files before reading or writing; apply the same check to canonical mutex metadata. 🔧 Fix: Harden claim publication metadata and signal handling 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:399` - Generation-claim recovery repeats the P0 prove-then-delete race: contender A proves the claim abandoned, contender B removes and recreates that pathname with its live PID, then A deletes B's metadata and directory here and can acquire the same claim. This contradicts “Never override a live mutex owner.” Bind recovery to the exact observed claim generation at this shared boundary instead of deleting a reusable pathname from earlier PID/age evidence. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:393` - The fresh claim uses a hardcoded two-second no-PID grace instead of `RECLAIM_MUTEX_STALE_AFTER`. When the configured mid-acquire threshold is raised for a slow environment, a live claimant delayed during metadata publication can still be removed after only two seconds. This contradicts the required mid-acquire-threshold rule; reuse the same validated threshold policy as the enclosing mutex. 🔧 Fix: Fence generation claim recovery by exact inode 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:420` - The recovery marker and inode recheck still do not coordinate with owner publication. Concrete path: creator A stalls after `mkdir` until its no-PID claim ages; reclaimer B proves it abandoned, creates the marker, and passes this inode check; A then publishes and verifies its live PID, after which B renames that same now-live claim here. Both can proceed through claim acquisition. This contradicts “Never override a live mutex owner.” Make publication and recovery participate in one shared claim-state transition so a marker prevents the creator from accepting ownership and recovery revalidates owner state before its destructive operation. 🔧 Fix: Coordinate claim publication with recovery fencing 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-lock.sh:436` - The final destructive operation is still a pathname rename performed after the exact-generation checks, while its deterministic tombstone is later deleted. A delayed recoverer can survive another contender retiring generation G and completing cleanup; after the enclosing directory inode is reused, a new live claim can occupy the same pathname, and the delayed rename can move it because the old tombstone no longer fences the operation. This leaves “Never override a live mutex owner” dependent on inode non-reuse. Use a non-reusable generation nonce or retain an irrevocable tombstone so the winner operation itself fails against every replacement. 🔧 Fix: Retain nonce-bound generation claim tombstones 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-lock.sh:18` - Nonce-bound `.lock-reclaim-claim-retired-*` tombstones are now permanent, safety-critical state, but the authoritative helper header still documents only `.lock-reclaim` and does not name the nonce field, tombstone namespace, retention purpose, or warn operators not to delete it. This violates CONTRIBUTING.md’s accurate-header rule and AGENTS.md’s requirement that producer headers own exact child fields and mutation mechanics. Document the retained ABA fence and emergency-handling rule in this header. 🔧 Fix: Document retained generation claim ABA fences 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-lock.sh:80` - Adding five header lines shifted the Usage block to lines 31–39, but `usage()` still extracts fixed lines 28–36. `--help` and unknown-command help now begin with tombstone prose and omit the final usage guidance. Update the range, preferably replacing fixed line numbers with explicit Usage block markers so future header edits cannot silently break help. 🔧 Fix: Stabilize usage extraction with explicit markers ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `git diff --stat aca3ad100ffcb43873837486a0f24ad3e6cdc7fa..bdf21aba08c8686c3403f29092bf34467217ccd3` and focused `sed`/`rg` inspection - `bash tests/fm-lock.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-session-start.test.sh` (initial stale-test/Bash-3.2 failures; passing after test-only fixes) - `bash tests/fm-supervision-instructions.test.sh` (initial stale-label failure; passing after test-only fix) - Manual CLI scenarios invoking `bin/fm-lock.sh`, `bin/fm-lock.sh status`, and `bin/fm-supervision-instructions.sh --lock-state RECLAIM_BUSY`, recorded in the evidence transcript
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Lint** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ linter found issues (exit code 1) 🔧 Fix: Remove dead reclaim state and clarify argument splitting ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix(tmux): recognize Grok 0.2.112 Esc:cancel busy footer
body:
## Intent Rebuild the Grok busy-signature fix on origin/main after #1049 (aca3ad1) replaced the old shared OR-ed busy pattern with harness-scoped constants. The live defect remains: FM_TMUX_GROK_BUSY_REGEX_DEFAULT was still only Ctrl+c:cancel while Grok 0.2.112 mid-turn footers show Esc:cancel. Decided design (do not reopen): change ONLY FM_TMUX_GROK_BUSY_REGEX_DEFAULT in bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh to include Esc:cancel while keeping Ctrl+c:cancel for older installs. Do NOT add Esc:cancel to the shared FM_TMUX_BUSY_REGEX_DEFAULT - that would reintroduce the cross-harness token bleed #1049 removed. The incomplete harness-scope migration for no-harness callers is a separate filed gap. Also update the stale comment above the constants, leave docs/configuration.md alone if already correct (FM_BUSY_REGEX empty override after #1049), and fix tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh so a green suite requires the live Esc:cancel footer (not only legacy Ctrl+c:cancel), with positive mid-turn and negative idle/overlay fixtures plus cross-harness isolation. Do not reassert dual-default byte-identity (obsolete by design). Do not touch harness-adapters SKILL.md or forbidden bootstrap/secondmate test files. Branch is a fresh rebuild (fm/grok-busy-signature-rebuild); leave frozen fm/grok-busy-signature and upstream PR 1040 alone. Push only to origin (yomi202703/firstmate). Empirical bar: prove Esc:cancel present mid-turn and absent when idle against real 0.2.112 panes. ## What Changed - `FM_TMUX_GROK_BUSY_REGEX_DEFAULT` in `bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh` now matches `Esc:cancel` in addition to `Ctrl+c:cancel`, so mid-turn Grok 0.2.112 panes read as busy while older installs keep working. The token stays Grok-scoped: the shared `FM_TMUX_BUSY_REGEX_DEFAULT` is untouched, so the cross-harness bleed removed in #1049 does not return. - Made `bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh` the single owner of the per-harness busy signatures: `bin/fm-watch.sh` drops its duplicated fallback literal (`BUSY_REGEX` now carries only an explicit `FM_BUSY_REGEX` override, which is the sole path that dereferences it) and its stale mirrored comment, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` no longer points harness-adapter authors at `fm-watch.sh` for busy signatures. - Added `test_grok_busy_signature_uses_real_capture_shapes` to `tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh`, built from fresh 2026-07-26 captures of grok 0.2.112: positive mid-turn footer, negative idle and overlay footers (including the `Esc:unselect` near-miss), both halves of the live tool-approval bar, and cross-harness isolation validated against a positively-asserted fixture. Test evidence in the pipeline confirms the suite fails against the base `bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh` and passes at branch HEAD. Known follow-ups left out of scope, both recorded by the pipeline: no-harness callers such as `fm_pending_reply_backend_observation` still match the shared default, and `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md` still documents the pre-0.2.112 Grok facts. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The source change is a one-token harness-scoped regex widening plus a behavior-preserving de-duplication of the fm-watch mirror, the approval-footer concern from round 1 was refuted by live 0.2.112 capture and is now pinned by both a positive and a negative fixture, and the only remaining findings are informational cleanups. ## Testing I drove a real grok 0.2.112 session in a disposable tmux pane and captured its actual footers - mid-turn shows `Shift+Tab:mode │ Esc:cancel │ Ctrl+.:shortcuts`, idle shows `Shift+Tab:mode │ Ctrl+.:shortcuts`, and the human-blocked project-dir overlay shows the `Esc:unselect` near-miss - then replayed those exact captures through fm_pane_is_busy at base and at branch: base reads the live mid-turn pane as IDLE (the reported defect) while the branch reads it BUSY, with idle and overlay still IDLE and no Esc:cancel bleed into claude/codex/opencode/pi/unknown/no-harness scopes. The targeted suite tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh passes at HEAD and provably fails on the base lib, so the green suite genuinely requires the Esc:cancel token. I also ran the adjacent tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh for the fm-watch.sh edit; one early run flaked on a timing-sensitive pause-absorption case while the machine was loaded by the live grok probe, and it passed on three subsequent HEAD runs and on a base-sources run, so it is not a branch regression. I could not reproduce a live tool-approval bar because this machine's global grok config auto-approves and changing it is outside the worktree boundary, but that fixture classifies identically at base and branch so it carries no regression risk. All probe sessions, sandboxes, and temp scratch files were removed and the worktree is clean.
Evidence: Live grok 0.2.112 footers (mid-turn / idle / human-blocked overlay) === live grok 0.2.112 mid-turn footer (Esc:cancel PRESENT) === Shift+Tab:mode │ Esc:cancel │ Ctrl+.:shortcuts === live grok 0.2.112 idle footer (Esc:cancel ABSENT) === Shift+Tab:mode │ Ctrl+.:shortcuts === live grok 0.2.112 human-blocked overlay footer (Esc:unselect near-miss) === Esc:unselect │ Tab:scrollback │ Shift+x:dismiss ```text === live grok 0.2.112 mid-turn footer (Esc:cancel PRESENT) === Shift+Tab:mode │ Esc:cancel │ Ctrl+.:shortcuts === live grok 0.2.112 idle footer (Esc:cancel ABSENT) === Shift+Tab:mode │ Ctrl+.:shortcuts === live grok 0.2.112 human-blocked overlay footer (Esc:unselect near-miss) === Esc:unselect │ Tab:scrollback │ Shift+x:dismiss ```
Evidence: fm_pane_is_busy verdicts on those real captures, base vs branch firstmate Grok busy classification against REAL grok 0.2.112 captures grok version: grok 0.2.112 (9bbd559437aa) live capture harness base branch ---------------------------------- --------- (aca3ad1) (fe4d7eb) midturn grok IDLE BUSY <- want BUSY idle grok IDLE IDLE <- want IDLE overlay-projectdir grok IDLE IDLE <- want IDLE cross-harness isolation on the SAME live mid-turn capture (branch build): harness=claude IDLE <- want IDLE harness=codex IDLE <- want IDLE harness=opencode IDLE <- want IDLE harness=pi IDLE <- want IDLE harness=kimi IDLE <- want IDLE harness=<none, shared default> IDLE <- want IDLE no-regression check on the human-blocked approval bar (fixture, harness=grok): approval bar WITH legacy Ctrl+c:cancel base=BUSY branch=BUSY (unchanged: already busy before this branch) approval bar WITHOUT legacy token base=IDLE branch=IDLE (Esc:cancel does not make an approval read busy) ```text firstmate Grok busy classification against REAL grok 0.2.112 captures grok version: grok 0.2.112 (9bbd559437aa) live capture harness base branch ---------------------------------- --------- (aca3ad1) (fe4d7eb) midturn grok IDLE BUSY <- want BUSY idle grok IDLE IDLE <- want IDLE overlay-projectdir grok IDLE IDLE <- want IDLE cross-harness isolation on the SAME live mid-turn capture (branch build): harness=claude IDLE <- want IDLE harness=codex IDLE <- want IDLE harness=opencode IDLE <- want IDLE harness=pi IDLE <- want IDLE harness=kimi IDLE <- want IDLE harness= IDLE <- want IDLE no-regression check on the human-blocked approval bar (fixture, harness=grok): approval bar WITH legacy Ctrl+c:cancel base=BUSY branch=BUSY (unchanged: already busy before this branch) approval bar WITHOUT legacy token base=IDLE branch=IDLE (Esc:cancel does not make an approval read busy) ```
Evidence: Full-screen capture of the live grok 0.2.112 mid-turn pane ⠴ Waiting for response… 5.9s 0.0s ⇣6.82k [stop] ╭───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ ❯ │ ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Grok 4.5 (high) · always-approve ─╯ Shift+Tab:mode │ Esc:cancel │ Ctrl+.:shortcuts ```text /private/tmp/gbp82574 6.8K / 500K ❯ Write a haiku about tmux panes. Do not use any tools. 11:27 AM ◆ user_prompt_submit [hooks: 1] ⠴ Waiting for response… 5.9s 0.0s ⇣6.82k [stop] ╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ ❯ │ ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Grok 4.5 (high) · always-approve ─╯ Shift+Tab:mode │ Esc:cancel │ Ctrl+.:shortcuts ```
Evidence: Full-screen capture of the live grok 0.2.112 idle pane ```text /private/tmp/gbp82574 17K / 500K ❯ Write a haiku about tmux panes. Do not use any tools. 11:27 AM ◆ user_prompt_submit [hooks: 1] ◆ Thought for 1.2s Split glass of green light 11:27 AM cursor leaps from pane to pane worlds share one keystroke Worked for 0.0s stop [hooks: 2] ╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ ❯ │ ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Grok 4.5 (high) · always-approve ─╯ Shift+Tab:mode │ Ctrl+.:shortcuts ```
Evidence: Full-screen capture of the live grok 0.2.112 project-dir overlay (Esc:unselect) ```text /private/tmp/gbp82574 ┃ ┃ Run Grok Build in a project directory? ┃ ┃ This gives Grok Build full context of your codebase for better results. ┃ ┃ 1 (○) gbp82574 (current) /private/tmp/gbp82574 █ ┃ 2 (○) firstmate ~/.treehouse/firstmate-b7e6f3/2/firstmate (now) █ ┃ 3 (○) agent-harness ~/.treehouse/agent-harness-dd5cf5/1/agent-harness (8s ago) █ ┃ 4 (○) agent-harness ~/harness/agent-harness (16s ago) █ ┃ 5 (○) firstmate ~/.treehouse/firstmate-7bab20/7/firstmate (23s ago) █ ┃ 6 (○) firstmate ~/.treehouse/firstmate-b7e6f3/5/firstmate (47s ago) █ ┃ 7 (○) Don't ask me again Always start in the current directory (reset in config.toml) █ ┃ z (○) Type your answer here ┃ ┃ ↑/↓ navigate · y copy Enter:submit ┃ Esc:unselect │ Tab:scrollback │ Shift+x:dismiss ```
Evidence: Non-vacuity proof: branch test run against the base fm-tmux-lib.sh ```text $ git checkout aca3ad1 -- bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh && bash tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh ok - fm_tmux_submit_enter_core: busy pane + pending composer returns empty (message queued) ok - fm_tmux_submit_enter_core: idle pane + pending composer stays pending (genuine swallow preserved) ok - fm_tmux_submit_enter_core: busy pane clears composer on first Enter - returns empty ok - fm_tmux_submit_enter_core: idle pane clears composer on first Enter - returns empty as before ok - fm_pane_is_busy: Claude spinner is scoped, multi-frame, and backward-compatible not ok - live Grok mid-turn footer must match harness=grok ```
- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 warning across 1 run (35m11s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 2 infos - ⚠️ `bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh:76` - Adding `Esc:cancel` to the Grok signature is empirically pinned for mid-turn and idle, but not for a tool-approval/permission bar - the one state where a false-busy verdict is safety-relevant. Grok 0.2.112's own embedded docs say Esc cancels immediately "while a turn is running", and a tool approval sits inside a running turn, so the approval bar plausibly advertises `Esc:cancel`. bin/fm-crew-state.sh:174 documents the opposite invariant ("A genuinely human-blocked agent (a permission dialog, not mid-tool-call) does not render the busy banner, so this corroboration does not mask that case: it stays correctly not-busy"). Failure path: blocked grok pane -> crew_pane_is_busy=busy -> crew_absorb_class=working -> crew_is_provably_working absorbs the wake (bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:355), so a crew waiting on a human approval stops surfacing to the captain until the wedge threshold. Legacy `Ctrl+c:cancel` had the same class of behavior (the new test pins it at tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh:232), so this may be accepted parity - but for 0.2.112 installs the approval state flips from surfaced to absorbed. Please confirm against a real 0.2.112 approval prompt and, if it does show `Esc:cancel`, add that fixture as a documented positive-or-negative decision. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:585` - The live defect is only closed on the harness-scoped path. `fm_pending_reply_backend_observation` (line 585) and the cursor-row footer guard in bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh:161 both match `${FM_BUSY_REGEX:-$FM_TMUX_BUSY_REGEX_DEFAULT}` with no harness argument, so a 0.2.112 grok pane whose footer reads only `Esc:cancel` still resolves to `fallback-idle` in the pending-reply observation (and its footer on the cursor row would not be recognized as an empty composer). Recording this only as the concrete consequence of the migration gap the intent declares out of scope for this branch; no action expected here. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:106` - The mirrored comment here still reads `grok: "Ctrl+c:cancel"` while bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh:64-70 was updated, and bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh:63 explicitly calls this file the mirror. Behavior is unaffected because window_is_busy delegates to fm_busy_lines_match. Related: the literal default on line 109 (`BUSY_REGEX=${FM_BUSY_REGEX:-'esc (to )?interrupt|Working\.\.\.|Ctrl\+c:cancel'}`) is unreachable - line 176 is its only use and sits inside `[ -n "${FM_BUSY_REGEX:-}" ]`, so the fallback literal can never be read. Dropping it to `BUSY_REGEX=${FM_BUSY_REGEX:-}` removes a duplicated copy of the shared pattern that exists only to drift on exactly this kind of fix. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh:245` - The three `case` blocks on lines 245-255 assert regex spelling rather than behavior, and each is already covered behaviorally in the same function: `Esc:cancel` presence by line 217, `Ctrl\+c:cancel` retention by line 232, and shared-default isolation by line 242. Because line 251 matches the literal `Ctrl\+c:cancel`, a behavior-identical rewrite (e.g. `Ctrl[+]c:cancel`, or folding both tokens into `(Esc|Ctrl\+c):cancel`) fails the suite with no defect present. Dropping the string assertions keeps the same guarantees without pinning the escape form. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh:235` - The isolation block on lines 235-242 is entirely negative against a fixture that is never positively asserted (it differs from the validated line-216 fixture by the `Ctrl+b:send to bg` segment). `pane_busy` also returns non-zero on any mock or sourcing failure, so if the Grok pattern stopped matching this exact string - e.g. a change in separator or spacing handling - all seven assertions would still pass and report isolation that was never exercised. Adding `pane_busy bleed grok || fail ...` on the same fixture before the negatives makes the block self-validating. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh:193` - Lines 193-195 add the live Grok `Esc:cancel` assertion inside test_claude_busy_signature_uses_real_capture_shapes, which now duplicates line 217 of the dedicated Grok test while its pass message (line 196) still claims only Claude coverage. Keeping the live-footer requirement in the Grok-owned test alone leaves one owner per harness signature and no duplicate fixture to update twice. 🔧 Fix: pin Grok approval footer, de-duplicate busy regex mirrors 2 infos still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:180` - After dropping the fallback literal, `BUSY_REGEX` is a pure alias captured at load time (line 113) while its only guard reads `FM_BUSY_REGEX` at call time (line 179). The two reads can no longer disagree in practice - nothing in the source graph assigns `FM_BUSY_REGEX`, and all sourcing happens above line 113 - but if a future caller ever sets it after load, the guard would pass while `BUSY_REGEX` is still empty, and `grep -qiE ""` matches every line, i.e. every pane reads busy. Using `grep -qiE "$FM_BUSY_REGEX"` at line 180 and deleting the variable removes the split read and one more name for the same setting. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:110` - The new comment names `bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh` as the owner of the per-harness patterns `window_is_busy` relies on, but fm-watch.sh never sources it directly - `fm_busy_lines_match` and the `FM_TMUX_*` constants arrive transitively via `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:70` (sourced at line 68). Not a regression: the else branch already depended on that symbol before this commit. But with the in-file literal now gone there is no local fallback at all, and the failure is silent - a missing `fm_busy_lines_match` returns non-zero, so every pane would read idle rather than erroring. Adding an explicit `. "$SCRIPT_DIR/fm-tmux-lib.sh"` next to the other sources makes the dependency match the comment; re-sourcing is documented idempotent at bin/fm-composer-lib.sh:49-50.

title: fix(bin): let a declared pause outrank a done or cancelled run
body:
## Intent Let a crew's declared `paused:` survive an attributed *terminal historical* no-mistakes validation run, so a correct pause is not permanently overruled by a stale run record. Correctness fix only (not a claimed 75-second stale loop): when `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` has `HAVE_RUN=1` for a true terminal outcome of **done** or **cancelled** (not the mapped presentation state) and the status log's last verb is `paused:`, emit `state: paused` with `source: status-log`, retaining the terminal run outcome as leading secondary detail. Mirror the existing CI-green status-log override shape for that emit style. What outranks a pause, by design: - **Active / working and parked** runs still outrank a declared pause (including a CI-green run still monitoring for merge that is only *mapped* to done). - A genuine **failed** run is **not** pause-overridable. An abort (`cancelled`) is a supervisor decision; overriding it with the crew's own pause declaration is sound. A failed run is the work itself failing and must surface whether or not any pause line is fresher. That restriction is the final accepted scope, not a temporary fallback. Rejected: changing only `crew_absorb_class` or `pause_state_class` (dual-authority drift); stopping terminal attribution entirely; TTL on cancelled runs; teardown on abort. Residuals left by design: live-agent first surface, no-verb turn-end while paused, hourly forgotten-pause re-surface. Tests cover cancelled/done + trailing paused (override), failed + trailing paused (still failed), and negatives that working/parked/ci-green-monitoring still win. No claim this eliminates residual first-surface or signal spam. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` tracks the attributed run's own terminal outcome (`RUN_TERMINAL`: none/done/cancelled/failed) alongside the mapped `RUN_STATE`, set only from the run's reported outcome/status across the coarse, outcome, and bare-status paths (not from CI-green presentation mapping). - When that outcome is genuinely terminal `done` or `cancelled` and the status log's last verb is `paused:`, the crew is emitted as `state: paused · source: status-log` with the **run outcome leading** the detail and the pause reason following (and no doubled separator when the pause carries no reason). - A terminal `failed` run continues to report `failed` even if the last status verb is `paused:`, so a validation failure is not demoted to a quiet external wait. Active, parked, and CI-green-still-monitoring runs likewise outrank pause. - `tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` adds cases for cancelled/done + paused, bare paused separator, failed-stays-failed, and active/parked/ci-green negatives; `docs/architecture.md` documents the second status-log exception and `AGENTS.md` points at the script header as the owner of the run-step-to-state mapping instead of restating it. ## Risk Assessment Low: Review-driven corrections gate the override on true terminal outcomes (so mapped CI-green done stays active authority), keep genuine failures visible by design, put terminal detail first for truncation, fix the empty-note separator, and document the exception. Scope is narrower than the first draft intent: `failed` is intentionally not pause-overridable. ## Testing Exercised the targeted crew-state suite (all cases pass, including the new pause-vs-terminal-run ones) and the watch-triage suite that consumes the verdict, then demonstrated the change end-to-end on a hermetic fleet fixture: with a cancelled run plus a declared pause the helper flips from `state: failed · source: run-step · run cancelled` to `state: paused · source: status-log · run cancelled · holding for upstream maintainer merge`, the watcher's absorb class flips from `none` (wake surfaces) to `paused` (absorbed), and the human `fm-fleet-view.sh` table cell flips from `failed / run-step` to `paused / status-log`; the done/checks-passed case behaves the same, while failed, active, and parked runs stay failed/working/parked with or without a trailing pause line. No screenshot applies - the affected surfaces are shell CLI output and a Markdown fleet table, both captured verbatim in the transcript artifact.

title: fix: harden Kimi submission and spinner matching

## Intent Fix the blocking Kimi first-Enter delivery defect by routing brief-pointer delivery through the shared verify-and-retry-Enter submit core, typing the pointer once and retrying Enter only while preserving the existing readiness gate and Kimi delivery postconditions: composer clearing, sparkle echo, and context leaving 0%. Keep unconfirmed delivery as a loud spawn failure. In the same PR, make the independent Kimi spinner conformance correction by requiring whitespace on both sides of the middot, preserve varied leading-whitespace fixtures without adding a never-observed zero-whitespace fixture, add the auditable matcher contract comment, and align harness-adapters documentation. Describe the spinner change as conformance rather than live breakage. The PR body must state that it carries two independent fixes and that reverting one reverts the other. Do not touch other harness signatures. ## What Changed - Route Kimi brief-pointer delivery through the shared verified submit core, typing the pointer once and retrying Enter while preserving readiness checks, delivery postconditions, target ownership, and loud failure. - Tighten Kimi spinner matching to require whitespace on both sides of the middot, align adapter documentation, and cover swallowed-first-Enter and observed-whitespace cases in the harness tests. - These are two independent fixes shipped in one PR; reverting the PR reverts both together. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The follow-up preserves the established Zellij and cmux target-ownership guard while the complete branch remains a well-bounded implementation of the Kimi submission retry and spinner conformance requirements. ## Testing Inspected the base-to-target delta, ran the focused Kimi harness suite, and captured deterministic tmux/Kimi test-double evidence demonstrating the complete delivery and spinner contracts; all checks passed, the worktree remained clean, and no screenshot was produced because this is a terminal-only flow whose actual rendered surface is preserved in the transcript.

title: feat(bin): add guarded Kimi turn-end wake
body:
## Intent Enable Firstmate's Kimi Stop turn-end wake through a guarded per-worktree token and private registry while preserving the captain's shared Kimi config, skills, and memory. Install only a surgical marker-delimited Firstmate-owned region in ~/.kimi-code/config.toml, preserve every unrelated byte, remain idempotent and removable, fail closed on missing or malformed config and on missing jq, keep the runtime hook silent and always exit 0, and ensure sessions without a Firstmate token are unaffected. Do not use an isolated Kimi home or a second JSON parser fallback. The PR body must state the exact removal command 'bin/fm-kimi-turnend-hook.sh remove' and include demonstrated no-interference evidence: a real non-Firstmate session with the hook installed and no token completed normally in 4.05 seconds with zero hook output and no side effect in cwd; across 10 no-token hook runs the measured overhead was median 9.8 ms and maximum 11.6 ms, about 0.24 percent of that turn. It must also report the real positive proof that a registered Firstmate target was touched. Validate the rebased change fully through green CI. ## What Changed - Add a guarded, silent Kimi Stop hook that surgically preserves shared config, skills, and memory; installation fails closed on unsafe config or missing `jq`, stays idempotent, and can be removed with `bin/fm-kimi-turnend-hook.sh remove`. - Register per-worktree tokens during Kimi crew spawn, touch only the authorized task turn-end marker, and clean up pointers and private registry entries during teardown. - Demonstrate no interference: a real non-Firstmate session completed normally in 4.05 seconds with zero hook output and no cwd side effects; 10 no-token runs measured 9.8 ms median and 11.6 ms maximum overhead, about 0.24% of that turn, while a registered Firstmate target was successfully touched. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The boundary fix now preserves appended captain TOML while retaining byte-identical pristine removal, includes focused regression coverage, and documents the deliberate newline behavior. ## Testing No separate baseline output was supplied. The focused Kimi harness test passed, and the recorded end-to-end flow demonstrated preservation of captain config, skills, memory, and a foreign hook; mode-700 registry creation; silent zero-exit no-token behavior with no cwd or target side effect; a registered target touch; idempotent installation; and byte-identical removal.
Evidence: Kimi turn-end end-to-end transcript ```text Kimi guarded turn-end hook end-to-end evidence config_marker_count_after_install=1 captain_skills_line_preserved=1 captain_memory_line_preserved=1 foreign_hook_line_preserved=1 private_registry_permissions=700 idempotent_second_install=yes ordinary_session_exit=0 ordinary_session_hook_output_bytes=0 ordinary_session_cwd_entries=0 target_touched_after_ordinary_session=no registered_session_exit=0 registered_session_hook_output_bytes=0 registered_target_touched=yes config_byte_identical_after_remove=yes managed_hook_removed=yes private_registry_removed=yes ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-kimi-turnend-hook.sh:220` - The required behavior says the installer must "remain idempotent and removable" and "preserve every unrelated byte," but `outside = original[: region[0]] + original[region[1]:]` can make removal fail after a normal edit. If the original config lacked a final newline, install uses the marker that owns the preceding newline; if the captain later appends valid TOML below the installed block, removal consumes both boundary newlines and concatenates the original final line with the appended first line. The resulting TOML is invalid, so `remove` refuses. Reconstruct this boundary so a Firstmate-owned separator is retained when a suffix exists, and cover the no-final-newline -> install -> append -> remove sequence. 🔧 Fix: Preserve Kimi config boundaries during hook removal 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-kimi-turnend-hook.sh:176` - The chosen fix explicitly required a comment explaining that the retained newline prevents joining the captain's preceding line to content appended after installation, but the new `separator` branch has no such comment. Add that explanation immediately above this branch so this deliberately asymmetric removal behavior is not later mistaken for an unnecessary newline. 🔧 Fix: Document Kimi removal newline safeguard ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-kimi-harness.test.sh` - Manual isolated-home flow: install twice, invoke a tokenless Stop payload, invoke a registered Stop payload, then run `bin/fm-kimi-turnend-hook.sh remove` and compare the restored config byte-for-byte - `git status --short` after testing to verify no transient worktree artifacts remained
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: docs(harness-adapters): document verified GPT-5.6 batching guidance
fix(decision-hold): find durably resolved decisions in the archive
body:
## The defect

`bin/fm-decision-hold.sh` resolved every task lookup through `task_show()`, which is `tasks-axi show <id> --full`.
That reads only the active backlog.

`.tasks.toml` sets `archive = "data/done-archive.md"` and `done_keep = 10`, so once ten newer Done items exist, tasks-axi prunes older Done items - including resolved captain-decision holds - out of `data/backlog.md` and into the archive.
`verify_hold_durable()` then failed with `captain decision <id> is absent from .../data/backlog.md`.
Scout teardown calls that gate, so the investigation could never be torn down again.

Observed on a live home: three resolved holds sat intact in `data/done-archive.md`, complete with their `Resolution recorded by fm-decision-hold` record, decision digest, and routed identities, while `tasks-axi show` returned `NOT_FOUND` for all three and the gate refused permanently.

The property that makes this worth fixing rather than working around is that **it is triggered by getting work done**.
The faster things land, the sooner resolved decisions age out, and the more scouts get permanently stuck.
A quiet week never exposes it.

## The fix

When a lookup misses in the active backlog, consult the configured archive before declaring the record absent.

- The archive path is read from `.tasks.toml` (`[markdown] archive`), never hardcoded.
  Absolute paths, relative paths, both quote styles, and odd spacing are handled; when the key is absent there is no archive and behavior is unchanged.
- The archive is **not** a parseable backlog document - it stores entries under `## Archived <date>` sections, which `tasks-axi` rejects outright.
  Rather than duplicating tasks-axi's entry parser, the archive is read by restoring the backlog headings in a private throwaway copy and letting tasks-axi parse that.
  Only column-0 headings are dropped, and entry bodies are always indented, so no archived content can be lost.

That last point is what makes the field parsing safe.
Because the record is parsed by tasks-axi itself, `state`, `held`, `kind`, `hold_kind`, and `body` come back byte-identical to `show --full`, including the escaped single-line body form that `verify_resolution_identity` pattern-matches against. No parallel parser to drift.

## Where the fallback applies, and why

The fallback lives in the single lookup owner, `task_show`. Per call site:

| Site | Effect | Why correct |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verify_hold_durable` | **Fixed.** An archived resolved decision now verifies. | The must-fix; teardown depends on it. |
| `verify_hold_active` | **Still refuses** an archived record. | It asserts a hold is *currently* active; an archived record is Done, so it fails on `state != queued`. The reason is now accurate (`not queued (state=done)`) instead of a misleading "absent". |
| `command_hold` existence probe | **Closes a related hole.** | A resolved-then-archived identity used to miss, so `hold` silently created a fresh queued hold reusing it, bypassing the "already durably resolved; use a new decision key" refusal. It now refuses. |
| `verify_hold_resolved` | Idempotent `resolve` retry works after archival. | Previously fell through to an "absent" failure. |
| `origin_exists_here` | An origin whose backlog item was archived is still owned by this home. | Same defect class. |
| `resolve` routed-task lookups | Refuses with "already done" rather than "does not exist". | Both refuse; the new reason is the true one. |
| `add` / `update` / `unblock` / `done` mutations | Unchanged - active backlog only. | An attempt to mutate an archived record fails loudly rather than silently. |

## The gate is not weakened

- A genuinely absent decision still fails; a miss never becomes a pass.
- A record found in the archive must satisfy the **same** durable-resolution conditions - finding it is not enough, it must still carry `Resolution recorded by fm-decision-hold.` and `Routed work:`.
- An archived entry can satisfy only the durably-resolved branch, never the actively-held one. The archive holds pruned Done items, so an entry there is never actively held.
- If the archive cannot be parsed, the lookup misses and the gate refuses. There is no optimistic pass path.

## Regression coverage, both directions

In `tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh`, using `tasks-axi prune --keep 0` to trigger exactly the archival that retention eventually performs:

1. An archived resolved decision verifies and lets teardown proceed - the fix.
2. A genuinely missing decision still refuses, by name.
3. An archived decision closed without a resolution record still refuses, with the right reason.

Tests 2 and 3 are the guard on the fix. Verified that test 1 fails without the code change, with the exact reported error:

```
fm-decision-hold: captain decision sample-archive-review-decision-route is absent from <home>/data/backlog.md
not ok - verification refused a resolved captain decision that retention had archived
```

## Recommendation, not implemented

The alternative shape - trusting the completion attestation already in `state/<id>.meta` instead of re-deriving from the backlog - was considered and deliberately **not** implemented.
It would weaken the gate: `decisions_reviewed=1` records that an inventory was *taken*, not that each decision is *still* durably held or resolved.
Re-checking the durable record at teardown time is precisely the gate's value.

## Scope

This defect only. No changes to retention, `.tasks.toml`, or `tasks-axi`. Raising `done_keep` would only reset the clock.

## Verification

GitHub Actions is disabled on this account, so this PR will show an empty check set. Local verification substitutes. What I actually ran:

```
bash tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh     10/10 ok (run under both LC_ALL=C and en_US.UTF-8)
bash tests/fm-teardown.test.sh                    32/32 ok
bash tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh           42/42 ok
bin/fm-lint.sh                                    clean, ShellCheck 0.11.0 (pinned)
bin/fm-test-run.sh --lane portable-parallel-1|-2|portable-serial --exclude-family real-herdr-gated
                                                  87 scripts
```

ShellCheck was not installed locally; I fetched the pinned 0.11.0 build so `bin/fm-lint.sh` ran at CI parity rather than being skipped.

Two lane failures are **pre-existing and unrelated**, each reproduced identically on the baseline commit with this change reverted:

- `tests/fm-pi-watch-extension.test.sh` - the OpenCode watch plugin does not arm after the session lock PID matches (fails the "watch arm did not run after the session lock matched" branch).
- `tests/fm-session-start.test.sh` - "MISSING diagnostic did not appear at all".

Separately, `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh` fails only under a UTF-8 locale: the coverage guard builds its inputs with `LC_ALL=C sort` but invokes `comm` without it (`bin/fm-test-run.sh:434-435`), so the collations disagree. It passes under `LC_ALL=C`, which is why CI is green. Worth a separate fix; deliberately untouched here.

Four further lane failures (`fm-backend-herdr`, `fm-composer-lib`, `fm-backend-cmux`, `fm-afk-inject-e2e`) each pass when run individually. They were contention artifacts from concurrent suite runs on a shared machine that also hosts other active firstmate homes, not defects in this change.

title: fix(tmux): classify bordered composers across all rows
body:
## Intent

Fix fm_tmux_composer_state so tmux locates a bordered composer structurally and classifies every content row through the existing shared ANSI and ghost handling, treating real text on any row as pending, all-empty rows as empty, and unreadable or structurally unsafe cases as unknown while preserving the existing non-bordered cursor-row compatibility fallback and busy-footer exception. This must fix the real Kimi early-Enter multi-row failure and Grok bottom-border cursor quirk without cursor-offset arithmetic, echoed-message matching, delays, or any change to kimi_wait_for_delivery, while retaining loud refusal when delivery cannot be confirmed and preserving all harnesses and backends. Deterministic two-row and three-or-more-row fixtures plus a real bin/fm-spawn.sh --harness kimi verification are required. The branch also independently verifies and documents Pi Calm compatibility with Pi 0.82.0 because the current baseline test exposed that supported-version gap. The PR body must explicitly state that this carries TWO independent changes - the structural composer reader and the Pi 0.82 Calm compatibility verification - and that reverting one reverts the other.

## What Changed

- Carries TWO independent changes - the structural tmux composer reader and Pi 0.82 Calm compatibility verification - so reverting this PR reverts both together.
- Locates complete bordered composers structurally, classifies every content row through shared ANSI and ghost handling, preserves the non-bordered fallback, and fails closed on unsafe or unreadable layouts. This covers Kimi’s multi-row early-Enter failure and Grok’s bottom-border cursor quirk.
- Expands composer, Kimi, submit, and backend regression fixtures, while updating Calm compatibility checks and documentation for Pi 0.82.0 alongside 0.81.1.

## Risk Assessment

🚨 High: Captain, malformed whitespace-only borders can still produce `empty`, violating the positive-proof boundary for injection and delivery confirmation.

## Testing

No separate baseline commands were supplied; targeted fixtures proved two-row and three-row pending text, all-empty and ghost-only boxes, Grok’s bottom-border cursor, unsafe geometry failing closed, non-bordered fallback, busy-footer handling, retry/refusal propagation, and preserved backends, while a real Pi 0.82.0 interactive Calm E2E passed. title: feat: add optional host-root mode
body:
## Summary

- add an opt-in `FM_HOST_ROOT` runtime contract that separates the FirstMate code/state root, the physical host instruction root, the target primary clone, and the isolated `FM_TARGET_WORKTREE`
- launch ordinary ship/scout workers from the host root while keeping every target Git, edit, test, build, review, and validation operation scoped to the recorded isolated worktree
- carry the contract through Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Grok, Kimi, tmux, Herdr, Zellij, Orca, and cmux without changing secondmate isolated-home semantics
- preserve behavior when `FM_HOST_ROOT` is unset and fail closed before destructive cleanup when host ownership, target isolation, endpoint absence, or physical path safety cannot be proven

This is the low-level runtime contract only. Reversible host installation and activation are intentionally deferred to a follow-up so this safety-sensitive change remains reviewable.

## Safety details

- resolves and compares physical paths, rejects host/target overlap, and verifies endpoint cwd before harness launch
- records host ownership with task metadata and durable decision authority
- uses absolute FirstMate command paths and explicit target-scoped worker/promotion instructions
- keeps unknown Orca creation and endpoint-stop races from discarding worktrees
- rejects unsupported host-root `local-only` tasks before fleet mutation
- preserves additive watcher and Kimi completion signaling without rewriting host configuration

## Validation

- `no-mistakes` run `01KYETZS2982GDXVG96QA3AK90`: review, focused test, documentation, canonical lint, and fork push passed with no remaining findings
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` with pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0
- focused host-root, backend, harness, lifecycle, review, decision, teardown, watcher, and secondmate regression coverage

title: fix(bin): stop the turn-end guard blocking during watcher arm confirmation
body:
## Intent Land an already-written turn-end guard fix upstream as a contribution PR from a fork. The bug: bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh is a Stop-hook backstop that blocks a turn from ending while work is in flight and no identity-matched watcher holds the home lock with a fresh beacon. bin/fm-watch-arm.sh forks the watcher and only then polls, for up to FM_ARM_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT seconds (default 10), for that child to acquire the lock and beat. Inside that confirmation window the lock is legitimately unowned, so fm_watcher_healthy correctly returns false. Because AGENTS.md section 8 requires arming the watcher as the last act of a turn, the Stop hook routinely fires inside that window and blocks a turn whose supervision is in fact being armed correctly. Observed live on 2026-07-25: four consecutive turns blocked, each followed seconds later by a foreground arm reporting a healthy watcher on a fresh pid. The chosen fix, deliberately: a marker, not a weakened predicate. bin/fm-watch-arm.sh writes state/.watch-arm-inflight immediately before forking the watcher and clears it on every terminal outcome, including the signal-trap cleanup path. fm_arm_in_flight in bin/fm-wake-lib.sh owns the read side. The guard consults it ONLY after fm_watcher_healthy has already failed, so the identity-matched lock and fresh-beacon check is never relaxed. A TTL of FM_ARM_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT + 5 seconds bounds a marker orphaned by a killed arm, so a genuine supervision lapse still blocks rather than trading a false alarm for a missed one. bin/fm-guard.sh is intentionally left unchanged because it is beacon-based and its grace window already absorbs this gap. Scope decisions the reviewer should know: the change is deliberately limited to the turn-end guard, its read-side helper, the arm marker, and the tests. bin/fm-watch.sh stale and re-arm behavior is intentionally NOT touched - separate work owns it and would collide. Regression coverage is colocated in tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh, three cases, all mutation-verified to fail without the fix: a fresh marker must not block in the default cross-harness mode, a fresh marker must not block in --claude cooperative mode and must not consume one of Claude's bounded re-blocks, and a stale marker must still block. The locals in fm_arm_in_flight are named arm_marker and arm_age rather than marker and age because bin/fm-lint.sh runs shellcheck with --external-sources, and a plain 'marker' collides with a test-local of the same name in tests/fm-afk-launch.test.sh and produces a false SC2031. Repo conventions applied: one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dashes, no agent commit co-author, shellcheck-clean bin scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh, tests colocated in the existing tests/.test.sh runner. docs/turnend-guard.md is the authoritative owner of this contract, so the mechanism is documented there in the Shared predicate section as current behavior; incident chronology stays in the PR, not in the doc. Delivery: origin is the upstream kunchenguid/firstmate and we have no push rights there. The branch must be pushed to the Nikita-Guzenko/firstmate fork and the PR opened against kunchenguid/firstmate:main. The PR body must explain the race concretely - what the guard did, why an arm in progress tripped it, and how the fix distinguishes the two. Nothing under .no-mistakes/ may be committed; that path stays gitignored in this repo and CI rejects tracked .no-mistakes paths. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-watch-arm.sh` now writes `state/.watch-arm-inflight` immediately before forking the watcher and clears it on every terminal outcome, including the signal-trap cleanup path, marking the window where the home lock is legitimately unowned while the child acquires it. - `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh` gains `fm_arm_in_flight`, the read side that treats the marker as valid only within a `FM_ARM_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT + 5`s TTL so an orphaned marker from a killed arm still lets a genuine supervision lapse block. - `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh` consults `fm_arm_in_flight` only after `fm_watcher_healthy` has already failed, so the identity-matched lock and fresh-beacon check is never relaxed; `docs/turnend-guard.md` documents the mechanism and `tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` adds three mutation-verified cases (fresh marker allows in default and `--claude` modes without consuming a re-block, stale marker still blocks). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Well-bounded, marker-based fix that only relaxes the turn-end guard after the strict identity check already failed, clears the marker on every terminal path, bounds orphans via a fail-safe TTL, and is covered by three mutation-verified regression tests matching the stated intent. ## Testing Baseline `bash tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` aborted at an environment-broken Pi extension test (node v22 refuses to import the `.ts` extension file — ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION), which is pre-existing and independent of this bash-only change; that abort also prevented the new `--claude` arm test (declared later) from running. Excluding the two node-`.ts`-import Pi tests, the suite passes 51/0 including all three new arm-marker regression cases. I also drove the real Stop hook directly to capture a CLI transcript showing the actual end-user surface: a fresh arm-inflight marker allows the turn to end silently, a stale marker still blocks with the exact required watcher-repair reason, and the no-marker path is unchanged; a mutation test against the base-commit guard confirms the false block returns without the fix. This is a CLI/hook change with no rendered UI, so the reviewer-visible evidence is the hook transcript rather than a screenshot.
Evidence: Real Stop-hook transcript (3 scenarios) `Scenario A arm in-flight: exit=0 silent (allow). Scenario B stale marker: exit=2 with 'TURN WOULD END BLIND - SUPERVISION IS OFF' + 'repair missing watcher supervision with bin/fm-watch-arm.sh as its own Claude Code background task'. Scenario C no marker: exit=2 (unchanged).` ```text === REAL Stop-hook transcript: bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh, work in flight, fresh beacon, no live lock === --- Scenario A: arm IN FLIGHT (fresh marker) — should ALLOW turn end, silent --- exit=0 output=[] RESULT: turn allowed to end silently (false alarm avoided) ✔ --- Scenario B: STALE arm marker (orphaned by killed arm) — should still BLOCK --- exit=2 output: ●━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ● TURN WOULD END BLIND - SUPERVISION IS OFF ● 1 task(s) in flight, but no live watcher holds this home lock (last beat: 0s ago). ● repair missing watcher supervision with bin/fm-watch-arm.sh as its own Claude Code background task, never shell &. ●━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ RESULT: real supervision lapse still blocks ✔ --- Scenario C: NO marker at all — baseline block preserved --- exit=2 (2=block) RESULT: unchanged strict behavior ✔ ```
Evidence: Mutation verification (fix reverted) `Base-commit guard + fresh arm-inflight marker → exit=2: without the fix the guard blocks a correctly-armed turn (the bug this change removes).` ```text === MUTATION TEST: fix reverted (base-commit guard), fresh arm-inflight marker present === exit=2 (expect 2 = false block returns without the fix) CONFIRMED: without the fix the guard blocks a correctly-armed turn — the bug the fix removes ✔ ```

title: fm-brief.sh: unescaped apostrophe inside a heredoc breaks bash parsing
body:
## Symptom
\`bin/fm-brief.sh <id> <repo>\` fails immediately with:
\`\`\`
bin/fm-brief.sh: line 314: unexpected EOF while looking for matching \`)'
bin/fm-brief.sh: line 388: syntax error: unexpected end of file
\`\`\`
This breaks every ship-brief scaffold, not just \`no-mistakes\`-mode ones, because the whole file must parse before any branch runs.

## Root cause
The no-mistakes-mode DOD heredoc (around line 314-331) is built with \`DOD=\$(cat <<EOF ... EOF)\` - a heredoc nested inside a \`\$(...)\` command substitution. One line in that heredoc body contains a literal apostrophe:
\`- Avoid \\\`--yes\\\`: it would silently bypass firstmate's authority check and any required captain escalation.\`

On this bash (confirmed on the local \`/bin/bash\`), an odd number of literal single-quote characters inside a heredoc body that is itself wrapped in \`\$(...)\` breaks the parser's paren-matching, even though heredocs otherwise ignore quoting. Minimal repro:
\`\`\`sh
DOD=\$(cat <<EOF
hello firstmate's world
EOF
)
echo "\$DOD"
\`\`\`
\`bash -n\` on that alone reproduces the same \`unexpected EOF while looking for matching \`)'\` error.

## Fix
Reword that line to avoid the bare apostrophe (e.g. \"the firstmate authority check\" instead of \"firstmate's authority check\"), or restructure the heredoc to not sit inside \`\$(...)\` (e.g. write to a temp var via \`read -r -d ''\` or build with \`printf\`). Add a regression test asserting \`bash -n bin/fm-brief.sh\` (and ideally a scaffold smoke test for every project mode) so a future edit to any of these heredocs can't silently reintroduce this.

## Impact discovered
Hit this live while dispatching a ship task; worked around it by hand-writing the brief instead of running the scaffold. Filing so it gets a proper fix through the normal pipeline instead of a hotfix under time pressure.

Register the new skill in `docs/documentation-audiences.json` under the `agent-runtime` audience so it is inventoried and link-checked (`fm-doc-audience-check.sh` passes with all 56 surfaces classified). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Documentation-only addition (a new internal skill, an AGENTS.md convention, and its inventory entry) with all cross-references, section pointers, frontmatter conventions, and the doc-audience inventory verified consistent and intent-conformant. ## Testing Ran the smallest set of structural gates that govern the three tracked surfaces this change ships (doc-audience-check script, fm-documentation-audiences, fm-instruction-owners, fm-stow-contract) — all pass, confirming the new skill is registered/linkable, the AGENTS.md additions honor the one-trigger and no-em-dash contracts, and the /stow boundary is intact. Since these are agent-facing documentation surfaces with no local markdown renderer available, I built a rendered HTML view of the new SKILL.md and the AGENTS.md diff and captured a headless-Chromium screenshot as reviewer-visible evidence; it clearly shows the five lens tags, the amended self-resolve/captain-ticket/defer/dismiss routing split, and the memlog convention's explicit graphify and /stow boundaries. It complements no-mistakes for document quality and planning integrity. It does not replace no-mistakes, code review, project-docs, Linear workflow, or the captain's decision authority. ## Inputs Read the target artifact in full before finding issues. Also read any cited SPEC, memlog, report, ticket, PR, or project document that the target depends on for its claims. If the artifact is large, split the review by section but keep one consolidated findings list. If the target claims to be rendered from a memlog, read the memlog first and verify that every rendered decision, non-goal, ticket, and acceptance criterion can be traced to a current entry. ## Lenses Use every required lens unless the caller explicitly scopes a narrower review. Tag each finding with exactly one primary lens. - `adversarial` tests whether a reasonable critic could reject the artifact's assumptions, scope, authority, or unstated tradeoffs. - `edge-case` tests unusual projects, absent integrations, missing credentials, concurrent work, privacy boundaries, or failure modes that the artifact does not cover. - `verification-gap` tests whether success signals, evidence, acceptance criteria, and rerender proofs are concrete enough to validate. - `structure` tests ownership, ordering, duplication, rendering boundaries, dependency flow, and whether a worker could act without guessing. - `prose` tests ambiguity, stale wording, captain-facing translation, excessive ceremony, and sentences that obscure the operational consequence. ## Finding format Return a compact findings table followed by any safe self-resolutions already applied or recommended. Use this schema for every finding: - `id`: stable local identifier such as `DRL-001`. - `lens`: one of the required lens tags. - `severity`: `minor`, `moderate`, or `major`. - `evidence`: exact source location or quote. - `risk`: what can go wrong if this remains as written. - `route`: `self-resolve`, `captain-ticket`, `defer`, or `dismiss`. - `recommended action`: the concrete edit, ticket, or reason to leave it alone. ## Routing findings Do not turn every unresolved captain-facing finding into a decision hold or ticket. Firstmate self-resolves smaller document revisions when the overall project direction already answers them. Use `self-resolve` for clarification, missing cross-references, local inconsistency, incomplete verification wording, stale phrasing, and limited scope choices that stay inside the approved initiative direction. Use `captain-ticket` only for large directional commitments such as product scope expansion, architecture or workflow commitments that constrain future work, security or privacy posture, irreversible or costly external commitments, or a conflict between approved sources that cannot be resolved from the existing direction. When `captain-ticket` is required, create or request a Linear issue assigned to the captain and summarize the decision needed in plain language. Use the decision-hold lifecycle only when the unresolved decision must be tracked locally rather than as a Linear issue, or when another firstmate contract specifically requires that lifecycle before completion. Use `defer` only when the artifact can remain useful without the answer and the deferred question has a named destination. Use `dismiss` only when the issue is invalidated by a cited source or is below the artifact's intended rigor. ## Memlog interaction checks A memlog is source material for one initiative's planning render, not a general memory bucket. It never replaces `/stow`, because `/stow` routes session knowledge to the most specific durable owner and may decide that a fact belongs in captain preferences, learnings, backlog, a project `AGENTS.md`, or shared tracked material instead. It never replaces graphify, because graphify indexes and queries a corpus but does not own decisions or rendering authority. If graphify is run over a corpus that includes rendered SPECs or memlogs, treat its output as navigation evidence only and trace decisions back to the memlog before changing tickets or briefs. If `/stow` finds a session decision for an active initiative with a memlog, the stow sweep may add or cite the memlog entry, then still route any broader reusable learning to the normal knowledge owner. ## Done criteria The review is done only after the findings list names the lenses used, each finding has a route, and any `captain-ticket` or local decision tracking destination is explicit. For a memlog-derived artifact, the review is done only after the report says whether the render is traceable from current memlog entries. Before treating an investigation or visual review as complete, load `decision-hold-lifecycle` if any unresolved decision remains outside a Linear ticket. ```

title: feat(fm-spawn): auto-inject scout role note for firstmate-repo scouts
body:
## Intent Mission fm-scout-role-guard: for firstmate-repo scout spawns, make bin/fm-spawn.sh structurally add the proven scout role disclaimer so callers no longer have to hand-write it. The behavior must only apply when kind=scout and the project directory belongs to the firstmate repo or one of its git worktrees; non-scout spawns and scouts for other projects must keep the original source brief. The disclaimer should say the worker is a scout, the repo AGENTS.md does not apply, it must not run bin/fm-session-start.sh, arm watchers, or touch state/, and its brief is its only job. If the source brief already contains ROLE NOTE:, do not duplicate it. Add tests in the repo's shell test style. ## What Changed Origin: addresses the 2026-07-25 learnings entry for the firstmate-repo scout identity-confusion trap. - `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now structurally prepends a scout `ROLE NOTE:` disclaimer to the delivered brief when `kind=scout` and the project directory is the firstmate repo or one of its git worktrees, so callers no longer hand-write it. Detection compares the resolved `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` of the project against `FM_ROOT` (new `git_common_dir_real` / `project_is_firstmate_checkout` helpers), and `prepare_delivered_brief` writes the augmented brief to `brief.with-scout-role-note.md`; the note tells the worker it is a scout, that the repo AGENTS.md does not apply, and not to run `bin/fm-session-start.sh`, arm watchers, or touch `state/`. - Non-scout spawns, scouts for other projects, and briefs that already contain `ROLE NOTE:` keep the original source brief unchanged. Brief delivery (`sq_brief`) and the Kimi pointer now reference `DELIVERED_BRIEF`/`DELIVERED_BRIEF_REAL` instead of the raw brief path. - Adds `tests/fm-spawn-scout-role.test.sh` covering the four cases: firstmate-root scout gets the note, an existing `ROLE NOTE:` is not duplicated, non-scout ships keep the source brief, and non-firstmate scouts keep the source brief. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a well-bounded, structurally-gated brief augmentation that correctly targets only firstmate-repo scouts, consistently updates every delivery path, is set -e-safe, and ships matching shell tests, with only a trivial redundant-variable observation. ## Testing Ran the new `tests/fm-spawn-scout-role.test.sh` both directly and through `bin/fm-test-run.sh` (all cases pass), then produced product-level evidence by driving the real `fm-spawn.sh` across five scenarios and capturing the actual delivered-brief content plus the exact brief path launched into the worker pane; the transcript confirms the role disclaimer is injected only for firstmate-repo scouts (root and worktree), is never duplicated when the source already has ROLE NOTE:, and is absent for non-scout and non-firstmate spawns. This is a CLI/backend change with no rendered UI surface, so the reviewer-visible artifact is a CLI transcript rather than a screenshot. Worktree left clean.

title: fix(bin): restore Bash 3.2 parsing of ship brief scaffolding
body:
## Intent Restore macOS Bash 3.2 compatibility in Firstmate ship brief scaffolding so the captain-approved Artemis follow-on work can be dispatched. The no-mistakes Definition-of-done heredoc is built inside command substitution, and an apostrophe in its prose prevents Bash 3.2 from finding the closing parenthesis. Rephrase that sentence without changing the brief's authority semantics, add version-independent regression coverage that forbids apostrophes in all ship Definition-of-done heredoc bodies, and preserve every generated brief safety contract. This is a CLI/text-generation change with no rendered UI surface, so the reviewer-visible artifact is the generated brief markdown and CLI transcripts rather than a screenshot. Everything passes with no findings.
