title: fix: teach exact keyed status token placement
body:
## Intent Fix the keyed status-event guidance in Firstmate's generated worker instructions so a decision or blocker cannot silently collapse to the default key because [key=] was placed after the first colon. Root cause: bin/fm-classify-lib.sh deliberately reads the optional key token from the event prefix before the first colon, so needs-decision: summary [key=route] is unkeyed (default) while needs-decision [key=route]: summary is keyed. Live workers were emitting trailing tokens because the generated brief prose said to reuse keys on later needs-decision/blocked/paused/done/failed/resolved events but did not consistently show exact token placement (parentheticals like "add the same [key=] if you opened it with one"). Deliberate choices: - Keep bin/fm-classify-lib.sh as the wire-format owner; do not change the parser to accept trailing tokens (status summaries may legitimately mention [key=...] as text). - Fix every ordinary ship, scout, and secondmate generated status-protocol variant in bin/fm-brief.sh so they demonstrate the exact form with the token between the verb and colon. - Preserve the valid unkeyed form for genuine one-off events (structured key default). - Explicitly teach that a trailing [key=...] after the colon is note text only and does not set the structured key. - Add focused regression coverage in tests/fm-brief.test.sh proving all scaffolds teach exact syntax and that trailing prose does not become the structured key; remove the old ambiguous parenthetical wording. - Smallest one-owner correction: worker-facing brief guidance only, not a parser change. ## What Changed - Update ship, scout, and secondmate briefs to place `[key=]` between the status verb and colon while preserving valid unkeyed events. - Clarify that trailing key tokens are note text only and add regression coverage for every scaffold and the existing parser contract. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-bounded, conforms to the stated intent across ship, scout, and secondmate guidance, preserves parser ownership and unkeyed events, and adds focused regression coverage. ## Testing Inspected the target change, ran the focused brief regression suite, generated and reviewed all three end-user worker scaffolds, directly demonstrated keyed versus trailing-token classifier behavior, verified the parser stayed unchanged, and found no failures or missing evidence.
Evidence: Generated guidance excerpts `Generated ship, scout, and secondmate briefs, each showing the key token before the colon, the valid unkeyed form, and the trailing-token warning.` ```text # Generated worker guidance excerpts ## ship 42: For concurrent or multi-item decisions and blockers, put the key token between the verb and the colon on every related event: `needs-decision [key=]: {summary}`, `blocked [key=]: {why}`, `paused [key=]: {why}`, `done [key=]: {outcome}`, `failed [key=]: {why}`, `resolved [key=]: {how}`. 43: Omit the token for a genuine one-off (structured key `default`); a trailing `[key=...]` after the colon is note text only and does not set the structured key. ## scout 35: For concurrent or multi-item decisions and blockers, put the key token between the verb and the colon on every related event: `needs-decision [key=]: {summary}`, `blocked [key=]: {why}`, `paused [key=]: {why}`, `done [key=]: {outcome}`, `failed [key=]: {why}`, `resolved [key=]: {how}`. 36: Omit the token for a genuine one-off (structured key `default`); a trailing `[key=...]` after the colon is note text only and does not set the structured key. ## secondmate 44:If its first reportable event is `working [key=]: {material phase}`, use the same key on its later `paused`, `done`, `failed`, `needs-decision`, or `blocked` event so the earlier working phase is superseded: e.g. `needs-decision [key=]: {summary}`, `blocked [key=]: {why}`, `paused [key=]: {why}`, `done [key=]: {outcome}`, `failed [key=]: {why}`. 47:The `[key=]` token always sits between the verb and the colon; a trailing `[key=...]` after the colon is note text only and leaves the structured key as default. ```
Evidence: Classifier behavior transcript Keyed input produced `route`; trailing and unkeyed inputs both produced `default`. ```text Wire-format behavior observed through bin/fm-classify-lib.sh Input (keyed): needs-decision [key=route]: choose route A or B Structured key: route Open decision record: route needs-decision choose route A or B Input (trailing-token): needs-decision: choose route A or B [key=route] Structured key: default Open decision record: default needs-decision choose route A or B [key=route] Input (unkeyed): needs-decision: choose route A or B Structured key: default Open decision record: default needs-decision choose route A or B ```
Evidence: Brief generation transcript `CLI output confirming all three worker briefs were scaffolded.` ```text scaffolded: /var/folders/k5/bgghp9854wz092fxzzx84skm0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYHEC96G32ZSSCVPQRRY23GA/generated-home/data/evidence-ship/brief.md (ship, mode=no-mistakes; replace {TASK}) scaffolded: /var/folders/k5/bgghp9854wz092fxzzx84skm0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYHEC96G32ZSSCVPQRRY23GA/generated-home/data/evidence-scout/brief.md (scout; replace {TASK}) scaffolded: /var/folders/k5/bgghp9854wz092fxzzx84skm0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYHEC96G32ZSSCVPQRRY23GA/generated-home/data/evidence-secondmate/brief.md (secondmate charter) ```
Evidence: Generated ship brief ```text You are a crewmate: an autonomous worker agent managed by firstmate. Work on your own; do not wait for a human. # Task {TASK} # Herdr lifecycle declaration - NOT ENABLED **HARD SAFETY GATE:** this scaffold cannot inspect the task text that replaces `{TASK}` later. If the task will start, stop, delete, restart, profile, or otherwise drive Herdr lifecycle behavior, stop and regenerate the brief with `--herdr-lab` before dispatch. Do not add Herdr lifecycle commands to this unguarded brief by hand. # Setup You are in a disposable git worktree of example-project, at a detached HEAD on a clean default branch. **Verify isolation before anything else.** Run `pwd -P` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; both must resolve to the disposable task worktree you were launched in, such as a treehouse pool path or an Orca-managed worktree, not the primary checkout firstmate operates from. The path check is authoritative: `git rev-parse --git-dir` and `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` can help inspect the repo, but they do not prove you are outside the primary checkout. If the top-level path is the primary checkout or not the worktree you were launched in, STOP - do not branch or commit here - append `blocked: launched in primary checkout, not an isolated worktree` to the status file and stop. 1. First action: create your branch: `git checkout -b fm/evidence-ship` 2. Run `no-mistakes doctor`; if it reports the repo is not initialized here, run `no-mistakes init`. # Rules 1. Never push to the default branch. Never merge a PR. 2. Stay inside this worktree; modify nothing outside it. 3. Use gh-axi for GitHub operations and chrome-devtools-axi for browser operations. 4. Report status by appending one line: `echo "{state}: {one short line}" >> '/var/folders/k5/bgghp9854wz092fxzzx84skm0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYHEC96G32ZSSCVPQRRY23GA/generated-home/state/evidence-ship.status'` States: working, needs-decision, blocked, paused, done, failed. Each append wakes firstmate, so report sparingly: only phase changes a supervisor would act on (setup done, bug reproduced, fix implemented, validation passed) and the needs-decision/blocked/paused/done/failed states. No step-by-step FYI progress lines; firstmate reads your pane for that. A mid-task `working:` line (including setup complete) is nonterminal: do not end the turn after it; continue the same stage until a defined `done:` gate under Definition of done. Use `paused: {why}` - distinct from `blocked:` - ONLY when you are deliberately idling on a known external wait you expect to clear on its own (an upstream release, a rate-limit reset, a scheduled window): firstmate then leaves your idle pane alone and rechecks it on a long cadence instead of treating it as a possible wedge. Use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need help. 5. If you hit the same obstacle twice, append `blocked: {why}` and stop; firstmate will help. 6. If a decision belongs above the implementation worker (product choices, destructive actions, ask-user findings), append `needs-decision: {summary of options}` and stop. Firstmate will apply the configured authority and reply with the decision. When firstmate replies or a blocker clears and you resume, append `resolved: {how it was decided or unblocked}` so the decision or blocker is durably closed and does not keep resurfacing. For concurrent or multi-item decisions and blockers, put the key token between the verb and the colon on every related event: `needs-decision [key=]: {summary}`, `blocked [key=]: {why}`, `paused [key=]: {why}`, `done [key=]: {outcome}`, `failed [key=]: {why}`, `resolved [key=]: {how}`. Omit the token for a genuine one-off (structured key `default`); a trailing `[key=...]` after the colon is note text only and does not set the structured key. 7. Never stop, restart, or update the shared `no-mistakes` daemon - it is one instance serving every lane/home, so restarting it kills other lanes' in-flight pipeline runs. On ANY no-mistakes daemon error, append `blocked: {the daemon error}` and stop; only firstmate manages the daemon. # Project memory If `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` already exists, or if this task produced durable project-intrinsic knowledge, run `/Users/james/.no-mistakes/worktrees/03f7a29d4e35/01KYHEC96G32ZSSCVPQRRY23GA/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh .` in the worktree. Record only project knowledge useful to almost every future session. For anything the codebase already shows, prefer a pointer to the authoritative file, command, or doc over copying the detail. If you touch a project `AGENTS.md` that lacks `## Maintaining this file`, add that short self-governance section from `/Users/james/.no-mistakes/worktrees/03f7a29d4e35/01KYHEC96G32ZSSCVPQRRY23GA/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh` in the same pass. Keep it proportionate: skip `AGENTS.md` edits for trivial tasks that produced no durable project knowledge. # Definition of done The task is complete only when committed on your branch. When you believe it is complete, append `done: {summary}` to the status file and stop. Firstmate will then instruct you to run /no-mistakes to validate and ship a PR. You drive no-mistakes by responding to its gates, not by implementing fixes. Follow the guidance no-mistakes itself provides for the mechanics: it loads when you invoke /no-mistakes, and `no-mistakes axi run --help` plus the `help` lines in each `axi` response are authoritative and version-matched to the installed binary. Do not hand-edit, commit, or fix findings yourself while a run is active - the pipeline applies every fix. Two firstmate-specific rules layer on top of that guidance: - ask-user findings are never yours to answer: escalate to firstmate (rule 6) and stop. Firstmate applies the authority contract in its `AGENTS.md` and obtains any required captain decision. When the decision comes back, feed it to the gate with `no-mistakes axi respond` and let the pipeline apply it - do not route the question to "the user" or implement the fix yourself. - Avoid `--yes`: it would silently bypass firstmate's authority check and any required captain escalation. After /no-mistakes reports CI green (the CI-ready return point - do not wait for it to keep monitoring in the background until merge), append `done: PR {url} checks green` and stop. You are finished. ```

Use `paused: {why}` (distinct from `blocked:`) only when your domain is deliberately idling on a known external wait you expect to clear on its own; use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need firstmate to act. Use this only for material phase changes, a captain decision, a real blocker, a failure, or work ready for review. This is also how you return the answer to a marked from-firstmate request above. A marked request requires one correlated answer after the work; it does not require a separate receipt or start acknowledgement. Never append `working:` merely to acknowledge receipt or announce that a marked request has started. When a routed-work phase has a supervisor-actionable material change worth reporting under the rule above, give that reported phase a stable key. If its first reportable event is `working [key=]: {material phase}`, use the same key on its later `paused`, `done`, `failed`, `needs-decision`, or `blocked` event so the earlier working phase is superseded: e.g. `needs-decision [key=]: {summary}`, `blocked [key=]: {why}`, `paused [key=]: {why}`, `done [key=]: {outcome}`, `failed [key=]: {why}`. When a keyed phase ends without another reportable state, append `resolved [key=]: {why it is no longer active}`. When a decision you escalated is answered or a blocker clears and your domain resumes, append `resolved: {how it was decided or unblocked}` for a genuine one-off, or `resolved [key=]: {how}` when you opened it with a key, so it is durably closed instead of resurfacing behind later unrelated events. The `[key=]` token always sits between the verb and the colon; a trailing `[key=...]` after the colon is note text only and leaves the structured key as default. Routine internal supervision, heartbeats, retries, and crewmate churn stay inside your own home and must not touch that status file. # Definition of done You are persistent by default. Do not exit just because your queue is empty. On startup and restart, run normal firstmate bootstrap and recovery through `bin/fm-session-start.sh` for your own home, but only to RECONCILE work that is already yours: in-flight crewmates, tracked backlog items, and durable watches recorded in this home. When you have no assigned or in-flight work after that reconciliation, go idle and wait silently for the main firstmate to route you a task. An empty queue is a healthy resting state, not a cue to invent work: never spawn a survey, audit, or any self-directed "find work" task on your own initiative. If this charter cannot be carried out, append `blocked: {why}` or `failed: {why}` to the main status file and stop. ```

title: chore: no-mistakes(review): move captain-identity owner contract to instruction-owners tests
body:
## Intent

Add a mandatory self-verify-access gate (rule 8) to the ship, scout, and secondmate brief scaffolds in bin/fm-brief.sh, so every generated brief instructs the worker to run the relevant identity check (az account show, aws sts get-caller-identity, gh auth status, vercel whoami, flyctl auth whoami, etc.) before appending blocked:/paused:/needs-decision: for a credential/permission/access reason, instead of accepting an untested boundary claim. Triggered by a real incident: a ship task sat blocked for three days framed as out of the worker's boundaries, when the worker had already used the same admin REST endpoint to read the access verdict. The rule text is a single shared ACCESS_GATE/ACCESS_RULE variable reused across all three brief variants. Extended tests/fm-brief.test.sh; bin/fm-lint.sh passes clean. This branch went through several deliberate captain-directed corrections, all already applied, none should be reverted or reworded: (1) removed a sentence that licensed write-path probing on successful reads, replaced with the opposite - a read never authorizes a write, do not probe. (2) Added a fleet-wide hard stop against acquiring the captain's identity. (3) Dropped a 'verified you could make it' capability claim that contradicted the no-probing rule - the escalation is now just the worker's verified own identity plus the exact change needed. (4) The captain-identity clause is framed around acquisition vs. provisioning, not around specific product names: forbidden is interactive sign-in as the captain, any approval prompt to a device he holds (MFA/authenticator push), or reaching for an ambient credential that sits on the machine only for his own administration (his signed-in az CLI is the canonical example); permitted is a credential deliberately provisioned for the worker's own work with known scope and attributed use. (5) AGENTS.md hard rule 6 states the same principle for firstmate itself, names the fleet's standing GitHub session as the current example of a provisioned credential, and plainly flags that this GitHub session is the captain's personal account rather than a dedicated fleet identity - a tracked gap, backlog id fm-fleet-github-identity-x1, deliberately not fixed in this change. (6) The ACCESS_GATE build was also rewritten from a heredoc-in-command-substitution to a plain double-quoted string, since the prose needs literal apostrophes and heredoc-in- has a known bash 3.2 parsing hazard (issue #166) that escaping would just work around awkwardly. American spelling (authorization, not authorisation) throughout. A prior run failed to push over the fork's SSH remote (git@github.com, host key + missing publickey auth) - fixed by re-running no-mistakes init --fork-url with an HTTPS fork URL instead, since gh is already authenticated over HTTPS and provisioning a new SSH key was unnecessary. Please review the current full diff on its own merits.

## What Changed

a82a28b no-mistakes(review): separate read-only identity checks from acting as the captain

0a5f90a no-mistakes(review): harden access gate against heredoc apostrophe bug
f9648e3 fix(brief): drop capability claim, make credential clause absolute, extend to AGENTS.md

95bdbbb no-mistakes(document): document access-verify gate in fm-brief.sh help header
1a277da no-mistakes(review): extend access gate to secondmate, pin pause verb in test
6e982ec no-mistakes(review): broaden access gate to paused/needs-decision, dedupe rule 8
3af336f fix(brief): remove write-probing sentence from the access-verify gate
e4eff69 feat(brief): add mandatory self-verify-access gate to generated briefs

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The round-3 change moves one static contract test between two already-registered test files with no production-code change, every relocated assertion verifies against its target file, and the earlier rounds' gate text and AGENTS.md rule are settled as the captain's confirmed final wording.

## Testing

Ran both directly affected test files plus the project's own `--changed` selection (30/31 pass; the single failure is an unrelated Pi-version pin in `fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh`), then went past unit assertions and scaffolded real briefs of all three kinds to read the gate as a crewmate would receive it: rule 8 in ship and scout, an `# Access boundaries` section in the secondmate charter, the configured pause verb interpolated, one rule-8 marker per brief, no escape leakage, and every intent-directed correction present in the rendered prose. I also proved the bash 3.2 rationale with a direct counterfactual rather than trusting the comment - the same prose as a heredoc in command substitution fails `/bin/bash -n` on one added apostrophe while the shipped double-quoted form parses and renders it literally - and confirmed the file's pre-existing 3.2 parse failure is identical at the base commit. No screenshot applies: the product surface is generated markdown consumed by an agent, so the rendered brief text itself is the end-user artifact. One divergence from the stated intent remains open for the author (AGENTS.md rule 6 no longer discloses the GitHub-session gap the intent says it does).

title: feat(qa): add fleet-wide Playwright UI test harness
body:
## Intent Build the fleet's standing Playwright agent test harness so any crewmate asked to QA a UI can run deterministic headless UI test cases (click/fill/assert) against a web app in an isolated browser, capture exact-viewport screenshot evidence, and harden the run into committed Playwright TypeScript specs the target project re-runs in CI. Captain approved Playwright for this on 2026-07-22 ("im happy with playwright just use the best things to get the job done"). Scope and deliberate decisions a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: - Distribution choice: fleet-wide reach means a firstmate tracked skill, so this ships as .agents/skills/playwright-qa/ with metadata.internal=true (agent-loaded, not installer-facing). Per-machine binaries and heavyweight dependencies deliberately stay OUT of the firstmate repo: Playwright installs into the TARGET project worktree, never into firstmate. That is why there is no package.json, node_modules, or Playwright dependency at the firstmate repo root, and why the example lives under the skill directory as reference material rather than as a firstmate build target. - bin/fm-playwright-scaffold.sh earns its place as a scaffold that drops a ready playwright.config.ts, a qa/ evidence directory, and an example spec into a project worktree, following the AXI CLI standard. It is intentionally a plain shell script with a colocated shell test (tests/fm-playwright-scaffold.test.sh), matching this repo's existing bin/ plus tests/ convention. - Safety rules are encoded in the skill on purpose: headless and isolated always, never attach to or drive the captain's own live Chrome, and screenshots plus specs are evidence that must exist before any visual deliverable is called verified. That is the R25b lesson: "did the agent actually check what it would look like for me?" must always be YES with proof. - Default named viewports are 1857x933 and 1440x900 by explicit request; they are not arbitrary. - Screenshots deliberately capture ONLY the viewport, not the full scrollable page. The captain decided this explicitly after an earlier review round raised it: every screenshot must be exactly the named viewport size so the evidence is a picture of one real screen, matching the harness promise. A full-page capture opt-in was considered and deliberately deferred to a later change, so its absence is intentional and should not be flagged as missing. - The skill deliberately keeps the "this versus chrome-devtools-axi" section short and points at the existing research file rather than duplicating it, per this repo's one-owner-for-a-contract rule. - The committed demo screenshots (qa/screenshots/demo-*.png) are intentional binary evidence proving the harness was actually run headless at both viewports against a static HTML page in this worktree. They are the proof artifact the definition of done requires, not stray build output. - Firstmate coding guidelines were followed for this shared tracked material: one sentence per line in docs, plain dashes, no agent commit co-author, a shellcheck-clean bin script, and a colocated test. Two commits on this branch came from an earlier no-mistakes run of this same change and are deliberately retained: - "no-mistakes(review): validate viewport width/height separately and reject duplicate names" is a review-gate fix to the scaffold script from that run. - "no-mistakes(test): fix multibyte glyph handling under C locale in composer classification" plus its accompanying changes to bin/backends/herdr.sh, bin/fm-composer-lib.sh, tests/fm-afk-inject-e2e.test.sh, and tests/fm-afk-inject-herdr-e2e.test.sh repair PRE-EXISTING test failures in this repo that are unrelated to the Playwright work: those tests assumed a UTF-8 locale and failed under a C locale. Firstmate explicitly decided to fold these locale-robustness fixes into this PR rather than splitting them into a separate change, so they are expected and authorized here. ## What Changed - Added the fleet-wide `playwright-qa` skill and reference project with deterministic headless click/fill/assert cases and committed exact-viewport screenshot evidence. - Added the AXI-style `fm-playwright-scaffold.sh` command and colocated tests to scaffold Playwright configuration, QA evidence directories, viewports, and starter specs in target projects. - Hardened viewport validation, duplicate viewport-name handling, and C-locale robustness in existing test helpers and AFK injection coverage; documented harness ownership and usage. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The changes are bounded, satisfy the stated Playwright harness requirements, and no material source defect was substantiated during review. ## Testing Focused scaffold behavior tests passed, the committed demo spec passed in isolated headless Chromium at both named viewports, screenshots were visually inspected and confirmed to be exact viewport sizes, duplicate-name rejection was checked, evidence was recorded, and no transient worktree artifacts remain.

title: fix(bin): keep heredoc bodies out of command substitutions so fm-brief.sh parses under stock macOS Bash 3.2
body:
## Problem

`bin/fm-brief.sh` does not parse at all under the bash that stock macOS ships, so scaffolding any brief is impossible on a stock Mac:

```
$ /bin/bash --version | head -1
GNU bash, version 3.2.57(1)-release (arm64-apple-darwin25)
$ /bin/bash -n bin/fm-brief.sh
bin/fm-brief.sh: line 314: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `)'
bin/fm-brief.sh: line 388: syntax error: unexpected end of file
```

Bash 3.2 scans a `$( ... )` command substitution for its closing paren with a quote tracker that does not skip heredoc bodies. An **odd** number of quote characters inside a heredoc written *inside* a command substitution makes that scan swallow the rest of the file. The word `firstmate's` in the no-mistakes definition-of-done block (introduced in #945) was that odd apostrophe, and it killed the parse of the whole file - so every delivery mode was broken, not just no-mistakes. Bash 4+ parses the construct, which is why Linux CI never caught it.

This is the second occurrence: #166 fixed the same class, but its guard was a grep for one specific phrase, which a different word walked straight past.

## Fix (structural, not cosmetic)

Heredoc bodies now live in emitter functions (`cat <<DELIM` inside a function, captured by the caller as `VAR=$(fn)`). A heredoc inside a function body is parsed at top level, where quote characters are ordinary text, so no future wording can re-arm the trap. Generated text is byte-unchanged - the diff touches only wrapper lines.

Nine instances existed across the toolbelt and all are converted:

| File | Instances |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/fm-brief.sh` | three delivery-mode definition-of-done blocks + the Herdr declaration (the fatal ones) |
| `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` | the generated `config/x-mode.env` cadence body |
| `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` | two embedded bounded-reader scripts + two jq filters |

The last five parsed today only because their quote characters happened to be balanced - the same latent trap, one edit from breaking.

`tests/*.sh` are deliberately untouched: six of them contain the construct (node/jq fixture bodies) but all parse cleanly under 3.2 today, and neither script the macOS CI lane executes is among them.

## Guard

`tests/fm-stock-bash-parse.test.sh` owns the class, not the phrase:

1. bans heredoc-inside-command-substitution across `bin/*.sh` and `bin/backends/*.sh` - portable, so it also fails on Linux where the parser itself cannot see the bug;
2. carries a positive-control fixture pair proving the banned shape really does break bash 3.2 while the function shape parses and emits identical text, so the guard cannot pass by being blind;
3. parses every bin script under a discovered bash 3.x (`FM_STOCK_BASH` overrides the search).

Against the pre-fix tree it fails and lists all nine sites; after the fix it passes.

The pre-existing `macos-stock-bash` CI job now runs this test in place of its single-file `bash -n bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` check, which the toolbelt-wide sweep strictly supersedes. No new job, runner, or lint surface was added. The test is registered in `bin/fm-test-run.sh`'s `pure-contract-unit` family map and lands in the `portable-serial` lane by complement, so `--check-coverage` stays consistent.

## Verification

On the real `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 (the only bash on the affected machine):

- defect reproduced at base, clean parse across all 92 scripts in `bin/` and `bin/backends/` after;
- all six scaffold shapes (three delivery modes, scout, `--herdr-lab`, secondmate charter) generate complete briefs;
- a freshly inserted lone apostrophe in brief prose still parses, while the same sentence in the old `DOD=$(cat <<EOF` form breaks it again - the trap is demonstrably disarmed;
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` clean at the pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0; `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` clean; `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` ok;
- `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` 15/15, plus `fm-stock-bash-parse`, `fm-fleet-snapshot-view`, `fm-bearings-snapshot`, `fm-x-mode`, `fm-bootstrap`, `fm-lint`, `fm-documentation-audiences`, `fm-instruction-owners` green.

Two suites fail identically at base with these changes stashed and are therefore environmental, not caused by this change: `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh` (timing-based scheduler asserts) and `tests/fm-session-start.test.sh` (concurrent session-lock).

Validated through the no-mistakes pipeline (intent, rebase, review, test, document, lint all green). It is opened from a fork because the contributing account has pull-only rights on this repo.

title: fix(bin): preserve task worktrees across exits and relaunches
body:
## Intent Second, separate defect on the same branch, urgently authorized: fix the preservation breach where a normally exiting non-Claude worker could trigger an automatic worktree return that deleted untracked content (an untracked handoff.md was lost this way in the O1 copy). Verified in a throwaway treehouse pool with a real pty: a task worktree held only by an interactive 'treehouse get' subshell lives exactly as long as that subshell; a pane falls back to that subshell the moment its agent exits normally, and treehouse's clean-and-return prompt defaults to YES, so one stray Enter recycles the pool slot and deletes every untracked file. Masking conditions: non-TTY stdin declines the same prompt (so scripted runs never showed it), a clean worktree returns silently with no prompt at all, and Claude-family panes rarely fall back to the shell. Earliest divergence is at ACQUISITION, not at exit. Chosen fix, deliberately: acquire every fresh ship/scout worktree as a durable treehouse lease under holder fm- and send the pane in with cd, which is exactly the durability firstmate already uses for secondmate homes in bin/fm-home-seed.sh; --lease support is already a bootstrap requirement, so a failed lease is terminal and there is intentionally NO fallback to the interactive form. The spawn's own abort path may release only a lease it just took and only when the worktree holds no uncommitted or untracked content - an automatic return must never delete work. Regression coverage: tests/fm-spawn-worktree-preservation.test.sh pairs a real-treehouse comparison of the unprotected and protected exit shapes with fake-based assertions on the acquisition contract, and tests/lib.sh gained a shared lease-aware treehouse stub that the existing spawn suites now use (their old exit-0 treehouse stub could not model lease output). A private report recording the verified facts and the recovery boundary was written outside the repo: no implementation code or commit was lost, but the untracked handoff.md cannot be recreated from summaries and must never be presented as recovered original content. Delivery correction from the captain: kunchenguid/firstmate is external upstream and must not be touched - upstream PR #1116 stays untouched, the push target and the PR repository and base must all be the captain-owned fork wuzihuang/firstmate, and no force-push over an unknown branch. The branch already exists on the fork at its exact prior pipeline head, so this push is a plain fast-forward. Constraint honored: no existing FM worktree or task record was touched, and no git reset, clean, force, or stash was used. ## What Changed - Lease fresh treehouse-backed ship and scout worktrees to `fm-`, enter them directly, and only release newly acquired leases on clean pre-recording aborts. - Relaunch existing tasks in their recorded project and worktree only after verifying the prior endpoint is gone and durable lease or adoption proof still matches; otherwise preserve state and refuse recovery. - Add legacy worktree adoption support, backend integration, documentation, and regression coverage for lease preservation and guarded recovery. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The latest change closes the holder-less native-lease recovery gap while preserving strict refusal for foreign or unprovable ownership, with focused regression coverage. ## Testing Inspected the focused change, then ran the real-treehouse and fake-backed preservation regression: it reproduced the unsafe interactive exit, proved a leased worktree preserves untracked content, verified byte-for-byte legacy adoption, terminal lease failure without fallback, and dirty-abort retention; all checks passed and the reviewer-visible CLI transcript was saved.
Evidence: Worktree preservation end-to-end transcript ```text 🌳 Setting up worktree... 🌳 Leased worktree at /tmp/fm-spawn-worktree-preservation.SQJfkW/pool/repo/.treehouse/repo-8f2f95/1/repo. Run 'treehouse return /tmp/fm-spawn-worktree-preservation.SQJfkW/pool/repo/.treehouse/repo-8f2f95/1/repo' to release it. ok - real treehouse: a subshell exit destroys untracked content, a leased copy entered with cd survives it ok - real treehouse: adoption preserves an unleased in-use copy byte-for-byte ok - a spawn leases its worktree and enters it with cd, never through the exit-sensitive subshell ok - a failed lease refuses the spawn instead of falling back to the exit-sensitive subshell ok - an aborted spawn never returns a leased copy that holds uncommitted or untracked content # all fm-spawn-worktree-preservation tests passed ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed (3) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1402` - A recovery relaunch enters the recorded worktree directly without establishing or verifying a durable treehouse lease. Legacy records created by the previous interactive acquisition path can therefore be relaunched into an unleased pool worktree that `treehouse get` or `prune` may later recycle, recreating the data-loss risk this change is intended to eliminate. Require proof of a matching durable lease—or safely acquire one—before relaunching; otherwise refuse while preserving the record. 🔧 Fix: Guard recovery relaunches with durable worktree proof 2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1042` - The owner required that a relaunch refuse when the current pool state is available or leased by another holder, but this branch accepts a matching adoption manifest without rechecking the pool. An adopted copy can later become available or acquire a foreign lease while its manifest remains unchanged (especially for a clean copy), allowing relaunch into an unprotected or differently owned worktree. Revalidate that the current pool entry remains an adoptable legacy state before accepting adoption proof. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1649` - A successful relaunch of a natively leased worktree rewrites metadata without `lease_holder` because `WT_LEASED` is empty on the recorded-worktree path. The next relaunch then rejects the still-valid native lease because the recorded holder is missing. Preserve the verified recorded holder when rewriting relaunch metadata. 🔧 Fix: Revalidate adoption ownership and preserve lease proof 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1040` - A record without `lease_holder=` is rejected even when treehouse proves the exact path is leased to `fm-<task-id>`. This conflicts with the required adoption no-op for an already matching native lease: `fm-adopt-worktree.sh` exits successfully without writing an adoption record, but the next spawn still refuses. Accept the proven matching lease and carry its holder into rewritten metadata, or make adoption repair the legacy metadata atomically. 🔧 Fix: Accept matching native leases for legacy records ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: fix(bin): restore brief scaffolding under stock macOS bash 3.2

## Intent Fix a blocking defect: bin/fm-brief.sh does not parse at all under the bash that stock macOS ships (GNU bash 3.2.57 as /bin/bash, no newer bash on PATH on the affected machine), so firstmate could not scaffold ANY crewmate brief on a stock Mac. Root cause: bash 3.2 scans a $( ... ) command substitution for its closing paren with a quote tracker that does not skip heredoc bodies, so an ODD number of quote characters inside a heredoc written INSIDE a command substitution swallows the rest of the file. The word 'firstmate' plus apostrophe plus 's' in the no-mistakes definition-of-done block (added in #945) was that odd apostrophe and it killed 'bash -n bin/fm-brief.sh' for the whole file, breaking every delivery mode. Bash 4+ parses the construct, so Linux CI never caught it, and the earlier #166 guard was a grep for one specific phrase that a different word walked straight past. The captain required the fix to be STRUCTURAL, not cosmetic: deleting the one apostrophe restores the parse but leaves the trap armed for the next contributor who writes "it's" or "don't". Change only bin/fm-brief.sh and tests/fm-brief.test.sh, invoke no Herdr lifecycle operations, and validate with bash -n, affected tests, bin/fm-lint.sh, and git diff --check. ## What Changed - Preserve the generated `firstmate's authority check` wording through safe variable substitution so `fm-brief.sh` parses on Bash 3.2 and Herdr lab briefs scaffold successfully. - Expand Herdr lab regression coverage across ship and scout briefs, including task-derived session naming, quoted helper paths, guarded lifecycle commands, trailing session scope, and prohibited direct or global operations. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the narrowly scoped quoting fix preserves generated wording and the expanded regression coverage matches the Herdr scaffold requirements without introducing material source risk. ## Testing The baseline script reproduced the unmatched-parenthesis failure under macOS Bash 3.2.57, while the target parsed cleanly; the affected behavior suite passed, and real ship/scout scaffolds produced reviewer-visible Markdown containing every required safety and wording detail without executing Herdr lifecycle operations. The working tree remained clean. Per this validation task’s explicit prohibition on linters and static analysis, `bin/fm-lint.sh` and `git diff --check` were not run.
Evidence: Generated Herdr-lab ship brief ```text You are a crewmate: an autonomous worker agent managed by firstmate. Work on your own; do not wait for a human. # Task {TASK} # Herdr isolation - HARD SAFETY CONTRACT This brief was explicitly scaffolded with `--herdr-lab` because the task will drive Herdr lifecycle behavior. On Herdr 0.7.3 the API socket is not relocatable by `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, or `HOME`. A named non-`default` session plus a trailing `--session ` on every call is the only viable local isolation. 1. Set `HERDR_LAB_HELPER='/Users/darrencarter/.no-mistakes/worktrees/437ec9ddfa86/01KYHX6WDV4155C1XVWA7WWCRJ/bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh'` and generate the session name with `HERDR_LAB_SESSION=$("$HERDR_LAB_HELPER" name review-herdr-ship)`. Install `trap '"$HERDR_LAB_HELPER" teardown "$HERDR_LAB_SESSION"' EXIT` before provisioning, then provision only with `"$HERDR_LAB_HELPER" provision "$HERDR_LAB_SESSION"`. 2. Run every task-specific non-lifecycle Herdr command through `"$HERDR_LAB_HELPER" run "$HERDR_LAB_SESSION" `. The helper appends the required trailing `--session "$HERDR_LAB_SESSION"`; `HERDR_SESSION` alone is never accepted as isolation. 3. Teardown only through `"$HERDR_LAB_HELPER" teardown "$HERDR_LAB_SESSION"`. It re-checks refuse-default immediately before stop and again immediately before delete, and fails closed on ambiguity. 4. If an experiment requires a deliberate mid-run session stop, use only `"$HERDR_LAB_HELPER" stop "$HERDR_LAB_SESSION"`; it performs the same immediate refuse-default check. 5. Forbidden commands: direct `herdr server stop`, every other server-global operation such as `herdr server live-handoff` or reload/update operations, direct `herdr session stop`, direct `herdr session delete`, and any Herdr call scoped only by ambient or inline `HERDR_SESSION`. 6. The helper records the live default session before provisioning and verifies the identical fleet state after teardown. A missing, stopped, or changed default session is a hard tripwire failure, never a cleanup warning to ignore. Never bypass the helper, even for a read-only lifecycle probe or cleanup after failure. The captain fleet uses the running `default` session. # Setup You are in a disposable git worktree of firstmate, at a detached HEAD on a clean default branch. **Verify isolation before anything else.** Run `pwd -P` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; both must resolve to the disposable task worktree you were launched in, such as a treehouse pool path or an Orca-managed worktree, not the primary checkout firstmate operates from. The path check is authoritative: `git rev-parse --git-dir` and `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` can help inspect the repo, but they do not prove you are outside the primary checkout. If the top-level path is the primary checkout or not the worktree you were launched in, STOP - do not branch or commit here - append `blocked: launched in primary checkout, not an isolated worktree` to the status file and stop. 1. title: fix(bin): parse cleanly under macOS system bash 3.2
body:
## Problem

On a stock macOS host the system shell is bash 3.2.57, and `/usr/bin/env bash` resolves to it when no newer bash is installed.
Running any ship scaffold (`bin/fm-brief.sh <id> <repo>`) failed:

```
bin/fm-brief.sh: line 314: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `)'
bin/fm-brief.sh: line 388: syntax error: unexpected end of file
```

Root cause (verified by bisection): bash 3.2's naive `$(...)` scanner tracks quote state through a heredoc body nested in a command substitution, so the apostrophe in the no-mistakes DOD wording ("firstmate's authority check", introduced in ec09871 / #945) inside `DOD=$(cat <<EOF ... EOF)` broke the parse of the entire rest of the script.
Every ship-task scaffold on a stock-bash mac failed; scout scaffolds escaped only because they `exit 0` before the parser reaches the ship-mode `case`.
The issue #166 regression test did not catch this because its `bash -n` runs under the dev bash, whose scanner accepts the wording.

## Fix

Structural, not a rewording: every `VAR=$(cat <<EOF ... EOF)` in `bin/` now uses the `IFS= read -r -d '' VAR <<EOF ... EOF || true` idiom plus a single trailing-newline strip, so no heredoc lives inside `$(...)` and future copy edits adding apostrophes, backticks, or parens cannot re-break parsing.
The emitted brief text is byte-identical: the diff touches only assignment wrappers (zero body lines), and the idiom was empirically verified equivalent to `$(cat <<EOF)` under bash 3.2, including expansion and backtick handling.

Converted sites:

- `bin/fm-brief.sh` - the three ship-mode DOD heredocs and the unguarded Herdr section (the reproduced failure).
- `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` (4 sites) and `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` (1 site) - the audit's remaining `$(cat <<` instances; they parse today only because their apostrophes happen to balance, so they were converted rather than listed.

## Regression coverage

`tests/fm-brief.test.sh` (extended in place because CI test lanes are explicit hand-maintained lists):

- `bash -n` now also runs under the system `/bin/bash` - the real 3.2 gate on macOS.
- A sweep syntax-checks every `bin/*.sh` and `bin/backends/*.sh` under `/bin/bash`, guarding the whole bug class.
- The per-mode scaffold test asserts non-empty output containing each delivery mode's definition-of-done marker.

Pipeline follow-ups on this branch: documentation of the heredoc rule, and the macOS CI lane now runs the fm-brief regression gate so the sweep executes under a real bash 3.2 in CI, not only on developer macs.

## Verification (on the affected stock-bash mac)

- Reproduced first on the default branch: `/bin/bash -n bin/fm-brief.sh` exit 2 with the exact error above.
- After the fix: `/bin/bash -n` clean on all bin scripts; real scaffolds for no-mistakes, direct-PR, local-only, `--scout`, and `--secondmate` all generate correctly under bash 3.2.
- `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` green; `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed` (~40 suites) exit 0; `bin/fm-lint.sh` green under pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0.
- Pre-existing, unrelated: `tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh` fails identically on the clean default branch on this host.

title: feat(bin): instruct crewmates to verify web behavior by driving the browser
body:
## Intent Make browser-based, act-like-a-user web debugging a standard, instructed capability for firstmate crewmates. Background: the generated crewmate brief's Rule 3 only said 'use gh-axi for GitHub operations and chrome-devtools-axi for browser operations', which was too weak - a recent web investigation could not confirm what a page actually rendered and fell back to reading code and querying the database instead. The captain asked to close that gap in the shared brief scaffold (bin/fm-brief.sh), which is firstmate's shared tracked instruction surface. Deliberate decisions, so they read as intent and not mistakes: - The guidance REPLACES the weak Rule 3 line rather than adding a redundant new section, because firstmate-coding-guidelines require one owner per contract and the scaffold keeps a terse voice. Rule numbering (1,2,3,4...) is deliberately preserved. - The rule is defined ONCE as a shared BROWSER_RULE heredoc and interpolated into both the ship scaffold and the scout/diagnostic scaffold, specifically so the two variants cannot drift. The test asserts byte-identical rendering in both variants for exactly this reason. - It deliberately names BOTH tools with distinct roles: chrome-devtools-axi for interactive drive-the-real-browser inspection of live rendered state, and the project's Playwright/e2e harness for a scripted repeatable run of the same user flow that becomes the regression test once a fix is authorized. - The scaffold is deliberately ENVIRONMENT-AGNOSTIC: the system-browser-via-Playwright line is the general fallback for when a bundled interactive browser cannot launch. No machine-specific quirk is hardcoded (the fleet-local WSL detail lives in the operator's learnings file, not this shared scaffold), so the absence of concrete environment detail here is intentional. - Scope was explicitly bounded by the captain to bin/fm-brief.sh plus its test: no project AGENTS.md edits, no Playwright installed into any project by this task, and diagnostic-reasoning deliberately left untouched. - Every existing safety line is preserved untouched: worktree isolation assertion, never-push-to-default, the status protocol, the Herdr hard safety gate, and the scout report contract. Earlier gate rounds on this branch already produced four no-mistakes(review) fix commits that are part of the accepted design and should not be re-litigated: the browser instruction is scoped to tasks involving user-visible web behavior rather than every task; a cannot-drive-a-browser case escalates via the existing blocked: status protocol instead of silently reporting success on rendered behavior never seen; the reproduction is recorded where the task's deliverable lives (branch for ship, report for scout); and drift guards were added to the test. You must distinguish who it is from, because the answer goes to a different place. A request relayed to you by the main firstmate is tagged with a leading `[fm-from-firstmate]` marker followed by an invisible system separator; this marker is untypable, so a human never produces it. When a message carries that marker, do the work, then respond via the STATUS/ESCALATION path below, never only in this chat: the main firstmate does not read your chat, so a chat-only reply is lost. Marked requests also carry a privacy-safe `corr=` token after the marker; include that exact token in your parent status reply (or in the status pointer to a detailed doc) so the parent can correlate the answer. Optional helper: `bin/fm-secondmate-report.sh` can append a correlated status line for you, but a plain `echo` that includes the same `corr=` is equally valid - do not depend on the helper being present. For a terse result, a status line is the whole answer. For a detailed answer (an investigation, a plan, an audit), write it to a doc under your home's `data/` and append a status line that points to that doc - the scout-report pattern - so the main firstmate is woken and can read it. Before treating an investigation or visual review as complete, load `decision-hold-lifecycle` from this home's `.agents/skills/` and pass its shared completion gate. A message with NO marker is the captain typing directly into your pane: treat it as authoritative captain intervention and stay conversational exactly as you would for any captain message; do not force it onto the status path. # Escalation to main firstmate Handle routine work yourself. Report only true captain-relevant outcomes or a declared external wait by appending one line: `echo "{state}: {one short line}" >> '/tmp/tmp.Nvg1fEQwK9/fmhome/state/demo-secondmate.status'` States: working, needs-decision, blocked, paused, done, failed. Use `paused: {why}` (distinct from `blocked:`) only when your domain is deliberately idling on a known external wait you expect to clear on its own; use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need firstmate to act. Use this only for material phase changes, a captain decision, a real blocker, a failure, or work ready for review. This is also how you return the answer to a marked from-firstmate request above. A marked request requires one correlated answer after the work; it does not require a separate receipt or start acknowledgement. Never append `working:` merely to acknowledge receipt or announce that a marked request has started. When a routed-work phase has a supervisor-actionable material change worth reporting under the rule above, give that reported phase a stable key. If its first reportable event is `working [key=]: {material phase}`, use the same key on its later `paused`, `done`, `failed`, `needs-decision`, or `blocked` event so the earlier working phase is superseded. When a keyed phase ends without another reportable state, append `resolved [key=]: {why it is no longer active}`. When a decision you escalated is answered or a blocker clears and your domain resumes, append `resolved: {how it was decided or unblocked}` (keyed with `[key=]` if you opened it with one) so it is durably closed instead of resurfacing behind later unrelated events. Routine internal supervision, heartbeats, retries, and crewmate churn stay inside your own home and must not touch that status file. # Definition of done You are persistent by default. Do not exit just because your queue is empty. On startup and restart, run normal firstmate bootstrap and recovery through `bin/fm-session-start.sh` for your own home, but only to RECONCILE work that is already yours: in-flight crewmates, tracked backlog items, and durable watches recorded in this home. When you have no assigned or in-flight work after that reconciliation, go idle and wait silently for the main firstmate to route you a task. An empty queue is a healthy resting state, not a cue to invent work: never spawn a survey, audit, or any self-directed "find work" task on your own initiative. If this charter cannot be carried out, append `blocked: {why}` or `failed: {why}` to the main status file and stop. ```

For a ship task that means a crewmate can add Playwright, its browser binaries, and the associated CI surface to any project and land it in the PR on its own authority. That sits in tension with rule 6 in the same brief ("If a decision belongs above the implementation worker (product choices...) append needs-decision and stop") and with AGENTS.md section 7's rule that standing autonomy never approves work that materially expands the engineering contract. But to a crewmate, "project paths" and "repository paths" most naturally name the worktree it is working in - the one place it is explicitly allowed to write - so the sentence can be read as forbidding the very writes rule 3 requires (installing the e2e harness, node_modules, test-results/, playwright-report/). title: feat(devenv): add a remote control plane for existing OrbStack devenvs
body:
## Intent Fork FirstMate to orchestrate six reusable OrbStack devenvs as isolated remote execution environments. Keep the Mac-side Captain as the only captain and give each VM a persistent secondmate home so Captain context stays clean. Herdr remains a separate, explicitly named session and every VM remains directly accessible in Herdr for debugging or intervention. Use an explicit devenv backend, with no main-as-base semantics, and fail closed on ambiguous registry, checkout, process, lease, or session state. Local task-scoped mutation is autonomous; merge, deploy, production, and shared-cloud actions remain human-controlled. This branch implements the control plane, safety contracts, documentation, and live smoke evidence only; production controller eligibility intentionally remains unavailable until the later resident process classifier supplies pipeline, interactive-agent, and checkout-process facts. Pi is optional and unrelated. ## What Changed - Adds an explicit `devenv` runtime backend (`bin/backends/devenv.sh`, wired through `bin/fm-backend.sh`) that discovers and validates the existing `~/.expanly-devenvs.json` registry, synthesizes `main` without base-image or privileged-worker semantics, and requires `ssh` and `jq` rather than being auto-detected. - Adds the control-plane scripts: `bin/fm-devenv-install.sh` installs and verifies a commit-pinned FirstMate runtime release on a VM; `bin/fm-devenv-remote.sh` serves the bounded `firstmate.devenv.v1` JSON protocol (`inspect`, `claim`, `status`, `release`) over a fixed remote command path; `bin/fm-devenv-controller.sh` plus `fm-devenv-lib.sh` / `fm-devenv-lease-lib.sh` own registry parsing, the durable task queue, lock-fenced claims, and 64-hex token-guarded leases. Every command failure prints one `fm-devenv-controller:` reason on stderr, and unknown or contradictory VM facts make an environment ineligible so work stays queued — automatic claim eligibility is deliberately unavailable until a resident process classifier can supply pipeline, interactive-agent, and checkout-process facts. - Adds test coverage for the registry, lease, remote protocol, installer, controller, and backend selection, plus an opt-in live smoke (`tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh`) whose ambient-Herdr tripwire tolerates spinner-frame title drift but refuses pane `revision` advance; documents the backend and its safety boundary in `docs/devenv-backend.md`, records the live one-VM round trip in `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md`, and adds the agent-only `devenv-orchestration` skill. Also included: `fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` now uses system `stat` on Darwin, and `bin/fm-brief.sh` shell parsing is restored for stock macOS bash 3.2. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Both round-2 findings are fixed durably rather than symptomatically - the post-claim dequeue now has no bounded-timeout lock acquisition past the point of no ambiguous failure, pinned by a deterministic regression that runs under a zero lock timeout - leaving only a two-line silent-diagnostic gap in the enqueue argument layer on an opt-in, non-spawn backend that still cannot select any environment. ## Testing Ran the devenv smoke suite through its documented runner (9 checks, exit 0, live path skipped without opt-in) and then verified its three behavioural claims against real Herdr bytes rather than fixtures alone: 40 live ambient snapshots showed 8 spinner-only transitions that all collapse to identical under the shipped normalizer with revision untouched; real `Action Required` blink bytes remain refused, and a counterfactual re-applying the deleted marker rule leaves only the pane-revision advance, confirming revision is the refusal reason the docs now state; and the real before/after comparison over a 25 s window correctly aborted while the ambient agent was producing output, matching the tightened prerequisite. The removed marker normalization left no dead fixture kinds or references, the worktree is clean, and the VM-shipped runtime payload is byte-identical to the commit whose live one-VM lease round trip is already recorded, so that run was not repeated. No failures and no flakiness observed.

Everything below was produced against real `herdr --session default api snapshot` bytes using `fm_devenv_smoke_normalize_snapshot` extracted verbatim from `tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh` (see `normalizer.sh`). | file | what it shows | | --- | --- | | `fm-test-run-smoke.log` | `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh` — 9 checks, exit 0 | | `ambient-stability.log` | 40 live snapshots, 0.35 s apart: 8 raw transitions differ, **0** differ after normalization | | `spinner-real-bytes.log` | one of those transitions in full: only `⠴`→`⠦` in the two title fields, `panes[].revision` and `agents[].revision` unchanged at 4649 | | `action-required-real-bytes.log` | real bytes straddling an `Action Required` blink: refused at HEAD, and refused even with the removed marker rule re-applied — the surviving delta is the `revision` 4207→4208 advance | | `live-ambient-tripwire.log` | the tripwire run over a real 25 s window while the ambient Codex agent was **producing output**: correctly aborts on `revision` 4686→4696 and scrollback growth, which is the case the documented prerequisite excludes | | `raw/snap-01..40.json` | the raw live snapshots behind `ambient-stability.log` | Read together: the one tolerated animation is real and revision-free, the Action-Required blink is refused because of the revision advance rather than the marker, and active output is still refused. ```
