✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ⚠️ `bin/fm-devenv-controller.sh:532` - `make -C "$checkout" devenv-start "NAME=$environment"` runs with stdout inherited inside `fm_devenv_claim_environment`, which is a subshell whose entire stdout is captured by `claim_result=$(fm_devenv_claim_environment ...)` at line 620 and then re-emitted by `printf '%s\n' "$claim_result"` at line 625. Every line make prints (recipe echo, orb/docker progress) is prepended to the `{"claimed":true,...}` object, so the documented machine-readable `claim` output stops being parseable on the stopped-VM path. The controller test's `make()` fake (tests/fm-devenv-controller.test.sh:271) appends to `$START_LOG` rather than stdout, so `test_claim_reinspects_under_lock_and_publishes_matching_state` passes despite the defect. Redirect to stderr (`>&2`) or `/dev/null`; keep the log-capable stream so start failures stay diagnosable. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-devenv-remote.sh:155` - `agent_present` and `herdr_session_present` are both assigned the same `$session_present` variable, which is derived solely from whether a Herdr session literally named `firstmate-expanly-<environment>` is running. When herdr exists on the VM but that one session is absent, the remote reports `agent_present:false` - a definite "no agent is working here" - even though a human or agent can be active in the `default` or any other session. `fm_devenv_select` (bin/fm-devenv-controller.sh:168) treats that `false` as a satisfied safety precondition. This contradicts the intent's "fail closed on ambiguous registry, checkout, process, lease, or session state" and "every VM remains directly accessible in Herdr for debugging or intervention": the intervention session is exactly the one this probe cannot see. It is currently masked because `pipeline_active`/`unknown_checkout_process` are hardcoded null, so no environment is eligible - but this field becomes load-bearing the moment the resident classifier lands. Either publish `null` until the classifier can prove agent absence across all sessions, or rename the field to what it actually measures. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-devenv-controller.sh:602` - `fm_devenv_claim_next` takes `$FM_DEVENV_QUEUE_LOCK` before selection and holds it through `fm_devenv_claim_environment`, which can run `make devenv-start` plus up to `FM_DEVENV_START_ATTEMPTS` (12) x `FM_DEVENV_START_INTERVAL` (5s) = 60s of polling. `fm_devenv_enqueue_json` needs the same lock and gives up after `FM_DEVENV_LEASE_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (default 5s). Concretely: a claim boots a stopped VM; 10 seconds later the agent follows the devenv-orchestration skill and runs `fm-devenv-controller.sh enqueue fm-next /path/packet.md`; the lock acquire times out and enqueue exits 1 with no output, so the task is silently not queued and the agent cannot tell a lock timeout from a duplicate task id. Serializing claims is correct (and tested), but enqueue does not need to wait behind a VM boot - either shorten the critical section to selection + queue mutation, or raise the enqueue lock timeout above the worst-case start budget. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-devenv-controller.sh:34` - `fm_devenv_controller_error` is defined but never called anywhere in bin/ or tests/. Every controller failure path - unreadable queue, lock timeout, duplicate task id, task-not-queue-head, invalid registry, remote claim refusal - is a bare `return 1` with nothing on stderr. `fm-devenv-lib.sh` and `fm-devenv-remote.sh` both emit reasons; the controller, which is the surface the devenv-orchestration skill drives, emits none. Failure scenario: `fm-devenv-controller.sh enqueue fm-a /path/a.md` exits 1 with empty stdout and stderr, and the operator cannot distinguish "task id already queued" (do not retry) from "queue lock busy" (retry) from "queue.json is corrupt" (repair). Wire the existing helper into the enqueue/claim/release failure returns. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh:370` - The live path ends with `pass "devenv smoke: live lease $live_token survived ..."`, printing the real 64-hex generation token into test output and any CI log that retains it. docs/verification/runtime-backends.md records the same line as `live lease [generation token redacted]`, i.e. the maintainer redacted it by hand when writing the evidence. The token is already released by that point so the exposure is not exploitable, but emitting it is avoidable and the test should produce the form the verification doc pins. Failure scenario: the smoke is run under a CI job or a shared Herdr pane that persists stdout, and a live-at-the-time lease token is written to a retained log. Replace with a redacted marker (or the first 8 characters) so the emitted line matches the recorded evidence. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:280` - `FIRSTMATE_POSSESSIVE="firstmate's"` exists only to keep the apostrophe out of the `DOD=$(cat <<EOF ... EOF)` heredoc, because stock macOS bash 3.2.57 mis-parses an unbalanced single quote inside a heredoc inside command substitution (confirmed locally: `/bin/bash -n` on a minimal reproduction fails with "unexpected EOF while looking for matching `'"). The variable carries no comment saying so, and the surrounding file documents every other non-obvious construct. Failure scenario: a later reader inlines the literal back into the heredoc as an obvious simplification, and `bin/fm-brief.sh` stops parsing under /bin/bash on macOS - a shell the repo explicitly supports via the `macos-stock-bash` CI job. Add a one-line comment naming the bash 3.2 limitation. 🔧 Fix: fix(devenv): split claim lock and surface controller errors 3 issues (1 warning, 2 infos) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-devenv-controller.sh:672` - The lock split moved the post-claim dequeue out of the held critical section: `fm_devenv_claim_next` now calls `fm_devenv_queue_remove` (line 672), which re-acquires `queue.lock` through `fm_devenv_lease_lock_acquire` with the default `FM_DEVENV_LEASE_LOCK_TIMEOUT` of 5s. That acquire can now fail, and its failure branch is the same one written for a genuinely corrupt queue: `fm_devenv_task_recovery "$task_id" queue_removal_failed_after_claim` fences the task as `recovery_required`, and the function returns 1 while the Mac lease at `environments/<env>.json` and the remote lease both remain live. Failure scenario: a claim completes its remote claim and Mac publication; in the same window another process is running back-to-back `enqueue` calls, so `fm_devenv_queue_remove` loses the 0.1s retry race for the full 5s budget; the claim reports "alpha is claimed but fm-a could not be dequeued", the task fence flips to recovery_required, and every retry is then refused by `fm_devenv_task_has_local_fence` (line 655) until a human deletes the fence and releases the orphaned lease. Before this commit the lock was already held at that point, so transient contention could not reach this path at all. Give the post-claim dequeue a bounded retry, or a longer timeout than a plain enqueue, so only a real queue fault - not lock contention - poisons a claim that already succeeded remotely. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-devenv-controller.sh:88` - `fm_devenv_queue_json` still returns 1 with nothing on stderr, and it is the only failure source for the two read-only commands: `queue` (line 808) and `status --json` (line 826, via `fm_devenv_status_json`). Every mutating path now diagnoses the same condition - enqueue prints "queue is unreadable or invalid; repair <path>" - and docs/devenv-backend.md documents the guarantee only for enqueue/claim/release, so this is a scoped gap rather than an over-claim. Failure scenario: `state/devenv/queue.json` is truncated; the devenv-orchestration skill translates "status" into `fm-devenv-controller.sh status --json`, which exits 1 printing nothing at all, while the registry path in the same command would have printed `fm-devenv-registry: invalid JSON`. The diagnostic surface an operator reaches first is the one that says least. Route the `queue` and `status` failures through `fm_devenv_controller_error` too. - ℹ️ `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md:32` - The maintained live evidence is a run against FirstMate commit 5c83c947 whose recorded assertion was that "both remote agent indicators remained false". This commit changes `agent_present` to null and updates `fm_devenv_smoke_assert_clean_inspect`/`fm_devenv_smoke_assert_lease` to require `.agent_present == null`, so that recorded run would not reproduce against the current test. The doc discloses exactly this in the added sentence at line 32, which is honest containment rather than a stale claim, and re-running requires a real clean feature VM that this review phase cannot exercise. Noting it so the maintainer can decide whether to re-run the opt-in smoke and refresh the version-scoped record before merge; no source defect follows from it. 🔧 Fix: fix(devenv): wait out queue-lock contention after a claim 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-devenv-controller.sh:809` - This commit broadened docs/devenv-backend.md line 74 from "Every `enqueue`, `claim`, and `release` failure prints one `fm-devenv-controller:` reason on standard error" to "Every command failure prints one ... reason", and closed the gap for `queue`, `inspect`, and `status --json`. Two bare returns remain in the `enqueue` argument-marshalling layer and are now the only silent failures left in the dispatcher: `case "$priority" in ''|*[!0-9-]*) return 1 ;; esac`, and the `task=$(jq -cn ...) || return 1` immediately below it. Failure scenario: an operator or the devenv-orchestration skill runs `fm-devenv-controller.sh enqueue fm-next /path/packet.md high` (or `1.5`, or any non-integer priority); the command exits 1 with nothing on stdout and nothing on stderr, so the caller cannot tell a malformed priority from a duplicate task id - the exact confusion the round-1 finding and the current doc sentence both promise is gone. Wrap both in `fm_devenv_controller_error` the same way the sibling paths in this function now are.
🔧 **Test** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed (3) ✅ - ⚠️ `tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh:197` - tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh cannot pass against a live ambient Herdr session. It snapshots `HERDR_SESSION` (default: `default`) before and after the lease round trip and requires byte equality. On this machine the operator's real `default` session snapshot changes on its own every ~2s because a running agent's `terminal_title` carries an animated spinner glyph (verified independently: two `herdr --session default api snapshot` calls 2s apart with zero control-plane activity differed only in `"terminal_title": "⠴ expanly-platform"` vs `"⠦ expanly-platform"`). The first live run failed with `ambient Herdr session changed during the lease round trip: default`. I obtained the passing run by pointing `HERDR_SESSION` at a second quiet dedicated session, and separately proved the real `default` session was unchanged across the round trip after normalising the leading spinner glyph. The author needs to decide whether the ambient tripwire should tolerate volatile title fields or whether the documented prerequisite should state that the ambient session must be idle. - ⚠️ `tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh:1928` - tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh failed once during a four-script batch run (`bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-devenv-controller.test.sh tests/fm-backend.test.sh tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` reported `family=snapshot-bearings ... failed=1`), then passed on five consecutive subsequent runs: the identical batch twice more and three standalone runs, each emitting 43 `ok -` lines and exit 0. I did not capture the failing assertion text before it scrolled, and could not reproduce it, so I cannot attribute it to a specific case. Flagging it because this file is newly gated at exactly 43 tests in CI, so an intermittent failure here would block the required lane. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-devenv-registry.test.sh tests/fm-devenv-lease.test.sh tests/fm-devenv-remote.test.sh tests/fm-devenv-install.test.sh tests/fm-backend-devenv.test.sh` — 5 scripts, 0 failures - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-devenv-controller.test.sh tests/fm-backend.test.sh tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` — run 3 times; 1 intermittent bearings failure on the first run, 0 failures on the other two - `/bin/bash tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh` — 3 standalone repeats, 43 `ok -` lines and exit 0 each - `FM_DEVENV_SMOKE_ENV=feature-dev FM_DEVENV_SMOKE_SESSION=fm-devenv-protocol-lab HERDR_SESSION=fm-devenv-ambient-lab bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh` — live one-VM lease round trip, 7 assertions, exit 0 - Manual: `bin/fm-devenv-install.sh --verify feature-dev` (mismatch reported) → `bin/fm-devenv-install.sh feature-dev` → `--verify` again (pinned at be77697) - Manual: `bin/fm-devenv-controller.sh inspect` against the real `~/.expanly-devenvs.json` — six environments enumerated - Manual: `bin/fm-devenv-controller.sh enqueue demo-control-plane <packet> 5 ...` → `queue` → `claim demo-control-plane feat/demo-control-plane` (exit 3, `no_safe_capacity`) → `queue` again (unchanged) → `status --json` - Manual: sourced `bin/fm-backend.sh` and ran `FM_BACKEND=devenv fm_backend_name`, `fm_backend_name`, `fm_backend_required_tools devenv`, `fm_backend_validate_spawn devenv` - Manual: `ssh expanly-feature-dev 'herdr session list'` — VM's own `default` session running, `firstmate-expanly-feature-dev` absent - Manual: `herdr --session default api snapshot` twice 2s apart with no control-plane activity, to isolate the ambient-tripwire failure cause - Manual: spinner-normalised `default` Herdr session snapshot compared immediately before and after the live round trip — identical 🔧 Fix: tolerate spinner-frame drift in devenv smoke ambient tripwire 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh:51` - The new normalizer only strips braille spinner frames (`⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏`), but this machine's ambient `default` Herdr session carries a second animated title prefix that it does not strip. Polling `herdr --session default api snapshot` every 1.5s for 12s with zero control-plane activity showed the same pane's `terminal_title` and `terminal_title_stripped` alternating between `[ ! ] Action Required | expanly-platform` and `[ . ] Action Required | expanly-platform`. Feeding those two real snapshots through the shipped `fm_devenv_smoke_normalize_snapshot` (loaded verbatim from the test file) leaves them different, so the live smoke would still abort with `ambient Herdr session changed during the lease round trip: default` (evidence: ambient-blink-proof.log). The `⠴`/`⠦` case from round 1 is genuinely fixed — that is confirmed against real snapshot bytes. The judgement call is scope: the blink appears while an agent is *waiting for input*, which a reader could reasonably consider covered by the new "requires the ambient session to be otherwise idle" prerequisite in docs/devenv-backend.md, since that sentence only explains `revision` advancing under active output. The author should decide whether to extend the normalized prefix set to the Action-Required blink or to tighten the documented prerequisite to say no agent may be signalling Action Required either. - ℹ️ `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md:33` - The recorded live one-VM lease round trip ran at commit be77697, and `expanly-feature-dev` still has that commit's runtime installed (`bin/fm-devenv-install.sh --verify feature-dev` reports the mismatch against b657ea0). I did not re-run it at HEAD, because re-running requires installing a new runtime release onto a live VM and starting the stopped dedicated `fm-devenv-protocol-lab` Herdr session, both of which are writes outside this worktree. That gap is inert rather than risky: the installer ships only `AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md bin .agents/skills .claude/skills skills`, and `git diff --name-only be77697 b657ea0` over exactly those paths is empty — the final commit changes only docs/ and tests/, so the remote runtime bytes are unchanged (evidence: runtime-payload-unchanged.log). The one behavioural delta, the ambient tripwire comparison, I exercised directly against real `herdr api snapshot` bytes instead. - `bash tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh` — 8 deterministic checks pass, including the two new regressions `test_fake_spinner_only_title_drift_is_accepted` and `test_fake_substantive_title_drift_is_refused` - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh tests/fm-backend-devenv.test.sh tests/fm-devenv-controller.test.sh tests/fm-devenv-remote.test.sh tests/fm-devenv-lease.test.sh tests/fm-devenv-registry.test.sh tests/fm-devenv-install.test.sh` — `FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=7 failed=0 skipped_gate=0` - Loaded the shipped `fm_devenv_smoke_normalize_snapshot` verbatim out of the test file and ran it over real `herdr --session default api snapshot` output: braille spinner frame advance `⠴`→`⠦` normalizes to identical; a substantive `terminal_title` change and a pane `revision` advance both still differ (normalizer-proof.sh / .log) - Captured two real ambient `default` snapshots 2s apart with zero control-plane activity to reproduce self-drift (`herdr --session default api snapshot`, ambient-raw-1.json / ambient-raw-2.json) - Polled `herdr --session default api snapshot` every 1.5s for 12s and extracted every `terminal_title` / `terminal_title_stripped` field, observing the `[ . ]` ↔ `[ ! ]` Action-Required blink and `revision` 3884→3886 under active agent output, then steady at 3926 once quiesced - `FM_BACKEND=devenv bin/fm-devenv-controller.sh inspect` against the operator's real `~/.expanly-devenvs.json` — six environments enumerated, `main` synthesized with no base privilege, `agent_present` published as null - Live end-to-end controller transcript with an isolated `FM_DEVENV_STATE_ROOT`: `enqueue demo-task` → `queue` → `claim demo-task feature/demo-branch` (exit 3, `no_safe_capacity`, task stays queued) → `status --json` - `bin/fm-devenv-install.sh --verify feature-dev` — reports the pinned-runtime mismatch against HEAD without installing or repairing - `git diff --name-only be77697 b657ea0 -- AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md bin .agents/skills .claude/skills skills` — empty, confirming the VM-shipped runtime payload is unchanged since the recorded live round trip - `git status --porcelain` — worktree clean, no transient artifacts left behind (all test state written under the evidence directory) 🔧 Fix: tolerate Action-Required marker blink in devenv smoke tripwire 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `docs/devenv-backend.md:86` - The title normalization is confirmed correct on real bytes, but it does not make the live smoke pass, because the same blink also advances `panes[].revision`. I loaded `fm_devenv_smoke_normalize_snapshot` verbatim from the shipped test file and applied it to 16 real `herdr --session default api snapshot` captures: the `[ . ]`/`[ ! ]` flip is fully collapsed in `terminal_title` and `terminal_title_stripped` on both the `panes[]` and `agents[]` records (evidence: round3/normalizer-real-bytes.log). A separate 40-sample trace at 0.35s shows the blink and the revision counter move in exact lockstep — `revision_advances=18 marker_flips=18 revision_without_flip=0 flip_without_revision=0` (evidence: round3/blink-vs-revision.tsv). The blinking record is `agents[1]`, a Codex agent with `agent_status: "blocked"`, i.e. precisely the "waiting on input" case the new prose says the ambient session may hold. Running the real comparison the round trip performs against the live ambient `default` session still aborts, with only the revision fields left differing (evidence: round3/live-tripwire-verdict.log). Control: the session has 8 panes, 2 agents, 5 workspaces and 5 tabs, and across 20s only that one record ever changed, so the tripwire itself is precise. The new deterministic tests cannot catch this because the `marker` fake fixture blinks the title while holding `revision` at 1, whereas real Herdr bumps it on every blink. This is a judgement call for the author, not something to auto-fix: the only way to make a blinking Action-Required agent tolerable is to also normalize `revision`, which the round-2 instruction explicitly forbids as weakening a structural tripwire. The alternative is to tighten docs/devenv-backend.md back to stating that no agent may be signalling Action Required in the ambient session, and to adjust the runtime-backends.md wording that presents the surviving revision advance as merely incidental. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh` — all 11 fake checks pass, including the three new Action-Required marker cases; live path gate-skips without opt-in - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh tests/fm-backend-devenv.test.sh tests/fm-devenv-controller.test.sh tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` — 4 scripts, 0 failures - Extracted `fm_devenv_smoke_normalize_snapshot` verbatim from `tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh` and applied it to 16 real `herdr --session default api snapshot` captures taken ~1.2s apart, diffing raw vs normalized at JSON leaf-path level - 40-sample live trace at 0.35s correlating `panes[7].revision` against `terminal_title` to test whether the marker blink is itself a repaint - Reproduced the round trip's actual ambient check end-to-end against the live `default` session: `fm_devenv_smoke_normalize_snapshot` before, an 8s wait, normalize after, byte-compare - Inspected the blinking record via `herdr --session default api snapshot | jq '.result.snapshot.agents[1]'` to confirm `agent_status: "blocked"` - Confirmed `git status --porcelain` is clean; no transient files left in the worktree 🔧 Fix: drop Action-Required marker normalization; refuse revision advance ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh` — 9 checks, exit 0, live path correctly skipped without opt-in env vars - `bash tests/fm-backend-devenv-smoke.test.sh` directly, covering `test_fake_spinner_only_title_drift_is_accepted`, the new `test_fake_action_required_blink_is_refused`, `test_fake_substantive_title_drift_is_refused`, and `test_fake_snapshot_mutation_is_refused` - Extracted `fm_devenv_smoke_normalize_snapshot` verbatim from the shipped test file and applied it to 40 real `herdr --session default api snapshot` captures taken 0.35 s apart: 8 raw transitions differed, 0 differed after normalization - Field-level diff of one real spinner transition showing only `terminal_title`/`terminal_title_stripped` changing `⠴`→`⠦` while `panes[].revision` and `agents[].revision` stayed at 4649 - Applied the HEAD normalizer to real bytes straddling an `Action Required` `[ . ]`/`[ ! ]` blink: still refused; re-applying the removed marker rule as a counterfactual left only the `revision` 4207→4208 advance - Ran the exact before/after ambient comparison `fm_devenv_smoke_round_trip` performs, over a real 25 s window against the live `default` session while its Codex agent was producing output — correctly aborted on `revision` 4686→4696 - `git diff --name-only be77697 HEAD -- AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md bin .agents/skills .claude/skills skills` — empty, so the VM-shipped runtime is unchanged since the recorded live round trip - `grep -rn 'unblink|MUTATE_KIND=marker|MUTATE_KIND=cleared|MUTATE_KIND=status|Action Blocked' tests/ bin/ docs/` — no leftovers; `bash -n` parses; `git status --porcelain` clean
⚠️ **Document** - 1 info - ℹ️ `AGENTS.md:471` - Judgment call, left unchanged: the new agent-only skill `devenv-orchestration` is not listed in AGENTS.md section 13's register of agent-only reference skills, unlike every other internal skill. I deliberately did not add it, because the change already places its precise load trigger in section 4 ("When the resolved backend is `devenv`, load `devenv-orchestration`..."), and a section 13 entry would duplicate that same trigger inside the always-loaded instruction file for a niche backend. If the project treats section 13 as a strictly complete register rather than a trigger index, add a one-line entry there and reduce the section 4 line to a pointer, so the trigger still has exactly one owner.

title: fix: propagate project yolo to delegated Pi sessions
body:
## Intent Honor FirstMate project +yolo for delegated Pi ship and scout sessions by propagating a process-scoped PI_PERMISSION_SYSTEM_YOLO=1 launch override into a compatible @gotgenes/pi-permission-system. The override must convert only ask decisions to allow, preserve explicit deny rules, survive config refresh without being persisted, and appear in effective status. Keep ordinary permission handling unchanged for yolo-off projects, non-Pi harnesses, secondmates, standalone Pi sessions, and all global configuration. Document the compatibility boundary and retain fail-safe behavior with older or absent permission-system packages. ## What Changed - Propagate process-scoped `PI_PERMISSION_SYSTEM_YOLO=1` to delegated Pi ship and scout launches for `+yolo` projects, while leaving yolo-off, non-Pi, and secondmate launches unchanged. - Document the compatible permission-system commit, deny-preserving and non-persisted behavior, and fail-safe handling for older or absent packages. - Add dispatch-profile regression coverage for eligible and excluded launch contexts; the focused and broader spawn suites passed in the pipeline. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the change is narrowly scoped, excluded launch contexts remain unchanged, and the external contract is now concretely pinned to [PR #671](https://github.com/gotgenes/pi-packages/pull/671) at commit `79829ffd`, with older or absent packages failing safely. ## Testing No baseline results were supplied; focused and related Firstmate runtime tests, generated launch evidence, pinned-package focused and full tests, direct permission lifecycle evidence, and an older-package fail-safe smoke check all passed. One initial full-suite attempt failed only because the temporary evidence test lacked its evidence-directory variable; it was removed and the untouched 2,685-test package suite passed on retry.

🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `docs/configuration.md:207` - The required compatibility boundary is not actually identifiable: this line defines it as whichever future release documents the variable, while the [latest v24.0.0 configuration reference](https://github.com/gotgenes/pi-packages/blob/pi-permission-system-v24.0.0/packages/pi-permission-system/docs/configuration.md) contains no `PI_PERMISSION_SYSTEM_YOLO` contract. title: feat(bin): garbage-collect a torn-down worktree's Xcode DerivedData
body:
## Intent Captain's request: make Xcode DerivedData cleanup permanent - every time a firstmate ship/scout worktree is torn down after landed work, also remove the DerivedData folder that belonged to that worktree, so orphaned DerivedData stops accumulating. Deliberate design decisions already made and accepted on this branch: - bin/fm-derived-data-gc.sh is the single owner of DerivedData GC, with two modes. --worktree is the teardown path and matches ONLY on info.plist WorkspacePath equal to or under the removed worktree; it never touches no-plist dirs. --orphans removes dirs whose WorkspacePath no longer exists, and only with the explicit --include-no-plist flag plus a mandatory age gate (default 48h) will it remove dirs with no usable info.plist. - Hard safety rules come from prior field incidents and are intentional: never delete *.noindex shared caches (ModuleCache, CompilationCache, SDKStatCaches, SymbolCache); never delete a dir whose WorkspacePath still resolves to an existing path, in either mode; never delete a no-plist dir without the age gate. Missing plutil or a missing DerivedData root is a deliberate quiet exit-0 no-op (fail safe, delete nothing). - fm-teardown.sh calls the helper after the worktree is safely removable. GC failure is deliberately only a warning and must never fail teardown of landed work. - Out of scope by the captain's instruction: CoreSimulator deletion, Docker/colima prune, and force-deleting no-plist dirs without an age gate. - FM_DERIVED_DATA_ROOT exists so tests can point at a fixture root. What this round adds, and why: The repo's automated reviewer left an unanswered P2 on bin/fm-derived-data-gc.sh: dir_mtime chained 'stat -f %m' into a 'stat -c %Y' fallback with ||. GNU coreutils stat has no BSD-style '-f ' - it reads -f as 'print filesystem status' and treats %m as a file operand, so it writes a multi-line filesystem summary for the real operand to STDOUT and still exits non-zero. The fallback epoch was appended to that summary, and the caller's age arithmetic then aborted the entire run under set -u with 'File: unbound variable', breaking --orphans --include-no-plist and the test suite on any host with that stat flavor. Deliberate choice: I validate each probe's output as a bare epoch rather than merely reordering the probes to put GNU stat first. Reordering fixes only this one stat pair; validation rejects ANY probe whose failure path writes to stdout, which is the actual class of defect. BSD order is kept first because DerivedData is macOS-only in practice, and the validation makes order irrelevant to correctness. The test was written failing-first: case (o) in tests/fm-derived-data-gc.test.sh was confirmed to fail on the unfixed helper ('expected exit 0, got 1') before the fix landed. It stubs a GNU-flavored stat on PATH so the regression is guarded on macOS too, not only where Linux CI happens to expose it - that PATH stub is intentional, not a test smell. The branch was also rebased onto current main (52 commits) this round; a git range-diff confirmed the three original commits replayed unchanged apart from one docs/scripts.md context line that main itself had edited. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-derived-data-gc.sh`, the single owner of Xcode DerivedData cleanup, with a teardown mode (`--worktree `, matching only on `info.plist` `WorkspacePath` equal to or under the removed worktree) and a manual `--orphans` sweep that needs an explicit `--include-no-plist` plus an age gate (default 48h) before touching plist-less dirs. It never removes `*.noindex` shared caches or a dir whose `WorkspacePath` still resolves, and quietly no-ops when `plutil` or the DerivedData root is missing. - `bin/fm-teardown.sh` now invokes that helper after the task worktree path is gone (skipping `kind=secondmate`); a GC failure only prints `warning: DerivedData GC failed ... (non-fatal)` and never fails teardown of landed work. - Hardened the helper's `dir_mtime` probe to validate each `stat` result as a bare epoch, so a GNU-flavored `stat` writing a filesystem summary to stdout no longer poisons the age arithmetic and abort the run under `set -u`; covered by a new `tests/fm-derived-data-gc.test.sh` suite (including a PATH-stubbed GNU `stat` regression case written failing-first), a teardown integration case, and a hermetic `FM_DERIVED_DATA_ROOT` fixture pinned in `tests/lib.sh`. Documented the helper and `FM_DERIVED_DATA_ROOT` in `docs/scripts.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, and `AGENTS.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: This round is test-only, applies both captain-approved fixes correctly, leaves the accepted deliverable (the dir_mtime validation and case (o)) and the deliberately deferred teardown guard untouched, and the two residuals are comment/dead-code nits with no behavioral effect. ## Testing I exercised the change at the product level rather than only through unit tests. The two targeted suites pass (`tests/fm-derived-data-gc.test.sh`, 10 cases; `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh`, 40 cases including the new DerivedData integration case). For the headline intent I wrote a driver that stands up a real git project and task worktree with landed work plus a realistic DerivedData root, then ran the shipped `bin/fm-teardown.sh`: the 4 MB DerivedData folder whose WorkspacePath pointed into the torn-down worktree was removed with an explicit `removed: …` line, while an unrelated live project's dir and the shared `ModuleCache.noindex`/`SymbolCache.noindex` caches survived. A second run with the DerivedData root made unwritable confirmed the deliberate fail-safe: teardown of landed work still exits 0 and only emits `warning: DerivedData GC failed … (non-fatal)`. For this round's fix I reproduced the original defect on the shipped CLI with a GNU-flavored `stat` on PATH (`line 224: File: unbound variable`, exit 1, nothing collected) and showed the same command succeeding after the fix, and I independently confirmed the author's failing-first claim by re-running the suite against the pre-fix helper, where only case (o) failed with exactly `expected exit 0, got 1`. The real `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData` was untouched throughout and the worktree is clean. No UI surface is involved — this is a shell/CLI change, so CLI transcripts are the end-user-visible artifact.

⚠️ **Review** - 2 infos - ⚠️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:1831` - The `[ ! -e "$WT" ]` guard makes the DerivedData GC a no-op for every treehouse-backed backend (tmux/herdr/zellij/cmux -- the default ship/scout path). `treehouse return --force` cleans and resets the pooled worktree but leaves its directory on disk; verified on this host, where `~/.treehouse/estimate-os-a2a014/treehouse-state.json` lists slots 1-3 with no `owner_pid` (returned/free) while `~/.treehouse/<pool>/<n>/<repo>` still exists, and treehouse's own removal verbs are `destroy` and `prune`, not `return`. Decision needed: accept the narrower teardown coverage and schedule `--orphans` somewhere to actually close the accumulation goal, or widen the teardown condition. - ⚠️ `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh:626` - The dd-gc integration test overrides the treehouse mock with one that `rm -rf`s the worktree, commented "as the real `treehouse return` does". The test is green but does not demonstrate that teardown collects DerivedData on the default backend. Retarget it at a backend whose worktree really disappears (Orca), or re-scope its stated claim. - ⚠️ `tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh:869` - `test_teardown_removes_orca_worktree_when_path_missing` sets `wt="$TMP_ROOT/missing-path-wt"` and never creates it, so teardown passes the new hook's `[ ! -e "$WT" ]` guard and invokes fm-derived-data-gc.sh with no `FM_DERIVED_DATA_ROOT`. The helper then defaults to `$HOME/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData` and runs `plutil -extract` over every entry in the developer's real DerivedData. No deletion is possible (matching is scoped to the temp worktree path) and Linux CI exits early on the missing root, but the macOS run is non-hermetic and scales with the real DerivedData size. Commit 42dd1e8 pinned a fixture root only in tests/fm-teardown.test.sh:497; the same pin belongs on the other teardown-invoking tests that can reach the hook. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-derived-data-gc.sh:178` - In `is_protected_cache`, `ModuleCache.noindex|CompilationCache.noindex|SDKStatCaches.noindex|SymbolCache.noindex` are fully subsumed by the trailing `*.noindex` alternative in the same pattern, so they are unreachable-as-distinct branches. Keeping the names as a comment above a bare `*.noindex)` case would preserve the field-incident documentation without reading as live matching logic. 🔧 Fix: pin hermetic DerivedData root suite-wide; re-scope teardown GC test 2 infos still open: - ℹ️ `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh:497` - Now that tests/lib.sh:47 exports a non-empty FM_DERIVED_DATA_ROOT for every sourcing suite, run_teardown's `${FM_DERIVED_DATA_ROOT:-$case_dir/derived-data-empty}` default is unreachable and the `$case_dir/derived-data-empty` directory created in make_case (line 75) is never read. Both roots are empty fixture roots so there is no behavioral difference, but the dead fallback reads as the live owner of the pinned root. Either drop the per-case root and its mkdir so tests/lib.sh is the single owner, or keep it and note in a comment that it is defense-in-depth only. - ℹ️ `tests/lib.sh:37` - The new comment says the pin keeps DerivedData GC hermetic "for every suite", but it only reaches suites that source tests/lib.sh. Four suites invoke bin/fm-teardown.sh without sourcing it: tests/fm-backend-autodetect-smoke.test.sh, tests/fm-backend-herdr-launcher-workspace-e2e.test.sh, tests/fm-backend-herdr-workspace-per-home-e2e.test.sh, and tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh. None can reach the GC today -- the first three drive real treehouse, whose `return` leaves the pooled worktree directory on disk so bin/fm-teardown.sh:1831's path-is-gone guard never fires, and the fourth is kind=secondmate, which that same guard excludes. Given this round's stated goal was removing an overstated scope claim from a comment, narrowing this one to "every suite that sources this library" (and naming why the non-sourcing teardown suites are safe) would keep it honest.

title: fix: suppress stale watcher wake prompts after drain
body:
## Intent Diagnose and fix delayed duplicate Firstmate wake prompts that arrive after durable queue events are drained and a task endpoint retires; reproduce safely in isolated state, cover Pi and every supported watcher path, preserve queue and watcher continuity, add regressions and documentation, and ship a green PR. ## What Changed - Reworked Pi and OpenCode watcher adapters to revalidate actionable wake delivery against the durable queue, defer while `.wake-queue.lock` is held, suppress already-drained events, and coalesce later closes behind one outstanding handling turn. - Hardened wake prompt latches so failed sends preserve pending reasons, OpenCode session-end events release the matching latch, and successor watcher restoration still happens before delivery. - Expanded regression coverage and watcher-continuity docs for drain-lock windows, retired-endpoint suppression, Pi/OpenCode coalescing, and verified TUI behavior. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The prior lock-window issue has been addressed with bounded lock-aware revalidation in both watcher adapters, with matching regression coverage and updated verification docs, and I found no remaining source-verifiable blocker in the changed surface. ## Testing Inspected the touched watcher and documentation surfaces, ran focused Pi/OpenCode watcher regressions including the native Pi E2E path, generated product-level transcripts for the durable queue/drain/retired-endpoint behavior, and confirmed the working tree remained clean.
Evidence: Pi wake coalescing transcript ```text Pi watcher evidence: coalesced durable wakes, real drain, retired stale endpoint, and new post-drain event Pi prompt 1: FIRSTMATE_OP watcher follow-up: FIRSTMATE WATCHER WAKE: signal: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYJ5FCT6JMFXPEP50DR947SM/pi-wake-coalescing-fixture/home/state/task.status | Run bin/fm-wake-drain.sh first and handle the queued wake. Watcher continuity is extension-owned. after initial signal close: prompts=1; arms=2; queue_rows=1 after stale close before drain: prompts=1; arms=3; queue_rows=2 during real drain lock after endpoint retirement: prompts=1; arms=3; queue_rows=0 real drain rows consumed=2: signal:task.status:signal: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYJ5FCT6JMFXPEP50DR947SM/pi-wake-coalescing-fixture/home/state/task.status || stale:default:w6:p2:stale: default:w6:p2 after drain committed with retired stale endpoint: prompts=1; arms=3; queue_rows=0 Pi prompt 2: FIRSTMATE_OP watcher follow-up: FIRSTMATE WATCHER WAKE: signal: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYJ5FCT6JMFXPEP50DR947SM/pi-wake-coalescing-fixture/home/state/new.status | Run bin/fm-wake-drain.sh first and handle the queued wake. Watcher continuity is extension-owned. after new post-drain signal: prompts=2; arms=4; queue_rows=1 final arm log: arm=3187575 | arm=3187628 | arm=3187685 | arm=3187895 ```
Evidence: OpenCode wake coalescing transcript ```text OpenCode watcher evidence: coalesced durable wakes, real drain, retired stale endpoint, and new post-drain event OpenCode prompt 1 to session-test: ⁣FIRSTMATE_OP: v1 watcher: WATCHER FIRED - drain queued wakes with bin/fm-wake-drain.sh and handle the reported wake. Watcher continuity is plugin-owned. | signal: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYJ5FCT6JMFXPEP50DR947SM/opencode-wake-coalescing-fixture/home/state/task.status after initial signal close: prompts=1; arms=2; queue_rows=1 after stale close before drain: prompts=1; arms=3; queue_rows=2 during real drain lock after endpoint retirement: prompts=1; arms=3; queue_rows=0 real drain rows consumed=2: signal:task.status:signal: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYJ5FCT6JMFXPEP50DR947SM/opencode-wake-coalescing-fixture/home/state/task.status || stale:default:w6:p2:stale: default:w6:p2 after drain committed with retired stale endpoint: prompts=1; arms=3; queue_rows=0 OpenCode prompt 2 to session-test: ⁣FIRSTMATE_OP: v1 watcher: WATCHER FIRED - drain queued wakes with bin/fm-wake-drain.sh and handle the reported wake. Watcher continuity is plugin-owned. | signal: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYJ5FCT6JMFXPEP50DR947SM/opencode-wake-coalescing-fixture/home/state/new.status after new post-drain signal: prompts=2; arms=4; queue_rows=1 final arm log: arm=3189022 | arm=3189077 | arm=3189136 | arm=3189355 ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `.opencode/plugins/fm-primary-watch-arm.js:205` - The required intent says to "fix delayed duplicate Firstmate wake prompts that arrive after durable queue events are drained and a task endpoint retires", but this hunk still treats an active `.wake-queue.lock` as deliverable (`if (existsSync(lock)) return { state: "unknown"...`) and `flushWakePrompt` only suppresses `empty`. During `fm-wake-drain.sh`, the lock is held after the queue is moved/truncated and before release; if restoration or a coalesced wake flushes in that window, the adapter can still send stale child output after the drain consumed the record and the endpoint retired. Pi has the same pattern at `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:204`. Defer/retry queue revalidation until the wake-queue lock clears, or use a shared lock-aware snapshot helper, then suppress on empty. - ⚠️ `docs/verification/supervision.md:125` - The branch changes the OpenCode watcher adapter, but the new verification record says the new OpenCode behavior was exercised only "at the plugin boundary". That does not satisfy the repo standard that harness adapter changes must be empirically verified against the real harness, nor the intent to cover every supported watcher path. Add/record a real OpenCode TUI verification for the new coalescing/latch behavior with date, version, command, and observed output. 🔧 Fix: Defer wake prompts during queue locks ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: feat(bin): give each project its own leased worktree pool on the repo's filesystem
body:
## Intent PR #1142 (per-project worktree pools): fix the two Behavior-tests-Herdr CI failures — post-create abort fixture updated for leased acquisition, and the projected-teardown focus regression root-caused (treehouse return --force killed the pane's shell before the presentation restore block) and fixed by closing the presentation pane before returning the worktree; 22/22 presentation e2e x3 + 132/132 backend suite green locally. Goal: green Herdr CI lane + the Require-no-mistakes signature on PR #1142. ## What Changed - Spawn now acquires crew worktrees through `treehouse get --lease` from a per-project pool placed on the repo's own filesystem. The new `bin/fm-treehouse-lib.sh` selects the pool by running treehouse under a per-command `HOME` and verifies the acquired worktree is colocated with the object store, preventing the cross-filesystem split that made `no-mistakes init`/`axi run` hang inside git's gitfile open. - Teardown and the spawn-abort cleanup path now close the Herdr presentation pane before returning the leased worktree (previously `treehouse return --force` killed the pane's shell first, letting Herdr's last-pane cleanup destroy the workspace and steal focus), and lease failures now surface treehouse's stderr instead of a generic error. title: feat(decide): add /decide skill and local decide page for batch captain decisions

## Intenção Adicionar skill /decide e script fm-decide-page.sh para coletar decisões pendentes do capitão em lote via página local. Objetivo: o capitão hoje recebe decisões pendentes em prosa no chat, uma a uma. A entrega cria uma superfície descartável: uma página local onde ele lê todas as decisões abertas de uma vez com evidência e recomendação, escolhe, e as escolhas voltam sozinhas ao firstmate sem copiar e colar. Entregues: - bin/fm-decide-page.sh: valida o JSON de entrada (esquema estrito, recusa inválido), inicia servidor HTTP em 127.0.0.1 com porta efêmera e segredo de uso único por execução, registra state/decide.check.sh no mecanismo de vigia já existente (fm-check-register.sh), grava state/decide-/responses/.json por decisão e marker ready, encerra sozinho após envio ou timeout. - .agents/skills/decide/SKILL.md: skill invocável pelo capitão (/decide), descreve o procedimento completo - inventário, geração da página, tratamento do wake, roteamento de cada escolha ao seu destino real. - docs/decide-page.md: esquema de entrada, formato de saída, integração com o vigia, propriedades de segurança (operador-atual). - AGENTS.md: exatamente uma linha de gatilho na seção 9. - docs/scripts.md, docs/documentation-audiences.json: inventário atualizado. - tests/fm-decide-page.test.sh: 29 testes cobrindo validação de entrada inválida, rejeição sem segredo (403), rejeição de chave desconhecida (400), gravação legível de submissão válida, e check imprimindo linha só quando há resposta nova - todos passam. Decisões de design: servidor Python embutido no script shell via heredoc; porta efêmera (OS-assigned); segredo token_urlsafe(32) por execução; submissão em lote única (todas as decisões de uma vez); check.sh estável (mesmos bytes a cada invocação, re-registro idempotente); marker processed evita re-disparo do vigia na mesma run. ## O que mudou - Novo `bin/fm-decide-page.sh`: valida o JSON de decisões com esquema estrito, sobe um servidor HTTP em `127.0.0.1` com porta efêmera e segredo de uso único por execução, grava `state/decide-/responses/.json` mais o marker `ready`, e encerra sozinho após o envio ou no timeout. O endurecimento aplicado na revisão inclui `ThreadingHTTPServer` com timeout de handler, segredo fora de `argv` (visível em `ps`), validação de `Host` e de `Content-Length`, `umask 077` no diretório de estado, recusa de `--timeout 0` e escrita atômica do `state/decide.check.sh` registrado no vigia (`fm-check-register.sh`). - Nova skill `/decide` (`.agents/skills/decide/SKILL.md`) com o procedimento completo — inventário via `tasks-axi list --kind captain --state held`, geração da página, tratamento do wake e roteamento de cada escolha ao destino real — mais uma única linha de gatilho na seção 9 de `AGENTS.md`. - Documentação e inventário: `docs/decide-page.md` (esquema de entrada, formato de saída, integração com o vigia e propriedades de segurança, agora descrevendo `__secret` como token anti-CSRF servido junto à página), `docs/scripts.md` e `docs/documentation-audiences.json`. - `tests/fm-decide-page.test.sh` com 29 testes cobrindo recusa de JSON inválido, 403 sem segredo, 400 para chave desconhecida, gravação legível da submissão válida e o check imprimindo linha apenas quando há resposta nova. ## Avaliação de risco ✅ Baixo: O commit de correção resolve corretamente todos os 11 achados aceitos, sem regressão verificável — as mudanças são localizadas, seguem convenções já existentes no repo (mktemp+mv em `$STATE`, `umask 077`) e mantêm o contrato validado pelos testes existentes; a entrega segue puramente aditiva e conforme ao intent. ## Testes Rodei a suíte alvo `tests/fm-decide-page.test.sh` (29 testes, todos passam) e depois validei o intent como o capitão o vive: subi a página com 3 decisões reais, abri em Chromium headless e capturei screenshots da página renderizada, da validação ao tentar confirmar sem escolher, das escolhas marcadas e da confirmação após o envio; em seguida confirmei no backend que as escolhas chegaram sozinhas ao firstmate — `responses/<key>.json` com exatamente a opção e a observação selecionadas na UI, marker `ready`, `state/decide.check.sh` imprimindo uma única linha `responses-ready: <run-id>` e ficando silencioso após o marker `processed`, e o servidor encerrado sozinho (porta fechada, nenhum processo remanescente). Também exercitei a recusa de JSON inválido pela CLI e conferi o gatilho único em AGENTS.md e o inventário de docs. ## Pipeline Atualizações de [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **Intenção** - aprovado ✅ Nenhum problema encontrado.
✅ **Atualização da base** - aprovado ✅ Nenhum problema encontrado.
🔧 **Revisão** - 12 problemas encontrados → corrigido automaticamente ✅ - ⚠️ `bin/fm-decide-page.sh:434` - O aviso de sucesso nunca aparece após o envio. `#submitted-notice { display: none; }` (bin/fm-decide-page.sh:373) é uma regra de folha de estilo, e o JS faz `notice.style.display = ""` — remover a declaração inline devolve o elemento à regra CSS, que continua `none`. Depois de um POST /submit bem-sucedido o formulário é ocultado e nada é exibido: o capitão vê uma página em branco e pode concluir que o envio falhou. (Contraste com `#banner`, que funciona porque o `display:none` dele é inline.) Correção: `notice.style.display = "block"`. - ⚠️ `.agents/skills/decide/SKILL.md:30` - O passo 1 da skill manda rodar `tasks-axi list --kind captain --status open`, mas o CLI instalado não tem `--status`; a flag é `--state <queued|in_flight|done|held>` (verificado com `tasks-axi list --help`). O primeiro comando do procedimento /decide falha, e o inventário de decisões abertas não é coletado. Provavelmente deveria ser `tasks-axi list --kind captain --state held`. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-decide-page.sh:615` - Servidor HTTP de thread única (`HTTPServer`) sem `timeout` no handler. Uma única conexão ociosa bloqueia todo o servidor: preconnect especulativo do navegador, ou um cliente que envia `Content-Length: 400000` sem corpo, deixa `self.rfile.read(length)` (linha 522) bloqueado indefinidamente e a página para de responder até o watchdog de timeout (padrão 1800s) derrubar o processo. Correção: `ThreadingHTTPServer` e `Handler.timeout`/`socket` timeout. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-decide-page.sh:638` - O segredo de uso único é passado como argumento de linha de comando para o `python3` do servidor, ficando visível em `ps` para qualquer usuário local durante toda a vida do servidor. Como o gate de 403 é a única barreira contra submissões forjadas, isso anula a proteção contra outros usuários da máquina. Correção: passar via variável de ambiente ou stdin em vez de `argv[3]`. - ⚠️ `docs/decide-page.md:97` - docs/decide-page.md afirma "The page embeds no credential" (e o cabeçalho do script, linha 45, repete "No secret, credential, or absolute path is embedded in the page"), mas a página embute o segredo em `<input type="hidden" name="__secret" value="__SECRET__">` (bin/fm-decide-page.sh:385, substituído em :485) — o próprio teste extrai o segredo do HTML (tests/fm-decide-page.test.sh:208-210). É uma propriedade de segurança documentada que é falsa; deveria descrever o segredo como token anti-CSRF servido junto à página. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-decide-page.sh:189` - `mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/responses"` usa o umask herdado (tipicamente 022), deixando as decisões, evidências e notas do capitão legíveis por qualquer usuário local. O restante do estado do firstmate é endurecido (fm-check-register.sh usa `umask 077`; o próprio decide.check.sh é chmod 0700). Correção: `umask 077` antes do mkdir, ou `chmod 0700 "$RUN_DIR"`. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-decide-page.sh:79` - `--timeout 0` passa na validação (`0` casa com `[0-9]`) apesar da mensagem dizer "must be a positive integer". Com 0 o watchdog derruba o servidor imediatamente, e o script ainda imprime uma URL já morta. Correção: rejeitar `0`. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-decide-page.sh:517` - `int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))` não trata header malformado nem negativo: `Content-Length: abc` levanta `ValueError` não capturado (traceback + resposta 500 quebrada) e `Content-Length: -1` faz `self.rfile.read(-1)` ler até EOF, contornando o limite de 512 KiB. Correção: try/except e rejeitar valores negativos com 400. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-decide-page.sh:216` - O heredoc do servidor usa `<<PYEOF` sem aspas, então o shell expande `$`, backticks e barras invertidas dentro do corpo Python. Hoje é inofensivo (não há `$` nem `\\` no bloco — apenas `\n` literais, que o bash preserva), mas qualquer f-string, regex ou template futuro com `$` será silenciosamente corrompido em tempo de geração. O bloco não usa nenhuma interpolação do shell, então `<<'PYEOF'` é equivalente e seguro. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-decide-page.sh:195` - `cat > "$CHECK_SH"` trunca e reescreve o check in-place a cada execução. Se o vigia tirar seu snapshot (`fm_custom_check_snapshot_prepare`) durante essa janela, o hash não bate com o trust file e o watcher dispara um wake ruidoso `check: rejected unauthenticated state checks`. Correção: escrever em temporário e `mv -f`, como fm-check-register.sh já faz para o trust file. - ℹ️ `docs/decide-page.md:106` - docs/decide-page.md descreve `port` como "removed after server exits", mas nada no script nem no servidor remove esse arquivo — ele permanece em `state/decide-<run-id>/port` indefinidamente, junto com `server.py`, mesmo quando a run expira sem submissão. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-decide-page.sh:490` - O servidor não valida o header `Host`, então uma página remota que consiga DNS rebinding para 127.0.0.1 na porta certa poderia ler `GET /` (obtendo o segredo) e submeter escolhas forjadas. Explorabilidade baixa (porta efêmera aleatória, janela de 30 min), mas a mitigação padrão é uma linha: rejeitar requisições cujo `Host` não seja `127.0.0.1:<porta>`. 🔧 Correção: fix(decide): harden decide page server, secret handling and docs ✅ Verificado novamente — nenhum problema restante.
✅ **Testes** - aprovado ✅ Nenhum problema encontrado. - `bash tests/fm-decide-page.test.sh` (29 testes, todos passam) - Lançamento real: `FM_HOME=<tmp> FM_STATE_OVERRIDE=<tmp>/state ./bin/fm-decide-page.sh --timeout 600 decisions.json` com 3 decisões (URL 127.0.0.1 em porta efêmera + registro `state/decide.check.sh`) - Navegação e interação reais em Chromium headless via CDP (`cdp_drive.py`): screenshot da página, tentativa de envio sem escolha (banner de validação), marcação das 3 opções + observação, envio via `fetch('/submit')` e banner de confirmação - Verificação do estado persistido: `state/decide-<run-id>/responses/*.json` (choice/note/timestamp/run_id) e marker `ready` - `FM_HOME=<tmp> bash state/decide.check.sh` antes e depois de `touch processed` (imprime uma linha `responses-ready: <run-id>`, silencioso depois) - `curl http://127.0.0.1:<porta>/` e `pgrep -f server.py` após o envio (auto-encerramento confirmado) - Recusa de entrada inválida via CLI: `./bin/fm-decide-page.sh bad.json` com uma única opção → exit 1 - Conferência do gatilho único em `AGENTS.md` e do inventário em `docs/scripts.md` / `docs/documentation-audiences.json`
✅ **Documentação** - aprovado ✅ Nenhum problema encontrado.
✅ **Análise estática** - aprovado ✅ Nenhum problema encontrado.
✅ **Envio** - aprovado ✅ Nenhum problema encontrado.

feat(bin): add managed Graphify project context to crewmate briefs
body:
## Intent

Make Graphify a fully managed, local project-scoped Firstmate context subsystem with safe transactional generations and bounded intake context.

## What Changed

- Adds `bin/fm-graphify.sh`, the single owner of a Firstmate-managed, project-scoped Graphify context subsystem: it provisions a pinned Graphify environment and all derived generations under `data/graphify/` (never an ambient `graphify`, never a write into a project clone), builds each graph from allowlisted source in a private staging copy, and publishes it atomically only when the source fingerprint still agrees - so an interrupted generation reports `stale` rather than `fresh`. Holder-recording locks and markers with an exclusive recovery region let a hard kill or reboot recover without an operator step, and a `schedule` lifecycle owner coalesces per-project events, carries invalidation with the revision it was raised for, and caps concurrent rebuilds home-wide.
- Wires the subsystem into the existing lifecycle: `fm-fleet-sync.sh`, `fm-merge-local.sh`, and `fm-pr-merge.sh` hand off to `schedule` only after reporting their own result (the PR-merge path passes `invalidate`, since a remote merge leaves the local clone behind), `fm-brief.sh` inlines `FM_BRIEF_TASK` and appends bounded provenance-rich graph context when the graph is fresh (missing/stale/failed is a silent no-op), and `fm-bootstrap.sh` reports `MISSING: graphify` with a consent-gated install command.
- Adds `tests/fm-graphify.test.sh` plus `fm-brief.sh`/`fm-bootstrap.sh` coverage, documents the operator workflow and state vocabulary in `docs/configuration.md` and the lifecycle boundary in `docs/architecture.md`, and fixes a pre-existing `--check-coverage` failure in `bin/fm-test-run.sh` where sorted lists were compared under the caller's locale instead of `LC_ALL=C`.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: Both round-4 findings are genuinely fixed with targeted regression tests and nothing unsafe remains - the two open items are informational, one an over-conservative consistency gap and one a redundant hash - but this is still a large new subsystem wired into fleet sync and both merge paths that orchestrates detached background workers, so it merits follow-up attention rather than being treated as well-bounded.

## Testing

test

- Outcome: 🔧 4 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ across 2 runs (34m29s)

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

<summary>✅ **intent** - passed</summary>

</details>

</details>

<details>
<summary>⚠️ **Review** - 3 infos</summary>

- 🚨 `bin/fm-graphify.sh:228` - The publish stage is the only rebuild step with no failure handler, and `status` has no case for a persisted `building` state. Line 230 does `json.loads(out)` where `out` is the build heredoc's combined stdout+stderr (captured with `2>&1` at line 192), so any stderr emission from the third-party `graphify` import or build (a DeprecationWarning, a progress line) makes this raise. The script then exits via `set -e`; the EXIT trap removes `.build.lock` and the stage, but `write_state fresh` (line 236) never runs, leaving `state.json` at `state="building"` carrying the NEW fingerprint while `graph.json` is still the OLD published generation. In both cases status stays `stale`, `query` exits 2, and briefs are scaffolded with no Graphify section forever; a manual `rebuild` immediately republishes. Evidence: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYJDMH4TSRVAJ4Z6JAR9557Q/graphify-crash-recovery-repro.txt and graphify-transactional-transcript.txt. Not fixed here because it needs a product-code change in bin/fm-graphify.sh, which is outside this test phase.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-graphify.sh:419` - A hard-killed generation permanently leaks its private staging copy and scratch dir: `data/graphify/projects/<name>/.generation.XXXXXX` (15 MB for the 900-module fixture, i.e. a full copy of the project's source) and `data/graphify/tmp.<pid>`. Both are removed only by the owning process's exit trap, and no later rebuild, refresh, or cleanup sweeps them, so each crash costs one more source-tree copy under the managed home. Observed after the SIGKILL test: both directories were still present after a subsequent successful `rebuild`.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-test-run.sh:393` - FIXED: `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` (the mandatory CI coverage guard) failed with exit 1 and only `comm: input is not in sorted order` on a standard LANG=en_US.UTF-8 machine - its lists are sorted with LC_ALL=C but `comm` compared them under the caller's locale. Pre-existing, not caused by this change, but it made the guard unrunnable locally. Added LC_ALL=C to the guard's comm invocations; it now passes in both en_US.UTF-8 and C and confirms the new test is lane-covered (total=100).
- ⚠️ `tests/fm-graphify.test.sh:14` - FIXED: tests/fm-graphify.test.sh left its entire fixture tree - including the real ~200 MB pinned Graphify venv - in TMPDIR after every run (88 such directories, 3.9 GB, had already accumulated). fm_test_tmproot registers its EXIT cleanup inside the command substitution that produces the path, so it never removes the caller's tree; every test in the repo leaks this way, but this one is ~200x more expensive. Gave the fixture an explicit EXIT teardown; the suite now leaves nothing behind.
- <code>`bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-graphify.test.sh` - all 13 cases including the real pinned-package E2E (no gate skip)</code>
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-brief.test.sh tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh`
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-fleet-sync.test.sh tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh`
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh tests/fm-instruction-owners.test.sh`
- <code>`bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-test-run.test.sh tests/fm-nm-test-contract.test.sh tests/fm-test-isolation-proof.test.sh` (regression cover for the coverage-guard fix)</code>
- <code>`bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` under both LANG=en_US.UTF-8 and LC_ALL=C</code>
- <code>Manual operator E2E in a throwaway FM_HOME with a registered clone: `fm-bootstrap.sh` readiness -> `fm-graphify.sh install` -> `status` -> `fm-fleet-sync.sh sample-api` -> `status`/`query` -> `FM_BRIEF_TASK=... fm-brief.sh fm-901 sample-api` -> `schedule ... invalidate` -> re-sync -> `cleanup` (evidence: graphify-e2e-highlights.txt)</code>
- <code>Manual containment check on the published graph: distinct source_file list, plus `grep -c` for the .env secret, the out-of-clone symlink target and node_modules content, plus `git -C <clone> status --porcelain`</code>
- <code>Manual transactional check: `setsid fm-graphify.sh rebuild big-service` on a 900-module project, `kill -9 -<pgid>` mid-generation, then sha256 of graph.json, `status`, `query`, `refresh`, `schedule` and a manual `rebuild` (evidence: graphify-transactional-transcript.txt)</code>

title: feat(bin): add optional brain-event lifecycle bridge
body:
## Intent Ensure the merged FirstMate brain lifecycle bridge can be safely activated on the MacBook without breaking stock macOS Bash or allowing tests to emit real brain events. ## What Changed - New `bin/fm-brain-event.sh` bridges fleet lifecycle transitions to an installed `brain-event` client, wired into spawn, promote, decision resolve, backlog handoff, PR merge and completed teardown. It hashes a stable non-secret transition identity into a deterministic `firstmate::` event id so retries materialize once, forwards provenance only (agent, source kind, task id, summary), no-ops silently when neither `FM_BRAIN_EVENT_COMMAND` nor a discoverable `brain-event` exists, bounds each call with `FM_BRAIN_EVENT_TIMEOUT` through `timeout`, `gtimeout` or a perl fallback, and is invoked with `|| true` at every call site so a missing or failing bridge never changes the lifecycle outcome. - Restored stock macOS Bash 3.2 compatibility in `bin/fm-brief.sh`: the apostrophe in "firstmate's authority check" sat in a heredoc nested inside a command substitution and made `/bin/bash -n` fail with an unexpected-EOF parse error, so the line was reworded and the two assertions pinning the old wording (`tests/fm-brief.test.sh`, `tests/fm-ask-user-authority.test.sh`) were updated. The `macos-stock-bash` CI job now runs `/bin/bash -n bin/fm-brief.sh`. - Pinned `FM_BRAIN_EVENT_COMMAND=/usr/bin/true` in `bin/fm-test-run.sh`, `tests/lib.sh` and `tests/herdr-test-safety.sh`, plus directly in the suites that source none of them and drive the real lifecycle scripts, so no suite emits fixture events into a developer's real brain; added `tests/fm-brain-event.test.sh` covering validation, discovery, idempotency and the no-op path. Documented the bridge in `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/configuration.md` and `docs/scripts.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Both halves of the intent are now source-verified - the stock macOS bash 3.2 regression is fixed and guarded by CI plus a wording test, and all 29 lifecycle-driving test suites reach the brain-event isolation guard - while the bridge itself fails open at every layer (absent brain-event, failing command, hung command, and absent bridge script all leave the lifecycle outcome unchanged). ## Testing I verified all three parts of the intent with product-level CLI evidence. Stock macOS Bash: the base commit's bin/fm-brief.sh genuinely fails to parse under /bin/bash 3.2.57 and the target parses clean, all 199 shipped scripts parse, the project's own macos-stock-bash CI job reproduces locally, a real brief renders on 3.2 with the reworded authority line, and a teardown with no PR url exercises the added empty-array expansion under set -u (the hazard bash -n cannot catch). Bridge activation: driving the real auto-discovered brain-event client with the real lifecycle scripts against a local ingest endpoint produced correctly scoped PLAN_CHANGE and TASK_DONE events, an idempotent replay, outbox durability across an unreachable brain, a silent no-op when uninstalled, a visible-but-non-fatal delivery failure, and a stalled store bounded to 4s by the perl fallback (this Mac has neither timeout nor gtimeout). Test isolation: with a spy brain-event first on PATH and the real client's endpoint, token and outbox redirected, the lifecycle suites and the full 100-suite change-scoped sweep produced zero spy invocations, zero endpoint events, and left the real outbox untouched. The only red suite is tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh, which fails on a local Pi version pin unrelated to this diff. This is a shell/CLI change with no rendered UI surface, so the evidence is CLI transcripts and the received event payloads rather than screenshots. The worktree is clean and the local capture server was stopped.

Stock macOS Bash (see bash32-compat.txt, stock-bash-runtime.txt, brief-render.txt) /bin/bash 3.2.57; base a5fe1bc fails to parse bin/fm-brief.sh, target parses clean. 199/199 shipped scripts parse; brief renders on 3.2 with the reworded authority line; the project's macos-stock-bash CI job reproduced locally (15/15 snapshot, 42/42 bearings). Teardown with an EMPTY pr url exercised on 3.2 -> the added TEARDOWN_EVENT_ARGS array expands cleanly under set -u (the one runtime hazard parse checks cannot catch). ## 2. Bridge activated (see bridge-activation-e2e.txt, brain-ledger.txt, events-received.jsonl) Real ~/.local/bin/brain-event client auto-discovered, real lifecycle scripts, stock bash. promote -> PLAN_CHANGE, teardown -> TASK_DONE with pr_url, replay is a server-side duplicate, unreachable brain queues and then flushes, uninstalled bridge is a silent no-op, failing store warns without changing the outcome, stalled store bounded to 4s by the perl fallback (this MacBook has neither timeout nor gtimeout). ## 3. title: fix(backends): avoid Herdr schema check SIGPIPE noise
body:
## Summary
Herdr watcher cycles repeatedly emitted `printf: write error: Broken pipe` from `bin/backends/herdr.sh` lines 1960 and 1961.
The firsthand reproduction occurred on roughly fifteen separate watcher cycles over several hours while running the unpatched code on current upstream `main`.
No existing upstream pull request touches this code path.
Searches for SIGPIPE, broken pipe, and the Herdr schema check found no duplicate proposal.
Three open pull requests address a different Bash 3.2 parse issue in `bin/fm-brief.sh` and are unrelated to this fix.

## Cause
`fm_backend_herdr_events_capable` piped the full `herdr api schema --json` output into `grep -Fq` for two capability checks.
Because `grep -q` exits after its first match, it closed the read end while `printf` was still writing the approximately 220 KB schema.
The resulting SIGPIPE caused Bash to print the broken-pipe diagnostic even though capability detection succeeded.

## Fix
Both pipelines now use here-strings, so the checks have no pipe that can trigger SIGPIPE.
The change is behavior-preserving because it keeps the same two capability checks and return values while removing the pipe entirely.
This fix has existed in the personal fork since 2026-07-23 and had not reached upstream.

## Testing
The regression test feeds a deliberately large schema through a first-match-and-exit `grep` stand-in and fails if broken-pipe or write-error text reaches stderr.
Live Herdr 0.7.5 evidence recorded client/server protocol 17/17, successful patched detection, empty patched stderr, and the two unpatched broken-pipe diagnostics against the same schema under Bash 3.2.
`bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`, all Bash syntax checks, `bin/fm-lint.sh` with ShellCheck 0.11.0, and `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh` passed.

## Evidence Note
The runtime-backend evidence note is included because `CONTRIBUTING.md` requires current empirical evidence for runtime session backend changes.
The note updates the documented Herdr capability gate that this fix touches.

title: fix(bin): re-own the Kimi turn-end hook region after a config rewrite
body:
Fixes #1064.

## Problem

The Kimi CLI rewrites its own `~/.kimi-code/config.toml` and drops every comment as part of TOML normalization. That erases the `# BEGIN FIRSTMATE KIMI TURN-END HOOK` / `# END ...` markers delimiting Firstmate's turn-end hook region, while leaving the `[[hooks]]` table itself byte-identical. The next crewmate spawn then refused:

```
fm-kimi-turnend-hook: refused: config.toml references fm-turn-end.sh outside the Firstmate-owned region.
```

So the second Kimi spawn onward could not launch, which made the Kimi crew adapter unusable for repeated work.

### Reproduction

Install into a fresh config, delete every comment line (the CLI's own normalization), then install again:

```
$ HOME=$repro bin/fm-kimi-turnend-hook.sh install          # ok, region written with markers
$ sed -i '' '/^[[:space:]]*#/d' $repro/.kimi-code/config.toml   # simulate the Kimi rewrite
$ HOME=$repro bin/fm-kimi-turnend-hook.sh install
fm-kimi-turnend-hook: refused: config.toml references fm-turn-end.sh outside the Firstmate-owned region.
rc=1
```

The `[[hooks]]` table survives the rewrite intact; only the two comment lines are gone.

## Fix

Region identification no longer depends on the comment markers surviving. Markers remain the fast path; when they are absent, the region is re-identified structurally:

1. Exactly one `[[hooks]]` entry may reference `fm-turn-end.sh`, and its parsed content must equal the hook entry the installer itself emits. That expected entry is derived by parsing the generated block rather than restated, so the block stays the single owner of the hook table's content.
2. The entry's text span is located by scanning `[[hooks]]` headers in document order, ending at the last non-blank, non-comment line before the next table header, so trailing blank lines and comments belonging to the following section are left alone.
3. The span is verified before use: the config with that span excised must parse, and must equal the original parsed document minus exactly that one entry. Any scanning mistake fails this check and refuses instead of rewriting the captain's config.
4. The verified span is then re-owned and re-marked in place. Repeated installs neither refuse nor accumulate duplicate hook tables, and removal still restores the surrounding bytes exactly.

Adoption runs before both the install and remove branches, so a config whose markers were stripped can also be cleanly uninstalled.

## Safety property preserved

The refusal exists to stop Firstmate clobbering a hook it does not own, and that is unchanged. A `[[hooks]]` table that references `fm-turn-end.sh` but is not the installer's own entry stays foreign and is still refused before any config write. All four shapes are covered by tests:

- a different script path
- Firstmate's entry plus an extra captain-added key
- two identical unmarked Firstmate blocks
- the inline-array `hooks = [{ ... }]` form

## Tests

`tests/fm-kimi-harness.test.sh` gains two cases:

- `test_kimi_hook_reowns_its_region_after_a_comment_stripping_rewrite` - fresh install, simulated comment-stripping rewrite, re-install succeeds and re-marks the region, exactly two hook tables remain (one foreign, one Firstmate's), a further install is byte-idempotent, and removal after another rewrite restores the original config byte-for-byte.
- `test_kimi_hook_still_refuses_unmarked_foreign_hook_tables` - the four foreign shapes above each refuse with the concrete reason, without changing config bytes and without writing the hook script.

All 21 cases in that file pass, as do `fm-turnend-guard`, `fm-documentation-audiences`, `fm-instruction-owners`, and `fm-lint`. `bin/fm-lint.sh`, `shellcheck`, and `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` are clean.

## Docs

`docs/turnend-guard.md` records the rewrite behavior and the structural re-ownership as a current Kimi fact, and its regression-coverage line now names the new coverage.

## Note for maintainers

The installer requires a `python3` with `tomllib`, so Python 3.11 or newer. On a host whose first `python3` on PATH is older, it refuses before touching the config. That behavior is pre-existing and unchanged here, but it is worth confirming on Kimi hosts.

title: fix(watch): keep a declared pause on its bounded cadence
body:
## The problem

A crew that declares `paused:` and then sits on long external monitors made the watcher churn. Every arm cycle started a watcher that immediately closed on `stale: <window>` for that same declared wait, so no watcher stayed up to hold the home lock, and the turn-end path then reported `watcher: FAILED - cycle ended without an actionable reason` and demanded a supervision repair. This repeated every few seconds and never settled. Declaring the pause helped the first surface only; the repetition continued.

## Root cause

Two independent defects, both reproduced before changing any code.

**Watcher, `bin/fm-watch.sh`.** `pause_state_class` demoted a still-declared pause to `none` whenever the crew's agent was still live, so a live declaration was designed to surface exactly once per stale hash. That holds only for a byte-static pane. A live crew's pane text keeps drifting, and on every drift the changed-hash branch reclassified the declaration as `none` and called `clear_pause_tracking`, which deletes `.paused-<key>` and the `.paused-resurfaced-<key>` cadence anchor. Two polls later the pane was stably stale again with no suppressor, so the same declared wait surfaced as a bare `stale:` wake and the cycle closed on it. Nothing bounded the repetition: the `FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS` cadence never applied to a live paused crew at all. A briefly busy pane wiped the same markers through the second clear in the busy branch.

Reproduction, five consecutive watcher cycles over a live paused crew whose pane gained one line between cycles:

```
round 1: EXITED -> stale: test:fm-op
round 2: EXITED -> stale: test:fm-op
round 3: EXITED -> stale: test:fm-op
round 4: EXITED -> stale: test:fm-op
round 5: EXITED -> stale: test:fm-op
stale wakes queued: 5
```

The same fixture with a byte-static pane surfaced once and absorbed the remaining four cycles, which isolates pane drift as the amplifier.

**Arm layer, `bin/fm-watch-arm.sh`.** Several arms can follow one watcher cycle. Only the arm that owns the watcher prints the wake reason; a follower attaches, then sees the cycle close with no successor and reported the typed failure for a close supervision had handled correctly:

```
round 1: armA rc=1 [watcher: already running pid N|watcher: attached pid=N (beacon 0s)|watcher: FAILED - cycle ended without an actionable reason|]
round 1: armB rc=0 [watcher: started pid=N (beacon fresh)|signal: .../op.status|]
```

## The fix

A declaration stays on its bounded `FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS` cadence once it has been surfaced inside the current window, whether or not its agent is still live, and its cadence markers survive both pane drift and a briefly busy pane. The withdrawal check at the top of the stale loop remains the one owner of clearing them.

Preserved: an active run still outranks the declaration and takes the ordinary wedge timer; a crew with no declaration still trips stale immediately; a forgotten pause still re-surfaces once per window as an awaiting-external recheck; a live declaration firstmate has not seen yet still surfaces once on first sight.

A follower arm now consults the durable wake queue, the shared record of what a cycle surfaced. A record appended at or after the cycle began, together with a fresh liveness beacon, explains the close, so the follower prints those queued reason lines and exits zero. A stale or absent beacon never qualifies, so genuinely down supervision still fails loudly and the guard keeps its real protection.

After the fix, the same five-cycle reproduction surfaces once and absorbs the rest, and both concurrent arms return zero with the queued reason.

## Tests

- `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` - a live declared pause surfaces once, absorbs across pane drift with its cadence markers and wedge-timer exemption intact, and returns to ordinary stale surfacing once withdrawn. Fails on the pre-fix watcher at drift cycle 2.
- `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh` - a follower arm whose cycle queued a wake reports that wake instead of a typed failure, and the same setup with an ancient beacon still fails loudly. The first fails on the pre-fix arm with exit 1.
- `tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` - the guard stays silent for a live beating watcher with wakes queued for the next turn, and still blocks when no beacon exists.

Also fixes a pre-existing race in the watcher-lock suite: the TERM-resistant peer fixture is now waited on until it has installed its signal handler, since the restart's signal could otherwise land during interpreter startup, kill the peer, and fail the attach assertion for reasons unrelated to the code under test. That failure reproduces on `main`.

## Validation

`bin/fm-lint.sh` clean, `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` clean, and `bin/fm-test-run.sh --family watcher-wake-lock` green (10 suites, 0 failed), plus the auto-arm, instruction-owner, and documentation-audience suites.
