title: feat(bin): retain recent Done outcomes as bounded fleet memory
body:
## Intent Implement the Firstmate-side memory source requested for Deck using the existing active backlog Done window plus durable archive split. Increase the tracked tasks-axi markdown done_keep policy from 10 to 50 and update its authoritative configuration documentation without duplicating the number elsewhere. Keep finished workers clean-up compatible while ensuring fm-fleet-snapshot still exposes recent structured Done outcomes as bounded memory after live metadata, status, and endpoints are gone. The safe Done shape should include structured title, repo, kind, completion date, and admitted artifact link, but must not expose task notes, decision bodies, report contents, raw status prose, absolute local paths, or arbitrary Done body prose. Prove tasks-axi pruning with an isolated temporary home: at 51 Done items it archives only the oldest and retains exactly the newest 50. Preserve decision holds, dependencies, archive format, Done chronology, session-start size bounds, secondmate isolation, and existing snapshot consumers. Do not edit Firstmate Deck and do not parse data/done-archive.md into Deck. ## What Changed - Raised the tracked `.tasks.toml` `done_keep` from 10 to 50 so the active backlog keeps a 50-item recent-completion window and pruning only archives past it; `bin/fm-teardown.sh` and `docs/configuration.md` now name the `done_keep` setting instead of restating the number, and `tests/fm-instruction-owners.test.sh` pins the documented value to `.tasks.toml`. - `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` now emits Done records as structured identity plus artifact only - `body_lines` emptied and `body_excerpt` null, with a `local main` body line lifted into `local_note` before the drop - so recent outcomes survive a torn-down worker's meta/status/endpoint cleanup without carrying task notes, decision bodies, report prose, or absolute local paths. Unstructured Done lines keep their position but have their raw prose replaced by the fixed marker `(unstructured done line)`. - Narrowed `bin/fm-bearings-snapshot.sh --fields bodies` to queued items only (Done rows now carry no bodies) and updated its help and omitted-surface label to match; added regression cases for 51-item pruning (archives the oldest, retains the newest 50) and for Done body suppression after worker cleanup. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The branch is well-bounded and every intent criterion verified end-to-end against the real tasks-axi binary and the changed scripts, and the single round-1 warning is now fixed with a one-line Done-scoped redaction that I confirmed closes the leak without touching in-flight/queued rows, main_inventory signals, or any other snapshot consumer. ## Testing Exercised the six targeted suites touching this change plus a manual end-to-end driver that reproduces the captain's actual experience. Pruning was proven in an isolated temporary home by closing 51 items through the real `tasks-axi` verbs `fm-teardown.sh` emits: exactly 50 stay in `data/backlog.md` newest-first, only `recent-01` moves into `data/done-archive.md`, and the `## Archived <date>` archive format is unchanged. Done-as-memory was proven by rendering `bin/fm-fleet-view.sh` on a home where a ship worker is live, then again after its meta, status log, worktree and tmux endpoint are removed - the worker drops out of Under Way while its Done row keeps id, title, repo, kind, completion verb/date and the admitted artifact (PR URL, `data/<id>/report.md`, or `local main`), with `body_lines: []` and `body_excerpt: null`. The same fixture carries a task note, a decision body, status prose, absolute `/Users/yelen/private/...` paths and a hand-written Done line; running base commit 514f0ab against that identical home leaks all of it through the snapshot, the view and `bearings --fields bodies`, while the target commit is clean on all five consumer surfaces and keeps the unstructured line in place as `(unstructured done line)`. Queued bodies are still revealed, so the redaction is not over-broad. Session-start bounding, decision holds, dependency resolution and secondmate handoff isolation all stay green, and `done_keep` appears only in `.tasks.toml` and `docs/configuration.md` with `fm-teardown.sh` now deferring to the config. No screenshot or rendered-HTML artifact applies: the change is entirely bash and markdown docs with no HTML, CSS or renderer surface, so the faithful end-user artifact is the CLI transcript of `fm-fleet-view.sh` / `fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` output, captured verbatim.

title: fix: conferma l'avvio del watcher su Windows/MSYS
body:
## Causa radice

Su Git Bash/MSYS il `ps` Cygwin 3.6.6 di questa macchina rifiuta `ps -p <pid> -o lstart= -o command=` con `ps: unknown option -- o`.
Il watcher partiva regolarmente, aggiornava `.last-watcher-beat` e pubblicava il PID nel lock, ma `fm_pid_identity` non produceva alcuna identità: il gate di salute dell'arm, correttamente fail-closed, rifiutava quindi il lock incompleto e terminava il figlio al timeout.
Quando il ledger veniva scritto, il cleanup del watcher aveva già rimosso il lock, da cui `lock_before=pid:none|identity:none` nei fallimenti osservati.

In più, il cold start MSYS può impiegare più dei 10 secondi precedenti per completare fork e migrazioni pre-lock.

## Fix

- `fm_pid_identity` usa `/proc/<pid>/stat` e `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` per capability anche su MSYS, non più solo quando `uname` restituisce Linux.
- L'identità resta resistente al riuso PID (`starttime` + cmdline completa) e il fallback `ps` resta locale-invariante e fail-closed.
- `uname` viene risolto una sola volta quando la libreria è caricata, evitando fork ripetuti nei poll stretti.
- Il timeout di conferma dell'arm resta 10 s sulle altre piattaforme e diventa 30 s solo per `msys*`, `mingw*` e `cygwin*`.
- Come autorizzato, gli adapter OpenCode e Pi attendono 35 s solo quando `process.platform === win32`; sulle altre piattaforme conservano 12 s. Il margine di 5 s evita che l'adapter termini un cold start MSYS lento ma riuscito mentre l'arm sta ancora confermando.
- Documentazione e regressioni per `/proc`, riuso PID, locale e MSYS sono aggiornate.

Il contratto non viene allentato: `started`/`attached` richiedono ancora PID vivo, identità esatta della stessa home e beacon fresco; un'identità assente o un beacon stantio restano un errore rumoroso e non-zero.

## Prova reale su Windows 11 / Git Bash

Tre cicli consecutivi puliti, incluso `--restart`:

```text
watcher: started pid=23083 (beacon fresh)
watcher: started pid=23452 (beacon fresh)   # --restart
watcher: started pid=23811 (beacon fresh)
```

Dettaglio del primo ciclo:

```text
CYCLE=2 ARM_PID=23072 MODE=arm
watcher: started pid=23083 (beacon fresh)
LOCK_PID=23083
LOCK_IDENTITY=proc-starttime=676830598 cmdline-hex=62617368002f632f55736572732f4e69636f6c612050696f204172656e612f2e74726565686f7573652f66697273746d6174652d3762616232302f312f66697273746d6174652f62696e2f666d2d77617463682e736800
BEACON_AGE=2
```

Riga ledger reale (il fixture termina intenzionalmente l'arm esatto dopo la prova, quindi `reason=arm-interrupted`/`TERM` sono attesi):

```text
arm_pid=23072	watcher_pid=23083	origin=started	started_at=1785263422	ended_at=1785263448	exit_code=143	signal=TERM	reason=arm-interrupted	beacon_age=4	lock_before=pid:23083|identity:proc-starttime=676830598 cmdline-hex=62617368002f632f55736572732f4e69636f6c612050696f204172656e612f2e74726565686f7573652f66697273746d6174652d3762616232302f312f66697273746d6174652f62696e2f666d2d77617463682e736800	lock_after=pid:none|identity:none	successor=none
```

Prova singleton concorrente:

```text
watcher: started pid=24176 (beacon fresh)
watcher: attached pid=24176 (beacon 4s)
```

Entrambi gli arm hanno osservato lo stesso lock PID `24176`; nessun watcher duplicato.
Con `FM_ARM_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT=10` sullo stesso host il caso torna deterministicamente a `confirmation-timeout`, confermando che il margine MSYS è necessario e non un colpo fortunato.

## Verifiche

- `bash -n bin/fm-watch-arm.sh bin/fm-wake-lib.sh tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh`
- `node --check .opencode/plugins/fm-primary-watch-arm.js`
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- ShellCheck 0.11.0 sui file shell modificati normalizzati LF
- nuove regressioni identità `/proc` e MSYS superate
- no-mistakes review concluso senza finding sul commit finale; push protetto completato (`01KYN5MHJJNQ53WE2Q64BPCVNS`)

La suite completa `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh` su questa macchina arriva oltre tutte le nuove regressioni e poi incontra due volte il failure preesistente del test di lock concorrente (`expected exactly one lock winner under concurrency, got 2`); la prova end-to-end a due arm sopra conferma comunque il singleton del percorso modificato.

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

title: feat(bin): enroll crewmates in Parlay on spawn and teardown
body:
## Intent Wire firstmate's own crewmate lifecycle to Parlay's chat panel: bin/fm-spawn.sh calls parlay listen --agent after a successful launch, and bin/fm-teardown.sh calls parlay agent-down on clean teardown, so Parlay's panel shows which firstmate agents are live. Both calls are deliberately best-effort/non-load-bearing: a missing, unauthenticated, or failing parlay CLI must never block or fail a spawn or teardown, since Parlay enrollment is an enhancement, not a dependency of the crewmate lifecycle. Key design decision: parlay listen --agent was discovered (by reading Parlay's own CLI source, not just the task description) to be a blocking command that execs into a never-returning poll loop, identical to parlay monitor - so the implementation backgrounds it (nohup + disown) rather than calling it synchronously, and records its pid at state/.parlay-listen.pid so teardown's fm_parlay_agent_down can stop that poller before deregistering. Both functions live in a new shared lib, bin/fm-parlay-lib.sh, sourced by both fm-spawn.sh and fm-teardown.sh, following the existing small fm-*-lib.sh convention (e.g. fm-pr-lib.sh). Deliberately did not add a new config/ file or opt-out toggle: the task brief explicitly said not to over-engineer this, and checking the existing wedge-alarm config-driven optional-channel pattern showed it was too heavyweight for this simpler need - a plain 'skip silently if parlay is not on PATH' check (command -v parlay) is the whole gating mechanism. Also out of scope by explicit brief instruction: no changes to Parlay's own repo (trillium/parlay) - listen and agent-down already exist there. Added tests/fm-parlay-lib.test.sh with unit coverage for both functions, with and without parlay on PATH, and the best-effort-failure-still-warns path, following the fake-binary PATH-shimming pattern used by the rest of tests/. Documented the new state/.parlay-listen.pid file as a one-line entry in AGENTS.md's existing state/ layout listing, matching how the neighboring grok/kimi turnend-token files are documented there. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-parlay-lib.sh` with `fm_parlay_agent_up` (backgrounds `parlay listen --agent ` via `nohup`+`disown` since the command execs into a never-returning poll loop, recording its pid at `state/.parlay-listen.pid`) and `fm_parlay_agent_down` (kills the recorded listen pid, then calls `parlay agent-down ` to deregister); both are best-effort and silently no-op when `parlay` is not on PATH. - `bin/fm-spawn.sh` sources the new lib and calls `fm_parlay_agent_up` after a successful crewmate launch; `bin/fm-teardown.sh` sources it and calls `fm_parlay_agent_down` during cleanup, still killing any recorded listen pid and removing the pidfile even when `parlay` is currently missing from PATH. - Documented `state/.parlay-listen.pid` in `AGENTS.md`'s state layout and added `fm-parlay-lib.sh` to the toolbelt table in `docs/scripts.md`. - Added `tests/fm-parlay-lib.test.sh` with unit coverage for both functions, with and without `parlay` on PATH. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a small, well-isolated best-effort integration (new fm-parlay-lib.sh sourced by fm-spawn.sh/fm-teardown.sh) placed after all failure-prone spawn/teardown steps so it cannot block the crewmate lifecycle; the one substantive issue found in round 1 (pid leak when parlay is absent from PATH) has already been fixed and covered by an updated test, and no new issues were found on this pass. ## Testing Ran the new fm-parlay-lib unit suite (all 5 cases pass, including the pid-leak fix) and additionally drove the real fm-spawn.sh/fm-teardown.sh scripts end-to-end against a fake parlay binary that blocks on `listen` like the real CLI does — confirming spawn backgrounds the listen call and records a live pid without blocking, teardown kills that poller, calls agent-down, and removes the pid file, and that both commands still succeed cleanly when parlay is entirely absent from PATH. No source changes were needed; no findings.
Evidence: End-to-end CLI transcript: fm-spawn.sh -> Parlay enrollment -> fm-teardown.sh -> deregistration, plus a parlay-absent sanity pass ```text === STEP 1: fm-spawn.sh (real script, real worktree, fake tmux+parlay) === warn: no registry at /var/folders/8k/0ll7yqm179v19qqg3qmgcq3m0000gn/T//fm-parlay-e2e.OJGTSY/case1/home/data/projects.md; defaulting project to no-mistakes off spawned parlay-e2e-z1 harness=claude kind=ship mode=no-mistakes yolo=off window=firstmate:fm-parlay-e2e-z1 worktree=/var/folders/8k/0ll7yqm179v19qqg3qmgcq3m0000gn/T//fm-parlay-e2e.OJGTSY/case1/wt spawn exit code: 0 === STEP 2: verify the real fm-spawn.sh actually enrolled the agent in Parlay === pid file recorded: /var/folders/8k/0ll7yqm179v19qqg3qmgcq3m0000gn/T//fm-parlay-e2e.OJGTSY/case1/home/state/parlay-e2e-z1.parlay-listen.pid -> pid 18456 confirmed: pid 18456 is a live backgrounded process (the never-returning 'parlay listen' poll loop) parlay calls so far: (no calls logged) === STEP 3: fm-teardown.sh (real script) tears the same task down === teardown parlay-e2e-z1 complete (window firstmate:fm-parlay-e2e-z1, worktree /var/folders/8k/0ll7yqm179v19qqg3qmgcq3m0000gn/T//fm-parlay-e2e.OJGTSY/case1/wt) Backlog: parlay-e2e-z1 just finished. Run tasks-axi done parlay-e2e-z1 --note "local main", then run tasks-axi ready for dependency-cleared candidates, check date gates, and dispatch only work whose blockers are gone and date is due. teardown exit code: 0 === STEP 4: verify the real fm-teardown.sh stopped the poller and deregistered === confirmed: listen poller pid 18456 was killed by teardown confirmed: pid file /var/folders/8k/0ll7yqm179v19qqg3qmgcq3m0000gn/T//fm-parlay-e2e.OJGTSY/case1/home/state/parlay-e2e-z1.parlay-listen.pid was removed by teardown final parlay calls log (listen, then agent-down): listen --agent parlay-e2e-z1 agent-down parlay-e2e-z1 === STEP 5: sanity - same flow with parlay ABSENT from PATH must never fail spawn/teardown === warn: no registry at /var/folders/8k/0ll7yqm179v19qqg3qmgcq3m0000gn/T//fm-parlay-e2e.OJGTSY/case1/home/data/projects.md; defaulting project to no-mistakes off spawned parlay-e2e-noparlay-z2 harness=claude kind=ship mode=no-mistakes yolo=off window=firstmate:fm-parlay-e2e-noparlay-z2 worktree=/var/folders/8k/0ll7yqm179v19qqg3qmgcq3m0000gn/T//fm-parlay-e2e.OJGTSY/case1/wt2 spawn (no parlay on PATH) exit code: 0 confirmed: no pid file recorded when parlay is absent (expected no-op) warning: parlay is not on PATH; skipping agent-down deregistration for parlay-e2e-noparlay-z2 teardown parlay-e2e-noparlay-z2 complete (window firstmate:fm-parlay-e2e-noparlay-z2, worktree /var/folders/8k/0ll7yqm179v19qqg3qmgcq3m0000gn/T//fm-parlay-e2e.OJGTSY/case1/wt2) Backlog: parlay-e2e-noparlay-z2 just finished. Update data/backlog.md - move parlay-e2e-noparlay-z2 to Done, keep Done to the 10 most recent, then re-scan Queued and dispatch only work whose blockers are gone and date is due. teardown (no parlay on PATH) exit code: 0 === SUMMARY === spawn1 rc=0 teardown1 rc=0 spawn2(no-parlay) rc=0 teardown2(no-parlay) rc=0 ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `bin/fm-parlay-lib.sh:31` - fm_parlay_agent_down gates its entire body, including the pid kill/cleanup, on `command -v parlay` (line 31). If the `parlay` binary is not resolvable on PATH at teardown time (different invocation context, uninstalled, PATH stripped in a hook/cron environment) even though it was present at spawn time, this function returns before ever reading or killing the recorded background `parlay listen` pid at state/<id>.parlay-listen.pid. fm-teardown.sh later unconditionally `rm -f`s that pidfile in its own cleanup regardless of what this function did, so the pid is lost and the backgrounded nohup'd `parlay listen` process is orphaned permanently with no remaining record to clean it up. This is locked in by tests/fm-parlay-lib.test.sh's test_agent_down_noop_without_parlay_on_path, which explicitly asserts the pidfile is left untouched in this scenario, so it reads as a deliberate choice rather than an oversight. Killing the already-recorded pid doesn't require `parlay` to be on PATH at all - only the final `parlay agent-down` deregistration call does - so gating the whole function on the binary's current presence conflates two independent concerns and can leak a background process indefinitely. 🔧 Fix: Fix parlay agent-down pid leak when parlay missing from PATH ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-parlay-lib.test.sh` (5/5 pass, including the review-commit's fix for killing a leaked listen pid when parlay is off PATH) - Manual end-to-end driver invoking the real `bin/fm-spawn.sh` and `bin/fm-teardown.sh` against a git worktree, fake tmux, and a fake `parlay` binary that blocks on `listen` (mirroring the real CLI's never-returning poll loop) — confirmed live backgrounded pid recorded on spawn, and killed + deregistered + pid file removed on teardown - Same spawn/teardown flow re-run with `parlay` absent from PATH — confirmed both commands still succeed (exit 0) with no pid file written, proving the enhancement never blocks the crewmate lifecycle - `bash -n` syntax check on bin/fm-spawn.sh, bin/fm-teardown.sh, bin/fm-parlay-lib.sh
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: feat(bin): add inert private Telegram bridge with enforced publish gate
body:
## Intent

Close every merge-blocking security finding from the two independent adversarial reviews of PR 1214's private Telegram bridge, so the bridge's outbound reply, publish-landing, watcher-cadence, pairing-replacement, cleanup, API-origin and retry paths are bounded by code rather than by agent instructions, with each reported counterexample committed as a negative regression. The bridge stays inert until a BotFather token and a completed pairing exist.

## What Changed

- Adds the private Telegram bridge under `bin/`: `fm-tg-pair.sh`, `fm-tg-poll.sh`, `fm-tg-reply.sh`, `fm-tg-task.sh` and the shared `fm-tg-lib.sh`. One pinned private peer is heard (numeric user id and chat id both matched, usernames never read), the watcher drives one bounded long poll per cycle, replies are staged and delivered to that single target with splitting and retry, and tasks can be linked back to the request that asked for them. With no BotFather token and no completed pairing the bridge is a hard no-op: poll exits 0 silently, reply refuses, and no `state/telegram/` is written.
- Moves the merge-blocking guarantees from agent instructions into code. `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` and `bin/fm-merge-local.sh` now refuse to land a task carrying a Telegram origin unless the pinned peer confirmed publishing in a fresh inbound message received after the preview, matched against the exact revision about to land and consumed once so an approval cannot be replayed; the origin key is immutable, and `fm-tg-task.sh release --yes --reason` is the audited per-task recovery when the pairing is revoked. The same round bounds API origin resolution and token transport, the poll and publish attempt budgets, error dedup and recovery re-announces, pairing replacement and state cleanup, retry into an already-closed request, project routing per subcommand, and refuses no-mistakes gate agents on the paired channel.
- Extracts message splitting, private artifact writes and `.env` reading out of `bin/fm-x-lib.sh` into `fm-message-split-lib.sh`, `fm-private-artifact-lib.sh` and `fm-env-file-lib.sh` shared by both channels, teaches the watcher cadence, arm command policy, PR-check migration and `fm-test-run.sh` family selection about the bridge, and lands the coverage and docs: `tests/fm-telegram-bridge.test.sh` with a fake local Bot API server in `tests/telegram-helpers.sh` (82 checks green), `tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh`, `docs/verification/telegram-bridge.md`, the configuration/architecture/AGENTS references and the `telegram-respond` skill. Every counterexample the two adversarial reviews reported is committed as a negative regression.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The round-4 change is a three-line reorder that resolves the last open finding exactly as recommended, it demonstrably weakens nothing for unreleased tasks, and it lands with a focused pull-request regression that asserts both the success and the absence of the specific refusal, leaving no outstanding findings across four review rounds.

## Testing

Ran the targeted telegram-bridge suite (82 checks) plus the changed landing-gate and cross-channel suites (fm-pr-merge 20, fm-x-mode 102, and the arm-pretool-check, supervision-instructions, turnend-guard and watcher-lock scripts) - all pass. Because passing tests alone do not show the intent, I also drove the real bridge entrypoints through a 13-scene operator CLI session against the hermetic fake Bot API and captured the full transcript: the bridge is silent and writes nothing until a token and a completed pairing both exist, and every path the intent names now refuses in code with a specific message and exit status - unauthenticated or cross-project replies, --retry into a closed exchange, hostile API origins, landing a Telegram-origin task with no live confirmation, self-written or stale or replayed publish confirmations, an unaudited release, a gate agent reaching the channel, a retired peer's leftover authorizations, cleanup through a symlinked bridge directory, and a tampered shim earning the fast watcher cadence. <details>
<summary>🔧 **Review** - 9 issues found → auto-fixed (3) ✅</summary>

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-tg-task.sh:220` - The publish confirmation is not bound to any inbound Telegram message. `arm-publish` prints the one-time code to stdout (bin/fm-tg-task.sh:209) and `confirm-publish` reads the "reply" from an arbitrary caller-supplied path (`--message-file <path>`, or `-` for stdin), then scans it for that code. Nothing checks that the code ever arrived in a message from the pinned peer, and nothing requires any elapsed time between arming and confirming, so the two-step gate rests on the skill's prose rule "never arm and confirm in the same turn" rather than on code. This is the same class the change already closed on the outbound side by removing `--text-file`; the bridge already holds the real inbound message in `state/telegram/inbox/<rid>.json` and `context/<rid>.json`, so the earliest supported shared boundary is to have `confirm-publish` read the confirming text from a request record for the pinned peer received after `armed_at`, instead of from a path.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-tg-lib.sh:1062` - The landing gate's only linkage evidence is the mutable task meta: `fmtg_meta_is_linked` decides by the presence of `tg_request=`/`tg_chat=`, and both `bin/fm-tg-reply.sh --final` (via `finalize`, bin/fm-tg-reply.sh:194) and `bin/fm-tg-task.sh unlink` (bin/fm-tg-task.sh:183) strip exactly those keys with no authorization check. Once cleared, `fm-pr-merge.sh` and `fm-merge-local.sh` skip the whole publish gate, so the skill's claim "you cannot bypass it by forgetting" (.agents/skills/telegram-respond/SKILL.md:113) does not hold for an out-of-order terminal reply. Suggested minimal repair at the shared boundary: have `fmtg_landing_guard` also treat an armed publish record for the task (`state/telegram/publish/<task>.json`) as linkage, so a task that entered the two-step flow still refuses after its meta link is cleared.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-tg-task.sh:204` - `prepared_revision` refuses with `exit 6` when the task has no recorded worktree, the worktree is gone, or `git rev-parse` yields nothing, but it is invoked as `HEAD_REV=$(prepared_revision)` and the script runs under `set -u` without `-e`. `exit` inside a command substitution terminates only the subshell, so both `arm-publish` (line 204) and `confirm-publish` (line 215) print the refusal to stderr and then keep going with an empty `HEAD_REV`. Fix by returning non-zero and checking the caller's status (or capturing `$?` after the assignment).
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-tg-lib.sh:508` - `FM_TELEGRAM_PAIR_SENDERS` is documented as an operator knob twice (docs/configuration.md:429 and :601) but no code ever reads it. `fmtg_load_config` does not resolve it, and the cap is read from the internal `FMTG_PAIR_SENDERS` default instead, so setting the documented variable silently does nothing. Either resolve `FM_TELEGRAM_PAIR_SENDERS` in `fmtg_load_config` alongside the other `FM_TELEGRAM_*` knobs, or drop it from the configuration reference.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-tg-lib.sh:201` - The upper clamp for `FM_TELEGRAM_PUBLISH_ATTEMPTS` resets an out-of-range value to the default 5 rather than clamping to 20 (`[ "$raw" -le 20 ] 2>/dev/null || raw=5`), unlike every sibling clamp in the file and unlike the documented contract "clamped to 1-20" (docs/configuration.md:602). `FM_TELEGRAM_PUBLISH_ATTEMPTS=50` yields 5, not 20. Behaviour stays safe (it fails toward the tighter budget), but it contradicts the documented range.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-tg-reply.sh:199` - The `--retry` path validates only that the preserved outbox record's `chat_id` still equals the pinned peer; it never calls `fmtg_request_authentic`, so the "already closed by a final reply" refusal (exit 7) that the header and docs promise for every send does not apply to a retry. A reply that failed mid-send leaves its outbox record in place (it is only removed on success), so after a later `--final` reply closes that request, `--retry <request_id>` still delivers the remaining chunks of the abandoned earlier reply. Adding the same authenticity/open check to the retry branch does not break the legitimate case, because a final reply only closes the request after all its chunks land.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-tg-task.sh:182` - The file header states "Every subcommand here compares the task's own recorded project against that pinned name and refuses on any mismatch (exit 6)", but only `link`, `arm-publish` and `confirm-publish` call `require_project_match`. `unlink` (line 182), `show` (line 187) and `clear-publish` (line 268) do not, so `show` prints another project's task link, linked chat and publish-record state, and `clear-publish` deletes another project's armed confirmation. Either add `require_project_match` to those three or narrow the header claim.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-tg-lib.sh:1135` - The `landing-target-mismatch` branch (exit 10) in `fmtg_landing_guard` is unreachable: `landed_at` and `landing_target` are written together in the same jq consume at line 1143, and the `already-landed` check at line 1119 returns 7 before the target comparison is ever evaluated. The documented exit code 10 therefore cannot be observed in practice. Harmless as defense in depth, but the exit-code list above the function advertises a refusal reason that never fires.
- ℹ️ `docs/configuration.md:521` - The Telegram section adds two separate `### Replies` headings (lines 496 and 521) with overlapping content: the first covers staging, request authentication and durable progress, the second covers single-target delivery, escaping, splitting, retry and dry run. Duplicate headings collide on the `#replies` anchor and split what the section elsewhere claims is a single-owner contract. Merging them into one heading would keep the reply contract in one place.

🔧 Fix: bind publish confirmation to a fresh peer message and harden landing gate
2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-tg-lib.sh:1163` - Making `tg_origin` immutable (the review-2 fix) means revoking the pairing permanently blocks every task that ever came from the bridge, with no supported recovery. Concrete sequence: (1) the paired person asks for a change, the agent runs `fm-tg-task.sh link <task> <rid>`, writing `tg_origin=` into the task meta; (2) the captain later runs `bin/fm-tg-pair.sh revoke --yes` (or the full opt-out, including `rm -rf state/telegram/`); (3) the finished task is landed with `bin/fm-merge-local.sh <task>` or `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh`. `fmtg_landing_gate_applies` still returns true on the surviving `tg_origin=`, and `fmtg_landing_guard` then fails at `peer=$(fmtg_peer_get ...) || { printf 'no-paired-peer'; return 6; }`, so the merge refuses with "task <id> is linked to a Telegram request but no peer is paired" (exit 6). Nothing clears the origin: `fm-tg-pair.sh` never touches `state/*.meta`, `unlink` deliberately preserves `tg_origin` and now also requires a pinned peer via `require_project_match`, and `clear-publish` requires one too. Re-pairing does not help either, because `fmtg_peer_records_clear` already wiped the publish records. This also makes docs/configuration.md:422 ("the home returns to exactly its pre-Telegram behavior") false for any previously linked task. The narrow repair that keeps the immutability you asked for is to let the gate stand down only when it provably has nothing to enforce - no pinned peer, no configured token, and no publish record for that task - rather than to add another path that erases the origin.
- ℹ️ `AGENTS.md:92` - The always-loaded task-meta key list still reads "fm-tg-task.sh link appends tg_request=, tg_chat=, and tg_request_ts= for a Telegram-bridged task (section 15)". It omits `tg_origin=`, which this round introduced as the one key the landing gate actually reads and the one key no clearing path removes. An agent working from AGENTS.md alone would not know it exists, that `--final`/`unlink` deliberately keep it, or that removing it from a meta by hand switches the publish gate off. docs/configuration.md and the telegram-respond skill were both updated for it; this surface was not.

🔧 Fix: add audited per-task release for stranded Telegram-origin landings
1 warning still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-tg-lib.sh:1222` - The explicit release does not reach the pull-request landing path, so the stranding this round fixed is only half fixed. `fmtg_landing_guard` evaluates `[ -n "$rev" ] || { printf 'unresolved-revision'; return 1; }` at line 1222, before the release short-circuit at lines 1229-1233. Concrete sequence: (1) a task carries `tg_origin=`, the pairing is revoked, and the captain runs `bin/fm-tg-task.sh release <task> --yes --reason "..."`; (2) the task is landed with `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh <task> <pr-url>`; (3) `TG_HEAD=$(fmtg_meta_get "$META" pr_head)` is empty because `bin/fm-pr-check.sh` records `pr_head` only when the forge CLI can supply it (see its own comment at line 65 and the `NEEDS_GH_AUTH` bootstrap diagnostic for the unauthenticated-gh state); (4) the guard returns `unresolved-revision` (exit 1) and the merge refuses with "the exact revision that task <id> would land could not be resolved, so the confirmation cannot be checked" - a message about verifying a confirmation that, for a released task, does not exist, and with no next step left since the task is already released and a second release is refused. The local path is unaffected because `bin/fm-merge-local.sh` already hard-fails at line 45 if `refs/heads/fm/<id>` is missing, which is why `test_a_revoked_pairing_does_not_strand_a_linked_task` passes - it only exercises `run_local_merge`. The release branch never reads `$rev` (it returns before every revision comparison), so moving the short-circuit above the `[ -n "$rev" ]` check restores the stated design without weakening anything: a task with no release still refuses on an unresolvable revision exactly as today.

🔧 Fix: evaluate task release before landing revision requirements

body:
The continuity gate RECOVERY_SCRIPTS only had `fm-wake-drain.sh` and `fm-watch-arm.sh`. Copilot/Codex primaries use `fm-watch-checkpoint.sh` for foreground supervision, but the gate blocked it — deadlocking spawning, steering, and teardown while any worker was in flight.

- `bin/fm-continuity-command-policy.mjs`: add `fm-watch-checkpoint.sh` to RECOVERY_SCRIPTS
- `bin/fm-continuity-pretool-check.sh`: update denial message to mention both paths
- `tests/fm-continuity-pretool-check.test.sh`: add `expect_allow "watch checkpoint recovery"` test case

All 4 tests pass, lint clean.

title: feat(bin): federated fleet add-on with multi-account spawn and quota-aware routing
body:
## Intent Two follow-ups a closing review flagged on the fleet quota work (PR #1187). First: tests/federation/test_fleet_ops.sh consulted the live quota-axi in its register/route lifecycle cases, so it went red whenever the operator's real subscription window was exhausted (observed 4/16 failing, all green after the window reset) — now hermetic via a stubbed quota-axi, with lifecycle semantics still genuinely exercised and one bounded case deliberately retained on the real quota_now path so live coverage is not silently deleted. Second: bin/fm-fleet-lib.sh had grown to 816 lines, past the repo's 800-line convention — split at a verified one-directional seam (surface->KB crossings: zero) into a new leaf bin/fm-fleet-quota-lib.sh, leaving 393 and 460 lines. Behaviour-preserving: proven by the committed golden fixtures being compared, never regenerated. ## What Changed - **Federated multi-operator fleet** — new `bin/fm-fleet.sh` CLI over `bin/fm-fleet-lib.sh`, coordinating several OS operators through a shared, cross-uid-safe, git-backed KB: `init`/`register`/`heartbeat`/`leave`, `queue`/`claim`/`handoff`/`reap` under a lock, scope routing with heartbeat-freshness staleness (with a non-GNU `date` fallback), and `status`/`view`, plus `fm-fleet-wait.sh` and `fm-fleet-join.sh`. Documented in `docs/fleet-addon.md`, `docs/fleet-quickstart.md`, `docs/fleet-token-economy.md`, and the `federation`/`multi-account` agent skills. - **Per-spawn `--account` axis** — account registry, resolution and validation across three isolation methods (`bin/fm-accounts-lib.sh`, `fm-account-env.sh`, `fm-account-exec.sh`, `fm-spawn-acct.sh`), riding `fm-spawn`'s existing raw-launch escape hatch so no core FirstMate script is modified and no secret lands on argv. Adds a user-scoped on-demand prereq installer (`fm-accounts-prereq.sh`) and one reviewable idempotent root step (`scripts/fleet-root-prereq.sh`). - **Quota/pace surface layer** — authed Copilot and Cursor usage readers (`bin/quota-copilot-usage.sh`, `bin/quota-cursor-usage.sh`, `bin/quota-sources/*`) feeding per-surface headroom, budget gating, and model-family → surface failover picking; that layer was split out of `fm-fleet-lib.sh` into a new leaf `bin/fm-fleet-quota-lib.sh` at a one-directional seam, bringing both files back under the repo's 800-line convention. Covered by `tests/federation/*.sh` with committed golden fixtures; `test_fleet_ops.sh` stubs `quota-axi` so lifecycle cases no longer depend on the operator's real subscription window, with one bounded case deliberately left on the live path. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: All three previously-flagged warnings are verified durably fixed with their failure sequences reconstructed and no remaining reachable path, the intent-scoped hermetic test and verbatim library split are untouched and re-verified (442 + 460 lines, goldens unchanged, budget golden output and exit code preserved), and the sole remaining finding is a single test fixture with no product impact. ## Testing Ran the four federation suites relevant to the two changed areas (fleet_ops, quota_surfaces, fleet, fleet_guards — all green), then went beyond pass/fail to demonstrate each claim end-to-end. Use a stamp that is inside the `[0-9TZ:-]` charset but off-shape — e.g. `s/\(FL-11.*\)@[0-9TZ:-]\{1,\}/\1@2000-01-01/` — which passes the candidate guard, fails the new `^....-..-..T..:..:..Z$` shape check, and would have been reaped by the old `date -u -d "2000-01-01"` path.
⚠️ **Test** - 2 infos - ℹ️ `tests/federation/test_fleet_ops.sh:180` - The deliberately-retained live case (`quota_now (LIVE, real quota-axi)`) still fails when the real quota-axi HANGS rather than answers: `FAIL: quota_now LIVE (rc=124 got '')`. The `timeout 10` bound works correctly (suite finished in 11s, not 600s), and this is distinct from the exhausted-window false red the change fixes — a hang is a genuinely broken environment, and going red on it is what "live coverage not silently deleted" means. Recording it only so the one remaining live-red mode is known; no change requested. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-fleet-lib.sh:1` - The intent states the split left `bin/fm-fleet-lib.sh` at 393 lines. That was exact at the split commit 282908c, but the later review commit 007cc36 added the non-GNU date fallback and other fixes, so at the target commit the file is 442 lines (quota lib unchanged at 460). Still well under the 800-line cap, so the stated goal holds — only the specific number would be stale if it is carried verbatim into the PR description. - `bash tests/federation/test_fleet_ops.sh` — normal environment, real quota-axi present (ALL PASS, 24 assertions) - `PATH=<exhausted-quota-axi>:$PATH bash tests/federation/.pre-hermetic-fleet-ops.tmp.sh` — pre-hermetic test from `git show 03ba378:tests/federation/test_fleet_ops.sh` under a stub reporting 0% remaining, reproducing the reported 4/16 failure - `PATH=<exhausted-quota-axi>:$PATH bash tests/federation/test_fleet_ops.sh` — fixed suite under the identical exhausted stub (ALL PASS) - `PATH=<PATH-minus-~/.local/bin> bash tests/federation/test_fleet_ops.sh` — quota-axi absent entirely (ALL PASS); same PATH against the pre-hermetic copy for contrast - `PATH=<sentinel-7.5-quota-axi>:$PATH bash tests/federation/test_fleet_ops.sh` — stub-isolation proof: lifecycle cases read 42/2/80 from SUITE_STUB while `fm_fleet_quota_now` on the real path returns 7.5 - `PATH=<hanging-quota-axi>:$PATH bash tests/federation/test_fleet_ops.sh` and `PATH=<nonzero-exit-quota-axi>:$PATH ...` — boundedness of the retained live case (11s elapsed under a 600s hang; garbage/nonzero exit passes as '-') - `bash tests/federation/test_quota_surfaces.sh` — 62 assertions including the seven G5 golden byte-comparisons, with FM_TEST_REGEN_GOLDEN deliberately unset - `bash tests/federation/test_fleet.sh` and `bash tests/federation/test_fleet_guards.sh` — KB/route/claim and guard suites against the post-split lib - Manual A/B: reconstructed the pre-split tree via `git show 1850451:bin/fm-fleet.sh` + `git show 1850451:bin/fm-fleet-lib.sh` and diffed `fm-fleet.sh quota|models|pick grok|pick claude|pick kimi|pick bogus|budget` pre-split vs HEAD under one shared stub env - Manual check: `diff <(git show 59ccbc9:tests/federation/golden/v2-*.golden) tests/federation/golden/v2-*.golden` plus `git status --porcelain tests/federation/golden/` after the suite run, confirming goldens were never regenerated - Manual leaf check: `bash -c '. bin/fm-fleet-quota-lib.sh; declare -F | grep -c fm_fleet_; fm_fleet_quota_now; fm_fleet_budget_ok; fm_fleet_pick_surface claude'` with fm-fleet-lib.sh never sourced, and the reverse consumer-contract check - `wc -l` on `git show 282908c:bin/fm-fleet-lib.sh` (393), `git show 1850451:bin/fm-fleet-lib.sh` (816), and HEAD's 442 + 460
⚠️ **Document** - 1 info - ℹ️ `.agents/skills/federation/SKILL.md:37` - Out-of-scope consolidation worth a follow-up: the fleet KB contract is stated in full twice — docs/fleet-addon.md "Shared KB" (maintainer-architecture) and .agents/skills/federation/SKILL.md "KB files" (agent-runtime) both restate the operators.md columns, the backlog.md sections, the item-line format, and the events.log TSV shape. The one-owner rule forbids two full copies, and this branch already shows the predicted drift: the corrected handoff semantics (a queued item is moved to ## Claimed as status:claimed) landed only in the skill, so handoff's state machine now lives in an agent-runtime surface while the sibling claim protocol lives in the maintainer-architecture surface. Reducing the skill's KB-files section to a pointer at docs/fleet-addon.md (keeping only the routing-eligibility rule agents genuinely need inline) would fix this, but it rewrites prose this change did not make stale, so I left it out of scope rather than multiplying edits here.

title: feat(skills): vendor the /watch video skill for the whole fleet
body:
## Intent Vendor the third-party /watch video skill (bradautomates/claude-video, upstream skills/watch @ 83da59fa78c3eee9e20f515fe75c438bb5166efd, v0.2.0, MIT) into firstmate's .agents/skills/watch/ so every firstmate home and clone gets it, replacing a machine-local user-scope install at ~/.claude/skills/watch/ that does not travel. The skill gives the agent a video input it otherwise lacks: it downloads with yt-dlp, extracts frames with ffmpeg, and pulls a transcript from captions with a Whisper API fallback. Key decisions the captain made deliberately, which a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: 1. THE VENDORED FILES ARE A VERBATIM COPY AND MUST NOT BE RESTYLED. The task was explicitly 'copy, do not re-derive' from a pre-tested staged package that was already verified working end to end on this machine. SKILL.md is kept BYTE-IDENTICAL to upstream below its vendoring banner comment. This repo's Markdown house style (one full sentence per line, plain dash '-' instead of em dash, see the 'Repo style rules' in .agents/skills/firstmate-coding-guidelines) is DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED to SKILL.md, LICENSE, or the Python scripts. Every such deviation would turn a future upstream sync into a merge conflict, which is the entire reason the banner exists. If a review or lint finding proposes reformatting, rewrapping, de-em-dashing, rewording, refactoring, adding type hints, fixing style, or otherwise editing anything inside .agents/skills/watch/, that finding is wrong for a vendored file and must not be applied. The same applies to code-quality findings about the upstream Python (scripts/*.py): they are upstream's to fix, not ours, and patching them locally breaks the sync contract. The only firstmate-authored content in that directory is the frontmatter metadata block (metadata.internal: true and the vendored-from pin) and the HTML banner comment directly below it. 2. Upstream's scripts/build-skill.sh and .skillignore were intentionally dropped as dev-only build tooling. The MIT LICENSE is intentionally retained and must stay for redistribution compliance. 3. The banner documents a real, verified operational trap rather than being decorative: scripts/frames.py passes ffmpeg's -vsync flag, which was removed from ffmpeg master builds (reproduced on N-125781-gacf6b520c1), so frame extraction needs a 7.x or 8.x release build. 4. AGENTS.md TRIGGER PLACEMENT WAS A DELIBERATE CHOICE, not an oversight. Firstmate's trigger-hygiene rule requires every new skill to declare a load trigger inline in AGENTS.md. Section 13 was explicitly ruled out because it is stated to be agent-only ('These skills are not captain-invocable'), and this skill is captain-invocable (user-invocable: true). The trigger was therefore placed as exactly ONE line in section 3, appended to the existing capability-tool paragraph that already routes gh-axi / chrome-devtools-axi / lavish-axi, since that is the repo's only 'capability to tool' declaration point. The one-line limit was an explicit constraint because AGENTS.md token cost is paid by every session of every fleet member. 5. A test was added by EXTENDING the existing tests/fm-instruction-owners.test.sh rather than creating a new runner, per the repo rule to colocate and extend. It deliberately asserts only the durable vendoring invariants a future edit could quietly break (LICENSE present and MIT, the upstream commit pin, the refresh banner, the bundled scripts, exactly one AGENTS.md trigger line, and absence from the agent-only list). It deliberately does NOT snapshot SKILL.md's contents, because a content snapshot would lock in bytes and break on every legitimate upstream refresh, which is the opposite of the goal. Verification already run and green on this branch: bin/fm-lint.sh (shellcheck 0.11.0), bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh, bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage, and tests/fm-instruction-owners.test.sh. ## What Changed - Vendors the third-party `/watch` video skill (bradautomates/claude-video @ `83da59f`, MIT) into `.agents/skills/watch/` as a verbatim copy — `SKILL.md` plus seven `scripts/*.py` and the upstream `LICENSE` — so every firstmate home and clone gets the video capability instead of relying on a machine-local user-scope install. The only firstmate-authored content is the frontmatter (`metadata.internal: true` and the upstream commit pin) and an HTML banner recording the vendoring contract, the first-run install/egress/key-source consent gate, the `rm -rf` cleanup caveat, and the verified ffmpeg `-vsync` version trap. Upstream's dev-only `build-skill.sh` and `.skillignore` were dropped. - Wires the skill into the repo's contracts: a one-line `/watch` load trigger in `AGENTS.md` section 3 (section 13 is agent-only, and this skill is captain-invocable), a `README.md` built-in-skills row plus a corrected `metadata.internal` rationale and a license note, an `agent-runtime` entry in the documentation-audience inventory, and a vendored-material exemption from the repo's Markdown and code-style rules in `firstmate-coding-guidelines` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`. - Extends `tests/fm-instruction-owners.test.sh` with the durable vendoring invariants (MIT LICENSE present, upstream commit pin, refresh banner, all bundled scripts parse under `py_compile`, exactly one `AGENTS.md` trigger line, absent from the agent-only list) rather than snapshotting `SKILL.md`, and broadens `bin/fm-test-run.sh`'s changed-path mapping from `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` to `.agents/skills/*` so a future upstream refresh of the Python scripts still selects tests instead of aborting. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is additive and well-bounded - a vendored skill directory plus one AGENTS.md line, one README row, one style-guideline clause, one audience-inventory entry, one changed-path mapping, and one colocated test - and I verified every integration point (audience check scope and link scan, families_for_changed_path arm ordering and family membership, test helper semantics, file modes, pycache suppression) plus the factual accuracy of every banner claim against the vendored Python; the only residual items are two informational documentation-durability notes in firstmate-authored text. ## Testing Ran the new vendored-watch contract test, the full changed-file selection (31 scripts, all passing, one expected gate skip) and the coverage guard, then demonstrated the skill itself: a synthetic four-scene video was processed by the bundled scripts into four correctly timestamped frames that were read back as images, and the same run succeeded from a fresh clone with an isolated HOME, showing the skill now ships with the repo rather than depending on the machine-local install. Byte-comparison against the pinned upstream commit confirmed the scripts, LICENSE and SKILL.md body are verbatim, and five targeted mutations in a scratch clone each tripped the new guard with its intended message. The only unverified claim is the ffmpeg master-build `-vsync` failure, which would require installing an ffmpeg master build; extraction was confirmed working on the recommended 7.1.5 release. - Evidence: Frames the skill extracted from the test video (contact sheet, 2x2, t=00:00/05/10/15) (local file: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYN7WXQYH8D2BPR0VHGK53Z9/watch-frames-contact-sheet.png)

Run `python3 /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYN7WXQYH8D2BPR0VHGK53Z9/clone-check/.agents/skills/watch/scripts/setup.py` to enable Whisper, then re-run._ --- _Work dir: `/tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYN7WXQYH8D2BPR0VHGK53Z9/clone-run` — delete when done._ (exit 0) $ ls /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYN7WXQYH8D2BPR0VHGK53Z9/fake-home # untouched: no user-scope install needed (empty) ```
Evidence: Fresh clone carries the skill on the harness discovery path $ ls .agents/skills/watch .agents/skills/watch/scripts LICENSE SKILL.md scripts/ config.py download.py frames.py setup.py transcribe.py watch.py whisper.py $ readlink .claude/skills -> ../.agents/skills $ ls .claude/skills/watch/SKILL.md -> present ```text === fresh clone of firstmate at 581c02e === $ ls .agents/skills/watch .agents/skills/watch/scripts scripts/ LICENSE 1.0K SKILL.md 25.4K config.py 2.1K download.py 5.3K frames.py 25.7K setup.py 11.8K transcribe.py 2.8K watch.py 16.1K whisper.py 16.6K $ readlink .claude/skills # harness discovery path ../.agents/skills $ ls .claude/skills/watch/SKILL.md .claude/skills/watch/SKILL.md 25.4K ```

## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 2 infos - 🚨 `docs/documentation-audiences.json:1` - The vendored `.agents/skills/watch/SKILL.md` is a tracked `*.md` file but was not added to the audience inventory's `surfaces` array. `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` computes `tracked - classified` over the fixed `*.md` scope and fails with `unclassified: .agents/skills/watch/SKILL.md`; `tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh::test_repository_inventory_passes` runs that same check against the real repo, so CI fails. Fix: add `{"path": ".agents/skills/watch/SKILL.md", "audience": "agent-runtime"}`, matching every other `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` entry. - ⚠️ `tests/fm-instruction-owners.test.sh:62` - `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed` aborts on this branch. In `families_for_changed_path`, `.agents/skills/watch/scripts/*.py` matches neither the `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` case nor any earlier case, so it falls to the `*)` branch, which greps tests for the literal path. Only `watch.py` (asserted with a literal path on line 66) and `LICENSE` (line 17) match; `frames.py`, `transcribe.py`, `whisper.py`, `download.py`, `setup.py`, and `config.py` are built from the loop variable and match nothing, producing `die "no changed-test mapping for source path: .agents/skills/watch/scripts/frames.py"` before any test runs. This recurs on every upstream refresh, which is precisely the documented maintenance path. Fix either by adding a `.agents/skills/*/scripts/*)` case mapping to `pure-contract-unit`, or by asserting each script with its literal path instead of a loop variable. - ⚠️ `AGENTS.md:154` - The trigger line does not mention that the skill's first run executes an installer that runs `brew install ffmpeg yt-dlp` unattended on macOS (scripts/setup.py `_install_macos`) and writes `~/.config/watch/.env`, nor that extracted audio is uploaded to Groq/OpenAI when a key is configured. AGENTS.md section 3 otherwise requires the captain's consent in the current session before any install, and this vendoring makes the skill fleet-wide. Consider a short clause on the trigger line, or a note in the vendoring banner, requiring captain approval before running the installer. - ⚠️ `README.md:167` - README's "Built-in skills" section states "Firstmate ships these user-invocable built-in skills" and tables `/afk`, `/ahoy`, `/bearings`, `/updatefirstmate`, and `/stow`. The watch skill declares `user-invocable: true` and is captain-invoked as `/watch`, so the table is now incomplete and readers will not discover it. Decide whether to advertise the vendored third-party skill (with its external ffmpeg/yt-dlp dependency) in the public list, and add a row if so. - ℹ️ `.agents/skills/watch/scripts/whisper.py:95` - Upstream's key lookup falls back to `Path.cwd() / ".env"` after `~/.config/watch/.env`. If /watch is invoked with the working directory inside a project clone that has its own `.env` containing `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `GROQ_API_KEY`, that project's key is silently used to transcribe the captain's audio. Vendored code, so no local patch: worth knowing as an operational trap, mitigated by invoking from a controlled directory or by exporting an explicit key. 🔧 Fix: classify vendored watch skill and gate its first run 3 infos still open: - ℹ️ `README.md:185` - The new `/watch` table row (line 174) describes a vendored third-party skill that is "not firstmate's own", but the Two-tier skill layout paragraph six lines below still asserts of `.agents/skills/`: "Every one of these assumes a live firstmate home and is meaningless, or actively misleading, installed anywhere else, so each carries `metadata.internal: true`". The watch skill is generic and works standalone, so that stated rationale no longer covers every entry. Marking it internal is still defensible (it avoids redistributing third-party code through firstmate's installer), but the reason given is now wrong for one of the listed skills. Suggest a short clause acknowledging the vendored exception and why it is still flagged internal. - ℹ️ `.agents/skills/watch/SKILL.md:112` - The first-run consent gate exists only in the AGENTS.md trigger line and the banner at the top of this file. The operative Step 0 exit-code table the agent actually follows says "Run installer" / "Run installer to scaffold `.env`" / "Run installer, then encourage a key" with no consent step, and the prose two lines below adds "The installer is idempotent - safe to re-run". On macOS that installer path runs `brew install ffmpeg yt-dlp` unattended (scripts/setup.py `_install_macos`). The banner is firstmate-authored and editable, so one added sentence there - naming the exit-code table explicitly, e.g. "when the Step 0 table below says Run installer, stop and get the captain's word first" - would bind the gate to the step where it fires, rather than relying on the agent carrying the banner forward through the procedure. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-instruction-owners.test.sh:63` - The vendoring test asserts only that each `scripts/*.py` file exists, and `bin/fm-lint.sh` covers shell only, so nothing in the repo checks that the vendored Python is even parseable. The documented maintenance path is a periodic re-copy from upstream, where a truncated or partial copy would land silently and only surface when the captain next runs /watch. A `python3 -m py_compile` sweep over the seven scripts inside this existing test is a durable invariant (it does not snapshot content, so a legitimate upstream refresh still passes) and would catch a botched refresh at CI time. 🔧 Fix: bind watch consent to Step 0 and parse-check vendored scripts 3 issues (1 warning, 2 infos) still open: - ⚠️ `.agents/skills/watch/SKILL.md:32` - The banner's consent binding names only the Step 0 exit-code table ("Wherever the Step 0 exit-code table below directs you to run the installer (exits 2, 3, and 4), stop and get the captain's word first"). That table is only reached from the `--check` path, which SKILL.md line 103 reserves for follow-up calls in a session. The genuine first run uses `--json` (line 86), and its `first_run: true` branch at lines 95-99 independently instructs "run the installer first" and "Run the installer to remediate" without referencing the exit-code table at all; Failure modes at line 277 adds a third install directive ("run `python3 \"${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/setup.py\"` (auto-installs ffmpeg/yt-dlp via brew on macOS)"). So on a real first invocation with missing binaries, an agent following Step 0 runs the unattended `brew install ffmpeg yt-dlp` via `cmd_install`/`_install_macos` without the binding sentence ever applying - the exact scenario the binding was added for. The general gate at banner line 27 and the AGENTS.md trigger still cover it in spirit, so this is an incomplete binding rather than a missing gate. Fix inside the firstmate-authored banner only (no upstream bytes change): broaden the sentence to every Step 0 and Failure-modes directive to run the installer, naming the `--json` `first_run: true` branch and the Failure modes bullet alongside the exit-code table. - ℹ️ `.agents/skills/watch/SKILL.md:236` - Step 5 instructs the agent to delete the working directory with `rm -rf <dir>`. By default that directory is a `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="watch-")` path (scripts/watch.py:86), which is harmless, but `--out-dir` (watch.py:83-84) makes it any caller-chosen path, and the deletion removes whatever else lives there. Firstmate treats destructive actions as a captain boundary and forbids writing to project clones, and the banner - the only firstmate-authored surface in this directory - documents the install, egress, key-source, and ffmpeg traps but says nothing about this agent-executed `rm -rf`. Consider one banner line noting that Step 5's cleanup is only safe on the default temp working directory and must not be run against an `--out-dir` the captain supplied. Upstream text stays untouched. - ℹ️ `README.md:177` - The new table row sits under "Firstmate ships these user-invocable built-in skills" with the note that "codex uses the same names with `$`, such as `$afk`", implying the row works across firstmate's verified harnesses (claude, codex, opencode, pi, pi-signed, grok, kimi). The vendored skill declares `allowed-tools: Bash, Read, AskUserQuestion` and drives its first-run key and detail-preference prompts through `AskUserQuestion` (SKILL.md:129, 131, 277). It is the only skill in `.agents/skills/` that references that tool - a grep across every other SKILL.md returns nothing. The flow degrades rather than breaks (a non-Claude agent would just ask in prose), so this is a documentation-accuracy note, not a defect: decide whether the row deserves a short "prompts assume Claude's question tool" caveat. 🔧 Fix: bind watch install consent to every path and flag rm -rf trap 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `.agents/skills/firstmate-coding-guidelines/SKILL.md:91` - `.agents/skills/watch/` is now shared tracked material under AGENTS.md section 1, so any future firstmate-repo task touching it loads `firstmate-coding-guidelines` first - and that skill's "Repo style rules" section (lines 92-95: one full sentence per line in tracked Markdown, never wrap multiple sentences onto one physical line, plain dash never an em dash) has no vendored-material exception. Neither does CONTRIBUTING.md; a grep for "vendor", "upstream copy", or "byte-identical" across both returns nothing. The vendoring contract's only protection today is the HTML banner inside SKILL.md itself, and the seven `scripts/*.py` files carry no marker at all - `bin/fm-lint.sh` is shell-only, so nothing flags them either. A future agent briefed on a style sweep, a lint cleanup, or a Markdown-rule pass will restyle SKILL.md's em dashes and multi-sentence lines and "improve" the Python, silently turning the next upstream re-copy into a merge conflict - precisely the failure the banner exists to prevent, but the banner only protects the file it lives in. The new test asserts the banner's presence, not that upstream bytes are unchanged, so CI would not catch it either. Suggested shape: one line under Repo style rules naming `.agents/skills/watch/` as vendored material exempt from the Markdown and code-style rules below its banner. Note the standing decision from the prior round routes further vendoring-framing findings to a backlog item rather than this PR - this one sits in a firstmate-authored file outside the vendored directory, so it is the captain's call whether it lands here or gets filed. 🔧 Fix: exempt vendored material from repo style rules 2 infos still open: - ℹ️ `.agents/skills/watch/SKILL.md:76` - The FFMPEG VERSION TRAP closes with "This fleet runs n7.1.5 installed to ~/.local/bin, verified end-to-end." That is one machine's install path and exact version, recorded in shared tracked material that ships to every firstmate home and every clone. The durable half of the note is correct and portable (-vsync was removed from ffmpeg master, reproduced on N-125781-gacf6b520c1; pin a 7.x or 8.x release), and I verified frames.py does pass -vsync at lines 256 and 615. Only the install-path and pinned-version sentence rots: another home reading "verified end-to-end" for "this fleet" may skip checking its own ffmpeg, hit a master build, and get "Unrecognized option 'vsync'" with zero frames. The repo's own hygiene rule against temporary paths and moving versions in durable records is the relevant precedent. Suggested shape: keep the trap and the release-build requirement, and either drop the machine-specific sentence or mark it explicitly as one home's verification datum rather than a fleet property. Firstmate-authored banner text, so no upstream bytes change. - ℹ️ `docs/documentation-audiences.json:178` - Adding .agents/skills/watch/SKILL.md to the inventory was necessary and correct (bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh fails on any unclassified tracked *.md), but classification also enrolls the file in the checker's local-link validation pass, which walks every tracked .md and fails on an unresolved relative link. That creates a forward-looking conflict with the byte-identical contract: if a future upstream refresh adds a relative markdown link to a file the vendoring procedure deliberately drops - the banner names scripts/build-skill.sh and .skillignore - the check fails and the only remedies are patching vendored text or retaining a dropped file. There is no exemption hatch, because REQUIRED_TRACKED_PATTERNS is asserted fixed at *.md so the file cannot be de-scoped. Nothing is broken today: the current SKILL.md contains no markdown or HTML links at all, and .agents/skills/watch/LICENSE is out of scope (no extension). Suggested shape: one clause in the banner's refresh procedure telling the next refresher to expect this, so the collision is a known step rather than a surprise CI failure.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-instruction-owners.test.sh` - new vendored-watch contract test passes - `bash bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed --base b6e351d` - 31 selected scripts, 0 failed, 1 expected gate skip - `bash bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` - FM_TEST_COVERAGE ok total=102 - Manual E2E: built a 4-scene 20s clip with ffmpeg, ran `python3 .agents/skills/watch/scripts/setup.py --json` (Step 0 preflight) then `python3 .agents/skills/watch/scripts/watch.py sample-video.mp4 --no-whisper --out-dir watch-run`, and read all four emitted JPEG frames back as images (Step 3) - Manual E2E from a fresh clone: `git clone` of the branch, then `HOME=<throwaway> python3 <clone>/.agents/skills/watch/scripts/watch.py sample-video.mp4 --detail efficient --no-whisper` - identical report with no user-scope install touched - Upstream parity: `curl` of bradautomates/claude-video@83da59fa78c3eee9e20f515fe75c438bb5166efd + `cmp` on all 7 scripts and LICENSE, plus a unified diff of SKILL.md below the vendoring banner - Local parity: `diff -r -x __pycache__ ~/.claude/skills/watch .agents/skills/watch` - only the added banner block differs - Mutation check of the new guard in a scratch clone: removed LICENSE, truncated scripts/frames.py to invalid syntax, duplicated the AGENTS.md trigger, stripped the vendored-from pin, and added `watch` to the agent-only reference list - each produced its intended `not ok` line - Selection-mapping demo: `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed --base HEAD --list` with only `.agents/skills/watch/scripts/frames.py` modified, run against both the target and the pre-change `bin/fm-test-run.sh`
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: Supervision: heartbeat stops reconciling/dispatching when the main-home fleet goes quiet (no periodic force-reconcile)
body:
# Firstmate: a quiet main-home fleet starves the heartbeat reconcile/dispatch loop

**Reporter:** Joseph (via firstmate self-diagnosis)
**Date:** 2026-07-28
**Component:** supervision — `bin/fm-watch.sh` heartbeat, Claude Stop-hook mode
**Severity:** medium (silent — work completes and decisions become ready, but neither surfaces)

---

## One-line

When a firstmate home's main-home fleet goes quiet — most work delegated to secondmates and/or an external runner that doesn't write to `state/*.status` — the heartbeat stops producing firstmate turns, so the two heartbeat duties in AGENTS.md §8/§10 (reconcile the fleet + re-evaluate/dispatch queued work) simply never run until the captain sends a message.

## Symptoms (operator-reported)

1. **Parallelism stopped.** No new crewmate tabs spawn; firstmate stopped proactively dispatching queued/ready work. The operator's prior experience was "massive parallel work by default."
2. **Tasks strand silently.** Completed work and captain-ready decisions accumulate without ever being surfaced or reconciled off `in_flight`.

## Root cause (code)

`bin/fm-watch.sh` (HEAD `a5fe1bc`):

- The heartbeat is a **fleet-scan backstop that surfaces only an "unsurfaced captain-relevant" status** (header, ~line 40). `heartbeat_scan_finds_actionable()` (~line 531) delegates to `scan_captain_relevant_statuses "$STATE"` (~lines 520/538), which iterates `"$STATE"/*.status` (`scan_signals`, ~line 418). The main loop only surfaces on `elif heartbeat_scan_finds_actionable` (~line 1001).
- Cadence: `HEARTBEAT=600` base, **backing off to `HEARTBEAT_MAX=7200` (2h)** when nothing surfaces (~lines 96–97).
- **There is no periodic force-reconcile path.** The heartbeat is a *status-verb change detector*, not a *backlog/fleet reconciler*: it never reads `data/backlog.md`, never re-derives whether an `in_flight` task is actually finished, and never re-evaluates a queued task's gate.

Therefore the §8/§10 heartbeat duties only run when firstmate actually *gets a heartbeat turn* — and a turn only fires when some crew emits an **unsurfaced captain-relevant status verb** in `state/*.status`. Two whole classes of work emit no such verb and are invisible:

- **Backlog / coordination items with no live crew** (queued work whose gate cleared; a firstmate-owned tracking task; a decision awaiting the captain). No status file → nothing to scan.
- **External or out-of-home channels** that don't write to this home's `state/*.status` (here: an external Electron runner whose status lives in its own worktree; also secondmate-internal work, by design).

When the main-home fleet is quiet — which is exactly what happens once most work is delegated to secondmates and an external runner — every heartbeat reads "no change," backs off toward 2h, and firstmate receives **zero** turns until the operator interacts.

## Evidence

- **Watcher triage log:** 28 consecutive heartbeats (10:07–14:57 local, 2026-07-28) all logged `absorbed heartbeat (no captain-relevant change)`. Zero firstmate heartbeat turns in ~5 hours.
- **Non-external stranding (proves the mechanism is general, not integration-specific):** `fm-captain-brief-queue` (`kind=task`, `repo=firstmate`) has sat `in_flight` since 2026-07-26 with no crew (no `.meta`, no `.status`). Two of its five briefs were never delivered; it only advances on operator interaction. A pure backlog item the heartbeat structurally cannot see.
- **External-channel stranding:** one manual reconcile scan of the external runner's worktrees surfaced 6 terminal/decision states (3 `needs-decision`, 3 `done`) that never reached the operator, because that runner writes to `<its-worktree>/.fm/status.log`, which the watcher never scans.

## Scope — what is ours vs. the question for you

- **Ours (local, not asking you to support):** our external runner dispatches outside `fm-spawn`, so it writes no `state/<id>.meta`/`.status`; supervision was never wired to it. We can fix this locally by having our liaison register a `.meta` + a `check.sh`/status bridge the watcher polls. Not a firstmate defect.
- **The genuine question for firstmate:** even ignoring the external runner, the heartbeat is purely event-driven and backs off to 2h with no forced reconcile, and it never re-derives backlog truth. **Is a quiet-but-nonempty home meant to strand its backlog work until the operator pokes it?** The "parallel by default" experience appears to assume a *noisy* main-home fleet; once an operator delegates most work to secondmates + external tools, the main home goes quiet and the proactive reconcile/dispatch loop silently stops. That regime seems increasingly common as secondmates get adopted.

## Possible directions (for discussion, not prescriptive)

- **A — Opt-in floor cadence:** `FM_HEARTBEAT_FORCE_RECONCILE=<secs>` delivers a firstmate turn on a fixed floor even when the scan finds nothing, so §8/§10 run periodically. Token-aware / capped.
- **B — Backlog-drift as actionable:** broaden the heartbeat scan to flag `in_flight` tasks whose recorded endpoint is dead/absent (or which have no endpoint at all) as actionable, so orphaned/quiet work surfaces without needing a status verb.
- **C — Document the contract:** if a quiet main home is *intended* to be operator-driven, document that delegating everything out of the main home suppresses proactive reconciliation, so operators keep a reconcile lever.

## Reproduction

1. In a home, create an `in_flight` backlog task with no live crew (no `.meta`/`.status`).
2. Keep the supervised fleet quiet — no crew emitting a captain-relevant status verb.
3. Observe: heartbeats absorb, back off toward 2h; firstmate never re-evaluates the backlog or dispatches the queued item; it advances only when the operator sends a message.

## Notes

- herdr is healthy here (0.7.5, protocol 17 both sides); this is not a backend issue.
- This home is 7 commits behind `origin/main` (`b6e351d`) due to a separate local self-update block; none of those 7 commits touch the heartbeat/reconcile path, so being behind is not the cause.

## Intent Wire fm-spawn.sh and fm-teardown.sh to auto-enroll/deregister crewmates in Parlay's chat panel via parlay listen/agent-down, best-effort and never load-bearing, with the pid-kill unconditional and only the parlay agent-down network call gated on parlay being on PATH. ## What Changed - `fm-spawn.sh` now best-effort enrolls each newly spawned crewmate in Parlay's chat panel (`parlay listen --agent`), recording the background listener's pid in `state/.parlay-listen-pid`; enrollment is skipped when `parlay` isn't on PATH and is never load-bearing for spawn success. - `fm-teardown.sh` unconditionally kills the recorded listener pid during cleanup, and separately calls `parlay agent-down` to deregister the crewmate only when `parlay` is present on PATH. - `fm-session-lock-lib.sh` resolves a Claude background-spare process's ancestry up to the outermost `claude` pid so session-lock detection isn't confused by spare processes. - Adds test coverage for the new Parlay enrollment/deregistration paths (`tests/fm-spawn-parlay.test.sh`, additions to `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` and `tests/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.test.sh`), updates `AGENTS.md`/`docs/sessionstart-nudge.md`/`docs/verification/supervision.md`, and renames an array variable in `tests/lib.sh`'s `fm_path_without` to clear shellcheck SC2178/SC2128. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a small, well-isolated, purely best-effort addition (backgrounded parlay listen call at spawn, unconditional pid-kill plus PATH-gated agent-down at teardown) that never blocks or fails spawn/teardown on parlay's absence or failure, mirrors the existing grok/kimi turnend-auth cleanup pattern, is placed correctly relative to other post-launch/pre-cleanup steps, and is covered by new tests for both the present-on-PATH and genuinely-absent-from-PATH cases. ## Testing `Ran the existing dedicated Parlay test suites (fm-spawn-parlay.test.sh and the full fm-teardown.test.sh, including its two parlay-specific cases) with all tests passing, then produced a manual CLI transcript exercising the real fm-spawn.sh -> fm-teardown.sh lifecycle against a call-logging fake parlay binary, confirming enrollment, unconditional pid-kill (with and without parlay on PATH), and the gated agent-down call all behave as intended; no issues found.`

title: fix(bin): tighten crewmate brief guidance on project memory, PR bodies, and GitHub reads
body:
## Intent Fix the crewmate brief scaffold so generic project-memory guidance is conditional and explicitly subordinate to task-specific constraints, retaining its usefulness without allowing a run-helper versus never-run contradiction. For PR-producing ship briefs whose task names a GitHub issue, require a closing keyword in the PR body while stating plainly that GitHub may ignore it and firstmate verifies issue state after merge regardless; omit PR-only wording from local-only tasks. Prefer gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/... REST reads over gh pr and gh issue subcommands, and forbid workers from polling merge-queue state because firstmate already tracks it; apply worker guidance to ship and scout briefs while keeping secondmate charters sensible. Keep generated output concise, test through the rendered fm-brief CLI seam with TDD coverage for ship, scout, secondmate, and delivery-mode behavior, and do not add an agent co-author. The PR body must include a Completion Evidence section stating what was proved and what was not proved. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-brief.sh` now makes the ship brief's project-memory section conditional: task-specific project-memory constraints take precedence, a task-level prohibition is decisive, and the `fm-ensure-agents-md.sh` helper step is reached only via the trailing `Otherwise, ...` branch — removing the run-helper-versus-never-run contradiction. - PR-producing ship briefs (both `direct-PR` and `no-mistakes` modes) emit a standalone `**PR body:**` step under Definition of done, before the step that creates the PR, requiring the closing keyword on its own line at the end of the body (never in the title) while stating plainly that GitHub may ignore it and firstmate verifies issue state after merge. Local-only briefs omit the step and keep their Rules list contiguous. - Rule 3 of ship and scout briefs was replaced with shared `GITHUB_READ_GUIDANCE`: prefer `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/...` REST paths over `gh pr`/`gh issue` subcommands, keep gh-axi/chrome-devtools-axi for other operations, and never poll merge-queue state. Secondmate charters are unaffected. - `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` adds `test_issue_linked_ship_requires_pr_closing_keyword` and `test_github_rest_guidance_targets_crewmate_briefs`, and strengthens `test_ship_project_memory_wording` with ordering assertions. ## Completion Evidence **Proved:** - `bash tests/fm-brief.test.sh` is green at head (18 checks), including the two new tests and the strengthened project-memory test. - TDD red state was demonstrated: restoring `bin/fm-brief.sh` from base `b6e351d` fails the suite with `not ok - project-memory contract did not subordinate the generic guidance to task-specific constraints` (exit 1); restoring head leaves `git status --porcelain` empty. - Behavior was exercised through the rendered `bin/fm-brief.sh` CLI seam for all four shapes — no-mistakes ship, direct-PR ship, local-only ship, scout, and a secondmate charter — and compared phrase-by-phrase against briefs rendered from the base commit. - Manual inspection confirms the local-only brief contains no `closing keyword` / `PR body` wording and no numbering gap between rules 3 and 4, and the secondmate charter contains neither `Never poll merge-queue state` nor the `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/...` guidance. - `git log --format='%B' b6e351d..ca36646 | grep -i co-authored` returns nothing: no agent co-author trailer on any commit. - Adjacent suites `tests/fm-instruction-owners.test.sh`, `tests/fm-ask-user-authority.test.sh`, and `tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh` pass. **Not proved:** - The brief now tells crewmates that "firstmate verifies issue state after merge regardless", but no such duty exists in the repo today: `AGENTS.md` section 7 records no issue-verification step, and no `bin/` script (`fm-pr-check.sh`, `fm-pr-merge.sh`, `fm-pr-poll.sh`) reads GitHub issue state. The wording is required by the stated intent, so it was kept, but its owner is undocumented and unimplemented — a follow-up must either implement and document the duty in `AGENTS.md` section 7 or soften the wording. This branch does not change firstmate behavior. - Lint did not run to completion in the pipeline (exit code 127, tool unavailable), so no linter verdict was obtained for these files. - No end-to-end run was performed in which a crewmate actually authored a PR body from a generated brief; coverage is at the rendered-brief text level only. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The final commit only reorders generated brief prose within the Definition-of-done block and tightens the corresponding CLI-seam assertion; re-rendering every delivery mode confirms all prior findings are resolved, no existing brief contract or rule numbering changed, and every source-verifiable intent criterion holds. ## Testing I exercised the change through the rendered fm-brief CLI seam rather than only the unit assertions: the fm-brief suite passes in full, and I proved the new tests are genuinely red by restoring the base script and re-running (first new assertion fails, exit 1), then restoring the worktree clean. I then generated real briefs for all five scaffold kinds at both base and head and compared them phrase by phrase — the project-memory section now leads with the task-specific precedence rule before the conditional `Otherwise, ...run the helper` line (removing the run-helper vs never-run contradiction), both PR-producing modes carry a standalone `**PR body:**` closing-keyword step under Definition of done that is emitted before the step creating the PR and states plainly that GitHub may ignore it while firstmate verifies issue state after merge, the local-only brief carries none of that PR-only wording and keeps its Rules numbering contiguous, ship and scout briefs both prefer `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/...` and forbid merge-queue polling, and the secondmate charter inherits neither worker-only instruction. Commits carry no agent co-author, and generated briefs grew only modestly (ship no-mistakes 68 to 76 lines). Three adjacent suites that reference fm-brief also pass. No screenshot applies here because the end-user surface is generated Markdown consumed by a crewmate agent, so I captured the actual rendered brief.md files as the product-level artifact instead. One thing I could not prove: the repo's Bash 3.2 parse hazard (issue #1179) — only Bash 5.2 is available locally, so while the structural heredoc-in-command-substitution guard passes and the new blocks use the safe `IFS= read -r -d ''` form, real 3.2 enforcement remains with the macos-stock-bash CI job. The intent's PR-body Completion Evidence requirement is a PR-phase deliverable outside this phase.

This is required good practice, not proof of closure: GitHub may ignore the keyword, and firstmate verifies issue state after merge regardless. When you believe it is complete, append `done: {summary}` to the status file and stop. Firstmate will then instruct you to run /no-mistakes to validate and ship a PR. Do not hand-edit, commit, or fix findings yourself while a run is active - the pipeline applies every fix.
