title: fix(composer): read an NBSP-padded empty composer as empty and fail unshown herdr wedge alarms
body:
## Intent Fix the root cause of firstmate's away-mode escalation delivery wedge: buffered captain-relevant escalations sat undelivered for ~9.5 hours in each of three separate stretches, and steers into an idle pane reported false "delivery unconfirmed" errors. This implements recommendations R1 and R3 of a completed, already-reviewed diagnosis (private report at data/away-injection-wedge-diagnosis/report.md). The design was reviewed and motivated before this work started; the task was explicitly to implement it, not to redesign it. Do not propose an alternative architecture for the fix. R1 (the fix). Real Claude Code 2.1.220 pads its EMPTY composer row with U+00A0 NBSP, so the captured row is exactly `❯` + \xc2\xa0. bash's [[:space:]] does not match U+00A0, so no trim could remove it, the leading-glyph strip left a lone NBSP behind, and the shared classifier concluded "real, unsubmitted content remains" -> `pending` on a genuinely idle pane, stably, on every poll. Away-mode injection and verified submit both proceed only on an affirmative `empty`, which is why delivery wedged. fm_composer_classify_content now normalizes the non-ASCII blanks a TUI can use as padding before its trims (U+00A0, U+2007, U+202F -> ASCII space; U+200B, U+FEFF dropped). Deliberate decisions in R1, so they are not mistaken for oversights: - The normalization lives in bin/fm-composer-lib.sh, the ONE fleet-wide owner of the empty|pending|unknown verdict, specifically so both ANSI readers (tmux capture-pane -e and herdr pane read) and all four adapters (tmux, herdr, Orca, cmux) are covered at once and cannot drift back into per-adapter copies. Per-adapter normalization was rejected for exactly that reason. - Callers already trim ASCII whitespace before calling, and that is deliberately NOT sufficient - the whole defect is that their trims cannot see U+00A0. The classifier re-trims both content and plain_content after normalizing so the rest of the function keeps the trimmed inputs its contract comment documents. - The safety property is load-bearing and asserted in tests: every character normalized here renders as blank and nothing else is touched, so the change can only ever make an OTHERWISE-BLANK row read as blank. It is impossible for real typed text to become `empty` - a row holding any visible glyph keeps that glyph byte for byte, NBSP-joined text stays `pending`, and an NBSP-padded dead-shell prompt stays non-empty (it becomes the documented `unknown` rather than `pending`). - The helper uses explicit \x byte escapes rather than literal characters or \u escapes, deliberately: they are locale-independent and express the exact UTF-8 bytes the live captures carry. Please do not "clean these up" into literal characters. Regression fixtures. tests/fm-composer-lib.test.sh and tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh gain fixtures carrying the LITERAL \xc2\xa0 byte pair captured from real Claude Code 2.1.220 (the herdr fixture includes the trailing CR from the real capture). The absence of that byte pair anywhere under tests/ is precisely why all three 9.5-hour delivery failures passed CI, so the literal bytes in these fixtures are the point of the change, not an accident. Each new fixture is paired with a real-text counterpart so the safety property is tested in both directions rather than only asserted in prose. R3 (hardening in the same subsystem, same incident). `herdr notification show` exits 0 even when it showed nothing: with [ui.toast] delivery off (herdr's default) it answers {"shown":false,"reason":"disabled"}. wedge_alarm_via_herdr read exit 0 as success, so a captain who configured the away-mode wedge alarm's herdr channel would get a healthy log line and be reached by nobody. It now parses the payload and treats an explicit "shown":false as a channel failure with the reported reason logged. Deliberate decisions in R3: - A payload with no `shown` field keeps its exit-status verdict rather than being treated as a failure. This is intentional backward compatibility with a herdr build that reports no outcome, not a missed case; it is covered by a test. - The payload is captured through a temp file rather than a command substitution on purpose: a command substitution would put the notifier in a subshell, so wedge_alarm_run_bounded would lose its process-group timeout and its WEDGE_ALARM_NOTIFIER_PID cleanup. The no-mktemp branch preserves the previous behavior. - The logged reason is sanitized to a bounded safe character class. herdr's reason is its own short token (not captain config), so it is logged rather than redacted - unlike the command: channel, which deliberately redacts. - tests/fm-daemon.test.sh's shared make_wedge_case herdr fake gained FM_FAKE_HERDR_PAYLOAD and FM_FAKE_HERDR_EXIT knobs; both are used by the new tests, and the existing tests keep their previous behavior when the knobs are unset. Explicitly out of scope, by decision, and not to be added here: R2 (a max-defer fallback delivery route that does not depend on composer content - queued as separate work), R4 (choosing an OS alert channel for this Windows/WSL host - a pending captain decision, since it governs how firstmate interrupts the captain on their own machine), and R5 (fast-forwarding the operational home - not a code change). Documentation placement follows this repo's knowledge-placement rules: the mechanism and its rationale live in the changed script's own comments; the one fleet-wide behavioral sentence went into docs/architecture.md, which already owns the shared-classifier statement, rather than being duplicated into the per-backend docs; and docs/verification/supervision.md records the newly observed herdr payload. That verification entry is real observed output - the exact command already recorded there was re-run on this host today (herdr 0.7.5, Linux 6.18 WSL2) and returned {"reason":"disabled","shown":false} with exit 0, displaying nothing. Verification already performed locally: the reproduction was reproduced and inverted (pre-fix `pending`, post-fix `empty`, real text `pending` both ways) on both readers, including through fm_tmux_composer_row_state for the tmux path. All 171 pre-existing composer and herdr tests stay green (composer-lib 9, composer-ghost 30, herdr 132), the daemon suite goes 99 -> 101, and cmux (55), orca (50), tmux-submit-busy (8), send-strict (6), crew-state (47), backend (29), afk-return (5) and afk-launch (48) all pass. bin/fm-lint.sh (pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0) and bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh are both clean. Five failures in a broader changed-file run were each attributed elsewhere: fm-backend-tmux-smoke needs a real tmux server, and fm-pi-watch-extension, fm-turnend-guard and fm-calm-pi-extension were proven to fail identically with this change reverted; fm-watcher-lock has no source-graph dependency on either changed file. ## What Changed - `fm_composer_classify_content` in `bin/fm-composer-lib.sh` — the single fleet-wide owner of the `empty|pending|unknown` verdict — now normalizes non-ASCII blank padding before its trims (U+00A0, U+2007, U+202F → ASCII space; U+200B, U+FEFF dropped), so the `❯` + U+00A0 row that real Claude Code 2.1.220 emits for an idle composer classifies as `empty` instead of permanently `pending`. Rows with any visible glyph are untouched: NBSP-joined text stays `pending`, and an NBSP-padded dead-shell prompt becomes `unknown`, never `empty`. - `wedge_alarm_via_herdr` in `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh` now captures the `herdr notification show` payload (via a temp file, preserving the bounded-run process-group timeout) and treats an explicit `"shown":false` as a channel failure with the sanitized reason logged, instead of trusting the always-0 exit code; a payload without a `shown` field keeps the exit-status verdict for older herdr builds. - Regression fixtures carrying the literal `\xc2\xa0` bytes (with trailing CR on the herdr path) land in `tests/fm-composer-lib.test.sh` and `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh`, each paired with a real-text counterpart; `tests/fm-daemon.test.sh` covers the unshown/shown/payload-less herdr outcomes via new fake-herdr knobs, and docs (`architecture.md`, `verification/supervision.md`, `wedge-alarm.md`) record the shared-classifier behavior and the observed exit-0 `{"shown":false,"reason":"disabled"}` payload. All four affected suites pass in the pipeline, including manual before/after demos of both fixes. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A tightly-bounded two-part fix that matches its reviewed design exactly: the blank-normalization can only make otherwise-blank rows read blank (verified in code and pinned by byte-literal regression fixtures in both directions), and the herdr payload check only converts a previously-false success into an explicit failure, with backward-compatible fallbacks covered by tests. ## Testing Ran the four targeted suites covering the changed files (composer-lib, herdr backend, daemon, composer-ghost — all green, including the six new regression tests), then demonstrated both fixes end-to-end with a base-vs-fixed transcript: the byte-exact real-claude `❯`+U+00A0 idle capture flips from a stable false `pending` (the delivery wedge) to `empty` through both the herdr and tmux readers while real typed text and NBSP-padded dead shells stay non-empty, and the herdr wedge-alarm channel now fails loudly with the reason logged on the real exit-0 "shown":false payload where the base silently reported success. No rendered UI surface exists for this daemon/TUI-classifier change, so the CLI transcript is the reviewer-visible evidence.
Evidence: Base-vs-fixed transcript: NBSP wedge inversion (both readers) and herdr alarm payload hardening === R1: the NBSP wedge — real captured bytes: `❯` + U+00A0 (+CR in the pane capture) === composer row bytes: e2 9d af c2 a0 (e2 9d af = ❯, c2 a0 = U+00A0 NBSP) --- herdr reader end-to-end (fm_backend_herdr_composer_state on the full pane capture) --- idle NBSP-padded composer : BASE(a2d5f26) -> pending FIXED(c995389) -> empty same row + real typed text : BASE(a2d5f26) -> pending FIXED(c995389) -> pending --- tmux reader (fm_tmux_composer_row_state on the raw row) --- idle NBSP-padded row : BASE(a2d5f26) -> pending FIXED(c995389) -> empty same row + real typed text : BASE(a2d5f26) -> pending FIXED(c995389) -> pending NBSP-padded dead-shell '$' : BASE(a2d5f26) -> pending FIXED(c995389) -> unknown (must never be empty) === R3: herdr wedge-alarm channel vs the real exit-0 {"shown":false,"reason":"disabled"} payload === BASE(a2d5f26) : rc=0 daemon log: <empty> — exit 0 read as delivery: healthy log, captain reached by NOBODY FIXED(c995389): rc=1 daemon log: wedge alarm: herdr accepted the notification but did not show it (reason: disabled); this channel reached nobody ```text === R1: the NBSP wedge — real captured bytes: `❯` + U+00A0 (+CR in the pane capture) === composer row bytes: e2 9d af c2 a0 (e2 9d af = ❯, c2 a0 = U+00A0 NBSP) --- herdr reader end-to-end (fm_backend_herdr_composer_state on the full pane capture) --- idle NBSP-padded composer : BASE(a2d5f26) -> pending FIXED(c995389) -> empty same row + real typed text : BASE(a2d5f26) -> pending FIXED(c995389) -> pending --- tmux reader (fm_tmux_composer_row_state on the raw row) --- idle NBSP-padded row : BASE(a2d5f26) -> pending FIXED(c995389) -> empty same row + real typed text : BASE(a2d5f26) -> pending FIXED(c995389) -> pending NBSP-padded dead-shell '$' : BASE(a2d5f26) -> pending FIXED(c995389) -> unknown (must never be empty) Away-mode injection and verified submit proceed ONLY on an affirmative 'empty': at BASE the genuinely idle pane reads 'pending' forever -> delivery wedges; at FIXED it reads 'empty' -> escalations inject, while real text still blocks injection. === R3: herdr wedge-alarm channel vs the real exit-0 {"shown":false,"reason":"disabled"} payload === BASE(a2d5f26) : rc=0 daemon log: ^ exit 0 was read as delivery: healthy log, captain reached by NOBODY FIXED(c995389): rc=1 daemon log: wedge alarm: herdr accepted the notification but did not show it (reason: disabled); this channel reached nobody ```

title: fix(watch): escalate busy workers with no completed turn
body:
## Intent Ship the captain-approved shared Firstmate fix for busy workers that complete no turn for too long. Incident: a busy pane (herdr native busy state and/or the harness's rendered busy footer, e.g. Pi's 'Working...') was unconditional, unbounded proof of liveness in every existing escalation path (the watcher's Layer 1 stale/wedge loop, the away-mode daemon's identical busy exemption), so a single hung foreground tool call (a catastrophic-backtracking regex with no timeout) ran for 25 hours completely undetected while sibling panes kept escalating normally. Captain-approved contract, deliberately narrow: (1) preserve every existing busy classifier and the meaning of busy - do not touch window_is_busy/herdr semantics; (2) add exactly one new default 3600-second setting, FM_BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS, bounding how long any busy worker may run with no completed turn; (3) a completed turn (state/.turn-ended, or the task's spawn record/meta before any turn has ever completed) resets that age; (4) once the age reaches the bound, route the pane through the EXISTING stale/wedge escalation machinery (wedge_timer_check, the same .stale-since-*/.wedge-escalations-* files, the same 'stale: ... (idle Ns, possible wedge, escalation N)' reason text, the same FM_WEDGE_DEMAND_INSPECT_COUNT demand-deep-inspection marker, the same fm_wake_append/wake() notification path) - add NO new notification kind, control plane, liveness subsystem, or backend-specific busy semantics; (5) the escalation is for human inspection only - it must never automatically interrupt, signal, kill, or restart the worker or its tool process, and I verified this by leaving a real hung process alive and untouched throughout the entire reproduction; (6) the normal watcher and away-mode supervision must not be left duration-blind - the watcher detects an over-age busy turn through the existing wedge escalation path in its per-window poll loop (bin/fm-watch.sh), and bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh recognizes that canonical enriched wedge suffix independently of its ordinary terminal/nonterminal/paused stale classification so the escalation reaches the existing escalation buffer while every unsuffixed stale event keeps its prior away-mode behavior unchanged; (7) document the one setting minimally (docs/configuration.md's watcher-tuning env list, plus one sentence in docs/architecture.md's existing supervision paragraph) - no new maintainer doc, no AGENTS.md change, since nothing here needs every-session visibility. Implementation: added busy_turn_over_age() (ages turn-ended, or meta before any turn completed) and BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS=${FM_BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS:-3600} next to the existing STALE_ESCALATE_SECS; refactored the two places that unconditionally did rm -f "$ssf" "$ewf" on a busy or not-yet-stale pane (the hash-matched busy branch and the hash-changed/new-hash branch) to instead call the existing wedge_timer_check when busy_turn_over_age is true, otherwise reset exactly as before; factored the repeated window_is_busy call into one busy_now read per poll per window so both branches see a consistent verdict. The initial commit intentionally left bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh untouched, on the premise that the watcher-side fix alone would be authoritative for both live-captain and away-mode supervision per the architecture doc's 'exactly one live supervision cycle' contract; the review step's ask-user findings (recorded below) showed that premise was incomplete for away-mode, since the daemon's own classify_stale and housekeeping recheck could not resolve or preserve an enriched over-age busy wedge, so bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh (and its test file tests/fm-daemon.test.sh) were extended, with captain authorization at each step, to recognize the canonical enriched wedge suffix independently of ordinary terminal/nonterminal/paused classification and route it to the existing escalation buffer, without reapplying the ordinary busy exemption and without changing any other away-mode behavior. Verification performed before implementing: reproduced the exact end-user failure using the actually-installed real Pi TUI (not a mock) in a disposable tmux fixture isolated from any firstmate-managed session/state - ran a real pi process, prompted it to run sleep 999999 via its bash tool with explicitly no timeout parameter, captured the live pane twice ~15s apart and confirmed via diff that the 'Elapsed N.Ns' footer text and spinner glyph changed (proving the pane hash churns every poll) while the SAME tool call/turn remained unfinished throughout - this is the real masking condition from the incident (a ticking elapsed counter defeats naive hash-stability staleness detection). Then, using the ORIGINAL pre-fix bin/fm-watch.sh (via git show HEAD: before this task's commit) replayed against those two real captured panes across 6 alternating poll cycles with a turn-ended marker backdated 90000s (matching the incident's ~25h scale), proved it never starts a wedge timer no matter how long the pane stays busy or how much its hash churns. Then ran the FIXED watcher against the identical real captures and state, and it correctly starts the wedge timer on first crossing (default-bound test used FM_BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS=1 for speed while separately proving in a dedicated test that the shipped PRODUCTION DEFAULT really is 3600s - a completed turn 5 minutes old must not wedge while one 66 minutes old must, bracketing the default without waiting a literal hour), then escalates through the exact existing stale-reason/escalation-counter path when the wedge timer is aged past STALE_ESCALATE_SECS, exactly mirroring how an already-existing 'provably-working non-busy' wedge case behaves today. The real hung sleep process (verified via ps aux) remained alive and completely untouched through every one of these steps, then was cleanly aborted afterward via Pi's own built-in Escape-to-interrupt (not by our code), proving the fix is genuinely inspection-only. Tests added (behavioral only, through the real fm-watch.sh subprocess and fake tmux/backend seams already used by the existing suite - no source-content/regex-over-source/snapshot/AST/implementation-string tests): a busy pane below the bound stays absorbed with no escalation and no wedge-timer file created; a busy pane with a STABLE pane hash still escalates once its turn-age crosses the bound (two-phase: first crossing starts the timer, a backdated timer then escalates); a busy pane whose pane hash CHANGES every poll (the real ticking-footer masking condition, reproduced by never pre-seeding the hash file so every poll takes the 'new hash' code branch) still escalates the same way; touching the task's turn-ended marker mid-test resets the age and clears an already-started wedge timer and escalation counter (proving reset behavior); three consecutive over-age polls reuse the existing escalation counter (1, 2, 3) and the third correctly carries the existing demand-deep-inspection marker, exactly mirroring the pre-existing analogous test for the non-busy provably-working wedge case; and a dedicated test brackets the shipped default (FM_BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS unset, so the code's own ${FM_BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS:-3600} fallback is what's under test) by showing a 5-minute-old completed turn does not wedge while a 66-minute-old one does. All 6 new tests pass, and the full conservative --changed regression set (41 test files covering the watcher, wake-queue, daemon, turnend-guard, and everything else touched by this change) passes 41/41 with 0 failures and 0 gate skips. bin/fm-lint.sh (shellcheck-clean) and bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh both pass cleanly. Final accepted diff on branch fm/fm-busy-turn-age-wedge-r1 spans six files: bin/fm-watch.sh, bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh, docs/architecture.md, docs/configuration.md, tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh, and tests/fm-daemon.test.sh - no AGENTS.md change, no new subsystem, and no touch to any backend adapter. ## What Changed - Bound busy panes with no completed turn using the new `FM_BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS` setting, defaulting to 3600 seconds, and route overdue panes through the existing wedge escalation path. - Preserve enriched possible-wedge reasons during away-mode supervision so every busy-turn escalation reaches the existing escalation buffer. - Document the setting and add regression coverage for stable and changing pane hashes, turn-age resets, repeated escalation, deep-inspection markers, and AFK routing. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The final change narrowly recognizes canonical enriched wedge reasons before status-specific absorption, preserves their full diagnostic payload, leaves unsuffixed stale handling unchanged, and introduces no worker-control action. ## Testing Inspected the exact target diff, ran the focused watcher and away-mode daemon behavioral suites, and captured a manual end-to-end CLI transcript showing a changing busy footer entering the existing wedge path, persisting its stale wake, and leaving the associated process alive; all checks passed and the worktree remained clean.
Evidence: Busy-turn wedge end-to-end transcript A changing busy footer started the existing wedge timer, then surfaced `stale: evidence:fm-busy-hung (idle 500s, possible wedge, escalation 1)`. The durable wake queue contained the same reason, and the task-associated process remained alive and untouched. ```text === End-user fixture === pane: Working... (90000.0s) task-associated process before watcher: pid=10512 state=alive === First over-age poll === watcher output: existing wedge timer created: yes === Next changed-footer poll after wedge threshold === pane: Working... (90001.1s) watcher surfaced: stale: evidence:fm-busy-hung (idle 500s, possible wedge, escalation 1) persisted wake queue contains same stale reason: yes task-associated process after escalation: pid=10512 state=alive (untouched) automatic action records: none (watcher has no interrupt/kill/restart action path) ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed (3) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:1003` - Required criterion (6) says away-mode supervision “must not be left duration-blind,” but this call emits `stale: <window> (idle …)`. The away daemon treats everything after `stale: ` as the window, so `classify_stale` cannot match task metadata, records a malformed marker, and housekeeping deletes it because no such window exists. Thus an over-age busy worker is still silently absorbed while AFK. Authorize fixing the shared stale-reason parsing boundary in `fm-supervise-daemon.sh`, or revise the stated away-mode guarantee. 🔧 Fix: fix: parse enriched AFK stale reasons 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:1193` - The accepted AFK fix is still incomplete: after parsing the canonical window, an enriched watcher wedge with a normal `working:` status is classified as transient, and housekeeping calls `stale_window_is_busy`; because the hung pane is still busy, line 995 deletes the marker without `escalate_add`. The new test uses an idle pane, so it misses the incident path. This still contradicts criterion (6), “away-mode supervision must not be left duration-blind.” Route an already-enriched `possible wedge` wake to the existing escalation buffer without reapplying the busy exemption, and cover it with a busy pane. 🔧 Fix: fix: preserve enriched wedges during AFK supervision 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:1197` - The accepted instruction says any watcher-emitted enriched possible-wedge event must reach the existing buffer, but this override only handles `self|transient stale`. A busy worker with an already-seen terminal status line makes `classify_stale` return `self|stale + terminal (already escalated...)`; the later self path clears its marker, so the enriched wedge and `demand-deep-inspection` detail are dropped. A `paused:` status is likewise excluded. Detect the canonical enriched wedge suffix independently of ordinary stale classification, while leaving unsuffixed stale events unchanged. 🔧 Fix: fix: route all enriched AFK wedges ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - Inspected `git diff daf6dcef4a092c7e858d2eaa91cd9c5a25f1e156..dbaf4a89c27979dfb5f15869272597f0e01d22b2` for the watcher, daemon, tests, and documentation changes. - Ran `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh`. - Ran `tests/fm-daemon.test.sh`. - Ran a manual `bin/fm-watch.sh` changing-footer fixture with an aged task record, backdated wedge timer, durable wake-queue inspection, and before/after process-liveness checks. - Verified `git status --short` remained clean after testing.
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix(session-lock): guard basename against dash-prefixed login-shell comm
body:
## Summary
- `ps -o comm=` reports a login shell's command name with a leading dash (e.g. `-zsh`), which `basename` was parsing as an illegal option flag instead of a filename, printing `basename: illegal option -- z` on every harness-ancestry walk during session-lock acquire.
- Guard both call sites with `basename --` to stop option parsing.

## Test plan
- [x] `bin/fm-lint.sh bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh` passes (ShellCheck 0.11.0)
- [x] `bin/fm-session-start.sh` no longer prints the `basename` error at the lock step
- [x] `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed` run; the one flagged failure (`fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh`) reproduces as a pass in isolation (34s vs 235s under parallel contention in the full run) and exercises unrelated secondmate-provisioning code, not session-lock ancestry

title: feat(bin): add fleet launcher menu backed by a single-owner launch library
body:
## Intent Build `bin/fm-launch.sh`, the firstmate fleet launcher, per an already-reviewed design: a probed five-entry harness menu, a Herdr-mandatory gate, a primary session started at `FM_HOME`, a reattach guard, tests and docs. Several points were ruled before implementation and are deliberate rather than oversights. All five menu entries ship with availability PROBED rather than declared - an entry is available only when its binary resolves on PATH, or, for a Pi-routed entry, when the provider named in its model appears in Pi's local auth record - and both probes are local filesystem reads with no network at menu time, which is what holds the design's sub-150ms first-paint target. Unavailable entries render dim, visible and unselectable with one actionable fix line each, deliberately not hidden, so the menu never changes shape and the numbering stays stable. The launcher must state at the front door that the session it starts runs WITHOUT permission prompts; that is a binding obligation recorded in `bin/fm-launch-lib.sh`'s header, binding on the session posture rather than on any particular flag, and it is placed in the menu header so it appears before the choice. The Windows surface (`firstmate.bat` and the WSL bridge) is explicitly out of scope and lands separately. This branch is stacked on the `bin/fm-launch-lib.sh` extraction and deliberately builds on it rather than duplicating it: menu entries carry no launch command, and every command is resolved through the library at launch time, because a downstream registry has already drifted once by hand-copying a launch string and dropping Claude's ghost-text suppression prefix. Two decisions were taken during the run and are recorded here: the rebase absorbed main's new `pi-signed` harness into the extracted library, moving the `FM_PI_HARNESS` prefix into the library as its single owner rather than leaving it duplicated in `bin/fm-spawn.sh`, while keeping `pi-signed` a distinct executable identity that never silently falls back to `pi`; and the launcher now refuses at the door when the home's effective runtime backend is not Herdr, instead of assuming it. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-launch.sh`, an interactive fleet launcher: it renders a harness preset menu with live availability probes, refuses non-Herdr backends up front, guards against reattaching over a live primary, holds a `state/.launch.lock` through session startup so concurrent launches can't husk-replace a booting primary, and rejects malformed selections (out-of-range, leading-zero, EOF) with one-line guidance. - Extracted per-harness launch knowledge out of `bin/fm-spawn.sh` into `bin/fm-launch-lib.sh` as its single owner (verified primary shapes, trust/bypass flags, consumer obligations), with refreshed evidence-anchor citations; `fm-spawn.sh` and `fm-backend.sh` now consume the library. - Added `tests/fm-launch.test.sh` and `tests/fm-launch-lib.test.sh` (stubbed end-to-end launch, reattach guard, launch lock, Herdr gate, behavioral library coverage) plus new `docs/launcher.md` and ownership-pointer updates across the harness-adapters skill, README, and configuration docs. One known, documented tradeoff remains: a brief post-lock-release window before the harness registers as an agent, scoped honestly in `docs/launcher.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: All four requested fixes are correctly implemented with colocated behavioral regression tests and verified citation anchors, the launch lock reuses the established fm-wake-lib primitive exactly as fm-spawn does, and the only remaining item is a documented, deliberately scoped tradeoff. ## Testing Ran the five targeted suites (new launch-lib and launcher suites, changed backend, documentation-audiences, and spawn dispatch-profile) — all passed, proving byte-level launch-command ownership moved to fm-launch-lib.sh without behavior change — then manually exercised the launcher's real CLI surface end-to-end: menu render with autonomy notice, clean quit, all scripted refusals (leading-zero, out-of-range, unavailable harness, EOF), the non-Herdr backend door, and a live launch-lock refusal against a held lock; the full transcript is the evidence artifact since a terminal transcript is this CLI product's rendered surface (no GUI exists to screenshot).
Evidence: fm-launch.sh end-user CLI transcript (menu render, quit, all refusal surfaces, backend door, launch-lock refusal) $ bin/fm-launch.sh --print-menu Firstmate Sessions start without permission prompts. 1 Claude high ← default 2 ChatGPT Sol gpt-5.6-sol · high via pi 3 Grok grok-4 · high via pi - sign in: pi /login 4 Codex high not installed - install codex 5 OpenCode - not installed - install opencode ⏎ Claude 1-5 select q quit [exit 0] $ printf '01\n' | bin/fm-launch.sh ...menu... '01' is not one of the menu choices. Choose 1-5, or q to quit. [exit 1] $ printf '1\n' | bin/fm-launch.sh # launch lock held by live concurrent pid ...menu... › 1 Claude · high Another launch is already starting a session here. Wait for it to finish, then reattach or retry. [exit 1] ```text fm-launch.sh end-user CLI transcript — branch fm/fm-launch-menu @ a4049ec ────────────────────────────────────────────────── $ bin/fm-launch.sh --print-menu # first paint: menu render, availability probes, autonomy notice Firstmate Sessions start without permission prompts. 1 Claude high ← default 2 ChatGPT Sol gpt-5.6-sol · high via pi 3 Grok grok-4 · high via pi - sign in: pi /login 4 Codex high not installed - install codex 5 OpenCode - not installed - install opencode ⏎ Claude 1-5 select q quit [exit 0] ────────────────────────────────────────────────── $ printf 'q\n' | bin/fm-launch.sh # clean quit, no side effects Firstmate Sessions start without permission prompts. 1 Claude high ← default 2 ChatGPT Sol gpt-5.6-sol · high via pi 3 Grok grok-4 · high via pi - sign in: pi /login 4 Codex high not installed - install codex 5 OpenCode - not installed - install opencode ⏎ Claude 1-5 select q quit [exit 0] ────────────────────────────────────────────────── $ printf '01\n' | bin/fm-launch.sh # leading-zero input refused (would octal-crash under set -eu before the fix) Firstmate Sessions start without permission prompts. 1 Claude high ← default 2 ChatGPT Sol gpt-5.6-sol · high via pi 3 Grok grok-4 · high via pi - sign in: pi /login 4 Codex high not installed - install codex 5 OpenCode - not installed - install opencode ⏎ Claude 1-5 select q quit '01' is not one of the menu choices. Choose 1-5, or q to quit. title: fix(bin): bind Codex session locks to thread identity
body:
api_response:
  body: "## What Changed

- `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh` now owns a Codex thread-identity sidecar (`state/.lock.codex-thread`, written as `<lock-pid>:<thread-id>`) alongside the numeric `state/.lock` pid: ownership requires the sidecar's pid to match the lock, the holder to still be a live `codex` process, the validated `CODEX_THREAD_ID` of the current command to match, and any harness ancestry that does resolve to still name that same lock pid — so a nested foreign harness cannot inherit ownership from the environment. Mismatched, malformed, or multi-line identities fail closed, and the numeric holder's own reacquisition rebinds the sidecar instead of leaving it read-only. Thread-id validation uses a whole-value `[[ =~ ]]` match, and the harness/Codex liveness probes were collapsed into one `fm_pid_alive_matching` helper.
- `bin/fm-lock.sh` publishes the identity sidecar during acquisition (clearing it when no Codex thread id is present), verifies self-ownership after writing the lock, and `fm-lock.sh status` prints one `identity:` line describing sidecar presence, pid agreement, holder liveness, and thread match so a live-holder-but-unverifiable state is diagnosable without hand-reading state files.
- `bin/fm-sessionstart-nudge.sh` drops its own eight-hop ancestry loop and delegates to `fm_session_lock_owned_by_self`, making the shared lib the single ownership owner for the nudge, `fm-lock.sh`, and the Claude Stop auto-arm; regression coverage was extended in `tests/fm-session-start.test.sh`, `tests/fm-sessionstart-nudge.test.sh`, and the opt-in `tests/fm-codex-continuity-live-e2e.test.sh`, with the codex-cli 0.146.0 process-shape and thread-id evidence recorded in `docs/verification/supervision.md` and the harness-adapters skill.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The three requested fixes landed correctly with focused tests and no behavior regressions I can find, but the branch as a whole still reshapes the shared session-lock ownership primitive that gates three hooks across all five harnesses — the session-start nudge predicate is now strictly stricter with only fake-`ps` coverage for non-Codex ancestry shapes — so it is safe to merge with the remaining informational items as follow-ups.

## Testing

No baseline test commands preceded this phase, so I ran the targeted set myself: the session-start suite carrying the three new Codex lock tests, the session-start-nudge suite, and the Claude Stop auto-arm suite as the other consumer of the changed ownership predicate — all pass. Because unit tests use a fake `ps` ancestry, I also proved the intent on the real codex-cli 0.146.0 installed on this machine: the opt-in live E2E passes both standalone and re-run from inside a Codex session (so outer vs nested thread ids were real), and a purpose-written probe executed inside an actual Codex command child produced a CLI transcript showing the sidecar bound to a thread id identical to that session's printed session id, a second thread of the same live Codex pid held read-only, `fm-lock.sh status` naming each failure mode, stale-holder rebinding on reacquisition, a live `claude`-named holder and a nested foreign harness both refused, a multi-line `CODEX_THREAD_ID` refusing to become lock authority, and the session-start nudge silent for the owning thread but printing its single marked line for a new thread and a nested harness. This change is shell/CLI only with no rendered surface, so the reviewer-visible evidence is the Codex session transcript and probe output rather than screenshots. The worktree is clean and all scratch homes and helper processes created during testing were removed.

title: test: reap leaked background processes on every suite ending
body:
## Intent Goal: stop crewmate worktrees of the firstmate repo from self-arming phantom watchers. Phantom fm-watch-arm.sh --restart plus fm-watch.sh pairs were observed live in several treehouse task worktrees; effects were an inflated shell count, polluted liveness reads, and a test suite that can hang. Important context the diff does not show. The task as originally briefed asked me to make the Claude Stop auto-arm eligibility check refuse to arm inside a linked git worktree. That premise was investigated and DISPROVEN: bin/fm-primary-scope-lib.sh already refuses when git rev-parse --git-dir differs from --git-common-dir, with a .fm-secondmate-home marker as the secondmate exemption, and tests/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.test.sh already covers all three cases (primary arms, marked secondmate home arms, linked child worktree stays inert) and passes. So no change was made to the auto-arm or to the scope predicate, deliberately - that would have been a no-op. The real cause was traced to a leaking test. Every live phantom carried test-harness env (FM_HOME=/tmp/fm-watcher-lock-tests./restart-healthy-peer), and the only producer of that case is tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh test_watch_restart_attaches_to_healthy_peer. It backgrounds a real arm and only kills it on its happy path, so when an assertion aborts the suite via fail(), or when timeout(1) kills a hung case, the arm and its child watcher are orphaned and keep polling an already-deleted temp home. Reproduced directly. The supervising firstmate ruled to fix exactly this leak and explicitly NOT to expand into fixing the attach failure. Decisions made, all deliberate: - tests/lib.sh gains the reaper because it already owns the temp-root cleanup registry, keeping one owner for teardown. - SIGKILL rather than SIGTERM is required, not sloppy: bin/fm-watch-arm.sh deliberately launches a successor watcher when its child cycle ends, so a catchable signal to the parent hands back a fresh process that was never registered. This is exactly why the original phantom respawned after being killed once. - The process tree is snapshotted BEFORE the first kill because a dead parent leaves its children reparented and unreachable by a ppid walk. - Cleanup is trapped on HUP, INT and TERM as well as EXIT because a bare EXIT trap does not run for a signalled shell, which is precisely why the hang path leaked. - All roots share one ps read so registering many short-lived helpers stays cheap. - Every background launch in tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh registers its pid at launch, including the short-lived lock contenders, for uniformity. - The new regression case runs FIRST in the suite so it still executes even when a later case aborts, and it covers all three endings: a clean pass, a fail() abort, and a TERM. It was verified to FAIL against a deliberately neutered reaper, so it is not a tautology. Known and deliberate non-goals, please do not flag these as omissions: - test_watch_restart_attaches_to_healthy_peer still fails on this machine. That failure is pre-existing on main, upstream CI is green, and it was classified as a load-sensitive flaky fixture rather than a runtime defect: the identical scenario reproduced standalone against the same bin/fm-watch-arm.sh passes and prints the intended watcher: attached line. Fixing it was explicitly ruled out of scope for this change. - fm_test_tmproot has a separate pre-existing quirk where a call inside command substitution loses its registration to the parent, so temp dirs accumulate. That is disk-only, affects every test file, and was intentionally left alone and reported instead. - Nothing was added to AGENTS.md on purpose, to respect its size discipline; the durable convention went to the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill and to the tests/lib.sh header, which are the classified owners. ## What Changed - `tests/lib.sh` now owns a process reaper alongside its temp-root registry: background pids are registered at launch, the process tree is snapshotted before killing so reparented children stay reachable, kills use SIGKILL (a catchable signal lets `fm-watch-arm.sh` respawn a successor watcher), each kill is gated by pid start-time identity to survive pid reuse and `ps` failures, and cleanup is trapped on HUP/INT/TERM as well as EXIT so a signalled or `timeout(1)`-killed shell still tears down. This closes the leak in `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh` where `test_watch_restart_attaches_to_healthy_peer` orphaned a real `fm-watch-arm.sh --restart` + `fm-watch.sh` pair whenever the suite aborted or hung — the source of the phantom watchers seen in crewmate worktrees. - `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh` registers every background launch (including short-lived lock contenders) and adds a regression case that runs first in the suite, covering all three suite endings (clean pass, `fail()` abort, and TERM); it was verified to fail against a deliberately neutered reaper. The auto-arm eligibility check itself was left untouched — `bin/fm-primary-scope-lib.sh` already refuses to arm in linked worktrees and its existing tests pass. - The reaper convention is documented in the `firstmate-coding-guidelines` skill and the `tests/lib.sh` header, with `tests/wake-helpers.sh` adjusted to match. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The follow-up commit is tests-only and implements all three requested fixes exactly as instructed (interruptible hang fixture, identity-gated root kills via the production fm_pid_identity primitive through a subshell, and a roots-emitting ps-failure fallback) while preserving every declared design constraint, with the only residual behaviors being rare, fail-open identity-read races that match the chosen safety direction. ## Testing Ran the changed watcher-lock suite via bin/fm-test-run.sh (all cases pass, new reaper regression case first, including the author's reportedly flaky peer-attach case which passed here), then demonstrated the fix end-to-end with a base-vs-branch comparison: a TERM'd wedged suite on the base harness orphans the exact phantom fm-watch-arm.sh + fm-watch.sh pair with the live-incident FM_HOME signature, while the fixed harness reaps every process and exits 128+TERM; a neutered-reaper run confirmed the regression test genuinely fails without the fix. No orphaned processes or temp scaffolding remain. No visual artifacts because this is a test-harness/CLI change with no rendered UI surface — CLI transcripts are the evidence.
Evidence: Full watcher-lock suite run on the branch (exit 0, reaper regression case first) ```text FM_TEST_BEGIN 2026-07-30T03:18:54Z tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh family=watcher-wake-lock expected_gate_skip=none ok - harness reaps a registered process and its child on a pass, an abort, and a signal ok - simultaneous watcher starts leave exactly one live process ok - fm_pid_identity real ps fallback is locale-invariant ok - fm_pid_identity is locale-invariant across LC_ALL/LC_TIME ok - /proc process identity ignores simulated btime changes ok - /proc process identity detects pid reuse ok - MSYS /proc process identity regression skipped on non-Windows host ok - killed watcher stale lock is reclaimed ok - live watcher lock with stale heartbeat is actionable ok - guard banner leads when down with pending wakes (repair-after-drain) and stays silent when fresh ok - ⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - 🚨 `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh:528` - The hang-mode leg of the new regression test simulates a wedged suite with a foreground `sleep 300`, but bash defers a trapped TERM until the current foreground command completes (verified empirically: a `bash -c 'trap "exit 143" TERM; sleep 300'` process stays alive after TERM). The leg only passes if the outer `kill -TERM` lands while the fixture is still inside its 0.1s poll loop; if the fixture has already dropped into `sleep 300` — which happens whenever the kid pidfile is written before the fixture's first poll check, and is more likely under full-suite load — the trap is deferred ~300s, `wait_for_exit` (tests/wake-helpers.sh:260) polls 8s then blocks in `wait` for the remaining ~292s, and returns 124 instead of 143, failing the assertion at line 553. Because this test deliberately runs first, the losing side of the race stalls the suite ~5 minutes and then aborts every subsequent case. Fix: make the wedge interruptible, e.g. `hang) sleep 300 & fm_test_reap "$!"; wait ;;` — the `wait` builtin returns immediately on a trapped signal, making the TERM leg deterministic (and the extra sleep is reaped by the fixture's own cleanup). - ⚠️ `tests/lib.sh:138` - FM_TEST_CLEANUP_PIDS accumulates every registered pid for the suite's whole lifetime and pids are never deregistered, even after a test explicitly `wait`s them (e.g. the lock-contender loops). At teardown fm_test_kill_tree unconditionally SIGKILLs each stale pid and also treats it as a tree root, so after pid wraparound (macOS pid space is ~99999; Linux pid_max is often 32768) a recycled pid can belong to an unrelated same-user process, which then gets SIGKILLed along with its descendants. The repo already has a pid-identity primitive (fm_pid_identity, used by test_watch_restart_rejects_reused_pid) that could gate the kill, or fm_test_kill_tree could skip pids whose start-time identity changed since registration. Flagging for the author because the intent declares registering short-lived contenders "for uniformity" a deliberate choice. - ⚠️ `tests/lib.sh:113` - fm_test_process_tree bails out with empty output when `ps -axo pid=,ppid=` fails (`|| return 0`), so fm_test_kill_tree kills nothing at all — not even the registered root pids that the caller knows are valid. On platforms whose ps lacks BSD `-o` output selection (MSYS/Cygwin ps, some busybox builds — and this very suite carries an MSYS-specific case, test_msys_pid_identity_uses_proc), the reaper silently no-ops, reintroducing the leak there, and the new first-position regression test would then fail the entire suite on those platforms because assert_reaped finds the fixture parent still alive. Degrade gracefully by emitting the given root pids when the ps read fails, so at least the registered processes are killed. - ℹ️ `tests/lib.sh:85` - fm_test_cleanup_on_signal runs `trap - EXIT` before exiting, so a test file that follows the pattern documented in this same header — define its own EXIT trap that does extra teardown (e.g. cleanup_all killing tmux sessions in the e2e suites) and calls fm_test_cleanup from inside — gets that extra teardown silently skipped on the signal path; only lib-registered dirs/pids are torn down. This is not a regression (previously nothing ran on a signalled shell) and fm_test_cleanup is idempotent per its own comment, so leaving the EXIT trap installed and simply exiting would run the file's custom teardown too at the cost of a harmless double cleanup. Noting as a design tradeoff. 🔧 Fix: gate reaper kills by identity and survives ps loss 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `tests/lib.sh:96` - Residual fail-open race in the identity gate: fm_pid_identity's identity includes the full /proc cmdline (or ps `command=`), and fm_test_reap reads it immediately after fork - if the identity read (itself ~10ms: fork bash, source bin/fm-wake-lib.sh) ever completes before the just-forked child execs its command, the recorded pre-exec bash cmdline can never match the teardown re-read, so that process is skipped and leaks. The same design makes the reaper a full no-op on a platform with neither a readable compatible /proc nor a BSD-capable ps (identity reads fail, all roots skipped). Both are deliberate consequences of the instructed governing property (never kill what cannot be proven ours), fail in the safe direction, and the realistic platform set (Linux, macOS, MSYS/Cygwin with /proc) is covered - noting the tradeoff only.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh` — full changed suite on the branch: exit 0, new reaper regression case runs first and passes (clean/abort/TERM endings), and a post-run /proc environ scan with a unique marker env var confirmed zero surviving background processes - `Manual leak reproduction on base commit a2d5f26: materialized base tests/ with shared bin/, ran a faithful reduction of test_watch_restart_attaches_to_healthy_peer (real backgrounded bin/fm-watch-arm.sh, then wedged), sent SIGTERM like timeout(1) — orphaned fm-watch-arm.sh + fm-watch.sh survived, carrying the incident's FM_HOME=/tmp/fm-watcher-lock-tests.*/restart-healthy-peer signature` - `Same manual scenario against the fixed harness at HEAD: suite shell exited 143 (128+TERM per the new signal cleanup contract) and zero tagged processes survived` - `Non-tautology check: neutered fm_test_kill_tree to a no-op in a temp copy of HEAD's tests and re-ran the suite — the new regression case immediately failed with 'registered process survived the harness teardown' (exit 1)` - `Post-test hygiene: killed all marker-tagged demo/neutered-run leftovers without touching other lanes' live fm-watch processes, removed temp harness dirs, verified worktree clean`

title: feat: reconcile tree-identical fleet sync divergence
body:
## Intent The developer wanted a narrowly guarded Firstmate fleet-sync recovery for genuinely diverged clean default branches whose freshly fetched local and remote commits have identical root trees, while atomically preserving the old local head under a deterministic collision-safe ref and moving the branch with expected-old and no-dereference checks. They required comprehensive isolated regression coverage and minimal architecture documentation, with all existing fast-forward, detached-recovery, refusal, pruning, refspec compatibility, locking, and bounded startup behavior preserved, including protections for symbolic refs, active Git operations, fetch races, and indeterminate transaction acknowledgements. They explicitly prohibited touching any real or motivating clone, weakening refusal tests, force/reset/stash/history loss, merging, or system-level changes, and accepted the proven pre-existing session-start failure and unavailable pinned x86_64 ShellCheck on the aarch64 host pending authoritative CI. Finally, they authorized creating the public homestills/firstmate fork via gh-axi, retaining kunchenguid/firstmate as authoritative origin, resuming the preserved no-mistakes pipeline head with all accumulated fixes, and driving it through push, CI/lint, and PR creation without merging. ## What Changed - Reconcile clean, genuinely diverged default branches when their local and fetched remote commits have identical root trees, preserving the old local tip under a deterministic ref before atomically advancing the branch. - Harden staged fetch publication and reconciliation against symbolic refs, concurrent ref changes, active Git operations, linked worktrees, transport-policy leaks, and interrupted cleanup while preserving configured refspec, tag, prune, and submodule behavior. - Expand fleet-sync and bootstrap regression coverage and documentation, including a larger fleet-size-aware bootstrap timeout allowance. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The latest fix safely constructs an escaped literal gitdir condition through a static include key, and the full reviewed range retains the intended ref, worktree, transport, pruning, and submodule safeguards without additional material issues. ## Testing Baseline startup and both focused automated suites passed; isolated CLI and bootstrap exercises demonstrated recovery, preservation, refusal, and idempotence, with three reviewer-visible text artifacts captured. This is a CLI-only change, so transcripts and persisted Git state are the actual user-facing evidence.
Evidence: Fleet-sync end-to-end transcript `Direct CLI transcript showing guarded recovery, unequal-divergence refusal, preserved old head, and idempotent rerun.` ```text End-to-end fleet-sync validation scenario: clean checked-out default branches after remote fetch BEFORE equivalent local head: 02d39939d8a919dfc33505cd76d8a8317b8c2492 equivalent remote head: 8c5ab45554fbb3ee00610c8a13fc7d432d5a2b60 equivalent local tree: 4800209844401a3eb4659bb2257b2f1354eb1804 equivalent remote tree: 4800209844401a3eb4659bb2257b2f1354eb1804 unequal local head: 9e1c761a70c4e2bf601bd6b0cc10e8909c0530a8 FIRST USER RUN equivalent: recovered: reconciled tree-identical squash on main to origin/main; preserved refs/fm-fleet-sync/squash-preserved/main/02d39939d8a919dfc33505cd76d8a8317b8c2492 unequal: STUCK: on diverged main, 1 commits behind origin/main - needs attention AFTER FIRST RUN equivalent HEAD: 8c5ab45554fbb3ee00610c8a13fc7d432d5a2b60 equivalent origin/main: 8c5ab45554fbb3ee00610c8a13fc7d432d5a2b60 equivalent preservation ref: refs/fm-fleet-sync/squash-preserved/main/02d39939d8a919dfc33505cd76d8a8317b8c2492 -> 02d39939d8a919dfc33505cd76d8a8317b8c2492 equivalent preservation ref kind: direct equivalent preserved/current trees: 4800209844401a3eb4659bb2257b2f1354eb1804 / 4800209844401a3eb4659bb2257b2f1354eb1804 equivalent worktree: clean unequal HEAD remains: 9e1c761a70c4e2bf601bd6b0cc10e8909c0530a8 unequal preservation refs: SECOND USER RUN equivalent: already current unequal: STUCK: on diverged main, 1 commits behind origin/main - needs attention VERIFICATION: PASS - equivalent divergence reconciled with the old head preserved; unequal divergence remained untouched; rerun converged. ```
Evidence: Bootstrap fleet-sync surface `Actual bootstrap output surfacing both the recovery and STUCK refusal.` ```text Session-start bootstrap fleet-sync surface BOOTSTRAP OUTPUT FLEET_SYNC: equivalent: recovered: reconciled tree-identical squash on main to origin/main; preserved refs/fm-fleet-sync/squash-preserved/main/02d39939d8a919dfc33505cd76d8a8317b8c2492 FLEET_SYNC: unequal: STUCK: on diverged main, 1 commits behind origin/main - needs attention POST-BOOTSTRAP STATE equivalent HEAD/origin: 8c5ab45554fbb3ee00610c8a13fc7d432d5a2b60 / 8c5ab45554fbb3ee00610c8a13fc7d432d5a2b60 equivalent preserved old head: refs/fm-fleet-sync/squash-preserved/main/02d39939d8a919dfc33505cd76d8a8317b8c2492 -> 02d39939d8a919dfc33505cd76d8a8317b8c2492 unequal HEAD remains: 9e1c761a70c4e2bf601bd6b0cc10e8909c0530a8 VERIFICATION: PASS - startup surfaced both the guarded recovery and the refusal, with the preserved and untouched heads intact. ```
Evidence: Post-reconciliation Git state `Persisted Git state proving genuine one-base divergence, identical root trees, synchronized refs, a direct preservation ref, and a clean worktree.` ```text Persisted Git state after guarded fleet sync old local head (preserved): 02d39939d8a919dfc33505cd76d8a8317b8c2492 fetched remote/current head: 8c5ab45554fbb3ee00610c8a13fc7d432d5a2b60 left/right commit counts: 2 1 common base count: 1 common base: 16e688467071779118cd54faa86e9b3aa695d2ce old/current root trees: 4800209844401a3eb4659bb2257b2f1354eb1804 / 4800209844401a3eb4659bb2257b2f1354eb1804 HEAD: 8c5ab45554fbb3ee00610c8a13fc7d432d5a2b60 refs/heads/main: 8c5ab45554fbb3ee00610c8a13fc7d432d5a2b60 refs/remotes/origin/main: 8c5ab45554fbb3ee00610c8a13fc7d432d5a2b60 refs/fm-fleet-sync/squash-preserved/main/02d39939d8a919dfc33505cd76d8a8317b8c2492: 02d39939d8a919dfc33505cd76d8a8317b8c2492 preservation ref kind: direct worktree: clean VERIFICATION: PASS - one-base genuine divergence had identical trees; current refs moved together and the direct preservation ref retained the old local head. ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 3 issues found → auto-fixed (5) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:777` - Refuse reconciliation when another worktree has the default branch checked out. Only this worktree's status and operation markers are checked, but `git worktree add --force ... main` can create a second checkout; this transaction then moves the shared branch beneath a dirty or mid-merge sibling despite the documented STUCK guarantee. Check other worktrees before preservation and again before committing. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:413` - Preserve repository-local transport configuration in the staged remote fetch. Copying only `remote.origin.*` drops local `url.*.insteadOf`, `core.sshCommand`, and HTTP/credential settings, so clones that previously fetched successfully can now use an unrewritten or unauthenticated URL and be skipped. Give the stage a controlled config-equivalent fetch environment. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:311` - Fail if the mirror-generated `remote.origin` section cannot be removed. Ignoring this failure can leave the stage's `$PROJ` URL and mirror refspec alongside the copied origin configuration, causing a subsequent fetch to read from the source clone or detect unintended local-branch updates instead of fetching the real origin. 🔧 Fix: Harden fleet sync worktree and transport safeguards 4 issues (2 errors, 2 warnings) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:596` - Detect rebases in linked worktrees before reconciliation. This only counts `branch refs/heads/main` records, but Git reports a rebasing worktree as detached while its `rebase-merge/head-name` or `rebase-apply/head-name` still targets `main`; reconciliation can therefore move the shared branch underneath an active sibling rebase. Inspect each linked worktree's operation metadata during both guards. - 🚨 `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:327` - Preserve valueless boolean configuration when copying fetch settings. A bare key such as `http.sslVerify` means true, while re-adding it with an empty value means false; the current serialization can therefore disable TLS verification in the staged fetch. Preserve value presence or canonicalize supported booleans explicitly. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:429` - Force the staging clone's remote name to `origin`. Git's `clone.defaultRemoteName` can otherwise create another name, after which the newly fatal `remote.origin` removal fails and skips synchronization. Pass `--origin origin` to make the expected staging invariant explicit. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:476` - Allow the trusted staging path only for the internal object-transfer fetch. A repository with `protocol.file.allow=never` and a non-file authoritative origin can fetch normally, but this new fetch from `$stage` is a file transport executed under that repository's configuration and will fail. Apply a command-scoped override to this internal transfer or copy objects without file transport. 🔧 Fix: Harden fleet sync rebase and fetch isolation 2 warnings still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:433` - Apply the scoped file-protocol override to this trusted local clone as well. A global, system, or command-scope `protocol.file.allow=never` blocks local-path clones, so repositories with a non-file origin that previously fetched successfully now skip before reaching the already-protected internal fetch. Keep the override off the authoritative-origin fetch. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:314` - Preserve repository-local `fetch.pruneTags`. The previous `fetch --prune origin` honored this setting, but the staged fetch allowlist drops it, so deleted remote tags remain in the stage snapshot and their deletions are never published. Copy this safe fetch setting alongside the origin configuration. 🔧 Fix: Preserve fleet sync file and tag semantics 2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:481` - Prevent the file-policy override from reaching recursive submodule fetches. This object-only fetch defaults to on-demand submodule recursion, and command-scoped configuration is inherited by its child fetches, so `protocol.file.allow=always` can enable file transports for populated submodules rather than only `$stage`. Disable recursion here and preserve configured submodule fetching separately under the repository's original transport policy. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:314` - Copy repository-local `protocol.allow` as well as `protocol.<name>.allow`. For example, an `ext::` origin enabled through generic `protocol.allow=always` succeeds under the previous direct fetch but is denied by the staged fetch because `ext` falls back to its default `never` policy. 🔧 Fix: Isolate fleet sync submodule transport policy 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:500` - Avoid embedding the raw Git-directory path in a `-c name=value` key. A valid project path containing `=` is split at that character, while glob metacharacters are interpreted by the `gitdir` condition; the scoped include can therefore fail or match more than the parent repository. Write a temporary conditional-include config using an escaped literal gitdir pattern, then include it through a static command key. 🔧 Fix: Escape scoped fleet sync Git-directory conditions ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bin/fm-session-start.sh` — baseline startup completed cleanly - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-fleet-sync.test.sh` - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` - `FM_HOME=/tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYRBXDVGNX50G28PRQDEA0HB/fleet-sync-e2e.tsNuz4/home bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh` — isolated equivalent and unequal divergence fixture, run twice with ref/tree/cleanliness assertions - `FM_HOME=/tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYRBXDVGNX50G28PRQDEA0HB/fleet-sync-e2e.tsNuz4/home bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` — verified startup-visible recovery and refusal output - Persisted-state checks using `git rev-list --left-right --count`, `git merge-base --all`, `git show-ref --verify`, `git symbolic-ref --quiet`, and `git status --porcelain` - `git status --short --branch --untracked-files=all` — tracked worktree remained clean

title: feat(bin): add hidden backlog triage view

## Intent Add a hidden "Backlog" triage category and explicit backlog status view to firstmate's task tooling. Captain triage vocabulary is do / defer / backlog / kill. Items held with a reason that starts with "backlog:" must be render-hidden from every routine surface (session-start compact listing, fleet snapshot, fleet view, bearings) until revived, and listed only via an explicit "show backlog" path. This differs from deferred (listed, with a revisit trigger) and parked (visible). Implementation choices made while doing the work: - Shared predicate and hint text live in bin/fm-tasks-axi-lib.sh (hold reason prefix "backlog:", case-sensitive) so surfaces do not re-state the convention. - Explicit human status view is bin/fm-backlog-list.sh: default hides backlogged items with a count hint ("N backlogged hidden - use bin/fm-backlog-list.sh --backlog to list"); --backlog lists only them; --include-backlog shows everything. - Fleet snapshot filters backlogged rows out of backlog.records by default, exposes hidden_backlogged_count and hidden_backlogged_hint, tags backlogged:true when included via --include-backlog; fleet-view and bearings inherit without per-surface duplication. - Session-start filters both the tasks-axi compact path and the manual title-line path with the same convention. - Deferred (future/hold-until) and parked without the backlog: reason prefix remain visible. - Tests in tests/fm-backlog-list.test.sh; registered under snapshot-bearings in fm-test-run.sh. - Hold/revive still use tasks-axi hold/unhold; no change to tasks-axi itself (external package). ## What Changed - Add a shared, case-sensitive `backlog:` hold classification that hides matching tasks from session-start, fleet snapshot/view, Bearings, scout reports, and secondmate projections while keeping deferred and ordinary parked holds visible. - Add `fm-backlog-list.sh` with routine, backlog-only, and include-backlog views, plus hidden-count hints and structured snapshot metadata. - Document the backlog triage workflow and add behavioral coverage for listing, filtering, limits, registry accounting, and explicit inclusion. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The latest correction filters hidden secondmate IDs before applying the registry record cap and computes record truncation/completeness from the visible record set, resolving the remaining issue without introducing a material new risk. ## Testing Confirmed the supplied target and clean baseline, then passed the backlog, fleet snapshot/view, bearings, and full session-start regression suites. End-to-end CLI fixtures demonstrated case-sensitive hiding, continued visibility for deferred and parked work, hidden-count hints, explicit backlog listing, and `backlogged: true` restoration through `--include-backlog`.

title: fix(bin): isolate Treehouse pools by firstmate home
body:
## Intent

Fix the cross-home treehouse pool binding hazard in firstmate, per the completed audit fm-treehouse-pool-root-audit. Treehouse keys its shared ~/.treehouse pool by origin URL, so main-home and secondmate clones of one remote share a pool and each slot binds permanently to whichever clone created it; deleting a secondmate home would orphan its slots and poison the pool. The ship scope, all implemented: (1) fm-home-seed.sh writes a repo-level treehouse.toml with a home-scoped pool root into each secondmate project clone so pools are isolated per home (refusing to clobber a project's own tracked treehouse.toml or an operator's untracked one); (2) fm-spawn.sh fail-closed refuses an acquired pool slot whose git common dir is not the spawning home's project clone, returning the slot with an actionable destroy message - this is a deliberate safety refusal, not a behavior regression; (3) fm-teardown.sh secondmate retirement destroys pool slots bound to the retiring home before removing it, refusing the retirement when treehouse will not destroy one, and --force adds --include-unlanded but deliberately never --include-in-use or --include-leased so another home's live task cannot be torn down; (4) docs in docs/configuration.md plus a one-line cross-reference in the secondmate-provisioning skill, and a new regression suite tests/fm-treehouse-pool-isolation.test.sh using temp fixtures only (never live pools or real homes). The main home intentionally keeps the default ~/.treehouse root; only secondmate clones get the pin. FM_TEARDOWN_POOL_SCAN_ROOTS is a deliberate test-only override of the scanned pool roots.

## What Changed

- Pin seeded secondmate project clones to home-scoped Treehouse pool roots without overwriting existing configs, while keeping seed writes escaped, ignored, and transactional.
- Reject pool slots bound to another home during spawn, and destroy home-bound slots before secondmate retirement with fail-closed safety checks.
- Document the pool-isolation lifecycle and add regression coverage for seeding, spawning, teardown, and legacy shared-pool handling.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The amended change is well-bounded, satisfies the stated pool-isolation and teardown constraints, and resolves the prior cleanliness, rollback, and TOML-escaping defects without introducing a material new risk.

## Testing

Inspected the complete target diff and documentation, then exercised production seed, spawn, and teardown entry points using temporary Git fixtures, including a real `treehouse` run with redirected `HOME`; pool roots were isolated, foreign bindings failed closed, retirement preserved foreign/live slots, neighboring lifecycle regressions passed, the reviewer-visible CLI transcript was captured, and cleanup left the worktree unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Evidence: Treehouse pool isolation evidence</summary>

`End-to-end CLI transcript demonstrating isolated pools, foreign-slot refusal, safe retirement, and force-flag boundaries.`

```text
ok - seed pins a home-scoped treehouse pool root into the secondmate clone only
ok - seed pins the pool root for a preexisting project clone too
ok - seed refuses to override a project's own tracked treehouse.toml
ok - seed refuses to overwrite an untracked treehouse.toml it did not write
ok - seed rollback restores configs and exclusions in preexisting clones
ok - seed TOML-escapes quotes and backslashes in the pool root
ok - two clones of one remote acquire same-named pools under different roots
ok - spawn accepts a pool slot bound to the spawning home's own clone
ok - spawn fail-closed refuses a pool slot bound to another clone and returns it
ok - secondmate retirement destroys exactly the pool slots bound to its own clones
ok - secondmate retirement fails closed when a bound slot is not disposable
ok - forced retirement discards unlanded home-bound slots but never in-use or leased ones
# all fm-treehouse-pool-isolation tests passed
```
</details>

- 🚨 `bin/fm-home-seed.sh:562` - The generated treehouse.toml remains visible to `git status`, so every seeded secondmate project clone is permanently dirty. `fm-fleet-sync.sh:338-367` consequently refuses its normal fast-forward path, leaving secondmate clones stale. Add the seed-owned file to the clone's git info/exclude after verifying it is safe to create or overwrite.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-home-seed.sh:592` - Writing treehouse.toml into a preexisting clone is not tracked by the seed rollback. If a later project, no-mistakes initialization, or registry update fails, rollback preserves the newly added config despite the script's transactional contract. Record and remove newly created configs, and back up/restore an existing seed-owned config.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-home-seed.sh:566` - The home path is interpolated into a TOML basic string without escaping. Supported paths containing `"` or `\` produce invalid or altered configuration, so Treehouse will fail instead of using the isolated root. title: feat(afk): make recurring composer deferrals record their own cause
body:
## Intent Implement R2 from the completed away-mode escalation wedge diagnosis (data/away-injection-wedge-diagnosis/report.md): give the away-mode delivery guard's max-defer escape somewhere to escape to. Background. Away mode buffers captain-relevant escalations and injects them into firstmate's own pane. The max-defer escape at bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh retried the identical guarded delivery path and could only alarm. A 9.5-hour wedge (three consecutive occurrences) proved that a systematic composer misclassification defers forever with zero diagnostic value: the buffered escalation recorded no record of WHICH verdict recurred or WHAT the offending composer row contained, so the follow-up investigation had to start from scratch. The diagnosed root cause was Claude Code rendering its empty composer as the prompt glyph plus U+00A0, which bash's [[:space:]] trims cannot see. Goal of THIS change. Make that class of wedge self-diagnosing. After N consecutive identical non-empty composer verdicts, record a distinguishable diagnostic: the verdict, the offending row's sanitized bounded bytes, and the reader that produced it, so the next investigation starts at the answer. Deliberate decisions made and approved by the supervising firstmate in a mandatory design review before implementation (design at data/composer-defer-diagnostic-fallback/design.md). A reviewer reading only the diff would not know these were chosen on purpose: 1. NO fallback delivery route is implemented, deliberately. R2 offered either the diagnostic or a composer-independent delivery route. Six candidate routes were evaluated and every one violates the hard safety property that we never type into a pane that might hold real input: typing on a "provably chrome" verdict needs a general proof that does not exist; herdr agent prompt drives the same PTY so it either merges with or destroys the captain's draft; baseline identity is sound but can never arm in the wedge it would fix (proof needs a confirmed submit or an affirmative empty verdict, and the incident had zero of both across 9.5 hours); cross-pane identity against a crewmate pane rests on an assumption AGENTS.md hard rule 4 contradicts and ends in typing on a probabilistic argument; a fresh pane hosts a second firstmate that the per-home session lock refuses. R2 itself names the diagnostic alone as the accepted minimum in that case, and firstmate approved shipping exactly that. Do NOT flag the absence of a delivery route as incomplete work. 2. The diagnostic does NOT gate on the backend independently reporting idle, even though R2's wording mentions it. That needs no new gate: inject_msg already returns early on pane_is_busy, which consults the backend's native busy state before the harness busy footer, so every deferral reaching the composer guard is already proven not-busy by both signals. The native state is recorded as evidence instead, because only herdr exposes a real native busy state (tmux returns unknown) and gating on an affirmative idle would make the diagnostic never fire on the tmux reference backend, which the diagnosed defect affected identically. 3. The new test fixture deliberately does NOT use the U+00A0 that caused the diagnosed wedge. The root-cause fix (R1) is being shipped in parallel and normalizes Unicode blanks in the shared classifier, so once it lands an NBSP row reads empty and an NBSP fixture would silently stop reproducing the identical-verdict condition. Stable non-blank content models what R2 actually targets: the NEXT systematic misclassification, not the one R1 fixes. This change adds NO blank normalization of its own and must not duplicate R1's. 4. Row bytes are recorded as hex rather than raw, and every field is bounded to 120 bytes with an explicit truncation marker. Both are safety choices, not style: a composer row can contain the terminal's own escape sequences and a diagnostic record is read with cat, so hex can never replay an escape into the reader's terminal; and the row can hold the captain's own unsent draft, so it must be bounded. For the same reason the wedge alert summary carries only the verdict, reader, and streak and never the row bytes, because that string is passed to an OS notifier or a configured command: directive. 5. The diagnostic sink lives in bin/fm-composer-lib.sh and is opt-in via FM_COMPOSER_DIAG_FILE, inert otherwise. Each reader calls it once where it already holds both the raw styled row and the ghost-stripped content. This is to honor the repo's one-owner rule: re-deriving composer row location in the daemon would duplicate exactly the logic that has drifted across adapters twice before. The daemon arms the sink only once already deep in a streak, so the recorded row comes from the same read as the recorded verdict rather than a second read. 6. Scope also includes two additions firstmate explicitly approved beyond R2's literal wording: a bounded sanitized pane tail when the reader found no candidate composer row at all (the dead-shell / unreadable class, which has no offending row but wedges just as permanently), and surfacing the record as away-return catch-up evidence so the captain's next investigation does not have to rediscover it. 7. Only tmux and herdr can be supervisor panes (the daemon refuses others loudly at startup), so those two readers are the complete affected set. The orca, cmux, and zellij composer surfaces were inspected and deliberately left unchanged; the sink is inert without the env var so their behavior is unchanged bit for bit. Verification already performed locally: bin/fm-lint.sh clean, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh clean, and 52 suites run. Sixteen new tests added across tests/fm-daemon.test.sh, tests/fm-composer-lib.test.sh, and tests/fm-afk-return.test.sh, all green. Four suites fail, and each was individually reproduced as identical at the base commit a2d5f26, so none is caused by this change: fm-calm-pi-extension, fm-pi-watch-extension, and fm-turnend-guard share one node ESM environment fault in the Pi tooling, and fm-watcher-lock is a watcher-singleton timing test perturbed by sibling firstmate lanes' live watchers on this host. tests/fm-backend-tmux-smoke.test.sh was excluded because it needs a real tmux server and hangs at the base commit too, and the real-herdr-gated family was excluded because this task's brief was scaffolded without the Herdr lab guard and must not drive Herdr lifecycle. ## What Changed - The away-mode daemon (`bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh`) now tracks consecutive identical non-empty composer verdicts across deferred escalation deliveries in a durable streak file that survives daemon restarts. After `FM_COMPOSER_DEFER_DIAG_COUNT` identical verdicts (default 20, `0` disables), it writes a diagnostic record — verdict, reader, streak, native busy state, and the offending row's sanitized bytes — to `state/.subsuper-composer-defer-diag`, the daemon log, and the wedge-alarm marker. The wedge alert summary carries only the verdict, reader, and streak, never row bytes; when the reader found no candidate row at all (dead-shell/unreadable pane), a bounded sanitized pane tail is recorded instead. Deliberately no fallback delivery route is added — the diagnostic alone is the approved scope. - `bin/fm-composer-lib.sh` gains an opt-in diagnostic sink (`fm_composer_diag_record`, armed via `FM_COMPOSER_DIAG_FILE`, inert otherwise) that the tmux and herdr composer readers call at the point they already hold both the raw styled row and the ghost-stripped content. Row bytes are rendered as hex and every field is bounded to 120 bytes with an explicit truncation marker, so a record read with `cat` can never replay terminal escapes and never leaks an unbounded captain draft. - Away-mode entry/return now manage the new artifacts: `fm-afk-return.sh` surfaces the diagnostic as catch-up evidence and clears it, and a fresh away entry clears stale diagnostics too, with the launcher's transactional backup/rollback extended to cover them. Docs (`docs/wedge-alarm.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, the afk skill) describe the new behavior, and 16 new tests cover the threshold trigger, streak reset/restart survival, sanitization bounds, wedge-marker/alarm content, and return-side surfacing. The no-mistakes review pass also fixed a stderr leak from the streak-file read that would have printed on every healthy delivery. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The round-1 fix commit resolves both prior findings precisely as instructed — a readability guard replacing the broken redirection-order suppression with identical fallback semantics plus a behavioral stderr regression test, and a comment-only correction of the diag sink contract — leaving the branch intent-conformant with no remaining issues. ## Testing Ran the three touched suites (fm-composer-lib, fm-daemon, fm-afk-return — all green, covering the 16 new tests) and a manual end-to-end demo through the real daemon inject path: five identical pending deferrals build the durable streak, the diagnostic records at the threshold with verdict/reader/bounded hex row bytes and native busy state as evidence, nothing is typed into the pane holding the draft, the wedge marker and daemon log carry the record, the notifier summary carries only verdict/reader/streak (no row bytes), and away-return surfaces the record as catch-up evidence then clears it; diff checks confirmed no delivery route and no blank normalization were added.
Evidence: End-to-end wedge lifecycle transcript (deferrals → diagnostic → wedge alarm → return catch-up → clear) === 5 daemon inject attempts (FM_COMPOSER_DEFER_DIAG_COUNT=5) === attempt 1: deferred;
