title: feat(bin): replace busy heuristics with semantic lifecycle state
body:
## Intent Ship the captain-approved semantic busy-state redesign for Firstmate (approved 2026-07-28, baseline data/fm-busy-signal-audit-r1/report.md). Goal: stop depending on per-vendor terminal UI regexes to decide whether a worker is busy, and replace them with one coherent contract where each harness adapter reports its own turn lifecycle through a machine-readable source the vendor already exposes. Binding design decisions made by the captain, which the diff deliberately follows and which a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: - Per-adapter semantic sources with EXPLICIT source attribution on every classification; no global OR of every vendor regex. - Missing, malformed, stale, unsupported, or unverified semantic data must classify as unknown, NEVER idle - and unknown must never be promoted to busy either. Consumers act only on an exact busy verdict, so an unreadable worker surfaces for inspection rather than being absorbed as still-working or written off as finished. Collapsing unknown into a Boolean to keep an old API was explicitly ruled out. - Endpoint death is the ONLY process-level override, and it yields dead, never busy. Child processes, CPU, process sleep state, and marker mtimes are explicitly forbidden as primary state signals (the audit found live false positives and false negatives for each). - state/.turn-ended files must remain wake NOTIFICATIONS, not reinterpreted as authoritative current state. - Adapter order: Pi -> OpenCode -> Claude -> Codex -> Grok, delivered as one ship with adapter-by-adapter commits. - Grok deliberately KEEPS a rendered-tail regex fallback because its structured lifecycle could not be credited-live-verified in the audit (the account hit a weekly limit). That fallback is isolated so it can only ever classify a Grok task. This is intentional, not an oversight. - Standalone Kimi is in scope but must prefer Wire request lifetime or documented hooks; inventing a Kimi UI regex was explicitly forbidden. What I implemented: bin/fm-busy-lib.sh is the single contract owner (verdict plus source, per-harness trusted sources, verification gates) and bin/fm-busy-event.sh is its only writer. Records are bound to an incarnation token minted at spawn, so a late event from a superseded incarnation is rejected and a leftover record classifies unknown. Pi/pi-signed use agent_start plus agent_settled confirmed by ctx.isIdle(); OpenCode uses semantic session.status (busy and retry active, idle idle) latched to the worker's own session so a subagent child cannot clear it; Claude uses UserPromptSubmit plus Stop, StopFailure, and SessionEnd. These three were live-verified against real turns on Pi 0.82.0, OpenCode 1.17.18, and Claude Code 2.1.220. Deliberate deviation worth reviewing carefully: Codex ships as unknown behind explicit probes rather than wired. The approved plan preferred the app-server turn lifecycle with capability negotiation and sanctioned lifecycle hooks as the intermediate, but on the installed codex-cli 0.145.0 NEITHER is reachable: the managed app-server daemon refuses to start outside the standalone install and an interactive TUI worker never attaches to it, and firstmate-written project hooks under /.codex/hooks.json never fired (interactive pane with directory trust granted, and codex exec, both with --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust) while global hooks fired in the same runs. Classifying unknown is the contract's own rule for unsupported state; wiring an unverified path would have been the failure mode this redesign exists to prevent. Standalone Kimi is likewise unknown because no binary is installed. Both gates record exactly what evidence opens them. Consumers converted: the watcher, the crew-state reader, and the away-mode daemon now decide through the contract, and the watcher's global OR regex default is deleted. Two rendered-text readers deliberately stay OUTSIDE the contract and are documented as such because they answer a delivery question rather than a state question: the submit acknowledgement in bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh, and the secondmate pending-reply observation (secondmates are intentionally not wired with busy events because an idle secondmate pane is healthy). Both are harness-scoped, not a global union. Three defects found during the branch review and fixed with tests, unrelated to the headline feature but caught by it: teardown was deleting a project's own tracked /.codex/hooks.json (left over from the intermediate Codex wiring); bin/fm-afk-launch.sh acquired its lifecycle lock BEFORE installing signal handlers, so a signal in that window leaked the lock and would block the next away-mode launch; and the busy-record parser clobbered its sourcing caller's positional parameters and glob setting. Repo conventions followed: one-sentence-per-line tracked Markdown, plain dashes, no agent co-author, shellcheck-clean via bin/fm-lint.sh, tests colocated in tests/ as .test.sh, and maintainer-verification evidence (versions, exact commands, observed output) in docs/verification/supervision.md with task chronology kept out. Full suite 104/104 files and 1895 assertions green, plus bin/fm-lint.sh, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh, and the coverage guard. ## What Changed - Add a source-attributed semantic busy-state contract with generation-bound records, atomic lifecycle updates, stale-event rejection, and explicit busy, idle, unknown, or dead verdicts. - Wire Pi, OpenCode, and Claude lifecycle events into the contract; isolate Grok’s fallback, leave unverified Codex and Kimi state unknown, and migrate watcher, crew-state, and away-mode consumers. - Harden spawn, interrupt, teardown, and away-mode lifecycle races, preserve project-owned Codex hooks, and expand busy-state tests and verification documentation. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The source review found no remaining material defect, but the branch changes critical cross-adapter lifecycle and supervision behavior, warranting moderate residual integration risk. ## Testing The author reported a green full-suite, lint, documentation, and coverage baseline; targeted local checks then exercised real adapter wiring, source attribution, unknown/dead safety behavior, incarnation rejection, crew-state and away-mode consumers, and launch locking. All passed after fixing and regression-testing a raw missing-metadata read error; the reviewer-visible CLI transcript demonstrates the end-to-end contract.
Evidence: Semantic busy-state lifecycle transcript ```text Claude immediately after spawn => busy fm-spawn Claude after Stop hook => idle claude-hook Claude after turn-ended notification touch => idle claude-hook Claude after UserPromptSubmit hook => busy claude-hook Same Claude record classified as Pi => unknown source-mismatch Late event from superseded incarnation => rejected Current incarnation after rejected late event => busy fm-spawn Malformed semantic record => unknown malformed Grok rendered-tail fallback => busy grok-regex Claude given the same Grok footer => unknown missing Codex given a rendered busy footer => unknown codex-unverified Standalone Kimi given a rendered busy footer => unknown kimi-unverified Armed busy record with endpoint gone => dead endpoint-gone ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 5 issues found → auto-fixed (4) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:590` - The required contract says unreadable semantic state must remain unknown and must not be written off as finished. Here any non-busy verdict, including `unknown malformed`, `unknown gen-mismatch`, and unverified states, falls through to the status log, which can emit `done`, `working`, or another stale state. Preserve and surface unknown here; consult the status log only after an exact idle verdict. - 🚨 `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:587` - The intent authorizes exactly two rendered-text readers outside the contract, but this adds a third reader that decides whether the primary worker is busy from vendor UI regexes before away-mode injection. Please confirm this additional exception or replace it with an approved semantic source; as written, regex drift can incorrectly defer an escalation or permit an injection during an active turn. - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1355` - The generated Claude wiring states that firstmate-controlled interrupts clear the record, but the actual `fm-send.sh <task> --key Escape` path only sends the key and never applies `idle --source fm-interrupt`. Because Claude emits no closing hook for Escape, an interrupted turn remains busy indefinitely and can keep wakes suppressed. Update the resolved Claude key-send boundary to record idle after a successful interrupt. - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1453` - The Pi `agent_settled` handler starts the idle writer but does not return or await its promise. A following `agent_start` can therefore complete its busy write before the earlier idle child process, leaving an active turn classified idle. Return the `busyEvent` promise so Pi serializes the lifecycle edge, and add a race-focused adapter test without the current artificial delay. - 🚨 `bin/fm-teardown.sh:1240` - Teardown forcibly removes the writer lock instead of synchronizing with it. An old apply can validate its generation, have its lock deleted here, and later overwrite a newly re-armed same-ID record, defeating the incarnation guarantee. Retire the record through a lock-owning operation in the busy-event writer, or wait for and acquire the lock before removing the generation and record. 🔧 Fix: Fix semantic busy-state lifecycle races 3 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:590` - Criterion: "Missing, malformed, stale, unsupported, or unverified semantic data must classify as unknown" so an unreadable worker is not "written off as finished." The hunk handles only exact busy, then lets every unknown verdict fall through to a possibly stale status log that can emit done, working, or parked. Preserve unknown here and consult the status log only after exact idle. - 🚨 `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:587` - Criterion: "Two rendered-text readers deliberately stay OUTSIDE the contract": the submit acknowledgement and secondmate pending-reply observation. This hunk retains a third vendor-regex reader that classifies the primary worker as busy before away-mode injection. Confirm this additional product exception or replace it with an approved semantic source. - 🚨 `bin/fm-teardown.sh:1252` - The new exact-gen retirement is not idempotent when semantic data is missing. Every newly spawned converted task records `busy_gen` in metadata, so if its sidecar is absent, teardown reaches this call after killing/removing the endpoint and worktree, then `retire` fails with "no armed busy-state gen" and leaves teardown incomplete. Under the writer lock, treat an absent incarnation as already retired while still refusing a different present generation, and remove any orphan record safely. 🔧 Fix: Make busy-state retirement idempotent 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:590` - Criterion: "Missing, malformed, stale, unsupported, or unverified semantic data must classify as unknown" so an unreadable worker is not "written off as finished." The hunk handles only exact busy, then lets every unknown verdict fall through to a possibly stale status log that can emit done, working, or parked. Preserve unknown here and consult the status log only after exact idle. - 🚨 `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:587` - Criterion: "Two rendered-text readers deliberately stay OUTSIDE the contract": the submit acknowledgement and secondmate pending-reply observation. This hunk retains a third vendor-regex reader that classifies the primary worker as busy before away-mode injection. Confirm this additional product exception or replace it with an approved semantic source. 🔧 Fix: Enforce semantic state boundaries for status and injection 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:589` - The required correction says to preserve away-mode injection through an adapter-semantic primary source, but this classifies the synthetic `.primary` ID without any production path that arms or writes that record. Only the test helper creates it. Consequently Claude, OpenCode, and Pi primaries return `unknown missing` whenever idle, so `inject_msg` always defers and eventually raises wedge alarms; Herdr can prove only busy, and Grok is the sole injectable harness. Wire `.primary` into the primary session's hook/plugin/extension lifecycle with an incarnation token, or use another verified primary lifecycle source. 🔧 Fix: Restore harness-scoped away-mode busy guard ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-busy-state.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-busy-adapter-wiring.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-wake-daemon-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-afk-launch.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-wake-daemon-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh && bash tests/fm-daemon.test.sh` after the missing-metadata fix - Manual lifecycle exercise using `bin/fm-busy-event.sh` and `fm_busy_classify`, recorded in `semantic-busy-state-transcript.txt`

title: fix(herdr): place workers in the launching workspace
body:
## Intent Fix Firstmate's Herdr worker placement when presentation spaces are disabled and multiple Herdr workspaces share the display label "Firstmate". This is a Discord-originated captain request (req-33o9Fl7gvy8-CcqOcTIn_g): workers were appearing in a different Herdr space than the Firstmate the captain was watching. Required behavior the captain specified: every Herdr worker must be created in the exact same workspace as the Firstmate or second mate process that launched it; bind the authoritative current parent identity across the complete spawn handoff (exact Herdr session plus exact launching parent pane/tab/workspace as the real runtime supports); resolve and validate from that exact identity rather than searching mutable non-unique display labels or using whichever workspace is globally focused; a second mate launching its own worker gets the same guarantee; a duplicate label elsewhere in the session must be irrelevant and must never be adopted, moved, closed, or mutated; and a missing, contradictory, stale, or cross-session binding must stop safely before creating or publishing a worker endpoint rather than falling back to label selection. Explicitly ruled out by the captain, so their absence from the diff is deliberate: no automatic duplicate-workspace deletion, no label-based adoption, no new registry, no generalized assignment system, no control plane, and no unrelated Herdr cleanup. The instruction was to use the simplest direct authoritative handoff the existing Herdr runtime already exposes. Deliberate decisions made while doing the work, each of which may look surprising in the diff: 1. Scope of the refusal. Read at its widest, "a missing parent identity must refuse" would refuse every Herdr spawn made by a Firstmate that is not itself running inside Herdr - a configuration docs/herdr-backend.md documents as supported (config/backend, FM_BACKEND=herdr) and that four existing E2E suites exercise. The implementation separates the two cases: a CLAIMED pane identity (HERDR_PANE_ID present) must resolve exactly or refuse; no Herdr ancestry at all means there is no launcher workspace in existence to inherit, so the per-home labeled container stays the resolver but must now identify exactly one workspace, with two same-labeled candidates refusing rather than adopting either. Whenever Firstmate runs under Herdr - the only situation the captain's report describes - the strict exact binding is therefore mandatory. This was flagged to the captain as the one interpretive call worth review; widening it is a single conditional in fm_backend_herdr_workspace_ensure. 2. The injected HERDR_TAB_ID and HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID are deliberately NOT read as the answer, even though Herdr 0.7.5 exports them. They are creation-time snapshots, and Herdr can move a pane between tabs and workspaces afterwards without rewriting a running process's environment. Only a live pane get is the current parent, which is what the captain asked placement to bind to. 3. fm_backend_herdr_list_live and the recovery path keep their historical first-label-match behavior on purpose. They address panes already recorded in task metadata rather than choosing where new work goes, so tightening them would be scope creep with real recovery risk. 4. tmux, Zellij, cmux, Orca, and the away-mode daemon terminal launcher were each inspected before being marked not applicable: none resolves its container by searching mutable labels (tmux reuses the launcher's own $TMUX session and tmux enforces unique session names; Zellij and cmux have no per-home workspace layer; Orca creates terminals from a worktree id; fm-afk-launch.sh creates a dedicated uniquely-labeled daemon workspace). 5. Eight existing real-Herdr test suites are touched for one reason: they run against an isolated lab session while inheriting the developer terminal's own Herdr pane, which the new cross-session check correctly refuses. That is environment-dependent, not a product problem - the same suites pass on a CI runner with no Herdr pane. tests/herdr-test-safety.sh now owns herdr_forget_inherited_pane and those suites call it before exporting their lab session. 6. Two fixes in the diff are unrelated to the placement defect and are included under the repo owner's standing instruction to fix lint and test failures encountered along the way rather than leaving them: tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh had the identical class of environment leak through CLAUDECODE, which outranks PI_CODING_AGENT in bin/fm-harness.sh and made its pi-signed ancestry case resolve "claude" whenever the suite ran inside Claude Code (verified failing on a clean unmodified tree); and fm-spawn.sh's usage() printed a fixed line range that had already been truncating its own help mid-sentence before this change made it worse. The separately held PR https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/1229 was deliberately not based on, modified, merged, or advanced; it was consulted only to avoid regressing presentation-spaces-enabled behavior. Verification performed: the defect was reproduced end to end on Herdr 0.7.5 protocol 17 through an isolated bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh session by running the real bin/fm-spawn.sh inside a launcher pane in the second "firstmate" workspace (worker landed in w1 while its launcher was in w2, with an unrelated third workspace focused throughout, which also falsifies any dependence on the focused workspace), and the new regression suite was confirmed to fail on pre-fix code with exactly that symptom. Full behavior suite: 97 suites, 0 failures, 9 opt-in gate skips. bin/fm-lint.sh and bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh clean. Every lab session torn down with the default fleet session verified byte-identical. ## What Changed - Bind Herdr worker and presentation-space creation to the launching pane's live session, socket, tab, and workspace identity, including second-mate launches and duplicate workspace labels. - Refuse stale, contradictory, cross-session, or ambiguous placement bindings before creating or publishing worker endpoints, while preserving unique per-home placement for launches outside Herdr. - Document the exact placement contract, expand unit and real-Herdr E2E coverage and test isolation, and ensure `fm-spawn` prints its complete usage text. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The fix round closes both prior identity gaps at the shared boundaries while preserving exact-ID placement, fail-closed behavior, duplicate-sibling isolation, and documented recovery semantics. ## Testing The real Herdr E2E demonstrated exact duplicate-label placement, untouched sibling and focused workspaces, second-mate inheritance, safe refusal, teardown isolation, and unchanged default fleet state; focused contract tests covered missing, stale, contradictory, cross-session, and cross-server identities, while screenshot capture was unavailable because Herdr's rendered surface is inside a terminal app blocked by the visual-control runtime.
Evidence: Captain-visible placement evidence ```text ok - real herdr E2E: with two 'firstmate' workspaces, a worker spawned from inside the second one lands in that exact workspace ok - real herdr E2E: the duplicate-labeled sibling workspace is left entirely untouched and focus is preserved ok - real herdr E2E: a secondmate launching its own worker gets the same exact-workspace guarantee, and its same-labeled sibling is untouched ok - real herdr E2E: an ambiguous home label with no launcher identity refuses before any worker endpoint exists ok - real herdr E2E: a launcher pane that no longer exists refuses before any worker endpoint exists ```
Evidence: Full real-Herdr E2E transcript ```text FM_TEST_BEGIN 2026-07-30T19:59:38Z tests/fm-backend-herdr-launcher-workspace-e2e.test.sh family=real-herdr-gated expected_gate_skip=herdr ok - real herdr E2E: with one 'firstmate' workspace and no herdr parent, a crewmate still lands in this home's own workspace without stealing focus ok - real herdr E2E: the normal unique-label path is unchanged when the launcher's own pane identifies the workspace ok - real herdr E2E: presentation spaces still create the isolated child workspace and bind it under the launcher's exact parent, without stealing focus ok - real herdr E2E: with two 'firstmate' workspaces, a worker spawned from inside the second one lands in that exact workspace ok - real herdr E2E: the duplicate-labeled sibling workspace is left entirely untouched and focus is preserved ok - real herdr E2E: a --secondmate launch still stands up that secondmate's own workspace instead of inheriting the launcher's ok - real herdr E2E: teardown closes only the worker's own pane and leaves the launcher, its workspace, and the same-labeled sibling intact ok - real herdr E2E: isolated lab session removed and default fleet session unchanged FM_TEST_END 2026-07-30T20:00:16Z tests/fm-backend-herdr-launcher-workspace-e2e.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=37561 gate_skip=false FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=1 failed=0 skipped_gate=0 duration_ms=37618 FM_TEST_SUMMARY_FAMILY family=real-herdr-gated count=1 duration_ms=37561 failed=0 FM_TEST_SLOWEST rank=1 script=tests/fm-backend-herdr-launcher-workspace-e2e.test.sh duration_ms=37561 fm-test-run: wrote timing artifact: /var/folders/5x/4nqprlbx0518k3ybcb1sz6gr0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYT90J16WCE625YGGXY3HK96/herdr-launcher-workspace-e2e.json ```

Since pane IDs repeat across servers, the same session name can resolve an unrelated pane on another server. title: docs: warn against liveness-only virtual displays
body:
## Intent Record the general virtual-display safety hazard in Firstmate shared tracked documentation so future maintainers considering Xvfb or an equivalent do not mistake process liveness for progress. Use the documentation audience inventory and knowledge-placement tree to put the full warning in one authoritative maintainer-facing owner, without duplicating existing contracts or growing AGENTS.md unless an always-loaded trigger is truly required. State that a virtual display can turn fail-fast startup into an indefinite wait on an unrecoverable-error dialog, that liveness without bounded progress is not evidence of success, that a dialog makes liveness-only launch checks invalid, and that maintainers should prefer the application own no-GUI flag plus a bounded startup or progress probe whose timeout fails the launch. Keep Craftless and Fabric chronology and task evidence out of maintained documentation, and preserve one complete sentence per Markdown line with plain dashes. Validate the documentation audience inventory and all relevant focused documentation and link checks. ## What Changed - Added a maintainer-facing warning that virtual displays can turn fail-fast startup into an indefinite wait on an unrecoverable-error dialog, making liveness-only launch checks invalid. - Clarified that liveness without bounded progress is not evidence of success; maintainers should prefer the application's no-GUI flag and a bounded startup or progress probe whose timeout fails the launch. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a bounded documentation-only addition in the existing maintainer-architecture owner with no material issues identified. ## Testing Validated the audience inventory, owner pointers, setup routing, local links, and maintainer-facing warning placement; manually inspected the required wording and style, with CLI evidence captured. No screenshot was needed for this Markdown-only change.
Evidence: Maintainer documentation excerpt and focused checks ```text Firstmate maintainer documentation evidence ============================================ Source surface: docs/architecture.md Audience owner: maintainer-architecture (docs/documentation-audiences.json) End-user-facing excerpt (`nl -ba docs/architecture.md | sed -n '112,122p'`): 115 ### Virtual-display launch safety 117 A virtual display such as Xvfb can turn fail-fast startup into wait-forever behavior because software that would exit without a display may instead open an unrecoverable-error dialog and wait indefinitely once a display exists. 118 Process liveness is not progress, so an alive process that has made no bounded startup or operational progress is not evidence that it is working. 119 Before selecting a virtual display, determine what the application does on an unrecoverable error when a display exists; if it opens a dialog, any liveness-only launch check is invalid. 120 Prefer the application's own no-GUI flag so rejected startup exits non-zero, and require a bounded startup or progress probe whose timeout fails the launch. Focused inventory and link validation (`bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`): fm-doc-audience-check: ok surfaces=57 local_links=160 Focused regression validation (`bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh`): ok - documentation inventory classifies every maintained prose surface exactly once ok - classification, setup routing, and maintained-prose scope fail safely ok - required documentation owner pointers cannot silently disappear ok - local links resolve while dates, versions, commands, and incident prose remain semantically reviewed ```

title: feat(herdr): opt-in per-primary-home workspace label
body:
## The problem

`fm_backend_herdr_workspace_label()` returned the hardcoded constant `firstmate` for any home without a `.fm-secondmate-home` marker. Only secondmate homes got a distinct label (`2ndmate-<id>`), and there was no way to change it.

That is fine for one primary home. It breaks as soon as two primary homes share a single Herdr session: both resolve to the same `firstmate` label, so `fm_backend_herdr_workspace_find` matches the first home's workspace and the second home's crew panes are created inside it, mixed in with the first home's panes. A workspace created by hand for the second home is never a candidate, because the lookup only ever matches that one constant.

This was hit in practice, with the second home's panes landing alongside seven panes belonging to the first home.

## The change

An opt-in, local, gitignored `config/herdr-workspace-label`. A primary home that shares a Herdr session with another primary home writes its own workspace label there.

**Absent means unchanged.** An absent, empty, or whitespace-only file resolves to `firstmate`, byte for byte what it does today. This is the point of the design, not a side effect: every existing home keeps working untouched, every already-recorded task label stays valid, and there is no migration step. A second primary home opts in explicitly rather than any home being moved for it.

**A secondmate marker still wins.** `.fm-secondmate-home` is checked first and keeps precedence over the config file, so a secondmate home still resolves to `2ndmate-<id>` regardless of what the file says. The existing per-secondmate guarantee cannot be configured away. This also keeps `fm-spawn.sh` correct: it narrowly overrides the home when a primary launches a secondmate, and the marker is what that path resolves on.

The label is read fresh on every call rather than cached at load time, so it stays stable across every respawn and recovery for the life of that home.

### Accepted value shape

Deliberately conservative, since the value is passed to the Herdr CLI:

- one line, 1 to 64 characters
- drawn from `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `-`
- first character a letter or digit
- not the reserved `2ndmate-` prefix

Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; inner whitespace is rejected by the character set. That set also excludes control characters, plus `/` (the separator in the legacy `<owner>/<task> · p:<token>` presentation-child labels) and a leading `-` (which the CLI would read as a flag). `2ndmate-` is refused because that namespace belongs to secondmate homes, and a primary home claiming it would recreate the same cross-home collision this change removes. Explicitly configuring `firstmate` is accepted and idempotent.

**An unusable value refuses; it never falls back.** Falling back to `firstmate` would put the home straight back into the collision the file was written to remove, so resolution returns an error naming the file and the accepted shape, and emits no label at all. That refusal is propagated through every caller: `workspace_find`, `workspace_ensure`, `container_ensure`, `list_live`, and the spawn path. `container_ensure` resolves the label before starting a Herdr server, so a bad value refuses without side effects, and `list_live` refuses rather than reporting an empty workspace, since "no live tasks" from a home whose own label cannot be resolved would read as a fleet with nothing running.

### Not inherited

The item is deliberately absent from the inheritance allowlist in `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh`. Propagating it would put two homes back into one workspace, which is exactly what it exists to prevent. Both the config-push path and the bootstrap inheritance pass go through that explicit allowlist, so no change was needed to either; a regression assertion in the existing propagation test now pins the exclusion.

## Adoption safety, re-verified empirically

With a custom label, workspace lookup will adopt a workspace a human created by hand. That is the same shape as the 2026-07-02 incident recorded in the comment above `fm_backend_herdr_workspace_prune_seeded_default_tab`, where an adopted workspace had its live pane closed.

The existing structural gate should already make this safe: only a workspace created by that same `fm_backend_herdr_workspace_ensure` call carries a non-empty `seeded_tab_id`, and only that exact id is ever a prune candidate. Rather than assume it still holds, this was re-verified against a real Herdr 0.7.5 (protocol 17) session:

- a pre-existing workspace carrying a configured label is adopted and reports an empty seeded-tab id
- after the task tab is created, the workspace still holds both its original tab and the new one

The gate is structural rather than label-derived, so it holds for any label, not only the derived ones. That evidence is recorded in `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md` with date, version, commands, and exact output, and is captured as a permanent regression in the prune-safety end-to-end test.

## Known limitation, stated plainly

The optional, default-off presentation-space ordering step recognizes only `firstmate` and `2ndmate-*` as top-level homes. A workspace under a configured label is therefore not recognized as a top-level home by the *other* homes on that session, so when one sits between another home's block and its new child, that placement step skips with a warning and leaves the layout in Herdr's current order.

This is presentation-only and never affects a worker: ordering is best-effort, always returns success, and never fails a spawn. A complete fix would require every home's configured label, which no single home can know, so this is documented in `docs/herdr-backend.md` rather than worked around.

## Tests

- 13 new cases in `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh`, all driving the public function surface rather than asserting source text: absent/empty/whitespace-only stays `firstmate`, a valid value wins, trimming, two primary homes not colliding, the secondmate marker beating a configured label, every rejected shape refusing loudly without falling back, and the container path creating, adopting, and refusing under a configured label
- a configured-label adoption section in `tests/fm-backend-herdr-prune-safety-e2e.test.sh`
- a second-primary-home section in `tests/fm-backend-herdr-workspace-per-home-e2e.test.sh` that drives the real spawn path end to end and asserts the crew lands in its own workspace, that recovery discovery stays scoped to it, and that cleanup closes only its own task

Three real-Herdr suites now point at a scratch config directory, because running them from a home that adopts this feature would otherwise change the very label they assert.

## Verification

- `bin/fm-lint.sh` clean (pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0)
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` ok
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` ok
- portable parallel shards 1 and 2: no failures
- real-Herdr gated family: 10 scripts, no failures, including the full presentation end-to-end suite

Two failures in the serial lane, `tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh` and `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh`, were confirmed pre-existing by stashing this branch and re-running on a clean tree. Neither touches the Herdr adapter.

## Documentation

Following the one-owner rule: `docs/configuration.md` owns the schema and per-field semantics, `docs/herdr-backend.md` owns the behavior description and cross-references it, `AGENTS.md` gets one line in its layout listing, and `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md` holds the empirical record.

title: fix(herdr): stop Broken-pipe stderr noise on every capability probe
body:
## Intent Fix the 'printf: write error: Broken pipe' stderr noise the herdr backend writes on every capability check. Root cause: fm_backend_herdr_events_capable in bin/backends/herdr.sh piped the large API schema into 'grep -Fq'; grep -q exits on first match and closes the read end of the pipe while printf is still writing, so printf gets EPIPE and prints the broken-pipe message to stderr on essentially every watcher cycle. Fix: replace the two printf|grep -Fq lines with in-memory 'case $schema in *token*' substring globs - no subshell, no pipe, no early-closing reader, so no EPIPE, and faster. Behavior must NOT change: the case glob is semantically identical to grep -F (literal substring match), returning success only when BOTH events.subscribe and pane.agent_status_changed are present and return 1 otherwise; neither token contains a glob metacharacter so the match is equivalent - detection unchanged, not weakened. The one other pipe-into-grep in the file (a grep -qE regex on a single stripped terminal line) is a tiny buffer that never overflows the pipe, produces no such noise, and can't take the same substring fix, so it was left unchanged. Added three colocated regression tests in tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh proving both-tokens-present is capable, either-token-missing is not capable, and the probe leaves stderr clean; the clean-stderr test runs under 'trap "" PIPE' against a >64KiB schema and was verified to fail against the old grep-piped code and pass against the fix. Firstmate-repo change to shared tracked tooling following firstmate-coding-guidelines. Delivery is via the wameson/firstmate fork (no push access to upstream kunchenguid/firstmate); the PR must be opened by no-mistakes so it carries the required signature line. ## What Changed - Replaced the two `printf '%s' "$schema" | grep -Fq ...` lines in `fm_backend_herdr_events_capable` (`bin/backends/herdr.sh`) with in-memory `case "$schema" in *token*` substring globs, so no subshell or pipe is created and `grep -q` can no longer close the read end early and trigger `printf: write error: Broken pipe` on stderr each watcher cycle. Detection is unchanged: the probe still succeeds only when both `events.subscribe` and `pane.agent_status_changed` are present. - Added three colocated regression tests in `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh` covering both-tokens-present (capable), a token missing (not capable), and a clean-stderr probe run under `trap "" PIPE` against a >64KiB schema; the stderr test was verified to fail against the old grep-piped code and pass against the fix. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A well-bounded, single-purpose fix that replaces two pipe-into-grep substring checks with semantically identical in-memory case globs, with three colocated regression tests that correctly reproduce and pin the EPIPE noise. ## Testing Exercised the herdr capability-probe fix end-to-end. The full `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh` suite passes (exit 0) with the three new colocated regression tests. I proved the fix matters and the test is meaningful by reproducing the exact end-user symptom — a 240KiB schema under `trap "" PIPE` makes the old `printf | grep -Fq` path emit `printf: write error: Broken pipe` twice to stderr, while the new `case "$schema" in *TOKEN*` globs leave stderr clean — and by reverting herdr.sh to the old code, which flips the suite to a failing `not ok - capability probe emitted 'Broken pipe'` (exit 1). Detection is confirmed unchanged (capable iff both tokens present). This is a shell/CLI-only change with no user-visible UI surface, so a CLI/stderr transcript is the appropriate evidence rather than a screenshot. Worktree restored clean; no transient artifacts left behind.
Evidence: Old-vs-new stderr behavior (240KiB schema under trap '' PIPE) ```text schema size (bytes): 240043 === OLD code (printf | grep -Fq) === stderr: bash: printf: write error: Broken pipe (x2, one per token) === NEW code (case glob) === stderr: ```
Evidence: Regression test catches old code (suite run against reverted herdr.sh) ```text suite exit=1 not ok - capability probe emitted 'Broken pipe' on stderr: .../bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 2559: printf: write error: Broken pipe .../bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 2560: printf: write error: Broken pipe ```
Evidence: Full evidence transcript ```text herdr Broken-pipe capability-probe fix — end-to-end evidence ============================================================ SYMPTOM REPRODUCTION (240KiB schema, under `trap "" PIPE` like the real watcher) OLD code — `printf '%s' "$schema" | grep -Fq TOKEN`: bash: line 3: printf: write error: Broken pipe bash: line 4: printf: write error: Broken pipe (one line PER token PER probe — emitted on essentially every watcher cycle) NEW code — `case "$schema" in *TOKEN*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac`: DETECTION UNCHANGED (bin/backends/herdr.sh fm_backend_herdr_events_capable): both tokens present -> capable (rc 0) events.subscribe missing -> not capable (rc 1) pane.agent_status_changed miss -> not capable (rc 1) REGRESSION TEST VALIDATED BOTH DIRECTIONS (tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh): against the FIX : ok - ...both tokens present -> capable, with no Broken-pipe stderr noise ok - ...missing events.subscribe -> not capable ok - ...missing pane.agent_status_changed -> not capable (full suite exit 0) against OLD code : not ok - capability probe emitted 'Broken pipe' on stderr: .../bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 2559: printf: write error: Broken pipe .../bin/backends/herdr.sh: line 2560: printf: write error: Broken pipe (full suite exit 1) ```

title: feat: support native-Windows fleet lock and add psmux session backend
body:
## Intent Sync windows-fleet-lock with origin/main and validate for collisions/regressions. Merged origin/main (39 commits, up to 930ca76) into windows-fleet-lock. Nine overlapping files auto-merged cleanly (all psmux/spawn work included: bin/backends/tmux.sh, fm-bootstrap.sh, fm-spawn.sh, fm-wake-lib.sh). Resolved 6 conflicts: (1) bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh - both sides refactored the harness-ancestry functions; combined our Windows/MSYS ancestry (CLAUDE_PID env anchor + PowerShell CIM walk) with main's POSIX refactor (fm_harness_ancestry_pids plus membership-based fm_session_lock_owned_by_self). Deliberate design choice: the Windows short-circuit now lives in the new fm_harness_ancestry_pids primitive so BOTH the lock write path and the ownership membership check inherit Windows support. (2) tests/fm-session-lock-ancestry.test.sh (new from main) - pinned FM_LOCK_OS_OVERRIDE=posix in the unit-layer lib_eval so main's fake-ps POSIX contract is exercised on any host; without it a Windows host resolves through the native WINPID path and ignores the fixture. No-op on Linux CI. (3) tests/fm-sessionstart-nudge.test.sh and 4 docs (architecture, configuration, documentation-audiences.json, sessionstart-nudge) - union of both sides; deliberately dropped main's now-stale nudge 8-parent-loop wording because post-merge both wrappers use the shared fm_session_lock_owned_by_self contract. Goal: branch fully up to date with main, no regressions. ## What Changed - Reworked session-lock harness identity into the shared `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh`, adding Windows/MSYS ancestry resolution (a `CLAUDE_PID` env anchor with a PowerShell CIM parent-chain fallback) behind a new `fm_harness_ancestry_pids` primitive, plus a membership-based `fm_session_lock_owned_by_self`; `fm-sessionstart-nudge.sh` now delegates to that contract instead of its inline `ps`/`kill` walk, and `fm-wake-lib.sh` defaults MSYS to `winsymlinks:lnk` so lock creation works on Git Bash without admin. - Added the native-Windows `psmux` session backend (`bin/backends/psmux.sh`) that reuses the tmux adapter and `fm-tmux-lib.sh` by parameterizing every `tmux` call through `FM_TMUX_CMD`, with psmux-specific `create_task` (window-id lookup, bash-shelled windows) and `current_path` normalization; wired it through `fm-backend.sh` (known/spawn lists, required tools, per-dispatch command reset) and `fm-spawn.sh` (banner-based worktree detection), plus a `winget` install hint in `fm-bootstrap.sh`. - Added psmux smoke and worktree-banner tests and expanded the nudge tests, pinned `FM_LOCK_OS_OVERRIDE=posix` in the ancestry test, and added `docs/psmux-backend.md` alongside updates to the architecture, configuration, scripts, sessionstart-nudge, and top-level docs. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The merge sync is clean and well-bounded: no conflict markers, write/read lock identity is consistent and fail-closed on Windows, FM_TMUX_CMD reset is symmetric across mixed-backend dispatch, docs are internally consistent, tests assert observable behavior, and every required intent constraint is satisfied with no forbidden behavior introduced. ## Testing Baseline: no repo-wide suite was run (targeted validation only). I ran the ancestry unit layer (4 cases pass) and, because this is a real native-Windows/MSYS host — the exact platform this branch targets and one Linux CI cannot reproduce — I drove the merged fm-session-lock-lib.sh contract end-to-end against a genuine live claude.exe process, proving the shared fm_harness_ancestry_pids primitive short-circuits to the harness WINPID and that both the lock write path and the ownership membership check inherit it, with correct fail-closed behavior. I then exercised the real fm-sessionstart-nudge.sh wrapper on Windows and confirmed it is silent when the current harness owns the lock and emits the marked nudge line otherwise, directly validating the merge goal that both wrappers use the shared ownership contract. The ancestry e2e cases and the OpenCode-plugin case cannot execute on native Windows (MSYS fork/orphan-to-init and Node spawning a .sh shebang); they are unchanged from main, Linux-CI-only, and already noted as no-op in Round 1, so remote CI owns them. No regressions found.
Evidence: Windows ancestry contract e2e (log) == live harness process: bash job -> claude.exe WINPID 19808 == 1. fm_harness_ancestry_pids -> 19808 (short-circuits to WINPID from CLAUDE_PID anchor) 2. fm_harness_ancestry_pid (LOCK WRITE path) -> 19808 3. fm_session_lock_owned_by_self (MEMBERSHIP check) -> OWNED 4. foreign lock (999999) -> correctly rejected 5. fm_harness_pid_alive: live claude.exe OK, dead/unrelated pid rejected 6. after killing the harness -> liveness fails closed ALL WINDOWS ANCESTRY CHECKS PASSED ```text == live harness process: bash job 8929 -> claude.exe WINPID 19808 == -- 1. fm_harness_ancestry_pids (the shared primitive) -- resolved harness ancestry: 19808 OK: short-circuits to the harness WINPID from the CLAUDE_PID anchor -- 2. fm_harness_ancestry_pid (LOCK WRITE path inherits Windows support) -- pid to write into .lock: 19808 OK -- 3. fm_session_lock_owned_by_self (MEMBERSHIP check inherits Windows support) -- OK: a lock naming our resolved harness WINPID reads as OWNED -- 4. fail-closed: a lock owned by an UNRELATED pid must NOT be claimed -- OK: foreign lock correctly rejected -- 5. fm_harness_pid_alive on Windows recognizes the live harness -- OK: live claude.exe WINPID recognized as a harness OK: dead/unrelated pid correctly not a harness -- 6. fail-closed when the harness anchor is gone (kill the process) -- OK: once the harness process exits, liveness fails closed ALL WINDOWS ANCESTRY CHECKS PASSED ```
Evidence: Real nudge wrapper on Windows e2e (log) == live claude.exe harness WINPID: 20636 == Case A: lock owned by THIS harness -> exit=0 output=[] -> SILENT (session already ran) OK Case B: lock owned by UNRELATED pid -> exit=0, output starts e2 81 a3 (U+2063 marker) -> nudged to take the helm OK REAL NUDGE WRAPPER BEHAVES CORRECTLY ON WINDOWS ```text == live claude.exe harness WINPID: 20636 == -- Case A: lock owned by THIS harness -> nudge must be SILENT -- exit=0 output=[] OK: owned lock -> silent (session already ran) -- Case B: lock owned by an UNRELATED pid -> nudge must be EMITTED -- exit=0 output bytes 0-3 (U+2063 operational marker expected): e2 81 a3 OK: unowned lock -> genuine primary is nudged to take the helm REAL NUDGE WRAPPER BEHAVES CORRECTLY ON WINDOWS ```
Evidence: Ancestry unit cases (log) ok - session-lock: a version-named Claude Code session is identified from its install path and argv[0] ok - session-lock: ordinary script paths under a harness directory are not harness processes ok - session-lock: ownership stops at the first non-harness gap above the contiguous run ok - session-lock: a live version-named session holding the lock is not mistaken for a stale owner ```text $ bash tests/fm-session-lock-ancestry.test.sh ok - session-lock: a version-named Claude Code session is identified from its install path and argv[0] ok - session-lock: ordinary script paths under a harness directory are not harness processes ok - session-lock: ownership stops at the first non-harness gap above the contiguous run ok - session-lock: a live version-named session holding the lock is not mistaken for a stale owner # The 4 unit cases exercise the merged fm_harness_ancestry_pids primitive # (and both its consumers, fm_harness_ancestry_pid + fm_session_lock_owned_by_self) # via the deterministic fake-ps POSIX path, pinned by FM_LOCK_OS_OVERRIDE=posix. # All pass on this native-Windows/MSYS host. # # The 3 end-to-end cases that follow (test_e2e_*) rely on MSYS emulating fork() # and orphaning a fixture tree to init(pid 1); that reparent-to-init contract # does not hold on native Windows, so those cases hang here. They are # Linux-CI-only and are covered by the authoritative remote CI. They were # NOT run to completion on this host (process stopped after the unit layer). ```
Evidence: Windows ancestry e2e harness (script) ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # End-to-end demonstration of the merged Windows harness-ancestry contract on a # REAL native-Windows / MSYS host (the platform this branch targets, which # Linux CI cannot exercise). Proves the intent's central design choice: # the Windows short-circuit lives in fm_harness_ancestry_pids, so BOTH the lock # WRITE path (fm_harness_ancestry_pid) and the ownership MEMBERSHIP check # (fm_session_lock_owned_by_self) inherit real Windows harness resolution. set -u LIB="$1" WORK="$2" mkdir -p "$WORK/state" # A genuine live Windows process whose image name is literally claude.exe, so # the CIM/PowerShell liveness probe (_FM_PS_ALIVE) recognizes it as a harness. cp "$(command -v sleep)" "$WORK/claude.exe" "$WORK/claude.exe" 120 & BGPID=$! sleep 1 CLAUDE_WINPID=$(cat "/proc/$BGPID/winpid") echo "== live harness process: bash job $BGPID -> claude.exe WINPID $CLAUDE_WINPID ==" # Force the Windows ancestry path (real MSYS host already selects it, but be # explicit) and anchor the harness via the CLAUDE_PID env var, exactly as a # real Claude Code session exports it. export FM_LOCK_OS_OVERRIDE=windows export CLAUDE_PID="$CLAUDE_WINPID" # shellcheck source=/dev/null . "$LIB" echo echo "-- 1. fm_harness_ancestry_pids (the shared primitive) --" PIDS=$(fm_harness_ancestry_pids) && echo " resolved harness ancestry: $PIDS" \ || { echo " FAIL: primitive did not resolve"; exit 1; } [ "$PIDS" = "$CLAUDE_WINPID" ] || { echo " FAIL: expected $CLAUDE_WINPID"; exit 1; } echo " OK: short-circuits to the harness WINPID from the CLAUDE_PID anchor" echo echo "-- 2. fm_harness_ancestry_pid (LOCK WRITE path inherits Windows support) --" WRITTEN=$(fm_harness_ancestry_pid) && echo " pid to write into .lock: $WRITTEN" \ || { echo " FAIL"; exit 1; } [ "$WRITTEN" = "$CLAUDE_WINPID" ] || { echo " FAIL"; exit 1; } echo " OK" echo echo "-- 3. fm_session_lock_owned_by_self (MEMBERSHIP check inherits Windows support) --" printf '%s\n' "$CLAUDE_WINPID" > "$WORK/state/.lock" if fm_session_lock_owned_by_self "$WORK/state"; then echo " OK: a lock naming our resolved harness WINPID reads as OWNED" else echo " FAIL: owned lock not recognized"; exit 1 fi echo echo "-- 4. fail-closed: a lock owned by an UNRELATED pid must NOT be claimed --" printf '%s\n' 999999 > "$WORK/state/.lock" if fm_session_lock_owned_by_self "$WORK/state"; then echo " FAIL: claimed a foreign lock"; exit 1 else echo " OK: foreign lock correctly rejected" fi echo echo "-- 5. fm_harness_pid_alive on Windows recognizes the live harness --" if fm_harness_pid_alive "$CLAUDE_WINPID"; then echo " OK: live claude.exe WINPID recognized as a harness" else echo " FAIL"; exit 1 fi if fm_harness_pid_alive 999999; then echo " FAIL: dead pid recognized as harness"; exit 1 else echo " OK: dead/unrelated pid correctly not a harness" fi echo echo "-- 6. fail-closed when the harness anchor is gone (kill the process) --" kill "$BGPID" 2>/dev/null wait "$BGPID" 2>/dev/null if fm_harness_pid_alive "$CLAUDE_WINPID"; then echo " FAIL: dead harness still reported alive"; exit 1 else echo " OK: once the harness process exits, liveness fails closed" fi echo echo "ALL WINDOWS ANCESTRY CHECKS PASSED" ```
Evidence: Windows nudge wrapper e2e harness (script) ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # Drive the REAL bin/fm-sessionstart-nudge.sh product surface on a native # Windows/MSYS host. Proves the merge goal that the nudge wrapper now uses the # shared fm_session_lock_owned_by_self contract, which inherits Windows harness # resolution: a primary whose current Windows harness already holds the lock is # silent; a primary whose lock is held by an unrelated pid is nudged. set -u ROOT="$1" WORK="$2" NUDGE="$ROOT/bin/fm-sessionstart-nudge.sh" # This validation runs inside a no-mistakes gate (NO_MISTAKES_GATE=1), which the # nudge treats as a gate agent and silences unconditionally. The real suite # unsets it too; drop it so the primary-scope + lock-ownership logic is what # actually decides the outcome here. unset NO_MISTAKES_GATE HOME_DIR="$WORK/primary" mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR/bin" "$HOME_DIR/state" git init -q "$HOME_DIR" git -C "$HOME_DIR" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -q --allow-empty -m init : > "$HOME_DIR/AGENTS.md" # A live Windows process named claude.exe, anchored via CLAUDE_PID as a real # Claude Code session would export it. cp "$(command -v sleep)" "$WORK/claude.exe" "$WORK/claude.exe" 120 & BGPID=$! sleep 1 CLAUDE_WINPID=$(cat "/proc/$BGPID/winpid") echo "== live claude.exe harness WINPID: $CLAUDE_WINPID ==" echo echo "-- Case A: lock owned by THIS harness -> nudge must be SILENT --" printf '%s\n' "$CLAUDE_WINPID" > "$HOME_DIR/state/.lock" outA=$(FM_LOCK_OS_OVERRIDE=windows CLAUDE_PID="$CLAUDE_WINPID" \ FM_GATE_REFUSE_BYPASS=0 FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$HOME_DIR" FM_HOME="$HOME_DIR" \ "$NUDGE" 2>&1) rcA=$? echo " exit=$rcA output=[$outA]" { [ "$rcA" = 0 ] && [ -z "$outA" ]; } \ && echo " OK: owned lock -> silent (session already ran)" \ || { echo " FAIL"; kill "$BGPID" 2>/dev/null; exit 1; } echo echo "-- Case B: lock owned by an UNRELATED pid -> nudge must be EMITTED --" printf '%s\n' 999999 > "$HOME_DIR/state/.lock" outB=$(FM_LOCK_OS_OVERRIDE=windows CLAUDE_PID="$CLAUDE_WINPID" \ FM_GATE_REFUSE_BYPASS=0 FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$HOME_DIR" FM_HOME="$HOME_DIR" \ "$NUDGE" 2>&1) rcB=$? echo " exit=$rcB" echo " output bytes 0-3 (U+2063 operational marker expected):" printf '%s' "$outB" | head -c 3 | od -An -tx1 case "$outB" in *"Run \`bin/fm-session-start.sh\` now"*) echo " OK: unowned lock -> genuine primary is nudged to take the helm" ;; *) echo " FAIL: expected the nudge line, got [$outB]"; kill "$BGPID" 2>/dev/null; exit 1 ;; esac kill "$BGPID" 2>/dev/null wait "$BGPID" 2>/dev/null echo echo "REAL NUDGE WRAPPER BEHAVES CORRECTLY ON WINDOWS" ```
- Outcome: 🔧 2 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ across 2 runs (30m10s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ℹ️ `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh:133` - In the embedded PowerShell harness scripts (_FM_PS_ANCESTRY line ~133 and _FM_PS_ALIVE line ~154), a node/python interpreter's CommandLine is matched with `\b$h\b` where $h includes bare `pi`. GOAL: shrink firstmate's always-loaded AGENTS.md contract to only what it alone can own, and convert the review's documentation-ownership table from prose into a mechanically enforced artifact. B1+B4 - AGENTS.md section 2 was 10,777 bytes, of which a 9,407-byte fenced directory tree restated docs/configuration.md. docs/configuration.md already declares itself the single owner of the operational-home layout and explicitly delegates exact child fields to each producing script's header. Before deleting anything I verified every artifact the tree named has such an owner; several (check-trust, pr-poll-retirement, turnend-claude-blocks, the grok/kimi turn-end tokens, pr-check-quarantine) are documented ONLY in bin/ scripts and not in docs/, which is exactly what the owner's declared boundary prescribes, so their removal from AGENTS.md is correct rather than a loss. What deliberately survives is every fact with no other owner anywhere in the repo: the status-line-is-a-wake-event rule, the never-touch rule for watcher/Claude-auto-arm/sub-supervisor state under state/ (I grepped the whole repo and this instruction exists nowhere else), the check.sh execution-trust boundary, the scout report surviving teardown, and B4's corrected secondmates.md wording (created lazily by fm-home-seed.sh, so absence means no secondmate is registered rather than a lost registry). The plan targeted -6,907 bytes; the measured result is -8,019 because collapsing the tree to five safety bullets beat the estimate. The report's own section 15.2 marks its after-column byte figures as engineering targets, not measurements, so beating one is expected. B2 - AGENTS.md section 13 was a hand-maintained 2,913-byte roster of 13 agent-only skill triggers, duplicating each skill's own frontmatter description, which some harnesses inject into the session prompt unprompted. New bin/fm-skill-index.sh renders that roster from frontmatter, selecting on the existing user-invocable:false marker (verified to match the old roster exactly, 13 for 13). It is composed into the session-start digest by bin/fm-session-start.sh. DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM THE REPORT, made on safety grounds and worth not flagging as a mistake: the report's section 7.3 table lists codex and kimi as 'likely' injecting skill descriptions, but its own section 15.2 admits those cells are unverified. I suppress the generated index ONLY where injection is positively verified - claude (proved by direct observation) and grok (harness-adapters records 'firstmate skills are discovered' plus a verified end-to-end invocation) - and emit it for every other harness including unknown. The asymmetry is intentional: a redundant index only costs bytes, whereas a wrongly suppressed one silently removes every agent-only skill's load trigger. The script header documents this and requires positive evidence before adding a harness to the suppression list. Section 13 kept three sentences rather than collapsing to the report's suggested single sentence, so it fell 619 bytes short of the -2,927 target: the ownership pointer to fm-skill-index.sh and the register-once rule are contract facts a future maintainer needs, not roster. Net across AGENTS.md is -10,166 bytes, 332 better than the combined plan target. Also honestly measured and contrary to the report's estimate: the report predicted the generated index would be byte-neutral on non-injecting harnesses. It actually costs 5,329 bytes there because frontmatter descriptions are richer than the old abridged roster. Net is therefore -10,166 on claude/grok and -4,837 elsewhere - still a reduction everywhere, but not the wash predicted. This is stated plainly rather than rounded away. B3 - docs/documentation-audiences.json gains an injection field (always/lazy/generated/referenced/never) and a one-sentence responsibility for each of its 57 surfaces, and bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh now REQUIRES both, refusing rather than defaulting a missing field. The one-sentence limit on responsibility is enforced by regex and is the point of the mechanism, per the commission: a surface that needs two sentences owns too much and should be split. This makes the always-loaded set a queryable list rather than a claim, and a test asserts it stays bounded to AGENTS.md plus its CLAUDE.md symlink. CROSS-REFERENCES updated for the one-owner rule: firstmate-coding-guidelines and fmx-respond skills pointed at 'section 13' as the place to register a trigger; README.md said triggers are named in AGENTS.md; docs/scripts.md gains a row for the new script. All corrected in the same change. CERTIFICATION already run locally: the plan requires a session-start smoke read for B1 proving no operator action lost its instruction - done under both a claude and an opencode primary, walking each instruction the removed tree carried. New tests/fm-skill-index.test.sh (6 cases) covers suppression, emission including unknown harnesses, roster derivation independently from frontmatter, folded multi-line description rendering, and digest composition. tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh gains 2 cases for the required fields. bin/fm-lint.sh and bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh are green. KNOWN PRE-EXISTING FAILURE, not introduced here: tests/fm-session-start.test.sh has one failing case ('MISSING diagnostic did not appear at all'). I stashed this branch's changes and re-ran it on the base commit f0d7cbe, where it fails identically - it is environment-dependent tool detection, unrelated to this change. CONSTRAINTS: this is firstmate's own shared tracked material, so repo style rules apply - one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never em dash, no agent co-author on commits, bin/*.sh shellcheck-clean via bin/fm-lint.sh, tests colocated in tests/ as .test.sh extending existing runners, and tests must exercise behavior through executable interfaces rather than asserting implementation-source bytes. ## What Changed - Cut AGENTS.md by 10,166 bytes: section 2's 9,407-byte directory tree that restated `docs/configuration.md` is collapsed to five safety bullets (keeping only facts with no other owner, e.g. the status-line wake rule, the never-touch `state/` rule, and the `check.sh` trust boundary), and section 13's hand-maintained 2,913-byte roster of agent-only skill triggers is reduced to a three-sentence ownership pointer. - New `bin/fm-skill-index.sh` renders the agent-only skill roster from each skill's frontmatter (verified 13-for-13 against the old roster) and is composed into the session-start digest by `bin/fm-session-start.sh`; the generated index is suppressed only on harnesses positively verified to inject skill descriptions (claude, grok) and emitted everywhere else, including unknown harnesses. - `docs/documentation-audiences.json` gains required `injection` and one-sentence `responsibility` fields for all 57 surfaces, enforced by `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` (refuses rather than defaults a missing field), with a test asserting the always-loaded set stays bounded to AGENTS.md plus its CLAUDE.md symlink; stale "section 13" cross-references in the firstmate-coding-guidelines and fmx-respond skills, README.md, and `docs/scripts.md` are updated, and new tests cover the skill index (6 cases) and the required audience fields. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A well-bounded documentation-consolidation and tooling change whose key claims I independently verified: the generated skill index matches the removed 13-entry roster exactly, suppression is limited to the two positively verified injecting harnesses per the stated intent, the stricter inventory check passes green on the updated 57-surface inventory, removed AGENTS.md facts have confirmed owners elsewhere, and new behavior-level tests cover the suppression/emission matrix and required-field enforcement. ## Testing Ran the two new/extended test suites (12/12 cases green), then manually verified every intent claim end-to-end: skill-index emission/suppression per harness including the positive-evidence rule for unknown harnesses, real session-start digest composition under opencode vs claude primaries, doc-audience-check refusing missing injection and two-sentence responsibility fields while green on the real 57-surface inventory, exact 13-for-13 roster parity with the old hand-maintained section 13, byte deltas matching the claimed -10,166 net and -8,019 section 2, survival of all five no-other-owner facts, and corrected cross-references; the single fm-session-start.test.sh failure was reproduced identically at the base commit, confirming it pre-exists this change. No visual evidence applies - this is a CLI/docs repo and the transcripts captured are the end-user surface.

title: fix(herdr): wait for shell readiness before project allocation
body:
## Intent Fix the verified Herdr startup race that prevented BullSwing project allocation. After Herdr creates a pane, wait on the exact returned pane's process information until exactly one foreground process exists and its PID equals the shell PID for ten consecutive samples approximately 100ms apart, bounded by ten seconds, and refuse without submitting treehouse get on timeout. Keep this Herdr-only, preserve the existing post-submit two-sample project-copy cwd settlement check and all other backend behavior, do not change the default backend or broaden cleanup, document the empirical boundary in docs/herdr-backend.md, add focused readiness and non-regression tests, and validate and ship through the no-mistakes pipeline to a private Firstmate PR without merging it. ## What Changed - Wait for the exact newly created Herdr pane to report ten consecutive shell-ready samples before submitting `treehouse get`. - Enforce a ten-second wall-clock deadline, preserve timed-out panes for diagnosis, and refuse project allocation without submitting commands when readiness fails. - Document the Herdr startup boundary and add focused coverage for readiness transitions, unstable samples, stalled CLI calls, timeouts, and spawn refusal. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The follow-up enforces a wall-clock deadline around each exact-pane process query, retains the ten consecutive readiness samples, refuses before treehouse submission on timeout, and leaves the existing post-submit cwd settlement logic and other backends unchanged. ## Testing Diff inspection, the focused fake-CLI Herdr suite, and an isolated real-Herdr E2E all passed; evidence demonstrates exact-pane readiness stabilization, reset after regression, bounded stalled/ordinary timeouts, and refusal without `treehouse get`. No screenshot was produced because this is a backend/CLI behavior with no rendered UI surface.
Evidence: Focused Herdr readiness transcript Readiness waited through instability, required ten consecutive shell-ready samples, honored the timeout, and `fm-spawn` submitted no `treehouse get` on failure. ```text ok - fm_backend_herdr_version_check: accepts the current protocol (14) ok - fm_backend_herdr_version_check: refuses an old protocol loudly ok - fm_backend_herdr_version_check: refuses loudly when herdr is not installed ok - fm_backend_herdr_workspace_label: a primary home (no marker) resolves to 'firstmate' ok - fm_backend_herdr_workspace_label: a secondmate home (.fm-secondmate-home) resolves to '2ndmate-' ok - fm_backend_herdr_workspace_label: trims whitespace around the marker's secondmate id ok - fm_backend_herdr_workspace_label: an empty marker file falls back to the primary label 'firstmate' ok - fm_backend_herdr_workspace_label: two different secondmate homes get two different, non-colliding labels ok - fm_backend_herdr_cli: sets HERDR_SESSION AND appends a trailing --session flag on every call ok - fm_backend_herdr_launcher_identity: a firstmate not running inside herdr has no launcher workspace to inherit ok - fm_backend_herdr_launcher_identity: HERDR_ENV=1 without a pane id selects the backend but binds no parent ok - fm_backend_herdr_launcher_identity: resolves the launcher's exact workspace even when a same-labeled workspace sorts first ok - fm_backend_herdr_launcher_identity: refuses a launcher pane that names a different herdr session ok - fm_backend_herdr_launcher_identity: refuses a claimed pane without exact server identity ok - fm_backend_herdr_launcher_identity: refuses a launcher pane whose injected socket belongs to another herdr server ok - fm_backend_herdr_launcher_identity: refuses when the launcher's own pane no longer resolves ok - fm_backend_herdr_launcher_identity: refuses when the launcher's pane and tab disagree about their workspace ok - fm_backend_herdr_launcher_identity: refuses when the launcher's workspace is gone from its own session ok - fm_backend_herdr_workspace_ensure: places a worker in the launcher's exact workspace, not the first same-labeled one ok - fm_backend_herdr_workspace_ensure: refuses to guess between two same-labeled home workspaces ok - fm_backend_herdr_workspace_ensure: a --secondmate container resolves that home's own workspace, not the launcher's ok -
