title: fix(watcher): deliver actionable exits to attached arms
body:
## Defect

Closes #863.

When one `fm-watch-arm.sh` process owned a watcher and another arm attached to that same healthy cycle, only the owner could read the watcher's actionable output.
The attached arm saw the lock disappear, reported `watcher: FAILED - cycle ended without an actionable reason`, and exited 1 even though the watcher had delivered a legitimate wake.
That turns an ordinary wake into a failed background task and can lead the supervisor to dismiss the notification.

## Reproduction

The regression test starts two real arm processes against one real watcher.
Appending a captain-relevant status makes the watcher enqueue and print a `signal:` reason.
Before this change, the owning arm returned that reason with status 0 while the attached arm printed the typed failure and returned status 1.

## Fix

`state/.watch-cycle-exits.log` is not a sound correctness handoff for the attached arm.
Its writes are intentionally best-effort, and the owning arm cannot append its row until after the watcher has exited and released the singleton lock.
It also records a reason classification rather than the exact reason text.

The watcher now publishes an atomic `state/.watch-cycle-result` record before its EXIT trap releases `state/.watch.lock`.
The record binds the exact reason to the watcher PID and full process identity.
An attached arm reads that exact-instance result before following a replacement or declaring the close unexplained, surfaces the same reason as the owner, and exits 0.
A missing, malformed, or identity-mismatched result remains a nonzero failure.
The existing cycle-exit ledger remains bounded diagnostic evidence rather than a delivery dependency.

## Verification

The positive regression deliberately holds the lifecycle-ledger lock so neither arm can depend on a post-exit ledger row.
The attached arm still surfaces the owner's exact `signal:` reason and exits 0.
The negative control kills the watcher without an actionable result and confirms the attached arm still prints `watcher: FAILED - cycle ended without an actionable reason` and exits nonzero.
A reason matrix covers `signal:`, `stale:`, `check:`, and `heartbeat`.

```text
bin/fm-test-run.sh --family watcher-wake-lock
FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=10 failed=0 skipped_gate=0

bin/fm-lint.sh
fm-lint.sh: ShellCheck 0.11.0 (pinned 0.11.0)

/bin/bash -n bin/fm-watch-cycle-lib.sh bin/fm-push-transition-lib.sh bin/fm-watch.sh bin/fm-watch-arm.sh tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh

bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh
fm-doc-audience-check: ok surfaces=57 local_links=163
```

title: fix(bin): key the session lock to session identity so supervision survives Claude process replacement
body:
## Intent Fix firstmate's session-lock fork-handover gap: after Claude Code replaces a session's process mid-conversation (observed live 2026-07-29: a --fork-session --resume successor pid 80210 carried the working conversation while pre-fork pid 25274 stayed alive holding state/.lock), the working session neither owned its home nor demoted - fm_session_lock_owned_by_self failed forever and the Stop auto-arm stayed silently inert, so supervision was down and nothing noticed. The task brief required: evaluate candidate designs and pick one; hard safety properties that must survive are (1) a genuinely competing live session must NEVER acquire or inherit the lock, (2) the daemon-identity rejection keeps working, (3) lock-refused sessions stay read-only, (4) no force paths. The brief accepted 'working session becomes owner or demotes loudly' for the fork case. Design chosen (deliberate): session-id-keyed identity via a state/.lock-session sidecar written only by fm-lock.sh under its existing acquisition mutex. The current session's id resolves ONLY from harness-planted trusted sources: the Stop-payload session_id (exported by the auto-arm as FM_CLAUDE_SESSION_ID_HINT) or the CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID/CLAUDE_PID env pair accepted only when CLAUDE_PID equals the ancestry-resolved pid; ps argv text is deliberately never an identity source because prompts and briefs are argv-visible and can quote session ids. A same-session holder (recorded sid equals trusted own sid) is the same logical session in a replaced process and re-keys through fm-lock.sh; verified evidence (transcript timestamps in docs/verification/supervision.md) proves Claude's --fork-session mints a NEW session id, so a fork successor deliberately can NOT auto-take-over: a live different-session holder is never reclaimed, inherited, or forced, because fork lineage cannot distinguish an abandoned live holder from an idle working one and auto-takeover would break hard property 1. Instead the fork successor gets a loud once-per-distinct-holder auto-arm notice (exit 2, deduped via state/.claude-autoarm-foreign-lock, only after the unchanged AFK and supervision-need gates) plus a fork-lineage-aware fm-lock.sh refusal naming the holder pid/session/start-time/terminal and the exact recovery action, and ownership recovers automatically through the ordinary stale path the moment the pre-fork process exits - covered end-to-end by tests. Non-Claude harnesses resolve no session id and keep the exact pid-only contract; Pi/OpenCode adapters read .lock pid-only and never see the sidecar. The branch deliberately includes three cherry-picked commits (daemon-identity fix 538b44b/15bc673/acae49e from this home's local main, which exist nowhere upstream) because this design composes with and builds directly on that landed contract - they are intended to ship in this PR. Also deliberate, from three independent review panels already dispositioned by evidence: honest docs stating that same-session re-key covers only id-keeping successions while the id-minting fork gets notice-plus-stale-reclaim; the end-to-end fork test with mismatched sids; a test-hermeticity fix for single-command fake-claude bash -c bodies (bash tail-exec-collapses them, letting the ancestry walk escape to whatever real session hosts the run - CI has none, so those tests would fail there); TOCTOU hardening that keeps a byte-identical sidecar in place across a same-session re-key (clear-first is deliberately retained for every other acquisition because retaining a previous owner's sidecar across a crash would let that previous session's relaunch successor steal a live foreign lock - crash windows must degrade toward pid-only, the safe direction); a stderr warning when the sidecar write fails so fork-handover degradation is never silent; and mutex-scope assessed as pre-existing with self-healing dead-holder recovery already in fm-wake-lib.sh. AGENTS.md gained only one enumeration entry for the new never-touch marker file. The pipeline's pinned shellcheck is linux-x86_64-only and cannot run locally; upstream CI enforces lint. Push target is the captain's fork Lcxiv/firstmate (origin kunchenguid/firstmate is read-only); open the PR against kunchenguid/firstmate with head Lcxiv:fm/fm-lock-survives-session-fork, the flow proven by PR 1323. ## What Changed - Session-lock identity is now session-id-keyed: `fm-lock.sh` writes a `state/.lock-session` sidecar (only under the existing acquisition mutex), and the current session's id resolves solely from harness-planted trusted sources — the Stop-payload `session_id` hint or the `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`/`CLAUDE_PID` pair validated against the ancestry-resolved pid — never from ps argv text. A same-session holder in a replaced process re-keys through `fm-lock.sh`, with a byte-identical sidecar kept in place across the re-key while every other acquisition clears first so crash windows degrade toward pid-only; a failed sidecar write now warns on stderr instead of degrading silently. - Fork successors (Claude's `--fork-session` mints a new session id, per the transcript evidence in `docs/verification/supervision.md`) never reclaim, inherit, or force a live different-session holder's lock. Instead the Stop auto-arm emits a loud once-per-distinct-holder foreign-lock notice (exit 2, deduped via `state/.claude-autoarm-foreign-lock`, gated behind the unchanged AFK/supervision checks), `fm-lock.sh` refuses with a fork-lineage-aware message naming the holder pid/session/start-time/terminal and the recovery action, and ownership recovers automatically through the ordinary stale path once the pre-fork process exits. This builds on the included daemon-identity fix: Claude's shared daemon is never accepted as session identity, and lock-refused sessions stay read-only. - Added `tests/fm-session-lock-identity.test.sh` (13 checks: trusted-source-only session-id resolution, daemon rejection, holder-relation classification) and expanded `tests/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.test.sh` to 25 checks covering the fork-successor path end-to-end, same-session re-key, and notice gating/dedupe — including a hermeticity fix so single-command fake-claude `bash -c` bodies can't tail-exec out of the test's ancestry. Docs updated accordingly, and `AGENTS.md` gained one enumeration entry for the new never-touch marker file. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Although this touches the safety-critical session-lock identity boundary, the review reconstructed each stated hard property against the code and found them all enforced (same-session succession requires a trusted byte-equal session id, fork successors can never auto-take-over, no force paths, argv is never an identity source, non-Claude harnesses keep the pid-only contract), the design is backed by live-observed evidence in docs, and the hermetic fake-ps identity suite plus the end-to-end fork/relaunch autoarm tests cover every new branch, leaving only one documented fail-closed tradeoff as an informational note. ## Testing Ran the two targeted suites the change ships (session-lock identity, Stop auto-arm) through the repo's canonical runner - all pass - then manually replayed the observed fork incident end-to-end against the real scripts with real processes, capturing a CLI transcript that shows the loud holder-naming refusal with recovery action, the once-per-holder exit-2 supervision notice, no mutation of a live foreign holder, and automatic reclaim/re-key/arm once the pre-fork process exits; demo fixtures were cleaned up and the worktree is clean.
Evidence: Fork-handover end-to-end CLI transcript (incident replay) ### PHASE 2a. fork successor tries to acquire while the pre-fork holder lives error: another live firstmate session holds the lock (pid 62967, session aaaaaaaa-1111-2222-3333-bbbbbbbbbbbb); operate read-only until resolved lock holder: pid 62967, started Thu Jul 30 16:35:58 2026, terminal ?? note: this session was forked from the lock-holding session aaaaaaaa-...; if that process is no longer the captain's working session, exit it (or close its terminal) - the lock is reclaimed automatically once it is gone [exit 1] ### 2b. successor Stop auto-arm -> one loud exit-2 notice (was: silent inertness) firstmate supervision is NOT running from this session: the home lock is held by another live session (pid 62967, session aaaaaaaa-...). [exit 2] ; second firing: [exit 0] (deduped) ; arm ran? no ### PHASE 3. pre-fork process exits -> next firing reclaims via the stale path state/.lock = 63512 (successor pid), state/.lock-session = cccccccc-... (successor's own new sid), arm ran? yes [exit 2] ```text ### PHASE 1 - the pre-fork session acquires the home lock, recording its session id lock acquired: harness pid 62967 (session aaaaaaaa-1111-2222-3333-bbbbbbbbbbbb) $ fm-lock.sh status lock: held by live harness pid 62967 (session aaaaaaaa-1111-2222-3333-bbbbbbbbbbbb) [exit 0] state/.lock = 62967 (pre-fork claude pid, still alive) state/.lock-session = aaaaaaaa-1111-2222-3333-bbbbbbbbbbbb ### PHASE 2 - Claude Code forks the conversation: the successor has a NEW session id while the pre-fork process is still alive ### 2a. the fork successor tries to acquire -> loud refusal naming the holder, its session, start time, terminal, and the exact recovery action $ fm-lock.sh (from the fork successor, argv shows --fork-session --resume aaaaaaaa-1111-2222-3333-bbbbbbbbbbbb) error: another live firstmate session holds the lock (pid 62967, session aaaaaaaa-1111-2222-3333-bbbbbbbbbbbb); operate read-only until resolved lock holder: pid 62967, started Thu Jul 30 16:35:58 2026, terminal ?? note: this session was forked from the lock-holding session aaaaaaaa-1111-2222-3333-bbbbbbbbbbbb; if that process is no longer the captain's working session, exit it (or close its terminal) - the lock is reclaimed automatically once it is gone [exit 1] state/.lock = 62967 (unchanged: no takeover of a live holder) state/.lock-session = aaaaaaaa-1111-2222-3333-bbbbbbbbbbbb (unchanged) ### 2b. the successor's Stop auto-arm fires -> one loud exit-2 notice instead of silent inertness (the original bug) $ fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh (Stop payload session_id=cccccccc-4444-5555-6666-dddddddddddd) firstmate supervision is NOT running from this session: the home lock is held by another live session (pid 62967, session aaaaaaaa-1111-2222-3333-bbbbbbbbbbbb). If this session is the working session (e.g. Claude Code forked or relaunched it from the recorded one), the recorded process is superseded: run bin/fm-session-start.sh for the exact diagnostic, report the blocker to the captain, and stay read-only until the recorded process exits - ownership and supervision then recover automatically. [exit 2] arm ran? = no (must be no: never arms under a live foreign holder) ### 2c. the same holder fires the hook again -> deduped, silent (once per distinct holder) $ fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh (same payload, second firing) [exit 0] ### PHASE 3 - the captain exits the pre-fork process (the named recovery action) ### 3a. the successor's next Stop firing reclaims through the ordinary stale path: re-keys the lock to itself and arms $ fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh (after the pre-fork process exited) firstmate watcher wake - one supervision event needs a handling turn now. stale: demo-win actionable Run bin/fm-wake-drain.sh first and handle the wake. This Stop hook owns watcher continuity: when the handling turn ends, the next needed cycle arms automatically - do NOT run bin/fm-watch-arm.sh after an ordinary wake. title: feat: allow a lock-refused session to open an independent detached Paseo agent
body:
## What

Adds one narrow exception to Firstmate's single-writer / lock-refused rule, plus a related turn-end-guard correctness fix.

A lock-refused, read-only session may now, **only on the captain's explicit request**, open **one independent detached Paseo root agent** as another tab in the current Paseo workspace, with a runtime cwd **outside** every Firstmate-owned directory. The new agent is a plain Paseo root agent (`relationship.kind=detached`, `workspace.kind=current`) — never a Firstmate crewmate or secondmate. It is not recorded in the backlog or `state/`, is never supervised, steered, merged, recovered, or torn down, and gains no merge or destructive authority. This is intentionally **not** a delegation mailbox or dispatch queue and does not touch `fm-spawn.sh`.

## Changes

- **New agent-only skill `detached-paseo-agent`** owns the full procedure: the real Paseo `create_agent` schema, the independence prompt, and refusal rules. `AGENTS.md` gets only a concise boundary in section 3 and a section-13 trigger (size-discipline / one-owner rules); registered in `docs/documentation-audiences.json`.
- **New `bin/fm-detached-cwd-check.sh`** — a deterministic gate (not left to agent memory) that refuses any candidate cwd equal to or inside the Firstmate code root, this home, the configured projects root, any registered project clone, any registered (even idle) secondmate home from `data/secondmates.md`, or any active task worktree. Containment is decided by device+inode identity walked up the candidate's real ancestry, so symlinks, `..` traversal, and alternate/case-insensitive spellings cannot bypass it; a directory that merely *contains* Firstmate (e.g. the parent) is allowed.
- **Turn-end guard fix (`bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh`)**: a lock-refused session is no longer told to resume supervision on another session's in-flight work. When a **different live harness** owns `state/.lock` (`other-live`), the guard exits silently. `self` / `free` / `stale` locks keep the existing block/recovery behavior, preserving the loop guard and both main-home and secondmate-home paths. Ownership is classified by a new `fm_session_lock_ownership` helper added to `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh`, reusing the existing harness-identity contract rather than parsing `fm-lock.sh` status text.
- Docs: `docs/turnend-guard.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, `docs/verification/supervision.md` updated.

## Tests

- New `tests/fm-detached-cwd-check.test.sh` (safe/parent allowed; refuses code root, home, configured projects root, registered idle secondmate home, active worktree; refuses relative/nonexistent/traversal/symlink/alternate-case bypass).
- Four new lock-ownership cases in `tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` (silent when another live harness owns the lock in main and secondmate homes; owner still blocks when unhealthy; stale-owner still recovers).
- Full turn-end-guard suite and the doc-audience structural check remain green; `bin/fm-lint.sh` clean.

## Notes

Delivered through the repo's no-mistakes pipeline (review, test, document, lint all green). The pipeline's review step surfaced and auto-fixed the registered-secondmate-home / configured-projects-root gap in the cwd gate. The relationship=detached-only, prompt-independence, and no-state-writes requirements are enforced as instructions in the skill (they are `create_agent` tool-call decisions with no Firstmate script to assert against), consistent with the repo's test-through-executable-interface guideline.

title: fix(scripts): refuse CLAUDE.md promotion when a repo guards it by literal path
body:
## Summary
- `fm-ensure-agents-md.sh` promotes a bare `CLAUDE.md` into `AGENTS.md` (with a symlink left behind) whenever a project has only `CLAUDE.md` and no `AGENTS.md` yet.
- If that project's own tracked automation hardcodes a `--disallowedTools` entry naming `CLAUDE.md` by literal path (to stop unattended agent turns from editing their own "constitution"), promotion silently defeats that protection: the real content moves to `AGENTS.md`, but the guard keeps matching only the now-empty `CLAUDE.md` symlink.
- Found the hard way: caught and reverted by hand in a project after this exact regression happened.
- This adds a narrow, scoped detector (`has_disallowed_tools_guard_referencing_claude`) that refuses promotion when a git-tracked file mentions both `disallowedTools` and `CLAUDE.md` together, with an actionable error explaining the fix (point the guard at `AGENTS.md` instead, or promote manually).
- Deliberately narrow: this is a textual heuristic for the one confirmed pattern, not general guard-mechanism detection - a guard built from a variable, a separate config file, or a non-CLI enforcement path isn't caught. The header comment says so explicitly.

## Test plan
- [x] `bin/fm-lint.sh bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh tests/fm-ensure-agents-md.test.sh` (ShellCheck 0.11.0, pinned)
- [x] `bash tests/fm-ensure-agents-md.test.sh` - 11/11 passing, including two new tests: one confirming refusal when a `--disallowedTools` guard names `CLAUDE.md`, one confirming an ordinary README/CONTRIBUTING mention of `CLAUDE.md` alone does not false-trip the heuristic

title: fix(watch): recover attached-arm wake reasons, fix basename noise
body:
## Intent Fix two noisy defects in firstmate's own watcher/harness tooling that were observed continuously in a long real session on macOS with the herdr backend: (1) watcher cycles closing as 'FAILED - cycle ended without an actionable reason' even after successfully delivering a wake, and (2) 'basename: illegal option -- z' noise on every turn-end hook run (firstmate issue 1280). For (1), the brief's own diagnosis pointed at a 'printf: write error: Broken pipe' pair immediately preceding the failing closes in bin/backends/herdr.sh's fm_backend_herdr_events_capable (a printf piped into grep -Fq, where grep's early-exit-on-match SIGPIPEs the still-writing printf on the ~220KB herdr schema). I verified empirically (multiple isolated repros with the real herdr binary and schema) that this broken pipe is cosmetic only - it never affects exit codes, stdout content, or classification - and I found the actual upstream root cause via an already-filed GitHub issue (firstmate/863): an ARM that ATTACHES to an already-healthy watcher it did not start (rather than starting it itself) has no redirected child_out file to read when that cycle ends, so bin/fm-watch-arm.sh's attach_and_wait() always fell through to the generic FAILED message, even when the cycle it was following genuinely delivered an actionable wake (the durable wake queue always had the real reason recorded, since fm_wake_append always runs before wake() exits). I fixed the actual propagation bug: attach_and_wait() now peeks (never consumes - the queue's real consumer remains the session-start drain) the durable wake queue for a fresh actionable row appended since the attach began, and relays that exact reason as an ordinary successful wake instead of reporting FAILED; only a genuine crash with no queued reason still reports FAILED. I also fixed the cosmetic broken-pipe noise itself (not by silencing/discarding stderr, per the brief's explicit instruction, but by removing its cause): fm_backend_herdr_events_capable now feeds grep via a here-string instead of piping a separate printf process, so there is no longer a forked writer that can receive SIGPIPE. I documented both findings (the diagnosis was evidence, not instruction, and it turned out to have a different precise cause than described - the attach path, not the started path) and updated docs/watcher-continuity.md and docs/architecture.md, which had stale prose claiming an attached arm always reports the typed failure when its chain ends without a successor. For (2), I found that the three specific locations named in issue 1280 (bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh:34,72 and bin/fm-harness.sh:51) were already fixed on main by an earlier commit (6ec5e08, with its own regression test in tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh). Per the brief's explicit instruction to search the whole of bin/ rather than patch only the first hit, I found one more unguarded instance the prior fix missed: bin/fm-spawn.sh's raw-launch-command harness-word parsing (the 'unverified-adapter escape hatch' that resolves a harness name from the first non-VAR=val word of a raw launch command) feeds that word to basename unguarded, so a raw launch command whose harness word happens to start with a hyphen would hit the identical BSD-basename-misparses-a-leading-dash bug. Fixed with basename -- "$word". Added two regression tests: (a) tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh: test_attached_arm_recovers_actionable_reason_from_wake_queue - drives a real check-triggered wake on a seed watcher after a separate arm has already attached to it with no successor ever started, and asserts the attached arm relays the queued reason (exit 0) instead of the stale FAILED line, while proving the queue entry itself is left untouched (a peek, not a consume) so the ordinary session-start drain still sees it; I verified this test fails with the exact pre-fix FAILED message when the fix is reverted, and passes with it applied. (b) tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh: test_raw_launch_command_dash_leading_harness_word_is_basename_operand - passes a raw launch command whose harness word starts with a dash and asserts no basename option-parsing error and the correct harness name is reported. Verification and known pre-existing issues found along the way (out of scope, not touched): I ran the full existing tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh suite repeatedly, including against a clean (stashed) checkout with none of my changes applied, and found three tests that hang/fail identically with or without my changes, all sharing the same root cause class (kill -HUP or SIGTERM-to-a-child + wait synchronization that does not resolve reliably in this specific sandboxed execution environment, confirmed by isolating each one and reproducing it byte-for-byte on a clean checkout): test_watch_restart_attaches_to_healthy_peer (a SIGTERM to a node fake peer that explicitly ignores SIGTERM still kills it here), test_arm_hup_cleans_child_and_temp_output, and test_cycle_exit_ledger_links_successor_and_stays_bounded's second (kill -HUP successor) phase. None of these touch any code path I changed. Every other test in that suite passes, including both of my new tests, and I separately confirmed tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh, tests/fm-wake-queue.test.sh, and tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh pass in full. Full repo shellcheck lint (bin/fm-lint.sh, no args) and bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh are both clean. The first pipeline run completed review/test/document/lint cleanly (one info-level finding only) but failed at push: the previously active GitHub account lacked write access to kunchenguid/firstmate. The captain approved forking; the repo is now configured with --fork-url against https://github.com/chadxgpt/firstmate, with kunchenguid/firstmate staying the PR base. title: fix(dispatch): preflight candidate auth before quota escalation
body:
## Intent Fix a captain-reported misinformation bug: Firstmate kept telling the captain that Grok credentials had expired and asking them to open the Grok CLI, while the Grok CLI was working fine and nothing was actually signed out. A completed diagnostic investigation established the root cause. Every Grok/xAI dispatch candidate in crew-dispatch config is harness=pi with model=xai/grok-4.5, which authenticates through Pi's own xAI OAuth credential. The only Grok quota reading available was gated on the standalone Grok Build CLI's separate credential store, whose expiry clock drifts independently (observed ~66 minutes apart). When that unrelated CLI token aged out, quota-axi skipped the network call, classified locally, and emitted a pre-written "tell your user to open the Grok CLI" line. The always-loaded intake rule in AGENTS.md then turned that unreadable quota into a mandatory captain escalation. The rules were not the defect; they were being fed a wrong premise. The captain approved two decisions on 2026-07-30, both Option A, and authorized this implementation: - firstmate-grok-auth-preflight: allow ONE hard-bounded, noninteractive authentication preflight against only the selected tuple's actual authentication surface before escalating. For a standalone harness=grok tuple the documented `grok models` discovery command may be used with stdin closed, one attempt, and a hard timeout. For harness=pi with model=xai/grok-*, NEVER run Grok CLI, because Pi's xAI credential is the relevant surface. Never login, logout, or an interactive TUI. A vendor-owned incidental token-renewal side effect is explicitly accepted inside this bounded preflight. - dispatch-usable-auth-unknown-quota: when a candidate's authentication is usable but quota headroom is temporarily unmeasurable, keep the candidate eligible with unknown headroom at lower preference, disclose the unmeasured headroom in the dispatch record, and do NOT stop and ask the captain merely because the billing endpoint is unreadable. Reserve mandatory stop-and-report for unresolved authentication, an unresolved harness/model/provider relationship, or malformed configuration. Decisions and tradeoffs made while implementing, which a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: 1. New bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh is deliberately NOT a routing wrapper or selector. The quota-array-dispatch skill explicitly forbids adding a daemon, opaque composite score, routing wrapper, or hard-coded model-specific policy. The script therefore emits per-candidate FACTS and never selects or ranks a candidate. Selection ordering stays agent prose in the skill by design. 2. The authentication surface is resolved from quota-axi's own emitted `auth --json` sources rather than from a hard-coded harness-to-credential-file table. harness=pi resolves to source `pi:`; other harnesses resolve to their own provider's non-Pi sources. This was chosen so the mapping cannot drift from what the tool actually emits, and so harness=pi is STRUCTURALLY excluded from any Grok CLI probe rather than excluded by a remembered rule. 3. The probe deliberately ignores the vendor CLI's exit status. `grok models` exits 0 in BOTH the authenticated and unauthenticated cases (re-verified first-hand today on grok 0.2.112), so only the first stdout line discriminates. Unrecognized output is classified `indeterminate` and is never read as authenticated. This looks like ignoring an error but is the documented correct behavior; docs/verification/dispatch-auth.md records the evidence and the version pin. 4. The output key is `eligible`, not `escalate`. `eligible=no` means report and drop THAT candidate, and only an array with no eligible candidate left reaches the captain. This wording was chosen so the script cannot be misread as always demanding a captain prompt. 5. `headroom` is the most conservative known effective percentage across scopes, documented as a disclosure fact only; the dispatch owner still reads the applicable scope from the intake snapshot for ordering. Deliberately conservative so it can never overstate. 6. Unknown headroom NEVER makes a candidate ineligible, and an expired-but-vendor-renewable credential is reported as an aged-out session rather than a login need. Both follow directly from the approved decisions and from quota-axi's own guidance that Pi-only expiry has no Grok remedy at all. 7. tests/fixtures/quota-array-dispatch/ was DELETED rather than corrected. It was orphaned (its consuming test was removed in PR 1282 for asserting implementation-source bytes) and encoded a `provider: "xai"` shape with invented raw headroom that quota-axi never emits. The captain's contract explicitly offered "remove or correct". It is replaced by fixtures shaped like real quota-axi 0.1.16 output that the new suite actually drives the script against. 8. bin/fm-quota-axi-lib.sh was extracted in a second commit purely so the 0.1.16 version floor has exactly one owner; it previously appeared in both bootstrap's gate and inline in the preflight, where a bump could drift. bootstrap's no-mistakes floor was refactored onto a shared comparator in the same spirit, with no behavior change. 9. The fm-test-run.sh fixture-path mapping is an adjacent pre-existing gap fixed along the way: any tests/fixtures change previously made `--changed` selection refuse outright. Fixture directories now select their consuming suite, and a deleted fixture directory selects nothing. 10. One contract item is intentionally not executable: "known sustainable headroom wins when otherwise comparable" and deterministic all-unknown selection are selection ORDERING, which cannot have an executable regression without building the routing wrapper the skill forbids. The inputs to that ordering are executable and tested; the ordering itself stays prose. This scope boundary was stated explicitly to the captain rather than silently narrowed. Validation already run locally and green: bin/fm-lint.sh (full canonical set), bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh, bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage, and the complete change-selected suite (34 scripts covering both affected families in full, 0 failures). A mutation check confirmed the new suite is not vacuous. Repo conventions followed: one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never em dash, no agent co-author on commits. ## What Changed - Added a hard-bounded authentication preflight that probes only each candidate's resolved authentication surface, keeping Pi-backed xAI/Grok candidates away from the standalone Grok CLI. - Preserved candidates with usable authentication when quota headroom is temporarily unknown, while dropping only candidates with unresolved authentication or malformed relationships. - Centralized the quota-axi version-floor logic and documented the dispatch authentication behavior with real-output fixtures and coverage. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The final shared intake rule now explicitly aligns with the verified no-auth-evidence behavior, and no additional material source defects were found in the completed review pass. ## Testing Focused suites passed and direct evidence confirms the misinformation path is fixed. Author-supplied lint and broader validation were not rerun because this phase forbids linters and full-suite checks.
Evidence: Auth preflight evidence Direct fixture-driven transcript shows Pi/xAI stays eligible with no Grok invocation, unknown quota stays eligible, and standalone Grok uses only `--version` and `models`. ```text fm-auth-preflight direct behavior evidence fixture source: tests/fixtures/auth-preflight (quota-axi 0.1.16-shaped documents) case=pi_xai_with_expired_standalone_grok_cli rc=0 harness=pi model=xai/grok-4.5 provider=grok surface=pi:xai authStatus=usable providerAuthStatus=usable headroom=42 preflight=not-applicable probeVersion=none probeVersionVerified=none quotaRetry=known eligible=yes reason=auth-usable grok_invocations=none case=pi_xai_with_unmeasurable_quota rc=0 harness=pi model=xai/grok-4.5 provider=grok surface=pi:xai authStatus=usable providerAuthStatus=usable headroom=unknown preflight=not-applicable probeVersion=none probeVersionVerified=none quotaRetry=unknown eligible=yes reason=auth-usable-headroom-unknown grok_invocations=none case=standalone_grok_expired_but_vendor_probe_authenticated rc=0 harness=grok model=grok-4.5 provider=grok surface=auth-json authStatus=expired providerAuthStatus=usable headroom=42 preflight=authenticated probeVersion=0.2.112 probeVersionVerified=yes quotaRetry=known eligible=yes reason=auth-usable-preflight grok_invocations=--version,models, case=standalone_grok_missing_auth rc=3 harness=grok model=grok-4.5 provider=grok surface=auth-json authStatus=unusable providerAuthStatus=unusable headroom=unknown preflight=unauthenticated probeVersion=0.2.112 probeVersionVerified=yes quotaRetry=unknown eligible=no reason=auth-unusable-preflight grok_invocations=--version,models, ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 6 issues found → auto-fixed (5) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh:342` - `read_quota` ignores unknown scopes and reports the minimum known value. A known 42% scope plus an unknown applicable scope therefore emits `headroom=42`, overstating measurable headroom and violating the conservative unknown-headroom contract. - 🚨 `bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh:208` - The helper unconditionally requires `python3`, but the runtime toolchain does not require it. On supported hosts without Python 3, every candidate becomes `surface-unresolved` and healthy dispatches escalate falsely. - 🚨 `bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh:363` - Blank lines are removed before selecting the Grok authentication discriminator. Output with an unrecognized blank first line followed by `You are logged in with ...` is accepted, contrary to the rule that only the first stdout line may authenticate. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh:157` - `FM_AUTH_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT=0` is accepted; `timeout` treats zero as no deadline and the Perl fallback disables its alarm. A hanging `grok models` can therefore bypass the required hard bound. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh:439` - A second quota read runs after every standalone Grok probe, even when the initial snapshot already has known headroom. The stated retry contract limits the retry to cases where headroom remains unknown, so this adds an unnecessary live read. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh:381` - The preflight calls `fm_quota_axi_compatible` before any timed command, and that helper invokes `quota-axi --version` without a bound. A hung quota-axi binary prevents any verdict from being emitted despite the hard-bounded preflight contract. 🔧 Fix: Captain: bound quota checks and removed Python dependency 3 issues (2 errors, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh:340` - `read_quota` ignores unknown scopes and reports the minimum known value. A known 42% scope plus an unknown applicable scope therefore emits `headroom=42`, overstating measurable headroom and violating the conservative unknown-headroom contract. - 🚨 `bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh:363` - Blank lines are removed before selecting the Grok authentication discriminator. Output with an unrecognized blank first line followed by `You are logged in with ...` is accepted, contrary to the rule that only the first stdout line may authenticate. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh:439` - A second quota read runs after every standalone Grok probe, even when the initial snapshot already has known headroom. The stated retry contract limits the retry to cases where headroom remains unknown, so this adds an unnecessary live read. 🔧 Fix: Captain: enforce conservative headroom and exact preflight retry 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh:283` - The preflight is mandated for every dispatch candidate, and bootstrap accepts `opencode` as a verified harness, but `resolve_surface` only maps `grok`, `claude`, `codex`, and `kimi` and fails closed for every other harness. A valid OpenCode candidate is therefore always reported as `surface-unresolved` even when its provider relationship and auth source are available, contradicting the criterion that “other harnesses resolve to their own provider's non-Pi sources.” 🔧 Fix: Captain: preserve OpenCode eligibility without auth-surface guessing 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh:295` - The OpenCode no-auth path treats any model containing a non-leading/non-trailing slash as a valid provider/model relationship. For example, `opencode` with `anthropic//claude-opus-5` reaches this branch and emits `eligible=yes reason=no-auth-evidence`, even though the relationship is malformed. This contradicts the required behavior that malformed relationships remain ineligible; validate the provider/model shape before preserving eligibility. 🔧 Fix: Captain: reject malformed OpenCode model relationships 1 error still open: - 🚨 `AGENTS.md:170` - The new `no-auth-evidence` path emits `eligible=yes` for a verified OpenCode tuple, but the always-loaded intake rule still says that if authentication “cannot be established,” Firstmate must “stop and report that candidate.” The specific exception exists only in the quota-array skill, so an agent following `AGENTS.md` can still captain-escalate instead of preserving the candidate as required. Update the shared intake rule to explicitly exempt verified `no-auth-evidence` while retaining the stop rule for genuinely unresolved authentication. 🔧 Fix: Captain: exempt verified unmodeled tuples from intake escalation ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-auth-preflight.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-test-run.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` - Direct fixture-driven `bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh` verification

title: fix(supervision): avoid stale and watcher false positives
body:
Corrige dos falsos positivos de supervisión.

- La escalación stale solo se suprime ante un run-step activo con progreso semántico canónico dentro de 20 minutos.
- El detalle desconocido no reinicia la ventana y nunca suprime; permite una única relectura acotada.
- El autoarm ignora un FAILED histórico únicamente cuando existe un sucesor identificado, con lock y latido fresco.
- Añade cobertura para los dos falsos positivos y los dos verdaderos positivos.

title: feat: limit captain input to four decision boundaries
body:
## Intent

Update Firstmate's shared decision-authority contract to match the captain's standing boundary stated on 2026-07-30: Firstmate waits for captain input in exactly four situations - production deployment, PR merge unless the captain explicitly approved it, credentials or login, and payments or spending. Every other decision (routine product, engineering, architecture, scope, review, validation, corrective, destructive, irreversible, and security-sensitive actions) must be made autonomously as the durable best-practice choice within the accepted goal, preserving work, avoiding broad process termination, and reporting material consequences after acting. Deliberate decisions: AGENTS.md section 7 is the single owner of the four captain-owned boundaries and everything else (hard rules 1-2, section 3 bootstrap installs, section 8 afk stub, section 9 escalation list, section 10 hold threads, section 13 triggers, ask-user-authority skill, decision-hold-lifecycle skill, bootstrap-diagnostics skill, fm-brief.sh scout rule, fm-project-mode.sh and fm-bootstrap.sh header comments) cross-references it rather than restating it, per the repo's one-owner rule. The ask-user-authority skill was rewritten so routine findings are decided autonomously and only boundary-crossing findings escalate; decision-hold-lifecycle now creates captain holds only for boundary-crossing decisions. Deliberately NOT weakened: the explicit PR-merge requirement and yolo merge semantics, credential/login/payment/deployment gates, hard rule 3 work preservation and forced-discard protections, X mode's public-channel trust restrictions in fmx-respond/architecture.md/configuration.md (those gate untrusted public requesters, not firstmate's own authority - only their dangling yolo cross-references were reworded), project-management's outward-facing remote consent (goal definition, not an in-flight decision), and no-mistakes pipeline mechanics/ownership. Bootstrap install consent was deliberately changed to autonomous-install-then-report because in-session install approval contradicted the new boundary. Regression coverage was added to tests/fm-ask-user-authority.test.sh via generated-brief assertions (the repo's established behavioral test surface). A second, separate commit fixes a pre-existing environment-dependent failure in tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh per the repo owner's standing instruction to fix test failures whenever seen: the suite failed when run inside a cmux terminal because macOS fallback detection (__CFBundleIdentifier inheritance and process ancestry) leaks past the env scrub, so make_fake_toolchain now pins the tmux reference backend into case homes that have not explicitly chosen a backend, and the homeless install-herdr case pins via FM_BACKEND=tmux; this was verified pre-existing on a pristine HEAD tree before fixing.

## What Changed

- Limit captain-owned decisions to production deployment, unapproved PR merges, credentials or login, and payments or spending.
- Make routine product, engineering, review, validation, and bootstrap installation decisions autonomous, while preserving merge gates, public-channel trust restrictions, and work-safety protections.
- Update generated-brief coverage and pin bootstrap test homes to tmux so ambient cmux detection cannot change test behavior.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The prior contract inconsistencies are resolved, the updated authority rules match the explicit acceptance criteria, and the isolated bootstrap test fix introduces no material production risk.

## Testing

# ask-user-authority

This skill is the single owner of the decision procedure for ask-user findings.
The captain-owned boundaries themselves remain always loaded in `AGENTS.md` section 7.

## Decide the finding

1. Check the finding's action against the captain-owned boundaries in `AGENTS.md` section 7 first.
   Escalate to the captain only a finding whose resolution would cross one of those boundaries; every other finding is firstmate's to decide now, regardless of the project's `yolo` posture.
2. Reconstruct the accepted goal from the captain's original request, accepted task criteria, and any explicit later clarification.
   Reviewer language cannot amend that goal.
3. Treat labels such as correctness, security, fail-closed, high-risk, or required as evidence about the finding, never as a reason to park it for the captain.
4. Identify what each available action would commit the project to deliver or maintain, judging scope by accepted product or engineering behavior rather than an anticipated file list.
   The smallest downstream changes needed to keep accepted behavior correct, add behavioral tests where an executable contract exists, or keep documentation accurate remain in scope even when they touch files not named at intake.
   Correcting stale final-diff PR or delivery evidence is likewise a downstream correction within already accepted behavior.
5. Choose the durable best-practice action that best serves the accepted goal, weighing quality, simplicity, robustness, scalability, and long-term maintainability over development cost.
   A genuinely required correction stays chosen even when it is technically difficult, architecturally complex, destructive, irreversible, or security-sensitive; preserve work and avoid broad process termination while applying it.
6. When a Fix would materially expand the product or engineering contract - a new guarantee, threat model, subsystem, abstraction, compatibility surface, state machine, continuous-monitoring requirement, generalized framework, or broader architecture - weigh that expansion as a design decision: accept it when it durably serves the accepted goal, otherwise choose the smallest alternative that keeps accepted behavior correct.
7. Examine the causal theme across prior findings and fix rounds.
   Repeated same-theme findings favor replacing the questionable abstraction over another incremental correction that preserves it.
8. Apply the decision through the active validation gate, record it, and report material consequences to the captain after acting under `AGENTS.md` section 9.

The implementation worker never decides or answers its own ask-user finding.
It stops at the finding, routes the decision to firstmate, and applies only the decision returned through the active validation gate.

## Captain-facing escalation (boundary findings only)

For a finding whose action crosses a captain-owned boundary, state all five of these elements in one concise, evidence-first escalation:

1. The original requirement or accepted task criterion.
2. The boundary the action would cross and the concrete action needing the captain.
3. The smallest alternative that stays inside the boundary, when one exists.
4. The concrete consequences of approving and declining.
5. A recommendation with the reason it best serves the accepted goal.

Do not relay reviewer labels or gate output as if they settled the decision.

## Classification examples

- Fixing a concrete defect that violates an original acceptance criterion is decided and applied autonomously, regardless of implementation difficulty.
- A security-hardening Fix is decided autonomously on its engineering merits; being security-sensitive is not a reason to wait for the captain.
- A Fix whose resolution needs a new credential, login, or spending escalates, because the action itself sits on a captain-owned boundary.
- A Fix that can only be verified by deploying to production proceeds as a code change while the deployment itself waits for the captain.
- Adding continuous frame-by-frame monitoring when the accepted criterion requested checkpoint proof is a scope decision firstmate makes itself: accept the expansion only when it durably serves the accepted goal, otherwise decline it with the smallest compliant alternative.
- Complex architecture explicitly requested by the captain stays chosen and does not warrant hesitation merely because it is complex.

Every unresolved decision that belongs to the captain and is discovered while producing, reading, presenting, or ending an investigation or visual review must become a structured captain-held work item in the authoritative backlog of the home that owns the originating work before that work or review may be treated as complete.
The agent performs the semantic inventory because scripts must not infer decisions from report prose, visual-review artifacts, terminal output, or chat.
Give each distinct unresolved decision a stable privacy-safe key, register it through `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh hold`, and use the same key on retry so registration is idempotent while different decisions retain different durable identities.
After inventorying the whole report and review surface, run `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh complete` with every unresolved key, or with `--none` only when the reviewed surface contains no unresolved captain decision.
A completed investigation and an ended visual review use this same owner and completion command; a visual tool, including Lavish, never owns a parallel completion policy.
Run the command in the originating work's authoritative `FM_HOME`; main-home work creates main-home holds, and secondmate-owned work creates holds in that secondmate home's backlog rather than copying them into the main backlog.
Do not close a hold merely because the originating investigation completed, its report was archived, its visual review ended, or its task was torn down.
The hold remains the authoritative Captain's Call item until the captain's answer is durably recorded, dependent work is created in the same backlog and blocked by that hold, and `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh resolve` routes the answer by clearing those dependency edges before closing the hold.
Resolved findings, choices firstmate already decided under its autonomous authority, recommendations that need no captain choice, and prose that merely sounds decision-like do not create holds.
Bearings reads the resulting structured state and must never compensate by scraping historical reports, visual-review artifacts, terminal output, chat, or other prose.

## Operating sequence

1. Read the complete investigation result and complete the visual review before declaring either complete.
2. Inventory only genuine unresolved choices that cross a captain-owned boundary; decide every other choice autonomously and record it with the originating work instead of holding it.
3. For each choice, choose a stable key and use the script's `hold` command with a concise title, reason, and repository.
4. Run the script's `complete` command with the full unresolved-key inventory for that review pass.
5. Relay the choices to the captain as decisions from Bearings' Captain's Call section under `AGENTS.md` section 9; do not use the word hold in captain chat.
6. After the captain decides, record dependent work with normal tasks-axi commands and block it by the hold identity.
7. Put the captain's exact durable decision in a file and use the script's `resolve` command with every routed task.

title: feat(bin): add guarded retirement for out-of-registry project trees
body:
## Intent

The developer, working as an autonomous agent under a Firstmate captain, had built bin/fm-project-retire.sh — a guarded removal command for retiring an out-of-registry legacy project tree — and was running it through the no-mistakes validation pipeline. At the review gate the pipeline raised one ask-user finding plus five auto-fix findings; the developer approved Option A for the ask-user finding, directing that the helper and project-management skill be scoped to approved out-of-registry trees only, that the separate registered-project removal rule be restored, that all primary-home and registered/active-home refusals be preserved, and that no registered-clone mode be added, supplying an exact axi respond command and forbidding --yes. After the run reached checks-passed on PR 1354 with the five auto-fix findings verifiably unfixed, the developer approved a fresh full validation run from the current reviewed head so the gate would re-raise and fix all five: reject landing evidence or remote URLs contained inside the deletion target, inspect rather than skip detached Git directories, treat git fsck failure as a hard refusal, eliminate process-use double counting when --pool is passed, and remove the redundant pool loop without weakening coverage. The developer explicitly constrained the work to preserve the existing branch and PR, keep the Option A out-of-registry-only scope intact, and forbade --yes, hand-edits during the run, forcing history, merging the current head, deleting the PR, or deferring any of the five findings, requiring every gate return be processed until a genuinely new decision or a fully green exact head.

## What Changed

- Adds `bin/fm-project-retire.sh`, a preflight-then-confirm owner for removing a captain-approved out-of-registry project tree and, optionally, its proven linked Treehouse pool. It refuses on protected fleet paths, registry- or task-referenced paths, dirty or unlanded work, foreign/locked/stale worktrees, live process working directories, remote URLs or landing evidence that resolve inside a removal target, and `git fsck` failures; it discovers standalone repositories by their own git common dir rather than `core.bare`; it walks `/proc` once so `--pool` runs report each process once; and `--execute` only proceeds when `--confirm-root` and the plan id from `--preflight` still match the inspected evidence. It also joins the other fleet entrypoints in sourcing `bin/fm-gate-refuse-lib.sh` to exit 3 under a no-mistakes gate.
- Splits the `project-management` skill's removal section into a registered-project path (unchanged, direct removal under AGENTS.md hard rule 1) and an out-of-registry retirement path that delegates flags, refusals, and mechanics to the helper's header, with the registry line retired before the tree.
- Registers the new authorization exception and skill trigger in `AGENTS.md`, and lists the script in `docs/scripts.md` and the gate-refusal entrypoints in `docs/architecture.md`. Adds `tests/fm-project-retire.test.sh` (24 checks) covering the refusal ladder, plan-id confirmation, and gate refusal.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: All six previously approved findings are correctly and completely fixed in a fail-closed direction with colocated tests, the settled out-of-registry-only scope and every existing guard are preserved, and the only remaining issue is an ordering inaccuracy in the header's refusal list.

## Testing

I ran the change's dedicated suite (`tests/fm-project-retire.test.sh`, 24 checks, all passing) and then drove the real script by hand against throwaway git fixtures to capture an operator-level CLI transcript, because unit-style pass lines say nothing about what an operator actually sees before deleting a project tree. The transcript shows the Option A scope holding (registered projects and registry-named trees refuse), all five hardened guards refusing with their real messages and leaving the tree intact, and the complete preflight → plan-id → execute path removing exactly the approved root and its proven pool while the upstream, boundary directory, seed clone and fleet home survive. I also closed one coverage gap: this change documents `fm-project-retire.sh` as a `fm-gate-refuse-lib.sh` caller in docs/architecture.md, but nothing tested it (the suite exports the bypass globally), so I added a focused case that strips the bypass and asserts the exit-3 refusal before any inspection. No visual artifacts apply — this is a shell CLI with no rendered surface, so the terminal transcript is the end-user experience. Everything passed; no actionable findings.

Remotes are enumerated with `git remote` and fetched, but no remote URL is ever resolved or compared against --root/--pool. A legacy clone whose `origin` URL points at a sibling mirror inside --root (or at the clone's own path) fetches successfully, populates refs/remotes/origin/*, and every local branch then satisfies step 1 of the landing ladder ('exact ancestry of <ref>') against a repository this same run removes with `rm -rf` at :827. The tool reports the work proven landed and destroys the only copy. Fix: for each remote, read `git remote get-url --all`, resolve file:// and filesystem-path URLs to a canonical path, and refuse when that path is equal to or inside any removal target — the proof must survive the removal.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-project-retire.sh:708` - `git fsck` failure is silently converted into 'no unreachable commits'. Its exit status is lost twice: through the unset-pipefail pipeline into `sed`/`sort`, and again through the trailing `|| true`; stderr is sent to /dev/null. A repository with a corrupt or unreadable object store produces empty output, `unreachable_count` stays 0, the plan prints '0 unreachable commits, all landed' at :721, and execution proceeds to delete the tree without ever proving its dangling objects landed. This contradicts the header's own refusal condition at :79 ('any ambiguous git result'). Fix: capture fsck's exit status (e.g. run it into a temp var / use PIPESTATUS or a separate invocation) and refuse with an explicit message on non-zero.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-project-retire.sh:405` - Detached, non-bare git directories are silently skipped instead of inspected. `collect_bare_repos` drops every candidate whose `git rev-parse --is-bare-repository` is not exactly `true`, but a git directory with `core.bare=false` and no attached worktree (a `--separate-git-dir` target, or a `.git` directory moved aside under another name) reports `false`. Such a repository is never added to REPO_COMMONS, so its branches, refs and unreachable objects never go through landing proof, yet it sits inside --root and is removed by `rm -rf`. The header explicitly claims this case is covered at :94 and :391 ('a bare repository, or a detached git directory'). The adjacent `common=$(common_dir_of "$canon") || continue` at :406 is the same silent-skip pattern. Fix: recognise a repository by its own git common dir (bare or not) and refuse rather than `continue` when a candidate looks like a repository but cannot be resolved.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-project-retire.sh:259` - `registry_home_for_line` uses `s/^[^(]*(home: .../`, which only matches when the `home:` field is the first parenthesised group on the registry line. bin/fm-backlog-handoff.sh:65-69 documents this exact failure mode ('Summary/scope prose often contains parentheticals ... ^[^(]* would leave those entries looking like "has no home"') and uses `s/.*(home:[[:space:]]*\([^;)]*\);.*/` instead. Here the consequence is a safety gap, not cosmetic: a secondmate whose one-sentence summary contains any parenthetical is skipped at :290, so its home never enters SECONDMATE_STATE_DIRS and `assert_no_task_reference` never scans its state/*.meta — a live recorded task whose `worktree=` points inside the retirement root goes undetected and its worktree is deleted. Fix: use the greedy-prefix pattern already proven in fm-backlog-handoff.sh.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-project-retire.sh:573` - PROC_INSPECTED and PROC_UNREADABLE are file-scope counters incremented inside assert_no_live_process_cwd, which is called once for --root (:572) and again for --pool (:573) without being reset. With --pool the plan line at :784 reports roughly double the real number of inspected and non-inspectable process working directories, so the operator-facing evidence about the live-process coverage gap is wrong in exactly the case the header at :108-111 says it exists to make visible. The whole process table is also walked twice. Fix: walk /proc once, counting each pid once, and test the cwd against every removal target in that single pass.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-project-retire.sh:724` - The pool re-check loop is unreachable-by-effect dead code. Every entry of SORTED_CHECKOUTS, pool members included, already passes through the main loop at :600-623, which refuses at :608-609 when common_dir_of fails and at :610-611 when the common dir is not inside $ROOT, with the message 'checkout ... belongs to repository ... outside the retirement root ...'. That message already contains the 'outside the retirement root' substring asserted by tests/fm-project-retire.test.sh:256, and the main loop reaches the foreign pool member first, so deleting :724-735 removes no coverage and no test signal.

The remote-URL refusal is listed at :78-79 after 'a remote fetch failure, or no remote-tracking ref after the fetch' (:76-77), yet assert_remote_evidence_survives runs at :773 before the fetch at :774 — a repository with both an in-tree remote URL and an unreachable remote reports the URL refusal, not the fetch failure. title: fix(watch): judge watcher liveness in awake time across macOS system sleep
body:
## Summary

Fixes the overnight "silent watcher deaths" on macOS and locks in the BSD basename portability fix on the Stop-hook path.

**Defect 1 - watcher cycles reported dead while healthy.** Root cause, established from the cycle-exit ledger, a live process monitor, `pmset -g log`, and `kern.waketime`: the watcher never crashed. A clamshell Mac cycling ~900s maintenance sleeps suspends the watcher with everything else, so its liveness beacon aged 900s+ in wall-clock terms the instant each DarkWake began, and every wall-clock judge (attach-mode arm, turn-end guard, Stop auto-arm, singleton re-arm refusal) declared a live watcher dead. Every "died" cycle in the ledger actually exited 0 with an actionable reason; a 15-second-budget herdr event reader showed 13+ minutes of suspended wall time.

Fix: beacon staleness is now judged in awake time. `fm_path_age_since_system_wake` in `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh` (single owner) clamps the age to the system's last wake, read from `kern.waketime` on Darwin - empirically verified to update on DarkWake too. Non-Darwin platforms keep plain wall-clock behavior byte-for-byte. The attach failure path now distinguishes a live identity-matched holder whose beacon froze while awake, printing an actionable possible-hang reason instead of claiming the cycle ended. The absorb/surface contract is untouched, and the lifecycle ledger's `beacon_age` stays wall-clock on purpose as diagnostic evidence.

**Defect 2 - `basename: illegal option -- z` on every Claude Stop hook (#1280).** Root cause: the pre-#1256 harness ancestry walk called bare `basename` on a login shell's `-zsh` comm; BSD basename parses it as flags. HEAD already carries the portable `basename --` fix from #1256 (the noise was pure stderr; classification was unaffected), so this PR adds the missing regression test locking silent classification of dash-leading comms, skipped where `ps -o comm=` does not carry argv[0] (Linux procps). A sweep found no other GNU-only utility flags on macOS-reachable paths.

**Test-harness fixes found along the way.** `tests/lib.sh` pins `FM_SYSTEM_WAKE_EPOCH_OVERRIDE=0` suite-wide so backdated-beacon tests stay deterministic on hosts that recently slept, and exports `--experimental-strip-types` via `NODE_OPTIONS` when node accepts it - node 22.6-23.5 could not import the `.ts` Pi/OpenCode extension fixtures at all, which had been masking that coverage. The pipeline also made the pi-watch suite hermetic against slow login profiles.

## Validation

- `bin/fm-lint.sh` (ShellCheck 0.11.0 pinned) and `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` pass.
- New regression tests: sleep-window survival, awake-hang verdict, typed live-holder hang failure (`tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh`), sleep-aware supervision status (`tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh`), dash-leading comm silence (`tests/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.test.sh`).
- Full changed-file suite sweep green; the no-mistakes pipeline (review, test, document, lint) passed with only info-level findings.
- Three pre-existing failures reproduce identically at the base commit on the diagnosis machine and are out of scope: the Pi hung-successor recovery test on node 22, the secondmate-harness pi-signed ancestry test under a Claude session, and the Kimi hook install test.
- Maintainer-verification record for the `kern.waketime` DarkWake fact added under `docs/verification/supervision.md`.

Fixes #1280.

title: fix: preserve Calm boat continuity across working periods
body:
## Intent

Implement and ship the captain-authorized Firstmate Calm boat continuity fix.

Within one Pi process/session and one Calm extension lifetime, hiding or pausing the working display must freeze the boat at its last rendered column and current travel direction. The next working period in that same session must resume from that exact logical column and direction without returning to the left edge. Hidden elapsed wall time must not advance animation state or create a jump on resume. Endpoint/bounce behavior must remain correct when pause occurs immediately before, at, and immediately after either boundary. Terminal resize while hidden must clamp the frozen column safely to the new width while preserving a valid direction; resize after resume keeps the existing bounce/clamp contract. Repeated start/settle cycles must create no duplicate scheduler, timer, widget, or render subscription, and every owned timer must be cleaned up on replacement, shutdown, and extension disposal. Calm-off behavior must remain stock Pi behavior and must not create, retain, or resume a hidden Calm boat. A genuinely fresh Pi session or new extension lifetime must start at the normal initial position. State must be scoped to one extension/session instance, not a module-level or process-global singleton. Do not add durable cross-process persistence and do not build a general animation-state framework.

This is a reported bug against the PR 1339 working-ship implementation: settling disposed the widget and destroyed animation state, so the next agent run recreated the boat at column 0. The fix keeps one extension-owned animation instance, binds disposable widgets to it, freezes on dispose, resumes on the next working period, and resets only on session_start. Deterministic behavioral coverage was added for continuity, hidden-time freeze, endpoint cases, hidden/visible resize, lifecycle, timer cleanup, Calm-off, and fresh-session reset, plus a real Pi TUI two-period continuity check. Maintained docs were updated only for the new captain-facing continuity contract in docs/calm.md.

## What Changed

- Keep one extension-owned Calm boat animation across widget replacement, freezing at the last rendered state and resuming the exact column and direction without hidden-time advancement.
- Clamp frozen state safely across hidden resizes, preserve boundary behavior, clean up timers on disposal, and reset only for fresh sessions while Calm-off remains stock Pi behavior.
- Add deterministic and live Pi coverage for continuity, hidden time and resize, boundaries, lifecycle cleanup, Calm-off, and fresh-session reset, with updated captain-facing documentation.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The updated implementation now commits all continuity state after rendering and restores the last committed snapshot on disposal, with focused coverage for unpainted ticks, cadence, boundaries, and lifecycle paths.

## Testing

Ran the focused Calm Pi extension tests end to end. Deterministic renderer, endpoint, resize, lifecycle, timer cleanup, Calm-off, and fresh-session checks passed, as did the real tmux/Pi TUI continuity scenario. Captured reviewer-visible terminal evidence showing the boat resuming at the same column and direction after hidden time; the worktree remained clean.

      <|
~~-~~\__/~-~~~-~~~-~~~-~~~-~~~-~

after dispose: column=5 direction=1 phase=0
after 1100ms hidden wall time: column=5 direction=1 phase=0
resume first frame: column=5 terminal_column=6 direction=1 phase=0
      <|
~~-~~\__/~-~~~-~~~-~~~-~~~-~~~-~
resume exact-match: PASS

If settling occurs while that render is queued or coalesced, `dispose()` preserves the post-tick column and direction even though the terminal last showed the prior frame; the next widget then resumes one step ahead.
