title: fix: restore evidence-based dispatch eligibility
body:
## Intent Fix a reported bug in the dispatch path shipped by PR #1349: Firstmate deterministically refused to dispatch supported Pi models in the openai-codex provider family, which blocked the upstream Lavish event-stream worker intake. Reproduction (real toolchain, Pi 0.82.0 / quota-axi 0.1.16): the Pi catalog lists openai-codex/gpt-5.6-terra and reports its provider family; the Codex provider is fresh with usable credentials and 64 effective percent remaining on its all_models scope; yet fm-auth-preflight.sh --harness pi --model openai-codex/gpt-5.6-terra returned eligible=no reason=surface-unresolved, repeatably. Cause: PR 1349 resolved a harness=pi tuple's credential surface by constructing the literal source id pi:, so the tuple looked for a pi:openai-codex source. That source does not exist because Pi's Codex family authenticates through the Codex store quota-axi already lists as auth-json/cli-rpc. The construction was only ever valid where Pi holds its own credential (pi:xai, pi:kimi-coding), which is why every previously configured Pi tuple resolved and the defect stayed hidden. Adding a synthetic pi:openai-codex source - one condition, nothing else changed - flips the verdict to eligible=yes, isolating the cause. The captain authorized this correction: replace deterministic auth-surface rejection with transparent first-mate judgment. The binding contract the captain set, which a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: - quota-axi stays data-only and reports whatever granularity the vendor supplies. It must never recommend, select, rank, or infer a Firstmate route. - The dispatching first mate, not deterministic shell, inspects one current quota snapshot plus each harness's authoritative model catalog and reasons transparently about provider family, authentication evidence, and quota applicability. - Provider-level or all-model evidence is valid evidence for every model established as belonging to that provider family. A model-specific quota window is an additional bound only for the model it names; an unrelated named-model window never constrains another model. - Missing exact model-level quota, a missing pi: source, or unmodeled authentication is disclosed uncertainty, never deterministic ineligibility. Only concrete contradictory evidence blocks a candidate: an authoritative catalog proving the model unsupported, or proof that the credential selected for that surface is unusable. - Deterministic shell must not select, rank, infer, or hard-code model-to-quota-provider mappings, aliases, prefixes, or provider-family relationships. It keeps only schema/config/version validation and concrete spawn safeguards. - Keep one quota snapshot per intake. Do not introduce a daemon, routing wrapper, policy engine, score, control plane, or generalized evidence resolver. Deliberate decisions made while implementing: 1. fm-auth-preflight.sh was RETIRED from dispatch eligibility, but not deleted outright. The captain approved firstmate-grok-auth-preflight on 2026-07-30, and that bounded vendor probe is a concrete nonduplicative evidence need: quota-axi classifies the Grok credential from a local file timestamp, so the vendor CLI is the only ground truth before blocking a candidate on credential grounds. It was narrowed and renamed to bin/fm-vendor-auth-probe.sh: it takes no harness, model, or provider, reads no quota, emits no eligible verdict, and holds only a fixed-argv safety allowlist. The safety envelope (fixed argv, never login/logout/TUI, stdin closed, hard bound, raw vendor output never printed) is enforced deterministically because firstmate-coding-guidelines requires deterministic enforcement for safety infrastructure rather than agent memory. 2. The rename is deliberate, not churn: the name 'preflight' promised the pre-dispatch gate that was retired, and leaving it would be a stale promise in the scripts inventory. 3. The brief permitted a source-text no-forbidden-mapping inventory check as defense in depth. I deliberately did NOT add one, because firstmate-coding-guidelines forbids tests asserting implementation-source bytes (PRs 1282 and 1304 removed exactly that pattern). Instead the absence of routing knowledge is proven behaviorally - the script rejects every shape of candidate identity, including alongside a valid probe name - plus a documented search of the complete diff and call graph showing no pi: source construction, no provider map, and no eligible= emitter anywhere in bin/. 4. Acceptance criteria about agent judgment (provider-only evidence applies to a family member, model windows bound only their own model, unknown stays eligible, contradictory evidence blocks, every candidate accounted for) are agent reasoning and cannot have an executable regression without building the routing wrapper the contract forbids. They are recorded instead in docs/verification/dispatch-auth.md as dated maintainer-verification evidence with exact commands and real output. This scope boundary is stated explicitly rather than silently narrowed. It mirrors PR 1349's own item 10. 5. The new behavior suite was mutation-checked with four mutations. One mutation (accepting and ignoring a --model flag) initially SURVIVED, exposing a real weakness in my own test - it only proved those inputs were rejected when no probe name followed. I strengthened the test to also supply candidate identity alongside a valid probe name, and re-verified the mutation is now caught. Three adjacent defects fixed along the way, each real and encountered during this work: a zero FM_*_TIMEOUT silently removed the hard bound because timeout 0 and perl alarm 0 both mean no deadline; the pinned Grok version had drifted to 0.2.117, so I re-verified both discriminator strings first-hand and confirmed the credential file is byte-identical after the probe before moving the pin; and bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed refused outright on any deleted bin/ script, which would block every retirement branch, fixed with the same existence rule the fixture case already applied. Policy owners updated without duplication: AGENTS.md section 4 carries only the concise always-loaded boundary (same line count), quota-array-dispatch owns the detailed judgment procedure, harness-adapters gets a concise catalog-responsibility correction distinguishing an authoritative negative from an unreachable surface, and docs/scripts.md, docs/configuration.md, and docs/verification/dispatch-auth.md drop the obsolete surface. Validation already run locally and green: bin/fm-lint.sh, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh, bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage, the complete change-selected suite (34 scripts, 0 failures), and the three spawn/harness suites run explicitly to confirm spawn's deterministic refusals remain intact. Repo conventions followed: one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never em dash, no agent co-author. ## What Changed - Replaced deterministic auth-surface rejection with transparent provider-family judgment over quota snapshots and authoritative harness catalogs. - Retired the dispatch preflight script and added a bounded vendor-auth probe with fixed-argv safety controls and strict timeout validation. - Updated policy and verification documentation, tests, and changed-file handling for the new dispatch behavior. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The previously reported all-zero timeout bypass is fixed and covered, and the remaining change is bounded with no additional material source risks found. ## Testing Focused behavior, runner, bootstrap, spawn/harness, and live-toolchain checks all completed successfully. No linters or full repository suite were run; evidence was recorded in the dedicated temporary artifact.
Evidence: Targeted dispatch validation evidence ```text Targeted dispatch validation evidence Repository target: 3f05bde6fa18d07dff7dfc5a1e7c47de42a9e72f Focused behavior suite $ bash tests/fm-vendor-auth-probe.test.sh ok - the probe accepts no harness, model, or provider and so can hold no routing mapping ok - the probe never reads quota, leaving one intake snapshot to the dispatch owner ok - every probe result exits alike because the script renders no verdict ok - only a registered probe name runs, and an unregistered one is a usage error ok - an authenticated vendor session is reported as ground truth ok - an unauthenticated vendor session is reported as ground truth ok - unrecognized, blank-led, and silent probe output is indeterminate, never authenticated ok - an absent vendor CLI is reported rather than assumed authenticated ok - a hanging vendor CLI is hard-bounded, reported, and cannot wedge an intake ok - zero and all-zero bounds fall back to the default instead of removing the hard bound ok - a malformed bound is replaced by the default rather than forwarded ok - the bounded probe runs with stdin closed and cannot read caller input ok - the vendor CLI is invoked only through its two fixed, non-destructive argv forms ok - the fact line is one sanitized line with no raw vendor output or credential material ok - a vendor CLI version change is recorded and disclosed for re-verification ok - the pinned verified vendor version is recognized ok - --help succeeds and names the registered probes Changed-test selection $ bin/fm-test-run.sh --list --changed --base 621299ab0cc5ed307951f1d924e15a92b0978c8a Selected tests included tests/fm-vendor-auth-probe.test.sh and tests/fm-test-run.test.sh. The deleted tests/fm-auth-preflight.test.sh was not selected, and selection did not abort on the deleted bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh. Live installed toolchain $ pi --list-models terra provider model context max-out thinking images openai-codex gpt-5.6-terra 272K 128K yes yes $ quota-axi --json | jq '.providers[] | select(.provider == "codex") | {provider, state: {status: .state.status, stale: .state.stale}, quotaSemantics: {status: .quotaSemantics.status, description: .quotaSemantics.description, effectiveAvailability: .quotaSemantics.effectiveAvailability}}' provider=codex state.status=fresh state.stale=false quotaSemantics.status=known effectiveAvailability[0].scope=all_models effectiveAvailability[0].effectivePercentRemaining=63 effectiveAvailability[0].boundedBy=weekly $ quota-axi auth --json | jq '.auth[] | select(.provider == "codex") | {provider, sources: [.sources[] | {source, status, error}]}' provider=codex sources=auth-json:available, cli-rpc:available $ bin/fm-vendor-auth-probe.sh grok probe=grok status=authenticated version=0.2.117 versionVerified=yes probe_exit=0 Compatibility suites $ bash tests/fm-test-run.test.sh ok - changed selection covers dependents and fails closed for unmapped source ok - empty changed selection emits deterministic text and JSON summaries ok - aggregate exit reflects any script failure $ bash tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh # all fm-spawn-dispatch-profile tests passed $ bash tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh # all fm-secondmate-harness tests passed $ bash tests/fm-kimi-harness.test.sh ok - fm-spawn: kimi launches, delivers its brief, and registers a guarded turn-end token ok - fm-spawn: unsafe Kimi global config refuses before pane creation ok - fm-spawn: missing Kimi executable refuses before pane creation ok - fm-spawn: kimi never sends the brief pointer before an observable ready signal Retirement check $ test -e bin/fm-auth-preflight.sh absent ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-vendor-auth-probe.sh:129` - The validation rejects only exact `0`. Values such as `00` or `000` pass to `timeout`/Perl `alarm` as zero, disabling the deadline and allowing a hung vendor CLI to run unbounded. Reject all-zero values before `run_timed`. 🔧 Fix: Reject all-zero vendor probe timeouts ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-vendor-auth-probe.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-test-run.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-kimi-harness.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` - `pi --list-models terra` - `quota-axi --json` and `quota-axi auth --json` filtered to Codex - `bin/fm-vendor-auth-probe.sh grok` - `bin/fm-test-run.sh --list --changed ...` - `git status --short`
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix(bin): derive harness wiring artifacts from a single per-harness owner
body:
## Intent Follow-up fix on the harness wiring-artifact single-owner branch (upstream PR 1359): teach tests/fm-backend.test.sh's build_old_bin synthetic bin/ tree about bin/fm-harness-adapter.sh and bin/harnesses/. WHY. This branch made bin/fm-teardown.sh source bin/fm-harness-adapter.sh, which eagerly loads every bin/harnesses/.sh. build_old_bin assembles a synthetic bin/ tree to run the PRE-change entrypoints against identical fixtures, and it was never taught about that new sibling. Whenever BASE_REF already carries the change, the extracted old teardown aborts under set -eu with 'fm-harness-adapter.sh: No such file or directory'. It passed locally only by accident - this pool worktree's local main is many commits stale, so BASE_REF resolved to a commit predating the change and the old teardown had no adapter to source. Fork CI resolved a BASE_REF that did carry it and failed on 'old fm-teardown.sh (scout, report present) should succeed'. VERIFICATION. Reproduced deterministically before fixing, in a throwaway clone with main forced to HEAD so BASE_REF collapses and old == new: the failure reproduces exactly, and with this fixture addition the same condition passes 28/28. Not inferred from reading the log. SCOPE. Fixture completion only - it changes what the synthetic tree CONTAINS, never what the conformance cases assert or compare. No production code changes, and no assertion was relaxed to make anything pass. CONTEXT. This is the third instance of one fixture class on this work: tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh needed the same two additions (already in this branch), and so did the abandoned busy-signature branch. Any change that gives a bin/ entrypoint a new sourced sibling must teach every synthetic bin/ tree about it, or the old-vs-new cases break the moment the baseline advances past the change. Treat that as the durable lesson rather than re-deriving it per branch. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-harness-adapter.sh` plus per-harness adapters under `bin/harnesses/` (claude, codex, opencode, pi, grok, kimi) as the single owner of each harness's turn-end/busy-state artifact set. `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now installs from that inventory and `bin/fm-teardown.sh` removes from it, replacing seven hand-maintained spellings (four worktree `rm -f` blocks, two state-dir blocks, and the dirty-check allowlist) that had drifted — the ordinary teardown path was still removing OpenCode's old `fm-turn-end.js` name and leaking the renamed plugin into pooled worktrees. - Teardown now removes the union of artifacts across every known harness, derives its dirty-check allowlist from the same inventory, and fails closed (excluding the full artifact union with a notice) when a launch name doesn't match a known adapter arm; state-dir artifact names are derived by byte-exact id+suffix concatenation rather than placeholder substitution. - Added `tests/fm-harness-artifacts.test.sh`, a drift guard that drives the real installer against the removal paths, and taught the `tests/fm-backend.test.sh` and `tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh` synthetic `bin/` fixture trees about the newly sourced adapter sibling so the old-vs-new conformance cases keep passing once the baseline carries this change (the fix Fork CI caught). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The suffix-concatenation rework satisfies every captain constraint from the prior round (bash-3.2 correctness, byte-exactness for hostile ids, no silent no-op path, behavioral coverage preserved), leaves no stale placeholder references, and does not touch the intent's fixture change or any conformance assertion. ## Testing Deterministically reproduced the fork-CI failure the fix targets (BASE_REF forced to carry the teardown→adapter change with the pre-fix fixture: old teardown aborts on missing fm-harness-adapter.sh), then confirmed the fixed fixture passes all 28 conformance cases under that exact condition and also passes on the stale-baseline path; the diff is fixture-only with no assertions relaxed. No UI surface is involved, so evidence is CLI test transcripts.

## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 4 issues found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - ⚠️ `tests/fm-harness-artifacts.test.sh:88` - test_installed_artifacts_are_all_removed asserts implementation-source bytes: it greps bin/fm-spawn.sh for redirection targets (line 104), counts 'remove_harness_worktree_artifacts "' call sites in bin/fm-teardown.sh (line 115), and greps for forbidden hand-listed rm patterns (line 119). The repo's own testing rule (.agents/skills/firstmate-coding-guidelines/SKILL.md: "Tests must ... never assert implementation-source bytes, including through parsers, regexes, snapshots, or indirect wrappers") forbids exactly this. The test header presents it as a deliberate drift guard ("read out of fm-spawn itself rather than restated here"), so this is an intentional exception to a stated project invariant that the author should confirm; it also couples the test to incidental source shapes (e.g. a future artifact written via `tee` or a variable-held path silently escapes the extraction pattern, though the `[ -n "$installed" ]` staleness guard partially mitigates that). - ℹ️ `bin/fm-harness-adapter.sh:228` - fm_harness_state_artifacts_all substitutes the task id via awk `gsub(/@ID@/, id)`, where `&` and `\` are special in the replacement string. The main teardown id is charset-validated by fm_task_id_path_safe, but child ids in cleanup_firstmate_home_children come from `basename "$child_meta" .meta` with no equivalent charset guarantee; an id containing `&` or `\` would produce a mangled filename and quietly skip removal (the old code rm'd the literal name, which handled any bytes). A shell substitution (`${name//@ID@/$id}`) is byte-exact and drops the edge case. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:819` - The derived dirty allowlist widens what a destructive teardown will silently discard: because a nested artifact contributes its top-level directory prefix, ALL untracked content under `.opencode/` is now ignored by the uncommitted-work refusal (previously `.opencode/` was not in the allowlist at all). This matches the pre-existing `.claude/` semantics and is forced by how `git status --porcelain` collapses untracked directories, and the function comment documents the shape — noting the tradeoff: a crewmate's genuine uncommitted work under `.opencode/` (e.g. opencode agent configs as deliverables) no longer blocks teardown. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-harness-adapter.sh:118` - fm_harness_launch_adapter_name re-spells fm-spawn's install-arm globs (claude*, opencode*, pi|pi-signed, codex*, grok*, kimi*) as a second copy that must be kept in step manually — the same two-spellings hazard this branch eliminates for artifact paths, retained at the arm-pattern level. The comment acknowledges it and tests cover representative examples (claude-nightly, opencode-beta, pinocchio), but a future new/changed install arm still needs a manual sync here; the failure mode is bounded because an unmatched name falls back to excluding the full artifact union with a notice rather than excluding nothing. 🔧 Fix: drive real installer in drift guard; byte-exact id substitution 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-harness-adapter.sh:236` - The byte-exact substitution fix regresses on bash ≤ 4.2: `printf '%s\n' "${name//@ID@/"$id"}"` performs pattern substitution inside double quotes, and in bash 4.2 and earlier the replacement string "does not undergo quote removal" (documented compat42 behavior — verified empirically: `shopt -s compat42` yields `"t9".pi-ext.ts` with literal quote characters). On stock macOS /bin/bash 3.2 every derived state-artifact name gains literal quotes, so remove_harness_state_artifacts silently removes nothing — exactly the silent-leak class this branch eliminates — and the replaced awk implementation had no such version sensitivity for normal ids. bin/ otherwise contains no bash-4+ constructs and macOS is an actively supported platform (issue 1280), so nothing else forces a newer bash; CI's modern bash means the new test coverage cannot catch it. Fix mechanically by hoisting into an unquoted-assignment context, e.g. `name=${name//@ID@/"$id"}; printf '%s\n' "$name"` — verified byte-exact both under bash 5.2+ patsub_replacement (quoting suppresses `&`) and under old-bash quote-removal semantics. 🔧 Fix: derive state artifacts by id+suffix concatenation, dropping @ID@ substitution ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: docs: define captain instruction precedence
body:
## Intent

Supersede the earlier narrow inherent-red-check merge exception with one always-loaded general Firstmate-local captain-instruction precedence rule.

This replaces the previous design entirely; do not keep or layer the narrow expected-red exception. Do not touch generated release PRs. Do not merge the PR.

Selected policy (own once in AGENTS.md section 1 prime-directive/authority area):
- A current, explicit, concrete captain instruction overrides a conflicting Firstmate-written standing rule or default only within the exact scope that instruction names.
- This local precedence never overrides platform, system, developer, or other higher-priority instructions outside this repository's Firstmate-written surface.
- Specificity and recency are required; the instruction must identify the concrete action, object, or bounded set it governs.
- Never infer an override, broaden scope, apply by analogy, carry to another object/action, or convert one request into standing authority.
- Ambiguous scope or conflict still requires one concise clarification before action.
- Destructive, irreversible, security-sensitive, discard, and merge actions still require the captain to state that concrete action explicitly; once stated and higher-priority instructions permit it, a conflicting Firstmate-written rule must not rigidly block the action.
- Standing yolo is not a substitute for a current explicit captain instruction where an explicit action is required.

Reconciliation:
- Remove the earlier narrow inherent-red-check exception in full from section 7.
- Keep ordinary "Never merge a red PR" default; without a current explicit captain merge instruction that default stands, and yolo cannot authorize a red merge.
- Point section 7 at the section 1 precedence owner rather than restating the full procedure.
- Tighten yolo wording to merges only green work.
- Update hard rule 2 to point at the section 1 precedence owner for overrides of Firstmate-written standing rules.
- No force-merge flag, label, waiver config, automatic inference, control plane, or policy engine.
- Scripts unchanged; this is agent authority policy.
- Commit and PR title use docs: prefix. Verified this repository has no release workflow, release-please config, or tags, so docs: is non-release-triggering.
- Update the existing PR https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/1362 final head, title, and body through this run; never merge.
- Captain explicitly authorized merging this policy PR once green, but the worker never merges.

## What Changed

- Add a single section 1 precedence rule for current, explicit, scoped captain instructions, limited to Firstmate-written policy and subordinate to higher-priority instructions.
- Point merge authority guidance to that rule, restrict `yolo` to green merges, and preserve the red-PR default unless the captain explicitly instructs the concrete merge.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Captain, the documentation-only change is well-bounded and conforms to the stated precedence, ownership, yolo, and red-merge requirements.

## Testing

Baseline diff and commit inspection, focused residue searches, predecessor-to-final policy reconciliation, a read-only live PR check, and reviewer-readable evidence generation all succeeded. No automated suite was run because this is an instruction-only Markdown change with no executable contract, source-byte regression tests are prohibited by the repository, and this phase forbids static-analysis checks. No rendered UI exists for this policy surface, so the diff and exact committed-section artifacts provide the end-user-visible evidence. The worktree remains clean, PR #1362 remains safely open and unmerged, and its final push, title, and body update is pending the outer pipeline's PR phase.

 An ask-user finding returns as `needs-decision`; firstmate decides only when the configured authority permits, otherwise escalates to the captain.
 Send the same worker one exact decision naming the decision key, step, action, affected finding IDs, instructions where needed, and exact response command.

title: fix(bin): recognize kimi variants and pi launcher basenames in harness detection
body:
## Intent Fix two measured inconsistencies in how firstmate recognizes a harness process name, and deliberately NOT ship the refactor that was originally planned here. BACKGROUND. This was scoped as increment C of a harness-interface effort: a shared per-harness process-identity table replacing three separate lists. I measured it against current main first and recommended dropping the refactor, which the captain approved. It would have replaced ~15 lines of clear in-place literals (12 case arms in bin/fm-harness.sh, one regex in bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh, one glob arm in bin/backends/tmux.sh) with 80-100 lines of table, dispatcher, three per-consumer generators, and two exceptions - and the exceptions would have encoded exactly the divergences fixed below rather than removing them, because the captain's ruling required preserving all three matching rules byte-identically. Its justifying defect (pi missing from the tmux alive list) is already fixed on main by #1145. That trips the design's own stop condition, so the inconsistencies are shipped and the machinery is not. Do not suggest reintroducing the table. THE MEASUREMENT, run over the same basenames through each rule: comm fm-harness session-lock tmux-alive kimi-nightly unknown yes alive pi-launcher unknown no alive Pi unknown no alive FIX 1: kimi was matched EXACTLY in bin/fm-harness.sh while its four markerless siblings (claude, codex, opencode, grok) are substring globs, and while both other consumers matched it as a substring. A kimi under a variant basename was recognized by those two but self-detected as unknown. It becomes a substring match, consistent with its siblings. FIX 2: pi-launcher and Pi - the launcher wrapper and the npm shim basename, both already known to bin/backends/tmux.sh's pane classifier - were missing from self-detection and from the session-lock ancestry regex. A firstmate under either reported unknown and could not prove session-lock ownership, so bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh's check would decline to arm. fm_session_lock_owned_by_self fails closed, so this was a false NEGATIVE, never a false ownership claim. Both basenames are added. DELIBERATE: the pi family stays ANCHORED. A bare 'pi' substring would also match pip, pipenv, and any path component containing 'pi', so each launcher basename gets its own exact arm rather than relaxing the anchor to a glob. Do not 'simplify' those exact arms into *pi*. VERIFICATION. Coverage extends tests/fm-kimi-harness.test.sh rather than adding a runner, and asserts behavior by executing bin/fm-harness.sh and bin/fm-lock.sh against fake ancestry - no source-content assertions, per the repo rule. Every case was verified to FAIL before the fix, not assumed: reverting kimi to an exact arm, dropping the pi-family arms, and reverting the session-lock regex each reproduce the original miss as a test failure. pip, pipenv, and piper are asserted to stay unrecognized so the anti-substring guard cannot be relaxed unnoticed. LOCAL SUITE NOTE. tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh fails on this machine with 'restart did not attach to the verified healthy peer'. I verified it fails IDENTICALLY on a clean checkout of current origin/main with none of these changes present - same test, same message, only the pid differs - so it is environmental, not a regression from touching fm-session-lock-lib.sh. fm-kimi-harness and fm-secondmate-harness pass, and lint is clean. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-harness.sh` self-detection now matches `kimi` as a substring glob (`*kimi*`), consistent with its markerless siblings (claude, codex, opencode, grok) and with the other two consumers — a variant basename like `kimi-nightly` no longer self-detects as `unknown`. - Added `pi-launcher` and `Pi` (the launcher wrapper and npm shim basenames, already known to `bin/backends/tmux.sh`'s pane classifier) as exact arms in `bin/fm-harness.sh` and as anchored alternatives in `FM_HARNESS_RE` in `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh`, so a firstmate under either can self-identify and prove session-lock ownership. The pi family deliberately stays anchored/exact so `pip`, `pipenv`, and paths containing "pi" remain unrecognized. - Extended `tests/fm-kimi-harness.test.sh` with behavioral cases (21 total, executed against fake ancestry via `bin/fm-harness.sh` and `bin/fm-lock.sh`); each new case was verified to fail against the pre-fix code, and `pip`/`pipenv`/`piper` are asserted to stay unrecognized so the anti-substring guard can't be relaxed unnoticed. The originally planned per-harness identity table is deliberately not shipped. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A 21-line behavioral fix that brings three already-existing matching rules into agreement on measured basenames, preserves the deliberately anchored pi-family matching everywhere, adds no forbidden refactor machinery, and is covered by behavioral tests with explicit negative guards for the pip/pipenv near-misses. ## Testing Ran the extended fm-kimi-harness test suite (21/21 pass), proved the new assertions fail against the base-commit bin scripts by temporarily reverting them, and captured an end-to-end before/after CLI transcript of fm-harness.sh self-detection and fm-lock.sh lock ownership that reproduces the intent's measurement table exactly — kimi-nightly and pi-launcher/Pi are now recognized, pip/pipenv/piper stay rejected, and no table refactor was shipped. This is a CLI-only change, so CLI transcripts are the reviewer-visible product surface; no screenshot applies.
Evidence: Before/after CLI transcript: harness self-detection and session-lock ownership per ancestor basename ########## BEFORE FIX (base f7d0d0a) ########## == fm-harness.sh self-detection == ancestor kimi-nightly -> unknown ancestor pi-launcher -> unknown ancestor Pi -> unknown ancestor pip -> unknown == fm-lock.sh ownership == ancestor pi-launcher -> REFUSED: error: cannot locate harness process in ancestry ancestor Pi -> REFUSED: error: cannot locate harness process in ancestry ########## AFTER FIX (7896c83) ########## == fm-harness.sh self-detection == ancestor kimi-nightly -> kimi ancestor pi-launcher -> pi ancestor Pi -> pi ancestor pip -> unknown (pipenv, piper likewise) == fm-lock.sh ownership == ancestor pi-launcher -> lock acquired: harness pid 3260685 ancestor Pi -> lock acquired: harness pid 3260738 ancestor pip -> REFUSED: error: cannot locate harness process in ancestry ```text ########## BEFORE FIX (bin files at base f7d0d0a) ########## == fm-harness.sh self-detection by ancestor basename == ancestor kimi -> kimi ancestor kimi-nightly -> unknown ancestor pi -> pi ancestor pi-signed -> pi ancestor pi-launcher -> unknown ancestor Pi -> unknown ancestor pip -> unknown ancestor pipenv -> unknown ancestor piper -> unknown == fm-lock.sh session-lock ownership by ancestor basename == ancestor pi-launcher -> REFUSED: error: cannot locate harness process in ancestry ancestor Pi -> REFUSED: error: cannot locate harness process in ancestry ancestor pip -> REFUSED: error: cannot locate harness process in ancestry ########## AFTER FIX (bin files at 7896c83) ########## == fm-harness.sh self-detection by ancestor basename == ancestor kimi -> kimi ancestor kimi-nightly -> kimi ancestor pi -> pi ancestor pi-signed -> pi ancestor pi-launcher -> pi ancestor Pi -> pi ancestor pip -> unknown ancestor pipenv -> unknown ancestor piper -> unknown == fm-lock.sh session-lock ownership by ancestor basename == ancestor pi-launcher -> lock acquired: harness pid 3260685 ancestor Pi -> lock acquired: harness pid 3260738 ancestor pip -> REFUSED: error: cannot locate harness process in ancestry ```
Evidence: Full fm-kimi-harness test run on fixed code (21/21 pass) ```text ok - Kimi hook install is idempotent and removal restores every foreign config byte ok - Kimi hook removal preserves owned newline boundaries and pristine bytes ok - Kimi hook install refuses missing, malformed, and surprising config without writing ok - Kimi hook install refuses without jq before any config write ok - fm-spawn: kimi launches, delivers its brief, and registers a guarded turn-end token ok - Kimi hook stays silent and inert without a Firstmate registry token ok - fm-spawn: unsafe Kimi global config refuses before pane creation ok - fm-teardown: Kimi task pointer and registry token are removed ok - fm-spawn: Kimi fallback expands the active HOME ok - fm-spawn: missing Kimi executable refuses before pane creation ok - fm-spawn: kimi treats a silent pointer drop as a failed spawn ok - fm-spawn: kimi never sends the brief pointer before an observable ready signal ok - fm-harness: markerless kimi is detected by ancestry after env-marker precedence, including a variant basename ok - fm-harness: every pi launcher basename resolves to pi while pip/pipenv stay unrecognized lock acquired: harness pid 3234721 ok - fm-lock recognizes Kimi ancestry and live lock holders lock acquired: harness pid 3234788 lock acquired: harness pid 3234854 ok - fm-lock recognizes pi-launcher and Pi ancestry while pip/pipenv stay rejected ok - busy detection: real Kimi moon-plus-middot captures require its harness while idle labels stay idle ok - fm-watch classifies Kimi as unknown rather than from its spinner, and Grok's fallback stays isolated ok - composer classifier: kimi's existing bordered > shape is already safe without an override ```
Evidence: Pre-fix test failure (bin files reverted to base): new assertion reproduces the original miss ```text not ok - a kimi variant basename detected as 'unknown', not kimi ```
Evidence: End-to-end demo script used for the before/after transcript ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # End-to-end demo: what fm-harness.sh self-detection and fm-lock.sh report # when the firstmate's ancestor process has a given basename. set -u ROOT=$1 DEMO=$(mktemp -d) trap 'rm -rf "$DEMO"' EXIT BASE_PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin mkdir -p "$DEMO/fakebin" "$DEMO/cfg" mk_ps() { # $1 = ancestor basename cat > "$DEMO/fakebin/ps" < %s\n' "$name" "$out" done echo echo "== fm-lock.sh session-lock ownership by ancestor basename ==" for name in pi-launcher Pi pip; do home="$DEMO/home-$name"; mkdir -p "$home/state" cat > "$DEMO/fakebin/ps" <&1); then printf ' ancestor %-14s -> %s\n' "$name" "$out" else printf ' ancestor %-14s -> REFUSED: %s\n' "$name" "$out" fi done ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ℹ️ `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh:17` - The anchored pi-family alternatives in FM_HARNESS_RE (^pi$|^pi-signed$|^pi-launcher$|^Pi$) can never match when the regex is grepped against a full `ps -o args=` line in the bare-interpreter fallback (fm-session-lock-lib.sh line 48 and 83), and the corresponding args fallback in fm-harness.sh line 77 only knows `*" pi "*|*/pi`. A pi-family harness presenting comm=node/python would still be unrecognized by these paths. This asymmetry is pre-existing (identical for ^pi$ before this change), theoretical (shebang shims present their own basename as comm), and outside the intent's measured scope, so no action is needed — recorded so a future consolidation doesn't mistake it for a regression from this change.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-kimi-harness.test.sh` on the fixed code — all 21 cases pass, including new `test_pi_launcher_basenames_detect_as_pi`, `test_pi_launcher_session_lock_identity`, and the extended kimi variant-basename assertion - Reverted `bin/fm-harness.sh` and `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh` to base f7d0d0a and re-ran the suite — it fails with `a kimi variant basename detected as 'unknown', not kimi`, proving the tests detect the pre-fix defect; then restored the fixed files - Manual end-to-end before/after run of `bin/fm-harness.sh` against fake ancestry for kimi, kimi-nightly, pi, pi-signed, pi-launcher, Pi, pip, pipenv, piper — reproduces the intent's measurement table (unknown→kimi, unknown→pi) with the anti-substring guard intact - Manual end-to-end before/after run of `bin/fm-lock.sh` under pi-launcher, Pi, and pip ancestry — lock refused before the fix, acquired after for the two real launchers, still refused for pip - `Verified the diff contains only the two literal fixes plus tests (no per-harness table/dispatcher machinery, per the forbidden constraint) and that the worktree is clean after testing`

title: fix(bin): stop losing a readable secondmate home's current work in snapshots
body:
## Intent Fix the Bearings snapshot path that reported the live `social-automate-prep` secondmate as `unknown` with "structured home snapshot timed out", leaving the captain with the false impression that no coding work was under way. DIAGNOSIS (the obvious explanation was disproved). The cross-home read passed the child home's parsed inventory to jq as --argjson. Linux execve caps a SINGLE argument at 131072 B (MAX_ARG_STRLEN), independent of the 2 MB ARG_MAX; macOS caps the whole argv+environment block. That home's backlog JSON measured 145632 B, so the read failed deterministically with E2BIG ("/bin/jq: Argument list too long"). The load-bearing counterfactual: raising FM_SNAPSHOT_SECONDMATE_TIMEOUT to 60s did NOT restore the record, it only changed which of two wrong reasons was displayed, because the child's runtime (measured 5.8-10.3s) straddled the 8s bound. The timeout was a masking condition, never the cause. The main home measured 127628 B, only 3444 B from the identical cliff, where the same overflow aborts the entire snapshot rather than degrading one record. THREE DELIBERATE DECISIONS a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: 1. TRANSPORT. Every payload that grows with a home's inventory now reaches jq over stdin instead of argv, with each filter asserting its document count so a missing document is a loud error rather than a silent null binding. Pure pipes were chosen over temp files deliberately: an earlier attempt at this same defect (PR #1098, closed unmerged) used mktemp with a $$-based fallback naming scheme and drew a P2 review finding about fallback-filename exhaustion at scale. Pipes have no filename allocation, no cleanup, and no collision surface. Scope was held to growth-scaled payloads; single per-task status strings were deliberately left on argv as a different and much rarer class with no evidence of failure. 2. CONTRACT CHANGE, INTENTIONAL. Transport failure is now separated from content contradiction. Previously ONLY the `child_current_unavailable` invalidity kind kept its structured surfaces; every other contradiction (orphan_in_flight, unowned_current, terminal_in_flight, unstructured_current, missing_backlog) demoted the whole home to the strict empty parent-event fallback, discarding its real work. On the live fleet that erased 20 pending captain decisions and 3 landed items. Now a home that never answered (timeout, budget exhaustion, non-zero exit, byte limit, malformed or stale output, unusable path) stays a strict empty fallback, while a home that answered with a schema-valid, in-bounds, same-observation summary keeps structured-home provenance with partial trust, an unknown classification naming the contradiction, and its independently derived surfaces. Safe because every retained surface is derived independently of the contradiction. This restores documented intent rather than inventing behavior: the bearings skill already said "Do not suppress separately projected decisions, landed records, or gates from a partial-structured home merely because that secondmate's own row is unknown", and docs/architecture.md carried the now-corrected claim that every other invalid path stays strict. Because the contract genuinely changed, existing assertions in tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh that encoded the old strict-erasure behavior were INTENTIONALLY updated; those edits are the point of the change, not test-fitting. What each assertion actually protected was preserved (invalidity reason PRECEDENCE, and that an unowned or orphaned child is never promoted into active_children) and tightened to check the concrete invalidity object. 3. BOUNDS, NOT AN UNBOUNDED WAIT. Solving this only by waiting longer was explicitly ruled out. The per-home bound went 8s -> 20s (sized above the measured spread of a real 13-task home), but a NEW cross-home budget (FM_SNAPSHOT_SECONDMATE_BUDGET, default 60s) caps the structured-home summary reads, so that aggregate falls from per-home-bound x home-count (20 x 8 = 160s) to 60s. A home the budget clips short, and a home it never reaches, both name the budget rather than a per-home timeout, so the causes stay distinguishable. The per-home parent-activity and terminal-evidence bounds sit outside that budget and the help and architecture doc say so explicitly. FOLLOW-UP COMMIT IN THIS RUN, SEPARATELY AUTHORIZED BY THE CAPTAIN. The prior validation run ended terminal with current-head CI still failing on the "Stock macOS Bash snapshot compatibility" job. That job was NOT reporting a portability defect: all 46 Bearings tests pass on stock Bash 3.2.57 (arm64-apple-darwin25). The job asserts an exact test count as a "tests actually ran" guard, and this branch added five checks, moving the count from 41 to 46 while the guard stayed at 41. The captain explicitly authorized exactly one post-pipeline correction on this branch: .github/workflows/ci.yml, the failing assertion and its own diagnostic message, 41 -> 46, with no other workflow semantics or files touched. The exact-count style was deliberately kept rather than loosened, because an exact count is what catches a silently skipped test, and it matches the sibling fleet-view guard (15). Verified locally before committing: bash -n over all 208 linted files clean, fleet-view suite 15, Bearings suite 46, ci.yml valid YAML. CONSTRAINTS HELD THROUGHOUT: parent events still never become current work; no secondmate chat is read; the child tree is never reconstructed or supervised from the main home; no home is mutated; the output schema is unchanged with no new fields; explicit provenance and freshness are preserved on degraded evidence. FIRSTMATE REPO RULES: shellcheck-clean bin scripts under bin/fm-lint.sh, tests colocated in tests/ extending the existing runner and exercising behavior through the executable interface rather than asserting implementation source bytes, one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never em dash, no agent co-author trailer, and contracts documented at their one authoritative owner (script header/help plus the maintainer architecture doc) rather than duplicated into AGENTS.md. ## What Changed - Every jq payload in the fleet and bearings snapshots that grows with a home's inventory (backlog/task documents, home summaries, reconciliation inputs, secondmate records, candidate PR rows) now travels over stdin instead of `--argjson`, with each filter binding `[inputs]` and asserting its document count. A large home no longer hits the 128 KiB `execve` single-argument cap and get reported as unavailable; fixed-size scalars stay on argv. - Transport failure is now separated from content contradiction in the cross-home read: a home that never answered (timeout, budget exhaustion, non-zero exit, byte limit, malformed or stale output, unusable path) still drops to the strict empty parent-event fallback, while a home that returned a schema-valid, in-bounds, same-observation summary keeps structured-home provenance with partial trust, an `unknown` classification naming the contradiction, and its independently derived children, decisions, holds, queued, and landed surfaces. - Rebounded the reads: per-home `FM_SNAPSHOT_SECONDMATE_TIMEOUT` default moved 8s -> 20s, and a new `FM_SNAPSHOT_SECONDMATE_BUDGET` (default 60s) caps the structured-home summary reads across all homes, charging only their measured elapsed time; a budget-clipped home and a never-reached home report the budget rather than a per-home timeout. Help text, `docs/architecture.md`, and the script header document the new contract, the Bearings suite adds five checks for large inventories, contradictory-home retention, and budget bounding, and the CI stock-macOS-Bash count guard moves 41 -> 46 to match. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Both round-1 warnings are resolved by commit 14346ed - the cross-home budget now charges only the structured-home summary reads, which simultaneously makes the header/help/architecture-doc claims accurate and removes the sub-second timing dependence that made the budget test fragile - and the rest of the branch (stdin transport with document-count assertions, the deliberate transport-vs-contradiction contract split, and the authorized 41 to 46 CI guard correction) verified clean with no new issues. ## Testing Ran the two targeted suites the change touches (Bearings 46/46, fleet-view 15/15) and then demonstrated the intent at the captain-visible CLI surface by replaying the same fixtures against base commit 66b0f77 and branch head 14346ed. The reported defect reproduces exactly on base - a healthy secondmate home with a 238 KB parsed inventory fails with `/bin/jq: Argument list too long`, so bearings prints `unknown / structured home snapshot failed` with an empty fleet - while the branch reads the same home and shows `active_child_work` with the live child, its landed rows, and its blocked gate. A separate transcript shows the intended contract change: a home whose inventory contradicts itself now keeps its pending captain decision and landed record with `structured-home` provenance and an unknown classification naming the contradiction, instead of being erased into the parent-event fallback. A third transcript shows the bounds are real, not a longer wait: four hanging homes cost 22s on base versus 7s on the branch, with per-home timeout, budget-clipped, and budget-never-reached reasons each attributed correctly and no hanging home promoted into current work. Finally the follow-up CI commit was verified by running the guard block itself (fleet-view 15, Bearings 46, both pass) and parsing ci.yml as YAML. No UI or rendered surface is involved - this is a CLI tool, so the end-user experience is the bearings TOON transcripts captured above. Everything passed; the worktree is clean and all fixtures live under the evidence directory.

title: feat(spawn): refuse dispatch onto a branch another live session is using
body:
## Why

A clean working tree at a known tip is not evidence that a branch is idle. The pre-dispatch check was point-in-time; the hazard has duration.

The incident: firstmate inspected a branch, saw a clean tree at a known tip, and dispatched a worker onto it. An interactive session in a **different directory for the same repository** was still working that branch and pushed twenty minutes later. The two sessions overlapped 31 minutes. The worker's push was rejected, it misattributed the cause to one of its own review helpers, and then "fixed" that non-problem in a way that broke something real.

The fault is the dispatcher's, not the worker's.

## What this adds

`bin/fm-branch-liveness.sh` - refuse-grade evidence that a session is currently alive on a branch. Three detectors, all must clear:

| detector | signal |
| --- | --- |
| `session` | live agent session transcripts, matched on `gitBranch` plus a `cwd` that resolves into the same **repository** |
| `checkout` | local checkouts of the repository on that branch **showing current activity** - a dirty tree, or an index/HEAD/reflog touched inside the activity window |
| `remote` | a branch head on the remote this checkout has never seen |

`bin/fm-spawn.sh` runs the check before any worktree or session provider is created, and refuses rather than warning.

### Design points worth knowing

- **Repository identity is git-common-dir or normalized remote URL, never path equality.** This is load-bearing: the collision was two different directories for one repository, so a path comparison would have missed it entirely.
- **Freshness comes from the transcript record's own timestamp, not file mtime.** Verified: the incident transcript's mtime was about three hours later than its last real turn, so mtime alone over-reports live sessions. mtime is still used as a cheap pre-filter, since it can only ever be newer than the last appended record.
- **The checkout detector requires activity, not merely having the branch checked out.** Branch state was already known to be insufficient; a clean, idle, abandoned checkout on the branch is not a live session and does not refuse.
- **The remote detector only runs when the branch already exists locally**, so ordinary per-task-branch dispatch never touches the network and an offline machine can still dispatch normal work.
- **Ownership resolution lives in `fm-spawn.sh`, not in the detector**, so the detector stays a pure "is anyone live on this branch" question.

### Fail-closed direction

Detection that cannot complete exits non-zero and refuses. `exit 0` means "checked, and nothing is there", so degrading an unreadable signal to `0` would restore exactly the silent all-clear that caused the incident.

An **absent** signal is deliberately different and clears: no transcript root means no agent sessions were ever recorded, and no remote means no remote actor. Both are real answers, not gaps.

### Override

`--allow-branch-collision` dispatches anyway. It is explicit, prints every finding as a warning, and records `branch_collision_override=1` in the task's durable metadata, so an overridden dispatch stays visible after the fact. It is not settable by config or environment.

### No false positives on the dispatcher's own workers

Those workers live in isolated worktrees of the same repository by design, so treating them as collisions would refuse every ordinary dispatch. The home, the project clone, the task's own worktree, and the task's own recorded metadata are excluded. The regression test for this uses a **control**: the same fixture refuses without the ownership evidence and clears with it, so the assertion cannot pass vacuously.

Ownership exclusion is scoped to the task's own record, so a *sibling* worker already live on a declared existing branch is refused rather than cleared. A firstmate worker is another live session too.

## Disclosed limitation - please read

**The brief scan matches command form only.** It looks for `git checkout` / `git switch` in the task brief and requires the branch to be declared with `--branch` when it names a branch other than the per-task one. A brief that names a branch **in prose** - "continue the work on story/1-4" with no git command - is **not** caught, so the guard silently checks the per-task branch instead of the branch the worker will actually use.

That exact case has already occurred in practice on another task, and **this guard would not have caught it**. The check itself is sound once pointed at the right branch; the gap is in inferring which branch that is. Closing it properly means declaring the branch at intake rather than recovering it from prose, which is outside this change.

Two further limits, stated rather than hidden, and both documented in the script header:

- The session detector reads Claude Code transcripts. Other harnesses are covered only through the harness-agnostic `checkout` and `remote` detectors.
- The checkout detector's candidate inventory is bounded to the clone's own worktrees, directories named by live sessions, and the home's project clones. An independent clone that no live session has touched is outside it; finding those would mean scanning the filesystem, which this guard deliberately does not do.

## Tests

12 cases in `tests/fm-branch-liveness.test.sh`, all passing, covering: a genuine cross-clone collision refused with named evidence; the same branch name in an unrelated repository cleared; a session quiet beyond the window not treated as live; the dispatcher's own recorded worktree cleared with a control run that refuses without the ownership evidence; sibling workers on their own branches never blocking an ordinary dispatch; the checkout detector refusing on activity rather than branch state; a remote head never seen locally refusing and clearing once fetched; a fresh per-task branch never reaching the network; unreadable signals failing closed while an absent signal stays a real answer; the dispatch path refusing and dispatching only under the explicit override; a brief pointing at another branch refusing until declared; and a task's own isolated copy on its own branch never blocking that task.

Lint (`bin/fm-lint.sh`), the documentation-audience check, and the test-coverage guard all pass.

title: feat(bin): persist chrome-devtools-axi SSO login for headless crewmate browser work
body:
## Intent Add a persistent chrome-devtools-axi Chrome profile convention so crewmates can perform Keycloak/SSO-gated browser and visual regression checks headlessly, without needing the captain to interactively log in on every launch. Fixed profile path is $FM_HOME/data/chrome-profile (data/ already gitignored, no new config/ override). Added bin/fm-chrome-login.sh as a captain-run-only helper for the one-time interactive login onto that persistent profile. Updated bin/fm-brief.sh's crewmate browser-work guidance (factored the previously duplicated rule into one shared BROWSER_RULE variable) so crewmates export CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_USER_DATA_DIR before browser work and, on a stale/missing login session, append blocked: {app} needs a fresh manual login via bin/fm-chrome-login.sh rather than attempting to authenticate themselves. Added docs/chrome-auth-persistence.md (linked from docs/configuration.md, classified operator-current) documenting rationale, setup, consumption, the single-profile concurrency limitation (deliberately unhandled), and expiry handling (just re-run fm-chrome-login.sh). Verified the persistence mechanism directly with chrome-devtools-axi: cookie+localStorage set on example.com persisted across a stop/relaunch against the same CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_USER_DATA_DIR, and did not persist with it unset (isolated mode) as a negative control - the exact property Keycloak SSO relies on. A prior pipeline run on this branch got through review/test/document/lint clean (one auto-fix review finding, an FM_ROOT vs FM_HOME path-consistency slip across the doc/script/brief, was fixed and re-reviewed) but failed at push because this account only has pull access to kunchenguid/firstmate. The captain forked to sambit-ekka/firstmate and no-mistakes was reinitialized with --fork-url to push there and open the PR cross-repo into kunchenguid/firstmate; resuming from that fork-aware push/PR path now. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-chrome-login.sh`, a captain-run-only helper that launches a headed `chrome-devtools-axi` session against a fixed persistent profile (`$FM_HOME/data/chrome-profile`) for one-time interactive SSO/Keycloak login. - Updated `bin/fm-brief.sh` to factor the previously duplicated browser-work rule into a shared `BROWSER_RULE` variable, instructing crewmates to export `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_USER_DATA_DIR` before browser work and, on a stale/missing session, append a `blocked:` status line pointing to `bin/fm-chrome-login.sh` instead of attempting to authenticate themselves. - Added `docs/chrome-auth-persistence.md` (linked from `docs/configuration.md`, listed in `docs/documentation-audiences.json` as `operator-current`, and referenced in `docs/scripts.md`) documenting the profile path convention, setup/consumption flow, single-profile concurrency limitation, and expiry handling. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a small, well-bounded doc+script addition (a new captain-run login helper, a deduplicated browser-work rule string, and cross-linked documentation) that matches the stated intent exactly, reuses established codebase conventions (usage-parsing idiom, FM_HOME/FM_ROOT resolution, documentation-audiences classification), and a prior path-consistency slip was already caught and fixed within this branch. ## Testing Both relevant test suites pass, the FM_ROOT/FM_HOME consistency fix noted in the intent is present and correct, and I reproduced the profile-persistence mechanism live via chrome-devtools-axi (positive persistence across stop/relaunch, negative in isolated mode), matching the author's own verification and the property Keycloak SSO depends on. Note: my first attempt used a session-only cookie (no expiry), which Chrome clears on full process quit regardless of profile persistence — that's expected browser behavior, not a defect; using an explicit max-age (as real SSO session cookies typically have) confirmed persistence correctly. - Evidence: example.com rendered after stop/relaunch against the same persistent Chrome profile, with cookie+localStorage confirmed intact via eval (local file: /var/folders/14/bbb3x64n5bd02h0qk406kks40000gq/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYVKV6RY6CFJYAD662HPZYDC/chrome-profile-persistence-after-relaunch.png) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

## Intent

add beads as third supported backlog backend

## What Changed

title: fix(bin): require the exact recorded tmux window in fm_backend_target_exists
body:
Fixes #1130. > Context: this fix was produced by a firstmate crew (a crewmate agent supervised by a first mate) running the no-mistakes pipeline end-to-end, during a pilot of firstmate itself. The change was reviewed and approved by a human captain at the review gate and test gate, and the full CI matrix passed on the fork (bsorescu/firstmate#1: lint, coverage guard, repo invariants, all portable shards, Herdr, macOS bash compatibility — 9/9 green). One pre-existing gap surfaced during review and was deliberately kept out of scope: `fm_backend_tmux_kill` cannot address a window whose name contains a dot (e.g. `fm-api.2`), and its best-effort contract swallows the failure — happy to file that as a separate issue/PR. ## Intent Fix fm_backend_target_exists (bin/fm-backend.sh) reporting a gone tmux window as alive - upstream issue kunchenguid/firstmate#1130. The tmux arm used a bare display-message probe that silently falls back to another window; it now requires the exact recorded window/pane via inventory or exact-answer equality, with fixtures corrected to model real tmux and red-first regression tests. ## What Changed - `fm_backend_target_exists` (bin/fm-backend.sh) no longer trusts a bare `tmux display-message -p -t` probe, which exits 0 while silently answering about another window when the recorded one is gone (kunchenguid/firstmate#1130). A `session:window` target is now proved by an exact window-index or window-name match in a `tmux list-windows` inventory of that session, a `%pane`/`@window` handle by exact-answer id equality, and a colon-less target — carrying no session to inventory against — fails closed. The window part is matched in full before the pane-index-stripped form, so a dotted window name like `fm-api.2` is not mistaken for `fm-api` + pane index while `firstmate:0.1` still resolves. - `bin/fm-crew-state.sh`'s `pane_readable` now routes its tmux arm through that shared primitive instead of duplicating the unsound probe, so a killed crew window reports `unknown / none / backend target gone` rather than a stale status-log-derived state. This also extends the fail-closed rule to tmux metas whose `window=` field has no session prefix, which now read gone. The stale comments in `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh` startup validation and `docs/tmux-backend.md` were updated to describe the inventory contract. - Tests: new red-first regression coverage in `tests/fm-backend-tmux-smoke.test.sh` (live vs. gone window, `%pane`/`@window` ids, dotted window names, colon-less refusal) and a `FM_FAKE_TMUX_WINDOW_GONE` case in `tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh`; fake-tmux fixtures across the backend, bearings, session-start, send, and wake suites gained the `list-windows` inventory arm real tmux answers with. `tests/fm-fleet-snapshot-view.test.sh` could not be run locally — it hangs identically on this branch and on the base commit, on an unrelated cmux stdin wedge — so that caller's suite needs remote CI to confirm. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: This round changes only two lines of comment text to a claim I verified directly (fm-crew-state.sh contains no awk), leaves the already-verified implementation byte-identical, and every earlier finding has been applied or explicitly decided by the captain. ## Testing I exercised the fix at the product surface rather than only in unit form: with a real tmux server on a private socket, bin/fm-crew-state.sh reports a killed crew window in a still-live session as \"unknown · none · backend target gone\" on the target commit, whereas the same scenario on base b6e351d still reports \"working · status-log\" because the bare display-message probe exits 0 answering about a decoy window. The change's new real-tmux smoke test is genuinely red-first (it fails on the pre-fix tree at the false-alive assertion), and all fixture-updated suites plus the remaining fm_backend_target_exists callers pass: fm-backend, fm-crew-state, fm-bearings-snapshot, fm-session-start, the three fm-send suites, fm-daemon, fm-send-strict and fm-secondmate-liveness. I found bin/fm-crew-state.sh's routing change had no test that would fail if reverted, so I added one focused regression case (plus a fixture arm modelling the real session-alive/window-gone shape) and confirmed it is red on base and green on the fix. One caller suite, fm-fleet-snapshot-view, hangs on this host in an unrelated cmux workspace lookup and hangs identically on the base commit, so it is pre-existing and left to CI; transient temp checkouts, logs and tmux sockets from my runs were removed and the only working-tree change left is the added regression case.

window 1: other-window window 2: fm-crew-1 $ fm-crew-state.sh crew-1 state: working · source: status-log · implementing the widget --- crew window killed (crewmate is gone) --- window 1: other-window - Outcome: ⚠️ 1 warning across 1 run (44m49s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 6 issues found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - 🚨 `tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh:32` - The fake tmux in make_fakebin handles only display-message and capture-pane; an unmatched `list-windows` falls through to `exit 0` with no output. Since fm_backend_target_exists now reads the session inventory, every tmux endpoint in this suite reads absent. Concretely: test_domain_alpha_stale_parent_event_does_not_become_current_work asserts `.terminal_evidence.captured == true` (line 225), but terminal_evidence_json (bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:971) short-circuits to captured:false when `.endpoint.exists == false` for window=firstmate:fm-domain-alpha; and line 345 asserts `.endpoint.exists == true` for the child meta window=firstmate:fm-phase8 (bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:472). Five sibling fixtures were updated for the inventory read; this one was missed. Add a `list-windows` arm that answers with the queried home's window names (e.g. `sed -n 's/^window=[^:]*://p' "$FM_HOME"/state/*.meta`, excluding the `*dead-*` ids the fixture deliberately models as gone) so the fixture keeps its existing alive/absent convention. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:148` - The authorized failure this change fixes remains reachable through a sibling path. pane_readable's tmux arm is the exact bare probe the new comment declares unsound: `tmux display-message -p -t "$1" '#{pane_id}' >/dev/null 2>&1`. Verified against real tmux 3.7b: for a gone window in a live session that call exits 0 while answering about a different window. So line 605 (`pane_readable "$BACKEND_TARGET" || emit unknown none "backend target gone"`) never fires for a killed task window; crew-state then falls through crew_pane_is_busy (capture-pane, which does fail correctly) to the status-log fallback and reports a stale state (e.g. working) for a crew whose endpoint is gone - the same false-alive class, feeding the watcher's provably-working triage. fm-crew-state.sh already sources bin/fm-backend.sh (line 62), so the earliest supported shared boundary is calling `fm_backend_target_exists tmux "$1"` here instead of duplicating a third symptom patch. Related: bin/fm-backend.sh:830 still says the function "Mirrors fm-crew-state.sh's pane_readable check", which this change makes false. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-backend.sh:862` - The pane-index strip can report a live window dead. Task ids legitimately contain dots (fm_task_id_path_safe, bin/fm-pr-lib.sh:97, rejects only a leading dot), so id `api.2` yields window `fm-api.2` and target `sess:fm-api.2` (bin/fm-spawn.sh:942,946). The numeric-suffix branch strips `.2`, the inventory is searched for `fm-api`, and the live endpoint reads dead. Verified against real tmux 3.7b: `display-message -p -t 'sess:fm-api.2' '#{window_name}'` resolves to the window actually named `fm-api.2`, and fm_backend_tmux_agent_state (bin/backends/tmux.sh:185) matches that exact name - so the two liveness readers now contradict each other for the same target. Fix without losing the intended `firstmate:0.1` support: match the full window part first and only fall back to the stripped form (awk `$1 == w || $2 == w || $1 == ws || $2 == ws`). - ℹ️ `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:1375` - The startup-validation comment now misdescribes the code: it claims "for backend=tmux this runs the exact same `tmux display-message -p -t \"$TARGET\" '#{pane_id}'` call as before", which is exactly the probe this change replaced. For a session:window supervisor target it is now a list-windows inventory read. Update the comment so the next reader does not trust a primitive that is no longer used. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-backend-tmux-smoke.test.sh:165` - The new %pane and @window exact-answer arms (bin/fm-backend.sh:849,852) have no test anywhere, yet they carry the subtlest premise of the fix: a gone id makes display-message exit 0 with EMPTY output (confirmed on tmux 3.7b), so only the equality comparison distinguishes it from a live handle. This smoke test already holds a real live pane and window id, so the regression is two lines next to the existing block: assert alive for `$(tmux display-message -p -t "$TARGET" '#{pane_id}')` and dead for a never-allocated id such as %99999/@99999. The bare-name rejection arm (line 874) is likewise untested. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-backend.sh:874` - The catch-all `return 1` makes a colon-less tmux target unconditionally dead. This is a supported recorded shape elsewhere: fm_backend_meta_for_window and fm_backend_resolve_selector accept a meta whose window field is a bare name (fixture `window=custom-window`, tests/fm-backend.test.sh:613), and fm-session-start.sh:360 probes `${target:-$window}` straight from that field. Such an endpoint previously always read alive (via the fallback bug) and now always reads dead - neither is correct. If bare-window metas are still supported, the accurate read is the all-sessions inventory that fm_backend_tmux_resolve_bare_selector (bin/backends/tmux.sh:31) already performs; if they are not, the hard refusal matches fm_backend_validate_task_endpoint (bin/fm-backend.sh:448) and only the doc comment needs to say so. 🔧 Fix: route crew-state through fixed target_exists, fix dotted windows 3 infos still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-backend.sh:880` - The rationale for matching in-shell instead of through awk asserts something I could not substantiate: "fm-crew-state.sh's fallback path, which runs under a deliberately minimal PATH, has none today". fm-crew-state.sh sets no PATH itself, and both of its callers - bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:206 and bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:337 (FM_CREW_STATE_BIN) - invoke it with the ambient PATH; no caller scrubs it. The rest of the justification holds (the loop is one fork, and fm-crew-state.sh genuinely uses no awk today - only grep/sed/cut/head/tail), so the fix is to drop or correct the minimal-PATH clause rather than change the code. Worth correcting because this codebase treats these rationale comments as contracts - the "Mirrors fm-crew-state.sh's pane_readable check" line was repaired this round for exactly that reason. - ℹ️ `bin/backends/tmux.sh:135` - Pre-existing and NOT introduced by this change - flagging only because the new smoke fixture creates such a window and its comment documents half of it. fm_backend_tmux_kill runs `tmux kill-window -t "=$session:=$window"`; verified on tmux 3.7b that for a window named `fm-api.2` both the plain form (`can't find pane: 2`) and the exact-match form (`can't find window: fm-api`) fail, and the deliberate `|| true` best-effort contract swallows the failure. Since task ids only have to be path-safe (fm_task_id_path_safe, bin/fm-pr-lib.sh:97), id `api.2` spawns window `fm-api.2` (bin/fm-spawn.sh:942), passes fm_backend_validate_task_endpoint (bin/fm-backend.sh:448 requires exactly `fm-$id`), and now correctly reads alive - but teardown removes the metadata while the tmux window survives. Addressing it would need a kill by stable @window id (fm_backend_tmux_create_task already captures one) and is a separate change; nothing here should block on it. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:609` - Note for the PR description the captain planned for the accepted fail-closed decision (colon-less tmux targets are dead by design, bin/fm-backend.sh:874): routing pane_readable through the shared primitive widens that decision's blast radius beyond the digests named in round 1. A tmux meta whose window field has no session prefix (a shape fm_backend_meta_for_window and fm_backend_resolve_selector still accept - fixture `window=custom-window`, tests/fm-backend.test.sh:613) now makes fm-crew-state.sh emit `unknown / none / backend target gone` instead of a status-log-derived state, which also propagates to fm-fleet-snapshot's current_state (bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:206) and to the watcher's crew_is_provably_working predicate. No code change requested - this is the deliberate, already-approved semantics; it just deserves a line in the write-up. 🔧 Fix: drop unsubstantiated minimal-PATH clause from inventory comment ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

✅ Low: All previous issues have been fixed; the beads backend integration is well-bounded, properly validated at runtime, and documented with clear feature limitations.

## Testing

Unit tests and integration tests all pass. Beads backend configuration is properly recognized, validated during bootstrap (checking task CLI and store reachability), integrated into session-start digest (queries with task list --label "status:ready"), and safely refuses unsupported operations like backlog handoff. title: feat(fm-brief): add --group flag for browsable data/ grouping
body:
## Intent

Reorganize the data/ directory so that all generated reports are grouped under a folder matching their project name, matching the existing projects/ structure. The developer required this change be applied properly to firstmate's own shared scripts/AGENTS.md contract (not just moved as files), with lint and tests passing before committing.

## What Changed

- Added an optional `--group=<name>` flag to `bin/fm-brief.sh` that symlinks `data/<name>/<task-id>` to `data/<task-id>`, letting related tasks (e.g. tasks under the same project/initiative) be browsed together while keeping `data/<task-id>/` as the single authoritative path all other scripts key off.
- Added validation to prevent inconsistent or self-referential state: rejects malformed group names (`.`, `..`, containing `/`), a group name equal to the task's own id, `--group` combined with `--secondmate`, a group name that collides with an existing task's own directory, and a task id that collides with an existing `--group` folder (detected via a `.fm-group` sentinel file); existing correct symlinks are treated as idempotent no-ops.
- Updated the script header comment documenting `--group` usage and all refusal branches, and added test coverage in `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` for the new refusal paths.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The two remaining test-coverage gaps from the prior round are now closed with tests that correctly exercise both new refusal branches (self-referential --group, reverse group/task collision) and match the established pattern in the file; the --group feature is now fully guarded and tested in both collision directions.

## Testing

`tests/fm-brief.test.sh passes in full, including the new test_group_symlink_behavior. data/ is gitignored so the real adrevila-v2 report move isn't in this commit; instead verified the mechanism manually in a scratch FM_HOME, producing symlinks data/adrevila-v2/{market-research,brd,trd} pointing to the flat data/<id> dirs.`

<details>
<summary>Evidence: CLI transcript of --group=adrevila-v2 demo</summary>

```text
=== Simulating adrevila-v2 report grouping via bin/fm-brief.sh --group ===

$ fm-brief.sh market-research adrevila --scout --group=adrevila-v2
scaffolded: /tmp/tmp.LkXHQepCeH/data/market-research/brief.md (scout; replace {TASK})
exit: 0

$ fm-brief.sh brd adrevila --scout --group=adrevila-v2
scaffolded: /tmp/tmp.LkXHQepCeH/data/brd/brief.md (scout; replace {TASK})
exit: 0

$ fm-brief.sh trd adrevila --scout --group=adrevila-v2
scaffolded: /tmp/tmp.LkXHQepCeH/data/trd/brief.md (scout; replace {TASK})
exit: 0

=== Resulting data/ layout (authoritative flat dirs + browsable group folder) ===
data
data/adrevila-v2
data/adrevila-v2/brd
data/adrevila-v2/.fm-group
data/adrevila-v2/market-research
data/adrevila-v2/trd
data/brd
data/brd/brief.md
data/market-research
data/market-research/brief.md
data/trd
data/trd/brief.md

=== Symlinks resolve to the authoritative flat task directories ===
data/adrevila-v2/market-research -> ../market-research
data/adrevila-v2/brd -> ../brd
data/adrevila-v2/trd -> ../trd
```
</details>

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

<details>
<summary>✅ **intent** - passed</summary>

✅ No issues found.

</details>

<details>
<summary>✅ **Rebase** - passed</summary>

✅ No issues found.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 **Review** - 3 issues found → auto-fixed (2) ✅</summary>

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:144` - The collision guard added in this branch only checks that `$DATA/$GROUP/brief.md` or `report.md` doesn't already exist. It runs after `mkdir -p "$DATA/$ID"` (line 142) has already created the new task's own directory, so when `--group` is passed the *same* value as the task id itself (e.g. `fm-brief.sh foo repo --scout --group=foo`), the check inspects `$DATA/foo/brief.md` — which doesn't exist yet because this invocation hasn't written it — and passes. The script then creates `$DATA/foo/foo` as a symlink to `../foo`, which resolves back to `$DATA/foo` itself: a self-referential symlink sitting inside the task's own authoritative directory. This is a simple oversight, not a product-behavior question — grouping a task under its own id is never meaningful, so it should just be rejected outright alongside the existing `*/* | . | ..` format check.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:141` - The new guard (this branch's second commit) refuses `--group=<name>` when `<name>` is already an existing task's own directory, but does not guard the mirror direction: if `<name>` was previously created purely as a --group folder (via some other task's `--group=<name>`), and a later task is scaffolded with id `<name>` itself (no --group), nothing detects the collision. Concrete sequence: `fm-brief.sh a repo --scout --group=widget` creates `data/widget/a -> ../a`; then `fm-brief.sh widget repo --scout` succeeds silently, and `data/widget/` becomes simultaneously task `widget`'s own authoritative directory *and* still contains the stray symlink `a` pointing to an unrelated task. Nothing else in the script inspects directory contents at this shared boundary, so the merge goes unreported. Since group names are commonged from project/initiative names (per the intent behind this feature) and task ids share the same `data/` namespace, this is plausibly reachable. The earliest shared boundary to close this would be marking group-only directories (e.g. a sentinel file dropped by the `--group` branch) and checking for it wherever a new task id is about to claim `$DATA/$ID`.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:144` - Every other flag-validation check in this script (format check at line 117, secondmate-incompatibility at line 125, herdr-lab/no-projects checks) runs before `BRIEF=...`/`mkdir -p "$DATA/$ID"`, so a refused invocation creates nothing.
