## Intent Implement the Windows-to-WSL launcher bridge for Firstmate by adding the repository-root firstmate.bat and bin/fm-wsl-entry.sh, so a Windows double-click reaches the existing bin/fm-launch.sh harness menu and Herdr launch/attach flow. The bridge must handle Windows repository paths containing spaces, enter WSL deterministically without relying on a login shell or caller working directory, propagate launcher arguments and exit status, and print actionable failures that remain visible after a double-click. Add executable regression coverage for the WSL entry and native batch command construction without requiring a live Windows/WSL session, plus current operator and contributor documentation. This is a new upstream contribution based only on origin/main; the pending launcher PR is a dependency and none of its commits may be copied into this branch. Keep the diff limited to the bridge, its tests/CI coverage, and documentation required to register and operate it. Do not place a launcher in E:/Agentic Engineering or retire any platform launcher in this change. ## What Changed - Add a repository-root Windows batch launcher and deterministic WSL entrypoint that support spaced paths, forward arguments and exit codes, and keep actionable failures visible. - Add regression coverage and a Windows CI lane for batch command construction, WSL entry behavior, and platform-specific line endings. - Document Windows/WSL prerequisites, launch behavior, troubleshooting, and contributor ownership. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The bridge is well-bounded, satisfies the source-verifiable intent, preserves the pending launcher as an uncopied dependency, and includes appropriate portable and native Windows regression coverage. ## Testing Inspected the base-to-target scope and ancestry, ran the focused bridge suite twice—including its native Windows cmd.exe path—manually captured both sides of the bridge with nonzero status propagation and reviewer-visible CLI transcripts, verified CRLF/LF checkout behavior, and confirmed testing left the worktree clean; all targeted checks passed. title: feat(bin): allow evidenced pre-merge task teardown
body:
## Intent Implement the captain's 2026-07-31 cleanup ruling in bin/fm-teardown.sh. Permit cleanup of a completed PR-based task before merge only when the latest completion exactly names the canonically recorded GitHub PR, live GitHub evidence shows that same open non-draft PR has an all-passing completed check suite with zero failed, pending, or skipped/cancelled/expected buckets and is mergeable, the live head exactly matches the recorded PR head, and repository evidence proves local HEAD is contained in that PR head; preserve the local task branch on this path and print its branch/PR identity on successful cleanup, without adding retention metadata or a reaper. Treat absent, duplicated, stale, contradictory, or unavailable completion, check, mergeability, identity, or head evidence as a refusal. Continue refusing red, pending, skipped, or conflicted PRs, uncommitted work, genuinely unpublished commits, and every existing unlanded-work safety condition; merely pushed remote reachability is intentionally insufficient and GitHub outages refuse. Replace the obsolete generic 'land its PR' diagnosis with evidence-specific refusal. Reuse the authenticated configured-remote PR-head fetch path, pin GitHub test mocks to exact canonical arguments, centralize branch finalization, and ensure the preserve notice survives detach failure without broadening retention behavior. Add regression coverage for the allowed path and every refusal boundary, retain existing merged/content/local-only/lock/backend behavior, and run required lint and focused teardown suites. ## What Changed - Allow completed PR-based tasks to tear down before merge only when canonical completion, live GitHub checks, mergeability, PR-head identity, and local commit ancestry all validate. - Preserve the task branch and report its PR identity on successful pre-merge cleanup, while returning evidence-specific refusals for missing, ambiguous, stale, failing, pending, skipped, conflicted, or unpublished states. - Centralize branch finalization, update teardown policy documentation, and expand regression coverage across allowed and refusal paths while retaining existing teardown behavior. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the fix commit resolves all prior findings and the full branch diff now conforms to the source-verifiable teardown safety criteria without introducing another material issue. ## Testing After session bootstrap and diff/coverage inspection, the focused teardown suite passed across the permitted pre-merge path and its refusal boundaries, and a separate CLI-level scenario demonstrated successful cleanup, exact branch/PR preservation notice, and an unchanged preserved ref; no UI artifact applies because this is a shell CLI policy change, and no source or transient working-tree artifacts remained.
Evidence: Focused teardown test suite ```text ok - local-only worktree with HEAD on a fork remote is torn down (fix holds) ok - teardown prompts tasks-axi backlog refresh when compatible ok - teardown honors config/backlog-backend=manual even when tasks-axi is compatible ok - local-only worktree with truly unpushed work is refused (safety preserved) ok - local-only worktree with work merged into local main is torn down (no regression) ok - completed green mergeable PR is cleaned before merge with its local branch preserved ok - preserved branch identity survives detach failure ok - green PR whose suite reports skipped checks refuses cleanup ok - unusable check suites refuse pre-merge cleanup with evidence-specific reasons ok - no-mistakes worktree with genuinely unlanded work is refused (safety preserved) ok - red PR refuses cleanup and preserves all task recovery state ok - pending PR checks refuse cleanup ok - conflicted PR refuses cleanup and preserves all task recovery state ok - green PR does not authorize cleanup of a genuinely unpublished later commit ok - patch-equivalent divergent local HEAD refuses pre-merge cleanup ok - absent or ambiguous completion, check, mergeability, identity, and head evidence all refuse cleanup ok - local-only worktree with unpushed work is torn down under --force (escape hatch) ok - teardown completes when an exact busy-state sidecar is already absent ok - herdr teardown removes pane-owned escalation dedupe state ok - herdr projection teardown retires its journal only after confirming the exact recorded pane is gone ok - herdr projection teardown retains the stale journal and attempts no workspace cleanup when exact-pane close is unconfirmed ok - squash-merged + deleted-branch worktree (PR merged) is torn down (the fix) ok - squash-merged PR accepts a local HEAD that is an ancestor of the final PR head ok - teardown discovers a merged PR by branch name and tears down when no pr= was ever recorded ok - squash-merged PR accepts replayed unpushed local patches contained in the PR head ok - merged PR does not allow teardown after a later local commit ok - fm-pr-check does not refresh PR head after HEAD moves ok - fm-pr-check records the remote PR head when the local worktree lags ok - worktree whose content already landed in the default branch is torn down (content fallback) ok - content fallback refreshes origin default before comparing trees ok - dirty worktree is refused even when its committed work has landed (dirty always wins) ok - gh lookup error with content not in default refuses (fail-safe) ok - provably-stale worktree index.lock (old, no live holder) is cleared and teardown succeeds ok - live-held worktree index.lock is never removed and teardown refuses ok - lsof errors leave worktree index.lock in place and refuse teardown ok - stale lock cleanup rechecks and refuses dirty worktree before return ok - normal repo index.lock is resolved from the worktree and cleared when stale ok - lock mtime read failures leave worktree index.lock in place and refuse teardown ok - transient index.lock cleared after first failed return is retried successfully without force-remove ok - persistent index.lock exhausts retries and refuses without force-removing the lock ok - empty retry wait overrides use the default without aborting teardown ok - fractional legacy retry wait remains supported without arithmetic ```
Evidence: Successful green, mergeable pre-merge teardown transcript ```text LIVE PR FIXTURE: state: open draft: false head: sha: dd7ffd60a98d8593e2f09a267d2169875dbb5e8c mergeable: true summary: "3 passed, 0 failed, 3 total" TEARDOWN CLI OUTPUT: Preserved local branch fm/task-x1: task-x1 was cleaned up before https://github.com/example/repo/pull/7 merged. Delete the branch once that PR lands. /tmp/fm-teardown-tests.IFeOgf/reviewer-e2e/project: already current teardown task-x1 complete (window firstmate:fm-task-x1, worktree /tmp/fm-teardown-tests.IFeOgf/reviewer-e2e/wt) Backlog: task-x1 just finished. Run tasks-axi done task-x1 --pr https://github.com/example/repo/pull/7, then run tasks-axi ready for dependency-cleared candidates, check date gates, and dispatch only work whose blockers are gone and date is due. EXIT STATUS: 0 PRESERVED REF: refs/heads/fm/task-x1 -> dd7ffd60a98d8593e2f09a267d2169875dbb5e8c ```

🔧 **Review** - 5 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-teardown.sh:643` - Intent requires “zero failed, pending, or skipped/cancelled/expected buckets” and explicitly says to continue refusing skipped PRs. This condition instead accepts skipped checks whenever `passed + skipped == total`; require `skipped == 0` and update the regression that currently expects skipped checks to pass. - 🚨 `bin/fm-teardown.sh:458` - Intent requires repository proof that local HEAD is contained in the PR head and refusal of genuinely unpublished commits. The patch-ID fallback accepts a divergent local commit merely because its patch matches a PR commit, even though local HEAD is not an ancestor of the PR head; use strict ancestry for the pre-merge path. - 🚨 `bin/fm-teardown.sh:562` - Intent says duplicated completion evidence must refuse. Only the final non-empty status line is inspected, so two identical completion events—or an earlier contradictory completion followed by a valid one—still authorize cleanup. Count and validate completion records rather than accepting solely from the last line. - 🚨 `bin/fm-teardown.sh:1476` - Intent requires that the preserve notice survive detach failure. The notice is emitted only inside the successful `checkout --detach` branch, so a detach failure silently omits the sole surviving branch/PR identity even though cleanup continues. Emit the preservation notice independently of detach success. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:1491` - Intent requires branch finalization to be centralized, but the Orca and non-Orca paths duplicate branch discovery, detach, preserve announcement, and deletion logic. Extract one finalization helper so both backends cannot drift—particularly around detach-failure handling. 🔧 Fix: Enforce strict pre-merge teardown evidence ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bin/fm-session-start.sh` - Inspected `git diff f7d0d0a703a717880656709d7906615505b3f2c0..052d4ce166b73f6c1f2edb4a59097abaa5230ccf` and the teardown test matrix. - `bash tests/fm-teardown.test.sh > /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KYWDZ21C7BTCTPBSPAH5EF5Q/fm-teardown-focused-suite.log 2>&1` - Ran a hermetic end-to-end `bin/fm-teardown.sh task-x1` scenario using exact canonical GitHub mock arguments and captured live-PR fixtures, CLI output, exit status, and the surviving branch ref in `green-mergeable-teardown-transcript.txt`. - Checked `git status --short` and searched for transient build/cache directories after testing; the working tree remained clean.

```text
Firstmate will then load its `no-mistakes-readiness` skill and return the task to you for the durable implementation-readiness preflight.
Do not invoke no-mistakes until that Firstmate-owned preflight reports `READY` for your current implementation commit.
If it reports `NOT_READY`, keep the work in this implementation session, correct it, commit it, and repeat the preflight instead of asking the pipeline to finish the feature.
After `READY`, Firstmate will instruct you to run /no-mistakes to validate and ship a PR.

You drive no-mistakes by responding to its gates, not by implementing fixes.
Follow the guidance no-mistakes itself provides for the mechanics: it loads when you invoke /no-mistakes, and `no-mistakes axi run --help` plus the `help` lines in each `axi` response are authoritative and version-matched to the installed binary.
Do not hand-edit, commit, or fix findings yourself while a run is active - the pipeline applies every fix.

Two firstmate-specific rules layer on top of that guidance:
- ask-user findings are never yours to answer: escalate to firstmate (rule 6) and stop.
  Firstmate applies the authority contract in its `AGENTS.md` and obtains any required captain decision.
  When the decision comes back, feed it to the gate with `no-mistakes axi respond` and let the pipeline apply it - do not route the question to "the user" or implement the fix yourself.
- Avoid `--yes`: it would silently bypass firstmate's authority check and any required captain escalation.

After /no-mistakes reports CI green (the CI-ready return point - do not wait for it to keep monitoring in the background until merge), append `done: PR {url} checks green` and stop. You are finished.
```
</details>

## Rescope

This pull request now builds on #1452, which established `bin/fm-secondmate-registry-lib.sh` as the strict owner of `data/secondmates.md` parsing and rejects ambiguous duplicate bindings.

- `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` already routes its parser call and registry helper handoffs through `fm-ff-lib.sh` to the strict owner, so it is unchanged.

- `bin/fm-update.sh` already calls the strict line parser through `fm-ff-lib.sh`; its other registry references are the path variable and explanatory comment, so it is unchanged.
- `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` contained the only remaining independent parser among the four audited scripts, and that parser is replaced here.
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh` has no registry references on current `main` and is unchanged.

## Validation

title: fix(watch): attach --restart to a healthy watcher instead of force-replacing
body:
## Intent

Repair the watcher restart contract so `bin/fm-watch-arm.sh --restart` attaches to an already healthy, identity-verified watcher without signaling it. Preserve home scoping, singleton ownership, stale-lock recovery, PID-reuse resistance, bounded replacement behavior, Bash 3.2 compatibility, and the live primary watcher. Keep this change separate from the parked #1336 branch.

## What changed

- Moved the shared healthy-watcher gate ahead of arm/restart mode dispatch.
- Both ordinary arm and `--restart` now attach to a healthy identity-matched watcher and follow that cycle.
- Replacement remains limited to an unhealthy holder recorded in the same `FM_HOME` lock.
- Strengthened `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh` with a ready-synchronized TERM-resistant peer, a no-TERM assertion, and failure-path fixture cleanup.
- Updated the maintained architecture contract for the new restart behavior.

## Diagnosis

- Initiating trigger: `--restart` entered its replacement path before checking shared watcher health.
- Masking condition: a peer that had already installed its TERM handler could survive the signal and make the later attach path appear correct.
- Visible symptom: the focused test observed `watcher: started` instead of attaching to the verified healthy peer, and the failed fixture could retain the test pipe.
- Counterfactual: ordinary arm attached successfully to the same healthy, identity-verified state, isolating the divergence to restart mode.

## Validation

No-mistakes run `01KYWKT69M4Y1NT901Z8JTEXW1` completed rebase, independent review, full tests, documentation review, lint, fork push, PR creation, and its checks-passed decision point on rebased head `eaf5c96`.

title: feat(bin): refuse a byte-identical or unpairable before/after evidence image pair
body:
## Summary
- Add `bin/fm-evidence-check.sh`, a deterministic check that refuses a merge when a PR's before/after evidence images are byte-identical, or when a directory's before-*/after-* images can't be paired at all - both are the fabricated- or unverified-visual-check shape this tool exists to catch.
- Pairing supports the naming conventions seen across the fleet's history: exact `before-<suffix>`/`after-<suffix>` (or reversed `<prefix>-before`/`<prefix>-after`), and a shared leading `<N>-` ordinal when the suffix instead describes state (e.g. `before-1-typed-not-saved.png` / `after-1-typed-with-save-button.png`). An explicit, greppable `.allow-identical` marker opts a genuinely-intentional identical pair back in.
- Wire it into `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh`: before merging, the check runs against the actual GitHub PR head (freshly fetched `refs/pull/<n>/head`, falling back to the recorded `pr_head=`, then the local worktree HEAD with a warning) rather than a possibly-stale local worktree, following the same head-resolution pattern `bin/fm-review-diff.sh` already uses.
- One-line pointer added to `AGENTS.md` so a ship brief capturing before/after evidence points a worker at `bin/fm-evidence-check.sh --help`, which remains the sole owner of the naming convention.

## Test plan
- [x] `bin/fm-lint.sh` (shellcheck clean)
- [x] `tests/fm-evidence-check.test.sh` (12 cases: identical pair refused, genuine diff passes, after-only/no-images pass silently, reversed convention, ordinal pairing on real fleet-history filenames, unpairable set refuses instead of a silent ok, a leftover mismatched pair beside a matched pair still refuses, a genuinely one-sided extra beside a matched pair still passes, `.allow-identical` opt-out, `--local` mode, usage errors)
- [x] `tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh` (identical-evidence pair refuses the merge, a genuinely different pair still merges, evidence is checked against the fetched remote PR head rather than a stale local worktree HEAD)

title: feat(bin): add checkpoint-commit discipline to briefs and an opt-in evidence write-through
body:
## Intent

Put checkpoint-commit discipline into firstmate's brief scaffold (bin/fm-brief.sh), and route scout evidence through an opt-in write-through to a separate private evidence repository.

Background the diff will not show. The scaffold's generated definition of done said a task is complete only when committed, which reads as 'commit at the end'. That is fine for accumulating code and wrong for anything expensive to reproduce, where the moment of maximum value is the moment of maximum exposure. The motivating near-miss: roughly two hours of measurement compute sat as untracked files while its harness was already committed, and other workers exited with many uncommitted files. So the generated contract now says: preserve expensive-to-reproduce evidence the moment it exists, ahead of any analysis drawn from it; never exceed about 15 minutes of changed files without a checkpoint commit; and the distinction that matters is cost to reproduce, not task size, because 'commit often' alone does not carry that.

Deliberate decisions a reviewer should not re-litigate:

- The destination sentence differs by task kind on purpose. A ship task's branch outlives the task; a scout's worktree and every commit in it are discarded at cleanup, so telling a scout to 'commit' raw evidence would lose exactly the irreplaceable output the contract protects. The scout is routed to its report directory instead, and the scout write boundary was widened to permit that write.
- The write-through is an opt-in LOCAL config key (config/evidence-repo) and never scaffold text. bin/fm-brief.sh ships to every firstmate user while the evidence repository is one captain's private repo, so no repository may ever be named in shared tracked material or a generated brief. A home without the key behaves exactly as before.
- Firstmate pushes as custodian at teardown; scouts never push, so the scout contract 'never push to any remote' is unchanged.
- The local commit is the custody guarantee and the push is best-effort, and teardown gates on the commit and NOT on the push. This asymmetry is required, not an oversight: gating cleanup on a push would make preserving evidence and reclaiming a worktree block each other. Please do not suggest collapsing it into one success path.
- No redaction pass, because the destination is private. The push therefore verifies visibility first and refuses to publish into a repository that is not private, which is where that precondition fails loudly if it ever stops holding.
- Layout is <evidence-repo>/<home-tag>/<task-id>/, keyed on FM_HOME rather than reusing fm-backend-hometag-lib.sh, because that library hashes FM_ROOT and several homes can share one code root. Derivable from the task alone, with no registry by decision.
- Size policy is a named constant: artifacts at or below 64 MiB commit whole, anything larger is recorded by size and SHA-256 only so corpus-scale material is described rather than committed.

Explicitly out of scope: a separate queued item fixes the inconsistent placement of [key=...] in this same file's keyed-decision examples. Those lines were left exactly as they are so the two changes do not collide.

Existing scaffold safety contracts were preserved without reflowing: the worktree-isolation assertion, the Herdr lifecycle declaration, the status protocol, and the delivery-mode definitions of done.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-brief.sh` now renders one shared `# Commit discipline` section into both the ship and scout scaffolds: preserve expensive-to-reproduce evidence the moment it exists and ahead of any analysis drawn from it, never exceed about 15 minutes of changed files without a checkpoint commit, and judge by cost to reproduce rather than task size. Only the destination sentence varies, since a ship task commits to its surviving branch while a scout's worktree is discarded at cleanup, so a scout copies raw evidence into its report directory instead; scout rule 2 was widened to permit exactly the files the scout puts there itself, leaving `brief.md` intact for respawn.
- New `bin/fm-evidence.sh` provides an opt-in custodian write-through: absent the local, gitignored `config/evidence-repo` it is a silent no-op, and when set it copies `data/<task-id>/` into `<evidence-repo>/<home-tag>/<task-id>/`, committing artifacts at or below 64 MiB whole (overridable via `config/evidence-max-direct-bytes`) and recording anything larger, plus symlinks, in `EVIDENCE-MANIFEST.txt` by size and SHA-256. The best-effort push is skipped unless every URL the push would reach is a `github.com` host (including the `github.com-<alias>` form) and resolves to a private repository, since artifacts are copied unredacted.
- `bin/fm-teardown.sh` invokes that custodian before destructive cleanup for non-secondmate homes, refusing cleanup when the local commit fails and warning instead under `--force`; the gate is on the commit and never on the push, so an unreachable remote cannot block reclaiming a worktree. `AGENTS.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, and `docs/scripts.md` document the two new config keys and the scout-written evidence beside its report, with new coverage in `tests/fm-brief.test.sh`, `tests/fm-evidence.test.sh`, and `tests/fm-teardown-evidence.test.sh`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Every substantive finding from the previous two rounds is now closed with behavioral tests that exercise the executable, the feature remains opt-in and off by default, and the only item left is a locale nit in a verification helper whose failure direction is already safe.

## Testing

I ran the three targeted suites (fm-brief, fm-evidence, fm-teardown-evidence) with no failures and confirmed they are picked up by CI lanes rather than only locally, then produced product-level evidence for the intent itself: real briefs generated by bin/fm-brief.sh showing the ship-versus-scout destination sentences and the widened scout write boundary alongside the untouched isolation, Herdr, status and done contracts; a real bin/fm-evidence.sh run showing the silent opted-out no-op, the committed layout, the 65 MiB manifest-only record with a matching SHA-256, the unfollowed symlink, per-home separation of a shared task id, and refusals to push into a genuinely public GitHub repo and an unverifiable host with the real gh-axi; and bin/fm-teardown.sh transcripts showing cleanup refused with the worktree kept when evidence could not be preserved, cleanup proceeding over committed evidence with an unreachable remote, an opted-out home unchanged, and --force warning instead of blocking. No UI surface is involved, so the evidence is CLI transcripts and generated brief markdown rather than screenshots. All scratch fixtures were removed and the worktree is clean.

```text
This project ships **direct-PR**: you raise the PR yourself, without the no-mistakes pipeline.
```

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-evidence.sh:234` - The private-visibility precondition - the only guard protecting unredacted evidence - can validate a different repository than the one being pushed to. remote_owner_name() (line 206) reduces any remote URL to its last two path segments with no host check, and remote_visibility() looks that slug up on github.com. If any private github.com repo with that slug is visible to the captain, remote_visibility returns "private" and line 353 pushes unredacted evidence to the actual non-GitHub remote whose visibility was never established. The header comment claims a deeper host path "simply yields a slug the GitHub lookup will not resolve", which only covers depth, not a same-depth non-GitHub host. Fix: require the remote host to be github.com (accepting the `github.com-<alias>` form the header deliberately preserves) and return non-zero otherwise, so the push is skipped rather than authorized by an unrelated repository.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-evidence.sh:330` - `git add -- "$dest"` on a directory pathspec silently skips files matched by the destination repo's .gitignore or a global core.excludesFile, so custody is falsely claimed. Concrete path: an evidence clone created from a template whose .gitignore contains `*.log` (or `tmp/`, `*.bin`, `data/`) receives a task whose artifacts include `probe.log`. The manifest at EVIDENCE-MANIFEST.txt is still added and changed, so `git diff --cached --quiet` at line 333 is false, the commit at line 335 succeeds, and line 336 prints "committed N artifact(s)" - while probe.log was never tracked. Teardown then destroys the worktree on the strength of that success. Use `git add --force -- "$dest"` so the custody claim matches what was actually committed.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-evidence.sh:275` - `cp -p` preserves the source mode into the destination, so a read-only artifact breaks the repeat-preserve path that tests/fm-evidence.test.sh:test_repeat_preserve_is_idempotent pins. Concrete sequence: a task's data/<id>/ contains a captured fixture at mode 444 (extracted from an archive, or chmod'ed to protect it). First preserve copies it and the destination file is also 444. Teardown is re-run (the header notes teardown runs this repeatedly across a fleet); cp cannot open the existing 444 destination for writing and fails with Permission denied, set -e aborts copy_artifacts, and line 328 reports CUSTODY_FAILED. bin/fm-teardown.sh:1228 then REFUSES cleanup, and the operator's only escape is --force. Use `cp -pf` (or unlink the destination first) so an unchanged re-copy cannot fail.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-evidence.sh:335` - Nothing serializes the git index operations, yet the header explicitly designs for concurrent multi-home use of one destination ("concurrent tasks in different homes - two secondmates ... never collide"). The layout prevents path collision but not index contention. Concrete path: a captain points two secondmate homes at the same evidence clone; two teardowns overlap while one is staging a large tree, and the second's `git add` (line 330) or `git commit` (line 335) fails with "Unable to create '.git/index.lock': File exists". That is CUSTODY_FAILED, so bin/fm-teardown.sh:1228 refuses cleanup even though the evidence is perfectly preservable. It fails safe (no data loss), but it produces a spurious hard refusal that only a manual re-run clears. Guard the add/commit pair with a mutex or retry on index.lock contention.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-evidence.sh:43` - The header - which usage() prints verbatim as `--help` output - says "an artifact at or below FM_EVIDENCE_MAX_DIRECT_BYTES is committed whole", but no such variable is read anywhere. The constant is FM_EVIDENCE_MAX_DIRECT_BYTES_DEFAULT (line 92) and the only operator control is config/evidence-max-direct-bytes. An operator following the help text would export FM_EVIDENCE_MAX_DIRECT_BYTES, see no effect, and get no diagnostic. Name the config key in the SIZE POLICY paragraph instead, as docs/configuration.md already does correctly.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-evidence.sh:236` - remote_visibility() pipes the already-captured $view through the identical `awk -F: '/visibility:/ ...'` program twice - once at line 236 only to test emptiness via grep -q, then again at line 239 to emit it. Parse once into a local, then test and print that value; it removes the risk of the two copies drifting apart.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-evidence.sh:283` - `find "$source" -type f` matches neither symlinks nor their targets, so a symlinked artifact in data/<id>/ (a common way to reference a large corpus without duplicating it) is absent from the copy AND from EVIDENCE-MANIFEST.txt. That contradicts the header's stated guarantee that "Every artifact is listed in the manifest either way": the omission is completely silent, so nothing signals that the evidence record is incomplete. Either follow symlinks (`find -L`) or record `-type l` entries in the manifest with an explicit disposition.

🔧 Fix: bind evidence push to a verified github destination
2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-evidence.sh:216` - The newly bound visibility precondition still validates only one of the destinations a push can reach. `git remote get-url --push "$remote"` documents "By default, only the first URL is listed", while git-config documents remote.<name>.pushurl as "A configured remote can have multiple push URLs; in this case a push goes to all of them" - I confirmed both in the local man pages. So remote_push_url returns URL #1, remote_host/evidence_host_is_github/remote_owner_name all describe URL #1, and the actual `git push --quiet "$(evidence_remote "$repo")" HEAD` publishes to every configured pushurl. Concrete path: the captain mirrors the evidence clone with `git remote set-url --add --push origin ssh://git@github.com/owner/evidence.git` and `git remote set-url --add --push origin ssh://git@gitlab.company.example/acme/evidence.git`. The check reads the github.com URL, gh-axi confirms private, and unredacted evidence is published to gitlab.company.example whose visibility was never established - the exact failure the round-1 fix set out to close, through a different door. Fix: read `git remote get-url --push --all "$remote"` and require EVERY returned URL to pass both evidence_host_is_github and the gh-axi private lookup; any URL that fails skips the push, keeping the commit-is-custody contract intact. Worth a test alongside test_non_github_remote_skips_the_push that adds a second, non-GitHub pushurl and asserts the push is skipped.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-evidence.sh:318` - unstaged_artifacts() builds one newline-joined `staged` string and then runs a `case "$nl$staged$nl" in *"$nl$rel$nl"*` substring scan once per artifact, which is O(artifacts x index-listing-length) inside the teardown path. The size policy deliberately keeps small files on the committed side, so a frame dump or fixture set of several thousand small artifacts is exactly the case that lands here, and that is millions of shell pattern comparisons on every preserve. Both halves are already sorted (`find ... | LC_ALL=C sort` and git's index order), so `comm -23` over the two sorted lists is linear and removes the hand-rolled membership test entirely. Note also that the `|| return 1` on line 321 guards the pipeline's exit status, which is `tr`'s and not git's - a git failure yields an empty `staged`, which reports every artifact as unstaged; that still fails toward custody failure, but the diagnostic then names every file instead of the real cause.

🔧 Fix: verify every push destination is private
1 info still open:
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-evidence.sh:340` - Both inputs to `comm -23` are produced with `LC_ALL=C sort` (lines 341-342) but `comm` itself runs under the ambient locale, so its own comparison can disagree with the order its inputs were built in. Under a full locale such as en_US.UTF-8 - common on a macOS captain's shell, though this container runs C.UTF-8 where the two happen to agree - glibc ignores `-`, `_`, `.` and space at the primary collation level and folds case, so a dest containing `EVIDENCE-MANIFEST.txt` and `evidence.log` is correctly C-sorted (`E` = 0x45 before `e` = 0x65) yet reads as descending to comm (`evidencelog` before `evidencemanifesttxt`). GNU comm's default order check is fatal once disorder is detected AND an unpairable line has been seen, so it exits 1 with "file 1 is not in sorted order"; unstaged_artifacts then returns non-zero and cmd_preserve reports `cannot verify the staged evidence for <id>`, refusing teardown for a task whose evidence was in fact fully committed. The unpairable line can come from a stale index entry - for example a path left in the index after a prior run's `rm -f` succeeded but its `cp` failed. The direction is safe: comm only consumes a file-1 line without emitting it on exact string equality, so no genuinely unstaged artifact can be silently skipped, and the all-staged happy path compares two identical lists and is unaffected. Fix is one word: `LC_ALL=C comm -23 ...` so the comparison matches the sort. Separately, the helper's comment claims a skip-worktree entry is caught, but such a path is present in `ls-files --cached`, so comm finds nothing while `git add --force` declines to update its content - the check detects "absent from the index", not "stale in the index", and the comment overstates it.

title: fix(watch): keep pause throttle across parked-pane redraws
body:
## Intent The developer wanted a narrowly scoped fix to a confirmed pause-throttle bug in the watcher's monitoring logic: when a worker is deliberately parked with a very large configured pause interval, any change in its pane's screen content caused `clear_pause_tracking` to delete the throttle on each new pane hash, so redraws bypassed the interval and produced extra monitoring notices. They required reproducing the current behavior end-to-end first (static parked pane stays quiet after its initial notice; content-churning parked pane wrongly emits extras) and keeping trigger, masking condition, and user-visible symptom distinct, following the project's coding-guidelines and diagnostic-reasoning skills. The fix had to preserve pause tracking across content changes while the same task remains honestly parked, while keeping the finite recheck cadence and all existing escalations for genuinely active, stuck, dead, resumed, or no-longer-paused work intact, plus regression coverage on the existing monitoring test surface for static and changing pane content and for the state transitions that must clear pause tracking. Explicitly out of scope: indefinite suspension, a new marker, backlog coupling, or any other mechanism to stop checks forever, since whether parked work may be excluded entirely was left as a separate captain decision. Acceptance required a failing pre-fix regression, equal interval behavior post-fix for static and churning panes, correct throttle clearing on leaving the parked state, passing existing monitoring/classification tests, and shipping the commit through the project's no-mistakes pipeline to a green PR. After the upstream PR was closed because plandrover/firstmate became the canonical repo, they asked to sync and re-run validation so the already-validated changes land in a green PR targeting origin rather than upstream. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-watch.sh`: a redrawn pane that still declares its wait no longer drops pause tracking on each new content hash. The redraw path now routes a `paused:`/`captain-held` crew through `handle_paused_stale`, falling back on the existing `.paused-` marker when the liveness class is inconclusive, so the re-surface cadence is measured from the status log and throttle marker rather than the pane hash. Real transitions (provably working again, no longer declaring the wait, proven busy, away mode) still clear it, and `surface_nonterminal_stale` now resets pause state unconditionally so each new episode restarts its cadence. - New `triage_log_pause_absorb` rate-limits the `absorbed stale (paused, ...)` line in `state/.watch-triage.log` to one per `FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS` window, so a long or churning wait cannot roll the rest of the absorbed-wake history out of that size-capped log; `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh` clears the new `.paused-logged-*` marker alongside the rest of the pause tracking. - Coverage and docs: `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` gains `test_live_paused_content_churn_keeps_throttle_until_resume` (static vs churning parked pane, plus throttle teardown on resume), `tests/fm-daemon.test.sh` asserts the marker teardown on a terminal wake, several pre-existing fixed-budget waits in the triage suite now wait on marker state instead, and `docs/architecture.md` records both the throttle survival and the log rate limit. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The follow-up is a small diagnostic rate-limiter plus a test-robustness pass on top of the already-reviewed eight-line pause-throttle fix; the new marker is cleaned up at every existing pause-clearing site in both the watcher and the daemon, `surface_nonterminal_stale`'s refactor removes a duplicated rm list rather than changing behavior, and no wake, escalation, or recheck path is altered. ## Testing I reproduced the bug end-to-end before trusting any test: a standalone driver runs the real bin/fm-watch.sh against a worker parked with a 900s pause interval and re-arms it as the captain loop does, so the evidence is the notices the captain actually receives in state/.wake-queue. Base f7d0d0a emits 6 notices in one interval (one extra per pane redraw, and its expiry recheck comes out mislabeled as a plain stale), while branch HEAD emits the correct 2 - the initial stale surface plus one bounded awaiting-external recheck once the interval expires; a static parked pane is correct on both versions, which pins the masking condition. A second driver shows the absorbed-pause debug line dropping from 18 identical triage-log entries per 20 polls to 1. The new regression test fails against the base watcher with exactly the user-visible symptom and passes on HEAD, and the full tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh suite ran green three consecutive times (41/41) at load average ~48-50, which also holds up this branch's earlier flakiness fixes. I found and closed one gap: the .paused-logged-* marker added to both the daemon's and the watcher's pause-tracking teardown had no assertion, so I added coverage in each place and confirmed both new assertions fail against the base source. No visual artifacts apply - this is a bash watcher/daemon change whose only end-user surface is the wake reasons and the triage log, both captured as CLI transcripts.
Evidence: Notice-count matrix and headline results Parked worker with a redrawing pane - what the captain is woken for Same fixture, same 900s configured pause interval, only bin/fm-watch.sh differs. pane content | base f7d0d0a (pre-fix) | branch HEAD d4100a7 (fixed) ---------------+--------------------------+----------------------------- static | 2 notices (correct) | 2 notices (correct) redrawing | 6 notices (4 spurious) | 2 notices (correct) The 2 correct notices are the initial stale surface plus one bounded recheck once the 900s interval expired, so the fix is a throttle, not a suspension. Absorbed-pause debug lines in state/.watch-triage.log, 20 polls of one parked worker: before the rate limit (e170248): 18 identical lines branch HEAD (d4100a7): 1 line tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh: 41/41 ok on three consecutive full runs at load average ~48-50. ```text Parked worker with a redrawing pane - what the captain is woken for Same fixture, same 900s configured pause interval, only bin/fm-watch.sh differs. pane content | base f7d0d0a (pre-fix) | branch HEAD d4100a7 (fixed) ---------------+--------------------------+----------------------------- static | 2 notices (correct) | 2 notices (correct) redrawing | 6 notices (4 spurious) | 2 notices (correct) The 2 correct notices are the initial stale surface plus one bounded recheck once the 900s interval expired, so the fix is a throttle, not a suspension. ## Intent Captain decided firstmate-repo changes should land locally instead of via automatic PRs against the upstream template repo. This is the AGENTS.md + CONTRIBUTING.md edit establishing that policy, validated with the exact local-only flow it describes. ## What Changed - Added an optional `--group=` flag to `bin/fm-brief.sh` for browsable `data/` grouping, with refusal checks for self-referential group ids and group/task directory collisions (both directions), plus test coverage in `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` and updated `--group` header documentation. - Updated `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` to establish that firstmate-repo changes ship locally instead of via automatic PRs against the upstream template repo, and fixed inverted merge-actor wording in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. - Added the `infisical-secrets` skill reference (`.agents/skills/infisical-secrets/SKILL.md`) and registered it in `docs/documentation-audiences.json`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The reviewed diff is a docs-only policy change (AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md) establishing local-only, no-PR shipping for firstmate's own repo, plus already-tested prerequisite commits (fm-brief.sh --group feature, infisical-secrets skill doc) stacked earlier on the branch; the policy wording is internally consistent with existing hard-rule-2/local-only-mode semantics, matches the stated intent exactly, and no leftover automation still auto-pushes/PRs firstmate's own repo changes. ## Testing This is a prose-only change (no executable code), so I checked it for internal consistency and factual accuracy rather than unit tests: AGENTS.md §1 and CONTRIBUTING.md's Development section now state the identical local-only flow (validate via `no-mistakes axi run --skip=push,pr,ci`, never push/PR, then captain-approved fast-forward into local main), the referenced `--skip` flag is real on the installed no-mistakes CLI, and the hard-rule-2 cross-reference fixed in 43e3327 matches the actual rule text. The one targeted automated check relevant to a documentation change, `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` and its test `tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh`, both pass. As a bonus, this very gate run — reviewing/testing this branch without pushing or opening a PR — is itself a live instance of the flow the docs describe; I did not (and per the test-phase boundary, could not) invoke `no-mistakes axi run` myself to re-demonstrate it directly. No issues found.

Never push that branch or open a PR against this repo. Report the validated branch to the captain; once approved, fast-forward-merge it into local `main`, the same captain-approval authority hard rule 2 already requires for any merge. CONTRIBUTING.md: ...validate locally on a feature branch through `no-mistakes axi run --skip=push,pr,ci` (review, test, and lint only); never push that branch or open a PR against this repo. Report the validated branch to the captain; once approved, fast-forward-merge it into local `main` - the same explicit merge approval any other merge requires. ```

title: feat(bin): enforce a configurable memory bound on crewmate spawns
body:
## Intent Give crewmate builds an enforced memory bound so the constraint rate-limiting the captain's benchmark programme stops being a convention. BACKGROUND / THE FINDING THIS FIXES. Firstmate had twice told the captain the host was protected by construction when raising build concurrency, citing the systemd cgroup on the no-mistakes daemon (MemoryHigh 6G, MemoryMax 8G). Measurement disproved that: the daemon cgroup holds only the daemon's own processes (daemon, log-sink, one claude agent, an npm chrome-devtools MCP, node, a git/gh chain - about 0.75 GiB), while crewmate tmux panes report cgroup 0::/, the ROOT cgroup, and were literally listed in /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.procs. Every cargo and rustc a crewmate ran was outside any envelope. The original WSL crash was a GLOBAL OOM kill of rustc, and that process class was still unbounded. The 6.00 GiB peak and 58446 throttle events on the daemon were its own model-call work, not compilation. This was verified before any code was written; the task rested on that claim. WHAT THE CAPTAIN ASKED FOR. An enforced bound covering the ENTIRE crew pane process tree, not a wrapper around a named build command, because crews compose their own cargo invocations and any per-command wrapper is bypassed the moment a crew types a different one. It must fail closed: a crew whose bound cannot be established must refuse to spawn rather than run unbounded, since a silent fallback to no limit would recreate today's situation while looking fixed. Exceeding the bound must kill that build, not the host, and the failure must be legible. The limit must be configurable because the right number changes with a hardware upgrade. Approaches were to be evaluated on merit rather than assumed. Live crews must not be disturbed - seven were running mid-pipeline - so new bounds apply to newly spawned crews only. DESIGN DECISIONS A REVIEWER WOULD NOT INFER FROM THE DIFF. 1. The bound wraps the HARNESS LAUNCH, not any build command. A crewmate pane is a plain shell that fm-spawn TYPES the harness launch line into; the crew then composes its own commands inside that harness. Binding the launch puts the harness and every process it ever forks in one transient systemd scope, which is why a compiler the crew invents later is still bounded. 2. The pane's own login shell is deliberately LEFT OUTSIDE the scope. Replacing it (typing 'exec systemd-run ...') was considered and rejected: the window would then die with the harness, destroying the distinction recovery depends on between a dead pane and a live pane whose agent exited (fm_backend_tmux_agent_state's dead vs no-agent). This residual boundary is documented rather than glossed over - a command typed straight into the pane shell after the harness exits is not bounded. 3. systemd-run --user --scope was chosen over a dedicated slice or a tmux-server-level cgroup because --scope inherits the caller's environment, cwd, and TTY (verified: interactive shell keeps its controlling terminal and job control under the bound), whereas a --user service would get a clean environment and break the harness. 4. MemorySwapMax=0 is set unconditionally and is NOT a tunable. MemoryMax alone bounds only resident memory, so a runaway build left with swap would page the host into thrashing instead of dying - precisely the failure being prevented. 5. memory.oom.group is deliberately left at its DEFAULT so the kernel kills the single largest member (the runaway compiler) rather than the whole scope, leaving the harness alive to report the failed build. That is the legibility requirement. 6. The setting is OPT-IN via config/crew-memory-bound and absent by default, so hosts with no systemd user manager (macOS, containers, CI) are unaffected until they opt in. Fail-closed applies once configured. Enforcement is PROVEN at every spawn rather than assumed: a throwaway scope is created and its memory.max is read back from the live cgroup before any window, worktree, or metadata exists. 7. Added to FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG so secondmate homes inherit the bound and their own crewmates are bound too - that list is the declared extension point and the lib documents that adding an item needs no other change. 8. crew_memory_max= is recorded in task metadata only when a bound is active, keeping an unbounded home's metadata byte-identical, so supervision can read a mid-compile SIGKILL as the bound working rather than an unexplained crash. TESTING DECISION. Per the captain's standing rule the defect gets the regression that would have caught it. The defect was a cgroup that EXISTED and enforced a limit on the WRONG processes, so the test asserts on the cgroup real descendants report for THEMSELVES, to grandchild depth, and fails if any lands in the root cgroup. This was proven to regress: neutering the wrapping makes it fail with three 0::/ reports. Three distinct fail-closed paths are covered (no systemd-run on PATH, a systemd-run that cannot create the scope, and one that reports success while leaving processes in the root cgroup), plus the fm-spawn-level refusal. The cgroup membership and kill checks stand down with a note on hosts with no systemd user manager so CI stays green. MEASURED EVIDENCE is recorded in docs/verification/crew-memory-bound.md, including kernel-read limits, the CONSTRAINT_MEMCG kill attribution naming the crew scope, host memory surviving the kill, preserved interactivity, and scope garbage collection. SCOPE NOTE: this is firstmate's own shared tracked material, so firstmate-coding-guidelines was applied - one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, shellcheck-clean via bin/fm-lint.sh under the pinned 0.11.0, colocated test named tests/fm-crew-memory-bound.test.sh, the new verification doc registered in docs/documentation-audiences.json, and no agent co-author. Validation on this host is shell and bash tests only, deliberately not competing for a build lane. ## What Changed - Adds `bin/fm-crew-memory-bound.sh`, which reads the opt-in `config/crew-memory-bound` (` []`), proves the host can enforce it at every spawn by creating a throwaway scope and reading `memory.max`, `memory.high`, and `memory.swap.max` back from the live cgroup, and wraps the harness launch in a transient `systemd-run --user --scope` with `MemorySwapMax=0` so the harness and every process it later forks sit inside one bound. - Wires the bound into `bin/fm-spawn.sh`: preflight and launch-shape check run before any window, worktree, or metadata exists, a configured-but-unenforceable bound (or a raw launch that is not one simple command) refuses the spawn instead of launching unbounded, the wrapping applies to crewmates only and never the secondmate agent, and `crew_memory_max=`/`crew_memory_high=` are written to `state/.meta` only when a bound is active. - Adds `crew-memory-bound` to `FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG` so secondmate homes inherit the ceiling for their own crewmates, plus `tests/fm-crew-memory-bound.test.sh` covering descendant cgroup membership to grandchild depth, kernel-read limits, the in-scope kill, and the fail-closed paths, with measured evidence recorded in the newly registered `docs/verification/crew-memory-bound.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The round-2 finding is closed correctly and completely - the keyword gate covers all 22 bash reserved words, its bare-word condition matches bash's actual recognition rules (verified empirically for the quoted and assignment-prefix cases), no built-in launch template is falsely refused at either check point, and the feature remains opt-in and byte-identical when config/crew-memory-bound is absent. ## Testing Ran the colocated regression suite (all 23 checks, with the live cgroup membership, kernel-limit and kill checks actually exercised on this systemd host) plus the documentation-audience test for the new verification doc, then proved the intent end-to-end by driving the real fm-spawn into real tmux crew panes: the crewmate's own post-launch cargo/rustc chain lands inside the crew scope to grandchild depth, the kernel reports the configured MemoryMax with swap denied, a runaway build dies with SIGKILL attributed to CONSTRAINT_MEMCG on that scope while the harness and the host survive, and both fail-closed paths refuse before any window or metadata exists. Also confirmed metadata is recorded only when bound, the setting is inherited into secondmate homes, a pre-existing crew is undisturbed, and that neutering the wrapping makes the regression test fail. If config/crew-memory-bound is edited in that window, the scope is created with the new value while meta records the old one, defeating the stated purpose of the meta field (letting supervision read a mid-compile SIGKILL as this bound doing its job). If the edit makes the bound invalid, wrap returns 1, fm-spawn exits 1, and the already-created window, worktree, and meta are left orphaned (spawn_abort_cleanup only releases locks and handles the orca/herdr paths). Pass the proven bound through instead, e.g. invoke wrap with FM_CREW_MEMORY_BOUND="$CREW_MEMORY_MAX${CREW_MEMORY_HIGH:+ $CREW_MEMORY_HIGH}", so the scope, the proof, and the meta record are the same value by construction. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1718` - The preflight at fm-spawn.sh:268 and the wrap at :1718 are both unconditional on $KIND, so `fm-spawn.sh <id> --secondmate` puts the secondmate agent itself inside a MemoryMax scope with MemorySwapMax=0, and :1670 records crew_memory_max= in its meta. Every document added by this change describes a narrower scope: AGENTS.md says 'a newly spawned crewmate's whole pane process tree', docs/configuration.md says 'every newly spawned crewmate', and the stated design says the config is inherited 'so secondmate homes inherit the bound and their own crewmates are bound too' - never that the secondmate agent is bound. The consequence differs in kind: a secondmate is a long-lived peer home, so if its harness becomes the largest member of the scope, the kernel SIGKILLs it (memory.oom.group is left at default) and the whole home's supervision loop goes down at a ceiling sized for build lanes. Confirm whether bounding secondmate agents is intended; if it is, the docs need to say so, and if it is not, gate the wrap on [ "$KIND" != secondmate ]. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-crew-memory-bound.sh:260` - wrap always emits `-- /bin/bash -c <launch>`. tmux resolves pane_current_command from /proc/<tcgetpgrp(fd)>/cmdline, and bash only replaces itself with the command when `bash -c` gets a single simple command with no redirections; otherwise it forks, job control is off, so the child shares bash's process group and tmux reports 'bash'. fm_backend_tmux_agent_state (bin/backends/tmux.sh:197) maps 'bash' to `dead`. All six built-in launch_template entries are simple commands, so they are safe, but the documented raw-launch escape hatch (fm-spawn.sh:521, 'pass a raw launch command to use an unverified adapter') accepts any shell text: a raw launch containing a redirection, a pipeline, or `&&` yields a live agent that supervision reads as dead, and stuck-crewmate-recovery then relaunches a crewmate that is still working in that worktree. Unbounded, the same raw launch works, because the interactive pane shell puts the harness in its own foreground process group. Either constrain/validate the raw-launch shape under an active bound or state the restriction where the escape hatch is documented. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-crew-memory-bound.sh:212` - prove_enforcement runs the probe as `/bin/sh -c`, while cmd_wrap emits `/bin/bash -c`. The preflight therefore does not exercise the interpreter the real launch depends on, so on a host that has a systemd user manager but no /bin/bash (NixOS, a bash-less distro image), preflight prints 'enforced=proven', fm-spawn prints 'spawned <id> ...' and writes full metadata, and the typed line then fails in the pane with no harness ever starting. It stays fail-closed rather than unbounded, but 'proven' means less than the launch requires. Using the same interpreter in the probe as in the wrapped launch closes the gap for free. 🔧 Fix: prove every crew memory limit, bound crewmates only 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-crew-memory-bound.sh:252` - require_execable_launch decides bindability purely from operator characters ('|', '&', ';', '<', '>', '(', ')', newline) and unbalanced quoting, but bash's exec-in-place optimization also requires command->type == cm_simple with neither CMD_TIME_PIPELINE nor CMD_INVERT_RETURN set. A raw launch prefixed with a reserved word contains none of the rejected characters and passes the scan: `bin/fm-spawn.sh <id> <repo> "time claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --model opus"` returns 0 from check-launch, fm-spawn binds it, and wrap emits `... -- /bin/bash -c 'time claude ...'`. bash sets CMD_TIME_PIPELINE, skips the no-fork path, forks, and stays the pane's foreground process-group leader, so tmux reports `bash` and fm_backend_tmux_agent_state (bin/backends/tmux.sh:197) maps it to `dead` while the crewmate is working - the exact state this guard was added to make unreachable, reached through the same escape hatch it was added to constrain. `! claude ...` (CMD_INVERT_RETURN) and `coproc claude ...` (cm_coproc) behave the same way. Close it in the same scan: after the walk, refuse when the first unquoted, unescaped word is one of bash's pipeline modifiers or reserved words (`time`, `!`, `coproc`, and the compound-command keywords for completeness), which keeps the guard fail-closed without touching any built-in template. 🔧 Fix: refuse keyword-prefixed launches under an active crew bound ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-crew-memory-bound.test.sh` - 23 checks, all live cgroup membership/limit/kill checks exercised (systemd user manager present, nothing stood down) - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` - the new `docs/verification/crew-memory-bound.md` registration - Mutation check: dropped the scope flags from `cmd_wrap`, re-ran the suite (fails on the descendant-cgroup assertion), restored the file and confirmed `git status --porcelain` clean - End-to-end crew pane: real `bin/fm-spawn.sh <id> <project> --harness claude` into a real tmux window on a private socket with `config/crew-memory-bound=128M`, then typed the crew's own `./build.sh` (cargo→driver→rustc) and `./limits.sh` into the running harness - Runaway build inside the bound: `./hog.sh; echo "cargo build exited $?"` in the crew pane -> `Killed` / `137`, harness alive at the same pid, `free -m` unchanged, out-of-scope `sleep` sentinel still running - `dmesg | grep fm-crew-crew-kill2-1785527724` - `constraint=CONSTRAINT_MEMCG`, `oom_memcg=` naming the crew scope, task table showing the 130 MiB member killed and the ~3.8 MiB harness spared - Fail-closed spawn: `bin/fm-spawn.sh crew-refused <project>` with a `systemd-run` that cannot create a scope -> refusal, no `state/crew-refused.meta`, no tmux window created - Fail-closed launch shape: `bin/fm-spawn.sh crew-shape <project> 'time claude -p hi'` and `bin/fm-crew-memory-bound.sh check-launch 'claude -p hi | tee /tmp/log'` -> both refused - `bin/fm-crew-memory-bound.sh read` / `preflight` on this host -> `enforced=proven`; `state/<id>.meta` compared bounded vs unbounded - `propagate_inheritable_config <primary>/config <secondmate>/config` -> `crew-memory-bound` lands in the secondmate home - Scope lifetime: `systemctl --user is-active fm-crew-...scope` active while the harness runs, `inactive` after the pane is closed
🔧 **Document** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh:16` - tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh's header comment (lines 16-19) enumerates the inherited config set and is now stale: it omits config/crew-memory-bound, which this change added to FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG. This phase may only edit documentation and doc comments, not tests, so I left it. Fix by adding config/crew-memory-bound to that list, or better, by replacing the inline list with a pointer to FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG in bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh. - ℹ️ `docs/configuration.md:334` - Follow-up consolidation, out of scope here: the inheritable config set is still restated in full prose in docs/configuration.md:334 (the fm-config-push output list) alongside the owner list in secondmate-provisioning, while FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG in bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh is the actual source of truth and its header states that adding an item needs no other change. Every added item must currently be hand-synchronized into each copy, which is exactly the drift this change exposed. A separate pass should reduce the remaining copies to pointers. 🔧 Fix: replace inherited-config enumeration with pointer in test header ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
⏭️ **Lint** - skipped - ⚠️ linter found issues (exit code 1)
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

The skill must reconcile structured decisions and task state to exclude resolved or duplicate items, then produce a self-contained explanation of every unresolved decision with full business context, history, underlying problems, realistic options with tradeoffs, impact analysis across multiple dimensions, risk ratings with mitigations, and specific actionable approval language. It should distinguish different decision types such as product choices, engineering risks, credentials, and destructive actions, avoiding jargon while preserving PR URLs and identifying when actions require interactive handling. The skill must not mutate fleet or project state as a side effect and should follow existing skill naming and front-matter conventions with one-sentence-per-line Markdown style. The implementation should be committed and validated through no-mistakes to a green PR targeting the captain's fork while preserving all pipeline fix commits, but not merged. ## What Changed - Added `.agents/skills/decision-brief/SKILL.md` defining a new user-invocable skill that generates reconciled executive briefs of all current Captain's Calls and pending decisions - Registered the skill in `docs/documentation-audiences.json` with `agent-runtime` audience - Added `/decision-brief` slash command entry to README.md skill table with description - Added escalation trigger in AGENTS.md section 9 to load `decision-brief` when captain requests breakdown or decision analysis ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Documentation-only change that adds a new skill following established patterns with no executable code or behavioral changes to existing functionality. ## Testing Validated the decision-brief skill through structural checks (YAML frontmatter parsing, documentation audience validation passing with 68 surfaces), content verification (7 sections, 5 decision categories, 11 required fields, 4 risk levels), integration testing (README, AGENTS.md, and documentation-audiences.json all updated correctly), and style compliance (one-sentence-per-line markdown, read-only guarantees). title: fix(bin): detect and repair crewmate panes that survive a restart unable to work
body:
## Intent Firstmate crewmate panes that survive a host crash or reboot come back looking perfectly healthy while being silently unable to work, and the existing endpoint-liveness check reports them ALIVE. This happened twice on 2026-07-31 and stopped the fleet both times. The captain asked to make firstmate detect and repair it, and required diagnosing the real mechanism first rather than building on their reconstruction. Verified mechanism (against herdr 0.7.5 and Claude Code 2.1.220): herdr persists only each pane's CREATION cwd, and its default [session] resume_agents_on_restore relaunches the agent from the integration-reported session ref (claude --resume ). That command is herdr's own, so it carries none of the launch shape fm-spawn resolved. The pane therefore returns without its autonomy flag - stalling forever on its first tool call waiting for an approval nobody is watching for - and in the project checkout, because the task worktree was only ever entered by a treehouse get subshell whose cwd the persisted creation cwd never followed. Detection: new bin/fm-crew-fitness.sh reports whether a recorded task's pane still carries the autonomy flags its own recorded launch command specified and is still in its recorded worktree. The session-start digest runs it for every live endpoint, because the crash that causes this takes the watcher down too, so session start is where it actually surfaces. Deliberate decisions: the flag set is intersected with the task's own recorded launch rather than mapped per harness, so a template change can never leave the check asserting a stale flag; exact argv-element matching is required rather than a substring scan, because a brief travels in argv and can quote the very flag being looked for; and both scripts fail closed toward 'unknown' rather than 'fit', since a false 'fit' is the exact silent failure being fixed. The endpoint is proven present through the recovery-grade state contract first, because tmux silently resolves an absent target to the caller's own window, which would otherwise condemn a vanished task by measuring firstmate's own pane. Repair: fm-spawn.sh now records the fully resolved launch command as launch= in the task's metadata so recovery is deterministic and does not re-derive flags under pressure, and new bin/fm-crew-relaunch.sh replays it in the recorded worktree. It refuses to relaunch over a live agent, refuses when the recorded worktree is unaccounted for, never allocates a second worktree, and never touches worktree contents - the three safety properties the captain required be preserved. The change also corrects a previously recorded learning about why a keystroke cannot repair this: bypassPermissions is a launch-time grant, so a process started without it does not offer that mode at all, independent of any key-transmission question about shift+tab. Scope was deliberately held to a recovery correctness fix rather than a new supervision subsystem, per the captain's instruction. Firstmate additionally asked me to consider folding in a spawn-time task-vs-task worktree ownership assertion if it were small. I implemented it, then testing against real treehouse and herdr disproved its premise, so I deliberately did NOT ship it and am reporting it back instead - it needs a liveness contract that is larger than this branch should carry. Covered by tests/fm-crew-fitness.test.sh (44 assertions) proving detection of both the manual-mode case and the wrong-cwd case, and proving the repair restores an autonomous agent in the correct worktree without duplicating a task or losing uncommitted work. This is firstmate shared tracked material, so it follows firstmate-coding-guidelines: one sentence per line in docs, shellcheck-clean scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh, colocated tests, no agent co-author. ## What Changed - Adds `bin/fm-crew-fitness.sh`, which reports whether a live task pane still carries the autonomy grants its own recorded `launch=` specified and is still in its recorded worktree, on a three-state `fit|unfit|unknown` verdict that fails closed toward `unknown`; `bin/fm-session-start.sh` now emits one fitness line per endpoint that read as alive, since the crash that causes this failure takes the watcher down too. - Adds `bin/fm-crew-relaunch.sh`, which replays a task's recorded launch command in its recorded worktree — refusing over a live or vanished endpoint, never allocating a second worktree, never touching worktree contents, and appending a recovery note to the brief first. To make that deterministic, `bin/fm-spawn.sh` records the fully resolved launch command as `launch=` in `state/.meta` and rejects newline-bearing launch strings that would corrupt the metadata. - Extends the backend layer with `fm_backend_pane_argv_has`, `fm_backend_pane_env_has`, `fm_backend_current_path_passive`, and dispatchers for `send_text_line`/`current_path`, implemented passively for tmux (`/proc` argv and environ) and herdr (`pane process-info`) and returning undeterminable elsewhere; covered by `tests/fm-crew-fitness.test.sh`, `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh`, and a new `tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh` case pinning the recorded `launch=` line, with the backend limits recorded in `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Every finding from both prior rounds is fixed with behavior-level test coverage and honest verification evidence, the new env reader preserves the never-toward-fit invariant by construction, and the two trickiest new mechanisms (the array-expansion guard and the shell quote round-trip) verify correct under direct exercise. ## Testing I ran the change's own suite (tests/fm-crew-fitness.test.sh, 66 assertions) plus the adjacent herdr/backend/spawn suites, then demonstrated the intent the way the captain would actually meet it: a real tmux pane running a stand-in harness in a real task worktree with uncommitted work, restored herdr-style as `claude --resume <id>` in the project checkout. The session-start digest reports that pane `endpoint: alive` and immediately below it `fitness: unfit (autonomy=lost cwd=wrong)` naming the lost `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and the wrong directory; relaunch refuses while the agent is live, dry-run changes nothing, and after exiting the agent the repair brings back an autonomous agent in the recorded worktree (`fitness: fit`) with the uncommitted file intact, the same worktree count, GOTMPDIR recreated, and a recovery note appended to the brief. I also found and closed a coverage gap — nothing asserted that fm-spawn.sh writes `launch=` into task metadata, the record both recovery scripts depend on — by adding a focused test that pins the recorded line to the literal command typed into the pane; it fails at the base commit and passes here. This is a terminal CLI surface with no GUI, so the reviewer-visible evidence is the captured tmux pane render and the session-start digest transcript rather than a screenshot. One adjacent suite, tests/fm-session-start.test.sh, fails on this host for a pre-existing fixture reason (real /usr/bin/node in the fixture PATH) and fails identically at the base commit.
