title: feat(bin): add per-turn quota instrumentation with state fingerprint proxy
body:
## Intent Give firstmate the ability to measure its own token cost per turn with state fingerprint proxy and quota accounting ## What Changed - New `bin/fm-turn-quota.sh` dispatcher over a writer/reader pair: the writer appends one tab-separated record per primary turn end to `state/quota-turns.log` (wake kind, state fingerprint, and Claude/Gemini quota remaining), and the reader prints a summary with per-wake-kind breakdown and quota deltas. Both treat the fingerprint strictly as a proxy — missing hashers or absent probes record an explicit absent marker rather than a fabricated zero, and absent rows are excluded from the no-op ratios with the exclusion count disclosed. - `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh` now invokes the writer at primary turn end as a fail-safe observer (all errors swallowed to `state/.turn-quota-error.log`, exit 0), gated on the consecutive-block ledger rather than `stop_hook_active` so a guard-forced continuation does not append a second record while genuinely new post-rewake turns still get measured. `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh` stamps `state/.turn-wake-kind` on every drain so each record is attributed to the wake that caused it. - Quota probes are portable and cheap: `sha256sum`/`shasum` and `timeout`/`gtimeout` fallbacks reuse the repo's existing helpers, both `quota-axi` and `antigravity-usage` results are mtime-cached, and the Gemini reading picks the scarcest dispatch-eligible pool instead of whichever model the tool lists first. Docs cover the new scripts, state artifacts, and the optional `antigravity-usage` probe; `tests/fm-turn-quota.test.sh` and new turn-end guard cases cover reader math, absent-marker honesty, unknown-subcommand failure, and per-turn recording. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The round-3 change is a narrow, correct replacement of an unreliable signal with the guard's own block ledger — every allow path clears the ledger so the skip can never outlive a single block chain, the post-rewake recording regression from round 2 is gone, and the behavior is directly covered by a new four-step test; only a cosmetic duplicate-jq simplification remains. ## Testing Ran the two directly affected test scripts plus the wake-queue suite (all pass), added one focused test for the Gemini accounting branch that had no automated coverage, and then demonstrated the feature the way the captain experiences it: a 6-turn simulated primary session driven through the real chain (wake drain stamping the wake kind, the real Claude Stop payload into fm-turnend-guard.sh --claude, the writer appending one row per turn), ending with the actual `bin/fm-turn-quota.sh report` output showing 6 turns, 50% proxy no-op, 1.42% Claude 5-hour per turn (2.83% per changed turn), Gemini deltas, and a per-wake-kind breakdown. The repo coverage guard fails under the machine's en_US.UTF-8 locale due to a comm/sort collation mismatch that reproduces identically at the base commit and passes under LC_ALL=C, so it is not attributable to this change; scratch demo state was removed and the worktree carries only the intentional test addition.

Total turns: 6 Proxy no-op (fingerprint unchanged): 3 (50.0%) Proxy changed (fingerprint changed): 3 (50.0%) --- Quota Consumed per Turn --- Claude 5-hour: total delta 8.50% | 1.42% / turn | 2.83% / changed turn Claude 7-day: total delta 2.00% | 0.33% / turn | 0.67% / changed turn Gemini / agy: total delta 12.50% | 2.08% / turn | 4.17% / changed turn --- Breakdown by Wake Kind --- WAKE KIND TURNS FP KNOWN NO-OP (OF FP KNOWN) CLAUDE 5H DELTA stale 1 1 1 (100.0%) 1.70% heartbeat 1 1 1 (100.0%) 1.70% signal 2 2 0 (0.0%) 3.40% captain 2 2 1 (50.0%) 1.70% ```
Evidence: Reproducible end-to-end demo script (drives the real wake-drain -> turn-end guard -> writer -> reader chain) ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # End-to-end demo of firstmate per-turn quota instrumentation. # Simulates a primary firstmate session over 6 turns: # watcher enqueues a wake -> bin/fm-wake-drain.sh records the wake kind -> # the real Claude Stop turn-end hook (bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh --claude) fires # -> bin/fm-turn-quota-writer.sh appends one instrumentation row. # Finally the captain-facing reader is run: bin/fm-turn-quota.sh report. set -eu REPO=${REPO:?set REPO to the firstmate checkout} DEMO=${DEMO:?set DEMO to a scratch dir} rm -rf "$DEMO" mkdir -p "$DEMO/home/state" "$DEMO/home/data" "$DEMO/home/bin" "$DEMO/fakebin" HOME_DIR="$DEMO/home" STATE="$HOME_DIR/state" # A genuine primary home: plain (non-worktree) checkout with AGENTS.md + bin/. cp "$REPO/AGENTS.md" "$HOME_DIR/AGENTS.md" git -C "$HOME_DIR" init -q git -C "$HOME_DIR" -c user.email=demo@example.invalid -c user.name=demo \ add AGENTS.md >/dev/null git -C "$HOME_DIR" -c user.email=demo@example.invalid -c user.name=demo \ commit -qm "demo home" >/dev/null printf '# backlog\n- task: demo\n' > "$HOME_DIR/data/backlog.md" # Stub provider CLIs. Each call reads a counter file so quota climbs turn over # turn, the way real usage does. cat > "$DEMO/fakebin/quota-axi" << 'SH' #!/bin/sh n=$(cat "$FAKE_TICK" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) printf '{"generatedAt":"2026-08-01T10:%02d:00Z","providers":[{"provider":"claude","windows":[{"id":"five_hour","percentUsed":%s},{"id":"seven_day","percentUsed":%s}]}]}\n' \ "$n" "$(awk -v n="$n" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", 12.0 + n*1.7}')" \ "$(awk -v n="$n" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", 41.0 + n*0.4}')" SH cat > "$DEMO/fakebin/antigravity-usage" << 'SH' #!/bin/sh n=$(cat "$FAKE_TICK" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) printf '{"timestamp":"2026-08-01T10:%02d:00Z","models":[{"modelId":"gemini-3-pro","isAutocompleteOnly":false,"remainingPercentage":%s},{"modelId":"gemini-3-flash-autocomplete","isAutocompleteOnly":true,"remainingPercentage":99.0}]}\n' \ "$n" "$(awk -v n="$n" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", 88.0 - n*2.5}')" SH chmod +x "$DEMO/fakebin/quota-axi" "$DEMO/fakebin/antigravity-usage" export FAKE_TICK="$DEMO/tick" # A healthy, identity-matched watcher lock: the normal supervised state in which # the turn-end guard allows the stop. (Without it the guard would block and # Claude Code would force a continuation of the SAME turn, which the # instrumentation deliberately does not double-count.) sleep 300 & WATCHER_PID=$! trap 'kill "$WATCHER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT mkdir -p "$STATE/.watch.lock" printf '%s\n' "$WATCHER_PID" > "$STATE/.watch.lock/pid" printf '%s\n' "$HOME_DIR" > "$STATE/.watch.lock/fm-home" printf '%s\n' "$REPO/bin/fm-watch.sh" > "$STATE/.watch.lock/watcher-path" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$STATE" bash -c '. "$1"; fm_pid_identity "$2"' _ \ "$REPO/bin/fm-wake-lib.sh" "$WATCHER_PID" > "$STATE/.watch.lock/pid-identity" export PATH="$DEMO/fakebin:$PATH" export FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$HOME_DIR" export FM_HOME="$HOME_DIR" export FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$STATE" turn() { # turn local n=$1 kind=$2 mutate=$3 printf '%s\n' "$n" > "$FAKE_TICK" # A real watcher enqueue for a non-captain wake; an empty queue = captain turn. if [ "$kind" != "captain" ]; then printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$((1000 + n))" "$n" "$kind" "task-demo" "demo wake" \ > "$STATE/.wake-queue" fi touch "$STATE/.last-watcher-beat" "$REPO/bin/fm-wake-drain.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true # What the turn actually did to the fleet (or did not do). eval "$mutate" # Real turn-end hook payload, exactly as Claude Code sends it. printf '{"session_id":"demo-session","stop_hook_active":false}' \ | "$REPO/bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh" --claude >/dev/null 2>&1 || true # Turns are minutes apart in reality; drop the 15s probe cache so each turn # reads fresh provider numbers instead of a cached one. rm -f "$STATE/.turn-quota-cache.json" "$STATE/.turn-quota-agy-cache.json" printf 'turn %s (%s) recorded\n' "$n" "$kind" } turn 1 captain 'printf "window=demo1\n" > "$STATE/task-demo.meta"' turn 2 signal 'printf "window=demo1\nstatus=working\n" > "$STATE/task-demo.meta"' turn 3 heartbeat ':' # pure supervision poll, changed nothing turn 4 stale ':' # nudged a stalled crewmate, nothing landed turn 5 signal 'printf "%s\n" "- landed demo" >> "$HOME_DIR/data/backlog.md"' turn 6 captain ':' # answered the captain: no disk change echo echo "### state/quota-turns.log (raw instrumentation rows)" cat "$STATE/quota-turns.log" echo echo "### bin/fm-turn-quota.sh report" "$REPO/bin/fm-turn-quota.sh" report ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ⚠️ `bin/fm-turn-quota-writer.sh:61` - Fingerprint fallback fabricates a "no-op" instead of an absent marker. `fp` is built from a `sha256sum` pipeline; when the pipeline yields nothing (missing `sha256sum`, unreadable state), line 61 substitutes the constant `0000000000000000`. Every subsequent turn then compares equal to that constant and records `fp_changed=0`, so the reader prints a fabricated "Proxy no-op (fingerprint unchanged): 100.0%". This violates the same absent-not-zero honesty invariant the suite already enforces for quota (`tests/fm-turn-quota.test.sh:40` "reader must never coerce missing Gemini quota to zero"). Emit an `absent` fingerprint marker and have the reader exclude those rows from the no-op ratio instead of a constant. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-turn-quota-writer.sh:56` - GNU-only tooling with no macOS fallback, contradicting the repo's own conventions. Line 56 uses `ls -l --full-time` (GNU-only), line 57/59 use bare `sha256sum`, and lines 79/104 use bare `timeout`. On macOS all three are absent by default, so: the .meta component of the fingerprint is empty, the final hash produces nothing (falling into the constant at line 61), and both `quota-axi`/`antigravity-usage` probes fail to 127 leaving quota permanently `absent` — the entire feature silently degrades to a fixed fingerprint plus no quota data. The repo already owns fallbacks for exactly these: `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:76-79` (`shasum -a 256` / `sha256sum`) and `bin/fm-quota-axi-lib.sh:26-31` (`timeout` / `gtimeout` / `perl` alarm). Reuse them; replace `ls --full-time` with a portable `stat` (the same file already does `stat -c %Y || stat -f %m` at line 75). - ⚠️ `bin/fm-turn-quota-writer.sh:104` - `antigravity-usage` is invoked uncached and synchronously on every turn end, up to 3s of added latency per turn, while `quota-axi` got a 15s cache (lines 72-81). The file header states "this writer must never block, delay, or fail a turn", and `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh:127` calls it inline before the guard predicate, so the delay lands on the captain's turn-end path. Apply the same mtime-based cache file to the antigravity probe (or background the whole writer), so consecutive turn ends do not each pay a fresh subprocess round trip. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh:127` - The writer call sits before the guard predicate, so guard blocks manufacture spurious no-op records and mislabel wake kind. In `--claude` mode the guard re-blocks up to FM_CLAUDE_TURNEND_BLOCK_BUDGET times; each block exits 2, Claude continues, and the next Stop re-enters `fm-turnend-guard.sh` and appends another record. Those continuation records almost always see an unchanged fingerprint (the continuation only arms the watcher), so every block event injects an extra `fp_changed=0` row and biases the headline "Proxy no-op" ratio upward. The first of those records also resets `state/.turn-wake-kind` to `captain` (writer line 141), so the continuation of a `signal` wake is attributed to `captain`. Additionally, codex/grok mode exits at `fm-turnend-guard.sh:110` when `stop_hook_active` is true, i.e. before the writer, so those harnesses do not record the same continuation turns — the metric is not comparable across harnesses. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-turn-quota-writer.sh:108` - Gemini quota selection is order-dependent and may measure the wrong model. `[.models[]? | select(.modelId | contains("gemini")) | .remainingPercentage] | first` takes whichever gemini entry the tool happens to list first. Against the live `antigravity-usage --json` on this machine that is `gemini-2.5-pro`, which is flagged `isAutocompleteOnly: true` — not a model the fleet dispatches work to. If model ordering changes or the pools diverge per model, the recorded "Gemini / agy" delta silently tracks a different budget than the one being spent. Pin an explicit modelId (or take the minimum remaining across dispatch-eligible gemini models) rather than relying on array order. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-test-isolation-proof.sh:112` - The `fm-test-isolation-proof.sh` change is dead code carrying a false audit rationale. `exclusion_reason` is only consulted from `list_exclusions_for_report` (line 184) over a fixed heredoc that does not include `fm-turn-quota.test.sh`, and the test is also absent from `list_parallel_candidates`, so adding the basename changes no behavior. Worse, it files the test under "watcher/wake/lock family; intentional process locks and daemon races" — the test uses no locks or daemons, and the same commit classifies it `pure-contract-unit` in `bin/fm-test-run.sh:131`. The block header states "Reasons are audit evidence; do not re-add a basename without clearing its reason." Drop the exclusion entry so the audit record stays truthful and consistent with the declared family. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-turn-quota-writer.sh:57` - The `|| echo "no-backlog"` fallback can never fire: the pipeline's exit status is `awk`'s, and `awk` succeeds with empty output even when `sha256sum` fails or the file is missing. `backlog_hash` becomes the empty string instead of the intended sentinel, so a missing backlog and a present-but-unhashable backlog are indistinguishable in the fingerprint. Test the file with `[ -f ]` (or capture and check the hash) before substituting the sentinel. The sibling `head_rev` on line 58 is a plain command and does work as written. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-turn-quota.sh:24` - The dispatcher's catch-all `*)` branch execs the reader with the unrecognized token still in `$@`, and the reader ignores unknown args. A typo such as `bin/fm-turn-quota.sh writ` silently prints a report instead of recording a turn — the failure mode is a silently-missing measurement, not an error. Exit non-zero with the usage line for unknown subcommands (keeping the bare no-arg default as `report`). - ℹ️ `bin/fm-turn-quota-reader.sh:39` - `c5_first`, `c7_first`, and `g_first` are initialized and assigned but never read — the report only uses the running `*_total_delta` sums. Dropping the three variables and their three assignment lines removes six lines of misleading dead state from the awk program. 🔧 Fix: fix portability, absent fingerprints, and probe caching in turn quota 2 issues (1 error, 1 info) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh:131` - The new `STOP_HOOK_ACTIVE != "true"` gate silently stops recording most Claude turns — the exact turns the feature exists to price. The gate treats `stop_hook_active=true` as "same turn re-entering after a block", but this same file states the opposite 85 lines above (lines 41-46): "Claude Code marks EVERY stop after ANY stop-hook-driven continuation stop_hook_active=true, including turns started by the asyncRewake auto-arm", and `docs/turnend-guard.md:54` repeats it: "Claude Code sets `stop_hook_active=true` on every stop after any stop-hook continuation, including `asyncRewake` rewakes, which re-opened the 2026-07-21 blind window". That is precisely why `--claude` mode ignores the flag for the block decision. Concrete path: `bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh` exits 2 with a rewake banner on any actionable arm close (signal:/stale:/check:/heartbeat); from that Stop onward every payload in the session carries `stop_hook_active=true`, so line 131 skips the writer for every subsequent turn — including genuinely new, token-spending wake-handling turns. The log then contains only the pre-first-rewake turns, and the report's "Total turns" and quota deltas understate real cost by an unbounded margin, contradicting the intent's required "measure its own token cost per turn". Earliest supported shared boundary: the guard already cooperates with the auto-arm's event-epoch ledger (`state/.claude-autoarm-epoch`, `FM_CLAUDE_AUTOARM_EPOCH_FRESH`, documented as "one event epoch yields exactly one recovery turn") — dedupe the quota record on that epoch, or record unconditionally with a continuation flag in the row and let the reader collapse it. Non-Claude modes already get the one-row property from the pre-existing early exit at line 108, so they need no gate here. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-turn-quota-reader.sh:153` - The per-wake-kind breakdown table cannot be reconciled by a reader: `w_total` (the TURNS column) counts all rows for that wake kind, while `w_pct` now divides by `w_known` (rows with a computable fingerprint). A wake kind with 4 rows of which 2 have absent fingerprints prints `TURNS 4` and `1 (50.0%)`, where 50% is of 2, not 4. The summary section discloses its exclusion count (`Fingerprint absent (excluded from proxy ratios)`), but the table does not. Print `w_known` as its own column or append the excluded count per row so the two numbers are self-consistent. 🔧 Fix: gate turn quota on block ledger, disclose breakdown denominator 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh:127` - `PAYLOAD` is now parsed by two separate `jq` subprocesses on every primary turn end: line 99 for the loop-guard flag and line 127 for `session_id`. The second one was previously only reached on the re-block path; moving it above the writer gate puts it on the hot path for every turn in every mode. The existing filter at line 99 already has the payload object in hand — emitting both values from one invocation (e.g. a tab-joined `"\(.stopHookActive // .stop_hook_active // false)\t\(.session_id // \"unknown\")"` read with one `IFS=$'\t' read`) removes a per-turn subprocess from the turn-end hook without changing behavior. Purely a simplification; the error-handling contract (both fall back to safe defaults, guard exits 0 on a malformed payload) must be preserved.

Left unedited as a judgment call; if operators should know Gemini/agy accounting is silently `absent` without that binary, docs/configuration.md "Toolchain" is the place, as an explicitly optional note. 🔧 Fix: note optional antigravity-usage probe in toolchain ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: feat(bin): converge proven rewritten default branches in fleet sync
body:
## Intent Give bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh a narrowly guarded convergence path for deliberately rewritten remote history. Converge a diverged local default branch only after an exact fetch proves the remote-tracking branch is real and fresh, every local-only commit tree has an identical counterpart on the remote branch, the primary working tree is clean, and every linked worktree is clean with no content absent from remotes or the rewritten default. Refuse loudly with the failing condition and offending commit whenever proof fails; never force, stash, clean, or discard work. Preserve ordinary behind-only fast-forward behavior. Cover identical-tree convergence, missing-tree refusal, dirty-tree refusal, linked-unlanded-work refusal, and legacy fast-forward behavior, and keep bootstrap dependency fixtures hermetic from host-installed binaries. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh` gains a proof-guarded convergence path for a diverged default branch: an exact `+refs/heads/:refs/remotes/origin/` fetch must produce a real remote-tracking branch, the local-only and remote-only commits must form equal-length `--topo-order --reverse` sequences whose trees match one-to-one by position, the clone must be clean, and every linked worktree must be clean with no content absent from remotes or the rewritten default. Only then does it `reset --hard` onto the freshly fetched base and report `converged rewritten ..`; nothing is forced, stashed, cleaned, or discarded. - Any failed proof refuses loudly through `report_convergence_refusal` with the failing condition, offending commit, and behind count. Dirty default-branch clones now route to the refusal message when truly diverged and keep the existing `STUCK:` report otherwise, while behind-only fast-forward and ahead-only `STUCK` behavior stay unchanged. - `tests/fm-fleet-sync.test.sh` adds coverage for identical-tree convergence, out-of-position tree refusal, unequal rewrite length refusal, dirty-tree refusal, and linked-unlanded-work refusal (27/27 passing); `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` isolates the orca backend fixture from a host-installed `orca` via a `BASH_ENV` shim. `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, and the bootstrap-diagnostics skill document the new converged and refusal lines. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Every finding from the prior two rounds is resolved — the convergence proof is now fail-closed on each inspection, topologically ordered, and positionally one-to-one with an equal-count guard — leaving a well-bounded change whose only mutating action is a `reset --hard` gated behind five independently tested proofs, with legacy fast-forward and STUCK paths untouched. ## Testing Ran the two targeted suites (fm-fleet-sync, fm-bootstrap) — all green — then drove the actual fm-fleet-sync.sh CLI over a purpose-built five-clone fleet home so every intent branch shows in one user-visible transcript: the proven identical-tree rewrite converged (`converged rewritten main 3ea42e6..f443c71 (2 local-only commit trees matched origin/main)`), while missing-tree, dirty-tree, and linked-unlanded-work clones each refused with the named condition plus offending commit and stayed untouched with their content intact, and the ordinary behind-only clone still fast-forwarded; an extra manual ahead-only case confirmed unpushed work is still reported STUCK and never reset. Also proved the bootstrap orca fixture is now hermetic: on this host (which has a real /usr/bin/orca) the pre-change fixture form prints nothing while the shimmed form emits the expected `MISSING: orca (install: ...)` line. No UI surface is involved — this is a shell CLI change, so CLI transcripts are the end-user-visible evidence. Worktree left clean; scratch repos removed, evidence files kept.

Evidence: Reproducible demo script for the end-to-end fleet sync run ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # End-to-end demo: one fleet home with five clones, one real fm-fleet-sync.sh run. set -eu ROOT=${ROOT:?set ROOT to the repo worktree} DEMO=${DEMO:?set DEMO to a scratch dir} rm -rf "$DEMO" mkdir -p "$DEMO/projects" "$DEMO/remotes" export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=fmdemo GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=fmdemo@example.invalid export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=fmdemo GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=fmdemo@example.invalid commit_file() { printf '%s\n' "$3" > "$1/$2"; git -C "$1" add "$2"; git -C "$1" commit -qm "$4"; } build_pair() { # local name=$1 local work="$DEMO/work-$name" remote="$DEMO/remotes/$name.git" clone="$DEMO/projects/$name" git init -q "$work"; git -C "$work" symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main commit_file "$work" file.txt v0 "C0" git clone --quiet --bare "$work" "$remote" git -C "$work" remote add origin "file://$(cd "$remote" && pwd)" git -C "$work" push -q -u origin main git clone --quiet "file://$(cd "$remote" && pwd)" "$clone" } push_rewritten_trees() { # ... local clone=$1 parent='' i=0 tree rewritten; shift for tree in "$@"; do i=$((i+1)) if [ -n "$parent" ]; then rewritten=$(printf 'rewritten commit %s\n' "$i" | git -C "$clone" commit-tree "$tree" -p "$parent") else rewritten=$(printf 'rewritten commit %s\n' "$i" | git -C "$clone" commit-tree "$tree") fi parent=$rewritten done git -C "$clone" update-ref refs/heads/rw "$parent" git -C "$clone" push -q --force origin refs/heads/rw:refs/heads/main git -C "$clone" update-ref -d refs/heads/rw } rewrite_identical() { # : origin/main replaced by same trees, new identities local clone=$1 c; local -a trees=() while IFS= read -r c; do trees+=("$(git -C "$clone" rev-parse "$c^{tree}")"); done \ < <(git -C "$clone" rev-list --reverse main) push_rewritten_trees "$clone" "${trees[@]}" } # 1. rewritten history, clean clone -> should converge build_pair rewritten-clean commit_file "$DEMO/projects/rewritten-clean" file.txt v1 "C1" rewrite_identical "$DEMO/projects/rewritten-clean" # 2. genuinely diverged (local revert content absent from remote) -> must refuse build_pair genuinely-diverged commit_file "$DEMO/projects/genuinely-diverged" file.txt v1 "C1" commit_file "$DEMO/projects/genuinely-diverged" file.txt v0 "revert C1" T0=$(git -C "$DEMO/projects/genuinely-diverged" rev-parse "main~2^{tree}") T1=$(git -C "$DEMO/projects/genuinely-diverged" rev-parse "main~1^{tree}") push_rewritten_trees "$DEMO/projects/genuinely-diverged" "$T0" "$T0" "$T1" # 3. rewritten history but dirty working tree -> must refuse build_pair rewritten-dirty commit_file "$DEMO/projects/rewritten-dirty" file.txt v1 "C1" rewrite_identical "$DEMO/projects/rewritten-dirty" printf 'uncommitted captain work\n' >> "$DEMO/projects/rewritten-dirty/file.txt" # 4. rewritten history but a linked worktree holds unlanded work -> must refuse build_pair rewritten-linked commit_file "$DEMO/projects/rewritten-linked" file.txt v1 "C1" rewrite_identical "$DEMO/projects/rewritten-linked" git -C "$DEMO/projects/rewritten-linked" worktree add -q -b feature "$DEMO/linked-work" commit_file "$DEMO/linked-work" linked.txt unlanded "linked unlanded commit" # 5. ordinary behind-only clone -> legacy fast-forward must still work build_pair plain-behind commit_file "$DEMO/work-plain-behind" file.txt v1 "C1 on origin" git -C "$DEMO/work-plain-behind" push -q origin main snapshot() { local p for p in rewritten-clean genuinely-diverged rewritten-dirty rewritten-linked plain-behind; do printf ' %-20s main=%s origin/main=%s dirty=%s\n' "$p" \ "$(git -C "$DEMO/projects/$p" rev-parse --short main)" \ "$(git -C "$DEMO/projects/$p" rev-parse --short origin/main)" \ "$([ -n "$(git -C "$DEMO/projects/$p" status --porcelain)" ] && echo yes || echo no)" done printf ' %-20s HEAD=%s (branch %s)\n' linked-worktree \ "$(git -C "$DEMO/linked-work" rev-parse --short HEAD)" \ "$(git -C "$DEMO/linked-work" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" } echo "=== BEFORE ==="; snapshot echo echo "=== \$ fm-fleet-sync.sh (whole fleet) ===" FM_HOME="$DEMO" FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$ROOT" "$ROOT/bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh" 2>&1 | sed 's/^/ /' echo echo "=== AFTER ==="; snapshot echo echo "=== content preserved on refusals ===" echo " genuinely-diverged/file.txt : $(cat "$DEMO/projects/genuinely-diverged/file.txt")" echo " rewritten-dirty/file.txt : $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$DEMO/projects/rewritten-dirty/file.txt")" echo " linked-work/linked.txt : $(cat "$DEMO/linked-work/linked.txt")" ```

✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 3 issues found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:413` - The local-only commit enumeration `done < <(git -C "$PROJ" rev-list "$DEFAULT" --not "$BASE" 2>/dev/null)` runs in a process substitution, so its exit status is unobservable and `set -e` cannot fire. If rev-list fails (corrupt object DB, unreadable ref), the loop body never executes, `local_count` stays 0, no refusal is printed, and control falls through to `git reset --hard "$BASE"` at line 429 — discarding every local-only commit on the default branch with zero proof performed. Every sibling inspection in this function (`log --format=%T` line 397, `rev-parse ^{tree}` line 405, `status --porcelain` line 415, `worktree list` line 336) explicitly refuses on failure; this is the only one that silently passes. Intent requires refusing loudly whenever proof fails. Fix: capture into a variable and gate on its exit status, e.g. `local_only=$(git -C "$PROJ" rev-list "$DEFAULT" --not "$BASE" 2>&1) || { report_convergence_refusal "local-only commits cannot be enumerated" "$local_rev" "$(first_line "$local_only")"; return 1; }`, then iterate the variable. Gate on exit status rather than on `local_count > 0`: an empty list is legitimate when the fresh refetch in refresh_remote_default_for_convergence moved $BASE forward past the pre-fetch divergence classification at line 545, making the reset an ordinary fast-forward. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:409` - `remote_tree_contains` tests membership in the entire `git log --format=%T "$BASE"` set, ignoring position, so a local-only commit whose tree recreates an OLDER remote tree is accepted as landed and then discarded by `reset --hard`. Reachable path: local main = C1,C2,C3 where C3 is a `git revert` of C2, so tree(C3) == tree(C1); origin/main is deliberately rewritten to C1',C2' with identical trees. rev-list yields C1,C2,C3; tree(C1) and tree(C2) match their counterparts and tree(C3) matches C1' — the proof passes, the clone is clean, and line 429 resets main onto C2'. The local revert commit is discarded and the working tree content flips back to the un-reverted state, contradicting the intent's 'never force, stash, clean, or discard work'. Distinguishing a rewritten counterpart from a coincidental older tree needs ordering: the matched remote positions for local-only commits taken in topological order should be monotonically non-decreasing along $BASE, with the local tip's match no older than any other local-only commit's match. Raising rather than fixing because it narrows the tree-membership criterion the intent itself states. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:527` - The new dirty-tree block re-derives 'truly diverged' as `! is-ancestor DEFAULT BASE && ! is-ancestor BASE DEFAULT`, the inverted twin of the classification at lines 545-546, and re-invokes `git status --porcelain` a third time at line 531 even though `dirty` (line 486) already captured that answer. Two copies of the same ancestry predicate in one safety-critical path will drift when either is changed. Computing the diverged/ahead-only/behind classification once before the dirty check and branching on it would remove both the duplicate predicate and the extra status call. 🔧 Fix: enforce positional tree proof in rewrite convergence 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:409` - The positional proof pairs `rev-list --reverse "$DEFAULT" --not "$BASE"` (line 409) against `rev-list --reverse "$BASE" --not "$DEFAULT"` (line 413), but `--reverse` only reverses git's default commit-date traversal. The proof's premise is an oldest-first sequence, which is a topological property; without `--topo-order` the pairing depends on committer clock values rather than on parent/child structure. Realistic effect is a spurious refusal (safe direction) whenever local-only committer dates are non-monotonic — tooling that sets GIT_COMMITTER_DATE, `rebase --committer-date-is-author-date`, or clock skew on a repo shared across machines. Incorrect acceptance is also reachable, though compound: local L1(treeA) then L2(treeB) with L1 dated newer reverses to [L2, L1]; if the remote rewrite reordered to R1(treeB), R2(treeA), then L2 pairs with R1 (B==B) and L1 with R2 (A==A), the proof passes, and `reset --hard` at line 470 moves the tip from treeB to treeA — the same discard class the positional fix was added to close. Fix: `git -C "$PROJ" rev-list --topo-order --reverse ...` on both lines 409 and 413, so the sequence is a topological guarantee instead of a clock artifact. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh:10` - The file header still documents the superseded membership rule: 'every local-only commit tree exists on the freshly fetched remote branch'. The implemented invariant is strictly narrower — the local-only and $BASE-only commits must be equal-length oldest-first sequences with one-to-one positional tree equality (lines 404-454), so a rewrite that adds or drops a commit relative to the local-only run now refuses with a count mismatch. Since this header is the stated safety contract for a `reset --hard` path, the stale wording will mislead the next reader about when convergence is possible. Update lines 9-11 to describe the positional one-to-one pairing and the equal-count requirement. 🔧 Fix: order rewrite convergence proof topologically ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-fleet-sync.test.sh` (27/27 ok, incl. `test_identical_tree_rewrite_converges`, `test_out_of_position_tree_rewrite_refuses`, `test_unequal_rewrite_length_refuses`, `test_identical_tree_rewrite_dirty_refuses`, `test_identical_tree_rewrite_linked_unlanded_refuses`) - `bash tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` (full file, exit 0; covers `test_orca_backend_gates_orca_tool_only_when_selected`) - Manual end-to-end: built a 5-clone fleet home (rewritten-clean, genuinely-diverged, rewritten-dirty, rewritten-linked, plain-behind) and ran the real `FM_HOME=... bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh` once over the whole fleet, capturing before/after refs, dirty state, and file content - Manual regression check: ahead-only clone with unpushed local commit stays `STUCK: on diverged main` and is not reset (`ahead-only-untouched.txt`) - Manual hermeticity check: ran `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` under the orca fixture with and without the new `BASH_ENV` shim on a host that has a real `/usr/bin/orca` on `BASE_PATH`
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: feat(bin): report a known-wrong program squatting a required tool name
body:
## Intent The captain asked that startup bootstrap report a wrong program squatting a required tool's name as a distinct WRONG_PROGRAM diagnostic instead of silently accepting it - on Linux /usr/bin/orca is GNOME's screen reader, not the Orca terminal runtime the home dispatches into. After review the captain corrected the approach: keep the plain presence check as the default and report WRONG_PROGRAM only when a present binary positively identifies as a KNOWN-WRONG program, matched against evidence verified on this machine (2026-08-01, GNOME Orca 46.1). The real Orca runtime CLI's help output was never observed on this machine, so a positive identity marker must never be guessed. Only orca gets a known-wrong signature; any other outcome (real CLI help, unknown help, no help, crash, timeout) keeps the presence result. Tests cover: known-wrong reported with its path, non-wrong help passes, unrecognised help treated as present, and tools without a known-wrong signature are never probed. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` now prints a distinct `WRONG_PROGRAM: - is , not the '' CLI this home needs (install: )` line when a required tool is present on `PATH` but positively identifies as a known-wrong program. The plain presence check stays the default: only `orca` has a verified known-wrong signature (GNOME's screen reader, matched on the width-stable `--speech-system` option string), tools without a signature are never probed, and real-CLI help, unrecognised help, no help, a crash, or a timeout all keep the presence result. - The identity probe runs ` --help` through the existing `timeout`/`gtimeout`/`perl` ladder bounded at 5s with stdin closed on every rung, so a squatting binary that reads stdin cannot hang session start or swallow the captain's keystrokes. - Documented the new line in the `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` header contract, the `bootstrap-diagnostics` skill (report the collision, never run the install command as a silent overwrite), the `AGENTS.md` prefix list that triggers that skill, and `docs/configuration.md`. `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` adds 5 cases covering the reported path, rewrapped/localized help, a non-wrong help match, unrecognised help, and unprobed tools. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: All three prior findings are fixed at the right boundary and re-verified against the real binary - the identity marker is now a width- and locale-stable option string, the probe closes stdin on every timeout rung, and the new diagnostic is documented in both the trigger list and the handling playbook - leaving a small, conservative change that can only ever degrade to the pre-existing presence result. ## Testing Ran the targeted bootstrap test file (all 26 checks pass, covering the five new known-wrong cases) plus the documentation-audiences test for the AGENTS.md and skill-doc edits, then proved the intent at the product level on this machine, which genuinely has GNOME Orca 46.1 at /usr/bin/orca: the base-commit script accepts that binary silently while the target commit prints the distinct WRONG_PROGRAM line naming the squatting path, and the same line is what the session-start digest passes through verbatim. Also exercised the forbidden side of the contract manually — a present orca whose help does not match the verified marker (including one that ignores --help and reads stdin) keeps the presence result with no invented rejection and no startup hang. The change is CLI-only, so the reviewer-visible artifact is a command transcript rather than a screenshot; the working tree was left clean.

body:
## Intent Fix the shared secondmate-registry parsing contract so valid natural-language punctuation cannot break guarded operations. Before editing, reproduce the landed child-cleanup failure through end-user public interfaces using an isolated fixture with an earlier parenthetical in a valid registered secondmate summary and parentheses plus semicolons in natural-language scope before the explicit structured suffix ends. Exercise guarded fm-teardown.sh child cleanup while a durable parent public-followup binding requires resolving the main home data/secondmates.md record. Show the old parser returns no home and cleanup refuses despite matching registered home and task metadata. Separate the punctuation trigger, the simple parser-compatible registry line that masks it, and the visible cleanup refusal. Confirm fm-home-seed.sh validate accepted the same operationally unparseable record. Do not mutate a real home, public reply, or existing task during reproduction. Fix parsing so generated structured fields resolve from their explicit suffix rather than the first parenthesis or first incidental semicolon. Audit every duplicated secondmate-registry parser in fm-home-seed.sh, fm-spawn.sh, fm-teardown.sh, and shared helpers. Use one authoritative parser owner where appropriate under the one-owner rule, with callers sharing validation and refusal behavior. Make validation reject every record operational consumers cannot parse. Preserve refusal without mutation for malformed, duplicate, ambiguous, unsafe, or identity-mismatched records. Do not weaken cleanup, public-followup, home identity, symlink, force, discard, or unlanded-work safeguards. Inspect divergent parsing paths and relevant history, test the punctuation counterfactual against the simple line, and seek disconfirming evidence before settling on the cause. Add executable regressions through public interfaces for home and project resolution, secondmate spawn or validation where relevant, and the exact guarded child-cleanup path that failed. Use isolated fixtures and never assert implementation source bytes. Run focused and full relevant tests, bin/fm-lint.sh, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh where maintained prose changes, and the complete configured no-mistakes pipeline. Preserve this complete task-specific contract and all accepted follow-ups in this intent, excluding generic scaffold boilerplate. This task is independent of the intent-handoff change and PR 1446. Do not change, synchronize, recover, resume, validate, or merge either unrelated task, either PR 1446 validation run, or any preserved PR 1446 head. ## What Changed - Add an authoritative secondmate registry parser that anchors structured fields to their explicit suffix, allowing parentheses and semicolons in natural-language summaries and scopes. - Share hardened binding validation across registry consumers so malformed, unsafe, duplicate, overlapping, or identity-mismatched records fail before guarded mutations. - Add public-interface regressions and documentation for punctuation-safe parsing, spawn resolution, validation, and guarded teardown behavior. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The shared parser now snapshots only a successfully and fully read regular registry, handles unterminated final records, rejects symlinks and ambiguous bindings, and validates identity before spawn or teardown mutation with matching public-interface regressions. ## Testing Inspected the parser consolidation and history, ran five focused relevant suites covering public-followup cleanup, secondmate safety, project handoff, registry-backed updates, and fleet snapshots, then manually exercised the punctuation-bearing guarded child-cleanup path. All checks passed, and the CLI evidence shows correct parent resolution, refusal for the owed reply, and preservation without mutation.
Evidence: Punctuated registry guarded-cleanup transcript Punctuation-bearing registry validation: accepted. Guarded teardown: refused because work-child still owes public commitment pf-teardown-valid. Child metadata and identity marker preserved; parent registry unchanged; no endpoint kill requested. ```text ok - marked secondmate teardown resolves its parent and fails closed when unavailable USER-SURFACE CHECK: punctuated registry validation result: accepted registry: - mate - synthetic (id is legacy); preserve this (home: /var/folders/5x/4nqprlbx0518k3ybcb1sz6gr0000gn/T//fm-public-followup.YyPwGL/teardown-valid-child; scope: synthetic (child); semicolon remains meaningful; projects: ; added 2026-07-30) GUARDED CHILD CLEANUP RESULT ●━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ● WATCHER DOWN - SUPERVISION IS OFF ● 1 task(s) in flight, but no watcher has a fresh beacon (last beat: never, grace 300s). ● Trust the emitted supervision protocol for this harness; do not use shell & for watcher repair. ● This is a supervision warning only; the guarded operation WILL still run. ● repair missing watcher supervision according to the session-start block for this harness; do not use shell &. ●━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ REFUSED: task work-child still owes a public reply through the myfirstmate relay. public commitment pf-teardown-valid is still pending-work for secondmate:mate/work-child Deliver it with bin/fm-public-followup.sh deliver , waive it with tasks-axi public-followup waive, or use --force after explicit discard approval. ✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed (3) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-teardown.sh:899` - Intent requires: “Preserve refusal without mutation for malformed, duplicate, ambiguous, unsafe, or identity-mismatched records.” This loop rejects malformed syntax but never proves a unique ID-to-home binding. Registries containing `A -> H` plus `B -> H`, or `A -> H` plus `A -> H2`, pass teardown preflight when H2 is unrelated. Teardown can then delete H and either leave B pointing at a deleted home or remove both A records. Move whole-registry uniqueness validation and the expected ID/home match to a shared pre-removal boundary. - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:569` - Intent requires callers to share refusal behavior for duplicate, ambiguous, and identity-mismatched records. The shared lookup now returns failure for malformed or duplicate matching records, but secondmate spawn bypasses home lookup when an explicit or metadata home exists, and its projects lookup failure is swallowed. Consequently `fm-spawn <id> <home> ... --secondmate` can create an endpoint and metadata despite a duplicate registry ID or a registry home that disagrees with the supplied home. Resolve one unique registry record and compare its canonical home before any spawn mutation. 🔧 Fix: Centralize secondmate registry binding validation 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-secondmate-registry-lib.sh:99` - Intent requires refusal for every malformed or duplicate record. The new authoritative loop drops a final record when the file lacks a trailing newline because `read` assigns the text but returns nonzero before executing the body. A valid `A -> H` line followed by an unterminated duplicate `A -> H2` is therefore accepted, allowing spawn or teardown mutation under the same ambiguity this boundary is meant to reject. Process the final nonempty read with `while read ... || [ -n "$line" ]`. - 🚨 `bin/fm-home-seed.sh:230` - Intent says: “Do not weaken ... symlink ... safeguards.” The new wrapper treats any path failing `-f` as an absent registry, so a broken `data/secondmates.md` symlink bypasses the shared validator even though that validator explicitly rejects symlinks. `fm-home-seed.sh validate` reports success, and a seed can later replace the unsafe symlink after other provisioning mutations. Distinguish a genuinely absent path from `[ -L "$REG" ]` and refuse the symlink before mutation. 🔧 Fix: Harden registry EOF and symlink validation 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-secondmate-registry-lib.sh:91` - Intent requires: “Make validation reject every record operational consumers cannot parse.” This boundary checks only file type and symlink status. If a regular registry cannot be opened for reading, the redirected loop processes zero records and an expected-ID-free `fm-home-seed.sh validate` reaches success with an empty temporary table. Explicitly open the registry before validation and convert any open/read failure into `SECONDMATE_REGISTRY_ERROR`. 🔧 Fix: Reject unreadable registries before parsing ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - Inspected `git diff` and relevant history from `68641a33c25e220ab3cab6cafe84eff971008714` through `cb222b3a4d93c35d68e2477b11d3dfc7f7511751`. - `tests/fm-public-followup.test.sh` - `tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh` - `tests/fm-backlog-handoff.test.sh` - `tests/fm-update.test.sh` - `tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh` - Ran the isolated `test_secondmate_teardown_requires_parent_binding` fixture and recorded validation, teardown refusal, preserved durable state, and absence of endpoint mutation.

title: feat(watcher): add a hot-check fast path for event-driven checks
body:
## Summary
- `state/<id>.check.sh` may pair with a sibling `state/<id>.check-hot` marker naming an events-pending file; each watcher cycle, if that file is currently non-empty, the check runs immediately through the exact same trusted dispatch as the `CHECK_INTERVAL` sweep (check-trust binding included), independent of `.last-check`.

title: fix(bin): verify PR checks from the forge before reporting ready
body:
## Intent Make 'checks green' an evidence-produced fact so Firstmate cannot report a PR ready when GitHub has run zero checks. Correct fm-crew-state's no-checks classification; add a bounded read-only exact-task/exact-PR resolver that returns green only for a matching recorded head, a nonzero applicable check count, and all-success conclusions; preserve no-checks, not-ready, and unknown as fail-closed non-ready verdicts; ensure forge/API failure never falls back to a friendly answer or creates repeated alarms; and keep worker-written 'done: ... checks green' as a wake signal only, never evidence. Do not add polling, alarms, GitHub writes, or broader verification redesign. Behavioral replays must cover zero checks rejection, genuine success, forge outage, head mismatch, cross-branch evidence isolation, and worker prose alone. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` gains `resolve_pr_checks_state`, a bounded read-only resolver that reads the exact task-bound PR through the canonical `fm-pr-lib.sh` parser and a single `gh pr view`, returning `green` only when the forge head matches a head this task owns (recorded `pr_head=` or the attributed full run's head) and the rollup is non-empty and all-successful. `no-checks`, `not-ready`, `forge-unsupported` and `unknown` all stay non-ready, so a missing `gh`/`jq`, an unparseable PR URL, a non-GitHub forge or an API failure resolves to unknown rather than to a friendly answer. - Every path that previously reported readiness on prose now routes through that resolver: the `checks-passed` run outcome, the ci-step log tail (whose `no CI checks reported - still monitoring` marker no longer counts as green, only as `no-checks`), and a worker-written `done: ... checks green` status line, which is now a wake signal that emits `unknown` with the unverified verdict unless the forge confirms it. Fix-round vetoes from the run TOON are restricted to full attribution so a foreign coarse-mode run cannot mark another crew not-ready. - `tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` adds a read-only fake `gh` plus replays for zero-checks rejection, verified success, forge outage, head mismatch, cross-branch evidence isolation and worker prose alone (58 cases pass, with the adjacent `fm-watch-triage` suite green); `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/configuration.md` are corrected to describe the evidence-gated verdict instead of the old marker-wins behaviour. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Every round-1 finding is closed with a targeted regression replay, the resolver remains fail-closed with no reachable false-green path, the newly sourced fm-pr-lib.sh is free of source-time side effects and name collisions, and all six replay categories the intent requires are now covered, leaving only one informational test-selection gap that mirrors a pre-existing repo pattern. ## Testing Ran the targeted fm-crew-state suite (58 cases, all pass) plus its main consumer fm-watch-triage (40 cases, all pass), then produced product-level evidence by driving the real bin/fm-crew-state.sh through all six required replays and replaying the identical fixtures against the base commit for contrast: previously every scenario, including zero checks and a head mismatch, printed "state: done - PR ready for review", whereas now only forge-verified green does, with each rejection naming its verdict and the forge-outage read staying byte-identical across repeats so there is no friendly fallback and no repeated alarm. An instrumented gh shim showed exactly one read-only `gh pr view --json headRefOid,statusCheckRollup` call per crew-state read in both the green and outage paths, confirming no polling, retries or GitHub writes were added. This change is a shell CLI surface with no UI, so the reviewer-visible evidence is CLI transcripts and a before/after comparison table rather than screenshots. Worktree left clean.
Evidence: Before/after captain-facing readiness comparison (six replays) ## 1. ZERO CHECKS REJECTION (GitHub has run no checks at all) BEFORE (1e24757): state: done · source: run-step · checks green: PR ready for review AFTER (4d98b31): state: unknown · source: run-step · checks no-checks: checks-passed outcome not captain-ready ## 2. GENUINE SUCCESS (matching head, non-zero all-success check set) BEFORE: state: done · source: run-step · checks green: PR ready for review AFTER : state: done · source: run-step · checks green: PR ready for review (verified from forge) ## 3. FORGE OUTAGE (gh cannot reach GitHub, read twice) BEFORE: state: done · source: run-step · checks green: PR ready for review (still monitoring for merge/close) [x2] AFTER : state: working · source: run-step · ci running (checks unknown) [x2, byte-identical] ## 4. title: fix: recognize fork-pushed work during teardown
body:
## Intent Fix bin/fm-teardown.sh so its landed-work check consults the remote the task actually pushes to, including the fork no-mistakes records as its push target (config.ForkURL), not only origin. Finished work pushed to that fork must tear down without manual --force; refusal must never be weakened; refusal messages must name the remotes that were consulted; ordinary single-remote behavior stays unchanged. Changes to bin/fm-teardown.sh and its regression tests in tests/fm-teardown.test.sh. ## What Changed - Refresh the task branch from configured Git remotes and the fork push target recorded by no-mistakes before deciding work is unpushed. - Resolve credential-masked fork targets through configured push URLs, clean up temporary tracking refs, and fail closed on unavailable or ambiguous targets with consulted remotes named in refusal output. - Expand teardown regression coverage for direct, configured, authenticated, rotated, ambiguous, and unverifiable fork targets. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-bounded, preserves fail-closed teardown behavior, prefers unambiguous pushurl targets, and covers the identified fork and credential-rotation paths without source-verifiable regressions. ## Testing With no prior baseline results supplied, the targeted regression file passed and end-to-end CLI evidence confirmed fork-pushed teardown succeeds without `--force` while ordinary and unverifiable unpushed work remains fail-closed with named remotes.
Evidence: End-to-end teardown CLI transcript ```text SCENARIO 1: branch exists only on the fork recorded by no-mistakes $ no-mistakes status repo: /tmp/fm-teardown-tests.Ii7Bmz/nm-fork-remote/project remote: https://github.com/example/upstream.git fork: /tmp/fm-teardown-tests.Ii7Bmz/nm-fork-remote/fork.git gate: /tmp/fm-teardown-tests.Ii7Bmz/nm-fork-remote/gate.git $ git remote -v origin /tmp/fm-teardown-tests.Ii7Bmz/nm-fork-remote/origin.git (fetch) origin /tmp/fm-teardown-tests.Ii7Bmz/nm-fork-remote/origin.git (push) $ git log --oneline HEAD --not --remotes -- 375b70a shippable fork work $ git --git-dir= show-ref refs/heads/fm/task-x1 375b70a1cb7813f2a8839de4e89472d039c6d49a refs/heads/fm/task-x1 $ bin/fm-teardown.sh task-x1 /tmp/fm-teardown-tests.Ii7Bmz/nm-fork-remote/project: already current teardown task-x1 complete (window firstmate:fm-task-x1, worktree /tmp/fm-teardown-tests.Ii7Bmz/nm-fork-remote/wt) Backlog: task-x1 just finished. Run tasks-axi done task-x1 --pr PR_URL, then run tasks-axi ready for dependency-cleared candidates, check date gates, and dispatch only work whose blockers are gone and date is due. RESULT: success — exit 0, no REFUSED message, task metadata removed, and no --force was used $ git show-ref --verify refs/remotes/fm-no-mistakes-fork/fm/task-x1 # after teardown RESULT: no temporary fork tracking ref remains after the safety check SCENARIO 2: ordinary origin-only task has a genuinely unpushed commit $ git remote origin $ bin/fm-teardown.sh task-x1 REFUSED: worktree /tmp/fm-teardown-tests.Ii7Bmz/nm-unpushed/wt has work not on any remote and not landed. remotes checked: origin unpushed commits: 4f7a104 unpushed work Push the branch, land its PR, or get the captain's explicit OK to discard, then --force. RESULT: refused — exit 1 and task metadata preserved SCENARIO 3: credential-masked fork target cannot be resolved safely $ bin/fm-teardown.sh task-x1 REFUSED: worktree /tmp/fm-teardown-tests.Ii7Bmz/nm-masked-fork-unmatched/wt has work not on any remote and not landed. remotes checked: origin, fork (via no-mistakes) fork push target could not be checked: no configured git remote matches the credential-masked no-mistakes fork target. unpushed commits: fa57f06 unverifiable fork work Push the branch, land its PR, or get the captain's explicit OK to discard, then --force. RESULT: refused — exit 1 and task metadata preserved ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed (3) ✅ - 🚨 `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh:532` - Both new fork tests use `wt_commit`, which creates an empty commit. Because its tree already matches `origin/main`, the pre-fix `content_in_default` fallback accepts it, so these tests pass without the new remote-fetch logic. Use `wt_commit_file` in both cases so the required regression tests fail on the base implementation. 🔧 Fix: Strengthen fork teardown regression coverage 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-teardown.sh:558` - Intent requires consulting `config.ForkURL` so finished fork-pushed work tears down, but this parses `no-mistakes status`, whose implementation prints `safeurl.Redact(repo.ForkURL)` rather than the raw push target. For a supported URL such as `https://user:token@host/repo.git`, no-mistakes pushes with the raw URL while teardown fetches `https://redacted@host/repo.git`, fails, and still refuses. Use a supported authenticated machine-readable/probe boundary that does not expose secrets, or explicitly decide that credential-bearing ForkURLs are unsupported. 🔧 Fix: Resolve authenticated fork targets safely 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-teardown.sh:531` - The criterion requires consulting “the remote the task actually pushes to,” but this returns the first masked match after checking `remote.<name>.url` before Git’s actual push destination, `remote.<name>.pushurl`. With `url=https://old:expired@host/repo.git` and `pushurl=https://new:token@host/repo.git`, both redact identically; teardown selects the stale fetch URL, fails to see the branch pushed through `pushurl`, and still refuses. Prefer/try matching pushurl candidates first and fail closed on unresolved ambiguity; cover this credential-rotation sequence. 🔧 Fix: Prefer unambiguous configured push targets ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: feat: wake firstmate for Better Stack incidents
body:
## Summary

- Adds opt-in Better Stack unresolved-incident monitoring through a home-scoped registered custom check.
- Wakes Firstmate within the existing five-minute slow-check cadence for newly opened incidents and suppresses already-delivered incident IDs in private home state.
- Reads `BETTER_STACK_API_TOKEN` only at runtime through Doppler project `fleet-observability`, config `prd`; no token value reaches repository files, state, command arguments, logs, or CI fixtures.
- Adds paginated API polling, bounded network timeouts, deduplicated diagnostics, queue-locked delivery receipts, crash recovery, and mocked behavior coverage with no live CI calls.
- Documents incident triage and explicitly retires interim Better Stack polling from heartbeat handling.

## Design choice

This uses the registered custom-check extension already sanctioned by `docs/architecture.md`, rather than adding another scheduler. That path already provides home scoping, hash-bound private snapshot execution, `FM_CHECK_TIMEOUT`, durable `check:` wake delivery, and watcher continuity when the project fleet is idle.

Bootstrap materializes and registers `state/better-stack-incidents.check.sh` only when the local `config/better-stack-incidents` presence flag exists. Removing the flag retires the runnable check while retaining private dedupe state.

## Delivery contract and accepted tradeoff

The poll follows safe Better Stack pagination and emits unresolved incident identities. The watcher owns durable incident-ID dedupe under the wake-queue lock, appends the `check:` wake, and converges a private recovery receipt into the seen marker after restart or queue drain.

Accepted captain decision: if queue append succeeds, receipt publication itself fails, and the queue is drained before recovery, one rare duplicate wake can occur. The wake handler deduplicates by incident ID. This bounded tradeoff is documented in `docs/configuration.md`.

## Pipeline evidence

No-mistakes run `01KYYJWYTDC5JZ2MGME3WXTWG3` completed intent, rebase, review, test, documentation, lint, and push before its PR step failed solely because the stored base still named deleted branch `beta`.

- Rebase: completed against the then-current base; six conflicts were resolved while preserving upstream contracts.
- Review: completed after fixes for API pagination, wake-boundary dedupe, recovery receipts, recovery tests, and ShellCheck findings. The final receipt-publication tradeoff was explicitly approved and documented.
- Test: completed in 141419 ms with focused mocked API and watcher coverage.
- Documentation: completed after the accepted tradeoff and watcher-owned dedupe contract were recorded.
- Lint: pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0 ran through the repository-owned local toolchain and corrected incident-script warnings. The pipeline wrapper later repeated its PATH-only missing-tool warning, so the environment-only gate was approved; final-tree canonical lint was rerun successfully below.
- Push: completed at pipeline head `1a5ac7b7` before base retirement prevented automatic PR creation.

After `beta` retirement, guarded `no-mistakes axi sync` preserved both divergent histories and refused an unsafe reset. The reconciliation commit makes this branch descend from the original task head, every pipeline fix head, and current `main`, without force-pushing or dropping commits. The final `main...HEAD` delta contains exactly 20 Better Stack task files.

## Final-tree validation on current main

- `tests/fm-better-stack-incidents.test.sh`: pass, including new incident, duplicate suppression, later-page pagination, unsafe pagination rejection, API error, missing token, authenticated watcher delivery, receipt recovery after queue drain, bootstrap activation/retirement, and idle-home supervision.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh`: pass with pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0.
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`: pass, 67 surfaces and 179 local links.
- `tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh`: pass.
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage`: pass, 100 tests covered across the maintained lanes.
- Shell and JavaScript syntax checks: pass.
- `bin/fm-secrets-check.sh leak-scan`: pass across all 20 changed files.
- `git diff --check`: pass.

## Operator triage

On an incident wake, load `diagnostic-reasoning` before scoping. If the delivery ladder caused the breakage, restore service through rollback first and investigate after recovery. Page the captain immediately only for security-shaped, irreversible, or product-affecting incidents; otherwise include the outcome in the next digest.

title: feat(fleet): federated dispatch, verified harness adapters, and in-place runtime handoff
body:
## Intent

Give firstmate a safe way to move a live ship/scout task from one worker runtime to another when the current one runs out of tokens, without losing the task's work (captain: continuity in coding tasks).

Concrete gap (2026-08-01, us-waves-2-5): Codex exhausted mid-pipeline with unlanded commits; teardown correctly refuses unlanded work; fresh spawn would lease a second worktree and split the task.

Build a supported relaunch-in-place path:
- bin/fm-runtime-handoff.sh: verified exit of current agent, preserve treehouse lease/worktree/branch/commits/uncommitted changes/original brief, rewrite only runtime/endpoint meta fields (preserve pr= etc.), re-deliver brief plus progress note telling replacement to re-attach live no-mistakes run via axi status (never abort/restart pipeline as handoff).
- fm-spawn.sh --reuse-worktree and --handoff-brief: launch half without new lease; refuse live/ambiguous endpoint, secondmate, orca, unverified harness.
- bin/fm-statusline-quota-lib.sh: best-effort statusline parse; unparseable means unknown never exhausted; no auto-migration daemon.
- Refuse rather than guess. Surface that Claude handoff targets share supervising firstmate Claude budget; do not encode policy.
- Tests for success and refusals; docs/skills/AGENTS pointers.

Out of scope: automatic quota monitoring daemon/scheduler/policy layer.

## What Changed

- **Fleet federation and multi-account add-on.** New `bin/fm-fleet.sh` coordinates multiple operators through a shared, cross-uid-safe, git-backed KB (register/heartbeat/leave, queue/claim/handoff/drain/reap, scope routing, token economy). `fm-fleet-quota-lib.sh` plus `quota-sources/{cursor,copilot}.sh` add per-surface headroom and pace readings aligned to the quota-axi 0.1.15 pace model, with `pick`/`models` selecting a surface by model family. `fm-accounts-lib.sh` adds an account registry with three isolation methods and an `--account` spawn axis via the raw-launch escape hatch; `fm-dispatch-select.mjs` makes crew dispatch subscription-aware, failing closed on stale, absent, or malformed telemetry instead of guessing. `fm-handoff-doc.sh` publishes session handoff documents (optionally with a git bundle), `fm-fleet-preflight.sh` reports which tier a home is ready for, and cross-operator behaviour stays behind the opt-in Admiral flag. Documented in `docs/fleet-addon.md`, `docs/fleet-quickstart.md`, `docs/fleet-token-economy.md`, and the `federation` / `multi-account` skills.

- **Verified crewmate adapters and per-project isolation.** Added verified adapters for cline (CLI 3.0.46), cursor-agent (Cursor CLI 2026.07), and copilot (GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.75), each with a folder/trust readiness gate and shared composer idle/glyph defaults, plus empirical evidence files under `docs/verification/`. Worktree acquisition moved to a leased per-project pool placed on the repo's own filesystem, with opt-in per-project session berths (`fm-berth.sh`), derived crew names (`fm-name.sh`), per-operator herdr presentation-lock scoping, uid-namespaced per-task temp roots, and pane-close-before-worktree-return ordering in abort/teardown. Watcher fixes: honour a declared pause when the crew's agent is alive (including the aged-recheck path) and fall back to pane-regex on stale native busy.

- **In-place runtime handoff.** `bin/fm-runtime-handoff.sh` relaunches a live ship/scout task on a different harness inside its existing worktree: it exits the current agent with the adapter's verified exit command, removes only the dead endpoint, rewrites just `harness=`/`model=`/`effort=`/`provider=` and the endpoint fields in `state/<id>.meta` (preserving `pr=` and every other line), and re-delivers the original brief plus a progress note telling the replacement to re-attach the live run via `axi status`. The launch half is `fm-spawn.sh --reuse-worktree` / `--handoff-brief`, which refuses live or ambiguous endpoints, secondmate tasks, orca-backed tasks, unverified harnesses, and `id=repo` batch dispatch rather than leasing a second worktree. `fm-statusline-quota-lib.sh` parses pane-visible quota signals best-effort and reports `unknown` — never `exhausted` — on unparseable input; no monitoring daemon or migration policy is introduced. Covered by `tests/fm-runtime-handoff.test.sh` (success, verified-exit, and refusal paths) alongside new suites for berths, names, dispatch selection, handoff documents, the three new adapters, and the federation surface.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The delta is a bounded set of mechanical corrections that each landed correctly and were verified against their consuming code, plus genuine new coverage for the previously untested verified-exit path, with no behavior change beyond the intended fixes.

## Testing

I ran the change's own suite (17 green), added the two refusals the intent names but the suite lacked — secondmate identity and orca-backed reuse — bringing it to 19 green, and confirmed the suite is actually claimed by the portable-serial CI lane. Because unit passes alone don't show the captain's continuity guarantee, I built an operator demo that replays the exact us-waves-2-5 incident against the real handoff and spawn scripts: the transcript shows codex's own /quit delivered, the treehouse lease log empty (no second worktree), HEAD, branch and both uncommitted files unchanged after the move, meta rewritten to harness=claude/model=opus/effort=high while pr= and pr_head= survive, the handoff prompt carrying the progress note plus the `no-mistakes axi status` re-attach instruction plus the untouched original brief, and three refusals firing with work intact. The adjacent spawn and teardown suites also pass. No UI surface is involved — this is a shell CLI, so the reviewer-visible artifact is the annotated command transcript. Nothing actionable found.

<details>
<summary>Evidence: Operator transcript: codex -> claude handoff on a live task with unlanded work (annotated, full)</summary>

```text

1. Codex runs out of tokens mid-pipeline. This is the live task's state:
$ cat $FM_HOME/state/us-waves-2-5.meta
```

<summary>🔧 **Review** - 8 issues found → auto-fixed ✅</summary>

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-runtime-handoff.sh:357` - The completion status line is written as `printf 'status: working: runtime handoff to %s; ...'`, so the emitted line is `status: working: ...`. The status-file grammar is `<verb>: <note>` and `status_line_verb` (bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:162) takes everything before the FIRST colon — confirmed: this line parses to verb=`status`, note=`working: runtime handoff to ...`. It is therefore not the `working` verb the code intends. fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:1026 reconciles activity entries only when `$e.verb == "working"`, so a handoff's progress event lands as an unrecognized verb and reconciles to `inconclusive` instead of corroborating against active_children. Drop the leading `status: ` so the line reads `working: runtime handoff to <harness>; ...`.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:276` - The intent requires the spawn half to "refuse ... unverified harness": "fm-spawn.sh --reuse-worktree and --handoff-brief: launch half without new lease; refuse live/ambiguous endpoint, secondmate, orca, unverified harness." The reuse guard only checks `[ "$HARNESS_SET" -eq 1 ]`. ARG3 is then set from HARNESS_ARG (line 585) and falls through the raw-launch branch at line 698 (`*' '*)  # raw launch command (unverified-adapter escape hatch)`), which bypasses `launch_template` entirely. So `fm-spawn.sh <id> --reuse-worktree --harness 'claude --some-flag'` relaunches an arbitrary command in the existing worktree holding unlanded work, and records `harness=claude` in meta from the command's basename. fm-runtime-handoff.sh:188-194 does enforce a verified-adapter allowlist, but --reuse-worktree is a documented public surface in its own right (docs/scripts.md:43). Adding `case "$HARNESS_ARG" in *' '*) refuse ;; esac` under the reuse guard would close it, but that narrows an existing escape hatch, so it is the author's call.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:476` - The `id=repo` batch-dispatch branch (line 469) runs before the reuse block and rebuilds `shared_args` from only --harness/--provider/--model/--effort/--backend. `--reuse-worktree` and `--handoff-brief` are silently dropped from the re-exec. The `--handoff-brief requires --reuse-worktree` guard at line 279 runs earlier, so it does not catch this. Invoking `fm-spawn.sh t1=repo --reuse-worktree --harness claude` therefore re-execs as a plain `fm-spawn.sh t1 repo --harness claude`, which takes the treehouse-get path at line 1703 and leases a SECOND worktree for a task that already owns one — exactly the split-task failure this change exists to prevent. Refuse `--reuse-worktree`/`--handoff-brief` in the batch branch (as it already does for --secondmate at line 486).
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-statusline-quota-lib.sh:56` - The verdict loop folds `context` into the same status as the quota percentages, so codex's `Context N% left` (a context-window reading, not a token budget) drives `low` at <=20% and `exhausted` at 0%. That contradicts the guidance the same commit reinforces in .agents/skills/stuck-crewmate-recovery/SKILL.md:52: "A low context reading is not wedging; modern harnesses auto-compact and keep going." A healthy codex worker sitting at 15% context before an auto-compact reports `status=low`, and at 0% reports `exhausted` — the exact false-exhaustion the header at line 11 warns would "migrate a healthy worker for no reason". `context_pct` is already emitted as its own field, so excluding it from the aggregate status loop keeps the signal without the conflation. Whether context should influence the aggregate verdict is a product call.
- ⚠️ `tests/fm-runtime-handoff.test.sh:95` - The verified-exit sequence is the load-bearing safety step of the handoff (send the adapter's exit command, poll wait_for_non_alive, then kill the dead husk — bin/fm-runtime-handoff.sh:244-303), and it has no coverage. Both success cases pass `--skip-exit` (lines 282, 323) and every refusal case either skips exit or refuses before reaching it. The `fm-send-stub` fixture created here is never wired to anything: fm-runtime-handoff.sh:259 invokes `"$SCRIPT_DIR/fm-send.sh"` by absolute repo path, so a PATH-based stub can never intercept it. A test driving the alive -> exit-sent -> dead transition (e.g. via an FM_SEND override or a fake tmux whose pane_current_command flips after send-keys) would cover the branch, and the unused stub should either be wired up or removed.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-statusline-quota-lib.sh:63` - The two scan loops are redundant. The first loop (lines 56-62) sets `low` and may set `exhausted`; when it did not set `exhausted`, the second loop (lines 65-73) resets status to `ok` and re-runs the identical scan minus the `0` case — which can never match anyway, since reaching the second loop proves no sample was 0. Every `low` assignment from the first loop is discarded. Collapse to a single loop that tracks a `saw_zero`/`saw_low` flag, or keep only the first loop's semantics.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-runtime-handoff.sh:282` - `if [ "$SKIP_EXIT" = 1 ] && [ "$STATE_NOW" = missing ]` sits inside the `*)` arm of a case whose earlier arms already matched `dead|missing` and `alive`, so `$STATE_NOW` can only be ambiguous/unreadable/unverified/unknown here and the `= missing` test is never true. The arm is effectively an unconditional refusal (which is the correct behavior); the dead condition just reads as though `--skip-exit` grants an exemption it does not. Reduce it to the plain refusal.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:1585` - fm-runtime-handoff.sh:306 writes `$STATE/$ID.handoff-prompt`, but teardown's explicit `rm -f` list (.status, .turn-ended, .meta, .pi-ext.ts, .grok-turnend-token, .kimi-turnend-token) does not include it, so every handed-off task leaves an orphan file in state/ after teardown. Add `"$STATE/$ID.handoff-prompt"` to that list (and to the secondmate child cleanup at line 1316 if reuse ever reaches it).

🔧 Fix: Fix handoff status verb, batch reuse guard, exit-path tests

title: feat(fleet): federated multi-operator dispatch, per-account isolation, and verified crewmate adapters
body:
## Intent Add agy as a verified firstmate runtime, with gemini-3.6-flash usable as a model on it. Captain asked to add agy and gemini 3.6 flash to the available fleet agent LLMs. Requirements and constraints from the task: - Empirically verify the agy adapter before adding it to the verified list (never dispatch on an unverified adapter). Follow harness-adapters verification procedure. - Binary agy 1.1.9 was confirmed working; wire launch, busy source/delivery signature, trust gate, composer if needed, detection, and harness-adapters knowledge. - Deliberately resolve model/effort overlap: effort is baked into model ids (-low/-medium/-high) AND available as --effort; establish which governs and how they interact. - Empirically establish: busy state, interrupt, exit, resume, trust dialogs, composer shape, brief delivery with -i, env marker/process ancestry. - Prove end-to-end: supervised launch receives brief, works, busy then idle, can be interrupted and exited cleanly. - Do NOT add agy to the verified list on partial evidence. - Do NOT change routing defaults or make agy a default for anything; this only adds an option. - Do not modify unrelated adapters. - Sequencing note: captain earlier asked agy integration follow upstream recommendations after PR #1461 merges; that PR still awaits maintainer approval. Build cleanly and self-contained for later reconciliation; call out in PR body anything upstream might shape differently. - Implementation committed on fm/fm-verify-agy-adapter: launch template and trust gate in fm-spawn, ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT detection before CLAUDECODE in fm-harness, delivery busy regex in fm-tmux-lib, bootstrap/dispatch verified lists, harness-adapters skill, docs/verification/agy-adapter.md, tests/fm-agy-harness.test.sh. Preferred model form: --model gemini-3.6-flash --effort low|medium|high (cap high; omit xhigh/max). Trust is keystroke-only Enter, no pre-seed of operator settings.json. ## What Changed - **Fleet add-on (`bin/fm-fleet*.sh`, `bin/fm-handoff-doc.sh`, `bin/fm-accounts-lib.sh`, `scripts/fleet-root-prereq.sh`)** — federated multi-operator knowledge base with shared-dir claim/lock, routing, and cross-uid-safe paths; operator lifecycle (register/heartbeat/leave/join) and a token economy with cross-operator overflow on exhaustion; a quota/pace surface layer aligned to quota-axi 0.1.15 with authed cursor and copilot usage readers; an account registry with three isolation methods plus a `--account` spawn axis and secure api-key exec shim; shared handoff documents, tier preflight, `fm-fleet-wait.sh`, and an opt-in Admiral flag. Adds `docs/fleet-addon.md`, `docs/fleet-quickstart.md`, `docs/fleet-token-economy.md`, federation/multi-account skills, and a `tests/federation/` suite. - **Verified crewmate adapters (`bin/fm-spawn.sh`, `bin/fm-harness.sh`, `bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh`, `bin/fm-composer-lib.sh`)** — cline 3.0.46, cursor-agent (Cursor CLI 2026.07), copilot (GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.75), and agy (Antigravity CLI 1.1.9) each wired end to end: launch template, busy/idle delivery signature, folder-trust readiness gate, harness detection, and shared composer idle/glyph defaults. agy uses `--model gemini-3.6-flash --effort low|medium|high` (xhigh/max rejected), keystroke-only Enter for trust with no operator settings pre-seed, and `ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT` detection ordered ahead of `CLAUDECODE`. Subscription-aware routing lands in `bin/fm-dispatch-select.mjs` with bootstrap validation that rejects raw or unverified harnesses; every adapter has an evidence file under `docs/verification/`. - **Spawn/session runtime** — per-project leased worktree pools placed on the repo's own filesystem, opt-in per-project session berths with per-berth herdr workspaces and derived crew names (`bin/fm-berth.sh`, `bin/fm-name.sh`, `bin/fm-treehouse-lib.sh`), uid-namespaced per-task temp roots, operator-scoped herdr presentation locks with an overridable wait bound, watcher pause/staleness and lock-identity fixes, teardown pane-close ordering before worktree return, and non-GNU `sed`/`date`/`getent` portability throughout. No routing default changed — agy and the other adapters are opt-in candidates only. Per the sequencing note, this branch is self-contained and does not depend on PR #1461 (subscription-aware crew routing, still awaiting maintainer approval); if upstream reshapes that routing surface, the agy entries in `crew_dispatch_validate` and `fm-dispatch-select.mjs`, and the shared trust-gate helper triples in `fm-spawn.sh`, are the spots that would need reconciling. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The fix round is small, precisely scoped to the three approved findings, adds a regression fence for the trust-gate ordering hazard it resolves, documents the remaining empirical uncertainty honestly, and leaves the adapter opt-in with no routing default changed. ## Testing Ran the 10 targeted suites covering the agy adapter and every neighbouring adapter/wiring surface the change touches — all green, including the copilot test fence repaired in the previous round — then proved the user intent end-to-end against the real binary rather than fixtures: the shipped fm-spawn launch template composed `agy --dangerously-skip-permissions --model 'gemini-3.6-flash' --effort 'low' -i "<brief>"`, the shipped agy_wait_for_trust_clear gate cleared a genuine project-trust dialog in 1s with a single keystroke, the seeded brief auto-ran and the crewmate's own tool child reported HARNESS=agy (proving both delivery and ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT detection), fm_busy_lines_match agy read busy then idle on the live pane, a single Esc interrupted with the session surviving, and /exit exited 0 with a resume id. All seven documented model/effort interaction rules reproduced live and firstmate's builder drops the xhigh/max values agy rejects; the captain-facing crew-dispatch config accepts agy+gemini-3.6-flash while still rejecting over-ceiling effort and unverified harness names, and no routing default or provider map gained agy.
