Both lines need agy added alongside cline/cursor-agent/copilot as crewmate-only. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-agy-harness.test.sh:51` - test_agy_model_and_effort_flags claims to fence agy's presence in the --model allowlist but greps the fixed string '|copilot|agy)', which also occurs at bin/fm-spawn.sh:82 (a usage comment) and :474 (the secondmate bare-name case). Scoping both greps to the extracted agy case arm (the file already does this well for the trust gate via AGY_GATE_SOURCE) would make the fences actually load-bearing. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1611` - With agy added there are now three verbatim-identical helper triples in fm-spawn.sh: cursor_capture / copilot_capture / agy_capture are byte-identical, cursor_spawn_fail / copilot_spawn_fail / agy_spawn_fail are byte-identical, and the three wait loops differ only in predicate names and env-var prefixes - plus three sequential 'if [ "$HARNESS" = X ]' blocks at lines 2103-2120. Noting the tradeoff rather than recommending it here: the task explicitly forbids modifying unrelated adapters, and this codebase deliberately gives each adapter its own constants so no harness can borrow another's identity. title: feat(bin): relaunch a live crewmate on another harness in place
body:
## What Changed

- Added `bin/fm-runtime-handoff.sh`, which exits a live ship/scout with its recorded harness's verified exit command, removes only the dead endpoint, relaunches a verified target harness in the same worktree and lease, and rewrites `harness=`/`model=`/`effort=` plus the new endpoint fields in `state/<id>.meta` while preserving `pr=`, `x_*`, and the rest. It writes a launch-only `state/<id>.handoff-prompt` (progress note plus the unchanged brief, telling the replacement agent to re-attach a live no-mistakes run via `no-mistakes axi status`) and refuses rather than guesses on missing meta or brief, `kind=secondmate`, `backend=orca`, a backend that differs from the recorded one, an unverified target harness, a non-isolated worktree, or an endpoint still alive after the exit budget; `bin/fm-teardown.sh` now removes the prompt file.
- Extended `bin/fm-spawn.sh` with `--reuse-worktree` and `--handoff-brief` as the launch half: it skips treehouse/Orca worktree acquisition, resolves the backend from the task's own meta when `--backend` is omitted, and refuses `--secondmate`, a missing `--harness`, `--handoff-brief` without `--reuse-worktree`, and `id=repo` batch dispatch.
- Added `bin/fm-statusline-quota-lib.sh` and `bin/fm-statusline-quota.sh` for a read-only best-effort capacity signal parsed from the statusline region of a pane capture only — transcript text carrying the same shapes cannot vote, unparseable is `unknown` rather than `exhausted`, and a context-window reading never decides exhaustion. Docs (`docs/architecture.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, `AGENTS.md`) and the `harness-adapters` / `stuck-crewmate-recovery` skills route mid-task runtime changes to the new script, with `tests/fm-runtime-handoff.test.sh` covering quota parsing, every refusal, the live exit path, meta rewrite, and work preservation.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Every error and warning from the prior rounds is verifiably fixed with targeted tests, this round's change is a narrow, well-tested tightening of one parser's input window whose anchoring premise I confirmed against all three capture backends, and only two informational comment/knob consistency items remain.

## Testing

Ran the change's own suite (tests/fm-runtime-handoff.test.sh, 31 assertions) plus the four adjacent suites the diff touches (fm-spawn-batch, fm-spawn-worktree-settle, fm-teardown, fm-documentation-audiences) — all green. Because passing tests alone do not show the operator experience, I also wrote and ran an end-to-end walkthrough that drives the shipped scripts through the actual journey: a claude ship task mid-flight with a landed commit, an uncommitted file, and a live PR in meta; fm-statusline-quota.sh reporting status=exhausted five_hour_pct=0 from the bottom statusline row while correctly ignoring a decoy quota line in the scrollback above it; fm-runtime-handoff.sh delivering /exit, killing only the dead endpoint husk, and relaunching the same task id on codex in the same worktree. Afterwards HEAD is unchanged, the uncommitted file is intact, harness/model/effort are rewritten while pr= and pr_head= survive, treehouse is never called, the original brief is byte-identical and embedded verbatim, and the handoff prompt instructs the replacement to re-attach the existing no-mistakes run rather than start a second one. Four operator-facing refusals (unverified harness, backend switch, batch --reuse-worktree, still-alive endpoint) all fire with clear messages and leave the work untouched. This is a shell/CLI change with no rendered UI surface, so the evidence is a CLI transcript rather than a screenshot. Worktree left clean; evidence lives only in the temp evidence directory.

title: fix(bin): detect wedges from task-bound state instead of pane idleness
body:
## Intent Stop the watcher from reporting a worker as a possible wedge when task-bound current-state evidence proves progress or an intentional wait. The stale detector must distinguish an exact trust/permission dialog, an active validation pipeline or gate, a harness turn in progress, a declared external pause with a live substrate, and the residual genuine possible-wedge case, using the existing fm-crew-state.sh interface rather than duplicating its logic. Active runs, parked gates, live turns, and declared pauses must suppress stale alarms; all disconfirmers must be bound to the task; unrelated heartbeats are not progress evidence. Only state transitions wake firstmate, identical candidates deduplicate across pane churn, and unreadable/unreachable state remains visible as unknown without alarming. Genuine wedges must still fire, including a readable idle worker with no run, gate, turn, pause, or status. Preserve the existing watcher cadence and do not add a poller, falsify paused status, or rework the wake queue, Stop-hook re-arm, turn-end guard, away-mode daemon policy, or secondmate pause cadence. Behavioral replay must suppress all three recorded false alarms while retaining a genuine-wedge alarm, and shared tracked changes must remain documented and tested. ## What Changed - Replaced the watcher's pane-idle wedge timer with a state-specific stale detector: `crew_absorb_class` becomes `crew_supervision_class` in `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh`, mapping one `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` read to `active-run`, `gate`, `harness-turn`, `external-pause`, `possible-wedge` or `unknown`, under a new `FM_CREW_STATE_READ_TIMEOUT` cap so a hung backend classifies as `unknown` rather than as a healthy disconfirmer. `bin/fm-watch.sh` now records each verdict as `:` in `state/.stale-candidate-` and wakes firstmate only on a transition, so identical candidates deduplicate across pane churn and a replacement task reusing the same backend target counts as new. - Bounded every disconfirmer that proves only rendering or readability: a busy pane footer, a `harness-turn` verdict and an unreadable `unknown` verdict now surface once as a turn-bound candidate when the task's own `state/.turn-ended` marker (or its spawn record before any turn completes) passes `FM_BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS`, and a declared external pause sends exactly one `awaiting external` recheck per `FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS` window anchored on status-log mtime. An exact trust dialog wakes for a keystroke; all wakes on these paths are inspection-only. The escalation-count ladder, `demand-deep-inspection` marker, `FM_WEDGE_DEMAND_INSPECT_COUNT` and `stale_is_terminal` are removed. - Rewrote `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` around the new classifier (32 assertions covering the three recorded false-alarm replays, the surviving genuine wedge, candidate dedup, both outer bounds and the trust-dialog wake), and refreshed `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/configuration.md` for the new marker, reason wordings and config entries. Review left one open info note: `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:1216` still matches the retired `idle *s, possible wedge, escalation *` reason shape that no producer emits, exercised only by `tests/fm-daemon.test.sh:153`, and was deferred rather than changed in the documentation phase. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Every disconfirmer in the rewritten stale path now carries a task-bound outer bound with a behavioural replay covering both suppression and escalation, the pause-recheck cadence is shared with the untouched secondmate path and reproduces its prior reason string exactly, and all nine findings raised across the previous rounds are closed with tests and documentation. ## Testing I ran the rewritten watcher-triage suite and the adjacent suites touched by the shared classifier and documentation changes, all passing, then built an end-to-end demo that drives the real watcher and the real fm-crew-state reader over five worker scenarios so the behaviour is visible the way a supervisor experiences it. On an idle, unchanged worker pane past the stale threshold, the watcher stayed asleep with an empty wake queue for an active validation run (absorbed active-run), a run parked at a review gate (absorbed gate), a declared external pause (absorbed external-pause), and a live harness turn, while the genuine wedge (a readable idle worker with no run, gate, turn, or pause) woke firstmate with "stale: demo:fm-wedged (possible wedge: no active run, gate, live harness turn, or declared external pause)" and that exact line was drained from the durable queue. This change is a bash watcher and classifier with no rendered surface, so there is no screenshot or HTML artifact; the CLI transcript of the watcher output and drained wake queue is the end-user-visible artifact. The temporary sandbox was removed and the worktree left clean.

Evidence: Demo harness used to produce the transcript ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # End-to-end demonstration of the task-bound stale detector. # # Drives the REAL bin/fm-watch.sh and the REAL bin/fm-crew-state.sh in a # sandboxed FM_HOME. Only the outside world is faked: `no-mistakes` (the # validation pipeline CLI) and `tmux` (the worker's terminal pane). Every # scenario has an idle worker pane that is already past the stale threshold - # exactly the shape that produced the recorded false alarms. # # What a supervisor actually experiences is printed for each scenario: # - the task-bound current-state line the detector reads # - whether the watcher woke firstmate (its printed reason line) # - what a firstmate turn would drain out of the durable wake queue set -u ROOT=${1:?usage: wedge-demo.sh } SANDBOX=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fm-wedge-demo.XXXXXX") WATCH="$ROOT/bin/fm-watch.sh" DRAIN="$ROOT/bin/fm-wake-drain.sh" CREW_STATE="$ROOT/bin/fm-crew-state.sh" cleanup() { rm -rf "$SANDBOX"; } trap cleanup EXIT seen_sig() { if [ "$(uname)" = Darwin ]; then stat -f '%z:%Fm' "$1"; else stat -c '%s:%Y' "$1"; fi } make_fakebin() { # local fb="$1/fakebin" mkdir -p "$fb" cat > "$fb/no-mistakes" <<'SH' #!/usr/bin/env bash set -u case "${1:-}" in axi) shift; [ "${1:-}" = status ] && printf '%s\n' "${FAKE_RUN:-}" ;; runs) printf '%s\n' "${FAKE_RUNS:-}" ;; esac exit 0 SH cat > "$fb/tmux" <<'SH' #!/usr/bin/env bash set -u case "${1:-}" in list-windows) printf '%s\n' "${FAKE_WINDOW#*:}"; exit 0 ;; capture-pane) cat "$FAKE_PANE"; exit 0 ;; display-message) printf '%%1\n'; exit 0 ;; esac exit 1 SH chmod +x "$fb/no-mistakes" "$fb/tmux" } # scenario [busy|idle] # The optional last argument records a real semantic busy-state event for the # task through bin/fm-busy-event.sh, the harness lifecycle contract's only # writer, so the harness-turn and declared-pause scenarios read the same way # they do for a live Claude crewmate. scenario() { local name=$1 task=$2 status_line=$3 pane=$4 run=$5 busy=${6:-} local dir="$SANDBOX/$name" state wt pid queue verdict head gen state="$dir/state"; wt="$dir/worktree" mkdir -p "$state" "$wt" make_fakebin "$dir" git -C "$wt" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null init -q git -C "$wt" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit -q --allow-empty -m init git -C "$wt" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout -q -b "fm/$task" head=$(git -C "$wt" rev-parse HEAD) printf '%s\n' "window=demo:fm-$task" "worktree=$wt" "kind=ship" "harness=claude" > "$state/$task.meta" if [ -n "$busy" ]; then gen=$("$ROOT/bin/fm-busy-event.sh" arm "$state" "$task") "$ROOT/bin/fm-busy-event.sh" apply "$state" "$task" "$busy" --gen "$gen" \ --source claude-hook --event "$busy" >/dev/null fi printf '%s\n' "$status_line" > "$state/$task.status" # This status line was already delivered on an earlier wake, so the demo # exercises the stale path rather than re-surfacing the same signal. seen_sig "$state/$task.status" > "$state/.seen-${task}_status" printf '%s' "$pane" > "$dir/pane.txt" export FAKE_WINDOW="demo:fm-$task" FAKE_PANE="$dir/pane.txt" export FAKE_RUN="${run//@HEAD@/$head}" FAKE_RUNS="" printf '\n================================================================\n' printf 'SCENARIO: %s\n' "$name" printf ' worker pane (idle, unchanged, past the stale threshold):\n %s\n' "$pane" printf ' last status line: %s\n' "$status_line" verdict=$(PATH="$dir/fakebin:$PATH" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$state" "$CREW_STATE" "$task") printf ' fm-crew-state.sh %s -> %s\n' "$task" "$verdict" PATH="$dir/fakebin:$PATH" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$state" FM_POLL=1 FM_SIGNAL_GRACE=1 \ FM_CHECK_INTERVAL=999999 FM_HEARTBEAT=999999 "$WATCH" > "$dir/watch.out" 2>"$dir/watch.err" & pid=$! local i=0 while [ "$i" -lt 120 ]; do kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break sleep 0.25 i=$((i + 1)) done if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then printf ' watcher after %ss: STILL SLEEPING on the fleet (firstmate not woken)\n' "$((i / 4))" kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true; wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true else printf ' watcher: WOKE FIRSTMATE and exited\n' fi if [ -s "$dir/watch.out" ]; then printf ' wake reason printed to the supervisor:\n' sed 's/^/ | /' "$dir/watch.out" else printf ' wake reason printed to the supervisor: (none)\n' fi queue=$(FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$state" "$DRAIN" 2>/dev/null || true) if [ -n "$queue" ]; then printf ' durable wake queue drained by the next firstmate turn:\n' printf '%s\n' "$queue" | sed 's/^/ | /' else printf ' durable wake queue drained by the next firstmate turn: (empty)\n' fi printf ' triage log:\n' sed 's/^/ | /' "$state/.watch-triage.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -3 || true } RUN_RUNNING='run: id: "01RUN" branch: fm/validating status: running head: "@HEAD@" pr: "" findings: none steps[2]{step,status,findings,duration_ms}: intent,completed,0,0 review,running,0,0' RUN_PARKED='run: id: "01RUN" branch: fm/at-gate status: awaiting_approval awaiting_agent: parked 2m10s head: "@HEAD@" pr: "" findings[1]{id,severity,file,line,action,description}: r1,error,b.go,,ask-user,changes product behavior gate: review' printf 'Task-bound stale detection, end to end (real fm-watch.sh + real fm-crew-state.sh)\n' # --- recorded false alarms: each must stay silent ----------------------------- scenario false-alarm-1-validation-running validating \ 'working: handed the branch to validation' \ 'implementing the fix > ' "$RUN_RUNNING" scenario false-alarm-2-parked-at-gate at-gate \ 'working: handed the branch to validation' \ 'implementing the fix > ' "$RUN_PARKED" scenario false-alarm-3-declared-external-pause waiting-upstream \ 'paused: waiting on the upstream API quota reset' \ 'waiting on upstream > ' '' idle scenario disconfirmer-live-harness-turn thinking \ 'working: reading the failing test' \ 'running the suite esc to interrupt' '' busy # --- the genuine wedge: must still fire --------------------------------------- scenario genuine-wedge wedged \ 'working: implementing step 2' \ 'idle prompt after an unfinished step > ' '' idle printf '\n================================================================\n' printf 'Done.\n' ```

## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:363` - `unknown` is absorbed silently and permanently by the stale path, which removes wedge detection entirely for whole harness classes. Chain: `crew_supervision_class` maps `unknown:*` to `unknown` (bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:105); `fm-crew-state.sh:592` emits `state: unknown · source: pane · harness state unavailable (...)` and exits there, so the status-log fallback is never reached; `fm_busy_classify` returns `unknown kimi-unverified` / `unknown codex-unverified` (bin/fm-busy-lib.sh:270,276) for every Kimi and Codex crew, because `fm_busy_kimi_verified` tests an empty `FM_BUSY_KIMI_VERIFIED_VERSIONS` and both `fm_busy_codex_appserver_observable` and `fm_busy_codex_hooks_verified` hard-`return 1`. It also returns `unknown missing` / `unknown gen-mismatch` / `unknown source-mismatch` for any crew whose busy record is absent or stale. Failure sequence: a Codex worker with no attributed no-mistakes run (i.e. the whole pre-validation coding phase) wedges on an idle pane; `window_is_busy` is false so the pane is stale; `crew_supervision_class` returns `unknown`; `handle_state_specific_stale` writes the candidate marker and only `triage_log`s, forever. Before this change the same crew returned `none` from `crew_absorb_class` and was surfaced immediately by `surface_nonterminal_stale`. This contradicts the intent's required "Genuine wedges must still fire, including a readable idle worker with no run, gate, turn, pause, or status", while the intent's "unreadable/unreachable state remains visible as unknown without alarming" was clearly aimed at the `unknown:none` cases the new test covers (`unreadable current-state source`, malformed output, missing attribution, unreachable reader) rather than `unknown:pane`. Suggested boundary: treat `unknown:pane` (harness busy state unavailable on a readable pane) as `possible-wedge`, or add a distinct class for it, and cover it in `test_crew_supervision_class_classifier`. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:336` - The costly current-state read now runs on every poll for every stale window, not once per newly-seen stale hash. `handle_state_specific_stale` is called from line 853 on each cycle where `n >= 2` and the pane is not busy, and it unconditionally calls `crew_supervision_class` -> `$FM_CREW_STATE_BIN`, which shells out to `no-mistakes` / `axi status` under a 10s bound (`FM_CREW_STATE_NM_TIMEOUT`, bin/fm-crew-state.sh:73). The removed code guarded this with `if [ "$(cat "$sf")" != "$h" ]`, so the read happened only on a new stale hash; `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:74-76` still tells callers not to run it on every wake. Failure scenario: a crew validating on CI (the exact false-alarm case this change fixes) sits stale for 20 minutes with POLL=15, producing ~80 bounded `no-mistakes` subprocess trees per window instead of one, multiplied across the fleet, and a slow/hanging `axi status` stretches each supervision cycle by up to 10s per stale window. If this cost is accepted deliberately, say so; otherwise re-add a bounded re-read throttle (e.g. skip the read when the last read for this key is younger than N seconds) that still lets transitions be detected. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:837` - `BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS` / `busy_turn_over_age` are deleted and `FM_BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS` is removed from docs/configuration.md, so a busy pane is again an unbounded wedge disconfirmer with no duration cap. Line 837 gates all stale triage on `busy_now -ne 0`, so a busy pane never reaches `handle_state_specific_stale` at all. The deleted code's own comment recorded the failure mode it existed for: a hung foreground tool call keeps rendering a changing busy footer while no turn ever completes. Failure scenario: a worker's harness blocks forever inside a foreground tool call, its pane keeps reporting busy, its `state/<id>.turn-ended` marker never advances, and no stale alarm is ever raised (previously it escalated once the turn-end marker reached 3600s, inspection-only). The intent lists "a harness turn in progress" as a disconfirmer but does not authorise making it unbounded, so confirm this removal is intended rather than collateral of the ladder deletion. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:334` - `state/.stale-candidate-<key>` is written but never removed by any reset or cleanup path, and unlike the markers it replaces it is deliberately hash-independent so it cannot self-heal. `clear_pause_tracking` (bin/fm-watch.sh:263) and the daemon's `clear_pause_tracking` (bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:472-474) both clear `.stale-`, `.stale-since-` and `.wedge-escalations-` but not `.stale-candidate-`, and fm-teardown.sh:1542 removes only task-keyed files. Failure scenario: task `feat-x` wedges, fires `possible-wedge`, and the marker is committed; the task is torn down and respawned, taking the same backend target `sess:fm-feat-x` and therefore the same key; the fresh worker wedges again; `crew_supervision_class` returns `possible-wedge`, which equals `previous`, so line 346 returns early and no alarm ever fires for the new worker. Secondary effect: one orphan file per retired window accumulates in `state/` indefinitely. Fix by adding `.stale-candidate-$key` to both `clear_pause_tracking` implementations and to teardown, or by storing `<task>:<class>` in the marker so a task change counts as a transition. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:416` - `stale_is_terminal` now has no production caller: the diff removed its only call site in bin/fm-watch.sh, and neither fm-supervise-daemon.sh nor any other bin/ script references it. Only tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh:81-92 still exercises it. Failure scenario: no runtime failure, but a shared-library function plus its test suite now describe triage policy the watcher no longer applies, which is the same drift the library header warns about. Either delete the function with its test, or note in the header why it is retained for a future consumer. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:100` - The mid-file header block still states the pre-change invariant for the stale path: "The no-verb signal / stale path is absorb-only-when-provably-working ... a crew that stopped its turn with no running pipeline and no busy pane is SURFACED" (lines 100-106). After this change that holds only for the no-verb signal path; the stale path now absorbs `unknown` and `external-pause` without any provably-working evidence. The top-of-file block (lines 12-19) and line 107-108 were updated but this paragraph was not. Failure scenario: a future reader trusts the stated invariant and assumes an unknown-state crew still surfaces, reintroducing the swallowed-finish class this file exists to prevent. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:334` - The watcher-internals inventory in AGENTS.md:114 was not updated for this change: it does not list `.stale-candidate-*` (the one new durable marker this change introduces) and still lists `.wedge-escalations-*`, which no code writes any more (only `rm -f` references remain at bin/fm-watch.sh:345, 858, 866). The intent requires that shared tracked changes remain documented; docs/architecture.md:17 documents the new marker but the state-file inventory does not. Failure scenario: an operator or cleanup script reading AGENTS.md as the inventory of watcher state misses `.stale-candidate-*` and either leaves it out of a reset or clears a marker it believes is still live. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:867` - `task=$(window_to_task "$w" "$STATE")` at line 867 is a leftover from the removed pause-reconciliation block: `task` is already set at line 808 for the same iteration and is not read anywhere in this branch (the only remaining statement is `[ -e "$pf" ] && clear_pause_tracking "$w"`). Failure scenario: no incorrect behaviour, just a redundant subshell and metadata scan on every changed-hash poll for every window, and a misleading suggestion that the branch depends on the task id. 🔧 Fix: bound busy and unknown stale disconfirmers by completed turn 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:437` - After the outer bound was added for `harness-turn` and `unknown`, `external-pause` is the one remaining disconfirmer that can silence an ordinary worker indefinitely. `handle_state_specific_stale` absorbs `external-pause` with no turn-marker check (line 437 case arm), and `handle_paused_stale` (the bounded `PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS` recheck) is now reachable only from the secondmate branch at line 942, so no ordinary worker ever gets a pause recheck in normal mode. The heartbeat backstop cannot cover it either, because `paused` is deliberately excluded from `FM_CAPTAIN_RE`. Failure scenario: a worker appends `paused: waiting on upstream review`, its pane stays readable and idle so `fm-crew-state.sh` keeps emitting `paused · status-log`, the upstream wait resolves or was mistaken, and firstmate is never told - the first round's docs/architecture.md removed the line that recorded this exact property ("A declared external wait trades that silence for one bounded recheck per pause window, so a forgotten pause cannot remain invisible indefinitely"). Note the intent authorises a declared pause as a disconfirmer but does not say it may be unbounded, and a dead substrate is already covered (fm-crew-state falls back to `unknown · none`, which the new bound now escalates). Options: apply the same `busy_turn_over_age` bound to `external-pause`, or restore the ordinary-worker `PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS` recheck through the candidate dedup. Not a blocker - your round-1 instruction scoped the bound to busy and unknown, so this is flagged for a decision rather than assumed. 🔧 Fix: bound declared pauses with one recheck per window 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:464` - Recording an interaction between the two bounds rather than a defect. A legitimately paused ordinary worker reaches `external-pause` only while the semantic busy contract returns an exact `idle` verdict, because fm-crew-state.sh:587-594 emits `unknown · pane` and exits before the status-log fallback for any other verdict. Failure scenario: a worker declares `paused: waiting on upstream`, sits idle for two hours, and its busy record is retired or goes gen-mismatched (fm_busy_record_read returns `gen-mismatch`, so fm_busy_classify yields `unknown gen-mismatch`); the class flips from `external-pause` to `unknown`, and because the task has completed no turn while paused, `busy_turn_over_age` is true and line 465 promotes it to `turn-bound`, so firstmate gets "no completed turn in Ns, past the 3600s bound, while its harness reported a live turn or no readable state at all" instead of the `awaiting external` recheck. This is the correct fail-toward-visible direction (firstmate genuinely cannot confirm the pause substrate is live), the wake is inspection-only and honestly worded, and it follows directly from the bound you asked for on `unknown`, so no change is proposed - it is noted because neither docs/architecture.md nor the configuration entry mentions that a pause whose busy record lapses surfaces under the turn-bound reason rather than the pause-recheck reason.

title: feat(bin): add guarded Pi-on-Herdr primary custody and exact recovery
body:
## Intent

Make a Pi-on-Herdr Firstmate primary recoverable without guessing or duplicating. Reconcile attach-first by exact recorded Herdr session/workspace/tab/pane identity; persist private canonical home, exact full Pi session id/path/directory/cwd, Herdr endpoint, and PID-start-bound lifetime lease custody; strictly reject malformed, duplicate, missing, noncanonical, non-regular, symlinked, header-mismatched, or cwd-mismatched session authority; resume only the full exact Pi ID from its exact recorded cwd with no interactive, partial, create-on-miss, label, focus, or ambient-session selectors; refuse live, unknown, contradictory, raced, or ambiguous ownership; bound exact named-server retries; require post-launch exact-session attestation before accepting input or reporting recovery; and fall back to attach-only/manual recovery whenever proof is incomplete. Every generated restored-pane command must safely preserve canonical paths containing POSIX shell metacharacters, including an apostrophe, with executable recovery coverage. Attach must pin the exact named session over contradictory ambient state, and every recovery or lease-handoff guard must be atomically published with complete PID/start identity so interruption cannot create an ownerless permanent blocker. Include idempotent reversible local files for a one-shot future-login server ensure and explicit phone/local attach helper, but do not install, enable, or configure login, remote access, Tailscale, or SSH. Keep schemas and state-machine mechanics in script headers, operator behavior in classified docs, test executable interfaces rather than source bytes, preserve unsupported axes as manual, and do not touch the live default Herdr fleet or real Pi session files. Update and freshly review the existing PR rather than opening a duplicate.

## What Changed

- Adds `bin/fm-primary-pi.sh` (`launch`, `recover`, `status`, `server-ensure`, `attest`) and the `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-custody.ts` Pi-side witness, which record private custody, lease, recovery-lock, and attestation state under `state/primary-pi/` and reconnect attach-first by exact recorded Herdr session, workspace, tab, and pane identity.
- Restart is allowed only from the full exact Pi session id in its recorded cwd, behind strict session-file validation, two matching idle-shell proofs, atomically published PID/start-bound lease and recovery guards, and post-launch exact-session attestation; the generated restored-pane command shell-quotes canonical paths (apostrophes included) and pins `FM_HOME`, `FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE`, and `FM_STATE_OVERRIDE`.
- Adds `bin/fm-primary-pi-install.sh` for idempotent, reversible, marker-owned local files (a next-login `server-ensure` plist and a `firstmate-attach` helper) that never call `launchctl` or touch login, SSH, or Tailscale settings and refuse paths carrying plist/shell metacharacters; wires both entrypoints into the gate-refusal guard, registers the three new suites in `bin/fm-test-run.sh`, and documents operator behavior and limits in `docs/herdr-backend.md`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The commit replaces the last non-atomically-published private object with the publication primitive already used by every guard, pins the resume environment in both directions, and corrects the status label, leaving no reachable ownerless-blocker path and no stale readers of the old lease layout.

## Testing

Targeted suites for primary custody, recovery, the installer, and the Pi custody extension all pass, and I demonstrated the intent end-to-end with an operator transcript driving the real scripts against a sandboxed fake Herdr and Pi in a home whose path contains an apostrophe: launch persists complete exact custody plus a PID/start-bound lease, a live primary is attach-first with duplicate launch refused, a simulated crash leaves a bare restored shell that recovery resumes by full exact Pi id from its exact recorded cwd, the verbatim generated pane command keeps every apostrophe path safely quoted and the resumed Pi lands in that directory, attestation reports ok before success, attach pins the recorded named session over an ambient contradictory one and a decoy focused workspace, corrupt and duplicate session authority both refuse, and install/uninstall are idempotent and reversible while never calling launchctl, SSH, or Tailscale and never writing the operator's real home. This is a shell CLI surface with no rendered UI, so no screenshot or visual artifact applies; the CLI transcript is the end-user-visible surface. The Pi extension typecheck test gate-skipped locally because no global tsc is installed, and typechecking is static analysis excluded from this phase, so CI owns that axis; the extension's runtime behavior is still covered by the passing node-driven custody extension tests.

```text
      printf '{"result":{"type":"pane_process_info","process_info":{"pane_id":"%s","shell_pid":10,"foreground_process_group_id":20,"foreground_processes":[{"pid":20,"argv0":"pi","name":"pi"}]}}}\n' "$TEST_PANE"
    else
      printf '{"result":{"type":"pane_process_info","process_info":{"pane_id":"%s","shell_pid":10,"foreground_process_group_id":10,"foreground_processes":[{"pid":10,"argv0":"-zsh","name":"zsh"}]}}}\n' "$TEST_PANE"
    fi
    ;;
  'agent attach') printf '%s\n' "${HERDR_SESSION-unset}" > "$TEST_ATTACH_ENV_FILE" ;;
  'pane run')
    # Record the exact generated restored-pane command, then run it the way the
    # restored pane would: from another directory, with a stray state override.
    printf '%s\n' "$4" > "$TEST_PANE_CMD_FILE"
    (cd / && env FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$TEST_STRAY_STATE" bash -c "$4") >> "$TEST_RESUME_LOG" 2>&1 &
    ;;
  *) printf '{"error":{"code":"unexpected"}}\n'; exit 1 ;;
esac
SH
chmod +x "$FAKEBIN/herdr"

cat > "$FAKEBIN/pi" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u
printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "$TEST_PI_LOG"
pwd -P > "$TEST_PI_CWD_FILE"
trap 'printf "shell\n" > "$TEST_MODE_FILE"; exit 0' TERM INT HUP
actual_id=${TEST_ATTEST_ID:-$TEST_FULL_ID}
pi_start=$(ps -o lstart= -p $$ | awk '{$1=$1; print}')
"$FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE/bin/fm-primary-pi.sh" attest \
  --token "$FM_PRIMARY_PI_TOKEN" --actual-id "$actual_id" \
  --session-file "$TEST_SESSION_FILE" --session-dir "$TEST_SESSION_DIR" \
  --cwd "$TEST_CWD" --pi-pid $$ --pi-start "$pi_start" --reason startup \
  $( [ "$FM_PRIMARY_PI_RECOVERY" = 1 ] && printf '%s' --recovery ) || exit 1
printf 'pi\n' > "$TEST_MODE_FILE"
while :; do sleep 1; done
SH
chmod +x "$FAKEBIN/pi"

FAKE_PS="$T/fake-ps"
cat > "$FAKE_PS" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
case "$*" in
  "-axo pid=,ppid=") printf '1 0\n10 1\n' ;;
  "-p 10 -o stat=") printf 'Ss\n' ;;
  *) exit 1 ;;
esac
SH
chmod +x "$FAKE_PS"

# Same documented test-harness escape hatch tests/lib.sh exports: this demo drives
# the real scripts against a temp-sandbox fleet from a gate worktree.
export FM_GATE_REFUSE_BYPASS=1
export PATH="$FAKEBIN:$PATH"
export FM_HERDR_PS_BIN="$FAKE_PS"
export FM_BACKEND_HERDR_IDLE_SHELL_PROOF_POLLS=2
export FM_HOME="$HOME_FIXTURE"
export FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$ROOT"
export FM_PRIMARY_HERDR_BIN="$FAKEBIN/herdr"
export FM_PRIMARY_SERVER_ATTEMPTS=2 FM_PRIMARY_SERVER_DELAY=0.02
export FM_PRIMARY_ATTEST_ATTEMPTS=100 FM_PRIMARY_ATTEST_DELAY=0.02
export HERDR_ENV=1 HERDR_SESSION='lab-exact' HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$SOCKET"
export HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID="$WORKSPACE" HERDR_TAB_ID="$TAB" HERDR_PANE_ID="$PANE"
export TEST_HERDR_LOG="$LOG" TEST_MODE_FILE="$MODE" TEST_SESSION='lab-exact' TEST_SOCKET="$SOCKET"
export TEST_PANE="$PANE" TEST_WORKSPACE="$WORKSPACE" TEST_TAB="$TAB"
export TEST_FULL_ID="$FULL_ID" TEST_SESSION_FILE="$SESSION_FILE" TEST_SESSION_DIR="$SESSION_DIR" TEST_CWD="$T"
export TEST_RESUME_LOG="$T/resume.log" TEST_PI_LOG="$T/pi.log" TEST_PI_CWD_FILE="$T/pi.cwd"
export TEST_ATTACH_ENV_FILE="$T/attach.env" TEST_PANE_CMD_FILE="$T/pane-run.cmd"
STRAY_STATE="$T/stray pane state"; mkdir -p "$STRAY_STATE"
CLEAN=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fm-demo-clean.XXXXXX"); CLEAN=$(cd "$CLEAN" && pwd -P)
export TEST_STRAY_STATE="$STRAY_STATE"

SCRIPT="$ROOT/bin/fm-primary-pi.sh"
INSTALLER="$ROOT/bin/fm-primary-pi-install.sh"
CUSTODY="$HOME_FIXTURE/state/primary-pi/custody.v1"
LEASE="$HOME_FIXTURE/state/primary-pi/lease"
LAUNCH_PID=''

cleanup() {
  local held pid
  for held in "$LEASE"; do
    [ -f "$held" ] || continue
    pid=$(grep '^pid=' "$held" | cut -d= -f2-)
    kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  [ -n "$LAUNCH_PID" ] && kill -TERM "$LAUNCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  sleep 0.3
  rm -rf "$T" "${CLEAN:-/nonexistent-clean}"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

say() { printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$*"; }
run() { printf '\n$ %s\n' "$*"; "$@" 2>&1; }
wait_for() { local i=0; while [ "$i" -lt 200 ]; do "$@" && return 0; sleep 0.05; i=$((i+1)); done; printf '(timed out waiting)\n'; return 1; }
lease_live() { [ -f "$LEASE" ] && [ "$(cat "$MODE")" = pi ]; }
lease_gone() { [ ! -e "$LEASE" ] && [ "$(cat "$MODE")" = shell ]; }

# Redact the machine-specific temp prefix so the transcript stays readable while
# keeping the apostrophe-bearing leaf visible.
redact() { sed "s#$CLEAN#<TMP>/fm-demo-clean#g; s#$T#<TMP>/fm-demo-captain's-recovery#g; s#$ROOT#<WORKTREE>#g"; }

{
printf "Guarded Pi-on-Herdr primary recovery, operator transcript\n"
printf "Canonical home lives under a path containing an apostrophe: fm-demo-captain's-recovery\n"

say "1. Ordinary wrapped launch takes lifetime custody"
"$SCRIPT" launch --pi pi > "$T/launch.out" 2>&1 &
LAUNCH_PID=$!
wait_for lease_live
printf '\n$ cat state/primary-pi/custody.v1\n'; cat "$CUSTODY"
printf '\n$ cat state/primary-pi/lease\n'; cat "$LEASE"
run "$SCRIPT" status

say "2. A live primary is attach-first and a duplicate launch is refused"
run env FM_PRIMARY_NO_ATTACH=1 "$SCRIPT" recover
printf '\n$ %s launch --pi pi   # second wrapper, same pane\n' "$SCRIPT"
"$SCRIPT" launch --pi pi 2>&1; printf '(exit %s)\n' "$?"

say "3. The primary dies; the pane is left as a bare restored shell"
printf '\n$ kill -TERM %s   # simulated crash or restart of the primary wrapper\n' "$LAUNCH_PID"
kill -TERM "$LAUNCH_PID"; wait "$LAUNCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true; LAUNCH_PID=''
wait_for lease_gone
run "$SCRIPT" status

say "4. Exact recovery resumes the full Pi id in the recorded pane"
run env FM_PRIMARY_NO_ATTACH=1 "$SCRIPT" recover
printf '\n$ cat <the exact command fm-primary-pi.sh generated for the restored pane>\n'
cat "$TEST_PANE_CMD_FILE"
printf '\n$ cat state/primary-pi/attestation.v1\n'; cat "$HOME_FIXTURE/state/primary-pi/attestation.v1"
printf '\n$ cat <cwd the resumed Pi actually started in>\n'; cat "$T/pi.cwd"
printf '\n$ cat <argv of every Pi this demo started: first the fresh launch, then the resume>\n'; cat "$T/pi.log"
run "$SCRIPT" status

say "5. Attach pins the exact recorded named session over ambient state"
printf '\n$ %s recover   # herdr status reports focused_workspace_id=decoy-workspace\n' "$SCRIPT"
env HERDR_SESSION='ambient-contradictory-session' "$SCRIPT" recover 2>&1
printf '\n$ cat <HERDR_SESSION seen by the herdr agent attach process>\n'; cat "$T/attach.env"
printf '$ tail -1 <herdr call log>\n'; tail -1 "$LOG"

say "6. Damaged session authority refuses instead of guessing"
printf '\n$ kill -TERM <resumed primary>   # back to a bare restored shell\n'
kill -TERM "$(grep '^pid=' "$LEASE" | cut -d= -f2-)" 2>/dev/null || true
wait_for lease_gone
printf '\n$ printf %s >> sessions/target.jsonl   # truncated JSONL record\n' "'{broken'"
printf '{broken\n' >> "$SESSION_FILE"
printf '$ %s recover\n' "$SCRIPT"
env FM_PRIMARY_NO_ATTACH=1 "$SCRIPT" recover 2>&1; printf '(exit %s)\n' "$?"
printf '\n$ <restore sessions/target.jsonl to the valid two-record session>\n'
write_session
head -1 "$SESSION_FILE"
printf '\n$ cp sessions/target.jsonl sessions/duplicate.jsonl   # ambiguous session id\n'
cp "$SESSION_FILE" "$SESSION_DIR/duplicate.jsonl"
printf '$ %s recover\n' "$SCRIPT"
env FM_PRIMARY_NO_ATTACH=1 "$SCRIPT" recover 2>&1; printf '(exit %s)\n' "$?"
rm -f "$SESSION_DIR/duplicate.jsonl"

say "7. Reversible local convenience files, nothing installed or enabled"
printf '\n$ %s install   # with the apostrophe-bearing home: refuses rather than emit unsafe files\n' "$INSTALLER"
env FM_PRIMARY_INSTALL_HOME="$T" "$INSTALLER" install 2>&1; printf '(exit %s)\n' "$?"
export FM_PRIMARY_INSTALL_HOME="$CLEAN/install-home"
export FM_HOME="$CLEAN/firstmate-home"
mkdir -p "$FM_PRIMARY_INSTALL_HOME" "$FM_HOME"
run "$INSTALLER" install
run "$INSTALLER" install
run "$INSTALLER" status
printf '\n$ cat ~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.firstmate.primary-herdr.plist\n'
cat "$FM_PRIMARY_INSTALL_HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.firstmate.primary-herdr.plist"
printf '\n$ cat ~/.local/bin/firstmate-attach\n'
cat "$FM_PRIMARY_INSTALL_HOME/.local/bin/firstmate-attach"
run "$INSTALLER" uninstall
run "$INSTALLER" status
printf '\n$ ls ~/Library/LaunchAgents ~/.local/bin\n'
ls -A "$FM_PRIMARY_INSTALL_HOME/Library/LaunchAgents" "$FM_PRIMARY_INSTALL_HOME/.local/bin" 2>&1
printf '\n$ grep -nE "launchctl|tailscale|ssh |ssh-|systemctl" <installer + recovery scripts>   # only prose, no invocation\n'
grep -nE 'launchctl|tailscale|ssh |ssh-|systemctl' "$INSTALLER" "$SCRIPT" || printf '(no matches)\n'
printf '\n$ ls "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.firstmate.primary-herdr.plist"   # the operator real home was never written\n'
ls "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.firstmate.primary-herdr.plist" 2>&1 || true

printf '\nend of transcript\n'
} 2>&1 | redact | tee "$OUT/primary-recovery-transcript.txt"
```

title: feat(bin): add agy (Antigravity CLI) as a verified crewmate harness
body:
## Intent Add agy as a verified firstmate runtime, with gemini-3.6-flash usable as a model on it. Captain asked to add agy and gemini 3.6 flash to the available fleet agent LLMs. This revision is rebased onto upstream/main (kunchenguid/firstmate) so a gate-raised PR contains ONLY the agy adapter commit (11 files, ~670 lines), not the captain-fork main delta. Requirements: empirically verify before adding to verified list; model/effort interaction (base requires --effort; baked suffixes work; conflict fails closed; cap high); busy esc-to-cancel; Esc interrupt; /exit resume; project-trust keystroke gate (past-trust first); -i brief auto-run; ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT before CLAUDECODE. No routing defaults. No unrelated adapters. Opt-in only. Implementation: fm-spawn launch+trust gate, fm-harness, fm-tmux-lib busy, bootstrap verified lists, harness-adapters skill, docs/verification/agy-adapter.md, tests/fm-agy-harness.test.sh, configuration/architecture docs. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-spawn.sh` gains an agy launch template (`--dangerously-skip-permissions … -i `), a post-launch project-trust keystroke gate (`agy_wait_for_trust_clear` — positive past-trust anchor first, single Enter, answered at most once), `--model` support, and effort resolution that caps `xhigh`/`max` at agy's `high` ceiling for base model ids while withholding `--effort` when the id already bakes a `-low`/`-medium`/`-high` suffix. agy is refused on `--secondmate` at all three resolution paths (bare name, `--harness=`, `config/secondmate-harness` chain), since `backends/tmux.sh` carries no agy liveness signature. - `bin/fm-harness.sh` detects agy via `ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT=1` checked before `CLAUDECODE`, plus an anchored argv fallback so substrings like "legacy" cannot false-positive; `bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh` adds the `esc to cancel` busy regex; `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` adds agy to the verified-adapter list with `low|medium|high` effort validation. - Adds `tests/fm-agy-harness.test.sh` (21 checks, registered in `fm-test-run.sh`) and `docs/verification/agy-adapter.md` recording the live P1–P7 model/effort probe matrix, trust-gate, interrupt, and `/exit` resume behavior on agy 1.1.9; `AGENTS.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and the `harness-adapters` skill are updated to state agy is crewmate-only with no routing defaults. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: All prior findings are resolved, the model/effort invariant now holds across the full documented probe matrix with a behavioral test enforcing it, and the only residual is an error-message diagnostics nicety on a path that already points the operator at the real error. ## Testing Ran the new agy adapter suite (21/21 ok) plus the adjacent secondmate, dispatch-profile, tmux-busy, composer, kimi, grok and documentation-audience suites, all green, then proved the intent end-to-end against the live Antigravity CLI 1.1.9: a real tmux crewmate launch built by fm-spawn's own launch template and flag resolvers for `harness=agy model=gemini-3.6-flash effort=xhigh` rendered `--effort high` (clamp visible as "Gemini 3.6 Flash (High)"), the cold project-trust dialog was cleared by the readiness gate with exactly one Enter, the seeded `-i` brief auto-ran and matched the `esc to cancel` busy signature, the agent ran fm-harness.sh and answered `HARNESS=agy` proving ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT detection from inside a real agy tool child, a single Esc produced the Interrupted marker, and `/exit` printed the `agy --conversation=<uuid>` resume handle; the P1-P7 model/effort matrix and firstmate's emitted argv for every tier were replayed against real agy, and crew-dispatch validation confirmed agy is accepted only when explicitly configured with an in-range effort. title: Pipeline `rebase` step uses the project's configured base — wrong base for a fork-to-upstream PR
body:
**What**
The pipeline's `rebase` step rebases onto the project's configured base. For a fork-to-upstream (direct-PR) project that's the fork's `main`, not the upstream the PR targets — so it lands on the wrong base, can never resolve the real conflict, and still looks like progress.

**Why**
A worker rebased a direct-PR branch onto the fork's `main` while the PR targeted `upstream:main`; the head could never have resolved the conflict. It also keeps drifting back into conflict as upstream moves.

**Shape (non-prescriptive)**
For direct-PR/fork projects, rebase onto the PR's actual upstream base; pick the correct base by ancestry (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) rather than by project config or recency.

**Context**
I maintain a fork-to-upstream PR against one of your repos and hit exactly this. Happy to contribute the PR via no-mistakes.

title: Make Lavish captain boards permanent and durable
body:
## Summary

Makes the Lavish captain surface a permanent property of the fork while preserving its bounded durable file protocol: no server, listener, resident process, shared browser profile, or shared port.

## Captain requirements

- Per-item annotations: boards capture question notes and comments keyed by individual option values, and `lavish-axi collect` persists them as first-class schema-version-2 answer data.
- Picture and screenshot spots: visual evidence under each decision `visuals/` directory renders inline as self-contained data URLs.
- Relvino design system: the fork vendors the dark-default Relvino tokens, including Inter, Ruby green, blue-500 `#007AFF`, semantic aliases, and 16px cards.
- Separate browser with no leaks: `bin/fm-lavish-board.sh` opens a named headed `chrome-devtools-axi` session with a throwaway profile; the fork itself remains bounded and serverless.
- Captain-shell operation: the helper resolves its co-located Lavish fork and accepts an explicit Firstmate home, without depending on `FM_HOME` or a stale global install.

## Durable-submission defect fixed

The first implementation persisted submission only in `window.__lavishPayload` plus the `LAVISH-SUBMIT v2` document-title marker. If the page closed before the polling check read that live JavaScript state, if the captain submitted in a different browser, or if polling had not run yet, the complete answer disappeared without a trace. That exact failure lost the captain a full board of answers tonight.

The submit handler now serializes the complete structured payload, builds a JSON `Blob`, creates an object URL, and clicks a synthetic download anchor named `lavish-answer-<decision-id>.json` before emitting the live-page marker. The done screen also shows the formatted raw JSON in a read-only selectable textarea when downloads are blocked. No `localStorage` fallback was added because `file://` access can throw `SecurityError`.

The one-shot checker searches fresh deterministic downloads first, atomically copies a matching payload into its declared durable state destination, and only falls back to the live-page marker when no download exists. It accepts browser collision suffixes while rejecting stale, malformed, and wrong-decision files.

## Closed-page proof

A real self-contained `file://` board was opened in an isolated headed Chrome session. I selected the durable-download option, entered a question note, an option comment, and an overall note, reviewed the batch, and submitted it. Chrome wrote `lavish-answer-closed-page-proof.json`. I then opened a blank tab, closed the actual board tab, confirmed only `about:blank` remained, and ran the checker afterward. The checker recovered the downloaded JSON into the durable payload destination with the selected value and all three annotations intact.

In other words: a submitted answer is recoverable after the page is closed. This directly covers the failure that lost the captain a full board of answers tonight; the proof did not read `window.__lavishPayload` from a live board.

## Other validation

- `bash tests/fm-lavish-board.test.sh` passed, including a closed-page download-first test that makes live-page evaluation fail if attempted.
- Focused board DOM/contract coverage passed before the final ordering-only change; a later rerun hit the known host-load `ps ENOBUFS` test-harness failure rather than a product assertion.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh bin/fm-lavish-board.sh tests/fm-lavish-board.test.sh tests/lib.sh` passed with pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0.
- `node --check tools/lavish/src/board.mjs` and `git diff --check` passed.

## Deliberately not built

- No server, listener, resident collector, filesystem watcher, shared port, or access to the captain main Chrome profile.
- No `localStorage` transport.
- No mutation of existing live decisions.
- No automatic answer acceptance without `lavish-axi collect` manifest validation.

This PR must not be merged without captain approval.

title: feat(bin): add durable process-event supervision
body:
## Intent

Ship a green replacement for old PR https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/1446 from branch fm/pr1446-current-main-replacement-r2, based on the current default branch, delivered through the already-open PR https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/1483. Preserve that open PR and every commit already on the branch, including the prior pipeline fix commits. Do not close, replace, or merge either PR.

Content-equivalent provenance is explicitly accepted. Literal Git ancestry to old PR head 2d013d0c22c8c937a90721a203fafc0f8e390f19 is explicitly not required. Retain every accepted prior PR 1446 pipeline fix in content, together with the complete corrected process-event behavior from protected reviewed head 1c624d30340d26840a4f0fcfaf42e8cc6bf156ea. Exclude rejected head 65c9667372ad4191b97924a8398ee8eafcb46b95, stale literal-ancestry enforcement, obsolete validation-history changes, and unrelated conflict-resolution artifacts.

PRIMARY CORRECTION FOR THIS RUN. A runner is its own process group leader and starts the blocking source inside that group, while the claim records only the leader PID and its process identity. A leader that dies while its owned group is still running must never be classified as a stale generation. SIGKILL of the runner leader alone must not permit stale-claim reconciliation to release ownership or start a second poller against one canonical source. The old generation's child process group must be safely terminated before its claim is released and any replacement starts. If generation-bound group ownership cannot be proved, or another home owns the claim, preserve the claim and refuse for retry rather than starting another source. A public-interface regression must cover the exact crash cut: start one blocking source through reconcile, SIGKILL only the detached runner leader, prove the old process group survives, reconcile again, and prove the old group is gone and no second source process runs. Retain counterexamples for a truly stale generation with no leader and no surviving group, a live matching owner, a reused mismatched PID, and uncertain identity.

Preserve all adjacent guarantees: one identity-matched owner per canonical source across homes; safe stale recovery when neither runner nor owned group remains; PID-reuse protection that never signals an unrelated process or process group; generation-bound claim release; bounded output and staging cleanup; and normal retire, missing-registration reconciliation, and home sweep cleanup.

Every durably captured source-and-sequence result must remain eligible for bounded re-announcement on the existing durable wake queue until a durable handled acknowledgement exists. Draining a wake before handling and then starting a replacement Firstmate session must resurface the same exact source and sequence without placing result payload text in an event line.

Handled acknowledgement must be generation-keyed, private, path-safe, durable, and idempotent. An acknowledgement may exist only after matching captured result and adapter records exist. A premature or mistyped acknowledgement must be rejected so it cannot suppress a future result. The owned handling interface must atomically check and deduplicate by exact source and sequence so an acknowledged effect is never authorized twice. Repeated acknowledgement must be safe and must never authorize a second handled effect. Publication must be serialized with acknowledgement under the shared per-source boundary so a concurrent reconcile cannot append a wake after handling wins. The handled marker must be created privately and fail safely when private mode cannot be secured. Lavish lifecycle classification must read the leading response envelope so prompt payload text cannot spoof a missing session. All four of these are already validated on this branch and must be preserved.

Turn-end and watcher supervision use one shared FM_SUP_NEEDED predicate across every supported primary tool, including X-mode-only homes. This unified behavior is an explicit accepted captain decision, not an accidental side effect or unrelated behavior: one consistent liveness invariant applies to every event source that requires active Firstmate supervision. Do not restore the prior tool-specific split and do not file it as a corrective follow-up.

Preserve the explicit source-side Lavish loss limitation. Do not claim generic exactly-once effects across a crash between an external effect and its acknowledgement.

Keep the authoritative skill, script help, operating documentation, and active verification evidence accurate and proportionate, including wherever they describe when ownership may be released relative to the runner-owned process group. Require focused process-event tests, all relevant Firstmate tests, bin/fm-lint.sh, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh, and every other current repository-required check. Keep changed shell scripts shellcheck-clean.

Do not add a second notifier, another owner, a polling control plane, automatic retry machinery, a dispatch-efficiency change, a remote-secondmates change, or unrelated behavior. Keep old PR https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/1446, every old branch, run, head, ref, isolated copy, and every remote-secondmates artifact unchanged. Do not reset, force, discard, or clean up preserved artifacts.

This is exactly one brand-new normal validation run on this branch. Never use rerun and never use --yes. Drive it through the existing PR 1483 and green CI, escalating only a genuinely new captain decision or blocker.

## What Changed

- Add a generic process-event runner and Lavish adapter that capture bounded private results and re-announce them through the durable wake queue until acknowledged by exact source and sequence.
- Enforce generation-bound ownership per canonical source, including PID reuse protection and runner process-group cleanup before recovery, retirement, or secondmate teardown.
- Unify watcher supervision for in-flight tasks, X-mode polling, and registered event sources, with operating documentation and public-interface regression coverage.

title: fix: close crewmate brief status-reporting gaps

## Intent Fix three status-reporting gaps in the crewmate brief scaffold produced by bin/fm-brief.sh. All three were observed across five crewmates in one session on 2026-07-28 and are brief-scaffold problems, not worker problems, so the fix belongs in the generated contract rather than in steering. Gap 1 - premature done: four separate no-mistakes workers appended done: after their own tests passed, without running the pipeline; one worker's own recap read 'Next: run /no-mistakes to validate and ship the PR' while its status already said done. The scaffold must make it unmissable that under no-mistakes, done means PR open with checks green, never a clean local commit. Gap 2 - stale status while parked on a backgrounded pipeline call: workers background the respond call, go idle, and leave the previous needs-decision: line standing, so supervision reads them as blocked on a decision already given while the quiet pane raises a stale alarm about once a minute. The remedy that worked: append paused: while parked and switch back to working: when it returns. Gap 3 (highest value) - a bare resolved: line leaves no readable state: bin/fm-crew-state.sh returns 'state: unknown, source: none' for a healthy worker whose latest line is a keyed resolved: event, because that verb carries no state. The worker becomes invisible rather than merely misreported and is indistinguishable from a dead endpoint. It recurred twice on 2026-08-01 (tasks tsa-396-postgres-flow-sources and arkrh-corpus-types-unbound-unconstructible), where the run lookup also returned nothing so both sources failed at once. Rule: always follow resolved: with a state line. Accepted approach and constraints: change the generated contract so the correct behavior is the obvious one, sharpening the existing status-protocol section rather than appending a new section or a wall of prose a worker would skim past; cover each of the three with a test against the generated brief text so a future scaffold edit cannot silently drop them; do not weaken or remove any existing safety clause, especially the worktree-isolation assertion. A separate concurrent task, fm-crew-state-blind-during-fix-round, fixes the reader side in bin/fm-crew-state.sh, so bin/fm-crew-state.sh and bin/fm-classify-lib.sh must not be edited here; keeping the two diffs disjoint matters because two branches touching the same files already collided once tonight. title: test: eliminate watcher peer startup race
body:
## Intent Fix the pre-existing flake in tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh, which was reported as a beacon-timing flake and reproduces on origin/main. Required approach was: reproduce in a loop of at least 50 iterations and record the baseline failure rate first; root-cause the specific racing timing assumption; fix the race rather than masking it (explicitly NOT by widening a sleep, adding a retry loop around an assertion, or loosening an assertion until it passes); wait on the actual condition rather than elapsed wall-clock time; then re-run the same 50-iteration loop and show 0 failures. Investigation result: despite the 'beacon-timing' framing, the beacon and lock-identity paths were ruled out by instrumentation. The real cause is a peer STARTUP race in the fixture test_watch_restart_attaches_to_healthy_peer. It launches a supposedly TERM-resistant node peer, records it as the watcher lock holder, and expects fm-watch-arm.sh --restart to attach to it. node is not actually TERM-resistant until the interpreter has evaluated process.on('SIGTERM'), and the restart sends TERM milliseconds after launch. When the peer lost that race it died on the default disposition, so the lock named a dead pid, the fresh child legitimately stole it, and the arm honestly reported 'watcher: started pid=N (beacon fresh)'. Instrumentation captured peer_alive=no with the recorded identity and beacon intact, which is what ruled out the beacon/identity hypotheses. The fix has the peer announce that its SIGTERM handler is installed, and the fixture waits on that exact condition (a readiness file) before recording the lock and arming. No assertion was loosened, no sleep widened, no retry wrapped around an assertion. The 200-iteration 0.05s readiness poll is a bounded wait on the real condition with an explicit failure message, not a blind sleep. Evidence: before, 50 runs from a pristine 'git archive HEAD' copy of origin/main under identical load, 10/50 failed, all of them this peer race. After, same command and load, 0/50. Also 0/50 in 50 consecutive one-at-a-time runs. All 10 suites selected by bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed pass, and bin/fm-lint.sh is clean. Deliberate scope decision by the captain, so it should not be flagged as an omission: while chasing this I separately found and fixed a real defect in bin/fm-watch.sh - the watcher ignores TERM/HUP for the remainder of its poll interval because bash defers a trapped signal until the running foreground command finishes, measured at 14.68s at the 15s default poll, which exceeds the 5s restart budget in fm-watch-arm.sh --restart. That verified fix plus its regression test were deliberately EXCLUDED from this PR to keep it scoped to the fixture race, on the captain's explicit decision, and are preserved as data/firstmate-watcher-lock-flake/term-hup-latency.patch for a separate follow-up task. Do not fold watcher changes into this PR. One methodology note in the commit message is deliberate and load-bearing: early loop runs were launched under nohup, which sets SIGHUP to SIG_IGN; an ignored disposition is inherited through fork and exec and cannot then be trapped, so kill -HUP inside test_arm_hup_cleans_child_and_temp_output became a no-op and produced a false 50/50 failure rate. That warning is recorded so the next person re-running this loop does not repeat it. ## What Changed - Make the TERM-resistant Node test peer publish a readiness file after installing its SIGTERM handler. - Wait for that exact readiness condition before recording the peer as lock holder and restarting the watcher, with an explicit timeout failure. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The narrowly scoped fixture change closes the demonstrated startup race by waiting on the exact handler-readiness condition, while preserving all behavioral assertions and avoiding production watcher changes. ## Testing The author-recorded baseline was 10 failures in 50 runs on origin/main; this phase independently exercised 50 full watcher-lock suites under six-way load and observed 0/50 failures, with the healthy-peer attach behavior present in every transcript and no test-created worktree changes. This is a CLI-only test-fixture change, so CLI transcripts rather than visual UI evidence were captured.
Evidence: 50-run healthy-peer attach evidence `healthy-peer attach summary: passes=50 failures=0` ```text target commit: 3db0341fbc750bae8f94024c3e21296ab515080b command shape: seq 1 50 | xargs -P 6 ... bash tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh (no nohup) assertion: ok - watch restart attaches to a verified healthy peer and later surfaces a successor gap iteration 01: PASS - verified healthy-peer attach iteration 02: PASS - verified healthy-peer attach iteration 03: PASS - verified healthy-peer attach iteration 04: PASS - verified healthy-peer attach iteration 05: PASS - verified healthy-peer attach iteration 06: PASS - verified healthy-peer attach iteration 07: PASS - title: fix: make watcher poll waits interruptible
body:
## Intent Fix the firstmate watcher ignoring TERM and HUP for a full poll interval, which overruns the restart budget. THE DEFECT: bin/fm-watch.sh ended each supervision cycle with a blind foreground `sleep "$POLL"`. Bash defers a trapped signal until the running foreground command returns, so the watcher was deaf to TERM/HUP/INT for the remainder of the interval and exit latency tracked FM_POLL exactly. The signal-grace linger had the same shape. bin/fm-watch-arm.sh --restart allows the outgoing watcher only 50 iterations of `sleep 0.1` (a 5s budget) before forking a replacement, so at the 15s default a restart forked a second watcher while the first was still alive and holding the lock; the replacement then saw a live holder and stood down, and the restart never produced the fresh watcher it reported wanting. This is the shape behind repeated 'restart did not attach to the healthy peer' behavior. It is distinct from the test-fixture startup race fixed separately. REQUIRED APPROACH (all followed): reproduce the latency measurement on this base and record the number in the commit message; start from a preserved verified fix rather than reimplementing it, understanding it rather than treating it as a black box; verify the signal is honored well inside the 5s restart budget and that a restart attaches to a healthy peer rather than starting a second watcher; keep the preserved regression test or replace it with a stronger one. MEASUREMENT reproduced on base 1e24757 against an isolated temporary home, signalling a watcher that had already taken its lock and entered its cycle wait. Before -> after: FM_POLL=1 TERM 0.54s -> 0.05s; FM_POLL=5 TERM 4.54s -> 0.06s; FM_POLL=15 (default) TERM 14.53s -> 0.06s; FM_POLL=15 HUP 14.52s -> 0.06s. These numbers are the whole argument for the change and are deliberately in the commit message and in docs/verification/supervision.md. THE FIX: run the cycle wait and the signal-grace linger as a tracked background child and `wait` on the named pid, so the trap runs the moment the signal lands. Same wait budget, no change to polling cadence or wake classification. The EXIT path reaps the sleep child rather than orphaning it (verified empirically: no leaked sleep child after a mid-interval stop). This is the preserved fix; I reviewed and agree with its approach, and adjusted its comment to the numbers measured on this base. ACCEPTANCE CRITERION THAT SHAPED THE DESIGN: watcher liveness and wedge detection must not be weakened - a watcher that has genuinely stopped must still be detected. This is the constraint that could turn this fix into a worse bug, so it is covered explicitly by a test asserting the heartbeat beacon keeps advancing across cycle waits and then freezes once the watcher stops. DELIBERATE SCOPE DECISION - the herdr push path is knowingly NOT fixed. event_wait_or_sleep's herdr reader waits inside a foreground command substitution, so a push-capable home remains up to FM_POLL deaf to its own stop signal. That reader owns a fifo directory and a child reader process that it removes on its own return path, so interrupting it from the caller would leak both on every stop - exactly the 'worse bug' the acceptance criteria warn against. Fixing it needs reader-side teardown as its own change. This limit is documented at the call site and in docs/verification/supervision.md; it is a deliberate boundary, not an oversight. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: another task touches bin/fm-watch.sh in the stale-wake suppression logic around the pane-hash guard. This change deliberately stays in the signal-handling and poll-wait path and does not touch stale-wake suppression. REGRESSION COVERAGE in tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh, all confirmed to fail or hold against the unpatched watcher: (1) the preserved test - watcher exits on TERM well inside a 10s budget at FM_POLL=60, fails unpatched with 'watcher ignored TERM for its whole poll interval'; (2) new - --restart hands the lock to a fresh live watcher within the arm's own 5s budget with no overlap between outgoing and incoming, fails unpatched; (3) new - liveness beacon advances while cycling and freezes once stopped, holds both before and after as a guard against trading exit latency for a watcher that keeps its lock while no longer cycling. CHERRY-PICKED DEPENDENCY: commit 3db0341 'fix(tests): wait for the TERM-resistant peer before restarting the watcher' is cherry-picked from PR 1487 (https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/1487). It is not this PR author's work, and the two PRs therefore deliberately share a commit. It is carried because this branch's base lacks it, and without it tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh flakes roughly half the time at test_watch_restart_attaches_to_healthy_peer for a reason unrelated to this change; PR 1487 is blocked on an upstream maintainer with no timeline, and shipping a knowingly unstable test signal fails the standing bar that a red result must always mean something. MERGE ORDERING CONSEQUENCE: if 1487 lands first this becomes a duplicate that git will reconcile, and if this PR lands first then 1487 shrinks. With it cherry-picked, the previously flaky case ran 12/12 green and the full suite is 33 assertions clean. VERIFICATION RUN: bin/fm-lint.sh clean, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh clean, all 10 suites selected by bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed passed, full tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh green at 33 assertions. REPO CONVENTIONS: firstmate tracked material follows one sentence per line in Markdown, plain dash never em dash, shellcheck-clean bin scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh, tests colocated in tests/ extending the existing suite, and no agent name as a commit co-author. ## What Changed - Make watcher poll and signal-grace waits interruptible by TERM, HUP, and INT, reaping the tracked sleep child during cleanup so restarts can hand off within their 5-second budget without changing polling cadence or liveness detection. - Add regression coverage for prompt termination, restart lock handoff, and heartbeat continuity; document measured latency improvements and the remaining herdr push-path limitation. - Cherry-pick commit `3db0341` from [PR #1487](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/1487) to stabilize the TERM-resistant peer fixture. This is not the author's work and is intentionally shared: if #1487 lands first Git will reconcile the duplicate, while if this PR lands first #1487 will shrink. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: the change is narrowly scoped, preserves watcher cadence and liveness semantics, explicitly documents the authorized Herdr limitation, and adds targeted regression coverage for prompt termination and restart handover. ## Testing The supplied baseline reported lint, documentation checks, all 10 changed suites, and 33 watcher assertions clean; this phase independently passed the focused watcher-lock suite and real-process TERM, HUP, signal-grace, restart-handoff, child-reaping, lock-cleanup, and heartbeat checks. This is a process/CLI change, so reviewer-visible evidence is a CLI transcript rather than an image.
Evidence: End-to-end watcher evidence `TERM/HUP cycle waits: 4 ms; TERM signal-grace: 4 ms; restart handoff: 158 ms with no overlap; sleep children and locks cleaned; heartbeat advanced while running and froze after stop.` ```text Firstmate watcher end-to-end evidence commit=c46e3b1febb00bec0cf395bb66d3ffad8fa87124 TERM cycle-wait: latency=4ms exit=1 lock=cleared sleep_child_reaped=yes HUP cycle-wait: latency=4ms exit=1 lock=cleared sleep_child_reaped=yes TERM signal-grace: latency=4ms exit=1 lock=cleared sleep_child_reaped=yes restart: latency=158ms old_pid=2138403 new_pid=2138572 old_alive_when_new_owned_lock=no new_alive=yes restart CLI: watcher: started pid=2138572 (beacon fresh) restart cleanup: replacement_alive=no lock=cleared heartbeat: advanced_while_running=yes frozen_after_stop=yes lock=cleared result=PASS (all latency, handoff, cleanup, and liveness checks met) ```
