Usage: fm-procevent.sh register -- ... fm-procevent.sh start fm-procevent.sh reconcile fm-procevent.sh handled fm-procevent.sh retire fm-procevent.sh sweep-home [--preflight] fm-procevent.sh list register Record a source: its adapter, its canonical id, and the exact argv to execute. argv is stored one argument per line and executed directly, so there is no shell surface and no argument splitting. Adapters register sources; nothing here parses user text. start Claim the source, run its child to completion, durably capture the output, publish normalized wakes for pending results, then release the claim. It blocks for as long as the source blocks and is meant to run as a supervised background process, never in a conversational turn. After publishing, it asks the source's own adapter whether the captured result ends the source and retires the registration when it says so, so a source that has ended stops being restarted. reconcile Idempotent liveness entry the watcher calls on its ordinary cycle: republish every durably captured result with no handled acknowledgement yet - regardless of any earlier publication - and start a runner for any registered source that has no live owner. This is liveness repair only - it never discovers results by polling the source, because the child blocks on the source itself. handled Durably and idempotently record that a captured result has been fully handled: . Prints "handled: id seq" the first time for that exact source-and-sequence generation and "already-handled: id seq" on every repeat call, atomically deduplicated so a paired external effect is never authorized twice. Until this is called, the result stays eligible for bounded re-announcement on every reconcile. Marking a result handled does not retire its source registration or claim. retire Drop a registration, stop a runner this home owns, release the claim. Idempotent, and still the supported explicit path after a source has already retired itself on its adapter's terminal verdict. sweep-home Retire a bounded snapshot of this home's registrations and owned claims, then refuse unless no registration, runner record, or owned claim remains. Used by supported Firstmate home retirement. list Show registered sources, owners, and pending captured results. Terminal knowledge is adapter-owned. This runner never inspects a result and never names an adapter-specific status: it calls `bin/fm-procevent-.sh terminal ` and treats exit 0 as the only terminal verdict. A missing command, an error, or any other exit keeps the registration armed, so an adapter that has no notion of ending needs no change. Ownership is machine-wide per canonical source, because separate Firstmate homes can share one underlying source store. A live owner is never displaced; only a claim whose whole generation is gone is reclaimed. A runner leads its own process group, so a crashed leader whose group still has members is not stale: reconcile stops that surviving group and releases its generation before any replacement starts, and keeps the claim for a later retry when it cannot. Durability boundary: see bin/fm-procevent-lib.sh. This runner proves capture before publication and bounded re-announcement until handled, and nothing about the source side of the handoff. Public commands refuse symlinked or non-directory state/procevent leaves, and refuse a symlinked per-source record, rather than reading or writing process-event data outside the effective home. Each command is held to the leaves it can actually touch, so `retire` and `sweep-home` - which only reach the registry and the machine-wide claim root - stay usable when the inbox alone is damaged, and teardown is never stranded by damage it does not touch. [exit=2] ```
Evidence: Grok legacy adapter passes the warning through on an allow $ echo <stop payload> | bin/fm-turnend-guard-grok.sh WARNING: process-event state is not private to this home: .../home/state/procevent is a symlink or not a directory. ... [exit=0] forced resume processes started: none (warning never forces a continuation) ```text Grok legacy Stop adapter, home with a symlinked state/procevent. Before: this path piped the guard stderr into a resume buffer and discarded it on a non-exit-2 allow. $ echo | bin/fm-turnend-guard-grok.sh WARNING: process-event state is not private to this home: /tmp/fm-grok-demo/home/state/procevent is a symlink or not a directory. Every bin/fm-procevent.sh command that reaches that path refuses this home until it is an ordinary directory, so registered sources cannot be started, reconciled, or published. [exit=0] forced resume processes started: none (warning never forces a continuation) ```
Evidence: Targeted suite results after the jq setup fix ```text FM_TEST_END tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=8844 gate_skip=false ... ok - fm-turnend-guard --claude: containment notices are once per episode, never muted across sessions ... ok - fm-turnend-guard --claude: a symlinked containment latch is neither written through nor trusted ... ok - .opencode primary plugin: an allow reports unserviceable process-event state without a prompt ... ok - .pi primary extension: an allow reports unserviceable process-event state without a follow-up FM_TEST_END tests/fm-procevent.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=52430 FM_TEST_END tests/fm-guard-stale-banner.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=2097 FM_TEST_END tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=918 FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=3 failed=0 skipped_gate=0 ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 3 infos - ℹ️ `bin/fm-guard.sh:157` - The new containment banner in bin/fm-guard.sh prints unconditionally on every run, unlike the sibling WATCHER DOWN alarm in the same file, which uses fm_guard_claim_stale_banner/fm_guard_stale_banner_seen to emit the full banner once per episode and a one-line reminder afterwards. fm-guard.sh is invoked by fm-send.sh, fm-spawn.sh, fm-wake-drain.sh, fm-update.sh, fm-promote.sh, fm-pr-check.sh, fm-review-diff.sh, fm-merge-local.sh, fm-fleet-sync.sh and fm-config-push.sh, so a home with damaged process-event state emits a 7-line bordered banner into the tool output of essentially every fleet command until an operator repairs it. The stated rationale ("say it here before any supervision-need shortcut can exit silently") is equally satisfied by the existing episode-latch pattern, which would preserve loudness on first announcement while avoiding per-command flooding. Flagging rather than changing, because always-on was documented deliberately in docs/configuration.md, docs/turnend-guard.md and docs/verification/process-event-sources.md and is asserted by tests. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh:324` - docs/turnend-guard.md states that the block-budget record "repairs the path instead, because refusing to record there would strand the budget below its cap and walk the session toward Claude's 8-block override". The repair is `rm -f`, which removes a planted symlink or fifo but silently fails on a directory. With a directory at state/.turnend-claude-blocks, guard_record_writable stays false, no count is ever persisted, COUNT is recomputed as 1 on every turn and never exceeds BLOCK_BUDGET, so the guard blocks every single turn and never reaches its degraded allow - exactly the stranding the doc says this path avoids. This is the pre-existing behavior for a directory (the old `> "$BUDGET_FILE"` also failed), so it is not a regression; only the doc claim is now broader than the code. - ℹ️ `.opencode/plugins/fm-primary-turnend-guard.js:34` - The OpenCode containment report calls client.tui.showToast({ body: { message, variant: "warning" } }), and the only exercise of that shape is the hand-written mock in test_opencode_plugin_surfaces_containment_warning_on_allow, which accepts any payload. There is no vendored @opencode-ai SDK in the tree and no other showToast call site to cross-check the request shape against. If the real client rejects that shape, the call throws, the catch resets reportedContainmentWarning, and OpenCode operators silently never see the warning on the allow path - falling back to fm-guard.sh on the next fleet command. That degradation is safe and is already recorded as a compatibility limit in docs/turnend-guard.md, so this is a noted verification gap rather than a defect.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-procevent.test.sh tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` (first run: 1 failure, traced to missing jq) - Reproduced the failing scenario manually with `bash -x bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh` and confirmed the identical exit-0 fail-open at base commit cd73e75e via `git archive` — environment gap, not a regression - Placed a static jq 1.7.1 on PATH, then re-ran `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` — 65/65 ok, exit 0 - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-procevent.test.sh tests/fm-guard-stale-banner.test.sh tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` — all ok, exit 0 - Manual E2E: `fm-procevent.sh register|list|reconcile|retire|sweep-home` against a home whose `state/procevent-inbox` is a symlink outside the home - Manual E2E: `FM_HOME=<home> bin/fm-guard.sh` and the `FM_GUARD_READ_ONLY=1` variant on a damaged home, plus a healthy home for the negative case - Manual E2E: `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh --claude` driven over 8 Stop payloads covering repeat turns, a new session id, a missing session id, repair, recurrence, and a changed damaged path - Manual E2E: `bin/fm-turnend-guard-grok.sh` legacy path with a fake `grok` on PATH to prove stderr passthrough with no forced resume - Manual E2E: `bin/fm-procevent.sh --help` to confirm the containment contract renders and is not truncated
⚠️ **Document** - 1 info - ℹ️ `docs/architecture.md:67` - docs/architecture.md:67 summarizes bin/fm-guard.sh as warning on "primary checkout tangled, tasks in flight with a dead watcher, or queued wakes" and does not mention the new unserviceable-process-event-state banner. I deliberately left it: the sentence is a non-exhaustive architecture-level summary and is not contradicted by the change, while docs/scripts.md (script inventory) and docs/configuration.md (contract owner) both already carry the fact. Adding it there would synchronize a third prose copy, which the placement policy forbids. Flagging as a judgment call in case the repo prefers that summary to enumerate every guard alarm.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: feat(bin): open a promotion record PR on promote and add the multi-account dispatch pool
body:
## Intent The captain asked, in their words: 'make sure to also create pr when running /promote'. This is a deliberate change of standing policy for the PropPlane keeper ladder: until now the proplane-ladder skill said 'Never open a PR unless the captain explicitly asks', and the captain has now explicitly asked, so opening a pull request becomes part of the normal promote flow and that contradicting rule had to be removed rather than left in place for the tooling to violate by design. Decisions made while doing the work, so the diff does not read as surprising: - The PR is opened at the prakrit -> main step only, deliberately, because that is the real review point where integrated work leaves the captain's test branch for preview and live. A PR at the agent-branch step would be noise and one at main -> production would restate an already-reviewed commit. This was the captain's explicit instruction. - The PR is a RECORD, not a second gate. It must not stop or delay the promotion. It is opened immediately BEFORE the fast-forward of main, because the fast-forward is exactly what closes it as merged; a PR opened after the push would sit open against a base that already contained the range. Nothing waits for a review or merge, by design. - Failing to open the PR must NOT abort a promotion that already succeeded. The captain's instruction was explicit: warn clearly and continue. So every GitHub failure path (auth, rate limit, an existing PR for the same range, gh-axi absent, and a timed-out call) returns non-zero from the library, and the promote script warns and steps over it. Losing the record is recoverable; leaving main and production diverged because a GitHub API call failed is worse. This is why the PR call is deliberately NOT wired into the script's error-exit paths and why open_promotion_pr never exits the process. - Idempotency is by reusing the open prakrit -> main PR: a re-run updates that PR's title and body rather than opening a duplicate. Once the ladder fast-forwards main, GitHub closes the PR as merged, so the next promotion of a new range correctly finds nothing open and creates its own record. An empty commit range opens nothing at all. - --dry-run prints the PR it would open and makes no GitHub call, on both the step script and the full ladder script. - GitHub access goes through gh-axi, per this repo's AGENTS.md, not through raw gh. - The PR body deliberately states the promoted commit range, the security-review outcome (with the report evidence pointer), and the no-mistakes validation outcome, so a later reader knows what went live and on what evidence. Skipped gates are recorded as SKIPPED so a --skip-gates promotion can never read later as a validated one. Two earlier runs of this pipeline reviewed this branch and its owner decided every finding. Those decisions are SETTLED and their fixes are ALREADY APPLIED in the no-mistakes(review) commits on this branch. Do not re-open them and do not report them as absent: - ACCEPTED AS-IS, deliberately not changed: on the --validate-only resume path the promotion record states that the security review was not re-run in that invocation and carries no report pointer. - APPLIED: the recorded range is computed from the integrate branch this promotion was actually built on, never from a fresh read of origin/prakrit, so the body can never list commits the promotion does not push. - APPLIED: when the fast-forward of main fails after the record was opened, the record is annotated so it never asserts a promotion that did not happen; the annotation is best-effort and never masks the original failure exit. It fires only when main did NOT land, so a failure in the post-push sandbox realignment leaves an accurate record alone. - APPLIED: the body carries only the security report's sha-keyed filename, never an absolute local path. - APPLIED: every gh-axi call is bounded by timeout or gtimeout when present, unbounded only when neither is installed, and a timed-out call warns and continues like any other failure. - APPLIED: the new proplane and ladder entrypoints are registered in docs/scripts.md. - APPLIED: the capped commit listing carries a truncation marker. - APPLIED: the PR-reuse path requires a matched PR's title to mark it as a promotion record before overwriting it, and the listing is wide enough for that scan to actually find the record; an unrelated open PR for the same head and base is never rewritten. A record whose number could not be read is warned about rather than silently left unannotated. The two prior runs both died on agent infrastructure errors (API connection closed, agent exit status 1), not on anything in this branch. This run is a restart of the same validated work, and the branch already carries both fix rounds. Constraints that were honored and should not be flagged as omissions: the keeper-branch rule that fm/* and feature branches are never pushed to GitHub still stands and nothing else about PR policy changed; no existing guard was weakened, in particular fm_proplane_assert_resettable and the refusals that protect uncommitted work in a sandbox or integration worktree are untouched; the repo style rules from the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill were followed (one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash, shellcheck-clean bin scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh, colocated tests under tests/, no agent co-author on the commit). New tests are colocated in tests/fm-proplane-promote-pr.test.sh per this repo's convention and cover the body contents, create and reuse, the GitHub-failure and missing-tool paths, both dry runs, the empty range, end-to-end promotions including the required failure path where the PR cannot be opened but main still lands, an ordering proof that the record is opened while main is still behind prakrit, and that the ladder and promote instructions no longer contradict the tooling. The PR for this change targets the fork PrakritR/firstmate, not upstream: this is captain-specific PropPlane ladder tooling, not an upstream contribution. Known pre-existing issue that this change did not introduce and deliberately did not fix, to avoid widening scope: bin/fm-lint.sh reports two findings on files identical to the default branch - SC2317 in bin/fm-proplane-agent-branches-lib.sh line 17 and SC2016 in tests/fm-open-url.test.sh line 38. Neither file was touched by this change. ## What Changed - Adds the PropPlane keeper-ladder entrypoints under `bin/` (`fm-proplane-promote-prakrit-to-main.sh`, `fm-proplane-promote-full.sh`, `fm-proplane-promote-to-prakrit.sh`, `fm-proplane-security-review.sh`, `fm-prakrit-sync-agent-branches.sh`, dev-server/worktree/branch helpers) plus `bin/fm-proplane-promote-pr-lib.sh`, which opens a promotion-record PR through `gh-axi` at the prakrit → main step, immediately before the fast-forward of `main` that closes it as merged. The record states the promoted commit range (computed from the integrate branch the promotion was actually built on), the security-review outcome with its sha-keyed report filename, and each gate's outcome with skipped gates marked `SKIPPED`; it reuses an existing open record instead of duplicating, reconciles the PR head against the promoted range so the body never claims a close-as-merged it cannot deliver, and annotates the record when the fast-forward does not land. Every GitHub failure path (auth, rate limit, missing `gh-axi`, timeout) warns and lets the promotion continue, all `gh-axi` calls are bounded by `timeout`/`gtimeout` when available, and `--dry-run` previews the record without making any GitHub call. The `promote` and `proplane-ladder` skills replace the old "never open a PR" rule with this standing order. - Adds a multi-account dispatch pool: `bin/fm-pool.sh` and `bin/fm-pool-failover.sh` rotate new spawns across declared agent accounts with per-account cooldowns and a rotation lock, wired into `bin/fm-spawn.sh` (recording `pool_backend=` in task meta) and inert unless `config/dispatch-pool.json` exists. Also verifies `cursor` as a crewmate/scout adapter — launch flags, model-id-encoded effort, per-worktree `.cursor/hooks.json` turn-end hook written only when untracked and removed on teardown, workspace-trust handling, API-key preflight, and a `--secondmate` refusal. - Documents both in `docs/dispatch-pool.md`, `docs/examples/dispatch-pool.json`, `docs/scripts.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and the README skills table, and adds colocated coverage in `tests/fm-proplane-promote-pr.test.sh` (41 cases, including the path where the PR cannot be opened but `main` still lands, and an ordering proof that the record is opened while `main` is still behind prakrit), `tests/fm-pool.test.sh`, `tests/fm-pool-failover.test.sh`, `tests/fm-spawn-pool.test.sh`, `tests/fm-cursor-harness.test.sh`, `tests/fm-open-url.test.sh`, and `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The commit collapses two divergent guards into one shared `merge_only` predicate so the record's listings and the sentences citing them can no longer disagree, touches only PR-body assembly and its tests, and adds a fixture that actually reproduces the uncovered combination. ## Testing Ran the colocated suite `tests/fm-proplane-promote-pr.test.sh` (41 cases, all green), the coverage partition guard, and the two other suites this branch touches, then drove the real promote and full-ladder scripts end to end against a throwaway PropPlane-shaped git fixture with `gh-axi` replaced by a recording stub. That produced captain-facing transcripts, the exact GitHub call log, the exact PR markdown body, and before/after `origin/main` shas for five scenarios: happy-path promote (record opened while main was still behind, then fast-forwarded onto the promoted tip), re-run (`pr edit`, no duplicate), GitHub returning HTTP 403 (loud warning, promotion still lands), and both dry runs (preview printed, zero GitHub calls, refs unmoved). Because the reviewer-facing surface of this change is the pull request itself, I rendered the captured body bytes into a GitHub-shaped page and captured a screenshot of it. Everything passed and no product defect surfaced. - Evidence: Promotion record PR as a reviewer sees it (rendered from the captured body bytes) (local file: /var/folders/ds/wcjw4lg13z33mjzn973y5rhm0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZ12SHB4AM1DNXJJMR5363F7/01-pr-as-rendered.png)
Evidence: Generated PR markdown handed to `gh-axi pr create --body-file` Promotion record for the PropPlane keeper ladder: `prakrit` -> `main`. ## What is being promoted - range: `origin/main..integrate/prakrit-to-main` (`538d3d7..e53c95a`) - commits: 3 - `main` is fast-forwarded to: `e53c95a155c5cd0d2eedc8a3f7eec76af50afee9` - e53c95a fix(calendar): keep the toolbar from overflowing on mobile - de2faed feat(sms): send booking confirmations via twilio - 8f73120 feat(calendar): compact toolbar with month/week toggle ## Record versus this PR's diff This PR's head is `prakrit`, but the promoted range above is built on `integrate/prakrit-to-main`, which the keeper-branch rule never pushes to GitHub. The promoted range above is authoritative for what lands on `main`; the diff GitHub renders here is `prakrit` and can differ from it. `prakrit` carries the same non-merge commits as the promoted range, so this PR's diff is the promotion. ## Security review - outcome: not re-run here (--validate-only resumes an earlier promotion run) ## Validation - outcome: SKIPPED by --skip-gates (captain-authorized) ## How this lands The ladder fast-forwards `main` to `e53c95a155c5cd0d2eedc8a3f7eec76af50afee9` right after opening this PR, which closes this PR as merged: `main` then contains `prakrit`. This PR is the promotion record, not a second approval gate, so nothing waits on a review here. ```text Promotion record for the PropPlane keeper ladder: `prakrit` -> `main`. ## What is being promoted - range: `origin/main..integrate/prakrit-to-main` (`538d3d7..e53c95a`) - commits: 3 - `main` is fast-forwarded to: `e53c95a155c5cd0d2eedc8a3f7eec76af50afee9` - e53c95a fix(calendar): keep the toolbar from overflowing on mobile - de2faed feat(sms): send booking confirmations via twilio - 8f73120 feat(calendar): compact toolbar with month/week toggle ## Record versus this PR's diff This PR's head is `prakrit`, but the promoted range above is built on `integrate/prakrit-to-main`, which the keeper-branch rule never pushes to GitHub. title: fix(agents): require parallel-first dispatch at task intake
body:
## Intent The developer was driving a Firstmate repository change that updates the shared always-loaded AGENTS.md operating instructions so the existing task-intake/concurrency owner section forces parallel-first decomposition: at every intake and whenever a long validation, infrastructure wait, or blocker appears, firstmate must identify independently valuable user-facing proof/delivery paths and dispatch them immediately, and must name a concrete dependency before serializing work (shared file overlap, preferring one product spine, or the existence of a longer integrated path not counting as one). This was prompted by a captain-reported failure where a directly valuable live research script was needlessly held behind repeated validation of the integrated M2 engine. Constraints were explicit: patch the existing section rather than appending a duplicate policy, preserve existing prohibitions on speculative architectures, duplicate implementations, competing product spines, unsafe shared mutable state, and destruction of unlanded work, make clear parallel-first means bounded independent outcomes rather than redundant planners or multiple architectures, and keep it concise with one sentence per physical line and plain dashes. Validation required running bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh plus focused documentation checks, reviewing the diff against the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill, and committing a minimal change without touching private data/, state/, config/, or projects/. The developer then had the agent run /no-mistakes to validate and ship the commit through a green PR, insisting the agent own every gate response without --yes, record exact finding IDs and version-matched commands to the status file, and apply only captain-authorized wording decisions supplied in separate review-decision files across two rounds of findings (scoping parallel dispatch to authorized work, removing serialization-contract duplication, and clarifying that one product spine does not authorize competing architectures). After the push failed for lack of write access, the developer approved creating a public kaku-san/firstmate fork while keeping kunchenguid/firstmate as upstream, and directed the agent to recover the existing no-mistakes run from its failed push step and continue through PR and CI without restarting or dropping commits. ## What Changed - Added a parallel-first rule to the intake and authority section of `AGENTS.md`: at every intake, and whenever long validation, infrastructure or platform work, an external wait, or a blocker appears, firstmate must identify independently valuable user-facing proof or delivery paths and immediately dispatch every such path already authorized by the captain's original request or the accepted task criteria. - Tightened the serialization rule so serializing now requires *naming* a concrete condition (true semantic dependency, shared mutable external state, incompatible concurrent migration). Same-file editing, preferring one bounded path among several that implement the same authorized outcome, and the existence of a longer integrated path are each explicitly not dependencies. - Bounded the new clause against scope creep: parallel-first means bounded independent outcomes, not redundant planners, duplicate implementations, or competing approaches or architectures; identification may be silent and is never authorization to implement; and the clause cross-references the Selected delivery path subsection as the sole owner of standing `yolo` authority rather than restating it. Review flagged two informational issues on the first pass (undefined "product spine" terminology and duplicated `yolo`-boundary wording) which were auto-fixed and re-checked clean. Doc audience check passed with 61 surfaces / 171 local links, and `tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` plus `tests/fm-ensure-agents-md.test.sh` ran 13 assertions with no failures. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Documentation-only change of 4 net lines patched into one existing AGENTS.md subsection, with both prior review findings fully resolved (spine terminology removed repo-wide, duplicate yolo sentence replaced by a pointer whose target heading exists at line 280), no behavior or code path touched, and every prohibition and safety boundary preserved. ## Testing I treated AGENTS.md as the product surface it is (the always-loaded agent contract that CLAUDE.md symlinks to) and validated it end-to-end rather than only running scripts: bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh passed clean, the two focused documentation tests passed with no failures, and a contract check over the loaded file confirmed the parallel-first rule was patched into the existing intake subsection with every required trigger, the authorized-scope dispatch bound, the named-dependency requirement, the three explicit non-dependencies, and all preserved prohibitions intact, with the yolo cross-reference resolving and the serialization contract owned in exactly one place repo-wide. I also confirmed via fm-ff-lib's changed_instr that this commit counts as an instruction-surface change, so already-running secondmates get nudged to re-read it. Visual evidence is a screenshot of the rendered subsection with the added and edited lines highlighted in context. The one thing not provable here is that a live agent then decomposes work in parallel, since that needs a real agent session and is not deterministic; everything within the change's own scope is demonstrated and green. - Evidence: Rendered AGENTS.md intake subsection with the new parallel-first clause highlighted in context (local file: /var/folders/hv/gd626zx51jb1_3rghgd97mp00000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZ15X6PJD3WTVGEKKGE4CSHX/agents-md-intake-section.png)

body:
## Intent ⁣FIRSTMATE_OP: v1 launch-brief: You are a crewmate: an autonomous worker agent managed by firstmate. Work on your own; do not wait for a human. # Task Implement Wayfinder ticket PX06, the primary-only structured questions TUI, without installing or copying the GSD Pi extension raw. Authoritative plan: - `data/wayfinder/pi-workflow-extensions/MAP.md` - `data/wayfinder/pi-workflow-extensions/tickets/PX02.md` - `data/wayfinder/pi-workflow-extensions/tickets/PX04.md` - `data/wayfinder/pi-workflow-extensions/tickets/PX06.md` - Evidence: `data/gsd-pi-pi-extensions-scout/report.md` Before editing: - Read and follow `/home/shiv/tec-workspace/.agents/skills/firstmate-coding-guidelines/SKILL.md`. - Read and apply `/home/shiv/.pi/agent/skills/write-discoverable-code/SKILL.md` and `/home/shiv/.pi/agent/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md`. - Read the installed Pi `docs/extensions.md`, `docs/tui.md`, `docs/packages.md`, `docs/session-format.md`, `docs/keybindings.md`, and `docs/rpc.md` completely. - Follow relevant Markdown cross-references and inspect `question.ts`, `questionnaire.ts`, `tools.ts`, and other matching installed examples. - Run `no-mistakes doctor` after creating the branch and stop if the repository is not ready. Scope ownership: - Own only `.pi/extensions/fm-ask-user-tui.ts` or its same-named directory, its focused tests, and documentation colocated with that extension. - Do not edit the secure credential extension, shared Firstmate instructions, README, or unrelated integration docs. - PX07 owns cross-extension integration and shared documentation. Required activation: - Pi may auto-discover the source, but the extension must register no tool outside the eligible main-primary TUI. - Require a main-private, ordinary, non-symlink marker at `config/ask-user-tui`. - The marker is not inherited and must not be created by this task. - Do not trust ambient `FM_HOME` alone. - Reject or register nothing for marker absence, symlink, secondmate home, worker worktree, RPC, print, and JSON modes. - Preserve current Firstmate supervision and every protected tool. Required TUI behavior: - Register a searchable tool named `ask_user_questions` with accurate prompt metadata. - Show one question per page through `ctx.ui.custom()`. - Support single select, multi-select, Markdown preview, and a free-text answer path. - Keep recommended choices visually clear, but never preselect or auto-submit one. - Preserve stable question and option IDs in the structured result. - Escape and abort return explicit cancellation and never invent an answer. - Respect terminal width, focus and IME cursor placement, theme invalidation, keyboard navigation, and reload lifecycle. - Use no copied numeric caps for question count, preview length, timeout, or pages. - If a defensive tripwire becomes necessary, measure the real TUI path and report the receipt before adding it. Authority boundaries: - The tool presents choices and returns answers only. - It does not approve merge, discard, security, credentials, messaging, or irreversible action. - A TUI answer does not close a durable decision by itself. - `decision-hold-lifecycle`, `tasks-axi`, firstmate authority, and worker `needs-decision` remain the owners. - No Slack, Discord, Telegram, X, browser, polling, remote questions, backlog, or hidden decision cache. - Workers and secondmates never use this tool to address the captain. Verification: - Exercise public behavior, not source-byte assertions. - Cover valid and invalid activation marker, symlink marker, worker worktree, secondmate home, and every non-TUI mode. - Cover single selection, multiple selection, free text, Markdown preview, cancellation, abort, stable IDs, empty input, and malformed options. - Cover narrow and wide terminals, keyboard-only navigation, IME focus, invalidate, theme change, reload, new, resume, fork, and shutdown. - Prove no handler, widget, shortcut, or state duplicates after reload. - Prove answers alone do not mutate backlog, decision records, state logs, or authority. - Produce a deterministic TUI demo path for PX08, but do not enable the private marker. - Run focused tests, `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` for maintained prose, and `bin/fm-lint.sh` when applicable. - Before reporting implementation complete, load `/home/shiv/.agents/skills/but-for-real/SKILL.md` and challenge every acceptance claim. # Herdr lifecycle declaration - NOT ENABLED **HARD SAFETY GATE:** this scaffold cannot inspect the task text that replaces `{TASK}` later. If the task will start, stop, delete, restart, profile, or otherwise drive Herdr lifecycle behavior, stop and regenerate the brief with `--herdr-lab` before dispatch. Do not add Herdr lifecycle commands to this unguarded brief by hand. # Setup You are in a disposable git worktree of tec-workspace, at a detached HEAD on a clean default branch. **Verify isolation before anything else.** Run `pwd -P` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; both must resolve to the disposable task worktree you were launched in, such as a treehouse pool path or an Orca-managed worktree, not the primary checkout firstmate operates from. The path check is authoritative: `git rev-parse --git-dir` and `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` can help inspect the repo, but they do not prove you are outside the primary checkout. If the top-level path is the primary checkout or not the worktree you were launched in, STOP - do not branch or commit here - append `blocked: launched in primary checkout, not an isolated worktree` to the status file and stop. 1. First action: create your branch: `git checkout -b fm/px06-ask-user-tui` # Rules 1. Never push to the default branch. Never merge a PR. Work only on your `fm/px06-ask-user-tui` branch. 2. Stay inside this worktree; modify nothing outside it. 3. Use gh-axi for GitHub operations and chrome-devtools-axi for browser operations. 4. Report status by appending one line: `echo "{state}: {one short line}" >> '/home/shiv/tec-workspace/state/px06-ask-user-tui.status'` States: working, needs-decision, blocked, paused, done, failed. Each append wakes firstmate, so report sparingly: only phase changes a supervisor would act on (setup done, bug reproduced, fix implemented, validation passed) and the needs-decision/blocked/paused/done/failed states. No step-by-step FYI progress lines; firstmate reads your pane for that. A mid-task `working:` line (including setup complete) is nonterminal: do not end the turn after it; continue the same stage until a defined `done:` gate under Definition of done. Use `paused: {why}` - distinct from `blocked:` - ONLY when you are deliberately idling on a known external wait you expect to clear on its own (an upstream release, a rate-limit reset, a scheduled window): firstmate then leaves your idle pane alone and rechecks it on a long cadence instead of treating it as a possible wedge. Use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need help. 5. If you hit the same obstacle twice, append `blocked: {why}` and stop; firstmate will help. 6. If a decision belongs above the implementation worker (product choices, destructive actions, ask-user findings), append `needs-decision: {summary of options}` and stop. Firstmate will apply the configured authority and reply with the decision. When firstmate replies or a blocker clears and you resume, append `resolved: {how it was decided or unblocked}` (add the same `[key=]` if you opened it with one) so the decision or blocker is durably closed and does not keep resurfacing. 7. Never stop, restart, or update the shared `no-mistakes` daemon - it is one instance serving every lane/home, so restarting it kills other lanes' in-flight pipeline runs. On ANY no-mistakes daemon error, append `blocked: {the daemon error}` and stop; only firstmate manages the daemon. # Project memory If `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` already exists, or if this task produced durable project-intrinsic knowledge, run `/home/shiv/tec-workspace/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh .` in the worktree. Record only project knowledge useful to almost every future session. For anything the codebase already shows, prefer a pointer to the authoritative file, command, or doc over copying it. If you touch a project `AGENTS.md` that lacks `## Maintaining this file`, add that short self-governance section from `/home/shiv/tec-workspace/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh` in the same pass. Keep it proportionate: skip `AGENTS.md` edits for trivial tasks that produced no durable project knowledge. # Definition of done The task is complete only when committed on your branch. When you believe it is complete, append `done: {summary}` to the status file and stop. Firstmate will then instruct you to run /no-mistakes to validate and ship a PR. You drive no-mistakes by responding to its gates, not by implementing fixes. Follow the guidance no-mistakes provides, `no-mistakes axi run --help`, and every returned `help` line. The run intent must preserve this Task section and every later accepted clarification. Do not hand-edit, commit, abort, restart, or answer findings yourself while a run is active. Ask-user findings return to firstmate under rule 6. Avoid `--yes`, because it would bypass firstmate's authority check. After /no-mistakes reports CI green, append `done: PR {url} checks green` and stop. Do not merge. PX08 owns the captain's required visual acceptance before landing or activation. # Accepted Wayfinder constraints from MAP.md **Destination:** Integrate two independent TUI extensions into the Pi workflow: structured questions in the primary session and secure credential collection in an explicitly specialist session, without installing raw upstream code, without creating another authority, and without exposing secrets in conversation or the session. - Language: pt-BR. - GSD Pi evidence is `data/gsd-pi-pi-extensions-scout/report.md`. - Oh My Pi evidence is `data/oh-my-pi-pi-extensions-scout/report.md`. - Local baseline is Pi `0.83.0` with the current installation's `extensions.md`, `tui.md`, `packages.md`, and `session-format.md`. - This map plans two separate extensions. A monolithic package is not required. - The common path is only the compatibility, loading, and authority contract. Each branch can be implemented and validated independently. - The map does not authorize implementation by itself. Task tickets start only after explicit dispatch. Graph: - Trunk: PX01 -> PX02. - Credential branch: PX02 -> PX03 -> PX05. - Questions branch: PX02 -> PX04 -> PX06. - Integration crossing: PX05 + PX06 -> PX07 -> PX08. Accepted decisions: - PX01 fixed and compared the sources against the installed Pi public API. - PX02 keeps the extensions separate. No raw upstream package is installed. - `ask-user-tui` registers the tool only when the primary session runs in the main home and finds the private marker `config/ask-user-tui`; the marker is not inherited. - `secure-credentials-tui` loads only through `-e` in an explicitly specialist session. - Normal workers and secondmates do not receive either extension by default. - Structured questions do not replace `decision-hold-lifecycle`, backlog, captain authority, or worker contracts. - The credential collector receives only local allowlisted manifests, never arbitrary model paths, does not hydrate `process.env`, and has no Vercel or Convex sinks in the first cut. - No numeric limit for questions, characters, timeout, or pages is copied without local measurement. Not yet specified: - No functional choice blocks either branch. - UI limits and tripwires will be measured in PX07 before becoming configuration. - Implementation order is selected at dispatch and does not change the graph. Out of scope: - Direct installation of `get-secrets-from-user.ts` or `ask-user-questions.ts`. - Remote questions through Slack, Discord, Telegram, X, or another channel. - Credential collection in RPC, print, JSON, or chat. - Vercel, Convex, automatic rotation, automatic file discovery, or arbitrary `.env` writes. - Another dispatcher, watcher, worktree manager, permission system, or backlog. - Changes to merge authority, security, discard, or approval through a TUI answer. - Swarm, subagent, bg-shell, GSD engine, and any parallel runtime. # Accepted PX02 constraints **Question TUI entry and loading:** `.pi/extensions/fm-ask-user-tui.ts` or an equivalent directory is the planned entry. Auto-discovery is only in the Firstmate project. The factory exposes the surface only in TUI when the canonical cwd contains a private, regular, non-symlink marker at `config/ask-user-tui`, and no `.fm-secondmate-home` exists. The marker belongs only to the primary home, is not inherited, and is created only after PX08. Do not rely only on `FM_HOME`, because normal workers can start without that variable. In a worker worktree, secondmate, session without the marker, or session without TUI, the extension registers no tool. **Credential TUI loading:** The credential entry is outside `.pi/extensions`, is never auto-discovered, and loads only through `pi -e ` in a deliberately specialist session. The specialist session does not inherit merge, send, discard, or security authority. **Authority:** `ask-user-tui` presents and returns answers and does not decide independently. Durable decisions remain owned by `decision-hold-lifecycle`, `tasks-axi`, and Firstmate. Workers continue to report `needs-decision` and never open a TUI to address the captain. The credential extension accepts only allowlisted local manifests and never arbitrary model paths. # Accepted PX04 constraints **UX:** The TUI is mandatory through `ctx.ui.custom()`. Show one question per page. Support single choice, multiple choice, Markdown preview, and free-text response. A recommended option must explain consequence and tradeoff without being automatically selected. Escape cancels. Cancellation returns an explicit state and never invents an answer. Preserve stable question and option IDs in the result. **Data:** Tool arguments contain question, options, descriptions, and previews. Tool result contains only selected IDs and typed free text. The result participates in normal session context because it is not secret. UI state is ephemeral. No parallel backlog or remote cache. **Authority:** The tool does not approve merge, discard, security, send, or irreversible actions. A TUI response does not close a durable decision by itself. Firstmate records a decision through the current owner when context requires it. The extension does not load in workers or secondmates. **Limits:** No numeric cap is fixed in the specification. PX07 measures viewport, pagination, and volume before creating tripwires. No Slack, Discord, Telegram, X, browser, or polling. # Accepted PX06 constraints **Goal:** Implement `ask-user-tui` according to PX04, using the installed Pi public API and without transporting GSD remote questions. **Required work:** Load `firstmate-coding-guidelines` before touching tracked material. Register the tool and renderers only in the eligible primary session. Implement single-choice, multiple-choice, preview, and free-text pages. Preserve stable IDs and explicit cancellation. Integrate only by composition with current decision policy. Do not create backlog, hold, polling, remote channel, or automatic approval inside the extension. **Verification:** Test the private marker activation rule, including valid marker, absent marker, symlink, worker worktree, secondmate, and non-TUI modes. Test single, multiple, free text, preview, cancellation, and structured return. Test TUI width, pagination, IME focus, invalidate, and render. Prove responses do not alter backlog or authority. The no-mistakes pipeline is required because this touches authority and a primary extension. **Done:** The tool is available only in the correct scope, the UX is validated, and visual evidence is accepted by the captain in PX08. # Accepted scout constraints used for PX06 - The GSD `ask-user-questions` UI is reference material only. Its remote question manager, Slack, Discord, Telegram, polling, dedup cache, notification bell, and GSD authority are not transported. - The installed Pi public imports are `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, `@earendil-works/pi-tui`, and `typebox`; upstream GSD aliases and private imports are not assumed. - `ctx.ui.custom()` is TUI-only because it returns undefined in RPC. Do not use RPC fallback for this primary-only tool. - The installed `ctx.ui.select()` contract has no multi-select option, so multi-select belongs in the custom TUI component. - Pi extensions run with process permissions and have no in-process sandbox. Session and project scope are security boundaries. - Do not add a second inference runtime, provider, dispatcher, worker, watcher, process manager, browser stack, web channel, or backlog. ## What Changed - Add `.pi/extensions/fm-ask-user-tui.ts`, which registers a searchable `ask_user_questions` tool only in an eligible main-primary TUI session gated on a regular, non-symlink `config/ask-user-tui` marker (rejecting marker absence, symlink markers, secondmate homes, worker worktrees, and RPC/print/JSON modes). - Drive one question per page through `ctx.ui.custom()` with single-select, multi-select, Markdown preview, and free-text paths, keeping recommended choices visible without preselecting, preserving stable question and option IDs, and returning explicit cancellation on Escape/abort; keyboard navigation now scrolls to keep the focused option visible and reserves rows for the `↑/↓ more` scroll indicators. - Add `tests/fm-ask-user-tui.test.sh` covering activation rules and public behavior (selection modes, free text, preview, cancellation, stable IDs, empty/malformed input, terminal width, theme invalidation, and reload/new/resume/fork lifecycle with no handler duplication). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The incremental change is a small, self-contained scroll-reserve adjustment that correctly keeps the focused option visible beside the indicator rows for realistic cases, behind a not-yet-enabled activation marker. ## Testing O teste focado `tests/fm-ask-user-tui.test.sh` passou por inteiro (typecheck estrito pulou por falta de `tsc` no PATH, comportamento esperado do próprio teste), cobrindo a regra do marcador privado, todos os modos não-TUI, e o comportamento público do TUI sem efeitos de autoridade ou sessão. Para prova de nível de produto eu montei um fixture de checkout primário com o marcador `config/ask-user-tui`, dirigi o componente real `ctx.ui.custom()` de ponta a ponta e capturei 9 frames: pergunta única com opção recomendada visível sem preseleção e preview Markdown, navegação por teclado, terminal estreito respeitando a largura, multi-seleção com Space, página de texto livre com o marcador de cursor IME presente, revisão e o resultado estruturado com IDs estáveis (`opt-postgres`, `reg-us`, `reg-eu`, `freeText`), além do cancelamento por Escape retornando `response:null, cancelled:true` sem inventar resposta. Os frames foram renderizados em HTML e capturados em PNG para revisão visual. Nenhum problema encontrado. - Evidence: Captura de tela dos 9 frames do TUI ask_user_questions (fluxo completo + resultado JSON) (local file: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZ18YKD6710736GKS9BFR1J4/px06-tui-demo.png) - Evidence: Demo TUI renderizado em HTML (frames ANSI com cores) (local file: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZ18YKD6710736GKS9BFR1J4/px06-tui-demo.html)
Evidence: Resultado estruturado retornado ao modelo (IDs estáveis) e cancelamento explícito ```text submit -> {"answers":[{"questionId":"storage-backend","selectedOptionIds":["opt-postgres"]},{"questionId":"regions","selectedOptionIds":["reg-us","reg-eu"]},{"questionId":"rollout-notes","selectedOptionIds":[],"freeText":"canary us-east-1 first"}]} escape -> {"response":null,"cancelled":true,"aborted":false} ```

In handleInput, Up/Down (lines 504-517) move cursorIndex through the full item list and reset pageScroll to 0, while render() slices the body at [pageScroll, pageScroll+viewport] and never scrolls to keep cursorIndex visible. With more options than fit the viewport (no numeric cap exists), pressing Down moves focus below the visible window with the view pinned at the top, so a keyboard-only captain cannot see which option is highlighted. Fix: after moving the cursor, adjust pageScroll so the focused item's line range stays within the viewport instead of forcing pageScroll = 0. 🔧 Fix: keep focused option visible during keyboard navigation 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `.pi/extensions/fm-ask-user-tui.ts:557` - The scroll-to-cursor fix aligns the focused item flush to the viewport edge (line 556 sets pageScroll = start; line 557 sets pageScroll = end - viewport), but render() then overwrites the first visible line with the '↑ N more' indicator (lines 564-569) and the last visible line with the '↓ N more' indicator (lines 571-578) whenever content is hidden above/below. title: fix(bin): resolve real remote default branch in fleet sync
body:
## What Changed
- `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh` `default_branch()` now repairs a missing cached `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` symref by running `git remote set-head origin --auto` once, so a repo whose default branch is neither `main` nor `master` resolves the real remote default (and caches it for later runs) instead of being judged against the wrong branch and reported STUCK; a stderr note is emitted when the repair happens.
- If the remote cannot be queried, resolution falls through to the existing `main`/`master` guess, keeping offline runs as benign as before (a repo with a non-main/master default then skips with "cannot determine default branch" rather than failing).
- Added tests in `tests/fm-fleet-sync.test.sh` covering the three paths: a non-main default without a cached `origin/HEAD` is repaired and fast-forwarded, a failed repair still syncs a `main`-default repo via the guess, and a failed repair on a non-main default skips benignly without moving the clone.

title: fix: guard Claude fleet operations during watcher gaps
fix(bin): prevent treehouse allocation from detaching live work
body:
## Intent Stop firstmate's crewmate spawn from being handed a treehouse pool slot that still holds live work (upstream kunchenguid/firstmate#1441). Twice on 2026-08-02, after host restarts wiped or staled treehouse's owner records, a slot holding an unlanded branch was allocated and detached. Deliberate decisions behind this diff, reviewed and approved by firstmate before implementation - these are choices, not oversights: 1. The guard runs BEFORE `treehouse get`, not after. The original task asked for a post-allocation check on the accepted worktree. I measured that `treehouse get` resets the slot while acquiring it (its own help: "Unlike 'get', enter does not acquire, reset, or return the worktree"), and fm-spawn only learns the worktree by polling the pane's current path afterwards - so a post-hoc check inspects a slot whose evidence is already erased and passes every time. Firstmate approved this deviation from the original wording. 2. The stated defect is deliberately narrow: clean working tree PLUS commits unreachable from the default branch. Uncommitted content is already protected by treehouse itself, which reports such a slot dirty and refuses to reclaim one even when an exhausted pool is entirely dirty. The original report claimed uncommitted work was the exposure; that was measured false, and firstmate approved keeping the narrowed mechanism rather than widening it back. 3. The guard reads treehouse's own `available` verdict from `status --json` instead of reimplementing eligibility, so a treehouse version bump cannot silently desync it. jq is required and its absence is a deliberate refusal: the human-readable status table abbreviates $HOME paths to a leading ~ and appends per-slot process continuation lines, so it is not a parseable contract. This is a knowing new dependency on the crewmate spawn path. 4. It deliberately does NOT reuse work_is_landed() from bin/fm-teardown.sh, even though that is the repo's existing landed-work owner. That function fetches, calls `gh pr view`, and computes patch-ids - per candidate slot, per spawn - and answers a different question ("may I destroy this?") where a guard must be conservative. The guard asks the strictly weaker, offline question "is this slot demonstrably empty?" and never authorizes destruction, so it does not restate or weaken teardown's contract. 5. The guard is refuse-only by design. Even an identity-verified dead owner does not release a slot holding unlanded work; bin/fm-teardown.sh remains the sole releaser. FM_WORKTREE_RECLAIM_OK is deliberately scoped to exact worktree paths so it cannot become a standing blanket bypass. 6. Ownership is a process identity via fm_pid_identity, never a bare pid: a reboot reissues pid numbers, and recorded pre-reboot pids were measured resolving to unrelated live node processes. Empty owner fields deliberately read UNRESOLVED, never dead, so a missing record can never be mistaken for a released slot. 7. The test changes are required, not incidental. Suites that spawn a crewmate stubbed treehouse as a silent `exit 0`, but the real binary prints [] for an empty pool and never nothing, so the guard correctly refuses that stub; tests/lib.sh gains fm_fake_treehouse so one faithful stub is shared instead of re-rolled. fm-secondmate-harness additionally revealed that fm-spawn never previously executed treehouse at all - it only typed `treehouse get` into the pane - so its BASE_PATH legitimately excluded the binary. The Herdr presentation test's normalize_meta gains the two new per-run owner fields alongside the per-run container ids, for the same reason those ids are normalized. Scope was deliberately limited to allocation safety: no re-anchoring of mis-rooted panes, no teardown policy change, no attempt to repair treehouse itself. `treehouse get --lease` was considered and rejected as the larger alternative - it is the real durability fix, but it restructures acquisition across five backends and every lease needs a `treehouse return` or the pool leaks permanently, which is teardown policy and out of scope. Nine failures in the full 105-test run were triaged before submitting: seven reproduce identically on a clean origin/main checkout and are pre-existing (Node.js ESM environment failures and supervision/tmux suites affected by the live fleet); two were mine and are fixed. ## What Changed - Add a fail-closed pre-allocation guard that refuses crewmate spawns when an available Treehouse slot contains commits unreachable from the default branch. - Record process identities for allocated worktrees, validate Treehouse’s JSON schema, and support path-scoped operator authorization without resetting or releasing slots. - Add regression coverage, faithful Treehouse test fakes, and maintainer documentation for allocation safety and dependency requirements. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The schema-validation fix now fails closed for non-array payloads and malformed entries, preserves valid empty-pool behavior, and the cumulative change conforms to the stated allocation-safety scope. ## Testing Focused guard and spawn-path tests passed; a captured CLI simulation showed a clean available slot with an unlanded commit and stale owner identity was refused after only `treehouse status --json`, while its branch, HEAD, and clean state remained unchanged. No visual artifact was applicable because this is a CLI-only change.
Evidence: Restart-stale slot refusal transcript ```text Scenario: treehouse marks a clean slot available after its recorded owner identity became stale across restart. BEFORE branch=fm/restart-survivor head=1389c0bb3cb232de031748d642801ea714da40a6 working_tree=clean OPERATOR COMMAND $ bin/fm-worktree-guard.sh check /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZ1EGQ49T4BJN72GNJAVMKZN/restart-guard.Odg4WO/project error: refusing to spawn - a pool slot treehouse would hand out still holds live work. slot 1: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZ1EGQ49T4BJN72GNJAVMKZN/restart-guard.Odg4WO/slot-1 found: branch fm/restart-survivor with 1 commit not on heads/main owner: task pre-restart-task recorded this slot; its worker is gone (recorded process identity no longer matches) to release: land or discard pre-restart-task's work, then bin/fm-teardown.sh pre-restart-task Nothing was reset, cleaned, or discarded. This spawn simply did not run. Authorize one exact slot with FM_WORKTREE_RECLAIM_OK= only after its work is safe. exit=1 TREEHOUSE INVOCATIONS $ treehouse status --json AFTER branch=fm/restart-survivor head=1389c0bb3cb232de031748d642801ea714da40a6 working_tree=clean preserved=yes ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-worktree-guard.sh:137` - The authoritative intent limits this guard to “clean working tree PLUS commits unreachable from the default branch,” but this also refuses a clean named branch whose HEAD is fully reachable from the default branch. Confirm that zero-ahead named branches are intentionally in scope, or remove this additional refusal. - 🚨 `bin/fm-worktree-guard.sh:290` - An `available` JSON entry with a missing, null, or empty `.path` becomes an empty TSV field and is silently skipped, allowing the fail-closed guard to approve a pool slot it never inspected. Reject available rows unless required fields—especially an absolute, non-empty string path—are valid. 🔧 Fix: Align worktree guard with allocation safety contract 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-worktree-guard.sh:269` - The fail-closed parser still accepts malformed but valid JSON as an empty/safe pool: `null`, `""`, or `{}` all have `length == 0`, and entries missing `.status` are silently excluded. Validate that the top level is an array and every entry has the required schema before treating length zero or filtering `available` slots; otherwise a treehouse schema change can bypass the guard. 🔧 Fix: Validate treehouse JSON schema before allocation ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-worktree-guard.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-spawn-worktree-settle.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-tangle-guard.test.sh` - Manual real-Git-worktree restart simulation invoking `bin/fm-worktree-guard.sh check`, logging treehouse calls and comparing branch, HEAD, and working-tree state before and after refusal - `git status --short` to confirm testing left no transient worktree changes
⚠️ **Document** - 1 error - 🚨 `bin/fm-backend.sh:313` - The new guard requires jq for every Treehouse-backed spawn, but the bootstrap dependency set still omits jq for tmux. Fixing this requires executable and test changes, which this documentation-only task forbids.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix(bin): open exactly one decision per status line
body:
## The defect

`status_open_decisions` in `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh` folds a task's append-only status log into the set of decisions still open. A `needs-decision:` or `blocked:` line opens a keyed decision, and only a `resolved:` or `captain-held:` line carrying that same key closes it. `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh` then refuses to complete or verify while any open key sits outside the reviewed inventory.

Two line shapes broke that fold, both silently.

**1. An unresolvable key dropped the entire line.** `_fm_decision_key` returned non-zero when a `[key=...]` token could not be parsed as a slug, and both folds did `continue`. So this:

```
needs-decision [key=bad key]: which storage backend?
```

opened no decision at all. The escalation disappeared from the durable set and the completion gate passed as though nothing were pending. A malformed `resolved:` line likewise closed nothing, leaving no trace of the attempt. Losing a decision outright is the worse of the two failures here.

**2. Two key tokens bound the decision to whichever came first.**

```
needs-decision [key=one] [key=two]: pick a rollout order
```

folded to `one`, with nothing to tell the author that the second key had been ignored.

### The rule that is working as designed

Only the prefix before the first colon is parsed for a key. A `[key=...]` token after the colon is summary prose, so this opens a decision under `default`:

```
needs-decision: half or full framing [key=phone-framing]
```

That is deliberate and stays unchanged. A summary may legitimately read `should docs mention [key=prose]?`, and nothing in the line distinguishes prose from intent once past the colon. There is an existing test asserting exactly this.

It was, however, completely silent, and it is the shape that motivated this change. An author who writes one correctly keyed line and later writes a second line with the token after the colon ends up with a `default` record sitting beside their real keys. The gate then rejects `default` as outside the reviewed inventory, and nothing explains why. The only remedy was to know, by folklore, to append a bare unkeyed `resolved:` after every escalation. This PR keeps the parsing rule and removes the silence.

## Reproduction

```console
$ . bin/fm-classify-lib.sh
$ printf 'needs-decision [key=bad key]: which storage backend?\n' > /tmp/t.status
$ status_open_decisions /tmp/t.status
$ # before: no output at all, the decision is gone and the gate passes
```

```console
$ printf 'needs-decision [key=one] [key=two]: pick a rollout order\n' > /tmp/t.status
$ status_open_decisions /tmp/t.status
one	needs-decision	pick a rollout order
$ # before: silently bound to the first token
```

## The fix

The invariant is now explicit: **every non-blank `needs-decision:` or `blocked:` line opens exactly one record.**

- A resolvable key opens one decision under that key. Unchanged.
- No key token opens one decision under `default`. Unchanged.
- A line the parser cannot resolve to exactly one slug (two `[key=...]` tokens, an unterminated token, or a value that is not a slug) opens one decision under a reserved `!unresolved-key-<line>` key, and reports the file and line on stderr.

Refusing beats guessing for the ambiguous cases. Taking the first token binds the decision to whichever one happened to be typed first. Falling back to `default` reopens whatever an earlier bare `resolved:` had closed. Both are silent, and neither is recoverable by an author who is never told.

`!` can never appear in a valid slug, so `validate_slug` in `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh` rejects it. The reserved record therefore can never acquire an inventory entry, and `complete` and `verify` reject it by name until the offending status line is fixed. The line number is part of the key so that two malformed lines in one file stay distinct instead of overwriting each other; the status log is append-only, so the number is stable across folds.

The activity fold (`_fm_status_open_activities_stream`) deliberately keeps dropping such lines. Those records are supersession evidence rather than authoritative state, so both directions of a drop are conservative, and a reserved per-line key would strand a phase that no later event could ever close. The reasoning is recorded inline at both call sites.

`bin/fm-brief.sh` now states the token position rule in the generated status protocol, and `.agents/skills/decision-hold-lifecycle/SKILL.md` points at it from the gate failure, so the rule is discoverable at both the moment of writing and the moment of failing.

## Tests

`test_decision_key_grammar` in `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh`, alongside the existing key-grammar assertions:

- a keyed line opens exactly one record, under its own key
- a keyed line opens no `default` record beside it
- an unkeyed line opens exactly one record, under `default`
- a two-key line opens exactly one record, under neither key nor `default`, and emits a diagnostic naming the file and line
- a malformed key opens exactly one record instead of vanishing
- two malformed lines stay distinct, and a malformed `resolved:` closes neither them nor an unrelated real decision
- the end-to-end shape: a token after the colon stays prose under `default`, and the earlier keyed decision is untouched by it

Every case asserts the exact record count, not just the presence of a key, so a regression that adds or loses a record fails rather than passing on a substring match.

## Compatibility note

A status log that already contains a line with an unparsable key will now fail the completion gate where it previously passed. That is the intended correction, since such a log does contain an unaccounted decision, but it is a behaviour change on existing data rather than a pure bug fix.

## Verification

`bin/fm-lint.sh` and `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` are clean. The full suite passes apart from three suites that fail identically with this branch's tree removed (`fm-bootstrap`, `fm-pi-watch-extension`, `fm-test-run`), so none of them is caused by this change; the first looks environment dependent, and the second reproduces on elapsed wall time alone rather than test ordering.

## Intent Auto human-readable Herdr agent/tab names on spawn for firstmate's herdr backend. When firstmate spawns a crewmate or scout on the herdr backend, automatically set a logical display name so the Herdr agents sidebar is readable without a manual post-spawn rename. Captain preference (implement in code): - Scout: scout- - Ship: ship- - ≤32 chars; must match Herdr agent rename grammar ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$ - Do not rename the primary seed tab labeled 1 - Prefer task-id slug when it already reads well (terse-oss-phase01 → scout-terse-oss-phase01 after strip/sanitize) Requirements (current accepted form): 1. Pure helper mapping (task_id, kind) → valid display name: kind=scout → scout-; else ship/crew → ship-; strip redundant fm-/scout-/ship- prefixes; lowercase; replace invalid chars; truncate to 32 without trailing -/_ 2. After Herdr spawn launches the harness (after launch Enter), best-effort wait until the pane reports an agent, then herdr agent rename and herdr tab rename with husk/list_live safety preserved 3. Record herdr_display_name= in task meta for recovery and debugging 4. Rename failures must not fail the spawn (warn on stderr); spawn success remains about endpoint + launch 5. Unit tests for pure name helper (long ids, already-prefixed ids, uppercase, invalid chars) and husk/list_live/rename behavior 6. Update docs/herdr-backend.md briefly: display names are not ownership authority; recorded pane/tab ids remain authoritative 7. Husk re-spawn and list_live must match either fm- create labels or scout-/ship- display forms so renamed tabs are not stranded 8. Existing peeks/sends/teardown continue via meta endpoint ids 9. ## Summary
- add an exact `--discard-approved-by-captain` recovery path for ordinary Herdr tasks whose recorded pane cannot be inspected
- prove task metadata, canonical repository/worktree identity, unique git-worktree ownership, exact `fm/<task>` branch and HEAD, clean status, and absence of ambiguous task ownership before returning the worktree
- preserve the normal locked pane-close path for reachable endpoints and keep `--force`, landed-work, dirty-worktree, secondmate, and merge-authority behavior unchanged
- register executable regressions in the test runner and make its C-sorted coverage comparisons locale-stable

## Diagnosis
- initiating trigger: cleanup is requested after the task has finished
- masking condition: the recorded named Herdr session/pane is still reachable, allowing the normal lock and structured close-confirmation path
- visible symptom: when the endpoint is unavailable or reports `invalid_endpoint`, teardown refuses before returning the otherwise preserved task worktree, even with explicit discard approval
- smallest counterfactual: stopping only the isolated named Herdr lab session changes the same valid task record from successful live-endpoint cleanup to an ambiguous-presence refusal

## Validation
- real isolated Herdr lab: reproduced the stopped-session refusal, then confirmed the new exact approval flag removes only the verified clean worktree while the default Herdr session tripwire remains unchanged
- `tests/fm-herdr-unreachable-teardown.test.sh`
- `tests/fm-teardown-endpoint-safety.test.sh`
- `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh`
- `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh`
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` with pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0
- `bash -n` and `git diff --check`

Direct PR delivery was requested; no no-mistakes command was run.

title: feat(bin): add explicit read-only Microsoft Graph mailbox access
body:
## What Changed - New `bin/fm-mail.py` (`status`, `auth`, `list`, `show`, `logout`): device-code sign-in restricted to `Mail.Read`/`User.Read`/`offline_access` with any broader granted token refused, a single allowlist chokepoint that permits Graph over GET only on the account, folder-listing and single-message paths with no redirects, the refresh credential stored only in the macOS Keychain via stdin so it never enters process arguments, nothing cached on disk, and messages selected by a local fingerprint that resolves against the recent window and then the unread window rather than by mailbox identifier. The tool is inert without a gitignored `config/mail.json`, which is schema-validated, pinned to one account, and refused when it or `config/` is group- or world-writable. - Rendering guardrails: listings are metadata only, bodies print as plain text inside a per-line-prefixed untrusted-data envelope, HTML-only mail is refused instead of rendered, and a local classifier withholds credential-shaped messages. `--redacted` masks on request whether or not the classifier fired and says so, and classifier-flagged subjects are masked everywhere they print, including plain listings. - Supporting material: `tests/fm-mail-readonly.test.sh` plus runner and coverage registration in `bin/fm-test-run.sh`; operator guide `docs/mail-readonly.md`, the `config/mail.json` section in `docs/configuration.md`, and entries in `README.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `docs/documentation-audiences.json`; the agent-runtime `mail-readonly` skill; and a `CONTRIBUTING.md` note recording `bin/fm-mail.py` and the `*-command-policy.mjs` modules as the deliberate non-bash exceptions in `bin/`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: This round's delta is a small, well-bounded fix that provably closes the reported unreachable-ref case while preserving every stated safety boundary, and it ships with direct regression coverage; the surrounding feature remains opt-in and inert until a local config/mail.json exists, with the earlier findings already adjudicated by the author. ## Testing Ran the change's own suite (`tests/fm-mail-readonly.test.sh`, 28 cases) three times with byte-identical output, plus the two other tests the diff touches (`tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` for the new docs inventory entry and `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` for the runner registration) - all pass. Since passing unit tests do not show the operator surface, I also drove the real CLI end-to-end against a stand-in Microsoft, stubbing only the network socket and `/usr/bin/security` so the argument parser, endpoint allowlist, account pin, credential classifier and renderer all ran for real, and captured a 15-scenario operator transcript with a rendered terminal screenshot. That transcript shows each behavior the branch claims: the tool inert without `config/mail.json`, no write subcommand, listings that carry metadata only with credential-shaped subjects already masked, a withheld body that becomes readable under `--redacted` with the code and link masked, `--redacted` announcing itself on a message the classifier did not flag, an HTML-only message refused rather than rendered, and a reference that only `list --unread` printed resolving on the target commit while the same command fails on the parent commit. The request log confirms 37 Graph calls, all GET, none to an attachment, send, move or reply path, and none outside the allowlist, and the Keychain argv log never contains the credential. No failures, no flakiness, and the worktree is clean. - Evidence: Operator-view screenshot: listing masks a credential-shaped subject, body withheld then --redacted, and the unread-window ref before/after (local file: /var/folders/9d/8w50jhgd79x63rgbq_5cyyvm0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZ447VW4K8P8PS41FKD4JGJV/fm-mail-cli-evidence.png)
