⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - 🚨 `bin/fm-mail.py:680` - sanitize_text() does not strip or normalize U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) or U+2029 (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR), while print_envelope() splits the body on "\n" only. A message body can therefore embed the envelope end marker behind a U+2028 and defeat the per-line "> " prefix, contradicting the module docstring's stated invariant at bin/fm-mail.py:33-35 that "every body line prefixed so nothing in the message can forge the envelope's end marker". The sanitizer already strips every other line-break equivalent (\x0b, \x0c, \x85 via CONTROL_RE) and all bidi/zero-width controls via INVISIBLE_RE, so this is a gap in an existing defense rather than an unconsidered case. Fix: in sanitize_text, replace   and   with "\n" (preferred, so they become prefixed lines) or add them to INVISIBLE_RE. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-mail.py:153` - CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS' first rule matches "one-time|verification|security|..." followed by "code|passcode|pin" but omits "password"/"passphrase"/"passwort". The inline-password rule at line 207 only fires on "password:" or "password=", so the very common phrasing "Your one-time password is 483920" (and German "Dein Einmalpasswort lautet ...") matches nothing at all: the body renders in full and the subject renders unmasked in `list`. The tool separately covers "otp", which is the same concept, showing the omission is an oversight in the enumeration rather than a scoping decision. Widening the noun group to include password/passphrase/passwort/kennwort closes both the English and German cases, but it also invalidates tests/fm-mail-readonly.test.sh:662-664, which deliberately pins "Einmalpasswort" as a message the classifier does not flag, so the author should confirm the intended coverage before that test's fixture is changed. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-mail.py:817` - cmd_show resolves a ref by re-listing with unread=False, so it searches the newest `--limit` messages overall, while cmd_list can print refs selected with `--unread`. A ref from `list --unread` is only resolvable when that message is also inside the newest N messages of the whole folder. On an active mailbox, an unread message older than the 100 newest messages (MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT) can never be shown, yet cmd_list unconditionally prints "Read one message with: fm-mail.py show <ref>" at line 807. The `--folder` selection has the same shape but is at least recoverable by passing `--folder` to `show`; the unread window is not recoverable at all. Options are to give `show` an `--unread` flag mirroring `list`, or to have cmd_show fall back to an unread-filtered window when the plain window misses; which one is right is a CLI design call. - ⚠️ `tests/fm-mail-readonly.test.sh:59` - write_config creates the config directory with `mkdir -p` and the Python scenario helper at line 280 uses os.makedirs, neither of which sets the mode, so the directory inherits the caller's umask. load_config (bin/fm-mail.py:264) refuses any config directory with mode & 0o022. Under umask 002 (the default for regular users on several Linux distributions and in many containers) mkdir yields 0775, 0775 & 0022 is non-zero, and every scenario in the suite fails with the directory-permission refusal instead of exercising its own assertion - e.g. test_configuration_validation_refuses_unsafe_input's first case would still exit 2 but assert_contains "client_id" would fail on the directory message. The suite already recognizes that the directory mode matters (it chmods 777 then back to 700 at lines 144-150) but only for that one subtest. Fix: chmod 700 the directory right after creating it in write_config and in the Python scenario helper. 🔧 Fix: resolve show refs against the unread window too 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-mail.py:830` - cmd_list's hint now carries `--folder` when the folder is non-default but never carries `--limit`, while MAX_LIST_LIMIT is 50 and DEFAULT_SEARCH_LIMIT is 25. After `list --limit 50`, the hinted `fm-mail.py show <ref>` searches only the newest 25 of each window, so a ref for a read message at position 26-50 misses both the recent and the unread window on the first try. This is fully recoverable and correctly messaged - cmd_show's error at line 845 names "widen --limit or list again", and MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT (100) covers every window `list` can produce, so no ref is unreachable. Noting it only because the hint was made folder-aware in this commit and reads as complete; appending " --limit %d" when args.limit exceeds DEFAULT_SEARCH_LIMIT, or raising DEFAULT_SEARCH_LIMIT to MAX_LIST_LIMIT, would close it if the author wants the hint to be exact. No action needed to merge.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-mail-readonly.test.sh` - 28 behavior cases, all pass (scope contract, GET-only Graph allowlist, no send/delete/move/attachment path, Keychain argv hygiene, account pin, rendering, redaction, classifier) - `Ran the same suite 3x back to back and diffed the output - byte-identical, no flakiness` - `bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` - covers the new `docs/mail-readonly.md` entry added to `docs/documentation-audiences.json` - `bash bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` - confirms the new test script and `bin/fm-mail.py` are registered in the runner (the two lines this change added to `bin/fm-test-run.sh`); FM_TEST_COVERAGE ok total=108 - Manual end-to-end CLI run: built a demo harness that stubs only `urllib.request.OpenerDirector.open` and `/usr/bin/security`, then drove `fm-mail.py status|list|show|logout` through 15 operator scenarios against a fake mailbox (harness at `<evidence>/harness/demo.sh`) - `fm-mail.py status` / `list` with no `config/mail.json` - tool is inert, refuses with a pointer, contacts nothing - `fm-mail.py send` and `fm-mail.py delete` - rejected as invalid choices; `--help` mentions no write scope - `fm-mail.py list --limit 5` - metadata only; the `743920` one-time-code subject and the German `Bestaetigungscode` subject are masked in the listing itself - `fm-mail.py list --folder archive` - the hint correctly becomes `show <ref> --folder archive` - `fm-mail.py show <ref>` on a credential-shaped message - body withheld with three stated reasons; `--redacted` then renders it with the code and link masked - `fm-mail.py show <ref> --redacted` on a message the classifier did NOT flag - prints "Masking was requested" plus "The classifier saw nothing credential-shaped", so the flag is never a silent no-op - `fm-mail.py show <ref>` on an HTML-only message - refused rather than rendered, so no tracking pixel is fetched - Before/after for commit 49b9cf2: `fm-mail.py show d2c66c31e704 --limit 4` on a ref that only `list --unread --limit 4` printed - succeeds on the target commit, fails with "no message with that reference in the newest 4 messages of inbox" on the parent commit 526ba4a - `Audited the harness request log: 37 requests to graph.microsoft.com, 0 non-GET, 0 attachment/send/move/reply paths, 0 hosts outside the allowlist; the one-lookup vs two-lookup pattern in the log confirms the unread window is only searched when the recent window misses` - `Audited the Keychain stub argv log - the refresh credential never appears in a process argument list`
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix(bin): resolve worker base branches from the remote, not the stale clone
body:
## The failure this prevents An audit concluded that a whole subsystem was not shipped - AscendApp's Remote Config sources under `AscendApp/Shared/Services/RemoteConfig/` - because the task workspace was created from the clone's stale cached default of `main`, while the remote has defaulted to `develop` all along. The files were simply absent from the branch the worker was handed, and firstmate relayed that conclusion to the captain as fact. Verified on the live clone: `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD` returns `refs/heads/develop`, while the clone's cached `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` still says `refs/heads/main` and the checkout sits on `main`. ## Intent Fix the defect where firstmate hands crewmate workers a stale branch, so they read and report on code nobody works on. Root cause and the decision behind the fix: a clone records its remote's default branch once, at clone time, in refs/remotes//HEAD, and nothing ever refreshes it. The bug is therefore entirely local staleness, NOT a project whose development branch differs from its remote default. The primary mechanism is deliberately to stop trusting that cached value: bin/fm-base-branch.sh resolves the base branch from the remote's own current state at spawn time via 'git ls-remote --symref HEAD'. A per-project 'base=' override in the data/projects.md registry is a deliberate SECONDARY escape hatch for the rare project whose development branch genuinely is not its remote default; it must not be the main mechanism and is deliberately NOT required for AscendApp, which now resolves to develop with no registry entry at all. Deliberate choices a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: - Failing to launch is recoverable; quietly reading the wrong code is not. So a declared base branch missing from the remote, an unreachable remote, a remote that reports no default branch, and a malformed base= declaration are all HARD ERRORS rather than a fall back to the local cache. That fail-loud asymmetry is the point of the change, not an oversight. - Base-branch resolution deliberately runs BEFORE any backend endpoint is created, so a refusal never strands a half-started worker pane. - bin/fm-spawn.sh fetches the branch with an explicit destination refspec rather than reusing anything already in the clone, precisely because a clone that has not been fetched recently is the stale state being fixed. The worktree is left at a DETACHED HEAD at that tip, matching the pooled-worktree convention and avoiding git's 'branch already checked out in another worktree' conflict. - The existing worktree-isolation assertion (refusing to launch outside an isolated worktree) is a safety contract and is deliberately preserved untouched; placement happens only after it passes. - Backward compatibility was an explicit requirement: the registry mode still comes from the first bracket token only, so every pre-existing entry parses to exactly the mode and yolo flag it did before, and a project needing no override needs no entry. fm-project-mode.sh's default two-word output is unchanged; the base query is a separate --base mode. - Observability was explicitly requested: base_branch= and base_branch_source= in the task's state record plus base=() on the spawn line, so this can never again be diagnosed only by noticing a report says something impossible. - Naming the branch in the generated brief is deliberately BEST-EFFORT (fm-brief.sh falls back to the generic wording and never fails to scaffold), because fm-spawn.sh is the single authority that resolves and enforces it. - A remote-less project resolves to its own local default; a remote-less clone on a detached HEAD resolves to nothing at all and deliberately leaves the worktree exactly where it was, preserving pre-existing behavior. Explicitly out of scope by the captain's instruction, noted rather than fixed: fm-teardown.sh, fm-merge-local.sh, fm-review-diff.sh, fm-fleet-sync.sh, fm-ff-lib.sh and fm-tangle-lib.sh still resolve the default branch from the same stale cached refs/remotes/origin/HEAD. This change deliberately does not touch worktree acquisition, delivery modes, or the away-mode/watcher/supervision paths. ## What Changed - New `bin/fm-base-branch.sh` resolves the branch a ship or scout worker must stand on from the remote's own current default (`git ls-remote --symref`) instead of the clone's cached `refs/remotes//HEAD`, with an optional per-project `base=` registry override as a secondary escape hatch. It resolves the requested remote, falls back to a sole differently named remote, and hard-errors on a missing branch, an unreachable or ambiguous remote, or a malformed override rather than falling back to the stale local cache. - `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now runs that resolution before any backend endpoint is created, fetches the branch with an explicit destination refspec, leaves the worktree at a detached HEAD on that tip, and records `base_branch=`/`base_branch_source=` in the task meta plus `base=()` on the spawn line. `fm-project-mode.sh` parses the order-independent `base=` bracket token and gains a `--base` query while its default two-word ` ` output stays unchanged; `fm-brief.sh` names the resolved branch in the scaffold best-effort, and `fm-promote.sh` reuses the recorded `base_branch=` in its suggested ship instructions. - New `bin/fm-git-net-lib.sh` puts every spawn-path git network call under a hard `FM_GIT_NET_TIMEOUT` deadline (timeout/gtimeout/perl watchdog, probed for `-k` support, with signal deaths and deadlines normalized to distinct refusal statuses) so the fail-loud contract can never degrade into a hang. Adds `tests/fm-base-branch.test.sh` and `tests/fm-spawn-base-branch.test.sh`, extends `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` and the `fm-test-run.sh` family routing, and updates AGENTS.md plus the architecture, configuration, and scripts docs. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Both round-3 items are implemented exactly as instructed with discriminating network-free tests, the resolution order is documented in a single owner with no stale copies elsewhere, and the only remaining item is a missing test for one already-correct code path. ## Testing I ran the three suites the change adds or touches, then the full --changed selection for this diff (37 scripts), and built a manual end-to-end reproduction of the reported incident driving the real fm-spawn.sh from both the base and target commits against identical fixtures. The base commit places the worker on the stale main tip with the Remote Config sources missing from its workspace - exactly the state that produced the false "not shipped" audit - while the target commit places it on the remote's live develop tip with those sources present, prints base=develop(remote-default) on the spawn line, and records base_branch/base_branch_source in the task state. I also exercised the deliberate refusals (declared branch absent from the remote, unreachable remote, malformed base=), confirmed a refusal creates no backend endpoint and leaves the worktree untouched, confirmed the registry override path and that every pre-existing registry form still parses to the same mode and yolo flag as before, confirmed remote reads are hard-bounded on both watchdog branches, and confirmed the brief names the branch when known. Everything passed except tests/fm-kimi-harness.test.sh, which fails identically at the base commit because this host's python3 is 3.10 and lacks tomllib. This change has no UI surface, so the evidence is CLI transcripts rather than screenshots.

⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:905` - A remote-less project that declares a `base=` override can never spawn. fm-base-branch.sh:94-100 deliberately handles this case - when no `$REMOTE` is configured it verifies `refs/heads/$DECLARED` exists locally and reports `"$DECLARED project-override $REMOTE"` - but the remote field it emits names a remote that does not exist. place_worker_on_base's case statement only special-cases `local-default`; `project-override` falls into the `*)` arm and runs `git -C "$WT" fetch ... "$BASE_BRANCH_REMOTE"`, which fails because there is no `origin`, so the spawn aborts with "could not fetch origin/<branch> ...; refusing to launch". The local-existence check at fm-base-branch.sh:95-98 is dead code. Neither tests/fm-base-branch.test.sh nor tests/fm-spawn-base-branch.test.sh covers no-remote combined with a declared override. Fix by distinguishing the remote-less override (e.g. emit a source that routes to the `refs/heads/$BASE_BRANCH` arm, or emit `-` as the remote and have place_worker_on_base treat an absent remote as the local-ref path). - ⚠️ `bin/fm-base-branch.sh:102` - The remote-less path resolves the base from `git symbolic-ref --short --quiet HEAD`, i.e. whatever branch the primary clone currently has checked out, and labels it `local-default`. bin/fm-ff-lib.sh:37-51 already owns this resolution and deliberately does the opposite - it reads the default-branch ref and falls back to main/master, with the comment on line 53-57 explaining that reading HEAD would let "a primary stranded on a feature branch" propagate that stray branch to the fleet. This change reintroduces exactly that failure mode for remote-less projects: if the clone happens to sit on a feature branch, every ship and scout worker is checked out onto it and the state record asserts `base_branch_source=local-default`, which reads as authoritative. Reuse `default_branch()` from fm-ff-lib.sh (or replicate its ref-then-main/master order) instead of reading HEAD. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-base-branch.sh:136` - None of the new network operations is bounded: `ls-remote --exit-code --heads` (line 116), `ls-remote --symref` (line 136), and the `git fetch` in bin/fm-spawn.sh:905. The script already recognises that a spawn path must not block - line 88-90 exports GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 precisely because "an interactive prompt in a spawn path hangs the launch instead of failing it" - but a stalled TCP connect or an unresponsive SSH host hangs identically and is not covered, so the fail-loud contract silently degrades into hang-forever. This now blocks every ship/scout spawn and, via bin/fm-brief.sh:255, every brief scaffold. Wrap the three calls in a bounded timeout (or set `-c http.lowSpeedLimit`/`GIT_SSH_COMMAND` connect timeouts) so an unreachable remote hits the existing refusal path instead of stalling. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:255` - fm-brief.sh invokes fm-base-branch.sh without `--name`, so the registry lookup uses the basename of the physically-resolved directory (`pwd -P` in fm-base-branch.sh:74), while bin/fm-spawn.sh:883-884 passes `--name "$(basename "$PROJ_ABS")"` derived from the logical path. For a project directory reached through a symlink whose link name differs from the target name, the brief can consult a different registry entry than the spawn does and therefore name a branch the worker is not actually placed on. Harmless in the common case and the brief is best-effort by design, but passing `--name "$REPO"` here would make the two agree. Note also that this adds a live network round-trip to every ship/scout scaffold that fm-spawn.sh repeats moments later. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1676` - AGENTS.md:93 enumerates the fields fm-spawn writes into `<id>.meta` (`window=, endpoint_task_id=, worktree=, project=, harness=, model=, effort=, kind=, mode=, yolo=, tasktmp=`) and was not extended with the new `base_branch=`/`base_branch_source=`, and docs/architecture.md:213 still describes `data/projects.md` as recording only "each project's delivery mode and optional `+yolo` autonomy flag" with no mention of the `base=` token. docs/scripts.md and the new architecture.md paragraph were updated, so these two are the remaining stale spots in the same contract surface. 🔧 Fix: fix remote-less base overrides and bound spawn network reads 5 issues (1 warning, 4 infos) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-git-net-lib.sh:47` - The perl fallback ends with `waitpid $pid, 0; exit($? >> 8)`, which discards signal deaths: when the child is killed by a signal, perl's `$?` carries the signal in the low byte and 0 in the high byte, so `$? >> 8` is 0 and fm_git_net_run reports success for a command that never completed. This branch is the primary path on stock macOS, where neither `timeout` nor `gtimeout` exists. The consequence lands in bin/fm-spawn.sh:913-919: a signal-killed `git fetch` yields fetch_status=0, so the code proceeds to `git checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD`. FETCH_HEAD is a per-worktree ref, and treehouse hands out pooled worktrees, so a reused worktree still holds FETCH_HEAD from an earlier task's fetch - the checkout succeeds and silently places the worker on a stale commit, which is the exact defect class this change exists to prevent. It also lets the `ls-remote --exit-code --heads` check at bin/fm-base-branch.sh:135 report a declared branch as present on the remote without ever verifying it. Propagate the signal instead, e.g. `exit($? & 127 ? 128 + ($? & 127) : $? >> 8)`. Note the same one-liner exists verbatim at bin/fm-vendor-auth-probe.sh:143, so this is a copied house pattern rather than a new invention, but the consequence here is materially worse than a probe reporting the wrong availability. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-git-net-lib.sh:43` - The `timeout`/`gtimeout` branches send only SIGTERM at the deadline, while the perl branch deliberately escalates (`kill TERM` then 0.2s then `kill KILL`). GNU `timeout` without `-k` keeps waiting if the child ignores or blocks SIGTERM, so on that path the "hard deadline" is not actually hard and the hang this lib exists to prevent can still occur. Adding `-k 5s` would make the two branches behave the same. Separately, the 125 sentinel documented at line 17 collides with GNU `timeout`'s own 125 ("timeout itself failed"), so `fm_git_net_reason` can claim the watchdog could not start when it did. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-base-branch.sh:106` - The remote-less branch is selected purely by `git remote get-url "$REMOTE"` failing, so an FM_BASE_BRANCH_REMOTE naming a remote that is not configured (a typo, or a project that uses `upstream` in one clone and not another) silently falls through to `default_branch "$PROJ_ABS"`. That helper hardcodes `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` (bin/fm-ff-lib.sh:39), i.e. the cached value this whole script exists to distrust, and the result is reported as an authoritative `local-default` with no fetch. Harmless at the default `origin` (removing a remote prunes its refs), but it turns a misconfigured override into the silent stale-branch outcome rather than the loud refusal the rest of the script guarantees. Refusing when FM_BASE_BRANCH_REMOTE was explicitly set but is not a configured remote would close it. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-base-branch.sh:121` - The intent states: "A remote-less project resolves to its own local default; a remote-less clone on a detached HEAD resolves to nothing at all and deliberately leaves the worktree exactly where it was, preserving pre-existing behavior." Switching to `default_branch` narrows that second clause: a remote-less clone at a detached HEAD that still has a `main` or `master` branch now resolves to it and the worktree IS moved; only a clone with no `main`/`master` reaches `none`. tests/fm-base-branch.test.sh and tests/fm-spawn-base-branch.test.sh were updated to match by renaming `main` to `trunk` before asserting `none`. This follows directly from the round-1 fix you accepted (which restated the invariant as "a clone with no resolvable default branch reports 'none'"), and the script header at lines 123-125 was updated accordingly, so this is almost certainly just stale intent wording - flagging it so the narrowing is an explicit decision rather than an unnoticed side effect. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-git-net-lib.sh:37` - `fm_git_net_run` and bin/fm-vendor-auth-probe.sh's `run_timed` (line 135-147) are now the same timeout/gtimeout/perl selection with the same perl one-liner in two places, differing only in the env prefix, the `</dev/null`, and the no-watchdog sentinel (125 vs 124). Now that a shared lib exists, having the probe source it would leave one copy of the watchdog to keep correct - relevant given the signal-status issue above lives in both. 🔧 Fix: harden bounded git watchdog and refuse misconfigured remotes 2 infos still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-git-net-lib.sh:53` - The timeout branch went from the portable `timeout "$secs" "$@"` to `timeout -k "0.2s" "$secs" "$@"`. Both the `-k` flag and the fractional `0.2s` duration are GNU-coreutils surface; a busybox `timeout` on PATH (older builds have no `-k` at all, and duration-suffix parsing varies) rejects the invocation with a usage error, so the command never runs and every bounded call - and therefore every ship/scout spawn - refuses. Because `command -v timeout` succeeds, the perl branch that would have worked is never reached. tests/fm-base-branch.test.sh:361 also asserts exactly 124 for the deadline, which holds for GNU timeout but not for a busybox one that exits 128+SIGTERM. Not a concern on the macOS + ubuntu-runner hosts this actually targets, but probing the flag once (or preferring the perl branch when `timeout -k 0s true` fails) would keep the fallback reachable. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-base-branch.sh:126` - The new refusal fires whenever `$REMOTE` is absent while any other remote exists, which is the behavior you asked for. The gap is the escape hatch it points at: the message says "Point FM_BASE_BRANCH_REMOTE at one of those", but FM_BASE_BRANCH_REMOTE is a process-wide environment variable while the refusal is per-project, and the registry's `base=` override names a branch rather than a remote. A fleet holding one clone made with `git clone -o upstream` alongside normal `origin` clones therefore has no setting that satisfies both: leaving it unset hard-fails every spawn for that project, setting it breaks all the others. Worth confirming whether that project shape should instead be expressible in data/projects.md (e.g. a `remote=` token alongside `base=`), or whether it is genuinely out of scope and the refusal message should just say so rather than suggesting a knob that cannot be set per project. 🔧 Fix: probe watchdog support and narrow remote refusal 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-git-net-lib.sh:114` - The canonical-deadline normalization you asked for ("the busybox 128+SIGTERM exit and GNU's 124 are indistinguishable to callers") is implemented at lines 114-116 but nothing exercises it. The new test_bounded_run_skips_a_watchdog_that_rejects_the_invocation covers only the other half - a fake `timeout` that rejects `-k` and is therefore skipped at selection - so the fake never actually runs a command, and every watchdog that does run in the suite (GNU timeout, gtimeout, perl) reports 124 natively and takes the line 111 shortcut. The unexercised path is the subtle one: it depends on the `elapsed >= secs` guard being right, which is what keeps an immediate signal death (143 at elapsed 0) from being mislabelled a deadline. A fake `timeout` that accepts `-k`, sleeps its seconds argument, then exits 143 would pin both halves - normalized to the canonical deadline when it ran the full bound, still 143 when it did not.
⚠️ **Test** - 1 info - ℹ️ `tests/fm-kimi-harness.test.sh` - tests/fm-kimi-harness.test.sh fails on this host ("not ok - Kimi hook install refused a realistic config") because bin/fm-kimi-turnend-hook.sh requires python3 with tomllib and the host python3 is 3.10.0. Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated: the same assertion fails when the test is run from the base commit cd73e75, and no file in this change touches the Kimi harness. Not fixable from within the worktree (it needs a python3 >= 3.11 on PATH, a global toolchain change). - `bash bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-base-branch.test.sh tests/fm-spawn-base-branch.test.sh tests/fm-brief.test.sh` - all pass - `bash bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed --base cd73e75e02a1c1e74811b00c5ee08ffae8a59e1e` (37 scripts; run in three chunks after the first invocation hit my own 10-minute command timeout) - only the pre-existing Kimi/tomllib failure - Manual before/after E2E: real `bin/fm-spawn.sh` from cd73e75 (extracted via `git archive`) and from 60a3a6b, run against identical fixtures with a stale cached `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD=main`, a remote defaulting to `develop`, and `AscendApp/Shared/Services/RemoteConfig/RemoteConfigService.swift` present only on develop - Manual check that a refused spawn creates no backend endpoint: fake `tmux`/`treehouse`/`herdr` logging every invocation during a `base=nonexistent-branch` spawn - Manual registry matrix comparing `bin/fm-project-mode.sh <name>` output at cd73e75 vs 60a3a6b across legacy, `[mode]`, `[mode +yolo]`, `[mode +yolo base=…]`, `[mode base=… +yolo]`, and malformed `base=` entries, plus the new `--base` query - Manual bounded-read check: `FM_GIT_NET_TIMEOUT=4 FM_GIT_NET_FORCE_FALLBACK=0|1 bin/fm-base-branch.sh` against an unroutable `git://192.0.2.1/...` remote - Manual `bin/fm-brief.sh` runs showing the resolved branch named in the scaffold and the generic fallback when unresolvable - `git -C <task worktree> status -sb` / `symbolic-ref -q HEAD` to confirm detached-HEAD placement on the resolved tip
⚠️ **Document** - 1 info - ℹ️ `docs/architecture.md:148` - docs/architecture.md now documents fail-loud, remote-resolved base branches for spawn, while fm-teardown.sh, fm-merge-local.sh, fm-review-diff.sh, fm-fleet-sync.sh, fm-ff-lib.sh and fm-tangle-lib.sh still resolve the default branch from the clone's cached refs/remotes/origin/HEAD (docs/architecture.md:148 and :284 describe that older behavior accurately). The intent marks those paths out of scope, so I left both the code and their docs untouched; a follow-up should either converge them on fm-base-branch.sh or state the asymmetry once in docs/architecture.md.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: docs: add instruction-ablation doctrine to maintenance guidance
body:
After a material model upgrade or evidence that instructions are stale, test removals in a bounded isolated run and restore only instructions whose absence causes repeated failures.

This single-sentence addition to AGENTS.md's 'Maintaining this file' section documents the instruction-ablation practice for keeping the always-loaded contract concise and fit.

title: fix(bin): harden Codex startup and session locks

## Intent The developer wanted a Firstmate repository change carried through the no-mistakes workflow to a review-ready PR with green checks. The concrete work was to fix a narrow bootstrap test-harness isolation issue and update stale startup prose examples, with focused startup, lock, and wake shell suites passing. They expected the normal gated phases to run, including review, tests, docs, lint, push, PR creation, and CI, but not to merge without explicit approval. The resulting PR was #1531 in kunchenguid/firstmate. ## What Changed - Fix Codex startup detection, lock ownership, and renewal paths so primary sessions, inherited worker environments, stale locks, and denied process scans keep the intended guard behavior. - Tighten bootstrap and session-start diagnostics for GitHub auth, sandbox network status, skill budget reporting, and marker precedence, with matching startup and supervision docs. - Expand shell coverage for bootstrap, session start, session-start nudge, guard, and secondmate harness startup isolation paths. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The branch changes are narrowly scoped to startup diagnostics, lock ownership/lease behavior, and documentation, and the previous Codex inherited-marker renewal path now routes through the shared current-identity check before renewal; I found no remaining source-verifiable blockers. ## Testing Inspected the focused diff and startup prose, ran the targeted bootstrap, lock, session-start, nudge, and wake/guard shell suites, then captured an end-user CLI transcript showing Codex thread lock acquisition, competing-session read-only refusal, guard lease renewal, silent duplicate SessionStart nudge, and the new bootstrap diagnostics; all exercised checks passed.

title: feat(bin): arm forge branch cleanup at project initialization
body:
## Intent

Close the one delegated link in firstmate's trunk-based branch-cleanup chain.

Problem: every step of the chain is enforced in bin/ except the forge step. Merge is a squash by default (bin/fm-pr-merge.sh); the local task branch is deleted at teardown after the landed-work test (bin/fm-teardown.sh); local branches whose upstream reads [gone] are pruned on sync (bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh). Nothing sets or checks the forge's delete_branch_on_merge setting. The two ends are coupled: fleet-sync only prunes a local branch once its upstream reads [gone], which only happens after the remote branch is deleted, so a repo with the setting off silently breaks BOTH ends - remote branches accumulate and locals are never pruned - while every script still reports success. This was verified in the field on a repo in this fleet.

What was asked for: project initialization should set or verify delete_branch_on_merge for no-mistakes and direct-PR projects so the chain is never half-armed. Requirements accepted at intake:
- Do it where initialization already happens, and keep the one-owner rule: the project-management skill owns the procedure, the script owns the mechanics.
- Lack of admin rights must NOT fail the project add. Users work against repos they cannot configure (this fleet contributes to a read-only upstream through a fork). Report it as an actionable diagnostic and continue.
- Verify, do not blindly set: report when it was already correct, when it was changed, and when it could not be.
- Consider recommending squash-only merges alongside it, but do NOT silently change a repo's merge methods - that is a stronger change than branch cleanup and belongs behind its own explicit decision.

Acceptance criteria: a newly added no-mistakes or direct-PR project ends with the setting on, or with a clear diagnostic naming exactly why it could not be; existing projects are unaffected until re-initialized; colocated tests cover already-on, turned-on, and no-permission; documentation reflects the new initialization behavior in whichever file already owns that contract, without creating a new file.

Constraints: nothing from any private project may appear in this work - no product names, routes, schemas, business detail, or examples drawn from the captain's repos, in code, tests, comments, commit messages, or docs; generic examples only, because this lands in a public upstream repository. Branches push to the configured fork and the PR opens against the upstream repository; do not push to origin directly.

Deliberate decisions made while implementing, which a reviewer reading only the diff would not know:
- New script bin/fm-project-branch-cleanup.sh owns the mechanics; the project-management skill's Initialize section owns the procedure. This split is required by firstmate's one-owner rule (see the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill, which was loaded before editing because this changes firstmate's own shared tracked material).
- It uses gh directly rather than gh-axi on purpose: gh-axi repo edit exposes no --delete-branch-on-merge flag, and bin/fm-pr-check.sh and bin/fm-teardown.sh already fall back to plain gh for capabilities the wrapper does not cover.
- All non-usage blockers (missing gh, unreachable or non-GitHub remote, HTTP 403 from a repo the account cannot administer, an edit that silently does not take) print a single BRANCH_CLEANUP_BLOCKED line and exit 0 by design. Exiting non-zero would fail the project add, which the intake explicitly forbids. Exit 2 is reserved for usage and precondition errors (missing argument, path that is not a Git working tree).
- The success path re-reads the setting after the edit rather than trusting gh repo edit's exit status, because the setting taking effect is the only real evidence; an edit that exits clean without applying is reported as blocked.
- The script reports other allowed merge methods as a BRANCH_CLEANUP_INFO advisory and never changes them, per the explicit instruction not to silently alter merge methods.
- Wiring: bin/fm-test-run.sh gained the new test in the pr-forge family and the new script in the pr-forge changed-file mapping (its coverage guard requires every tests/*.test.sh to be in a lane). docs/scripts.md gained a toolbelt row. No new documentation file was created, as instructed.
- tests/fm-project-branch-cleanup.test.sh covers the three required cases plus missing gh, an ineffective edit, merge-methods-reported-not-changed, and the exit-2 preconditions. The missing-gh case symlinks bash, git, and sed into an otherwise empty PATH so the gh lookup genuinely finds nothing while the script's own interpreter still resolves.

## What Changed

- New `bin/fm-project-branch-cleanup.sh` verifies, and sets when needed, a project clone's GitHub `delete_branch_on_merge`, re-reading the setting after the edit so only an applied change reports `BRANCH_CLEANUP: enabled`. A missing `gh`, an unreachable or non-GitHub remote, a 403 from a repository the account cannot administer, and an edit that does not take each print one `BRANCH_CLEANUP_BLOCKED:` line and exit 0; exit 2 is reserved for usage and precondition errors. A fork's parent and any other allowed merge methods are reported as `BRANCH_CLEANUP_INFO:` advisories and never changed.
- The `project-management` skill's Initialize section now runs that script for every `no-mistakes` and `direct-PR` project, brings `direct-PR` into the forge step while leaving `local-only` out, and instructs the relaying agent to pass blocked and info lines through with their concrete reason and continue the add.
- Wiring and coverage: `bin/fm-test-run.sh` places the new suite in the `pr-forge` family and maps the new script's changed path to that lane, `docs/scripts.md` gains a toolbelt row, and colocated `tests/fm-project-branch-cleanup.test.sh` covers 9 cases including already-on, turned-on, no-permission, missing `gh`, an ineffective edit, the fork advisory, and the exit-2 preconditions.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The round-5 delta is a scoping phrase in one diagnostic string plus the restored header sentence and a widened test needle, with no behavior change, and the cumulative branch is now verified clean against every acceptance criterion and every constraint from the prior rulings.

## Testing

Ran the new colocated suite (9/9 pass), the test-runner coverage guard and lane/changed-path selection checks that this diff wires, and the documentation-audiences suite for the SKILL.md and docs/scripts.md edits. For product-level evidence I drove the unmodified script the way project initialization does and captured a CLI transcript: against the real GitHub CLI and real repository it reports already-on with a logged call trail proving no edit was attempted (verified read-only beforehand that the setting was on and the account has READ only, so nothing could be mutated); against a stub forge it turns the setting off→on and confirms it with a re-read, reports HTTP 403 as an exit-0 diagnostic while leaving the setting untouched, and reports fork and merge-method advisories without issuing any merge-method edit. A simulated add relays the blocker and still completes, and a caller grep shows only initialization invokes the step. No UI surface is involved, so the artifact is a CLI transcript rather than a screenshot. Everything targeted at this change passes; the only failure was one intermittent, pre-existing timing race in the test runner's own jobs=2 scheduler case.

title: fix(bin): refuse merges of unverified pull request heads
body:
## Intent Make bin/fm-pr-merge.sh refuse to merge a pull request head it has not verified. Context: on upstream PR 1530 every validation gate passed with zero findings and the pipeline reported checks-passed, but upstream CI was held at action_required because a cross-repo fork PR needs maintainer approval before workflows dispatch. Zero check runs existed and that absence was read as success. The pipeline binary is installed at ~/.local/bin/no-mistakes with no source in this repo and is deliberately NOT in scope. What is in scope: bin/fm-pr-merge.sh was 84 lines and verified nothing - no reference to check_runs, conclusion, statusCheckRollup, or mergeable anywhere - so the captain's standing 'never merge a red PR' rule was enforced only by firstmate remembering to check by hand every time. The change: before merging, fm-pr-merge.sh re-reads the pull request's CURRENT head in one 'gh pr view --json headRefOid,mergeable,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup' call and refuses when (1) zero check runs exist on that head, (2) any check run is not SUCCESS, (3) the PR is not MERGEABLE, or (4) a review requests changes. Every refusal names the concrete failing condition and the exact head SHA it evaluated, and leaves the task untouched: no recorded pr=, no armed merge poll, no gh-axi merge call. Deliberate decisions a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: - Re-evaluation happens at merge time rather than from a recorded value, because a PR can go red between an earlier check and the merge and state/.meta may carry a stale pr_head=. All four facts come from ONE gh call so the head named in a refusal is the same head the checks were read from. - The zero-check-runs refusal is deliberately separate from the failure-count refusal and has its own distinct message. This is the entire point of the task: an empty rollup and an all-successful rollup BOTH report zero failures, so folding them together reintroduces the defect. Verified against live data: PR 1530 returns checks=0/unsuccessful=0 while PR 1527 returns checks=10/unsuccessful=1. - ONLY SUCCESS passes. A skipped, neutral, cancelled, queued, or in-progress check all refuse. This was raised explicitly with the captain as a tradeoff (a project that path-filters jobs would hit the override routinely) and the captain confirmed keeping it fail-closed with no benign-conclusion allowlist, on the evidence that the last three merged PRs in this repo all produce 10/10 SUCCESS. Do not propose relaxing this to a skipped/neutral allowlist; it is a deliberate, confirmed choice. - mergeable=UNKNOWN refuses. GitHub computes mergeability asynchronously, so UNKNOWN means 'not yet known', never 'fine'. - An absent or failing gh, an unreadable head, or an unreadable check count all refuse rather than merging unverified. - --allow-unverified is the captain's explicit override: never a default, never inferred from an environment variable, and recognised only BEFORE the optional -- separator (after it, it is forwarded to gh-axi, which rejects it). It records merge_verification=override; a verified merge records merge_verification=verified plus merge_verified_head=, so absence of both keys reads as unknown rather than as verified. That positive record is deliberate, on the same absence-is-not-evidence reasoning as the guard itself. - Both new meta keys are written BEFORE any pr= line, because fm_pr_metadata_identity_parse in bin/fm-pr-lib.sh refuses any unknown key appearing after pr=. Writing them before keeps that identity contract valid at every instant, including the window before fm-pr-check.sh rewrites the file. Scope fence held deliberately: the torn-down-metadata refusal ('task metadata is unavailable' for a released task) is an open captain decision on a separate backlog item and is explicitly unchanged - the new guard composes with it and still fires after it, with a test asserting no forge lookup happens for a released task. No changes to teardown, metadata handling, routing, or dispatch. Verification approach: every refusal has a negative control that constructs the failing condition and watches the guard fire, plus positive controls proving a genuinely green PR still merges. I mutation-tested the guard seven ways (removing the zero-check branch, removing verification entirely, adding an env-var override fallback, treating non-success as success, skipping the mergeable check, skipping the review check, dropping the head SHA from the message, and reverting the count validation) and confirmed each mutant is killed by exactly the right assertion. Tests are colocated behavioural tests that drive the executable and never assert implementation-source bytes. One test is gated on jq and drives the script's real -q query through a fixture-backed fake forge against API-shaped JSON (empty rollup, null rollup, all-success, in-progress, ACTION_REQUIRED, legacy StatusContext success and failure), so the query itself is under test and not just the branch logic; jq produces byte-identical output to the gojq engine gh embeds. I also found and fixed the same absence-as-success shape in my own first validator: it concatenated the two counts before the digit check, so an empty check count paired with a zero failure count passed validation and then fell through both numeric comparisons into a merge. Each count is now validated independently, with its own negative control. tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh's gh mock matched ' headRefOid ' with surrounding spaces and so did not answer the new multi-field verification call; it was taught that call with a green default, since the merge path now makes an additional forge read. That suite passes. Docs updated at their owners: bin/fm-pr-merge.sh's header owns the refusal list and override mechanics, docs/architecture.md's merge paragraph, docs/scripts.md's one-line summary, and AGENTS.md's meta-key inventory plus one sentence in the merge-authority section. bin/fm-lint.sh and bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh are clean. ## What Changed - Re-verify a pull request’s current head before merging and refuse heads with missing or non-successful checks, non-mergeable state, requested changes, or unreadable verification data. - Add an explicit `--allow-unverified` override and record whether the merge used a verified head or the override in task metadata. - Add behavioral coverage for verification, override, race, and failure paths, and document the guarded merge contract. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The requested two-stage verification is implemented correctly and the prior race is substantially narrowed, but the explicitly accepted and documented non-atomic window between final verification and merge remains pending the repository-owner decision. ## Testing Inspected the target diff, ran the focused merge-guard and caller-security behavioral suites, then exercised the real CLI with empty and green rollups; the guard refused the unverified head without side effects and merged only the verified head, with the complete interaction preserved as evidence.

title: feat(bin): add opt-in visual-evidence contract to generated ship briefs
body:
## Intent Make firstmate's brief scaffold (bin/fm-brief.sh) generate a visual-evidence contract for frontend ship tasks. WHY: Firstmate briefs currently say nothing about how a change should be *shown*. Observed repeatedly: workers describe a UI change in prose, screenshot the 'before' only when pushed, dump one full-page image at the top instead of evidence beside each claim, and never produce an 'after' artifact at all. Every review then costs a round of the captain asking for what should have arrived the first time. Root cause: prototyping costs budget at the moment of choosing and only repays a round later, so no worker spends it unprompted. The brief has to require it. THE CONTRACT THE GENERATED BRIEF MUST REQUIRE (five points, specified by the requester): 1. Before is a screenshot of the real page at the real route - never a description of the current look. 2. After is always an artifact. In order of preference: a screenshot of the change running in a throwaway prototype; a rendered mock in the project's own design system; a diagram. Prose alone is not an acceptable 'after'. If prototyping the after looks too expensive, that is evidence the change is under-specified - not an exemption. 3. One tight screenshot per claim, placed beside the claim it evidences - not a page dump at the top that the reader must map back onto the text. 4. Crop and annotate to the region that changed. A full-page image proving a button moved makes the reviewer do the diffing. 5. Prose is reserved for what cannot be shown - rationale, trade-offs, open questions. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: fm-brief.sh emits this section for frontend ship tasks and does not bloat briefs where it is irrelevant. How 'frontend' is determined was explicitly left to the implementer's design, with an explicit flag called acceptable and probably better than inference, since the scaffold cannot see the task text. The generated wording must be self-contained so a worker reading only the brief knows what to produce. Colocated tests must cover that the section appears when requested and is absent otherwise. --help and any doc that already owns the scaffold's contract must be updated, and NO new doc may be added. DECISIONS MADE WHILE IMPLEMENTING (deliberate, not accidents): - Chose an explicit opt-in --visual-evidence flag over inference, as the requester suggested: {TASK} is filled in after scaffolding, so the scaffold cannot see whether the work is visual. - Ship-only. --scout and --secondmate are rejected with an error and no file written. Rationale: the contract is about how a delivered change is shown for review, and a scout already owes evidence through its report. - Deliberately asymmetric with --herdr-lab: omitting --visual-evidence emits NOTHING - no 'NOT ENABLED' declaration - because a missing visual contract costs a review round, not safety, and the acceptance criteria forbid bloating briefs where it is irrelevant. This asymmetry is intentional and should not be 'fixed' into a declaration. - Verified and preserved byte-identical output for briefs scaffolded without the flag (ship, scout, and secondmate), by giving the section variable its own leading newline and keeping the trailing one. - Built the section with 'IFS= read -r -d ... </evidence/`, which the flag also renders into the brief's rule 2 as the single stay-inside-the-worktree exception, in the same class as the status-file append. Artifact links are required beside each claim in the PR body as soon as it exists or in the hand-back when no PR is opened, with prose that carries the claim on its own. - Docs updated in their existing owners with no new file: the script header (which is `--help`), an AGENTS.md section 11 dispatch trigger beside the `--herdr-lab` trigger plus a home-layout entry for `/evidence/`, and the one-line `fm-brief.sh` row in `docs/scripts.md`. `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` adds colocated cases covering that the section renders in full when requested, is absent otherwise, and that the flag is rejected for scout and secondmate briefs. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Round 5 adds two sentences to the opt-in section plus one documentation-inventory line, both previously identified fixes; byte-identity for all seven unflagged variants still holds including Rule 2, every positive and negative assertion matches real generated output, and no acceptance criterion is left unmet. ## Testing Exercised the change as an end user of the scaffold: ran the full colocated tests/fm-brief.test.sh (19 cases, all pass, including the two new visual-evidence cases), then generated real briefs with and without --visual-evidence and rendered them side by side as screenshots showing the five-point contract present in the flagged brief and completely absent - with no "NOT ENABLED" declaration - in the unflagged one. Verified the deliberate no-bloat guarantee by regenerating six unflagged scaffolds (ship across all three delivery modes, scout, secondmate, --herdr-lab) from both the base and target commits into an identical home path and confirming byte-for-byte identical output; verified the ship-only guard rejects --scout and --secondmate with exit 1 and no file written; verified macOS stock Bash 3.2 both parses the script and produces a brief identical to the Bash 5 output with no leaked heredoc marker; verified --help and the doc-inventory test after the AGENTS.md and docs/scripts.md edits, and that no new file was added. A mutation check against the pre-change script confirmed both new tests actually fail without the feature. Everything passed and no issues surfaced; transient temp homes were removed and the worktree is clean. - Evidence: Rendered generated briefs, side by side: without the flag (left) vs --visual-evidence (right) (local file: /var/folders/40/vfb2wp5n78d1nbkbdk7sv6f40000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZ0S73WYZREZE8F9ZB0SH1C9/brief-flag-vs-no-flag.png) - Evidence: Cropped: the visual-evidence section the flag adds to the generated brief (local file: /var/folders/40/vfb2wp5n78d1nbkbdk7sv6f40000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZ0S73WYZREZE8F9ZB0SH1C9/visual-evidence-section-crop.png)
Evidence: Generated ship brief with --visual-evidence (raw markdown a crewmate reads) ```text You are a crewmate: an autonomous worker agent managed by firstmate. Work on your own; do not wait for a human. # Task {TASK} # Herdr lifecycle declaration - NOT ENABLED **HARD SAFETY GATE:** this scaffold cannot inspect the task text that replaces `{TASK}` later. If the task will start, stop, delete, restart, profile, or otherwise drive Herdr lifecycle behavior, stop and regenerate the brief with `--herdr-lab` before dispatch. Do not add Herdr lifecycle commands to this unguarded brief by hand. # Setup You are in a disposable git worktree of example-web-app, at a detached HEAD on a clean default branch. **Verify isolation before anything else.** Run `pwd -P` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; both must resolve to the disposable task worktree you were launched in, such as a treehouse pool path or an Orca-managed worktree, not the primary checkout firstmate operates from. The path check is authoritative: `git rev-parse --git-dir` and `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` can help inspect the repo, but they do not prove you are outside the primary checkout. If the top-level path is the primary checkout or not the worktree you were launched in, STOP - do not branch or commit here - append `blocked: launched in primary checkout, not an isolated worktree` to the status file and stop. 1. First action: create your branch: `git checkout -b fm/redesign-settings-page` # Rules 1. Never push to the default branch (push only your `fm/redesign-settings-page` branch). Never merge a PR. 2. Stay inside this worktree; modify nothing outside it. The single exception is this task's own visual-evidence directory `'/tmp/firstmate-demo-home/data/redesign-settings-page/evidence'` in the firstmate home, described under Visual evidence below. That is the same class of write, to the same home, as the status file you append to in rule 4: every brief already writes that one file outside its worktree. It authorizes nothing else - not another task's record directory, not that home's shared files, not any other path. 3. Use gh-axi for GitHub operations and chrome-devtools-axi for browser operations. 4. Report status by appending one line: `echo "{state}: {one short line}" >> '/tmp/firstmate-demo-home/state/redesign-settings-page.status'` States: working, needs-decision, blocked, paused, done, failed. Each append wakes firstmate, so report sparingly: only phase changes a supervisor would act on (setup done, bug reproduced, fix implemented, validation passed) and the needs-decision/blocked/paused/done/failed states. No step-by-step FYI progress lines; firstmate reads your pane for that. A mid-task `working:` line (including setup complete) is nonterminal: do not end the turn after it; continue the same stage until a defined `done:` gate under Definition of done. Use `paused: {why}` - distinct from `blocked:` - ONLY when you are deliberately idling on a known external wait you expect to clear on its own (an upstream release, a rate-limit reset, a scheduled window): firstmate then leaves your idle pane alone and rechecks it on a long cadence instead of treating it as a possible wedge. Use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need help. 5. If you hit the same obstacle twice, append `blocked: {why}` and stop; firstmate will help. 6. If a decision belongs above the implementation worker (product choices, destructive actions, ask-user findings), append `needs-decision: {summary of options}` and stop. Firstmate will apply the configured authority and reply with the decision. When firstmate replies or a blocker clears and you resume, append `resolved: {how it was decided or unblocked}` (add the same `[key=]` if you opened it with one) so the decision or blocker is durably closed and does not keep resurfacing. 7. Never stop, restart, or update the shared `no-mistakes` daemon - it is one instance serving every lane/home, so restarting it kills other lanes' in-flight pipeline runs. On ANY no-mistakes daemon error, append `blocked: {the daemon error}` and stop; only firstmate manages the daemon. # Visual evidence - show the change, do not describe it This task changes a user-visible surface, so every claim about how it looks must arrive as a capture of the real thing, not as prose. The medium follows the surface: a browser view is captured as a screenshot of the real page at the real route, terminal or CLI output as the real transcript of the real command, a generated file or payload as its real content. 1. **Before is a capture of the real surface as it stands today.** Run the project, reach the affected surface, and capture it: the real page at the real route, the real command with its real output, the real generated content. A written description of the current look is never a before. The one exception is a surface that does not exist yet - say so in a line and go straight to the after. 2. **After is always an artifact, never prose alone.** In order of preference: a capture of the change running in a throwaway prototype; a mock rendered in the project's own design system; a diagram. If prototyping the after looks too expensive, that is evidence the change is under-specified - settle what it should be first. It is not an exemption. The single carve-out is a change no still capture can hold, meaning motion, timing, or a measurement, and then a recording or the measured result is the artifact. Name the form you used and why a still could not carry the claim. "I could not show it" with nothing attached is not a carve-out; it is a missing after. 3. **One tight capture per claim, placed beside the claim it evidences.** Do not dump a single full-page image or an entire transcript at the top and leave the reader to map it back onto the text. 4. **Crop and annotate down to the region that changed.** A full-page image offered as proof that one element moved, or a whole log offered as proof of one changed line, makes the reviewer do the diffing. 5. **Prose is reserved for what cannot be shown** - rationale, trade-offs, and open questions. ## Producing the artifacts Build every prototype and capture inside this worktree, under `.fm-scratch/`: create the directory and write a single `*` line into `.fm-scratch/.gitignore`, which hides the whole directory from git without touching the project's own ignore file. A prototype is scratch: never commit it to your `fm/redesign-settings-page` branch, and expect it to die with this worktree. Capture browser surfaces with `chrome-devtools-axi`. If you conclude an artifact cannot be produced without writing outside this worktree and its evidence directory, append `blocked: {why}` and stop; that is an escalation, not a licence to write anywhere else. ## Delivering the artifacts Copy every artifact you present out of `.fm-scratch/` into this task's own evidence directory, which outlives this worktree: run `mkdir -p '/tmp/firstmate-demo-home/data/redesign-settings-page/evidence'` and copy them there, keeping the layout flat with one file per claim. Link each artifact by its path beside the claim it evidences - in the pull request body when this project opens one, in the summary you hand back when it does not - never as a block at the bottom. When the pull request is opened for you, add those links to its body with `gh-axi` as soon as it exists; when you open it yourself, write them into the body you author; when there is no pull request, name this directory in the hand-back you return. Adding those links is not a code edit and not a findings fix, so it is not the hand-editing that an active validation run forbids. Write each claim so the prose carries it on its own: a path is opaque to a reader who cannot open the file, so the sentence states what changed and the artifact confirms it. That is not prose standing in for an after; the artifact stays mandatory. Accept the one limitation rather than working around it: a reviewer who is not on this machine cannot open these files, so for work whose pull request goes to a public upstream the artifacts are the captain's verification rather than the upstream reviewer's, and the self-carrying prose above is what keeps that pull request readable for both. That is also why the artifacts go nowhere else, not to a gist and not to any other host: a secret gist is unlisted rather than access-controlled, so anyone holding the link could read captures of a private product. # Project memory If `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` already exists, or if this task produced durable project-intrinsic knowledge, run `/Users/axvon/.no-mistakes/worktrees/74bf7f97ec45/01KZ0S73WYZREZE8F9ZB0SH1C9/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh .` in the worktree. Do NOT run /no-mistakes. The configured merge authority decides whether to merge the PR; firstmate relays the outcome. ```

when you open it yourself, write them into the body you author; when there is no pull request, name this directory in the hand-back you return. +Adding those links is not a code edit and not a findings fix, so it is not the hand-editing that an active validation run forbids. +Write each claim so the prose carries it on its own: a path is opaque to a reader who cannot open the file, so the sentence states what changed and the artifact confirms it. That is not prose standing in for an after; the artifact stays mandatory. +Accept the one limitation rather than working around it: a reviewer who is not on this machine cannot open these files, so for work whose pull request goes to a public upstream the artifacts are the captain's verification rather than the upstream reviewer's, and the self-carrying prose above is what keeps that pull request readable for both. +That is also why the artifacts go nowhere else, not to a gist and not to any other host: a secret gist is unlisted rather than access-controlled, so anyone holding the link could read captures of a private product. + # Project memory If `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` already exists, or if this task produced durable project-intrinsic knowledge, run `/Users/axvon/.no-mistakes/worktrees/74bf7f97ec45/01KZ0S73WYZREZE8F9ZB0SH1C9/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh .` in the worktree. Record only project knowledge useful to almost every future session. ```
Evidence: Ship-only guard: scout and secondmate rejected, no brief written $ bin/fm-brief.sh vis-scout someproj --scout --visual-evidence error: --visual-evidence applies only to crewmate ship briefs exit=1 $ FM_SECONDMATE_CHARTER=ops bin/fm-brief.sh vis-mate --secondmate --no-projects --visual-evidence error: --visual-evidence applies only to crewmate ship briefs exit=1 $ ls $FM_HOME/data # no brief written for either rejected scaffold demo-plain-02 demo-visual-01 projects.md ```text $ bin/fm-brief.sh vis-scout someproj --scout --visual-evidence error: --visual-evidence applies only to crewmate ship briefs exit=1 $ FM_SECONDMATE_CHARTER=ops bin/fm-brief.sh vis-mate --secondmate --no-projects --visual-evidence error: --visual-evidence applies only to crewmate ship briefs exit=1 $ ls $FM_HOME/data # no brief written for either rejected scaffold demo-plain-02 demo-visual-01 projects.md ```

Evidence: fm-brief.sh --help documenting the new flag ```text Scaffold a crewmate brief or persistent secondmate charter at data//brief.md under the active firstmate home. For ordinary tasks, the standard Setup/Rules/Definition-of-done contract is filled in. Firstmate then replaces the {TASK} placeholder with the task description, acceptance criteria, and context, and may adjust other sections when the task genuinely deviates (e.g. working an existing external PR instead of shipping a new one). Usage: fm-brief.sh [--scout] [--herdr-lab] [--visual-evidence] fm-brief.sh --secondmate {...|--no-projects} --scout writes the scout contract instead: the deliverable is a report at data//report.md (no branch, no push, no PR) and the worktree is scratch. --secondmate writes a persistent secondmate charter. The project list is cloned into the secondmate home, while the natural-language scope tells the main firstmate when to route work there; routine churn stays in its own home; captain-relevant escalations and marked from-firstmate replies append to this home's status file. --no-projects writes a project-less charter for a domain whose subject is the firstmate repo itself (its home is a firstmate worktree, its crews take pooled worktrees of the same repo). It is mutually exclusive with a project list, and omitting both still fails loudly so an accidental omission is never silent. Set FM_SECONDMATE_CHARTER='' to fill the charter text. Set FM_SECONDMATE_SCOPE='' to write a routing scope distinct from the charter text. --herdr-lab is mandatory when the task will issue Herdr lifecycle commands. It adds the hard isolation contract backed by bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh. The flag must be explicit because {TASK} is filled after scaffolding and the caller-supplied repo string cannot reliably identify this repo. Briefs made without it carry a loud declaration so an omitted contract cannot be silent. --visual-evidence adds the visual-evidence contract to a ship brief, for work that changes a user-visible surface. The generated contract requires: a "before" that is a capture of the real surface as it stands today, unless the surface does not exist yet; an "after" that is always an artifact, preferring a capture of the change running in a throwaway prototype, then a mock rendered in the project's own design system, then a diagram; one tight capture per claim placed beside that claim; cropping and annotation down to the region that changed; and prose reserved for rationale, trade-offs, and open questions. The after has one carve-out, for motion, timing, or a measurement no still capture can hold, which the worker must name and justify; an unattached "I could not show it" stays a missing after. The medium follows the surface (a browser view is a screenshot of the real route, CLI output is the real transcript of the real command, a generated file is its real content), so the contract fits non-browser surfaces too. Prototypes and captures are built inside the task worktree under a self-ignoring .fm-scratch/ and are never committed to the code branch; the artifacts that are presented are copied to this task's own record directory, data//evidence/, which the flag also names as the single exception to the brief's stay-inside-the-worktree rule 2 - the same class of write as the status file, scoped to this task and nothing else. Each artifact is linked by its path beside the claim it evidences - in the pull request body as soon as it exists, whoever opened it, or in the hand-back when the mode opens none - and the prose must carry that claim on its own, because a reviewer who is not on this machine cannot open the file: for upstream-facing work the artifacts are the captain's verification rather than the upstream reviewer's, which is an accepted limitation and the reason captures go to no other host. Prototyping the after costs budget when the worker chooses and only repays a review round later, so the brief has to require it or no worker spends it. The flag is explicit because {TASK} is filled in after scaffolding, so the scaffold cannot tell whether the work is visual. It is ship-only, and omitting it emits nothing at all: unlike Herdr lifecycle isolation, a missing visual contract costs a review round, not safety, so briefs for work with no user-visible surface must not carry a declaration. For ship tasks, the definition of done is shaped by the project's delivery mode (data/projects.md via fm-project-mode.sh; see the project-management skill and AGENTS.md task lifecycle): no-mistakes implement -> /no-mistakes pipeline -> PR -> captain merge (default) direct-PR implement -> push + open PR via gh-axi (no pipeline) -> captain merge local-only implement on branch, stop and report "ready in branch" (no push/PR); captain approves, firstmate merges to local main Ship briefs begin with a worktree-isolation assertion before the branch step. Scout tasks ignore mode - their deliverable is a report, not a merge. Every scaffold's status protocol distinguishes the configured declared-external-wait verb (FM_CLASSIFY_PAUSED_VERB, default "paused") from "blocked:": pause for a known external wait expected to clear on its own, blocked when firstmate must act. Ship tasks include a project-memory section so durable project-intrinsic learnings can be committed to AGENTS.md through the project's delivery path; it carries the AGENTS.md authoring bar (widely useful knowledge only, pointers over copied detail) and has the crewmate add the fm-ensure-agents-md.sh self-governance section when a touched project AGENTS.md lacks it. Refuses to overwrite an existing brief. ```
