✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 3 issues found → auto-fixed (4) ✅ - ⚠️ `AGENTS.md:475` - The dispatch trigger fires on "a user-visible surface", but the generated contract is browser-specific: bin/fm-brief.sh:394 demands "a screenshot of the real page at the real route" and "navigate to the affected view", and line 400 says "Capture screenshots with `chrome-devtools-axi`". Firstmate itself is a CLI/tmux tool and firstmate-repo ship briefs are routine (tests/fm-brief.test.sh:303 scaffolds with repo `firstmate`), so a ship task changing terminal or tmux output satisfies the trigger and receives a contract it cannot satisfy. The intent's acceptance criterion scopes this to "frontend ship tasks"; "user-visible surface" is wider. Narrowing the trigger to a browser-rendered surface (or widening the contract's point 1 to cover non-browser surfaces) would close the gap. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:394` - Point 1 requires the "before" to be a screenshot of the real page at the real route and explicitly rejects a prose description, but gives no alternative when the surface does not exist yet. A ship task adding a new route or component has no page to capture, so a worker reading only the brief - which the acceptance criteria require to be self-contained - is told to produce something impossible and must either fabricate a substitute or spend a needs-decision round. A single clause ("if the surface is new, say so and go straight to the after") would resolve it, but it changes the requester's verbatim point 1. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:392` - The contract tells the worker to place artifacts in "the PR description when this project opens a PR, otherwise the summary you hand back". In local-only mode the definition of done at bin/fm-brief.sh:349 is a single status append (`done: ready in branch fm/<id>`) with no PR and no report doc, and the worktree holding any captured images is torn down, so there is no durable place for screenshots. tests/fm-brief.test.sh:373 deliberately asserts the contract renders for local-only, so this mode is in scope by design. Naming a concrete location for the non-PR modes (for example a file committed on the branch) would make the wording self-contained across all three delivery modes. 🔧 Fix: broaden visual-evidence contract beyond browser and name artifact location 2 infos still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:398` - The section adds "Those artifacts and the status file are the only things you write outside the worktree.", which directly contradicts the ship brief's Rule 2 (bin/fm-brief.sh:426, rendered earlier in the same document as "Stay inside this worktree; modify nothing outside it.") with no back-reference. The scout brief avoids this by enumerating the exceptions inside its own rule 2 (bin/fm-brief.sh:291), but amending the ship rule 2 unconditionally would break the byte-identity invariant the author deliberately preserved for unflagged briefs. A short back-reference in the section ("as an exception to rule 2 above") would resolve it without touching the shared rules block. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:398` - The non-PR half of the destination is now concrete (`$DATA/$ID/`), but the PR half is not. In the default no-mistakes mode the PR body is authored by the pipeline, not the worker (see the DOD at bin/fm-brief.sh:357-375, which never tells the worker to author or edit the PR description), so "the PR description when this project opens a PR" names a surface the worker does not own and gives no timing. Separately, GitHub has no API or CLI path to attach image files to a PR body, so a screenshot - the flagship artifact the contract requires - has no reachable landing place in either PR mode using the `gh-axi` the brief mandates. Pointing all modes at `$DATA/$ID/` as the file home and having the PR body reference them would close it; the captain's round-1 instruction addressed only the non-PR case, so this is the residual half rather than a departure from that decision. 🔧 Fix: keep visual-evidence artifacts in-worktree, deliver via evidence ref 4 warnings still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:437` - `git switch --orphan` clears tracked files, and the project's root `.gitignore` is one of them. I verified in a scratch repo that on the orphan ref `git status --untracked-files=all` then lists `node_modules/`, `dist/`, and `.env` as untracked candidates - only `.fm-scratch/` stays hidden, because its ignore file is nested inside it. The contract then tells the worker to copy captures to that root, commit, and (in the PR modes, line 410) push the ref to a remote, but never says how to stage. A worker running `git add -A` there commits build output and secrets to a pushed branch, which defeats the access-control rationale the evidence-ref design exists to serve. One clause fixes it: stage the capture files, README.md, and capture scripts by name, and never `git add -A` on the evidence ref because the project's own ignore rules are not present there. Worth fixing in this change rather than as a follow-up, given the credential path. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:410` - In direct-PR mode Rule 1 renders as "Never push to the default branch (push only your `fm/<id>` branch). Never merge a PR." (built at bin/fm-brief.sh:344), but the delivery block tells the same worker to push `fm/<id>-evidence`. The mitigating clause "it is the only other ref you push, a sibling of your own branch and never the default branch" answers Rule 1's first sentence but not the parenthetical exclusivity. This is the same shape as the Rule 2 carve-out the captain ruled out last round, now on Rule 1, and the no-mistakes and local-only Rule 1 variants do not conflict - only direct-PR does. Because RULE1 is already built per-mode, widening just the direct-PR parenthetical when VISUAL_EVIDENCE is set would reconcile it without touching output for unflagged briefs. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:412` - The deletion requirement says `fm/<id>-evidence` "must be deleted once the pull request lands" without distinguishing the local ref from the pushed one, and the AGENTS.md line added at AGENTS.md:476 says only "delete that ref". I traced both cleanup paths: bin/fm-teardown.sh:1573 and :1589 delete only the branch checked out in the worktree, which is `fm/<id>`, and bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh `prune_gone_branches` only reclaims local branches whose upstream tracking ref is `[gone]` - the contract's push carries no `-u`, so the evidence ref has no upstream and is never pruned either. So after a PR merges both a local and a remote `fm/<id>-evidence` survive, which is exactly the stale-branch outcome the deletion requirement exists to prevent. Naming the remote explicitly fixes the wording; pushing with `-u` would additionally let the existing prune path reclaim the local copy once the remote is deleted. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:410` - "Push `fm/<id>-evidence` to the same remote your code branch goes to" is not resolvable in the default no-mistakes mode. That mode's DOD (bin/fm-brief.sh:369-387) has the worker commit and then hand off to /no-mistakes, which owns the push; per the intent's own constraints the code branch goes to a configured fork while `origin` is upstream. At the point the contract has the worker push the evidence ref the code branch has not been pushed anywhere, so the worker has no way to read the target and a wrong guess sends private-product captures to upstream - the opposite of the access-control property the sentence claims. Either defer the evidence push until after the code branch has an upstream and read it (`git config branch.fm/<id>.remote`), or name the target explicitly. 🔧 Fix: deliver visual evidence to task record dir, drop evidence ref 2 warnings still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:435` - "Link each artifact by its path beside the claim it evidences - in the pull request body when this project opens one" gives no owner and no timing for the default no-mistakes mode. That mode's DOD at bin/fm-brief.sh:375-393 has the worker commit, hand off to /no-mistakes, and then "Do not hand-edit, commit, or fix findings yourself while a run is active" - the pipeline authors the PR body, so the worker is never told when or how its per-claim links get into it. Round 3 covered this with "when the pull request is opened for you, add those links to its body with `gh-axi` as soon as it exists", but that sentence lived inside the per-mode delivery block the captain ordered removed and nothing replaced it, so the round-2 finding pr-mode-artifact-destination-underspecified is reachable again. The intent makes this a criterion: "The generated wording must be self-contained so a worker reading only the brief knows what to produce." Restoring a mode-agnostic version of that timing clause closes it without reintroducing anything from the withdrawn mechanism. - ⚠️ `AGENTS.md:86` - The change adds a new durable, crewmate-written location `data/<task-id>/evidence/` but does not add it to AGENTS.md's home-layout inventory, which at line 86 already documents the exact sibling artifact from this same scaffold: "`<id>/report.md` scout task deliverable, written by the crewmate; survives teardown". I confirmed the parallel is real - bin/fm-teardown.sh:1688 removes only `$STATE/$ID.*`, so the evidence directory survives teardown just like the report. The intent requires that "any doc that already owns the scaffold's contract must be updated", and this block is the existing owner of where crewmate deliverables live; adding one line beside the report entry satisfies it without a new doc. 🔧 Fix: restore PR-body link timing and document evidence dir ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-brief.test.sh` - full colocated suite, 19 cases pass including `test_visual_evidence_contract_is_opt_in_and_complete` and `test_visual_evidence_is_ship_only` - `FM_HOME=<tmp-home> bin/fm-brief.sh redesign-settings-page example-web-app --visual-evidence` - real ship brief containing the contract; compared against `bin/fm-brief.sh tune-retry-backoff example-web-app` (no flag, no section, no declaration) - Rendered both generated briefs with `markdown-it` and captured them side by side via `chrome-devtools-axi open file://... && chrome-devtools-axi screenshot --full-page`, plus a crop of the added section - Byte-parity check base cd73e75 vs target edf2187: generated ship (no-mistakes/direct-PR/local-only), scout, secondmate, and --herdr-lab briefs into an identical home path and `diff -r` - all six identical, matching SHAs - `bin/fm-brief.sh vis-scout someproj --scout --visual-evidence` and `FM_SECONDMATE_CHARTER=ops bin/fm-brief.sh vis-mate --secondmate --no-projects --visual-evidence` - both exit 1, no brief written - `/bin/bash -n bin/fm-brief.sh` (GNU bash 3.2.57) plus generating a flagged brief under `/bin/bash` and diffing against the Bash 5 output - identical, zero leaked `EOF` markers - `bin/fm-brief.sh --help` - verified the flag, medium-follows-the-surface wording, .fm-scratch production, data/<task-id>/evidence delivery, and rule 2 carve-out are documented - `bin/fm-brief.sh both example-web-app --visual-evidence --herdr-lab` - both contracts render, in order - `bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` - structural doc inventory still passes after the AGENTS.md and docs/scripts.md edits - `git diff --diff-filter=A --name-only cd73e75 edf2187` - confirms no new doc file was added - Mutation check: ran `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` against a temp repo whose `bin/fm-brief.sh` is the pre-change version - the new test fails (`visual-evidence brief missing its section heading`), and the pre-change script silently accepted `--scout --visual-evidence` and wrote a scout brief
⚠️ **Document** - 1 info - ℹ️ `docs/scripts.md:21` - Judgment call worth surfacing: an earlier review commit (a99dd81/edf2187) named the artifact location in the docs/scripts.md fm-brief.sh row, and the final commit also documented data/<task-id>/evidence/ in the AGENTS.md home-layout inventory, leaving the path stated in three places (script header, AGENTS.md, scripts.md). I kept AGENTS.md as the owner for the path (it already owns data/<id>/brief.md and report.md) and the script header as the owner for flag mechanics, and reduced the scripts.md row back to its one purpose clause, per that file's own preamble and the one-owner rule in .agents/skills/firstmate-coding-guidelines/SKILL.md. If the intent of that review was specifically that scripts.md name the path, this consolidation reverses it.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: feat(bin): add implementation habits to ship briefs
body:
## Summary

Add three concise implementation habits to ship briefs generated by `bin/fm-brief.sh`:

1. Consult an existing `graphify-out/graph.json` for callers, importers, and blast radius before editing source, without rebuilding or refreshing the graph. This uses existing structural knowledge instead of spending tokens rediscovering repository relationships.
2. Preserve failure evidence and never claim success without satisfying the project delivery mode. This exists because two workers on this fleet declared themselves done today, 2026-08-02, after local tests passed even though they never ran their delivery pipeline, pushed their work, or opened a PR.
3. For genuinely test-shaped work, retain failing-test-first evidence, the smallest passing change, behavior-preserving cleanup, and the final passing command. This keeps implementation claims tied to observable proof without imposing the workflow on investigations or documentation.

## Scope and safety

The habits appear in normal ship briefs and `--herdr-lab` ship briefs. They remain absent from scout, `--herdr-lab --scout`, and secondmate scaffolds where they do not apply.

The existing worktree-isolation assertion, status protocol, and delivery-mode definitions of done are unchanged. Behavioral coverage pins those safety sections while checking every scaffold variant.

## Validation

- `bash tests/fm-brief.test.sh`
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` with ShellCheck 0.11.0

## Intent

Place the crew-control read-only HTTP MCP server into the depohmel/firstmate fork. The server wraps firstmate's fleet scripts (fm-fleet-view.sh, fm-crew-state.sh, data/backlog.md) and exposes three read-only tools over HTTP: fleet_overview, crew_state, and backlog. It uses FM_HOME for the firstmate home path (no hardcoded /home/dep paths), has module path github.com/depohmel/firstmate/crew-control, and is placed in crew-control/ at the repo root. The README, config, and go.mod header describe it as living in the firstmate fork with famclaw as the MCP client, not as an out-of-repo famclaw addon. Push to the fork remote only, never to kunchenguid.

- Implemented HTTP server wrapping firstmate's fleet scripts (fm-fleet-view.sh, fm-crew-state.sh, data/backlog.md)
- Configured server to use FM_HOME for firstmate home path instead of hardcoded paths
- Added module path github.com/depohmel/firstmate/crew-control
- Placed module in crew-control/ at repo root as specified in intent

✅ Low: The change appears to be a well-scoped implementation of a new module that places a read-only HTTP MCP server in a specific fork. The implementation follows the specified requirements and doesn't introduce any obvious bugs or security concerns.

title: fix(codex): anchor trusted hook payload root

## What Changed

- Anchor trusted Codex hook payload validation to the configured worktree root and align pretool/spawn handling with that boundary.
- Add integrity, pretool, and dispatch/lifecycle regression coverage for hook-root anchoring.
- Refresh the related architecture, guard, supervision, and harness documentation.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is bounded to Codex hook-root anchoring, trusted policy resolution, launch environment propagation, documentation, and regression coverage; no material source defect is substantiated.

title: test(turnend-guard): cover Codex checkpoint foreground-only health boundary
body:
## Intent

Prevent Codex Stop hooks from falsely reporting blind supervision while a foreground checkpoint is actually active, without weakening the guard after a checkpoint ends or when work is truly unsupervised. The committed change adds an isolated lifecycle regression that proves an active healthy checkpoint permits the Stop hook and a timed-out checkpoint re-blocks an in-flight primary, plus protocol documentation that makes the boundary explicit. Validate, push, open a PR, and stop when CI is green; do not merge.

## What Changed

- Added `test_codex_checkpoint_health_ends_when_foreground_command_returns` to `tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh`, an isolated-clone regression proving `fm-watch-checkpoint.sh` makes the Stop guard permissive while its foreground command holds the watcher lock, and that the guard re-blocks an in-flight primary once the checkpoint times out and the lock is released.
- Updated `docs/turnend-guard.md`'s regression coverage list to mention the new Codex checkpoint foreground-only health boundary test.
- Clarified `docs/supervision-protocols/codex.md` step 5 to state explicitly that a checkpoint only proves watcher health while its foreground command owns the watcher lock, and that the Stop guard correctly blocks an in-flight primary once it returns, until the next checkpoint starts.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is test-and-docs-only (no changes to bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh, bin/fm-watch.sh, or bin/fm-watch-checkpoint.sh); it adds a regression test that exercises real, already-correct lock/beacon lifecycle behavior confirmed by reading the guard and watcher source, and follows an established real-process test pattern already used in tests/fm-watch-checkpoint.test.sh.

## Testing

Ran the targeted test file tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh (the only file touched besides docs), which exercises bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh and bin/fm-watch-checkpoint.sh end-to-end via real subprocesses and a live watcher lock/beacon in an isolated git clone; the new test explicitly demonstrates a foreground Codex checkpoint making the Stop hook allow (exit 0, silent) while its lock is live, then re-block (exit 2, 'TURN WOULD END BLIND') once the checkpoint times out and the lock is gone — matching the required intent. title: feat(bin): add disabled-by-default browser custody owner
body:
## Intent

Build Firstmate's first disabled-by-default visible-browser custody layer from the approved browser-capability synthesis: add a single fm-browser owner, policy/receipt/state lifecycle, safe cleanup and teardown hooks, browser work instructions, docs, tests, and a public/manual acceptance path. Do not launch any real browser, access credentials/cookies/sessions, use private origins, install or update tools, or enable real engines in this change; real browser control must remain refused unless an explicit future policy and supervised smoke path authorize it.

## What Changed

- Adds `bin/fm-browser.sh` as the sole browser lifecycle owner (`capabilities`/`plan`/`open`/`status`/`navigate`/`snapshot`/`interact`/`request-action`/`close`/`inspect`/`reconcile`/`expire`), gated by a gitignored `config/browser-policy.json` (`fm-browser-policy.v1`) that defaults to disabled: real engine launch is refused outright and only `FM_BROWSER_MOCK_ENGINE=1` exercises the lifecycle, with value-redacted receipts, ephemeral per-session profiles, exact-path cleanup that quarantines on failure, and a session capacity cap.
- Wires custody into existing surfaces: `bin/fm-browser-lib.sh` blocks `bin/fm-teardown.sh` on uncleaned task bindings, `bin/fm-session-start.sh` reports custody state in the fleet digest, `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` validates the policy file and flags a missing `agent-browser`, `bin/fm-brief.sh --browser` emits the browser safety contract, and the policy inherits through `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh`.
- Adds the `browser-capability` skill, browser capability/architecture/verification docs plus audience, scripts, configuration, README and AGENTS updates, source-only refuse-by-default engine adapters under `bin/browser-engines/`, a no-TCC `bin/fm-window-helper.sh` contract stub, and five browser test scripts including a real-engine smoke that gate-skips unless explicitly authorized.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: This round's diff only hardens the already-disabled, mock-only custody core - five fixes land with new regression tests (receipt validation, empty-path quarantine, capacity release) and two are mechanical deletions - leaving one piece of dead code; the `exit 1` in `bin/fm-teardown.sh` that drove last round's medium is unchanged and is covered by a finding the user accepted as-is.

## Testing

I ran the four browser test scripts plus the opt-in smoke, then the seven scripts covering the shared files this diff touches (fm-test-run, fm-bootstrap, fm-brief, fm-session-start, fm-teardown, fm-documentation-audiences, fm-shared-captain-inheritance) - all pass. Because passing units alone would not show the intent's forbidden half, I built three operator walkthroughs against a throwaway FM_HOME: with no policy file `capabilities` reports disabled and `open` returns `browser-disabled`, and flipping the policy to `enabled:true` still returns `real-engine-disabled`; private, local, file and credential-bearing origins each refuse before engine execution with distinct codes; a canary typed through `--value-file` appears in zero of the four persisted records while the receipt stores `"target": "redacted"`; `close` removed exactly the recorded profile directory and left the empty parents intact; and the teardown guard blocked cleanup of a task with an open session, ignored an unrelated task, and released after a clean close. The strongest artifact is the real-engine gate unlocked at both positions - even with `FM_BROWSER_REAL_SMOKE=1 FM_BROWSER_REAL_ENGINE_VERIFIED=1` the smoke exits 1 with "no verified implementation yet" rather than launching anything. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shows the teardown guard that bin/fm-teardown.sh runs before cleaning a task,
# driven by a genuinely open session from the real fm-browser.sh mock lifecycle.
set -u

ROOT=$1
SANDBOX=$2
FMB="$ROOT/bin/fm-browser.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
. "$ROOT/bin/fm-browser-lib.sh"

HOME_DIR="$SANDBOX/home"
mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR/config" "$HOME_DIR/state" "$HOME_DIR/data"
cat > "$HOME_DIR/config/browser-policy.json" <<'EOF'
{"schema":"fm-browser-policy.v1","enabled":true,"maxActiveSessions":1,"allowedAuthClasses":["anonymous"]}
EOF

export FM_BROWSER_MOCK_ENGINE=1
export FM_BROWSER_RUNTIME_OVERRIDE="$SANDBOX/runtime"

echo "== 1. Open a session for task ship-42 and leave it open =="
PLAN=$(FM_HOME="$HOME_DIR" "$FMB" plan --task ship-42 --origin https://example.com --json)
RECEIPT=$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.loads(sys.argv[1])["receipt"])' "$PLAN")
OPEN=$(FM_HOME="$HOME_DIR" "$FMB" open --task ship-42 --plan "$RECEIPT" --json)
HANDLE=$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.loads(sys.argv[1])["handle"])' "$OPEN")
printf 'session handle: %s\n' "$HANDLE"
printf '\ntask binding recorded on disk:\n'
python3 -m json.tool "$HOME_DIR/state/browser/v1/task-bindings/ship-42.json" | sed 's/^/  /'

echo
echo "== 2. Teardown guard, exactly as bin/fm-teardown.sh invokes it =="
echo '$ fm_browser_refuse_unclean_task "$FM_HOME" ship-42   # then: || exit 1'
if fm_browser_refuse_unclean_task "$HOME_DIR" ship-42; then
  printf 'RESULT: guard allowed cleanup (unexpected)\n'
else
  printf 'RESULT: exit 1, task teardown is blocked\n'
fi

echo
echo "== 3. An unrelated task with no browser binding is never blocked =="
if fm_browser_refuse_unclean_task "$HOME_DIR" ship-99; then
  printf 'RESULT: exit 0, unrelated task tears down normally\n'
else
  printf 'RESULT: guard blocked an unrelated task (unexpected)\n'
fi

echo
echo "== 4. Close the session through the owner, then re-run the guard =="
FM_HOME="$HOME_DIR" "$FMB" close --handle "$HANDLE" --reason operator --json | python3 -m json.tool | sed -n '/postconditions/,/]/p;/profileOutcome/p;/"state"/p' | sed 's/^/  /'
printf '\ntask binding after close:\n'
python3 -m json.tool "$HOME_DIR/state/browser/v1/task-bindings/ship-42.json" | sed 's/^/  /'
echo
echo '$ fm_browser_refuse_unclean_task "$FM_HOME" ship-42'
if fm_browser_refuse_unclean_task "$HOME_DIR" ship-42; then
  printf 'RESULT: exit 0, task teardown may proceed\n'
else
  printf 'RESULT: still blocked after a clean close (unexpected)\n'
fi

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-browser.sh:402` - `remove_profile` compares the profile path recorded at `open` time against `RUNTIME_ROOT` re-read from the environment at `close` time, so any `close` run without the same `FM_BROWSER_RUNTIME_OVERRIDE` that `open` used fails the containment check and quarantines the session. Either persist the runtime root in the session record and compare against that, or add an explicit operator-facing resolve path.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-browser.sh:405` - `shutil.rmtree` is unguarded. On EACCES/ENOTEMPTY/EBUSY the OSError escapes `remove_profile` and `cmd_close` entirely, so `save_session` at line 423 is never reached: the session file keeps its prior `active` state, no quarantine receipt is written, and the profile may be half-deleted - the exact failure the quarantine branch exists to record. The traceback also prints the full profile path to stderr, contradicting the module header's claim that this command never exposes profile paths and the `browser-capability` skill's rule against private paths in captain-facing output. Wrap the rmtree and route failure into the existing `removed = False` quarantine path with a redacted message.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-browser.sh:310` - `args.plan` is the only identifier in this file that reaches a path join without `safe_id` - `handle` (line 205) and `task` (line 212) are both validated. `plan_path` does `PLANS / (receipt.replace("sha256:", "") + ".json")`, so `--plan ../../../../tmp/x` escapes the plans directory; the `replace` is also not prefix-anchored and strips every occurrence, not just a leading one. Impact today is bounded because line 316's `if not MOCK: die(...)` fires before plan content is used, leaving a `.json` existence oracle plus a task/mode/auth comparison rather than an arbitrary-read-and-use, but the gap widens the moment a real engine lands. Run the receipt through `safe_id` (or match it against `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`) before joining.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-session-start.sh:395` - `BROWSER_OUT=$("$SCRIPT_DIR/fm-browser.sh" inspect --all --json 2>&1) || BROWSER_OUT=$?` overwrites the captured output with the numeric exit status on failure, defeating the `2>&1` capture. A broken or misconfigured browser owner renders in the fleet digest as a bare `1` instead of the policy/parse error, in the one read-only section agents rely on for custody state. Capture the status separately (`rc=$?`) and print the captured text.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-browser.sh:77` - `quarantined` is a member of `LIVE_STATES`, so a quarantined session is counted by `active_sessions()` and consumes a slot in the capacity check at line 322 permanently - session records are never deleted. With the default `maxActiveSessions: 1`, a single quarantine event blocks every subsequent `open` in that home with `capacity-reached` and no way to reclaim the slot. Quarantine means "cleanup unproven", not "engine live"; it should not be part of capacity accounting (or the accounting needs an explicit release path).
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-browser.sh:327` - Four configuration surfaces are accepted but have no effect. (1)/(2) `anonymousIdleSeconds` and `anonymousHardSeconds` appear only in the line 159 default dict and are never consulted; line 327 derives both `idleDeadlineEpoch` and `hardDeadlineEpoch` from the plan's `ttlSeconds`, so `idleDeadlineEpoch` is dead state and the hard deadline ignores policy - yet `docs/browser-capability.md:25-26` publishes both fields in the schema block, implying effect. (3) `--expiry-action close-exact` is computed into `due[].eligible` but `actionTaken` is hardcoded `none-alert-only`. (4) `cmd_open` never compares the plan's `createdAt` + `ttlSeconds` against now, so an arbitrarily stale plan receipt still opens. Alert-only expiry is a stated design choice, but the published-yet-inert timeout fields and the unexpired-plan gap are worth confirming as intentional for this stage.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-test-run.sh:700` - The new `.agents/skills/browser-capability/SKILL.md)` arm prints exactly `pure-contract-unit`, which is what the generic `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md)` arm two lines below already produces. The specific arm is dead duplication and can be dropped. (If the intent was to also route this skill to the browser tests, note those live in `pure-contract-unit` already, so the mapping is correct either way.)
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-browser-lib.sh:37` - `fm_browser_refuse_unclean_task` spawns `python3` three times against the same binding JSON - once via `fm_browser_task_cleaned`, then once each for `state` and `handle`. This runs on every `bin/fm-teardown.sh` invocation. A single interpreter call emitting cleaned/state/handle together (read into the three shell variables) is a straightforward non-functional dedup on a hot path.
- ℹ️ `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh:435` - The only pre-existing test the branch modifies raises the slow scheduler fixture's `sleep` from 0.5 to 2, unrelated to the browser capability and unexplained by the stated intent. It reads as flake hardening, but it widens the window in which the replacement fixture may start from ~0.45s to ~1.95s, so the assertion "scheduler did not wait for the oldest worker" now tolerates a scheduler that stalls nearly two seconds, and it adds 1.5s to every run of this test. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-browser.sh:395` - `if not profile_path: return False` never fires: `Path("")` is `PosixPath('.')` and every `Path` is truthy. A session record with a missing/empty profile path therefore resolves to the current working directory and falls through to the containment check at line 402, which happens to reject it. The guard fails safe today but is misleading; test the raw string before constructing the `Path`.

title: perf: shard portable serial tests across CI runners
body:
## Intent

Speed up the 'Behavior portable serial' CI job so it completes with a comfortable buffer below its timeout-minutes limit.

Problem: on firstmate PR 1495 the 'Behavior portable serial' CI job was cancelled - not because tests failed (every step passed), but because its main step ('Run portable serial remainder') ran ~19m51s and the job hit its ~20-minute timeout-minutes at the exact boundary. It runs the behavior suite serially, which is too slow, so it intermittently times out and cancels. Same class of issue as the recently merged windows CI slowness fix (no-mistakes PR 645 - branchsync serial floor).

Goal: reduce the serial job's wall time SIGNIFICANTLY so it finishes with a comfortable margin - well under half the timeout, not a few seconds under. Approaches in preference order: parallelize the serial remainder where safe (shard/concurrent execution); keep only genuinely serial-only tests (shared mutable state, ports, global fixtures) in the serial set and move the parallel-safe majority to parallel; speed up the slowest individual tests; trim redundant setup. Preserve full behavioral coverage - never weaken or delete tests to gain speed. Provide concrete before/after wall-time evidence versus the timeout. Widening timeout-minutes is acceptable only as belt-and-suspenders on top of a real speedup, never as the primary fix.

Measured evidence gathered before implementing: on green CI run 30725985757 the lane's 69 scripts summed to 1143762 ms (19m04s) against the 20-minute cap; job setup (checkout, ShellCheck, tmux check, tasks-axi install) is only about 7s, so the cost is entirely test wall time and there is nothing meaningful to trim in setup. The single longest script, tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh at 199573 ms, is the hard floor for any shard count.

Chosen approach and the reasoning behind it: shard the portable serial lane across four SEPARATE CI runners rather than introducing concurrency inside one runner. Each shard stays strictly serial in itself. Because separate GitHub jobs get separate machines, no two of these stateful scripts (watcher, lock, AFK, real tmux, daemon, secondmate lifecycle, bootstrap, live-harness opt-in, GUI-backend) ever share a machine, so this split deliberately needs NO concurrency isolation proof - unlike the existing portable parallel lanes, which are restricted to the proven-isolated set owned by bin/fm-test-isolation-proof.sh. Moving serial tests into the proven-isolated parallel set was deliberately NOT done, because that would require a new concurrent isolation proof archive and is the riskier path. Individual test internals were deliberately left untouched to avoid weakening coverage or introducing flakiness; sharding alone reaches the target.

Deliberate design decisions a reviewer would not infer from the diff alone:
- Serial-lane membership stays DERIVED (everything neither proven-isolated nor real-herdr-gated) rather than enumerated, so a newly added test lands in the lane by default instead of falling out of every lane. Shard assignment is computed at runtime by longest-processing-time bin packing, so new tests need no manual shard placement.
- The per-script duration table embedded in bin/fm-test-run.sh is intentionally a BALANCE HINT ONLY, not a correctness input. The coverage guard keeps the partition complete and disjoint whatever the hints say, so a stale hint costs a slower shard rather than lost coverage. Unmeasured scripts get a conservative default near the measured per-script mean. docs/fm-test-portable-shards.md owns the refresh procedure.
- Lane names deliberately carry the shard count (portable-serial-<k>of<n>) and bin/fm-test-run.sh refuses any lane whose ofN disagrees with its configured count. ci.yml deliberately derives the same N from strategy.job-total rather than a literal. This is fail-closed on purpose: changing the shard count in either file alone makes the lane fail loudly instead of silently leaving part of the required suite unrun. The plain-<k> naming was rejected precisely because it has that silent coverage hole.
- timeout-minutes was TIGHTENED from 20 to 15, not widened. Expected work per shard is 285941 ms (~4m46s), about a third of the cap, leaving roughly 3x hang-tripwire margin. Timeouts in this repo are hang tripwires, not expected healthy durations.
- fail-fast: false on the matrix is deliberate so one shard's failure never hides another shard's result.
- --check-coverage was extended to additionally prove the serial shards are non-empty, pairwise disjoint, and exactly equal to the serial lane. No test is weakened, skipped, or removed anywhere in this change.

Also included deliberately, as an engineering-excellence fix for flakiness encountered while validating: tests/fm-test-run.test.sh's --jobs scheduler fixture proved slot-refill behavior with a 0.5s-versus-0.05s wall-clock sleep race, which failed on a loaded machine during this work. It is replaced with an explicit signal handshake between the fixtures (the slow fixture blocks until the replacement fixture signals, and the replacement reads the evidence before signalling), with a bounded deadline so a genuinely wait-for-oldest scheduler still reports instead of hanging. Verified 3/3 under sustained ~20x CPU saturation where the old shape had already flaked.

Local verification already performed: bin/fm-lint.sh clean; bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh ok; --check-coverage reports FM_TEST_COVERAGE ok total=104 parallel=24 serial=69 serial_shards=4 herdr=11; all four shards balance to 285.9s with 1 ms imbalance; tests/fm-test-run.test.sh, tests/fm-lint.test.sh and tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh pass; portable-serial-1of4 executed end to end with 15/15 green (FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=15 failed=0 skipped_gate=2, exit 0); bin/fm-test-run.sh parses under stock macOS Bash 3.2.

This is firstmate's own shared tracked material (.github/workflows/, bin/, docs/, CONTRIBUTING.md, tests/), so the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill applies: one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never em dash, no agent commit co-author, shellcheck-clean bin scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh, tests colocated in tests/ extending the existing runner, tests must exercise executable interfaces rather than assert implementation source text, and every contract stated in full exactly once with cross-references elsewhere. The authoritative before/after wall time will come from this PR's own CI run.

## What Changed

- Split the portable serial behavior lane into four duration-balanced CI jobs that remain serial per runner, disable matrix fail-fast, and tighten the timeout from 20 to 15 minutes.
- Add deterministic longest-processing-time shard assignment, fail-closed shard-count validation, lane discovery, and coverage checks proving the serial shards are non-empty, disjoint, and complete.
- Document shard timing and refresh procedures, and replace the scheduler test's timing race with a bounded signal handshake.

title: fix(bin): correct session lock and attached watcher supervision
body:
## Intent

Fix both contributor-reported firstmate supervision faults in-house (the contributor is offline). Both are genuine and still open on the default branch; a completed investigation with reproductions and file:line evidence was the spec.

FAULT 1 - the Claude Stop auto-arm fails to claim the home. In bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh the process-ancestry walk matched only the basename of `ps -o comm=` against a fixed harness-name list. Claude Code's native installer names the per-session executable by its version (e.g. .../share/claude/versions/2.1.220), so that basename matches nothing. Three real failure shapes, all required to be fixed: CASE C (unconditional on Linux, where procps reports the kernel exec name and ignores argv[0]) - the version-named session is missed, nothing matches, the hook exits 0, the epoch is never written and supervision never auto-arms; CASE A - a claude-named daemon that directly parents sessions wins the outermost-contiguous-claude rule ahead of the session itself, so the hook exits 0 and never arms; CASE B (previously unreported, most dangerous) - a live session's lock is reclaimed as stale and rewritten to a shared daemon pid, corrupting the home's session-ownership record. The accepted direction was: stop consulting only the basename (`ps -o args=` still carries claude on both platforms), and correctly distinguish a session's own spare/worker chain from a shared daemon. An explicit constraint was NOT to simply revert the outermost-claude rule from #1206 - it was added for a real reason (Claude's nested bg-spare hook worker chain) and is pinned by an existing test.

FAULT 2 - an attached arm reports a delivered cycle as FAILED. In bin/fm-watch-arm.sh the watcher's single reason line reaches only the arm that owns the cycle as a child; an arm that ATTACHED to an existing cycle cannot observe it and reported "watcher: FAILED - cycle ended without an actionable reason" after a SUCCESSFUL cycle. No supervision event is lost - the durable wake queue holds it - so the damage is the false alarm and the manual re-arm it triggers. It was required to be fixed IN bin/fm-watch-arm.sh, deliberately NOT in the Stop hook, so it composes with an adjacent in-flight auto-arm branch that rewrites the hook's classify section; that branch only softens this on the Claude path, so this fix had to cover every harness (codex, opencode, pi, grok, kimi).

DESIGN DECISIONS MADE WHILE DOING THE WORK (deliberate, not oversights):

- Harness identity now also reads WHOLE PATH COMPONENTS of `ps -o comm=` and of argv[0], not a loose substring. That strictness is the point: a loose match would also match ordinary firstmate paths such as bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh or ~/.claude/hooks/*.sh, which must never be treated as harness processes. Both evidence sources are needed because macOS reports argv[0] in `ps -o comm=` while Linux reports the bare exec name there and carries the path in argv[0].
- Session-lock OWNERSHIP is now decided against the session's whole contiguous harness ancestry (set membership) rather than one chosen pid. This is the faithful implementation of the question the library header already documents ("does the current process descend from that same harness?"). It SUBSUMES the outermost-pid rule rather than reverting it: the bg-spare lock owner is still matched wherever it sits in the contiguous run, and a daemon-parented session now recognizes its own inner lock. The existing pinned bg-spare test still passes unchanged.
- Lock WRITING (fm_harness_ancestry_pid) deliberately still returns the outermost pid of the contiguous run. A shared daemon and a same-session worker chain are structurally identical in the process tree, so no reliable ancestry-only discriminator exists; rather than invent a fragile heuristic (pgid, start time, child counts), the write choice keeps the one pid that lives as long as the session. Writing an inner worker pid instead would make the lock look stale moments after a hook returns and would weaken the competing-live-session boundary. This is a knowingly accepted limitation, documented in the function comment.
- The pre-existing LOOSE basename match (which would, for example, also match a process literally named fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh) was deliberately left unchanged: it is pre-existing behavior outside the three reported shapes, tightening it risks breaking unverified real harness executable names, and an existing test pins loose matching of a dash-leading "-codex".
- Fault 2 uses state/.wake-queue.seq as a watermark taken at each cycle begin. That counter is monotonic and is never rewound by a drain, so it proves delivery even after a handling turn consumed the records. When the records are still queued the arm reprints their payloads (the same actionable reason the owning arm would have printed) and exits 0. When they were already drained it prints a deliberately NON-actionable informational line, "watcher: cycle delivered <N> wake(s) already drained", and exits 0 - deliberately not a synthesized signal:/stale:/check:/heartbeat line, so the model is not sent chasing a second copy of an already-handled wake. Only a cycle the queue shows delivered nothing is still the typed nonzero failure. The same helper is applied to the owned-child clean-close path for uniformity.

TESTS - the investigation found the critical gap that tests/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.test.sh passes 17/17 while never naming a fake harness anything but "claude". Required: regressions reproducing a version-named session process, a daemon-parented session, and an attached non-owning arm observing a delivered wake, each failing on the previous code.

- Two NEW test files were added deliberately instead of extending tests/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.test.sh, because the adjacent in-flight branch rewrites that file and the goal was composability.
- tests/fm-session-lock-ancestry.test.sh pins both platforms' ps reporting semantics behind a deterministic fake process table, and runs the REAL Stop auto-arm hook inside real process trees for the version-named, daemon-parented, and combined shapes. Those fixture trees are deliberately orphaned to init before the hook fires so the ancestry walk terminates inside the fixture and can never escape into the session running the suite.
- tests/fm-watch-arm.test.sh drives a real bin/fm-watch.sh singleton and a real attached bin/fm-watch-arm.sh through a real status-driven wake.
- Every fault case was verified to FAIL on the previous code (CASE C and CASE A: hook exit 0, never armed; CASE B: the live session's lock rewritten to the daemon pid; fault 2: "watcher: FAILED" after a successful cycle). Some added cases intentionally PASS on the previous code as well - the boundary tests (ordinary script paths under a harness directory are not harness processes, ownership stops at the first non-harness gap, and a cycle that delivered nothing still fails loudly). Those are guards for the widening this change makes and are intentionally not fault regressions.

SCOPE - the standing instruction was to keep changes confined to bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh and bin/fm-watch-arm.sh plus their tests, so they compose with an adjacent in-flight supervision branch that touches neither file. Four files were changed beyond that, each a deliberate, flagged decision rather than scope creep: docs/watcher-continuity.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/verification/supervision.md each stated the exact contract this change supersedes (an unexplained close is always FAILED; outermost-pid resolution as the mechanism that reaches the lock owner), so leaving them would have left the repo's documented contract wrong; and bin/fm-test-run.sh gained the two new suites in the watcher-wake-lock family, because otherwise `--family watcher-wake-lock` would miss exactly the subsystem this change covers. None of those four files is in the in-flight branch's file list.

This is firstmate's own shared tracked material, so firstmate-coding-guidelines applies: one-sentence-per-line markdown, plain dash never an em dash, no agent co-author on commits, shellcheck-clean bin scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh, tests colocated in tests/ as <subject>.test.sh exercising behavior through executable interfaces rather than asserting implementation source text, and maintainer-verification records updated when the behavior they attest to changes.

This changes LIVE fleet supervision, so landing is coordinated: report when CI is green and do not expect an immediate merge.

## What Changed

- Recognize version-named Claude sessions from exact executable-path and `argv[0]` components, and validate lock ownership across the full contiguous harness ancestry while preserving outermost lock writes.
- Bind watcher deliveries and successor tracking to PID identity so attached arms report delivered wake reasons, including after queue drains, while cycles that delivered nothing still fail loudly.
- Add real-process regression coverage, register the new suites in the watcher-wake-lock family, and update the supervision documentation.

title: feat(bin): add jcode as a verified harness adapter
body:
## What

Adds `jcode` (v0.64.2 verified) as a new verified harness adapter. jcode runs as a headless single-shot `jcode run --no-update --quiet run --model <m> --cwd <worktree> "<brief>"` process when launched as a crewmate — no TUI, no composer, no trust dialog, no permission surface. Its **process lifecycle IS the turn lifecycle**: process-alive = busy, process-exit = turn-end. This is the most direct semantic busy source of any verified adapter, with no hook installer needed.

## Adapter wiring

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/fm-spawn.sh` | Launch template, `resolve_jcode_binary()` (PATH then `~/.local/bin/jcode`), task-local process-death wrapper `$TASK_TMP/jcode-run.sh` (0700) that fires `idle/jcode-process` and touches `state/<id>.turn-ended` via an EXIT trap on normal/error/SIGINT/SIGTERM exit. The wrapper runs jcode as a child (not `exec`) so the trap fires; SIGKILL cannot run any trap and is covered by the endpoint-gone classifier per the dead-endpoint precedence rule. |
| `bin/fm-busy-lib.sh` | New semantic source `jcode-process`, gated behind `FM_BUSY_JCODE_VERIFIED_VERSIONS="v0.64.2"`. An unverified version classifies `unknown jcode-unverified`, never idle. Source trust table accepts `jcode-process` for `harness=jcode*`. |
| `bin/fm-harness.sh`, `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh` | `jcode` added to `FM_HARNESS_RE` for markerless ancestry detection. |
| `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` | `jcode` added to the harness list and the jq-verified list with its verified version. |
| `bin/backends/tmux.sh` | tmux liveness classifier matches `*jcode*` as `alive`; the bare shell after exit still classifies as `dead`. |
| `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md` | New `## jcode (VERIFIED 2026-08-02, jcode v0.64.2)` section with the full fact table and the flagship-feature preservation note (`--ndjson` streaming, `--json` machine-readable output, `--resume <session_id>` continuity, `jcode memory list/search/export/import/stats` long-term memory). **tmux is the verified spawn backend for jcode crews** because jcode is not a Herdr-native agent; herdr reports it through its generic agent classifier only, and herdr's native busy state returns `unknown` for jcode. |
| `docs/verification/supervision.md` | New row in the semantic busy-state table with the 2026-08-02 live-pass evidence (real tmux window: `busy fm-spawn` during run, `idle jcode-process` after exit, stale-gen apply refused by the writer). |

## Live-verified end-to-end

Mirrored `fm_backend_tmux_create_task`'s stable-window-id targeting against the real busy-state contract:

- Armed the gen → `v1 gen=g1785708964 seq=1 state=busy source=fm-spawn event=launch-brief`
- Launched `jcode --no-update --quiet run --model glm-5.2-nvidia-only --cwd <worktree> "<brief>"` inside the tmux window through the real `$TASK_TMP/jcode-run.sh` wrapper
- During run → `fm_busy_classify_live tmux <window-id> jcode verify <state-dir>` returned `busy fm-spawn`
- After process exit → returned `idle jcode-process` (record: `seq=2 state=idle source=jcode-process event=process-exit`)
- Stale-gen apply refused by `fm-busy-event.sh` (`error: stale busy-state gen`)

Also verified: `--json` parseable for the watcher (session_id + token usage), `--resume <session_id>` continuity (recalled seed word on resume), wrapper EXIT trap fires on normal exit, error exit (bad model), and SIGTERM mid-run. Token accounting (`[Tokens] upload/download/cache_read/cache_write`) preserved through the headless path.

## Regression

- `bash -n` clean on all 6 touched shell scripts.
- `tests/fm-busy-state.test.sh` PASS.
- `tests/fm-busy-adapter-wiring.test.sh` PASS.

## Notes

- No secrets or scratch paths leaked into the diff (verified pre-commit).
- The crewmate launch shape forces full autonomy by design: `jcode run` has no permission system to approve or skip (verified empirically — bash + cross-folder file writes + git init/commit all ran with exit 0 and no prompt).
- jcode auto-update is pinned off via `--no-update` on the launch command so a crewmate cannot upgrade jcode mid-fleet.

title: feat(bin): add a two-way visual fleet board over the bearings projection
body:
## Intent Complete PR 1549 by adding the ONE commit it is missing: the captain's explicitly-requested width uncap for the visual fleet board (bin/fm-fleet-board.sh). CONTEXT ON WHY THIS RUN EXISTS. PR 1549 already carries the whole board and passed a full green pipeline, but 'no-mistakes rerun' re-submitted from the PREVIOUS run's head rather than the local head, so the width commit was silently excluded and the merged PR still contained max-w-7xl. This run reconciles that: local was reset onto the pipeline's pushed head 8355b76 (preserving every pipeline fix commit - the parked/done roll-up, the architecture/bearings docs, and the node-guard/dash-key/apos-decode test fixes) and the width commit was cherry-picked on top. Nothing else changed. THE CHANGE UNDER REVIEW (one commit): the board is deliberately uncapped in width. The captain added this criterion explicitly - a narrow column defeats the at-a-glance purpose the board exists for, so extra width must buy MORE cards, not wider ones. max-w-7xl is removed from the header and main containers ON PURPOSE. Column scaling uses plain-CSS auto-fill grids (.fm-grid-cards / .fm-grid-rows), NOT Tailwind arbitrary-variant breakpoints such as min-[1800px]: - a real browser proved the Tailwind browser runtime generates NO rule for those, so the grid silently stayed at two columns on a 2600px viewport while cards just got wider. Every auto-fill track carries a min() floor so a narrow screen keeps exactly one full-width column and nothing scrolls sideways. Verified in a browser on this exact tree: 1 column at 500px, 2 at 1440px, 5 at 2600px, and up to 6 at 3440px, with zero horizontal overflow at any nesting level. Do NOT reintroduce a max-width cap and do NOT switch to Tailwind arbitrary variants. New test case (m) guards all of it; two of its assertions were found inert when first written (one matched the CSS rule instead of an element using it, the other passed while one of two grids lost its floor) and both were fixed after watching those mutations pass. STANDING CONSTRAINTS, unchanged from the earlier green run: 1. ONE CLASSIFIER. The board consumes fm-bearings-snapshot.sh --json only; it never re-derives a bucket from fm-fleet-snapshot.sh and holds no second classifier. 2. THE BOARD NEVER WRITES FLEET STATE. It renders and collects; answers return via 'lavish-axi poll' and firstmate applies them with bin/fm-decision-hold.sh. 3. The headline roll-up is a CAPTAIN DECISION already made: parked counts as stuck (warning badge), done counts in neither headline and leaves the under-way denominator. Do not re-litigate it and do not prune the defensive needs-decision/stale/cancelled values. 4. A bare '#number' inside bearings-supplied prose renders verbatim on purpose; the board has no repository context and must not fabricate a URL. 5. The review-surface API is resolved at submit time, not at load, because Lavish injects it after the page scripts run. 6. Tests execute the artifact rather than asserting source bytes; the negative controls are intentional. 7. Performance is out of scope (owned by fm-snapshot-perf). KNOWN OPEN ITEM, deliberately NOT addressed here: the 'offline-copy' ask-user finding from the previous run - the page-level 'Opened as a plain file' notice also appears when a served board's answer fails to send, where that claim is untrue. The captain owns it and it is filed as fm-fleet-board-offline-copy for their return. docs chart the board in `docs/architecture.md`, index it in `docs/scripts.md`, and point the bearings skill at it instead of hand-built `lavish-axi` renderers. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The branch adds exactly the one intent-mandated width-uncap commit on top of board content byte-identical to the previously green pipeline head; title: fix(bin): deliver requested spawn effort or refuse launch, never silently omit it
body:
## What Changed

- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now validates a requested Codex effort against the live `models_cache.json` catalog: supported levels (including `max` on models that advertise it) are delivered via `model_reasoning_effort`, unsupported levels refuse the spawn with the model's advertised range, and missing or inconclusive catalog evidence warns and passes the requested value through for Codex to validate.
- Effort requests that can never reach the launch command now refuse before any side effects (project allocation, endpoint creation, metadata publication) instead of silently launching at the harness default while task metadata records the requested effort: grok `xhigh`/`max`, opencode, kimi, unknown harnesses, and any launch command lacking an `__EFFORTFLAG__` placeholder. `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` crew-dispatch validation now shares one effort list for claude/codex/pi so `codex:max` passes through to spawn-time live validation.
- Docs and the harness-adapters skill (`docs/architecture.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md`, the fm-spawn header) drop the stale "effort is omitted" claims and document the deliver-or-refuse behavior and launch placeholders; test suites were extended accordingly (dispatch-profile catalog delivery/refusal/pass-through cases, hermetic `CODEX_HOME` wiring in the kimi and secondmate suites, updated bootstrap validation), all passing in the pipeline's Test phase including a watch-it-fail run against the base commit.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: A deliberate, well-documented behavior change (loud refusal of undeliverable efforts plus live-catalog Codex validation) whose refusal ordering, lock cleanup on the new exit paths, set -eu interactions, and test hermeticity all verify cleanly in source; the single finding is a pre-existing sibling gap on the model axis suitable for follow-up.

## Testing

Ran the four touched suites (dispatch-profile, kimi, secondmate, bootstrap) with verified exit codes — all green; proved the new codex-catalog test detects the old behavior by watching it fail against the base-commit fm-spawn.sh; and captured before/after CLI transcripts of the real fm-spawn.sh showing max-effort delivery from the live catalog, loud pre-launch refusals with no metadata side effects, and warn-and-pass-through on catalog uncertainty, versus the base commit's silent effort omission with misleading metadata.

title: fix(bin): speed up the fleet snapshot and keep it reporting without scratch space

## What Changed - Removed the fleet snapshot's dominant cost: the blank-line guard in `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh`'s status folds now uses a `case` glob instead of `${line//[[:space:]]/}` (which costs ~1.8s per 3KB status line on stock macOS bash 3.2), and `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` builds task rows in bounded concurrent batches (`FM_SNAPSHOT_TASK_JOBS`, default 8) with signal-safe scratch-dir cleanup. Measured on a 10-row fixture, the snapshot dropped from 16.0s to 1.2s with byte-identical output. - When scratch space is unavailable (`mktemp` fails or is missing), the snapshot degrades to the byte-identical serial path instead of failing, so fleet reporting keeps working. - Froze the snapshot JSON contract with a golden fixture (`tests/golden/fm-fleet-snapshot-shape.json`) plus new tests asserting the parallel and serial paths emit identical bytes (CI's expected test count raised from 15 to 20), and recorded the before/after measurements in `docs/verification/fleet-snapshot-performance.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The fix commit durably resolves both prior findings — signal-scoped scratch-dir cleanup verified against bash signal semantics at the sole call site, and the no-scratch control made falsifiable via a provenance assertion that distinguishes the structured nested-home read from every degraded path — with the frozen byte contract, test count, and fixture design all intact. ## Testing Ran the focused snapshot/fleet-view suite on the target commit (20/20 ok, exit 0), proved the new byte-identity guard fails red under real concurrent-path divergences before trusting it, and demonstrated the user intent end-to-end by racing the pre-change script against the new one on an identical fixture fleet under stock bash 3.2: 16.0s before versus 1.2s after at the default concurrency, with byte-identical emitted JSON, plus a 3.6s→0.016s isolated classify-fold hotspot with identical fold output; the only finding is an informational pre-existing tmpdir leak in the shared test library.

title: feat(bin): add spawn quota gate and durable dispatch log
body:
## Stacked on #1547 This branch is stacked on the still-open #1547 (`fm/dispatch-log-k4`) - both touch `bin/fm-spawn.sh`, so this PR's history includes #1547's commits (the dispatch-log feature) underneath its own quota-gate commits. **Merge #1547 first** (its commits land on `main`, and this PR's diff shrinks to just the quota-gate changes), **or merge this PR instead to land both** #1547's and this PR's changes together in one go - either order gets the same end state. Both PRs are currently blocked on the same external gate, not on anything in the code: GitHub requires a repo admin to approve first-time-fork-contributor workflow runs before CI can execute, and `sctru`'s account has pull-only access to `kunchenguid/firstmate` (no push/merge rights). A repo admin needs to approve the pending Action runs on whichever PR(s) proceed and then merge. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-quota-gate.sh`, which calls `quota-axi --json`, floors the minimum `percentRemaining` across the Claude provider's `five_hour`/`seven_day` windows, and reports `ok`/`sonnet-only`/`pause` (configurable via `FM_QUOTA_SONNET_ONLY_PCT`/`FM_QUOTA_PAUSE_PCT`), failing open to `ok remaining=unknown` on any missing/unparseable data. - Wired the gate into `bin/fm-spawn.sh` for crewmate/scout spawns (secondmate exempt): refuses the spawn at the `pause` level, and refuses an explicit opus/fable `--model` request at the `sonnet-only` level, both overridable with `FM_QUOTA_OVERRIDE=1`. - Added `bin/fm-dispatch-log.sh`, appending durable `spawn`/`teardown` JSON-Lines events to `data/dispatch-log.jsonl` from `bin/fm-spawn.sh` and `bin/fm-teardown.sh` (best-effort, non-fatal), plus a `summary` subcommand to filter by date range and group counts by model/harness/kind/repo/effort. - Added test suites for both new scripts (`tests/fm-quota-gate.test.sh`, `tests/fm-dispatch-log.test.sh`) and documented the new scripts/env vars in `docs/scripts.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, and `AGENTS.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: This follow-up commit is a small, surgical documentation/logic fix that closes the one real correctness gap (fractional percentRemaining) with a verified-correct jq change and otherwise only corrects stale comments to match already-intended, tested behavior. ## Testing All 18 existing fm-quota-gate.test.sh tests pass unmodified on the target commit; since none of them covered the fractional-percentRemaining flooring fix that is the entire point of the last commit, I added a focused regression test and manually verified (with a before/after transcript saved as evidence) that the fix genuinely changes behavior — without it, a fractional quota value like 40.9 silently fails open instead of correctly gating to sonnet-only, which the new test now catches.
Evidence: Manual verification: floor fix prevents silent fail-open on fractional quota percentages target commit (fixed): five_hour=40.9 -> "sonnet-only remaining=40", exit 1 (correctly gated) prior commit 9c76627 (pre-fix): same input -> "ok remaining=unknown", exit 0 (silently failed open, would have let an opus/fable spawn through unchecked) ```text === target commit aad5824 (bin/fm-quota-gate.sh, 'min | floor' fix applied) === Input: five_hour=40.9, seven_day=97.3 (default sonnet-only threshold=40) sonnet-only remaining=40 exit code: 1 === prior commit 9c76627 (pre-fix: 'min' without floor) — same input === warning: fm-quota-gate.sh: no numeric percentRemaining found for claude's five_hour/seven_day windows; failing open ok remaining=unknown exit code: 0 ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
⏭️ **intent** - skipped ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 2 warnings - ⚠️ `bin/fm-quota-gate.sh:66` - MIN_REMAINING is validated with the shell pattern `''|*[!0-9]*`, which only accepts plain non-negative integers. quota-axi's `percentRemaining` is data computed from usage ratios and is not guaranteed to be a whole number (e.g. 39.7). If it is ever fractional, jq's `min` (line 63) returns that fraction, the integer-only case check at line 66-67 treats it as unparseable, and the script silently falls into `fail_open` -> `ok remaining=unknown`. That means the entire quota-pause/sonnet-only safety gate this PR adds could be permanently defeated (always reporting ok) for a real, valid quota-axi response, not just for genuinely missing/malformed data as the header's fail-open contract (lines 29-33) describes. All test fixtures in tests/fm-quota-gate.test.sh use integer percentRemaining values only, so this gap is untested. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:600` - The sonnet-only refusal only fires when MODEL's lowercased value contains "opus" or "fable" (line 601-602). When a caller omits --model, MODEL stays empty (declared at line 194, only ever set from the CLI flag or, for secondmate only, fm-harness.sh secondmate-model at line 560-561) - the comment at line 577 ("MODEL is fully resolved by this point for every kind") does not hold for this case, it's just unset. docs/configuration.md:256-257 explicitly documents that a profile's model field is optional and "an omitted model or effort means the selected harness uses its own default for that axis." In that documented path, QUOTA_MODEL_LC is empty and never matches *opus*|*fable*, so a crewmate/scout spawn whose harness happens to default to an Opus/Fable-class model sails through the sonnet-only band undetected - the exact class of spawn this backstop exists to catch. No test in tests/fm-quota-gate.test.sh exercises a sonnet-only spawn with no --model at all (all sonnet-only tests pass an explicit model). - ℹ️ `bin/fm-quota-gate.sh:56` - `quota-axi --json` is invoked with no timeout, and this script now runs synchronously on every crewmate/scout spawn (bin/fm-spawn.sh:580). If quota-axi ever stalls (e.g. a network-backed provider check), every future spawn would hang rather than failing open. bin/fm-quota-axi-lib.sh already treats quota-axi as a command that may need timeout protection (it supports timeout/gtimeout/perl-based wrapping for `--version`), though that lib's only current caller, fm-bootstrap.sh, also invokes it with no timeout - so this isn't a new pattern, just an unaddressed one now on a hotter path. 🔧 Fix: Floor fractional quota percentRemaining; fix stale MODEL-resolved comment 2 warnings still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-quota-gate.sh:71` - Fixed: the jq filter now does `min | floor` before the shell's integer-only validation, so a fractional percentRemaining (e.g. 39.7) floors to 39 instead of silently triggering fail-open. Verified directly with jq: fractional windows floor correctly, the no-matching-window case still yields empty output (fail-open preserved), and plain-integer fixtures are unchanged. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:577` - Fixed as scoped: the misleading "MODEL is fully resolved by this point for every kind" comment in bin/fm-spawn.sh is replaced with an accurate description (MODEL is the caller's explicit --model or empty), and bin/fm-quota-gate.sh's header now states the sonnet-only check only inspects an explicit --model request. No behavioral change was made (correctly, per instructions - inferring a harness's implicit default model is out of scope), so callers who need sonnet-only protection against an opus/fable-class harness default must now pass --model explicitly per the documented caveat.

title: fix(bin): let an attached watcher arm take over instead of alarming
body:
Only the arm that forks a watcher holds its stdout, so an attached arm can never read the wake reason of the cycle it follows: a healthy wake close and a death look identical to it. Under the Claude Stop-owned protocol the successor arm starts only at the next Stop, far beyond the attached arm's confirmation window, so every attached arm ended in a false "FAILED - cycle ended without an actionable reason". Worse, the alarm's repair text asked for another manual arm, which created another attached arm and closed a feedback loop.

Fix: an attached arm that outlives its followed cycle takes over as the next owner instead of alarming. The false-alarm reproduction from the investigation is included as a regression test.

Observed live on 2026-08-02 (4+ consecutive false FAILED alarms with a fresh liveness beacon each time); root-cause investigation and scratch-home validation preceded the fix.

Catch `WatchError` around the caption `run_quiet` and degrade to a warning. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-video-watch-impl.py:841` - The transient byte ceiling does not bound peak on-disk usage, and the resulting local failure is reported as a remote-access refusal. `MEDIA_FORMAT_SELECTOR` is `bv*[height<=720]+ba/...` with `--merge-output-format mp4`, and yt-dlp applies `--max-filesize` per downloaded format, so a ceiling of N permits roughly 2N on disk at merge time (separate video file + audio file + merged output). Meanwhile `resolve_media_ceiling` only reserves `FREE_SPACE_MARGIN_BYTES` (512 MiB) beyond the ceiling itself (impl.py:699-710). Failing sequence: 5 GiB free, default 4 GiB ceiling (unclamped because 4 GiB < 4.5 GiB usable), a ~3 GiB source; the merge fills the disk, yt-dlp exits non-zero writing no `video.*`, so `run_ytdlp_download` returns `(None, hit_ceiling=False, returncode!=0)` and line 841 raises code 4 "public video download failed without safe public access" - the exit class reserved for unsupported/authenticated/DRM sources - for what is purely a local disk-space failure. That misroutes the operator and contradicts the wrapper header's claim that transient media is "bounded by --max-media-bytes ... enforced before download and again after acquisition" (bin/fm-video-watch.sh:16-19). Deciding whether the ceiling should mean peak bytes (halve the per-format limit or widen the free-space margin) or stay a final-artifact bound with a distinct disk-space exit class is the author's call. - ⚠️ `README.md:176` - The new skill declares `user-invocable: true` (.agents/skills/watch/SKILL.md:6) but is not added to README.md's "Built-in skills" table, whose stated scope is "Firstmate ships these user-invocable built-in skills". At line 1098 `focused = start is not None or end is not None`; at line 1157 the same call passes `ranges[0].reason == 'focused_range'`, which `select_ranges` sets exactly when `start is not None or end is not None` (impl.py:634-641). Move the warning after the candidate check: emit "the run continued without caption evidence" only when `None` is returned, and emit a distinct "caption retrieval did not finish; the transcript may be incomplete" when a candidate is used anyway.
