title: fix: pass backlog JSON via slurpfile in fleet snapshot
body:
Fixes https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/1558

**Problem:** the fleet snapshot dies when the backlog grows large.

**Root cause:** `backlog_json` output exceeds jq's 128KB per-argument limit — `--argjson backlog` fails with `Argument list too long`, so the snapshot aborts before producing output (observed with a 161KB backlog JSON).

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Grow `data/backlog.md` so its JSON serialization exceeds ~128KB (161KB reproduces it).
2. Run the fleet snapshot command that binds the backlog via `--argjson backlog`.
3. Observe the snapshot abort with `Argument list too long` and no output.

**Fix:** switch the three call sites from `--argjson` to `--slurpfile` with process substitution — passes a short file path and keeps the rebinding inside the jq program.

title: feat(spawn): refuse to spawn when the machine has no memory headroom
body:
## Intent

Firstmate could saturate the operator's machine to the point he could not use it. Make every spawn path read real machine state first and refuse to spawn when there is no headroom: crewmate, scout, and secondmate, in every home, demonstrated for each.

MEASURED CORRECTION FROM THE OPERATOR, accepted mid-task and superseding the original CPU-oriented framing. Build against these measurements, not against guesses. CPU IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT: total CPU usage was about 4.6 of 10 cores and not one fleet agent appeared among the top consumers. The machine was OUT OF MEMORY: 24 GB installed with about 1.1 GB free (independently measured at 155 MB unused with 9.6 GB held by the compressor), swap 21.5 GB almost fully consumed at 20.2 GB used, and 25.7 million swapouts. The 1m load average of 299 was processes FROZEN ON PAGING, not work queued for CPU. Consequence for the design: a guard reading load average reads catastrophic while cores sit half idle, and a guard reading CPU utilisation reads plenty of room while the machine drowns - NEITHER is the right instrument. So FREE MEMORY and SWAP PRESSURE are the primary binding signals and load average is corroborating at best. This also explains why pausing three whole domains did not drain the machine: a paused agent keeps its memory, so idle agents still consume the binding resource, and therefore the live-process signal must weigh MEMORY FOOTPRINT rather than process count.

Signals must not be load average alone, because load is a lagging one-minute signal: a fleet can double before it moves. The implemented binding signals are free memory, swap in use, the kernel's own instantaneous memory-pressure verdict, and the memory firstmate's own agents hold measured over whole process trees. Load average is measured and always printed as corroborating context but does not refuse by default. There is deliberately no composite score, because the refusal message must be explainable: each signal is compared against its own limit and reported with its own measured and wanted values.

DELIBERATE DECISIONS A REVIEWER READING ONLY THE DIFF WOULD NOT KNOW, all chosen on purpose and not oversights:
- load_per_core_max defaults to "off" deliberately. On the measured machine load read 299 while the cores were idle, so making load binding by default would read the wrong instrument. An operator who wants a CPU-side ceiling sets a number explicitly.
- The fleet signal is weighed by resident memory over process trees rather than by agent headcount, precisely because pausing agents did not release memory. Trees rather than bare agent processes, because an agent's language runtimes and tool servers are memory the fleet caused and holds. Resident sizes are summed per process so pages shared between processes are counted more than once; the figure is therefore an upper bound and is labelled as resident rather than presented as exact.
- The cumulative swapout counter is reported as context but is deliberately NOT a gate, because a single read cannot distinguish "swapping now" from "swapped a week ago", and sampling twice would make this a monitor. The operator explicitly excluded building a daemon, monitor, or background service: this is a check at spawn time only.
- A machine with no swap configured reads as a real answer and passes that signal, rather than being treated as an unreadable signal.
- The free-memory probe uses genuinely unused pages on Darwin (what `top` reports as "unused") and MemAvailable on Linux, deliberately not MemFree, and the default floor is calibrated for the Darwin reading where the OS keeps unused memory low by design.

HARD CONSTRAINTS, all required by the operator:
- The guard prevents NEW load and must NEVER kill, stop, reap, or deprioritize existing work. This was called out as the trap in the task: the saturation came from workers that were ALREADY ALIVE, so a naive reading of "restore headroom" leads straight to killing live agents and destroying unlanded work. Refusing to spawn is the entire remit. The check runs before any backend, worktree, lock, or metadata mutation, so a refusal leaves nothing half-created.
- The operator being able to use his machine outranks fleet throughput. When the two conflict, throughput loses.
- A guard that cannot read a signal must not silently pass. An unreadable signal becomes an explicit "unknown" and by default REFUSES, because headroom could not be proven; on_unknown = allow is the documented opt-out. This repo was bitten three times in one day by a failed read being reported as a definite negative result, which is why this is explicit.
- A malformed settings file refuses with its parse error rather than reverting to defaults, because a mistyped limit that silently reads as the default is indistinguishable from no limit at all.

The threshold must be operator-settable rather than a hardcoded constant, following how this repo already handles operating choices rather than inventing a new mechanism: a local gitignored config/spawn-capacity file, documented in docs/configuration.md where this repo documents such settings, and added to the existing inherited-config list so every secondmate home shares one setting - all homes share one physical machine, so per-home guesses would be wrong.

The refusal must be legible: it states what it measured and what it wanted, in plain terms, so the operator can see the actual numbers and decide whether to override. A bare "capacity exceeded" was explicitly rejected.

Because firstmate's own test suite runs on exactly the busy machines this guard protects, spawn-driving suites now run against pinned measurements in tests/capacity-pin.sh. Those substitute MEASUREMENTS only - the guard still evaluates every rule against them, and there is deliberately no environment variable that disables the guard.

DELIVERY REQUIREMENT FROM THE OPERATOR, to be stated plainly in the pull request body and not only in chat: this change could not be validated while the machine was overwhelmed, because the daemon it depends on could not be scheduled under memory pressure. That is the strongest argument for the guard existing and it belongs in the permanent record.

KNOWN PRE-EXISTING FAILURES, not caused by this change and explicitly excluded by the operator: tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh was already red on base commit cd73e75, independently confirmed twice, and must not be chased or counted against this work. tests/fm-test-run.test.sh fails two timing-sensitive concurrency assertions ("scheduler waited for oldest worker" and "jobs=2 must refill the first completed slot"); these were verified to reproduce with this change's bin/fm-test-run.sh edit stashed out, and they fail because the machine is currently paging.

## What Changed

- Added `bin/fm-capacity-lib.sh`, a machine-capacity admission check that `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now calls before the task lock and before any backend, worktree, or metadata mutation, so crewmate, scout, and secondmate spawns in every home are admitted or declined by the same gate and a refusal leaves nothing half-created. It measures free memory, swap in use, the kernel's memory-pressure verdict, and the resident memory firstmate's own harness process trees hold (matching interpreter-launched harnesses via the existing harness regex plus a `ps -o args=` fallback), reports 1m load per core as corroborating context that does not refuse by default, and prints each signal with its measured and wanted value instead of a bare "capacity exceeded". It only declines new work — it never kills, stops, reaps, or deprioritizes anything already running. A signal that cannot be read becomes an explicit unknown and refuses unless `on_unknown = allow`; a malformed settings file refuses with its parse error rather than falling back to defaults; a machine with no swap configured is treated as a real answer.
- Made the limits operator-settable through a local gitignored `config/spawn-capacity` (`mode`, `min_free_memory_mb`, `max_swap_used_pct`, `max_memory_pressure`, `max_fleet_memory_pct`, `load_per_core_max`, `on_unknown`), added `spawn-capacity` to `FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG` so every secondmate home shares one setting for the one physical machine, and added `bin/fm-capacity.sh report|check` for a read-only reading of the same signals without attempting a spawn. Documented the settings, the memory-not-CPU rationale, and the machine-wide scope of the fleet measurement in `docs/configuration.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `.agents/skills/secondmate-provisioning/SKILL.md`.
- Added `tests/fm-spawn-capacity.test.sh` (19 cases) and `tests/capacity-pin.sh`, the single owner of pinned machine measurements sourced by `tests/lib.sh` and by the four suites that do not use it, so spawn-driving suites evaluate every rule against fixed measurements rather than whatever the host's memory pressure happens to be. There is deliberately no environment variable that disables the guard. `bin/fm-test-run.sh` now maps the new capacity files to the spawn-driving test families.

The reason this guard exists is also the reason it could not be validated while the machine was overwhelmed: the daemon it depends on could not be scheduled under memory pressure. Verification was completed once the machine had headroom again, including live-machine refusals for each spawn kind, an override run that admitted a spawn, and a malformed-settings refusal.

Note on the pre-existing failures excluded from this work: `tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh` was already red on base commit `cd73e75`, and `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh` fails two timing-sensitive concurrency assertions that reproduce with this branch's `bin/fm-test-run.sh` edit stashed out.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: All three previously accepted defects are closed with verified fixes — the fleet matcher now follows the repo's own interpreter-fallback precedent and fails to an explicit unknown rather than a fabricated zero, the inherited-config enumerations are consistent, and the test-selection mapping is a superset of fm-spawn.sh's — leaving a well-bounded, additive guard that runs before any mutation, never touches live work, and has no remaining substantiated defect.

## Testing

I ran the two targeted suites (`tests/fm-spawn-capacity.test.sh`, 19 cases, and `tests/fm-shared-captain-inheritance.test.sh`, 8 cases), both green, then went further because the runner itself happened to be in exactly the saturated state the guard exists for - 0.1 GB free of 24 GB, 97% of swap consumed, 27.2 million swapouts, kernel pressure `warn`, and a 1m load of 334 over idle cores. With the pinned test measurements deliberately removed, I drove the real `bin/fm-spawn.sh` against that live machine state and captured an operator-level CLI transcript: crewmate, scout, secondmate, and a spawn from inside a secondmate home each refused with every signal printed as measured-against-wanted, and each left no `.meta`, no tmux command, no treehouse worktree, and no lock behind. The same transcript shows the operator raising the limits and being admitted on that identical machine, a malformed settings file refusing with its parse error rather than reverting to defaults, and the primary's `config/spawn-capacity` propagating byte-identical into a secondmate home. Per the intent I did not run `tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh` or `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh`, which are documented pre-existing failures excluded from this work. This change is CLI-facing with no rendered UI surface, so the evidence is command transcripts rather than screenshots. No findings; the worktree is clean.

That is precisely the failure mode the intent forbids ("A guard that cannot read a signal must not silently pass" / "bitten three times in one day by a failed read being reported as a definite negative result"), and it disables the one signal the header calls "the immediate, attributable signal". The same block also uses awk `$4` for the command, so a macOS executable path containing a space yields a wrong basename. No test covers this: every capacity test injects FM_CAPACITY_FLEET_* measurements, so the real ps-tree parsing has zero coverage. The code path itself is correct (propagation is driven entirely by FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG, with no second hardcoded allowlist in bin/), so this is documentation drift rather than a functional gap — but the intent explicitly requires the setting be "added to the existing inherited-config list" following how the repo already handles operating choices, and these lists are how the repo documents that list.

title: fix(bin): preserve released-task PR landing path
body:
## Intent Repair the sanctioned landing path so a task released before its pull request lands can still be landed through it. The captain's 2026-07-31 parked-completion ruling releases a ship worker once its PR is done, green and mergeable - that is, BEFORE the PR lands. But bin/fm-teardown.sh removes state/.meta on release, and both bin/fm-pr-merge.sh and bin/fm-pr-check.sh refused with "task metadata is unavailable" without it. So following the ruling stranded four green fork PRs (#20, #13, #1 and #30, the captain's Windows launcher bridge) from the only sanctioned merge command. AGENTS.md section 7 forbids reaching around that guard with a lower-level command, so the guard had to be REPAIRED rather than bypassed, and no existing refusal weakened. Governing principle chosen deliberately: derive landing identity from the forge, never from the caller. A caller-supplied head is an assertion; a forge-read head is evidence. Design decisions a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: - Preserving the whole meta past teardown was considered and deliberately REJECTED: state/*.meta is the fleet inventory (the session-start digest, endpoint validation and secondmate child sweeps all enumerate it), so a surviving meta would make a released task look live. That is why a separate private state/.landing artifact exists instead of reusing the meta path. - Reading the code showed teardown was ALSO disarming the merge watch on release (remove_pr_poll_artifacts), and the poll's validity and retirement checks hardcoded the meta path. Rather than duplicate that logic, one resolver fm_pr_identity_record_path was introduced (meta while the task is live, landing record once released) and the library call sites route through it. This is deliberate scope beyond the literal defect: without it a released task's merge watch could not be rearmed, and the watcher's existing merged-retirement would reject an authentic poll. - The landing record carries no task id inside it; the filename is the binding, exactly as state/.meta already works. The version tag line fm-landing-v1 is first so the file can never be mistaken for a meta, and every other line sits where the existing fm_pr_metadata_identity_parse contract already accepts it (project= before pr=, only pr_head= after it), so that identity parser is reused unchanged rather than forked. - A merge through a landing record deliberately arms NO poll: a released task has nothing left to watch and gh-axi pr merge is synchronous, so arming a poll milliseconds before merging it would be churn. The spent record is removed after the merge, but only when no poll artifacts exist for that id, because the poll's registration binds to the record and the watcher would otherwise reject an authentic check. - Teardown writes the record UNLESS the forge positively reports the PR merged. That fail direction is deliberate: an unreachable forge is not evidence that anything landed, a record written for an already-merged PR is only an inert file, while omitting one for an open PR is what strands it. A failed write warns and does not block cleanup, because bin/fm-pr-merge.sh can rebuild the record from the PR itself. - Reconstruction from the PR URL is automatic rather than behind a flag, deliberately: a flag firstmate must remember is itself a way to strand work, which is the exact failure mode being fixed. The refusal that matters is preserved and is now stronger evidence than a local file's existence, because it is forge-verified. A task with no meta, no landing record and no PR the forge can resolve is still refused before gh-axi is called. - bin/fm-pr-check.sh now also asks the forge for the head when a live task's worktree is already gone, which previously recorded no pr_head. That is an intentional small improvement, not an accident. - fm_pr_landing_record_write restores the caller's umask after mktemp so teardown's later steps (including fm-fleet-sync's git operations) do not inherit 077. - One AGENTS.md contract line was touched on purpose and kept minimal: section 7's teardown sentence gained one additive sentence documenting the captain's early-release case and its mechanism, rather than rewriting the existing "only after landing is confirmed" timing rule, which belongs to the captain rather than to this change. Explicitly out of scope and left undone on purpose: a landing record whose PR merges by some other route lingers as an inert private file (removing it inside the watcher's identity-bound retirement function was considered and rejected as unnecessary risk to the most safety-critical function), and the session-start digest does not list pending landings (teardown reports them once instead). This must COMPOSE WITH, not replace, the unverified-head refusals being added in parallel on branch fm/pipeline-reports-green-on-absent-ci (upstream PR 1533): empty check rollup, non-success conclusion, unmergeable, changes-requested, with --allow-unverified as the only override. That branch is not landed yet, so trunk still has the old unverified 84-line bin/fm-pr-merge.sh. A read-only git merge-tree probe confirmed that bin/fm-pr-lib.sh, bin/fm-pr-check.sh, bin/fm-teardown.sh and AGENTS.md auto-merge cleanly with it, and that bin/fm-pr-merge.sh, docs/architecture.md and tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh conflict. The intended resolution is additive: resolve identity first, then verify the head, and point their merge_verification= and merge_verified_head= writes at the resolved record instead of $META. Their keys are written before pr=, which the landing record format already accepts. Verification standard applied: colocated behavioural tests only, never asserting implementation-source bytes. For every path added, the failing condition was constructed and watched to fail before the passing case was confirmed - pre-change controls plus five separate mutation controls (drop the open-PR guards; arm a poll in landing mode; never remove the spent record; never skip an already-merged PR; require a meta again for poll validity). Suites green locally: fm-pr-merge 14/14, fm-teardown 41/41, fm-pr-check-security 37/37, fm-teardown-endpoint-safety 5/5, fm-secondmate-safety 70/70, plus bin/fm-lint.sh, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh and the test-coverage guard. CI pins treehouse v2.0.1 while local runs use v2.1.0, so locally green does not prove CI green. ## What Changed - Persist a minimal landing identity during teardown so released tasks can still merge their open pull requests through the sanctioned command. - Resolve and forge-verify PR identity from live metadata, landing records, or automatic reconstruction while rejecting malformed or mismatched records. - Update merge-watch handling, documentation, and behavioral coverage for released-task landing records and their cleanup. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The corrective commit fully addresses the prior identity-rebinding and malformed-record issues, and the complete branch review found no remaining material source risks or intent contradictions. ## Testing The three targeted behavioral suites passed, and a direct CLI exercise demonstrated that a torn-down task retains a private forge-bound landing record, lands through `fm-pr-merge.sh`, arms no poll, and retires the spent record; preserved malformed, mismatched, closed, and unresolvable-PR refusals were also exercised. This is a CLI-only change, so visual UI evidence is not applicable.
Evidence: Released-task sanctioned landing transcript `Shows torn-down metadata absent, private landing identity present, the sanctioned merge invocation succeeding, no poll armed, and the spent landing record removed.` ```text Released task state before sanctioned landing ------------------------------------------------ task-x1.meta: absent (worker is torn down) task-x1.landing mode: 600 fm-landing-v1 project=/released/project pr=https://github.com/example/repo/pull/20 pr_head=2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 Captain runs the sanctioned merge command ------------------------------------------- $ bin/fm-pr-merge.sh task-x1 https://github.com/example/repo/pull/20 forge: merged pull request 20 in example/repo Persisted state after synchronous merge --------------------------------------- merge invocation: pr merge 20 --repo example/repo --squash task-x1.landing: absent (spent record retired) merge poll artifacts: absent (released task has nothing to watch) ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh:98` - The required principle says “derive landing identity from the forge, never from the caller,” and the landing filename is the task binding. However, when a landing record already names PR A, this path queries the caller-supplied URL for PR B and then overwrites the record with B before merging it. Thus any open PR can be rebound to the released task ID and merged after a typo or incorrect invocation. Parse the existing record and require its canonical `pr=` to match the requested URL; use reconstruction only when no record exists. The same rebinding occurs in `fm-pr-check.sh`. - 🚨 `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh:81` - All resolver failures are treated as an absent record, although `fm_pr_identity_record_path` deliberately rejects malformed landing records. A malformed regular `<id>.landing` is therefore silently reconstructed and overwritten instead of being refused, defeating the documented tamper/corruption guard. Distinguish a genuinely absent landing path from an existing invalid one and refuse the latter; `fm-pr-check.sh` has the same issue. 🔧 Fix: Captain, enforce landing identity before reconstruction ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh` - Manual CLI verification using a released-task state fixture: `FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$PWD" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE=".../state" bin/fm-pr-merge.sh task-x1 https://github.com/example/repo/pull/20` - Inspected persisted state before and after merging with `stat`, `sed`, and file-existence checks - `git status --short` after testing to confirm no working-tree artifacts remained
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix(bin): make generated ship briefs self-drive delivery
body:
## Intent

Make generated ship briefs require workers to run validation end to end after committing rather than stopping for firstmate. In no-mistakes mode, require the worker to invoke the pipeline, poll and drive it until a firstmate-required gate or terminal outcome, and explicitly reject waiting for the next decision point while active. Preserve the existing authority, daemon, active-run, ask-user, --yes, CI-ready, and legitimate stop-state protections. Check direct-PR and local-only for equivalent wait-to-be-told wording and correct them if present. Add colocated behavioral tests, generate and read every delivery mode, and keep bin/fm-brief.sh shellcheck-clean.

## What Changed

- Make generated no-mistakes ship briefs require workers to start and drive validation through a firstmate-required gate or terminal outcome.
- Prevent direct-PR and local-only workers from waiting for firstmate before completing their delivery steps, and align validation ownership documentation.
- Add behavioral coverage for self-driven delivery wording across all ship modes.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is narrowly scoped and consistently makes workers own delivery progression while preserving authority escalation, daemon safety, active-run restrictions, ask-user handling, --yes avoidance, CI-ready completion, and legitimate stop states.

## Testing

Inspected the targeted diff, ran the colocated behavioral test, then generated and read all three delivery-mode briefs end to end; the worker self-drive wording and existing safety/authority protections were present, all focused tests passed, and reviewer-visible transcripts and complete generated briefs were captured.

   known external wait you expect to clear on its own (an upstream release, a rate-limit reset,
   a scheduled window): firstmate then leaves your idle pane alone and rechecks it on a long
   cadence instead of treating it as a possible wedge. Use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need help.
5. If you hit the same obstacle twice, append `blocked: {why}` and stop; firstmate will help.
6. If a decision belongs above the implementation worker (product choices, destructive actions, ask-user findings),
   append `needs-decision: {summary of options}` and stop. Firstmate will apply the configured authority and reply with the decision.
   When firstmate replies or a blocker clears and you resume, append `resolved: {how it was decided or unblocked}` (add the same `[key=<slug>]` if you opened it with one) so the decision or blocker is durably closed and does not keep resurfacing.
7. Never stop, restart, or update the shared `no-mistakes` daemon - it is one instance serving
   every lane/home, so restarting it kills other lanes' in-flight pipeline runs. On ANY no-mistakes
   daemon error, append `blocked: {the daemon error}` and stop; only firstmate manages the daemon.

Keep it proportionate: skip `AGENTS.md` edits for trivial tasks that produced no durable project knowledge.

# Definition of done
This project ships **local-only**: no remote, no PR, no pipeline.
The task is complete only when committed on your branch `fm/evidence-local-only`. Do NOT push, do NOT open a PR, do NOT merge.
Keep your branch a clean fast-forward onto the current default branch - if `main` has advanced, rebase onto it so the eventual merge stays a fast-forward.
When it is implemented and committed, append `done: ready in branch fm/evidence-local-only` to the status file and stop.
Do not end your turn waiting for firstmate to tell you to rebase or report the ready branch - those delivery steps are yours.
The configured merge authority approves the ready branch, then firstmate merges it into local `main` through the guarded fast-forward path.

title: feat(bin): require an explicit per-task delivery contract
body:
Implements the revised explicit delivery-mode contract adopted from scout `fm-delivery-explicit-mode-design-r1` (report Q7 contract, Q8 slices). Supersedes #1480, which is closed; only its project-management prose and test scenarios were salvaged, not its `.delivery` record architecture.

## Problem

A task's delivery mode and `yolo` posture were resolved by a silent per-project registry lookup, independently, in two places: `fm-brief.sh` when shaping the definition of done, and `fm-spawn.sh` when writing task metadata. Nothing forced a per-task decision, and an adjusted brief could say one thing while the recorded task delivery said another.

## What changes

**`fm-brief.sh`** requires `--mode` on ship scaffolds, validates the closed set, and records the choice as a fixed machine-readable `Delivery contract: mode=<mode>` line in the generated definition of done. `--mode` is refused on scout and secondmate scaffolds; `--yolo` is refused outright, since the worker never owns approval decisions.

**`fm-spawn.sh`** requires `--mode` and `--yolo` on ship spawns and validates both closed sets. Before any endpoint exists it reads the brief's recorded contract line and refuses a mismatch; a brief scaffolded before that line existed warns once and launches on the flag. A batch carries one shared contract that every pair still checks against its own brief. Scout and secondmate spawns refuse the flags, and a scout now records no `mode=`/`yolo=` at all - teardown already defaults an absent mode to `no-mistakes` and the snapshot renders it empty. When the explicit mode carries less rigor than the project's standing posture, a one-line deviation notice prints and the spawn continues, so the registry stays advisory rather than an enforced default.

**`fm-promote.sh`** requires the same two flags, because a scout carries no posture to inherit, and writes them into the task record alongside the `kind=` flip. The mode is now decided by the firstmate that just read the scout report rather than frozen from scout-spawn time.

**`fm-project-mode.sh`** remains the single registry parser for the mechanical consumers that have no task in hand (fleet sync's `local-only` skip, home seeding's refusal and no-mistakes init). It accepts the conditional `no-mistakes-prod-only` annotation and maps it to its most rigorous leg for them, and grows `--raw` so the deviation notice can tell a conditional policy apart from a flat mode.

**Instruction surface**: AGENTS.md section 7 owns the intake resolution, including the `no-mistakes-prod-only` surface classification and the unregistered-project fallback; the project-management skill defines the conditional policy as a registration-time posture with its defaults and initialization consequences; the registry blurb, script table, and architecture section follow.

## Deliberate boundaries

- The deviation notice fires on a rigor downgrade only (`no-mistakes` > `direct-PR` > `local-only`). Registered `local-only` shipped as `direct-PR` is not announced, matching the adopted contract; that case exposes a remote and may be worth revisiting.
- An unregistered project resolves to the same `no-mistakes` standing default, so a downgrade there is announced too. The notice names the standing posture rather than a registry line, because for an unregistered project there is none.
- No task-scoped state file, no new control plane, and no brief/spawn merge: the agreement invariant costs one grep of the brief.

## Verification

- `bin/fm-lint.sh` clean; `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` ok (61 surfaces, 175 local links); `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` ok.
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed --base main`: 35 scripts, 0 failed.
- New `tests/fm-task-delivery.test.sh` covers the spawn contract (required and closed-set flags with no metadata written, scout/secondmate refusal, brief agreement plus the legacy-brief warning, the deviation-notice matrix, scouts recording no posture), promotion, and the registry mapping. Extended `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` covers the brief contract, including that the explicit mode wins over the registered posture.
- Every suite touched by the call-site updates was run directly and passes, including the real-Herdr, Orca, cmux, busy-state, gate-refuse, and tangle-guard suites.

title: fix(bin): bind Herdr labs to verified parent sessions
body:
## Intent

Fix Firstmate's isolated Herdr lab helper so task-owned labs work safely when the parent fleet runs in a verified named session and the `default` session is stopped. This correction is required to complete the already-approved Arena CRM end-to-end validation.

Reproduce the current operator-visible failure through the public helper interface with the real fleet shape: the parent worker belongs to a running named session, `default` is stopped, and `fm-herdr-lab.sh provision` refuses before creating any lab resources. Separate the initiating trigger, masking condition, and visible symptom. Compare this path with the proven running-`default` path, inspect relevant history, test the smallest counterfactual, and seek falsifying evidence.

Implement the smallest robust architecture that binds each lab to the verified parent fleet session rather than hardcoding `default`, while preserving compatibility for a genuine running `default` parent. Protect the exact parent session identity and state across provision, run, stop, and teardown. Never stop or delete the parent. Refuse ambiguous, missing, changed, or unverified parent identity rather than guessing, and do not infer a parent merely because it is the only running session when stronger task or runtime identity exists. Keep exact mechanics authoritative in the helper header and `--help`. Update only authoritative maintainer documentation and active verification evidence. Review all supported backends and primary harness integration surfaces for applicability.

Add executable public-interface regression tests for at least: a running named parent with stopped default, running default compatibility, multiple running sessions, missing parent, parent state change, attempts to target the protected parent, and complete task-lab cleanup without changing unrelated sessions. Do not assert implementation source bytes. After deterministic tests pass, validate one real isolated lab lifecycle against the current named fleet session using only the patched local helper, and prove the protected parent is byte-for-byte or semantically identical afterward. Run `bin/fm-lint.sh`, `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`, all relevant tests, and the full repository test suite.

Preserve the hard Herdr isolation safety contract. Herdr 0.7.3's API socket is not relocatable by `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, or `HOME`; a named task session plus a trailing `--session <name>` on every task call is the only viable local isolation. Before implementation, reproduce only through the existing helper's safe refusal path and stop if it unexpectedly creates a resource. Do not issue direct Herdr lifecycle commands, including read-only lifecycle probes. Use deterministic test doubles through the helper public interface until the patched helper proves parent-binding and refusal invariants. For the real proof, set `HERDR_LAB_HELPER` to the patched local helper, generate the task session name only through it, supply exact parent identity through its verified public interface, install its documented teardown trap before provisioning, and provision only through it. Route every task-specific non-lifecycle Herdr command through the helper so it appends the trailing task-session selector. Use only the helper for teardown and deliberate task-session stop, with an immediate re-check that the target is not the protected parent before every stop and delete. Never use direct `herdr server stop`, server-global operations, direct `herdr session stop`, direct `herdr session delete`, or Herdr calls scoped only by ambient session state. Record the exact verified parent before provisioning and verify identical protected-parent state after teardown; missing, ambiguous, stopped, or changed parent is a hard tripwire failure.

Ship the committed fix through no-mistakes and raise a checks-green PR into the Firstmate repository default branch. Do not merge it. The preserved Arena pipeline E2E proof may resume only after this fix lands and affected homes update.

## What Changed

- Bind isolated Herdr task labs to an explicitly verified running parent session, preserving `default` compatibility while refusing missing, ambiguous, changed, cross-runtime, or protected-parent targets.
- Re-check the protected parent and task target across prepare, provision, run, stop, and teardown; record a parent-state tripwire and remove only the task lab after a matching post-teardown check.
- Propagate verified parent identity through Herdr briefs and launch/test harnesses, with updated maintainer documentation and public-interface regression coverage for named-parent and cleanup safety paths.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Captain, the amended parent-socket guard now fails closed for Herdr-managed callers while retaining explicit unmanaged-parent support, with matching public-interface coverage.

## Testing

The deterministic public-interface lifecycle passed with reviewer-visible logs; the full suite was started and its real-Herdr tests correctly failed closed because this environment lacks a verifiable parent session, preventing the required live lifecycle proof.

title: fix(bin): stop crew-state from reporting a stale terminal run as current
body:
## Intent The developer dispatched a scout (diagnosis-only) task to determine why bin/fm-crew-state.sh can report an older terminal failed no-mistakes run as the current state when the same task branch has a newer active run or a newer run with green PR checks. They required reproducing the behavior with isolated fixtures or the script's existing test harness rather than mutable live fleet records, documenting expected versus observed state, setup, inputs, and repeatability, and comparing a failing chronology against a proven one that selects the intended run. The report had to identify the authoritative branch/HEAD/run chronology selection rule, the earliest incorrect divergence, whether the bug depends on run enumeration order or stale branch/head metadata, the smallest counterfactual that changes run selection, and the narrowest safe fix with regression-test cases, while distinguishing observed facts from hypotheses. They explicitly constrained the work to not implement a fix, not edit tracked files, never push or open a PR, and to deliver findings solely as a standalone written report at a specified path. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` now gives the same-branch nonterminal run reported by bare `axi status` chronology-based ownership: a run whose head advanced gate-side with pipeline fix commits (and is divergent from or unavailable to the unchanged submitting worktree) stays the current validation owner, instead of losing attribution and letting an older exact-head terminal failed run mask the crew's real state. - Stale runs are still rejected: a run head built on a former branch tip that the local reflog shows was rewritten away after submission is treated as abandoned, and when that head cannot be resolved in the crew worktree the staleness judgment runs against the run's own gate worktree object database located by run id under `NM_HOME` (accepting leniently only when that database is gone). Local work strictly ahead of the run head, and terminal or coarse historical rows, keep the strict head binding, and the coarse `no-mistakes runs` fallback now stops at the branch's newest row rather than searching older history after an identity miss. - `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/configuration.md` document the updated run-selection rule and the `NM_HOME` gate-database input, and `tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` adds 9 chronology/staleness cases (58-case suite passing per the pipeline's Test step). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is confined to one script's run-attribution logic with every new rule documented and conservatively fail-lenient, the split between chronology-owned nonterminal attribution and strictly head-bound terminal/coarse attribution holds up against all the legitimate workflows I traced (merge reuse, squash reuse, amend churn, gate-side advance), and nine new hermetic regression tests cover both the stale-rejection and legitimate-advance twin of each scenario. ## Testing Ran the full fm-crew-state behavior suite (58 cases, all pass) and the four downstream suites that consume the helper (fm-watch-triage, fm-wake-queue, fm-backend, fm-backend-orca, all pass), then demonstrated the fix end-to-end with a hermetic before/after repro running the base-commit script vs the fixed script over identical fixtures: the base script wrongly reports an older exact-head failed run as current (`state: failed`) in both incident variants, while the fixed script correctly reports the newer active run (`state: working · validating (running)`) and the newer green-checks run (`state: done · checks green`).
Evidence: Before/after CLI transcript (base 4ee4a0a vs target f164729, both incident scenarios) === SCENARIO 1: newer ACTIVE run vs older exact-head failed run === ===== BEFORE (base 4ee4a0a: bug) ===== $ fm-crew-state.sh todo2 (exit 0) state: failed · source: run-step · run failed ===== AFTER (target f164729: fixed) ===== $ fm-crew-state.sh todo2 (exit 0) state: working · source: run-step · validating (running) === SCENARIO 2: newer run with GREEN PR checks vs older exact-head failed run === ===== BEFORE (base 4ee4a0a: bug) ===== state: failed · source: run-step · run failed ===== AFTER (target f164729: fixed) ===== state: done · source: run-step · checks green: PR ready for review (still monitoring for merge/close) ```text === SCENARIO 1: newer ACTIVE run vs older exact-head failed run === Fixture: branch fm/todo-flag2, worktree HEAD 5157fdb (unchanged since submission) no-mistakes axi status -> CURRENT run 01RUN: status=running, head=deadbee (gate-advanced, not in crew repo) no-mistakes runs -> OLDER run: failed fm/todo-flag2 5157fdb (exact worktree head) ===== BEFORE (base 4ee4a0a: bug) ===== $ fm-crew-state.sh todo2 (exit 0) state: failed · source: run-step · run failed ===== AFTER (target f164729: fixed) ===== $ fm-crew-state.sh todo2 (exit 0) state: working · source: run-step · validating (running) === SCENARIO 2: newer run with GREEN PR checks vs older exact-head failed run === no-mistakes axi status -> CURRENT run 01NEW: ci step running, PR open, head=deadbee (unavailable locally) no-mistakes axi logs -> 'all CI checks passed - still monitoring until merged or closed' no-mistakes runs -> OLDER run: failed fm/todo-flag2 5157fdb (exact worktree head) ===== BEFORE (base 4ee4a0a: bug) ===== $ fm-crew-state.sh todo2 (exit 0) state: failed · source: run-step · run failed ===== AFTER (target f164729: fixed) ===== $ fm-crew-state.sh todo2 (exit 0) state: done · source: run-step · checks green: PR ready for review (still monitoring for merge/close) ```
Evidence: Standalone repro script (hermetic fixture, runs base vs fixed script) ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # E2E before/after repro for the fm-crew-state.sh run-selection fix. # # Incident shape (from the diagnosis): a crew's branch has a NEWER active # no-mistakes run (bare `axi status` selects it; its mutable head advanced # gate-side and is unavailable to the crew worktree) plus an OLDER terminal # `failed` run whose head equals the worktree HEAD exactly. The buggy helper # rejected the current run on strict head identity, fell to the coarse runs # list, matched the OLDER failed row by exact head, and reported the crew as # failed while it was actually mid-validation. set -u WORK=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd) REPO_ROOT=$1 # fixed worktree (target commit) BASE_BIN="$WORK/base/bin" FIXED_BIN="$REPO_ROOT/bin" # --- one shared hermetic fixture --------------------------------------------- FIX="$WORK/fixture" rm -rf "$FIX" mkdir -p "$FIX/state" "$FIX/fakebin" export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=fmtest GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=fmtest@example.invalid export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=fmtest GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=fmtest@example.invalid # Crew worktree: real git repo on the task branch, unchanged since submission. git -C "$FIX" init -q wt git -C "$FIX/wt" commit -q --allow-empty -m 'task implementation' git -C "$FIX/wt" checkout -q -b fm/todo-flag2 LOCAL_SHORT=$(git -C "$FIX/wt" rev-parse --short=7 HEAD) # Fake `no-mistakes`: bare `axi status` serves the branch's CURRENT run - # nonterminal (running), head deadbee (gate-advanced, unavailable locally). # `no-mistakes runs` serves the coarse history: an OLDER failed run whose # short-sha equals this worktree's HEAD exactly. cat > "$FIX/fakebin/no-mistakes" < "$FIX/fakebin/tmux" <<'SH' #!/usr/bin/env bash set -u case "${1:-}" in display-message) printf '%%1\n' ;; capture-pane) printf 'all quiet\n> \n' ;; esac exit 0 SH chmod +x "$FIX/fakebin/no-mistakes" "$FIX/fakebin/tmux" # Task metadata, exactly what fm-spawn records for a ship task. cat > "$FIX/state/todo2.meta" < "$FIX/state/todo2.status" run_version() { #

If no-mistakes changes that layout, the gate worktree is already cleaned up, or the branch reflog has expired/been pruned, the staleness judgment silently degrades to lenient accept, reintroducing the stale-nonterminal-run masking for the unresolvable-head shape. This fail-lenient tradeoff is documented in the function comments as deliberate, but it is worth knowing the protection is best-effort and layout-coupled. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:389` - The nonterminal chronology leniency granted by nm_primary_run_matches is not extended to the coarse `no-mistakes runs` fallback: a genuinely current run whose head advanced gate-side, reachable only via a coarse row (e.g. when bare `axi status` answered for another branch), fails nm_coarse_head_matches_worktree and loses attribution, falling back to pane/log state. Mitigated because `axi status` reliably reports the current branch's own active run, and coarse rows carry no run id for a gate-odb lookup, so this asymmetry is essentially forced; noting it as a known limitation. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:445` - nm_run_head_built_on_rewritten_tip iterates every entry of the branch reflog, spawning up to two `git merge-base --is-ancestor` processes per entry, and runs on every heartbeat state read whenever the run head misses strict binding (the typical shape while pipeline fix commits advance a run gate-side). For short-lived task branches the reflog is small so this is fine, but a long-lived reused branch with a large reflog would make each crew-state read spawn hundreds of git processes. A bounded scan (e.g. capping reflog entries examined) could be a follow-up if this ever shows up in heartbeat latency.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` - full 58-case behavior suite including the 9 new chronology/staleness cases (all pass) - Manual before/after E2E repro: ran base-commit (4ee4a0a) and fixed (f164729) `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` over one hermetic fixture (real git repo, fake no-mistakes/tmux) - scenario 1: newer active run with gate-advanced unavailable head vs older exact-head failed run; scenario 2: newer CI-monitoring run with green checks vs older exact-head failed run; base reports `state: failed` in both, fixed reports `state: working · validating` and `state: done · checks green` - `bash tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` (exit 0) - `bash tests/fm-wake-queue.test.sh` (all pass) - `bash tests/fm-backend.test.sh` (all pass) - `bash tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh` (exit 0)

title: feat(bin): add deterministic agent lifecycle control
body:
## Intent Fix the CONFIRMED, reproduced spawn/teardown race on PR #1568's branch. This is a scoped addition to an otherwise complete and previously green PR - add ONLY this fix. THE DEFECT (reproduced with real agents, not theoretical): Forced secondmate teardown enumerates a home's task set, acquires per-task control and metadata locks for exactly that snapshot, and then RE-ENUMERATES the same directory while removing. A fresh (non-relaunch) fm-spawn takes only its own per-task .spawn-.lock, so a task id that did not exist at snapshot time is invisible to the preflight but visible to the cleanup. Measured: a record published 0.249s after teardown began was destructively processed - metadata removed, tmux window closed, worktree returned to the pool - while BOTH commands reported success and nothing refused. A per-task lock cannot protect a task that does not exist yet. THE FIX (exactly the mechanism the reproduction report prescribes, nothing more): Serialize fresh task publication and forced teardown through a shared per-home TASK-SET lock, held from enumeration through cleanup. - New fm_task_set_lock_path in bin/fm-wake-lib.sh: /state/.task-set.lock, guarding WHICH tasks a home has, as opposed to fm_meta_lock_path which guards one task's record. One owner for the path and the rationale. - bin/fm-teardown.sh acquires it per home inside collect_descendant_task_locks, BEFORE enumerating that home, parent home before child home, and holds it through cleanup_firstmate_home_children via the existing descendant lock-release path. Refuses the whole forced teardown on contention, changing nothing. - bin/fm-spawn.sh acquires the same lock on the FRESH path only, before its own per-task locks, and releases it after publication. A relaunch is exempt because it republishes a task that already exists and is therefore already covered by that task's control lock, which the teardown preflight tests. The spawn REFUSES rather than waits, because the home may be moments from removal. Either the spawn publishes first and the teardown's preflight covers it, or the teardown owns the set and the spawn refuses. Both directions fail closed. ACQUISITION ORDER (stated in bin/fm-teardown.sh so it cannot drift): each home's task-set lock first, parent home before child home; then per-task locks in that same preorder, sorted by id within a home, each control lock before its matching metadata lock. No child lock holder reaches back for a parent lock, so acquisition cannot cycle. bin/fm-spawn.sh follows the same order. TESTS: two behavioral tests in tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh pin both directions by HOLDING the lock with a live process rather than racing on timing, so neither can go quietly vacuous: a forced teardown refuses while a task is being published (naming the contention, removing nothing, killing no window), and a fresh spawn refuses to publish while a forced teardown owns the set (publishing no record and leaving no lock behind). SCOPE LIMITS - this PR is otherwise finished and was already green; do NOT expand: - Do NOT change bin/fm-send.sh's --key interrupt behavior; that divergence is separately filed as fm-send-key-interrupt-postcondition-r1. - Do NOT rewrite bin/fm-busy-lib.sh or bin/fm-busy-event.sh to force the control-plane interrupt contract onto fm-send. - Do NOT add a `clear` verb or expand the control-plane verb allowlist. - Do NOT add durable launch-specification state for prefixed raw-command harnesses. - Do NOT extend this serialization to the NON-forced teardown path, which refuses on any existing child and is already fail-closed. - Keep every fix from the earlier rounds of this branch intact: prefixed-harness family resolution across the lifecycle verbs, the captain's interrupt contract (delivery proven, cancellation unconfirmed, busy never force-cleared), the honest failed-exit message, the pre-stop kind-capability and ambiguous-relaunch refusals, and the descendant lifecycle-lock preflight. REQUIREMENTS: bin/fm-lint.sh clean; behavioral tests through the executable interface, never asserting implementation source text; deterministic and idempotent enforcement; one-owner rule for the lock path and its rationale; one sentence per line in tracked Markdown; plain dash; genuine full-matrix green CI. This is firstmate's shared tracked supervision-adjacent infrastructure, so hold the highest bar. ## What Changed - Add exact-task `interrupt`, `exit`, and transactional `relaunch` lifecycle commands with verified harness and backend capabilities. - Serialize fresh task publication and forced recursive teardown with per-home task-set locks, alongside descendant lifecycle-lock preflight. - Document the control plane and add behavioral coverage for control, relaunch, Herdr, and secondmate teardown safety. ## Risk Assessment 🚨 High: The confirmed destructive spawn/teardown race remains reachable when cleanup deletes the directory containing the newly introduced lock. ## Testing After correcting an initial test-selection harness issue, focused executable-interface tests and two end-to-end contention checks confirmed both race directions fail closed, preserve existing state, avoid window teardown or task publication, and leave no unintended lock residue; reviewer-visible CLI/state evidence was captured and the worktree remained clean.
Evidence: End-to-end task-set lock contention transcript for forced teardown and fresh spawn ```text === Direction 1: publisher owns task-set lock; forced teardown === $ FM_HOME= fm-teardown.sh domain --force exit=1 ●━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ● WATCHER DOWN - SUPERVISION IS OFF ● 1 task(s) in flight, but no watcher has a fresh beacon (last beat: never, grace 300s). ● Trust the emitted supervision protocol for this harness; do not use shell & for watcher repair. ● This is a supervision warning only; the guarded operation WILL still run. ● repair a missing or failed watcher cycle with the Pi tool fm_watch_arm_pi, or restart Pi with -e /Users/kunchen/.no-mistakes/worktrees/016d88035d58/01KZHR9GCYD6J6QBH838MKX9TY/.pi/extensions/fm-primary-turnend-guard.ts -e /Users/kunchen/.no-mistakes/worktrees/016d88035d58/01KZHR9GCYD6J6QBH838MKX9TY/.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts if the extensions are not loaded. ●━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ REFUSED: secondmate home /var/folders/0k/bf8mwt2n5qddzk24r20gfk0c0000gn/T//fm-secondmate-safety.oJDUG2/evidence-teardown-subhome is publishing a task right now (task-set lock is held); forced teardown changed nothing child_home_exists=yes child_metadata_exists=yes parent_metadata_exists=yes tmux_kill_window_calls=0 publisher_lock_still_owned=yes === Direction 2: teardown owns task-set lock; fresh spawn === $ FM_HOME= fm-spawn.sh newtask --scout exit=1 error: this home's task set is locked by another operation (a forced teardown is enumerating or removing its tasks); refusing to create task newtask rather than racing it new_task_metadata_exists=no spawn_task_lock_left_behind=no teardown_lock_still_owned=yes ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 error - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:909` - The required criterion says “bin/fm-spawn.sh acquires the same lock on the FRESH path only, before its own per-task locks,” but the added lock hunk is reached only after `spawn_remote_secondmate` at line 619. A fresh remote-secondmate spawn acquires `.spawn-<id>.lock`, publishes `<id>.meta`, and exits without the task-set lock, so forced teardown can still snapshot first and then remove that newly published record/home while both operations succeed. Move task-set serialization to the earliest shared fresh-spawn boundary, including the remote publication path. 🔧 Fix: Serialize remote secondmate publication with forced teardown 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:930` - Moving remote-secondmate dispatch below ordinary backend selection makes remote spawns inherit parent backend failures. For example, with FM_BACKEND/config backend set to orca or cmux, lines 643-651 reject --secondmate before spawn_remote_secondmate runs, although that path explicitly hardcodes Herdr and previously ignored ambient backend selection. Dispatch remote secondmates after acquiring the task-set lock but before ordinary backend resolution; resolve the ordinary backend only after return code 3 selects the local path. - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:924` - A remote secondmate spawn no longer supports a missing parent state directory. The task-set acquisition requires $STATE to exist because fm_lock_abs_path must cd into it, but the existing mkdir -p "$STATE" is now inside spawn_remote_secondmate and therefore unreachable. Such a spawn falsely reports task-set contention and publishes nothing. Establish the state directory before acquiring the shared lock, retaining the function's fail-closed error handling. 🔧 Fix: Preserve remote spawn routing and state initialization 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-teardown.sh:1893` - The required per-home serialization is skipped when `<home>/state` is absent. That state is accepted by teardown validation, while a supported concurrent fresh spawn creates the directory, acquires its new lock, and publishes after this early return; forced cleanup can therefore remove the newly published task/home without ever owning the same task-set lock. This leaves the confirmed race reachable. Refuse forced teardown when a descendant home's state directory is absent, or otherwise establish a stable state-directory boundary before enumeration without violating the requirement that a refusal changes nothing. 🔧 Fix: Serialize teardown when descendant state is absent 1 error still open: - 🚨 `tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh:2447` - This test does not exercise the new fail-closed branch in collect_descendant_task_locks as required. Because the regular file exists before teardown starts, validate_firstmate_home_children_removal at bin/fm-teardown.sh:2281 rejects it first via operational-directory validation; deleting lines 1897-1899 would still leave this test passing. Add an executable-interface case that reaches collection, such as an in-home state-directory symlink that passes the earlier containment validation but must be refused by the new -L check. 🔧 Fix: Cover symlinked descendant state refusal 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-teardown.sh:1923` - The task-set lock is stored inside the home that forced cleanup later deletes (lines 2220 and 2523). Once `rm -rf` or `treehouse return` unlinks `<home>/state/.task-set.lock`, a concurrent fresh spawn can recreate `state`, acquire the same textual lock path, and publish while teardown still owns its now-unreachable lock; cleanup can then delete that new record or leave an orphaned task. This violates the required invariant that teardown holds serialization through cleanup. Establish retirement/exclusion at a stable shared boundary that home removal cannot unlink, and make fresh spawn validate it before creating state or publishing.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - Inspected the target diff and task-set lock implementation paths in `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh`, `bin/fm-spawn.sh`, and `bin/fm-teardown.sh`. - Ran focused functions from `tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh`: `test_force_teardown_refuses_non_directory_descendant_state`, `test_force_teardown_refuses_symlinked_descendant_state`, `test_force_teardown_locks_descendant_with_absent_state`, `test_force_teardown_refuses_while_a_task_is_being_published`, `test_fresh_spawn_refuses_while_a_forced_teardown_owns_the_task_set`, and `test_fresh_remote_secondmate_spawn_refuses_while_task_set_is_owned`. - Manually held the live per-home task-set lock and invoked `fm-teardown.sh domain --force`, verifying refusal, preserved metadata/home, zero tmux window kills, and preserved owner lock. - Manually held the live per-home task-set lock and invoked `fm-spawn.sh newtask <project> --scout`, verifying refusal, no metadata publication, no per-task lock residue, and preserved owner lock. - Checked `git status --short` after testing to confirm no transient working-tree artifacts remained.

body:
## Intent Add the approved narrow Wayfinder-derived ambiguity heuristic to both ordinary Claude/Pi mode and Firstmate without installing Wayfinder or introducing a new map, tracker taxonomy, or lifecycle. This Firstmate repository change must specialize the shared rule through the existing scout, backlog, dependency, and decision-hold owners: create backlog work only for decisions precise enough to state now, keep remaining uncertainty as Not yet specified until prerequisites resolve, and ensure planning completion never authorizes a Ship. Keep the change concise and documentation-only. ## What Changed - Added a planning rule to `AGENTS.md`: when work is both ambiguous and likely to span multiple sessions, create backlog work only for decisions that can be stated precisely now, and keep the rest in the scout report or parent backlog body as `Not yet specified` until prerequisite decisions resolve. - Clarified precedence so `Not yet specified` covers only downstream scope that is not yet a captain choice — an unresolved captain decision still registers as a hold under `decision-hold-lifecycle`. - Constrained the rule to the existing backlog, scout, dependency, and decision-hold owners: no parallel map or ticket lifecycle, and planning completion never authorizes a Ship. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A three-line documentation-only addition to AGENTS.md that reuses existing owners and explicitly defers to decision-hold-lifecycle precedence, satisfying every stated intent constraint with no code or behavior surface touched. ## Testing I treated the agent-loaded AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md text as the end-user surface and captured it as a rendered transcript, showing the new planning rule sitting inside the existing Intake and authority section rather than in any new structure; alongside that I verified the four cited owners (backlog, scout, dependency, decision-hold-lifecycle) all pre-exist, that decision-hold precedence and the never-authorizes-a-Ship constraint are stated and consistent with the existing skill policy, and that no Wayfinder artifact was introduced. Targeted automated tests for the touched surfaces — documentation-audience classification, AGENTS.md file conventions, and the decision-hold lifecycle owner — all passed, and the worktree is clean. No screenshot applies: this is an agent-instruction markdown file with no rendered UI surface, so the reviewer-visible artifact is the section as an agent reads it.
Evidence: Agent-loaded AGENTS.md planning rule (as read via CLAUDE.md) + owner/constraint checks == Section as an agent reads it (CLAUDE.md, Intake and authority) == ... Do not build wrappers, control planes, policy layers, custom verifiers, or automation unless the direct path exposes a concrete blocker or repeated need that justifies the added machinery. When planning work that is both ambiguous and likely to span multiple sessions, create backlog work only for decisions that can be stated precisely now; keep the rest in the scout report or parent backlog body as `Not yet specified` until prerequisite decisions resolve. `Not yet specified` covers only downstream scope that is not yet a captain choice; an unresolved captain decision still registers as a hold under `decision-hold-lifecycle`, which keeps precedence. An explicit project wins, a clear follow-up inherits its referent, and otherwise match the request against the registry, work under way, and project code or README. Proceed on one confident match while naming the project in plain language; ask one concise question when multiple or no projects plausibly match. Route by the nature of the work against each registered secondmate scope, not by a non-exclusive clone list. Keep `local-only` work in the main home. Send in-scope work to the fitting secondmate unless it is blocked or the captain explicitly redirects it; do not read the secondmate's chat because marked routed replies return through its status or referenced document. If no secondmate scope fits, use the main home or discuss creating an appropriate persistent secondmate. For one-off or infrequent operational work, start with the simplest direct end-to-end path. Do not build wrappers, control planes, policy layers, custom verifiers, or automation unless the direct path exposes a concrete blocker or repeated need that justifies the added machinery. title: fix(bin): harden tmux agent liveness across harnesses
body:
## Intent

Make firstmate's tmux agent-liveness classification robust across ALL harnesses, prove it with real-harness tests, and establish a standing policy that harness-dependent checks are validated for real and are not brittle. This came out of an independent critique of PR #1568.

BACKGROUND (root cause, verified before this change): fm_backend_tmux_agent_state in bin/backends/tmux.sh classified an agent's liveness by matching #{pane_current_command} against a per-harness name allowlist. Claude Code 2.1.220 now sets its process title to its version string ('2.1.220'), which matches no pattern and fell through to 'ambiguous'. That breaks the agent-control plane on tmux (its hard gate refuses on 'ambiguous') and degrades the bootstrap secondmate-liveness sweep on main today. The kernel comm (ps -o comm=) still correctly returns 'claude'. This is a BRITTLE surface check breaking on a minor harness UX/version change.

REQUIRED WORK:
1. Robust classifier fix (all harnesses). Fix fm_backend_tmux_agent_state to fall back from #{pane_current_command} to the kernel comm of the pane's foreground/descendant process (ps -o comm=), which is immune to a harness rewriting its process title. Do NOT merely add a '2.1.*' pattern - that is exactly the brittle approach that breaks on the next release. The fix must classify correctly for every verified harness: claude, codex, opencode, pi, pi-signed, grok, kimi.
2. Re-verify all harnesses and refresh evidence. Empirically confirm each installed harness classifies 'alive' with the new logic. Refresh docs/verification/runtime-backends.md (the stale 2026-07-07 process-name claim) with dated, per-harness, per-version evidence.
3. Anti-brittleness is a first-class requirement. Across the harness-dependent checks touched, prefer robust structural/kernel/semantic signals over matching against rendered UX surface (process titles, spinner glyphs, keybind-bar text, banners) that a harness can change in a minor update. Where a surface-level signal is genuinely unavoidable, it MUST be backed by a guard that fails loudly (in CI or the live-harness verification) when a harness update breaks it, rather than silently degrading. Call out any remaining brittle checks that could not be fully hardened, with the guard that now protects them.
4. A drift guard that runs in CI. Add a cheap, version-pinned 'still classifies alive' assertion for every installed harness so a future harness release that renames its process (or otherwise breaks classification) fails a check instead of silently disabling supervision/control. Put it in the live-harness-optin family (bin/fm-test-run.sh) following the existing shape (e.g. fm-opencode-primary-live-e2e.test.sh), gated appropriately.
5. Standing policy for harness-dependent validation, IN ITS CURRENT ACCEPTED FORM AFTER AN EXPLICIT CAPTAIN CORRECTION. The policy substance is: harness-DEPENDENT validation MUST be proven with real-harness end-to-end tests, not stubbed/fake-agent tests; such real-harness/manual testing is explicitly PERMITTED to consume tokens (the token cost is justified); and harness-dependent checks must prefer robust signals over brittle UX-surface matching, backed by a drift guard that fails loudly where a surface signal is unavoidable. An earlier revision of this branch placed a four-line version of that rule in AGENTS.md section 4 with the mechanics in the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill. The captain then corrected that placement: the policy belongs in firstmate-coding-guidelines ONLY, and the AGENTS.md block must be REMOVED ENTIRELY, with no inline stub left behind, because AGENTS.md already carries that skill's load trigger in sections 7 and 13 so the skill is read before any firstmate-repo change, and AGENTS.md must stay lean per its size discipline. The current accepted form is therefore: zero policy text in AGENTS.md, and firstmate-coding-guidelines as the single owner of both the rule and how to satisfy it, with the substance intact. This supersedes the earlier AGENTS.md placement; the relocation is a deliberate captain decision, not an accidental deletion of a rule.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE (do NOT do here): the fm-control-specific all-harness e2e test and the #1568 re-verification land on the #1568 branch (fm/fm-agent-lifecycle-control-r1) AFTER this task, because fm-control.sh only exists there; do not touch that branch. Do not implement new control-plane features. Do not harden the unrelated busy-state/composer/spinner surfaces in this change; they were surveyed and reported as follow-up work instead.

This task edits firstmate's shared tracked material (bin/, tests/, docs/, AGENTS.md, .agents/skills/), so the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill was loaded and followed (knowledge-placement decision tree, one-owner rule, inline-stub pattern, AGENTS.md size discipline, one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never em dash, shellcheck-clean bin scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh, colocated tests/<subject>.test.sh, dated maintainer-verification evidence).

DELIBERATE DECISIONS AND TRADEOFFS (a reviewer reading only the diff would not know these):
- The second signal is scoped to the pane tty's FOREGROUND PROCESS GROUP (rows where pgid = tpgid), deliberately NOT a walk of the pane's descendants as the original critique's wording suggested. A descendant walk would report a harness-named process left running in the BACKGROUND of an otherwise idle pane as a live agent, producing a false 'alive'. The foreground-group scoping also covers multi-process launchers (the Pi Launcher path runs a pi-signed wrapper and a pi engine in one group) with no special case. Both properties are asserted by tests.
- The two sources are combined with a UNION rule for 'alive' (either source naming a verified harness is enough), while a readable foreground process group is authoritative for the negative verdicts. This is deliberate and asymmetric: a false 'dead' is the one verdict that can launch a duplicate agent onto a live worktree, so the change can never turn a previously-'alive' endpoint into 'dead'.
- fm_backend_tmux_classify_process_name was extracted as the single owner of the name vocabulary so the two independent sources cannot drift into disagreeing about what a name means. The allowlist patterns themselves are unchanged from the previous implementation.
- Empirically established (and recorded) that the two sources read genuinely different fields: on macOS #{pane_current_command} is the rewritable kernel name a process sets as its title, while ps -o comm= reports the executable identity it was launched with; on Linux the two are read the other way round. That is why the classifier requires only that SOME source attributes the pane and never depends on a specific one, and why the tests assert only that platform-independent property.
- Kimi turned out to be installed after all, at the ~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi fallback path that bin/fm-spawn.sh's own resolver uses, so all SEVEN adapters were verified for real rather than six plus a documented gap. The live guard mirrors that same resolution order.
- TWO tests were added rather than one, because they fail for different reasons: tests/fm-tmux-agent-liveness.test.sh is a portable regression using real processes and NO harness (so it runs everywhere CI runs tmux and catches a code regression), and tests/fm-harness-liveness-drift-live-e2e.test.sh is the env-gated live guard that catches a vendor release renaming its process. The portable test was confirmed to fail against the pre-fix classifier.
- A previous pipeline round on this branch correctly fixed a cross-platform defect in that portable test: the symlink case's source-divergence assertion holds on macOS but not on Linux, where both name sources can expose the symlink name. The divergence assertion now lives only on the compiled version-string case, which diverges on both supported platforms, and the file header and the skill were updated to record that lesson. That pipeline fix commit is preserved in the branch history and must not be dropped.
- The portable test uses symlinks to a real system binary rather than copies, because a copied platform binary fails code-signing validation and is killed on macOS arm64. One case needs a genuine executable file (macOS takes the title from the resolved symlink target), so it compiles a tiny spinner with cc and prints an explicit skip line when no compiler exists; both CI runners have cc.
- The live drift guard launches each harness BARE with no prompt, so it consumes no model tokens, and it deliberately does NOT assert WHICH source carried the verdict (a per-release, per-platform detail that would turn a healthy harness upgrade into a failing test). It asserts only that a title-independent source still attributes the harness, reports absent harnesses explicitly, and refuses a pass that checked nothing.
- docs/tmux-backend.md gained two subheadings ('Agent liveness probe' and 'Composer, busy state, and delivery') so that a pre-existing pointer in bin/backends/tmux.sh to a docs/tmux-backend.md 'Agent liveness probe' section became honest; no anchors link into that file.

VERIFICATION PERFORMED: all seven adapters relaunched for real on tmux 3.6a / macOS 26.5.2 arm64 on 2026-08-03 and confirmed 'alive' - claude 2.1.220, codex-cli 0.146.0, opencode 1.18.11, pi 0.82.0, pi-signed 0.82.0, grok 0.2.118, kimi 0.31.1. Also recorded as new evidence of the brittleness: codex reported 'codex-aarch64-a' at 0.145.0 but 'codex' at 0.146.0, and kimi's foreground comm moved from 'kimi-code' at 0.29.1 to 'kimi' at 0.31.1. bin/fm-lint.sh clean, stock macOS bash 3.2 parse clean, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh clean, and the backend-dispatch (10), secondmate (9) and session-bootstrap (8) test families all pass.

## What Changed

- Harden tmux agent-liveness classification by combining pane titles with foreground process-group `comm` and argv[0] identities through one shared harness-name classifier.
- Add portable real-process regression coverage and an opt-in live drift guard for every installed Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Grok, and Kimi adapter.
- Document refreshed per-harness verification evidence and establish the real-harness, anti-brittleness validation policy in the coding guidelines.
