title: docs: require deliberate context discipline
body:
## What

Adds one context-discipline rule to firstmate's two instruction surfaces, so agents keep their own context small and compact at a boundary they choose.

Auto-compact fires on a token threshold, not a semantic boundary. It routinely lands mid-gate, mid-investigation, or mid-recovery, and the summary keeps the prose while dropping the operational state the agent needed next. With auto-compact off at the harness level, the failure mode flips: an agent that does not manage its own context runs out of it rather than being rescued.

## Where, and why only there

Two audiences, one place each - duplicated instructions drift.

- **`AGENTS.md` section 1** for firstmate. Placed at the tail of "Identity and prime directives", which already carries standing self-conduct that is not a numbered hard rule. Section 3 was rejected because its heading is scoped "run once at every session start"; section 8 was rejected because it is fleet supervision, where the rule would read as being about supervising crew rather than about the agent's own context.
- **`bin/fm-brief.sh`'s `# Rules`, as rule 8** for crewmates, who never read `AGENTS.md`.

Ship and scout share a single `CONTEXT_RULE` shell variable, so the two rule lists cannot diverge. The secondmate charter is deliberately excluded: a secondmate is a firstmate in its own home and reads its own `AGENTS.md`. The new test asserts that exclusion.

Also corrects a line in `.agents/skills/stuck-crewmate-recovery/SKILL.md` that had become false. It told firstmate "A low context reading is not wedging; modern harnesses auto-compact and keep going." With auto-compact off, that is the exact rule firstmate applies when deciding whether to help a crewmate approaching exhaustion, so leaving it would have made this change actively counterproductive. The correction is that firstmate should *notice*, not that firstmate should intervene: the existing guarantee that a low reading is never grounds to interrupt, exit, or relaunch a working crewmate is preserved explicitly.

## The rule states a principle and names no mechanism

Two review rounds established this the hard way. Earlier drafts named a "how" - a scratch notes file, the `stow` skill, a recovery step - and every named mechanism collided with a contract that already owned it: the scratch file tripped `fm-teardown.sh`'s dirty check, the `stow` pointer summoned its mandatory complete pass at every seam, and the recovery-step pointer routed a nudge through an *interrupt*, landing mid-edit - precisely the "partway through" moment this change exists to prevent.

Three for three is not bad luck, so the mechanisms are gone. The rule says what must be true and stops: keep context small; compact at a seam you choose; write down what must survive before you compact; no threshold and no cadence. It names no destination file, no skill, and no recovery step. Notably, no teardown exemption was added to accommodate a scratch file - that would have traded a rule collision for a permanent hole in the unlanded-work check.

No machinery: no context-measuring script, no hook, no threshold checker. No safety boundary was reworded or reordered.

## Rendered `# Rules` section from a scaffolded ship brief

```
7. Never stop, restart, or update the shared `no-mistakes` daemon - it is one instance serving
   every lane/home, so restarting it kills other lanes' in-flight pipeline runs. On ANY no-mistakes
   daemon error, append `blocked: {the daemon error}` and stop; only firstmate manages the daemon.
8. Keep your context small and compact it deliberately. Read what the task needs, not what sits
   near it, and point at an authoritative file instead of copying it. Compact at a seam you
   choose - a finished investigation, a landed step, a closed decision - never partway through
   one. Anything that must survive (findings, a decision, a blocker) is written down BEFORE you
   compact, never only in this chat. No threshold, no cadence: compact when you judge it right.
```

The scout contract renders rule 8 identically; the secondmate charter omits it.

## Verification

- New behavior test `test_context_discipline_rule_reaches_every_crewmate_scaffold` asserts the rule renders in all three ship delivery modes and in the scout contract, and is absent from the secondmate charter. **Proven to fail against the pre-change script** (restored `bin/fm-brief.sh` from `HEAD`, reran, got `not ok - brief-ctx-nomistakes: ship brief lost the context-discipline rule`) - a green run on unchanged code would have proved nothing.
- `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` green.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` **could not run locally**: ShellCheck is not installed on this machine, and installing it would have reached outside the worktree. CI owns that gate.

title: fix(pi): stop the turn-end guard follow-up wedging a Pi primary
body:
A firstmate PRIMARY session running on the Pi harness hung forever on "Working..." for any input, including `hi` — a collapsed tool call, no error, no stderr, no timeout.

## Root cause

`pi.sendUserMessage(content, { deliverAs: "followUp" })` called from inside an awaited extension handler does not queue a follow-up. It starts a fully re-entrant nested agent run inside the parent run's still-open stack frame.

Verified against the installed Pi SDK, version 0.83.0:

- `core/agent-session.js` — `_emitAgentSettled()` sets `this._isAgentRunActive = false` and *then* awaits `this._extensionRunner.emit({ type: "agent_settled" })`.
- `core/agent-session.js` — `get isStreaming() { return this._isAgentRunActive; }`, so inside an `agent_settled` handler the session reports NOT streaming.
- `core/agent-session.js` — `prompt()` honors `options.streamingBehavior` (what `deliverAs` maps to) only inside `if (this.isStreaming) { ... return; }`. Not streaming means the follow-up queueing branch is skipped entirely.
- `core/agent-session.js` — execution falls through to `_runAgentPrompt()`, which sets `_isAgentRunActive = true`, runs a whole new agent turn, and in its `finally` calls `_emitAgentSettled()` again.
- `core/extensions/runner.js` — `emit()` awaits each extension's handler serially, so one slow settled handler holds the run frame open for *every* extension. This was established during this work and matters for the watcher race below.

The trigger: `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh` returns exit 2 deterministically whenever tasks are in flight and no healthy watcher holds the home lock. That condition fired the re-entrant send on every single turn.

## The fix

### 1. New owner for follow-up delivery

`.pi/extensions/lib/fm-followup-delivery.ts` is the single owner of when an operational follow-up may be sent:

- `withSettledFrame(body)` marks an `agent_settled` handler as holding Pi's run frame open.
- `deliverOperationalFollowUp(pi, content)` holds a delivery while any Firstmate settled frame is open, then sends from a fresh macrotask once every frame has closed.

Both Pi extensions import the same module, so the frame count is shared in the extension host process.

**A plain macrotask hop is not sufficient, and this was proven rather than assumed.** The first implementation deferred by a macrotask only; the watcher test written for this change failed against it. The turn-end guard's helper spawn genuinely holds Pi's parent `_runAgentPrompt` frame open for hundreds of milliseconds, so a watcher arm-child close landing in that window still nested. The frame gate is what makes delivery safe.

`deliverAs: "followUp"` is still passed deliberately: a send can legitimately land while some *other* run is genuinely streaming, and without it Pi throws `Agent is already processing`. That rationale now lives in the delivery module header.

### 2. `fm-primary-turnend-guard.ts`

- The `agent_settled` handler body runs inside `withSettledFrame`, and delivery is no longer awaited inside it. The existing one-shot `guardFollowupActive` semantics are preserved, so the follow-up turn does not re-trigger the guard.
- **Consecutive-block ceiling.** `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh` applies `FM_CLAUDE_TURNEND_BLOCK_BUDGET` only in `--claude` mode; the Pi path reaches `block_stop()` and returns 2 before any budget logic runs, so on Pi there was no ceiling at all. After `FM_PI_TURNEND_BLOCK_BUDGET` (default 3) consecutive follow-ups the extension stops re-prompting and posts one visible, non-blocking transcript warning instead. Any healthy turn (guard exit 0) resets both the count and the warning.
- **Spawn timeouts.** `runGuard()` and `runChecker()` (used by both `runPretoolCheck` and `runCdCheck`) now share one `collectSpawn` helper with a hard budget — `FM_PI_TURNEND_GUARD_TIMEOUT_MS` (15000) and `FM_PI_PRETOOL_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` (10000). On expiry the child is killed and the result is treated as *allow*, matching the fail-open posture `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh` documents in its own header. An unbounded spawn awaited inside a hook is the same bug class as the re-entrant send: `runChecker` is awaited inside the `tool_call` hook, so a wedged checker would hang a tool call the same way.

### 3. `fm-primary-pi-watch.ts`

`sendWake()` routes through the shared delivery module. Watcher arm, retry, continuity, and the session-generation ownership rules in its header are unchanged.

### 4. Supporting changes

- `positiveInteger` extracted from `fm-primary-pi-watch.ts` into `.pi/extensions/lib/fm-extension-env.ts` so both extensions share one owner.
- `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md` still documented the raw `pi.sendUserMessage(..., { deliverAs: "followUp" })` call as the correct Pi primary pattern — exactly the call this change removes. A future agent reading it would have reintroduced the bug. It now points at `lib/fm-followup-delivery.ts` as the owner and states the failure mode.

### Scope

**No file under `bin/` is modified.** This is deliberate: PR #1592 is concurrently rewriting the block-budget logic in `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh`, so the ceiling is implemented in the extension rather than in the guard script where `FM_CLAUDE_TURNEND_BLOCK_BUDGET` already lives.

## How this was verified

Tests are colocated per `firstmate-coding-guidelines` and extend the existing suites rather than adding a runner. The shared Pi session fake lives in the new `tests/pi-extension-helpers.sh`, using the established `tests/*-helpers.sh` convention that `bin/fm-test-run.sh` already maps.

The fake reproduces the real SDK ordering: the run flag is cleared before the settled emit, several handlers share one open frame, and a send from a settled frame starts a nested run. It counts `reentrantRuns` — agent runs started while another run frame is still open — which is precisely the defect.

### Fail-before / pass-after evidence

Each fix was individually reverted to confirm its test actually catches the defect:

| Change reverted | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Deferred delivery in the guard | `not ok — Pi guard follow-up must be delivered outside the agent_settled frame` |
| Deferred delivery in the watcher | `Error: the wake started 1 nested agent runs` |
| Consecutive-block ceiling | `not ok — Pi guard must bound consecutive follow-ups and reset on a healthy turn` |
| Spawn timeouts | the suite **hangs** past a 120s timeout — the bug shape itself |

With the fixes in place all of these pass.

An earlier iteration is worth recording: the watcher test failed against a macrotask-only fix with `1 run frames stayed open`, which is what drove the design to the frame gate.

### Suites run

- `tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` — 66 ok, 0 failures
- `tests/fm-pi-watch-extension.test.sh` — 21 ok vs 20 on the untouched base commit (the +1 is the new test), 0 new failures
- `tests/fm-session-start.test.sh`, `tests/fm-supervision-instructions.test.sh`, `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh`, `tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh`, `tests/fm-lint.test.sh`, `tests/fm-startup-memory-budget.test.sh` — all clean
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` — clean against the pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` — ok, 61 surfaces, 175 local links
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed` — resolves the new files correctly, no unmapped-path refusal

### Documentation

Routed to existing owners rather than restated inline: `docs/configuration.md` for the three new environment variables, `docs/turnend-guard.md` for the Pi adapter behavior and regression pointers, `docs/verification/supervision.md` for the empirical Pi 0.83.0 SDK facts.

## What could NOT be verified

Stated plainly:

1. **No real Pi primary was driven.** All verification is against the SDK source plus the session fake. The opt-in `FM_PI_LIVE_E2E=1 tests/fm-pi-primary-live-e2e.test.sh` path has its fixtures updated for the new modules but was not run.
2. **The frame gate covers Firstmate's own settled handlers only.** A third-party extension registering a long-awaiting `agent_settled` handler would re-open the same window, and no extension API can observe that. This limit is documented in the module header.
3. **`no-mistakes` did not run.** The pipeline refused to launch because the globally configured gate agent is `pi`, which it will not run against a repo with `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`. The run failed at launch with zero steps executed. This PR was opened on an explicitly approved direct-PR path instead.
4. **Pre-existing failures in the development environment, not caused by this change** — each reproduces identically on the untouched base commit:
   - `tests/fm-pi-watch-extension.test.sh` — roughly five Pi and five OpenCode arm-recovery tests (e.g. `expected one successor plus two retries, got 1`). Consistent, not flaky. They were excluded from the pass/fail comparison above on both sides equally.
   - `tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh` — `/export did not complete while calm mode was on`.
   - `tests/fm-pi-primary-types.test.sh` — two `fm-calm.ts` type errors against Pi 0.83.0. The files changed here typecheck clean.
5. **A verification claim was withdrawn during this work.** An early draft of the `docs/verification/supervision.md` entry recorded an exact `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh` exit-2 reproduction command. Attempting it in a synthetic primary fixture returned exit 0 rather than 2, so rather than record output that was not actually observed, that block was replaced with a pointer to the regression test that owns the predicate. The SDK facts in that record were each read directly from the installed `dist/` and stand.

title: feat(bin): refuse task-branch pushes that would discard remote work

## Intent Prevent Firstmate workers from losing review-round commits when pushing stale task branches. Add a fail-closed pre-push guard that determines the actual remote branch head and refuses every push effect that would discard remote-reachable work, regardless of force/reset/ordinary command shape; the refusal must name every lost commit and subject. It must refuse when offline, when upstream or remote identity is unavailable or ambiguous, and whenever preservation cannot be proved safely. It must allow an ordinary descendant push and a genuine content-preserving rebase whose replacement commits have changed identities, judging exact reproduced patch content rather than SHA alone; no easy bypass is allowed. Prove the guard red-first and cover dropped commits, clean pushes, patch-equivalent rebases, whitespace-different content, offline, no-upstream, and a provably absent explicit first-push branch. Wire the guard into the generated ship brief immediately before every worker push, with explicit remote and branch on first push. Also require a worker resuming after review to fetch and cleanly fast-forward to the actual PR head before editing, stopping and reporting rather than manually reconciling if it cannot fast-forward. Require commits at each real step—after the failing test is shown failing, after the fix passes, and after documentation when applicable—without imposing per-file commits. Preserve existing brief behavior and tests. Record the independent five-topology scratch proof and compare every broader-suite failure against a clean detached origin/main: seven failures were reproduced there, while the Herdr end-to-end failure passed on both main and the feature branch and must remain classified only as non-reproducible shared-runtime behavior, neither proven pre-existing nor a reproducible regression. ## What Changed - Adds `bin/fm-push-guard.sh`, a fail-closed pre-push check that fetches the exact remote target ref and refuses any push that would discard remote-reachable work, naming every lost commit and subject. It passes an ordinary descendant push and a content-preserving rebase or cherry-pick where each remote-only commit has a verbatim `patch-id --verbatim` match locally, and fails closed on merges, a missing or partial upstream, an explicit target disagreeing with the configured upstream, an unreachable remote, a git too old for verbatim patch ids, and any other unprovable case. A provably absent remote branch passes only in the explicit two-argument first-push form, and there is no bypass flag. - Extends the generated ship brief in `bin/fm-brief.sh` to require running the guard from the worktree immediately before every push (with explicit remote and branch on a first push), to require fetching and cleanly fast-forwarding to the actual PR head before resumed post-review edits (stop and report rather than reconcile by hand), and to require commits after the failing test, after the fix, and after documentation, without a per-file commit rule. - Adds `tests/fm-push-guard.test.sh` (9 cases: dropped commits, explicit-target mismatch, missing `patch-id --verbatim`, clean descendant, patch-equivalent rebase, whitespace-different refusal, no upstream, offline, explicit first push) plus a new `fm-brief.test.sh` case, routes the suite through `bin/fm-test-run.sh` for both the family and changed-path paths, and documents the guard in `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, the docs audience registry, and a new `docs/verification/push-safety.md` recording the five-topology scratch proof and the broader-suite comparison against clean detached `origin/main` (seven failures reproduced there; the Herdr end-to-end failure passed on both main and this branch and is classified only as non-reproducible shared-runtime behaviour). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Every path in the guard fails closed, the four prior findings are fixed at the correct boundary with genuine regression coverage, and the change adds a new script plus brief text without altering any existing runtime or brief-parsing behaviour. ## Testing Ran the four targeted suites covering the change (push guard, brief, test-runner routing, documentation audiences) and all passed, then proved red-first by running the test-only commit's tree where both new suites fail for the absent guard script and absent brief wording. title: feat(bin): merge current main into omp adapter and bound runtimes
body:
## Summary

- Merge the current `origin/main` tip `cf9511217d885cd2127d50993e672c2dfa0539cf` into the published long-lived OMP adapter history without rebasing.
- Preserve the OMP harness adapter, `.omp/extensions/` turn-end guard, and OMP busy-state wiring while adopting main's newer session-lock, supervision, delivery-contract, remote-secondmate, trace-context, and tmux-liveness changes.
- Bound OMP crewmates to `--max-time=3h` by default, with a per-home `config/omp-max-time` override and `off` escape hatch. Other harnesses remain unchanged.
- Add the generated ship instruction to commit work at natural boundaries so an unexpected stop cannot destroy a large uncommitted tree.

## Behavior change

Before this PR, OMP crewmates had no runtime bound unless an operator intervened manually, and generated ship instructions did not require natural-boundary checkpoints.

After this PR, every OMP crewmate receives `--max-time=3h` by default. The first non-empty, non-comment line of `config/omp-max-time` may override that duration with seconds, minutes, or hours, or may be `off` to restore an unbounded launch. This is an intentional behavior change for existing installs.

Generated ship instructions now tell workers to commit work in progress at natural boundaries so an unexpected stop cannot destroy uncommitted work.

The three-hour default is based on the 2026-08-02 evidence: healthy tasks finished in 20-60 minutes, while one converge ran for 9h24m until manual intervention. Three hours is roughly three times the longest healthy task and remains operator-overridable.

## Conflict resolution

### Original merge through `4ee4a0a`

- Resolved session-lock ancestry, attached-watcher supervision, and queued-wake conflicts toward main because those commits corrected stale adapter-side behavior.
- Resolved the explicit per-task delivery-contract conflicts toward main's required `--mode` and `--yolo` contract while retaining the adapter branch's OMP-only project-extension approval and launch wiring.
- Retained the adapter branch's `omp` harness detection, launch template, `.omp/extensions/` turn-end guard, busy-state behavior, documentation, and tests wherever they were additive.
- Combined documentation and test conflicts when main and the adapter branch covered different behavior.

### Refresh merge through current main `cf9511217d885cd2127d50993e672c2dfa0539cf`

- Combined main's trace-context and remote-route metadata documentation with the branch's captain-authorized merge-check override metadata.
- Took main's centralized tmux process-classification fix and main's portable distinct-process fixture.
- Retained the branch's OMP runtime identity evidence and OMP session-start diagnostics, while keeping main's test footer.

## Verification

Passed after the current-main merge:

- `bin/fm-lint.sh`
- `tests/fm-omp-harness.test.sh`
- `tests/fm-brief.test.sh`
- `tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh`
- `tests/fm-session-start.test.sh`
- `tests/fm-tmux-agent-liveness.test.sh`
- `tests/fm-backend-tmux-smoke.test.sh`
- `tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh`
- Portable parallel lane 1: 11 scripts, zero failures, one expected optional dependency skip.
- Portable parallel lane 2: 13 scripts, zero failures.

Mutation proof for OMP runtime threading:

1. Removed the launch-template threading.
2. `tests/fm-omp-harness.test.sh` failed with `configured omp launch did not thread the max-time override` and showed the missing `omp --auto-approve --max-time=10m` fragment.
3. Restored the threading.
4. The test passed with `omp max-time defaults to 3h, supports override and off, validates input, and stays omp-only`.

Real Herdr regression evidence collected before the final main refresh also passed for focus-safe cleanup and exact stale-session cleanup on Herdr 0.7.5 protocol 17.

## Known findings

The complete local suite is not green, and these findings are intentionally recorded rather than hidden:

- Portable serial shard 1 initially had one fixture failure in `tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh` after current main made the tmux adapter source `fm-session-lock-lib.sh`. The fixture now includes that required sibling, and the test passes standalone. The entire shard was not rerun after that fixture correction.
- Portable serial shard 2 still reports `tests/fm-remote-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh`: `failing seed exited before remote provisioning`. Per captain direction, this was not pursued further and should be treated as a current-main integration finding.
- The same shard also reports `tests/fm-backend.test.sh`: `fm-send --key: old vs new exit code: expected exit 1, got 0`.
- Portable serial shards 3 and 4 and the remaining real-Herdr lane were not rerun after the final current-main merge because the captain directed immediate delivery.
- The installed global `tasks-axi` 0.2.2 lacks the `public-followup` command used by current main. `tests/fm-public-followup.test.sh` passes with a worktree-local `tasks-axi` 0.2.4.

title: feat(skills): add Lavish PR walkthrough skill
body:
## Intent

Add a short captain-invocable skill to the firstmate repo, lavish-pr-review, capturing the ask 'make a lavish that walks me through this PR with code snippets'.

Goal: when the captain says '/lavish-PR-review', 'make a lavish walkthrough of PR N', 'walk me through this PR visually', or 'lavish me that PR with code snippets', firstmate should produce a Lavish artifact that explains a pull request well enough for a merge decision - not a diff dump and not a code review.

Required content, deliberately kept short (procedure skill, not an essay; existing skills in .agents/skills/ are the length and tone model):
- Trigger phrasing in the frontmatter description, precise enough to fire on this ask and not on ordinary review or ship requests.
- The deliverable is a walkthrough for understanding and a merge decision - distinct from /code-review, which judges the change, and distinct from a scout report.
- Dispatch shape: this is project work, so it goes to a worker, not to firstmate directly; the worker reads the PR branch READ-ONLY and never commits, pushes, or comments on the PR.
- The content spine: what the feature is and what it is easy to confuse it with; the data model with the real schema and any hand-written database constraints; the read and write paths shown through the snippets that carry the real invariants rather than the plumbing; the user-facing surface; what changed in the most recent commits as before/after; what is deliberately not done; and a closing risk read plus any product calls presented as decisions.
- Snippet discipline: real code from the branch with file:line references, trimmed to what is being explained, never a whole file.
- Lavish mechanics: open the relevant lavish-axi playbook entries before writing HTML, follow lavish-axi design and match the SUBJECT project's design system rather than the generic CDN default, write the artifact under .lavish/, then open it and poll in the FOREGROUND so feedback returns to the worker - never background the poll.
- When the captain's feedback asks for code changes rather than artifact changes: do not make them, raise them so firstmate routes the work properly.

Deliberate decisions and constraints:
- The skill deliberately does NOT restate the general crewmate lifecycle, status protocol, or delivery rules - those already have owners in AGENTS.md, per the one-owner rule in the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill.
- It was derived from a live example brief written for one specific PR, but is intentionally generalized to any PR with no project-specific detail copied in.
- Frontmatter is captain-invocable: user-invocable: true with metadata.internal: true, matching neighbouring built-in skills such as ahoy, bearings, and stow; it is NOT an agent-only skill, so it does not carry user-invocable: false.
- Shortness is an explicit acceptance criterion: roughly a screen and a half maximum.
- Registration was checked rather than assumed, and the skill is registered in the three places this repo expects: a one-line load trigger in AGENTS.md section 7 (per the trigger-hygiene rule that every new skill needs its trigger declared inline), a row in the README 'Built-in skills' table for user-invocable skills, and an agent-runtime surface entry in docs/documentation-audiences.json. bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh passes.
- Repo style rules from firstmate-coding-guidelines are followed, including one sentence per line in tracked Markdown and plain dashes rather than em dashes.

## What Changed

- Adds the captain-invocable `lavish-pr-review` skill for visual PR walkthroughs focused on merge decisions, with real branch code snippets and read-only worker dispatch.
- Defines the walkthrough content spine, snippet discipline, Lavish artifact workflow, and handling for feedback that requests project code changes.
- Registers the skill in `AGENTS.md`, the README built-in skills table, and `docs/documentation-audiences.json`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is a bounded documentation/skill addition that satisfies the stated walkthrough, dispatch, Lavish, feedback, style, and registration requirements.

## Testing

No baseline test command was provided. The focused documentation-audience check and regression test passed, and the acceptance transcript directly records the captain-facing trigger, read-only worker dispatch, required walkthrough content, Lavish mechanics, feedback boundary, and three registration surfaces. The changed-file suite and isolated rerun reproduced two unrelated harness failures in Pi Calm and Kimi; the worktree remained clean and no transient project artifacts were created.

title: fix(bin): stop teardown refusing task worktrees that hold no unlanded work
body:
## Intent Stop bin/fm-teardown.sh from refusing to tear down a finished task worktree that holds no real unlanded work, so the unlanded-work guard only fires on genuine work and does not get routinely waved through with an override. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-teardown.sh` no longer treats every dirty `git status` as unlanded work: when a second copy on the same branch advances the ref, the copy's index and working tree still agree, so teardown proves the shared content tree IS the tree of a commit already reachable from a remote (or the local default branch in local-only mode) and clears the refusal, naming the commit. The proof is gated by an index-only shape pre-check so genuine dirty worktrees stay read-only, runs against an index copy so the task's real index is never staged into, and is bounded by `FM_TEARDOWN_STALE_CONTENT_SCAN_LIMIT` (default 500, non-numeric/zero falls back). Any real edit, staged-then-modified file, or crewmate-authored untracked file still refuses. - Firstmate's own worktree scaffolding is now a single list (`FM_WORKTREE_SCAFFOLD_PATHS`) shared by removal, the dirty filter, and the content proof, with `--untracked-files=all` porcelain and exact-path matching so a crewmate's new file beside `.claude/` scaffolding no longer hides behind a directory-level tolerance; tracked paths are never deleted. - `bin/fm-spawn.sh` delivers claude hooks from `state/.claude-settings.json` via `--settings` (inserted after the command word for raw `claude` launches) instead of writing into the worktree; unverified wrappers and operator-supplied `--settings` fall back to the copy's untracked `.claude/settings.local.json`, and a project that tracks that path gets no hooks and no busy arm rather than a busy record nothing can clear. Plus bash 3.2 hardening (`fm-backend.sh` refuses a missing adapter before sourcing, spawn aborts on an unwritable meta file), docs updates, and new teardown/spawn/busy-wiring test cases. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Every prior concern is closed: the teardown clearance requires whole-tree equality with a commit reachable from a remote and is cheaply pre-gated to index-only shapes so it can only ever add refusals, the scan-limit override is validated, and the claude hook fallback now carries recorded empirical evidence on the installed version - with allow and refuse tests on both sides and no behavior change in this round. ## Testing Ran the full fm-teardown suite (all cases pass, including the eight new collision allow/refuse cases) and the two other directly-changed suites, then went beyond unit coverage with an end-to-end repro that drives the real bin/fm-teardown.sh against actual git fleets: the base-commit script falsely REFUSES a finished, fully-pushed task whose branch advanced under a follow-up worktree, and the branch script tears the same fleet down cleanly while printing why the stale signal is not work. Safety held in every negative variant - a genuine uncommitted edit, a crewmate's new file under .claude/, and content on no remote all still refuse with the task record intact, refused worktrees come out byte-identical (nothing staged into the real index), and no --force override is involved in the clearance; the success path also reproduces under macOS system bash 3.2. The change is CLI-only with no rendered UI surface, so the reviewer-visible evidence is command transcripts rather than screenshots.
Evidence: Before vs after: the same finished task, base commit refuses, branch tears down ```text $ git -C wt status --porcelain --untracked-files=all # what the captain sees M feature.txt D followup.txt --- BEFORE (base ef2c3a2) --- $ fm-teardown.sh task-x1 REFUSED: worktree .../wt has uncommitted changes. uncommitted changes present Commit them (or get the captain's explicit OK to discard, then --force). exit status: 1 task record state/task-x1.meta: STILL PRESENT --- AFTER (this branch) --- $ fm-teardown.sh task-x1 teardown: worktree .../wt reports differences only because its branch advanced in another copy; its content is exactly commit b241f98b377b4bd1e15e385940b64c085d50ef7b, which is already landed, so nothing here is unlanded work treehouse: returned .../wt to the pool teardown task-x1 complete (window firstmate:fm-task-x1, worktree .../wt) exit status: 0 task record state/task-x1.meta: removed (task torn down) ```
Evidence: Guard still refuses genuine work on the same collision shape ```text AFTER + a genuine uncommitted edit exit=1 REFUSED (uncommitted changes) AFTER + firstmate scaffolding AND crewmate .claude/commands/new-cmd.md exit=1 REFUSED, file preserved on disk AFTER + the copy's content is on no remote exit=1 REFUSED AFTER + only firstmate's own leftover hook scaffolding exit=0 torn down AFTER on system bash 3.2.57(1)-release, same collision exit=0 torn down ```
- Evidence: Full transcript set (7 teardown scenarios + post-refusal integrity proof) (local file: /var/folders/kn/l_75ymkd6lqc1jgyfx7tvyh80000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZ90M8AV36W5CJ1DKBGK04AS/transcripts)
Evidence: End-to-end repro script (rebuilds every fleet and transcript from scratch) ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # End-to-end reproduction of the worktree-branch-collision false refusal. # # Builds a real firstmate-shaped fleet (bare origin, project clone, task worktree on # fm/task-x1, state dir with a task meta file), lands the task's work on the remote, # then lets a SECOND copy on the same branch advance the branch ref - the exact shape # a follow-up task produces. The original copy now reports staged modifications for # work that is already pushed. # # It then runs the REAL bin/fm-teardown.sh twice against identical fleets: # before/ - fm-teardown.sh from the base commit # after/ - fm-teardown.sh from this branch # and repeats the "after" run for three genuine-work variants that must still refuse. set -u BASE_COMMIT=${BASE_COMMIT:?set BASE_COMMIT} REPO=${REPO:?set REPO} OUT=${OUT:?set OUT} SANDBOX=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fm-collision-repro.XXXXXX") export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=fmtest GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=fmtest@example.invalid export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=fmtest GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=fmtest@example.invalid mkdir -p "$OUT" # --- old fm-teardown.sh, wired to the current bin/ for its libs ----------------- OLD_BIN="$SANDBOX/old-bin" mkdir -p "$OLD_BIN" for f in "$REPO"/bin/*; do ln -s "$f" "$OLD_BIN/$(basename "$f")"; done rm -f "$OLD_BIN/fm-teardown.sh" git -C "$REPO" show "$BASE_COMMIT:bin/fm-teardown.sh" > "$OLD_BIN/fm-teardown.sh" chmod +x "$OLD_BIN/fm-teardown.sh" # Build one complete fleet. Args: name make_fleet() { local name=$1 case_dir fakebin case_dir="$SANDBOX/$name" fakebin="$case_dir/fakebin" mkdir -p "$case_dir/state" "$case_dir/config" "$fakebin" # treehouse stub that performs the real pool return (hard reset + clean), so the # transcript shows what teardown would actually do to the copy's contents. cat > "$fakebin/treehouse" <<'SH' #!/usr/bin/env bash # `treehouse return --force ` wt=${3:-} [ -d "$wt" ] || exit 0 git -C "$wt" checkout -q --detach 2>/dev/null || true git -C "$wt" reset -q --hard 2>/dev/null || true git -C "$wt" clean -qfd 2>/dev/null || true echo "treehouse: returned $wt to the pool" SH cat > "$fakebin/tmux" <<'SH' #!/usr/bin/env bash exit 0 SH # No GitHub PR for this branch: the remote itself is the landing proof. cat > "$fakebin/gh-axi" <<'SH' #!/usr/bin/env bash case "${1:-} ${2:-}" in "pr list") printf '%s\n' "count: 0 (showing first 0)" "pull_requests[]: []" ; exit 0 ;; "pr view") echo "error: pull request not found" >&2 ; exit 1 ;; esac exit 0 SH cat > "$fakebin/gh" <<'SH' #!/usr/bin/env bash case "${1:-} ${2:-}" in "pr view") echo "error: pull request not found" >&2 ; exit 1 ;; esac exit 0 SH cat > "$fakebin/no-mistakes" <<'SH' #!/usr/bin/env bash exit 0 SH chmod +x "$fakebin"/* git init -q --bare "$case_dir/origin.git" git -C "$case_dir/origin.git" symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main git clone -q "$case_dir/origin.git" "$case_dir/_seed" 2>/dev/null git -C "$case_dir/_seed" commit -q --allow-empty -m "origin baseline" git -C "$case_dir/_seed" push -q origin main rm -rf "$case_dir/_seed" git clone -q "$case_dir/origin.git" "$case_dir/project" git -C "$case_dir/project" remote set-head origin main 2>/dev/null || true git -C "$case_dir/project" worktree add -q -b fm/task-x1 "$case_dir/wt" main touch "$case_dir/state/.last-watcher-beat" cat > "$case_dir/state/task-x1.meta" < "$case_dir/wt/feature.txt" git -C "$case_dir/wt" add -- feature.txt git -C "$case_dir/wt" commit -q -m "add feature" git -C "$case_dir/wt" push -q -u origin fm/task-x1 git -C "$case_dir/project" fetch -q origin printf '%s\n' "$case_dir" } # A follow-up task puts a SECOND copy on the same branch and commits. The branch ref # advances under the original copy. Args: case_dir [push|nopush] collide() { local case_dir=$1 push=${2:-push} second="$1/wt2" git -C "$case_dir/project" worktree add -q --detach "$second" fm/task-x1 printf '%s\n' "follow-up rewrite" > "$second/feature.txt" printf '%s\n' "follow-up addition" > "$second/followup.txt" git -C "$second" add -A git -C "$second" commit -q -m "follow-up commit" git -C "$second" update-ref refs/heads/fm/task-x1 HEAD if [ "$push" = push ]; then git -C "$second" push -q origin fm/task-x1 git -C "$case_dir/project" fetch -q origin fi } run_teardown() { # case_dir bin_dir local case_dir=$1 bin_dir=$2 FM_GATE_REFUSE_BYPASS=1 \ FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$REPO" \ FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$case_dir/state" \ FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$case_dir/config" \ PATH="$case_dir/fakebin:$PATH" \ ${TEARDOWN_SHELL:-} "$bin_dir/fm-teardown.sh" task-x1 } # Print the captain-visible situation, run teardown, print the outcome. # Args: transcript_path title case_dir bin_dir scenario() { local out=$1 title=$2 case_dir=$3 bin_dir=$4 rc { echo "==============================================================================" echo "$title" echo "==============================================================================" echo echo "\$ git -C wt status --porcelain --untracked-files=all # what the captain sees" git -C "$case_dir/wt" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all echo echo "\$ git -C wt log --oneline -1 HEAD # branch ref (moved by the follow-up copy)" git -C "$case_dir/wt" log --oneline -1 HEAD echo echo "\$ fm-teardown.sh task-x1 ($(basename "$bin_dir")/fm-teardown.sh)" echo "------------------------------------------------------------------------------" } > "$out" set +e run_teardown "$case_dir" "$bin_dir" >> "$out" 2>&1 rc=$? set -e { echo "------------------------------------------------------------------------------" echo "exit status: $rc" if [ -f "$case_dir/state/task-x1.meta" ]; then echo "task record state/task-x1.meta: STILL PRESENT (task not torn down)" else echo "task record state/task-x1.meta: removed (task torn down)" fi if [ -f "$case_dir/wt/notes.txt" ] || [ -f "$case_dir/wt/.claude/commands/new-cmd.md" ]; then echo "crewmate's untracked file: still on disk (preserved)" fi echo } >> "$out" printf '%s exit=%s\n' "$title" "$rc" } # --- 1. collision, work landed: BEFORE (base commit) --------------------------- c=$(make_fleet before); collide "$c" scenario "$OUT/01-before-false-refusal.txt" \ "BEFORE (base $BASE_COMMIT): finished task, work pushed, branch advanced by a follow-up copy" \ "$c" "$OLD_BIN" # --- 2. same fleet, AFTER (this branch) ---------------------------------------- c=$(make_fleet after); collide "$c" scenario "$OUT/02-after-teardown-succeeds.txt" \ "AFTER (this branch): same fleet, same collision" \ "$c" "$REPO/bin" # --- 3. AFTER + a genuine uncommitted edit ------------------------------------- c=$(make_fleet after-real-edit); collide "$c" printf '%s\n' "work nobody has seen" > "$c/wt/feature.txt" scenario "$OUT/03-after-real-edit-still-refuses.txt" \ "AFTER + a genuine uncommitted edit: the guard must still refuse" \ "$c" "$REPO/bin" # --- 4. AFTER + an untracked crewmate file ------------------------------------- c=$(make_fleet after-untracked); collide "$c" git -C "$c/wt" config core.excludesFile /dev/null mkdir -p "$c/wt/.claude/commands" printf '%s\n' '{"hooks":{}}' > "$c/wt/.claude/settings.local.json" # firstmate's own scaffolding printf '%s\n' "# new slash command the crewmate wrote" > "$c/wt/.claude/commands/new-cmd.md" scenario "$OUT/04-after-untracked-work-still-refuses.txt" \ "AFTER + firstmate scaffolding AND a crewmate's new .claude/commands file: must still refuse" \ "$c" "$REPO/bin" # --- 5. AFTER, collision but content on no remote ------------------------------ c=$(make_fleet after-unpushed) # Real work the crewmate committed but never pushed: this copy's content tree is on # no remote, so the collision shape alone must not clear the refusal. printf '%s\n' "work only this copy has" > "$c/wt/feature.txt" git -C "$c/wt" add -- feature.txt git -C "$c/wt" commit -q -m "unpushed work" collide "$c" nopush scenario "$OUT/05-after-unpushed-still-refuses.txt" \ "AFTER + the copy's content is on no remote: must still refuse" \ "$c" "$REPO/bin" # --- 6. AFTER + only firstmate's own leftover scaffolding ---------------------- c=$(make_fleet after-scaffold); collide "$c" git -C "$c/wt" config core.excludesFile /dev/null mkdir -p "$c/wt/.claude" printf '%s\n' '{"hooks":{}}' > "$c/wt/.claude/settings.local.json" printf '%s\n' "$c/state/task-x1.turn-ended" > "$c/wt/.fm-grok-turnend" scenario "$OUT/06-after-leftover-scaffold-succeeds.txt" \ "AFTER + only firstmate's own leftover hook scaffolding: still no work, tear down" \ "$c" "$REPO/bin" # --- 7. AFTER, same collision, driven by macOS's system bash 3.2 --------------- c=$(make_fleet after-bash32); collide "$c" TEARDOWN_SHELL=/bin/bash scenario "$OUT/07-after-bash32-succeeds.txt" \ "AFTER on system bash $(/bin/bash -c 'echo $BASH_VERSION'): same collision" \ "$c" "$REPO/bin" echo echo "sandbox: $SANDBOX" echo "transcripts: $OUT" ```

✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 5 issues found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:956` - Raw launch commands for claude wrappers lose all turn-end and busy-state wiring they used to get. Before this change, `case "$HARNESS" in claude*)` armed the busy contract and wrote `$WT/.claude/settings.local.json`, which a wrapper like `claude-yolo` (execing claude in the same cwd) loaded automatically. Now wiring is gated on `CLAUDE_HOOK_SETTINGS=1`, which is only set when the command word is exactly `claude` and carries no operator `--settings`. Result: for `claude-yolo ...` (and for an operator passing their own `--settings`), no busy state is armed, no `$TURNEND` touch ever fires, so the watcher never sees a turn boundary for that task - only a warn line at spawn. A middle path exists: keep writing `$WT/.claude/settings.local.json` (plus `exclude_path`) for wrapper launches when that path is untracked, which preserves wiring and still avoids the tracked-file case that motivated the move. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:930` - `dirty_is_landed_stale_content` is invoked for every non-empty dirty result, so the common genuine-dirty case (crewmate has real uncommitted work, teardown will refuse) now pays a full `git add -A` plus two `write-tree` against an index copy - hashing every modified and untracked file and writing blob/tree objects into the shared object store - before refusing anyway. Repeated teardown attempts on a dirty worktree accumulate unreferenced loose objects from a path that is otherwise read-only validation. A cheap, provably equivalent pre-gate avoids it: the collision shape only ever produces porcelain lines with an index-side change and a space in column 2, so if any surviving line is `??` or has a non-space column 2, the index and worktree already differ and `index_tree = work_tree` can never hold - return 1 before building trees. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:878` - `STALE_CONTENT_SCAN_LIMIT=${FM_TEARDOWN_STALE_CONTENT_SCAN_LIMIT:-500}` is used verbatim as `git log --max-count="$STALE_CONTENT_SCAN_LIMIT"` with no numeric validation. A typo'd or non-numeric value (e.g. `FM_TEARDOWN_STALE_CONTENT_SCAN_LIMIT=500 commits`, or an empty-after-expansion string) makes `git log` fail, `scan=$(...) || return 1` fires, and the whole clearance silently never engages - reinstating exactly the false refusal this change removes, with no diagnostic. `NM_TEARDOWN_TIMEOUT` right below at line 1304 already establishes the repo's convention: `case "$X" in ''|*[!0-9]*) X=<default> ;; esac`. Apply the same guard here. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1928` - Moving the hook file to `state/` also dropped `exclude_path '.claude/settings.local.json'`, so that path is no longer added to the worktree's `.git/info/exclude`. Firstmate no longer creates the file, but Claude Code can still write it during a session (permission/local-settings changes). Previously it was invisible to git; now it shows as untracked, and a crewmate running `git add -A` before committing would sweep local claude settings into the project's PR. Teardown still tolerates and deletes it, so this only affects what lands in commits. Re-adding the `exclude_path` call is harmless even when the project tracks the path (ignore rules never apply to tracked files), if keeping that protection is wanted. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:26` - The header (line 26) and the `dirty_is_landed_stale_content` comment (line 944) both name `git checkout -B <branch> origin/<branch>` in a second worktree as the mechanism that advances the branch ref. Git refuses that when another worktree holds the branch, which the change's own test acknowledges: tests/fm-teardown.test.sh:952 says "`git checkout -B` and `git branch -f` both refuse a branch that another worktree already holds" and reproduces the symptom with a detached worktree plus `git update-ref` instead. The stated root cause is therefore not reachable as written, which matters because the comments are the repo's record of why the guard exists and what shape it must recognize. Worth correcting to the mechanism actually observed in the field. 🔧 Fix: gate stale-content proof, validate scan limit, rewire claude wrappers 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:971` - For the operator-supplied-`--settings` raw launch, the new fallback sets CLAUDE_HOOK_MODE=worktree-local, arms the busy contract (line 1898), and writes hooks to `$WT/.claude/settings.local.json` - relying on those hooks still firing while claude also loads the operator's own `--settings` file. docs/verification/supervision.md enumerates exactly three verified properties on Claude Code 2.1.220, and the pairing it verified is `--settings` alongside the project's `.claude/settings.json`; nothing covers `--settings` alongside `.claude/settings.local.json`. SKILL.md even describes the fallback as "the file claude reads with no flag at all", which is true for the `claude-yolo` wrapper case but not for this one, where a flag IS present. If `--settings` shadows rather than merges with the local-settings layer, this path arms a busy record that no hook can ever clear and the watcher sees the task as permanently busy - the exact invariant the surrounding comments say must never be broken. The wrapper case (line 966) is unaffected since it carries no flag. Either verify the pairing and record it beside the other three, or keep this one branch on CLAUDE_HOOK_MODE=none until it is verified. 🔧 Fix: verify claude settings.local merge alongside operator --settings ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` - full teardown suite including the 8 new collision cases (stale index allow, bad scan-limit override, leftover scaffolding allow; real edit / untracked file / crewmate .claude sibling / tracked scaffold path / no-remote content refuse) - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-busy-adapter-wiring.test.sh tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh` - the other directly-changed suites - Manual end-to-end repro `repro-teardown-collision.sh`: builds real bare origin + project clone + task worktree + state meta, lands work on the remote, lets a second worktree on the same branch advance the ref, then runs the real `fm-teardown.sh task-x1` - Scenario 01: same fleet driven by `git show ef2c3a2:bin/fm-teardown.sh` (base commit) - reproduces the false REFUSED, exit 1 - Scenario 02: same fleet driven by this branch's `bin/fm-teardown.sh` - teardown completes, task record removed, exit 0 - Scenarios 03/04/05: collision plus a genuine uncommitted edit, plus a crewmate's `.claude/commands/new-cmd.md` next to firstmate scaffolding, plus content on no remote - each still REFUSED, exit 1, task record and crewmate files preserved - Scenario 06: collision plus only firstmate's own leftover `.claude/settings.local.json` and `.fm-grok-turnend` - torn down, exit 0 - `Scenario 07: successful collision teardown re-run under macOS system bash 3.2.57` - `git -C <wt> status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` on both refused worktrees after teardown - unchanged, proving the index-copy proof stages nothing into the task's real index
🔧 **Document** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ℹ️ `docs/configuration.md:232` - Operator-visible consequence of the new claude hook delivery - a project that tracks .claude/settings.local.json leaves claude crewmates with no hooks and no armed busy contract, so they classify unknown - currently lives only in .agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md (agent-runtime) and docs/verification/supervision.md (maintainer-verification). docs/configuration.md "Harness support" is the operator-current surface and already documents comparable per-harness hook installs for grok, Kimi, and Pi. I did not add it there: the repo's knowledge-placement decision tree stops at tier 2 (a nameable situation - spawn), so a second copy would violate the one-owner rule. Flagging it as a judgment call in case the author wants a one-line pointer from configuration.md to the harness-adapters owner instead. 🔧 Fix: document claude hook delivery and stale-copy teardown exception ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
🔧 **Lint** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ linter found issues (exit code 1) 🔧 Fix: quote hyphenated CLAUDE_HOOK_MODE values to satisfy SC2100 ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: feat(secondmate): two-way command transfer between firstmate and captain
body:
## Intent

Build a capability that transfers a persistent secondmate ('lane') between firstmate command (today's only mode) and captain command, in both directions, and makes the whole fleet behave correctly in either state. The failure being prevented is a lane with two commanders or none: the captain talking to a lane that is still routing everything through firstmate, or firstmate steering and answering for a lane the captain is driving himself.

Deliberate decisions made while doing this work, so they are not mistakes:

1. AGENTS.md hard rule 4 ('crewmates never address the captain') was intentionally made CONDITIONAL on one recorded, deliberate transfer. It is not weakened and not optional: no other worker kind may address the captain, and a worker never decides its own command state. This wording change is the point of the task, not an accident.

2. Command state has exactly ONE owner: the optional trailing 'command:' field on the lane's data/secondmates.md registry line. state/ was explicitly rejected as the owner because it is the volatile tier and state/<id>.meta is rewritten by every fm-spawn relaunch, so a recovery respawn would silently pull a lane back under firstmate command with nobody deciding it. The seeded home's data/command.md is a DERIVED, main-authoritative copy so the lane knows its own state - it is not a second owner; the registry always wins and a divergence is reported, never resolved by a reader. This mirrors the existing data/captain-shared.md pattern.

3. The onramp deliberately has NO --force or override flag of any kind. Its seven refusals are stop-and-report by design; the acceptance criteria required that a caller cannot wave them through. 'onramp <id> --force' is intentionally a usage error.

4. Unsafe state #7 is deliberately broader than 'a validation run mid-gate': ANY non-terminal run-step-sourced state refuses, because ask-user decision authority binds for a whole run's length, so transferring mid-run would split one run's authority across two people.

5. bin/fm-classify-lib.sh's scan_captain_relevant_statuses was deliberately NOT made command-aware. It is shared by two consumers whose correct behaviour is opposite: the always-on watcher must absorb a captain-commanded lane (the captain is reading that pane), while the away-mode daemon must keep escalating it (the captain is away and reading only the digest). Each consumer applies the predicate itself. This asymmetry is intentional and commented at both sites.

6. The session-start liveness sweep deliberately STILL relaunches a confirmed-dead captain-commanded lane - relaunching is infrastructure, not command - but that relaunch is deliberately never silent even when verbose facts are off, because the captain's conversation in that pane did not survive the restart and he must be told.

7. FM_SECONDMATE_COMMAND_OPERATIONAL is a deliberate, narrow, single-lane escape hatch in fm-send.sh for messages that are infrastructure rather than work: the handback request, and the 're-read your own instructions/config' nudges after a sync. Without it a captain-commanded lane would silently run stale config after a config push. It names one exact lane; exempting one never exempts another. A damaged command record exempts nothing.

8. Firstmate deliberately stops routing work into a captain-commanded lane (fm-backlog-handoff refuses). In-scope work stays in the main backlog under a captain-kind hold naming the lane, reusing the mechanism AGENTS.md section 10 already names rather than inventing new machinery.

9. Partial-transfer safety is deliberate and asymmetric: the step that REMOVES an authority always runs before the step that GRANTS one, so onramp writes the registry first and offramp writes the home marker first. An interrupted transfer can leave a lane inert with no commander, which is reported, but never with two commanders.

10. The offramp is deliberately not the mirror image of the onramp. It forces the returning lane to write its own fresh position report at the exact path it was asked for, and refuses to complete without one. There is intentionally no bypass for a dead lane: the documented answer is relaunch and re-request.

11. Tests assert tracked instruction surfaces (AGENTS.md, the generated charter, the skill inventory) by CONTENT. That is deliberate and is the documented exception in this repo's own firstmate-coding-guidelines skill: those surfaces are themselves the artifact an agent consumes and have no executable interface behind them. Everything else is asserted through executable interfaces, including two cases that drive a real fm-watch.sh subprocess and assert the wake queue.

12. bin/fm-bearings-snapshot.sh and bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh were deliberately left out of scope. Neither is named in the acceptance criteria, both are large schema-pinned generators, and the need is met by the session-start digest plus 'fm-secondmate-command.sh status'.

13. Three test fixtures (fm-gotmp, fm-backend, fm-afk-return) build partial bin/ directories that copy only the siblings their subject sources. They gained the new fm-secondmate-command-lib.sh because fm-classify-lib.sh and fm-teardown.sh now source it - the same maintenance pattern those fixtures already document for earlier extractions.

14. A second commit fixes a defect found in the first: two handback requests inside the same second reused one file path, which could orphan a report the lane was already writing. Transfer record paths are now collision-safe, and a re-request reuses an open request's path until it is answered.

## What Changed

- Added `bin/fm-secondmate-command.sh` and `bin/fm-secondmate-command-lib.sh`, which move a persistent secondmate lane between firstmate command and captain command in both directions (onramp with seven no-override refusals; offramp as request → lane-written position report → complete). The optional trailing `command:` field on the lane's `data/secondmates.md` registry line is the single owner of that state, with the lane home's `data/command.md` as a derived, main-authoritative copy; a divergence is reported, never silently resolved.
- Taught the surrounding fleet machinery to honour command state: `fm-send.sh` refuses steers into a captain-commanded or unrecorded lane except through the narrow single-lane `FM_SECONDMATE_COMMAND_OPERATIONAL` exemption (handback request and post-sync re-read nudges), `fm-backlog-handoff.sh` refuses routing work into such a lane, `fm-teardown.sh` refuses to retire one, `fm-home-seed.sh` preserves command state across a reseed, the session-start digest and structured fleet view expose each lane's state and drop the send affordance, and the always-on watcher absorbs captain-relevant events for those lanes while the away-mode daemon still escalates them.
- Updated the instruction surfaces to match: AGENTS.md hard rule 4 is now conditional on one recorded transfer, a new `secondmate-command-transfer` skill owns the procedure, and the afk/bootstrap/provisioning skills, architecture and configuration docs, and generated charter brief were synced. Covered by a new `tests/fm-secondmate-command.test.sh` (30 cases, two driving a real `fm-watch.sh` subprocess against the wake queue) plus additions across the safety, sync, send-marker, pending-reply, bootstrap, fleet-view, and afk-return suites.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: Large change (~2.6k lines) that adds hard-refusal guards to steering, work routing, and lane retirement, but it is backed by substantial executable coverage, the earlier review rounds closed the material defects, and the three remaining items are latent robustness and duplication concerns rather than live failures.

## Testing

Ran the branch's relevant automated suites (20 test files covering fm-secondmate-command, secondmate safety/sync/liveness/lifecycle, send marker, pending replies, backlog handoff, teardown, bootstrap, session start, fleet snapshot/view, watch triage, daemon, brief, instruction owners, documentation audiences) and then demonstrated the feature end to end against a real tmux-backed lane: onramp refusals (away mode, open decision, no --force), the actual transfer with registry field, derived lane-side command.md, position record and the notice arriving in the lane's pane, firstmate refusing to send/interrupt/route work/retire while the captain holds the lane, divergence reported by both `status` and the startup check, and a handback that only completes on the exact fresh report the lane wrote, after which steering and work routing work again. Everything passed except one pre-existing, environment-dependent case in tests/fm-session-start.test.sh (Herdr husk relaunch needs jq on the test PATH), which I reproduced identically at the base commit.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end demonstration of two-way secondmate command transfer against a REAL
# tmux-backed lane. Produces a CLI transcript an operator would see.
set -u

ROOT=${FM_DEMO_ROOT:?}
EV=${FM_DEMO_EVIDENCE:?}
DEMO="$EV/demo-fleet"
rm -rf "$DEMO"
mkdir -p "$DEMO"

PRIMARY="$DEMO/primary"
LANE="$DEMO/lane-sm-alpha"
export TMUX_TMPDIR="$DEMO/tmuxtmp"
mkdir -p "$TMUX_TMPDIR"

mkdir -p "$PRIMARY"/{data,state,config,projects,bin} "$LANE"/{data,state,config,projects,bin}
printf '# Firstmate\n' > "$PRIMARY/AGENTS.md"
printf '# Firstmate\n' > "$LANE/AGENTS.md"
printf 'sm-alpha\n' > "$LANE/.fm-secondmate-home"
printf 'Second mate charter.\n' > "$LANE/data/charter.md"
printf 'manual\n' > "$PRIMARY/config/backlog-backend"

cat > "$PRIMARY/data/secondmates.md" <<EOF
# Secondmates

- sm-alpha - Owns the alpha domain. (home: $LANE; scope: alpha work; projects: alpha; added 2026-01-01)
EOF

cat > "$PRIMARY/data/backlog.md" <<'EOF'
# Backlog

## Queued

- [ ] alpha-tuning - tune the alpha ingest path
  ## Intent
  Reduce ingest latency.
EOF

# --- a real tmux lane whose foreground process reads as a live agent ---------
AGENT_STUB="$DEMO/agentbin/claude"
mkdir -p "$DEMO/agentbin"
cat > "$AGENT_STUB" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
sleep 3000
SH
chmod +x "$AGENT_STUB"
tmux kill-server 2>/dev/null
tmux new-session -d -s firstmate -n fm-sm-alpha "bash -c 'exec -a claude sleep 3000'"
sleep 1

cat > "$PRIMARY/state/sm-alpha.meta" <<EOF
window=firstmate:fm-sm-alpha
endpoint_task_id=sm-alpha
worktree=$LANE
project=$LANE
harness=claude
kind=secondmate
mode=secondmate
yolo=off
backend=tmux
home=$LANE
projects=alpha
EOF

# Run from the demo fleet, the way a real firstmate session runs from its own
# home rather than from inside this repo's gate worktree.
cd "$DEMO" || exit 1

export FM_HOME="$PRIMARY"
export FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$ROOT"
export FM_SEND_SETTLE=0
CMD="$ROOT/bin/fm-secondmate-command.sh"

step() { printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$1"; }
run() { printf '\n$ %s\n' "$*"; "$@" 2>&1; printf '[exit %s]\n' "$?"; }
pane() {
  printf '\n--- lane pane (tmux capture-pane firstmate:fm-sm-alpha) ---\n'
  tmux capture-pane -p -t firstmate:fm-sm-alpha | sed '/^$/d' | tail -6
  printf -- '--- end pane ---\n'
}

printf 'SECONDMATE COMMAND TRANSFER - END-TO-END DEMO\n'
printf 'primary home: %s\nlane home:    %s\nlane pane:    real tmux window firstmate:fm-sm-alpha\n' "$PRIMARY" "$LANE"

step "1. Starting point: firstmate commands the lane"
run cat "$PRIMARY/data/secondmates.md"
run "$CMD" status

step "2. There is no override flag - 'onramp --force' is a usage error"
"$CMD" onramp sm-alpha --force >/dev/null 2>"$DEMO/force.err"; rc=$?
printf '\n$ fm-secondmate-command.sh onramp sm-alpha --force\n[exit %s]\n%s\n' "$rc" "$(head -4 "$DEMO/force.err")"

step "3a. Unsafe state: the captain is away, so there is no one to hand the lane to"
: > "$PRIMARY/state/.afk"
run "$CMD" onramp sm-alpha
rm -f "$PRIMARY/state/.afk"

step "3b. Unsafe state: the lane still has a question open with firstmate"
printf 'needs-decision [key=alpha-schema]: which index shape do we ship?\n' >> "$PRIMARY/state/sm-alpha.status"
run "$CMD" onramp sm-alpha
run grep -c 'command: captain' "$PRIMARY/data/secondmates.md"
printf 'resolved [key=alpha-schema]: ship the compound index\n' >> "$PRIMARY/state/sm-alpha.status"

step "4. Hand the lane to the captain"
run "$CMD" onramp sm-alpha
printf '\n(the same command run twice is an idempotent no-op, not a second transfer)\n'
run "$CMD" onramp sm-alpha
run grep -n 'sm-alpha' "$PRIMARY/data/secondmates.md"
run "$CMD" status
printf '\n--- the lane reads its own state at %s ---\n' "$LANE/data/command.md"
cat "$LANE/data/command.md"
pane

step "5. The position record the captain inherits"
POS=$(ls "$PRIMARY/data/sm-alpha"/command-position-*.md | tail -1)
printf '\n%s\n' "$POS"
sed -n '1,20p' "$POS"

step "6. Firstmate stops acting on a lane it does not command"
run "$ROOT/bin/fm-send.sh" sm-alpha "start on the alpha ingest work"
pane
run "$ROOT/bin/fm-send.sh" sm-alpha --key C-c
run "$ROOT/bin/fm-backlog-handoff.sh" sm-alpha alpha-tuning
run "$ROOT/bin/fm-teardown.sh" sm-alpha

step "7. A lane whose two records disagree is reported, never guessed"
sed -i 's/^command: captain/command: firstmate/' "$LANE/data/command.md"
run "$CMD" status sm-alpha
run env FM_HOME="$PRIMARY" FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$ROOT" "$ROOT/bin/fm-bootstrap.sh"
sed -i 's/^command: firstmate/command: captain/' "$LANE/data/command.md"

step "8. Handing back needs the lane's own fresh position report"
run "$CMD" offramp-complete sm-alpha --report "$LANE/data/made-up.md"
run "$CMD" offramp-request sm-alpha
pane
REPORT=$(sed -n 's/^report=//p' "$PRIMARY/state/sm-alpha.command-handback" | tail -1)
run "$CMD" offramp-complete sm-alpha --report "$LANE/data/some-other-file.md"
printf '\n(the lane writes the report it was asked for)\n'
cat > "$REPORT" <<'EOF'
# Position report - sm-alpha

Under captain command I shipped the compound index and left the ingest
benchmark half-written. Nothing is unresolved. The main firstmate should
pick the benchmark back up.
EOF
run "$CMD" offramp-complete sm-alpha --report "$REPORT"
run grep -n 'sm-alpha' "$PRIMARY/data/secondmates.md"
run "$CMD" status
printf '\n--- the lane reads its own state at %s ---\n' "$LANE/data/command.md"
sed -n '1,6p' "$LANE/data/command.md"
pane

step "9. Firstmate commands the lane again"
run "$ROOT/bin/fm-send.sh" sm-alpha "start on the alpha ingest work"
pane
run "$ROOT/bin/fm-backlog-handoff.sh" sm-alpha alpha-tuning

tmux kill-server 2>/dev/null
printf '\n=== demo complete ===\n'

<summary>⚠️ **Review** - 3 infos</summary>

- 🚨 `bin/fm-home-seed.sh:1051` - Re-seeding an existing lane silently returns it to firstmate command. `seed_home` unconditionally overwrites `$home/data/command.md` with `command: firstmate` (line 1051), and `write_registry` (line 837) rebuilds the registry line from scratch, dropping any `; command: captain` field — it explicitly preserves `label:` across a reseed but has no equivalent handling for `command:`. Re-seeding a populated home is a documented, supported operation (secondmate-provisioning SKILL.md line 49, and the reseed-preserves-label comment at line 819), and `validate_home_assignment` allows reseeding the same id to the same home. Because the authority and its derived copy revert together, `secondmate_command_check` in fm-bootstrap.sh sees no divergence and stays silent, so the transfer disappears with no signal. This is the same 'a respawn silently pulls a lane back with nobody deciding it' failure the design rejected `state/` to avoid. Fix: preserve a prior `command:` field in `write_registry` the way `label:` is preserved, and leave an existing `data/command.md` alone (or refuse the reseed outright while the lane is captain-commanded, as fm-teardown.sh does).
- 🚨 `bin/fm-secondmate-command.sh:416` - Neither transfer direction notifies the running lane. `cmd_onramp` writes the registry and `data/command.md` and returns; `cmd_offramp_complete` (line 489) does the same. The charter generated by bin/fm-brief.sh:198 only tells the lane to read `data/command.md` 'at every session start', so a long-running agent keeps operating under the previous contract until it restarts. Right after an onramp the captain types into a pane whose lane still believes `command: firstmate` — per the charter it must not address him and must route its outcome to the main firstmate. Right after `offramp-complete` the reverse holds: the lane still believes `command: captain` and will address the captain on firstmate's next steer, violating hard rule 4. Both are the two-commanders state the feature exists to remove. The skill claims otherwise at .agents/skills/secondmate-command-transfer/SKILL.md:49 ('flips the registry, and tells the lane'), and test_onramp_transfers_registry_marker_and_position_record asserts only that the file exists. The infrastructure exemption FM_SECONDMATE_COMMAND_OPERATIONAL already exists for exactly this class of message; decide whether to send a re-read nudge on both transfer completions or to document a required lane restart.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-secondmate-command.sh:458` - The handback request goes through fm-send.sh with the lane's meta kind=secondmate, so MARK_FROM_FIRSTMATE=1 and a durable pending-reply expectation is created for it. If the lane does not answer within the grace window, the watcher's `fm_pending_reply_tick` calls `fm_pending_reply_send_recovery`, which re-invokes fm-send.sh (bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:684) WITHOUT FM_SECONDMATE_COMMAND_OPERATIONAL — the new guard at bin/fm-send.sh:238 refuses it, the record goes to recovery_failed, and firstmate gets a delivery-failure escalation for a lane it is forbidden to steer. The built-in retry for the one message the offramp depends on can therefore never succeed. Second consequence: `offramp-complete` deletes the handback record but leaves the pending-reply expectation, so an expectation the lane never resolved keeps `open_pending_replies_for` non-empty and permanently refuses the next `onramp` at guard 6 — a refusal with no override flag, caused by the transfer machinery's own artifact. If data/secondmates.md is missing, truncated, or resolved from the wrong root, firstmate silently steers a lane the captain holds. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:565` - The structured fleet view firstmate reads to decide what to act on carries no command field, and still emits `actions.send: "bin/fm-send.sh fm-<id> '<request>'"` for every secondmate including captain-commanded ones; bin/fm-bearings-snapshot.sh aggregates secondmate records the same way. A `command` field on the secondmate record, and dropping the `send` affordance when it is `captain`, would close it.

- ℹ️ `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:512` - `fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` calls `fm_secondmate_command_state` but never sources `bin/fm-secondmate-command-lib.sh`; it only gets the function transitively because `fm-classify-lib.sh` (sourced at line 140) now sources it. Add the explicit `. "$SCRIPT_DIR/fm-secondmate-command-lib.sh"` next to the other sources at lines 137-143.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-secondmate-command.sh:208` - The body of the lane-facing `data/command.md` contract is written verbatim in two places: `write_home_marker` here (lines 208-212) and `seed_home` in bin/fm-home-seed.sh (lines 1086-1090). Those five lines are the instructions a lane actually reads to decide whether it may address the captain, so a change applied to one writer and not the other means a lane's contract depends on whether its marker was last written by a seed or by a transfer. The unrecognized-value refusal message is likewise duplicated between `write_registry` (fm-home-seed.sh:854) and `seed_home` (fm-home-seed.sh:1075). Extract a single marker-body writer into bin/fm-secondmate-command-lib.sh (which both scripts already source) and have both paths call it, keeping only the differing `recorded:`/`position:` fields at the call site.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:1448` - Teardown removes `state/<ID>.status`, `.turn-ended`, `.meta` and the harness token files, but not the new `state/<ID>.command-handback` record written by `cmd_offramp_request`. Failure scenario: a lane with an outstanding handback request has its registry `command:` field hand-repaired to `firstmate`, is torn down, and its id is later reused for a new lane; the stale handback record survives, and the next `offramp-request` reuses a report path pointing into the removed home, so the lane can never write the report the offramp requires and the handback wedges with a misleading path.
