title: feat(bin): seed the first commit of a brand-new empty GitHub repo
body:
## Intent Add a narrow, scripted sixth exception to firstmate's hard rule #1 ('never write to a project'), covering exactly one case: seeding the very first commit of a genuinely brand-new, zero-commit GitHub repo, so its default branch exists and a crewmate can get a worktree at all. Git cannot create a worktree for a branch with zero commits - that is a git limitation, not a firstmate policy - so a just-created empty repo (gh-axi repo create does not auto-initialize with a README) was previously a dead end: no crewmate could touch it and firstmate was not allowed to either. This happened for real with a project called promo-reel-forge. Built bin/fm-seed-empty-repo.sh (takes a project dir or registry name), following the existing patterns in bin/fm-project-mode.sh and bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh for resolving a project's dir/registry entry and origin remote. Deliberate design decisions: - The safety net is a LIVE GitHub API check via gh-axi, never a trusted flag or argument: it checks repos/OWNER/REPO size==0, that the branches list is empty, AND that the commits API call fails with the expected "Git Repository is empty" signature (verified as a substring match) rather than succeeding or failing for some unrelated/inconclusive reason (auth, rate limit, network) - an inconclusive failure refuses loudly rather than being treated as confirmation of emptiness, since silently proceeding on an ambiguous signal would defeat the point of the safety net. - Only after that full verification does it run exactly one empty-allowed commit ("Initial commit") and a plain push to the default branch - no file content, no other commits, never a force-push. - Extra defense-in-depth refusals: dirty working tree, local branch already has a commit (already seeded), local branch name disagreeing with the remote's declared default branch, no origin remote, origin remote not on github.com, gh-axi unavailable. - Owner/repo slug parsing reuses the same sed pattern already used in bin/fm-bearings-snapshot.sh's repo_slug helper. - Refusal messages use REFUSED: for the safety-net verification failures (mirroring bin/fm-merge-local.sh's guarded-refusal style) and error: for ordinary usage/precondition failures. Added a colocated test suite at tests/fm-seed-empty-repo.test.sh (11 cases) following the repo's tests/lib.sh conventions: a fake gh-axi in a per-case fakebin controls the three API responses via env vars, and real local git objects are used throughout, including for the one happy-path test where the origin remote is a real local bare repo whose path deliberately contains a github.com/owner/repo segment so the script's github.com URL-parsing regex sees a valid slug while the actual git push stays fully local (no network). Both the script and the test file are shellcheck-clean under the repo's pinned shellcheck 0.11.0 via bin/fm-lint.sh, and bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh passes. Updated AGENTS.md per the coding-guidelines skill's decision tree (detailed procedure belongs in the owning skill, not inline in AGENTS.md): - Section 1: added the sixth exception to the existing prose list of sanctioned project-write exceptions in hard rule #1, pointing to section 6 for the procedure. - Section 6: added one sentence noting that project-management's initialization procedure also covers this narrow empty-repo case via the new script, deferring detail to that skill. - .agents/skills/project-management/SKILL.md: added the actual procedural paragraph directly after the existing "## Initialize" section (the closest existing match to the task's described "Initialize (no-mistakes mode only)" block), spelling out that this path is strictly for a zero-commit repo and never applies again once the project has any real history - every subsequent change goes through a crewmate as normal. This is firstmate's own tracked repository, so I (a firstmate crewmate) was authorized to edit AGENTS.md, bin/, and .agents/skills/ directly per the task brief; ran bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh afterward per the brief's project-memory instructions and confirmed it was a no-op (AGENTS.md's "Maintaining this file" section was already present). Note on this run: two earlier runs against this same branch content failed for reasons unrelated to the code under review - one hit a 403 push failure because origin was read-only and a writable fork remote had not yet been registered (now fixed via `no-mistakes init --fork-url`), and after that a stray empty commit I had accidentally created via a malformed shell command was surgically removed from branch history via `git rebase --onto` (verified byte-identical tree content before/after, both fix commits preserved), and the most recent attempt's review step failed only because the reviewing agent's own OAuth session had expired mid-run, not because of any issue with the change itself. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-seed-empty-repo.sh`, a guarded script that resolves a project's directory/registry entry and origin remote, performs a live GitHub API check (repo size 0, empty branches list, and a commits-API call that fails with the expected "Git Repository is empty" signature) as the safety net, then pushes exactly one empty "Initial commit" to the default branch so a crewmate can obtain a worktree against a repo git otherwise cannot branch. - Added defense-in-depth refusals for a dirty working tree, an already-seeded local branch, local/remote default-branch name mismatch, missing or non-GitHub origin, and unavailable `gh-axi`, distinguishing safety-net verification failures (`REFUSED:`) from ordinary precondition failures (`error:`). - Added a colocated 11-case test suite (`tests/fm-seed-empty-repo.test.sh`) using a fake `gh-axi` to control the three API responses and real local git objects throughout, and isolated `FM_STATE_OVERRIDE` handling in those tests to prevent cross-test state leakage. - Documented the new sixth exception to hard rule 1 in `AGENTS.md`, the initialization procedure in `.agents/skills/project-management/SKILL.md`, and added the script to the `bin/` toolbelt reference table in `docs/scripts.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A narrow, well-isolated addition (new script + colocated tests + doc pointers) with no changes to existing behavior; the safety net (triple live-verified GitHub API check before any commit/push, no force-push, fails closed on any ambiguous signal) is sound, its output parsing matches gh-axi's actual API response format (verified live against a real GitHub repo), and all 11 tests exercise the refusal paths that matter. ## Testing Ran the full colocated test suite (11/11 passing) and performed manual end-to-end verification with real local git objects (no network) that reproduces the exact promo-reel-forge scenario: seeding a genuinely empty repo succeeds and unblocks `git worktree add` that previously failed with git's own limitation, while an inconclusive GitHub API failure is refused loudly with zero commits created, confirming the safety-net design decision works as intended.
Evidence: End-to-end CLI transcript: seed happy path, worktree-add before/after payoff, and inconclusive-failure refusal ```text === fm-seed-empty-repo.sh end-to-end demo === 1) Simulated a genuinely empty GitHub repo (zero commits, local and remote). 2) Ran the script exactly as an operator would: $ bash bin/fm-seed-empty-repo.sh $PROJ To file://.../remotes/github.com/example/promo-reel-forge * [new branch] main -> main seeded: pushed the first commit to example/promo-reel-forge (main); $PROJ is ready for cloning and dispatch 3) Verified the actual crewmate payoff: git worktree add for a task branch. BEFORE (unseeded repo, git's own limitation): $ git worktree add -b task/demo wt main fatal: not a valid object name: 'main' exit code: 255 AFTER (seeded via fm-seed-empty-repo.sh): $ git worktree add -b task/demo wt main Preparing worktree (new branch 'task/demo') HEAD is now at f04cf07 Initial commit exit code: 0 4) Verified the safety-net design decision: an inconclusive commits-API failure (e.g. rate limit) is refused loudly, never treated as confirmation of emptiness, and no commit is created. $ bash bin/fm-seed-empty-repo.sh $PROJ # commits API fails with 403 rate-limit, not the "empty" signature REFUSED: could not confirm example/some-repo has zero commits; the commits API call failed for an unexpected reason: error: "gh: API rate limit exceeded (HTTP 403)" exit code: 1 $ git -C $PROJ log --oneline fatal: your current branch 'main' does not have any commits yet # no commit was created ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Rebase** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `AGENTS.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main 🔧 Fix applied. ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Review** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-seed-empty-repo.test.sh` — all 11 cases pass (happy path, non-zero size, non-empty branches, commits-API success, inconclusive commits-API failure, no origin, non-GitHub origin, dirty tree, already-seeded, branch mismatch, gh-axi missing) - Manual E2E: built a real local bare 'GitHub' remote at a github.com/owner/repo-shaped path with zero commits, ran `bin/fm-seed-empty-repo.sh` against a real clone of it with a gh-axi stub answering size=0/branches=[]/commits=409-empty, confirmed the script pushed exactly one 'Initial commit' to both local and remote - Manual E2E payoff check: confirmed `git worktree add -b task/demo wt main` fails with `fatal: not a valid object name: 'main'` against the unseeded repo, and succeeds after seeding — demonstrating the actual crewmate-dispatch blocker the change fixes - Manual E2E safety-net check: ran the script against a live-shaped inconclusive commits-API failure (403 rate limit, not the 'Git Repository is empty' signature) and confirmed it printed `REFUSED: could not confirm ... failed for an unexpected reason` and created no commit - `Reviewed AGENTS.md, .agents/skills/project-management/SKILL.md, and docs/scripts.md diffs against the described intent (sixth hard-rule-1 exception, section 6 pointer, toolbelt table entry)`
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: feat(bin): propagate trace context to remote secondmates
body:
## Intent

Extend firstmate's per-task W3C trace-context propagation to the REMOTE second mate spawn path, and fix the two-owner inheritable-config allowlist drift and stale docs surfaced by the PR #995 review (finding 6). This is firstmate-side follow-up to #995 (merged to main), which added per-task trace context but only for the local spawn path. Delivery contract: mode=no-mistakes.

BACKGROUND. The trace feature resolves and injects a per-task carrier at the local spawn path in bin/fm-spawn.sh. A REMOTE second mate is instead routed through spawn_remote_secondmate, which exits roughly 1400 lines BEFORE that resolve/export site and writes its own metadata block with no traceparent= and no FM_TRACE_CONTEXT snapshot. So a remote second mate was silently UNTRACED even when the capability was enabled.

REQUIRED WORK, as accepted.
(1) Give the remote second mate a consistent per-task trace: resolve the per-task carrier the same way the local path does (fm_trace_context_resolve against the task's own meta, honoring the frozen FM_TRACE_CONTEXT enablement decision), record traceparent= in the remote meta block, and deliver both the carrier and the FM_TRACE_CONTEXT snapshot to the remote agent, matching the local path's per-task-boundary semantics: never inherit an ambient/parent carrier, and reuse a recorded carrier on relaunch/recovery. Keep it default-off and identical in spirit to the local behavior #995 established.
(2) Reconcile the split inheritable-config allowlist to one owner, so future inheritable-config additions cannot silently drift between the two sides.
(3) Fix the now-inaccurate docs: docs/trace-context.md and the docs/configuration.md 'Trace context propagation' section overstated coverage by implying all secondmate spawns were covered.
(4) Add behavioral tests proving a remote-routed second mate now gets a per-task carrier recorded and delivered, and that per-task boundary and relaunch stability hold on the remote path too, following the existing fake-boundary style of tests/fm-trace-context-spawn.test.sh and the remote fake-ssh harness of tests/fm-remote-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh. Prefer exercising the real spawn code over source-text matching.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE, as instructed: do not change the local-path trace behavior #995 established, and do not add real remote/SSH infrastructure - use the existing fake-ssh test harness only.

DELIBERATE DECISIONS AND TRADEOFFS MADE WHILE DOING THE WORK, which a reviewer reading only the diff would not know:
- The allowlist drift was WIDER than the review reported. The review named only bin/fm-remote-inherit.sh (the remote receiver). The sender, bin/fm-remote-inherit-push.sh, carried its own separate hardcoded copy that had drifted the same way. Both remote ends now derive from the single canonical FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG declaration in bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh through a new fm_config_inherit_items helper. This widening is intended, not scope creep: fixing only the receiver would have left the identical class of bug in place on the sender.
- A new bin/fm-spawn.sh --traceparent option is a deliberate new CLI surface, not an accident. It is accepted ONLY for --secondmate spawns and ONLY as a strictly validated W3C traceparent. It exists because a remote second mate's task identity is owned by the PARENT home that holds the task metadata an observer reads, while the pane export necessarily happens on the remote host. Local spawns never pass it and resolve their own carrier exactly as before, which is how the out-of-scope constraint on local behavior is honored.
- The strict validation on that flag is a security boundary, deliberately fail-closed with a loud refusal rather than a silent omission: it is the only caller-supplied value that can reach an 'export TRACEPARENT=' in a pane, so a malformed or shell-metacharacter value must be refused rather than passed through. This is intentionally different from #995's rule that entropy/resolution FAILURES omit telemetry without aborting a spawn; an explicitly supplied invalid carrier means a broken or hostile caller, not an entropy failure.
- print_route in bin/fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh now echoes the carrier the remote endpoint ACTUALLY holds, and the parent records that read-back value rather than what it intended to deliver. This is deliberate: when the remote host already had a live agent and reused its endpoint instead of relaunching, recording the intended value would have claimed an identity the running agent never received. Recording the read-back keeps #995's guarantee that the recorded carrier is the identity the child actually got.
- config/trace-context is session-scoped enablement rather than durable configuration, so a new FM_SESSION_SCOPED_INHERITABLE_CONFIG declaration plus predicate now governs it in ONE place, consumed by both the local propagate_inheritable_config and the new remote push skip. This replaced an inline literal comparison in the local library. It required marking the two live-convergence remote call sites (bin/fm-bootstrap.sh and bin/fm-config-push.sh) with FM_CONFIG_INHERIT_LIVE=1, symmetric with how those same files already mark their local convergence calls.
- A consequence was weighed and deliberately accepted: adding an item to the shared allowlist means a local code root NEWER than its remote code root will now refuse the inheritance transfer rather than silently skipping it. That is correct fail-closed behavior and matches the existing convergence model where /updatefirstmate updates remote code roots, and there is deliberately no separate allowlist version negotiation. It is documented in the fm-config-inherit-lib.sh header.
- The new grouped-redirect change in bin/fm-trace-context-lib.sh fixes a PRE-EXISTING stderr leak, verified byte-identical on main: an absent session lock printed a raw shell redirect failure because a trailing 2>/dev/null on a bare read does not suppress the input-redirect open failure. It was previously invisible only because every existing test seeds a lock file; the new remote resolve site made it visible. The function's documented contract was already to fail silently, so this restores intended behavior rather than changing it.
- The new test was verified to genuinely catch the bug rather than pass vacuously: stashing the bin/ changes and re-running reproduces the untraced remote second mate ('an enabled remote spawn must record a valid carrier in the parent metadata (got \"\")'), and it passes with the fix.
- The new test is registered in the secondmate family in bin/fm-test-run.sh, matching its sibling remote lifecycle suite.

## What Changed

- Propagate per-task W3C trace context through remote Secondmate spawns, including strict carrier validation, frozen enablement delivery, endpoint read-back, and stable relaunch identity.
- Centralize local and remote inheritable-config allowlists, preserving session-scoped trace configuration during live convergence and silencing missing session-lock reads.
- Update trace-context documentation and add fake-SSH behavioral coverage for delivery, task isolation, relaunch stability, allowlist enforcement, and invalid carriers.

title: feat(notes): add disabled-by-default Apple Notes local channel
body:
## Intent Implement a disabled-by-default Apple Notes ↔ Firstmate local-runtime capability based on the accepted architecture and security reports. It must use one dedicated fixed-operation macOS bridge with stable bundle identity, hardened runtime and App Sandbox, refuse release rather than add the currently required target-wide temporary Notes Apple Events exception, and remain inert unless a later captain-present staged activation occurs. Keep one exact unshared iCloud account/folder-ID binding; strict bounded plaintext envelopes; low Notes-origin authority; immutable capture-before-offer state; concurrent-safe claims, dedupe, rate limits, reconcile-before-create outbound receipts, body-free authenticated bounded checks, local emergency disable, durable private audit, and pointer-safe rollback. Provide fixture-only offline tests, docs and agent handling instructions, supervision integration, and a generated-runtime patch compatible with existing Calm and separately prepared primary persistence. Do not access live Notes, send Apple Events, request or mutate TCC/iCloud permissions, create Notes folders/notes, activate a local runtime, install recurring checks, or add login behavior. Current GO/NO-GO must be NO-GO for even the one later harmless captain-present outbound test until an operation-level sandbox route and suitable Apple signing identity are available. The unrelated Pi Calm E2E failure must not be suppressed or altered; clean origin/main and this Notes branch reproduce the same /export assertion, while the combined Calm+persistence+Notes runtime candidate passes because it includes the pre-existing Calm repair patch. ## What Changed - Add the guarded Apple Notes channel core (`bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py`, `fm-notes-channel.sh`, `fm-notes-poll.sh`): strict bounded plaintext envelope parsing, one exact iCloud account/folder-ID binding, capture-before-offer state, concurrent-safe claims/dedupe/rate limits, reconcile-before-create outbound receipts, durable audit chain, and local emergency disable, with `pair-production`/`record-pairing` now gated behind the disabled-state check before they can run. - Add the dedicated `FirstmateNotesBridge` Swift executable (`libexec/FirstmateNotesBridge`) plus `bin/fm-notes-bridge-build.sh` to compile, sign, and release it as a hardened-runtime, App-Sandboxed binary that refuses release rather than add a target-wide temporary Notes Apple Events exception. - Wire supervision and guard integration (`bin/fm-supervision-lib.sh`, `bin/fm-guard.sh`, `bin/fm-test-run.sh`) for the new check trigger, and add docs (`docs/apple-notes-channel.md`, `docs/verification/apple-notes-channel.md`, `.agents/skills/apple-notes-channel/SKILL.md`) and fixture-only offline tests (`tests/fm-notes-channel.test.sh`, `tests/fm-notes-bridge-build.test.sh`, updated `tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh`). ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The new commit precisely fixes both prior error-level findings (pair-production and record-pairing now call channel.disabled() before constructing the real ProductionProvider, and record-pairing now also refuses to overwrite an existing binding), following the same pattern already used by `enable`; the remaining outstanding items are warning/info severity and were explicitly accepted by the user as follow-ups, not blockers. ## Testing The three targeted offline suites (Apple Notes channel behavior, bridge build/release gating, and turnend-guard supervision integration) all pass, and their assertions collectively demonstrate the required disabled-by-default, sandboxed, NO-GO-until-signed, audit/dedupe/rollback-safe behavior end-to-end via the fixture provider and a compiled hardened fixture app; no code changes were needed and the working tree is clean. ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 12 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:2843` - `pair-production` (bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:2843-2864) constructs a real `ProductionProvider` and calls `provider.pair_fixed_tree()` — a live subprocess invocation of the actual macOS bridge executable capable of triggering a real Automation/TCC prompt — without ever calling `channel.disabled()`. Its guard only checks `config["provider"] != "production" or config["enabled"] or config.get("binding") is not None`. That is exactly the state left by `init-production` (enabled=False, binding=None), and also the state left after `disable --emergency` before any pairing occurred. Concrete failure scenario: `init-production` is run, then something sets `state/apple-notes-channel/DISABLED` (an unrelated disable=True error, or a deliberate emergency disable) while the config is still provider=production/enabled=False/binding=None; running `pair-production --request-automation` afterward still passes the guard and invokes the real bridge. This contradicts the documented, required invariant in docs/apple-notes-channel.md:45 ("Production entrypoints check state/apple-notes-channel/DISABLED and the config's enabled flag before constructing a provider") and the user intent's requirement that the capability "remain inert unless a later captain-present staged activation occurs" with an effective "local emergency disable". `enable` (line 2888-2898) demonstrates the correct pattern (`if channel.disabled(): raise ChannelError("disabled", ...)`) that pair-production/record-pairing omit. - 🚨 `bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:2865` - `record-pairing` (bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:2865-2887) never checks `channel.disabled()` (same gap as pair-production) and never checks `config.get("binding") is None` before overwriting `config["binding"]`. This means an already-paired channel's exact iCloud account/folder binding can be silently replaced with a different tree by re-running `record-pairing --binding-hash <hash>` with new stdin JSON, with no requirement that the channel first be unpaired, and even while the DISABLED marker is set. This contradicts the user intent's required "one exact unshared iCloud account/folder-ID binding" invariant and docs/apple-notes-channel.md:168 ("Do not clear DISABLED, rebind, restore, or begin a new audit epoch without captain-present reconciliation"). - 🚨 `libexec/FirstmateNotesBridge/Sources/main.swift:448` - The Swift bridge's `read_inbox_note` ("bounded listed-note read") only enforces the size cap on `plaintext` (main.swift:448) before returning; the `html` field (fetched via the `body` Notes property, main.swift:455) has no size check at all in Swift, and the Python caller (fm-notes-channel-impl.py, scan() around line 2138-2144) passes `note["html"]` straight into `parse_envelope`/`StrictNotesHTML.feed()` with no `limits["html_bytes"]`-style cap anywhere in DEFAULT_LIMITS either. A note with small plaintext but a very large HTML body (e.g. rich formatting/tables) bypasses the documented byte cap entirely on both sides, causing unbounded Apple-Event transfer size and unbounded HTML parsing work/memory in the scan loop, contradicting the required "strict bounded plaintext envelopes" guarantee. - 🚨 `bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:75` - `ANY_SCHEME_RE = re.compile(r"\b([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]*):(?://)?")` (bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:75), used at line 698-702 to reject non-HTTPS URL schemes in the message body, matches any ordinary word followed by a colon, not just URL schemes. A perfectly ordinary message body such as "Status: waiting for review" or "Plan: refactor auth" is rejected with `unsafe-url-scheme` because `scheme_match.group(1)` is "Status"/"Plan", not "https". Verified directly: `ANY_SCHEME_RE.finditer("Status: what is the state of X?")` yields a match on "Status". No test fixture body contains an ordinary colon (all are colon-free except the one deliberately malicious `file:///etc/passwd` case), so this false-positive rejection of common natural-language phrasing is untested and would make the channel reject a large fraction of legitimate low-authority captain messages. - ⚠️ `libexec/FirstmateNotesBridge/Sources/main.swift:505` - In the Swift bridge's `createOwned`, `summary`/`outcome`/`action` all go through `boundedString` (blocks control chars/bidi-overrides/noncharacters), but `evidence` items (main.swift:505-506) only check non-empty and length ≤ 1024 bytes. Each evidence string is rendered as its own `<li>` line (line 524) which Notes converts to a plaintext line, and `receiptValue` (lines 551-558) later reconstructs `message_id`/`content_sha256` by scanning the note's plaintext for a unique `"key: value"`-prefixed line. An evidence string like `"message_id: <forged>"` becomes indistinguishable from the real receipt line once rendered, causing `findOwned` to see two matching lines and return `nil`/ambiguous results, breaking the reconcile-before-create idempotency guarantee. Currently unreachable because every caller of `create-owned-note` (stage_acknowledgment, prepare_test_intent in fm-notes-channel-impl.py) supplies only fixed, hardcoded evidence strings, and the Python-side `validate_outbound_intent` already runs `validate_text_controls` on each evidence item (though it does not block colon-prefixed key-like content). Worth hardening before `evidence` is ever populated from anything other than today's fixed literals. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:2316` - `_rate_count` (bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:2316-2329), used to gate the claim and outbound-publish rate limits, only suppresses `json.JSONDecodeError`/`ValueError` per audit line; a syntactically valid JSON line missing the `"at"` key raises an uncaught `KeyError` from `event["at"]`. That `KeyError` is not caught by the inner `contextlib.suppress`, so it propagates out of `claim()`/`publish()` into `main()`'s generic handler (`except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError)`, line 2997-3006), which returns an error WITHOUT calling `safe_disable()` — unlike every other audit-corruption path (`verify_audit`, `_audit_locked`), which explicitly raises `ChannelError(..., disable=True)`. This means one specific shape of audit-log corruption can silently undercount rate-limit history (if it hits the suppressed exceptions) or permanently break claim/publish (if it hits the uncaught KeyError) without ever setting the DISABLED marker, inconsistent with the audit-chain's otherwise strict fail-closed design. - ⚠️ `libexec/FirstmateNotesBridge/Sources/main.swift:405` - The Swift bridge's `list-inbox-metadata` (main.swift:405-412) fetches the full `plaintext` property (a real Apple Event body read) for every eligible (non-shared/non-locked/no-attachment) note, solely to compute a byte count that is then discarded, up to `maximumObjects` (200) notes per call. This contradicts the documented separation between "bounded Inbox metadata listing" (implied body-free) and the distinct "bounded listed-note read" operation, and means a metadata-only scan already performs up to 200 full-body Apple Events reads per cycle with no per-note or aggregate size limit before the length is measured. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:2244` - `reconcile_local()` (bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:2244-2258), invoked by `poll` immediately before `scan()`, reads and writes `offers/*.json` without holding `scan_lock`, unlike `scan()` and `publish()` which both wrap their work in `with self.scan_lock():`. A concurrent `scan()`/`claim()` in another process could race on the same offer files. Practical impact is limited since `claim()` is idempotent and the worst outcome is a duplicate/stale "ready" notification, but it's an inconsistency in the otherwise careful locking discipline. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:2575` - `doctor()` (bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:2575-2592) unconditionally constructs `ProductionProvider(self, config)` (line 2588) whenever `config["provider"] == "production"`, without checking `self.disabled()` or `config["enabled"]` first, even though it separately reports `disabled_marker` in its own output. `ProductionProvider.__init__`/`_verify_identity()` does not call Notes or request TCC (only local file/codesign checks via two `/usr/bin/codesign` subprocess calls), so the practical blast radius is small, but it still contradicts the documented "production entrypoints check DISABLED before constructing a provider" invariant that `enable` correctly follows. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:2047` - `_next_receive_seq()` (bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:2047-2053) globs and reads every capture file in `data/apple-notes-channel/captures/` each time a new capture is created within a scan (up to `capture_per_scan`=20 times per scan), and the scan-tail checkpoint block (lines 2198-2220) re-globs and re-reads all captures again. No local capture pruning/archival exists in this diff, so this is an O(new × total-lifetime-captures) cost per scan against a fixed 8-second `scan_deadline_seconds`. `scan-deadline` errors are non-disabling, so as captures accumulate over the channel's lifetime this could eventually cause scans to chronically fail the deadline without ever disabling the channel, silently halting ingestion. Worth persisting `last_receive_seq` in the checkpoint (already written) rather than rescanning, before this becomes a real problem at scale. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-notes-channel.test.sh:52` - The embedded fixture tool in tests/fm-notes-channel.test.sh defines `drift` and `fault` subcommands able to inject `binding-drift`/`identity-drift`/`tcc-denied`/`tcc-not-determined` faults (fixture tool lines 51-52, 68-71), but no test in the suite actually exercises them; only `create-after-commit-once` is used. The required "a missing/renamed/moved/duplicated/shared/reparented object disables the channel rather than searching or repairing" invariant (and the corresponding TCC-denial handling) is therefore unverified end-to-end by the offline test suite, even though the underlying detection code (`probe_binding`, `_verify_identity`) exists. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-notes-channel-impl.py:2055` - `Channel.scan(self, *, poll: bool = False)` never references its `poll` parameter anywhere in the method body, even though `run()`'s `poll` command passes `poll=True` expecting some effect; and `mode_of()` (line 210-211) is defined but never called. Safe non-functional cleanup. 🔧 Fix: Gate disabled state before pair-production and record-pairing ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `./bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-notes-channel.test.sh tests/fm-notes-bridge-build.test.sh tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` (all offline, fixture-only; exit=0, failed=0 across all three) - `Reviewed tests/fm-notes-channel.test.sh assertions covering: account/folder-ID confinement, atomic claim+replay identity, reconcile-before-create ACK publication, crash-seam recovery (capture-before-offer, outbound response loss), parser/metadata rejection (locks, oversize, hidden HTML, bidi), high-impact-prose authority downgrade, identity reconciliation (aliases/collisions/edits), 100x2 concurrent dedupe/audit-chain scale test, owner-only file modes, authenticated bounded-check install without activation, emergency disable, audit-chain tamper detection, and hardlink refusal` - `Reviewed tests/fm-notes-bridge-build.test.sh assertions covering: static inspect reporting zero Apple Events plus the sandbox release blocker, release refusing before compile/sign (NO-GO enforcement), fixture app compiling as a dedicated hardened sandboxed app with no live entitlement, and the typed status/eval API surface (no arbitrary eval operation)` - `Reviewed tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh new case confirming an activated Notes bounded check (state/notes-watch.check.sh) registers as a supervision need without counting as an in-flight task` - `git status --porcelain` post-run to confirm no transient artifacts were left in the working tree
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: feat(bin): surface validation daemon liveness at session start
body:
## Intent Surface the shared no-mistakes validation daemon's liveness at session start, so a multi-day outage stops being invisible. Motivation (from a prior diagnosis of this daemon): it died on 2026-07-26, 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-02, and stayed down 2.5 days, 2.9 days and 8 hours respectively before anything restarted it. Nobody noticed on any of the three occasions. Every shipping task in the fleet depends on this daemon; when it is down, work simply stops being validated, and a silent outage is indistinguishable from a quiet fleet. That diagnosis names this gap as the one that made the other daemon failures expensive, and specifies the fix as one cheap read surfaced where a coordinator already looks. Scope deliberately chosen and bounded: a liveness check surfaced alongside the existing bootstrap diagnostics in bin/fm-bootstrap.sh, costing one pid-file read plus one signal-0 test. It was an explicit requirement NOT to add a subsystem, watcher, poller, or background monitor, and to follow existing bootstrap diagnostic conventions rather than invent a new reporting shape. So the new VALIDATION_DAEMON line joins the existing MISSING/TANGLE/FLEET_SYNC family, its handling is documented in the .agents/skills/bootstrap-diagnostics skill that owns responses to actionable lines, and AGENTS.md section 13's trigger list gained the new label. bin/fm-bootstrap.sh's header owns the line format, per this repo's one-owner rule. HARD SAFETY BOUNDARY, deliberate and required: the check OBSERVES ONLY. It must never stop, start, restart, update, or reconfigure the shared daemon - several tasks are parked mid-run against it and killing it would destroy live work. It also deliberately never invokes the no-mistakes CLI at all, because ordinary CLI commands auto-start a daemon as a side effect, which would silently violate that boundary. Automatic restart-on-down behaviour was explicitly ruled out of scope: starting a genuinely down daemon is firstmate's call, and conflating detection with remediation is out of scope here. A trap that already caught a by-hand reading and is deliberately encoded: the pid file is JSON, shaped like {"pid":929670,"started_at":"2026-08-03T03:25:46Z"}, not a bare integer. A naive cat piped into a signal check therefore reports a LIVE daemon as DEAD - exactly the mistake that had to be retracted a moment after it was made. So the file is parsed as JSON, and an unparseable or missing pid file is its own distinct outcome rather than 'down'. Three states are kept distinct and must never be collapsed into two: alive (pid parsed and the process answers), down (pid parsed and nothing answers, or no pid file exists), unknown (pid file present but no pid can be read). Reporting unknown as down would produce false alarms; reporting it as alive would recreate the exact silence this check exists to end. A recorded pid of 0 is deliberately classified unknown for the same reason - kill -0 0 signals the caller's own process group and would answer 'alive' for an absent daemon. started_at is used to report how long the daemon has been up or down where that is cheap and useful: a 2.9-day outage must read as a 2.9-day outage, not merely as 'down'. Design decision worth knowing: the outage LENGTH is taken from the mtime of logs/daemon.log, the last moment the daemon demonstrably wrote anything, because started_at only records when the recorded daemon started and is not a death instant - the same evidence the original diagnosis used to recover the real death times. Both clauses are omitted rather than guessed when their source is absent. Consistent with how existing bootstrap checks behave, a healthy daemon is SILENT; its uptime appears only as a BOOTSTRAP_INFO fact under FM_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE_FACTS=1. A daemon root that does not exist is also silent, because that home has never run the daemon and there is no outage to report. The check runs in detect-only (read-only, second-session) bootstrap runs too, since a multi-day outage is exactly what a concurrent session also needs to see. The root is resolved from NM_HOME, the daemon's own selector, defaulting to ~/.no-mistakes. Verification discipline that was required and followed: the new tests were run against the unfixed code and witnessed RED before anything was changed (five of the six went red; the sixth asserts silence, which unfixed code trivially gives, and was not claimed as a red run). Down-detection is proven POSITIVELY - the tests construct a pid that certainly does not exist by spawning a process, reaping it, and asserting with signal 0 that nothing answers - rather than only confirming 'alive' against the live daemon. Colocated tests cover alive, down, missing pid file, and malformed pid files, per the repo rule that tests exercise behavior through an executable interface (bin/fm-bootstrap.sh itself) and never assert implementation-source bytes. One test-infrastructure change is deliberate: tests/lib.sh now exports NM_HOME pointing at a nonexistent root. Without it, whether the machine's real daemon happens to be alive would leak into every suite that asserts exact bootstrap output; the cases that own this check set NM_HOME per invocation, which wins. This is the same hermeticity discipline the suites already apply to PATH and to ambient terminal-runtime markers. Known pre-existing, unrelated failure, deliberately NOT fixed here: tests/fm-session-start.test.sh fails at 'MISSING diagnostic did not appear at all'. It reproduces identically on unmodified code - the case removes node from its fake bin, but this host has node in /usr/bin which is on the suite's default base path, so it needs FM_TEST_BASE_PATH set to a node-free base. It is out of scope for this task. ## What Changed - Add a read-only session-start check that reports down or unreadable validation-daemon state while keeping healthy and never-used daemon roots silent. - Parse JSON PID records safely and include available uptime or last-active duration evidence without invoking or restarting the daemon. - Document the new `VALIDATION_DAEMON` diagnostic and add hermetic bootstrap coverage for alive, down, missing, and malformed PID states. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The follow-up correctly uses Node to parse well-formed JSON, enforces a positive safe-integer PID, preserves the three-state and read-only contracts, and adds executable coverage for the rejected shapes. ## Testing The focused bootstrap suite passed, and end-to-end detect-only session-start checks demonstrated healthy silence, verbose uptime, down reporting with a 2.9-day outage, and distinct unknown reporting without altering daemon process state.
Evidence: Session-start daemon liveness transcript ```text End-user surface: bin/fm-bootstrap.sh in detect-only session-start mode [alive, normal mode: healthy state is silent] [alive, verbose facts] BOOTSTRAP_INFO: validation daemon alive (pid 2567366, up 2.9d) [down: reaped PID, log last active 2.9 days ago] VALIDATION_DAEMON: down - recorded pid 2567382 is not running; started 3.2d ago, last active 2.9d ago [unknown: JSON pid is 0 and must not probe process group] VALIDATION_DAEMON: unknown - cannot read a pid from /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZ41AFT7YQX11F3PWM4KNEVV/fixtures/unknown/daemon.pid; last active 2.9d ago [safety observations] alive PID before/after bootstrap: still running down PID was positively reaped: not running ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-validation-daemon-lib.sh:94` - Required intent says “the file is parsed as JSON” and malformed files must produce `unknown`, but this `sed` regex merely extracts any numeric `"pid":` substring. title: fix(bin): keep fleet snapshots reliable at scale
body:
## Intent

Fix the structured fleet view (bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh and bin/fm-fleet-view.sh), which fails silently and completely once the backlog grows past a size the fleet has already reached. This is a defect repair, not a feature change: do not redesign the fleet view's output format and do not change what it reports.

DEFECT 1, the size limit. main_inventory_json() passed the entire backlog JSON and the entire tasks JSON to jq as --argjson COMMAND-LINE arguments. Linux caps any single argv entry at MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 131072 bytes, independent of the much larger ARG_MAX total (2097152 here, which is why a total-size intuition misleads). data/backlog.md is already ~96-104KB of markdown and its JSON expansion exceeds the per-argument cap at the current backlog size, several records carrying long captain-hold reasons. The cure was to stop putting bulk data in argv. The user asked me to choose deliberately between stdin, process substitution, and a temp file, and to say why. I chose stdin: values are emitted by a small json_inputs helper and bound positionally in the jq filter with `input`. Rationale, which a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: temp files would need mktemp plus cleanup traps that fire correctly inside the command-substitution subshells this script uses throughout; process substitution adds a /dev/fd dependency and cannot be built dynamically from a variable-length list; and stdin binding additionally makes a MISSING value abort jq (exit 5, "break") rather than silently binding null, so the mechanism is fail-closed by construction, which is the whole point of the second defect.

The user explicitly asked me to audit the WHOLE file rather than patch only the reported line 567. I did, and the same latent failure was present in five further places, all fixed in this change: secondmate_home_summary_json (confirmed independently dying at line 595), the cross-home union in secondmate_current_json, both per-secondmate record builders and the records accumulation, parent_evidence_reconciliation_json, secondmate_landed_from_current_json, and the final document assembly, which carried the whole backlog through argv a SECOND time. Deliberate decision: values with a fixed small shape (booleans, integers, single-path presence objects, single-line status/crew-state objects) intentionally stay on --arg/--argjson, because they cannot grow with the backlog, the fleet, or a status history. That asymmetry is intentional and documented in the json_inputs comment, not an oversight.

DEFECT 2, the fail-open, which the user identified as the serious one and the defect class this fleet cares most about: a check that reports success while establishing nothing. AGENTS.md section 8 directs heartbeat handling to review the fleet from this structured view, so fleet supervision silently degrades as the fleet and backlog grow, without any signal that it has.

Important correction the reviewer should know: the originally reported measurement showed exit status 0, but that reading was confounded, because `echo $?` there followed a pipe to `wc -l` and so reported wc's status. The snapshot does exit 1 on the oversized-backlog path. However a genuine fail-open does exist in the same script and I found and fixed it: a per-task row that failed to build was absorbed by the collecting `| jq -s`, so a LIVE WORKER silently vanished from the fleet inventory while the snapshot still exited 0. Reproduced directly: snapshot rc=0 with stderr "line 490: jq: Argument list too long" and task ids ["small-task"] where big-task had disappeared. Task rows and scout report pointers now abort the snapshot with a diagnostic instead of quietly shrinking the reported fleet, the previously unguarded scout report scan is now checked, and the find scan is captured before sorting so its exit status is not masked by the pipe. An empty fleet remains a valid observation that exits 0, so absence stays distinguishable from failure. A failure contract paragraph was added to the script header, which is the owner tier for this kind of mechanics per the repo's firstmate-coding-guidelines.

VERIFICATION DISCIPLINE, which the user made non-optional because the defect is precisely a false success. Proving the fix by "it stopped printing an error" was explicitly not acceptable. I witnessed the negative control fail first: both new oversized-input tests were run against the CURRENT UNFIXED code and confirmed RED before the fix was applied. test_oversized_backlog_renders_instead_of_dying failed with "expected exit 0, got 1", and test_oversized_task_decisions_keep_the_task_visible failed with "a task with an oversized decision set was dropped from the inventory: [quiet-task]". The other two new tests (the nonzero-exit-with-diagnostic contract and the empty-fleet-is-not-failure contract) are green both before and after by design; they are contract locks required by the definition of done, not proof of the fix, and that distinction was stated plainly rather than glossed. The oversized backlog fixture is generated programmatically inside the test, deliberately NOT copied from the captain's real backlog, and the test asserts the generated backlog's JSON expansion actually exceeds the 131072-byte cap so it cannot quietly stop covering the defect if record sizes drift.

DEFINITION OF DONE: the fleet view renders correctly against the current real backlog (verified at 87 structured records / ~104KB via a scratch copy, grown from the 76 cited when the task was written); a genuine snapshot failure exits nonzero and says what failed; an empty-but-valid fleet still exits 0 and is not confused with failure; and a regression test drives the snapshot with a backlog large enough to exceed the per-argument cap and asserts BOTH that real output is produced AND that a genuine failure surfaces as a nonzero exit.

REPO CONSTRAINTS accepted: this is firstmate's shared tracked material, so the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill was loaded and followed - one sentence per line in tracked markdown, plain dash never an em dash, no agent name as a commit co-author, shellcheck-clean bin scripts via the pinned bin/fm-lint.sh, tests colocated by extending the existing tests/fm-fleet-snapshot-view.test.sh rather than inventing a new runner, and tests that exercise behavior through an executable interface rather than asserting implementation-source bytes.

BASE CONSTRAINT accepted, and deliberate: this worktree sits on upstream trunk 4ee4a0a while the fleet actually runs fork trunk 631c248, 33 commits ahead. The user directed that code being WRITTEN must keep the upstream base, because upstream contribution branches must be cut from upstream trunk or they silently carry unlanded fork work into the contribution. I verified that all three files in scope are byte-identical between 4ee4a0a and 631c248, so the divergence does not touch this task's surface. Do not flag the base as stale.

Verification run: 19/19 tests in tests/fm-fleet-snapshot-view.test.sh pass (15 pre-existing plus 4 new, no regression), tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh passes as the primary downstream consumer of this snapshot contract, plus fm-secondmate-safety (70 ok), fm-secondmate-liveness (15 ok) and fm-decision-hold-lifecycle (9 ok); bin/fm-lint.sh and bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh are both clean.

## What Changed

- Stream growing backlog, task, and secondmate JSON through stdin so fleet snapshots and views continue working beyond Linux’s per-argument size limit.
- Fail closed with diagnostics when task rows, scout report scans or sorting, secondmate records, or final snapshot assembly cannot complete, while preserving successful empty-fleet snapshots.
- Add regression coverage for oversized backlogs and decision sets, snapshot and scout-sort failures, and valid empty fleets.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The follow-up correctly propagates scout-report sort failures while preserving valid empty results, and the full change remains a well-bounded defect repair consistent with the stated output and failure contracts.

## Testing

After two initial runs exceeded the command tool’s 30-second observation window, the focused suite completed successfully in a persistent PTY; manual executable checks then demonstrated a 142,820-byte backlog rendering all 80 records with clean stderr, and confirmed the current empty fleet still returns a valid explicit view.

title: fix(bin): separate task read and contribution bases
body:
## Intent GOAL: Give a dispatched worker a reliable way to READ the code the fleet actually runs while WRITING against the correct contribution base. These are two different references and the spawn path previously provided only one. EVIDENCE THIS FIXES: Measured 2026-08-03 across four concurrently live workers, every one sat at base 4ee4a0a while the fleet's running trunk was 631c248, a 33-commit gap. Two concrete failures already occurred: one task found bin/fm-worktree-guard.sh ENTIRELY ABSENT from its base and had to rebase before its brief's citations resolved; another recorded that line numbers taken against upstream are simply wrong for the running fleet and said this nearly corrupted its report. Every brief citing a file or line number was silently unreliable until this landed. THE DESIGN QUESTION WAS ALREADY SETTLED BEFORE THIS WORK AND WAS NOT TO BE REOPENED. Both naive fixes were attempted and rejected on measurement: (a) resetting slots to the fork trunk silently carries 33 fleet-only commits into every upstream contribution, forbidden by the captain's 2026-07-31 discipline, and it already corrupted upstream PR 1520 into 32 commits and +10,089 against a true 5 and +886; (b) resetting slots to upstream main is impossible because upstream is missing 29 tracked files including 10 bin/ scripts the fleet runs (fm-worktree-guard.sh, fm-admission.sh, fm-launch.sh, fm-wake-ledger.sh, fm-model-registry-lib.sh, fm-wsl-entry.sh among them), so every task would be dispatched onto a trunk lacking the code it edits. The resolved answer, decided 2026-08-03: the spawn path carries TWO values, a slot base carrying the fleet's running code so a task can read and run it, and a contribution target from which its branch is cut so the PR stays clean. WHAT WAS ASKED FOR: make both references explicit and available - the slot base a worker's worktree sits on so file reads and line citations resolve against what the fleet runs; the contribution target its branch is cut from; record both in the task's metadata so they are inspectable after the fact rather than inferred; and make the generated brief state both plainly with the read-here/write-there rule so a worker cannot get this wrong by default, which is the part that actually prevents the failure. Where the two coincide nothing should change; where they differ the worker must be told. A REFINEMENT WORTH EVALUATING AND REPORTING ON BUT EXPLICITLY NOT REQUIRED: a task whose target files do not exist upstream cannot be an upstream contribution at all and must land on the fork, so the contribution target may be derivable rather than declared. DECISIONS AND TRADEOFFS MADE WHILE DOING THE WORK (deliberate, not oversights): - Added a new file bin/fm-task-base-lib.sh, slightly beyond the named scope of fm-spawn.sh/fm-brief.sh/metadata/tests. Justified by the one-owner rule in the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill: both the spawn and the brief generator need the same resolution, and duplicating it in two places would guarantee drift. - fm-brief.sh is TOLD the pair rather than deriving it, exactly like the existing --mode delivery contract, because its REPO argument is a caller-supplied string and not a checkout it could read. This mirrors the established delivery-contract precedent: required value -> recorded in a machine-readable brief line -> spawn refuses a brief/flag mismatch. - Derivation recognizes two fork shapes: a separate 'upstream' remote, and an origin whose fetch URL differs from its push URL (firstmate's own layout, where origin FETCHES upstream and PUSHES the fork). - On the optional refinement: deriving the contribution target from whether target files exist upstream CANNOT be done at dispatch, because the spawn does not know the task's target files. So derivation sets the default, an explicit flag overrides it, and the generated brief pushes the check to where the information exists - a worker whose named files are absent from its contribution base is told to append 'blocked:' and stop rather than recreate the file or rebase onto the running trunk. This is a deliberate design answer to the parked task, not an omission. - An upstream trunk that exists but cannot be read locally is recorded as the literal 'unresolved' and REFUSED rather than silently degraded onto the slot base, because that silent degradation is exactly the pollution being prevented. - A scout cuts no branch, so it records contribution_target=n/a and base_state=read-only and refuses --contribution-target; its slot is still placed at the fleet trunk, which is what fixes report citations. - The slot placement is a reset rather than the secondmate path's fast-forward, because a fast-forward silently skips a diverged slot and leaves the stale base in place. It is guarded: a slot with uncommitted changes, or sitting on a task branch that may hold unlanded work, is left untouched and launched as-is with a notice. - The pollution guard is an ancestor test (the contribution target must be an ancestor of the branch head), chosen because it catches a polluted branch both freshly cut and after the worker commits on top. - When the two references coincide the generated brief is byte-identical to before, verified by diffing two scaffolds. CONSTRAINTS AND EXCLUSIONS THAT WERE HONORED: Do not restructure treehouse allocation. Do not change the worktree guard's measurement logic - a related branch worktree-guard-measures-upstream-not-fork-trunk holds a parked unlanded branch at e6e9227 containing the guard's measurement fix, that half is verified and accepted, it must not be redone and must not be reverted, and this change was deliberately kept separable so that rebase stays cheap. VERIFICATION DISCIPLINE REQUIRED AND PERFORMED: every negative control was witnessed failing FIRST and the red runs recorded. Five were run - the guard neutered to always return clean, the unresolved case degraded onto the slot base, the slot placement removed, the metadata recording removed, and the brief's branch step reverted to a plain checkout - and each failed exactly the test that covers it before passing again restored. The pollution case was CONSTRUCTED rather than inferred: a branch is cut from the slot base and the guard must refuse it, and correctness is never proven by absence. Against the live repository the resolution returns slot 631c248 and contribution 4ee4a0a and the guard refuses the fork trunk with the exact 33-commit count. DELIVERY EXPECTATION SPECIFIC TO THIS TASK: the upstream PR is expected to show ZERO checks executed, because every upstream run from this account sits at action_required awaiting maintainer approval that cannot be granted here. That is expected and is not a failure of this change. If the pipeline reports checks-passed off that empty set it is a known false green and must not be accepted as real CI evidence. ## What Changed - Resolve and record separate slot and contribution bases so workers read the fleet’s running code while branches start from the correct delivery target. - Place reusable worktrees at the slot base, render mode-aware read/write contracts in task briefs, and refuse unresolved, mismatched, or polluted branch bases. - Add architecture documentation and comprehensive task-base coverage for fork layouts, overrides, metadata, brief generation, and spawn safeguards. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The updated change cleanly addresses all four prior defects and satisfies the source-verifiable intent without introducing another material issue. ## Testing The focused two-base test passed across resolution, brief generation, slot placement, metadata, scouts, mismatch handling, unresolved bases, batch overrides, and pollution prevention; manual CLI evidence additionally shows the end-user brief and a constructed two-commit pollution refusal. No visual artifact was captured because the changed surface is shell CLI/generated Markdown rather than UI.
Evidence: Two-base brief and pollution-guard evidence ```text $ fm-brief.sh evidence-demo fixture --mode no-mistakes --slot-base --contribution-target # Base references - read here, write there Base contract: slot=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa contribution=bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb This task has TWO base commits and they are NOT the same. Confusing them is the failure this section exists to prevent. - **Read at `aaaaaaaaaaaa`.** That is the code the fleet ACTUALLY RUNS, and it is where this worktree starts. Any file path or line number in your task description was taken against it. - **Write at `bbbbbbbbbbbb`.** That is the base your work is CONTRIBUTED to, and the branch step below cuts from it. Once you branch, your working tree holds the contribution base, not the running fleet code. From then on read the running code with `git show aaaaaaaaaaaa:` instead of assuming the file in front of you is what the fleet runs. Never cut or rebase your branch onto `aaaaaaaaaaaa`: that silently carries every commit the fleet has landed but never contributed into your PR, which is exactly what this separation prevents. Verify your branch before pushing: `git merge-base --is-ancestor bbbbbbbbbbbb HEAD` must succeed. If a file your task names does not exist at `bbbbbbbbbbbb` at all, then this task cannot be a contribution to that base. 1. First action: create your branch: `git checkout -b fm/evidence-demo bbbbbbbbbbbb` $ pollution guard in a genuinely diverged topology REFUSED: branch 'polluted-slot-branch' does not descend from contribution target 'contribution'; it carries 2 commit(s) absent from that target, so a PR from it would contribute work the target never had ACCEPTED: branch cut from contribution target ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 4 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1059` - The required contract says the brief must state both references and spawn must refuse drift, but a distinct/unresolved ship brief with no `Base contract:` only warns and launches. Because that legacy brief still uses plain `git checkout -b`, the worker branches from the fleet slot and can produce the exact polluted PR this change must prevent. Refuse launch when bases differ and the contract line is absent. - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1057` - The required brief/metadata agreement is skipped entirely for scouts. A stale or manually altered scout brief can name a different slot SHA from the one recorded and checked out by spawn, making its promised citation base false. Validate the scout's `slot=... contribution=n/a` contract before launch too. - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1010` - Contribution-target derivation ignores delivery mode, so `local-only` tasks on fork-shaped repositories branch from upstream even though their delivery contract requires a fast-forward merge into local `main`. Such a branch may not descend from local `main` and cannot satisfy the documented merge path; resolve local-only contributions against the local trunk or require an explicit target. - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:516` - Batch dispatch parses `--slot-base` and `--contribution-target` but does not add them to `shared_args`, so explicit overrides are silently discarded during each re-exec and every task uses derived values instead. Either forward both flags or reject them for batch mode. 🔧 Fix: Captain: enforce mode-aware spawn base contracts ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-task-base.test.sh` - Generated a ship brief with `bin/fm-brief.sh evidence-demo fixture --mode no-mistakes --slot-base <fleet-sha> --contribution-target <upstream-sha>` and inspected its rendered read-here/write-there instructions and branch command. - Constructed a genuinely diverged Git topology with upstream-only and fleet-only commits, then invoked `task_base_verify_branch` against branches cut from each side and captured the refusal/acceptance transcript. - `git status --short` after testing to confirm no working-tree artifacts were introduced.
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix(bin): refuse merges without verified green checks
body:
## Intent Close a measured false-success class: an empty or non-verifying check set must never be readable as "green" anywhere firstmate decides to merge. THE MEASURED EVENT. On 2026-08-02 a validation pipeline reported checks-passed while the pull request's check-run set was EMPTY. Nothing was red because nothing had run. The terminal claim was reported rather than computed, so "no evidence of failure" was treated as "evidence of success". This violates the fleet's standing rule that absence is never evidence, at the highest-stakes point it has: the captain's merge authority is explicitly "never a red PR", and a PR with zero check runs is not green, it is unverified, which the old path could not distinguish. The specification is data/eval-merge-eligibility-gate/report.md section 4.2 item R2 and section 3.1, and the rule was already designed as LD-2 (the empty-set law) in data/loop-ld-control-safety/report.md. THE RULE IMPLEMENTED. The weakest non-empty relevant member decides. An empty check-run set is never pass; it is a distinct outcome meaning not verified. A set containing only neutral/skipped/cancelled members is likewise not pass. The terminal verdict is computed from the returned data, never copied from a reported claim. NOT RUN, FAILED, UNAVAILABLE and PASSED must remain four distinguishable states and must never be collapsed; a forge read that fails is UNAVAILABLE and must not read as either pass or fail. DELIBERATE DECISIONS A REVIEWER READING ONLY THE DIFF WOULD NOT KNOW: 1. This branch CARRIES FORWARD an existing, sound, but unlanded repair branch (fork/fm/pipeline-reports-green-on-absent-ci, three commits cut from upstream cd73e75) rather than reimplementing it. Firstmate explicitly directed this: carrying it forward with its proof is better than a fresh implementation. Its first three commits are preserved verbatim, including its own no-mistakes review and document commits. Only one docs/scripts.md conflict was resolved, keeping the base's newer fm-promote.sh wording and taking the branch's fm-pr-merge.sh wording. 2. The check rollup is counted in THREE disjoint buckets, not two. The carried branch counted only "not SUCCESS", which collapsed a skipped, cancelled, queued, in-progress or action_required run into the same words as a failed one. Failures (FAILURE, ERROR, TIMED_OUT, STARTUP_FAILURE) and non-verdicts are now counted and reported separately, because "nothing examined this head" must never be reported as "something rejected this head". A rollup whose buckets do not account for its unsuccessful members is reported as unreadable rather than resolved either way. 3. An empty rollup now names WHY it is empty, via a check-suites read on the refusal path only. Firstmate specifically required this: "no checks configured" and "checks exist but are awaiting approval" are DIFFERENT states and both must be refused as not-verified rather than passed. action_required is a real, common, reachable case, not hypothetical: a cross-fork PR holds workflows pending maintainer approval, and this account has pull-only on the upstream repository, so those checks will never run. GitHub reports both causes as the same empty statusCheckRollup, so the check-suites read is the only way to separate them. This enrichment can never turn a refusal into a merge. 4. SCOPE WAS DELIBERATELY WIDENED by firstmate to cover bin/fm-crew-state.sh as well as the merge path, "since a guard in one with a false green in the other is not a fix". Two false greens were closed there: the ci-log reader mapped "no CI checks reported - still monitoring" to green, and the terminal handler repeated the pipeline's reported checks-passed claim unchecked. An unreadable log deliberately stays unknown, because a log that could not be read is not evidence that nothing ran. 5. A TEST WAS DELIBERATELY INVERTED. tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh's test_ci_monitoring_no_checks_terminal_surfaces_done ASSERTED the defect: it required "state: done" and "checks green" for a run that saw zero checks. That assertion encoded the exact 2026-08-02 false success, so it is replaced by test_ci_monitoring_no_checks_terminal_is_not_green plus a matched positive control. This is intended, not an accidental weakening of coverage. 6. VERIFICATION DISCIPLINE WAS THE POINT OF THE TASK, because the defect IS a false success and proving a fix by "it no longer misbehaves" is worthless. Every negative control was run against the CURRENT UNFIXED code and watched go red before any fix was applied: 14 of 15 on the carried branch, 4 more on the three-bucket extension, and 1 on crew-state, which emitted the defect verbatim as "state: done, source: run-step, checks green". Every refusal is paired with a matched POSITIVE control, because a guard that "refuses everything" would satisfy a red-only pin too and would be a worse defect than the one being fixed. Verified against real GitHub data and not only fixtures: live PR 1583 (empty rollup, two check suites held at action_required) refuses end to end with zero merge calls, and real open green PR 1577 (13 successful checks) verifies and reaches the merge call recording merge_verification=verified. 7. --allow-unverified is the captain's explicit override, deliberately never inferred from the environment, rejected after the -- separator so it cannot leak to gh-axi, and recorded as merge_verification=override so an unverified merge stays visible afterwards. KNOWN BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, ACCEPTED: the guard also refuses a rollup containing a failing member, so pull requests carrying a FAILURE on the honour-system "PR must be raised via no-mistakes" check now refuse and need that check fixed or an explicit override. This is the correct application of the standing "never merge a red PR" rule. EXPLICIT EXCLUSIONS. Do NOT change the required-checks configuration on any GitHub repository; repository settings are the captain's. Do NOT attempt to resolve the separate atomic merge head-binding race; it is a registered open captain decision, and the script header documents why gh-axi currently drops --match-head-commit. Do NOT merge anything. STYLE CONSTRAINTS from the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill, since this is firstmate's own shared tracked material: one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash and never an em dash, never an agent name as commit co-author, bin/*.sh shellcheck-clean via bin/fm-lint.sh, tests colocated in tests/ extending the existing scripts rather than a new runner, and tests exercising behaviour through an executable interface rather than asserting implementation-source bytes. AGENTS.md additions were kept to three lines total by patching existing sentences rather than appending new clauses, per that skill's size discipline. ## What Changed - Re-verify each pull request’s current head before merging, refusing empty, failed, incomplete, unreadable, unmergeable, or review-blocked states. - Distinguish failed checks from checks without verdicts, enrich empty-rollup refusals, and record verified or explicitly overridden merge metadata. - Require crew-state reporting to corroborate `checks-passed` claims with CI evidence, preserving unavailable evidence as unknown instead of green. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The corrective commit consistently requires explicit green evidence across terminal, active-run, status-log, and coarse-run mappings, while preserving unavailable and non-ready states distinctly and adding executable matrix coverage against recurrence. ## Testing The focused merge and crew-state behavioral suites passed, and end-to-end CLI evidence confirmed that absence remains unverified and blocked while real successful checks remain green and merge-eligible; no visual artifact was applicable because the changed end-user surfaces are shell CLIs.
Evidence: Merge eligibility CLI transcript ```text ok - fm-pr-merge refuses a head with zero check runs and names it as empty, not failing ok - fm-pr-merge still merges a green, mergeable, unreviewed PR === EMPTY CHECK SET: USER-VISIBLE REFUSAL === error: refusing to merge head 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111: no check runs exist on this head exit=1; merge_calls=0 === VERIFIED CHECK SET: MERGE PATH === armed: state/task-x1.check.sh merge_call=pr merge 32 --repo example/repo --squash merge_verification=verified merge_verified_head=deadbeefcafefeed0000000000000000deadbeef ```
Evidence: Crew-state CLI transcript ```text === REPORTED checks-passed, BUT ZERO CHECK EVIDENCE === state: blocked · source: run-step · run reported a passing result its own CI log does not record: nothing verified this head === REPORTED checks-passed, CORROBORATED BY CHECK EVIDENCE === state: done · source: run-step · checks green: PR ready for review ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:515` - The required criterion says “An unreadable log deliberately stays unknown” and that terminal verdicts must be computed rather than copied from reported claims. Here, `checks-passed` becomes `done` for every result except `not-ready`, so an unavailable/unreadable CI log returns `unknown` and still surfaces as “checks green.” Handle `green`, `not-ready`, and `unknown` distinctly; the latter must remain unknown rather than green. 🔧 Fix: Preserve unavailable CI corroboration as unknown 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:583` - The required criterion says “NOT RUN, FAILED, UNAVAILABLE and PASSED must remain four distinguishable states” and that a terminal verdict is never copied from a reported claim. When a working run has a status-log claim containing “checks green,” an unavailable CI log produces `CI_LOG_STATE=unknown`, but this condition accepts every value except `not-ready` and emits `done`. Require `CI_LOG_STATE=green` explicitly; preserve `unknown` as unavailable instead of trusting the status-log claim. 🔧 Fix: Require explicit green evidence across crew-state mappings ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - Inspected `git diff --stat` and changed files for `4ee4a0a2790cfaa5e47b30fa462f16546f2ab5b6..2dea7d6d46c7c83c8073688e7fb2f6f074caa5f0` - `tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh` - `tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` - Executed the merge harness's `test_zero_check_runs_refuses` and `test_all_successful_checks_still_merges` cases while capturing user-visible stderr, merge-call logs, and persisted verification metadata - Executed `fm-crew-state.sh` through its behavioral harness with identical terminal `checks-passed` claims backed first by a no-checks log and then by an all-checks-passed log
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix: require resolved decisions before scout teardown
body:
## Intent Publish an already-authored fix that closes a hole in scout teardown's decision-hold verification gate, as a small reviewable PR against kunchenguid/firstmate. The bug: bin/fm-decision-hold.sh's read-only `verify` subcommand, which scout teardown calls before removing any source state, used verify_hold_durable. That helper accepts a captain decision that is EITHER actively held OR durably resolved. An actively held row is by definition an unanswered decision, so the gate that exists to stop teardown erasing a source before its decisions are answered passed on exactly the state it was meant to refuse. A scout whose inventoried decision was still open could be torn down, taking its report's context with it. `verify` now requires a positive durable resolution for every inventoried key (verify_hold_resolved). The deliberate second half, which a reviewer reading only the diff would likely question as unrelated: strengthening the gate alone would introduce a worse failure mode. tasks-axi prunes resolved Done rows out of the live backlog into data/done-archive.md, so a correctly resolved decision returns NOT_FOUND from a live lookup once pruned, and its originating scout would become permanently unverifiable with no recovery short of recreating the row. This home has already lost five gate scouts to that exact class of failure. So resolution lookup falls back to the archive: a new task_show_durable reparses exactly one unique resolved captain row out of data/done-archive.md when the live lookup reports NOT_FOUND. The asymmetry is intentional and load-bearing - the fallback widens what counts as FINDABLE, never what counts as RESOLVED. A missing, duplicated, malformed, or indeterminate record still keeps teardown refusing. Deliberate decisions to preserve, not flag: - The two halves ship together on purpose. Shipping them separately was tested empirically in a throwaway clone and rejected: the archive-fallback half alone leaves "unresolved captain decision allowed teardown", and the strengthened-verify half alone leaves "identical resolution retry could not use the durable archive". Each half fails a regression case the other passes, so a split would ship a knowingly broken intermediate, and one ordering would make the permanently-unverifiable failure class easier to hit. - archived_task_show reconstructs a minimal synthetic backlog document and pipes it to tasks-axi show --file /dev/stdin rather than parsing the archived row's fields directly. This is deliberate: it keeps tasks-axi the single parser of the row format so the archive path cannot drift from the live path. - The strict "exactly one match" requirement in archived_task_show is deliberate. A duplicated archived identity is ambiguous, and ambiguity must refuse rather than guess. - The documentation edits to README.md, docs/decision-hold-lifecycle.md, and .agents/skills/decision-hold-lifecycle/SKILL.md correct statements this change itself falsifies (they previously said a hold could be closed on teardown, and described the old verification semantics). They are in scope for that reason and for no other; no unrelated documentation was added or improved. - tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh gains three cases that drive the halves apart on purpose: resolved-then-pruned must allow teardown, unresolved must still refuse it, and never-existing or indeterminate must still refuse it. Constraints: this is a cherry-pick of commit b437c69 rebased onto the current default-branch head, verified to preserve its exact 5 files / 216 insertions / 31 deletions. The repository style rules in the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill apply (one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never an em dash, bin/*.sh shellcheck-clean, no agent co-author on commits). Locally the full suite passes, bin/fm-lint.sh is clean at pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0, and bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh reports ok at 64 surfaces / 185 local links.
