title: fix: preserve crew run attribution during validation
body:
## Intent Fix bin/fm-crew-state.sh losing its authoritative source mid-validation, which blinds supervision exactly when a run is busiest. SYMPTOM. fm-crew-state.sh reported "working / run-step / validating" then flipped to "unknown / none / no current-state source available" and stayed there across ~10 minutes while the crew's pane was unmistakably alive. Because fm-classify-lib.sh's crew_is_provably_working() reads the same source, a working crew stops being provably-working, so bin/fm-watch.sh cannot take its absorbed-stale path and every idle repaint raises a fresh "possible wedge" escalation. WHAT WAS WANTED (the accepted requirements): 1. Distinguish "no run exists for this branch" from "the run lookup could not complete". A lookup failure must not read the same as an absence. Degrade to the last known run-step, or to an explicit degraded marker - never to "unknown". 2. A fix round that advances the tip must still attribute to its own run. The skip rule is correct for a stale or rewritten run and wrong for the run that is currently authoring those commits. 3. Neither change may weaken genuine wedge detection for a crew that really has stopped. This is the constraint that makes the task non-trivial: an over-broad "assume still working" degrades into never detecting a real wedge. 4. Required approach: reproduce both causes deterministically in tests BEFORE fixing - a lookup that times out, and a run whose recorded sha is behind a tip the run itself advanced. Then fix both, then prove a genuinely stopped crew is still detected as wedged. That third test is the one that stops this fix from becoming a worse bug. 5. Acceptance criteria: a timed-out or failed run lookup yields a degraded-but-known state, not unknown; a run that advanced the tip via its own fix commits still attributes to that run; a genuinely stopped crew is still detected, covered by an explicit test; tests fail against the original code and pass after. LATER ACCEPTED ADDITION - A THIRD MECHANISM. Mid-task, a third distinct mechanism was reported from a live run and I was asked to verify it myself rather than take it on faith, reproduce it before designing around it, and say so if the runs row turned out to be keyed on something other than branch. Verification result, which is part of the accepted scope: - The reported premise ("the branch is entirely ABSENT from no-mistakes runs --limit 200, which returned only 13 rows") was WRONG. In the crew's own worktree the listing returned 35 rows and the branch was the FIRST row. The 13-row figure came from a different repository; "no-mistakes runs" lists per-repository and the helper runs it inside the crew's worktree. The row is not keyed on anything other than branch. - But the underlying finding was RIGHT and is a genuine third mechanism, distinct from the two above. Verified live on task arkrh-corpus-types-unbound-unconstructible: "axi status" in the crew's own worktree returned that crew's own branch, status running, parked at fix_review with 3 findings and branch_sync.state pipeline_owned - but the head it reported (1c17405c) is NOT an object in that worktree at all ("git rev-parse --verify" fails with "malformed object name"), because the pipeline commits in a copy the worktree has never fetched. The lookup completed in under a second and the tip had not moved, so this is neither the timeout cause nor the code-identity-skip cause. - Accepted requirement: a head we cannot RESOLVE is different evidence from a head that DIVERGED, and must be handled, still without weakening wedge detection. SCOPE DISCIPLINE (accepted exclusions): - fm-parked-decision-stale-noise is a DIFFERENT mechanism with the same visible symptom and is explicitly NOT in scope; fixing one will not fix the other. The diff is kept to source-resolution and attribution logic. - tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh belongs to another concurrent branch and must not be edited. - Tests must run only inside the task worktree against a temporary home, never against the primary checkout's live state/. WHAT I IMPLEMENTED, and the design decisions a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: Mechanism 1 - lookup failure vs absence. nm_run swallowed the exit status with "|| true", so a no-mistakes call killed by its own timeout was indistinguishable from "this branch has no run". The status is now propagated (124 on timeout, and a deliberate 127 when the call cannot be bounded at all because no timeout/gtimeout/perl exists). A failure degrades to the crew's last observed run-step under a NEW source token, "run-step-degraded", recorded in a new state/.run-step file. Deliberate decision: empty stdout counts as a failure, not an absence - verified empirically against the installed CLI that "axi status" answers a branch with no run of its own with some OTHER branch's run as informational display, so it has no empty "nothing to report" answer to confuse this with. Mechanism 2 - fix-round tip advance. An actively-executing run (running/fixing/ci) now keeps attribution when the tip advanced past the sha it recorded, because it authored that advance. Deliberate narrowing: a PARKED run commits nothing while waiting on a response, so a tip that moved past it is still local work outside the run and must still invalidate. That narrowing is what keeps the pre-existing test "local work advanced past run head invalidates attribution" passing rather than being loosened. Mechanism 3 - pipeline-owned head. nm_head_relation now separates "unresolved" (sha is not an object here) from "diverged" (resolvable but on neither side of HEAD). A LIVE run answered for THIS branch may be attributed despite an unresolvable head. Deliberate asymmetry: the historical runs listing never earns that benefit, because it has no notion of "current" - only the branch-scoped "axi status" answer does. Terminal runs are refused in every widened case. SAFETY DESIGN (the third acceptance criterion, deliberately load-bearing): - Nothing is degraded for a crew never seen validating: no record, no replay. - The degrade is age-bounded by a new FM_CREW_STATE_DEGRADED_MAX_AGE knob (default 900s; 0 disables the degrade entirely), so a permanently unreachable daemon stops absorbing wedge suspicion instead of hiding a real wedge forever. - Placement is a safety property, not a style choice: the degraded answer sits BELOW the endpoint checks and the exact busy verdict, so live positive evidence (a gone endpoint proving the crew stopped, a busy harness proving it is working now) always outranks a remembered step; and ABOVE the unreadable-harness and status-log fallbacks, because an observed run-step beats an append-only event log. This is why the busy-verdict "unknown" emit was deferred into a BUSY_STATE variable rather than emitted inline - it still outranks the status-log fallback exactly as before. - A completed lookup that finds no run never degrades: absence stays absence. - run-step-degraded is deliberately EXCLUDED from bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh's decision-clearing live-activity sources: it is good enough to keep a crew provably working for wedge triage, but never good enough to clear a captain decision. Only a comment was added there to make that deliberate exclusion explicit. Also: bin/fm-classify-lib.sh's crew_absorb_class accepts run-step-degraded as working evidence (that is the whole point - it is what the watcher's absorb path consumes); bin/fm-teardown.sh removes the new state/.run-step record for both a task and a secondmate's children; AGENTS.md documents the new state file in its layout listing; docs/architecture.md and docs/configuration.md document the invariant and the new knob. fm-crew-state.sh's header previously claimed "Read-only and side-effect free". That claim is now deliberately narrowed in the header: it writes exactly one thing, the run-step record, which is what makes degrading to a last known step possible at all. Verified that no doc or test depended on the old claim. EVIDENCE: 5 reproduction tests fail against the original code and pass after; 7 safety/guard tests pass on BOTH sides, which is exactly what makes them guards rather than reproductions. Verified per-test in both directions, not only as a whole suite. Verified against the live arkrh task read-only using a temp state dir: the shipped reader could not attribute and fell through to the pane, while this branch reports "working / run-step / validating (running)". KNOWN PRE-EXISTING FAILURES, deliberately out of scope and each already queued separately: tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh, tests/fm-session-start.test.sh, tests/fm-test-run.test.sh. All three were confirmed failing on the base branch with these changes stashed. The rest of the non-e2e suite (76 files) passes, plus fm-lint.sh and fm-doc-audience-check.sh. ## What Changed - Distinguish failed run lookups from confirmed absence and replay recent observed run steps through an age-bounded `run-step-degraded` source without overriding stopped or dead crew evidence. - Preserve attribution for actively authoring fix rounds and current pipeline-owned heads unavailable in the worktree, while rejecting terminal, diverged, or unsupported historical runs. - Integrate degraded run steps with watcher classification, teardown, configuration, and documentation, with regression coverage for attribution failures and wedge-detection safeguards. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The latest change removes unsupported authoring inference from coarse historical rows while retaining detailed current-run attribution, and the bounded cache lifecycle now preserves genuine wedge detection. ## Testing Alongside the supplied baseline context, this phase directly reproduced all five acceptance regressions on the original code, passed the focused target suite, captured end-to-end CLI evidence, and confirmed real watcher subprocesses still surface stopped crews and escalate genuine wedges. No source changes were made, and transient test data was removed.
Evidence: End-to-end crew-state and watcher-triage transcript ```text SCENARIO 1 - real bounded timeout after an observed validating step state: working · source: run-step-degraded · validating (running) · run lookup unavailable (last known 1s ago) watcher triage: absorbed stale (provably working) SCENARIO 2 - active fix round after its own commit advanced the branch tip recorded run head: cbf65580a934d17eed40b88c2997f770ce3a6a17 advanced worktree tip: 737d8713664a2f6d72efa8613e0d07e26e4d3f4d state: working · source: run-step · validating (fixing) SCENARIO 3 - live branch-scoped run with pipeline-owned unresolved head worktree resolution: head 1c17405cdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef is unavailable locally state: parked · source: run-step · parked at review: 3 finding(s) SCENARIO 4 - completed lookup finds no run and the crew is idle state: unknown · source: none · no current-state source available watcher triage: possible wedge surfaced (not provably working) SCENARIO 5 - remembered validation expires during continued lookup failure state: unknown · source: none · no current-state source available watcher triage: possible wedge surfaced (not provably working) ```
Evidence: Five regressions reproduced against original code ```text TARGET TESTS AGAINST ORIGINAL CODE (base 1e247571aa75e00b00c7a01c4830025ecd44dc61) test_lookup_timeout_degrades_to_last_known_run_step not ok - a timed-out lookup must not read as unknown (unexpected: 'state: unknown') --- output --- state: unknown · source: none · no current-state source available result: expected baseline failure (exit 1) test_real_timeout_bound_degrades_to_last_known_run_step not ok - a genuinely killed query degrades (missing: 'source: run-step-degraded') --- output --- state: unknown · source: none · no current-state source available result: expected baseline failure (exit 1) test_missing_run_head_with_failed_fallback_degrades not ok - missing run head preserves the recorded step (missing: 'source: run-step-degraded') --- output --- state: working · source: status-log · current stage still in progress result: expected baseline failure (exit 1) test_fix_round_advanced_tip_attributes_via_axi_status not ok - an active run behind its own fix commit keeps attribution (missing: 'source: run-step') --- output --- state: unknown · source: none · no current-state source available result: expected baseline failure (exit 1) test_pipeline_owned_unresolvable_head_attributes not ok - a live run whose head this worktree cannot see still attributes (missing: 'source: run-step') --- output --- state: unknown · source: none · no current-state source available result: expected baseline failure (exit 1) ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed (5) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:790` - The accepted criterion says a failed lookup must use the last-known step or “an explicit degraded marker - never unknown,” but this branch emits `run-step-degraded` only when a record exists; otherwise it falls through to `unknown`, which the new `test_lookup_timeout_without_known_run_step_still_surfaces` explicitly expects. Decide whether to add a non-working explicit degraded state/source that preserves wedge detection, or explicitly amend the requirement to permit unknown when no record exists. - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:615` - A completed lookup with no attributable run leaves `<id>.run-step` intact. The reachable sequence is: observe a working run and write the record, complete a later lookup that finds no run, then have the next lookup fail within 900 seconds; the old working record is replayed and `crew_is_provably_working` absorbs the stopped crew. Invalidate the record at the completed-no-run boundary and add a seed -> absence -> timeout regression test. 🔧 Fix: Invalidate stale run-step records after confirmed absence 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:618` - The new invalidation still depends on the historical listing completing. Reachable sequence: seed a working record, let branch-scoped `axi status` complete for this same branch with a terminal unresolvable head, then let `runs` time out; this branch sets `LOOKUP_FAILED` without clearing the record, so the old working step is replayed and the terminal crew remains provably working. Clear the record as soon as a current-branch answer provides non-attributable/terminal evidence, independently of the fallback call, and cover seed -> terminal same-branch answer -> fallback failure. 🔧 Fix: Invalidate cached run-step on same-branch rejection 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:610` - This early clear conflates disproving evidence with the existing `missing` head relation. Reachable sequence: seed a working record, receive a successful same-branch status response with its head omitted, then let the runs-list fallback fail; line 610 deletes the record before the failure is known, so an idle crew returns to unknown instead of its degraded known step. Preserve the record and classify the lookup as failed for `missing`; clear only when terminal status or a concrete relation such as diverged/non-authoring run-behind invalidates attribution, and extend the existing missing-head test with seed -> fallback failure. 🔧 Fix: Preserve cached run-step for inconclusive missing heads 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:769` - The cache update occurs after two terminal early exits. Reachable sequence: a running read records `working`, a later matching run plus `done: ... checks green` emits `done` at lines 736/747 without updating or clearing the record, then a failed lookup replays the stale working step and makes the finished crew provably working again. Update or invalidate the cached step before every run-derived terminal emit, and cover seed -> CI-ready status-log verdict -> timeout. 🔧 Fix: Persist CI-ready verdicts before terminal emits 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:464` - The accepted criterion says, “A PARKED run commits nothing…so a tip that moved past it…must still invalidate,” but this hunk treats every coarse historical `running` row as authoring. Reachable path: `axi status` returns another branch, a parked run’s coarse row is `running`, local work advances the tip, and `authoring=1` accepts `run-behind`, causing the stopped crew to remain provably working. Decide whether coarse rows must reject `run-behind`, or add a detailed source that can prove the run is actively authoring before widening attribution. 🔧 Fix: Reject coarse run-behind rows without authoring proof ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` - Ran `test_lookup_timeout_degrades_to_last_known_run_step`, `test_real_timeout_bound_degrades_to_last_known_run_step`, `test_missing_run_head_with_failed_fallback_degrades`, `test_fix_round_advanced_tip_attributes_via_axi_status`, and `test_pipeline_owned_unresolvable_head_attributes` against base commit `1e247571aa75e00b00c7a01c4830025ecd44dc61` - Exercised the real `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` reader and `crew_is_provably_working` classifier across timeout, fix-round, unresolved-head, completed-absence, and expired-record scenarios - Ran `test_nonterminal_stale_not_working_surfaced` from `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` against a real `fm-watch.sh` subprocess - Ran `test_nonterminal_stale_provably_working_absorbed_then_escalated` from `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` against a real `fm-watch.sh` subprocess
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix(bin): classify a matched passive CI monitor pause as paused
body:
## What Changed - `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` now lets a newest `paused:` event override the run-step verdict in exactly one narrow case: a full, matched passive CI monitor (`running`/`ci` with a PR, only `ci,running` attached, no gate or fixing step) whose run head *is* this worktree's head, whose ULID-decoded start predates the event, and whose semantic worker is affirmatively idle or confidently gone. It emits `paused · run-step` carrying the matched run id and head; active, fixing, gated, terminal, ancestor-only-head, and busy/unknown cases keep run-step authority, and no pause prose is parsed. - `bin/fm-watch.sh` absorbs only that run-step-sourced pause past the live-worker safeguard, caching the canonical verdict behind a fingerprint (status signature and last line, code head, busy generation/state, long recheck deadline) so a self-declared status-log pause still takes a fresh read. The per-window state-file key derivation and the pause/stale marker retirement moved into `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh` (`fm_state_file_key`, `fm_clear_pause_state`, `fm_clear_pause_tracking`) so the watcher and the away-mode daemon can no longer key or orphan those markers differently. - Added `bin/fm-stat-lib.sh` as the single probe-bound owner of portable file metadata (mtime, size, signature, full mode, uid, device, inode, nlink, identity), replacing the `uname`-guess and `stat -f || stat -c` shapes across the supervision graph, fleet snapshot, and herdr readers (issue #1601), with BSD full mode read from raw `st_mode`. `tests/fm-stat-flavor.test.sh` enumerates the covered files and exercises GNU/BSD/native flavors; `tests/lib.sh` also pins commit signing off so fixtures are hermetic. Docs in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, and `docs/configuration.md` were updated to match. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The only substantiated defect from the prior round is fully resolved - every fixture installer now provides bin/fm-stat-lib.sh and the redundant watcher key assignment is removed without changing behaviour - leaving a well-tested, explicitly scoped refactor whose two remaining observations the user already accepted as informational. ## Testing Ran the four suites that directly own this change (fm-crew-state, fm-stat-flavor, fm-watch-triage, fm-daemon) and the seven further suites whose fixtures it touched - all green, with no flakiness across repeated watcher-timing cases. Because passing unit tests alone do not show the captain-facing behavior, I also built two manual end-to-end demonstrations that run the real production scripts at the base commit and the target commit over identical fixtures. At the reader surface, an idle crew whose only attached work is a passive CI monitor bound to its exact head now reports `state: paused · source: run-step · ... passive CI monitor remains attached (run <id>, head <sha>)` where the base reported `state: done`; at the supervision surface, the real watcher stops waking the captain for that crew and instead absorbs it onto the external-wait cadence with a `state/.watch-triage.log` entry, while the base watcher exited with a queued `stale:` wake. A safety matrix over the same fixture shape confirms a busy worker, an active pre-CI review step, a fixing run, an ancestor-only head match, and a run newer than the pause event are all unaffected. No visual artifact applies - this change has no rendered UI surface; the end-user experience is CLI output and the watcher's triage log, both captured as transcripts.

title: fix(bin): report the condition each watcher and crew-state check actually tested
body:
## Intent Fix two state readouts in firstmate's own tooling that report a confident verdict they never verified. Both were observed live on 2026-08-02. They are the same failure mode - a check that INFERS a state instead of reporting the condition it actually tested - and the captain deliberately scoped them as ONE task so the fix is one idea rather than two unrelated patches. A reviewer should expect a single shared correction applied at two sites, not two independent bug fixes. DEFECT 1 - the watcher-down banner stated a false reason. bin/fm-guard.sh printed "WATCHER DOWN - SUPERVISION IS OFF / 3 task(s) in flight, but no watcher has a fresh beacon (last beat: 16s ago, grace 300s)." A 16s-old beacon is well inside a 300s grace, so the sentence contradicted its own numbers. fm_watcher_healthy rejects if EITHER the lock's pid is dead/absent/mismatched OR the beacon is stale, but the banner rendered its explanation purely from beacon age. bin/fm-watch.sh runs one poll cycle and EXITS after delivering an actionable wake, so during the entire wake-handling window the lock pid is legitimately absent - and the banner blamed the beacon. Fix 1a (the mandated minimum): the health check now records WHY it rejected. bin/fm-wake-lib.sh gained FM_WATCHER_UNHEALTHY_REASON (a stable token to branch on) and FM_WATCHER_UNHEALTHY_DETAIL (the clause a message prints verbatim), set by every rejecting condition: no-lock-pid, dead-pid, foreign-home, foreign-path, no-identity, unreadable-identity, identity-mismatch, stale-beacon. The banner now interpolates the condition that actually failed instead of inventing one. Fix 1b (the captain asked me to decide on the evidence and implement my recommendation, with the reasoning in the PR): I concluded a distinct THIRD state IS warranted, and implemented it. A clean cycle-exit awaiting re-arm is not the same state as a dead watcher, and the brief's binding constraint - the banner must never again claim supervision is off during a normal handoff - cannot be met by renaming the reason alone, because the HEADLINE itself must change. bin/fm-wake-lib.sh gained fm_watcher_clean_handoff, and bin/fm-guard.sh now reports healthy / handoff / down. The handoff state rests entirely on durable records the watcher ALREADY writes, with no change to how supervision runs: (1) the health check rejected on an EMPTY lock, which is the normal footprint of a cycle that ended because fm_lock_release runs on the way out, whereas a killed watcher leaves its lock behind with a dead pid; (2) the beacon is still inside the grace window; and (3) the last recorded watcher act in this home was a terminal delivery, i.e. mtime(.watch-deliveries.log) >= mtime(.last-watcher-beat). Point 3 is sound because of an ordering invariant the watcher already maintains: it touches the beacon at the TOP of every poll iteration and publishes the delivery ledger only immediately before exit, so a watcher that died mid-cycle published nothing and left the beacon strictly newer. Every constituent check fails toward ALARMING - an unwritable ledger, a missing ledger, or an unreadable mtime all still report a dead watcher. Approaches the captain explicitly FORBADE and that I did not take: widening the grace period, and suppressing the banner on a timer. A genuinely dead watcher must still alarm loudly and promptly. DEFECT 2 - a healthy run reported as failed, and the captain called this the more dangerous of the two because a false "failed" on live work invites stuck-crewmate recovery against a task that is fine. bin/fm-crew-state.sh reported "state: failed / source: run-step / run failed" for a task while no-mistakes axi status reported it running at the push step. nm_runs_status_for_branch walks the coarse newest-first runs list, and on a same-branch row whose recorded short-sha does not bind to the live worktree HEAD it CONTINUED walking into an OLDER same-branch row and reported that row's status. The captain's proposed rule - once the newest same-branch row is rejected on sha, no older same-branch row should be accepted at all, because any older row is by construction superseded work - I verified against the code and confirmed correct. The fix is one line: an unbindable newest same-branch row now returns nothing (fall back to the pane/status reading) rather than falling through. The captain explicitly warned against "fixing" this by deleting the sha identity check, and I did not - the identity check is retained and is exactly what makes the newest row the only candidate. VERIFICATION DISCIPLINE THE CAPTAIN REQUIRED, and which explains several test choices in the diff: every reproduction was written FIRST and proven to FAIL against current main before any fix was made, and all reproductions are kept as permanent regression tests. Both true-positive directions were mandatory and are covered: test_banner_still_blames_a_genuinely_stale_beacon and test_vanished_watcher_still_alarms_at_the_same_beacon_age prove the guard still alarms on a genuinely dead watcher, and test_genuinely_failed_newest_row_still_reports_failed proves crew state still reports a genuinely failed run as failed. test_handoff_whose_rearm_never_came_escalates_to_the_full_banner proves the new soft state cannot become a permanent excuse. tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh drives the REAL bin/fm-watch.sh to a real actionable cycle exit and then runs the REAL bin/fm-guard.sh against it, so the handoff premise is proven end-to-end against the live processes rather than by code reading or fixtures alone. tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh gained test_hook_blocks_on_a_clean_cycle_exit_awaiting_rearm to pin that the softer pull-guard reading does NOT leak into the turn-end block decision - at a turn boundary an un-rearmed watcher is still no supervision. EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE by the captain's instruction: the bin/fm-teardown.sh transient 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel:' empty-return. CONSTRAINTS the captain set and that the diff honors: do not change the watcher's cycle-and-exit design, do not change the Stop-hook re-arm path, do not change grace defaults. None of those changed - the diff changes only what a check REPORTS, never how supervision runs. TWO FILES THE ORIGINAL BRIEF DID NOT NAME, which the captain reviewed and explicitly approved keeping: bin/fm-watch-arm.sh and bin/fm-push-transition-lib.sh each lost a duplicate definition of WATCH_DELIVERY_LOG/WATCH_DELIVERY_LOCK (2 insertions / 2 deletions each) in favor of the single owner in bin/fm-wake-lib.sh. This is firstmate's one-owner rule from the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill: three definitions of one path is worse than a two-file diff. I proved to the captain this does not change arm/re-arm behavior - byte-identical resolved paths, no STATE reassignment in either file, and the arm and watcher-lock suites green. A DELIBERATE BEHAVIORAL DELTA THE CAPTAIN REQUIRED BE CALLED OUT RATHER THAN SHIPPED SILENTLY: consolidating the ledger path gave it the same \${VAR:-default} form as every sibling path in bin/fm-wake-lib.sh, so an ambient exported WATCH_DELIVERY_LOG is now honored where the old unconditional assignment ignored it. Nothing in bin/ or tests/ sets it. The captain asked for this widening to be stated explicitly in the PR description and for a test pinning that an exported value is honored - both are done. Writing that test exposed a real bug in my own first cut: the accessor re-derived the DEFAULT path and ignored the override, which would have split the publisher from its readers and re-created this branch's exact false alarm through the config surface the same change opened. The accessor now answers with WATCH_DELIVERY_LOG for this home so publisher and readers move together, and test_delivery_ledger_override_moves_publisher_and_reader_together pins both halves against the real watcher and the real guard. Docs: docs/turnend-guard.md and docs/architecture.md gained one-line cross-references for the three-state distinction under the one-owner rule, plus updated regression-coverage sentences. bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh passes. Repo conventions that are deliberate and should not be flagged: one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash rather than em dash, no agent co-author on commits, and bin/fm-lint.sh (pinned shellcheck 0.11.0) is the single owner of the lint definition - it passes with exit 0. Known host condition, not a code defect: this machine is running at load average 14-17 from concurrent sessions. tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh is flaky here and failed with a DIFFERENT test on each of three runs, two of which were on unmodified main with my changes reverted. tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh's test_no_timeout_uses_perl_bound also failed once in a parallel run purely on wall-clock starvation; it passes in isolation on the current code, and the crew-state change can only make that lookup return EARLIER, never add calls. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh` now records why the watcher health check rejected, via `FM_WATCHER_UNHEALTHY_REASON` (a stable token) and `FM_WATCHER_UNHEALTHY_DETAIL` (the printable clause) set by every rejecting condition - no-lock-pid, dead-pid, foreign-home, foreign-path, no-identity, unreadable-identity, identity-mismatch, stale-beacon - and adds `fm_watcher_clean_handoff`, which recognizes a cycle-exit awaiting re-arm from durable records the watcher already writes: an empty lock (`fm_lock_release` ran on the way out), a beacon still inside grace, and `mtime(.watch-deliveries.log) >= mtime(.last-watcher-beat)` from the watcher's existing beacon-first/ledger-last ordering. Every constituent check fails toward alarming, so an unwritable, missing, or unreadable ledger still reports a dead watcher. - `bin/fm-guard.sh` reports three states instead of two - healthy / handoff / down - interpolating the condition that actually failed rather than always blaming beacon age. `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` stops walking past a rejected newest same-branch row: when the newest row's recorded short-sha does not bind to the live worktree HEAD it now returns nothing and falls back to the pane/status reading, instead of reporting a superseded older row's status. The sha identity check is retained. Watcher cycle-and-exit design, the Stop-hook re-arm path, and grace defaults are unchanged - only what a check reports moved. - `bin/fm-watch-arm.sh` and `bin/fm-push-transition-lib.sh` drop their duplicate `WATCH_DELIVERY_LOG`/`WATCH_DELIVERY_LOCK` definitions in favor of the single owner in `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh`. **Deliberate behavioral delta:** the consolidated path takes the same `${VAR:-default}` form as its siblings, so an ambient exported `WATCH_DELIVERY_LOG` is now honored where the old unconditional assignment ignored it; nothing in `bin/` or `tests/` sets it, and the accessor answers with that value so publisher and readers move together. New regression tests cover both true-positive directions (a genuinely stale beacon and a vanished watcher still alarm; a genuinely failed newest row still reports failed), a handoff whose re-arm never came escalating to the full banner, the exported-ledger-override case, and the turn-end hook still blocking on a clean cycle exit; `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh` drives the real `bin/fm-watch.sh` to an actionable cycle exit and then the real `bin/fm-guard.sh` against it. Docs gained cross-references for the three-state distinction plus a verification record. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change only alters what two state checks report, never how supervision runs: the handoff state rests on a verified ordering invariant in the live watcher (publish before lock release, beacon at poll top), every constituent check fails toward alarming, the turn-end block is explicitly pinned as unchanged, and the crew-state fix is a one-line narrowing that falls back to a strictly more honest source. ## Testing I ran the four suites the diff modifies (fm-guard-stale-banner, fm-crew-state, fm-watcher-lock, fm-turnend-guard) plus fm-watch-arm, fm-supervision-events and fm-documentation-audiences for the ledger-consolidation and docs edges, and all passed. I also copied the new tests into the base checkout and confirmed each new assertion fails there, backing the repro-first claim. title: feat: gate remote second mates on Herdr readiness
body:
## Intent

Extend bin/fm-remote-doctor.sh (shipped in PR #1623) into the readiness gate for remote second mates: it detects Herdr + the Aqua-scoped LaunchAgent + PATH/tools, gains an idempotent --fix for automatable gaps, and the remote lifecycle runs doctor -> --fix -> re-doctor before it provisions or launches. Remote second mates REQUIRE Herdr and fail closed without it.

LOCKED PRODUCT DECISIONS (captain, 2026-08-03/04 - do not reopen or re-litigate; a finding that challenges one should be answered by pointing at the decision):
1. Remote second mates REQUIRE Herdr and fail closed. Local second mates are unchanged (tmux/herdr/etc. still fine).
2. The doctor detects Herdr + an Aqua-scoped LaunchAgent setup + related PATH/tools and flags gaps.
3. doctor --fix addresses ALL automatable gaps (LaunchAgent install/load when possible, PATH/entrypoint shims if in scope, start Herdr when a GUI session allows). It does NOT silently perform human-only steps.
4. Human-only gaps (auto-login, first console login, Claude/Codex /login, keychain password, FileVault) MUST be communicated clearly with exact operator actions - never silent, never claimed as fixed.
5. Primary flow on remote seed AND on relaunch/liveness recovery: doctor check -> doctor --fix -> re-doctor -> only then provision/launch. The operator should not have to babysit LaunchAgents.
6. Keep ONE doctor owner - deliberately no separate fm-remote-session-ensure.sh script.
7. SSH cannot create an Aqua GUI session from nothing - a headless/no-GUI host is a clearly-communicated human gap, not a silent failure.

WHAT WAS BUILT AND WHY, including decisions a reviewer reading only the diff would not know:

A. bin/fm-remote-doctor.sh keeps its #1623 PATH and required/optional tool reporting and extends the same simple line protocol rather than redesigning it. New lines: mode=, platform=, one 'check <name>=ok|skip|fixable:|human:' line per check, 'fix <name>=applied|failed:' lines under --fix, and one 'action: <name>: <exact operator step>' line per remaining gap. Checks: herdr resolves on the entrypoint PATH (human gap - Firstmate deliberately does not download or vendor herdr); Aqua GUI login session via launchctl print gui/<uid> (best effort); the Firstmate-owned launch agent; its LimitLoadToSessionType=Aqua scope; whether it is loaded into gui/<uid>; herdr server reachability for session 'default'; and the ~/.local/bin entrypoint symlink. Any remaining fixable or human gap exits non-zero. jq was added to REQUIRED_TOOLS because the Herdr backend genuinely needs it; that intentionally changes the base doctor contract from #1623 and tests were updated accordingly.

B. Chosen and documented stable identity: label dev.firstmate.herdr at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.firstmate.herdr.plist, named in the script header and docs/remote-secondmates.md. The plist runs the resolved absolute herdr binary with 'server --session default', LimitLoadToSessionType=Aqua, RunAtLoad, KeepAlive, and a log under ~/Library/Logs. The Aqua-scope check is a whitespace-insensitive read of the plist Firstmate itself owns (no plutil/defaults dependency, so it works on any host).

C. --fix is idempotent and re-derives every check from the host after repairing, so what it prints is the state AFTER repair, never the intent of one; a second --fix on a healthy host writes nothing and does not re-bootstrap. It refuses the dangerous actions by never attempting them: it never writes kcpassword or any auto-login password, never changes FileVault, never stores an account password, and never overwrites an operator-owned ~/.local/bin/fm-remote-entrypoint.sh that is not Firstmate's own symlink (that case is reported as a human gap on purpose). On Darwin the launch agent owns the server, so a stopped server is restarted through launchd rather than by starting a stray server outside the Aqua session; only a host with no launch agent (e.g. Linux) starts it directly.

D. The doctor sources the existing herdr adapter (bin/fm-backend.sh + bin/backends/herdr.sh) for session-scoped invocation and for starting the server, so bin/backends/herdr.sh stays the single owner of those mechanics rather than the doctor restating them. SCRIPT_DIR is resolved with shell builtins only, deliberately, so a host missing a required tool still reaches the report that names it instead of dying on a bare PATH.

E. New bin/fm-remote-readiness-lib.sh owns the check -> --fix -> re-check sequence once, because two callers need it (fm-remote-home-seed.sh and fm-spawn.sh's remote route) and duplicating the sequence would drift. This is NOT the separate session-ensure script decision 6 forbids: it holds no checks, no repairs and no messages, only the caller-side ordering, and the doctor remains the single owner. It returns 255 distinctly so SSH-unknown completion preserves the route instead of reading as a refusal.

F. Wiring: fm-remote-home-seed.sh's existing preflight now runs the full sequence and fails with the doctor's own remaining-gap text. fm-spawn.sh's spawn_remote_secondmate runs the same gate before publishing anything or transferring inherited material, and prints its one-line summary BEFORE the doctor text specifically because the startup liveness sweep reports only the first line. Liveness/recovery relaunch deliberately gets the gate for free because bin/fm-bootstrap.sh already respawns a dead or missing remote secondmate through fm-spawn.sh --secondmate; no new relaunch point was invented, per the brief.

G. Herdr is now required as the remote second mate's actual backend, not merely as host readiness: fm-spawn's remote route forces backend=herdr and refuses an explicit different --backend, and fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh's launch refuses any selection other than herdr, so neither side can drop the requirement. The remote home's own config/backend still governs the workers that second mate supervises; only the second-mate agent itself is pinned. Orca and cmux remain unsupported for secondmate, unchanged.

H. Tests are behavioral and never assert implementation source text. New tests/fm-remote-doctor.test.sh drives the real doctor against a controlled account fixture: a private HOME, a fake uname selecting the platform under test, a state-backed fake launchctl that refuses bootstrap without a GUI session exactly as launchd does, a fake herdr, and a fully isolated PATH so a 'no herdr' fixture is genuinely herdr-free. It asserts the emitted line protocol and observable effects, including that recording fdesetup/security/defaults stubs are never invoked and that no kcpassword or loginwindow preference is ever written. The remote lifecycle e2e now answers the readiness gate at its SSH fixture boundary on purpose, because the real doctor there would inspect and repair the RUNNER's own Mac account; it asserts the caller-side check/--fix/re-check call sequence and fail-closed behavior instead, and tests/fm-remote-doctor.test.sh owns the doctor's real behavior.

I. Consequence of decision 1 that was accepted, not overlooked: forcing herdr meant the two remote e2e suites could no longer launch on their existing fake-tmux fixture, so tests/remote-herdr-fixture.sh adds a shared stateful fake Herdr CLI modelling the workspace/tab/pane/agent facts the adapter reads (same verified behaviors as tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh's stateful fake, plus the pane IO a real launch performs). That is why those two test files change substantially. The remote lifecycle suite got slower as a result (roughly 13s to 60s standalone) because the Herdr adapter makes many more calls per operation than tmux did; this cost was accepted deliberately and reported to the captain rather than avoided by weakening the requirement.

J. Docs: docs/remote-secondmates.md gained a readiness/repair/human-steps section naming the launch agent label and path, what --fix does versus the human steps, and the honest statement that the doctor's behavior against a genuine Mac account remains an operator smoke test since CI only exercises fixtures; docs/scripts.md, docs/herdr-backend.md (one-line cross-reference), docs/verification/trace-context.md, and the secondmate-provisioning skill were updated. AGENTS.md was deliberately NOT changed - the brief asked to avoid bloating it and the facts have owners elsewhere.

K. Repo conventions followed: shellcheck-clean via bin/fm-lint.sh, one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never em dash, no agent name as commit co-author, tests colocated in tests/ and registered in bin/fm-test-run.sh's secondmate family.

Out of scope by explicit instruction: creating ~/fm-homes on the mini, requiring Herdr for LOCAL second mates, implementing macOS auto-login inside --fix, and the MacBook primary-migration cutover.

## What Changed

- Expand the remote doctor to detect Herdr, Aqua LaunchAgent, tool, server, and entrypoint readiness, with idempotent repairs and explicit operator actions for human-only gaps.
- Gate remote provisioning, launch, and recovery on a check-fix-recheck sequence, and require Herdr as the remote second-mate backend while leaving local second mates unchanged.
- Add behavioral doctor and lifecycle fixtures, register the new coverage, and document the readiness and repair workflow.

The constituent program PRs #8 through #14 merged into `program-integration` without individual review rounds by design. The repository workflows run only for PRs targeting `main`, so this PR is the program's single review gate and receives the full no-mistakes pass followed by the review ladder.

- A work-stage model with transition emission.
- Captain-ruling detection outside chat.

- Pending-decisions generation.
- Linear projection of Firstmate work.
- The complete decision round trip from the captain queue to routed work.

This branch contains seven commits, one for each program increment represented by #8 through #14. No constituent PR reported repository workflow checks because they targeted `program-integration`; CI begins here against `main`.

title: fix: reclaim leaked Treehouse leases safely
body:
## Summary

Treehouse lease recovery is implemented and committed on `fm/worktree-lease-reclaim-w9` at `ab7e3a0b`.
The branch was rebased onto current `origin/main` commit `69182d1b`, including resolution of the teardown-suite conflict without dropping the original recovery cases or main's newer cases.
Six dead-task leases were returned without force after proving clean worktrees, zero stashes, exact task ownership, and remote reachability; their original commits remain reachable and no task lost work.
The legacy production pools gained six available slots in total: Firstmate gained three, Relvino gained one, ruby-b2c-app gained one, and ruby-b2c-frontend gained one.
Failed spawns now attempt a lease-owner-checked non-forcing rollback, session start reports bounded per-pool low-water diagnostics, and the new reaper refuses live endpoints, dirty or work-shaped ignored files, misleading holders, unsupported task kinds, unprovable PR state, and open PRs discovered either from metadata or the branch itself.
The recovered review chain is contained in the rebased branch, including the tri-state landing and teardown fixes that distinguish conservative safety refusal from operational failure.

## What changed

`bin/fm-spawn.sh` now rolls back every post-acquisition abort path through the safe Treehouse return boundary.
The rollback re-proves the exact `firstmate-<task-id>` lease while holding the checkout lock and invokes `treehouse return .` with closed stdin; a dirty or changed lease is retained for inspection rather than forced.

`bin/fm-treehouse-reap.sh` adds two operator paths.
`capacity` performs a bounded scan of both the active home's pools and `~/.treehouse`, counts only clean unleased slots as available, and labels pools below the default 50 percent threshold as `LOW`.
`reap --auto` considers every ship task with metadata because status files are wake-event history, not current-state or liveness evidence; both automatic and explicit recovery require exact metadata-to-worktree identity, exact lease ownership, endpoint absence, no open PR, strict raw cleanliness, no stash, and the ordinary landed-work proof before a non-forcing return.
Open PR discovery checks both `worktree_git_ref` and the actual attached branch, closing the legacy-metadata gap observed during the live recovery.
The final endpoint and PR proofs run again under the checkout lock after the slower local scans, so a task that revives or gains an open PR cannot be released on a stale earlier observation.

`bin/fm-teardown.sh --reap-dead` supplies the authoritative teardown proof and repeats endpoint, identity, cleanliness, stash, and landing checks under the checkout lock immediately before release.
It reconciles metadata when Treehouse was already returned and treats an already-absent task temp directory as successful cleanup.
Ignored files are inventoried and summarized on every release path; known dependency, build, cache, and coverage output may pass, while drafts, notes, reports, docs/data/skill-shaped content, recent hand-edited-looking files, and ambiguous inventory are named and retained.
Safety refusals use a dedicated tri-state result that `fm-treehouse-reap.sh` treats as a successful conservative pass, while broken inspection, publication, locking, and landing machinery remains an operational error.
`bin/fm-report-stack.mjs` accepts a bounded lock-wait override for explicit maintenance so report publication can safely queue behind a busy overnight fleet.

`bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` runs only the bounded read-only capacity check at session start and emits `TREEHOUSE_CAPACITY` diagnostics in the existing bootstrap style.
The bootstrap diagnostic skill explains how to handle low and unavailable results and explicitly rejects pool-size increases as a substitute for leak repair.

The live releases were:

| Pool and slot | Task | Preserved original HEAD | Proof after return |
|---|---|---|---|
| `~/.treehouse/firstmate-21f368/6` | `fm-main-green-g7` | `923164a161d6640c741a9db540db32550e90d573` | `origin/fm/fm-main-green-g7` contains HEAD |
| `~/.treehouse/firstmate-21f368/7` | `ci-shard-behavior-tests-c5` | `f7d16e22a94cb1a83ea6df8e8219d5ecadfc0d32` | remote branches contain HEAD; PR 56 merged |
| `~/.treehouse/firstmate-21f368/10` | `test-isolation-seal-t3` | `fb54e5d0b2d1b16c9491edf0d868d1c75662c288` | `origin/fm/test-isolation-seal-t3-fresh-0731` contains HEAD |
| `~/.treehouse/relvino-90e018/15` | `frontend-correction-specs` | `a6e55c5f4e9857bcc1d3bd30463f3378a1e3ad36` | `origin/fm/frontend-correction-specs` contains HEAD and the durable report remains |
| `~/.treehouse/ruby-b2c-app-4adbed/1` | `b2c-activation-api-v1` | `924801d4650ed686b8f79961a5008fdf3cfb2dae` | `origin/fm/b2c-activation-api-v1-final-20260731` contains HEAD and the durable report remains |
| `~/.treehouse/ruby-b2c-frontend-5c0665/1` | `b2c-desktop-owner-o2` | `512f23b5dcbb7cb0e39d15f2fc1cf34671c1e757` | remote branch contains HEAD; PR 63 merged |

The Relvino and ruby-b2c-app open-PR tasks were clean and remote-contained, so their one-time incident releases met the delegated recovery authority and lost no work.
The final automated reaper is more conservative: the live exercise exposed their missing `pr=` metadata, so branch-derived open-PR discovery was added and regression-tested before commit.

## Verification

The observed legacy production capacity changed as follows:

| Pool | Before | After | Current detail |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `~/.treehouse/firstmate-21f368` | 7 available | 10 available | 16 recorded slots, 4 leased, 2 dirty, threshold 8 |
| `~/.treehouse/relvino-90e018` | 10 available | 11 available | 16 recorded slots, 2 leased, 3 dirty, threshold 8 |
| `~/.treehouse/ruby-b2c-app-4adbed` | 0 available | 1 available | 1 recorded slot, none leased or dirty |
| `~/.treehouse/ruby-b2c-frontend-5c0665` | 0 available | 1 available | 1 recorded slot, none leased or dirty |
| `~/.treehouse/firstmate-7bab20` | 1 available | 1 available | unchanged and healthy |
| `~/.treehouse/ruby-b2c-app-b3376f` | 1 available | 1 available | unchanged and healthy |

The replacement-worker read-only capacity exercise on 2026-08-04 found the recovered legacy pools had improved further: Firstmate was 12/16 available with two leases and two dirty slots, Relvino was 13/16 with no leases and three dirty slots, and all three one-slot legacy B2C pools were fully available.
All six slots released during the incident recovery still had no lease holder.
Each preserved original HEAD remained reachable from the remote-tracking branches named in the release table, which re-proved that no released task lost work.

The active home-managed pools were also scanned on 2026-08-04: Firstmate was 2/13 available with 11 current leases, Relvino 4/14 with 10 current leases, ruby-b2c-app-4adbed 1/2, and ruby-b2c-app-b3376f 1/1.
The new diagnostic reports the Firstmate and Relvino active-home pools as `LOW`, so this pressure is visible at session start and can be routed through the conservative automatic reaper before any pool-size decision.

All 32 historical scratch pools were reported explicitly: 31 are unleased but dirty and one is leased under `firstmate-cm1` with a broken Git registration and no matching live-home task identity.
None was modified.

The focused verification passed:

- checkout return boundary traversal and low-file-descriptor tests;
- backlog refusal before worktree acquisition, including the missing-row regression;
- spawn freshness rollback, remote-free local-only behavior, dirty-acquisition retention, and transaction rollback;
- session-start low-capacity diagnostic coverage;
- dead-task reaping for clean remote-reachable work, already-returned reconciliation, dirty and live-endpoint refusals, exact-holder mismatch, open PRs with and without recorded metadata, unsupported scouts, and capacity classification;
- stale `working` status with a dead endpoint is reclaimed by `--auto`, while the same status with a live endpoint remains held;

body:
## Intent

The captain requires every completed pull request to receive an immediate manual retrospective before review or merge: ask every materially involved worker how the work could have been completed faster and more effectively without weakening safety, verify the claims, and distill only reusable evidence-backed improvements into the authoritative AGENTS.md, skill, script, test, documentation, or private preference owner. This must be part of finishing the PR rather than ordinary backlog debt, while a truthful no-op remains valid. Do not mutate an already-validated PR; use an immediate separate delivery when tracked changes are justified. Preserve Firstmate's project-write, merge-authority, no-mistakes, visual-review, one-owner, and safety boundaries. Implement the policy now in Firstmate's shared instructions and an internal trigger-specific skill, with no script because no deterministic mechanic is justified yet.

## What Changed

- Adds the internal, agent-only `.agents/skills/post-pr-retrospective/SKILL.md`: it defines the bounded question asked of every material worker over its verified `harness-adapters` send path, covers unreachable contributors (torn-down scouts, replaced workers, automated validation steps) from their recorded artifacts instead of relaunching them, sets a five-condition evidence bar before an answer counts as a reusable improvement, and defers to AGENTS.md section 6 for destination routing while adding only the retrospective-specific rules (script plus regression test, skill plus one load trigger, `firstmate-coding-guidelines` before shared tracked material, a project's `AGENTS.md` written only by a crewmate via `bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh`, chronology stays in the report).
- Wires the policy into `AGENTS.md`: section 7's PR-ready path now requires loading the skill and completing its routing before presenting or merging a ready PR, with a truthful no-op allowed but ordinary backlog deferral disallowed, and section 13 gains the matching non-captain-invocable load trigger. The skill keeps the already-validated PR unmutated by routing justified tracked changes into an immediate separate delivery that only has to be initiated, not merged, before presentation.
- Classifies the new skill as `agent-runtime` in `docs/documentation-audiences.json`, which `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` and `tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` require for every tracked prose surface. One review info note remains open: the skill's frontmatter description still says "PR recap" where the body and AGENTS.md now name section 7's PR-ready captain report. The Test phase flagged `tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh` as a pre-existing machine-local flake unrelated to these three files.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is instruction-only and well-bounded, the blocking documentation-inventory failure is fixed and verified by set comparison, and every boundary-wording concern now matches AGENTS.md sections 1, 6, and 7, leaving only a one-line terminology leftover in the skill's frontmatter.

## Testing

Ran the repo's own change-based selection (28 pure-contract-unit scripts) plus the directly relevant documentation-audience suite, then proved the actual intent with real-harness transcripts rather than assertions on instruction bytes, which this repo's coding guidelines explicitly forbid: an isolated `claude` session loaded with the tracked AGENTS.md and skills invoked `Skill(post-pr-retrospective)` as its first move at the PR-ready moment, quoted the section 7 trigger, and sequenced ask-workers, artifact-only coverage for the torn-down scout, verification, immediate routing, recap, and merge-waits-for-captain; the same prompt against the base commit produced no retrospective and stated no skill was triggered. GBrain local reranker verification

This record captures the local GPU reranker that story #6 can configure without rediscovering the runtime, model, endpoint, or request contract.
The evidence below was refreshed on 2026-08-04 on the four-GPU RTX 5060 Ti host.

Pinned deployment

The artifact source is ggml-org/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-Q8_0-GGUF.
The serving source is ggml-org/llama.cpp.

Runtime selection and build

The llama.cpp b10252 release had no official Linux CUDA binary, and its official Linux Vulkan binary found no NVIDIA device because this host has no NVIDIA Vulkan ICD manifest.
The deployed runtime therefore uses nixpkgs' maintained CUDA build rather than Ollama's CPU-only bundled server or an ad hoc CMake build.
The pinned nixpkgs expression reproduces the installed result:

NIXPKGS_ALLOW_UNFREE=1 nix build --impure \
  --out-link "$HOME/.local/share/gbrain-reranker/runtime" \
  --expr 'let
    pkgs = (builtins.getFlake "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/241313f4e8e508cb9b13278c2b0fa25b9ca27163").legacyPackages.x86_64-linux;
  in pkgs.llama-cpp.override { cudaSupport = true; }'

The command resolved to the package result recorded above when repeated with --no-link --print-out-paths.
The build log reported CUDA compiler /nix/store/s449s8l8qwi5vikvnvmnrbj2ynyq8597-cuda12.9-cuda_nvcc-12.9.86/bin/nvcc, CUDA 12.9.86, and GNU 14.3.0 as the CUDA host compiler.
The Nix CUDA setup hook supplied the split toolkit outputs through CUDAToolkit_ROOT and CUDAToolkit_INCLUDE_DIR, which avoids treating the standalone cuda_nvcc output as a conventional complete toolkit.
The resolved discovery inputs were:

Service contract

The enabled user unit is ~/.config/systemd/user/gbrain-reranker.service.
User lingering is enabled, so default.target activation persists across host boots without a system-level unit or sudo.
The unit pins the GPU by UUID with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, loads the CUDA backend explicitly with GGML_BACKEND_PATH, and exposes the host driver through a directory containing only a libcuda.so.1 symlink.
The server is launched with --reranking --offline --no-webui --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8081 --ctx-size 4096 --batch-size 512 --ubatch-size 512 --parallel 1 --n-gpu-layers 999.
The service uses Restart=on-failure, a two-second restart delay, a startup HTTP health probe, journal output, and a 200-message-per-30-second log rate limit.

Story #6 should configure GBrain with:

gbrain config set provider_base_urls.llama-server-reranker http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1
gbrain config set search.reranker.model llama-server-reranker:qwen3-reranker-0.6b-q8_0
gbrain config set search.reranker.enabled true

The model alias is explicit and does not depend on a serving catalog shorthand.

title: fix(pi): isolate worker launches from primary extensions
body:
## Intent

Fix the reproduced Pi/Firstmate isolation defect where a Firstmate-launched Pi or pi-signed ship worker or scout running inside an isolated worktree of the Firstmate repository is trusted by Pi and therefore auto-discovers the repository's tracked primary Pi extensions in addition to its task-specific worker extension. The expected runtime behavior is deterministic: workers and scouts must load only worker-scoped lifecycle behavior, including their task-specific turn-end and busy-state reporting, while tracked primary Pi extensions remain active for genuine main Firstmate primaries and persistent secondmate primaries launched through the documented entry points. The fix must be enforced in runtime code, not by relying on worker instructions or refusing project trust, must cover both pi and pi-signed, and must not alter other runtime adapters except where a shared identity marker is deliberately owned.

The diagnostic intent accepted for the implementation was to reproduce the worker path through the public launcher or closest executable harness, separate the initiating trigger, masking condition, and visible symptom, compare worker launch environment against genuine-primary launch identity, identify the earliest reliable identity boundary, test the counterfactual where only primary extension behavior is disabled for workers while task-specific turn-end reporting remains active, and seek disconfirming evidence across Pi, pi-signed, Firstmate-repository workers, ordinary project workers, and secondmate primaries.

Acceptance intent for the regression coverage and docs: primary Pi extensions must refuse or no-op under a positively identified ship/scout direct-report context without weakening genuine primary or secondmate supervision; fm-spawn must mark Pi and pi-signed ship/scout launches before Pi starts and must not mark secondmate primary launches; executable tests must cover a Firstmate-repository linked worktree worker case with leaked primary root override, genuine primary controls, pi and pi-signed ship/scout/secondmate launch construction, and task-specific worker extension turn-end/busy-state behavior; authoritative supervision/session-start/watcher docs and verification evidence must be updated without duplicating contracts.

During no-mistakes review, the captain approved fixing the missing signed-Pi scout launch regression coverage, so the accepted intent includes adding executable coverage for the pi-signed scout direct-report launch marker path alongside the existing pi and secondmate controls. The approved validated push target is the DDay-FG/firstmate fork while the upstream project remains kunchenguid/firstmate.

## What Changed

- Updated `fm-spawn` to mark Pi and pi-signed ship/scout launches before Pi starts, without marking secondmate primary launches.
- Expanded regression tests and supervision docs to cover Firstmate worktree isolation, leaked primary-root overrides, pi/pi-signed launch markers, genuine primary controls, and secondmate primary behavior.

title: fix: resolve detached Codex hooks through Herdr pane identity
body:
## What changed

Add a narrowly scoped Herdr fallback for Firstmate session-lock ownership when a Codex project hook runs in a detached helper process.

## Root cause

Codex 0.146.0 can execute the Firstmate hook without a parent-process path back to the Codex process. The existing lock implementation only trusted ancestry, so `fm-lock.sh` reported `cannot locate harness process in ancestry` and correctly forced the Firstmate home into read-only mode, even though Codex was the active foreground agent in the exact Herdr pane.

## Fix

When ordinary ancestry resolution finds no harness, and only when Herdr has injected `HERDR_ENV=1` and `HERDR_PANE_ID`, query `herdr pane process-info` and accept a foreground native Codex process as the lock identity. Non-Herdr sessions retain the existing fail-closed ancestry behavior. Added a regression test for the detached Codex hook shape.

## Validation

- `tests/fm-session-lock-ancestry.test.sh` — all tests pass, including the new detached Codex/Herdr case.
- Live WSL/Herdr validation with Codex 0.146.0 and Herdr 0.7.5: `fm-lock.sh` acquired the lock and `fm-session-start.sh` entered the locked path.
- `bash -n` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Full ShellCheck lint was unavailable because ShellCheck is not installed in the test environment.
- The broader session-start test has an unrelated OpenCode fixture failure (`exit 127`) because OpenCode is not installed.

Evidence: Rendered maintainer verification page ```text GBrain local reranker verification

GBrain local reranker verification

This record captures the local GPU reranker that GBrain can use without rediscovering the runtime, model, endpoint, or request contract. The evidence below was refreshed on 2026-08-04 on the four-GPU RTX 5060 Ti host.

Runtime selection and build

The llama.cpp b10252 release had no official Linux CUDA binary, and its official Linux Vulkan binary found no NVIDIA device because this host has no NVIDIA Vulkan ICD manifest. The deployed runtime therefore uses nixpkgs' maintained CUDA build rather than Ollama's CPU-only bundled server or an ad hoc CMake build. The pinned nixpkgs expression reproduces the installed result:

NIXPKGS_ALLOW_UNFREE=1 nix build --impure \
  --out-link "$HOME/.local/share/gbrain-reranker/runtime" \
  --expr 'let
    pkgs = (builtins.getFlake "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/241313f4e8e508cb9b13278c2b0fa25b9ca27163").legacyPackages.x86_64-linux;
  in pkgs.llama-cpp.override { cudaSupport = true; }'

The command resolved to the package result recorded above when repeated with --no-link --print-out-paths. The build log reported CUDA compiler /nix/store/s449s8l8qwi5vikvnvmnrbj2ynyq8597-cuda12.9-cuda_nvcc-12.9.86/bin/nvcc, CUDA 12.9.86, and GNU 14.3.0 as the CUDA host compiler. The Nix CUDA setup hook supplied the split toolkit outputs through CUDAToolkit_ROOT and CUDAToolkit_INCLUDE_DIR, which avoids treating the standalone cuda_nvcc output as a conventional complete toolkit. The resolved discovery inputs were:

llama.cpp normalized architectures 120 and 121 to 120a and 121a, then completed all 720 build steps.

Service contract

The enabled user unit is ~/.config/systemd/user/gbrain-reranker.service. User lingering is enabled, so default.target activation persists across host boots without a system-level unit or sudo. The unit pins the GPU by UUID with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, loads the CUDA backend explicitly with GGML_BACKEND_PATH, and exposes the host driver through a directory containing only a libcuda.so.1 symlink. The server is launched with --reranking --offline --no-webui --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8081 --ctx-size 4096 --batch-size 512 --ubatch-size 512 --parallel 1 --n-gpu-layers 999. The service uses Restart=on-failure, a two-second restart delay, a startup HTTP health probe, journal output, and a 200-message-per-30-second log rate limit.

GBrain v0.40.6.1 or newer is required because that release added the llama-server-reranker recipe. Configure GBrain with:

gbrain config set provider_base_urls.llama-server-reranker http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1
gbrain config set search.reranker.model llama-server-reranker:qwen3-reranker-0.6b-q8_0
gbrain config set search.reranker.enabled true

The model alias is explicit and does not depend on a serving catalog shorthand.

Endpoint checks

The startup health probe and an operator check use:

curl --fail --silent http://127.0.0.1:8081/health

The fixed ordering fixture uses:

curl --fail --silent --show-error http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3-reranker-0.6b-q8_0",
    "query": "What is the capital city of France?",
    "documents": [
      "Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy in plants.",
      "The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth.",
      "Paris is the capital and largest city of France."
    ],
    "top_n": 3
  }'

The observed result correctly placed the relevant passage at index 2 first:

{
  "model": "qwen3-reranker-0.6b-q8_0",
  "results": [
    { "index": 2, "relevance_score": 0.995586633682251 },
    { "index": 1, "relevance_score": 0.000018410755728837103 },
    { "index": 0, "relevance_score": 0.000016911413695197552 }

}

GPU, recovery, and privacy evidence

nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=gpu_uuid,pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv,noheader reported:

<gpu-uuid>, <pid>, <home>/.local/share/gbrain-reranker/runtime/bin/llama-server, 1504 MiB

The process mappings contained the pinned libggml-cuda.so, CUDA driver 570.207, and CUDA 12.9 cuBLAS libraries. A user-service restart replaced the serving process while the unit remained enabled and the health endpoint returned {"status":"ok"}. Sending SIGKILL to the serving process caused systemd to replace it, increment NRestarts from 0 to 1, and restore both the health and ordering checks. After reranking, ss -anpt showed only the loopback listener for the serving process and no established remote socket. The server's --offline flag prevents runtime downloads or other network access, and the journal showed model loading from the local GGUF path only.
