title: fix(watch): retire vanished-pane tracking to stop phantom stale/wedge cycles
body:
## Intent

Fix the Firstmate watcher so panes that no longer exist on the backend and have no state/*.meta stop accruing stale timers and wedge escalations, with deterministic cleanup or ignoring of their pane-specific .hash-*, .count-*, .stale-*, .stale-since-*, .wedge-escalations-*, and pause records while live recorded panes remain completely unaffected. Root-cause and reproduce the real stale-loop teardown race first, then add colocated regression coverage that removes a pane mid-escalation and proves there are no further phantom wakes, plus a live stale-pane control that still escalates normally. Also cover the related signal-grace teardown residue: deleted .status and .turn-ended paths must not be surfaced after their snapshot sources vanish, and orphaned .seen-* and heartbeat suppression records must retire. Do not broadly kill shared watchers and do not drive real Herdr lifecycle behavior; use hermetic scratch/fake-backend coverage.

## What Changed

- Retire per-pane tracking state (`.hash-*`, `.count-*`, `.stale-*`, `.stale-since-*`, `.wedge-escalations-*`, pause records) in `bin/fm-watch.sh` once a pane no longer exists on the backend and has no `state/*.meta`, so phantom stale timers and duplicate wedge escalations stop accruing for panes that are actually gone, while live recorded panes are unaffected.
- Fix `prune_orphaned_signal_tracking` and `revalidate_signal_snapshot` to build the `.hb-surfaced-<task>` marker filename via the canonical `_hb_surfaced_path` helper (matching the `tr ':/.' '___'` transform used when the marker is written) instead of reconstructing it from the raw task id, so dotted task ids no longer have their live heartbeat-suppression marker wrongly deleted every main-loop cycle. Also retire orphaned `.seen-*` and heartbeat suppression records, and stop surfacing `.status`/`.turn-ended` after their signal-grace snapshot sources vanish.
- Add regression coverage in `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` for: a pane vanishing mid wedge-escalation (no phantom wake, all pane-keyed state retired, live-pane control still escalates), a dotted task-id `.hb-surfaced-*` marker surviving prune, and a vanished signal batch mid signal-grace sleep being retired cleanly.
- Document the pane-vanish stale/wedge/signal-grace retirement invariant in `docs/architecture.md`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The only change since the prior round is the requested fix — replacing the ad-hoc task-id-to-marker filename construction with the canonical _hb_surfaced_path helper and adding a colocated dotted-task-id regression test — which I independently verified with a standalone repro against the real functions, and the broader phantom-stale-pane fix remains well-tested and intent-conformant.

title: feat(herdr): enable presentation spaces by default
body:
## Intent

Flip Herdr's disposable per-task presentation workspace from OPT-IN to DEFAULT-ON, with an explicit opt-out. This is firstmate shared tracked material, so firstmate-coding-guidelines applies: one-owner rule, AGENTS.md size discipline, one sentence per line in Markdown, plain dash never an em dash, shellcheck-clean bin scripts, bin/fm-lint.sh before done, colocated tests. Add regression tests. This change alters LIVE fleet spawn behavior, so landing is timing-coordinated with the captain: drive it to CI-green and report the PR, do not expect immediate merge.

Prior mechanics: config/herdr-presentation-spaces was presence-based opt-IN (present = on, absent = off, flat default). Owner docs are docs/herdr-backend.md "Optional presentation spaces" and docs/configuration.md. Every reader had to be found before changing semantics; the known readers were the spawn presentation path (bin/fm-spawn.sh) and the secondmate inheritance/propagation path (secondmate-provisioning / fm-config-push / bootstrap convergence).

New semantics: presentation spaces ON by default; a home opts OUT explicitly. The opt-out mechanism had to be the cleanest one CONSISTENT with existing config conventions, and justified; the brief named content-based on/off defaulting to on when absent (like config/calm) or a distinct presence-based opt-out flag as candidates, and asked for the minimal, least-surprising design, escalating as an ask-user finding only if genuinely ambiguous.

Chosen design and justification (not ambiguous, so not escalated): a content value in the SAME config/herdr-presentation-spaces file. Absent file = on. Whole-file whitespace-stripped, case-folded value "off" = off; "on" = on; empty file = on; any other value warns to stderr and keeps the default on rather than failing a spawn over a purely visual setting. Three reasons: (1) it matches the repo's existing scalar-config convention and reuses the same whole-file whitespace-stripped parse used by config/backlog-backend and config/crew-harness, with config/calm already using on/off; (2) migration is automatic and one-directional because the historical opt-in was an empty touched file which still resolves to on, so no previously enabled home can be turned off and no migration sweep is needed; (3) inheritance becomes correct by construction rather than by item-specific special-casing.

Three non-trivial requirements, all handled:
1. Migration / no silent flip. An existing home that HAS the opt-in file wanted it ON and stays ON (empty file resolves on). A home that had it absent now becomes on by default; that flip is the INTENDED one and is documented deliberately in docs/herdr-backend.md rather than left accidental.
2. Inheritance/propagation. The config is inherited into secondmate homes and primary-ABSENT previously converged to REMOVING the destination copy (= off). Under default-on, absent means ON at BOTH ends, so the generic absence mirror in bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh already converges a secondmate to the primary's default-on instead of turning it off, and only an explicit primary "off" propagates the opt-out. The exact convergence was traced through fm-config-push and the bootstrap sweep and confirmed to need no logic change; that is why no item-specific propagation branch was added, and a regression asserts the RESOLVED verdict in the destination home rather than mere file presence. A secondmate can never end up off because the primary left the default.
3. Default-on safety. Presentation remains a best-effort visual projection and NEVER task or lifecycle authority; that contract is unchanged. The projection and cleanup paths were verified against real Herdr 0.8.0. Known rough edges default-on exposes are called out: on the projected-create path a failed journal publication or workspace create stops that spawn instead of falling back flat, so a Herdr create failure is now a visible spawn failure in every Herdr home rather than only opted-in ones (every earlier degradation - no session server, contended presentation lock, absent or ambiguous parent - still warns and continues flat); and recovery-path presentation lock contention is a deliberate hard refusal that default-on makes reachable from any Herdr home (one concurrent cross-home recovery case refused under machine load and passed on immediate rerun). The change is contained to the Herdr backend because no other runtime backend has a projection path.

Implementation decisions: the gate moved out of an inline `[ -f ... ]` test in bin/fm-spawn.sh into fm_backend_herdr_presentation_enabled in the Herdr adapter (bin/backends/herdr.sh), so the semantics have one owner that regressions can exercise through an executable interface. Docs updated to keep each config's authoritative semantics in its one owner: docs/herdr-backend.md renamed its section to "Presentation spaces" and owns accepted values, default, migration, and inheritance; docs/configuration.md and docs/architecture.md keep one-line cross-references updated to the new anchor; AGENTS.md's config line and journal pointer updated. A dated maintainer-verification entry was added to docs/verification/runtime-backends.md for the Herdr 0.8.0 protocol 19 projection-suite run.

Tests added, exercising real behavior rather than source text: tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh covers default-on when unset, the legacy empty opt-in file still resolving to on with no warning, explicit off (including whitespace and case variants), and an unrecognized value warning while keeping the default. tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh covers inheritance of BOTH default-on and explicit opt-out into a secondmate home through the real config-push convergence path, asserting the resolved verdict. The real-Herdr e2e (tests/fm-backend-herdr-presentation-e2e.test.sh) gained a real-spawn case proving an unconfigured home is projected by default, and its existing projected case now exercises the legacy empty opt-in file. Existing real-Herdr tests that assert the FLAT layout (launcher-workspace, workspace-per-home, backend-autodetect) now declare their opt-out explicitly instead of depending on a default that changed.

Verification already run locally: bin/fm-lint.sh clean, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh clean, the full changed-set suite (76 scripts) green, and the real-Herdr presentation suite green standalone on Herdr 0.8.0 (23 cases).

## What Changed

- Enable Herdr disposable presentation workspaces by default, with `off` as the explicit opt-out and invalid values warning while remaining enabled.
- Preserve legacy empty-file opt-ins and propagate default-on or explicit opt-out behavior consistently to secondmate homes.
- Update Herdr documentation and regression coverage for config parsing, inheritance, default projection, opt-out, and flat-layout scenarios.

title: fix(bin): abort parked runs and reap leaked processes before teardown
body:
## Intent

Harden bin/fm-teardown.sh's pre-teardown cleanup sequence with two intertwined fixes, delivered as one coordinated PR because both restructure what teardown does before it removes the worker.

Fix 1 - abort/conclude an active no-mistakes run before removing the worker: tearing down a task worker while its no-mistakes pipeline run is still PARKED at a gate (status stays running / parked awaiting_agent with no responsive agent) leaves an ORPHANED active run holding a fleet slot indefinitely. Observed twice on 2026-08-03 (a run parked 7h39m, and a run parked at a CI approval gate after the worker was cleaned post-CI-green), each requiring a manual no-mistakes axi abort --run <id> to reap. Fix: teardown (and the worker-cleanup path) must conclude or abort any active/parked no-mistakes run owned by this task before removing the worker, using the supported no-mistakes abort interface (no hand-manipulation of run state), only aborting a run this task owns and never touching another task's run. Preserve the existing landed-work/unlanded-work teardown safety exactly as-is (never force, never discard unlanded work) - this fix adds a cleanup step, it does not relax that gate. A run with an autonomous step still under way (running/fixing/ci, not parked at a gate) is intentionally left alone since no-mistakes drives those against its own gate-repo clone, not the crew's worktree, so they are not orphaned by removing the worktree - only genuinely gate-parked runs (awaiting_approval/fix_review/an awaiting_agent field/a gate field) with no terminal outcome are aborted. A bootstrap/heartbeat sweep that detects and reports orphaned runs fleet-wide was explicitly scoped OUT as a follow-up rather than included here, to keep this PR to the smaller teardown-scoped change.

Fix 2 - reap leaked descendant processes at teardown: a task's descendant processes can survive teardown and be orphaned to init (ppid=1), pinning CPU cores for hours/days. Observed 2026-08-03: two Go test binaries (branchsync.test 18.5h CPU, steps.test 92.6h CPU) with -test.timeout=10m blown past by ~100x, reparented to launchd, referenced by no live task meta. Fix: at teardown, reap the task's descendant/worktree-rooted processes rather than only clearing the agent endpoint, scoped precisely to this task's own worktree and per-task tasktmp root (both unique per task, never shared) via a process cwd scan (lsof -a -d cwd, not the slow recursive +D file-tree walk) so it can never kill another task's or the primary's processes. A bootstrap orphan-reaper sweep for pre-existing orphaned ppid=1 processes was explicitly scoped OUT as a follow-up, to keep this PR to the smaller teardown-scoped change.

Ordering and interaction: the run is concluded/aborted BEFORE the process reap and BEFORE the worker/worktree is removed, since a still-active run may own live processes. The whole pre-teardown sequence is idempotent and safe to re-run (a partial teardown that is retried converges: an already-aborted run reads back terminal and is skipped, and a process already reaped is simply absent from the recheck). Every existing teardown refusal (uncommitted/unlanded work) is kept exactly as-is.

Implementation: bin/fm-teardown.sh gained conclude_task_no_mistakes_run (Fix 1) and reap_task_worktree_processes (Fix 2), both called unconditionally (including under --force) right after every landed/discard-work safety refusal passes and before any worktree return, branch delete, or backend kill; skipped for kind=secondmate since that lifecycle is owned by separate machinery. The branch+code-identity run-attribution rule (used to prove a run belongs to this exact task) was factored out of bin/fm-crew-state.sh into a new shared bin/fm-nm-run-lib.sh so both scripts share one ownership contract instead of two copies that could drift and misattribute a run. Colocated regression tests in tests/fm-teardown.test.sh exercise the real teardown path (never matching source text): a task's own simulated parked run is aborted and a parked run on another branch is left untouched; a leaked descendant process under the worktree and under tasktmp are both reaped; and a combined test proves the causal ordering (abort and reap both complete before the destructive worktree return, verified via real process liveness and a call-log, not line-number correlation).

PR-body requirement: state plainly that this PR carries TWO independent-but-coupled teardown-hardening fixes (abort-active-run-before-reap and leaked-descendant-process reaping), so a later reverter knows reverting it undoes both.

## What Changed

- This PR carries two independent but coupled teardown fixes: abort a task-owned gate-parked no-mistakes run, then reap processes rooted under its worktree or tasktmp before removing the worker.
- Share branch and code-identity attribution between crew-state reporting and teardown, while leaving autonomous and other tasks’ runs untouched and refusing teardown when cleanup cannot be confirmed.
- Add executable teardown regressions covering run ownership, abort confirmation, process identity and convergence, and abort-before-reap-before-removal ordering.

## Accepted residual risk

Reviewed and consciously accepted rather than hardened further (stop-and-ship best-effort posture):

- **Abort is run-id-scoped, not fully atomic on live state.** `no-mistakes axi abort --run <id>` targets the exact verified run, but the CLI has no compare-and-cancel primitive conditioned on the run still being parked at the instant of the call. A run that autonomously resumes in the narrow window between our verification read and the abort call could still be cancelled. Closing this fully needs an upstream `no-mistakes` capability that does not exist today.
- **The initial run lookup stays fail-open.** A `no-mistakes` communication failure (timeout, daemon unreachable) reads the same as "no active run" rather than refusing teardown. Making a successful query a hard precondition for every ship-task teardown would expand this fix's blast radius fleet-wide - blocking teardown for tasks that never had an active run at all - well beyond its intended best-effort scope.
- **Forced secondmate child cleanup isn't covered yet.** `cleanup_firstmate_home_children` still removes a torn-down secondmate's own ship/scout children directly, without routing them through `conclude_task_no_mistakes_run`/`reap_task_worktree_processes`. Filed as a follow-up: `fm-teardown-secondmate-child-abort-reap-r1`.

Both code paths carry inline comments documenting the same rationale at the point of the tradeoff.

title: feat(bin): consolidate delivery verification, completeness gate, worklogs, and grounded briefs
body:
## Intent Consolidate every outstanding firstmate fix from seven open branches into ONE branch and ONE PR, so the captain's fork rebases onto a moving upstream once instead of seven times. He had just synced: origin/main was exactly level with upstream/main (cd73e75, 0 ahead 0 behind), and that clean base was the whole opportunity. The seven branches overlapped heavily and had to be untangled BY CONTENT, not by branch name. Four of them (feat-completeness-gate, feat-cross-repo-grounding, fm/fm-rebase-upstream, rebase-onto-upstream) turned out to be lineage variants of ONE feature - the Z3 completeness gate - across three separate SHA lineages, not four separate features. fm/fm-rebase-upstream even applies the same five gate commits TWICE on itself. So the result is five genuinely distinct fixes, delivered as six linear commits off current main with no merge commits: 1. fm-verify-delivered.sh and its false-clean fix (from fm/fm-verify-delivered-false-clean, PR #3). 'Inspected nothing' and 'search failed' are deliberately their own non-clean exit outcomes so an inspection that examined no files can never report clean. 2. Agent-maintained crewmate working log at data//log.md (from fm/crew-worklog, PR #4). Deliberately NOT the status file: status appends wake firstmate and must stay sparse, the log never wakes anything. 3. Timestamped status appends plus reported evidence age (from fm/status-timestamps). 4. The Z3 completeness gate (deduplicated from the four branches). 5. Per-repo ground truth injected into briefs (from feat-cross-repo-grounding, PR #1). DELIBERATE DECISIONS a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: Gate version chosen by content, not recency. Blob comparison showed feat-completeness-gate and fm/fm-rebase-upstream carry BYTE-IDENTICAL gate files (eabdd0c8/e3cdafdd/e90258bd), rebase-onto-upstream a near-identical third copy. feat-cross-repo-grounding's 9568dac won because it is the only lineage where invalid facts exit 64 and BLOCK - in the other three a typo or corrupted record falls through the engine's error path as a PASS - and it is the only one whose fm-merge-local.sh caller treats 64 as blocking. The one genuine content conflict, resolved deliberately, not papered over. Three branches fix the SAME bug (the gate false-blocking teardown of squash-merged work whose branch was deleted) three different ways. fm/fm-rebase-upstream's 4c0ba6f fixes it at the call site by splitting teardown's gate into a scout half before the bash landed check and a ship half after. rebase-onto-upstream's e3581a5 fixes it by deleting the gate's landedness derivation entirely. 9568dac fixes it in the gate while KEEPING the local-only derivation. I chose 9568dac: fixing it in the gate means every caller benefits (--gate merge and --gate done are callers too, not just teardown), and keeping the local-only derivation is intentional because local-only work has no PR to squash-merge, so plain git CAN correctly decide whether that branch is merged - that is what lets the gate block an unmerged local-only branch before fm-merge-local.sh runs. Two tests cover exactly that path. e3581a5's underlying one-owner argument is preserved: for remote-backed ship work the gate now defers COMPLETELY to fm-teardown.sh, which is what AGENTS.md hard rule 3 requires. 4c0ba6f's split is intentionally NOT carried, because with the gate no longer re-deriving remote-backed landedness it can no longer false-block, so a second call site would add a duplicate invocation that changes no outcome, and its call sites predate exit 64 so they would read invalid facts as a pass. PR #1 was explicitly evaluated, not silently included or dropped. The captain said it is 'out of date'. That describes the BRANCH (265 commits behind main, one failing check) and not the feature, which is the staleness this consolidation exists to remove. The ground-truth feature is coherent, additive, non-blocking, exists nowhere else, so it is included in its newest form (83feaff) and given the test coverage it never had. TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY DROPPED, both intentional: (a) bin/__pycache__/fm-completeness.cpython-313.pyc, a compiled build artifact committed on all four gate branches - it is generated output and main already gitignores it; (b) the .gitignore __pycache__/ addition from 9568dac, redundant because current main already carries both __pycache__/ and *.pyc. Nothing else from the seven branches is absent: the union of files those branches touch matches this branch exactly apart from those two. ADAPTATIONS forced by main's drift, all deliberate: the bootstrap capability line is emitted as 'BOOTSTRAP_INFO: completeness gate available' behind FM_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE_FACTS=1, matching main's current convention for a no-action capability fact (as tasks-axi does), instead of the source branches' unconditional 'COMPLETENESS_GATE: available' - this also avoids adding a new actionable diagnostic prefix. README toolbelt/env-var/test-list rows from the rebase branches are NOT carried because main restructured README and moved those surfaces into docs/, so the equivalent content went to docs/scripts.md and docs/configuration.md and README got a Features bullet. AGENTS.md additions were kept deliberately minimal per the firstmate-coding-guidelines size-discipline rule: only the two operationally essential facts are inline (the FM_CAPTAIN_APPROVED assertion firstmate must use for a local merge, and the data/repos/.md record it maintains), with mechanics left in script headers and docs/. The fm-crew-state evidence-age test was updated to main's current busy-verdict contract (reaching the status-log fallback now needs an armed idle record; asserting the live-pane path needs a semantic busy record that outranks it) - the feature itself is unchanged. TEST COVERAGE ADDED because two consolidated features shipped without any, and --changed selection refused three new source paths for having no consuming suite: new tests/fm-ground.test.sh, ground-truth assertions in tests/fm-brief.test.sh, and an assertion that the completeness gate ships its default rules file and engine (without it every non-overriding verdict in that suite would fail open and still print ok). HARD CONSTRAINTS: all seven source branches must be left exactly as found - never deleted, force-pushed, or rewritten - because they are the only copy of this work and the recovery path if any judgment call above is wrong. Verified untouched at c98385b, 9568dac, 39c5b05, e3581a5, 8c81c17, 7c8ced1, 469cec8. The PR must be opened on tomharper/firstmate with base main; the captain has just fixed gh repo set-default so this resolves correctly, but the owner must still be read back and verified because that failure mode is silent (it is what put PRs 1305, 1248 and 1262 on a repo he cannot merge). KNOWN PRE-EXISTING FAILURES, not regressions from this branch: fm-test-run --changed selects 81 suites and reports total=81 failed=4 (fm-teardown, fm-session-start, fm-pi-watch-extension, fm-bearings-snapshot). All four were re-run against a pristine origin/main extract and fail there IDENTICALLY. fm-teardown matters most because this branch adds a gate call to fm-teardown.sh - it is not the cause: the same assertion fails with FM_COMPLETENESS_GATE=0 and fails on pristine main where the gate does not exist at all. They look environment-dependent (concurrency timing, absent herdr adapter, absent Pi extension) and are out of scope here. Every family this branch touches is clean: pure-contract-unit 26/26, backend-dispatch 9/9, secondmate 9/9, unclassified 12/12. bin/fm-lint.sh clean on pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh ok, coverage guard ok at 107. ## What Changed - Adds `bin/fm-verify-delivered.sh` with distinct non-clean exit outcomes for "inspected nothing" and "search failed" (so an inspection that examined no files can never report clean), and an optional Z3-backed completeness gate (`bin/fm-completeness-check.sh` + `bin/fm-completeness.py` with a shipped default rules file) wired into teardown and local merge — invalid facts exit 64 and block, remote-backed landedness defers entirely to `fm-teardown.sh` while local-only branches are still checked by git, and the review pass aligned the gate's dirty-worktree residue filter and env-override forwarding with the scripts it guards. - Extends crewmate lifecycle tooling: per-repo ground truth (`bin/fm-ground.sh`, `data/repos/.md`) is injected verbatim into ship/scout briefs, briefs scaffold an agent-maintained `data//log.md` working log kept separate from the wake-triggering status file, every status append is UTC-timestamped, and `fm-crew-state.sh` reports evidence age (with `age: unknown` for legacy untimestamped lines); the one-shot escalation dedup now compares stamp-stripped line bodies. - Adds test suites for the new surfaces (`fm-verify-delivered` with one regression test per exit outcome, `fm-completeness` including exit-64 and residue-filter parity, `fm-ground`, plus ground-truth/worklog/timestamp assertions in the brief, crew-state, watch-triage, and pending-reply suites) and documents the gate, `fm-verify-delivered` env vars, and `FM_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE_FACTS`-gated bootstrap capability line across README, AGENTS.md, and docs/. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: All four round-1 findings are fixed at the reported root cause with regression tests, and intent conformance still holds, but the branch remains a large consolidation (2547 insertions) that wires a new gate into two irreversible lifecycle paths (teardown and local merge), so it warrants attention on merge even with no open defects. ## Testing Ran the ten targeted suites covering every consolidated feature (250 assertions, all passing, gate solver tier live on z3 4.15.2), produced six CLI transcripts demonstrating each intent-critical behavior end-to-end — gate verdicts with exit-64 invalid-fact blocking, the squash-merge false-block fix with local-only derivation preserved, verify-delivered's four-outcome contract, ground-truth/worklog/timestamped-append brief scaffolding, evidence-age reporting, and the verbose-facts bootstrap capability line — and confirmed the known fm-teardown suite failure is pre-existing and byte-identical with the gate disabled. No UI surface is involved (pure CLI change), so transcripts are the product-level evidence. Worktree left clean.
Evidence: Completeness gate CLI verdicts (SAT/UNSAT/exit-64/off-switch) $ fm-completeness-check.sh --kind ship --landed mergd --worktree clean fm-completeness-check: invalid --landed 'mergd' (expected one of: merged pushed local_merged none) exit=64 # a typo blocks instead of falling through as a pass ```text # Z3 completeness gate - CLI verdicts (z3 4.15.2) $ fm-completeness-check.sh --kind ship --landed pushed --worktree clean completeness gate: SAT - task clears every invariant exit=0 $ fm-completeness-check.sh --kind ship --landed none --worktree holds_unlanded_work completeness gate: BLOCKED - task is provably premature violated: "SHIP_REQUIRES_LANDED", "NO_UNLANDED_AT_TEARDOWN" reason: [SHIP_REQUIRES_LANDED] ship task declared done but the work is not landed (not merged, pushed to a remote/fork, or merged into local main) (directive #3); [NO_UNLANDED_AT_TEARDOWN] worktree still holds unlanded work; teardown would discard it (directive #3) exit=2 $ fm-completeness-check.sh --gate merge --kind ship --landed merged --captain-approval pending completeness gate: BLOCKED - task (merge) is provably premature violated: "MERGE_NEEDS_CAPTAIN_WORD" reason: [MERGE_NEEDS_CAPTAIN_WORD] merge performed without the captain's explicit approval (directive #2) exit=2 $ fm-completeness-check.sh --gate merge --kind ship --landed merged --captain-approval granted completeness gate: SAT - task (merge) clears every invariant exit=0 # Invalid fact (typo) BLOCKS with exit 64 instead of falling through as a pass: $ fm-completeness-check.sh --kind ship --landed mergd --worktree clean fm-completeness-check: invalid --landed 'mergd' (expected one of: merged pushed local_merged none) exit=64 # Off-switch: $ FM_COMPLETENESS_GATE=0 fm-completeness-check.sh --kind ship --landed none --worktree holds_unlanded_work exit=0 ```
Evidence: Squash-merge false-block fix: remote-backed defers to fm-teardown.sh, local-only still blocks same git state (HEAD on no remote-tracking ref): remote-backed (mode=no-mistakes): SAT exit=0 — defers landedness to fm-teardown.sh work_is_landed mode=local-only: BLOCKED exit=2 — SHIP_REQUIRES_LANDED, NO_UNLANDED_AT_TEARDOWN dirty worktree (remote-backed): BLOCKED exit=2 ```text # The consolidated squash-merge fix: the gate no longer re-derives remote-backed landedness # (identical git state: HEAD holds commits visible on no remote-tracking ref) $ fm-completeness-check.sh --gate teardown --id ship-r # remote-backed (mode=no-mistakes) completeness gate: SAT - ship-r (teardown) clears every invariant exit=0 (defers landedness to fm-teardown.sh work_is_landed - no false block) $ fm-completeness-check.sh --gate teardown --id ship-l # local-only: git CAN decide, so the gate still blocks completeness gate: BLOCKED - ship-l (teardown) is provably premature violated: "SHIP_REQUIRES_LANDED", "NO_UNLANDED_AT_TEARDOWN" reason: [SHIP_REQUIRES_LANDED] ship task declared done but the work is not landed (not merged, pushed to a remote/fork, or merged into local main) (directive #3); [NO_UNLANDED_AT_TEARDOWN] worktree still holds unlanded work; teardown would discard it (directive #3) exit=2 # uncommitted changes still block even for remote-backed work: $ fm-completeness-check.sh --gate teardown --id ship-r # now with a dirty worktree completeness gate: uncommitted changes present in /var/folders/pj/563x6y950m9ccbkkgrt5h3y00000gn/T//fm-gate-defer.nr2LSC/proj completeness gate: BLOCKED - ship-r (teardown) is provably premature violated: "NO_UNLANDED_AT_TEARDOWN" reason: [NO_UNLANDED_AT_TEARDOWN] worktree still holds unlanded work; teardown would discard it (directive #3) exit=2 ```
Evidence: fm-verify-delivered four-outcome contract (VIOLATIONS / CLEAN / INSPECTED NOTHING) INSPECTED NOTHING: pathspec 'schema-generator/app' matches no file at checkme >>> NOT a clean result. The check examined no files, so it proved nothing. exit=3 ```text # fm-verify-delivered.sh brand-identity - the four-outcome exit contract ## A string-only comparison file -> VIOLATIONS (exit 1) === files referencing a brand-identity helper with NO graph identifier === repo: /var/folders/pj/563x6y950m9ccbkkgrt5h3y00000gn/T//fm-verify-demo.Al8goM/viol rev: checkme path: schema-generator/app NO GRAPH IDENTIFIER: app/check.py INSPECTED: 1 candidate file(s) out of 1 under schema-generator/app VIOLATIONS: 1 of 1 inspected file(s) reference a brand-identity helper with no graph identifier anywhere in the file. >>> DO NOT report brand-identity work as complete. exit=1 ## Every inspected file resolves through the graph -> CLEAN (exit 0) === files referencing a brand-identity helper with NO graph identifier === repo: /var/folders/pj/563x6y950m9ccbkkgrt5h3y00000gn/T//fm-verify-demo.Al8goM/clean rev: checkme path: schema-generator/app INSPECTED: 1 candidate file(s) out of 1 under schema-generator/app CLEAN: all 1 inspected file(s) reference a graph identifier somewhere in the file, comments and docstrings included, which is not proof they consult it; 1 referencing, 0 with no graph reference. exit=0 ## Pathspec matches no files -> INSPECTED NOTHING (exit 3), NOT clean (the false-clean fix) === files referencing a brand-identity helper with NO graph identifier === repo: /var/folders/pj/563x6y950m9ccbkkgrt5h3y00000gn/T//fm-verify-demo.Al8goM/empty rev: checkme path: schema-generator/app INSPECTED NOTHING: pathspec 'schema-generator/app' matches no file at checkme in /var/folders/pj/563x6y950m9ccbkkgrt5h3y00000gn/T//fm-verify-demo.Al8goM/empty >>> NOT a clean result. The check examined no files, so it proved nothing. >>> Fix the search before reporting anything about this claim. exit=3 ```
Evidence: Brief scaffolding: ground-truth injection, log.md worklog, timestamped status append ```text # fm-brief.sh - ground truth, working log, and timestamped status append ## Ground-truth file registered for repo "acme" at data/repos/acme.md: repo-path: /opt/acme - Storage is Postgres, never SQLite. - Deploys run on Cloudflare Workers. $ fm-brief.sh demo-ship acme # ship brief for a grounded repo warn: no registry at /var/folders/pj/563x6y950m9ccbkkgrt5h3y00000gn/T//fm-brief-demo.Ye86D5/home/data/projects.md; defaulting acme to no-mistakes off scaffolded: /var/folders/pj/563x6y950m9ccbkkgrt5h3y00000gn/T//fm-brief-demo.Ye86D5/home/data/demo-ship/brief.md (ship, mode=no-mistakes; replace {TASK}) ## Ground-truth section injected verbatim into the brief (brief.md lines 3-11): # Repo ground truth - authoritative, do not re-derive or guess The facts below about this repo are established. Treat them as binding: never improvise architecture (storage, providers, models, how it runs) that contradicts them, and never reach for the cheapest available tool - every choice here is studied. repo-path: /opt/acme - Storage is Postgres, never SQLite. - Deploys run on Cloudflare Workers. ## Agent-maintained working log scaffold (data//log.md, NOT the status file): 32:Keep a working log at `/var/folders/pj/563x6y950m9ccbkkgrt5h3y00000gn/T//fm-brief-demo.Ye86D5/home/data/demo-ship/log.md` and write it as you go, not at the end. ## Status append instruction is one copy-pasteable timestamped line: 44: `echo "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) {state}: {one short line}" >> '/var/folders/pj/563x6y950m9ccbkkgrt5h3y00000gn/T//fm-brief-demo.Ye86D5/home/state/demo-ship.status'` $ fm-brief.sh demo-none otherproj # ungrounded repo still scaffolds, and warns stderr: fm-brief: WARNING - no ground truth for 'otherproj' (data/repos/). The crewmate starts ungrounded and may guess the architecture; consider adding a data/repos/ file first. stderr: warn: no registry at /var/folders/pj/563x6y950m9ccbkkgrt5h3y00000gn/T//fm-brief-demo.Ye86D5/home/data/projects.md; defaulting otherproj to no-mistakes off stderr: scaffolded: /var/folders/pj/563x6y950m9ccbkkgrt5h3y00000gn/T//fm-brief-demo.Ye86D5/home/data/demo-none/brief.md (ship, mode=no-mistakes; replace {TASK}) brief.md scaffolded: yes no empty ground-truth section carried ```
Evidence: fm-crew-state evidence age from timestamped status appends state: done · source: status-log · age: 2h14m · report at data/feat-age/report.md state: working · source: status-log · age: 1s · chasing the flaky spec state: done · source: status-log · age: unknown · legacy line with no timestamp ```text # fm-crew-state.sh - status appends carry timestamps, and the verdict reports the evidence age ## Status log written via the timestamped append the brief scaffolds: 2026-08-04T21:38:17Z done: report at data/feat-age/report.md $ fm-crew-state.sh feat-age # done reported 2h14m ago state: done · source: status-log · age: 2h14m · report at data/feat-age/report.md 2026-08-04T23:52:17Z working: chasing the flaky spec $ fm-crew-state.sh feat-age # fresh append -> age in seconds state: working · source: status-log · age: 1s · chasing the flaky spec $ fm-crew-state.sh feat-age # untimestamped legacy line -> age: unknown state: done · source: status-log · age: unknown · legacy line with no timestamp ```
Evidence: Bootstrap capability line behind FM_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE_FACTS=1 default: (no completeness/z3 line) FM_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE_FACTS=1: BOOTSTRAP_INFO: completeness gate available (no MISSING/install prompt for z3) ```text # fm-bootstrap.sh - gate capability is a verbose no-action fact, never a MISSING line $ FM_BOOTSTRAP_DETECT_ONLY=1 fm-bootstrap.sh # default: silent about the gate (no completeness/z3 line - correct) $ FM_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE_FACTS=1 FM_BOOTSTRAP_DETECT_ONLY=1 fm-bootstrap.sh # verbose facts opt-in BOOTSTRAP_INFO: completeness gate available # and it is never a MISSING/install prompt: (no MISSING line for z3 - correct) ```
Evidence: Targeted suite outputs (10 suites, 250 ok) ```text ok - the gate ships its default rules file and engine ok - off-switch FM_COMPLETENESS_GATE=0 exits 0 ok - fail-open on missing rules file exits 0 ok - FM_COMPLETENESS_STRICT=1 enforces (exit 3) on tooling breakage ok - fail-open on corrupt rules file exits 0 ok - strict mode enforces (exit 3) on corrupt rules file ok - unknown argument exits 64 ok - undeclared axis value exits 64 (blocking, not fail-open) ok - malformed --meta key exits 64 ok - scout without report is blocked ok - scout with report clears ok - ship not landed is blocked ok - ship pushed + clean clears ok - merge without approval is blocked ok - merge with approval clears ok - merge gate honors FM_CAPTAIN_APPROVED=granted ok - merge gate blocks when approval unset (defaults pending) ok - graded ship is SAT despite unmet soft rules ok - --id scout derivation blocks with no report ok - --id scout derivation clears once report exists ok - contradictory rules file fails open ok - strict mode enforces on contradictory rules file ok - local-only master-default repo with unmerged work is blocked ok - local-only master-default repo clears once merged ok - firstmate turn-end markers and .claude/ are not unlanded work ok - a genuinely dirty worktree still blocks ```
Evidence: fm-teardown pre-existing failure: identical with gate on vs FM_COMPLETENESS_GATE=0 ```text ok - local-only worktree with HEAD on a fork remote is torn down (fix holds) ok - teardown prompts tasks-axi backlog refresh when compatible ok - teardown honors config/backlog-backend=manual even when tasks-axi is compatible ok - local-only worktree with truly unpushed work is refused (safety preserved) ok - local-only worktree with work merged into local main is torn down (no regression) ok - no-mistakes worktree with HEAD on origin is torn down (no regression) ok - no-mistakes worktree with genuinely unlanded work is refused (safety preserved) ok - local-only worktree with unpushed work is torn down under --force (escape hatch) ok - teardown completes when an exact busy-state sidecar is already absent ok - herdr teardown removes pane-owned escalation dedupe state ok - herdr flat teardown refuses before returning the isolated copy under lock contention and the retry completes cleanly ok - herdr flat teardown never erases records when pane presence is unparseable not ok - herdr-preflight-missing-adapter: the retryable pre-return refusal was not explained visibly ```
- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 info across 1 run (13m4s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 4 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `bin/fm-completeness-check.sh:97` - The completeness gate's dirty-worktree derivation filters only `?? .claude/`, while fm-teardown.sh:768 (validate_worktree_teardown_safety) filters `^\?\? (\.claude/|\.fm-(grok|kimi)-turnend$)`. git_unlanded_facts' own comment says it mirrors fm-teardown.sh "so the gate never diverges from the script it guards", but it does. Failure sequence: fm-spawn.sh:1569/1584 writes `$WT/.fm-grok-turnend` (or `.fm-kimi-turnend`) into the worktree and only best-effort excludes it via exclude_path (bin/fm-spawn.sh:1362-1368, which returns silently when `git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude` yields nothing). If that exclusion did not take, `git status --porcelain` lists `?? .fm-grok-turnend`; teardown's own check drops it, the gate's does not, so the gate sets worktree=holds_unlanded_work, violates NO_UNLANDED_AT_TEARDOWN, exits 2, and fm-teardown.sh:1553 hard-refuses at line 1549 - before validate_worktree_teardown_safety ever runs - blocking teardown of a worktree teardown itself considers clean. Fix: use the identical regex `^\?\? (\.claude/|\.fm-(grok|kimi)-turnend$)` in git_unlanded_facts. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:821` - The one-shot escalation dedup changed from `grep -Fqx "blocked: $payload"` (whole line) to `grep -Fq` (substring anywhere in the file) to tolerate the new leading UTC stamp. That also silently weakens the guard: any existing line that merely contains `blocked: <payload>` as a substring now suppresses a genuinely new escalation. fm-classify-lib.sh is already sourced here (line 71-72 of the diff), so the precise fix is to fold the file through `status_line_body` and compare the stripped body for equality, keeping the original whole-line semantics under the stamp contract. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-verify-delivered.sh:66` - AGENTS.md:39 now makes running bin/fm-verify-delivered.sh a hard-rule precondition before reporting any capability as delivered or marking any task done, but the script's only verdict-producing mode (brand-identity) is hardcoded to one downstream private project: BRAND_PATHSPEC="schema-generator/app", BRAND_CANDIDATE_RE/BRAND_GRAPH_RE naming that project's helpers, and resolve_brand_repo defaulting to $FM_HOME/projects/inception. For every other repo or claim, only task-id mode applies, and its own output says "CHECKLIST: ... This is a checklist, NOT a clean verdict." In a repo shipped to other captains, the mandated check therefore has no verdict path for their work. Worth confirming whether the AGENTS.md hard-rule wording should be scoped to the modes the script actually supports, or whether a generic mode is intended to follow. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:1549` - The gate is invoked as `"$FM_ROOT/bin/fm-completeness-check.sh" --gate teardown --id "$ID"` with none of FM_HOME/FM_STATE_OVERRIDE/FM_DATA_OVERRIDE/FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE forwarded, and fm-merge-local.sh:55 does the same. title: fix(bin): resolve symlinks before validating startup-memory config
body:
## Problem

`bin/fm-startup-memory-budget-lib.sh` rejects a symlink outright in three places instead of resolving it:

- `fm_startup_memory_budget_config_dir_safe` - `config directory is symlinked`
- `fm_startup_memory_budget_file_valid` - `file is symlinked`
- `fm_startup_memory_measure_file` - `memory file is not an ordinary regular file`

This makes a legitimate layout unusable. An operator who keeps private configuration in a separate tree and symlinks it into the firstmate home (for example, because the checkout is a public fork and `config/` and `data/` must stay private) gets:

```
STARTUP_MEMORY_BUDGET: invalid config/startup-memory-budget - config directory is symlinked
```

on every session. The budget is never read, `bin/fm-startup-memory-budget.sh report` cannot run, and the internal `/stow` skill cannot verify it finished within budget - so the startup-memory limit is silently unenforced rather than merely unread. The recurring diagnostic reads as routine noise, which is how it stays that way.

## Change

Resolve the symlink chain first, then apply the existing checks to the resolved target.

The genuine anti-substitution guard is the hardlink-count check, and it is unaffected by how the name was reached - so applying it to the resolved target is strictly stronger than refusing the link. Still rejected, each with its own concrete message: a broken chain (`file is absent`), a cyclic or over-deep chain (`file link could not be resolved`), a non-regular target (`file is not a regular file`), a hardlinked target (`file is hardlinked`, including when reached through a symlink), and every existing content/format rule.

`fm_startup_memory_measure_file` is included deliberately. Memory files are commonly linked in individually rather than through a linked `data/`, so fixing only the two config paths moves the failure from the budget read to the accounting command instead of fixing it.

Chain resolution is walked in-shell because BSD and GNU userlands disagree about `realpath` and `readlink -f`.

## Verification

`tests/fm-startup-memory-budget.test.sh` updated and extended; the previous tests pinned the old refusals, so those assertions now pin the resolve-then-validate behavior, and new cases cover symlink-to-hardlinked-target, broken link, link-to-directory, link cycle, symlinked config dir, and config dir linked to a non-directory.

```
$ bash tests/fm-startup-memory-budget.test.sh
ok - primary bootstrap materializes only the visible default and preserves valid captain choices
ok - budget parser accepts one exact positive value and rejects malformed or unsafe inputs
ok - budget accounting sums the three startup files and reports safe failures
ok - budget propagation converges through config push with exact rereads, absence, and safe rejection
# all fm-startup-memory-budget tests passed
```

```
$ bin/fm-lint.sh
fm-lint.sh: ShellCheck 0.11.0 (pinned 0.11.0)
```

Also passing locally: `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh`, `tests/fm-shared-captain-inheritance.test.sh`, `tests/fm-gitignore-config.test.sh`, and `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` (`ok surfaces=64 local_links=193`).

End to end on a home mirroring the affected layout (symlinked `config/` plus per-file memory symlinks) - before:

```
startup-memory-budget: invalid config/startup-memory-budget - config directory is symlinked
```

after:

```
estimator=ceil(UTF-8 bytes / 3) conservative-local-estimate
role=primary
effective_budget_tokens=7500
file=data/captain.md bytes=14 estimated_tokens=5 status=present
file=data/captain-shared.md bytes=0 estimated_tokens=0 status=absent
file=data/learnings.md bytes=10 estimated_tokens=4 status=present
total_estimated_tokens=9
budget_status=within-budget
```

`docs/configuration.md`'s "Startup memory budget" section is updated, since it documented the old refusal.

Line 2303 (`exit 1` when TRACEPARENT input cannot be cleared) and line 2291 (`spawn_send_text_line "$T" "export GOTMPDIR=..."`, unguarded under `set -eu`) both leave the process without ever calling `abort_unpublished_meta`, so `discard_unpublished_endpoint` never runs and `META_PUBLICATION_FAILURE_DETAIL` is empty in `spawn_abort_cleanup`. Orca terminals and a pending herdr projection are still unwound by the EXIT trap, but a tmux, zellij, cmux, or non-projected herdr endpoint survives with no task record naming it and no warning printed - the exact outcome the new header contract ("a spawn that never publishes one would otherwise strand a window no teardown can find") says is prevented. Before this branch the record was published ahead of both sends, so teardown could still find the window. Fix: set `META_PUBLICATION_FAILURE_DETAIL` and call `abort_unpublished_meta` (or at least `discard_unpublished_endpoint`) on the uncleared-input refusal, and guard the GOTMPDIR send the same way instead of letting `set -e` abort silently. 🔧 Fix: route pre-publication spawn aborts through unpublished-endpoint cleanup ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

Confirmed mechanism, reproduced standalone against byte-identical worker scripts: fm_remote_job_prepare_state (bin/fm-remote-job-lib.sh:384-392) recreates state/, jobs/, and logs/ but never worker.lock, so after a teardown removes the state root the worker's own stale-job sweep brings back everything except the lock directory; worker_publish_quarantine (bin/fm-remote-job-worker.sh:175) then mktemps into that missing directory and fails, and worker_shutdown re-arms its own trap and returns 0, swallowing the signal while heartbeats keep succeeding. Flagged so a reviewer reading a red Behavior portable serial 4 knows it is the tracked separate defect. - ⚠️ `tests/fm-remote-job-orphan-reap.test.sh:102` - Separate pre-existing flake in the same file, unrelated to the TERM defect: 1 of 15 runs failed at tests/fm-remote-job-orphan-reap.test.sh:102 with `could not start the fixture remote job worker`. fm_remote_job_start_linux_worker backgrounds the worker with nohup and returns immediately without waiting for readiness (bin/fm-remote-job-lib.sh:947-956), while the fixture's start_worker pgreps for the worker argv on the very next line, so a slow fork yields an empty pid. The file is byte-identical to the base commit, so this predates PR 1716; adding a bounded wait would be a safe test-only fix but would broaden this PR's scope and break the byte-identical-to-base property that is itself evidence here. Left for the author to decide. - `bash tests/fm-trace-context-lib.test.sh` - 25 assertions green against production, including the new "brief, prompt, report, and status prose cannot influence any field of a fixed-entropy carrier" - Mutation evidence: scratch copy of `bin/fm-trace-context-lib.sh` whose `fm_trace_context_resolve` flips the sampled flag 01->00 for `brief=prose-beta`; new assertion fails with `expected='00-1111...-2222...-01' got='...-00'` - Mutation control: the pre-746b2fe prose assertion (from `git show 337d077:tests/fm-trace-context-lib.test.sh`) run against the same mutant - passes, showing the replaced check was ineffective - `git diff 833a9a2 HEAD -- tests/fm-remote-job-orphan-reap.test.sh` - empty, confirming the 337d0771 weakening is fully backed out - `bash tests/fm-remote-job-orphan-reap.test.sh` x15 - 12 green, 2 red on `the serving child ignored TERM`, 1 red on a separate pre-existing fixture-start race - Manual end-to-end reproduction of the shutdown defect via `repro-term-swallowed.sh`: starts a real worker through `fm_remote_job_start_linux_worker`, removes the state root, waits for the worker's own sweep to recreate it, verifies `worker.lock` is absent, sends a lone TERM, then shows the worker alive and `worker.ready` reappearing after deletion - `bash bin/fm-test-run.sh --list --lane portable-serial-4of4 | grep orphan-reap` - confirms the red assertion lands in Behavior portable serial 4 - `bash tests/fm-spawn-prepublication-abort.test.sh` - 12 assertions green (the 6589211 pre-publication abort cleanup) - `bash tests/fm-trace-context-spawn.test.sh` - 12 assertions green, matching the count documented in docs/verification/trace-context.md - `bash tests/fm-role-context.test.sh` - green, preserved role-aware context split - `grep -n 'OPEN DECISIONS' docs/configuration.md` - the captain-preserved cursor sentence is intact at line 18 - `git status --porcelain` after cleanup - clean; scratch mutant copy and repro temp roots removed, no stray worker processes
⚠️ **Document** - 1 info - ℹ️ `docs/fm-test-portable-shards.md:71` - The portable serial CI shard table still reports the 2026-08-02 partition (15/18/17/19 = 69 scripts), while the lane now selects 100 scripts across 24/25/23/28. Only 3 of that 31-script delta comes from this branch's new suites; the base commit already selected 97. A correct refresh needs per-shard timing artifacts from a green CI run, which the doc's own procedure prescribes (gh run download ...) and which cannot be produced here, and editing the counts alone would leave the estimated durations inconsistent with them. Left unchanged as an out-of-scope follow-up: refresh portable_serial_weight_hints in bin/fm-test-run.sh from a green run's artifacts and update this table in the same change.

title: feat(skills): add pr-shepherd skill for gated PR landing
body:
## What Changed - Adds the user-invocable `.agents/skills/pr-shepherd/SKILL.md` skill (411 lines): a phased pipeline that inventories reviewer findings on an open PR, requires a per-finding disposition table before "comments addressed" may be claimed, drives critical CI green, and then either merges under an explicit authority path or stops at a merge-ready report (`--no-merge` forces report-only). - Rewrites `AGENTS.md` hard rule 2 so merge authority has one owner: alongside a project's `yolo` posture, a captain-recorded shepherd/merge posture in `data/captain.md` or an inherited `data/captain-shared.md` is a standing relaxation, but only for a routine green merge, only when captain-authored (never filed by `/stow` or inference), and never for an admin or branch-protection-bypass merge. Section 7 delivery defaults and the captain-instruction precedence section were updated to point at that rule instead of restating a conflicting version of it. - Registers the skill across the captain-facing surfaces: a `/pr-shepherd` row in the README command table, a load trigger in AGENTS.md section 7, an `agent-runtime` entry in `docs/documentation-audiences.json`, operator-facing posture placement guidance in `docs/configuration.md`, and a `CONTRIBUTING.md` merge line that now defers to hard rule 2. Review flagged and the branch fixed a self-authorization gap (a firstmate-written posture standing in for the captain's word) and the resulting contradiction between hard rule 2 and the precedence section; a merge-authority conformance run put 5 Phase-7 situations through `claude -p`, all 5 matching the intended contract. Three open infos remain as clarity/follow-up notes, including trimming the duplicated authority prose in `docs/configuration.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The branch is a well-bounded documentation and skill delivery across exactly the five intended paths with no executable code changed, and every finding from the prior two rounds is now resolved consistently across hard rule 2, section 7, the precedence section, the skill, and the configuration doc. ## Testing Baseline was a clean worktree at the target commit with no code to build, since the change is agent-instruction and documentation text. I ran the smallest relevant existing tests — the documentation-inventory test that registers and link-checks the new skill and the new configuration.md paragraph, plus the authority, delivery, brief, and AGENTS.md-promotion contract tests the repo's own changed-file map selects — and all passed. Because passing tests alone do not show gated PR landing works, I also demonstrated the captain-facing surfaces directly: the `/pr-shepherd` slash entry as rendered from the shipped frontmatter through the `.claude/skills` symlink Claude Code scans, a real `bin/fm-session-start.sh` run against an isolated throwaway home showing a captain-recorded shepherd posture reaching firstmate's session digest, and a five-situation conformance run that fed the shipped merge-authority text to a fresh agent — it correctly refused to merge with no posture, with red CI, with a branch-protection bypass, and with a firstmate-inferred `/stow` bullet, and merged only on a routine green PR under a captain-written posture. There is no rendered UI in this change, so no screenshot or video artifact exists; the end-user surface is a CLI/agent instruction set, and the artifacts are the corresponding transcripts. Overall result: everything passed and no actionable findings remain.

Blast radius is also wider than the existing relaxation it is placed alongside: `+yolo` is per project, whereas a `data/captain-shared.md` bullet inherits into every secondmate home and covers every project at once. AGENTS.md:538 requires the captain to state destructive, irreversible, security-sensitive, and merge actions explicitly and currently, and AGENTS.md:539 says standing authority is not a substitute for a current explicit instruction where an explicit action is required. Bypassing enforced branch protection is squarely in that class, and path (a) is a file firstmate writes, so this carve-out lets a recorded line stand in for the current explicit word the precedence section demands. Recommend restricting `--admin` to authority path (c) only. - ⚠️ `AGENTS.md:538` - The captain-instruction precedence section still reads "Destructive, irreversible, security-sensitive, discard, and merge actions still require the captain to state that concrete action explicitly", which now directly contradicts the amended hard rule 2 at AGENTS.md:29 and the amended section 7 line at AGENTS.md:299, both of which say a recorded standing posture authorizes a routine PR merge with no new per-PR captain word. An agent reading section 1 concludes it may merge; an agent reading the precedence section concludes it may not. Whichever way the captain wants it resolved, one of the two sentences needs to be updated so the instruction surface has a single answer. - ⚠️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:1921` - `create_task`'s husk/dup match was widened from the exact create label `fm-<id>` to the lossy display names produced by `fm_backend_herdr_display_name` (line 465), which lowercases, maps every non `[a-z0-9_-]` char to `-`, strips leading `fm-`/`scout-`/`ship-`, collapses runs, and truncates to 32 chars. Distinct labels that previously could never collide now do. Concretely: task ids `auth.fix` and `auth-fix` are both valid (`fm_task_id_path_safe` allows `A-Za-z0-9._-`, up to 64 chars) and both derive `ship-auth-fix`; likewise `Auth` vs `auth`, `ship-x` vs `x`, and any two ids sharing their first 27 characters. Spawning task B then inspects task A's renamed tab: if A's pane is a husk, `create_task` closes A's tab (A's recorded `herdr_tab_id` in meta goes stale); if A is live, B's spawn is refused with a message naming B's label for a tab that is not B's. A second path needs no id collision at all: a human-created plain shell tab in the home workspace named `ship-notes` or `scout-work` reports `no-agent`, so `fm_backend_herdr_tab_is_husk` classifies it as a husk and a spawn of task `notes`/`work` closes it. Recommend only treating a display-name label as this task's when it round-trips losslessly back to this exact id (e.g. skip the display-name candidates when the derived slug is not byte-identical to the id), keeping `fm-<id>` as the always-safe match. - ℹ️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:3164` - `fm_backend_herdr_list_live` is documented (herdr.sh:51-57) as the authoritative recovery/orphan-discovery path that identifies task windows BY LABEL. With the prefix widened to `^(fm|scout|ship)-`, the labels it now emits are lossy display names, so an operator or recovering agent can no longer derive the task id from the reported label (`ship-auth-fix` maps back to `auth.fix`, `auth-fix`, `Auth-Fix`, or a truncation of a longer id). The same regex also reports any unrelated tab in this home's workspace whose label happens to start with `ship-`/`scout-` as a firstmate task. Net this is still an improvement over renamed tabs being invisible to the sweep, so noting it as a tradeoff rather than a defect; if id recovery matters for the sweep, emitting the matching `state/<id>.meta` binding alongside the label would close it. - ℹ️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:572` - `[ -n "$tab" ] && [ "$tab" != 1 ]` compares a tab *id* against the *label* "1". Real herdr tab ids are `w1:t3`-shaped (docs/verification/runtime-backends.md:251), so this arm can never be false and provides none of the protection its comment claims; docs/herdr-backend.md:77 then states "The primary seed tab labeled `1` is never renamed" as a guarantee. The only real protection is the caller contract (fm-spawn.sh never passes the seed tab id) plus the projected-tab clearing at fm-spawn.sh:2162. Recommend dropping the dead comparison and letting the comment/doc state the caller contract, or making it a genuine check against the tab's label. 🔧 Fix: Scope branch to pr-shepherd and tighten merge authority 3 infos still open: - ℹ️ `AGENTS.md:29` - The rewritten hard rule 2 drops the old "is the only standing relaxation for routine decisions" qualifier and ends "...are the only standing relaxations, and each covers a routine green merge only." Read scoped to hard rule 2 that is exactly right, but read literally it says `yolo` covers only routine green merges, which conflicts with section 7 line 300 ("With `yolo` on, firstmate decides routine gates only within the captain's original request and accepted task criteria") and with line 506's "regardless of the project's `yolo` posture" note on ask-user findings. Because hard rule 2 is priority-1 text, the misreading direction is conservative (firstmate escalates ask-user findings it could have decided), so this is a clarity nit rather than a safety gap; "each relaxes this rule only for a routine green merge" would remove the ambiguity. - ℹ️ `AGENTS.md:308` - The red-merge sentence still enumerates only one standing relaxation: "standing `yolo` cannot authorize a red merge". Now that a captain-recorded posture is a second standing relaxation, this list is asymmetric. The gap is already closed by hard rule 2's "each covers a routine green merge only" (line 29) and by the skill's hard rule 3, so no red merge is actually reachable through a recorded posture; naming both here would just keep section 7 readable on its own. - ℹ️ `.agents/skills/stow/SKILL.md:48` - AGENTS.md:30 now states that `/stow` never files a session finding as new merge authority, but stow's own skill still instructs the sweep to look for "captain preferences expressed in passing" and to retain "authority and safety boundaries" (line 30) with no carve-out for merge postures, and stow is the skill actually holding the pen when `data/captain.md` is written. AGENTS.md is always loaded and priority-ordered, so the prohibition does reach that agent; and the captain explicitly scoped this branch to five paths, so mirroring the carve-out into stow's own file is deliberately out of scope here. Noting it only as the natural follow-up if the wording should live next to the write it governs. 🔧 Fix: Clarify hard rule 2 merge scope and red-merge relaxations ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain. </details> <details> <summary>✅ **Test** - passed</summary> ✅ No issues found. - <code>`bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` — validates the new `.agents/skills/pr-shepherd/SKILL.md` is classified exactly once in docs/documentation-audiences.json and that every local link/anchor added to docs/configuration.md and AGENTS.md resolves</code> - <code>`bash tests/fm-ask-user-authority.test.sh` — authority contract still reaches primary workers and secondmates through generated instructions</code> - <code>`bash tests/fm-task-delivery.test.sh` — AGENTS.md section 7 delivery/`yolo` contract (the section whose merge paragraph changed)</code> - <code>`bash tests/fm-ensure-agents-md.test.sh` — AGENTS.md promotion/self-governance handling</code> - <code>`bash tests/fm-brief.test.sh` — spawn brief scaffolds that carry the authority policy</code> - <code>Manual: merge-authority conformance run — extracted the shipped hard rule 2, section 7 merge defaults, and the skill's Merge authority section, then ran 5 Phase-7 situations through `claude -p` (no posture / captain-recorded posture / posture+red CI / posture+branch-protection bypass / firstmate-inferred `/stow` bullet); 5/5 decisions matched the intended contract</code> - <code>Manual: `FM_HOME=<temp> FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE=<throwaway repo> bin/fm-session-start.sh` against an isolated home whose `data/captain.md` records a shepherd posture — the session context digest prints the posture firstmate must read before merging</code> - <code>Manual: rendered the captain-visible `/pr-shepherd` slash entry from the shipped frontmatter via `.claude/skills/pr-shepherd/SKILL.md` (symlink the harness scans), plus the README command row, doc-inventory entry, and the AGENTS.md load trigger</code> - <code>Manual: `claude -p` skill enumeration inside the worktree with tools disabled, confirming `pr-shepherd` is among the project skills the harness loads</code> - <code>Manual: grep sweep for leftover contradictions of the old "`yolo` is the only standing routine authority" claim across AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/, and .agents/skills/</code> </details> <details> <summary>⚠️ **Document** - 1 info</summary> - ℹ️ `docs/configuration.md:145` - docs/configuration.md lines 145-147 now carry near-verbatim copies of AGENTS.md hard rule 2's authority constraints (captain-authored only, /stow never files one, absence means none, routine green merge only, never an admin bypass) while the same block also names hard rule 2 as the owner. Those sentences were added deliberately by the branch's own review-fix commit 6b4b30b, so I left them rather than undo review-driven hardening, but they are synchronized prose: if hard rule 2's relaxations change, this operator-facing copy drifts silently. title: feat(bin): bound startup status projection with byte budgets
body:
## Intent Implement Phase 3's tracked startup-projection improvements from the Firstmate context-effectiveness audit while preserving deterministic recovery value and preventing long status prose and nearly full private memory files from dominating every new Firstmate session. Reproduce and bound the executable startup failure where one 8KB status event defeats a line-only tail, then replace raw tail output with a deterministic structured historical projection that leaves durable logs unchanged and includes the newest recognized event, unresolved correctly keyed decisions from the existing authoritative fold, omitted-event counts, and exact full-log paths. Apply explicit per-event, per-task, and 12KB fleet-wide startup status-text limits selected from measured fleet distributions and safety fixtures, with receipts that preserve each truncation's original byte count and source path. Preserve state verbs, decision keys, complete PR URLs, exact-head identity, and run identity in structured fields even when prose is truncated. Keep fm-crew-state.sh as the targeted current-state authority, remain portable on macOS Bash 3.2 and newer Bash, and do not add LLM summaries, semantic retrieval, another decision fold, or destructive log compaction. Make healthy startup-memory headroom below the 7,500 estimated-token ceiling visible and testable, using a 6,000-token healthy target and tracked /stow guidance, without deleting or editing private captain data. Cover 8KB input, multiple tasks crossing the total limit, key/URL/head/run preservation, truncation receipts, omitted counts, full-log pointers, empty and missing logs, older unresolved decisions, unchanged normal small projected text, deterministic ordering, and stock Bash 3.2. Keep configuration and architecture ownership concise, run focused and complete startup/session tests, pinned lint, documentation checks, and required project validation. Generally useful Firstmate behavior must ship through a reviewed upstream no-mistakes PR under the clean-main policy. Open one focused PR and never merge it. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-session-start.sh` replaces the fixed `tail -n 5` status dump with a deterministic structured projection per task. Each present log now emits its newest recognized lifecycle event, every open keyed decision from `fm-classify-lib.sh`'s existing authoritative fold (emitted once and back-referenced when the newest event *is* that decision), a legacy verb-less newest line, source/recognized/omitted counts, and the exact full-log path. Event text is bounded per record (768 B), per task (1536 B), and fleet-wide (12 KiB, all three overridable via `FM_SESSION_START_STATUS_*_BYTES`), with a receipt naming original bytes, emitted bytes, limiting scopes, and source path; state verbs, decision keys, PR/MR URLs, 40/64-hex exact heads, and run identities are lifted into structured fields before any cut, `LC_ALL=C` pins byte-exact ordering and truncation, and a partial UTF-8 tail is trimmed. Append-only `state/*.status` logs are read-only and unchanged, and `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` remains the targeted current-state authority. - `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh` splits each status parser into an assigning `_into ` form with the historical printing form delegating to it, so whole-file folds and the new projection cost no subshell per line; the printing API and observed output for existing consumers are unchanged. - `bin/fm-startup-memory-budget.sh report` adds `healthy_target_tokens` at 80 percent of the effective ceiling (6,000 tokens under the default 7,500) and a `healthy_margin_status` of `healthy-margin`, `near-ceiling`, or `over-budget`, computed through new portable decimal multiply/divide helpers in `bin/fm-startup-memory-budget-lib.sh`. The `/stow` skill now curates to that healthy target and must report healthy-margin status rather than mere budget compliance; `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, and a `docs/verification/stow-memory.md` real-agent record follow, and CI's stock macOS Bash 3.2 job now runs the session-start and startup-memory suites. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: All seven previously accepted findings are verified fixed with reproductions on stock Bash 3.2, and the one structurally broad piece - the shared fm-classify-lib.sh parser refactor - was differentially proven output-identical to the prior implementation across malformed, blank, tab-bearing, and multi-key fixtures while cutting fold cost from 7.46s to 0.69s on a 2000-line log. ## Testing I reproduced the executable startup failure on the base commit - one 8,192-byte status event printed verbatim past the 5-line tail, giving a 17,475-byte digest - then captured the same fixture on the target commit at 10,361 bytes with the event bounded to 768 emitted bytes while state verb, decision key, complete PR URL, 40-hex exact head, run id, omitted counts, truncation receipt, and exact full-log path all survived, and `cksum` confirmed the raw logs were untouched. A 20-task fleet drove the fleet-wide budget to exactly 12288 bytes with post-exhaustion tasks still emitting every recovery field, three repeat runs plus an `en_US.UTF-8` run were byte-identical, and `fm-startup-memory-budget.sh report` walked one home through healthy-margin, near-ceiling, and over-budget against the 6,000-token healthy target.
