✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ⚠️ `bin/fm-session-start.sh:403` - When the newest recognized event IS the still-open decision, the projection emits the same text twice and charges it twice against the per-task and fleet-wide byte budgets. Reproduced with a two-line log (`working: step one` / `needs-decision [key=api]: pick a or b`): both `open_decision_1` and `newest_recognized_event` print `event_text=needs-decision [key=api]: pick a or b`, and `task_text_budget_used_bytes=74` for 37 bytes of distinct prose. This is the normal shape for any task actually waiting on the captain - exactly the case the digest exists to surface - so the default 1536-byte task budget delivers half the intended recovery text. Suggest skipping the `newest_recognized_event` record (or emitting only a back-reference) when the newest line's key and verb already matched a projected open decision. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-session-start.sh:360` - The projection replaces `tail -n 5` with a full read of every status log, and the counting loop forks a subshell per line via `verb=$(status_line_verb "$line")`; `status_open_decisions` at line 371 then re-reads the same file with ~2 more command substitutions per line. Status logs are append-only and nothing in bin/ rotates or truncates them, so session-start cost now grows linearly (in forks) with a task's entire historical event count. Measured on this branch with a synthetic 2000-line log: ~2s for the counting loop plus ~2s for the fold, versus ~0s for `tail -n 5`; several long-lived tasks would add tens of seconds to the one command whose purpose is a fast bounded startup. The counting loop's verb parse is pure parameter expansion and can be inlined (or exposed as a variable-assigning helper in fm-classify-lib.sh) to remove the per-line fork, and the same pass can collect the counts the fold already computes instead of scanning twice. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-session-start.sh:379` - `omitted` is computed as `event_count - 1` whenever any event was recognized, which assumes exactly one event is projected. Events emitted as `open_decision_N` are still counted as omitted. Reproduced with a 4-line log (needs-decision route / working / resolved other / done): the digest prints `omitted_event_count=3` while 2 of the 4 events were actually projected. The intent lists omitted-event counts as required recovery evidence, so an inflated count misleads the agent about how much history the full log still holds. Subtract the number of projected records (open decisions plus the newest event, deduplicated) rather than a fixed 1. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-session-start.sh:257` - `status_projection_is_recognized_verb` accepts only the standard verb set, but fm-classify-lib.sh:40-45 documents and supports legacy free-text status lines that lack a leading verb (`PR ready`, `checks green`, `ready in branch`, `merged`) and treats them as captain-relevant. Reproduced with a log containing only `PR ready for review` and `merged upstream at abc`: the projection prints `recognized_event_count=0` and `newest_recognized_event: (none)`, emitting zero event text, where the previous tail printed both lines. The counts and full-log path survive, so recovery is still possible via a targeted read, but a legacy-only task now contributes no prose at all to the digest. Confirm this is the intended trade-off, or fall back to projecting the newest non-blank line (with `state_verb=unrecognized`) when no recognized verb exists. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-session-start.sh:259` - The recognized-verb set honors `FM_CLASSIFY_PAUSED_VERB` (line 260) but hardcodes `resolved` and `captain-held`, ignoring `FM_CLASSIFY_RESOLVE_VERB` and `FM_CLASSIFY_CAPTAIN_HELD_VERB`, which fm-classify-lib.sh:213-214 and 227 do honor. A home that overrides either verb would have those events counted as unrecognized and excluded from `newest`, disagreeing with the fold running over the same file. Read all three through their documented override defaults for consistency. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-session-start.sh:335` - `cut -b "1-$allowance"` truncates on a byte boundary, so a status note containing multi-byte UTF-8 (a crew note with an accented word or an emoji) can end `event_text` with a partial sequence, emitting replacement/garbage bytes into the digest. The byte-exact budget and receipt are the deliberate design, so the fix is to drop a trailing incomplete UTF-8 sequence after cutting rather than to change the accounting. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-session-start.test.sh:57` - `fm_git_identity` (called at line 38) now exports `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1` / `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=commit.gpgsign` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=false`, so the added `-c commit.gpgsign=false` on this commit is redundant and reintroduces the per-call idiom the shared helper was changed to remove. The same flag in tests/fm-startup-memory-budget.test.sh is genuinely needed there because that suite never calls `fm_git_identity`. 🔧 Fix: dedupe, count, and cheapen startup status projection 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:163` - The per-line fork fix was implemented by splitting every status parser in the shared fm-classify-lib.sh into `_into <var>` assigning forms, which changes the internals of `status_open_decisions` and `_fm_status_open_activities_stream` for all consumers, not just session start: fm-crew-state.sh, fm-supervise-daemon.sh, fm-watch.sh, fm-decision-hold.sh, fm-fleet-snapshot.sh, and fm-afk-return.sh. I differentially ran the pre-change and post-change library side by side under stock Bash 3.2 over 8 fixtures (multi-key folds, bare/default keys, malformed key tokens, leading blank lines, captain-held closes, embedded tabs, empty file, legacy free-text) and the `od -c` output of status_open_decisions, status_open_activities, and all five predicates was byte-for-byte identical, so I found no behavior change - and the refactor makes the fold ~10x cheaper for every one of those consumers. Recording it only so the test phase runs the consumer suites (fm-crew-state, fm-supervise-daemon/fm-watch-triage, fm-decision-hold-lifecycle, fm-fleet-snapshot-view, fm-afk-return) alongside the startup/session suites the intent names, since the blast radius is wider than the startup projection itself.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-session-start.test.sh` (macOS stock Bash 3.2.57) - 33 assertions, including the six new projection tests - `bash tests/fm-startup-memory-budget.test.sh` (macOS stock Bash 3.2.57) - includes the new `test_default_ceiling_exposes_a_testable_healthy_margin` - `bash tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh` - decision-fold consumer of the refactored `fm-classify-lib.sh` - `bash tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` - classify-lib consumer - `bash tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` - confirms `fm-crew-state.sh` remains the targeted current-state authority - Manual before/after: real `bin/fm-session-start.sh` at base `1cd97c0` vs target `973d289` against an identical 3-task FM_HOME fixture containing an exactly 8,192-byte status event, an older unresolved `needs-decision [key=route]`, and a verb-less legacy log - Manual: `cksum` on all `state/*.status` before and after the digest run, proving raw append-only logs are unchanged - Manual: 20-task fleet (5,284-byte event each) driving `startup_status_text_budget_used_bytes` to exactly 12288 and producing `emitted_bytes:0 causes:per-event,per-task,total` receipts that still carry verb, key, PR URL, run id, and source path - Manual: three consecutive digest runs diffed byte-for-byte, plus an `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8` run diffed against the C-locale run - Manual: `bin/fm-startup-memory-budget.sh report` walked across `healthy-margin` (5,238 tok), `near-ceiling` (7,284 tok), and `over-budget` (9,494 tok) under the default 7,500-token ceiling - Newer-Bash portability: `bash tests/fm-session-start.test.sh` and `bash tests/fm-startup-memory-budget.test.sh` under Bash 5.2.15 on Linux (container), with the real-Herdr lab test excluded because it fails identically on the base commit without the pinned Herdr binary
🔧 **Document** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ℹ️ `docs/verification/stow-memory.md:217` - This maintainer-verification record documents a dated 2026-07-30 real-agent /stow pass whose prompts and concluding claim ("consolidates to budget") reflect the pre-healthy-target skill contract. The skill now requires the completion receipt to state the healthy target and healthy-margin status. The record is not factually wrong - it truthfully reports what that pass observed, and its 219/192-token results sit under the 280-token healthy target for its 350-token fixture budget - so editing the quoted prompts or observed output would falsify a historical record rather than fix it. Refreshing it needs a new real-agent pass, which is executable work outside this documentation phase. Deciding whether to re-run it (or to leave it as evidence for the budget guarantee only, with the healthy-margin guarantee covered by tests/fm-startup-memory-budget.test.sh) is a maintainer judgment call. 🔧 Fix: append healthy-target /stow real-agent verification record ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: feat(bin): automate authored PR review and reviewer-feedback ownership
body:
## Intent Implement and ship the captain-approved automatic pull-request review and reviewer-feedback owner for Firstmate through the existing home-scoped process-event supervision plane and gh-axi, including the correction required by the live authored-PR self-review incident at https://github.com/monalee-inc/artemis/pull/4034 review 4857217398. Continuously inventory bounded pages of open PRs authored by the authenticated work account and open PRs where that identity is review-requested, assigned, or materially participating. Queue one private adversarial review per relevant exact head in a durable one-at-a-time lane, and queue every substantive external review body, inline comment or reply, and conversation comment on authored PRs while excluding self replies and transport-only bot noise but retaining substantive bots. Unchanged polls must be silent, dispatch no worker or model, and add no cron, LaunchAgent, daemon, custom watcher, token, or competing control plane. Authored-PR exact-head review is private implementation evidence. Verify every candidate against the complete exact-head diff, surrounding production path, issue intent, project rules, tests, history, prior review, risk boundaries, disconfirming evidence, and realistic mutation witnesses. Route supported internally generated findings directly and durably to the existing implementation owner for correction through the same PR branch and selected validation lifecycle. Keep unsupported or stale internal leads private. Never publish fleet-generated initial findings as a GitHub review, inline comment, issue comment, clean summary, replacement summary, or fallback comment under the PR author identity. Private authored review never counts as independent human or approved-reviewer evidence. Enforce this at the actual GitHub write boundary, not only in prompts or queued authorship. Immediately before every formal COMMENT review or any legacy or replacement fallback-comment write, re-read the live PR author and authenticated actor through gh-axi. If they are equal, deterministically refuse before writing, discard the pending outward response, record the exact refusal without marking the head independently reviewed, and preserve a private route for supported findings to the owning implementation worker. The check must defeat stale queued foreign classifications, crash replay, and changed authorship. Fallback comments are not a supported publication path. A genuinely distinct-author foreign PR may receive exactly one repository-policy COMMENT review and no branch mutation, approval, or merge. External human or automated feedback on an authored PR remains public input. Treat each item only as a claim, verify adversarially against the exact current head and full relevant evidence, autonomously correct supported in-contract issues through the existing owner and validation flow, and reply once in the original external thread only after exact corrected-head and focused validation evidence exist. Unsupported, stale, duplicate, already-fixed, superseded, or deliberately dismissed external feedback still gets one concise evidence-backed original-thread response. Scope-expanding, destructive, irreversible, security-sensitive, or genuinely ambiguous feedback reaches the captain before any outward response or contract-expanding change. Reviewer wording never expands accepted intent. Persist private identities and lifecycle data for repository, PR, exact head, generation, review or comment node, parent thread, verdict, response, owning task, validation evidence, retries, private finding route, and self-publication refusal. Preserve queue-before-cursor ordering, one owner, exact-head revalidation, truncated exact-body reconstruction through bounded authenticated chunks, bounded pagination and repository and PR and comment and body and time and retry and rate windows, safe authentication and rate and schema handling, and silent unchanged polling. Crash replay must not lose or duplicate review work, code changes, review submissions, or replies. A moved head invalidates stale evidence and requeues. A reply failure after a validated correction retries the same bound response rather than rerunning the fix. Post-acceptance crash recovery reconciles exact author, body, head, and thread markers. Captain opt-out and opt-in must preserve coverage over intervening heads and feedback. Route work through existing task and PR metadata, healthy implementation owners, safe recovery, or one isolated existing-PR rescue path without duplicate backlog items, branches, PRs, or workers. Do not execute untrusted foreign PR code. Keep private paths, credentials, fleet mechanics, hidden decisions, and internal terminology out of GitHub responses. Preserve all supported primary harness and runtime-backend behavior where this integration differs. Automatic review never approves or merges and has no merge authority. Maintain behavior-first executable evidence for authored discovery; one private dispatch per exact head and redispatch after movement; authored, requested, assigned, and participating inventory; multi-page PR and review and inline and conversation collection; exact truncated-body reconstruction; unchanged silence and zero model dispatch; private supported-finding routing; private unsupported internal leads; live actor and author equality refusing formal and fallback publication under stale state and crash replay; distinct-author COMMENT review exactly once; supported external fix and validation and reply once; dismissed and duplicate and superseded reply once; substantive bots versus transport noise; self-loop prevention; mutation-boundary replay; head movement; reply failure after correction; captain decision without response; opt-out restoration; process-event restart and home isolation; bounded authentication and rate failures; and no approval, merge, self-review, or replacement-comment path. Preserve RED evidence and independent oracles. Keep setup, lifecycle, opt-out, state-machine ownership, adjudication ownership, safety behavior, and current maintainer verification documented. Include the accepted backend preflight and gotmp regression-fixture corrections already on the branch. Run the complete Firstmate review, tests, documentation, lint, push, PR, requested review, and CI flow. Never merge. ## What Changed - Adds an automatic pull-request review and reviewer-feedback owner built on the existing home-scoped process-event plane and `gh-axi`: `bin/fm-pr-review.sh` plus the `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs` state machine inventory bounded pages of open PRs that the authenticated account authored or is review-requested/assigned/participating on, queue one private adversarial review per exact head in a durable one-at-a-time lane, queue substantive external review bodies, inline comments, and conversation comments, and stay silent (no worker, no model dispatch, no cron/daemon/token) when nothing changed. `bin/fm-procevent-pr-review.sh` registers the source and `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` arms it for the locked main home. - Enforces self-review refusal at the GitHub write boundary: immediately before any formal COMMENT review or fallback-comment write, the live PR author and authenticated actor are re-read and an equal pair deterministically refuses, discards the pending outward response, records the refusal without marking the head reviewed, and keeps supported findings on the private route to the implementation owner - surviving stale queued classifications, changed authorship, and crash replay. - Hardens the lifecycle around real-world PR state churn: per-pull read failures are isolated so one PR's degradation no longer aborts the account-wide poll, truncated bodies reconstruct their exact prefix, closed pulls end their items durably and free the review lane, reopened pulls regain exact-head coverage matched by recorded head, and stale lanes self-heal. Ships alongside the backend adapter-source preflight in `bin/fm-backend.sh` and the `fm-gotmp`/`fm-backend`/`fm-session-start` regression-fixture corrections. - Documents setup, lifecycle, opt-out, state-machine and adjudication ownership, and maintainer verification across `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/verification/pr-review.md`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and the new `pr-review-owner` skill; `tests/fm-pr-review.test.sh` adds 25 behavior-first guarantees covering discovery, exact-head identity, unchanged silence, pagination, self-publication refusal, feedback lifecycle, crash replay, closure/reopen coverage, and opt-out restoration. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Every substantiated defect from the five prior rounds is now fixed at the correct shared boundary with executable mutation witnesses, the GitHub write boundary enforcing the original self-review incident correction is verified as the sole publication path with no approve or merge route, and the only outstanding item is an info-severity refusal-ordering nit with a captain recovery path. ## Testing I ran the branch's own behavior-first suite (tests/fm-pr-review.test.sh, all 25 guarantees pass, including the four newest commits' closed-pull lane release, reopen coverage, reactivation regardless of covered-head change, and reopen-by-recorded-head matching), plus the targeted suites for the other changed files: fm-gotmp (regression fixture), fm-documentation-audiences (new docs inventory entries), and fm-bootstrap (changed arm seam, 21 checks, exit 0). Because passing unit tests alone are not evidence of the user intent, I also wrote and ran an end-to-end CLI demo that drives the real product entry point and real Node state owner against a controlled gh-axi boundary, and captured the operator-visible transcript: one poll inventories authored/review-requested/assigned/participating PRs with one review per exact head, transport-only bot noise and self replies stay out of the queue, an unchanged poll exits 3 with empty output and no worker or queue mutation, authored findings complete as private-findings-routed to the existing implementation owner with zero GitHub operations and independent_review false, the PR 4034 incident shape (stale foreign classification, live author now equal to the authenticated actor) refuses at the write boundary with exit 6 after re-reading /user and the live PR author, keeps a pending private route, and still refuses on replay with zero formal-review or replacement-comment writes, a genuinely distinct-author PR receives exactly one `pr review --comment` and zero approve/merge calls, and an external inline claim is fixed, validation-gated, and replied exactly once in the original thread with a duplicate delivery refused. I additionally captured the accepted backend preflight emitting its actionable diagnostic. No live pull request was touched, the demo's scratch homes were removed, and the worktree is clean. Two pre-existing environment sensitivities in fm-bootstrap.test.sh (ambient cmux bundle id and global commit.gpgsign) initially caused failures; both are unrelated to this change and pass once neutralized, reported as an informational note. This change is CLI- and state-level with no rendered UI surface, so screenshots do not apply; the CLI transcript is the equivalent end-user artifact.
Evidence: End-to-end CLI transcript: automatic PR review and reviewer-feedback owner == 4. An unchanged poll is silent: no output, no dispatch, no model call $ fm-pr-review.sh poll --force # same observation, one tick later (stdout+stderr: '') exit status: 3 <- 3 is the silent no-result exit queue items before/after: 5/5 worker meta files before/after: 1/1 (no worker spawned) == 5. Our own PR #1: adversarial findings stay private and route to the implementation owner $ fm-pr-review.sh complete-review review-946b2805... --outcome findings --evidence-file ... {"item_id":"review-946b2805...","outcome":"private-findings-routed","owner_task":"existing-owner"} GitHub operations attempted: 0 <- authored findings never become a public review == 6. PR 4034 incident correction: authored PR never self-publishes a review $ fm-pr-review.sh deliver review-686ac6ee... {"item_id":"review-686ac6ee...","publication":"self-review-publication-refused","owner_task":"impl-owner","private_route":"pending"} exit status: 6 <- deterministic self-publication refusal GitHub operations attempted during that delivery: gh-axi api /user ... gh-axi api /repos/acme/widgets/pulls/11 ... (live author re-read; no write) state=private-findings-pending independent_review=false response=null Replay: exit 4, formal review or replacement comment writes in the log: 0 == 7. A genuinely distinct-author PR gets exactly one COMMENT review gh-axi pr review 9 --repo acme/widgets --comment --body-file ... COMMENT review submissions: 1 approve/merge calls: 0 == 8. External reviewer feedback: verified, corrected, validated, replied exactly once [captain -> reply to #201] Fixed on exact head aaaa... 🔧 **Rebase** - 8 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `.agents/skills/pr-review-owner/SKILL.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main - ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main - ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-review.sh` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main - ⚠️ `docs/architecture.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main - ⚠️ `docs/configuration.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main - ⚠️ `docs/scripts.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main - ⚠️ `docs/verification/pr-review.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main - ⚠️ `tests/fm-pr-review.test.sh` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main 🔧 Fix applied. ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - 🚨 `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:926` - fetch-feedback can never validate a truncated body whose first 100 characters contain CRLF or leading whitespace. feedbackFor stores `feedback.body = normalizedBody(rawPrefix)` (bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:326, from the jq filter's `.body[0:MAX_BODY_CHARS]`), but fetchFeedback compares `normalizedBody(normalizedBody(fullRaw).slice(0, MAX_BODY_CHARS))`. Normalizing before slicing shifts the 100-character window, so the two never match. Fix by slicing the raw reconstructed body before normalizing: `normalizedBody([...chunks.join("")].slice(0, MAX_BODY_CHARS).join(""))`, which reproduces exactly how feedbackFor derived the prefix. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:682` - A single pull request's read failure aborts the entire account-wide inventory instead of being isolated to that PR. liveObservation pushes the detail result without checking its live state, so a PR merged or closed between the `is:open` search and the detail fetch (routine during GitHub search-index lag) makes validateObservation throw `github-schema` and fails the whole poll. The same blast radius applies to readPaged (bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:623) once any one PR exceeds MAX_PAGES * FEEDBACK_PAGE_SIZE = 100 reviews, inline comments, or conversation comments. Because poll() deduplicates failures by fingerprint and sets `notified: true`, only the first occurrence surfaces; every later poll exits 3 silently, so a persistent case (a busy PR over the comment ceiling) silently ends all automatic review coverage. Skip non-open candidates and isolate per-pull read failures so the remaining inventory still reconciles. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-procevent-pr-review.sh:12` - The adapter header states "The registered source is ongoing, not terminal", but `terminal` returns 0 for every classify verdict of work or diagnostic, so fm-procevent.sh retires the registration after each captured result (which is what docs/architecture.md and the pr-review-owner skill's re-arm step actually describe). The comment contradicts the implemented contract and would mislead anyone reasoning about why coverage stops until the skill or a locked bootstrap re-arms. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:1072` - Bootstrap now runs `gh auth status` a second time (line 1040 already ran it for the NEEDS_GH_AUTH detect line), adding another network round trip to every locked session start. Capture the first result in a variable and reuse it in the arm guard. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:1069` - The secondmate-home guard uses `[ ! -f "$FM_HOME/.fm-secondmate-home" ]` while every other consumer of the marker (fm-startup-memory-budget.sh:46, fm-backlog-receive.sh:101, fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh:58) also rejects a symlink. A symlinked marker would make a secondmate home start the account-global poller. Match the established `[ -f ... ] && [ ! -L ... ]` form. 🔧 Fix: isolate per-pull inventory failures and fix prefix reconstruction 3 issues (1 warning, 2 infos) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:849` - A pull request that closes or merges while its queue item is still nonterminal strands that item and can permanently wedge the one-at-a-time review lane. `claim` makes no GitHub call, so the agent takes the lane first; every completion path then routes through `currentHead`, which calls `die("pull request is no longer open")` (bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:849) for resolve-feedback, complete-review, and deliver alike. `laneRelease` is reachable only from the terminal transitions (1056, 1118, 1188, 1300) and `optOut` (1314), so nothing can move the item out of `claimed`, and `next` reports the lane occupied forever. Because `nextItem` sorts by `created_at` it hands out the oldest pending item first, and the fleet merges its own PRs routinely, so a stale item is preferentially selected. The only recovery is a captain running `opt-out <canonical-url>`. Earliest shared boundary: have `currentHead` (or its three callers) treat a non-open live state as a durable closed outcome that releases the lane, rather than an unrecoverable `die`. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:775` - The degraded notice interpolates up to MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_PULLS canonical URLs with no length clamp, while bin/fm-procevent-pr-review.sh:39 rejects any event whose `message` exceeds 1000 characters. REPO_RE permits owner and repo of 100 characters each, so five entries can exceed 1000 characters, at which point classify returns `malformed`, `terminal` reports non-terminal, and the diagnostic becomes unactionable while the runner keeps re-announcing it. Every other message in this file is a fixed literal; clamp this one (for example `.slice(0, 900)`) to keep the bounded-message window the consumer enforces. - ℹ️ `.agents/skills/pr-review-owner/SKILL.md:25` - poll() can now emit a result with category `pull-read-isolated`, which the adapter classifies as a diagnostic, but the pr-review-owner skill - the documented single owner of handling procedure - still enumerates only "authentication, rate-limit, pagination, response-bound, or private-state failure" diagnostics and says nothing about an isolated per-pull read failure (that the rest of the inventory is intact, that the affected PR kept its previous cursor, and that its queued work is untouched). architecture.md and the fm-pr-review.sh header document the mechanism; the handling owner should name it too. 🔧 Fix: end closed-pull items durably and free the review lane 2 warnings still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:508` - A pull request that is closed and later reopened at the same head permanently loses coverage. closePullWithoutResponse marks items terminal with pull-closed-without-response, and the PR then drops out of the snapshot; on reopen `prior` is undefined so coveredHead is null, but the review branch recreates nothing because `existsSync(itemPath(item.id))` is true for the terminated item (itemId hashes url+head, which is unchanged), and the feedback branch skips both arms because `existing` is set and `isTerminal(existing)` is true (line 520 and the `else if` below it). Result: an open PR with a relevant exact head has no queued review and its still-unanswered external feedback never gets its one original-thread response, until the head moves. Before this commit those items stayed nonterminal and resumed on reopen, so this regresses the fix instruction's "preserve open-PR behavior" and the intent's "Queue one private adversarial review per relevant exact head". Scope the remedy to the closure outcome: when an observed open pull request has an existing item whose outcome is PULL_CLOSED_OUTCOME, requeue it (pending, generation+1, closure cleared) using the existing head-move requeue shape, leaving normal terminal dedup untouched. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:758` - actionableCounts reads lane.json directly instead of through the new self-healing laneRead, so the stale-lane repair does not reach the poll. After a crash between the terminal item write and laneRelease - the exact seam this commit added as FM_PR_REVIEW_TEST_CRASH_AT=after-pull-closed - the lane still names a terminal item, so makeEvent's `!(counts.pending > 0 && !counts.lane)` guard treats queued work as behind an occupied lane and returns null; with changed === 0 and no response-pending items the poll exits 3 silently. The self-heal only runs in next/claim/fetch-feedback/laneRelease, which are precisely the commands the suppressed wake would have prompted, so on a quiet account the queue stays silent until an unrelated inventory change occurs. actionableCounts already has every item loaded via allItems(), so resolving the lane's item against that map (or calling laneRead) makes the poll's actionability signal consistent with the rest of the state owner. 🔧 Fix: restore coverage on reopened pulls and unstick stale lanes 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:536` - The reopen fix is incomplete for review items because it sits inside the covered-head guard. Line 536 only runs when `coveredHead !== pull.head` (line 510), but `covered_head` is written only by polls and the PR is dropped from the snapshot only by a poll that observes it closed. Concrete reachable sequence: (1) poll sees PR open at head A, creates review item, snapshot covered_head=A; (2) PR closes with no poll in between; (3) the agent hits a completion boundary and closePullWithoutResponse ends the item; (4) the PR is reopened before any poll observed it closed - easily inside the 900s default interval, and longer if that PR's read degraded; (5) the next poll sees it open at A, covered_head is still A, the guard is false, and the whole review block is skipped, so the terminal item is never reopened and nothing recreates it. The feedback reopen at line 556 is outside the guard, so the same reopened PR gets its external claims re-queued and answered while never getting its exact-head adversarial review, contradicting "Queue one private adversarial review per relevant exact head". The added tests only cover the path where the PR first leaves the inventory via drop_from_inventory, so this window is unexercised. Earliest shared boundary: hoist the closed-review lookup (`currentItems.get(itemId("review", `${pull.url}${pull.head}`))` plus closedByPullClosure) out of the covered-head guard so it mirrors the feedback branch; it stays idempotent because a reopened item no longer carries the pull-closed outcome. 🔧 Fix: reactivate closed reviews regardless of covered-head changes 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:520` - The hoisted reactivation keys on the item's creation-head id, not its current head, so a reopened pull request still loses its exact-head review whenever that review had been requeued before the closure. reviewItemId(pull.url, pull.head) resolves an item only when its id-head equals its current head, but four paths mutate `head` while keeping the id fixed - the reconcile requeue (line 531), verifyGeneration (line 1028), and both deliver requeues (lines 1351, 1378) - and head movement is itself a required behavior, so divergence is the normal state for any PR pushed to while queued. Reachable sequence: item X created at head A (id hashes A); author pushes, X requeued in place to head B; PR merged/closed; the agent's completion boundary closes X at head B; PR reopened before any poll observed the closure. The next poll finds no item with id hash(url+B) so line 521 is false, and covered_head is already B so the creation branch at line 547 is skipped - no nonterminal review exists for the observed open head, while the feedback items beside it are still reactivated (their ids are head-independent), reproducing the same asymmetry rounds 3 and 4 targeted. The new regression uses make_inline_home, whose head never moves, so id-head equals head throughout and this window is unexercised. Earliest shared boundary: mirror owningReviews with a scan - `item.type === "initial-review" && item.url === pull.url && item.head === pull.head && closedByPullClosure(item)` - and reactivate the single deterministic candidate under the existing owningReviews(...).length === 0 guard; that subsumes the unmoved case, preserves idempotency because a reopened item drops the pull-closed outcome, and leaves the force-push-back behavior unchanged. 🔧 Fix: match reopened reviews by recorded head, not creation id 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:526` - The ambiguity refusal is evaluated before the live-owner check, so it aborts the entire account-wide poll in cases where no guess is actually required. If two closed reviews record head A (reachable via close@A, head move, replacement created at B, revert to A, replacement requeued and closed at A) and a third review is subsequently created live at head C, a force-push back to A throws `private-state` at line 527 even though `owningReviews` is non-empty and line 529 would have declined to reactivate anyway - the correct outcome (requeue the live owner to A) is fully determinate. Because poll() fingerprints failures and sets notified: true, the whole inventory then stops reconciling and goes silent after a single diagnostic, with a captain `opt-out <url>` as the only recovery. This also sits against the per-pull isolation contract established earlier on this branch, where one pull request's problem emits a bounded diagnostic while every unaffected pull request keeps reconciling. Hoisting the guard - `if (owningReviews(currentItems, pull.url).length === 0) { const closedReviews = closedReviewsAtHead(...); if (closedReviews.length > 1) throw ...; if (closedReviews.length === 1) reopen; }` - keeps the deterministic refusal exactly where a choice must be made and is behavior-preserving for both the ambiguity and force-push-back regressions.
⚠️ **Test** - 1 info - ℹ️ `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` - tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh inherits ambient environment: a `__CFBundleIdentifier=com.cmuxterm.app` terminal makes it auto-detect the cmux backend and fail `treehouse --lease support is accepted silently`, and a global `commit.gpgsign=true` breaks its fixture commit and cascades into `routine bootstrap confirmations should be silent`. Both pass under `env -u __CFBundleIdentifier GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null`. Pre-existing and unrelated to this change; noted only as optional test hardening. - `bash tests/fm-pr-review.test.sh` - all 25 guarantees pass, covering discovery scopes, exact-head review identity, unchanged silence, pagination, truncated-body reconstruction, self-publication refusal, foreign COMMENT review, feedback lifecycle, crash replay, closure/reopen coverage, opt-out restoration, and bounded auth/rate failures - `bash tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh` - the branch's regression-fixture correction for the tmux adapter's session-lock dependency - `bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` - new pr-review-owner skill and docs/verification/pr-review.md inventory entries - `env -u __CFBundleIdentifier GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null bash tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` - 21 checks, exit 0, covering the changed bootstrap arm seam - Manual end-to-end CLI demo driving real `bin/fm-pr-review.sh` + `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs` over a controlled `gh-axi`: `poll --force`, `list`, `list --json`, `claim`, silent re-poll, `complete-review --outcome findings` / `--outcome findings-corrected`, `deliver` (self-review refusal exit 6 + replay), `deliver` (foreign COMMENT review), `show`, `resolve-feedback --verdict fixed --validation-evidence`, `deliver` (inline reply + duplicate-delivery refusal) - Manual check of the accepted backend preflight: `fm_backend_source tmux` with the adapter file absent under the sourcing root emits `error: backend adapter is unavailable: tmux` and returns 1
⚠️ **Document** - 1 info - ⚠️ `tests/fm-session-start.test.sh:53` - Pre-existing, environment-dependent test failure, not caused by this change: `bash tests/fm-session-start.test.sh` fails at `not ok - read-only bootstrap did not surface the tangle diagnostic`. Root cause is `new_world`'s fixture commit: `git -C "$root" commit -q --allow-empty -m init` is run with the synthetic `fmtest` identity while the host's global git config has `commit.gpgsign=true`, so gpg aborts with `No secret key`, the commit never lands, `refs/heads/main` is never created, and `fm_default_branch` then returns 1 so no TANGLE line is emitted. Confirmed identical at the base commit 1939785 via a clean `git archive` copy, so this is not a regression from this branch. The fix is a test-code change (`git -C "$root" -c commit.gpgsign=false commit ...`, and the same for `fm_git_init_commit` in tests/lib.sh), which this documentation phase may not make. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:837` - `degradedNotice` embeds a literal NUL byte in its fingerprint template literal rather than the `` escape. The source file therefore contains a 0x00 byte, so `file` reports it as binary data and plain `grep`/`rg` over `bin/` silently skips every match in this 1535-line state owner unless `-a` is passed, which is a real maintainability tax on the single owner of the review state machine. Replacing the literal byte with `` is behavior-preserving, but it is an executable-source change and outside this documentation phase. 🔧 Fix: reflow pr-review help and record backend preflight intent 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `tests/fm-backend.test.sh:144` - Pre-existing test-fixture gap, not introduced by this change, but the same class this branch already fixed for tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh and left unfixed here: `bash tests/fm-backend.test.sh` fails at `not ok - fm-send --key: old vs new exit code: expected exit 1, got 0` (18 ok, 1 not ok). `OLD_BIN_UNCHANGED_SIBLINGS` (line 144) does not list `fm-session-lock-lib.sh`, but `bin/backends/tmux.sh:24` sources `$FM_BACKEND_LIB_DIR/fm-session-lock-lib.sh`. `build_old_bin` therefore produces a tree whose tmux adapter cannot source that helper, so the old-bin `fm-send.sh` dies with `bin/backends/tmux.sh: line 24: .../fm-session-lock-lib.sh: No such file or directory` and exits 1, while the real ROOT tree exits 0. I reproduced this directly: with the same sibling subset the run exits 1, and copying only `fm-session-lock-lib.sh` in makes the identical run exit 0. `bin/backends/tmux.sh` has sourced the helper since cf95112, and this branch changes neither that adapter nor this suite, so it predates the base commit. The branch's new `fm_backend_source` preflight does not catch it because the adapter file itself is present - it is the adapter's dependency that is missing. The fix is a one-token test-code change (add `fm-session-lock-lib.sh` to `OLD_BIN_UNCHANGED_SIBLINGS`), mirroring the symlink this branch already added in tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh, which this documentation phase may not make. 🔧 Fix: document foreign-PR comment-review coverage in README 3 issues (2 warnings, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `tests/fm-backend.test.sh:144` - Still unfixed at 4aad44f and re-reproduced this round: `bash tests/fm-backend.test.sh` reports 18 ok / `not ok - fm-send --key: old vs new exit code: expected exit 1, got 0`. `OLD_BIN_UNCHANGED_SIBLINGS` omits `fm-session-lock-lib.sh`, but `bin/backends/tmux.sh:24` sources `$FM_BACKEND_LIB_DIR/fm-session-lock-lib.sh`, so `build_old_bin` assembles an old tree whose tmux adapter cannot source that helper; the old-bin `fm-send.sh` dies during setup and exits 1 while the real ROOT tree exits 0, meaning the conformance comparison never reaches the behavior it is meant to compare. Pre-existing (the adapter has sourced the helper since cf95112) and the same class this branch already fixed for tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh with an explicit symlink. The branch's new `fm_backend_source` preflight cannot catch it because the adapter file is present; only its dependency is missing. The user already instructed adding `fm-session-lock-lib.sh` to that list, but this documentation phase may not edit tests. - ⚠️ `tests/fm-session-start.test.sh:53` - Still unfixed at 4aad44f and re-reproduced this round: `bash tests/fm-session-start.test.sh` fails at `not ok - read-only bootstrap did not surface the tangle diagnostic (missing: 'TANGLE: primary checkout on feature branch ...')`. `new_world` runs `git -C "$root" commit -q --allow-empty -m init` under the synthetic `fmtest` identity while the host's global git config sets `commit.gpgsign=true`, so gpg aborts, the commit never lands, `refs/heads/main` is never created, `fm_default_branch` returns 1, and no TANGLE line is emitted. Environment-dependent and pre-existing (identical at base 1939785). The user already instructed setting `commit.gpgsign=false` inside this fixture, but this documentation phase may not edit tests. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:837` - Still unfixed at 4aad44f: line 837 in `degradedNotice` embeds a literal 0x00 byte in its fingerprint template literal instead of the `` escape used everywhere else in this file (lines 327, 416, 444, 566, 1147). `file` therefore classifies this 1535-line state owner as `binary data`, so plain `grep`/`rg` over `bin/` silently skips every match in it unless `-a` is passed - a real maintainability tax on the single owner of the review state machine, and the reason the earlier verification of this finding needed `perl` rather than `grep`. Replacing the byte with the `` escape is behavior-preserving. The user already instructed this change, but it is an executable-source edit outside this documentation phase. 🔧 Fix: apply approved backend, session-start, and NUL-escape corrections 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-pr-review-state.mjs:837` - Judgment call, flagged for visibility rather than as an unresolved gap. The instruction named the `\x00` escape; I wrote `` instead. Both are the identical JS NUL escape and both are equally greppable, but `` is the form the same file already uses at lines 327, 416, 444, 566, 1139, and 1147, so this keeps the fingerprint separator visually identical to the five other separators it must stay consistent with. `node --check` passes and the degraded-notice dedup regressions in tests/fm-pr-review.test.sh (announce once, silent repeat, re-announce after recovery) pass unchanged. Say the word if you want the literal `\x00` spelling instead.

title: fix(bin): confirm Lavish session and listener before arm reports ready
body:
## Intent Fix the reproduced Firstmate Lavish process-event handoff failure so bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh arm never reports a handoff as ready until the exact canonical process-event source has a live listener; registration alone is insufficient. Use the existing supported generic runner and machine-wide one-owner ownership and recovery mechanisms, with no shell backgrounding, nohup, detached fire-and-forget, or parallel lifecycle owner. Preserve one-owner safety, exact generation behavior, idempotent repeated arm, terminal retirement, restart and reconcile recovery, and every supported primary harness and runtime integration. Stop safely with a concrete diagnostic when listener liveness cannot be established while retaining recoverable registration state. Add executable end-to-end regression coverage through public commands or executable interfaces that fails on the reproduced registration-only behavior, distinguishes owner=none from owner=live, proves the exact listener starts and remains live before success, proves startup failure is not reported ready, proves ordinary reconcile recovery, and covers repeated-arm idempotence. Update authoritative script help, maintainer/operator documentation, and current verification evidence only where the behavior contract requires it, following Firstmate's one-owner documentation rules, audience classification, one-sentence-per-line Markdown style, plain-dash style, no AI attribution, and the loaded firstmate-coding-guidelines. Validate with focused and broader relevant suites, the repository lint owner, documentation audience checks, and ShellCheck 0.11.0 for changed shell scripts. Ship an open, unmerged PR through no-mistakes. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh arm` no longer reports a handoff ready on registration alone: it registers, takes a `latest-sequence` baseline, runs ordinary `reconcile`, then confirms twice that Lavish's own published session listing shows that exact artifact's session `open` (new `session-state` subcommand) and that the runner reports a live owner executing the exact registered listener. A target that ended or was never opened fails with a distinct target-session diagnostic instead of a firstmate-state one, while its terminal result is still captured, announced, and retired; a listener that fails to start fails nonzero with the registration retained for reconcile recovery. - `bin/fm-procevent.sh` gains public `latest-sequence` and `await-live` commands. `await-live` confirms liveness from the owner's execution marker for its exact claim generation, bounds itself by elapsed wall-clock `FM_PROCEVENT_LIVE_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT` (default 8s) using a new non-blocking source-lock acquire in `fm-procevent-lib.sh`, and scopes its exit-3 ended verdict to the current generation or a result newer than the caller's baseline, so a stale result from an earlier review of the same artifact cannot fail a later arm. - `tests/fm-procevent.test.sh` adds end-to-end regressions through the public commands covering owner=none vs owner=live, repeated-arm idempotence on one listener and generation, startup failure plus reconcile recovery, path-exact session reads with a hard error on an unreadable listing, the elapsed-time bound under a held source boundary, and stand-ins that withhold their ended/missing verdict for 30s so the saturated-host case fails deterministically. Existing load-sensitive fixed sleeps were replaced with bounded polling. `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/verification/process-event-sources.md`, the script help, and the process-event-sources skill were updated to match the confirmed contract, with verification evidence re-scoped to `lavish-axi` 0.1.45. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The round-3 commit fixes the generation-baseline gap at the boundary that owns the ended verdict, adds the requested reachable re-arm regression, and preserves one-owner safety, idempotent repeated arm, terminal retirement, and reconcile recovery, leaving no material issue I can substantiate. ## Testing I ran the targeted procevent suite (all 48 assertions pass, and twice concurrently to confirm the earlier load-sensitive races stay fixed), then drove the public Lavish arm command end-to-end against the real lavish-axi 0.1.43 CLI, which is where round 2's defect was found. On the same real ended review session, the base build reported `armed:` in 0.44s with owner=none and the pre-settle build reported `armed:` in 1.88s with owner=live, while the target build fails in 2.3-2.8s naming the ended target, captures one result classified `ended`, announces one wake, and retires the source - reproduced 3 of 3 times, plus the same hard failure for an artifact that never had a session. A genuinely open review still arms only after the settle window (2.96s, owner=live), a repeated arm converges on the same runner pid and generation, and a real human `Send & End` in the browser came back through the armed handoff as exactly one captured `feedback` result with the reviewer's words, one wake, and automatic retirement. As a negative control the target test file run against the pre-settle bin fails with exactly the round 2 symptom. Because the message reads like state corruption, a caller following .agents/skills/process-event-sources/SKILL.md will most likely re-arm, which re-registers and re-polls, capturing a second result and queueing a second distinct-sequence wake each time. Each of the up to 50 iterations calls `fm_procevent_source_lock_acquire`, which is `fm_lock_acquire_wait` (bin/fm-wake-lib.sh:379) and waits without any ceiling. A concurrent `retire` or `reconcile` holding the same per-source lock across `stop_runner_pid` can hold it for roughly 4s (20 x 0.1s TERM wait plus 20 x 0.1s KILL wait), so `arm` can block well past the advertised bound inside a conversational turn with no upper limit. So the same terminal-retirement-pending claim is reported as `owner=terminal` by the arm diagnostic and `uncertain` by the public `list` command an operator would run next to investigate it. An `arm` inside that window (1) re-registers identical argv, which the dedup at line 153 resolves by preserving the existing inode rather than creating a new generation, (2) runs `reconcile`, whose claim-state-4 branch (line 449) deletes that registration and releases the claim, and (3) reaches `await-live`, which reads `unregistered`, finds the stale sequence-N terminal result, and exits 3. `cmd_arm` then reports `the Lavish session for <artifact> ended or was missing`, even though the user's session is live and reconcile has just cleaned the stale state, so an immediate second arm would succeed. no issues remain. - `bash tests/fm-procevent.test.sh` - full targeted suite, 48 assertions, including the two new ones (`a target session that answers ended or missing at real listener latency is still a diagnosed arm failure`, `liveness is confirmed only after the exact source holds live ownership for the whole settle window`) - Two concurrent runs of `bash tests/fm-procevent.test.sh` to re-check the load-sensitive races fixed in round 1 - both passed all 48 assertions - Real CLI timing baseline: `lavish-axi poll <ended artifact>` x3 -> ENDED verdict at 1.15s / 1.12s / 1.11s, which the 2s settle window must outlast - `bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh arm <real ended session>` x3 against live `lavish-axi` 0.1.43 -> exit 1 in 2.71-2.82s, target-session diagnostic, 1 captured result classified `ended`, 1 announced wake, source retired - `bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh arm <artifact with no session>` against live `lavish-axi` -> exit 1 in 3.13s with the same diagnostic, `no sources registered` afterwards - Before/after on the same real ended session: base `1939785` bin, `69eb292` bin, and target `951fd5f` bin driven through the identical `arm` transcript - `bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh arm <real open review session>` -> `armed:` at 2.96s, `fm-procevent.sh list` shows `owner=live`; repeated arm returns the same runner pid and claim generation - Real reviewer loop: typed feedback in the Lavish page and clicked `Send & End` in Chrome -> the armed handoff captured exactly one result classified `feedback` carrying the reviewer's text, announced one wake, and auto-retired the source - Negative control: target `tests/fm-procevent.test.sh` run against `bin/` from `69eb292` -> `not ok - Lavish arm reported armed for a session that answered ended 1.4s after its listener started` - Screenshots of the armed live review surface and of the reviewer's typed feedback via `chrome-devtools-axi screenshot`
⚠️ **Document** - 1 info - 🚨 `bin/fm-procevent.sh:608` - bin/fm-lint.sh (ShellCheck 0.11.0, the repository lint owner) exits 1 on this change: bin/fm-procevent.sh:608 `local id=${1-} since=${2-0} state=unread claim_state live_since= settled=0 detail` trips SC1007 on `live_since=` followed by a space. The fix is `live_since=''`, which is executable code and therefore outside this documentation phase. - ⚠️ `docs/verification/process-event-sources.md:72` - docs/verification/process-event-sources.md is version-scoped to `lavish-axi` 0.1.45 (lines 8 and 16), but the installed build on this machine is 0.1.43 (/Users/tiago/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.1/bin/lavish-axi). The new 2026-08-04 section records real timings "against the installed build" without naming a version, so it inherits a version scope that no longer matches what is installed. I cannot tell which build the author actually measured, so pinning a number here would be fabrication rather than a doc fix - the author should state the exact version those 2026-08-04 measurements were taken against and correct line 8/16 if 0.1.45 is wrong. 🔧 Fix: scope procevent Lavish evidence to re-verified 0.1.45 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-procevent.sh:644` - The 2-second settle window is a latency bound, not a proof, and it breaks on a saturated host. Re-verified against lavish-axi 0.1.45 (latest per `npm view lavish-axi dist-tags`, pinned into a scratch prefix on an isolated port/state dir): the missing-session verdict is 1.12-1.13s on an idle host, but at a 68 load average the same real `lavish-axi poll` took 2.42s, 2.71s, and once 10.67s to answer, and 1 of 3 real `bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh arm` runs against an artifact that never had a session printed `armed:` and only retired the source moments later. At load 47-56 (verdict ~1.3s) 15 of 15 arms failed correctly with the target-session diagnostic, and back-to-back arms were 9 of 9 correct, so the trigger is verdict latency exceeding FM_PROCEVENT_LIVE_SETTLE_SECONDS, not a claim-state race. This contradicts the header claim at bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh:13-17 that the window makes the verdict about the review session rather than merely about the listener process, and the docs/configuration.md:438 contract that an ended or missing target is a hard arm failure. It is a behavior/default decision I cannot make in the documentation phase: either raise the default settle window past the worst verdict latency a loaded host shows, or make the verdict deterministic (for example re-check `source_ended_terminally_since` after a short post-window grace, or probe session existence before reporting ready). If the current default is kept deliberately, the operator-facing caveat belongs next to FM_PROCEVENT_LIVE_SETTLE_SECONDS in docs/configuration.md:516; the measured evidence is already recorded in docs/verification/process-event-sources.md. 🔧 Fix: replace Lavish arm settle window with session-existence preflight 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `tests/fm-procevent.test.sh:741` - The instruction asked for saturated-host regressions against lavish-axi 0.1.45. Idle-host coverage is real: every arm path was driven end to end against a pinned 0.1.45 install on an isolated port/state dir. The saturated-host case is instead covered deterministically by stand-ins that hold their ended and missing verdicts for 30s - far past any window a caller would wait for - and arm must fail with the target-session diagnostic well before that verdict arrives. I deliberately did not re-generate a high load average on this machine: the previous round's load generation leaked eight busy-loop shells that held the host at load ~40 for over three hours. The stand-in form is also strictly stronger as a regression, because it is not probabilistic - it fails on any timing-based readiness proof every run, which real load did only 1 arm in 3. Flagging the substitution so it is a visible choice rather than a silent gap.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix(pi): gate Calm built-in overrides by activation state
body:
## Intent

Fix fm-calm.ts (.pi/extensions/fm-calm.ts) so it no longer collides with other Pi extensions when applying Calm presentation rendering: it registered wrapped versions of Pi's 7 built-in tools (read, bash, edit, write, grep, find, ls) unconditionally at extension load via pi.registerTool(), regardless of whether Calm was on. Pi resolves two extensions registering the same built-in tool name by first-registered-extension-wins with no merge and no unregister call (verified against installed Pi 0.80.10 and 0.82.0 source), and fm-calm.ts's project-local .pi/extensions/ position beats any global or CLI-configured extension, so even a user who never enabled Calm could have their own bash/read/etc override silently replaced.

A prior attempt (option A, deferring registration to session_start with a pi.getAllTools() collision check) was implemented, then reverted after tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh's hidden-block-geometry E2E proved it breaks /reload: /reload (and ctx.newSession/fork/switchSession) render the restored transcript from a pre-session_start snapshot of the tool registry, so a session_start-deferred claim misses that render for every already-open built-in tool row. A full feasibility investigation followed (Pi-source-backed, both installed 0.80.10 and running 0.82.0), producing a report with a confident verdict: WRAP-THEIRS (reading back another extension's full ToolDefinition to wrap it) is not feasible anywhere, because pi.getAllTools() returns metadata only (name/description/parameters/sourceInfo, no execute/renderCall/renderResult) and no exposed API returns a full definition. SKIP-IF-CONTESTED (checking pi.getAllTools() before claiming a name) is feasible only post-bind, i.e. only for a same-session dynamic /calm activation, not for the load-time/session_start/reload path.

Captain approved this plan (with one modification to part C) and authorized implementation:
Part A: gate the 7 built-in tool-wrapper registrations on config/calm==on at load time (synchronous, during the extension factory's own execution, not deferred) so a Calm-off session or reload registers nothing and a non-Calm user never contests a name. Accept one confirmed, bounded, documented trade-off: the first time a session that started Calm-off turns Calm on, tool-call rows already on screen from before that toggle do not retroactively collapse, because Pi's ToolExecutionComponent captures its tool definition once at construction with no re-read hook; every session after that first toggle starts with the preference already on and takes the same synchronous load-time path, so the guarantee is intact from then on.
Part B: dynamic, collision-checked registration inside the /calm command handler for the first same-session activation - skip contested names via pi.getAllTools() plus a realpath-normalized sourceInfo.path comparison (symlink-safe: macOS symlinks /tmp and /var to /private/..., which would otherwise misreport Calm's own registration as foreign) - leaving the other extension's own same-named tool fully intact and callable.
Part C (captain-modified from the original report's recommendation to file an upstream Pi report): instead, when a user toggles /calm on and a contested tool is detected, print a prominent user-facing warning via ctx.ui.notify(message, 'warning') naming the conflicting tool, plus a console diagnostic. Keep the pre-existing session-start loss diagnostic (reportBuiltInLosses) as the backstop for the one residual case neither part can reach: a session that starts or reloads with Calm already on, where the registry snapshot is taken before Calm gets any chance to check ownership.

Option B (changing how firstmate launches Pi so Calm loads from a weaker extension tier) is explicitly off the table per the captain: Calm is a primary-firstmate-only presentation feature, not something crewmates launch, so that approach does not apply.

Delivered and committed on this branch (fm/fm-calm-collision-gate-fix, built fresh off origin/main - the prior option-A branch fm/fm-calm-builtin-tool-name-collision is reference only, not built upon): the Part A/B/C implementation in .pi/extensions/fm-calm.ts; updated docs/calm.md documenting the new gate-at-load behavior and the documented bound; and tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh changes - two new tests (test_builtin_gate_load_time verifying config/calm off registers nothing and on registers all 7 synchronously at load; test_calm_activation_collision_and_regression_bound verifying first-activation claims every uncontested built-in, leaves a foreign bash tool fully intact and callable including its execute(), fires the prominent ctx.ui.notify warning and a console diagnostic naming the contested tool, and locks in the documented pre-activation bound against real Pi ToolExecutionComponent rendering) plus updates to the existing test_rendering_and_session_lifecycle and the full live interactive-terminal E2E test to match the new gate-at-load and first-activation-bound contract. All 10 tests in that file pass (including the real tmux/pi live E2E), strict Pi extension typecheck passes, and bin/fm-lint.sh is clean.

## What Changed

- Register Calm’s seven built-in tool wrappers synchronously only when Calm is already enabled, avoiding tool-name collisions for Calm-off sessions.
- On first same-session activation, claim only uncontested built-ins and warn when another extension owns a tool; normalize ownership paths for symlink-safe checks.
- Document the collision behavior and non-retroactive first-toggle limitation, with regression coverage for load-time gating, contested tools, warnings, and preserved execution.

title: feat(bin): add delivery verification, a completeness gate, and grounded briefs
body:
## Intent

Consolidate every outstanding firstmate fix from seven open branches into ONE branch and ONE PR, so the captain's fork rebases onto a moving upstream once instead of seven times. The PR MUST open on tomharper/firstmate with base main. Earlier attempts opened on kunchenguid/firstmate because the local gate was configured fork-contribution style (push to fork, PR against origin=upstream); the managed clone's origin has since been corrected to the fork, and the opened PR's owner must still be read back and verified because that failure mode is silent and has already bitten several PRs.

Four of the seven branches were lineage variants of ONE feature (the Z3 completeness gate) across three SHA lineages, not four features; fm/fm-rebase-upstream even applies the same five gate commits twice on itself. The result is five genuinely distinct fixes:
1. fm-verify-delivered.sh and its false-clean fix (fm/fm-verify-delivered-false-clean, PR #3): "inspected nothing" and "search failed" are deliberately their own non-clean exit outcomes so an inspection that examined no files can never report clean.
2. Agent-maintained crewmate working log at data/<id>/log.md (fm/crew-worklog, PR #4): deliberately NOT the status file, because status appends wake firstmate and must stay sparse while the log never wakes anything.
3. Timestamped status appends plus reported evidence age (fm/status-timestamps).
4. The Z3 completeness gate, deduplicated across the four branches.
5. Per-repo ground truth injected into briefs (feat-cross-repo-grounding, PR #1).

DELIBERATE DECISIONS a reviewer reading only the diff would not know. The gate version was chosen by content, not recency: two branches carry byte-identical gate files and a third a near-identical copy, and feat-cross-repo-grounding's 9568dac won because it is the only lineage where invalid facts exit 64 and BLOCK (in the others a typo or corrupted record falls through the engine's error path as a PASS) and the only one whose fm-merge-local.sh caller treats 64 as blocking. Three branches fix the SAME bug (the gate false-blocking teardown of squash-merged work) three different ways; the in-gate fix was taken so every caller benefits, not just teardown, and the local-only landedness derivation was deliberately KEPT because local-only work has no PR to squash-merge so plain git can decide it correctly - that is what lets the gate block an unmerged local-only branch before fm-merge-local.sh runs. For remote-backed ship work the gate defers COMPLETELY to fm-teardown.sh per AGENTS.md hard rule 3. The call-site split from fm/fm-rebase-upstream is intentionally NOT carried because it would add a duplicate invocation changing no outcome and its call sites predate exit 64.

PR #1 was explicitly evaluated: the captain called it out of date, which describes the branch (265 commits behind, failing check) and not the feature, so the ground-truth work is included in its newest form with the test coverage it never had.

TWO DELIBERATE DROPS: bin/__pycache__/fm-completeness.cpython-313.pyc, a compiled build artifact committed on all four gate branches, and the redundant .gitignore __pycache__/ addition, because main already carries both patterns. Nothing else from the seven branches is absent.

ADAPTATIONS forced by main's drift, all deliberate: the bootstrap capability line is emitted as a BOOTSTRAP_INFO fact behind FM_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE_FACTS=1 matching main's current convention; README toolbelt/env/test-list rows are not carried because main moved those surfaces into docs/; AGENTS.md additions were kept minimal per firstmate-coding-guidelines size discipline.

REVIEW FIXES ALREADY APPLIED AND ACCEPTED on this branch across earlier runs of this same pipeline - do not re-litigate them. The gate's dirty-worktree filter now matches fm-teardown.sh's residue filter including the grok/kimi turn-end markers, so the gate cannot refuse a teardown the guarded script considers clean. The pending-reply dedup was restored from substring back to whole-line semantics via status_line_body under the stamp contract. Both fm-completeness-check.sh invocations forward FM_HOME/FM_STATE_OVERRIDE/FM_DATA_OVERRIDE explicitly like their neighbours. AGENTS.md hard rule 5 was SOFTENED BY EXPLICIT CAPTAIN DECISION to offer bin/fm-verify-delivered.sh as available evidence rather than a mandatory precondition, because that script's only verdict-producing mode is hardcoded to one private downstream project while this repo ships to other users; generalizing the script was explicitly ruled OUT OF SCOPE. fm-procevent-remote-reply.sh's validator now folds incoming lines through status_line_body so stamped and legacy unstamped remote-secondmate replies both validate, keeping the stamp contract's single owner rather than copying its glob. And a malformed rules-file weight now fails open as a rules error instead of exiting 64, keeping exit 64 strictly for invalid FACTS.

HARD CONSTRAINT: all seven source branches must be left exactly as found, never deleted, force-pushed, or rewritten, because they are the only copy of this work and the recovery path. Verified untouched at c98385b, 9568dac, 39c5b05, e3581a5, 8c81c17, 7c8ced1, 469cec8.

A further accepted review round is also already applied and must not be re-litigated: the remote-reply continuity-broken escalation is now stamped through fm-classify-lib.sh's writer so no firstmate-side append is left unstamped; both gate call sites now treat rc 0 as the ONLY proceed case and block on every other rc, so a missing or non-executable gate wrapper can no longer be read as approval (the documented fail-open behaviour is unchanged because the gate itself exits 0 for SAT, for the off-switch, and for fail_open); the blocked-verdict extraction no longer anchors on the dead 'counterexample' key so a blocked claim still names its violated invariant; and the unused 'unpushed' revision walk moved inside the local-only branch that is its only reader, a cost and placement change that alters no resolved value.

PIPELINE CONTEXT: review and test already PASSED at an earlier head in this same pipeline. Two subsequent runs failed for purely ENVIRONMENTAL reasons, never a defect in this branch: one hit a Claude session limit at the document step, and one lost the claude binary from the daemon's PATH mid-run while that binary was being reinstalled. Both have cleared, the agent is verified runnable, and custody was returned through the gate's own recovery path each time.

KNOWN PRE-EXISTING FAILURES, not regressions: fm-teardown, fm-session-start, fm-pi-watch-extension and fm-bearings-snapshot fail identically against a pristine main extract. fm-teardown matters most because this branch adds a gate call to fm-teardown.sh, but it is not the cause: the same assertion fails with FM_COMPLETENESS_GATE=0 and on pristine main where the gate does not exist. They are environment-dependent and out of scope.

## What Changed

- Adds three new capabilities as scripts under `bin/`: `fm-verify-delivered.sh`, which checks a task's delivery claims against merged code and treats "inspected nothing" and "search failed" as their own non-clean exits so an inspection that examined no files can never report clean; `fm-ground.sh`, which resolves per-repo ground truth from `data/repos/<key>.md`; and an optional Z3-backed completeness gate (`fm-completeness-check.sh`, `fm-completeness.py`, `fm-completeness.rules.json`) that derives task facts and solves them against a rules file, exiting 64 on invalid facts, failing open on rules-file breakage, and deferring entirely to `fm-teardown.sh` for remote-backed ship work. The gate is wired into `fm-teardown.sh` and `fm-merge-local.sh`, both of which now treat rc 0 as the only proceed case and print cause-specific remediation when the gate blocks.
- Reworks briefs and status reporting: `fm-brief.sh` scaffolds an agent-maintained working log at `data/<id>/log.md` (deliberately separate from the status file, which wakes firstmate and must stay sparse) and injects the resolved per-repo ground truth into ship and scout briefs; `fm-classify-lib.sh` now stamps every status append with a timestamp and owns the stamp contract, with `fm-crew-state.sh`, `fm-fleet-snapshot.sh`, `fm-fleet-view.sh` and `fm-secondmate-report.sh` reporting evidence age from it, and `fm-pending-reply-lib.sh` / `fm-procevent-remote-reply.sh` folding lines through `status_line_body` so stamped and legacy unstamped replies both validate.
- Consolidates the above from seven separate fix branches into a single branch (four of which were lineage variants of the one completeness gate), and carries the 18 already-merged upstream commits — remote secondmates, the Aqua job worker, trace-context propagation, tmux liveness hardening — that the base commit predates. Deliberately omitted: the committed `bin/__pycache__/*.pyc` build artifact and a redundant `.gitignore` entry, both already covered by main.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The delta itself is small, correct, and covered by tests for every case it changes, but the cumulative branch under review remains a five-feature consolidation of roughly 2,900 lines across 37 files that inserts a new blocking gate into two irreversible lifecycle paths (teardown and local merge), which is more than a well-bounded change even though all findings from three review rounds are now resolved.

## Testing

I ran the nine targeted suites covering this branch's own surfaces (completeness gate, verify-delivered, brief, ground, crew-state, pending-reply, remote-reply, watch-triage, fleet-snapshot-view) and they all pass, with the z3 solver present so the gate's real SAT/UNSAT matrix executed rather than skipping. Because passing suites alone are not evidence of the intent, I also drove all five consolidated fixes through their actual operator-facing CLI into one transcript: fm-verify-delivered returning CLEAN, VIOLATIONS, INSPECTED NOTHING and SEARCH FAILED as four distinct verdicts against purpose-built repos; a real ship brief scaffolded with the repo's ground truth injected as a binding do-not-re-derive section, the working-log section, and the line stating the log never wakes firstmate; timestamped status appends read back as ages 0s, 19h1m and unknown for a legacy line; the gate blocking and clearing scout, ship and merge claims, exiting 64 on an invalid fact while a malformed rules weight fails open (and refuses with exit 3 under strict mode); a real three-step fm-teardown.sh run against the live gate that refuses a dirty worktree with "commit or stash", refuses the committed-but-unmerged local-only branch with the fm-merge-local.sh remediation instead, then completes once the work is merged; and fm-merge-local.sh blocking on gate rc 126 and 127. I additionally confirmed the two deliberate drops (no tracked .pyc, .gitignore unchanged from main). The only failure anywhere is the pre-existing fm-teardown herdr-preflight assertion the intent declares out of scope, and I re-confirmed it is independent of this branch by reproducing it with FM_COMPLETENESS_GATE=0. No visual artifacts apply: every surface this change touches is a shell CLI with no rendered UI, so CLI transcripts are the end-user experience. PR-owner verification is the push/PR phase's responsibility and was not performed here.

fm_status_append_once "$DEDUP" "continuity broken: remote secondmate reply never arrived"
