title: fix(herdr): require 0.8.0 for default presentation spaces
body:
## Intent

Fix the Herdr presentation focus-steal, implementing the captain's decision A on a completed diagnostic report. The reproduction from that report had to become the regression test.

ROOT CAUSE (from the report, verified against current code): default-on presentation projection makes every crewmate teardown a workspace-emptying removal. Firstmate's focus-safe removal plan falls back to a plain explicit close whenever the doomed pane's shell is not a provably lone/childless/idle shell (a persistent gitstatusd, zsh-async worker, or direnv fails that proof permanently). On Herdr below 0.8.0 that close steals the captain's active workspace for ~140ms per teardown, because both upstream focus fixes (PR #1877 commit 165dca45, PR #1912 commit a979916) are absent before 0.8.0.

THREE REQUIRED DELIVERABLES:
1. Version floor (primary). Gate DEFAULT-ON presentation behind a Herdr 0.8.0 floor: at/above 0.8.0 project as today; below it automatically fall back to the flat per-home layout and emit ONE clear warning naming the version and the upgrade as the fix, explicitly NOT spammed per event; an explicit opt-in (config/herdr-presentation-spaces = on) is still honored below the floor so a home that deliberately opted in is never silently downgraded. Determine the running Herdr version robustly, preferring a structural/protocol signal over a brittle string, verifying the exact floor-to-protocol mapping against real binaries, and backing any surface signal with a loud guard. Also fix the now-incorrect adapter comment claiming the mitigation 'stays safe without any version gate', and reconcile docs/herdr-backend.md 'Presentation spaces' and the affected docs/verification/runtime-backends.md entries.
2. Stop swallowing cleanup restore stderr at bin/fm-teardown.sh, where the focus-preserving close was called as '... 2>/dev/null || true', discarding the helper's real warnings. A failed/refused restore must become visible WITHOUT turning a benign cleanup into a teardown-blocking hard failure; the existing teardown safety posture must be preserved.
3. Extend tests/fm-backend-herdr-focus-flash-e2e.test.sh with a Part C presenting the adapter with a doomed pane whose shell holds a PERSISTENT child, in a geometry where the closing workspace's right neighbour is NOT the focus anchor. That is the exact fallback case the existing suite structurally cannot reach (Part B always hands it a bare idle shell, so the pane-death route always engages). On a defective (<0.8.0) release it must assert either no wrong-focus sample or an explicitly accepted bounded one; with the floor in place the flat fallback means no steal. Part C must fail on the fallback path on a defective release without the fix.

EXPLICIT CONSTRAINTS ACCEPTED: version detection and focus behavior are harness/version-dependent, so per firstmate-coding-guidelines they need BOTH a portable regression in tests/ pinning the floor/gating logic with real logic and no live Herdr, AND live coverage in the live-harness-optin family, failing loudly and naming the version, with the dated result recorded in docs/verification/runtime-backends.md pointing at the refresh command. Real Herdr lifecycle was to be exercised ONLY through bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh on a named non-default session, never the live default fleet session and never 'herdr server stop'. firstmate-coding-guidelines applied throughout: one-owner rule for contracts, docs audience classification via bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh, one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never em dash, shellcheck-clean via bin/fm-lint.sh, colocated tests, dated maintainer-verification evidence. The captain also asked that the second call site with the same exposure (bin/fm-herdr-session-cleanup.sh, same helper) be covered consistently by the version-floor gating rather than left as a second ungated path, WITHOUT expanding beyond making that path consistent with the floor decision, and that there be no product behavior changes beyond the floor plus the two secondaries. The documented no-code mitigation for affected reporters remains writing 'off' to config/herdr-presentation-spaces.

DECISIONS AND TRADEOFFS MADE WHILE DOING THE WORK (a reviewer reading only the diff would not know these):
- The protocol floor was MEASURED, not assumed. Seven real upstream macOS aarch64 release binaries were downloaded and each asked for its own 'status --json' through the guarded lab helper: 0.7.3 and 0.7.4 report protocol 16, 0.7.5 and the pre-fix 2026-07-21 preview report 17, the first post-fix (2026-07-29) preview reports 18, and the 2026-08-04 preview and 0.8.0 both report 19. No build lacking both upstream fixes reaches 19 and every pre-fix build tops out at 17, so protocol 19 is a safe structural expression of the 0.8.0 floor. The one post-fix build below 19 is a preview still reporting a 0.7.5 version, so it is deliberately and conservatively treated as below the floor: that costs a preview build its projection and never lets an unfixed build through, and it matches the captain's stated 0.8.0 floor rather than silently lowering it to protocol 18.
- Two independent signals are read (protocol number, and the release core of the version string with any prerelease/build suffix stripped) and EITHER can carry a positive verdict, so no single vendor field is load-bearing. A readable protocol below the floor is decisive on its own; only losing BOTH signals reports indeterminate, which falls back flat rather than guessing.
- The 'one clear warning, not per event' requirement is implemented with a per-home, per-detected-release dedupe marker under state/, because the projection decision is remade on every spawn and an undeduplicated warning would repeat on every crewmate. Keying it by release means an upgrade or a downgrade is announced again.
- Config parsing was extracted into fm_backend_herdr_presentation_preference as the single owner, returning off / on / default, so the gate composes an explicit choice with the floor. An empty file remains the historical presence-based opt-in and therefore counts as a DELIBERATE 'on' honored below the floor; an unrecognized value is NOT a deliberate opt-in, so it warns and follows the unconfigured default. fm_backend_herdr_presentation_enabled gained an optional second state-dir argument for the warning dedupe.
- On the second call site: I first implemented a below-floor warning inside the shared close helper (with a new plain-empties plan token so it only fired when the close would actually empty a non-focused workspace), then deliberately REMOVED it and kept the floor with ONE owner, the spawn-time gate. Reasons: it required an extra 'herdr status --json' subprocess on every emptying plain close; it shifted roughly fifteen ordered canned-response test fixtures because those fixtures script status responses in sequence; and the case it reported only arises after a home deliberately opted in below the floor. Session-start cleanup must keep retiring existing husks below the floor or homes leak workspaces forever (the report explicitly rejected refusing the close), and that call site already does not swallow stderr, so it is consistent with the floor and with the teardown fix without a parallel gate. This is a deliberate one-owner choice, not an oversight.
- CI pins Herdr 0.7.4, which is BELOW the new floor, so tests/fm-backend-herdr-presentation-e2e.test.sh's 'a home that configured nothing is projected by default' case would have started failing in CI. That case was made release-aware (assert the projection at/above the floor, assert the flat fallback plus the naming warning below it) rather than pinned to one outcome. This is required correctness under the floor, not scope expansion; every other case in that suite uses an explicit opt-in or opt-out and is unaffected.
- Deliberately NOT done, to stay in scope: the CI Herdr pin was not bumped to 0.8.0 (wider blast radius, deserves its own change), and fm_backend_herdr_kill_serialized's own '2>/dev/null' was left alone since the captain named only the projected-close call site.
- A pre-existing, unrelated failure exists in tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh (the C9 spawn supervision case): the worktree-tangle alarm fires because that test's repo root is a feature branch. It fails identically on the clean base commit and is not caused by this change; fixing it would mean altering tangle-guard scoping, a safety boundary deserving its own change.

VERIFICATION PERFORMED: bin/fm-lint.sh and bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh both clean; the herdr unit suite passes with 169 assertions; the focus-flash regression passes on both real Herdr 0.7.5 (steal_live=1, floor_verdict=1, bounded four-sample wrong-focus window fully restored) and 0.8.0 (steal_live=0, floor_verdict=0, zero wrong-focus samples); Part C was proven to FAIL without the fix by temporarily removing the floor logic and rerunning on 0.7.5; and the entire real-herdr-gated lane passes on both the CI-pinned 0.7.4 and 0.8.0 (11 scripts, 0 failed each). The new opt-in live guard re-measures the release-to-protocol mapping against digest-pinned upstream binaries and passed on all four releases it checks.

## What Changed

- Gate default-on Herdr presentation spaces behind the 0.8.0 release floor using protocol and version signals, with flat-layout fallback, deduplicated upgrade warnings, and preserved explicit opt-in behavior.
- Surface focus-restore warnings during projected teardown without making benign cleanup failures teardown-blocking.
- Add portable and live regression coverage for version-floor classification, release mapping, and persistent-child cleanup fallback focus behavior, with updated backend documentation and verification evidence.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Captain, the change is well-bounded, preserves the authorized containment, and consistently enforces the server-aware presentation floor at the fresh-projection boundary.

## Testing

Author-reported lint and documentation checks were not rerun because this phase forbids linters. Portable Herdr behavior passed; real 0.7.5 reproduced the focus steal and showed the flat default fallback with explicit opt-in preserved; real 0.8.0 preserved focus and projected by default; measured binaries confirmed the protocol-19 floor; and teardown now has a passing regression for visible, non-blocking restore failure. One adjacent presentation concurrency test was unstable.

title: fix(bin): classify settled Muse session logs as idle
body:
## Intent Open up muse (Muse Code) crewmate idle busy-state detection now that the credentialed smoke evidence exists, and - per an explicit later captain decision that supersedes the original task text - REMOVE the idle gate entirely rather than opening it as a version allowlist. Original task: the muse busy-state classifier in bin/fm-busy-lib.sh folds muse's durable session event log. Its BUSY half was always trusted (an open run is positive proof a turn is in flight), but its IDLE half was held behind an opt-in, fm_busy_muse_idle_verified / FM_BUSY_MUSE_IDLE_VERIFIED_VERSIONS, because a settled log only proves no run is open at that instant. If a real multi-step turn had spanned several runs, an ungated idle would have reported a working crewmate as finished, so a settled log classified 'unknown'. The credentialed multi-step smoke that would settle the question was deferred until a META_API_KEY was available. It has now been run. Evidence already collected (do not re-run the smoke): on Muse Code 0.1.0-R708.1, model muse-spark-1.2-contributor, provider meta, authenticated through stored ~/.config/muse/auth.json so the key never entered argv. Multi-step turn, session log ~/.local/share/muse/sessions/2026/08/06/629b3bc1-5dd7-4a0d-a901-69701850922c/session.jsonl: exactly ONE run started/terminal pair brackets the whole 828-record turn, terminal=completed, turn_duration_ms=75243, 23 tool batches inside it. Interrupt turn, session log .../e4e0b4f4-38d0-46dc-b669-dfb5de92e0e0/session.jsonl: five consecutive in-flight samples read busy, and an Escape mid tool loop closed the run with terminal=cancelled reason='cancelled during model step' rather than leaving it open. Captain decision driving this change: do NOT keep the gate as a version list or boolean. Delete fm_busy_muse_idle_verified and FM_BUSY_MUSE_IDLE_VERIFIED_VERSIONS and every branch that treated a settled log as unknown, so a settled session log classifies 'idle muse-session-log' unconditionally. Busy is unchanged (open run => busy). Resolution failures - no sidecar binding, no matching log, an unreadable or run-free log - deliberately stay 'unknown', because those prove nothing about the turn either way. Supporting rationale recorded in the code comment and docs: a version allowlist would have been false precision, because the session log's own metadata carries only semver 0.1.0 and a build sha and cannot distinguish this build from another 0.1.0 release. Accompanying deliverables, all deliberate: docs/verification/muse.md replaces its 'Deferred: the credentialed multi-step smoke' section with dated 2026-08-06 completed evidence (log paths, exact commands and observed counts, the interrupt result) and explains the gate's removal, while keeping post-upgrade refresh guidance because muse auto-updates its binary underneath the fleet. That doc also records a correction found while verifying: the previously suggested command grep -c '"event":{"kind":"started"' returns 56 on that log rather than 1, because every tool batch effect reuses the same inner event shape, so the count must be scoped to '"kind":"run"'. .agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md updates the muse busy/idle facts to state idle is trusted from a settled session log with no version allowlist. bin/fm-spawn.sh drops a now-stale 'and the idle gate' cross-reference in a comment. tests/fm-muse-harness.test.sh replaces the gate open/closed test with one asserting default-on idle for BOTH completed and cancelled terminals, and two neighbouring tests that previously asserted 'unknown' only as a weak proxy for 'did not leak another session's state' now assert 'idle' directly, which is a strictly stronger assertion. This is firstmate's own shared tracked material, so firstmate-coding-guidelines applies: one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never an em dash, no agent name as commit co-author, bin/*.sh shellcheck-clean via bin/fm-lint.sh, tests colocated in tests/ exercising behavior through the executable interface rather than asserting implementation source text, and docs/verification records carrying dated commands and output rather than task chronology. Delivery: no-mistakes pipeline to a PR. Do not merge it. ## What Changed - Remove the Muse idle gate so settled completed or cancelled session logs classify as idle, while open runs remain busy and resolution failures remain unknown. - Record the credentialed multi-step and interrupt evidence, corrected run-scoped counting command, and post-upgrade refresh guidance. - Update harness guidance and executable tests for default-on idle detection and session isolation. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is narrowly scoped, preserves unresolved Muse states as unknown, and conforms to the authoritative requirement to trust settled logs without any idle gate or version allowlist. ## Testing Two broad subject-script attempts were interrupted before reaching the changed cases; the focused executable slice passed, and direct before/after evidence showed completed and cancelled logs changed from unknown to idle while open remains busy and run-free or unresolved inputs remain unknown.
Evidence: Before/after Muse classifier transcript base completed: unknown muse-session-log target completed: idle muse-session-log target cancelled: idle muse-session-log target open: busy muse-session-log target run-free: unknown muse-session-log target unbound: unknown muse-session-log ```text Muse supervision classifier transcript ====================================== base completed: unknown muse-session-log target completed: idle muse-session-log target cancelled: idle muse-session-log target open: busy muse-session-log target run-free: unknown muse-session-log target unbound: unknown muse-session-log ```
Evidence: Focused Muse regression output `Six focused executable behavior cases passed, covering lifecycle folding, nested decoys, binding isolation, literal workspace matching, unresolved inputs, and completed/cancelled idle.` ```text ok - the run fold tracks open, settled, interrupted, reopened, and run-free logs ok - a nested terminal record never settles an in-flight run ok - the session binding folds only the log matching this task's worktree ok - workspace bindings compare decoded paths literally ok - every unproven muse binding classifies unknown rather than idle ok - a settled session log reads idle for both completed and interrupted turns ```

This new comment records only the smoke result, docs merely say the opt-in was not pinned, and line 69 still references a nonexistent "verification gate." Add the required rationale to both owners and remove the stale gate reference. 🔧 Fix: Document Muse idle trust and remove stale gate reference ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: feat(bin): sync upstream fleet and remote secondmate workflows
body:
## Intent

Bring this fork of firstmate up to date with its upstream parent.

Remotes: origin = VirtualRoboticHands/firstmate (ours), upstream = kunchenguid/firstmate (parent).
Starting state: 3 ahead, 23 behind, merge-base 33a4287.

Requirements:

1. Fetch both remotes, then merge upstream/main into a branch off origin/main. Take the whole set of upstream commits - this is a full catch-up, not a cherry-pick.

2. Verify the three fork-only commits still have effect after the merge. A clean textual merge does not prove semantic survival: for each, confirm its actual change is still present in the merged tree - the away-mode injection guard (9221162), the validation-ownership documentation (b2f9836), and the self-drive brief behavior (56f35bd). If upstream independently rewrote any of those areas, say so explicitly and describe how the two versions were reconciled; do not silently let upstream's version win.

3. Run the repo's full test suite on the merged result and report the outcome honestly. If tests fail, report them; do not paper over them.

4. Review upstream commit 4ee4a0a "feat(bin): require an explicit per-task delivery contract" specifically, since it may change how task dispatch behaves for this home. Read what it actually does and report in the PR body whether adopting it changes behavior this home depends on, and whether anything in this home needs updating to match.

5. Sanity-check that upstream commit d0461e4 "prevent false watcher-down alarms in Claude sessions" is present in the merged result. This home is hitting that exact bug live, where the watcher-down banner fires on nearly every guarded command despite healthy supervision.

6. Note in the PR body any upstream commit that introduces a new config file, env var, or required tool version, since this home's local config may need to catch up. ef2c3a2 (AXI tool floors) and 4a9979a (report stale AXI tools) are known candidates.

Constraints:

- Do not rebase, squash, or rewrite history. Use a real merge so both lineages are preserved.
- Do not force-push anything.
- Do not resolve a conflict by discarding this fork's work. If a conflict appears, stop and report the exact conflict rather than resolving it by dropping fork work.
- Do not merge the PR; it goes to the captain for approval.
- Do not modify data/, state/, config/, or projects/ - this home's private runtime state.

This is firstmate's own shared tracked material, so the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill applies: one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash rather than em dash, no agent commit co-author, shellcheck-clean bin scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh, tests colocated in tests/ as <subject>.test.sh extending existing runners, and tests must exercise behavior through an executable or public interface rather than asserting implementation-source bytes.

Work completed and accepted so far:

- The merge is commit 6203e8e, a real two-parent merge of upstream/main into fm/firstmate-upstream-sync, zero textual conflicts, 137 files changed.
- All 23 upstream commits and all 3 fork commits are ancestors of the result.
- The merge was textually clean but semantically collided in two assertions in tests/fm-brief.test.sh, because upstream's 4ee4a0a and this fork's 56f35bd changed the same brief surface without seeing each other. Commit f623114 reconciles both without dropping either side's intent: upstream's no-mistakes definition-of-done marker was retargeted from a sentence 56f35bd deleted to the self-drive sentence that replaced it (measured to appear only in the no-mistakes variant, so it still discriminates that variant from direct-PR), and this fork's faster-delivery test now passes the explicit --mode that 4ee4a0a made required, with an added exit-status check so a future refusal fails loudly instead of surfacing as a missing-file grep error.
- Four remaining test failures are environmental or pre-existing, not defects in the merged code, and are to be reported rather than fixed here or papered over by loosening assertions:
- tests/fm-on.test.sh, tests/fm-remote-doctor.test.sh, and tests/fm-session-start.test.sh share one root cause: each isolates by building a bare /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin PATH and expecting a removed tool to become unreachable, but this host has node, tasks-axi, quota-axi, gh-axi, and lavish-axi all reachable on that bare path, so no MISSING diagnostic is emitted. Their sibling herdr assertion passes because herdr genuinely is not installed, confirming the probe works and only the host install layout differs. The fm-session-start.test.sh assertion is unchanged at the fork tip and so was already failing on this host before the catch-up.
- tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh asserts completely empty launch output, and the captured output contains zero WATCHER DOWN occurrences but does carry the unrelated WORKTREE TANGLE banner that fires because this task branch is not main; this is evidence d0461e4 works rather than evidence against it.
- tests/fm-pi-watch-extension.test.sh is untouched by the merge and by every upstream commit.

- One further failure, tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh "older Claude escape footer should be busy", was a pre-existing defect in this fork rather than a merge regression, proven by running that file at the pre-merge fork tip where it fails identically. Fork commit 9221162 narrowed the Claude rendered busy signature to the elapsed spinner and dropped "esc to interrupt" without updating that test. It was escalated to Firstmate rather than decided by the worker, and the captain chose to restore the escape affordance with a discriminator so both older and current Claude Code installs are detected correctly, to verify against the live harness, to keep tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh passing for both footer shapes, and then to drive the pipeline to green CI.

Accepted implementation of that decision: Claude's rendered busy verdict is now the elapsed spinner OR the escape affordance, so either signal alone proves an active turn and no single vendor string is load-bearing. The affordance counts only where Claude actually renders it, adjacent to a "·" footer separator as one field of a multi-field hint row, and that adjacency is the discriminator. Live verification on Claude Code 2.1.223 established that a clean idle pane, a post-turn idle pane, and idle panes with background shells render no escape affordance, while a real turn renders it continuously and renders the elapsed spinner only intermittently: an 18-second turn sampled every 0.6 seconds carried the affordance on every sample and the spinner on none, so the spinner-only guard had a measured blind window in which an active turn read as idle and supervision could inject mid-turn.

A bare, undelimited "esc to interrupt" line stays idle for Claude on purpose, and that resolves a genuine collision. The same byte sequence was asserted busy by tests/fm-tmux-submit-busy.test.sh for older Claude and pinned idle by the away-delivery regression in tests/fm-daemon.test.sh, which models the ambiguous Claude Code 2.1.221 idle footer as a pane that must still accept a buffered digest. No function of the rendered text alone separates them. The delimiter discriminator was verified to satisfy every real 2.1.223 footer and the wedge guard, leaving only the bare-line fixture, which is a test simplification rather than a rendering Claude produces, so the older-Claude case is pinned in its real delimited form and the bare form is pinned idle so the collision cannot be silently reintroduced. The residual gap, an older Claude Code rendering the affordance with neither a separator nor a spinner, is indistinguishable from that idle footer and resolves toward delivery rather than a wedge.

Required supporting work for a harness-dependent check, per the firstmate-coding-guidelines "Harness-dependent checks" section: a portable CI regression that drives the two signals apart and asserts the divergence itself, plus an opt-in live guard in the live-harness-optin family that exercises every installed harness, reports an absent or undrivable harness explicitly rather than passing silently, refuses a pass that checked nothing, and fails naming the harness and version; and a dated per-harness record in docs/verification/runtime-backends.md pointing at that guard as the refresh command. The stale Claude Code 2.1.221 claim in docs/verification/supervision.md is corrected to point at that owner.

- The full-suite run hung on two leaked fixture processes, both on /tmp fixture homes and never the real fleet home, terminated by exact PID: tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh leaked the fm-watch.sh child it backgrounds against /tmp/fm-secondmate-safety.<rand>/watch-home so its own kill-then-wait cleanup never returned and the test held the suite open for 34 minutes, and a bin/fm-remote-job-worker.sh from an earlier remote-reply test was orphaned to ppid=1 for 42 minutes with its fixture directory already deleted. Both are to be reported as an upstream test-hygiene defect, not fixed in this merge. This is directly relevant to upstream 7ef26c4, whose reap_task_worktree_processes matches processes by cwd under a task's worktree or tasktmp at task teardown and therefore cannot cover them: no task teardown runs for a test fixture, and both leaked processes had cwd set to the repo root rather than their fixture directory. 1cd97c0 addressed fixture temporary directories rather than fixture processes, and the orphaned worker outliving its already-deleted directory is the counterexample.

## What Changed

- Merge the complete upstream lineage while preserving the fork’s away-mode injection guard, validation-ownership guidance, and self-driving direct-PR/local-only briefs; also restore reliable Claude active-turn and watcher detection using footer-positional busy signals.
- Add remote secondmate provisioning, Aqua-backed remote jobs, fleet lifecycle cleanup, Herdr presentation spaces, and optional W3C trace propagation through the new gitignored `config/trace-context` flag or `FM_TRACE_CONTEXT` override.
- Require explicit per-task delivery contracts (`--mode` and `--yolo`) for ship dispatch and promotion, so this home’s callers must pass them but its private config needs no migration; bootstrap now enforces current AXI-family floors, including gh-axi 0.1.29 and lavish-axi 0.1.45, and reports stale installations.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The shared positional matcher now satisfies the required Claude and caller invariants, but the overall change remains a large upstream integration with accepted environmental test limitations.

## Testing

The earlier full-suite run exposed only documented environmental, pre-existing, and fixture-cleanup problems; this phase’s portable classifier test, real-tmux away-delivery test, and opt-in live-harness check all passed and produced reviewer-visible transcripts, with no source changes or transient worktree artifacts left behind.

title: fix(teardown): gate the herdr presentation lock on the projection being on
body:
`fm-spawn.sh` already gates its projection work on `fm_backend_herdr_presentation_enabled`, but teardown reached for the presentation session lock **unconditionally**, at two sites: the endpoint preflight (`teardown_herdr_preflight_target`) and the plain pane close.

So a home that wrote `off` to `config/herdr-presentation-spaces` still had its cleanup depend on a feature it had switched off. That is an inconsistency on any platform - spawn honours the opt-out, teardown ignored it.

Where the lock namespace cannot satisfy its own validity check the consequence is worse than cosmetic. Teardown refuses, the task's state files are retained by design, supervision stays permanently "needed", and there is no manual recovery. `--force` does not help: it skips only the dirty and landed-work checks, and the same preflight runs in both branches.

Both sites now consult the same predicate. **Default behaviour is unchanged** - the projection is on unless a home opts out, so a contended lock still refuses exactly as before.

The focus-preserving close itself is kept in the opted-out path; it simply no longer demands a lock whose only purpose is ordering a projection this home does not have.

## Relationship to #1790

#1790 fixes the underlying reason the namespace can be unobtainable on Windows, and is the more important of the two. This one is independent: it is a real inconsistency in its own right, and it is what lets an opted-out home tear down cleanly regardless of why the lock is unavailable. Neither depends on the other, and they touch disjoint files.

## Testing

New `test_herdr_flat_teardown_opted_out_of_presentation_ignores_the_session_lock` makes the lock unavailable in both ways it can be unavailable - held by a contending process, or unresolvable because the namespace cannot be validated - and asserts teardown still completes, closes the pane, returns the isolated copy, and clears its records. The existing `test_herdr_flat_teardown_refuses_orphaning_records_then_retry_completes` is the negative control: with the projection at its default, a contended lock must still refuse.

Verified end to end against a real stuck task on the affected host: a finished task that had been uncollectable for a day tore down cleanly, state files cleared, worktree returned to the pool, and the delivered work intact on its branch.

`tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` reaches the same point on this branch as on unmodified `main` on that host (9 ok, then a pre-existing failure caused by the namespace fault that #1790 addresses), so this introduces no regression there.

ShellCheck is not installable on that host, so `bin/fm-lint.sh` could not be run for CI parity.

It can exceed the harness inline-display limit - observed at ~70KB, where Claude Code persisted the hook output to a file and showed only a ~2KB inline preview. AGENTS.md section 3 already requires reading the COMPLETE digest once and trusting it. A session that treats the short preview as the digest silently misses the drained wake queue, OPEN DECISIONS, context, and fleet state. Fix - MINIMAL instruction change ONLY. This is firstmate shared, tracked material, and the captain's explicit constraint is: do NOT bloat instructions. title: fix: preserve fleet state in truncated session-start digests
body:
## Intent

Promote a digest-composition investigation's recommendations (its sections 5.1-5.3) into one coherent ship in bin/fm-session-start.sh, the firstmate session-start digest. Captain authorized. This is firstmate shared, tracked material, so firstmate-coding-guidelines applies: one-owner rule for contracts, colocated tests in tests/ that exercise behavior through the executable interface rather than implementation source text, one sentence per line in Markdown, plain dash never em dash, no agent co-author, and shellcheck-clean via bin/fm-lint.sh.

Motivating evidence from the investigation: the digest is delivered through a harness that truncates an oversized payload from the TAIL. A measured 70KB digest was really delivered as lines 1-435 of 578, cutting off eight lines before the live-task inventory, so that session took the helm without ever seeing which tasks were live or where their endpoints were. The CONTEXT block (five curated memory files) was 50.4% of the digest and sat in front of the recovery-critical fleet state.

Three required changes:

1. REORDER (highest value; a safety change, zero bytes saved). Emit the FLEET STATE section BEFORE the bulky CONTEXT memory files, so tail truncation drops recoverable curated memory instead of recovery-critical live fleet identity (live-task inventory, window/worktree/backend/endpoint-liveness). Use the existing SESSION_START_STAGES ordering contract. Explicitly do NOT reorder the LOCK/BOOTSTRAP/WAKE-QUEUE safety preamble. Move or duplicate the NEXT STEP read-once contract near the top so it too survives truncation.

2. CAP STATUS-TAIL LINE LENGTH. print_status_tail had no per-line bound; an observed status line ran 865 characters. Cap each tail line at 220 reusing the OPEN DECISIONS cap shape already in bin/fm-wake-drain.sh (a ' [truncated]' marker). This is safe because the section already prints each task's full status log path for targeted follow-up, and AGENTS.md section 8 already treats a status line as a wake event rather than current state (bin/fm-crew-state.sh owns current state).

3. BACKLOG LISTING. Drop done rows at startup (tasks-axi supports --state; retained completion history is a reporting surface, not a recovery input). ALWAYS keep every in_flight and held row with its hold_kind/hold_reason. Bound the plain queued listing, preferring the ready set plus all held/blocked rows in full plus an accurate '(N more queued)' remainder counter. Never silently truncate blocked or held items.

Scope boundaries the captain set: this is complementary to, and must NOT duplicate, a separate already-merged full-read safety-net change. It does NOT touch AGENTS.md. It must not change the startup memory budget scope or its estimator (separately deferred).

Required tests: colocated tests for the reorder ordering (FLEET STATE precedes CONTEXT, safety preamble unchanged), the status-tail per-line cap, and the backlog-state filtering (done dropped, in_flight/held always kept in full, queued bounded with an accurate '(N more)' counter), exercising real script output rather than source text.

Decisions and tradeoffs I made while implementing, which a reviewer reading only the diff would not know:

- I chose the section order LOCK, BOOTSTRAP, WAKE QUEUE, SUPERVISION, READ-ONCE CONTRACT, FLEET STATE, CONTEXT, NEXT STEP. Supervision stays between the wake queue and context exactly as AGENTS.md section 3 already states in prose.
- I MOVED the read-once contract rather than duplicating it, because the one-owner rule forbids two copies of the same contract. Because it now precedes the payload it governs, I added the condition that voids it: a STARTUP TRUNCATED banner naming a stage that never ran. The closing NEXT STEP reminder now points back at it instead of restating it.
- I added a new stage name 'read-once' to SESSION_START_STAGES so the truncation banner still names exactly which stages never ran; the existing banner test was updated for the new order.
- I did NOT reorder content WITHIN the FLEET STATE section (backlog listing still precedes the work-under-way inventory). AGENTS.md section 3 item 5 enumerates that internal order and AGENTS.md is out of scope; change 3 shrinks the backlog listing enough that the intra-section risk is much reduced. This was a deliberate scope decision, not an oversight.
- For the 220 cap I extracted the cut and its marker into a new shared owner, bin/fm-line-cap-lib.sh, and refactored bin/fm-wake-drain.sh's OPEN DECISIONS section onto it, rather than copying the logic into a second place. fm-wake-drain.sh keeps its own composite policy (the 4000-byte global cap and its 'N more omitted' disclosure); the lib owns only the per-line cut. The drain passes a per-item allowance one short of the cap because its global budget also charges for the trailing newline, preserving its existing byte math exactly. The lib exposes an assigning form (fm_cap_line_var) and a printing form (fm_cap_line) built on it, one rule with two call shapes, so the drain - which runs at the top of every wake-handling turn - pays no command substitution per item.
- The cap counts characters rather than bytes. Status lines are plain ASCII in practice so the two coincide, and character semantics can never cut a multibyte character in half into an invalid sequence. This matches the existing OPEN DECISIONS shape it reuses.
- I added a regression test for the OPEN DECISIONS per-item cap, which previously had none, since I refactored that code path.
- For the backlog I composed four tasks-axi group filters (--state in_flight, --state held, --state queued --blocked, and tasks-axi ready) rather than post-processing one listing, so this script never reimplements task state. The groups can overlap: an in-flight item that is also held appears in both, which I disclose in the group label. Only the ready group is bounded, so the remainder counter is exact.
- I renamed FM_SESSION_START_BACKLOG_LIMIT to FM_SESSION_START_QUEUED_LIMIT and changed its default from 80 to 20. This is deliberate: the knob's meaning genuinely changed (it no longer bounds the whole listing, and bounding the whole listing was unsafe because it could drop a held or blocked row), so keeping the old name would have been misleading. The old name is referenced nowhere else in the repo. docs/configuration.md's env inventory records the new knob.
- The manual (non-tasks-axi) backend path got the same rules: done rows dropped, every in-flight title line kept, every queued title line whose own text carries a hold or blocked-by marker kept, the rest bounded with an exact remainder. Its keep-pattern uses bracket expressions rather than backslashes because awk's -v applies escape processing before the regex is compiled.
- I dropped tasks-axi's per-group help block from each of the four composed listings. Keeping them would have repeated the same two pointers four times, each carrying this home's full backlog path, giving back much of the saving; the section already prints one equivalent pointer of its own.
- I tightened one pre-existing assertion that checked for the bare string 'STARTUP TRUNCATED', because the read-once contract now legitimately names that banner as the condition that voids it; the test now pins the actual banner line.

Verification performed: bin/fm-lint.sh clean, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh clean, bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage clean, and bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed ran 63 test scripts with zero failures. I also ran the real digest end to end against a throwaway home with the real tasks-axi installed to inspect the rendered output.

## What Changed

- Move the read-once contract and FLEET STATE ahead of bulky CONTEXT content while preserving the lock, bootstrap, and wake-queue safety preamble.
- Add a shared 220-character line cap with a ` [truncated]` marker for session status tails and wake-drain open decisions.
- Omit completed backlog rows, retain all in-flight, held, and blocked rows, and bound ready queued rows with an exact remainder count and documented configuration.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is well-bounded, conforms to the stated digest ordering and truncation requirements, preserves existing wake-drain byte accounting, and adds behavioral coverage through executable output.

## Testing

The author-reported baseline had already covered lint, documentation checks, coverage registration, and 63 changed test scripts; this phase reran the focused session-start and shared OPEN DECISIONS behavior suites and captured an actual CLI digest proving the safety preamble remains first, FLEET STATE precedes CONTEXT, the long status event is capped at 220 characters with its recovery path retained, done work is absent, held/blocked/in-flight work remains visible, and seven ready items bounded to three disclose an exact four-item remainder.

`Actual CLI digest shows LOCK -> BOOTSTRAP -> WAKE QUEUE -> SUPERVISION -> READ-ONCE CONTRACT -> FLEET STATE -> CONTEXT -> NEXT STEP. It retains in-flight, held, and blocked rows, shows 3 of 7 ready rows with “(4 more queued)”, omits done rows, and caps the long status line at exactly 220 characters with “ [truncated]”.`

## Intent Record the captain ruling dated 2026-08-06: firstmate may not promote an investigation to implementation on its own authority, because a report remains evidence rather than authorization. Add only the narrow exception in AGENTS.md section 7: when the captain had already requested the fix and commissioned the investigation as a step toward that requested fix, the recorded implementation authorization carries through and firstmate should not re-ask. Do not broaden this exception: it applies only to prior captain authorization already on record and never when the investigation revealed new scope, risk, or cost, which must return to the captain. Do not add any routine-autonomy promotion clause, preserve every existing safety boundary in the touched text, keep the addition to one or two sentences, and do not restructure AGENTS.md or rewrite neighboring rules. Follow repo Markdown style: one sentence per line, plain dash, and no agent co-author. Do not edit the model benchmark files; its existing durable decision rule already records that invented promotion fails condition 2 for every candidate, yielding KEEP OPUS 5 without consulting token cost. ## What Changed - Clarify that prior captain authorization carries through an investigation commissioned toward an already requested fix. - Require newly revealed scope, risk, or cost to return to the captain before implementation. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The single-sentence policy addition is narrowly scoped, preserves the existing authorization boundary, explicitly returns newly revealed scope, risk, or cost to the captain, and makes no forbidden benchmark or neighboring-rule changes. ## Testing No baseline test command was supplied; targeted diff inspection and an end-user-facing documentation contract check passed, with a transcript showing the effective Section 7 wording and all required authority boundaries. title: fix: pin gh base repo to origin
body:
## Intent Fix gh resolving this repo to the upstream fork owner instead of us. THE DEFECT: The firstmate primary checkout has two remotes - origin = VirtualRoboticHands/firstmate (ours) and upstream = kunchenguid/firstmate (the fork parent) - and no remote.origin.gh-resolved, so gh picks the base repo by remote name and prefers 'upstream'. CONSEQUENCE, observed twice on 2026-08-06: gh-axi PR and issue listings for firstmate silently returned the UPSTREAM project's items as though they were ours (a session-start listing showed upstream PRs 1777/1779/1780 as ours). More seriously, this is the read-side half of the failure that opened one of our own branches as a pull request on a third party's repository (kunchenguid PR 1789), proposing our fork-sync into their project; that had to be closed by hand. The pipeline's push target was already repointed on the captain's 2026-08-06 option-A decision, so THIS TASK IS THE SEPARATE READ-SIDE HALF ONLY. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: 1. Default gh/gh-axi calls made from this repo target VirtualRoboticHands/firstmate. 2. Deliberate upstream contribution still works - contributing upstream must remain possible as an explicit, deliberate act; do not make it impossible, just no longer the silent default. 3. A negative control, per the captain's testing standard: prove the fix by demonstrating the wrong-target behaviour before it and the right-target behaviour after. State that evidence in the PR body - do not assert it. 4. The fix must survive a fresh clone or a new worktree if achievable; if it cannot be (e.g. it depends on local git config a new worktree will not inherit), say so EXPLICITLY and describe what a new worktree needs, rather than quietly shipping a fix that only works here. CONSTRAINTS: Do not touch the upstream remote itself, and do not delete or rename remotes. Do not push anything to kunchenguid/firstmate - nothing in this task should reach a third party's repository. Pushing under .github/workflows/ needs the workflow OAuth scope, so avoid that path unless the fix genuinely requires it (it did not; that path is untouched). Repo style rules are owned by the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill: one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never an em dash, no agent co-author on commits, shellcheck-clean bin/ scripts, colocated tests named .test.sh in tests/ extending the existing runner, tests must exercise behavior through an executable or public interface and never assert implementation-source bytes. APPROACH AND DELIBERATE DECISIONS TAKEN: - New bin/fm-gh-resolve.sh sets remote.origin.gh-resolved=base (exactly what 'gh repo set-default' writes) and nothing else. Deliberately NOT an env var (GH_REPO would leak into crewmate environments and project work) and deliberately not a remote change, because gh-resolved is the only mechanism gh actually offers and the constraints forbid touching remotes. - It is deliberately a silent no-op when ANY remote already carries a gh-resolved key in any config scope, so an operator's deliberate choice - INCLUDING one deliberately aimed at the fork parent to contribute upstream - is preserved. That is how criterion 2 is protected structurally rather than by convention. - It is deliberately a silent no-op when the checkout has fewer than two GitHub remotes, since gh already resolves unambiguously and there is nothing to disambiguate. - Deliberately scoped to firstmate's OWN repo only. Project clones under projects/ are never written to, because AGENTS.md hard rule 1 forbids firstmate writing to a project; that scope limit is intentional, not an oversight. - Exit status is deliberately 0 for every reachable outcome including a reported problem: the diagnostic line, not the exit code, is the signal, matching the sibling TANGLE check's contract in fm-bootstrap.sh. - Wired into fm-bootstrap.sh next to its sibling worktree-tangle check: it repairs on the locked path and only WARNS with a GH_RESOLVE line on the detect-only path, because AGENTS.md requires that a lock-refused read-only session never mutates while still learning its listings may be wrong. - Adding a seventh lock-gated mutating sweep made the existing 'six MUTATING sweeps' counts in AGENTS.md, bin/fm-bootstrap.sh and bin/fm-session-start.sh wrong, so all three were corrected rather than left to drift. Likewise the bootstrap-diagnostics skill previously claimed the TANGLE repair was 'the only sanctioned firstmate-initiated git write to the primary', which this change makes false; that sentence was corrected rather than left as a stale absolute. ANSWER TO CRITERION 4, STATED EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN GLOSSED: the pin is LOCAL git config. A linked git worktree DOES inherit it (all worktrees share one .git/config), so crewmate worktrees need nothing extra. A fresh CLONE does NOT inherit it, because git clone carries no local config. The durable answer is therefore the bootstrap wiring, not the config value: fm-bootstrap runs the repair on every locked session start, so a fresh clone is pinned the first time firstmate opens a session in it. A clone that never runs a firstmate session start needs one manual bin/fm-gh-resolve.sh (or an equivalent gh repo set-default). Both halves of that claim are asserted in tests/fm-gh-resolve.test.sh so neither can rot into a guess. EVIDENCE ALREADY GATHERED FOR THE PR BODY (criterion 3), all captured with real gh 2.97.0: BEFORE, in the real checkout, 'gh repo view --json nameWithOwner' returned kunchenguid/firstmate and 'gh pr list' returned upstream PRs #1798/#1797. On a byte-identical replica of the same two-remote layout, the same commands returned kunchenguid/firstmate and #1798/#1797 before the fix, and VirtualRoboticHands/firstmate with an empty PR list after it; the empty list was independently confirmed genuine because 'gh pr list -R VirtualRoboticHands/firstmate --state open' returns [] and our fork's own PRs number 1-3. 'gh pr list -R kunchenguid/firstmate' still returns the parent's PRs after the fix, proving deliberate upstream contribution survives. The remote inventory was byte-identical before and after. TESTS: tests/fm-gh-resolve.test.sh (registered in the session-bootstrap family in bin/fm-test-run.sh) covers the repair, its idempotence, non-clobbering of a deliberate pin, the no-op cases, the untouched remote inventory, https/scp-like/ssh URL forms, the detect-only-vs-locked bootstrap split, the worktree-inherits / clone-does-not pair, and a gh-gated vendor probe that announces a skip rather than passing silently when gh is absent or unauthenticated. KNOWN PRE-EXISTING FAILURE, NOT INTRODUCED BY THIS CHANGE: tests/fm-session-start.test.sh fails one case ('MISSING diagnostic did not appear at all') on this machine. This was confirmed by stashing all of this branch's changes and running it against the clean base commit 5a2af5f, where it fails identically. It is environment-dependent (the case removes node from a fakebin and expects a MISSING: node diagnostic, which does not appear when real node is on PATH) and is out of scope for this task. ## What Changed - Add `fm-gh-resolve.sh` to pin ambiguous default `gh`/`gh-axi` calls to the GitHub `origin` while preserving deliberate repository pins, explicit `-R` targeting, and the existing remote configuration. - Run the resolver during locked bootstrap, emit a read-only `GH_RESOLVE` warning when the lock is unavailable, and document how linked worktrees inherit the pin while fresh clones are repaired on their first locked session start. - Add focused coverage for resolver and bootstrap behavior, including real negative-control evidence: default `gh` calls resolved to `kunchenguid/firstmate` and its PRs before the fix, then to `VirtualRoboticHands/firstmate` after it, while explicit upstream queries continued to work and the remote inventory remained unchanged. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is narrowly scoped, preserves deliberate upstream targeting, respects detect-only locking, and durably repairs fresh clones through bootstrap without altering remotes. ## Testing Focused automated tests passed, including repair, preservation, bootstrap, and clone/worktree behavior; live authenticated gh and gh-axi negative controls reproduced the wrong upstream default before repair and the correct fork default afterward, while explicit upstream targeting remained functional and the remote inventory stayed unchanged.
Evidence: Real gh negative-control transcript `Before repair, default gh resolved kunchenguid/firstmate and returned upstream PRs. After repair, it resolved VirtualRoboticHands/firstmate and returned the fork's empty PR list. Explicit upstream targeting continued to work, and remotes were unchanged.` ```text $ gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner # before fix kunchenguid/firstmate $ gh pr list --limit 3 --json number --jq map(.number) # before fix [1800,1799,1798] $ bin/fm-gh-resolve.sh BOOTSTRAP_INFO: pinned gh base repo to VirtualRoboticHands/firstmate (origin) in /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZBAQEYVTTRPD6JDTRD13GYC/gh-negative-control-repo $ git config --get remote.origin.gh-resolved base $ gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner # after fix VirtualRoboticHands/firstmate $ gh pr list --limit 3 --json number --jq map(.number) # after fix [] $ gh pr list -R kunchenguid/firstmate --limit 3 --json number --jq map(.number) # deliberate upstream [1800,1799,1798] $ remote inventory unchanged yes ```
Evidence: Real gh-axi negative-control transcript `Before repair, gh-axi listed upstream PRs 1800, 1799, and 1798. After repair, its default list targeted the fork and was empty. Passing -R kunchenguid/firstmate still listed upstream PRs.` ```text $ git config --unset remote.origin.gh-resolved && gh-axi pr list --limit 3 # negative control count: 3 (showing first 3) pull_requests[3]{number,title,state,author,draft,review}: 1800,"fix: preserve captain authority over scout promotion",open,VirtualRoboticHands,no,none 1799,"Exempt Cursor MCP: tool names from subagent guard",open,beraterkanelcelik,no,none 1798,"fix: preserve fleet state in truncated session-start digests",open,kunchenguid,no,none help[2]: Run `gh-axi pr view ` to view details Run `gh-axi pr create --title "..." --body-file ` to create $ bin/fm-gh-resolve.sh && gh-axi pr list --limit 3 # fixed default BOOTSTRAP_INFO: pinned gh base repo to VirtualRoboticHands/firstmate (origin) in /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZBAQEYVTTRPD6JDTRD13GYC/gh-negative-control-repo count: 0 pull_requests: [] help[2]: Run `gh-axi pr create --title "..." --body-file ` to create a PR Run `gh-axi pr list --state closed` to see closed PRs $ gh-axi pr list -R kunchenguid/firstmate --limit 3 # explicit upstream count: 3 of 497 total pull_requests[3]{number,title,state,author,draft,review}: 1800,"fix: preserve captain authority over scout promotion",open,VirtualRoboticHands,no,none 1799,"Exempt Cursor MCP: tool names from subagent guard",open,beraterkanelcelik,no,none 1798,"fix: preserve fleet state in truncated session-start digests",open,kunchenguid,no,none help[2]: Run `gh-axi pr view -R kunchenguid/firstmate` to view details Run `gh-axi pr create --title "..." --body-file -R kunchenguid/firstmate` to create ```

title: fix(classify): refuse to close a task on an unbacked done:
body:
## Intent Make it MECHANICALLY IMPOSSIBLE for a crewmate to close a task with a bare `done:` on a local commit that has no PR behind it. Seven sessions had already failed that way: hero-studio-restore, ci-merge-group-trigger and a third on 2026-07-31, then call-sales-script, tg-pricelist-capture and call-sales-script again on 2026-08-06, and finally the crew that implemented this very rule, which reported `done:` on its own unpushed commit hours after writing the refusal. Each time firstmate read the line, closed the task, and told the owner it had shipped; the costliest left branch fm/call-sales-prepayment never pushed to origin at all. The user explicitly ruled out a wording fix. bin/fm-brief.sh already stated the correct order in prose before every one of those cases, and the no-mistakes brief hands the worker the SAME word `done` for its intermediate "implemented and committed" gate as for the final shipped one, so no reader can tell the two apart from the line alone. The seventh case proves memory cannot carry it: the rules author broke the rule the same day. The user named bin/fm-classify-lib.sh as the anchor point, required exactly one added condition rather than a rewrite of event classification, and set three acceptance conditions: (1) a fake done must not close the task, (2) the worker must learn immediately rather than be silently reclassified, (3) delivery modes must differ because local-only has no PR by design. They also forbade bloating AGENTS.md beyond a one-line pointer and forbade touching paused/blocked/needs-decision. Design decisions I made and why, so they do not read as mistakes in the diff: - fm-classify-lib.sh owns ONE new condition (status_done_is_unbacked) plus the single refusal text, scoped by the tasks recorded delivery mode from state/.meta. no-mistakes and direct-PR require a full https://.../pull/ or /merge_requests/ URL; local-only, scout, secondmate and an absent/unrecognized mode are deliberately NOT constrained, because a false refusal on a scout report would be worse than the failure being closed. - Under mode=no-mistakes an unbacked done: is the crews legitimate INTERMEDIATE report, so the refusal text names a different next action there (instruct /no-mistakes) than under direct-PR (push and open the PR). Both are equally "not a completion". - Three consumers act on it, deliberately: fm-crew-state.sh reports `blocked` instead of `done` so everything derived from it (fleet snapshot, bearings) is covered; fm-wake-drain.sh prints a REJECTED DONE section on EVERY drain including the empty-queue path, carrying a ready-to-send steer so the worker is corrected within one wake and the rejection cannot be seen once and forgotten; scan_captain_relevant_statuses still surfaces the line but renders the refusal with it. - fm-teardown.sh also refuses, because teardown is what actually CLOSES a task: a branch merely pushed with no PR still passes the landed-work check. It refuses only when kind=ship AND the last line is an unbacked done AND no pr= was recorded by fm-pr-check.sh, so a genuinely shipped task is never refused; --force still bypasses like every other teardown gate. - Known and deliberate limit: the rule checks that a PR link is PRESENT, not that the PR is green. Greenness stays with fm-pr-check.sh and the no-mistakes CI step; verifying it in a pure classifier would mean a network call from a side-effect-free read. Evidence: both new test files were confirmed RED against the pre-change scripts (an unbacked done: reported state: done) and are green now. bin/fm-lint.sh exits 0, --check-coverage is ok at 124 scripts, and the doc audience check passes. The full behavior suite was run twice; every remaining failure was compared against a clean clone of the pre-change tree and traced to this box (tasks-axi 0.2.3 vs the 0.2.4 floor, and a tangle banner that fires for any checkout on a feature branch), not to this change. Two regressions this change did cause were found that way and fixed in their own commits: the fm-bearings-snapshot fixture used an unbacked `done: complete` for a mode=no-mistakes child, and tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh did not link fm-classify-lib.sh into its fake teardown roots. ## What Changed - Added a single `status_done_is_unbacked` condition (plus its refusal text) to `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh`, scoped by the task's recorded delivery mode from `state/.meta`: `no-mistakes` and `direct-PR` require a real `pull/` / `merge_requests/` URL, while `local-only`, `scout`, `secondmate` and unknown modes are deliberately not constrained; the `no-mistakes` refusal names a different next action (`/no-mistakes`) than `direct-PR` (push and open the PR). - Wired three consumers to the new predicate: `fm-crew-state.sh` now reports `blocked` instead of `state: done` for an unbacked done (covering fleet snapshot and bearings), `fm-wake-drain.sh` emits a `REJECTED DONE` section with a ready-to-send steer on every drain including the empty-queue path, and `fm-teardown.sh` refuses to tear down a `kind=ship` task whose last line is an unbacked done with no recorded `pr=` (genuinely landed work still tears down; `--force` still bypasses). - Added `tests/fm-done-requires-pr.test.sh` and `tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh`, fixed two regressions this change caused (the `fm-bearings-snapshot` terminal-child fixture and linking `fm-classify-lib.sh` into `fm-gotmp` fake teardown roots), and updated `AGENTS.md`/docs with a one-line pointer. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Additive, well-bounded change adding a single classifier condition wired into four consumers exactly as the intent specifies, with verified sourcing, no reachable false-refusal path, stable dedup signatures, and RED→GREEN tests; no source-verifiable defects found. ## Testing Exercised the classifier, drain, crew-state reader and teardown paths that implement the rule. The decisive product-level evidence is a CLI transcript driving the real bin/fm-classify-lib.sh: a fake `done:` on the never-pushed fm/call-sales-prepayment branch is refused under mode=no-mistakes ("instruct the crew to run /no-mistakes") and mode=direct-PR ("steer the crew to push and open the PR"), and accepted only for local-only/scout/unrecorded modes and for a done: line carrying a real pull/1800 URL — satisfying all three author acceptance conditions (fake done doesn't close, worker learns immediately, delivery modes differ). The teardown test confirms the same refusal at the point that actually closes a task. No UI surface is involved (shell classifier/CLI change), so evidence is CLI transcripts and test output rather than screenshots. All targeted tests pass; the full suite was intentionally not run per the targeted-validation boundary.
Evidence: Classifier e2e: fake done: refused across delivery modes, PR-backed done: accepted ### Fake done: on unpushed local commit (target commit) mode=no-mistakes -> REJECTED: not a completion - ... instruct the crew to run /no-mistakes and expect "done: PR <url> checks green". mode=direct-PR -> REJECTED: not a completion - mode=direct-PR delivers through a PR and this line carries none ... steer the crew to push and open the PR. mode=local-only -> ACCEPTED (closes task) mode=scout -> ACCEPTED (closes task) mode= -> ACCEPTED (closes task) ### done: carrying the PR URL is NOT refused mode=no-mistakes -> ACCEPTED mode=direct-PR -> ACCEPTED ```text ### Fake done: on unpushed local commit, across delivery modes (target commit) mode=no-mistakes -> REJECTED: not a completion - the crew reported its implementation, validation has shipped no PR yet. Do not close the task or report it to the captain; instruct the crew to run /no-mistakes and expect "done: PR checks green". mode=direct-PR -> REJECTED: not a completion - mode=direct-PR delivers through a PR and this line carries none, so the branch may not even be pushed. Do not close the task; steer the crew to push and open the PR, then re-report "done: PR ". mode=local-only -> ACCEPTED (closes task) mode=scout -> ACCEPTED (closes task) mode= -> ACCEPTED (closes task) ### A genuinely shipped done: (carries the PR URL) is NOT refused mode=no-mistakes -> ACCEPTED (closes task) mode=direct-PR -> ACCEPTED (closes task) ```
- Evidence: fm-done-requires-pr test log (local file: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZBAND6Y2PQBR0ZVBZF24XQK/fm-done-requires-pr.log)
Evidence: fm-teardown test log (ship-refuse path) ```text ok - local-only worktree with HEAD on a fork remote is torn down (fix holds) ok - teardown prompts tasks-axi backlog refresh when compatible ok - teardown honors config/backlog-backend=manual even when tasks-axi is compatible ok - local-only worktree with truly unpushed work is refused (safety preserved) ok - local-only worktree with work merged into local main is torn down (no regression) ok - no-mistakes worktree with HEAD on origin is torn down (no regression) ok - no-mistakes worktree with genuinely unlanded work is refused (safety preserved) ok - local-only worktree with unpushed work is torn down under --force (escape hatch) ok - title: fix(bin): accept effort on opencode/kimi profiles as documentation
body:
The crew_dispatch_validate() jq in fm-bootstrap.sh was rejecting any effort value for opencode and kimi harnesses. But fm-spawn.sh already records the requested effort= in task metadata while omitting the effort flag for harnesses that lack one (opencode and kimi have no verified effort flag). So an effort on an opencode/kimi profile is intended as documentation of desired effort, not an error.

Change the effort_ok() branch for opencode/kimi to accept any non-empty string effort (the malformed_optional_fields check upstream already validates it's a non-empty string). Other harnesses (claude/codex/grok/pi/pi-signed/muse) retain their accepted-set validation.

Add tests covering opencode/kimi effort-accepted cases and regression that invalid pi effort is still rejected.

Co-authored-by: Pi Crewmate <noreply@firstmate.local>

title: fix(bin): passive reads never start the herdr server
body:
## Intent Make herdr passive reads non-mutating, so observing a pane can never start a herdr server. Root cause: fm_backend_herdr_capture, fm_backend_herdr_capture_ansi and fm_backend_herdr_busy_state all went through fm_backend_herdr_target_ready, whose contract is to ensure the server. fm-watch.sh's Layer 1 busy poll calls fm_backend_capture every cycle, so simply observing a home restarted a stopped server within one poll interval. Herdr persists layout in session.json, so the restarted server restores workspaces and panes without the agent processes that were living in them; the next capture then succeeded against a fresh empty shell and hashed as a healthy quiet pane. It also made a home's 'no work left' condition unreachable, because a probe that starts what it observes can never observe an ending, so the Stop-armed watcher cycle never settled. ## What Changed - Split the herdr adapter's readiness into action vs. read: new `fm_backend_herdr_target_readable` parses the target and requires an already-running server without starting one, and `capture`, `capture_ansi`, and `busy_state` now use it instead of the server-ensuring `fm_backend_herdr_target_ready`, so an observation can no longer revive a layout whose panes no longer host their agents. - Stopped `bin/fm-watch.sh` from silently skipping an unreadable pane: a failed capture now runs the side-effect-free `fm_backend_target_exists` probe and, when the endpoint is absent and `state/.meta` is still present, raises exactly one `stale: (endpoint gone)` wake through the existing `fm_wake_append` plus `wake` pairing. The `.endpoint-gone-` marker records the wall-clock epoch of the first absent sighting and the verdict only fires after `FM_ENDPOINT_GONE_CONFIRM_SECS` (default 30, sized against fm-teardown.sh's pane-kill to meta-removal gap) have really elapsed, replacing a two-consecutive-poll count that a short `FM_POLL` could collapse to milliseconds; `fired` remains the one-wake suppression state and `clear_pause_tracking` clears the marker. - Documented the read/action split and the elapsed-time endpoint-gone contract in `docs/herdr-backend.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/configuration.md` (new `FM_ENDPOINT_GONE_CONFIRM_SECS` knob), `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md` (stopped-server probe transcript) and `AGENTS.md` (`.endpoint-gone-*` state file), and added coverage in `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh` (reads fail against a stopped server, actions still start it) and `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` (`test_endpoint_gone_floor_is_elapsed_time_not_poll_count` proving the verdict is held back before the floor and fires once after it). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Tightly scoped fix that replaces a poll count with a justified wall-clock floor, preserves every required guard, reset path, and the wake-append pairing, ships a two-sided behavioral regression test that exercises the real watcher, and updates both documentation owners; the only residual items are pre-existing tradeoffs and a verification gap, none of which block merge. ## Testing I exercised the two targeted test files the change touches and the one it was meant to unbreak: tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh passes with 48 ok including the new two-sided elapsed-time regression test, and tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh passes with 36 ok, so the concurrent-publication test that failed in CI job "Behavior portable serial 1" is green again with that file left untouched. To prove the new test earns its keep rather than passing vacuously, I reverted bin/fm-watch.sh to the PR head and confirmed both the original CI failure and the new test's own failure message reproduce, then restored the fix and watched both go green. For end-user-visible evidence I drove a real fm-watch.sh process against a genuinely absent endpoint at FM_POLL=0.02: with the production default floor the watcher stays alive across roughly two hundred consecutive absent polls, prints nothing, enqueues nothing, and the marker holds a wall-clock epoch; once the floor has really elapsed it exits after printing exactly one "stale: fmdemo:ship-widget (endpoint gone)" line, flips the marker to "fired", and the wake is readable on the durable queue; a relaunch on the same still-gone endpoint with the floor at zero stays silent, showing the suppression rather than the floor holds the second wake. The same transcript run against the pre-fix watcher fires within about forty milliseconds at a thirty-second floor, which is the defect stated verbatim. I also confirmed the unset-knob default holds the verdict, and checked that every rm -f reset path including clear_pause_tracking still targets the renamed marker. No failures, no flakiness, and the working tree was left clean after removing the temporary single-test driver.
Evidence: Manual watcher transcript with the fix: both sides of the time floor plus one-wake suppression ### Scenario: pane 'fmdemo:ship-widget' is unreadable and its endpoint is genuinely absent. ### Poll interval FM_POLL=0.02s, so ~50 absent sightings per second. == A. Default production floor (FM_ENDPOINT_GONE_CONFIRM_SECS=30), observed 4s == watcher process: STILL RUNNING after 4s (~200 consecutive absent polls) watcher stdout : '' <- empty: no premature endpoint-gone wake durable queue : '' <- empty: nothing enqueued gone marker : '1786045809' (wall-clock epoch of first absent sighting, 3s ago) == B. Same absent endpoint, floor already elapsed (FM_ENDPOINT_GONE_CONFIRM_SECS=1) == marker age is now 3s, so the 1s floor is provably past watcher process: EXITED <- woke firstmate, as designed watcher stdout : 'stale: fmdemo:ship-widget (endpoint gone)' gone marker : 'fired' <- one-wake suppression state durable queue : 1786045813 1 stale fmdemo:ship-widget stale: fmdemo:ship-widget (endpoint gone) == C. Suppression: relaunch on the same still-gone endpoint, floor 0 == watcher process: STILL RUNNING <- 'fired' suppresses a second wake even at floor 0 watcher stdout : '' <- empty: exactly one wake per disappearance ```text ### Scenario: pane 'fmdemo:ship-widget' is unreadable and its endpoint is genuinely absent. ### Poll interval FM_POLL=0.02s, so ~50 absent sightings per second. == A. Default production floor (FM_ENDPOINT_GONE_CONFIRM_SECS=30), observed 4s == watcher process: STILL RUNNING after 4s (~200 consecutive absent polls) watcher stdout : '' <- empty: no premature endpoint-gone wake durable queue : '' <- empty: nothing enqueued gone marker : '1786045809' (wall-clock epoch of first absent sighting, 3s ago) == B. Same absent endpoint, floor already elapsed (FM_ENDPOINT_GONE_CONFIRM_SECS=1) == marker age is now 3s, so the 1s floor is provably past watcher process: EXITED <- woke firstmate, as designed watcher stdout : 'stale: fmdemo:ship-widget (endpoint gone)' gone marker : 'fired' <- one-wake suppression state durable queue : 1786045813 1 stale fmdemo:ship-widget stale: fmdemo:ship-widget (endpoint gone) == C. Suppression: relaunch on the same still-gone endpoint, floor 0 == watcher process: STILL RUNNING <- 'fired' suppresses a second wake even at floor 0 watcher stdout : '' <- empty: exactly one wake per disappearance ```
Evidence: Same transcript against the pre-fix watcher: the gone verdict fires within ~40ms despite a 30s floor == A. Evidence: Original CI failure reproduced on the reverted watcher and green with the fix # tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh with bin/fm-watch.sh at PR head 6ba1fda: not ok - concurrent watcher never saw complete poll # with the fix restored (exit 0, 36 ok): ok - concurrent watchers observe only complete private poll publications ```text ok - raw-byte parser accepts canonical URLs and rejects the complete adversarial matrix ok - GitLab merge requests are followed on any instance and never wake falsely ok - validated merged polls notify once and retire before the next watcher cycle ok - merged poll retirement preserves every persistent secondmate lifecycle artifact ok - queue, receipt, and every fixed-path removal crash point recover without loss or repeated execution ok - open/red, closed-unmerged, malformed, and forge errors remain armed until an exact merged transition ok - replacement, nonterminal, tampered, and custom results receive no deletion authority ok - queue failure and untrusted receipts preserve canonical poll evidence ok - GitHub and GitLab exact merged results share one retirement path ok - PR and teardown entrypoints reject invalid arguments before every side effect ok - valid direct and merge flows record exact metadata and reject multiline head metadata ok - rejected metacharacter bytes remain inert at generation and watcher time ok - static poll is silent except for one merged line and remains watcher-bounded ok - interrupted atomic preparation cleans private temporaries and publishes nothing not ok - concurrent watcher never saw complete poll ```

Same absent endpoint, floor already elapsed (FM_ENDPOINT_GONE_CONFIRM_SECS=1) ==" echo "marker age is now $(( $(date +%s) - $(cat "$MARKER") ))s, so the 1s floor is provably past" run_watch 1 3 if kill -0 "$WPID" 2>/dev/null; then echo "watcher process: still running (verdict never fired)" else echo "watcher process: EXITED <- woke firstmate, as designed" fi echo "watcher stdout : '$(cat "$OUT")'" echo "gone marker : '$(cat "$MARKER")' <- one-wake suppression state" echo "durable queue :" sed 's/^/ /' "$STATE/.wake-queue" kill "$WPID" 2>/dev/null || true; wait "$WPID" 2>/dev/null || true echo echo "== C. Suppression: relaunch on the same still-gone endpoint, floor 0 ==" run_watch 0 3 if kill -0 "$WPID" 2>/dev/null; then echo "watcher process: STILL RUNNING <- 'fired' suppresses a second wake even at floor 0" else echo "watcher process: exited again (duplicate wake)" fi echo "watcher stdout : '$(cat "$OUT")' <- empty: exactly one wake per disappearance" kill "$WPID" 2>/dev/null || true; wait "$WPID" 2>/dev/null || true rm -rf "$DEMO" ```

✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 3 infos - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:983` - Residual teardown race above the 30s floor. bin/fm-teardown.sh's path between the pane kill (teardown_treehouse_return) and `rm -f "$STATE/$ID.meta"` (:2352) contains genuinely unbounded steps - the `no-mistakes axi abort` call, `rm -rf "$TASK_TMP"`, remove_firstmate_home, remove_pr_poll_artifacts - so a teardown slower than 30s still trips a spurious `stale: <window> (endpoint gone)` wake. This is not a regression (the PR's original 2-poll rule was also 30s at the default FM_POLL=15) and the 30s value is justified in the intent, so it is a tradeoff rather than a defect. The durable close would be a teardown-in-progress sentinel in $STATE that the watcher reads instead of a time guess; that is a shared-boundary change beyond this fix's authorized scope. - ℹ️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:64` - The new gone verdict is load-bearing on `fm_backend_target_exists` being side-effect-free, which for herdr is `herdr pane get <pane> --session <s>` (bin/fm-backend.sh:852). The new verification section in docs/verification/runtime-backends.md:221 sampled only capture, busy_state, and target_ready against a stopped server - `pane get` was not sampled. If herdr's `pane get` auto-starts a stopped server, target_exists returns true on every poll, the marker is rm'd each cycle, the verdict can never fire, and the window drops out of Layer 1 silently - the exact silent skip this block claims to eliminate. The read-only assumption predates this branch, but the comment at herdr.sh:63-64 now asserts it explicitly, so one lab probe of `pane get` against a stopped server would close the gap. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:983` - A backwards wall-clock step (NTP correction, VM/WSL resume) after the marker epoch is stamped makes `$(date +%s) - gone_since` negative, and since nothing re-stamps a marker that is already numeric, the verdict is stuck until the endpoint reappears or the marker is cleared. A forward jump has the inverse effect and fires early. Both are inherent to any wall-clock floor and self-heal on the next successful capture; noting it only because the marker is never re-stamped once numeric.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` (exit 0, 48 ok, includes `test_endpoint_gone_floor_is_elapsed_time_not_poll_count` and the adapted `test_endpoint_gone_confirmed_then_surfaced_once`) - `bash tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh` (exit 0, 36 ok, `concurrent watchers observe only complete private poll publications` green; file not modified) - Before/after ordering: `git checkout 6ba1fda -- bin/fm-watch.sh` then reran both files - reproduced `not ok - concurrent watcher never saw complete poll` and, with the new test isolated, `not ok - an absent endpoint fired before its time floor elapsed; the confirmation is counting polls, not seconds`; restored the fix and both pass - Manual end-to-end CLI demo driving a real `bin/fm-watch.sh` against a genuinely absent endpoint at `FM_POLL=0.02` on both sides of the floor, plus the one-wake suppression relaunch (`/tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZC978JP30V9NX7FVFZ2KD5G/demo-endpoint-gone-floor.sh`) - Same manual demo run against the reverted (PR-head) watcher to show the pre-fix behavior firing within ~40ms at `FM_ENDPOINT_GONE_CONFIRM_SECS=30` - Built-in default check: watcher launched with `FM_ENDPOINT_GONE_CONFIRM_SECS` unset at `FM_POLL=0.02` for 4s - stayed alive, printed nothing, enqueued nothing, marker held a numeric epoch - Code-level constraint check that every `rm -f` reset path survived the marker format change, including `clear_pause_tracking` (bin/fm-watch.sh:374), the endpoint-present reset (bin/fm-watch.sh:975), and the post-branch reset (bin/fm-watch.sh:993)
