title: watcher: use herdr native idle state for declared-pause cadence
body:
Fix the watcher's declared-pause cadence for live-but-idle herdr agents.

Problem: A crew with a declared paused:/captain-held status and a herdr agent whose agent_status is idle would previously get pause_state_class = none on every new pane hash, because fm_backend_agent_alive returns alive for any registered herdr agent. The watcher then surfaced a bare stale: wake roughly every time the idle pi TUI footer re-rendered.

Fix:
- Add fm_backend_agent_is_idle in bin/fm-backend.sh: for herdr it returns true only when the native agent_status is confidently idle; other backends return false.
- In bin/fm-watch.sh pause_state_class, check native idle before the existing live-agent fallback so that declared-pause + herdr idle keeps the bounded PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS cadence instead of firing per-hash bare stales.
- Unknown/unreadable liveness still classifies as none; tmux and backends without a native idle semantic keep current behavior; working, terminal, wedge-escalation, secondmate, and afk paths are untouched.

Tests:
- Add install_fake_herdr to tests/wake-helpers.sh.
- Extend tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh with four herdr cases: declared-pause + live-idle agent uses pause cadence and survives new pane hashes; declared-pause + dead agent unchanged; declared-pause + unreadable liveness surfaces; non-paused + idle agent unchanged.

Motivated by the 2026-08-06 p5 noise pattern observed for task-mctaskface-mvp-p1 on default:wA:p5.

title: fix(bin): seed remote secondmates from supplied origins
body:
## Intent Make remote secondmate seeding create no primary-home side effects beyond registering the remote route, and accept project origins from any host or forge. Firstmate shared, tracked material; captain direction 2026-08-04 after a real seed had to clone 6 repos into the primary home then remove them. Problem: remote seed required a local projects/ clone only so it could read 'git remote get-url origin' into the provisioning manifest, forcing a disposable primary-side clone and a no-mistakes init during remote setup. Captain's accepted requirements: 1. No primary side effects outside registering the remote route and the unavoidable primary-private registration records (data/secondmates.md, the charter brief under data/, and meta when launched). Seeding must NOT require cloning into primary projects/, a no-mistakes init on the primary, or a fleet sync as a precondition. 2. No rigid deterministic origin-URL machinery: no mandatory local clone, no single forced URL template. 3. The firstmate agent resolves the origin (captain, registry text, prior clones elsewhere, gh, explicit paste) and supplies it into seed/provision; the scripts validate and transport what the agent provided rather than discovering it by side-effecting the primary. 4. NEW captain requirement, decided mid-validation and explicitly in scope for this task: accepted origin URLs must be HOST/FORGE-AGNOSTIC, never a github whitelist. https/http/ssh/git schemes with any host, domain, port and path, plus the scp-like user@host:path form, must all pass - Bitbucket, GitHub Enterprise self-hosted, GitLab hosted and self-hosted, Gitea/Codeberg/sr.ht, and arbitrary self-hosted git. Validate STRUCTURE plus SAFETY only, never the forge or domain; fail closed on malformed input, injection vectors, and unsafe local/file: paths. E2E-verify NON-github origins: bitbucket.org, a self-hosted enterprise domain (git.example.com), a self-hosted GitLab, and a bare scp-like custom host. 5. Captain's decision on the review gate's documentation-owner finding [doc-owner-split]: REFINED FIX - bin/fm-project-origin-lib.sh is the sole owner of accepted URL forms, docs carry a one-line pointer, and the secondmate-provisioning skill KEEPS its distinct agent-operating-behavior lines (the agent supplies the origin; no clone/init/fleet-sync) because that is a different contract, not URL-acceptance duplication. The earlier pipeline fix round removed those skill lines, so this run restores them per that decision; do not re-delete them. Non-goals ruled out by the captain: copying project trees from primary to remote (the remote still clones from origin), and removing the need for remote host credentials to fetch the origin. Decisions and tradeoffs: - The project positional accepts =. A bare is a deliberate backward-compatible convenience that reads an already-present clone's origin, never a reason to create one; that is why the mandatory clone check was deleted rather than the fallback. - bin/fm-project-origin-lib.sh is the single owner of accepted forms and states in its header that there is no host, domain, or forge allowlist and there must never be one. Verified before changing anything: the validator never had a forge whitelist - bitbucket, GHE-style domains, self-hosted GitLab with a port, Gitea, Codeberg, sr.ht, raw IPv4, and underscore hosts already passed on structure. Two genuine gaps found and closed: a bracketed IPv6 literal in the scp-like form (e.g. [2001:db8::1]:/srv/repo.git) was refused and is now accepted, and a '/../' traversal inside a local or file: origin was accepted and is now refused because it names a path on the cloning host's own filesystem. - Both ends validate: the sending parent before transport and the receiving host before cloning, so a manifest is never trusted because the sender looked at it. - Origins read from an existing local clone go through the same validator, so an exotic remote (e.g. git+ssh://) is now refused where it previously passed. Deliberate and fail-closed; the error names the URL and the = escape hatch. - Deliberately unchanged: the project's registered delivery mode still comes from the primary's data/projects.md (unregistered and local-only projects are still refused), and the manifest wire schema fm-remote-home-provision.v1 is unchanged because only the origin's SOURCE changed, so an older remote code root still provisions. - Verification: the E2E lives in the existing tests/fm-remote-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh rather than a new runner. It seeds a registered project the primary has never cloned and asserts the primary projects/ tree is byte-identical afterwards via a hash snapshot, plus refusals for missing origin, unsafe origin, local-only, and unregistered project, and a receiving-host rejection of an unsafe manifest origin. A second case seeds four non-GitHub origins in one seed (bitbucket.org, git.example.com, ssh:// self-hosted GitLab with port, scp-like git@host.internal) and asserts each URL reached the remote side's git clone unchanged and each clone carries its own origin's content. Because the suite is offline, a fixture origin resolver on the remote code root records the exact clone source production code hands to git and serves it from a local bare repository; it is removed afterwards and the remote code root is asserted clean. tests/fm-project-origin.test.sh leads its accepted matrix with non-GitHub hosts and demonstrates the ext:: hazard against real git before pinning its refusal, so no test asserts implementation source text. Delivery note: the previous run for this branch was cancelled because a GitHub Actions outage meant no workflow run was ever created for its pushed head, so its CI monitor could never see checks. That outage has lifted; this run re-pushes a fresh head for a genuine CI result. yolo is off, so the captain merges. ## What Changed - Allow remote secondmate seeds to accept `=`, removing the requirement for a matching project clone in the primary home while retaining the existing-clone fallback for bare project names. - Validate supplied origins at both provisioning boundaries with a shared, host-agnostic validator that supports standard URL and scp-like forms while rejecting malformed, executable, and unsafe local paths. - Document and cover no-primary-project side effects, non-GitHub origins, unsafe manifests, and registered delivery-mode enforcement. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-bounded, removes the mandatory primary clone path, validates supplied origins at both transport boundaries, and the authority-validation fix closes the previously identified malformed and option-shaped host paths without introducing a forge allowlist. ## Testing No separate baseline commands were supplied; both targeted executable tests passed, their evidence runs demonstrated forge-agnostic remote cloning and no primary project-tree mutation, and final cleanup verification found no testing changes in the worktree.
Evidence: Project origin validation transcript `Accepted ordinary clone URLs and refused executable, option-shaped, and unsafe forms. All tests passed.` ```text ok - ordinary clone URLs are accepted and clone with the command the remote host runs ok - executable transports, option-shaped values, and unusable spellings are refused ALL TESTS PASSED ```
Evidence: Remote secondmate lifecycle E2E transcript `Demonstrates supplied-origin remote seeding without primary project-tree changes, receiver-side validation, and unchanged Bitbucket, self-hosted, and scp-like origins reaching remote clones. All tests passed.` ```text ok - overlapping remote home provisioning serializes through publication and rollback ok - remote seed rollback preserves serialized competing routes ok - unknown readiness preserves its route and brief for reconciliation ok - remote seeding checks, repairs, and re-checks readiness, then stops on a remaining gap ok - remote seeding proceeds once the repair closes every gap ok - remote seeding provisions a supplied origin without touching the primary project tree ok - remote provisioning re-validates a supplied origin at the receiving host ok - seeding carries bitbucket, self-hosted, and scp-like origins through to the remote clone ok - remote seed registers the route and provisions the whole home and project clone on that host ok - remote inheritance rejects incomplete and superseded payload generations ok - mixed local and remote routes validate without migration ok - remote spawn launches on the remote-local backend and records a host-qualified route ok - legacy and mismatched remote endpoints fail closed before backend access ok - non-herdr remote endpoints are refused without changing either route ok - remote spawn serializes inheritance through launch publication ok - marked send and routed reply complete through the existing parent correlation owner ok - partial remote inheritance retains reread intent through bootstrap convergence ok - config push and bootstrap serialize remote inheritance convergence ok - remote inherited config retains and retries a failed live reread nudge ok - fleet snapshot projects mixed local and remote structured state ok - remote update imports and fast-forwards the persistent home on its configured host ok - startup repairs remote readiness before probing without relaunching ok - startup reports alive legacy backends without changing their routes ok - unreachable remote state remains unknown with no local respawn or failover ok - remote retirement refuses child work, then removes only its own endpoint while a shared-session sibling survives ALL TESTS PASSED ```

Consequently malformed origins such as `https:///repo.git`, `ssh://:2222/repo.git`, and invalid IPv6 spellings pass; option-shaped SSH hosts can also reach Git. Tighten validation at this shared sender/receiver boundary to require a structurally valid host/authority and reject option-shaped hosts, while retaining host/forge agnosticism. 🔧 Fix: Validate project origin authorities safely ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: fix(skills): reconcile inherited secondmate plans with shipped state
body:
## Intent Add a small record-intake instruction to the secondmate CREATION/seed path in firstmate's secondmate-provisioning skill, so a new mate that takes over an existing or inherited domain reconciles against authoritative shipped-state instead of inheriting a plan backlog blind. WHY (captain's chosen safeguard, 2026-08-06): this is the fix for a stale-record recurrence forensically diagnosed in two scout reports (data/fm-stale-record-discord-forensic-s1/report.md and data/fm-stale-record-discord-attribution-s2/report.md). A predecessor secondmate home shipped 21+ merged PRs for a product; when it was retired into a successor, the handover carried backlog.md, captain.md, learnings.md and a brief, but NOT done-archive.md. Because .tasks.toml sets done_keep = 10, a live backlog structurally cannot hold more than ten completions, so the successor inherited 49 open plan rows and zero record of 21 shipped PRs. Already-delivered work therefore resurfaced as 'open'. The verified gap: creation/seeding pulls in charter + inherited config + captain-shared + project clones + (separately) QUEUED backlog only, with ZERO instruction about a domain's shipped/done history, so it assumes a greenfield mate. CAPTAIN'S EXPLICIT REFRAME AND SCOPE DECISION: do NOT build a bespoke retirement/consolidation export process - retirement is too rare to be the leverage point. Strengthen secondmate CREATION instead, which every transfer relies on. This deliberately fixes BOTH the rare retirement/consolidation case AND the COMMON case of creating a mate for an in-progress project. The captain accepted the tradeoff that reconciliation cost is now paid at every inherited-domain creation rather than once at handover, because creation-side reconciliation works even when the predecessor's export was poor or its home is already gone. THE FIX, as captain-specified: add a small RECORD-INTAKE instruction to secondmate-provisioning's creation/seed section requiring that, when a new mate takes over an EXISTING or INHERITED domain (a project already in development, or a predecessor's domain), the creating agent MUST (1) reconcile the inherited plans against the domain's authoritative SHIPPED-state - origin/main plus the live deployment - NOT the imported backlog and NOT an absent/fresh local view; (2) pull in only genuinely-open work plus the domain's durable knowledge (learnings/decisions still live); (3) NEVER inherit a plan backlog blind, meaning never carry plan rows for work already shipped. The greenfield-vs-inherited distinction must be explicit so a genuinely new domain is not burdened. EXPLICIT SCOPE EXCLUSION: this ship is the record-intake creation instruction ONLY. The separate fix to close open-decisions by construction on the decision key and de-overload the 'resolved' verb (the doer's self-blindness defect, also diagnosed in those reports) is captured as its own separately queued ship, fm-decision-key-close-by-construction-r1, and must NOT be implemented here. Also deliberately out of scope: the s1 report's R1 recommendation for a mechanical export gate at retirement - the captain ruled retirement out of scope as too rare. DELIBERATE DESIGN DECISIONS MADE WHILE IMPLEMENTING (per firstmate's firstmate-coding-guidelines, which was loaded first as the brief required): - ONE-OWNER RULE: the reconcile-against-shipped-state procedure lives entirely in the secondmate-provisioning skill, which owns secondmate creation/seeding. A new '## Record intake for an existing or inherited domain' section was placed in the creation/seed path, immediately after 'Charter and seed' and before 'Backlog handoff'. git grep confirms no second copy of the contract exists. - AGENTS.md WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNTOUCHED, and this is correct, not an omission. AGENTS.md section 6 already carries the load trigger ('Load secondmate-provisioning before creating, seeding, ...'), which fires on exactly this path, so no new trigger line was needed. AGENTS.md size discipline is a first-class rule in this repo (the file grew 585 -> 958 lines from inline conditional detail); its token cost is paid by every session of every fleet member, so conditional detail belongs in the skill whose cost is paid only by sessions that load it. The captain explicitly said 'Do not bloat AGENTS.md.' - One single-line reinforcement WAS added in the 'Backlog handoff' section ('For an existing or inherited domain, complete record intake first so no already-shipped plan row is handed off as open work.'). The guidelines permit exactly one deliberate one-line reinforcement at a genuine risk point; this is that point, because it is where plan rows physically move between homes. It is a pointer, not a restatement of the contract. - The skill's frontmatter description 'Covers' list gained 'record intake for an existing or inherited domain' so the new content is discoverable at load time. - The fetched-clone precondition was folded in as ONE clause of obligation 1 rather than a separate rule, because an unfetched or missing clone is precisely the 'absent/fresh local view' trap the captain named. This is a proportionate inclusion of the s1 report's R4, not scope creep. - The inadmissible-evidence list explicitly names the imported backlog, the predecessor's own notes, instruction-surface prose, and an absent/unfetched local view, because the forensic proved the failure mode was judging 'already shipped' from Firstmate's own prose (harness-adapters skill contents, AGENTS.md sections, captain-shared.md) with not one origin/main commit, PR, or deployment cited. - The done_keep causal fact is stated once, as the non-obvious reason the rule exists: a live backlog keeps only the configured recent Done entries by design, so an inherited queue structurally over-represents plans and under-represents deliveries. - Residual-uncertainty capture was included because the forensic showed the successor inherited silence about what was never reconciled. NO TEST WAS ADDED, and this is a deliberate, correct decision rather than an oversight. Both this repo's guidelines and no-mistakes' own test-quality rule forbid a test whose only evidence is that it greps, parses, or snapshots implementation/instruction source text for particular strings. A test asserting that this skill's Markdown contains the intake step would be exactly that forbidden anti-pattern. There is no executable consumer of agent-skill prose, so no public or executable interface exists to exercise here. The brief anticipated this explicitly: 'otherwise this is a documentation-contract change and the audience check is the gate.' The gate that does apply, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh, was run and passes (ok surfaces=65 local_links=205). STYLE CONSTRAINTS OBSERVED (repo rules): one full sentence per line in tracked Markdown, never multiple sentences on one physical line; plain dash '-' only, never an em dash; no agent name as commit co-author. This is firstmate shared, tracked material, delivered under mode=no-mistakes. ## What Changed - Distinguish greenfield secondmate domains from existing or inherited domains that require record intake before acting on inherited plans. - Require inherited plans to be reconciled against fetched `origin/main` state and the live deployment, rather than backlogs, predecessor notes, or incomplete local views. - Seed only genuinely open work and durable knowledge, capture unresolved uncertainty, and complete reconciliation before backlog handoff. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The documentation-only change is narrowly scoped, conforms to the required record-intake contract, preserves the greenfield distinction, and introduces no substantiated source risk. ## Testing No baseline command was supplied; targeted validation inspected the complete one-file contract diff, confirmed its agent-runtime audience, and ran the maintained-prose/link checker successfully. No unit test was added because agent-skill prose has no executable semantic consumer and a source-text assertion is expressly forbidden. No screenshot was captured because this is an agent-only Markdown instruction surface with no rendered UI.

For `no-mistakes` projects, seeding initializes only projects newly cloned into a secondmate home and refuses to mutate a preexisting clone that is not already initialized. +## Record intake for an existing or inherited domain + +Classify the domain before seeding, because this step applies to only one of the two cases. +A greenfield domain has no delivered domain work yet: nothing already shipped in its projects, no live deployment, and no predecessor records to import. +Seed a greenfield domain normally; there is nothing to reconcile and this section adds no work to it. +An existing or inherited domain is any domain whose product is already in development, and any predecessor's domain a new mate takes over, including a consolidation after a retirement. +Both of those cases require record intake before the new mate acts on any inherited plan. + +For an existing or inherited domain, the creating agent must: + +1. Reconcile every inherited plan against the domain's authoritative shipped state, which is `origin/main` for each relevant project plus the live deployment. + A fetched clone of each relevant project is a precondition of that reconciliation, so wire the home to its projects before reconciling rather than on first task. + The imported backlog, the predecessor's own notes, instruction-surface prose, and an absent or unfetched local view are all inadmissible as shipped-state evidence. +2. Seed the new home with only genuinely open work plus the domain's durable knowledge, meaning the learnings, decisions, and delivery posture that are still live. +3. title: feat: arm validation gates for no-mistakes ship tasks
body:
## Intent

Automatically arm a registered, silent no-mistakes validation poll for each no-mistakes ship task. The poll wakes supervision only for a terminal run or an agent-awaiting run parked beyond the configurable 240-second default. It is local, credential-free, and silent for healthy runs.

## What changed

- Added the tracked validation-poll scripts and trusted check registration path.
- Arm the validation poll at no-mistakes ship-task lifecycle transitions, including promotion and compatible reconciliation paths.
- Preserve the one-slot check lifecycle: validation owns the slot before a PR exists; the canonical PR merge poll takes priority after PR handoff and validation never overwrites it.
- Added lifecycle coverage for registration, silence, terminal/parked wakes, unregistered-check refusal, and both validation-to-merge transition directions.

## Validation

- Passed focused validation-gate, spawn, delivery, update, Orca, and remote-secondmate lifecycle suites.
- The end-to-end transcript confirms healthy silence; terminal and over-threshold parked wakes; local `axi status` polling without provider calls; and preserved PR merge polling.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` ran in the no-mistakes pipeline; all change-introduced ShellCheck warnings/errors were corrected. The configured linter still reports existing informational notices outside this change, which the pipeline recorded and approved under the scope cap.

## Explicit deferred follow-ups (scope cap)

- **R31 — first self-update reconciliation:** A home that updates from pre-change `fm-update.sh` can fast-forward without executing the new reconciliation, leaving an existing quiet `kind=ship` / `mode=no-mistakes` task unarmed. Add an update-boundary reconciliation or durable retry so the first update repairs those existing tasks.
- **R32 — safe watcher handoff after self-update:** A pre-change watcher can observe a newly registered validation poll as a generic custom check during a respawn or PR handoff, without the newer slot/revalidation protections. Add an atomic or restart-safe watcher handoff at the update boundary.

These two genuine existing-home/self-update concerns are deliberately deferred to keep this delivery limited to the proven fresh-task validation-gate behavior.

title: feat(bin): prevent cross-kernel localhost shadowing
body:
## Intent

Implement Firstmate-wide prevention and closure for cross-kernel localhost shadowing. Provide one reusable inspect/recover/verify helper for a project, reserved port, and expected canonical SHA, with its --help as the single mechanics owner. Inspect Windows and WSL listener/process/Git/task identity and report redacted ownership evidence. Permit automatic mutation only for an independently proven stale native-Windows Node/Astro dev PID from the same repository, with an immediate identity recheck, no active Firstmate task, a private pre-mutation evidence record, and a clean expected current-main WSL replacement; refuse every ambiguous, changed, unrelated, production-like, unavailable-inspection, missing-identity, active-task, or wslrelay case, and never use process-name or port-wide kills. After exact-PID termination, restart only the verified project Astro launcher and require the expected wslrelay/WSL pair plus matching Windows- and WSL-origin browser-context fingerprints. Include deterministic tests, a concise AGENTS trigger, maintained documentation and verification evidence, and the test-family mapping. The separate global iteration-sandbox skill edit is intentionally excluded from this repository commit. Deliver as a draft PR, do not merge.

## What Changed

- Added a reusable localhost inspect/recover/verify helper covering Windows and WSL listener, process, Git, and task identity evidence.
- Added guarded exact-PID recovery for stale native-Windows development processes, task-state locking, deterministic localhost tests, and changed-path test-family mapping.
- Updated AGENTS.md, runtime-backend documentation, and verification evidence for cross-kernel localhost protection.

## Risk Assessment

🚨 High: Required safety invariants remain reachable through active WSL tasks, ambiguous WSL ownership, and non-main or unrelated relay identities, while the new lock helper also breaks changed-test selection until mapped.

## Testing

Validated the localhost inspect/recover/verify contract and deterministic refusal/recovery paths, ran the focused localhost and test-runner suites, confirmed changed-file selection includes the localhost tests, captured CLI evidence, and found no remaining actionable issues.

<details>
<summary>Evidence: Localhost helper contract</summary>

```text
usage: fm-localhost.py [-h] {inspect,recover,verify} project port expected_sha

Inspect or narrowly recover localhost ownership across native Windows and WSL.

positional arguments:
  {inspect,recover,verify}
  project
  port
  expected_sha

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

mechanics (authoritative):
  The tuple is <project> <port> <expected-sha>. <project> must be the intended
  clean WSL default-branch checkout, and <expected-sha> must be its full 40-hex
  canonical commit. inspect reports every Windows and WSL listener with owner
  kernel, address, PID, process, redacted command, checkout, branch, SHA, dirty
  state, normalized Git source, task association, classification, and recovery
  verdict. It reads Windows listeners and process identity through fixed
  non-interactive PowerShell, WSL listeners through ss and /proc, and task
  associations from this Firstmate home's state/*.meta. It never reads a
  process environment, credentials, production data, or hosted data.

  recover is deliberately narrower than inspect. It may stop exactly one PID
  only after complete observations, including a fresh mutation-boundary
  recheck, independently prove that the same PID still owns every
  native-Windows binding of the reserved port; the unchanged
  process is node.exe whose first script argument resolves to that checkout's
  node_modules/astro/astro.js or astro.mjs and is followed immediately by `dev`;
  that checkout is dirty,
  divergent, or otherwise noncanonical; no task record names that checkout or
  PID; WSL has no unrelated port owner; and the requested replacement is clean,
  on the repository default branch, at expected-sha. Unknown commands, changed
  PIDs or commands, multiple Windows owners, unrelated sources, task records,
  missing identity, Windows inspection failure, canonical Windows source,
  production-like commands, and every wslrelay.exe owner refuse recovery.
  Recovery never kills by process name or port and never targets wslrelay.exe.

  Immediately before mutation, recover re-resolves listener, PID, command,
  checkout, Git, and task evidence. The termination boundary repeats that
  complete proof after the evidence is fsynced while holding the shared
  Firstmate task-state publication boundary; task creation and metadata
  publication use that same boundary. It writes a mode-0600 record beneath
  $FM_HOME/state/localhost-evidence before invoking fixed PowerShell that again
  requires the exact PID, port, node.exe identity, unchanged command hash, and
  exact Astro script path followed by `dev`. After the exact PID exits, it
  re-resolves the clean expected checkout and runs only that project's package.json
  `scripts.dev` when that script is proven to be Astro, using `npm run dev --
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port <port>`; an already-running expected WSL server is reused
  rather than duplicated.

  verify sends the same bounded browser-like request to http://localhost:<port>/
  from WSL and native Windows, compares status/body-length/SHA-256 fingerprints,
  then repeats the listener-pair inspection. It passes only when Windows reports
  wslrelay.exe, WSL reports the clean expected Astro server, and both route
  fingerprints match the post-route pair. A nonzero exit means
  inspection, recovery, or verification did not prove the requested safe state.
```

<details>
<summary>⚠️ **Review** - 6 issues (5 errors, 1 warning)</summary>

- 🚨 `bin/fm-localhost.py:1009` - The intent requires “no active Firstmate task” and says to “refuse every ... active-task ... case.” The changed recovery path snapshots task state at `mutation = inspect_system(...)` (line 1009), then writes evidence and later calls `terminate_exact(...)` (line 1025) without a shared lock or atomic task-metadata publication boundary. A task can become active, or its `.meta` can be observed mid-write, between those operations, so the PID can still be terminated. Make task creation/publication and localhost mutation honor the same shared state boundary.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-localhost.py:359` - The intent requires “refuse every ... missing-identity ... case” and an “expected wslrelay/WSL pair.” `classify_windows` returns `wslrelay` from only `process` name (`if lower_name == "wslrelay.exe": return "wslrelay"`, lines 359-360), before checking `executable`; `verified_pair` then accepts that classification at line 883. A WMI result with a missing or noncanonical executable identity can therefore pass verification as the relay. Require complete, canonical relay executable identity before classifying it as `wslrelay`.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-localhost.py:883` - Listener counts are treated as ambiguity even when every binding belongs to the same owner. `verified_pair` requires exactly one Windows and one WSL row (lines 883-885), while `termination_boundary_listener` also rejects `len(boundary.windows) != 1` at line 966. A legitimate Node or wslrelay process with IPv4 and IPv6 bindings is therefore refused despite `recovery_verdict` already proving a single PID owns all bindings. Group and compare the complete listener sets by owner PID, refusing only distinct or inconsistent owners.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-localhost.py:1164` - The intent requires refusal for “unavailable-inspection” cases. When Firstmate task-state inspection is unavailable, `inspect_system` sets `task_error` and returns, but the changed `inspect` CLI exits success because line 1164 checks only `windows_error` and `wsl_error`. This lets callers treat an incomplete ownership inspection as successful; include `task_error` in the inspect exit condition.

🔧 Fix: Ben harden localhost task and listener proof boundaries
6 issues (5 errors, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-localhost.py:728` - The intent requires “no active Firstmate task” and says to “refuse every ... active-task ... case.” `recovery_verdict` checks task associations only for Windows listeners at lines 728-730; WSL listeners already carry `tasks` but those associations are ignored, and `verified_pair` does not check them either. An active task owning the expected WSL server can therefore still allow exact-PID mutation and verification. Enforce the task-free invariant across both kernels at the shared pair/recovery boundary.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-localhost.py:731` - The intent requires “refuse every ambiguous ... case.” Recovery only rejects multiple Windows PIDs, then accepts any number of WSL listeners if each individually matches the expected source. Two distinct WSL PIDs can therefore pass eligibility, the Windows PID is terminated, and only the post-stop check discovers the ambiguity. Reject a non-empty WSL listener set whose ownership is not consistent before any mutation.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-localhost.py:733` - The intent requires a “clean expected current-main WSL replacement.” Both the recovery WSL checks and `verified_pair` validate checkout, SHA, cleanliness, and source, but never require `listener.git.branch == expected.default_branch`. - 🚨 `bin/fm-localhost.py:696` - The intent requires an “expected wslrelay/WSL pair” and refusal of “unrelated” or “missing-identity” cases. `canonical_wslrelay_identity` accepts any absolute drive path ending in `wslrelay.exe`, including an unrelated executable such as `C:\Users\x\wslrelay.exe`; `verified_pair` then accepts it as the Windows relay. title: fix(bin): close decisions when answers are sent
body:
## Intent Fix, at its structural root, why Firstmate's OPEN DECISIONS list shows captain decisions as still open long after they have been answered. Diagnosed failure: the decision fold (bin/fm-classify-lib.sh, rendered by bin/fm-wake-drain.sh) opens a decision on a keyed needs-decision:/blocked: status line and closes it only on a resolved (or captain-held transfer) line carrying the exact same key; when the answer to a decision is itself the start of work, the worker's natural next line is working [key=] in a different key namespace, so no resolved [key=] is ever written and the decision orphans as permanently open. The commissioned fix is design (E) 'answerer-closes', validated before building: remove the writer-dependency at its source by having the ANSWERING firstmate - which already holds the decision key from the OPEN DECISIONS listing and is already required by AGENTS.md section 7 to name it - append the closing resolved [key=X] line to the owned state/.status itself at answer time, needing zero cooperation from the busy worker. Implementation: fm-send.sh gains a repeatable --resolve-key flag; after the submit is confirmed it appends 'resolved [key=]: answered: ' to this home's state/.status. Deliberate design decisions: (1) the close is a LOCAL ledger append for every target kind - crewmate, scout, local secondmate, and remote secondmate - because the open-decision ledger always lives in the answerer's own state dir (a remote mate's escalations reach it through the parent-replies ingest), so remote differs from local only at the message transport layer, per the captain's standing architecture principle; (2) fail-closed pre-send check: every named key must currently be open per the authoritative status_open_decisions fold or fm-send refuses BEFORE sending, so a mistyped key cannot deliver an answer while silently orphaning its decision; (3) closure happens only after fully confirmed delivery - a failed or unconfirmed send never closes a key, and an append failure after a delivered answer exits nonzero with the exact manual close command so the decision stays open and re-surfaces (the safe direction); (4) a send without the flag never closes anything, and the fold semantics are untouched so a routine working:/done: line still can never clear a captain decision - explicitly required by the task; (5) the flag is refused with --key, with explicit backend targets (no task ledger in this home), with an empty message, and for malformed or duplicate keys; (6) the wake-drain OPEN DECISIONS section prints a one-line answer-with-close command hint so the mechanism is taught at the moment of use. Complementary fixes required for a COMPLETE solution: defect 2 (overloaded resolved contract) is fixed in all three fm-brief.sh scaffolds by separating resolved's two duties - keyed-phase bookkeeping vs decision closure - stating that a decision stays open until a resolved line carrying its exact key lands, that a later done:/working: line never closes it even when the answer is what started that work, and that the worker self-closes only a blocker or wait that clears WITHOUT a firstmate reply (the one path where no answer is ever sent); defect 1 (a mate is structurally blind to decisions it escalated into the parent's ledger) deliberately gets NO separate mate-side ledger: with answerer-closes the parent-side ledger's owner both opens (via the mate's escalation or remote ingest) and closes (at answer time), so a mate-side mirror would only re-create cross-home coupling; the pending-reply/corr machinery is deliberately NOT used for closure, as the task requires. The fix must NOT be just cleverer key-matching in the fold. Tests must be behavioral through the executable interface, not source-text assertions: tests/fm-send-resolve-key.test.sh drives the real fm-send over stubbed tmux and stubbed ssh transports (FM_SSH_BIN) through the real fm-on route, and asserts closure through the real consumer (fm-wake-drain.sh's OPEN DECISIONS output), covering the exact answer-starts-work orphan scenario, refusal-before-send on a not-open key, failed local and failed remote sends closing nothing, multi-key answers, the marked local-secondmate path (closing line carries the plain answer, no marker/corr bytes), and flag-misuse refusals; the new suite is mapped into the backend-dispatch test family so the CI coverage guard stays exact. Constraints honored: firstmate-coding-guidelines (one-owner rule - the mechanics live in the fm-send.sh header, with one-line pointers in AGENTS.md sections 7 and the ask-user flow, a closure-ownership cross-reference in fm-classify-lib.sh's fold-contract comment, and one maintainer sentence in docs/architecture.md; one sentence per line in tracked markdown; plain dash, no em dash; shellcheck-clean bin scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh; colocated tests named .test.sh; never add an agent name as commit co-author). Delivery: no-mistakes, yolo OFF - the captain owns the merge. Note: GitHub Actions is in a major outage right now; the run is expected to park at the CI step - that is expected and must not be treated as a failure, and stuck CI must not be cancelled or retried. ## What Changed - Add repeatable `fm-send --resolve-key` support that validates open decision keys before delivery and appends local `resolved` events only after confirmed sends. - Teach wake output and worker guidance that answers close decisions explicitly, while unrelated `working` or `done` events leave them open. - Add executable coverage for local, remote, multi-key, failure, misuse, and answer-starts-work scenarios. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-bounded and implements the required answerer-owned closure only after confirmed delivery, with fail-closed key validation and behavioral coverage across local, secondmate, and remote paths. ## Testing Inspected the target change, ran the three focused behavioral suites, and captured CLI evidence showing the historic answer-starts-work orphan is closed while routine work cannot close decisions; duplicate keys refuse before delivery, and a failed post-delivery ledger append leaves the decision visible with manual recovery guidance. All checks passed and no source or transient worktree files were left behind.

OPEN DECISIONS: close one by answering it: bin/fm-send.sh --resolve-key '' $ fm-send.sh rollout --resolve-key rollout-plan "Use phased rollout; gate each region" WARNING: watcher still down (same stale episode; last beat: never, grace 300s) - full banner already printed this episode. exit: 0 delivered to worker: Use phased rollout; gate each region $ worker records work under a different key (the historic orphan trigger) resolved [key=rollout-plan]: answered: Use phased rollout; gate each region working [key=regional-implementation]: building region gates $ fm-wake-drain.sh # after answer starts work (no OPEN DECISIONS section) ```

The under-40k stretch goal is withdrawn: trimming other sections expands scope beyond what was approved, and the always-loaded contract there needs deliberate redesign, not a passing cut. - The PR body must state plainly: the final size, that the large-memory warning threshold is still exceeded, and that further reduction would need its own considered effort. The Test gate confirmed the exact size delta, the presence of all four relocated rules, that all pointer targets exist, and that `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` passes on the result. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Docs-only trim of one AGENTS.md section that matches the authoritative intent exactly: the final size (53,563 chars) is as accepted, all four relocated normative rules appear in the new prose, and every dropped annotation's claimed owner (other AGENTS.md sections, docs/configuration.md, or the producing script headers) was verified to exist and cover it. ## Testing Verified the section-2 trim end-to-end against the intent: exact before/after char counts (63,377 → 53,563), a single-hunk section-2-only diff with symlinks untouched, all four relocated safety rules present in the new prose, the sweep's coverage claims confirmed in their owning sections, every new pointer target existing on disk, no em/en dashes in added lines, and the intent-named bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh acceptance check passing; the change is a plain-Markdown agent-context surface, so the evidence is a CLI transcript of the new section rather than a screenshot.
