title: fix(bin): stop reporting live runs as failed when their unpushed tip is unresolvable
body:
## Intent Fix a measured false-verdict defect in the shared no-mistakes run-attribution rule, bin/fm-nm-run-lib.sh:fm_nm_head_matches_worktree, and its two consumers (bin/fm-crew-state.sh, bin/fm-teardown.sh). RESUMING: this branch already carries commit 078c7eff, the fix round produced by THIS pipeline's own review gate on run 01KZC6Q944NDA19ET6955Q530V (review completed, 0 findings remaining). That run then died at the test step because the agent's Claude session limit was hit mid-step ("You've hit your session limit"), not because any test failed; custody was returned with no-mistakes axi sync --recover, preserving the review fixes. Re-validating the same content. THE DEFECT (measured live 2026-08-06). A lane actively running its lint step was reported "state: failed / source: run-step / run failed". Mechanism, traced end to end: fm_nm_head_matches_worktree resolves the run head THROUGH THE WORKTREE (git -C "$wt" rev-parse --verify "${run_head}^{commit}" || return 1). During validation, no-mistakes commits its fix rounds in its own gate-repo clone and does not push until the push step, so the live run's tip is routinely NOT an object the crew worktree has (measured: worktree HEAD d4032f07, live run head 5152b3ab, "Not a valid object name"). The lookup failure returned "no match", collapsing "I cannot determine this" into "this is not mine". The helper's own header documents that the descendant case MUST match because "pipeline fix commits advanced the run tip past local HEAD" - yet the implementation cannot see those commits, so the documented normal case was structurally unmatchable during every fix round. The rejected run then fell through to the coarse runs-list scan, which applies the same rule per row: the live running row was skipped and an OLDER, genuinely FAILED run sitting at the worktree's own head matched and won (COARSE_STATUS=failed, RUN_SOURCE=coarse, RUN_STATE=failed). A working lane was reported dead. THE FIX. 1. fm_nm_head_matches_worktree is now three-valued instead of two-valued: 0 MATCH (head resolves here and equals or descends from local HEAD), 1 NO MATCH (no head reported at all, so no identity claim to test; or the head resolves here and is a strict ancestor of, or diverged from, local HEAD), 2 UNRESOLVABLE (a head was reported but this worktree cannot answer for it - object not in reach, no readable local HEAD, or the ancestry check itself errored). The header states the full contract and the measured rationale, and states that neither caller may turn 2 into a terminal verdict. Resolution stays read-only and side-effect free: the helper never fetches to make an absent object appear. The helper remains the single owner of the rule - no second copy per consumer. 2. bin/fm-crew-state.sh, primary attribution path: a branch-name match whose head is UNRESOLVABLE and whose run makes no terminal claim is attributed as this worktree's live run (the expected pre-push state) instead of being rejected into the coarse fallback. The review gate tightened the terminal test: nm_run_claims_terminal treats EITHER a non-empty outcome OR a terminal status word (completed/failed/cancelled) as a terminal claim, so an unresolvable head can never be reported failed/done through the no-outcome mapping. 3. bin/fm-crew-state.sh, coarse fallback: the runs list is newest-first, so the FIRST row for the branch IS the branch's current run and any row below it can only be staler. The scan now binds that newest row and stops, accepting it on verdict 0, accepting it on verdict 2 only while it is still "running", and otherwise declining - never walking past it to let an older terminal row win. 4. bin/fm-teardown.sh: unchanged behavior, with an explicit comment recording the direction. Both non-zero verdicts (1 and 2) DECLINE to abort, so teardown never aborts a run it cannot positively attribute. That is the safe direction and it is preserved: the previous false "no match" already failed toward declining, and verdict 2 fails the same way. 5. Three-value discipline throughout: "cannot determine" is never coerced into PASS or FAIL - the same contract fm-verify enforces for check results, applied here to run attribution. TESTS. New tests/fm-nm-run-lib.test.sh (7 cases) pins all three verdicts directly, including the case no existing test covered: a run head genuinely absent from the worktree, reproduced faithfully by cloning the fixture origin into a separate gate clone, committing there, and asserting the sha is unreachable from the worktree - the real unpushed-pipeline-tip shape. tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh gains 4 reader tests, two of which reproduced the measured "state: failed / source: run-step / run failed" verbatim before the fix. tests/fm-teardown.test.sh gains a test that a parked run with an unresolvable head is never aborted. Every test was witnessed red against the pre-fix logic or a mutation before green. bin/fm-test-run.sh registers the new file in the pure-contract-unit family. Test fixtures pin every git call to the test temp root after an earlier draft's empty repo path ran destructive git against the real checkout; that lesson is recorded in the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill's repo style rules, with the bash mechanism corrected by the review gate. DOCS. docs/architecture.md's one-line description of the attribution boundary had become inaccurate, so it now describes the three-valued rule and the unknown-head behavior and points at bin/fm-nm-run-lib.sh as the owner. CONSTRAINTS HONORED. Upstream PR 1816 owns current-run SELECTION and is deliberately not touched or duplicated; note that 1816 does NOT fix this class, because it applies the same worktree-visibility test and therefore rejects the same live rows. bin/fm-crew-state.sh is concurrently being changed by another lane (structured --json mode), so the reader change is kept minimal and confined to the attribution/fallback path so an ordinary rebase can reconcile. KNOWN PRE-EXISTING FAILURE, NOT CAUSED BY THIS CHANGE: tests/fm-backend.test.sh fails at "not ok - old fm-teardown.sh (scout, report present) should succeed" with "fm-decision-hold: compatible tasks-axi is required". Verified via git stash to fail identically at the unmodified contribution base 345de4e7aad1 - it is an environment tooling requirement, unrelated to this change. tests/fm-nm-run-lib.test.sh, tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh, tests/fm-teardown.test.sh, and bin/fm-lint.sh all pass at this head. ## What Changed - `fm_nm_head_matches_worktree` in `bin/fm-nm-run-lib.sh` now returns a three-valued verdict — 0 match, 1 no match, 2 unresolvable — instead of collapsing "this worktree cannot resolve the run head" into "not mine". An unresolvable head is the routine mid-validation shape (no-mistakes commits fix rounds in its own gate clone and doesn't push until the push step), and the previous two-valued rule made the documented descendant case structurally unmatchable during every fix round. Resolution stays read-only: the helper never fetches to make an absent object appear. - `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` now attributes a branch-matched run with an unresolvable head as this worktree's live run whenever it makes no terminal claim (a new `nm_run_claims_terminal` guard treats either a non-empty outcome or a terminal status word as terminal, so verdict 2 can never surface as failed/done), and the coarse runs-list fallback binds only the newest row for the branch and stops — never walking past it to let an older finished run win, which is how a working lane got reported "state: failed / run failed". `bin/fm-teardown.sh` behavior is unchanged: both non-match verdicts still decline to abort, now with the direction documented, so teardown never kills a run it cannot positively attribute. - title: Use task branch prefix
body:
## Summary

- Give new Firstmate task branches a single naming owner in `bin/fm-branch-lib.sh`.
- Generate `ivannovak/dev-5579` for ticketed task ids and `ivannovak/dev-000-<task-id>` for unticketed work.
- Keep existing `fm/` branches readable for review, local merge, teardown, and fleet PR inventory; no existing branch or PR is renamed.
- Update branch-generation, promotion, parsing, reporting, tests, and maintained documentation together.

Ticketed descriptions are intentionally omitted. Adding them would require new backlog-title lookup machinery, so this keeps the correct smaller change requested; unticketed task ids already provide the description after `dev-000-`.

## Validation

- `bin/fm-lint.sh`
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`
- Focused six-test selection: 6 passed, 0 failed (`fm-branch`, `fm-brief`, `fm-review-diff`, `fm-bearings-snapshot`, `fm-tangle-guard`, `fm-task-delivery`).
- Single-owner mutation proof: temporarily changed `FM_BRANCH_PREFIX` to `throwaway/`; the unchanged consumer test failed with unpiped `UNPIPED_EXIT_CODE=1`, then the owner was restored to `ivannovak/`.
- Broad changed-file selection: 53 of 59 passed; six unrelated host/harness tests failed (`fm-calm-pi-extension`, `fm-kimi-harness`, `fm-muse-harness`, `fm-teardown` Herdr preflight, `fm-gotmp`, and `fm-backend-herdr-focus-flash-e2e`).

## CI status

CI did not run. This is a fork PR, and GitHub Actions requires the captain to approve workflow runs. An empty check set must not be interpreted as checks green.

title: feat: route pipeline PR creation through configured credentials
body:
## Intent Give firstmate a supported way to route the no-mistakes pipeline's PR-creation step through bin/fm-gh.sh, which holds the vault credential authorized for createPullRequest, instead of no-mistakes using its own gh path. Background: on 2026-08-06 no-mistakes autonomously created a clip-engine PR via its own gh invocation; repo, identity, and head were all correct so nothing needed undoing, but the pipeline's PR step cannot currently be intercepted once review has responded, and the configured default GitHub token lacks createPullRequest, so pipeline PR creation fails on most repos while bin/fm-gh.sh succeeds. The core constraint is PURE-KUN POSTURE: do NOT locally patch the installed no-mistakes tool, because we track Kun Chen's tools clean. First investigate what no-mistakes ALREADY supports by reading its installed docs, help, and config surface for any supported hook, wrapper, gh-binary override, PATH-based interception, or config knob that lets the PR step run through a caller-supplied command, and prefer any supported configuration over new code. If a supported seam exists, implement the firstmate-side wiring in this repo with tests. If NO supported seam exists, implement the best non-invasive firstmate-side mitigation available without forking no-mistakes (for example a PATH shim exposed only inside task worktrees IF that is robust and honest), AND write a concrete upstream proposal document at docs/proposals/nm-pr-step-interception.md describing the config seam we want upstream in kunchenguid's no-mistakes, precise enough to turn into an upstream PR. Investigation outcome that shaped this diff: no supported seam exists. Confirmed against the installed v1.41.2 binary and the upstream source at release 1.46.0, commit 20892e6. internal/scm/github executes gh by the bare name with no binary-path or credential parameter; neither the global config.yaml nor the per-repo .no-mistakes.yaml exposes a GitHub credential, a gh path, or a PR-step command override; Bitbucket Cloud by contrast reads NO_MISTAKES_BITBUCKET_EMAIL, NO_MISTAKES_BITBUCKET_API_TOKEN, and NO_MISTAKES_BITBUCKET_API_BASE_URL, an asymmetry the upstream proposal targets; and stepCmd in internal/pipeline/steps/common_exec.go already honors a step-scoped PATH and credential environment whenever StepContext.Env is populated, but internal/pipeline/pipeline.go declares that field as test-only and the production executor never sets it, so the mechanism exists while a supported way to configure it does not. A deliberate correction to the original task framing, made after reading the source: a worktree-scoped PATH shim is NOT possible. The PR step runs inside the no-mistakes daemon, whose environment is resolved once from a login-shell probe at startup, so nothing placed inside a task worktree is on the PATH that resolves gh. Any shim is therefore PATH-wide by construction. That limit is documented plainly rather than papered over, and the shim is consequently explicitly opt-in and never installed automatically. Deliberate decisions a reviewer reading only the diff would not know. The credential itself is kept out of tracked material and read from a gitignored config/gh-credential command prefix, so this shared template repo carries no machine-specific vault path and a home with no such file is a transparent pass-through that behaves exactly as before. The shim routes only `pr create` and `pr edit`, the two mutations a fine-grained token is forbidden from, and delegates every other invocation, including the pipeline's own `pr list` and `pr view` reads, straight to the real gh so the privileged credential is never spent on reads. Installation is a symlink rather than a copy because the shim locates fm-gh.sh relative to its own real path. No spawn or brief plumbing was added, and none is needed, because interception happens where the PR step actually runs, in the daemon, so one installation covers every pipeline run. The installer refuses to overwrite a non-symlink gh or remove a symlink it does not own, and reports PATH precedence because a shim the daemon never resolves is indistinguishable from no shim at all. The wrapper expands its credential prefix as ${PREFIX[@]+"${PREFIX[@]}"} rather than "${PREFIX[@]}" because under set -u, bash 3.2, the system bash macOS still ships, rejects an empty array's expansion as an unbound variable. That was a real bug found and fixed during this work: it broke the unconfigured pass-through path that every home without config/gh-credential takes, and it is pinned by a self-skipping legacy-shell regression. This task touches firstmate's shared tracked material, so the firstmate-coding-guidelines contract applies: one full sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash and never an em dash, shellcheck-clean bin scripts through bin/fm-lint.sh, colocated tests named .test.sh under tests/, every new prose surface classified in docs/documentation-audiences.json, and active empirical evidence recorded as a maintainer-verification record under docs/verification/. Acceptance criteria: the chosen mechanism is demonstrated working, by test or recorded evidence, for at least one simulated PR-step invocation routing through bin/fm-gh.sh; no local modification of the installed no-mistakes tool; and documentation states exactly which mechanism was chosen and why, and what remains for upstream. ## What Changed - Add `fm-gh.sh` to inject a locally configured PR-capable credential while preserving transparent pass-through behavior when unconfigured. - Add an opt-in, PATH-wide `gh` shim and safe installer that route only `pr create` and `pr edit`, delegate other commands, verify precedence, and protect foreign symlinks. - Document the no-mistakes limitation and proposed upstream credential seam, with regression and maintainer-verification coverage for the chosen routing mechanism. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the three prior defects are closed without introducing a new reachable failure path, and the change remains an explicit, well-documented containment with the durable fix deferred upstream. ## Testing Reviewed the target implementation and documentation, ran the focused behavioral suite, captured an end-to-end simulated PR-creation transcript, and confirmed testing left the target commit's worktree clean; all exercised behavior satisfied the intent.
Evidence: Simulated PR-step routing transcript ```text $ bin/fm-gh-shim-install.sh --install --dir installed: /gh -> /bin/fm-gh-shim.sh delegates to: $ bin/fm-gh-shim-install.sh --check --dir shim: installed at /gh real gh: first gh on evaluated PATH: /gh precedence: wins $ gh pr create --head feature --base main --repo example/project --title Routed --body-file - https://github.com/example/project/pull/42 Delegation record from the real gh boundary: delegated argv: gh pr create --head feature --base main --repo example/project --title Routed --body-file - delegated GH_TOKEN: delegated GITHUB_TOKEN: ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 3 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-gh-shim-install.sh:108` - Refuse foreign symlinks before `ln -sf`. The current guard permits any existing symlink, so installation can silently replace a package-manager or user-owned `gh` link and cannot restore it on uninstall. Allow only an absent target or a link already owned by this installer. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-gh.sh:18` - Use `GH_TOKEN` in the supported credential prefix or explicitly clear it. `gh` prioritizes `GH_TOKEN` over `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so a daemon carrying a forbidden `GH_TOKEN` will ignore the documented injected `GITHUB_TOKEN` and still fail at `pr create`. Add a regression with a bad ambient `GH_TOKEN`. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-gh.sh:41` - Trim whitespace before classifying comments. A line such as ` # explanation` is currently returned as the prefix and makes the wrapper attempt to execute `#`, despite the documented first-non-comment-line contract. 🔧 Fix: Harden PR credential routing and shim ownership ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-gh-shim.test.sh` - `bash /var/folders/pj/3vh4dgp11qs_j186lws96lmw0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZCZSKGXZP5CNWSWX2CBZGVN/pr-routing-evidence.sh` - `git status --short` confirmed the worktree remained clean after testing
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix: move network checks off the session-start blocking path
body:
## Intent Re-land the network-free session-start change cleanly on current main. It previously shipped green as PR #1845 but was cut from a pre-#1842 base and can no longer merge cleanly, so this is a fresh branch off current origin/main with the #1845 work re-applied and every conflict resolved. The old branch was deliberately NOT force-pushed, to avoid an AXI custody deadlock with its still-active run; #1845 gets closed as superseded once this lands. What the change delivers (preserve this intent fully): session start prints its digest from local state alone, with zero synchronous external-network call on the blocking path. Every network check a session start owes - GitHub auth, dead-secondmate relaunch, secondmate convergence, pending handoff delivery, and project clone refresh - still RUNS with its safety guarantees intact, but concurrently in a bounded detached worker owned by the new bin/fm-startup-network.sh, reported in the digest's own NETWORK CHECKS section. bin/fm-bootstrap.sh remains the single owner of every sweep; the new FM_BOOTSTRAP_NETWORK phase split ('skip'/'only') is a partition of the unsplit run and changes only WHEN each sweep runs, never WHETHER. Unrecognized values fall back to 'all' on purpose so a typo can never silently skip a safety sweep. The duplicate tasks-axi compatibility probe is collapsed so the verdict is computed once (10 tasks-axi invocations per startup become 7). Captain-accepted design decision on the deferred-report race, already settled and deliberate: suppress the deferred sweep wake ONLY after a durable harvest acknowledgement. No per-generation bookkeeping - next-session re-derivation covers the overwrite case, because these sweeps are idempotent detectors. Do not flag the absence of per-generation bookkeeping as a gap; it was chosen. Conflict resolution decisions made here, all deliberate: - AGENTS.md section 3: the digest's step list is renumbered to state emission order directly (supervision block and its read-once contract, fleet state, network checks, then context). This preserves #1826's fleet-state-BEFORE-context ordering and its 'last of the bulk sections' and read-once-contract wording, while adding the new NETWORK CHECKS step. #1842's --resolve-key answerer-closes lines in section 7 are untouched and verified present. - tests/fm-backend.test.sh: resolved to main's version from #1851. The #1845 branch had widened the old-bin shim with 'cp -R' to stop a hand-maintained sibling list from omitting the new bin/ script; main's git-archive-of-the-whole-historical-bin-tree already subsumes that reason entirely, so main's is strictly better and the branch's variant is dropped on purpose. - #1846 turned out NOT to touch bin/fm-bootstrap.sh at all (it changed bin/fm-procevent-remote-reply.sh, which this branch never touches), so its remote status-stream mirror is preserved untouched. Its arming call from the secondmate_sync sweep simply now happens in the deferred stage: the mirror behavior AND the off-blocking-path deferral both hold. Empirical verification done on this base, recorded in docs/verification/supervision.md: against a fixture home with one remote secondmate whose host hangs 25s per SSH connection, session start went from 1m21.15s with 3 blocking SSH attempts (default-branch tip 8398d31) to 3.36s, and the deferred worker's published report came back byte-identical to the three sweep lines the blocking baseline printed, with the unreachable route preserved in both and the result surfacing as a queued 'check: startup-network' wake. That doc's latency record was re-measured against the current tip rather than left citing the now-historical 345de4e. This is firstmate shared, tracked startup/supervision infrastructure, held to the highest bar: deterministic and idempotent enforcement, the one-owner rule for contracts, behavioral tests through the executable interface only, one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never em dash, and bin/fm-lint.sh clean. ## What Changed - Render the session-start digest entirely from local state while GitHub auth, secondmate maintenance, pending handoffs, and project refreshes run concurrently in a bounded detached worker. - Split bootstrap into guarded local and network phases without changing sweep ownership or allowing unknown phase values to skip safety checks. - Surface deferred results through a durable `NETWORK CHECKS` report and completion wake, while reusing the tasks-axi compatibility verdict to eliminate duplicate probes. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The deferred-worker design is well-bounded, preserves the bootstrap phase partition and lock-safety invariants, and the fix round correctly prevents failed report publication from being acknowledged as successful. ## Testing After diff-based scoping, the focused bootstrap, session-start, and deferred-worker suites passed; an initial load-sensitive acknowledgement-test failure was stabilized and rerun successfully, while a public CLI fixture demonstrated immediate startup return, all five checks reported as pending, completed deferred results, and durable wake delivery.
Evidence: Deferred startup network CLI transcript ```text $ fm-startup-network.sh start --locked 1 --harvest-pid start returned in 0s while the simulated network sweep continues for 6s $ fm-startup-network.sh report IN PROGRESS - the deferred network checks have not finished yet. NOT yet confirmed: GitHub authentication, dead-secondmate relaunch, secondmate convergence, pending handoff delivery, and project clone refresh with its drift reporting. Started 0s ago, bounded at 120s. The result is durable in state/.startup-network.report and arrives as a `check: startup-network` wake. Read it now with /var/folders/0k/bf8mwt2n5qddzk24r20gfk0c0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZD0R6Q631YMPE0FVDBHEDE1/fixture/root/bin/fm-startup-network.sh report; until it lands, treat none of it as confirmed. $ fm-startup-network.sh report completed off the startup path in 6s: GitHub authentication, dead-secondmate relaunch, secondmate convergence, pending handoff delivery, and project clone refresh with its drift reporting. NEEDS_GH_AUTH: GitHub authentication needs attention SECONDMATE_LIVENESS: unreachable route preserved; relaunch safely refused FLEET_SYNC: secondmate convergence completed HANDOFF_DELIVERY: pending handoff delivery completed PROJECT_REFRESH: project clone refresh completed These ran AFTER the sections above were composed, so re-read any record a line here names. $ persisted wake queue check startup-network check: startup-network: deferred startup network checks finished (done); read them with /var/folders/0k/bf8mwt2n5qddzk24r20gfk0c0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZD0R6Q631YMPE0FVDBHEDE1/fixture/root/bin/fm-startup-network.sh report ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-startup-network.sh:333` - The required guarantee says every deferred check remains "reported ... with its safety guarantees intact," but this hunk ignores failure to replace `.startup-network.report` and still publishes the generation as `done`. If that atomic write fails, harvest can acknowledge an absent or previous generation's report as the current completed result, silently losing or misreporting findings. Publish a failed state with an explicit `NETWORK_CHECKS` diagnostic instead of completing when the report write fails. 🔧 Fix: Fail deferred startup when report publication fails ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `git diff --stat 8398d3109b8d153d86081bb358eea00a13a8ff1c..b343fc2272bcd7fc8ebdb5f0b852b99050062a99` and changed-file inspection - `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` - `tests/fm-session-start.test.sh` - `tests/fm-startup-network.test.sh` before and after the test-only timing stabilization - `/var/folders/0k/bf8mwt2n5qddzk24r20gfk0c0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZD0R6Q631YMPE0FVDBHEDE1/fixture/run-evidence.sh`
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: Add latent PR worker hibernation lifecycle
body:
## Summary

- add crash-safe latent worker hibernation for exact authenticated GitHub PR heads
- preserve recoverable commits under protected local refs while releasing worker processes and temporary Treehouse slots
- add resume, attention, startup recovery, merge finalization, visibility, and project-removal safeguards
- use durable `pr_ready_head`/`pr_head` identity rather than status-log pause tails for eligibility
- keep GitLab and tasks with dirty/divergent work, open decisions, validation, or pending obligations active
- reconcile the branch with main's deferred session-start network stage (#1860, #1918)

## Reconciliation with main

This branch and `main` both restructured how session start sequences its work, so the merge was a composition decision rather than a hunk-by-hunk pick.

`main` split `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` into a local pass and a network-only pass (`FM_BOOTSTRAP_NETWORK=skip|only`), moved four network sweeps into the detached bounded worker owned by `bin/fm-startup-network.sh`, and reports them in the digest's own `NETWORK CHECKS` section. This branch added an additional mutating sweep - latent transaction recovery - written against the pre-deferral ordering, where that local/network split did not exist.

Picking either side would have destroyed the other: taking the branch's shape puts the network back on the blocking path, which is the exact regression #1860 fixed; taking main's shape leaves the hibernation sweep attached to a stage that no longer runs, so the lifecycle would look installed while being inert.

### Where the hibernation lifecycle belongs, and why

The lifecycle splits cleanly along the same seam main introduced, because its two session-start-relevant halves have different network characters.

**`recover-all` (crash recovery) runs on the LOCAL pass, inside main's `local_phase` guard.** `latent_recover_one` reconciles an interrupted hibernation transaction against `git rev-parse` on the local clone, the local metadata hash, and the local manifest. It makes no external-network call, so deferring it would buy no startup latency. It would also cost correctness: the deferred stage is bounded at 120s and routinely still `IN PROGRESS` when the digest is composed, so a half-applied transaction would remain unreconciled underneath the very `FLEET STATE` section that reports that task's endpoint. It is placed alongside the PR-check migration and the startup-memory budget, and it is gated by `FM_BOOTSTRAP_DETECT_ONLY` exactly as they are, so a lock-refused read-only session never touches it.

**`enter` (hibernation itself) stays off the session-start path entirely.** This is the network half - `latent_fetch_exact_head` fetches the exact PR object and the authenticated canonical poll must be valid before a worker is released. It is event-driven and always has been: `bin/fm-pr-check.sh` drives it when a PR is registered, and `bin/fm-watch.sh` drives it from the supervision poll. Neither is on the blocking startup path, so no part of hibernation needed to move into the deferred stage. Session start therefore still makes no blocking external-network call.

The loop in bootstrap only probes for a transaction journal, so a home with no interrupted hibernation pays a single failed glob.

### Documentation

The sweep count was six on main and seven on the branch, and the two lists disagreed. It is now seven in all three places that state it - `AGENTS.md` section 3, `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh`'s header, and `bin/fm-session-start.sh`'s ordering comment - with main's "the four network ones among them run in the deferred stage" clause preserved, which stays accurate because latent recovery is local. The `bootstrap-diagnostics` trigger list is the union of both sides (`NETWORK_CHECKS:` from main, `LATENT_RECOVERY:` from this branch) in both `AGENTS.md` and the skill's own front matter.

## Verification

Run against the merged tree in an isolated scratch `FM_HOME`, not read off the diff.

### 1. Composed ordering, with both stages present

`bin/fm-session-start.sh` emits main's nine-stage ordering intact:

```
LOCK → BOOTSTRAP → WAKE QUEUE → (supervision block) → FLEET STATE → NETWORK CHECKS → CONTEXT → NEXT STEP
```

With a latent transaction journal planted at `data/fm-hib-probe/latent/transaction`, the hibernation sweep reports inside the blocking `BOOTSTRAP` section:

```
LATENT_RECOVERY: quarantined fm-hib-probe
```

and the network stage reports separately, off the blocking path:

```
NETWORK CHECKS
completed off the startup path in 1s: GitHub authentication, dead-secondmate relaunch,
secondmate convergence, pending handoff delivery, and project clone refresh with its drift reporting.
```

### 2. Watching it fail

The sweep's wiring was broken deliberately and session start re-run each time.

| Wiring | `LATENT_RECOVERY` in digest |
| --- | --- |
| intact (as merged) | present |
| sweep removed | **absent** |
| sweep moved to the deferred network phase | **absent from the entire digest** |
| restored | present |

The second break is the more instructive one. Moved to the deferred phase the sweep is not merely delayed - the digest completes with `NETWORK CHECKS` still `IN PROGRESS - ... Started 2s ago, bounded at 120s`, so the recovery result is unavailable at the moment the digest reports that task's endpoint. That is the "installed but inert" failure this placement avoids.

Phase gating was then checked directly against `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh`:

| Pass | Sweep runs? | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FM_BOOTSTRAP_DETECT_ONLY=1` (lock-refused read-only) | no | no |
| `FM_BOOTSTRAP_NETWORK=skip` (locked local, blocking path) | yes | yes |
| `FM_BOOTSTRAP_NETWORK=only` (deferred worker) | no | no - must not repeat |

An earlier version of this check used `FM_BOOTSTRAP_NETWORK_PHASE`, which is the internal normalized variable rather than the input `FM_BOOTSTRAP_NETWORK`. It silently fell back to the complete run and appeared to show the sweep repeating on the deferred pass. The instrument was wrong, not the code; the table above is from the corrected run.

### 3. The network deferral survives

A project clone was pointed at an unroutable origin (`https://10.255.255.1/`) so the fleet-sync fetch would hang, then session start was timed:

- session start returned in **2s**, exit 0
- the deferred worker took **21s**, of which `phase fleet-sync ... elapsed=20000` ms was the hung fetch
- the digest printed `IN PROGRESS`, named each unconfirmed check, and never reported one as passed

The 20s of blocked network never touched the blocking path, and the hibernation sweep still reported on it in the same run.

### 4. Hibernated-task visibility in the composed digest

A `tier=latent` task with no window or worktree is reported as released rather than misread as broken:

```
endpoint: released (state: quarantined · source: latent-manifest · latent recovery integrity failed)
```

Without this branch's `fm-session-start.sh` case that line reads `endpoint: unknown (no window recorded)`.

### 5. Regression test

`tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` gains `test_latent_recovery_sweep_runs_on_the_local_half`, which pins the sweep to the local half, asserts the network half does not repeat it, and asserts a detect-only session does not run it. Each of its three assertions was watched failing before it landed, with unpiped exit 1:

- sweep removed → `not ok - the local half did not run latent transaction recovery`
- sweep moved outside both guards → `not ok - the deferred network half repeated latent transaction recovery`
- only the detect-only guard dropped → `not ok - a detect-only session ran latent transaction recovery`

Restored, it returns `ok - bootstrap: latent transaction recovery runs on the local half only` with exit 0.

## Safety boundaries preserved

- **Lock-refused read-only sessions** run no mutating sweep, hibernation recovery included (verified above).
- **Sweeps only when this session holds the lock** - the latent sweep sits inside the same `FM_BOOTSTRAP_DETECT_ONLY` guard as the other local sweeps.
- **Hibernation is not teardown** - `bin/fm-latent.sh`'s header keeps that statement, `finish` `exec`s into `bin/fm-teardown.sh`, and teardown still requires the forge's exact merged head to contain the saved generation before deleting the ref.
- **Exact-PR-head verification before releasing a worker** - `latent_enter` still proves PR identity, ancestry, cleanliness, obligations, validation, endpoint, and recovery-ref state twice, before and after backend termination.
- **No force or discard bypass** anywhere in the lifecycle.

## Local evidence

- `bin/fm-lint.sh` passed, ShellCheck 0.11.0 (pinned 0.11.0), exit 0, including a `CI=true` full-parity run over the complete file set
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` passed: `ok surfaces=65 local_links=216`
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` passed: `FM_TEST_COVERAGE ok total=133 parallel=24 serial=98 serial_shards=4 herdr=11`
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --all`, verbatim: `FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=133 failed=10 skipped_gate=15 duration_ms=3861068`, exit 1

Every test that covers this merge passed on the merged tree:

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/fm-latent.test.sh` (whole hibernation lifecycle) | `exit=0` |
| `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` (incl. the new placement test) | `exit=0` |
| `tests/fm-session-start.test.sh` | `exit=0` |
| `tests/fm-startup-network.test.sh` | `exit=0` |
| `tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` (latent-tier reconciliation) | `exit=0` |

Nine of the ten failures were reproduced on clean `main` (833a9a2) and are pre-existing in this
environment - missing or wrong-version external dependencies (Orca, Pi, Kimi, Muse, Herdr 0.7.5
against a documented 0.8.0 floor, and remote SSH):

`fm-backend-orca`, `fm-calm-pi-extension`, `fm-gotmp`, `fm-kimi-harness`, `fm-muse-harness`,
`fm-remote-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e`, `fm-remote-secondmate-trace-context`,
`fm-backend-herdr-focus-flash-e2e`, `fm-backend-herdr-presentation-e2e`.

The tenth was a real defect in the hibernation commit; it is described and FIXED below, so the teardown suite is now green.

## Exit-status defect found in the hibernation commit, and fixed here

`tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` case `herdr-preflight-missing-adapter` fails differently before and
after the hibernation commit, and the difference is a genuine behavioural regression that this
merge only carries forward. It is reported here rather than silently repaired, because fixing it
changes the feature rather than the merge.

Bisected in one clone under identical untangled git conditions, so the only variable is the code:

| Commit | `bin/fm-latent.sh` | teardown exit | assertion reached |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `8398d31` merge base | absent | **1** | fails later, on the stderr-wording assertion |
| `833a9a2` current main | absent | **1** | fails later, on the stderr-wording assertion |
| `c150076` hibernation commit | present | **0** | fails earlier: "teardown continued without its required preflight" |
| `2583e05` this merge | present | **0** | same as `c150076` |

The later stderr-wording failure is pre-existing in this environment on every commit above.
The `1 -> 0` exit-status change is introduced exactly by `c150076`.

Mechanism, isolated to one line and then reduced to a minimal reproduction. Disabling only
`trap teardown_lifecycle_lock_release EXIT` at `c150076` restores `exit 1`, with the
`unresolvable-lock` mode unchanged at `exit 1` in both:

| c150076 | `missing-adapter` | `unresolvable-lock` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| with the trap | **0** | 1 |
| trap disabled | 1 | 1 |

The cause is not the handler's body. Under `set -e`, a `source` of a MISSING file is a fatal shell
abort, and that abort reaches an EXIT trap with `$?` **already 0**:

```
set -eu; cleanup() { echo "STATUS-INSIDE-TRAP=$?"; }; trap cleanup EXIT; . /nonexistent/adapter.sh
  -> STATUS-INSIDE-TRAP=0, script exits 0
same script with no trap installed
  -> script exits 1
```

So merely installing an EXIT trap converts this fatal abort from `exit 1` into `exit 0`, whatever the
handler does. Ordinary `exit 1` refusals are unaffected: they arrive at the trap with `$?`=1 and exit 1.

Severity: teardown still **refuses correctly and destroys nothing**. Probed directly at the point of
refusal on the merged tree: `worktree_exists=YES branch=fm/task-x1 meta=YES status=YES`. The defect
is that the refusal is invisible to the caller - a refusal that reports success. That matters because
`AGENTS.md` treats a teardown refusal as a stop-and-investigate result, and `fm-latent.sh finish`
`exec`s into `fm-teardown.sh` and would read the masked status.

### Reachable beyond teardown refusal

The hibernation commit adds **two** whole-script EXIT traps: `fm-teardown.sh:190` and
`fm-latent.sh:78`. Both scripts run under `set -eu`, and both reach `fm-backend.sh`'s LAZY adapter
source (`fm-backend.sh:609`) after their trap is installed, so both can hit the fatal-abort class:

- `bin/fm-teardown.sh` - proven end to end by the repository's own test (`missing-adapter`, `rc=0`).
- `bin/fm-latent.sh` - `fm-latent.sh:503` (`fm_backend_source herdr`) sits on the `enter` path, after
  the trap. Reproduced against the REAL `bin/fm-backend.sh` with `bin/backends/herdr.sh` removed:
  the script's own construct exits **0** with the trap and **1** without it.

That second one is the more consequential consumer, because `bin/fm-watch.sh:723` BRANCHES on the
status (`if fm-latent.sh enter "$id" ...; then`), so a fatal missing-adapter failure would be read as
a successful hibernation. `bin/fm-pr-check.sh:134` calls `enter` with `|| true` and is unaffected
either way.

Scope is bounded, and deliberately verified rather than assumed: this affects ONLY the
fatal-source-abort class. Ordinary safety refusals - dirty worktree, unlanded work, latent integrity,
lock contention - use explicit `exit 1` (46 sites in teardown) and still exit non-zero with the trap
installed, as the `unresolvable-lock` column above shows.

No handler-side rescue of `$?` works, because the status is gone before the handler runs: `return $rc`,
`exit $rc`, and a bare `:` handler all still produce `exit 0`.

### The fix

The only evidence that survives a fatal abort is that the script never reached a completion point, so
each script now marks its legitimate terminations and its handler treats a `$?=0` arrival WITHOUT
that mark as an abort, exiting 1. The lock-release work the traps exist for is unchanged, and
ordinary refusals are untouched - they carry their own non-zero `$?` straight through.

Teardown's abort message is conditional on whether teardown had begun changing the task, so it can
never claim "nothing was changed" once something might have been. That flag is set EARLY, at the
point teardown commits to its destructive phase: an over-eager flag only makes the message more
conservative, while a late one would let it overclaim.

### Watched failing first, on the real scripts

Both captured unpiped, before and after, driving the real code rather than a synthetic shape:

| Script | Trigger | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bin/fm-latent.sh` | real `enter` path, lazily sourced adapter removed | **rc=0** - `not ok - fm-latent.sh enter reported success (rc=0) after a fatal abort` (suite exit 1) | **rc!=0** - `ok - fm-latent.sh preserves a non-zero exit status through its EXIT trap on a fatal abort` (suite exit 0) |
| `bin/fm-teardown.sh` | repo's own `herdr-preflight-missing-adapter` case | **rc=0** - `not ok - ... teardown continued without its required preflight` (suite exit 1) | **rc!=0** - suite exit 0, 57 assertions passing, 0 failures |

The new `tests/fm-latent.test.sh` case asserts the abort ACTUALLY fired (`grep -q "No such file or
directory"`) before asserting the status, so it cannot pass vacuously if the fixture stops triggering
the abort.

### Suite result after the fix, by CI lane

The monolithic `--all` run was repeatedly killed by the environment partway through, so the suite was
re-run as the six lanes CI actually composes. Every summary line is verbatim:

| Lane | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `portable-parallel-1` | `FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=11 failed=0 skipped_gate=0` |
| `portable-parallel-2` | `FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=13 failed=0 skipped_gate=0` |
| `portable-serial-1of4` | `FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=21 failed=0 skipped_gate=2` |
| `portable-serial-2of4` | `FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=26 failed=4 skipped_gate=3` |
| `portable-serial-3of4` | `FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=25 failed=2 skipped_gate=5` |
| `portable-serial-4of4` | `FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=26 failed=2 skipped_gate=5` |

122 tests, 8 failures, and all 8 are the SAME pre-existing environment failures baselined against
clean `main` earlier: `fm-calm-pi-extension`, `fm-remote-secondmate-trace-context`,
`fm-remote-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e`, `fm-muse-harness`, `fm-kimi-harness`, `fm-backend-orca`,
`fm-gotmp`, and `fm-backend-herdr-focus-flash-e2e`.

Against the pre-fix `--all` run (`total=133 failed=10`) the delta is exactly one failure REMOVED -
the teardown preflight case this commit fixes - and nothing added. `grep` for
"continued without its required preflight" across every lane log returns 0 occurrences. The
remaining `real-herdr-gated` lane is opt-in and needs Herdr >= 0.8.0; this host has 0.7.5.

Regression check that the fix does not invent failures: `fm-gotmp` still fails exactly as it does on
clean `main`, and its output contains none of the new abort messages, so that pre-existing failure is
untouched. `fm-bootstrap` + `fm-crew-state` (78 assertions) and `fm-session-start` +
`fm-startup-network` (59 assertions) are green, `bin/fm-lint.sh` passes at CI parity, and the
coverage guard reports `total=133`.

## CI

title: fix(bin): resolve harness ancestry on Windows/Cygwin sessions
body:
## Summary

- `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh`'s ancestry walk relies on `ps -o comm=/args=/ppid=`, which Git for Windows' bundled Cygwin `ps` does not support at all (only `-aefls/-p/-u/-W`). Every call failed outright, so `fm-lock.sh` reported `cannot locate harness process in ancestry` on every Windows session and the session could never acquire its lock. `/proc/<pid>/{exename,cmdline,ppid}` is read as a same-host fallback only when `ps -o` produced nothing, which keeps Linux/macOS behavior unchanged (they never hit that branch).
- Fixing that alone was not enough: Cygwin/MSYS2 report a process's parent as the synthetic orphan pid 1 the moment the real parent was never spawned through their own pid database - true for every `bash.exe` a native `claude.exe` launches, since each Bash-tool invocation is a fresh, otherwise-unrelated subprocess. The real ancestry still exists at the Windows OS level, so the walk now continues through the real Windows process table (`Win32_Process` via `powershell.exe`) once the POSIX-visible chain dead-ends without a harness match, and `fm_harness_pid_alive` gained the matching Windows-native liveness check for a pid recorded that way.

Verified live in the environment that surfaced the bug: `fm_harness_ancestry_pid` now resolves to the real `claude.exe` process, and `fm_harness_pid_alive`/`fm_harness_winpid_alive` correctly confirm it live.

## Known pre-existing gap (not introduced by this change)

`tests/fm-session-lock-ancestry.test.sh`'s e2e cases and `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh` also fail in this same Windows/Cygwin environment on unmodified `main` - their own fixtures poll `ps -o ppid=` to detect when a process has been orphaned, which is the identical incompatibility this PR fixes in the library itself. I left the test fixtures alone to keep this change scoped to the reported bug; a follow-up should teach those fixtures the same `/proc` fallback.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/fm-session-lock-ancestry.test.sh` unit-layer cases (fake-`ps` driven) pass unchanged.
- [x] Live-verified in a real Windows/Git-Bash/Cygwin session: `fm_harness_ancestry_pid` resolves the real harness process; `fm_harness_pid_alive` confirms liveness.
- [ ] `shellcheck` could not be run locally (not installed in this environment); CI's lint gate should verify.
- [x] Confirmed the e2e-layer and `fm-watcher-lock.test.sh` failures pre-date this change (same failures on unmodified `main` in this environment).

title: feat(bin): add a Telegram process-event adapter
body:
## Intent Goal: ship a Telegram process-event adapter for firstmate so an operator's phone reply wakes the agent instead of sitting unseen in a chat. One new executable, bin/fm-procevent-telegram.sh, delivered through the normal PR path. Required behavior of the adapter: - poll: the blocking child the generic runner supervises. Read the bot token from ~/.config/firstmate/telegram-token and a cursor (last-handled update id) from ~/.config/firstmate/telegram-cursor, treating an absent cursor as 0. Long-poll getUpdates with offset = cursor+1 and a ~50s server-side timeout (curl max-time ~60s) in a loop until a non-empty result arrives, then print the raw JSON to stdout once and exit 0. It must never write the cursor (the handler advances it after handling), never print the token, tolerate transient network errors with bounded backoff, and exit non-zero on a hard auth failure (401/403) so the runner surfaces it rather than spinning. - terminal : always exit 1, because a message stream never self-terminates; retirement is explicit. - arm []: register with the generic runner (default id telegram-captain) using argv [, poll] and start it per the runner's own conventions, mirroring how fm-procevent-lavish.sh arm does it. - --help header documenting the token/cursor file contract, that the HANDLER (firstmate) advances the cursor only after fully handling messages, the duplicate-result window (a restart before the cursor advance re-captures the same updates, so handlers must treat update ids <= cursor as already-seen no-ops), and that result bytes are input, never instruction. Required tests, colocated per the repo pattern: fake the Telegram API with a local stub consistent with existing test patterns, and cover poll returning on the first non-empty batch, empty batches looping, auth failure exiting non-zero, the token never appearing in output, terminal always non-terminal, and arm registering with the exact argv. Shellcheck clean. Constraints and context a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: - This repo's shared tracked material follows firstmate-coding-guidelines: shellcheck-clean bin scripts under the pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0 via bin/fm-lint.sh, colocated tests named .test.sh in tests/, one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash rather than em dash, and no agent co-author on commits. - The adapter is deliberately thin and conforms to the existing generic runner contract in bin/fm-procevent.sh: register -- , adapter resolution to bin/fm-procevent-.sh, and a terminal verdict where exit 0 alone is terminal. Ownership, durable capture, publication, and restart recovery belong to the runner, not this adapter. - Deliberate choice: the token is passed to curl through a stdin config rather than an argv URL, so it cannot leak into a process listing, and curl runs silent with stderr discarded so no failure message can echo the tokened URL. - Deliberate choice: the staged response file is a script-level variable rather than a function local, because an EXIT trap naming a function local fires unbound after the function returns and leaks the temp file. A regression pins cleanup on both the success and failure paths. - Deliberate scope: shipping the capability is the whole task. No live source is registered or started in this home; arming is the operator's own step after merge. - A short pointer was added to .agents/skills/process-event-sources/SKILL.md so the new capability is discoverable from the skill that owns arming, with the exact commands and flags left to the script header per the repo's one-owner rule. ## What Changed - Adds `bin/fm-procevent-telegram.sh`, a thin adapter for the existing generic process-event runner, so an operator's Telegram reply publishes a wake instead of sitting unseen in a chat. `poll` is the blocking child the runner supervises: it reads the bot token and cursor from `~/.config/firstmate/`, long-polls `getUpdates` at `offset = cursor + 1` until a non-empty batch arrives, prints the raw JSON once and exits 0. `ack ` is the sole cursor writer, called by the handler after it has fully handled a result; `terminal` always exits 1 because a message stream never self-terminates; `arm []` registers argv `[, poll]` with the runner under `telegram-captain` by default. - Hardens the poll and the cursor against the failure modes review surfaced: the token goes to curl through a stdin config (never argv, never stdout, stderr discarded), 401/403 and 409 exit non-zero so the runner surfaces the blocker rather than spinning, 429 honors the server's `retry_after` bounded by `FM_TELEGRAM_MAX_BACKOFF_SECONDS`, the batch is capped so a published result stays under the runner's output limit and parseable, the staged response file is cleaned on the success, failure and process-group SIGTERM paths, and `ack` does its compare-and-commit under the shared lock helper so concurrent acks cannot rewind the cursor. - Documents the capability where it is discoverable: a pointer plus the ack-before-`handled` ordering rule in `.agents/skills/process-event-sources/SKILL.md`, the three `FM_TELEGRAM_*` knobs in `docs/configuration.md`, and a `docs/scripts.md` row - with exact commands left to the script header per the one-owner rule. New colocated suite `tests/fm-procevent-telegram.test.sh` fakes the Bot API and covers first non-empty batch, empty-batch looping, auth/conflict exits, retry_after clamping, token absence from output, temp-file cleanup, ack idempotence and serialization, non-terminal `terminal`, and the exact `arm` argv (24/24 assertions pass; shellcheck clean). Note: the branch also carries `19e4f28` (AGENTS.md layout-tree trim and the PR-body signature check in `.github/workflows/no-mistakes-required.yml`), unrelated local-main work that is in this delta because it was never pushed to `origin/main`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Both round-3 findings were fixed exactly as directed - a behavior-preserving teardown consolidation in cmd_ack that keeps the lock-before-output ordering and EXIT-trap coverage of the die paths, plus a documentation reordering with its rationale - leaving the branch with no substantiable defects on a capability nothing in this home arms. ## Testing I ran the colocated suite `tests/fm-procevent-telegram.test.sh` through `bin/fm-test-run.sh` (24/24 assertions pass, including the process-group-stop temp-file regression and the concurrent-ack serialization loop) and confirmed via `--check-coverage` that the new file is classified rather than orphaned. Because passing assertions alone do not show an operator's phone reply waking the agent, I also built and ran a full end-to-end walkthrough that drives the real generic runner against a fake Telegram Bot API which honours the offset it is given and genuinely blocks for the server-side timeout: the poll sits blocking on a silent chat at offset=1, the operator's reply arrives mid-poll, and it lands as a durable captured result plus exactly one normalized wake; the handler then acks 901 and marks the wake handled, and the restarted poll asks for offset=902 so the acknowledged message is never re-delivered. The transcript also shows the documented duplicate-result window on an unacked restart, a repeat ack reporting `already-acked`, `terminal` exiting 1 so the source stays armed, a rejected token failing after exactly one API call instead of spinning, and explicit retirement ending the source. The bot token reached curl six times over the stdin config and appears zero times in the transcript. This change is a bash CLI adapter with no rendered surface, so the reviewer-visible evidence is the CLI transcript rather than a screenshot. Everything passed, the worktree is clean, and all scratch directories were removed.
Evidence: Operator end-to-end transcript (arm -> phone reply -> captured result + wake -> ack -> no re-delivery -> retire) == 4. The runner supervises the blocking poll; the chat is silent so far poll is still blocking after 5s with an empty chat; getUpdates offsets asked for so far: offset=1 == 5. The operator replies from their phone operator sent: "ship it - merge the PR" (update 901) [runner exit 0] == 6. An acknowledged message is never re-captured the restarted poll now asks Telegram for: offset=902 update 901 is still queued at the fake server but sits below that offset, so it is not re-delivered. operator sends a second reply (update 902) --- newest captured result --- {"ok":true,"result":[{"update_id":902,"message":{"chat":{"first_name":"Nathan"},"text":"actually hold off, CI is red"}}]} == 10. The token reached the API but never any output above token bytes delivered to curl over the stdin config: 6 (token occurrences in this entire transcript: 0) ```text == 1. The contract an operator reads before arming $ /home/nathan/.no-mistakes/worktrees/8d4bd6329c9b/01KZCV73CWGPQ6FW5C7T0TVACJ/bin/fm-procevent-telegram.sh --help Telegram adapter for the generic process-to-event runner: a phone reply from the operator wakes firstmate instead of sitting unseen in a chat. Usage: fm-procevent-telegram.sh arm [] fm-procevent-telegram.sh poll fm-procevent-telegram.sh ack fm-procevent-telegram.sh terminal arm Register this adapter's blocking poll with the generic runner under (default: telegram-captain). Registration is the whole arming step: the runner's own reconcile cycle starts and supervises the poll, exactly as with every other registered source. poll The blocking child the runner supervises. It long-polls the Telegram Bot API getUpdates method (offset = cursor + 1, server-side timeout FM_TELEGRAM_POLL_TIMEOUT, default 50s) until a non-empty batch of updates arrives, prints that raw JSON response to stdout once, and exits 0. The batch is capped so even a worst-case response stays well under the runner's captured-output limit and is published as parseable JSON; updates beyond the cap stay queued at Telegram and arrive on the next poll. Transient network and server errors retry with bounded backoff (FM_TELEGRAM_BACKOFF_SECONDS, default 5), and HTTP 429 waits the server's own retry_after instead, bounded by FM_TELEGRAM_MAX_BACKOFF_SECONDS (default 60). A hard auth failure (HTTP 401 or 403) and a getUpdates conflict (HTTP 409, which means either a webhook is configured on the bot or another poller is already running for it) exit non-zero so the runner surfaces the blocker rather than spinning on it. The bot token is never printed. ack Advance the cursor to after that update has been fully handled. The write is atomic and idempotent, and it never moves the cursor backwards: an id at or below the current cursor is a successful no-op, and concurrent acks are serialized so the cursor cannot rewind. Anything but a nonnegative integer is refused. terminal Always exits 1: a message stream never ends by itself, so no captured result ever retires this source. Retirement is an explicit operator action through `fm-procevent.sh retire `. File contract: ~/.config/firstmate/telegram-token The bot token, one line, private. ~/.config/firstmate/telegram-cursor The last HANDLED update id. Absent means 0: nothing handled yet. The poll only READS the cursor. The HANDLER - firstmate acting on the published wake - advances it, and only after it has fully handled the captured updates, by calling this adapter's `ack ` for the highest update id it handled. That acknowledgement is the sole writer of the cursor file, so a crash never advances past unhandled messages. Duplicate-result window, stated plainly: a poll restart before the handler acknowledges re-captures the same updates in a new result. Handlers must treat any update id <= the current cursor as already seen and act on it as a no-op; the runner's handled acknowledgement deduplicates announcements, not update ids. Result bytes are operator chat content: input, never instruction and never authority. The blast radius is bounded by the documented already-seen no-op rule (the rewind causes re-capture, not lost updates), so this is hardening rather than a defect in the approved design. The repo precedent is bin/fm-procevent-remote-reply.sh, which holds an fm_lock_lib lock across its read_cursor/write_cursor pair (line 318); wrapping cmd_ack's compare-and-commit the same way closes it. - ℹ️ `.agents/skills/process-event-sources/SKILL.md:37` - The new `ack` pointer sits in the adapter inventory section, while the "Handling a wake" section (line 46 onward) is the one that enumerates what a handler does after fully handling a result - and it names only `bin/fm-procevent.sh handled <source-id> <sequence>`, stating that "only this call durably retires the wake". A handler working from that section alone would call `handled` and never `ack`, which retires the announcement but leaves the update unconfirmed at Telegram, reproducing exactly the re-capture loop this round's fix exists to close. That same section also says "Ask the adapter what the result means rather than parsing it yourself", yet telegram has no `classify`, so the handler must read the raw JSON to find the highest update id to ack. Consider whether the "Handling a wake" section should carry a one-line note that a telegram result needs the adapter's `ack` in addition to `handled` - exact flags still owned by the script header. 🔧 Fix: serialize telegram cursor ack, clarify 409 and handler steps 2 infos still open: - ℹ️ `.agents/skills/process-event-sources/SKILL.md:55` - The new handler procedure documents the two acknowledgements in the order `handled` then `ack` ("after `handled`, call the telegram adapter's `ack`"). The reverse order is what makes the adapter's own already-seen rule usable. As written: a crash between the two leaves the wake retired but the update unconfirmed at Telegram, so it is redelivered as a brand new result under a new sequence, and because the cursor never moved the handler sees update ids above the cursor and fully re-acts on the same operator message - a duplicated effect with no signal that it is a repeat. The skill's own boundary paragraph already disclaims exactly-once so neither order breaks a stated guarantee, and your round-2 direction specified the relationship but not the sequence - so this is your call, not a defect. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-procevent-telegram.sh:213` - cmd_ack carries the same two-line teardown (`release_cursor_lock` then `trap - EXIT HUP INT TERM`) on both exit paths, at lines 214-215 and 219-220. The branch only differs in whether it commits and in which message it prints, so the teardown can run once after the branch: set the message inside the if/else, then release, clear the traps, and print. That removes the duplicated pair without changing behavior - the lock still drops before any output, and the EXIT trap still covers the `die` paths inside the critical section. As it stands a third path added later (say a distinct verdict for an id equal to the cursor) has two places it must remember to mirror. 🔧 Fix: document ack-before-handled order, dedupe ack teardown ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: fix: remove startup-memory budget gate
body:
## Intent

Remove Firstmate startup-memory budget gate. In the internal .agents/skills/stow skill and the public skills/stow skill only if mirrored, stop requiring before/after bin/fm-startup-memory-budget.sh reports and stop refusing reset-safe solely because estimated tokens exceed config/startup-memory-budget. Preserve real memory hygiene: inspect every owned memory file completely, inspect-then-update, prune stale or duplicate material, route knowledge to its authoritative owner, preserve unique current facts and ownership boundaries, and return a completion receipt with file actions and an honest reset-safe verdict based on whether durable findings are captured. Remove or shrink AGENTS.md and documentation budget contracts without leaving dual owners. Stop materializing or inheriting config/startup-memory-budget when nothing agent-facing needs it; prefer deleting the dead config, bootstrap, inheritance, helper, and diagnostic surfaces rather than leaving an inert knob or metrics dashboard. Update or remove tests and docs/verification/stow-memory.md so CI matches the new contract, including bootstrap and secondmate inheritance coverage, with no tests or agent paths that force the old gate. Keep docs concise. Verify no leftover budget-gate requirements in source, docs, tests, stow internal/public boundaries, AGENTS/docs ownership, bootstrap/inheritance paths, or reset-safe logic. Tests and no-mistakes PR checks must be green.

## What Changed
- Drop the `/stow` startup-memory budget gate: no before/after `bin/fm-startup-memory-budget.sh` reports, and reset-safe is no longer refused solely for estimated-token overage; the receipt still reports per-file actions and an honest reset-safe verdict based on captured durable findings and unresolved ownership exceptions.
- Delete the budget helper/CLI, bootstrap materialization, inheritance special-casing, and `config/startup-memory-budget` docs/ownership surfaces so the dead knob is fully gone rather than left inert.
- Update AGENTS.md, stow/bootstrap-diagnostics/secondmate-provisioning skills, configuration docs, and tests (including bootstrap and secondmate inheritance coverage) so CI and agent paths match the new contract.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Well-bounded deletion of the startup-memory budget gate with consistent cleanup across skills, bootstrap/inheritance, helpers, docs, and tests, and no leftover agent-facing contract paths.

## Testing

Amend the existing authoritative delivery lifecycle in AGENTS.md without duplicating contracts: bead-backed work is not complete merely because its PR merged; before cleanup Firstmate must attach the project required Closure-Receipt and run the canonical bead close command. Tracker-serialization work must land in the same attended shift as the work it records and closure truth must never live solely on an unlanded branch. Amend the generated ship contract in bin/fm-brief.sh so workers on bead-backed tasks include the bead ID in the PR title, while keeping the rule conditional and introducing no br workflow for projects that are not bead-backed. Add executable generated-brief coverage through the existing public interface, never brittle source-byte assertions. Keep the change concise in existing owner locations; do not change project files, captain-private files, merge authority, or unrelated behavior. Verify documentation ownership and audience checks plus relevant brief and lint tests, then ship through no-mistakes to a green PR. Acceptance evidence must identify bin/fm-brief.sh as owner of the bead-ID PR-title rule and AGENTS.md as owner of both Closure-Receipt plus bead close delivery completion and same-shift tracker landing. ## What Changed - AGENTS.md's delivery lifecycle now states that for bead-backed work a merged PR is not completion: before cleanup, Firstmate must attach the project's required Closure-Receipt and run the canonical bead close command, and tracker-serialization work must land in the same attended shift rather than living only on an unlanded branch. - `bin/fm-brief.sh` adds rule 8 to generated ship briefs: on bead-backed projects, workers include the task's bead ID in the PR title; projects that are not bead-backed must not have a `br` workflow imposed on them. - `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` gains `test_bead_pr_title_rule_is_conditional_for_ship_briefs`, which generates a real ship brief through the public interface and asserts both the conditional bead-ID rule and the no-imposition guard are present. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A 20-line additive doctrine/brief change that satisfies every required intent constraint in the correct owner locations, avoids all forbidden behaviors, and includes a correctly wired public-interface test. ## Testing Ran the targeted brief, documentation-audience, and lint test suites (all pass, including the new conditional bead-ID brief test), then generated a real ship brief end-to-end to capture the rendered worker-facing rule and the AGENTS.md doctrine excerpt; evidence identifies bin/fm-brief.sh as owner of the bead-ID PR-title rule and AGENTS.md as owner of Closure-Receipt/bead-close completion and same-shift tracker landing.
