Adding one more harness (e.g. `opencode`) to the loop with `expected=persistent` restores the coverage the codex case used to provide. 🔧 Fix: Verify Codex config from cleanup; fix Pi heading, coverage 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `tests/fm-sessionstart-hook-live-e2e.test.sh:473` - Moving the verdict into cleanup also collapsed two comparisons into one, and the phase label is now advanced without evidence. `codex_config_arm "$lab" "the headless probes"` (line 469) is the only snapshot, and `CODEX_CONFIG_PHASE="the interactive probe"` (line 473) is assigned as soon as `probe_process_opens` returns, before anything has compared `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`. Two consequences: (1) if the headless `codex exec` probes dirtied the live config, the guard does not notice, so it goes on to launch the interactive probe against a live home that is already polluted — several more minutes of real model turns and a second chance to write — where the previous code aborted right after the headless phase; (2) when the difference is finally reported from `codex_config_verify`, both messages at lines 187 and 189 name "the interactive probe" even though the headless phase caused it, pointing the operator at the wrong command while they hand-edit their live config. Note the single-shot caching plus the `rm -f ... "$CODEX_CONFIG_BEFORE"` on the clean path (line 180) is what makes a second check impossible today. Fix: after `probe_process_opens`, call `codex_config_verify || exit 1` and then re-arm with `codex_config_arm "$lab" "the interactive probe"`; `codex_config_arm` already resets `CODEX_CONFIG_VERDICT` and re-snapshots, so the cleanup-on-every-exit guarantee is preserved for whichever phase is live. 🔧 Fix: Verify Codex config per probe phase, not once ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
⚠️ **Test** - 1 warning - ⚠️ `tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh:1255` - tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh hangs indefinitely (does not fail) in test_hook_claude_mode_terminal_boundary_excludes_starting_owner on hosts without /bin/cat. Its fake `cat` shim calls `/bin/cat` by absolute path to reach the real binary past the fakebin shadow; on NixOS that path does not exist, so the shim never writes the `ready` FIFO and the test blocks on `read` forever (50 ok emitted before the stall, killed after ~25 min on two separate runs). Pre-existing and unrelated to this change: both bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh and this test file are byte-identical between 833a9a2 and a0fe8da. A hang is worse than a failure here because it stalls the suite rather than reporting; the author may want the shim to resolve the real cat portably. - `bash tests/fm-guard-stale-banner.test.sh` - 20/20 ok, including the three new checkpoint cases (fresh beacon without a watcher is healthy, stale beacon still alarms, detected Codex selects the checkpoint model) - `FM_TEST_BASE_PATH=<paths with git/bash/treehouse> bash tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh` - 47/47 ok, including `C9 spawn: secondmate launch pins auto-arm, checkpoint, or persistent supervision to its own harness` - `bash tests/fm-busy-adapter-wiring.test.sh` - 8/8 ok - `env -u NO_MISTAKES_GATE FM_TEST_BASE_PATH=<...> bash tests/fm-sessionstart-nudge.test.sh` - 18/18 ok - `bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` - 4/4 ok - `bash tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` - 50 ok then hangs in test_hook_claude_mode_terminal_boundary_excludes_starting_owner (missing /bin/cat on this host; pre-existing, files byte-identical to base) - Manual end-to-end: `/tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZH1CF7RP1GJHYGCXKFR01NT/codex-watcher-demo.sh` drives the real `bin/fm-guard.sh` in a throwaway home with Codex process ancestry (no FM_SUPERVISION_MODEL override) against the base tree and the target tree, for both the between-checkpoints case and a 20-minute stale beacon - Manual: `/tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZH1CF7RP1GJHYGCXKFR01NT/live-guard-offline-check.sh` exercises the live guard's `shell_quote` (argv fidelity through tmux, with the old `"$*"` form as a control) and `codex_config_arm`/`codex_config_verify` (per-phase verdict, leaked-lab-path failure, unattributable-write failure, no blind restore) against a fake CODEX_HOME - Baseline comparison: same suites run from a `git archive` extraction of base commit 833a9a2 to confirm the two environment failures are pre-existing - `bash -n tests/fm-sessionstart-hook-live-e2e.test.sh` - parses cleanly (the live guard itself was deliberately not executed)
🔧 **Document** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ℹ️ `docs/verification/supervision.md:311` - The Turn-end guard section records a dated command/output evidence block for each prior pull-guard predicate correction (2026-08-02 and 2026-08-04, the latter scoped to "the Claude Stop auto-arm model, where the watcher runs only between turns"), but this change's Codex foreground-checkpoint extension of that same predicate - plus the fm-spawn.sh secondmate pin from persistent to checkpoint - has no corresponding record, which the repo's own guideline ("update the corresponding verification evidence when behavior changes") calls for. I did not write one because I could not generate representative evidence in this worktree: ShellCheck is absent, so bin/fm-lint.sh cannot produce the CI-parity line the sibling records carry, and bin/fm-test-run.sh on tests/fm-guard-stale-banner.test.sh plus tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh was still running after ~15 minutes against a recorded baseline of ~80s for four suites. title: fix(bin): stop fm-watch-arm false FAILED when a cycle close lost a startup race
body:
## Intent

Fix bin/fm-watch-arm.sh reporting a false 'cycle ended without an actionable reason' FAILED alarm when a watcher cycle genuinely delivered a wake, without weakening detection of a real supervision failure

## What Changed

- In `owned_child_finished()` (`bin/fm-watch-arm.sh`), extend the existing successor/delivery-ledger check that previously ran only on a clean (`rc=0`) child exit to also run on nonzero and signal exits, since a nonzero close can itself be caused by a startup race (the PR-check migration guard or lock acquire rejecting an ambiguous mid-startup lock) rather than a genuine crash — only a close with no live successor and no ledgered delivery is now reported as `watcher: FAILED - cycle ended without an actionable reason`.
- Reclassify cycle-log reason tags accordingly (`unexpected-clean-exit`, `nonzero-exit`, `signal-exit`, and their `-delivered-wake` variants) so the durable lifecycle ledger reflects which path a close took.
- Add `test_arm_reports_sibling_delivered_wake_after_losing_a_startup_race` to `tests/fm-watch-arm.test.sh`, covering an arm whose own forked child loses the PR-check migration race to a live sibling and must report that sibling's delivered wake instead of a false failure; adjust `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh`'s killed-watcher case to set `FM_ARM_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT` now that nonzero exits go through the same bounded successor-check window as clean exits.
- Update `docs/watcher-continuity.md` to describe the widened recheck path and document the new test coverage.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The fix correctly extends the existing successor/delivery-ledger reconciliation (previously only applied to rc=0 clean exits) to every child close that never printed its own wake, closing the exact false-alarm path described in the intent (a startup race lost to a sibling watcher) without weakening genuine-failure detection — a real failure with no successor and no delivery record still logs the reason and returns nonzero. The duplicate FAILED-message removal (93044d1) cleanly resolves a redundancy introduced earlier in the same branch (a292cbc), leaving a single, doc-consistent FAILED message. Docs, header comments, and tests were all updated in lockstep, and the new regression test exercises the real subprocess race (PR-check migration ownership rejection) rather than asserting on source text, satisfying the test-quality bar. The only behavioral trade-off — genuine crashes now wait up to CONFIRM_TIMEOUT (10s default) before declaring FAILED instead of failing instantly — is a bounded, intentional consequence of the same mechanism already used for clean exits, not a detection weakening.

title: feat(bin): give each secondmate its own durable runtime
body:
## Intent Each secondmate gains its own durable runtime: harness, model and effort recorded in its data/secondmates.md registry entry and re-resolved on every spawn, so a per-mate choice survives recovery, /updatefirstmate and any other relaunch instead of reverting to the home-wide config/secondmate-harness pin. That config file stays the fallback default. Per-axis and backward compatible: a mate may pin only a model or only an effort and inherit the rest; a record carrying none of the fields is the pre-existing form and behaves exactly as before; a recorded harness deliberately suppresses the config file's model/effort tokens because those were written against that file's own harness. Precedence per axis, strongest first: explicit per-spawn --harness/--model/--effort flag, then the mate's recorded field, then config/secondmate-harness. Deliberately NO rules engine and NO new config file - the captain ruled out a secondmate-dispatch.json because secondmates are persistent and rarely change. Fail-closed: an unverified harness, an effort outside low|medium|high|xhigh|max, an unusable model (including the reserved '-' and 'default' route sentinels), an unknown or repeated key, or a missing field terminator makes the record malformed and is refused at edit time, at fm-home-seed.sh validate, and again before any launch. Local and remote routes resolve identically and the remote route keeps refusing anything but a verified adapter, now by calling the registry lib's shared allowlist rather than its own copy. bin/fm-home-seed.sh gains a 'runtime' action as the create-time and change-time path, taking the registry lock and validating the whole rewritten registry before replacing it. Captain's explicit decision during review: a re-seed of an already-registered mate PRESERVES its recorded harness/model/effort and must never silently reset it to the home-wide pin; both registry writers emit the runtime segment through the shared secondmate_registry_render_line boundary, with a test that re-seeds a registered mate and asserts the pin survives. bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh's independent jq copy of the record regexes was widened to match, so pinned mates no longer show a null home in the fleet and bearings snapshots. The branch also carries a pre-existing flaky-test fix: test_config_reread_serializes_concurrent_pushes bounded a backgrounded config push by 100 x 0.02s spins, which a loaded host misses; it now uses a 60-second wall-clock deadline. That flake was proven to pre-exist on an unmodified checkout of the same base commit (failed 3/3 there). Contributed from a fork per CONTRIBUTING.md: origin is the parent repo and the gate pushes to eduardstan/firstmate, so this is a cross-fork head. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-secondmate-registry-lib.sh` now parses an optional per-mate runtime segment (`harness:`, `model:`, `effort:`, each independently optional) between `projects:` and `added` on both the local and remote record forms. It fails closed: an unverified adapter, an effort outside `low|medium|high|xhigh|max`, an unusable model (including the `-` and `default` route sentinels), an unknown or repeated key, or a missing field terminator makes the record malformed. A record carrying none of the fields parses exactly as before. The lib also exports the shared adapter allowlist and a `secondmate_registry_render_line` writer boundary. - `bin/fm-spawn.sh` resolves each axis independently — explicit per-spawn `--harness`/`--model`/`--effort`, then the mate's recorded field, then `config/secondmate-harness` — and suppresses the config file's model/effort tokens when a harness is recorded. The remote route reads the record in-shell (so a malformed pin surfaces instead of falling through to the local path) and enforces verified adapters via the registry lib's allowlist rather than its own copy. - `bin/fm-home-seed.sh` gains a `runtime =` action that takes the registry lock, validates every value and the whole rewritten registry before replacing it, and `-` clears an axis; `write_registry` carries a registered mate's recorded runtime forward across re-seed and both writers emit through the shared render boundary. `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh`'s jq record parser was widened to the same vocabulary so pinned mates no longer report a null home and unreadable pins are flagged. Also bounds the pre-existing flaky `test_config_reread_serializes_concurrent_pushes` by a 60-second wall-clock deadline instead of 100 × 0.02s spins. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-bounded and matches every source-verifiable acceptance criterion — per-axis precedence resolves identically on both routes, refusal is enforced at edit, validate, and pre-launch, both registry writers preserve the pin through the shared render boundary, legacy records parse unchanged, and a cross-parser check of the fleet-snapshot jq copy found no case where it accepts a record the launcher refuses. ## Testing Ran the seven new per-mate runtime tests in tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh, the two new registry-runtime tests in tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh, and the previously flaky test_config_reread_serializes_concurrent_pushes three times in a row — all pass. The remote-route e2e assertion in tests/fm-remote-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh also passed, though that whole long linear file was still executing when this phase closed, so remote CI owns its full result. Beyond the automated tests I drove the real CLI end to end as a captain would and captured the transcript: two secondmates in one home pinned to different runtimes launch on their own harness/model/effort, a relaunch and a re-seed both preserve the pin, an explicit --model still wins, invalid harness/effort/model values and an unknown record key are refused at edit time, at validate, and before launch with no launch command emitted, and the fleet snapshot keeps pinned mates' homes non-null while flagging only the malformed record. The worktree is clean; no source or test files were modified.

one axis only, rest inherited - docs - demo charter (home: /tmp/.../docs; scope: demo charter; projects: ; model: cheap-1; added 2026-08-08) $ fm-spawn.sh infra --secondmate # launch command handed to the pane ... codex --model 'gpt-x' -c 'model_reasoning_effort="xhigh"' --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox ... $ fm-spawn.sh docs --secondmate ... claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --model 'cheap-1' --effort 'high' ... $ fm-spawn.sh infra --secondmate --model sonnet # title: fix(bin): distinguish delivery-only secondmate actions
body:
## Intent Fix second-mate pending-reply tracking without weakening genuine escalation. Mark explicit delivery-only action requests at creation as reply_expected=0 so confirmed delivery resolves them without any correlated status line, recovery request, or false escalation; apply that classification to the config and instruction re-read nudge producers that simply ask the second mate to perform an action, including the /updatefirstmate instruction re-read workflow as explicitly authorized. Keep ordinary question and report requests reply-expected by default so missed correlated replies still recover and escalate exactly as before. Add a supported operator-facing close/resolve path in fm-pending-reply-lib.sh and a CLI so awaiting_report, recovery_sent, or escalated stuck records can be resolved without hand-editing parent-owned state, preserving audit provenance and closing the exact durable OPEN DECISIONS key idempotently. Delivery-only terminal state publication must be atomic and crash-recoverable, and reconciliation must repair delivered reply_expected=0 records before retiring confirmation evidence. Keep the change surgical. Tests must first reproduce the old false escalation red, then prove delivery-only green, prove the operator close path, and preserve genuine reply-expected escalation coverage. The remote-secondmate lifecycle e2e timing assertion was exonerated by failing 3/3 on both this branch and the untouched base; it is pre-existing, out of scope, must not be fixed here, and should only be re-run if it trips CI. ## What Changed - Add explicit `--delivery-only` secondmate requests that resolve atomically on confirmed delivery, including crash recovery, while preserving reply recovery and escalation for ordinary questions and reports. - Classify bootstrap, configuration, and `/updatefirstmate` re-read nudges as delivery-only actions to prevent false pending-reply escalations. - Add an audited, idempotent operator CLI for resolving stuck pending replies and closing their exact durable escalation decisions, with supporting documentation and regression coverage. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the terminal scan marker now preserves crash-safe exact-key closure while making subsequent resolved-record ticks O(1), with no source-verifiable regression found in the cumulative change. ## Testing The supplied base reproduced the false delivery-only behavior, both focused target test runs and test-selection checks passed, and the CLI/state transcript demonstrates delivery-only closure, preserved genuine escalation, idempotent operator resolution, and crash recovery. The exonerated remote-secondmate lifecycle e2e was not rerun, as required.
Evidence: Base regression replay baseline_exit=1 not ok - delivery-only control flag leaked into the request body ```text not ok - delivery-only control flag leaked into the request body ```
Evidence: Target focused suite ```text ok - normal correlated reply resolves once (idempotent) ok - completed turn with no report triggers exactly one recovery ok - recovery attempts reconcile without reinjection ok - recovery reply resolves the original expectation ok - second missed turn escalates once and remains durable ok - failed escalation publication remains retryable and publishes once ok - legacy escalation closes under the shared default key ok - legacy escalation cannot close an unrelated default-key decision ok - foreign correlated blocker cannot impersonate a pending-reply escalation ok - concurrent resolution closes one keyed escalation exactly once ok - concurrent escalation yields to a late correlated reply ok - transport success cannot masquerade as reply success ok - undelivered records remain immutable across scan paths ok - delivery confirmation fallback reconciles durably ok - unrelated events and stale correlation ids cannot resolve ok - restart preserves expectation and exact parent destination ok - wrong-home reports are detected but do not silently acknowledge ok - direct unmarked captain input creates no expectation ok - fm-send marked secondmate path creates pending and embeds corr ok - delivery-only secondmate action resolves on delivery and never false-escalates ok - /updatefirstmate re-read nudge is delivery-only ok - delivery-only partial commit repairs before marker retirement ok - operator resolve command closes awaiting, recovery, and escalated records ok - operator resolve closes an unjournaled durable escalation ok - status-pointed document resolves the expectation ok - optional helper report resolves without being required for correctness ok - backend busy/idle observation covers Pi/Claude paths without conversation scrape ok - tmux and zellij unknown states use bounded capture fallback ok - pending replies scope Kimi capture fallback by recorded harness ok - tick skips terminal records and reuses target observations ok - correlations are reused only for matching open task records ok - tick end-to-end: miss -> one recovery -> escalate -> durable ok - failed transport discards undelivered expectation only ok - all pending-reply tests passed ```
Evidence: CLI and persisted-state evidence `Delivery-only resolved on delivery with zero escalation lines. An ordinary request recovered and escalated normally. The operator CLI closed the exact decision once and left OPEN DECISIONS empty. Interrupted publication reconciled before confirmation retirement.` ```text PENDING-REPLY END-TO-END EVIDENCE ================================= 1. Explicit delivery-only action through the real fm-send CLI $ FM_HOME= bin/fm-send.sh hibit --delivery-only "re-read the inherited config" correlation=ca0c81888a6eed24 reply_expected=0 phase=resolved resolved_via=delivery after completed turn with no correlated report: phase=resolved, escalation_lines=0 2. Ordinary question remains reply-expected and genuinely escalates $ FM_HOME= bin/fm-send.sh hibit "is the release ready?" correlation=f1a551387ddd09a4 reply_expected=1 after delivery: phase=awaiting_report after first missed turn: phase=recovery_sent, recovery_sends=1 after second missed turn: phase=escalated blocked [key=pending-reply-f1a551387ddd09a4]: pending-reply-missed: task=hibit pending-reply-id=f1a551387ddd09a4 request=is the release ready? 3. Supported operator CLI closes the exact durable decision idempotently $ FM_HOME= bin/fm-pending-reply-resolve.sh f1a551387ddd09a4 "confirmed in operator review" resolved pending reply f1a551387ddd09a4 for task hibit phase=resolved resolved_via=operator resolved_note=confirmed in operator review durable close lines=1 OPEN DECISIONS after close= 4. Confirmed delivery survives an interrupted terminal-state publication before reconciliation: reply_expected=0, delivered_epoch=12000, phase=awaiting_report, confirmation_marker=present after reconciliation: phase=resolved, resolved_via=delivery, resolved_epoch=12000, confirmation_marker=retired ```

If escalation appends its durable `blocked` line and crashes before persisting that epoch, resolving the still-`recovery_sent` record marks it resolved while leaving the decision permanently open; retries take the same early return. Make the shared close helper detect and close the exact library-owned escalation line even when its epoch journal is missing, or make escalation publication and journaling crash-atomic. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-test-run.sh:896` - The new `fm-pending-reply*` → `secondmate` mapping does not select `tests/fm-pending-reply.test.sh`, because that test is absent from `family_for_basename`’s `secondmate` case. Additionally, `fm-send.sh` changes select only backend/pure-contract families. Future changes to the implementation can therefore omit its delivery-only and operator-resolution tests. title: fix(skills): use a subshell for no-mistakes init in project-management
body:
## Summary
- The project-management skill's no-mistakes-initialization example used a bare top-level `cd projects/<name> && no-mistakes init && no-mistakes doctor`, which the repo's own cd-guard PreToolUse policy denies (a persistent cd into a project clone from the primary firstmate shell risks silently relocating later firstmate-owned commands).
- Wraps the example in a subshell, `(cd projects/<name> && no-mistakes init && no-mistakes doctor)`, so the primary shell's directory never changes, and references docs/cd-guard.md.

## Test plan
- Documentation-only change to an internal agent-only skill file; no script behavior changed.
- Validated through the no-mistakes pipeline: intent, rebase, review, test, and document steps all passed with zero findings. Lint was skipped (ShellCheck not installed in this environment; no shell scripts were touched by this change).

title: fix(skills): enforce read-before-write for all stow findings
body:
## Intent

Port ONLY the read-before-write discipline into the PUBLIC installer-facing stow skill skills/stow/SKILL.md. This is firstmate shared, tracked material, so firstmate-coding-guidelines applies: one-owner rule, knowledge-placement decision tree, one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never an em dash, no agent co-author on commits.

What to add: the discipline of inspecting the CURRENT contents of a memory/notes/backlog target BEFORE replacing it; classifying the change as new / duplicate / superseding / obsolete; and writing a CONSIDERED replacement rather than a blind append or overwrite. title: feat(bin): run the fleet from a configurable update source, absorb upstream separately
body:
## Intent

Make the captain's own fork the source firstmate runs from, so improvements are usable the moment they land, while contributions to the upstream open-source project become fire-and-forget good citizenship. The captain does not want to monitor upstream pull requests; opening them is good faith, tracking them is not worth a development slot or recurring wake-ups.

Requirements as accepted:
1. The fork becomes the update source. bin/fm-update.sh and bin/fm-ff-lib.sh must fast-forward this home and every secondmate home from the captain's fork, not upstream. No hardcoded URL where a configurable belongs; follow the existing conventions in docs/configuration.md and make the source explicit and inspectable.
2. Upstream becomes a separate, deliberate absorb, fast-forward only exactly like today, reporting rather than forcing when the fork and upstream have genuinely diverged. Never rewrite history on either remote.
3. Opening an upstream pull request must arm no merge poll, hold no development slot, and generate no recurring wake-ups. Landing firstmate work on the fork is what completes a task; an upstream PR is a side effect never waited on.
4. AGENTS.md section 12 and the updatefirstmate skill must describe the model that actually ships, concisely, preserving every safety boundary, with one owner per contract and no contradictory descriptions.
5. Secondmate homes follow the same source through the existing guarded path, including the remote-routed case.

Safety boundaries that had to survive unchanged: fast-forward only, never force, never rewrite history, never discard unlanded work; a home mid-work must not be disrupted and a target that cannot cleanly fast-forward is skipped and reported; a tracked-files fast-forward never touches gitignored operational state; merge authority stays with the captain and nothing here grants autonomous merging.

Deliberate decisions a reviewer reading only the diff would not know:
- The update source defaults to 'origin' on purpose, so this shared template is unchanged for anyone who configures nothing; only a home that opts in points elsewhere.
- config/update-remote and config/upstream-remote hold git remote NAMES, not URLs, so no captain's fork address enters tracked material and the address stays inspectable via git remote.
- Both resolvers assign to variables rather than printing. A printing variant read through a command substitution loses the refusal reason with the subshell, which was found by watching a test fail.
- config/upstream-remote is deliberately NOT inherited by secondmate homes: only the home that ships firstmate's tracked material has an upstream, and an inherited remote name a secondmate's checkout lacks would lose the check rather than gain it. config/update-remote IS inherited.
- The remote-routed update reads the inherited choice from the secondmate home rather than taking a new command argument, deliberately: this is the command that updates the remote code root, so passing an argument an older root could not parse would deadlock the very update that would teach it.
- bin/fm-pr-check.sh refuses only on a POSITIVE upstream identity match; a configured remote with no resolvable forge identity warns and continues, so one home's contribution setting cannot block an unrelated project's merge poll.
- fm-update.sh still exits 0 when a target is skipped; that is the pre-existing contract for this script and was deliberately left unchanged. The new non-zero exits are an unusable configured source (1) and upstream absorb divergence (3).
- Two remote layouts are supported and documented because the captain's home may be arranged either way; docs/configuration.md explains why this is the mirror image of the contributor arrangement in CONTRIBUTING.md rather than a contradiction with it.

The branch also merges the current fork main, which carries separately-landed recovery work (crew-state skipped-delivery guard, codex effort ceiling, branch-prefix convention, PR review activity). That merge was clean and is not part of what this change set is proposing; those merges were performed directly on the fork under the captain's instruction and are not this change's own work.

Verification already performed, not asserted: the new source was proven end to end against the captain's real fork history with both secondmate homes; the fast-forward-only refusals were reproduced live with unpiped non-zero exits; and every safety check was watched failing first via six mutations to production code, each reverted to green. Do not merge the resulting pull request; merge authority is the captain's.

## What Changed

- New `bin/fm-update-source-lib.sh` resolves `config/update-remote` (defaulting to `origin`, so an unconfigured home is unchanged) and `config/upstream-remote` as git remote *names*, assigning to variables rather than printing so a refusal reason survives. `bin/fm-update.sh` and `bin/fm-ff-lib.sh` switch from a hardcoded `origin` base mode to `remote:<name>` — default-branch resolution and fetch dedup are now keyed per remote — and `update-remote` joins `FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG` so secondmate homes, including the remote-routed code root, follow the same source through the existing guarded path. `upstream-remote` is deliberately not inherited.
- New `bin/fm-absorb-upstream.sh` makes pulling upstream into the fork a separate deliberate command: fast-forward only, never `--force`, never touching the local checkout or pushing to upstream, with `--dry-run` and a `diverged ahead=<n> behind=<n>` report that exits 3 instead of reconciling. `fm-update.sh` gains a non-zero exit for an unusable configured source while keeping its pre-existing exit-0-on-skip contract.
- PR polling refuses to arm for a pull request at the configured upstream: the check lives in the shared `fm_pr_poll_prepare` primitive (`bin/fm-pr-lib.sh`) so both `fm-pr-check.sh` and the `fm-pr-check-migrate.sh` rebuild path are covered, and it fires only on a positive forge-identity match — an unresolvable remote warns and continues. Docs move with the code (AGENTS.md §12, the `updatefirstmate` skill, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, `docs/architecture.md`), and new suites cover update, absorb, PR security, and branch behaviour. The branch also carries separately-landed fork main work merged in cleanly: the crew-state skipped-delivery guard, PR review-activity wake with a seeded cursor, the Codex effort ceiling, and the branch-prefix convention.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The remediation moves the upstream refusal to the one arming primitive every path funnels through while failing open on every unanswerable case so unrelated repositories keep waking firstmate, and both directions plus the migration rebuild and crash-recovery paths are covered by tests; the only remaining item is an info-level temp-pointer cleanup idiom with no live failure.

## Testing

I ran the three suites that own this change (fm-update, fm-absorb-upstream, fm-pr-check-security) plus the documentation-audiences test and the runner's coverage guard, all green, then proved the intent end to end against a real sandbox fleet rather than relying on unit passes: a fork-only commit became usable across the primary home and both secondmate homes under `update-source: fork` while origin stayed behind, every fast-forward-only refusal reproduced with its real exit code, upstream absorb reported all four verdicts without writing to upstream or moving the local checkout, and an upstream pull request armed no poll at either the entrypoint or the shared arming primitive while fork and unrelated-project PRs armed normally. Because nothing pinned the secondmate-inheritance contract, I added one focused test and watched it fail under three separate production-code mutations before reverting to green. The change is CLI-only with no rendered surface, so the reviewer-visible artifact is a command transcript rather than a screenshot. One suite covering the remote-routed update could not run here: it dies under the system bash 3.2 in a file this change never touched, which needs a CI runner rather than a fix in this diff.

========================================================================

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-check.sh:82` - The upstream-PR refusal is not at the boundary the two arming paths share, so the invariant "no merge poll is armed for a PR at the configured upstream" remains reachable. bin/fm-pr-check.sh:82-95 is the only place that checks; bin/fm-pr-check-migrate.sh arms polls independently at :802-803 (`canonical_repair_from_pending`) and :1055-1056 (main rebuild loop), taking provider/url/host/path/number straight from `state/<id>.meta` via `metadata_pr_is_canonical` and calling the same `fm_pr_poll_prepare` + `fm_pr_poll_publish_prepared` primitives with no upstream check. Concrete sequence: a home on the documented arrangement 1 (origin=fork, upstream=the open-source project) has an existing task with `pr=https://github.com/<upstream>/firstmate/pull/N` armed before `config/upstream-remote` existed; `fm_pr_poll_artifacts_valid` gates on `cmp -s "$template" "$check"` (bin/fm-pr-lib.sh:598), so any change to bin/fm-pr-poll.sh invalidates every armed poll, `migration_needed` (bin/fm-pr-check-migrate.sh:383) returns true at the next bootstrap, and the loop rebuilds and re-arms that upstream poll -- producing exactly the recurring wakes the change exists to prevent. The earliest shared boundary both callers already funnel through is `fm_pr_poll_prepare` in bin/fm-pr-lib.sh; putting the upstream identity refusal there (or in a shared helper in fm-update-source-lib.sh that both fm-pr-check.sh and fm-pr-check-migrate.sh call) makes the invariant hold instead of adding a second symptom patch. Needs a decision on what migration should do with an already-armed upstream poll (quarantine unarmed vs. warn), which is why this is not a mechanical fix.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-update-source-lib.sh:47` - `fm_update_source_config_value` silently ignores a `config/update-remote` that is a symlink or unreadable (`[ -f "$path" ] && [ ! -L "$path" ] && [ -r "$path" ] || return 0`), returning nothing, which makes `fm_update_source_remote_var` take the empty-value branch and set `FM_UPDATE_SOURCE_REMOTE=origin` with return 0 (line 89). That is the exact outcome bin/fm-update.sh:64-65 says must never happen ("a misconfigured value must never silently resolve back to origin") and that the unsafe-name branch correctly refuses on. It is also stricter than every other firstmate config reader: bin/fm-harness.sh:101, bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:1174, and bin/fm-spawn.sh:752 all use a plain `[ -f ]`, which follows symlinks, so an operator who manages the gitignored `config/` dir by symlinking into a dotfiles repo gets working `crew-harness`/`backend`/`crew-dispatch.json` but a silently-ignored `update-remote`. Under the documented arrangement 2 (origin = the open-source project) the whole fleet then fast-forwards from upstream instead of the fork, printing a confident `update-source: origin`, with no diagnostic anywhere. If the symlink rejection is deliberate hardening, it should set FM_UPDATE_SOURCE_ERROR and return 1 like the unsafe-name path rather than falling through to the default.
- ⚠️ `docs/configuration.md:351` - Adding `update-remote` to FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG (bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:72) makes it flow through every derived consumer, but two hand-written enumerations of that same set were not updated, so the docs now contradict the code. docs/configuration.md:351 lists what `bin/fm-config-push.sh` reports per home as `crew-dispatch.json, crew-harness, backlog-backend, backend, herdr-presentation-spaces, startup-memory-budget, trace-context, and data/captain-shared.md` -- a complete enumeration (it includes trace-context) that is now missing `update-remote`, even though the report is built from `fm_config_inherit_items` / `fm_config_reread_changed_items` (bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:94, :576), which iterate FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG. .agents/skills/secondmate-provisioning/SKILL.md:128 has the same omission for the per-home reread instruction file, whose item set comes from the same iteration. SKILL.md:107 was correctly updated, which makes the mismatch internal to one document. This is the "no contradictory descriptions" constraint in the intent's requirement 4, at the file docs/configuration.md that the change itself declares the owner of this contract.

🔧 Fix: enforce upstream-PR poll refusal in the shared arming primitive
1 info still open:
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-pr-lib.sh:494` - The new upstream-refusal branch in `fm_pr_poll_prepare` drops the three temp-file pointers with bare assignments (`FM_PR_POLL_DATA_TMP=` / `_CHECK_TMP=` / `_REG_TMP=`) instead of calling `fm_pr_poll_cleanup`, which is the idiom every other early return in that function uses. `fm_pr_poll_cleanup` both removes the files and clears the pointers; the bare assignments only clear them, so anything still on disk becomes unreachable to the EXIT-trap cleanup at bin/fm-pr-check-migrate.sh:334. Reachable sequence: in the migrate main loop, task A's `canonical_arm_or_suppress` prepares successfully, then `fm_pr_poll_publish_prepared` fails partway -- `fm_pr_poll_revoke_final` removes only the DESTINATIONS, leaving e.g. `FM_PR_POLL_CHECK_TMP`/`_REG_TMP` pointing at live mktemp files -- and the loop continues; task B is at the upstream identity, so prepare takes the refusal branch and blanks those pointers; the EXIT trap then finds all three empty and removes nothing, orphaning mode-0600 `state/.fm-pr-poll-check.XXXXXX` and `.fm-pr-poll-registration.XXXXXX` files permanently. No secret escapes (same dir, same mode), and the refusal branch itself creates nothing, so this is a robustness gap rather than a live defect -- but leaving private temps behind is exactly what the rest of this file is built to prevent. Replacing the three assignments with `fm_pr_poll_cleanup` is behavior-identical on every currently reachable path and strictly safer.

</details>

<details>
<summary>⚠️ **Test** - 1 warning</summary>

- ⚠️ `tests/fm-remote-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh:360` - tests/fm-remote-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh is the only automated coverage of the remote-routed `update` path (requirement 5's remote case) and cannot run in this environment: it fails deterministically at bin/fm-remote-home-seed.sh:190 with `PROJECT_NAMES[@]: unbound variable` under the system bash 3.2.57, long before reaching the update assertions. That file is byte-identical to the base commit, so this is a pre-existing bash-version limitation, not a regression from this change; fixing it would need a newer bash installed system-wide, which is outside the worktree boundary. I compensated by reproducing cmd_update's two new lines directly (resolve the inherited choice from the secondmate home, then run the updater with FM_UPDATE_REMOTE against a code root with no home config), which reported `update-source: fork` - but the ssh/route plumbing around them is unverified locally and needs CI on a bash 4.4+ runner.
- <code>`bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-update.test.sh tests/fm-absorb-upstream.test.sh` - 18 update contracts (T1-T20) and 6 absorb contracts (A1-A6), all pass</code>

# Verification and known gaps (added by the author)
## 8. Known coverage gap: the remote-routed update path

`tests/fm-remote-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh` is the only automated
coverage of the remote-routed `update` path - requirement 5's remote case - and
it **cannot run in this environment**. It fails deterministically inside
`bin/fm-remote-home-seed.sh`, which expands `"${PROJECT_NAMES[@]}"` while that
array is empty; the system bash here is 3.2.57, which rejects an empty-array
expansion under `set -u` as an unbound variable, long before the test reaches any
update assertion.

This is **pre-existing, not a regression from this change**, verified three ways:

- `git diff 833a9a2 <head> -- bin/fm-remote-home-seed.sh tests/fm-remote-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh`
  is empty: both files are byte-identical to the base commit.
- The same test was already failing in the full-suite triage for this branch, and
  was re-run against the untouched base commit in a separate clone, where it
  fails identically.
- The mechanism reproduces directly: `/bin/bash -c 'set -u; A=(); echo "${A[@]}"'`
  prints `A[@]: unbound variable` on bash 3.2.57.

**What is therefore unproven here:** that `fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh update`
carries this fleet's configured update source into a remote host's shared code
root end to end. The logic is covered by inspection and by the local-route tests,
but not exercised against a real remote route on this machine.

The captain accepted this gap deliberately: both of his secondmate domains are
local, so the remote-routed path is not live for him, and widening this change to
repair a bash 3.2 incompatibility mid-validation would risk the work it is
attached to for no present benefit. The bash-3.2 compatibility repair is filed as
its own follow-up item rather than fixed here.


## Scope note: what is and is not in this diff

This branch merges the current state of the fork it is developed against, which
carries separately-landed recovery work (crew-state skipped-delivery guard,
codex effort ceiling, branch-prefix convention, PR review activity). Those merges
are not this change proposing that work; they were landed on the fork under their
own decisions. The change this pull request is actually proposing is the
configurable update source, the separate upstream absorb path, and the
upstream-PR poll refusal.

title: feat(bin): add prime-agent as a verified harness adapter
body:
## Intent firstmate gains prime-agent as a verified harness adapter - crewmate, scout and secondmate capable - with its own supervision protocol, primary guard extensions under the .prime/agent layout, teardown that stops its daemon session, and composer recognition so steers verify. Scope context a reviewer reading only the diff would not have. The task was deliberately NARROWED partway through by the captain, because prime-agent already runs firstmate workers today through fm-spawn's raw-launch escape hatch and Herdr already reads their busy/idle state from prime-agent's own built-in reporter. The instruction was to ship only what that escape hatch genuinely cannot do - (1) teardown shutting down prime-agent's detached daemon, (2) composer recognition so bin/fm-send.sh verifies instead of false-failing, (3) secondmate capability - plus the minimum harness registration those three require, and nothing beyond it. Deliberate exclusions the captain asked for, so their absence is intended and not an oversight: - No firstmate-owned busy-state extension. prime-agent's own built-in Herdr reporter already publishes pane state, so the per-task extension carries ONLY the turn_end wake touch and nothing is armed; a seeded busy record would have no firstmate writer that could ever clear it. The accepted cost is that an idle prime-agent worker classifies "unknown missing" rather than "idle", while a busy one classifies "busy herdr-native". That is the pre-existing escape-hatch behaviour and unknown surfaces rather than hides. - No tmux agent-process classification and no tmux composer arm. This home runs Herdr, and that check is harness-dependent on rendered output, so per the repo's own coding guidelines it must be proven against a real prime-agent pane under real tmux before it ships. The resulting gap is recorded explicitly in the adapter's skill section: a mid-turn steer to a tmux-hosted prime-agent worker still reads unknown and fails loudly rather than silently. - No harness-adapters model-discovery row, and no remote-secondmate allowlist entries; remote secondmates stay refused on prime-agent because none exists here. Deliberate design decisions that may look surprising in the diff: - bin/fm-harness.sh tests prime-agent's own markers BEFORE the CLAUDECODE fast path. This ordering is required, not stylistic. prime-agent's resident session worker inherits the long-lived per-user daemon supervisor's environment rather than the launching client's, so a supervisor first started from a Claude session hands CLAUDECODE=1 to every later prime-agent worker and no launch-side env -u can reach it. This was reproduced live as a crewmate reporting itself as claude. The same inheritance is why FM_PI_HARNESS, which works as the launch boundary for pi-signed, never reaches a prime-agent tool subprocess at all. The precedence flip is deliberately narrow: it requires PI_CODING_AGENT=true alongside the prime-agent marker, so a lone stale PRIME_AGENT_* still resolves to claude, and both directions are pinned by tests. - .prime/agent/extensions/ holds a SEPARATE pair of primary extensions rather than sharing the .pi/ ones. prime-agent has no agent_settled event at all and registering one is silently accepted but never fires, so the guard reconstructs the settle from agent_end following prime-agent's own built-in Herdr reporter. ctx.isIdle() is deliberately NOT the gate: it was measured false throughout a live run. The watcher extension is the Pi one minus its Calm rendering layer, which prime-agent's API cannot support and never sees anyway. Both files import the shared operational-input encoder from the .pi/ tree on purpose, to keep one owner rather than a second copy that would drift. - bin/fm-prime-agent-lib.sh exists as a lib rather than a copy in each caller because teardown and secondmate relaunch need exactly the same retirement. It never uses `prime-agent shutdown`, which would stop the captain's own sessions and every other home's workers, and it deliberately ignores `prime-agent status`, which marks even a live session's forkserver "stale". - The Herdr composer arm requires TWO independent signals before promoting a bare ">" row to a composer. The fleet-wide safety rule that a bare shell glyph on an unstructured row is a dead shell is NOT relaxed. Both signals are needed because /quit leaves prime-agent's reporter identity behind on a pane that has already returned to a login shell, and on the reporter alone a shell with PS1='> ' was verified live to become an injection target. - prime-agent is added to bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh even though the pid it records is a detached daemon worker that outlives the pane. That is safe only because fm-spawn --secondmate now retires the worker bound to a home before relaunching it there. The wedge and the fix were both reproduced live rather than argued. Everything relied on about prime-agent's Herdr integration comes from reading dist/core/extensions/builtin/herdr-agent-state.js, because prime-agent ships zero mentions of that integration across all 36 of its doc files. That source dependency is recorded in the adapter section so a future upgrade re-reads the source rather than trusting a release note. Delivery constraints for this run: the branch fm/prime-adapter must not be reset or replaced. Do not change any git remote - origin is the parent kunchenguid/firstmate and the gate pushes to the fork eduardstan/firstmate exactly as CONTRIBUTING.md prescribes. The branch sits on upstream main, so a rebase warning about bundling ~52 commits is a fork/upstream divergence artifact and the rebase step is to be skipped rather than rebased onto origin/main. The PR must open against the parent repo, not the fork. ## What Changed - Registers `prime-agent` across the harness surface: `bin/fm-harness.sh` detects it from its own `PRIME_AGENT_*` markers alongside `PI_CODING_AGENT=true` **before** the `CLAUDECODE` fast path (its daemon worker inherits the long-lived supervisor's environment, so a supervisor first started under Claude otherwise misreports every later worker), `bin/fm-spawn.sh` gains crewmate and secondmate launch shapes plus `--model`/`--thinking` mapping, and it is accepted as a verified harness by bootstrap crew dispatch and secondmate liveness. Adds a `prime-agent` supervision protocol doc and a separate pair of primary extensions under `.prime/agent/extensions/` (turn-end guard reconstructing settle from `agent_end`, and a watcher extension), wired into session-start load reporting and the supervision instructions. - Adds `bin/fm-prime-agent-lib.sh` as the single owner of retiring prime-agent's detached daemon sessions by recorded cwd (bounded CLI calls, never `prime-agent shutdown`). `bin/fm-teardown.sh` stops sessions bound to a worktree or removed home before the generic process reaper, `fm-spawn --secondmate` retires the worker bound to a home before relaunching it, and `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh` lists prime-agent as a lock-holding harness while treating a worker with no attached client and no in-flight activity as not alive. - Teaches the Herdr backend two prime-agent-specific reads: a pane whose reporter still claims `prime-agent` but whose process subtree holds none is reported `no-agent` (its reporter identity survives `/quit`), and a bare `>` row is promoted from dead shell to composer only when the live foreground process **and** the native reporter both say prime-agent. New tests cover detection in both directions, launch shapes, composer promotion and its refusal, daemon retirement, lock ancestry, and the watcher extension. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The adapter is broad (2378 insertions touching fleet-wide session-lock liveness, the Herdr pane-agent-state classifier, and every home-removal path) and several safety-critical verdicts rest on prime-agent's internal `dist/` JSON shapes that an upgrade can change silently, but every fix-round claim verified against that source holds and only two low-severity issues remain, so it is safe to merge with those as follow-ups. ## Testing `Ran the five test scripts this change touches — the new prime-agent harness, prime watcher-extension, session-lock ancestry and the herdr backend suite all pass; the Pi/prime TypeScript no-emit check gate-skips here because neither tsc nor the global pi-coding-agent package is installed and installing them is outside the worktree boundary, so CI owns that one. Because the machine has real prime-agent 0.7.1 and real herdr, I went past the fixtures: I launched a real prime-agent session in a temp directory, confirmed its detached daemon worker outlived its client, and watched fm_prime_agent_stop_sessions_under retire exactly that session while the captain's live session and one unrelated session stayed untouched. I fed the real inherited environment of a live prime-agent daemon worker into both the base and target fm-harness.sh: base answers "claude" (the reported live misidentification), target answers "prime-agent". In an isolated fm-herdr-lab session I ran the real prime-agent TUI in a pane — its bare ">" composer classifies "empty" on the target but "unknown" at base, which is exactly the false-fail steers were hitting — then reproduced the /quit hazard, where the reporter still claims agent: prime-agent on a login shell with PS1='> ' and the target still refuses it as a composer and reports no-agent. tmux-side classification is intentionally out of scope per the intent, and this home has no tmux, so nothing there was exercised. Evidence is CLI transcripts rather than screenshots because every surface here is shell-level; the herdr pane renders were captured as text through herdr's own read API.`
Evidence: Live teardown of a real detached prime-agent daemon session (only the target worktree's session stops) $ ps -o pid,stat,args -p 3321054 # daemon worker outlived the pane's client process 3321054 Ssl prime-agent BEFORE: [{"id":"7d92f3b43dd7","lifecycle":"live","cwd":"/home/eduard/.treehouse/fm-7bab20/1/fm"},{"id":"13171cb33bf2",...},{"id":"c32a348db616","lifecycle":"draft","cwd":"/tmp/fm-prime-e2e.fMp7f8"}] $ . bin/fm-prime-agent-lib.sh; fm_prime_agent_stop_sessions_under /tmp/fm-prime-e2e.fMp7f8 prime-agent: stopping detached session c32a348db616 bound to /tmp/fm-prime-e2e.fMp7f8 AFTER: [{"id":"7d92f3b43dd7","lifecycle":"live",...},{"id":"13171cb33bf2",...}] ```text 0.7.1 ### prime-agent / real daemon, no stubs $ ps -o pid,stat,args -p 3321054 # daemon worker outlived the pane's client process PID STAT COMMAND 3321054 Ssl prime-agent $ prime-agent list --json | jq '[.sessions[]|{id,lifecycle,cwd}]' # BEFORE teardown [{"id":"7d92f3b43dd7","lifecycle":"live","cwd":"/home/eduard/.treehouse/fm-7bab20/1/fm"},{"id":"13171cb33bf2","lifecycle":"draft","cwd":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-eduard-Dropbox-Projects-fm/ad8ca542-8c91-48e4-af74-978f07febf2b/scratchpad/prime-suspend"},{"id":"c32a348db616","lifecycle":"draft","cwd":"/tmp/fm-prime-e2e.fMp7f8"}] $ . bin/fm-prime-agent-lib.sh; fm_prime_agent_stop_sessions_under /tmp/fm-prime-e2e.fMp7f8 prime-agent: stopping detached session c32a348db616 bound to /tmp/fm-prime-e2e.fMp7f8 $ prime-agent list --json | jq '[.sessions[]|{id,lifecycle,cwd}]' # AFTER [{"id":"7d92f3b43dd7","lifecycle":"live","cwd":"/home/eduard/.treehouse/fm-7bab20/1/fm"},{"id":"13171cb33bf2","lifecycle":"draft","cwd":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-eduard-Dropbox-Projects-fm/ad8ca542-8c91-48e4-af74-978f07febf2b/scratchpad/prime-suspend"}] ```
Evidence: Harness detection under the real environment of a live prime-agent daemon worker (base vs target) relevant inherited vars (pid 2210194, prime-agent 0.7.1): CLAUDECODE=1 PI_CODING_AGENT=true PRIME_AGENT_INTERNAL_DAEMON_WORKER=1 $ /tmp/fm-harness-base.sh # base 833a9a2 (before this change) claude $ bin/fm-harness.sh # target 1894f52 (this change) prime-agent ```text ### fm-harness.sh run under the REAL environment of a live prime-agent 0.7.1 daemon worker (pid 2210194) relevant inherited vars: CLAUDECODE=1 PI_CODING_AGENT=true PRIME_AGENT_INTERNAL_DAEMON_WORKER=1 FM_PI_HARNESS= PRIME_AGENT_CODING_AGENT_DIR= $ /tmp/fm-harness-base.sh # base 833a9a2 (before this change) claude $ bin/fm-harness.sh # target 1894f52 (this change) prime-agent ```
