printf -- '--- the failure is declared on the task status log (the wake surface) ---\n'
cat "$home/state/$id.status"

banner "4. A second refused dispatch does not re-declare the unchanged terminal fact"
spawn >/dev/null 2>&1
printf -- '--- status log after a second refusal (still exactly one failed: line) ---\n'
cat "$home/state/$id.status"

banner "5. The only way past exhaustion: a deliberate, recorded --attempt-budget raise"
spawn --attempt-budget 3 | tail -2
printf -- '--- metadata: attempt 3 of raised budget 3 ---\n'
grep -E '^(attempt|attempt_budget)=' "$home/state/$id.meta"
printf -- '--- durable record: the raise is recorded, so the override is inspectable ---\n'
cat "$home/state/$id.attempt"

banner "6. Secondmates are exempt: --attempt-budget is refused on a --secondmate spawn"
FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE='' FM_HOME="$home" \
  FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$home/state" FM_DATA_OVERRIDE="$home/data" \
  FM_PROJECTS_OVERRIDE="$home/projects" FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$home/config" \
  FM_SPAWN_NO_GUARD=1 FM_BACKEND=tmux FM_FAKE_PANE_PATH="$wt" \
  PATH="$fakebin:$PATH" \
  "$ROOT/bin/fm-spawn.sh" sm-demo "$home/sm" claude --secondmate --attempt-budget 3 2>&1
printf -- '--- exit code: %s ---\n' "$?"

banner "7. There is no reset verb on the owner CLI"
FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$ROOT" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$home/state" "$ROOT/bin/fm-attempt.sh" reset "$id" 2>&1
printf -- '--- exit code: %s ---\n' "$?"

<summary>⚠️ **Review** - 3 infos</summary>

- ℹ️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:881` - bin/fm-attempt.sh deliberately defines exit code 3 for a refused retry "so a caller can tell 'this task is out of budget' from 'you called me wrong'", but its primary caller collapses it: fm-spawn's early gate runs `fm-attempt.sh check ... || exit 1`, so any automation invoking fm-spawn cannot distinguish budget exhaustion from every other spawn failure by exit status and must parse stderr. Propagating the distinct code (e.g. `|| exit $?`) would preserve the contract the constant was created for; nothing in-tree currently depends on it, so this is a nice-to-have.

The header documents refusal-recording and the declare-once design is intentional per the stated intent, and the recovery skill directs firstmate to the side-effect-free `show`, so this is a documented sharp edge rather than a defect; clarifying the usage line ("committing no increment; a refusal is recorded") would remove the trap.

This fails loudly rather than silently passing (the negative control shares the same format assumption, so drift surfaces as a red test, which matches the intent's no-silent-skip requirement), but expect a one-line touch-up when CFVC-11 lands if its formatting differs.

title: feat(bin): split task identity into role/deliverable/stage axes and rename promote to reflag
body:
## Intent

CFVC-16 fleet-side implementation, executing the captain's 2026-08-07 naming ruling. The captain framed this as COHESION work, not cosmetic terminology work. Binding constraints from the ruling: mapping-first migration, durable-state safety, red-capable verification, explicit retirement conditions, and no indefinite aliases or dual ownership left behind; verify against current HEAD before each migration step. Platform-side work (D3/D13/D19 and the platform registers) belongs to a separate task and is deliberately untouched here.

Scope delivered:
1. D10: rename the scout-to-ship operation bin/fm-promote.sh to bin/fm-reflag.sh using mapping-first migration - a bounded compatibility shim at the old name with a stated retirement condition, callers and docs migrated, and that retirement condition recorded; never an indefinite alias.
2. D16, the structural centerpiece: split task metadata kind= into three orthogonal machine-readable fields, role=crew|secondmate, deliverable=scout|ship, stage=commissioned|reflagged|delivered. The migration sequence was binding: dual-write first, deterministic backfill of existing records, migrate readers ONE AXIS AT A TIME, and retire the deprecated kind= alias only after a full proven cycle. Every consumer that branches on kind= (spawn, teardown, brief scaffolding, classification, wake ledger, recovery) was inventoried against HEAD before the first write change.
3. D17: requested_agent_role goes on the role axis, with no new conflated dimension. That field does not exist fleet-side today, so this ships as the axis plus the documented rule that role-typed facts land on it.
4. D18: the fleet's canonical vocabulary-collision registry as one owner file, seeded with every ruled disposition - AXI not renamed, the Skill senses, the qualified watcher versus Watch Register forms, promotion's two senses with the fleet verb now reflag, execution NO-CONTACT, and the qualified lifecycle forms - with pointers from where each collision bites.
5. Red-capable tests throughout, including witnessed-red coverage for dual-write, backfill determinism, each reader migration, and the alias retirement refusing stale writers.

Decisions and tradeoffs a reviewer reading only the diff would not know:

- stage=delivered is part of the captain's ruled value set but is deliberately written by no path yet. Stamping it belongs after a confirmed landing inside bin/fm-pr-merge.sh's private metadata rewrite, whose ordering, device, and single-link invariants that path owns, so wiring it there was left as a follow-up rather than bolted on beside this split. Both the library header and the registry say so explicitly so its absence is not misread as "this task did not land". This is intentional, not an oversight.

- kind= remains dual-written on purpose. The captain's ruling permits retiring it only after a full proven cycle, so this change stops short of removing it. No reader consults it any more, and a record whose alias contradicts its explicit axes is REFUSED rather than silently resolved, because either side could be the stale one and letting teardown choose between a protected ship worktree and a scratch scout worktree by luck is how unlanded work gets discarded.

- Backfill deliberately does NOT derive stage from the alias. The old field was written both by a spawn and by the scout-to-ship operation, so a record predating the split cannot distinguish a commissioned ship from a reflagged one; backfill records the lower-information value rather than inventing a fact the old field never carried.

- A real durable-state bug was found and fixed during this work: a task's metadata doubles as PR identity, and its parser refuses any unrecognized key appearing after the pr= line, which is what stops a tampered record from smuggling a second identity past an armed merge poll. The first version of the backfill appended, so the startup sweep would have invalidated exactly the records carrying a live merge watch, and the watcher would have silently stopped honoring those polls. Axis writes now land before pr= through one shared helper used by both the backfill and the reflag, and the regression pins the position rather than only the parse.

- teardown's admission release reminder was moved into bin/fm-admission-lib.sh, which already owns that policy. Its test previously reconstructed the function by parsing teardown's source with awk and eval-ing the fragment, so it broke the moment the function read a variable defined outside it - and a test that asserts implementation source is what CONTRIBUTING forbids. The reminder now takes its inputs as arguments and the test calls it directly.

- fm-brief.sh's internal kind variable became ROLE plus DELIVERABLE so the scaffold selects on the same axes the record carries. That makes --scout --secondmate a describable but impossible combination (a persistent direct report whose deliverable is a scout report), which is now explicitly refused instead of silently resolving last-flag-wins as before.

- The fleet view's type column previously rendered the deprecated field and could only show one of the three facts a row carries. It now renders role/deliverable and appends the stage when it is not the spawn default, so a reflagged ship is visible as one.

- Several test fixtures assemble a partial bin/ from copies or symlinks of individual scripts; the new library had to be carried into those fixtures or the entry point they exercise dies looking for it.

Verification: full changed-file sweep of 74 suites, 1563 passing assertions. Nine failing assertions remain, and each was verified pre-existing by running the same suite against a pristine copy of the base commit: Pi and node ESM .ts loader failures, tmux unavailability in this sandbox, a session-start MISSING diagnostic, a tmux agent-liveness classification, a launch-template ghost-text assertion, a watcher-lock restart attach, and a secondmate-harness case that emits the worktree-tangle banner whenever the suite runs from any task branch.

## What Changed

- Split the task-metadata `kind=` field into three orthogonal axes — `role=crew|secondmate`, `deliverable=scout|ship`, `stage=commissioned|reflagged|delivered` — with dual-write plus deterministic backfill (axis writes land before `pr=` via a shared helper so live merge-watch records keep their PR identity), readers migrated one axis at a time across spawn, teardown, brief scaffolding, classification, wake ledger, and recovery, contradictory alias/axis records refused rather than silently resolved, the v1 wire surfaces dual-carrying `kind` beside the new axes, and the fleet view rendering the identity axes. Verified by a new 9-case migration-contract suite (`tests/fm-task-axis.test.sh`) plus a full 74-suite changed-file sweep.
- Renamed the scout-to-ship operation `bin/fm-promote.sh` to `bin/fm-reflag.sh` with an atomic single-commit record rewrite (hardened by the pipeline's review pass), a bounded compatibility shim at the old name with a recorded retirement condition, and callers, briefs, and docs migrated; seeded the fleet's canonical vocabulary-collision registry (`docs/vocabulary-collisions.md`) with every ruled disposition, including that `stage=delivered` is deliberately written by no path yet.
- The branch also carries 46 fork-trunk commits not yet on origin/main — the fleet launcher menu and `fm-launch-lib.sh`, model registry with the zero-budget spawn gate, fleet admission control, wake-outcome ledger, LoopSpec schema and register, research-approved-work scanner, remote secondmate infrastructure, worktree guard, and a series of supervision and merge-safety fixes — which the pipeline's rebase stage flagged as bundled until main is pushed to origin.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The fix round cleanly resolved all six prior findings per the given guidance - atomic single-commit reflag rewrite, dead helper removed, witnessed-red refusal coverage added, and additive dual-carry of the deprecated alias on both v1 wire surfaces with explicit recorded retirement conditions - leaving a disciplined, well-tested migration with no remaining material issues.

## Testing

Ran the new task-axis suite plus seven touched/reader suites (all green), then demonstrated the migration end-to-end with the real CLIs in a scratch home — backfill sweep with pr=-safe insertion, shim forwarding with retirement marker, reflag dual-write, contradictory-identity refusals in reflag/teardown/sweep, fleet-view Identity rendering, v1 wire dual-carry, and the brief flag-combination refusal — and confirmed via a temporary fault injection that the PR-identity regression is red-capable; no visual artifacts because every end-user surface here is a terminal CLI, captured as transcripts.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end demo of the CFVC-16 fleet-side identity-axis migration.
# Drives the real CLIs against a scratch home the way a firstmate session would.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

  display-message) case "$*" in *pane_current_command*) printf 'codex\n' ;; *) printf '%%1\n' ;; esac ;;

esac
exit 0
SH
cat > "$DEMO/fakebin/no-mistakes" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
exit 0
SH

export PATH="$DEMO/fakebin:$PATH"
export FM_HOME="$HOME_DIR" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$HOME_DIR/state" \
  FM_DATA_OVERRIDE="$HOME_DIR/data" FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$HOME_DIR/config"
# Same exemption tests/lib.sh uses: this demo drives the real fleet scripts from
# a no-mistakes gate worktree, which the gate-lifecycle guard would refuse.
export FM_GATE_REFUSE_BYPASS=1

say() { printf '\n$ %s\n' "$*"; }

printf '### 1. A home full of PRE-SPLIT records: only the deprecated kind= field, no axes.\n'
cat > "$HOME_DIR/state/old-scout.meta" <<EOF
window=firstmate:fm-old-scout
kind=scout

EOF

window=firstmate:fm-polled-ship
kind=ship
worktree=$HOME_DIR/projects/polled-ship-wt

pr_head=$sha
EOF
mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR/projects/stale-wt" "$HOME_DIR/projects/beta"
cat > "$HOME_DIR/state/stale-writer.meta" <<EOF
window=firstmate:fm-stale-writer
endpoint_task_id=stale-writer
kind=ship
deliverable=scout
worktree=$HOME_DIR/projects/stale-wt
project=$HOME_DIR/projects/beta
EOF
cat > "$HOME_DIR/state/mate.meta" <<EOF
window=firstmate:fm-mate
kind=secondmate
EOF
for f in old-scout polled-ship stale-writer; do
  printf -- '--- state/%s.meta ---\n' "$f"; cat "$HOME_DIR/state/$f.meta"
done

printf '\n### 2. Session-start backfill sweep (bin/fm-bootstrap.sh) converges old records\n'
printf '###    and REFUSES the record whose alias contradicts its axes.\n'
say 'bin/fm-bootstrap.sh   (task-axis lines of its report)'
"$ROOT/bin/fm-bootstrap.sh" 2>&1 | grep -i 'axis' || true

printf '\n--- state/old-scout.meta after the sweep (axes derived from kind=scout) ---\n'
cat "$HOME_DIR/state/old-scout.meta"
printf -- '--- state/polled-ship.meta after the sweep (axes land BEFORE pr=, identity intact) ---\n'
cat "$HOME_DIR/state/polled-ship.meta"
printf -- '--- state/stale-writer.meta after the sweep (REFUSED: left untouched) ---\n'
cat "$HOME_DIR/state/stale-writer.meta"

printf '\n### 3. Reflag the scout through the DEPRECATED name bin/fm-promote.sh:\n'
printf '###    the bounded shim warns, forwards to bin/fm-reflag.sh, and records its use.\n'
say 'bin/fm-promote.sh old-scout --mode no-mistakes --yolo on'
"$ROOT/bin/fm-promote.sh" old-scout --mode no-mistakes --yolo on 2>&1
printf -- '--- state/old-scout.meta after the reflag (dual-written alias + moved axes) ---\n'
cat "$HOME_DIR/state/old-scout.meta"
printf -- '--- state/.reflag-shim-used (evidence for the shim retirement condition) ---\n'
cat "$HOME_DIR/state/.reflag-shim-used"

printf '\n### 4. A contradictory record is REFUSED, never resolved by luck.\n'
say 'bin/fm-reflag.sh stale-writer --mode no-mistakes --yolo on'
"$ROOT/bin/fm-reflag.sh" stale-writer --mode no-mistakes --yolo on 2>&1
printf 'exit status: %s\n' "$?"
say 'bin/fm-teardown.sh stale-writer'
"$ROOT/bin/fm-teardown.sh" stale-writer 2>&1 | tail -2
printf 'teardown left the record in place: %s\n' "$(test -f "$HOME_DIR/state/stale-writer.meta" && echo yes || echo NO)"

printf '\n### 5. The fleet view now renders the identity axes; a reflagged ship is visible as one.\n'

The intent's binding red-capable-verification constraint covers the other migration steps thoroughly; this is the one new user-visible refusal without a witnessed-red assertion.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-admission.sh:315` - bin/fm-admission.sh:315 still consumes the deprecated task-identity alias: the active_workers.count evidence detail groups snapshot tasks by `.kind // "crewmate"`. It works during the dual-write window because fm-fleet-snapshot.sh still emits kind on task rows, but the recorded retirement condition in docs/vocabulary-collisions.md is "stop writing kind=, and drop it from the fleet snapshot's task rows" - at which point this detail silently degrades to a single "crewmate=N" bucket. The site is not listed in the registry row's "where it bites" pointers and fm-admission.sh was not touched by this change, so the retirement step could miss it. Decide whether to migrate it to role/deliverable now (which changes the recorded admission evidence string) or add it to the registry's pointers so the retirement step finds it.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:1534` - Two versioned JSON surfaces changed field names without a schema-tag bump: fm-fleet-snapshot.v1's scout_reports[] renamed `kind` to `deliverable` (bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:1534) and dropped the old fallback to the backlog record's kind (report_deliverable at line 1525 vs the previous report_kind), and fm-bearings.v1's in_flight rows replaced `kind` with `role`/`deliverable`. All in-repo consumers were migrated in lockstep and tasks[] additively keeps kind beside the new axes, but any external consumer keying on the renamed fields under the unchanged v1 tags breaks silently (open issue #2007 shows external interest in fm-fleet-snapshot.v1). The fallback drop also relabels a torn-down task's surviving report as deliverable=scout where the old code could report the backlog row's kind - defensible since backlog kind is a different vocabulary (captain/program), but worth confirming it was weighed. If the renames are the intended migration posture, no code change is needed - consider noting the wire-format change in the registry row's retirement plan.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:467` - bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh calls fm_task_role/fm_task_deliverable/fm_task_stage (lines 467-469) but never sources bin/fm-task-axis-lib.sh itself - it works only because fm-ff-lib.sh (sourced at line 143 for an unrelated helper) pulls the axis lib in transitively. Every other consumer sources it explicitly with a shellcheck directive. If the ff-lib dependency is ever dropped or refactored, the axis calls fail inside command substitutions and every task row silently emits empty role/deliverable/stage. Relatedly, several script headers still describe identity selection via kind= (bin/fm-teardown.sh:32/57/66, bin/fm-spawn.sh:133-135, bin/fm-send.sh:28, bin/fm-config-push.sh:35, bin/fm-update.sh:67, bin/fm-ff-lib.sh:414) - accurate during the dual-write window but pointing future writers at the deprecated field.

title: feat: roll out the feature-first focused validation operating model
body:
## Intent Implement the approved feature-first validation operating model in Firstmate's shared tracked surface. Acceptance criteria: - Make a mapped focused validation slice the default preflight before a full review, with a clear stop rule when the changed surface is isolated and proven. - Encode that independent workers have no artificial concurrency cap, while preserving explicit serialization for the same branch or head, mutable database, fixed port or compose project, production or edge state, shared gate daemon, and shared tracked surface. - Encode that every UI-touching ship receives a separate Luna visual-review worker, while bounded non-visual implementation and test work defaults to DeepSeek Flash. - Retain per-run test isolation indefinitely and replace the warm-stack recommendation with isolation-preserving optimizations such as deterministic fixtures, immutable dependency or image caches, focused health checks, and unique writable test artifacts. - Keep the full no-mistakes review for production-facing, mixed, security-sensitive, edge, deployment, and uncertain work, and document scheduling around daemon-update windows rather than removing that gate. - Preserve the approved ESIM boundary: direct-PR with focused validation is limited to internal tooling, automation, scripts, and operator process; product-facing or uncertain changes remain on the full path. - Place each rule in its authoritative owner rather than duplicating contracts across AGENTS.md, skills, briefs, and docs. - Add or update executable regression coverage for any changed script or enforceable behavior, following firstmate-coding-guidelines. - Run the relevant focused tests, documentation audience checks, shell lint, and repository validation before handing the branch to the no-mistakes pipeline. Constraints: - Load firstmate-coding-guidelines before editing shared tracked material. - Do not modify captain-private config files, projects/, or unrelated operational policy. - Do not add a visual review worker for this non-UI policy task. - Keep all implementation and evidence in this isolated Firstmate worktree and commit the result on the task branch. ## What Changed - Adds `.agents/skills/focused-validation/SKILL.md` as the single procedure owner for the feature-first validation model (mapped focused-validation slice, isolated-and-proven stop rule, internal-only fast-path boundary, isolation-preserving optimizations) and makes `AGENTS.md` section 7 the always-loaded contract: every ship runs a mapped preflight with recorded timing, direct-PR stays limited to internal-only work, the full no-mistakes review remains the gate for product-facing, mixed, security-sensitive, edge, deployment, and uncertain work, daemon-update windows are avoided for scheduling, and UI-touching ships get a separate vision-capable (Luna) visual-review worker while bounded non-visual work defaults to DeepSeek Flash. - `bin/fm-brief.sh` now emits a shared `# Focused validation` section (worker-facing step, `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed` / `tests/.test.sh` file-to-test-family map, stop rule, and skill pointer) in every ship brief for all three delivery modes, with each mode's definition-of-done requiring the slice and its timing before completion; `bin/fm-project-mode.sh`, `.agents/skills/project-management/SKILL.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/examples/crew-dispatch.json` were updated to match the new boundary and dispatch semantics. - Adds regression coverage in `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` asserting the focused-validation section, stop rule, map, and skill pointer appear in no-mistakes, direct-PR, and local-only briefs (with mode-specific DOD rules) and never in scout briefs, and registers the new skill in `docs/documentation-audiences.json`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a policy-documentation and brief-scaffold rollout with the round-1 warning fixed exactly per the user's option-B instruction (boundary deferred to the authoritative skill, six-category list preserved in AGENTS.md and the skill), with matching regression coverage and no runtime code paths altered beyond generated brief text. ## Testing Ran the two focused test files covering the changed executable surface (tests/fm-brief.test.sh with the new preflight test, and tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh exercising the real audience-check consumer), plus the dispatch-profile plumbing test; all pass. Demonstrated end-to-end by generating real ship briefs in all three delivery modes (evidence: brief-directpr.md, generated-briefs-modes.txt), running bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed against this branch's base to show the mapped slice selecting the exact test families, confirming the new skill's frontmatter loads in the real harness consumer, parsing crew-dispatch.json, and grepping for stale warm-stack or contradictory text (none found). Worktree left clean; no failures or missing evidence.
Evidence: Generated direct-PR ship brief with focused-validation section and DOD ```text You are a crewmate: an autonomous worker agent managed by firstmate. Work on your own; do not wait for a human. # Task {TASK} # Herdr lifecycle declaration - NOT ENABLED **HARD SAFETY GATE:** this scaffold cannot inspect the task text that replaces `{TASK}` later. If the task will start, stop, delete, restart, profile, or otherwise drive Herdr lifecycle behavior, stop and regenerate the brief with `--herdr-lab` before dispatch. Do not add Herdr lifecycle commands to this unguarded brief by hand. # Setup You are in a disposable git worktree of some-proj, at a detached HEAD on a clean default branch. **Verify isolation before anything else.** Run `pwd -P` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; both must resolve to the disposable task worktree you were launched in, such as a treehouse pool path or an Orca-managed worktree, not the primary checkout firstmate operates from. The path check is authoritative: `git rev-parse --git-dir` and `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` can help inspect the repo, but they do not prove you are outside the primary checkout. If the top-level path is the primary checkout or not the worktree you were launched in, STOP - do not branch or commit here - append `blocked: launched in primary checkout, not an isolated worktree` to the status file and stop. 1. First action: create your branch: `git checkout -b fm/demo-directpr` # Rules 1. Never push to the default branch (push only your `fm/demo-directpr` branch). Never merge a PR. 2. Stay inside this worktree; modify nothing outside it. 3. Use gh-axi for GitHub operations and chrome-devtools-axi for browser operations. 4. Report status by appending one line: `echo "{state}: {one short line}" >> '/tmp/fv-demo-home.SUKw6C/state/demo-directpr.status'` States: working, needs-decision, blocked, paused, done, failed. Each append wakes firstmate, so report sparingly: only phase changes a supervisor would act on (setup done, bug reproduced, fix implemented, validation passed) and the needs-decision/blocked/paused/done/failed states. No step-by-step FYI progress lines; firstmate reads your pane for that. A mid-task `working:` line (including setup complete) is nonterminal: do not end the turn after it; continue the same stage until a defined `done:` gate under Definition of done. Use `paused: {why}` - distinct from `blocked:` - ONLY when you are deliberately idling on a known external wait you expect to clear on its own (an upstream release, a rate-limit reset, a scheduled window): firstmate then leaves your idle pane alone and rechecks it on a long cadence instead of treating it as a possible wedge. Use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need help. 5. If you hit the same obstacle twice, append `blocked: {why}` and stop; firstmate will help. 6. If a decision belongs above the implementation worker (product choices, destructive actions, ask-user findings), append `needs-decision: {summary of options}` and stop. Firstmate will apply the configured authority and reply with the decision. A decision or blocker you opened stays open until a `resolved` line carrying its exact key lands; a later `done:` or `working:` line never closes it, even when the answer is what started that work. Firstmate's reply normally writes that closing line at answer time; when a blocker or wait clears WITHOUT a firstmate reply, append `resolved: {how it cleared}` yourself (same `[key=]` if you opened it with one) as you resume. 7. Never stop, restart, or update the shared `no-mistakes` daemon - it is one instance serving every lane/home, so restarting it kills other lanes' in-flight pipeline runs. On ANY no-mistakes daemon error, append `blocked: {the daemon error}` and stop; only firstmate manages the daemon. # Project memory If `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` already exists, or if this task produced durable project-intrinsic knowledge, run `/home/andrzej/.no-mistakes/worktrees/f17d52d226fc/01KZKA5M1N4KWHX693H5BVA048/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh .` in the worktree. Record only project knowledge useful to almost every future session. For anything the codebase already shows, prefer a pointer to the authoritative file, command, or doc over copying the detail. If you touch a project `AGENTS.md` that lacks `## Maintaining this file`, add that short self-governance section from `/home/andrzej/.no-mistakes/worktrees/f17d52d226fc/01KZKA5M1N4KWHX693H5BVA048/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh` in the same pass. Keep it proportionate: skip `AGENTS.md` edits for trivial tasks that produced no durable project knowledge. # Focused validation Run the mapped focused validation slice for this change before reporting done, and record its timing. Map the touched files to the project's test surface: for firstmate-repo tasks run `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed` from the worktree root or the touched `tests/.test.sh` scripts; for other projects use the focused test families that project's `AGENTS.md` names. The stop rule is an isolated and proven surface: the touched files resolve to one module and one test family, no shared middleware, config, deploy, or edge file, no external mutation, and existing focused tests cover the module and pass. An isolated and proven surface qualifies for the fast path only for `direct-PR` work inside the internal-only boundary; work outside that boundary still climbs to the full review. Follow `/home/andrzej/.no-mistakes/worktrees/f17d52d226fc/01KZKA5M1N4KWHX693H5BVA048/.agents/skills/focused-validation/SKILL.md` for the internal-only boundary, the ladder, the isolation proof, and the file-to-test-family map. # Definition of done Delivery contract: mode=direct-PR This task ships **direct-PR**: you raise the PR yourself, without the no-mistakes pipeline. The task is complete only when committed on your branch. Run the mapped focused validation slice from the Focused validation section and record its timing before pushing; it is the review for this fast path. If the changed surface is not isolated and proven under the stop rule, or the slice fails, fix within the task - or append `needs-decision` instead of pushing when the surface turns out to fall outside the internal-only boundary defined in `/home/andrzej/.no-mistakes/worktrees/f17d52d226fc/01KZKA5M1N4KWHX693H5BVA048/.agents/skills/focused-validation/SKILL.md`. When it is implemented and committed, push your branch and open a PR with `gh-axi`, then append `done: PR {url}` to the status file and stop. Do NOT run /no-mistakes. The configured merge authority decides whether to merge the PR; firstmate relays the outcome. ```
Evidence: no-mistakes and local-only DOD preflight rules + scout exclusion ```text === no-mistakes DOD === Delivery contract: mode=no-mistakes The task is complete only when committed on your branch. Run the mapped focused validation slice from the Focused validation section and record its timing before appending `done: {summary}`; a slice that fails must be fixed before the pipeline starts. When you believe it is complete, append `done: {summary}` to the status file and stop. Firstmate will then instruct you to run /no-mistakes to validate and ship a PR. === local-only DOD === Delivery contract: mode=local-only This task ships **local-only**: no remote, no PR, no pipeline. The task is complete only when committed on your branch `fm/demo-localonly`. Do NOT push, do NOT open a PR, do NOT merge. Run the mapped focused validation slice from the Focused validation section and record its timing before appending `done: ready in branch`. Keep your branch a clean fast-forward onto the current default branch - if `main` has advanced, rebase onto it so the eventual merge stays a fast-forward. When it is implemented and committed, append `done: ready in branch fm/demo-localonly` to the status file and stop. The configured merge authority approves the ready branch, then firstmate merges it into local `main` through the guarded fast-forward path. === scout: section absence === 0 0 (absent, expected) ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 3 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:367` - The direct-PR DOD's escalation clause and the brief's Focused validation section (line 428) name only "product-facing, mixed, or uncertain" as surfaces that must leave the fast path, while the accepted boundary (AGENTS.md:277, AGENTS.md:333, focused-validation SKILL.md:43) also requires the full no-mistakes review for security-sensitive, edge, and deployment work. A direct-PR worker whose surface turns out security-sensitive, edge, or deployment gets no escalation instruction — the DOD says to "fix within the task" and push, so a task misclassified at intake can ship without the full review the intent requires; the full list is only one pointer hop away in the skill, not in the operative DOD. Recommend naming the full six-category boundary in the DOD escalation clause (or explicitly deferring the list there). - ℹ️ `docs/examples/crew-dispatch.json:7` - The example dispatch profiles name concrete model IDs (opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna at line 7/24/31, opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash at line 16) that are not verified against any in-repo harness catalog, and the third rule's why (line 27) asserts "Sol is explicit-only, never automatic" without defining Sol anywhere in the repository. Staleness is hedged in the why text ("verify the current model name in the harness catalog at dispatch") and by AGENTS.md:261, and the example is not consumed by bootstrap validation, so a stale copy fails closed at the real config with a CREW_DISPATCH invalid error rather than silently dispatching. Informational. - ℹ️ `AGENTS.md:502` - Section 11 now claims every ship brief carries the scaffolded focused-validation preflight section, but scout-promoted ships keep their scout brief (bin/fm-promote.sh only rewrites task meta; it never re-scaffolds the brief), and the promotion follow-up message template at bin/fm-promote.sh:125 does not mention the preflight. The always-loaded AGENTS.md section 7 requirement still covers firstmate when composing the steer, so the requirement is not lost, but the scaffolded reminder channel is absent on the promotion path; consider mentioning the mapped preflight in the promote follow-up template. 🔧 Fix: Defer brief escalation boundary to focused-validation skill ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-brief.test.sh` - full file incl. new test_focused_validation_preflight_in_ship_briefs (section present in all 3 ship modes, timing + map + stop rule + skill pointer, mode-specific DOD rules, scout brief excludes section, no primary-checkout path leak); 21 checks pass - `bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` - real fm-doc-audience-check.sh consumer accepts docs/documentation-audiences.json with the new .agents/skills/focused-validation/SKILL.md entry; all pass - `bash tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh` - harness profile plumbing (pi receives --model/--thinking max; opencode model flags) underpinning the Luna/DeepSeek Flash example rules; all pass - End-to-end brief generation: `bin/fm-brief.sh <id> some-proj --mode direct-PR|no-mistakes|local-only` and `--scout` under a demo FM_HOME - captured real generated brief sections as evidence (direct-PR DOD: preflight is 'the review for this fast path' with needs-decision escalation; no-mistakes DOD: slice must pass 'before the pipeline starts'; local-only DOD: preflight before `done: ready in branch`; scout brief has no section) - `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed --base 74230fcd --list` - the mapped focused slice resolves this branch's diff to tests/fm-brief.test.sh, tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh, and related families (the exact families run here) - `Skill frontmatter validated by the real consumer: the pi harness parsed .agents/skills/focused-validation/SKILL.md at session start and exposed it as an available skill with its description (name/user-invocable/metadata.internal correct)` - `python3 json.load` on docs/examples/crew-dispatch.json - valid JSON; rules encode the separate Luna visual-review worker for UI-touching ships and DeepSeek Flash default for bounded non-visual work - `Repo-wide grep: no stale warm-stack recommendation anywhere; AGENTS.md section 7 text encodes the serialization list (same branch/head, mutable DB, fixed port/compose, prod/edge state, shared gate daemon, shared tracked surface), no-artificial-cap dispatch, internal-only ESIM boundary, and daemon-update-window scheduling rule`
⚠️ **Document** - 2 infos - ℹ️ `docs/examples/crew-dispatch.json:31` - The big-ambiguous-work rule's `why` ends with "Sol is explicit-only, never automatic", but no profile in the file names a Sol model and neither AGENTS.md section 7 nor the Luna/DeepSeek Flash routing contract mentions it; it reads as fleet-specific shorthand with no owner or pointer, so a future session cannot tell whether it is load-bearing guidance or a leftover note. This is fresh content of the change itself, not a fact the change made stale, so I left it untouched per scope discipline. - ℹ️ `.agents/skills/focused-validation/SKILL.md:27` - The skill says the changed-file map is "owned by that script's header", while bin/fm-test-run.sh's header declares ownership and the map implementation lives in families_for_changed_path() in the body; harmless shorthand, not stale, left as-is.

title: fix(bin): reconcile Herdr-authoritative idle against stale Firstmate busy records
body:
## Intent Fix Firstmate supervision so a Herdr-backed Pi worker that has actually settled idle cannot stay falsely classified as working because an older Firstmate Pi busy record is stuck on agent-start, and make Pi interactive question/approval waits visible. Root cause (reproduced live on Pi 0.84.1 + Herdr 0.8.0, Pi integration v8): on /reload or another session replacement Pi emits session_shutdown then session_start(reason=reload) with ctx.isIdle() already true and NO paired agent_settled. The generated per-task Pi extension had no session_start handler, so a reload landing while the record was busy left it permanently stale while herdr:pi recovered to idle via its own session_start reconciliation. Writer fix (bin/fm-spawn.sh generated Pi extension): reconcile busy-state from ctx.isIdle() on any non-startup session_start (startup keeps the launch-brief busy seed, matching the arm); serialize every apply through one in-process queue so close-together events cannot be applied out of order (handlers still return an awaitable promise); wrap the ONE shared ctx.ui object to emit herdr:blocked with a non-sensitive method-name label around any dialog (confirm/select/input/editor/custom, incl MCP approval/elicitation). Pi 0.84.1 exposes no generic dialog event and nothing emits herdr:blocked, so ctx.ui wrapping is the strongest safe local detection; detection/relay only, the question is never answered, and title/body/args never leak. Reader fix (defense in depth, one owner each): fm_backend_herdr_authoritative_state (bin/backends/herdr.sh) exposes herdr status only from a verified full-lifecycle integration (screen_detection_skipped plus a herdr: lifecycle source), never screen detection; fm_backend_authoritative_state dispatches it (bin/fm-backend.sh). fm_busy_classify (bin/fm-busy-lib.sh) returns a deterministic conflict verdict when a valid busy record is contradicted by an authoritative live idle, never plain busy - no fixed busy TTL, and a long foreground tool (authoritative working) never becomes a false conflict. fm-crew-state.sh maps the conflict: reconcile against the task's terminal/external-wait status, else report incomplete-idle so supervision continues/recovers it through the existing surface machinery; blocked stays in the transition-policy owner (fm-transition-lib.sh). Deliberate decisions/constraints: keep every contract in its existing owner (no new state machine, skill, daemon, or control plane); preserve tmux/cmux/zellij/Orca/secondmate-idle/paused/blocked/long-foreground-tool/missing-integration/screen-detection behavior (all non-herdr backends return unknown -> unchanged); do not make the watcher invent work or send prompts; the ctx.ui wrapper is monkey-patching a live shared object from our own extension (not node_modules) and is fully defensive so it can never break a dialog. Added executable-interface regression tests (no source-byte assertions) for the stale-busy vs authoritative-idle incident, authoritative working, screen-detected idle, missing integration, terminal/no-terminal reconciliation, session_start reload/startup reconciliation, and the ctx.ui blocked wrapper (nested, cancel, throw, idempotent, redaction). Updated docs/herdr-backend.md and docs/verification/supervision.md. Verified in a named non-default Herdr lab with the live default fleet untouched. This is a reviewed PR only - do not merge. ## What Changed - Generated Pi extension (`bin/fm-spawn.sh`) now reconciles busy-state from `ctx.isIdle()` on any non-startup `session_start` (startup keeps the launch-brief busy seed), serializes every handler apply through one in-process queue so close-together events cannot be applied out of order, and wraps the shared `ctx.ui` object to emit `herdr:blocked` with a non-sensitive method-name label around each dialog (confirm/select/input/editor/custom, incl. MCP approval/elicitation) — detection/relay only, never answering. - Reader-side defense in depth: `fm_backend_herdr_authoritative_state` (`bin/backends/herdr.sh`) exposes herdr idle only from a verified full-lifecycle integration and never from screen detection, dispatched via `fm_backend_authoritative_state` (`bin/fm-backend.sh`); `fm_busy_classify` (`bin/fm-busy-lib.sh`) returns a deterministic `conflict` verdict when a valid busy record is contradicted by an authoritative live idle; `fm-crew-state.sh` maps `conflict` to reconcile against terminal/external-wait status or report incomplete-idle; `fm-control.sh` treats `conflict` like `busy` for the `do_exit` pre-exit interrupt. - Added executable-interface regression tests for the stale-busy-vs-authoritative-idle incident, session_start reload/startup reconciliation, and the `ctx.ui` blocked wrapper, and updated `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/herdr-backend.md`, and `docs/verification/supervision.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The only delta since the prior review is a one-line, precisely-scoped fix that makes do_exit treat the new conflict verdict like busy for the pre-exit interrupt (resolving the sole round-1 finding) plus matching regression coverage, and the rest of the branch was already reviewed as solid and intent-conforming. ## Testing Baseline: ran the five targeted regression suites that own this change (fm-busy-state, fm-busy-adapter-wiring, fm-crew-state, fm-backend-herdr, fm-control) — all green. Since passing tests alone are not sufficient evidence, I additionally authored and ran a product-level CLI demonstration that drives the actual generated Pi extension and the real classifier/backend chain end-to-end, reproducing the Pi 0.84.1 /reload incident and capturing the operator-visible verdicts: a stale busy record reconciles to `idle pi-ext` on reload-idle, stays `busy` on startup, the reader chain emits `conflict herdr-idle-stale-busy` for a verified live idle while screen-detected idle stays `unknown`, and the ctx.ui wrapper emits herdr:blocked with only the method label (LEAKED=false). This is a backend/shell supervision change with no rendered UI surface, so a CLI transcript (not a screenshot) is the correct reviewer-visible artifact. title: fix(paired-review): resolve pair roles by stable identity, not stale pane ids
body:
## Problem

A live driver/navigator pair could not be composed or recomposed: `fm-pair-compose.sh` refused with `reciprocal adjacency` even when both roles were live, correctly labelled, and adjacent.

Two defects, both in how the coordinator read Herdr:

1. **Pane ids are positional and are reassigned on every move.** Herdr's own `pane move` response carries `previous_pane_id` alongside the new `pane`. The coordinator took `herdr_pane_id` from task metadata and carried it through its own workspace and split moves, so every later check ran against an id that no longer named any pane.

2. **The reciprocal check read the wrong field.** `pane neighbor` returns the *queried* pane in `pane_id` and the adjacent pane in `neighbor_pane_id`. The extraction was `.result.pane.pane_id // .result.neighbor.pane_id`, which resolves to the query itself, so each pane was compared against itself and adjacency could never hold — independently of any move.

Verified read-only against the running Herdr session and a live pair (`w5K:p1` driver, `w5K:p2` navigator, same tab, genuinely adjacent):

```
$ herdr pane neighbor --direction right --pane w5K:p1
{"result":{"neighbor":{"direction":"right","neighbor_pane_id":"w5K:p2","pane_id":"w5K:p1",...}}}

old expression -> w5K:p1   (the query; compared against itself -> refusal)
new expression -> w5K:p2   (the true neighbour)
```

## Fix

A role's stable identity is its registered agent name (`<pair-id>-driver`, `<pair-id>-navigator`) bound to that role's isolated copy. Composition and the new `recover` subcommand both resolve the role's *current* pane, workspace, and tab from Herdr's own agent inventory under that identity, and stored pane ids are treated as hints only.

- `pair_resolve_role` resolves exactly one live agent per role and proves it sits in the expected isolated copy before any pane, workspace, or tab is used. Missing, duplicated, or copy-mismatched identity returns non-zero rather than guessing. Before composition publishes the role names, the copy alone is the identity, and an ambiguous copy refuses.
- `pair_verify_topology` proves both roles distinct, in one workspace and tab, and reciprocal neighbours (now reading `neighbor_pane_id`), and names the failed invariant otherwise. A topology generation is recorded only after it returns.
- `recover <recovery.json>` re-verifies a live pair after Herdr moves a pane and appends the next topology generation. An unchanged topology is reported rather than appended twice; any refusal leaves the recorded topology and the live pair untouched.
- Composition re-resolves each role after each of its own moves, so its moves reassigning pane ids is no longer a failure.

`fm-send` delivery semantics are untouched: it remains the only pair signal path, and Herdr is still read for topology only, never used to inject text.

## Tests

The fake Herdr in `tests/fm-pair-compose.test.sh` encoded the same wrong response shapes as the helper, which is exactly why this defect passed CI. It now models the real CLI: pane ids reassigned on every move, `neighbor_pane_id` distinct from the queried pane, agent names as the stable identity, and an unrelated agent present in the session so resolution has to discriminate.

New coverage:

- Published topology records the panes the roles occupy now, not the launch ids.
- A stale recorded pane id does not refuse a live, adjacent pair.
- A moved pair is recovered from role identity into a new generation with the new panes.
- Recovery is idempotent — an unchanged topology appends nothing.
- Recovery refuses, records no generation, and leaves the evidence byte-identical on a copy-mismatched, missing, duplicated, or split-tab role identity; a restored endpoint then recovers normally.
- Composition refuses on duplicated, lost, and copy-drifted role identity, and no failing scenario records a topology generation or releases the barrier.

Confirmed non-vacuous: the new suite fails against the pre-fix helper.

## Validation

```
bash tests/fm-pair-compose.test.sh            ok
bash tests/fm-temporary-supervisor.test.sh    ok  (other custom-skills coverage)
bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh ok
bin/fm-lint.sh                                clean
bin/fm-lint.sh custom-skills/paired-review/fm-pair-compose.sh   clean
bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh                  ok surfaces=123 local_links=284
```

The helper had 12 pre-existing SC2016 findings (deliberate Markdown code spans and jq variables in single-quoted strings); three narrow directives make the changed script shellcheck-clean without a blunt file-scope suppression.

## Notes

- `custom-skills/**` is outside `bin/fm-lint.sh`'s canonical CI set, so this helper is only linted when passed explicitly. Widening that set touches the lint owner and was left out of scope.
- Copy proof relies on Herdr's `foreground_cwd` (the pane's `cwd` is the project directory, not the role copy). If that field were ever unavailable, composition refuses with a named invariant rather than proceeding on an unproven identity — the intended fail-safe direction.
- The live pair `dms-workspaces-autoledgers-sync-build` was recovered manually and is untouched here; no existing pair is mutated or cleaned up by this change.

title: feat(bin): bake validation ladder into no-mistakes DOD scaffold
body:
## Intent

Implement post-mortem proposal P4, captain-authorized verbatim: bake the captain's standing validation ladder into bin/fm-brief.sh's no-mistakes Definition-of-done scaffold so task briefs stop hand-paraphrasing it and can no longer drop words from it. The exact text and location are specified in data/ladder-local-e2e-postmortem/report.md section P4: the five-bullet '## Validation ladder (captain standing policy — part of definition of done)' block must be inserted into the DOD heredoc of the no-mistakes mode branch, after the 'Delivery contract: mode=no-mistakes' line, VERBATIM as the report specifies — rewording is explicitly forbidden. The em dashes inside the block are part of the captain-authorized verbatim text and are deliberate; the repo's plain-dash style rule governs tracked Markdown prose, and this block lives in a shell heredoc reproducing authorized text exactly. The ladder is no-mistakes-mode policy only: scout, direct-PR, and local-only scaffolds must NOT carry it. Also required: update the script's usage header where it describes the DOD contents (done as a short fixed-block note near the mode list), keep shellcheck clean per bin/fm-lint.sh (verified locally with the pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0), and extend the colocated tests/fm-brief.test.sh to assert the ladder block's presence in a generated no-mistakes brief and its absence in scout and direct-PR scaffolds (absence in local-only is additionally asserted for the same reason). Task briefs may still add surface-specific scenarios on top; they just no longer carry the ladder itself. Contribution path: this home's origin is the upstream template that cannot be pushed to directly - the fork flow per CONTRIBUTING.md is in use (no-mistakes init --fork-url, push through the gate), and the pipeline opens the cross-repo PR against the upstream repo; the PR then awaits upstream review, which is expected.

## What Changed

- Bake the captain-authorized five-bullet validation ladder verbatim into the no-mistakes Definition-of-done scaffold after the delivery-contract line.
- Document the fixed ladder in the usage header and test its presence in no-mistakes briefs and absence from scout, direct-PR, and local-only scaffolds.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is bounded and satisfies the requested no-mistakes-only verbatim ladder insertion with coverage for its presence and absence in other scaffolds.

## Testing

The focused behavior test and end-user CLI scaffold checks succeeded. Evidence shows the verbatim ladder appears only in no-mistakes briefs and is absent from direct-PR, local-only, and scout briefs; the worktree stayed clean. ShellCheck was not rerun because this prompt explicitly prohibited linters/static analysis.

2. Run `no-mistakes doctor`; if it reports the repo is not initialized here, run `no-mistakes init`.

# Rules
1. Never push to the default branch. Never merge a PR.
2. Stay inside this worktree; modify nothing outside it.
3. Use gh-axi for GitHub operations and chrome-devtools-axi for browser operations.
4. Report status by appending one line:
   `echo "{state}: {one short line}" >> '/var/folders/14/9jywyxlx31v7rrm2dz9b7j6r0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZKN03FC22PJ35VRZJV8EFFS/brief-home/state/evidence-no-mistakes.status'`

title: feat: expand autonomous fleet supervision and delivery
body:
## Intent

Build the mechanism that wakes firstmate to autonomously refill fleet capacity. Twice this week the captain returned to an under-capacity fleet: workers finished, finished work parked, and the ready queue sat undispatched all night because nothing structurally forced a refill. The fix: make the watcher's heartbeat wake CARRY refill evidence, and make refillable work able to WAKE firstmate, so acting on it is part of the existing wake-handling contract instead of a judgment call the model can skip.

This changes firstmate's shared tracked material, so the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill governs it: one-owner rule, AGENTS.md size discipline, repo style (one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never an em dash, shellcheck-clean bin scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh, no agent commit co-author), and colocated behavior-through-interface tests in tests/.

Accepted design, including every decision made and approved during this validation:

1. bin/fm-refill.sh is the single owner of the refill probe and its one-line format, refill: ready=<n> live=<m> ids=<id,id,...>. Ready work comes from the configured backlog backend (compatible tasks-axi ready, which already excludes blocked and captain-held work); live capacity counts state/*.meta records of kind=ship or kind=scout whose recorded endpoint is alive, reusing the existing cheap liveness helper the session-start digest uses (fm_backend_target_exists) rather than a second liveness reader.

2. The evidence rides the DURABLE QUEUE payload of the heartbeat wake record, and the watcher's printed reason line stays exactly 'heartbeat'. This is a deliberate deviation from the original one-extra-printed-line suggestion: bin/fm-watch-arm.sh, bin/fm-watch-checkpoint.sh, and bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh match watcher stdout as heartbeat($|:), bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh's is_wake_reason matches heartbeat exactly, and tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh asserts grep -Fx heartbeat. Every supervision protocol drains the queue with bin/fm-wake-drain.sh before handling a wake, so the payload reaches all six primary harnesses unchanged.

3. FAIL OPEN ON DATA. A manual backlog backend, a missing or incompatible tasks-axi, an unreadable backlog, malformed or incomplete backend output, or a probe past its hard bound emits no refill line, and the heartbeat goes out exactly as it would have otherwise. Malformed output is a probe failure, never a false ready=0; ready=0 is reported only for the backend's exact supported empty response, so silence means 'cannot answer' and never 'nothing ready'. The bound is hard in both implementations: kill-after escalation on timeout/gtimeout, and TERM escalating to KILL in the portable Perl fallback that stock macOS actually uses.

4. APPROVED SCOPE EXPANSION from the review gate: the commission was a mechanism that WAKES firstmate on refillable work, so the refill condition itself fires a wake in normal mode - dispatchable ready work with live capacity below FM_REFILL_MIN_LIVE (default 1) produces an actionable wake even when no unsurfaced captain-relevant status exists - on the existing heartbeat cadence and its doubling backoff, never a per-poll path, and still fail-open when the probe cannot answer. In away mode the same actionable refill condition is routed into the sub-supervisor's EXISTING escalation digest so it reaches a handling turn, while evidence-free heartbeats stay force-self-handled. That wiring is bounded: away mode itself is not redesigned and none of its approval boundaries change, so it still never expands authority for merges, ask-user findings, destructive, irreversible, or security-sensitive choices.

5. AGENTS.md section 8's heartbeat bullet carries the minimum contract language - a heartbeat carrying a refill line requires the handling turn to dispatch every eligible ready item or record in the backlog why each named item stays queued - patched into the existing bullet rather than a new section. docs/architecture.md's 'Event-driven supervision' section is the single owner of heartbeat wake semantics and states the new behavior, with bin/fm-refill.sh named as owner of the probe, its bound, and the line format. docs/scripts.md carries the one-row toolbelt entry.

6. Colocated coverage in tests/fm-refill.test.sh and tests/fm-daemon.test.sh: payload shape with ready ids and live ship and scout capacity (dead, secondmate, and window-less records excluded), captain-gated work non-dispatchable while a genuinely empty queue still reports ready=0, id capping with the count intact, every fail-open path including malformed output producing silence, the hard bound including the no-timeout-binary portable fallback, a normal-mode heartbeat firing from refillable work alone, an away-mode heartbeat with refill evidence reaching the escalation path while an evidence-free one stays self-handled, and a heartbeat still firing unchanged when the probe is broken.

SETTLED DECISIONS for this run, both made by the task owner during validation:
- Delivery base is origin/main (quinnbot-ai/firstmate is the canonical trunk). Local main being ahead of the kunchenguid upstream is expected fork state, not unpushed work bundled into this PR. Do not rebase or cherry-pick onto upstream/main; approve the rebase step's base finding.
- review, test, document, and lint already completed green on this exact head (8414c13e) in run 01KZKSCFF5MAQ59GE5GTXDX6DT and are skipped deliberately. Only the PR and CI steps remain; the earlier attempt failed solely because gh pr create was refused by a fine-grained personal access token, and the authorized gh shim is now installed ahead of the real binary on PATH.

Scope discipline: this is also the seed of a future upstream proposal (upstream-closeout-refill-proposal), so the change stays well-scoped and free of unrelated cleanups. This repo's .firstmate/test-inventory.json is 'testless' (the Python-literal contract; this repo's tests are shell), so no receipt regeneration applies.

## What Changed

- Add durable autonomous intake and routing for heartbeat capacity refills, captain links, process events, public follow-ups, and local or remote secondmate handoffs.
- Harden fleet execution across runtime backends with liveness tracking, wake-queue and session-lock safety, spawn/teardown recovery, Calm presentation parity, trace context, startup budgets, and GitHub/CI fallbacks.
- Expand shell validation with declarative runtime gates, durable test progress journals, stock macOS Bash CI, and broad interface and E2E coverage.

title: fm-brief.sh: initiative briefs generate a self-contradicting Definition of done, and the failure mode is losing the slice
body:
## What happens

`bin/fm-brief.sh` generates a `Definition of done` that tells the worker **not to push**, and to **rebase onto `main` if `main` has advanced**. For any initiative slice both are wrong: the slice must push to its own remote branch, and `main` is production for the target repository and is never touched.

The worker's copy is deleted at teardown. If it obeys the generated text, the slice's work is gone.

## Evidence

Across one 11-slice initiative, **6 of 11 workers reported this contradiction independently and unprompted** in their completion records. It was not surfaced by a supervisor asking about it.

The current workaround is a hand-written override paragraph in every brief, naming the two lines it overrides and placing itself before them. That is a prompt-level patch to a structural defect, and it has to be written correctly by a supervisor on every single dispatch.

Measured effect of getting the override right: an established-facts block cut re-reading of injected files from 67 calls to 13 across a wave, while isolation re-proving did not change at all, because that section still contradicted itself and the other did not.

## Why this outranks other brief improvements

Every other brief defect costs attention or a retry. This one costs the work. A stronger model spends tokens resolving the contradiction; a cheaper model resolves it the other way and the branch is never pushed, so teardown discards a completed slice with nothing to recover.

## Proposed fix

`fm-brief.sh` already takes `--mode`. Add the initiative case, and generate lifecycle text that matches it:

- check out the named existing remote branch (`git fetch origin <branch> && git checkout -B <branch> origin/<branch>`), because the spawn acquires the worktree after the branch is created and it comes up detached;
- push that branch;
- never rebase onto the base branch, and stop and report if the branch appears to need moving.

Then there is no contradiction to override, and no supervisor step that can be skipped.

title: fm-send.sh forwards an unknown --file flag as the message body instead of rejecting it
body:
## What happens

`bin/fm-send.sh` has no `--file` flag. Passing one does not error: the literal string `--file /path/to/instructions.md` is delivered to the worker as the message body.

## Evidence

Observed in a live initiative. The steer appeared to succeed, and the work proceeded correctly **only because the worker independently recognised the path and read it**. A worker that treated the message as text would have received an instruction consisting of a flag name.

## Why it matters more than the missing flag

The failure is silent and looks like success. `fm-send` is otherwise fail-closed - it refuses without an explicit `FM_HOME` precisely so a steer cannot be misrouted - so an unrecognised flag being passed through as content is inconsistent with the script's own contract.

## Proposed fix

Either accept `--file <path>` and send the file's contents, or reject unknown flags rather than forwarding them as message text. Rejecting is the smaller change and matches the script's existing posture.

Until then the documented workaround is to write the pointer explicitly as message text: "Read `<path>` and follow it."

title: A received corr= token can be dropped silently: two prose reminders have now failed to prevent it
body:
## What happens

A request carrying the `[fm-from-firstmate]` marker is discharged only by a line appended to the parent's status file carrying its exact `corr=<id>` token. Nothing enforces that. A secondmate can do the work correctly, answer in chat, and end the turn with the request still open, at which point the parent reposts it.

## Evidence

Four marked requests needed reposts across two sessions in one home (`02aae6657f4aafd9`, `b8a21c18adafd4e5`, `e84148fd84ea5f1d`, and one further token). In every case the work was completed correctly and no correlated line was written.

A prose reminder was written into that home's learnings after the first occurrence. **It did not prevent recurrence**, and a second, longer entry was then written after three more. Two prose reminders have now failed at the same thing.

The failure mode is specifically batching: when several marked requests arrive together, or arrive mid-turn while tools are running, the newest gets answered and the older correlations are silently dropped. Superseded content is not an exemption, because the parent tracks tokens rather than topics.

## Why prose cannot hold this

A rule that must hold under concurrency, or on a long turn where several tokens arrived at different moments, is exactly the class that belongs on a mechanical rung rather than in a document. The worker-facing half of this already has one: `fm-send --resolve-key` closes an open decision at answer time. The secondmate-answering-its-parent half has no equivalent.

## Proposed fix, in order of strength

1. A turn-end guard that refuses while a `corr=` token received this session has no matching status line, naming the outstanding tokens. This is the mechanism that would actually have caught all four.
2. A helper that writes the correlated line, so answering is one call rather than a remembered `echo`.
3. Surfacing outstanding correlations in the session-start digest, so a dropped one is visible at the next turn rather than when the parent reposts.

title: Never identify an agent by its worktree path: pooled slots are reused across initiatives
body:
## The bug class

Treehouse **pools and reuses** worktree slots across initiatives. Any logic that identifies an agent, its owner, or its work by the directory it is standing in is wrong the moment two initiatives share a machine.

## Evidence

Measured on one day, one machine: initiative K's agents ran in slots 26 and 44; initiative D's ran in slots 26, 40, and 42. Slot 26 held six of D's slices sequentially **and** K's work. A separate slot held agents from six different initiatives in a single night.

Directory matching therefore fails in both directions at once - it mixes another initiative's workers into a measurement, and it drops your own workers that ran in a slot you did not expect.

## One confirmed instance, already fixed

The `agent-forensics` script scoped sessions by worktree directory name. It has been given a `--home` filter that recovers the **dispatching firstmate home** from the status-file path in each launch brief, which is the only durable link between a transcript and who ordered it. Both transcript formats name their session directories after the working directory, so one directory legitimately contains several initiatives' transcripts interleaved.

Side effect worth copying: a raw-substring pre-filter before JSON parsing took a scoped run from a >120 second timeout to **1.05 seconds**, and cannot produce a false negative because the brief's own bytes are in the file.

## What has not been audited

Everything else that answers "whose is this?" from a path. Specifically worth checking:

- teardown and its refusal conditions,
- lease reclamation and stale-worktree cleanup,
- watcher attribution and any wake routed by directory,
- anything that sweeps a namespace for matching names.

## The rule worth encoding

The durable identity is the dispatching firstmate home, not the checkout. `fm-send` already fails closed unless `FM_HOME` is explicit; that is the right precedent and it should be the rule everywhere an owner is inferred.

title: feat(bin): add fm-firefox isolated Firefox/Marionette session owner
body:
## Intent Productize the already live-proven Firefox web-ext + Marionette/WebDriver route as a reusable, harness-agnostic Firstmate tool plus a just-in-time agent skill. The captain explicitly authorized adding this capability to the shared tool set. Deliverable: one new shell CLI bin/fm-firefox.sh that owns the lifecycle of a single isolated, disposable Firefox process driven over Marionette. Deliberate architecture decisions (not mistakes): (1) chose a thin harness-agnostic shell CLI over a new MCP server, AXI daemon, or global service, because the tool-layer-placement scout established that harness-agnostic CLI surfaces take precedence and every Pi worker already inherits the same MCP config, so a daemon would add a second browser control plane with no reach benefit; (2) the single supported install route is Marionette Addon:Install(temporary) so the tool can own exactly one -no-remote Firefox process it launched, rather than delegating launch to web-ext (which spawns its own process); web-ext is intentionally only reported by doctor as an optional, unmanaged alternative, not used; (3) the Marionette client is a small raw-protocol python3 implementation embedded in the CLI, so the tool's only hard deps are a Firefox binary and python3 (no marionette_driver dependency); marionette_driver is used only by the opt-in live test as an independent verification client. Safety contract implemented: always create a fresh, empty, task-owned profile (never attach to, copy, or enumerate a live Firefox/Zen profile); self-allocate a loopback Marionette endpoint and refuse the shared default 127.0.0.1:2828; launch exactly one -no-remote Firefox; apply -remote-allow-system-access only to that disposable process and only when --system-access is requested; expose truthful machine-readable JSON receipts; and on stop tear down only the process/profile/port it created after proving the recorded PID is still our Firefox by its profile path, refusing ambiguous PID/port/profile ownership rather than guessing or killing an unrelated process. Cookie/privacy scope is deliberately truthful, not a guarantee the tool can make: the CLI proves its own Firefox profile is fresh and task-owned but states in its receipt/help that a project-specific native messaging host can still independently discover unrelated Gecko cookie profiles (e.g. Zen) unless the project supplies its own verified cookie-off contract. The tool provides a generic caller env/cookie-off hook (--env, --cookie-off KEY=VALUE) that it forwards into the launched process without interpreting it, recording only the keys (never values) as a caller-asserted contract, so no MediaGrabber business logic is baked into Firstmate. Constraints honored: does not depend on the still-open MediaGrabber PRs #8/#9; never claims generic browser isolation controls project native-host cookie behavior; does not modify any global Pi/MCP configuration; the tool is invoked purely through the shell and is harness-independent. Also added: an agent-only .agents/skills/firefox-marionette skill (with one one-line AGENTS.md section 13 load trigger) teaching when to choose this route over Playwright/CDP/FoxMCP, the browser-vs-OS boundary, the no-live-profile safety contract, dependency checks, receipts, cleanup, and the native-host cookie caveat, pointing to the CLI --help rather than duplicating flags; operator documentation at docs/firefox-marionette.md and current verification evidence at docs/verification/firefox-marionette.md, both registered in docs/documentation-audiences.json, plus a docs/scripts.md toolbelt row; and registration of both new tests in bin/fm-test-run.sh (hermetic in pure-contract-unit, live in live-harness-optin) with shard weight hints. Two tests were added: a hermetic command-surface test (tests/fm-firefox-marionette.test.sh) that drives a fake Firefox speaking the real Marionette wire format and asserts observed behavior and receipt fields only (never implementation source bytes) - covering dependency failure, clean-profile creation, loopback allocation, ownership refusal, extension-path validation, truthful receipts, exact cleanup, interruption/error cleanup, and the native-host cookie caveat/caller-hook contract; and an opt-in live test (tests/fm-firefox-marionette-live-e2e.test.sh, gated by FM_FIREFOX_LIVE_E2E=1) that uses a synthetic local extension and a loopback HTTP page (no external URL) to prove real add-on install plus web-content and extension/browser-context control without pixel clicks, verifies no existing Firefox/Zen process or the shared endpoint changed, and leaves no Firefox child/profile/port behind, self-skipping when Firefox/python3/WebDriver deps are absent so standard CI stays hermetic. The live proof was run on this Mac against Firefox 153.0.3. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-firefox.sh`, a harness-agnostic shell CLI that owns the full lifecycle of a single isolated, disposable Firefox driven over Marionette: it always creates a fresh task-owned profile, self-allocates a loopback Marionette endpoint (refusing the shared `127.0.0.1:2828`), launches exactly one `-no-remote` process, installs the addon via a small embedded raw-protocol python3 Marionette client (so hard deps are only a Firefox binary + python3), exposes truthful JSON receipts/`doctor` output, forwards an uninterpreted `--env`/`--cookie-off` caller hook (recording keys only), and on `stop` tears down only the process/profile/port it created after verifying the recorded PID is still our Firefox by profile path. A start-time INT/TERM/EXIT trap kills the launched pid and removes the fresh profile if interrupted before the session state file is committed, closing the orphaned-process/profile window. - Added a just-in-time `.agents/skills/firefox-marionette` agent skill (with an AGENTS.md section 13 load trigger), operator docs at `docs/firefox-marionette.md`, verification evidence at `docs/verification/firefox-marionette.md`, both registered in `docs/documentation-audiences.json`, and a `docs/scripts.md` toolbelt row. - Added two tests registered in `bin/fm-test-run.sh`: a hermetic command-surface test (`tests/fm-firefox-marionette.test.sh`) that drives a fake Firefox speaking the real Marionette wire format and asserts observed behavior plus receipt fields (dependency failure, clean-profile creation, loopback allocation, ownership refusal, extension-path validation, exact/interrupted cleanup, native-host cookie caveat), and an opt-in live e2e test (`tests/fm-firefox-marionette-live-e2e.test.sh`, gated by `FM_FIREFOX_LIVE_E2E=1`) that proves real add-on install and web/extension-context control against a loopback page, verifies no existing process or the shared endpoint changed, and self-skips when deps are absent so standard CI stays hermetic. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Artımlı değişiklik, Round 1'deki tek uyarıyı (interrupt-penceresi süreç/profil sızıntısı) doğru bir INT/TERM/ERR trap + in-flight teardown ile kapatıyor; ampirik olarak trap'in sinyalde tetiklendiği, lokalleri dinamik kapsamla gördüğü ve açık hata yollarını bozmadığı doğrulandı, ayrıca doğrudan bir hermetik test eklendi. ## Testing Ran the smallest intent-relevant tests: the hermetic fm-firefox-marionette test (14 checks, real Marionette wire protocol against a fake Firefox — dependency refusal, clean owned profile, loopback allocation + 2828 refusal, truthful receipts, ownership-proven refusal, extension-path validation, exact cleanup, interruption/error/SIGTERM teardown, native-host cookie caveat) and the opt-in live e2e against the real Firefox 153.0.3 named in the intent (real temporary add-on install, web-content + extension-context control over Marionette with no pixel clicks, proof that no unrelated Firefox/Zen process or the shared 2828 endpoint changed, and zero leftovers). Both exit 0. The doctor JSON surface was exercised directly and reports honestly. This is a shell CLI with no rendered UI surface, so product-level evidence is the live-e2e CLI transcript and JSON receipts rather than a screenshot. No transient artifacts remained (default state root empty, worktree clean).
Evidence: Live e2e transcript vs real Firefox 153.0.3 `ok - fm-firefox live E2E (Mozilla Firefox 153.0.3): real add-on install, web-content and extension-context control, no unrelated browser touched, no leftovers` ```text ok - fm-firefox live E2E (Mozilla Firefox 153.0.3): real add-on install, web-content and extension-context control, no unrelated browser touched, no leftovers ```

title: feat(bin): make CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md promotion opt-in via --promote
body:
## Summary

`bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh` used to silently rewrite a project's real `CLAUDE.md` into `AGENTS.md` and inject the canonical self-governance section whenever the only memory file present was a real `CLAUDE.md`. Crewmates run this script as a routine step on every ship task, so an unrelated task on a project whose `CLAUDE.md` is its own working agreement would land a PR that renamed and edited the project's memory file, leaving the `CLAUDE.md` type change uncommitted and the repo with two near-identical drifting copies.

Make promotion explicit. The default run leaves a real `CLAUDE.md` untouched, prints one line naming the project memory file and pointing at `--promote`, and exits 0. `--promote` keeps today's rename, symlink, and self-governance injection byte-for-byte. Every other branch (skeleton creation, existing `AGENTS.md`, correct symlink, case-variant refusal, conflict paths) is unchanged.

`bin/fm-brief.sh`'s Project memory wording now reflects the default. The two existing promote tests pass `--promote` and keep their assertions. Two new tests cover the default path: the project's `CLAUDE.md` keeps its type and bytes, no `AGENTS.md` is created, and the self-governance section is not injected into the project's `CLAUDE.md`. `docs/architecture.md` is patched to keep its single sentence accurate without duplicating the script's contract.

## Test plan

- `bin/fm-lint.sh` is clean (single owner of the lint definition).
- `shellcheck` is clean for `bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh`, `bin/fm-brief.sh`, and `tests/fm-ensure-agents-md.test.sh`.
- `tests/fm-ensure-agents-md.test.sh` runs all 11 cases green: the 9 existing tests plus 2 new ones (`test_default_run_leaves_real_claude_md_untouched` and `test_default_run_does_not_inject_self_governance_into_claude_md`).
