title: feat(bin): add durable primary focus lifecycle
body:
## Intent The developer wanted a conventional-commit pull request title and a concise “What Changed” summary covering the entire branch delta from the specified base to target commits. The branch’s goal was to add a Phase 0 durable primary-focus lifecycle using one atomic focus snapshot owner, with fail-open suspend-before-switch prompt handling across primary harnesses so interrupted work remains resumable. They required that prompts never be blocked, no scheduler or second state store be introduced, the work not depend on the Phase 2 refill-wake branch, and the schema and mutation contract remain documented in the script header and help output. They also wanted the full no-mistakes pipeline to own fixes, pushing, and PR creation so CI would be green, while all intentional file and system changes stayed within the current worktree. ## What Changed - Added an atomic, revisioned primary-focus snapshot with suspend-before-switch, resume, completion, checkpoint, and compare-and-swap operations. - Wired bounded, fail-open prompt adapters for Claude, Grok, Pi, and OpenCode, capturing available session and event identity and emitting best-effort supervision wakes. - Documented the lifecycle contract and harness coverage, with regression tests for focus transitions, concurrency, hook behavior, and related watcher synchronization. ## Risk Assessment 🚨 High: The prior findings were addressed, but delayed callback retries can still corrupt focus ordering, and Grok can silently omit the resume identity required by the documented lifecycle. ## Testing Baseline delta inspection, the dedicated focus suite, opt-in shared-hook smoke, manual Claude-to-Grok suspend/resume/complete lifecycle, fail-open persistence failure, process-event, turn-end, and watch-triage checks succeeded; persisted CLI evidence and help-contract output were captured, while one non-UI watcher real-process suite showed load-sensitive flakiness and did not complete within the bounded retry.
Evidence: End-to-end focus lifecycle transcript ```text END-TO-END PRIMARY FOCUS LIFECYCLE 1. Claude pre-prompt adapter receives an initial captain prompt. { "revision": 1, "active": { "focus_id": "f1786495965.48384.18969", "state": "active", "summary": "Finish the release notes", "resume_kind": "claude-session", "resume_pointer": "claude-session-17" }, "suspended": [] } 2. Grok pre-prompt adapter receives new work; prior focus is durably suspended first. { "revision": 2, "active": { "focus_id": "f1786495970.49453.6653", "state": "active", "summary": "Investigate the deployment alarm", "resume_kind": "grok-session", "resume_pointer": "grok-session-42" }, "suspended": [ { "focus_id": "f1786495965.48384.18969", "state": "suspended", "summary": "Finish the release notes", "resume_kind": "claude-session", "resume_pointer": "claude-session-17" } ] } 3. A fresh owner process resumes the interrupted Claude focus by durable focus_id. { "revision": 3, "active": { "focus_id": "f1786495965.48384.18969", "state": "active", "summary": "Finish the release notes", "resume_kind": "claude-session", "resume_pointer": "claude-session-17" }, "suspended": [ { "focus_id": "f1786495970.49453.6653", "state": "suspended", "summary": "Investigate the deployment alarm", "resume_kind": "grok-session", "resume_pointer": "grok-session-42" } ] } 4. Completing the resumed focus leaves no active owner and preserves the other resumable work. { "revision": 4, "active": null, "suspended": [ { "focus_id": "f1786495970.49453.6653", "state": "suspended", "summary": "Investigate the deployment alarm", "resume_kind": "grok-session", "resume_pointer": "grok-session-42" } ] } 5. Fail-open proof: an unwritable state path cannot block prompt dispatch. hook_exit_status=0 (0 means dispatch remains unblocked) ```
Evidence: Documented schema and mutation contract ```text Usage: fm-focus.sh show [--state-dir DIR] [--json] fm-focus.sh switch [--state-dir DIR] [--expected-revision N] [--focus-id ID] [--task-id T] [--project P] [--owner-kind primary-direct|playbot|crew|secondmate] [--resume-kind K] [--resume-pointer P] [--checkpoint C] [--summary S] [--fingerprint F] fm-focus.sh suspend [--state-dir DIR] [--expected-revision N] [--reason suspended|paused_explicit] fm-focus.sh resume [--state-dir DIR] [--expected-revision N] [--focus-id ID] fm-focus.sh complete [--state-dir DIR] [--expected-revision N] [--outcome completed|failed] fm-focus.sh set-checkpoint [--state-dir DIR] [--expected-revision N] --checkpoint C Owner of state/.focus.json (atomic snapshot, CAS revision, suspend-before-switch). Schema (v1): { "v": 1, "revision": , "active": null | FocusEntry, "suspended": [ FocusEntry, ... ] } FocusEntry: { "focus_id": string, "task_id": string, "project": string, "owner_kind": "primary-direct" | "playbot" | "crew" | "secondmate", "state": "active" | "suspended" | "paused_explicit" | "blocked" | "completed" | "failed", "resume_kind": string, "resume_pointer": string, "checkpoint": string, "summary": string, "fingerprint": string, "created_at": , "updated_at": } Mutation contract: - Exactly one writer holds the mkdir lock for a read-modify-write. - Publish is always write-temp then rename; never in-place rewrite. - --expected-revision N refuses with exit 1 unless the on-disk revision is N. Without it, the command advances the revision while holding the lock. - switch records the previous nonterminal active focus as suspended before making the new focus active. - The atomic snapshot is the whole truth; this owner never event-sources. - Wake delivery is best effort after publish and never changes mutation success. Exit codes: 0 success or idempotent no-op; 1 refusal; 2 usage. ```
- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 warning across 1 run (26m40s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

⚠️ **Review** - 2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) - 🚨 `bin/fm-focus-prompt-hook.sh:142` - The fingerprint is derived only from prompt text, so a legitimate later submission of identical text (for example, repeated “continue” prompts) matches the active focus and becomes a no-op at fm-focus.sh:466. Include a per-submission/session event identity or otherwise distinguish callback retries from separate turns. - 🚨 `.codex/hooks.json:14` - The Codex lifecycle relies exclusively on a project UserPromptSubmit hook, but the repository's own verification evidence at docs/verification/supervision.md:194 says Codex project lifecycle hooks do not fire. Codex prompts therefore silently bypass focus recording; provide a verified reachable adapter or explicitly exclude Codex from Phase 0 claims. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-focus-prompt-hook.sh:155` - The fallback resume pointer stores only the harness name, so every focus from a given harness receives the same non-session-specific pointer. This cannot identify the interrupted session or distinguish suspended focuses, despite the new restart-proof resumability claim; capture a real verified session/task pointer or narrow that claim. 🔧 Fix: Fix focus submission identity and resume provenance 2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-focus.sh:466` - Idempotency checks only the active fingerprint. If event A is suspended by event B and a delayed retry of A arrives, the retry reactivates a duplicate A and suspends B even though A already exists in the stack. Treat a fingerprint found anywhere in the snapshot as an already-recorded submission. - ⚠️ `.grok/hooks/fm-primary-focus-lifecycle.json:8` - The Grok adapter does not pass its documented `GROK_SESSION_ID`, and the shared hook only extracts session identity from stdin. If the prompt payload omits that field, Grok focus entries have no resume pointer despite the new resumability claim. Pass the inline-defaulted environment value as `--session-id`.

An isolated retry cleared that exact case and several subsequent cases, but exceeded the 180-second outer bound before completing the suite. Core focus lifecycle, process-event, turn-end, and watch-triage suites passed, so this appears flaky rather than a demonstrated focus-lifecycle failure. - `git status --short --branch` - `git log --oneline 614fae60879372978a4480e22ec4d41eef083b3c..1727e6cbd64926c6574f323187950186f2697267` - `git diff --stat --name-status 614fae60879372978a4480e22ec4d41eef083b3c..1727e6cbd64926c6574f323187950186f2697267` - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-focus.test.sh` - `FM_FOCUS_HOOK_LIVE=1 bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-focus-hook-live-e2e.test.sh` - Manual lifecycle through `fm-focus-prompt-hook.sh --claude`, `fm-focus-prompt-hook.sh --grok`, `fm-focus.sh resume`, and `fm-focus.sh complete`, including persisted JSON and an unwritable-state fail-open check - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-procevent.test.sh tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh tests/fm-watch-arm.test.sh tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh` - `timeout -k 5 180 bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-watch-arm.test.sh` - `bin/fm-focus.sh --help`

Documentation-only scope prevented fixing it, so the full `git diff --check` remains failing. 🔧 Fix: Keep focus lifecycle documentation authoritative ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: fix: resurface durable supervision work after re-arm
body:
## Intent

Fix FIRSTMATE shared tracked supervision/startup infrastructure so that after the primary watcher re-arms following any accepted down stretch, whether caused by a blocking tool or ordinary idle downtime, nothing queued during that window is lost: every durable queued wake must drain and every still-open decision must re-surface in OPEN DECISIONS, including keyed remote-secondmate decisions ingested through parent-replies.

First reproduce the captain-reported miss end to end as closely as feasible: a durable queued wake and a still-open remote-secondmate parent-replies decision survive a watcher-down interval but were not surfaced by re-arm, only by an unrelated later drain. Diagnose the proven root cause by tracing parent-replies ingestion through task status logs and the incremental open-decisions fold, confirming durability across ingest surfaces, and checking re-arm and cursor behavior. Preserve the one-owner fold contract and the cursor correctness invariant. Do not attempt to keep the watcher live while a blocking tool suspends a turn.

Ship the smallest targeted deterministic, idempotent re-arm recovery so re-arm triggers the existing durable drain and fold path rather than relying on an incidental later drain. Remote decisions must use the authoritative task status-log surface already owned by the fold, not a second ledger. Pin the E2E reproduction as portable tests using durable on-disk state through real interfaces, showing both durable queued wakes and remote parent-replies open decisions re-surface after a down interval, including decision-only recovery and a persistent successor remaining live. Review affected supported watcher adapters/backends, keep lint clean, and provide the reproduction and post-fix E2E evidence in the PR body. Do not merge the PR; yolo is off. Escalate any ask-user finding to Firstmate instead of deciding it, and never use --yes.

## What Changed

- Trigger the existing durable wake-drain and OPEN DECISIONS fold when a watcher re-arms after downtime, including keyed remote-secondmate decisions ingested through parent replies.
- Keep queued wakes durable until generation-bound post-handling acknowledgement, preserving recovery evidence across watcher lock handoffs and interrupted handling.
- Add portable on-disk regression coverage for queued-wake replay, decision-only recovery, stale acknowledgements, and persistent successor liveness.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: No new material defects were substantiated, but the change substantially expands a concurrency-sensitive durable wake and acknowledgement state machine across multiple supervision paths.

## Testing

Inspected the base-to-target change, ran the four smallest affected suites, corrected and retried one fixture that had not adopted generation-bound acknowledgement, and captured a focused real-interface E2E transcript showing both queued wakes and the keyed remote decision resurfacing after downtime; all targeted checks now pass.

<details>
<summary>Evidence: Watcher re-arm E2E transcript showing durable wakes, OPEN DECISIONS, decision-only recovery, empty acknowledged queue, and live successor</summary>

```text
=== Re-arm user-visible wake ===
check: rearm-resurface
=== Durable wake drain + OPEN DECISIONS ===
1786341299	1	check	remote-reply-ios	check: process-event result captured: remote-reply-ios:7
1786341299	2	check	startup-network	check: startup-network
OPEN DECISIONS (still open, folded from the durable status logs - not just the latest line):
ios [key=remote-signoff] needs-decision: remote secondmate is held for captain sign-off
OPEN DECISIONS: close one by answering it: bin/fm-send.sh <task> --resolve-key <key> '<answer>'
=== Decision-only later re-arm ===
watcher: started pid=82287 (beacon fresh)
check: rearm-resurface
OPEN DECISIONS (still open, folded from the durable status logs - not just the latest line):
ios [key=remote-signoff] needs-decision: remote secondmate is held for captain sign-off
OPEN DECISIONS: close one by answering it: bin/fm-send.sh <task> --resolve-key <key> '<answer>'
WAKE_ACK_REQUIRED: after handling completes run bin/fm-wake-drain.sh --ack-through 0 --recovery-generation 83390.1786341303.ZIXVSi
=== Authoritative parent status log ===
needs-decision [key=remote-signoff]: remote secondmate is held for captain sign-off
=== Durable queue bytes after acknowledgement: 0 ===
=== Persistent successor after acknowledgement ===
watcher: started pid=85240 (beacon fresh)
```
</details>

## Pipeline

<summary>🔧 **Review** - 3 issues found → auto-fixed (14) ✅</summary>

- 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:809` - Recovery checks the queue and later removes the downtime marker without one atomic boundary. A real startup-network publisher can append after the size/read check but before line 816; the marker is then removed, and ordinary watcher polling never examines that queue row, recreating the reported miss. Hold the wake-queue lock through the final empty decision and marker consumption, or retain recovery state until the shared drain confirms consumption.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:748` - Downtime is recorded only from the EXIT trap. If the tracked watcher is abruptly reaped (for example SIGKILL or process-group teardown that bypasses traps), no marker is written; wakes queued while it is down survive, but the replacement returns at line 808 and never triggers the drain. Record/infer the predecessor generation at a durable shared arm/watch boundary rather than relying solely on cleanup execution.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:812` - The re-arm gate uses the whole-file scan instead of the cursor-backed fold's trusted-open fallback. If a status read transiently fails or becomes partial while a previously folded decision remains in the cursor, this scan can return empty and line 816 permanently consumes the marker; the existing drain would have preserved and printed the trusted open set. Trigger recovery through a cursor-safe shared boundary without creating a competing fold owner.

3 issues (2 errors, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:751` - This contradicts the required behavior “after the primary watcher re-arms following any accepted down stretch ... nothing queued during that window is lost.” In the autoarm model, a watcher can deliver wake A, cleanup removes the marker here, the handling turn drains A, and a durable remote/startup wake can then arrive before the next turn-end rearm. That successor sees neither a marker nor a stale lock, so it remains asleep and the later wake is still missed. Preserve recovery state for the entire watcher-down generation, including downtime following a delivered wake, while preventing persistent successor loops at the shared drain/arm handoff.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:740` - Abrupt-exit recovery still depends on this process receiving FM_LOCK_RECOVERED_PID, but fm-pr-check-migrate.sh runs first and can acquire, steal, and release the stale watcher lock when migration is required. After a SIGKILL with no marker, that subprocess consumes the only recovery evidence; this watcher then acquires a clean lock, leaves WATCHER_RECOVERY_PENDING=0, and misses durable queued work. Persist the recovery signal whenever any supported preflight/lock owner consumes a dead watcher lock, rather than relying on a process-local return variable.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:754` - Creating the marker with `: > "$WATCHER_DOWNTIME_MARKER"` follows an existing symlink and can truncate an arbitrary file writable by the watcher. Create the marker without following links, such as via a same-directory temporary file and atomic rename, or reject/remove a symlink first.

🔧 Fix: Persist safe recovery markers across migration lock recovery
2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:751` - This contradicts the required behavior “after the primary watcher re-arms following any accepted down stretch ... nothing queued during that window is lost.” After a watcher delivers wake A, cleanup removes the recovery marker; under the Claude auto-arm path, the handling turn can drain A, then receive a durable wake B before its turn-end successor starts. That successor sees neither a marker nor a stale lock, so B remains missed until an unrelated drain. Preserve recovery state across the entire delivered-wake handling gap and consume it at the shared drain/arm handoff without causing persistent-successor loops.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:754` - Cleanup ignores recovery-marker publication failure and then releases the watcher lock. For example, `fm_recovery_marker_publish` deliberately fails when `.watcher-down` is an ordinary directory; after a TERM exit, the successor therefore sees neither a marker nor a stale lock and can miss downtime work. If publication fails, retain stale-lock recovery evidence or fail closed visibly rather than releasing the last recovery signal.

🔧 Fix: Retain stale lock when recovery marker publication fails
3 issues (2 errors, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:751` - The required guarantee says “after the primary watcher re-arms following any accepted down stretch ... nothing queued during that window is lost,” but this branch removes recovery state after every delivered wake. In the Claude auto-arm path, wake A closes the watcher, its handling turn drains A, wake B is durably queued before the turn-end successor arms, and that successor sees neither a marker nor a stale lock, so B remains unsurfaced. Preserve recovery state through the delivered-wake handling gap and consume it at the shared drain/arm handoff.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-pr-check-migrate.sh:314` - After migration steals a dead watcher's lock, a transient marker-publication failure releases the replacement lock here, discarding the only stale-owner evidence. If the condition clears and startup is retried, migration acquires a clean lock, publishes no marker, and the watcher can miss downtime work. Retain stale-lock evidence on this failure path as watcher cleanup now does.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:752` - An ordinary directory at `.watcher-down` is treated as pending recovery, but `rm -f` cannot consume it and the failure is ignored. Every persistent successor therefore immediately emits `rearm-resurface` and exits instead of remaining live. Reject or quarantine malformed markers before arming, or consume recovery state with a checked operation that cannot leave the marker active.

🔧 Fix: Preserve delivery-gap recovery and quarantine malformed markers
2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh:493` - The acknowledged-marker path releases the wake-queue lock before consuming the marker. A publisher can durably append after the empty check at line 490 but before the marker move at line 499; the marker is then removed and the live watcher never examines that queued row, recreating the reported miss. Hold the queue lock through the final empty decision and marker consumption.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:148` - The drain ignores recovery-marker acknowledgement failure. If the atomic replacement in fm_recovery_marker_ack fails, the marker remains pending:handling; successors consequently keep waiting rather than recovering later queued work, while this drain reports success. Handle acknowledgement failure explicitly so recovery state cannot remain spuriously active.

🔧 Fix: Serialize recovery consumption and report acknowledgment failures
1 error still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-watch.sh:737` - This contradicts the required guarantee that after re-arm following “any accepted down stretch ... nothing queued during that window is lost.” The new recovery gate recognizes only `FM_LOCK_RECOVERED_PID` or a marker, but `fm-watch-arm.sh --restart` line 397 removes an identity-mismatched stale watcher lock when its dead PID has been reused by an unrelated live process. After a SIGKILL leaves no marker, that removal erases the only downtime evidence; the launched watcher acquires a clean lock and can sleep over durable queued work. Publish recovery state at `clear_stale_recorded_watcher_lock` before removing the verified stale watcher lock, or retain equivalent evidence through that boundary.

🔧 Fix: Centralize recovery publication before clearing watcher evidence
2 errors still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh:512` - This contradicts the requirement that “nothing queued during that window is lost: every durable queued wake must drain.” Arm-check consumes the marker while holding the queue lock, then releases it; a publisher already waiting on that lock subsequently appends after marker consumption, while the successor remains live and never examines the row. The new test demonstrates this exact missed state at tests/fm-watch-arm.test.sh:430-433 but treats it as success. Make the append/arm handoff preserve recovery evidence for a waiting publisher, and require the test to observe the concurrent wake being surfaced and drained.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh:626` - The required guarantee after “any accepted down stretch” remains vulnerable because FM_LOCK_RECOVERED_PID is assigned only after line 622 removes the stale watcher lock and line 624 creates its replacement. If the reclaiming watcher or migration process is killed between those operations, no marker or watcher lock remains; the next watcher starts clean and can sleep over queued work. Publish recovery evidence inside the stale watcher-lock reclaim boundary before removal, rather than relying on a process-local flag produced after replacement.

🔧 Fix: Guarantee recovery evidence across queue and lock handoffs
1 error still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh:770` - This contradicts the required criterion that “every durable queued wake must drain.” An external publisher such as startup-network can append a durable row here and then be killed, or fail marker publication at line 773; its caller ignores that failure, while the live watcher never examines the queue and has neither a downtime marker nor a stale watcher lock to trigger recovery. Additionally, marker publication removes the old marker before replacement, creating another crash window that can erase existing evidence. Under the queue lock, atomically publish recovery evidence before committing the row, replacing the marker with one rename and no remove-before-rename gap.

🔧 Fix: Publish recovery evidence before durable wake commits
1 error still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh:403` - Every durable wake append and watcher recovery transition now invokes `perl`, but Perl is not part of the supported universal toolchain and other project code explicitly treats it as optional. On a supported host without Perl, marker publication fails before the queue row is committed; ignored callers such as startup-network silently drop the wake, while watcher cleanup/reclaim cannot release or recover the lock. Use an already-required runtime or a portable same-directory atomic replacement implementation.

🔧 Fix: Replace recovery marker Perl dependency with Node
1 error still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh:495` - This contradicts “nothing queued during that window is lost: every durable queued wake must drain.” After a watcher delivers wake A, cleanup publishes `pending:handling`; if its handling turn is interrupted before `fm-wake-drain.sh` acknowledges it, the persistent successor treats the marker as `wait` forever and never surfaces A. Only a later unrelated publisher or watcher restart changes the marker, recreating the incidental-later-drain failure. Give pending handling state a durable owner/lease or let the successor recover when no handling owner remains, at the shared drain/arm handoff.

🔧 Fix: Keep interrupted wakes durable until handling acknowledgment
2 errors still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh:495` - This contradicts the required “persistent successor remaining live” behavior. Pi and OpenCode start and verify a successor before delivering the original wake; that successor observes `pending:handling` with the original row still queued, selects `recover`, and exits with another rearm-resurface wake. Each replacement can repeat this before handling begins. Preserve the pre-delivery successor instead of treating the still-durable original row as a new recovery event.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:144` - The accepted requirement says a delivered wake must not leave durable state until handling is fully complete/acknowledged, but the initial drain atomically empties the queue before returning control to the handling turn. If the turn is interrupted immediately after the drain returns, the marker is already acknowledged and the row is gone, so a successor cannot re-drain it. The new regression only kills the drain before this line and therefore does not cover an interrupted handling turn after drain completion. Add a real post-handling acknowledgement boundary, or escalate the concrete lifecycle decision as requested rather than treating drain completion as handling completion.

🔧 Fix: Add post-handling durable wake acknowledgements
2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:145` - This contradicts the required criterion that “every still-open decision must re-surface in OPEN DECISIONS.” During decision-only recovery the queue is empty, so this branch acknowledges the recovery marker before printing OPEN DECISIONS. If the handling turn is interrupted after the drain returns, the successor sees an acknowledged marker and empty queue, remains asleep, and the unchanged open decision is again stranded until an unrelated drain. Keep decision-only recovery pending until an explicit post-handling acknowledgement, rather than auto-acknowledging it on the empty-queue path.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:168` - The new drain contract leaves emitted rows queued until this command is run, but bin/fm-afk-return.sh still invokes the drain, immediately removes its catch-up gate, and reports “catch-up clear” without executing or retaining an acknowledgement step. A clean AFK return with queued non-blocking wakes can therefore permit ordinary work while the queue and recovery marker remain active, causing successor replay. Integrate the post-handling acknowledgement into the AFK return gate before declaring catch-up complete.

🔧 Fix: Enforce post-handling acknowledgement across recovery and AFK return
1 error still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:125` - This contradicts “after the primary watcher re-arms following any accepted down stretch ... every still-open decision must re-surface.” The printed acknowledgement carries only a queue sequence; when it runs, this branch snapshots and acknowledges whichever marker is current. If a watcher goes down after the drain but before handling completes, its newer downtime marker can therefore be acknowledged by the older handling turn. The next successor sees an acknowledged marker and empty queue and sleeps without re-surfacing still-open decisions from that down stretch. Bind the acknowledgement command to the marker token captured by the original drain and CAS only that generation; a newer marker must remain pending.

🔧 Fix: Bind wake acknowledgements to recovery generations
2 errors still open:
- 🚨 `tests/fm-wake-queue.test.sh:192` - These regressions still require concurrent drains to consume rows exactly once and later wait for the queue to become empty before acknowledgement (lines 540-566). The new contract deliberately retains rows until the generation-bound post-handling ACK, and `.wake-queue.empty.*` is no longer created, so these tests cannot validate the implemented behavior. Update them to assert replay before ACK and consumption only after the emitted ACK command succeeds.
- 🚨 `tests/fm-watch-arm.test.sh:331` - The interrupted-decision regression acknowledges using the generation captured before the successor recovery. That successor's handling cleanup and the replay drain each publish a newer marker generation, so the CAS must reject this command. Parse and acknowledge the generation emitted by `replayed-decision-drain.err`; otherwise the required interrupted decision-recovery regression asserts an impossible outcome.

🔧 Fix: Align wake regressions with generation-bound acknowledgements
✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

</details>

<details>

title: chore(skills): vendor third-party agent skills and scope them out of the docs audience inventory
body:
## Intent Land the third-party skills that were installed into this firstmate repo but never committed, and stop the scrape-cache directory from ever being committed. Required work: 1. Commit the ten vendored skill directories under .agents/skills/ (deploy-to-vercel, last30days, vercel-cli-with-tokens, vercel-composition-patterns, vercel-optimize, vercel-react-best-practices, vercel-react-native-skills, vercel-react-view-transitions, web-design-guidelines, writing-guidelines) plus skills-lock.json, the installer's provenance/hash lock for those skills. 2. Add .firecrawl/ to .gitignore. It is a ~6.6MB Firecrawl scrape cache holding unrelated job-research JSON: machine-local runtime data, not source, and it must never enter this shared repo. 3. last30days is ~16MB, of which ~14MB is assets/. Requirement was to check whether those assets are genuinely required at runtime and exclude them if they are demo/sample data, saying so clearly in the PR body. Verified: no SKILL.md, script, or reference file references assets/ or any asset filename, and the skill's own .skillignore classifies assets/ as non-runtime packaging/dev/eval material. So assets/ is excluded and the skill lands at 2.4MB. That path is also gitignored so a reinstall does not reintroduce it as untracked drift. 4. These skills are vendored third-party material, not firstmate-authored, and each carries its own upstream metadata. They are deliberately landed exactly as installed, byte-identical (verified with diff -rq against the source checkout). Do NOT rewrite, reformat, restyle, or 'fix' their content. The repo's own style rules (one sentence per line, plain dash) apply only to material we author, not to vendored upstream files. Findings that propose editing anything under a vendored skill directory should be rejected. 5. Requirement was to check whether any of the ten skills sets metadata.internal=true, since AGENTS.md section 2 says .agents/skills/ entries carry that marker so installers can distinguish firstmate-internal skills from installer-facing ones. Verified: all 19 pre-existing tracked skills carry metadata.internal: true and none of the ten vendored ones do; no script or CI check reads the marker today. Per the accepted instruction this is flagged in the PR body rather than fixed by editing vendored files. Accepted follow-on requirement, authorized by the captain mid-task after the original brief had fenced bin/ off: landing this vendored prose broke bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh, which enumerates every tracked Markdown file and demands an exact entry in docs/documentation-audiences.json. It failed two ways at once - 206 upstream files reported unclassified, and even fully classified it still failed link validation on ordinary upstream authoring (16 illustrative (url) placeholders and 15 absolute example paths such as /dashboard, which are code samples rather than repository links). Fixing those links would mean editing vendored files, which requirement 4 forbids. The authorized fix is to extend bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh so skills listed in skills-lock.json are out of the audience-inventory scope, plus a colocated test. skills-lock.json is the authority for which skills are vendored, so it drives the exclusion rather than a second hand-maintained list. The exclusion is reported as vendored_skills= on every run so it is visible rather than silent, and a lock naming a skill that is not a single path segment, or that cannot be parsed, refuses rather than quietly excluding another tree. docs/documentation-audiences.md is the owner of the scope contract and got one sentence recording the exclusion. Explicit scope limit the captain set on that follow-on: exactly bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh plus its colocated test tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh (and the one-sentence owner-doc update). Nothing else under bin/ may be touched, and no vendored skill file may be edited. A concurrent worker is shipping an unrelated change to other files under bin/. Acceptance criteria: working tree clean with no untracked leftovers from these paths; .firecrawl/ gitignored and not committed; and the PR body explains what was vendored and from where (provenance from skills-lock.json), the last30days size decision, the .firecrawl ignore rationale, and the metadata.internal finding. Known pre-existing and out of scope: bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed has no changed-test mapping for vendored skill script paths, so that local convenience selector now errors in this repo. CI does not use --changed (it uses --check-coverage, --lane, and --family, all verified passing), and bin/fm-test-run.sh is outside the authorized scope, so this is recorded as a follow-up rather than fixed here. Some tests/ failures for zellij, herdr, and orca backends and one in fm-backend.test.sh reproduce on the base commit and are unrelated to this change. ## What Changed - Committed ten vendored third-party skills under `.agents/skills/` exactly as the installer wrote them (byte-identical, verified with `diff -rq` against the source checkout), plus `skills-lock.json` as their provenance/hash lock: `deploy-to-vercel`, `vercel-cli-with-tokens`, `vercel-composition-patterns`, `vercel-optimize`, `vercel-react-best-practices`, `vercel-react-native-skills`, `vercel-react-view-transitions`, `web-design-guidelines` and `writing-guidelines` from `vercel-labs/agent-skills`, and `last30days` from `mvanhorn/last30days-skill`. `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` now record the vendored tier alongside the firstmate-authored one, including that these files are never hand-edited here - fixes belong upstream. - Gitignored `.firecrawl/` (a ~6.6MB Firecrawl scrape cache of unrelated job-research JSON - machine-local runtime data, not source) and `.agents/skills/last30days/assets/`. `last30days` is ~16MB on disk, ~14MB of it `assets/`; no `SKILL.md`, script, or reference file references `assets/` or any asset filename, and the skill's own `.skillignore` classifies `assets/` as non-runtime packaging/dev/eval material, so it is excluded and the skill lands at 2.4MB. Ignoring the path also keeps a reinstall from reappearing as untracked drift. - Extended `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` so prose under any skill named in `skills-lock.json` is out of the audience-inventory scope - vendored upstream Markdown otherwise failed both classification (206 unclassified files) and link validation (illustrative `(url)` placeholders and absolute example paths like `/dashboard` that are code samples, not repo links). `skills-lock.json` drives the exclusion rather than a second hand-maintained list, the count is reported as `vendored_skills=` on every run so the exclusion is visible, and a lock entry that is not a single path segment - or a lock that cannot be parsed - refuses instead of silently excluding another tree. Added `tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` coverage and one sentence in `docs/documentation-audiences.md`, the scope contract's owner. Two findings surfaced during the work and are reported rather than fixed, since fixing them would mean editing vendored files: - All 19 pre-existing tracked skills carry `metadata.internal: true`; none of the ten vendored ones do. No script or CI check reads that marker today. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed` has no changed-test mapping for vendored skill script paths, so that local convenience selector now errors in this repo. CI does not use `--changed` (it uses `--check-coverage`, `--lane`, and `--family`), and `bin/fm-test-run.sh` was outside the authorized scope, so this is left as a follow-up. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is almost entirely byte-identical vendored content plus a small, well-tested, tightly scoped exclusion in the docs audience checker that fails closed on malformed or unsafe lock entries. ## Testing Exercised the change the way a contributor and CI would hit it: ran the docs audience check directly on the repo (passes, and now prints the visible `vendored_skills=206` exclusion count), reproduced the pre-fix failure by running the base-commit version of the same script against the vendored tree, ran the colocated test file covering the new exclusion plus the two refusal paths (non-single-segment skill name, unparseable lock), and manually verified the acceptance criteria - ten skills and skills-lock.json tracked, last30days at 2.4MB with no assets/, and .firecrawl/ plus the assets path gitignored such that recreating them leaves the working tree clean. No UI surface is involved, so evidence is CLI transcripts rather than screenshots. Everything passed and no transient artifacts were left behind.
Evidence: Audience check + colocated test run $ bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh fm-doc-audience-check: ok surfaces=67 local_links=233 vendored_skills=206 $ bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh ok - documentation inventory classifies every maintained prose surface exactly once ok - vendored third-party skill prose stays out of scope while a malformed lock refuses ok - classification, setup routing, and maintained-prose scope fail safely ok - required documentation owner pointers cannot silently disappear ok - local links resolve while dates, versions, commands, and incident prose remain semantically reviewed ```text $ bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh fm-doc-audience-check: ok surfaces=67 local_links=233 vendored_skills=206 $ bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh ok - documentation inventory classifies every maintained prose surface exactly once ok - vendored third-party skill prose stays out of scope while a malformed lock refuses ok - classification, setup routing, and maintained-prose scope fail safely ok - required documentation owner pointers cannot silently disappear ok - local links resolve while dates, versions, commands, and incident prose remain semantically reviewed ```
Evidence: Before/after: base script fails, fixed script passes # Base (pre-fix) check against the vendored tree: fm-doc-audience-check: unclassified: .agents/skills/deploy-to-vercel/SKILL.md, ... [206 paths] # Fixed check on the same tree: fm-doc-audience-check: ok surfaces=67 local_links=233 vendored_skills=206 ```text # Base (pre-fix) check against the vendored tree - fails, 206 files unclassified: -audience-check: unclassified: .agents/skills/deploy-to-vercel/SKILL.md, .agents/skills/last30days/SKILL.md, .agents/skills/last30days/references/save-html-brief.md, .agents/skills/vercel-cli-with-tokens/SKILL.md, .agents/skills/vercel-composition-patterns/AGENTS.md, .agents/skills/vercel-composition-patterns/README.md, ...[206 paths] # Fixed check on the same tree: # Fixed version on the same tree fm-doc-audience-check: ok surfaces=67 local_links=233 vendored_skills=206 exit=0 ```

## Intent

Validate the CI-hardening fix on PR #1726 (head 6fdc6b9, preserved rebase 8a323b80): harden the Pi/OpenCode watcher recovery fixtures in tests/fm-pi-watch-extension.test.sh against CI scheduling races - the wall-clock recovery budgets (250ms readiness and retire overrides) raced spawn-to-script-start latency and SIGTERM-to-close observation under contention, so the budgets now carry ~5x slack (750ms) while the unretired tests keep their deliberate 20ms retire (their fixtures ignore TERM); the prompt fail-loud cap moved to 10s (the paced flow can approach 5s) and the single-flight stability check is a bounded 100ms window covering the 5-10ms retry delay instead of setImmediate; every inner Node failure now surfaces the captured output. title: fix(bin): prevent completed worker reuse against reassigned pool slots
body:
## Intent Fix fleet-safety defect: prevent completed/failed worker endpoints and stale task records from mutating a pooled project copy reassigned to a newer task. Add three interlocked guards: spawn collision detection (fm-backend.sh + fm-spawn.sh), teardown collision bypass (fm-teardown.sh), and fm-send terminal denial (fm-send.sh). Add regression tests. ## What Changed - Added spawn-time collision detection (`fm_backend_worktree_canonical_owner` in `bin/fm-backend.sh`, wired into `bin/fm-spawn.sh`) so a task can detect when the pooled project copy it was assigned is already owned by a newer, live task. - Hardened `bin/fm-teardown.sh` with a collision bypass: when a stale task's meta collides with a slot that has been reassigned, teardown removes only its own stale meta and skips the worktree/treehouse pool return and hook removal, leaving the new owner's meta and worktree intact. - Made `bin/fm-send.sh` refuse to deliver input to a task that has already reported done/failed, blocking terminal endpoints from mutating a recycled pool slot. - Added `tests/fm-pooled-path-collision.test.sh` (10 regression tests) covering collision detection, teardown bypass/return/new-owner survival, and fm-send terminal refusal. The review flagged one residual case: a SIGKILL mid-teardown can leave a stale meta that a later owner treats as live. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-bounded, biases entirely toward not destroying reassigned worktrees, matches the authorized three-guard intent, and is covered by regression tests; the single concern is a narrow, recoverable (slot-leak, not data-loss) edge reachable only via an interrupted teardown and safe to address as a follow-up. ## Testing Ran the change's targeted regression suite `tests/fm-pooled-path-collision.test.sh` (10/10 pass) and then produced product-level CLI evidence exercising each of the three guards as an operator would experience them: the fm-send terminal-task refusal for done/failed tasks, the fm-teardown collision notice that retires stale volatile records while protecting the reassigned pool slot (no treehouse return, new-owner meta/worktree untouched), and the fm-spawn canonical-path collision detection that refuses reuse yet self-excludes relaunch. This is a shell/CLI change with no UI surface, so the reviewer-visible artifact is a CLI transcript of the actual refusal/notice messages and resulting state rather than a screenshot. Preserve a726b54's fresh verified-remote and forge-identity protections. Accept forge proof only when the canonical recorded PR is reported merged and the recorded pr_head exactly equals the current branch HEAD; otherwise use cumulative tree equivalence against a freshly verified remote default branch as fallback. Uncommitted changes must always refuse, missing or mismatched PR metadata, an unmerged or unreachable forge, remote ambiguity, and differing content must refuse loudly with actionable guidance. Add no bypass flags and leave --force semantics unchanged. Cover exact-head squash success, a 112-line post-review head mismatch, unmerged PR, dirty worktree, unreachable forge with unequal content, remote identity mismatch, and content equivalence with unrelated default-branch work. Do not exercise teardown against the live BIZ-BUG-001 worktree during validation. ## What Changed - Add durable Telegram topic-board and direct-message services across approved groups, with per-topic routing, decision buttons, recurring inbox wakeups, and idempotent replies. - Improve fleet continuity with reboot recovery, semantic busy state, quota-aware authenticated dispatch, bounded startup memory, deterministic X follow-ups, and Herdr/Calm runtime refinements. - Fail closed when tearing down landed work: accept verified exact-head squash PRs or freshly verified remote content equivalence while retaining remote and forge identity protections. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The follow-up correctly pins the GitHub forge lookup to the recorded host and adds a focused regression case without changing teardown semantics. ## Testing The full targeted teardown suite and direct CLI transcript passed using disposable fixtures only, never the BIZ-BUG-001 worktree; allowed cases removed task metadata, while every refusal preserved it.

title: docs: name capacity-limited shared build/test infra as a serializing condition
body:
## Summary
- Patches AGENTS.md section 7's existing serialize-only-for sentence (~line 280) to name capacity-limited shared build or test infrastructure (a device simulator or emulator, a device farm, a single machine's build capacity) as a concrete shared-mutable-external-state condition that requires serializing concurrent work.
- States that partitioning such a resource per worker is the cheaper answer than serializing, wherever it can be partitioned.

## Why
Three same-day failures on one machine came from dispatching two iOS workers concurrently: a validation test-step failure initially misdiagnosed as a code defect (actually another worker's xcodebuild holding the same simulator), two workers driving the same named simulator, and 22 orphaned simulator clones (52GB) from abnormal exits stalling unrelated work. The existing rule already covered this case as "shared mutable external state" but was never read that way, so this patches the existing sentence rather than adding new prose.

## Test plan
- [x] `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` passes
- [x] no-mistakes pipeline: intent, rebase, review, test, document steps all passed (lint skipped: ShellCheck unavailable in this environment, no scripts changed)

title: fix: resurface durable supervision work after re-arm
body:
## Intent

Fix FIRSTMATE shared supervision and startup infrastructure so that after the primary watcher re-arms following any accepted down stretch, whether caused by a blocking tool or ordinary idle downtime, nothing queued during that window is lost.
Every durable queued wake must drain and every still-open decision must re-surface in OPEN DECISIONS, including keyed remote-secondmate decisions ingested through parent-replies.
The implementation must preserve the one-owner status-log fold and incremental cursor correctness invariant.
It must not keep a watcher live during a blocking tool.
Recovery uses lease-free, at-least-once durable re-drain with generation-bound post-handling acknowledgement, never an owner or lease abstraction.

## What Changed

- Re-arm now detects and recovers durable queue work and still-open decision recovery after watcher downtime.
- Remote secondmate parent-replies continue to materialize onto task status logs, which remain the only OPEN DECISIONS fold surface.
- Durable wakes remain queued until an explicit, generation-bound post-handling acknowledgement succeeds.
- Recovery evidence is published before any clear or durable-row transition that could otherwise lose a wake across a crash.
- Persistent Pi and OpenCode successor handling, legacy markerless queues, prompt-delivery boundaries, and AFK return use the same lease-free re-drain discipline.
- Portable behavior regressions cover remote decision re-folding, interrupted handling, stale acknowledgement rejection, legacy adoption, evidence publication failure, prompt-delivery interruption, and AFK evidence handling.

## Risk Assessment

This change modifies supervision continuity and durable wake delivery paths.
The implementation is deliberately at-least-once and idempotent so an interruption causes replay rather than loss.
All required checks are being monitored by no-mistakes.

## Testing

- The pre-fix reproduction showed a watcher re-arm remaining live while durable queued wakes and a keyed remote-secondmate decision were only surfaced by a later unrelated drain.
- The post-fix portable E2E regression verifies re-arm drains queued wakes and re-folds the remote decision into OPEN DECISIONS.
- Focused recovery tests cover decision-only recovery, interrupted handling replay, generation-bound acknowledgement, legacy queue adoption, prompt-delivery interruption, AFK return, Pi and OpenCode successor behavior, and daemon lifecycle handling.
- The serial-4 AFK duplicate-marker report was repeated four times in isolated end-to-end runs and did not reproduce.
- The serial-4 issue was fixture or concurrent-load flakiness, not an AFK product behavior fix.

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

<!-- no-mistakes-pipeline-attestation:v1 {"head_sha":"b697f5c4cf2bc196b9adee13aab26a3210654088","steps":[{"step":"intent","status":"completed"},{"step":"rebase","status":"completed"},{"step":"review","status":"completed"},{"step":"test","status":"completed"},{"step":"document","status":"completed"},{"step":"lint","status":"completed"},{"step":"push","status":"completed"},{"step":"pr","status":"completed"},{"step":"ci","status":"running"}]} -->

The no-mistakes pipeline completed intent, rebase, review, test, documentation, lint, push, and PR creation.
The CI monitor remains authoritative for the current branch head and must be green before merge.

## Hazard-to-commit map

Each numbered entry names the concrete loss or loop failure prevented and the commit or commits that implement its correction.

1. Re-arm previously slept over durable wakes and open status-log decisions after watcher downtime.
Commit c47a03b introduces the re-arm recovery path and its portable remote-secondmate decision regression.
2. A whole-file recovery check could bypass the cursor-backed open-decision guarantee.
Commit 101bc78 routes recovery through the cursor-safe boundary.
3. A preflight migration or stale-lock reclaim could consume the only evidence of watcher downtime.
Commits be57416, 37eda06, and 524b318 persist recovery evidence before clearing or reclaiming watcher state.
4. A recovery-marker publication failure or malformed marker could erase evidence or loop successors.
Commits eed55e7 and c344adb retain evidence on publication failure and quarantine invalid marker state.
5. Queue and marker operations could race, allowing a publisher or acknowledgement to consume the wrong recovery state.
Commits ff4fc17, 524b318, 08a1062, and faa015e serialize handoffs, publish evidence before durable rows, and bind acknowledgements to a generation.
6. A missing optional runtime could disable durable recovery publication.
Commits 79acdab and 317b4b4 replace that dependency with the supported portable path and validate it in CI.
7. A wake removed at drain time could be lost when handling was interrupted.
Commits abc124b, 5cec23b, and 55713d4 retain rows until a generation-bound post-handling acknowledgement and pin replay behavior.
8. An unchanged decision-only recovery could be acknowledged before its handling turn completed.
Commit 02f289a retains decision recovery through the same post-handling acknowledgement discipline.
9. A stale acknowledgement could erase a newer recovery interval.
Commit faa015e adds generation compare-and-swap acknowledgement coverage.
10. Persistent Pi and OpenCode successors could recurse on queued pending work, while pre-upgrade queues lacked a generation.
Commit a8b344e adopts legacy queues and prevents successor recovery loops.
11. A crash before the successor or delivery boundary could strand a pending wake.
Commits 7aa2a41 and 39d591e preserve lease-free durable re-drain until the launch boundary is established.
12. A healthy watcher is not proof that the handler received its prompt.
Commit 80f1c04 moves the handling transition after confirmed Pi or OpenCode prompt delivery so a pre-prompt crash re-drains the wake.
13. AFK return could acknowledge a wake before publishing its evidence.
Commit 3c8d6cb publishes AFK evidence before acknowledgement.
14. AFK return could still acknowledge immediately after evidence, before the handling turn completed.
Commit 5c14b67 returns the generation-bound acknowledgement to the handler and retains the wake until that explicit acknowledgement.
15. Regression expectations and documentation had to describe at-least-once replay rather than destructive drain semantics.
Commits 4b454cb, 7042ac6, and ab560ec align behavioral coverage, documentation, and lint with the final contract.

title: fix(composer): unify safe composer detection across backends
body:
## Intent Follow-up commit on the already-validated composer thin-adapter branch (PR https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/2066, checks green): one docs-only change updating docs/verification/runtime-backends.md 'Composer classification matrix' with the genuine trusted-checkout live guard rerun performed after checks passed - the already-agreed post-green step resolving the test step's test-live-trust warning. The pipeline's untrusted gate worktree could not verify claude/grok/muse (first-launch trust dialogs, which the guard refuses to confirm by design); the rerun from the trusted checkout at the final validated head verified all six installed harnesses (claude 2.1.226, codex 0.146.0, opencode 1.14.46, pi 0.84.0, grok 1.0.0, muse 0.1.0-R708.1), the strict blank-row deferral, and the hardened zellij false-positive probe live, with no prompt submitted to any harness. Honesty contract: the record states only what actually ran; kimi remains explicitly absent with no live result claimed. Everything else on the branch is already validated; no code changes in this commit. ## What Changed - Centralize composer shape classification, Unicode whitespace handling, and strict container-proof rules in `fm-composer-lib.sh`, leaving backend adapters responsible only for capture capabilities. - Route Kimi readiness and backend submit verification through the shared classifier, replacing Zellij’s pane-change heuristic with composer-scoped paste and delivery confirmation. - Add portable and live matrix coverage for supported harness shapes and document the trusted-checkout verification results, with Kimi explicitly recorded as absent. ## Risk Assessment 🚨 High: The shared classifier has a source-proven false-empty path that can overwrite unsubmitted user input on three supported backends and requires an explicit product tradeoff to resolve. ## Testing Confirmed the commit changes only the verification document, the installed harness versions and explicit Kimi absence match its recorded output, the live guard remains safely opt-in, and the updated end-user documentation renders correctly. The live run was not repeated because this gate worktree is intentionally untrusted; the change records the supplied trusted-checkout rerun.
Evidence: Rendered Composer classification matrix documentation ```text Composer classification matrix

Composer classification matrix¶ ↑

The shared composer classifier (bin/fm-composer-lib.sh, fm_composer_classify_screen) owns every composer shape fleet-wide; each backend contributes only a capture and a capability descriptor. The live half of that guarantee was verified on 2026-08-10 from an already-trusted checkout at the branch's final validated head, against every installed harness on tmux 3.6a, macOS arm64, on an isolated private socket, with no prompt submitted to any harness. An earlier gate-worktree run could not verify claude, grok, or muse because the pipeline's isolated worktree is untrusted and their first-launch trust dialogs are a real unreadable-composer state the guard refuses to confirm; this trusted-checkout rerun covers all three, and the hardened zellij probe additionally observed its typed text before Enter and accepted only a non-delivery classifier verdict.

FM_COMPOSER_MATRIX_LIVE=1 tests/fm-composer-matrix-live-e2e.test.sh

Every installed harness's real idle composer reached a proven empty, including pi through the tmux foreground-process identity probe, grok through the titled-bottom-border tolerance, and opencode through the left-bar shape; codex and opencode first parked on vendor update-available modals that the strict classifier correctly refused until the guard's single non-submitting Escape dismissed them. The strict blank-row posture held live (a blank shell row deferred injection), and a zellij pane changing for reasons unrelated to submission never confirmed a delivery, replacing the retired content-diff heuristic's false positive. Kimi was not installed on the verification machine; its bordered shape is pinned by the portable byte-capture regressions in tests/fm-composer-lib.test.sh, which also carry the other five adapters' capability profiles for every harness under both a UTF-8 locale and LC_ALL=C. This guard is the refresh command after any harness upgrade; rerun it and update the versions above rather than trusting this table across releases.

--- # Reviewer companion: hazard-by-hazard map and evidence ## What this is One comprehensive, captain-approved refactor of the composer-classification architecture (audit `data/fm-composer-consolidation-audit-s1`, decisions corr=a66f17eb1dffbe7f): every composer shape now lives in ONE shared owner (`bin/fm-composer-lib.sh`, `fm_composer_classify_screen`), the five backend adapters are capture-only plus a declarative capability descriptor (`styled`/`cursor`/`identity`/`rows` as data), fm-spawn's kimi regex (a fourth shape copy) is retired, the whole 30-cell correctness matrix is fixed, and the captain's STRICT blank-row posture applies fleet-wide. A new harness shape is teachable in one place and every backend learns it in the same commit. ## Matrix before/after (idle-empty composer; correct verdict = empty) Before = production code at 85e750a, measured by the audit. After = this branch (portable byte-capture regressions under UTF-8 AND `LC_ALL=C`; live guard for the tmux column). | harness | tmux (UTF-8) | tmux (LC_ALL=C) | cmux | orca | herdr | zellij | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | claude | empty → empty | **pending → empty** | empty → empty | **unknown → empty** | empty (**C: pending**) → empty | **unknown → empty** | | codex | empty → empty | empty → empty | unknown → unknown\* | **pending(banner!) → unknown\*** | empty → empty | **unknown → empty** | | pi | empty(permissive) → empty(identity-proven) | same | unknown → unknown\* | unknown → unknown\* | empty → empty | unknown → unknown\* | | muse | empty → empty | empty → empty | **unknown → empty** | **unknown → empty** | **unknown → empty** | **unknown → empty** | | opencode | **unknown → empty** | **unknown → empty** | **unknown → empty** | **unknown → empty** | **unknown → empty** | **unknown → empty** | | grok | **unknown → empty** | **unknown → empty** | empty → empty | empty → empty | empty → empty | **unknown → empty** | \* the CORRECT reachable verdict for that capability profile (approved design, report §4.3 pt 7): a plain capture cannot distinguish codex's idle hint from typed text (the old orca `pending` came from a startup **banner**, a confidently wrong answer), and a backend without an identity probe cannot prove pi's blank separated row (the strict rule). Net: 13/30 correct before (2 locale-dependent, 1 permissive artifact, 1 false pending) → 25/30 proven-empty + 5 principled defers, 0 false pending, 0 false empty. ## The discrete safety fixes, each its own commit The base commit plus 18 review-round fix commits each prevent a concrete failure. Review rounds were driven gate-by-gate with captain decisions (yolo off); the review agent's adversarial passes found real hazards in both the original code and its own fixes, and each is separately reviewable: **Base commit `ba885d0`** — the consolidation itself plus the audit's six matrix fixes: (1) locale-safe Unicode-space normalization closing #1988 for tmux/herdr (claude's `❯`+U+00A0 read `pending` under `LC_ALL=C`, deferring every away-mode escalation in daemon contexts; cmux's adapter-local NBSP case deleted); (2) muse's `⟩` in the shared glyph set (empty muse composers read `unknown` forever on herdr/cmux/orca); (3) orca learns the borderless bare shape and drops backward paging (every steer to a borderless harness exited unconfirmed; a codex startup banner classified as `pending` composer text); (4) tmux tolerates grok's titled bottom border (every grok steer failed `delivery unconfirmed`; away mode never injected); (5) opencode's left-bar shape (unreadable on every backend); (6) zellij's content-diff submit heuristic replaced by a real `dump-screen --ansi` classifier (the fleet's only FALSE-POSITIVE: any pane change - a clock, a spinner - confirmed delivery and could close a `--resolve-key` decision for a message never received). Plus the strict posture, the pi identity probe for tmux, and the tri-state groundwork. **Review fix commits** (`git log ba885d0..568d205`, oldest first): 1. `c69e0e9` — prevent Pi identity-proof bypass: a lone agent-glyph draft between Pi rules read `empty` after a swallowed Enter; identity now reroutes it to the separated shape (pending) where the capability exists. On identity-less backends bare-wins is the captain-decided tradeoff (byte-identical to Claude's real composer; Pi delivery there is never confirmed anyway; the zellij delta independently protects sends). Also extends the matrix tests toward the full capture x profile x locale cross-product. 2. `9b6917f` — prevent the fix above regressing the #2029 cell: absent/non-Pi identity keeps the bare verdict, so Claude's `❯`+NBSP row stays `empty` on tmux; removed the test fixture that masked the regression with an impossible identity. 3. `f8eb6f7` — harden box structure and titled-border geometry against the widened shape set. 4. `9adb9bb` — prevent false delivery confirmation on an unreadable baseline: the submit core's idle baseline is now tri-state and affirmative (an unreadable pre-typing read disables the unknown→empty turn-started conversion entirely); plus the zellij live-guard fails loudly on setup/source/pane-discovery failures instead of passing vacuously. 5. `29b0844` — prevent a box's bottom border from ever being read as an input row. 6. `612ba2e` — prove the zellij probe actually typed (zellij actions exit 0 while doing nothing): observation before Enter, `send-failed` fails the guard. 7. `e06a12d` — preserve Pi identity uncertainty and scan full left-bar drafts (a multi-row opencode draft below the hint row was missed). 8. `2c2678d` — verify zellij text landed before submitting (typing proof by observation, not exit codes). 9. `11fc737` — scope that observation to the classified composer (a screen-wide substring passed on transcript echoes while an unrelated draft sat in the composer, and rejected legitimate wrapped sends). 10. `0b1d28c` — prove THIS paste landed by composer-scoped pre/post delta (containment passed when the text was already present, or when furniture like opencode's footer matched a short steer such as "high"). 11. `e1a9072` — prevent false `send-failed` on wrapped pastes: cursorless extraction includes the bare composer's wrap region. 12. `0b83c7f` — prevent dead-shell injection: a stale `❯` above an exited agent's live `$` prompt read `empty` cursorlessly; a lower shell-prompt row now invalidates the candidate. 13. `8b68139` — handle bordered shell-glyph placeholders in extraction (a `│ > Type a message... │` baseline broke the paste proof). 14. `cf63973` — prevent injection over streaming output: a bare glyph row with contiguous output directly below no longer reads `empty` cursorlessly (blank/rule-separated harness footers stay inert). 15. `9b44a85` — the same claimed-region rule for box and left-bar candidates (opencode's `╹▀▀▀` floor counted as the shape's own boundary). 16. `d1b2a29` — preserve user bytes: prompt-glyph stripping applies only to the shape's actual prompt row, never wrapped continuation rows (steers quoting `$ cmd` lines were stranded as `send-failed`). 17. `dd32ccf` — prevent steer text executing at a live shell: extraction can never absorb a shell-prompt-shaped row as wrap continuation (a paste landing AT the shell could delta-pass, and Enter would have executed it); agent-glyph continuations stay preserved. 18. `3b7822e` — keep wrapped glyph continuations through submit retries (transcript prompt echoes re-anchor to the live bottom prompt; wrap regions are non-glyph-leading rows only). 19. `174c3b7` — prevent typed placeholder text confirming delivery: the idle pattern proves emptiness only in a shape's own placeholder position; styled text surviving ghost-stripping elsewhere stays pending; plain-capture regex collisions on glyph rows fail safe. 20. `75dd1d4` — restore the two cells the previous fix over-tightened (plain glyph-bearing boxed placeholder stays empty - the grok cell; row-leading agent glyphs re-anchor so normal transcripts select the live bottom prompt instead of blocking away-mode injection indefinitely). 21. `d25a77b` — align the zellij paste proof with those final semantics (boxed placeholder baselines; superseded fixture reworked). `3cea3ae`/`568d205` (docs alignment), `81cb5df` (lint), `74d0ede` (CI fixes), `59eb8f4` (trusted-checkout live rerun record) complete the branch. ## Away-mode validation under STRICT (captain decision blank-row-injection-posture) Path: `inject_msg` → `pane_input_pending` → `fm_backend_composer_state` → thin capture → `fm_composer_classify_screen` (strict rule applied once, in the shared owner). - **Defers** on everything not positively proven: blank cursor rows, dead-shell prompts, bare busy-footer rows, unidentified text, modal dialogs (live-observed: codex/opencode update modals correctly refuse classification), stale composers above live activity. Pinned by `tests/fm-daemon.test.sh`, `tests/fm-composer-lib.test.sh` (`test_strict_blank_row_divergence` - the posture cannot silently regress), `tests/fm-composer-ghost.test.sh`, and live. - **Still injects** when proven: real-tmux end-to-end (`tests/fm-afk-inject-e2e.test.sh`) - defers on human partial input then delivers cleanly after idle; retries a swallowed Enter (wrapped digests included) with exactly one submission; delivers exactly one clean digest into a proven-empty composer. Escalation buffers survive every deferral. - **Send path**: only exact `empty` confirms; the tmux turn-started conversion requires an affirmatively proven idle baseline; zellij requires a composer-scoped typed-text delta - a changed pane is never again a delivery confirmation. ## Live verification `FM_COMPOSER_MATRIX_LIVE=1 tests/fm-composer-matrix-live-e2e.test.sh` from the trusted checkout at this branch's final head (2026-08-10): claude 2.1.226, codex 0.146.0, opencode 1.14.46, pi 0.84.0, grok 1.0.0, muse 0.1.0-R708.1 all classify empty live; strict blank-row deferral held; the hardened zellij probe (typing observed before Enter) confirmed the false-positive dead. Kimi is not installed here - no live result exists or is claimed; its bordered shape is pinned by the portable regressions. Recorded in `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md` "Composer classification matrix". ## Sequencing vs open PRs #1995 / #2047 Both target issue #1988 in the shared owner and were open at intake. This branch implements the locale-safe normalization itself using #1995's exact function names (`fm_composer_normalize_spaces_var` / `fm_composer_normalize_trim_var`) so the implementations converge: if this merges first, #1995's normalization hunks and #2047's fm-composer-lib hunk become redundant (their doc/test additions may still be worth cherry-picking); if either merges first, this branch rebases onto the same names. Captain sequencing call.
