title: fix(bin): carry codex max reasoning effort instead of dropping it
body:
## Intent Make bin/fm-launch-lib.sh carry 'max' effort for the codex harness instead of silently dropping it. effort_flag_for_harness codex max returned an empty string, so a codex-harness dispatch at max carried no effort flag and the model silently ran at its catalog default with nothing reporting the downgrade; the comment justifying the omission claimed the bundled catalog advertises only low|medium|high|xhigh, which is now false. Required outcome: effort_flag_for_harness codex max emits the effort flag, every other currently-supported level stays byte-identical to before, and the comment records that max is verified against the current catalog and rollout evidence instead of asserting the stale catalog claim. 'ultra' (sol and terra only) must stay UNSUPPORTED and must not be added - it has no evidence here. No other harness's effort mapping changes; pi already carries max correctly. bin/fm-launch-lib.sh is the single owner of verified launch commands and their flags, so no second effort mapping may be introduced anywhere else. A colocated test must assert the max arm and must be proven red-capable against the unfixed line rather than trusted on the absence of a dropped flag. Out of scope and deliberately excluded: the two other open guarantee gaps from the same investigation (a missing effort floor, and the sub-agent default, which is a settled decision). Scope note carried beyond the original brief: bin/fm-bootstrap.sh's crew_dispatch_validate held its own copy of the codex effort vocabulary and would have rejected a configured codex max band as an invalid effort, making the launch-site fix unreachable from standing dispatch config, so that existing stale copy was corrected to match with a comment naming fm-launch-lib.sh as the owner, and the harness-adapters effort table's identical stale claim was updated to the dated evidence plus the model-pairing rule. This is firstmate's shared tracked material: one sentence per line in prose, plain dashes, shellcheck-clean bin scripts, colocated tests named after their subject, and no agent as a commit co-author. ## What Changed - `effort_flag_for_harness codex max` in `bin/fm-launch-lib.sh` now emits `-c 'model_reasoning_effort="max"'` instead of returning empty, so a codex dispatch at max no longer runs silently at the model's catalog default. Every other level stays byte-identical, `ultra` stays unsupported, and the comment now records dated codex-cli 0.146.0 catalog and rollout evidence in place of the stale "catalog advertises only low|medium|high|xhigh" claim. A max band paired with a model that lacks it is now refused with a visible 400 `unsupported_value` rather than downgraded. - `crew_dispatch_validate` in `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` held its own jq copy of the codex effort vocabulary and would have rejected a configured `codex:max` as an invalid effort, making the launch-site fix unreachable from standing dispatch config; that copy now matches, with a comment naming `bin/fm-launch-lib.sh` as the owner. `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s harness-adapter ownership span records the jq copy as coupled tracked material, and the `harness-adapters` skill effort table carries the same dated evidence plus the model-pairing rule. - Colocated coverage moved with it: `tests/fm-launch-lib.test.sh` asserts the max arm and the omitted `ultra` arm, `test_codex_omits_invalid_max_effort` became `test_codex_threads_max_effort` asserting the literal launch line, and the bootstrap validation table swapped its codex row for codex-max-accepted plus codex-ultra-flagged. Each assertion was proven red against the unfixed line, in both directions, rather than trusted on the absence of a dropped flag. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A one-token case-pattern addition plus a matching jq list, comment/doc evidence refresh, and colocated tests that assert the exact flag string in both directions; every other harness arm is byte-identical and no second effort mapping exists in the tree. ## Testing Exercised the codex max band end-to-end: a real fm-spawn run now sends `codex --model 'gpt-5.6-luna' -c 'model_reasoning_effort="max"' --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` to the crewmate pane, where the unfixed line sent no effort flag despite recording `effort=max` in task metadata; a full 7x8 effort-flag matrix diff shows codex:max as the only changed pair, with ultra still omitted and every other harness untouched; standing dispatch config with a codex max band is now accepted at session start while codex:ultra and grok:max are still refused. The launch-site, spawn-level, and config-validation assertions were each driven red against the unfixed source (and the ultra guard red in the opposite direction) before being trusted green, and the four targeted suites pass. One setup problem was fixed rather than worked around: tests/lib.sh points NM_HOME at $TMPDIR/fm-test-absent-nm-home, which is populated on this machine from an unrelated run, so fm-bootstrap.test.sh first failed on spurious `VALIDATION_DAEMON: down` noise; re-running under a fresh TMPDIR made it green without deleting the out-of-worktree directory. Transient scratch temp was removed and the worktree verified clean and identical to the target commit.
Evidence: End-to-end: real fm-spawn codex max launch command (fixed vs unfixed line) $ fm-spawn.sh evidence-codex-max <proj> --model gpt-5.6-luna --effort max # harness: codex spawn exit=0 --- literal command sent to the crewmate pane ------------------------- codex --model 'gpt-5.6-luna' -c 'model_reasoning_effort="max"' --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --- recorded task profile (state/evidence-codex-max.meta) ---------------- harness=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna effort=max RESULT: the max band reached the launch command. ===== same dispatch against the UNFIXED line ===== codex --model 'gpt-5.6-luna' --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox harness=codex / model=gpt-5.6-luna / effort=max RESULT: the max band was DROPPED - codex would run at its catalog default. ```text $ fm-spawn.sh evidence-codex-max /tmp/fm-tmpdir-01KZNTKZ/fm-evidence-codex-max.rzRuzv/case/project --model gpt-5.6-luna --effort max # harness: codex warning: /tmp/fm-tmpdir-01KZNTKZ/fm-evidence-codex-max.rzRuzv/case/home/data/evidence-codex-max/brief.md records no delivery contract line (scaffolded before ship briefs recorded one); launching on the explicit --mode no-mistakes - confirm its definition of done matches spawned evidence-codex-max harness=codex kind=ship mode=no-mistakes yolo=off window=firstmate:fm-evidence-codex-max worktree=/tmp/fm-tmpdir-01KZNTKZ/fm-evidence-codex-max.rzRuzv/case/wt spawn exit=0 --- literal command sent to the crewmate pane ------------------------- codex --model 'gpt-5.6-luna' -c 'model_reasoning_effort="max"' --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --- recorded task profile (state/evidence-codex-max.meta) ---------------------------- harness=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna effort=max RESULT: the max band reached the launch command. ```
Evidence: Only codex:max changed - full 7-harness x 8-level effort-flag matrix diff @@ -10,7 +10,7 @@ codex medium -> [-c 'model_reasoning_effort="medium"' ] codex high -> [-c 'model_reasoning_effort="high"' ] codex xhigh -> [-c 'model_reasoning_effort="xhigh"' ] -codex max -> [] +codex max -> [-c 'model_reasoning_effort="max"' ] codex ultra -> [] codex default -> [] codex <empty> -> [] (one changed line across all 56 harness/level pairs) ```text --- /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZNTKZVANF54NEB80VWPCF91/effort-matrix.before.txt 2026-08-10 08:51:26.048624513 -0400 +++ /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZNTKZVANF54NEB80VWPCF91/effort-matrix.after.txt 2026-08-10 08:51:26.108624500 -0400 @@ -10,7 +10,7 @@ codex medium -> [-c 'model_reasoning_effort="medium"' ] codex high -> [-c 'model_reasoning_effort="high"' ] codex xhigh -> [-c 'model_reasoning_effort="xhigh"' ] -codex max -> [] +codex max -> [-c 'model_reasoning_effort="max"' ] codex ultra -> [] codex default -> [] codex -> [] ```
Evidence: Standing crew-dispatch.json: codex max accepted, ultra and grok max still refused $ cat config/crew-dispatch.json {"rules":[{"when":"big feature","use":{"harness":"codex","model":"gpt-5.6-luna","effort":"max"}}]} $ fm-bootstrap.sh # what firstmate prints at session start (no CREW_DISPATCH refusal - config accepted) $ cat config/crew-dispatch.json {"rules":[{"when":"big feature","use":{"harness":"codex","model":"gpt-5.6-sol","effort":"ultra"}}]} $ fm-bootstrap.sh CREW_DISPATCH: invalid config/crew-dispatch.json - invalid effort: codex:ultra $ cat config/crew-dispatch.json {"rules":[{"when":"deep current work","use":{"harness":"grok","model":"grok-4","effort":"max"}}]} $ fm-bootstrap.sh CREW_DISPATCH: invalid config/crew-dispatch.json - invalid effort: grok:max ```text ########## Standing dispatch config: a codex 'max' band is now usable ########## $ cat config/crew-dispatch.json {"rules":[{"when":"big feature","use":{"harness":"codex","model":"gpt-5.6-luna","effort":"max"}}]} $ fm-bootstrap.sh # what firstmate prints at session start (no CREW_DISPATCH refusal - config accepted) ########## 'ultra' still has no evidence here and is still refused ########## $ cat config/crew-dispatch.json {"rules":[{"when":"big feature","use":{"harness":"codex","model":"gpt-5.6-sol","effort":"ultra"}}]} $ fm-bootstrap.sh # what firstmate prints at session start CREW_DISPATCH: invalid config/crew-dispatch.json - invalid effort: codex:ultra ########## other harness ceilings unchanged (grok max still refused) ########## $ cat config/crew-dispatch.json {"rules":[{"when":"deep current work","use":{"harness":"grok","model":"grok-4","effort":"max"}}]} $ fm-bootstrap.sh # what firstmate prints at session start CREW_DISPATCH: invalid config/crew-dispatch.json - invalid effort: grok:max ```
Evidence: Red proof: launch-site and spawn-level tests fail against the unfixed codex arm ########## RED PROOF: codex arm reverted to low|medium|high|xhigh ########## not ok - codex must carry max, not drop it silently FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=1 failed=1 not ok - codex launch did not thread the max reasoning effort (missing: 'codex --model 'gpt-5.6-luna' -c 'model_reasoning_effort="max"' --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox') FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=1 failed=1 ```text ########## RED PROOF: bin/fm-launch-lib.sh codex arm reverted to low|medium|high|xhigh ########## --- end-user surface: same codex max dispatch, unfixed line --- $ fm-spawn.sh evidence-codex-max /tmp/fm-tmpdir-01KZNTKZ/fm-evidence-codex-max.6Cr0pH/case/project --model gpt-5.6-luna --effort max # harness: codex spawn exit=0 --- literal command sent to the crewmate pane ------------------------- codex --model 'gpt-5.6-luna' --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --- recorded task profile (state/evidence-codex-max.meta) ---------------------------- harness=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna effort=max RESULT: the max band was DROPPED - codex would run at its catalog default. --- tests/fm-launch-lib.test.sh (colocated test) --- not ok - codex must carry max, not drop it silently FM_TEST_END 2026-08-10T12:52:18Z tests/fm-launch-lib.test.sh exit=1 duration_ms=101 gate_skip=false FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=1 failed=1 skipped_gate=0 duration_ms=132 --- tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh (spawn-level) --- not ok - codex launch did not thread the max reasoning effort (missing: 'codex --model 'gpt-5.6-luna' -c 'model_reasoning_effort="max"' --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox') FM_TEST_END 2026-08-10T12:52:43Z tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh exit=1 duration_ms=24320 gate_skip=false FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=1 failed=1 skipped_gate=0 duration_ms=24352 ```

title: feat(bin): add read-only sweep for GitHub writes missing the attribution token
body:
## Intent Put the retained-probe known-positive label where a triager actually stands, and record that the preserved evidence note agrees with the guide. Follow-up commit on the existing validated branch for the sol-attribution-convention task: keep every prior pipeline fix commit present, never abort-and-restart or replace the branch. Base task context, unchanged: implement the captain's ruled attribution convention for browser-Sol GitHub writes (token SOL-AI:, reachable at prompt-composition time via bin/fm-attribution-sweep.sh --convention, owned by docs/model-write-attribution.md) and make omissions DETECTABLE after the fact via that sweep, because write-time enforcement is impossible on this identity. Do NOT build write-time enforcement. The sweep stays read-only, reports candidates plus evidence rather than claiming authorship, and keeps could-not-observe as an outcome distinct from clean. This commit implements the supervisor's explicit instruction that the triage labelling is LOAD-BEARING and must be explicit and easy to apply, not a footnote, because an unlabelled permanent known-positive gets investigated as a real finding by someone every single time. Two changes. 1. The sweep's own summary now tells the reader that some candidates are known permanent ones: a 2026-08-02 capability probe left five deliberately unprefixed writes in place as the sweep's only real-world red control, that reporting them is correct behaviour rather than a finding, and that a candidate dated 2026-08-02 should be checked against the recognition table in docs/model-write-attribution.md before being investigated. A document a reader has to know to open is not a label; the pointer has to be in the output they are holding. Two colocated assertions cover this and were proven red-capable by removing the pointer and watching the suite fail. 2. docs/model-write-attribution.md now records that the preserved evidence note at data/sol-capability-probe/github-evidence.md AGREES with the guide - it keeps the artifacts, calls them a deliberate permanent known-positive, states a sweep reporting them is working correctly, and defers recognition to the guide by name. The page also states plainly that this agreement is load-bearing and has already failed once: the note previously opened by saying the artifacts had been deleted, which would lead a reader to conclude any 2026-08-02 candidate must be genuine, the exact inversion the section exists to prevent. It records that NO TEST can catch a repeat, because the note is private to the operator's home and gitignored, therefore absent from every clone and every CI run, so a check asserting agreement between the two documents would pass without reading anything and report green while examining nothing. Hand reconciliation is named as the only real control. Preserve that reasoning: do not add or suggest an automated check across that boundary, and do not soften the statement into an implied guarantee. Standing constraint for this run, from the supervisor: any review finding that asserts the CONTENTS of a file under data/ is unverifiable from this worktree, because data/ is gitignored and the probe evidence path does not exist here. Such findings must be routed to firstmate rather than acted on. A finding in an earlier round quoted a line of that note which no longer exists, and acting on it would have reintroduced the inversion one level further out. Other constraints still in force: firstmate shared tracked material, so firstmate-coding-guidelines applies; one sentence per line in prose; plain dashes, never em dashes; shellcheck-clean bin/ scripts; colocated tests; never add an agent as a commit co-author; never carry the captain-address convention into a commit message, PR title, or PR body; use gh-axi for GitHub, never raw gh. Out of scope: refreshing the portable-serial shard table in docs/fm-test-portable-shards.md, which is pre-existing drift filed separately. ## What Changed - New `bin/fm-attribution-sweep.sh`: a read-only, GET-only sweep that lists issue comments, reviews, and commits made under one account that lack the `SOL-AI:` attribution token. Every scope ends in exactly one of observed-clean, candidates, or could-not-observe, so an unreachable API, exhausted budget, or truncated page never folds into a clean run; candidates print evidence instead of asserting authorship, and `--convention` / `--token` make the convention reachable at prompt-composition time. `--since` is validated for both spelling and component ranges (`30d`, month 13, day 32, hour 24 all exit 64 before any GitHub call), a run that resolves no repository cannot report clean, and the request/page budgets are printed rather than silently narrowing what was examined. - The sweep's summary now labels the retained 2026-08-02 capability-probe writes as a known permanent red control, states that reporting them is correct behaviour rather than a finding, and points a triager at the recognition table before they investigate; the sweep still does not filter them out. - New `docs/model-write-attribution.md` owns the convention, the sweep's coverage limits, and the five-artifact recognition table, and records that the preserved private evidence note agrees with the guide, that this agreement has already failed once, and that hand reconciliation is the only control since the note is absent from every clone and CI run. Registered in `docs/scripts.md` and `docs/documentation-audiences.json`; colocated `tests/fm-attribution-sweep.test.sh` (51 assertions) is wired into `bin/fm-test-run.sh`'s `pr-forge` family, and the two new labelling assertions were proven red-capable by deleting the pointer. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The only substantive prior finding is fixed and pinned by tests on both sides (impossible dates refused, real timestamps still swept), the envelope extraction is a pure mechanical deduplication with every call site verified, and the remaining gap is a single missing test input for one already-implemented guard. ## Testing Ran the colocated sweep contract suite and the docs-audience test (both green), then produced product-level evidence rather than relying on pass/fail: a real CLI transcript of a sweep whose window covers 2026-08-02, where retained probe comment 5158866063 is reported beside an unrelated candidate and the printed summary tells the reader the 2026-08-02 candidates are known permanent ones, that reporting them is correct behaviour, and where the recognition table lives; a follow-the-pointer check showing that heading and that exact identifier in docs/model-write-attribution.md; a mutation run proving the two new assertions go red when the pointer paragraph is removed; and a CLI transcript showing impossible --since components refused with exit 64 and no GitHub calls while a leap-second timestamp still sweeps. The change is CLI-output and markdown prose, so the end-user surface is the terminal transcript itself, which is captured verbatim; there is no rendered UI to screenshot. Worktree left clean and scratch copies removed.
Evidence: Triager CLI transcript: probe candidate reported with the known-positive label in the summary FM_SWEEP_CANDIDATE repo=sbracewell64/firstmate kind=comment ref=5158866063 when=2026-08-02T15:17:41Z url=https://github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate/issues/24#issuecomment-5158866063 evidence=assoc=OWNER,via_app=chatgpt-codex-connector,token=absent FM_SWEEP_CANDIDATE repo=sbracewell64/firstmate kind=comment ref=5209911402 when=2026-08-09T18:02:10Z url=https://github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate/issues/2077#issuecomment-5209911402 evidence=assoc=OWNER,via_app=none,token=absent FM_SWEEP_SUMMARY scopes=1 observed=1 could_not_observe=0 declared=0 candidates=2 requests=1 outcome=candidates ... Some candidates are known permanent ones. A capability probe on 2026-08-02 left five deliberately unprefixed writes in place as this sweep's only real-world red control, and reporting them is correct behaviour rather than a finding. Before investigating any candidate dated 2026-08-02, check it against the table in docs/model-write-attribution.md under "The retained probe writes". $ echo $? 10 ```text FM_SWEEP_BEGIN 2026-08-10T16:57:28Z account=sbracewell64 since=2026-08-01T00:00:00Z token=SOL-AI: repos=1 budget=300 FM_SWEEP_CANDIDATE repo=sbracewell64/firstmate kind=comment ref=5158866063 when=2026-08-02T15:17:41Z url=https://github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate/issues/24#issuecomment-5158866063 evidence=assoc=OWNER,via_app=chatgpt-codex-connector,token=absent FM_SWEEP_CANDIDATE repo=sbracewell64/firstmate kind=comment ref=5209911402 when=2026-08-09T18:02:10Z url=https://github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate/issues/2077#issuecomment-5209911402 evidence=assoc=OWNER,via_app=none,token=absent FM_SWEEP_SCOPE repo=sbracewell64/firstmate kind=comments outcome=observed examined=2 declared=0 candidates=2 FM_SWEEP_SUMMARY scopes=1 observed=1 could_not_observe=0 declared=0 candidates=2 requests=1 outcome=candidates This sweep cannot determine who wrote anything. A candidate is a write under this account that does not carry SOL-AI: - which is equally what an undeclared model session and the captain's own hand-typed comment look like in every field GitHub exposes. The evidence on each line is a signal, not an attribution; the captain judges. Some candidates are known permanent ones. A capability probe on 2026-08-02 left five deliberately unprefixed writes in place as this sweep's only real-world red control, and reporting them is correct behaviour rather than a finding. Before investigating any candidate dated 2026-08-02, check it against the table in docs/model-write-attribution.md under "The retained probe writes". This run covered everything since 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z, as given by --since, and writes outside it were not examined at all - a clean result says nothing about them. Widen the window with --since or FM_SWEEP_WINDOW_DAYS=, and raise --budget with it: reviews and commits each spend about one request per pull request in the window, so a wider window on the current budget of 300 will report could-not-observe instead of a result. $ echo $? 10 ```
Evidence: The summary's pointer resolves to the recognition table for the reported candidate $ grep -n "^## The retained probe writes" docs/model-write-attribution.md 113:## The retained probe writes, and how to recognise them $ grep -n "5158866063" docs/model-write-attribution.md 122:| Issue comment | `5158866063` | body carries the nonce | ```text $ # A triager holding candidate 5158866063 follows the pointer the summary gave them. $ grep -n "^## The retained probe writes" docs/model-write-attribution.md 113:## The retained probe writes, and how to recognise them $ grep -n "5158866063" docs/model-write-attribution.md 122:| Issue comment | `5158866063` | body carries the nonce | 164:These five already earned their keep: proving the sweep against them is what exposed a real defect, an early filter that skipped app-performed writes and would therefore have hidden comment `5158866063` - the single most representative example of what the sweep exists to catch. $ # ...and the section states the preserved evidence note agrees with the guide. $ sed -n "/^### Why they exist/,/^### Why they were not deleted/p" docs/model-write-attribution.md ### Why they exist They are what a browser model session produced on 2026-08-02 when it was asked to prove it could comment, review, and push a commit. That measurement is the evidence the whole convention rests on: every one of them recorded the account owner with `author_association: OWNER` and no bot marker, which is why write-time enforcement was ruled impossible and detection after the fact was chosen instead. Independent evidence is preserved outside this repository at `data/sol-capability-probe/github-evidence.md`. That note agrees with this section: it records the decision to keep the artifacts, calls them a deliberate permanent known-positive, states that a sweep reporting them is working correctly, and leaves the question of how to recognise them to this page. It enumerates only four artifacts, omitting scaffolding commit `3e05033a95a1`, which appears there as a parent SHA rather than as a swept write. The table above supersedes it on the set, and every entry was verified against the live API rather than copied from the note. Those two documents agreeing that the artifacts still exist is what keeps this section usable, and they have already disagreed once. The note previously opened by saying the artifacts had been deleted, which would lead a reader here to conclude that any candidate dated 2026-08-02 must be genuine - the exact inversion this section exists to prevent. No test can catch a repeat, because the note is private to the operator's home and absent from every clone and CI run, so a check asserting agreement would pass without reading anything. Whoever edits either document reconciles both by hand. ### Why they were not deleted ```

title: fix(bin): carry codex max reasoning effort instead of dropping it
body:
## Intent Make bin/fm-launch-lib.sh carry 'max' effort for the codex harness instead of silently dropping it. effort_flag_for_harness codex max returned an empty string, so a codex-harness dispatch at max carried no effort flag and the model silently ran at its catalog default with nothing reporting the downgrade; the comment justifying the omission claimed the bundled catalog advertises only low|medium|high|xhigh, which is now false. Required outcome: effort_flag_for_harness codex max emits the effort flag, every other currently-supported level stays byte-identical to before, and the comment records that max is verified against the current catalog and rollout evidence instead of asserting the stale catalog claim. Verified 2026-08-10 on codex-cli 0.146.0: the catalog advertises max for gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-sol-wm, gpt-5.6-terra and codex-auto-review, and a max run on gpt-5.6-luna was accepted. 'ultra' (sol, sol-wm and terra only) must stay UNSUPPORTED and must not be added - it has no evidence here. No other harness's effort mapping changes; pi already carries max correctly. bin/fm-launch-lib.sh is the single owner of verified launch commands and their flags, so no NEW second effort mapping may be introduced anywhere else. A colocated test must assert the max arm and be proven red-capable rather than trusted on the absence of a dropped flag. Accepted scope beyond the original brief: bin/fm-bootstrap.sh's crew_dispatch_validate held an EXISTING second copy of the codex effort vocabulary and would have rejected a configured codex max band as invalid, making the launch-site fix unreachable from standing dispatch config, so that stale copy was corrected to match with a comment naming fm-launch-lib.sh as the owner, and the harness-adapters effort table's identical stale claim was updated to the dated evidence plus the model-pairing rule. Which levels a given model accepts is a routing concern rather than this flag's: a model without max is now refused with a visible 400 unsupported_value, which is the accepted tradeoff over the prior silent downgrade. Out of scope and deliberately excluded: the general per-harness-per-effort parity harness (filed as follow-up effort-vocabulary-parity-test), and the two other open guarantee gaps from the same investigation (a missing effort floor, and the sub-agent default, a settled decision). Context for this run: this branch was cut fresh from the fork trunk to remediate a wrong-venue pull request, and it carries a document-step commit from the prior run, so this run exists to validate THESE exact bytes rather than relying on a run bound to a different head. This is firstmate's shared tracked material: one sentence per line in prose, plain dashes, shellcheck-clean bin scripts, colocated tests named after their subject, and no agent as a commit co-author. ## What Changed - `effort_flag_for_harness codex max` in `bin/fm-launch-lib.sh` now emits `-c 'model_reasoning_effort="max"'` instead of returning empty, so a codex dispatch at max no longer runs silently at the model's catalog default; `low|medium|high|xhigh` stay byte-identical, `ultra` stays unsupported, and the stale "catalog advertises only low|medium|high|xhigh" comment is replaced with the dated codex-cli 0.146.0 catalog and rollout evidence. - `crew_dispatch_validate` in `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` held an existing jq copy of the codex effort vocabulary that would have rejected a configured `codex:max` band before it reached the launch site; that copy now admits `max` and carries a comment naming `bin/fm-launch-lib.sh` as the owner. No new effort mapping was added anywhere. - Colocated tests pin the new behavior — `tests/fm-launch-lib.test.sh` asserts the codex `max` flag and continued `ultra` omission, `tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh` pins the literal launch command end to end, and `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` covers codex `max` accepted / codex `ultra` flagged. Docs follow: the harness-adapters effort table records the model-pairing rule (a model without `max` is refused with a visible 400 `unsupported_value` rather than downgraded), `docs/configuration.md` notes harness acceptance is not model acceptance, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` records bootstrap's jq copy in the adapter-ownership span. Note on delta scope: the supplied base (`33a4287`, upstream main) makes the mechanical diff the entire fork trunk (254 files) because this branch was cut fresh from the fork trunk to remediate a wrong-venue PR. The trunk commits are already-landed fork work with their own prior gate runs; the change under review here is `720f06e..HEAD`, described above. The pipeline's Rebase step was skipped for the same reason, and its Review, Test, and Document infos are recorded assumptions rather than defects — including a local-environment test trap where `tests/lib.sh`'s deterministically-absent `NM_HOME` path is populated on this machine (a fresh `TMPDIR` makes the bootstrap suite pass). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A four-line vocabulary change plus its one pre-existing jq mirror, fully covered by positive assertions at the launch site, config validator, and end-to-end spawn command, with every other harness arm and level left byte-identical. ## Testing Ran the three suites that own this behavior (fm-launch-lib, fm-spawn-dispatch-profile, fm-bootstrap) plus fm-secondmate-harness as the other codex effort-flag consumer - all green. One spurious fm-bootstrap failure came from a local path collision where the "absent" NM_HOME fixture path holds a real no-mistakes home; rerunning under a fresh TMPDIR cleared it, and it is unrelated to the change. Beyond the suites I produced product-level evidence: a real fm-spawn run showing the literal codex launch command gaining `-c 'model_reasoning_effort="max"'` where the pre-fix library launched with no effort flag despite meta recording effort=max, a real fm-bootstrap session-start transcript showing a configured codex max band go from refused to accepted while codex ultra and grok max stay refused, and a full base-vs-target matrix proving exactly one (harness, effort) cell changed. Each new assertion was driven red by mutating the source and restored, leaving the worktree clean at 6667295. This change has no UI surface, so the artifacts are CLI transcripts rather than screenshots.

title: feat(bin): add guarded Linux dependency checker
body:
## What Changed

- Add `fm-deps.sh` to audit Linux workspace dependencies, report their status, offer individually confirmed upgrades in interactive runs, and keep `--check` report-only.
- Coordinate dependency checks with guarded Firstmate and secondmate updates through shared host locking, identity-bound journals, and recovery of pending reread and nudge actions.
- Document the checker and its configuration, and extend changed-file selection and regression coverage across dependency, bootstrap, update, and secondmate sync flows.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Captain, the latest commit correctly rejects symlinked journal storage and avoids cumulative waits on nested transaction locks without weakening update durability.

## Testing

Preflight and the corrected changed-file selector succeeded; all directly relevant and supporting behavioral suites passed. After correcting an evidence-fixture lock-path error, the live `--check` command exited successfully with zero mutations, while the PTY run showed eight separate consent prompts and zero completed upgrades after all were declined. Reviewer-visible transcripts were saved, and the working tree remained clean.

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

<details>
<summary>⏭️ **intent** - skipped</summary>

✅ No issues found.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 **Review** - 4 issues found → auto-fixed (22) ✅</summary>

- 🚨 `bin/fm-deps.sh:342` - Post-update actions are not durable. If instruction rereading is declined or any `fm-send.sh` call fails, processing stops after `fm-update.sh` has already advanced the checkouts; the next run sees them as current and emits no targets, permanently losing the remaining reread notifications. Persist pending notifications before attempting delivery and retry every target.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:105` - Remote and local probes such as `npm view`, `gh-axi release list`, `git ls-remote`, and Herdr inspection are unbounded and run sequentially. One stalled client can prevent all later checks and the summary; run probes through the repository's existing timeout helper and disable interactive Git credential prompts.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:429` - The displayed npm version is discarded in favour of `@latest`, and successful exit status is accepted without verifying the active executable. A dist-tag race or mismatched npm prefix can therefore install or report a version different from the one approved; install `$latest` explicitly and verify the post-update version before counting success.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:354` - These npm upgrades are two-step operations. If installation succeeds but `setup hooks` fails, a later run sees the package as current and never retries hook setup, leaving an incomplete installation; persist or independently re-check the hook postcondition.

🔧 Fix: Harden dependency updates and bound probes
4 issues (2 errors, 2 warnings) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-deps.sh:514` - Persistence still stops at the first marker-write failure. Because `fm-update.sh` has already advanced every target, a corrupt or unwritable marker for one second mate prevents all later targets from being recorded, and the next update run cannot regenerate them. Stage the complete action inventory atomically, or continue recording every target before returning failure.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-deps.sh:960` - When a pending Firstmate reread is declined or invalid, the failure only increments `FAILURES`; the script then continues into dependency prompts and may perform upgrades while its required instructions remain unread. Stop the mutation path until the reread marker is cleared.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:580` - The new second-mate retry record stores only a selector and message, then sends to whichever current metadata owns that selector. Reuse the existing identity-bound nudge record and startup retry path, which verify the target is still the same second mate, home, and instruction commit before delivery.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:462` - A pending hook record becomes permanently unrecoverable when the active package version changes: the retry rejects the mismatch, while the ordinary check can report the newer version as current without updating or clearing the marker. Safely supersede the record and obtain consent to run hook setup for the active approved version.

🔧 Fix: Harden dependency update durability and retry ownership
3 issues (1 error, 2 warnings) still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:772` - The action manifest remains selector-only until reread confirmation. If a secondmate is removed or reassigned while confirmation is pending, this late lookup binds and sends the action to the replacement. Persist home, commit, and remote placement with the initial inventory, then validate them at delivery.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-deps.sh:542` - This unconditionally removes a shared nudge path after sending without holding its owning fleet/remote transaction lock or confirming the record is unchanged. A concurrent bootstrap/config writer can replace the marker while `fm-send.sh` runs, after which this removal erases the newer retry action. Consume the queue through its locked owner or compare-and-delete an immutable snapshot.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:74` - Zero-padded zero values such as `00` pass this validation, but `timeout 00` disables the deadline, defeating the probe bound. Reject values whose digits are all zero before calling `fm_run_timed`.

🔧 Fix: Bind update identities, preserve retries, and enforce timeouts
1 error still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-deps.sh:436` - This fixed manifest path is overwritten without any per-home transaction lock. Two checker invocations can both pass the pending-action check; after one updater emits real targets, the other can report already-current/none and replace this inventory before consumption, permanently losing required notifications. Serialize pending processing through update/action publication, or use exclusive manifests that are safely merged.

🔧 Fix: Serialize Firstmate update actions per home
3 issues (1 error, 2 warnings) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-deps.sh:1440` - The lock is not run-wide: this unlocked precheck can return false, after which another invocation may update Firstmate and publish or consume `reread=yes` while this process continues executing the old sourced script and performing global upgrades. If the checkout becomes current, `check_firstmate` never rechecks pending actions and this run can exit successfully; serialize complete checker executions per home, or guard every mutation and pending-action recheck with the same lock.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:423` - Lock acquisition is unbounded, while the callback holds the lock across reread input and every `fm-send.sh` delivery. An unattended prompt or stuck send therefore makes every concurrent invocation, including `--check`, hang before producing a summary; bound acquisition and return a clear deferred/busy result.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:1440` - Action processing is now conditional on a detector that does not validate the pending directory itself. An empty symlink or non-directory at `.fm-deps-pending` produces no matching actions, so the checker can continue and report success despite an unusable durable action store; validate the directory before declaring there is no pending work.

🔧 Fix: Serialize checker runs and validate action storage
3 issues (2 errors, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-deps.sh:480` - The run lock is stored under each isolated `FM_HOME`, but npm, APT, NVM, and most CLI upgrades are host-global. A primary and local secondmate can therefore acquire different locks and mutate the same installations concurrently; use a host/installation-wide dependency lock, retaining a separate per-home action lock where needed.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-deps.sh:65` - The recorded HEAD is sampled after Bash has already opened and begun sourcing the implementation, so it does not identify the code actually loaded. If another invocation fast-forwards between script loading and this sample, old code can record the new SHA and pass the post-lock comparison; re-exec the current implementation under ownership or use an update generation that reliably defers overlapping starts.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:66` - This new revision probe is unbounded, and `|| true` converts every failure into an empty value that disables stale-code verification. A stalled Git blocks before any summary, while a failed probe permits upgrade-capable checks without revision protection; use the bounded probe path and fail or defer when the revision cannot be captured.

🔧 Fix: Serialize dependency checks across homes and re-exec
3 issues (1 error, 2 warnings) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-deps.sh:526` - The host lock is observed only by `fm-deps.sh`; `fm-update.sh`, bootstrap, and spawn still fast-forward Firstmate or secondmate checkouts without it. A primary lifecycle operation can therefore replace a secondmate's loaded checker while that checker owns the host lock and performs upgrades; make every tracked-checkout updater participate in the same protocol or defer updates while the lock is held.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:512` - An existing `FM_DEPS_HOST_LOCK_DIR` may be any owned absolute directory, but this unconditionally changes it to mode 0700. A mistaken override pointing at a home, cache, worktree, or `/` when running as root alters unrelated permissions; only chmod a newly created dedicated directory, and reject unsafe existing targets.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:510` - Two first-ever invocations can both observe the host-lock directory as absent; the loser of `mkdir` returns a hard “invalid directory” failure instead of proceeding to bounded lock contention. On `EEXIST`, revalidate the newly created directory and continue.

🔧 Fix: Coordinate dependency checks with checkout updates
3 issues (1 error, 2 warnings) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-deps.sh:1167` - Post-update actions are still created only after `fm-update.sh` completes. An interruption or unexpected child exit after a fast-forward but before action persistence leaves no manifest; the next run sees current checkouts and never requests the required reread or nudges. Journal an identity-bound transaction before changing HEAD and finalize it as each target advances.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:990` - The updater returns only selectors, so action identities are re-resolved from mutable metadata after the update. A concurrent retirement or reassignment can therefore bind and later nudge a replacement secondmate; capture home, commit, and remote placement during the same update sweep that selected each target.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-dependency-lock-lib.sh:28` - The predictable lock directory under world-writable `/tmp` can be pre-created by another local user. The ownership check then rejects it, while `/tmp`'s sticky bit prevents the intended user removing it, disabling checks and updates until administrative cleanup; use a verified owner-private runtime directory such as `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`.

🔧 Fix: Journal updates and secure runtime locks
4 issues (2 errors, 2 warnings) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-deps.sh:804` - Remote `prepared` and `updated` journals are handled identically. If `fm-on.sh` fails before updating—or execution stops after journal publication—the next run sends a nudge and deletes the journal without verifying the remote checkout; because the primary may already be current, the updater may never retry and the remote secondmate remains stale. Persist a verified remote commit/outcome and reconcile or retry `prepared` records before converting them to nudges.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-dependency-lock-lib.sh:61` - The default host-lock root depends on each process's `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `TMPDIR`, or `HOME`. Two same-UID invocations with different valid environment directories acquire different locks and can concurrently mutate host-global dependencies and checkouts. Resolve one stable per-user, per-host lock location independent of caller-specific environment.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-dependency-lock-lib.sh:63` - An invalid optional runtime candidate immediately aborts instead of trying later safe candidates. For example, with no `/run/user/$UID` and `TMPDIR=/tmp`, the private `HOME` fallback is never reached, disabling dependency checks and checkout updates. Continue past invalid candidates and fail only when none is safe.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-update.sh:221` - Every nonzero callback result—including journal-finalization failures after a successful fast-forward—is relabelled as `dependency lock is unavailable`. Preserve callback failures separately and emit an explicit update/journal diagnostic so operators are not directed toward the wrong remediation.

🔧 Fix: Harden remote update recovery and host locking
4 issues (3 errors, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-dependency-lock-lib.sh:108` - The lock namespace changes when `/run/user/$UID` appears or disappears. A headless process can acquire the account-home fallback, then a login creates `/run/user/$UID` and a second invocation acquires a different lock, allowing concurrent host-global mutations. Use one lifecycle-stable location or coordinate both namespaces during transitions.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-update.sh:168` - The initial remote update does not pass the new expected-placement values. After the journal captures one target, a concurrent registry reassignment can make `fm-on.sh` update the replacement while the result remains attributed to the original identity. Bind the initial call to the captured placement just like recovery.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-on.sh:106` - Expected placement covers only host and home, although the route's executable code source also includes `root`. A root-only cutover therefore passes recovery validation and executes the pending update from a different checkout. Persist `remote_root` in the journal and validate it in `fm-on.sh`.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-dependency-lock-lib.sh:69` - Lock-path discovery invokes NSS-backed `id -un`, `getent`, and `dscl` without a deadline before bounded lock acquisition begins. A stalled directory service can therefore hang every checker and checkout updater indefinitely; bound these lookups or use a nonblocking stable identity source.

🔧 Fix: Stabilize host locking and bind remote placements
3 issues (2 errors, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-deps.sh:1735` - `--check` unconditionally processes pending actions. Prepared remote journals execute `fm-on.sh ... update`, while pending nudges call `fm-send.sh` and clear records, so the documented report-only mode can mutate remote checkouts and message agents. In check-only mode, report pending reconciliation without executing or clearing it.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-deps.sh:853` - The remote journal validates and persists `remote_root`, but drops it when converting the journal into a retry nudge. If the route root changes before delivery or during a retry, `fm-send.sh` re-resolves and executes through the replacement root, then clears the old action. Persist and validate the root through the nudge record and expected-placement send path.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-dependency-lock-lib.sh:111` - The supposedly stable host-lock namespace is keyed by mutable `uname -n`. If the hostname changes while one invocation holds the old path, another invocation can acquire a new path and concurrently mutate host-global dependencies or checkouts. Use a lifecycle-stable machine identity or coordinate both namespaces during transitions.

🔧 Fix: Harden dependency checks, retries, and host locking
1 warning still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-secondmate-nudge-lib.sh:80` - Remote retry markers written by the base schema contain neither `remote_host` nor `remote_root`, so this strict matcher rejects every surviving pre-upgrade marker. Bootstrap and config push then preserve the marker but abort convergence on every run, leaving the remote secondmate permanently unnudgeable without manual state repair. Add an explicit legacy-marker reconciliation or migration path that re-establishes current placement safely.

🔧 Fix: Migrate legacy remote nudge markers safely
1 warning still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:1247` - Every shared nudge marker globally blocks later Firstmate updates, but ownerless bootstrap/config markers have no terminal path when their secondmate is retired or its recorded home changes: dependency action processing ignores them, bootstrap cannot match them, and teardown does not remove them. One failed nudge can therefore defer all future checker-driven self-updates indefinitely; retire or quarantine these markers atomically during route teardown/reassignment, or make this gate consider only actionable live records.

🔧 Fix: Retire stale secondmate nudge markers safely
3 issues (1 error, 2 warnings) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-deps.sh:688` - This claims and replaces the shared marker without taking the per-secondmate remote-inheritance lock used by bootstrap and config push. If either sender already read the old marker, it can later unconditionally remove the newly published `fm-deps` marker after sending the old action; the update journal is then cleared and the required reread notification is permanently lost. Serialize retirement/publication with that per-ID lock, or require every sender to compare-and-delete an immutable snapshot.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:1276` - Any nonempty owner is declared actionable before validating its schema or live identity. An `owner=fm-deps` marker for a retired or reassigned secondmate is repeatedly rejected and restored by delivery processing, while this check permanently defers every later Firstmate update. Validate owned records and quarantine them once their recorded identity is definitively obsolete.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:1354` - A stale ownerless marker is ignored here but never retired. When Firstmate is already current, no later publication removes it, while remote bootstrap and config push reject its mismatched placement before convergence; a reassigned remote secondmate can therefore remain stuck indefinitely. Quarantine the marker during confirmed route retirement/reassignment or add a safe non-check cleanup path.

🔧 Fix: Serialize and retire stale nudge records
3 warnings still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:323` - The newly shared marker lock uses unbounded `fm_lock_acquire_wait`, whose failure branch cannot run while a live or stuck owner remains. A stalled sender can therefore hang the entire bootstrap before retrying markers or completing a local fast-forward; use bounded acquisition and report the nudge as deferred.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:1391` - Ordinary lock contention returns status 75, but this collapses it into generic failure (as do the delivery loops). The top level therefore records a false failure and continues upgrade-capable checks instead of using its busy/deferred path; preserve status 75 through cleanup and delivery.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:127` - `dpkg-query -W` exits nonzero when a package has never been installed, so this return bypasses the intended empty-installed result. Fresh systems consequently report GitHub CLI or tmux as UNKNOWN failures instead of MISSING; distinguish an absent package from an actual probe failure and still inspect the APT candidate.

🔧 Fix: Harden nudge contention and APT absence handling
2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:327` - After `process_secondmate` has already fast-forwarded the home, this busy branch returns without creating a retry marker. A concurrent sender can deliver its older reread before that fast-forward, later clear its marker, and leave the new instruction commit permanently unnudgeable because subsequent bootstraps see the checkout as current. Journal the new identity and commit before advancing HEAD, or otherwise guarantee a durable action before returning.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-deps.sh:1685` - `handle_firstmate_update_actions` can now return 75 when a nudge transaction is busy, but this converts it to status 1 after `fm-update.sh` may already have updated and journaled checkouts. The run consequently reports a failed guarded update instead of a safe deferral; preserve 75 here and have `check_firstmate` count it as deferred rather than failed.

🔧 Fix: Journal nudge updates and preserve busy deferrals
1 error still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:355` - This replace-mode write overwrites any existing undelivered nudge before the Git fast-forward succeeds. If execution is interrupted, the speculative marker no longer matches the current HEAD; if the merge fails, `fm_ff_abort_fast_forward` deletes it outright. A prior failed notification—including an `owner=fm-deps` action—can therefore be lost while the home remains unadvanced and later skipped sweeps cannot reconstruct it. Preserve and restore the previous marker, or use a separate prepared-update journal.

🔧 Fix: Preserve prior nudges across speculative updates
1 error still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:355` - The preserve branch has no supersession path for speculative markers. If bootstrap stops after recording commit B but before advancing the home, then the primary advances to C, retry rejects B because the home is still at A while this gate rejects C because the marker names B; every later bootstrap repeats the deadlock. Store prepared updates separately with before/after/phase metadata and reconcile or safely supersede them after validating ancestry.

🔧 Fix: Reconcile interrupted secondmate sync journals
2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:419` - Journal-to-marker conversion is not protected by the host-wide checkout lock. Recovery snapshots `HEAD` at line 396 while holding only the per-ID lock, and normal finalization likewise runs after `ff_target` releases the host lock; another guarded updater can advance the home before publication, causing a marker for the stale commit to replace the journal. If delivery fails, exact-HEAD retry cannot consume that marker. Hold the host lock through reconciliation and publication, then acquire the per-ID lock in a consistent order.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:380` - Interrupted sync journals have no retirement or reassignment cleanup. Missing metadata or a changed home returns while preserving the journal, and no teardown or stale-action path references `.secondmate-sync-pending`; reusing that ID at a new home then makes every later update reject the old journal. Quarantine or remove it under the per-ID transaction lock during confirmed retirement or reassignment.

🔧 Fix: Serialize sync journal recovery and retire obsolete records
2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:400` - Reassignment cleanup quarantines only the sync journal. An interruption after publishing its nudge marker but before removing the journal leaves both records; this branch retires the journal, but retry retains the old-home marker and `fm_ff_before_fast_forward` then rejects every update for the replacement home. Atomically quarantine a matching stale companion marker under the same per-ID lock while preserving unrelated or current markers.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:469` - Host-lock contention is paid separately for every pending journal. Because all iterations contend on the same lock, N interrupted secondmates can delay bootstrap by N times `FM_DEPS_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (five seconds by default); acquire the host lock once for the batch, or stop and mark the remaining journals deferred after the first busy result.

🔧 Fix: Retire stale nudges and batch journal recovery
1 warning still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:485` - This acquires the host-wide lock whenever `.secondmate-sync-pending` exists, even when it contains no journals. The directory remains after successful recovery, so every later bootstrap can wait the full `FM_DEPS_LOCK_TIMEOUT` behind an active dependency check despite having no recovery work; verify at least one regular `.pending` file exists before locking.

🔧 Fix: Skip host locking for empty sync queues
2 warnings still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:485` - The queue preflight accepts a symlinked `.secondmate-sync-pending` directory because `[ -d ]` follows links. Regular journals behind it pass the final-component `! -L` check, allowing recovery to remove or quarantine files outside state even though the journal writer rejects symlink parents. Require the directory itself to be a non-symlink and report invalid storage.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:470` - Batch recovery holds the host-wide dependency lock while waiting up to `FM_DEPS_LOCK_TIMEOUT` separately for every journal's per-secondmate lock. Multiple busy send/config transactions can therefore monopolize the host lock for N times the timeout and block unrelated dependency checks and checkout updates; use a nonblocking per-ID acquisition while holding the host lock and defer busy journals.

🔧 Fix: Reject unsafe queues and defer nested lock contention
✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

</details>

title: docs: fold captain's global concision rule into AGENTS.md section 9
body:
## Intent Add the captain's global communication rule to firstmate's AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md is a symlink; the edit lives in AGENTS.md). The captain's verbatim rule: 'In all interactions and responses, be extremely concise and direct. Skip conversational filler and pleasantries.' Placement was the crux: section 9 (Escalation and captain etiquette) already owns captain-facing communication style and already carried a narrower concision rule ('Every escalation must stand alone and remain concise'). Per the repo's one-owner rule, the broader rule was integrated into section 9's existing language rather than added as a separate overlapping statement or a new section. The narrower escalation-concision sentence was absorbed into and subordinated to the broader statement so section 9 reads as one coherent concision contract, not two rules about concision side by side. The captain's wording is kept substantively intact (extremely concise and direct, no conversational filler or pleasantries). One guard sentence was deliberately added so concision cannot be read as licence to drop what section 9 still mandates: the captain must still be addressed, internal terms must still be translated to outcomes (the outcome-not-mechanics rules), and responses must still include the evidence the captain needs to act. That guard is intentional, not scope creep. Scope is docs only: AGENTS.md section 9, no new section, no behaviour/script/skill changes, minimal restructuring. Repo style followed: one full sentence per line, plain dashes. bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh passes (surfaces=67, local_links=233). Delivery is a PR for the captain to merge. ## What Changed - Integrated the captain's global communication rule ("be extremely concise and direct, skip conversational filler and pleasantries") into section 9 of `AGENTS.md`, subordinating the pre-existing narrower escalation-concision sentence so section 9 reads as one coherent concision contract rather than two overlapping rules. - Added a guard sentence clarifying that concision never licenses dropping the mandatory captain address, the outcome-not-mechanics translation, or the evidence the captain needs to act. - Docs-only edit; `CLAUDE.md` continues to serve the updated text via its symlink and `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` still passes (surfaces=67, local_links=233). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A well-bounded docs-only edit that integrates the captain's concision rule into section 9's existing language, follows the one-owner rule, and whose intentional guard sentence references obligations that genuinely exist elsewhere in the file. ## Testing Ran the doc audience-check script cited as the acceptance gate (bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh), which passed with surfaces=67 and local_links=233 exactly as the intent states; confirmed the diff is docs-only (AGENTS.md, no new section), that the captain's verbatim concision rule, the absorbed escalation-concision clause, and the intentional guard sentence all render in section 9, and that the CLAUDE.md symlink serves the same edit. No rendered UI surface exists for this agent-facing markdown doc, so visual/screenshot evidence is not applicable; the CLI transcript of the audit plus the rendered section 9 text is the appropriate product-level evidence. All checks pass.
Evidence: Doc audience-check transcript + rendered section 9 fm-doc-audience-check: ok surfaces=67 local_links=233 AGENTS.md section 9: In all interactions and responses, be extremely concise and direct, and skip conversational filler and pleasantries. This concision never licenses dropping the mandatory captain address, the outcome-not-mechanics translation above, or evidence the captain needs to act. Every escalation therefore stands alone and remains concise: lead directly with concrete evidence, then the consequence, options when applicable, and a recommendation. CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md (symlink) diff scope: AGENTS.md only, 3 insertions, 2 deletions, no new heading ```text === bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh (validates doc audience inventory / links) === fm-doc-audience-check: ok surfaces=67 local_links=233 === AGENTS.md section 9, rendered (the integrated concision contract) === In all interactions and responses, be extremely concise and direct, and skip conversational filler and pleasantries. This concision never licenses dropping the mandatory captain address, the outcome-not-mechanics translation above, or evidence the captain needs to act. Every escalation therefore stands alone and remains concise: lead directly with concrete evidence, then the consequence, options when applicable, and a recommendation. Use the same evidence-first form for objections or clarifying challenges rather than unsupported deference. === CLAUDE.md is a symlink -> AGENTS.md, so it serves the same edit === lrwxr-xr-x@ 1 wameson staff 9 Aug 10 09:03 CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md === diff scope: docs-only, AGENTS.md, no new heading === AGENTS.md | 5 +++-- 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-) ```

title: feat(bin): enforce route, pool, floor and admission at the spawn chokepoint
body:
## Intent Lane 2 of the captain's routing-enforcement commission (data/routing-enforcement-commission-2026-08-09/commission.md): enforce the approved routing, admission, eligibility and failover architecture as ONE activation-safe tranche, per backlog item routing-activation-tranche and the rev-5 CERTIFIED-WITH-CORRECTIONS policy validation (data/routing-policy-validation-rev5/report.md). Preserve the one-owner layering: routing owns WHO via config/crew-dispatch.json rules, scheduling owns WHEN via _scheduling, admission owns WHETHER via _scheduling.admission_control. Build on the landed model-registry owners (bin/fm-spawn.sh via bin/fm-model-registry-lib.sh already enforce the zero-budget allowlist, registered routability and concurrency caps at spawn) - compose them, never duplicate them. Scope: (1) route-floor and pool enforcement at the spawn chokepoint - a ship/scout dispatch carrying a concrete profile is checked against the configured route it claims, meaning floor met, model in that route's pool, effort inside the route's band, and a violating dispatch is REFUSED with the violated rule named as route id, exact config path, observed versus configured; config/crew-dispatch.json is home-local so the enforcement code reads it from FM_HOME at runtime and fails open to current judgment-guided behavior when the file is absent, so other homes without the config keep working. (2) admission at the chokepoint - consult bin/fm-admission.sh before allocation, band soft queues the work via its recorded substrate tasks-axi hold --kind load and is distinguishable from a refusal, band hard refuses naming the signals, preferred admits, honoring its read-only contract so the caller applies the outcome. (3) eligibility and failover per the validated policy's recorded semantics - an unavailable primary fails over only inside the SAME route's pool in order, no candidate meeting the floor means STOP and escalate naming route, floor, every candidate and why, never degrade below a floor, never substitute an unlisted sibling per the mixed-key rule. (4) red-capable both ways - a dispatch violating a floor, a pool, and an admission band each proven REFUSED with the rule named, red proven first, a compliant dispatch proven unaffected, existing live lanes proven undisturbed with no retroactive re-check of running work. (5) no live lane interrupted by activation, workers finish under the rules they were dispatched under, and no new watcher, scheduler or queue. Accepted rulings already applied and to be preserved: the routing library is the single owner of routing eligibility and must never call the model-registry owners itself, the caller supplies the registry-checked answer; an indeterminate or unreadable determination must refuse LOUDLY naming what it could not determine and never fall through or die silently; the shipped docs/examples/crew-dispatch.json ships with admission control switched OFF so copying it arms nothing, while this repo's own local config keeps its enforcement; a home with no routed pool and a home with no dispatch config stay untouched. Shared tracked material, so firstmate-coding-guidelines applies. Fork-trunk context: the contribution base is the fork trunk 720f06e2a685 so the fork is the correct venue; the pipeline rebase gate answer is skip. ## What Changed - Adds `bin/fm-route-lib.sh` as the single owner of the ROUTE, ELIGIBLE and FAILOVER decisions read from the home-local `config/crew-dispatch.json`, plus `bin/fm-route.sh` as its operator interface (`routes`, `check`, `eligible`, `next --after`, `availability hold|release`, `--json`), with exit status carrying the answer — 0 allowed, 1 rule violated, 2 unreadable input, 3 NO_CANDIDATE terminal stop. Eligibility composes the landed model-registry owners (zero-budget, routability, concurrency) instead of re-deciding them, and failover only ever substitutes inside the same route's pool, in pool order. - Wires that enforcement into `bin/fm-spawn.sh`: ship and scout dispatches take `--route`, and a model outside the claimed route's pool, below its capability floor, outside its effort band, or held by the availability record is refused naming the route id, the exact JSON config path, and configured versus observed. Admission is consulted via `bin/fm-admission.sh` before any allocation, with a `queue` band deferring through `tasks-axi hold --kind load` (`FM_SPAWN_ADMISSION_DEFERRED`) as a distinct answer from a `refuse` band (`FM_SPAWN_ADMISSION_REFUSED`), and a batch taking one fleet snapshot for all its members. Homes with no routed pool — including every home on the plain profile schema and every home with no dispatch config — are unaffected, and enforcement applies only to the next dispatch. - Follow-up review commits close routing fail-opens (malformed `tool_loop`/`context_ceiling` floors and an unreadable `state/model-health.json` now refuse with their own tokens rather than skipping the axis or misnaming the config), refuse an ambiguous bare-name `next --after` match, and make registry enrichment lazy with unchecked substitutes labelled. `docs/examples/crew-dispatch.json` now ships with admission control `enabled: false`; `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the fleet-admission/model-onboarding skills document the routed pools and chokepoint admission. Covered by a new `tests/fm-route-enforcement.test.sh` (38 cases) plus updates to the reasoning-required suite. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: All five ruled corrections landed exactly as ordered with individual covering behavior tests, the fail-open that drove the previous medium rating is closed, enforcement stays opt-in and inert for a home with no routed pool or no dispatch config, and the only residual findings are two informational notes about a `--help` string and a `--json` field's semantics. ## Testing Ran the lane's own `tests/fm-route-enforcement.test.sh` (38/38 pass) plus four adjacent chokepoint suites (`fm-reasoning-required`, `fm-spawn-dispatch-profile`, `fm-admission`, `fm-spawn-batch`, all pass), then went beyond unit coverage with two CLI transcripts driving the real spawn, route and admission commands against purpose-built routed, profile-only and unconfigured homes. The decisive artifact is a before/after red proof: the identical floor-violating, pool-violating and no-route dispatches spawn successfully and create task metadata on the fork trunk `720f06e`, and are refused on `7ca24d4` naming route id, exact JSON config path and configured-versus-observed with no metadata left behind, while the compliant dispatch spawns unchanged in both columns. The transcript additionally shows admission consulted before allocation (hard band refuses naming the controlling signal with zero treehouse allocation calls; soft band defers under a distinct token and really invokes `tasks-axi hold --kind load`), in-pool-only failover with the terminal no-candidate stop that names every candidate and refuses to lower the floor, unrouted and no-config homes spawning untouched with no routing token recorded, the shipped example evaluating inert, and a pre-activation lane's record byte-identical afterward. Two setup obstacles were mine, not the product's, and I fixed them: the gate shell exports `NO_MISTAKES_GATE` and refuses fleet lifecycle from a gate worktree, so the harness clears it and sets the documented `FM_GATE_REFUSE_BYPASS=1` that `tests/lib.sh` uses. No UI, HTML or rendered surface exists in this change — it is shell-script enforcement whose only end-user surface is stderr refusal text and `state/<id>.meta`, so CLI transcripts are the faithful artifact rather than screenshots. One limitation I did not overcome: activation safety is proven by an untouched live-lane record and the absence of any new watcher, not by running a genuinely long-lived worker across the activation boundary. Everything passed and the worktree is clean.

title: feat(bin): make the merge override waive one named check instead of the whole verdict
body:
## Intent

Make bin/fm-pr-merge.sh's --allow-unverified override waive exactly one NAMED check instead of the whole merge verdict. Captain-authorised 2026-08-10: 'make the override name what it waives.'

The measured hole: fm-pr-merge.sh already enforces the empty-check-set law correctly - it refuses a zero-length rollup on its own count so that 'examined and found broken' never reaches the captain wearing the words of 'never examined', or the reverse, and it counts failing and unrun members separately. That is not the hole. The hole is --allow-unverified, which bypassed that refusal wholesale. Under it three completely different situations were indistinguishable and all merged: the structural attestation red that is expected and unavoidable on a fork-landing branch; a genuinely failing check, which is a real defect; and an empty check rollup, which means nothing examined the head at all. It was the one live path by which unexamined bytes could land, used 13 times over three days. It was constrained only by prose - the ruling at data/captain-rulings-2026-08-10/fork-landing-certification-standard.md requires every other required check to be green before the override may be used. Prose is not a mechanism. This task converts that ruling into code.

What was built: --allow-unverified <check-name> waives exactly the named check and nothing else. Every other refusal reason still refuses: a zero-length rollup, any other failing check, any unrun check, an unmergeable state, a blocking review. A bare --allow-unverified with no name is refused, not treated as total - a nameless override is the defect. The waived check's name is recorded on the merge record (merge_waived_check=) alongside the existing merge_verification= fields, so the record says WHICH check was waived and not merely that something was. If the named check is not present on the head at all that is a refusal too, so a typo cannot become a total override. Waiving the head's only check run also refuses, because nothing then examined the head.

This NARROWS an existing authority and grants nothing new. bin/fm-pr-merge.sh remains the single owner of the merge decision; no second place decides mergeability. No existing refusal was weakened while adding the flag's argument: the three-value distinction the header protects - examined-and-broken versus never-examined - survives intact. What the override means for anyone entitled to use it is unchanged; only its precision changed.

Acceptance criteria, red-capable in both directions and both proven: a pull request red ONLY on the named check merges under --allow-unverified <that-check>; the SAME pull request with a second red still refuses under the same override, naming the second reason; a pull request with an empty rollup still refuses under the override; a bare --allow-unverified is refused; a named check absent from the head is refused; existing behaviour with no override is byte-identical, proven rather than assumed. Each was proven by constructing the failing condition and watching the assertion fail against the unfixed code before trusting it pass; absence of a refusal was never taken as evidence.

Constraints: firstmate shared tracked material, so firstmate-coding-guidelines applies - one sentence per line in prose, plain dashes, shellcheck-clean bin/, colocated tests in tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh, never add an agent as a commit co-author, never write the captain-address convention into a commit message.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh`'s `--allow-unverified` now takes a check name and no longer skips verification: `verify_current_head` runs on every path, and the named check's members are subtracted from the rollup counts by three extra jq lines that are added to the query only when a name is given, so a merge with no override sends byte-identical query text. Every other refusal still refuses — an empty rollup, any other failing check run, any other check run with no result, an unmergeable state, and a blocking review.
- The ways a waiver could widen back into a total override are each refused: a bare `--allow-unverified` or `--allow-unverified=<name>`, a name that is empty, dash-leading, or carries a quote, backslash, or control character, a name matching no check run on the head, a name carried by more than one check run (added in the review round, since GitHub can put several runs under one name), and a waiver that leaves no other check run on the head.
- An overridden merge now records `merge_waived_check=<name>` next to `merge_verification=override` and still records no `merge_verified_head=`; `record_merge_verification` strips and re-emits the new key ahead of `pr=` so the metadata identity contract still parses. `AGENTS.md` and `docs/architecture.md` were updated to the named-check form, and `tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh` gained ten override cases plus an API-shaped-JSON fixture matrix.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The delta since the last review only tightens the override further (a name carried by more than one check run now refuses, with canned and real-jq coverage) and drops a redundant state variable, leaving a change that is confined to one script plus its colocated tests and two doc lines, strictly narrows an existing authority, and satisfies every source-verifiable acceptance criterion in the intent.

## Testing

Ran the colocated suite `tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh` (43/43 ok) plus the adjacent `tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh` (exit 0), then drove the real script from a shell across every acceptance case to capture a CLI transcript showing the command, the refusal or merge, whether a `pr merge` reached the forge, and the resulting merge record — including the record line naming which check was waived. Proved the no-override path unchanged by replaying the same green PR through the pre-change script and diffing stdout, stderr, the verbatim forge argv, the merge call, the exit status, and the merge record (all identical), and proved the hole by watching the pre-change script merge an empty rollup and an all-red head under the old bare flag. Also confirmed each new assertion is red against the unfixed code rather than trusted to pass. No UI surface is involved: this is a bash CLI and a state-file record, so the reviewer-visible evidence is the CLI transcript and the persisted merge record rather than a screenshot. Working tree left clean; no fixtures leaked.

A later recovered poll can inherit the stale timestamp and time out prematurely. Route terminal emissions through a shared cleanup boundary keyed by repository and PR. 🔧 Fix: Harden Actions fallback failure and completeness handling 3 issues (2 errors, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-gh-ci-fallback.sh:133` - After a fallback poll persists pending state, a later readable primary result returns here before the repository/PR state path is resolved or cleared. If the permission denial recurs on the same head, the fallback reuses the old `first_seen` and can time out immediately, so the requested terminal-reset invariant remains reachable. Resolve the supported invocation's state key before the primary call and clear fallback state whenever the readable primary path takes ownership. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-gh-ci-fallback.sh:180` - The state key is not an injective canonical repository identity: valid repositories `foo/bar_baz` and `foo_bar/baz` both become `foo_bar_baz`, while casing variants of one GitHub repository create separate keys. Because the shim is PATH-wide, one repository can delete or inherit another repository's deadline, defeating the bounded-poll invariant. title: feat(bin): enforce guarded delivery and Forgejo PR lifecycle
body:
## Intent

Implement two permanent Firstmate delivery safeguards.

First, no-mistakes completion means the full delivery contract, never merely a clean implementation commit or a worker-written `done:` line.
A worker begins the required no-mistakes flow immediately after implementation, commit-only status never reconciles as completed, checks-passed remains PR-ready rather than merged completion, and backlog completion stays downstream of guarded delivery.
Direct-PR and local-only semantics remain unchanged.

Second, enforce task-declared issue title and link requirements before a PR is registered or merged.
Carry the expected issue key and title/link rules explicitly from task intake through the generated brief and durable metadata, use one shared provider-validation seam, reject missing or mismatched provider fields before publishing PR metadata or arming merge monitoring, and keep diagnostics free of provider-controlled shell syntax.
The validation contract is generic task metadata and does not hard-code a tracker or project.

Keep tasks-axi as bookkeeping rather than delivery authority, avoid a general project-policy language, and preserve unrelated provider behavior.

## What Changed

- Made no-mistakes delivery a post-commit contract: commit-only `done:` events cannot complete tasks, checks-passed remains PR-ready, and guarded merge or teardown gates backlog completion.
- Added shared provider validation for explicit issue keys and task-declared title/link rules carried through briefs and metadata.
- Rejects invalid or changed provider fields before PR registration, merge monitoring, or guarded merge.
- Preserves multiline provider bodies, sanitizes diagnostics, and keeps recorded-PR proof authoritative for landing.

## Risk Assessment

Medium.
The change spans lifecycle reconciliation, provider validation, migration, teardown, and generated worker instructions.

## Testing

- Targeted lifecycle, brief, crew-state, provider-validation, PR-check, PR-merge, teardown, spawn-metadata, and promotion suites passed.
- ShellCheck passed through the repository-owned lint command.

title: feat(bin): add the ryder persistent-PTY session backend
