title: fix(bin): preserve delivery guardrails across lifecycle
body:
## Intent Reconcile the new merge conflicts on the existing pull request https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/2115 so it is mergeable against its advanced base, preserving the prior validated PR fixes and all existing commits. Before editing, inspect the current PR head, base head, mergeability, changed files, and failing checks with gh-axi rather than relying on the earlier 00d2a000 head. Use the smallest root-cause conflict and CI fixes, with focused regression coverage where a behavioral contract exists, then run the repository checks. Update only PR 2115's existing source branch fm/firstmate-delivery-guardrails-clean through the existing PR; never reset, discard, force-push, push the default branch, or open a second PR. Treat unavailable fork workflow approval as an external maintainer wait while still running every relevant local check. The previous worker endpoint is gone and its preserved copy is clean and detached; this is a replacement isolated worker, not concurrent ownership. Decisions and tradeoffs made while doing the work: The PR was mergeable:false / dirty with exactly two conflicts against origin/main at 07450b9, which had advanced two commits past the merge base 76355e2. Reconciliation is deliberately a merge of origin/main into the PR branch, not a rebase, because a rebase would require the force-push this task forbids. The branch already contains an earlier merge commit, so a merge is the established shape here. Conflict 1 is the AGENTS.md state/.meta line. Main deliberately replaced the long field enumeration with a pointer stating that each producing script's header owns the exact fields, with docs/configuration.md routing operator-facing details. Main's pointer was kept as the newer editorial decision rather than restoring this branch's enumeration. Because this branch's added issue_key, delivery_title_rule, and delivery_link_rule meta fields were documented ONLY in the enumeration main deleted, and no script header or doc mentioned them anywhere else, one header line was added to bin/fm-spawn.sh so main's pointer remains true for those fields. The pr_head hardening this branch added needed no such line: bin/fm-pr-check.sh's header already documents storing one validated canonical pr= and the forge's exact pr_head=. Conflict 2 is preserve_relaunch_meta's owned key list in bin/fm-spawn.sh. This branch added issue_key, delivery_title_rule, and delivery_link_rule to that list; main added spawn_gen to the same list. It is resolved as the union of both sides. The awk filter prints only keys NOT in the owned set, so any key missing from it leaves a stale value behind across a relaunch while fm-spawn also emits a fresh one. Regression coverage: busy_gen's regeneration across relaunch was already guarded at tests/fm-control-relaunch.test.sh, but main's new spawn_gen had no relaunch-level test, which is exactly the contract the conflict was over. That test now seeds a stale spawn_gen before the relaunch and asserts both that exactly one spawn_gen line survives and that its value changed. The line-count assertion is deliberate and not redundant: the test's meta_field helper reads with tail -1, so a preserved stale duplicate would otherwise be masked by the newly appended value. The guard was verified by counterfactual - removing spawn_gen from the owned key list makes it fail, restoring it makes it pass. Checks already run locally and green before validation: bin/fm-lint.sh (ShellCheck 0.11.0), bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh (surfaces=67, local_links=237), and tests/fm-control-relaunch.test.sh, tests/fm-inactive-reconcile.test.sh, and tests/fm-task-delivery.test.sh. ## What Changed - Updates delivery, PR-check, promotion, teardown, spawn, and crew-state scripts to preserve and validate delivery metadata across lifecycle operations. - Documents the delivery guardrails and script-owned metadata contracts. - Adds regression coverage for PR security, delivery flows, relaunch metadata, and teardown behavior. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: No concrete changed-line defect was substantiated, but the change spans lifecycle teardown, provider-backed PR validation, migration, and delivery metadata with integration-sensitive behavior. ## Testing Ran the three targeted behavior scripts and captured reviewer-visible CLI evidence. The relaunch regression reproduced failure when `spawn_gen` was unowned and passed after restoration. The supplied lint/doc baseline was not rerun because this phase forbids linters and static analysis; no full repository suite was run.
Evidence: Focused delivery guardrails transcript ```text Firstmate targeted behavior evidence (2026-08-11) Commands exercised: rtk bash tests/fm-control-relaunch.test.sh rtk bash tests/fm-inactive-reconcile.test.sh rtk bash tests/fm-task-delivery.test.sh Observed end-to-end behavior: tests/fm-control-relaunch.test.sh exit=0 ok - fm-control relaunch: a same-harness relaunch replaces the agent in the same endpoint and worktree ok - fm-control relaunch: durable task metadata survives replacement launch publication tests/fm-inactive-reconcile.test.sh exit=0 ok - main direct terminal presentation has a durable receipt ok - reused task ids retain per-incarnation terminal receipts tests/fm-task-delivery.test.sh exit=0 ok - fm-spawn: task text cannot shadow generated delivery fields ok - fm-spawn: delivery rules require a bound issue key Adversarial regression check: Temporarily removed spawn_gen from preserve_relaunch_meta's owned-key set. counterfactual exit=1 not ok - a relaunch must leave exactly one spawn incarnation line counterfactual correctly failed After restoring spawn_gen: restored control-relaunch exit=0 ok - fm-control relaunch: a same-harness relaunch replaces the agent in the same endpoint and worktree ```

title: fix(spawn): refresh pooled worktrees from origin before launch
body:
## Intent URGENT recurring firstmate infrastructure fix for Treehouse pooled worktrees, after near-miss data-loss incidents where a crew received a stale origin/main base, branched from it, and its PR appeared to delete work merged since that base. Make bin/fm-spawn.sh guarantee every fresh ship or scout crew, including direct-PR and no-mistakes work, begins from the current tip of the project's origin default branch before the crew creates its branch, so stale bases cannot produce spurious-deletion PRs. Fetch origin, correctly resolve the current remote default branch rather than hardcoding main, and refresh the clean pooled worktree to current origin/; the operation must be deterministic and idempotent, preserve uncommitted work by refusing a non-clean worktree rather than discarding it, and fail loudly rather than silently continue if origin is unreachable, the default branch cannot be resolved, or the base cannot be made current. Keep this invariant in fm-spawn as the single owner instead of relying on a brief Setup rebase/reset step, because the spawn-side mechanism covers every crew type consistently before any worker edits. Evaluate that alternative in the PR rationale. Add portable behavior regression coverage through fm-spawn's real base-setup path using a fake/local origin whose main advances after a stale pool worktree is allocated, assert the spawned worktree equals current origin/main and a branch created afterward retains advanced-main content without spurious deletions; also cover non-main default-branch resolution and unreachable-origin refusal. Keep the diff minimal and focused on worktree base setup, avoiding the independent Pi --tui-mode version-gate region. Ensure bin/fm-lint.sh is clean. Deliver this through no-mistakes as a PR with genuine green checks, do not merge it, and report the PR when CI is green. ## What Changed - Fetch and resolve origin’s default branch, then reset clean pooled worktrees to its current tip before fresh ship or scout launches. - Refuse spawning when origin or its default branch cannot be resolved, or when the worktree is dirty or cannot be refreshed safely. - Add regression coverage for stale bases, non-main defaults, direct-PR and scout launches, idempotency, and failure paths. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is focused, fail-closed, preserves dirty worktrees, resolves the remote default branch dynamically, and includes behavior-level regression coverage for the required scenarios. ## Testing Exercised fm-spawn’s real base-setup path for stale main and trunk bases, repeated/idempotent refreshes, no-mistakes and direct-PR ships, scouts, dirty-worktree preservation, unresolved defaults, and unreachable origins; related spawn tests also passed after correcting one fixture. CLI and Git-state evidence was captured. Lint was left to the pipeline’s separate lint phase as required.

title: fix(spawn): gate Pi TUI mode by CLI capability
body:
## Intent Fix the fleet-wide regression in firstmate shared tracked material caused by PR #2005 adding `pi --tui-mode regular` to Pi and pi-signed crew launch templates. Make fm-spawn VERSION-SAFE: pass `--tui-mode regular` only when the resolved Pi executable actually supports it, while older Pi versions such as 0.82.0 spawn cleanly without the flag; preserve PR #2005 regular-TUI behavior on supporting versions such as 0.84.0. Prefer cheap feature detection from the installed pi/pi-signed capability surface (`--help` or usage) over a hardcoded version gate, and fail safe by omitting the flag when support cannot be determined. Apply the same logic to both Pi and pi-signed templates and do not change non-Pi launch behavior. Add a portable regression test colocated with the existing tests that exercises fm-spawn real command composition with mocked/faked older and newer Pi executables, asserting omission for unsupported Pi and inclusion of `--tui-mode regular` for supporting Pi. Do not assert fm-spawn source text. Keep the diff minimal and shellcheck-clean, with the harness-dependent-checks two-tests rule respected: the portable mocked-version regression is required, and a live-harness-optin guard is only needed if warranted by the real Pi probe. Deliver through no-mistakes, yolo off, and stop at `done: PR checks green`; do not self-merge or wait for same-session merge. ## What Changed - Resolve and pin Pi and pi-signed executables, adding `--tui-mode regular` only when their help output advertises support. - Omit the flag when probing fails or older Pi versions lack support, without changing non-Pi launch templates. - Add mocked command-composition coverage for Pi 0.82.0 and 0.84.0 behavior and document the version-safe launch mechanics. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is narrowly scoped, pins probing and launch to the same Pi executable path, safely gates the flag, and adds behavioral coverage for both supported and unsupported versions. ## Testing The targeted spawn-profile suite passed across Pi-family and non-Pi launch paths; end-user command transcripts demonstrate both Pi identities omit `--tui-mode` for 0.82.0, include `--tui-mode regular` for 0.84.0, and fail safe on an inconclusive probe, while a base-commit reproduction shows the original unsupported-flag regression.

## Summary

- restrict path-based harness identity to Claude’s version-named install layout
- inspect only a bare interpreter’s immediate script argument using whole path components

## Decisions

- Kept this PR narrow to the reported path-only false positive. The tmux classifier retains its existing substring basename policy because this issue’s exec_bridge regression does not prove a broader exact-identity refactor is required, and observed vendor identities such as codex-aarch64-a and kimi-code still depend on that flexibility.
- This change does alter holder-liveness matching, disclosed here so it can be tracked separately. `fm_harness_pid_alive()` (`bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh:159`) reaches the shared harness-identity rule by calling `fm_harness_process_matches()` (`:164`), and that rule now strips one leading `-` from the reported basename before the exact match. A login-shell-style harness invocation (`exec -a -codex ...`) previously failed to match and was therefore judged not alive; it now matches and is judged a live holder. This readmits genuine harness processes that the first version of this fix had wrongly excluded, and it does not restore substring path matching, so the reported exec_bridge false positive stays fixed.
- Withdrawing the earlier claim that this PR does not change holder-liveness semantics: it does, as described above. What still holds is the narrower claim that this PR does not change the lock write boundary. Composability with PR #2132’s recycled-PID identity work should therefore be re-checked against the dash-stripped matching rule rather than assumed.
- The separate Codex Desktop app-server lifetime problem remains unchanged and out of scope.

title: fix: accept status keys after verb colon
body:
## Summary

- Accept `[key=<slug>]` when it is the first token after a status verb's colon, while preserving the existing pre-colon grammar.
- Keep key-like text later in ordinary note prose non-structural.
- Fix the shared parser cause behind both #2109 and #2081, including keyed `needs-decision`, `resolved`, and `fm-send --resolve-key` behavior.

## Reproduction

Before the fix, the issue's scratch-status reproduction returned the named key for the pre-colon form and silently returned `default` for the post-colon form:

```text
pre-colon: alpha    needs-decision    needs-decision [key=alpha] no colon form
post-colon: default needs-decision    [key=beta] colon form
```

The added classifier regression failed before the implementation change with:

```text
not ok - a leading post-colon key token did not open its named decision
FM_TEST_END ... exit=1
```

After the fix, that regression passed as part of `classifier primitives`, two post-colon keys remained distinct, and a post-colon `resolved` event closed only its named key.
The end-to-end `fm-send --resolve-key` regression also passed with a post-colon `needs-decision` event.

## Validation

- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` - passed with pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0.
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` - passed (`surfaces=67 local_links=233`).
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-send-resolve-key.test.sh` - passed, 10 tests, exit 0.
- The new classifier assertion failed before the fix and passed after it.

`tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` has a pre-existing unrelated timing problem after the classifier tests complete.
On the changed branch, the first run passed `classifier primitives`, then failed later with `not ok - dead-agent declared pause flooded stale wakes across six unchanged polls` and exited 1.
The changed-branch rerun again passed `classifier primitives`, then stopped producing output and was interrupted after 250094 ms, exiting 130.

Firstmate authorized one bounded comparison against exact base commit `7f828ea2f28c83aa9e3afd44a2a5ee64795005f8` with both changed files restored to that commit.
That run printed `BASE_DIFF_BEGIN` followed immediately by `BASE_DIFF_END`, passed the same earlier classifier cases, then hung in the unrelated watcher timing cases and reached the 240-second bound:

```text

BASE_DIFF_BEGIN
BASE_DIFF_END
ok - classifier primitives: keyed decisions and activity phases, captain relevance, window-to-task, and overrides
```

- Firstmate switched this lane to direct delivery after three guarded custody-recovery refusals reported `state=blocked_recover_gate_diverged` and `changed=false`; no files or refs changed, so no work was lost.

title: fix: bind session locks to process identity
body:
## Intent

Fix issue #2001 so session-lock liveness cannot mistake a recycled PID owned by another Firstmate home's harness for the original lock holder. Preserve the numeric lock contract and same-home live holders, recover the reported legacy no-sidecar incident when readable live FM_HOME evidence proves wrong-home ownership, add regression coverage that fails before the fix and passes after it, and keep all validation in scratch homes.

Closes #2001

## What Changed

- Bind session-lock ownership to a per-PID process-identity sidecar so recycled harness PIDs no longer keep stale locks alive.
- Preserve conservative handling for legacy same-home locks while reclaiming legacy locks proven by readable live FM_HOME evidence to belong to another Firstmate home.
- Share the identity-aware ownership predicate across ordinary acquisition, session-start routing, and Claude Stop auto-arm recovery.
- Add regression coverage reproducing recycled-PID ownership and verifying lock acquisition, Stop auto-arm, session-start behavior, and preservation of the unrelated harness process.
- Document the identity-checked session-lock liveness contract.

## Reproduction

Before the fix, a real harness-shaped process was started with FM_HOME set to scratch home B, that live PID was written into scratch home A's legacy state/.lock, and bin/fm-lock.sh status was run for home A. It reported the lock as held by a live harness even though /proc/<pid>/environ proved the process belonged to home B.

The regression was separately verified to fail at the pre-fix base because home A refused to reclaim the lock. At the fixed head, home A treats that wrong-home lock as stale, acquires a new lock, and leaves home B's harness alive and untouched.

## Decisions

- Firstmate authorized the narrow legacy no-sidecar recovery required by issue #2001: when readable live FM_HOME evidence proves the recycled PID belongs to another home, reclaim the lock; preserve same-home holders and remain conservative when evidence is missing or unreadable.

## Risk Assessment

Low. The change is limited to session-lock ownership validation, preserves the numeric lock file and existing conservative fallback behavior, and adds executable coverage for both wrong-home recovery and same-home preservation.

## Validation

- `bash tests/fm-sessionstart-nudge.test.sh`

title: fix(spawn): durably lease task worktrees
body:
## Summary

- acquire every non-Orca crewmate/scout worktree synchronously in the controller with a durable Treehouse lease labeled by task id, then move the backend shell into that exact path
- preserve the project cwd and surface Treehouse diagnostics when acquisition fails
- return a newly acquired lease if spawn aborts before publishing teardown-owning metadata, while retaining `fm-teardown.sh` as the successful spawn release boundary
- add real isolated Treehouse lifecycle coverage for stopped-but-preserved and concurrently-live workers, abort rollback, teardown release, and later slot reuse
- keep the Herdr post-create-abort fixture valid for the controller-acquired path by returning a real non-git directory, so it continues to exercise serialized cleanup rather than a failing shell `cd`

## Reproduction

Before the fix, the spawn behavior test captured a bare `treehouse get` without `--lease`; the regression assertion failed against the pre-fix script because the task endpoint acquired only a PID-liveness lease.
In an isolated scratch Treehouse pool, a stopped-but-preserved worker and a concurrently-live worker demonstrated the reported risk: an ordinary acquisition could recycle a slot whose allocator process had exited even though the task still owned the worktree.

The fixed lifecycle test uses a real isolated Treehouse pool.
It demonstrates three distinct durable leases for stopped-preserved and concurrently-live holders, verifies pre-metadata spawn abort returns its lease, then proves a slot becomes reusable only after the existing `fm-teardown.sh` release boundary.

## CI failure reconciliation

- The prior `Behavior tests (Herdr)` failure came from the abort fixture returning an empty Treehouse path after acquisition moved into `cd "$(...)"`; the failed `cd` allowed the pane to disappear without the explicit close event the test intended to assert. The fixture now returns and enters a real non-git directory, preserving the intended validation failure and serialized cleanup path.
- `Behavior portable serial 3` was cancelled downstream when the Herdr job failed; it had no independent assertion failure. The new exact-head run re-executes it.
- The prior provenance job failed because the manually created PR lacked the required no-mistakes signature. This body now records the pipeline provenance below after review, focused tests, documentation, lint, and the authorized fork push completed.

## Validation

- `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-tangle-guard.test.sh` - passed with real isolated Treehouse lifecycle coverage

title: feat(bin): make a task's pull request venue follow its contribution target
body:
## Intent Make a task's pull request venue follow the task's own contribution target instead of a fixed upstream assumption. Background defect, measured: this fleet's landing target is the fork sbracewell64/firstmate, and origin FETCHes upstream kunchenguid/firstmate while PUSHing the fork. The pipeline's PR step ignored that split. One lane had its PR opened at the upstream venue against an explicit ruling to land on the fork; two others each had to hand-answer a rebase gate warning that rebasing would bundle 46 commits of unrelated work, which is this home's fork-only landing queue. Every fork-targeted task either landed at the wrong venue or needed a manual gate answer. Required first step, done: establish from the code how the venue is chosen today BEFORE designing any seam, and prefer the smallest change that makes the venue follow the task over any new abstraction. What that established, and the resulting accepted scope: the venue decision lives inside the no-mistakes tool, not in this repo's material. Its PR step is a statically linked binary whose venue model is one value per repository, fixed at init and held in its own database as upstream_url plus fork_url; it pushes the branch to fork_url and opens the pull request against upstream_url. There is no per-task seam: axi run accepts only --intent/--skip/--yes, the repo-level config key set contains no venue key, and the tool reads no fleet-side record at all. The rebase gate measures against that same per-repo default branch. So the criteria requiring the pipeline itself to raise the PR at a chosen venue, or to change the rebase base, are not deliverable from this repo, and no change to unreachable code was fabricated. Re-running init so upstream_url is the fork was rejected: it is repo-global and would send every PR to the fork including genuinely upstream-targeted contributions, breaking the upstream direction and re-opening the inversion. The accepted deliverable is the fleet-side half: a durable per-task landing-base (venue) record, a guard refusing a pull request whose venue contradicts that record, and a report stating which half lives in the tool. Delivered as: - bin/fm-task-base-lib.sh: task_base_venue derives the venue from the contribution target's trunk, keying on the same shape resolver task_base_upstream_ref so BOTH fork layouts work - a separate upstream remote, and an origin whose fetch and push URLs differ. Upstream is tested first, which is the safety property: fork-only commits are unreachable from the upstream trunk, so no fork-only target can resolve the upstream venue. Fork candidates include the local trunk, origin's trunk, and the landing ref bin/fm-landed-lib.sh maintains for when the local branch lags the fork trunk at the forge. A target on neither trunk is refused rather than guessed. task_base_venue_identity reduces a remote URL to a comparable host/owner/repo across transport, port, case, .git and nested forge paths. Derivation reads the target VALUE, not the resolved base state, because the target can be overridden after resolution and the venue must move with it. - bin/fm-spawn.sh: records contribution_venue= and contribution_venue_url= per ship, resolved after every --slot-base/--contribution-target override so a retargeted task records the venue it was actually retargeted to. A scout opens no PR and records neither. - bin/fm-pr-check.sh: refuses a pull request whose venue contradicts the record, before anything is armed, naming both venues. Three-valued: only a contradiction refuses, and a task with no recorded venue, or the unresolved sentinel, is reported unchecked rather than read as agreement. It never infers a venue from the pull request itself. It compares the HOST/PROJECT_PATH snapshots rather than the FM_PR_* globals, which later parses re-clobber. - AGENTS.md: durable-record inventory extended to name the new fields and their guard. - docs/gitlab-merge-watch.md: its verbatim fm-pr-check transcripts refreshed, because the new venue line made them under-report the command's real output. Lines captured from the real script through the suite's hermetic harness rather than composed. Nothing else in that file is in scope. The conventional fork layout - origin is the fork plus a separate named upstream remote - is a FIRST-CLASS tested topology, not an edge case, because the fleet may move to it to remove the recurring rebase warning at its source. Both directions are proven in a real fixture of that layout, and separately in the fetch/push-split layout, each in one checkout so what is demonstrated is that the venue follows the task rather than that it merely moved. Inversion requirement: nothing may let a contribution branch carry fork-only commits into an upstream PR. Closed on both sides - the venue can never resolve upstream for a fork-only target, and the pre-existing task_base_verify_branch still refuses a branch that does not descend from its contribution target. Verification requirement: a red-capable negative control, proving each new test fails against the unfixed behavior before trusting it green; absence of a warning is never evidence. Every venue test was run against the unfixed code and observed red, including the two covering the conventional layout and the lagging fork trunk, while tests covering behavior that was already correct stayed green in both - the split is the evidence. Scope constraints: this is firstmate's shared tracked material and follows firstmate-coding-guidelines (one sentence per line, plain dashes, shellcheck-clean bin scripts, tests colocated by extending existing suites rather than adding a runner, no agent commit co-author, no fleet conversational conventions in anything other tools read). The pipeline's PR-body marker must never be hand-written; it is an attestation the pipeline writes for itself. The related task nomistakes-upstream-rebase-drops-fixes owns the separate content half and was deliberately not absorbed; both halves terminate at the same in-binary rebase/push seam, which is reported rather than merged into this task. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-task-base-lib.sh` gains `task_base_venue` plus `task_base_venue_identity`/`task_base_venue_identity_alias`: the venue is derived from the contribution target's trunk through the same shape resolver as `task_base_upstream_ref`, so both fork layouts work — a separate `upstream` remote, and an origin whose fetch and push URLs differ. The upstream trunk is tested first (fork-only commits are unreachable from it, so a fork-only target can never resolve upstream); fork candidates are the local trunk, origin's trunk, and the landing ref `bin/fm-landed-lib.sh` maintains for a lagging local trunk. An unreadable upstream trunk or a target on neither trunk is refused rather than guessed, and remote URLs are reduced to a comparable `host/owner/repo` across transport, port, case, `.git` and nested forge paths, with SSH host aliases resolved through a time-bounded `ssh -G` only in the branch that needs it. - `bin/fm-spawn.sh` records `contribution_venue=` and `contribution_venue_url=` per ship, resolved after every `--slot-base`/`--contribution-target` override so a retargeted task records where it was actually retargeted; a scout records neither. `bin/fm-pr-check.sh` refuses, before anything is armed, a pull request whose host/project path contradicts that record, naming both venues; it is three-valued — no record, or the `unresolved` sentinel, is reported as `venue: unchecked` rather than read as agreement — and it never infers a venue from the pull request itself. - Supporting material: `AGENTS.md` and `docs/architecture.md` name the new fields and their guard; the verbatim `fm-pr-check` transcripts in `docs/gitlab-merge-watch.md` were re-captured through the suite's hermetic harness for the new venue line; `bin/fm-test-run.sh` maps `bin/fm-task-base-lib.sh` into both the `pure-contract-unit` and `pr-forge` lanes; new coverage lands in `tests/fm-task-base.test.sh` and `tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh`. The other half of the venue decision — pushing the branch and opening the pull request — lives inside the no-mistakes binary as one fixed `upstream_url`/`fork_url` pair per repository with no per-task seam, so it is reported here rather than changed. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Every finding from both prior rounds is fixed and verified by inspection, the fixes are small and idiomatic (existing timeout owner, existing selection-map pattern), and the single remaining item is comment accuracy in the test-selection map with no live coverage hole. ## Testing Ran both targeted suites (tests/fm-task-base.test.sh, tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh) green, confirmed the changed-file map now selects both, then demonstrated the intent end-to-end by driving the real fm-spawn.sh and fm-pr-check.sh over real diverged git fixtures in both fork topologies — one checkout records two different venues depending only on the task's contribution target, a fork-based task's PR raised upstream is refused before arming while its fork PR arms, an unrecorded venue reports unchecked and still arms, a scout records no venue, and the inversion guard still refuses fork-only work aimed upstream. A red-capable negative control against the pre-change code turned 15 of 16 new tests red (the one green-in-both is the paired positive control for already-correct behavior, matching the intent's stated split) while four pre-existing tests stayed green in both, and the three refreshed docs/gitlab-merge-watch.md transcripts reproduce verbatim against the real script. This is a shell/CLI change with no rendered UI surface, so CLI transcripts rather than screenshots are the end-user-visible artifact. No failures, no flakes; the worktree is clean and the temp task directories the demonstration created were removed.
Evidence: End-to-end venue transcript: real fm-spawn.sh + fm-pr-check.sh, both fork layouts LAYOUT 1 - origin FETCHES upstream, PUSHES the fork $ git remote -v origin https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate.git (fetch) origin https://github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate.git (push) $ git rev-list --count origin/main..main # fork-only commits upstream lacks 3 $ git rev-list --count main..origin/main # upstream commits the fork lacks 1 --- Task A: contribution target is the UPSTREAM trunk --- contribution_target=ecabff0c905940fe07d96586b554b080c418121c base_state=distinct contribution_venue=github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate contribution_venue_url=https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate.git --- Task B: SAME repo, retargeted onto the FORK trunk --- contribution_target=bf7406aba05e86192c9fa99e6dd53cd32c27549d base_state=coincident contribution_venue=github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate contribution_venue_url=https://github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate.git --- THE MEASURED DEFECT: the fork-targeted task PR raised UPSTREAM --- $ fm-pr-check.sh split-fork-a1 https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/2140 error: https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/2140 is at github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate, but task split-fork-a1 records its contribution venue as github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate This task was based on github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate, so raising its pull request at github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate would contribute every commit those two repositories do not share. Reopen the pull request at github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate, or re-dispatch the task against the venue you meant. $ echo $? 1 --- The same task PR raised at the fork it was based on --- $ fm-pr-check.sh split-fork-a1 https://github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate/pull/7 venue: github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate matches the recorded contribution venue armed: state/split-fork-a1.check.sh $ echo $? 0 --- The upstream-targeted task PR raised upstream: still correct --- $ fm-pr-check.sh split-upstream-a1 https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/2141 venue: github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate matches the recorded contribution venue armed: state/split-upstream-a1.check.sh $ echo $? 0 LAYOUT 2 - origin IS the fork, plus a separate upstream remote $ git remote -v origin https://github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate.git (fetch) origin https://github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate.git (push) upstream https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate.git (fetch) upstream https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate.git (push) Task A (upstream target) -> contribution_venue=github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate [base_state=distinct] Task B (fork target) -> contribution_venue=github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate [base_state=coincident] $ fm-pr-check.sh upremote-fork-a1 https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/2142 -> error, exit 1 $ fm-pr-check.sh upremote-upstream-a1 https://github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate/pull/8 -> error, exit 1 $ fm-pr-check.sh upremote-fork-a1 https://github.com/sbracewell64/firstmate/pull/9 -> armed, exit 0 $ fm-pr-check.sh upremote-upstream-a1 https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/2143 -> armed, exit 0 THREE-VALUED: a task recorded before this field existed $ fm-pr-check.sh legacy-a1 https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/2144 venue: unchecked (task legacy-a1 records no contribution venue) armed: state/legacy-a1.check.sh $ echo $? 0 INVERSION GUARD - unchanged and still closed $ task_base_verify_branch <repo> <upstream-target> fm/fork-work rc=1 branch 'fm/fork-work' does not descend from contribution target 'ecabff0c...'; it carries 4 commit(s) absent from that target, so a PR from it would contribute work the target never had $ task_base_verify_branch <repo> <fork-target> fm/fork-work # positive control rc=0 (clean) ```text ================================================================ LAYOUT 1 - title: fix(stow): bound secondmate receipt waits
body:
## Intent

Bound `/stow`'s foreground wait for live secondmate receipts so one slow or missing reply cannot make the command take many minutes, while keeping late and delivery-unknown replies durable.

Closes #2095

## Decisions

- Firstmate treated preserving delivery-unknown pending receipts and atomically validating every delegated endpoint with the authoritative last-value-wins `kind` parser as required corrections to the new helper's stated safety and durability contracts, not as scope expansion.
- After the approval-blocked workflows completed, Firstmate adopted the No Mistakes pipeline head only after a range-diff proved it preserved all five original commits and added exactly three bounded, in-scope review and documentation fixes.

## Reproduction

Before the fix, I exercised the live-secondmate path in a scratch `FM_HOME` with a fake secondmate endpoint that accepted the marked stow request but never produced its correlated completion receipt. An outer watchdog expired with status 124 while the pending-reply record remained `awaiting_report`, demonstrating that the existing per-secondmate wait could hold `/stow` indefinitely in practice.

The regression test failed before the implementation because the bounded fleet delegate did not exist (status 127 instead of the expected bounded pending status 3). It passes after the fix: the helper dispatches every live secondmate first, applies one shared foreground deadline, returns pending within that bound, and leaves the late-reply record durable. Additional cases cover an immediate correlated receipt and ambiguous remote delivery, which must retain its `delivery_unknown` record.

## Validation

- `tests/fm-stow-cascade.test.sh` — 9 tests passed
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` — passed with pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` — passed
- `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh` — passed
- no-mistakes review, test, documentation, and lint gates — passed
- Database — not involved
- Browser validation — not applicable; this repository has no browser-facing surface
- Cypress — not run; this repository has no Cypress suite

The no-mistakes push gate hit the documented read-only `origin` 403, so the validated branch was pushed to the `4mb1t10n` fork as required.

title: docs(agents): enforce knowledge placement
body:
## Summary

- Apply Firstmate's own knowledge-placement and one-owner rules to the always-loaded `AGENTS.md` contract.
- Replace the duplicated operational-home inventory and session-start stage narration with concise owner pointers.
- Move exceptional validation-supersession mechanics into a precisely triggered agent-only skill.
- Remove the conditional Relay section while preserving the pre-trigger supervision rule inline and keeping all five prime safety rules unchanged.
- Add an executable documentation-audience word-budget guard so future growth fails the maintained documentation check.

## Reproduction

Before the fix, `wc -w AGENTS.md` reported 8,972 words.
The original file also carried 58 field-level layout entries, seven narrated session-start stages, seven lines of validation-supersession procedure, and a 222-word always-loaded Relay section.
Running the new executable documentation-audience limit against the original head fails with `AGENTS.md exceeds agent-runtime word limit: 8972 > 7500`.
At this PR's final head, the same checker passes and `AGENTS.md` contains 6,689 words.

## Decisions

Section 14's Relay activation, generated-state, cadence, and protocol details moved to `docs/configuration.md`, their existing authoritative owner.
Relay mention handling, public-safety policy, reply/dismissal, task linking, completion follow-ups, and pairing-token authorization boundaries moved to `fmx-respond`, which loads on every `x-mention`, `x-mode-error`, `public-followup`, startup-surfaced public commitment, and Relay-linked milestone or terminal wake before any reply or lifecycle action occurs.
The pairing token remains consent for public replies and normal reversible lifecycle actions, never for destructive, irreversible, or security-sensitive action.
That rule needs no earlier effect because no such reply or action occurs before the mandatory `fmx-respond` trigger loads the owner.
The Relay-only supervision rule does need effect before a mention can wake the session, so it remains explicitly inline in AGENTS.md section 8: a Relay-only home requires the live supervision cycle even with no other fleet work.

The validation-supersession procedure moved into `validation-supersession`, which loads only when a current explicit captain instruction completely invalidates an active no-mistakes run.
AGENTS.md retains the prohibition on hand-editing, committing, aborting, restarting, or starting a second validation run while no-mistakes owns the branch.

The no-mistakes review added the new skill to the section 13 agent-only catalog.
Its documentation pass also replaced the coding-guideline skill's stale enumeration of documentation-check responsibilities with a pointer to the single owner.

## Validation

- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` with pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh`
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed --base origin/main`: 29 passed, 0 failed, 2 declared tool-gated skips
- no-mistakes review, targeted tests, documentation review, and lint all completed without remaining findings on exact head `545ad48120fb53eeca158156b97f61796b23d085`

Browser validation is not applicable because this repository has no browser-facing surface.

title: feat(bin): add a rebase-equivalence diagnostic that names dropped validated content
body:
## Intent Detect a rebase that silently changes the content a validation pipeline already validated, and record honestly that nothing prevents it. THE DEFECT, MEASURED - two instances, 2026-08-09, and it remains OPEN. (1) fork-trunk-serial2-base-red: the push-time rebase produced a head that had DROPPED the teardown fix, its two regression tests, and the ordered containment correction; ledger lines in bin/fm-teardown.sh at that head: zero. (2) upstream PR 2010: the rebase dropped the pipeline's OWN accepted review-fix hunks - the bin/fm-attempt.sh header, the bin/fm-teardown.sh retire rationale, and docs/architecture.md. Both were caught only by comparing content by hand; NO pipeline signal reported either. A reviewer reading such a request is reviewing something the pipeline never judged. A refusal must name the concrete divergence - which paths, which direction - so the next actor can fix the state rather than guess. WHAT SHIPS, AND WHAT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT. The pipeline's push step is unreachable: no-mistakes is a single compiled binary whose configuration exposes agent selection, timeouts, per-step auto_fix counts, intent extraction and test-evidence storage, with no custom step, pre-push hook or validation plugin. A worker-side check was then tried and abandoned, and an automatic gate at firstmate-side intake was built and WITHDRAWN, both on measured evidence. What ships is bin/fm-rebase-equivalence.sh as a firstmate-invoked DIAGNOSTIC that reports and never gates. Nothing in the delivery path refuses, blocks or delays a request on head comparison, and neither bin/fm-pr-check.sh nor bin/fm-pr-merge.sh can fail because of it; tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh pins that. WHY NO GATE CAN STAND ON THIS YET. The gate needs the validated head, and that head is destroyed at push: the pipeline overwrites head_sha with the pushed head in 68 of 68 pushed runs, measured across a live database, so afterwards no retained record holds it. Three sources were tried and each failed differently. The worker's own head is older content, because a run commits its fixes onto its copy of the branch. submitted_head_sha predates those fix commits, so an accepted fix that rewrote a line reads as that line being dropped - it refuses 6 paths on a real run whose review fix legitimately rewrote them, with 62 of 69 pushed runs exposed. A watcher snapshot taken before the push narrows that to one poll interval rather than eliminating it, and a stale snapshot refuses a good push with a false accusation indistinguishable from a true one; worse, a missing snapshot refused intake, and because bin/fm-pr-merge.sh routes through bin/fm-pr-check.sh the request then became permanently unmergeable with no recovery path. A safety mechanism that can silently and permanently destroy delivery is worse than the defect it was built to prevent. The snapshot machinery was therefore removed entirely rather than wired to the diagnostic, because a stale snapshot would put a silently wrong head into a report a human treats as considered. DEFECT RECORDED OPEN. docs/verification/rebase-equivalence.md opens by stating that a pipeline rebase can still silently drop validated content and nothing prevents it, what the diagnostic detects, that it prevents nothing because it is not in the delivery path, why each validated-head source failed, and that closing it requires the pipeline to retain its pre-push head - a change in the validation tool, not here. The defect is recorded as backlog item rebase-drop-defect-remains-unprevented, filed with its closing condition and blocked by unenforced-commitment-register so it migrates into that register when the register lands; it is not in the register, because the register does not exist yet. Shipping a diagnostic must not make the defect read as closed. THE PREDICATE. Each head is measured against its own base, because a tip-to-tip diff also reports trunk content the branch merely lacks, which a landing preserves rather than deletes. Occurrence counts are compared rather than presence, so a dropped hunk cannot be covered by copies already in the file. File modes are content, since a rebase that drops a chmod +x lands non-executable scripts. Presence is read from the tree, so a submodule pointer is not invisible on both sides. Only the repository the request URL names may answer for it: a bare request number is refused outright, because it names no repository, so no source can be proven to be the one the request belongs to - measured, a bare number fell back to origin and returned a confident DROPPED verdict over 12 paths of an unrelated project's request. Fetches are non-interactive so an authenticating remote refuses rather than hanging, and the fetched validated ref is released from a trap armed when it is created, so it cannot leak on any refusal path. Verdicts are three-valued and only PASS is a pass: an unresolvable input, a head compared against itself, an empty flag value, a changed binary path, a bare request number, and a comparison that could not be completed are all could-not-observe. Merge-result equality was tried and rejected on evidence: the validated head is still on its pre-rebase base, so merging it into the post-rebase trunk conflicts in 90+ files while the rebased head merges clean. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: the diagnostic detects a rebase that drops content and names the losing paths with the direction; it clears a rebase that preserves content; it cannot report a pass by not running, so an unreachable or erroring comparison is could-not-observe rather than a silent skip; and nothing it does can block, refuse or delay delivery. Every predicate was proven red-capable - the failing case constructed, watched failing against the fix removed, and only then trusted passing. That discipline caught, among others, a regression that reported 36 ok and 0 failures while never executing at all because the suite had exited 127 on a helper typo. A NOTE ON PROSE. Several defects in this work were comments and documentation asserting behavior the code did not have - a page claiming a withdrawn gate was live, a citation of a renamed-away test, a claim that a commitment was recorded when it had only been requested, and test comments describing the opposite of their assertions. A claim written beside code is checked by nothing, so it drifts from the moment it is written. Prose in this change should be read as adversarially as the code. CONSTRAINTS: firstmate's shared tracked material, governed by the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill. One sentence per line in tracked prose; plain dashes; shellcheck-clean bin scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh; colocated tests; never add an agent as a commit co-author; never write the captain-address convention into a commit message, pull request, or anything crewmates and other tools read. Never use git stash in a pooled worktree. Keep to the comparison and do not take on its neighbours; the related venue work is a separate task and a shared seam is reported rather than absorbed. This branch's contribution base is upstream main, so upstream is its correct venue. ## What Changed - New `bin/fm-rebase-equivalence.sh`: a firstmate-invoked diagnostic that compares a pre-rebase validated head against the post-rebase candidate head, each measured against its own base. It compares occurrence counts rather than presence, treats file modes as content, reads presence from the tree, fetches the candidate from `refs/pull//head` (or `refs/merge-requests//head`) only via a remote proven to name the repository the request URL names, and refuses a bare request number outright. Verdicts are three-valued - only `PASS` is a pass, and an unresolvable input, self-comparison, empty flag, binary path, or incomplete comparison is `CANNOT-OBSERVE`. Fetches run non-interactively (`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `-oBatchMode=yes`), signals terminate rather than falling through to a pass, and the fetched validated ref is released from a trap. - Nothing gates on it. `bin/fm-pr-check.sh` gains only a comment recording why the withdrawn intake gate must not be reintroduced; `tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh` adds `test_head_comparison_never_blocks_a_merge`, which runs the real check then merge with no snapshot and asserts the merge reaches the forge, and `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` pins the comparison's absence from the generated worker brief. - `docs/verification/rebase-equivalence.md` records the defect as still OPEN - both 2026-08-09 reproductions, why each validated-head source failed, and that closing it needs the pipeline to retain its pre-push head - and is registered in `docs/documentation-audiences.json`; `AGENTS.md` and `docs/scripts.md` describe the script as a deliberate diagnostic. `tests/fm-rebase-equivalence.test.sh` covers the predicate at 48 checks, all passing. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The delta closes the previous round's fail-open with a correct trap split and a deterministic red-capable regression, the two prose fixes now match the code, and every source-verifiable acceptance criterion holds - the only residue is one assertion message whose stated timing is out of date. ## Testing `Ran the four targeted suites touched by this change (rebase-equivalence 48 ok, pr-check-security 37 ok including the new never-blocks pin, fm-brief, documentation-audiences) and then, because a passing suite cannot show the end-user experience, reproduced the measured defect end-to-end: a stand-in forge holding the pushed heads only under refs/pull//head, a stand-in gate repo holding the validated head, and a worker cloned --no-local that holds neither. Invoked exactly as firstmate would, the diagnostic reported DROPPED with the losing paths and the direction over the incident head, PASS over a faithful replay onto the same moved trunk, DROPPED as dropped-mode over a head that replayed every line but lost the executable bits, and CANNOT-OBSERVE for a bare request number, an unfetchable request, and an unreachable validated remote, so no unreachable comparison passed by not running. Nothing gates on it: bin/ contains one comment and zero invocations, bin/fm-pr-merge.sh has no comparison residue, and the real intake and merge scripts both complete with the merge reaching the forge. The worktree was left clean; the only finding is a documentation citation of a script that does not exist.`

Line 104's "Those objects are reachable" then dangles - the snapshot it referred to no longer exists, and the sentence is actually about the pipeline's git objects. A reader skimming headings takes away the opposite of what ships. Rewrite the heading and lines 99-100 in the past tense ("was snapshot", "recorded") and re-anchor line 104. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-rebase-equivalence.sh:279` - The non-interactive-fetch invariant is not enforced when GIT_SSH_COMMAND is already set in the environment. `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="${GIT_SSH_COMMAND:-ssh -oBatchMode=yes}"` keeps a caller-supplied value verbatim, dropping `-oBatchMode=yes`. A SIGINT or SIGTERM anywhere in that window leaves refs/fm-rebase-equivalence/validated/<oid> behind, pinning the fetched objects in what lines 137-139 call a SHARED object store for a gate worktree - the exact accumulation the release exists to prevent. The intent states the ref "is released from a trap armed when it is created"; it is not. Arm `trap release_validated_ref EXIT INT TERM` immediately after the fetch, then re-arm with the WORK cleanup at this line. Relatedly, the comment block at lines 455-458 explains a release "the moment the object id resolves" that no longer happens there and should be folded into the trap's own comment. - ⚠️ `tests/fm-rebase-equivalence.test.sh:714` - This case does not test what its comment claims. `run_check_pr "$WORKER" "$B" "$V" 8` omits --validated-remote, so it is refused by the guard at bin/fm-rebase-equivalence.sh:263 ("--candidate-pr needs --validated-remote") and never reaches the bare-number logic at all; the bare-number rule is now an outright refusal for naming no repository, not a base-resolution failure. The assertion checks only `expect_code 2`, which cannot tell the two refusals apart, so the case is green regardless. docs/verification/rebase-equivalence.md:363 repeats the stale framing ("a bare request number that can name no base"). The real coverage is the dedicated case at line 926; either drop this line or add --validated-remote and assert the refusal text. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-rebase-equivalence.sh:513` - The footprint diff (line 513) and the per-path diff (line 566) pass --no-ext-diff but not --no-textconv, while the counted candidate/base/validated copies come from `git show <commit>:<path>` (line 549), which always emits the raw blob. In a repository with a `diff=<driver>` gitattribute whose driver defines textconv, the harvested + lines are converted text that can never match the raw candidate file, producing a confident false `dropped-content` verdict. This repo has no .gitattributes, but --repo takes any directory, so the exposure is real for the diagnostic's stated use against other checkouts. Add --no-textconv alongside --no-ext-diff on both diffs. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-rebase-equivalence.sh:347` - Dead assignments in the bare-number branch. PR_NUMBER and PR_NAMESPACES are set here, but with PR_URL_SOURCE empty the flow reaches line 394 unconditionally and refuses. Only the `*[!0-9]*` shape check at lines 348-350 is still live, and it is redundant with the `*)` fallback at line 356 which emits the same message. The branch can collapse to the single refusal, which also removes the misleading comment at lines 352-353 ("both head namespaces are tried") describing a fetch that never happens. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-rebase-equivalence.sh:321` - --validated-remote establishes no provenance: I verified with git 2.53 that `git fetch <remote> +<oid>:<ref>` exits 0 and creates the ref whenever the object is already present locally, even when the remote does not contain that object at all. So the flag's real guarantee is "the caller named a full object id", not "the head came from the pipeline". docs/verification/rebase-equivalence.md:115 argues this correctly (an oid is content, so it names the run record's commit or nothing), but the script header at lines 30-35 reads as a stronger claim ("there is deliberately no fallback to a local ref") - a wrapper doing `--validated-head "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" --validated-remote no-mistakes` would silently compare the worker's older head, reproducing the false-refusal defect the flag exists to remove. tests/fm-rebase-equivalence.test.sh:761 corroborates this by passing --validated-remote "$GATE" for a head $GATE does not hold, and still expecting a completed comparison. Worth tightening the header wording to "only a full object id is accepted, and the remote is only how it is obtained". - ℹ️ `bin/fm-rebase-equivalence.sh:397` - Asymmetric ref cleanup. refs/fm-rebase-equivalence/candidate/<n> (line 397) and refs/fm-rebase-equivalence/base/<n> (line 428) are never released, while the validated ref is deliberately released because - per lines 137-139 - accumulating refs pins objects against gc in a shared object store. Each diagnostic run therefore leaves a full PR head and a full trunk branch pinned, one pair per request number. This looks intentional (docs/verification/rebase-equivalence.md:164-166 uses their persistence as evidence the fetch ran), so flagging as a tradeoff rather than a defect. 🔧 Fix: fix(bin): enforce batch-mode ssh, trap the validated ref at creation, disable textconv 3 issues (2 warnings, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-rebase-equivalence.sh:210` - The `--help` text still carries the provenance claim the header now explicitly refutes. Lines 34-38 say the --validated-head/--validated-remote pair establishes "exactly this and no more: the caller named a full object id, and that id resolves here. It is not provenance... the remote is never evidence that the head came from the pipeline." But usage() at lines 210-212 still reads "--validated-remote names the pipeline's own repository and takes the validated head from there rather than from this clone, because a run commits its own fixes and this clone's branch therefore holds older content." Same file, two contradictory claims about the same flag, and the one a caller actually reads is the wrong one. The review instruction was to rewrite the claim to say what the flag establishes; the header was rewritten, usage() was not. docs/verification/rebase-equivalence.md:119 asserts "the script header says so in those words" - true of the header, not of --help. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-rebase-equivalence.sh:345` - Both signal traps clean up and then return, so INT and TERM are swallowed and the run continues with its working directory deleted. `trap release_validated_ref EXIT INT TERM` (line 345) and `trap 'release_validated_ref; rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT INT TERM` (line 516) never exit, so bash resumes at the next statement after the handler. Failure scenario: a human Ctrl-Cs the diagnostic just after the per-path loop at line 745 finishes. The handler removes $WORK, execution resumes, `[ -s "$UNCERTAIN" ]` and `[ -s "$DROPS" ]` are both false because those files no longer exist, and the script prints `REBASE-EQUIVALENCE: PASS validated content is carried by the candidate` and exits 0. A cancelled run reports a pass - the outcome the acceptance criteria forbid ("it cannot report a pass by not running"). A signal landing mid-loop instead dies on the failed `>> "$UNCERTAIN"` redirect under `set -e`, exiting 1 with no verdict line. Split the signal trap from EXIT so it terminates: `trap 'release_validated_ref; rm -rf "$WORK"; printf '"'"'REBASE-EQUIVALENCE: CANNOT-OBSERVE interrupted\n'"'"'; exit "$VERDICT_CANNOT"' INT TERM`, keeping the plain cleanup on EXIT. The trap shape predates this commit, but line 345 is new and its comment claims signal coverage. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-rebase-equivalence.sh:299` - Appending `-oBatchMode=yes` unconditionally changes behavior for callers whose GIT_SSH_COMMAND is not OpenSSH-compatible. A caller exporting `plink -batch`, `tortoiseplink`, or a wrapper that rejects unknown options now gets a hard failure on every ssh-form --candidate-remote or --validated-remote, where previously their command was used verbatim and worked. The direction is safe - CANNOT-OBSERVE, never a false PASS - and this is the fix that was explicitly directed, so noting the tradeoff rather than objecting to it. Worth one sentence in the git_fetch comment so the next reader knows a non-OpenSSH client refuses by construction. 🔧 Fix: fix(bin): terminate on signals instead of falling through to PASS 2 infos still open: - ℹ️ `tests/fm-rebase-equivalence.test.sh:884` - Stale assertion message describing a release mechanism the code no longer has. The failure text reads "the fetched validated ref must be released once the head resolves", but the release moved to a trap two commits ago and now happens at process exit via `cleanup` (bin/fm-rebase-equivalence.sh:172-189); nothing releases it at resolve time. The check itself is still correct - the ref must be absent after the run - only the stated timing is wrong. Reword to something like "must not survive the run". Flagging because the standing instruction for this branch is to re-read every remaining comment, help string and assertion message against the code, and this is one the trap rework left behind. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-rebase-equivalence.sh:194` - `cannot_observe` still calls `release_validated_ref` explicitly, which is now redundant: `trap cleanup EXIT` is armed at line 189, before `cannot_observe` is even defined, and `cleanup` calls `release_validated_ref` on every exit path including every refusal. The explicit call only changes ordering - the ref is dropped before the verdict prints rather than after - with no behavioral difference. Noting it so a reader does not infer from its presence that the EXIT trap misses refusal paths; it is harmless belt-and-braces and removing it is optional. </details> <details> <summary>⚠️ **Test** - 1 info</summary> - ℹ️ `docs/verification/rebase-equivalence.md:270` - docs/verification/rebase-equivalence.md:270 illustrates the file-mode predicate with `bin/fm-new.sh`, a script that exists in no branch of this repository (`git log --all -- bin/fm-new.sh` is empty, and it is absent from docs/scripts.md). The sentence reads as naming a real script, which is the prose-drift class the intent calls out. No behavior is affected; every mode claim it makes is exercised by two passing tests and reproduced end-to-end. Substituting a real script name (or wording it as hypothetical) would close it. - <code>`bash tests/fm-rebase-equivalence.test.sh` - 48 checks, all ok (drop, resurrect, mode, glob-literal, textconv, forge fetch, repository-identity, signal, verdict-vocabulary cases)</code> - <code>`bash tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh` - 37 checks, all ok, including the new `test_head_comparison_never_blocks_a_merge` which runs the real `bin/fm-pr-check.sh` then `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` with no snapshot and asserts the merge reaches the forge</code> - <code>`bash tests/fm-brief.test.sh` - includes the new `test_no_mistakes_dod_pins_rebase_equivalence_absence`</code> - <code>`bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` - covers the docs/documentation-audiences.json entry added for the new page</code> - <code>Manual end-to-end reproduction via `/tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZQB4V95Z6ESP3359Z4BVY3G/repro-pipeline-rebase.sh <worktree>`: forge + gate + `--no-local` worker fixture built from this repo's real files, then `bin/fm-rebase-equivalence.sh --repo <worker> --validated-head <sha> --validated-remote <gate> --candidate-pr https://github.com/example/pipeline-repro/pull/{2010,2011,2012,4242}` plus the bare-number and unreachable-validated-remote refusals</code> - <code>`git -C <worker> for-each-ref 'refs/fm-rebase-equivalence/**'` - confirms the validated ref is released while candidate/base refs persist</code> - <code>`grep -rn 'fm-rebase-equivalence|REBASE-EQUIVALENCE' bin/` and `grep -c candidate bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` - no invocation in the delivery path, no merge-path residue</code> - <code>`git log --all -- bin/fm-new.sh` and `ls bin/` - checked the documentation's script citations against the tree</code> </details> <details> <summary>⚠️ **Document** - 1 info</summary> - ℹ️ `docs/fm-test-portable-shards.md:67` - docs/fm-test-portable-shards.md still reports the 2026-08-02 measurement (69 serial scripts; shard counts 15/18/17/19), while the lane now derives 103 scripts across 24/27/25/27 shards. This drift predates the change (the new tests/fm-rebase-equivalence.test.sh only adds one more), and refreshing it correctly requires downloading fm-test-timing-portable-serial artifacts from a green CI run and re-doing the bin packing, which is out of scope here. title: fix(bin): reconcile inactive terminal outcomes
body:
## Intent

Implement the report-approved inactive terminal-outcome reconciliation for Firstmate supervision. On the existing watcher poll loop and locked session start only, deterministically inspect long-inactive, non-captain-held direct crewmates with fm-crew-state and surface only authoritative done or failed outcomes. Keep a durable outcome receipt distinct from heartbeat markers until the secondmate parent report or main captain presentation is acknowledged. Have secondmate homes idempotently report their own terminal children through the established local or remote parent channel. Have the main home independently inspect validated secondmate structured summaries, create one marked correlated pending-reply request for a missing report, and preserve the obligation. Never treat a healthy parked or idle secondmate as wedged. Never call GitHub, a forge, PR APIs, PR polls, or state check scripts. Use the independent 60..1800 second bounded gate instead of heartbeat backoff and add behavioral tests for both levels, missing reports, restart idempotency including remote mirror input, heartbeat cap, nonterminal and captain-held exclusions, no false wedge, and zero forge calls. Also preserve structured-summary compatibility and prevent Bearings PR enrichment from treating a descendant directory as its ancestor git worktree.

## What Changed
- Add bounded watcher and locked-startup reconciliation for authoritative inactive `done` or `failed` crewmate outcomes, with durable receipts acknowledged only after parent reporting or captain presentation.
- Extend bounded, paginated secondmate summaries with terminal children so homes report outcomes through local or remote parent channels and main homes create one correlated pending-reply obligation for missing reports without forge access.
- Preserve episode identity across relaunches, harden structured-summary compatibility, and prevent Bearings PR enrichment from treating descendant directories as repository worktrees.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The reconciliation changes now appear to satisfy the stated durability, compatibility, bounded-cadence, pagination, and no-forge requirements without a substantiated remaining defect.

## Testing

Inspected the change, repaired stale remote-summary protocol assertions, added the missing behavioral descendant-worktree regression, and reran both targeted suites successfully; evidence demonstrates durable two-level reconciliation, paging and restart behavior, exclusions, heartbeat independence, no false wedge, zero forge calls, and safe Bearings PR enrichment. This is CLI behavior, so no visual screenshot was applicable.

title: fix(watch): rearm AFK stale escalation
body:
## Summary

- re-hand off an unchanged non-paused AFK stale pane after the daemon marker clears so the daemon re-arms its existing bounded wedge cadence
- preserve the immediate one-shot handoff for each distinct stale hash
- preserve the daemon's long cadence for `paused:` panes and its existing transient/wedge treatment for `captain-held:` panes
- expose the hash-routing choice through a small pure decision function for protected, function-level regression coverage
- correct the architecture description of the AFK stale cadence

## Reproduction

Before the behavioral fix, I extracted the existing inline hash decision without changing it and exercised it through a pure function seam with synthetic state inside the isolated worktree.
An identical frozen hash returned `decision=ignore` instead of re-handing off after the daemon cadence completed; the assertion exited 1.

After the final fix, the function-level fixture confirmed that a new hash surfaces immediately, an unchanged hash stays daemon-owned while its marker exists, the same unchanged hash re-hands off after that marker clears, and a paused hash stays daemon-owned even with no wedge marker.
It also confirmed that `captain-held:` remains eligible for the existing transient/wedge handoff rather than being reclassified as paused.
The no-mistakes Test step ran the isolated pure-function harness without launching the protected watcher or touching shared state.

## Validation

- no-mistakes intent, rebase, review, targeted test, document, lint, fork push, and PR steps completed successfully in follow-up run `01KZRHSDPNWN8N76KTWB65E7E5`
- the no-mistakes Test step independently confirmed the regression passes on the fixed target and fails on the base
- `bin/fm-lint.sh`
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`
- `git diff --check`
- focused source-safe decision fixture: pre-fix exit 1, post-fix exit 0
- browser validation is not applicable because this repository has no browser-facing surface
- Cypress was not run because this repository has no Cypress suite
- no database or local stack is involved

The broader `fm-watch-triage` suite has PRE-EXISTING timing/process instability and is out of scope for this PR.
Two changed-tree attempts passed the new regression and then failed at different existing timing-sensitive assertions: `a stable-hash busy pane past the turn-age bound did not start a wedge timer` and `stale suppressor not advanced on absorb`.
With this change absent, a single comparison run at base SHA `7f051002b65adb196fdf3804a13d965046782d36` passed the same preceding stale-path checks and then hung in the existing `wedge-escalation` fixture while waiting on its hermetic watcher.
That base result establishes the instability is not caused by this change; this PR deliberately does not alter the suite's unrelated timing behavior.

## Decisions

- Firstmate required the inline AFK unchanged-hash decision to be extracted into a pure named function because the defective branch was below `fm-watch.sh`'s source guard and was not callable for faithful regression coverage.
  The guard was respected rather than bypassed: the pure function lives in the already-sourced classifier library, and coverage sources that library directly with synthetic inputs instead of sourcing or launching the watcher.
- Firstmate classified the `fm-watch-triage` timing/process instability as pre-existing after it reproduced on base `7f051002b65adb196fdf3804a13d965046782d36` with this change absent, and kept that unrelated repair out of scope.
- Firstmate verified that the no-mistakes run's recorded preserved head `5ae4492a` was phantom and does not exist in this repository. Both guarded custody recovery attempts - `no-mistakes axi sync --recover` and the supported `--keep-local` variant - refused without changing files or refs because the gate branch remained at the real validated work head `de61bf5`. Under a bounded validation exception, Firstmate determined the completed review, targeted test, documentation, and lint evidence stands, authorized stopping recovery attempts, and authorized pushing the intact clean head `de61bf5` directly to the `fork` remote.
- Firstmate decided under `issue-1956-paused-cadence` that only `paused:` hashes retain the daemon-owned long recheck cadence.
  `captain-held:` remains transient/wedge because issue #1956 does not change that existing daemon contract.
- Firstmate decided under `issue-1956-cadence-owner` that the daemon marker is the sole AFK wedge cadence owner.
  The watcher re-hands off an unchanged non-paused hash only after that marker clears, preventing duplicate watcher and daemon timers.

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

The initial no-mistakes pipeline completed every validation step through lint; only its push to read-only `origin` failed with the expected 403.
The follow-up no-mistakes run rebased the fix, applied the Firstmate decisions, completed validation, pushed to the authorized fork, and updated this PR.
Exact-head GitHub workflows are awaiting upstream approval before their jobs can execute.

Closes #1956

title: feat(bin): expand fleet orchestration and harden certification
body:
## Intent Make verifier independence a DERIVED, three-valued fact that certification fails closed on, and close the path that let an unverifiable certification claim exist. Commission section 13a: no lifecycle claim may be written directly when its truth can be derived from an authoritative source. Built on the prior unlanded branch (9ac500a), rebased onto the fork trunk with all 502 lines preserved. Two earlier runs were INTERRUPTED by the validation agent exiting (weekly window exhaustion), never by a verdict on the code; their seven review-fix commits were recovered via axi sync --recover and are present at this head. Review reached completed on the second run at low risk. All five suites pass locally on this exact head: 188 cases, zero failures, plus a clean bin/fm-lint.sh. 1. IDENTITY, PER RUN AND PER AGENT-BACKED STEP, from the pipeline's own agent_invocations rows (read-only), written AT INVOCATION TIME and therefore evidence of what actually ran - not a configuration read afterwards, since agent:auto resolves at run creation. The reviewing invocation is identified by purpose, so review-fix (which rewrites code) is never read as the critic. 2. INDEPENDENCE IS DERIVED, NEVER WRITTEN. The prior commit's --critic-process/--critic-vendor/--critic-model let a caller STATE the reviewing identity and a stated value won over the record; that writable assertion is the defect this seam closes. Those arguments are removed and a test requires every one to be refused writing nothing. fm-certify.sh accepts no argument that asserts a result or waives a predicate. 3. THREE VALUES, reusing bin/fm-verify-lib.sh's observation type one level up: independent / not-independent / could-not-observe. An identity never captured is could-not-observe and can never read as independent. 4. FOUR DIMENSIONS: process, model, vendor, credential pool. The pipeline's checkers draw on shared subscription windows, so a different harness does not imply an independent verifier. A same-pool different-model checker reports as exactly that. 5. INDEPENDENCE IS A PROPERTY OF A RUN AGAINST SPECIFIC BYTES, NEVER OF A BRANCH. Process and identity are both computed PER RUN; a branch view reports its WEAKEST MEMBER rather than summing across runs or dissolving two differing answers into mixed-then-could-not-observe. A run that never reached review provides no evidence and WEAKENS the branch to could-not-observe rather than being invisible; a cancelled or failed run was never a verifier and is not a member, and excluding it must not silently strengthen the branch. 6. THE SAFETY ASYMMETRY. Unobserved or unfinished evidence may only ever weaken a claim of INDEPENDENCE, never a finding of DEPENDENCE. An observed not-independent is a positive finding that survives; nothing unobserved erases it. Corrected in three places: the overall verdict matched NO_VERIFIER_RAN before FAIL, fm-certify.sh's fold stated 'could-not-observe dominates', and the process fold discarded an observed dependence behind an unobserved run. 7. ABSENCE MUST NEVER BECOME A VERDICT IN EITHER DIRECTION. IFS=tab collapses consecutive tabs (reproduced on bash 5.3.9), which shifted numeric columns and manufactured an observed dependence the pipeline never recorded - maximally durable under the asymmetry above. Equally, an unread status must not read as in-flight, and provenance must not claim a derivation that never opened the database. 8. NAMES ARE NEVER INFERRED. The pipeline's vocabulary (anthropic, claude-opus-5) relates to the fleet's (claude, opus) only through a DECLARED mapping (pipeline_providers, pipeline_model_ids, validated as arrays of strings); where absent, the dependent dimensions read could-not-observe. 9. CERTIFICATION FAILS CLOSED, NAMING THE GAP. bin/fm-certify.sh computes CERTIFIED over the predicates APPLICABLE to the route taken. Exit 0 certified, 3 observed unmet, 4 could-not-observe. fm-decision-surface.sh check certified composes it so the claim cannot be made from memory. Explicitly named bytes always win over the recorded summary, and the reason says which source answered. 10. THE FOURTH, STRUCTURAL VALUE: NOT_APPLICABLE, carried WITH THE ROUTE. A fork-landing branch is deliberately unsigned because signing duplicates a live contribution; a local-only route opens no pull request. Never folded into could-not-observe (we looked and the route structurally cannot produce evidence, versus we could not look), never dropped, and it rides on the state line so quoting the state word alone cannot overstate what was certified. Applicability is DERIVED from push target and delivery mode, never from an argument, and an underived route is reported unknown rather than as a concrete route name. 11. CERTIFICATION MUST STILL ANSWER AFTER TEARDOWN. Teardown deletes task-local state, so a check reading only state/.meta was permanently unevaluable for every completed task - which is exactly when certification is claimed. Inputs are sourced from the wake ledger's terminal task record, written immediately before the metadata is deleted. Any input with no durable home is could-not-observe, named as such, and NEVER back-filled. 12. SECURITY: the positional task id is guarded with fm_task_id_path_safe at the boundary, refusing a hostile identifier rather than sanitizing it, because it otherwise reached git -C via an arbitrary .meta and could turn a read into command execution. fm-decision-surface.sh no longer passes its target through unguarded. 13. RED-CAPABLE PROBES. Every named regression case was absent before its fix and each was executed failing against its own pre-fix tree via git archive into scratch: a zero-session run CERTIFIED at exit 0; a branch dissolving two differing reviewers into unknown; an observed dependence erased by an unobserved run; a dependence fabricated from an unrecorded identity; a hostile task id accepted rather than refused; and a certified check dying for every torn-down task. Constraints: firstmate shared tracked material; one sentence per line in prose; plain dashes; shellcheck-clean bin scripts; colocated tests; no agent commit co-author. Fork-targeted: both bases are the fork trunk, so the rebase gate is answered skip. ## What Changed - Add fleet launch, admission, model-governance, LoopSpec, retry-budget, research reconciliation, and local or remote secondmate workflows. - Introduce typed task/status records, deterministic decision and crew-state surfaces, durable wake outcomes, and safer supervision, worktree allocation, and teardown behavior. - Harden delivery and certification with verified PR checks, head-bound attestations, and three-valued verifier independence derived per run from durable evidence, failing closed when identity or applicability cannot be observed. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The follow-up cleanly closes the writable applicability path, derives delivery mode from durable task evidence, preserves unknown versus not-applicable semantics, and introduces no remaining material source-verifiable concerns. ## Testing All five targeted suites and the end-to-end CLI checks passed; the transcript directly shows certification succeeding only with derived independent evidence, observed dependence and missing evidence failing closed with distinct exits, and writable critic assertions being refused. No screenshot was applicable because this change’s end-user surface is a shell CLI.
