title: fix(bin): reclaim orphaned worker lock scratch
body:
## Summary

- Reclaim orphaned atomic-publish scratch files after the existing worker-liveness checks establish that an ownership lock is stale.
- Clear the same known scratch patterns from both worker cleanup paths and the Linux supervisor cleanup path.
- Name the exact wedged ownership lock when an unexpected symlink or unknown entry prevents safe reclamation.
- Add a behavioral regression that creates a stale `worker.lock` containing an orphaned `.quarantine.*` file and proves a replacement worker becomes ready.

## Verification

- No-mistakes review completed with no findings.
- No-mistakes testing completed successfully, including a pre-fix run that proved the new regression fails without the fix.
- No-mistakes documentation validation completed successfully.
- No-mistakes lint completed successfully, including the shellcheck-clean `bin/` requirement.

## Decisions

- Fixed all three identical instances of the canonical-file-removal-then-`rmdir` pattern in `bin/fm-remote-job-worker.sh`: `worker_acquire_lock`, `worker_cleanup`, and `worker_supervisor_cleanup_dead_child`.
  Evidence: all three can encounter scratch names created by `worker_publish_lock_owner` or `worker_publish_quarantine`, and all three previously removed only canonical names before attempting `rmdir`.
- Did not implement the optional signal-trap hardening suggested by the issue.
  Evidence: changing `trap -` to `trap ''` narrows one interruption window but cannot prevent SIGKILL, OOM termination, or crashes from orphaning scratch files, while the stale-lock reclamation fixes the permanent deadlock without changing signal semantics.
- Refuse symlinked scratch entries instead of following or removing them.
  Evidence: this matches the existing symlink-refusal boundary for canonical `pid`, `start`, and `command` entries in the same ownership paths.
- Clear scratch entries only after the existing live-owner, readiness-probe, and recent-lock checks have all failed.
  Evidence: this preserves the same no-live-worker safety envelope already required before reclaiming canonical lock entries, so mutual exclusion is not weakened.
- Emit a worker error containing the exact `worker.lock` path when scratch cleanup is unsafe or unknown entries keep the directory nonempty.
  Evidence: the former generic acquisition failure did not identify the state root whose ownership lock required attention.

Closes #1972

title: feat(bin): expand deterministic fleet orchestration
body:
## Intent Stop the wedge alarm firing on workers that are demonstrably working, in firstmate's shared supervision code. MEASURED PROBLEM: roughly eight false wedge escalations in one day (2026-08-10), each costing a full coordinator turn to peek panes and conclude nothing was wrong, arriving in bursts precisely when the fleet was busiest recovering. Every one was a worker running a long command; a validation run emits nothing to its pane for minutes at a time. ROOT CAUSE: a wedge marker reaching its escalation point is already checked once against bin/fm-crew-state.sh, and a crew reported as provably working has its marker refreshed instead of escalated. That guard is correct in intent and missed every time, because the reader answers a 'failed', 'aborted' or 'interrupted' verdict from the RUN STEP, which is authoritative and deliberately never reads the pane. Those verdicts describe how a RUN ended and observe nothing about the crew. Three lanes were escalated while holding a run left 'failed' by an earlier session-limit kill, at the moment their workers were actively starting fresh runs: a lane BETWEEN an interrupted run and its replacement had no provably-working evidence anywhere the guard looked, though its pane showed a live shell and an advancing turn. WHAT IS BUILT, reusing existing sources rather than adding machinery: bin/fm-crew-state.sh records the crew's own semantic turn signal (bin/fm-busy-lib.sh) AND the crew's agent liveness alongside a run-level terminal verdict, leaving that verdict, its source and its precedence untouched. bin/fm-classify-lib.sh's crew_absorb_class treats a run-level terminal verdict as the ABSENCE of a crew-level verdict and asks the crew-level sources: agent-corroborated turn signal, then identity-bound descendant-CPU advancement (state/.childcpu), exactly as it already did for a verdict the reader could not decide. A LIVE SHELL IS NOT A LIVE AGENT - accepted ruling, and the safety core of this change. A busy turn record is trusted for up to FM_BUSY_MAX_BUSY_AGE_SECS (default 3600s) and its timestamp is stamped when the turn OPENS, never ticking within it, so an agent killed behind a still-live shell would otherwise read 'busy' and be ABSORBED for up to an hour. That is could-not-observe turned into silence, the precise failure this task exists to remove. A busy record alone therefore never returns working: it must be corroborated by agent liveness that re-derives on every read. A shell outliving its agent IS the dead-agent case, and the case where the alarm matters most. THREE VALUES, NEVER TWO: provably working suppresses the escalation; provably idle - and a dead or missing agent, and a gone endpoint - escalates on the unchanged schedule; and CANNOT TELL still escalates, saying it could not be observed. That includes a busy record whose agent cannot be corroborated, and turn evidence that expired, was never written, or could not be read. Turning could-not-observe into silence would be a far worse defect than the noise being fixed. PERMITTED LIVENESS SOURCES ONLY: fm_backend_agent_state / fm_backend_agent_alive (backend-native, re-derived per call) and fm_child_cpu_state (identity-bound, advancement-based). NEVER a process-pattern search (pgrep -f, ps piped to grep, or any command-line or process-name match): in this fleet that has twice matched the wrong process, because the pattern appeared in a worker's brief or in the searching process's own command line. EXPLICIT EXCLUSIONS: no suppression by age, count or rate - that hides a genuine wedge along with the noise, and is the same mistake ruled out for repeat decision escalations. Step DURATION is not used as a liveness signal - it is written at step boundaries, not continuously, so an unchanged duration is not evidence of a stall. ONE POLICY ACROSS BOTH TRIAGE MODES: bin/fm-classify-lib.sh is the shared owner of the triage predicates, and the per-wake watcher (bin/fm-watch.sh) and the away daemon (bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh) must keep applying that one policy. Which semantic classes a liveness reading may answer for, and which classes count as 'the crew state absorbed nothing' for the declared-pause dead-agent recovery, are asked of that library rather than named in the consumers, so a class added later cannot quietly opt out of an existing recovery path. ACCEPTANCE, red-capable in both directions and proven by construction: a lane with a FAILED run record and a live working pane is NOT escalated, watched escalating against the unfixed code first; a genuinely idle lane still escalates on the unchanged schedule; a lane whose liveness cannot be observed still escalates, and says so; a dead agent behind a live shell escalates rather than being absorbed; and the unobserved class is subject to dead-agent pause recovery. tests/fm-classify.test.sh carries the last two by those exact names and is registered in the watcher-wake-lock family with bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage green. REPO RULES: firstmate shared tracked material, so firstmate-coding-guidelines applies - one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dashes and never an em dash, shellcheck-clean bin/ under bin/fm-lint.sh, colocated tests in tests/, no agent name as a commit co-author, and no captain-address convention in commit messages. REBASE GATE: the contribution base is the fork trunk, so the rebase gate will warn that roughly 68 commits would be bundled. The answer is SKIP - those are this fleet's own landing queue and must never enter contribution history. ## What Changed - Add fleet launch, admission, model verification, and local or remote secondmate lifecycle workflows, including Windows-to-WSL support. - Introduce typed task and status state, deterministic decision surfaces, executable LoopSpecs, retry budgets, wake accounting, and decision reconciliation. - Harden supervision, validation, worktree allocation, and PR landing, including agent-corroborated crew liveness that suppresses false wedge alarms while preserving escalation for idle, dead, or unobservable workers. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The corrective commit now distinguishes authoritative endpoint absence from unreadable or unverified liveness, preserves all three classification outcomes, and adds the required red-capable regression cases with exact pass text. ## Testing Inspected the targeted change, then ran classifier, crew-state, watcher, daemon, and coverage-registration checks; end-to-end CLI fixtures confirmed failed-run lanes with live work are absorbed, while idle, dead-agent, and unobservable lanes still escalate through both triage modes. All checks passed, the worktree remained clean, and no screenshot was applicable because this is shell-based supervision behavior with no rendered UI.

body:
## Summary

Updates `VISION.md` so the public vision matches the captain's own framing from the 3k-stars reflection tweet: experience as the primary goal, multi-session pain as the problem, clone-and-run ease, self-evolution (including community), and explicit harness/backend orthogonality.

This is a docs-only PR for captain review. Direct-PR delivery (no no-mistakes pipeline). Do not merge without captain word.

## What changed (5 elements)

1. **Experience north star as primary goal** (opening + One captain, one interface + restart + aligns/resists)
   - Opening now states the biggest aim is not a smart workflow / useful tool / impressive technology, but an experience: peacefulness, confidence everything is under control, ease of mind that nothing falls through the cracks when the captain looks away.
   - Captaincy metaphor kept: well-managed crew with a first mate carrying out direction.
   - **Reconciled former L14-15 garnish framing:** replaced "Experience features on top of this interface are welcome only when..." with "Peace of mind is the purpose of this interface, not a garnish on top of it," then re-scoped presentation/convenience features as servants of that experience (still opt-in, still never in the way of the captaincy).
   - Durable restart section now explicitly connects records-based durability to how that experience holds when attention leaves.

2. **Multi-session juggling pain narrative** (One captain, one interface)
   - Added problem statement before the interface rules: parallel sessions, context-switching, relearning each session, focus/flow/peace replaced by tab-juggling; harnesses/orchestrators only make jumping easier without removing the burden.

3. **Clone-and-run setup ease** (Scope)
   - Alongside template/clone/own: "Setup stays that simple by design: clone the repo, run your agent in it, and that is it."

4. **Self-introspect + self-evolution, including community** (The fleet outlives any vendor)
   - Elevated hot-modifiable to self-evolving; added "ask the first mate and it figures it out" plus community self-evolution of the shared surface.

5. **Harness- and backend-agnostic / not another harness** (The fleet outlives any vendor)
   - Explicit "not another harness and not another orchestrator app"; "new way of working" orthogonal to harness and session manager; names example harnesses and backends while preserving distro shape.

## Aligns / resists

Structure preserved (two adjudication sentences at the end).

- **Aligns** now leads with deepening peace of mind, confidence, and ease of looking away; also includes self-evolving.
- **Resists** adds trading that experience for more noise or more context-switching, and couples-to-one-vendor expanded to "one vendor or session manager."

Unchanged in substance: authority/consent, scripts-vs-agents, delegation-with-spine, token efficiency, scope boundaries.

## Checks

- One sentence per physical line; plain dash (no em dash).
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` → ok (VISION.md remains `public-product`).

## Source

Captain tweet https://x.com/kunchenguid/status/2086834015278137549 (full verbatim capture in scout report for this task). Scout findings only; ship is the VISION.md fold authorized after promotion.

title: fix(spawn): launch claude crewmates unattended without a permission-prompt regression
body:
## Intent Investigate whether the current Claude Code CLI has a way to launch fully unattended - no interactive workspace-trust prompt, no bypass-permissions confirmation prompt - while still granting the SAME full autonomy --dangerously-skip-permissions currently gives (crewmates must be able to run any tool/command without further interactive per-action approval; do not trade the startup dialogs away for a regression to per-tool approval prompts, that would break every existing ship/scout brief). Check claude --help for any --permission-mode or trust-related flag, project or global config file settings (e.g. a trusted-workspaces list Claude Code itself reads), and any documented non-interactive/CI launch mode. Verify empirically end to end in a scratch worktree/session before changing the fleet launch command - per the coding-guidelines 'Harness-dependent checks' section, this class of change must be proven against the real installed harness, not assumed from a flag name. If a safe combination is found, update: bin/fm-spawn.sh's Claude launch command; .agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md's claude section to correct the dialog-handling guidance to match the new verified behavior; add the two required 'Harness-dependent checks' tests (a portable regression in tests/ that pins the launch-flag logic, and the live-harness-optin guard family); and docs/verification/runtime-backends.md with dated empirical evidence. CONTRIBUTING.md/AGENTS.md only if the one-owner rule requires it. If no safe non-interactive option exists, say so precisely and stop without making a change. Result: found a safe combination, verified empirically end to end against the real installed Claude Code 2.1.227 CLI before and after the change. --settings '{"skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt":true}' answers the Bypass Permissions mode warning purely via an added CLI flag, with no shared-state mutation. The workspace-trust dialog has no CLI flag, so bin/fm-spawn.sh now pre-writes projects[].hasTrustDialogAccepted: true into the resolved .claude.json store via one jq command sent through the crewmate's own pane (the same channel that already ships GOTMPDIR) before the launch command is sent. Neither change reduces crewmate autonomy: --dangerously-skip-permissions still bypasses every per-tool approval prompt, confirmed via the live guard's 'bypass permissions on' status-line check. Updated bin/fm-spawn.sh, .agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md, added tests/fm-claude-unattended-launch-live-e2e.test.sh (registered in bin/fm-test-run.sh's live-harness-optin family), updated tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh, tests/fm-trace-context-spawn.test.sh, and tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh (the last via the pipeline's own review-step auto-fix, since I initially missed that file's identical exact-adjacency launch-string assertion), and docs/verification/runtime-backends.md with a new 'Claude unattended launch' section carrying dated empirical evidence. AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md were checked and do not need changes for this scoped fix. This is a retry: two prior runs on this branch failed on pure infrastructure problems already resolved by the user, not on this change - first a no-mistakes daemon git-identity error (user set git config --global identity), then a push permission error against kunchenguid/firstmate (user forked to trmacfarlane/firstmate). Review, test, document, and lint already passed clean in the prior run; the review step's one auto-fix commit is already on this branch. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-spawn.sh`'s claude launch template now adds `--settings '{"skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt":true}'` to answer the "Bypass Permissions mode" warning, and sends a jq-based pre-write of `projects[].hasTrustDialogAccepted: true` (for both the raw and symlink-resolved worktree path) into the resolved `.claude.json` store through the crewmate's own pane before the launch command, so the workspace-trust dialog is pre-answered; falls back to a stderr warning when `jq` is unavailable. - `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/SKILL.md`'s claude section is rewritten to document the new unattended-launch behavior, the `jq` best-effort fallback, and that per-tool autonomy from `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is unaffected; the version-verified banner is updated to note the 2026-08-11 re-verification. - `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md` gains a "Claude unattended launch" section with dated empirical evidence (Claude Code 2.1.227) for the fix and the reusable live e2e guard. - Adds `tests/fm-claude-unattended-launch-live-e2e.test.sh` (registered in `bin/fm-test-run.sh`'s live-harness-optin family) and updates `tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh`, `tests/fm-trace-context-spawn.test.sh`, and `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh` to match the new launch-string and pretrust-command assertions. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-scoped, additive (a new --settings flag plus a best-effort pre-trust write with documented, non-corrupting failure modes and a graceful jq-missing fallback), matches the empirically-verified mechanism described in the intent, all callers/tests that assert the exact literal launch string were updated consistently, and no stale documentation of the old dialog-handling behavior remains anywhere in the repo. ## Testing All targeted portable regression tests pass, and a fresh manual end-to-end reproduction against the real installed Claude Code 2.1.227 CLI confirms the unattended-launch mechanism (--settings flag + pre-written trust) eliminates both dialogs while leaving --dangerously-skip-permissions' full per-tool autonomy intact; the branch's own live-harness e2e test could not be executed here only because a pre-existing, unrelated gate-agent safety guard blocks any no-mistakes test-phase agent from driving fm-spawn.sh's real fleet lifecycle, which is expected behavior, not a regression.
Evidence: Manual live verification transcript: fresh worktree launched unattended with --settings + pre-trust, no dialogs, bypass permissions on, Bash tool ran with no per-tool prompt ```text === Manual verification: fresh worktree, --dangerously-skip-permissions alone (no --settings, no pre-trust) === Result: workspace-trust dialog appeared (captured before the fix's mechanism was applied). === Manual verification: same worktree, WITH --settings '{"skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt":true}' AND pre-written projects[].hasTrustDialogAccepted=true === export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/fm-claude-manual-verify.sW7Zyu/claude-config tmacfarlane@HPCNZ-odrZQ:/tmp/fm-claude-manual-verify.sW7Zyu/worktree$ export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/fm-claude-manual-verify.sW7Zyu/claude-config tmacfarlane@HPCNZ-odrZQ:/tmp/fm-claude-manual-verify.sW7Zyu/worktree$ CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=false claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --settings '{"skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt":true}' ╭─── Claude Code v2.1.227 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ │ Tips for getting started │ │ Welcome back Tom! Switch anytime with /model. ❯ run: ls Read 1 file, listed 1 directory (ctrl+o to expand) ● The directory contains a single file: README.md, whose content is just "hi". ✻ Cooked for 6s ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ❯  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ⏵⏵ bypass permissions on (shift+tab to cycle) · ← for agents Now using usage credits tmux focus-events off · add 'set -g focus-events on' to ~/.tmux.conf and reattach for focus tracking ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

Commands typed into a still-foreground bash prompt queue reliably in the pty regardless of timing, so this is not a correctness risk, only a very slightly larger latency margin than before.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh` — 26/26 passed, including the claude launch-string assertions with --settings - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-trace-context-spawn.test.sh` — 12/12 passed, including the updated --dangerously-skip-permissions-anchored ordering assertions - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh` — full suite passed, including the two --settings launch-string assertions - `FM_CLAUDE_UNATTENDED_LAUNCH_LIVE=1 bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-claude-unattended-launch-live-e2e.test.sh` — correctly refused with 'no-mistakes gate agent must not drive the fleet (NO_MISTAKES_GATE set)', a pre-existing unrelated safety guard, not runnable from this gate context by design - Manual live reproduction against the real installed `claude --version` (2.1.227): launched a fresh scratch worktree/config dir via tmux with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=false claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --settings '{"skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt":true}'`, confirmed the trust dialog only (no bypass-permissions warning), then pre-wrote hasTrustDialogAccepted via jq and relaunched — confirmed no dialogs, 'bypass permissions on' status line, and an unapproved Bash tool call

title: fix(supervision): keep parked crews and the Stop auto-arm from taking supervision down
body:
# fix(supervision): keep parked crews and the Stop auto-arm from taking supervision down

Two compounding defects take fleet supervision down whenever a crewmate is waiting on a captain decision.
Observed live four times in one session with two crews running: firstmate had to re-arm the watcher by hand each time, and only the turn-end guard caught it.

Branch head `b63954d6`, 6 commits on top of `7f828ea`, 14 files, +1226/-42.

## Regression window

This home fast-forwarded on 2026-08-10 from `cd73e75` to `85e750a`, 55 commits.
Two of those land squarely on the failing area, and both diffs were read before designing the fix.

- `33a4287` fix(bin): harden Claude supervision auto-arm recovery (#1495).
- `88b2a94` fix(bin): correct session lock and attached watcher supervision (#1545).

The behaviour both commits intended is right, and neither is reverted here.
The bug is in their edges: #1545 widened harness identity to whole path components and `argv[0]` so a version-named Claude Code binary could be recognised, which was necessary and correct, but the same widening also made Claude Code's shared infrastructure processes look like sessions.

## Defect 1 - a crew parked on a captain decision is classified as a possible wedge

`bin/fm-watch.sh` suppressed a stale-pane wedge only through `pause_state_class` -> `status_is_paused_or_captain_held`, which matched exactly two verbs, `paused` and `captain-held`.
A crew awaiting a captain answer writes `needs-decision:`, which is the verb `bin/fm-brief.sh`'s own generated status protocol tells it to use, and that verb was in neither set.

Two things then compounded.
`needs-decision:` is captain-relevant, so `stale_is_terminal` reported the pane terminal and it never reached the pause classification at all.
And a crew parked at an ask-user gate of a still-running validation still reports a running step, so `crew_absorb_class` returned `working` and routed the motionless pane into the provably-working wedge timer.
Its idle pane then escalated 1, 2, 3 with `demand-deep-inspection`, and every armed cycle ended within about 60 to 90 seconds on the parked crew's window rather than the working one.

Two fixes were explicitly ruled out before design and are not used here.
Telling crews to write `paused:` instead is wrong, because that verb declares a bounded EXTERNAL wait expected to clear on its own, and a captain decision is not that.
`captain-held` cannot be the answer either, because it is written only by `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh` after it verifies a structured backlog hold, which is the investigation and visual-review path, so a mid-pipeline ask-user finding answered through the validation gate never travels that path.
The suppression set was what was wrong, not the crew's verb.

### What changed

A still-open keyed captain decision is now the third declared-idle class, alongside the declared external-wait pause and the verified captain-held transfer.

It is read from the durable open-decision fold (`status_open_decisions`) rather than the last status line, so a later unrelated `working:` or `done:` line cannot silently end it, and so the same class covers `blocked:`, which is the same "firstmate action is needed" wait.
It deliberately outranks a provably-working run-step verdict, because that verdict winning is the actual root cause of the escalation loop.
It inverts only the liveness asymmetry of the other two classes: firstmate itself owes the answer, so a live parked endpoint goes straight to the bounded cadence, while a crew that died holding the decision is the anomaly that still gets its one surface.

Two properties were required and are enforced by tests.

1. An open decision must stay visible.
   Suppressing the wedge never suppresses the decision: the fleet-wide `scan_open_decisions` fold surfaces the same open set on every wake drain, and the class ends once the crew's status advances past the line that opened the decision, so suppression is bounded rather than lasting the whole lifetime of an unclosed key.
2. A genuinely dead crew must still surface.
   Liveness is rechecked on every cadence pass, not only at first sight, so a crew that parks while alive and then dies still surfaces; only a confident live verdict clears the one-shot death marker, so an ambiguous `unknown` read cannot make a dead crew flap; and the away-mode daemon clears the same marker, so the invariant also holds across an AFK round trip.

## Defect 2 - the Stop-owned auto-arm stops re-claiming the home

The turn-end guard reported `TURN WOULD END BLIND` with tasks in flight, stating explicitly that the auto-arm had not claimed, four times.
`state/.claude-autoarm-epoch` read `epoch=2246 owner_pid=1208559 outcome=rewake` throughout and never advanced, `state/.turnend-claude-blocks` stayed `count=1 epoch=2246`, and `bin/fm-watch-arm.sh` run manually succeeded every time immediately.
So the arm path was healthy and only the claim path failed.

### The stated hypothesis was tested and disproved

The first hypothesis was that the auto-arm treats an epoch whose recorded owner has since died as already handled and declines to claim.
That was tested against the real hook in four deliberately constructed dead-owner lock states - a symlink lock to an owner dir with a dead pid, a dangling owner-lock symlink, a leftover steal lock, and a plain-directory lock with a dead pid - and disproved.
Every one reclaimed the lock and armed normally, and the epoch ledger's `owner_pid` is never read by any claim path.

### The actual cause

Claude Code hosts an `asyncRewake` Stop hook inside the worker chain of its shared per-user daemon, `claude daemon run` -> `claude bg-pty-host` -> `claude bg-spare`.
That branch never contains the session pid `state/.lock` records, and since #1545 all three of those infrastructure processes carry `claude` branding in `argv[0]`.
So `fm_harness_ancestry_pids` returned a confident ancestry that provably excluded the hook's own session, `fm_session_lock_owned_by_self` failed, `fm_harness_pid_alive` on the recorded owner succeeded, and the hook exited 0 silently on every firing, permanently.

This was confirmed against a live process table on 2026-08-10 with Claude Code 2.1.227, where the daemon, `bg-pty-host` and `bg-spare` processes sat in a different branch from the session recorded in `state/.lock`.

### What changed

Claude Code's shared infrastructure subcommands are no longer treated as a session, in either the ancestry walk or lock-owner liveness.
The match is anchored on the first argument after `argv[0]` specifically so a real session can never be misread as infrastructure because its prompt text happens to contain one of those words - a crewmate launch brief is passed as argv.

`bg-spare` and `bg-pty-host` stay transparent to the pre-match climb, because a session-hosted hook chain legitimately passes through them, but the `daemon` subcommand is a hard stop: reaching it without having already matched a session proves the caller is in the shared infrastructure chain, so the walk terminates unresolved rather than climbing past and latching onto whatever harness sits above the daemon.
That last point matters because the naive narrowing made all three transparent, which would have let the walk cross a gap and report an unrelated harness as this session's ancestry - the exact gap-crossing `test_harness_beyond_a_gap_never_owns_the_lock` exists to forbid, and it would have let the hook arm a home it cannot prove it owns.

A live recorded owner reached with no resolvable ancestry is recorded durably in `state/.claude-autoarm-unresolved-ancestry` and cleared on the next successful claim, and the turn-end guard names that cause instead of reporting only that nobody claimed.
Only the genuine live-competing-owner branch supplies a pid to that banner, so a shared-daemon pid or an already-dead pid can never be rendered as "owned by another live session", and the banner is gated on the record's own freshness so a stale fault cannot misdiagnose a later, different failure.

The guard's bounded block budget was keyed on epoch change, so a frozen ledger pinned the count below its threshold and the designed attended fail-open was unreachable.
Same-epoch suppression now applies only while the auto-arm demonstrably owns that epoch, or within a single guard run, which preserves the existing one-recovery-turn-per-epoch and failed-suppressed idempotence contracts.

## Migration window: why a pre-upgrade shared-infrastructure lock is stale but NOT claimable

Excluding the infrastructure subcommands also changes the lock WRITE path (`fm_harness_ancestry_pid`, used by `bin/fm-lock.sh`), so a `state/.lock` written before this change can hold the shared daemon pid.
Without a deliberate fix, a different live session's Stop hook would see that recorded owner as not live and could claim a home another live session recorded.

This was raised by review as a net narrowing that self-heals on first re-acquire, and it was fixed anyway rather than accepted as a documented transient.
The reasoning is recorded because it overrides that judgement.
This is a session lock, whose failure mode is two live sessions both believing they own one home and both mutating it.
The window opens during a fleet self-update, which means it opens for every home AT ONCE rather than rarely - the worst possible distribution for a transient, not a mitigating one.
It is also the precise boundary this change promises to preserve, that a genuine competing live session stays inert, and a net narrowing that still briefly permits the thing the boundary forbids is not good enough for a lock.

So such a recorded owner is recognised as not a valid session owner AND is not claimable by a Stop hook, which leaves the ordinary session-start acquisition to replace it with a real session pid with no window.

## What this change does NOT fix

For the exact ledger state observed live - `epoch=2246`, `outcome=rewake`, never advancing - the block-budget change ALONE produces no observable difference.
The epoch file's mtime ages past `EPOCH_FRESH`, so `autoarm_owns_recovery`'s rewake branch never accounts that epoch, and the unowned fall-through then correctly advances `COUNT` past `BLOCK_BUDGET`.
But `terminal_fail_open` still declines, because `failure_episode_verified` accepts only `outcome=failed` or `failed-suppressed`, so the guard re-blocks every turn exactly as before until Claude Code's own consecutive-block override ends the episode.
The real improvement for that state is the new unresolved-ancestry banner line, not the budget.
Gating the alarm on a recorded failure is a deliberate existing contract and is left unchanged; this is stated plainly as a limitation rather than overstated.

## Tests, and the proof each fails before the fix

Every regression was proven failing against the previous code before the code was changed, by stashing only `bin/` and running the new tests against pristine sources.
Observed failures on the unfixed code:

- `test_open_captain_decision_stale_is_bounded_not_wedged` failed with `stale: test:fm-parked (idle 1s, possible wedge, escalation 1)` - the parked crew ended the supervision cycle.
- `test_daemon_worker_chain_is_never_session_ancestry` failed because the shared `claude daemon run` was reported as this session's harness ancestry.
- `test_e2e_unresolvable_ancestry_is_recorded_not_silent` failed because the firing left no durable record, so it repeated silently forever.
- `test_hook_claude_mode_frozen_epoch_still_advances_the_block_budget` failed because a frozen epoch never reached the attended fail-open.

All pass after the fix, and the full suites are green.

New coverage added across three existing suites, extending them rather than inventing a runner:

`tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh`
- `test_open_captain_decision_stale_is_bounded_not_wedged`
- `test_open_captain_decision_dead_crew_still_surfaces`
- `test_open_captain_decision_park_then_die_still_surfaces`
- `test_open_captain_decision_class_ends_when_the_crew_moves_again`
- `test_open_captain_decision_death_surfaces_once_across_an_unknown_read`
- `test_open_captain_decision_dead_holder_recheck_names_the_exited_agent`
- `test_open_captain_decision_dead_crew_survives_an_afk_round_trip`

`tests/fm-session-lock-ancestry.test.sh`
- `test_daemon_worker_chain_is_never_session_ancestry`
- `test_harness_above_the_daemon_is_never_this_sessions_ancestry`
- `test_e2e_unresolvable_ancestry_is_recorded_not_silent`
- `test_e2e_unresolvable_ancestry_is_recorded_on_a_malformed_lock`
- `test_e2e_competing_live_session_stays_silently_inert`
- `test_e2e_pre_upgrade_daemon_pid_lock_is_stale_but_not_claimable`

`tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh`
- `test_hook_claude_mode_frozen_epoch_still_advances_the_block_budget`
- `test_hook_claude_mode_unresolved_ancestry_banner_needs_a_current_record`
- `test_hook_claude_mode_banner_never_calls_a_non_live_pid_a_live_session`

All are portable regressions that pin the logic with real processes and no harness: they drive the real `fm-watch.sh`, the real Stop auto-arm inside real orphaned process trees, a deterministic fake process table for both platforms' `ps` semantics, and the real guard.
None asserts implementation-source bytes, through parsers, regexes, snapshots or wrappers.

A hard constraint applies to these suites and was violated once during development, which is worth recording: a test must never invoke the blocking watcher without a bound the test itself controls.
A watcher blocks by design until it has an actionable wake, so in a fixture worktree with no crews it never returns.
The divergence assertions matter too, so no case can go quietly vacuous: the competing-live-session case asserts no fault record is written, and the cursor case asserts the incremental fold still reports the open decision after the watcher has advanced the shared cursor.

## Per-harness compatibility review

Reviewed against every supported primary harness, not only the one in this fleet.

- **claude** - directly affected on all three axes (Stop auto-arm identity, the unresolved-ancestry record, the guard's block budget). Covered by `fm-claude-stop-autoarm.test.sh`, `fm-session-lock-ancestry.test.sh` and `fm-turnend-guard.test.sh`.
- **codex** - bounded foreground checkpoints. Reaches `fm-turnend-guard.sh` only in default mode, which blocks before the changed Claude-mode budget path. Never launched with a bare `daemon`, `bg-pty-host` or `bg-spare` first argument, so the identity narrowing cannot false-positive on it.
- **opencode** and **pi** / **pi-signed** - plugin and extension driven turn-ends, same default-mode guard path. The `pi-signed` -> `pi` wrapper ancestry is untouched, because the narrowing keys on those three subcommands only.
- **grok** - background-notify cycles with native Stop delegation, same default-mode guard path.
- **kimi** - hook registry token path, unaffected for the same reasons.
- **muse** - crewmate and scout only, never a primary; affected only as a crew through the harness-neutral classifier change.

The shared classifier (`bin/fm-classify-lib.sh`) and watcher (`bin/fm-watch.sh`) changes are harness-neutral and apply to all of them, which is why the open-decision class is covered by portable regressions rather than harness-specific ones.
`docs/verification/supervision.md` was updated because this work falsified its recorded claim that the `bg-spare` hook worker chain always reaches the lock owner.

## Known scope boundaries, filed rather than fixed

- **Away mode does not park an open-decision crew on the same cadence.** The new class is watcher-only: `afk_present` is evaluated before it, and the other call site is guarded by `! afk_present`, so under away mode the class is inert and `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh` behaves exactly as it does on `main`. Away mode is not newly broken, and `docs/configuration.md` is scoped to that actual behaviour rather than claiming parity. Extending the class to away mode would be its own scoped change.
- **The ShellCheck environment gap.** `bin/fm-lint.sh` is the single owner of the lint definition and refuses to run under any version other than the pinned 0.11.0. Where that binary is absent the lint step exits 127, which is a missing tool rather than a lint failure; `bin/fm-lint.sh` was run against this exact head with pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0 and passes clean, and `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` passes.

## Notes on scope

`AGENTS.md` is touched only to add the one new never-touch state file, `state/.claude-autoarm-unresolved-ancestry`, to its always-loaded state-directory layout inventory, which would otherwise be wrong.
Everything else about script behaviour lives in the scripts' own headers and in the classified documentation owners.
Incident chronology is deliberately kept out of tracked docs and lives here in the PR body.

title: fix(brief): support configurable ship branches
body:
## Intent

Make ship branch names configurable without weakening the generated brief's safety contract or creating an unmergeable local-only task.

Closes #1887

## What changed

- Add `fm-brief.sh --branch <name>`, defaulting to the existing `fm/<task-id>` name.
- Reject empty, leading-dash, whitespace, quote, shell-unsafe, and invalid Git branch names.
- Substitute the selected branch throughout ship briefs while leaving scout and secondmate scaffolds unchanged.
- Record the selected ship branch in task metadata.
- Make the local-only merge gate and live bearings PR mapping consume the recorded branch with the legacy default for older task records.
- Add behavioral regressions for the reported custom-convention condition, metadata persistence, local-only landing, bearings mapping, validation failures, and default compatibility.

## Decisions

- Firstmate required the coordinated metadata, merge, and bearings scope because issue #1887 explicitly establishes that a brief-only override creates an unsafe unmergeable local-only task.
- Firstmate determined that an earlier abandoned narrow implementation, preserved at `fork/fm/fm-1887`, must deliberately not be used as this branch's base because it omits the consumer changes required by the issue.
- The bearings join reads task metadata paths already supplied by the canonical snapshot and streams its lookup JSON through stdin so it remains composable with PR #2137's jq-streaming work.
- Legacy briefs and task records fall back to `fm/<task-id>`, preserving existing homes and promoted scouts without migration.

## Validation

- `bash tests/fm-brief.test.sh`
- `bash tests/fm-spawn-worktree-settle.test.sh`
- `bash tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh`
- `bash tests/fm-bearings-snapshot.test.sh`
- `bash tests/fm-tangle-guard.test.sh`
- `bin/fm-lint.sh`
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`

The no-mistakes pipeline could not start because its internal gate retained the preserved earlier branch history and correctly rejected a non-fast-forward overwrite.
The coordinated implementation was instead pushed under the distinct fork branch requested by firstmate.

title: feat(bin): bind every recorded commitment to a probe that says whether it is real
body:
## Intent

Build the typed register of RECORDED-BUT-NOT-YET-REAL commitments, make it fail closed at session start, and register the network-egress ruling as its first entry.

THE PROBLEM. A commitment recorded with no enforcement probe reads as protection while protecting nothing, and this fleet hit that exact failure four separate ways in one day. (1) A ruling recorded and not enforced: data/captain-rulings-2026-08-06/capability-host-network-egress.md holds that agents get no unrestricted raw egress and that network is a typed Runtime-issued capability the host ENFORCES, while in fact every worker launches with enforcement disabled by construction and the capability catalog's own network.request row honestly records owner null, verifier null. (2) A guard with no caller: task_base_verify_branch was believed to close an inversion and has no runtime caller at all. (3) A derived-state row that went stale while being trusted: fm-decision-surface.sh owners reports invoking_known_next_stage as PENDING while CFVC-15 landed exactly that replacement, in a hand-maintained literal inside the composer that exists to stop firstmate hand-maintaining state. (4) A dated exception that expired into prose: E-05 self-expired 2026-08-08 and the writes were applied because a human filed a reminder, so the mechanism that saved it was diligence, not structure. Each was found by a person looking; none would have surfaced on its own.

WHAT TO BUILD. A machine-readable register carrying, per entry: a stable id; what was recorded and where the authoritative record lives (a ruling file, a captain authorisation, a decision hold, a config exception); the ENFORCEMENT PROBE, a path, symbol, command or predicate whose success means the commitment is now real; the expected state, so the probe's answer is interpretable; and the current derived state, computed, never written. The probe is the load-bearing field, and an entry without one is not admissible, because that is exactly the shape of the four failures above.

FAIL CLOSED AT SESSION START. Surface unenforced entries where they cannot be missed and make the absence of an all-clear structural. Session start must NOT be able to report a clean or quiet state while an entry's probe says the commitment is unenforced or its work is undispatched. An entry whose probe cannot RUN is could-not-observe, reported as such, and never read as enforced - three values, as everywhere else in this fleet. An entry whose probe now PASSES retires automatically, because a commitment that became real should stop nagging without anyone editing a list, and a register that needs hand-maintenance is the defect it was built to fix. bin/fm-bootstrap.sh already runs detect-only checks at every session start and already has an actionable-diagnostic vocabulary to print into: extend it, and do not build a parallel surfacing path.

FIRST ENTRIES. network-egress-ruled-not-enforced, whose probe is workers launched with permission enforcement disabled and network.request's owner and verifier being null; expected state after closure is enforcement present, current state is RULED-NOT-ENFORCED. This is the captain's "make the gap visible now" and is the only part of the network-egress work that starts now; the steps that actually close it are staged separately behind network-egress-enforcement-visible-then-staged and must NOT be attempted here. Plus captain-authorised work that is not yet in flight: an authorisation is a commitment like any other, and its probe is whether a live task, branch or pull request owns it.

THIRD ENTRY CLASS, CAPTAIN-RULED 2026-08-10 and folded into the schema rather than deferred: a ruled review finding. Measured four times in one day, a ruled criterion was reported APPLIED while not being MET, every time caught only by a worker re-checking its own work, and firstmate had made the criterion explicit in writing before the fourth and it still happened. Root cause is identical to the other entries: the criterion lives in firstmate prose, the fix lives in code, and nothing binds them. Applied is an action; met is a predicate, and the pipeline only knows the action happened. A ruling that says fix must supply a PROBE whose success means the criterion is met, and a resolved status event for a key that has a registered probe must NOT be accepted as resolved until that probe passes, with the open-decision fold continuing to show it. bin/fm-classify-lib.sh already owns keyed open and resolved semantics and bin/fm-status-event-lib.sh owns the envelope, so extend that fold and do not add a surface.

THREE TIERS, and the third is not optional because forcing a probe where none is possible would recreate this same failure one level up. executable: the probe runs directly and its exit status is the answer. cited-control: the probe confirms a named test exists and passes now while the watched-it-fail observation is cited as a named artifact rather than a claim - this is the strongest routinely achievable form and is the DEFAULT. attested: for a criterion that genuinely cannot execute, such as a comment being accurate; that tier must be MARKED and VISIBLE and never silently read as verified. A probe that cannot RUN is could-not-observe, never a pass.

THE PINNED BLOCK FORMAT, built to exactly, so what firstmate writes and what the register reads cannot drift. Firstmate writes decision files at data/<task-id>/decision-<key>.md, and every such file that directs fix carries exactly one fenced probe block with tier of executable, cited-control or attested; run is required for the first two and is a command run from the task worktree; control is required for cited-control and names the test or artifact watched to fail first; reason is required for attested, which carries no run. Exit 0 means the criterion is met, non-zero means not met, and unable to execute means could-not-observe and never a pass. Firstmate is applying this format to its own rulings from 2026-08-10 onward, before the mechanism lands.

NO BACK-FILLING. Do not back-fill decision keys ruled before 2026-08-10 with invented probes. They read could-not-observe, on the same principle that forbids back-filling historical verifier identities, because a fabricated record is indistinguishable from a real one afterwards.

WHAT THIS MUST NOT DO. It must not discourage a worker from re-checking its own work: all four catches came from exactly that, and the probe is a floor beneath diligence, not a replacement for it.

WHAT NOT TO DO. Do not remove or weaken any bypass flag: that work is staged behind a capability path that does not exist yet, disarming workers first breaks every lane and provides nothing, and the commission is explicit that bypasses retire only after bindings and adapters are proven. Do not reopen the network-egress ruling, which commission section 8 forbids: this is an implementation gap the ruling already authorises closing, not a question needing an answer. Do not suppress an entry by age, count or rate, which is the same mistake as suppressing a repeat escalation because it hides a genuine unmet commitment along with the noise; the fix is to make truth visible, never to make the question quieter. Do not build a greenfield reconciliation runtime: bin/fm-decision-surface.sh is already this fleet's derived-state composer with typed verdicts including unevaluable, and bin/fm-verify-lib.sh already owns the three-valued observation type, so extend them and say plainly if either genuinely does not fit.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. Red-capable: register an entry whose commitment is unmet, prove session start surfaces it and cannot report all-clear, then satisfy the probe and prove the entry retires with no hand edit. An entry whose probe cannot run reports could-not-observe and is proven distinguishable from both enforced and unenforced. The four failures listed above are each expressible as an entry - not all four need registering, but the shape must be demonstrated to cover them, and any that does not fit is a finding worth reporting. A hand-written status word cannot satisfy any entry, demonstrated.

CONSTRAINTS. This is firstmate's shared tracked material, governed by the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill. One sentence per line in prose; plain dashes; shellcheck-clean bin via bin/fm-lint.sh; colocated tests; never add an agent as a commit co-author; never write the captain-address convention into a commit message, pull request, or anything crewmates and other tools read. Session start is on the critical path of every session in this fleet, so anything added there must be cheap, detect-only, and must not mutate: a slow or noisy session start will be turned off, and then it protects nothing. git stash is SHARED across every worktree of this repo and must never be used in a pooled worktree. Several lanes are live and touching bin/, so expect to rebase and resolve a clean reconciliation per the captain's standing delegation.

LATER ACCEPTED REQUIREMENTS, folded in and superseding anything narrower above.

SESSION START MUST EXECUTE NO PROBE - this is a safety requirement, not a performance one. Session start may report RECORDED state; it may never execute a probe to find out. The whole chain counts, not just the bootstrap relay: fm-session-start.sh runs fm-admission.sh, which runs fm-fleet-snapshot.sh, which calls status_open_decisions per task, which reaches the closure gate and would run arbitrary decision run: commands inside task worktrees. Turning a cheap detect-only sweep into arbitrary execution on the critical path of every session is a regression that gets session start turned off, and then the register protects nothing. Not executing must NOT mean accepting: a resolution whose probe was not run stays visibly unverified and still open, never silently closed, because fail-open here is worse than the cost it avoids.

PROBE-RESULT CACHING, with a hard constraint. A cached probe result must carry its observation time, and a stale one must re-run or report could-not-observe; it must never silently serve an old answer as a current one, because caching a derived fact is exactly how derived state goes stale while being trusted. Key the cache on what the probe's answer actually depends on - the decision file bytes plus the worktree head - never on the task status file cksum, because the open-decision fold is DRIVEN by status appends so that key invalidates precisely when it is needed and helps only idle tasks. The probe bound is 10s. The observation time must be surfaced on the path that CONSUMES the result: bin/fm-classify-lib.sh must not capture the closure gate's stdout and discard it on the accept path, or the guarantee exists only for a human running the command by hand, which is a criterion reported applied and not met.

DECLARED-BUT-UNPROBED CONDITIONS. An entry whose recorded commitment has a half no probe reaches must declare that half rather than dropping it, and must not retire on the covered half alone: a half-covering probe returning one confident value is a check that cannot see something giving the reassuring answer. The declaring field's type is validated, and a malformed one makes the entry inadmissible rather than silently skipping the guard and letting a passing probe reach SATISFIED on a partial answer.

DERIVE, DO NOT ENUMERATE. If a list enumerates something the codebase already knows, derive it; a hand-maintained literal goes quietly vacuous the day a member is added, which is one of the measured failure shapes. Where a member genuinely cannot be derived, an unknown member yields could-not-observe, never silent exclusion.

NEW PERSISTENT STATE. Any new artifact under state/ is added to the AGENTS.md state inventory with its writing owner and lifecycle, and is reaped by teardown.

RULING PROBES ASSERT SPECIFIC CASES BY EXACT WORDING. Two firstmate rulings carry probes that grep the test suite for exact `ok` line substrings, so the corresponding cases must be named to match them verbatim: `unknown harness member yields could-not-observe`, `stale row asserts satisfied only when the probe inspects the row`, `session start executes no probe`, and `cached result carries observation time on the accept path`. A probe must assert the SPECIFIC case rather than merely invoking the suite that would contain it, because a suite passes whenever the suite is green, which says nothing about coverage.

OUT OF SCOPE for this round, agreed as a separate follow-up commit, and must NOT be added here: the registration gate refusing a probe that already passes at registration time; the externally-blocked third state and its guards; the property-asserting probe kind; the two probe kinds for project-worktree resolution and battery results; the rebase-drop-defect-remains-unprevented entry; and the schema document with worked examples per tier. A round that grows while it is being validated is how a fix ships without its criterion met.

## What Changed

- Adds `bin/fm-commitment-register.sh` plus a tracked `commitments/` register (`schema.json` and two entries: `network-egress-ruled-not-enforced`, `network-egress-enforcement-staged-work`). Each entry declares a typed probe (one of six kinds) whose result derives `SATISFIED` / `UNMET` / `UNOBSERVED` on every read - never stored - so an entry retires with no hand edit once its probe passes, an entry with a malformed or missing probe is inadmissible, and an entry declaring an unprobed half in `unobserved_conditions` cannot retire on the covered half alone. Probe targets are constrained to the tracked code root, and the path-bearing fields are derived from the schema rather than enumerated.
- Makes the absence of an all-clear structural: `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` relays open entries as `COMMITMENT:` diagnostics (and reports an absent interpreter loudly rather than silently), and `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh`'s existing keyed open/resolved fold now refuses a `resolved` event whose `data/<task-id>/decision-<key>.md` carries a pinned probe block until that probe passes, surfacing the refusal reason and the cached result's observation time on the consuming path. Session start's two calls that reach that fold (`fm-wake-drain.sh`, `fm-admission.sh`) carry `FM_COMMITMENT_NO_DECISION_RUN=1`, so the closed set of typed probes still runs there but no arbitrary decision-file `run:` executes on the critical path - and an unevaluated key stays visibly open, never silently closed.
- Supporting changes: `bin/fm-launch-lib.sh` gains a derived harness roster and `launch_permission_posture` accessor (unparseable arms stay in the roster as unknown rather than being dropped), probe results cache under `state/commitment-probe-cache/` keyed on decision-file bytes plus worktree head with a freshness bound and reaped by `bin/fm-teardown.sh`, `bin/fm-test-run.sh` maps the new suite into changed-file selection, and AGENTS.md / docs / the bootstrap-diagnostics and ask-user-authority skills record the register, its state artifact, and the probe-block format. Colocated coverage lands in `tests/fm-commitment-register.test.sh` alongside additions to the bootstrap, session-start, launch-lib and teardown suites.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Both round-4 items are fixed and the derivation is genuinely load-bearing rather than decorative - I independently reproduced the schema-driven path-arg set, confirmed it matches the script's own call sites via the new bidirectional control, and verified the vacuity case fails closed - leaving only a stale copy of superseded wording that lives outside the repository.

## Testing

Ran the five targeted suites this change touches (commitment register, bootstrap, session start, launch-lib, teardown) and they all pass, after isolating two pre-existing host-environment leaks in the fixtures (a system /usr/bin/node defeating a test's node removal, and a populated /tmp/fm-test-absent-nm-home) by pointing FM_TEST_BASE_PATH and TMPDIR at clean locations. Because passing tests alone do not show the intent, I also drove the real operator commands end-to-end and captured CLI transcripts: the shipped register reporting both first entries UNMET against this repository, a real fm-session-start.sh going from "(silent - all good)" to a COMMITMENT line and back to silence once the probe passed with the entry file byte-identical, SATISFIED/UNMET/UNOBSERVED proven distinguishable from a single entry, a hand-written status word refused, a half-covered commitment unable to retire, a decision-file run: command provably not executed by session start yet still not accepted, cached-verdict provenance surfaced on the fold's accept path and in fm-fleet-snapshot.sh --json, and all four measured failure shapes expressed as real entries each with its control. This is a shell/CLI surface with no rendered UI, so command transcripts are the end-user experience and no screenshot applies. The worktree is clean and scratch directories were removed.

title: fix: guard ship brief completion and watcher cleanup
body:
## Intent

Fix Firstmate core ship-brief generation in bin/fm-brief.sh: implementation completion must emit "working: implementation committed; awaiting no-mistakes", never done; reserve terminal done for the delivery mode's true terminal state, which in no-mistakes mode is a PR with green checks; add a generator regression rejecting more than one terminal done instruction. Fix generated keyed needs-decision syntax so the key appears before the colon where the status fold and fm-send --resolve-key read it; prove a generated keyed decision opens and matching resolved/--resolve-key closes it, while preserving existing unkeyed needs-decision behavior. Exclude the generic unkeyed needs-decision form from the keyed template. Do not include the attribution-guard fix, which ships separately in agent-env. Follow up on PR 2157's GitHub Behavior portable serial 2 timeout: reproduce and fix the watcher cleanup self-deadlock when TERM interrupts recovery-marker publication, add a deterministic regression, and push the updated branch so every GitHub check actually passes. Do not merge.

## What Changed

- Generate no-mistakes ship briefs that keep implementation completion nonterminal, reserve `done` for true delivery completion, and emit keyed decisions in parser-compatible syntax while preserving unkeyed decisions.
- Prevent TERM-triggered watcher cleanup deadlocks by releasing nested recovery locks while retaining wake-queue serialization through recovery publication.
- Add regression coverage for terminal instructions, decision resolution, and interrupted stale-lock recovery, with the watcher continuity documentation updated accordingly.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Captain, the change is well-bounded, satisfies the source-verifiable intent, and the follow-up resolves both previously reported watcher cleanup defects at the shared lock boundary.

## Testing

No pre-supplied baseline commands were present; targeted brief, decision, and watcher tests passed, manual CLI evidence demonstrated the generated contract and both keyed and legacy decision closure, the watcher deadlock reproduced on the base runtime and cleared on the target with recovery serialization intact, and no UI screenshot was applicable to these Markdown generator and daemon changes.

title: docs(agents): serialize no-mistakes runs within a Herdr crew group
body:
## Intent Add a standing operating rule to AGENTS.md section 7's Validate subsection: when firstmate has dispatched several crewmates onto the same shared project as part of a Herdr multiagent workflow, hold off triggering a new /no-mistakes run on one of them while another crewmate in that same group already has an active run (a live run-step state such as running/fixing/CI, not one merely parked at a gate awaiting a captain decision, since capacity is free while parked). Retrigger once the active run reaches a terminal or gated state. This addresses real resource contention the captain observed: multiple crewmates running /no-mistakes concurrently on the same shared project made CI runners unresponsive for hours and caused a daemon reattach timeout on a stalled run. This is a firstmate dispatch-timing rule only - it never manages, stops, or restarts the shared no-mistakes daemon itself, which is already established as an existing boundary elsewhere in AGENTS.md. Scope was deliberately narrowed from an earlier draft (which had proposed a blanket per-home serialization rule for any two tasks) to specifically the Herdr multiagent same-project scenario, per explicit captain clarification. This is a docs-only prose change (2 lines added) inline in AGENTS.md per firstmate-coding-guidelines - no new skill, no new script, no mechanism/queue implementation. ## What Changed - Added a rule to AGENTS.md section 7's Validate subsection: when firstmate has dispatched several crewmates onto the same shared project as part of a Herdr multiagent workflow, hold off triggering a new no-mistakes run on one of them while another crewmate in that same group already has an active run (running, fixing, or CI), retriggering once that run reaches a terminal or gated state. - Clarified this is a dispatch-timing rule only, scoped to firstmate's own triggering decisions within a Herdr crew group, and does not manage, stop, or restart the shared no-mistakes daemon. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A precisely-scoped 2-line docs-only addition to AGENTS.md's Validate subsection that matches every constraint in the stated intent: correct location (section 7/Validate), correct narrow scope (Herdr multiagent same-project dispatch timing), correct definition of "active" run state excluding gate-parked tasks, retrigger condition specified, and explicit disclaimer that it does not manage the shared daemon; no mechanism, script, or queue was added. ## Testing This is a pure prose addition to AGENTS.md with no executable interface, so per the test-quality rule no grep/string-matching test was written; instead the diff was verified for exact scope (2 lines, docs-only) and the new text was read in full context and cross-checked for placement, internal consistency, and consistency with the pre-existing daemon-restart boundary in stow/SKILL.md - all constraints in the intent are satisfied. ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

title: fix(brief): make the no-mistakes done gate behavioral and keyed decisions parse
body:
## Problem

Two recurring crewmate failure modes, both traced to what the generated brief actually says.

**1. Seven no-mistakes crewmates in two days** (a4, b1, c2, e1, e2, f1, f2) declared `done:` after a green local gate without ever invoking the pipeline, each costing the supervisor the same correction steer. The root cause was the scaffold's own definition of done, which opened with:

> The task is complete only when committed on your branch.
> When you believe it is complete, append `done: {summary}` to the status file and stop.
> Firstmate will then instruct you to run /no-mistakes to validate and ship a PR.

The premature `done:` line was *correct by the brief*. Two `done:` gates in one section, and the first one told the worker to stop and wait.

**2. Two crewmates wrote `needs-decision: [key=slug]`** with the key after the colon. `_fm_decision_key` read the token only from the verb prefix *before* the colon, so those decisions folded into the shared `default` bucket and `fm-send --resolve-key <real-key>` refused. Filed upstream as #2109.

## Changes

**`bin/fm-brief.sh` - no-mistakes definition of done.** Removed the commit-and-wait opening. The section now names exactly one done line, denies the near-miss finishes by name, and puts the pipeline invocation on the worker:

```
On this task `done:` means EXACTLY one line: `done: PR {url} checks green`.
An implementation commit is NOT done. A green local test, lint, build, or review run is NOT done. Nothing is done until a PR exists and its CI is green.
Running the pipeline is YOUR step, not firstmate's: the moment your implementation is committed, invoke the no-mistakes skill yourself (`/no-mistakes`, or `$no-mistakes` on codex) without waiting to be told.
Never append a `done:` line before that pipeline has produced a PR with green checks.
```

Four lines replacing three, with no pipeline mechanics duplicated - the no-mistakes skill remains their owner. The codex invocation form is named because the *worker* now types it rather than firstmate; `harness-adapters` still owns the full matrix.

`AGENTS.md` section 7's Validate step follows: firstmate triggers validation only when the worker has not already started it. Left unchanged, it would have been a second contradictory owner of that trigger.

**Keyed-decision grammar - both owners fixed.** The task asked which fix is right; the answer is both, for different reasons:

- *Scaffold (prevention).* Ship and scout rule 6 now show `needs-decision [key=<slug>]: {summary of options}` plus the example `needs-decision [key=api-shape]: REST or RPC`. This is what stops new workers from writing the broken shape.
- *Parser (containment).* `_fm_decision_key` now also accepts a well-formed `[key=<slug>]` token at the head of the note. Wording alone reaches only workers that read the new brief - not the ones already running, on other harnesses, or writing from a remote home whose lines are mirrored into the same stream. And per #2109, silently rewriting an explicitly stated key into a shared bucket is the unsafe half: two decisions collapse into one record, so an answer can close the wrong one while the real decision stays open.

`status_line_note` strips an accepted post-colon token so the note text, the reserved-key vocabulary check, and displays all see the real note.

A **malformed** bracket note (`[key=not a slug]`) deliberately stays ordinary note text on the historical `default` key rather than returning failure. Failure would drop the line out of the fold entirely, losing the decision - strictly worse than mislabeling it. Pre-colon behavior is unchanged.

Review caught one thing the original commit missed, fixed in `015eeb2`: `FM_OPEN_DECISIONS_FOLD_VERSION` had to be bumped. Without it, a decision persisted in a cursor open-set under the old grammar could never be closed by a later `resolved [key=x]` line - a permanently open ghost record.

## Tests

Colocated, behavior-only, through the real executables:

- `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` - the done gate names one line, denies an implementation commit and a green local gate, puts the invocation on the worker, and no longer offers a pre-PR done line; ship and scout protocols show the key before the colon.
- `tests/fm-wake-drain-open-decisions.test.sh` - a post-colon key opens its own decision, a pre-colon `resolved` closes it across positions, and a malformed bracket note folds as an ordinary default decision instead of vanishing.

Existing suites green: `fm-brief`, `fm-wake-drain-open-decisions`, `fm-wake-drain-open-decisions-cursor`, `fm-decision-hold-lifecycle`, `fm-pending-reply`, `fm-crew-state`, `fm-watch-triage`, `fm-remote-reply`, `fm-fleet-snapshot-view`. Parser changes use only bash 3.2 constructs.

Local lint reported ShellCheck absent on this machine (exit 127), so `bin/fm-lint.sh` could not run for CI parity; the CI lint job covers it.

## Note

This is a fork PR: the pushing machine has no write access to this repository. Upstream CI may not run for fork PRs.

title: fix: refresh stale Pi instructions after compaction

## Intent Build the Firstmate self-update instruction-staleness fix. Audit compact, resume, clear, and reset for every verified harness, and refresh only every supported harness and rebuild pair that reuses stale root instructions and has a working Firstmate delivery channel. Record the AGENTS.md SHA-256 baseline only on a genuine source=startup true session start, keyed to the active lock/session identity. Never create or replace that baseline on resume, clear, reset, compact, fork, or any other rebuild. When a supported stale-cache rebuild detects a missing, wrong-session, or changed baseline, inject the complete current AGENTS.md before the bulky digest. Preserve drift across the session so every later affected rebuild re-injects after an update, while equal rebuilds emit nothing. Add behavioral tests and a real isolated Pi plus private tmux E2E that first reproduces stale behavior on origin/main then verifies the fixed compact path. Do not claim live validation beyond Pi compact. Keep all test work isolated from the live fleet and do not use Herdr lifecycle. Captain explicitly declined speculative oversized-instruction delivery machinery: current AGENTS.md is 66199 bytes, below the existing 512 KiB Pi delivery cap, so preserve the existing cap rather than adding a mechanism for an unobserved oversized file. Fix genuine correctness and honesty defects within this minimal scope, including Pi continuation/fork true-start classification. ## What Changed - Record an immutable, session-keyed AGENTS.md SHA-256 baseline only after a genuine startup completes. - Re-inject the complete current AGENTS.md before Pi and pi-signed compaction digests when the baseline is missing, belongs to another session, or has drifted. - Correct Pi continuation and fork source classification, with behavioral coverage and an isolated real-Pi/tmux compaction regression test. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-bounded, preserves the immutable true-start baseline invariant, limits refresh to verified Pi compaction delivery, and includes behavior-focused regression coverage. ## Testing Portable behavioral tests exercised true-start baseline ownership, immutable drift handling, source routing, continuation/fork classification, unsupported harness behavior, delivery bounds, and failure paths; isolated real Pi 0.84.0 plus private tmux then reproduced stale post-compact instructions on origin/main and verified the fixed compact path re-injected the updated contract. title: feat(bin): add opt-in per-task Fast Repair delivery path
body:
## Intent

Implement a strict opt-in per-task Fast Repair path in FirstMate, entered by one exact explicit prefix, that fails closed unless reproduction, root cause, isolation, and every forbidden-risk exclusion are proven; uses Codex gpt-5.6-luna at medium effort; skips scouts and extra plan/design reviews for eligible repairs; requires a regression test and focused module tests before an early direct PR; keeps broader tests and PR checks running concurrently; never auto-merges and always requires captain merge approval; adds an approximately 20-second progress cadence only for Fast Repair; leaves all project modes, dispatch, delivery, merge, teardown, and normal watcher behavior unchanged; documents invocation and refusal rules; and adds full eligibility, refusal, dispatch, direct-PR, cadence, and unchanged-normal regression tests.

## What Changed

- Adds `bin/fm-fast-repair.sh`, which owns the new per-task Fast Repair path: a typed eligibility record that fails closed unless reproduction, root cause, isolation, and every forbidden-risk exclusion are proven; `evidence` runs and records a regression family plus a different focused family through the tracked `bin/fm-test-run.sh` runner and proves the selected regression artifact fails at the recorded reproduction commit and passes at the tested head; `publish-pr` then opens the direct PR early, `broader` runs a wider family concurrently, and `ready` only reports green when the broader family and all required PR checks pass.
- Threads `fast-repair` through the existing entrypoints as a task mode, not a project mode: `fm-brief.sh` scaffolds a Fast Repair definition of done that skips scouts and extra reviews, `fm-spawn.sh` re-proves eligibility and pins the built-in `codex` / `gpt-5.6-luna` / `medium` profile with `yolo=off` (refusing a conflicting or raw launch command, and reusing the recorded profile on relaunch), `fm-promote.sh` refuses to promote a scout into it, and `fm-teardown.sh` removes the new evidence and progress artifacts with id-exact matching. `fm-watch.sh` gains a ~20-second task-scoped progress cadence that runs only while task metadata records `fast_repair=eligible`, interrupts waits only on a changed result, retires from forge polling after the first green rollup, and leaves normal polling, stale handling, and backend cadences untouched.
- Documents the path in new `docs/fast-repair.md` (invocation prefix, eligibility, refusals, delivery) with pointers from `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, and the audiences manifest; adds `fm-test-run.sh --list-shard-plan` so `docs/fm-test-portable-shards.md` derives its shard table from the runner; and adds regression tests for eligibility, refusal, dispatch, direct PR, cadence, teardown, relaunch, and unchanged normal-path behavior.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: A large new subsystem (~4.5k lines) adds concurrent fork/marker/handoff machinery inside the watcher supervision loop and a new removal path in teardown, but every Fast Repair gate fails closed, the non-Fast-Repair watcher and teardown paths are verifiably inert, and both pipeline fix rounds land narrow corrections backed by regression tests that genuinely fail before the fix.

## Testing

I ran the targeted Fast Repair test scripts and the watcher, dispatch, relaunch, teardown, delivery, brief, and documentation scripts that the change touches; all passed with no failures or gate skips. Because passing tests alone do not show the feature, I also built a fixture project with a real off-by-one defect and drove the shipped scripts end to end against a recording forge fake: near-miss prefixes and an unproven root cause or in-scope schema change are refused; a complete typed record is accepted and stored private; the dispatch gate accepts the real detached pooled worktree and rejects a foreign repository; the generated brief tells the crewmate to skip scouts and extra reviews and gives the exact evidence, publish, broader, and ready commands; the regression test fails pre-fix and passes at the tested head; a PR before evidence and a non-new regression selector are refused; the direct PR opens right after the focused gates; the broader family runs and is refused when it repeats the focused family while checks are still pending; a failed rollup and an all-cancelled rollup are never called green; ready prints the approved counts; the whole path made zero merge or auto-merge forge calls with yolo=off; and a broader failure after green still surfaces locally. For cadence I ran the real watcher with no interval override inside a 600-second poll: the eligible Fast Repair task polled at +20s and +20s while an ordinary no-mistakes task polled the forge zero times and wrote no cadence state. This surface is CLI and generated-prose only, so there is no rendered UI to screenshot; the CLI transcripts are the end-user surface. I removed nothing from the working tree and it is clean; evidence files stay in the dedicated evidence directory.
