#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end Fast Repair walkthrough against a realistic fixture project.
#
# It builds a small "secretary" project with a real off-by-one defect, then
# drives the shipped Fast Repair path exactly as firstmate and a crewmate would:
# refusals, typed intake, dispatch gate, brief, evidence (regression fails
# before the repair and passes at the tested head), early direct PR, concurrent
# broader family, readiness, and the merge-authority boundary.
#
# The forge is a recording fake, so nothing leaves this machine.
set -u

ROOT=${FM_SOURCE_ROOT:?set FM_SOURCE_ROOT to the firstmate checkout}
WORK=${1:?usage: demo-fast-repair-e2e.sh <work-dir>}
ID=fr-secretary-count

rm -rf "$WORK"
mkdir -p "$WORK"
PROJECT="$WORK/project"
TASKWT="$WORK/task-worktree"
HOME_DIR="$WORK/firstmate-home"
FAKEBIN="$WORK/fakebin"
FORGE="$WORK/forge"
mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR/state" "$HOME_DIR/data" "$FAKEBIN" "$FORGE"

FAST="$ROOT/bin/fm-fast-repair.sh"
BRIEF="$ROOT/bin/fm-brief.sh"
SPAWN="$ROOT/bin/fm-spawn.sh"

step() { printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$*"; }
run() { # <label> <cmd...>
  local label=$1; shift
  printf '\n$ %s\n' "$label"
  "$@" 2>&1 | sed 's/^/  /'
  printf '  [exit %s]\n' "${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
}
fm() { # fast-repair helper with this home, called from outside the project
  ( cd "$WORK" && PATH="$FAKEBIN:$PATH" FM_HOME="$HOME_DIR" \
    FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$HOME_DIR/state" FM_DATA_OVERRIDE="$HOME_DIR/data" "$FAST" "$@" )
}

########################################
# 1. The project, with the reported defect
########################################
mkdir -p "$PROJECT/lib" "$PROJECT/tests" "$PROJECT/bin"
cat > "$PROJECT/lib/search.sh" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Secretary local draft search.
search_count() { # <query> <deleted-count>
  local matches=$1 deleted=$2
  # Defect: the deleted drafts are never removed from the reported count.
  printf '%s\n' "$matches"
}
SH
cat > "$PROJECT/tests/secretary-search.test.sh" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Focused module test: search returns the raw match count when nothing is deleted.
set -u
. "$(dirname "$0")/../lib/search.sh"
[ "$(search_count 5 0)" = 5 ] || { echo "not ok - undeleted search count"; exit 1; }
echo "ok - search reports every live draft"
SH
cat > "$PROJECT/tests/secretary-suite.test.sh" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Broader suite: the module plus its neighbours.
set -u
. "$(dirname "$0")/../lib/search.sh"
[ "$(search_count 5 0)" = 5 ] || { echo "not ok - suite live count"; exit 1; }
[ "$(search_count 0 0)" = 0 ] || { echo "not ok - suite empty count"; exit 1; }
echo "ok - secretary suite"
SH
cat > "$PROJECT/bin/fm-test-run.sh" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tracked project test runner: families, selectors, and typed markers.
set -u
family_tests() {
  case $1 in
    secretary-regression) printf '%s\n' tests/secretary-count-regression.test.sh ;;
    secretary-search) printf '%s\n' tests/secretary-search.test.sh ;;
    secretary-suite) printf '%s\n' tests/secretary-suite.test.sh ;;
    *) return 2 ;;
  esac
}
if [ "${1:-}" = --list-families ]; then
  printf '%s\n' secretary-regression secretary-search secretary-suite; exit 0
fi
if [ "${1:-}" = --list ] && [ "${2:-}" = --family ]; then family_tests "$3"; exit $?; fi
if [ "${1:-}" = --family ] && [ "$#" = 2 ]; then
  family=$2
  scripts=$(family_tests "$family") || exit 2
elif [ "$#" = 1 ]; then
  scripts=$1
  case $1 in
    tests/secretary-count-regression.test.sh) family=secretary-regression ;;
    tests/secretary-search.test.sh) family=secretary-search ;;
    tests/secretary-suite.test.sh) family=secretary-suite ;;
    *) exit 2 ;;
  esac
else
  exit 2
fi
status=0
for script in $scripts; do
  printf 'FM_TEST_BEGIN %s %s family=%s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$script" "$family"
  if bash "$script"; then code=0; else code=1; status=1; fi
  printf 'FM_TEST_END %s %s exit=%s duration_ms=0 gate_skip=false\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$script" "$code"
done
exit "$status"
SH
chmod +x "$PROJECT/bin/fm-test-run.sh" "$PROJECT/tests"/*.test.sh
git -C "$PROJECT" init --quiet -b main

title: fix(bin): pin decision-key placement in generated crewmate briefs
body:
## Problem

`bin/fm-classify-lib.sh` parses `[key=<slug>]` only between the status verb and the colon, but the generated brief scaffolds never said so.
On 2026-08-10 a worker wrote every decision marker after the colon, so the open-decision fold recorded all of them under the single `default` key and the individual escalations were lost.

This replaces #1969, which carried the same intent but was pushed directly and so permanently fails the required `PR must be raised via no-mistakes` check.

## Changes

- The ship, scout, and secondmate scaffolds in `bin/fm-brief.sh` now pin key placement between the verb and the colon, state the slug grammar (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; no spaces and no angle brackets), and give both the bare and keyed self-close forms.
- Every keyed example a scaffold hands out uses a literal slug, so a worker who copies an example verbatim produces a line the parser accepts.
  The previous `[key=<work-slug>]` placeholder was itself rejected by the parser when copied as written.
- `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh` changes no behavior.
  It gains only a comment recording that a malformed slug names nothing, so such a line is ignored on both the opening and the closing side, and a second comment recording the fold-version bump duty at the constant's declaration.
- `FM_OPEN_DECISIONS_FOLD_VERSION` stays at 2 because the fold semantics are unchanged.

Making a malformed opening key visible rather than inert was explored during review and deliberately withdrawn: every representation tried either evicted a real decision, evicted another malformed entry, or produced an entry no `resolved` line could ever name, which permanently wedged the away-return gate in `bin/fm-afk-return.sh`.
That work is tracked separately, where a bounded and closable design can include that consumer from the start.

## Validation

- `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` renders each scaffold and feeds its own key examples through the real classifier, so an unparseable example fails the suite.
- `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` covers the exact 2026-08-10 incident line, the correctly placed form, and a malformed closing key closing nothing.
- `tests/fm-wake-drain-open-decisions-cursor.test.sh` covers a cursor written under another fold version being refolded rather than trusted.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` passes.

title: fix(composer): keep a titled composer rule from discarding a live composer
body:
## Summary

A focused Claude pane's composer classified `unknown` instead of `empty` under the herdr backend, which indefinitely defers away-mode escalation injection: the daemon reads `unknown` as "cannot prove this composer is safe to type into" and correctly declines. The composer was in fact idle and empty.

This is the herdr counterpart of the cmux borderless-composer fix (#2029). Same underlying shape, different backend surface, and it survived that fix because it fails through a different rule.

## Root cause

Claude draws its borderless composer between two horizontal `─` rules. While a pane is **focused**, herdr overlays the pane's terminal title on the **top** rule, so that rule renders as dashes *plus text*:

```
─────────────────── [ Check Firstmate setup readiness ] ─────────────────
❯
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

The dashes-only separator predicate correctly rejects that titled row, so the separated-shape pair never opens. The composer's own **bottom** rule is then an unmatched separator sitting *below* the `❯` row the scan had already matched correctly. The separated-shape staleness rule reads an unmatched separator below a candidate as proof the candidate is stale scrollback, discards the correct match, and returns `unknown`.

Only a focused pane carries the title overlay, which is why supervisor panes failed while worker panes stayed readable — the asymmetry that makes this easy to miss.

## The fix: narrow the consumer, not the predicate

The dashes-only separator predicate also feeds the Pi identity conjunction, where being wrong about what closes a separated composer would promote an unidentified blank region into an injection target. That is a genuine safety gate, so it is left strictly as-is.

Instead the staleness invalidation now spares a bare agent glyph that is immediately sandwiched between a rule above (solid *or* titled) and the window's only separator directly below — Claude's composer box. Adjacency on **both** edges is what preserves the staleness rule everywhere else: a glyph genuinely stranded in scrollback has transcript rows, not its own box edges, between it and the separator below.

`_fm_composer_rule_row` is anchored at both ends and requires every non-dash residue to be ASCII-printable or whitespace, so a row carrying box-drawing structure of its own can never pass as a plain rule.

## Why two distinct defects had to be fixed for this to work

This shape needs the glyph row read as *empty* **and** the composer row kept from being discarded. Either one alone still yields a wrong verdict:

| Top rule | Glyph row | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| titled (focused) | `❯` + U+00A0 NBSP | `unknown` | `empty` |
| titled (focused) | `❯` + ASCII space | `unknown` | `empty` |
| clean (unfocused) | `❯` + U+00A0 NBSP | `empty` | `empty` |
| clean (unfocused) | `❯` + ASCII space | `empty` | `empty` |

Claude renders its idle prompt as `❯` followed by U+00A0, not an ASCII space. The NBSP half of this pair — accepting a glyph row whose only content is a non-ASCII whitespace character — was fixed for all backends by #2102 via the shared `FM_COMPOSER_UNICODE_SPACES` normalisation, which is why the bottom two rows already pass on `main`. That normalisation is character-safe rather than byte-slicing, so it holds under `LC_ALL=C` too (the hazard behind #883).

This PR fixes the remaining titled-rule half. The two are independent: on `main` the titled cases fail regardless of which whitespace character the glyph row carries, because the row is discarded before its content is ever judged.

## Verification

**Live probe, before and after on identical bytes.** The real focused pane was captured once (2504 bytes of ANSI) and classified with both versions of the library, so no pane state change between runs can explain the difference:

```
pre-fix  library on captured bytes -> unknown
post-fix library on captured bytes -> empty
```

**Live guard** (`FM_COMPOSER_MATRIX_LIVE=1 tests/fm-composer-matrix-live-e2e.test.sh`), herdr 0.8.0 + claude 2.1.226.634:

```text
ok - herdr (herdr 0.8.0) + claude (claude 2.1.226.634 ...): focused pane w1:p9 titled composer rule is recognized as a rule
ok - herdr (herdr 0.8.0) + claude (claude 2.1.226.634 ...): idle pane w1:p1 (focused=false) classifies empty
ok - herdr (herdr 0.8.0) + claude (claude 2.1.226.634 ...): idle pane w1:p9 (focused=true) classifies empty
```

The `focused=true` line is the exact shape that failed. Because the title overlay exists only on a focused pane, no tmux fixture can render it — this is the harness-dependent half of the required test pair, and the guard emits an explicit note rather than passing silently when no focused Claude pane was available to exercise it.

**Portable regression** covers all four matrix cells with no harness present and asserts the divergence deliberately, so the case cannot go vacuously green. Reverting only the consumer narrowing reproduces the exact failure (`expected empty, got 'unknown'`).

**Negative cases confirm no widening of `empty`.** Wrongly reading a composer as empty is worse than the original bug, since it would let the daemon type into a shell prompt or over half-typed input:

- dead shell glyphs `$ > % #` on a titled row -> `unknown`
- blank row between two rules -> `unknown` (strict blank-row posture preserved)
- typed text, titled and clean -> `pending`
- glyph stranded above a genuinely live pair, non-adjacent separator, no rule above, bordered row above -> `unknown`
- Pi: idle -> `empty`, working -> `unknown`, identity probe absent -> `unknown`

The strict separator predicate that gates Pi identity still rejects a titled rule, so recognizing the rule did not relax that gate.

## Testing

- `tests/fm-composer-lib.test.sh` — 29 ok, 0 failures
- `tests/fm-composer-ghost.test.sh` — 33 ok, 0 failures
- `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh` — 171 ok, 0 failures
- `tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` — 49 ok, 0 failures
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed` — 57 scripts selected, 0 failures
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` — clean (pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0)
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` — clean (`surfaces=67 local_links=236`)

Dated per-harness evidence recorded in `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md` under a new "Herdr focused-pane titled composer rule" section, pointing at the live guard as the refresh command.

title: fix(spawn): durably lease pooled worktrees before handoff
body:
## Intent Implement GitHub issue #1924, "Worktree pool hands over and resets an idle worker's slot before anything downstream can object", in kunchenguid/firstmate against main. Reproduce the exact reported behavior before changing production code and explain that reproduction in the PR. Fix only this defect with the smallest reversible change: ordinary non-Orca task and scout spawns must acquire pooled worktrees through Treehouse durable leases held by the task id so an idle or concurrently live worker's slot cannot be offered and reset before downstream validation, while preserving every other caller and existing teardown release behavior. Add executable-interface regression coverage that fails against the pre-fix behavior and passes after the fix, and report both directions in the PR. Do not refactor, rename, tidy adjacent logic, change unrelated script contracts, flags, or output, touch captain-private data/state/config/projects, or alter safety, guard, and supervision boundaries beyond what this issue requires. Keep affected backend integration rationale and the authoritative worktree architecture documentation accurate without broadening behavior. Validate with the repository shell tests, every covering test, the pinned shell lint, documentation checks, and a manual scratch Treehouse exercise; no database or stack is involved. Browser validation is not applicable because this repository has no browser-facing surface. Cypress must not be run because this repository has no Cypress suite. Treat the identical tests/fm-teardown.test.sh leaked-process-reap failure at merge-base 7f051002b65adb196fdf3804a13d965046782d36 as a demonstrated pre-existing flake outside issue #1924; do not improvise an unrelated fix. Push only to the fork remote as branch fm/fm-1924, never origin and never force-push. Open the PR in kunchenguid/firstmate with base main and head 4mb1t10n:fm/fm-1924 using a body file, never inline body. Never merge and never enable auto-merge. At the exact final PR head, read gh-axi PR checks and mergeable_state; if no CI checks are configured, state exactly that rather than calling it green. Closes #1924 ## What Changed - Acquire fresh non-Orca task and scout worktrees with task-owned durable Treehouse leases, then move each backend into the exact leased path. - Return leases when spawning aborts, including bounded retries for transient Git `index.lock` failures. - Update backend/worktree documentation and executable regression coverage for lease acquisition, path validation, and abort cleanup. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is narrowly scoped and now durably leases ordinary non-Orca task worktrees, arms abort cleanup immediately after acquisition, and accepts only the exact leased path before publishing metadata. ## Testing The focused executable regression passed, and a real scratch Treehouse exercise demonstrated that an idle task-held lease remains unavailable to a concurrent requester and becomes available only after explicit return; abort cleanup, exact-path validation, and transient-lock retry also passed. No browser or visual evidence was captured because this repository has no browser-facing surface; the CLI transcripts are the end-user evidence.
Evidence: Focused regression transcript ```text ok - fm_primary_tangle_branch: feature branch alarms; default/detached/non-git stay silent ok - fm-guard: bordered tangle banner fires only for a feature branch and suppresses repair commands in read-only mode ok - fm-bootstrap: TANGLE problem line fires only for a feature branch and suppresses repair commands in detect-only mode ok - fm-brief: ship brief asserts worktree isolation before the branch step ok - fm-spawn: aborts unless the resolved worktree is a genuine, isolated worktree ok - fm-spawn: an abort after acquiring a durable treehouse lease returns it to the pool ok - fm-spawn: cwd-discovery failure returns its durable lease ok - fm-spawn: an abort's lease return retries a transient git index.lock instead of leaking the pool slot ok - fm-spawn: appends windows by session-colon, pins the name, and targets the window id ```
Evidence: Manual durable Treehouse lease lifecycle ```text $ treehouse get --lease --lease-holder task-alpha 🌳 Setting up worktree... 🌳 Leased worktree at /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZR8QWFY8GX5JZARYY22SQEW/treehouse-scratch/repo/.treehouse/repo-440483/1/repo. Run 'treehouse return /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZR8QWFY8GX5JZARYY22SQEW/treehouse-scratch/repo/.treehouse/repo-440483/1/repo' to release it. leased_path=/tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZR8QWFY8GX5JZARYY22SQEW/treehouse-scratch/repo/.treehouse/repo-440483/1/repo $ treehouse status --json (task-alpha lease) [{"name":"1","path":"/tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZR8QWFY8GX5JZARYY22SQEW/treehouse-scratch/repo/.treehouse/repo-440483/1/repo","status":"leased","lease_id":"4520c60a9f9f0081fbe38baf73d1466b","lease_holder":"task-alpha","leased_at":"2026-08-11T11:26:25.633557072Z","processes":[]}] $ treehouse get --lease --lease-holder task-beta 🌳 Setting up worktree... 🌳 Leased worktree at /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZR8QWFY8GX5JZARYY22SQEW/treehouse-scratch/repo/.treehouse/repo-440483/2/repo. Run 'treehouse return /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZR8QWFY8GX5JZARYY22SQEW/treehouse-scratch/repo/.treehouse/repo-440483/2/repo' to release it. second_path=/tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZR8QWFY8GX5JZARYY22SQEW/treehouse-scratch/repo/.treehouse/repo-440483/2/repo verified: task-alpha leased slot was not re-offered to task-beta $ treehouse return --force "$first" 🌳 Worktree returned to pool. $ treehouse status --json (after task-alpha return) [{"name":"1","path":"/tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZR8QWFY8GX5JZARYY22SQEW/treehouse-scratch/repo/.treehouse/repo-440483/1/repo","status":"available","lease_id":"","lease_holder":"","leased_at":null,"processes":[]},{"name":"2","path":"/tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZR8QWFY8GX5JZARYY22SQEW/treehouse-scratch/repo/.treehouse/repo-440483/2/repo","status":"leased","lease_id":"29147d20a07170e1312715e548f6586c","lease_holder":"task-beta","leased_at":"2026-08-11T11:26:25.813448064Z","processes":[]}] $ treehouse return --force "$second" 🌳 Worktree returned to pool. verified: both durable leases returned cleanly ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:2223` - A durable lease can leak permanently if `treehouse get --lease` succeeds but the backend target disappears, `cd` fails, or cwd discovery never observes the worktree. The timeout exits at line 2266 before cleanup is armed at line 2269, leaving no metadata for teardown and no process-liveness fallback. Acquire and capture the path at a boundary owned by `fm-spawn.sh`, then arm cleanup before sending the backend `cd`; add executable coverage for acquisition followed by cwd-discovery failure. 🔧 Fix: Arm durable lease cleanup before cwd discovery 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:2228` - The acquired lease path is captured, but cwd discovery still accepts any isolated worktree after two matching reads. If the backend `cd` fails while the endpoint remains in another worktree, or reports the same stale worktree twice, `WT` becomes that unrelated path; metadata then records it, cleanup is disarmed, and teardown returns the wrong worktree while the task-id lease remains leaked. Treat `TREEHOUSE_ABORT_WT` as authoritative and require the discovered physical cwd to equal it before publishing metadata. 🔧 Fix: Bind backend cwd to captured durable lease ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - Inspected `git diff 76355e20b4f44d968ca43c14e1bb21c100ac90d7..acbcd73104d2bb395041dfe6832c0442669173e3` to identify the affected executable paths and acceptance behavior. - `tests/fm-tangle-guard.test.sh` - Manual scratch exercise using real Treehouse v2.1.1: `treehouse get --lease --lease-holder task-alpha`, a concurrent lease for `task-beta`, `treehouse status --json`, and `treehouse return --force` for both paths. - `git status --short` after testing to confirm no working-tree artifacts remained.
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix: allow explicit home for watcher commands
body:
## Intent

Fix #2002 so non-pane shells do not remain unarmable when they must override a sibling home's inherited `FM_HOME`. Permit exactly one non-empty literal `FM_HOME=<path>` prefix on the final watcher arm or checkpoint command while preserving every other watcher safety denial and unrelated behavior.

Closes #2002

## What Changed

- Allow exactly one non-empty literal `FM_HOME=<path>` prefix for a final `fm-watch-arm.sh` or `fm-watch-checkpoint.sh` invocation.
- Reject unquoted tilde-prefixed values because Bash expands them before execution.
- Preserve wholly quoted literal tilde paths, while intentionally rejecting mixed quoted/unquoted tilde prefixes.
- Add behavioral regression coverage across all supported hook transports and document the narrow exception.

## Reproduction

Before the fix, a scratch non-pane shell with an inherited sibling `FM_HOME` could not safely arm the intended home: the explicit command `FM_HOME=<intended-home> bin/fm-watch-checkpoint.sh --seconds 180` was rejected as `watcher-nested`. The new E05 behavioral case failed before the implementation and passed afterward across Codex, Claude, Grok, OpenCode, and Pi hook transports.

Manual post-fix scratch verification showed the explicit-home checkpoint command exiting 0 with no stdout or stderr through all five transports. Representative unrelated safety violations remained denied, including empty or alternate assignments, unquoted tilde expansion, background execution, pipelines, and redirection.

## Decisions

- Firstmate directed the narrow follow-up fix to reject unquoted tilde expansion while preserving wholly quoted literal `FM_HOME` paths, with focused failing-before/passing-after coverage and no general shell-parser redesign.
- Firstmate, under delegated routine authority, declined compatibility for mixed quoted/unquoted tilde prefixes. Therefore values such as `FM_HOME=~'user'/firstmate` remain denied; only wholly quoted literal tilde paths are preserved.

## Validation

- `tests/fm-arm-pretool-check.test.sh` passed, including the cross-transport behavioral matrix and focused tilde-prefix cases.
- Manual executable-hook verification passed for the explicit-home checkpoint command through all five supported transports.
- The full repository suite at the feature head reported ten failures outside the touched suite. The same ten failure suites reproduced at merge-base `7f051002`; the historical control additionally exposed two remote-worker timing failures and a longer watcher-lock hang. These results are pre-existing and outside this change's scope.
- Browser validation is not applicable because this repository has no browser-facing surface.
- Cypress was not run; this repository has no Cypress suite.
- No database is involved.

## Risk

The change is limited to the watcher arm/checkpoint command policy and its behavioral tests. Other assignments, shell composition, and watcher safety boundaries remain denied as before.

title: fix(bin): preserve Codex Desktop fleet-lock ownership
body:
## Intent

Implement GitHub issue #1933 in kunchenguid/firstmate, whose authoritative title is "Fix Codex Desktop fleet-lock recognition", and fully resolve it with the smallest reversible change.

Recognize managed Codex Desktop only from the exact paired markers CODEX_CI=1 and a UUID-shaped CODEX_THREAD_ID. Preserve existing behavior and safety for unmanaged callers, malformed or partial markers, live competing sessions, different Codex threads, and every non-Codex harness. Keep state/.lock numeric and use the thread sidecar as durable ownership proof across short-lived Codex Desktop tool subprocesses.

At the shared lock publication boundary only, retain the original numeric PID solely when the valid recorded Codex thread sidecar exactly proves the same current owner. This must prevent PID churn across repeated Codex re-emits so existing completion tracking continues to re-emit rather than falling back to full startup. Do not patch downstream raw-PID comparisons and do not broaden the lock contract. Add regression coverage for repeated acquisitions/re-emits that proves both stable numeric PID and real bin/fm-sessionstart-run.sh completion routing. Keep this semantically composable with open PR #2132: same-thread retention must leave any existing .lock.pid-identity.<pid> sidecar untouched; fresh/replacement publications remain compatible with that PR's process-identity validation.

Rationale for the PR Decisions section, attributed to firstmate: durable ownership across short-lived tools while preserving existing callers is an accepted #1933 requirement, and PID churn on repeated Codex re-emits directly defeats that guarantee, so the correction is required scope rather than an expansion.

Reproduce the reported symptom before the fix and document reproduction and before/after regression evidence in the PR. Run focused shell tests, lint, documentation checks, and covering tests. Exercise the fix manually only in scratch locations, never live data/ or state/. Do not touch data/, state/, config/, or projects/. Do not refactor, rename, tidy adjacent logic, change other scripts' contracts/flags/output, or alter unrelated safety/supervision boundaries.

TEST EXCLUSION — DO NOT RUN OR RERUN tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh. Its branch run and exact base run at base SHA 7f051002b65adb196fdf3804a13d965046782d36 both already failed identically with "not ok - first config push did not reach pointer delivery"; this config-push fixture is pre-existing and out of scope. Record both outputs and the base SHA in the PR; do not fix it. A separate fm-session-start.test.sh ambient-node fixture failure was also confirmed pre-existing at base during the prior pipeline test stage; do not change production or tests for it, and use the intended node-free test PATH if that suite is run.

No database is involved. Browser validation is not applicable. Never run Cypress locally; this repository has no Cypress suite. State those facts in the PR.

Push only to fork (https://github.com/4mb1t10n/firstmate.git), never origin. Open the PR against kunchenguid/firstmate main with head 4mb1t10n:fm/fm-1933, writing the body to a file rather than inline. Never force-push, merge, or enable auto-merge.

Closes #1933

## Decisions

- **Firstmate — 2026-08-11:** Same-thread numeric PID retention is required by issue #1933 because durable Codex Desktop ownership across short-lived tool subprocesses would otherwise fail completion re-emission. The correction remains confined to the shared lock-publication boundary and preserves non-Codex and competing-thread safety.
- **Firstmate — 2026-08-11:** Clear inherited Codex markers at verified OpenCode, Kimi, and Muse launch boundaries so non-Codex children cannot be misclassified as managed Codex Desktop sessions; focused regression coverage supports the boundary.

## What Changed

- Recognize managed Codex Desktop sessions only from paired `CODEX_CI=1` and UUID-shaped `CODEX_THREAD_ID` markers, using a thread sidecar as durable lock ownership proof.
- Preserve the numeric lock PID for repeated acquisitions by the same Codex Desktop thread so clear and compact completion routing continues to re-emit instead of restarting.
- Prevent spawned OpenCode, Kimi, and Muse workers from inheriting Codex Desktop markers, with regression and live opt-in coverage for marker validation, lock contention, PID stability, and re-emits.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is narrowly scoped, preserves the required lock and harness invariants, and the fix-round launch-boundary hygiene is behaviorally covered wit

title: feat(bootstrap): hint at reverted WSL2 mirrored networking when remote secondmate host is unreachable
body:
## Intent

WSL2 mirrored-networking hint for unreachable remote secondmate hosts

## What Changed
- Add `fm_wsl2_mirrored_networking_hint` to `bin/fm-remote-readiness-lib.sh`, which detects when the local host is WSL2 without `networkingMode=mirrored` set in `.wslconfig` and returns a one-line remediation hint (recreate the `[wsl2]` config, then `wsl --shutdown` from Windows and relaunch); supports `FM_WSL_CONFIG_PATH` and `FM_WSL_USERS_DIR` test-only overrides for locating the per-user `.wslconfig`.
- Wire the hint into `secondmate_liveness_one` in `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` so all three "remote host unavailable" skip messages append `(<hint>)` when the heuristic matches, leaving the existing message unchanged otherwise.
- Document the two new override env vars in `docs/configuration.md`.
- Add unit test coverage in `tests/fm-secondmate-liveness.test.sh` for WSL2 hint detection, including username resolution and case-insensitive matching of the `networkingMode` config value.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The fix-round change correctly makes wsl2_hint computation lazy (only on actual remote_rc==255 unreachability) and memoizes it per-call via the ${wsl2_hint+x} guard, resolving the prior round's perf finding without introducing new bugs; the change is small, well-bounded, and matches the WSL2 hint intent.

## Testing

Ran tests/fm-secondmate-liveness.test.sh end-to-end: it exercises fm_wsl2_mirrored_networking_hint directly with a faked uname -r and faked/overridden .wslconfig (via FM_WSL_CONFIG_PATH/FM_WSL_USERS_DIR and a faked cmd.exe) across all branches (non-WSL2 host, mirrored already configured, config absent, config present without mirrored mode, username resolution via cmd.exe, sole-glob fallback, case-insensitive match), and separately exercises the surrounding secondmate_liveness_sweep behavior in bin/fm-bootstrap.sh via full subprocess runs. All 22 assertions pass. One gap: no test drives the actual call site in secondmate_liveness_one (the remote_host + SSH-unreachable/255 branch) with a faked WSL2 uname simultaneously, so the composed end-user output line combining the unreachable message with the hint is not directly exercised - the existing fm-remote-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh proves that same code path's base message is correct on the (non-WSL2) test host, and the hint-appending logic is a trivial, unit-tested string concatenation, so this is a low-risk narrow gap rather than an untested feature.

- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 info across 1 run (2m36s)

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

title: feat(guard): refuse destructive tmux commands at the tool boundary
body:
## What this fixes

A worker that runs `tmux kill-server` from its pane ends the tmux server that hosts the captain's session, itself, and every sibling worker.
Nothing appears in any system log, because a deliberate `kill-server` is an orderly shutdown.

On 2026-08-11 that happened for real, 50 seconds after dispatch:

```sh
export TMUX_TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
S=fmrepro$$
tmux new-session -d -s "$S" -n realwin 'sleep 300'
...
tmux kill-server 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$TMUX_TMPDIR"
```

The isolation was a no-op, so every command addressed the live shared server, and the final `kill-server` took the captain's session and three other working agents.

## What this adds

A fourth member of the existing PreToolUse guard family, following the established three-part shape rather than inventing a fourth:

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/fm-tmux-command-policy.mjs` | The classifier, sole owner of the decision and its reason codes. Reuses `Lexer`, `splitProgram` and `commandPosition` from `bin/fm-arm-command-policy.mjs`, so it never duplicates shell lexing, and never evaluates, expands, sources or runs any byte of the command. |
| `bin/fm-tmux-pretool-check.sh` | The transport, modelled on `bin/fm-cd-pretool-check.sh` including its fail-open cases and per-harness deny shapes. |
| `docs/tmux-guard.md` | The contract, matching `docs/cd-guard.md`. |

The discriminator is **which tmux server the command addresses**, not the presence of the token `tmux`.
`kill-server`, `kill-session`, `kill-window` and `kill-pane` are denied unless an explicitly named socket (`-L`/`-S`) or a genuinely private `TMUX_TMPDIR` with `$TMUX` unset proves the target is isolated.

## One deliberate divergence from the brief, with evidence

The brief asked to allow "anything under `env -u TMUX`".
**This does not ship that**, because it is not safe, and the measurement is direct:

```
$ env -u TMUX tmux list-sessions
firstmate: 3 windows (created Tue Aug 11 14:08:45 2026) (attached)
```

With `$TMUX` unset, tmux falls back to the **default** socket, which is exactly where the captain's server lives (`$TMUX` reports `/tmp/tmux-1000/default,...`).
`env -u TMUX tmux kill-server` therefore still destroys the shared server.
Accepting it would have left the incident reproducible behind a twelve-character prefix that reads as safe.

`env -u TMUX` is required but not sufficient: a socket must also be named, or `TMUX_TMPDIR` must relocate the default socket into a private directory (which does work, and is allowed).

## The deny message teaches the fix

Every deny names `env -u TMUX tmux -L fm-test-$$ ...`, states that `TMUX_TMPDIR` is ignored while `$TMUX` is set, states that unsetting `$TMUX` alone falls back to the default socket, gives the pre-flight isolation check, and names the scripts that own real teardown.
The test suite pins those contents so the teaching cannot be dropped.

## Who the guard binds, and why the control plane is safe

**It binds everyone** - firstmate's primary session and every crewmate or scout worktree.
This deliberately inverts the cd-guard, which is inert in a linked worktree; here the worker is the threat.

The legitimate control-plane calls (`bin/backends/tmux.sh:137` `kill-window`, `bin/fm-afk-launch.sh:216` `kill-session`) need **no carve-out at all**, because this is a *tool-boundary* check: it only ever sees the command an agent submits to its shell tool, and those calls happen inside script processes that no PreToolUse hook observes.
They are outside the guard's aperture by construction rather than by an exemption that could be spoofed.

This is proven, not assumed: `test_control_plane_kill_still_works` runs both kill shapes against a live private server and asserts they remove their target and only their target, then asserts the tool-boundary commands that drive those scripts (`bin/fm-teardown.sh`, `bin/fm-control.sh`) are allowed.

`kill-session` and `kill-window` are denied even with an explicit target: on the shared server the session hosting an agent's pane **is** the captain's, and a targeted `kill-window` is indistinguishable at classification time from taking a sibling worker's window. A false block costs one retry with `-L`; a false allow costs the fleet.

## Empirical findings that shaped the classifier (tmux 3.7b)

All measured on an isolated server or through a read-only listing:

- **tmux resolves unambiguous command-name prefixes.** `tmux kill-serv` exited 0 and ended the server. `kill-w` and `kill-p` resolve too. `k`, `kill`, `kill-s` are rejected as ambiguous.
- **Every tmux command name beginning with `k` is a kill command** (checked against the full 169-name command and alias list), so treating "is a prefix of a destructive name" as destructive cannot catch a benign command, and over-approximating the ambiguous prefixes costs nothing since tmux rejects them anyway.
- **`killp` and `killw` are real aliases**; `kill-server` and `kill-session` have none.
- **`$TMUX` overrides `TMUX_TMPDIR`** - reproduced read-only, the incident's root cause.

Unlike the cd-guard, malformed syntax **fails closed** when the raw text mentions a tmux kill: a blocked backlog write is a correctness hazard, but a false allow here destroys the fleet.

## Harness coverage

Wired into all five harness hook trees this repo configures, exactly as the cd-guard is:

| Harness | Wiring | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude | `.claude/settings.json` PreToolUse Bash matcher, third check | `test_harness_wiring_present`; plus `tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` proves the entry runs under native Claude and stays inert under Grok |
| Codex | `.codex/hooks.json` PreToolUse, same anchoring/self-verification as the siblings | `test_harness_wiring_present` |
| Grok | `.grok/hooks/fm-tmux-check.json` | `test_harness_wiring_present`, plus `test_grok_hook_variables_carry_defaults` |
| OpenCode | `.opencode/plugins/fm-tmux-check.js` | `test_harness_wiring_present` |
| Pi / pi-signed | `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-turnend-guard.ts` `tool_call` handler | `test_harness_wiring_present` |

All five entry shapes are additionally exercised end to end: every one of the 65 matrix cases runs through Codex-shaped stdin, Claude-shaped stdin, Grok-shaped stdin, OpenCode CLI and Pi CLI.

### Gaps named rather than silently accepted

None is a regression; these are the existing reach of this repo's hook wiring, and they are documented in `docs/tmux-guard.md` "Known residual gaps".

- **`kimi` and `muse` have no PreToolUse hook mechanism configured in this repo at all**, so they carry none of the four guards.
- **A Pi worker loads only the per-task extension `bin/fm-spawn.sh` generates** (`state/<task-id>.pi-ext.ts`), not `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-turnend-guard.ts`, so it currently receives none of the three PreToolUse seatbelts. Pre-existing, and applies equally to the watcher-arm and cd guards.
- **Codex and Grok gate project hooks behind folder trust**, which `fm-spawn` does not establish for a worker pane.
- **Workers on a project clone load that project's config, not firstmate's.** The incident worker was a firstmate-repo worker, which is covered.

Closing the Pi per-task and trust-gated paths means changing `bin/fm-spawn.sh` launch plumbing, which collides with `tmux-endpoint-false-alive` and belongs in follow-up work.

**No live harness run yet.** Cross-harness entry shapes are covered by the portable suite, but no harness has been launched against this guard; `docs/tmux-guard.md` records that honestly and gives the probe pair for when it is run.

## Tests

`tests/fm-tmux-pretool-check.test.sh`, 16 tests, colocated per repo convention.

The incident regression is a **real reproduction**, not a fixture assertion. It stands up a throwaway server on a private socket as a stand-in for the captain's, confirms a pane on it inherits a `$TMUX` pointing at that private socket *before* anything destructive runs (and refuses to proceed otherwise), runs the incident script byte for byte inside that pane, asserts the stand-in server died - proving `TMUX_TMPDIR` was a no-op - then asserts the guard denies the same command text.

The 65-case matrix covers the allowed isolated forms (`-L`, clustered `-L`, `-S`, `env -u TMUX` + `TMUX_TMPDIR` in both word orders), every non-destructive tmux command, and the firstmate teardown scripts, so the guard cannot regress into blanket refusal.

```
tests/fm-tmux-pretool-check.test.sh   exit=0  ok=16  not ok=0
tests/fm-cd-pretool-check.test.sh     exit=0  ok=13  not ok=0
tests/fm-arm-pretool-check.test.sh    exit=0  ok=146 not ok=0
tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh        exit=0  ok=64  not ok=0
bin/fm-lint.sh                        exit=0  (ShellCheck 0.11.0, pinned)
bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh          ok surfaces=68 local_links=236
```

`tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` needed a two-line update: it owns a cross-cutting assertion over every tracked `.claude/settings.json` entry, so the new hook had to join its stub list and its expected guarded count (5 -> 6).

## Scope

`bin/fm-backend.sh`, `bin/backends/tmux.sh` target resolution, and `bin/fm-spawn.sh` endpoint recording are untouched, per the stated boundary. Moving worker windows onto their own socket remains the separate structural half.

title: Hand-rolled Lavish decision boards silently deliver partial answer sets, and tokenized board links expire
body:
## Summary

Firstmate directs agents to use `lavish-axi` for structured decisions, but provides no reliable multi-question decision-board control.

This exposes two user-visible defects:

1. Hand-rolled boards can silently send only individually queued answers, reject custom-text-only responses, and lose unsent drafts when the browser tab closes.
2. Tokenized top-level artifact links expire after another Lavish shell load, token rotation, or server restart. Browser back/forward cache can then falsely make an expired link appear valid during local verification.

Both defects are Firstmate-side workflow and authoring problems. No `lavish-axi` change is required.

## Impact

Reviewers can spend significant time answering a decision round, believe the complete set was submitted, and later discover that only part of it arrived or that the delivered link no longer works.

This is silent decision loss in a sign-off workflow and should be treated as a high-severity reliability defect.

## Reproduction

### Partial submission

1. Create a multi-question board using native required radio groups and per-question queue buttons.
2. Complete every card but queue only one.
3. Press `Send to Agent`.
4. Only the queued card arrives; completed but unqueued answers are omitted without a complete-set warning.
5. A custom-text-only answer can be blocked by unrelated required-radio validation.
6. Closing the tab discards unqueued drafts.

### Expiring delivery link

1. Deliver the tokenized top-level artifact URL containing `artifact_revision` and `artifact_load_token`.
2. Open the Lavish session shell again or restart the server.
3. Open the delivered URL.
4. Lavish returns HTTP 409: `This artifact load is no longer current. Reload Lavish to continue.`
5. History navigation in an already-used browser profile may still render cached board content, masking the broken server-side link.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A complete round submits every expected decision atomically.
- [ ] An incomplete attempt submits nothing and identifies every missing card.
- [ ] Cards support predefined choices, choices with rationale, and custom free text.
- [ ] Drafts survive tab closure and reload.
- [ ] Concurrent views synchronize without stale-view data loss.
- [ ] Confirmed rounds become durably read-only and reject duplicate submission.
- [ ] Supplemental annotations survive reload and accompany the final submission.
- [ ] Successor rounds start without inherited drafts.
- [ ] The delivered board URL survives token rotation and server restart.
- [ ] Delivery verification requires a server-direct HTTP 200 and a fresh-navigation browser network 200; rendered cached content is insufficient.
- [ ] Portable and real-browser regressions cover submission, drafts, synchronization, locking, stable delivery, token rotation, and restart.

## Proposed implementation

A working implementation is ready:

- A validated JSON-to-board generator.
- A tracked browser runtime and stylesheet.
- Whole-set validation with one atomic submission.
- Stable decision keys and exact free-text payloads.
- Draft autosave and cross-view synchronization.
- Durable submitted-state locking.
- A token-free stable board URL derived from Lavish’s artifact asset route.
- Cache-immune verification.
- Portable and opt-in real-browser regression tests.
- A remote-review procedure covering clean round transitions and proactive closeout.

The stable decision surface intentionally does not provide Lavish’s annotation overlay because that SDK is injected only into tokenized artifact loads. The ordinary Lavish session remains available for annotations and conversation.

## Validation

The implementation passes:

- Portable decision-board regression tests.
- Real-browser regression against `lavish-axi` 0.1.46 and 0.1.50.
- Token rotation and full server-restart survival.
- Exact prompt delivery and duplicate-submission prevention.
- Lint and documentation-audience checks.

## Non-goals

- No changes to `lavish-axi`.
- No general-purpose form framework.
- No changes to plain-chat yes/no decisions.

## Delivery plan

Submit a linked PR against `main` through the repository’s required no-mistakes workflow.

title: fix: make Relay replies audience-aware and evidence-backed
body:
## What Changed - Add fail-closed public and private-trusted Relay audiences, persisting the audience across inbox, task-link, reply, and follow-up state while rejecting unsafe transport drift. - Require durable task linkage before publishing work acknowledgements and strengthen Relay guidance around evidence-backed progress, failures, confirmations, and final replies. - Reserve the third follow-up slot for terminal outcomes and expand Relay mode coverage for audience handling, acknowledgement validation, retention recovery, and follow-up enforcement. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The durable audience is now preserved across polling, answer retention, task linking, and follow-ups, with publication guarded at the shared reply boundary and executable behavioral regressions covering the previously reachable disclosure paths. ## Testing Inspected the change intent, ran the targeted Relay behavior suite successfully, and captured an end-user CLI transcript proving that unlinked work acknowledgements and private-to-public transport drift are refused while the reserved terminal follow-up remains deliverable.
Evidence: Relay safety CLI dry-run transcript ```text $ fm-x-reply.sh req-ack --kind work-ack --task-id missing ... fm-x-reply: work-ack refused; task metadata is missing or unsafe: state/missing.meta exit=1; preview_created=no $ fm-x-reply.sh req-ack --kind work-ack --task-id task-ack ... fm-x-reply: DRY RUN - would POST to https://myfirstmate.io/connector/answer (recorded: state/x-outbox/req-ack.json): Work is durably linked and has started. req-ack { "text": "Work is durably linked and has started." } $ fm-x-reply.sh req-private "Private operational detail" (transport drifted to public remote) fm-x-reply: private-trusted reply requires the current validated loopback transport exit=1; preview_created=no $ fm-x-followup.sh task-final - <<< "Third progress update" fm-x-followup: reserved final slot for task-final; use --final or wait for the terminal result exit=1; binding=x_request=req-final; count=x_followups=2 $ fm-x-followup.sh task-final --final - <<< "Terminal result" fm-x-reply: DRY RUN - would POST to https://myfirstmate.io/connector/followup (recorded: state/x-outbox/req-final.json): Terminal result. req-final { "endpoint": "followup", "text": "Terminal result." } binding_after_final=cleared ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
⏭️ **intent** - skipped ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Rebase** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `.agents/skills/fmx-respond/SKILL.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main - ⚠️ `docs/configuration.md` - merge conflict rebasing onto origin/main 🔧 Fix applied. ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed (3) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-x-reply.sh:307` - Enforce the durable `reply_audience` in `fm-x-reply.sh` before preview/network publication. Currently a request stamped `private-trusted` can be polled on loopback, then—after configuration changes—its initial answer is posted to a public remote relay because the resolved audience is ignored. Follow-ups also rely on an earlier wrapper check, leaving a configuration-change race before the subprocess posts. Make this shared publishing boundary reject private-trusted replies unless the current transport is still validated loopback. 🔧 Fix: Enforce durable reply audience at publication boundary 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-x-reply.sh:347` - Do not let `--reply-audience public` downgrade durable private context. A caller can currently invoke `fm-x-reply.sh <private-request> --reply-audience public ...`; line 347 preserves that supplied value instead of the registry/inbox's `private-trusted`, so the publication guard is skipped and private content can reach a public relay. Resolve durable context independently and combine audiences using the strictest ceiling: any durable `private-trusted` value must remain private, while genuinely missing legacy context may default to public. Add an executable regression covering this explicit-downgrade path. 🔧 Fix: Prevent explicit audience downgrade of private replies 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-x-reply.sh:475` - Preserve the resolved audience when retaining context after a successful initial reply. If poll-time registry persistence failed but the stamped inbox still provides `private-trusted`, this call creates a new registry record without an audience, which defaults to `public`; after inbox cleanup, a follow-up resolves as public and can publish through a public relay. Pass the effective `REPLY_AUDIENCE` into `fmx_context_registry_set` and add an executable regression covering poll-registry failure, private initial reply, inbox removal, and public-transport follow-up refusal. 🔧 Fix: Preserve private audience during answer retention ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - Intent inspection with `git diff b5d430d6fdcd961ce9b681bf196f365c1825c284..99ea5f76a718b1d0b771d2938763afece379e4f3 -- bin/fm-x-*.sh docs/configuration.md tests/fm-x-mode.test.sh` - Focused automated behavior suite: `bash tests/fm-x-mode.test.sh` - End-to-end dry-run through `bin/fm-x-link.sh`, `bin/fm-x-reply.sh`, and `bin/fm-x-followup.sh`, capturing acknowledgement linkage, audience drift, and reserved-final behavior
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Lint** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed (3) ✅ - ⚠️ linter found issues (exit code 127) 🔧 Fix: Captain, lint passes with pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ linter found issues (exit code 127) 🔧 Fix: Pass lint with pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ linter found issues (exit code 127) 🔧 Fix: Pass lint with pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0 ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: feat(skills): add /ui-studio skill for fast local UI-iteration lane
body:
## Summary

- Adds `.agents/skills/ui-studio/SKILL.md`: captain-invocable skill (`user-invocable: true`, `metadata.internal: true`) for `start`, `land`, and `status` subcommands. Documents the worktree ownership exception, Herdr pane launch steps, merge-path decision (direct `gh-axi pr merge`, no `fm-pr-merge.sh` since the studio lane has no task meta), and heartbeat land-nudge policy.
- Adds `bin/fm-ui-studio.sh`: shellcheck-clean helper managing the git worktree lifecycle (create/reuse/refuse on un-landed commits), Storybook background launch with URL polling, Vibe annotation server health/start, and the land pipeline (rebase + lint + test + build + push + PR). All output is `KEY=VALUE` on stdout for structured firstmate parsing.
- Adds `tests/fm-ui-studio.test.sh`: 18 behavioral tests covering argument handling, worktree lifecycle, land gate failures, and status state-file reading. Uses real git repos.
- Updates `AGENTS.md` section 6 with one-line trigger alongside `/stow`.

## Design notes

The `fm-pr-merge.sh` merge path requires an existing `state/<id>.meta` file and cannot be used for the studio lane, which deliberately has no firstmate task ID. The land subcommand documents this explicitly and uses `gh-axi pr merge` directly. This is documented in SKILL.md as the chosen approach, not a needs-decision escalation.

## Test plan

- [ ] `bash tests/fm-ui-studio.test.sh` - all 18 tests pass
- [ ] `bash -n bin/fm-ui-studio.sh` - syntax clean
- [ ] Argument handling: no args, unknown subcommand, missing project all exit correctly
- [ ] `status` on a fresh home returns structured output without errors

title: feat(bin): add native Paseo runtime backend and auto-detection
body:
## Intent

Design, implement, test, and document a tracked native Paseo runtime backend (bin/backends/paseo.sh) and auto-detection layer for Firstmate across supported harnesses.

## What Changed

- Implemented `bin/backends/paseo.sh` adapter providing task spawning (`paseo run`), prompt delivery (`paseo send`), log capture (`paseo logs`), and lifecycle state management.
- Integrated Paseo into `bin/fm-backend.sh` and `bin/fm-spawn.sh` with runtime auto-detection (`PASEO_AGENT_ID` / `PASEO_AGENT_CWD`), task endpoint validation, and metadata persistence (`paseo_agent_id`).
- Updated Firstmate CLI utilities, supervisor scripts, documentation, and added unit tests in `tests/fm-backend-paseo.test.sh`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The native Paseo backend integration is clean, well-bounded, and verified with proper worktree base-freshness ordering and error handling.

## Testing

Exercised Paseo backend auto-detection, task creation, Treehouse worktree allocation, GOTMPDIR and TRACEPARENT environment passing, log capture, prompt submission, stop signaling, and agent archiving across 11 test suites and an end-to-end simulation; all checks passed.

title: feat(bin): isolate each launched agent's browser profile and session
body:
## Intent The developer (acting as "firstmate", the captain) tasked the agent with giving firstmate-launched agents an isolated browser profile so a spawned agent could not reach the captain's authenticated browser sessions, prompted by a scout report showing chrome-devtools-axi could read/write arbitrary files and eval JS in a page. They required the agent to first establish the actual connection mechanism by measurement rather than guessing, then follow the existing bin/fm-spawn.sh precedent of scoping env vars to launched agents, and finally prove isolation by attacking it from a real spawned crewmate while confirming legitimate public-page browsing still worked. Hard constraints: do not weaken the captain's own browsing, do not touch ~/.claude/settings.json or anything outside the worktree, do not read the captain's authenticated content while investigating, and report rather than edit if the mechanism lived in personal config. During the /no-mistakes validation the developer made several explicit calls: narrow the docs/configuration.md claim to name only the profile-reaching variables the pin covers and state which CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_ variables are not pinned, rather than pinning the other five (out of scope); instead of adding a version floor to the universal toolchain list, make the isolation detect a missing named-session capability and refuse with an explanation rather than degrade silently, kept proportionate so it never blocks non-browser work; and move the refusal shim into the task's own temp root to remove the cross-agent PATH-shadowing surface by construction. They also resolved two push blockers (routing pushes to their fork, then setting the fork push target on no-mistakes' own gate clone) and repeatedly instructed the agent never to use --yes and to append resolved lines keyed to each decision. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now prepends browser-isolation environment to every launch command, so each agent gets a throwaway Chrome profile and a per-task `chrome-devtools-axi` session instead of the operator's authenticated bridge on the shared `default` port. `bin/fm-pr-lib.sh` owns the three things both sides must agree on: the injective per-task session name (`fm_task_browser_session`), the pinned env list (`fm_browser_isolation_pins`), and a bounded `--help` capability probe (`fm_browser_tool_supports_named_sessions`). - When that probe cannot confirm named sessions, spawn mints a fresh owner-only shim directory under `state/.browser-refusal//` and puts a refusing `chrome-devtools-axi` on that one agent's `PATH` rather than degrading silently; the spawn aborts before side effects if the directory cannot be vouched for, and its own abort path plus `bin/fm-teardown.sh` reclaim it. Teardown also closes each task's bridge by name - including retired secondmate children - gated on the same capability verdict so a stop never lands on the operator's shared bridge. - Adds `tests/fm-spawn-browser-isolation.test.sh` (launch-pin coverage across harness templates, all capability outcomes, shim vouching and reclaim), an opt-in live guard `tests/fm-browser-isolation-live-e2e.test.sh` with a `FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_TIMEOUT` knob, a shared `fm_browser_isolation_launch_prefix` helper in `tests/lib.sh`, new `bin/fm-test-run.sh` family routing for the spawn/pr-lib/timeout-lib paths, and documents the behavior in `docs/configuration.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/scripts.md` and `docs/verification/browser-isolation.md`. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: Both previously reported defects are fixed and my independent sweep found no remaining stale launch-literal assertions, but the branch still changes every spawn and every teardown to shell out to a third-party executable and to prepend an environment block to every launch command, so the residual risk is breadth of blast radius rather than any known defect. ## Testing Ran the browser-isolation and dispatch suites plus every suite touched by the diff (all pass except the four pre-existing host failures already confirmed at the base commit in round 1), then exercised the opt-in live guard twice against a real spawned claude agent: once at a raised timeout, where both stages passed and the agent's shell was proven to inherit the pin and reach only an unauthenticated sign-in page, and once at a deliberately starved 10s timeout, which demonstrates the newly documented FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_TIMEOUT knob binds where the header says it does and fails with the "nothing was verified" message the header warns must not be read as an isolation break. Also captured fresh screenshots of the agent-pinned browser session hitting the Google sign-in form for Gmail and rendering a public page normally, confirming isolation without breaking legitimate browsing. No regressions found; the working tree is clean and no probe processes, lab directories, or browser bridges were left behind.
Evidence: Live guard passes end-to-end against a real spawned claude agent (raised timeout) $ FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE=1 FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_HARNESSES=claude FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_TIMEOUT=600 tests/fm-browser-isolation-live-e2e.test.sh # chrome-devtools-axi 0.1.26 # hostile environment alone selects: -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --autoConnect --chrome-arg=--user-data-dir=/Users/roswell.balentien/.fm-live-guard-never-launched ok - the pinned environment overrides a hostile one and selects an isolated profile (0.1.26) ok - claude: a real agent inherits the pin and reaches only an unauthenticated sign-in page # 2 checks passed exit=0 ```text $ FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE=1 FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_HARNESSES=claude FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_TIMEOUT=600 tests/fm-browser-isolation-live-e2e.test.sh # chrome-devtools-axi 0.1.26 # hostile environment alone selects: -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --autoConnect --chrome-arg=--user-data-dir=/Users/roswell.balentien/.fm-live-guard-never-launched ok - the pinned environment overrides a hostile one and selects an isolated profile (0.1.26) ok - claude: a real agent inherits the pin and reaches only an unauthenticated sign-in page # 2 checks passed exit=0 ```
Evidence: The newly documented timeout knob binds at the value given (starved to 10s) $ FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE=1 FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_HARNESSES=claude FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_TIMEOUT=10 tests/fm-browser-isolation-live-e2e.test.sh # chrome-devtools-axi 0.1.26 ok - the pinned environment overrides a hostile one and selects an isolated profile (0.1.26) not ok - claude: the agent never reported its environment within 10s; the probe could not run, so nothing was verified exit=1 ```text # Demonstrating the knob the header now documents actually bounds stage 2. # Same run, deliberately starved to 10s instead of the documented 300s default: $ FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE=1 FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_HARNESSES=claude FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_TIMEOUT=10 tests/fm-browser-isolation-live-e2e.test.sh # chrome-devtools-axi 0.1.26 # hostile environment alone selects: -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --autoConnect --chrome-arg=--user-data-dir=/Users/roswell.balentien/.fm-live-guard-never-launched ok - the pinned environment overrides a hostile one and selects an isolated profile (0.1.26) not ok - claude: the agent never reported its environment within 10s; the probe could not run, so nothing was verified exit=1 ```
Evidence: Header a maintainer now reads, and the matching default in code ```text Round 2 fix (commit cfcb363): the timeout knob is now visible to a maintainer reading the guard's header - tests/fm-browser-isolation-live-e2e.test.sh:34-44 # # Run with FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE=1. The stage 2 harness probe spends a small # number of model tokens per installed harness; set # FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_HARNESSES to a space-separated subset to narrow it. # FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_TIMEOUT is the number of seconds stage 2 waits for a # probed agent to report back, and defaults to 300. Reach for it when the run is # competing for the machine with other agents or Chrome instances, or on a slow # host - never because a result looks like an isolation failure. Exhausting the # bound means the probe never reported, so nothing was verified either way; it is # not evidence that isolation broke. set -u The documented default is the one the code reads (tests/fm-browser-isolation-live-e2e.test.sh:352): while [ "$waited" -lt "${FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_TIMEOUT:-300}" ]; do Nothing else changed in this commit: cfcb363 no-mistakes(test): document FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_TIMEOUT in live guard header tests/fm-browser-isolation-live-e2e.test.sh | 6 ++++++ 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+) ```
- Evidence: Screenshot: the agent's pinned browser session on mail.google.com lands on the Google sign-in form, not a mailbox (local file: /var/folders/xl/gfd9bj992zj1qjv30f3rdv8w0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZRP8YGHYWPGMRANA2FXWMYZ/round2-isolated-agent-gmail.png) - Evidence: Screenshot: legitimate public browsing still works in the same isolated session (local file: /var/folders/xl/gfd9bj992zj1qjv30f3rdv8w0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZRP8YGHYWPGMRANA2FXWMYZ/round2-isolated-agent-public-page.png)
Evidence: Resolved URL behind the Gmail screenshot (agent-pinned session) pins: CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_AUTO_CONNECT=0 CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_BROWSER_URL= CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_USER_DATA_DIR= CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_CHROME_ARGS= CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_PORT= CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_SESSION=fm-evidence-round2 page: title: Gmail url: "https://mail.google.com" uid=g385:46_0 RootWebArea "Gmail" url="https://accounts.google.com/v3/signin/identifier?...service=mail&flowName=WebLiteSignIn..." ```text page: title: Gmail url: "https://mail.google.com" refs: 107 snapshot: uid=g385:46_0 RootWebArea "Gmail" url="https://accounts.google.com/v3/signin/identifier?continue=https%3A%2F%2Fmail.google.com%2Fmail%2Fu%2F0%2F&dsh=S1578422980%3A1786465990836647&emr=1&followup=https%3A%2F%2Fmail.google.com%2Fmail%2Fu%2F0%2F&osid=1&passive=1209600&service=mail&flowName=WebLiteSignIn&flowEntry=ServiceLogin&ifkv=Ac50bxuzarwvIy2x2TLgW5xZ_2IL0FhOpibfs-EypPc5cSZ9YVeydxxcny6VrT__lVoED4g9PW7mNw" ```
- Outcome: 🔧 2 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ across 2 runs (40m13s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - 🚨 `tests/fm-kimi-harness.test.sh:195` - The exact-equality launch assertions in tests/fm-kimi-harness.test.sh were not updated for the browser-isolation prefix that bin/fm-spawn.sh:1414 now prepends to every launch command. The suite's fake tmux appends the full `send-keys -l` literal to launch.log, so `launch` is now "CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_AUTO_CONNECT=0 CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_BROWSER_URL= CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_USER_DATA_DIR= CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_CHROME_ARGS= CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_PORT= CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_SESSION='fm-<id>' '<fakebin>/kimi' --model 'kimi-code/k3' --auto", which fails `[ "$launch" = "'$FAKEBIN_DIR/kimi' --model 'kimi-code/k3' --auto" ]` at line 195 and the analogous fallback assertion at line 452. fm-kimi-harness.test.sh is in the pure-contract-unit family, which bin/fm-test-run.sh now selects for bin/fm-spawn.sh changes. Fix the same way tests/fm-spawn-browser-isolation.test.sh's sibling suite did: compose the expected string with a browser_isolation_prefix helper (see tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh:151) instead of restating the bare harness invocation. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:1478` - stop_task_browser_bridge is fm-teardown.sh's first caller of fm_run_timed, but the script never sources bin/fm-timeout-lib.sh itself - it gets the function only transitively through the new source line at the top of bin/fm-pr-lib.sh. tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh already had to add a fm-timeout-lib.sh symlink to its fake root to keep the fixture working, which is that hidden dependency surfacing; any future fixture or refactor that provides fm-pr-lib.sh without its sibling, or that drops the source from fm-pr-lib.sh, breaks teardown at runtime rather than at load. Adding an explicit `. "$SCRIPT_DIR/fm-timeout-lib.sh"` beside teardown's other library sources (near line 158) makes the dependency local to the user, matching how bin/fm-bearings-snapshot.sh and bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh declare it. 🔧 Fix: share browser-isolation launch prefix; source timeout lib in teardown 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `tests/lib.sh:197` - fm_browser_isolation_launch_prefix hardcodes the session name as 'fm-$id', which is only the pass-through form of bin/fm-pr-lib.sh's fm_task_browser_session. That function switches to a hashed 64-character form (fm-<first 44 chars>-<16 hex>) for any task id longer than 60 characters. Every current caller uses a short id, so the helper is correct today, but it is now the shared expectation for every suite that pins a whole launch string, and a future case using a long id would get a silently wrong expected value. The failure would at least be loud (the two call sites print expected vs actual), so this is a comment-level gap rather than a defect: the helper's block comment explains why the pin list is restated as a literal but says nothing about the id-length assumption. Adding one sentence naming the <=60-character bound and pointing at fm_task_browser_session would close it without deriving the value from the code under test.
🔧 **Test** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - ℹ️ Four suites fail identically at the base commit 76355e20b4f44d968ca43c14e1bb21c100ac90d7 on this host, so they are pre-existing environment failures rather than regressions from this change: `tests/fm-kimi-harness.test.sh` (the system /usr/bin/python3 has no `tomllib`, so the Kimi hook installer refuses), `tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh` (teardown leaves the tasktmp dir in that fixture), `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` (herdr-preflight-missing-adapter case), and `tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh` ("Orca spawn should fail when metadata cannot be written"). I confirmed this by extracting the base tree with `git archive` and running the same scripts there. Side effect worth knowing: the Kimi suite aborts before reaching this change's new launch-prefix assertions, so that specific assertion was not exercised on this host - the equivalent coverage did run in tests/fm-spawn-browser-isolation.test.sh. - ⚠️ Stage 2 of `tests/fm-browser-isolation-live-e2e.test.sh` (the real-agent probe) timed out once in three runs: "claude: the agent never reported its environment within 300s". That run overlapped with my own concurrent chrome-devtools-axi sessions and Chrome launches on the same machine, and the two runs with nothing else running both passed, so the likely cause is machine contention against the fixed 300s bound rather than a product defect. It is an opt-in manual guard, not a CI lane, but the bound is tight enough on a loaded machine that a maintainer may want FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_TIMEOUT raised or documented as the knob to reach for. Evidence of the timing failure is kept at live-guard-run2-timeout.txt. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-spawn-browser-isolation.test.sh` - 20/20 checks pass (launch-prefix pin on every harness template and the raw escape hatch, per-task session names, all four capability outcomes, shim-directory vouching, pre-abort, and reclaim) - `FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_KEEP=1` re-run to preserve the lab, then captured the real agent's own `env | grep CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI` output and the URL its browser resolved to for https://mail.google.com - Manual lab walkthrough driving the real `bin/fm-spawn.sh` through a fake tmux pane: captured the launch command with a current chrome-devtools-axi (0.1.26), and with a fake tool whose --help omits CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_SESSION - Manual: executed the generated refusal shim as the agent would (`PATH=<minted dir>:$PATH chrome-devtools-axi open https://mail.google.com`) and compared against the same tool on the captain's own PATH - `Manual: ran the teardown-side stop composition (fm_browser_isolation_pins + fm_task_browser_session) with CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_PORT=9224 and SESSION=default exported, logging what the tool was actually asked to stop` - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-backend.test.sh tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh tests/fm-backend-zellij.test.sh` - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh tests/fm-test-fixture-cleanup.test.sh` - all pass - Baseline comparison: `git archive 76355e2 | tar -x -C /tmp/fm-base-check` then re-ran the four failing suites there to confirm they fail identically before the change 🔧 Fix: document FM_BROWSER_ISOLATION_LIVE_TIMEOUT in live guard header ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-spawn-browser-isolation.test.sh tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh tests/fm-browser-isolation-live-e2e.test.sh tests/fm-teardown-endpoint-safety.test.sh` - title: feat(bin): add --driver and --split-gate brief scaffolds for the no-mistakes gate split
body:
## Intent Implement chunk 1 of the approved no-mistakes builder/driver gate split: the brief scaffolds in bin/fm-brief.sh, per the design report at data/nm-builder-driver-design/report.md sections 4.1, 4.2, and 9 and the v1.46.0 delta report at data/nm-split-recheck/report.md. Scope is deliberately limited to chunk 1: no caller changes (fm-spawn.sh and fm-control.sh untouched) and zero behavior change for existing flows - the default no-mistakes scaffold must stay byte-for-byte unchanged when the new flags are absent. Deliverables: (1) a new --driver variant, valid only with --mode no-mistakes, generating data//driver-brief.md per the design section 4.2 outline with the machine-readable contract line 'Delivery contract: mode=no-mistakes phase=driver'; the driver brief is complete as generated (no {TASK} placeholder) and deliberately overwritable/idempotent because firstmate regenerates it at every builder-to-driver flip - an intentional, documented exception to brief.md's no-overwrite rule; (2) a new --split-gate opt-in flag changing only the no-mistakes builder definition of done to: implement, commit, write or append a handoff cycle at data//handoff.md, append 'done: built fm/ at , handoff ready', and stop, with all gate-driving text removed from the builder scaffold; (3) the handoff-file contract (five required sections per cycle: Intent, Change inventory, Verification notes, Review anticipation, Escalation guidance; append-per-cycle, earlier cycles never rewritten; 1-2k token target per cycle) documented in fm-brief.sh's header comment, which owns scaffold contracts; (4) colocated tests in tests/fm-brief.test.sh matching the existing idiom: driver output structure and contract line, --split-gate definition of done, default scaffold free of split text without the flag, deliberate idempotent driver regeneration alongside brief.md's preserved no-overwrite refusal, and a flag-misuse refusal matrix (--driver without --mode no-mistakes or with direct-PR/local-only/--scout/--secondmate/--herdr-lab/--split-gate; --split-gate outside a no-mistakes ship brief). Three v1.46.0 refinements are deliberately folded into the driver scaffold text: the supersession rule mentions the branch_sync.state user_owned no-op case where a repeated --recover is harmless because the run went terminal without changing the submitted head; one rule says that on error.code nested_gate_context the driver stops and reports rather than retrying, since it would mean a wiring bug; and the outcome rule does not restate old checks-passed wording because the daemon alone decides readiness, including the trusted no_ci: true case. Deliberate choices a reviewer reading only the diff might otherwise flag: the driver brief intentionally omits the Herdr section and refuses --herdr-lab because a driver runs gate commands only and never task commands; the driver scaffold forbids ALL driver file edits, a deliberate design-report tightening of the original proposal; the split-gate builder keeps its doctor/init setup step, isolation assertion, rules, and project-memory section unchanged - only the definition of done differs; the scaffolded-output message gains a split-gate-builder marker only under the new flag so default output is untouched. The branch also carries a pipeline document-step commit updating fm-brief.sh's row in docs/scripts.md from the previous run, preserved per the custody-recovery contract. Repo style rules apply: plain dash never em dash, one sentence per line in generated markdown prose, shellcheck-clean under the pinned 0.11.0 via bin/fm-lint.sh, colocated tests extending the existing runner, and the handoff contract documented once in the script header rather than AGENTS.md because the AGENTS.md contract cutover is a later chunk by design. Default outputs were verified byte-for-byte identical against the pre-change script for all three ship modes, scout, herdr-lab, and secondmate scaffolds. Push goes to the configured fork egomez714/firstmate with the PR opened against upstream kunchenguid/firstmate, per the captain's decision. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-brief.sh` gains two opt-in flags, both valid only with `--mode no-mistakes`: `--driver` writes a new gate-driver brief to `data//driver-brief.md` (complete as generated with no `{TASK}` placeholder, carrying the `Delivery contract: mode=no-mistakes phase=driver` line, gate/park/outcome rules, the `user_owned` supersession no-op case, a stop-and-report rule on `error.code: nested_gate_context`, and no Herdr section), and `--split-gate` replaces the no-mistakes builder's definition of done with implement, commit, write or append a handoff cycle at `data//handoff.md`, append `done: built fm/ at , handoff ready`, and stop - leaving that brief's setup, isolation assertion, rules, and project-memory sections untouched. Misuse of either flag (wrong mode, scout, secondmate, `--driver` with `--split-gate` or `--herdr-lab`) refuses with an explanatory error and writes nothing. - `brief.md` keeps its no-overwrite refusal; `driver-brief.md` is deliberately regenerable so firstmate can rewrite it at each builder-to-driver flip. The script header now documents the handoff-file contract (per-cycle Intent, Change inventory, Verification notes, Review anticipation, Escalation guidance; append-only, 1-2k tokens per cycle) and both new flags. Default scaffolds are unchanged when the flags are absent; only `--split-gate` adds a marker to the scaffolded-output message. No callers were touched. - `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` adds four tests in the existing idiom covering driver brief structure and contract line plus idempotent regeneration alongside `brief.md`'s preserved refusal, the `--split-gate` definition of done, absence of split text in the default no-mistakes scaffold, and an 11-row flag-misuse refusal matrix. `docs/scripts.md` updates the `fm-brief.sh` row to mention the split-gate builder and gate-driver variants. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Purely additive opt-in scaffolding behind new flags with loud refusals on misuse, default outputs verified byte-for-byte identical to the base commit for all six scaffold variants, and behavioral colocated tests covering structure, idempotent regeneration, and the full flag-misuse matrix. ## Testing Ran the colocated suite `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-brief.test.sh` (24 tests green, including the four new driver/split-gate tests) plus four adjacent brief and docs contract suites, then went beyond unit coverage to prove the intent directly: I reconstructed the pre-change script from the base commit and diffed its output against the new one across all ten default scaffold cases under an identical FM_HOME, confirming every generated brief is byte-for-byte identical by sha256 and the scaffolded-message stream is unchanged.
