title: fix(bin): pin decision-key placement and quarantine malformed decision keys
body:
## Intent Re-deliver the existing change currently on fork branch fm/fm-1969-reraise through the no-mistakes pipeline using git push no-mistakes so the pipeline itself creates a replacement pull request and writes the deterministic ## Pipeline provenance section. Preserve the settled scope: pin decision-key placement in generated brief scaffolds, add closing-side strictness so a malformed key can never resolve a real decision, and retain the three named tests. Do not hand-write, paste, or reconstruct the ## Pipeline section, its URL line, or any part of it in the pull request body. Do not redesign or widen the change. The fork pull request may park at maintainer workflow approval; action_required with zero checks passed and zero failed is not green, while the PR provenance compliance check must genuinely pass. After the replacement pull request exists with pipeline-written provenance, close pull request #2168 with a one-line comment pointing to the replacement. Never merge a pull request. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-brief.sh`: every generated scaffold (ship, scout, secondmate) now states that a key goes between the verb and the colon, gives the slug grammar (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`), and uses a parseable literal example (`[key=api-shape]`) instead of the placeholder ``; the self-close instruction now spells out both the bare `resolved: {how it cleared}` and keyed `resolved [key=api-shape]: {how it cleared}` forms rather than the ambiguous trailing-key phrasing. - `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh`: `_fm_decision_key` is now total — a slug the grammar rejects is folded into a content-addressed quarantine key (`malformed-key..`) instead of making the caller drop the line, so a malformed escalation stays visible to the AFK-return gate, stays closable by an ordinary `resolved [key=...]` line, and cannot evict the `default` record, a well-formed key, or another distinct malformed key. `FM_OPEN_DECISIONS_FOLD_VERSION` bumped 2 → 4 so cursors persisted under the old semantics are re-folded, with the bump duty documented at the declaration. - Tests: `tests/fm-afk-return.test.sh` adds cases for a malformed blocker key staying visible/closable and for slugs that collide after sanitization keeping separate records; `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` asserts the new scaffold wording and runs every keyed example the briefs hand out through the real parser and open-decision fold; `tests/fm-wake-drain-open-decisions-cursor.test.sh` and `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` cover foreign fold versions and malformed-key triage. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The core fix is correct and behaviorally proven - quarantine keys are injective, bounded, legal under every closing consumer's slug grammar, and cannot close a real decision - but the change alters shared open-decision fold semantics that four consumers depend on (fm-afk-return, fm-wake-drain, fm-decision-hold, fm-fleet-snapshot) while only two have behavioral coverage, so it is safe to merge with the noted consumer blast radius tracked as follow-up. ## Testing Ran the four test scripts touched by this change (fm-brief, fm-afk-return, fm-watch-triage, fm-wake-drain-open-decisions-cursor) — all pass, including the three named new tests and the fold-version guard; fm-watch-triage is slow (~31 min) but clean. Because passing tests alone do not show the operator-visible behavior, I also produced two CLI transcripts against the real scripts: a before/after `bin/fm-afk-return.sh` run showing that a worker's malformed-key blocker was previously invisible to the return gate and is now presented under a legal content-addressed quarantine key that an ordinary `resolved [key=...]` line closes without evicting the well-formed blocker; and a rendered-brief transcript showing the pinned `[key=api-shape]` placement in all three scaffolds, with those exact example lines round-tripping through the real parser and fold, plus proof that malformed closing keys resolve nothing real and that the historical trailing-key incident line still reads as `default`. No UI surface is involved (bash CLI and generated markdown briefs only), so the evidence is command transcripts and rendered brief excerpts. Scratch directories were removed and the worktree is clean; PR creation and the pipeline-written provenance section belong to other phases and were not exercised here.
Evidence: AFK-return gate: malformed decision key before vs after BEFORE (base 76355e2): $ bin/fm-afk-return.sh begin firstmate-actionable blocker: repair-task [key=vendor-release] synthetic vendor window is closed !!! the malformed-key blocker never reached the return gate AFTER (015eed6): $ bin/fm-afk-return.sh begin firstmate-actionable blocker: repair-task [key=vendor-release] synthetic vendor window is closed firstmate-actionable blocker: repair-task [key=malformed-key.api-shape.76a95cf3] firstmate must pick the synthetic API shape before work resumes $ echo 'resolved [key=malformed-key.api-shape.76a95cf3]: chose the synthetic API shape' >> repair-task.status remaining blocker records: key=vendor-release ```text ============================================================== BEFORE (base 76355e2): malformed decision key ============================================================== --- worker's durable status file (what the stopped worker wrote) --- blocked [key=vendor-release]: synthetic vendor window is closed blocked [key=api shape]: firstmate must pick the synthetic API shape before work resumes --- $ bin/fm-afk-return.sh begin (what the human sees on return) --- fm-afk-return: catch-up must finish before the captain request firstmate-actionable blocker: repair-task [key=vendor-release] synthetic vendor window is closed fm-afk-return: handle each blocker now, or close it with resolved [key=...] and append a durable reclassification reason, then run bin/fm-afk-return.sh check [exit 3] --- recorded return-gate blocker records --- key=vendor-release note=synthetic vendor window is closed !!! the malformed-key blocker never reached the return gate: the stopped !!! worker's escalation is invisible and there is nothing to close. ============================================================== AFTER (015eed6): malformed decision key quarantined ============================================================== --- worker's durable status file (what the stopped worker wrote) --- blocked [key=vendor-release]: synthetic vendor window is closed blocked [key=api shape]: firstmate must pick the synthetic API shape before work resumes --- $ bin/fm-afk-return.sh begin (what the human sees on return) --- fm-afk-return: catch-up must finish before the captain request firstmate-actionable blocker: repair-task [key=vendor-release] synthetic vendor window is closed firstmate-actionable blocker: repair-task [key=malformed-key.api-shape.76a95cf3] firstmate must pick the synthetic API shape before work resumes fm-afk-return: handle each blocker now, or close it with resolved [key=...] and append a durable reclassification reason, then run bin/fm-afk-return.sh check [exit 3] --- recorded return-gate blocker records --- key=vendor-release note=synthetic vendor window is closed key=malformed-key.api-shape.76a95cf3 note=firstmate must pick the synthetic API shape before work resumes --- human closes the quarantined record by hand --- $ echo 'resolved [key=malformed-key.api-shape.76a95cf3]: chose the synthetic API shape' >> repair-task.status remaining blocker records: key=vendor-release ```

Firstmate will apply the configured authority and reply with the decision. 40: When you use a key, put it between the verb and the colon, as in `blocked [key=api-shape]: {why}`; never put it after the note. 43: Firstmate's reply normally writes that closing line at answer time; when a blocker or wait clears WITHOUT a firstmate reply, append the closing line yourself as you resume: `resolved: {how it cleared}`, or `resolved [key=api-shape]: {how it cleared}` if you opened it with a key. --- scout brief: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZR5Z7GTG0MPQCNYDZGE6SK8/.scratch-brief.T3cI/data/demo-scout/brief.md --- 32:6. If a decision belongs to a human (product choices, destructive actions), append `needs-decision [key=api-shape]: {summary of options}` and stop. Firstmate will reply with the decision. 33: When you use a key, put it between the verb and the colon, as in `blocked [key=api-shape]: {why}`; never put it after the note. 36: Firstmate's reply normally writes that closing line at answer time; when a blocker or wait clears WITHOUT a firstmate reply, append the closing line yourself as you resume: `resolved: {how it cleared}`, or `resolved [key=api-shape]: {how it cleared}` if you opened it with a key. --- secondmate brief: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZR5Z7GTG0MPQCNYDZGE6SK8/.scratch-brief.T3cI/data/demo-second/brief.md --- 44:When you use a key, put it between the verb and the colon, as in `blocked [key=api-shape]: {why}`; never put it after the note. 46:For a decision on that phase, append `needs-decision [key=api-shape]: {summary}`. 47:If its first reportable event is `working [key=api-shape]: {material phase}`, use the same key on its later `paused`, `done`, `failed`, `needs-decision`, or `blocked` event so the earlier working phase is superseded. 48:When a keyed phase ends without another reportable state, append `resolved [key=api-shape]: {why it is no longer active}`. 50:The main firstmate's answer normally writes that closing line at answer time; when a blocker or wait clears WITHOUT an answer from the main firstmate, append the closing line yourself as your domain resumes: `resolved: {how it cleared}`, or `resolved [key=api-shape]: {how it cleared}` if you opened it with a key. ============================================================== 2. A worker copies the brief's examples verbatim ============================================================== --- BEFORE this change the brief taught `[key=]` / `[key=]` --- (angle brackets are illegal in the slug grammar). Copied verbatim: needs-decision [key=]: pick the API shape status_open_decisions -> malformed-key.-work-slug-.0a142b21 needs-decision pick the API shape (quarantined under a legal, human-closable key instead of vanishing) --- AFTER: the brief's own example, copied verbatim --- needs-decision [key=api-shape]: pick the API shape status_open_decisions -> api-shape needs-decision pick the API shape --- and the brief's own self-close example closes it --- needs-decision [key=api-shape]: pick the API shape resolved [key=api-shape]: captain chose B status_open_decisions -> '' (empty = closed) ============================================================== 3. Closing-side strictness: a malformed key resolves nothing real ============================================================== needs-decision: which DB? needs-decision [key=q2]: real choice resolved [key=bad key]: typo resolved [key=]: copied placeholder status_open_decisions -> default needs-decision which DB? q2 needs-decision real choice (both real decisions still open: each malformed close names only its own quarantine key, so it can never resolve a real decision) ============================================================== 4. The real 2026 incident line: trailing key after the note ============================================================== blocked: report complete; decision-hold gate needs tasks-axi>=0.2.4 [key=decision-hold-gate] status_open_decisions -> default blocked report complete; decision-hold gate needs tasks-axi>=0.2.4 [key=decision-hold-gate] (key=default: a trailing token is note prose, never a key - which is exactly why the brief now pins placement between verb and colon) ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 3 infos - ⚠️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:334` - Rule 6 in every scaffold changed from a bare `needs-decision: {summary}` to an always-keyed `needs-decision [key=api-shape]: {summary}`, so every worker escalation now flows through slug parsing. On the OPENING side a malformed slug is still dropped outright: `_fm_decision_key` returns 1 and `_fm_decision_fold_line` (bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:260) discards the line. Concrete path: worker appends `needs-decision [key=api shape]: drop the users column?` (space, `/`, `#`, or angle brackets all do it) -> the record never enters the open set -> `print_open_decisions_section` (bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:67) omits it and `scan_open_blockers` (bin/fm-afk-return.sh:72) reports no blocker, so the AFK-return gate passes while the worker is stopped waiting. Only the live watcher still sees the raw line (`status_line_verb` strips the token before matching), so the durable ledger is where it is lost. This is strictly better than the pre-change `<work-slug>` placeholder (guaranteed malformed if copied), and the intent authorizes closing-side strictness only, so this is a residual gap rather than a regression - but the earliest shared boundary that would close it is `_fm_decision_fold_line`: fold an unparseable key on `needs-decision`/`blocked` into the `default` record instead of dropping the line, while keeping the malformed-close strictness on `resolved`/`captain-held` exactly as it is (this is what commit dde1ed5 did before ce7b310 scoped it back). Confirm the prose-only pinning is the intended stopping point. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:246` - The example slug is now a literal (`api-shape`) rather than an obvious placeholder, so a worker that copies it verbatim produces a parseable key. Tradeoff: two concurrent decisions in one task both keyed `api-shape` collide - `_fm_decision_drop` in `_fm_decision_fold_line` evicts the first record, so the earlier summary disappears from the open set. The two "Use your own slug in place of that example" lines are the only guard. Noted as the deliberate tradeoff behind commit e5cdba1; a literal that reads less copyable (e.g. `your-slug-here`) would still parse while discouraging reuse. - ℹ️ `.agents/skills/afk/SKILL.md:64` - Sibling agent-facing artifact outside the pinned scaffolds still hands out `resolved [key=...]`. `...` is a *valid* slug under the `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` grammar, so a verbatim copy parses and resolves a key nothing ever opened - it looks like a successful close but drops nothing. It fails safe (the blocker stays open and `fm-afk-return.sh check` keeps failing loudly, and firstmate's real path goes through `fm-send --resolve-key`, which validates writer-side), so no action here; flagged only because the intent forbids widening this change. 🔧 Fix: quarantine malformed decision keys instead of dropping them 3 issues (1 warning, 2 infos) still open: - ⚠️ `tests/fm-brief.test.sh:766` - `test_brief_key_examples_parse_through_the_real_fold` is now vacuous: commit fa7ef1a made `_fm_decision_key` never return nonzero and never return `default` for a `[key=...]` token, so the guard it was added as (4403e4e) can no longer fail. Concrete: revert bin/fm-brief.sh to the pre-change `needs-decision [key=<work-slug>]: {summary}` placeholder - the exact defect 1ef0b96 fixes - and the test still passes. `_fm_decision_key` returns `malformed-key.-work-slug-`, so the `|| fail` at line 766 is dead code, `[ "$key" != default ]` at 768 passes, the `needs-decision|blocked` branch finds `malformed-key.-work-slug-\tneeds-decision\t` in `status_open_decisions` output, and the `resolved` branch seeds its own `needs-decision [key=$key]` line from the same derived key so closure always matches. Only the separate literal `assert_grep 'needs-decision [key=api-shape]:'` in `test_pause_verb_override_renders_all_brief_scaffolds` would still catch it, and that is a source-content grep, not the semantic guard. Fix: after `key=$(_fm_decision_key "$line")`, fail when the derived key begins with `$FM_DECISION_MALFORMED_KEY_PREFIX` (that is exactly "the brief handed out a slug the parser rejects" under the new fold). - ℹ️ `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:210` - Quarantine key derivation is many-to-one, so two malformed escalations can still evict each other. `k=${k//[!A-Za-z0-9._-]/-}` followed by truncation to 40 bytes maps distinct slugs onto one record: `needs-decision [key=api shape]: X` then `needs-decision [key=api/shape]: Y` both derive `malformed-key.api-shape`, and `_fm_decision_drop` in the needs-decision branch evicts X so only Y survives in the open set (same for two malformed slugs sharing the first 40 sanitized bytes). Also, `malformed-key.` is itself a legal slug, so the header comment's claim that a malformed line "never overwrites the `default` record or any well-formed key" is unenforced - a writer choosing the literal key `malformed-key.api-shape` collides with the quarantine record. Both are strictly better than the base behavior (which dropped every malformed line outright), and the authorized properties hold for the single-malformed-key case, so no action; flagged because the header states the stronger invariant as fact. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:570` - The same `|| continue` removal was applied to `_fm_status_open_activities_stream`, widening the parent-activity fold too - the authorized widening was about the open-decision/AFK-return path. Reachable consequence: a worker writes `working [key=api shape]: doing X` (typo) and later the corrected `done [key=api-shape]: finished`; the phase opened under `malformed-key.api-shape` is never closed by the `api-shape` terminal line, so bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:956 reports an ended phase as still open indefinitely. Bounded: that function's own header states the fold is supersession evidence only, never authoritative crew state, and output is capped by FM_SNAPSHOT_PARENT_ACTIVITIES. The symmetric case (a malformed-keyed `working` with no terminal line) is more correct than before, so this is a tradeoff note rather than a defect. 🔧 Fix: brief key-example guard rejects quarantined slugs 3 issues (1 warning, 2 infos) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:210` - Quarantine key derivation is many-to-one, so the authorized property "no eviction of a real decision" is not established. `k=${k//[!A-Za-z0-9._-]/-}` then `${k:0:40}` maps distinct malformed slugs onto one record. Verified against the real fold: a status file containing `needs-decision [key=api shape]: drop users column?` followed by `needs-decision [key=api/shape]: rename orders table?` yields exactly one row, `malformed-key.api-shape\tneeds-decision\trename orders table?` - the `_fm_decision_drop` in the needs-decision branch evicted the first worker's escalation, and that worker is stopped waiting on it. Same collision for any two slugs sharing the first 40 sanitized bytes, and for non-ASCII keys, which collapse to punctuation (`[key=ünïcødé]` -> `malformed-key.-n-c-d-`). The mirror of this also weakens the closing-side strictness the intent requires: `resolved [key=api/shape]` closes the quarantined record opened by `[key=api shape]`, a real decision it does not name. The header at lines 177-180 states the invariant more narrowly ("never overwrites the `default` record or any well-formed key"), which is true, but it is not the property the widening was authorized against - and `malformed-key.` is itself a legal slug, so a writer choosing `[key=malformed-key.api-shape]` collides too. This is still strictly better than the base behavior (which dropped every malformed line), so it is not a regression; but the round-1 authorization said to stop and report if all three properties cannot hold simultaneously. Collision-free derivation that keeps all three: append a short checksum of the RAW key bytes to the sanitized stem (e.g. `malformed-key.<sanitized-stem>.<8 hex>`), so identical raw keys still fold onto one record - which is correct - while distinct ones never merge; the result stays bounded in charset and length and remains a legal, hand-closable slug. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:570` - The same `|| continue` removal was applied to `_fm_status_open_activities_stream`, which is outside the authorized widening (the round-1 instruction scoped it to open decisions and the bin/fm-afk-return.sh consumer). Reachable consequence: `working [key=api shape]: starting` opens a phase under `malformed-key.api-shape` that the later, corrected `done [key=api-shape]: finished` never closes, so bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:956 reports an ended parent phase as still open. Bounded and self-limiting - that fold's own header states it is supersession evidence only, never authoritative crew state, and the snapshot keeps only the last FM_SNAPSHOT_PARENT_ACTIVITY records, so an old phantom is the first thing dropped. Noted because the symmetric case (a malformed `working` with no terminal line) is genuinely more correct than before; flagged only as scope. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-brief.test.sh:669` - The five prose assertions added to `test_pause_verb_override_renders_all_brief_scaffolds` are substring greps over the rendered brief - permitted, since the brief is the generated prompt artifact - but four of them are now redundant with `test_brief_key_examples_parse_through_the_real_fold`, which proves the same contract by executing each rendered example through the real parser and fold. Only the `assert_no_grep 'resolved: {how it cleared}` yourself (same `[key=<slug>]`'` guard at line 682 adds unique regression value (it matches the exact removed wording, confirmed with grep -F). The semantic guard also does not check that the `needs-decision` and `resolved` examples share a slug, so cross-example key drift would pass both tests; adding that one comparison would be worth more than the four prose greps. 🔧 Fix: content-address quarantined decision keys so collisions cannot evict 3 infos still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:220` - `sum=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | LC_ALL=C cksum 2>/dev/null) || sum=''` followed by the `''|*[!0-9]*) sum=0` guard means any cksum failure degrades silently to a constant checksum: every malformed slug then derives `malformed-key.<stem>.00000000`, `api shape` and `api/shape` collide again, and the eviction this round was authorized to remove returns with no signal. The repo already hard-depends on coreutils elsewhere in this same file (`stat`, `wc`, `tail`), so this is practically unreachable rather than a live defect - noted because the fallback quietly voids the one property the derivation exists to guarantee, and a pure-bash byte accumulator over `$raw` would keep it under any environment. Related: the header at lines 176-190 states two absolutes the code does not enforce - `cksum` is 32-bit so distinct slugs can collide (birthday ~65k distinct malformed slugs on one task), and `malformed-key.` is itself a legal slug, so a writer choosing `[key=malformed-key.api-shape.76a95cf3]` lands on the quarantine record directly. Both are acceptable engineering; the comment just reads as a proof rather than a practical bound. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:234` - Making malformed opening keys visible reaches a consumer outside the two the widening was scoped and tested against (bin/fm-afk-return.sh, bin/fm-wake-drain.sh): bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:333 and :382 hard-fail with "open structured decision <origin>/<key> has no captain-held inventory entry" for any key `status_open_decisions` reports. A single typo'd `needs-decision [key=api shape]:` on a live (non-terminal, or secondmate) task therefore now fails `fm-decision-hold.sh complete` and `verify` until the operator either closes it with `resolved [key=malformed-key.api-shape.76a95cf3]` or opens a durable backlog item for that key via `hold --title/--reason`. Both escapes work because the quarantine key passes `validate_slug` (bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:84), and the key is printed verbatim by fm-afk-return.sh:119, so nothing is unrecoverable - this is the intended "stop hiding the escalation" semantics landing in a second gate. Flagged only so the blast radius is on record; no test covers this consumer. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:190` - Intent conformance note, reconciled rather than raised as a contradiction. The intent states "Preserve the settled scope" and "Do not redesign or widen the change", and the shipped change does widen it: `_fm_decision_key` no longer fails, `_fm_decision_fold_line` and `_fm_status_open_activities_stream` lost their `|| continue`/`|| return` drop, a quarantine namespace was added, and the fold version went 2 -> 4 instead of 2 -> 3. That widening was explicitly directed by the author in this same run (round 1: "WIDEN NOW", round 3: "Make quarantine key derivation injective"), which supersedes the pre-run scope text, so it is not an unauthorized deviation. The originally named cursor test was also renamed `test_fold_version_2_cursor_is_never_trusted` -> `test_cursor_from_a_foreign_fold_version_is_never_trusted` and now writes `version=0`; the three required coverage items (trailing-key incident line, correctly placed keys, fold-version bump) are all retained, and the rename makes that test survive future version bumps. Raised so the PR body's "settled scope" framing is not taken at face value.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-brief.test.sh` (includes the new `test_brief_key_examples_parse_through_the_real_fold`) - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-afk-return.test.sh` (includes `test_malformed_blocker_key_stays_visible_and_closable` and `test_colliding_malformed_blocker_keys_stay_distinct`) - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` (classifier primitives: trailing-key incident line, malformed closing keys) - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-wake-drain-open-decisions-cursor.test.sh` (new `test_cursor_from_a_foreign_fold_version_is_never_trusted`, guarding the FM_OPEN_DECISIONS_FOLD_VERSION 2->4 bump) - Manual before/after run of `bin/fm-afk-return.sh begin` / `check` against the base (76355e2) and target (015eed6) `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh`, with a worker status file containing `blocked [key=vendor-release]:` plus `blocked [key=api shape]:` - Manual render of ship, scout, and secondmate briefs via `bin/fm-brief.sh`, then feeding each rendered `[key=...]` example line through `status_line_verb` / `_fm_decision_key` / `status_open_decisions` from `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh` - Manual closing-side strictness check: `resolved [key=bad key]` and `resolved [key=<slug>]` against an open `default` and `q2` decision - Manual replay of the real trailing-key incident line `blocked: ... [key=decision-hold-gate]` through `status_open_decisions`
⚠️ **Document** - 1 info - ℹ️ `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:920` - bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:920 still guards `key=$(_fm_decision_key "$escalation") || key=''`. That failure branch is now unreachable — _fm_decision_key returns a quarantine key instead of `return 1` for a malformed slug. title: Telemetry daemon stops publishing forever if the mqttpub child dies
body:
Found by review during https://github.com/gilvent/windiag-ai/issues/21 (branch fm/po-descriptor) and deliberately left out of that ticket's scope, because it predates it and fixing it means changing publish and respawn semantics that ticket does not otherwise touch.

## The defect

When the `mqttpub` child process dies, the telemetry daemon does not notice, does not respawn it, and does not crash. It carries on sampling and writing into a pipe nobody is reading, so the node goes permanently silent with no error anywhere.

The daemon has what looks like a respawn path, but it cannot fire: it keys off `publisher.write()` returning null, and a write into the popen buffer still returns a byte count once the reader is gone. Review verified this by running the real daemon in the project image with a publisher shim that exits after one line - `spawn_publisher()` was never called again. That inert branch and its misleading header comment are being removed on fm/po-descriptor, with a pointer to this issue, so the code no longer claims a recovery it does not perform.

## Why it matters more now

Spec https://github.com/gilvent/windiag-ai/issues/16 makes push the only way collection data reaches the platform. Before that, a silently dead publisher still left the on-demand HTTP path working. After it, a board in this state contributes nothing at all, and the platform's only clue is that the node's data simply stops - while its retained status still says it is online, because the daemon process is alive and its last will never fires.

## Scope

Detect a failed or dead publisher and recover from it. Two things to settle while doing so:

- How death is detected. The write-return check does not work; something like reaping the child, checking its liveness before or after a write, or handling the signal is needed instead.
- What happens on repeated failure, so a board that cannot spawn a publisher does not sit in a tight respawn loop.

Worth checking in the same pass whether liveness should reflect a dead publisher at all, since a node whose daemon is running but whose publisher is gone currently reports itself online and healthy.

title: feat: add deterministic condition-to-action watcher
body:
## Intent Build a new firstmate primitive: a condition->action watcher, so firstmate can set up 'do X as soon as Y is true' once and have it run almost tokenlessly, instead of the captain or firstmate repeatedly polling 'are we ready yet?'. When the condition trips, a DETERMINISTIC action fires without waking firstmate, and firstmate is woken exactly once at the end with the captured outcome. Required by the captain: build ON the existing watcher/check infrastructure rather than inventing a parallel system - after inventorying the custom check.sh registration/trust binding, the watcher poll loop, procevent, fm-check-register, and fm-pr-check merge-poll arming, the chosen integration is a new 'when' adapter on the existing process-to-event channel (bin/fm-procevent-when.sh), because procevent already owns durable capture, restart-on-death, wake publication, and adapter-owned terminal retirement, and needs zero changes to fm-watch.sh; the check.sh channel was deliberately rejected for the action half because FM_CHECK_TIMEOUT=30s would kill a long action mid-run. Hard design boundary from firstmate's VISION: scripts own exact mechanics, agents own judgment - the primitive is ONLY for cases where BOTH condition AND action are genuinely exact/deterministic; the existing check-fires-then-wake-firstmate-and-decide flow stays available and unchanged for judgment-needing actions, and the eligibility judgment is deliberately documented as firstmate's pre-arm decision (in the process-event-sources skill) because scripts cannot classify an argv as destructive; the primitive must NEVER be used for destructive, irreversible, or security-sensitive actions. Mandatory fail-safe semantics, all implemented and tested: fail safe (action error, ambiguous/flaky condition past an error budget, expired deadline, and mutated spec all wake firstmate with a terminal captured outcome rather than silently proceeding or retrying); robust condition (fires only on a configurable count of consecutive true polls, condition exit 0=true 1=clean-false other=error, so a flapping one-shot true never fires); idempotent single-fire (a durable O_EXCL fired marker is claimed BEFORE the action so a restart or re-poll reports 'ambiguous' instead of double-firing); the action's bytes are trust-bound at registration the same way fm-check-register.sh binds a custom check (spec + sha256 trust record under state/when/, refused without execution on mismatch); the end-of-run wake carries the action's captured outcome (status, exit code, bounded output) via the procevent durable result. The motivating acceptance scenario is 'run no-mistakes update --beta once no validation runs are active' but the primitive is general (any exact condition + any registered deterministic action), not hardcoded to no-mistakes. This changes firstmate's shared tracked material, so the firstmate-coding-guidelines were followed: mechanics live in the script header + --help, the operating contract in docs/configuration.md's procevent section (single owner), arming/handling/eligibility in the process-event-sources skill, only one-line pointers in AGENTS.md (state layout line + section 13 trigger extension), one-sentence-per-line Markdown, plain dashes, shellcheck-clean bin script via bin/fm-lint.sh, and behavioral tests in tests/fm-procevent-when.test.sh that exercise the public adapter + generic runner interface with real processes (never asserting implementation-source bytes): 8 scenarios covering arm/refuse-duplicate/retire, exactly-once fire with outcome wake on the durable queue, flapping condition never firing, action failure captured, condition error budget, expired deadline, crash-restart ambiguity instead of double-fire, and mutated-spec trust refusal. No harness-dependent checks are involved, so no live-harness dual test is needed. Docs rows added to docs/scripts.md and the FM_WHEN_OUTPUT_TAIL_BYTES env var documented in docs/configuration.md. ## What Changed - Add a process-event `when` adapter that polls for consecutive true conditions and runs a registered action at most once. - Trust-bind watch specifications and action bytes, with terminal outcomes for failures, deadlines, tampering, and ambiguous interrupted runs. - Document the safety contract and add behavioral coverage for arming, firing, retirement, output capture, timeouts, and fail-safe paths. ## Risk Assessment 🚨 High: Two mandatory trust-binding fail-safe guarantees remain concretely bypassable and require explicit resolution before merge. ## Testing After inspecting the change, the focused behavioral suite passed, including action-byte mutation refusal; a manual end-to-end CLI run also demonstrated one action invocation, one durable wake, captured successful output, and terminal retirement.
Evidence: End-to-end condition-to-action watcher transcript ```text $ fm-procevent-when.sh arm beta-update --interval 0.1 --stable 2 --condition condition.sh ready --action action.sh invocations.log armed: when-beta-update starts on the watcher's next cycle; or run: bin/fm-procevent.sh reconcile reminder: deterministic, safe, reversible actions only; judgment and destructive actions stay on the wake-and-decide path $ fm-procevent.sh reconcile reconciled: published=0 started=1 stopped=0 uncertain=0 $ touch ready # condition becomes true $ cat captured-result when: when-beta-update status: fired detail: the condition held and the action exited 0 condition_polls: 3 action_exit: 0 output: beta update completed deterministically $ cat invocations.log invoked $ wc -l invocations.log state/.wake-queue 1 /var/folders/0k/bf8mwt2n5qddzk24r20gfk0c0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZS7F8KPPV6FK4R4X11F8MHD/end-to-end-demo/invocations.log 1 /var/folders/0k/bf8mwt2n5qddzk24r20gfk0c0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZS7F8KPPV6FK4R4X11F8MHD/end-to-end-demo/home/state/.wake-queue 2 total $ awk -F "\\t" "{print \\$5}" state/.wake-queue check: procevent when when-beta-update 1 $ test ! -e state/procevent/when-beta-update.source && echo retired-after-terminal-outcome retired-after-terminal-outcome ```
Evidence: Durably captured watcher outcome ```text when: when-beta-update status: fired detail: the condition held and the action exited 0 condition_polls: 3 action_exit: 0 output: beta update completed deterministically ```
- Outcome: 🔧 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ across 2 runs (5m57s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 2 errors - 🚨 `bin/fm-procevent-when.sh:187` - Intent requires “the action's bytes [to be] trust-bound at registration,” but the trust hash covers only the serialized argv/spec. Replacing the executable or script at the unchanged action path after arming leaves the spec hash valid, and line 382 executes the replacement. Confirm the intended trust boundary and bind/validate the action artifact at registration and immediately before invocation if executable bytes are required. - 🚨 `bin/fm-procevent-when.sh:297` - The Perl timeout fallback kills only the direct child PID. A condition or action wrapper that spawns a descendant can time out while that descendant continues running, so an action-failed outcome may be captured before the action's effects finish. Use the existing bin/fm-timeout-lib.sh shared boundary, which isolates and terminates the whole process group. - 🚨 `bin/fm-procevent-when.sh:355` - The deadline is checked only before starting a condition poll. A poll begun just before expiry can complete true after the deadline and immediately break toward the action, violating the required fail-safe expired-deadline behavior. Recheck the deadline after each poll and immediately before claiming the fired marker. - 🚨 `bin/fm-procevent-when.sh:156` - Duplicate refusal is a check-then-publish sequence with no shared lock. Two concurrent arms for the same name can both pass the absence check, overwrite each other's spec/trust/registration, and both report success instead of refusing one registration. Serialize the adapter's absence check through completed process-event registration at one per-source boundary. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-procevent-when.sh:348` - Condition and action output is written without a size limit to the temporary run file; FM_WHEN_OUTPUT_TAIL_BYTES is applied only after the command exits. A verbose command can therefore consume arbitrary disk space during its timeout. Capture through a rolling bounded tail and validate the configured byte limit before execution. 🔧 Fix: Harden when watcher concurrency, deadlines, timeouts, and output 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-procevent-when.sh:191` - Required intent says “the action's bytes are trust-bound at registration,” but the hash covers only the spec containing argv. Replacing the executable or script at the same action path after arming leaves the hash valid, and line 401 executes the replacement. Bind the authorized action artifact's hash at registration and validate it immediately before invocation, or confirm a different intended trust boundary. - 🚨 `bin/fm-procevent-when.sh:327` - Required intent says a “mutated spec” must wake with a terminal outcome rather than proceed, but the spec is validated only once when the long-running process starts. After the first false poll, mutating the on-disk spec and then making the condition true still executes the previously loaded action. Revalidate the trust binding before each poll and immediately before claiming the fired marker.

End-to-end verification armed a watch, replaced the action script after registration, and observed the mutated script execute with a durable `status: fired` outcome. This violates the required check-style byte trust binding. body:

## Interface verification (against installed `atelier-axi` 0.3.3)

- `poll <html-file> [--agent-reply "..."] [--full]` — the `--full` flag is additive and unused by the adapter; the wrapped shape is unchanged from the predecessor.
- `setup hooks` exists → install command keeps `&& $1 setup hooks`.
- Missing-session output: `error: No active Atelier Editor session for this file` / `code: NOT_FOUND`; the `session:`/error envelope the adapter parses is unchanged.

## Testing

- `bin/fm-lint.sh` (pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0): pass.

title: fix(bin): honor decision keys after the verb colon
body:
## Intent Fix firstmate GitHub issue #2109: status decision keys silently collapse to 'default' when the [key=X] token follows the verb colon. The open-decisions key parser in bin/fm-classify-lib.sh (status_open_decisions and its incremental cursor-backed variant status_open_decisions_incremental) only recognized a key in the documented position 'needs-decision [key=X]: ...' (token before the verb colon). A worker writing 'needs-decision: [key=X] ...' (token after the colon) had its stated key silently parsed as 'default' - a shared bucket - so two open decisions on one task collapsed into one record, an answer could close the wrong record, and bin/fm-send.sh --resolve-key X refused with 'no open decision or blocker with that key'. Observed live on independent claude and codex tasks, so the misplaced-colon shape is common worker output. Chosen behavior, per the issue's stated preference: accept ': [key=]' as an EQUIVALENT form - extract the stated key correctly regardless of its position relative to the verb colon (silently rewriting a stated key to 'default' is the unsafe option and must end). Requirements carried from the task: (1) both status_open_decisions AND status_open_decisions_incremental must agree - the fix goes through the shared single-owner key extractor (_fm_decision_key) feeding the one fold rule (_fm_decision_fold_line) so the incremental cursor path cannot diverge from the full fold, and FM_OPEN_DECISIONS_FOLD_VERSION is bumped (2->3) so persisted cursors folded under the old interpretation are discarded and rebuilt from byte 0 as that constant's contract requires; (2) the same position-robust extraction applies symmetrically to 'resolved [key=X]:' / 'blocked [key=X]:' (and captain-held and the activities fold) so an answer closes the right record from either position; (3) a genuinely keyless line keeps its meaning - bare 'needs-decision:' with no [key=...] still folds to 'default'. Deliberate scoping decisions: only a complete [key=] token at the HEAD of the note (immediately after the first colon, ignoring leading whitespace) states a key - a token deeper inside the note is prose, so a summary merely mentioning '[key=x]' cannot open or close that decision; when both positions carry a token the documented before-colon position wins and the note-head token stays note text; a consumed note-head token is stripped from the note so both positions yield byte-identical fold records (this also keeps the reserved-key namespace vocabulary check in _fm_decision_key_transition_allowed working symmetrically); a stated-but-malformed slug (charset violation in a complete token) is rejected in both positions exactly like the pre-existing before-colon behavior - the folds skip the line - never silently rewritten to 'default'. The documented before-colon form remains the canonical taught form (briefs and fm-send still write it); the note-head form is parser tolerance. Regression tests are required to be behavioral through the real functions, never source-text asserts: new tests/fm-classify-decision-key.test.sh sources the real lib and covers the documented before-colon form -> X, the colon-first form -> X (the fixed case), bare keyless -> default (unchanged, open and close), resolved/blocked symmetry in both positions including cross-position open/close, two colon-form decisions staying distinct and independently closable, mid-note prose mentions not hijacking keys, malformed stated keys rejected in both positions, and the incremental path matching the full fold on the same input including across appends; it is registered in bin/fm-test-run.sh's pure-contract-unit family. One end-to-end case was also added to tests/fm-send-resolve-key.test.sh pinning the exact reported symptom: a colon-first open is listed under its stated key and fm-send --resolve-key answers and closes it. Acceptance criteria: no silent collapse of a stated key; bin/fm-lint.sh clean (it covers bin/*.sh and tests/*.sh); minimal focused diff (bin/fm-classify-lib.sh, bin/fm-test-run.sh family registration, the two test files). Delivery: this no-mistakes run must reach a PR with genuinely green CI; yolo is OFF - the captain merges, no self-merge. ## What Changed - Accept complete `[key=]` tokens immediately after the verb colon while preserving the canonical before-colon form and keyless `default` behavior. - Keep key extraction consistent across full and incremental decision folds, reject malformed stated keys, and bump the persisted fold version to rebuild stale cursors. - Add behavioral unit and end-to-end coverage for position-tolerant opening, closing, and `fm-send --resolve-key` handling. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The focused shared-parser change satisfies the stated invariants, keeps full and incremental folds aligned, bumps persisted fold state, and adds behavioral regression coverage without a substantiated source defect. ## Testing After inspecting the focused diff and clean worktree baseline, targeted parser, fm-send, and cursor-rebuild tests passed; manual checks confirmed captain-held/activity symmetry and an end-to-end colon-first decision was listed under its stated key, answered successfully, persisted as resolved, and disappeared from OPEN DECISIONS. CLI transcript evidence was captured; no visual screenshot was applicable.
Evidence: Colon-first keyed decision listed, resolved through fm-send, and closed ```text === Worker status (colon-first key) === needs-decision: [key=seam-max-bound] cap the seam at 4 or 8 === Firstmate OPEN DECISIONS before answer === OPEN DECISIONS (still open, folded from the durable status logs - not just the latest line): t2109 [key=seam-max-bound] needs-decision: cap the seam at 4 or 8 OPEN DECISIONS: close one by answering it: bin/fm-send.sh --resolve-key '' === Captain answers with fm-send --resolve-key seam-max-bound === exit=0 delivered-to-worker=cap it at 4 === Persisted status ledger after answer === needs-decision: [key=seam-max-bound] cap the seam at 4 or 8 resolved [key=seam-max-bound]: answered: cap it at 4 === Firstmate OPEN DECISIONS after answer === (none) ```

✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Review** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-classify-decision-key.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-send-resolve-key.test.sh` - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-classify-decision-key.test.sh tests/fm-send-resolve-key.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-wake-drain-open-decisions-cursor.test.sh` - Manual fold checks exercised colon-first `captain-held`, activity open/close symmetry, and canonical before-colon precedence when both positions contain keys. - Manual end-to-end fixture ran `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh`, then `bin/fm-send.sh t2109 --resolve-key seam-max-bound 'cap it at 4'`, and drained again.

title: fix(bin): coalesce unacknowledged stale notifications
body:
## Intent Prevent Firstmate from amplifying an unavailable primary session by coalescing equivalent stale notifications while the same stale key is durably queued and unacknowledged. Keep the existing queue lock and queued-key owner authoritative, avoid another primary turn or escalation-count increase for absorbed detections, and keep polling so distinct stale keys, signals, checks, process events, Relay events, and other workers still surface. Once generation-bound acknowledgement removes the row, an unchanged target may emit exactly one new stale notification only after a full configured cadence; genuine successive acknowledged escalations must still reach demand-deep-inspection, while worker activity or turn completion resets recurrence. Apply this at the adapter-neutral watcher/queue boundary, including Herdr's native transition path, without creating sessions, deleting history, interrupting workers, or mutating a live primary home. Validate through executable watcher, queue, acknowledgement, unrelated-notification, activity-reset, deep-inspection, and supported integration tests, with only current architecture and maintainer-verification documentation updated. ## What Changed - Atomically coalesce equivalent stale notifications while the same key remains durably queued and unacknowledged, without suppressing unrelated wake kinds or stale keys. - Apply coalescing across watcher cadence paths and Herdr transitions, restarting a full cadence after acknowledgement and advancing escalation counts only for acknowledged recurrences. - Expand queue, watcher, acknowledgement, activity-reset, deep-inspection, and Herdr regression coverage; bound watcher test cleanup waits and document the updated lifecycle. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-bounded: stale coalescing is atomic under the existing queue lock, preserves distinct notifications, delays post-ack recurrence for a full cadence, and covers Herdr's transition path without introducing a substantiated defect. ## Testing Re-ran the previously partial watcher validation plus queue and Herdr integration suites, exercising coalescing, acknowledgement cadence, unrelated notifications, activity resets, deep inspection, process-event replay, and bounded cleanup; all completed successfully, and a CLI transcript directly demonstrates the operator-visible queue behavior. title: fix(spawn): prevent silent tmux fallback
body:
## Intent Resolve GitHub issue #2156, `fm-spawn can silently select tmux when dispatch expects a visible Herdr worker`. Reproduce the operator-visible failure through the real spawn/public interface in a generated, named non-`default` Herdr lab, with every Herdr operation isolated through `bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh`; separate the trigger (spawn without an explicit per-task backend), masking conditions (configuration and runtime detection), and visible symptom (a tmux worker despite expected visible Herdr placement). Compare and preserve the proven paths for explicit `--backend`, `config/backend`, primary-runtime detection, and intentional behavior for primaries inside and outside multiplexers; inspect relevant history, test the smallest counterfactual, and seek disconfirming evidence. Implement the smallest one-owner contract that prevents an unexpected or operator-invisible backend selection without clear evidence or an applicable explicit choice. An unconfigured, undetected new spawn must fail closed before endpoint creation or metadata publication; explicit, configured, and detected primary-runtime selections retain their documented behavior, non-spawn compatibility remains intact, and local secondmate recovery preserves its recorded backend unless explicitly overridden. Review all supported primary harness/backend integration surfaces and update only authoritative documentation where behavior changes. Add executable public-behavior regression coverage across explicit, configured, primary-runtime, and true-default auto-detection paths, never source-byte assertions. Repair all independent-review findings: make the unresolved path fail closed rather than continuing into detached tmux; make explicit-backend precedence coverage non-vacuous by testing `HERDR_ENV=1` without a competing tmux runtime marker; and prove refusal occurs before endpoint creation and metadata publication. Validate focused routing and recovery tests, `bin/fm-lint.sh`, `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`, and proportionate broader coverage for this safety-critical routing path. ## What Changed - Refuse new task spawns before endpoint or metadata creation when no configured backend or runtime marker resolves. - Preserve explicit backend precedence, recorded-backend recovery for local secondmates, and tmux compatibility for non-spawn callers. - Document the selection semantics and add regression coverage for refusal, configuration, and recovery paths. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: fix bounded; unmatched new spawns refuse, while local recovery preserves its recorded backend. ## Testing Revisados base, target e issue #2156; pruebas enfocadas pasaron y transcripciones CLI demuestran que el fallback anterior creaba tmux, el código actual rechaza antes del endpoint y una selección configurada sigue funcionando.
Evidence: Base vs actual: fallback tmux eliminado ```text SCENARIO: no config/backend and no tmux/herdr/cmux runtime marker BASE 614fae60879372978a4480e22ec4d41eef083b3c warning: /base-data/evidencebase/brief.md records no delivery contract line (scaffolded before ship briefs recorded one); launching on the explicit --mode no-mistakes - confirm its definition of done matches spawned evidencebase harness=claude kind=ship mode=no-mistakes yolo=off window=firstmate:fm-evidencebase worktree=/comparison-worktree exit_status=0 tmux_endpoint_created=yes metadata_published=yes CURRENT 0ed8caaf84a62f130714f3f73945f3962d8e3a59 + test-phase changes error: no runtime backend setting or primary-runtime marker matched this spawn; refusing before endpoint creation. Set config/backend or pass an authorized --backend . exit_status=1 tmux_endpoint_created=no metadata_published=no ```
Evidence: Spawn sin backend: rechazo seguro ```text $ bin/fm-spawn.sh evidenceunresolved claude --mode no-mistakes --yolo off environment: no config/backend and no tmux/herdr/cmux runtime marker error: no runtime backend setting or primary-runtime marker matched this spawn; refusing before endpoint creation. Set config/backend or pass an authorized --backend . exit_status=1 endpoint_operations=none metadata_published=no ```
Evidence: Contrafactual: tmux configurado funciona ```text $ bin/fm-spawn.sh evidenceconfigured claude --mode no-mistakes --yolo off configuration: config/backend=tmux; no runtime marker warning: /evidence-config-data/evidenceconfigured/brief.md records no delivery contract line (scaffolded before ship briefs recorded one); launching on the explicit --mode no-mistakes - confirm its definition of done matches spawned evidenceconfigured harness=claude kind=ship mode=no-mistakes yolo=off window=firstmate:fm-evidenceconfigured worktree=/evidence-config-worktree exit_status=0 endpoint_operations: tmux new-window -dP -F #{window_id} -t firstmate: -n fm-evidenceconfigured -c /evidence-config-project metadata_published=yes metadata_backend_field=absent (compatibility means tmux) ```

title: feat: expand fleet automation and harden lifecycle safety

## Intent T1 lifecycle-safety fix for guarded teardown of legacy detached Herdr ship records. Reproduce and fix the live PR 94 shape where the backlog is done and the PR was squash-merged, but the preserved task branch has five task commits that are no longer individually reachable from a remote and stale metadata remains in flight. Implement a non-destructive proof path that retires only verified task metadata and returns only the worktree when the complete task content and canonical task/PR identity are verifiably landed despite squash-shaped history. The proof must be configuration-independent, exact about the unreached candidate content, and immediately adjacent to the mutation boundary. Do not infer landing from status prose, delete refs or commits, force, or accept ambiguous, dirty, partially landed, target-drifted, externally changed, or identity-mismatched worktrees. Preserve every branch ref and commit. Require exact squash-equivalent content and canonical PR identity, permit reordered commits only when their aggregate content is exactly equivalent, archive task scratch on successful retirement, and leave an auditable note. Keep existing teardown, merge identity, PR check, detached-task, lint, and docs behavior intact. Never merge the PR. ## What Changed - Add remote secondmate provisioning and recovery, durable process-event handling, public follow-ups, capacity refill, and link-intake workflows. - Expand Herdr, Zellij, Pi, and Claude runtime behavior with Calm presentation, lifecycle coordination, trace context, progress journals, and hardened GitHub/CI integration. - Safely retire legacy detached squash-merged tasks only after exact content and canonical repository/PR identity proofs, while preserving refs and commits, archiving scratch data, and recording an audit note. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The bounded corrections now support untracked fork delivery through exact configured-remote identity and bind fetched target history to GitHub’s canonical default-tip OID without introducing a substantiated source defect. ## Testing The initial focused suite passed but missed a Git-configuration masking case; that unsafe behavior was reproduced, fixed at both cleanliness boundaries, regression-tested by the green focused suite, and demonstrated through success, late-change refusal, and content-mismatch refusal CLI evidence.

A valid upstream-contribution PR has its head in a fork; once that source branch is deleted, the detached squash path is entered and now refuses despite an exact head OID and squash-equivalent patch. Firstmate creates branches with `git checkout -b`, while documented no-mistakes fork delivery selects the registered `fork_url` without establishing branch tracking. A valid fork PR pushed without `-u`, then deleted and pruned, therefore reaches this block with no branch remote and is refused despite exact head and content proofs. Bind the head repository to the canonical no-mistakes push registration, or unambiguously match it against configured remote URLs instead of tracking metadata. - 🚨 `bin/fm-teardown.sh:903` - The required “configuration-independent” proof and refusal of “target-drifted” state are contradicted by fetching `$base_url` without binding `FETCH_HEAD` to GitHub’s canonical default-tip OID. Local `url.*.insteadOf` configuration rewrites direct URLs - the new fixtures rely on this behavior - so changed repository config can fetch an alternate `main` containing the recorded merge even after canonical GitHub `main` no longer does. Query the exact repository’s current default-tip OID and require `FETCH_HEAD` to match before the ancestry proof. 🔧 Fix: Bind fork and canonical target identities ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` before the fix - Manual exact-squash teardown with `status.showUntrackedFiles=no` and an untracked file, reproducing unsafe metadata removal and worktree return - `bash tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` after adding explicit `--untracked-files=all` checks - `Manual five-commit squash fixture proving metadata retirement, worktree return, preserved branch and commit, archived scratch, and an audit receipt` - `Manual late-change fixture proving the mutation-adjacent check detects config-hidden untracked content and preserves metadata, worktree, and ref` - `Manual non-equivalent squash fixture proving exact-content mismatch refusal with metadata, worktree, and ref preserved`
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Lint** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ linter found issues (exit code 1) 🔧 Fix: Fix teardown ShellCheck diagnostics ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix(spawn): prevent duplicate worktree ownership across live tasks
body:
## Intent Prevent a new task from ever reusing an isolated project copy already owned by another live task. Reproduce the duplicate-allocation path in an executable regression test before changing behavior. Before any checkout, branch switch, reset, or other project-copy mutation, compare the candidate's canonical path against every live ordinary task record in this Firstmate home and refuse with the conflicting task identity. Close the check-to-publication race under the appropriate task/allocation lock so two concurrent spawns cannot both claim one copy. Treat paused, blocked, working, idle, quiet, and otherwise still-recorded live tasks as owners; endpoint activity must not release a copy. Ignore only records proven retired through the existing cleanup owner, and stop safely on malformed or ambiguous ownership records. Preserve behavior across every supported spawn-capable runtime provider and ordinary ship/scout work. Do not use broad process killing, forcing, stashing, resetting, or deleting another task's state. Keep full mechanics in the authoritative fm-spawn script header/help and focused documentation without bloating AGENTS.md. Include concurrency, refusal, malformed-record, and provider regression coverage; run the complete relevant test suite, fm-lint, documentation checks, and shellcheck. Ship through the no-mistakes PR path, do not merge, and report the full PR URL only when checks are green. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now runs a new `assert_spawn_worktree_unowned` check while holding the task-set lock: after allocating an isolated worktree and before any fetch/checkout/reset or other mutation, it canonicalizes the candidate path and compares it against every other ordinary (ship/scout) task record in the home's state directory, refusing allocation with the conflicting task id when a live owner matches. Malformed, duplicate, non-regular, or ambiguous ownership records also refuse allocation, and an Orca-backed refusal disables abort cleanup so the disputed copy is never removed. - Regression coverage added across `tests/fm-spawn-worktree-settle.test.sh`, `tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh`, `tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh`, and `tests/fm-spawn-pool-base-freshen.test.sh` for the refusal, malformed-record, concurrency, and provider paths. - `docs/architecture.md` documents the ownership refusal boundary and the test files that own its regression coverage. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a well-bounded fail-closed ownership check placed before the first spawn-owned mutation, correctly serialized under the pre-existing task-set lock held from allocation through publication, covered by behavioral regression tests for refusal, ambiguity, concurrency, and the Orca provider, with no reachable path found that reintroduces the duplicate-allocation failure. ## Testing Ran the four touched test suites at the target commit (all pass), proved the new ownership regression tests fail against the pre-fix fm-spawn.sh from the base commit (reproducing the duplicate-allocation bug before the fix), and manually demonstrated the end-user behavior: a spawn handed a worktree owned by a paused live task is refused with the conflicting task's identity, publishes no second owner, and leaves the owner's record and branch untouched.
Evidence: Manual CLI transcript: spawn refuses worktree owned by paused live task === SETUP: live task demo-owner-1 (paused) owns isolated worktree === $ fm-spawn.sh demo-contender-2 <project> --mode no-mistakes --yolo off error: isolated worktree '<case>/wt' is already owned by live task demo-owner-1; refusing allocation for task demo-contender-2 exit status: 1 === RESULT === demo-contender-2.meta: not published (owner remains exclusive) demo-owner-1.meta: still present (owner untouched) owner worktree HEAD unchanged: a2537bd3e27e18cf9ae279ae1836c66b8ddbe912 ```text === SETUP: live task demo-owner-1 (paused) owns isolated worktree === owner meta (/tmp/fm-spawn-manual-demo.DDnw9H/demo/home/state/demo-owner-1.meta): window=firstmate:fm-demo-owner-1 endpoint_task_id=demo-owner-1 worktree=/wt project=/project harness=codex kind=ship === ACTION: spawn new task demo-contender-2, allocator hands back the same worktree === $ fm-spawn.sh demo-contender-2 --mode no-mistakes --yolo off warning: /home/data/demo-contender-2/brief.md records no delivery contract line (scaffolded before ship briefs recorded one); launching on the explicit --mode no-mistakes - confirm its definition of done matches error: isolated worktree '/wt' is already owned by live task demo-owner-1; refusing allocation for task demo-contender-2 exit status: 1 === RESULT === demo-contender-2.meta: not published (owner remains exclusive) demo-owner-1.meta: still present (owner untouched) owner worktree HEAD unchanged: a2537bd3e27e18cf9ae279ae1836c66b8ddbe912 ```
Evidence: Red/green regression proof (tests fail pre-fix, pass post-fix) Pre-fix (base 614fae6): not ok - spawn reused a copy already recorded by settle-owner-z3; not ok - Orca spawn reused a worktree owned by orcaownerz7 Post-fix (target 48d4049): all fm-spawn-worktree-settle tests passed, including 'a paused recorded task keeps exclusive ownership', 'ambiguous ordinary-task ownership stops allocation safely', 'concurrent spawns cannot both publish ownership of one isolated copy' ```text === Regression proof: new ownership tests vs pre-fix bin/fm-spawn.sh (base 614fae6) === --- tests/fm-spawn-worktree-settle.test.sh (pre-fix: FAILS, reproducing the bug) --- ok - a single transient stale pane_current_path read is not accepted as the worktree ok - an already-settled pane confirms via the existing inter-poll sleep, not an extra full cycle not ok - spawn reused a copy already recorded by settle-owner-z3 --- tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh (pre-fix: FAILS) --- not ok - Orca spawn reused a worktree owned by orcaownerz7 === Same tests vs fixed bin/fm-spawn.sh (target 48d4049): PASS === --- tests/fm-spawn-worktree-settle.test.sh --- ok - a single transient stale pane_current_path read is not accepted as the worktree ok - an already-settled pane confirms via the existing inter-poll sleep, not an extra full cycle ok - a paused recorded task keeps exclusive ownership of its isolated copy ok - ambiguous ordinary-task ownership stops allocation safely ok - concurrent spawns cannot both publish ownership of one isolated copy # all fm-spawn-worktree-settle tests passed ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 2 infos - ℹ️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1744` - assert_spawn_worktree_unowned refuses ALL new allocations in the home when any live task's recorded worktree cannot be canonicalized (deleted dir, unreachable mount), even though a nonexistent owner worktree can never equal an existing candidate. This is stricter than needed and could cause a home-wide spawn outage after one dangling record or transient mount failure, but it is the fail-closed behavior the intent authorizes for ambiguous ownership records and the refusal identifies the offending task. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:2290` - On an Orca ownership refusal, ORCA_ABORT_CLEANUP=0 skips both worktree removal (correct — the copy may belong to the live owner) and terminal close, leaking the terminal created for the refused spawn. The new test explicitly asserts this, so it is a deliberate conservative tradeoff to avoid disturbing resources attached to the owner's copy; noting for awareness that refused Orca spawns leave a terminal behind for manual cleanup.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-spawn-worktree-settle.test.sh` at target 48d4049 (all pass, including paused-owner refusal, ambiguous-record stop, and concurrent-spawn single-publisher race) - `bash tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh` at target (all pass, including the new owned-candidate refusal that preserves the owner's Orca worktree and terminal) - `bash tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh` at target (all pass, batch spawns now use distinct worktrees per task) - `bash tests/fm-spawn-pool-base-freshen.test.sh` at target (all pass, idempotence check reworked to same-task repeat) - Red/green regression check: checked out pre-fix `bin/fm-spawn.sh` from base 614fae6 and re-ran the settle and Orca suites — both new ownership tests fail pre-fix, proving they reproduce the duplicate-allocation bug - Manual end-to-end verification: built a Firstmate home with a paused live owner task, invoked `fm-spawn.sh` for a contender pointed at the same worktree, and confirmed refusal naming the owner, exit 1, no contender metadata published, owner metadata intact, owner branch HEAD unchanged
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Lint** - 1 warning - ⚠️ linter found issues (exit code 127)
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: feat(bin): add guarded local-only branch return for secondmate projects
body:
## Intent Add a guarded local/NAS-only branch-return capability so persistent second mates can supervise explicitly registered local-only projects without GitHub, external upload, merge authority, or destructive cleanup. Main Firstmate must retain validation and captain-controlled fast-forward landing. The capability must be explicit and route-bound, use ordinary no-hardlink clones with filesystem-only remotes, refuse unsafe paths, repository identity or ancestry drift, branch collisions, dirty or missing source work, ambiguous ownership, unexpected external remotes, missing objects, and destination drift. Return only the exact fm/ branch without merging or granting push authority; support idempotent receipts, guarded main-home landing, and cleanup only after exact returned-commit reachability is proven. Update the existing owner contracts rather than creating a parallel authority path, add comprehensive behavioral regressions, run normal validation, commit, and ship through no-mistakes as a pull request without merging. ## What Changed - Add `bin/fm-local-branch-return.sh` and a shared `bin/fm-local-project-route-lib.sh`: a locked, receipt-producing operation that fetches exactly one `fm/` branch from a registered local secondmate project copy into the bound main-home repository, validating the private route capability, repository identity/ancestry, clean source state, stable tips, and branch-owner collisions before an update-ref CAS — with no merge, push, or source cleanup, and idempotent replay of matching receipts. - Allow local-only projects on local secondmate routes: `fm-home-seed.sh` now clones them with `--no-local` from the canonical main-home source, forces filesystem-only remotes, and publishes a rollback-aware capability record under `data/local-project-routes/`; `fm-spawn.sh` refuses local-only ship and scout tasks in a secondmate home unless that capability validates the bound copy; `fm-merge-local.sh --secondmate` lands a returned branch fast-forward only after re-verifying the receipt, capability, and destination against drift; `fm-teardown.sh` accepts cleanup of returned local-only worktrees only when the exact returned commit is proven reachable from the refreshed default branch. - Update the owner contracts and docs (AGENTS.md, secondmate-provisioning and project-management skills, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/scripts.md`) and add behavioral regressions in `tests/fm-local-branch-return.test.sh` plus adjusted teardown/brief/safety tests. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Both accepted round-1 findings are correctly implemented and behaviorally tested (scout spawns now run the same capability revalidation as local-only ship spawns; the unused parameter was dropped at all call sites), and the overall change satisfies every source-verifiable intent constraint with fail-closed guards throughout. ## Testing Ran the new fm-local-branch-return behavioral suite (9/9 pass), the three local-only teardown guard tests including the new bound-local-origin reachability case, the full fm-brief suite for the updated owner-contract wording, and a manual end-to-end CLI demo whose transcript shows seeding, no push authority, exact-branch return without merging, idempotent receipts, captain-controlled fast-forward landing, and external-remote refusal; everything passed with no product issues found. No visual artifact applies since this is a shell CLI capability with no rendered surface.
Evidence: End-to-end CLI transcript: local-only secondmate seed → return → replay → guarded landing → refusal ```text ### 1. Main Firstmate home registers a sensitive LOCAL-ONLY project (no GitHub) $ cat /tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/main-home/data/projects.md - alpha [local-only] - sensitive local project (added 2026-08-10) ### 2. Captain seeds the secondmate home with the local-only project (explicit, route-bound) $ env FM_HOME=/tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/main-home /home/lz/.no-mistakes/worktrees/529d11e0d8c5/01KZSN2VDKA0HKM8VMFH9QYNB2/bin/fm-home-seed.sh ops /tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/secondmate-home alpha home=/tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/secondmate-home ### 3. The seeded copy is an ordinary no-hardlink clone whose only remote is the local filesystem $ git -C /tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/secondmate-home/projects/alpha remote -v origin /tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/main-home/projects/alpha (fetch) origin /tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/secondmate-home/projects/alpha (push) ### Route capability record written in the MAIN home (the guarded grant): $ cat /tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/main-home/data/local-project-routes/ops/alpha.route schema=fm-local-project-route.v1 secondmate_id=ops project=alpha main_home=/tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/main-home main_project=/tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/main-home/projects/alpha main_git_common_dir=/tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/main-home/projects/alpha/.git main_git_identity=64770:3555052 secondmate_home=/tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/secondmate-home secondmate_project=/tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/secondmate-home/projects/alpha secondmate_git_common_dir=/tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/secondmate-home/projects/alpha/.git secondmate_git_identity=64770:3555109 anchor_oid=757d88ea8880737c443584d307e3437453e6a178 ### 4. Secondmate task does work on branch fm/demo-task in a worktree $ git -C /tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/worktrees/demo-task log --oneline -1 fef98bb demo task result ### 5. The secondmate has NO push/merge authority into the main project: $ git -C "/tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/worktrees/demo-task" push origin HEAD:main remote: error: refusing to update checked out branch: refs/heads/main remote: error: By default, updating the current branch in a non-bare repository remote: is denied, because it will make the index and work tree inconsistent remote: with what you pushed, and will require 'git reset --hard' to match remote: the work tree to HEAD. $ git -C /tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/main-home/projects/alpha log --oneline main 757d88e initial ### 6. Replaying the same return is an idempotent receipt $ env FM_HOME=/tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/main-home /home/lz/.no-mistakes/worktrees/529d11e0d8c5/01KZSN2VDKA0HKM8VMFH9QYNB2/bin/fm-local-branch-return.sh ops demo-task already returned fm/demo-task at fef98bb9b4b2632211268310d871217918fc909b into /tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/main-home/projects/alpha ### 8. Only the MAIN Firstmate lands it, through the captain-controlled fast-forward gate $ env FM_HOME=/tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/main-home /home/lz/.no-mistakes/worktrees/529d11e0d8c5/01KZSN2VDKA0HKM8VMFH9QYNB2/bin/fm-merge-local.sh --secondmate ops demo-task merged fm/demo-task into local main (757d88e -> fef98bb) in /tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/main-home/projects/alpha $ git -C /tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/main-home/projects/alpha log --oneline main fef98bb demo task result 757d88e initial ### 9. Refusal example: an unexpected external remote on the secondmate copy blocks any return $ FM_HOME=
fm-local-branch-return.sh ops leak-task REFUSED: secondmate local-only project has a non-local remote; local-only secondmate routes accept only absolute filesystem or file:/// transports (exit 1) $ git -C /tmp/fm-local-return-demo.uT5V6z/main-home/projects/alpha branch --list fm/leak-task ```
Evidence: fm-local-branch-return behavioral suite output (9 scenarios) ok - local-only secondmate branch returns without landing, replays idempotently, then lands only through the main gate ok - branch collision refuses without changing either repository ok - dirty source work is refused and preserved ok - wrong and ambiguous repository bindings are refused ok - symlinked and unsafe route paths are refused without changing the branch ok - unexpected ancestry is refused and source work is preserved ok - absent capability and conflicting task ownership both refuse ok - destination identity drift and missing source objects refuse ok - local-only seeding and return both guarantee that every configured remote is local filesystem only ```text ok - local-only secondmate branch returns without landing, replays idempotently, then lands only through the main gate ok - branch collision refuses without changing either repository ok - dirty source work is refused and preserved ok - wrong and ambiguous repository bindings are refused ok - symlinked and unsafe route paths are refused without changing the branch ok - unexpected ancestry is refused and source work is preserved ok - absent capability and conflicting task ownership both refuse ok - destination identity drift and missing source objects refuse ok - local-only seeding and return both guarantee that every configured remote is local filesystem only ```
Evidence: Local-only teardown guard tests (incl. new bound-local-origin reachability case) ok - local-only worktree with truly unpushed work is refused (safety preserved) ok - local-only worktree with work merged into local main is torn down (no regression) ok - local-only returned work can be cleaned only after its bound local origin contains it ```text ok - local-only worktree with truly unpushed work is refused (safety preserved) ok - local-only worktree with work merged into local main is torn down (no regression) ok - local-only returned work can be cleaned only after its bound local origin contains it ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1646` - The new local-only capability guard in fm-spawn.sh fires only for KIND=ship (`[ "$KIND" = ship ] && [ "$MODE" = local-only ]`). Since --mode is refused on --scout spawns, MODE is empty for scouts, so a scout task against a hand-cloned local-only project inside a secondmate home still spawns (creating a scratch worktree in the copy) without route-capability revalidation. The updated secondmate-provisioning SKILL.md states "A local-only task in a secondmate home is valid only while fm-spawn.sh revalidates the parent binding and the private route capability before launch", which overstates the implemented guard. No landing-authority leak exists (fm-local-branch-return.sh requires kind=ship), but either the guard should extend to scout spawns of local-only projects in secondmate homes or the doc claim should be narrowed to ship tasks. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-local-branch-return.sh:169` - Branch returns are single-shot per task id: after a receipt is published, a worker revision that adds commits to fm/<task-id> can never be re-returned — the receipt head check ("existing branch-return receipt is owned by different work") and the destination branch-owner check both refuse, and there is no guarded path to supersede or retire a receipt short of manual main-home surgery.
