title: feat(config): configure plan and review workflow skills
body:
## Intent Implement the bounded MVP of kunchenguid/firstmate issue #1244 exactly as specified in that issue: a local, gitignored config/crew-skills.json that maps workflow phases to skills, so a captain's own workflow applies to every dispatch without retyping it per task or forking the shared AGENTS.md orchestrator file. Required scope, all from the issue's acceptance criteria: - config/crew-skills.json with top-level 'phases' defaults for the plan and review phases, plus per-project overrides under 'projects.'. - Resolution precedence: an explicit per-task instruction wins, then projects.., then phases., then today's built-in behavior (no added skill). - Absent config file must leave behavior identical to today. - Bootstrap validation that fails loudly as 'CREW_SKILLS: invalid config/crew-skills.json - ' and BLOCKS dispatch rather than silently falling back; a skipped review is worse than a stopped dispatch. - Both skill locations resolve: repo-level .agents/skills//SKILL.md and user-level ~/.claude/skills//SKILL.md. - Secondmate homes inherit the file through the existing local-material allowlist. - Invocation reuses the existing harness-adapters skill-invocation contract rather than restating per-harness syntax, degrading to natural language where no command form is verified. - The resolved skill per phase is recorded in the task's meta as skill_plan= / skill_review=. - The file is gitignored, documented in docs/configuration.md, with a copyable starting point under docs/examples/. Deliberate exclusions the user set: this is an MVP bounded to the plan and review phases only - the issue's suggested 'implement' and 'validate' phases are explicitly out of scope and rejected by validation. It must NOT replace or weaken any delivery gate: for no-mistakes-mode projects the configured review skill runs IN ADDITION TO the pipeline, never instead of it. Replacing the delivery gate would need a separate, explicit, obviously-scary opt-in and is not built here. No database or browser stack is involved; Cypress is never run locally. Decisions and tradeoffs made while doing the work, which a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: - bin/fm-crew-skills.sh is the single executable owner of validation and resolution, following the config/crew-dispatch.json precedent the issue explicitly cites; docs/configuration.md owns the schema prose and AGENTS.md keeps only a short trigger, per the repo's firstmate-coding-guidelines knowledge-placement tree and one-owner rule. - The brief records the resolved skill and fm-spawn.sh refuses a brief/spawn mismatch, so editing the config after a brief was scaffolded cannot silently change a task's workflow mid-flight. This fail-closed drift check is deliberate, not incidental. - I fixed a real defect found while reviewing inherited uncommitted work: on --relaunch, skill_plan/skill_review were never recovered from the task record, so the meta rewrite silently DROPPED them and a relaunched task lost its configured workflow. Relaunch now reuses the recorded value exactly as it already reuses mode and yolo, rather than re-resolving from a possibly since-edited config. A regression test covers both preservation and the --skill-review-on-relaunch refusal. - Tests are behavioral and colocated in tests/ per repo convention, covering resolution precedence, bootstrap validation, secondmate inheritance, brief rendering, promote, and meta recording. They are not introduced here and are not in scope to fix. Targets main and fully closes the issue, with a standalone 'Closes #1244' in the commit. The PR must not be merged by me under any circumstances. ## What Changed - Add local `config/crew-skills.json` resolution for plan and review skills, with explicit task, project, and global precedence plus repo- and user-level skill discovery. - Validate configuration during bootstrap and fail dispatch on invalid skills or brief/spawn drift while preserving resolved skills in task metadata and across relaunches. - Inherit crew skill configuration into secondmate homes and document the schema with a copyable example and behavioral test coverage. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-bounded, satisfies the source-verifiable acceptance criteria, preserves the additive no-mistakes gate, and the prior source-content-only test was correctly replaced with behavioral inheritance coverage. ## Testing Targeted behavioral tests and an end-to-end CLI demonstration validated resolution precedence, fail-closed schema handling, inheritance, brief generation, promotion, spawn/relaunch metadata persistence, gitignore coverage, and the copyable example. title: feat(bin): wake once on a GitHub pull request closed without merging
body:
## Intent Re-deliver upstream contribution 1931 from eduardstan/firstmate branch fm/fm-pr-closed-unmerged-1897 on a fresh feature branch based on current kunchenguid/firstmate origin/main. Preserve the sound behavior: a GitHub pull-request merge watch must wake firstmate once when the watched PR is closed without merging, keep the poll armed so reopen/merge still wakes, forget the closure after a positive open reading, and retain the original security and teardown guarantees. Resolve current-main compatibility on merit, but do not guess if upstream has already changed the same behavior. Deliver through the genuine no-mistakes route, with origin remaining kunchenguid/firstmate and the push target remaining the eduardstan/firstmate fork, so the pipeline itself creates the deterministic Pipeline section and opens a PR against kunchenguid/firstmate whose PR must be raised via no-mistakes check passes. Leave PR 1931 open and untouched; never forge the Pipeline section, merge a PR, push a default branch, add AI attribution, or repoint origin. Per the captain's decision, the rewritten base commit message must state only the delivered behavior: GitHub emits closed; the poll stays armed with repeated closure wakes held to one by the seen marker; retirement authority remains merged-only; it must not claim GitLab closed support, closure retirement, or closed-result retirement receipts. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-pr-poll.sh` now emits `closed` for a GitHub pull request closed without merging and `open` for one still open, alongside the existing `merged` line; the GitLab path still emits `merged` only, and every other reading and error stays silent. - `bin/fm-watch.sh` queues a `check: : closed` wake for a closed reading without retiring the poll, so a reopen or later merge still wakes; repeats are held to one wake by a new `state/.seen-pr-closed-` marker (`fm-pr-lib.sh`) written only after the durable wake is appended, cleared on a positive `open` reading, cleared whenever a poll is published for that task, and cleared for path-safe ids during teardown's poll-artifact removal. - `fm_pr_poll_prepare` now stores the poll state directory in `FM_PR_POLL_STATE_DIR` and `fm_pr_poll_publish_prepared` validates artifacts against it instead of deriving the directory from the check destination path; `AGENTS.md` and `docs/architecture.md` document the closed/open results, and `tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh` covers the closed wake, its single-wake suppression, marker clearing on open and on teardown, and the poll staying armed. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Change is tightly bounded to the GitHub poll's result vocabulary plus one dedupe marker whose only power is suppressing a single wake; retirement authority, poll validation, and teardown guarantees are untouched, every re-arm path clears the marker, and the wake ordering keeps failures on the repeat-rather-than-swallow side. ## Testing Ran the single relevant targeted suite (tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh, 39 tests, all passing, ~7 minutes) covering the new closed-wake tests alongside the existing parsing, atomicity, retirement, symlink-refusal, and teardown guarantees, then went beyond unit level with two manual end-to-end runs driving the real fm-pr-check.sh, fm-watch.sh, fm-pr-poll.sh, and fm-wake-drain.sh with only the forge CLIs faked. The captured transcripts show what a firstmate operator actually experiences: a closed-without-merge PR queues exactly one `check: ...: closed` wake in the persisted state/.wake-queue and in the wake-drain output, the poll's artifacts remain armed across further closed cycles with the `.seen-pr-closed-<id>` marker suppressing repeats, a reopened PR clears the marker without waking anyone, its second closure wakes again, and a final merge still wakes and retires the poll while preserving `pr=`/`pr_head=` metadata; the provider transcript confirms GitLab emits `merged` alone and every unreadable or failed lookup stays silent. This change is CLI/daemon-level with no rendered user interface, so no screenshot or visual artifact applies — the reviewer-visible surface is the wake text and persisted state, both captured verbatim. No failures, no flakiness observed, and the worktree is clean with all evidence written only under the dedicated evidence directory.

title: feat(bin): have ship briefs check the target project's own workflow conventions
body:
## Intent

Add a project-agnostic instruction to the ship-task brief template generated by bin/fm-brief.sh: before starting implementation, the crewmate should check the target project's own repo for its own implementation/workflow conventions (e.g. CONTRIBUTING.md, an AGENTS.md workflow section, or an agent-loaded skill such as .claude/skills/*) and follow them for delivery methodology (e.g. incremental/vertical-slice delivery or test-first development), in addition to firstmate's own delivery-mode and status-reporting rules, which are unrelated and stay unchanged. The instruction must stay strictly generic: no naming of jeeves-ui, tracer bullets, TDD, do-work, or any other specific project/methodology/skill inside firstmate's own shared code - this is a standing check-and-follow mechanism for any current or future project, motivated by discovering jeeves-ui's .claude/skills/do-work has no reliable way to fire for a crewmate on a non-claude harness. Added as a new numbered Setup step (dynamically numbered per delivery mode via a new WORKFLOW_STEP variable, since existing SETUP2 already occupies step 2 in no-mistakes mode) right after the branch-creation step and before Rules, matching the existing Setup/Rules/Project-memory tone. Also updated the script's own header usage comment to document this new generated Setup content, per repo convention that a script's header stays accurate to its behavior. Loaded and followed the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill before editing since this touches firstmate's own shared tracked material (bin/fm-brief.sh). Verified via bin/fm-lint.sh (shellcheck clean) and the existing colocated tests/fm-brief.test.sh (all pass, unmodified since the tests assert behavior/structure, not literal generated bytes), plus manually generated sample briefs for all three delivery modes (no-mistakes, direct-PR, local-only) to confirm correct step numbering.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-brief.sh` now adds a new numbered Setup step to the generated ship-task brief, instructing the crewmate to check the target project's own repo for its own implementation/workflow conventions (e.g. `CONTRIBUTING.md`, an `AGENTS.md` workflow section, or an agent-loaded skill such as `.claude/skills/*`) and follow them for delivery methodology, in addition to firstmate's own delivery-mode and status-reporting rules.
- The step is inserted right after the branch-creation step and before Rules, with its step number driven by a new `WORKFLOW_STEP` variable set per delivery mode (2 for `direct-PR`/`local-only`, 3 for `no-mistakes` mode, where step 2 is already occupied by the `no-mistakes doctor`/`init` instruction).
- Updated the script's header usage comment to document this new generated Setup content.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is a small, well-scoped addition (9 lines in one file) that adds a generic, dynamically-numbered Setup step with correct per-mode numbering, keeps prose project-agnostic as required, updates the header comment to match, and does not touch tests since existing tests assert structure/content rather than exact numbering.

## Testing

Ran the full colocated fm-brief.test.sh suite (20/20 pass, unmodified as intended since tests assert structure not literal bytes) and fm-lint.sh (shellcheck clean). Manually generated sample ship briefs for all three delivery modes and confirmed the new instruction renders as step 3 in no-mistakes mode (after the existing step-2 `no-mistakes doctor` line) and step 2 in direct-PR/local-only mode, sitting between branch creation and the Rules section exactly as specified, with wording that stays project-agnostic (grep confirms no mention of jeeves-ui, tracer bullets, TDD, or do-work) and is clearly separated from firstmate's own unrelated delivery-mode/status rules. The header comment was also updated to document this new generated content. No issues found.

<details>
<summary>Evidence: Sample generated brief - no-mistakes mode (Setup step 3)</summary>

```text
You are a crewmate: an autonomous worker agent managed by firstmate. Work on your own; do not wait for a human.

# Task
{TASK}

# Herdr lifecycle declaration - NOT ENABLED
**HARD SAFETY GATE:** this scaffold cannot inspect the task text that replaces `{TASK}` later.
If the task will start, stop, delete, restart, profile, or otherwise drive Herdr lifecycle behavior, stop and regenerate the brief with `--herdr-lab` before dispatch.
Do not add Herdr lifecycle commands to this unguarded brief by hand.

# Setup
You are in a disposable git worktree of some-proj, at a detached HEAD on a clean default branch.

**Verify isolation before anything else.** Run `pwd -P` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; both must resolve to the disposable task worktree you were launched in, such as a treehouse pool path or an Orca-managed worktree, not the primary checkout firstmate operates from.
The path check is authoritative: `git rev-parse --git-dir` and `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` can help inspect the repo, but they do not prove you are outside the primary checkout.
If the top-level path is the primary checkout or not the worktree you were launched in, STOP - do not branch or commit here - append `blocked: launched in primary checkout, not an isolated worktree` to the status file and stop.

1. First action: create your branch: `git checkout -b fm/sample-no-mistakes`
2. Run `no-mistakes doctor`; if it reports the repo is not initialized here, run `no-mistakes init`.
3. Before implementing, check this repo for its own implementation/workflow conventions - for example a `CONTRIBUTING.md`, an `AGENTS.md` workflow section, or an agent-loaded skill such as `.claude/skills/*` - and follow them for delivery methodology (such as incremental delivery or test-first development). This is separate from firstmate's own delivery-mode and status-reporting rules below, which still apply unchanged.

# Rules
1. Never push to the default branch. Never merge a PR.
2. Stay inside this worktree; modify nothing outside it.
3. Use gh-axi for GitHub operations and chrome-devtools-axi for browser operations.
4. Report status by appending one line:
   `echo "{state}: {one short line}" >> '/var/folders/14/bbb3x64n5bd02h0qk406kks40000gq/T/tmp.UjFcjlQQg1/home/state/sample-no-mistakes.status'`
   States: working, needs-decision, blocked, paused, done, failed.
   Each append wakes firstmate, so report sparingly: only phase changes a supervisor
   would act on (setup done, bug reproduced, fix implemented, validation passed) and the
   needs-decision/blocked/paused/done/failed states. No step-by-step FYI progress lines;
   firstmate reads your pane for that.
   A mid-task `working:` line (including setup complete) is nonterminal: do not end the
   turn after it; continue the same stage until a defined `done:` gate under Definition of done.
   Use `paused: {why}` - distinct from `blocked:` - ONLY when you are deliberately idling on a
   known external wait you expect to clear on its own (an upstream release, a rate-limit reset,
   a scheduled window): firstmate then leaves your idle pane alone and rechecks it on a long
   cadence instead of treating it as a possible wedge. Use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need help.
```

## Intent Add first-class Forgejo pull-request support to the Firstmate guarded PR lifecycle and ship an upstream pull request through the configured fork escidmore/firstmate to kunchenguid/firstmate, without merging it. Extend the authoritative parser and provider identity for only canonical Forgejo URLs shaped https://///pulls/, while strictly rejecting userinfo, ports, trailing dots or slashes, query or fragment data, encoded separators or control bytes, malformed namespaces, and GitHub or GitLab lookalikes. Arm and execute Forgejo merge polling through the installed forgejo-axi command using the validated host explicitly as --base-url and validated owner/repository plus pull number as separate arguments; keep poll errors silent and emit merged only for exact merged truth. Make fm-pr-check refuse Forgejo monitoring when forgejo-axi is unavailable, record the canonical provider-tagged identity, and record a head only when safely available without a JSON dependency. Merge Forgejo PRs through forgejo-axi while preserving metadata recording, default squash where supported, repository/base-URL/expected-head override rejection, extra-argument safety, and refusal of failed, pending, non-mergeable, head-changed, or review-required work; preserve existing GitHub and GitLab behavior and add no GitLab merge parity. Trace and support every parser consumer, including polling, metadata identity, teardown landing proof, review-diff resolution, migration, retirement, and cleanup, so a guarded Forgejo merge can be monitored and safely cleaned without manual state edits. Add focused behavior and security tests for canonical /pulls/ URLs and hostile near misses beside existing parser, check, poll, merge, teardown, and review-diff tests, and update concise authoritative provider-enumeration comments and docs. Keep the implementation minimal and provider-specific, without a speculative forge abstraction. Use current forgejo-axi help and behavior rather than guessed flags or output; the task-stated /Users/host/.local/bin/forgejo-axi path was absent, so the installed command at /etc/profiles/per-user/host/bin/forgejo-axi was inspected and used. Run Forgejo and guarded teardown lifecycle tests only through a generated isolated non-default Herdr lab, never against the active default Herdr session. Preserve the deterministic pre-existing single-link X-shim focused-runner failure because origin/main reproduces it identically; do not weaken hard-link validation or expand into unrelated Relay/X integration work. Require focused Forgejo security, poll, merge, review-diff, guarded teardown, source-aware ShellCheck, canonical Firstmate lint, documentation-audience, syntax, and diff-hygiene evidence. Keep commits and PR prose factual, current-state only, and free of agent attribution. Never merge the pull request. ## What Changed - Adds canonical Forgejo pull-request identities with strict URL validation, project-remote authorization, tool availability checks, and optional head capture. - Extends guarded polling and merging through `forgejo-axi` with explicit repository identity, exact merged-state handling, expected-head and mergeability safeguards, while preserving GitHub behavior and refusing GitLab merges. - Propagates Forgejo support through migration, retirement, review-diff, teardown, and cleanup paths, with focused security/lifecycle tests and updated provider documentation. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the changed provider, polling, merge, review-diff, migration, teardown, and compatibility paths are bounded and no material source defect was substantiated. ## Testing All targeted parser/security/poll/retirement, merge, review-diff, guarded teardown, project-origin, and changed remote-job behavior completed successfully. The initial attempt was invalidated by the user BASH_ENV prepending the real Forgejo CLI over fixture shims; rerunning with `BASH_ENV=/dev/null` passed. No linters or static analysis were run because this was the assigned test phase; evidence was written to the dedicated evidence directory.

fm-pr-merge records pr= and pr_head= before invoking gh-axi pr merge ok - fm-pr-merge propagates a real merge failure without silently succeeding ok - fm-pr-merge forwards extra flags to gh-axi pr merge after the -- separator ok - fm-pr-merge refuses before merging when task meta is missing ok - fm-pr-merge refuses malformed PR URLs before calling gh-axi ok - fm-pr-merge refuses unsafe PR URL segments before recording state ok - fm-pr-merge refuses repo override args before recording state ok - fm-pr-merge does not add default --squash when the caller passes an explicit merge method ok - fm-pr-merge respects --method= as an explicit merge method ok - fm-pr-merge parses a GitHub PR URL into gh-axi number and --repo arguments ok - fm-pr-merge records and merges a ready Forgejo pull through forgejo-axi ok - fm-pr-merge refuses a Forgejo pull whose checks or mergeability are not ready ok - fm-pr-merge propagates Forgejo server refusals such as required review ok - fm-pr-merge refuses Forgejo base URL and expected-head overrides before recording ok - fm-pr-merge refuses Forgejo hosts absent from project remotes === tests/fm-review-diff.test.sh === ok - fm-review-diff falls back to recorded pr_head when pull head cannot be fetched ok - fm-review-diff fetches refs/pull//head when pr_head= is absent ok - fm-review-diff retains origin resolution for numeric PR metadata ok - fm-review-diff resolves a Forgejo /pulls/ URL through refs/pull//head ok - fm-review-diff preserves registered scp transport for canonical Forgejo pull heads ok - fm-review-diff rejects worktree-scoped cross-host Git rewrites before fetch ok - fm-review-diff refuses Forgejo fetches absent from project remotes ok - fm-review-diff rejects noncanonical PR metadata targets ok - fm-review-diff prefers freshly fetched PR head over a stale recorded pr_head= ok - title: Fix stale wake loop for declared paused workers
body:
## Summary

Fix the self-sustaining stale-wake loop for a worker that has delivered work and is waiting on a captain decision.

## Root cause and fix

The root cause and fix are in `bin/fm-watch.sh`, not `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh`.

`pause_state_class()` treated a live ordinary worker with a declared `paused:` status as `none` when a fresh watcher cycle first encountered its frozen pane hash.
That routed the first stale observation to `surface_nonterminal_stale()` and emitted `stale:`.
A new cycle repeated that first-observation path indefinitely.

The watcher now treats an explicit `paused:` status as durable cross-cycle pause evidence while the agent is alive.
It retains the existing bounded long-cadence pause recheck instead of starting wedge escalation.

## Acceptance criterion 3 evidence

The colocated watcher test covers both distinguishable cases:

- A delivered worker with an open, green PR and `paused:` declaration awaiting a merge decision is absorbed across two fresh watcher cycles, emits no stale wake, and starts no wedge timer.
- A worker with the same declared pause whose agent has crashed still emits a prompt bare `stale:` wake and clears pause tracking.

This preserves stale supervision for a genuine crash or wedge rather than suppressing both cases.

## Validation

- `bin/fm-lint.sh`
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed`

This task did not use the no-mistakes pipeline because its configured `pi` gate agent cannot neutralize repository agent-instruction files and therefore refused to launch.

title: fix(bin): reclaim orphaned lock and job-claim scratch files
body:
## Intent Fix issue #1972 in kunchenguid/firstmate: the remote job worker's ownership lock can deadlock permanently on an orphaned lock temp file, so no worker can ever start again for an account's state root. Root cause from the issue: worker_publish_quarantine in bin/fm-remote-job-worker.sh stages an atomic rename through a uniquely named $WORKER_LOCK/.quarantine.XXXXXX scratch file. If a worker dies between creating that scratch file and the rename, the orphan is left behind with no owner to finish or discard it, and every later reclaim of the ownership lock fails because the lock directory never becomes empty. bin/fm-remote-entrypoint.sh and bin/fm-remote-doctor.sh --fix then report only "remote job worker did not report ready after startup" roughly 48 seconds late, giving no indication that the ownership lock is wedged. Recovery previously required deleting worker.lock by hand. Goal: make an orphaned atomic-publish scratch file unable to wedge worker ownership permanently, and make the failure diagnosable - the reported error must name the exact wedged ownership lock instead of a generic startup timeout. Requirements: colocated test coverage that reproduces the reported condition and fails against the pre-fix behavior while passing with the fix, since a test asserting only the new happy path is insufficient; bin/ scripts must stay shellcheck-clean; every existing safety boundary must be preserved, escalating rather than shipping if the fix appeared to require weakening one; and every non-obvious decision must be recorded with its evidence under a "## Decisions" section in the PR body. Constraints and exclusions: do not weaken the mutual exclusion the worker lock provides - reclaiming an orphan must be provably safe against a concurrently live worker, escalating rather than shipping a racy reclaim; and do not refactor beyond this defect and any identical instance of the same pattern. The change surface is bin/fm-remote-job-worker.sh and its colocated test; other files in this repository belong to concurrently active lanes and must not be edited. Delivery: target branch main. Never merge and never enable auto-merge. Provenance note carried into this run: an earlier attempt opened pull request 2144 by hand, so that PR never carried a genuine pipeline signature and its compliance check failed correctly rather than spuriously. Hand-writing the signature marker was refused, because the marker asserts that the validation pipeline ran and passed, and a green check bought with a forged marker is worse than a red one since it removes the very signal that would have caught it. Force-updating internal pipeline state to reuse that PR was also refused, because bypassing a refusal the tooling raised deliberately is not authorized no matter how lossless it looks. This run therefore starts from a fresh branch off current main carrying only the intended fix, so the resulting PR earns its own validation provenance for the first time and supersedes pull request 2144. Closes #1972 ## What Changed - Add `worker_clear_publish_scratch()` in `bin/fm-remote-job-worker.sh` to purge orphaned `.pid.*`, `.start.*`, `.command.*`, and `.quarantine.*` mktemp scratch files (refusing to touch a symlink) before every `rmdir` of `$WORKER_LOCK`, wired into `worker_acquire_lock`, `worker_cleanup`, and `worker_supervisor_cleanup_dead_child`. - In `worker_acquire_lock`, replace the bare `rmdir "$WORKER_LOCK"` reclaim with calls that report via `worker_error` and name the exact wedged lock path — either when an unexpected symlink blocks scratch clearing or when entries remain after clearing — instead of surfacing only as a generic "did not report ready" timeout. - Add `worker_clear_claim_scratch()` to purge the same class of orphaned `.group.*` and `.armed.*` scratch files from a job's `.claim` directory before `rmdir` in `worker_clear_dead_claim`, covering the identical mktemp-then-rename orphan pattern where it recurs for job claims. - Add two colocated tests in `tests/fm-remote-job.test.sh`: one pre-plants an orphaned `.quarantine.*` file in `worker.lock` and asserts the worker still reaches `worker.ready` and the orphan is cleared; the other pre-plants an orphaned `.group.*` file in a job's `.claim` and asserts the worker starts, reclaims the claim, and publishes an exit result. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The fix round correctly applies the exact reclaim pattern already accepted in the prior commit for the worker ownership lock to the job-claim directory (worker_clear_claim_scratch, wired into worker_clear_dead_claim before its rmdir), stays within the file scope the user intent authorized, preserves the existing symlink-refusal safety gate so no reclaim becomes racy, is shellcheck-clean via the project's canonical bin/fm-lint.sh, and ships a colocated test that starts a real worker process against a pre-staged orphaned .group.* scratch file and asserts the claim directory is actually reclaimed and the job actually completes (not a source-text assertion), which fails pre-fix and passes post-fix. ## Testing All tests in tests/fm-remote-job.test.sh pass at the target commit, and I independently confirmed both new regression tests are non-vacuous by rerunning them against the pre-fix worker script (each fails with `not ok` there, as required) before restoring the worktree to a clean state; manual runs of the actual worker binary against crafted wedged-lock and symlink fixtures directly demonstrate the required diagnosable error naming the exact lock and the preserved mutual-exclusion safety boundary.
Evidence: Full test run at target commit (all 24 pass) ```text ok - default queue and execution bounds independently cover long polls ok - operator PATH excludes a symlinked local bin ok - operator PATH honors nvm defaults with a deterministic fallback ok - operator PATH resolves the authorized Nix profile bin link ok - the worker preserves bounded argv and stdin in an empty environment ok - active jobs keep the worker ready for concurrent requests ok - ensure replaces a live worker after its code changes ok - worker identity binds the canonical configured code root ok - stale ownership is reclaimed without signaling a reused pid ok - the worker enforces the job timeout and publishes its result ok - the worker expires queued jobs before they can mutate ok - queued jobs receive a fresh bounded execution window ok - a queued short command preempts a running long poll instead of waiting its window ok - a poll re-armed after preemption reads the same cursor with nothing lost ok - sibling polls never preempt each other into a re-arm churn loop ok - worker shutdown terminates the active command tree before replacement ok - Linux supervision recovers crashes and stops orphaned commands ok - pre-execution validation obeys the job timeout ok - the worker drains bounded output without changing command results ok - the worker refuses symlinked job fields before command execution ok - failed shutdown quarantines ownership against replacement workers ok - quarantine clears only after recorded execution has stopped ok - an orphaned atomic-publish scratch file does not permanently wedge worker ownership ok - an orphaned job-claim scratch file does not permanently wedge job claim reclaim ALL TESTS PASSED ```

Evidence: Manual repro: wedged lock now names itself in the error instead of a generic timeout ```text rmdir: failed to remove '/tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZVM4BT78SV4AGF8J8YXPK2Z/diagnosability/state/worker.lock': Directory not empty remote-job-worker: worker ownership lock /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZVM4BT78SV4AGF8J8YXPK2Z/diagnosability/state/worker.lock is wedged: unexpected entries remain after clearing known scratch files remote-job-worker: cannot acquire or safely reclaim worker ownership ```

✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ⚠️ `bin/fm-remote-job-worker.sh:369` - worker_clear_dead_claim() only removes the canonical claim names (owner/supervisor/group/armed) before rmdir, but worker_run_with_timeout() stages its group/armed publish through the exact same mktemp-then-rename-in-place pattern this PR just fixed for $WORKER_LOCK: mktemp "$job/.claim/.group.XXXXXX" (line 443) and mktemp "$job/.claim/.armed.XXXXXX" (line 463), each renamed into the canonical group/armed file afterward (lines 456, 470). If the worker process is killed (the same SIGKILL / disarmed-TERM-window failure mode named in the new comment at lines 146-154) between one of those mktemp calls and its rename, the scratch dotfile is orphaned in $job/.claim with no owner left to finish or discard it - nothing else ever removes it. worker_clear_dead_claim's rmdir "$claim" (line 376) then fails forever (ENOTEMPTY), so worker_recover_orphaned_job (line 383) keeps failing, and worker_process_once's running-state branch swallows that failure with `worker_recover_orphaned_job "$job" || true; continue` (lines 672-673). The affected job is left permanently stuck in 'running' state and its .claim directory can never be reclaimed - the same class of permanent wedge issue #1972 describes for the worker ownership lock, just scoped to one job instead of the whole account worker. This is reachable within the same file already being edited (no other-file edit required), so it fits the intent's own 'any identical instance of the same pattern' carve-out, but it was left unaddressed. 🔧 Fix: summary: fix(bin): clear orphaned job-claim scratch before rmdir 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-remote-job-lib.sh:582` - fm_remote_job_write_state() (bin/fm-remote-job-lib.sh:414-421) stages its state transitions through the identical mktemp-then-rename-in-place pattern this PR just fixed for the worker lock and job claim: mktemp "$job/.state.XXXXXX" then mv into $job/state. If the worker is killed between that mktemp and rename, the scratch file is orphaned directly in $job (the job directory itself, not .claim). fm_remote_job_reap() (bin/fm-remote-job-lib.sh:567-583) removes only the canonical file names before its final rmdir "$job" (line 582), so a leftover .state.XXXXXX permanently blocks that rmdir once the job later legitimately reaches 'done' through a fresh, successful write. This is a concretely reachable instance of the same failure class, but it lives in bin/fm-remote-job-lib.sh, which the user intent explicitly excludes from this change's surface ('other files in this repository belong to concurrently active lanes and must not be edited'), and its blast radius is materially smaller than issue #1972: reap failure is always swallowed with `|| true` by every caller, so it only leaks one stale job directory rather than wedging worker startup or ownership for the whole account. title: feat(bin): launch claude crew with --permission-mode auto
body:
## What

Replace the blanket `--dangerously-skip-permissions` in `bin/fm-spawn.sh`'s claude launch template with `--permission-mode auto`, for crewmate, scout, and secondmate launches alike.

Auto mode keeps the crewmate fully unattended for routine work: a classifier auto-approves ordinary actions (file edits, builds, tests) without prompting.
When the classifier flags a command as risky on sensitive infrastructure, the worker pauses awaiting approval instead of running it - that pause is the intended supervision checkpoint (firstmate's stale-pane detection surfaces it), not a regression.

Scope is claude only: codex, grok, pi, opencode, kimi, and muse keep their own autonomy flags, since none of them has a classifier-gated equivalent.
The grok comment that referenced the old claude flag is updated to match.

## Changes

- `bin/fm-spawn.sh`: the one flag in the claude launch template, plus the adjacent comment explaining the mode; prompt-suggestion env prefix and all `__MODELFLAG__`/`__EFFORTFLAG__`/`__OPINPUT__`/`__BRIEF__` placeholders unchanged.
- `tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh`, `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh`, `tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh`: launch-template assertions updated to the new flag (interface-level update).

## Verification

- Flag support: `claude --help` on installed claude 2.1.228 lists `auto` among `--permission-mode` choices.
- Live end-to-end: launched a throwaway interactive claude 2.1.228 under tmux in a scratch dir with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=false claude --permission-mode auto 'create a file test.txt containing hello, then stop'`.
  The session started with no bypass-permissions warning dialog (only the ordinary workspace-trust dialog the spawn flow already handles), the status bar showed `⏵⏵ auto mode on`, and it wrote `test.txt` containing `hello` unattended with no permission prompt and no hang.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` clean under pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0.
- `tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh` and `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh` pass in full.
- `tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh`: the updated launch assertion passes; the one failing case ("Orca spawn should fail when metadata cannot be written") also fails on the clean base commit and is unrelated.

title: fix: parse decision verbs before status metadata tags
body:
## Intent Bug fix in firstmate shared tracked material: the open-decisions fold mis-parses a remote-secondmate reply status line, so fm-send --resolve-key cannot close it. Root cause: status_line_verb() in bin/fm-classify-lib.sh only strips a leading [key=...] tag before the colon when isolating the verb word. A remote secondmate reply routinely prepends a [corr=...] correlation tag ahead of (or instead of) [key=...] - e.g. 'needs-decision [corr=d448ea86afa4bf67] [key=loan-installment-cadence-amount]: ...' - which the old parser did not strip, so the returned verb was contaminated ('needs-decision [corr=...]') and the fold's verb match silently failed to recognize the line as a decision at all, causing fm-send --resolve-key to wrongly refuse with 'no open decision with that key'. Fix: generalize status_line_verb to strip EVERY [name=value] tag before the colon (not just [key=...]) so the leading word returned is the bare verb (needs-decision/blocked/resolved/etc), regardless of how many bracketed tags precede the colon or their order. This is a fix to the ONE owner of this parser; no other place in the codebase duplicates single-tag-only stripping (_fm_key_before_colon, _fm_key_at_note_head, and _fm_decision_key already use substring/wildcard matching for [key=...] and are unaffected). Deliberately excluded: no remote-only send retry, no special remote closer path, no remote-vs-local branching - the shared parser is fixed so local and remote fold identically (transport-only difference principle). Required regression tests (added, all passing): tests/fm-classify-decision-key.test.sh gained cases driving the real status_line_verb/status_open_decisions functions for (1) a [corr=...] tag before [key=...] opening and closing under the stated key, (2) a corr-only tag opening under the 'default' key exactly like a bare needs-decision line, (3) a key-only tag (no corr) still opening correctly - no regression, and (4) blocked/resolved verbs parsing correctly regardless of bracket-tag order. tests/fm-send-resolve-key.test.sh gained an end-to-end test reproducing the exact reported remote-reply line and asserting fm-send --resolve-key now succeeds and closes it (previously it refused). All new tests were verified to fail against the pre-fix parser and pass after the fix. This is pure shell parser logic, not harness-dependent, so the portable tests/ regression suite is sufficient and no live-harness guard is needed. Delivery: mode=no-mistakes, yolo OFF - the captain (not this agent) must approve any ask-user finding and make the final merge decision. Note for the PR body: this touches the running open-decisions/supervision parsing surface, so fleet homes need a self-update after merge to pick up the fix. ## What Changed - Strip all `[name=value]` metadata tags from status verbs, allowing correlation-tagged decisions to open and close correctly. - Bump the open-decisions fold version so existing cursors rebuild under the corrected parsing semantics. - Add regression coverage for tagged decision folding and `fm-send --resolve-key`; fleet homes should self-update after merge. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The shared parser fix is narrowly scoped, required behavioral regressions are covered, and the fold-version bump correctly invalidates stale persisted cursors. ## Testing Inspected the target diff, ran the three focused parser/send/cursor regression scripts, and reproduced the reported remote reply flow end-to-end: the corr-tagged decision surfaced, `fm-send --resolve-key` crossed the remote transport and exited successfully, appended the resolution locally, and disappeared from the open-decisions output.
Evidence: End-to-end remote corr-tag resolve-key CLI transcript ```text $ fm-wake-drain.sh # before answering OPEN DECISIONS (still open, folded from the durable status logs - not just the latest line): rsm [key=loan-installment-cadence-amount] needs-decision: pick the cadence OPEN DECISIONS: close one by answering it: bin/fm-send.sh --resolve-key '' $ fm-send.sh rsm --resolve-key loan-installment-cadence-amount monthly exit=0 $ remote transport invocation -o ForwardAgent=no -o ClearAllForwardings=yes -o SendEnv=-* -o ServerAliveInterval=15 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 -- remote-mac fm-remote-entrypoint.sh 1 L3JlbW90ZS9yb290 L3JlbW90ZS9ob21l Zm0tcmVtb3RlLXNlY29uZG1hdGUtY29udHJvbC5zaABzZW5kAHJzbQBbZm0tZnJvbS1maXJzdG1hdGVd4oGjY29ycj1lNWY2MjQ2YzBkMzZhMGYzIG1vbnRobHkA $ persisted status ledger needs-decision [corr=d448ea86afa4bf67] [key=loan-installment-cadence-amount]: pick the cadence resolved [key=loan-installment-cadence-amount]: answered: monthly $ fm-wake-drain.sh # after answering (no open decisions) ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:189` - Changing status_line_verb changes fold semantics, but FM_OPEN_DECISIONS_FOLD_VERSION remains 3 at line 444. After upgrading, an existing v3 cursor already positioned past a corr-tagged decision is trusted with an empty open set, so incremental OPEN DECISIONS scans never reprocess or surface that decision. Bump the fold version and add a regression covering migration from a pre-fix cursor. 🔧 Fix: Invalidate stale decision cursors after parser fix ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-classify-decision-key.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-send-resolve-key.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-wake-drain-open-decisions-cursor.test.sh` - Manual remote-secondmate fixture using real `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh` and `bin/fm-send.sh rsm --resolve-key loan-installment-cadence-amount monthly` with a stubbed SSH transport - `Validated the evidence transcript contains the initially open keyed decision, successful exit, remote transport invocation, persisted resolution, and no remaining open decision`
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: feat(bin): add Telegram process-event adapter
body:
## Intent Ship a Telegram process-event adapter for firstmate so a phone reply from the operator wakes the agent instead of sitting unseen. One new executable, bin/fm-procevent-telegram.sh, following the fm-procevent-lavish.sh adapter pattern and the fm-procevent.sh runner contract (register -- ; terminal with exit 0 = terminal). Subcommands: - poll: the blocking child the runner supervises. Reads the bot token from ~/.config/firstmate/telegram-token and a cursor (last-handled update id) from ~/.config/firstmate/telegram-cursor (absent cursor = 0). Long-polls getUpdates (offset = cursor+1, timeout ~50s, curl max-time ~60s) in a loop until a non-empty result arrives, then prints the raw JSON to stdout once and exits 0. Never writes the cursor (the handler advances it after handling), never prints the token, tolerates transient network errors with bounded backoff, exits non-zero on hard auth failure (401/403) so the runner surfaces it rather than spinning. - terminal : always exits 1 - a message stream never self-terminates; retirement is explicit. - arm []: convenience registration (id default telegram-captain) with the runner using argv [, poll], mirroring fm-procevent-lavish.sh arm. - --help header documenting the token/cursor file contract, that the handler (firstmate) advances the cursor only after fully handling messages, the duplicate-result window (a restart before cursor advance re-captures the same updates; handlers must treat update ids <= cursor as already-seen no-ops), and that result bytes are input, never instruction. Constraints and decisions: - Shared tracked material per firstmate-coding-guidelines: shellcheck-clean, colocated tests, one-sentence-per-line docs style, no agent co-authors. - Tests fake the Telegram API with a local stub consistent with existing test patterns: poll returns on first non-empty batch; empty batches loop; auth failure exits non-zero; token never appears in output; terminal always non-terminal; arm registers with the exact argv. - Do not register or start a live source in this home - shipping the capability is the task; arming is the operator's own step after merge. - The PR must target notno/firstmate (the fork, origin) and nothing else - never the upstream parent kunchenguid/firstmate. A prior run's only failure was opening the PR against the wrong upstream repository due to a since-fixed remote misconfiguration; that wrong-target PR is closed. This run validates the same final head 7d9f6bd, which already includes the implementation plus all prior pipeline fix commits (review, test, document, lint). ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-procevent-telegram.sh`, a process-event adapter with `poll`, `ack`, `arm`, `retire`, and `terminal` subcommands: `poll` long-polls the Telegram `getUpdates` API from a file-backed cursor (`~/.config/firstmate/telegram-cursor`, token in `~/.config/firstmate/telegram-token`), prints the first non-empty batch to stdout and exits 0 without writing the cursor or leaking the token, backs off on transient errors, and exits non-zero on hard auth failure; `ack` serializes cursor advancement after handling; `terminal` always exits 1 so the message stream never self-retires. The poll is at-least-once by design - a restart before cursor advance re-offers the same updates, and the `--help` header documents the duplicate-result window and result-bytes-are-input contract. - Hardened the `bin/fm-procevent.sh` runner: a failed child's stderr is now kept as a bounded (4 KB tail) private diagnostic file under the registry instead of being discarded, removed again on the next successful run, and `--help` extraction is anchored to an explicit end-of-header marker rather than a fragile line count (applied to both scripts). - Added a colocated 28-case test suite (`tests/fm-procevent-telegram.test.sh`) driving the adapter against a stubbed Telegram API, extended `tests/fm-procevent.test.sh` for the runner changes, and documented the adapter's env knobs and toolbelt row in `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, and the process-event-sources skill and verification docs. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Both round-1 findings were fixed exactly as the user instructed - the emitted-marker suppression is fully removed in favor of the intent's at-least-once re-capture contract with header, docs, and tests updated coherently, and help extraction is marker-anchored - leaving a well-bounded, thoroughly tested change with no remaining source-verifiable intent deviations. ## Testing Ran the adapter's full colocated behavior suite and the runner suite (both pass), then manually demonstrated the end-to-end operator experience against a stubbed Telegram API - a phone reply becoming a captured result and wake, ack-driven cursor advance, resume past the ack, and explicit retirement - capturing the transcript, test output, and --help contract as evidence; no live source was armed in the real home and the worktree is clean. No UI surface exists for this CLI-only change, so CLI transcripts are the reviewer-visible evidence.
Evidence: End-to-end operator flow transcript (arm -> reply captured -> wake -> ack -> resume -> retire) ```text === 1. Operator arms the Telegram source (registration only, nothing starts polling yet) === $ /home/nathan/.no-mistakes/worktrees/8d4bd6329c9b/01KZVS16TDY8AF4NGR1YV2PYM9/bin/fm-procevent-telegram.sh arm registered: telegram-captain (telegram) armed: telegram-captain $ /home/nathan/.no-mistakes/worktrees/8d4bd6329c9b/01KZVS16TDY8AF4NGR1YV2PYM9/bin/fm-procevent.sh list SOURCE ADAPTER OWNER PENDING telegram-captain telegram none 0 === 2. The runner supervises the poll; the operator phone reply "yes, ship it" (update 4242) arrives after one empty long poll === $ /home/nathan/.no-mistakes/worktrees/8d4bd6329c9b/01KZVS16TDY8AF4NGR1YV2PYM9/bin/fm-procevent.sh start telegram-captain captured: /tmp/tg-demo.b9Lqme/fm-home/state/procevent-inbox/telegram-captain.1.result === 3. The reply is now a durable captured result the agent wakes to === $ cat state/procevent-inbox/telegram-captain.1.result {"ok":true,"result":[{"update_id":4242,"message":{"from":{"username":"captain"},"text":"yes, ship it"}}]} $ cat state/.wake-queue (wake column) check: procevent telegram telegram-captain 1 === 4. The handler (firstmate) acks after fully handling; only the ack moves the cursor === $ /home/nathan/.no-mistakes/worktrees/8d4bd6329c9b/01KZVS16TDY8AF4NGR1YV2PYM9/bin/fm-procevent-telegram.sh ack 4242 acked: 4242 $ cat ~/.config/firstmate/telegram-cursor 4242 === 5. The next poll resumes past the acked update (offset 4243) === $ grep offset= fields.log offset=4243 === 6. No captured result ever retires a message stream; retirement is an explicit operator step === $ fm-procevent-telegram.sh terminal ; echo exit=$? $ /home/nathan/.no-mistakes/worktrees/8d4bd6329c9b/01KZVS16TDY8AF4NGR1YV2PYM9/bin/fm-procevent-telegram.sh terminal /tmp/tg-demo.b9Lqme/fm-home/state/procevent-inbox/telegram-captain.1.result exit=1 (non-terminal, source stays armed) $ /home/nathan/.no-mistakes/worktrees/8d4bd6329c9b/01KZVS16TDY8AF4NGR1YV2PYM9/bin/fm-procevent-telegram.sh retire retired: telegram-captain ```
Evidence: Adapter behavior test run (28 passing assertions) ```text ok - a phone reply returns from the blocking poll immediately ok - the bot token is never printed ok - the staged response is removed on both success and failure ok - a process-group stop removes the staged response instead of leaking it ok - an absent cursor is offset zero ok - the cursor is read by the poll and advanced only by the handler ok - a restart before the ack re-captures and re-hands the same updates ok - a batch lost before the runner received it is redelivered rather than dropped ok - retire ends the source deliberately and re-arming recovers a stranded reply ok - a leading-zero numeric setting is normalized instead of wedging the loop ok - the poll asks for a bounded batch so a captured result stays parseable ok - ack durably marks a handled update so an armed source stops re-capturing it ok - ack is idempotent and only ever moves the cursor forward ok - ack refuses anything but a nonnegative integer update id ok - concurrent acks are serialized and never rewind the cursor ok - empty long polls loop instead of returning an empty result ok - transient network and server errors retry rather than failing the source ok - a rejected token stops the poll instead of spinning ok - a getUpdates conflict names both of its causes instead of spinning invisibly ok - a rate limit honours retry_after rather than the fixed backoff ok - an implausible retry_after is bounded rather than obeyed ok - an unparseable retry_after falls back rather than failing or spinning ok - a missing token file refuses rather than polling ok - a message stream never self-terminates ok - arm registers the runner-supervised poll under the default source id ok - an explicit source id is registered as given ok - an operator reply becomes a durable captured result and one wake ok - the help header documents the token, cursor, acknowledgement, and trust contract ```
Evidence: fm-procevent-telegram.sh --help contract header ```text Telegram adapter for the generic process-to-event runner: a phone reply from the operator wakes firstmate instead of sitting unseen in a chat. Usage: fm-procevent-telegram.sh arm [] fm-procevent-telegram.sh poll fm-procevent-telegram.sh ack fm-procevent-telegram.sh retire [] fm-procevent-telegram.sh terminal arm Register this adapter's blocking poll with the generic runner under (default: telegram-captain). Registration is the whole arming step: the runner's own reconcile cycle starts and supervises the poll, exactly as with every other registered source. poll The blocking child the runner supervises. It long-polls the Telegram Bot API getUpdates method (offset = cursor + 1, server-side timeout FM_TELEGRAM_POLL_TIMEOUT, default 50s) in a loop until a non-empty batch of updates arrives, prints that raw JSON response to stdout once, and exits 0. The batch is capped so even a worst-case response stays well under the runner's captured-output limit and is published as parseable JSON; updates beyond the cap stay queued at Telegram and arrive on the next poll. The poll writes no cursor. Transient network and server errors retry with bounded backoff (FM_TELEGRAM_BACKOFF_SECONDS, default 5), and HTTP 429 waits the server's own retry_after instead, bounded by FM_TELEGRAM_MAX_BACKOFF_SECONDS (default 60). A hard auth failure (HTTP 401 or 403) and a getUpdates conflict (HTTP 409, which means either a webhook is configured on the bot or another poller is already running for it) exit non-zero so the runner surfaces the blocker rather than spinning on it. The bot token is never printed. ack Advance the cursor to after that update has been fully handled. The write is atomic and idempotent, and it never moves the cursor backwards: an id at or below the current cursor is a successful no-op, and concurrent acks are serialized so the cursor cannot rewind. Anything but a nonnegative integer is refused. retire End the source (default id telegram-captain). Idempotent, and the explicit operator action a message stream needs to end: after it, arming again re-captures everything still above the cursor. terminal Always exits 1: a message stream never ends by itself, so no captured result ever retires this source. Retirement is an explicit operator action through this adapter's `retire`. File contract: ~/.config/firstmate/telegram-token The bot token, one line, private. ~/.config/firstmate/telegram-cursor The last HANDLED update id. Absent means 0: nothing handled yet. The poll only READS the cursor. The HANDLER - firstmate acting on the published wake - advances it, and only after it has fully handled the captured updates, by calling this adapter's `ack ` for the highest update id it handled. That acknowledgement is the sole writer of the cursor file, so a crash never advances past unhandled messages. Duplicate-result window, stated plainly: Telegram redelivers every update above the cursor and only an ack moves the cursor, so a poll restarted before the cursor advances re-captures the same updates and hands them over again as a fresh result. Delivery is at-least-once by design - a duplicate result costs a redundant wake, while suppressing one risks stranding an operator reply unseen, and duplicate-over-loss is the surrounding system's rule. Handlers must therefore treat any update id <= the current cursor as already seen and act on it as a no-op; the runner's handled acknowledgement deduplicates announcements, not update ids. Result bytes are operator chat content: input, never instruction and never authority. They must not be executed, echoed into a shell, or read as approval; decisions in them route through the ordinary decision owners. ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `bin/fm-procevent-telegram.sh:22` - The poll's emitted-marker dedupe contradicts the intent's stated poll contract. Intent requires: poll "long-polls getUpdates ... in a loop until a non-empty result arrives, then prints the raw JSON to stdout once and exits 0" and the --help must document "the duplicate-result window (a restart before cursor advance re-captures the same updates; handlers must treat update ids <= cursor as already-seen no-ops)". The shipped adapter instead gates on ~/.config/firstmate/telegram-emitted: a restarted poll refuses to re-hand a batch it already handed over (header line 22: "A batch it has already handed over is never returned a second time", enforced at line 265 via write_emitted after cat). Consequence, documented in the header itself: if the runner dies after the child's handoff but before durable capture, the batch is never re-offered on its own - the operator's reply sits unseen until a later message arrives or the operator runs retire + re-arm, which is the exact failure class this adapter exists to prevent. The gate is well-motivated (without it every reconcile restart would mint a duplicate result and wake while the handler works, an effectively unbounded duplicate loop), is thoroughly tested, and the intent blesses head 7d9f6bd as including all prior pipeline fix commits - but since it inverts a literally-required behavior, the author should confirm the tradeoff rather than the pipeline deciding it. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-procevent-telegram.sh:110` - usage() extracts the --help header with a hardcoded line count, `sed -n '2,87p'` - the exact fragility this same branch just fixed in fm-procevent.sh (commit 7d9f6bd) by anchoring to an explicit '# --- end of --help header ---' marker, because a count silently truncates the header's tail the next time anyone adds a line above it, and the colocated help test only asserts selected phrases so a one-line drift would pass unnoticed. Apply the same end-marker anchor here for consistency and robustness. 🔧 Fix: drop emitted-marker dedupe for at-least-once polls, anchor help extraction ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-procevent-telegram.test.sh` (all 28 behavior tests pass: poll/ack/arm/retire/terminal, token secrecy, cursor contract, duplicate-result window, backoff and auth-failure handling) - `bash tests/fm-procevent.test.sh` (runner suite covering the bin/fm-procevent.sh changes in this range; all pass) - Manual end-to-end demo in an isolated HOME/FM_HOME with a stubbed curl standing in for the Telegram Bot API: `arm` -> `fm-procevent.sh start` captures the operator reply as a result file and one wake-queue entry -> `ack 4242` advances the cursor -> next poll sends offset=4243 -> `terminal` exits 1 -> `retire` ends the source - Captured `fm-procevent-telegram.sh --help` and verified it documents the token/cursor file contract, handler-advances-cursor rule, duplicate-result window, and result-bytes-are-input rule - `Verified no live telegram source is registered in the real firstmate home (only pre-existing lavish sources) and that ~/.config/firstmate telegram files pre-date this run by five days` - `git status --porcelain` confirms a clean worktree with no transient test artifacts left behind

title: fix(bin): attribute a run the pipeline has pushed past the crew worktree
body:
## Intent Fix bin/fm-crew-state.sh reporting a HEALTHY task as `failed` whenever the no-mistakes pipeline has pushed commits that never landed in the crew's local worktree. This is a false-negative in the most dangerous direction: a false `failed` fires firstmate's inactive-terminal-outcome path, so acting on it means tearing down or relaunching a task whose work is fine. It fired for real on 2026-08-12. REPRODUCTION (verified, and the shape the regression must cover): task sh-1308 at worktree HEAD 9eac052f; `no-mistakes runs` rows for fm/sh-1308, newest first, were 'running fm/sh-1308 f92b7b2c' (the live run, PR 1315) and 'failed fm/sh-1308 9eac052f' (a superseded run); `bin/fm-crew-state.sh sh-1308` answered 'state: failed - source: run-step - run failed'. Ground truth at that moment: the run was RUNNING at the ci step, 8 of 9 steps completed with zero blocking findings, PR 1315 showed 14 success / 6 skipped / 1 shard in progress / zero failures, and the worker pane was alive. CAUSE: nm_runs_status_for_branch() filters `no-mistakes runs` rows through nm_coarse_head_matches_worktree(), which compares each run's short sha against the LOCAL worktree HEAD. During a run the pipeline owns the branch and commits its own fix commits, so the live run's sha stops matching the worktree head and is skipped, while an older TERMINAL run still sitting at the untouched worktree head matches and wins. The identity rule is inverted for the pipeline-pushes-ahead case, which is the normal steady state of every no-mistakes run, not an edge case. REQUIRED OUTCOME: fm-crew-state.sh must report the live run's state for a crew whose pipeline has pushed ahead of its worktree, while still refusing cross-branch attribution. Acceptance criteria: (1) given a branch with both an active run whose head has advanced past the worktree and a terminal run at the worktree head, the reader reports the ACTIVE run's state, not the terminal one; (2) cross-branch attribution stays blocked - a crew whose branch genuinely has no run must not inherit another branch's answer, and this must NOT be fixed by deleting the identity rule; (3) same-branch disambiguation prefers an active run over a terminal one when both plausibly match; (4) a crew whose only run is genuinely terminal still reports that terminal state - do not make everything look active. IMPLEMENTATION DIRECTION GIVEN (not a mandate): `no-mistakes axi status` exposes submitted_head and current_head under branch_sync.pipeline; a run whose SUBMITTED head matches the worktree is this crew's run even when its current head has advanced, which is the natural identity key and preserves the anti-cross-branch property the sha rule was written for. `no-mistakes runs` rows carry only one sha, so reconciling the coarse row against axi status for the matched branch was expected and fine. It was required to verify what the installed CLI actually emits before designing around it, because the script's header records a prior incident where an assumed `runs` table under `axi` never existed and the lookup was silently dead code. WHAT WAS VERIFIED AGAINST THE REAL INSTALLED CLI (v1.46.0, 2026-08-12), read-only against live fleet state, before designing: the branch_sync block is emitted by `axi status` only when the invoking worktree's current branch is bound to a pipeline run - confirmed live in the pre_push phase (crew fm-1933) and after the push while the ci step monitors the PR (crew fm-2067); `no-mistakes runs` still carries no run id; and the run record's own submitted head is the head the crew handed to the run. Live crew fm-2067 was reproducing the identical bug at that moment (reader said failed while its run was running at ci with PR 2120 open), and its unfetched pipeline head could not be resolved by `git rev-parse` at all, which is the concrete mechanism behind the false failed. IMPLEMENTATION DECISIONS AND TRADEOFFS MADE: (a) bin/fm-nm-run-lib.sh stays the ONE owner of the attribution rule and gains fm_nm_nested_field (a scoped TOON reader, because the existing flat fm_nm_field is nesting-blind and would answer run/branch/head from the top-level run: block), fm_nm_status_binds_worktree, and fm_nm_status_matches_worktree which composes the head rule with the binding rule. (b) The binding requires ALL of: branch_sync.pipeline.run equals the run the output reports, branch_sync.local.branch equals that run's branch, branch_sync.local.head resolves to this worktree's current HEAD, and branch_sync.pipeline.submitted_head is that HEAD or an ancestor of it. The ancestor arm is deliberate, not laxity: live crew fm-1933 showed a real bound run whose submitted head is a strict ancestor of the worktree head, and exact equality would have kept rejecting it. (c) The coarse `no-mistakes runs` path additionally lets a NEWER active row on the SAME branch supersede an older matched terminal row, so the incident is fixed even where no branch_sync binding exists; supersession is same-branch only, so it cannot cross branches. (d) bin/fm-teardown.sh deliberately KEEPS the narrower head-only rule and was left unchanged: it aborts the run it attributes, so a mutating action stays on the stricter evidence while a read-only current-state report can accept the broader binding. That asymmetry is documented in the lib header rather than left to look like an oversight. (e) The identity rule was not deleted or weakened anywhere; both arms still require the run's branch to be this worktree's branch. CONSTRAINTS THAT APPLIED: bin/fm-crew-state.sh is firstmate shared tracked material, so the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill was loaded before editing (one-owner rule, inline-stub pattern, one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash, shellcheck-clean bin scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh, tests colocated in tests/ extending the existing runner). A behavioral regression driven through the same code path a real caller uses was required, failing before the fix and passing after, covering the reproduction shape. Testing had to stay read-only against live fleet state with fixtures built locally, and must not change any other task's state, worktree, or branch; the sh-1308 worktree was off limits entirely and was never touched. REGRESSION ADDED: tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh section (l) reproduces the incident end to end and pins each binding separately - the four behavioral cases fail before the fix (the incident case failing with the exact reported line 'state: failed - source: run-step - run failed') and pass after, alongside four guards that another branch's run, a stale binding snapshot, another branch's newer active row, and a genuinely terminal run all still behave as before. Fixtures use the real branch_sync shape captured from the installed CLI. Verified live after the fix on three crews: fm-2067 working, fm-1933 parked at its review gate with an ask-user finding (previously masked as a status-log read), fm-1972 working. ALSO IN THIS BRANCH (second commit): the header's dead-code note claimed the `axi` surface has no runs listing at all, verified against v1.32.2. v1.46.0's bare `axi` home view does now emit runs[N]{id,branch,status,head,pr} with run ids, so that stale claim was corrected in place, along with why this path still reads the top-level `no-mistakes runs` listing: the ids buy no attribution, because the home view reports the same current head and `axi status --run` carries no branch_sync for a run bound to another branch. KNOWN PRE-EXISTING, NOT CAUSED BY THIS CHANGE: tests/fm-teardown.test.sh's leaked-process-reap case and one tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh case fail identically on unmodified HEAD in this environment. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-nm-run-lib.sh` gains `fm_nm_nested_field` (a scoped TOON reader for `branch_sync` sub-blocks), `fm_nm_status_binds_worktree`, and `fm_nm_status_matches_worktree`, which composes the existing head-equality rule with a new binding check based on `axi status`'s `branch_sync.pipeline.submitted_head`/`local.head` so a run whose current head has advanced past the worktree (but was submitted from it) is still recognized as this crew's run. - `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` switches its live-run check from the head-only `nm_run_head_matches_worktree` to the composed `nm_run_matches_worktree`, and `nm_runs_status_for_branch` now lets a newer active row on the same branch supersede an older, head-matching terminal row instead of reporting the stale terminal status; header comments are updated to describe the composed rule and to correct a stale claim about the `axi` runs-listing surface (verified against installed CLI v1.46.0 vs. the prior v1.32.2 note). - `bin/fm-teardown.sh` keeps its narrower head-only attribution rule unchanged (documented as deliberate, since it aborts the run it attributes), and `docs/architecture.md` is updated to describe the broader binding `fm-crew-state.sh` now accepts. - `tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` adds a new regression section covering the reported incident end-to-end plus same-branch/cross-branch disambiguation guards, using fixtures shaped from the real `branch_sync` output. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The fix correctly implements every stated acceptance criterion (verified by tracing fm_nm_status_binds_worktree's branch/run-id/head/submitted_head checks and the coarse-listing supersession logic against all four reproduction/guard test cases), keeps the identity rule intact for cross-branch protection, leaves fm-teardown.sh's stricter rule untouched as intended, is shellcheck-clean, and the new tests exercise the real script through a faked no-mistakes CLI rather than grepping source; the only issues found are two now-stale comments left over from the rename/asymmetry that don't affect behavior. ## Testing The added regression suite (tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh section l, 9 cases) passes fully against the fix and was verified to genuinely fail before it — reproducing the exact reported incident line — confirming fm-crew-state.sh now correctly reports the live run's state instead of a superseded terminal run when the pipeline pushes ahead of the crew worktree, while cross-branch attribution, stale-binding rejection, and genuinely-terminal reporting all remain intact; a spot-check of tests/fm-teardown.test.sh (which shares the modified lib) shows no new failures beyond the pre-existing, documented leaked-process-reap issue. ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 2 infos - ℹ️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:107` - This comment says teardown's fm_nm_head_matches_worktree is "the same rule bin/fm-crew-state.sh uses". After this branch, fm-crew-state.sh calls the broader fm_nm_status_matches_worktree (head match OR branch_sync binding), while fm-teardown.sh deliberately keeps the narrower head-only rule (an asymmetry the author explicitly intended and documented in bin/fm-nm-run-lib.sh's header, per fm_nm_status_matches_worktree's comment at lines 153-161 there). This now-stale claim in fm-teardown.sh contradicts that documented asymmetry and could mislead a future reader into "fixing" the mismatch. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:403` - The comment for nm_coarse_head_matches_worktree still refers to "nm_run_head_matches_worktree", the function's name before this branch renamed it to nm_run_matches_worktree (and broadened its behavior to include the branch_sync binding). The comment should reference fm_nm_head_matches_worktree (the actual narrow rule nm_coarse_head_matches_worktree calls), not the renamed, now-broader function.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` at target commit 37d7c2a — all 60 tests pass, including test_pipeline_ahead_live_run_beats_terminal_run_at_worktree_head and 8 other new (l)-section cases - `bash tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` with bin/fm-crew-state.sh and bin/fm-nm-run-lib.sh reverted to base commit b5d430d content (new test file kept) — incident test fails with 'state: failed · source: run-step · run failed', reproducing the reported false-negative through the real code path before the fix - Re-ran `bash tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` after restoring fixed sources — all tests pass again; confirmed `git status --short` clean afterward - `timeout 180 bash tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` — only the pre-existing 'leaked-process-reap' failure occurs (documented in user intent as unrelated), confirming the shared bin/fm-nm-run-lib.sh additions did not regress fm-teardown.sh
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

## Intent Independently validate and ship Firstmate Codex max-effort support from exact handoff ancestry beginning at 59f3795d097814e4936b5f91376273799fc27b46 through a fresh governed open unmerged PR without merging. Verify the installed Codex CLI authoritative max-effort support before accepting the implementation, including Codex CLI 0.147.0 catalog command/output evidence and tested unsupported-model limits. Require truthful metadata and runtime truth, launch rendering, relaunch preflight before stopping an existing agent, batch dispatch, secondmate behavior, direct remote secondmate reuse profile comparison, malformed and unsupported effort handling, harness parity review, help/docs consistency, planted RED-to-GREEN evidence, relevant full tests, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh, and bin/fm-lint.sh for changed scripts. Preserve dispatch precedence and every other adapter/backend.\n\nPreserve all accepted fail-closed remote contracts: resolve the requested profile, then run the shared capability and effective-effort preflight immediately before any inheritance transaction, readiness, route publication, metadata publication, or private-material transfer; refused launches have no side effect and never stop or retarget endpoints. Validate resolved Codex model and effort before relaunch stop. Before remote secondmate reuse, compare normalized authoritative live harness/model/effective-effort against the requested resolved profile; exact match may reuse, while mismatch or unavailable/unverifiable runtime truth refuses without retargeting or stopping the live endpoint. Never infer applied effort from an omitted adapter flag. Default effort is authoritative only for adapters with verified default semantics; every other adapter is unverifiable and refuses remote preflight, route publication, and reuse, including sibling adapters. Apply Codex capability validation before route publication and exact reuse. Keep local crewmate/scout unsupported-effort metadata/flag omission behavior distinct from remote secondmate refusal before readiness, inheritance/private-material transfer, and metadata publication. Retain and update the authoritative verification record without overclaiming.\n\nDo not mutate the live fleet, private config or task metadata, install/update software, spend, deploy, merge, reset, rebase, stash, replace, or change credentials. Do not repeat the already isolated stalled remote fixture loop; accept only an honest fixture/environment warning when supported by prior focused verification, and report it exactly. If workflow-scope OAuth rejection occurs, stop without credential escalation. Continue all returned no-mistakes gates through docs, lint, push, PR, and CI; if CI is not configured, report that exactly. ## What Changed - Added model-qualified Codex `max` effort validation using the installed catalog, with fail-closed handling for malformed, unsupported, or unknown profiles before launch or relaunch stop. - Hardened remote secondmate preflight, route publication, and reuse to require verifiable effective effort and exact live profile matches without retargeting or stopping endpoints. - Updated local dispatch behavior, documentation, authoritative Codex 0.147.0 evidence, and coverage for batch, relaunch, remote lifecycle, and adapter parity scenarios. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Review is in progress; no source risk assessment yet. ## Testing The focused spawn behavior is reproducibly passing; only the environment-limited lint evidence and the intentionally excluded remote fixture remain unresolved. ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
