title: fix(bin): enforce website deployment completion gates
body:
## Intent Fix PR 13 website deployment visual-verification gate bypasses at exact head 364df005 with the smallest coherent fence-aware structural validator at the operative Definition-of-done boundary, preserve custom-domain fresh-browser visual verification with distinguishing revision content, interaction evidence, and screenshot while rejecting HTTP-only and preview-only evidence, keep non-web briefs ungated, remove unnecessary SHA provenance machinery, add executable fenced/task-only/full-fenced regressions, retain only changes required by this accepted intent, use the existing no-mistakes PR path, and do not merge. ## What Changed - Added a shared fence-aware website gate requiring custom-domain fresh-browser verification, distinguishing revision content, deployed-site interaction evidence, and a preserved screenshot; HTTP-only, preview-only, and bare-reachability evidence are rejected. - Made web/non-web surface declarations fail-closed across brief creation, ship spawning, and scout promotion, anchored to the operative Definition-of-done section so non-web briefs remain ungated. - Added regressions and updated fixtures/documentation for missing, duplicated, fenced, task-only, incomplete, and compliant website-gate contracts. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is bounded to a shared fence-aware validator, its brief/promotion/spawn boundaries, documentation, and behavioral regressions; no material source-verifiable defect remains. ## Testing All three focused suites passed with no gate skips; reviewer-visible CLI evidence was preserved.
Evidence: Targeted test runner result ```text FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=3 failed=0 skipped_gate=0 ```
Evidence: Website gate evidence ```text Website gate end-to-end CLI evidence Command: FM_HOME= bin/fm-brief.sh evidence-web-gate website --mode no-mistakes --web Result: generated a ship brief with an operative web surface contract. Validator result: web Generated Definition of done boundary: # Definition of done Surface contract: web Web gate contract: custom-domain/chrome-devtools-axi/revision-marker/screenshot ## Website deployment completion gate This is a website or web-deployment ship task, so the task is not complete until firstmate can accept all of the following evidence together: - Verify the deployed revision against the real custom production domain, never only on a preview or staging URL. - Perform a fresh-browser visual verification against the real custom production domain with the existing chrome-devtools-axi tool: start a fresh browser session, run `chrome-devtools-axi open `, render the page, and inspect the actual result, not a headless or CDP shortcut. - Confirm that the rendered page visibly contains concrete distinguishing revision content - a marker introduced by this change - and record the exact marker checked. - Exercise a concrete interaction on the deployed custom-domain page and record the observed result from that deployed site. - Capture screenshot evidence of that verified custom-domain page with `chrome-devtools-axi screenshot`, and preserve the screenshot as durable task or PR evidence. - Explicitly record the custom production URL, marker, and screenshot evidence before reporting done. HTTP 200, a preview URL, or bare reachability alone is explicitly rejected as insufficient acceptance evidence. Do not append a done status or claim completion when any visual, marker, custom-domain, or screenshot evidence is missing. Delivery contract: mode=no-mistakes The task is complete only when committed on your branch. When you believe it is complete, append `done: {summary}` to the status file and stop. Firstmate will then instruct you to run /no-mistakes to validate and ship a PR. You drive no-mistakes by responding to its gates, not by implementing fixes. Follow the guidance no-mistakes itself provides for the mechanics: it loads when you invoke /no-mistakes, and `no-mistakes axi run --help` plus the `help` lines in each `axi` response are authoritative and version-matched to the installed binary. When starting no-mistakes, make `--intent` preserve all relevant content from this brief's `# Task` section plus every later accepted Firstmate requirement, clarification, constraint, exclusion, and supersession, carrying only each requirement's current accepted form; retain direct requirements instead of substituting a diff summary, and exclude generic operational, status, delivery, and other scaffold boilerplate unless it is task-specific. Do not hand-edit, commit, or fix findings yourself while a run is active - the pipeline applies every fix. Two firstmate-specific rules layer on top of that guidance: - ask-user findings are never yours to answer: escalate to firstmate (rule 6) and stop. title: fix: guard Lavish source placement across homes
body:
## Intent

Ship the captain-authorized Firstmate-side reliability repair from the completed diagnosis at data/lavish-command-board-reliability-diagnosis/report.md (scout task lavish-command-board-reliability-diagnosis, 2026-08-12). Incident: the captain's persistent Lavish command board sent feedback that produced no visible handling, because the board's process-event source was armed in the main Firstmate home while the artifact and session belong to a dedicated secondmate home. The machine-wide claim arbitrates liveness, not placement, so the arming home's runner consumed every feedback batch into its own inbox and wake queue while the owning home's registration sat inert and every surface it could inspect looked healthy (report sections 4/R1, 7/E6-E7, and 12). Before implementing, I synced with upstream firstmate https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate, verified the URL and default branch main, and based the work on the latest upstream state; the primary checkout and the captain's live Lavish board/session were not modified.

Required scope, implement ONLY the recommended Firstmate-side repair (report Option B) with focused executable regression coverage:
1. A bounded, deduplicated diagnostic when a registered process-event source is shadowed by a live owner from another Firstmate home. It must make the foreign owner and the action needed visible through existing supervision/wake mechanisms, and must never treat a foreign claim as this home's healthy listener.
2. A Lavish arm-time home-affinity guard: an artifact must be armed from the home that owns it by default, and a legitimate shared-artifact case must have an explicit, auditable override rather than an implicit bypass. Existing canonical artifact identity and machine-wide claim behavior must be preserved.
3. One concise placement/transfer rule added to the authoritative process-event/secondmate instructions and any directly relevant charter scaffold or operator documentation: the artifact-owning home arms the source, and transferring an existing session means retiring the old registration before arming it in the new owner home.
4. Extend the existing process-event test suite through public behavior for: the same source registered in two homes with a foreign live claim; the foreign-shadow diagnostic and its deduplication; default cross-home arm refusal; the explicit legitimate override; healthy same-home arm; replay/handled behavior; and the existing Send & End retirement path.

Explicit exclusions the captain set, which are deliberate and must not be "fixed" in review: do NOT modify lavish-axi's installed or upstream package in this task, and do NOT implement non-destructive take/ack, listener leases, or other lavish-package hardening - those are a separate Captain's Call (report sections 11 Option C and 14). The lavish-layer loss windows (report E4a/E4b) and the silent concurrent-poller race (E11) therefore remain documented non-guarantees after this change, and the existing "never at-least-once, no-loss, or lossless" wording must stay intact. The captain's live board session and its retained feedback must be preserved: no test may send feedback to the captain's real session or create, replace, or end that board, so all coverage runs against fixtures in isolated homes with an isolated claim root. Do not add a new control plane, broker, secret store, or external dependency; reuse the existing process-event, wake, claim, and supervision mechanisms and make the smallest coherent change.

Decisions and tradeoffs made while doing the work, which a reviewer reading only the diff would not know:
- The shadow diagnostic is published as an ordinary `check` wake with key `procevent-shadow:<id>` and payload `check: procevent-shadow <adapter> <source-id> owner=<home>`, deliberately reusing the existing durable wake queue rather than adding any new notification path. Its boundedness comes from the queue's own existing `fm_wake_queued_keys` read, so a persistent shadow contributes at most one unacknowledged record per source instead of one per watcher cycle, and it is announced again after acknowledgement while the misplacement stands (silence after one acknowledgement would recreate the invisibility this repair exists to remove). No new marker file or state was introduced for the dedupe.
- `bin/fm-watch.sh` proactively surfaces only queue keys matching `procevent:*`, so the new key needed the matcher widened to `procevent:*|procevent-shadow:*`; without that, the diagnostic would sit queued in exactly the quiet home the incident describes. Its surfacing reason line was renamed from "process-event result captured" to "process-event wake queued" because the same line now covers a diagnostic where nothing was captured; keeping the old wording would have been inaccurate. No existing test pinned that wording.
- `list` now prints OWNER `foreign` instead of `live` when another home holds the live claim. The ambiguous `live` reading was a verified masking condition of the incident (report section 3, masking condition 4), so this is an intentional user-visible output change.
- The arm-time guard uses the arming home's own tree (realpath containment under $FM_HOME) as the mechanical proxy for "the home that owns the artifact", refusing with a message that names the rule and the exact override. The refusal happens before anything is registered. Consequence accepted deliberately: the incident's own corrected configuration - a secondmate home owning a board whose file lives under the main home's tree - is exactly the legitimate shared-artifact case and now requires the explicit `--cross-home` flag, which is the intended auditable override, not an oversight. Already-armed live sources re-arm from stored argv through reconcile, so no running source is disturbed and no migration is needed.
- The override's audit trail is the required explicit flag plus the printed `cross-home:` line naming what was overridden; a new durable audit record was deliberately not added, because the shadow diagnostic already makes any wrong placement supervision-visible and a new state file would be the control plane the captain excluded.
- Knowledge placement followed firstmate-coding-guidelines' one-owner rule: the full agent-facing placement/transfer rule lives in .agents/skills/process-event-sources/SKILL.md (with the new wake's handling procedure), the operating contract sentence lives in docs/configuration.md which owns that contract, the flag mechanics live in the adapter header/--help, AGENTS.md got only its one-line trigger extended, and bin/fm-brief.sh's secondmate charter got a two-line pointer. docs/verification/process-event-sources.md got two rows mapping the new guarantees to the tests that prove them.
- Verification performed: tests/fm-procevent.test.sh and tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh extended and passing (procevent suite green, watch-triage 47/47, watch-arm 14/14 unchanged), bin/fm-lint.sh and bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh clean, and each new test confirmed to fail when its corresponding source change is reverted.

Delivery requirements from the captain: use the no-mistakes path, drive every gate through to checks-passed, do not merge, keep the PR scoped to this repair and its tests/docs, and include the diagnosis report path in the PR evidence or status so the captain can review the causal basis.

## What Changed

- Added cross-home process-event shadow diagnostics with bounded wake deduplication and proactive watch surfacing for foreign live claims.
- Added Lavish arm-time home-affinity enforcement with an explicit `--cross-home` override, plus related charter, configuration, and operator documentation.
- Extended process-event and watch-triage regression coverage for shadowing, placement guards, overrides, replay/handling, and Send & End retirement.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The repair is narrowly scoped to existing claim, durable-wake, watcher-marker, and Lavish adapter boundaries, with no material reachable regression or intent contradiction identified.

## Testing

The focused process-event and watcher suites passed, covering cross-home shadow diagnostics and deduplication, Lavish arm affinity and explicit override, healthy same-home behavior, replay/handled semantics, proactive wake surfacing, and Send & End retirement; CLI evidence was captured without contacting the captain’s live Lavish session.

title: fix: recover startup from stopped session owners
body:
## Intent

Reproduce and fix the FirstMate session-lock liveness defect where a stopped harness process can block session startup. Use only an isolated FirstMate test home and synthetic processes created for this task, and reproduce through the real lock-acquisition or bootstrap-facing interface wherever safely feasible. Capture expected and observed behavior, setup, input, and repeatability; separate initiating trigger, masking condition, and operator-visible symptom; compare the stopped path with a proven active-owner path; inspect history and blame; identify the earliest meaningful divergence; test the smallest counterfactual and seek disconfirming evidence; distinguish facts from hypotheses and implement only once the cause explains failure and proven paths. Make the smallest correction at the authoritative process-liveness boundary, preserving true active-owner exclusion and failing safely when process state cannot be classified. Account for supported Linux and macOS process-inspection surfaces and every caller of the changed contract. Convert the end-to-end reproduction into deterministic executable or public-interface regression coverage for active owners, stopped owners, unknown or error classification, and other causally load-bearing states without asserting source text. Review affected startup, lock, recovery, supported-harness, and runtime-backend integrations, marking axes not applicable only after inspection. Run focused tests, documentation audience checks for prose changes, pinned shell lint for shell changes, the relevant full test family, and git diff --check. Do not alter any live home lock, signal or kill any existing session, bypass supervision, touch another operational home, install globally, change credentials, discard work, merge, or modify external systems. Do not change watcher code: an independent untouched origin/main baseline reproduced the same watcher TERM and recovery-lock self-deadlock with identical affected watcher and test bytes, and the tri-state lock-liveness patch is not on that path, so treat that full-family hang as a pre-existing independent defect and proceed from focused green evidence. Deliver a reviewed green PR and do not merge it.

## What Changed

- Classify session-lock owners as active, stopped, absent/terminal, or unknown, fencing only identity-verified stopped process groups before takeover while preserving active-owner exclusion and safe refusal for ambiguous states.
- Record immutable owner and process-group identities, migrate corroborated legacy leases, and require the verified lease across startup, bootstrap, deferred-network, and Claude auto-arm callers.
- Add Linux/macOS regression coverage and documentation for active, stopped, unknown, PID-reuse, legacy-owner, and surviving-process-group scenarios.

## Risk Assessment

🚨 High: The durable lock fix still contains reachable paths that either admit surviving prior execution or permanently wedge future session acquisition.

## Testing

Baseline public-interface reproduction failed as expected on the base and recovered in 2/2 target runs; active, stopped, unknown, Linux/macOS state mapping, startup, deferred work, bootstrap, Stop-hook, session-open, and supported-runtime integrations all passed with CLI/log evidence. Initial environment-sensitive fixtures and an outdated active-takeover expectation were corrected and rerun green. title: fix(bin): collapse duplicate supervision wakes
body:
## Intent

Collapse DUPLICATE firstmate supervision wakes WITHOUT losing any legitimate update, in firstmate's shared tracked wake/supervision machinery (bin/fm-wake-lib.sh, bin/fm-wake-drain.sh, bin/fm-watch.sh, the remote-reply capture path bin/fm-procevent-remote-reply.sh / bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh, and the status-signal vs check-wake generation), diagnosing each case to its exact source before changing anything. The four observed duplicate-wake cases to fix: (1) a single remote-secondmate note arrives as BOTH a captured remote-reply check wake AND a signal (status) wake - same content, two wakes, two handling turns - it must produce ONE handling turn; (2) an already-handled remote-reply sequence replays as later check wakes with an empty/already-handled drain - already-handled sequences must stay QUIET; (3) firstmate's own bookkeeping closes (a 'resolved [key=...]' line this home writes locally to fold a stale decision) generate signal wakes that re-wake the same session - a home's own bookkeeping close must not wake itself, identified by provenance (this home wrote them), never by content-guessing that could swallow a real update; (4) a long-running scout fires turn-ended pings while still working and the wake is annotated with a stale HISTORICAL status line that looks like progress - do not present a stale historical status line as a new update. HARD SAFETY BAR (do not regress): NEVER drop a genuinely NEW remote reply, NEW decision, NEW blocker, a merge, a failure, or the FIRST occurrence of any status change; dedup ONLY proven duplicates, proven replays, and self-echoes; when uncertain whether a wake is a duplicate, KEEP the wake (fail toward waking); one remote note produces ONE firstmate handling turn, not two; NEVER silence a later DIFFERENT note on the same task (dedup keys must distinguish content/sequence, not just task id). Deliverable: implement the dedup at the correct layer for each case, patching the one owner of that layer (one-owner rule), no scattered content-guessing across the wake path; write the EXACT dedup rules down in the PR description and in the owning script headers / relevant docs; REGRESSION TESTS driving the real wake functions (source the libs, no harness) proving both directions: (a) each of the 4 duplicate cases collapses to a single or no wake as specified, and (b) a genuinely-NEW remote reply, a NEW decision, a NEW blocker, a merge result, a failure, the FIRST status change, and a later DIFFERENT note on the same task ALL still wake - the (b) cases are the mandatory safety proof. This is harness-agnostic shell (not harness-dependent), so a portable tests/ regression is sufficient. Follow firstmate-coding-guidelines: one-owner rule, one-sentence-per-line Markdown, plain dash, shellcheck, bin/fm-lint.sh; tests must exercise behavior through the executable interface (the real wake-append/drain/generation functions), never assert implementation-source bytes; prefer deterministic idempotent enforcement for this supervision-critical machinery. Implementation decisions made: the process-event runner gained an adapter-declared 'self-announcing' seam - the remote-reply adapter declares that its mirrored status append is the single durable announcement, so the runner applies (autohandles) first and publishes a check wake only for captures the adapter could not fully apply, which collapses case 1 to one signal wake and makes case 2's byte-identical replays (e.g. a cursor-loss whole-log recapture) fully quiet; every other adapter keeps strict publish-before-apply so no adapter without a downstream channel can go silent. fm-wake-lib.sh became the one owner of the watcher's signal signature/.seen-* marker format plus a guarded self-announced append primitive (advance the seen marker only over exactly this home's own appended bytes, only when everything earlier was already announced, failing toward waking on any pending or interleaved foreign write); fm-send's answerer-closes append, fm-pending-reply-lib's escalation close, and fm-decision-hold's captain-held transfer use it (case 3), while escalation OPENs stay plain appends because a new blocker must wake. The drain's historical (turn-ended-only) annotation is skipped only when the status file's signature provably matches its seen marker (case 4). fm-classify-lib treats a kind=secondmate task's status signal as never absorbable-by-busy-evidence because that stream is the routed-reply channel the parent must read - this keeps the one surviving wake for a remote note deliverable. Also fixed a pre-existing exit-path deadlock reproduced by the regression runs: a TERM landing inside a recovery-marker critical section left fm_lock_try_acquire spinning forever against this same process's abandoned lock hold; a self-held lock (holder pid equals this process frame) is now reclaimed, while a subshell still waits on its parent's live hold. Since this touches the running supervision/wake surface, running firstmate homes need a self-update after merge.

## What Changed

- Make remote-reply captures self-announcing: fully applied captures rely on their mirrored status signal, byte-identical replays stay quiet, and incomplete application retains the fallback `check` wake.
- Suppress self-authored bookkeeping closes only when the prior signature was already seen and the append covers exactly this home’s bytes; otherwise fail toward waking. Historical turn-end annotations are omitted only when the status signature exactly matches its seen marker.
- Always surface secondmate status signals, reclaim abandoned same-process lock holds, and add regression coverage proving new replies, decisions, blockers, merges, failures, first status changes, and later different notes still wake.

## Risk Assessment

🚨 High: The primary durable dedup guarantee remains reachable through a normal concurrent reconciliation path and should not merge without correction or explicit approval.

## Testing

Real wake libraries, watcher/drain executables, process-event and remote-reply paths collapsed all four duplicate cases while preserving new replies, decisions, blockers, merges, failures, first status changes, and later different notes; no visual artifact applies to this shell-only supervision surface, so reviewer-visible behavioral logs were captured.

title: feat: require deployment evidence at completion gate
body:
## Intent Ponytail-ultra rebuild of the deployed-website evidence rule, replacing an earlier and much larger implementation that the captain explicitly invalidated. Background the reviewer needs: a previous branch enforced this idea with a mandatory web/non-web classification on every ship brief, a custom fence-aware Markdown parser that located an operative "# Definition of done" section, a SHA-256 provenance stamp, and broad churn across roughly 25 test fixture files. The captain reviewed that work, closed its pull request, and ordered a rebuild from the clean current upstream base that keeps ONLY the accepted outcome. This branch is that rebuild, started fresh from origin/main; none of the old implementation is carried over. Accepted outcome to preserve, and nothing more: - One explicit rule stating that deployed website work must be proven with production-domain evidence of the intended revision, an interaction, and a screenshot. - The smallest enforcement of that rule on the EXISTING rail, reusing the independent completion-verification mechanism that already exists rather than building a parallel one. - Preview-only or HTTP-status-only completion is rejected. Explicitly dropped by captain decision, and deliberately absent from this diff: - The mandatory web / non-web classification on ship briefs. - The custom Markdown parser. - The broad fixture churn. - Any new subsystem, abstraction, configuration surface, or scaffolding for later. Deliberate decisions a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: 1. Choice of rail. The "independent completion-verification mechanism that already exists" was identified as bin/fm-decision-hold.sh's `complete` / `verify` gate. Its own header calls `complete` the shared investigation and visual-review completion gate, and scout teardown calls the read-only `verify` before removing any source state, so teardown cannot erase evidence before the gate has succeeded. That is an existing independent completion verifier, so the deployed-website proof attaches to it instead of a new gate, a new script, or a second control plane. 2. Attestation shape mirrors the rail's existing design. This rail is deliberately agent-attested and script-verified: the agent supplies semantics (`--none` or decision keys) and the script deterministically verifies the artifacts. The deployment proof follows the identical pattern - the agent attests that a deployment happened by passing the four flags, and the script deterministically refuses an incomplete attestation. No inference from prose, terminal output, or chat, consistent with the rail's standing rule that it never reads report bodies to guess. 3. Four explicit flags, not one packed value. `--deployed-site`, `--revision`, `--interaction`, `--screenshot` are the rule's own four evidence items. A single combined value would have required a parser, which is one of the things the captain explicitly ordered removed; four plain flags need none. 4. What is deterministically enforced versus attested. The script enforces: all four flags together or none at all, an `https://` production domain, one-line values via the existing `validate_one_line` helper, and a screenshot path that actually exists on disk. The existing-file check is what mechanically defeats an HTTP-status-only or "I looked at it" completion, because a claim with no artifact cannot pass. That preview URLs are unacceptable is stated in the rule and attested by the agent; deterministically classifying a hostname as preview versus production would need a policy list, which would be exactly the configuration surface the captain excluded. 5. Non-deployment work is untouched by construction. The flags are optional; omitting them leaves the previous code path byte-for-byte identical in behavior. The existing `--none` and decision-key semantics, including the rule that `--none` cannot be combined with keys, are preserved through the rewritten argument loop, which was restructured only because the old loop assumed every remaining argument was a decision key. 6. Durable recording. An accepted attestation is appended to live task metadata as `deployed_site=`, `deployed_revision=`, `deployed_interaction=`, `deployed_screenshot=`, matching the file's existing `key=value` shape, so the proof survives the worktree teardown that would otherwise destroy it. 7. Knowledge placement follows the repo's own rules. The rule text went to `.agents/skills/decision-hold-lifecycle/SKILL.md`, which is already the single policy owner for this completion gate, with only a minimal trigger amendment in AGENTS.md (two lines, naming website deployment alongside investigations and visual reviews). Mechanism and regression evidence went to `docs/decision-hold-lifecycle.md`, the existing mechanism doc. No new prose surface was created and no contract is stated twice. 8. One regression test, proven to be a real one. `tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh` gained a single behavioral case driving the public CLI: partial attestation refused, non-existent screenshot refused, non-https site refused, complete proof accepted and durably recorded. It was verified to FAIL when the enforcement block is disabled and pass with it in place, so it genuinely fails if the rule stops being enforced. No implementation source bytes are asserted. Known-unrelated pre-existing failures, verified earlier to reproduce identically on upstream origin/main with these changes absent, and therefore deliberately not addressed here: tests/fm-arm-pretool-check.test.sh (a watcher-bundled PreToolUse denial), tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh (a Pi runtime crash in the installed pi-coding-agent), and `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` (comm invoked without LC_ALL=C against LC_ALL=C-sorted inputs, a locale collation mismatch in this environment). Constraints in force: this is firstmate's own shared tracked material, so the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill applies - one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never an em dash, no agent co-author on commits, bin/*.sh shellcheck-clean via bin/fm-lint.sh, colocated tests extending the existing suite rather than a new runner, and tests that exercise public behavior rather than implementation source. bin/fm-lint.sh and bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh both pass on this branch. Delivery: no-mistakes mode, full rigorous path, report the pull request URL when checks are green. Do NOT merge - the captain merges. If a review gate raises an ask-user finding, it must be routed to firstmate with its key rather than answered here. ## What Changed - Adds deployed-website evidence requirements to the existing completion gate, including production-domain revision, interaction, and screenshot proof. - Validates and durably records accepted deployment attestations, with documentation and regression coverage for incomplete or invalid evidence. - Generalizes decision-status parsing for multiple bracket tags and updates cursor folding behavior with migration coverage. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The changed gate closes the reviewed bypasses and preserves the existing non-deployment completion path. ## Testing Focused lifecycle tests and CLI evidence checks passed; no UI surface was changed, so rendered UI screenshot evidence was not applicable.
Evidence: Deployed-site completion CLI transcript `Public CLI evidence: incomplete attestations exit 1; complete HTTPS proof exits 0 and records deployed_site, deployed_revision, deployed_interaction, and deployed_screenshot.` ```text Public CLI evidence for deployed-site completion gate CASE partial exit=1 fm-decision-hold: a deployed website completion needs --deployed-site, --revision, --interaction, and --screenshot together CASE missing-screenshot exit=1 fm-decision-hold: --screenshot must name an existing screenshot file: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZW3T5DSRK5EEZTHF9ASB2KP/fixture.fPnp8D/home/data/sample-site-deploy/absent.png CASE non-https exit=1 fm-decision-hold: --deployed-site must be the https production domain that was actually verified CASE accepted exit=0 complete: sample-site-deploy decision inventory reviewed DURABLE METADATA deployed_site=https://sample.example deployed_revision=sample-marker-1 deployed_interaction=clicked the sample control and the sample panel opened deployed_screenshot=/tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZW3T5DSRK5EEZTHF9ASB2KP/fixture.fPnp8D/home/data/sample-site-deploy/production.png ```

✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 3 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:374` - The required durable-recording criterion says an accepted attestation must be appended to live task metadata so it survives teardown. This path accepts report-only origins after metadata is gone, skips the append guarded by `has_meta` at lines 370-377, and still returns success; require deployment attestations to have live metadata before accepting them. - 🚨 `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:333` - The required rule is all four deployment flags together or none. Presence is inferred from concatenated values, so a trailing `--screenshot` with no value (or all four flags with empty values) leaves every variable empty, skips validation, and succeeds as a no-deployment completion. Track option presence separately and reject missing values. - 🚨 `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:340` - The required evidence is an `https://` production domain, but this check validates only the scheme prefix. A value such as `https://` or `https:// ` passes when the other evidence is valid even though it is not a domain; add a minimal non-empty authority/hostname check while retaining agent attestation for preview-vs-production classification. 🔧 Fix: Closed deployment evidence gate bypasses and durability gaps ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: feat: add Herdr sibling worker tabs
body:
Introduces the captain-approved configurable Herdr sibling worker-tab workflow for directly delegated transient crewmates and scouts.

## What changed
- `config/herdr-presentation-spaces=tabs` places each delegated worker as one real human-titled task tab beside its launcher, with no auxiliary tab, workspace, or card, and no focus steal.
- State markers on the one real tab: `●` working, `◐` review-ready, `?` captain decision, `!` failed or stopped, `✓` completed.
- Completed workers sleep view-only in their real tab and are retained until explicitly cleared; active work is always preserved on stop; resources are released only after the result is safe.
- Resource pressure never auto-cleans workers; only a concrete measurement (retained completed-worker RSS > 10 GiB or available memory < 2 GiB) emits the single `Captain, completed workers - resource pressure.` message.
- Transcript summaries are required (Goal/Outcome/Files/How/Verification for ship; Question/Findings/Evidence/Recommendation for scout); captain-facing outcome notices stay minimal and batched.
- Existing workspace-per-worker behavior, non-Herdr backends, and secondmate isolation are unchanged.

## Lifecycle corrections
- Serialized duplicate-title selection at the shared session boundary with collision-free suffixes.
- Retained completed-tab relaunch refusal enforced through both `fm-control` and the shared `fm-spawn` relaunch path.
- Atomic, agent-free, authoritative completion transition that graduates only genuinely `done` workers to `✓` and preserves `!`/`?` for retained stopped/failed/decision workers.

## Validation
Passed review, test (unit + real-Herdr E2E + pressure regression), document, and lint (ShellCheck 0.11.0) steps in the no-mistakes pipeline.

title: fix(pr-merge): refuse to merge a PR whose forge checks are red or unreadable
body:
## Intent Make bin/fm-pr-merge.sh refuse to merge a pull request whose forge reports a failing check, so that "never merge a red PR" is enforced by the one merge path instead of by session attention. Why: on 2026-08-10 the merge-queue run for nguzen/aln pull request 182 failed at 17:54 UTC and the pull request was merged at 17:59 UTC by the same account; the defect in that commit then blocked every production deploy until 2026-08-12, and the product owner asked about missing changes twice. bin/fm-pr-merge.sh read no check state at all, and the no-mistakes CI monitor on this box cannot read check results either (its gh pr checks call fails), so two blind spots combined into a two-day outage. Requirements the user stated, all deliberate: 1. Read the forge check state before merging and REFUSE with an error exit code, listing exactly what is red. 2. The merge queue must be covered: it re-runs the checks on the combined commit, so its verdict can differ from the branch verdict. A branch-only read was explicitly called insufficient. 3. An explicit override flag for a deliberate red merge (for example an infrastructurally broken check). Without the flag, refuse. 4. An unreadable check state is a REFUSAL, not permission. Forge silence must never read as green - that is the exact class of error that caused the incident. 5. Do not break GitLab/Forgejo behavior already present in bin/fm-pr-lib.sh; where check state is unavailable, the refusal must be intelligible rather than cryptic. Named trap, verified 2026-08-12: gh pr checks exits non-zero both when something failed and when something is still running, so classification by exit status is impossible - only output values can classify. That is why this change does not use gh pr checks at all. Decisions made while implementing, so they are not mistakes: - New sourced library bin/fm-pr-checks-lib.sh owns the classification; bin/fm-pr-merge.sh only decides. It reads two sources: gh pr view --json number,baseRefName,statusCheckRollup for the PR head, and gh api "repos///actions/runs?event=merge_group&per_page=100" filtered to head_branch prefix gh-readonly-queue//pr-- for the merge queue. Both classified with jq by value. - Only the NEWEST queue attempt is judged, so a superseded red attempt cannot block a re-queued green pull request; within that attempt the newest run per workflow wins so a re-run replaces its own result. - Branch-side CANCELLED and STALE count as failures (the branch is not green and nothing re-runs them), while queue-side cancelled/stale count as inconclusive because the queue itself discards and re-runs those attempts as PRs ahead land. - Every read failure - missing gh or jq, a failed call, a bound hit, output that does not parse, a payload describing a different pull request, or a payload missing the fields that were requested - returns unreadable and refuses. jq and gh are hard requirements on this path, consistent with bin/fm-fleet-view.sh and bin/fm-bearings-snapshot.sh. - pending (checks still running) is permitted but printed as a visible note; only failing and unreadable refuse. The forge branch protection remains the backstop for pending. - The gate runs BEFORE bin/fm-pr-check.sh, so a refused merge records no pr= metadata and arms no merge poll, matching the script prior refusals. - --allow-failing-checks skips the read entirely (it must also override an unreadable verdict, which is the infrastructural-breakage case) and announces itself on stderr. Own flags are consumed before the -- separator; an unknown own flag is a usage error with exit 2 rather than a flag silently forwarded to gh-axi. This does mean extra gh-axi flags must now come after --, which is the documented usage and what every existing test already does. - GitLab is untouched: bin/fm-pr-merge.sh already refuses a GitLab merge request URL by provider before the gate can run, and the library header records that it is GitHub-only for that reason. - AGENTS.md gained one line recording that --allow-failing-checks IS a red merge and needs the same explicit captain instruction any red merge needs, so the flag cannot be treated as a routine convenience. docs/architecture.md and docs/scripts.md were updated to match. Verification already performed: the library classifies the live incident correctly - nguzen/aln#182 as failing (branch check "e2e visual QA (Playwright)" plus merge-queue check CI) and #183 as green. tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh gained seven cases (red branch, red merge queue with a green branch, superseded queue attempt, unreadable rollup read, unreadable queue read, payload for another pull request, override flag, unknown own flag) and passes 17/17; tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh passes 36/36 after its gh mock was taught the two new reads; bin/fm-lint.sh, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh and bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage are clean. Both guards were mutation-checked: blinding the queue read fails only the queue case, and accepting an unreadable verdict fails only the unreadable case. One factual correction to the original report, deliberately reflected in the code and the commit message: pull request 182 was red on BOTH sources, not only the queue - its own branch run failed the same visual-QA check at 17:56:50. The branch-green/queue-red split is therefore covered by a synthetic test fixture rather than by that live pull request, and both sources are read because either can be red alone. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-pr-checks-lib.sh`, a sourced GitHub-only library that classifies a PR's forge check state from two independent sources — the PR head's `statusCheckRollup` (via `gh pr view`) and the newest merge-queue attempt's Actions runs (via `gh api ...runs?event=merge_group`) — using jq value inspection rather than `gh pr checks` exit codes, which cannot distinguish failing from still-running. - Gated `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` on that verdict before it runs `fm-pr-check.sh`: a failing or unreadable state refuses the merge with a non-zero exit and prints exactly which checks are red, while `pending` is permitted with a visible note. Branch-side `CANCELLED`/`STALE` count as failures; queue-side cancelled/stale count as inconclusive since the queue re-runs them. Only the newest queue attempt (newest run per workflow) is judged so a superseded red attempt cannot block a re-queued green PR. - Added an `--allow-failing-checks` override (consumed as an own flag before `--`, announced on stderr) that skips the read entirely for deliberate red/infrastructural merges; an unknown own flag is now a usage error (exit 2) rather than being forwarded to gh-axi. - Expanded `tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh` (17/17) and `tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh` with fixtures for red branch, branch-green/queue-red, superseded queue attempt, unreadable rollup/queue reads, foreign-PR payload, the override flag, and the unknown-flag case; updated `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/scripts.md` to record that `--allow-failing-checks` is itself a red merge. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Well-bounded, additive change with a new sourced classifier and a pre-state merge gate; every required intent criterion is met, error paths fail closed to refusal, and it is covered by mutation-checked tests. ## Testing Ran the two changed suites and built an end-to-end demo. The primary target, tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh, passes 17/17 and directly exercises each intent requirement including the merge-queue-red / branch-green split and the unreadable-is-refusal rule. tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh completed with exit 0 and no failures, confirming the new forge reads don't regress the existing recording/derivation and teardown-safety behavior. title: docs(orchestrator): put task decomposition and child routing with the supervisor
body:
## What

Clarifies the ownership boundary in `custom-skills/orchestrator/SKILL.md`. Wording only - no runtime behavior changes and no authority is broadened.

## Why

The skill read as though firstmate's part of a programme extended past intake:

- Step 2 was titled "Resolve the runtime" with no possessive, so it read as the place any profile gets settled.
- Its line *"Each worker it dispatches resolves its own profile through the ordinary per-task routing"* left the resolver unnamed. `custom-skills/program-orchestration/SKILL.md` is explicit that the **supervisor** resolves the worker's concrete runtime, model, and effort after selecting a host; the orchestrator skill did not say so.

## What changed

A new **The boundary** section states both halves positively:

- **Firstmate** takes the intake inputs, confirms every named project is already cloned, resolves the *supervisor's* own runtime profile, writes the packet and the brief, launches the session, and confirms it is processing that brief. From there it holds lifecycle only, plus escalations and the return.
- **The supervisor** owns the programme from launch on: it reads `CONTRACT.md` and `program-orchestration`, decomposes the authorized work into task cards, maps dependencies and custody, resolves each child worker's concrete harness/model/effort through the ordinary per-task routing, records that routing on the child's card, spawns/supervises/reconciles children, and owns programme evidence and delivery.

Supporting edits:

- Step 2 retitled **"Resolve the supervisor's runtime"**, with the resolver of child profiles named explicitly and a completion criterion that the only profile resolved is the supervisor's.
- Step 4 names the scaffold's **Task** and **Scope and seams** sections instead of restating the `{TASK}`/`{SCOPE}` tokens, which `fm-supervisor-brief.sh`'s header and closing line already own. Its completion criterion now requires the brief to hand the authorized work over whole, not pre-decomposed.
- The explicit-profile safety rule is stated for **every** launch in the programme, not just the supervisor spawn.
- One supervisor / one leased home, the `--supervisor` spawn, and `data/secondmates.md` staying byte-identical are all unchanged.

## Validation

Two checks added to the colocated `custom-skills/tests/fm-orchestrator-policy.test.sh`, covering the four required properties:

| Required property | How it is checked |
|---|---|
| No `{TASK}` / `{SCOPE}` placeholder | `assert_no_grep` on both tokens |
| No claim that firstmate resolves/selects/maps/records a child worker profile | no line may match `firstmate` **and** `worker\|child` **and** `harness\|model\|effort\|profile\|routing` |
| Positive statement that the supervisor owns decomposition and per-child profile resolution | fixed-string asserts on the three ownership sentences |
| Every supervisor and worker launch requires explicit `--harness`, `--model`, `--effort` | every non-`--help` `fm-spawn.sh` line in the skill must carry all three, plus the rule sentence |

Each new assertion was mutation-checked - five deliberate breakages (reintroduced placeholder, a firstmate-owns-child-model line, dropped decomposition statement, dropped `--effort`, dropped per-child resolution statement) each turned the suite red, and the suite returned green once reverted.

```
./custom-skills/tests/fm-orchestrator-policy.test.sh   # 9 ok, exit 0
./tests/fm-temporary-supervisor.test.sh                # exit 0
./custom-skills/tests/fm-paired-review-policy.test.sh  # exit 0
./custom-skills/tests/fm-planner-policy.test.sh        # exit 0
./bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh                         # ok surfaces=126 local_links=304
shellcheck -e SC1091 custom-skills/tests/fm-orchestrator-policy.test.sh  # clean
```

`SC1091` is pre-existing on the `tests/lib.sh` source line and is not in `bin/fm-lint.sh`'s target set.

title: fix(bin): prevent false Pi watcher alarms during hand-offs
body:
## Intent DIAGNOSE then SHIP: the WATCHER DOWN banner printed at fm-send time is a FALSE ALARM on a healthy Pi primary. This touches firstmate's shared, tracked material (the send-time supervision-health guard), so firstmate-coding-guidelines applies: one-owner rule, one-sentence-per-line Markdown, plain dash never em dash, shellcheck-clean bin scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh, tests colocated in tests/ extending the existing suite, and tests must exercise behavior through an executable interface and never assert implementation source bytes. OBSERVED: almost every fm-send from a Pi primary home printed the full 'WATCHER DOWN - SUPERVISION IS OFF' banner (or the same-episode one-liner) even when the Pi extension already owned the watcher-arm child and the last beacon beat was seconds old. The send still succeeded, but firstmate then needlessly narrated 'repair the watcher'. Pi watcher continuity is EXTENSION-owned (.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts), not bash-arm-owned, so a momentary send-time beacon gap or lock-holder mismatch must not read as 'supervision is off'. DIAGNOSIS PERFORMED (diagnostic-reasoning procedure, evidence gathered live, not guessed). Trigger: any guarded command (fm-send calls fm-guard.sh with a CONTINUE_LINE) on a Pi primary. Mask: the Pi extension deliberately tears the watcher down on every actionable wake and spawns the replacement itself, so state/.watch.lock is legitimately unheld during each hand-off - all 799 cycles in the live Pi primary's state/.watch-cycle-exits.log end with lock_after=pid:none, the no-watcher window measured 0.2s to 198s (median 31s, p90 117s, 5.5% of wall clock), and a live 20Hz sampler on the real Pi primary captured the guard verdict flipping to reason=no-watcher with lockpid=none and the beacon 63s old, then back to healthy 0.32s later. Symptom: fm_supervision_model classified pi as 'persistent', which requires a live identity-matched watcher process holding the lock (fm_watcher_healthy), so that window rendered the full alarm. Earliest divergence between the healthy and genuinely-down paths: the Claude primary's 'autoarm' model already treats the identical state (fresh beacon, no live lock holder) as healthy by design because its watcher only runs between turns; Pi had no equivalent model, so healthy extension-owned hand-off and real supervision loss were indistinguishable. Smallest counterfactual that flips it: give the verdict an extension-ownership proof. FIX (smallest change): add an 'extension' supervision model for pi and pi-signed in fm_supervision_model. Under it a live identity-matched watcher remains the ordinary healthy state, and an unheld lock is healthy ONLY while the beacon is fresh within FM_GUARD_GRACE AND a live Pi session provably owns continuity. That proof is the new fm_pi_extension_owns_supervision in bin/fm-wake-lib.sh: both Pi primary extensions (fm-primary-pi-watch.ts and fm-primary-turnend-guard.ts) must be recorded in their state markers at their current on-disk build hashes by the process named in state/.lock, and that process must still be alive. Requiring the turn-end guard extension as well as the watch extension is deliberate: it is the structural backstop, so a home missing it has no benign hand-off to tolerate. SAFETY BAR HELD (explicitly required, do not relax): this is NOT a blanket suppression. A genuinely missing, failed, or unhealthy watcher must still print loudly - turn-end-guard extension missing or version-drifted, no live arm ownership (extension unloaded or the Pi session exited), and genuinely stale supervision (beacon past grace) all still fire the full banner immediately or within grace. The queued-wakes-pending warning is kept exactly as is because it is real. The PID-strict fm_watcher_healthy used by bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh is deliberately untouched. Claude (autoarm), codex, opencode, grok, kimi, tmux, and unknown primaries keep their existing persistent-model watcher-down detection unchanged; the tolerance is scoped to the extension model alone. REGRESSION PROVING BOTH DIRECTIONS, through the executable interface (bin/fm-guard.sh driven with real state files and real processes), added to the existing tests/fm-guard-stale-banner.test.sh rather than a new runner: healthy extension-owned Pi hand-off -> NO watcher-down banner and no down-episode opened; no ownership evidence -> banner still fires naming the missing watcher process; each of the five ownership signals broken individually (dead Pi session, missing watch marker, missing turnend marker, drifted watch build, drifted turnend build) -> banner still fires, so no single signal is load-bearing alone; beacon past grace with a fully live correctly-loaded Pi session -> banner still fires naming the stale beacon; queued-wakes-pending during a healthy hand-off -> still fires and does not resurrect the banner; a persistent-watcher primary with Pi markers present on disk -> still alarms, pinning the model scoping; a live identity-matched watcher under the extension model -> silent through the strict path; and Pi and pi-signed primaries routing themselves to the extension model through real bin/fm-harness.sh detection with no FM_SUPERVISION_MODEL override, which is the end-user path. HARNESS-DEPENDENT-CHECK CLASSIFICATION (per firstmate-coding-guidelines): the fixed guard logic is pure - it reads state files, file hashes, and process liveness, and reads no vendor-emitted process name, rendered output, spinner glyph, banner, or keybind - so a portable tests/ regression driving bin/fm-guard.sh with real files and processes is sufficient and no new live-harness-optin guard is needed. The only vendor-dependent input is bin/fm-harness.sh's pre-existing PI_CODING_AGENT marker detection that selects the model, and the same suite exercises that path directly. ONE-OWNER CLEANUP: bin/fm-session-start.sh carried its own private copies of the Pi extension marker predicate and its hash helper. Those were folded into bin/fm-wake-lib.sh (fm_pi_extension_version, fm_pi_extension_loaded) so the ownership contract is stated once, and fm-session-start.sh now sources fm-wake-lib.sh and calls them. This was verified not to collide with any fm-session-start.sh function or variable. DOCS: bin/fm-guard.sh's header, bin/fm-wake-lib.sh's model documentation, and docs/turnend-guard.md (the owner of the guard-predicate contract) describe the new model; bin/fm-supervision-lib.sh's header restatement of the models was reduced to a cross-reference rather than a third copy. docs/verification/supervision.md records the dated maintainer-verification evidence including the live Pi primary reproduction. DELIVERY: mode=no-mistakes, yolo OFF - the captain merges. Escalate any ask-user finding rather than deciding it. Note in the PR that homes pick this change up only after merge plus a firstmate self-update, since it changes the send-time supervision banner. Stop at CI green. ## What Changed - Route Pi and pi-signed primaries through an extension supervision model that accepts fresh-beacon, unheld-lock hand-offs only when a live session owns current builds of both Pi extensions. - Preserve watcher-down alarms for stale beacons, unhealthy held locks, missing or drifted ownership evidence, and persistent-watcher harnesses while keeping queued-wake warnings unchanged. - Centralize Pi extension marker helpers, expand executable guard regressions, and document the supervision contract and verification evidence. Homes receive the fix after merge and a Firstmate self-update. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The fix is narrowly scoped to Pi extension-owned hand-offs, preserves strict handling for held unhealthy locks and stale beacons, and includes executable-interface coverage for the required paths. ## Testing The baseline reproduced the false banner; targeted guard and session-start tests passed, and end-to-end CLI evidence shows a healthy Pi hand-off stays silent without opening an episode while a missing ownership marker still emits the full warning. The broader session-start test exceeded its time limit only after all relevant changed-path checks had passed.

title: feat: support Cursor Agent CLI as a primary harness
body:
## Intent

Make Cursor Agent CLI usable as a firstmate PRIMARY harness, not just a crewmate/scout adapter. This is firstmate SHARED, TRACKED material touching the core supervision surface: the turn-end guard, the watcher/supervision protocol, session start, and the away-mode daemon.

The authoritative spec was a completed feasibility scout report (data/fm-cursor-primary-feasibility-s1/report.md) that had already located every primitive with file:line references, live evidence, exact bundle offsets, the config schema, and a gap list G1-G9. The instruction was to IMPLEMENT that report rather than re-investigate or redesign it, and to escalate rather than silently diverge if the report turned out to be wrong about a concrete fact.

Captain-ordered sequence, done in this order:
1. G1/G2/G9 - ship a TRACKED project-scope .cursor/hooks.json registering stop and sessionStart (plus preToolUse for the watcher-arm seatbelt). Add a cursor mode to the turn-end guard that, when the shared predicate returns 2, prints {"followup_message":"<the U+2063 FIRSTMATE_OP: turn-end-guard follow-up>"} on stdout and exits 0, and NEVER exits 2, because the report proved exit 2 is a silent no-op on cursor's stop step. Self-bound the follow-up loop on BOTH loop_count from the stop payload AND a loop_limit in the registration - both, not either, because a naive always-follow-up hook loops forever. This step alone had to deliver "no turn ends blind" for a cursor primary.
2. G4/G3 - register sessionStart to run the digest through firstmate's run-tier session-start wrapper, emitting the digest as additional_context, supplying --source ourselves because cursor's payload has no Claude-style source field, with timeout 180 so it sits above bin/fm-session-start.sh's own 120s budget. Add docs/supervision-protocols/cursor.md using the park model the report recommended, and a cursor branch in bin/fm-supervision-instructions.sh. The original brief also asked to route cursor's native preCompact for the compact case; see the SUPERSEDED SCOPE section below - that half has been CUT by explicit owner decision and is NOT part of this change.
3. G5, the one substantive gap the report identified - teach the away-mode path the same idle-to-busy / "ctrl+c to stop" transition acknowledgement the crew steer path already uses, keyed on the token transition rather than the composer-empty verdict cursor never produces. The explicit instruction was to genuinely TRY the ack, and if a primitive truly could not work, to STOP and escalate the concrete gap with evidence rather than papering over it or quietly shipping cursor-primary as not-away-mode-capable.
4. G6 - lift the cursor launch refusals LAST, only after steps 1-3 landed and live evidence was recorded in docs/verification/supervision.md. Do not lift the --secondmate refusals early.
Also add cursor to the primary-tier tables and adapter facts so the always-loaded contract records that cursor now HAS a hooks system and can be a primary; the report explicitly framed this as an ADDITION rather than a correction, since no existing line was factually wrong (they were all scoped to "has been verified").

Binding constraints accepted for this work: firstmate's coding guidelines apply (one-owner rule for contracts, one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never an em dash, shellcheck-clean bin scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh, no agent co-author on commits). Tests must exercise behavior through an executable interface and must never assert implementation source bytes. The cursor stop and sessionStart hooks are HARNESS-DEPENDENT checks, so they required BOTH a portable tests/ regression using real processes with no harness installed AND a live-harness-optin guard in the bin/fm-test-run.sh family that is env-gated, self-skipping, and fails naming the harness and version - proven against the REAL cursor-agent, never a stub - plus dated per-harness evidence in docs/verification/supervision.md and docs/verification/runtime-backends.md. All live validation had to run in an isolated throwaway firstmate home on a separate tmux server, never against the live home or the fleet's default tmux/herdr session, and hooks were never to be installed at user or global scope because a global hook fires inside every live cursor crew agent in the fleet.

SUPERSEDED SCOPE - READ THIS BEFORE FLAGGING ANYTHING AS MISSING. The preCompact staged-digest feature has been REMOVED from this change by an explicit, current decision of the repository owner, and deferred to a clean follow-up. This is an accepted exclusion, not an omission, not an oversight, and not a regression. Do NOT re-implement it, do NOT restore bin/fm-precompact-cursor.sh or any equivalent adapter, do NOT re-register preCompact in .cursor/hooks.json, and do NOT reintroduce any staged-context path in bin/fm-turnend-guard-cursor.sh. A regression in tests/fm-cursor-primary.test.sh deliberately asserts that preCompact stays UNREGISTERED; that assertion encodes the intended contract and must not be weakened or deleted.

Why it was cut: an earlier review of this same branch surfaced two ask-user concurrency findings in that path - a superseded park could still deliver a duplicate follow-up, and an in-flight staged claim could strand the required post-compaction digest indefinitely. Each attempt to close them enlarged a critical section inside a hook that Cursor AWAITS at the turn boundary, where blocking is the most dangerous failure available. Native preCompact firing was also never observed, because a real compaction could not be forced in the isolated session, so the surface had no empirical basis to justify that risk. The owner therefore directed shipping the proven core only.

The shipping scope of this change is exactly three things, all live-verified against the real cursor-agent: the turn-end follow-up park, the run-tier session start, and away-mode escalation delivery. Cursor's compaction surface is recorded as DEFERRED and uncovered, in the same sense as the Codex interactive TUI, with the static reason stated: preCompact can return only user_message and is absent from Cursor's additional_context step set, so it cannot inject a digest and needs its own design. A cursor primary therefore does not re-emit its digest after a compaction, and that is the intended, documented behavior of this change.

Decisions and findings made while doing the work that a reviewer reading only the diff would not know:

- Step 3 was solved at the ROOT cause instead of the transition-ack path the report proposed, and the result is FULL away-mode parity rather than a documented gap. The report was right that cursor's tmux composer verdict is unknown, but that is true only of the CURSOR-ANCHORED read: cursor parks its terminal cursor below its footer, so tmux's cursor row is not a composer locator. Read cursorlessly - the same rule herdr, zellij, cmux, and orca already use for every harness - the same live capture classifies correctly as empty when idle and pending with real typed text. bin/fm-tmux-lib.sh therefore reclassifies a pane only when it can prove the pane's foreground process is genuinely Cursor, via the existing single owner bin/fm-cursor-lib.sh, so the strict blank-cursor-row posture stays in force for every other harness and a dead shell still never reads empty. That restored a genuine composer-empty proof and the away-mode daemon needed NO cursor-specific branch at all. Verified live: bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh's own inject_msg into a real cursor pane returned 0 and the pane processed the typed escalation.
- Two defects were found by the live run that the report did not predict, and both are fixed here. First, bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh could not locate cursor in the process ancestry, so EVERY cursor session start refused the fleet lock with "cannot locate harness process in ancestry" and produced a read-only digest; cursor's identity is not expressible as a command-name pattern (its installed names are cursor-agent and the far-too-generic legacy alias agent, and it runs as a bundled node script), so the lib now delegates to bin/fm-cursor-lib.sh rather than widening the name regex. Second, fm_supervision_model classified cursor as persistent, so the mid-turn pull guard reported WATCHER DOWN between turns even with a beacon seconds old; cursor's park runs the watcher only between turns, exactly like Claude's Stop auto-arm, so cursor is now classified autoarm, including the FM_SUPERVISION_MODEL value baked into a secondmate launch.
- A hazard this change would otherwise have introduced was found and closed: cursor also loads <project>/.claude/settings.json, so a cursor primary in a firstmate checkout fires BOTH registrations for every event cursor's Claude-compatibility map covers, which would run session start twice and evaluate each PreToolUse seatbelt twice. bin/fm-hook-host-lib.sh lets each tracked Claude-shaped entrypoint stand down on a cursor-delivered payload. The predicate deliberately reads the delivered payload's own cursor_version and NOT the environment, because cursor exports CURSOR_INVOKED_AS, CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR, and CURSOR_VERSION into every child process, so an env guard would also fire inside a Claude session started by hand from a cursor pane and would silently disable Claude's own supervision - the exact hazard docs/turnend-guard.md already records for GROK_SESSION_ID. Claude-shaped Stop does not currently fire under cursor but is guarded anyway, because cursor has no asyncRewake and a future build firing it would run bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh synchronously inside cursor's stop step and hold that turn open for its multi-hour timeout, which is the wedge grok 1.0.0 produced.
- Supersession is a deliberate addition beyond the report's gap list, driven by a live finding: a captain message typed while the hook is parked is accepted and runs its turn immediately, but cursor does NOT terminate the parked hook, so its follow-up is still delivered when the park finally closes. Without handling, every captain message during a park would leak one process and one duplicate wake. state/.cursor-park-owner is a generation baton so the newest stop wins and a superseded park stands down without emitting.
- The two loop bounds nest deliberately rather than duplicating each other: the registered loop_limit (200) is cursor's own ceiling and the only bound that still holds if the adapter is broken or replaced, while FM_CURSOR_TURNEND_LOOP_CEILING (180) sits below it so firstmate's bound bites first and can emit one final loud notice instead of supervision going silently dark at cursor's ceiling. A delivered wake is productive work and resets the separate bounded repair-nag budget; only consecutive unproductive nags consume it.
- preCompact staging was built, then withdrawn under the owner decision recorded in SUPERSEDED SCOPE above. The removal commit is deliberate and complete: adapter, registration, staged path in the park, and tests, with every doc owner updated to describe the surface as deferred rather than shipped.
- A third refusal the report's gap list missed was also lifted, in bin/fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh, so the remote path does not contradict the local one.
- Two pre-existing tests asserted shellcheck cleanliness with a bare shellcheck call, a second and weaker copy of the lint definition that bin/fm-lint.sh owns (it omits --external-sources). They broke the moment these checkers sourced a shared library, and now delegate to that single owner instead. The existing test asserting that a cursor secondmate spawn is refused was replaced with one asserting the new contract: --trust so the home's project hooks load at all, its own home pinned as the workspace, and the autoarm supervision model inherited across the launch.
- Deliberately NOT fixed here, by explicit captain decision: tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh fails with "/export did not complete while calm mode was on". That failure reproduces on a clean clone at the unmodified merge base 4930d2c, so it is pre-existing and unrelated to this change; fixing it would be scope creep and the captain will file it separately.

Delivery: mode=no-mistakes with yolo OFF, so the captain merges. Any ask-user finding must be escalated rather than answered here. The PR must state that homes need a self-update after merge because this changes the running primary supervision surface, and must state explicitly that cursor primary away-mode support is COMPLETE rather than partial.

## What Changed

- Register project-scoped Cursor hooks for run-tier session start, pre-tool guards, and bounded stop-hook watcher parking, enabling primary and secondmate operation.
- Add Cursor-aware process, session-lock, supervision, and tmux composer handling so Cursor primary away-mode escalation support is complete.
- Add portable and opt-in live coverage plus primary-harness documentation, while keeping compaction refresh explicitly deferred; homes need a self-update after merge because the running primary supervision surface changed.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The implementation appears intent-conformant and the prior documentation overclaim is corrected, but the change remains a broad, concurrency-sensitive expansion of core supervision and harness lifecycle behavior.

## Testing

The focused process-level regressions and manual protocol probe validated Cursor turn-end parking, loop bounds and supersession, session-start context, composer/away-mode classification, session locking, and secondmate launch behavior. The credentialed real-Cursor guard self-skipped as designed; it was not opted in because it documents Cursor user-data writes outside the permitted worktree boundary. No baseline test commands were supplied, and the worktree remained clean.

```text
stop_output={
  "followup_message": "⁣FIRSTMATE_OP: v1 watcher: firstmate watcher wake - one supervision event needs a handling turn now.\nstale: product-probe requires attention\n\nRun bin/fm-wake-drain.sh first, handle the wake, then run its exact WAKE_ACK_REQUIRED --ack-through command. Until that post-handling acknowledgement, interruption leaves the wake durable for idempotent re-handling. This stop hook owns watcher continuity: when the handling turn ends, the next needed cycle parks automatically - do NOT run bin/fm-watch-arm.sh after an ordinary wake."

```

title: fix(bin): stop task-scoped chrome-devtools-axi sessions at teardown
body:
## Intent Make browser-session cleanup structural in firstmate so agent-driven browser work stops leaving visible headed Chrome windows on the operator's machine. Incident (2026-08-12): 34 visible Chrome windows accumulated over ~3h of crewmate validation, one at 35h CPU - the WebGL/GPU manual verification via chrome-devtools-axi genuinely needs headed mode (headless Chrome has no GPU), so the window is a necessary tool that nothing ever puts away; a headed session stays alive until something runs 'chrome-devtools-axi stop' with the matching session name. Documenting this in a project AGENTS.md was already tried and relies on every future worker remembering, which is the same weakness as a guard nothing calls. Investigated both candidate seams named in the brief: bin/fm-brief.sh (the generated contract) and bin/fm-teardown.sh (task-worktree cleanup). Implemented both, since they reinforce each other: (1) bin/fm-brief.sh now adds an UNCONDITIONAL line (not gated behind a flag like --herdr-lab, since it's cheap boilerplate for any task, unlike Herdr's rare high-blast-radius lifecycle commands) telling every ship/scout crewmate to set CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_SESSION= when using chrome-devtools-axi and to stop it themselves when done checking. (2) bin/fm-teardown.sh adds a new best-effort Fix 4, stop_task_chrome_devtools_axi_session, that unconditionally runs 'CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_SESSION= chrome-devtools-axi stop' during the existing pre-destructive cleanup sequence (alongside Fix 1/Fix 2), before the worktree is returned. This is the mechanism that cannot be skipped: chrome-devtools-axi's own stop command is a documented no-op when no session by that name exists (verified live), so it is safe to call unconditionally for every ship/scout task regardless of whether it touched a browser, and it performs the tool's own graceful cleanup (releases the port, removes ~/.chrome-devtools-axi/sessions/ state) rather than a blunt process kill. Verified end to end by hand before writing the fix: started a real chrome-devtools-axi session named after a task id, confirmed its bridge.pid and live process, ran the exact function extracted from fm-teardown.sh, and confirmed the process died and the session directory was cleaned up; separately confirmed the no-op path exits 0 cleanly. Investigated whether cwd-based process reaping (the existing Fix 2, which already kills any process whose cwd matches the task's own worktree, and which I confirmed by direct testing DOES already reach the chrome-devtools-axi bridge and its Chrome child since they inherit the launching shell's cwd) would be sufficient alone; concluded it is a useful independent safety net but not authoritative, since it depends on process-tree/cwd fidelity that the officially exposed named-session stop API does not, so Fix 4 was implemented as the primary, authoritative mechanism rather than relying on Fix 2. Added a new colocated test in tests/fm-teardown.test.sh (test_task_scoped_chrome_devtools_axi_session_is_stopped) using a hermetic fakebin chrome-devtools-axi stub, asserting teardown invokes stop with the task-scoped session name; this repo's existing fm-teardown.test.sh and fm-brief.test.sh suites both still pass in full, and bin/fm-lint.sh (shellcheck) is clean. This is firstmate's own shared tracked material (bin/), so firstmate-coding-guidelines applies: one sentence per line in tracked prose/comments, plain dash never em dash, no agent name as commit co-author, shellcheck-clean bin scripts, and tests colocated in tests/ following the existing .test.sh naming and fakebin-stub pattern. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-teardown.sh` gains Fix 4, `stop_task_chrome_devtools_axi_session`, which runs `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_SESSION=$ID chrome-devtools-axi stop` in the existing pre-destructive cleanup sequence (alongside Fix 1 and Fix 2, skipped for `kind=secondmate`). It is best-effort: a missing binary or a failing stop never blocks teardown, and `stop` is a no-op when no session by that name exists. - `bin/fm-brief.sh` adds an unconditional line to both the ship and scout scaffolds telling the crewmate to set `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_SESSION=` before using `chrome-devtools-axi` and to stop that session itself when done, so the session name teardown targets is a contract rather than a hint. - `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` adds a hermetic `chrome-devtools-axi` fakebin stub for all cases plus `test_task_scoped_chrome_devtools_axi_session_is_stopped`, asserting teardown invokes `stop` with the task-scoped session name and still exits 0. `AGENTS.md` records that this covers crewmate sessions only, not a session the primary agent starts itself. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The change is small, best-effort, and cannot block teardown, but its placement after two abort-capable steps and its dependence on the crewmate following brief prose leave the exact incident partly reachable, so it is safe to merge with those as follow-ups. ## Testing `Exercised the change the way an operator hits it: opened a real headed chrome-devtools-axi session named after a task id from a directory outside the task worktree (so only the new named-session stop could reach it), walked away without stopping it, then ran the real bin/fm-teardown.sh for that task - the bridge process and the visible Google Chrome process both died, the session's bridge.pid/port registration was released, and the CLI reported no active session; the same unconditional stop is a clean exit-0 no-op for a task that never browsed. Also generated real ship and scout briefs and confirmed the emitted contract names the session after that brief's own task id, which is exactly the name teardown stops. Both colocated suites (tests/fm-teardown.test.sh, tests/fm-brief.test.sh) pass in full, and the new teardown test fails when pointed at the pre-fix script, so it guards the regression rather than merely passing. Artifacts are the CLI transcript of the real teardown run, the generated brief text, and a screenshot taken through the live leaked session before teardown; an OS-level capture of the Chrome window itself was not possible because this session lacks macOS automation/screen-recording permission and a full-screen capture was deliberately avoided for privacy, so the window's lifecycle is shown by before/after process state in the transcript instead. Minor observation, not a defect in this change: chrome-devtools-axi's own stop leaves a 1-byte snapshot-generation file, so the sessions/ directory itself survives even though the window, process, and port are gone. No transient files were left in the worktree and no browser processes were left running.`

Run tasks-axi done task-x1 --pr PR_URL, then run tasks-axi ready for dependency-cleared candidates, check date gates, and dispatch only work whose blockers are gone and date is due. teardown exit: 0 ## 4. after teardown: nothing left running on the operator's machine $ ps -o pid=,etime=,command= -p $bridge $chrome bridge(72900)=gone headed-chrome(72921)=gone $ ls /Users/inactdev/.chrome-devtools-axi/sessions/task-x1 # the bridge pid/port registration is gone snapshot-generation $ CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_SESSION=task-x1 chrome-devtools-axi browser: no active session ## 5. the same unconditional stop is a clean no-op for a task that never browsed $ CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_SESSION=task-never-browsed chrome-devtools-axi stop status: stopped (no-op) exit: 0 RESULT: PASS - teardown stopped the headed session; bridge and visible Chrome both gone ```

Use gh-axi for GitHub operations and chrome-devtools-axi for browser operations. If you use chrome-devtools-axi, set `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_SESSION=task-x1` first. A headed session (needed for GPU/WebGL checks - headless Chrome has no GPU) stays open as a real Chrome window until something stops it, so also run `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_SESSION=task-x1 chrome-devtools-axi stop` yourself once you are done checking; teardown stops that same named session as a backstop, but only because it carries this exact name. $ FM_HOME=<home> bin/fm-brief.sh task-x2 some-proj --scout If you use chrome-devtools-axi, set `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_SESSION=task-x2` first. ```text $ FM_HOME= bin/fm-brief.sh task-x1 some-proj --mode no-mistakes scaffolded: /tmp/fm-fix4/brief-home/data/task-x1/brief.md (ship, mode=no-mistakes; replace {TASK}) --- generated ship brief: data/task-x1/brief.md (Rules section as the crewmate reads it) --- # Rules 1.
