✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 4 issues (2 warnings, 2 infos) - ⚠️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:2413` - Fix 4 is placed last in the pre-destructive block, after two steps that can either abort teardown or destroy its target first. Under `set -eu`, `conclude_task_no_mistakes_run` (return 1 at bin/fm-teardown.sh:1531) and `reap_task_worktree_processes` (return 1 on lsof failure or on a process surviving 3 passes) exit the script from inside the then-block, so `stop_task_chrome_devtools_axi_session` never runs. tests/fm-teardown.test.sh:1049 already asserts exit 1 for the lsof-error path. Separately, when reap does succeed it SIGKILLs the bridge pid first (the intent states the bridge's cwd matches the worktree), after which stopBridge reads a dead pid, returns false and prints `stopped (no-op)` - so the graceful process-group stop that would reap chrome-devtools-mcp and Chrome together is skipped in the common success path too. This contradicts the header's own claim that Fix 4 is authoritative and Fix 2 is a net. Move `stop_task_chrome_devtools_axi_session` to the first line of the `if [ "$KIND" != secondmate ]` block, before `conclude_task_no_mistakes_run`. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-brief.sh:320` - The intent says documentation "relies on every future worker remembering, which is the same weakness as a guard nothing calls", yet Fix 4 can only stop a session the crewmate actually named $ID, and the only thing establishing that name is the new brief sentence. A crewmate that runs `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_HEADED=1 chrome-devtools-axi open <url>` without the env var (forgotten, or in a subshell/subagent that did not carry it) gets session name `default`; teardown then stops session `$ID`, a no-op, and the headed window survives - the 2026-08-12 incident. Fix 2 only catches it when the bridge's cwd is still exactly the worktree root. bin/fm-spawn.sh:2801 already exports GOTMPDIR into the pane shell before launch, on a channel whose own comment says it reaches "every backend and harness - ship, scout, and secondmate"; adding `export CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_SESSION=$ID` there makes the name structural, and the teardown header's "by construction" claim actually true. Flagging rather than fixing since it changes the seam the author deliberately chose. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:2410` - `if [ "$KIND" != secondmate ]` skips Fix 4 for a secondmate home, but `cleanup_firstmate_home_children` (bin/fm-teardown.sh:2202, called at :2339 under --force) removes each child ship/scout worktree directly and never runs any browser cleanup for them. Those children are exactly the crewmates the brief tells to name a session after their own task id, and their ids are enumerable from `$sub_state/*.meta`. Concrete path: secondmate home with a live child ship task that opened a headed session, `fm-teardown.sh <secondmate-id> --force` -> child worktree removed, child's Chrome window survives. The header's justification ("a secondmate home's own runtime lifecycle is owned by the dedicated process-event and firstmate-home removal machinery") covers the home, not the child tasks - no other machinery stops their named sessions. Narrower than the main path since non-forced teardown refuses while children exist. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:1540` - chrome-devtools-axi session state and port are global per user - `~/.chrome-devtools-axi/sessions/<name>` and a name-derived port (dist/src/sessions.js) - but firstmate task ids are only unique within one home's state dir and are operator-chosen (bin/fm-spawn.sh:893). Two homes on the same machine (main plus a secondmate) can both hold a task named e.g. `auth-fix`. Tearing down one then runs `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_SESSION=auth-fix chrome-devtools-axi stop` and kills the other home's live bridge and Chrome mid-verification; the same collision also makes the two crewmates share one bridge and port while both are running. A home-scoped discriminator in the brief's session name (task id plus a short home tag) would remove both.

title: fix(fm-brief): document keyed status form with the key before the colon
body:
Two workers in a row wrote `needs-decision: [key=slug] ...` because the brief scaffold's status-protocol rule only showed the unkeyed shape while later rules mentioned `[key=<slug>]` without showing its placement.

This documents the keyed form in every scaffold variant that carries the status protocol (ship, scout, secondmate):
- shows the canonical shape `needs-decision [key=chosen-slug]: {summary}` with the tag BEFORE the colon
- describes a complete `[key=slug]` token at the head of the note as an accepted equivalent fallback since #2202 (before-colon wins when both are present) - deliberately no false claim that the after-colon form files under the `default` key
- keeps the unkeyed `{state}: {one short line}` shape documented; `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh` remains the single owner of keyed open/resolved semantics

Test coverage extends tests/fm-brief.test.sh through the executable (generates each brief variant and asserts on its output), never asserting implementation-source bytes.

Validated by the no-mistakes pipeline (review, test, document clean; lint gate approved locally because ShellCheck is absent in the worker environment - CI enforces it). Shipped as a fork PR because the worker credential has no push access to this repo.

title: fix(remote-job): reclaim interrupted lock publications
body:
api_response: body: "## Intent Prevent a remote job worker killed during atomic lock-owner publication from permanently stranding every replacement worker. Reclaim only dot-prefixed mktemp residue created by the existing lock publication paths after the existing stale-owner proof succeeds, preserve all process-identity, quarantine, timeout, no-signal, and no-discard safety boundaries, and add a behavioral regression through the public worker interface. Ship this generic fix to canonical Firstmate through a green PR; never merge it. ## What Changed - Added `worker_discard_lock_temporaries` to `bin/fm-remote-job-worker.sh`, which removes dot-prefixed `mktemp` residue (`.pid.*`, `.start.*`, `.command.*`, `.quarantine.*`) left inside the worker lock directory when a worker is killed between `mktemp` and `mv`. - Wired the discard into `worker_acquire_lock` after the existing stale-owner proof and symlink refusal, immediately before `rmdir`, so a provably stale lock can actually be released instead of failing `rmdir` on a non-empty directory and stranding every replacement worker. - Added a regression case to `tests/fm-remote-job.test.sh` that kills a running worker, plants `.quarantine.aBc123` residue in an aged lock directory, and asserts the next `fm_remote_job_ensure_worker` clears the residue, starts under a fresh pid, and reports identity — verified to fail when the new call is removed. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Additive, tightly scoped 15-line change confined to the single code path that removes the worker lock directory, gated behind the pre-existing stale-owner proof, with identity/quarantine/no-signal boundaries intact and a behavioral regression test through the public worker interface. ## Testing I ran the targeted remote-job behavior suite (`tests/fm-remote-job.test.sh`), which passes in full including the new interrupted-publish regression case, and confirmed that case genuinely pins the fix by deleting the reclaim call and watching the suite fail at exactly that assertion before restoring the tree. For product-level evidence I wrote a harness that drives the same ensure-worker/stage/wait sequence `fm-remote-entrypoint.sh` performs for every `fm-on.sh <route> fm-*.sh` call, against a real fixture checkout and a live worker process, then simulated a worker killed between mktemp and mv: on the base commit every subsequent operator invocation fails permanently with `remote job worker is unavailable`-class errors, while on this commit the next invocation reclaims the lock, starts a fresh worker with a different pid, and returns the job's output with exit 0. No visual artifact applies — this is an SSH-relayed CLI/daemon path, so the CLI transcripts are the end-user surface. Working tree is clean; all evidence lives in the dedicated evidence directory.
Evidence: Operator transcript — BASE 96876db: interrupted publish strands every replacement worker === worker variant: BASE 96876db (before fix) === $ fm-on.sh secondmate fm-report-job.sh # healthy account, first run firstmate remote job ran on the secondmate account [exit 0] serving worker pid=56498 --- simulating a worker killed mid-publication (mktemp done, mv not) --- lock directory left behind: . .. .pid.aBc123 $ fm-on.sh secondmate fm-report-job.sh # replacement worker attempt 1 error: remote job worker did not report ready after startup [exit 64] $ fm-on.sh secondmate fm-report-job.sh # replacement worker attempt 2 error: remote job worker did not report ready after startup [exit 64] $ fm-on.sh secondmate fm-report-job.sh # replacement worker attempt 3 error: remote job worker did not report ready after startup [exit 64] ```text === worker variant: BASE 96876db (before fix) === $ fm-on.sh secondmate fm-report-job.sh # healthy account, first run firstmate remote job ran on the secondmate account FM_HOME=/private/var/folders" truncated: true original_length: 13311

title: fix(bin): resolve crew state by recorded window
body:
## Intent Implement the provided crew-state window lookup handoff for Firstmate. Add the smallest correct behavior change to bin/fm-crew-state.sh: when the argument is not a task ID with matching state/.meta, resolve it through the existing window_to_task helper from bin/fm-classify-lib.sh, then report the resolved task using the unchanged output contract. Both default:w38:p2 and w38 must resolve to the task whose metadata records that window. Unmatched and ambiguous windows must remain explicit unknown results and must never choose arbitrarily. Preserve existing task-ID behavior and the output line shape. Add behavior-level tests in the existing tests style without asserting source text. Do not change wake formatting or stale classification. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` now accepts a recorded window or terminal reference: when the argument has no `state/.meta`, it resolves through `window_to_task` and counts the metadata files whose `window=` or `terminal=` equals the argument, so both `default:w38:p2` and its bare `w38` form report the state of the task that records them. Exact task ids keep their existing path, and the emitted line shape is unchanged. - Zero matches and more than one match both emit the existing `unknown`/`none` result (`no metadata for ` and `ambiguous metadata for `) rather than picking a task. - `docs/configuration.md` records that `fm-crew-state.sh` resolves toward a task rather than an endpoint, and `tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` covers window/terminal references matching the task-id output plus the unmatched and ambiguous unknown cases. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is an 18-line addition guarded entirely behind the existing missing-meta branch, leaves every task-ID path, the emit contract, and all callers (which pass resolved task ids) untouched, and ships behavior-level regression tests that specifically trap window_to_task's arbitrary ${w##*:} fallback. ## Testing I treated "unit tests pass" as insufficient and drove the helper as a supervisor would from the shell, building a fixture where `state/p2.meta` records `window=default:w38:p2` / `terminal=w38` on a real git worktree with a fake `no-mistakes` reporting a running run bound to that HEAD, then asked the same question five ways against both the base and the changed script. Before (base 96876db): `p2` → `state: working · source: run-step · validating (running)`; `default:w38:p2` and `w38` → `state: unknown · source: none · no metadata for …`. After (1174c4d): `p2`, `default:w38:p2`, and `w38` all → `state: working · source: run-step · validating (running)`; `default:w404:p2` → `state: unknown · source: none · no metadata for default:w404:p2`; the two-crew window → `state: unknown · source: none · ambiguous metadata for …` for both the full and bare forms, so `window_to_task`'s suffix fallback can never silently pick one. One setup issue, fixed, not a product bug: running the suite plainly on this host failed at `not ok - empty no-mistakes status triggered extra lookups (0 calls)`. `bash -x` showed `RUN_OUT=error: repo not initialized (run 'no-mistakes init' first)` — this machine's `BASH_ENV=/Users/host/.config/bash/env` prepends `~/.local/bin` to PATH in every non-interactive bash, so the real `no-mistakes` shadowed the test's fake in the one case that deliberately uses a restricted PATH with no `timeout`. Running as `env -u BASH_ENV bash tests/…` fixes it. It reproduces identically with the base script swapped in, so it is pre-existing and environmental; I changed no repo files for it and read (never modified) the machine config. Scope: only the suite covering the changed file was run — no full-repo suite, no linters, formatters, or static analysis. All scratch fixtures lived in `mktemp -d` dirs outside the worktree; the base-script swap was restored and `git status --porcelain` plus `git diff --stat` are both empty. Evidence files were written only under the designated evidence directory.
Evidence: Before/after CLI transcript — crew state by task id, window, and terminal BEFORE - base 96876db $ fm-crew-state.sh p2 -> state: working · source: run-step · validating (running) $ fm-crew-state.sh default:w38:p2 -> state: unknown · source: none · no metadata for default:w38:p2 $ fm-crew-state.sh w38 -> state: unknown · source: none · no metadata for w38 $ fm-crew-state.sh default:w404:p2 -> state: unknown · source: none · no metadata for default:w404:p2 ambiguous (alpha+beta) -> state: unknown · source: none · no metadata for <ref> AFTER - this change 1174c4d $ fm-crew-state.sh p2 -> state: working · source: run-step · validating (running) $ fm-crew-state.sh default:w38:p2 -> state: working · source: run-step · validating (running) $ fm-crew-state.sh w38 -> state: working · source: run-step · validating (running) $ fm-crew-state.sh default:w404:p2 -> state: unknown · source: none · no metadata for default:w404:p2 ambiguous default:w38:p2 -> state: unknown · source: none · ambiguous metadata for default:w38:p2 ambiguous w38 -> state: unknown · source: none · ambiguous metadata for w38 ```text ============================================================== BEFORE - base 96876db ============================================================== fleet state: state/p2.meta (window=default:w38:p2 terminal=w38) -- task id (unchanged behavior) ------------------------------ $ fm-crew-state.sh p2 state: working · source: run-step · validating (running) -- full window reference ------------------------------------- $ fm-crew-state.sh default:w38:p2 state: unknown · source: none · no metadata for default:w38:p2 -- bare terminal reference ----------------------------------- $ fm-crew-state.sh w38 state: unknown · source: none · no metadata for w38 -- window nothing records ------------------------------------ $ fm-crew-state.sh default:w404:p2 state: unknown · source: none · no metadata for default:w404:p2 -- window two crews record (alpha.meta + beta.meta) ---------- $ fm-crew-state.sh default:w38:p2 state: unknown · source: none · no metadata for default:w38:p2 $ fm-crew-state.sh w38 state: unknown · source: none · no metadata for w38 ============================================================== AFTER - this change 1174c4d ============================================================== fleet state: state/p2.meta (window=default:w38:p2 terminal=w38) -- task id (unchanged behavior) ------------------------------ $ fm-crew-state.sh p2 state: working · source: run-step · validating (running) -- full window reference ------------------------------------- $ fm-crew-state.sh default:w38:p2 state: working · source: run-step · validating (running) -- bare terminal reference ----------------------------------- $ fm-crew-state.sh w38 state: working · source: run-step · validating (running) -- window nothing records ------------------------------------ $ fm-crew-state.sh default:w404:p2 state: unknown · source: none · no metadata for default:w404:p2 -- window two crews record (alpha.meta + beta.meta) ---------- $ fm-crew-state.sh default:w38:p2 state: unknown · source: none · ambiguous metadata for default:w38:p2 $ fm-crew-state.sh w38 state: unknown · source: none · ambiguous metadata for w38 ```
Evidence: Transcript generator (builds the throwaway fleet state, worktrees, and fake no-mistakes) ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # End-user demo: ask fm-crew-state.sh for a crew's current state by task id, by # full window reference, and by bare terminal reference. # # Usage: window-lookup-demo.sh
Evidence: Targeted suite result ```text $ env -u BASH_ENV bash tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh … ok - window references resolve to the recorded task ok - unmatched window remains unknown ok - ambiguous windows remain unknown all fm-crew-state tests passed EXIT=0 $ (base bin/fm-crew-state.sh swapped in) env -u BASH_ENV bash tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh not ok - full window reference changed the task state line BASE_SUITE_EXIT=1 ```

⚠️ **Review** - 3 infos - ℹ️ `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:97` - The window/terminal match predicate is now implemented twice: window_to_task (bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:625) already walks $STATE/*.meta with the identical predicate, and the new loop re-walks it only to count matches. Both parse metadata the same way today (grep '^key=' | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2-), so this is currently just a wasted second scan — window_to_task also runs unconditionally at line 97 even when its result is discarded on the ambiguous/zero-match paths. It matters because the two copies live in different files: if window_to_task's matching ever changes (prefix normalization, session-qualified matching), MATCHES could be 1 while RESOLVED_ID names a different task, and the script would report another crew's state as a confident unique match. Line 112 only catches a resolved id with no meta file, not a resolved id pointing at a different existing meta. Fix while keeping window_to_task as the resolver per intent: capture the matching candidate's basename inside the loop and use it to confirm RESOLVED_ID, or move the window_to_task call below the count so it runs only on the unique-match path. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh:1177` - test_window_references_resolve_task asserts only that by_window and by_terminal equal by_id, never what that line is. The assertions are sound as written (unknown-path details embed the queried id, so a resolution regression does produce a diverging line), but the test never states the positive outcome it is protecting. One added assert_contains "$by_id" "state: working" documents the expected state and keeps fixture drift (branch/worktree/FM_FAKE_AXI_STATUS changes) from reducing the comparison to an uninformative all-unknown match. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:752` - Informational, pre-existing, and outside this handoff's stated scope: the 'never choose arbitrarily' guarantee added by this change is local to bin/fm-crew-state.sh. stale_is_terminal still calls window_to_task directly, so an unmatched window falls through to ${win##*:} and can read an unrelated task's .status file. title: feat(delivery): add neutral domain-review consumer
body:
api_response:
  body: "## Intent

Add a narrow provider-neutral extension point for consuming an already completed exact-head domain review as the review input to no-mistakes delivery without carrying any company, product, provider, repository, evidence, or strategy semantics in canonical Firstmate. Use one explicitly selected trusted external consumer and an opaque private handoff; enforce a clean exact repository root, independently resolved repository identity, exact current HEAD, versioned neutral JSON, digest shapes, nonaccepted exit preservation, and allowlisted output that discards extra provider-private fields. Consumption may skip exactly the duplicate no-mistakes review step and must preserve fixes, tests, documentation, lint, branch custody, push, PR creation, CI, captain decisions, red-PR prohibition, merge authority, and invalidation after any change. Keep the policy and protocol with one authoritative owner, add concise triggers and inventories, cover behavior only through public executable and generated-brief interfaces across delivery paths and provider-defined labels, follow Firstmate coding and documentation rules, and ship a green canonical Firstmate PR without merging it.

## What Changed

- Adds `bin/fm-domain-review-consume.sh`, which invokes one explicitly selected trusted external consumer with an opaque handoff and validates the result Firstmate-side: regular non-symlink consumer and handoff files, an exact clean repository root, independently resolved repository identity, exact current `HEAD` (re-bound after the consumer returns), the `firstmate-domain-review-consumption.v1` schema/status/strategy, and digest shapes — preserving nonaccepted exit codes and emitting only allowlisted neutral fields so provider-private data is discarded.
- Wires the policy into the always-loaded surfaces: an `AGENTS.md` trigger plus the new `.agents/skills/consumed-domain-review/SKILL.md` owner (consumption may replace exactly the duplicate no-mistakes review step and nothing else), and `bin/fm-brief.sh` now renders that review-consumption line in generated briefs across delivery modes.

Pipeline review flagged an unrelated self-update doc rewrite and a head/cleanliness rebind gap; both were auto-fixed on the branch, and the recorded verification evidence in `docs/verification/consumed-domain-review.md` was filled in from the final head. Test, lint, and document phases pass.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: All three previously accepted findings are correctly fixed with matching test and verification-doc coverage, the unrelated self-update doc rewrite is fully reverted so the change is now confined to the neutral extension point, and no new defect is present in the added helper or its call sites.

I also generated real briefs for all three delivery modes and confirmed the single policy-gated skip sentence appears only on the no-mistakes path with the surrounding delivery steps intact. Both CLI transcripts are saved as evidence; no linters or static analysis were run, and the temporary fixture repo was rem"

title: feat(update): reconcile fork with canonical upstream
body:
api_response:
  body: "## Intent

Make /updatefirstmate safely reconcile a configured Firstmate fork with canonical https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate main through the existing update and fast-forward owners. Fetch both sources, classify equal, fork-ahead, canonical-ahead, unavailable, or diverged histories, select an automatic target only when one history contains the other, preserve fork-only commits, and stop before moving any primary, linked, standalone, or remote secondmate home when either source is unavailable, histories diverge, a worktree is dirty, local commits would be lost, or a clean fast-forward is impossible. Never push, force, merge, stash, overwrite, discard, or treat text merging as semantic proof. Import only the exact selected commit into standalone homes before applying the same guards, expose distinct source outcomes, keep the existing update owner and documentation owners, cover local and remote behavior through public interfaces, follow Firstmate coding and documentation rules, and ship a green canonical Firstmate PR without merging it.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-update.sh` now fetches both the configured fork origin and canonical `kunchenguid/firstmate` main, classifies the pair as equal, fork-ahead, canonical-ahead, unavailable, or diverged, and only selects a fast-forward target when one history contains the other — stopping before touching any primary, linked, standalone, or remote home when a source is unavailable or the histories diverge, and reporting each source's outcome as a distinct line.
- `bin/fm-ff-lib.sh` takes an explicit resolved commit as its fast-forward base instead of the now-removed `origin` base mode, imports exactly that commit into standalone homes before applying the existing dirty-worktree / would-lose-commits / not-fast-forwardable guards, and routes update fetches through a helper that disables terminal and askpass prompting so an unreachable source fails fast; `bin/fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh` passes the same source-relationship lines back through the remote boundary.
- Extended `tests/fm-update.test.sh` (canonical-ahead reaching linked and standalone homes, source divergence, canonical fetch failure) plus remote-update assertions in the lifecycle e2e, and synced the `updatefirstmate` / `secondmate-provisioning` skills, `README.md`, and the architecture, configuration, remote-secondmates, and scripts docs with the new behavior.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: All four accepted round-1 findings are fixed at the right shared boundaries with no regressions found — the removed origin base_mode has no remaining caller or test dependency, the remote source-line reordering preserves the `tail -1` result contract, and the only residual is a pre-existing ssh-transport gap on a path this branch did not introduce.

## Testing

<code>Ran the targeted suites `tests/fm-update.test.sh` (12 cases incl. the new canonical-ahead, source-divergence, and canonical-unavailable cases), `tests/fm-secondmate-sync.test.sh`, and `tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` — all green. Because unit output alone does not show the end-user experience, I built three throwaway git fixtures and captured real `fm-update.sh` / `fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh update` CLI transcripts: local classification across equal / fork-ahead / canonical-ahead / diverged / canonical-unavailable plus a dirty-secondmate case, the remote code-root-and-home update and its refusal on diverged sources, and the parent-side `remote secondmate <id> on <host>: …` source lines for both success and refusal. Each transcript records HEADs before and after, showing that stops leave every checkout untouched and fork-only work survives. The remote lifecycle e2e cannot complete on this machine due to a pre-existing bash 3.2 limitation that also fails at the base commit; no newer bash is installed and installing one is out of scope, so remote coverage came from the transcripts. No UI surface is involved — this is a shell CLI change, so CLI tran"

title: fix(backend): stop reading every dead tmux endpoint as alive
body:
## The defect

The tmux endpoint-liveness probe was `tmux display-message -p -t "$target" '#{pane_id}'`.

`display-message` is an informational command, not a query.
When its target does not resolve it falls back to the **caller's own current pane** and still exits 0:

```
$ tmux display-message -p -t "=firstmate:=fm-does-not-exist" '#{pane_id}'
%0            <- exit 0, and %0 is the asking pane
```

Measured on tmux 3.7b, it succeeds for a missing window, for a window in a session that does not exist at all, and for a bogus window id.
As a predicate it is very nearly unconditionally true.

The consequence is silent and only surfaces after a crash.
A tmux server crash takes every crewmate with it; the restarted firstmate then recreates a session named `firstmate`, so every recorded `firstmate:fm-<task>` target resolves to the new session's own pane.
Observed live: the session-start fleet digest reported all six dead workers as `endpoint: alive`, `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` reported three of them as actively `working`, and nothing was routed into recovery.

## The fix

Probe with `tmux list-panes -t "$target"` instead.

| Predicate | Missing window | Real window |
|---|---|---|
| `display-message -p -t` | **wrongly succeeds** | succeeds |
| `has-session -t` | correctly fails | succeeds |
| `list-panes -t` | correctly fails | succeeds |

`list-panes` was chosen over `has-session` because it asks the question the caller actually means - is there a pane there - and it discriminates correctly on every target form firstmate records, including bare window ids (`@N`) and wholly missing sessions, where a session-existence check is the wrong question.
The existing exact-match target construction is unchanged; the target string is still passed through verbatim.

The defect had two call sites, kept in agreement only by a `Mirrors fm-backend.sh's ...` comment.
`bin/fm-crew-state.sh`'s `pane_readable` now calls `fm_backend_target_exists` directly for tmux instead of holding a second copy, so the two cannot drift apart again.

## Coverage

`tests/fm-backend-tmux-smoke.test.sh` - the repo's one suite that talks to a real tmux server, isolated on a private socket - now asserts both directions:

- a window that exists reads as existing,
- a window that does **not** exist **inside a session that does** reads as not existing,
- a window in a wholly missing session reads as not existing,
- a window that was real and has been killed reads as not existing.

The second case is the whole defect and is what a future refactor must not regress.
Verified the test genuinely catches it: reverting only the probe to `display-message` fails on
`fm_backend_target_exists reported a missing window inside the live session 'smoke' as existing`.

Three fake `tmux` fixtures (`fm-send-strict`, `fm-crew-state`, `fm-session-start`) modelled only `display-message` and fell through to `exit 0` for every other subcommand, so under a correct probe they answered "alive" for targets their own tests intended to be dead.
They now model `list-panes` with the same liveness rule each fixture already applied to `display-message`.

`fm_backend_agent_state` was already correct and stays correct, confirmed by hand on a throwaway server and asserted in the smoke test:

```
live window       -> agent_state=dead    target_exists=yes
never existed     -> agent_state=missing target_exists=no
killed window     -> agent_state=missing target_exists=no
```

## Validation

- `bin/fm-lint.sh` clean (ShellCheck 0.11.0, the pinned version).
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed --base main`: 57 suites, 1 failure - `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh`, which fails identically on unmodified `main` in this environment (a `comm: input is not in sorted order` locale issue, unrelated to this change and left untouched).

title: Watcher arm can wedge supervision ownership on a stalled watcher child
body:
## Problem

Supervision liveness for the watcher was previously reduced to process existence. If a watcher child stayed alive but stopped producing fresh liveness beacons (a stalled child), the arm layer kept treating it as healthy. A stale watcher lock could then block a new watcher from starting, and supervision ownership stayed wedged until a session restart.

Seen in the field 2026-08-12: supervision went silent with no fresh beacon, and recovery required a restart.

## Fix

PR #2320 changes the arm layer to keep verifying the owned child after start: a live but stale-beacon child is retired with a bounded TERM/KILL sequence (much shorter than the liveness grace), stale ownership is released through the watcher-down recovery transition, and the arm fails loudly so a persistent adapter can retry without a session restart.

## Tests

Ships with updates to tests/fm-watch-arm.test.sh and tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh.

title: feat(bin): add decline and repair paths for decision holds
body:
## Intent Give bin/fm-decision-hold.sh a DECLINE close path, because the captain-decision-hold gate that scout teardown depends on had no way to close a hold the captain declined. SCOPE IS DELIBERATELY BOUNDED AND WAS EXPLICITLY RULED BY THE REQUESTER. A previous run's auto-fix rounds expanded this change into a per-hold atomic close lock, a staging-backlog 'tasks-axi mv' close transaction, a bin/fm-decision-hold-close.mjs helper, and a tasks-axi compatibility floor bump. That expansion was REVIEWED AND REJECTED by the requester and deliberately reverted. The decision, verbatim in effect: this is a low-frequency operator action that needs NO atomic close lock, NO mv transaction, and NO compatibility floor bump, and auto-fixes must not smuggle a tasks-axi floor bump. Concurrency hardening of the close boundary against other tasks-axi writers is OUT OF SCOPE for this change and belongs to separate work. Do not re-propose it, and do not treat its absence as a defect: it is the accepted design. The confirmed gap being fixed: command_resolve requires at least one --routed-to task ('at least one --routed-to task is required'). When the captain DECLINES a held decision there is no follow-up work to route, so resolve cannot express the answer. In the real incident the captain declined two captain-held benchmark decisions (minctx-half-run, upstream-submission); with no routable work they were closed with 'tasks-axi done' DIRECTLY, outside the script. The durable-resolved attestation the script writes was therefore never recorded, so 'fm-decision-hold.sh verify nm-review-benchmark-fullrun-r1' fails with 'captain decision ... is neither actively held nor durably resolved', which BLOCKS that scout's teardown. The three required behaviors, as specified: 1. Decline close path: close a hold with a recorded captain decision file and NO routed work, recording the captain decision into the hold body/attestation and marking the hold durably resolved exactly like resolve does, minus the dependency-edge routing. Implemented as a new 'decline' verb (the brief allowed either 'resolve --decline' or a new verb). 2. Repair path: repair a hold already CLOSED OUTSIDE the script, where the backlog item is Done but the durable-resolved attestation is missing and verify fails. It records the missing durable-resolved state with a decision file so verify passes, without reopening or re-routing. Implemented as a new 'repair' verb. 3. Do NOT weaken the gate. Only a genuinely declined/resolved/repaired hold passes; both new paths require a real captain decision file and must not let an un-decided hold slip through. Deliberate decisions a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: - Stated correction to one premise in the original request. It asserted that a genuinely UNANSWERED hold, still actively held with no decision recorded, must still FAIL verify and block teardown. That is not the existing design and was deliberately NOT changed: verify_hold_durable treats an ACTIVELY HELD hold as durable, because the hold itself is the durable Captain's Call record and is designed to OUTLIVE the investigation. The pre-existing regression 'captain holds are idempotent, distinct, teardown-safe, Bearings-visible, and durably routed before close' tears down an origin while both holds are still open, so making verify fail there would break the documented lifecycle. The gate property pinned instead: no path may reach the durably-resolved state without a real captain decision, and neither new verb may close or repair a hold that is still actively held. This was flagged to and accepted by the requester. - repair requires surviving captain-hold provenance (hold_kind=captain), not just kind=captain and state=done. This was a review finding the requester explicitly decided to FIX: without it, an ordinary captain-kind task that was never held could be closed, repaired, and then pass verify. tasks-axi preserves hold_kind through a close, so it is the surviving proof of a real captain hold. - decline REFUSES while any task in the same backlog is still blocked by the hold, and points at resolve, because tasks-axi automatically clears blocked_by edges when the blocker closes; declining a hold with routed work would silently release that work without recording it, which is what resolve exists to record. The dependency scan uses 'tasks-axi list --fields blocked_by' as a cheap prefilter (first column is always an unquoted id) and confirms every candidate against its own 'tasks-axi show --full' record, because list rows quote titles and multi-entry blocked_by values. This is a best-effort check at a low-frequency operator action, NOT a concurrency guarantee, by explicit decision above. - repair takes NO --routed-to: once a hold is Done, tasks-axi has already cleared its edges, so any routed identity claimed at repair time could not be verified, and recording an unverifiable claim would weaken the record. Routed context belongs in the decision file text. - Both new paths reuse resolve's existing digest-based retry identity, so an exact retry is idempotent while a changed decision is rejected. A declined or repaired hold records '(none)' as the routed identities; slug validation rejects parentheses so no real task id can collide with that token. A new 'Resolution mode:' line (routed|declined|repaired) makes the durable record self-describing; verify_resolution_identity's existing strict parse is unaffected and records written by the previous version still validate. - Fixed a small pre-existing formatting wart in the shared body builder: command substitution stripped the newline before the routed-work list, so entries rendered as 'Routed work:- task-id' on one line in backlog.md. Each entry now gets its own durable line. - Duplicated resolution-record matching and blocked_by normalization were factored into single helpers (body_has_resolution_record, normalized_blocked_by) per the repo's one-owner rule. - Ownership split kept as required: bin/fm-decision-hold.sh is the single owner of the mechanics (header and --help updated for the new verb surface), .agents/skills/decision-hold-lifecycle/SKILL.md is the single owner of the policy (updated for when to decline and when to repair), docs/decision-hold-lifecycle.md records the mechanism plus refreshed verification evidence, and docs/scripts.md's one-line table entry was updated. Regression tests, all exercising the real fm-decision-hold verbs through the executable interface in a scratch FM_HOME with synthetic 'sample' identities, never asserting implementation source text. This is harness-agnostic shell, so a portable tests/ regression is sufficient and no live-harness guard is needed. The three mandatory cases: - 'a declined decision closes with a recorded answer and no routed work': declined through the new decline path with a decision file and no routed work, then verify PASSES and Bearings drops it from the open Captain's Call. Also covers empty/missing decision file refusal, idempotent retry, drifted-decision rejection, refusal while work is still routed, and resolve still rejecting a no-routed-to invocation. - 'a decision closed outside the script is repairable and then clears teardown': reproduces the exact incident by closing the hold with a direct 'tasks-axi done', asserts verify FAILS and real scout teardown REFUSES while preserving state, then repair with a decision file makes verify pass and teardown succeed. Mandatory case. - 'an unanswered decision still blocks completion and resists both unrouted close paths': an uninventoried unresolved decision still fails complete, verify, and teardown; decline and repair both refuse when no hold exists; repair refuses a still-actively-held hold, leaving it queued and held with no resolution record; and repair refuses a closed captain-kind task that was never held. Mandatory case. - The pre-existing resolve regressions, including the routed close path and the quoted blocked_by edge cases, are unchanged and still pass (12 of 12 in the suite). All three new gate guards were mutation-checked: removing the repair open-hold guard, the repair provenance guard, or the decline routed-work guard each makes the suite fail. Verified locally: bash tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh (12 ok), plus fm-fleet-snapshot-view, fm-bearings-snapshot, fm-brief, fm-teardown, fm-documentation-audiences, bin/fm-lint.sh (ShellCheck 0.11.0 pinned), bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh, and git diff --check. Out of scope, deliberately: the real repair of nm-review-benchmark-fullrun-r1's two declined holds is a main-home operation on state that does not live in this worktree and must not be attempted here; the main firstmate runs it after this merges. tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh currently fails on '/export did not complete while calm mode was on', which reproduces identically on unmodified main at 85cefa9 with Pi 0.84.1 and is unrelated to this change. Delivery: the requester merges. Do not merge. ## What Changed - Add `decline` to record a captain decision and close a hold without routed work, while refusing holds that still block dependent tasks. - Add `repair` to durably attest captain holds closed outside the script, requiring a decision file and preserved captain-hold provenance. - Document the unrouted close lifecycle and add regression coverage for decline, repair, retry safety, and gate protections. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-bounded, implements the required decline and repair paths with decision and provenance guards, and introduces no substantiated material source risks. ## Testing The focused 12-case lifecycle regression and an end-to-end operator flow confirmed decline persistence, repair of an out-of-band close, strict refusal before repair, cleared Bearings state, and successful teardown; the inspected diff also had no whitespace errors.

title: fix(bin): surface buried wake status lines once
body:
## Intent Fix a wake-surfacing gap where an answer to a question Firstmate itself asked can be silently buried. This is firstmate shared tracked material: the wake drain and status-classification machinery (bin/fm-wake-drain.sh, bin/fm-wake-lib.sh, bin/fm-classify-lib.sh). The incident to reproduce and fix: a status file received a note: answer line, then immediately a routine note: line (an unrelated re-read acknowledgement). A subsequent wake drain annotated ONLY the newest line (the routine re-read note); the substantive answer note directly above it was never surfaced. Two enablers: (1) the drain annotation surfaces only the newest line of a status file, not all new lines since the last acknowledgement; (2) note: lines never fold into OPEN DECISIONS, so an answer to a question Firstmate asked has no other surfacing path. Requirements: 1. A drain must surface ALL new status lines since the last acknowledgement, never just the newest. If a full change to that is too broad, at MINIMUM surface every unanswered pending-reply resolution and every note: line since the last ack (do not drop the substantive lines behind a routine newest one). 2. It must NEVER re-surface an already-handled line as new. Bias fail-toward-showing-MORE (never silently drop a new line) but also never re-present already-handled work as if new. Use the durable last-ack cursor/handled markers the machinery already keeps; do not content-guess. 3. Keep every existing surfacing behavior intact (the wake-queue records, signal/stale/check wakes, the OPEN DECISIONS fold for needs-decision/blocked). This is additive, not a rewrite. Regression tests are required and must exercise the real drain/classify functions (source the libs, no harness) with the exact incident shape and assert observable output: (a) a note: answer followed by a routine note:, last-ack cursor set before both, drain surfaces BOTH (or at minimum the answer note), not only the newest routine line; (b) already-acknowledged lines are NOT re-surfaced on the next drain; (c) a brand-new note after an ack IS surfaced; (d) the existing OPEN DECISIONS fold for needs-decision/blocked still works. A portable tests/ regression is sufficient because this is harness-agnostic shell: the drain logic decides WHICH status lines to surface. Run bin/fm-lint.sh and shellcheck before done. Delivery: mode=no-mistakes, yolo OFF, captain merges. Escalate any ask-user finding; do not answer them. Note in the PR that this changes running wake-surfacing machinery, so homes pick it up after merge plus a firstmate self-update. Also note in the PR that a portable tests/ regression is sufficient. Stop at CI green. Cursor commit attribution is off globally, so no co-author trailer is expected. Implementation choice made while doing the work: dumping every new working:/done: line fleet-wide on every drain, including empty-queue, would break the existing silent empty-queue contract. The accepted minimum is therefore: queued-signal annotations now emit every unread line since the open-decisions presentation cursor (not only the newest), and a fleet-wide UNREAD STATUS section (including empty-queue) surfaces still-unread note: lines and reserved-key pending-reply resolutions once, then the existing cursor advances so they are not replayed. OPEN DECISIONS for needs-decision/blocked is unchanged. ## What Changed - Surface every unread status line in queued-signal annotations and add a fleet-wide `UNREAD STATUS` section for unread `note:` lines and pending-reply resolutions, while preserving `OPEN DECISIONS` behavior. - Track presentation with transactional identity/offset cursors, locking, and teardown cleanup so handled lines are not replayed and uncertain reads fail toward showing more. - Add portable `tests/` regressions exercising the real drain/classification functions and document that running homes pick up the wake-surfacing changes after merge plus a Firstmate self-update. ## Risk Assessment 🚨 High: The implementation still violates the core never-re-surface invariant through a concrete, ordinary status sequence and should not merge without resolving that behavior. ## Testing Exercised the real wake drain/classification path, cursor failure and symlink cases, wake-record preservation, complete unread annotations, non-replay after acknowledgement, new-note surfacing, and unchanged OPEN DECISIONS behavior; targeted tests and the end-user CLI demonstration passed. Per phase rules, lint and shellcheck were not run in this test phase.
Evidence: End-to-end wake-drain transcript showing both incident notes, no replay, a new note, and OPEN DECISIONS ```text END-TO-END WAKE DRAIN EVIDENCE 1) Queued signal after answer note + routine note (both must surface): 1786646681 1 signal crew-answer.status signal: crew-answer.status wake annotation: unread wake-EVENT since last drain, not current state: crew-answer.status: note: captain answered: use REST not RPC wake annotation: latest wake-EVENT observed at drain, not current state: crew-answer.status: note: routine re-read acknowledgement UNREAD STATUS (new since last drain, not re-printed after this presentation): crew-answer note: captain answered: use REST not RPC crew-answer note: routine re-read acknowledgement 2) After generation-bound wake acknowledgement, immediate drain (must not replay handled notes): [no stdout] 3) Brand-new note plus buried OPEN DECISION on a later empty-queue drain: UNREAD STATUS (new since last drain, not re-printed after this presentation): crew-answer note: brand-new follow-up after acknowledgement OPEN DECISIONS (still open, folded from the durable status logs - not just the latest line): crew-answer [key=transport] needs-decision: confirm REST transport OPEN DECISIONS: close one by answering it: bin/fm-send.sh --resolve-key '' ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 error - 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:263` - Requirement 1 says every unread note/pending-reply resolution must surface, but unread presentation and cursor advancement are separate scans after releasing the wake lock. Concrete path: `print_unread_status_section` scans through offset M; a writer then appends a `note:` answer; `print_open_decisions_section` sees that append and advances the shared cursor past it, although notes produce no OPEN DECISIONS output. The next drain therefore treats the unseen answer as handled. Combine snapshot/read/fold advancement at a shared boundary and advance only to the captured endpoint that presentation processed. - 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:103` - The accepted minimum requires surfacing every unread `note:` and pending-reply resolution, but the 4000-byte cap omits later lines and then `print_open_decisions_section` advances the cursor across them. The omission count does not surface their substantive contents, and they can never appear on a later drain. Do not advance the presentation cursor beyond the first omitted line, or otherwise preserve omitted lines for a subsequent drain. 🔧 Fix: Fix unread status cursor races and overflow 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:734` - The required “never silently drop a new line” invariant remains reachable: if the unread-span Perl read fails, `status_new_lines_since_cursor` converts that failure into empty success; `print_status_sections` then runs the independent open-decisions scan, whose retry can succeed and advance the shared cursor past the unseen note. Propagate unread read/presentation failure and prevent cursor advancement, or read and fold one successfully presented snapshot chunk at a shared boundary. - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:527` - Replacing the incremental `tail -c` read with Perl invalidates `test_read_failure_never_silently_returns_empty`, which still injects failure through a fake `tail`. The read now succeeds and advances the cursor, so the test's unchanged-cursor assertion will fail. Update the behavioral fault-injection seam to target the actual byte reader, preferably through an explicit overridable helper. 🔧 Fix: Preserve cursors when status span reads fail 4 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:730` - Requirement 1 says new notes must never silently drop, but a transient `wc -c` failure returns successful empty output. `print_unread_status_section` then succeeds, and the independent OPEN DECISIONS scan can retry successfully and advance the cursor past the unseen note. Propagate this failure so no cursor advances unless the captured unread span was read successfully. - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:679` - Requirement 2 forbids re-presenting handled lines as new, but an existing cursor whose `cat`, identity, or size read transiently fails is treated as offset 0. If the subsequent reads succeed, all historical `note:` lines before the durable acknowledged offset are emitted again. Distinguish a genuinely missing cursor from an unreadable existing cursor and abort presentation without advancing on the latter. - 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:111` - A failed stdout write does not fail `print_unread_status_section`: later loop iterations and the final shown-count check overwrite `printf`'s status. The OPEN DECISIONS fold then advances the cursor even though the note was not emitted, permanently dropping it. Check every presentation write and prevent cursor advancement after any output failure. - 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:190` - The requested shared snapshot/read/fold boundary is still split into two status-span reads. Concrete path: the unread read succeeds and prints a note, the second read in `status_open_decisions_incremental` transiently fails, that helper returns trusted state as success without advancing the cursor, and the next drain presents the already-handled note again as new. Reuse one successfully captured span for both presentation and folding, and commit its endpoint only after successful presentation. 🔧 Fix: Make status presentation transactional under I/O failures 4 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh:1138` - The required “NEVER re-surface an already-handled line as new” invariant still fails in queued-signal annotations. If reading an existing durable cursor transiently fails, `fm_wake_status_cursor_offset` converts the error to offset 0; `fm_wake_print_annotations` then labels historical handled tail lines as unread wake events. Propagate the cursor error and skip/fail annotation enrichment rather than treating it as a genuinely missing cursor. - 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:181` - Status presentation is not serialized after the wake-queue lock is released. Concrete path: drain A snapshots endpoint M; a writer appends through N; drain B presents and commits N; A then commits its older M cursor. The next drain re-presents M..N as new. Add a shared status-presentation lock spanning snapshot, output, and cursor commit, or compare-and-refuse stale cursor replacement at the shared commit boundary. - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:669` - The claimed error-safe transaction commits task cursors through independent `mv` calls. After all unread lines have been printed, a successful first move followed by a failed later move leaves the later task at its old cursor, so its already-presented lines are replayed next drain. Use one atomically replaced durable presentation manifest, or another commit boundary that cannot partially acknowledge the fleet snapshot. - 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh:1165` - The accepted implementation explicitly requires queued-signal annotations to emit every unread line since the cursor, but this reads only the final 8192 bytes (and the later global/read caps omit more). For a queued status containing more than 8192 bytes of unread working/done lines, older lines appear in neither annotations nor UNREAD STATUS, while the presentation cursor advances through them. Preserve all queued unread lines or leave omitted bytes unacknowledged for a later drain. 🔧 Fix: Simplify unread status cursor and presentation locking 3 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:814` - The required “NEVER re-surface an already-handled line as new” invariant remains reachable during supported status-file rotation. The snapshot records an inode, but `status_new_lines_since_cursor` ignores that identity: if the file is replaced after snapshot capture but before this read, replacement lines are printed; the later commit rejects the changed inode, so the next drain prints those same lines again. Validate the captured identity before presentation or serialize rotation with the presentation boundary. - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:646` - The new shared manifest retains task rows after `fm-teardown.sh` removes the task status and legacy cursor. If that task ID is later reused and the filesystem reuses its device/inode identity, this code trusts the stale offset and silently skips that prefix of the new status log. Retire the task's manifest row transactionally during teardown, or use a non-reusable status generation identity. - 🚨 `tests/fm-wake-drain-open-decisions-cursor.test.sh:253` - This regression expects empty output and an unchanged fold cursor when reading the per-task fold cache fails, but `status_open_decisions_incremental` deliberately treats that failure as an invalid cache, refolds the authoritative log, prints the still-open decision, and advances over the appended working line. The test will therefore fail and also mistakes the intentionally recurring OPEN DECISIONS section for replayed unread status. Assert that no handled UNREAD STATUS line is replayed while the open decision remains visible, or restore explicit abort semantics in the implementation. 🔧 Fix: Align cursor failure regressions with transactional presentation 3 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:814` - The snapshot records each status inode, but the unread read validates only size. If a supported status-file rotation occurs after snapshot capture, replacement lines can be printed from the new inode; the later commit rejects the old snapshot identity, causing those handled lines to be presented again next drain. Validate snapshot identity before reading, or serialize status replacement with the presentation lock. - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:646` - The shared manifest retains a task row after teardown removes that task's status and legacy cursor. Because task IDs are reusable, filesystem inode reuse can make a new status log match the stale identity and offset, silently skipping its initial bytes. Retire the manifest row during teardown or persist a non-reusable task incarnation identity. - 🚨 `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:189` - Annotations are emitted before the unread and OPEN DECISIONS scans complete. Concrete path: a queued note is successfully printed as an annotation, the subsequent unread-span read fails, and no manifest commit occurs; after acknowledging the queue, the next empty drain presents that same handled note as new UNREAD STATUS. Build the complete presentation successfully before emitting any section, using one captured status span per task. 🔧 Fix: Retire stale presentation cursors during task teardown 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:728` - This contradicts the requirement to “keep every existing surfacing behavior intact … signal … wakes.” Concrete race: a task appends `done: shipped`; before the watcher acquires the wake-queue lock to publish its signal, an empty-queue drain snapshots the status, selectively prints neither `done:` nor an annotation, and commits this endpoint for every task here. The later direct signal then sees its cursor at EOF and emits only the raw `signal: task.status` row, permanently losing the existing latest-event annotation and its substantive status text. Do not acknowledge routine bytes that were not presented, or serialize signal publication and presentation at their shared boundary so a direct signal retains its event content. 🔧 Fix: Preserve routine status until signal annotation 2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:730` - This contradicts “It must NEVER re-surface an already-handled line as new.” If an unread routine line precedes a `note:`, the note is printed by UNREAD STATUS, but this code resets the committed endpoint to the old cursor because the routine line was not presented. Every subsequent empty-queue drain therefore prints the handled note again. The same occurs with `needs-decision`, `working`, then `note:`. A contiguous cursor cannot both preserve the unpresented prefix for a later signal and acknowledge the later note; use a durable handled marker/range for presented informational lines or coordinate status append and signal publication at a shared boundary. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-line-cap-lib.sh:14` - The owner comment says UNREAD STATUS has a global byte cap and omission disclosure, but this change deliberately removed those caps to surface all unread bytes. Update this comment and AGENTS.md's “bounded UNREAD STATUS” wording so maintainers are not directed toward the forbidden capped behavior. 🔧 Fix: Correct unread status cap documentation 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:730` - This contradicts “It must NEVER re-surface an already-handled line as new.” If an unread routine line precedes a `note:`, UNREAD STATUS prints the note, but this resets the endpoint to the old cursor because the earlier routine line was not presented; every later empty-queue drain therefore prints the handled note again. Historical signal annotations have the same issue because only `direct` tasks are marked fully presented. A contiguous cursor cannot preserve an unpresented prefix while acknowledging a later presented note; use durable handled ranges/markers or coordinate status append and signal publication at their shared boundary.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-wake-drain-unread-status.test.sh tests/fm-wake-drain-open-decisions.test.sh tests/fm-wake-drain-open-decisions-cursor.test.sh` (initially exposed two regressions; passed after fixes) - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-wake-queue.test.sh` (updated obsolete capped-output expectations, then passed) - `Manual end-to-end drain: queued an answer note followed by a routine note, acknowledged the wake, drained again to verify no replay, then appended a new note and needs-decision to verify both UNREAD STATUS and OPEN DECISIONS output`
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Lint** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ linter found issues (exit code 1) 🔧 Fix: Fix wake surfacing ShellCheck warnings ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: feat(herdr): add passive no-mistakes observer panes
body:
## Intent Implement the captain-approved live no-mistakes observer for Firstmate Herdr tasks. Only when explicit local config/herdr-no-mistakes-observer-panes is present, automatically create exactly one adjacent unfocused right-hand Herdr pane for an ordinary ship task with a live task pane and a matching active no-mistakes run for that task branch and current code identity. The pane displays no-mistakes attach --run in the task isolated worktree. It is visual-only and must never start, restart, cancel, answer, approve, fix, or run a validation pipeline. Keep lifecycle in one focused helper, atomically bind task id, run id, session, task pane, observer pane, and worktree in a private sidecar, reuse only a fully agreeing live sidecar, and refuse ambiguity without duplicates. Remain inert and unsupported on non-Herdr backends. On terminal runs, disappeared task endpoints, and normal cleanup, close only the exact verified observer pane after proving it is neither the task pane nor the active captain pane, then retire the sidecar only after confirmation. Missing, stale, conflicting, or unreadable sidecars never authorize closure. Do not alter presentation journals or task ownership, recovery, or delivery. Cover executable behavior for idempotence, disabled/non-Herdr no-op, terminal and mismatched runs, stale sidecar refusal, safe cleanup, and task-pane preservation. Use only isolated Herdr labs for tests and never touch the default session or active project pipelines. ## What Changed - Adds an opt-in Herdr helper that creates one unfocused right-hand `no-mistakes attach` observer pane only for a matching active task run, with an atomic sidecar binding its task, run, pane, session, and worktree identities. - Reconciles observers while tasks are actively validating and retires only verified observer panes on terminal runs, vanished endpoints, or teardown while preserving ambiguous, stale, or conflicting sidecars. - Documents the local configuration flag and adds isolated Herdr and watcher coverage for idempotence, no-op paths, retries, and safe cleanup. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The observer lifecycle is conservatively bound, serialized through teardown, and the changed executable coverage addresses the previously identified ambiguity, attach-retry, non-Herdr, mismatch, and busy-watcher paths. ## Testing Real isolated-Herdr lifecycle testing passed: one unfocused adjacent observer, idempotence, disabled/non-Herdr/mismatched no-ops, stale-sidecar refusal, terminal cleanup, task-pane preservation, attach retry, and ambiguous-split quarantine. The focused watcher reconciliation scenario also passed. The disposable headless Herdr lab has no screenshot endpoint, so saved runtime transcripts provide the reviewer-visible evidence; the worktree remains clean.
Evidence: Real Herdr observer lifecycle ```text ok - enabled matching Herdr run creates one unfocused passive observer with an exact sidecar ok - observer creation is idempotent for the complete live binding warning: herdr no-mistakes observer: task task metadata is unreadable or conflicting; preserving sidecar ok - conflicting metadata preserves the exact observer sidecar and pane warning: herdr no-mistakes observer: task observer sidecar is stale or conflicting; refusing a duplicate viewer ok - stale sidecar refuses duplicate creation and remains quarantined warning: herdr no-mistakes observer: task sidecar run binding is stale or unreadable; preserving it ok - stale cleanup never closes the task or observer pane ok - terminal matching run closes only the exact observer pane and preserves the task pane ok - mismatched branch is inert ok - enabled preference remains inert for non-Herdr tasks ok - disabled preference is inert warning: herdr no-mistakes observer: task observer attach command could not start; retaining its exact sidecar for retry ok - pending attach retries in its exact bound pane without a duplicate warning: herdr no-mistakes observer: task split response was ambiguous; preserving its quarantine reservation warning: herdr no-mistakes observer: task observer sidecar is stale or conflicting; refusing a duplicate viewer ok - ambiguous split responses remain quarantined without duplicate panes all fm-herdr-no-mistakes-observer tests passed ```
Evidence: Watcher observer reconciliation ```text ok - a busy task reconciles its observer without waiting for staleness ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 4 issues found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-herdr-no-mistakes-observer.sh:271` - A successful split with an ambiguous/mismatched pane response is left unbound; the next reconcile sees no sidecar and splits again, so duplicates remain reachable. This contradicts the required “refuse ambiguity without duplicates” behavior. Persist a non-closure-authorizing quarantine/reservation before a split can be retried. - 🚨 `bin/fm-herdr-no-mistakes-observer.sh:279` - If `pane run` fails after sidecar publication, the code retains a fully reusable sidecar. Every later reconcile returns through the reuse path and never attempts to display `no-mistakes attach`, leaving the only observer pane blank for the live run. This contradicts the required “pane displays no-mistakes attach --run <run-id>” behavior; the recovery state needs an explicit, safe policy. - 🚨 `tests/fm-herdr-no-mistakes-observer.test.sh:136` - The required executable coverage for “disabled/non-Herdr no-op” is incomplete: the test removes the opt-in file before invoking the non-Herdr case, so the result is explained by disabled configuration and never proves the non-Herdr guard while explicitly enabled. - 🚨 `tests/fm-herdr-no-mistakes-observer.test.sh:84` - The required executable coverage for mismatched runs is absent. The test exercises a stale sidecar run id, but never supplies an `axi status` for a different branch or code identity and proves that no observer is created. 🔧 Fix: Hardened observer reservations and attach recovery 3 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:686` - The required "automatically create exactly one" observer is not reached for every matching live run. Production wiring invokes reconcile only from `crew_absorb_class` after a stale/idle watcher path asks for current state; while the task pane is busy, no reconcile occurs, so a short live run can finish without any observer. Add a lifecycle-aware reconcile trigger independent of stale-pane triage. - 🚨 `bin/fm-herdr-no-mistakes-observer.sh:284` - An existing but malformed or re-bound task metadata file is treated exactly like a disappeared endpoint. For example, changing its backend or Herdr pane makes `task_binding` fail, then this branch calls `retire_exact` with metadata disabled and can close the sidecar pane. This contradicts "Missing, stale, conflicting, or unreadable sidecars never authorize closure." Distinguish an actually absent metadata record from an unreadable/conflicting one and preserve the sidecar in the latter case. - 🚨 `bin/fm-teardown.sh:2388` - Normal teardown releases the observer's per-task and session locks when `retire` returns, before teardown destroys the task endpoint. A watcher can then reconcile a still-active run, create a new observer, and leave that new pane and sidecar behind after teardown removes the task. title: Brief scaffold: forbid shared worktree and pool administration
body:
## The hole

A generated crewmate brief tells the worker:

> Stay inside this worktree; modify nothing outside it.

That is a rule about **files**. A worker can satisfy it completely and still run a `git worktree remove` loop over the pool its own worktree came from. Removing a worktree is not an edit outside a directory - it is a change to administration that every lane shares - so the sentence does not reach the act at all.

When it happens, the lanes that lose their working directory are the ones still running. Commits survive, because pooled worktrees share one repository and the branch refs live in the primary clone, but the working copies do not, and nothing uncommitted is protected by that.

The worker in that situation is not disobeying. It is following a brief that asked it to do something reasonable and never said how not to, and the constraint is easy to write into an individual brief by hand afterwards. The next brief written without it has the same hole, which is why this belongs in the scaffold rather than in one brief.

## What changed

Rule 7 of the ship and scout scaffolds now covers shared infrastructure as one class: the worktree itself, the pool it came from, the repository every lane's worktree shares, and the `no-mistakes` daemon. Rule 2 points at it instead of reading as complete.

**It names the act, not a provider.** Creating, removing, returning, pruning, moving, or reassigning any worktree or pool slot is forbidden. `git worktree add/remove/prune`, `treehouse get/return`, and `orca worktree create/rm` appear as examples, followed by an explicit catch-all for whatever other worktree provider is in use. The supported worktree providers and runtime backends differ in their commands but not in the damage, so a rule written against one provider leaves the identical hole open on every other one - which is exactly the class of failure this change exists to close.

**It says what to do instead.** A prohibition that blocks the only route somebody can see gets worked around. A worker that genuinely needs a second checkout, a worktree or branch removed, or a daemon action stops and reports with `blocked: {what you need and why}`, the same exit the scaffold already uses everywhere else, and firstmate does it.

**It is stated together with the shared-daemon rule**, which the scaffold already carried. Those two are the same class: one instance serving every lane and home, an action that looks local but is global, one owner, and the same exit. Stating them apart would present them as unrelated warnings and teach the shape twice; stated together, a reader who meets one meets the reasoning behind both.

## Test

`tests/fm-brief.test.sh` gains a case that **generates** briefs - all three ship modes plus a scout - and reads the rule out of the generated brief. It does not grep the script, per this repo's rule that tests exercise behaviour through an executable interface and never assert implementation-source bytes.

It asserts the act is forbidden, that the rule reaches a provider it does not name, that at least two providers appear as mere examples rather than as the definition, that the stop-and-report exit is present, that the shared daemon is stated in that rule and mentioned nowhere else in the brief, and that the file-scope rule points at it.

Confirmed non-vacuous: against the previous scaffold it fails on the missing act, and it also fails on variants that drop the unnamed-provider clause or the rule 2 pointer.

`bin/fm-lint.sh` passes (ShellCheck 0.11.0). The brief suite is green, as are the four adjacent suites that consume the scaffold.

## Intent Captain-decided ship (option B, gated): add an UNDOCUMENTED /calm max to Firstmate's Pi Calm presentation layer, as a silent personal dogfood. Feasibility was already proven by a prior investigation; this task implements the accepted spec, it does not re-investigate. Product: /calm becomes three-state instead of a boolean. off = stock Pi transcript (unchanged). on = today's Calm (unchanged): hides thinking labels, owned tool shells, operational rows, and KEEPS mid-turn assistant text. max = today's Calm plus hiding mid-turn assistant working notes. Command surface: deliberately no new top-level command. '/calm max' enters max from any state and repeating it stays max. Plain '/calm' with no argument steps max -> on (the revert the captain explicitly asked for), and keeps the existing on -> off and off -> on toggle. Any other argument keeps the existing toggle rather than erroring, so the command still accepts whatever follows it as it always has. Persistence is THE failure mode this change had to prevent: config/calm now writes 'max' as a literal third value (one trailing newline, same atomic replace as before), and session start / resume / fork / reload must restore max as max rather than treating it as unrecognized and dropping to off. Hide rule, taken verbatim from the prior investigation and proven against the Pi the fleet actually runs (signed 0.84.1): hide assistant text blocks when the message's own stopReason is 'toolUse', and when it is 'length' with tool calls present. Deliberately do NOT hide while stopReason is 'pending' - that would also stop the real reply from streaming - so a brief on-screen flash before the marker flips is an accepted, intended tradeoff, not a defect. title: fix(codex): invoke lifecycle hook scripts directly instead of via login shell
body:
## Intent

Prevent repeated FirstMate Codex lifecycle hook timeouts by removing redundant login-shell wrappers that source operator profiles and can perform slow network credential setup before the real hooks run. Preserve the established SessionStart, PreToolUse, and Stop behavior, including both watcher-arm and persistent-cd safety policies, their stdin contracts, fail-open behavior, host filtering, and primary-checkout scoping. Keep the implementation simple by directly invoking the existing tracked scripts, which already own those responsibilities. Add behavior-level executable-interface regression coverage that fails if a nested login shell returns or stdin stops reaching any lifecycle target unchanged. Do not weaken safety policy coverage or introduce a new abstraction.

## What Changed

- `.codex/hooks.json`: replaced the `bash -lc '...'` wrappers for the SessionStart, PreToolUse (arm + cd), and Stop hooks with a direct `exec ./bin/fm-*.sh` invocation of each tracked script, removing the login-shell payload-buffering/root-verification logic that previously ran before the real hook.
- `tests/fm-codex-hooks.test.sh`: added a new regression test that stubs the four target scripts and a fake `bash`, runs each hooks.json command through `/bin/sh -c`, and asserts it invokes the expected script directly (no nested shell), forwards stdin unchanged, and exits 0.
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh`: registered `fm-codex-hooks.test.sh` in the test family list so it runs with the suite.
- `docs/cd-guard.md`, `docs/sessionstart-nudge.md`, `docs/turnend-guard.md`: updated the Codex integration descriptions to reflect that the hook execs the script directly and the script itself owns root anchoring, rather than the hook wrapper anchoring/verifying the root before dispatch.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is a narrow, well-scoped simplification: I confirmed by reading fm-primary-scope-lib.sh, fm-hook-host-lib.sh, and all four target scripts that stdin acquisition, jq-missing fail-open, Cursor host-duplicate filtering, and primary-checkout scoping are already fully owned internally by fm-sessionstart-run.sh, fm-arm-pretool-check.sh, fm-cd-pretool-check.sh, and fm-turnend-guard.sh, so the removed wrapper checks were genuinely redundant; I also empirically verified against the actual installed `codex` CLI (v0.147.0) that hook `command` entries are spawned via plain `/bin/bash -c \"<command>\"` (no `-l`/login flag — confirmed via `shopt -q login_shell` returning false and `ps -o args=` showing no `-l`), so the explicit `bash -lc` removed here was the sole source of login-shell profile sourcing and its removal fully eliminates that overhead rather than merely reducing it; the new regression test executes the real hooks.json commands and would fail against the pre-fix content (a fake `bash` in PATH would be invoked and exit non-zero) and pass after, giving genuine behavioral coverage of the fix.

## Testing

Ran the new tests/fm-codex-hooks.test.sh both standalone and through bin/fm-test-run.sh (single-script and --check-coverage), all green; additionally proved it is a real regression test by swapping in the pre-fix hooks.json (old login-shell wrapper), observing the expected failure (nested bash intercepted, exit 97), then restoring the fixed hooks.json and confirming it passes again. Verified by reading the four target hook scripts that they independently already implement stdin handling, fail-open, host filtering, and primary-checkout scoping, so the simplified direct-exec hook registration does not drop any safety coverage.

## Pipeline
