title: fix(bin): seed project-less remote homes under Bash 3.2
body:
## Intent Fix the project-less remote-home seed path on Bash 3.2. The reported end-user path is a stock macOS primary running bin/fm-remote-home-seed.sh ... --no-projects to seed a project-less remote second-mate home, reportedly exiting under set -u with PROJECT_NAMES[@]: unbound variable; diagnose rather than trusting that diagnosis. Reproduce the real --no-projects path on actual Bash 3.2/macOS when safely reachable, or document the exact empirical limitation and run the closest representative Bash 3.2 path without calling it equivalent. Compare the failing project-less path with a proven project-bearing seed path and inspect relevant history. Guard every empty PROJECT_NAMES expansion unsafe under Bash 3.2, including the project loop and manifest count, while preserving project-bearing behavior. Add regression coverage through the executable/public --no-projects interface and the project-bearing control path under the oldest supported Bash semantics available to the test. Run focused tests, bin/fm-lint.sh, and required documentation audience checks. Keep origin read-only, push the topic branch only to fork, open the pull request against kunchenguid/firstmate from hsuperman:fm/fm-noprojects-bash32, and do not merge the pull request. The implementation uses an explicit project count and skips the project-array loop when --no-projects is selected; the regression reproduces the pre-fix Bash 3.2 failure and verifies both zero-project and project-bearing manifests. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-remote-home-seed.sh` now tracks an explicit `PROJECT_COUNT` while parsing arguments and uses it for both the `--no-projects`/at-least-one-project validation and the manifest's `project_count` line, and it skips the `"${PROJECT_NAMES[@]}"` loop entirely when `--no-projects` is set — so a project-less seed no longer expands an empty array, which aborts under `set -u` on stock macOS Bash 3.2. Project-bearing seeding is unchanged. - Added `tests/fm-remote-home-seed.test.sh`, which drives the public seed executable through a fake ssh transport under the oldest available Bash (`FM_TEST_BASH_BIN`, default `/bin/bash`) and asserts a `--no-projects` run publishes a `project_count=0` manifest with no `project=` records, plus a project-bearing control run that publishes `project_count=1` with its record. - Registered the new test in `bin/fm-test-run.sh`'s remote family and in the macOS Bash 3.2 CI job, and documented it in the remote second-mates test list. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is narrowly scoped to guarding empty-array expansions on the `--no-projects` seed path, leaves project-bearing behavior byte-identical, adds real behavioral regression coverage through the public CLI on stock Bash 3.2, and I verified by reading the code that no unguarded `PROJECT_NAMES` expansion and no zero-project mismatch remains reachable through `fm-brief.sh` or `fm-remote-home-provision.sh`. ## Testing I diagnosed the failure rather than assuming it, then exercised the real user path: using a genuine GNU bash 3.2.57 interpreter (the same upstream release as stock macOS, obtained from the bash:3.2 image and run on the host so git and the rest of the toolchain stayed available), I ran the public `bin/fm-remote-home-seed.sh ... --no-projects` command against both the base and target source trees. Pre-fix it aborts with the exact reported `PROJECT_NAMES[@]: unbound variable` at the project loop, delivers no provisioning manifest and registers nothing (and silently exits 0); post-fix the same command reports the remote home, ships a `project_count=0` manifest with no project records, and writes its registry line, while the project-bearing control produces an identical `project_count=1` manifest before and after. The new regression test fails on the base commit under Bash 3.2 and passes on the target commit, and passes under Bash 5.3 in both cases, which is why only the added stock-macOS CI job can catch this; the related seed-consuming secondmate tests all pass through the repo runner. This is a CLI/shell change with no rendered surface, so the evidence is CLI transcripts and the delivered provisioning manifest rather than screenshots. Linting and documentation-audience checks were left to their own phases. All transient test material was removed and the worktree is clean.

title: feat(calm): hide mid-turn working notes by default
body:
## Intent Make today's `/calm max` behavior the ORDINARY Calm `on` state and REMOVE `max` entirely, collapsing the three-state presentation level added in PR #2334 back to two-state. The captain ran `/calm max` after #2334 landed, dogfooded it, and decided that mid-turn hide should be the default Calm rather than an opt-in level. Product requirements: - `off` is stock Pi transcript, completely unchanged. - `on` is the previous ordinary Calm PLUS hiding mid-turn assistant working notes. - The hide rule itself is EXACTLY #2334's `max` rule and must NOT change: hide assistant `text` blocks when the message's own `stopReason` is "toolUse", and when it is "length" with tool calls present; never hide while `stopReason` is "pending" (suppressing streaming text would also stop a genuine reply from streaming). The change moves that hide from the max-only path into the ordinary on path. - Remove the `/calm max` command argument entirely. Plain `/calm` is the on/off toggle again, with no argument parsing for "max" and no third state. - `config/calm` persists only `on` / `off`. MIGRATION - the failure mode the captain explicitly flagged: a home upgraded from #2334 may already have `max` persisted in `config/calm`. After this change, reading `max` MUST restore as `on`, NEVER drop to off. The config reader stays tolerant of the legacy `max` value and maps it to on, and a test proves a `config/calm` containing `max` reads as on with the mid-turn hide active. Docs - this deliberately ADVERTISES the behavior, reversing #2334's silent dogfood, because the mid-turn hide is now the default: docs/calm.md states that Calm on hides mid-turn assistant working notes while keeping the final reply and keeping storage, /export, and model context intact; docs/configuration.md's config/calm schema says the written values are on/off again and notes that a legacy persisted `max` is read as on for backward compatibility; docs/calm-mode-feasibility.md drops its now-stale level-scoped `max` wording. Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: do not change the hide RULE, do not keep a `max` command argument or a third state, do not change `off` behavior. Implementation decisions made while doing the work, which a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: - Rather than keeping a two-value string union, the visibility policy owner (.pi/extensions/lib/fm-calm-visibility.ts) was collapsed back to the pre-#2334 boolean shape: CALM_PRESENTATION_LEVELS, CalmPresentationLevel, calmPresentationLevel(), and CALM_MAX_HIDDEN_CLASSES were all removed, and "assistant-working-note" was simply dropped from CALM_VISIBLE_CLASSES. This deliberately keeps the one-owner rule intact - the allowlist alone decides what Calm hides - instead of layering a second level-conditional mechanism on top of it. calmTranscriptClassIsVisible() went back to a single-argument pure allowlist check, which .pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts also consumes. - loadCalmPreference() returns a boolean again and reads `stored === "on" || stored === "max"`, which is the whole migration. - The live tmux E2E assertion for the restored mid-turn message "I will run one command." was intentionally FLIPPED from assert_contains to assert_not_contains, because under the new default that narration must hide against the real Pi renderer; a matching assert_contains was added after Calm is toggled back off to prove `off` behavior is unchanged. The redraw wait loop was extended to wait for that row to disappear so the assertion is not racy. Verification already performed locally: the renderer fixtures were run against a scratch install of Pi 0.84.1 matching the signed fleet build, pinned via FM_PI_PACKAGE_DIR, because the signed app bundle ships no importable dist/ and the global npm install is only 0.80.10. Strict no-emit typecheck passes against Pi 0.84.1, bin/fm-lint.sh and bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh are clean, and the exported /export artifact was decoded and Chrome-rendered to confirm the newly hidden working note is still fully present in both the session JSON and the rendered DOM. KNOWN PRE-EXISTING FAILURE, deliberately not fixed here: tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh's live tmux E2E fails at "/export did not complete while calm mode was on". This was reproduced on unmodified origin/main at the merge base, so it is NOT caused by this change. The export itself succeeds and writes a correct 292KB artifact; only the transient "Session exported to: ..." footer status line the test waits for is no longer present under Pi 0.84.1. The captain has filed it as a separate follow-up and explicitly instructed not to widen this change to fix it. If the Test or CI step hits this failure, treat it as a pre-existing merge-base failure rather than a regression in this diff. Delivery: firstmate shared tracked material, mode no-mistakes, yolo OFF - the captain merges. This changes the running Calm default, so homes pick it up after merge plus a firstmate self-update. ## What Changed - Make ordinary Calm `on` hide mid-turn assistant working notes while preserving streaming text, final replies, stored messages, and exports. - Remove the `max` presentation level and return `/calm` and persisted preferences to a two-state `on`/`off` model. - Read legacy persisted `max` preferences as `on`, with updated documentation and renderer coverage for migration and unchanged Calm-off behavior. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change cleanly collapses Calm to two states, preserves the exact hide rule and off behavior, migrates legacy max preferences to on, and adds behavior-level coverage and matching documentation. ## Testing Targeted Pi 0.84.1 renderer, migration, persistence, toggle, tmux UI, and export checks demonstrated the two-state behavior end-to-end: ordinary Calm hides mid-turn notes, off restores stock rendering, legacy max migrates to on, and hidden content remains stored and exportable; temporary test files were cleaned and the worktree remained clean. - Evidence: Side-by-side real Pi 0.84.1 Calm-on and Calm-off terminal rendering (local file: /var/folders/0k/bf8mwt2n5qddzk24r20gfk0c0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZYGHE0E9EHVJ1Y23QHCQ13F/calm-on-off-visual.png)

Preserve known unsupported harness ceilings such as Grok, but make any requested effort an adapter cannot deliver explicit at spawn time and record verified delivered-profile provenance so task metadata cannot silently imply launch delivery. Adopt the preserved r1 fix and review series onto a new r2 branch without deleting or rewriting the preserved branch, resolving against current origin/main behavior. title: fix(bin): serialize recorded special-key input with Codex effort switching
body:
## Intent

Advance the Codex effort-switch feature from the current fork `main` (`4930d2c`) through a fresh correction branch.
Recorded-task `bin/fm-send.sh --key` transactions now participate in the same per-task endpoint input lock as ordinary text sends and `bin/fm-codex-effort.sh`, while explicit unrecorded endpoint behavior remains unchanged.

## What changed

- Added the recorded-task input lock to the public `fm-send --key` path.
- Kept the lock held through special-key delivery and the existing Escape composer-clear and interrupt-bookkeeping transactions.
- Added deterministic public-interface regression coverage for recorded-task `Enter` racing the effort helper.
- Retained coverage for Muse `Escape` composer clearing and Claude `Escape` interrupt bookkeeping racing ordinary sends.
- Reconciled the effort-switch implementation with current fork-main code, including durable recovery, teardown cleanup, runner mapping, and current Codex 0.147 footer evidence.
- Explicit backend targets still bypass recorded-task bookkeeping and the task input lock.

## Validation evidence

Passed:

- `bash tests/fm-codex-effort.test.sh` - all effort, recorded `Enter`, Muse `Escape`, and Claude `Escape` races passed.
- Focused runner execution of send, effort, control, backend, teardown, watcher-lock, documentation, and runner suites - all behavior assertions passed except the environment limitations below.
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` - `ok surfaces=69 local_links=243`.
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` - `FM_TEST_COVERAGE ok total=144 parallel=24 serial=108 serial_shards=4 herdr=12`.
- `git diff --check main...HEAD` and `bash -n` for all changed shell files.
- Complete diff review against `main` (`4930d2c`) found no unexpected files or whitespace/syntax defects.

Environment-limited:

- `bin/fm-lint.sh` - blocked because pinned ShellCheck `0.11.0` is not installed (`ShellCheck not found`).
- `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh` - blocked in its absent-Herdr fixture because this host has an absolute `/usr/sbin/herdr` (`herdr 0.8.0`).
- `tests/fm-backend-tmux-smoke.test.sh` - tmux `3.7b` starts, but its task shell did not complete setup.

Not run by instruction: no-mistakes, Herdr lifecycle operations, merge, default-branch modification, or force-push.

## Scope

- Base: `pranaypratyush/firstmate:main` at `4930d2c`.
- Branch: `fm/firstmate-pr1-special-key-lock-correction`.
- The existing `fm/firstmate-codex-effort-switch-rebase` branch was not modified.

title: feat(spawn): add --linear-issue for Orca worktree creation
body:
## Intent Add first-class Linear issue linking when Firstmate creates an Orca-backed worker. The normal bin/fm-spawn.sh path must accept one optional Linear issue identifier or URL, document it in the script-owned help and header, and pass the exact value to the existing orca worktree create --linear-issue option so the worktree is linked at creation time. Preserve existing behavior when omitted. Reject use on another backend with a clear error rather than silently ignoring it. Keep backend interfaces minimal and do not add broad configuration, other issue trackers, or speculative support. Add executable regression coverage through the public spawn/backend interface for exact forwarding, omission, and unsupported-backend behavior; tests must assert behavior rather than source text. Review all supported backend and harness integration surfaces affected by this spawn option and keep unaffected paths unchanged. Update docs/orca-backend.md only if operator-facing current behavior needs it, while exact flag mechanics remain owned by fm-spawn help/header. Run focused tests, bin/fm-lint.sh, documentation checks for prose changes, and the relevant broader suite. Commit the implementation, validate it through no-mistakes to green CI, and report the full PR URL. Prefer the existing fake-Orca/backend regression harness as evidence and use a disposable real Orca smoke only if tests cannot safely prove the boundary. ## What Changed - `fm-spawn.sh` accepts an optional `--linear-issue ` on ship and scout spawns and passes the exact value through to `fm_backend_orca_worktree_create`, which appends `--linear-issue ` to `orca worktree create` so the worktree is linked as Orca creates it. Omitting the option leaves the existing create command byte-identical. - The option is refused with a specific error instead of being ignored when the resolved backend is not `orca`, and on `--relaunch`, `--secondmate`, and batch dispatch; an empty value is also rejected. Usage lines and the script header document the new flag. - `tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh` covers exact forwarding through the fake-Orca harness, absence of the flag when unset, refusal on `backend=tmux` before any backend mutation or metadata write, and the relaunch/secondmate/batch refusals. `docs/orca-backend.md` notes that Orca-created worktrees can be Linear-linked and points flag mechanics at `fm-spawn.sh`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Additive, tightly bounded optional flag with a single forwarding call site, byte-identical behavior when omitted, four reachable pre-mutation refusals for every path where it cannot take effect, and behavior-level regression coverage through the public spawn interface. ## Testing Ran the focused Orca backend suite (40 tests, including the change's three new spawn regressions) and the batch-spawn suite (5 tests), both green. Because passing unit tests alone don't show the operator experience, I also drove `bin/fm-spawn.sh` end-to-end against the repo's fake-Orca CLI and captured the actual command lines Firstmate issues: a ship spawn with `--linear-issue` emits `orca worktree create … --linear-issue <exact-url> --json` and exits 0; the same spawn without the flag emits the unchanged command; a scout spawn forwards the value identically (a surface the new tests don't cover, sharing the single call site at bin/fm-spawn.sh:2089); and `--backend tmux --linear-issue` fails with `--linear-issue requires backend=orca; resolved backend is 'tmux'` having made zero backend calls and published no metadata. Two fixture gaps surfaced and were fixed in my evidence script rather than the product — this gate worktree exports `NO_MISTAKES_GATE` (needing the harness's `FM_GATE_REFUSE_BYPASS=1`) and the synthetic project needed a real `origin` remote to clear the stale-base check. `fm_backend_orca_worktree_create` has exactly one caller, so no other backend or harness surface is affected. Linting and documentation checks were deliberately not run; they fall outside this phase.
Evidence: End-to-end CLI transcript: Firstmate --linear-issue → orca worktree create ## 1. Ship spawn WITH --linear-issue $ fm-spawn.sh linearshipe1 <project> claude --backend orca --mode no-mistakes --yolo off --linear-issue https://linear.app/acme/issue/ENG-42/link-at-create exit status: 0 -- orca CLI commands Firstmate issued -- orca worktree create --repo id:repo-ship-linear --name fm-linearshipe1 --no-parent --setup skip --linear-issue https://linear.app/acme/issue/ENG-42/link-at-create --json ## 2. Ship spawn WITHOUT --linear-issue (existing behavior preserved) $ fm-spawn.sh linearshipe2 <project> claude --backend orca --mode no-mistakes --yolo off exit status: 0 -- orca CLI commands Firstmate issued -- orca worktree create --repo id:repo-ship-plain --name fm-linearshipe2 --no-parent --setup skip --json ## 3. Scout spawn WITH --linear-issue $ fm-spawn.sh linearscoute3 <project> claude --backend orca --scout --linear-issue https://linear.app/acme/issue/ENG-42/link-at-create exit status: 0 -- orca CLI commands Firstmate issued -- orca worktree create --repo id:repo-scout-linear --name fm-linearscoute3 --no-parent --setup skip --linear-issue https://linear.app/acme/issue/ENG-42/link-at-create --json ## 4. Refused: --linear-issue on a non-Orca backend $ fm-spawn.sh linearrejecte4 <project> claude --mode no-mistakes --yolo off --backend tmux --linear-issue ENG-42 exit status: 1 -- operator-facing error -- error: --linear-issue requires backend=orca; resolved backend is 'tmux' -- backend mutation attempted? -- no: refused before touching any backend -- metadata published? -- no ```text # Evidence: Firstmate --linear-issue -> orca worktree create --linear-issue Linear issue under test: https://linear.app/acme/issue/ENG-42/link-at-create ## 1. Ship spawn WITH --linear-issue ### ship + --linear-issue (exact value must reach Orca) $ fm-spawn.sh linearshipe1 claude --backend orca --mode no-mistakes --yolo off --linear-issue https://linear.app/acme/issue/ENG-42/link-at-create exit status: 0 -- orca CLI commands Firstmate issued -- orca worktree create --repo id:repo-ship-linear --name fm-linearshipe1 --no-parent --setup skip --linear-issue https://linear.app/acme/issue/ENG-42/link-at-create --json ## 2. title: feat: make Herdr the default runtime backend
body:
## Intent

Make Herdr the repo-wide default and verified reference runtime backend for new Firstmate spawns, while preserving tmux as a fully supported, spawn-capable, explicitly selected legacy backend.

Keep new-spawn selection and recorded-endpoint compatibility distinct: an unconfigured new spawn defaults to Herdr and records backend=herdr, while an existing metadata record without backend= continues to resolve as tmux.

## What Changed

- Changed new-spawn resolution to explicit --backend, then FM_BACKEND, then config/backend, then runtime auto-detection, then Herdr.
- Made auto-detected tmux print the opt-out notice while default or auto-detected Herdr remains silent.
- Preserved the legacy absent-backend metadata interpretation as tmux and made new default Herdr metadata explicit.
- Made Herdr, jq, and treehouse the default resolved-backend toolchain, with tmux required only when tmux is selected.
- Reframed Herdr as the default verified reference backend and tmux as the fully supported legacy opt-in alternative.
- Kept Herdr active limits and all tmux-specific safety, liveness, submit, composer, test, and verification coverage intact.

## Changed Surfaces

- AGENTS.md: runtime-backend selection, default, auto-detection, and reference-status guidance.
- CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md: Herdr-first setup and pinned installer guidance, with tmux retained as the opt-in alternative.
- bin/fm-backend.sh and bin/fm-spawn.sh: selection order, notices, metadata compatibility contracts, help, and required tools.
- bin/backends/herdr.sh: reference-backend framing while preserving adapter limits and behavior.
- bin/backends/tmux.sh: legacy verified-backend framing without reducing support.
- docs: configuration, architecture, backend guides, script references, verification evidence, examples, and documentation-audience ownership.
- CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml installs pinned Herdr for default-path end-to-end coverage and retains tmux for tmux-specific tests.
- tests: default and selection assertions now expect Herdr, default spawn metadata requires backend=herdr, and tmux behavior remains covered through explicit selection.

## Judgment Notes

- Herdr reference status means it is the default and fully supported backend. It does not mean limit-free: the documented OpenCode busy-queue gap, lack of mid-session liveness, ghost or placeholder dependence, and colliding-label limits remain explicit.
- The supervisor and away-mode backend axis did not change. FM_SUPERVISOR_BACKEND detection still prefers TMUX_PANE, then the Herdr pane markers, then the warned legacy firstmate:0 tmux fallback; away mode still supports only tmux and Herdr supervisor panes.
- CI now installs Herdr through the pinned bin/fm-install-herdr.sh path for default-path end-to-end coverage. tmux stays installed so explicit-tmux and tmux-specific regression coverage remains intact.

## Validation

- bin/fm-lint.sh passed with the repository-owned ShellCheck version.
- bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh passed.
- Backend, bootstrap, session-start, spawn, and tmux-specific suites passed.
- The guarded real-Herdr family passed through bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh with the default fleet session unchanged.
- no-mistakes review, tests, documentation review, lint, and fork push passed.
- GitHub CI is awaiting upstream approval for this fork PR; no merge action is requested here.

title: feat: add captain-message continuity routing

## Intent Re-deliver the captain-message continuity router through the no-mistakes pipeline, starting from an already-validated head, so the router that lands is the fixed one and its PR passes the `PR must be raised via no-mistakes` provenance check. The captain-message router routes an incoming captain chat message relative to primary-session open asks, so a late or unrelated reply does not silently steer the wrong turn. It is not watcher continuity. `docs/captain-message-router.md` is the authoritative description. An existing PR (branch `fm/captain-message-router-pr`) carries an EARLIER, BROKEN version of this work. Every CI check on it is green except `PR must be raised via no-mistakes`, which fails on provenance because the branch was pushed by hand rather than produced by a pipeline run. This branch deliberately does NOT build on that branch and must never be rebased onto or merged with it. A later no-mistakes run already implemented and validated the fixes but its PR was never raised. That run's head was preserved as commit 10c2674ea4591d0f94366e04af34ff306f0d1780, and this branch was created directly at that commit. Relative to the broken PR's version, this validated head fixes: - The spawn failure: the old code passed the entire assembled prompt (~8.6 KB, unbounded as session briefs accumulate) as a single argv argument to `cursor-agent`. The fix writes the prompt to a mode-0600 temp file and passes only a short instruction naming that file, so no chat history, session brief, or captain message rides the process list and no argument-size limit applies. This temp-file handoff is deliberate and must not be "simplified" back into an argv expansion such as "$(cat "$prompt_file")". - Timeout bounding through `bin/fm-timeout-lib.sh` (whole process group, exit 124 on the bound) instead of depending on a `timeout`/`gtimeout` binary being installed, so the bound also holds on stock macOS. Depending on an external timeout binary is a rejected approach. - Atomic pending-route staging with rollback, and a fail-open failure row when publication fails, instead of silently returning success. - A secret-redaction defect in the keyword-lookahead logic. - Self-reroute protection: a router that names the current session as its own reroute target now degrades to `same` with `confidence=det` and a recorded failure, instead of failing to parse. Acceptance criteria this change must satisfy: 1. The delivered branch descends from 10c2674ea4591d0f94366e04af34ff306f0d1780, not from `fm/captain-message-router-pr`. 2. `tests/fm-captain-message-router.test.sh` passes offline with no credentials. 3. The live regression `tests/fm-captain-router-live-e2e.test.sh` (env-gated by FM_CAPTAIN_ROUTER_LIVE_E2E=1, self-skipping without credentials) passes with a real model call and records `confidence=model`, with no `router agent exited` row in that run's `failures.log`. 4. The full prompt never appears in process arguments; this is asserted through behavior rather than by reading the code alone. 5. The router remains fail-open in every failure path: a spawn error, timeout, unparseable reply, or staging failure must let the captain's message through against the current session with `confidence=det` and a recorded failure row. The captain is never locked out. Invalid CLI usage exiting 2 is the single deliberate non-fail-open path. 6. The router never runs from a child crew worktree, a scout worktree, or a no-mistakes gate agent; only a primary home. The existing primary-scope and gate-refuse guards are deliberate and must be preserved. Deliberate scope decisions a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: - The starting head was independently verified as already correct: the offline suite passes 30/30, the credentialed live regression returns `verdict=same target=sess-router confidence=model` with a non-empty explanation and an empty `failures.log`, and both `bin/fm-lint.sh` and `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` are clean. Because nothing was proven broken, no further code changes were made on purpose - the instruction was to fix only what those runs prove is broken. - Do not redesign the router and do not add capability. Scope is limited to re-delivering the validated head through the pipeline. - Router runtime state under `state/captain-router/` is local-only and deliberately untracked; it must not be committed. - No real credential, token, or captain message content may appear in a test fixture, a log, or a commit. - Do not weaken, skip, or disable any CI check, and do not edit the `Require no-mistakes` workflow (`.github/workflows/no-mistakes-required.yml`). The `PR must be raised via no-mistakes` check must pass on its own because the pipeline raised the PR, never by being bypassed or worked around. - Unrelated in-flight work (a Blender AXI benchmark and broader context-continuity work) must be left untouched. ## What Changed - Add a Pi primary-session hook and Bash router that maintain open-ask anchors and per-session briefs, classify captain messages as `same`, `reroute`, or `new`, and stage cross-session handoffs. - Keep routing fail-open with validated targets, self-reroute normalization, primary-only and gate-agent guards, private redacted model handoffs, process-group timeouts, and atomic pending-route publication. - Wire the router into Pi session-start checks and secondmate launches, document its runtime contract, and add offline behavioral and opt-in live-model regression coverage. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The fixes are narrowly scoped, close all previously identified reachable failure paths, preserve the required safety boundaries, and add behavioral regression coverage without weakening provenance controls. ## Testing Baseline manual probes demonstrated argv privacy, fail-open behavior, rollback, and scope guards; the focused offline suite and credentialed real-model E2E also passed with `verdict=same target=sess-router confidence=model`, a recorded explanation, and an empty failure log, while the provenance workflow remained unchanged from the base and the required validated-head ancestry still failed.

title: fix(bin): defer a terminal failed run-step to a later declared pause once custody is returned
body:
## Summary

An obsolete no-mistakes run's terminal `failed` verdict outranked a later declared `paused:`/`blocked:` status event in `bin/fm-crew-state.sh`'s current-state reconciliation, so a crew legitimately parked after rerouting delivery (e.g. a denied push, custody recovered via `axi sync --recover`, delivery continued via a fork PR) kept short-cadence stale-escalating as failed. Live incident: fm-key-position's run failed on a push step (upstream denies direct push), delivery rerouted via a fork PR, custody was recovered, and the crew declared `paused: ... external wait` - `fm-crew-state.sh` kept reporting `failed` regardless.

**Chosen precedence rule:** a declared `paused:`/`blocked:` status event defers a terminal `failed` run-step only when `no-mistakes axi sync --check`'s structured output confirms the branch's custody was returned (`state`/`safety` both read `custody_returned`, worktree clean). This is read directly from the already-captured `axi status` output on the `RUN_SOURCE=full` attribution path; the narrower `RUN_SOURCE=coarse` (cross-branch) path does not get the override, since its captured data can belong to a different branch. Any unconfirmed, errored, or non-matching custody check fails closed to the run-step's `failed` verdict, and the rule never touches working/parked/done, so an active or current run always keeps outranking status prose.

A related pre-existing bug was also fixed in `bin/fm-watch.sh`'s `pause_state_class()`: an authoritative `paused` verdict was being discarded back to `none` by a liveness gate whenever the crew's agent was confirmed alive, so a live parked crew never actually got the bounded pause cadence - only a dead one did. Fixed with a minimal early return for `class=paused`, mirroring the existing `class=working` early return.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` - 57/57 passing, including new coverage for the paused/blocked override, fail-closed cases (stranded custody, dirty worktree, unavailable check, never-needed-recovery), and the coarse-path narrowing
- [x] `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` - 50/50 passing, including a new regression test for a live agent's declared pause being absorbed rather than surfaced
- [x] `bin/fm-lint.sh` clean (shellcheck)
- [x] Validated end-to-end through the no-mistakes pipeline itself, including recovering this branch's own custody after an identical push-denial (see commit history)

title: fix(bin): bind worker ownership to leased Treehouse worktrees
body:
## Intent

Diagnose and unblock Firstmate worker launches that enter an already-selected clean Treehouse slot but verify ownership against a different dirty slot. The operator-aligned incident selected verified-clean Treehouse slot 35 for a captain-authorized fixture task; two ordinary supported worker launches entered slot 35, while launch verification resolved unrelated dirty slot 2 and stopped before publishing ownership. Failed shells were removed, slot 35 remained clean and available, and unrelated slots were preserved.

Prefer no code change, and first determine from current script help, documented interfaces, and executable behavior whether one supported Firstmate launch invocation can bind verification and ownership publication to the worker already-selected slot. If such an invocation exists, prove it in an isolated representative fixture with a selected clean slot corresponding to 35 and an unrelated dirty slot corresponding to 2, report the exact safe invocation and evidence that the resulting worker identity resolves to the selected slot, and make no tracked change or PR. If no supported invocation exists, validate the committed smallest durable repair: preserve the one-owner contract for path and task identity resolution rather than adding another resolver; review every supported runtime backend and worker harness integration affected by the changed owner rather than patching only Pi on Herdr; and use executable regression coverage reproducing selected-slot-versus-unrelated-dirty-slot behavior and proving publication succeeds or refuses against the correct selected slot.

Validate the committed repair with focused tests, repository lint, documentation checks, and the relevant complete test owner. Keep all accepted safety constraints: do not modify, clean, return, reuse, or launch into any Arena slot or project copy; do not inspect or expose project secrets; preserve unrelated local branches, worktrees, processes, and runtime resources; use only the named non-default Herdr lab helper/session contract for task-specific Herdr lifecycle behavior; the Arena second mate alone owns retrying the fixture worker and only after a supported invocation is proven or this repair has landed. Do not merge. Open a PR only after the repair clears the no-mistakes pipeline and report the PR when CI is green.

## What Changed

- `fm-spawn.sh` now leases non-Orca ship/scout worktrees through Treehouse, validates the allocator-returned path, retries and verifies the worker endpoint’s `cd`, and preserves active leases after aborted launches.

- Reworked shell regression fixtures to cover stale or unrelated pane paths, exact leased-path publication, backend targeting, isolation guards, and harness/trace wiring.

## Risk Assessment

🚨 High: The durable-lease path can strand a selected slot on normal pre-publication failure, breaking task-to-slot recovery and allowing retries to consume additional slots.

title: fm-send falsely reports 'delivery unconfirmed; verdict=pending' for live idle herdr/pi panes (sends actually succeed)
body:
## Summary

`fm-send.sh` returns a **false-negative failure** when steering a live, idle
`herdr`+`pi` worker. It prints:

```
error: text not submitted to default:w1:p7 (delivery unconfirmed; verdict=pending; tried meta=/home/dev/firstmate/state/<task>.meta; backend=from-meta)
```

…exits **non-zero**, but the message **was actually delivered** and the worker
**acted on it** (it executed the exact instructions embedded in the rejected
send). So fm-send delivers successfully every time yet tells the caller it
failed — a false negative, not a send failure.

## Environment

- firstmate harness: pi `0.84.1` (primary on `/home/dev/firstmate`)
- backend: herdr `0.7.4` (socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`), send adapter
  `bin/backends/herdr.sh`
- pi extensions loaded in the worker: `fm-calm`, `@monotykamary/pi-retry`
  (both installed via the project bootstrap)
- gh `2.97.0` authed to github `idevakk` (`repo` scope); git credential helper
  wired to `gh auth git-credential`
- Task: `fix-sysres-disc`, worker pane `default:w1:p7` (herdr),
  `harness=pi, backend=herdr`

## Concrete evidence (captured)

`herdr pane get w1:p7` shows the pane is **live and idle**, not dead/stale:

```json
{ "agent": "pi", "agent_status": "idle", "pane_id": "w1:p7", ... }
```

Live processes exist in the worktree:

```
pid=163814 comm=bash
pid=164130 comm=pi
```

After `fm-send` "failed", a tail read of the same pane shows **the steer text
verbatim in the conversation** plus the worker's acknowledgment and action:

```
PR #4 is already open directly on GitHub at a9e50f5 (iDevakk) - I opened it,
... Reconcile the no-mistakes gate mirror to a9e50f5 by running:
no-mistakes axi sync --recover --keep-local ...

Captain-authorized: PR #4 is already live on GitHub at a9e50f5 (iDevakk) ...
Running the explicitly-authorized axi sync --recover --keep-local ...
No GitHub push, no force.
```

i.e. the text landed and was processed, despite fm-send reporting
`verdict=pending` and exiting non-zero. Repeated sends behave identically.

## Code path

`bin/fm-send.sh` (line ~491):

```sh
elif verdict=$(fm_backend_send_text_submit "$TARGET_BACKEND" "$T" "$MESSAGE" "$retries" "$sleep_s" "$settle" "$EXPECTED_LABEL"); then
  ...
# line ~522
case "$verdict" in ...) ;; ... ;;
  ... ) echo "error: text not submitted to $T (delivery unconfirmed; verdict=${verdict:-unknown}; tried $RESOLUTION_TRIED)" >&2
```

`fm_backend_send_text_submit` dispatches by backend to
`fm_backend_herdr_send_text_submit` (`bin/backends/herdr.sh:2765`).

For an **idle** agent (`bin/backends/herdr.sh:2765`):
- `fm_backend_herdr_send_literal` types the text, then `Enter` is sent in a
  retry loop.
- After each Enter it calls `fm_backend_herdr_wait_for_working`
  (`bin/backends/herdr.sh:3005`) to confirm the agent actually woke up.
- Only a `busy` (working) status confirms delivery; `idle`/`unknown` does not,
  so it retries; after `FM_SEND_RETRIES` (default 3) it yields `pending` →
  fail-closed at fm-send.sh:522.

`fm_backend_herdr_wait_for_working` (`bin/backends/herdr.sh:3005`):

```sh
for ((i = 0; i < polls; i++)); do
  sleep "$interval"          # interval = budget / (polls-1)
  raw=$(fm_backend_herdr_agent_status_raw ...)
  bs=$(fm_backend_herdr_classify_submit_agent_status "$raw")
  case "$bs" in
    busy) printf 'busy'; return 0 ;;   # ONLY this confirms a send
    idle) saw_idle=1 ;;
  esac
done
# saw_idle -> prints 'idle' (not a match in the caller) ; else 'unknown'
```

with budget defaults (`bin/backends/herdr.sh:2986`):
`FM_BACKEND_HERDR_SUBMIT_POLLS=6`, `FM_BACKEND_HERDR_SUBMIT_MIN_SLEEP=0.6`,
so per-attempt confirmation budget ≈ 3.6s; ×3 retries (FM_SEND_RETRIES=3,
FM_SEND_SLEEP=0.4) ≈ ~11s+ total.

## Root cause (hypothesis, strong)

A pi agent that is `idle` (waiting at a prompt) takes longer than the
~3.6s per-attempt confirmation budget to transition `idle → working` after
receiving input. Waking the pi session re-initializes the extension stack
(`@monotykamary/pi-retry` watchdog + `fm-calm`) on top of the pi runtime, and
the native `agent_status` is never sampled as `busy` within the budget. The
`Enter`/text is delivered (herdr `send-keys`), but `wait_for_working` only ever
sees `idle`, exhausts retries, and returns `pending`. fm-send then lies to the
caller.

Two compounding factors make the false negative likely:
1. **Budget too short** for a cold idle pi wake (extension init latency).
2. **Sampling misses the working window**: an `idle → brief busy → idle`
   lifecycle (agent wakes, reads input, idles again quickly) can be missed
   across 6 samples at 0.6s, since only `busy` confirms.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Spawn a pi worker on the herdr backend; let it reach `agent_status=idle`.
2. `FM_HOME=<home> bin/fm-send.sh <task> "<unique-marker-text>"`
3. Observe fm-send print `verdict=pending` and exit non-zero.
4. `herdr pane read <pane>` shows the marker text was received and the agent
   acted on it.

## Impact

- Every steer to an idle herdr+pi worker **falsely fails**; captains are forced
  to work around it (e.g., direct `git push` + `gh pr create`) instead of
  driving the worker.
- Worse: because the caller believes the send failed, the captain may re-send
  or give up, while the worker has already acted — confusing and error-prone.
- The fail-closed surface is correct; the *detection* of failure is wrong.

## Suggested directions for the maintainer

- **Lengthen/extend the confirm window** for herdr: more polls at startup, or a
  graduated budget (idle→working wake is slower than the steady-state send).
  `FM_BACKEND_HERDR_SUBMIT_POLLS` / `FM_BACKEND_HERDR_SUBMIT_MIN_SLEEP`.
- **Treat a confirmed wake-up as success**: after the last retry, do one final
  native `agent_status` read (with a short grace) and, if the agent eventually
  went `busy`, classify the send as confirmed rather than `pending`.
- **Differentiate causes in the error**: "no live target / target gone" vs.
  "text sent but agent did not transition to working within budget" vs.
  "agent went working but sampling window missed it" — only the first is a true
  send failure. Currently all three collapse to `verdict=pending`.
- **Question**: should a false `pending` be caller-retried or treated as
  terminal? If the text was delivered, retrying re-sends duplicates.

## Workaround (in use)

Bypass fm-send for the steer: perform the action directly (e.g. direct
`git push` + `gh pr create`) and monitor the worker pane via `herdr pane read`
to observe/confirm delivery, rather than relying on fm-send's verdict.

title: fix(teardown): spare deliberately detached daemons from the lane reap
body:
## Summary

Task teardown's leaked-process reap no longer kills deliberately detached daemons.

`reap_task_worktree_processes` (Fix 2 in the script header) sends TERM then KILL to every process whose current working directory is under the task's worktree or tasktmp.
A `limactl hostagent` inherits the cwd of the shell that launched it and never chdirs, so a `colima restart` run from inside a task worktree binds the Colima VM's lifetime to that lane, and teardown shuts the VM down.
Observed twice on 2026-08-10.

The reap selector now spares any process carrying **both** halves of the detached-daemon signature:

1. already reparented to init (`PPID == 1`), and
2. leader of its own process group (`PID == PGID`).

An ordinary lane process is still a child of the task's shell or harness, so it fails at least one half and is reaped exactly as before.

## Changes

- `bin/fm-teardown.sh`
  - New `task_pid_is_detached_daemon` predicate reading `ps -p <pid> -o ppid=,pgid=`.
  - The filter is applied inside the shared selector `task_pids_under_roots`, **not** at the kill sites.
    That placement is deliberate: the post-reap check that refuses teardown when processes "remain after N reap attempts" reads the same list, so filtering at the kill sites alone would have left a spared daemon tripping that refusal and blocking every teardown of that lane.
  - Unreadable or non-numeric ppid/pgid is deliberately **not** treated as the signature, so an unverifiable process stays reapable and the reap is not weakened where that read fails.
  - Every spared process is reported once, by pid and command: `teardown: sparing detached daemon for <task>: pid <pid> (<command>)`.
    Deduplicated per pid via a script-level list, because the selector runs several times per reap pass.
  - Behavior and the Colima rationale documented in the script's existing header comment (Fix 2 paragraph). No new documentation file.
- `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` - two colocated behavioral cases driving the real teardown path:
  - a detached daemon (PPID 1 + own group leader) survives teardown, the visibility line is emitted with its pid and command, and an ordinary lane process in the same worktree is still reaped;
  - a reparented process that is **not** its own group leader (only half the signature) is still reaped, and no sparing line is emitted for it.

Nothing else in teardown's semantics changes: unlanded-work refusals, reassigned-slot protection, and the rest of the contract are untouched.

## Validation

Run through the local no-mistakes pipeline; review, test, document, and lint all completed green.
The push step could not reach the upstream repository from this machine (no write access), so the branch was pushed to a fork and this PR opened manually; no pipeline CI ran locally.

Additional local evidence:

- `bin/fm-lint.sh` clean (ShellCheck 0.11.0, the pinned version).
- The two new tests were confirmed **red without the fix** and green with it.
- `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` otherwise passes (58 cases) and `tests/fm-teardown-endpoint-safety.test.sh` passes.

## Known limitation

`bin/fm-teardown.sh` runs `treehouse return --force` a few lines after the corrected reap, on the treehouse-managed worktree path.
`treehouse return` describes itself as "Terminate lingering processes and return a worktree" and terminates by cwd, so on a treehouse-managed lane a daemon spared by this change can still be killed seconds later by that sibling step.
`treehouse` is an external dependency outside this repository, so extending the guard there was deliberately left out of this change and is tracked as separate follow-up work.

## Pre-existing test failure (not from this change)

`tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` contains one failing case, `herdr-preflight-missing-adapter`, reproduced identically on the unmodified tree before any change here.
It passes `FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$ROOT"` while removing `bin/backends/herdr.sh` only from a copied tree, so the copied teardown still resolves the adapter from the real root and does not refuse.
Flagging it because it aborts the suite before later cases run; it is unrelated to this fix.

title: fix(bin): name a provider quota-killed step instead of reporting a bare failure
body:
## Intent Make firstmate able to tell a provider-quota-killed no-mistakes step apart from a genuine step failure, without a human reading pane output. BACKGROUND AND MEASURED PROBLEM. When the account hits its provider session or weekly limit, whichever pipeline step agents are mid-step get killed. The provider CLI prints its limit banner to stdout and exits 1 with an EMPTY stderr, so no-mistakes records a bare 'claude exited: exit status 1:' and marks the step failed. From axi status alone that is indistinguishable from a step that failed on a real defect. A three-day quota analysis measured this at $346 cost-equivalent, 14.4% of the whole window, with 19 step logs carrying 25 limit-hit events and one branch (fm/tbl-table) restarted five times. On 2026-08-09 several stalls went unnoticed for roughly twenty minutes each because the only evidence was a line buried in a pane. SCOPE, AND A DELIBERATE NARROWING THE SUPERVISOR ACCEPTED. The original request also asked for pause-and-resume so a killed step resumes instead of restarting from zero. Investigation established that resume behaviour lives in the no-mistakes pipeline itself, which is a third-party Go repo (kunchenguid/no-mistakes) we have read-only access to. The upstream check was explicitly required before building anything and was done: at main (v1.48.0) this is NOT fixed - internal/agent/retry.go's classifyTransient has needles for rate_limit_error, overloaded_error and HTTP 429/503/529 but nothing matching the limit banner, and because the banner goes to stdout the classifier only ever sees the bare exit-1 with empty stderr. Upstream PR #623 takes a different approach (provider fallback) and is unmerged; issues #407 and #400 describe this bug and are open since early July. The supervisor therefore ruled that THIS change is the firstmate-side visibility half only, and explicitly accepted that it does NOT recover the restart waste and must say so plainly in the PR body rather than reading as the full fix. WHAT THE CHANGE DOES. In bin/fm-crew-state.sh, a run that ALREADY reads failed now gets one further log-tail check, reusing the pattern the file already uses for the ci step (nm_ci_checks_state). When the failing step's log carries the provider's own 'hit your limit' banner, the state reports 'blocked' naming the killed step and the reset time instead of a bare 'failed'. Because the extra read only happens for an already-failed run, the heartbeat path costs nothing. DELIBERATE DECISION: 'blocked', NOT 'paused'. The original tasking said classify a usage-limit exit as a pause. That is correct upstream, where the step genuinely parks and resumes. It is wrong here because nothing resumes: the run is terminally failed and needs a re-run once quota returns, which is firstmate action. In this codebase 'paused' means a bounded external wait expected to clear on its own, and crew_absorb_class maps it to absorb-on-a-long-cadence. Reporting 'paused' would tell the watcher to sit quietly on a run that never comes back, making stalls LESS visible - the opposite of the goal. 'blocked' and 'failed' both map to 'none' in crew_absorb_class, so surfacing behaviour is unchanged; the state just arrives named, with the reset time. This departure from the literal original wording is intentional and was reported to and accepted by the supervisor. EXPLICIT REQUIREMENT: DO NOT WEAKEN ANY OTHER FAILURE PATH. A genuine step failure must still fail loudly. Only the provider's own 'hit your limit' banner reclassifies. Deliberately excluded, each with a regression test: a bare exit status 1 with no banner (the genuine-failure case); a bare SIGTERM/exit 143, because a deliberate axi abort and the daemon reaping lingering run-worktree processes (v1.47.0) produce the same code, so it is ambiguous on its face - this knowingly leaves the report's four SIGTERM kills unrecovered rather than risk swallowing a real abort or crash; transient rate_limit_error/HTTP 429, already retried internally by no-mistakes; a deliberate 'cancelled' outcome; and the coarse runs-list attribution path, which carries no steps table and no log to judge on. REGRESSION TEST PROVEN FAIL-FIRST. Four cases in tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh. Fail-first was explicitly required and was proven, not assumed: with the implementation reverted to HEAD and the new tests in place, the suite reports 'not ok - quota-killed step must not read as a plain failure' with actual output 'state: failed - source: run-step - run failed'. A second commit makes the fixture use the REAL concatenated banner shape taken from ~/.no-mistakes/logs/01KZGYR8NW7NHRW6EJTF7YSD1K/test.log, where the provider writes the banner onto the end of the agent's own prose line rather than on its own line, so a line-anchored matcher fails the test instead of passing against unrealistic tidied input. CONSTRAINTS HONOURED. Shared no-mistakes material, so correctness over speed. The shared no-mistakes daemon was never restarted or reconfigured, and ~/.no-mistakes/repos/ was never hand-modified. No step's behaviour was changed - only how a killed one is classified and surfaced. Local verification: fm-crew-state 33/33 and fm-watch-triage 46/46, both exit 0, clean tree. ShellCheck was NOT run locally (not installed, and disk was down to 1.4GB), so CI lint parity is unverified and the lint step is the first thing that may need attention. DELIVERY. Ship to the benlamlih/firstmate fork as push target with the PR opened against kunchenguid/firstmate main. Do not force anything and do not rewrite the branch - every existing commit stands. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-crew-state.sh`: a run that already reads `failed` now gets one further log-tail check, reusing the pattern the file already uses for the ci step. When the failing step's log carries the provider's own "hit your <window> limit" banner, the state reports `blocked` naming the killed step and a bounded reset phrase instead of a bare `failed`. The extra read only happens for an already-failed run, so the heartbeat path costs nothing. Nothing else reclassifies: a bare exit 1 with no banner, a bare SIGTERM/exit 143, a transient `rate_limit_error`/HTTP 429, a deliberate `cancelled` outcome, and the coarse runs-list path all still report `failed`, each with a regression test. - `bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh`: a run-step-sourced `blocked` now counts as terminal alongside `done` and `failed`, so a quota-killed crew still gets a durable terminal-outcome record and wakes the supervisor - the killed agent appends nothing further, so this scan is its only surfacing path. `blocked` from any other source stays outside the scan. Upward, the parent-channel append reports `done` or `failed` only, with the precise state and quota detail carried in the line's text, because `blocked` would open a keyed decision in the parent ledger that nothing on this path ever resolves. - `tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` and `tests/fm-inactive-reconcile.test.sh` cover the reclassification and each excluded failure path; the quota fixture uses the real concatenated banner shape captured from a live kill, where the provider writes its banner onto the end of the agent's own prose line, so a line-anchored matcher fails rather than passing against tidied input. `docs/architecture.md` and `AGENTS.md` record the new log-tail exception next to the existing ci one. `blocked`, not `paused`, is deliberate: nothing resumes here. The quota window clears on its own, but the run is terminally failed and needs a re-run, which is firstmate action. `blocked` and `failed` both map to `none` in `crew_absorb_class`, so surfacing behaviour is unchanged - the state just arrives named, with the reset time. This is the visibility half only and does **not** recover the restart waste. Resume-after-kill lives in the no-mistakes pipeline, a third-party repo we have read-only access to; at main (v1.48.0) `classifyTransient` has no needle matching the limit banner, and since the banner goes to stdout the classifier only ever sees a bare exit 1 with empty stderr. Upstream PR #623 takes a different approach and is unmerged; issues #407 and #400 are open. A killed step still restarts from zero. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Both round-2 findings are closed at the right boundary - the upward verb invariant lives in parent_report_verb rather than in any one caller, and the charset restriction makes the length cap honest in the same expression that sanitizes - with no loss of the surfacing the change exists to provide, no change to the done/failed upward path, and the four original failure-path regression cases untouched. ## Testing Ran the fm-watch-triage suite against the current pipeline head to close the round-1 ENOSPC gap - it passes clean, so the round-2/3 changes to the parent-report and decision-fold behaviour introduced no regression there - plus the fm-crew-state and fm-inactive-reconcile suites this branch actually touches, all passing. On top of that I produced two CLI transcripts that exercise the real scripts end to end against the genuine concatenated provider banner, showing a quota-killed step reported as blocked with its step and reset time while a genuine failure, a bare SIGTERM, a transient rate limit and a deliberate cancellation all still fail loudly, and showing the killed crew surfacing upward as a terminal outcome without leaving an uncloseable decision in the parent ledger. No visual artifact applies: this change has no rendered UI surface - the end-user surface is the one-line crew-state string and the supervisor's wake queue, both captured verbatim in the transcripts. The host disk problem from round 1 is resolved and no scratch leaked outside the evidence directory.
Evidence: Quota-kill classification transcript (6 scenarios: what the captain sees) firstmate quota-kill classification, end to end worktree HEAD: d87567a == 1. QUOTA KILL - session limit with a reset time (the fix) == --- what the captain sees: fm-crew-state.sh feat-alpha state: blocked · source: run-step · provider quota limit hit during test: resets 7:40pm (Europe/Paris) - run failed, needs re-run when quota returns --- watcher fold: crew_absorb_class blocked -> none == 2. QUOTA KILL - weekly limit banner == --- what the captain sees: fm-crew-state.sh feat-beta state: blocked · source: run-step · provider quota limit hit during review: resets Jul 9 at 9pm (America/Chicago) - run failed, needs re-run when quota returns --- watcher fold: crew_absorb_class blocked -> none == 3. GENUINE FAILURE - bare exit 1, no banner (must still fail loudly) == --- what the captain sees: fm-crew-state.sh feat-gamma state: failed · source: run-step · run failed --- watcher fold: crew_absorb_class failed -> none == 4. BARE SIGTERM / exit 143 - ambiguous, must still fail loudly == --- what the captain sees: fm-crew-state.sh feat-delta state: failed · source: run-step · run failed --- watcher fold: crew_absorb_class failed -> none == 5. TRANSIENT rate_limit_error / HTTP 429 - must still fail loudly == --- what the captain sees: fm-crew-state.sh feat-eps state: failed · source: run-step · run failed --- watcher fold: crew_absorb_class failed -> none == 6. title: status_open_decisions key-fold breaks when needs-decision: puts colon before [key=...]
body:
## Bug

\`_fm_decision_key()\` in \`bin/fm-classify-lib.sh\` extracts the decision key from the substring **before the first colon** in a status line:

\`\`\`sh
_fm_decision_key() {  # <status-line> -> key slug, or "default" when no token
  local prefix=${1%%:*} k
  case "$prefix" in
    *\[key=*\]*)
      ...
```

This only works for lines shaped like \`resolved [key=foo]: text\` (bracket before the colon). It silently falls through to the generic \`"default"\` key for lines shaped like \`needs-decision: [key=foo] text\` (colon before the bracket) -- which is what a crewmate following \`AGENTS.md\`'s own \`needs-decision: {summary of options}\` example naturally produces when it puts a \`[key=...]\` tag inside that summary.

## Impact

Observed live in \`state/xpp-gsi-batch-promote-queued-phases.status\`: three separate \`needs-decision:\` lines each used the \`needs-decision: [key=...]\` form. All three folded into the single generic \`"default"\` bucket, each overwriting the previous one instead of tracking independently. A later correctly-formatted \`resolved [key=github-oidc-stack-gsi-rollout-grant-undeployed]: ...\` line then failed to match anything (the real open entry was keyed \`"default"\`), so \`bin/fm-send.sh --resolve-key <key>\` refused every attempt to close the other two decisions with "no open decision or blocker with that key ... already closed, mistyped, or transferred" -- even though they were never actually resolved.

## Suggested fix

Either:
1. Make \`_fm_decision_key\` scan the whole line for a \`[key=...]\` token instead of only the pre-colon prefix, or
2. Tighten the \`needs-decision:\`/\`blocked:\` scaffold guidance (and any brief-generation template) to require the \`verb [key=...]:\` form explicitly, with an example, so crewmates cannot produce the silently-broken form.

(1) is more robust since it doesn't rely on every crewmate remembering exact placement.

## Evidence

Live file (trimmed) showing three \`needs-decision:\` lines all in the broken \`verb: [key=...]\` form, and a \`resolved [key=...]:\` line in the working \`verb [key=...]:\` form that failed to close anything:

\`\`\`
needs-decision: [key=gsi-irt-status-freeze] ...
needs-decision: [key=gsi-org-seats-prod-orphan-cleanup] ...
needs-decision: [key=github-oidc-stack-gsi-rollout-grant-undeployed] ...
resolved [key=github-oidc-stack-gsi-rollout-grant-undeployed]: ...
\`\`\`

title: fix(herdr): fetch captures as ansi to avoid 0.8.0's scroll-based history harvest
body:
## Problem

On herdr 0.8.0, a text-format `pane read --source recent` against an idle alternate-screen agent triggers the new history harvest: herdr injects real ScrollUp wheel events into the pane for up to 15s and then snaps back to the bottom (herdrdev/herdr#2669, closed as a dup of herdrdev/herdr#2387; the mechanism lives in herdr's `src/server/alt_screen_read.rs`).

Since `fm_backend_herdr_capture` polls agent panes with exactly that read, every visible pane kept scrolling up and snapping back on its own, all day, on herdr 0.8.0.

## Fix

`--format ansi` reads skip the harvest entirely and return herdr's retained rows instantly — the same content the text format returned before 0.8.0 (the harvest did not exist then). The capture now fetches ansi and strips escapes locally with the shared `fm_composer_strip_ansi` (already sourced by the adapter).

The capture test now pins `--format ansi` so a regression cannot quietly reintroduce the scrolling.

herdr has merged a mitigation upstream (herdrdev/herdr#2426, speeds the harvest from ~8.6s to ~0.7s, unreleased as of 2026-08-14), but skipping the harvest on firstmate's high-frequency polls remains the right call regardless.

## Validation

`tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh`: 132/132 pass.

title: fix(afk): make away-mode escalation wedge alarms self-diagnosing
body:
## Intent Diagnose and durably fix the away-mode sub-supervisor escalation-delivery wedge in Firstmate shared tracked material. Three captain-confirmed tmux windows with a Claude Code primary resolved the correct captain pane, buffered captain-relevant escalations, retried without mid-window delivery, raised max-defer alarms, and recovered the queue only on return. Apply diagnostic-reasoning discipline: separate trigger, mask, and symptom; compare against a proven injection path or explicitly record that no retained successful daemon injection exists; empirically test the Claude busy guard, composer-state guard including ghost suggestions, context lines, and queued-message displays, and housekeeping retry cadence against real scratch tmux Claude panes. Preserve related issues #2270 shutdown hang and #2251 watcher-arm wedge as distinct unless directly touched. The daemon must deliver a buffered escalation within one bounded housekeeping interval after the captain pane becomes genuinely idle and empty, or its wedge alarm must identify the exact blocker such as busy, pending, pending-unproven, unknown, target failure, or submit verdict and retain bounded offending pane content in readable and ANSI or hex form so the alarm alone is diagnostic. Add behavioral regression coverage for every composer misclassification found, with the production reproduction as the end-to-end regression. Never inject into a busy turn, genuinely typed composer, dead shell, or otherwise unproven composer. Update the AFK, composer/backend, wedge-alarm, and maintained verification documentation where those contracts live. Evidence established that the affected operational checkout was stale at 833a9a2 and lacked the already-landed shared classifier fix 7f05100: Claude 2.1.226 rendered an idle prompt as the agent glyph plus U+00A0 under LC_ALL=C, which the stale classifier called pending while the current classifier calls empty; current code retries every 15 seconds and real idle gaps are eligible. Preserve that current safe classifier rather than duplicating or weakening it, turn the exact NBSP shape into daemon end-to-end coverage, and make future guard failures self-diagnosing. Captain decided that maintained verification must explicitly record that no retained successful daemon injection evidence exists because the mechanism was defective from first deployment, with the classifier comparison and production-shaped e2e as the diagnostic baseline. Ship through the repository no-mistakes pipeline to a GitHub PR with tests, lint, docs, and CI green; do not merge. Captain deploy-on-green authority is on record for this PR. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh` now records the exact blocker on every failed injection attempt (`busy`, `pending`, `pending-unproven`, `unknown`, `target-missing`, or a `submit-*` verdict) together with a bounded 12-line/4096-byte pane snapshot in both ANSI-stripped readable text and ANSI-preserving hex; the max-defer wedge alarm log line, durable `.subsuper-inject-wedged` marker, tmux status flash, and active alert all name that verdict, and the marker embeds the pane evidence. - The AFK inject e2e fixture now renders Claude Code 2.1.226's byte-exact idle composer shape (`❯` + U+00A0) under `LC_ALL=C` — the production shape the stale classifier misread as `pending` — and `tests/fm-daemon.test.sh` adds max-defer regression tests asserting the exact verdict plus readable and hex pane evidence for busy, pending, and unknown-composer blockers. - Documentation updates: the AFK skill doc states the one-housekeeping-interval delivery bound and consolidates the max-defer contract, `docs/wedge-alarm.md` and `docs/herdr-backend.md` describe the new alarm evidence, and `docs/verification/supervision.md` records the NBSP away-delivery regression diagnosis and that no retained successful daemon injection evidence exists (the classifier comparison and e2e are the diagnostic baseline). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: All new daemon code executes only on already-failing injection paths and adds diagnostics without changing guard or delivery semantics; evidence propagation, marker-consumer compatibility, backend helper existence, and every source-verifiable intent requirement (classifier preserved, NBSP e2e regression, exact-blocker alarm with bounded readable+hex evidence, no-retained-injection baseline recorded, all four doc contracts updated) were verified against the source. ## Testing Ran the three targeted suites named by the change's verification docs (composer classifier, daemon units, real-tmux injection e2e) — all pass; title: feat(linear): add durable event ledger
body:
## Intent

Build the accepted Linear integration design specified by data/fm-linear-integration-design/report.md and replace the eight silent failures documented in data/fm-linear-integration-design/failure-log.md. Nothing the captain says may be lost: persist events durably to the inbox before cursor advancement, with at-least-once idempotent handling. Filter Firstmate writes by author identity and remove the legacy absorb flag, state snapshot, seen file, and createdAt comment cursor. Surface comment edits by content-aware dedupe while ignoring unchanged parent bumps from replies. Route every outbound state, assignee, and comment write through one journaled door, mutate state and assignee atomically, use client-supplied comment IDs for retry safety, verify by read-back, and emit loud wake lines for every unknown or failure. Include behavior tests proving second-poll silence, cursor rewind replay, captain input during a Firstmate write, edited comments, and SIGKILL recovery without half state or duplicate comments. Keep shell scripts shellcheck-clean, tests colocated, Markdown one sentence per line, and do not add agent co-authors. Validate the full pipeline and open a PR with green checks. Do not activate or switch the live Firstmate home to the new mechanism yet: the captain has not reviewed it, and the old poller must continue running until that review.

## What Changed

- Add an opt-in Linear poller that durably records authority-attributed comments and board events before cursor advancement, with content-aware deduplication and loud failure wakes.
- Route Firstmate state, assignee, and comment writes through a journaled command with atomic ownership transitions, stable comment IDs, read-back verification, and crash-safe recovery.
- Wire Linear into bootstrap, watcher cadence, agent guidance, documentation, and regression coverage for idempotent polling, cursor replay, edited comments, concurrent captain input, and SIGKILL recovery.

## Risk Assessment

🚨 High: Captain, the deep-scan bypass can silently replay stale state and regress a newer durable issue head, so the change should not merge without review and correction.

## Testing

Baseline diff inspection, the focused Linear suites, runner integration tests, and two end-to-end CLI evidence scenarios all passed; evidence demonstrates idempotent polling, durable edited input, atomic journaled writes, and SIGKILL-safe retry without duplicate comments, while the source tree and live home remained unchanged.

```text

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

<summary>✅ **intent** - passed</summary>

✅ No issues found.

</details>

<details>
