title: fix(afk): hard-cap away-mode escalation re-injection
body:
## Intent Fix the away-mode sub-supervisor daemon (bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh) so a composer-confirmation false-negative (Claude-primary + herdr backend, issue #2361 family: the digest lands and starts a real turn but the idle composer is briefly misread as still pending) degrades to a SINGLE wedge alarm instead of an all-night (~10h) re-injection loop. Captain chose option b: hard-cap re-injection rather than trying to distinguish delivered-but-unconfirmed from genuinely-undelivered. Bound re-injection per buffered content to the initial typed attempt plus at most one max-defer escape retry; raise the wedge alarm exactly once for that content, then hold the buffer durably WITHOUT re-injecting or re-alarming. The buffer must stay durable (state/.subsuper-escalations) so return catch-up still surfaces it - nothing is lost after queue publication. The cap is per-buffered-content (content-addressed markers), never a permanent mute: a genuinely distinct escalation re-arms it and raises its own single alarm; any positively confirmed delivery clears the cap and resumes normal injection. The existing wedge-alarm behavior (durable .subsuper-inject-wedged marker, active alert, tmux status-line flash, once-per-episode rate limit) is preserved. Key correctness decision made while implementing: ONLY a typed-but-unconfirmed attempt counts toward the cap; a pre-typing DEFERRAL (pane busy, composer holding a human's half-typed line, afk off - nothing was typed) must keep retrying every tick so the digest lands the moment the pane frees, and conflating the two strands a legitimate escalation. inject_msg and escalate_flush therefore return exit 2 for typed-but-unconfirmed vs exit 1 for a pre-typing deferral; the max-defer escape caps a deferral only when that exact content was already typed-unconfirmed (the false-negative's own residual text still in the composer), so the wedge alarm fires exactly once rather than twice. Backend-independent (tracked in state files, not any backend pane surface). Constraints honored: do not change the injection guards' empty/pending/unknown semantics - bound only the retry count; do not weaken the daemon's reliability properties (nothing lost after publication, bounded-latency wedge detection, declared external waits rechecked on their own cadence); keep the change minimal and focused; one-owner docs (patched daemon header comments and docs/wedge-alarm.md, with a docs/configuration.md cross-reference - no duplication); portable regression tests in tests/fm-daemon.test.sh (persistent non-confirmation caps injection <=2, single alarm, durable buffer, cap re-arm on new content, marker clearing on confirmed flush) plus the afk inject e2e for both tmux and herdr backends covering the deferral landing cleanly after the pane frees; bin/fm-lint.sh shellcheck-clean. ## What Changed - Hard-cap re-injection in `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh` so a composer-confirmation false-negative (Claude-primary + herdr backend, #2361 family) degrades to a single wedge alarm instead of an all-night re-injection loop: per buffered content, injection is bounded to the initial typed attempt plus at most one max-defer escape retry, the wedge alarm fires exactly once, and the buffer is then held durably in `state/.subsuper-escalations` without re-injecting or re-alarming. The cap is content-addressed (per-buffered-content markers) — a genuinely distinct escalation re-arms it and raises its own single alarm, and any positively confirmed delivery clears the cap and resumes normal injection. - Split deferral semantics so `inject_msg`/`escalate_flush` return exit 2 for a typed-but-unconfirmed attempt (counts toward the cap) versus exit 1 for a pre-typing deferral (pane busy, human's half-typed line, afk off) which keeps retrying every tick so the digest lands the moment the pane frees; the max-defer escape only caps a deferral when that exact content was already typed-unconfirmed. Injection guard empty/pending/unknown semantics and the daemon's reliability properties are unchanged. - Added regression tests in `tests/fm-daemon.test.sh` (persistent non-confirmation caps injection, single alarm, durable buffer, cap re-arm on new content, marker clearing on confirmed flush) and updated one-owner docs: daemon header comments, `docs/wedge-alarm.md`, a `docs/configuration.md` cross-reference, and the afk `SKILL.md` stale-artifact list. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Well-bounded fix to a reliability-critical away-mode daemon path, but the new state machine is content-addressed and fully exercised by the added portable regression tests, exit-code and marker semantics were traced across all callers and lifecycle clearers with no material issues, and it conforms to every required intent constraint. ## Testing Baseline: the full tests/fm-daemon.test.sh suite passes (including the two new bounded-re-injection cap tests), as do the tmux and real-herdr afk inject e2e suites covering the pre-typing deferral landing cleanly after the pane frees and the persistent-pending max-defer wedge. Beyond pass/fail I produced reviewer-visible CLI transcripts that drive the real daemon housekeeping loop tick-by-tick: a base-vs-target comparison shows the pre-fix daemon re-injecting and re-alarming on all 8 ticks (the overnight loop) while the fixed daemon holds flat at exactly one typed attempt and one alarm with the buffer kept durable, and a second transcript shows a pre-typing deferral (a human's half-typed line) is never capped and the digest lands the instant the pane frees — the exact correctness decision the intent requires. Sandbox filesystem/network restrictions initially broke temp-dir creation and lib sourcing; both were environment issues I worked around by disabling the sandbox for the test runs. I did not run bin/fm-lint.sh because the task rules prohibit running linters, so the intent's shellcheck-clean claim is not independently verified here. Working tree left clean; evidence files retained in the dedicated evidence directory.
Evidence: Base-vs-target: re-injection loop capped to one alarm BASE (pre-fix): tick 1..8 -> typed 1..8, alarm 1..8 (re-injects+re-alarms every tick) TARGET (fixed): tick 1..8 -> typed=1, alarm=1, wedged=yes, buffer=DURABLE (held flat) == prefix-base final: typed=8 alarm=8 buffer=DURABLE == == postfix-capped final: typed=1 alarm=1 buffer=DURABLE == ```text Scenario: Claude-primary composer-confirmation false-negative (issue #2361 family). The digest lands and starts a real turn, but the idle composer is misread as still pending, so every housekeeping tick's batch flush believes delivery failed. 8 consecutive ticks (each crosses one FM_MAX_DEFER window in this harness). Real daemon housekeeping() is driven per tick; the fake tmux persist-swallows the submit-ack so the pane is never positively confirmed empty. ############################################################ # BASE (pre-fix, commit bdae21e) -- NO re-injection cap ############################################################ tick | typed(cumulative) | alarms(cumulative) | wedged | buffer -----+-------------------+--------------------+--------+-------- 1 | 1 | 1 | yes | DURABLE 2 | 2 | 2 | yes | DURABLE 3 | 3 | 3 | yes | DURABLE 4 | 4 | 4 | yes | DURABLE 5 | 5 | 5 | yes | DURABLE 6 | 6 | 6 | yes | DURABLE 7 | 7 | 7 | yes | DURABLE 8 | 8 | 8 | yes | DURABLE == prefix-base final: typed=8 alarm=8 buffer=DURABLE == ############################################################ # TARGET (fixed, commit 3d48654) -- hard-capped re-injection ############################################################ tick | typed(cumulative) | alarms(cumulative) | wedged | buffer -----+-------------------+--------------------+--------+-------- 1 | 1 | 1 | yes | DURABLE 2 | 1 | 1 | yes | DURABLE 3 | 1 | 1 | yes | DURABLE 4 | 1 | 1 | yes | DURABLE 5 | 1 | 1 | yes | DURABLE 6 | 1 | 1 | yes | DURABLE 7 | 1 | 1 | yes | DURABLE 8 | 1 | 1 | yes | DURABLE == postfix-capped final: typed=1 alarm=1 buffer=DURABLE == ```
Evidence: Pre-typing deferral is never capped and lands when the pane frees ticks 1-4 (human half-typed line): typed=0, capped=no, failed=no, buffer=DURABLE tick 5 (human cleared it): typed=1, buffer=empty -> digest landed the moment the pane freed ```text tick | composer holds | typed | capped-marker | failed-marker | buffer -----+----------------------+-------+---------------+---------------+-------- 1 | human half-typed line | 0 | no | no | DURABLE 2 | human half-typed line | 0 | no | no | DURABLE 3 | human half-typed line | 0 | no | no | DURABLE 4 | human half-typed line | 0 | no | no | DURABLE 5 | (human cleared it) | 1 | no | no | empty Result: deferral never set a cap/failed marker (ticks 1-4), buffer stayed durable, and the digest LANDED (typed 0->1) the moment the pane freed on tick 5. ```
Evidence: Reproduction harness: tick-by-tick daemon driver ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # Reviewer evidence: drive the REAL daemon housekeeping loop tick-by-tick under # the overnight composer-confirmation false-negative and show that the fixed # daemon caps re-injection while the pre-fix daemon loops every tick. set -u ROOT="$1"; DAEMON_PATH="$2"; LABEL="$3" . "$ROOT/tests/wake-helpers.sh" export FM_TEST_DAEMON_SOURCED=1 . "$DAEMON_PATH" TMP_ROOT=$(fm_test_tmproot fm-wedge-evid) FM_DAEMON_PRIMARY_HARNESS=claude; export FM_DAEMON_PRIMARY_HARNESS dir=$(make_bordered_case "$LABEL") state="$dir/state"; fakebin="$dir/fakebin" sent="$dir/sent.log"; : > "$sent" alert="$dir/alert.log"; : > "$alert" touch "$dir/.swallow" escalate_add "$state" "needs-decision: pick A" echo $(( $(date +%s) - 600 )) > "$state/.subsuper-escalations.since" afk_enter "$state" WEDGE_ALARM_LAST_EPOCH=0 printf 'tick | typed(cumulative) | alarms(cumulative) | wedged | buffer\n' printf -- '-----+-------------------+--------------------+--------+--------\n' for i in $(seq 1 8); do printf '\xe2\x95\xad\xe2\x94\x80\xe2\x94\x80\xe2\x94\x80\xe2\x94\x80\xe2\x94\x80\xe2\x95\xae\n\xe2\x94\x82 > \xe2\x94\x82\n\xe2\x95\xb0\xe2\x94\x80\xe2\x94\x80\xe2\x94\x80\xe2\x94\x80\xe2\x94\x80\xe2\x95\xaf\n' > "$dir/composer" PATH="$fakebin:$PATH" FM_FAKE_COMPOSER="$dir/composer" FM_FAKE_SENT="$sent" \ FM_FAKE_SWALLOW="$dir/.swallow" FM_FAKE_PERSIST_SWALLOW=1 FM_INJECT_CONFIRM_SLEEP=0.02 \ FM_WEDGE_ALARM_LOG="$alert" FM_WEDGE_ALARM_CHANNEL=osascript \ FM_ESCALATE_BATCH_SECS=1 FM_MAX_DEFER_SECS=1 housekeeping "$state" 2>/dev/null || true typed=$(grep -c 'Supervisor escalate' "$sent" 2>/dev/null); typed=${typed:-0} alarms=$(grep -c . "$alert" 2>/dev/null); alarms=${alarms:-0} wedged="no"; [ -s "$state/.subsuper-inject-wedged" ] && wedged="yes" buf="empty"; [ -s "$state/.subsuper-escalations" ] && buf="DURABLE" printf ' %2d | %2d | %d | %-3s | %s\n' \ "$i" "$typed" "$alarms" "$wedged" "$buf" done printf '\n== %s final: typed=%s alarm=%s buffer=%s ==\n' "$LABEL" \ "$(grep -c 'Supervisor escalate' "$sent")" "$(grep -c . "$alert")" \ "$([ -s "$state/.subsuper-escalations" ] && echo DURABLE || echo lost)" ```
Evidence: Reproduction harness: deferral-not-capped driver ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # Reviewer evidence for the KEY correctness decision: a PRE-TYPING deferral # (pane busy / composer holding a human's half-typed line - nothing was typed) # must NEVER count toward the cap. title: fix(herdr): detach Linux server startup from Bash command substitutions
body:
## Intent

Opravit reálnou Linux chybu Firstmate Herdr backendu, kdy `fm-remote-doctor --fix` na Ubuntu ARM64 při startu `herdr server --session fm-remote` nevrátí řízení, takže standardní remote seed transakčně selže. Oddělit příčinu od symptomu a zachovat doložený závěr, že Linux Bash command substitution čeká na EOF, protože foreground Herdr child zdědí její interní deskriptory, nikoli předpokládat, že problém je jen samotný foreground režim Herdr. Start musí být jednoduchý a bounded: po readiness se doctor vrátí, server skutečně žije a je ready, start failure se nemaskuje, readiness se nedokazuje slepým sleepem a failed start ukončí a reapne pouze přímý vlastněný start child. Nesmí se změnit stop, delete ani lifecycle jiných Herdr sessions, nesmí vzniknout wrapper, daemon manager, obecná policy vrstva ani backend refactor a nesmí se regresovat macOS, Bash 3.2 ani podporované Herdr verze.

Regrese musí jít přes spustitelné veřejné rozhraní `bin/fm-remote-doctor.sh --fix`, zachytit Linuxové čekání na foreground background-child, ověřit skutečný bounded návrat, následnou readiness, never-ready failure a cleanup bez uniklých procesů a nesmí testovat přesné bajty zdrojového kódu. Testovací watchdog smí ukončit pouze svou přesně vlastněnou process group a musí odmítat zombie stav. Aktuální CI nález je test-only race v okamžitém PGID snapshotu po `$!`: oprava má zůstat malá a pouze bounded čekat na skutečný kernelový přechod child procesu do jeho `setsid` process group, ne přidávat sleep jako důkaz readiness ani měnit produkční chování.

Podle následného kapitánského rozhodnutí a fresh-audit rework plánu je aktuální řešení malý řez z nového `main`: minimální descriptor detach v `bin/backends/herdr.sh`, deterministická Linux behaviorální regrese v existujícím doctor testu a stručná dokumentace současného bounded chování. Nepřidávat ani nezpevňovat `bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh`, nepřidávat samostatnou CI gate, neměnit obecný Herdr pin 0.7.4 ani výchozí install/CI lane. Dřívější velký head `d8f69ff0` zůstává pouze v rescue refs a nesmí se vracet do řešení. Reálný Oracle host ani jeho persistentní home nejsou autorizované; žádná živá `default` Herdr session se nesmí dotknout a žádný proces se nesmí zabíjet podle command patternu.

Projít dotčené call sites a zachovat stdin, stdout, stderr, race a PID ownership hranice. Dokumentaci měnit pouze jako současný veřejný kontrakt v existujících vlastnících. Validovat cílené Linux/ARM64 behaviorální běhy, macOS Bash 3.2, `bin/fm-lint.sh`, doc audience check a diff check; no-mistakes test krok je na výslovný pokyn přeskočen přes `--skip test`, protože samostatná evidence se spouští mimo něj, zatímco plná sada patří do required CI. Autorizovaná doručovací cesta je fork `V4f1k/firstmate`, aktualizovat existující PR z větve `fm/firstmate-herdr-linux-detach` proti `main`, ohlídat required CI do zelena a nic nemergovat ani force-pushovat.

## What Changed

- Updated Herdr named-server startup to detach inherited descriptors above stdio, explicitly redirect stdio, and preserve bounded readiness polling with failure cleanup limited to the direct start child.
- Added Linux-only behavioral coverage through `bin/fm-remote-doctor.sh --fix` for ready and never-ready foreground Herdr starts, including bounded return, process-group ownership, cleanup, and zombie rejection.
- Documented the bounded Linux transport behavior and the corresponding remote-secondmate doctor contract.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Captain, změna je dobře ohraničená na descriptor detach, bounded start/cleanup a behaviorální regresní fixture; statický review neprokázal zdrojový blocker.

title: fix(bin): make supervision recovery owner-aware and durable
body:
## Intent

Fix the Claude primary-session supervision failure observed on 2026-08-14, where work was in flight, no watcher was live, and the turn-end guard could repeat forever while the Stop auto-arm did not claim recovery. First add a durable, bounded, self-trimming, best-effort state trace that records every auto-arm entry and selected pre-claim gate without changing hook output, status, or failure behavior. Reproduce only in a throwaway home with real Claude, let the evidence choose among sibling starvation, the foreign live session-lock owner gate, and discarded asyncRewake, and deliberately seek falsification: no entry on the blocked Stop would falsify the identity-gate diagnosis, while an owner claim without delivered Stop feedback would support discarded rewake. The evidence showed the hook ran and took gate-live-session-owner, while lock-owner asyncRewake worked, so preserve the identity gate and its prevention of two sessions arming one home; do not weaken the guard, arm from the read-only session, reorder hooks, or teach the falsified short-circuit mechanism. Align the guard with session ownership so the read-only competing session can finish and the lock-owning session remains the sole mutable supervision owner and restores supervision on its next Stop. Add a portable real-process regression and an env-gated real-Claude live guard, and prove both RED against unfixed code and green after the fix. After two genuinely identical guard blocks, terminate the exchange in exactly one captain-facing question, reset the identical-block count when evidence changes, and suppress repeated escalation. ## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Captain, the final change consistently uses one supervision snapshot, closes the false-X-mode race, and leaves the durable ownership and queue-delivery invariants intact.

The marker remains pending and later arms repeatedly re-announce the same recovery instead of supervising. Preserve an outstanding generation during republication and consume rows through the acknowledged sequence even when the episode generation has advanced.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh:495` - The required behavior says to “terminate the exchange in exactly one captain-facing question” after two identical blocks. The second block instructs the model to escalate the choice to the captain, while the next unchanged Stop emits another captain-facing question here; a compliant model therefore asks twice. Choose one question owner—either make the second block terminal, or let the model ask and allow the subsequent Stop silently.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh:226` - The requirement says to reset after evidence changes and count only “genuinely identical” blocks, but this signature records only aggregate counts and modes. If task A completes and task B starts before the next Stop, the signature remains unchanged and the new state inherits A’s block count. Include a stable fingerprint of the actual task and process-source identities, preferably from the shared supervision-status boundary while excluding volatile age fields.

Resolve the selected executable once, probe its `--help`, and pass the flag only when that exact executable supports it.
- ⚠️ `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:253` - Recovery confirmation runs synchronously without a timeout. If a live but stalled process owns `.watcher-down.lock`, `--handling-delivered` waits indefinitely and freezes the Pi event loop immediately after wake delivery; the OpenCode sibling has the same path. Bound the child execution or make it asynchronous, leaving the durable recovery marker pending when confirmation fails.

2 errors still open:
- 🚨 `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh:223` - The accepted criterion says to “reset the identical-block count when evidence changes,” but this signature uses `FM_SUP_*` values sampled once at line 165, before the configurable auto-arm wait. A process-source runner can terminal-retire its `.source` during that wait while the sibling auto-arm observes no remaining need and makes no claim; on the second attempt the guard still compares source A’s stale fingerprint, reaches count 2, and emits the captain question despite changed evidence. Refresh shared supervision status at the block-accounting boundary and pass/reset when the need disappeared before permitting terminal escalation.
- 🚨 `docs/turnend-guard.md:71` - The accepted clarification requires the second identical observation to be terminal, with the guard owning the only question and subsequent unchanged Stops passing silently, and the intent requires authoritative turn-end and operating-protocol records to be updated. These changed docs still say the second banner tells the model to ask and a later Stop emits the question; `docs/supervision-protocols/claude.md:15` repeats that obsolete model-owned sequence. Update both authoritative documents to match the implemented second-Stop ownership rule.

With no watcher, the actionable result remains unsurfaced until unrelated activity. Make the shared supervision-needed boundary include pending wake delivery, and update the new regression to retire through the real process path or seed its durable wake before asserting the outcome.

## Intent Make Firstmate-supervised Pi and Pi-signed ordinary worker sessions honor the same home-level Calm presentation preference as the primary session, so routine tool calls, results, collapsed thinking, and working noise are hidden by default when config/calm is on. Preserve complete transcript and session data, exports, tool execution, ordering, and supervision behavior because this is presentation only. Reuse the existing fm-calm.ts implementation and its one-owner preference contract rather than duplicating Calm logic in spawn code. Use the smallest safe launch integration for ordinary Pi and Pi-signed workers without affecting non-Pi workers or adding ordinary-worker wiring to second mates whose primary contract already owns its extensions. New workers must read the owning home's config/calm at startup, with on enabling Calm and off, absent, unreadable, or unrecognized values retaining stock presentation. Avoid extension double-loading, tool-definition collisions, project trust requirements, project pollution, and any reliance on task repositories containing Firstmate files. Document that already-running workers do not receive unsafe live injection and need the supported relaunch path for an immediate preference change while preserving work and transcript data. Add focused portable executable-behavior tests across supported Pi launch shapes, run Firstmate lint and documentation checks, open a PR, and stop without merging it. ## What Changed - Load the tracked `fm-calm.ts` extension for ordinary Pi and Pi-signed workers using the spawning Firstmate home’s resolved preference paths, without changing non-Pi or second-mate launches. - Add single-owner coordination so explicitly loaded and project-discovered Calm copies cannot double-register presentation behavior. - Document worker startup and relaunch behavior, and expand coverage across preference states, Pi launch shapes, trust boundaries, and extension ownership. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: No source changes were made; the substantive review assessment is pending permission to continue from already collected evidence. ## Testing Targeted launch behavior passed, but native Calm presentation validation remains incomplete pending permission to retry with the environment warning suppressed. - Outcome: ⚠️ 1 warning across 1 run (6m10s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

title: chore(skills): add review-artifacts skill for Firstmate Lavish review decks
body:
## Intent

Establish a consistent, reusable Firstmate design language and review workflow for every Firstmate-produced Lavish artifact and standalone HTML decision document, with Impeccable required for both design preflight and the bounded finish/reviewer pass. Use one smallest authoritative conditional procedure under .agents/skills and add only a concise AGENTS.md load trigger. Define a named restrained language around Frame -> Show -> Compare -> Decide -> Record -> Ship with reusable, accessible, responsive, portable tokens and components for page chrome, typography, surfaces, numbered sections, evidence, options, recommendation and risk states, structured decision controls, and truthful completion status. Provide minimal reusable template/assets under that skill rather than copying prior artifacts, while leaving screenshots and product mockups governed by the subject project's own design authority; require agents to inspect that authority first and use a documented unbranded fallback only when none exists. Link to Impeccable's authoritative installation/site without vendoring or rewriting it, and stop safely across supported harnesses when it is absent rather than installing without approval. Integrate Lavish by requiring every matching playbook, native structured controls for nontrivial decisions, completion-aware long polling through Firstmate's existing process-event adapter, and the established external-feedback trust boundary; keep trivial yes/no decisions in chat. Make exact decisions durable through existing owners before implementation handoff. Do not create duplicate setup contracts or install automation without repository evidence, and update public/operator setup only if the documentation-audience inventory identifies it as owner. Validate representative architecture, comparison, product-mockup, and decision-input content at desktop and mobile widths. Ensure no remote tracking, secrets, unsafe scripts, inaccessible controls, horizontal overflow, or hidden decision state, and limit AGENTS.md growth to the trigger pointer.

## What Changed

- Added the `review-artifacts` skill (`.agents/skills/review-artifacts/SKILL.md`) defining the Firstmate Review Deck language — the Frame → Show → Compare → Decide → Record → Ship sequence, subject-design-authority inspection rules with an "Unbranded Subject" fallback, and required Impeccable preflight/finish passes for any Lavish artifact or standalone HTML decision/review document.
- Added reusable, portable template/asset files for the skill: `template/review.html`, `assets/review-deck.css` (tokens/components for page chrome, typography, surfaces, numbered sections, evidence, options, recommendation/risk states, and decision controls), and `assets/review-deck.js` (structured feedback and completion-status behavior).
- Registered the skill's load trigger in `AGENTS.md` (one line under the non-captain-invocable skills list) and added its `SKILL.md` path to `docs/documentation-audiences.json` under the `agent-runtime` audience.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The fix-round commit is a small, well-contained 20-line change that correctly resolves the previously identified copy-button label race using a generation counter tied to the single source of truth for state text (setState), with no new files touched and no regressions found on re-inspection.

## Testing

No existing automated test suite covers this portable HTML/CSS/JS artifact, so I performed manual, evidence-producing browser verification (the appropriate method for a UI/HTML template change) at desktop and mobile widths, plus a targeted reproduction of the copy-button race condition. Both bugs fixed by the two prior 'no-mistakes(review)' commits (evidence text overflow via overflow-wrap: anywhere, and the copy-button label race via a generation-aware async guard) were exercised directly and confirmed resolved at the target commit; no new issues were found, and no remote calls, secrets, or overflow were present.

- Evidence: [Mobile (390x844) — 120-char unbroken token wrapping correctly in evidence/timeline fields, proving the overflow-wrap fix](https://github.com/ductiletoaster/firstmate/blob/44dd6fa867fb7a26dd06364c9976929fe51f36dc/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/firstmate-review-design-language/review-deck-mobile-overflow-fix.png)

- ⚠️ `.agents/skills/review-artifacts/assets/review-deck.js:63` - The commit a6c0a02 ('Fix evidence text overflow and stale copy-button label') resets the copy button's label back to 'Copy visible answer' inside setState() (line 22-23), which runs on the form's 'change' and 'submit' handlers. But the copy button's own click handler is async: it awaits navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) (line 62) before setting textContent to 'Copied' (line 63). If the reviewer clicks Copy and then changes their selection before the clipboard promise resolves, the 'change' handler resets the label to default first, but the pending click handler's `copyButton.textContent = "Copied"` still runs afterward and overwrites that reset — leaving the button reading 'Copied' even though the visible answer has since changed to something that was never copied. The earliest shared boundary to close this is inside the click handler itself: capture a snapshot/generation token of the output text (or reuse the same setState reset path) before awaiting, and only apply 'Copied' if nothing has superseded it since — rather than patching the symptom via another sibling event listener.

title: docs: pin Herdr alt-screen scrollback bounds and capture viewport stability
body:
## Intent Document that alternative-screen harnesses, including Claude Code, expose no scrollback history to Herdr, so any capture of such a pane is bounded to the visible window regardless of the requested --lines. Place this knowledge in docs/herdr-backend.md near the existing capture/peek sections (the 'Current transport behavior' paragraph about pane read --lines N and the 200-line floor), without duplicating what the doc already says. Add a non-regression test 'a firstmate capture never moves the pane viewport' to tests/fm-backend-herdr-smoke.test.sh, following the exact recipe in section 8 of the scout report data/fm-herdr-scroll-scout/report.md (the source of truth): seed real scrollback with seq 1 500, read .result.pane.scroll before and after the firstmate capture functions, and fail if the viewport moved. The test must pass locally and would fail if a capture moved the viewport. Follow repo style: one sentence per line in the docs, plain dash, shellcheck-clean test. Stay bounded: no doc refactor and no additional tests. ## What Changed - `docs/herdr-backend.md` now states, next to the existing capture/transport section, that alternative-screen harnesses (including Claude Code) expose no scrollback history to Herdr, so any capture of such a pane is bounded to the visible window regardless of the requested `--lines`. - `tests/fm-backend-herdr-smoke.test.sh` gains a viewport-stability check: it creates a throwaway pane, seeds real scrollback with `seq 1 500`, records `.result.pane.scroll` before and after running the firstmate capture helpers (`capture`, `capture_ansi`, `composer_state`), and fails if the pane's scroll position changed. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Changement purement additif (2 lignes de doc + un bloc de smoke test auto-isolé) : tous les critères de l'intent sont vérifiés en source, les fixes des rounds précédents sont matériellement en place et corrects, et le nouveau code est shellcheck-clean. ## Testing Ran the full real-herdr smoke suite (the smallest unit containing the new check, which depends on the suite's isolated-session setup): all checks pass including the new viewport-stability one, with real seeded scrollback confirmed via .result.pane.scroll. Then demonstrated the test's failure mode end-to-end by fault injection: attaching a real herdr client and scrolling the pane in copy-mode between the before/after reads moved offset_from_bottom from 0 to 29 and made the test's exact assertion fire, so the test provably fails when a capture moves the viewport. Also verified the doc sentences sit in the intended 'Current transport behavior' spot without duplication. No browser/GUI surface exists for this docs+shell-test change; the end-user surfaces are the doc text and CLI test output, captured as text artifacts including the herdr client's terminal screen during the injected scroll. Shellcheck was not run here (lint phase owns it). No transient artifacts left in the worktree.

Evidence: Fault-injection script (reproducible demonstration) ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # Fault injection for the new viewport-stability check in # tests/fm-backend-herdr-smoke.test.sh: reproduce the test's exact scenario # (throwaway pane, seq 1 500, read .result.pane.scroll before/after), but # deliberately MOVE the viewport between the two reads - the way a scrolling # capture would - by attaching a real herdr client in a detached tmux session # and scrolling up in copy-mode. If the test's assertion # ([ "$scroll_before" = "$scroll_after" ]) fires on this moved viewport, the # non-regression test demonstrably fails when a capture moves the viewport. set -u ROOT=${FM_ROOT:?set FM_ROOT to the firstmate worktree} EVID=${FM_EVID:?set FM_EVID to the evidence dir} # shellcheck source=/dev/null . "$ROOT/tests/herdr-test-safety.sh" herdr_forget_inherited_pane SESSION="fm-lab-fault-scroll-$$" export HERDR_SESSION="$SESSION" TMUX_S="fm-fault-scroll-tmux-$$" cleanup() { tmux kill-session -t "$TMUX_S" 2>/dev/null herdr_safe_stop_and_delete "$SESSION" } trap cleanup EXIT fm_herdr_lab_prepare "$SESSION" || { echo "FATAL: lab prepare failed"; exit 2; } # shellcheck source=/dev/null . "$ROOT/bin/fm-backend.sh" fm_backend_source herdr || { echo "FATAL: fm_backend_source herdr failed"; exit 2; } CONTAINER_RAW=$(fm_backend_herdr_container_ensure /tmp) || { echo "FATAL: container_ensure failed"; exit 2; } CONTAINER=${CONTAINER_RAW%%$'\t'*} SEEDED=${CONTAINER_RAW#*$'\t'} IDS=$(fm_backend_herdr_create_task "$CONTAINER" "fm-fault-scroll" /tmp "$SEEDED") || { echo "FATAL: create_task failed"; exit 2; } read -r _TAB PANE < "$EVID/fault-injection-herdr-client-screen.txt" 2>/dev/null || true scroll_after=$(herdr pane get "$PANE" --session "$SESSION" | jq -c '.result.pane.scroll') echo "scroll_after=$scroll_after" # Leave copy mode so teardown is clean. tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_S" q 2>/dev/null sleep 0.3 if [ "$moved" -ne 1 ] || [ "$scroll_before" = "$scroll_after" ]; then echo "FAULT INJECTION FAILED: could not move the viewport; detection not demonstrated" exit 2 fi # Replay the test's exact assertion over the moved viewport. if [ "$scroll_before" = "$scroll_after" ]; then echo "unexpected: assertion passed despite the moved viewport" exit 2 else echo "not ok - a firstmate capture moved the pane viewport: $scroll_before -> $scroll_after" echo "DEMONSTRATED: the suite's viewport-stability assertion FAILS when the viewport moves" fi ```
Evidence: Doc excerpt: new sentences in 'Current transport behavior' after the 200-line-floor paragraph ```text It is the same semantic signal the native path uses and the same one the tmux submit core reads, so a pane already mid-turn before the text was typed still reports `pending` rather than borrowing another turn as proof of this delivery. The composer verdict itself is deliberately unchanged: a right-aligned status token on the composer row stays content for every other caller, including the away-mode pre-injection guard. The poll density bounds the residual possibility of an extremely fast complete turn; a missed transition can cause only a redundant Enter on an empty composer, never duplicate message text. `pane read --lines N` can return empty output when N is below the viewport height. The capture owner requests at least 200 lines from Herdr and trims locally to the caller's bound. This generous floor is required for small composer and peek reads. Alternative-screen harnesses, including Claude Code, expose no scrollback history to Herdr at all. Any capture of such a pane is therefore bounded to the visible window regardless of the requested `--lines`. Herdr's native agent state can read idle while a harness waits on its own long foreground tool. ```

🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - ⚠️ `tests/fm-backend-herdr-smoke.test.sh:308` - Le test de stabilité du viewport ne valide jamais que scroll_before est non vide et non null. `.result.pane.scroll` n'est référencé nulle part ailleurs dans le dépôt ; si `herdr pane get` échoue ou si le champ disparaît/est renommé dans une version future de Herdr, jq produit `null` (ou vide) avant ET après, la comparaison passe à vide et le test ne peut plus jamais échouer — ce qui contredit silencieusement sa raison d'être (« would fail if a capture moved the viewport »). Ajouter un garde-fou du type `{ [ -n "$scroll_before" ] && [ "$scroll_before" != null ]; } || fail "could not read .result.pane.scroll"` avant les captures. - ⚠️ `tests/fm-backend-herdr-smoke.test.sh:309` - Les codes de retour des trois invocations de capture sont jetés (`>/dev/null` sans `|| fail`). `fm_backend_herdr_capture` et `fm_backend_herdr_capture_ansi` retournent 1 en cas d'échec CLI (bin/backends/herdr.sh:2596,2606) ; si une capture échoue, le scroll est trivialement inchangé et le test passe sans avoir exercé le comportement épinglé. Toutes les autres captures de cette suite sont gardées par `|| fail` — appliquer le même garde ici (composer_state retourne toujours 0 et n'en a pas besoin, mais son verdict pourrait aussi être vérifié différent de `unknown`). 🔧 Fix: guard scroll read and capture failures in viewport test 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `tests/fm-backend-herdr-smoke.test.sh:316` - L'assertion `[ "$cs" != unknown ]` ajoutée par le round de fix traite le verdict `unknown` comme un échec de capture, alors que c'est le verdict conçu et légitime du classificateur pour un écran sans composer : la règle stricte de bin/fm-composer-lib.sh (sélection cursorless, lignes 1261-1263, et le catalogue de formes) dit qu'un glyphe de prompt shell (`>` `$` `%` `#`) n'est jamais une preuve de conteneur. Le pane jetable du test héberge un shell brut affichant la sortie de `seq 1 500` ; sur toute machine avec herdr installé et un prompt par défaut, composer_state retourne `unknown` et le test échoue systématiquement avec un message trompeur (« could not capture » alors que la capture ANSI a réussi). Il ne passe sur la machine de l'auteur que parce que son prompt starship `❯` coïncide avec le glyphe composer bare de claude. Correction : supprimer l'assertion et revenir à la forme du commit initial `fm_backend_herdr_composer_state "$SCROLL_TARGET" >/dev/null` — le but de cet appel est d'exercer le chemin de capture pour la stabilité du viewport, et le succès de la capture est déjà garanti par les deux appels précédents gardés par `|| fail` qui utilisent les mêmes primitives (capture et capture_ansi). - ℹ️ `tests/fm-backend-herdr-smoke.test.sh:309` - Les deux findings du round 1 sont matériellement corrigés : le garde-fou non-vide/non-null sur scroll_before (lignes 309-310) élimine le passage à vide (un échec du pane get d'après ne peut plus produire de faux succès puisque scroll_before est garanti non-null), et les deux captures sont gardées par `|| fail` (lignes 311-314). Seule la déclinaison composer_state du second fix introduit le défaut signalé séparément. 🔧 Fix: drop machine-dependent composer_state assertion in viewport test ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: fix(bootstrap): pin AXI toolchain to exact reviewed versions with consent-gated installs
body:
## Intent

Implement the captain-authorized, bounded Firstmate-only AXI supply-chain and version hardening identified by data/axi-adoption-census/report.md. Keep the existing gh-axi, chrome-devtools-axi, lavish-axi, quota-axi, tasks-axi, and no-mistakes axi interfaces; add no catalog tool or custom AXI; do not change product repositories or project AGENTS.md; exclude prediction-system. Pin tracked bootstrap and CI installation to the reviewed exact versions gh-axi@0.1.30, chrome-devtools-axi@0.1.29, lavish-axi@0.1.50, quota-axi@0.1.25, and tasks-axi@0.2.5 unless authoritative compatibility evidence requires otherwise. Replace the current latest-floor contract with an explicit reviewed-version policy: detect any older, newer, missing, or malformed installation and route it through the existing detect-first, operator-consent install path without any unattended upgrade or downgrade. Eliminate Firstmate-owned npx -y and floating-latest guidance or execution for these required tools, without editing globally installed vendor skills or installing vendor setup hooks. Source-review one exact chrome-devtools-mcp release from authoritative npm and repository evidence, recording package identity, release tag and commit, Node requirements, direct entrypoint, integrity and provenance, and relevant privacy, telemetry, update-check, browser-profile, and stdio/remote transport behavior. Add that exact browser component to the single authoritative reviewed toolchain registry and bootstrap mechanics, resolving its stable global entrypoint portably from npm prefix rather than a machine-specific Homebrew path, so correctly provisioned chrome-devtools-axi cannot fall through to floating latest. Add executable/public-interface regressions for exact pin detection, newer and older mismatch behavior, malformed or contaminated output, package identity, missing browser entrypoint, portable prefix resolution, consent-gated exact installs, and the shared exact install interface used by CI; never test implementation source bytes. Update only current operator documentation and active maintainer verification evidence, keeping task chronology private. Preserve the three narrow raw gh --json reads until gh-axi proves equivalent fields, build no wrapper, and do not patch or wrap third-party unknown-flag behavior. The explicitly authorized machine action is only npm install -g chrome-devtools-mcp@the-reviewed-exact-version after provenance is established; verify that exact installed version and entrypoint, then prove it in a task-specific isolated chrome-devtools-axi session against https://example.com with no auto-connect or persistent user-data directory and stop only that named session. Preserve existing backlog, quota routing, PR, browser, rich-review, and no-mistakes compatibility. Require the repository-pinned shellcheck through bin/fm-lint.sh, relevant executable tests, documentation-audience validation, full checks, review, PR, and green CI. Do not merge; Firstmate changes require explicit captain approval. The PR must explain exact pins, source-review evidence, machine verification, compatibility risk, and rollback.

## What Changed
- Added `bin/fm-reviewed-toolchain.sh` as the single authoritative registry of exact reviewed versions (gh-axi@0.1.30, chrome-devtools-axi@0.1.29, lavish-axi@0.1.50, quota-axi@0.1.25, tasks-axi@0.2.5, chrome-devtools-mcp@1.7.0), with a strict `--version` parser that rejects malformed, prerelease, or multi-token output, `check` requiring exact equality, and a shared consent-gated `install` interface.
- Replaced the latest-floor policy in `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` (removed `GH_AXI_MIN`/`LAVISH_AXI_MIN`/`FM_QUOTA_AXI_MIN` floors) with exact-pin detection that reports any older, newer, missing, or mismatched build as MISSING for operator-approved install; `bin/fm-quota-axi-lib.sh` and `bin/fm-tasks-axi-lib.sh` now delegate to the shared reviewed-version check, and chrome-devtools-mcp is verified through its npm-global package directory with its entrypoint resolved portably from `npm prefix -g` instead of a Homebrew path, so a provisioned chrome-devtools-axi cannot fall through to floating latest.
- Switched CI's `npm install -g tasks-axi` steps to the shared `fm-reviewed-toolchain.sh install`/`check` interface, expanded the bootstrap and per-tool test suites to cover exact-pin, mismatch, contaminated-output, package-identity, and portable-prefix cases, and added `docs/verification/axi-toolchain.md` source-review evidence plus updated operator docs for the reviewed-version policy.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is a well-bounded policy conversion to a single exact-version registry that fully matches the authoritative intent, every consumer and test fixture was updated consistently, the strict parser was confirmed compatible with real tool output on this host, and the only findings are two informational robustness notes.

## Testing

Ran the core fm-bootstrap regression suite plus six other touched suites (all passing except one fm-teardown case proven pre-existing at the base commit), exercised the new reviewed-toolchain registry CLI against the real host where all six tools check clean at their exact pins, demonstrated older/newer/contaminated version rejection via fake shims, and proved the pinned browser transport live: an isolated chrome-devtools-axi session rendered https://example.com with npx blocked (zero fallback invocations), was screenshotted, and only that named session was stopped.

- Evidence: [Screenshot: example.com rendered in the isolated pinned-toolchain session (npx fallback blocked)](https://github.com/twelvesixsports/firstmate/blob/c2dd2958f2be4954c31b4e811f5c2131e16e533d/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/firstmate-axi-hardening/example-com-isolated-session.png)

title: feat(pi): compact Firstmate Pi sessions at 175K context tokens
body:
## Intent Configure project-local Pi auto-compaction for the Firstmate repository at a 175,000-token context threshold, without changing global Pi behavior or any other project. Accepted design and evidence, decided before the work started: - The active Firstmate Pi model is openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol with an exact 272000-token context window. - Pi has no direct threshold setting. It compacts when contextTokens > contextWindow - reserveTokens (verified in the installed Pi 0.84.1 shouldCompact implementation), so the threshold must be expressed as the reserve that remains. - Therefore set project-local .pi/settings.json compaction to enabled: true, reserveTokens: 97000, keepRecentTokens: 20000, yielding 272000 - 97000 = 175000 for this model. - keepRecentTokens: 20000 is deliberately Pi's own default recent-history window, restated so the compaction block reads as one deliberate choice rather than a partial override. It is not an accidental duplicate of a default. - The setting must stay Firstmate-specific: ~/.pi/agent/settings.json is deliberately NOT edited. Pi deep-merges a project settings file over the global one, so global behavior and other projects are unchanged. - Documentation must state that the 175K trigger is model-dependent: changing the context window changes the effective trigger unless the reserve is adjusted. - Documentation must state that the setting takes effect for new or restarted Pi sessions, not an already-running process. Requirements as accepted: 1. Add the smallest valid project-local Pi settings file, carrying only the compaction block, without changing or duplicating extension configuration. Firstmate's Pi extensions load from .pi/extensions/ by directory convention and are deliberately absent from the settings file. 2. Update the single appropriate Firstmate operator/configuration owner with current behavior, the formula, the scope, and the restart requirement. docs/configuration.md was chosen as that owner. This must deliberately NOT be added to always-loaded AGENTS.md. 3. Add the smallest runnable check that parses the JSON and proves the effective threshold equation for the current model, reusing the existing tests/.test.sh + tests/lib.sh pattern rather than adding any framework. The model context window is a documented constant in the test so the check stays portable and needs no Pi install in CI. 4. Review all affected Pi primary integration surfaces and confirm no other harness or backend behavior changes. This was done: nothing in bin/, CI workflows, or fleet/secondmate sync reads .pi/ beyond extensions/, and .claude, .codex, .grok, and .cursor surfaces are untouched. 5. Run targeted checks, bin/fm-lint.sh, and repository-required validation. Verification already performed: the new test passes, bin/fm-lint.sh is clean on the new file, bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage is ok, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh is ok, and the fm-test-run, fm-lint, and fm-documentation-audiences contract tests pass. tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh fails, but it fails identically with these changes stashed on the clean base, so that failure is pre-existing and unrelated. Delivery: push to the doitdigital0495/firstmate fork and open a cross-fork PR against kunchenguid/firstmate main, drive CI green, and do not merge. ## What Changed - Added project-local `.pi/settings.json` with a compaction block (`enabled: true`, `reserveTokens: 97000`, `keepRecentTokens: 20000`), so Pi sessions started in this repo compact once context passes 272000 - 97000 = 175000 tokens for the current Firstmate Pi model. The global `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` is untouched, so other projects keep Pi's defaults. - Documented the setting in `docs/configuration.md`: the threshold formula, its model-dependence, the `reserveTokens` side effect on summary output size (Pi also derives the summarization output cap from it), the project-trust prerequisite for project-local Pi settings, and that changes only apply to new or restarted Pi sessions. Added pointers from `README.md` and the `harness-adapters` skill. - Added `tests/fm-pi-compaction-settings.test.sh`, which validates the JSON, asserts the reserve yields a 175000 threshold against the documented model window, and checks the settings file carries only the compaction block. It skips when `jq` is unavailable, matching the existing optional-`jq` test convention. Review left three informational notes open (a hardcoded model window in the test, the strict top-level-keys assertion, and a rounding nit in a documented figure); lint, coverage, and the test suite pass. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Additive, config-and-docs-only change: one project-local Pi settings file whose values were verified against the installed Pi implementation, plus a self-guarding test; no script, backend, or harness behavior is touched. ## Testing Ran the new tests/fm-pi-compaction-settings.test.sh plus the repo's coverage check and the related contract tests, then went past unit level: a small script drove the installed Pi 0.84.1 SettingsManager and shouldCompact against this worktree, reading the real gpt-5.6-sol context window (272,000) from the operator's own Pi model store. It shows Firstmate sessions compacting exactly above 175,000 tokens, and an untrusted project or any unrelated project falling back to Pi's 16,384 default (255,616), which matches the documented behavior and proves global Pi behavior is unchanged. Only tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh fails, and it fails identically with the new settings file removed, so it is pre-existing and unrelated. This is a CLI/config change with no rendered UI surface, so no screenshot applies; the CLI transcript is the end-user-visible evidence. Worktree left clean.
Evidence: Pi 0.84.1 end-to-end compaction threshold transcript Pi version: 0.84.1 Active Firstmate Pi model: openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol contextWindow=272000 (from the operator's own Pi model store) Firstmate repo (trusted project, .pi/settings.json applied): effective compaction settings: enabled=true reserveTokens=97000 keepRecentTokens=20000 effective trigger: 272000 - 97000 = 175000 tokens contextTokens=174999 -> shouldCompact=false contextTokens=175000 -> shouldCompact=false contextTokens=175001 -> shouldCompact=true Same repo, project NOT trusted (Pi ignores the project file): effective compaction settings: enabled=true reserveTokens=16384 keepRecentTokens=20000 effective trigger: 272000 - 16384 = 255616 tokens contextTokens=255615 -> shouldCompact=false contextTokens=255616 -> shouldCompact=false contextTokens=255617 -> shouldCompact=true Unrelated project on the same machine (no project settings): effective compaction settings: enabled=true reserveTokens=16384 keepRecentTokens=20000 effective trigger: 272000 - 16384 = 255616 tokens contextTokens=255615 -> shouldCompact=false contextTokens=255616 -> shouldCompact=false contextTokens=255617 -> shouldCompact=true RESULT: Firstmate Pi sessions auto-compact at 175000 context tokens; global and other projects keep Pi's 16384 default reserve. ```text Pi version: 0.84.1 Active Firstmate Pi model: openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol contextWindow=272000 (from the operator's own Pi model store) Firstmate repo (trusted project, .pi/settings.json applied): effective compaction settings: enabled=true reserveTokens=97000 keepRecentTokens=20000 effective trigger: 272000 - 97000 = 175000 tokens contextTokens=174999 -> shouldCompact=false contextTokens=175000 -> shouldCompact=false contextTokens=175001 -> shouldCompact=true Same repo, project NOT trusted (Pi ignores the project file): effective compaction settings: enabled=true reserveTokens=16384 keepRecentTokens=20000 effective trigger: 272000 - 16384 = 255616 tokens contextTokens=255615 -> shouldCompact=false contextTokens=255616 -> shouldCompact=false contextTokens=255617 -> shouldCompact=true Unrelated project on the same machine (no project settings): effective compaction settings: enabled=true reserveTokens=16384 keepRecentTokens=20000 effective trigger: 272000 - 16384 = 255616 tokens contextTokens=255615 -> shouldCompact=false contextTokens=255616 -> shouldCompact=false contextTokens=255617 -> shouldCompact=true RESULT: Firstmate Pi sessions auto-compact at 175000 context tokens; global and other projects keep Pi's 16384 default reserve. ```
Evidence: End-to-end verification script ```text // End-to-end check of Firstmate's project-local Pi auto-compaction setting, // driven through the installed Pi 0.84.1 modules (no reimplementation). import { SettingsManager } from "/home/daan/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/settings-manager.js"; import { shouldCompact } from "/home/daan/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/compaction/compaction.js"; import { mkdtempSync, readFileSync } from "fs"; import { tmpdir } from "os"; import { join } from "path"; const REPO = process.argv[2]; const store = JSON.parse(readFileSync("/home/daan/.pi/agent/models-store.json", "utf-8")); const model = store["openai-codex"].models.find((m) => m.id === "gpt-5.6-sol"); const W = model.contextWindow; console.log(`Pi version: ${JSON.parse(readFileSync("/home/daan/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/package.json","utf-8")).version}`); console.log(`Active Firstmate Pi model: openai-codex/${model.id} contextWindow=${W} (from the operator's own Pi model store)\n`); const emptyGlobal = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "pi-global-")); // operator global with no compaction block const otherProject = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "other-project-")); // unrelated project, no .pi/settings.json function report(label, cwd, trusted) { const s = SettingsManager.create(cwd, emptyGlobal, { projectTrusted: trusted }).getCompactionSettings(); const trigger = W - s.reserveTokens; console.log(`${label}`); console.log(` effective compaction settings: enabled=${s.enabled} reserveTokens=${s.reserveTokens} keepRecentTokens=${s.keepRecentTokens}`); console.log(` effective trigger: ${W} - ${s.reserveTokens} = ${trigger} tokens`); for (const t of [trigger - 1, trigger, trigger + 1]) { console.log(` contextTokens=${t} -> shouldCompact=${shouldCompact(t, W, s)}`); } console.log(""); return trigger; } const firstmate = report("Firstmate repo (trusted project, .pi/settings.json applied):", REPO, true); report("Same repo, project NOT trusted (Pi ignores the project file):", REPO, false); report("Unrelated project on the same machine (no project settings):", otherProject, true); console.log(firstmate === 175000 ? "RESULT: Firstmate Pi sessions auto-compact at 175000 context tokens; global and other projects keep Pi's 16384 default reserve." : `RESULT: FAIL, trigger is ${firstmate}`); ```
Evidence: New repo contract test output ```text $ bash tests/fm-pi-compaction-settings.test.sh ok - compaction enabled, keeps 20000 recent tokens, triggers at 175000 for a 272000 context window ok - settings file carries no extension configuration; extensions come from .pi/extensions/ and the -e wiring ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ⚠️ `.pi/settings.json:4` - reserveTokens is an absolute 97000 but applies to every Pi session started in this repo, whatever model it runs. The 175K trigger only holds for a 272000-token window; a Pi model with a 128K window compacts at 31000, and any model with a window <= 97000 yields a non-positive threshold, i.e. compaction on essentially every turn. Crewmates working the firstmate repo can be dispatched on a different Pi model via config/crew-dispatch.json, so this is reachable, not hypothetical. Docs note the model-dependence but nothing guards the degenerate case; consider whether the reserve should be paired with a pinned model expectation or a floor. - ⚠️ `docs/configuration.md:44` - "The Firstmate Pi extensions in `.pi/extensions/` load by directory convention" does not match the code: bin/fm-spawn.sh:1126/2711-2723, bin/fm-session-start.sh:732-733 and bin/fm-supervision-instructions.sh:91-92 all pass the extension files explicitly with `-e <abs path>`. The stated rationale for omitting extension config from the settings file is therefore wrong; the real reason is that spawn/session-start supply the paths. Reword to reference the explicit `-e` wiring. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-pi-compaction-settings.test.sh:14` - MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOW=272000 is a hardcoded copy of the model's window, so the test proves the arithmetic, not reality. If the primary Pi model changes to a different window, the test still passes green while the effective trigger silently moves. Acceptable for a no-Pi-in-CI check, but the test cannot catch the exact drift the docs warn about. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-pi-compaction-settings.test.sh:39` - test_no_extension_configuration asserts the settings file's top-level keys are exactly "compaction", so any future legitimate project-local Pi setting (unrelated to extensions) fails this test rather than the extension-specific concern it names. Asserting the absence of an extensions key would express the intent without blocking unrelated settings. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-pi-compaction-settings.test.sh:22` - reserveTokens is used directly in $((MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOW - reserve)) without a numeric check. If the key is missing, jq yields the literal "null", and under `set -u` the arithmetic aborts the script with a bare "null: unbound variable" instead of the intended fail() message. Add a numeric guard (e.g. case "$reserve" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fail ...) so the failure reports the actual problem. 🔧 Fix: fix Pi compaction docs accuracy and test guards 3 issues (2 warnings, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `.pi/settings.json:4` - Pi uses compaction.reserveTokens for two unrelated things: the compaction trigger (compaction.js:163, contextTokens > contextWindow - reserveTokens) and the output cap of the summarization call itself (compaction.js:461 maxTokens = min(0.8 * reserveTokens, model.maxTokens); compaction.js:625 uses 0.5 * reserveTokens for the turn-prefix summary). Setting 97000 instead of Pi's 16384 default raises the allowed summary output from ~13,107 to ~77,600 tokens (turn-prefix ~48,500). The intent and docs treat reserveTokens purely as a threshold knob; the side effect is that a compaction summary is now permitted to be large enough to consume much of the headroom the compaction was meant to reclaim, plus the token cost. Verify this is acceptable, or document it alongside the threshold formula. - ⚠️ `docs/configuration.md:45` - The docs state only that a changed value reaches new or restarted Pi sessions. Pi additionally gates project-local .pi/settings.json behind project trust (pi-coding-agent docs/settings.md: trust decisions live in ~/.pi/agent/trust.json; non-interactive runs with -p / --mode json / --mode rpc never prompt and need --approve or defaultProjectTrust). In an untrusted clone or a fresh worktree path, the settings file is ignored and Pi silently uses the 16384 default, compacting at ~255,600 tokens rather than 175,000 - with no error to signal it. Add the trust prerequisite, mirroring the existing Cursor --trust note at docs/configuration.md:224. - ℹ️ `tests/fm-pi-compaction-settings.test.sh:42` - test_no_extension_configuration ignores jq's exit status: keys=$(jq -r 'keys[] | select(...)' "$SETTINGS") followed by [ -z "$keys" ]. If jq errors (unreadable file, non-object top level), keys is empty and the test reports a pass instead of a failure. Append `|| fail ...` as the threshold test does on line 21. 🔧 Fix: document Pi reserve side effects and trust, harden test 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `tests/fm-pi-compaction-settings.test.sh:19` - The test calls jq unconditionally. Repo convention (tests/fm-backend-cmux.test.sh:16, tests/fm-backend-autodetect-smoke.test.sh:41, and others) is `command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "skip: jq not found"; exit 0; }` because bootstrap treats jq as optional (required only for Relay/herdr/cmux). Without jq this test fails the run and reports the misleading message "$SETTINGS is not valid JSON" instead of skipping. Add the same skip guard at the top of the file. 🔧 Fix: skip Pi compaction settings test when jq missing 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `docs/configuration.md:42` - Default turn-prefix ceiling is floor(0.5 * 16384) = 8192, but the docs state "roughly 13,100 and 8,100". The 13,100 figure is right (floor(0.8*16384)=13107); 8,100 understates 8,192. Say "roughly 8,200".
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-pi-compaction-settings.test.sh` - new contract test, both cases pass - End-to-end: `node /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01M01370WPXN3ZPNDY85JT9SV1/pi-compaction-e2e.mjs $PWD` - loads the repo through Pi 0.84.1's own SettingsManager + shouldCompact, reads gpt-5.6-sol contextWindow=272000 from the operator's real ~/.pi/agent/models-store.json, and shows the trigger boundary at 175,000 for this repo vs 255,616 for an untrusted project and an unrelated project - `bash bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` - ok, total=147 - `bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` and `bash tests/fm-test-run.test.sh` - pass - `bash tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh` with and without .pi/settings.json present - same single failure both ways ("Pi follow-up adjacent case rendered a duplicate captain answer"), confirming it is pre-existing - Read Pi 0.84.1 `core/compaction/compaction.js` (shouldCompact, DEFAULT_COMPACTION_SETTINGS reserveTokens=16384/keepRecentTokens=20000) and `core/settings-manager.js` (deep-merge of project over global, trust gating) to confirm the documented formula and scope claims - `git status --porcelain` - worktree clean, no transient artifacts left

title: feat(calm): hide internal operational turn acknowledgements from captain chat
body:
## Intent The developer's goal was to clean up Firstmate's Pi chat so the visible captain transcript contains essentially only captain input and captain-facing outcomes, without weakening monitoring: no visible synthetic wake entries for duplicate, obsolete, or already-drained notifications, and no "no action needed" assistant replies, while every AGENTS.md section 8 safety property (durable queue ordering, one healthy supervision cycle, no blind turn end, lock and away-mode ownership, cleanup) stayed intact. They required real root-cause work separating trigger, masking condition, and symptom, a real Pi live E2E plus an isolated Herdr-backed path through the lab helper, deterministic regression coverage that fails on the old implementation, lint and strict typecheck, and explicitly forbade fixing it by disabling stale detection, cutting cadence, swallowing actionable records, or moving to another harness. They then approved shipping through no-mistakes, delegated the gate decisions (option A for the watcher startup barrier, option A for the teardown retire race) while barring --yes and any merge, and approved a public fork (doitdigital0495/firstmate) to work around read-only push access. Finally the developer completely superseded the behavior-changing implementation: abort the active run, settle branch custody, reset to the stated clean base, and reimplement as presentation-only — hiding only the rendered operational acknowledgement while leaving all model/session delivery and vanilla Firstmate behavior untouched and important outcomes visible — then validate and ship that via a cross-fork PR against kunchenguid/firstmate main driven to CI green, without merging. ## What Changed - Calm now hides the rendered acknowledgement an internal operational turn produces: the Pi user layout marks a turn internal when it hides an operational input, and the assistant layout drops a reply that is exactly the no-action phrase from chat while leaving model and session delivery untouched. - The internal-turn verdict is latched per assistant row on first render, so re-layout (invalidate, resume, compaction rebuild) cannot re-filter an already-rendered row under a later turn's flag; the flag is cleared only for genuinely captain-side input roles, not for replayed assistant rows. - Added `calmReplyIsBareAcknowledgement` plus the operational-turn flag accessors in `fm-calm-visibility.ts`, a deterministic regression test in `tests/fm-calm-pi-extension.test.sh` that fails against the pre-change libs, and updated `docs/calm.md`, `docs/calm-mode-feasibility.md`, and `README.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Well-bounded presentation-only change confined to three Pi extension modules, filtering exactly one prescribed phrase with per-row latching and regression tests for the resize and rebuild paths; every residual edge fails toward showing more, not hiding captain-relevant output. ## Testing Ran the Calm Pi extension suite plus a purpose-built live Pi TUI end-to-end run in tmux with a stub model provider, capturing the captain's actual chat screen at five steps: with Calm off the internal watcher wake and its "Captain, shipshape." reply are both on screen; after /calm both halves of that internal exchange are gone; a captain-typed turn answered with the exact same phrase stays visible; an internal turn answering with a review-ready PR link stays visible; and /calm off restores the whole transcript. The saved session JSONL shows every message, including the hidden ones, delivered and stored unchanged, confirming the change is presentation-only. The new deterministic test passes and fails when run against the base implementation. Two failures in the same suite reproduce at the base commit and stem from the locally installed Pi 0.84.1 versus the suite's pinned 0.81.1, so they are pre-existing rather than regressions. - Evidence: Pi chat screen across the five e2e steps (annotated composite) (local file: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01M0139H212RQ7XZZ5N1J37QZS/pi-calm-operational-reply.png)
Evidence: Calm off: internal wake row + acknowledgement visible ```text pi v0.84.1 escape interrupt · ctrl+c/ctrl+d clear/exit · / commands · ! bash · ctrl+o more Press ctrl+o to show full startup help and loaded resources. Pi cascades invalidate() to every chat child (pi-tui tui.js invalidate() -> root.invalidate(); alt-screen implicitDocument.invalidate(); triggered on terminal cell-dimension change, screen switch, mermaid-mode change). So an already-rendered row is re-filtered under a flag belonging to a later turn: a genuine 'Captain, shipshape.' reply to a captain prompt, rendered while the flag was false, disappears from the transcript once an internal wake sets the flag true and any invalidate fires. Fix: latch the turn state per component on the first updateContent (e.g. state.calmOperationalTurn ??= calmOperationalTurnIsActive()) so a message's visibility is decided by its own turn, not by whatever turn is current at re-layout time. - ℹ️ `.pi/extensions/lib/fm-calm-operational-user-layout.ts:123` - The role!=='user' early return delegates without clearing the flag, but Pi routes captain-run bash (`!cmd`) through addMessageToChat with role 'bashExecution', and compaction summaries / custom messages likewise. Those are genuine captain-side inputs, so the stated invariant ('the only way the flag stays set is an actually-hidden operational input') does not hold on those paths. Impact today is nil because none of them start a model turn, but clearing the flag on the non-'user' path would make the code match its documented contract. - ℹ️ `.pi/extensions/lib/fm-calm-assistant-layout.ts:50` - updateContent runs on every streaming delta and stopReason is not yet 'toolUse' mid-stream, so a reply that begins 'Captain, shipshape.' and then continues with real content will be hidden for the frames where the accumulated text matches exactly, then reappear. Cosmetic flicker only - the final message renders correctly - and per-component latching of the turn flag would not remove it. 🔧 Fix: latch operational-turn verdict per assistant row 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `.pi/extensions/lib/fm-calm-operational-user-layout.ts:123` - The new blanket setCalmOperationalTurn(false) on the role !== "user" path also fires for assistant messages. Pi's renderSessionItems (session resume and post-compaction rebuildChatFromMessages, interactive-mode.js:2908) replays assistant messages through addMessageToChat, and the assistant branch constructs AssistantMessageComponent, whose constructor calls updateContent (assistant-message.js:31). So on every rebuild the flag is cleared immediately before the operational turn's assistant component latches state.calmOperationalTurn, the latch captures false, and the acknowledgement that was hidden live reappears in chat after a resume or compaction. Same defeat happens live if any extension emits a role "custom" message mid-turn (interactive-mode.js:2530). Narrow the clear to the genuinely captain-side roles that were the point of the previous fix (bashExecution, custom, compactionSummary, branchSummary) and leave the flag untouched for assistant/toolResult, so replay latches the same verdict as the live render. - ℹ️ `.pi/extensions/lib/fm-calm-operational-user-layout.ts:153` - setCalmOperationalTurn(true) runs without consulting patch.hidesOperationalInput(), so with Calm off the operational input is rendered visibly yet the turn is still marked internal. Harmless today because hideOperationalReply separately gates on calmPresentationHides, and it is what makes a mid-session Calm toggle repaint both halves consistently, but the comment's claim that the flag 'may only stay set for an operational input this layout actually hid' is not literally true. 🔧 Fix: clear internal-turn flag only for genuine captain input 2 infos still open: - ℹ️ `.pi/extensions/lib/fm-calm-operational-user-layout.ts:123` - The role !== "user" early return deliberately no longer clears the internal-turn flag (needed so a rebuild does not wipe it before the assistant row latches). Consequence: any model turn started by something other than a role "user" text message (captain-run bash, a custom/slash-command message) inherits the previous internal turn's flag, and a reply that is exactly the no-action phrase would be hidden. Impact is bounded to that one phrase and this is the tradeoff explicitly chosen in the prior round, so recording only. - ℹ️ `.pi/extensions/lib/fm-calm-assistant-layout.ts:116` - The latch depends on the operational input being replayed immediately before its reply. If compaction drops the operational input but keeps the acknowledgement, the replayed assistant row latches whatever the flag happens to be and a previously hidden "Captain, shipshape." reappears. Fails in the safe direction (shows more, never hides), so no action; noted because the rebuild test only covers the both-items-present ordering.

title: fix(bin): add CLAUDE.md symlink hygiene guard
body:
## Intent

Investigate why jmp-hub's CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md symlink (a captain-decided one-source-of-truth convention; the symlink direction must never be reversed or removed) keeps turning into a plain file on fm/* worker branches, causing repeated 'distinct types on each side' merge conflicts (documented in PR #621). The leading hypothesis to test first was that no-mistakes' prompt-injection defense neutralizes AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md by writing through the symlink before running the gate agent, which would explain why every pipeline-processed branch is affected. That hypothesis had to be confirmed or refuted with hard evidence (commit SHAs, authorship, git log -p), not argued from plausibility. Investigation in a read-only clone of jmp-hub at projects/jmp-hub (never modified) found: CLAUDE.md became a symlink only in commit 80f54e46 (PR #612, 2026-08-05 02:28, author V4f1k). Checked all 103 current origin/fm/* branches: every branch whose CLAUDE.md is a plain file provably does NOT have 80f54e46 as an ancestor (it simply predates the symlink conversion and hasn't synced since - not corruption). Every branch descended from 80f54e46 still has the correct symlink. No no-mistakes-authored commit (grep for 'no-mistakes(document/review):' commits) ever changes CLAUDE.md's file mode, and the currently-running no-mistakes worktree for jmp-hub still has an intact symlink. This refutes the leading hypothesis with direct evidence. The actual mechanism: merging/rebasing a pre-conversion branch against a post-conversion base hits git's ordinary 'distinct types on each side' conflict on CLAUDE.md (exactly reproduced in PR #621's merge commit 7166a1ec, which resolved it correctly by keeping the symlink), and that manual conflict resolution is error-prone - fm/don768-kanban-brana's merge (86204b0f) dropped CLAUDE.md entirely instead of keeping the symlink, requiring a manual restore the next day (5dd137c0). This is not a bug in firstmate's own bin/ tooling (bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh was already confirmed symlink-aware and ruled out first) nor in no-mistakes; it is an operational hazard of syncing stale branches, so per the task's explicit instructions the deliverable is a safety net rather than a root-cause code fix: bin/fm-claude-symlink-check.sh is a new, project-agnostic, read-only guard script. It silently skips (exit 0) any repo whose resolved base branch does not manage CLAUDE.md as a symlink, so it is a no-op everywhere except a project that has actually adopted this convention. Where the base does manage it as a symlink, it verifies the worktree's CLAUDE.md still matches (present, is a symlink, correct target) and on failure prints the exact recovery commands (git checkout <base> -- CLAUDE.md, or ln -sfn <target> CLAUDE.md) and exits 1. It auto-detects the base branch (preferring the freshest locally-available remote-tracking ref, falling back to a local branch) or accepts an explicit ref for testing, mirroring the existing default_branch() pattern already duplicated in bin/fm-ff-lib.sh and bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh (deliberately not refactored into a shared lib - that consolidation is out of scope for this fix per explicit instructions to avoid repo-wide cleanup as a side effect). It is wired into bin/fm-brief.sh's shared 'Project memory' section so every ship-mode brief (no-mistakes, direct-PR, local-only) instructs the worker to run it right before reporting done - i.e. before a PR ever exists, not just left available. Test coverage: tests/fm-claude-symlink-check.test.sh (7 scenarios: matching symlink passes, regular-file demotion fails with both recovery commands present, missing file fails, wrong-target symlink fails, a repo with no symlink policy skips silently, a repo with no CLAUDE.md at all skips silently, and auto-detection of origin's default branch works) plus a new assertion in tests/fm-brief.test.sh confirming the hygiene-check section renders in all three delivery modes. bin/fm-test-run.sh gained one line classifying the new test into the existing pure-contract-unit family (same family as the closely related fm-ensure-agents-md.test.sh). Deliberately out of scope, per explicit instruction: do not touch jmp-hub at all (read-only investigation only, verified via git log/ls-tree/diff against the local read-only clone and its fetched remote branches, never committing there), do not un-break or rewrite history on any of the 34+ affected fm/* branches (most are dead; rewriting other workers' branches is not this task's job), do not reverse or remove the CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md symlink direction (captain's standing decision), and no repo-wide renaming/cleanup beyond this fix's own files. Full local verification already done directly (captain's standing instruction: the full bin/fm-test-run.sh suite is CI's job via --check-coverage in ci.yml, not duplicated locally) - bin/fm-lint.sh is clean on every touched script (fm-claude-symlink-check.sh, fm-brief.sh, fm-test-run.sh), the new and touched test files pass standalone and through the real bin/fm-test-run.sh harness, and the pure-contract-unit family run is green except two pre-existing, environment-dependent failures (missing tasks-axi and the @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent npm package in this session) confirmed unrelated to this diff by isolated reruns - neither failing test file references any file this change touches.

## What Changed

- Added `bin/fm-claude-symlink-check.sh`, a project-agnostic read-only guard that detects broken `CLAUDE.md` symlinks and prints recovery commands.
- Wired the guard into all ship-mode briefs and documented it in `docs/scripts.md`.
- Added comprehensive guard and brief-rendering coverage, registering the new test in the existing test family.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Captain, the change is bounded and I found no material source-verifiable regressions or intent violations.

## Testing

Fresh focused tests passed standalone and through the real harness. Manual CLI evidence confirms failure diagnostics, recovery guidance, committed-restore enforcement, and silent no-policy behavior; generated briefs contain the guard in all three delivery modes. No linters or full-suite tests were run, and the worktree is clean.

<summary>Evidence: CLI guard failure and recovery transcript</summary>

```text
$ bin/fm-claude-symlink-check.sh <broken worktree>
exit=1
error: CLAUDE.md in /private/var/folders/mz/3dbzbvkd1375djgpnq7r7hj40000gp/T/tmp.o8ktVF2HQK/symlink-policy is a regular file, but main manages it as a symlink -> AGENTS.md.
This is the classic 'distinct types on each side' merge fallout: a pre-conversion branch clobbered the symlink.
Restore it: git -C '/private/var/folders/mz/3dbzbvkd1375djgpnq7r7hj40000gp/T/tmp.o8ktVF2HQK/symlink-policy' checkout 'main' -- 'CLAUDE.md'   (or: ln -sfn -- 'AGENTS.md' '/private/var/folders/mz/3dbzbvkd1375djgpnq7r7hj40000gp/T/tmp.o8ktVF2HQK/symlink-policy/CLAUDE.md')
$ git checkout main -- CLAUDE.md; bin/fm-claude-symlink-check.sh <uncommitted restore>

Commit the restored symlink: git -C '/private/var/folders/mz/3dbzbvkd1375djgpnq7r7hj40000gp/T/tmp.o8ktVF2HQK/symlink-policy' --literal-pathspecs add -f -- 'CLAUDE.md' && git -C '/private/var/folders/mz/3dbzbvkd1375djgpnq7r7hj40000gp/T/tmp.o8ktVF2HQK/symlink-policy' --literal-pathspecs commit -m 'fix: restore the CLAUDE.md symlink' -- 'CLAUDE.md'
$ bin/fm-claude-symlink-check.sh <committed restore>
exit=0
ok: CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md matches main in /private/var/folders/mz/3dbzbvkd1375djgpnq7r7hj40000gp/T/tmp.o8ktVF2HQK/symlink-policy (working tree and branch tip)

exit=0 output_bytes=0
```
