title: fix(spawn): suppress the shell auto-update prompt before treehouse get
body:
## The failure

Once oh-my-zsh's periodic update check falls due, every new interactive shell prints:

```
[oh-my-zsh] Would you like to update? [Y/n]
```

`treehouse get` starts exactly such a shell inside the worktree. The prompt blocks on stdin, so the `cd` never lands and the spawn dies on the worktree settle timeout with `did not enter a worktree`.

The symptom is badly misleading: spawns work all session, then **every** spawn fails at once, on both the tmux and herdr backends, with nothing wrong in firstmate, treehouse or the worktree pool. Observed live 2026-08-13 across a whole fleet.

## The fix

Export `DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE=true` into the pane before `treehouse get`, so the subshell it starts inherits it.

**Ordering is the entire fix.** Sent afterwards, the prompting shell has already started. The regression test therefore asserts the *order* the two lines reach the pane, not merely that both were sent.

## Test

`tests/fm-spawn-shell-autoupdate.test.sh` drives `fm-spawn.sh` against a fake tmux that logs `send-keys` payloads in call order, then asserts the suppression is the first of the two and `treehouse get` the second.

Verified it actually catches the regression: with the export line removed the test fails with `first relevant send was 'treehouse get', expected the auto-update suppression`, and passes again once restored.

## Scope

- Only the non-secondmate, non-orca `treehouse get` path is touched. Relaunch, secondmate and orca spawns acquire no worktree through that path and are unaffected.
- Backend-agnostic: the line goes through `spawn_send_text_line`, so tmux and herdr both get it.

## Verification gap, stated rather than buried

`bin/fm-lint.sh` could not run here - ShellCheck is not installed on this machine, and the script refuses any version other than the pinned 0.11.0 rather than giving false parity. `bash -n bin/fm-spawn.sh` is clean and the new test passes; CI's shellcheck run is the real check.

## Rollback

Revert the two added lines in `bin/fm-spawn.sh`. Spawns then fail again, but only once the update check next comes due.

title: fix(afk): stand supervision down for a live away daemon, not the away flag
body:
## Intent

GOAL: In firstmate's away mode ("AFK"), both the native watcher-continuity mechanism and the turn-end guard were believed to stand down on the SOLE PRESENCE of the flag file state/.afk, without ever checking that the away-mode daemon is still alive. A dead daemon therefore left the home with NO supervision AND NO alarm at the same time, silently.

THE DEFECT AS REPORTED (measured 2026-08-15). When state/.afk exists, bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh explicitly stands down (around line 157) because the away daemon is supposed to own the watcher, and bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh was reported to disarm its check too (around line 349). Both were believed to stand down on flag presence, never on daemon liveness. Measured consequence the same evening: the daemon was killed THREE times by the host - at 18:59:48 after 2h43, then around 19:16:5x after 14 minutes, then again a few minutes after the following turn end. Each time state/.afk remained present, so both mechanisms stayed disarmed: no live supervision, no alarm, no guard to signal that a turn was ending blind. Only a host notification announcing the process death woke the first mate. Nothing was lost - the wake queue is durable and the drain recovers everything - but detection latency was bounded by nothing. The defect is NOT that the daemon dies. It is that a home in away mode with a dead daemon has NEITHER supervision NOR a guard, and that this combination is SILENT. The flag was treated as proof of supervision when it is only a declaration of intent.

SECOND REPORTED FACT, which shapes the fix. The daemon could never deliver anything in this configuration: the first mate runs as a host background task and has no captain pane to inject into, so discover_supervisor_target falls back. Evidence: the state/.subsuper-inject-wedged marker written at 18:55 reporting 302s undelivered, and two batches of escalations left in state/.subsuper-escalations, never received as a message. Away mode was doubly inoperative - it neither survived nor spoke to anyone - while disarming the two mechanisms that do work. The native /afk path therefore assumes two things it never verifies: durable background work, and a reachable captain pane. A host-backgrounded session has neither.

WHAT WAS ASKED. (1) Investigate first, code second. Four candidate approaches were offered with no imposed preference: (a) make both mechanisms' stand-down depend on daemon LIVENESS rather than flag presence, building on the daemon lock's existing identity record; (b) leave the turn-end guard active in away mode and have it demand live supervision from whatever source; (c) make the pair "flag present + daemon dead" a loud alarm, on par with the injection wedge; (d) have the /afk skill refuse to enter away mode when its two preconditions - durable background work and a reachable injection target - are not established, rather than entering a mode that disarms real supervision. Read the real code before deciding, and justify the choice in the PR. (2) Implement, with colocated tests.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT NOT TO BREAK. Daemon ownership of the watcher is deliberate and must remain possible: the fix must not create two competing supervision cycles, and must not let the native mechanism re-arm on top of a live daemon. The target is: when the daemon is alive, nothing changes; when it dies or cannot deliver, it is visible and repairable.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. With a LIVE away daemon, current behavior is preserved identically: one supervision cycle, the daemon's. With the flag present and the daemon DEAD, the home is no longer both unsupervised and unalarmed: that state is detected and surfaced visibly. Entering away mode can no longer suggest a supervision that does not exist when its preconditions do not hold. Colocated tests covering at minimum: live daemon (no change), dead daemon under a present flag, and away-mode entry behavior depending on whether the preconditions hold. Documentation updated wherever this contract is described (docs/turnend-guard.md, docs/watcher-continuity.md, the /afk skill, per what the fix touches).

WHAT READING THE REAL CODE ESTABLISHED, and the resulting decisions (these correct two premises above and explain choices a reviewer seeing only the diff would find surprising):

1. Reproduced end to end on fixture homes across three states (no flag / flag + live daemon / flag + dead daemon), running the real mechanisms. bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh:117 does stand down on flag presence alone - confirmed, and it is the real supervision hole. But bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh:349 is NOT a stand-down: it is failure_episode_verified, which REFUSES the attended fail-open under away mode, i.e. stricter, not weaker. The turn-end guard did block; what it lacked was naming the decisive fact. The same flag-presence stand-down was found in two more adapters the report did not mention: bin/fm-turnend-guard-cursor.sh (5 sites) and .opencode/plugins/fm-primary-watch-arm.js (shouldArm).

2. Found while reading, and worse than the reported symptom: bin/fm-session-start.sh asserted "away-mode supervision is active; the daemon owns the watcher" from flag presence alone, and the emitted supervision block told the model to keep normal harness supervision paused. On restart the flag was actively lying to the first mate about who was supervising.

3. The second reported fact is structural: fm_afk_launch_start_native writes the flag BEFORE any daemon exists and cannot wait for a harness-native background job, while the terminal-backed path has fm_afk_launch_wait_ready plus rollback. That is the entry hole.

DECISION: approach (a), because it subsumes (b), (c) and (d) instead of stacking three separate mechanisms. fm_afk_supervision_state in bin/fm-wake-lib.sh is the single owner of a three-value vocabulary - off / daemon / armed-no-daemon - proven from the process identity already recorded in the daemon lock, so a reused pid never passes as the daemon. The predicate already existed, buried in bin/fm-afk-start.sh (daemon_lock_held_by_live_daemon plus daemon_pid_matches); it was extracted to the shared library and its former callers rewired, rather than writing a second implementation. (b) follows: in armed-no-daemon the native mechanisms stay armed, so live supervision is restored from whatever source. (c) follows: the state is named in the Stop auto-arm's rewake and failure banners, the turn-end guard's block reason, the pull guard's banner, the session-start digest, and the emitted supervision block. (d) follows without a new precondition engine: since supervision is never inferred from the flag again, an unconfirmed native entry degrades to ordinary harness supervision instead of removing it; the /afk skill additionally must confirm `daemon` via the new read-only `bin/fm-afk-launch.sh status` before reporting away mode active. This deliberately avoids building a preconditions/policy layer, per the standing instruction to prefer the simplest direct path unless a concrete blocker justifies more machinery - the daemon already validates its injection target at startup and refuses loudly, and that refusal is no longer silent once the flag stops disarming everything.

DELIBERATE CHOICES A REVIEWER SHOULD NOT FLAG AS MISTAKES:
- fm_supervision_needed is deliberately NOT modified. Making "away mode armed" a supervision need would touch a very central predicate and could make an idle home arm-and-rewake in a loop. Accepted consequence, stated in docs/watcher-continuity.md: an armed-no-daemon home with nothing in flight raises at the first real supervision need and at the next session start, not immediately.
- No mechanism ever clears state/.afk. Leaving away mode is the captain's decision; a home that silently dropped the flag would resume per-wake injection instead of batching. Several tests assert the flag survives.
- The stand-down predicate short-circuits on the flag's absence, so the common no-away-mode path pays no extra process spawn.
- The OpenCode plugin (JavaScript) shells out to `bin/fm-afk-launch.sh status` rather than reimplementing the identity check, to keep one owner; an unreadable answer keeps it armed, which is the safe direction.
- --afk on bin/fm-supervision-instructions.sh now takes the state name, keeping legacy 0/1 accepted as off/daemon.
- Existing away-mode tests were converted into the "live daemon" cases and each gained its "dead daemon" mirror, with the same flag on disk in both, so only liveness distinguishes them.
- tests/fm-session-start.test.sh's fake `ps` gained an lstart passthrough to the real /bin/ps: process identity reads must stay truthful, since a faked identity would make every liveness proof built on it vacuous.

VERIFICATION ALREADY RUN LOCALLY: bin/fm-lint.sh clean, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh clean, and green suites fm-afk-launch, fm-turnend-guard, fm-session-start, fm-claude-stop-autoarm, fm-pi-watch-extension, fm-daemon, fm-watch-triage, fm-guard-stale-banner, fm-supervision-instructions, fm-cursor-primary, fm-afk-return.

DELIVERY CONTEXT: this fork's upstream runs NO CI on fork PRs, so the pipeline's ci step cannot go green there; an open PR with the rest of the pipeline green is the normal terminal state for this repository.

## What Changed

- Added a single owner for away-mode supervision ownership in `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh`: `fm_afk_supervision_state` resolves `off` / `daemon` / `armed-no-daemon` by proving the daemon lock's recorded process identity (so a reused pid never passes), plus the `fm_afk_daemon_owns_supervision` stand-down predicate and the one shared `fm_afk_daemon_down_notice` alarm sentence. The predicates were extracted from `bin/fm-afk-start.sh`'s private `daemon_lock_*` helpers rather than reimplemented, and `bin/fm-afk-launch.sh` gained read-only `status` and `down-notice <cover>` subcommands so non-bash callers reach the same owner.
- Rewired every flag-presence stand-down onto daemon liveness: the Claude Stop auto-arm, the Cursor stop-hook park (5 sites), the OpenCode plugin's `shouldArm`, and `bin/fm-watch.sh`'s triage gate (memoized once per poll cycle) now stand down only for a live daemon. In `armed-no-daemon` the native mechanisms stay armed and name the broken away mode on the Stop rewake and failure banners, the Cursor / Pi / OpenCode wake follow-ups, the turn-end guard's block reason and attended fail-open, the pull guard banner, and the session-start digest and supervision block; `--afk` on `bin/fm-supervision-instructions.sh` now takes the state name with legacy `0`/`1` still accepted, and `failure_episode_verified` refuses the attended fail-open only for a live daemon. Nothing clears `state/.afk`.
- The `/afk` skill must now confirm `daemon` via `bin/fm-afk-launch.sh status` before reporting away mode active. Documented the contract in a new "Away-mode stand-down" section of `docs/watcher-continuity.md` and in `docs/turnend-guard.md`, and added colocated coverage: `tests/lib.sh` grew `fm_fake_afk_daemon` / `fm_fake_afk_flagged_no_daemon` fixtures, and the existing away-mode cases became live-daemon cases each mirrored by a dead-daemon case with the same flag on disk across the afk-launch, claude-stop-autoarm, cursor-primary, pi-watch-extension, watch-triage, session-start, supervision-instructions, and turnend-guard suites.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: Le changement est large (12 scripts bin/, 2 adaptateurs JS/TS, 6 protocoles de supervision) et assouplit une porte de fail-open, mais l'invariant central - seul un démon vivant possède la supervision - est appliqué de façon cohérente derrière un propriétaire unique, couvert par des tests colocalisés qui distinguent les trois états avec le même drapeau sur disque, et documenté ; les trois constats restants sont une lacune de cohérence bornée sur un chemin nouvellement atteignable et deux points de robustesse latents, tous traitables en suivi.

## Testing

J'ai exécuté les 11 suites ciblées annoncées dans l'intention (fm-afk-launch, fm-turnend-guard, fm-session-start, fm-claude-stop-autoarm, fm-pi-watch-extension, fm-daemon, fm-watch-triage, fm-guard-stale-banner, fm-supervision-instructions, fm-cursor-primary, fm-afk-return) : toutes vertes, aucun échec, aucune saut de porte. Comme des tests unitaires verts ne prouvent pas l'intention, j'ai écrit et lancé une démonstration end-to-end qui reproduit le défaut mesuré puis montre le correctif : des homes fixtures portant exactement le même fichier state/.afk, ne différant que par la vivacité du processus enregistré dans le verrou du démon, traversés par les vrais mécanismes une fois avec le bin/ du commit de base et une fois avec celui de la branche. Résultat : sur la base, flag présent et démon mort, le hook Stop se met en veille en silence (exit 0, watcher jamais armé) - le home sans supervision ni alarme décrit dans le rapport ; sur la branche, le même home arme le watcher, sort en 2 et affiche la bannière nommant le mode away cassé et le seul mécanisme qui le couvre. Avec un démon vivant, base et branche produisent une sortie identique (exit 0, aucun armement) : la propriété "quand le démon est vivant, rien ne change" tient. La garde de fin de tour, qui bloquait déjà dans les deux cas, dit désormais "Away mode is flagged but its daemon is NOT running" au lieu de "Away mode owns watcher supervision" quand le démon est mort, et conserve mot pour mot l'ancienne formulation quand il est vivant. Le digest de démarrage de session ne prétend plus qu'un démon mort possède le watcher, dans ses trois emplacements (bloc de supervision, sous-section AFK, prochaine étape). Enfin, l'entrée native écrit le flag mais `status` répond armed-no-daemon, donc le skill /afk ne peut plus déclarer le mode away actif, et le home reste couvert par la supervision ordinaire. Aucun mécanisme n'a effacé state/.afk sur les 13 homes traversés. Pas de preuve visuelle : le changement est entièrement CLI/terminal, sans surface rendue en HTML ou en interface graphique, et la transcription capture fidèlement ce que la session voit, bannières encadrées comprises. Worktree laissé propre, temporaires supprimés.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end demonstration of "stand supervision down for a LIVE away daemon,
# not for the away flag" (branch fm/fm-afk-standdown-demon-mort).
#
# Builds fixture firstmate homes that differ ONLY in away-daemon liveness:
#   off              no state/.afk
#   daemon           state/.afk + a live process recorded in the daemon lock
#   armed-no-daemon  state/.afk + a DEAD pid recorded in the same lock
# and runs the REAL mechanisms a first mate meets at turn end and at restart,
# once against the base commit and once against this branch.
#
# Usage: afk-liveness-e2e.sh <worktree-root> <base-commit>
set -u

ROOT=$1
BASE=$2
TMP=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fm-afk-e2e.XXXXXX")
PIDS=()
cleanup() {
  local p
  for p in "${PIDS[@]:-}"; do kill "$p" 2>/dev/null || true; done
  [ -n "${TMP:-}" ] && [ -d "${TMP:-}" ] && /bin/rm -rf -- "${TMP:?}"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

hr() { printf '\n================================================================\n%s\n================================================================\n' "$1"; }
sub() { printf '\n--- %s\n' "$1"; }

# --- two checkouts of the toolbelt: the base commit and this branch ----------
mkdir -p "$TMP/base-checkout" "$TMP/head-checkout"
git -C "$ROOT" archive "$BASE" bin | tar -x -C "$TMP/base-checkout"
cp -R "$ROOT/bin" "$TMP/head-checkout/bin"

# A throwaway git repo to stand in for FM_ROOT (the toolbelt checkout the
# session-start digest inspects); scripts still come from the two bin/ dirs.
git init -q -b main "$TMP/fmroot" && git -C "$TMP/fmroot" commit -q --allow-empty -m init

# --- fixture homes ----------------------------------------------------------
# make_home <name> <off|daemon|dead> <bin-dir>
make_home() {
  local name=$1 kind=$2 bindir=$3 home="$TMP/$1" pid lock dead
  mkdir -p "$home/state" "$home/data" "$home/config"
  git init -q "$home" >/dev/null && git -C "$home" commit -q --allow-empty -m init
  : > "$home/AGENTS.md"
  cp -R "$bindir" "$home/bin"
  # one task in flight: the home genuinely needs supervision
  printf 'task=demo\n' > "$home/state/demo.meta"
  lock="$home/state/.supervise-daemon.lock"
  case "$kind" in
    off) : ;;
    daemon)
      date '+%s' > "$home/state/.afk"
      sleep 900 >/dev/null 2>&1 & pid=$!
      PIDS+=("$pid")
      mkdir -p "$lock"
      printf '%s\n' "$pid" > "$lock/pid"
      bash -c '. "$1"; fm_pid_identity "$2"' _ "$home/bin/fm-wake-lib.sh" "$pid" > "$lock/pid-identity"
      ;;
    dead)
      date '+%s' > "$home/state/.afk"
      dead=999999
      while kill -0 "$dead" 2>/dev/null; do dead=$((dead + 1)); done
      mkdir -p "$lock"
      printf '%s\n' "$dead" > "$lock/pid"
      printf 'dead away-mode daemon identity\n' > "$lock/pid-identity"
      ;;
  esac
  # The arm stub stands in for a real watcher launch: it records that it ran and
  # reports the actionable close the real bin/fm-watch-arm.sh reports. Written
  # over the copied executable, so it keeps that file's mode.
  cat > "$home/bin/fm-watch-arm.sh" <<'ARM'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "$$" >> "$FM_HOME/state/arm-ran"
printf 'watcher: started pid=%s (beacon fresh)\n' "$$"
printf 'stale: demo-task no progress for 21m\n'
exit 0
ARM
  printf '%s\n' "$home"
}

# The Stop hook runs as a child of the harness holding the session lock.
FAKEBIN="$TMP/fakebin"; mkdir -p "$FAKEBIN"; ln -sf /bin/bash "$FAKEBIN/claude"
run_stop_hook() {
  local home=$1 rc=0
  printf '%s\n' '{"session_id":"demo","stop_hook_active":false}' \
    | FM_HOME="$home" "$FAKEBIN/claude" -c '
        printf "%s\n" "$$" > "$FM_HOME/state/.lock"
        "$FM_HOME/bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh"
      ' 2>&1 || rc=$?
  printf '\n[hook exit=%s]  [watcher arm ran: %s]  [state/.afk still present: %s]\n' \
    "$rc" \
    "$([ -e "$home/state/arm-ran" ] && echo yes || echo 'NO - hook stood down')" \
    "$([ -e "$home/state/.afk" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
}

run_turnend_guard() {
  local home=$1 rc=0
  printf '{"stop_hook_active":false}' \
    | CLAUDECODE=1 FM_HOME="$home" bash "$home/bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh" 2>&1 || rc=$?
  printf '\n[guard exit=%s]\n' "$rc"
}

run_session_start() {
  local home=$1
  FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$TMP/fmroot" FM_HOME="$home" "$home/bin/fm-session-start.sh" 2>/dev/null
}

# The three places the digest speaks about away mode: the supervision operating
# line, the fleet-digest AFK subsection, and the closing next-step block.
digest_slice() {
  local out
  out=$(cat)
  printf '\n[supervision operating instructions]\n'
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E '^- Away mode:'
  printf '\n[fleet digest, AFK subsection]\n'
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -A4 '^AFK$' | tail -n +3 | grep -v -E '^(=+|-+)?$'
  printf '\n[next step]\n'
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -A2 '^Away mode '
}

hr "1. bin/fm-afk-launch.sh status - the read-only supervision verdict (this branch)"
for k in off daemon dead; do make_home "s-$k" "$k" "$TMP/head-checkout/bin" >/dev/null; done
for k in off daemon dead; do
  printf '  %-30s -> %s\n' "fixture home away mode: $k" "$(FM_HOME="$TMP/s-$k" "$TMP/s-$k/bin/fm-afk-launch.sh" status)"
done
printf '\n  (the "daemon" and "dead" homes carry the SAME state/.afk file on disk;\n   only the liveness of the process recorded in the daemon lock differs.)\n'

hr "2. TURN END, Stop-owned watcher auto-arm (bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh)"
sub "BASE $BASE - away flag present, daemon DEAD (the reported defect)"
make_home "b-dead" dead "$TMP/base-checkout/bin" >/dev/null
run_stop_hook "$TMP/b-dead"
sub "THIS BRANCH - away flag present, daemon DEAD"
make_home "h-dead" dead "$TMP/head-checkout/bin" >/dev/null
run_stop_hook "$TMP/h-dead"
sub "THIS BRANCH - away flag present, daemon ALIVE (must be unchanged: one supervision cycle, the daemon's)"
make_home "h-live" daemon "$TMP/head-checkout/bin" >/dev/null
run_stop_hook "$TMP/h-live"
sub "BASE $BASE - away flag present, daemon ALIVE (control)"
make_home "b-live" daemon "$TMP/base-checkout/bin" >/dev/null
run_stop_hook "$TMP/b-live"

hr "3. TURN END, supervision guard block reason (bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh)"
sub "BASE $BASE - away flag present, daemon DEAD"
make_home "b-guard-dead" dead "$TMP/base-checkout/bin" >/dev/null
run_turnend_guard "$TMP/b-guard-dead"
sub "THIS BRANCH - away flag present, daemon DEAD"
make_home "h-guard-dead" dead "$TMP/head-checkout/bin" >/dev/null
run_turnend_guard "$TMP/h-guard-dead"
sub "THIS BRANCH - away flag present, daemon ALIVE (unchanged guidance)"
make_home "h-guard-live" daemon "$TMP/head-checkout/bin" >/dev/null
run_turnend_guard "$TMP/h-guard-live"

hr "4. SESSION START digest (bin/fm-session-start.sh) - what the first mate is told on restart"
make_home "b-ss-dead" dead "$TMP/base-checkout/bin" >/dev/null
make_home "h-ss-dead" dead "$TMP/head-checkout/bin" >/dev/null
make_home "h-ss-live" daemon "$TMP/head-checkout/bin" >/dev/null
sub "BASE $BASE - away flag present, daemon DEAD: supervision line, AFK section, next step"
run_session_start "$TMP/b-ss-dead" | digest_slice
sub "THIS BRANCH - away flag present, daemon DEAD"
run_session_start "$TMP/h-ss-dead" | digest_slice
sub "THIS BRANCH - away flag present, daemon ALIVE (unchanged)"
run_session_start "$TMP/h-ss-live" | digest_slice

hr "5. ENTERING away mode natively: the entry can no longer claim a supervision it has not got"
# start-native writes the flag BEFORE any harness-native background job exists
# and cannot wait for it, so this is the entry the /afk skill must confirm.
make_home "h-entry" off "$TMP/head-checkout/bin" >/dev/null
sub "bin/fm-afk-launch.sh start-native (this branch)"
FM_HOME="$TMP/h-entry" "$TMP/h-entry/bin/fm-afk-launch.sh" start-native
printf '  [exit=%s]  [state/.afk written: %s]\n' "$?" "$([ -e "$TMP/h-entry/state/.afk" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
sub "what the /afk skill must now read before it may report away mode active"
printf '  bin/fm-afk-launch.sh status -> %s\n' "$(FM_HOME="$TMP/h-entry" "$TMP/h-entry/bin/fm-afk-launch.sh" status)"
printf '  (not "daemon", so the skill reports away mode NOT running instead of active)\n'
sub "and the home is not left blind: the Stop-owned auto-arm still covers it"
run_stop_hook "$TMP/h-entry"

hr "6. Flag ownership: no mechanism cleared state/.afk anywhere above"
for h in "$TMP"/h-* "$TMP"/b-* "$TMP"/s-daemon "$TMP"/s-dead; do
  [ -d "$h/state" ] || continue
  printf '  %-16s state/.afk present: %s\n' "$(basename "$h")" "$([ -e "$h/state/.afk" ] && echo yes || echo NO)"
done
printf '\n'
```

La bannière de rewake (ligne 256) est exacte, elle, puisque l'armement a réussi. Le test `test_failed_arm_under_dead_afk_daemon_names_both_failures` valide que les deux échecs sont nommés, sans juger la cohérence de la phrase. Piste : passer à `afk_daemon_down_notice` un `<cover>` distinct sur le chemin d'échec (l'argument existe déjà justement parce que c'est la seule partie variable), ou faire porter à ce chemin une variante qui ne revendique aucune couverture.

🔧 Fix: launch away-mode launcher via bash, drop false cover claim
2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh:347` - `failure_episode_verified` went from `[ ! -e "$STATE/.afk" ] || return 1` to `! fm_afk_daemon_owns_supervision "$STATE" || return 1`. That is not just "naming the fact" - it makes the attended fail-open REACHABLE in `armed-no-daemon`, where the flag previously refused it outright. Concrete sequence: home in away mode + daemon killed + task in flight -> the Stop auto-arm now arms (fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh:120), fails, writes `.claude-autoarm-failure-notified` with `outcome=failed` -> next Stop, watcher still unhealthy, `budget_account_current_epoch` exhausts the block budget -> `failure_episode_verified` now returns 0 -> `terminal_fail_open` returns 0 -> the guard exits 0 printing `FIRSTMATE SUPERVISION IS GENUINELY DOWN: ... Keep this session attended and diagnose the automatic Stop-hook and watcher startup before relying on unattended supervision.` The new test `test_hook_claude_mode_dead_away_daemon_keeps_the_bounded_progression` (tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh:1535) asserts exactly this exit 0, so the loosening is deliberate and its rationale (avoid blocking forever against an ownership that does not exist) is sound - I am not asking to revert it. The problem is the message on that newly reachable path: it is the ONLY surface in this whole change that does not name the broken away mode, and it asks for attendance on a home whose `state/.afk` declares the captain away. That is the same defect round 3 fixed one file over: `afk_daemon_down_notice` was given an empty `<cover>` in the auto-arm failure banner precisely because "an alarm that claims a supervisor in the same breath as its failure" is the contract violation this task exists to stop. Here the terminal notice claims an ATTENDANT instead of a supervisor, with the same falsity. The intent also recorded this predicate as "stricter, not weaker. The turn-end guard did block; what it lacked was naming the decisive fact" - the diff both weakens it and leaves the fact unnamed on the resulting path. Suggested resolution, matching the pattern already established in this branch: prefix the systemMessage with `fm_afk_daemon_down_notice "$STATE" ""` (empty cover - nothing is covering the home at that point) and drop or qualify the "keep this session attended" clause when the state is `armed-no-daemon`, with an assertion in the dead-daemon test that the fail-open notice names the away mode.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:35` - Round 2 was asked to align every header sentence in this file that still asserted the removed flag-presence contract, and it fixed lines 12, 16, 55 and 151 - but line 35 still reads `Unless afk is active.` inside the `stale: <window>` reason description. That sentence documents exactly the branch the change re-gated: `stale` handoff is now conditioned on `afk_daemon_owns_triage` (bin/fm-watch.sh:1076), i.e. a LIVE daemon, and an `armed-no-daemon` home keeps the ordinary stale triage. A reader working through this header - which is explicitly the file's entry point, and which the same round rewrote three lines above and twenty lines below - is told the flag alone still switches this path. Mechanical fix: match the wording already used at lines 17-18 and 55, e.g. `Unless a live away-mode daemon owns triage.` (The same stale phrasing also survives in docs/configuration.md:364, "While away mode is active the daemon owns the watcher and its default cadence applies"; worth aligning in the same pass, but it is outside the file whose behavior changed.)

🔧 Fix: name broken away mode on the fail-open and stale contract text
1 warning still open:
- ⚠️ `.opencode/plugins/fm-primary-watch-arm.js:248` - Les deux adaptateurs JS/TS ajoutés au tour 3 accrochent la notice partagée avec un cover NON VIDE sur leurs chemins d'ÉCHEC, ce qui revendique une couverture dans la phrase même qui annonce que ce mécanisme est cassé.

Chemin concret côté OpenCode : `restoreAfterActionableClose` épuise ses retries -> `setArmStatus("failed")` -> `scheduleRetry` appelle `surfaceFailure` (.opencode/plugins/fm-primary-watch-arm.js:247, appelé aux lignes 312/318/326) avec « watcher: FAILED - OpenCode could not restore watcher continuity after N retries » -> `awayModeDownNotice(paths)` (ligne 129) dont le cover est figé à 'this plugin-owned watcher cycle' -> le prompt livré au modèle contient à la fois « OpenCode could not restore watcher continuity » et « away mode is supervising nothing and this plugin-owned watcher cycle is the only cover ». Le même défaut existe sur le chemin de restauration (ligne 403) dès que `result.failure` est non vide.

Côté Pi, c'est structurellement identique : `surfaceFailure` (.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:287) passe par `sendWake`, qui accroche la notice inconditionnellement (lignes 268-272) avec le cover 'this extension-owned watcher cycle', y compris pour « watcher: FAILED - Pi extension could not restore watcher continuity after N retries » (lignes 367-380).

C'est exactement le constat `autoarm-failure-banner-claims-cover` tranché au tour 3 pour la bannière bash, et le contrat que ce changement vient d'écrire l'interdit explicitement : docs/watcher-continuity.md:44 « A banner that has just reported its own mechanism broken passes no cover at all, and the sentence then says nothing is covering the home: an alarm that claims a supervisor in the same breath as its failure is the same "supervision that does not exist" this contract exists to stop. » `bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh:273` respecte cette règle (cover vide, asserté par `assert_not_contains "is the only cover"`), mais les deux adaptateurs ne PEUVENT pas la respecter : `fm_afk_launch_down_notice` (bin/fm-afk-launch.sh:601-608) refuse un cover vide avec le code 2, donc la variante « nothing is covering this home » - que `fm_afk_daemon_down_notice` sait pourtant produire - n'est pas atteignable depuis un appelant non-bash. `unit_down_notice_speaks_only_for_a_flagged_dead_daemon` verrouille même ce refus.

Piste alignée sur le propriétaire unique déjà en place : accepter un cover vide sur `down-notice` (distinguer « argument absent » de « argument vide »), le passer depuis `surfaceFailure` des deux adaptateurs et depuis le chemin `result.failure` non vide, et étendre les deux cas de test existants (`opencode_wake_notice_case`, `pi_wake_notice_case`) avec l'assertion symétrique du chemin bash.

🔧 Fix: let adapter failure wakes state that nothing covers the home
3 issues (1 warning, 2 infos) still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-turnend-guard-cursor.sh:263` - Le plafond de boucle du park Cursor est désormais atteignable en `armed-no-daemon` et y arrête définitivement la supervision sans jamais nommer l'away mode cassé. Le bloc plafond s'exécute AVANT la porte away-mode (`:271`), et la porte interne de `emit_followup` (`:123-127`) est passée de `[ -e "$STATE/.afk" ]` à `fm_afk_daemon_owns_supervision`, donc elle ne fait plus descendre que pour un démon VIVANT. Avant ce changement, la simple présence du drapeau y faisait sortir en 0 et cette bannière n'était jamais émise en mode absent. Séquence concrète : primary Cursor, `state/.afk` présent, démon tué, tâche en vol, absence longue -> le park réarme à chaque fin de tour (c'est le comportement voulu par ce changement) et livre ses réveils, chacun consommant un tour piloté par le hook sans message du capitaine -> à `LOOP_COUNT == LOOP_CEILING` (défaut 180, `:65`) `emit_followup` émet « FIRSTMATE SUPERVISION FOLLOW-UP CEILING REACHED ... automatic wake delivery stops here to bound the loop ... Supervision resumes automatically at the next turn end after the captain's next message » puis `exit 0` (`:134`) sans armer -> aux tours suivants `[ "$LOOP_COUNT" -eq "$LOOP_CEILING" ] || exit 0` sort en silence, plus aucun park, plus aucun watcher. Le home finit donc non supervisé, et le seul message qu'il reçoit conditionne la reprise au « prochain message du capitaine » - l'événement que `state/.afk` déclare précisément absent - sans nommer l'away mode cassé ni la seule réparation réelle (relancer le démon, qui n'a lui aucun plafond de boucle). C'est strictement meilleur qu'avant, où le park était inerte dès la première minute ; mais c'est la troisième surface Cursor et la seule que `docs/watcher-continuity.md` n'énumère pas parmi celles qui nomment l'état, alors qu'elle est la seule à annoncer l'arrêt de la supervision automatique. Piste alignée sur le motif déjà en place : accrocher `fm_afk_daemon_down_notice "$STATE" ''` à cette bannière (rien ne couvre le home une fois le plafond atteint), ou arbitrer que le plafond ne s'applique pas en `armed-no-daemon` puisque son unique condition de sortie est inatteignable dans cet état. À arbitrer par le capitaine : l'intent énumère explicitement où l'état est nommé et cette surface n'y figure pas.
- ℹ️ `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:269` - La valeur par défaut `cover = "this extension-owned watcher cycle"` de `sendWake` inverse le contrat que cette même ronde vient d'écrire pour le propriétaire partagé de la notice. Côté bash, un argument ABSENT est refusé en rc 2 (`bin/fm-afk-launch.sh:604-611`, « down-notice needs a cover argument; pass an empty one when nothing covers this home ») précisément pour attraper un appelant qui a oublié la clause, et `docs/watcher-continuity.md:46` le formalise : « Omitting the argument altogether stays a caller error and exits 2, so a caller that forgot the clause is caught rather than silently promoted ». Ici, un appelant qui omet l'argument est au contraire silencieusement promu à une REVENDICATION de couverture - exactement le défaut que les rondes 3 et 5 ont corrigé deux fois. Les deux appels actuels (`:292` et `:484`) sont explicites, donc le défaut est latent, mais la garde est inversée sur la seule surface où elle compte. Correction mécanique : rendre `cover` obligatoire (`cover: string`) puisque les deux appelants le passent déjà. Note sur le pendant OpenCode : `awayModeDownNotice(paths, cover)` (`.opencode/plugins/fm-primary-watch-arm.js:132`) n'a pas de défaut, mais un `cover` omis produirait `spawn` avec un argument `undefined`, qui rejette dans un `.catch(() => {})` (`:407`) et perdrait le réveil ENTIER, pas seulement la notice - l'échec y est silencieux plutôt que bruyant.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh:299` - `fm_afk_daemon_lock_owner` reproduit mot pour mot le corps de `fm_lock_link_owner`, défini 150 lignes plus bas dans LE MÊME fichier (`:450`) : même `readlink`, même garde `[ -n "$owner" ]`, même `case` absolu/relatif avec `dirname`. L'extraction depuis `bin/fm-afk-start.sh` (où la réutilisation était moins visible) a atterri juste à côté du propriétaire existant de cette résolution sans l'appeler. La branche `[ -L ]` peut simplement déléguer : `if [ -L "$lock" ]; then fm_lock_link_owner "$lock"; return; fi` - sémantique identique, puisque `fm_lock_link_owner` échoue de lui-même sur un non-lien. Secondairement, cette branche est elle-même redondante pour l'usage qui en est fait : `[ -d "$lock" ]` est déjà vrai pour un lien vers un répertoire et `cat "$lock/pid"` traverse le lien, ce que `fm_watcher_healthy` (`:98`) exploite déjà en lisant `"$lockdir/pid"` sans résoudre quoi que ce soit ; le cas du lien pendant retombe de toute façon sur pid vide donc `armed-no-daemon`, comme aujourd'hui. Le dépôt impose la règle du propriétaire unique pour tout contrat énoncé à plusieurs endroits, et deux copies dans un même fichier dérivent dès que seule l'une est éditée.

</details>

✅ No issues found.

title: feat(opencode): reload AGENTS.md after context compaction
body:
Add an OpenCode plugin that re-injects this repo's AGENTS.md after context compaction so the firstmate operational contract is not lost.

Changes:
- New plugin `.opencode/plugins/fm-primary-agents-reload.js` using `experimental.session.compacting` and `experimental.chat.system.transform` hooks, with idempotence via a reload marker.
- `.opencode/opencode.json` adds `AGENTS.md` to `instructions` as a fallback; validated against the published opencode schema.
- Regression tests in `tests/fm-primary-agents-reload.test.sh`.

Note: no-mistakes review is unavailable because Claude Code is blocked by org subscription and no other supported review agent is installed, so this ships as a direct PR.

title: fix(bin): absorb a decision-parked crew on the long re-surface cadence instead of wedge-escalating
body:
## Intent

Prevent the watcher (bin/fm-watch.sh) from wedge-escalating every FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS (240s, the live 4-minute cycle) a worker whose task carries a still-open captain decision (needs-decision/blocked the keyed status_open_decisions fold has not closed) and whose pane is provably working. Instead absorb such a worker on the long PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS re-surface cadence, exactly like a declared pause but kept distinct. Resume the normal wedge cadence immediately when the decision closes, so a crew still mute after the answer re-escalates. Preserve exact current behavior for workers without an open decision (no wedge-detection regression). Co-located tests cover the three cases: open decision absorbed and not wedge-escalated at 240s; closure resumes normal cadence and a mute crew re-escalates; a closed decision wedge-escalates like today. Docs updated where the cadence is described.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-watch.sh`: a provably-working stale pane whose task carries a still-open captain decision now routes to a new `handle_decision_held_stale`, which absorbs it on the long `PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS` cadence instead of arming the wedge timer that re-escalated it every `FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS`. It keeps its own `.decision-held-*`/`.decision-resurfaced-*` markers, reason text and triage-log label, distinct from a declared pause; the pause absorb and this one now share one `absorb_stale_on_long_cadence` implementation of the cadence. The absorb marker records the hash and the `size:mtime` status signature it was taken on, so a later poll re-folds the decision only when a new status line could have closed it, the marker never re-routes a differently-classified pane, and it survives a busy blip at the same hash but dies when the hash changes. On closure, `clear_decision_held_tracking` resets the stale suppressor and wedge timer so the next poll is a clean first-sight and a still-mute crew re-escalates as before. The gate is the provably-working verdict already proved on those paths, so panes without an open decision keep today's behavior untouched.
- `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh` adds the `task_has_open_decision` predicate over the existing keyed `status_open_decisions` fold, and `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh` clears `.decision-held-*` alongside the other watcher stale markers in `clear_pause_tracking`.
- `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` gains six tests driving a real watcher subprocess: open decision absorbed and not wedge-escalated at the threshold, a not-working crew with an open decision still surfacing immediately, the marker not outliving its absorb, the absorb surviving a same-hash busy blip, closure resuming the normal cadence for a mute crew, and a closed decision wedge-escalating as today. `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/configuration.md` and the `AGENTS.md` state-file inventory describe the new cadence and markers.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: Le changement modifie un chemin de supervision critique (232 lignes dans la boucle chaude du watcher) après quatre rounds de correction, mais l'état actuel satisfait tous les critères de l'intent, l'invariant du marqueur decision-held est vérifiable et étanche, aucune régression n'est introduite pour les workers sans décision ouverte, et six tests co-localisés couvrent le comportement observable ; seul subsiste un compromis assumé sur la non-reconduction de la preuve provably-working derrière un pane figé.

## Testing

Baseline : les trois fichiers de tests correspondant aux fichiers modifiés (fm-watch-triage, fm-classify-decision-key, fm-daemon) passent intégralement, sans échec ni flake observé. Preuve produit : un transcript CLI rejoue le scénario réel (crew qui poste needs-decision puis reste idle sur un pane provably-working) contre le watcher du commit de base puis celui de la branche - la base réveille firstmate 3 fois en 12 minutes avec « possible wedge, escalation 1/2/3 » jusqu'au demand-deep-inspection, la branche n'en réveille aucune et journalise « absorbed stale (decision held, awaiting captain) » en désarmant le timer wedge même planté comme franchi. Le même transcript montre le recheck borné unique par fenêtre PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS avec ses marqueurs propres (.decision-held-*/.decision-resurfaced-*, .paused-* jamais posé), la reprise immédiate de la cadence wedge dès qu'un « resolved » ferme la décision (crew resté muet ré-escalade), et un crew sans décision ouverte qui escalade exactement comme aujourd'hui. Aucune surface UI n'est concernée (watcher CLI/daemon), donc l'évidence visuelle est un transcript CLI. Worktree laissé propre, arbre bin/ du commit de base extrait uniquement dans un répertoire temporaire éphémère.

<details>
<summary>Evidence: Transcript E2E : base ef35d79 vs branche, meme fixture de decision ouverte</summary>

Source: [Transcript E2E : base ef35d79 vs branche, meme fixture de decision ouverte](https://github.com/Kallas95/firstmate/blob/aa1b68b67c09c3041ec116dcc886e3fe64df2e18/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-stale-sur-decision-ouverte/decision-held-e2e.txt)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end demonstration of the decision-held stale absorb, driving the REAL
# bin/fm-watch.sh binary (not a unit harness) against a realistic state dir:
# one crew that posted a captain decision (needs-decision) and then sat idle on
# a provably-working pane.
#
# The same fixture is replayed through the BASE-commit watcher and the watcher on
# this branch, so the transcript shows the user-visible difference: how many
# times firstmate's LLM is woken while the captain has not answered yet. Each
# "wake" below is one watcher poll cycle; the watcher exits when it surfaces a
# reason, which is what re-arms firstmate and costs a full captain turn.
#
# Usage: decision-held-e2e.sh <repo-root> <base-bin-tree>
set -u

REPO=${1:?repo root}
BASE_TREE=${2:?base bin tree}

# shellcheck source=/dev/null
. "$REPO/tests/wake-helpers.sh"
TMP_ROOT=$(fm_test_tmproot fm-decision-held-e2e)

FIXED_WATCH="$REPO/bin/fm-watch.sh"
BASE_WATCH="$BASE_TREE/bin/fm-watch.sh"
DRAIN="$REPO/bin/fm-wake-drain.sh"

WINDOW="fleet:fm-api-shape"
KEY=$(printf '%s' "$WINDOW" | tr ':/.' '___')
PANE_LINE='claude - idle - waiting on the captain to answer'
WOKEN=0

hr() { printf '\n%s\n' "==============================================================================="; }
say() { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }

# A crew that has asked the captain a question and gone quiet: an open
# needs-decision as the last status line, an idle unchanged pane, and a backend
# that still reports its agent working (the provably-working verdict).
new_case() {  # <name>
  local dir state
  dir=$(make_case "$1"); state="$dir/state"
  printf '%s\n' "$PANE_LINE" > "$dir/pane.txt"
  printf 'window=%s\nkind=ship\n' "$WINDOW" > "$state/api.meta"
  printf 'needs-decision [key=api-shape]: ship the v2 endpoint as PATCH or POST?\n' > "$state/api.status"
  prime_status_seen "$state" "$state/api.status"
  printf '%s' "$(hash_text "$PANE_LINE")" > "$state/.hash-$KEY"
  printf '1\n' > "$state/.count-$KEY"
  printf '%s\n' "$dir"
}

# Drain and acknowledge, exactly as firstmate does when it is woken, so the next
# cycle starts from a clean queue and a consumed recovery generation.
settle() {  # <dir> <show-queue:0|1>
  local dir=$1 show=$2 state="$dir/state"
  FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$state" "$DRAIN" > "$dir/drain.out" 2>"$dir/drain.err" || true
  if [ "$show" = 1 ]; then
    grep -E "$(printf '\t')(stale|signal|heartbeat)$(printf '\t')" "$dir/drain.out" \
      | sed 's/^/      captain queue: /' || true
    sed -n 's/^\(api \[key=.*\)$/      captain queue: \1/p' "$dir/drain.out" || true
  fi
  ack_drain_err "$state" "$dir/drain.err" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

# One watcher wake cycle. Prints what the captain actually experiences: either
# the watcher surfaced a reason on stdout and exited (firstmate woken, one turn
# spent), or it stayed alive and absorbed the wake silently.
poll() {  # <dir> <watch-bin> <label> [VAR=VAL...]
  local dir=$1 watch=$2 label=$3; shift 3
  local state="$dir/state" out="$dir/watch.out" pid surfaced=0
  : > "$out"
  env PATH="$dir/fakebin:$PATH" FM_FAKE_TMUX_WINDOW="$WINDOW" \
    FM_FAKE_TMUX_CAPTURE="$dir/pane.txt" FM_FAKE_TMUX_CURRENT_COMMAND=zsh \
    FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$state" FM_CREW_STATE_BIN="$dir/fakebin/fm-crew-state.sh" \
    FM_POLL=1 FM_SIGNAL_GRACE=1 FM_CHECK_INTERVAL=999999 FM_HEARTBEAT=999999 \
    "$@" "$watch" > "$out" 2>"$dir/watch.err" &
  pid=$!
  wait_for_exit "$pid" 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '\n--- %s\n' "$label"
  if [ -s "$out" ]; then
    surfaced=1; WOKEN=$((WOKEN + 1))
    printf '    >>> FIRSTMATE WOKEN (watcher exited, one captain turn spent):\n'
    sed 's/^/          /' "$out"
  else
    printf '    absorbed - watcher still polling, firstmate never woken\n'
  fi
  tail -n 1 "$state/.watch-triage.log" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/.*\] /      triage log: /'
  printf '      state: '
  [ -e "$state/.decision-held-$KEY" ] && printf 'decision-held-marker=set '
  [ -e "$state/.decision-resurfaced-$KEY" ] && printf 'decision-resurfaced-throttle=set '
  if [ -e "$state/.stale-since-$KEY" ]; then
    printf 'WEDGE-TIMER-ARMED(idle %ss) ' "$(( $(date +%s) - $(cat "$state/.stale-since-$KEY") ))"
  else
    printf 'wedge-timer-disarmed '
  fi
  printf '\n'
  settle "$dir" "$surfaced"
}

# Move the wedge timer 500s into the past: the pane has now been idle far past
# FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=240, i.e. the live four-minute wedge cycle has come due.
age_wedge_timer() {  # <dir>
  echo $(( $(date +%s) - 500 )) > "$1/state/.stale-since-$KEY"
}

export FM_FAKE_CREW_STATE='state: working · source: pane · harness busy'

hr
say "SCENARIO"
say "  crew 'api' posts: needs-decision [key=api-shape]: ship the v2 endpoint as PATCH or POST?"
say "  ...then waits. Its pane is idle and unchanged; the backend still reports the agent working"
say "  (provably working). The captain has not answered yet."
say "  FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=240 - the live four-minute wedge cycle."

hr
say "PART 1 - BASE COMMIT ef35d79 (bug reproduction): a wedge escalation every 4 minutes"
WOKEN=0
base=$(new_case base-open-decision)
poll "$base" "$BASE_WATCH" "t+0     first sight of the idle pane" FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=240
for n in 1 2 3; do
  age_wedge_timer "$base"
  poll "$base" "$BASE_WATCH" "t+$((n * 4))min   captain still has not answered" FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=240
done
say ""
say "  >>> firstmate turns spent on this un-answered decision: $WOKEN"

hr
say "PART 2 - THIS BRANCH: same fixture, same 240s threshold, wedge timer planted as crossed"
WOKEN=0
fix=$(new_case fixed-open-decision)
poll "$fix" "$FIXED_WATCH" "t+0     first sight of the idle pane" FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=240 FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS=3600
for n in 1 2 3; do
  age_wedge_timer "$fix"   # plant a long-crossed wedge timer anyway
  poll "$fix" "$FIXED_WATCH" "t+$((n * 4))min   captain still has not answered" FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=240 FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS=3600
done
say ""
say "  >>> firstmate turns spent on this un-answered decision: $WOKEN"

hr
say "PART 3 - THIS BRANCH: the long re-surface cadence still rechecks the decision once a window"
say "  (age the status file past FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS - the bounded recheck, not a wedge)"
back=$(( $(date +%s) - 500 ))
if [ "$(uname)" = Darwin ]; then touch -mt "$(date -r "$back" '+%Y%m%d%H%M.%S')" "$fix/state/api.status"
else touch -m -d "@$back" "$fix/state/api.status"; fi
prime_status_seen "$fix/state" "$fix/state/api.status"
poll "$fix" "$FIXED_WATCH" "t+1h    one bounded recheck per window" FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=240 FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS=240

hr
say "PART 4 - THIS BRANCH: the captain answers, the crew stays mute - wedge cadence resumes"
ans=$(new_case answered-then-mute)
poll "$ans" "$FIXED_WATCH" "t+0     open decision, absorbed as in part 2" FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=240 FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS=3600
say ""
say "  captain answers: appending 'resolved [key=api-shape]: go with PATCH' to the status log"
printf 'resolved [key=api-shape]: go with PATCH\n' >> "$ans/state/api.status"
prime_status_seen "$ans/state" "$ans/state/api.status"
poll "$ans" "$FIXED_WATCH" "t+1s    decision closed - held tracking cleared, wedge timer re-armed" FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=240 FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS=3600
age_wedge_timer "$ans"
poll "$ans" "$FIXED_WATCH" "t+4min  the crew is STILL mute after the answer" FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=240 FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS=3600

hr
say "PART 5 - THIS BRANCH: a crew with no open decision wedges exactly like today"
old=$(new_case closed-decision)
printf 'needs-decision [key=api-shape]: ship the v2 endpoint as PATCH or POST?\nresolved [key=api-shape]: go with PATCH\n' \
  > "$old/state/api.status"
prime_status_seen "$old/state" "$old/state/api.status"
poll "$old" "$FIXED_WATCH" "t+0     first sight - normal absorb, wedge timer armed" FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=240 FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS=3600
age_wedge_timer "$old"
poll "$old" "$FIXED_WATCH" "t+4min  no open decision -> wedge escalation, unchanged" FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=240 FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS=3600

hr
say "DONE"

Fuite la plus atteignable, bin/fm-watch.sh:1291 : sur un changement de hash, `.decision-held-$key` n'est supprimé que dans le `else` (:1293). Si `busy_now -eq 0` et `busy_turn_over_age "$task"`, c'est `wedge_timer_check` qui s'exécute (:1291) et le marqueur SURVIT. Même trou en :1279/:1281 pour le poll pas-encore-stable.

Séquence concrète : (1) un crew provablement actif est parké sur `needs-decision [key=k]`, absorbé en decision-held au hash h1 (`.decision-held-` = mtime du statut, `.stale-`=h1) ; (2) le crew est parké depuis plus d'une heure, donc son `.turn-ended` dépasse `BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS` (3600 s) par construction - le capitaine répond dans le pane, le crew redémarre, le pane devient busy et son hash passe à h2 : branche :1291, marqueur conservé ; (3) l'agent meurt avant la fin du tour, le pane se fige à h2 ; (4) `n>=2`, `busy_now != 0`, `cat "$sf"` = h1 != h2 -> première vue -> `crew_is_provably_working` faux -> surface immédiate (correct) et écriture de `.stale-`=h2, sans toucher `.decision-held-` (:1186-1190, ou :1244 via `surface_nonterminal_stale`) ; (5) poll suivant : `sf` == h2 -> :1192 -> `handle_decision_held_stale` -> aucune ligne de statut n'a été appendue depuis (2), donc mtime stocké == mtime courant -> pas de re-fold -> `absorb_stale_on_long_cadence` -> `rm -f .stale-since- .wedge-escalations-` et un seul réveil par `PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS`. Un crew mort avec une décision jamais close (donc jamais refermée par le fold, donc `clear_decision_held_tracking` jamais atteint) est avalé une heure durant, en boucle. C'est exactement le trou que le round 1 exigeait de fermer.

Deuxième fuite, même cause : `clear_pause_tracking` (watcher :406-412) et son homologue du démon (bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:467-474) suppriment `.stale-$key` sans supprimer `.decision-held-$key`, ce qui rouvre une première vue au hash inchangé avec le marqueur intact.

Corollaire : le même enchaînement peut désarmer le wedge d'un crew SANS décision ouverte (première vue :1181-1183 -> timer armé, marqueur résiduel -> :1192 le désarme au poll suivant), ce qui contredit « Preserve exact current behavior for workers without an open decision (no wedge-detection regression) ».

Correction : faire que la présence du marqueur signifie exactement « la dernière première vue a absorbé ce hash en decision-held ». Sortir `"$STATE/.decision-held-$key"` du `else` en :1281 et :1293 pour le supprimer dans les deux branches, et l'ajouter aux chemins de première vue qui n'absorbent pas en decision-held (:1186-1190 surface terminale, :1181-1183 timer wedge terminal, :1235-1237 timer wedge non terminal, et `surface_nonterminal_stale`).
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:447` - Le jeton de fraîcheur qui borne le re-fold est une mtime en secondes entières (bin/fm-watch.sh:447 via `status_mtime_or_now`, comparée en :449). Le dépôt possède déjà un jeton conçu pour ce cas précis : `fm_wake_signal_sig` (bin/fm-wake-lib.sh:1028) renvoie « size:mtime », et le commentaire de `scan_signals` (bin/fm-watch.sh:549-552) explique que la signature taille+mtime existe justement parce que « same-second writes cannot slip through » une comparaison de mtime seule.

Conséquence si la collision se produit : une ligne `resolved`/`captain-held` qui atterrit après la lecture du fold mais dans la même seconde que la mtime enregistrée laisse `[ "$(cat "$held")" != "$mtime" ]` faux, le fold de revalidation ne tourne jamais, et le pane reste épinglé sur la cadence longue au lieu de reprendre la cadence wedge - ce que l'intent exige (« Resume the normal wedge cadence immediately when the decision closes »). La fenêtre est étroite (il faut que l'append de clôture, l'append précédent et le poll tombent dans la même seconde) et l'état se répare au premier changement de hash ou append suivant, d'où la sévérité info.

Correction : stocker `fm_wake_signal_sig "$STATE/$task.status"` comme payload du marqueur et comparer là-dessus, en continuant de passer la mtime seule comme ancre d'âge à `absorb_stale_on_long_cadence` (les deux sont déjà des paramètres distincts). Les fichiers de statut étant append-only, la taille change à chaque append, donc la détection devient exacte.
- ℹ️ `docs/configuration.md:583` - docs/configuration.md:583 énumère trois consommateurs de `FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS` (« an idle declared external wait, a dead-agent captain hold, or a provably-working crew parked on a still-open captain decision ») puis les rattache tous à « the watcher or away-mode daemon ». Le troisième cas n'existe que dans le watcher : bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh n'a aucune notion de decision-held (seuls `.subsuper-paused-`/`.paused-*` y sont gérés), et en mode AFK la branche `afk_present` du watcher (bin/fm-watch.sh:1146-1152) surface une fois par hash distinct et passe la main au démon sans jamais consulter `task_has_open_decision`. Un opérateur qui lit cette ligne peut croire que le mode away absorbe aussi les panes parkés sur une décision. Correction : restreindre le troisième item au watcher, par exemple « ... or, in the watcher only, a provably-working crew parked on a still-open captain decision ».

🔧 Fix: scope decision-held marker to its absorbed hash and signature
1 warning still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:1312` - Le `rm -f "$STATE/.decision-held-$key"` de la branche de reset (bin/fm-watch.sh:1312) s'exécute aussi quand le hash du pane n'a PAS changé, et il n'existe alors aucun chemin de retour vers la cadence longue : un seul poll busy suffit à replonger définitivement un crew parké sur une décision dans le cycle de 240 s que ce changement supprime.

Cette branche est le `else` de `[ "$n" -ge 2 ] && [ "$busy_now" -ne 0 ]`, DANS l'arm `if [ "$h" = "$prev" ]` (:1167). Elle couvre donc deux cas distincts : hash inchangé + pas encore stable (n<2), et hash inchangé + pane busy. Le commentaire qui justifie la suppression (:1304-1306, « The decision-held marker names a stale hash this pane is no longer sitting on, so it dies here whichever sub-branch runs ») n'est vrai que du reset hash-changé (:1325) ; ici le pane est toujours assis sur exactement le hash que le marqueur nomme.

Séquence d'échec concrète et atteignable :
1. Crew provablement actif (source `run-step`) parké sur `needs-decision [key=x]`, pane figé au hash h, absorbé en decision-held : `.decision-held-` = `h\t<sig>`, `.stale-` = h, `.stale-since-` supprimé (:359-361).
2. Parké depuis plus de `BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS` (3600 s par défaut), donc `busy_turn_over_age "$task"` est vrai par construction.
3. Un poll où le contrat busy sémantique renvoie `busy` alors que la capture du pane est identique à la précédente - exactement la forme que le helper de test ajouté par ce changement modélise (`record_pi_state`, tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh:127 : « the shape a real backend reports when an agent starts or dies behind an unchanged screen ») : `busy_now=0`, `h = prev` -> branche :1300 -> `.decision-held-` supprimé (:1312), puis `wedge_timer_check` arme `.stale-since-` (:1313-1314).
4. Poll suivant, le harness est de nouveau idle : `n >= 2`, `busy_now != 0` -> branche terminale (la dernière ligne est `needs-decision`) -> `cat "$sf"` == h, donc pas de première vue -> `decision_held_absorbed` faux (marqueur effacé) -> `elif [ -e "$ssf" ]` vrai -> `wedge_timer_check` (:1230).
5. 240 s plus tard : `stale: <win> (idle Ns, possible wedge, escalation 1)` + `wake`. `wedge_timer_check` supprime `$ssf` (:314), le poll suivant le réarme, et le cycle recommence toutes les 240 s, avec `demand-deep-inspection` à la 3e. Le pane étant figé, `.stale-` reste à h : la première vue ne se reproduit JAMAIS, donc `handle_decision_held_stale` n'est plus jamais atteint.

Cela contredit l'intent (« Prevent the watcher from wedge-escalating every FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS a worker whose task carries a still-open captain decision and whose pane is provably working ») : après le blip, ce worker-là ré-escalade bien toutes les 240 s.

Le chemin `paused` n'a pas ce trou parce qu'il se répare : son reset passe par `clear_pause_tracking` (:1318-1319) qui supprime AUSSI `.stale-$key`, donc le poll suivant repart en première vue et `handle_paused_stale` reprend la cadence longue. Le reset decision-held ne touche pas `.stale-`, d'où l'absence de récupération.

Correction : ne pas supprimer le marqueur en :1312. Le scoping par hash ajouté au round 3 (`decision_held_absorbed`, :479-483) rend cette suppression inutile - un marqueur ne peut de toute façon matcher qu'un pane resté sur son propre hash - et la conserver rend le blip inoffensif : au poll suivant `decision_held_absorbed` est vrai, `handle_decision_held_stale` reprend la cadence longue et `absorb_stale_on_long_cadence` désarme le `.stale-since-` que le blip avait armé (:361). Le reset hash-changé (:1325) reste correct et suffit. Variante équivalente si l'on tient à la suppression : ajouter `"$STATE/.stale-$key"` au même `rm -f` pour forcer une première vue, au prix d'une relecture d'état coûteuse par blip. La correction proposée laisse passer test_decision_held_marker_does_not_outlive_its_absorb (sa phase B change le hash, donc c'est :1325 qui s'applique). Aucun test co-localisé ne couvre le blip busy à hash inchangé.

🔧 Fix: keep decision-held marker across a same-hash busy blip
1 info still open:
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:1224` - La preuve « provably working » qui autorise l'absorb decision-held est prise une seule fois, en première vue (`bin/fm-watch.sh:1201` et `:1257`), et n'est jamais renouvelée tant que le pane reste sur le même hash. Les deux chemins de poll ultérieur (`:1224` et `:1281`) routent sur `decision_held_absorbed`, qui ne vérifie que la correspondance hash + marqueur, et `handle_decision_held_stale` ne relit jamais l'état du crew (contrat explicite d'`absorb_stale_on_long_cadence`, `:346-347`).

Conséquence concrète et atteignable : un crew absorbé en decision-held parce que `crew_absorb_class` renvoyait `working` (source `run-step` d'un pipeline no-mistakes en cours, ou `pane` via le contrat busy sémantique du backend) cesse d'être provablement actif - le run-step se termine ou meurt - sans que l'écran rendu change d'un octet. Comme `.stale-` vaut toujours ce hash, aucune première vue ne se reproduit, donc `crew_is_provably_working` n'est plus jamais évalué : le pane reste sur la cadence `PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS` (3600 s) au lieu de reprendre l'escalade wedge à `STALE_ESCALATE_SECS` (240 s) que l'ancien code appliquait via `elif [ -e "$ssf" ]`. L'intent borne pourtant l'absorb à un worker « whose pane is provably working ».

Pourquoi ce n'est pas bloquant : le pane continue de re-surfacer une fois par heure avec une raison exacte (« decision held Ns, awaiting captain - ... confirm the decision is still open »), donc rien n'est silencieusement avalé ; le chemin `paused` a exactement la même propriété via `handle_paused_stale` ; et cette absence de relecture d'état sur les polls ultérieurs est le design explicitement demandé au round 1 (« route to handle_decision_held_stale for a cheap re-validate ... instead of wedge_timer_check ») puis confirmé au round 4 en préférant la rétention du marqueur à la relecture coûteuse. La rétention n'élargit d'ailleurs pas le trou : même avant le round 4, un pane figé sans blip busy conservait son marqueur d'un poll à l'autre.

Aucune action demandée - c'est un compromis assumé, consigné ici pour qu'il reste visible si la cadence est réajustée plus tard. Si on voulait le fermer, le point d'accroche naturel serait un re-check `crew_is_provably_working` amorti dans `handle_decision_held_stale` (par exemple une fois par fenêtre de re-surface, pas à chaque poll), pas un chemin parallèle supplémentaire.

</details>

<details>
<summary>✅ **Test** - passed</summary>

✅ No issues found.
- <code>`bash tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` - 55 cas OK, dont `test_open_decision_stale_absorbed_on_long_cadence_not_wedged`, `test_open_decision_not_working_surfaces_immediately`, `test_decision_held_marker_does_not_outlive_its_absorb`, `test_decision_held_absorb_survives_a_busy_blip_at_the_same_hash`, `test_open_decision_closure_resumes_normal_cadence`, `test_closed_decision_stale_wedge_escalates_like_today`</code>
- <code>`bash tests/fm-classify-decision-key.test.sh` - fold status_open_decisions et cles de decision (lib modifiee par le change), 5 cas OK</code>
- <code>`bash tests/fm-daemon.test.sh` - 99 cas OK (bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh touche : clear_pause_tracking purge aussi .decision-held-*)</code>
- <code>Verification manuelle E2E : `git archive ef35d79 bin` extrait dans un tmp ephemere, puis `bash decision-held-e2e.sh <repo> <base-tree>` rejoue la meme fixture (needs-decision ouverte, pane idle inchange, crew provably working, FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=240) contre le bin/fm-watch.sh de base puis celui de la branche, avec drain+ack de la file de wakes entre chaque cycle comme le fait firstmate</code>

</details>

<details>
<summary>⚠️ **Document** - 1 info</summary>

- ℹ️ `AGENTS.md:398` - Judgment call: AGENTS.md's `stale:` handling entry (line 398) was deliberately left untouched. The new wake reason `stale: <win> (decision held <n>s, awaiting captain - ...)` is self-describing and instructs the reader inline ("confirm the decision is still open"), exactly like the pre-existing `paused ...s, awaiting external` re-surface reason which AGENTS.md also does not enumerate. Adding it would be conditional detail charged to every session, which the firstmate-coding-guidelines AGENTS.md size discipline routes away from the always-loaded contract. Recorded here only so the omission reads as deliberate rather than missed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>✅ **Lint** - passed</summary>

✅ No issues found.

</details>

<details>
<summary>✅ **Push** - passed</summary>

✅ No issues found.

</details>

title: docs(agents): compact section 4 dispatch procedure and one section 2 duplicate
body:
## What and why

`AGENTS.md` auto-loads into **every** firstmate and secondmate session (section 12: only `AGENTS.md`, `bin/`, `.agents/skills/` are loaded by a running firstmate), so its token cost is paid on every turn of every fleet member. This is a conservative `/pochisti` pass: it removes **only** content whose owning skill or a sibling section already states in full, and preserves every safety boundary.

This file is a safety contract, so the target was correctness, not a percentage. Realistic savings here are modest by design.

**Before → after:** 67064 → 66259 chars · 9110 → 9009 words · ~16766 → ~16565 est tokens (chars/4) · **−805 chars / −201 est tokens (−1.20%)**. No section heading renumbered (headings are cross-referenced by scripts/tests, e.g. `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh`, `tests/fm-task-delivery.test.sh`).

## Per-section classification (every section gets exactly one verdict)

| # | KB | heading | verdict | evidence / owner |
|---|----|---------|---------|------------------|
| 0 | 0.9 | # Firstmate | keep | address/identity behavioral rules used every turn |
| 1 | 3.5 | 1. Identity and prime directives | keep | hard rules 1–5, all safety |
| 2 | 12.7 | 2. Layout and state | **compact** | removed 1 summary line duplicating the state listing (owner: same section, lines 81–83) |
| 3 | 7.4 | 3. Session start | keep | actionable digest + recovery contract read every session |
| 4 | 4.0 | 4. Harness and runtime dispatch | **compact** | duplicated selection procedure — owners: `quota-array-dispatch` + `harness-adapters` (see below) |
| 5 | 1.3 | 5. Recovery | keep | recovery safety contract |
| 6 | 2.6 | 6. Project and knowledge management | keep | skill triggers + knowledge-routing rules |
| 7 | 14.1 | 7. Task lifecycle | keep | load-bearing delivery/merge/validate/teardown decision contract |
| 8 | 5.3 | 8. Supervision protocol | keep | supervision safety + away-mode stub (already a model inline-stub) |
| 9 | 4.0 | 9. Escalation and captain etiquette | keep | captain-facing translation table, used on every message |
| 10 | 1.8 | 10. Backlog contract | keep | queue safety + note-hygiene rules |
| 11 | 1.4 | 11. Crewmate briefs | keep | brief safety contract |
| 12 | 0.5 | 12. Self-update | keep | update surface + load-order fact |
| 13 | 3.3 | 13. Agent-only reference skills | keep | each row is a skill load trigger |
| 14 | 1.5 | 14. Relay | keep | public-reply consent boundary |
| 15 | 0.9 | Captain instruction precedence | keep | override safety, entire |
| 16 | 0.4 | Maintaining this file | keep | self-governance |

15 of 17 sections are `keep`. Only 2 were touched.

## What was cut, by class

**Class: duplicated (section 4).** `.agents/skills/quota-array-dispatch/SKILL.md:15` *explicitly declares the ownership split*: AGENTS.md section 4 owns the intake boundary, load trigger, malformed-config refusal, every-candidate accounting, and strongest-reasoning/tie safety rules — while the **skill** owns the completion-aware selection procedure and **`harness-adapters`** owns model/provider discovery and the effort fallback. Both owner skills load at the exact decision point (`harness-adapters` before every spawn per section 4; `quota-array-dispatch` before choosing among an array per the same section + section 13), so the restated procedure is a pure duplicate available whenever it applies. Collapsed to pointers:
- provider-relation establishment + quota-granularity rule (was "Establish model support and provider family…") → owned by `quota-array-dispatch` "Establish the provider relation" §, signposted in the retained load-trigger line.
- `quota-axi … remains data-only` → owned by `quota-array-dispatch:17`, signposted in the same line.
- the `191` selection-procedure tail ("choose with inspectable effective headroom and usable runway…") → owned by the skill's Selection order.
- effort fallback enumeration ("low for well-understood…, xhigh for ambiguous…, intermediate levels proportionally…") → owned **verbatim** by `harness-adapters:116-121`.

**Class: duplicated (section 2).** Removed one summary sentence restating the `captain.md` / `captain-shared.md` / `learnings.md` roles (incl. the harness-memory-canonical fact) already spelled out in the state-directory listing directly above it (lines 81–83; `learnings.md` line 83 states "the same contract as captain.md").

No `false-now` and no `historical` content was found; this file is current contract.

## What I deliberately KEPT despite length or apparent duplication

- **Every `never do X` / eligibility line in section 4**, incl. "disclosed uncertainty keeps a candidate eligible, never a credential or login escalation" and "never launch another harness's CLI to judge a candidate." These carry safety flavor and were treated as ambiguous → kept.
- **The never-max guard** ("never select max from that fallback without explicit captain preference") — `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1408` cross-references "AGENTS.md section 4 forbids selecting max without captain preference," so it must stay in section 4. Kept.
- **The verified-harness list and unverified-adapter fallback** (section 4) — `bin/fm-control-lib.sh:62` cross-references "section 4's verified-adapter list." Kept.
- **The full section 2 state listing incl. every `never touch` marker** — it is the agent's navigation map for `state/`; the "never touch" annotations are load-bearing safety. Kept whole (only the one duplicated *summary* line was removed).
- **Section 3's 7-step digest enumeration** — although `bin/fm-session-start.sh`'s header owns the mechanics, the steps are actionable behavioral contract the agent interprets every session (lock-refused mode, OPEN DECISIONS / UNREAD STATUS semantics). Kept.
- **`line 132`** (wake-event-vs-current-state + `fm-crew-state.sh` owner) — a permitted one-line reinforcement at a genuine risk point; kept while removing the adjacent duplicated summary.

## Verification

- Grepped the repo for every removed rule's wording: each surviving copy lives only in its owner (`harness-adapters:119-120`, `quota-array-dispatch:17,47-48`, state listing line 81); no orphaned AGENTS.md fragment remains, and the never-max cross-ref (`fm-spawn.sh:1408`) still resolves.
- All 17 section headings intact; no renumbering.
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` → **ok** (68 surfaces, 253 local links).
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` → clean (no script changed).
- `.no-mistakes.yaml` defines no local `commands.test` (it explicitly reserves the full behavior suite for CI); this change is prose-only and touches no script, so no script behavior can change.

## Guard note

`AGENTS.md` size discipline already has an owner: `.agents/skills/firstmate-coding-guidelines/SKILL.md` ("Size discipline" + the knowledge-placement decision tree). No new guard file added — the existing skill is the standing check against regrowth, and this PR does not change it.

Preserve the implementation intent: fix updatefirstmate fork-sync HTTP 404 by retaining GraphQL-primary fork discovery and strict configured-upstream identity checks; use authenticated REST parent metadata only when GraphQL reports a fork with an empty parent; replace the encoded-ref-sensitive sync path with GitHub’s guarded merge-upstream endpoint; validate the documented owner-only base_branch response against the API-confirmed full parent owner/default branch; fail closed on missing, disagreeing, or malformed topology, wrong owner or branch, API failure, conflict, non-fork state, or changed OIDs; preserve guarded local fast-forward behavior and forbid direct ref mutation, force, or updater bypass. Retain deterministic regression coverage for fallback success, genuine missing parent, REST disagreement/refusal, no fallback when GraphQL parent exists, merge-upstream success/current/failure/malformed/wrong-owner/wrong-branch/conflict, syntax, lint, and snapshot/update tests. Before and during validation, preserve the exact-head identity contract: local branch, remote branch, GitHub PR head, and worktree must remain clean and equal to c1f608b58ec03a50f6792160ab93b9755337826f; base must remain 3f1920aaced2f04e20dbc65f9c97923637c3b5d9; GitHub must remain conflict-free; and /home/pranay/.treehouse/firstmate-7e2c14/12/firstmate/data/fm-update-fork-sync-ref-path-review-2026-08-16/report.md must apply to that exact head. title: docs(agents): collapse §2/§3 restated mechanics to their SSOT owners
body:
## What

SSOT pointer-collapse of the restated mechanics in **AGENTS.md §2 (Layout and state)** and **§3 (Session start)** only. Every other section is byte-for-byte unchanged (`git diff` touches lines 67-78, 84-85, 107, 116 in §2 and 155-173 in §3).

## Before → after

| Section | Before | After | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| §2 Layout and state | 13,049 B (~3,260 tok) | 11,815 B (~2,950 tok) | −1,234 B (~−9.5%) |
| §3 Session start | 7,627 B (~1,910 tok) | 4,279 B (~1,070 tok) | −3,348 B (~−44%) |
| whole file | 568 lines | 556 lines | −12 lines |

## The lever

§2's own intro already names the owner ("`docs/configuration.md` is the single owner … each producing script's header and help own exact child fields and mutation mechanics") and §3's intro already names "`bin/fm-session-start.sh` … the single owner of composed commands, ordering, and digest contents." The per-entry field-lists and the 7-step digest enumeration were duplicating those owners. This collapses that duplication to a pointer while keeping the map usable and every safety note.

## Pointers introduced (each verified to contain the moved content)

§2 config/data/state entries — each keeps its one-line purpose + every safety flag; mechanics point to:

- `config/crew-harness`, `config/secondmate-harness` → `docs/configuration.md` "Harness support" (owns default-mirroring, the secondmate-crewmate inheritance, the fallback chain, and "not inherited because secondmates do not launch secondmates").
- `config/crew-dispatch.json` → `docs/configuration.md` "Crew dispatch profiles".
- `config/backlog-backend` → `docs/configuration.md` "Backlog backend".
- `config/backend` → `docs/configuration.md` "Runtime backend" (owns selection order and accepted/rejected values incl. codex-app rejection).
- `config/calm`, `config/startup-memory-budget`, `config/trace-context` → `docs/configuration.md` "Pi Calm preference" / "Startup memory budget" / "Trace context propagation".
- `config/herdr-presentation-spaces` → `docs/herdr-backend.md` "Presentation spaces"; `config/cmux-socket-password` → `docs/cmux-backend.md` "Setup"; `config/wedge-alarm` → `docs/wedge-alarm.md`.
- `data/projects.md`, `data/secondmates.md` → section 6 (dropped "parsed/maintained by <script>" provenance).
- `state/pending-replies/` → `fm-pending-reply-lib.sh` + `docs/configuration.md` (dropped the field list); `state/.startup-network.*` → `fm-startup-network.sh` (dropped the field list).

§3 — the 7-step digest enumeration → `bin/fm-session-start.sh`'s header, which owns the exact ordering and each section's contents (its header even states it "Collapses AGENTS.md sections 3 and 5 into ONE script"). The step narration duplicated the wake-queue handling contract, which **section 8** owns (drain, OPEN DECISIONS, UNREAD STATUS, `--ack-through` durability).

## Invariants preserved (not dropped)

- Lock acquired first; mutating sweeps and network checks run only when locked; a lock-refused session stays read-only (also §3 line 149) and runs no network checks.
- The digest presents the durable wake queue once; section 8 owns handling and acknowledgement.
- Exactly one supervision block is emitted; the script never starts supervision itself.
- Endpoint liveness is a presence check only — use `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` for real state.
- `ABSENT` marker semantics kept above (§3 line 146).

## Safety confirmation

Safety-token counts across the changed §2/§3 region are unchanged: `LOCAL, gitignored` 17→17, `never touch` 5→5, `NOT inherited`/`not inherited` preserved, `firstmate-private` 2→2, and the `bin/fm-send.sh` **fails closed** note is intact. The only two removed safety-token occurrences are guard-output UX ("read-only advisory" wording) and sweep mechanics ("skipped or failed guarantees" for `SECONDMATE_LIVENESS`), both owned by `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` and routed via `bootstrap-diagnostics`; the lock-refused read-only invariant they described is fully retained at §3 line 149. Every "never touch" / security / trust / quarantine / provenance line in the `state/` tree (check.sh, procevent, pr-poll-*, autoarm/cursor internals) is verbatim.

## Verification

- `git diff` confined to §2/§3; all other sections identical.
- Every retired phrase grep-confirmed present in its named owner.
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` → ok (68 surfaces, 253 local links).
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` → clean (no changed lint targets).
- No test asserts the changed prose (tests use those config files as runtime inputs only, never as AGENTS.md text).

title: feat: add approved ship workflow and active-work dashboard
body:
## Intent

Implement the approved FirstMate two-phase ship-end-to-end workflow and private canonical dashboard record for the private FirstMate fork and local installation only. Require a typed durable task-scoped preflight record before material ship execution; direct preflight is read-only until explicit captain approval; preserve delivery, yolo, merge, production, and same-task recovery authority. The trusted Agent bridge submits already-authorized typed records; FirstMate accepts no caller-provided Slack authorization evidence, origin, contract, approval, or authority claims. Maintain dashboard.json schema v1 as a private atomic 0600 canonical dashboard, with active work only, genuine Needs you events, Building or Checking, and exact pause-excluding cumulative active time from producer transition timestamps. Endpoint loss must stop active timing, recover silently when supported, and become Needs you only after confirmed unrecoverable failure. Fast Repair is excluded from the final scope: remove all Fast Repair files and connected mode, watcher, spawn, teardown, documentation, and test surface, retaining only generic pre-existing shared helpers needed by the normal workflow. Do not merge, deploy, self-update, write production data, or target upstream/original FirstMate.

## What Changed

- Add a durable, fingerprint-bound preflight record that requires approval before ship dispatch, promotion, or recovery; trusted Agent bridge records use a private handoff.
- Add the private schema-v1 active-work dashboard with atomic publication, transition-based active-time tracking, endpoint recovery, and watcher/status integration.
- Retain validated Relay source-thread URLs on task links and update the ship workflow skills, documentation, and test coverage.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The change affects several lifecycle owners, but the inspected approval, timing, recovery, and private-record paths fail closed; no material source defect was found.
