title: fix(bin): refuse spawn worktrees outside the project's own repository
body:
## Intent Close a safety hole in validate_spawn_worktree() in bin/fm-spawn.sh: the worker-isolation assertion accepts a worktree belonging to the wrong repository, including firstmate's own home. The defect: validate_spawn_worktree() asserts that the worktree path resolves, is a real git top-level, that the resolved path equals that top-level, and that it is not the project's own primary checkout. It never asserts that the worktree belongs to the project's repository. Found live dispatching a scout task: a spawn whose terminal never left the firstmate home recorded worktree=/Users/young/work/firstmate and passed, because the firstmate home is a valid git top-level distinct from the project clone. The worker would have been launched against firstmate's own primary checkout, which AGENTS.md sections 7 and 8 exist to prevent. The two-consecutive-reads guard does not cover this: it defends against a transient stale path, and a pane that never moved trivially agrees with itself. Call sites to keep correct: the Orca path, the relaunch path, and the treehouse get path. Required outcomes: 1. Reproduce the incorrect-repository acceptance before fixing, demonstrating that the old assertion accepts a worktree from a different repository than the project, including the firstmate-home case, with the evidence in the PR. 2. Verify repository identity positively: resolve the worktree's git common dir (or its .git file pointer) and require it to land inside the project's repository. A worktree of any other repository, most dangerously firstmate's own, must be refused. Identity must be proven, never inferred from path shape or string prefix. 3. Fail closed when identity cannot be established: unreadable pointer, unresolvable path, command failure, or unexpected output must refuse the launch with a clear diagnostic naming what could not be established. An inconclusive check is never a pass. Keep the existing refusal style: loud, specific, non-zero. 4. Regression tests covering the firstmate-home misrouting case, wrong-repo-in-general, and the identity-unknown path, plus assertions that legitimate worktrees still pass so the fix cannot pass by refusing everything. Colocate under tests/ as .test.sh, extend the existing pattern rather than inventing a runner, and exercise behavior through an executable or public interface, never asserting implementation source bytes directly or through a wrapper. 5. Backend compatibility review across each supported backend's path into the assertion (treehouse-provided for tmux, herdr, zellij, cmux; Orca owns its own worktree and does not run treehouse get), confirming the new check is correct for each or stating why an axis is not applicable after inspecting its integration surface. 6. Full validation: bin/fm-lint.sh (shellcheck is mandatory for bin/*.sh) and the relevant existing test suites, reporting what was run and its result. This change touches firstmate's shared tracked material, so the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill's knowledge-placement, one-owner, compatibility, and repo-style rules are binding. Later accepted corrections, decided by the captain, to be carried in this run: - Add a distinct FM_HOME_RETURN_NOT_OWNED outcome so that only proven foreign ownership releases the pooled treehouse lease. Every other refusal cause, including mktemp, manifest, and first-move failures that leave this run's own marker on the slot, must preserve the lease rather than releasing it and poisoning the pool slot. - Retain repository-root-only project registration, and correct only its misleading diagnostic, which currently describes a project directory that is a genuine subdirectory of its own repository as "nested inside another git repository". - Fold in the helper-shadowing auto-fix. - Keep the no-op finding as a no-op. Preserve all existing safety contracts. Do not merge; the captain approves the merge personally. Further accepted requirements after the first PR went red in upstream CI (PR https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/2562, head 7dcdb4e6, 12 of 13 checks passed): - FIX IN THIS TASK - a regression this branch introduced. The check "Behavior portable serial 1" failed because tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh reports "not ok - teardown exited non-zero with a valid tasktmp". Root cause established: bin/fm-teardown.sh line 192 now unconditionally sources bin/fm-home-return-lib.sh, but the fake root built by tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh symlinks each library teardown sources and was never given the new one, so the real teardown subprocess fails at source time and exits non-zero. Evidence that this is ours: upstream CI on the exact base commit 64d61ae is green, the test file is byte-identical between base and this branch, and running the test from a clean export reproduces "teardown exited non-zero with a valid tasktmp" on this branch while base fails only a different, macOS-local assertion. Fix it so the fixture provides every library the real teardown requires, following the pattern and commentary already used for the other symlinked siblings in that fixture, and check whether any other test fixture enumerating teardown's sourced libraries needs the same addition. - DO NOT FIX HERE, keep this PR scoped - tests/fm-pi-watch-extension.test.sh reported "not ok - Pi must deliver the actionable wake after bounded hung-successor recovery: expected exit 0, got 1" in the same CI shard. This branch touches no Pi, watcher, or wake code (the changed files are bin/fm-ff-lib.sh, bin/fm-home-return-lib.sh, bin/fm-home-seed.sh, bin/fm-spawn.sh, bin/fm-teardown.sh, bin/fm-test-isolation-proof.sh, bin/fm-test-run.sh, two docs, one skill pointer, and the two new identity test files), and the test passes from a clean export of this branch, so it is not attributable to this change and is being recorded as a separate follow-up item. Do not expand this task to chase it. Validate the final head exactly once, push normally to the existing fork branch, and do not merge; the captain approves the merge personally. ## What Changed - `validate_spawn_worktree()` in `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now proves repository identity instead of only checking worktree shape: it compares the physically resolved `--git-common-dir` of the task worktree against the project's, requires the project directory to be its own repository's top level (so the identity is not walked up to from a subdirectory), and separately refuses any worker root that is a firstmate home (active home, firstmate repo root, a directory carrying the seeded-home marker, or the holder of this fleet's `state`/`data`/`config`/`projects` directories). Every unresolvable path, git failure, or unexpected output fails closed with a diagnostic naming what could not be established; secondmate spawns still skip the assertion. - New `bin/fm-home-return-lib.sh` owns the shared "clear a leased home's identity, then return it to the treehouse pool" transaction used by both retirement (`bin/fm-teardown.sh`) and failed-seed rollback (`bin/fm-home-seed.sh`), staging owned artifacts aside and restoring them if the return fails. Its outcome codes distinguish `FM_HOME_RETURN_NOT_OWNED` — proven foreign ownership, the only refusal on which a pooled lease may be released — from refusals that leave this run's own marker on the slot. `bin/fm-spawn.sh` also drops its duplicated operational-directory validator in favor of `validate_operational_dirs` from `bin/fm-ff-lib.sh`. - Added `tests/fm-spawn-worktree-identity.test.sh` and `tests/fm-teardown-home-identity.test.sh` (wrong-repo, firstmate-home misrouting, identity-unknown, and legitimate-worktree cases), registered both in `bin/fm-test-run.sh` families and `bin/fm-test-isolation-proof.sh`, taught `families_for_changed_path()` that teardown/home-return changes re-select `session-bootstrap`, and gave the `tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh` fake root the `fm-home-return-lib.sh` symlink the real teardown subprocess now requires at source time. Docs in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md`, and the project-management skill were updated for the repository-identity requirement and repository-root-only project registration. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: All four prior findings are verifiably closed and the fix round is small and correct, but the branch as a whole is large (~2570 lines) and installs a new launch-blocking spawn gate plus a repository-root-only project-registration refusal — both explicitly captain-authorized and covered by 18 behavior-driven regression cases, so it is safe to merge with only the test-fixture deduplication as a follow-up. ## Testing I reproduced the reported defect end-to-end before validating the fix: running the new identity suite against a clean export of the head with only bin/fm-spawn.sh reverted to base shows the old assertion accepting firstmate's own home and printing `spawned ... worktree=<firstmate home>`. On the fixed head the same scenario is refused with a specific non-zero diagnostic naming the repository mismatch, and I captured the actual operator-facing CLI refusal text for all cases — foreign repository, unreadable/empty/garbage worktree identity, unresolvable project identity, self-hosted firstmate-home signals, and the corrected non-top-level project-registration wording that no longer accuses a foreign repository — alongside the two accept cases that still spawn, so the fix cannot pass by refusing everything. The Orca and relaunch call sites are driven by their own cases; the tmux/herdr/zellij/cmux backends share the single treehouse-get path that the suite drives with a fake tmux. I also reproduced the CI regression (teardown exiting non-zero because the fake root lacked fm-home-return-lib.sh) and confirmed the fixture fix clears it, and swept the tests tree to confirm no other fixture enumerates teardown's sourced libraries. Related existing spawn, relaunch, teardown, and tangle-guard suites pass; two suites fail one assertion each, but identically on the base commit, so they are pre-existing macOS-local failures rather than regressions. This is a shell/CLI change with no rendered UI surface, so the reviewer-visible evidence is CLI transcripts rather than screenshots. Lint was not run — it belongs to a different phase.

title: fix(herdr): stop events-capability probe spamming broken-pipe under ignored SIGPIPE
body:
## Problem

On herdr homes with parked panes, the watcher's push-capability probe
(`fm_backend_herdr_events_capable` in `bin/backends/herdr.sh`) spammed
`printf: write error: Broken pipe` to the watcher's stderr, alongside repeated
watcher restarts.

## Root cause (reproduced end-to-end)

The probe matched the ~220KB `herdr api schema` output with
`printf '%s' "$schema" | grep -Fq TOKEN`. `grep -Fq` exits on the first match
while the Bash `printf` builtin is still writing the rest of the schema down the
pipe. When the watcher inherits an **ignored SIGPIPE** from its launcher, that
write returns `EPIPE` instead of dying silently, so `printf` reports
`write error: Broken pipe` on every probe.

Reproduced in a throwaway home (8 parked herdr panes, ignored SIGPIPE): exactly
two broken-pipe lines at the two `grep -Fq` calls, while the watcher cycle
itself stayed healthy - confirming the message was noise co-occurring with the
restarts, not the killer.

## Fix

Match the schema with pure-Bash glob `case` (no subprocess, no pipe), which
cannot break a pipe and is immune to the caller's SIGPIPE disposition. The
capability verdict is unchanged and was reverified against real herdr 0.7.5 via
`tests/fm-backend-herdr-eventwait-smoke.test.sh`.

The watcher read path was separately verified end-to-end to already survive
transient/malformed/failed herdr reads (reader dying mid-stream, failing pane
reads) without killing the cycle, so no behavioral change was made there. The
`cycle ended without an actionable reason` string is intentionally untouched: it
is a typed sentinel the Stop-hook re-arm/guard contract parses, and it is not
driven by the herdr read path.

## Tests

New colocated regression case in `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh` that fixes the
triggering environment (ignored SIGPIPE, large fake api schema, early tokens),
proves via a control that the environment really can break a pipe, then asserts
the probe stays quiet while returning the correct capable/incapable verdict.
Confirmed the test fails against the pre-fix `grep` pattern and passes against
the fix. Full herdr suite green.

Validated through the no-mistakes pipeline (review, test, document, lint all
green; findings info/no-op only). The `document` step added the one-line
invariant note in `docs/herdr-backend.md`.

title: A DECLINED captain decision cannot be resolved, so scout teardown blocks forever
body:
## Summary

A captain decision that is **declined** cannot be durably resolved, so the scout completion gate blocks teardown permanently.

`resolve` requires `--routed-to <task-id>` and mandates that every routed task exists **and is blocked by the hold**. That is the right contract for a decision that produces work. It is structurally impossible for a decision whose answer is *"no, do not do this"* — there is no dependent task, and inventing one to satisfy the flag would be manufacturing state.

The only remaining way to close such a hold is the ordinary backlog path (`tasks-axi done`). But `complete` and `verify` do not accept that as resolution, so scout teardown refuses forever.

## Observed

Real case, 2026-08-18, on `activity-above-line-status-audit`:

1. A crewmate registered `activity-above-line-status-audit-decision-mention-dead-letter-replay-r3` — legitimately, because the plan document it was reading still marks R3 as an open captain decision.
2. The captain had already **declined** R3 five days earlier and explicitly said not to raise it again. Firstmate closed the hold as already-decided using `tasks-axi done`.
3. Teardown then refused: `REFUSED: scout task ... has not passed the unresolved-decision completion gate.`
4. `complete <task> --none` → `is neither actively held nor durably resolved`
5. `complete <task> <key>` → same
6. `hold <task> <key>` (attempting to re-create so the gate could see it) → **`is already durably resolved; use a new decision key for a new decision`**

Steps 4/5 and step 6 **contradict each other** on the same identity in the same second: one path reports it unresolved, the other reports it already resolved. Whatever state it is in, no command accepts it.

The record is still present in `data/backlog.md` (state Done); it had not yet been moved by retention, so this is **not** #2513, though the symptom rhymes. #2513 is about the record being archived out of view. This is about a record that is visible and Done being unacceptable to the gate.

## Why it matters

The gate exists so a scout cannot be torn down before its captain decisions are recorded — that is a good rule and worth keeping. But a *declined* decision is the most common kind that produces no routed work, and it is exactly the kind this contract cannot express. The result is that doing the right thing (respecting a standing captain ruling and closing the duplicate rather than re-asking) leaves a worktree permanently un-teardownable.

## Suggested direction, not a prescription

Allow a decision to be resolved with **no** routed work when the answer is a decline — e.g. `resolve ... --decision-file <path> --declined` with no `--routed-to`, writing the decision text into the hold body and marking it durably resolved. That preserves the property the gate protects (the answer is durably recorded) without requiring dependent work that by definition does not exist.

Whatever the fix, the contradiction between `hold` and `complete` on the same identity should be resolved too — a single source of truth for "is this hold settled".

title: fix(bin): report remote secondmate delivery and state truthfully
body:
## Intent Fix the remote-secondmate FALSE-NEGATIVE in bin/fm-send.sh, and the parallel fm-crew-state.sh / fm-peek.sh remote misreports, so remote delivery and remote state report the truth instead of a scary false failure. Captain-authorized ship via no-mistakes on firstmate's shared tracked bin/ machinery. Observed bug (captain-captured live reproduction against the real remote secondmate axi-a1): steering a remote mate printed 'error: text not submitted ... (verdict=pending; ... endpoint=verified)' from the remote leg and 'error: text not sent to remote: (remote send failed; ...)' locally, while the message actually landed and was acted on. Root cause: the remote send crosses fm-on.sh to a host-local fm-send leg (fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh cmd_send) whose unconfirmed submit read-back (verdict=pending - typically a busy claude mate whose harness queues the steer; herdr deliberately refuses to borrow an already-busy pane's turn as submit proof) was flattened into exit 1 and then into a local hard failure that also discarded the pending-reply expectation. The same blind spot made fm-crew-state report a healthy remote mate as 'worktree gone' (its recorded worktree is a remote-host path checked locally) and fm-peek fail with "can't find session: remote" (remote meta defaulted to the tmux backend with target remote:). Required behavior (user's acceptance criteria): (1) The remote path's real confirmation IS the same verified submit run host-locally on the remote machine; the one unconfirmable case (busy mate, queued steer) is only observable through harness-rendered queue text, which repo guidelines forbid relying on without live-harness proof, so the honest fallback applies: a clearly-worded delivered-with-confirmation-pending NON-failure, never an 'error: not sent' when the endpoint was verified. (2) Exit status AND message must reflect delivered-or-pending, killing the resend/duplicate reflex. (3) Delivery semantics unchanged and NO fail-open: a genuinely non-delivered send (endpoint not resolved/verified, real remote failure, ssh exit 255 transport-unknown) still fails loudly with a real error and the remote leg's stderr attached. (4) fm-crew-state/fm-peek read the true remote source over fm-on.sh; an unreachable or unreadable remote reads as unknown-remote, explicitly not proof of death; only the remote host's own dead/missing verdict may say the endpoint is gone. (5) Regression tests exercise the real executables over a stubbed ssh transport (the FM_SSH_BIN process seam, which tests/fm-on.test.sh already proves preserves exit status) - never source-byte assertions, never a live mac-home dependency: delivered-not-failure, genuine-failure-still-fails, ssh-255 preserves the expectation as delivery_unknown, remote state readers not falsely dead, plus a poisoned local tmux proving local adapters are never consulted for a remote target. Deliberate design decisions (do not flag as mistakes): (a) fm-send gains a documented exit-status contract: 0 confirmed, 3 delivered-unconfirmed (text typed into the live verified endpoint, Enter sent, read-back unconfirmed), other nonzero real failure; cmd_send deliberately performs no rc mapping so exit 3 crosses the ssh boundary intact. (b) On the parent side, remote rc 3 is treated as delivered: non-error notice, exit 0, pending-reply expectation marked delivered (awaiting_report - NOT delivery_unknown, because delivery_unknown escalates a blocked captain decision quickly and this pattern is frequent and empirically benign; the awaiting-report lifecycle's single recovery ask plus one escalation backstops the rare genuinely lost steer), and --resolve-key decisions close (leaving them open would re-surface the decision and drive the exact duplicate-answer resend this fix kills; every remote text send is marked and carries the expectation backstop). This is a deliberate, documented narrowing of the 'unconfirmed never closes a key' rule for the remote delivered-pending case only. (c) A LOCAL unconfirmed submit now exits 3 with an honest non-error message but keeps its prior bookkeeping (undelivered expectation discarded, resolve keys never closed) because a local operator can cheaply verify with fm-peek; only the exit code and wording changed locally. (d) The herdr backend's verdict semantics are deliberately untouched. (e) The stale workaround note in .agents/skills/stuck-crewmate-recovery (which documented these very false negatives as 'unreliable') is updated to the new contract. (f) The data/learnings.md 'Remote secondmates' note update is deliberately EXCLUDED from this PR as a separate post-merge follow-up. (g) No herdr session or lifecycle management anywhere; all tests are hermetic. PR note required: this changes shared tracked bin/ transport machinery every home relies on; running homes pick it up only after merge plus a firstmate self-update, and landing timing is coordinated with the main firstmate. ## What Changed - Treat remote exit 3 as delivered with confirmation pending while preserving pending-reply and decision bookkeeping; genuine failures and SSH 255 still fail loudly. - Route remote `fm-crew-state` and `fm-peek` reads through `fm-on.sh`, reporting unreadable remotes as unknown rather than dead. - Add hermetic SSH-stubbed regressions and update operator docs. This shared `bin/` machinery reaches running homes only after merge and a coordinated firstmate self-update. ## Risk Assessment 🚨 High: The remote delivery changes are well bounded, but the state fix can still produce a false current-state report through a documented stale-log sequence, contradicting a required acceptance criterion. ## Testing With no pre-supplied baseline command, targeted executable tests and a reviewer-visible CLI transcript confirmed delivered-pending sends succeed without false errors, real and transport-unknown failures remain loud with correct expectation state, and remote state/peek reads avoid local adapters.
Evidence: Remote secondmate end-to-end CLI transcript Source: [Remote secondmate end-to-end CLI transcript](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/blob/c7f0a5bbc2103d73ae55254690207af6ea4de5c9/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-remote-send-confirmation-fix-r1/remote-secondmate-e2e-transcript.txt) ```text Remote secondmate end-user behavior (real executables, stubbed FM_SSH_BIN) $ fm-send.sh rsm "please rename the metric" # remote leg returns delivered-unconfirmed (3) fm-send: delivered to remote secondmate rsm; the remote pane accepted the text and Enter, and only the synchronous submit confirmation is still pending. This is not a failure - do not resend; the pending-reply expectation stays armed. exit=0 pending-reply phase=awaiting_report delivered_epoch_set=yes $ fm-send.sh rsm "please rename the metric" # genuine remote failure error: remote endpoint metadata invalid error: text not sent to remote:rsm (remote send failed; tried meta=/var/folders/0k/bf8mwt2n5qddzk24r20gfk0c0000gn/T//fm-remote-evidence.8zRjuw/home/state/rsm.meta; placement=remote) exit=1 $ fm-send.sh rsm "please rename the metric" # SSH transport exit 255 error: text delivery to remote secondmate rsm is unknown; do not resend - same-host reconciliation is required exit=1 pending-reply phase=delivery_unknown $ fm-crew-state.sh rsm # remote endpoint says alive; worktree does not exist locally state: unknown · source: remote-endpoint · alive on remote-mac (an idle secondmate is healthy) $ fm-crew-state.sh rsm # remote transport unreachable state: unknown · source: remote-endpoint · unknown-remote: remote-mac unreachable or endpoint unreadable (not proof of death) $ fm-peek.sh rsm 20 ● remote mate is applying the requested refactor local-adapter-check=PASS (poisoned local tmux was never consulted) ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 error - 🚨 `bin/fm-crew-state.sh:173` - Criterion (4) requires fm-crew-state to “read the true remote source over fm-on.sh,” but after fm-on only returns `alive`, this hunk emits the canonical state from the local append-only status log. title: fm-brief's Herdr safety gate quotes {TASK}, so filling the brief with a global replace corrupts the gate
body:
## The trap

`bin/fm-brief.sh` tells firstmate to "replace every `{TASK}` placeholder". The scaffold's own
Herdr safety gate then quotes that placeholder in prose:

```
**HARD SAFETY GATE:** this scaffold cannot inspect the task text that replaces `{TASK}` later.
```

So a global replace - the literal instruction - substitutes the entire task body into the middle
of the safety gate's sentence. The result reads as a second, garbled copy of the task and the
safety gate's meaning is destroyed.

Hit on 2026-08-18 filling a ship brief. Caught only because the task body appeared twice in a
heading scan; nothing in the tooling flags it.

## Why it matters

The corrupted text IS a safety contract. AGENTS.md section 11 calls the scaffold "a safety
contract, not a suggestion", and this one specifically exists because the scaffold cannot see the
task text. A silent corruption of that sentence is the one failure the gate was written to
prevent.

It also scales badly: the longer the task body, the less obvious the corruption, because the
duplicate is buried far from the heading.

## Suggested fix

Pick either, but pick one:

1. Make the placeholder unique. Use a distinct token for the fillable slot, for example
   `{TASK_BODY}`, and leave the prose reference as `{TASK}`. A global replace then cannot reach
   the safety gate.
2. Do not quote the placeholder in prose. Reword the gate to "the task text filled in above",
   so there is nothing for a replace to hit.

Option 1 is preferable: it keeps the gate's wording precise about what it cannot inspect.

A third, weaker option is a validation pass in `fm-brief.sh` that refuses a brief whose task body
appears more than once. That catches the symptom rather than removing the trap, and it cannot
distinguish a legitimate repetition.

title: feat(skills): adopt Flux GitOps and safe BWS workflows
body:
## Intent Adopt the approved official Flux CD skills and add a narrow Firstmate amendment for classic Flux. Requirements: - Adopt only official fluxcd/agent-skills gitops-knowledge and gitops-repo-audit at a pinned, verified revision. - Do not install or expose gitops-cluster-debug. - Verify source identity, license, selected bytes, and revision before adoption. - Do not copy third-party content into a conflicting owner. Preserve attribution and license requirements. - Add a narrow Firstmate-owned amendment that states when classic Flux architecture overrides the official skill's Flux Operator preference. - Keep project-specific versions, paths, namespaces, repository URLs, and stages out of the global amendment. - Cover manual tracked-manifest installation, digest-pinned images, read-only Git credentials, suspend and resume, and Git-revert rollback. - Add precise load triggers without duplicating full procedures in AGENTS.md. - Add deterministic verification for the pinned third-party revision and selected skills. - Add tests without network dependence in routine CI. ## What Changed - Vendor the official Flux CD `gitops-knowledge` and `gitops-repo-audit` skills at a verified pinned revision while explicitly excluding `gitops-cluster-debug`. - Add classic Flux guidance plus network-free provenance, license, checksum, contents, and symlink verification integrated with the test runner. - Add a public Bitwarden Secrets Manager skill with safe authentication probing, metadata redaction, deterministic secret resolution, loader wiring, and fixture-based tests. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The adoption is tightly pinned and the verifier now enforces source metadata, exact selected-file inventories, checksum integrity, symlink rejection, and exclusion of unapproved skills without a remaining substantiated defect. ## Testing The focused network-free behavior test and maintainer-facing verifier both passed, demonstrating the pinned official source/revision, licensed and checksummed vendor contents, selected skill exposure, and tamper rejection; the direct CLI transcript was saved as reviewer-visible evidence, and no UI evidence was applicable because this is a CLI/skill-adoption change.
Evidence: Flux skills verification transcript Source: [Flux skills verification transcript](https://github.com/prandelicious/firstmate/blob/b186752dc2bd25ed9a4098be0fecb8ced81eb57f/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/firstmate-flux-skills-adoption/flux-skills-verification.txt) `Verifier confirms official fluxcd/agent-skills v0.2.0 at commit 9b05787530a3e200a9ac031fc8a477566e0b7adc, exposing only gitops-knowledge and gitops-repo-audit.` ```text Flux CD skills adoption — maintainer-visible verification Command: bin/fm-flux-skills-verify.sh Output: fm-flux-skills-verify: ok fluxcd/agent-skills v0.2.0 (9b05787530a3e200a9ac031fc8a477566e0b7adc); skills: gitops-knowledge gitops-repo-audit Focused behavior test: bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/flux-skills-adoption.test.sh Observed behaviors: - accepts the committed vendor tree - rejects checksum tampering - rejects unlisted adopted files - requires the upstream license - rejects adopted-skill and top-level symlinks - parses manifest values as inert data Result: passed on 2026-08-18 (Asia/Manila workspace session). ```
- Outcome: 🔧 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ across 2 runs (3m58s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Rebase** - 1 warning - ⚠️ `.agents/skills/bws/SKILL.md` - branch carries 1 commit(s) that exist on your local main branch but were never pushed to origin/main; rebasing would bundle this unrelated work (34 file(s)) into the PR: - f15b59e Add public bws skill with firstmate stub for dual-surface loading (#1) Push main to origin, or rebase your branch onto origin/main, before gating.
🔧 **Review** - 4 issues found → auto-fixed (4) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-flux-skills-verify.sh:26` - The verifier executes the tracked MANIFEST as shell code after only wrapping values in quotes. A value containing `$(...)`, backticks, or an embedded quote will execute during routine CI. Parse the fixed keys as data without `source` or evaluation. - 🚨 `bin/fm-flux-skills-verify.sh:54` - Checksum verification only checks listed entries. An extra or replaced file anywhere beneath an adopted skill is accepted if omitted from CHECKSUMS, so the selected-byte invariant is not enforced. Compare a sorted inventory of every adopted-tree file against the checksum paths before hashing. - 🚨 `bin/fm-flux-skills-vendor.sh:109` - The requirement says to “Preserve attribution and license requirements,” but the adoption neither vendors the upstream LICENSE nor makes the refresh script copy it; NOTICE even instructs maintainers to retain an upstream license that is absent. Include and verify the pinned revision's license text. - 🚨 `tests/flux-skills-adoption.test.sh:25` - These assertions raw-grep MANIFEST and natural-language skill stubs for implementation strings, violating the supplied test-quality rule. Parse MANIFEST into a normalized semantic model and exercise the loader/verification interface for routing and amendment selection instead of treating prompt text as behavioral evidence. 🔧 Fix: Harden Flux manifest and checksum verification 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-flux-skills-verify.sh:91` - The selected-byte inventory still ignores symbolic links because `find` includes only `-type f`. A future vendor refresh can copy an upstream symlink via `cp -a`, omit it from CHECKSUMS, and still pass verification; the link may expose unverified content outside the adopted tree. Reject symlinks at the vendor/verification boundary or include their link targets in the authenticated inventory. 🔧 Fix: Reject symlinks in adopted Flux skills 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-flux-skills-vendor.sh:70` - The required criterion “Verify source identity, license, selected bytes, and revision before adoption” is not fully met: this query checks the repository's current metadata before resolving the pinned commit, so it can accept a pinned revision whose LICENSE differs from the current repository license (or reject a valid historical revision after a later license change). Verify the license at the resolved commit, such as through GitHub's license endpoint with `ref=$commit` or against the cloned revision's license file. 🔧 Fix: Pin Flux license verification to revision 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-flux-skills-verify.sh:111` - The top-level inventory checks only regular files and directories, so a committed symbolic link such as `skills/vendor/fluxcd-agent-skills/extra-skill -> ...` is ignored and verification still passes. This violates the selected-content invariant and the requirement to adopt only the two approved skills. Reject every top-level entry not in the exact expected set, including symlinks. 🔧 Fix: Reject unexpected top-level Flux vendor entries ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
🔧 **Test** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `skills/vendor/fluxcd-agent-skills/NOTICE.md:11` - The vendored third-party distribution contains MANIFEST, NOTICE.md, and checksums but no copy of the upstream Apache-2.0 LICENSE, despite NOTICE.md explicitly requiring the upstream license to be retained. Add the pinned upstream LICENSE to the vendor tree and make both refresh and deterministic verification preserve and checksum it. - `bin/fm-flux-skills-verify.sh` - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/flux-skills-adoption.test.sh` - `bin/fm-flux-skills-vendor.sh --tag v0.2.0 --dry-run` - `git status --short` after testing to confirm no transient worktree changes remained 🔧 Fix: Preserve and verify vendored upstream license ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain. - Inspected `bdae21ed09d2cca4f57caed4bda9d30d8f9d9be8..202399816f6e1ba16b007acc94aafa51fd2fb63c` and the focused verifier/test interfaces against the supplied intent. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/flux-skills-adoption.test.sh` — exercised committed-tree acceptance plus rejection of checksum tampering, unlisted files, missing LICENSE, symlinks, and executable manifest data. - `bin/fm-flux-skills-verify.sh` — manually exercised the maintainer-facing network-free verification command and captured its identity, revision, and adopted-skills output. - `git status --short` — confirmed testing left no transient worktree changes.
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: feat(bootstrap): report a home that is over its startup-memory allowance
body:
## Intent

Firstmate has a per-home startup-memory allowance (config/startup-memory-budget, default 7500 estimated tokens) and an estimator for it, but nothing read that meter except the /stow memory-curation pass itself. Confirmed 2026-08-18: the only callers of bin/fm-startup-memory-budget.sh were bin/fm-stow-cascade.sh, bin/fm-test-run.sh, and the stow skill's prose. bin/fm-bootstrap.sh's startup_memory_budget_setup validated the config file and materialized the default but never compared actual usage against it. Observed consequence on the primary home the same day: memory reached 32,568 estimated tokens against a 7,500 allowance and was injected at every session start, with no signal anywhere until a pass was run by hand. The only thing that could report the drift was the thing you had to remember to run.

Goal: emit one line in the session-start digest when a home is over its allowance, naming the measured total, the allowance, and the command that curates it. Silent when within budget, exactly like the other detect-only bootstrap checks. It must work in a secondmate home, where the allowance is the inherited primary-authoritative value.

Explicitly OUT of scope, deliberately: no curation, no pruning, no blocking, no gate. This is a meter reading only. Curation is judgement work owned by the /stow skill, and a check that refused to start a session would be the wrong instrument. Reviewers should not ask for the check to act on what it measures.

Accepted constraints and decisions made while implementing:
- Placed with the existing detect-only bootstrap checks (bin/fm-bootstrap.sh's detect_local_config, called right after crew_dispatch_validate) rather than inventing a new surface or a new config file.
- Reused bin/fm-startup-memory-budget-lib.sh (fm_startup_memory_budget_read, fm_startup_memory_measure_file, fm_startup_memory_decimal_le); the estimator was deliberately not re-implemented.
- The line follows the existing <LABEL>: <detail> shape of its neighbours and deliberately reuses the existing STARTUP_MEMORY_BUDGET label rather than adding a second label, so the bootstrap-diagnostics skill keeps one entry family. Its handling entry was added to .agents/skills/bootstrap-diagnostics/SKILL.md in the same change, as required.
- Deliberate silences, all intended: a home whose memory files are absent measures zero and stays silent; a home exactly at its allowance stays silent (the comparison is <=); an unreadable or absent allowance stays silent here because startup_memory_budget_setup already owns that diagnostic and duplicating it would double-report the same problem; a memory file that is not an ordinary regular file also stays silent here because the /stow pass owns that loud report. These are one-owner decisions, not missed error handling.
- A secondmate home never materializes its own allowance, so the check reads the inherited primary-authoritative config file it converges from the primary.
- docs/configuration.md's existing 'Startup memory budget' section got one line recording that session start now reads the same accounting and never curates or blocks; per the repo's one-owner rule this is a cross-reference, not a second copy of the contract.

Acceptance criteria, all met: a portable regression in tests/ colocated with the existing pattern (three cases added to tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh) proving the line appears when over budget, and does not appear when within budget or when the memory files are absent, plus a secondmate-home case reading the inherited allowance; the over-budget case is pinned at exactly one token past the allowance so the comparison boundary itself is covered. The check adds no network call and costs three stat-sized reads, so it adds no measurable delay to session start. bin/fm-lint.sh passes (shellcheck 0.11.0 clean; actionlint is absent from this environment so the workflow half of the gate did not run and is reported as unconfirmed rather than passed). bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh passes.

Known pre-existing failure, deliberately out of scope for this branch: tests/fm-session-start.test.sh's 'the digest waited for the 12s unreachable-host probe instead of returning from local state' case fails identically on the clean base commit with this change stashed (50s on base, 27s with the change), so it is an environment-dependent pre-existing failure and not caused by this work. Do not fold a fix for it into this change.

This change is generic - every firstmate user pays the same cost for the same reason - so it belongs upstream rather than as a local fork. We hold read-only on the upstream repository, so the pull request may sit awaiting its maintainer; that is expected.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh`'s `startup_memory_budget_setup` now compares measured memory usage against the home's startup-memory allowance and emits one `STARTUP_MEMORY_BUDGET:` line in the session-start digest when usage exceeds it, naming the measured total, the allowance, and the curation command; it stays silent when within budget, when memory files are absent, or when the allowance itself is unreadable (already reported elsewhere), reusing the existing `fm-startup-memory-budget-lib.sh` estimator rather than reimplementing it.
- A secondmate home reads its inherited primary-authoritative allowance for this comparison rather than materializing its own.
- `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` gains three cases covering the over-budget report (pinned at exactly one token past allowance), the silent within-budget/absent-files case, and the secondmate inherited-allowance case.
- `.agents/skills/bootstrap-diagnostics/SKILL.md` and `docs/configuration.md` document the new detect-only line as a cross-reference to the existing startup-memory-budget contract.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is a small, well-isolated detect-only diagnostic that reuses existing library primitives without modification, is placed in the existing local-only bootstrap phase, adds no network calls or state mutation, and is covered by three new tests pinning the silent/over-budget/secondmate-inherited cases including the exact comparison boundary; it fully satisfies every required and forbidden constraint in the stated intent.

## Testing

Ran the full tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh suite (the file this change added its three new tests to) against the real bin/fm-bootstrap.sh binary; all cases passed including the three new startup-memory-budget-meter cases, which produced the exact expected digest line text (over-budget message, silent-within-budget, and inherited secondmate allowance) with no failures observed across two full runs.

title: feat(bin): add optional crew identities for captain-facing surfaces
body:
## Intent

Build and ship a backwards-compatible HMS Surprise crew-identity presentation and persona layer for Firstmate using the Master and Commander operating metaphor: the human is Captain Jack Aubrey, the primary Firstmate is First Lieutenant Tom Pullings, and persistent secondmates plus ordinary crewmates can be presented by distinct character names from a blended roster spanning the 2003 film and Patrick O Brian Aubrey-Maturin novels. Preserve every mechanical task id, kind=secondmate value, status filename, backend target, recovery binding, routing selector, and the secondmate control-plane concept. Implement a small configurable design useful to all Firstmate users while keeping this captain private assignments out of committed defaults. Include a ready-to-use researched roster of at least 29 identities with canonical shipboard roles, operational affinity tags, and concise public citations without copyrighted prose. Add a durable documented local configuration and schema for assigning identities to the primary Firstmate and persistent or task agents, supporting the Aubrey/Pullings hierarchy and distinct active assignments. Identity assignment must survive relaunch and recovery and appear in captain-facing fleet, session, and status surfaces. Herdr Space titles use exact short canonical title plus surname; the primary is Lt Pullings. Project-owning persistent secondmates must append the exact registered repository slug, preserving lowercase and hyphens, as Title Surname — repo-name, including Lt Babbington — npi-brain, Mr Allen — developer-setup, Dr Maturin — llm-usage-dashboard, and Lt Mowett — pco-projects-mda. Project-less agents remain name-only. Labels must remain stable and safely reconcile across relaunch, legacy pre-feature Spaces, adoption without launcher ancestry, and mutable project registry transitions without changing mechanical routing or restart bindings; ambiguous matches must refuse loudly with accurate ids and titles. Full names and expanded ranks belong only in charters and detailed views. Integrate optional identity capture into brief, provision, and spawn lifecycle without breaking existing homes, registry lines, briefs, or metadata with no identity. Preserve exact byte-for-byte existing brief output when crew identity fields are absent, including omitting any extra blank line. Prevent or loudly report duplicate active assignments through deterministic fallback or explicit unassigned handling. Add focused behavioural tests for parsing, backward compatibility, identity-free brief bytes, relaunch persistence, uniqueness, captain-facing rendering, exact repository-slug labels, legacy journal and Space migration, mutable registry transitions, adoption, and accurate ambiguity diagnostics. Update authoritative documentation and AGENTS guidance proportionately with natural British spelling, without converting technical secondmate terms into flavour copy. Do not overwrite the existing private provisional assignments gentech to Mr Allen sailing master, usage-dashboard to Dr Stephen Maturin, and pco-mda to Second Lieutenant William Mowett. The captain cancelled all special Pullings colour treatment, so do not introduce it. Validate all relevant suites and no-mistakes checks, push the feature branch to the configured fork, open a direct PR against kunchenguid/firstmate, and do not merge it.

## What Changed

- Add `bin/fm-crew-identity.sh`, a presentation-only identity layer that validates a local `config/crew-identities.json` (schema `firstmate-crew-roster.v1`), resolves captain/primary/per-task assignments, renders labels, and refuses ambiguous or duplicate active assignments; ships a researched `rosters/master-and-commander.json` roster with canonical roles, affinity tags, and cited sources, plus a `docs/examples/crew-identities.json` sample. Task ids, `kind=secondmate`, status filenames, backend targets, and routing selectors are unchanged.
- Wire identity resolution into the lifecycle and captain-facing surfaces — `fm-brief.sh` (byte-identical output when no identity fields are present), `fm-bootstrap.sh`, `fm-session-start.sh`, `fm-spawn.sh`, `fm-fleet-snapshot.sh`, `fm-fleet-view.sh` — and into the Herdr backend, where Space titles use `Title Surname`, appending ` — repo-slug` for project-owning secondmates; label reconciliation is safe across relaunch, adoption without launcher ancestry, and registry transitions, with `bin/fm-crew-identity-migrate-herdr.sh` for legacy Spaces.
- Extend the shell test suites (Herdr backend, brief, bootstrap, session start, spawn dispatch, fleet snapshot/view, session cleanup) covering parsing, identity-free brief bytes, relaunch persistence, uniqueness, slug labels, migration, adoption, and ambiguity diagnostics; update `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/herdr-backend.md`, `docs/remote-secondmates.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and the provisioning skill, and gitignore the local identity config.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The re-reviewed fix round is a one-line predicate swap on an already-ID-bound reclaim path plus a matching behavioural regression; it closes the reported project-owning-slug refusal without widening unbound discovery (find_all_labelled still uses label_is_own only).

## Testing

Ran the seven changed non-Herdr suites and the full fm-backend-herdr suite through fm-test-run.sh — all passed with no gate skips. Beyond the suites I exercised the feature the way a captain would: generated a real secondmate charter in an identity-free home and byte-compared it to the base commit's output (identical md5, no stray blank line), generated the same charter in an identity-configured home (adds only the Crew identity block), ran fm-fleet-snapshot.sh and fm-fleet-view.sh to capture the rendered captain-facing table showing "Primary identity: Lt Pullings" and per-task Lt Babbington / Dr Maturin while task ids, kind=secondmate and routing columns stayed unchanged, and drove the fm-crew-identity CLI for canonical titles, charter-level full names, and the loud duplicate-assignment refusal. Herdr Space titling with exact repository slugs (Lt Babbington — npi-brain and friends), legacy journal migration, adoption and mutable-registry drift are covered by named assertions in the Herdr suite, captured as an artifact; that surface is a terminal-multiplexer workspace title with no rendered UI to screenshot, so the evidence is CLI/label transcripts rather than images. Working tree left clean.

<details>
<summary>⚠️ **Review** - 1 info</summary>

- 🚨 `rosters/master-and-commander.json:199` - Intent conformance: the criteria require the exact label "Lt Babbington — npi-brain", but the committed roster gives william-babbington `"space_label": "Capt Babbington"`, so a project-owning secondmate assigned that identity renders "Capt Babbington — npi-brain". The other four named cases (Lt Pullings primary, Mr Allen — developer-setup, Dr Maturin — llm-usage-dashboard, Lt Mowett — pco-projects-mda) all match exactly. Author must confirm whether the roster label should be "Lt Babbington" (his lieutenant-era title) or whether the intent text is superseded.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1087` - Secondmate relaunch hard-fails when the inherited config/crew-identities.json disappears from that home while its Space already carries the identity title. Path: state/sm-1.meta records crew_roster/crew_identity, so the branch runs fm_backend_herdr_workspace_identity_rename_exact; with no config, workspace_identity_base_label returns empty, desired falls back to the legacy "2ndmate-sm-1", and workspace_label_is_own("Mr Allen — developer-setup", "") returns 1 — the rename refuses and relaunch exits 1, blocking the secondmate until the Space is renamed by hand. Consider treating an absent config plus a recorded identity as "leave the title alone" rather than a fatal refusal.

🔧 Fix: correct crew Space labels and preserve titles without config
2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1087` - Relaunch renames the secondmate Herdr Space with fm_backend_herdr_workspace_identity_rename_exact, which re-derives the desired title from the home's CURRENT inherited config/crew-identities.json instead of the crew_roster=/crew_identity= the same block just read from state/<id>.meta. docs/configuration.md states the opposite invariant: 'relaunch reads those metadata fields rather than current config, so a later local edit cannot silently change an active agent's identity.' Reachable path: the captain removes or reassigns agents.sd-1 on the primary and inheritance copies the edited config into the secondmate home; relaunch sd-1 -> fm_backend_herdr_workspace_identity_base_label returns unassigned (exit 3) -> workspace_label = 'Unassigned crew' -> rename_exact prints 'refusing an ambiguous Herdr Space title' -> relaunch exits 1. With a changed (not removed) assignment, workspace_label_is_own('Mr Bonden — stream-deck-configuration', <new base>) refuses and relaunch exits 1 again; had it matched, the Space would be retitled to an identity the metadata does not record, diverging from every metadata-driven captain surface. The round-2 fix only closed the config-ABSENT case (bin/backends/herdr.sh:465 `fm_backend_herdr_crew_identity_config_present || return 0`), so the same authorized relaunch-blocking failure remains reachable with config present. Earliest shared boundary: pass the recorded roster/identity into rename_exact (as fm_backend_herdr_projection_identity_rename_exact already takes) rather than re-deriving from live config.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-crew-identity.sh:266` - fm_crew_identity_check_active is called on the relaunch path (bin/fm-spawn.sh:1060) with the metadata-recorded identity, but its configured_owner lookup reads the live config: re-keying agents so the same identity is reserved for a different task id makes relaunch abort with "crew identity '<roster>/<id>' is reserved for configured task '<other>'". Same class as the Space-title finding — a live-config edit blocking an already-running agent's relaunch, contrary to the documented metadata-wins relaunch rule.

🔧 Fix: use recorded crew metadata for relaunch identity checks
4 issues (2 warnings, 2 infos) still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:492` - Reassigning an identity in live config permanently blocks every new spawn in that home until the Space is renamed by hand. The owned-title set is derived only from the CURRENT config, so a home's own previous identity title is not recognised. Reproduced against the real code: with config primary=thomas-pullings and the home's Space titled 'Lt Pullings', the captain edits primary to william-mowett; fm_backend_herdr_workspace_label now returns 'Lt Mowett' and fm_backend_herdr_workspace_label_is_own 'Lt Pullings' returns 1 (legacy 'firstmate' does not match, base differs, no ' — ' form). fm_backend_herdr_workspace_identity_rename_exact then prints "...is not one of this home's own titles..." and returns 1, so fm_backend_herdr_workspace_ensect returns 3 (bin/backends/herdr.sh:2039 for the launcher-ancestry path, :2075 for the label path) and bin/fm-spawn.sh:2084 exits 1. Every crewmate/scout spawn in that home fails; bin/fm-crew-identity-migrate-herdr.sh cannot repair it because it calls the same refusal. The same applies to a secondmate home after agents.<sd-id> is reassigned. This is not the ambiguity case the intent asks to refuse loudly - the Space demonstrably belongs to this home. Earliest boundary: include the home's previously-titled identity (e.g. from the secondmate task's recorded crew_identity, or by accepting any roster space_label of the configured roster for a Space this home is exactly bound to) in the owned set, so a deliberate reassignment retitles rather than deadlocks.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:249` - One odd state/<id>.meta now kills the entire fleet snapshot. crew_identity_record_for_meta_json counts crew_roster/crew_identity with awk (which follows symlinks), then reads them with fm_crew_identity_meta_value, which rejects symlinks via `[ -f ] && [ ! -L ]` and returns 1; line 613 propagates that as `|| return 1`, task_json_lines fails, and the script exits with "fm-fleet-snapshot: task snapshot failed". Every other field on that loop uses fm_meta_get, which tolerates anything and returns empty, so a symlinked meta previously rendered fine and now blanks the whole fleet view for the captain. Degrade to the existing status:"invalid" record instead of returning 1.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:2035` - In a home with crew identities enabled but no agents.<task-id> entry, CREW_IDENTITY resolves to "unassigned", so HERDR_PRESENTATION_IDENTITY_LABEL becomes "Unassigned crew" and fm_backend_herdr_projection_workspace_label drops the concise task label entirely: every concurrently projected unassigned crewmate Space reads "└ Unassigned crew · p:<token>". Nothing mechanical breaks (cleanup still matches on the unique token), but the captain loses the only human-readable discriminator between simultaneous task Spaces, which the pre-feature title provided. Documented as deliberate in docs/herdr-backend.md, so flagging rather than changing: consider "└ Unassigned crew · <concise-task> · p:<token>".
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-crew-identity-migrate-herdr.sh:127` - MIGRATED starts at 1 to pre-count the primary Space, but fm_backend_herdr_workspace_identity_rename_exact returns 0 without renaming when the title already matches, and each secondmate/projection increment has the same property. The closing "migrated N exact Herdr Space title(s)" therefore reports titles considered, not titles changed, and always claims at least 1 even on a fully converged re-run.

🔧 Fix: allow identity reassignment retitle and degrade odd metadata
2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/backends/herdr.sh:1801` - The new recorded prior-identity marker widens fm_backend_herdr_workspace_label_is_own, and fm_backend_herdr_workspace_find_all_labelled uses that same predicate (line 1801), so after a reassignment one home can adopt and rename a Space that now legitimately belongs to another home. Path: primary home P has primary=thomas-pullings; a spawn titles its Space 'Lt Pullings' and records .fm-herdr-space-identity='Lt Pullings'. Captain reassigns P to william-mowett and gives thomas-pullings to secondmate home sd-1, whose Space is 'Lt Pullings — npi-brain'. P then spawns with no herdr ancestry, so workspace_ensure falls to find_all_labelled (herdr.sh:2102). With base='Lt Mowett', label_is_own('Lt Pullings — npi-brain','Lt Mowett') fails on base but matches prior 'Lt Pullings' via label_matches_base's slug form, so sd-1's Space is returned as P's own; ensure adopts it and rename_exact retitles it 'Lt Mowett'. The secondmate's Space is hijacked and P's worker lands in it, instead of the loud ambiguity refusal the intent requires ('ambiguous matches must refuse loudly'). Before this fix round that case refused. Earliest boundary: scope the recorded-prior allowance to the id-bound rename path (launcher ancestry or recorded task metadata) and keep find_all_labelled matching only the home's CURRENT base identity plus its legacy title.
- ⚠️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:464` - Reassignment recovery now depends on a stateful marker file that only exists once this build has already applied or confirmed a title. A home whose Space was titled by an earlier build of this branch, renamed by the captain by hand, or whose FM_HOME marker was cleaned, has no .fm-herdr-space-identity: after a config reassignment rename_exact sees current='Lt Pullings', label_is_own fails on all three arms (legacy 'firstmate', base 'Lt Mowett', empty prior), returns 1, workspace_ensure returns 3 and bin/fm-spawn.sh exits 1 for every crewmate/scout — and bin/fm-crew-identity-migrate-herdr.sh calls the same refusal so it cannot repair it. Narrower than pre-fix, but the same authorised failure remains reachable. Note the accepted instruction asked for stateless recognition of 'a canonical label from the same configured roster'; the author chose marker state instead, which is arguably safer (a roster-wide rule would worsen the cross-home adoption above) — worth an explicit decision rather than a silent substitution.

🔧 Fix: split bound and discovery Space title ownership
2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:1824` - Narrowing label discovery to the CURRENT assignment means a reassigned primary home with no launcher ancestry no longer finds its own stale-titled Space and silently creates a second one. Path: config primary=thomas-pullings, primary Space titled 'Lt Pullings'; captain reassigns primary to william-mowett; next spawn has no herdr parent pane, so fm_backend_herdr_workspace_ensure falls to fm_backend_herdr_workspace_find_all_labelled (herdr.sh:1824) with base='Lt Mowett'. label_is_own('Lt Pullings','Lt Mowett') is now false and the legacy arm is deliberately skipped because 'firstmate' is not home-unique, so there is no match and ensure creates a fresh 'Lt Mowett' Space, leaving the old one orphaned for the captain to close by hand. Before 241f5c8 that Space was adopted and retitled. Secondmate homes still recover via their unique '2ndmate-<id>' legacy title, so only the primary is exposed. This is the direct cost of the accepted 'discovery may match only current-title/unique-legacy' instruction and is arguably the right trade (it is what stops cross-home adoption), but it partially regresses the intent's 'safely reconcile across ... adoption without launcher ancestry' and leaves visible Space litter, so it needs an explicit decision rather than being absorbed silently. Options: fall back to the recorded .fm-herdr-space-identity title for the primary's own discovery only when exactly one candidate matches it and the config reserves it for nobody, or document the orphan and have fm-crew-identity-migrate-herdr.sh report it.
- ℹ️ `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh:477` - The pre-existing 'another crew member's title is still refused' assertions only pass now because the fix round added an otherwise-unused assignment (agents.sd-9=stephen-maturin at line 477, agents.sd-2 at line 424, agents.fmdev at line 555) to make 'Dr Maturin' reserved. That is honest - the refusal really is reservation-driven now - but the loss is real and undocumented: on a bound path an unreserved canonical roster title is now accepted and renamed, and no test names that boundary explicitly. Worth a comment on those three configs stating the title is reserved deliberately, so a future edit removing the assignment does not quietly turn a refusal test into an acceptance test.

🔧 Fix: let reassigned primary reclaim its own stale Space
1 warning still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:1839` - Round 5 reopens unbound title discovery to the recorded prior-identity marker, which is the exact widening the accepted round-4 instruction forbade ("Historical/prior identity markers and arbitrary canonical roster labels must never widen unbound find/adopt matching; discovery may match only the existing safe current-title/unique-legacy rules"). fm_backend_herdr_workspace_reclaimable_prior_base (herdr.sh:509) guards only on "live config reserves this identity for nobody", but unreserved does not mean unoccupied: a home that carried the identity keeps its Space title until it next reconciles. Reachable path: primary home P is thomas-pullings and records marker 'Lt Pullings'; captain reassigns primary=william-mowett and gives thomas-pullings to secondmate sd-1, whose Space becomes 'Lt Pullings — npi-brain'; captain later drops agents.sd-1. Now config_assigns(thomas-pullings) is false, so prior='Lt Pullings' is reclaimable, and the match uses fm_backend_herdr_workspace_label_matches_base, which also accepts the slug form — find_all_labelled returns sd-1's live Space to P, which adopts and retitles it to 'Lt Mowett'. The round-5 test only covers the reserved-by-another-home case, so it passes with this hole open. Narrowest containment if the reclaim is kept: require an exact `lbl = prior` match (a persistent home's prior is always name-only), which removes the slug-suffixed cross-home shape; the author should confirm whether unbound reclaim is wanted at all given the round-4 decision.

🔧 Fix: bind Space reassignment to exact recorded workspace id
2 issues (1 error, 1 info) still open:
- 🚨 `bin/backends/herdr.sh:2235` - fm_backend_herdr_workspace_reclaim_recorded_binding compares the live Space label to the recorded marker with exact string equality, but the marker records the NAME-ONLY base title while a project-owning persistent secondmate's Space is titled '<Title Surname> — <repo-slug>'. Reachable path: home sd-1 assigned samuel-allen owns developer-setup; its Space is 'Mr Allen — developer-setup' and the marker records 'Mr Allen\t<session>\tw-a' (written by workspace_ensure create or by the relaunch rename at bin/fm-spawn.sh:1087). Captain reassigns agents.sd-1 to another identity. Next spawn in that home has no herdr parent pane: find_all_labelled matches nothing (current base differs, legacy '2ndmate-sd-1' is not the title), reclaim runs, binding resolves, current='Mr Allen — developer-setup' != recorded='Mr Allen', so it prints "refusing to retitle an inconsistent binding" and workspace_ensure returns 3 - every crewmate/scout spawn in that home exits 1 until the migration script is run by hand. The binding is exact and provably this home's, so this is not the inconsistency the accepted contract meant to refuse; the sibling predicates (label_is_own_bound, label_matches_base at herdr.sh:449) already accept the slug form. Fix: replace the equality with fm_backend_herdr_workspace_label_matches_base "$current" "$recorded". The round-6 regression only exercises a name-only primary, so it passes with this case broken.
- ℹ️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:2232` - After a reassignment, a marker pointing at a Space the captain has since closed makes workspace_ensure return 3 for every spawn in that home until the marker file is deleted by hand (no automatic fallback to create). This is exactly what the accepted instruction prescribed ('missing, stale, ambiguous, or inconsistent bindings must stop with a guarded-migration diagnostic'), and the diagnostic names both remedies - noting the operational cost, not asking for a change.

🔧 Fix: accept repository-slug titles on bound Space reclaim
1 info still open:
- ℹ️ `bin/backends/herdr.sh:548` - In fm_backend_herdr_workspace_label_is_own_bound, the roster-stem branch returns 1 as soon as fm_crew_identity_config_assigns says the old identity now belongs to another home, short-circuiting the recorded-prior-title arm below. So if the captain both reassigns this home AND hands its old identity to another home before that other home reconciles, the bound reclaim path refuses ('is not one of this home's own titles') even though the session/workspace-id binding proves ownership, and spawns in that home stop until the migration script is run. That is the loud refusal the accepted contract asks for in a genuinely ambiguous title state, so noting the operational cost only — not requesting a change.

</details>

<summary>✅ **Test** - passed</summary>

✅ No issues found.
- <code>`bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-brief.test.sh tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh tests/fm-session-start.test.sh tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh tests/fm-herdr-session-cleanup.test.sh tests/fm-control-relaunch.test.sh tests/fm-fleet-snapshot-view.test.sh` — exit 0</code>

The latest fixture paths also completed. I did not run ShellCheck because this test phase forbids linters; the bounded lint command was tested with a non-analyzing pinned stub.

The dashboard shows ship-demo-a1 in Checking with 92 active seconds.` ```text $ fm-ship-end-to-end.sh verify-current ship-demo-a1 fingerprint=ed35cd385c119e6ea22250c4641c256e0ddee288e2280a65ebf2765249c76c60 $ jq preflight-record-projection {"schema_version":1,"workflow":"ship-end-to-end","task_id":"ship-demo-a1","fingerprint":"ed35cd385c119e6ea22250c4641c256e0ddee288e2280a65ebf2765249c76c60","origin":"direct","state":"approved","producer_revision":2,"approval":{"authority":"direct-captain","evidence":"direct-captain","approved_at":1700000046,"complete_plan_bypass":false},"contract":{"delivery_boundary":"Pull request only","external_boundaries":"No production write","questions":[]}} $ fm-dashboard.sh show {"generated_at":1700000047,"projection":{"empty_text":"Nothing needs you.","needs_you":[],"in_progress":[{"id":"ship-demo-a1","name":"Ship approved workflow","phase":"Checking","active_seconds":92}]}} ```

Confirm this expanded scope or remove it. 🔧 Fix: Remove unrelated Cursor hook registry 4 issues (3 errors, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-sessionstart-run.sh:83` - The intent says “Do not ... add unrelated features.” Cursor still loads `.claude/settings.json`, whose SessionStart entry invokes this wrapper. title: chore: update pull request
body:
## Intent

Codify a standing crewmate rule into firstmate's brief scaffolds (bin/fm-brief.sh): when a crewmate works in a fresh isolated worktree and must run the app/site locally to verify its work, it must copy in the gitignored runtime config the app needs to start (e.g. .env/.env.local), because a fresh worktree does not carry gitignored files so local runs silently fail. Live gap: digiscale-outreach and BOLIA-5369 crewmates could not run their apps to verify.

Requirements and accepted decisions:
- Extend BOTH the ship scaffold AND the scout scaffold (scouts also run apps in worktrees to reproduce bugs) so every generated brief carries the rule, phrased CONDITIONALLY so it is harmless when the task never runs the app.
- Constraints in the rule: copied files stay gitignored (never commit, never let them enter the PR/diff, never print secret values in status/logs/PR); source discovery from a firstmate-provided path or a sibling local checkout of the same repo on the machine; fail-closed - if the source cannot be found, append blocked:/needs-decision: and ask firstmate rather than guessing or fabricating config.
- BOUNDED to the runtime config actually needed to start/verify the app (env files and direct equivalents). Explicitly NOT a blind sweep of every gitignored path - never copy node_modules, build output, caches, or unrelated secrets.
- One-owner rule: state the rule ONCE. Authored once as a shared RUNTIME_CONFIG_SECTION variable (mirroring how HERDR_SECTION and DOD are built once) inserted into the ship and scout heredocs; the secondmate charter deliberately does NOT carry it. NOT duplicated into AGENTS.md. The header comment is a short summary pointing at the scaffold as the full-rule owner.
- Instruction-only by deliberate choice (allowed by the task): no config-copy helper script, because source discovery and which env files an app needs are irreducibly context-dependent, and git already prevents committing gitignored files.
- Built the shared section with the Bash 3.2-safe 'IFS= read -r -d ' idiom, never a heredoc wrapped in a command substitution.
- Colocated test in tests/fm-brief.test.sh asserts, through the public bin/fm-brief.sh output (not source bytes), that ship AND scout briefs contain the rule and all four constraints, and that the secondmate charter omits it.

Note: this repo's workflow lint reports actionlint not installed (exit 127) locally; pre-existing environmental gap, no workflow files were touched.

## What Changed

Final changed paths and statuses:

```text
M	bin/fm-brief.sh
M	tests/fm-brief.test.sh
```

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: A small, additive, instruction-only change that authors one shared conditional section using an already-proven idiom, inserts it into exactly the two intended scaffolds while correctly excluding the secondmate charter, and is covered by a behavior-level test over the generated brief artifact; it fully satisfies the stated intent with no reachable defect.

## Testing

Ran the colocated behavior suite (all green) and, for product-level evidence, generated actual ship, scout, and secondmate briefs from the public fm-brief.sh CLI; the ship and scout briefs render the complete conditional runtime-config rule (bounded scope, source discovery, fail-closed-to-firstmate, never-commit/never-print) and the secondmate charter omits it, matching the intent. Artifacts are the generated brief markdown files themselves (the tool's public output contract), which are the appropriate reviewer-visible surface for this CLI change - there is no rendered UI to screenshot. Transient generated home dir removed; working tree clean.

**Verify isolation before anything else.** Run `pwd -P` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; both must resolve to the disposable task worktree you were launched in, such as a treehouse pool path or an Orca-managed worktree, not the primary checkout firstmate operates from.
The path check is authoritative: `git rev-parse --git-dir` and `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` can help inspect the repo, but they do not prove you are outside the primary checkout.
If the top-level path is the primary checkout or not the worktree you were launched in, STOP - do not branch or commit here - append `blocked: launched in primary checkout, not an isolated worktree` to the status file and stop.

   needs-decision/blocked/paused/done/failed states. No step-by-step FYI progress lines;
   firstmate reads your pane for that.

# Project memory
If `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` already exists, or if this task produced durable project-intrinsic knowledge, run `/Users/emil.christensen/.no-mistakes/worktrees/0169613fbf23/01M0ABN4NCRTDB7CJ637BBCJDZ/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh .` in the worktree.

For anything the codebase already shows, prefer a pointer to the authoritative file, command, or doc over copying the detail.
If you touch a project `AGENTS.md` that lacks `## Maintaining this file`, add that short self-governance section from `/Users/emil.christensen/.no-mistakes/worktrees/0169613fbf23/01M0ABN4NCRTDB7CJ637BBCJDZ/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh` in the same pass.
Keep it proportionate: skip `AGENTS.md` edits for trivial tasks that produced no durable project knowledge.

# Definition of done
Delivery contract: mode=no-mistakes
The task is complete only when committed on your branch.
When you believe it is complete, append `done: {summary}` to the status file and stop.
Firstmate will then instruct you to run /no-mistakes to validate and ship a PR.

You drive no-mistakes by responding to its gates, not by implementing fixes.
Follow the guidance no-mistakes itself provides for the mechanics: it loads when you invoke /no-mistakes, and `no-mistakes axi run --help` plus the `help` lines in each `axi` response are authoritative and version-matched to the installed binary.
When starting no-mistakes, make `--intent` preserve all relevant content from this brief's `# Task` section plus every later accepted Firstmate requirement, clarification, constraint, exclusion, and supersession, carrying only each requirement's current accepted form; retain direct requirements instead of substituting a diff summary, and exclude generic operational, status, delivery, and other scaffold boilerplate unless it is task-specific.
Do not hand-edit, commit, or fix findings yourself while a run is active - the pipeline applies every fix.

Two firstmate-specific rules layer on top of that guidance:
- ask-user findings are never yours to answer: escalate to firstmate (rule 6) and stop.
  Firstmate applies the authority contract in its `AGENTS.md` and obtains any required captain decision.
  When the decision comes back, feed it to the gate with `no-mistakes axi respond` and let the pipeline apply it - do not route the question to "the user" or implement the fix yourself.
- Avoid `--yes`: it would silently bypass firstmate's authority check and any required captain escalation.

After /no-mistakes reports CI green (the CI-ready return point - do not wait for it to keep monitoring in the background until merge), append `done: PR {url} checks green` and stop. You are finished.
```
