title: feat(brief): make PR bodies open with a beneficiary TLDR
body:
## TLDR

- We introduced a required TLDR at the top of every PR body to give the captain, who is the merge authority on every project, a body they will actually read before approving a merge.
- We introduced a fixed "who it serves and what it protects" shape for those bullets to protect reviewers from bodies written from the change's own point of view, which is the specific reason the current ones go unread.
- We introduced a worked one-line example rather than a paragraph of explanation to protect the brief scaffold from growing harder to read while fixing a communication problem.
- We introduced a plainly stated limit on the no-mistakes variant to protect the contract's credibility, since the pipeline owns that PR body's final shape and the brief must not imply otherwise.
- We introduced a regression test over the generated briefs to give the fleet confidence that all three delivery modes keep exactly the contract intended for each.

## Detail

`bin/fm-brief.sh` previously said only "push your branch and open a PR with `gh-axi`" and gave no guidance on the body at all. That silence is what this change fixes.

**direct-PR** is where a worker writes the body itself, so the contract lands in full: open with a short bullet TLDR before any detail, each bullet naming who the change serves and what it protects or gives them, with one concrete worked example inline. Detail may follow underneath, but it may not come first and it may not be the whole body.

**no-mistakes** is where the contract can only reach partway, and the brief now says so rather than implying a guarantee it cannot make. The pipeline generates the body from its own template (`## What Changed`, `## Risk Assessment`, `## Testing`, `## Pipeline`), which no-mistakes owns, not firstmate. What the worker does control is the `--intent` and change summary it feeds in, so the brief directs those to lead with the beneficiary framing and states that this is as far as the contract reaches. Nothing here tries to defeat or post-process the template.

**local-only** raises no PR and is deliberately untouched.

Four lines were added to the scaffold in total.

## Testing

- `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` gains `test_pr_body_tldr_contract`, asserting the contract and its worked example in direct-PR, the limitation wording in no-mistakes, that no-mistakes does not claim control of the generated body, and that local-only carries no PR-body contract at all. All 21 tests in the file pass.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` is clean (ShellCheck 0.11.0, actionlint 1.7.12).
- This PR's own body is written to the new contract, as its first test.

title: fix(bin): recognize teardown work that landed under rewritten commits
body:
## Intent Fix a false refusal in bin/fm-teardown.sh's landed-work safety check: after a rebase, a branch whose content landed in full under rewritten commits could never be reclaimed, because the check only asked whether the branch's COMMITS were reachable from main. Rebase is the normal path here - bin/fm-merge-local.sh is fast-forward-only, so every second chain landing into a moved default branch must rebase first - so every multi-chain local-only graph ended with parent nodes that ordinary teardown could never reclaim, and the documented remedies (merge again, or --force) were both wrong for work that was not actually at risk. The fix teaches the check about patch equivalence (the `git cherry` / patch-id relationship) so content that landed under a rewritten commit is recognised as landed, and removes the NEED for --force in this case rather than making --force easier to reach. The safety property must NOT weaken. Teardown must still refuse genuinely unlanded work: it keeps refusing when a commit's patch is genuinely absent from main, keeps refusing on uncommitted changes regardless of patch state, and --force stays gated on explicit captain authority. Decisions made deliberately during this work - please treat these as intended, not as mistakes: 1. Terminator-aware comparison: a difference that is only a trailing newline must NEVER read as landed. If equivalence cannot be proven including line terminators, it is NOT landed - refuse. 2. Location-preserving proof: reverse-apply must not match an identical block at the wrong location. If location cannot be established, treat as NOT landed and refuse. 3. Net-zero sequences are allowed only AFTER per-patch proof that both inverse patches genuinely landed - never inferred from an empty net diff. 4. Governing invariant: this change may turn a false "landed" into a refusal freely, but may only turn a refusal into an allow on positive proof. 5. A patch that landed and was later reverted, partially reverted, relocated, replaced, or had one hunk or one added line undone must refuse. A landed patch that main later added unrelated lines on top of (a genuine superset) may allow. 6. The reference scan is bounded to the paths the subject commits touch and batched through one `git log -p | git patch-id` pipeline, so cost does not grow with the default branch's history. Acceptance criteria the change must meet, and the tests that must prove them genuinely distinguishing (no single implementation may pass all three by weakening the check): - a test proves teardown allows reclaim when a branch's patch landed under a rewritten commit; - a test proves teardown still REFUSES when the branch has a commit whose patch is not on main; - a test proves teardown still refuses on uncommitted changes even when all commits landed. Verified locally before this run: the full tests/fm-teardown.test.sh suite passes (78 assertions, 0 failures); bin/fm-lint.sh is clean including pinned actionlint; bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh passes. The distinguishing property was proven empirically - the allow test fails against the pre-fix guard from origin/main, and the refuse test fails against a deliberately weakened build whose patch check returns success unconditionally. The final commit on this branch only clears three shellcheck findings that bin/fm-lint.sh (the repo's canonical lint gate, which CI invokes directly) reported in the new code: it asserts the numstat record carries its path field, gives two locals explicit empty-string initialisers, and checks a diff's exit status directly. All three are behavior-preserving or fail-closed. This repo is firstmate's own shared tracked material and bin/fm-teardown.sh is a safety-critical guard, so .agents/skills/firstmate-coding-guidelines/SKILL.md applies: one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dashes, shellcheck-clean bin scripts, tests colocated in tests/ as .test.sh, and tests must exercise behavior through an executable interface rather than asserting implementation source bytes. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-teardown.sh`'s landed-work check no longer relies on commit reachability alone: a new `patches_are_in_ref` arm accepts a branch when every commit the default branch cannot reach is present there as a patch (the `git cherry` / patch-id relationship), which is the only way work rewritten by a rebase can be recognized. The reference scan runs through one batched `git log -p | git patch-id` pipeline bounded to the paths the subject commits touch, and the old `content_in_default` was split into `default_landing_ref` plus a ref-parameterized `content_in_ref`. - The patch arm allows only on positive proof: `subject_patches_are_in_reference` requires every subject patch on the reference side and then a per-path `changes_are_represented_in_tree` proof that reverse-applies each path's binary/full-index patch against a scratch index of the reference tree, rejecting hunks that matched at an offset (relocation), trailing-newline-only differences, non-blob or mode changes, and any path the tree has since deleted lines from; a net-zero subject range is allowed only after both inverse patches are individually proven and the tip tree still matches over those paths. The merged-PR path keeps its patch-id-only contract, and `validate_worktree_teardown_safety` still refuses on uncommitted changes with a distinct message when the commits did land. - `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` adds ~20 behavior-level cases through the teardown executable covering the rebase allow, an absent-patch refusal, dirty-worktree refusal after landing, plus reverted, partially reverted, relocated, replaced, superset, rename, net-zero and patch-history-failure variants; `docs/gitlab-merge-watch.md` updates its one-line description of teardown's fallback to name the default-branch checks. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: A 400-line rewrite of a safety-critical destructive-action guard is large in blast radius, but every new arm is fail-closed, the loosening is gated behind a per-commit patch-id match plus a location-preserving tree-representation proof, and 20 new behavior-level tests cover the three required distinguishing criteria plus revert/relocate/replace/newline/net-zero adversarial cases — so it is safe to merge with the informational notes as follow-ups. ## Testing Ran the subject's own suite (tests/fm-teardown.test.sh: 79 assertions, 0 failures) and then exercised bin/fm-teardown.sh directly in sandboxed repos to capture the operator-visible CLI output for each acceptance criterion: teardown now completes for a branch whose patch landed under a rewritten commit, still refuses with 'commits not yet on main' when a commit's patch is absent, and still refuses on uncommitted changes with copy that correctly credits the landed commits. Re-running the same rebase scenario against the pre-fix script from the base commit reproduces the original false REFUSED, so the fix is genuinely distinguishing rather than a weakened check; transcripts and suite results are saved as evidence and the worktree was left clean.
Evidence: Teardown CLI transcript after the fix (three acceptance scenarios) Source: [Teardown CLI transcript after the fix (three acceptance scenarios)](https://github.com/IanQiu979/firstmate/blob/6576899eb0e046e1516382481bb0de79d7418c1a/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-teardown-false-refusal-after-rebase/teardown-cli-transcript-after-fix.txt) SCENARIO 1 (patch landed under a rewritten commit): * f58ae1b add feature | * f27dbd5 rebased: add feature.txt | * 1938898 unrelated main commit [branch commits are NOT reachable from main - rebase rewrote them] $ fm-teardown.sh task-x1 teardown task-x1 complete (window firstmate:fm-task-x1, worktree .../evid-landed-rebase/wt) [exit status: 0] SCENARIO 2 (a commit's patch never landed): REFUSED: local-only worktree .../evid-unlanded-commit/wt has work not yet merged into main and not on any remote. commits not yet on main: e1ea9f4 add extra a41a0b4 add feature [exit status: 1] SCENARIO 3 (all commits landed, worktree dirty): REFUSED: local-only worktree .../evid-dirty/wt has uncommitted changes; its commits already landed in main. uncommitted changes present Commit the uncommitted changes (or get the captain's explicit OK to discard, then --force). These are correct today only because every entry point is evaluated inside an `if`/`&&` condition (`if [ -n "$unmerged" ] && patches_are_in_ref ...` at 1728, `if ! work_is_landed ...` at 1756), which suppresses errexit for the whole call subtree. A future caller invoking `patches_are_in_ref` as a plain statement would make the script exit at the first non-zero git status instead of returning "not landed". Consequence is fail-closed (teardown aborts non-zero), so this is a maintenance hazard rather than a safety hole; an inline note or `|| status=$?` idiom would make the dependency explicit. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:1199` - The `numstat` (pre->post) binary guard at 1199/1210 is unreachable as a distinct case. Whenever pre->post is binary, `post` is binary, so the `current_numstat` (post->tree) binary guard at 1216 already fires. The check is harmless and fail-closed; it exists mainly to give the `numstat` local a use for SC2034. Dropping it (and the now-unused local) would remove a branch that no input can reach on its own.

title: fix: enforce worker capacity and bound lint memory
body:
## Intent Fix the recurring FirstMate and no-mistakes OOM failure on the VPS. Enforce a safe active-worker limit, bound ShellCheck memory without changing deterministic diagnostics, and validate the approved FirstMate ship workflow recovery. Do not merge, deploy, or self-update. ## What Changed - Add a fail-closed active-worker capacity guard, defaulting to one worker, with launch reservations and inherited settings across local and remote secondmate homes. - Run ShellCheck one root at a time in each bounded lint worker, while replaying unique diagnostics in deterministic order. - Register remote capacity routes through the job protocol and set a fixed Git identity for CI behavior fixtures. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change has a bounded worker-capacity guard, shared host accounting, remote route registration, and lint diagnostic replay. No source defect was found in the reviewed paths. ## Testing Focused behavior checks verified worker admission for local, nested, and remote routes; secondmate limit inheritance; ship-launch recovery behavior; remote job routing; and byte-exact deterministic ShellCheck diagnostics with one or two bounded workers. The direct CLI transcript shows the user-visible capacity refusal. This is a CLI-only change, so no visual UI artifact applies.
Evidence: FirstMate capacity refusal transcript Command: fm-spawn.sh candidate /unused codex --mode no-mistakes --yolo off Fixture: one active Codex ship worker; default maximum is one. Exit status: 1 stderr: error: worker capacity reached (1/1 active); queue this task or wait for a worker to finish ```text Command: fm-spawn.sh candidate /unused codex --mode no-mistakes --yolo off Fixture: One active Codex ship worker; config/max-active-workers is absent, so the default limit is 1. Exit status: 1 stderr: error: worker capacity reached (1/1 active); queue this task or wait for a worker to finish ```
- Outcome: 🔧 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ across 2 runs (14m40s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Rebase** - 1 warning - ⚠️ `.agents/skills/secondmate-provisioning/SKILL.md` - branch carries 9 commit(s) that exist on your local main branch but were never pushed to origin/main; rebasing would bundle this unrelated work (15 file(s)) into the PR: - ca581238 fix(ci): provide Git identity for behavior fixtures - 4000723b fix: bound ShellCheck memory per lint root - 4501bb58 no-mistakes(document): Document worker capacity inheritance - 1d2edea7 no-mistakes(review): Allow remote pre-inherited capacity validation - f6d0e4f1 no-mistakes(review): Enforce capacity limits during dead-worker relaunches - ab6850ec no-mistakes(review): harden worker capacity reservations and secondmate inheritance - f70f7bde no-mistakes(review): reserve worker capacity through startup and inheritance - d70824e9 no-mistakes(review): fix worker-capacity admission and configuration validation - 51339e56 fix(spawn): bound active worker capacity Push main to origin, or rebase your branch onto origin/main, before gating.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed (11) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-worker-capacity-lib.sh:95` - The counter uses each home's `$STATE` only. A local secondmate on the VPS gets a separate full limit, so it can start a worker while the primary is already at its limit. This keeps the VPS OOM path reachable. Use one host-scoped admission lock and counter shared by the primary and local secondmate homes. 🔧 Fix: Share worker capacity across local secondmate homes 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:914` - A local secondmate that was already running before this change never received `FM_WORKER_CAPACITY_HOST_STATE`. When it later runs the updated spawn script, this default selects its own `$STATE`, so it can see a free local slot and start a worker while the primary host is already at capacity. This leaves the VPS OOM sequence reachable. Resolve the host state at this boundary from the validated local `.fm-secondmate-parent` binding when the environment value is absent; use the parent `state/` directory or fail closed. 🔧 Fix: Resolve legacy secondmate capacity host state 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:693` - A remote secondmate that was already running before this change has no `FM_WORKER_CAPACITY_HOST_STATE`. This branch resolves its `route=remote` fallback to its own `state/`, which excludes the secondmate endpoint recorded in `state/parent-route/<id>.meta`. With a limit of 1, that secondmate can still start one child worker, leaving two live endpoints on the remote host. Resolve and validate the local `state/parent-route` record for the remote binding, then use it as the shared host state. 🔧 Fix: Count legacy remote secondmates in host capacity 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-worker-capacity-lib.sh:145` - Host counting stops after direct secondmate homes. A nested secondmate's workers are not counted: with a limit of 3, primary -> secondmate -> nested secondmate counts as 2, then the nested home can start multiple workers. Nested state is handled by the teardown path. Recursively count validated descendant secondmate homes, including their pending reservations, at this shared admission function. 🔧 Fix: Recursively count nested secondmate worker capacity 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:723` - A legacy nested local secondmate has no `FM_WORKER_CAPACITY_HOST_STATE`. This fallback uses only its direct parent's `state/`, so it excludes workers in the root primary and sibling homes. For example, after the root is at its limit, the nested home can still admit workers under its separate lock. Resolve validated local parent bindings recursively to the root host state; if the chain reaches a remote parent, use its validated `parent-route` state. - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1039` - A remote secondmate is admitted against the primary host before `spawn_remote_secondmate` identifies its route. At a full primary limit, line 1044 rejects the remote launch even though remote endpoint metadata is deliberately excluded from this host count and the remote control path has its own capacity guard. Skip the primary-host reservation for validated remote secondmate launches, and let the remote host admission own it. 🔧 Fix: Resolve nested and remote capacity admission 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:724` - Remote secondmate homes on the same remote machine resolve distinct `<home>/state/parent-route` directories as their host state. Each route therefore takes a different lock and counts only its own endpoint tree. With `max-active-workers=1`, two remote routes on the same host can both start an endpoint, so the host OOM path remains reachable. Make remote admission use one host-wide state/index at the remote-control boundary. - 🚨 `bin/fm-worker-capacity-lib.sh:104` - Pending reservations are counted independently of metadata. If the spawner is killed after Enter but before line 2979 removes its reservation, later counts include both the live endpoint and the stale pending file. This permanently reduces capacity; at a limit of 1 it blocks all future work after that endpoint exits. Reconcile pending records with their matching metadata under the admission lock, while retaining a reservation only when launch state is still uncertain. 🔧 Fix: Share remote capacity and reconcile stale reservations 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh:43` - `CAPACITY_STATE` is scoped to `$FM_ROOT`, not the remote host. Two routes on the same VPS may use different configured remote roots; each then locks and counts its own `<root>/.firstmate-worker-capacity`, so `max-active-workers=1` still permits one worker from each route. This keeps the OOM sequence reachable. Decide whether the required limit is host-wide as the intent says; if so, move admission state to the shared remote-account/job boundary and register all configured route states, including legacy routes outside one home-parent directory. - 🚨 `bin/fm-lint.sh:75` - The required criterion says to “bound ShellCheck memory without changing deterministic diagnostics,” but this hunk invokes ShellCheck separately for every root. A sourced canonical file is then diagnosed once through its importer and again as its own root. The existing parity fixture expects each such diagnostic exactly once (`tests/fm-lint.test.sh:615-618`), so this changes emitted diagnostics. Preserve the source-graph diagnostic contract while applying the memory bound. 🔧 Fix: Share remote job capacity and deduplicate lint diagnostics 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-worker-capacity-lib.sh:11` - The required criterion is “Enforce a safe active-worker limit,” but this hunk says “An absent file keeps the historical unlimited behaviour.” The current worktree has no `config/` directory, so `fm-spawn.sh` receives limit `0` and bypasses admission. The OOM path remains reachable until an external config file exists. Confirm that optional, external configuration is authorized, or require a safe default. 🔧 Fix: Default worker capacity to one 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-worker-capacity-lib.sh:123` - A SIGKILL after reservation creation but before metadata publication leaves a pending file with no matching `.meta`. This path counts it forever, so later spawns can be refused permanently. During reconciliation, expire and release no-metadata reservations after the grace period. - 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1819` - An explicit primary limit of `1` can be skipped when the secondmate home does not ignore `config/`. The missing destination uses default `1`, so this equality check accepts it as inherited. This conflicts with the new behavioral case at `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh:505`; require the destination file when the primary explicitly has one. 🔧 Fix: Expire stale reservations and enforce inheritance 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-worker-capacity-lib.sh:294` - Remote capacity routes are never removed. A successful remote retirement deletes its secondmate home, but its `.worker-capacity-route-<id>.state` remains. The next host count requires that recorded route directory to exist and fails closed, so all later worker spawns on that host are refused. Remove the route record after successful retirement, under the shared capacity lock. - 🚨 `bin/fm-worker-capacity-lib.sh:240` - The shared remote index only discovers sibling homes below the current home parent. A live legacy remote secondmate in another configured remote-home directory is not registered, so its endpoint is absent from the count. With a limit of 1, a new route can start a worker while that legacy route already has one. Register all known routes at the remote job boundary, not only siblings. 🔧 Fix: Register and release remote capacity routes 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-remote-job-lib.sh:510` - The required criterion is “Enforce a safe active-worker limit,” but the new route registration records only the home for the job being staged. A live legacy route in another remote-home directory that has not staged a job since this change has no `routes/<id>.home` record. A later launch on a new route counts only itself and can pass a full host limit. Register all live configured remote routes before admission, or use a host-level registry that survives upgrades. 🔧 Fix: Register all remote routes before admission ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
🔧 **Test** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-lint.sh:458` - The bounded lint wrapper changes diagnostic bytes from the base behavior: replay adds a trailing blank line. A ShellCheck-compatible executable fixture shows the content and order are otherwise unchanged, but base output differs for both jobs=1 and jobs=2. This breaks the required deterministic diagnostic parity. - `git diff --stat f5a12e8bb9f62c61e723c420981442d1c62718a9 c91f413d9a8e9b1c7f2ea8d3be8fd8bed89cc73a` - `bash tests/fm-worker-capacity.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-on.test.sh` - ShellCheck-compatible interface fixture: base `fm-lint.sh` versus target with `FM_LINT_JOBS=1` and `FM_LINT_JOBS=2` - Focused `fm-secondmate-harness` selectors: backend precedence, crew/secondmate capacity, and stale-reread recovery 🔧 Fix: Preserve exact bounded lint diagnostic bytes ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain. - `bash tests/fm-worker-capacity.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-lint.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-remote-entrypoint.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-on.test.sh` - `bash tests/fm-remote-job.test.sh` - `FM_LINT_JOBS=1 bin/fm-lint.sh ` - `FM_LINT_JOBS=2 bin/fm-lint.sh ` - `fm-spawn.sh candidate /unused codex --mode no-mistakes --yolo off` with one active fixture worker
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: Refuse agent co-author trailers in briefs and at merge time
body:
## Summary
- Merged commits on deeplabs `main` picked up `Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` trailers, which the AGENTS.md style rule forbids. Investigation traced this to the underlying coding tool's own default git-commit-message convention, not anything in the crewmate brief itself.
- Adds an explicit rule 8 to both the ship and scout brief scaffolds in `bin/fm-brief.sh`, telling the crewmate to override that default and never add an agent/AI co-author trailer, including on scratch commits.
- Adds a shared mechanical guard, `bin/fm-agent-coauthor-lib.sh`, and wires it into both merge paths (`bin/fm-pr-merge.sh`, `bin/fm-merge-local.sh`) so a merge is refused - before it lands - if any commit in the range carries a `Co-authored-by:`/`Co-Authored-By:` trailer naming a known AI agent (by name token or automated noreply address).
- Scope: the guard applies to every project's delivery path, not just firstmate's own repo, since the underlying cause (a harness-level commit default) is not project-specific.

## Test plan
- [x] `bin/fm-lint.sh` (shellcheck) passes clean on all touched/new scripts
- [x] `tests/fm-agent-coauthor-lib.test.sh` (new): scan correctly allows clean/human trailers and blocks Claude/OpenAI-style and mixed trailers
- [x] `tests/fm-merge-local.test.sh` (new): end-to-end against a real git repo - refuses and leaves `main` untouched when the task branch carries an agent trailer; merges cleanly otherwise
- [x] `tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh` and `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` (existing) still pass unmodified against the updated scripts
- [x] Manually verified the guard against a real `git log` range and a live commit

title: fix(bin): preserve inactive reconciliation scan progress
body:
## Intent Diagnose and fix the firstmate CI timing flake in the watcher-wake-lock test family (captain-authorized ship), making the test deterministic WITHOUT weakening any assertion. The flake intermittently failed CI job 'Behavior portable serial 2' and blocked the docs-only GROK_BOT.md PR #2590 (run 32170177284: family=watcher-wake-lock count=4 failed=1); a prior run on the same branch passed, proving a flake, not a regression. Reproduction first was required: the failing assertion was recovered from the run's attempt-1 logs and reproduced locally - it is tests/fm-inactive-reconcile.test.sh's 'next bounded scan did not resume with the following child' (line ~385), preceded by grep failing on a missing state/.wake-queue. Root cause (verified with an instrumented capture and an aligned-start counterfactual sweep): bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh computes its aggregate scan deadline in whole seconds (date +%s + FM_INACTIVE_RECONCILE_BUDGET_SECS), so the test's 1-second budget has an effective value in (0,1]; a scan starting just before a wall-clock second boundary quantizes its whole budget away mid-scan and exits having visited no child (return 3 at the remaining<=0 check) while write_scan_marker has already advanced the durable cursor past the never-examined child - so the second scan never wakes for child b and the wake queue never exists. A second defect: the outer fm_run_timed process-group kill fired at exactly the budget, routinely preempting the scan's own clean bounded exit path. The fix is a real ordering/progress fix, deliberately NOT a sleep-bump and NOT a test weakening: (1) every scan now visits at least its first due child, with that child's state-read bound floored at one second, so no scan invocation can be a zero-work no-op (in production budgets >=2s the quantization could never reach zero, so production behavior is unchanged); (2) the outer process-group kill moves to budget+1 seconds so the scan's own deadline enforces the budget and the kill is purely a backstop for a scan wedged in an unbounded wait (e.g. a live-held wake-queue lock) instead of racing the clean exit. The previously flaky assertion is untouched. The ONLY test edit is the sibling test_full_scan_budget_includes_wake_lock_wait elapsed bound 3s->4s, deliberately tracking the backstop move to budget+1; its property - the scan cannot ride the 30-second live lock hold - is preserved. Scope is deliberately narrow: only bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh and tests/fm-inactive-reconcile.test.sh change; the separate fm-procevent flake and the prior fm-watch-arm-test-flaky-hang-r1 follow-up were confirmed to be different root causes and are intentionally not touched. Evidence: pre-fix the extracted failing test failed 3x in ~380 local runs and an aligned-start sweep failed 7/40 (6/8 at the 920ms hot spot); post-fix the same loops ran 570/570 clean (3x150 parallel + 80 instrumented + 40 aligned including the hot spot), the full watcher-wake-lock family passes 15/15, and bin/fm-lint.sh plus bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh are clean. ## What Changed - Guarantee each inactive reconciliation scan visits its first due child with at least a one-second state-read bound, preventing cursor advancement without examination. - Move the process-group kill backstop to one second after the scan deadline so clean bounded exits are not preempted. - Document the revised deadline behavior and align the wake-lock timing test with the later backstop. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The narrowly scoped change preserves assertions, guarantees first-child progress under deadline quantization, and cleanly separates the internal deadline from the outer process-group backstop without introducing a substantiated reachable defect. ## Testing The focused reconciliation suite passed, including the moved wake-lock backstop; the formerly flaky child-b wake assertion then passed 12 ordinary repetitions and 8 wall-clock-boundary-aligned repetitions, with persisted wake behavior captured in evidence logs and no worktree residue.

title: fix(bin): spawn into a local-only project that has no origin remote
body:
## Intent A local-only project with no remote cannot be spawned into at all. Fix that. The bug, reproduced: data/projects.md documents local-only as a posture whose project "may have no remote", and the project-management skill says the same: "A local-only project may have no remote and skips no-mistakes initialization." But bin/fm-spawn.sh's freshen_spawn_worktree_base begins with an unconditional `git -C "$worktree" fetch --quiet origin`, so a repo with no origin fails immediately with: error: could not fetch origin for pooled worktree ''; refusing to launch from a potentially stale base. Reproduced 2026-08-17 spawning a ship task into a freshly created local-only project with a single commit and no remote configured. The spawn aborts before writing task metadata, so it fails cleanly - the worktree lease is released and no state/.meta is left behind - but the task simply cannot start. Reproduce it independently before fixing, with a throwaway local repo, so the real thing gets fixed. The fix: when the repository has no origin remote configured, there is no stale base possible: the local default branch IS authoritative, so the freshen step has nothing to do and must be skipped rather than treated as a failure. Detect the genuine absence of the remote, skip freshening, and continue the spawn from the local default branch. Preserve the existing guard exactly where it still applies. If an origin remote IS configured and the fetch or default-branch resolution fails, that must keep refusing loudly as it does today - an unreachable remote is a real stale-base risk and this change must not weaken it. The distinction is "no remote configured" versus "remote configured but unreachable", and those two must not collapse into one code path. Accepted decision (spawn-remoteless-skip-scope, already answered and applied): the remoteless skip must never be silent. Taking that path prints exactly one loud NOTICE naming the project and the local default branch launched from, so a project that lost a remote it was meant to have stays visible rather than being silently assumed local-only. Check whether the same unconditional-remote assumption exists anywhere else on the spawn, teardown, or merge path for a remoteless local-only project, and fix what is found in the same change rather than leaving a second instance of this bug for later. bin/fm-merge-local.sh and bin/fm-teardown.sh are the obvious places to check, since teardown's landed-work test already has a documented local-only fallback for "the common case where there is no remote at all" - confirm that path genuinely works with no remote rather than assuming it does. Acceptance criteria: 1. A ship spawn into a local-only project with no remote succeeds and the worker starts in a genuine isolated worktree on the local default branch. 2. A spawn into a project WITH a remote whose fetch fails still refuses, with its current message unchanged. Prove both halves. 3. Tests colocated in tests/ following the existing pattern, covering the no-remote skip, the remote-present-but-unreachable refusal, and whatever second instance of the assumption is found. Drive the two cases apart deliberately so neither can pass vacuously. 4. bin/fm-lint.sh passes. 5. Update whichever owner documents this behavior, per the knowledge-placement tree - the script header and --help own exact mechanics. Do not restate the contract in a second place. Constraints: this is a narrow correctness fix. Do not restructure the spawn path, do not change the worktree pooling model, and do not relax any other guard. If an unrelated problem is found, note it in the PR description rather than fixing it. This task changes firstmate's own shared, tracked material, so the firstmate-coding-guidelines contract applies: knowledge-placement tree, one-owner rule, one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never an em dash, shellcheck-clean bin scripts, and tests colocated in tests/ that exercise behavior through an executable interface rather than asserting implementation source bytes. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-spawn.sh` splits base-ref resolution into a new `spawn_worktree_base_ref` helper that keeps "no origin remote configured" and "origin configured but unreachable" as separate paths: a genuinely remoteless project skips the origin fetch and takes `refs/heads/` as its base authority, while a configured-but-unfetchable origin still refuses with its existing `could not fetch origin ...` message. A remoteless project whose local default branch cannot be resolved refuses too, and the clean-worktree and reset checks still run afterwards in both cases. - The remoteless skip is never silent: it prints exactly one `NOTICE` naming the project path, the skipped origin freshen, and the local default branch taken as the base authority. The `fm-spawn.sh` header documents these mechanics, and `docs/architecture.md`'s one-line base-freshness summary now says the authority is origin's default branch when a remote is configured and the local default branch when the project has none. - `tests/fm-spawn-pool-base-freshen.test.sh` grows remoteless ship and scout launches, an unresolvable-local-default refusal, and a notice-before-a-later-refusal case; both the remoteless and unreachable-origin fixtures now advance the local default branch past the pool base so neither verdict can pass vacuously, and origin-backed cases assert the notice is absent. `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` adds two cases that drive `bin/fm-merge-local.sh` and teardown against a project with no remote at all - landed work tears down, unlanded work still REFUSES - confirming that path already worked without needing a code change. ## Known limitation A project with no origin remote whose local default branch is named something other than `main` or `master` still refuses to launch. The shared default-branch helper (`default_branch` in `bin/fm-ff-lib.sh`) resolves only `origin/HEAD`, `main`, and `master`, so a remoteless project on, for example, a `trunk` default branch still stops with `could not determine the local default branch ... refusing to launch from a potentially stale base`. Widening that helper was deliberately left out of scope for this change. It is re-implemented identically in `bin/fm-merge-local.sh`, `bin/fm-teardown.sh`, `bin/fm-review-diff.sh`, `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh`, and `bin/fm-tangle-lib.sh`, so fixing it for spawn alone would leave those callers disagreeing about what a project's default branch is - a worse defect than the one being fixed. The failure mode if it ever bites is a loud, diagnosable refusal rather than silent wrong behaviour, and the repair is small when a real case appears. The existing refusal is covered by `tests/fm-spawn-pool-base-freshen.test.sh`; no test pins this gap as desired behaviour. ## Note on the lint step `bin/fm-lint.sh` passes, with ShellCheck 0.11.0 matching the pin. The separate workflow linter `bin/fm-lint-workflows.sh` reported `actionlint not found` (exit code 127) because `actionlint` is not installed on this machine, and installing it would mean writing outside this task's worktree. This change touches no `.github/workflows/` files, and CI installs the pinned `actionlint` itself, so workflow linting is still enforced before merge. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The fix adds one narrowly guarded branch that can only intercept repo shapes which previously hard-refused (a fetch cannot succeed without a configured origin URL), keeps the unreachable-origin guard and its messages byte-identical, uses the same remote-detection idiom as teardown/merge/review, and is covered by non-vacuous tests on both halves plus the remoteless teardown/merge path. ## Testing I reproduced the reported failure from scratch with my own harness before trusting the fix: a freshly built local-only repo with one commit and no remote, a real pooled git worktree, and the real fm-spawn.sh from base d843712 - it aborted with the documented `could not fetch origin` refusal and wrote no task metadata. The same harness against the target commit launches the ship task, prints exactly one loud NOTICE naming the project and the local default branch, and resets the pooled worktree from its stale base onto the local main tip; the companion case with an origin configured but unreachable still refuses, exit 1, with the message byte-identical to before and no fallback to the local branch, so the two conditions are demonstrably separate code paths. For the second instance of the assumption I drove the real fm-merge-local.sh and fm-teardown.sh on a remoteless project and captured the transcript: the approved local merge lands on local main with no remote present and teardown accepts, while unmerged work is still refused without being discarded. On the automated side, tests/fm-spawn-pool-base-freshen.test.sh passes at the target and fails precisely at the remoteless case when run against the pre-fix script (all pre-existing guard cases still passing), and tests/fm-teardown.test.sh passes in full. This is a CLI-only change with no rendered UI surface, so the reviewer-visible evidence is CLI transcripts rather than screenshots. I did not run bin/fm-lint.sh, which is out of scope for this phase; everything else in the acceptance criteria checked out and the worktree is clean.

title: fix(bin): correct declared-pause liveness triage
body:
## Intent

Fix an inverted safety check in bin/fm-watch.sh: healthy workers parked on a declared wait are woken every cycle, while dead ones get the quiet long cadence. It is exactly backwards, and it has been costing a full supervision turn per false alarm since at least 2026-08-12 (six spurious stale wakes across four correctly parked tasks in roughly forty minutes).

The diagnosis was handed over already done, to VERIFY rather than repeat. pause_state_class reads the status log correctly - crew_absorb_class returns `paused` for a worker with a declared `paused:` line - and that verdict is then thrown away by two liveness short-circuits that both return `none`: one when `.paused-<key>` exists and the recheck marker is fresh, and one unconditionally, in each case for a non-secondmate window whose agent is not `dead`. The dispatcher routes `none` to surface_nonterminal_stale, which emits the bare unannotated `stale: <win>` and then writes `.paused-<key>`, `.paused-rechecked-<key>` and `.paused-resurfaced-<key>`. Consequence: handle_paused_stale, the absorber holding the long PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS cadence, was reachable for a non-secondmate worker ONLY when its agent was dead. Secondmates escaped entirely because both short-circuits were gated on window_kind != secondmate. This was verified against the code before changing it, and traced to its origin: PR #743 added the inversion in a review-fix commit titled "Gate pause suppression on confirmed agent death".

Intended behaviour, as specified: liveness decides whether a declared pause is TRUSTWORTHY, not what the class is. A live agent on a declared pause is the normal healthy case and belongs in handle_paused_stale, absorbed on the long cadence. A dead agent on a declared pause is the anomaly - the pause can no longer be true, because nothing is left to end it - and deserves the immediate surface. The existing re-surface throttle is kept so a genuinely long wait still gets rechecked periodically; the goal is to stop the per-cycle churn, not to make firstmate blind to a wait that has gone stale.

An explicitly assigned open question was what `unknown` should mean, since fm_backend_agent_alive can return it and textually it took the same `!= dead` branch as a live agent. DECISION MADE DELIBERATELY: `unknown` keeps the declaration trusted, same as `alive`. fm_backend_agent_alive folds an unreadable read, an ambiguous foreground process, and an unverified backend into `unknown`, so it is a gap in measurement rather than evidence the worker is gone; fm_backend_agent_state reserves confident verdicts for `alive` and `dead`/`missing` for that same reason. Reading `unknown` as death would permanently strip pause absorption from every worker on a backend that cannot answer, which is the same bug in a narrower form, while trusting it costs at most one bounded recheck per PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS window because that recheck remains the backstop. This decision is justified in the commit message, as required.

This change DELIBERATELY overturns part of PR #743's tested guarantee, and that is intended, not an oversight. A dead agent's declared pause now surfaces as a plain stale wake instead of the annotated "awaiting external ... confirm the wait still holds" recheck, because that annotation told firstmate a wait was still live for a worker that had already exited. The flood #743 actually fixed is preserved and still asserted: exactly one wake across six unchanged polls, since the per-hash stale suppressor and the pause markers take over the moment the first surface lands. Two of #743's assertions (`bare -eq 0` and the "awaiting external" grep for the dead-agent cases) were rewritten because they encoded the inversion, and the pre-existing `alive-decision-gate` sub-case, which asserted that a live parked worker must surface immediately, was replaced by the correct contract. This matches the fix shape recorded independently in the fleet backlog entry for this task, which asks for exactly this live/dead split including the immediate bare surface for a dead agent.

Test approach was specified and followed: the regression was written FIRST and proven RED against the prior HEAD, and it can fail in both directions. All four liveness verdicts - alive, dead, unreadable, ambiguous - are driven through the real tmux liveness classifier via the existing fake-tmux fixture (pane commands grok, zsh, node and empty resolve to alive, dead, ambiguous and unreadable respectively), and both `unknown` sources are exercised so neither one alone carries the verdict. Assertions are on the classification's observable effects rather than on wake wording, as required: the pause is fresh under a high re-surface threshold, so the bounded cadence cannot wake at all, which makes a queued stale wake mean "declaration rejected" and no wake mean "absorbed". Existing fixtures whose scenarios describe a LIVE parked worker but used `zsh` as the pane command (a dead-agent read, which only passed before because dead was the absorbing path) were switched to an agent command so they model what they claim; that is a fixture correction, not a weakened assertion. A `queued_stale_wakes` test helper was added because an absorbed cycle never creates the wake-queue file, so a raw awk over it errored instead of counting zero.

Scope was constrained to bin/fm-watch.sh and its tests, with an explicit instruction not to redesign the watcher, add a config knob, introduce a new state file, or build a wrapper. The fix is the inversion of two conditions, extracted into one named predicate (pause_declaration_is_trustworthy) so the duplicated liveness read has a single owner; the now-dead `class = none && agent dead -> paused` promotion collapsed into the trusted path. No config knob, no new state file, no wrapper, no redesign. Two owners outside bin/fm-watch.sh were updated because they stated the now-inverted policy in prose: docs/architecture.md's watcher paragraph, and a comment in bin/fm-classify-lib.sh which restated the watcher's liveness policy - that restatement was removed rather than corrected, so the policy keeps one owner (the firstmate repo's one-owner rule for contracts).

FOLLOW-UP FIX, 2026-08-19, captain ruling. Fork integration review found a real defect in this change and the captain ruled it must be fixed here, on this pull request, because this is the live review artifact. The dead-agent guarantee only held for a pane that sat perfectly still. When a pane's content differs from the previous poll the hash counter resets, so the two-consecutive-hash stale path is never reached and the changing-hash dispatcher decides alone, and that dispatcher still collapsed `working` and `none` into a single clear_pause_tracking catch-all. A confidently dead agent therefore had its pause and stale markers erased every poll with no wake queued, and a dead agent's idle shell is exactly the pane most likely to churn - a clock, a timestamped prompt, a spinner the exited agent left behind - so its hash never repeats and firstmate was never told the worker was gone.

This was a regression introduced by this change rather than a pre-existing gap: before it, that path returned `paused` for a dead agent, so a churning dead pane still re-surfaced once per PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS. It went from bounded-but-eventually-surfaced to permanently silent, which is strictly worse than the behaviour being replaced.

The fix brings the third dispatcher into line with the two that review already corrected, rather than inventing a new rule: clearing is reserved for `working`, where an authoritative run supersedes the declaration and the pane returns to ordinary wedge tracking, and `none` routes to surface_nonterminal_stale. That target is what keeps the flood bound intact, because it records the `surfaced` marker, so the next poll returns `paused` and a churning dead pane still costs exactly one wake rather than one per poll.

The regression was proven RED first and fails for its stated reason rather than by timing: "dead churning declared pause was cleared instead of surfacing", while its live half already passed, so the test discriminates. It drives a pane whose captured content differs on every read through the real tmux liveness classifier, asserts that live and churning stays absorbed across repeated polls, then that the same window with a confirmed-dead agent surfaces exactly once and stays quiet across three further churning polls. The once-only flood bound, the dead-agent guarantee, the unknown-is-trusted semantics, and the authoritative-working reclassification all remain asserted by their existing tests and green, the full watcher triage suite passes with 53 tests, and bin/fm-lint.sh is now fully clean including pinned actionlint workflow lint.

The captain ruled to take the finding's own remedy and accept the triage reordering, explicitly relaxing this task's standing no-redesign constraint for that one concrete reorder and nothing wider, and he required the absolute dead-agent wording to stay while the code is made true to it rather than the statement being weakened.

Three review findings against it remain open and must be closed: the preflight covers only a confidently dead agent, so a declared pause whose agent reads alive or unknown still falls through the capture-failure skip and can go silent indefinitely with its bounded cadence never running; the surfaced early return skips authoritative run-step reconciliation, so an active run starting later while the append-only status still reads paused is never reconciled; and the commit history must state that both bypasses are pre-existing upstream defects rather than regressions from this branch, and must explain what the reordering changes about triage order.

That last requirement must be satisfied by the message of a NEW commit. An earlier attempt at this stage failed because the required explanation was added by amending an already-recorded pipeline commit, which the gate correctly refused as an out-of-band rewrite that would have lost the reviewed change. Nothing may amend, reset, or replace an existing commit on this branch.

The reorder's own new regression does not yet pass, so completing it is part of this stage rather than a separate concern. Acceptance is unchanged and every existing guarantee must stay green and be re-run rather than assumed: the once-only flood bound, the dead-agent guarantee on every path including a missing terminal window and a stale busy record, the unknown-is-trusted classification with its bounded-recheck caching, the authoritative-working reclassification, and the changing-hash live-to-dead regression. A failed capture must never be read as death; only a confident dead or missing liveness verdict may invalidate a declaration, and a live or unknown agent must stay absorbed on every newly reachable path so healthy parked workers are not turned back into per-cycle wakes.

TEST COST TAKEBACK, 2026-08-19. CI on the previous head executed once a maintainer released the fork-approval gate, and it carried real information: one shard failed and a second was cancelled. Both were diagnosed separately rather than assumed related. The failure, "concurrent watcher never saw complete poll" in tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh, was caused by this change and legitimately so: that fixture never provided a tmux fake, so capture failed and the window was silently DROPPED under the old loop, and totality now records a verdict and surfaces it, so the watcher exits before completing its poll. The test encoded the old broken behaviour as its expectation. It was fixed by giving the fixture the tmux fake it never had so capture succeeds, leaving its merged assertion untouched; the totality guarantee was NOT weakened to make an old test pass. The cancelled shard was independent of that failure - the shard matrix sets fail-fast: false, proven directly because a sibling shard kept running after the failure and passed - and was a timeout at 15m19s against a 15-minute limit, caused by this branch's added tests growing that shard's runtime.

That growth was split into inherent cost and accidental waste before anything was changed. The waste was the fixed-budget liveness wait, which burns its whole budget to prove a negative; the live phase of the churning-pane test now waits for the pane's recorded hash to advance, returning as soon as a poll completes and asserting strictly more than before. The same conversion was attempted on that test's dead-agent phase and reverted, because a dead already-surfaced pause absorbs cheaply and writes no artifact by design, so there is nothing to observe completing and a bounded liveness wait is the honest instrument; the reason is recorded in the test. The established result is a per-test reduction from 32s to 18s in-suite. A suite-level saving is deliberately NOT claimed: across two runs with only that test changed the suite moved 299s to 315s, so run-to-run spread exceeded the saving and a single pair of measurements cannot establish a delta in either direction. The shard limit was deliberately not raised and the shard partition deliberately not rebalanced, because shard 3 was already at 13m02s before this branch existed, making that imbalance a separate concern rather than this change's defect.

title: fix(bin): preserve declared-pause cadence across pane churn
body:
## Intent Fix a supervision bug in firstmate's always-on watcher: a crew whose latest status line is a declared 'paused:' external wait still emitted plain bare 'stale: ' wakes at short cadence, instead of the FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS (3600s) labeled resurface rechecks that handle_paused_stale in bin/fm-watch.sh is supposed to produce. Field evidence spanned three dated observations and was reproduced live on 2026-08-18 (task carrier-rev-detection, codex/sol, declared paused): bare stale wakes ~60-140s apart, and an earlier case at ~9-minute cadence, with no pause-resurface labeling. The defect was observed to be neither harness-specific nor task-specific. Accepted requirements: (1) root-cause the leak using diagnostic-reasoning discipline - reproduce it with a scripted scenario and compare against the working absorb case recorded for task fm-spawn-codex-tier; (2) fix it so a declared pause reliably converts stale re-fires to the long-cadence labeled resurface, including immediately after a new status append; (3) cover it with a regression test for the append-then-stale ordering; (4) a separate observation in the evidence record - a 61h-old state/.turn-ended marker on a reboot-resumed session, suggesting the turn-end hook may not fire for resumed sessions - must be REPORTED in the PR body as a separate finding if confirmed distinct, and deliberately NOT fixed in this change. Scope fence accepted at intake: bin/fm-watch.sh and its libs' absorb/suppressor path only. Deliberately NOT touched: the away-mode daemon (bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh), fm-classify-lib.sh policy semantics, and backends. This is firstmate's own shared tracked material, so the firstmate-coding-guidelines contract applies (knowledge-placement decision tree, one-owner rule, AGENTS.md size discipline, one sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never em dash, shellcheck-clean bin scripts, tests colocated in tests/ extending the existing runner rather than a new one, and tests must exercise behavior through an executable interface rather than asserting implementation source bytes). What the investigation established, and the reasoning behind the diff a reviewer would not otherwise know: Root cause: the declared-pause bounded cadence was anchored on the PANE HASH rather than on the declared pause itself. pause_state_class never returns 'paused' for a live agent - it returns 'none' for any non-secondmate crew whose backend does not confidently report the agent dead - so a declared pause on a live crew rode entirely on the .paused- cadence flag. Two call sites discarded that flag whenever the pane hash moved: the hash-change branch mapped 'none' to clear_pause_tracking (removing .paused-, .paused-resurfaced- and .stale-), and the non-terminal stale first-sighting branch then saw an unclassified hash and called surface_nonterminal_stale, emitting a bare stale. Every redraw of an idle paused pane (a ticking clock, a token counter, the crew's own echoed output) therefore reopened a "first sighting" and leaked another bare stale about two polls later, matching the observed 60-140s and ~9-minute cadences. This also explains the "not harness-specific, not task-specific" observation: the real differentiator is pane churn, not the harness. fm-spawn-codex-tier absorbed correctly on identical code purely because its pane stayed hash-stable. Deliberate correction to the hypothesis recorded in the task record: the record's leading hypothesis was that a status append moves the status hash and lets plain stales leak before handle_paused_stale absorbs. A disconfirming control run shows that on the UNFIXED code, appending a 'paused:' line to an already-stale pane with no pane redraw absorbs correctly. The status append alone was never the trigger; the pane redraw is. The fix is aimed at the redraw path accordingly, and the regression test still covers the append-then-stale ordering as required. The chosen fix treats .paused- as the cadence record it is already documented to be: once set, a still-declared pause stays on the bounded cadence across hash changes, and the stale suppressor advances to the new hash so a redraw cannot be re-classified as a fresh sighting. Only a 'working' verdict (the crew genuinely resumed) ends the cadence at those two sites; the loop head remains the single owner of ending it when the status line itself stops declaring a pause. A live agent's FIRST sighting still surfaces once - this is deliberate and preserves the pre-existing external-decision-gate contract asserted by test_exited_declared_pause_is_bounded_but_live_gate_surfaces, so a live decision gate is never hidden behind the pause cadence. Deliberate design argument for why this is a convergence rather than new policy: the away-mode daemon already holds exactly this invariant. pause_marker_record in bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh keys its pause marker by task and documents "Recording is create-if-absent so the timestamp is stable across a churny idle pane (many distinct stale hashes map to one marker), keeping the cadence hash-immune." The always-on watcher was the one path that had not applied it. That is also why the daemon is correctly left untouched: it does not share the defect. Documentation changes are deliberate and scoped to statements this fix makes inaccurate: three comment blocks in bin/fm-watch.sh (the handle_paused_stale header, the PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS block, and the 'none' bullet in the non-terminal stale case list), and one sentence in docs/architecture.md whose claim about "an unchanged paused: endpoint" and "only when the backend confidently reports its agent dead" no longer describes the behavior. Per the one-owner rule these patch existing language in place rather than appending new paragraphs. No AGENTS.md change is intended: by the knowledge-placement decision tree this fix is watcher mechanics, which belongs in the script's own header comments, and AGENTS.md size discipline explicitly argues against adding it there. The regression test is deliberately structured in four phases (pre-pause bare surface, the status append plus redraw, four rounds of pane churn, then the aged labeled resurface) and includes an explicit non-vacuity assertion that the stale suppressor advanced to the final redraw's hash, so a zero-leak count can never pass hollow. It was confirmed to FAIL on the unfixed code (4 leaked bare stale wakes) and pass on the fix. Rounds are acknowledged as they go so an unrelated downtime-recovery resurface cannot stand in for the stale wake under test. Verification already performed locally: 266 assertions green with zero failures across tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh (50), fm-watcher-lock (31), fm-watch-arm (14), fm-daemon (99, which matters because the daemon shares fm-classify-lib.sh), fm-wake-queue (19) and fm-crew-state (53); bin/fm-lint.sh clean at pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0; bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh clean. actionlint is not installed locally, but no workflow files were changed. On requirement (4), the intended PR-body finding is deliberately conservative and must not be upgraded into a confirmed defect claim: the turn-ended observation IS mechanically distinct from this bug, because bin/fm-watch.sh reads .turn-ended in only two places - busy_turn_over_age, which is gated on a provably BUSY pane, and scan_signals - so a stale marker could not have produced these idle-pane bare stales, and the symptom it would produce is a different one (a wedge escalation labeled "possible wedge, escalation N"). However it is NOT confirmed as a hook defect: the originally cited task has since been torn down, and on the live home today every task with an old marker is either an endpoint firstmate deliberately closed or a declared pause, both of which legitimately complete no turns. One case is suggestive but inconclusive because firstmate also appends to crew status files, so a recent status line does not prove the crew took a turn. The PR body should report it as distinct-in-mechanism, unconfirmed-as-a-defect, and recommend a separate live reproduction per harness. ## What Changed - Preserve declared-pause cadence across pane hash changes, advancing stale suppression without reopening bare first sightings, and clarify the hash-immune behavior in watcher and architecture documentation. - Add regression coverage for status-append-then-stale ordering, repeated pane redraws, suppressor advancement, and labeled long-cadence resurfacing. - Separate finding, deliberately not fixed: stale `.turn-ended` markers are mechanically distinct from this idle-pane leak and could produce BUSY-pane wedge escalation instead. A resumed-session hook defect remains unconfirmed and needs separate live reproduction per harness. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is narrowly scoped and preserves the declared-pause cadence across both pane-hash changes and subsequent stale classification without weakening resume, AFK, secondmate, or wedge handling. ## Testing Alongside the supplied prior baseline, this phase independently passed the targeted watcher suite, reproduced four bare notifications on the base commit, proved its stable-pane control absorbs, and showed the target emits zero repeated bare notifications plus one labeled long-cadence recheck; the distinct turn-ended observation remains deliberately out of scope and an obligation for the outer PR-body phase.
Evidence: Pause-cadence end-to-end comparison `Base with pane churn: 4 bare stale notifications. Base stable-pane control: absorbed correctly. Target with identical churn: 0 bare notifications, followed by exactly 1 labeled external-wait recheck.` ```text Watcher pause cadence end-to-end evidence Base: 03bb1d8b78a8632ae2d9cea4c10868eb100e885e Target: 59fe27a217b3b1757f6aefea27ee461d42abf387 Scenario: append paused: to a live crew, then redraw its idle pane four times. BASE WITH PANE CHURN - reproduced leak not ok - four pane redraws under a declared pause leaked 4 bare stale wakes End-user watcher output: stale: test:fm-churn stale: test:fm-churn stale: test:fm-churn stale: test:fm-churn Bare notifications: 4 BASE STABLE-PANE CONTROL - working absorb path ok - a declared pause is absorbed on first sight, then re-surfaced as a recheck past the threshold, never wedge-escalated TARGET WITH THE SAME PANE CHURN - fixed path ok - a live crew's declared pause survives pane churn after a status append and only re-surfaces on its labeled long cadence Declared status log: working: waiting on the upstream tool release paused: awaiting the upstream tool release Absorbed paused-stale polls recorded: 16 Bare queued notifications after four redraws: 0 Labeled long-cadence rechecks queued after aging: 1 End-user watcher output after aging the pause: stale: test:fm-churn (paused 500s, awaiting external - declared pause, rechecked on a long cadence not a wedge; confirm the wait still holds) Pause cadence marker: present Wedge timer: absent Result: pane churn, not the status append alone, distinguishes the failing base path. The target keeps the declared pause cadence across redraws, emits no repeated bare notification, and later emits exactly one labeled external-wait recheck. ```
Evidence: Base-commit reproduction `not ok - four pane redraws under a declared pause leaked 4 bare stale wakes` ```text not ok - four pane redraws under a declared pause leaked 4 bare stale wakes ```
Evidence: Target focused regression `ok - a live crew's declared pause survives pane churn after a status append and only re-surfaces on its labeled long cadence` ```text ok - a live crew's declared pause survives pane churn after a status append and only re-surfaces on its labeled long cadence ```

title: fm-spawn: differently-cased project path on a case-insensitive FS makes spawn treat the project checkout as the pooled worktree (freshen can hard-reset a live working copy)
body:
## Summary

On a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS default), passing `fm-spawn.sh` a project path whose letter-casing differs from the on-disk casing makes the spawn treat the **project checkout itself** as the pooled treehouse worktree. `freshen_spawn_worktree_base` then targets the user's live working copy and, if that copy is clean, runs `git reset --hard origin/<default>` on it. In our case only untracked files in the working copy made the clean-check refuse:

```
error: pooled worktree '/Users/joao/Developer/aiXplain/aiXplainPU' is not clean; refusing to discard uncommitted work while refreshing its base
```

The path passed to fm-spawn was `/Users/joao/Developer/aixplain/aixplainPU` (lowercase `aixplain`); the on-disk casing is `/Users/joao/Developer/aiXplain/aiXplainPU`.

## Mechanism

1. `PROJ_ABS_REAL` is computed from the caller-supplied path via `cd`/`pwd -P`, which **preserves the caller's casing** (pwd does not canonicalize case on macOS).
2. The wait-for-`treehouse get` loop (fm-spawn.sh ~2193-2215) polls the pane's OS-reported cwd, which carries the **true on-disk casing**. While the pane is still sitting in the project directory (before `treehouse get` moves it), that true-cased path already differs *as a string* from `PROJ_ABS_REAL`, so two consecutive identical reads accept the project directory as the worktree.
3. `validate_spawn_worktree` (~1668) compares `wt_real != proj_real` with the same casing skew, so it passes too.
4. `freshen_spawn_worktree_base` (~1686) then fetches and — when `status --porcelain` is empty — hard-resets the **project checkout** to `origin/<default>`, and the worker would be launched inside it.

This is very likely also the root cause of the previously observed benign variant where `worktree=` in `state/<id>.meta` records the project path while the agent itself lands in the correct treehouse worktree (timing decides which flavor you get).

## Repro

On macOS (APFS case-insensitive):

1. Have a project at e.g. `~/Developer/MyProj` (note casing), registered outside `projects/`.
2. `bin/fm-spawn.sh some-task ~/developer/myproj --mode direct-PR --yolo off ...`
3. If the working copy is dirty: spawn aborts with the "pooled worktree ... is not clean" error naming the project path. If clean: the project checkout is hard-reset to `origin/<default>` and the worker launches in the primary checkout (the exact tangle the isolation assertion exists to prevent).

## Suggested fix

Canonicalize casing before comparison — e.g. compare device+inode (`stat`) instead of path strings, or canonicalize both sides with a case-insensitivity-aware realpath (on macOS, `python3 -c 'import os,sys;print(os.path.realpath(sys.argv[1]))'` does not fix casing either; comparing `stat -f '%d:%i'` of the two directories is the robust identity test). The `wt_real = proj_real` identity check and the treehouse-wait loop's "pane left the project" check should both use filesystem identity, not string equality.

Preserve the strict delivery_boundary=pr-only behavior and its regression coverage: reject merge, deploy, combined, and arbitrary delivery values; never merge, deploy, self-update, or create another task. Keep the watcher declared-pause and PR-only changes intact. Fix ShellCheck host safety robustly: FM_LINT_JOBS unset must default to one worker, explicit FM_LINT_JOBS=2 and --jobs 2 remain supported, and even one pathological root such as tests/fm-pending-reply.test.sh under --external-sources must not consume unbounded memory or kill the lint parent. Find the root cause, choose a host-safe lint approach that keeps meaningful coverage for that root, and add executable regression evidence. Do not silently skip the root, change unrelated pre-existing ShellCheck diagnostics, or install/action changes for missing actionlint 1.7.12. Use one lint invocation at a time during validation. Update existing PR #2602 only. Do not merge or deploy. ## What Changed - Adds Cursor harness support, crew run-state recovery, inactive-crew reconciliation, and condition-based watcher actions. - Adds PR-only ship preflight records and improves decision-hold, wake, and remote delivery status handling. - Bounds ShellCheck lint batches, adds GitHub workflow linting, and expands regression coverage and documentation. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The Linux memory limit bounds each ShellCheck process, preserves the required serial fallback, and the added regression exercises the fallback path through the lint interface. ## Testing Focused lint regression tests passed. A real single-worker lint reproduced ShellCheck memory exhaustion on `tests/fm-pending-reply.test.sh`, then completed the bounded source-isolated fallback and reported its existing SC2329 diagnostics without killing the lint parent. Focused end-to-end checks confirmed that only `pr-only` is accepted and that a declared pause is absorbed first, then re-surfaced as an external-wait recheck without wedge escalation.

jobs=1 splits each ShellCheck process into bounded one-root batches ok - a pathological source graph is limited and receives explicit serial fallback coverage ok - jobs=1 and jobs=2 stop complete worker trees with and without telemetry ok - 🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-lint.sh:90` - Required criterion: “even one pathological root such as tests/fm-pending-reply.test.sh under --external-sources must not consume unbounded memory or kill the lint parent.” The changed hunk invokes ShellCheck with that single root but has no memory or process limit, so its transitive source graph can still exhaust host memory and be OOM-killed.
