title: fix(bin): honor declared pauses in busy-pane wedge checks
body:
## Intent Task: the watcher's wedge-escalator repeatedly flags a scout that is legitimately in a declared `paused:` state (hosting a Lavish review, awaiting captain feedback) as a possible wedge, generating a stream of `stale:`/`possible wedge, escalation N` wakes even though the worker declared it is idle on an expected external wait. This produces constant false-wedge supervision noise for a healthy paused review scout. Fix: honor a worker's own declared `paused:` (external-wait) state so a review-hosting pause is rechecked only on the long cadence and is NOT escalated as a wedge. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT (do not regress true-wedge detection): the fix must NOT make us miss genuine wedges. A worker that is actually stuck - one that has NOT declared a pause, or whose declared pause has exceeded even the long recheck cadence with no liveness - must still escalate. The discriminator is the worker's own `paused:` declaration together with a liveness signal, not blanket-silencing the wedge escalator. The watcher already partially distinguished this (it prints "declared pause, rechecked on a long cadence not a wedge"); the task was to find why it still escalated the review scout as a wedge (e.g. an early escalation firing before the pause is honored, or the review-hosting pause not being treated as a declared pause) and close that gap. Acceptance criteria: (1) reproduce the false escalation - a scout in `paused:` (review-hosting) no longer produces `stale/possible wedge` escalation wakes and is rechecked on the long cadence only; (2) a genuinely stuck worker (no declared pause, or unresponsive/looping) STILL escalates as before, proven rather than asserted by inspection; (3) tests cover both directions - paused-declared -> no false wedge, truly-stuck -> still escalates. This task touches firstmate's shared tracked material (bin/), so firstmate-coding-guidelines applies. Root cause found by end-to-end reproduction, not inspection. The stale path in bin/fm-watch.sh already honored a declared pause via pause_state_class/handle_paused_stale. A review-hosting scout never reached it: it blocks in ONE long foreground call (`lavish-axi poll`) so its pane reads BUSY, and the stale branch requires a non-busy pane. The separate busy-pane completed-turn bound (BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS / busy_turn_over_age) consulted no declared-pause vocabulary at all and routed the pane straight into wedge_timer_check, re-escalating "possible wedge, escalation N" - and past FM_WEDGE_DEMAND_INSPECT_COUNT, "demand-deep-inspection" - every FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS for as long as the review stayed open. This matches upstream issue #2614's observation that the escalator "damps only panes whose agent process is gone, not live-idle panes in a declared wait". Reproduced first as a failing test that emitted `stale: test:fm-review-scout (idle 2s, possible wedge, escalation 1)`. Fix: a new busy_turn_bound_check owns which absorber takes a crossed busy-turn bound. When the crew's own last status line declares an external wait or a verified captain-held transfer (status_is_paused_or_captain_held, the same shared vocabulary the stale path and the away-mode daemon already use), the pane takes the bounded FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS recheck via handle_paused_stale; every other case keeps the unchanged wedge timer with the identical reason, escalation counter, and demand-deep-inspection marker. The discriminator is deliberately the declaration TOGETHER with liveness - the caller has already confirmed the pane is busy - and never a blanket silencing: a crew that declared nothing, or whose pane is not live, escalates exactly as before, and a declared pause still re-surfaces once per long cadence so a forgotten wait cannot rot invisibly. Deliberate decisions a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: - Away mode is intentionally left untouched (the `! afk_present` guard). While state/.afk exists the away-mode daemon owns triage and its classify_stale already reads the same declared-pause vocabulary and returns a `pause|...` classification, so a queued wedge-worded wake is absorbed there; the watcher must hand off a plain identity rather than decorate one, which an existing test asserts. Verified in bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh rather than assumed. - Both busy-turn call sites now track whether the pause cadence took the pane this poll (paused_bound) and skip the follow-on clear_pause_tracking in that same poll. Without it the busy-pane "real work resumed" clear would erase the .paused-resurfaced throttle handle_paused_stale had just written, turning the long cadence back into a per-poll re-surface. - The non-busy live-idle declared-pause path was deliberately NOT changed: pause_state_class returning `none` for a live agent (so it surfaces once) is existing intended behavior covered by test_exited_declared_pause_is_bounded_but_live_gate_surfaces, which distinguishes a dead-agent declared pause from a still-live external-decision gate. - The change is backend- and harness-neutral: it reads the existing status-line vocabulary plus the existing semantic busy verdict, and no vendor process name, rendered glyph, or banner, so it needs no live-harness opt-in guard. Tests: one three-phase regression fixture on a single pane pins all three halves of the contract - (A) the declared pause on a busy over-age pane is absorbed with no wedge timer and no escalation counter even with the wedge threshold set as low as it goes, (B) past the long cadence it re-surfaces exactly once labelled as a declared-pause recheck and never as a possible wedge, with its re-surface throttle intact, and (C) lifting the declaration on the SAME busy over-age pane restores the wedge escalation, which is what proves the discriminator is the worker's declaration rather than a silenced escalator. The pre-existing truly-stuck coverage (stable hash, ticking changing hash, repeated escalation reaching demand-deep-inspection, and the 3600s default bound) all still pass unchanged. Also included deliberately, and expected to look unrelated in the diff: tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh was already failing on the base commit before any of this change and flaking under load, and the user's standing instruction is to fix test failures and flakiness encountered along the way. All of it was one root cause - fixed liveness budgets (wait_live "$pid" 15/20/30/40) reaped watchers while fm-watch.sh was still doing its bounded startup work, so assertions about post-poll state either passed vacuously or failed spuriously. Waits that describe a poll's outcome now use a new wait_poll_cycle helper that drops any stale liveness beacon, waits for this watcher to write a fresh one, then waits for it to advance, which proves one whole poll cycle completed; the heartbeat test waits for the absorbed heartbeat it actually asserts on rather than assuming one cycle produced it; and every wait_for_exit budget is normalized to the 10s already used elsewhere in the file (a larger budget can only remove a false negative, never weaken an assertion). Three consecutive full runs of the suite are clean. Docs updated to keep current behavior accurate: docs/architecture.md gains one sentence naming the declared-wait exception to the busy-pane bound, and docs/configuration.md's FM_BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS line gains a clause pointing at FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS. bin/fm-lint.sh, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh, and the watcher/daemon/lock/queue/crew-state suites are green locally. ## What Changed - Route over-age busy panes with declared external waits or captain-held transfers through the long pause recheck cadence instead of wedge escalation, while preserving escalation for undeclared waits. - Add regression coverage for paused review scouts, pause resurfacing, and restored wedge detection after a pause is lifted; stabilize watcher tests by waiting for complete poll cycles. - Document the busy-pane pause exception and its `FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS` configuration. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is narrowly scoped, preserves unpaused busy-pane wedge escalation, bounds declared pauses with long-cadence resurfacing, and adds behavioral coverage for both outcomes. ## Testing Reproduced the false wedge on the base watcher, ran the targeted watcher triage suite, and captured an end-to-end three-phase transcript proving paused review waits use long-cadence rechecks while undeclared busy panes still wedge-escalate; all target checks passed and the worktree remained clean.
Evidence: Base-commit false-wedge reproduction Source: [Base-commit false-wedge reproduction](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/blob/dfb52e2b241505202e8196d54cf30d23ece8ab25/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-watcher-honor-paused-review-scout-r1/baseline-false-wedge-reproduction.txt) ```text not ok - a declared pause on a busy review pane was escalated: stale: test:fm-review-scout (idle 503s, possible wedge, escalation 1) expected regression-test exit code against base: 1 ```
Evidence: Paused review versus genuine wedge end-to-end transcript Source: [Paused review versus genuine wedge end-to-end transcript](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/blob/dfb52e2b241505202e8196d54cf30d23ece8ab25/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-watcher-honor-paused-review-scout-r1/watcher-paused-vs-wedge-transcript.txt) ```text PHASE A — live busy pane with declared pause watcher stdout: paused cadence marker: present wedge timer: absent escalation counter: absent PHASE B — same declared pause beyond long cadence watcher stdout: stale: test:fm-review-scout (paused 503s, awaiting external - declared pause, rechecked on a long cadence not a wedge; confirm the wait still holds) resurface throttle: present wedge timer: absent PHASE C — declaration lifted on same live busy pane watcher stdout: stale: test:fm-review-scout (idle 501s, possible wedge, escalation 1) escalation counter: 1 ok - a busy pane under a declared pause is rechecked on the long cadence, and lifting the pause restores the wedge escalation ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - ⚠️ `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh:98` - `wait_poll_cycle` returns success when its timeout expires without observing the beacon advance, contradicting its completed-cycle contract. Tests relying on absent output/state can therefore pass without executing the asserted poll. Return 1 on timeout so callers fail rather than pass vacuously. 🔧 Fix: Fail poll-cycle waits on timeout 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh:848` - `wait_poll_cycle` now returns 1 both when the watcher exits and when its 30-second timeout expires. This caller treats every failure as an exit and invokes unbounded `wait "$pid"`; if the watcher remains alive after a timeout, the suite hangs indefinitely. Check `kill -0` after failure and reap/fail a still-live watcher before using `wait` for an exited one. 🔧 Fix: Prevent poll timeout test hangs ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` - Executed `test_busy_declared_pause_is_rechecked_not_wedge_escalated` against the base commit’s `bin/fm-watch.sh`; reproduced `possible wedge, escalation 1`. - `Executed the same three-phase watcher fixture against the target: declared pause absorbed, long-cadence recheck surfaced without wedge wording, then removing the declaration restored wedge escalation.`
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: Bound watcher triage test cleanup wait
body:
## Summary

- Bound the triage test `reap()` helper to a 5-second TERM grace period, then use SIGKILL before the final wait.
- Added a regression test with a child that ignores TERM and verified cleanup takes the bounded timeout and leaves no child.
- Confirmed the suspected `fm-watch.sh` signal-window mechanism is refuted: the temporary TERM trap records `FM_CHECK_SIGNAL_PENDING`, then the trap is replaced with `exit 1` and the pending flag is checked before `wait`, so TERM is acted on rather than swallowed indefinitely. No watcher signal handling was changed.

## Verification

- `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` passes in 2m36s.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` passes with ShellCheck 0.11.0.
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --all` reached the changed test successfully, but the suite has one unrelated existing failure in `tests/fm-backend-herdr-focus-flash-e2e.test.sh`: “the Part C doomed pane never acquired a stable persistent sleep child process”.

title: fix(lock): make the session lock work on Windows/MSYS
body:
## Problem

On Windows (Git Bash/MSYS) a firstmate home can never take the helm. Every session start refuses the fleet lock with `cannot locate harness process in ancestry` and falls back to read-only, so the home cannot spawn, steer, merge, or drain wakes. It is not intermittent — it is every session, on every Windows host.

Three independent causes stack up:

**1. MSYS `ps` implements none of the `-o` field selectors the ancestry walk depends on.** It accepts only `[-aefls] [-u UID] [-p PID] [-W]`, so every `ps -o comm=` / `-o args=` / `-o ppid=` call in `fm_harness_ancestry_pids` fails and no pid is ever resolved.

**2. The Win32 process table alone cannot answer the walk either.** MSYS emulates `fork()` with a helper process that exits immediately, leaving the child's recorded `ParentProcessId` aimed at a dead — and eventually recycled — pid. A pure Win32 climb dies at the first forked shell, which is the shape of every `bash bin/fm-*.sh` invocation.

**3. Once the walk was fixed, the lock hung outright.** The lock proves ownership through a real symlink (`ln -s`, then `[ -L ]` + `readlink`), but MSYS's default symlink mode *copies* the target instead of linking it. `[ -L ]` is then false for a link that was just created successfully, `fm_lock_points_to_owner` can never confirm ownership, and `fm_lock_acquire_wait` spins forever. That is a hang rather than a refusal, and it takes the wake queue and watcher down with it.

## Fix

`bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh` gains a process-table portability layer:

- POSIX hosts keep the exact `ps -o` calls they always used, byte for byte, so a fake `ps` on `PATH` still drives the library deterministically in tests.
- Windows detection is a lazy capability probe, never a `uname` check: a host whose `ps` answers `-o` is POSIX here by definition.
- On Windows the ancestry climbs the MSYS side with MSYS `ps` — which does know those parents — and crosses the namespace boundary exactly once, at the outermost MSYS process, whose WINPID is real and whose Win32 parent is a live native process. Skipping the MSYS processes themselves is safe: on Windows every verified harness is a native executable, so no harness can hide in the stretch that is jumped.
- The pid published in `state/.lock` is a Windows pid, which stays self-consistent because every reader of it goes through these same primitives.

`bin/fm-wake-lib.sh` sets `MSYS=winsymlinks:nativestrict` on MSYS hosts so the lock's symlinks are real. `nativestrict` is deliberate: a host without Developer Mode now fails visibly instead of silently reinstating the copy behaviour that causes the hang. An operator who already set `MSYS` is left alone.

## Performance

Reading the Win32 table costs a full PowerShell start, and MSYS forks are expensive, so a naive implementation pushed session start *over* its 120s runtime bound. Three changes brought it back:

- PowerShell writes the table straight to a short-lived cache file (addressed by its Windows path) instead of piping ~120KB through a shell variable.
- The ancestry walk is one `awk` pass emitting the whole chain, instead of three lookups per hop.
- The capability probe caches into the caller's shell instead of re-forking `ps` per field per hop.

| Operation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Ancestry resolution | 19.3s | 3.0s |
| `fm-lock.sh status` | 7.2s | 2.1s |
| Full session start | 134s (truncated at bound) | 82s |

The PowerShell invocation also closes stdin and uses a single-line `-Command`: it inherits the caller's stdin and `-Command` does not stop it waiting on that handle, and a `-Command` string carrying embedded newlines across the MSYS argument boundary is read as an incomplete statement. Either one hangs the acquire.

## Verification

Windows 11 26200 / Git Bash, Claude harness:

- Lock acquires cleanly on **6 of 6** cold attempts, with zero leftover claim-lock or owner state.
- Full session start completes in **82s**, inside its bound, with wake queue, supervision instructions, and deferred network checks all running.
- `tests/fm-session-lock-ancestry.test.sh` passes its 4 unit cases — identical to unmodified `HEAD`.
- That suite's end-to-end layer fails **identically before and after** this change (verified by running it against a clean `HEAD` worktree). It builds orphaned POSIX process trees with `setsid` and `ln -s /bin/bash`, which cannot run on this platform at all.

The POSIX code path is unchanged, so macOS and Linux behaviour is byte-for-byte what it was.

## Note for maintainers

I could not run `no-mistakes` for this change: its installer refuses this platform outright with `Unsupported OS: mingw64_nt-10.0-26200`, as does `treehouse`. That may be worth a separate issue — the pipeline a Windows contributor is asked to use cannot currently be installed on Windows.

title: fix(bin): count a trust-registered custom check as supervision need
body:
## Intent Fix a firstmate supervision predicate gap: a firstmate home whose only duty is a trust-registered custom check (bin/fm-check-register.sh) never got a watcher armed, because bin/fm-supervision-lib.sh's fm_supervision_status only counted state/*.meta task records, state/x-watch.check.sh, and state/procevent/*.source when deciding FM_SUP_NEEDED. A registered check matches none of those, so FM_SUP_NEEDED stayed false and the Claude Stop auto-arm believed the home had nothing to supervise, exiting 0 at every turn end without ever arming a watcher. This caused two real outages on the fleet auditor's home: a seven-hour cadence lapse and, more recently, its hand-armed background watcher being reaped. Scope delivered: 1. bin/fm-supervision-lib.sh now counts a trust-registered check - a state/.check-trust binding paired with its state/.check.sh, written by bin/fm-check-register.sh - as supervision-needed (new FM_SUP_CHECKS counter, presence-based like the existing FM_SUP_SOURCES/x-watch.check.sh checks, not full cryptographic re-validation - that stronger check already happens on the actual check-execution path). bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh and bin/fm-guard.sh banners were updated to name "custom check(s) registered" specifically instead of falling through to the X-mode wording when only a check is registered. docs/turnend-guard.md's "Guard predicates" section, the authoritative doc for this contract, was updated to list the new input alongside the existing ones (one-owner rule). 2. tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh gained test_predicate_registered_check_needs_supervision: it registers a real check via bin/fm-check-register.sh in a scratch home with no state/*.meta task record, then asserts fm_supervision_needed reports true and FM_SUP_CHECKS is 1. Verified this test fails against the pre-fix predicate (git show HEAD:bin/fm-supervision-lib.sh swapped in) with "not ok" and passes with the fix. 3. Investigated (do not fix - this was scoped as a report only) whether the watcher's liveness signal can distinguish "this home's watcher" from "another home's watcher running the identically-named script", since the auditor said a naive process check was fooled and telling them apart required reading each process's working directory. Findings for the PR body: - The automated liveness check already has a cheap, correct, already-implemented discriminator that does NOT depend on process name or cwd: bin/fm-wake-lib.sh's fm_watcher_lock_matches_pid/fm_watcher_healthy require the watcher lock's recorded state/.watch.lock/fm-home to equal the querying home, plus a full process-identity fingerprint (proc stat starttime plus the complete NUL-separated cmdline, from fm_pid_identity) - not a bare pgrep/ps-by-name match. So the automated predicate used by fm-guard.sh and fm-turnend-guard.sh was never vulnerable to the same-script-name confusion the auditor hit by hand. - The real detectability gap is structural and separate from cross-home confusion: under the "autoarm" supervision model (the Claude Stop auto-arm model implicated in this incident), fm_watcher_supervision_verdict in bin/fm-wake-lib.sh intentionally skips the identity-matched liveness check entirely and returns healthy purely from state/.last-watcher-beat freshness, by design, because that model's watcher is expected to be absent between turns. A watcher that dies immediately after touching the beacon is therefore indistinguishable from one merely idle between turns, for up to the full grace window - this is the "outage is undetectable from the beacon" behavior described in the task, and it is a deliberate model tradeoff, not a bug to fix here. - Separately, the auditor's own ad-hoc manual check (something like `ps aux | grep fm-watch.sh`) is genuinely fooled across homes that share one tracked code root: FM_HOME is passed via environment, not argv, so the command/script path in `ps` output is identical for every home's watcher process, and bin/fm-watch.sh never `cd`s into FM_HOME, so a process's cwd is not a reliable, by-construction discriminator for that kind of eyeballing (it only happens to differ if the arming script's own cwd happened to differ). - Cheap, correct, zero-code-change discriminators already exist for manual diagnosis too: read state//.watch.lock/fm-home directly (the same marker the automated check trusts), or read /proc//environ for FM_HOME= on a live candidate process. Making a bare `ps`+cwd check reliable as well would need a small watcher change (e.g., an explicit `cd "$FM_HOME"` early in bin/fm-watch.sh) - out of scope here per the brief's "do NOT redesign the watcher" constraint, and should become its own follow-up task if wanted. Constraints honored: did not touch the watcher, the Stop hook mechanism, or the beacon mechanism itself; did not run pkill -f bin/fm-watch.sh or otherwise disturb any sibling home's watcher while testing; loaded firstmate-coding-guidelines before editing this repo's shared tracked material. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-supervision-lib.sh`'s `fm_supervision_status` now counts trust-registered custom checks — a `state/.check-trust` binding paired with its `state/.check.sh` — in a new `FM_SUP_CHECKS` counter and sets `FM_SUP_NEEDED=true` for them, so a home whose only duty is a registered check is no longer treated as idle by the Claude Stop auto-arm and the guards. - `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh` and `bin/fm-guard.sh` gained a `custom check(s) registered` branch in their block reason, banner, and need description, instead of falling through to the X-mode relay wording when only a check is registered. - Tests: `tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` adds `test_predicate_registered_check_needs_supervision` (asserts `fm_supervision_needed` is true and `FM_SUP_CHECKS` is 1 with no `state/*.meta`) and `test_hook_blocks_registered_check_only_home`; `tests/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.test.sh` adds `test_arms_for_registered_check_need_without_inflight`, each registering a real check via `bin/fm-check-register.sh`. - Docs: `docs/turnend-guard.md`'s "Guard predicates" section lists the new input as the one owner of the contract, and `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, `docs/subagent-guard.md`, and `docs/supervision-protocols/grok.md` now point at that section instead of restating a stale input list. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The behavior change is a single presence-based counter added at the one shared supervision predicate every consumer already calls, it fails safe (over-requiring supervision rather than under-requiring it), it has a genuine pre-fix-failing regression test, and no duplicated sibling predicate leaves the reported outage reachable; the only gaps are a stale in-file comment and missing hook-level coverage for the new banner branches. ## Testing Ran the two owning suites (fm-turnend-guard, fm-claude-stop-autoarm) plus the two adjacent supervision-predicate consumers, all green, and added two focused regression tests covering the auto-arm and turn-end-block layers where the reported outage actually occurred — the change shipped only predicate-level coverage. Confirmed the regression property by swapping the pre-fix supervision lib back in: all three check-related tests fail there and pass with the fix. This is a CLI/hook change with no rendered UI surface, so the transcript is the end-user-visible artifact. No real watcher was started and no sibling home was disturbed; the worktree carries only the two intentional test-file additions.

title: fix(startup-memory): measure symlinked memory files instead of refusing them
body:
## The defect

`fm_startup_memory_measure_file` refuses any symlinked path. A home whose `data/captain.md` is a symlink into an existing notes vault therefore gets **no budget accounting at all**: the report aborts before a single file is counted, while that same file still enters every session's context. The guard was silent exactly where it was needed.

Concrete case: a firstmate home embedded in a personal vault keeps `data/captain.md` as a symlink to the vault's own captain file, because the vault is the source of truth and several vault scripts read it. `bin/fm-startup-memory-budget.sh report` then exits with `memory file is not an ordinary regular file` and reports nothing.

## The change

A symlink whose target is an ordinary file is measured through the link, because those are the bytes a session actually loads.

Special-file protection is unchanged: `[ -f ]` already follows the link and holds only for a regular target, so directories, FIFOs, devices and sockets still bounce with their own refusal.

Broken and cyclic links no longer share one generic sentence:
- a broken link is named as a broken symlink, never as a present zero-byte file;
- a cycle is refused through a bounded chain walk, so it neither hangs nor leaks a raw kernel loop error.

Regular files and absent paths behave byte for byte as before.

## Evidence

Live report in the vault-linked home now totals 7480/7500 estimated tokens instead of aborting.

7 new cases in `tests/fm-startup-memory-budget.test.sh` cover: symlink to a regular file, symlink to a directory, symlink to a FIFO, broken symlink, self-referential symlink, two-link cycle, and an unchanged regular-file baseline. Lint clean.

Two pre-existing failures in `tests/fm-on.test.sh` and `tests/fm-remote-job-orphan-reap.test.sh` reproduce identically on a clean base without this commit, so they are unrelated to this change.

title: fm-teardown dies with 'File: unbound variable' on Linux, leaving task metadata behind and generating stale wakes forever
body:
## Symptom

`bin/fm-teardown.sh <id>` returns the worktree successfully and then dies with:

```
/home/dev/utils/firstmate/bin/fm-busy-event.sh: line 107: File: unbound variable
```

Teardown is left **incomplete**: `state/<id>.meta`, `.status`, `.busy-gen`, `.busy-state`, `.busy-state.lock/` and `.turn-ended` all survive. Because `<id>.meta` remains, the watcher keeps monitoring an endpoint whose agent is gone, so the task generates recurring `stale:` wakes forever after it is finished. Re-running teardown fails identically, so it is not self-healing.

Observed on Linux (WSL2, GNU coreutils) after a normal successful task completion — PR merged, worktree clean, nothing unusual about the task.

## Root cause

`bin/fm-busy-event.sh` around line 106:

```sh
mtime=$(stat -f %m "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || echo "$now")
age=$((now - mtime))
```

The intent is "try the macOS form, fall back to the GNU form". On GNU coreutils that fallback **never runs**, because the two tools mean different things by `-f`:

- macOS/BSD `stat -f <format>` = output format.
- GNU `stat -f` = **display filesystem status**, and it treats `%m` as a *filename argument*.

So GNU stat reports `cannot read file system information for '%m'` on stderr (suppressed by `2>/dev/null`), still succeeds for the real path, and **exits 0** while printing:

```
  File: "/tmp/whatever"
```

Reproduction, no firstmate involved:

```
$ D=$(mktemp -d); stat -f %m "$D"; echo "exit=$?"
stat: cannot read file system information for '%m': No such file or directory
  File: "/tmp/tmp.XXXX"
exit=0
```

Exit 0 means the `||` chain short-circuits, so `mtime` becomes `File: "/tmp/..."`. Then `$((now - mtime))` performs arithmetic evaluation on `File`, which under `set -u` raises **`File: unbound variable`**.

Note the bug is invisible until the stale-lock branch is reached (`tries >= 40`), which is why it appears only under contention rather than on every teardown.

## Suggested fix

Order the probes so the ambiguous one cannot win, and validate the result before doing arithmetic on it:

```sh
mtime=$(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || stat -f %m "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || echo "$now")
case "$mtime" in (*[!0-9]*|'') mtime=$now ;; esac
age=$((now - mtime))
```

Putting `-c` first fixes GNU; the numeric guard makes it safe on any platform where either probe returns something unexpected, so a future portability surprise degrades to "treat the lock as fresh" instead of killing teardown.

Worth grepping for the same `stat -f %m ... || stat -c %Y` idiom elsewhere in `bin/` — if it is copied anywhere else it has the same defect.

## Operational impact

Until it is fixed, a finished task can be left with live-looking metadata that produces endless stale wakes, and the operator has to clear `state/<id>.*` by hand after confirming the task is genuinely complete.

title: fix(bin): keep resolved captain decisions verifiable after Done pruning
body:
## Intent

Resolved decision records are pruned before the scout completion gate can verify them, which blocks teardown. Observed 2026-08-17: resolving more than markdown.done_keep captain decisions and then closing a scout pruned the early resolved decision tasks; bin/fm-teardown.sh then correctly refused the teardown because fm-decision-hold verify could no longer find the inventory it needs. A temporary recovery used a separate private tasks-axi config with done_keep=100; that workaround must NOT become the fix.

Acceptance criteria: (1) Reproduce the failure deterministically with done_keep=10: resolve more than that many decision records, close the scout, and show teardown refusing because the verification inventory is gone. (2) Make decision resolution and completion retention-safe, so a resolved decision record survives long enough for its scout's completion gate to verify it, without weakening that verification. Raising or overriding done_keep is not an acceptable fix. (3) Add behavioral regression coverage that fails on the current code and passes after the fix, colocated with the code it covers. (4) Keep the decision-hold lifecycle contract and the teardown refusal intact. The fix must never let teardown accept unverified or unlanded work.

Constraints and context: this is firstmate's own shared tracked material; the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill was loaded and followed (one sentence per line in Markdown, plain dashes, no agent co-author, shellcheck-clean bin scripts via bin/fm-lint.sh, colocated tests that exercise executable behavior). .agents/skills/decision-hold-lifecycle owns the lifecycle contract, bin/fm-teardown.sh owns the completion gate, and .tasks.toml holds the backlog backend config. The captain-private trees data/, state/, config/, and projects/ were not touched.

Deliberate design decisions taken while doing the work, which the diff alone would not explain: Root cause: every hold close (resolve/answer/decline) is an ordinary tasks-axi done, and every tasks-axi done prunes the Done section to done_keep, moving the oldest closed records (never deleting them) into the append-only done archive data/done-archive.md pinned by the tracked .tasks.toml; fm-decision-hold's reads only ever consulted the live backlog through tasks-axi show, which cannot read the archive because its "## Archived <date>" headings are not task sections. Chosen fix: fm-decision-hold.sh reads a record from the live backlog first and then from the done archive, through tasks-axi's OWN parser over a private read-only temp view of the archive in which each "## Archived <date>" heading is rewritten to "## Done" (every other byte is the archive's own); the script never parses task lines itself and never writes the archive. Precedence is deliberately live-first: an archived record counts as durable ONLY when it is done, kind captain, and already carries the resolution record this script wrote before it was pruned; an archived record that is still held or was closed outside the script (no resolution record) still fails verify and still blocks teardown, so the gate is not weakened. Exact close retries (resolve/answer/decline/repair) against an archived resolved record stay idempotent while a drifted decision or routed set is still refused; hold refuses to reopen an archived identity and points at a new decision key; repair reaches only live records (it cannot record a decision onto an archived record, because only tasks-axi may write the archive and it has no verb for that) and says so explicitly; an unreadable archive (mktemp/sed/tasks-axi failure) is reported loudly as a distinct failure (return code 2 with a stderr reason) rather than mistaken for an absent record. The archive path is $DATA/done-archive.md, the same fixed-layout convention the rest of firstmate uses for $DATA/backlog.md and documented in docs/configuration.md; the script does not re-implement tasks-axi's config resolution. Considered and rejected: passing --no-prune on the script's own tasks-axi done calls (does not protect against other closes in the home pruning the records, and would knowingly exceed the configured Done retention), recording a resolution attestation in the origin's meta (weaker than reading the actual durable record and does not help post-teardown completion, retries, or reopen refusal), and re-adding a live copy of an archived record in repair (would create duplicate identities across archive and live backlog). Tests: two colocated regressions in tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh run at the tracked done_keep = 10 (asserted from the copied .tasks.toml): the first answers twelve inventoried decisions through the routed, declined, and answered paths, closes the scout, asserts the three oldest resolved records are in the archive and gone from the live backlog, and proves verify, a later complete pass, every exact retry, an explicit prune --keep 0, and teardown succeed while a drifted retry and a reopen are refused and the archive bytes never change; it fails on the unfixed code with the exact incident message ("captain decision ... is absent from .../data/backlog.md"). The second closes a hold outside the script, lets ten more closes prune it, and proves verify and teardown still refuse, no close path or repair can record an answer, and neither the archive nor the live backlog gains a resolution record. Docs: docs/decision-hold-lifecycle.md gained the mechanism paragraph and a dated verification record (with exact tool outputs refreshed to today's runs); .agents/skills/decision-hold-lifecycle/SKILL.md gained one policy sentence at the risk point ("never raise or override done_keep to keep the gate passing"); docs/configuration.md gained one cross-reference sentence. No AGENTS.md change was needed. Verification: decision-hold suite 18/18, tests/fm-teardown.test.sh 58/58, bin/fm-lint.sh clean under the pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0 and actionlint 1.7.12, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh ok. Three unrelated suites in the --changed selection fail identically on a pristine origin/main export on this box (root ignores chmod 000 in fm-bearings-snapshot, a Pi calm-extension case, and the coverage guard's comm ordering in fm-test-run) and are pre-existing environment issues, not part of this change.


Later accepted captain decisions on this work: (1) the document-step finding verification-record-placement (move the dated verification record out of docs/decision-hold-lifecycle.md into docs/verification/) was APPROVED as-is and filed separately as fm-doc-verification-record-split, so the record deliberately stays inline in this change; (2) the lint gate that exited 127 because ShellCheck was absent on the gate host was approved because the changed scripts are ShellCheck-clean under the pinned 0.11.0 and CI enforces the lint job; (3) the CI monitor of the previous run added commit 906190752011e9e69824b65f618939166fc9e7be "no-mistakes: apply CI fixes" to bin/fm-remote-job-worker.sh and tests/fm-remote-job.test.sh after a pre-existing intermittent failure of tests/fm-remote-job.test.sh ("remote job worker did not report ready after startup", which failed identically on unrelated PR #2627 in the same minute); the captain decided that fix is OUT OF SCOPE for this PR and must be filed as its own work, so commit 08350b3 reverts it additively and the PR must contain only the decision-hold retention work - bin/fm-remote-job-worker.sh and tests/fm-remote-job.test.sh must show no net change against the merge-base, and the remote-job flake is an accepted re-run risk exactly as on main that must not be chased in this change.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh` now resolves a record from the live backlog first and then from the done archive at `$DATA/done-archive.md`, through tasks-axi's own parser over a private read-only view in which each dated `## Archived` heading is presented as the `## Done` section its records were pruned from; the script never parses task lines and never writes the archive, the view is staged in a subshell whose EXIT trap removes it, and every way the archive can exist yet not be read (no temp directory, failed rewrite, unrecognized block heading, other tasks-axi failure) is reported by name instead of being read as an absent record.
- The gate keeps its strength: an archived record satisfies `verify` only when it already carries the resolution record this script wrote, so an out-of-band close still fails verification and still blocks teardown; exact `resolve`/`answer`/`decline`/`repair` retries against an archived resolved record stay idempotent while a drifted decision or routed set is refused, `hold` refuses to reopen an archived identity, `repair` reaches only live records and says so, and `resolve` counts a routed task in either tier as durable but clears edges only on still-live ones.
- Added seven colocated regressions in `tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh` covering pruning at the tracked `done_keep = 10`, a routed retry whose routed work was archived, an archived out-of-band close, a relative `TMPDIR`, an unreadable archive on both the verify and origin-ownership paths, and view cleanup on a killed lookup; documented the retention mechanism and a dated verification record in `docs/decision-hold-lifecycle.md`, added the "never raise or override `done_keep`" policy line to `.agents/skills/decision-hold-lifecycle/SKILL.md`, and cross-referenced the archive path in `docs/configuration.md`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is well-bounded to one gate script plus colocated regressions and docs, every archive-read outcome I traced fails closed rather than passing the gate, both pipeline fix rounds are correct against the current code, and all source-verifiable acceptance criteria and scope constraints hold exactly.

## Testing

I exercised the change at the product surface a captain actually uses: an isolated firstmate home on the tracked backlog config (done_keep = 10), twelve captain decisions registered, inventoried and answered through the routed, declined and answered paths, the scout closed, then fm-decision-hold.sh verify and bin/fm-teardown.sh. Running that identical script against the merge-base bin/fm-decision-hold.sh reproduces the incident exactly (verify reports the oldest resolved decision absent from data/backlog.md, teardown REFUSES and leaves the origin metadata in place); against the change verify succeeds, teardown completes and removes the origin, and the done archive is byte-identical before and after the gate reads it. A control scenario in the same driver proves the gate is not weakened: a hold closed outside the script and then pruned into the archive is still refused by teardown on both versions, with a more precise reason after the fix. On the automated side the full colocated suite tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh is 23/23, each of the seven new regressions fails on the merge-base script with the exact incident messages and passes on the change (verified by swapping only that one production file and restoring it), and tests/fm-teardown.test.sh is 58/58 so the refusal contract is intact. I also confirmed the stated scope constraints: bin/fm-remote-job-worker.sh and tests/fm-remote-job.test.sh have no net change against the merge-base, and no diff hunk raises or overrides done_keep. This is a shell CLI change with no rendered surface, so the reviewer-visible evidence is CLI transcripts rather than screenshots. The worktree is clean and the script is back at b248f76; no transient files were left behind.

Source: [Reproduction driver used for both transcripts](https://github.com/alvarodecamps/firstmate/blob/b6be962a929761b3ec47f2b18889b99d936b1f9e/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-decision-hold-retention-prune/repro-decision-hold-retention.sh)

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end reproduction of the 2026-08-17 retention incident, driven exactly as
# a captain meets it: register captain decisions, answer them, close the scout,
# then run bin/fm-teardown.sh.
#
# Usage: FM_REPO=<firstmate checkout> repro-decision-hold-retention.sh <label>
set -u

FM_REPO=${FM_REPO:?set FM_REPO to the firstmate checkout under test}
LABEL=${1:-run}
export FM_GATE_REFUSE_BYPASS=1   # same exemption tests/lib.sh uses inside a gate worktree

TMP_ROOT=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fm-retention-repro.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf -- "$TMP_ROOT"' EXIT

say() { printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$*"; }
cmd() { printf '$ %s\n' "$*"; }

make_home() {  # <name>
  local home="$TMP_ROOT/$1" t
  mkdir -p "$home/data" "$home/state" "$home/config" "$home/projects" "$home/fakebin"
  cp "$FM_REPO/.tasks.toml" "$home/.tasks.toml"
  printf '## In flight\n\n## Queued\n\n## Done\n' > "$home/data/backlog.md"
  for t in tmux treehouse no-mistakes gh gh-axi; do
    printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit 0\n' > "$home/fakebin/$t"
    chmod +x "$home/fakebin/$t"
  done
  printf '%s\n' "$home"
}

tasks_in() { local home=$1; shift; (cd "$home" && tasks-axi "$@"); }

decisions() {  # <home> <args...>
  local home=$1; shift
  PATH="$home/fakebin:$PATH" FM_HOME="$home" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$home/state" \
    FM_DATA_OVERRIDE="$home/data" FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$home/config" \
    "$FM_REPO/bin/fm-decision-hold.sh" "$@"
}

teardown() {  # <home> <id>
  local home=$1 id=$2
  PATH="$home/fakebin:$PATH" FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$FM_REPO" FM_HOME="$home" \
    FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$home/state" FM_DATA_OVERRIDE="$home/data" \
    FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$home/config" "$FM_REPO/bin/fm-teardown.sh" "$id"
}

seed_scout() {  # <home> <id> <headline>
  local home=$1 id=$2 headline=$3
  mkdir -p "$home/data/$id"
  tasks_in "$home" add "$id" "$headline" --kind scout --repo sample --start >/dev/null
  { printf 'window=firstmate:fm-%s\n' "$id"
    printf 'worktree=%s/projects/sample-scratch\n' "$home"
    printf 'project=%s/projects/sample\n' "$home"
    printf 'harness=codex\nkind=scout\nmode=scout\n'; } > "$home/state/$id.meta"
  printf 'done: report complete\n' > "$home/state/$id.status"
  printf '# %s\n\nThe evidence is complete.\n' "$headline" > "$home/data/$id/report.md"
}

printf '################  firstmate decision-hold retention  ################\n'
printf 'label            : %s\n' "$LABEL"
printf 'repo under test  : %s\n' "$FM_REPO"
printf 'fm-decision-hold : sha256 %s\n' "$(shasum -a 256 "$FM_REPO/bin/fm-decision-hold.sh" | awk '{print substr($1,1,16)}')"
printf 'script version   : %s\n' "${FM_SCRIPT_VERSION:-unstated}"

############################################################################
say "SCENARIO A - twelve answered captain decisions, then scout teardown"
############################################################################
HOME_A=$(make_home retention)
ID=sample-retention-review
cmd "cat .tasks.toml   # the tracked backlog retention config, unmodified"
sed 's/^/    /' "$HOME_A/.tasks.toml"

seed_scout "$HOME_A" "$ID" "Investigate sample retention"

printf '\n-- register twelve captain decisions and inventory them --\n'
for k in 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 10 11 12; do
  decisions "$HOME_A" hold "$ID" "choice-$k" --title "Choose sample option $k" \
    --reason "captain choice $k pending" --repo sample >/dev/null || exit 1
  printf 'Use sample option %s.\n' "$k" > "$HOME_A/decision-$k.txt"
done
cmd "fm-decision-hold.sh complete $ID choice-01 .. choice-12"
decisions "$HOME_A" complete "$ID" choice-01 choice-02 choice-03 choice-04 choice-05 \
  choice-06 choice-07 choice-08 choice-09 choice-10 choice-11 choice-12 | sed 's/^/    /'

printf '\n-- the captain answers all twelve (routed, declined, answered) --\n'
tasks_in "$HOME_A" add sample-retention-work "Apply sample option 01" --kind ship \
  --repo sample --blocked-by "$ID-decision-choice-01" >/dev/null
cmd "fm-decision-hold.sh resolve $ID choice-01 --routed-to sample-retention-work"
decisions "$HOME_A" resolve "$ID" choice-01 --decision-file "$HOME_A/decision-01.txt" \
  --routed-to sample-retention-work | sed 's/^/    /'
cmd "fm-decision-hold.sh decline $ID choice-02"
decisions "$HOME_A" decline "$ID" choice-02 --decision-file "$HOME_A/decision-02.txt" | sed 's/^/    /'
for k in 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 10 11 12; do
  decisions "$HOME_A" answer "$ID" "choice-$k" --decision-file "$HOME_A/decision-$k.txt" | sed 's/^/    /'
done

printf '\n-- firstmate closes the scout in the backlog --\n'
cmd "tasks-axi done $ID --report data/$ID/report.md"
tasks_in "$HOME_A" done "$ID" --report "data/$ID/report.md" >/dev/null

say "where the twelve resolved decision records now live (done_keep = 10)"
cmd "grep -c 'decision-choice' data/backlog.md   # live backlog"
printf '    %s of 12 still live\n' "$(grep -c 'decision-choice' "$HOME_A/data/backlog.md")"
cmd "grep -c 'decision-choice' data/done-archive.md   # done archive"
printf '    %s of 12 archived by ordinary Done pruning\n' "$(grep -c 'decision-choice' "$HOME_A/data/done-archive.md" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
cmd "grep 'decision-choice' data/done-archive.md"
grep 'decision-choice' "$HOME_A/data/done-archive.md" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/    /'

ARCHIVE_A="$HOME_A/data/done-archive.md"
BEFORE_SUM=$(shasum -a 256 "$ARCHIVE_A" | awk '{print $1}')

say "the captain-facing gate: fm-decision-hold.sh verify"
cmd "fm-decision-hold.sh verify $ID"
decisions "$HOME_A" verify "$ID" > "$HOME_A/verify.out" 2> "$HOME_A/verify.err"
VRC=$?
sed 's/^/    /' "$HOME_A/verify.out"; sed 's/^/    /' "$HOME_A/verify.err"
printf '    exit=%s\n' "$VRC"

say "the captain-facing gate: bin/fm-teardown.sh"
cmd "fm-teardown.sh $ID"
teardown "$HOME_A" "$ID" > "$HOME_A/teardown.out" 2> "$HOME_A/teardown.err"
TRC=$?
sed 's/^/    /' "$HOME_A/teardown.out"; sed 's/^/    /' "$HOME_A/teardown.err"
printf '    exit=%s\n' "$TRC"
if [ "$TRC" -eq 0 ]; then
  printf 'SCENARIO A RESULT: teardown ACCEPTED the fully answered scout.\n'
else
  printf 'SCENARIO A RESULT: teardown REFUSED the fully answered scout (the incident).\n'
fi
printf 'origin metadata after teardown: %s\n' \
  "$([ -f "$HOME_A/state/$ID.meta" ] && echo 'still present (teardown blocked)' || echo 'removed (teardown completed)')"
printf 'archived decision records still present: %s of 12 (never deleted)\n' \
  "$(grep -c 'decision-choice' "$ARCHIVE_A" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
AFTER_SUM=$(shasum -a 256 "$ARCHIVE_A" | awk '{print $1}')
printf 'done-archive.md sha256 before the gate ran : %s\n' "$BEFORE_SUM"
printf 'done-archive.md sha256 after  the gate ran : %s\n' "$AFTER_SUM"
printf 'the gate read the archive without writing it: %s\n' \
  "$([ "$BEFORE_SUM" = "$AFTER_SUM" ] && echo yes || echo 'NO - the archive was rewritten')"

############################################################################
say "SCENARIO B - control: a hold closed OUTSIDE fm-decision-hold, then archived"
############################################################################
HOME_B=$(make_home outofband)
GID=sample-archived-gap-review
seed_scout "$HOME_B" "$GID" "Investigate an archived sample gap"
decisions "$HOME_B" hold "$GID" gap --title "Choose the sample gap" \
  --reason "captain gap choice pending" --repo sample >/dev/null
decisions "$HOME_B" complete "$GID" gap >/dev/null
cmd "tasks-axi done $GID-decision-gap    # closed outside fm-decision-hold: nothing was decided"
tasks_in "$HOME_B" done "$GID-decision-gap" >/dev/null
for p in 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 10; do
  tasks_in "$HOME_B" add "sample-pad-$p" "Sample pad $p" --kind ship --repo sample >/dev/null
  tasks_in "$HOME_B" done "sample-pad-$p" >/dev/null
done
printf 'the unanswered hold is now archived, not live: live=%s archived=%s\n' \
  "$(grep -c "$GID-decision-gap" "$HOME_B/data/backlog.md")" \
  "$(grep -c "$GID-decision-gap" "$HOME_B/data/done-archive.md" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
cmd "fm-teardown.sh $GID"
teardown "$HOME_B" "$GID" > "$HOME_B/teardown.out" 2> "$HOME_B/teardown.err"
BRC=$?
sed 's/^/    /' "$HOME_B/teardown.out"; sed 's/^/    /' "$HOME_B/teardown.err"
printf '    exit=%s\n' "$BRC"
if [ "$BRC" -eq 0 ]; then
  printf 'SCENARIO B RESULT: teardown ACCEPTED unverified work - THE GATE IS WEAKENED.\n'
else
  printf 'SCENARIO B RESULT: teardown REFUSED unverified work - the gate holds.\n'
fi
printf 'origin metadata after teardown: %s\n' \
  "$([ -f "$HOME_B/state/$GID.meta" ] && echo 'still present (teardown blocked)' || echo 'removed (teardown completed)')"
printf '\n################  end %s  ################\n' "$LABEL"
```

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:569` - `hold` now refuses every archived identity, including one closed outside the script with no resolution record, and that removes the last non-`--force` recovery for that state. Sequence: `hold S k` -> someone runs `tasks-axi done S-decision-k` directly -> 10 more closes prune it into the archive. `verify` fails (correct), `repair` fails at line 989 ("repair reaches only live records"), and `hold S k` now fails here instead of re-creating the live record and letting `answer` close it, which is what it did before this change. `complete`'s `sorted_key_union` only ever adds keys, so the suggested remedy ("use a new decision key") cannot clear the gate: `k` stays in `decision_keys` forever and `verify_hold_durable` keeps failing on it, so teardown is permanently refused except via `--force`. The message is also inaccurate for this case - nothing was decided, and `absent_hold_reason` (line 325) already distinguishes the two states precisely. Re-adding a live copy is genuinely unsound now (duplicate ids across archive and live backlog), so the fix is a supported recovery verb, not reverting this refusal - e.g. let `repair` record onto a fresh live identity that supersedes the archived one, or split the message so it names the unresolved case and its actual remedy.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:736` - `command_resolve` still reads routed tasks with live-only `task_show`, so the same Done-pruning failure class this PR fixes stays reachable on the resolve retry path. T is later completed and 10 more closes prune it. The retry re-enters here with `resolution_recorded=1` and dies at line 736 with "routed task T does not exist in the active home" - even though the hold body durably records `- T`, which the block at lines 741-746 already accepts as proof for the blocked-by check. No other path can close the hold: `answer`/`decline` hit `verify_resolution_identity` with `(none)` vs the recorded `T` ("records different routed work"), and `repair` refuses because state is queued. The origin is then permanently unverifiable. Earliest supported boundary: use `record_show` for the dep lookup (or skip the live lookup entirely when `resolution_recorded=1` and the body already lists `- $dep`), and do the same at line 754.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:339` - Optional simplification: the `archived_rc=0; archived_show ... || archived_rc=$?; case ... 0)/1)/*)` dispatch is repeated at five sites (`origin_exists_here` 339-347, `absent_hold_reason` 318-330, `verify_hold_durable` 498-506, `command_hold` 566-572, `command_repair` 963-970), and the out-of-band message at line 325 is byte-identical to the one at line 989. title: fm-watch-triage declared-pause test fails when .wake-queue is absent
body:
## Reproduction

Run bash tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh at commit 03bb1d8.

The suite reaches the exited-declared-pause case without creating state/.wake-queue.

The two awk reads then fail with can't open file for exited-declared-pause/state/.wake-queue.

The test finally reports not ok - dead-agent declared pause flooded stale wakes across six unchanged polls.

## Expected

The test should either create the bounded paused-recheck wake queue it asserts against or handle an absent queue without producing an empty integer comparison.

## Scope

This reproduces before the fm-batch-tooling changes and should be fixed independently.

title: feat(bin): add bounded PR delivery loop
body:
## Intent Push PR delivery loop via fork; five captain fixes only; defer secondmate/post-merge orchestration ## What Changed - Add a bounded main-home PR delivery scan that discovers open PRs for registered merge-capable projects, classifies live GitHub evidence, tracks reason-coded holds, and emits a `check: pr-delivery` wake for eligible PRs. - Guard delivery merges against head changes by recording remote PR heads and passing the expected head to GitHub at merge time. - Integrate the delivery loop into session startup and watcher polling, with its wake-handling skill, documentation, and coverage tests. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is bounded and the reviewed durable-fix paths correctly guard merge heads, delivery-state symlinks, closed-PR state, and ambiguous task bindings. ## Testing Inspected the target change from a clean worktree, ran the focused delivery-discovery and guarded-merge suites, and exercised the public delivery CLI in an isolated fake-forge home; it emitted the merge-eligible wake and left no eligible PR in the blocked queue.

title: feat(bin): reclaim Next.js build output from pooled copies
body:
## Intent Make Next.js build-cache reclamation structural instead of something noticed only when the disk fills. Why now, with measured numbers: on 2026-08-18 one idle Artemis copy held a 15 GB packages/frontend/.next on a volume with 11 GB free; reclaiming that single directory took free space to 27 GB. A 2026-08-07 measurement found ~25.6 GB spread across eight copies. This is pure build output that regenerates, so it is the largest low-risk reclaim available, and it keeps coming back because nothing removes it. Two pieces were asked for, and only two: 1. Teardown removes the copy's .next before returning it to the pool. That is where the problem is created: a copy goes back to the pool carrying gigabytes nobody will ever use again. 2. A way to sweep idle copies without disturbing a live one. Explicit constraints the user set: - NEVER delete from a copy whose task is running. A dev server holding that directory will simply rewrite it, and removing it mid-build is worse than leaving it alone. A copy must be PROVEN unowned before it is touched: no owning task record, plus the same clean-tree and stash checks teardown already makes. - Report what was reclaimed rather than sweeping silently. A cleanup that says nothing is indistinguishable from one that did nothing, and the operator needs to know where the space went. - Refuse by shape: do NOT build a daemon, a watcher, a scheduler, or a disk-pressure monitor. The direct path is teardown doing its job plus one sweep entry point a human or firstmate can run. Extra machinery is only justified by naming a concrete blocker in the direct path first. This is a deliberate architectural exclusion, not an oversight. - Do NOT delete anything that is not regenerable build output. Never node_modules, never source, never git data. .next is the target. Other caches worth including must be NAMED with their measured size rather than folded in by pattern. Decisions and tradeoffs made while doing the work, which a reviewer reading only the diff would not know: - One discovery rule lives in bin/fm-next-cache-lib.sh and is shared by both surfaces so "what counts as reclaimable" is stated once. A directory qualifies only if it is named .next AND git ignores it AND its parent is a Next.js app root (next.config.* beside it, or a package.json naming next). Both proofs are deliberate: gitignore status means tracked content can never match, and the app-root proof is what makes "regenerable build output" true rather than assumed, so a gitignored directory that merely happens to be called .next is left alone. - Verified against current Next.js documentation: distDir defaults to '.next', and cleanDistDir defaults to true, so next build already clears that directory itself on every production build, preserving only .next/cache. Removing it is the same operation the framework performs one build earlier. - A project with a custom distDir is deliberately NOT discovered. Reading a build config to decide what to delete would make the deletion set depend on untrusted project code. Such a project keeps its cache until someone names the directory. This is the safe direction to be wrong in, and is an intentional gap, not a bug. - Other caches were measured and deliberately left out rather than swept by pattern, as the user required: a project's .tmp scratch root at ~8.7 GB pooled holds audit output, coverage JSON, browser recordings, and review artifacts - agent work product that nothing regenerates, so it is out of scope. A dist directory measured ~102 MB pooled and is tracked in some projects. .turbo, .cache, .parcel-cache, .vite, and .output all measured zero. - The sweep requires FOUR independent proofs before touching a copy: the pool reports it available, no task record in this home or any locally registered secondmate home names it as its worktree, its tree is clean, and it has no stashes. The pool lease is checked first on purpose: the worktree pool is shared across firstmate homes (verified: two different clones resolve to the same pool), so treehouse's lease is the only ownership signal that spans all of them. The stash check is an addition beyond what teardown does today, because a stash is unlanded work a clean tree does not show and nobody is watching an idle copy to notice it disappear. - Every "could not determine" outcome is treated as "owned": an unreadable or unparseable pool, an unrecognized pool status, a path that is not an inspectable git worktree, or a git command that fails all skip the copy. A missing treehouse makes the whole sweep refuse with exit 2 rather than fall back to the checks it can still make. - A copy whose ownership could not be established is ALWAYS reported by name, even though its size cannot be measured, because the same broken inspection that hides its owner also hides how much it is holding; a size-gated skip line would pass such a copy over in silence. - One race is left open deliberately and documented in the script header: a copy can be leased between the pool reporting it available and the removal running. Closing it would need a lease this tool does not own, and the consequence is bounded - the copy was leased to start fresh work, so it loses output it was about to regenerate anyway. Losing that race costs a rebuild, not work. - The sweep never touches the project clone under projects/, only pooled copies. Firstmate reads its clones and only crewmates change them, and measurement confirmed the clones hold no build output anyway. - Teardown's reclaim runs after every unlanded-work refusal has passed and after the worktree's processes are reaped, so nothing can still be writing the directory it removes, and it is never fatal: the output regenerates from source, so it is never the work product a refusal protects. A test pins that ordering and fails if the reclaim is moved after the pool return. A later user requirement, accepted and implemented: because the change makes teardown DELETE something before returning a copy, the tests must cover a copy that IS owned and a copy whose ownership CANNOT be determined, not just the clean case. Both are now covered - five owned cases and six cannot-determine cases, each asserting the build output survives. One unrelated pre-existing bug was found and fixed in a separate commit, deliberately included rather than left broken: on stock macOS Bash 3.2 (what /usr/bin/env bash resolves to on the machines this fleet runs on), `.` on a missing file terminates the whole shell with status 0, ignoring both the `|| return 1` beside the source and the enclosing `if !`. A missing backend adapter therefore ended fm-teardown.sh mid-run while REPORTING SUCCESS, so a caller records a task as cleaned up when nothing was cleaned up and the safety refusal never prints. Bash 5 returns 1 as written, which is why the Linux CI lanes never saw it and tests/fm-teardown.test.sh's herdr preflight case failed only locally. fm_backend_source now tests the adapter file before sourcing it, through one helper the five backends share; the guard is read and written with eval because that file is also sourced from zsh, where ${!var} and printf -v do not mean what they mean in bash. A new case in tests/fm-backend.test.sh fails without the fix. Three other pre-existing local test failures were investigated and deliberately NOT fixed, because they are host-environment limitations rather than code defects and would pass on CI's Linux runners: tests/fm-kimi-harness.test.sh (python3 on PATH is 3.8.20, and tomllib needs 3.11+), tests/fm-muse-harness.test.sh (macOS SIGKILLs a copied system bash, so the ancestry fixture cannot launch - verified rc=137), and tests/fm-composer-lib.test.sh (half-block glyph matching under Bash 3.2's weak multibyte support). Fixing three more unrelated subsystems would have expanded this task well past its scope. RE-SCAFFOLD, 2026-08-18: this branch was re-created from upstream/main on the captain's explicit ruling and the work cherry-picked across unchanged. The first attempt was branched from the fork's main, so its rebase gate correctly warned that 35 unrelated fork commits (78 files) would enter the upstream pull request. The captain ruled to make that gate's premise true rather than approve or skip it, and this branch is the result: it now carries exactly four commits relative to upstream/main and nothing else. The carried patch was verified byte-identical to the pre-re-scaffold work - the only difference between the two diffs is one AGENTS.md hunk header line number, because upstream's AGENTS.md is longer than the fork's; the inserted line lands in the same paragraph, under the same anchor sentence. A fourth commit was added during the re-scaffold and is part of this change: the suite's fixture commits inherited the host's commit.gpgsign setting, which on the upstream base made them fail to write a commit object and killed the script with exit 128 before its first assertion - a crash that prints no "not ok" line and therefore reads as a pass to anything counting failures. Every fixture git invocation now passes -c commit.gpgsign=false explicitly, so these cases depend on no personal signing key and no ambient harness setting. Deliberately NOT included, because it would import unrelated fork divergence into an upstream pull request: upstream's tests/lib.sh has no commit.gpgsign guard, while the fork's does. On a host that signs commits by default, pristine upstream/main already fails tests/fm-teardown.test.sh (exit 128) and tests/fm-backend.test.sh (exit 1) for that reason alone, before any change here. Those are pre-existing upstream host-environment failures, verified against a clean upstream/main checkout, and fixing them belongs in its own change rather than being folded in here. ## What Changed - Add shared `.next` eligibility checks and a sweep command that reports or reclaims build output only from available, proven-unowned pooled copies, failing closed when ownership cannot be established. - Reclaim qualifying Next.js build output during teardown before returning completed copies to the pool, with dry-run support, explicit outcome reporting, documentation, and comprehensive safety coverage. - Make missing backend adapters return a refusable error instead of terminating callers on stock macOS Bash. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, the changes now fail closed: explicit targets are report-only, deleting targets require primary-worktree identity, and duplicate pool fields are rejected. ## Testing The focused cache and backend suites passed on macOS Bash 3.2 after neutralizing the documented ambient signing setting for the backend retry; direct CLI transcripts demonstrate reported idle reclamation, teardown reclamation, source preservation, live-copy protection, and fail-closed unknown ownership.
Evidence: Cache sweep CLI evidence Dry-run preserved output; reclaim removed only `.next`; in-use and undetermined copies preserved output and were reported. ```text OPERATOR CHECK 1: dry-run on an available, unowned pooled copy sweep: would reclaim 8K from /private/var/folders/r8/cylyt7xd7t50y9x5wc05my380000gn/T/fm-next-cache-sweep.3OKyh7/cli-evidence/pool/1/packages/frontend/.next sweep: would reclaim 8K from 1 copy RESULT: build output still exists after dry-run OPERATOR CHECK 2: reclaim the same idle pooled copy sweep: reclaimed 8K of Next.js build output from /private/var/folders/r8/cylyt7xd7t50y9x5wc05my380000gn/T/fm-next-cache-sweep.3OKyh7/cli-evidence/pool/1/packages/frontend/.next sweep: reclaimed 8K from 1 copy RESULT: build output removed; Next.js config and tracked source remain OPERATOR CHECK 3: pool reports the copy in use sweep: skipped-as-owned /private/var/folders/r8/cylyt7xd7t50y9x5wc05my380000gn/T/fm-next-cache-sweep.3OKyh7/cli-evidence/pool/1 (in use by the pool), holding 4K sweep: nothing to reclaim; 1 copy were skipped as owned (listed above) RESULT: live copy build output preserved OPERATOR CHECK 4: ownership cannot be determined sweep: undetermined /private/var/folders/r8/cylyt7xd7t50y9x5wc05my380000gn/T/fm-next-cache-sweep.3OKyh7/cli-evidence/pool/1 (the pool did not report it available) sweep: incomplete ownership input: one or more announced pool candidates could not be fully assessed for /private/var/folders/r8/cylyt7xd7t50y9x5wc05my380000gn/T/fm-next-cache-sweep.3OKyh7/cli-evidence/projects/app; reclamation refused sweep: reclamation incomplete; 1 project could not be inspected RESULT: exit=1; build_output_preserved=yes ```
Evidence: Teardown CLI evidence Teardown reported reclaim, exited successfully, removed `.next`, and preserved tracked Next.js source. ```text OPERATOR CHECK: tear down a landed task copy holding Next.js build output ●━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ● WATCHER DOWN - SUPERVISION IS OFF ● 1 task(s) in flight, but no live watcher process holds this home lock (last beat: 0s ago). ● Trust the emitted supervision protocol for this harness; do not use shell & for watcher repair. ● This is a supervision warning only; the guarded operation WILL still run. ● repair missing watcher supervision according to the session-start block for this harness; do not use shell &. ●━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ teardown: reclaimed 8K of Next.js build output from /private/var/folders/r8/cylyt7xd7t50y9x5wc05my380000gn/T/fm-next-cache-sweep.yiqbrg/teardown-cli-evidence/wt/packages/frontend/.next /private/var/folders/r8/cylyt7xd7t50y9x5wc05my380000gn/T/fm-next-cache-sweep.yiqbrg/teardown-cli-evidence/project: already current teardown task-x1 complete (window firstmate:fm-task-x1, worktree /private/var/folders/r8/cylyt7xd7t50y9x5wc05my380000gn/T/fm-next-cache-sweep.yiqbrg/teardown-cli-evidence/wt) Backlog: task-x1 just finished. Update data/backlog.md - move task-x1 to Done, keep Done to the 10 most recent, then re-scan Queued and dispatch only work whose blockers are gone and date is due. RESULT: exit=0; build_output_removed=yes; tracked_next_source_preserved=yes ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 5 issues found → auto-fixed (6) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-next-cache-lib.sh:105` - “Never delete anything that is not regenerable build output” is contradicted by checking only whether the `.next` directory itself is ignored. Git does not track directories, so an ignored `.next` can contain force-added tracked descendants; line 163 then deletes them, and a later failed pool return leaves tracked content missing. Reject candidates when `git ls-files` reports any descendant, treating inspection failure as non-reclaimable. - 🚨 `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:145` - “Every ‘could not determine’ outcome is treated as ‘owned’” is contradicted by this pipeline. Without `pipefail`, `treehouse status` may emit valid JSON and exit nonzero while Python exits 0, allowing an `available` entry to reach deletion despite a failed authoritative pool lookup. Capture and check treehouse’s status before parsing, or protect the pipeline with pipefail. - 🚨 `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:123` - “A copy must be PROVEN unowned: no owning task record” is contradicted by silently skipping missing state directories, malformed registry entries, and failed metadata reads; the caller also ignores loader failure. An unreadable registered-secondmate record can therefore be omitted and its available, clean copy swept. Make task-record enumeration an all-or-nothing proof and refuse when any local registry or candidate metadata cannot be read. - 🚨 `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:138` - The required “no owning task record names it as its worktree” proof uses literal `grep -Fx` path equality. On case-insensitive macOS, differently-cased paths can identify the same directory but fail this comparison; if its lease is available or released, the remaining checks pass and a live task’s cache can be removed. Compare filesystem identity, such as device and inode, at this boundary. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:292` - After a project’s pool lookup fails, `RC` changes but no incomplete/unknown count is recorded, so the final output can still assert “no idle copy holds Next.js build output.” That contradicts the requested honest reporting because the sweep could not establish that fact. Track incomplete projects and report an incomplete sweep instead. 🔧 Fix: Captain: fail closed on uncertain cache ownership 4 issues (2 errors, 2 warnings) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:167` - “No task record ... names it as its worktree” remains bypassable because `stat` does not follow a final symlink by default. If metadata names `/pool/link` and treehouse reports its target, the literal paths and lstat inodes differ, so an available, clean copy reaches deletion; a broken final symlink also returns its own inode instead of the required unknown result. Make this boundary compare resolved referents and return undetermined when a final symlink cannot be resolved. - 🚨 `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:124` - The all-or-nothing task-record proof still accepts a syntactically parseable but non-absolute local `home:` and then treats it as absent relative to the caller’s current directory. The shared registry contract rejects such homes as unsafe; here the intended home’s task records can be omitted and its copy swept. Before the absence exception, reject any local home that is not an absolute, resolvable registry path. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:216` - “An unreadable or unparseable pool ... skips the copy” is contradicted by silently dropping dictionary entries with no usable `path`. A status-0 response containing such an entry is accepted as a complete pool and can produce the absolute “no idle copy” summary. Treat a missing or non-string path as a malformed pool and make the whole project incomplete. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:313` - “A copy whose ownership could not be established is ALWAYS reported by name” is contradicted by `[ -d "$wt" ] || continue`. A named pool entry whose path is missing or inaccessible disappears silently instead of being reported as undetermined. Pass it through the ownership verdict so identity failure produces the existing named skip line. 🔧 Fix: Captain: fail closed on incomplete cache ownership 4 issues (2 errors, 2 warnings) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:235` - The required rule that an incomplete ownership check must refuse is still bypassable: both `grep` comparisons treat every nonzero status as “no match.” If `grep` is unavailable or exits 2, an exact task-owned copy can be classified free and reclaimed. Distinguish no-match (1) from inspection failure and return the undetermined verdict on the latter. - 🚨 `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:274` - The malformed-pool refusal does not reject NUL characters. Python accepts fields such as `avail\^@able`, but Bash command substitution cannot represent NUL and can collapse that value to `available`, authorizing deletion without the pool’s exact availability proof. Reject NUL before emitting the line protocol. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:421` - The captain’s requirement that no silent set-narrowing survive remains contradicted: the old `git ... || continue` was only rewritten as a nested `if`. With one readable project and one project directory whose Git metadata cannot be inspected, the latter disappears from `TARGETS` and the sweep can still claim completeness. Record that directory as an incomplete project or refuse discovery. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:464` - If every attempted removal fails, `RC` becomes 1 but `RECLAIMED`, `SKIPPED`, and `INCOMPLETE` remain zero, so the final summary falsely says no idle copy holds build output even though the failed directory remains. Track removal failures and qualify the summary accordingly. 🔧 Fix: Captain: fail closed across cache ownership inputs 3 issues (2 errors, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:530` - The required “sweep never touches the project clone” and task-record ownership proofs are not established by `[ -d "$wt" ]` plus inode identity. `git rev-parse --git-dir` also succeeds for repository subdirectories: a pool response naming the project clone deletes its `.next`, while naming a live copy’s child directory bypasses the task record for its root. Captain, this is the same completeness class after the promised exhaustive enumeration, so the stated boundary calls for removing sweep deletion authority rather than another local patch. - 🚨 `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:698` - A valid free copy can be inspected and planned before a later malformed entry refuses the project. The plan is then discarded without reporting that copy, but `INSPECTED` remains incremented and the summary says “nothing to reclaim in 1 copy” even though its `.next` remains. This contradicts the required honest summary and “ALWAYS reported by name” rule; keep project refusal atomic but treat discarded plans as incomplete, not empty. - ⚠️ `tests/fm-next-cache-sweep.test.sh:1559` - If `FM_NEXT_CACHE_TEST` contains a misspelled or removed test name, every wrapper invocation silently skips and the suite exits successfully without running an assertion. Track whether the selector matched and fail when it did not, so targeted RED/green evidence cannot be vacuous. 🔧 Fix: Captain: prove pool provenance and honest sweep outcomes 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-next-cache-sweep.sh:845` - The required positive proof that a candidate “must not be the project clone” remains bypassable. `sweep_project` accepts an explicit project subdirectory because `git rev-parse --git-dir` succeeds there; provenance then compares the candidate clone root against that subdirectory rather than the actual project root. Thus a pool response naming the clone can pass the worktree-root/registry checks and have its `.next` deleted.
