title: fix(bin): compare directory identity, not path spelling, when resolving a spawn worktree
body:
## Intent The developer (as firstmate, delegating to a crewmate) directed a fix for a path-comparison bug in bin/fm-spawn.sh where two differently-cased spellings of the same working directory (e.g. on a case-insensitive filesystem) could cause fm-spawn.sh to silently launch a crewmate in the primary firstmate checkout instead of an isolated worktree. The diagnosis was already complete: string comparisons of paths in the FM_ROOT resolution, the treehouse wait loop, and the isolation guard all needed to be replaced with device+inode comparisons (via stat) so that two spellings of the same real directory compare equal, without weakening the guard's hard-refusal behavior when isolation can't be proven. The developer required a regression test simulating a differently-cased cwd to prove the fix, required the crewmate to verify isolation in its own disposable worktree before touching anything, and mandated the standard firstmate delivery workflow: branch creation, no-mistakes validation pipeline with gated fix/review responses (never self-applying fixes or committing during an active validation run), and status reporting only at meaningful phase changes. The crewmate additionally found and fixed a second, opposite-direction bug in the same comparison chain (false refusal of legitimate spawns) and added a corresponding pinned test, then began running the /no-mistakes validation pipeline, which is still in progress in the transcript. ## What Changed - Replaced string comparisons of canonicalized paths in `bin/fm-spawn.sh` with device+inode identity checks (`path_identity`, using `stat -f`/`stat -c`) across the project-path resolution, the treehouse settle-wait loop, the isolation guard (`validate_spawn_worktree`), and the relaunch pane-settle check, so two differently-cased spellings of the same directory (e.g. on a case-insensitive filesystem) are recognized as one directory instead of two. - Preserved fail-refuse behavior: an unreadable or empty identity is treated as unproven isolation, which still waits or refuses rather than assuming success. - Added `tests/fm-spawn-path-case.test.sh` covering the primary-checkout-recorded-as-worktree case, the worktree-under-alt-spelling acceptance case, and the guard's continued refusal of a non-worktree-root path, and registered it in `bin/fm-test-run.sh`'s `backend-dispatch` test family. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change replaces string-based path comparisons with device+inode identity comparisons (via a new path_identity helper) at exactly the three call sites the bug report identified, preserves fail-closed behavior when identity can't be proven (empty stat output never matches), removes the now-dead real_path_or_raw helper with no leftover references, passes shellcheck and bash -n cleanly, and ships a well-constructed regression test (skips gracefully on case-sensitive filesystems, pins both directions of the bug plus the guard's legitimate refusal case) that was correctly registered in the test runner's family list. ## Testing Verified the fix by running the new regression test against both the target and base commits: it fails on base (reproducing the exact case-spelling tangle bug where the primary checkout gets recorded as the isolated worktree) and passes cleanly on target, and the full backend-dispatch test family shows no regressions beyond one pre-existing, environment-only failure (missing `tasks-axi` binary) reproduced identically on the base commit. ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Review** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bash tests/fm-spawn-path-case.test.sh` on target commit f76e50a — all 3 pinned cases pass (project-under-alt-spelling not recorded as worktree; worktree-under-alt-spelling still accepted; guard still refuses a non-worktree-root path) - `bash tests/fm-spawn-path-case.test.sh` on base commit f242264 (via a detached temp worktree, cleaned up afterward) — fails exactly as expected, reproducing the primary-checkout-recorded-as-worktree bug the fix addresses - `bin/fm-test-run.sh --family backend-dispatch` (15 test files including fm-spawn-path-case.test.sh and the related fm-spawn-worktree-settle.test.sh) — 14/15 pass; one unrelated pre-existing failure in fm-backend.test.sh's legacy teardown fixture, traced to a missing `tasks-axi` binary and reproduced identically on the base commit - `bash tests/fm-backend.test.sh` standalone — confirmed the pre-existing 'symlinked prefix does not trip the isolation guard' case (adjacent path-identity behavior) still passes, and confirmed the one failing case is environment-only (tasks-axi absent), not code-related

title: fix(afk): prevent repeated Herdr escalation delivery

## Intent

Fix repeated away-mode escalation delivery on the Herdr backend. Reproduce and identify the causal path across Herdr submit confirmation, escalation-buffer retirement, daemon shutdown/flush, and terminal reconciliation, using the observed repeated buffered status/paused-wait digest, wedge marker, stale supervision, and delayed exact-terminal cleanup only as diagnostic evidence rather than prescribing the patch. Ensure a successfully delivered escalation retires exactly once and cannot be re-injected by catch-all scans or stale buffered state. Preserve type-once, Enter-only retry, durable delivery, affirmatively empty composer, and no-loss contracts. Preserve safe shutdown semantics so unconfirmed or failed delivery remains durable while confirmed delivery cannot block SIGTERM shutdown indefinitely. Keep every Herdr lifecycle action inside the named non-default afk-herdr-repeated-escalation-submit lab via bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh, never touch the captain's default Herdr session, and never bypass the helper or use forbidden server-global/direct lifecycle commands. Add executable regression coverage through public interfaces for confirmed and unconfirmed delivery, buffer retirement, repeated scan/dedupe behavior, shutdown during and after flush, and guarded terminal reconciliation where applicable. Keep executable repeated scan/dedupe coverage on the real daemon heartbeat path, scope the Herdr CLI deadline only around supervisor-target existence, composer, and submit transport calls so worker reads retain existing timeout behavior, and require affirmative fm-herdr-lab helper provenance plus a running named non-default lab before Herdr E2E or launch tests perform lifecycle actions. Review every affected supported primary harness and runtime backend, scope backend-specific changes, and document non-applicable axes with evidence. Update authoritative maintainer/runtime documentation and current verification evidence only where behavior or guarantees change, without incident chronology; keep docs/herdr-backend.md as the Herdr-specific mechanism owner, retain operational pointers elsewhere, and remove duplicated mechanism detail. Run focused tests, bin/fm-lint.sh, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh, and safe automated Herdr verification available in the isolated lab. The captain will manually test the UI after the PR is ready and instructed that manual UI testing not be performed here. Preserve every previously accepted pipeline fix commit. Do not discard state, force cleanup, kill shared supervision broadly, hand-edit, cherry-pick, reset, drop commits, force-push, merge, modify unrelated behavior, or weaken any safety contract.

## What Changed

- Make away-mode shutdown cooperative so confirmed Herdr submissions retire through one path, while unconfirmed work remains durable and cleanup cannot resend it.
- Bound Herdr supervisor target, composer, and submit calls without changing worker-read timeouts, and safely stop the daemon's verified watcher process group.
- Add guarded lab and daemon regression coverage for repeated scans, shutdown timing, buffer cleanup, and terminal reconciliation, with updated runtime documentation.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is well-bounded and closes the confirmed-delivery shutdown race while preserving unconfirmed buffers, heartbeat deduplication, transport scope, and guarded Herdr lab ownership.

## Testing

No baseline output was supplied; targeted portable tests, terminal reconciliation, a red-before-green base counterfactual, and guarded Herdr 0.8.0 live scenarios passed after a command-scoped locale correction. title: fix(bin): stop fm-crew-state from false-failing healthy active validations
body:
## Intent Fix bin/fm-crew-state.sh to correctly report healthy running no-mistakes validations instead of false-failing. Changes: 1. Added nm_coarse_status_is_active() treating pending and running as active in the runs-list lookup 2. Added pending case in coarse status handling with detail 'validating (pending)' 3. Added stale-run override: when axi status reports failed but runs-list shows active for same branch+head, report working instead of failed 4. Added CI_READY_LOG_SUPERSEDED variable to suppress ci-ready shortcut when the run provably cannot be the one that appended a checks-green status-log line 5. Changed stale-record override detail string to 'validating (stale-record override)' for audibility 6. Extended CI_READY_LOG_SUPERSEDED to cover coarse running rows (no step detail means we cannot verify status-log's checks-green belongs to current run) Tests updated: test_coarse_running_run_has_no_ci_log_and_suppresses_ci_ready verifies coarse running suppresses ci-ready when no step detail is available. All 46 existing tests pass. shellcheck -x passes cleanly on changed scripts. ## What Changed - Added `nm_coarse_status_is_active()` (treating `pending` and `running` as active) and a `pending` case in the coarse-status handler so a freshly created, not-yet-started run reports `working` with detail `validating (pending)` instead of an unrecognized status. - Added a stale-record override: when `axi status` reports `failed` but the branch's newest runs-list row for the same head is still active, the verdict flips to `working` with detail `validating (stale-record override)`, so a superseded failed record no longer false-fails a healthy crew while genuine terminal failures still surface. - Introduced `CI_READY_LOG_SUPERSEDED` to suppress the `checks green` ci-ready shortcut both for the stale-record override and for coarse `pending`/`running` rows (which carry no step detail), preventing a green status-log line left by an earlier run from misreporting `done`; updated the `FM_CREW_STATE_RUNS_LIMIT` doc note and added/updated tests covering these paths. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-bounded, carefully scoped to the failed-verdict path, preserves the newest-row and green-not-demoted invariants, and is covered by behavioral regression tests reproducing the false-fail and masking scenarios. ## Testing shellcheck -x passes on the changed script; the entire fm-crew-state test suite (60 tests, including the 7 new ones for pending/running coarse rows, stale-record override, genuine-failure safety, checks-green non-demotion, and superseded ci-ready suppression) passes; and a reproducible hermetic driver exercising the real bin/fm-crew-state.sh shows the base commit false-failing a healthy stale-record+active-run crew as `state: failed` while the target commit correctly reports `state: working · validating (stale-record override)`. Evidence: Reproducible hermetic before/after driver script Source: [Reproducible hermetic before/after driver script](https://github.com/RajeshRajendiran/firstmate/blob/84a400d3b1a3d07ec21cc5a0895cb22d66b41216/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-crew-state-false-failed/demo-stale-override.sh) ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # End-to-end demonstration of the fm-crew-state.sh false-fail fix. # Drives the REAL bin/fm-crew-state.sh (and the base-commit version) through a # minimal hermetic fake `no-mistakes` / `tmux` / `herdr` toolbin - the same # technique the test suite uses - so no real no-mistakes install is required. # Prints the helper's actual verdict for the buggy (base) and fixed (target) # versions side by side for the stale-record-override scenario. set -u PROJ="$PWD" while [ "$PROJ" != "/" ] && [ ! title: feat(bin): add guarded user-skill canonicalization command
body:
## Intent

Implement the captain-approved canonical user-skill layout and synchronization tool for Firstmate. Add an idempotent operator command with clear help that defaults to dry-run and requires explicit apply. Canonical user-installed skills under $HOME/.agents/skills; create relative per-skill links for Claude under $HOME/.claude/skills and Codex under ${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills; remove only verified duplicate user-skill copies or links from Gemini, OpenCode, and Pi roots because they discover the canonical store natively. Migrate or reconcile real skill directories only when trees are byte-identical or no canonical copy exists, and refuse before mutation on conflicts, broken or unsafe links, unexpected entries, special files, or ambiguous ownership. Never touch Codex skills/.system, Firstmate repository-internal .agents/skills, public skills/, Claude plugins or caches, project clones, unrelated home files, or additional skills/plugins. Support the registered remote Mac through an explicit guarded registered route that runs the same checks and cannot silently select another host or home; keep plugin distribution separate. Include executable temporary-home tests for canonicalization, relative links, duplicate removal, conflict refusal, .system preservation, dry-run, idempotence, safe and unsafe links, and remote command construction/home binding. Add concise operator documentation with exact local and remote dry-run/apply examples. Do not run migration against the captain's real local or remote roots. Verify one Codex link in an isolated temporary home; because a live authenticated Codex discovery check could mutate captain environment state, record that limitation and keep application conservative. Keep the full operational contract authoritative in the script header/help, with supporting usage in the appropriate operator documentation rather than AGENTS.md.

## What Changed

- Added `bin/fm-user-skill-sync.sh`, an operator command that converges user-installed skills on the canonical `$HOME/.agents/skills` store: it creates relative per-skill links for Claude and `${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}`, removes only verified duplicate copies from the Gemini, OpenCode, and Pi roots, preserves Codex `skills/.system` and plugin installs, defaults to a complete read-only plan with `--apply` as the only mutation switch, and refuses the whole run before mutating on conflicts, unsafe or broken links, unexpected entries, unreadable roots, or managed roots that resolve to the same or a nested directory by filesystem identity. `--remote <secondmate-id|ssh-alias>` routes through a registered secondmate record and `bin/fm-on.sh`, binding the configured host, code root, and remote home with no fallback, and refusing ambiguous aliases before opening a transport.
- Added `tests/fm-user-skill-sync.test.sh` (24 temporary-home cases) covering canonicalization, relative and whole-root links, duplicate removal under default and restrictive umasks, byte and permission-bit conflict refusal, control-character and `CODEX_HOME` separator handling, dry-run, idempotence, `.system` preservation, interrupted apply and preflight reporting, managed-root collision refusal, and remote command construction/home binding; registered the suite in `bin/fm-test-run.sh` under `pure-contract-unit`.
- Documented the layout and exact local/remote dry-run and apply examples in `docs/configuration.md`, listed the script in `docs/scripts.md`, added `docs/verification/user-skills.md` recording the isolated-Codex-link verification and the unverified live-discovery boundary, and corrected the `docs/remote-secondmates.md` remote-write-surface claim to include this routed operation.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The fix rounds only replaced a vacuous test assertion with genuine multi-record host/root/home binding and ambiguity-refusal coverage and refreshed a verification transcript to match the suite exactly; no production behavior changed and the underlying sync command remains fail-closed with a total preflight before any mutation.

## Testing

I ran the focused temporary-home suite for the new command (all 24 cases pass) and then exercised the command the way an operator would, in a disposable HOME: help, dry-run default that changed nothing, explicit apply that canonicalized a real skill tree into $HOME/.agents/skills with relative Claude and Codex links, removal of the verified Gemini and Pi duplicates, Codex .system left untouched, a second apply reporting already-converged, a byte-conflict refusing with both trees intact, and the registered remote route binding exactly one record's host/root/home under a stubbed ssh while an ambiguous alias refused before any transport opened. Everything ran against sandbox roots only — the captain's real local and remote skill roots were never touched, and live authenticated Codex discovery remains unverified as the change's own verification record states. The captured CLI transcript is the reviewer-visible artifact; the change is CLI-only, so there is no UI surface to screenshot. The working tree is clean of test byproducts.

############ 1. Help / operating contract ############

$ /Users/tim/.no-mistakes/worktrees/832fb889ab00/01M0EG441CN960PFMP8TRFA69S/bin/fm-user-skill-sync.sh --help
Converge user-installed skills into one canonical cross-harness layout.

The canonical content store is $HOME/.agents/skills. Claude Code and Codex
receive relative per-skill links in their user skill roots. Gemini, OpenCode,
and Pi discover the canonical store natively, so verified duplicates in their
legacy user roots are removed. Codex's vendor-owned skills/.system entry and
plugin installations are never inspected or changed.

Every local run performs a complete read-only preflight before acting. Dry-run
is the default; --apply is the only mutation switch. A conflict, unsafe or
broken link, special file, malformed skill directory, unexpected root entry,
overlapping managed roots, or ambiguous tree refuses the whole run before any
mutation. An existing managed root that cannot be listed is refused rather
than read as empty, so convergence is never claimed for a root this run could
not inspect. Skill trees may contain directories and regular files only and
must include SKILL.md, and no nested name may carry a control character. A
duplicate is verified only when its tree matches the retained copy in
structure, bytes, and permission bits, and the canonical copy is established
mode-faithfully so that proof holds under any umask. Managed roots are
compared by filesystem identity rather than path spelling, so a
case-insensitive volume or an aliased path cannot present one directory under
two ownership roles.

Preflight refusal is total: nothing is mutated. Once --apply begins executing
the accepted plan, each step is re-verified against the live filesystem and a
step that no longer matches the plan stops the run there, leaving the earlier
steps applied. Each step is individually safe and convergent, so rerunning the
command after resolving the interference replans from the current state.

Remote operation is routed only through a registered remote secondmate record
and bin/fm-on.sh, which binds the configured SSH host, code root, and remote
home without fallback. It executes this same tracked script in the remote
account. Plugin distribution remains a separate operation.

Usage:

  fm-user-skill-sync.sh --remote <secondmate-id|ssh-alias> [--dry-run|--apply]

Environment:

  CODEX_HOME  Optional absolute Codex home (default: $HOME/.codex).

  $HOME/.agents/skills                 canonical content
  $HOME/.claude/skills                 relative links

  $HOME/.config/opencode/skills        duplicate cleanup only
  $HOME/.opencode/skills               duplicate cleanup only
  $HOME/.pi/agent/skills               duplicate cleanup only

############ 2. Default is dry-run (docs: bin/fm-user-skill-sync.sh) ############

If the remote account sets `CODEX_HOME` in its shell profile, the run creates per-skill links under an unused `~/.codex/skills`, leaves the real Codex skills root unscanned and unreconciled, and prints "user skills converged". The glob at line 458 picks up `.DS_Store`; its name passes the charset check at line 462 (only `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`), it is neither a link nor a directory, so line 471 dies with "unexpected entry in managed skill root". This fails closed and matches the intent's "refuse on unexpected entries", so it is safe — but it makes the command unrunnable on a Finder-visited `~/.claude/skills` or `~/.agents/skills` until the operator manually removes the file, and the diagnostic does not say that removing it is the resolution. The same file nested inside one copy of a skill tree also turns an otherwise byte-identical duplicate into a "conflicting skill trees" refusal. title: feat(bearings): add interactive Lavish fleet board
body:
## Intent Build the captain-approved /bearings lavish mode for firstmate: an interactive Lavish fleet board the captain acts on directly, per the design proposal iterated with the captain at data/bearings-lavish-design-s1/report.md (its section 8 is the implementation spec). Scope, all approved by the captain: (1) a shipped reusable board template at .agents/skills/bearings/assets/board-template.html - the captain approved this exact mockup visual design (myfirstmate design system inlined, Captain's Call as a one-card-at-a-time stack with counter and auto-deal, dispatch picker on Charted Next, repo names never internal task ids on rows) - with ONE JSON data slot (fm-bearings-board.v1) plus a fail-closed schema guard that renders an error card, so per-invocation agent work is composing the payload only, never authoring UI; (2) a new bin/fm-bearings-board.sh owning build mechanics: fail-closed payload validation via jq, slot injection with a round-trip check and backslash-u003c escaping of angle brackets so a string in payload text cannot terminate the data block, a stable board path ($FM_HOME/.lavish/bearings-board.html keeps the Lavish session URL and canonical source id stable), any-origin bind ALWAYS before arm (deterministic enforcement of the bind-before-arm rule instead of agent memory), and arm-if-absent via the existing fm-procevent-lavish adapter; (3) captain ruling Option B for cross-origin keyed answers: raise fm-procevent-lavish.sh's question-key cap from 64 to 128 chars (real full hold identities measure 69-81; the slug-shape security property is unchanged) and add an any-origin binding mode to fm-decision-hold.sh - bind --any-origin records an '(any)' marker (parentheses cannot collide with slug origins, same trick as the existing '(none)' routed token), binding prints the marker verbatim and answers accepts it, so fm-procevent.sh's feed seam needs ZERO changes; in any-origin mode each key is a full hold identity split at its FIRST -decision- occurrence (origins containing -decision- are documented as unsupported for any-origin and keep per-origin bind), keys with no separator (merge./dispatch. board instructions) are skipped and feed nothing BY DESIGN so non-decision answers structurally cannot touch the hold ledger, and every existing close guard (routed-work skip, idempotent replay, absent-hold skip) applies unchanged through the same one intake; (4) captain ruling on merge authority, documented in the bearings skill: a board 'Merge now' answer IS the captain's explicit merge word for that one exact PR with mandatory safeguards - PR resolved from the task's own state/.meta pr= record never from board bytes, wake-time re-verification that the PR is open and CI-green, refuse red or changed PRs, merge only through bin/fm-pr-merge.sh, chat echo with the full PR URL; only the exact answer value 'merge' authorizes, a freeform note makes it instruction text; (5) .agents/skills/bearings/SKILL.md documents the lavish invocation option (explicit option like 'file', composes with include PRs), board payload composition rules, board-wake handling, and keeps the four-section chat contract unchanged (lavish mode still renders the digest with the board URL inline); one-line board-wake routing trigger added to process-event-sources SKILL.md and a one-sentence any-origin mention in decision-hold-lifecycle SKILL.md (one-owner rule: the script headers own the mechanics). Tests are deliberate: tests/fm-bearings-board.test.sh (payload refusals, injection round-trip through the built page asserting the builder's owned output artifact, bind-before-arm, idempotent re-arm, template slot integrity) plus an any-origin test in tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh that drives the REAL runner feed seam end to end (cross-origin closure, an 81-char identity through the adapter's executable interface, 129-char and non-slug refusals, routed-work and nonexistent-identity skips, idempotent replay); fm-test-run.sh maps the new test file into the pure-contract-unit family (CI's coverage guard requires complete inventory). This changes shared bin/ and skills the whole fleet relies on: homes pick it up after merge plus a firstmate self-update, and landing timing is coordinated with the main firstmate. Design deliverables (report.md, mockups) live in gitignored data/ and are deliberately NOT in this diff. ## What Changed - Add the reusable Lavish fleet board template and builder with strict payload validation, safe JSON injection, a stable session path, bind-before-arm ordering, and idempotent registration. - Extend decision handling with any-origin bindings and full hold-identity keys while preserving existing closure guards and isolating non-decision answers. - Document lavish invocation and wake handling, including guarded merge and dispatch actions, with regression coverage for board builds and cross-origin answers. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The changes are well-guarded, satisfy the stated intent, and include behavior-level coverage for the shared routing and ordering invariants. ## Testing The focused board-builder and decision-hold lifecycle tests passed, including validation, safe injection, bind-before-arm, idempotent re-arm, cross-origin closure, length limits, and ledger guards; manual Chrome verification also showed the rendered fleet board and working Captain's Call auto-deal interaction. - Evidence: [Rendered Bearings fleet board](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/blob/8a7ccd407c090eb9555d7bf5bd7ba5160e2e8ffe/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/bearings-lavish-design-s1/bearings-board.png) - Evidence: [Captain's Call after queueing an answer and auto-dealing the merge card](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/blob/8a7ccd407c090eb9555d7bf5bd7ba5160e2e8ffe/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/bearings-lavish-design-s1/bearings-board-auto-deal.png)
Evidence: Board build, any-origin binding, and arming transcript Source: [Board build, any-origin binding, and arming transcript](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/blob/8a7ccd407c090eb9555d7bf5bd7ba5160e2e8ffe/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/bearings-lavish-design-s1/board-build-transcript.txt) ```text board: /tmp/fm-board-evidence.h0dZZF/.lavish/bearings-board.html served: /tmp/fm-board-evidence.h0dZZF/.lavish/bearings-board.html bound: lavish-dfb77f484347927e (any-origin) armed: lavish-dfb77f484347927e ```
Evidence: Browser interaction before/after auto-deal record Source: [Browser interaction before/after auto-deal record](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/blob/8a7ccd407c090eb9555d7bf5bd7ba5160e2e8ffe/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/bearings-lavish-design-s1/board-interaction.txt) ```text Before queue: Choose the release course (card 1 of 3) After queue: Merge: responsive chart renderer (card 2 of 3 · 1 answered) ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 5 issues found → auto-fixed (6) ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-bearings-board.sh:77` - The required “fail-closed payload validation via jq” is incomplete: Captain's Call options are only checked to be an array. A payload option such as {"label":"Approve"} passes validation, but line 490 converts its missing value to the answer "undefined", allowing a captain click to durably close a hold with the wrong answer. Validate every renderer-consumed field and type-specific invariant at this builder boundary. - 🚨 `.agents/skills/bearings/assets/board-template.html:576` - The required criterion “repo names never internal task ids on rows” is contradicted by explicit `t.repo || t.id` fallbacks here and at lines 591 and 633. Because the builder does not require row repos, valid payloads can expose internal IDs. Require repo values and remove the ID display fallbacks while retaining IDs only for dispatch routing. - 🚨 `.agents/skills/process-event-sources/SKILL.md:85` - Board-wake routing recognizes a bearings board only when the result contains `merge.` or `dispatch.` keys. A board submission containing only full hold-identity decision answers therefore follows generic Lavish handling: the runner closes the hold, but bearings handling is not loaded, so the required fresh rebuild and chat action echo do not occur. Route wakes by the stable board source/artifact identity rather than by optional answer kinds. - 🚨 `.agents/skills/bearings/SKILL.md:140` - The supervision section says the skill changes no fleet state and explicitly forbids merging or dispatching, contradicting the required board-wake handling at lines 84-99 that directs this same skill to dispatch selected work and execute captain-authorized merges. This creates ambiguous operational authority at the security-sensitive wake path; scope the read-only rule to digest/build invocation and explicitly permit the guarded wake-time actions. - ⚠️ `.agents/skills/bearings/assets/board-template.html:550` - A valid payload with `captains_call: []` reaches `showCard(0)` with no cards and renders “card 1 of 0” over an empty decorative stack instead of a Captain's Call empty state. Handle the zero-card state before applying stack indexing/navigation. 🔧 Fix: Harden bearings board validation and wake handling 3 issues (2 errors, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-bearings-board.sh:76` - The required key routing contract is not enforced: validation accepts a `type:"merge"` card whose key is a full decision-hold identity. Clicking its `merge` option then reaches the any-origin intake and closes that decision hold, while wake handling does not recognize it as `merge.<task-id>`. Enforce the required type/key namespaces at this builder boundary, including the merge card's exact authorization option. - 🚨 `.agents/skills/bearings/assets/board-template.html:411` - The required template-level “fail-closed schema guard that renders an error card” checks only the schema name. Parseable malformed data such as `captains_call:null` passes this guard and then throws at `.length`, leaving a broken page rather than the error card. Validate renderer-required structure before rendering and route any rendering exception through `renderBoardError`. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-bearings-board.sh:89` - `pr_url` is accepted as any string and assigned directly to anchor `href` values. A payload containing `javascript:` or another active scheme passes validation and creates a captain-clickable unsafe link. Require full HTTPS URLs for Captain's Call and Landed PR links at the payload boundary. 🔧 Fix: Require HTTPS for bearings board PR links 3 errors still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-bearings-board.sh:81` - Validation still does not enforce the documented routing contract: a `type:"merge"` card may use a full decision-hold identity as its key and omit the exact `merge` option. Selecting an option on such a card can close that hold through the any-origin intake instead of reaching guarded `merge.<task-id>` handling. Require full hold identities for decision/credential cards, `merge.<task-id>` for merge cards, and an exact `merge` authorization option on merge cards. - 🚨 `.agents/skills/bearings/assets/board-template.html:411` - The required template-level fail-closed schema guard checks only the schema name. Parseable malformed data such as `{"schema":"fm-bearings-board.v1","captains_call":null}` passes and then throws at line 428, leaving a broken page instead of the required error card. Validate renderer-required structure before rendering and catch rendering failures through `renderBoardError`. - 🚨 `.agents/skills/bearings/assets/board-template.html:532` - Captain input can exceed the adapter's 512-character answer contract without an error: decision notes are silently truncated here, changing the durable answer, while a dispatch selection whose comma-joined IDs exceed 512 characters is queued at line 665 but completely omitted by `fm-procevent-lavish.sh answers`. Enforce the protocol bound visibly without truncating captain text, and bound or chunk dispatch selections so every queued action survives extraction. 🔧 Fix: Fail closed and bound bearings board answers 1 error still open: - 🚨 `.agents/skills/bearings/assets/board-template.html:547` - The 512 limit counts JavaScript UTF-16 code units, while `fm-procevent-lavish.sh` reads the result as bytes and applies Perl `length`. title: feat(bin): refuse merges whose evidence commit is not the PR head
body:
## Intent

Turn a merge-time check that firstmate currently performs BY HAND into a guard that cannot be skipped: refuse a merge when the evidence a worker reported was measured on a commit that is no longer the pull request's head.

Problem, with real instances: a worker measures its full-suite figure and the standing injection-exploit result, reports them, and the validation pipeline then commits AGAIN on top (a fix round, a document step, or a rebase onto a newer base). The figures in the report and in the PR description now describe a commit that is no longer the head that would merge. Observed four times across 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-09, and again on 2026-08-19. In each case a reported suite figure described a commit that a later fix round, document step or rebase had already superseded; one was overtaken twice. Every one was caught only because the reported commit was compared against the live head by hand.

Why it matters: the reported suite figure and the security-check result are the two things firstmate verifies before a merge, precisely because the pipeline has been observed declaring checks-passed on a red suite, and because a target repository may have no automated checks configured at all. A figure that silently describes an earlier commit turns that verification into theatre.

Approach, and what is explicitly NOT the fix: more discipline is not the fix - instructing every brief to "re-measure on the final head" has already been done and still loses the race, because the pipeline can commit after the worker's last action. The guard lives in firstmate's own merge path: bin/fm-pr-merge.sh refuses when the commit the evidence was measured on does not equal the pull request's head. The reported commit is recorded machine-readably in the durable task record (state/<id>.meta) rather than the PR body, so the guard reads a record firstmate owns and no PR-description edit can forge. A guard that refuses must state exactly which commit it expected and which it found, or it will be worked around rather than fixed; the refusal message says what to re-measure and on which commit.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A merge attempt whose recorded evidence commit differs from the live PR head is REFUSED, with both commits named in the message.
2. A merge attempt whose evidence commit matches the head proceeds unchanged.
3. The guard does not fire spuriously when no evidence commit has been recorded yet; that case refuses loudly rather than passing silently, and the refusal is documented and clearable by recording the measurement.
4. bin/fm-brief.sh's scaffolds require the worker to record the commit its figures were measured on, in the form the guard reads.
5. Colocated shell tests cover matching commit, mismatched commit, and absent record, exercising the real script rather than a re-implementation.
6. shellcheck clean on every bin/ script touched.

Constraints: push remote is the fork clca/firstmate; the PR opens from that fork into kunchenguid/firstmate base main; never push to kunchenguid/firstmate; never force-push any branch but this one; never add an agent name as a commit co-author; do not touch projects/, data/, state/, or config/.

ACCEPTED DECISIONS ALREADY APPLIED AND COMMITTED - do not re-litigate these; they are settled requirements in their current form:

A. Identity-record parse SHAPE is deliberately tolerant, by decision. Three separate scripts append keys after pr= in state/<id>.meta - bin/fm-evidence-record.sh (evidence_head=, evidence_note=), bin/fm-spawn.sh (traceparent=, control_relaunch_tx=), and bin/fm-decision-hold.sh (decisions_reviewed=, decision_keys=) - and nothing prevents a fourth. An enumerated allowlist was wrong three times running, and each future appender would be a latent refusal of a merge on valid work. So the parser tolerates any well-formed key=value line it does not recognise. Tolerance is NOT laxity: a line that is not key=value at all, a second pr=, an invalid pr_head=, or a truncated record are still refused loudly, and the keys the guard reads (pr=, evidence_head=) are still located correctly regardless of what surrounds them. A regression test parses and merges a record carrying a key the parser has never seen. Do not propose narrowing this back to an allowlist or adding another named key.

B. merge-head TOCTOU: KEEP the local comparison. gh pr merge --match-head-commit exists, but bin/fm-pr-merge.sh merges through gh-axi pr merge, whose flag set has no head-match flag, and routing around gh-axi to plain gh contradicts the standing instruction to use gh-axi for GitHub operations. The gh-axi-side change is filed separately. The remaining window is seconds rather than the hours the manual habit left open, which is a strict improvement. Do not propose a partial atomic-merge implementation.

C. Evidence writes are interrupt-safe: fm_pr_evidence_write and bin/fm-evidence-record.sh mirror the cleanup trap bin/fm-pr-check.sh already wraps around the same operation, so two writers of one record do not have asymmetric interrupt behaviour.

D. Unconfirmable-head refusals are split: "gh is not on PATH" and "gh could not answer" are distinct messages with distinct actionable fix lines, so a host with gh-axi but no plain gh is not worse off than before this change and is not pointed at gh auth status to diagnose a missing binary.

E. bin/fm-brief.sh's definition of done records the measured commit BEFORE any finishing line, and recording is part of the finishing condition rather than an appendix, in both PR-based modes; a worker reading in order can no longer stop before reaching the instruction the guard depends on. The scout, local-only, and charter variants were checked and have no such ordering problem. A colocated assertion pins the ordering and the condition.

Known-good measurement carried forward: on commit 4268fc9 the full suite is 2259 pass / 11 fail across 150 suites, and all 11 failures reproduce unchanged at base 81bcb10 with the same assertions, so this change introduces zero new failures. The pre-existing failing suites are arm-pretool-check, backend-orca, composer-lib, gotmp, muse-harness, remote-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e, remote-secondmate-trace-context, teardown, turnend-guard, wake-queue, and watcher-lock.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` now runs an evidence guard before it records any state or arms any poll: it reads the task's `evidence_head=` from `state/<id>.meta`, fetches the pull request's live head, and refuses when the two differ (printing both commits, the recorded note, and the re-record command), when no evidence commit is recorded, when the record is malformed, and when the head cannot be confirmed — with separate messages for `gh` missing from PATH and `gh` failing to answer.
- New `bin/fm-evidence-record.sh` is the only writer of that record, backed by `fm_pr_evidence_read`/`fm_pr_evidence_write`/`fm_pr_evidence_note_valid` in `bin/fm-pr-lib.sh`, which replace the record atomically under the shared per-task metadata lock with an interrupt-safe cleanup trap, validate the SHA, and bound the optional note to one control-character-free line of 200 characters (non-ASCII allowed, counted by character). `fm_pr_metadata_identity_parse` now tolerates any well-formed `key=value` line after `pr=` instead of an enumerated allowlist, while still refusing non-record lines, a second `pr=`, and an invalid `pr_head=`.
- `bin/fm-brief.sh` emits an evidence-recording section in both PR-based ship scaffolds (`no-mistakes` and `direct-PR`), shell-quoted and bound to the scaffolding `FM_HOME`/state directory, placed above every finishing line and folded into the definition of done; `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/scripts.md` document the guard and its remedy, and tests add `tests/fm-evidence-record.test.sh` plus new cases in the merge, brief, and PR-identity suites covering matching, mismatched, absent, and unconfirmable heads against the real scripts (registered in `bin/fm-test-run.sh`'s `pr-forge` family).

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is well-bounded and fail-closed by design: every new refusal happens before any state is written or poll armed, the tolerant metadata parse was verified to still reject the injection shapes it claims to (second `pr=`, non-record lines) while surviving `fm-spawn.sh`'s relaunch rewrite, tests drive the real scripts rather than re-implementations, and every source-verifiable acceptance criterion checks out - the three remaining findings are informational nits, none of which affects the guard's decision on a normally configured host.

## Testing

Baseline targeted suites (fm-pr-merge, fm-evidence-record, fm-brief, fm-pr-check-security) all passed, and the lane coverage guard accepts the new suite. On top of that I drove the real bin/fm-pr-merge.sh and bin/fm-evidence-record.sh through a sandboxed replay of that incident: the merge refuses when nothing is recorded, proceeds when the recorded commit is the live head, and refuses naming both the measured commit and the moved head after a simulated pipeline commit — with no gh-axi merge submitted on any refusal. The refusal's printed recording command was executed verbatim from a shell carrying none of the merge's environment and cleared the block, proving the guard is escapable only by re-measuring. I also confirmed the tolerant metadata parse (an unseen key keeps the armed poll valid and merges; a non-record line is refused) and the two distinct unconfirmable-head refusals for a failing gh versus an absent gh, and captured real generated briefs showing the recording section above every finishing line in both PR-based modes. Evidence is two CLI transcripts in the evidence directory. Criterion 6 (shellcheck) was deliberately not exercised: this phase is barred from running linters and the lint phase owns it. No UI surface is involved, so no visual artifact applies.

# Definition of done
Delivery contract: mode=no-mistakes
The task is complete only when committed on your branch AND the commit your reported verification was measured on is recorded.

## Record the commit your evidence was measured on
Whatever you report as verification - a full-suite figure, a targeted test result, an exploit that stays blocked, a benchmark - firstmate merges on the strength of it, so it must name the commit it describes.
Immediately after each such run, from this worktree, record it:

`` `
Record it again after EVERY re-measurement, and after anything that moves your branch head - a review fix round, a documentation commit, a rebase onto a newer base - because your earlier figures then describe a commit that is no longer the head.
The merge refuses when the recorded commit is not the pull request's head, and it refuses when nothing is recorded, so an unrecorded measurement stops the task rather than shipping unverified.

When you believe it is complete, append `done: {summary}` to the status file and stop.
Firstmate will then instruct you to run /no-mistakes to validate and ship a PR.

You drive no-mistakes by responding to its gates, not by implementing fixes.
Follow the guidance no-mistakes itself provides for the mechanics: it loads when you invoke /no-mistakes, and `no-mistakes axi run --help` plus the `help` lines in each `axi` response are authoritative and version-matched to the installed binary.
When starting no-mistakes, make `--intent` preserve all relevant content from this brief's `# Task` section plus every later accepted Firstmate requirement, clarification, constraint, exclusion, and supersession, carrying only each requirement's current accepted form; retain direct requirements instead of substituting a diff summary, and exclude generic operational, status, delivery, and other scaffold boilerplate unless it is task-specific.

title: fix(backends): accept Orca's composite worktree id in endpoint validation
body:
**TL;DR:** Cleaning up or controlling a task that ran through Orca no longer gets refused, so finished tasks stop piling up as stale working copies. ## The problem Before Firstmate cleans up a task or interrupts it, it checks the task's saved record to be sure it is acting on the right thing. That check only allowed a narrow set of characters in the saved worktree id. Orca's worktree id does not fit in that set. Orca identifies a worktree as its repo id, two colons, then the full path, like `1fa7dc1c-...::/Users/glen/orca/workspaces/platform/fm-my-task`. So the check rejected the record and refused, every time, for every task run through Orca. The visible result: cleanup refused to run, and finished Orca tasks left their working copies behind. Interrupting, exiting, or relaunching an Orca task was blocked the same way. ## The solution The identity check now understands Orca's two-part id: a repo id, then `::`, then an absolute path. - Records that use Orca's real id format pass, so cleanup and control work on them. - Bad values are still rejected: a missing half, a second `::`, a relative path, or control characters. - Plain single-part ids still pass, so older records keep working. - No other runtime's checks changed. ## Before / after ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: every Orca task refused"] direction TB B1["Task record
repoid::/abs/path"] --> B2{"Identity check
letters, digits, . _ @ % + - only"} B2 -->|colon and slash rejected| B3["Refused
cleanup and control blocked"] end subgraph AFTER["AFTER: real ids pass, bad ones still refuse"] direction TB A1["Task record
repoid::/abs/path"] --> A2{"Identity check
knows Orca's two-part id"} A2 -->|valid| A3["Proceeds
cleanup and control work"] A2 -->|malformed| A4["Refused
empty half, double colons,
relative path, control chars"] end BEFORE ~~~ AFTER classDef bad fill:#fde2e2,stroke:#c0392b,stroke-width:2px,color:#5a1212; classDef good fill:#e2f0d9,stroke:#1e7a3c,stroke-width:2px,color:#14401f; class B3,A4 bad; class A3 good; ``` ## What this unblocks, and what it does not This clears the way to clean up stale Orca task records and their working copies across the fleet. It does not clear all of them. Some older Orca records are separately missing the fields that name their terminal, and those still refuse for that different reason. Repairing those records is a separate job and is deliberately not in this change. ## How this was validated Reproduced against a live Orca task record: the identity check refused it on the current main branch, and accepts it with this change, returning the right runtime and terminal. Checked the id format against the real Orca CLI rather than assuming it. `orca worktree show --worktree "id:::" --json` resolves and returns that same two-part string as the worktree's own id, which confirms Firstmate should store and replay it as-is, and that the removal call will accept it. New tests cover the behaviour through the executable interface: the two-part id validates and selects the right terminal, ten malformed shapes each refuse while preserving the task record, and an end-to-end cleanup run asserts the two-part id reaches `orca worktree rm` unchanged and the record is removed.
Technical detail (for reviewers) `bin/fm-backend.sh` gains `fm_backend_orca_worktree_id_valid`, called from the single existing `orca)` branch of `fm_backend_validate_task_endpoint`. The existing owner is patched rather than adding a second validation path. It accepts either a bare atom (delegating to `fm_backend_endpoint_atom_valid`, so legacy records and existing fixtures are unaffected) or exactly one `::` separating a valid atom repo id from an absolute path with no `[[:cntrl:]]` characters. A second `::` is rejected so the parse stays unambiguous. A reference patch supplied with this work required `::` and rejected bare ids. That was changed deliberately: requiring it would have broken existing test fixtures and any record holding a bare Orca worktree id. Callers of `fm_backend_validate_task_endpoint` are `bin/fm-teardown.sh`, `bin/fm-control.sh`, `bin/fm-spawn.sh --relaunch`, and `bin/fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh`. `fm-send.sh`, `fm-peek.sh`, and `fm-crew-state.sh` do not call it and were never blocked by this defect. Considered and rejected: cross-checking the id's path component against the record's `worktree=` field. It matches in all 21 live Orca records, but the two can legitimately diverge through symlink resolution on macOS (`/tmp` vs `/private/tmp`), and a false refusal would re-break cleanup. Out of scope for a charset fix. A literal newline or carriage return cannot survive the record's line format, so the negative tests cover the control characters that can appear on one line (tab, CR, BEL) alongside relative paths, empty atoms, double `::`, and bare values containing `/` or `:`. Tests live in `tests/fm-teardown-endpoint-safety.test.sh` (validation and refusals) and `tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh` (end-to-end cleanup). `docs/orca-backend.md` is corrected in the same change: its `orca_worktree_id=` placeholder hid the two-part shape and is what led to the original assumption.

title: Would be great if you can make this work for Gitlab
Default unregistered projects to direct-PR delivery mode
body:
## Summary

Changes firstmate's default delivery resolution for unregistered projects and missing registries from `no-mistakes` (with yolo off) to `direct-PR` (with yolo off).

### Rationale

Previously, any project not registered in `data/projects.md` (such as firstmate itself or personal side projects) resolved by default to the heaviest `no-mistakes` pipeline with yolo off. For small, personal side projects, this ran extensive multi-round automated reviews and fixes that could argue with earlier fixes for hours.

By defaulting unregistered projects to `direct-PR` with `yolo off`:
- Worker agents implement, test locally, push a feature branch, and open a PR via `gh-axi`.
- The heavyweight `no-mistakes` pipeline is skipped unless explicitly requested or registered.
- Captain approval remains 100% authoritative: with `yolo off`, no PR is merged without the captain's explicit word.
- The registration gap is still reported to the captain so registry visibility is preserved.

### Delivery Posture Resolution Table

| Project Registry State | Standing Delivery Mode | Default YOLO | Approval Authority |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registered with explicit mode `[<mode>]` | `<mode>` (`no-mistakes`, `direct-PR`, `local-only`) | `off` (unless `+yolo`) | Captain (or firstmate for routine green gates if `+yolo`) |
| Registered with conditional policy `[no-mistakes-prod-only]` | Task surface classified at intake (`direct-PR` for internal/tooling, `no-mistakes` for product) | `off` (unless `+yolo`) | Captain (or firstmate for routine green gates if `+yolo`) |
| Legacy registered entry (no bracket) | `no-mistakes` | `off` | Captain |
| **Unregistered project / absent registry** | **`direct-PR`** | **`off`** | **Captain** |

### Test Verification

- `tests/fm-task-delivery.test.sh`: Passed all 7 test suites, including explicit checks for unregistered projects defaulting to `direct-PR off`, warnings on missing projects/registries, and downgrade notice matrix.
- `tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh`: Passed all assertions with isolated home project-mode checks updated.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh`: Passed ShellCheck 0.11.0 and actionlint 1.7.12 cleanly.
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`: Passed (69 surfaces, 256 local links).

title: fix(bin): bind tmux endpoint presence to exact session/window resolution
body:
## Root cause

`fm_backend_target_exists` (bin/fm-backend.sh) and `fm_backend_tmux_agent_state` (bin/backends/tmux.sh) resolved a recorded `session:window` endpoint using tmux's default fuzzy/prefix name matching instead of exact matching:

- `tmux list-panes -t <session>:<window>` and `tmux list-windows -t <session>` match a *prefix* of the session name, and the window-name comparison after inherited a similar prefix/glob laxness.
- A stale recorded endpoint whose window (or whole session) no longer exists could therefore still resolve against an unrelated window or a differently-named live session, reading ALIVE when the actual recorded endpoint is dead.
- On the cheap session-start fleet digest, a false ALIVE hides a dead worker from the supervisor.
- On the deeper recovery classifier (`fm_backend_tmux_agent_state`), a false ALIVE is worse: it can suppress a legitimate relaunch, or (in the renamed-session case) risk authorizing a duplicate relaunch onto a live worktree.

## Fix

- Bind both the session and window axes to tmux's `=` exact-match prefix, relying on exit status alone rather than a name comparison against captured output.
- In the recovery classifier, add a fuzzy re-probe when the exact session is absent: if a live session's name merely prefixes the recorded one, reuse that probe's window list to test membership — recorded window present reports `unreadable` (protects a renamed-but-live agent from a duplicate relaunch), absent reports `missing` (safe to recover, since no live session holds that window).
- A transient failure of the fuzzy re-probe itself (signal/fork hiccup) now reports `unreadable`, not `missing`, so a transient tmux glitch never licenses a duplicate relaunch.
- The cheap digest path (`fm_backend_target_exists`) intentionally does not re-probe on a renamed session: a renamed-but-live session reads dead there, which is documented in docs/tmux-backend.md as the safe direction for a passive read (false-dead only makes a supervisor look, never authorizes an action).

Files: `bin/fm-backend.sh`, `bin/backends/tmux.sh`, `docs/tmux-backend.md`, `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md`, plus colocated regression tests under `tests/`.

## Regression tests

Colocated tests fabricate a `state/<id>.meta` pointing at nonexistent tmux windows/sessions (dead-window-in-live-session and whole-session-gone cases) and assert dead/missing instead of the previous false ALIVE. Each new test fails on the pre-fix code and passes on this branch.

## Verification

Full no-mistakes pipeline run (review, test, document, lint) passed at head `51b38755`; only the push step failed, due to the invoking machine's GitHub identity (KakkoiDev) lacking write access to kunchenguid/firstmate. Delivered manually via a personal fork per captain's instruction: pushed `KakkoiDev:fm/fm-liveness-bug-r2`, opening this PR against upstream.

title: fix(bin): resolve captain decision holds across the backlog retention archive
body:
## Intent

Fix a defect in firstmate's own decision-hold completion gate: it can never pass once a closed captain hold is archived by backlog retention.

THE DEFECT. `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh verify` and `complete` resolved the stored key inventory against `data/backlog.md` only. `tasks-axi` retention sweeps closed Done rows into `data/done-archive.md`. So once a hold that was answered and closed got archived, the gate reported "captain decision <id> is absent from <FM_HOME>/data/backlog.md" and could never pass again.

REAL REPRODUCTION, NOT A SYNTHETIC ONE. The bug was reproduced on the live fleet home before any change: the `uls-app-shell-ux-audit` review registered 19 captain decisions, all 19 answered and closed; 5 remained in `data/backlog.md` and 14 had been archived into `data/done-archive.md`. `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh verify uls-app-shell-ux-audit` failed on the first archived one, so a completed investigation could not be cleaned up through the normal path even though every decision had a durable answer. After the fix, that same live command passes, with both data files byte-identical afterwards. THE PR BODY MUST NOTE that the reproduction came from a real 19-decision review where 14 holds had been archived, so the bug only manifests when a review runs long enough for retention to fire, which is why it went unnoticed. It is a perverse failure mode: it only breaks when a review goes WELL, because working through more decisions over a longer session is exactly what pushes the earliest answered ones past the retention window.

NOT A `repair` CASE. The decisions WERE answered and the answers ARE durable; they simply moved file. Recording a fresh "repair" decision would fabricate a record that already exists elsewhere, which is worse than the bug.

WHAT WAS FIXED. The gate now resolves a hold identity across the archive as well as the live backlog, in one owner rather than duplicated per call site. Points settled with evidence rather than assumption, as the task required:
- Where archived rows go: read from the configured retention in `.tasks.toml` (`archive = "data/done-archive.md"`) and from tasks-axi's own config resolution rather than hardcoding a filename. tasks-axi exposes NO read path back into the archive: `show`/`list` see the active backlog only, `--file` cannot name the archive because its own default archive path would then collide with it, and no flag or environment variable prints the archive path. That is why the archive path resolution had to be mirrored, and it is mirrored in exactly one place.
- Whether the archive preserves proof the decision was genuinely ANSWERED: verified yes. All 14 archived rows carry `state: done`, `kind: captain`, `hold_kind: captain`, and the full `Resolution recorded by fm-decision-hold.` block with the captain's recorded answer. A fix that merely stopped complaining would have been worse than the bug; the archive genuinely carries the proof, so the gate keeps its meaning.
- Which commands were affected: all of them, and they were fixed as a consistent set in two directions. Reads that ask whether a durable captain decision EXISTS now span both files (`verify`, `complete`, the idempotent-retry paths of `resolve`, `answer`, `decline`, and `repair`, the hold-identity check in `hold`, and origin ownership). WRITES deliberately stay on the active backlog, because the archive is a record tasks-axi cannot rewrite, and every mutation path that cannot reach its target now says exactly that instead of reporting the record as missing. That also closes a second latent problem: re-holding an archived identity used to create a colliding live row.

DESIGN DECISION. `bin/fm-tasks-axi-lib.sh` gained the single owner of the archived read. It renders an archived record through tasks-axi itself, against a private throwaway copy whose `## Archived <stamp>` block headers are rewritten to the `## Done` section header tasks-axi's grammar recognises. Entry parsing, body decoding, and field rendering therefore stay owned by tasks-axi and are not reimplemented; an archived record renders byte-identically to a live `show <id> --full`.

THE GATE MUST NOT BECOME TOOTHLESS - THIS IS THE WHOLE RISK IN THIS FIX, AND THE PR BODY MUST STATE EXPLICITLY THAT THE GATE STILL REFUSES A GENUINELY UNANSWERED DECISION, NAMING THE TEST THAT PROVES IT, so a reviewer does not have to infer it. The proving test is `test_archived_decision_without_an_answer_still_fails_the_gate` in `tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh`: it closes a hold out of band and archives it in one step, then asserts that `verify` still refuses, that teardown still refuses, and that `repair` refuses with an honest message naming why an archived row cannot have a missing answer written onto it - mere presence in the archive is never accepted as proof. Its companion `test_archived_answer_still_satisfies_the_completion_gate` asserts the positive direction (an answered hold keeps satisfying the gate after retention archives it, an identical close retry stays idempotent against the archived record, a DIFFERENT answer is still rejected) and also asserts teeth of its own: a decision raised after the archived inventory was reviewed still shuts the gate. Both tests were confirmed to FAIL against the unfixed code before being accepted, so neither is vacuous.

CONSTRAINTS HONORED. The fix does not disable retention, does not hand-edit `data/backlog.md`, and does not move archived rows back. A worker on this fleet had already refused to hand-edit the backlog to satisfy the broken gate and was right to: editing the record to please a checker destroys the audit trail the checker exists to protect.

VERIFICATION ALREADY PERFORMED. Live `verify uls-app-shell-ux-audit` passes and leaves both data files unchanged. Teeth re-proved against a COPY of that same real home data: a genuinely open unheld decision still refuses, and an archived record stripped of its answer still refuses. Full `tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh` suite: 18/18 pass. `bin/fm-lint.sh` clean (ShellCheck 0.11.0, actionlint 1.7.12 pinned) and `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` clean. Four suites (remote-doctor, on, bootstrap, session-start) fail in this worktree, but they fail identically on the untouched base commit, so they are pre-existing and unrelated to this change - do not attribute them to this work.

REPO CONVENTIONS. This is firstmate's own shared tracked material, governed by the `firstmate-coding-guidelines` skill: one full sentence per line in tracked Markdown, plain dash never an em dash, shellcheck-clean `bin/` scripts, colocated tests in `tests/` extending the existing `<subject>.test.sh` pattern rather than a new runner, tests exercising behavior through an executable interface rather than asserting implementation source bytes, mechanics documented in the script's own header rather than duplicated into prose, and no agent name as a commit co-author.

DELIVERY. The base branch is this repo's default branch, `main` - confirmed via `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, not assumed. The PR base must be verified with `gh api` after the PR is opened, because the pipeline has repeatedly opened PRs against the wrong branch on the other project in this fleet.

LATER ACCEPTED CAPTAIN DECISIONS, IN THEIR CURRENT FORM. During the first review gate the pipeline raised that `command_hold`, now resolving the identity across the archive, dead-ended an archived-but-unanswered identity with the false message "already durably resolved; use a new decision key". The captain's explicit decision was option A: CORRECT THE MESSAGE ONLY, so an archived-but-unanswered identity is reported truthfully. Do NOT add a recovery path, do NOT move archived rows back into the live backlog, and do NOT add any way to clear a stale key from an origin's recorded inventory - that is new capability and it cuts against this change's standing constraint that archived rows are never moved back. Refusing is already the correct behavior and stays; only what the gate SAYS while refusing was wrong.

THE GOVERNING PRINCIPLE THE CAPTAIN STATED, WHICH THE PR BODY MUST CARRY: the point of this whole change is that the gate tells the truth about whether a captain answer exists, so a false reassurance inside it would be worse than the original bug. That is why the archived-but-unanswered identity is now reported truthfully and why no recovery path was added.

Two message-accuracy corrections have already been applied under that decision and are part of the accepted work: `command_hold` now distinguishes an archived row that carries the recorded captain answer from one that does not, and the consequence about the key remaining in the origin's recorded inventory is stated only when it is actually true rather than unconditionally.

Three further accuracy items were identified, accepted, and are NOW APPLIED and covered by their own tests. Each is a diagnostic-accuracy correction only, changing nothing about which inputs pass or refuse and no exit status:
- `task_show_durable` is `task_show || task_show_archived`, and tasks-axi prints its NOT_FOUND block to stdout, so `||` does not discard it and an archived hit captures the miss diagnostic concatenated ahead of the real record. It is harmless today only because `show_field` anchors on `^ <field>: `, which is accidental safety. The live miss must contribute nothing to the captured value.
- `fm_tasks_axi_archive_show` collapses a failed `mktemp -d`, a failed copy, and a tasks-axi error into the same bare failure it uses for "no such archived record", so `absent_decision_message` positively claims the decision is absent from the archive when the archive may never have been read. On a home with a full or read-only TMPDIR the gate would refuse for a reason that is not true. An unreadable archive must be reported as unreadable, while the refusal and its exit status stay exactly as they are.
- The inventory-consequence guard conditions on the origin's recorded `decision_keys` alone, but an open `needs-decision [key=<key>]` line in the origin's status log also keeps the origin refused, so the message now understates in that case having previously overstated. State the consequence when it is actually true and omit it when it is not, covering both.

THE TEST REQUIREMENT THE CAPTAIN SET: a test must cover the archived-but-unanswered case SPECIFICALLY, not only the archived-and-answered one. That is satisfied by `test_archived_decision_without_an_answer_still_fails_the_gate`, which builds an out-of-band close that retention archived and asserts that `verify` refuses, that teardown refuses, that `repair` refuses with its archived-row reason, and that re-`hold` is refused without claiming the decision is durably resolved and without recreating a live row. It must stay covered.

A FOURTH ACCEPTED CAPTAIN DECISION, ALSO OPTION A, IS APPLIED. The review found that `command_hold` told the truth about an archived answerless close but its live, not-yet-archived sibling still refused with the same false "already durably resolved; use a new decision key" claim. The captain's explicit decision was to extend the truthful message to that live path too. THE PR BODY MUST CARRY THIS REASONING: it is the SAME false message in the SAME function that this change exists to correct, so fixing one branch and leaving the identical claim in its sibling would ship a truthfulness fix that only tells the truth half the time.
The two answerless-close messages are deliberately different and must stay distinguishable, because the situations genuinely differ: an archived row cannot be rewritten, so its refusal says neither repair nor a fresh key can record the missing answer; a live row still can be, so its refusal points at `repair` as the supported way to record the captain's actual decision and never suggests a fresh key. A hold this script closed properly still reports that it is durably resolved, so correcting the false message did not erase the true one. All three are asserted: the live case and the genuinely-resolved case in test_out_of_band_close_is_repairable_before_teardown, and the archived case in test_archived_decision_without_an_answer_still_fails_the_gate, which asserts its refusal does NOT point at repair.

DELIVERY NOTE ON THIS BRANCH'S HISTORY. Three earlier validation runs ended on infrastructure problems on this machine rather than on anything in this change, not on anything in this change: the first exited mid-fix on a usage-limit reset, and the second stalled with its fix agent idle (6m55s elapsed, 3s CPU, no child process) after it had already committed the three corrections. The captain confirmed another lane failed identically at the same moment. A third run then looped in its first fix round for over three hours, restarting its fix agent at least four times, each restart logging one opening line and producing nothing further, while other lanes on the same machine completed normally. Each time, the branch was recovered through the gate's own supported custody-recovery path, and manual reconciliation proved the preserved head contained every local commit unchanged plus the accepted corrections, rebased onto a newer default branch. No work was hand-edited outside the pipeline and nothing was dropped. Every accepted correction is committed, and the full tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh suite passes 22 of 22 with lint clean and the live reproduction still passing.

DELIVERY REMINDER RESTATED BY THE CAPTAIN: never pass --yes; the PR base must be verified with `gh api` before the URL is reported, because the pipeline has repeatedly opened PRs against the wrong branch on the other project in this fleet.

ALL FOUR PREVIOUSLY OUTSTANDING REVIEW FINDINGS ARE NOW APPLIED AND COMMITTED, and each is covered by a regression:
- `command_hold` no longer collapses "archive read, id genuinely absent" into "archive could not be read", so it refuses instead of creating a live row on an absence that was never established. That was the only path on this change that turned an unreadable archive into a WRITE. The archived read's status now reaches its callers, and one origin-ownership refusal never reports an origin as foreign on the strength of an archive it could not open.
- `task_show_durable` captures and drops the live miss rather than leaving tasks-axi's NOT_FOUND block concatenated ahead of an archived record. No caller can observe that difference today, so it is stated as defensive hardening, not a behavior change.
- The regression that claimed to prove that correction could not fail against the previous implementation, which is false assurance and the wrong thing to ship on a change about not giving false assurance. It is replaced by one that genuinely discriminates: the archived record alone decides the `repair` verdict for a retained decision. The unreadable-archive refusal is separately driven end to end through a genuinely unreadable archive, and it skips explicitly when the running user can read the file regardless of its mode rather than passing vacuously.
- `docs/decision-hold-lifecycle.md`, the declared owner of this mechanism's regression evidence, is refreshed from a real suite run, and the `fm-tasks-axi-lib.sh` row in `docs/scripts.md` now names the archived-record read.

DELIVERY NOTE ON THIS BRANCH. Earlier validation attempts on the predecessor branch could not get through the pipeline: runs died on capacity or looped in a fix round, and its validation record was finally stranded because a dead run's recorded head no longer existed locally, so every custody recovery refused. On the captain's ruling that record was abandoned rather than fought, and this branch was created from the last clean verified head, with the four fixes deliberately re-applied file by file from the stranded head used as reference only, never merged or cherry-picked wholesale, because that head also carried unrelated rebase content. Nothing was adopted unverified. Current state: the full tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh suite passes 23 of 23, bin/fm-lint.sh is clean on both pinned linters, bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh is clean, and the live reproduction still passes with both fleet data files unchanged.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh` now resolves a captain decision's durable record across both `data/backlog.md` and the retention archive it gets pruned into, so `verify`, `complete`, the idempotent-retry paths of `resolve`/`answer`/`decline`/`repair`, the `hold` identity check, and origin ownership all stop reporting an answered-then-archived decision as absent. Writes deliberately stay on the active backlog, because tasks-axi cannot rewrite the archive, and every mutation path that cannot reach its target now says exactly that; an archive this home cannot open is reported as unreadable rather than as proven absence, so `hold` refuses instead of creating a live row that would collide with a record retention already filed. The bug was reproduced on a real 19-decision review where 14 holds had already been archived, so it only manifests when a review runs long enough for retention to fire - a perverse failure mode that breaks precisely when a review goes well, which is why it went unnoticed.
- `bin/fm-tasks-axi-lib.sh` gained the single owner of the archived read: it mirrors tasks-axi's `.tasks.toml` archive-path resolution (tasks-axi exposes no read path back into the archive) and renders an archived record through tasks-axi itself against a private throwaway copy whose `## Archived <stamp>` headers are rewritten to the `## Done` header its grammar recognises, so entry parsing, body decoding, and field rendering are not reimplemented. `command_hold`'s refusal messages were corrected to tell the truth: an archived answerless close is distinguished from one that carries the recorded answer, the "stays in the origin's recorded inventory" consequence is stated only when it is actually true (recorded `decision_keys` or an open `needs-decision` line), and the same false "already durably resolved" claim was removed from the live, not-yet-archived sibling branch too - it is the same false message in the same function this change exists to correct, so fixing one branch and leaving it in the other would tell the truth only half the time. The governing principle is that the gate must tell the truth about whether a captain answer exists, which is why an archived-but-unanswered identity is now reported truthfully and no recovery path was added.
- The gate does not become toothless: it still refuses a genuinely unanswered decision, proven by `test_archived_decision_without_an_answer_still_fails_the_gate` in `tests/fm-decision-hold-lifecycle.test.sh`, which archives an out-of-band close and asserts that `verify` refuses, teardown refuses, `repair` refuses with an honest archived-row reason that never points at `repair` as a way out, and re-`hold` refuses without recreating a live row. Its companion `test_archived_answer_still_satisfies_the_completion_gate` covers the positive direction plus its own teeth, and further regressions drive the unreadable-archive refusal end to end (skipping explicitly when the running user can read the file regardless of mode) and prove the archived record alone decides the `repair` verdict. Docs were updated alongside: `docs/decision-hold-lifecycle.md` (the declared owner of this mechanism's regression evidence) refreshed from a real suite run, `docs/scripts.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, and the lifecycle skill.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The archive-spanning reads are owned in one helper with explicit read/write and absent/unreadable separation, every assumption the new code makes about tasks-axi (NOT_FOUND shape, Done-section grammar, hold_kind survival through prune, --file precedence, default archive path) was confirmed against the installed tool, the two fix rounds are correct and behavior-driven tested, and the stray tool config is fully untracked.

## Testing

I reproduced the reported defect as an end user would hit it - a review whose answered captain decisions had been swept into data/done-archive.md by tasks-axi retention - and captured a before/after CLI transcript showing the base commit refusing with "absent from .../data/backlog.md" and the target commit verifying successfully on identical data, with both data files byte-identical afterwards. The same transcript proves the gate did not become toothless: an archived row closed with no captain answer is still refused by verify, repair refuses naming that an archived row cannot be rewritten, and re-hold refuses truthfully without claiming durable resolution and without recreating a live backlog row. The full targeted lifecycle suite passes 26 of 26, and each new archive-related regression was independently confirmed to fail against the base-commit code, so none is vacuous. No linters or broad suites were run, and the worktree is clean.

- ℹ️ `bin/fm-tasks-axi-lib.sh:246` - fm_tasks_axi_archive_show uses `[ -f "$archive" ] || return 1`, which returns the documented "archive was read and does not hold that id" status for an archive it never opened. If a path component is unsearchable (e.g. `chmod 000 $FM_HOME/data`) the file exists but `[ -f ]` is false, so absent_decision_message positively claims "absent from <backlog> and its done archive" about a file that was never stat-able. This is the same false-absence class the change exists to eliminate; the committed unreadable-archive tests chmod the archive file itself, where `[ -f ]` still succeeds, so this variant is uncovered. Refusal and exit status are unaffected either way.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:546` - In command_hold the two new answerless-close refusals run before the `[ "$kind" = captain ]` and title checks. A closed non-captain row occupying the identity `<origin>-decision-<key>` is therefore refused with "captain decision <id> was closed with no recorded captain answer ... use repair to record the captain decision that was made", while `repair` refuses that same id with "backlog item <id> is not kind captain". Hoisting the kind/hold_kind checks above the answerless branch preserves the refusal and makes the stated reason true. Contrived to reach (requires a hand-created colliding id) and no change to which inputs pass.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-decision-hold.sh:279` - absent_decision_message re-derives the archived-read status with a fresh mktemp, whole-archive copy, and tasks-axi subprocess, even where the caller already holds it: command_hold has `archive_status` in hand when it calls the message on status 2, and command_repair already knows the durable record came from the archive. Besides the duplicated read per refusal, a readability change between the two reads makes the printed reason describe a different state than the one the refusal was based on. Threading the known status into the message would remove both.

🔧 Fix: refuse unexaminable archives and settle hold identity kind first
