title: fix(bin): forbid agent commit co-authors in every generated crewmate brief
body:
## Intent

Firstmate repo task: stop agent co-author trailers from reaching landed history.

THE DEFECT: AGENTS.md carries the rule 'Never add an agent name as a commit co-author', but it is not reaching crewmates, because the generated brief scaffold never states it and firstmate does not reliably restate it by hand. Measured 2026-08-17: agent Co-Authored-By trailers are present across landed history in projects/InsightEngine (Claude Opus 5, Claude Code) and projects/orca-command-center (Orca, Claude Opus 5 1M context), including commits landed that same night. This is a rig defect, not a worker discipline problem: a rule that only lives in a file the worker never reads is not a control.

DELIVERABLE 1, pick the mechanism and say why. Two candidates were named: A, emit the rule in the standard brief contract so bin/fm-brief.sh states it in the generated Rules section of every ship brief and no brief can omit it; B, strip or refuse agent Co-Authored-By trailers on the commit path. The task required weighing them (A is advisory and depends on worker compliance; B is deterministic but needs a commit path firstmate actually controls across every harness and backend), considering whether both are warranted, and making the reasoning visible in the PR body rather than buried. CHOSEN: A only, deliberately, for these reasons which belong in the PR body: (1) firstmate owns no commit path that every worker goes through; workers commit inside project worktrees under eight verified harnesses plus muse, on five runtime backends. (2) The existing PreToolUse infrastructure (bin/fm-arm-pretool-check.sh) only sees a command string, so it cannot see a message supplied via -F, a heredoc, EDITOR, or a later --amend; a shell-layer guard is silently bypassed by ordinary usage. (3) The only guard that catches every message source is a git commit-msg hook, which lives in the project's shared .git common dir and is repo-wide config; installing one means firstmate writing into project git config, colliding with any project that already sets core.hooksPath, and affecting commits made outside firstmate entirely, trading a documentation gap for a project-mutation surface. (4) The no-mistakes pipeline is an external binary and not extensible here. (5) A is sufficient because the defect was never worker non-compliance, it was that the rule lived exclusively in AGENTS.md, which is firstmate's own instruction surface and which a crewmate in a project worktree never reads; the brief is the one document every crewmate does read, so stating it there closes the actual gap.

DELIVERABLE 2, implement it with a colocated test that fails against the current code and passes after, showing both. Implemented as rule 8 of the standard Rules section in bin/fm-brief.sh: 'Never add an agent name as a commit co-author: no Co-Authored-By: trailer naming Claude, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Orca, or any other agent, model, or tool.' Applied to BOTH the ship and the scout scaffold, deliberately: bin/fm-promote.sh keeps the scout brief loaded and sends ship instructions by message, so a promoted worker never receives a ship brief and its scratch work becomes ship commits under scout rules. A one-sentence pointer was added to the fm-brief.sh header, which is the owner of what the generated scaffolds contain. Test added to the existing colocated tests/fm-brief.test.sh as test_every_crewmate_scaffold_forbids_agent_co_authors, covering all four scaffolds (no-mistakes, direct-PR, local-only, scout). Evidence shown to the captain: before the change it reported 'not ok - no-mistakes brief did not carry the no-agent-co-author commit rule'; after, the suite is 21 ok / 0 not ok. The test asserts on the GENERATED brief output, which is fm-brief.sh's own generated public artifact, not on implementation source bytes.

DELIVERABLE 3, sweep the already-landed local-only commits: determine which existing commits carrying agent co-author trailers are still local-only (not pushed to any remote) and therefore still amendable, REPORT the list, and do NOT amend or rewrite any history. Done and reported: exactly one fleet-wide, InsightEngine acfb2e1f 'chore(planning): archive v1.0 ATX-1457 milestone', 2026-07-15, trailer 'Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>', reachable only from tag v1.0-atx-1457 and on no local or remote branch. Nothing was amended. Everything else is already pushed and stays as it is: InsightEngine has 1,563 trailered commits on remote refs, orca-command-center 61, and this repo's one (bc1a21b) is on fork/main.

HARD CONSTRAINTS accepted and honored, do not flag these as omissions: do not rewrite git history (no rebase -i, no filter-branch, no commit --amend on anything but the worker's own in-progress commit); do not touch anything under projects/ (the sweep was strictly read-only); do not weaken or restate the AGENTS.md rule in a second place, so AGENTS.md stays the owner and the brief is the allowed single-line reinforcement at the risk point, and AGENTS.md was deliberately NOT edited at all (minimal means zero here). Per .agents/skills/firstmate-coding-guidelines, a single deliberate one-line reinforcement at a genuine risk point is permitted and is what rule 8 is.

Commit hygiene was itself in scope: the delivered commit carries no Co-Authored-By trailer naming any agent. Verified: git log -1 --format='%(trailers)' is empty.

Verification already run locally: tests/fm-brief.test.sh 21 ok / 0 not ok; bin/fm-lint.sh clean (ShellCheck 0.11.0 pinned; actionlint absent locally and no workflow was touched); bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh ok (surfaces=69, local_links=255); adjacent suites green: fm-ask-user-authority, fm-secondmate-safety 77 ok, fm-subagent-pretool-check 13 ok, fm-tangle-guard 6 ok.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-brief.sh` now emits rule 8 in the standard Rules section of both the ship and the scout scaffold: "Never add an agent name as a commit co-author: no `Co-Authored-By:` trailer naming Claude, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Orca, or any other agent, model, or tool." The scout scaffold gets it too because `bin/fm-promote.sh` keeps the scout brief loaded and sends ship instructions by message, so a promoted worker's scratch work becomes ship commits under scout rules. A one-line pointer was added to the `fm-brief.sh` header, which owns what the generated scaffolds contain.
- `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` gains `test_every_crewmate_scaffold_forbids_agent_co_authors`, asserting on the generated `brief.md` for all four scaffolds (no-mistakes, direct-PR, local-only, scout) that both the rule text and the forbidden `Co-Authored-By:` trailer name are present. Against the base commit it reports `not ok - no-mistakes brief did not carry the no-agent-co-author commit rule`; with the change the suite is 21 ok / 0 not ok.
- Mechanism choice, stated here rather than buried: this is the brief-contract fix (A), not a commit-path guard (B), and A alone is deliberate. Firstmate owns no commit path every worker goes through — workers commit inside project worktrees across eight verified harnesses plus muse on five runtime backends. The existing `bin/fm-arm-pretool-check.sh` PreToolUse hook only sees a command string, so it cannot see a message supplied via `-F`, a heredoc, `EDITOR`, or a later `--amend`; a shell-layer guard is silently bypassed by ordinary usage. The only guard catching every message source is a `commit-msg` hook, which lives in the project's shared git common dir, collides with any project that sets `core.hooksPath`, and would affect commits made outside firstmate entirely — trading a documentation gap for a project-mutation surface. The no-mistakes pipeline is an external binary and not extensible here. The defect was never worker non-compliance: the rule lived only in `AGENTS.md`, firstmate's own instruction surface, which a crewmate in a project worktree never reads. `AGENTS.md` stays the owner and was deliberately left unedited; the brief is the one document every crewmate does read.

Read-only sweep of already-landed agent co-author trailers (nothing amended, no history rewritten, nothing under `projects/` touched): exactly one trailered commit is still local-only and therefore amendable — InsightEngine `acfb2e1f` "chore(planning): archive v1.0 ATX-1457 milestone" (2026-07-15, trailer `Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>`), reachable only from tag `v1.0-atx-1457` and on no local or remote branch. Everything else is already pushed and stays as it is: InsightEngine 1,563 trailered commits on remote refs, orca-command-center 61, and this repo's one (`bc1a21b`) on `fork/main`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Additive, well-bounded change: two identical instruction lines in the two brief heredocs that cover all four crewmate scaffolds, plus a colocated test that executes the real script and asserts on its generated brief artifact; no control flow, no existing assertion or downstream rule-number reference is affected.

## Testing

Exercised bin/fm-brief.sh directly and captured the generated brief.md — the document a crewmate actually reads — for all four scaffolds under both base and target code: rule 8 forbidding agent Co-Authored-By trailers is absent before and present after in every one, with rules 1-7 unchanged. The colocated suite passes 21 ok / 0 not ok at target, and the same target test file run against a pristine base-commit checkout fails on the new assertion, establishing the fail-before/pass-after regression. Also confirmed no history rewrite (base is ancestor, one new commit), no files touched outside bin/ and tests/, and zero Co-Authored-By trailer lines on the delivered commit. No screenshot applies: the change has no rendered UI surface — its end-user surface is generated markdown text, which is captured verbatim in the artifacts. Worktree left clean and temp scratch directories removed.

title: fix(bin): fold path spellings in worktree and watcher identity checks
body:
## Summary

Two safety checks in firstmate's own tooling compared paths as raw strings, so one directory reached under two spellings read as two different locations. Both defeat checks that protect the never-write-to-projects prime directive.

## Defect 1: case-variant home path defeats identity checks

**A finding that departs from the original framing:** the task prescribed normalizing with `pwd -P`, and `fm-spawn` already did that (landed in #294, a month before the incident). `pwd -P` resolves symlinks but **preserves the caller's spelling** of each component:

```
cd /x/Home && pwd -P   ->  /x/Home
cd /x/home && pwd -P   ->  /x/home     # same inode, different string
realpath /x/home       ->  /x/Home     # folds to the on-disk name
```

Perl's `Cwd::realpath` and Python's `os.path.realpath` behave like `pwd -P`, so the new helper deliberately shells out to `realpath(1)` despite an existing perl-realpath idiom elsewhere in the repo.

Reproduced the near-miss: a worktree pointed at the primary clone with a case-variant project path was **ACCEPTED** before the fix, **REFUSED** after.

New `fm_canonical_path` / `fm_canonical_file_path` in `fm-wake-lib.sh` are applied on both sides of the spawn isolation assertion and both watcher-lock identity comparisons (`fm-wake-lib.sh` and `fm-watch-arm.sh` shared the weakness). The guard failure produced false "watcher down" alarms after a session resume.

## Defect 2: pool slot reuse leaves stale meta worktree pointers

`fm-spawn` now records the canonical path the lease actually settled on. `fm-teardown` refuses when the recorded worktree holds a different task's `fm/<id>` branch, before the step that deletes that branch and resets the worktree.

## Deliberate design decisions

- The spawn-side double-lease check **warns rather than refuses**. A lingering record is usually a finished task awaiting cleanup, so refusing would block routine spawns on stale metadata. The destructive end refuses.
- The teardown refusal requires **positive proof**: a detached `HEAD` (how a landed task legitimately ends) or a non-`fm/` branch name does not block cleanup.
- `--force` deliberately does **not** override the refusal: it authorizes discarding this task's own work, never another task's.

## Review round

The review gate caught that the guard covered only the non-orca destructive path while the orca branch ran the identical `checkout --detach` + `branch -D` sequence unguarded. Extended to orca, plus `canonical_existing_dir` (feeding orca's path-match equality check) had the same `pwd -P` weakness and could cause a spurious refusal on a legitimate orca teardown. The hazard class is now closed on every supported backend.

## Verification

- `bin/fm-lint.sh` passes (pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0, actionlint 1.7.12).
- New tests are proven to fail without their fix and pass with it.
- Tests skip on case-sensitive filesystems, where the variant path cannot exist.
- Four pre-existing test failures (`fm-teardown` herdr-preflight, `fm-watch-arm`, `fm-wake-queue`, `fm-backend-orca` metadata-write) were each confirmed failing identically on the clean baseline via `git stash` / `git checkout` — unrelated to this change.

body:
## Intent Reproduce, root-cause, and fix the Pi primary supervision feedback loop that flooded the captain's main command lane with repeated Follow-up FIRSTMATE_OP watcher messages, primarily check: rearm-resurface, despite no actionable queued event. The fix must keep exactly one healthy supervision cycle live while work is under way; make ordinary child completion and ordinary successor/re-arm behavior silent under extension ownership; inject Pi model follow-ups only for genuine actionable events, explicit missing/failed/unhealthy-cycle repair, or other documented captain-relevant outcomes; never suppress durable actionable wakes; and avoid disabling supervision, dropping wakes, broad-killing processes, arbitrary timer lengthening, or relying on model memory to ignore messages. Diagnostic requirements included reproducing the loop or representative harness, separating initiating trigger, masking conditions, and visible symptom, comparing quiet re-arm paths, inspecting Pi generation ownership, child-close classification, rearm-resurface publication, turn-end guard interaction, wake-drain acknowledgement, session replacement, and continuity docs/tests. Implementation requirements included the smallest deterministic owner fix, regression coverage for many ordinary child-close/rearm cycles and assistant turn ends proving zero synthetic follow-up storm, separate proof of one delivery for real signal/stale/check/heartbeat and queued recovery events, bounded repair for explicit failed/unhealthy states, session replacement/generation transitions, duplicate-owner/no-op rearm behavior, affected Pi identities/shared watcher code, updated owning docs/verification evidence, focused tests, lint/docs checks, completeness eval, and no live Pi restart from this worker. The captain requested that the current Pi session be restarted once safe; this change must report whether restart remains necessary to clear already-enqueued messages and load the landed extension fix, but must not perform that restart. Ship through no-mistakes and open a PR against verbagem/firstmate only; never merge it. ## What Changed - The Pi primary watch extension (`.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts`) now classifies a `check: rearm-resurface` child close as a new `empty-rearm` kind when no captain-relevant work is pending: it restores the supervision cycle silently, confirms recovery handling without injecting a follow-up message, and only sends a wake if a queued-work re-check or a restoration failure shows something actionable. Real signal/stale/check/heartbeat events and failure repairs still deliver exactly once. - `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh` gains a read-only `--captain-work-pending` mode that prints `quiet` only when the wake queue, open decisions, and unread surface lines are all empty, using the cursor-safe whole-file decisions fold; any scan failure reports `pending` so callers can over-deliver but never suppress. - Extended the extension, turn-end guard, and wake-drain test suites with regression coverage for repeated silent empty-rearm cycles, pending-work delivery, and the new peek mode, and updated `docs/scripts.md`, `docs/watcher-continuity.md`, and `docs/verification/supervision.md` to document the behavior. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Both prior fix rounds verifiably resolve the earlier findings via the shared read-only drain peek, every failure mode biases toward delivery rather than suppression (satisfying the never-suppress-durable-wakes requirement), and the new tests exercise the real drain and extension behavior; the only remaining observation is a bounded corrupt-queue tradeoff the design explicitly chose. ## Testing Exercised the three targeted suites (Pi watch extension, wake-drain unread-status, turn-end guard) — all pass — and proved the regression is real by running the new empty-rearm storm test against the base commit, where it fails with 17 synthetic follow-ups, versus zero on the fixed target; also captured a live CLI transcript showing the captain-work peek reports quiet/pending correctly without consuming unread captain-relevant state, and confirmed the docs answer the restart-necessity question without performing a restart.
Evidence: Pre-fix follow-up storm reproduction (new regression test vs base commit 1cb900c — fails with 17 follow-ups) Source: [Pre-fix follow-up storm reproduction (new regression test vs base commit 1cb900c — fails with 17 follow-ups)](https://github.com/verbagem/firstmate/blob/1f0a70047172ee155cdfaa8a2e5c29185ab7ab6c/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/pi-watcher-rearm-followup-storm-fix-5087/storm-test-before-fix.txt) ```text === New storm regression test vs BASE (pre-fix) extension @1cb900c — expected to FAIL === HARNESS OUTPUT: file:///Users/temp/.no-mistakes/worktrees/acee6d463bcf/01M0GT7YWQ3136H3ZB7S0FR97K/[eval1]:29 if (prompts !== 0) throw new Error(`empty rearm emitted ${prompts} follow-ups`); ^ Error: empty rearm emitted 17 follow-ups at file:///Users/temp/.no-mistakes/worktrees/acee6d463bcf/01M0GT7YWQ3136H3ZB7S0FR97K/[eval1]:29:26 Node.js v24.12.0 not ok - Pi empty rearm-resurface cycles must not create follow-up storms: expected exit 0, got 1 exit=1 ```

⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - 🚨 `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:173` - The empty-rearm silence gate checks only wakeQueueHasRows(), but the `check: rearm-resurface` delivery it suppresses was also the mechanism that resurfaced decision-only recovery and unread `note:` status lines: bin/fm-wake-drain.sh's empty-queue fast path prints the cursor-folded OPEN DECISIONS set and unread status sections on every drain, and the pre-change docs/watcher-continuity.md sentence (rewritten by this diff) promised "a still-open decision or a buried note: answer reappears even when recovery has no queue row of its own." Reachable path: signal wake delivered and acked but decision left open → Pi watcher dies uncleanly → stale-lock reclaim sets WATCHER_RECOVERY_PENDING=1 → `check: rearm-resurface` with empty queue → new code silently confirms handling and never triggers a drain, so the open decision stays buried unboundedly (Claude/OpenCode arm paths still deliver it). The user intent marks as required: "never suppress durable actionable wakes" and follow-ups for "other documented captain-relevant outcomes" — decision-only recovery is documented and regression-tested (fm-watch-arm.test.sh "decision-only OPEN DECISIONS recovery"). If unintended, the silence predicate should come from the shared drain/classify boundary (empty queue AND no open decisions AND no unread status lines), not a queue-file re-implementation in the extension. - ⚠️ `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:499` - Race in the silent empty-rearm path: a durable row appended by an external process (fm-supervise-daemon, parent-reply ingestion) between the post-restoration wakeQueueHasRows() recheck (line 495) and confirmRecoveryHandling (line 499) is left undelivered. fm_wake_append republishes the recovery marker to pending:downtime (preserving the generation) before writing the row; the extension's --handling-delivered then flips it to pending:handling, so the successor's resurface loop sees action 'wait' and never wakes, and no model turn runs to drain the row — it sits queued until the next unrelated event. Cheap containment: after confirmRecoveryHandling succeeds, recheck wakeQueueHasRows() once more and sendWake if rows appeared (appends after confirm are safe because they republish pending:downtime, which the settled successor's arm_check loop turns into a fresh wake). - ℹ️ `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:484` - The `empty-rearm` close branch (lines 484-508) duplicates the `actionable` branch's restoration scaffolding (retryFailures reset, restoring flag, restoreAfterActionableClose, generationIsLive dance); the two differ only in the post-restoration delivery decision. They could be one branch with a delivery predicate, but merging risks subtle behavior drift in a supervision-critical path, so leaving as-is is defensible. 🔧 Fix: gate empty-rearm silence on shared captain-work peek 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `docs/verification/supervision.md:310` - The fix round changed the empty-rearm quiet gate (queue-only → shared --captain-work-pending peek) and expanded the delivery test to cover open-decision and unread-note re-arms, but this verification evidence section still records the pre-fix-round run: the quoted pass line 'ok - Pi real signal, stale, check, heartbeat, and queued recovery reasons still deliver once' no longer matches the suite's actual pass line ('...queued recovery, open-decision, and unread-note reasons still deliver once', tests/fm-pi-watch-extension.test.sh:573), and line 303's narrative describes the superseded queue-only silence rule. Update the evidence text (and quoted pass lines, after the pipeline's test step re-runs the suites) so the recorded receipt matches the shipped implementation, including the new fm-wake-drain-unread-status peek tests. 🔧 Fix: refresh supervision evidence for captain-work peek gate 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:53` - The peek's queue gate is `[ -s "$FM_WAKE_QUEUE" ]`, but the ack path deliberately preserves malformed rows (`NF < 5 { print }`, line 257) and `fm_wake_print_deduped` never presents them. A crash-torn append leaving a malformed-only queue file would make every future quiet `check: rearm-resurface` report `pending` — one follow-up per recovery whose drain surfaces nothing, with no path that ever clears it. title: fix(bin): keep session-lock ownership across Claude process reparenting
body:
## Intent Make per-home session-lock ownership survive Claude Code process reparenting without weakening protection against genuinely competing live sessions. Empirically determine which Claude session identifier remains stable and is available from both hook payloads and ordinary commands; if none qualifies, document and use only the specified same-installation background-host fallback rather than inventing an identifier. Extend state/.lock compatibly so line 1 remains the numeric PID, legacy bare-PID locks keep their ancestry behavior, dead owners remain reclaimable, identity-matched reparenting atomically refreshes the PID, and different live identities still refuse with the existing message. Keep fm-lock status, startup, watcher, auto-arm, Pi, OpenCode, Cursor, and every lock reader consistent with the structured format. Make structurally inert Claude Stop auto-arm recovery consume the existing bounded turn-end block budget, blocking at most the configured default of three times before one loud attended fail-open. Add comprehensive behavioral tests for every ownership branch, exact refusal, reparented auto-arm ownership and guard release, legacy and stale recovery, identity propagation, and bounded inert recovery. Update script contracts and operator and verification docs with the ownership model, safety boundary, bounded progression, and exact empirical evidence. Do not touch live locks, watcher processes, worker processes, or shared daemons, and ship on branch fm/firstmate-session-identity-lock-fix-s5 through review, tests, docs, lint, push, PR, and green CI. Captain additionally requires the fuller in-process reset correction: keep foreign live-identity refusal, add ancestry-membership fallback for /clear and /compact, executable coverage and verification docs; bind published identity to publishing-session provenance with a competing nested-Claude regression; and automatically repair an unreadable ownership record only when no valid live or ambiguous owner can be established, preserving refusal otherwise. ## What Changed - Extended `state/.lock` into a compatible structured record — numeric owner PID on line 1, plus `harness=` and optional `session=` fields — and reworked `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh` to own parsing, publishing, and the ownership decision: a matching harness + session identity owns the lock across reparenting and atomically refreshes the recorded PID under the acquisition lock, legacy bare-PID locks keep the unchanged contiguous-ancestry behavior, dead owners stay reclaimable via `fm-lock.sh`, unreadable records are only reclaimed when they name no live foreign harness owner, and a different live identity still hits the existing refusal. The Claude session identity is bridged from the SessionStart hook payload through `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` and bound to its publishing session's PID, so an identity inherited by a nested session is refused rather than trusted. - Updated every lock reader and adapter to the structured format — `fm-lock.sh` status/acquire, `fm-session-start.sh` completion proofs (now re-stamped on re-emit), `fm-sessionstart-run.sh`/`fm-sessionstart-nudge.sh`, `fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh`, `fm-turnend-guard.sh`, `fm-trace-context-lib.sh`, `fm-wake-lib.sh`, `fm-startup-network.sh`, `fm-bootstrap.sh`, and the Pi, OpenCode, and Cursor watch/guard extensions. - Made structurally inert Claude Stop auto-arm recovery consume the existing bounded turn-end block budget: the guard records unclaimed recovery under its own `state/.claude-autoarm-failure-unclaimed` marker (kept separate from the auto-arm's delivered-notice marker), blocks at most `FM_CLAUDE_TURNEND_BLOCK_BUDGET` (default 3) times before one loud attended fail-open, and the auto-arm now waits out bounded guard-held owner-lock sections instead of standing down. Adds `FM_CLAUDE_AUTOARM_OWNER_WAIT_MS` and `FM_CLAUDE_AUTOARM_STRUCTURAL_RECHECK_MS`. - Added behavioral coverage across `tests/fm-session-lock-ancestry.test.sh`, `tests/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.test.sh` (+ live e2e), `tests/fm-sessionstart-nudge.test.sh`, `tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh`, and `tests/fm-trace-context-lib.test.sh` for every ownership branch, the exact refusal message, reparented arm ownership and guard release, legacy/stale recovery, identity propagation and nested-session provenance, and bounded inert recovery; documented the ownership model, safety boundary, bounded progression, new tunables, and the recorded Claude 2.1.237 identity evidence in `docs/`. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: A broad (~1850-line) change to the per-home session-ownership invariant that every harness adapter, hook, and sweep depends on, but it is well-bounded by a single shared library owner, backed by real-process behavioral regressions for each ownership branch, documented with the required empirical evidence, and the three prior review rounds' concrete failure paths are verifiably closed — the two remaining findings are informational hardening/consistency items. ## Testing Targeted suites for the changed surfaces (session-lock ancestry/identity, Claude Stop auto-arm, turn-end guard, session-start nudge/run wrapper, trace-context lib) all pass with no failures or gate skips, and I did not run the full repository suite. Because passing unit cases alone do not show the operator experience, I additionally drove the real lock, auto-arm and turn-end guard scripts inside genuine Claude-named process trees and captured three CLI transcripts: session-lock ownership across every branch (reparenting refresh, competing live identity refusal with the exact existing wording, legacy bare-PID preservation, dead and mangled record handling, /clear re-identification, inherited host identity), reparented auto-arm ownership with watcher arm and guard release, and the bounded inert progression of three blocked stops followed by one loud attended fail-open. All observed behavior matches the stated intent; no product or setup failures were found, and all fixture processes and scratch directories were cleaned up leaving the worktree unmodified.
Evidence: Session-lock ownership transcript (real fm-lock.sh, 8 ownership branches) Source: [Session-lock ownership transcript (real fm-lock.sh, 8 ownership branches)](https://github.com/timoconnellaus/firstmate/blob/6ac48ec5f55cffe7b078f2e23ae7586e6a15cb41/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/firstmate-session-identity-lock-fix-s5/session-lock-ownership-transcript.txt) 3. Reparented session: same identity, different LIVE pid -> ownership kept, pid refreshed BEFORE: 79974 harness=claude session=sess-alpha (claude session pid 79977) $ bin/fm-lock.sh status lock: held by this session (live harness pid 79977) $ bin/fm-lock.sh; echo "exit=$?" lock acquired: harness pid 79977 exit=0 $ cat state/.lock 79977 harness=claude session=sess-alpha 4. A genuinely competing LIVE session (different identity) still refuses (claude session pid 80282) $ bin/fm-lock.sh status lock: held by live harness pid 79974 $ bin/fm-lock.sh; echo "exit=$?" error: another live firstmate session holds the lock (pid 79974); operate read-only until resolved exit=1 record after refusal (owner untouched): 79974 harness=claude session=sess-alpha ```text ======================================================================== 1. title: ci: require no-mistakes pipeline step attestation
body:
## Summary
- Keep the existing no-mistakes signature requirement for human PRs.
- After that signature, require the v1 HTML pipeline-attestation comment from no-mistakes >= 1.46.0.
- Fail if attestation is missing or unparseable, or if `review`, `test`, or `document` is anything other than `completed` (quota/agent skips included). Bot exemptions are unchanged.

This is a direct-PR: GitHub will run the current main (signature-only) check against this PR, so `PR must be raised via no-mistakes` is expected red until merge. The new attestation logic applies to later PRs after this lands.

title: feat(skills): add the /updatethecaptain repeating worker report loop
body:
## Intent

Let the captain ask to be kept posted on the workers and get a plain-English update covering every worker straight away and then every ten minutes - what each has finished, what it is doing now, what is left, and how long it needs - with any question a worker has for the captain surfaced at the top of the message, running until no worker is left or the captain stops the updates.

## What Changed

- Added the `updatethecaptain` skill (`.agents/skills/updatethecaptain/SKILL.md`): it builds the in-flight worker list from `bin/fm-bearings-snapshot.sh --all-in-flight` plus `bin/fm-crew-state.sh`, reports every worker in plain English across four parts - finished, working on now, still to do, how long it needs - places any worker question for the captain at the top of the message, reports once immediately, repeats on each timer wake, and ends when the list is empty. The companion `updatethecaptain-stop` skill disarms the loop and is a no-op when nothing is armed.
- Added `bin/fm-captain-report-timer.sh` with `arm` / `status` / `disarm`, which generates a trust-bound custom watcher check (`state/captain-report.check.sh` plus its trust binding and a private `state/.captain-report-timer` stamp) so the ten-minute repeat rides the existing authenticated check dispatch rather than a background process. Default interval 600s, accepted range 60-86400, idempotent arm and disarm, and the armed check plus its stamp and trust binding are rolled back if registration or verification fails.
- Wired the feature into the surrounding surfaces: AGENTS.md section 9 routes `/updatethecaptain` and `/updatethecaptain-stop` to the skills and section 3 documents the new stamp artifact, the README built-in-skills table and `docs/scripts.md` gained the new entries, `docs/documentation-audiences.json` classifies both SKILL.md files, and `tests/fm-captain-report-timer.test.sh` adds 13 cases covering cadence, idempotence, rollback, and a real `bin/fm-watch.sh` dispatch drained through `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is purely additive, rides the existing authenticated custom-check dispatch rather than introducing a new execution path, carries a focused test suite, and every round-1 concern the user chose to fix is now resolved with correctly scoped, minimal edits.

## Testing

I ran the change's own suite (tests/fm-captain-report-timer.test.sh, 13 cases green), the doc/AGENTS.md suites its non-code edits touch, and the runner's coverage guard, then drove the captain's actual experience end-to-end against the real binaries: the skill's fleet read listing three live workers, an unadorned arm landing on the ten-minute cadence, a nine-minute sweep staying quiet, two consecutive ticks each dispatched by a real bin/fm-watch.sh and durably queued by fm-wake-drain.sh (the committed suite only proves one, so this is where the repeat is demonstrated), the loop ending by itself once the rebuilt worker list is empty, and /updatethecaptain-stop disarming cleanly and staying harmless when nothing is running. I also re-probed the round-1 timing flake with 14 concurrent copies of the suite - 182/182 cases ok, no failures. No screenshot applies: the change ships no rendered UI, only a skill contract and a shell timer, and the captain-facing surface is a chat message, which I captured as the three markdown report files. Those report bodies are prose the skill instructs the agent to write rather than code output, so I authored them by following SKILL.md against the fleet state stage 1 really produced, which lets a reviewer check the four-part-per-worker format, the question pinned at the top, the closing line for a finished worker, and an overrun stated plainly before the new estimate. Everything passed and I found nothing actionable.

<summary>Evidence: Captain-visible E2E transcript of the whole report loop</summary>

```text
==============================================================
 STAGE 1 - the captain types /updatethecaptain
 Step 2 of the skill: read every worker under way from this

If this assertion fails (a concurrent write or a TOCTOU race between register.sh's own final verify and this one), `state/captain-report.check.sh` is left behind mode 0700 with a trust binding that no longer matches its bytes. bin/fm-watch.sh:938-947 then fails `fm_custom_check_snapshot_prepare` for it, appends it to `rejected_checks`, and lines 962-967 append a wake and call `wake` for "rejected unauthenticated state checks" - which exits the watcher and burns a firstmate turn on every check sweep (FM_CHECK_INTERVAL, default 300s) indefinitely, since nothing ever removes the orphan. Mirror the rollback: remove CHECK, STAMP, and TRUST before dying here too.
- ⚠️ `README.md:178` - The "Built-in skills" section states "Firstmate ships these user-invocable built-in skills" and its table enumerates all five existing skills carrying `user-invocable: true` (/afk, /ahoy, /bearings, /updatefirstmate, /stow). Both new skills also carry `user-invocable: true` (.agents/skills/updatethecaptain/SKILL.md:7, .agents/skills/updatethecaptain-stop/SKILL.md:7) but neither is added to the table, so the documented captain-facing command set is now incomplete for a feature the captain is expected to invoke by name. Add `/updatethecaptain` and `/updatethecaptain-stop` rows.
- ℹ️ `AGENTS.md:99` - The `state/` inventory in section 3 enumerates every artifact class the runtime writes, including private dot-files such as `.pr-check-quarantine/`, `.pr-check-migration.log`, and `.pr-check-migration-scan-v1`. The timer's new stamp `state/.captain-report-timer` (bin/fm-captain-report-timer.sh:53, mode 0600, one epoch-seconds line) is a new artifact class and is not listed, so the inventory no longer describes everything a home can contain. `captain-report.check.sh` and `captain-report.check-trust` are already covered by the generic `<id>.check.sh` / `<id>.check-trust` entries.

title: fix(dashboard): require a real ask before a card can claim needs-attention
body:
## Intent

Make needs-attention on the Admiral's Fleet Dashboard structurally require an actual ask. The Admiral caught a card set to needs-attention with reason 'You reported flares not changing the lights - being chased now' - a progress report, not something he could act on. needs-attention is the loudest status on the board and means blocking on him; a card that merely reports progress spends his attention and teaches him the loud status does not always mean him, repeating a failure that already made one always-red marker into noise.

Scope delivered:
1. bin/fm-dashboard.sh and the HTTP API (both create-task and set-status/patch paths): setting needs_attention now REQUIRES a --reason / reason field. Previously it was optional and the UI fell back to generic placeholder text ('Needs his decision or action to continue.'). The API now refuses the status change without a reason rather than substituting a default; the CLI also refuses locally before the round-trip.
2. Reject reasons that are obviously not an ask, mechanically and conservatively - not a language model. Implemented as a small fixed list of report-shaped phrases (REPORT_SHAPED_PHRASES in bin/fleet-dashboard/server/validation.py: 'being chased', 'in progress', 'investigating', 'looking into', 'working on', 'keeping an eye on', 'monitoring', 'no update yet', 'will update', 'update to follow', 'tracking down', 'digging into', 'following up on', 'under investigation', 'still chasing'), matched as a case-insensitive substring anywhere in the reason text (not just at the start, since the motivating example tacked the report phrase onto the end of a sentence). Documented in docs/dashboard.md with the tested false-negative rate: caught 15/15 report-shaped reasons built from the list, missed 10/10 reworded report-shaped reasons deliberately avoiding every listed phrase (expected blind spot - it recognizes vocabulary, not the general concept of a report), and produced zero false positives against 10 genuine asks.
3. Explicitly did NOT block on any other status: working with a vague note is not touched, review needs no ask by design and is untouched. Only needs_attention is guarded.
4. Updated .agents/skills/fleet-dashboard/SKILL.md: reason is required, and the test for a real ask is 'what would he DO' - if the honest answer is 'read it' or 'know it', it is not needs-attention.
5. Updated docs/dashboard.md with a new 'The needs-attention reason guard' section covering both enforcement points, the false-negative rate, and an explicit statement that the fleet auditor's separate judgment-based check (whether the ask is genuinely real, not just non-report-shaped) is not replaced by this mechanical guard and vice versa - the server checks words, the auditor checks whether the ask is real.

Constraints honored: existing needs-attention cards with weak reasons are untouched - migrates nothing, only governs what can be set from now on. The board's live server keeps working (server-side change is additive validation, not a breaking schema change). Added tests/fm-dashboard.test.sh coverage exercising both the CLI-local rejection and the server-side rejection independently (direct curl call with empty reason), plus the report-shaped-phrase rejection and successful creation/transition with a genuine ask, for both the add and status code paths.

## What Changed

- `needs_attention` now requires a reason server-side: `POST /api/tasks` (create-into-status) and `POST /api/tasks/{id}/status` both route the reason through a new `validate_needs_attention_reason` in `bin/fleet-dashboard/server/validation.py` and return 400 instead of falling back to placeholder text; `store.add_task` gained a `needs_attention_reason` column write, scoped to that status only. `bin/fm-dashboard.sh` refuses locally in both `add` and `status` before the round-trip, and `add --reason` is now refused for any status that cannot store one.
- Reasons that read as progress reports are rejected mechanically against a fixed `REPORT_SHAPED_PHRASES` list ("being chased", "in progress", "investigating", …), matched only when a phrase opens or closes the leading or trailing clause — with short leading-hedge ("still", "we") and trailing-hedge ("now", "it") lists — so a report phrase used as an ordinary noun mid-clause ("approve the $400 monitoring subscription renewal") still passes. The card overlay in `web/app.js` opens a reason field when `needs-attention` is chosen, keeps confirm disabled until it has text, and surfaces the server's refusal inline.
- Added `tests/fm-dashboard.test.sh` coverage for CLI-local and direct-curl server rejection, report-shaped-phrase rejection, genuine asks containing report words, and a corpus test asserting the documented catch/miss/false-positive counts (15/15 caught, 18 accepted misses, 0 false positives on 14 asks). `docs/dashboard.md` gains a "needs-attention reason guard" section covering both enforcement points, the accepted blind spots and why widening the hedge list was reverted, and the boundary with the fleet auditor's judgment check; `SKILL.md` records that the reason is required and the "what would he DO" test. `--help` now derives its header range from the comment block instead of a fixed line count.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The guard sits at the single shared server boundary with no reachable bypass (PATCH cannot set status, no other caller touches set_status/add_task), the documented catch/miss/false-positive rates reproduce exactly against the current code and are pinned by an executed table-driven test, and the remaining known misses and the reason-persistence gap for non-waiting statuses are explicitly recorded as accepted rather than left implicit.

## Testing

Ran the targeted dashboard suite (tests/fm-dashboard.test.sh, all 17 checks pass) plus the two adjacent suites touching the same surfaces (card-link, documentation-audiences), then verified the intent end-to-end against a live server on an isolated FM_HOME: the CLI, the raw HTTP API on both the create and status paths, and the board UI each refuse needs-attention without a reason and refuse the exact 'being chased now' reason that motivated the change, while a genuine ask goes through and renders on the card; a pre-guard card with the old placeholder text is left untouched and every other status still needs no ask. Captured a CLI transcript and three UI screenshots (required-reason prompt, inline server refusal, board showing only actionable asks). Everything passed; the only note is that the shipped matcher is clause-edge rather than anywhere-substring, narrower than the intent text describes but documented and pinned by tests.

The intent states tests were added exercising "the CLI-local rejection and the server-side rejection independently (direct curl call with empty reason), plus the report-shaped-phrase rejection and successful creation/transition with a genuine ask, for both the add and status code paths" — the add path is missing two of those four. Concretely: add `"$DASH" add ... --status needs-attention --reason "looking into the checkout timeout"` expecting a non-zero exit, and a `curl -X POST /api/tasks` with `{"status":"needs_attention"}` and no reason expecting HTTP 400.
- ℹ️ `bin/fleet-dashboard/server/validation.py:43` - Several REPORT_SHAPED_PHRASES entries are ordinary nouns/verb phrases that occur inside genuine asks, and the match is an unanchored case-insensitive substring, so the guard hard-refuses them. "Approve the $400 monitoring subscription renewal" and "Decide whether to keep the monitoring alerts on overnight" both match `monitoring`; "Pick which contractor keeps working on the deck" matches `working on`; "Approve the invoice for the in progress work" matches `in progress`. Each of those is a real blocking ask that the API will refuse with HTTP 400. The rejection message does name the matched phrase, so an agent can reword — but the failure mode when it does not is that the card silently stays in `working` and the Admiral is never asked, which is the inverse of the failure this guard exists to prevent. Flagging because the fixed list is a deliberate design choice (documented in docs/dashboard.md), not something to change unilaterally: worth confirming whether `monitoring`, `working on`, and `in progress` earn their place given they are the three most likely to appear in a legitimate ask.
- ℹ️ `docs/dashboard.md:101` - docs/dashboard.md:101-103 makes specific quantitative claims about the guard — caught 15/15 report-shaped reasons, missed 10/10 reworded ones, zero false positives against 10 genuine asks — but no check in the repo reproduces them. Nothing fails when someone adds, removes, or narrows a REPORT_SHAPED_PHRASES entry, so those numbers can silently become false while still reading as measured fact. That matters more than usual here because the same section is what tells the fleet auditor the exact shape of the blind spot it is supposed to compensate for. A table-driven test that calls validate_needs_attention_reason over the three corpora (rejects the report-shaped set, accepts the genuine-ask set) would pin the claim to executed behavior rather than prose.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-teardown.sh:989` - Pre-existing on this branch, not introduced by the reviewed commit, but it undercuts the same signal the change is protecting: teardown advances any non-`complete` linked card to `testing`, with `needs_attention` given no special treatment. store.set_status then nulls `needs_attention_reason` (store.py:306), so a card the Admiral was actually blocking on is silently demoted to the status that is explicitly "optional to him" and its ask is discarded — no audit-log entry, no trace on the card beyond a status_history row. Sequence: card set to needs-attention with a genuine ask, task later torn down normally, card lands in testing with the ask gone. Worth deciding whether teardown should skip `needs_attention` the way it skips `complete`, or log a discrepancy when it overrides one.
- ℹ️ `bin/fleet-dashboard/web/app.js:145` - The generic fallback "Needs his decision or action to continue." is still rendered on the card banner. This is consistent with the intent's constraint that existing needs-attention cards are not migrated — pre-guard rows can legitimately have a NULL reason and still need something to render — so it is correct to keep, not a leftover. Noting it only because the intent describes that placeholder as the old behavior being replaced, and a later reader may mistake its presence for an incomplete cleanup; it is now reachable only for cards created before this guard existed.

🔧 Fix: anchor needs-attention report guard to clause edges, test rates
2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fleet-dashboard/server/validation.py:70` - The fix round's edge anchoring introduced a false-negative class that the documented corpus does not cover: a listed report phrase preceded by a subject and a copula now passes. `_sits_at_an_edge` strips only `_LEADING_FILLER` ({still, currently, now, just, already, we, we're, i, i'm, im}) from the front, so on "We are investigating the checkout timeout" the leading scan strips `we`, hits `are` (not in the set) and breaks, while the trailing scan breaks on `timeout` - the reason is accepted. Same for "The team is looking into the failed backup" (leading breaks immediately on `the`) and "Work in progress on the deck" (trailing breaks on `deck`). Concrete reachable path: `bin/fm-dashboard.sh status <id> needs-attention --reason "We are investigating the checkout timeout"` succeeds and renders a pure progress report in the loudest status on the board - exactly the failure the change exists to prevent, and a case the author's original substring match caught. This matters more than an ordinary blind spot because docs/dashboard.md:101 and tests/fm-dashboard.test.sh's REPORT_SHAPED corpus present "caught all 15" as measured evidence, and all 15 examples happen to place the phrase at a hedge-strippable edge; not one has the subject+copula shape, so the stated rate overstates what the guard achieves. The narrow mechanical scope and the fleet auditor backstop (SKILL.md sweep step 4) are deliberate and I am not asking for a redesign - but either extend `_LEADING_FILLER` with the copulas/auxiliaries (is, are, am, was, were, be, been, 's, 're) that cover the common case, or add at least one subject+copula example to the REPORT_SHAPED corpus and state this shape as a known miss so the documented catch rate is honest about it. Related, smaller: `_edge_clauses` (line 102) keeps only the first and last clause, so a report clause sandwiched in the middle ("Approve overtime - still investigating the delay - thanks") is skipped entirely; that one is at least described in the docs.
- ℹ️ `bin/fleet-dashboard/server/validation.py:45` - The authoritative intent text no longer describes the shipped implementation, in three source-verifiable ways. (1) It states the phrases are "matched as a case-insensitive substring anywhere in the reason text (not just at the start, since the motivating example tacked the report phrase onto the end of a sentence)"; the code now matches only when a phrase opens or closes the leading or trailing clause (`find_report_shaped_phrase`, line 130). (2) It enumerates the list as ending in "...'keeping an eye on', 'monitoring', 'no update yet'..."; `REPORT_SHAPED_PHRASES` at line 45 has no bare `monitoring` - it was split into `monitoring the` and `monitoring it` (16 entries, not 15). (3) It records "produced zero false positives against 10 genuine asks"; docs/dashboard.md:103 and the pinned test corpus now say 12 genuine asks. All three changes were explicitly directed by your round-1 fix instructions, so this is the intent/PR narrative being stale rather than the code deviating from what you last asked for - flagging only because I cannot resolve an intent-vs-code divergence myself. Suggest updating the intent/PR description text to describe edge-anchored matching, the split `monitoring the`/`monitoring it` entries, and the 12-ask corpus.

🔧 Fix: catch copula-led report reasons, document noun-subject miss
3 issues (2 warnings, 1 info) still open:
- ⚠️ `bin/fleet-dashboard/server/validation.py:87` - Adding bare copulas to `_LEADING_FILLER` introduced a new false-positive class on genuine asks. `_sits_at_an_edge` strips filler tokens unconditionally from the front, so any reason that *opens* with a copula now has it stripped, and the report phrase immediately behind it matches. Verified against the current code vs. the pre-e367b79 code: "Is working on Saturday ok with you?", "Is digging into the crawlspace approved?", "Is monitoring the pool worth $80 a month?", and "Was looking into the second quote worth the delay?" were all ACCEPTED before this commit and are all REFUSED now. Each is a real blocking ask phrased as a question - the most natural form for a decision request - and refusing it leaves the card silently in `working` with the Admiral never asked, which docs/dashboard.md:97 itself names as "the exact inverse of the failure this guard exists to prevent." The intended case is subject+copula ("We are investigating X"), not a bare leading copula; requiring that a copula only be stripped when a first-person subject was already stripped ahead of it keeps "We are investigating the checkout timeout" / "I was digging into the bounced payouts" caught while leaving "Is working on Saturday ok?" alone. The pinned corpus cannot catch this: GENUINE_ASKS in tests/fm-dashboard.test.sh has no question-form entry, so the documented "zero false positives against 12 genuine asks" stays green while the residual FP surface grew. Flagging as ask-user because the copula list was your explicit round-2 instruction - the narrowing to subject+copula is the part that needs your call.
- ⚠️ `bin/fleet-dashboard/server/validation.py:91` - The `"'s"` and `"'re"` entries added to `_LEADING_FILLER` are unreachable, so the contracted-copula gap the fix round claims to have closed is still open. `_tokens` (line 121) tokenizes with `[a-z0-9']+`, which keeps the apostrophe attached to the preceding word: "It's" produces the single token `it's`, never `it` + `'s`. A standalone `'s`/`'re` token can only arise from text like "we 's", which does not occur. Consequence: "It's still chasing the supplier" - the exact string your round-2 instruction named as one of the two cases "wrongly ACCEPTED" and being fixed - is still accepted (verified against the current code), as is "It's investigating the leak". The fix round also did not add it to the REPORT_SHAPED corpus, so nothing in the test suite would reveal that the case was missed; only "We are investigating..." / "I was digging into..." / "We were keeping an eye on..." were added, all of which pass via the pre-existing `we`/`i` entries plus the new bare copulas. Two separable parts: (a) `'s` and `'re` are dead entries and should be removed regardless, and (b) catching "It's still chasing X" requires an `it's`/`it` token, which is a pronoun and therefore outside the closed set you explicitly ruled out - so either accept it as a documented miss alongside the noun-subject class in docs/dashboard.md, or authorize adding the third-person contraction. Needs your call, not a unilateral fix.
- ℹ️ `bin/fleet-dashboard/server/validation.py:52` - Splitting bare `monitoring` into `monitoring the` / `monitoring it` (round 1) leaves a miss class that no corpus or doc records. Verified: "Monitoring the disk usage" and "Monitoring it now" are refused, but "Monitoring disk usage" and "Still monitoring disk usage" are accepted - plain progress reports opening on a listed report verb. The determiner is the only thing separating them. docs/dashboard.md:101 lists "Monitoring the alert queue overnight" in the caught-18 corpus, which reads as "monitoring reports are caught", and the two documented miss classes at line 102-104 are reworded phrasing and subject-noun forms - neither covers this. Note the original motivation for the split no longer applies the same way: the false positives it was trimming for ("approve the $400 monitoring subscription renewal", "decide whether to keep the monitoring alerts on overnight") are mid-clause and are already excluded by the edge anchoring added in the same round, so bare `monitoring` may now be safe at the trailing edge even if a leading noun-adjunct use ("Monitoring costs need your approval") argues for keeping the split at the leading edge. Either way, worth either restoring coverage or adding this to the documented blind-spot list so the 18/18 figure is not read as covering all monitoring-shaped reports.

🔧 Fix: revert copula hedges, document accepted guard misses
2 infos still open:
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-dashboard.sh:207` - `add` now accepts `--reason` for any starting status, but the value is silently discarded unless the status is needs_attention: `create_task` (api.py:110) passes it only as `needs_attention_reason`, and `store.add_task` (store.py:211) nulls it when `status != "needs_attention"` while hardcoding `waiting_on_id`/`waiting_reason` to NULL in the INSERT. Concretely: `fm-dashboard.sh add --title X --captain dj --prompt "..." --status waiting --reason "waiting on the plumber"` exits 0, prints a normal row, and the card carries no waiting reason - whereas the sibling `fm-dashboard.sh status <id> waiting --reason "..."` honors exactly that flag. Before this change `--reason` on `add` was a hard `add: unknown argument` error, so the change converted a loud failure into a silent data drop for that combination. The usage comment at line 19 does say "ignored for every other starting status," so this looks deliberate rather than accidental - flagging only because the asymmetry with `status` is the kind a caller learns the wrong way. Cheapest options if you want it closed: `die` when `--reason` is passed with a status that ignores it, or plumb `waiting_reason` through `add_task` the way `set_status` does.
- ℹ️ `bin/fleet-dashboard/server/api.py:110` - The needs_attention guard is the same six lines in `create_task` (110-115) and `set_status` (169-174) - identical `reason = body.get("reason") or None` plus try/except translating InvalidReasonError to ApiError(400). A one-line helper would dedupe it. Noting rather than asking for a change: this matches the existing convention in the same file (`add_note` inlines the `validate_review_link` try/except the same way), so the duplication is consistent with its surroundings rather than a new pattern, and both copies are correct.

🔧 Fix: refuse add --reason for statuses that cannot carry one
4 infos still open:
- ℹ️ `docs/dashboard.md:125` - The residual false-positive class is wider than the single example the docs give, and includes the question form the round-3 revert was made to protect. Verified against the current code: "Do you want us to keep working on this?", "Should we keep working on this?", "Which vendor should we keep working on?", "Do you want us to stop investigating?", "Decide if we should keep monitoring it" are all REFUSED (trailing edge, after the trailing-filler strip of "this"/"it"), as are real asks carrying a report clause in a separate sentence - "Investigating the outage. Should we call the vendor?", "Still investigating - do you want us to call the vendor tonight?", "Approve the overtime; the crew is in progress". Each is a genuine blocking ask, and refusing one leaves the card in `working` with the Admiral never asked. Reporting this as informational only, not as a defect: docs/dashboard.md:125 already states the general rule ("a genuine ask that *opens or closes* a clause on one of these phrases is still refused"), names it deliberate, and says the zero-false-positive figure is a property of the corpus rather than a guarantee - so the behaviour is honestly recorded, and the rejection message names the matched phrase so an agent can reword. The only gap is that the one worked example given is trailing "in progress"; a reader takes from the section above it that question-form asks were the thing the copula revert protected, and "Do you want us to keep working on this?" shows that protection only covers copula-led questions, not questions that end on a report phrase. If you ever revisit the docs, one extra example there would close that impression - explicitly not worth another fix round on its own.
- ℹ️ `tests/fm-dashboard.test.sh:321` - test_documented_guard_rates_still_hold pins the outcome counts but not two of the three corpus sizes, so the documented denominators can still drift silently - which is the exact thing the test exists to prevent. `counts != (15, 0, 0)` catches a shrunk REPORT_SHAPED (14 caught fails), but deleting entries from REWORDED_REPORTS or GENUINE_ASKS leaves their counts at 0 and the test green, while docs/dashboard.md:119 ("Against **18** report-shaped reasons the list was never meant to reach") and :124 ("Against **14** genuine asks") become false. Concretely: drop "Monitoring disk usage" and "Still monitoring disk usage" from REWORDED_REPORTS and the suite still passes, but the documented 18 is now 16 and the recorded bare-verb miss class has no executed evidence behind it. Two asserted lengths - `len(REWORDED_REPORTS) == 18` and `len(GENUINE_ASKS) == 14`, alongside the existing count check - close it. Mechanical, no behaviour change.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-dashboard.sh:228` - Round 4's new refusal message tells the caller to use `fm-dashboard.sh status <id> $status --reason ...` for whatever status they passed, but only two statuses actually carry a reason on the card. store.set_status (store.py:305-306) writes `waiting_reason` only for `waiting` and `needs_attention_reason` only for `needs_attention`; for `working`, `paused`, `testing`, and `complete` both columns are set NULL and the text survives only as a status_history note, which `cmd_show` never renders (it prints notes tabs and the two status reasons, nothing from status_history). The CLI's own header at line 32 says as much: "ignored for other statuses". So `add --title X --captain dj --prompt ... --status testing --reason "ready for his eyes"` now dies with advice to run `status <id> testing --reason ...`, which will exit 0 and put the text somewhere `show` does not display - the caller is redirected from one silent drop to another. The refusal itself is right and is what you asked for; only the suggested alternative overreaches. Naming `waiting` specifically ("only `waiting` and `needs-attention` carry a reason on the card") would make the message true for all six other statuses. Flagged as ask-user because it is user-facing copy you have been deliberately wording.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-dashboard.sh:21` - Recording, not re-litigating: the --intent text still describes the round-1 implementation, and round 4 added a user-visible behaviour it does not mention at all. The intent says phrases are "matched as a case-insensitive substring anywhere in the reason text" (code is edge-anchored via find_report_shaped_phrase), lists bare "monitoring" among 15 phrases (REPORT_SHAPED_PHRASES has "monitoring the"/"monitoring it", 16 entries), and states rates of 15/15, 10/10, 0/10 (shipped docs and the pinned test say 15/15, 0/18, 0/14). New since that was adjudicated: `add` now hard-refuses `--reason` for any status but needs-attention (bin/fm-dashboard.sh:227-228, header at line 21), which is not in the intent's delivered-scope list in any form - before this branch it was an "unknown argument" error, so it is not a regression against the base, just undescribed. You already ruled on this class in round 2 ("the real shipped docs were already correct, only the review's own --intent argument was stale"), and every divergence here was directed by your own fix instructions, so no code or doc change is warranted - the note exists so that whatever text becomes the PR description is refreshed from the shipped docs rather than from the original intent paragraph.

🔧 Fix: narrow add --reason refusal to statuses storing a reason
1 info still open:
- ℹ️ `bin/fleet-dashboard/server/validation.py:45` - Recorded for the PR description, not for another fix round - you already ruled on this class twice (round 2: "the real shipped docs were already correct, only the review's own --intent argument was stale"; round 5: ignored). The --intent text still describes the round-1 implementation: it says phrases are "matched as a case-insensitive substring anywhere in the reason text" (the code is edge-anchored via find_report_shaped_phrase, validation.py:143), lists bare "monitoring" among 15 phrases (REPORT_SHAPED_PHRASES holds "monitoring the"/"monitoring it", 16 entries), and states rates of 15/15, 10/10, 0/10 (shipped docs and the pinned test measure 15/15, 0/18, 0/14 - I re-ran all three corpora against the current code and they match the docs exactly). It also does not mention that `add` now hard-refuses --reason for any status but needs-attention (bin/fm-dashboard.sh:230-238), which is new since the intent was written but not a regression against the base, where --reason on `add` was an "unknown argument" error. Every divergence was directed by your own fix instructions, so no code or doc change is warranted - only that whatever text becomes the PR description is refreshed from docs/dashboard.md rather than from the original intent paragraph.

</details>

<details>
<summary>⚠️ **Test** - 1 info</summary>

- ℹ️ `bin/fleet-dashboard/server/validation.py:26` - The shipped guard is narrower than the user intent's description of it. The intent states the report-shaped phrases are "matched as a case-insensitive substring anywhere in the reason text" and lists bare 'monitoring'; bin/fleet-dashboard/server/validation.py matches only at clause edges (with a small hedge list) and carries 'monitoring the'/'monitoring it'. Verified behavior: "The bilge pump is being chased by the yard", "Monitoring disk usage", "The rebuild is in progress and the vendor has not called" and "We are investigating the checkout timeout" are all ACCEPTED, where anywhere-substring matching would refuse them. The motivating example is still refused, the narrowing is documented in docs/dashboard.md as accepted misses with the false-positive reasoning, and the counts there (18 reworded misses, 14 genuine asks) supersede the 10/10 in the intent, pinned by test_documented_guard_rates_still_hold. No action needed for testing; noted so the divergence from the written intent is a deliberate, visible choice rather than a surprise.
- <code>`bash tests/fm-dashboard.test.sh` — full file, 17 checks pass, incl. `test_needs_attention_requires_a_real_ask`, `test_a_genuine_ask_mentioning_a_report_word_is_accepted`, `test_add_refuses_a_reason_for_a_status_that_cannot_carry_one`, `test_documented_guard_rates_still_hold`</code>
- <code>`bash tests/fm-dashboard-card-link.test.sh` — adjacent dashboard surface, passes</code>
- <code>`bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` — docs/dashboard.md changed, passes</code>
- <code>Manual end-to-end: started a real dashboard server on an isolated FM_HOME/port and drove `bin/fm-dashboard.sh status <id> needs-attention` with the motivating reason, with no reason, and with a genuine ask; captured the full transcript</code>
- <code>Manual server-side enforcement bypassing the CLI: `curl -i -X POST /api/tasks/<id>/status -d '{"status":"needs_attention"}'` → HTTP 400, and `-d '{...,"reason":"still chasing the supplier"}'` → HTTP 400</code>
- <code>Manual create path: `fm-dashboard.sh add --status needs-attention` with no reason, with 'looking into ...', and with a real ask</code>
- <code>Manual UI walkthrough via `chrome-devtools-axi` in an isolated browser session: opened a card, selected Needs Attention, screenshotted the required-reason form with submit disabled, submitted the report-shaped reason and screenshotted the inline refusal, then submitted a genuine ask and screenshotted the board</code>
- <code>Manual no-migration check: inserted a pre-guard `needs_attention` row carrying the old placeholder reason directly into the demo database, then `fm-dashboard.sh show` / `list --status needs-attention` confirm it is unchanged and still listed</code>

</details>

<details>
<summary>⚠️ **Document** - 1 info</summary>

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-dashboard.sh:590` - bin/fm-dashboard.sh:590 renders --help via a hardcoded `sed -n '2,64p'` over the usage header. This change added ten lines to that header (the add/status --reason contract), pushing the header's last four blocks past line 64, so `--help` now silently stops at "captain shorthands" and no longer prints server URL resolution, the --connect-timeout/--max-time bounds and their env overrides, or the exit-code table (0/4/1). Confirmed by running `bin/fm-dashboard.sh --help` and diffing its tail against the base commit; no test covers help output. The .agents/skills/fleet-dashboard/SKILL.md tells agents to run `--help` for exact current syntax, so this is documentation lost from its rendered surface. Fix is to widen the range to '2,74p' (or make it stop at the first non-comment line), which is an executable line rather than a doc comment, so this phase left it alone.

🔧 Fix: derive --help header range instead of fixed line count

- ℹ️ `bin/fm-status-board.sh:104` - The drift-prone pattern this round fixed in bin/fm-dashboard.sh exists in at least a dozen other scripts, each rendering --help via a hardcoded line range over its own header comment: bin/fm-status-board.sh:104 ('2,96p'), bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh:62 ('2,47p'), bin/fm-afk-launch.sh:149 ('2,34p'), bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh:489 ('2,40'), bin/fm-backlog-receive.sh:31, bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh:302, bin/fm-afk-start.sh:46, bin/fm-remote-inherit.sh:23, bin/fm-kimi-turnend-hook.sh:23, and others. title: fix(bin): follow the checkout's configured upstream instead of a hardcoded origin
body:
## Intent Make the fleet's self-update follow the repository we actually develop in, not the upstream it was forked from. A firstmate checkout can have "origin" pointing at the public template it was forked from while its own branch tracks a separate fork it actually develops on (e.g. this checkout: origin=joliverMI/firstmate is the fork we develop on, upstream=kunchenguid/firstmate is the public template), and the two can genuinely diverge. bin/fm-update.sh compared against origin/main unconditionally and never advanced a home tracking a different upstream past the divergence point. Scope: 1. bin/fm-update.sh must resolve the update source from the branch's configured upstream (git tracking branch) rather than hardcoding origin/main; where no upstream is configured, keep today's origin/main behavior and say so explicitly rather than guessing. 2. Audit every other place in bin/ that assumes origin is the development remote (fleet sync and anything else that fetches, compares, or reports divergence); fix them together under the same resolution, or state explicitly why a given script is already correct (e.g. project-clone scripts that intentionally always use origin because project clones have no fork/upstream split). 3. Do not change push or PR targeting behavior in this task; that remains owned by standing repo convention and is currently working correctly. 4. Determine whether the right fix for the remote code root (a clone whose own origin points at upstream rather than the fork) is repointing that clone's origin at the fork, or teaching the remote update path which remote to use, and recommend one with reasoning; do not apply a repoint as part of this change. 5. Prove the outcome end to end, not just via code inspection: after the fix, a fleet update must leave fork-only files (bin/fm-dashboard.sh and fm-spawn.sh's --card flag) present in a remote secondmate home that updates through the fixed path. Constraints: fast-forward-only safety is absolute and unchanged - never force, never stash, never discard unlanded work, never merge; a dirty or genuinely diverged target is still skipped and reported, not forced. Do not touch anything under projects/. The PR targets joliverMI/firstmate, never kunchenguid/firstmate. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-dev-remote-lib.sh` as the single owner of development-remote resolution: `resolve_update_base` reads the default branch's configured upstream (`%(upstream:remotename)` / `%(upstream:remoteref)`) and falls back to `origin/` with an explicit note when no remote upstream is configured. `bin/fm-ff-lib.sh` now fetches and fast-forwards through it (per-remote `fetch_once` keying, `default_branch` takes a remote argument), so `/updatefirstmate` advances a checkout that tracks a fork instead of comparing against a diverged `origin/main`; the fast-forward-only guards (no force, stash, merge, or dirty/diverged advance) are untouched. - Applied the same resolution to the other paths that fetch, diff, or report divergence: `fm-review-diff.sh` (base ref and `refs/pull//head` fetch), `fm-teardown.sh` (cached `resolve_dev_remote` for PR-object and landed-content checks), `fm-spawn.sh` (pooled-worktree base freshening), and the changed-file base in `fm-lint.sh` and `fm-test-run.sh`. `fm-fleet-sync.sh` is documented as deliberately origin-only because it walks project clones under `projects/`, which have no fork/upstream split; push and PR targeting are unchanged. - Added `tests/fm-remote-update-follows-fork.test.sh`, which drives `fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh update` against a fork/upstream fixture and asserts fork-only files land in the secondmate home, plus new cases in the lint, review-diff, test-run, and spawn-pool-base-freshen suites and `fm-test-run.sh` selection entries for the new library and test. Docs and skills were reworded from "origin" to "configured upstream", and `docs/remote-secondmates.md` records the recommendation to set the remote code root's branch upstream rather than repoint its `origin`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is broad (one new shared resolver plus six consumers touching self-update, pooled-worktree provisioning, teardown's landed-work gate, and diff-base selection), but every resolution failure mode falls back to the prior `origin` behavior or refuses rather than forcing, fast-forward-only safety is untouched, each fixed path gained a real behavioral regression test, and only two narrow fail-safe issues survived verification. ## Testing Ran the change's targeted suites (fork-follow e2e, fm-update, fm-lint, fm-review-diff, fm-test-run, fm-spawn-pool-base-freshen, fm-gotmp, fm-teardown, fm-secondmate-sync, fm-bootstrap, fm-fleet-sync) — all pass — and, because passing unit tests alone do not show the fleet actually following the fork, drove the real remote-update entrypoint end to end against a fixture built from this repository's own history, A/B-ing the pre-fix and post-fix bin/ over identical fixtures: the old path reported "already current" and left the secondmate home without bin/fm-dashboard.sh or --card, while the fixed path reported "updated 4f0a4f5..a28663a"/"synced:" and delivered both, with --card proven by its real argument-validation error rather than help text. I also captured the explicit no-upstream origin/main fallback note and confirmed fast-forward-only safety (diverged and dirty roots skipped, nothing forced, stashed, or discarded). No visual artifact applies: this change is git plumbing behind a CLI update path with no rendered surface, so the reviewer-visible evidence is the CLI transcript. Two failures I hit are environment-only and pre-existing at the base commit (locale-sensitive coverage guard, missing ruby); the working tree is clean and all evidence lives in the evidence directory.
