title: fix(bin): supervise quiet panes on evidence, not on repetition
body:
Refs #3206.

This is the watcher-triage half of #3206: the ordinary `bin/fm-watch.sh` stale path escalating panes that are deliberately, legitimately quiet. It does **not** touch the Grok busy-footer matching that issue also asks for, and it is independent of the alternative patch referenced there (josh-padnick/firstmate#10) - happy to defer or rework if you prefer that direction.

## Violated invariant

Pane-idle supervision must escalate on evidence the supervisor has not already seen.
The crew's own latest declaration sets the recheck cadence, an escalation firstmate has already handled does not repeat on the detection cadence, and a lost endpoint is covered by neither.

The watcher broke that three ways. Each was reproduced against a real watcher poll loop over a scratch state root with a real tmux endpoint **before** any change.

## Root cause

**1. The declared-wait allowance was keyed to the pane hash, not the declaration.**

A live declared wait earns one prompt surface, so an external-decision gate is never hidden behind the long pause cadence. That allowance was keyed to the pane hash. A quiet pane that redraws - a progress tick, a token counter, a resized footer - produces a new hash every few seconds, and each new hash re-earned the same immediate wake. A crew that declared a 40-60 minute wait was surfaced 19 times in 6 minutes on the fixture and never once reached the long cadence its declaration is supposed to buy.

The allowance is now keyed to the declaration's own status-log signature. A redraw under a wait firstmate already knows about is absorbed; only a fresh append re-arms the prompt surface. Measured on the same fixture: 19 stale wakes down to 1.

**2. `wedge_timer_check` deleted its own timer when it escalated.**

The next poll therefore restarted the same short `STALE_ESCALATE_SECS` countdown against an unchanged pane while the escalation counter compounded. Nothing in the bookkeeping consumed the one fact that mattered - that firstmate had already drained the previous escalation, inspected the pane, found it healthy, and acknowledged it. A live crew was alarmed every ~250s for ~35 minutes, reaching `demand-deep-inspection`, with every single wake already handled.

The interval is now evidence-driven. An escalation still queued unacknowledged keeps the detection cadence, so a ladder nobody has read still climbs to `demand-deep-inspection` unchanged. An **acknowledged** repeat on an unchanged pane doubles the required quiet interval, up to `FM_WEDGE_ACKED_BACKOFF_MAX_SECS` (default 1800). The durable wake queue is the acknowledgement authority, read only inside the narrow band where it can change the answer - never once per poll per pane.

**3. A recorded window absent from a successful backend inventory produced no wake at all.**

The stale loop skipped such a window on the pane-capture failure, so a crew that died mid-wait was silent indefinitely, with its own `paused:` line explaining the silence. `paused:` declares that an *external dependency* is pending; it never declares that the worker itself may disappear.

Such an endpoint now surfaces on its own evidence, before and independently of any declared wait, and re-arms if the endpoint returns. Only a `missing` verdict qualifies - every other unreadable answer keeps the previous silence, so a backend hiccup cannot manufacture a wake.

### The two-consecutive-polls decision

The lost-endpoint alarm initially fired on a single `missing` verdict, which is also the normal shape of an ordinary cleanup: `bin/fm-teardown.sh` closes the runtime endpoint *before* it removes the task record, and the watcher enumerates windows from that record without taking the metadata lock. A poll landing in that gap sees a window that is genuinely absent and genuinely still recorded, and alarmed "inspect and recover" for a task completing normally - the same class of false wake this branch exists to remove.

The alarm now requires the missing verdict on two consecutive polls of the same window (`ENDPOINT_GONE_CONFIRM_POLLS`). A worker that is not coming back pays one poll interval of detection latency, which is irrelevant against a process that is already gone; a completing task pays nothing, because its record disappears well before the next poll. Only an unbroken run counts - any other verdict, including the transient `unreadable` a backend hiccup produces, drops the pending confirmation, so two hiccups a minute apart can never add up to an alarm. The pending record also expires after `ENDPOINT_GONE_CONFIRM_POLLS` intervals, so a marker left behind by a retired task cannot let a single missing verdict alarm instantly the next time that window name is recorded.

## Scope

`blocked:` and `needs-decision:` are unaffected - only the `paused:` and captain-held verbs are declared waits. The escalation ladder still reaches `demand-deep-inspection` for an undeclared quiet pane with no prior handled acknowledgement.

## Test evidence

Regression coverage drives the real `bin/fm-watch.sh` poll path against scratch-home fixtures in `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh`, not a reimplementation:

- `test_declared_pause_survives_a_redrawing_pane` - the declared-wait cadence across redraws, plus its `blocked:` exclusion.
- `test_acknowledged_wedge_escalation_backs_off` - an acknowledged repeat backs off; an unacknowledged one does not.
- `test_endpoint_gone_alarms_despite_a_declared_pause` - a dead endpoint still alarms under a standing `paused:` line.
- `test_teardown_race_does_not_alarm_as_a_lost_endpoint` - a first missing poll records only a pending confirmation; the task record is then removed as cleanup finishes and no alarm is queued.

The two existing ladder fixtures now pin the backoff cap so they measure the ladder rather than its spacing.

`tests/wake-helpers.sh` gains an opt-in missing-window flag file so a fixture can take an endpoint away and give it back mid-run, driving both the inventory and the capture - the pair real tmux actually presents for an absent target. Real-tmux evidence for that capture-failure behaviour (tmux 3.6a, macOS arm64) is recorded in `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md`. While adding it, `watch_bg`'s documented extra-env arguments were fixed: they went through as expanded words, which bash does not treat as assignments, so they became the command name.

Validated through the repo's `no-mistakes` pipeline (review, tests, document, lint all green) before rebasing onto current `main`.

title: fix(bin): stop stale-alarm churn on declared-paused and acked-quiet panes
body:
## Intent Fix the watcher's stale-alarm churn against tasks that are legitimately quiet: a task whose latest declared status is `paused:` must go on a long recheck cadence, and repeated identical staleness the supervisor has already handled must back off instead of escalating. This is firstmate's own repo; follow .agents/skills/firstmate-coding-guidelines/SKILL.md. The defect, with two dated reproductions. (1) 2026-08-25, task flp-mcp-bench: crew declared `paused: benchmark batch running, ~40-60 min expected`; 4 stale wakes fired in ~10 min anyway. (2) 2026-08-26, task qwenglm-bench, the decisive one: stale wakes fired at ~250s pane-idle, escalations 1 through 7 over ~35 min, cadence unchanged by the primary draining, handling and acking every one; the crew was MID-TURN continuously for over an hour (long foreground wait loops on a benchmark run) with ZERO crew turn-ends in the window, so any hypothesis that the crew's own turn-ends reset pause/stale bookkeeping cannot explain it; `paused: glm-5.3-flash arm running (3 memos, ~45-60m each), ETA ~150m` was appended between escalations 6 and 7 and escalation 7 fired ~4 min later, so the declared-paused long-cadence contract (AGENTS.md section 8) was not honored at all; the escalation counter compounded to demand-deep-inspection even though every prior stale had been handled and acked with the pane verified healthy each time. Investigation contract: reproduce before reading code - stand up a scratch home (never the live state/), with a fake crew pane that stays mid-turn and quiet, append a `paused:` status line, and run the real watcher against it; confirm the alarm cadence and the paused-state non-honoring on the real invocation path before any fix. Then localize: the stale predicate and its bookkeeping live in bin/fm-watch.sh (state/.paused-*, .stale-*, .stale-since-*, .wedge-escalations-* are its private records) and status classification lives in bin/fm-classify-lib.sh. Establish as fact, from code and the reproduction together: (a) whether the stale path consults the task's latest declared status at all; (b) what actually advances the escalation counter and what, if anything, was supposed to reset it; (c) whether the primary's own turn-ends disturb per-task pause records. Name the violated invariant explicitly in the fix commit. Required behavior after the fix: a task whose latest status line is `paused:` gets a long recheck cadence for pane-idle staleness, defined as a named constant with a comment, on the order of 20-30 min rather than 250s, and a subsequent non-paused status line restores the normal cadence; a `blocked:` or `needs-decision:` line is NOT paused and keeps the normal cadence; after the primary acknowledges a stale wake for a pane, an unchanged-still-idle pane does not re-fire on the same short cadence with an incremented escalation but backs off, while new evidence (a status append, a pane content change followed by fresh idleness) legitimately re-arms; the escalation ladder still exists and still reaches demand-deep-inspection for a pane stale WITHOUT a paused declaration and WITHOUT prior handled acks, so genuine wedge detection is not blunted; and a genuinely dead endpoint (process gone) must still alarm promptly regardless of a stale paused: line. Accepted decision on the dead-endpoint alarm: the endpoint-gone check must require the missing verdict on TWO consecutive polls before waking, which kills the teardown-race false alarm (bin/fm-teardown.sh closes the runtime endpoint before it removes the task record, and the watcher enumerates windows from that record without taking the metadata lock, so a poll landing in that gap sees a window genuinely absent and genuinely still recorded) while keeping the dead-endpoint alarm. Scope fence: only the watcher's stale/pause/escalation bookkeeping and whatever classification helper it needs. Do not restructure fm-watch.sh's arming, wake-queue, PR-poll, procevent, or Relay paths; do not change status-line syntax or invent new status states; do not touch supervision protocol docs beyond the minimal accurate update if behavior wording changes. No new configuration knobs unless the fix is impossible without one. Tests: regression tests must run the real watcher poll path against a scratch home fixture, not a reimplementation - one proving a declared-paused quiet pane does not fire on the short cadence; one proving the post-ack backoff; one proving a non-paused quiet pane still escalates; one proving a dead endpoint still alarms despite a paused line. Wire them where this repo's existing script tests live so CI runs them. Delivery: this ships as an OUTSIDE CONTRIBUTION. kunchenguid/firstmate is the upstream template we do not own; the captain's account is shadohead, an outside contributor with a fork at https://github.com/shadohead/firstmate. Push the branch to the shadohead fork and open the PR against kunchenguid:main. The PR body must reference upstream issue #3206, which reports this exact wedge-escalation-on-declared-paused bug, and must summarize the root cause, the two-consecutive-polls decision, and the validation evidence. State plainly in the PR body that this addresses only the watcher-triage half of #3206 and does NOT touch the Grok busy-footer matching that issue also asks for, and that it is independent of the alternative patch referenced there (josh-padnick/firstmate#10). Do not merge; merge authority stays with the upstream maintainer. ## What Changed - Keyed a declared wait's single prompt surface to the status log's `size:mtime` signature (`declared_wait_already_surfaced`) instead of the pane hash, so a `paused:` task whose pane merely redraws (progress ticks, token counters, resized footers) drops onto the long `PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS` cadence rather than re-earning an immediate stale wake on every redraw; a fresh status append re-arms the allowance. - Backed off the wedge escalation ladder for repeats firstmate has already drained and acknowledged: `wedge_escalation_due` now doubles the required quiet interval per acknowledged repeat up to the new `WEDGE_ACKED_BACKOFF_MAX_SECS` (default 1800s), while an unacknowledged escalation keeps the short detection cadence and still climbs to `demand-deep-inspection`, so genuine wedge detection on undeclared panes is preserved. - Added `endpoint_gone_check` with new `.endpoint-gone-*` markers so a missing-from-backend verdict alarms only after two consecutive polls, running before any declared-wait consideration; this kills the `fm-teardown.sh` teardown-race false alarm while still surfacing a genuinely dead endpoint under a standing `paused:` line. Documented the tunables and added four real-watcher regression tests covering paused-quiet suppression, post-ack backoff, undeclared escalation, and the dead-endpoint alarm. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-bounded to the watcher's stale/pause/escalation bookkeeping, is heavily commented, satisfies every required acceptance criterion, and ships regression tests that drive the real watcher poll path; the only notes are a minor config-knob addition and a harmless marker-cleanup inconsistency. ## Testing Ran the full fm-watch-triage suite against the real fm-watch.sh (exit 0, 0 failed), with the four new scratch-home regression tests passing; confirmed CI coverage wiring; then produced a product-level incident-reproduction transcript from the real watcher showing the exact wake strings for all four required behaviors (paused-redraw churn eliminated to zero extra wakes, non-paused pane still reaching demand-deep-inspection, dead-endpoint alarm firing on two consecutive missing polls despite a paused line) plus a raw tmux 3.6a backend-signal reproduction matching the committed verification doc. No product failures, setup issues, or flakiness; transient runner files were removed and the worktree is clean. This is a validation-by-testing pass only - the intent's delivery step (push to fork, open upstream PR) was intentionally not performed.
Evidence: Incident reproduction: literal watcher wake strings for all four required behaviors SCENARIO A (declared paused pane redrawing): extra stale wakes across 5 redraws = 0; pane never placed on short wedge timer -> long declared-wait cadence honored SCENARIO B (non-paused quiet pane): round1 possible wedge escalation 1 / round2 escalation 2 / round3 escalation 3 demand-deep-inspection SCENARIO C (dead endpoint under paused: line): WAKE> stale: bench:gone (endpoint gone: the recorded window is absent from its backend on two consecutive polls, so the worker's process is no longer running - a declared wait does not cover this; inspect and recover or clean up) ```text ========== SCENARIO A: declared paused: pane that keeps redrawing (flp-mcp-bench shape) ========== poll 1 (first sight of declared wait): WAKE> stale: bench:flp-mcp polls 2-6 (pane REDRAWS every tick under the SAME standing declaration): RESULT: extra stale wakes queued across 5 redraw ticks = 0 (pre-fix: every redraw re-fired an immediate stale wake; post-fix expects 0) RESULT: pane never placed on the short wedge timer -> long declared-wait cadence honored ========== SCENARIO B: NON-paused quiet pane still escalates to demand-deep-inspection ========== round 1 WAKE> possible wedge escalation 1 round 2 WAKE> possible wedge escalation 2 round 3 WAKE> possible wedge escalation 3 demand-deep-inspection ========== SCENARIO C: dead endpoint (process gone) alarms despite a standing paused: line ========== WAKE> stale: bench:gone (endpoint gone: the recorded window is absent from its backend on two consecutive polls, so the worker's process is no longer running - a declared wait does not cover this; inspect and recover or clean up) RESULT: lost-endpoint marker recorded (one wake, not a flood) ========== DONE ========== ```
Evidence: Four new regression tests - standalone pass transcript ok - an acknowledged wedge escalation backs off on an unchanged pane and still fires past the longer interval ok - a standing declared wait keeps its long cadence across pane redraws, a fresh declaration re-arms one prompt surface, and blocked: never earns the cadence ok - a lost endpoint alarms once on its own evidence even under a standing declared pause ok - an ordinary teardown's single missing poll never alarms as a lost endpoint ```text ok - an acknowledged wedge escalation backs off on an unchanged pane and still fires past the longer interval ok - a standing declared wait keeps its long cadence across pane redraws, a fresh declaration re-arms one prompt surface, and blocked: never earns the cadence ok - a lost endpoint alarms once on its own evidence even under a standing declared pause ok - an ordinary teardown's single missing poll never alarms as a lost endpoint ```
Evidence: Raw tmux 3.6a lost-endpoint backend signal reproduction ALIVE: list-windows -> 'verifywin' (rc=0), capture-pane rc=0 (readable) GONE: list-windows rc=1 (window absent = 'missing' verdict), capture-pane rc=1 (capture FAILS, not empty output) - the pair the watcher uses to tell a lost endpoint from a quiet one ```text # tmux 3.6a - lost-endpoint backend signal (private socket, no user config) # This is the raw tmux behavior the watcher's endpoint_gone_check depends on. --- ENDPOINT ALIVE --- $ tmux list-windows ... -> 'verifywin' (rc=0) $ tmux capture-pane ... rc=0 <- readable, window present in inventory --- ENDPOINT GONE (worker process killed) --- $ tmux list-windows ... -> 'no server running on /tmp/fmverify.37359.sock' (rc=1) <- window absent from inventory = 'missing' verdict $ tmux capture-pane ... rc=1 <- capture FAILS (not empty output), which is what distinguishes gone from quiet ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 2 infos - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:244` - FM_WEDGE_ACKED_BACKOFF_MAX_SECS (bin/fm-watch.sh:244, docs/configuration.md) is a new configuration knob. The intent states: 'No new configuration knobs unless the fix is impossible without one.' The fix is possible without it - the sibling ENDPOINT_GONE_CONFIRM_POLLS was hardcoded as a plain constant. It does follow the pattern of the adjacent tunables (STALE_ESCALATE_SECS, PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS, WEDGE_DEMAND_INSPECT_COUNT) and the ladder tests override it, so it is defensible, but it deviates from an explicit constraint and should be confirmed. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:831` - The .paused-declared-<key> marker written at bin/fm-watch.sh:939 is never removed by clear_pause_state or clear_pause_tracking (bin/fm-watch.sh:826-836), unlike every other .paused-* marker they clear. This is functionally harmless because declared_wait_already_surfaced re-validates the recorded signature against the current status file, so a stale marker can only match a status that is byte-and-mtime identical to when it was surfaced (i.e. the same standing declaration), never a false positive. It is a minor cleanup inconsistency, not a bug.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` - full suite, exit=0, total=1 failed=0; the four new tests (test_acknowledged_wedge_escalation_backs_off, test_declared_pause_survives_a_redrawing_pane, test_endpoint_gone_alarms_despite_a_declared_pause, test_teardown_race_does_not_alarm_as_a_lost_endpoint) all pass driving the real watcher subprocess - `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` - confirms the new tests are wired into CI lanes (rc=0) - `Bespoke scratch-home reproduction against the real fm-watch.sh capturing literal wake strings: paused-pane redraw churn = 0 extra stale wakes, non-paused pane escalation 1/2/3 + demand-deep-inspection, endpoint-gone alarm under a standing paused: line` - `Raw tmux 3.6a backend-signal reproduction (private socket, no user config): capture fails and window drops from list-windows when the endpoint is gone, matching docs/verification/runtime-backends.md` - `Verified bin/fm-teardown.sh closes the runtime endpoint before removing the .meta record, confirming the teardown-race gap the two-poll confirmation guards against`
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix(bin): report a cancelled validation run as stopped, not failed
body:
## Intent Fix a defect in bin/fm-crew-state.sh and contribute it upstream to this project (kunchenguid/firstmate), based on current main, kept small and obviously correct for a maintainer with none of the contributor's context. THE BUG: bin/fm-crew-state.sh reports a task as FAILED when its validation run was CANCELLED. That is wrong whenever the cancellation was deliberate, and it does not merely mislabel a row - it manufactures a false escalation. WHAT HAPPENED, TWICE IN ONE DAY: the tool provides 'no-mistakes axi abort --run ' specifically so an orphaned CI monitor can be reaped after its worker is gone; its own help says so. Doing exactly that, on work whose checks were already GREEN and whose pull request was open and mergeable, made the task read 'state: failed - source: run-step - run cancelled'. Supervision then surfaced it on its own as an inactive terminal outcome awaiting presentation, for a pull request that was open, mergeable and had zero failing checks. Had nobody been watching, a success would have been reported as a failure. THE SITES: three mappings in bin/fm-crew-state.sh, all collapsing the same way (the coarse runs-list row, outcome: cancelled, and top-level status: cancelled), plus the contract comment in the file header stating the same intent. WHAT IS WRONG AND WHAT IS NOT: cancelled is not failed. A failure means the work did not pass; a cancellation means somebody stopped the run. Those are different outcomes with different consequences, and collapsing them asserts something the evidence does not support - the same defect class as the merge claim already fixed in this file, where outcome=passed was rendered as 'PR merged/closed' for runs that merged nothing. It was explicitly ruled out to simply relabel it 'done': a cancelled run genuinely did not complete, and calling it success would be the opposite error. The accepted reading is a distinct terminal state meaning stopped, whose detail says the run was cancelled rather than that it failed. DECISIONS MADE DELIBERATELY WHILE DOING THE WORK, all three of which were required to be decided and explained rather than assumed: 1. Terminal state: cancelled now maps to a new terminal word 'stopped', added to the file header's documented output vocabulary. Not 'done' (the run genuinely did not complete) and not 'unknown' (that word means no reliable current-state source exists, whereas here the source is authoritative and says exactly what happened). The detail string 'run cancelled' is deliberately unchanged, so only the state word moves. 2. Whether the status log should win when it records a declared wait: decided NO, deliberately. In both real cases a paused: line naming the wait was already in the status log and was lost to the run-step source. Granting the log precedence over an authoritative terminal run-step was rejected because it would reintroduce the exact staleness this reader exists to prevent - the status log is an append-only event log that goes stale, so a paused: line left behind by a wait that has since cleared would mask a genuinely dead task as a healthy declared wait. A stopped crew still surfaces normally, so nothing is lost by leaving precedence with the run-step. This is a deliberate non-change; do not flag the absence of log precedence as an oversight. 3. What keys on 'failed' downstream: every consumer of this reader's output was swept rather than assumed. Exactly two read the state word as a decision - bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh, whose allowlist is 'done' or 'failed' alone and which is the consumer that manufactured the false escalation, and fm-classify-lib.sh's crew_absorb_class, whose allowlist is 'working' or 'paused' with everything else defaulting to surfacing the wake. 'stopped' correctly falls outside the first allowlist (this is the fix) and behaves identically to 'failed' in the second (a cancelled run was in neither before and is in neither now, so a stopped crew still surfaces exactly as before). bin/fm-fleet-view.sh, bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh and bin/fm-bearings-snapshot.sh render the state word verbatim or test only for 'working', so all are unaffected. Their test suites were run and pass. SCOPE CONSTRAINT AND ITS ONE DELIBERATE, APPROVED EXCEPTION: the change was scoped to two files, the reader and its tests, and must not widen beyond making this outcome honest or restructure the reader. A third file, AGENTS.md, was then explicitly approved after being escalated rather than taken unilaterally, because AGENTS.md's validation-judgment line stated this reader's contract as 'failed or cancelled is failed' - the defect at doctrine level. Shipping the reader fix while leaving that sentence asserting the opposite of the code would leave the next reader unable to tell which is authoritative. The approved edit was strictly ONE line, correcting the statement to match the behaviour and nothing else: no restructuring of the section, no added commentary, no explanation of the change there, because the explanation belongs in the pull request body. This three-file change is deliberate and approved, not scope drift. TESTS: red then green, to the bar the existing tests in tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh already set, which includes a negative test proving a guard is real by making it fail without the guard. Required coverage was the case that actually bit: a run whose steps all succeeded and whose PR is green, cancelled afterwards, must not read as failed. The fixture for that case was copied from the real aborted run's actual axi status output rather than invented. Three cancelled tests were added (outcome-cancelled after green, status-cancelled without an outcome line, and the coarse runs-list row) and each was individually verified to FAIL against the old mapping. A fourth is a negative control pinning that a genuine failure still reports 'failed', verified to fail if 'failed' is ever softened into 'stopped', so the split cannot become cosmetic. VERIFICATION ALREADY RUN LOCALLY: the full tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh suite passes; the adjacent consumer suites fm-inactive-reconcile, fm-classify-corr-token, fm-classify-decision-key, fm-fleet-snapshot-view and fm-bearings-snapshot pass; bin/fm-lint.sh is clean; bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh is clean. The change is independent of any harness and any runtime backend - it sits in the no-mistakes run-status mapping, upstream of every harness or backend read, and is not a harness-dependent check in the sense of the repo's coding guideline, so no live-harness guard or runtime-backends evidence refresh is owed. DELIVERY: this is an outside contribution, so the pull request body must be written for a maintainer who has never seen the contributor's environment - the symptom, how it reproduces, why cancelled and failed are different, what the tests prove, and one sentence saying AGENTS.md was touched and why. The body must not reference the contributor's internal task ids, operators, workers, or hosting. Do not merge; it is not the contributor's repository to merge into. This project requires maintainer approval before checks will run on a fork contribution, so green checks may not be reachable from the contributor's side. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` maps a cancelled run to a new terminal state word `stopped` instead of `failed`, at all three mapping sites (the coarse runs-list row, `outcome: cancelled`, and top-level `status: cancelled`). The detail string stays `run cancelled` and a genuine failure still reads `failed`, so only the state word moves. This was not a cosmetic mislabel: `bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh` records a durable terminal outcome and wakes the supervisor for a `done` or `failed` state alone, so using `no-mistakes axi abort` to reap an orphaned CI monitor - which is exactly what that command is documented for - made finished work whose checks were already green surface as a failure escalation for an open, mergeable PR. `done` would be the opposite error, since a cancelled run genuinely did not complete, hence a distinct word. - `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` now counts `stopped` alongside `done`/`failed` in its terminal in-flight inventory-drift check, so the new word does not silently drop out of that signal. Swept the downstream consumers for real: the captain fleet table renders `stopped / run-step`, `crew_absorb_class` is byte-identical before and after so a stopped crew's wake still surfaces, and the `terminal_in_flight` inventory check keeps firing (I reproduced the review-round regression by running the pre-fix `fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` against the fixed reader, where the check went silent). Verified red-then-green by driving each of the three new cancelled tests alone against the base reader — all three fail with the exact pre-fix output — and mutation-checked the fourth negative control by softening the coarse `failed` arm, which makes it fail. `tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh` and the five consumer suites (inactive-reconcile, fleet-snapshot-view, bearings-snapshot, classify-corr-token, classify-decision-key) all pass with zero failures and no flakiness observed. title: bug: a group-writable state/ directory silently kills every process-event source (watcher reconcile swallows 'not a private directory')
body:
_Filed from the reporter's secondary account because the primary one (NewAiCoder, reporter of #3517 and #3336) is rate-limited today; same person, not automation._

## What happened
`fm-procevent.sh` refuses to run when the state root is group- or world-writable (`state_root_bind` -> `fm_procevent_private_directory_valid` rejects any mode with the 022 bits set: "process-event state root is not a private directory"). That is a sound rule. But the watcher's `reconcile` call swallows the error, so on a home whose `state/` happened to be mode 775 (created by an earlier tool with a permissive umask) **no `when` source ever started for two days**: every pipeline-state watch `fm-spawn` armed was registered, hash-bound, and never polled. The only symptom was lanes sitting idle after CI went green, which reads like a worker problem.

Running `bin/fm-procevent.sh reconcile` by hand printed the error once; `chmod 750 state/` fixed it and the next reconcile started all 15 registrations.

## Suggested fix (any one of)
- session-start bootstrap prints a `PROCEVENT:` diagnostic line when the state root fails the private-directory check (and offers the chmod), like the other actionable bootstrap lines
- `fm-procevent-when.sh arm` runs the same check and refuses loudly at arm time instead of registering a source that can never run
- the watcher's reconcile surfaces the error as a `check:` wake once, not silently

## Environment
Linux, bash 5, latest main as of this week.

title: fix(bin): bind and fold Muse 1.1.1 session logs regardless of field order
body:
## Intent The request, verbatim: "How complex is the fix for muse ? Can we build it and push upstream ?" - followed, after the scope below was explained, by: "go". ### Outcome On Muse Code 1.1.1, Firstmate binds a Muse task to its session log AND reports that worker as busy while a turn runs and as settled after the turn ends, exactly as it did on Muse Code 0.1.0. AMENDED 2026-09-11 after the reproduce step: Muse 1.1.1 changed the log in two ways, a new leading `retained_frame` wrapper that moved session metadata off line 1 and the run-event field order, so both the log-binding discovery and the run-event fold must become format-independent for the outcome to hold. Firstmate authorised expanding to the binding after verifying the finding. **Nearest contrast:** session logs written by the older Muse Code 0.1.x must still be read exactly as they are today - the same run events extracted, and the same busy, settled and none verdicts. ### Problem **Why now.** Muse Code 1.1.1 (build 1.1.1-R2514.1) serialises each session-log run event with `"event"` before `"kind":"run"`, for example `{"payload":{"event":{"kind":"started",...},"kind":"run","run_id":"..."}}`, where Muse Code 0.1.0 wrote `"kind":"run","run_id"` first and `"event"` last. **What is missing.** `fm_busy_muse_run_events` in `bin/fm-busy-lib.sh` matches the 0.1.0 byte order, so on a 1.1.1 log it extracts no events at all. Observed on two real Muse Code 1.1.1 logs holding complete run lifecycles - two started with two terminal, and one started with one terminal, with terminal values `completed` and `cancelled` - the fold extracted zero events and `fm_busy_muse_run_state` returned `none` for both. Because Muse has no hook surface and its session log is the only busy source, Firstmate cannot tell a running Muse worker from a finished one on 1.1.1. **What already exists.** In the same file, `fm_busy_cursor_turn_state` folds a JSONL transcript structurally: with `jq` when it is installed and an awk JSON tokenizer otherwise, matching top-level fields of structurally valid JSON so text inside a record can never close a turn. The Muse run lifecycle itself is unchanged in 1.1.1: each turn is a `started` event paired with a `terminal` event whose `terminal` field is `completed` or `cancelled`, and cleanup records still carry a nested `"record":{"kind":"terminal"}` that is not a run ending. ### Contract Must: - Extract the same run id, event kind and terminal value from a 1.1.1-ordered log as from the equivalent 0.1.x-ordered log. - Keep the existing output that `fm_busy_muse_run_state`, `fm_busy_muse_active_run_id` and `fm_busy_muse_run_terminal` consume, so no caller changes. - Work both with and without `jq` installed, as the Cursor fold does. - Treat a malformed line as contributing nothing, never as opening or closing a run. Must not: - Count a nested cleanup record's `terminal` as a run ending, in either field order. - Count text inside an event, such as a prompt that contains `"kind":"terminal"`, as a run ending. - Change any other busy source. (The Muse log-binding discovery is now IN scope by the 2026-09-11 amendment: it must find the log whether session metadata is on line 1 or after a leading `retained_frame`, without changing how a task's session sidecar is written.) ### Scope and authority **Authorized:** the Muse run-event fold AND the Muse session-log discovery/binding path in `bin/fm-busy-lib.sh` (the functions that locate a task's session log and fold its run events); the Muse cases in `tests/fm-muse-harness.test.sh` and the live guard `tests/fm-muse-signals-live-e2e.test.sh`; the two documentation places that state the old byte order as fact, the comment block above the Muse fold and the Muse harness reference; one dated Muse Code 1.1.1 log-folding entry in the maintainer verification records. **Out of scope:** the Cursor, Grok and every other busy source; Muse interrupt, exit, trust-dialog, composer and process-identity handling; the Grok reasoning-effort ceiling, which a separate open pull request already covers; refactoring the Cursor tokenizer into a shared helper. **Return before:** changing the fold's output format or any of its callers; changing how a Muse task's session sidecar is WRITTEN by fm-spawn rather than how the log is READ (metadata now reports `workspace_root` as the parent directory of the checkout, e.g. `.../Documents/git`, not the worktree, so if correct binding cannot be achieved by reading alone, stop and return); adding a newly required tool dependency; accepting any change outside the Muse fold that review proposes; claiming Muse Code 1.1.1 is verified for anything beyond session-log folding. ### Completion proof - A portable regression feeding both 0.1.x-ordered and 1.1.1-ordered fixtures, each with and without `jq`, asserting the busy, settled and none verdicts and the terminal values. - **Negative proof of the nearest contrast:** the existing 0.1.x fixtures pass unchanged, with identical fold output before and after the change. - The nested cleanup-record trap asserted in the 1.1.1 order. - The live Muse guard run against a real installed Muse Code 1.1.1: failing without the change, passing with it, with the Muse version named in its output. - A dated maintainer-verification entry recording Muse Code 1.1.1 session-log folding, and only that. ### Expected change envelope **Class:** making one existing parser independent of field order. **Surface:** one function in the busy library, its tests, the two documentation places above, and one verification entry. **Not expected:** no new service, state, protocol, privilege, repository or required dependency, and no behaviour change for any other harness. ## What Changed - `fm_busy_muse_run_events` in `bin/fm-busy-lib.sh` no longer matches a fixed byte prefix. It now parses each session-log line as JSON, using `jq` when it is installed and an awk JSON tokenizer when it is not. It then matches `payload_type=runtime.session`, `payload.kind=run`, `payload.run_id` and `payload.event.kind`/`terminal` by structure. As a result, Muse Code 1.1.1's `event`-before-`kind` order produces the same tab-separated run_id, kind and terminal output as 0.1.x, so callers are unchanged. Malformed lines, nested cleanup `record.kind=terminal` payloads, and prompt text that contains `"kind":"terminal"` add nothing. - Muse session-log discovery used to parse only the first line of a log. It now scans the lines in the first 64 KiB for the `runtime.session.metadata` record, so a 1.1.1 log that starts with a `retained_frame` record still binds to its task through `workspace_root`. The session sidecar is written the same way as before. - Tests and docs: - `tests/fm-muse-harness.test.sh` adds 1.1.1-shaped fixtures. New cases assert the busy, settled and none verdicts and the terminal values, with and without `jq`, against the matching 0.1.x output. They also cover the nested cleanup trap in 1.1.1 order, prompt-text and malformed lines, and binding after a `retained_frame`. - The live guard `tests/fm-muse-signals-live-e2e.test.sh` puts the Muse version in its output and samples the fold while the session file grows. Only after that does it check that workspace binding picked the same log. On exactly `Muse Code 1.1.1 (1.1.1-R2514.1)` it skips the prompt-glyph check with a TAP `# SKIP`. - The Muse harness reference and the fold comment no longer describe the old field order. `docs/verification/muse.md` gains a dated entry covering only Muse Code 1.1.1 session-log folding. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is bounded to the Muse fold and binding path. It matches recorded 0.1.0 shapes, and on every real 1.1.1 log on this host the jq and awk paths produced identical events and verdicts. The fix round implements the user's six live-guard instructions exactly, with no extra machinery. ## Testing Real Muse Code 1.1.1 is installed here, so every scenario that needs it was driven live in an isolated tmux server and XDG data tree, each with and without the change. The live guard failed on the base commit: the old guard could not bind a log, and the new guard with the old library never saw the turn busy. At 1d1b809 it passed, naming the version, and it passed 10 of 10 back-to-back repeats, so it is not flaky. A live end-to-end driver used a real git worktree, a predecessor Muse session, and a binding written exactly as fm-spawn writes it. It held an echo turn open for 12 s and sampled the shared meta classifier: unknown, then busy muse-session-log for the whole turn, then idle muse-session-log, identically with jq and with a PATH that has no jq. Two real Escape interrupts were each read as cancelled and then idle, in both PATH modes. On the base tree the same flow stayed unknown throughout. The real bin/fm-control.sh interrupt command could not be run because its NO_MISTAKES_GATE guard refuses gate agents, so its key sequence was sent to the pane directly and its acknowledgement reads were checked. A fold-comparison driver showed identical base and new output on 0.1.x fixtures and on 0.1.x-ordered rewrites of the host's real logs. It reproduced the bug on the unmodified real 1.1.1 logs (0 events, none) and showed the fix (settled, with terminals completed and cancelled). Nine adversarial trap lines held with and without jq. The portable harness regression passed, and a version-string wrapper confirmed the glyph check still fails loudly off the exact 1.1.1 build. The fold comparison, the portable regression, and the docs diff review were offline checks, not runs against the live product, so they are recorded as untested for live validation. This change has no rendered UI, so the evidence is CLI transcripts plus captures of Muse's own terminal UI at each point. Scratch trees and the stale tmux socket files my runs left were removed, and the worktree is clean. - Live validation: ✅ go - 6 of 12 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Live guard on real Muse Code 1.1.1 fails without the change and passes with it, naming the Muse version in its output | ✅ pass | live | live-guard-without-change.log (both base variants fail), live-guard-with-change.log (all ok lines name 'Muse Code 1.1.1 (1.1.1-R2514.1)'), live-guard-repeat-10x.log (10/10) | | A Firstmate-bound Muse 1.1.1 task reads 'busy muse-session-log' for the whole running turn and 'idle muse-session-log' once it ends (jq installed) | ✅ pass | live | muse-111-live-classify-with-change-interrupt.log section 3: unknown, then 10 busy samples across the 12s turn, then idle. title: feat: add fail-closed command guard proofs
body:
## Intent The captain authorized building the `fm-command-guard-proof.v1` capability into Firstmate and opening a PR to Firstmate upstream right away. His words: "cứ full package và tạo pr right away đến upstream đi, tôi không đảm bảo nó sẽ được approve đâu, nên hãy làm kĩ, clean" - build the full package (the command guards and the verifiable proof together, not a guard-first / probe-later split), open the upstream PR now, and make it careful, clean, and minimal because upstream approval is not guaranteed. What the capability must be (stated in full so this stands alone): Firstmate's two mutating command entrypoints, `bin/fm-send.sh` and `bin/fm-control.sh`, must each answer an exact non-mutating probe invoked as `--guard-capabilities --json` by writing exactly one JSON object to stdout and exiting zero, of the form `{"schema":"fm-command-guard-proof.v1","command":"send"|"control","verified":true,"guards":[...]}`. The `send` proof must advertise the guards `spawn-generation`, `endpoint`, and `remote-host`; the `control` proof must advertise `spawn-generation`. A command may advertise a guard only if it actually enforces that guard, fail-closed, on every path the proof covers. The guards are real caller-supplied optional-environment checks enforced at the command's mutation boundary, so a programmatic client can prove a command will act only on the exact worker it authorized: - spawn-generation: when `FM_SEND_EXPECTED_SPAWN_GEN` / `FM_CONTROL_EXPECTED_SPAWN_GEN` is set, the command must reread the canonical task generation under the appropriate lock and refuse (nonzero, before any durable change, delivery, or lifecycle action) on a missing or mismatched generation; unset preserves ordinary behavior. For relaunch the precondition is the old generation, and success still publishes a fresh one. - endpoint (send only): when `FM_SEND_EXPECTED_ENDPOINT` is set, it must equal the canonical current backend target derived under the per-task metadata lock, or the send refuses before it enqueues, transports, or submits anything. - remote-host (send only): keep the existing rule that when `FM_SEND_EXPECTED_REMOTE_HOST` is set it must equal the canonical current remote host. The `send` proof covers every owned task-selector send path, including the typed-local path, so the proof never claims more than the command enforces; the explicit backend-target send form (an endpoint outside this home's task ledger) is excluded from the proof's authority claim, and that boundary is documented. `control` stays generation-only in v1: no control endpoint guard. Fail-closed throughout: any probe argv other than exactly those two arguments stays an ordinary command, never a positive capability; a missing or unreadable home, state, or metadata is a refusal; a set expected value with no current value to compare is a mismatch, not an ignored guard; the probe itself creates no state, records, or side effects. Do not change any Set Sail code. Delivery is through Firstmate's no-mistakes pipeline with a PR to upstream, and the captain approves the merge. Scope decision by the captain during validation, 2026-09-13: land the converged core in this PR and defer the remote second-mate spawn-generation coordination to a focused follow-up PR. The captain's choice was "Split: land core now" - exclude remote task selectors from the advertised spawn-generation guard in v1, ship the local guards, the probe, and the control path now, and build full remote parent-generation publication separately. This adds a second documented boundary alongside the existing backend-target exclusion: the send guard's advertised coverage - both the spawn-generation and endpoint guards - covers every owned local task-selector send path, including the typed-local path, and remote task selectors are excluded from that advertised coverage in v1. The remote transport path is a documented exclusion, deferred to a focused follow-up PR that will carry the validated identity to the host, enforce it under the remote metadata lock, and publish remote parent generation. Under this exclusion the proof never claims send-guard coverage the command does not enforce for remote selectors, so the parent no longer needs to carry endpoint, host, or generation into the remote command in v1, and the remote spawn need not publish a spawn-generation or perform a route recheck under generation in v1. The existing remote-host rule is unchanged. An empty state that would otherwise emit positive proof is a refusal, consistent with the fail-closed criterion above that a missing or unreadable home, state, or metadata is a refusal. ## What Changed - Added the `fm-command-guard-proof.v1` schema, exact `--guard-capabilities --json` probes, fail-closed preflight checks, and configuration/documentation for `fm-send.sh` and `fm-control.sh`. - Enforced caller-supplied generation, endpoint, and remote-host validation at guarded send boundaries, plus generation validation before control lifecycle actions, with lock-scoped revalidation and deferred stale-lease cleanup. - Reworked task-selector send locking and remote inbox delivery, and added focused proof, race, side-effect, and remote-delivery regression coverage with test-runner registration. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Captain, no source-verifiable material defects were found in the changed scope. ## Testing Drove the changed shell commands against isolated temporary homes and fake runtime endpoints. title: feat: reply in the captain's language
body:
## What

The captain-address rule is fully governed, but the **reply language** is not: a captain who writes in Turkish (or any non-English language) still gets English prose back. This adds two things:

1. A response-language rule in the identity section of `AGENTS.md`, layered onto the existing captain-address rule rather than around it.
2. A `config/response-language` knob documented in `docs/configuration.md`, following the existing local-gitignored-config pattern.

## Behaviour

- **Default: follow the captain.** Reply in whatever language the captain writes in. When the captain switches languages mid-conversation, the most recent captain message wins.
- **Optional pin:** a local, gitignored `config/response-language` file holding one non-empty line (`Turkish`, `Deutsch`, ...) names the language instead. Absent or empty leaves the default in force.
- **Chat prose only.** Commit messages, PR and issue descriptions, briefs, code, and comments keep the repository's existing language.
- **Never translated:** technical identifiers, paths, command names, and quoted command output.
- **Address rule preserved:** a Turkish-speaking captain is still addressed as "captain", inside the Turkish prose - the existing obligation is not replaced.

## Files

```
AGENTS.md             |  8 ++++++++
docs/configuration.md | 10 ++++++++++
2 files changed, 18 insertions(+)
```

## Verification

Run locally on the branch (`5cb844e`):

```
bash bin/fm-lint.sh --fast
  fm-lint.sh: ShellCheck 0.11.0 (pinned 0.11.0)
  fm-lint-workflows.sh: actionlint 1.7.12 (pinned 1.7.12)
  fm-lint-workflows.sh: 3 workflow files valid
  LINT_RC=0

bash tests/fm-ensure-agents-md.test.sh        RC=0   (6 checks ok)
bash tests/fm-gitignore-config.test.sh        RC=0   (5 checks ok)
bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh RC=0   (4 checks ok)
```

ShellCheck and actionlint were installed via the repo's own pinned installers (`bin/fm-install-shellcheck.sh`, `bin/fm-install-actionlint.sh`), so the local versions match CI exactly.

## Falsifier

If a firstmate still replies in English after this lands while the captain writes Turkish, and no `config/response-language` file is present, then the rule does not reach the reply path and this change failed its purpose. A secondary falsifier: if `AGENTS.md` grows by more than roughly 5%, the "keep this file concise" convention in its own closing section has been violated.

## Note on process

This reaches you as a plain branch push rather than through the `no-mistakes` pipeline described in `CONTRIBUTING.md`: that gate requires `no-mistakes` v1.46.0+, while the currently published npm release resolves to 0.62.1. Flagging it rather than silently implying the documented path was followed.

title: fix(bin): break teardown deadlock over a reassigned pool slot
body:
## What Changed

- `bin/fm-teardown.sh` now reads the slot-owner claim before the exclusive-record scan, for both the task's own slot and each child slot retired with a secondmate home. A claim naming another task skips the scan and gates off the slot's cleanup steps; a claim naming this task passes over an older crewmate record for the same slot only while that record's endpoint reads dead or missing, and refuses (even with `--force`) on any other endpoint state. Secondmate and Orca records still refuse either way.
- When teardown passes over a stale record it writes `slot_reassigned_to=<claimant>` into it under that record's metadata lock, so the mark stands in for the claim once the slot returns to the pool: that record's own teardown then releases nothing, and forced child cleanup reuses the preflight's reassignment verdict instead of re-reading a claim an earlier child in the same sweep may have already dropped.
- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` refuses a non-Orca crewmate `--relaunch` when the recorded worktree's claim names another task, carries the `slot_reassigned_to=` mark, or cannot be read. `tests/fm-teardown-endpoint-safety.test.sh` and `tests/fm-control-relaunch.test.sh` add cases for both teardown orders, the live-endpoint and secondmate refusals, the forced-secondmate child case, and the relaunch refusal; `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/agent-control.md` record the new ordering and marks.
- Teardown only queues that mark during the record scan and writes it once every refusal has passed, before its own records are written or any slot is returned, so a refused teardown leaves the other task's record unchanged (`test_refused_claimant_teardown_leaves_a_stale_record_unmarked`).
- A relaunch reads its slot claim under the Treehouse project lock that slot allocation and return take, refusing while either is in progress, and holds it until the replacement's record is published, so no spawn can claim the slot between the check and the launch (`test_spawn_relaunch_refuses_while_a_slot_allocation_holds_the_project_lock`).

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The change reorders safety checks in destructive teardown code and adds a persistent slot_reassigned_to mark, which relaunch and teardown both honour. I traced the main ownership-then-exclusivity order, the descendant preflight and cleanup gating, the mark's locking (including locks this process already holds for descendants), and the relaunch refusal under the metadata lock, and found no remaining path to the deadlock or to returning another task's slot. Because a mistake here destroys another worker's slot, the change should still be merged with care.

## Testing

I stood up a real fleet sandbox - a throwaway git repo with a real Treehouse pool (four leased slots), a dedicated tmux server on its own TMUX_TMPDIR, and a temp FM_HOME - and drove the shipped fm-teardown.sh and fm-spawn.sh exactly as an operator would, verifying results against real `treehouse status` and real tmux state rather than stubs. The claimant-first teardown that deadlocked on 2026-09-16 now completes and genuinely returns slot 1 to the pool; the stale record is marked and its own teardown leaves the returned slot untouched; relaunch refuses both on a live rival claim and on the mark; a rival record with a live agent still refuses with nothing mutated; a secondmate home still refuses a leftover claim; and forced secondmate teardown of two children sharing a slot returned it exactly once with the checkout intact. Replaying one fixture against the base commit reproduced the deadlock in both orders, so the fix is demonstrably the difference. The two repository test files this change touches also pass in full. This change has no UI surface - it is a shell CLI - so the evidence is command transcripts showing operator-visible stderr, pool state, and endpoint state. Driving the CLIs required the repository's documented test-harness escape hatch FM_GATE_REFUSE_BYPASS=1, because this gate agent's environment carries NO_MISTAKES_GATE; the drive touched only the temp sandbox.

title: fix(bin): stage contribution-input backlog through --slurpfile
body:
## Intent The captain, 2026-09-18, ruling D6 on the fleet backlog triage board: "Ship the fix now - it is small and it fires every session". Context needed to read it: bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh has one remaining call site that passes a whole backlog JSON document to jq through --argjson on argv: the contribution-input output mode near the end of the script (`jq -n --argjson backlog "$BACKLOG_JSON" --argjson tasks "$contribution_tasks" ...`). Linux limits one argv string to 128 KiB (MAX_ARG_STRLEN), so on the analytics home, whose backlog is about 85 KB in markdown and larger once structured, the read dies with "jq: Argument list too long" and the contribution-input read fails at every analytics session start. The earlier fix fix-fleet-snapshot-argjson-limit (done 2026-09-03) moved the other three call sites to a temporary transport directory and --slurpfile; this site was missed. The verified line is reported in data/fleet-backlog-triage-board/report.md: the remaining --argjson backlog pass is that contribution-input jq invocation near the end of bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh. ## What Changed - Moved the `--contribution-input` output mode in `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` off the `jq -n --argjson backlog "$BACKLOG_JSON" ...` argv pass, the last call site still doing so. It now stages the backlog and contribution-tasks documents into the shared temporary transport directory and assembles them with `jq --slurpfile`, so a backlog larger than Linux's 128 KiB single-argv limit (MAX_ARG_STRLEN) no longer aborts the read with "jq: Argument list too long". The transport-directory creation and backlog staging were reordered ahead of the contribution-input branch so it can reuse them. - Added a regression test in `tests/fm-contributions.test.sh` that builds a backlog whose structured form exceeds 128 KiB and asserts `--contribution-input` returns all 400 records intact through to the consumer. - Extended `tests/fm-home-summary-refresh.test.sh` to exercise `--contribution-input` in the large-backlog scenario, asserting the backlog records and tasks array survive alongside the existing json and secondmate-home-summary mode checks. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A small, well-bounded fix that moves the one remaining contribution-input jq call from --argjson to the established temp-transport --slurpfile pattern with byte-identical output, correct branch ordering, trap-based cleanup, and a behavioral large-backlog regression test. ## Testing I derived the scenarios from the intent (large-backlog argv overflow at the contribution-input jq site) and drove them live against the real script and its consumer. On the base script a 229 KB backlog (~1 MB structured, far over the 128 KiB argv limit) reproduces exactly `jq: Argument list too long` at line 1978 and silently emits nothing, causing the consumer to report all contributions as vanished (known:0, unreadable_records:1). On the fixed script the same backlog produces a valid 900-record document that the consumer reads intact (known:900). The existing contribution-input test suite stays green, confirming the small-backlog happy path is preserved, and I added a durable regression test that fails before the fix and passes after. Evidence is a CLI transcript artifact; there is no UI surface for this CLI/JSON change. - Live validation: ✅ go - 4 of 4 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Large analytics-home backlog: --contribution-input emits every record instead of overflowing argv | ✅ pass | live | Ran `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh --contribution-input` with a 229 KB / ~1 MB-structured backlog; exit 0, 900 records emitted, structured backlog 1,005,853 bytes (>131072 argv limit). Artifact: contributi… | | Adversarial/regression: base --argjson path dies with 'Argument list too long' and emits nothing | ✅ pass | live | Base commit script run from bin/ with libs loaded reproduced `jq: Argument list too long` at line 1978 with 0 bytes of output - the exact reported failure the fix removes. | | Downstream consumer reads the large contribution input intact | ✅ pass | live | `bin/fm-contributions.sh snapshot input.json --all` on the fixed output reports known:900; on the base empty output reports known:0 / unreadable_records:1, showing the real end-user damage the fix pre… | | Small-backlog happy path (existing behavior) preserved after the slurpfile change | ✅ pass | live | `bash tests/fm-contributions.test.sh` full suite exits 0, including all pre-existing --contribution-input scenarios (unobserved-head, away-yolo, etc.). |
Evidence: contribution-input argv-overflow before/after transcript Source: [contribution-input argv-overflow before/after transcript](https://github.com/haroarthur/firstmate/blob/7cef27e8c4e242793042af7f16f5ba1731901f49/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fix-fleet-snapshot-argjson-overflow/contribution-input-argv-overflow.md) ```text # Evidence: contribution-input survives the 128 KiB argv limit Change: `fm/fix-fleet-snapshot-argjson-overflow` (target 57bd5dc, base daaffdb). title: fix(bin): mirror captain hold and release into the worker status log
body:
## Intent

Fixes #4766.
Keep https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/4893 (issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/4766) mergeable: it conflicts with upstream main. Merge current upstream main into the branch, resolve the conflicts, and keep the PR's accepted behaviour and its opt-in shape unchanged, with only the smallest integration change upstream's forge settlement needs so a settled hold is retracted from the worker status log.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh hold` now declares the hold on a worker lane's `state/<id>.status` as one self-announced `captain-held [key=captain-hold-<task>-<n>]` line. Every settlement path (close, release, repair, reconcile close, and upstream's forge `settle-pr`) appends the matching keyed `resolved` retraction, and also retracts a `complete` transfer that is still a lane's last event once none of its named calls is open. A decision-only hold with no lane writes no status log.
- New `bin/fm-hold-status-lib.sh` replaces `last_status_line`, `status_declared_wait_line`, and `status_current_line` for the scripts that source it, and adds `last_worker_status_line`, `status_hold_settled`, and `status_worker_signature`. A standing hold stays visible to the watcher and the away-mode daemon, a settled hold is read past to the worker's last event, and readers of the worker's own state (crew state, inactive reconcile, AFK return brief, Herdr groups, Rex marks, capacity, OSC status) never let hold lines displace it. The watcher's re-surface throttle now uses the worker-only signature, so a hold or its settlement does not re-surface a lane.
- The decision fold in `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh` ignores hold-command retractions (`FM_OPEN_DECISIONS_FOLD_VERSION` 9 to 10), so a retraction cannot answer a worker's newer question. `fm_wake_status_append_self_announced` in `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh` now handles a status file that did not exist before the append. Docs and regression tests cover the mirror lifecycle, including the merge with upstream's forge PR settlement.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The merge leaves the PR's patch byte-identical per file except for upstream context lines, the one-line forge `settle-pr` retraction with its behavioural regression test, and the fold-emit adaptation; the fix round only sources the existing hold library in two readers, and both of its tests fail without that change.

## Testing

I drove hold, release, a worker re-ask during settlement, forge PR settlement (merged and closed, close and release) and the missing opt-in flag live against disposable homes, and every check passed. Six targeted suites and an 11-test lifecycle subset passed. The full captain-hold lifecycle suite and 36 of 54 watcher pause tests were not run in this turn because of the time limit, and real Herdr lifecycle was out of scope. No UI surface changed, so there is no screenshot.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 7 of 8 scenarios driven live against the product

| Operator holds a decision-only task with no worker lane: no status log is created for it | ✅ pass | live | live-hold-transcript.txt section S2 |

| Forge PR settlement: with config/hold-pr-settle set and a declared PR policy, fm-contributions.sh poll sees the PR merged or closed (local gh emulator, synthetic PR) and the held lane's status log get… | ✅ pass | live | live-hold-transcript.txt section S4 (14 checks) and tests/fm-contributions.test.sh (82 ok) |
| Adversarial opt-in boundary: without config/hold-pr-settle, pr-policy is refused, poll and settle-pr settle nothing, the hold stays open and the declaration stays standing | ✅ pass | live | live-hold-transcript.txt section S5 |
| Capacity ranking and OSC 7501 worker status read past a settled hold: a lane whose log ends in a hold retraction still counts as finished and reports state=done | ✅ pass | live | tests/fm-osc7501.test.sh t_settled_hold_keeps_done (runs the real fm-osc7501.sh watch) and tests/fm-capacity-auto.test.sh test_reclaim_ranks_idle_lanes, both suites exit 0 |
| Watcher pause throttling under a hold mirror: a settled hold over a done or paused lane surfaces once per cadence and never wedge-escalates, with upstream watcher key format | ✅ pass | live | suite-fm-watch-triage-pause-partial-18-of-54.log: the four hold tests added by this change passed (real fm-watch.sh against fixture homes); the run was cut after 18 of 54 tests with 0 failures |
| Real Herdr lifecycle with a held lane (Herdr groups view reading the hold mirror in a live fm-lab session) | ⏸️ untested | no | The verification plan puts real Herdr lifecycle out of scope, and an earlier turn recorded that bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh refuses on this host with 'fleet-state tripwire requires exactly one running default… |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Live driver: real bin/ CLIs + real tasks-axi against a disposable home.
set -u
REPO=$1
. "$REPO/tests/lib.sh"

NOW=2026-09-16T08:00:00Z
HEAD_A=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
eval "$(sed -n '/^new_home() {/,/^}/p;/^record() {/,/^}/p;/^forge_home() {/,/^}/p;/^with_home() {/,/^}/p' "$REPO/tests/fm-contributions.test.sh")"
reader() { bash -c '. "$1/bin/fm-classify-lib.sh"; . "$1/bin/fm-hold-status-lib.sh"; last_status_line "$2"' bash "$ROOT" "$1"; }
plain() { bash -c '. "$1/bin/fm-classify-lib.sh"; last_status_line "$2"' bash "$ROOT" "$1"; }
opens() { bash -c '. "$1/bin/fm-classify-lib.sh"; . "$1/bin/fm-hold-status-lib.sh"; status_open_decisions "$2"' bash "$ROOT" "$1"; }
show() { echo "--- $1"; sed -E 's/ \[at=[0-9]+\]/ [at=T]/' "$1"; }
FAILS=0
check() { if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then echo "PASS $1"; else echo "FAIL $1: got [$2] want [$3]"; FAILS=$((FAILS+1)); fi; }
H="$ROOT/bin/fm-captain-hold.sh"; T="$ROOT/bin/fm-tasks-axi.sh"

echo "=== S1 hold then release on a worker lane"
home=$(new_home s1)
printf 'kind=ship\n' > "$home/state/lane.meta"
printf 'done: PR ready https://github.com/o/r/pull/8\n' > "$home/state/lane.status"
with_home "$home" "$T" add lane 'Ship the thing' >/dev/null
with_home "$home" "$H" hold lane --reason 'Merge now or wait?'; echo "hold rc=$?"
show "$home/state/lane.status"
check 's1 held lane reads as captain-held' "$(reader "$home/state/lane.status" | sed -E 's/ \[at=[0-9]+\]//')" 'captain-held [key=captain-hold-lane-1]: Merge now or wait?'
with_home "$home" "$H" hold lane --reason 'Merge now or wait?' >/dev/null; 
check 's1 repeated hold adds no second declaration' "$(grep -c captain-held "$home/state/lane.status")" 1
printf 'merge it\n' > "$home/ans"
with_home "$home" "$H" answer lane --decision-file "$home/ans" --release; echo "answer rc=$?"
show "$home/state/lane.status"
check 's1 retraction written' "$(grep -c '^resolved \[key=captain-hold-lane-1\]' "$home/state/lane.status")" 1
check 's1 hold-aware reader returns worker line' "$(reader "$home/state/lane.status")" 'done: PR ready https://github.com/o/r/pull/8'
if with_home "$home" "$H" open lane; then echo "FAIL s1 still open"; FAILS=$((FAILS+1)); else echo "PASS s1 hold no longer open"; fi
with_home "$home" "$H" answer lane --decision-file "$home/ans" --release >/dev/null 2>&1
check 's1 retried answer appends no second retraction' "$(grep -c '^resolved \[key=captain-hold-lane-1\]' "$home/state/lane.status")" 1

echo "=== S2 lane-less decision-only hold mints no status log"
with_home "$home" "$H" hold q-only --title 'Pick a colour' --reason 'Blue or green?' --repo sample >/dev/null; echo "hold rc=$?"
check 's2 no status log for lane-less hold' "$(ls "$home/state" | grep -c '^q-only')" 0

echo "=== S3 worker re-asks while hold settles (adversarial)"
home=$(new_home s3)
printf 'kind=ship\n' > "$home/state/lane.meta"
printf 'working: started\n' > "$home/state/lane.status"
with_home "$home" "$T" add lane 'Ship the thing' >/dev/null
with_home "$home" "$H" hold lane --reason 'Which route?' >/dev/null

printf 'route A\n' > "$home/ans"
with_home "$home" "$H" answer lane --decision-file "$home/ans" --release >/dev/null; echo "answer rc=$?"
show "$home/state/lane.status"
check 's3 worker question still open after hold settlement' "$(opens "$home/state/lane.status")" $'route\tneeds-decision\tA or B?'
check 's3 latest event is the worker question' "$(reader "$home/state/lane.status")" 'needs-decision [key=route]: A or B?'
check 's3 no retraction under the worker key' "$(grep -c '^resolved \[key=route\]' "$home/state/lane.status")" 0

echo "=== S4 forge settlement (fm-contributions.sh poll, local gh emulator)"
for mode in merged closed; do
  home=$(new_home "s4-$mode"); forge_home "$home"; rm "$home/state/delivery.meta"
  touch "$home/config/hold-pr-settle"
  for action in close release; do
    id="question-$action"
    printf 'kind=ship\n' > "$home/state/$id.meta"
    printf 'done: PR ready\n' > "$home/state/$id.status"
    with_home "$home" "$T" add "$id" 'Decide this PR' --pr https://github.com/o/r/pull/8 >/dev/null
    with_home "$home" "$H" hold "$id" --reason 'Decide this PR' >/dev/null
    with_home "$home" "$H" pr-policy "$id" https://github.com/o/r/pull/8 terminal "$action" >/dev/null
  done
  printf '%s\n' "$mode" > "$home/forge/state"
  with_home "$home" "$ROOT/bin/fm-contributions.sh" poll; echo "poll($mode) rc=$?"
  for action in close release; do
    id="question-$action"; show "$home/state/$id.status"
    check "s4 $mode/$action retraction names the PR event" "$(grep -c "^resolved \[key=captain-hold-$id-1\] \[at=[0-9]*\]: captain call PR $mode: https://github.com/o/r/pull/8 ($action) by fm-captain-hold" "$home/state/$id.status")" 1
    check "s4 $mode/$action hold-aware reader returns done" "$(reader "$home/state/$id.status")" 'done: PR ready'
    echo "    (plain classifier reader, for contrast: $(plain "$home/state/$id.status" | sed -E 's/ \[at=[0-9]+\]//'))"
    if with_home "$home" "$H" open "$id"; then echo "FAIL s4 $id still open"; FAILS=$((FAILS+1)); else echo "PASS s4 $mode/$action hold closed"; fi
  done
  with_home "$home" "$ROOT/bin/fm-contributions.sh" poll >/dev/null
  check "s4 $mode repeat poll appends nothing" "$(cat "$home"/state/question-*.status | grep -c '^resolved')" 2
done

echo "=== S5 forge settlement opt-in absent (adversarial)"
home=$(new_home s5); forge_home "$home"; rm "$home/state/delivery.meta"
printf 'kind=ship\n' > "$home/state/q.meta"; printf 'done: PR ready\n' > "$home/state/q.status"
with_home "$home" "$T" add q 'Decide this PR' --pr https://github.com/o/r/pull/8 >/dev/null
with_home "$home" "$H" hold q --reason 'Decide this PR' >/dev/null
with_home "$home" "$H" pr-policy q https://github.com/o/r/pull/8 terminal close; echo "pr-policy without opt-in rc=$?"
printf 'merged\n' > "$home/forge/state"
with_home "$home" "$ROOT/bin/fm-contributions.sh" poll >/dev/null; echo "poll rc=$?"

if with_home "$home" "$H" open q; then echo "PASS s5 hold stays open"; else echo "FAIL s5 hold closed without opt-in"; FAILS=$((FAILS+1)); fi

echo "FAILS=$FAILS"
exit $FAILS

## Intent Implement Phase 1 only from data/fm-intake-classify-r1/plan.md: an opt-in Jev System One intake classifier recommending ship, scout, or answer-now plus urgency, without replacing firstmate judgment or auto-spawning. Do not implement Phase 2 wake triage. No broad suite, lint, or static analysis was run. The successful Jev response and forbidden Phase 2 wake boundary remain untested because the isolated run lacked a TypeSafe credential and a Herdr-lab-scaffolded lifecycle surface. - Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 3 of 6 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Operator leaves classification unconfigured and the optional classifier remains inert. | ✅ pass | live | Live intake-classifier CLI transcript: exit 0, empty stdout, exact `intake-classify: off` stderr, zero network syscalls, and zero created home files. | | Operator opts in and receives a Jev ship, scout, or answer-now recommendation with urgency; implementation authorization gates only ship. | ⏸️ untested | no | No TYPESAFE_API_KEY is available. title: fix(bin): create herdr task panes in their leased worktree
body:
## Intent

Create each task pane with its worktree as the working directory, so a reboot cannot resume a worker in the primary checkout.

This is the durable fix behind fm-reboot-resumes-workers-in-primary, split out of it by review on 2026-09-19. Task panes are created with the PRIMARY checkout as their recorded cwd; the agent then works in its worktree, but Herdr restores the pane's own cwd after a reboot, so every resumed worker comes back in the primary. This machine rebooted twice that morning (06:17 and 08:32) and both times every task pane resumed in ~/firstmate or ~/Yapii. The containment change detects and relaunches such a worker, but only once a firstmate session or the watcher runs, which leaves a window where a worker can act inside the primary checkout - the one thing the worktree-isolation rule exists to prevent - and nothing repairs it if no session starts at all.

## What Changed
- `bin/fm-spawn.sh`: herdr crewmate spawns now take a durable Treehouse lease up front with `treehouse get --lease --lease-holder`. The spawn reuses the task's own existing lease on relaunch if it has one. The task pane is then created with that worktree as its cwd, not the primary checkout, so a pane Herdr restores after a reboot comes back in the worktree. When a slot was leased, the spawn no longer types `treehouse get` into the pane. It just waits for the pane to reach the leased worktree. If a spawn aborts, the slot is returned only when that is safe. It stays leased, and a retained-lease record is written, when the spawn reused the task's earlier lease, the task pane survived, the agent had already launched, or the return failed.
- `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` adds a `TREEHOUSE_LEASE:` diagnostic that reports each retained slot along with the command to reclaim it. The `bootstrap-diagnostics` skill and `AGENTS.md` now document how to handle it (detect only, and inspect the slot before reclaiming). `bin/fm-teardown.sh` now closes a herdr crewmate's task pane, and confirms it is gone, before returning its worktree. The worktree is no longer returned from under a live pane shell.
- Adds `tests/fm-spawn-herdr-task-cwd.test.sh` and registers it in the test runner and isolation proof. Updates the herdr presentation, launcher-workspace e2e and bootstrap tests, and refreshes the stale comments in `herdr.sh`, `fm-wake-lib.sh` and `docs/herdr-backend.md`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The latest fix round is narrow and correct: it retains the lease once launch is delivered, keeps the pre-delivery flat return, and records the slot with a per-slot marker. But the whole branch reorders the spawn/teardown/abort lease lifecycle for every Herdr ship/scout task, and it knowingly defers two things (automatic reclamation, and a retried respawn after an aborted reuse starting in a fresh slot), so it merits merging with attention rather than as a trivial change.

## Testing

I drove real Herdr lab sessions through bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh with real fm-spawn and treehouse, and every lab was torn down with the default-session tripwire intact. Both real-Herdr e2e suites passed completely, including the new pane-cwd assertions and the projected restart assertion that the restored pane comes back in its worktree. My own lab script showed a flat pane restored in its worktree after a restart, while the base commit restored the same pane in the primary checkout, which reproduces the bug. The script also showed that an abort after launch keeps the live pane and the leased slot and writes a retained-lease record, which fm-bootstrap.sh surfaces as a TREEHOUSE_LEASE: line. The remaining abort and reuse edge cases are covered only by the focused spawn tests (fake herdr/treehouse), which all passed; they were not driven live. This is a CLI change with no rendered UI, so the evidence is lab transcripts. I cleaned up the scratch treehouse pools and the /tmp base snapshot, and the worktree is clean.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 5 of 6 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |

| A projected spawn creates its task pane in the worktree | ✅ pass | live | launcher-workspace-e2e.log presU assertion |
| After a Herdr server restart, a restored flat task pane resumes in its worktree, not the primary checkout | ✅ pass | live | live-lab-target.log RESULT A: PASS; the base commit in live-lab-base.log reproduces the bug |
| After a restart, a restored projected task pane resumes in its worktree | ✅ pass | live | presentation-e2e.log restart check (includes the restored cwd == worktree assertion) |
| Adversarial: an abort after launch delivery keeps the slot leased with the pane alive, records it, and session start prints a TREEHOUSE_LEASE: line | ✅ pass | live | live-lab-target-abort.log |
| Adversarial: aborts before delivery return the lease, an aborted reuse keeps its unlanded work, and a failed lease creates no pane | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result: only the fake-backed test (tests/fm-spawn-herdr-task-cwd.test.sh) exercised these cases. Forcing these exact failures in the real herdr and treehouse… |
