#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Live lab: flat task pane cwd + restart restore, and post-delivery abort retention.
# Usage: live-lab-scenarios.sh <firstmate-root> <label>
set -u
ROOT=$1; LABEL=$2
. "$ROOT/tests/herdr-test-safety.sh"
herdr_forget_inherited_pane
H="$ROOT/bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh"
S=$("$H" name "$LABEL") || exit 1
export HERDR_SESSION="$S"
TMP=$(mktemp -d "$(cd /tmp && pwd -P)/fm-live-cwd.XXXXXX")
WTS=()
cleanup() {
  for wt in ${WTS[@]+"${WTS[@]}"}; do treehouse return --force "$wt" >/dev/null 2>&1; done
  "$H" teardown "$S"; echo "teardown rc=$?"; rm -rf "$TMP"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
"$H" provision "$S" || { echo "provision failed"; exit 1; }
lab() { "$H" run "$S" "$@"; }
echo "lab session: $S   root: $ROOT ($(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD))"
PROJ="$TMP/proj"; mkdir -p "$PROJ"; git -C "$PROJ" init -q; echo x > "$PROJ/README.md"
git -C "$PROJ" add . ; git -C "$PROJ" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@e.invalid commit -qm init
git clone -q --bare "$PROJ" "$PROJ.origin.git"; git -C "$PROJ" remote add origin "file://$PROJ.origin.git"
mkhome() { mkdir -p "$1/state" "$1/config" "$1/data/$2"; echo off > "$1/config/herdr-presentation-spaces"
  printf '# Task\n## Captain'"'"'s intent\nLive cwd check.\n\n## Firstmate spec\nNothing.\n' > "$1/data/$2/brief.md"; }
spawn() { # home id
  env -u HERDR_ENV -u HERDR_PANE_ID -u HERDR_SOCKET_PATH HERDR_SESSION="$S" FM_SPAWN_NO_GUARD=1 \
    FM_HOME="$1" FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$ROOT" ${EXTRA_PATH:+PATH="$EXTRA_PATH:$PATH"} \
    "$ROOT/bin/fm-spawn.sh" "$2" "$PROJ" "sh -c 'echo live-ok; exec sleep 600'" --backend herdr --mode no-mistakes --yolo off; }
field() { grep "^$2=" "$1" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2-; }

if [ "${SKIP_A:-0}" != 1 ]; then
echo; echo "=== Scenario A: flat spawn, pane cwd, then server restart ==="
HA="$TMP/homeA"; mkhome "$HA" liveA
spawn "$HA" liveA > "$TMP/a.out" 2>&1; echo "spawn rc=$?"; tail -3 "$TMP/a.out"
WT=$(field "$HA/state/liveA.meta" worktree); WTS+=("$WT"); PANE=$(field "$HA/state/liveA.meta" herdr_pane_id)
echo "primary checkout : $PROJ"; echo "recorded worktree: $WT"; echo "task pane        : $PANE"
lab pane get "$PANE" | jq -c '.result.pane | {pane_id, cwd, foreground_cwd}'
"$H" stop "$S" >/dev/null && echo "lab server stopped (simulated reboot)"
"$H" provision "$S" >/dev/null && echo "lab server restarted"
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do R=$(lab pane get "$PANE" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.foreground_cwd // empty'); [ -n "$R" ] && break; sleep 0.3; done
echo "restored pane after restart:"; lab pane get "$PANE" | jq -c '.result.pane | {pane_id, cwd, foreground_cwd}'
if [ -n "$R" ] && [ "$(cd "$R" && pwd -P)" = "$(cd "$WT" && pwd -P)" ]; then echo "RESULT A: PASS restored pane resumed in its worktree"
else echo "RESULT A: FAIL restored pane resumed in '${R:-none}' (primary=$PROJ)"; fi

fi
[ "${SKIP_B:-0}" = 1 ] && exit 0
echo; echo "=== Scenario B: flat spawn aborts after launch delivery (In-flight commit fails) ==="
HB="$TMP/homeB"; mkhome "$HB" liveB
printf '%s\n' '# Backlog' '' '## In flight' '' '## Queued' '' '## Done' > "$HB/data/backlog.md"
printf 'backend = "markdown"\n\n[markdown]\npath = "data/backlog.md"\n' > "$HB/.tasks.toml"
FB="$TMP/failbin"; mkdir -p "$FB"
cat > "$FB/tasks-axi" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# fault injection: the backlog In-flight commit fails
case "${1:-}" in
  --version) echo 0.2.5 ;;
  update) [ "${2:-}" = --help ] && { echo --archive-body; exit 0; }; echo 'error: row could not be moved' >&2; exit 1 ;;
  mv) [ "${2:-}" = --help ] && { echo 'usage: tasks-axi mv [<id>...]'; exit 0; }; echo 'error: row could not be moved' >&2; exit 1 ;;
  show) printf 'task:\n  state: queued\n  held: no\n  blocked: no\n' ;;
  start) echo 'error: row could not be moved' >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
exit 0
SH
chmod +x "$FB/tasks-axi"
EXTRA_PATH="$FB" spawn "$HB" liveB > "$TMP/b.out" 2>&1; echo "spawn rc=$? (expected non-zero)"; tail -6 "$TMP/b.out"
echo "task record present? $([ -e "$HB/state/liveB.meta" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
M=$(ls "$HB"/state/.treehouse-lease-retained/*.retained 2>/dev/null | head -1)
echo "retained-lease record: ${M:-NONE}"; [ -n "$M" ] && cat "$M"
BWT=$(field "$M" worktree); [ -n "$BWT" ] && WTS+=("$BWT")
BP=$(lab pane list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.panes[]? | select((.label // "")=="fm-liveB") | .pane_id' | head -1)
[ -z "$BP" ] && BP=$(printf '%s' "$(field "$M" reason)" | grep -oE 'w[0-9]+:p[0-9]+$' | head -1)
echo "live pane for liveB:"; lab pane get "$BP" 2>/dev/null | jq -c '.result.pane | {pane_id, cwd, foreground_cwd}' || echo "(pane lookup failed for '$BP')"
echo "treehouse status of slot:"; (cd "$BWT" 2>/dev/null && treehouse status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -c --arg p "$BWT" '[.. | objects | select((.path? // "")==$p)] | .[0] | {path, status, lease_holder}')
echo; echo "--- fm-bootstrap.sh session-start output (TREEHOUSE_LEASE lines) ---"
FM_HOME="$HB" FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$HB" timeout 300 "$ROOT/bin/fm-bootstrap.sh" 2>&1 | grep 'TREEHOUSE_LEASE' || echo "(no TREEHOUSE_LEASE line)"

## CI status

Both workflows, CI and Require no-mistakes, show `action_required` with zero jobs: GitHub is holding them for a maintainer to approve running them on a PR from a fork. No step ran, so nothing failed. No code change was made for this; the runs need approval in the Actions UI.

## Real-Herdr verification

The Herdr end-to-end suites were run locally against real Herdr, each inside a named non-default isolated lab session through `bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh`, never against the live default session. They passed, including the new assertion that a task pane restored after a server restart comes back in its task worktree. `tests/fm-control-herdr-smoke.test.sh` fails locally at "a real agent-named foreground process reads 'shell' rather than 'agent'"; it fails identically on the base commit without this change, so it is pre-existing and unrelated.

## Deliberate limits and follow-up

- **Nothing reclaims a retained slot automatically.** An aborted spawn that cannot safely return its leased worktree keeps the lease and records it, and session start reports it on a `TREEHOUSE_LEASE:` line for a deliberate reclaim. Automatic reclamation is separate follow-up work.
- **A retried respawn after an aborted reuse starts in a fresh slot.** Sequence: a reboot leaves a husk in leased slot A; a same-identity respawn reuses A; launch or the In-flight commit fails, and the rollback removes the record while A is retained and recorded; the retry finds no record naming A and leases a fresh slot B. A still holds the previous worker's unlanded work, and `treehouse return --if-lease-holder` discards that work, so the slot must be inspected before it is reclaimed. Letting the reuse gate fall back to the retained-lease record would make an abort-time diagnostic record into spawn-path input, so it is left as its own follow-up.
- **A hand-edited retained-slot record is out of scope.** The writer refuses an empty holder or worktree, rejects embedded newlines, and commits atomically; the writer is the guard.

title: fix(herdr): confirm each pre-launch line submits
body:
## Problem

Firstmate could not start a worker on the herdr backend at all. Three launches on 2026-09-21 against herdr 0.9.1 - with the server running and the `default` session up - left the pane at a plain shell prompt with no agent ever starting, including one through `bin/fm-control.sh relaunch`, which reported the replacement dead after 90s. The backend was unusable and work had to fall back to tmux.

The visible symptom was a merged line: the staged launch source appended to an earlier `export` line, producing

```
export: not valid in this context: /tmp/fm-.../launch.s*.sh
```

## Root cause

`herdr pane run` is not at fault, contrary to the initial hypothesis. A pane capturing its own raw stdin receives every call faithfully, ordered and unbracketed, including back-to-back and concurrent ones:

```
CAPTURED=b'AAA\rBBB\r'
```

The carriage return is absorbed by the *receiving shell*, and only when two conditions hold together: the pane's shell has not finished taking over the tty at the first write, **and** a nested shell (`treehouse get`) follows. Neither condition alone reproduces, which is why the defect looked like an intermittent primitive.

## Fix

The fix lives in the send primitive rather than at each call site, so both `bin/fm-spawn.sh` and the `--relaunch` path are covered by one change.

After `pane run`, the primitive polls the pane until the line is confirmed submitted, reading two independent signals:

- the unwrapped render (`pane read --source recent-unwrapped`), anchored on a pre-write capture tail so only output produced by *this* write can confirm it
- the pane's foreground process group (`pane process-info`)

An absorbed carriage return is recovered with a bounded number of bare Enter keys, never by retyping the command. An unconfirmed line is cleared and reported so the caller refuses to append to it, preserving the existing 0/1/2 `send_text_line` contract shared with the cmux backend.

No sleeps are used to paper over the race, no call site changed, and no other backend is touched.

## Review findings fixed

Review raised two genuine false-submit defects in the first version of the confirmation, both fixed in this branch:

- **History-match false submit.** The fallback matched the text anywhere in the pane's unwrapped history. On `fm-spawn --relaunch` into an existing pane, that history already holds byte-identical `export` lines from the original spawn, so a line that had not yet rendered could read as submitted and the next line could merge with no Enter recovery. Confirmation is now bound to occurrences produced after the write.
- **Baseline window slide false unseen.** The first fix counted occurrences and assumed that count only grows. The unwrapped `recent` read is a windowed snapshot, so an old copy can scroll out of the top while the new echo arrives at the bottom, leaving the count flat and reading an accepted line as unseen. Confirmation is now anchored on the pre-write capture tail instead of a count.

## Evidence

A new live regression, `tests/fm-backend-herdr-launch-line-e2e.test.sh`, drives real `bin/fm-spawn.sh` launches and a relaunch inside an isolated herdr lab, never touching the fleet's `default` session. A pure unit assertion over a fake pane could not have caught this defect.

- Against the pre-fix adapter the test reproduces the original failure, including the `export: not valid in this context:` error.
- Against the fix on real herdr 0.9.1: 8 spawns and 2 relaunches, every pre-launch line landing as its own submitted command.

Ten portable cases cover the classifier and the primitive's four outcomes. The herdr fakes in the control, session-start and remote suites now model `pane run` and `pane read`.

One check inside the new e2e test was itself corrected: a two-line prompt redraws upward when the long launch line wraps, wiping the row just above it, so the render check now anchors on the first export row rather than the last.

## Documentation

The stale claim that the run primitive submits atomically is corrected in `bin/backends/herdr.sh`, `docs/herdr-backend.md`, and `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md`, which also gains the dated evidence for the current guarantee.

## Disclosed limitation

Two herdr tests are red on this branch and are **not** fixed here - they fail identically on the base commit under herdr 0.9.1 and are out of scope for this change:

- `tests/fm-backend-herdr-focus-flash-e2e.test.sh` - "the idle-shell proof never ran"
- `tests/fm-backend-herdr-presentation-e2e.test.sh` - "workspace order was not firstmate, stable primary block, secondmates"

They block the required CI herdr lane and need a separate change.

title: fix(bin): allow home no-op cd and safe reassigned teardown
body:
## Intent Kapten berulang kali melihat error cd-guard di transcript sesi ini dan minta diperbaiki: `/tmp/pi-clipboard-5cf01c57-0066-4d73-9f87-c5c41e355efa.png` menunjukkan dua perintah yang diblokir, keduanya berbentuk `cd ~/personal/firstmate && bin/fm-... --help`, dengan pesan `[persistent-cd] a persistent top-level directory change in the primary firstmate checkout is blocked ...`. Reproduksi (firstmate, di primary checkout): - `echo '{"tool_input":{"command":"cd ~/personal/firstmate && bin/fm-tasks-axi.sh --help"}}' | bin/fm-cd-pretool-check.sh` → deny `persistent-cd`, exit 2. - `bin/fm-cd-command-policy.mjs --command 'cd ~/personal/firstmate && bin/fm-tasks-axi.sh --help'` → deny juga. Dampaknya: perintah yang sebenarnya tidak memindahkan shell (target-nya home itu sendiri, tempat primary shell sudah berada) tetap diblok, jadi setiap agent yang menulis prefiks `cd && ...` melihat error yang tidak ada gunanya dan berulang. title: feat(bin): add opt-in contribution wakes for pull-request movement
body:
Fixes #3239. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-contributions.sh` now records each pull request's requested reviewers and teams (`review_requests`) in its observation, and `bin/fm-contributions.jq` gains a `movement` function that turns a replaced head, leaving draft, or a newly requested reviewer or team on an open pull request into pending `head`, `ready-for-review`, and `review-requested` signals. - These signals are off by default: `poll` emits them only when a regular file exists at `config/contribution-pr-movement`. Observations still refresh while the file is absent, so enabling it does not replay earlier changes. A first observation, or a stored one without `review_requests`, is the baseline, and merged or closed observations report no movement. - `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, the `bearings` and `operational-home-layout` skills, and the `bin/fm-pr-check.sh` comment describe the new flag, and `tests/fm-contributions.test.sh` adds cases for each movement type with the flag on and off, the baseline rules, the single watcher wake, and settled head changes. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The three movement signals are computed only when config/contribution-pr-movement is a regular file, so an unconfigured home produces main's events, seen, pending, wakes and status wording, and both earlier fix rounds are present in the code. ## Testing I drove the real fm-pr-check.sh, its registered contribution check, and fm-contributions.sh pending in disposable homes against a local gh emulator with synthetic pull request data. Without the config file, head, draft, reviewer and team movement created no signal and no wake, a maintainer comment still woke once, and the result matched base commit 427056c4 byte for byte. With the file, each movement created one pending signal and one wake, re-polls added nothing, enabling later did not replay old movement, and removing the file stopped new signals while keeping pending ones. A directory at the config path and a merged pull request both stayed silent. The targeted file tests/fm-contributions.test.sh also passed with exit 0, including the watcher checkpoint path. No UI surface exists, so the evidence is a CLI transcript. Real GitHub was not touched. - Live validation: ✅ go - 7 of 8 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Unconfigured home (local gh emulator, synthetic PR 8): head replaced, PR leaves draft, reviewer and team requested - no pending signal and no wake | ✅ pass | live | movement-transcript.txt section S1: pending empty, queued check wakes 0, while the stored observation shows the new head and review_requests | | Unconfigured home on the branch behaves exactly like base 427056c4 for the same steps, and a maintainer comment still wakes once | ✅ pass | live | movement-transcript.txt sections S1 and S6: RESULT line reports byte-identical pending view and wakes 1 == 1 | | Creating config/contribution-pr-movement after movement was observed does not replay it; a later reviewer request wakes once | ✅ pass | live | movement-transcript.txt section S2: wakes stay 1 after enabling, then 2 with one review-requested signal for 'second' | | Configured home: head, leaving-draft, reviewer and team movement each create one pending signal and one wake; unchanged re-polls add nothing | ✅ pass | live | movement-transcript.txt section S3: 4 pending signals, 4 wakes, unchanged after two re-polls | | Removing the config file stops new movement wakes and keeps the existing pending signals | ✅ pass | live | movement-transcript.txt section S4: head replaced again and third reviewer requested, still the same 4 pending and 4 wakes | | Adversarial: a directory at config/contribution-pr-movement does not enable movement; a merged PR in an enabled home reports no movement | ✅ pass | live | movement-transcript.txt section S5: pending empty and 0 wakes in both homes | | The real watcher checkpoint stays quiet on an unchanged PR and surfaces one 'check: contributions' wake for a replaced head in an enabled home | ✅ pass | live | fm-contributions-test.log: 'ok - watcher stays quiet on an unchanged pull request and surfaces its movement once' from `bash bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-contributions.test.sh`, which runs bin/fm-watch… | | Movement on a real GitHub pull request wakes an enabled home | ⏸️ untested | no | Driving this needs a push, draft toggle, or reviewer request on a live GitHub pull request. The run has no authority to change a live pull request for a test, and the verification plan states the same… |

directory at the config path, and merged PR while enabled --- config/contribution-pr-movement is a directory, head replaced pending: queued check wakes: 0 --- enabled, PR merged with a different head and a reviewer pending: queued check wakes: 0 ===== S6: UNCONFIGURED home on base 427056c4 (main) - same steps as S1 --- main: after all movement + maintainer comment pending: {"type":"comment","body":"Please clarify the contract","head":null} queued check wakes: 1 RESULT: unconfigured branch home == main (pending view byte-identical, wakes 1 == 1) ```

exit 1; } for f in new_home record forge_home with_home registered_checks queued_wakes; do eval "$(awk -v f="$f" '$0 ~ "^"f"\\(\\) \\{" {p=1} p {print} p && /^}/ {exit}' "$WT/tests/fm-contributions.test.sh")" done show() { # home label printf -- '--- %s\n' "$2" printf 'pending: '; with_home "$1" "$ROOT/bin/fm-contributions.sh" pending | jq -c '.[] | {type,body,head}' printf 'queued check wakes: %s\n' "$(queued_wakes "$1")" } setup() { # name on|off local home; home=$(new_home "$1"); forge_home "$home" >&2 [ "$2" = off ] || touch "$home/config/contribution-pr-movement" with_home "$home" "$ROOT/bin/fm-pr-check.sh" delivery https://github.com/o/r/pull/8 >/dev/null || fail register registered_checks "$home" >/dev/null printf '%s\n' "$home" } move_all() { # home: head replaced, draft->ready, reviewer and team requested printf 'true\n' > "$1/forge/draft"; registered_checks "$1" >/dev/null printf 'false\n' > "$1/forge/draft" printf '%s\n' "$HEAD_B" > "$1/forge/head" printf '[{"login":"reviewer"}]\n' > "$1/forge/requested.json" printf '[{"slug":"core","name":"Core"}]\n' > "$1/forge/teams.json" registered_checks "$1" >/dev/null } maintainer_comment() { jq -n '[{id:12,user:{login:"maintainer"},author_association:"OWNER",body:"Please clarify the contract", html_url:"https://github.com/o/r/pull/8#issuecomment-12",updated_at:"2026-09-16T08:01:00Z",submitted_at:"2026-09-16T08:01:00Z"}]' \ > "$1/forge/comments.json" registered_checks "$1" >/dev/null } ROOT=$WT echo "===== S1: UNCONFIGURED home (no config/contribution-pr-movement), branch code" h=$(setup s1-off off); ls "$h/config"; show "$h" "after first poll, nothing moved" move_all "$h"; show "$h" "after head replaced + left draft + reviewer + team requested" jq -c '.records[0].observation | {head,draft,review_requests}' "$h/data/delivery/contributions.json" maintainer_comment "$h"; show "$h" "after a maintainer comment (existing trigger must still wake)" S1_PENDING=$(with_home "$h" "$ROOT/bin/fm-contributions.sh" pending | jq -c '[.[]|{type,body,head,token}]'); S1_WAKES=$(queued_wakes "$h") S1_VIEW=$(with_home "$h" "$ROOT/bin/fm-contributions.sh" pending | jq -S .) echo; registered_checks "$h" >/dev/null show "$h" "a second reviewer requested while enabled" echo; echo "===== S3: CONFIGURED home, each trigger wakes exactly once" h=$(setup s3-on on); show "$h" "after first poll, nothing moved" move_all "$h"; echo "===== S4: REMOVE the file - new movement silent, pending kept" rm "$h/config/contribution-pr-movement" printf '%s\n' "$HEAD_A" > "$h/forge/head"; printf '[{"login":"reviewer"},{"login":"third"}]\n' > "$h/forge/requested.json" registered_checks "$h" >/dev/null; show "$h" "file removed, head replaced again, third reviewer requested" echo; echo "===== S5: ADVERSARIAL - directory at the config path, and merged PR while enabled" h=$(setup s5-dir off); mkdir "$h/config/contribution-pr-movement" printf '%s\n' "$HEAD_B" > "$h/forge/head"; registered_checks "$h" >/dev/null show "$h" "config/contribution-pr-movement is a directory, head replaced" h=$(setup s5-merged on); printf 'merged\n' > "$h/forge/state"; printf '%s\n' "$HEAD_B" > "$h/forge/head" printf '[{"login":"reviewer"}]\n' > "$h/forge/requested.json"; registered_checks "$h" >/dev/null show "$h" "enabled, PR merged with a different head and a reviewer" echo; echo "===== S6: UNCONFIGURED home on base 427056c4 (main) - same steps as S1" ROOT=$BASE h=$(setup s6-base off); move_all "$h"; maintainer_comment "$h"; show "$h" "main: after all movement + maintainer comment" B_PENDING=$(with_home "$h" "$ROOT/bin/fm-contributions.sh" pending | jq -c '[.[]|{type,body,head,token}]'); title: fix(bin): retain pending inbox note wakes through acknowledgement
body:
## Intent Rebase of upstream PR https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/5493 onto current upstream main (30ef650d) with its intent unchanged; the only conflicts were the bin/fm-wake-drain.sh header comment and docs/watcher-continuity.md, which upstream had restructured into subsections, so the pending-inbox-note acknowledgement rule was placed into the new "Acknowledgement cutoffs" subsection. Original intent: captain inbox notes were being dropped - an inbox note check wake was announced, the wake queue drained and acknowledged through a range covering it, and the root never saw the note, while fm-inbox.sh announce refuses to re-append. The fix keeps an inbox: check wake row queued while state/inbox/.note is still pending, so an --ack-through cannot discard it before the note is handled with bin/fm-inbox.sh drain --ack ; main acknowledgement keeps the row claimed for the next drain, branch acknowledgement releases it for the next grant or main drain. Deliver a regression test that appends one inbox note wake among 40 status wakes and asserts the note is presented and survives an ack-through, plus same-turn handling, late arrivals, and branch grants. No new behavior beyond the original PR; do not expand scope. ## What Changed - Keep an `inbox:` check wake queued while its note is pending. Main acknowledgement retains its claim; branch acknowledgement releases it for a later grant or main drain. - Document when the wake can be consumed and add regression coverage for presentation among 40 status wakes, same-turn handling, late arrivals, and branch grants. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The pending-note retention is bounded to acknowledged inbox wake rows, and the reviewed main and branch paths preserve the intended claim and grant behavior. ## Testing The targeted regression test covered 40 status wakes, same-turn handling, late arrivals, and branch grants, but did not establish live results for those scenarios. A direct lab CLI run confirmed that a pending note reappears after wake acknowledgement and its row is consumed after the note is handled. - Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 1 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A pending inbox note is presented again after the caller acknowledges its wake, then its row is consumed after the note is handled | ✅ pass | live | Inbox note CLI transcript | | A note among 40 status wakes is presented and survives wake acknowledgement | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload records only a regression test, not a live product run of this scenario; drive it against the running product to establish a live result. | | Handling a note in the same turn allows its wake row to be consumed | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload records only a regression test, not a live product run of this scenario; drive it against the running product to establish a live result. | | A late arrival remains grantable while an earlier pending note is retained | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload records only a regression test, not a live product run of this scenario; drive it against the running product to establish a live result. | | An away-branch acknowledgement releases a pending note for the next branch grant | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload records only a regression test, not a live product run of this scenario; drive it against the running product to establish a live result. |

title: fix(bin): enforce no AI self-attribution in crewmate commits and PRs
body:
## Intent A real commit on a captain project (toolbox-all-in-one, PR #11, since amended and fixed) carried a `Co-Authored-By: Claude ` trailer, despite `bin/fm-spawn.sh`'s launch template already passing Claude Code's `attribution: {"commit": "", "pr": "", "sessionUrl": false}` settings and its own comment claiming "a spawned worker never writes a Co-Authored-By trailer." That claim is now proven false by direct evidence. The captain's standing rule (AGENTS.md section 1: "Never add an agent name as a commit co-author," also in this skill's repo style rules) must actually hold for every future crewmate spawn, not just be asserted in a comment. ## What Changed - Added a check for AI self-attribution, `bin/fm-attribution-pretool-check.sh`. It rejects a `Co-Authored-By` trailer that names an AI, a "Generated with" line, or a Claude session link, and it checks both inline messages and passed message files. It runs in two places: - As the `commit-msg` hook, which rejects the commit. - As a Bash PreToolUse hook in each claude task worker's worktree `.claude/settings.local.json`. There it also denies `gh`/`gh-axi` PR create, edit, comment, review and merge, and `gh api` writes, when they carry attribution. Read-only commands such as `git log | grep`, `gh pr view` and GET `gh api` are always allowed. - `fm-spawn.sh` now sets a per-worktree `core.hooksPath` for every ship and scout worktree on every harness. It points at the new `bin/git-hooks` dispatcher (`fm-worktree-git-hook.sh`, managed by `fm-worktree-hooks-lib.sh`), which enables `extensions.worktreeConfig` if needed: - Its `commit-msg` runs the attribution check. Every hook then hands off to the project's own hook of the same name. - If the hook can't be installed, the spawn is refused. That includes projects whose shared config sets `core.bare` or `core.worktree`. - `fm-teardown.sh` removes the pointer again. - The ship and scout briefs now include a shared rule against attribution (`fm_attribution_rule` in `fm-dod-lib.sh`). The code comments and docs (`configuration.md`, `scripts.md`, `runtime-backends.md`, the claude harness reference) now say that Claude Code's `attribution` setting alone doesn't stop the model typing a trailer itself. The docs also list what the hook doesn't cover: `--no-verify` commits and commits made by no-mistakes pipeline agents. New tests are `fm-attribution-pretool-check.test.sh` and a live e2e test. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The latest fix round is small and correct: a literal \n or \r in command text now counts as a line start, so the escaped-newline PR footer is denied again and the mid-sentence allow cases still pass. Both new deny regressions would have failed before the fix. The branch as a whole still adds enforcement to every crewmate spawn (a worktree-wide core.hooksPath, the commit-msg hook and the PreToolUse guard), and those regex heuristics have needed several correction rounds, so it deserves moderate caution. ## Testing I ran two tests: the focused attribution regression test, which passed, and the opt-in live Claude e2e, where real Claude Code tried an attributed commit, got a refusal in its own tool result, and then landed a clean commit. I also recorded two manual transcripts. One is a codex-harness fm-spawn followed by real git commits: AI trailers and footers were refused, human co-authors were allowed, the project's hooks still ran, the primary checkout was untouched, and teardown cleared the pointer. The other is adversarial PreToolUse probes for PR text and gh api. Everything behaved as intended. title: fm-send doorbell left unsubmitted in idle Claude worker composer on Herdr; re-ring then skips it as pending text
body:
## Summary

On the Herdr backend with idle Claude Code workers, `bin/fm-send.sh` sometimes types the steering doorbell line into the worker's composer but the submitting Enter never lands. The line then sits unsubmitted in the composer, and the watcher's re-ring does not clear it, so the worker never reads the durable inbox message until someone presses Enter.

## Evidence (one evening, host load 17-29 on an 8-core Mac)

- Four occurrences on three different Claude Code workers (Sonnet and Opus).
- `fm-send` output: `fm-send: doorbell did not reach default:<ws>:<pane>; the steer is durably recorded at .../inbox/00N.msg and the watcher will re-ring`
- A later send to one of them: `fm-send: doorbell skipped (composer visibly holds pending text); ...`, because the earlier unsubmitted doorbell was still in the composer.
- Peek showed the composer holding `: Firstmate instruction waiting: list '.../inbox'/*.msg ...`, unsubmitted, with the worker idle.
- In one case a worker that had reported `done` sat idle for about 10 minutes (stale wake `idle 625s, possible wedge`) because its rework steer never submitted.
- `herdr pane send-keys <pane> Enter` submitted it immediately every time.

## Impact

Durable steers silently wait unread, and later steers are skipped because the composer "holds pending text": the unsubmitted doorbell blocks its own re-ring.

## Expected

When the composer holds exactly the doorbell line that Firstmate itself typed, the re-ring (or the next `fm-send`) should submit it with Enter rather than treat it as foreign pending text. Alternatively, retry Enter under the same idle-baseline confirmation the away-mode submit path already uses.

title: fm-remote-doctor.sh --fix hangs over SSH when it starts the Herdr server (first remote seed or secondmate spawn after a host reboot never returns)
body:
Speaking as a user's firstmate.

## Symptom

On a Linux remote second-mate host, after the host reboots, the first `bin/fm-spawn.sh <id> --secondmate` or `bin/fm-remote-home-seed.sh` against that host hangs forever.
It was seen twice, on two different remote second mates (both NixOS VMs), right after a VM reboot.
Interrupting the local command and rerunning it works, because by then the server is already up.

On the remote host, the leftover process tree looks like this after the local command is interrupted (pids and paths generic):

```
  PID  PPID   SID COMMAND
 3901     1  3747 bash ~/firstmate/bin/fm-remote-doctor.sh --fix
 3904  3901  3747 herdr server --session fm-remote
```

The `bash ... fm-remote-doctor.sh --fix` process is not the doctor itself: it is a background fork of the doctor that never exec'd, and it still holds the SSH channel's stdout and stderr pipes:

```
/proc/3901/fd: 0 -> /dev/null, 1 -> /dev/null, 2 -> /dev/null,
               10 -> pipe:[13112] (write end), 11 -> pipe:[13113] (write end)
```

## Trigger, masking condition, symptom

- Trigger: `fm-remote-doctor.sh --fix` runs over a non-interactive SSH command channel while the `fm-remote` Herdr server is down (for example, right after a reboot), so `start_herdr_server` calls `fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure` and actually launches the server.
- Masking condition: if the server is already running, `fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure` returns before forking anything, so nothing hangs. That is why the second run always passes.
- Symptom: sshd waits for EOF on the command's stdout and stderr, which never comes, so the `fm-on.sh ... fm-remote-doctor.sh --fix` call never returns, and neither does the seed or spawn that ran it.

## Root cause

`start_herdr_server` calls `fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure "$HERDR_SESSION_NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1`.
While a redirect on a function call is active, bash keeps copies of the original stdout and stderr (here the SSH channel's pipes) on high descriptors (10 and 11).
Those copies are close-on-exec, so they only matter to a process that never execs.

Inside `fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure`, the server is started as `fm_backend_herdr_cli "$session" server >/dev/null 2>&1 &`.
The background job is a forked bash running a function, and that function runs `herdr server` as a child and waits for it instead of exec'ing it.
So the fork stays a bash process for the server's whole lifetime, inheriting fds 10 and 11, and keeps the caller's stdout and stderr open.
The doctor itself exits normally, but the channel never reaches EOF.

It is not specific to the doctor: any caller of `fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure` that reads the command's output to EOF, while that output is redirected at the call site, has the same exposure.

## Reproduction

This needs no real Herdr and no SSH.
A stub `herdr` whose `server` subcommand stays alive like the real one, plus a caller that reads to EOF the way an SSH command channel does, is enough:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/repro/bin
cat > /tmp/repro/bin/herdr <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
case "$1" in
  status) [ -e /tmp/repro/running ] && r=true || r=false; printf '{"server":{"running":%s}}\n' "$r" ;;
  server) : > /tmp/repro/running; while [ ! -e /tmp/repro/stop ]; do sleep 0.1; done; rm -f /tmp/repro/running ;;
esac
SH
chmod +x /tmp/repro/bin/herdr
# From a firstmate checkout; `| cat` finishes only at EOF, like sshd.
PATH=/tmp/repro/bin:$PATH bash -c '. bin/backends/herdr.sh; fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure demo >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "ensure rc=$?"' | cat
# Hangs on the current main until `touch /tmp/repro/stop`; returns at once with the fix.
```

Two counterfactuals confirm the cause:

- Calling `fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure` without the call-site `>/dev/null 2>&1` (so bash saves no copies of the caller's stdout and stderr) makes the channel close at once, even on the current code.
- With the fix below, the channel closes at once and the server runs as its own session leader, reparented, with only `/dev/null` on stdio and no leftover shell copy.

## Proposed fix

Launch the server fully detached, at the one place every caller goes through (`fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure`):

- stdio on `/dev/null`;
- every other inherited descriptor closed;
- the launch subshell replaced by the server (`exec`), in a new session: `setsid(1)` where present, `perl`'s `POSIX::setsid` where it is not (macOS), and a plain `exec` otherwise, which still leaves no shell copy behind.

The existing bounded readiness poll then returns once the server reports running.
The macOS launch-agent start path in the doctor goes through `launchctl` rather than this function, so it is unchanged.
`fm_backend_herdr_cli`'s own `server` branch keeps its foreground behavior (an existing client-selection test drives it directly).
The per-session client choice moves into a small shared helper, so the detached launch uses exactly the client `fm_backend_herdr_cli` would.

The regression test sits in `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh`, next to the existing `server_ensure` test.
It drives the doctor's call shape under a caller that reads to EOF, bounded at 10 seconds, and also checks that the server left the caller's session when python3 is available.

Patch against upstream `main` at a256cb525a50a2bc14d3d3ab1a92b179c6214aae:

```diff
diff --git a/bin/backends/herdr.sh b/bin/backends/herdr.sh
index cf908fa1..7c5898d4 100644
--- a/bin/backends/herdr.sh
+++ b/bin/backends/herdr.sh
@@ -369,6 +369,17 @@ fm_backend_herdr_workspace_label() {
   printf 'firstmate'
 }
 
+# fm_backend_herdr_session_client: the herdr client for <session> - the one
+# already selected for that exact session, or the first `herdr` on PATH (see
+# "client selection" below).
+fm_backend_herdr_session_client() {  # <session>
+  if [ "${FM_BACKEND_HERDR_CLIENT_SESSION:-}" = "$1" ]; then
+    fm_backend_herdr_bin
+  else
+    printf '%s' herdr
+  fi
+}
+
 # fm_backend_herdr_cli: run `herdr <args...>` scoped to <session>, setting
 # BOTH the HERDR_SESSION env var AND appending a trailing `--session <name>`
 # CLI flag. Verified empirically (docs/herdr-backend.md "Session targeting: the
@@ -385,11 +396,9 @@ fm_backend_herdr_workspace_label() {
 # fm_backend_herdr_version_check, which is intentionally session-independent
 # (reads only .client.* fields).
 fm_backend_herdr_cli() {  # <session> <herdr-subcommand-and-args...>
-  local session=$1 rc=0 err failed_bin selected_bin client_bin=herdr
+  local session=$1 rc=0 err failed_bin selected_bin client_bin
   shift
-  if [ "${FM_BACKEND_HERDR_CLIENT_SESSION:-}" = "$session" ]; then
-    client_bin=$(fm_backend_herdr_bin)
-  fi
+  client_bin=$(fm_backend_herdr_session_client "$session")
   # stderr is buffered (stdout streams untouched) so a protocol_mismatch
   # refusal can be recognized and retried once on a compatible client; see
   # "client selection" below. A failed command's stderr is replayed verbatim.
@@ -1645,6 +1654,32 @@ fm_backend_herdr_projection_order_best_effort() {  # <session> <created-workspac
   return 0
 }
 
+# fm_backend_herdr_close_inherited_fds: close every descriptor above stderr in
+# the calling shell, for the detached server launch below.
+fm_backend_herdr_close_inherited_fds() {
+  local entry fd
+  for entry in /dev/fd/*; do
+    fd=${entry##*/}
+    case "$fd" in ''|*[!0-9]*) continue ;; esac
+    [ "$fd" -gt 2 ] || continue
+    eval "exec $fd>&-" 2>/dev/null || true
+  done
+}
+
+# fm_backend_herdr_exec_new_session: replace the calling shell with <cmd...>
+# running in a new session, away from the caller's session and controlling
+# terminal. util-linux setsid(1) is absent on macOS, where perl's POSIX::setsid
+# covers it; with neither, the command still replaces the shell.
+fm_backend_herdr_exec_new_session() {  # <cmd> [args...]
+  if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    exec setsid "$@"
+  fi
+  if command -v perl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    exec perl -MPOSIX -e 'POSIX::setsid(); exec { $ARGV[0] } @ARGV or die "exec $ARGV[0]: $!\n"' "$@"
+  fi
+  exec "$@"
+}
+
 # fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure: start the herdr server for <session>
 # headless (no TUI client) if not already running, mirroring tmux's `tmux
 # has-session || tmux new-session -d`. Verified: a bare socket CLI call does
@@ -1653,6 +1688,14 @@ fm_backend_herdr_projection_order_best_effort() {  # <session> <created-workspac
 # every later pane, so remove home, harness identity, and supervision selection
 # inherited from whichever agent happened to start it. Bounded poll for the
 # server to report running.
+#
+# The server is launched fully detached: stdio on /dev/null, every other
+# inherited descriptor closed, and the launch subshell replaced by the server
+# in its own session. A background fork that stayed a shell would keep the
+# caller's descriptors - including the copies bash saves while a caller's
+# `>/dev/null 2>&1` redirect is active - open for the server's lifetime, so a
+# caller reading to EOF, such as an SSH command channel running
+# bin/fm-remote-doctor.sh --fix, would never finish.
 fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure() {  # <session>
   local session=$1 running out i
   running=$(fm_backend_herdr_cli "$session" status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.server.running // false' 2>/dev/null)
@@ -1660,7 +1703,11 @@ fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure() {  # <session>
   (
     unset FM_HOME FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE FM_STATE_OVERRIDE FM_DATA_OVERRIDE FM_PROJECTS_OVERRIDE FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE \
       CURSOR_AGENT CURSOR_INVOKED_AS CLAUDECODE PI_CODING_AGENT FM_PI_HARNESS GROK_AGENT FM_SUPERVISION_MODEL
-    fm_backend_herdr_cli "$session" server >/dev/null 2>&1 &
+    (
+      fm_backend_herdr_close_inherited_fds
+      export HERDR_SESSION="$session"
+      fm_backend_herdr_exec_new_session "$(fm_backend_herdr_session_client "$session")" server --session "$session"
+    ) </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
   ) || return 1
   for i in $(seq 1 20); do
     running=$(fm_backend_herdr_cli "$session" status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.server.running // false' 2>/dev/null)
diff --git a/tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh b/tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh
index bdfaabc2..4e891c6a 100755
--- a/tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh
+++ b/tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh
@@ -158,6 +158,38 @@ SH
   printf '%s\n' "$fb"
 }
 
+# make_herdr_long_lived_server_fakebin: a `herdr` stub whose `server` stays
+# up, like the real one, until $FM_HERDR_SERVER_STOP exists. It records its pid
+# and, when python3 is available, its session id.
+make_herdr_long_lived_server_fakebin() {  # <dir> -> echoes fakebin dir
+  local dir=$1 fb="$1/fakebin"
+  mkdir -p "$fb"
+  cat > "$fb/herdr" <<'SH'
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -u
+case "${1:-}" in
+  status)
+    if [ -e "$FM_HERDR_SERVER_MARKER" ]; then
+      printf '{"server":{"running":true}}\n'
+    else
+      printf '{"server":{"running":false}}\n'
+    fi
+    ;;
+  server)
+    printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$FM_HERDR_SERVER_PID"
+    if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      python3 -c 'import os; print(os.getsid(0))' > "$FM_HERDR_SERVER_SID"
+    fi
+    : > "$FM_HERDR_SERVER_MARKER"
+    while [ ! -e "$FM_HERDR_SERVER_STOP" ]; do sleep 0.1; done
+    rm -f "$FM_HERDR_SERVER_MARKER"
+    ;;
+esac
+SH
+  chmod +x "$fb/herdr"
+  printf '%s\n' "$fb"
+}
+
 # make_herdr_statefake: a STATEFUL `herdr` stub that models the parts of herdr's
 # real container behavior the workspace-leak fix (and the default-tab-prune
 # safety fix) depend on, so a full spawn->teardown cycle can be replayed
@@ -1189,6 +1221,38 @@ test_container_ensure_starts_server_and_workspace() {
   pass "fm_backend_herdr_container_ensure: version-gates, starts the server, ensures the firstmate workspace, echoes session:workspace_id + the seeded default tab id"
 }
 
+# The doctor's call shape (bin/fm-remote-doctor.sh start_herdr_server) under
+# a caller that, like an SSH command channel, finishes only at EOF on the
+# command's output. The started server must hold none of that output open.
+test_server_ensure_detaches_server_from_a_caller_reading_to_eof() {
+  local dir fb waiter i eof_seen=0 caller_sid server_sid
+  dir="$TMP_ROOT/server-detach"; mkdir -p "$dir"
+  fb=$(make_herdr_long_lived_server_fakebin "$dir")
+  (
+    PATH="$fb:$PATH" FM_HERDR_SERVER_MARKER="$dir/running" FM_HERDR_SERVER_STOP="$dir/stop" \
+      FM_HERDR_SERVER_PID="$dir/server.pid" FM_HERDR_SERVER_SID="$dir/server.sid" \
+      bash -c '. "$0/bin/backends/herdr.sh"; fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure fmtest >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "ensure rc=$?"' "$ROOT" \
+      | cat > "$dir/out"
+    : > "$dir/eof"
+  ) &
+  waiter=$!
+  for i in $(seq 1 100); do
+    [ ! -e "$dir/eof" ] || { eof_seen=1; break; }
+    sleep 0.1
+  done
+  : > "$dir/stop"
+  wait "$waiter" 2>/dev/null || true
+  [ "$eof_seen" = 1 ] || fail "server_ensure: the started server held the caller's output open, so a caller reading to EOF never finished"
+  assert_contains "$(cat "$dir/out")" "ensure rc=0" "server_ensure did not report the server running"
+  if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    caller_sid=$(python3 -c 'import os; print(os.getsid(0))')
+    server_sid=$(cat "$dir/server.sid" 2>/dev/null)
+    [ -n "$server_sid" ] || fail "server_ensure: the fake server recorded no session id"
+    [ "$server_sid" != "$caller_sid" ] || fail "server_ensure: the server stayed in the caller's session $caller_sid"
+  fi
+  pass "fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure: starts the server detached, so a caller reading to EOF finishes once it is ready"
+}
+
 test_server_ensure_scrubs_home_and_harness_identity() {
   local dir log marker fb output name
   dir="$TMP_ROOT/server-env"; mkdir -p "$dir"; log="$dir/env"; marker="$dir/running"
@@ -5788,6 +5852,7 @@ test_workspace_ensure_other_home_ignores_the_launcher_identity
 test_container_ensure_refuses_an_ambiguous_home_label
 test_container_ensure_starts_server_and_workspace
 test_server_ensure_scrubs_home_and_harness_identity
+test_server_ensure_detaches_server_from_a_caller_reading_to_eof
 test_container_ensure_reuses_existing_workspace
 test_container_ensure_creates_with_no_focus_flag
 test_container_ensure_uses_secondmate_home_label
```

## Local verification

- The new test fails on unpatched `main` (`not ok - server_ensure: the started server held the caller's output open, so a caller reading to EOF never finished`, after its 10-second bound) and passes with the patch in under a second.
- The rest of `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh` and `tests/fm-remote-doctor.test.sh` give the same results with and without the patch on the test host.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` (ShellCheck 0.11.0, actionlint 1.7.12) is clean.
- The `setsid`, `perl`, and plain-`exec` launch paths were each checked with an SSH-like caller (pipes on stdin, stdout, and stderr; wait for the child, then for EOF): all three close the channel at once.

title: Require a filled CLEAR block before a worker starts
body:
## Summary
- New ship and scout briefs include a CLEAR block, and the start refuses to launch until Context, Layout, Examples, Audience, Role, Fallback, and Evidence each have real text.
- Briefs written before that heading still launch. A new brief whose heading was deleted cannot be told apart from those older briefs, so that case is not refused.
- The fill procedure is the clear-prompt skill. Role matches the job: a page, proposal, or statement of work is a writer, and a code change is a careful builder. The skill points at helix-craft `practice/clear-prompt.md` and does not paste the blank sheet.

## Test plan
- [x] A scaffolded brief that still contains `{CLEAR}` does not spawn, and the refusal names the token.
- [x] A brief with the seven filled lines gets past the gate, including an Evidence line that mentions the token.
- [x] A legacy brief with no CLEAR heading still launches.
- [x] A block missing Evidence is refused by name.
- [x] Existing placeholder tests still pass.
- [x] Secondmate charters do not carry a CLEAR block.

title: fix(bearings): stop truncating Charted Next titles and reasons on the lavish board
A key= token after a bracketed tag collapses the decision into 'default', so two keyed blockers merge and --resolve-key refuses the stated key
body:
## Summary

A status line that puts an unbracketed `key=<slug>` after a bracketed tag, for example

```
blocked [at=1790943990] key=nm-mirror-rebased: mirror refuses
```

is folded as an open decision under the shared `default` key, and the stated key is dropped. Two such blockers with different keys therefore collapse into a single `default` entry, and the first one silently disappears from OPEN DECISIONS. `fm-send --resolve-key nm-mirror-rebased` then refuses with "no open decision or blocker with that key".

This is the "stated key silently collapses into default" failure that #2109 fixed for the note-head position. The same mistyped key without a preceding tag (`blocked key=a: ...`) is not a transition at all, so the two shapes behave inconsistently.

## Steps to reproduce

On main at 65e2aa44:

```
$ printf '%s\n' \
    'blocked [at=1790943990] key=nm-mirror-rebased: mirror refuses' \
    'blocked [at=1790944213] key=nm-agent-grok-refused: grok refused' > t.status
$ bash -c '. bin/fm-classify-lib.sh; status_open_decisions t.status'
default	blocked	grok refused
```

With the documented bracketed form, both stay open:

```
$ printf '%s\n' 'blocked [key=a] [at=1]: mirror refuses' 'blocked [key=b] [at=2]: grok refused' > t.status
$ bash -c '. bin/fm-classify-lib.sh; status_open_decisions t.status'
a	blocked	mirror refuses
b	blocked	grok refused
```

Without a preceding tag the line is ignored:

```
$ printf '%s\n' 'blocked key=a: mirror refuses' > t.status
$ bash -c '. bin/fm-classify-lib.sh; status_open_decisions t.status'
(no output)
```

These lines came from real worker output: a ship worker wrote exactly the first two lines, one after the other, about two different blockers.

## Expected

A stated key is never silently rewritten to `default`. Either:

- an unbracketed `key=<slug>` token in the tag region (after the verb, before the first colon) is read as the stated key, the same way the bracketed `[key=<slug>]` and the note-head position are, or
- the line is rejected as malformed and surfaced, so the blocker is not merged into another one.

The first option keeps the blocker visible and answerable with the key the worker gave.

## Actual

- `status_line_verb` (`bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:657`) cuts the verb at the first `[`, so everything after the first bracketed tag (including ` key=...`) is dropped and the line reads as a bare `blocked` transition.
- `_fm_decision_key` (`bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:738`) finds no `[key=...]` before the colon and none at the note head, so it returns `default`.
- The grammar comment above it (around lines 581-635) says an arbitrary `name=value` token is not skipped and keeps the line a non-transition. That holds only when no bracketed tag comes before the token.
- `fm-send --resolve-key` checks `status_open_decisions` (`bin/fm-send.sh` around line 633), so it refuses the worker's own key.

## Notes

The fix is contained to `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh` plus tests. Whichever option is chosen, both shapes (with and without a preceding tag) should behave the same.

title: fix(bin): isolate Treehouse pools per Firstmate home
body:
## Intent Send the local Treehouse pool fixes upstream to kunchenguid/firstmate as a PR (chosen option: replay the local fixes on top of the latest upstream, and also open upstream PRs for them). Context: the local firstmate main carries three commits that exist nowhere upstream and fix Treehouse pool isolation per firstmate home: machine-wide pools caused Claude ships to refuse in secondmate homes because of double allocation. The commits are 9a465e24 "fix: isolate Treehouse pools per firstmate home", 587e57cd "fix: preserve legacy Treehouse return roots", and ebb44105 "fix: keep per-home Treehouse pools outside the home and credential-capable". title: Herdr presentation recovery gives up after 5s while a concurrent spawn holds the session lock longer (flaky concurrent secondmate recovery)
body:
`tests/fm-backend-herdr-presentation-e2e.test.sh` "concurrent secondmate recovery" fails intermittently on CI (2 of 2 on one run in a downstream fork, passing on rerun), and the cause is in `bin/fm-spawn.sh`, not the test.

Herdr presentation recovery takes the session-scoped presentation-order lock through `spawn_herdr_presentation_order_lock_acquire "$HERDR_SES"` (`bin/fm-spawn.sh:3657` on current main). That helper makes one bounded attempt: 50 tries of 0.1 s, then it gives up. Giving up is correct for a clean projected create, which falls back to the flat layout. Recovery has no fallback, so it exits with `herdr presentation recovery could not acquire its session lock; refusing a concurrent resume`.

A concurrent spawn holds the same lock from before worktree acquisition until its projected layout mutation is done. On a loaded CI runner that hold measured about 4-6 s, so whenever it passes 5 s the recovery fails. Whether it does depends only on runner speed.

The failing order can be forced: delay the concurrent spawn inside the lock past 5 s. Recovery then fails every time on current main.

Done means recovery waits for the current lock holder to release (for example `fm_lock_acquire_wait`) instead of using the bounded try, and the regression test forces the >5 s hold in the normal test path.

A downstream fork fixed it this way in https://github.com/ironerumi/firstmate/pull/69. Clean creates keep the bounded attempt and flat fallback; only recovery waits.

body:
## Intent

Complete the existing Codex app-server prerequisite delivery on fm/codex-appserver-lifecycle. Focused tests, relevant regressions, and the isolated integrated canary passed. Validate and deliver the rebased prerequisite through the configured personal fork and a focused PR. Do not add app-server functionality, touch machine-control or OpenClaw, or merge.

## What Changed

- Adds opt-in `--codex-appserver` launches for fresh Codex ship and scout workers, with task-bound lifecycle tracking and an isolated workspace.
- Routes worker reports, steering, keyed decision answers, and interrupt/exit through the supervisor; results enter delivery reconciliation only after correlated terminal success.
- Documents the transport’s supported environment and adds focused app-server verification coverage.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The change adds a substantial app-server lifecycle and private Git delivery path, but this review found no source-backed defect or intent contradiction in the inspected changes.

## Testing

The prior payload records a focused selector test and live Codex app-server checks for scout success, failure, and interruption. The selector test was not driven against the live product.

- Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 3 of 4 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The canary selector preserves the default suite, deduplicates selections, accepts one or several scenarios, and rejects unknown names before spawning a worker. | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload records a focused test command but marks this scenario live=false, so it does not establish a result driven against the live product. |
| A scout report remains unpublished until successful completion, publishes exactly once after a held-answer retry, matches the task and generation, and survives task teardown. | ✅ pass | live | Live Codex canary transcript; scout success trace and published report |
| A failed scout turn publishes no report and does not produce a completed task projection. | ✅ pass | live | Live Codex canary transcript; scout failure trace |
| Interrupting a scout after report submission leaves no published report or completed projection and reaps the app-server. | ✅ pass | live | Live Codex canary transcript; scout interruption trace |

```text
# UNIQUE_SCOUT_REPORT

The supervised scout completed the requested decision callback and received the supervisor answer `UNIQUE_HELD_ANSWER` in this active turn.
This report is the complete standalone delivery artifact for the assigned app-server worker verification.
The conclusion is limited to the interaction directly observed by this worker: the decision request returned an answer, and the worker then submitted its result through the prescribed reporting tool.

## Assigned verification

The captain's stated intent was to verify the real supervised app-server worker.
The concrete scout instruction required a `firstmate_report` call of type `needs-decision` with the message `SCOUT_HELD_QUESTION`, followed by waiting for its answer.
After that answer, the worker was required to submit a result with message `UNIQUE_SCOUT_RESULT` and a complete Markdown report containing `UNIQUE_SCOUT_REPORT` and the answer.
This report supplies that delivery evidence without creating a separate report file.

## Observed decision exchange

The worker invoked the reporting tool with type `needs-decision` and the exact message `SCOUT_HELD_QUESTION`.
The tool call completed and returned the exact text `UNIQUE_HELD_ANSWER`.
The returned answer was available within the same active turn before this result submission was prepared.
The worker did not substitute an assumed answer, infer approval from elapsed time, or consult a filesystem inbox.
The answer recorded here is the actual tool response rather than a placeholder or a predicted supervisor response.

## Report delivery

The result submission uses the exact message `UNIQUE_SCOUT_RESULT`.
Its report field contains this entire Markdown document, including the required marker and the observed supervisor answer.
The worker leaves publication of the canonical task report to the supervisor, as specified by the transport contract.
No local report file was written as an alternative delivery channel.
This submission is delivery evidence; it does not independently assert that the supervisor has recorded terminal success or finished publishing the report.
Those downstream actions remain outside the worker's observations at the time this report is submitted.

## Scope and constraints

The worker read the fallback firstmate coding guidelines from the path provided in the brief because the named skill was absent from the session's available skill catalog.
The task required no code changes, and no code changes were made.
The worker did not commit, modify fleet state, write status files, write report files, or poll inboxes.
No branch operation was necessary for this scout task.
The observed evidence concerns the supervised reporting exchange, rather than broad application correctness, repository test coverage, or unrelated runtime behavior.
No claims about those untested areas are needed to establish completion of the assigned interaction.

## Conclusion

The held decision request returned `UNIQUE_HELD_ANSWER`, satisfying the prerequisite for result delivery.
The required result message and complete report are now submitted through `firstmate_report`.
The supervisor can use the exact request marker, answer, result marker, and report marker to correlate this scout's execution with the supervised app-server verification.

Is it task or incident evidence - chronology, transcripts, branches, temporary paths, failed hypotheses, or delivery proof?\n   If yes: keep it in the private task report or PR evidence by default, after distilling every unique current fact into its authoritative owner.\n7. Is it mechanics - exact flags, exact commands, exact paths?\n   If yes: the script's own header comment plus its `--help` output, not prose in `AGENTS.md`, a skill, or a second documentation owner.\n\nStop at the first tier that answers yes.\nDo not place a fact at a more convenient tier than the one this tree gives you.\nThe machine-consumed inventory in [`docs/documentation-audiences.json`](../../../docs/documentation-audiences.json) is the single classification owner for maintained prose surfaces; do not add parallel front matter or a second audience list.\n\n## One-owner rule\n\nEvery contract - a data format, a state machine, a decision procedure - is stated in full exactly once.\nEvery other mention of it is a one-line cross-reference, never a restatement.\nA single deliberate one-line reinforcement at a genuine risk point is allowed, for example a \"don't forget X\" placed exactly where forgetting X is costly.\nRestating the contract's substance a second time is not allowed: the two copies will drift the moment only one is edited.\nWhen you touch a contract, patch, replace, or prune the owner's existing language rather than appending a new clause or paragraph wherever possible, then grep the repo for its other mentions and update the cross-references, not duplicate the change into a second full copy.\n\n## Inline-stub pattern\n\nWhen content moves out of `AGENTS.md` into a skill, decide what stays behind by asking one question: what must survive with no skill loaded?\nThat is the trigger condition for loading the skill, plus any safety-critical fact that fires on a wake the skill itself is not loaded for.\nEverything else - the procedure, the mechanism, the surrounding detail - moves out completely.\nDo not leave a partial restatement behind \"just in case\".\nA partial copy is exactly the duplication the one-owner rule forbids.\nThe model to copy is `AGENTS.md` section 8's \"Away-mode and quiet-mode stub\": it keeps only the skill-invocation triggers inline and points everything else at the `/afk`, `/quiet`, and `away-quiet-supervision` skills.\n\n## Size discipline\n\nApply the decision tree above to every line you are about to add to `AGENTS.md`.\nIf an addition needs more than a few lines of conditional detail (detail that matters only in a specific situation) or reference detail (a wire format, an exact schema, historical rationale), you are almost certainly adding it to the wrong file.\n`AGENTS.md`'s token cost is paid by every session of every fleet member, every time, whether or not that session ever hits the situation the new lines describe.\nA skill's cost is paid only by the sessions that actually load it.\nWhen in doubt, write the fact into the skill or doc first by patching that owner's existing language, and add only the one-line trigger to `AGENTS.md`.\n\n## Trigger hygiene\n\nA new skill is dead weight if nothing loads it.\nEvery new skill needs its load trigger declared in its description, which is the always-loaded trigger index; add an inline `AGENTS.md` pointer only in the operating section whose always-loaded rule must name it.\nState the trigger as a condition (\"load before X\", \"load on Y wake\"), never as a vague pointer.\nBriefs for tasks that touch firstmate's own tracked material should tell the crewmate to load this skill.\n`bin/fm-brief.sh`'s `REPO` argument is a caller-supplied string with no reliable signal that it names firstmate's own repo, unlike a project registered in `data/projects.md`, so there is no clean point inside the scaffold to detect this case automatically.\nFirstmate adds this skill's load instruction to firstmate-repo briefs by hand instead.\n`CONTRIBUTING.md`'s \"Development\" section carries the same instruction as a durable reminder.\n\n## Compatibility and enforcement\n\nBefore changing shared tracked behavior, review every affected supported primary harness and runtime backend rather than checking only the adapters active in the current fleet.\nMark an axis not applicable only after inspecting its integration surface, and update the corresponding verification evidence when behavior changes.\n\nFor critical safety, routing, startup, and supervision infrastructure, prefer deterministic and idempotent enforcement over relying on agent memory alone.\nKeep instructions as the authority and discovery layer, but make repeated execution converge safely and make invalid or unsafe states fail closed wherever the runtime can enforce them.\n\n### Harness-dependent checks\n\nThis section is the single owner of the rule and of how to satisfy it.\n\nA check is harness-dependent when its verdict comes from something the vendor emits: a process name, rendered output, a spinner or keybind glyph, a banner, or a key the harness binds.\nAnything in that class must be proven end to end against the real harness, because a stub or fake agent can only confirm the assumption already written into the stub.\nThat proof is authorized to spend tokens; the cost is small against a check that silently stops working.\n\nBuild the check on the most structural signal that answers the question, and prefer a kernel or protocol fact over anything a release note could change.\nWhen a rendered surface is genuinely the only source, read more than one independent signal and let any of them carry a positive verdict, so no single vendor string is load-bearing.\nWhere a surface signal is unavoidable, back it with a guard that fails loudly naming the harness and version rather than degrading quietly.\n\nEvery such check needs two tests, because they fail for different reasons:\n\n- A portable regression in `tests/` that pins the logic with real processes and no harness, so CI enforces the classifier everywhere it runs tmux.\n  Drive the signals apart deliberately and assert the verdict survives losing one; assert the divergence itself so the case cannot go quietly vacuous.\n  Confirm which signal a given construction actually blinds on each supported platform rather than assuming, because the same trick can break different sources on macOS and Linux.\n- A live guard in the `live-harness-optin` family (`bin/fm-test-run.sh`) that exercises every INSTALLED harness for real and fails naming the harness and version.\n  Report an absent harness explicitly rather than passing silently over it, and refuse a pass that checked nothing.\n  Open it with `fm_live_gate` from `tests/lib.sh`, which is the single owner of that decision: a guard that spends no model tokens runs by default wherever its tools are installed, a guard that submits prompts stays opt-in, and its own variable or `FM_LIVE` forces it on (an absent tool then fails rather than skips) or off.\n  The portable serial CI lane has no credentials and installs the public Pi package, so token-free guards exercise the available Pi surfaces while unavailable tools capability-skip; run a prompt-submitting guard after every harness upgrade and before trusting refreshed per-harness evidence.\n\nRecord the dated per-harness result in `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md`, and point at the live guard as the command that refreshes it, rather than leaving a version-scoped observation to rot into a false claim.\n\n## Documentation change review\n\nFor every changed maintained prose surface, identify its inventory audience, authoritative owner, current-behavior relevance, destination for supporting evidence, and any unique safety fact that removal could lose.\nMove or delete evidence only after the current owner and regression pointer are verified.\nAfter all documentation, review-fix, and lint-fix commits, review the complete branch diff again against those criteria rather than reviewing only the latest commit.\nRun `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`; it enforces classification, README setup routing, local link targets, and owner pointers without keyword-linting legitimate evidence prose.\n\n## No-mistakes test configuration\n\nNever configure a deterministic suite-walk `commands.test` in any repository's no-mistakes config, whether it selects the full suite, changed tests, a family, or a fixed script list.\nTargeted validation belongs to the no-mistakes evidence path, while CI owns broad deterministic regression coverage.\nFirstmate PR #3644 demonstrated the cost: pinning a 75-162-script walk took 32.7 minutes per validation, while removing it restored the 3.6-minute targeted-validation posture.\n\n## Repo style rules\n\n- Put one full sentence per line in tracked Markdown.\n- Never wrap multiple sentences onto one physical line.\n- Plain dash `-`, never an em dash.\n- Never add an agent name as a commit co-author.\n- `bin/*.sh` and `bin/backends/*.sh` must pass `shellcheck`.\n- Run Firstmate production-library tests and commands that source `bin/` scripts under `bash` explicitly, never through the tool shell's default interpreter.\n- Run `bin/fm-lint.sh` before treating a script change as done; it is the single owner of the lint definition that CI and the no-mistakes pre-push gate both invoke, its own header owns what that definition covers, and it refuses to run under any other version of either linter.\n- When a task names a specific tool, implement the work with that tool, or explicitly flag the substitution and its new dependency footprint for review before shipping.\n- Colocate tests with the existing pattern in `tests/`, name them `<subject>.test.sh`, and extend an existing script rather than inventing a new runner.\n- Tests must exercise behavior through an executable or public interface and must never assert implementation-source bytes, including through parsers, regexes, snapshots, or indirect wrappers.\n- A maintainer-verification record under `docs/verification/` records active empirical facts, not assumptions or task chronology.\n- Include the date, version, exact commands run, and exact output needed to support the current guarantee.\n- Keep incident chronology and delivery evidence in private task reports or PR evidence unless a concise rationale is required to maintain a current safety boundary.\n", "exitCode": 0, "durationMs": 0}, "threadId": "01a114d3-335a-78c0-b319-d46628e3b741", ## Intent Upstream pull request https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/6870 (fork branch avivl/omp-daemon-worker-lock on git@github.com:avivl/firstmate.git, current head e4226052196b6238c07b64f26e13459b63a96034) "fix(bin): exclude omp daemon workers from session lock anchoring" is approved by the upstream owner's reviewer and auto-merges once its checks are green, but it now conflicts with main. Main took #7415 ("re-anchor a Claude session's lock so /clear keeps ownership") on 2026-10-17, which edits the same test file, and a trial merge shows one conflict: tests/fm-session-lock-ancestry.test.sh. The branch is 3 commits ahead (one fix commit 79aaf0c4 plus two "Merge branch 'main'" commits) and 56 behind origin/main. The captain approved this one upstream push with the words: fix it, for pr://6870. The task is to resolve the conflict, keep every behavior and test of the PR and of main, and re-raise the PR through the no-mistakes pipeline once on the final head. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh`: added `fm_omp_daemon_worker`, which recognizes omp daemon worker processes (`omp __omp_worker_*` as the first argument). `fm_harness_process_matches` now never treats one as a harness, and the ancestry walk in `fm_harness_ancestry_pids` stops at one without a verdict. A new `fm_harness_ancestry_under_omp_worker` helper reports whether the walk hit such a worker first. This keeps a `name`d omp bash call from recording the shared daemon broker as the session in `state/.lock`. - `bin/fm-lock.sh`: when no harness can be found and the ancestry runs through an omp daemon worker, the error now says the command is running under a `name`d bash call and should be rerun without `name`. The branch also resolves the conflict with #7415 (re-anchoring a Claude session's lock so `/clear` keeps ownership) in the test file, keeping the tests from both sides. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The conflict resolution now has one definition and one call of each test from both main and the PR, and the lock-library change is narrowly scoped to excluding omp `__omp_worker_*` processes from anchoring. ## Testing I ran the merged session-lock ancestry suite, which drives real fm-lock.sh processes. session-lock: a same-session confirmation waits for the claim lock and refreshes a re-keyed id ok - session-lock: a waiting confirmation does not steal another session's lock ok - session-lock: a failed lock write restores the previous sidecar ok - title: Task-owned procevent source outlives its owner's teardown: retire refuses, launch-failed check wakes every cycle
body:
A crew-hosted Lavish board source (adapter lavish, kind task-owned, owner_task a scout) was armed by the worker with `bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh arm <artifact.html> --for <task>`. The scout completed, its report was read, the completion gate passed and `bin/fm-teardown.sh <task>` returned the worktree to the pool. The source registration survived: its argv points at the now-recycled worktree path, so every watcher cycle emits `check: process-event source failed to start: procevent:<id>:launch-failed:<gen>` and costs the primary a handling turn.

Every documented retirement path refuses for this state:
- `fm-procevent.sh retire <id> --if-absent` -> `error: source registration does not match the expected owner`
- `fm-procevent.sh retire <id> --if-matches lavish -- <exact argv from the .source record>` -> same owner-mismatch error
- `fm-procevent.sh handled <id> <seq>`: there is no captured result sequence to acknowledge; the launch never produces one (only `<id>.<gen>.last-launch` exists), so the task-owned conclude step cannot run.

Expected: either teardown of the owner task retires (or re-homes) the task-owned sources it owns, or `retire` accepts an explicit owner-absent path when the owner task's meta no longer exists, so an orphaned board cannot wake the primary indefinitely.

Observed on the current main (c5f48e4c) on a Pi/herdr crew with treehouse worktrees; the source record is `state/procevent/<id>.source` with `kind=task-owned` and `owner_task=<torn-down task>`.

title: Per-home config/spawn-env to propagate extra env (e.g. TREEHOUSE_ROOT) into worker panes
body:
## Problem

There is no per-home way to propagate extra environment variables into a spawned worker's pane.

`bin/fm-spawn.sh` types `treehouse get` (and later the harness launch command) into the backend pane, whose shell is the user's ordinary login shell. Variables set in firstmate's own process environment therefore never reach `treehouse get` or the worker. The only values the spawn establishes in the pane are hard-wired: `GOTMPDIR`, `FM_TASK_ID`, `COMPACT_ADVISER_DISABLE`, the trace context, and the fixed pass-through list in the launch environment. Nothing under `config/` or `docs/configuration.md` adds to that list.

## Concrete use case: `TREEHOUSE_ROOT`

Treehouse pools worktrees under `$HOME/.treehouse/` by default. On a machine whose agent approval rules (omp/bash permission policies) only auto-approve `git -C <path>` and similar commands when the path/cwd is inside a trusted root such as `~/Git/.worktrees`, every worker hits an approval prompt on routine commands like `git -C <worktree> checkout -- .`, because its worktree lives under `~/.treehouse`.

Setting `TREEHOUSE_ROOT=~/Git/.worktrees` for firstmate spawns only would fix this, but today the only options are:

- write `treehouse.toml` into each project clone (a project-tree write, which firstmate's own rules forbid for tuning its spawn behavior), or
- export `TREEHOUSE_ROOT` in the user's shell profile, which moves the pool for every treehouse use on the machine, not just firstmate spawns.

## Proposal

Add an optional `config/spawn-env` per home:

- plain `KEY=VALUE` lines; blank lines and `#` comments ignored;
- validated at spawn (strict key shape `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`, refuse malformed lines rather than skipping them, refuse overriding the variables the spawn itself owns such as `FM_TASK_ID`, `GOTMPDIR`, backend identity);
- each entry exported into the worker pane through the same pre-launch channel that already ships `GOTMPDIR`, but **before** `treehouse get`, so it governs worktree acquisition as well as the worker process;
- documented in `docs/configuration.md`; absent file means no change in behavior.

Secondmate homes could inherit it with the other local material, subject to the existing inheritance rules.

title: fix(bin): name the task id on stale wakes for parked and deferred workers
body:
## Intent Fix item 1 of upstream firstmate issue #6932: a stale wake for a parked worker names the pane, not the task. The parked/declared-wait resurface line goes out as `stale: $win ($reason)` from `resurface_absorbed` with no task id, so the supervision host passes the pane target to `fm-branch-report.sh --task`, the report is refused with exit 3, and the host retries with the task id. Expected: the stale wake names the task id, so the host reports on the first attempt. The maintainer noted that open PR #6761 adds `task=` to the possible-wedge and dead-endpoint reasons only, which partly helps but does not cover the parked-wait line. Go (2026-10-24): rebase https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/6937 onto current main and check https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/6936 still applies cleanly and passes. The maintainer re-checked on main 2ee22508 and confirmed both items are still real; #6937 is conflicting with main, #6936 is mergeable. (Referenced substance: PR #6937 is this branch's existing PR, which delivers the item-1 fix above; it must be rebased onto current main with its conflicts resolved and pushed to update that same PR. PR #6761, still open and unmerged, appends a trailing ` task=` to the watcher's possible-wedge and dead-endpoint stale reasons; this change uses the same `task=` format for the other stale lines. PR #6936 is a separate fix for item 2 of issue #6932 (`fm-wake-drain.sh --ack-through` printing one confirmation line on success) that lives on its own branch; it is only checked here, not changed.) Go (2026-11-26): rebase PR 6937 onto current main because GitHub reports merge conflicts with main, resolve the conflicts while keeping the accepted behavior of the fix, run the local tests for the touched files, and re-validate so the pipeline pushes; change nothing else on the PR and post no comments. (Resolution note: main moved more watcher triage cases into fm-watch-triage-busy.test.sh and restructured fm-watch-triage.test.sh, so the conflicts were resolved by taking main's test files and re-applying this fix's task-named assertions in their new locations; the bin/ and docs/ diff is unchanged from the previously reviewed head.) ## What Changed - `bin/fm-watch.sh` now ends each long-cadence stale recheck with ` task=`: the declared pause, the superseded declared wait, the deferred wait, the deferred write, and the validating run. The steering-inbox stale reasons get the same suffix. A stale wake that had no parenthetical (first sight, away mode, the afk handoff to the daemon) is now written as `stale: (task=)`, and a named picker follows the id as `(task=, blocked-on-prompt: )`. - `bin/fm-push-transition-lib.sh` appends ` task=` to the waiting-on-human stale reason. `bin/fm-branch-prompt.sh` tells the supervisor to report with the `task=` value and not with the window or pane at the start of the line. `docs/architecture.md` shows the new form of the daemon handoff wake. - The watcher triage, wake-queue, supervision-events, and supervision-host tests now expect the task-named stale lines. A new `tests/fm-daemon.test.sh` case checks that `handle_wake` still resolves the window from `stale: (task=)` and classifies a declared pause as before. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change only appends the task id to stale wake reason text, and every consumer I traced (daemon handle_wake and stale_dialog_name, the secondmate declared-pause matcher at bin/fm-watch.sh:960, the Pi dispatch trigger-key parse, and the harness wake-line matchers) still resolves the window and classifies the wake the same way; both fix-round commits (fe9120aa, 765124c8) match their findings and add no new logic. ## Testing I drove the real watcher against a real tmux pane in a disposable lab home on both the target and the base commit, then ran the real supervision host with a real Claude engine through three handled wakes, fed the emitted lines to the real daemon parser, and ran the push-transition suite.
