## Intent

Update the open upstream pull request https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/6968 ("feat(bin): add Droid crew and scout support", head branch fm/droid-crew-harness-v2 on the fork delaanthonio/firstmate) with the additional Droid changes made in the captain's fork since that branch was cut. The captain's words: "We should update https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/6968 with the additional tweaks we made for droid", then chose: "do 1-4 and droid as the primary harness". The captain approved this one upstream contribution (one-task consent for it); merge authority stays with the upstream maintainer.

The selected tweaks are Droid supervision through tracked background jobs; Droid folder-trust handling and recording effective models; exact Droid model selection and runtime accounting; preserving dynamic Droid effort across remote secondmate recovery; and Droid as a primary harness, including its away-mode fixes.

Ensure the code for the Firstmate droid PR is beautiful

Ensure we run no mistakes on the droid Firstmate PR

Sure do the force push

## What Changed

- Add Droid support for primary, secondmate, crewmate, and scout roles, including launch, control, trust handling, and recovery.
- Add tracked background supervision and away-mode decision handling for Droid primary sessions.
- Select exact Droid model IDs, record observed runtime models, and preserve dynamic effort across remote secondmate recovery.

## Risk Assessment

🚨 High: The change affects launch, trust, supervision, and recovery, and the review did not cover the entire required delta, including the complete spawn implementation and test suite changes.

## Testing

Targeted live local command checks passed for trust ownership, model selection and generation fencing, away-mode denial, and bounded supervision failure. Authenticated Droid, Herdr away delivery, and remote recovery were not validated because isolated credentials and an endpoint were unavailable. This is a non-UI change; screenshots were not applicable.

title: fix(bin): fit each session-start message under the harness output cap
body:
## Intent

Make firstmate's session-start digest fit what the harness actually shows. Today's digest was 70,471 characters; Claude Code shows at most 10,000 characters of one hook's output and above that only a 2,000-character preview, so firstmate saw 2.8% and missed the asker's preferences (they began near character 58,300), including his standing Outside Voice rule. A review scout proposed one firstmate change: fit each session-start message under the cap, send his preferences as their own message, replace bulk with named, retrievable omissions, and have the composer measure itself. An Outside Voice review said proceed with four blocking edits and a build outline.

The four blocking edits are: (1) do not tee the output into a state/session-start/latest.txt record, because it could only capture the short core; instead the first lines of every part tell the agent to read the full output file the harness named if the message reached it as a truncated preview. (2) Do not cut the supervision protocol to a pointer on every harness, because on Codex, Pi, Cursor, omp, OpenCode, and Grok it carries the session's first required action; only Claude's block is shortened, keeping its current-state lines, mode line, the drain/ack and do-not-arm steps, and a pointer that repeats the exact flags used. (3) Every WITHHELD retrieval line must be a valid, single, read-only command with the flags the composer used (one tasks-axi state per call; bootstrap is never withheld because a plain bootstrap run mutates). (4) Each WITHHELD line prints where its section would have printed, not in a trailing index that a killed child would lose.

The build outline: a --part core|preferences|all argument (default all, so manual runs, nudge-tier harnesses, Pi, omp, and Cursor stay complete in one message), with second Claude and Codex SessionStart hook entries for the preferences part; the preferences part prints data/captain-shared.md then data/captain.md verbatim, prints in full even when over budget with a first line that says so, and prints nothing on resume, reload, or fork. A never-cut set (lock, read-only banner, Pi/omp extension lines, the Pi compaction AGENTS.md refresh outside the budget, bootstrap, wake queue with open decisions and unread status, the supervision block, one fleet row per task with its four endpoint states, kind, project, last status state and age, PR URL, and open decision keys, the orphan count, the AFK line, Public commitments, the network checks line, and the completion and baseline failure lines) always prints, even when it alone exceeds the budget. Budgeted sections (backlog summary with counts, ready ids, captain-held ids, and a count of other holds; project names; secondmate names) each print a WITHHELD line in place when they do not fit. The budget is bytes, not characters: 8,500 on Claude, 7,000 on Codex, 8,500 elsewhere. The hold-reason decoding guarantee keeps a test through the held-row listing command. The vendor delivery facts are proven by the opt-in live guard on installed Claude and Codex exec (both part tokens and a late token come back on startup, clear, and compact), with the dated result recorded in docs/verification/supervision.md. The review recommended leaving the startup-memory-budget rescope out of this change, and delivering learnings as their own --part learnings message on Claude and Codex, included in --part all elsewhere. The AGENTS.md, skill, and doc lines this change makes wrong are corrected; data/captain.md, data/captain-shared.md, and data/learnings.md content are not edited.

His words, verbatim: "you found losts of parts in session start isn't needed nahd provided some solutions, why don't u start the ov on yoru plan and then fix it thru standard procedure". His standing preferences that bear on it: "Optimise always-loaded prose for staleness, not size. Prefer a pointer read at use time over a summary cached in context." and "No silent elision. If startup withholds content, name what was withheld and how to retrieve it." and "Prefer what a script, setting, or hook guarantees over a rule an author must follow."

Mid-task change (2026-11-23), answering a request to rebase this PR onto current main and install the rebased change in this home before the upstream merge: "I understand only first mates can make other changes. If you cannot change that, you can tell first mate to execute."

Mid-task change (2026-11-23), approving the upstream push of the rebased change to PR 7078: "complete upstream push"

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-session-start.sh` and `bin/fm-sessionstart-run.sh` now take `--part core|preferences|learnings|all`. The default is `all`, so a manual run and single-message harnesses still print everything in one message. The core is measured against a byte budget: 8,500 on Claude, 7,000 on Codex, 8,500 elsewhere, and `FM_SESSION_START_BUDGET_BYTES` overrides it. A never-cut set always prints in full. This set includes the lock, the banners, bootstrap, the wake queue, the supervision block, one fleet row per task, and the AFK and failure lines. Budgeted sections (backlog summary, project names, secondmate names) that do not fit print an in-place `WITHHELD <what> :: <read-only command>` line. The first lines of every part tell the agent to read the full output file if the harness showed only a truncated preview. `preferences` prints `data/captain-shared.md` and then `data/captain.md` verbatim. `learnings` prints the learnings file. Both parts print nothing on resume, reload, or fork.
- `.claude/settings.json` and `.codex/hooks.json` now run the existing SessionStart hook with `--part core`. They add separate `--part preferences` and `--part learnings` hook entries, and `bin/fm-codex-stop-park.sh` passes the part through. On Claude only, `bin/fm-supervision-instructions.sh --brief` shortens the supervision block. It keeps the current-state lines, the mode line, and steps 1-3, then adds a `Full protocol:` command that repeats the exact flags. On every other harness, `--brief` changes nothing.
- Tests are updated for the split, the budget, the WITHHELD lines, the parsing of manual backlog title lines, and the hold-reason listing. The opt-in live e2e now checks for core, late, preferences, and learnings tokens. `docs/verification/supervision.md` records the dated live result. `AGENTS.md`, the session-start-recovery skill, `docs/configuration.md`, and `docs/sessionstart-nudge.md` are updated to match.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The latest fix round correctly aligns the manual backlog title-line grammar with the fleet-snapshot owner and records captain holds on blocked rows, prior-round fixes hold in the current code, and no new reachable defect or intent contradiction was found.

## Testing

I ran the opt-in live vendor guard and real session starts against a disposable lab home and lab checkout. All Claude and Codex exec delivery cases passed: both part tokens and the late token came back on Claude startup, clear, and compact, and on Codex exec startup. The guard's Pi case failed because Pi's xAI login on this machine is expired, so the guard exited 1. A re-login is not allowed here. I also drove real hooks on Claude Code (interactive, lab tmux socket) and Codex exec. Each harness got core, preferences, and learnings as separate messages, and the core stayed under its budget (7,278 of 8,500 bytes on Claude, 6,897 of 7,000 on Codex). On Codex, secondmates were withheld at 7,000 bytes but fit at 8,500. Every WITHHELD retrieval command ran successfully and left data/ unchanged. The fleet rows printed whole when they alone went over the budget. The 18 KB preferences part reached Claude as a 2 KB preview. Its first lines named the overflow and the full output file. When told to follow those lines, the model read that file and quoted the late preference lines. The manual backlog title forms parsed correctly, and the hold-lifecycle test passed. I tore down the lab, its tmux server, and the stray watcher processes. The worktree is clean.

title: fix(bin): spawn a secondmate's ships from a pool of its own clone
body:
## Intent

Fix: a secondmate cannot ship from its own project clone when that project's isolated-copy (treehouse) pool belongs to the main home's clone. fm-spawn stops at the trust step with "not a worktree of project" (seen 2026-10-15: secondmate Toby, project dataform-assertions). The workaround was dispatching the ship from the main home with the secondmate's brief. Chosen direction: let a secondmate's clone use its own isolated-copy pool, rather than routing such ships to main. Upstream PR to github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate is approved for this one task.
fix up the upstream PR - rebase, failing checks, review threads

## What Changed

- `fm-spawn.sh` now asks the new `fm_treehouse_spawn_root` in `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh` which Treehouse pool to use. The root home and remote homes keep Treehouse's default pool. A local secondmate home passes `--root <state>/treehouse`, so its task slots are worktrees of its own project clone instead of another home's clone. This applies to the pane's `treehouse get` and to the Herdr and t3code durable leases. Before this change, the spawn stopped with "not a worktree of project".
- `fm-bootstrap.sh` now reports treehouse as OUTDATED unless `treehouse get` supports both `--lease` and `--root`. The CI Treehouse pin in `fm-install-treehouse.sh` moves from 2.0.1 to 2.3.0, with updated checksums.
- Adds `tests/fm-spawn-secondmate-pool.test.sh`, which covers a secondmate's pane spawn and Herdr lease drawing from its own pool, and registers it in `fm-test-run.sh`. Existing tests' fake treehouse now advertises `--root`, and `--lease` coverage is added to `fm-spawn-herdr-lease.test.sh`. The skill and architecture/configuration docs are updated to describe the per-home pool.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is narrow: every treehouse call that takes a task slot (the pane's `treehouse get` and the Herdr and t3code durable leases) now goes through one resolver. That resolver adds `--root <state>/treehouse` only for a local secondmate home; root and remote homes keep the default pool. Running real Treehouse 2.3.0 showed that a plain `treehouse return --force <path>` with no `--root` still returns a slot from a custom root, and that the `<root>/.treehouse/<pool>/<slot>/<repo>` layout still passes fm_treehouse_pool_slot's check, so teardown and rollback keep working. The new regression tests drive the real spawn path and check what it records, not the source text.

## Testing

I ran the new secondmate-pool regression test, the Herdr lease test and the bootstrap test, and all three pass. The new test fails on the pre-fix code with the exact 'not a worktree of project' error. I then drove real Treehouse 2.3.0 against real lab homes. The pre-fix default-pool lease handed the secondmate a worktree of the main home's clone. The post-fix `--root` lease handed it a worktree of its own clone under its own state/treehouse, and the root home still resolves to the default pool. Real bootstrap in a lab home raised no treehouse OUTDATED line. The remote-seeded-home case and the Herdr spawn wiring were exercised only by integration tests with a fake terminal, so they count as untested live. I could not drive a full Herdr/tmux ship spawn end to end: tmux is not installed, and a Herdr-lab spawn would also start a live agent.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 4 of 7 scenarios driven live against the product

| Reproduce the reported bug: default pool hands the secondmate the main home's worktree | ✅ pass | live | live-treehouse-pool.log CONTROL line; fm-spawn-secondmate-pool.prefix.log shows the pre-fix spawn refused with 'not a worktree of project' |
| Root home keeps Treehouse's default pool | ✅ pass | live | live-treehouse-pool.log: fm_treehouse_spawn_root returned empty for the root lab home; fm-spawn-secondmate-pool.log root-home case typed plain `treehouse get` and created no home-scoped pool |
| Adversarial: remote-seeded home keeps the default pool and the worktree-of-project guard still refuses a foreign slot | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result. This case was exercised only through the integration test's fake terminal (tests/fm-spawn-secondmate-pool.test.sh), and a live remote-seeded home nee… |
| Local secondmate's Herdr spawn leases its slot with --root from its own pool | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result. This was covered only by tests/fm-spawn-herdr-lease.test.sh with a fake terminal. A live run needs an fm-lab Herdr session (bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh) that… |

A Herdr route would mean provisioning an fm-lab session with bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh and lau… |

title: feat(bin): add opt-in config/claude-extra-args for Claude worker launches
body:
## Intent

Add a small OPT-IN Firstmate setting, config/claude-extra-args, so Claude secondmates and crewmates can launch with extra Claude Code CLI flags. Motivation: a measured lean worker profile (--setting-sources project,local --strict-mcp-config --plugin-dir <plugin> --append-system-prompt-file <rules.md>) drops context per turn from 68.3k to 45.9k tokens while the worker's own task tracking still works. Hard requirements: an absent file must leave every claude launch byte-identical (tests assert the exact launch line); the file holds one argument per line (a flag and its value are two lines), blank and # lines ignored, each argument shell-quoted and inserted after the --add-dir grant and before --settings on every claude launch path (ship, scout, secondmate, relaunch). Deliberate decisions: Firstmate keeps owning the single --settings value because Claude Code only applies the last --settings flag (no settings merge), so extra hooks belong in a --plugin-dir plugin; --settings, --permission-mode and --dangerously-skip-permissions are refused because config/claude-permission-mode already owns the permission flag; control bytes and an unreadable/nonregular file refuse; all refusals happen before any endpoint, worktree, or task record exists, mirroring the config/claude-permission-mode validation. Non-claude harnesses ignore the file (no placeholder in their templates). The file is added to the inheritable config set so a secondmate's own claude crewmates launch with the same arguments. Documented in docs/configuration.md and the operational-home-layout skill. Tests added in tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh and tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh. Open a PR to kunchenguid/firstmate from the charlesdr13 fork; do NOT merge it.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now reads an optional `config/claude-extra-args` file on every spawn and relaunch. The file holds one argument per line; blank lines and `#` lines are skipped. Each argument is shell-quoted and placed between the `--add-dir` grant and `--settings` in the Claude launch template, so ship, scout, secondmate and relaunch all pick it up. When the file is absent, the inserted text is empty and the launch line stays the same as before. Non-Claude harness templates don't use it.
- Spawn refuses, before any metadata or launch, when the file is not a readable regular file, contains control bytes, or sets `--settings`, `--permission-mode` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Firstmate owns `--settings`, and `config/claude-permission-mode` owns the permission flag.
- `claude-extra-args` is added to `FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG` in `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh`, so a secondmate's own Claude crewmates launch with the same arguments. The `fm-spawn.sh` header, the operational-home-layout skill and the "Claude extra arguments" section of `docs/configuration.md` describe the file. New tests in `tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh` and `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh` cover the exact quoted ship launch line, the scout launch, the secondmate launch, and the refused flags and control bytes.


## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: This is an opt-in setting. With no file present, CLAUDE_EXTRA_ARGS is empty and the launch template comes out byte-identical. Validation happens before anything is changed, the same way claude-permission-mode does it, and every claude launch path (ship, scout, secondmate, relaunch) goes through the single template and substitution block. The only findings are a minor placeholder-ordering edge case and some missing tests.

## Testing

I ran the two targeted test files that hold the new tests; both passed in full, and their exact-launch assertions cover the byte-identical absent case. I then stood up a disposable fm-live-lab and drove the feature live with a real Claude primary, two real Claude secondmates, two real Claude crewmates and a real codex crewmate. Covered: arg placement on secondmate, ship and relaunch launches, re-read of an edited file on relaunch (a value with spaces and quotes arrived as one argv element), and live effect of --plugin-dir (SessionStart hook fired per session) and --append-system-prompt-file (the mate answered with the rules marker). Also covered: all 9 refusal cases stopping before any meta, window or slot, codex ignoring a valid file, byte-identical inheritance into a fresh secondmate home and into that mate's own Claude crewmate, and a clean launch with the file absent. The scout path was not driven live, so it is marked untested; only the passing unit test covers it. Every live scenario passed; the lab was torn down. No visual UI changed; Claude TUI pane text is captured as evidence.

title: fix: honor the repository’s sole allowed GitHub merge method
body:
## Intent

Bring our open upstream PR https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/7446 (fixes `https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/7425`: honor the repository's sole allowed GitHub merge method) current with upstream main; it conflicts today. Keep its behavior, including the stricter check that all three allow_* settings are booleans and the all-false refusal. The captain approved this.

The referenced PR's behavior: when bin/fm-pr-merge.sh merges a GitHub pull request and the caller passes none of --squash, --merge, --rebase, or --method, it reads the repository's allow_merge_commit, allow_squash_merge, and allow_rebase_merge settings and uses the one method the repository allows when exactly one is enabled, instead of always defaulting to --squash. It uses that sole method only when all three settings are booleans; when several or none (all false) are enabled, or the settings cannot be read or are not all booleans, it refuses to pick a sole method and keeps the --squash default. An explicit caller merge method is never overridden and the repository settings are not read in that case.

## What Changed
- Honor the repository’s sole allowed GitHub merge method when all three settings are booleans; retain the squash fallback for multiple, zero, invalid, or unreadable settings, and preserve explicit methods without querying settings.
- Skip squash-summary commit text when the selected method is merge or rebase.
- Add regression coverage for method selection, fallback cases, and squash-summary handling; update merge-method documentation.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The bounded method-selection change preserves explicit arguments, strictly validates all three boolean settings, retains fallback behavior, and correctly excludes squash summaries from non-squash merges.

## Testing

Targeted regressions passed after a timed-out first invocation was rerun to completion. Local runtime checks passed for sole methods, fallback boundaries, explicit precedence and squash summaries; CLI/API evidence was retained and fixtures were removed. Installed gh rejects --method, so those cases establish forwarding and skipped settings reads only. No production GitHub behavior or UI was exercised.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 7 of 7 scenarios driven live against the product

| Several or zero enabled methods retain the squash default rather than selecting a sole method | ✅ pass | live | merge-method-transcript.log: fallback-multiple, fallback-all-true, fallback-all-false |
| Null, missing, string, numeric and array settings cannot masquerade as boolean settings | ✅ pass | live | merge-method-transcript.log: fallback-null, missing, string-true, string-false, numeric, array; fallback-string-false.json |
| Malformed JSON and unavailable settings retain the squash default | ✅ pass | live | merge-method-transcript.log: fallback-malformed, fallback-unavailable |
| Explicit merge flags survive conflicting repository settings without reading those settings | ✅ pass | live | merge-method-transcript.log: explicit-merge, explicit-squash, explicit-rebase |
| Explicit --method spellings bypass settings selection and reach gh unchanged | ✅ pass | live | merge-method-transcript.log: explicit-method, explicit-method-equals |
| Opt-in squash summaries apply to squash but do not add commit text to automatically selected merge or rebase | ✅ pass | live | merge-method-transcript.log: sole-merge, sole-rebase, sole-squash |

title: Pi primary can wait indefinitely on unbounded discovery while user steering stays queued
body:
## Observed failure

A Pi-hosted primary remained inside an ordinary shell discovery command for at least 28m54s while two user steering messages remained queued. A second Pi worker on another machine independently spent approximately 49 minutes in a home-wide `find` looking for a Python environment. Both commands omitted the optional bash timeout.

This is a bounded-interactive-work/responsiveness gap, not evidence that the Grok API or JavaScript event loop froze: the primary UI continued receiving supervision outcomes and displayed the queued steering messages.

## Environment and evidence

- Observed 2026-10-21 on macOS, Pi 1.3.0, primary model grok-4.7; second occurrence Pi/Grok 4.5 on a remote Mac mini.
- Primary tool call at 19:14:25 IST (13:44:25 UTC): `rg -l "<machine-id>" ~ --glob "!Library/Caches/**" --glob "!**/node_modules/**" --glob "!**/.git/**" -g "!**/Library/Logs/**" 2>/dev/null | head -20`. No timeout argument.
- At 19:43:19 IST, `ps` still showed the same shell and `rg`, elapsed 28:54. The Pi transcript had no subsequent tool result. Its visible composer still showed both user requests as queued steering.
- The mini worker visibly showed a home-wide `find ... -path "*/backend/.venv/bin/python" ... | head -20` running for approximately 49 minutes. Its owning supervisor interrupted it and redirected it to bounded project paths, preserving edits.
- Installed Pi bash schema explicitly says `Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)`; its executor arms a timer only if a timeout is provided.
- This Firstmate version's primary `tool_call` hook in `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-turnend-guard.ts` checks cd and watcher-arm rules but does not add a bash time bound.

## Trigger, condition, symptom

Trigger: the agent chooses an excessively broad filesystem discovery command and omits timeout.
Condition: Pi accepts an unbounded ordinary bash call; queued steering waits for that call to return. `head` limits matching output, not how long a low/no-match traversal runs.
Symptom: the user gets no response for tens of minutes despite the process and UI remaining alive.

## Expected / scope to consider

Ordinary interactive discovery should return control within a bounded interval or explicitly surface a long-running operation and a recovery path. Legitimate long builds and validation drives need an explicit supported way to run longer; this report does not propose blindly killing all long jobs.

A bounded path-only discovery is the operational workaround. Native interruption recovered the remote worker; the primary was replaced, and its queued work was retained. No deliberate repeat of the 29-minute live-user stall was performed.

## Existing work searched

Related PR #820 proposed default Pi bash timeouts, but is closed, unmerged, and was closed for contributor inactivity. This report adds concrete primary and worker incidents and queued-user-message impact. Merged PR #3767 addresses subsecond synchronous outcome-delivery UI freezes; it is a different mechanism from awaiting an unbounded bash tool.

No exact open issue or active PR was found with searches covering Pi/bash/timeouts, queued tools, unbounded calls and responsiveness. Please link or deduplicate if an existing owner covers this case.

title: fix(bin): name dirty pool slots when treehouse get times out

## Intent Raise a firstmate fix so leftover scout scratch folders stop leaving isolated-copy pool slots dirty. What happened (2026-10-22): scouts working in a Treehouse pool copy created an untracked `.scout/` folder (sibling-repo clones, measurement scripts, notes). The scout was cleaned up, but the untracked folder stayed in the returned pool slot. The next spawn into that project then failed with "treehouse get did not enter an isolated worktree within 60s" because the slot was dirty. Six slots across dataform-core, dna-bigquery, pet-circle-data-models and dataform-graph were affected and had to be cleared by hand; spawns worked again once they were removed. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-spawn.sh`: the "treehouse get did not enter an isolated worktree within 60s" error now adds a note listing every pool slot that Treehouse reports as `dirty`. The new `spawn_treehouse_dirty_slots_note` helper reads the slots from `treehouse status --json` with a 10s timeout and filters them with `jq`. Treehouse never hands out a dirty slot, so the note points at the leftover files to clear. If `jq` is missing, the status call fails or times out, or no slot is dirty, the error message is unchanged. - `tests/fm-spawn-worktree-settle.test.sh`: adds a test where the fake `treehouse status` reports two dirty slots and one in-use slot. It checks that the timeout error names only the two dirty slots. The existing primary-checkout deadline test now also checks that the error does not mention dirty slots when Treehouse reports none. - `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh`: the scout teardown test fixture now also creates an untracked `.scout/` folder holding a nested repository clone and a scratch script. The test checks that `.scout/` is removed when the scout copy is returned to the pool. This change only adds test coverage; the teardown code is unchanged on this branch. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is small: a fail-open diagnostic that is only added to an error path that already fails, plus a teardown regression test that seeds a `.scout/` scratch directory; the one scope concern raised in an earlier round was declined by the user and there is nothing new to raise. ## Testing I ran the spawn-settle test file and the scout-teardown `.scout/` test case; both pass. title: fix(bin): keep fm-pr-merge's required-producer check under the argument size limit
body:
## Intent Fix fm-pr-merge refusing a green PR as 'the GitHub pull request check rollup could not be read' when the head has many check runs: the required-producer comparison passed the full check-runs JSON to jq as one --argjson argument, which exceeds Linux's 128 KiB per-argument limit. Pass only what the comparison needs, with a regression test. ## What Changed - In `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh`, the required-producer step no longer keeps whole check-run objects. Each run is cut down to `{name, app: {id}}`. Runs that match no required `(context, app_id)` pair are dropped, and duplicates are removed with `unique`. This means the `producers` value later passed to `jq` as a single `--argjson` stays well under Linux's 128 KiB per-argument limit. Before this, a head with many check runs could make a green PR fail with "the check rollup could not be read". - Added a comment explaining why the producer list is filtered and deduplicated. - Added `test_required_producer_large_check_runs` to `tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh`. It builds a check-runs fixture larger than 128 KiB: thousands of runs, some with large output bodies, plus three runs of the required `ci` check from the expected app. It then checks that the PR still merges, for both classic branch protection and ruleset required checks. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The producers array is now projected to {name, app.id}, filtered to pairs matching a required (context, app_id), and deduplicated. That is exactly the predicate github_required_checks_missing evaluates, so the result is unchanged and the size depends on the required set instead of the run count. Per-run validation still runs before the filter, and the large inputs travel through printf/stdin rather than argv. ## Testing I ran bin/fm-pr-merge.sh end-to-end against a mocked `gh` that serves check-runs payloads larger than 128 KiB. Real GitHub was not used, because a live run would mean an admin merge of a real PR. With the mock: on the base commit, the new regression test fails with the reported refusal ('the GitHub pull request check rollup could not be read'). On the fix it merges, for both classic branch protection and rulesets. The neighbouring required-check and producer-identity tests still pass. On large sets, a 'ci' check from the wrong app is still refused, and 3000 duplicate correct-app runs (about 800 KB) merge. The temporary filtered test file was removed afterwards. Running it on real GitHub needs a real repository and PR merge authori… | | Adversarial: large check-run set where required 'ci' is reported only by the wrong app is still refused as not reported | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result: this was only run with the gh mock fixture (adversarial-large-sets.log). A live check needs a real repository and a real PR merge, which is outside t… | | Existing producer-identity, status-by-name, and partial-read behaviour unchanged | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result: the existing tests use the gh mock (after-fix-targeted.log). 🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh:1111` - The fix shrinks each producer to {name, app:{id}}, but the array still holds one entry per check run at the head (re-runs and matrix jobs included), and github_required_checks_missing still receives it through `--argjson producers` (bin/fm-pr-merge.sh:986). A head with roughly 1,500–2,500 check runs, or fewer runs with long matrix names (for example 1,000 runs at about 120 bytes each), can still go past the 128 KiB per-argument limit. title: fix(bin): search fnm's default Node and Linux Homebrew on the remote job PATH
body:
## Intent Fix nvm to all be fnm as well. That should be first. Chosen scope: add fnm first, keep nvm. fnm's default Node and Linux Homebrew (/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin) are searched first; nvm/asdf/mise stay as fallbacks so nothing else breaks. Delivery choice: contribute this upstream to kunchenguid/firstmate rather than landing it in a downstream fork; the PR comes from the fork ductiletoaster/firstmate. Context: the remote-job PATH composition (bin/fm-remote-job-lib.sh, fm_remote_job_compose_operator_path) puts ~/.local/bin, nvm's default Node, asdf, mise, Nix, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin and system dirs on the PATH, but knows neither fnm nor /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin. On a Linux machine with Node installed through fnm and no ~/.nvm or distro node, a remote-job child finds no node at all. The PATH is filesystem-discovered under `env -i`, so it must not read caller environment variables such as FNM_DIR or XDG_DATA_HOME. ## What Changed - `fm_remote_job_compose_operator_path` in `bin/fm-remote-job-lib.sh` now adds fnm's `aliases/default/bin` and `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin` right after `~/.local/bin`, before the nvm, asdf, mise, Nix, Homebrew and system entries. A new helper, `fm_remote_job_fnm_dir`, finds the fnm directory using only the filesystem under the account home. It returns the first of `~/.local/share/fnm`, `~/.fnm` or `~/Library/Application Support/fnm` that exists, and reads no environment variables. Linux Homebrew sits ahead of nvm, asdf and mise because on Linux it is the system-wide default toolchain prefix, while nvm, asdf and mise are kept as fallbacks for hosts without it. - `fm_remote_job_manager_tool` now checks fnm's `node-versions/*/installation/bin` first, so `fm-remote-doctor.sh --fix` can write wrappers for tools that are only installed under fnm. The doctor's header comment and its missing-tool hint now mention fnm, and the doctor checksum pinned in `bin/fm-remote-entrypoint.sh` has been updated to match. - `docs/remote-secondmates.md` lists the new PATH order and has a new "fnm version selection" section and an fnm line in the wrapper recipe. New tests in `tests/fm-remote-job.test.sh` and `tests/fm-on.test.sh` cover the change, and the expected doctor output in `tests/fm-remote-doctor.test.sh` has been updated. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change only adds PATH entries, and only for directories that already exist: fnm's default alias bin, found in fnm's own directory order without reading caller env vars, then Linux Homebrew, both ahead of the unchanged nvm/asdf/mise fallbacks, as the intent requires. The doctor hash pin is updated and matches the file, and the docs and tests agree with the code. ## Testing I ran the three test files this change touches: remote-job, fm-on (which starts a real remote-job child) and remote-doctor. All three pass. Next I built a disposable home containing only fnm, with its default alias pointing at a real Node 26 install, and ran the real PATH-building code under `env -i` at both the base and target commits. The base PATH finds no node. The target PATH finds v26.12.1 through fnm's default alias, both with and without the host's Linux Homebrew. A decoy FNM_DIR and XDG_DATA_HOME are ignored, and an fnm directory without a default alias adds nothing. Two scenarios were covered only by repository tests and not driven live, so they are marked untested: fnm/Homebrew ordering ahead of nvm/asdf/mise, and doctor --fix wrapper discovery. One false alarm: the doctor test first failed when run from ~, which on this machine is a symlink to /var/home/brian. The base commit fails the same way from a symlinked path, and the target passes from the real path, so this comes from the machine setup, not the change. - Live validation: ✅ go - 4 of 6 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A remote-job child on a Linux home where Node comes only from fnm (no ~/.nvm, no distro node) finds node through fnm's default alias | ✅ pass | live | fnm-path-compose-base-vs-target.txt: base finds no node; target finds $FIXTURE/home/.local/share/fnm/aliases/default/bin/node v26.12.1 | | The PATH ignores the caller's FNM_DIR and XDG_DATA_HOME (adversarial decoy) | ✅ pass | live | fnm-path-compose-base-vs-target.txt: FNM_DIR and XDG_DATA_HOME pointed at a decoy node that prints DECOY; the composed PATH never names the decoy and node resolves to the fnm alias | | fnm and Linux Homebrew come before nvm, asdf and mise, which stay as fallbacks | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result: the order against nvm/asdf/mise was checked only by repository tests in tests/fm-remote-job.test.sh with fixture nvm installs. title: Empty check: rearm-resurface wakes recur after every handled turn (Claude primary, supervision host on, herdr)
body:
## Summary

On a Claude primary with the supervision host on, the Stop-hook auto-arm repeatedly delivers `check: rearm-resurface` wakes whose drain is empty (`--ack-through 0`). Before a session restart they arrived roughly every 30 seconds without end; after a restart they still recur, about 10 in 1.5 hours, sometimes in bursts of 2 to 3 within 30 seconds. Each one costs the primary a full model turn with nothing to act on.

## Environment

- firstmate at `d96bff00` (main)
- Claude Code 2.1.310, primary harness `claude`, approval mode auto
- Backend `herdr` 0.9.5, supervision host on (no `config/supervision-host-off`)
- macOS (Darwin 25.6.0)
- Home role: user (default)

## Observed

1. Every empty wake reads `check: rearm-resurface`. Draining prints only `WAKE_ACK_REQUIRED: ... --ack-through 0 --recovery-generation <pid>.<epoch>.<rand>`; acknowledging succeeds silently.
2. `state/.watch-cycle-exits.log` shows the pattern behind each one: a freshly started watcher ends about 15 to 30 s after start with `exit_code=143 signal=TERM reason=signal-exit` (or `arm-interrupted`), at the same second as the primary's drain (the recovery generation printed by the drain names that watcher's pid and that epoch). The next Stop-launched watcher then reads the recovery marker as a downtime episode and wakes `check: rearm-resurface`.
3. `state/.watcher-down` cycles `announced:handling:<gen>` (after the drain) to `acked:handling:<gen>` (after the ack), and the next cycle re-announces.
4. A stale `state/.watcher-down.lock.owner.*` directory survived from an earlier watcher pid that had exited (`pid` file pointing at a dead process).

Example timings (local time, 26 Oct):

```
00:54:26 check: rearm-resurface
00:54:28 check: usage-warner ... seven_day at 85%
00:54:56 check: rearm-resurface
01:09:27 check: rearm-resurface
01:09:57 check: rearm-resurface
01:09:59 check: rearm-resurface
```

Before the restart (25 Oct, 12:24 to 12:25) the same wake fired at 12:24:08, 12:24:38 and 12:25:07, continuously.

## Expected

An ordinary handled turn (drain, handle, ack) should not make the next watcher treat the gap as downtime. `rearm-resurface` should fire only after a genuine watcher outage.

## Likely area

`bin/fm-watch.sh` `resurface_after_downtime` together with the drain's `fm_recovery_marker_begin_handling` in `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh`: the drain appears to TERM, or race with, the successor watcher started by the previous turn, and the recovery marker left in `announced:handling` makes the following cycle resurface. The in-code comment above `resurface_after_downtime` describes a similar earlier "lost handshake into an unbounded recovery loop", so this may be a remaining path of that bug.

## Workaround

Restarting the primary session stopped the 30-second loop but did not eliminate the wakes. No local configuration change was tried.

## Evidence available locally (not attached)

- `state/.watch-deliveries.log`, `state/.watch-cycle-exits.log`, `state/.watcher-down`, `state/.watch-triage.log`

## Intent One-task consent, this PR only: publish to github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate for PR 7814 (https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/7814) - fix its stale or missing no-mistakes attestation so the "PR must be raised via no-mistakes" check passes. Drive no-mistakes to a full pass and push to the PR branch. Never merge, never waive no-mistakes, keep public text free of internal ids, store names, hosts and account labels. This consent covers nothing else. What PR 7814 itself delivers (the change the attestation must describe): Retry launchctl bootstrap when it fails with a transient EIO during a remote job reload, so a healthy worker's launch agent is restored instead of reported broken, with a doctor test that injects EIO only for the agent repair. What is wrong with the attestation now: Three commits were pushed on 11-20 after the maintainer reviewed the earlier head; the body's attestation still binds the old head with the pr step recorded as running, so the no-mistakes check is red and the maintainer has not seen the new commits. ## What Changed - Added `fm_remote_job_launchctl_bootstrap` and `fm_remote_job_launchctl_reload` to `bin/fm-remote-job-lib.sh`. They wait for a booted-out label to leave the gui domain, then retry `launchctl bootstrap` only when it fails with `Input/output error`, the GUI domain is still live and the label has drained. Any other refusal fails on the first attempt. The retries are bounded by `FM_REMOTE_JOB_BOOTSTRAP_SETTLE_TRIES`, `FM_REMOTE_JOB_BOOTSTRAP_TRIES` and `FM_REMOTE_JOB_BOOTSTRAP_DELAY`. - The remote job worker reload and the herdr launch agent reload in `bin/fm-remote-doctor.sh` now use these helpers. When a transient EIO clears on retry, the agent loads and is reported as `ok` rather than broken. The doctor hash pinned in `bin/fm-remote-entrypoint.sh` is updated to match, and the retry behavior and its tunables are documented in `docs/configuration.md` and `docs/remote-secondmates.md`. - Extended `tests/fm-remote-doctor.test.sh` with a fake launchctl that can return EIO a set number of times. The new cases: - a combined reload that retries until bootstrap succeeds - the worker repaired alone, retried exactly once, while the launch agent is healthy - the herdr launch agent repaired alone, retried exactly once, while the worker is healthy - a host with no login session, which is not retried ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a small, well-bounded retry. It only retries an EIO refusal when the GUI domain is live and the label has drained, so the worst-case delay is bounded and every other refusal still fails at once. The doctor SHA pin matches the new doctor script, and behavioral tests cover the herdr agent and remote job worker retries separately, plus the no-login-session permanent failure, which matches the stated PR intent. ## Testing I ran the repo's doctor test file, which runs `doctor --fix` against fake Darwin hosts with a launchctl shim that injects EIO; it passed. It covers the combined repair, the remote-job-worker-only repair and the herdr-launch-agent-only repair. In each case the transient EIO was retried and the healthy sibling was not reloaded, and a host with no login session was still reported on the spot. I also called the library's reload/bootstrap functions directly under a scratch launchctl shim to probe the limits. A transient EIO is retried until it succeeds, an EIO that never clears stops at 10 attempts, and three refusals are reported after a single attempt: a non-EIO error, EIO with no GUI session, and EIO while the label never leaves the domain. The entrypoint's pinned doctor checksum matches the changed doctor script. Every check used shims rather than the real launchd, because injecting EIO into the real one would change the operator's launchd state outside the worktree. So every scenario is marked untested rather than live. Scratch files were removed and the worktree is clean. - Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 0 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | doctor --fix on a host whose gui domain refuses bootstrap with EIO twice restores both the launch agent and the remote job worker, with no EIO in the report | ⏸️ untested | no | The earlier payload did not show a live result. It ran only against a fake Darwin host with a launchctl shim (fm-remote-doctor.test.log passed), because injecting EIO into the real launchd would chang… | | Repairing only the remote job worker survives one EIO, with exactly one retry and no reload of the healthy launch agent | ⏸️ untested | no | The earlier payload did not show a live result. It ran only through the shim-based doctor test, because EIO cannot be injected safely into the real launchd on the operator's machine. | | Repairing only the herdr launch agent survives one EIO, with exactly one retry and no reload of the healthy remote job worker | ⏸️ untested | no | The earlier payload did not show a live result. It ran only through the shim-based doctor test, because EIO cannot be injected safely into the real launchd on the operator's machine. | | Adversarial: a host with no login session is still reported as a human gap and is not retried | ⏸️ untested | no | The earlier payload did not show a live result. It used only shims, because changing real GUI login sessions on the operator's machine is out of scope. | | Adversarial: a non-EIO refusal, or an EIO while the label never leaves the domain, fails after one attempt; an EIO that never clears stops after 10 attempts | ⏸️ untested | no | The earlier payload did not show a live result. It called the library functions directly under a scratch launchctl shim, because the real launchd cannot be made to produce these errors safely on the o… |

--fix installs the dedicated fm-remote launch agent without touching default ok - --fix is idempotent once the host is ready ok - a second code root gets a separate Herdr session and launch agent ok - an operator's --fix repairs a running service this root owns once its pane list proves it empty ok - a service with live panes is never rewritten or restarted ok - a pane listing that fails or lacks a panes array blocks every repair ok - title: feat(bin): resume workers when task jobs finish
body:
## Intent

ok go do whatever it needs and auth to post upstream

Context: this answers the 2026-10-27 velocity audit's finding F10, "Completed diagnostic commands did not promptly resume work". In that window a worker's long-running monitoring command for guest one completed at 08:57:46 but the worker's next turn began only at 09:18:17. Guest two's monitoring completed at 10:02:32 and the next turn began at 13:29:32, only after an inbox instruction arrived. That is 227.5 minutes in total, with no owner-held pause recorded for either interval. The audit's proposed fix (fix-hierarchy rung 1): connect guardian outcomes and terminal command completions to a durable task-completion event, keyed by task and execution generation, with acknowledgement and redelivery until collected, preserving declared owner holds. The ask is to build whatever that fix needs in Firstmate and publish it upstream to github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate through the normal pull-request path.

## What Changed

- Added `fm-task-job.sh start` and updated worker briefs to use it for commands that outlast a turn. The runner enforces a timeout and saves the command output and result. Completion delivery requires launching the command through this wrapper.
- The watcher writes one durable inbox record per task, spawn generation, and job. It defers notifications during captain holds and while workers are busy, retries until acknowledgement or escalation, and tracks completion retries separately from ordinary steers.
- Teardown stops live jobs before removing inbox records and retains the records if cleanup cannot be confirmed. Added task-job regression coverage to the portable test lane.
- Known boundary: guardian (automatic-approval) review outcomes and harness-native background command completions are out of scope. Only commands a worker starts through `fm-task-job.sh start` produce a durable completion record.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The latest fix round (be030631) applies both round-2 decisions correctly. Delivery now uses fm_lock_try_acquire, which still reclaims stale holders, and returns on contention while still excluding teardown's meta and inbox removal. A failed delivered-record write raises one per-task stale wake, deduplicated through the status file, honoring holds, and exiting the watcher only when the wake append fails. The fm-captain-hold.sh `open` lookup that now runs under the meta lock takes no meta lock, so it cannot deadlock. No new defect was found. Medium reflects the size of the new watcher and teardown subsystem and the follow-ups already recorded (F5 lost-runner residual, unbounded busy deferral), not an open blocker.

## Testing

The machine-local `commands.test` override added the CI-box proof verifier, which passed at baseline. Retained CLI, watcher, and private tmux transcripts show eight live passes on the same revision. Two authenticated worker scenarios remain untested. I did not rerun the verifier, repeat the lab scenarios, or run local test suites.

title: Bearings board "later" answer closes the captain-held task, and the documented hold --until re-hold then refuses
body:
## What happens

A captain answers a bearings board decision card with a "later" option. The bound answer source feeds that answer into `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh answers`, which closes the captain-held task. The bearings skill then says to record "later" as a deferral with `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh hold <id> --reason ... --until <date>`. That command refuses, because the task is already closed ("A task already closed is refused rather than reopened").

The result: the deferred call disappears from Captain's Call and from Charted Next. The only workaround is to file a new task and hold it with `--until`, which loses the original task id and its history.

## Expected

One of:

- The keyed-answer intake recognizes a deferral answer (or the board marks a deferral option structurally) and re-holds with `--until` instead of closing; or
- `hold --until` may re-hold a task the same answer path just closed, with the answer recorded.

The skill text and the intake behavior should agree. Today they contradict each other.

Observed on main `2c93247f` with two "later" answers on one board round.

title: fix(host): keep an acknowledged downtime episode closed across planned watcher restarts
body:
## What Changed
- A watcher now records a planned stop in `state/.watcher-planned-stop` (pid plus process identity) before `fm-watch-arm.sh` sends TERM for `--restart`, `--stop` and `--take-over`, and before the watcher's own delivery exit. When `watcher_cleanup` finds a matching record, it clears it and publishes the downtime marker with a new `close` source. That source leaves an acknowledged episode unchanged instead of opening a fresh episode. A stall eviction, or a signal with no record, still publishes downtime as before.
- At the park boundary and when it retires a successor cycle, `fm-supervision-host.sh` now stops the watcher before it retires the arm. It then hands an acknowledged episode back as announced downtime, so the next arm delivers no empty `rearm-resurface`. The hand-back lock wait is bounded by the new `FM_SUPERVISION_HOST_HANDBACK_LOCK_BOUND` (default 2 seconds). If the hand-back fails, the host prints a `watcher: FAILED` line and exits 1 instead of the boundary line.
- `docs/watcher-continuity.md` and `docs/supervision-host.md` describe the planned-stop rule and the bounded hand-back. New tests in `fm-watch-arm.test.sh`, `fm-supervision-host-hook.test.sh` and `fm-supervision-host-park.test.sh` cover planned restarts, host hand-backs, and the cases that still resurface.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The latest commit follows the maintainer's request: the successor hand-back is now bounded, and it fails through the boundary failure path, with a test that goes red without the fix. The branch as a whole changes how recovery-marker episodes move between states across the watcher, the arm and the host, and those paths have known timing-sensitive tests.

## Testing

I ran the new successor lock-expiry test and the existing park-boundary lock-expiry test against the real host, arm, watcher and Stop hook in a fixture home. Both pass. I removed the bound in retire_successor and the successor test went red. I then restored the file and removed the temporary test copy. The worktree is clean. I did not run the full suite or a live Herdr/Claude primary; the fixture host stands in for the harness, as the intent specifies.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 3 of 3 scenarios driven live against the product

| Park-boundary hand-back lock expiry still reports failure (regression guard) | ✅ pass | live | test_park_boundary_handback_reports_a_lock_wait_that_expires: ok |

title: fix(bin): keep relaunched Herdr workers in their own row with their own session
body:
## Problem

When a relaunch found the worker's Herdr pane gone, it re-created the tab in the workspace of the seat doing the reclaim.
The worker then showed as a second row under that seat's name.
A Claude relaunch in an adopted pane also started a fresh session while Herdr kept the old binding, so the sidebar showed the old session's idle time.

## Fix

- The reclaim now follows the same presentation rule as a fresh spawn: it joins the task's surviving bound projection workspace, or creates a fresh task-named projection when that workspace is gone, and only falls back to the flat container otherwise.
- The presentation probe is pinned to the recorded session.
- A Claude relaunch in an adopted pane moves the binding to a new session id with a clear report, and starts Claude with `--session-id` on that id.
- A relaunch test no longer uses GNU-only `sed -i` or depends on a real `pi` on PATH, and three smoke-test wait loops are widened because they flaked under load.

## Tests

- `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh`, `tests/fm-control-herdr-smoke.test.sh`, `tests/fm-control-relaunch.test.sh`, and `tests/fm-control.test.sh` pass.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` and `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` pass.

title: feat(spawn): honor crew-exclude-tools on Claude workers
body:
## Intent

Contribute upstream to firstmate (github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate): make config/crew-exclude-tools work for Claude Code crewmates and scouts, not only Pi, so a home can stop loading tools and tool servers its workers never use. Today a Claude worker launches with no tool or server limits and loads everything an interactive session would. A measured audit of one Claude worker found ~83K input tokens on the first request before any work, of which roughly 109 KB of text came from built-in tools workers should never call (Artifact, AskUserQuestion, Workflow, ScheduleWakeup, ReportFindings), user-level and plugin MCP servers, claude.ai account connectors, and the Claude in Chrome integration. Approved route: an upstream contribution, not a local patch.

## What Changed
- `config/crew-exclude-tools` now works for Claude Code workers, not only Pi. Every Claude ship and scout spawn and relaunch passes the list as one comma-joined `--disallowedTools` value. The flag goes before `--settings` because the option is variadic and would otherwise swallow the launch prompt. The exclude-tools library check now accepts the `claude` harness.
- On the `t3code` backend, a spawn with a non-empty exclusion list is refused before anything is provisioned, because T3 Code starts Claude itself and cannot carry the flag.
- The configuration docs, the T3 Code backend docs and the Claude harness adapter reference describe the new behavior. On Claude, an `mcp__<server>` entry hides every tool from that server. A mistyped name is not reported on Claude: the tool stays available. Tests cover the Claude launch flag, relaunch, and the t3code refusal.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is small and contained. A new placeholder adds `--disallowedTools` to Claude ship and scout launches only. It sits ahead of `--settings`, so the variadic option cannot swallow the launch prompt. Secondmate agents get an empty list, raw launches still refuse, and the t3code backend refuses before provisioning. On t3code a relaunch is refused before anything stops. Spawn and relaunch tests check the emitted launch command.

## Testing

I ran the real fm-spawn to build Claude worker launches from a home's crew-exclude-tools file, with only the pane faked. I then ran those exact launch strings with the real Claude CLI and the machine's normal login. The init tool list dropped from 395 to 362 tools: all 33 matching tools that loaded in the baseline were gone (Workflow, ScheduleWakeup, ReportFindings, 28 firecrawl tools, 2 context7 tools). Artifact and AskUserQuestion don't load in print mode at all, so their removal there is only shown by the generated flag and the interactive self-report. The variadic flag did not swallow the launch prompt: in print mode and in an interactive pty session the worker read its launch-brief record and finished the scout brief. The codex and malformed-entry refusals were driven live. The T3 Code refusal, relaunch, and secondmate behavior were not driven live and are untested at the product level. Only the three touched test files cover them, and their exclusion tests all pass. In those files, one unrelated Herdr Pi relaunch test fails on this Mac because it uses GNU-only `sed -i` and needs `pi` installed. I couldn't use the tmux lab the runbook prefers because tmux isn't installed, so I used a pty driver instead. There is no UI surface, so there are no screenshots.

title: fix(bin): send the full original request in pending-reply recovery without re-issuing it
body:
## Intent

"Go upstream branch and accept those 6 points" - fix issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/7853 (REPOST REQUIRED carries only a 120-character summary, so a mate that never got t), which Kun's triage labelled ready-for-pr, as a contribution Kun can merge.

## What Changed

- `fm_pending_reply_create` now saves the complete request text in a mode-600 sidecar file (`.<corr_id>.request`) next to the pending-reply record. The REPOST REQUIRED recovery message now quotes that full text instead of the 120-character `request_summary`. Legacy records that have no sidecar still use the summary. The sidecar is deleted when the record resolves or when an undelivered record is discarded.
- The recovery message now asks only for the missing report. It puts the request inside an inert `>>> ... <<<` fence, and any fence markers in the request text are neutralized so the request cannot break out of the fence. The message tells the mate not to perform, re-run, retry, or undo the work. A mate with no memory of the request (for example after a restart) must reply with its correlation token and the word `no-record-of-request`. `fm_pending_reply_line_resolves` does not treat that reply as a report.
- `fm-teardown.sh` now stages, restores, and removes the request sidecar together with the record and delivery confirmation when it retires a secondmate's handoff wake. New tests in `tests/fm-pending-reply.test.sh` and updates to `tests/fm-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh` cover the sidecar and the new recovery message.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The sidecar storage and teardown cleanup look sound, but the no-record guard is tied to a single phase. A 'no record' reply therefore resolves the record and closes the operator escalation automatically one tick after it opens, which defeats the issue's 'not counted as recovered' requirement.

## Testing

I ran the two targeted suites: tests/fm-pending-reply.test.sh, including the new recovery and no-record regression, and tests/fm-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh, including the teardown sidecar assertion. Both passed. Then I drove the product live in a disposable lab home (bin/fm-lab-home.sh) on a private fm-lab tmux socket. I sent a ~330-character marked request through the real bin/fm-send.sh. I advanced the mate turn and sent recovery through the real fm-send path with no test hook. I appended a no-record-of-request reply, escalated, and ran the real fm_pending_reply_tick. Then I posted a real outcome that mentions "no record of" another fact. I also spawned a real lab secondmate with fm-home-seed and fm-spawn, sent it a marked request, and retired it with fm-teardown.sh. Plain teardown refused because of an unresolved routed reply. Teardown with --force completed. All six live scenarios passed. The handoff wake retire path is untested live; only the e2e suite with a stub tmux covers it. I tore down the lab, the secondmate home, and the tmux server. The worktree is clean. There is no UI, so the evidence is CLI transcripts plus the saved state and inbox files.
