title: Local-only: no supported way to land a revised, re-approved commit after the first done head is latched
body:
## Problem

A local-only task latches its first accepted `done` head as `local_done_head`, and `bin/fm-dod-lib.sh` says revised work "needs a new task/approval record". In practice there is no supported way for that new record to adopt an already-reviewed revised commit.

What happened (Firstmate `bb8dd209`, Linux): a local-only task reported ready at commit A. The captain then asked for more changes on the same task, which produced commit B on the same branch, and approved B for landing. The guarded local merge refused B because the task's pinned head is A, which is the intended behavior. Following the documented route, a fresh task was created to carry B. But a fresh task gets its own `fm/<task-id>` branch and worktree and expects its worker to produce the work, so nothing records "land this existing approved commit". The fresh task never ran (it also hit a full worktree pool). The approved changes ended up applied to the home by hand outside the guarded merge.

## Question / suggestion

What is the intended flow for a local-only change that is revised and re-approved after its first `done`?

Options that would keep the immutability guarantee:

- a guarded "supersede" step that records a new captain approval for an exact descendant commit of the pinned head on the same task branch, with the approval kept as an audit record; or
- a supported way for a new task to adopt an exact existing commit (no worker launch), whose own `local_done_head` is then latched to it.

Either would let the guarded merge land revised local-only work instead of pushing operators toward manual application.

title: feat(bin): add opt-in receipts for acknowledging review findings
body:
## Intent

In the maintainer's triage, restore and opt-in PRs merge automatically after a green full suite, while new-default PRs (ones that change what an unconfigured home does) wait for the maintainer's own decision.
https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8190 (branch `fm/up-8046-ack-receipt` on the fork tiago-peixoto/firstmate, for issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8046) was triaged new-default: "Token-only acks of finding-carrying signals are now refused on every home."
The approved adjustment: refuse token-only acks only when one new off-by-default config file exists. A home without the new file must behave exactly as current upstream main, including homes that use any existing setting; this moves the PR to opt-in.
The maintainer rejected an earlier conversion (PR 8263) that reused existing settings, because homes already using them would get the new behavior without turning on anything new; so the gate is one new file used for nothing else.
Update method for this PR: merge current upstream main into the PR branch, never rebase, never force-push.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-contributions.sh` reads a new presence flag, `config/contribution-ack-receipts`. Only when that file exists, `ack` refuses a token-only acknowledgement of a signal that carries reviewer findings (an inline review comment, a re-raised unanswered thread, or a review with text). Such a signal then needs `ack <task> <url> <token> handoff` (a steering-inbox record of the owning task, sent or already handled, must name the signal's source URL) or `ack ... disposition <evidence-url> <summary>` (the evidence must be another comment or review on the same contribution, or the signal's own source once teardown has removed the task record). The accepted receipt is stored in the task's record as `receipts[]`, and is not copied to a late owner of the same contribution.
- Without the file, the `ack` branch, the saved-record validation in `bin/fm-contributions.jq`, and the 500-character body preview keep their previous code paths: `ack` takes exactly one event token and neither requires nor creates receipts. `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh` passes the same flag to the shared record validation when it settles a PR hold.
- `docs/configuration.md` gains a "Contribution acknowledgement receipts" section, with matching one-line updates in `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, and the `bearings` and `operational-home-layout` skills. `tests/fm-contributions.test.sh` adds 16 tests covering the off-by-default behavior, the effective config directory, both receipt forms and their refusals, late owners, and hold settlement.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Every new behavior (receipt refusal, receipt validation in valid_record, body trimming, settlement validation) is gated on the single new file config/contribution-ack-receipts, and with the file absent the ack branch, record validation and saved preview trace to the same results as upstream main; the only unconditional change is del(.receipts) on a late owner's copy, which is the recorded round 1 decision and a no-op where no receipts exist.

## Testing

I drove the real bin/fm-contributions.sh (poll, pending, ack) in a disposable home, with only `gh` replaced by a local emulator serving a synthetic pull request o/r#8. For three default homes (no config, review-bot allowlist, FM_CONTRIBUTIONS_REPLY_AGE) I ran the same command sequence on the upstream base scripts and on the head scripts and the transcripts (output, exit codes, saved records) were identical. With the new flag file I confirmed token-only acks of an approved review with findings, an inline comment and its re-raise are refused and leave the signal pending, that invalid receipts are refused, that a valid handoff or disposition is saved, that signals without findings still ack by token, that file contents are ignored, and that removing the file restores token-only acks while keeping saved receipts. The existing tests/fm-contributions.test.sh also passed through bin/fm-test-run.sh (exit 0, failed=0), which covers the late-owner receipt-copy regression and hold settlement. No full suite, lint, or Herdr run was done, and handoff steers were written with the product's fm_task_inbox_write library rather than a live fm-send to a real worker pane. No visual evidence applies because the surface is a CLI.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 9 of 9 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unconfigured home (local CLI, emulated gh, synthetic PR o/r#8): token-only ack of an approved review with findings succeeds with no output, no receipt and the same saved record as upstream main | ✅ pass | live | default-unconfigured.base.txt vs default-unconfigured.head.txt, default-unconfigured.diff is empty |
| Adversarial: home using existing settings (config/contribution-review-bots, or FM_CONTRIBUTIONS_REPLY_AGE with an inline comment and its re-raise) but not the new file still acks by token alone, ident… | ✅ pass | live | default-review-bots.diff and default-reply-age.diff are empty; transcripts in default-review-bots.head.txt and default-reply-age.head.txt |
| Without the new file, receipt arguments (handoff, disposition) are rejected with the upstream error 'ack needs one exact event token' | ✅ pass | live | default-unconfigured.head.txt, exit 1 on both receipt forms, identical on base |

## Issues

Closes #8046

title: fix(bin): run captain slash commands as commands in local Claude secondmates
body:
## Intent

A slash command the captain types to the main firstmate for a second mate (for example /pstack:sharpen or /pstack:how) does not run in the second mate: it arrives as chat, and the second mate's skill tool refuses skills marked disable-model-invocation. Build a local fix and then file the fix to firstmate main. It must be a fix that works with 100% certainty, and the smallest one.

Context: bin/fm-send.sh puts the from-firstmate marker before every message to a local secondmate, so a leading "/" invocation reaches the harness as marker-prefixed chat; its help names this as follow-up fm-send-secondmate-harness-invocation-r1 and says the marker currently stays in front for byte compatibility. Local issue draft, in substance: `bin/fm-send.sh <secondmate> '/some-skill args'` prefixes the from-firstmate marker before the typed text, so the secondmate's harness receives marker-prefixed chat instead of a parser command; the secondmate's model then tries its own skill tool, which refuses any skill with `disable-model-invocation: true` (most pstack skills). Expected: a captain-named slash command routed to a local secondmate executes as the harness's own command, with the reply still routed through the secondmate's status channel. Reproduce: seed a local Claude secondmate; run `FM_HOME=<home> bin/fm-send.sh <mate> '/pstack:sharpen <text>'`; the mate reports the skill is not model-invocable and does not run it. Workaround in use: send the skill's SKILL.md path and ask the mate to read and follow it.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-send.sh`: a marked message to a local Claude secondmate is now sent as `/<command> <marker>corr=<id> <rest>` when it opens with `/` and the command is an installed skill or custom command. Claude's parser then runs the command, so skills with `disable-model-invocation` work, and the reply still goes through the secondmate status channel. A new helper, `fm_send_claude_command_installed`, finds the command in the secondmate home's `.claude` or in the account's user root (`skills/N/SKILL.md` or `commands/N.md`). For a `plugin:name` command, it uses an enabled plugin from `plugins/installed_plugins.json` and follows the Claude settings order. Built-ins, unknown commands, non-Claude secondmates, and remote secondmates keep the marker in front and arrive as chat, as before.
- When the rewritten command is longer than 800 bytes, the script refuses it before it types anything and removes the new pending-reply record, because Claude pastes longer typed input as a block and does not parse it as a command. The header comments, the inbox-plane comments, and `docs/agent-control.md` now describe the new behavior and no longer describe the old marker-first limit.
- Tests: `tests/fm-send-secondmate-marker.test.sh` gets new cases for the slash rewrite, which commands resolve, and the 800-byte refusal. `tests/fm-send-remote-delivery.test.sh` now checks that a slash command to a remote secondmate keeps the marker in front of its inbox record.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The rewrite applies only to marked typed sends to local claude secondmates whose command resolves to an installed skill, command, or enabled plugin, and every unresolved or oversized case falls back to the old marker-first bytes; the remaining model-dependent concerns were already declined by the user.

## Testing

`I built a disposable lab: a marked parent home, a seeded secondmate home, and a real Claude Code 2.1.330 secondmate on a private tmux socket. I ran fm-send.sh from a shell on the same socket and drove five scenarios live, then ran the two targeted test files. The user-only skill command ran natively. The enabled pstack plugin skill also ran natively: the transcript shows its <command-name> tag. Both replies reached the parent status channel with their corr. An 817-byte command was refused with exit 1: the secondmate pane did not change, the transcript had no copy of the text, and no pending-reply record stayed. A 792-byte command ran natively and received all 146 words. The built-in /rename arrived as marker-first chat and did not run. Both test files passed. Pane captures, fm-send transcripts, status lines and transcript tags are in the evidence directory's r3/ folder. I removed the lab completely. This is a CLI/TUI change, so pane text captures are the visual evidence. I did not take screenshots.`

title: fix(bin): retire watcher state after endpoint teardown
body:
## Intent

Make sure this is fixed, and publish the fix to firstmate's upstream. On 2026-11-10 the captain said of this item and its sibling: "I want to make sure it is fixed", and then, having been offered either a bounded one-task contribution consent or a standing maintainer opt-in for publishing upstream, "You have my consent on both issues." That authorizes fixing this item and publishing it under a one-task contribution consent; the home's standing role is deliberately unchanged.

Context needed to read that ask: this item was filed 2026-11-08 after four PeakPeek tasks were cleaned up and monitoring kept raising "stopped responding" alerts for a freed workspace. A verification scout established the following against head 913bb7a7:

- The leak half is still present, unbounded and untested: cleanup never removes the watcher's per-endpoint marker families (.count-, .hash-, .stale-, .stale-since-, .paused-, .paused-rechecked-, .paused-resurfaced-), and bin/fm-watch-key-lib.sh:13-23 documents that as intended behaviour. 31 orphaned markers in this home's state/ were live proof, and the away daemon's mirror list at bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh:605-627 already omits .hash- and .count-.
- The harm half was NOT reproducible in the steady state, for two independent reasons: the staleness loop is gated on recorded_windows, which is meta-gated, so an endpoint with no state/<id>.meta cannot raise a notification from it; and the v3 key rotation from 10b71638 (#7923) left every pre-existing marker inert.
- BUT on 2026-11-10 a freed endpoint did produce one delivered stale notification immediately after its own task's cleanup. Evidence: state/.watch-deliveries.log's final row records stale: default:t12 directly after the row for that task's completion signal; no state/<id>.meta referenced that endpoint at the time; state/ held no marker naming it, because v3 stores these as .count-v3.<sha256> and .hash-v3.<sha256>; state/.watch-triage.log has no classification row for it, so it was delivered rather than absorbed; and the durable wake queue was already empty with no acknowledgement pending. Most plausible cause: a race between cleanup removing the task record and the monitoring pane sweep that had already inventoried that endpoint. Cost was one supervisor turn; it did not repeat or escalate.

So the gate narrows the harm but does not eliminate it. The sibling item fm-away-idle-stale-hash-q1 shares this root cause and is deliberately serialized behind this task: do not implement it here.

Follow-up approval on 2026-11-24 to finish PR https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8356: address both Greptile review findings required by maintainer kunchenguid - (1) in bin/fm-watch.sh wedge_timer_check and resurface_absorbed, recheck endpoint retirement after slow classification, deferral, guard, and status/throttle reads immediately before each escalation count write or ordinary/capped stale wake append; (2) in bin/fm-watch.sh post-classification paths, recheck and reconcile endpoint retirement after pause_state_class so concurrent teardown while returning working cannot recreate .stale- or .stale-since- markers, with test coverage where the current-state reader removes the record while returning working - and complete a full validation run with lint enabled so the PR carries a valid pipeline attestation bound to the new head.

## What Changed

- Centralized v3 watcher marker-family enumeration and cleanup, retiring freed endpoint markers during teardown while preserving markers for shared endpoints and pruning post-removal wake entries.
- Added retirement rechecks throughout watcher classification and escalation paths so concurrent teardown cannot publish stale wakes, write escalation state, or recreate stale markers.
- Added teardown and watcher race coverage, registered the new test shard, and documented the marker lifecycle.

## Risk Assessment

🚨 High: A concurrent cleanup can still produce the stale notification this change claims to eliminate, so the durable-fix invariant is not guaranteed.

## Testing

Ran the dedicated watcher race suite and direct teardown integration suite; both passed, with evidence showing stale-wake suppression, marker retirement/preservation, and post-removal wake pruning. No lint or static analysis was run per phase rules.

title: feat(bin): support Auggie as a primary harness
body:
## Intent

Support Augment's auggie CLI as a primary harness for Firstmate, so a Firstmate session run inside auggie is detected as auggie and acquires the session lock instead of falling back to read-only. Auggie runs as a node bundle, so a node process is identified structurally only when its main script resolves into the @augmentcode/auggie package, never from "any node" and never from a script merely named auggie elsewhere; an exact auggie command name is also accepted, like every other harness's exact name. Node options before the script, including every Node option that takes a value in either the --opt value or --opt=value form (for example --require /x or --require=/x), must not hide the script, on both the /proc argv path and the flattened ps-argument path, with tests.

Auggie is a primary only: fm-spawn must refuse auggie as a crewmate, scout, or secondmate worker with a clear primary-only error, whether it comes from config, an explicit harness argument, or a raw launch command. For raw launch commands, the guarantee is limited to the forms the refusal really covers, each with a test: a simple command running auggie directly or behind common wrappers such as env, command, exec, nohup, sudo, or timeout (including leading assignments, sudo VAR=value assignments, quoted program paths with spaces, redirections like 2>log, and wrapper options). An env -S split string is checked best-effort: a split string that holds the whole command is inspected, but a payload split across -S and the remaining argv is not guaranteed. Compound launches (chained commands, subshell groups, command substitutions) are checked best-effort and not guaranteed. Shell -c strings, heredoc stdin, and eval are not inspected and not guaranteed. fm-spawn --help, the documentation, and the comments must state these limits. Auggie worker support is out of scope.

The tracked .augment/settings.json PreToolUse hook matches only the bash tool, because Auggie warns at startup that launch-process is a deprecated tool name; the documentation must not mention launch-process.

## What Changed

- Detect Auggie primary sessions and preserve session-lock ownership using exact command names or package-resolved Node scripts, including Node options before the script.
- Reject Auggie worker launches from configuration, explicit arguments, and supported raw command forms; document parsing limits.
- Add bash-only PreToolUse hooks, foreground checkpoint supervision instructions, compatibility documentation, and regression coverage.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The integration changes shared command parsing and session-lock identity, but no new material defect was substantiated within the accepted scope and recorded decisions.

## Testing

All live scenarios and targeted suites passed after correcting a test’s PID-1 adoption assumption for subreaper hosts. Retained CLI evidence, awaited every check, and removed the disposable lab.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 4 of 4 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A real Auggie primary detects itself and acquires and reconfirms its session lock; valued Node options and spaced paths preserve detection | ✅ pass | live | Real Auggie primary and hook blocking; Live Node identity boundaries |
| Ordinary Node programs, including a script named auggie outside its package, are rejected as Auggie | ✅ pass | live | Live Node identity boundaries |
| Configured, explicit, and supported raw Auggie launches refuse ships, scouts, and secondmates with the primary-only explanation | ✅ pass | live | Live worker refusal transcripts |
| Published help states inspection limits, and bash-only hooks load cleanly and block backgrounded watcher commands | ✅ pass | live | Real Auggie primary and hook blocking; Registered bash hook behavior; Published spawn help |

title: A PR state change the captain asked to hear about costs a model turn before it reaches the captain, and a PR with no task cannot be followed at all
body:
## Problem

When the captain asks to be told when a pull request merges, closes, or goes red, Firstmate has no path that delivers that one line to the captain directly.
Every PR observer on main (the merge poll from `bin/fm-pr-check.sh`, the opt-in `config/pr-health-monitor`, the supervision host's captain outcomes) ends in a wake to the primary model, which then relays the state in its own words.
The forge already produced the exact fact (`merged`, `closed`, `checks failed on <sha>`), so the model turn adds a full context re-read and a paraphrase, and nothing else.

A PR the captain names that no ship task owns cannot be followed at all: `fm-pr-check.sh` takes a task id, `fm-pr-health.sh` and `fm-contributions.sh` own only PRs a task recorded or a live task copy is on, and "repository-wide PR discovery never establishes ownership".

## Observed

On a home with the supervision host on, a merged-PR poll result becomes a `check: pr-poll: merged` wake, the host's engine spends a turn judging it a captain outcome, main spends another turn relaying it, and the captain reads a sentence that carries the same information as the poll's one-word output.
A 30-day measurement across several homes found about 10% of all machine-triggered supervisor turns ended with nothing to say, and merge and PR-state wakes are among the reasons.
When the captain asks "tell me when upstream PR N merges" for a PR no task opened, the only option is to spawn a task around it or to check by hand.

## Expected

- The captain can name a PR or merge request to follow, with or without a task behind it.
- A state change on a followed PR (merged, closed without merge, checks turned red, review requested changes) reaches the captain as one line with the forge's own words and the PR URL, written directly to the captain-facing surface, with no model turn in between.
- A task-owned PR that merges still runs the existing cleanup and backlog path; the direct line is in addition to that, not a replacement for it.
- The model is still woken when the state change needs a decision or an action, and not otherwise.

## Why it matters

Merge and PR-state events are frequent and fully machine-readable, so they are the cheapest class of event to take off the model.
Each one today costs a context re-read of a large primary session to produce a sentence the forge already wrote.

## How to verify

Follow a PR with no task behind it, merge it on the forge, and confirm the captain-facing surface shows one line with the PR URL and the merged state while the primary's transcript shows no new turn for it.
Repeat with a PR closed without merging and with a check that fails on a new head.

title: fix(bin): keep the watcher liveness beacon fresh across a long cycle
body:
## What Changed

- `bin/fm-watch.sh` now refreshes `state/.last-watcher-beat` between the units of a long cycle (pending-reply records, signals, windows, status scans, checks, secondmates, captain calls, pane captures, Rex/Herdr sweeps) instead of only at the top of a cycle. Child sweeps and command-substitution subshells write a separate `state/.last-watcher-progress` marker that `watcher_wait_child_progress` relays into beacon refreshes, so a frozen parent still ages its beacon; cycle counting moved to a new `state/.watch-cycle` marker, which the watch triage test helpers now wait on.
- Grace resolution is unified in `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh`: `fm_beacon_grace`, `fm_watch_settings_load`, and isolated-subshell `fm_poll_derived_grace`/`fm_watcher_stall_bound` replace the flat `${FM_GUARD_GRACE:-300}` defaults. Guard, arm, turn-end guards and their agy/cursor wrappers, supervision host and handoff, inbox, away-return, and the shared auto-arm/supervision predicates all derive the same `max(300, FM_POLL + 60)` value, load `config/watch.env` then `config/x-mode.env`, and still honor an explicit `FM_GUARD_GRACE`; direct `bin/fm-watch.sh` launches now load home settings too.
- `fm_nm_bounded` runs each no-mistakes query in its own process group that traps HUP/INT/TERM and kills and reaps that group, so a stop reaches a display sweep's child queries while a query's own timeout stays query-local. Added `tests/fm-watch-beacon-progress.test.sh` and `tests/fm-nm-bounded-owned.test.sh`, with duration hints, and documented the beacon, grace, and progress contracts in `docs/turnend-guard.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/watcher-continuity.md`, and the operational home layout skill.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: No new actionable defects were found, but cross-process progress reporting and process-group cancellation retain concurrency and portability risk.

## Testing

Live-validated the beacon-progress fix end to end from the gate worktree against disposable lab homes: a real watcher running a check sweep longer than its grace kept the beacon age at 3s against a 4s grace inside a cycle whose cycle marker never changed, the real guard printed no watcher-down banner, and a real arm attached to it ('watcher: attached pid=...'). Adversarially, SIGSTOP on the watcher while its check child kept working (done-lines 4 to 5) let the beacon age to 7s and produced the WATCHER DOWN banner, and after SIGCONT the beacon refreshed again; a 320s-old beacon on a home with FM_POLL=300 read healthy via the derived max(300, poll+60) grace while the same beacon with explicit FM_GUARD_GRACE=300 alarmed, proving the pre-fix flat default would have fired. The repository's real-process suite (tests/fm-watch-beacon-progress.test.sh) passed all 19 assertions including the descendant-inertness, signal-scan, display-sweep freeze, and stalled-holder eviction cases. No UI surface was involved, so no screenshots were possible or needed; evidence is CLI transcripts and logs. Working tree left clean and all lab homes, watchers, and helper processes were torn down.

Branch: `fix/watcher-beacon-progress` (target `6129fae8`, base `68918448`).
All runs below were executed from the gate worktree against disposable lab
homes (`bin/fm-lab-home.sh create`, removed in the same run) or the repository's

store was touched.

## Scenario 1 + 2: a working long cycle stays fresh, raises no banner, accepts a successor

`manual-live-run.log`, `manual-live-evidence/m1-*.out`, `midcycle-proof.log`

- Lab home, three registered checks that each `sleep 2.5`, `FM_GUARD_GRACE=4`,
  `FM_POLL=1`, real `bin/fm-watch.sh` on that home.
- Over the observation window the beacon age never exceeded 3s against a 4s
  grace (`max_beacon_age_over_14s=3s`), and during one *unfinished* cycle
  (`cycle_changes=0` for the whole 9s sample, four 3s checks = a >=13s cycle)
  the beacon advanced 2 times mid-cycle with age staying <=3s

  touch would have aged with the cycle and passed the 4s grace.

- Real `bin/fm-watch-arm.sh` attached to the working watcher instead of

title: Lint partitions run at the 30-minute normal-tier bound
body:
The two `Lint` partitions in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` now take most of their 30-minute normal-tier bound on healthy runs, and many runs reach it.
A cancelled `Lint` job turns the `Full suite` verdict red on a pull request whose code passes every other lane.

## Evidence

Healthy durations on `main` (successful CI runs, 2026-11-08 to 2026-11-12):

| Run | Head | Lint 1 | Lint 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| [43209319634](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/actions/runs/43209319634) | `a9ae3c0c` | 18 min | 25 min |
| [43177783470](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/actions/runs/43177783470) | `afc5b760` | 26 min | 25 min |
| [43148560146](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/actions/runs/43148560146) | `a02b0898` | 27 min | 25 min |
| [43048776651](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/actions/runs/43048776651) | `bb3b2d69` | 29 min | 27 min |
| [42515104354](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/actions/runs/42515104354) | `3e9c781d` | 29 min | 20 min |

All CI runs created since 2026-11-11 (60 runs, 49 finished `Lint` jobs):

- 24 passed, in 18 to 27 minutes.
- 13 were cancelled at exactly 30 minutes, across 9 branches.
- 8 were cancelled before 30 minutes, and 4 failed; I did not examine those 12.

Examples of 30-minute cancellations that made the `Full suite` verdict red:

- [43248501409](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/actions/runs/43248501409) (#8390): `Lint 1`.
- [43262703761](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/actions/runs/43262703761) and [43279750546](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/actions/runs/43279750546) (#7948): `Lint 1` on two consecutive heads; every behavior lane passed.
- [43248524396](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/actions/runs/43248524396): `Lint 2`.

In the cancelled jobs, every file that `fm-lint` finished reported `reason=ok`; the step ends with `The operation was canceled.`

## Why this is not a timeout change

`docs/fm-test-portable-shards.md` "Timeouts" sets the normal tier at 30 minutes as a hang tripwire with headroom, and says a lane that reaches its tier bound needs a distribution or runtime fix, not a larger timeout.
The lint lane now has almost no headroom on healthy `main` runs (up to 29 minutes), so ordinary runner variance reaches the bound.

## Possible fixes

- Add a third lint partition (`partition: [1, 2, 3]`; `--partition Nof3` already follows `strategy.job-total`), so each partition returns to well under the bound.
- Or find the files that dominate runtime from the `fm-lint-telemetry-*` artifacts and rebalance or speed them up.

Related: #8415 is a separate test (`fm-extension-binding`) that also reaches its own deadline on slower runners.

title: False "WATCHER DOWN" banner when the liveness beacon mtime is slightly ahead of the clock (negative age fails the digit test)
body:
## Summary

`bin/fm-guard.sh` prints the full "WATCHER DOWN - SUPERVISION IS OFF" banner while the watcher is healthy, whenever the liveness beacon's mtime is one or two seconds **ahead** of the clock read taken by the guard. The banner's own text shows it: `last beat: -2s ago, grace 300s`.

## Root cause

`fm_watcher_supervision_verdict` in `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh` decides freshness with:

```bash
age=$(fm_path_age "$beat")
case "$age" in
  ''|*[!0-9]*) ;;
  *) [ "$age" -lt "$grace" ] && fresh=true ;;
esac
```

`fm_path_age` returns `now - mtime`. When the beacon is stamped slightly in the future the result is negative (`-1`, `-2`). The pattern `*[!0-9]*` matches the minus sign, so a negative age is treated as "not a number" and `fresh` stays `false`. In the autoarm model that skips the healthy branch unless `fm_autoarm_midturn_healthy` proves a generation, so the guard reports `no watcher has a fresh beacon (last beat: -2s ago, grace 300s)`.

The beacon is touched by a different process than the one reading it, and mtime granularity or rounding can put it a second ahead of the clock read taken a moment later. The exact source of the skew was not established here (WSL2, state directory on a Windows-backed path).

## Evidence

On a Claude primary with the supervision host on and 9 to 11 tasks in flight (firstmate at `90da2e55`), the banner appeared at least eight times in one session. Every time the beat read `-1s`, `-2s` or `0s`; wakes kept arriving normally and no repair was needed.

## Suggested fix

Clamp a negative age to zero before the digit test, for example `[ "$age" -lt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && age=0`. Add a guard fixture test with a beacon mtime of `now + 2` that must not print the banner.

## Related

The same sessions also show the empty `check: rearm-resurface` wake after nearly every turn end, already reported in #7761. The related report #8374 ("Is supervision live" has eight predicates and two grace rules) covers the predicate sprawl this check lives in.

Drafted with Claude Code.

title: ci: pack every job to ~15 min from measured timings, warn at 20 min, faster lint
body:
Speaking as Kun's firstmate: this is the CI time-cap change the captain asked for (FM-FMOSS-CI-TIMECAP-SHIP).

Closes #8417

## What changed
- **Shards packed from measured timings.** `tests/fm-test-ci-timings.tsv` holds the slowest successful per-script duration from recent green main runs. Refreshing it is a separate follow-up, not part of this PR. The serial lane now bin-packs to about 15 minutes per job, in 19 serial shards.
- **Oversized test files split.** `fm-watch-triage` is split into `fm-watch-triage-busy`, and `fm-captain-hold-lifecycle` into `fm-captain-hold-teardown`. Moved tests are byte-identical apart from scaffolding, and each test still runs exactly once.
- **Fewer fixed waits in remote-secondmate e2e.** Two fixed sleeps there became bounded polls. The deliberate negative `sleep 3` stays.
- **20-minute budget guardrail.** `bin/fm-ci-budget-warn.sh` runs in the timing-aggregate job. It emits a `CI budget` warning annotation when a job's measured command time (test or lint command run time, not runner setup or checkout) reaches 20 minutes, and it never fails a job. It only sees lanes that uploaded timing data, so a lane cancelled at the 30-minute cap shows up as a failed job instead of a warning.
- **Faster Lint.**
  - PRs lint only changed files.
  - A PR switches to the full canonical lint when it touches a lint definition, or a file that another script sources.
  - Pushes to main still run the full lint across 4 partitions.
  - ShellCheck and actionlint are cached, keyed on a hash of their installer scripts. A cache miss still downloads and checks the SHA-256.

## Unchanged
- Every `timeout-minutes` value. The 30-minute per-job limit stays.
- Every `runs-on` label. #8382's Ubuntu 26.04 move is handled separately.
- `fetch-depth: 0` on the test, herdr and hc jobs.
- No auto-retry, no `continue-on-error` on real jobs, and no new secrets or network access.

## Modeled job times
| Job | Modeled |
|---|---|
| Serial 1 | 15.67 min (`fm-remote-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e`, one sequential lifecycle that can't be split) |
| Serial 2 | 15.00 min (rest of `fm-watch-triage`) |
| Serial 3–19 | 14.71 min each |
| Parallel 1 and 2 | 10.36 min packed each |

## Verification
- Coverage check passes: `total=342 serial_shards=19 serial_unhinted=0`.
- These pass locally:
  - `tests/fm-ci-workflow.test.sh`
  - `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh`
  - `tests/fm-lint.test.sh`
  - Workflow lint with actionlint 1.7.12
  - All split and changed test files
- Four rounds of adversarial review; the final round returned no findings.

This edits `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so the captain merges it himself.

title: fix(bin): keep cloned projects' Claude instructions out of secondmates
body:
## Intent Speaking as mikeastwoody's firstmate: raised as a pull request rather than an issue after a reproduced, high-confidence analysis. Problem: a firstmate home keeps its project clones under `projects/` inside the supervisor's session root. Claude Code treats a read of a single file inside the session root (the Read tool, or a Bash `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed -n` or `grep `) as a trigger to load, once per file, every `CLAUDE.md` between the root and that file with its `@imports`, the `.claude/rules/*.md` there that have no `paths:` or whose `paths:` match, and user rules whose `paths:` match. They arrive as `` instruction text, so a supervisor that never writes to projects pays for another project's instructions on a plain read (about 124 KB from a single read in a real home) and receives instructions written for a different role. Change: keep cloned projects' Claude instruction files out of the supervisor where firstmate owns the settings file, and document the same protection for the primary, which the operator launches. Claude Code's `claudeMdExcludes` matches absolute paths with picomatch and resolves no relative path, `./`, `~` or variable, and a bare `**/projects/**` also excludes the home's own `CLAUDE.md` when the home itself lives under a directory named `projects`; so the patterns are absolute and anchored to the physical path of that home's own projects directory: `/projects/**/CLAUDE*.md`, `/projects/**/AGENTS.md` and `/projects/**/.claude/rules/**`. Secondmate Claude sessions get them in the settings file firstmate already passes with `--settings`. Workers are unchanged, because they need their project's instructions, and the operator's `.claude/settings.local.json` is never written. `docs/configuration.md` and the Claude harness reference document the snippet and its caveats for the primary. ## What Changed - A Claude secondmate's `--settings` file now carries `claudeMdExcludes` patterns. The patterns are anchored to the physical path of the home's own `projects/` directory: `/projects/**/CLAUDE*.md`, `**/AGENTS.md` and `**/.claude/rules/**`. They come from the new `bin/fm-claude-project-memory-lib.sh`. If the home's path holds a control character or a picomatch metacharacter, `bin/fm-spawn.sh` writes no patterns and warns at launch. The `feedbackDrafts`, attribution and hook keys are unchanged, and crewmates and scouts get no exclusion. - `docs/configuration.md` gains a "Claude and cloned projects' instructions" section. It gives the primary's `.claude/settings.local.json` snippet and its caveats: absolute physical paths only, never a bare `**/projects/**`, and never in tracked or user settings. The section also lists the cases that get no exclusion: T3 Code, raw launch commands and pattern-unsafe paths. The Claude harness reference, `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md` and `docs/t3code-backend.md` now record when Claude Code loads nested project memory and how `claudeMdExcludes` matches. - Hermetic tests in `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh` cover the patterns, `keep-ai-trailers` and the skip for a pattern-unsafe path. A new opt-in live guard, `tests/fm-claude-project-memory-live.test.sh`, runs the installed `claude` against a scripted local server (`tests/fixtures/fm-claude-read-replay.py`) and uses no tokens. It checks that one Read inside a clone loads that clone's instructions without the patterns, loads none with them, and that the home's own `CLAUDE.md` still loads. `bin/fm-test-run.sh` and the CI timings register the guard. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change adds one additive settings key only to the secondmate's firstmate-owned --settings file. It anchors the patterns to the mate home's physical projects path and refuses to write any path holding picomatch or control characters. Crewmates and the operator's settings.local.json stay untouched, as the intent requires. The earlier review's subshell and documentation fixes are in place, and the tests check observable output against an independent, spelled-out oracle and the real Claude binary. ## Testing I covered five scenarios. All six real-claude runs were live: the branch's live guard (two arms), the secondmate path in which real fm-spawn output was fed to real claude (baseline against generated settings), and the primary snippet arms (none, documented snippet, bare `**/projects/**`). Every arm behaved as the intent requires. I also drove fm-spawn on a pattern-character home path. The crewmate case and the new secondmate spawn cases passed as targeted hermetic tests. I stopped the remainder of fm-secondmate-harness, which is broad regression left to CI, after its three relevant cases passed. Labs were removed; the worktree is clean. title: feat(bin): select the Forgejo CLI from the registry forge binding
body:
## Intent

Revise the open pull request https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8454 and report whether it meets the repository's CONTRIBUTING.md.

That pull request lets a project's registry binding name its Forgejo CLI - `forge=forgejo:tea|fgj|fj` - and routes arming, the merge watch, the merge itself, teardown's merged proof and the terminal read through one resolver in `bin/fm-pr-lib.sh`; `fj` is refused by name for watch and merge because it has no request passthrough.

It has been through two review rounds and stands at 22 commits, head `2700df59`.

Both halves are wanted. Revise whatever the review still requires, and give a verdict on compliance: CONTRIBUTING.md requires a contribution targeting `main` to be raised through no-mistakes (v1.46.0 or newer) with a deterministic signature and a parseable structured attestation bound to the current head that reports the review, test and document steps as completed.

As of 2026-11-21 GitHub reports no checks at all on that pull request, so the required "PR must be raised via no-mistakes" workflow has never reported for its head; one Greptile P2 about an unpinned login reader was answered by the author as addressed.

Do not open a second pull request, do not comment on the existing one, and do not merge anything.

## What Changed

- A Forgejo project's registry binding may now name its CLI (`forge=forgejo:tea|fgj|fj`), read back with the new `bin/fm-project-mode.sh --forge-cli`; a bare `forge=forgejo` means `auto`, which resolves to `tea` and only `tea`, so an unnamed project never adopts another CLI's stored login, and a binding the parser refuses fails closed instead of falling back.
- `bin/fm-pr-lib.sh` gains the single resolver (`fm_pr_forgejo_resolve`, `fm_pr_forgejo_cli_login`, `fm_pr_forgejo_api`, `fm_pr_forgejo_cli_preference`), and arming, the merge watch (via the recorded preference in the poll sidecar and an optional seventh poll argument), the merge, the terminal read, teardown's merged proof, the ship brief and the Definition of done all read the pull request record and merge through it; tea's login list is matched as JSON, `fgj`'s host login is read from `fgj auth token --hostname` exit status, and `fj` is refused by name for watch and merge and by the brief because `forgejo-cli` has no authenticated request passthrough.
- Adds `docs/forgejo-cli-alternatives.md` recording the `fgj` and `fj` evidence and updates the Forgejo/architecture/configuration docs, with new security, merge, brief, project-mode and delivery tests covering CLI resolution, login predicates, `fj` refusals, malformed-binding fail-closed behavior, and the head-bound merge.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The resolver, sidecar-preference binding, arming/merge refusals and the head-bound fgj merge call all trace correctly with no wrong-value or credential-exposure path found, leaving only stale header/refusal-text corrections plus the attestation this run's later push and CI steps must produce.

## Testing

Exercised the whole Forgejo CLI-selection change through the real product: registry query and validation, arming and the armed merge watcher, the terminal/teardown read, generated ship briefs, and every refusal, using the machine's real tea and fj logins against a real codefloe.com Forgejo instance in a disposable lab home (read-only, nothing merged or commented). All driven scenarios passed, including the adversarial ones (fj refused by name at both arming and merge with a real authenticated fj, an fgj-registered project refusing rather than falling back to the logged-in tea, a malformed binding failing closed at both entry points, and auto never producing an fgj/fj-derived record). Two scenarios could not be driven live: a successful fgj-backed read/merge (fgj holds no login here and logging in would mutate credentials) and any real head-bound merge (the intent forbids merging). Evidence is five command transcript logs from those live runs; no visual/UI surface exists for this CLI change.

title: feat(bin): choose a codex account per ship or scout from a declared list
body:
## Intent

Add automatic switching between several Codex (ChatGPT) accounts for Codex workers, the same way firstmate already switches between several Claude accounts.

Context: firstmate merged a declared Claude account list in https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8121 ("choose a Claude account per ship or scout from a declared list", config/claude-accounts): each Claude ship or scout is dispatched on one declared account, each account is measured separately for quota, and the one with headroom is chosen at intake. Codex has no equivalent. A Codex login lives in the folder CODEX_HOME points at (default ~/.codex), and quota-axi reads CODEX_HOME when set, but firstmate cannot declare several Codex homes, measure each, or launch a Codex worker on a chosen one. So a user with a work and a personal ChatGPT plan cannot have Codex workers use whichever account has room; once one plan is exhausted, Codex either stops or bills overage.

Earlier upstream attempts, all stale (open about two months, two with merge conflicts, none merged): https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/3735 (per-profile Codex account dispatch), https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/4024 (route Codex dispatch across account homes), https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/4682 (forward firstmate's CODEX_HOME onto codex worker launches), and proposal issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/4379 (multiple accounts per provider in quota-aware dispatch).

Done when: a home can declare several Codex homes; each declared account's Codex quota is measured separately; Codex dispatch chooses an account by the same quota gates and ranking rules as the Claude account list; a Codex worker launches on the chosen account's CODEX_HOME and the task record shows which account it used; a relaunch keeps the recorded account; a home with no declaration behaves exactly as today; docs and tests cover it like the Claude feature.

Follow-up (2026-11-25): PR https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8457 now has merge conflicts with upstream main. Rebase it onto current main, resolve the conflicts, re-validate, and update the same PR so it can merge.

## What Changed

- A home can now declare several Codex homes in `config/codex-accounts`, one per line: `ordinary` (the default `~/.codex`) or the absolute path of a Codex home. When the list exists, every Codex ship or scout spawn must name a declared entry with `--account`. Before launch, the entry is checked with `codex login status`, and a signed-out entry is refused. The worker then launches with `CODEX_HOME` set to that home, or unset for `ordinary`, and `CODEX_API_KEY` and `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` are removed from its environment. The task record gets `account=<entry>`, and a relaunch keeps that account unless `--account` moves it. Without the list, every Codex launch is unchanged and `--account` is refused. Codex secondmates never read the list (`bin/fm-worker-account-lib.sh`, `bin/fm-spawn.sh`, `bin/fm-control.sh`).
- New `bin/fm-codex-account-quota.sh` checks each declared entry's quota on its own by running `quota-axi --provider codex --profile-only` with that entry's `CODEX_HOME`. The quota read, its output rows and its exit codes now live in a shared `bin/fm-account-quota-lib.sh`, which `bin/fm-claude-account-quota.sh` also uses. Each read's time limit is `FM_ACCOUNT_QUOTA_SECONDS`, and Claude still honors the old `FM_CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_QUOTA_SECONDS`. The `quota-array-dispatch` skill now picks Codex accounts with the same gates and ranking as Claude accounts.
- Docs cover the feature in a new "Several Codex accounts" section in `docs/configuration.md`, plus updates to AGENTS.md, the skills and the runtime-backends verification notes. New tests: `tests/fm-codex-account-quota.test.sh`, and Codex cases in the worker-account, relaunch, live-e2e and Claude quota tests.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Prior work

This follows the pattern of #8121 (the declared Claude account list): the same file format, required `--account`, sign-in refusal, `account=` record, relaunch reuse, and data-only per-account quota rows, now keyed by runner instead of duplicated.
It credits the earlier Codex attempts #3735 (per-profile Codex account dispatch), #4024 (route Codex dispatch across account homes), #4682 (forward firstmate's `CODEX_HOME` onto Codex worker launches), and the proposal in #4379 (multiple accounts per provider in quota-aware dispatch).
Unlike those, it does not tie accounts to dispatch profiles or forward firstmate's own `CODEX_HOME`: a home declares its Codex homes once, Firstmate measures each and picks one per ship or scout at intake, and a home with no list launches Codex exactly as before.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The Codex account list uses the same select, check, record and relaunch path as the Claude list. A home without config/codex-accounts returns early and launches exactly as before. Both recorded CI decisions (Codex secondmates never read the list, and the old Claude quota timeout is still honored) are in place, and behavior tests cover spawn, relaunch, refusals and quota reads.

## Testing

I ran four targeted suites. The live sign-in guard, the Codex quota suite and the worker-account suite all passed. The control-relaunch suite was stopped by the 10-minute background limit after 65 of about 100 cases, with no failures and every account case passing, so its remaining cases are unverified locally and CI covers them. I also drove a real Codex scout in a disposable lab home on a private tmux socket. Each declared home was measured on its own. The worker launched on the chosen CODEX_HOME, and Codex itself used that home's stored key (its 401 error shows the masked key `sk-fm-la…onal`). The account is recorded and kept across relaunch, the bad choices are refused before any launch, and a home with no list behaves as before. The lab was torn down afterwards. There is no UI change, so there are no screenshots; terminal transcripts and pane captures are the evidence.

## Intent Publish the three supervision fixes that this home already carries locally as commit ab904a55, to firstmate's upstream, with the captain's one-task consent recorded on this brief. The three fixes: (1) name GitLab and Forgejo beside GitHub wherever prose pointed task merges at bin/fm-pr-merge.sh as if it were GitHub-only, so GitLab merge requests are not hand-merged around the tool's recording and red-pipeline guards; (2) bin/fm-control.sh relaunch refuses --model without --harness before anything stops, and prints the fm-spawn recovery command when a secondmate's replacement fails to launch; (3) a new bin/fm-ask-freshness.sh refuses an over-age triage row before a captain ask is presented, with a pointer line in AGENTS.md section 7. Option (a): bring the PR branch up to date with current origin/main by merging it in (keeping history), resolve the one conflict in bin/fm-test-run.sh by keeping main's timing table (now tests/fm-test-ci-timings.tsv) and adding back only the PR's line tests/fm-ask-freshness.test.sh 1000, and push through a new no-mistakes run. Nothing else changes. ## What Changed - Adds `bin/fm-ask-freshness.sh`, which reads every markdown table in a triage report and checks each row's timestamp column (`--column`, default `checked_at`) against `--max-age` (default `2h`; seconds or `` parts such as `1h30m`). It prints each row with its age. It exits 0 when every row is within the limit. It exits 1 when any row is over-age or has an unreadable timestamp, and names those rows on stderr. It exits 2 on usage or input errors: no table, no body row, or a table without the timestamp column. Fenced code blocks are skipped using CommonMark's opening-fence rules, so inline code that starts with backticks does not hide later tables. - Adds `tests/fm-ask-freshness.test.sh` covering the gate, and adds its line (`tests/fm-ask-freshness.test.sh 1000`) to `tests/fm-test-ci-timings.tsv`. `docs/fm-test-portable-shards.md` explains that the 1000 ms is a provisional local measurement until CI refreshes it. - Adds a sentence to AGENTS.md section 7 requiring a captain ask taken from a triage list to pass through the gate first, so an over-age row is re-checked instead of presented. Also adds a row for the script to the table in `docs/scripts.md`. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The code is a well-bounded, standalone, fail-closed gate with behavioural tests, and the merge resolution is correct, but the branch carries only fix 3 of the three fixes the intent says to publish, so a human needs to confirm the scope. ## Testing I drove the real fm-ask-freshness.sh CLI against throwaway Markdown triage reports with a pinned clock. title: T3 Code backend: Claude primary loses worker-report wakes with no T3-native retry path
body:
Claude primary in a T3 Code 0.1.9 thread, `config/backend=t3code`, supervision host on (default), main `427056c4` plus the #8235 change.

T3 releases a provider session after 30 idle minutes unless a turn or tracked background work is live (pingdotgg/t3code#15235; `ProviderSessionManager.ts` in 0.1.9). The Stop hook's parked `asyncRewake` is neither.

Seen on 2026-11-14, Mac awake: the watcher beacon stopped with no line in `state/.watch-cycle-exits.log`, worker reports woke nobody, and the next session start printed "watcher still down". The timing fits the idle stop; the termination itself was not captured.

`docs/supervision-host.md` says automatic retries reach Claude only through a tmux or herdr pane, and `/afk` refuses the away daemon on a host home, so nothing covers this setup.

Workaround: a T3 scheduled task bound to the primary's thread, switched on by a private Stop hook while workers run, plus a T3-tracked background wait while workers run.

Ask: a t3code doorbell for the retry owner (`t3_thread_send` into the primary's thread, as the away daemon already does), started outside the provider process so the idle stop cannot end it.

Related: #4479, #2662.

title: fix(supervision-host): count refused engine commands as engine errors
body:
## Summary When Claude Code refuses the supervision engine's commands, the engine records no outcome and the host hands every wake back to main without saying why. This PR makes that failure visible: a turn whose commands were refused and that recorded no outcome now counts as an engine error, trips the existing broken-session latch, and hands back with a line saying the commands were refused. Fixes #8514 ## Root cause The earlier root-cause comment on #8514 was mistaken: `--safe-mode` is not what drops the engine's allow rules. On the affected machine, the organization-managed setting `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly: true` drops every non-managed allow rule (`--allowedTools`, `--settings`, user and project rules) with or without `--safe-mode`. Only managed allow rules and commands Claude classifies as read-only run. Replacing `--safe-mode` would change nothing, so the engine's launch flags are unchanged. The measurements are recorded in `docs/verification/supervision.md` under "Refused engine commands, 2026-11-15". ## Changes - `bin/fm-supervision-engine-lib.sh`: the engine result line reports `denied=`, the number of entries in the `permission_denials` array (0 when the field is absent or not an array). - `bin/fm-supervision-host.sh`: a turn with `denied > 0` and no recorded report is an engine error that feeds the latch, with the hand-back reason "the engine's commands were refused by its permission rules (N refused)". A turn that reported and acknowledged its wake stays handled, and its ledger line records the count. - `bin/fm-afk-return.sh`: the away return brief counts these turns as engine errors, matching the latch. - `docs/supervision-host.md` and `docs/verification/supervision.md`: updated hand-back and latch rules, plus the dated measurements. ## Testing - Stub-engine tests through the real host and away-return scripts, in throwaway homes: a non-array `permission_denials` counts as 0 refusals; refused no-report turns hand back with the refused-commands line, record `denied=1`, and the second trips the latch with a 300-second cooldown; a handled turn with one refused call stays handled with no error or latch; the return brief counts refused no-report turns as engine errors. - An earlier round drove the real host with the Claude Code 2.1.325 engine in disposable lab homes: refused wakes hand back naming the refusal, two in a row trip the latch once, and the base commit hands the same wakes back silently. ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

title: fix(bin): ring the steer doorbell past a pending composer draft on tmux and paseo
body:
## Intent Fix a stray character in a target pane's composer silencing the steer doorbell on tmux and paseo: the ring now clears the pending draft, rings, and retypes the draft only when it round-trips exactly, so steers are no longer left unread. ## What Changed - `fm_task_inbox_ring` (`bin/fm-task-inbox-lib.sh`) now wraps the old ring logic, which is renamed `fm_task_inbox_ring_core`. Before, other pending text in the composer made the ring defer. Now, on tmux and paseo, the ring captures the draft, clears the composer, rings the doorbell, clears any doorbell text left behind, and types the draft back unsubmitted. Clearing uses `C-e`, then a bounded number of `C-u` presses, then `BSpace` as a fallback. The ring still defers as before in these cases: - any other backend - the composer already holds this record's own doorbell - the draft can't be round-tripped exactly (it doesn't fit on one visible row, isn't shown verbatim on its row, or starts with `-`) - the clear fails - The ring sets a new `FM_TASK_INBOX_RING_NOTE`, which `fm-send.sh` prints to stderr. The note says whether the draft was left in place, partly cleared, typed back, or lost, and never includes the draft text. - Supporting changes: - New `fm_backend_send_literal` dispatcher (tmux and paseo only). - `fm_composer_extract_selected_content` now records which screen rows it read in `FM_COMPOSER_EXTRACT_ROWS`. - The tmux literal send now sends a trailing `;` as `\;`, so tmux no longer drops it. - `tests/fm-task-inbox.test.sh` gains tests covering the new ring behaviour. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The draft rescue runs only on tmux and paseo; every other backend defers before any key is sent, as before. A draft is cleared only when it reads as one visible, unnormalized row that does not start with a dash. Leftover doorbell text is cleared before the draft is typed back, and the notes are honest about the trailing-space limit. The tmux trailing-';' escape matches how tmux parses arguments (with a trailing '\;' tmux keeps the ';'), which also fixes the fm-spawn launch-command caller. ## Testing I drove four scenarios live against a real Claude Code worker in a disposable lab tmux server, using the real fm-send.sh. On the change: a one-row draft 'x' and a draft 'foo;' were each cleared, the doorbell rang, the worker did the steer (it created the file and moved the record to handled/), and the exact draft came back unsubmitted, with the 'typed back' note printed. A wrapped two-row draft was left untouched and the ring deferred with the 'cannot be restored exactly' note. On the base commit, a lone 'x' made fm-send skip the doorbell, which is the original bug. The targeted tests/fm-task-inbox.test.sh passed, including the stub check that non-tmux/paseo backends defer with no key sent; that path was not driven live, so it is recorded as untested. Paseo could not be driven live because its CLI is not installed. I saved pane captures and fm-send transcripts as evidence and tore the lab down. title: Calm mod fails claude plugin validate --strict on Claude Code 2.1.326
body:
## Behavior

On Claude Code 2.1.326, `tests/fm-calm-claude-mod-plugin.test.sh` fails on `main` (427056c4):

```
not ok - Claude Code 2.1.326 (Claude Code) refused the Calm mod at …/.claude/mods/firstmate-calm under strict validation
```

`claude plugin validate --strict` on `.claude/mods/firstmate-calm` now reports:

- TS5097 ("An import path can only end with a '.ts' extension…") on `hooks/register.ts:47,55,66,78` and on the `lib/` imports.
- Type drift in the mod's own tests: `Spinner` props now require `suffix`, `UserMessage` requires `isExpanded`, the `fs.stat` hook signature changed, and the `cells` union changed.

Without `--strict` the result is `Validation passed with warnings` (exit 0), so Calm still loads. Only the strict gate fails.

CI does not catch it because the test is live-gated on an installed `claude` binary, and the Ubuntu CI jobs have none, so it skips there. Anyone running the suite locally with Claude Code ≥ 2.1.326 sees it red.

## Ask

Update the Calm mod for Claude Code 2.1.326's validator, so `claude plugin validate --strict` passes again. One option is to make the `.ts` import paths acceptable to the validator (or adjust the mod's tsconfig to allow them), then update the test-only types to the new component and hook signatures.

## Feasibility

The fix is confined to `.claude/mods/firstmate-calm` (the import specifiers plus the mod's test types). Runtime behavior is unchanged, since the mod already loads.

title: fix(bin): read pending-reply record fields without starting processes
body:
Refs #8550 (part 3 of 4) ## Intent A Mac running firstmate continuously needs a restart about every two weeks: the macOS pid-version counter overflows 15 to 17 days after boot, and firstmate scripts start about 87% of all processes on that host. Upstream issue: https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8550 (labelled ready-for-pr on 2026-11-17). Maintainer triage (https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8550#issuecomment-6958332963): take sources 3 and 4 as separate focused PRs. A change that keeps identical behavior and only starts fewer processes needs no opt-in; its contract class is restore-equivalent. Changing a default cadence is new-default and is out of scope. Include before/after per-hour process counts and portable (bash 3.2 and Linux) behavior coverage. A performance change must not change what supervision does. This PR is source 3: `fm_pending_reply_get` in bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh (l.233-237) is `grep | tail -1 | cut` wrapped by callers in `$(...)`, a subshell and three external processes per field read, used about 94 times in that lib plus bin/fm-backlog-handoff.sh and bin/fm-teardown.sh. It starts about 3% of all processes on the measured host. ## What Changed - `fm_pending_reply_get` in `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh` now reads the record with an in-shell `while read` loop instead of `grep | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2-`, which started three external processes per field read. The name, the arguments and the results stay the same: the last line for the key wins, a missing key, missing file or unreadable file prints nothing, and values keep `=`, spaces, a trailing CR and an unterminated final line. No caller and no polling interval changes. - One result differs: under a UTF-8 locale GNU grep dropped a matching line that holds invalid UTF-8, so that read came back empty. The loop returns the bytes, as the old pipeline did under the C locale. - `tests/fm-fork-free-helpers.test.sh` adds `test_pending_reply_get_matches_the_grep_pipeline`. It compares the helper byte for byte against the replaced pipeline (run under `LC_ALL=C`) across 12 record shapes plus a missing file, through the file's existing `run_everywhere` runner. The commit message records the measured process starts on Linux (strace over 20 `fm_pending_reply_tick` calls): 623 per tick before and 407 after, about 149,400 and 97,600 per hour at a 15 second poll. ## Related https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/7203 makes a near-identical swap of `fm_pending_reply_get` inside a broader watcher-beacon change (open, conflicting with main). This PR is the focused part-3 change the issue 8550 triage asked for, and whichever lands second takes a one-function conflict. https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8208 changes a different function in the same lib and does not conflict. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: One function swaps a three-process pipeline for an in-shell loop that mirrors the loop fm_pending_reply_set already uses, every caller passes a literal identifier key so regex and literal matching agree, and the only behavior difference is a disclosed invalid-UTF-8 display case on Linux. ## Testing I ran the two test files from the verification plan (tests/fm-fork-free-helpers.test.sh on bash 5.3 and again with a locally built bash 3.2.57 as an extra interpreter, and tests/fm-pending-reply.test.sh), all passing. I then compared the base-commit function against the new one over 48 field reads on 12 record shapes under both bash versions and three locales with zero differences, counted process starts with strace -f over 20 real fm_pending_reply_tick calls before and after on one shared fixture (19,920 down to 11,280, with identical written state), and ran the caller tests tests/fm-backlog-handoff.test.sh and tests/fm-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh, both passing. tests/fm-teardown.test.sh hit my own 480 second cap while running in parallel (62 cases passed, none failed) so I do not count it; the teardown caller is covered by the lifecycle end-to-end test instead. No UI surface exists, so there is no visual evidence. - Live validation: ✅ go - 5 of 6 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A script reads a field from a pending-reply record and gets the same bytes as the old grep \| tail -1 \| cut pipeline (last line wins, '=' in values, CR, unterminated last line, near-miss keys, blank li… | ✅ pass | live | old-vs-new-differential.log: 48 reads, differences=0 for bash 5.3.9 under C, C.utf8 and en_US.utf8; fork-free-helpers-bash5.log shows the new equivalence case ok | | The same field reads behave identically on bash 3.2 (the stock macOS shell version), using a GNU bash 3.2.57 built locally on Linux | ✅ pass | live | old-vs-new-differential.log: differences=0 for bash 3.2.57 under C, C.utf8 and en_US.utf8; fork-free-helpers-bash32.log: 8 ok with bash 3.2.57 first on PATH | | The watcher tick (fm_pending_reply_tick) starts fewer processes after the change: no grep, tail or cut starts remain | ✅ pass | live | tick-process-counts.log: before 19,920 process-start syscalls over 20 ticks (1,440 each of grep, tail, cut); after 11,280 with zero grep, tail or cut. Per hour at 240 ticks: about 239,000 before, abou… | | A performance change must not change what supervision does: the tick writes identical state before and after, and pending-reply recovery, escalation and resolve behavior still passes | ✅ pass | live | tick-process-counts.log: 'IDENTICAL: 161 lines across 9 files', phases 2 awaiting_report and 3 resolved; tick-state-after.txt; pending-reply-test.log exit=0 | | The other callers still work: backlog handoff (bin/fm-backlog-handoff.sh) and secondmate teardown (bin/fm-teardown.sh) read task_id and delivered_epoch from records correctly | ✅ pass | live | backlog-handoff-test.log: ALL TESTS PASSED, exit=0; secondmate-lifecycle-e2e-test.log: 6 ok, exit=0 | | The same reads on a real Mac with stock /bin/bash 3.2 and BSD userland | ⏸️ untested | no | This host is Linux and no macOS machine is reachable from the worktree. I substituted a locally built GNU bash 3.2.57, which covers the shell version but not macOS itself. Remote CI on a macOS runner,… |

- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 info across 1 run (21m37s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **Intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ℹ️ `bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:241` - The intent says the change "keeps identical behavior and only starts fewer processes". One read differs, and the commit message discloses it. On Linux under a UTF-8 locale, GNU grep suppressed a matching line that holds invalid UTF-8, so the old `grep "^${key}=" "$rec" | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2-` returned an empty value. The new loop (`case "$line" in "$key="*) value=${line#"$key="}`) returns the bytes. Reachable path: fm_pending_reply_summarize strips control characters only, so a request text with a stray byte such as 0xE9 is stored in request_summary. The readers at bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:962 and :1155 then show the summary where they showed nothing before. No phase, epoch, or task_id decision changes, because those values are ASCII. The Mac host in the intent is not affected by this locale rule of GNU grep. The new behavior equals the old pipeline under the C locale and looks like the correct one. Decision needed: accept this disclosed difference under the restore-equivalent contract, or require the loop to reproduce the empty read.

title: fix(bin): wait for the supervision arm to close without starting processes
body:
Refs #8550 (part 4 of 4) ## Intent A Mac running firstmate continuously needs a restart about every two weeks: the macOS pid-version counter overflows 15 to 17 days after boot, and firstmate scripts start about 87% of all processes on that host. Upstream issue: https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8550 (labelled ready-for-pr on 2026-11-17). Maintainer triage (https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8550#issuecomment-6958332963): take sources 3 and 4 as separate focused PRs. A change that keeps identical behavior and only starts fewer processes needs no opt-in; its contract class is restore-equivalent. Changing a default cadence is new-default and is out of scope. Include before/after per-hour process counts and portable (bash 3.2 and Linux) behavior coverage. A performance change must not change what supervision does. This PR is source 4: `await_close` in bin/fm-supervision-host.sh (around l.661) polls for the arm to close, starting processes on every poll. It starts under 2% of all processes on the measured host. ## What Changed - `await_close` in `bin/fm-supervision-host.sh` now stops refreshing the arm's recorded identity after the first refresh that succeeds once the arm has printed output. `refresh_process` returns 0 or 1 so the caller can tell, and a failed refresh still retries on every poll. - The half-second arm exit probe goes through a new `probe_interval`. On Bash 4.1 and later it is a `read -t 0.5` on a private FIFO that nothing writes, which starts no process. Bash 3.2, a FIFO that cannot be opened, or a read that returns early keeps the child `sleep 0.5`. The poll interval, the probe interval, and the readiness and boundary checks are unchanged. - `tests/fm-supervision-host.test.sh` replaces the child-sleep cadence test with one that shims the commands a parked host could start and asserts none run on Bash 4.1 and later (only `sleep 0.5` on Bash 3.2), and adds a test that a killed arm ends the wait and passes through. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change only replaces the child sleep with a builtin read timeout on Bash 4.1+ and stops the identity refresh once the arm has printed, and the traced paths (identity pinned to UTC and start time, no exec in fm-watch-arm.sh, early read return falls back to sleep, Bash 3.2 keeps the old sleep) keep supervision behavior unchanged; the one unproven point is that the three selected tests have never run under stock macOS Bash 3.2, which the CI step of this run will show. ## Testing I ran the three await_close behavior tests against the real host script on Linux under Bash 5.3 and under a Bash 3.2.57 that I built in a temp directory, and all passed. I then started the real host in a disposable fixture home under strace at the base commit and at the target commit, and counted the processes the parked host created in a 60-second window: 714 before and 0 after on Bash 5.3, 727 before and 118 after on Bash 3.2. The host's output and exit code for the same close were identical before and after. macOS was not available, so the macOS stock Bash lane stays with remote CI. No UI surface is involved, so there is no screenshot. - Live validation: ✅ go - 4 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Linux Bash 5.3: a host parked on a live arm (fixture home, stub arm) starts zero processes while waiting, where the base commit started about 42,800 per hour | ✅ pass | live | process-counts-before-after.txt: before-bash5.3 714 in 60 s, after-bash5.3 0 in 60 s (strace -f on the real bin/fm-supervision-host.sh park); test_parked_host_starts_no_process_once_its_arm_reported o… | | Bash 3.2 on Linux: the parked host falls back to half-second child sleeps only, dropping from about 43,600 to about 7,100 processes per hour | ✅ pass | live | process-counts-before-after.txt: before-bash3.2 727, after-bash3.2 118 (101 x sleep 0.5) in 60 s; linux-bash32-await-close-tests.log: 3 planned, 3 ok | | Supervision behavior unchanged: a needs-decision status close reaches main with the same output and exit code 0 before and after the change | ✅ pass | live | process-counts-before-after.txt: host exit codes 0 0 0 0 and normalised host.out identical between base and target on Bash 5.3 and 3.2; test_attended_main_only_close_passes_straight_to_main ok on both… | | Adversarial: an arm killed with SIGKILL without printing a close still ends the host's wait within 3 seconds and passes through with exit 0 | ✅ pass | live | test_arm_that_disappears_ends_the_wait ok in linux-bash5-await-close-tests.log and linux-bash32-await-close-tests.log | | macOS stock /bin/bash 3.2 lane: the await_close tests pass on a real Mac | ⏸️ untested | no | This host is Linux and no macOS machine or runner is reachable from the worktree. title: feat(bin): repeat presented completed results until handling acknowledgement behind config/result-replay
body:
Fixes #8549

## Relation to other pull requests

This PR lands first.
https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/2801 (open since 2026-08-25 and conflicting with main) would carry the new optional fifth receipt field in `status_commit_presentation_snapshot` when it rebases.
This change covers only the ordinary drain and does not touch PR 2801's wake-context packet path (`bin/fm-wake-context.sh`).
The open-decisions reader in https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8158 stays separate and is untouched.

## Intent

A completed status result (a `done:` line) disappears from later drains once one drain has printed it, even when its handling acknowledgement never ran. The queue row survives, but the result text does not, so an interrupted turn loses the completed result.
Upstream issue: https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8549 (labelled ready-for-pr by the maintainer on 2026-11-17).
Maintainer triage (https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8549#issuecomment-6958334279): confirmed on main 427056c4. `print_status_sections` in bin/fm-wake-drain.sh commits the presentation receipt (`status_commit_presentation_snapshot`, bin/fm-classify-lib.sh) as soon as the bytes reach stdout, independent of `--ack-through`. AGENTS.md says UNREAD STATUS lines are not re-printed after presentation, and also that interruption before acknowledgement leaves work durable for idempotent re-handling; the two promises disagree for completed results. Contract class: new-default, so update the AGENTS.md wording in the same PR; without a config gate it goes to the maintainer's captain before merge. Issue #5593 (no replay after an acknowledgement) must stay fixed. Coordinate with open PR #2801, which stages replay-safe status cursors for opt-in wake packets. Keep PR #8158 separate. Replay must be bounded and handled results must repeat silently.
Investigation report with the reproduction (substance): in an isolated fixture, create a status file containing `done: UNIQUE_COMPLETED_RESULT`, queue its ordinary status signal, run bin/fm-wake-drain.sh capturing stdout and stderr, do not run the printed `--ack-through` command, then run the drain again. The first output includes the completed result; the second output contains the same raw queue row but no completed-result text, because the presentation receipt already advanced both its annotation and backstop offsets to the end of the status file. Sending the first stdout to /dev/null gives the same loss. An empty-queue fixture prints the completion once through the outcome backstop, prints no handling acknowledgement command, and then stays silent. A filtered consumer that runs the printed acknowledgement without reading the result loses it entirely; a caller that deliberately sends the matching acknowledgement still asserts that it handled the result. The report proposes that the existing presentation receipt retain exact completed-result identities until their matching handling acknowledgement, without adding another queue, while ordinary note deduplication stays unchanged, with regression coverage for concurrent appends, status file replacement, separate reader ownership, bounded replay, and silent repeats of handled results.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh` and `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh` add the opt-in presence flag `config/result-replay`. With the flag, a main drain records each `done:` line it presents in the existing `.status-presentation-cursor` receipt (a new optional fifth field) and repeats it under a new `UNHANDLED RESULTS` section on every later drain. The repeat stops only when main runs the `WAKE_ACK_REQUIRED` acknowledgement for the same recovery generation that covers every wake row presented to main. A drain that holds a pending result with an empty queue prints that acknowledgement with `--ack-through 0`. Without the flag the drain keeps its one-shot presentation, and notes, decisions and other status lines stay one-shot in both modes.
- Replay is bounded: the receipt keeps each result's text cut to 219 characters and the four newest results per task, and a drain repeats at most 4000 bytes and names what it drops or omits. An omitted result stays pending through the acknowledgement. Supervision-branch drains neither add nor retire results, an acknowledgement from an earlier generation or a partial one retires nothing, and a replaced status file keeps its pending result. `.pi/extensions/lib/fm-branch-dispatch.ts` now accepts the five-field cursor row instead of treating it as malformed.
- `AGENTS.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/watcher-continuity.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/scripts.md` and the `operational-home-layout` skill describe the flag, the `UNHANDLED RESULTS` section, and that by default an interruption keeps the queued wake row but not the completed result's text. The new `tests/fm-wake-drain-result-replay.test.sh` holds 11 regression cases for the behaviours above, and `tests/fm-pi-branch-extension.test.sh` covers the five-field cursor row.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The fix round's retire condition (generation match and PRESENTED_MAX <= ACK_THROUGH) traces correctly through the full, partial, stale, empty-queue and branch-held acknowledgement paths, the new behavior stays behind the opt-in config/result-replay flag, and the reworded AGENTS.md and docs match the code.

## Testing

I drove the real bin/fm-wake-drain.sh in a disposable state and config fixture through the issue 8549 reproduction and its guards: interrupted turn, stdout sent to /dev/null, empty queue, matching acknowledgement, partial acknowledgement, wrong generation, bounded replay, notes, and the default home. Every scenario behaved as intended, and the four targeted test files (result replay, unread status, outcome backstop, Pi branch extension) exited 0. No visual evidence applies because the surface is CLI text. The fixture was removed and the worktree is clean.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 10 of 10 scenarios driven live against the product
