- ⚠️ `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:1118` - A partial acknowledgement retires results that belong to wake rows it did not acknowledge. The retire condition is `ACK_REMOVED > 0 || PRESENTED_MAX <= ACK_THROUGH`, and results are bound only to the recovery generation, which stays the same across drains until a full acknowledgement. Concrete sequence with config/result-replay on: drain 1 presents row 1 and prints `--ack-through 1 --recovery-generation G`; the turn is interrupted; row 2 arrives with a `done:` line; drain 2 presents rows 1 and 2 plus the new result (marked `s`) and prints `--ack-through 2 --recovery-generation G`; the caller runs the earlier command (`--ack-through 1`, generation G). ACK_REMOVED is 1 and the generation matches, so status_retire_shown_results drops the row 2 result. Row 2 stays queued, but its result text never repeats, which is the exact loss the intent describes ('The queue row survives, but the result text does not'). The existing code already treats an earlier acknowledgement replayed after a newer drain as a real caller sequence (the 'nothing was acknowledged through' branch below). Smallest fix: retire only when `PRESENTED_MAX <= ACK_THROUGH`, dropping the `ACK_REMOVED -gt 0` alternative, and add a regression case to tests/fm-wake-drain-result-replay.test.sh for this sequence. Not executed in this review (tests are a later phase); derived by tracing bin/fm-wake-drain.sh lines 1073-1122.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:2039` - The fix is opt-in behind `config/result-replay` (status_result_replay_enabled), so the reported failure still reproduces unchanged on a default home: commit message says 'The default drain is unchanged', and tests/fm-wake-drain-result-replay.test.sh asserts the second default drain omits the result. The intent states the failure as 'A completed status result ... disappears from later drains' and classifies the contract as 'new-default, so update the AGENTS.md wording in the same PR; without a config gate it goes to the maintainer's captain before merge'. The gate avoids the captain review, but it also means AGENTS.md keeps both disagreeing promises for default homes ('those lines are not re-printed after this presentation' and 'interruption before that acknowledgement deliberately leaves the work durable'). Decision needed: confirm that an opt-in gate is the intended delivery for issue 8549, or make replay the default (removing the gate and its off-path branches in status_commit_presentation_snapshot, print_unhandled_results_section, print_result_ack_required, and the ack path) and send it to the maintainer's captain. The gate is the only introduced component the intent does not strictly require; the per-task bound, byte cap, retained text, branch-reader preservation, and empty-queue acknowledgement each map to a stated requirement.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:2139` - The intent requires 'Coordinate with open PR #2801'. `gh pr diff 2801 --repo kunchenguid/firstmate` shows that PR rewrites status_commit_presentation_snapshot (adds a third `target` parameter and a staged cursor) and changes bin/fm-wake-drain.sh, AGENTS.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/configuration.md, all of which this change also edits. This change adds a fifth row field and new commit-time logic inside the same function, so the two will conflict textually and the staged-cursor path in PR 2801 would need to carry the pending-results field. Nothing in this branch records how the two were coordinated. Decide the merge order and say so in the pull request description.

title: fix(firstmate-calm): restore strict validation on Claude Code 2.1.326
body:
Fixes #8558

## Intent

Open the upstream PR for kunchenguid/firstmate#8558 (https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8558), which the maintainer confirmed and labelled ready-for-pr with contract class "restore": on Claude Code 2.1.326, `claude plugin validate --strict` refuses the Calm mod (`.claude/mods/firstmate-calm`): TS5097 on the `from "../lib/*.ts"` imports in hooks/register.ts (lines 47, 55, 66, 78) and the lib imports, plus test-only type drift (Spinner props need `suffix`, UserMessage needs `isExpanded`, the fs.stat hook signature, the `cells` union), so tests/fm-calm-claude-mod-plugin.test.sh fails. The maintainer's PR conditions: (1) keep the change inside .claude/mods/firstmate-calm, covering the import specifiers or the mod's tsconfig plus the test-only types; (2) confirm the mod still loads and validates on an earlier verified Claude Code version if one is available; (3) add a 2.1.326 verification row to docs/calm-mode-feasibility.md with the live test output. Runtime behavior must not change.

## What Changed
- Suppress TS5097 diagnostics on Calm mod `.ts` imports while preserving runtime import paths.
- Update test fixtures for required engine fields and the `ui.blit` cells union.
- Document Claude Code 2.1.326 strict-validation output and compatibility with 2.1.322 and 2.1.327.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is bounded to import diagnostic suppressions, engine-compatible test fixtures, and verification documentation, with no production runtime behavior changes.

## Testing

Reproduced the baseline refusal, passed targeted validation and engine-hosted plugin tests on 2.1.326 and 2.1.322, and verified real UI loading, toggles, and the activation boundary. Initial driver timing and rollout assumptions were corrected before successful re-execution. Evidence includes raw CLI logs and rendered terminal captures, not desktop screenshots; mocked plugin tests are supplementary rather than live UI proof. No model requests were submitted, and all disposable processes and files were cleaned up.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 3 of 3 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

title: feat: follow captain-named PRs with direct outcome lines
body:
## Intent Build the fix for firstmate issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8367 upstream: a PR state change the captain asked to hear about costs a model turn before it reaches the captain, and a PR with no task behind it cannot be followed at all. The issue asks that the captain can name a PR or merge request to follow, with or without a task; that a state change on a followed PR (merged, closed without merge, checks turned red, review requested changes) reaches the captain as one line with the forge's own words and the PR URL, written directly to the captain-facing surface with no model turn in between; that a task-owned PR that merges still runs the existing cleanup and backlog path; and that the model is still woken when the change needs a decision or an action. The maintainer labelled the issue ready-for-pr on 2026-11-11 (https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8367#issuecomment-6809587226 is the triage comment; re-read the whole thread first) with two conditions: a follow exists only because the captain asked for that PR and lives in a durable record so it survives a restart; and the direct line reads as an outcome on firstmate's own captain-facing surface, not as raw machinery. The maintainer also noted that PR 5341 (contribution monitor waking on PR movement) still goes through a model wake and covers only owned PRs, so it does not cover this. Build it opt-in from the first commit. The maintainer's triage on https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8598 classed it new-default (new-default-reason=always-loaded-skill-trigger): every runtime piece is already off without config/pr-follow, but the new pr-follow skill's description joins the always-loaded skill trigger index, so an unconfigured home's agent context changes. New-default PRs wait for the maintainer's own decision, while opt-in PRs merge automatically after a green full suite. Fixes `#8367` ## What Changed - Adds `bin/fm-pr-follow.sh` (`add --requested `, `remove`, `list`, `arm`, `poll`), gated by the opt-in `config/pr-follow` presence flag. It keeps captain-requested GitHub PR and GitLab MR follows in a durable `data/pr-follows.json`, with or without a task, and records the current forge state as a baseline at enrollment. `fm-bootstrap.sh` arms it as one ordinary check on the existing watcher, and `fm-pr-poll.sh --snapshot` supplies the forge reads. - A changed condition (merged, closed without merge, a newly failing check, review requested changes) is appended as a new idempotent `notice` verdict in `bin/fm-branch-outcome.sh`, with its own `notices` / `mark-notices` cursor separate from the model-facing read and processed cursors. The Pi supervision extension and the Claude Calm mod render each notice as one transcript line with the forge's words and the PR URL, with no model turn. Both publish a `state/.pr-follow-surface` heartbeat, and enrollment refuses (and existing follows pause) when no such surface is live. A non-merge change on a task-owned PR also queues a supervision wake, and task-owned merges stay on the existing cleanup and backlog path. - No always-loaded skill is added: `fm-session-start.sh` prints one pointer line to the new "Explicit PR follows" section of `docs/configuration.md` only while the flag exists. Adds `tests/fm-pr-follow.test.sh`, `tests/fm-pr-follow-live-e2e.test.sh`, Calm notice tests and a session-start opt-in test, plus entries in `docs/scripts.md`, `docs/calm.md`, the operational-home-layout skill and `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Every runtime path is gated on config/pr-follow, the ungated edits (the notice verdict in the outcome store, Calm and Pi parsers, startup-replay) behave identically when no notice row exists, and I found no reachable wrong result in the poll, receipt, or display paths; GitLab and pi-signed remain unexercised, as earlier declined findings already record. ## Testing I ran the live end-to-end test against real Pi and Claude Calm TUIs with screen captures, drove the follow CLI by hand through six scenarios in a disposable home, and ran the follow regression test, the session-start test, and the 56 native Calm plugin tests from a private copy; all passed. The secondmate pool test failed inside the gate worktree but passed from a plain archive of both the merge commit and upstream main. Strict Calm plugin validation failed with TS5097. Pi-signed and real GitLab were not exercised because those tools are absent, and I did not run the 17-minute teardown test. - Live validation: ✅ go - 11 of 13 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Captain follows a taskless PR on an idle real Pi TUI; merged, closed and red-check changes each appear as one line with forge words and URL, with no model turn or wake | ✅ pass | live | live-e2e-output.txt and live-screen-pi.txt: real pi 1.5.2 in tmux, fm-lock.sh without a .lock-session sidecar, substituted gh reads | | Captain follows a taskless PR on an idle real Claude Code TUI with the Calm mod; the same three changes appear as one line each with no model request | ✅ pass | live | live-e2e-output.txt (three '● fm: ⚓' lines, exit=0) and live-screen-claude.txt (capture taken after two of the three lines) | | Unconfigured home: add and arm refuse, poll does nothing and reads no forge; no follow skill is in the skill index | ✅ pass | live | manual-cli-transcript.txt section 1; live test asserts Pi's loaded project skills contain no pr-follow entry; tests/fm-session-start.test.sh shows no digest line without the flag | | Opted-in enrollment stores the PR and the captain's words durably, creates no task and no initial notice, and a later process reports the merge once | ✅ pass | live | manual-cli-transcript.txt sections 2-3: list shows URL and request, 0 meta files, 0 outcomes, then one MERGED notice after two polls | | Adversarial: a stale (120 s old) surface heartbeat refuses new enrollment, pauses polling with one message, and writes no outcome until the surface returns | ✅ pass | live | manual-cli-transcript.txt section 3; tests/fm-pr-follow.test.sh covers wrong owner, wrong Claude session and unsupported surface | | Notices stay out of the model-facing queue: unprocessed is empty and the wake queue is empty while the notices reader returns the line | ✅ pass | live | manual-cli-transcript.txt section 3 (wake queue 0 lines, unprocessed empty, notices returns seq 1) | | Red checks, requested changes and closed-without-merge each add exactly one line; a repeated poll adds none | ✅ pass | live | manual-cli-transcript.txt section 4 (seq 2-7, one line per change per followed URL) | | Task-owned PR: a red check queues a model wake naming the task; a merge leaves task custody and the existing merge observer untouched | ✅ pass | live | manual-cli-transcript.txt section 5: wake queue line 'followed PR needs action for ship', fm-pr-poll.sh --validated prints merged, ship.meta still present | | Opted-in home gets exactly one follow guidance line in the session-start digest | ✅ pass | live | bash tests/fm-session-start.test.sh exit 0, case 'follow instructions add exactly one digest line only while the home opts in' | | Calm replay keeps notice sequence positions without repeating ordinary outcomes | ✅ pass | live | claude plugin test on a private copy of the Calm mod: 56 pass, 0 fail across 3 files | | Pi-signed primary shows followed-PR lines | ⏸️ untested | no | The pi-signed CLI is not on PATH and has no repository-local path. Install pi-signed on this host to drive it. | | Real GitLab merge request follow through glab | ⏸️ untested | no | glab is not installed, so only the fixture-backed GitLab path in tests/fm-pr-follow.test.sh ran. Install glab with a GitLab login to drive it. A recorded decision already accepted this gap. | | Upstream secondmate pool spawning is unchanged by the merge | ✅ pass | live | tests/fm-spawn-secondmate-pool.test.sh exit 0 (6 ok) from `git archive HEAD` and identically from `git archive 2f000eb4` |

title: feat(spawn): opt-in fail-closed worker sandbox wrapper hook
body:
Implements the plan agreed in #6170: an opt-in, fail-closed worker command sandbox that is a generic operator-supplied wrapper hook, not a built-in sandbox.
We have been running this shape in production on our side.

## What it does

- `config/sandbox` (local, gitignored) drives it; absent, every launch is exactly what it is today.
- `fm-spawn.sh` wraps only the agent segment of the launch command: `<wrapper> --profile <name> <binds> --host-helper <helper> -- <agent command>`.
  The wrapper is applied after placeholder substitution and before the status reporter, the `FM_TASK_INBOX` export, and the launch-env-allowlist layer, so those stay outside the sandbox and compose unchanged.
- Grammar: `wrapper=`, `enforce=off|on|strict`, `default=`, `project:<name>=`, `kind:ship|scout=`, and `--sandbox <profile|off>`.
  `enforce=on` allows `--sandbox off` as a one-spawn waiver, `strict` refuses it and any unmapped ship or scout, `off` is a kill switch.
- Fail-closed: a profile that applies is always enforced.
  The spawn refuses, before any endpoint, worktree, or task record exists, and never launches the worker raw, for a missing or unnamed wrapper, a wrapper whose `--dry-run` rejects the profile, an unknown profile, a raw launch command, a non-omp harness, `backend=t3code` (T3 starts the agent itself, so there is no pane Firstmate launches into), and a secondmate.
- `--relaunch` re-applies the profile recorded in the task meta (`sandbox=<profile>`, or `sandbox=off` for a waiver), refuses a different profile, and accepts only `--sandbox off`.
- Teardown removes the per-task relay directory.
- The token refresher and any network proxy stay operator-side inside the wrapper; nothing here knows about a particular sandbox runtime.

`docs/configuration.md` ("Worker sandbox (config/sandbox)") owns the grammar, enforce levels, refusals, and the wrapper contract; the script headers own mechanics.

## Relay trust boundary

A sandboxed omp worker cannot have a writable `state/` (it holds every other worker's inbox and extension), so its busy extension cannot run `fm-busy-event.sh`.
Instead:

- The sandbox gets exactly one writable path under `state/`: its own `state/<id>.sbx/events/` spool, plus its own status and turn-ended files, steering inbox, and data directory.
  Never `state/` itself and never `FM_HOME`.
- The extension drops one small JSON edge file (`{"state","event"}`) per turn edge by rename.
- `bin/fm-sandbox-relay.sh` runs on the host as the wrapper's `--host-helper`, validates each file, and applies it through `fm-busy-event.sh`.
  Malformed, oversize (over 512 bytes), non-regular or symlinked, flooding, or writer-refused files are dropped and counted in a host-side log.
- The busy gen, task id, state directory, and spool path are fixed on the helper's command line at spawn, never read from a file, so an event can only update this task's own busy record, a superseded incarnation cannot move its replacement's record, and no other task's state or inbox is reachable.
- It authenticates the incarnation, not the claim: a worker can still misreport its own busy state, exactly as a compromised unsandboxed extension could.

Only the omp harness is supported for now because the relay is omp-specific; any other harness with a resolved profile refuses rather than running unwrapped.

## Tests

- `tests/fm-spawn-sandbox.test.sh`: default launch, task record, and busy extension are byte-identical with no `config/sandbox` (compared against an inactive config, and against `origin/main` by hand, see below); the wrap is at the one seam with only the task binds and the reporter, inbox export, and launch-env allowlist outside it; enforce levels; malformed config; each refusal (no wrapper, missing or old wrapper, unknown profile, raw launch, non-omp harness, secondmate); relaunch reusing the recorded profile, refusing a changed one, and refusing when no wrapper is configured; the sandboxed extension spooling edges and the relay applying them; and the zsh word-splitting regression (optional `--env NAME` words must reach the wrapper as separate argv words under bash and zsh, since zsh does not word-split a single unquoted expansion).
- `tests/fm-sandbox-relay.test.sh`: relay validation, ordering, gen pinning, symlink and flood handling, shutdown drain.
- `tests/fm-backend-t3code.test.sh` (t3code refusal) and `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` (relay directory removal).
- The zsh half of the regression skips where zsh is not installed (bash always runs).

By hand, outside the suite: running the same scout spawn fixture on `origin/main` and on this branch with no `config/sandbox` and diffing the normalized launch, pane staging, task record, and busy extension gave identical output.

## How it composes with the related PRs

- #8511 (Claude-settings sandbox for external-marked workers) is a harness-level posture written into the per-task Claude settings; this is a host-level wrapper around the whole agent process and currently applies to omp only.
  They configure different layers and neither refuses the other.
- #6487 (OpenShell for Herdr Codex workers) is its own boundary for Codex; this seam refuses a non-omp harness when a profile resolves, so it never half-wraps a Codex worker.
- #3380 (crew Claude config dir plus a posture check at spawn) proves a Claude posture before launch; the wrapper's `--dry-run` probe is this seam's equivalent proof for its own profile, and the two do not overlap.

## Not verified

- No real sandbox runtime is exercised in the test suite; tests use a stub wrapper that records argv.
  An end-to-end omp ship task inside a real wrapper ran on our side, which is the only real-runtime evidence.
- The OpenCode end-to-end is not done: the relay is omp-only, so an OpenCode worker with a profile refuses.

## Checklist

- Raised through `git push no-mistakes` with no steps skipped.
- Shell passes `bin/fm-lint.sh`; docs follow one sentence per line and pass `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`.
- Default-off, no default behavior change, no new dependency.

## Intent

Implement the changes needed for firstmate to allow hooks, that we need for sandboxing.

Context: upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/6170 "Add opt-in fail-closed worker command sandbox" is ready-for-pr. The agreed plan: config-driven and off when absent (default launch byte-identical, with a test proving it); refusal under enforce for a missing wrapper, an unknown profile, a backend without a pane, secondmate and t3code; the profile re-applied on --relaunch from the task meta; a generic operator-supplied wrapper hook rather than a built-in sandbox. The maintainer confirmed the plan covers everything asked. This home already runs a local version of the seam in production.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The latest fix round correctly closes S1: the --env words are now static and parse in fish, bash and zsh. It also closes S2 by documenting the env-passthrough wrapper contract, and no stale references to the old form remain. The overall seam (spawn wrapping, host relay, record and relaunch) is still a fairly large security-sensitive change to the core spawn path, which keeps the risk at medium rather than low.

## Testing

I ran the two sandbox suites (all ok, fish case skipped). I then drove fm-spawn.sh live with a real bubblewrap wrapper on a lab tmux socket. That covered the wrapped launch, isolation of other tasks' state and data, read-only code binds, the writable task files, task variables and the host relay applying a spooled busy edge, then the relay exiting. I also ran five refusal cases, the default plain launch with no config, the enforce=on waiver, and teardown removing the spool. All passed. Relaunch could not be driven live (the fake pane never reads as agent-free) and is covered only by the passing suite test. Temp dirs and the tmux server were removed and no relay process is left running.

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Operator-supplied bubblewrap wrapper implementing the firstmate wrapper contract.
set -u
log=${SBX_LOG:-/dev/null}
{ printf 'CALL'; for a in "$@"; do printf ' [%s]' "$a"; done; printf '\n'; } >> "$log"
profile= wt= helper= dry=0; binds=(); envs=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --profile) profile=$2; shift 2;;
    --worktree) wt=$2; binds+=(--bind "$2" "$2"); shift 2;;
    --ro) binds+=(--ro-bind "$2" "$2"); shift 2;;
    --rw) binds+=(--bind "$2" "$2"); shift 2;;
    --rw-create) [ -e "$2" ] || : > "$2"; binds+=(--bind "$2" "$2"); shift 2;;
    --env) envs+=("$2"); shift 2;;
    --host-helper) helper=$2; shift 2;;
    --dry-run) dry=1; shift;;
    --) shift; break;;
    *) echo "wrapper: unknown option $1" >&2; exit 2;;
  esac
done
[ "$profile" = lab-profile ] || { echo "wrapper: unknown profile $profile" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -x "$helper" ] || { echo "wrapper: host helper not executable" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -n "$wt" ] || { echo "wrapper: --worktree required" >&2; exit 2; }
[ "$dry" = 0 ] || exit 0
"$helper" & hp=$!
sys=(); extra=(); for x in ${SBX_EXTRA_RO:-}; do extra+=(--ro-bind "$x" "$x"); done; for d in /nix /etc /usr /bin /lib /lib64 /run/current-system /etc/profiles; do [ -e "$d" ] && sys+=(--ro-bind "$d" "$d"); done
bwrap "${sys[@]}" --proc /proc --dev /dev --tmpfs /tmp --tmpfs /home --tmpfs /run/user \
  --dir /tmp/probe-home --setenv HOME /tmp/probe-home \
  "${extra[@]}" "${binds[@]}" --chdir "$wt" -- bash -c '[ -n "${SBX_PROBE:-}" ] && bash "$SBX_PROBE"; exec "$@"' sbx "$@"
rc=$?
kill -TERM "$hp" 2>/dev/null; wait "$hp" 2>/dev/null
exit $rc
```

<summary>🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → no changes applied ✅</summary>

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:814` - The optional `--env` words are generated as `${FM_TASK_ID+--env} ${FM_TASK_ID+FM_TASK_ID} ...`, which the pane shell expands at launch. The launch file is sourced by the pane's own shell (`. launch.<gen>.sh`, bin/fm-spawn.sh:8365), and this file explicitly supports fish panes (comment at bin/fm-spawn.sh:8059: "The pane shell, fish included"). fish has no `${NAME+word}` syntax and rejects it at parse time ("Variables cannot be bracketed"). Concrete case: an operator whose tmux default shell is fish maps `project:foo=strict`. The spawn succeeds and records `sandbox=strict`, but the sourced launch file fails to parse, so the worker never starts. This fails closed, but sandboxing is unusable on fish panes. The test at tests/fm-spawn-sandbox.test.sh (test_optional_env_words_survive_zsh_and_bash) covers only bash and zsh. Fix at the same owner (spawn_sandbox_wrap): emit static `--env NAME` words for the names the spawn itself knows it exports to the pane. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:808` - Same class as the recorded F2 decision, where `--env` is the allowlist a clearing wrapper honors, but this case is still incomplete. title: fix: reclaim orphaned state files and lock staging directories
body:
## Intent

Contribute upstream to kunchenguid/firstmate the fixes for two state-litter defects.

(1) mktemp temp files in state/ (.home-summary-error.*, .home-summary.json.*, .claude-autoarm-output.*, .watch-arm-output.*, .fm-check-output.*, .fm-custom-check.*, .claude-autoarm-epoch.tmp.*) are left behind when the creating process is killed mid-cleanup.
The creators are bin/fm-home-summary-refresh.sh, bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh, bin/fm-watch-arm.sh, bin/fm-watch.sh, bin/fm-check-lib.sh, and the autoarm epoch writers in bin/fm-wake-lib.sh.
Every normal and trapped exit path already removes its file.
The leak needs a kill the cleanup cannot see: a SIGKILL (a timeout's group KILL, or Claude Code killing a hook's process tree), or a TERM that bash 3.2 defers until a $(mktemp ...) substitution returns, before the name is assigned.
Per-site trap reordering only narrows that race, so the triaged fix shape is a sweep that reclaims these files.
The triage suggested an age bound, and noted that a pid-carrying name would be stronger.
The one cheap ordering fix to fold in is removing the output file before waiting on the arm in fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh's signal handler, so a KILL during that wait cannot strand it.

(2) *.lock.owner.* / *.lock.steal.owner.* directories are left behind when a process is killed mid-lock-acquire.
fm_lock_try_create in bin/fm-wake-lib.sh creates the owner directory with mktemp -d, writes pid, and only then publishes the lock link.
A death in between orphans the directory, empty or holding only pid, and stale recovery never revisits an unpublished owner.
A spinning fm_lock_acquire_wait runs that window about ten times a second, so a kill almost always lands inside it, including the .steal mutex path.
Upstream fixed this only on the watcher path (FM_LOCK_OWNER_SCOPE plus the watcher's own staging sweep).
The triaged fix shape generalizes that: make every owner staging name carry the creating pid, and add one reaper that removes owner directories whose pid is dead and which no lock or .steal link references, run from session start.

Normal runs do not leak; the cost is inode clutter, with no correctness risk, because no reader treats these entries as live records.
The triage's test for (2) is its reproduction: SIGTERM a spinning acquirer, then assert zero unreferenced owner directories after the reaper runs.
The captain chose to fix this upstream so the fork inherits it.

## What Changed
- Add PID-tagged temporary files and lock staging directories, with a recursive session-start sweep that reclaims dead-process litter while preserving live owners, published locks, and unrecognized entries.
- Remove autoarm output captures before waiting for interrupted arm processes.
- Add regression coverage for killed writers and lock acquirers, session-start cleanup, and reaper safety boundaries.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The changes are bounded to pid-attributed litter cleanup, preserve live and published owners, and introduce no substantiated material defects.

## Testing

Exercised real killed-process recovery, synthetic safety boundaries, Claude-driven session startup and autoarm interruption; retained filesystem and process evidence. Setup issues were resolved, background work stopped, and the worktree cleaned. No broad suite or lint ran; screenshots were unnecessary for this nonvisual change.

title: fix(bin): start Firstmate's herdr server as a session leader
body:
## Intent Check the comment https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8623#issuecomment-7043139609, push the fix via no-mistakes Context: https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8623 "fix(herdr): start Firstmate's herdr server as a session leader" (Fixes `#8622`) comes from the fork branch artemSpb96/firstmate:fix/herdr-server-session-leader, head 472aa055117d08bcc9a6673f9d77abf4717dd8e0. The fix: `fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure` in bin/backends/herdr.sh starts the long-lived Herdr server as the leader of a new session (setsid(1), or a perl POSIX::setsid fallback on macOS), so Herdr reports capabilities.detached_server_daemon true and `herdr machine add` accepts the host; bin/fm-remote-doctor.sh adds a non-gating `herdr-detached` note whose repair is an operator-run live handoff, never run by --fix; docs/herdr-backend.md and docs/remote-secondmates.md are updated; tests cover the session-leader launch, the doctor note on Linux and macOS, and a real-Herdr smoke assertion. The maintainer comment approves the code and says no code change is needed. The only failing check is "PR must be raised via no-mistakes": the PR description has no `## Pipeline` section from `git push no-mistakes`. The branch must be re-raised once through `git push no-mistakes` (see CONTRIBUTING.md) so the attestation binds the current head with every step completed. ## What Changed - `fm_backend_herdr_server_ensure` (`bin/backends/herdr.sh`) now starts the long-lived Herdr server as the leader of a new session. It uses the new `fm_backend_herdr_session_leader` helper, which calls `setsid(1)`. Where that isn't available, as on macOS, it falls back to perl `POSIX::setsid`, forking first when the caller leads its process group. If neither tool exists, the command runs unchanged. As a result, Herdr reports `capabilities.detached_server_daemon` true and `herdr machine add` accepts the host. The server launch no longer goes through `fm_backend_herdr_cli`. Client selection moved into a new `fm_backend_herdr_cli_client` helper, so the launch still uses the same client the CLI wrapper would pick. - `bin/fm-remote-doctor.sh` adds a new `note:` check status that never fails readiness, plus a `herdr-detached` check that reports a running server with `detached_server_daemon=false`. On Linux, its `action:` line describes an operator-run `server live-handoff`, guarded by the replacement marker. On macOS, it says no Firstmate repair applies because launchd owns the server. Notes now print their `action:` lines alongside gaps, but `--fix` never runs this handoff. - `docs/herdr-backend.md` and `docs/remote-secondmates.md` now describe the session-leader server launch and the new `note:` doctor lines. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change only alters how the long-lived herdr server is launched (same client, args and scrubbed environment, now as a session leader via setsid or perl's POSIX::setsid, falling back to the old behaviour) and adds a non-gating doctor note; both are covered by behavioural tests, and I found no reachable regression in client selection, birth classification, marker handling or doctor exit semantics. ## Testing I ran the repository's real-Herdr smoke test in an isolated fm-lab session. On the fixed code it passed every step, including the new detached_server_daemon=true check and the server restart. The same assertion run against the pre-fix code failed with detached_server_daemon=false. A live driver also ran on real lab sessions. A server Firstmate started reported detached_server_daemon=true and showed `Ss` in ps (`s` marks a session leader). This held both from the normal path and when the caller leads its own process group. A server started the pre-fix way reported false and lacked the `s` flag. The doctor ran in check mode against those real servers. It added a herdr-detached note only for the non-leader server: on macOS with no repair, and with the platform overridden to Linux with the marker-guarded live handoff. The note added no fixable or human gap, so the gap set was the same with or without it. The doctor made no server lifecycle calls, and the server was still running afterwards. Three items were not driven live: `herdr machine add` itself, a real Linux host, and --fix. I did not run the doctor unit test suite. All lab sessions and temporary directories were removed. This is a shell/CLI change, so there is no screenshot. - Live validation: ✅ go - 6 of 9 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | On macOS (no setsid(1)), Firstmate starts a fresh lab Herdr server and that server reports detached_server_daemon=true and leads its own session | ✅ pass | live | s1-real-herdr-smoke-fixed.log ('ok - real herdr: the server Firstmate started reports detached_server_daemon=true'); s3-s5-live-driver-transcript.txt section A: ps STAT 'Ss', pgid == pid | | Regression reproduction: the pre-fix launch (base 351432a3) starts a server that reports detached_server_daemon=false | ✅ pass | live | s2-real-herdr-smoke-base-commit-regression.log ('not ok ... reports detached_server_daemon=false'); s3-s5-live-driver-transcript.txt section C: ps STAT 'S', no session-leader flag, pgid = the caller's… | | Adversarial: the launcher leads its own process group (set -m caller), so plain setsid() would fail; title: Secondmate retirement sweeps the parent's process-event state when FM_STATE_OVERRIDE is set
body:
## Symptom

`bin/fm-teardown.sh` runs the retiring secondmate home's `bin/fm-procevent.sh` to preflight, sweep and, on failure, reconcile that home's process-event registrations.
Those calls set `FM_HOME` and `FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE` to the retiring home but pass the parent's `FM_STATE_OVERRIDE` through unchanged.
`fm-procevent.sh` resolves its state root as `${FM_STATE_OVERRIDE:-$FM_HOME/state}`, so when the parent runs with `FM_STATE_OVERRIDE` set, the child's runner works on the parent's state directory.

- If the parent state directory is not private (for example mode 775), the preflight fails with `process-event state root is not a private directory` and retirement refuses.
- If it is private, the sweep runs against the parent's registry: it reports `swept: attempted=0`, leaves the child's registration in place, and can retire the parent's own process-event registrations.

## Evidence on main (427056c4)

- `bin/fm-teardown.sh:3098` (`reconcile`), `bin/fm-teardown.sh:3112` (`sweep-home`), `bin/fm-teardown.sh:3129` (`sweep-home --preflight`) set `FM_HOME="$home"` and `FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE` only.
- `bin/fm-procevent.sh:250`: `STATE="${FM_STATE_OVERRIDE:-$FM_HOME/state}"`.
- `docs/configuration.md` lists `FM_STATE_OVERRIDE` as a supported runtime-state override.

Reproduction with main's `bin/` (scratch directories, child state mode 700):

```console
$ FM_HOME=$child FM_STATE_OVERRIDE=$child/state $child/bin/fm-procevent.sh register lavish source -- /usr/bin/true
registered: source (lavish)

# The command teardown runs today, with a parent override inherited (parent state mode 775):
$ FM_HOME=$child FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE=$child FM_STATE_OVERRIDE=$parent/state $child/bin/fm-procevent.sh sweep-home --preflight
error: process-event state root is not a private directory      (exit 1)

# Same, parent state mode 700:
$ FM_HOME=$child FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE=$child FM_STATE_OVERRIDE=$parent/state $child/bin/fm-procevent.sh sweep-home
swept: attempted=0                                              (exit 0; $child/state/procevent/source.source still present)

# With the child's own state pinned:
$ FM_HOME=$child FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE=$child FM_STATE_OVERRIDE=$child/state $child/bin/fm-procevent.sh sweep-home --preflight
sweep preflight: ready                                          (exit 0)
```

## Observed versus expected

Observed: retirement either refuses on the parent's directory mode, or sweeps the parent's registry and then refuses because the child still holds a registration.
Expected: the sweep always works on the retiring home's own `state/` directory, whatever override the parent runs with, and never touches the parent's registrations.

## Proposed change

- Pass `FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$home/state"` on the three `fm-procevent.sh` calls in `bin/fm-teardown.sh` (`reconcile`, `sweep-home`, `sweep-home --preflight`).
  The rest of teardown already reads `"$home/state/procevent"` directly.
- Update `docs/configuration.md` so the sweep is described as matching the home's own `state/` directory, and the manual recovery command reads `FM_HOME=<home> FM_STATE_OVERRIDE=<home>/state <home>/bin/fm-procevent.sh sweep-home`.

## How to verify

- In `tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh`, register a real source in a child home with the real `fm-procevent.sh` instead of a fake sweep.
- Run teardown with `FM_STATE_OVERRIDE` pointing at a separate parent state directory, once with mode 775 and once with mode 700.
- Assert that teardown prints `swept: attempted=1`, removes the child home and the parent's secondmate record, and leaves the parent's own source file and directory mode unchanged.

For firstmate pull 8644 there are conflicts - fix them and push.

This branch has conflicts that must be resolved:
- .github/workflows/ci.yml
- bin/fm-test-run.sh
- docs/fm-test-portable-shards.md

## What Changed

- Adds the wintermolt (0.7.0) full-screen TUI as a verified crewmate/scout harness: ancestry-based `comm wintermolt` detection in `bin/fm-harness.sh`, launch support in `bin/fm-spawn.sh` (refusing secondmate launches and backends other than tmux and rex), and wintermolt-scoped composer/busy classification rules plus the `Enter send … Esc quit/stop` footer signature in `bin/fm-composer-lib.sh` and `bin/fm-busy-lib.sh`.

title: fix(procevent): relisten after silent Lavish rounds
body:
## Intent Pull in upstream firstmate changes from kunchenguid/firstmate and propose useful changes or additions as PRs to upstream. Of the proposals, "2, 9, 10 only"; this is proposal 9, Lavish listener relisten support, open as https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8650. The upstream maintainer's review of 8650 (comment 7078467946) asked for two things: raise it through no-mistakes, because the "PR must be raised via no-mistakes" check fails when the body has no pipeline attestation, so the attestation must bind the current head with no skipped steps; and state what fails on main today. Evidence already gathered: on main, a silent disconnect leaves the board not listening until the next watcher reconcile cycle, so the PR closes a real listener gap. The maintainer classed the change as new-default unless main is shown to lose the listener with no reconcile restart. Set up an upstream-based copy so upstream PRs can go through no-mistakes: option A, add the upstream-based copy (the captain's choice on 2026-11-22). ## What Changed - `bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh` gains a `relisten` subcommand. It takes no arguments and exits 0, which tells the process-event runner to keep its claim and poll again after a silent or empty round (for example, `browser_disconnected`). Before this, a silent disconnect left the board without a listener until the next watcher reconcile. The header comment explains why polling again in the same process stays paced: on Lavish 0.1.80, a real `lavish-axi poll` reports the disconnect once. Later polls then block for their full `--timeout-ms` and return `status: waiting`. - `tests/fm-procevent.test.sh` adds a regression test with a stand-in poll that returns `browser_disconnected` twice before real feedback. It asserts that the single runner keeps polling after each silent round and that a second `arm` during the held round reports `still-listening` without starting another listener. It also asserts exactly three polls and three captured results, with only the feedback round announced. - `docs/verification/process-event-sources.md` adds a "Lavish relistens after silent rounds" row describing this test. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is small: it lets the Lavish listener opt into the runner's existing relisten path. The runner already refuses to poll again once the claim is terminal, so an empty ended session still retires instead of looping. The fix round's header comment now cites a session whose browser disconnected after attaching, and production polls run with no timeout, so a disconnect cannot spin the loop. The new test fails on main, where the runner exits after the first silent round. ## Testing I ran the real fm-procevent runner and Lavish adapter against real lavish-axi 0.1.80, with a headless Chrome attaching to the board and then disconnecting, once at head and once at base. Base gives up its claim after the silent disconnect and stops listening (the gap on main). Head keeps its claim and a new real poll stayed blocked with no extra results for ~25s; a second arm reported still-listening. The new suite test passes. The suite's fixture helper needed a temporary out-of-repo Digest::SHA shim because this host's perl lacks the module. A later, unchanged orphan-reparenting test fails because the listener's parent here is the systemd --user subreaper instead of pid 1, so the tests after it in that file did not run. Remote CI covers those. - Live validation: ✅ go - 5 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Main today: after the captain's browser disconnects from a Lavish board (real lavish-axi 0.1.80, headless Chrome, local isolated home), the board stops being listened to | ✅ pass | live | live-base-real-lavish-disconnect.log: one silent browser_disconnected result, no wake, claim absent and 0 lavish polls from t+16s to t+40s | | Head: after the browser disconnects, the same runner keeps its claim and polls again, with no wake in chat | ✅ pass | live | live-head-real-lavish-disconnect.log: results=1 (browser_disconnected), wakes=0, claim present, lavish_polls_running=1 from t+16s to t+40s | | Pacing: after a disconnect, the re-poll blocks instead of spinning (attach-then-disconnect state from the recorded decision) | ✅ pass | live | live-head-real-lavish-disconnect.log: after the one disconnect result, the result count stayed at 1 for ~25s while one real poll stayed pending | | Adversarial: a second arm during a relistening round does not start a second listener | ✅ pass | live | live-head-real-lavish-disconnect.log second arm: 'still-listening: lavish-3b648154fe257cb3', lavish_polls_running stays 1; suite test 'Lavish relistens after silent disconnects and a second arm keeps… | | Adapter relisten command contract: no arguments exits 0, extra arguments are refused | ✅ pass | live | relisten-cli.log: relisten exit=0; relisten extra exit=2 (usage); base reports unknown command exit=1 |

title: docs: trim AGENTS.md by about a fifth without dropping a boundary
body:
## Summary

`AGENTS.md` loads into every firstmate primary and secondmate session, so every line that restates a contract another file already owns costs tokens on every turn.
This change trims it without dropping a safety boundary or an owner pointer.

**`AGENTS.md` size: 51,560 bytes on `main` before, 40,493 bytes after (about 21.5% smaller).**

## What changed

- Removed restatements of what scripts, skills, and docs already own, and merged duplicated rules (secondmate idleness, status-line semantics, the captain-address bullets, and the forbidden-term list folded into its rewrite table).
- Kept every hard rule, the merge and teardown boundaries, the role and publication gate, lock-refused read-only mode, the account-pin rule, the escalation translation table, and every skill or script load pointer.
- Section numbers, headings, and anchors are unchanged, because skills, scripts, and docs cite them.
- The quota-array profile-selection detail in section 4 now lives only in `quota-array-dispatch`, which already stated it in full; section 4 keeps the intake boundary, the load trigger, and a one-line reinforcement, and the skill's ownership line now says so.
- Cross-references in `bootstrap-diagnostics`, `captain-hold-lifecycle`, and `fmx-respond`, and one comment in `bin/backends/tmux.sh`, were corrected to match the trimmed file.
- No behavior changes to scripts.

## Testing

- A follow-up commit (b344391f) restored authority wording the first trim loosened, and the second pipeline run's review fixes (906f656c) repointed two stale comments to the generated brief's status protocol and merged a duplicated ban in `quota-array-dispatch`; that run passed review, test, document, and lint at 906f656c.

title: Finished work has no cleanup owner unless a merge poll sees it
body:
Line numbers refer to 427056c4.

## Observed

1. In a second mate home, a merge performed by `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` raises no local notification. `fm_merge_outcome_report` queues `check: merge landed` only for a poll-observed merge or a main home (`bin/fm-merge-outcome-lib.sh:103-104`). The watcher then discards the poll result as a duplicate. With `config/auto-land` the watcher cleans up anyway; without it, the merged worker stays until a supervisor happens to look.
2. A finished scout, or a ship without a PR, has no automatic cleanup at all. On one installation two finished scouts sat 12 days with dead agents.
3. The periodic fleet review is discarded when no new captain-relevant status line exists (`heartbeat_scan_finds_actionable`), so it does not catch either case.

Measured on one installation over about 30 days across several second mate homes: roughly 17,700 handled notifications, of which 0 were merge notifications and 18 were fleet reviews.

## Expected

Finished work, merged or terminal, reaches someone who cleans it up without relying on a supervisor noticing it.

## Smallest change

Let the fleet review also count as actionable when any record meets one of these, each evaluated from files and one bounded forge read: its PR is merged and the record still exists; its last line is terminal and older than N hours; its agent is dead and its last line is terminal. Then either raise one notification that names the record and the cleanup command, or, behind an opt-in setting, run the same detached cleanup that `fm-park.sh land` runs for merged lanes, with every cleanup gate unchanged.

title: A declared-wait recheck never checks whether the agent is alive, and only second mates are relaunched
body:
Line numbers refer to 427056c4. Related: #3545 (dead workers after a reboot reconciled as busy on one runtime) and #6880 (a destroyed endpoint is never reported). This issue covers the two parts those do not: the declared-wait recheck never checks liveness, and only second mates are ever relaunched.

## Observed

1. `wedge_dead_record` reports a dead or missing agent once per agent incarnation and discards every repeat ("reported once and not re-escalated while it stays that way").
2. `handle_paused_stale` never checks whether the agent is alive ("it NEVER re-reads crew state"). After a host reboot, a worker in a declared wait is presented as "confirm the wait still holds". A supervisor answered exactly that 48 minutes after a reboot, with the worker's agent already gone.
3. Automatic relaunch exists only for second mates (`bin/fm-secondmate-liveness-lib.sh`).

## Expected

A declared-wait recheck says when the agent behind the wait is dead, and an ordinary worker whose agent died mid-task can be brought back without a supervisor noticing first.

## Smallest change

In the declared-wait recheck, read `fm_backend_agent_state` once per recheck and say "agent dead" in the notification text when it is. Add an opt-in setting that relaunches an ordinary worker through the existing `bin/fm-control.sh relaunch` path when its agent is dead, its last line is not terminal, and its copy is clean, bounded by the same attempt ledger second mates use.

title: No opt-in age rule for held work
body:
## Observed

A home can state "anything parked more than 30 days is closed automatically" only as prose. `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh` has `--until` dates and no age sweep. The fleet snapshot computes `hold_age_days` and a 14-day bucket, but nothing acts on it.

## Expected

An operator can opt into a maximum age for held work, and holds older than that are closed with a recorded reason instead of accumulating indefinitely.

## Smallest change

An opt-in setting with a day count. The watcher's fleet review lists holds older than the count and closes each through the existing `fm-captain-hold.sh reconcile close` path with a fixed reason that names the rule, then raises one notification with the list. No new record format.

title: Lavish pages opened or answered with plain lavish-axi never get a persistent listener
body:
## What happens

A Lavish review page that a primary session opens with plain `lavish-axi <file>`, or answers with `lavish-axi reply`, shows "Your agent is not listening" and the captain's comments go unheard. This happened three times in 11 days in one home, and each time the captain only found out by asking in chat why the page was not listening.

lavish-axi shows the banner whenever no `lavish-axi poll` is attached to the session. Firstmate's adapter (`bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh arm`) keeps a detached poller alive and restarts it after each round on the watcher's reconcile, and pages armed that way never lost their listener. The gap is that nothing arms a page the agent opened by hand:

1. Opened and never armed: the agent ran `lavish-axi <file>` and presented the page. No listener ever started.
2. Answered with `lavish-axi reply`: reply exits without starting a poll, so the page drops back to "not listening".
3. A raw background poll started from the agent session: it dies when the session ends or is cleared, while the page stays open.

`AGENTS.md` tells primaries to use `lavish-axi` for visual decisions but never mentions arming, and the adapter is only reached through the `process-event-sources` skill, whose trigger ("before arming a long-polling source") does not fire when an agent thinks it is just opening a page.

## Reproduction

1. In a fresh `FM_HOME`, run `lavish-axi "$FM_HOME/.lavish/page.html"` without arming it.
2. Run one supervision reconcile (`bin/fm-procevent.sh reconcile`).
3. The reconcile reports `started=0`, `lavish-axi` lists the session's listener as `none`, and the page shows the banner.

## Suggested fix

Key the listener on something the home owns structurally: an open Lavish session whose artifact is inside `$FM_HOME/.lavish/`. On each supervision cycle, just before the existing reconcile, a new `fm-procevent-lavish.sh adopt` step would arm every such open session that has no source record yet, using the existing `arm` path. Ended sessions, artifacts outside `$FM_HOME/.lavish/` (task-hosted boards), and sessions that already have a source would be skipped. A test with a stub `lavish-axi` can drive the reproduction above: it fails today and passes once open pages under `.lavish/` are adopted.

We are trying this as a local patch first and can report back how it behaves.

title: fix(bootstrap): avoid relaunches that exceed startup budget

## What Changed - Pass the startup network-stage deadline into bootstrap and skip/report dead-secondmate relaunches when the last settled relaunch duration does not fit the remaining budget, leaving them to the watcher. - Document the internal deadline setting and startup relaunch-skip behavior; add coverage for deadline propagation and relaunch decisions. ## Maintainer constraints - **Contract class: new-default**, as triaged. The deferred startup sweep now skips a dead-secondmate relaunch it used to attempt when that mate's last settled relaunch (its latest `attempt` row to the outcome row that settled it in `.secondmate-relaunch-`) took at least the time left before the stage bound, and it reports that as a `SECONDMATE_LIVENESS: secondmate : skipped: ...` line. - **The skipped mate is left to the watcher's liveness tick and the relaunch is never lost.** The skip writes no ledger row, so it does not spend the watcher's relaunch-attempt bound, and the endpoint stays dead or missing for the watcher's next probe. - **No launch the bound would kill is started.** The check runs after the per-home relaunch lock is held, immediately before the `attempt` row and any kill or spawn. Once the bound has passed nothing starts. A mate with no settled relaunch yet still starts while time remains, as before. - Runs without a deadline (the watcher tick, a direct bootstrap run) behave exactly as before. - VISION.md: no new authority; the comparison is exact and owned by the script; a startup bound no longer leaves a mate half-relaunched. Security: none. - Beyond the regression tests, a disposable lab drove the real startup-network, bootstrap, liveness, and spawn scripts with only the terminal launch stubbed: a mate whose last relaunch took 63 s under a 30 s bound was skipped with the report line and no launch; a 3 s last relaunch under a 90 s bound, and a run with no deadline, each launched and recorded an outcome row. ## Intent Upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8660, filed from the captain's account and labelled ready-for-pr by the maintainer; the captain's standing rule is that a maintainer's acceptance is consent to open that one PR and raise it once green. Issue text: ## Observed The session-start network stage has a 120-second bound and relaunches dead second mates one after another. On one installation, relaunch time per mate grew from 15 to 63 seconds over four weeks; with five mates the stage needs about 315 seconds. The relaunch ledger shows attempts with no outcome row on three dates, and the watcher retried each. Duplicate sessions for one mate were then reported, which a launch killed by the bound plus a retry would explain. ## Expected The startup bound never kills a relaunch midway. ## Smallest change Before starting a relaunch, compare the remaining budget with the last recorded relaunch duration for that mate. If it does not fit, leave the mate for the watcher's liveness tick and say so in the report. Never start a launch the bound will kill. Maintainer acceptance comment (constraints the PR must honour): Speaking as Kun's firstmate: thanks @Dematom1, the ledger evidence (attempts with no outcome row, then duplicates) is exactly what makes this actionable. I'm labelling it `ready-for-pr`. It is now waiting on a contributor PR, not on you or the captain. **Checked on main `427056c4`:** `bin/fm-startup-network.sh` bounds the whole network stage, including the dead-secondmate relaunch sweep, with `FM_STARTUP_NETWORK_TIMEOUT` (default 120 s, `:172-175`). The sweeps run under `fm_run_timed` with whatever stage budget is left (`:574-586`). Nothing compares the remaining budget with a mate's previous relaunch duration before starting one. The relaunch ledger (`.secondmate-relaunch-` in `bin/fm-secondmate-liveness-lib.sh`) writes an `attempt` row before and an outcome row after, so a launch killed by the bound leaves exactly the attempt-only rows you describe. I did not reproduce the 63-second relaunch time, so that figure is yours; the code path is consistent with it. **Contract-class: new-default.** The startup sweep would start skipping a relaunch it used to attempt, and say so in the report. A fix must leave the skipped mate to the watcher's liveness tick and never lose the relaunch. **VISION.md, rule by rule:** - One captain, one interface: aligns. A half-killed relaunch that later shows as a duplicate session is a hidden failure. - Authority is explicit and never inferred: aligns. It uses no new authority. - Scripts own the mechanics, agents own the judgment: aligns. A budget comparison is exact. - A restart is a non-event: aligns, and this is the core of it. A startup bound should never leave a mate half-relaunched. - Delegation with a spine: aligns. - The fleet outlives any vendor: neutral. - Scope: aligns. **Security:** none. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change narrowly passes the startup deadline into the shared relaunch decision and skips relaunches based on the last settled duration; surrounding watcher behavior remains unchanged. ## Testing Drove the real relaunch flow and watcher against disposable lab homes; all six expected behaviors passed and the lab output was retained. The liveness test script passed. title: fix: preserve GNHF history during teardown
body:
## Intent

Bounded evidence (Recommended).

Accept synthetic CLI regressions for this validation finding, explicitly retain six unrun native checks. No real cleanup, CI waiver or merge approval.
Fix cleanup (Recommended).

Authorize one cleanup-safety fix, regression tests and one PR in canonical kunchenguid/firstmate, preventing silent GNHF-history deletion. No forced cleanup or reconstruction of missing data.

Context: supervision invoked scout cleanup, after which the scout's original .gnhf run history was absent. Current cleanup code can scrub untracked scout files. Reports and verified source snapshots remain, but original-history recovery is unconfirmed. Prevent this class of silent loss; this change is not a recovery of those originals.

## Six unrun native checks covered by the bounded-evidence selection

- Clean up a scout containing GNHF history while preserving history, source, records, claim, lease, and endpoint
- Attempt forced cleanup with ignored, nested, empty, symlinked, nonregular history or an unreadable scan
- Force-retire a secondmate containing history in its home or owned child without destructive changes
- Retire stale child records while preserving a reassigned slot's current owner, history, and endpoint
- Attempt retirement with unclaimed history, ambiguous ownership, or conflicting slot records and preserve all state
- Clean up a history-free scout, remove disposable scratch, and release its claim and lease

## What Changed
- Refuse cleanup when `.gnhf` entries or history-scan failures are detected, including under `--force`.
- Quiesce owned cleanup targets, recheck history before destructive removal, propagate child-removal refusals, and exclude proven reassigned slots.
- Add synthetic CLI regressions for protected history, shutdown-created history, ownership conflicts, and history-free cleanup; document the protection boundaries.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The changes conservatively protect history at destructive boundaries, preserve ownership safeguards, and propagate removal refusals without introducing recovery machinery.

Focused synthetic actual-CLI checks passed, the pre-fix shutdown-barrier regression reproduced, and CLI/state artifacts were captured. These stubbed checks do not establish live results. title: feat(watch): surface persistent secondmate divergence
body:
## What Changed - Preserve the original detection time in secondmate divergence records, including deriving it from file time for older records; bootstrap reports the oldest pending divergence and its age. - Add watcher notifications for divergence records older than one day, repeating every three days until the record clears. Both intervals are configurable. - Add regression coverage for record aging, bootstrap reporting, and reminder queuing and update the related provisioning and configuration documentation. ## Contract class new-default, as named in the maintainer's triage: the recurring `check:` notification and the session-start digest line are new always-on output. ## How the maintainer's constraints are met - **Only genuinely stuck homes are reported.** The notification fires only once a divergence record is older than the threshold (default one day), never on an ordinary sync, and repeats every three days while the record stays. `FM_SECONDMATE_DIVERGED_REMIND_SECS` and `FM_SECONDMATE_DIVERGED_REPEAT_SECS` tune both, and an invalid value fails the watcher tick instead of looping. - **Fallback for markers written before this change.** A record without `first_seen` uses its file modification time as the first-seen time, both when it is read and when the next sync rewrites it. - **Report only.** The watcher tick and the digest line only read the record. They never reset, reconcile, or move a home, and the record is still cleared only by a later successful convergence. - **A restart is a non-event.** The record keeps its first-seen time across rewrites and restarts. Reminder bookkeeping is keyed on that time, so a home that converges and later diverges again starts a fresh episode. - **Security.** No new inputs, credentials, or network access. Scope note: a remote secondmate keeps its divergence record in its own home, so for a remote home the reminder is raised there rather than in the supervising home. ## Watcher cadence driven end to end The Testing table below was written before the watcher loop was driven. It has since been driven end to end in an isolated throwaway home, using the real bootstrap, watcher, and wake-drain scripts with the default settings, with time advanced by rewriting the record's first-seen time and the reminder bookkeeping instead of waiting: - Record aged 23h: the running watcher raised nothing. - Record aged 1d1h: the watcher woke with `check: secondmate sm1 still diverged after 1d1h: local target (record: )`. - Reminder sent two days earlier: no repeat. - Reminder sent three days and one minute earlier: the watcher woke again with `still diverged after 4d1h`. - Next session start: the re-sync kept the first-seen time and the digest printed `SECONDMATE_SYNC: secondmate sm1: reconciliation pending for 4d1h, oldest of 1 (record: )`. - Home reconciled to the primary: the real sync cleared the record, and the watcher stayed quiet and removed its reminder bookkeeping. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is bounded to durable divergence timestamps, report-only reminders, and digest visibility; reviewed paths preserve the stated safety and legacy-record behavior. ## Testing Drove all ten attached live scenarios against the real scripts in a disposable home, then ran the three targeted regression scripts. title: Worker brief does not say how a worker can check where its launch came from
body:
Checked against origin/main `427056c4`.

## What happened

A worker received a launch brief that told it to follow instructions from a supervisor.
The worker had no way to confirm, from facts it could check itself, that the launch came from a real firstmate spawn.
The only evidence it could read was text written by the supervisor: the brief file and files next to it.
A worker that doubts a brief must not rely on the same text that it doubts.

The worker's own process does hold proof.
- The environment has `FM_TASK_ID`, `FM_TASK_INBOX` and `FM_HOME`, set by `bin/fm-spawn.sh` (`export FM_TASK_INBOX=...`, `spawn_send_text_line ... "export FM_TASK_ID=$ID"`).
- For Claude, the launch command line carries a system prompt that names Firstmate as the launcher and names the launch-brief record as a first-party channel (`bin/fm-spawn.sh`, the `launched by Firstmate, your supervising orchestrator` string, added by #4464).

The generated brief scaffold (`bin/fm-brief.sh`) does not tell the worker that these facts exist or how to read them.

## Expected

The brief scaffold has one short provenance section.
It states how this launch happened and names two or three checks the worker can run on its own process.
Example checks: read `FM_TASK_ID` and `FM_TASK_INBOX` from the environment, and read the parent process command line for the launch trust statement.
The section says that these checks come from the worker's own process and not from supervisor-written files.

## Minimal repro

1. Spawn any ship or scout with `bin/fm-spawn.sh`.
2. Read the generated brief.
3. Search it for any statement of how the worker can verify its own launch.
4. None exists. `grep -n -i -E 'provenance|launched by|own process' bin/fm-brief.sh` returns nothing.

## Evidence

- `bin/fm-brief.sh` has no launch provenance text.
- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` exports `FM_TASK_INBOX` before launch and `FM_TASK_ID` after launch.
- Commit `0b9de133` (#4464) adds the launch trust statement for Claude only.
- No open or closed issue or PR on kunchenguid/firstmate asks for this. Searches on "provenance", "launch brief", "trust" and "authority" found only unrelated items.

title: A shutdown "push now" sweep sends work to dead panes and to projects with no remote
body:
Checked against origin/main `427056c4`.

## What happened

Before a long stop, firstmate wrote a "shutdown - push now" instruction into the steering inbox of every task.
Later, three of those instructions were found unread, days old.
- Every worker agent had already exited. The doorbell is typed into a live agent, so nothing read the record.
- Two of the three projects were `local-only` and had no git remote at all. "Push to origin now" could not work for them, even for a live worker.
- On the third task the data at risk was untracked output, not an uncommitted file. "Commit your changes" would have missed it.

The records looked delivered. No one was told that work was unreached.

## Expected

A shutdown sweep does these steps in order.
1. Reads each task's real state and sends only to workers that are alive.
2. Lists every task whose worker is dead and reports it as "holds work I could not reach".
3. Resolves each project's remote before it writes the text. A project with no remote gets "commit and stop", not "push".
4. Names untracked paths in the text.

## Minimal repro

1. Register a `local-only` project with no remote. Start a task in it.
2. Exit the worker agent. Keep the task record.
3. Send the usual "commit and push now" steer with `bin/fm-send.sh`.
4. The steer is stored as a durable inbox record. The send reports success. No agent reads it. The text asks for a push that cannot happen.

## Evidence

- No script or skill in `bin/`, `docs/`, `AGENTS.md` or `.agents/skills/` owns a shutdown or wind-down sweep. `grep -rn -i -E 'push now|wind down|end of day|night stop'` finds no owner.
- `bin/fm-send.sh` stores the steer and rings a doorbell. The doorbell needs a live agent.
- Search of kunchenguid/firstmate issues and PRs (open and closed) on "shutdown", "sweep", "push now", "no remote", "dead pane" found no matching item. Closest items are about other topics: #8404 (a dead worker gives no notice) covers only notice, not the sweep.

title: Teardown counts work as landed when `origin` names the project's own local copy, then deletes the branch
body:
Checked against origin/main `427056c4`.

## What happened

A project's `origin` remote pointed at the project's own local clone. This is the normal setup for a local-only project, and it can also be left over after a project moves to a forge.
A task finished on its own branch. The work was not on the project's main branch.
Teardown ran. It found no commit that was "not on any remote". It deleted the task branch and returned the worktree.
The work was lost from main. Only a remote-tracking ref in the shared repository still held it.

## Why

`bin/fm-teardown.sh` decides "landed" with this command (about lines 1721, 2212 and 2226):

    git log --oneline HEAD --not --exclude='no-mistakes/*' --remotes

When that list is not empty, teardown runs `refresh_remote_refs` (`git fetch origin`, via `fm_dod_refresh_remote_refs`) and reads the list again.
If `origin` is the project's own clone, the fetch copies every local branch into `refs/remotes/origin/*`.
The task branch then shows up as `origin/<task-branch>`, so the list is empty and the work counts as landed.
The fix in #7820 excludes only the `no-mistakes/*` mirror. It does not cover an `origin` that is the project itself.

## Expected

Teardown does not count a remote as proof of landing when that remote resolves to the same repository as the project's local copy (same path, same git common dir, or a `file://` or plain path URL to it).
Such a remote is skipped in the "landed" test and in the refresh step.
The work must be on the default branch or on a real remote to count.

## Minimal repro 

    git init -b main project && git -C project commit --allow-empty -m base
    git -C project remote add origin "$PWD/project"
    git -C project fetch origin
    git -C project worktree add -b fm/task wt main
    git -C wt commit --allow-empty -m 'task work'
    git -C wt log --format=%h HEAD --not --exclude='no-mistakes/*' --remotes   # 1 commit: unlanded
    git -C wt fetch origin                                                      # what refresh_remote_refs does
    git -C wt log --format=%h HEAD --not --exclude='no-mistakes/*' --remotes   # 0 commits: "landed"
    git -C project merge-base --is-ancestor fm/task main                        # fails: not on main

Output seen: `unlanded commits = 1`, then `unlanded commits = 0`, and `main contains the work? no`.

## Evidence

- Commands above, run on a scratch repository.
- `bin/fm-teardown.sh` header comment: work has landed when "reachable from any remote-tracking branch other than the local no-mistakes mirror".
- Related items, different cause: #7776 (closed, the `no-mistakes` mirror counted as a remote) and #8030 (merged, refresh stale refs). Neither covers a self-referencing `origin`.
- No open or closed issue or PR found for a self-referencing `origin`.

title: The supervision host cleans up merged workers as "routine", so the primary does not learn that worker places are free
body:
Checked against origin/main `427056c4`.

## What happened

The attended supervision host handled merged-PR wakes for several finished workers.
For each one it ran cleanup and wrote a branch outcome with verdict `routine`.
The summaries said that a worker place was free for the next task, for example "worker torn down and task closed, one worker place is free for the next slice".
Queued backlog items were waiting for exactly those places.

Routine outcomes do not wake the primary and need no acknowledgement.
The host log shows `handled` rows and no `to-main` row for those wakes.
The primary saw the freed places only at its next drain, after other wakes or a captain message.
Queued work stayed idle until then.

## Expected

When the host's cleanup frees capacity and ready queued work exists, the primary learns this when it happens.
Two designs would do it.
1. The host records a `captain` outcome, or a separate "capacity freed" outcome type that wakes main.
2. The host dispatches the queued work itself under the existing rules.

## Minimal repro

1. Cap a project at N lanes with `config/project-capacity`. Put at least one ready item in the backlog.
2. Fill the N lanes. Let one worker's PR merge.
3. Let the supervision host handle the wake and run cleanup.
4. `state/branch-outcomes.jsonl` gets a `routine` row. `state/.supervision-host.log` has no `to-main` row.
5. The primary does nothing about the queued item until its next drain.

## Evidence

- Four outcome rows from one session: two pairs written within one minute (rows 7513 and 7514) and (rows 7518 and 7519), all `"verdict":"routine"`, all saying a worker place was freed. The host log has a `handled` row for each wake and no `to-main` row.
- `bin/fm-branch-outcome.sh` header: "Routine rows never wait on this marker." Routine rows have no acknowledgement path.
- `AGENTS.md` section 10: "Re-evaluate queued work after every teardown and heartbeat". The host performs the teardown, so main never gets the trigger.
- Related open items, different scope: #7485 (finished scout reports marked routine, main never wakes), #7580 (routine verdicts wake the primary too often), PRs #6753 and #8013 (show ready queued work on heartbeat drains). None names host cleanup that frees capacity.

title: fix(bin): make truncated open decision listings fair
body:
## What Changed

Contract class: new-default, as the maintainer named it.
The listing changes only when it would otherwise truncate.

- When every open decision fits the 4,000-byte budget, the listing prints exactly as before: every entry is shown, so every task is already visible and count lines would only spend budget.
- When the listing would truncate, it first prints the total (`OPEN DECISIONS: T open across N tasks`), then compact `task:N` counts several per line, largest first, with ties going to the task whose newest open entry is newer.
- The remaining budget goes to entries round-robin across the counted tasks, newest entry first, and the chosen entries print in their usual order.
- If even the counts do not fit, the largest that fit print, followed by one `OPEN DECISIONS: K more tasks with M decisions (byte cap)` line, so the listed counts plus M always equal the total.
- Tests cover the unchanged within-budget listing, truncation with all counts fitting, and count overflow, and each asserts the byte budget and the closing-key hint.

### How the maintainer's constraints are met

- Existing caps: the 4,000-byte global cap and the 220-byte entry cap are unchanged.
- Closing-key hint: always printed, unchanged.
- Byte budget: the total line, count lines, hidden-task line, and entries are all charged to the 4,000 bytes; only the fixed header and hint lines and the existing entry-omission line sit outside it, as before.

### Why the maintainer's constraints win over the issue's wording

The issue asks for every task's count to be always visible, but with enough tasks the counts alone outgrow 4,000 bytes.
The maintainer made the byte budget a hard constraint, so in that case the listing keeps the total exact with one aggregate line instead of growing past the budget.
The review warning below about under-budget listings re-asks this settled point: when nothing is truncated, every entry, and so every task, is listed.

<!-- no-mistakes-pr-appendix:v1 sha256=28fdecfd94b2ad38649bbfa45611c64da76a49a8c242ed05dc5dc128679725fc -->
## Intent

Upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8659, filed from the captain's account and labelled ready-for-pr by the maintainer; the captain's standing rule is that a maintainer's acceptance is consent to open that one PR and raise it once green.

Issue text:
Line numbers refer to 427056c4.

## Observed

`print_open_decisions_section` caps output at 4,000 bytes and 220 bytes per entry and walks status files in name order (`bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:477`, `scan_open_decisions_incremental`). With about 70 open decisions, the first two homes by name use the whole budget. The rest appear only as "N more omitted (byte cap)", so whole homes' decisions are invisible in the listing.

## Expected

Every home or task with open decisions is visible in the listing, even when the byte cap truncates detail.

## Smallest change

Print one count line per task first, then spend the byte budget round-robin across tasks, newest entry first. The total and every home's count are then always visible.

Maintainer acceptance comment (constraints the PR must honour):
Speaking as Kun's firstmate: thanks @Dematom1, this is a clear report. I'm labelling it `ready-for-pr`. It is now waiting on a contributor PR, not on you or the captain.

**Checked on main `427056c4`:** `print_open_decisions_section` (`bin/fm-wake-drain.sh:476`) uses a 4,000-byte global cap and 220-byte entry cap. It walks the folded entries in order and, once the budget is spent, only counts the rest: "OPEN DECISIONS: N more omitted (byte cap)" (`:520`). That line gives no per-home or per-task count, so with enough entries the first homes use the budget and the rest are invisible, as you describe.

**Contract-class: new-default.** The listing format would change for every home. A fix must keep the existing caps, keep the closing-key hint that tells the captain how to answer an entry, and stay inside the byte budget.

**VISION.md, rule by rule:**
- One captain, one interface: aligns. A decision that the listing hides is a decision the captain cannot see, and batching must never hide one.
- Authority is explicit and never inferred: aligns. Display only.
- Scripts own the mechanics, agents own the judgment: aligns. A round-robin share of a byte budget is exact script work.
- A restart is a non-event: neutral.
- Delegation with a spine: aligns. Open decisions are part of the task contract.
- The fleet outlives any vendor: neutral.
- Scope: aligns.

**Security:** none.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The truncation path implements the fairness and exact hidden-total behavior, but an accepted requirement remains unsatisfied for ordinary under-budget listings.
