title: After #8147: a read-only report of captain answers beside the recommended pick
body:
Once a captain ask carries a recommended pick (#8147 adds a required `--rec` and a `Rec:` line in the hold reason) and an option answer keeps its displayed meaning (#8152), both halves of a decision are in the durable record: what the first mate recommended, and what the captain said.
Nothing reads the two against each other.

## Problem

A captain who answers many calls cannot see where the first mate's recommendations are off.
An answer that follows the recommendation and one that overrules it look the same in the backlog: each is a closed call with a `Captain decision:` block.
In my own use of a similar decision loop, most answers follow the recommendation, so the few that depart are where the information is: they show which kinds of call the recommendation gets wrong.
Today, finding them means reading every closed call by hand.

## Proposed

A read-only subcommand, for example `fm-captain-hold.sh departures [--since <date>] [--repo <repo>]`.
For each closed captain call that has a `Rec:` line, it prints the task id, the repo, the recommended pick and the captain's recorded answer, side by side.
A summary line counts the calls answered, those answered as recommended, those that departed, and those it could not compare.

- A call is compared only when that is mechanical: the answer selects an option (#8152 keeps which one) and `Rec:` names an option.
- A free-text answer, a free-text `Rec:`, or an older hold with no `Rec:` line is listed as "not compared" and never guessed at. No model reads the words.
- It writes nothing, changes no hold and authorizes nothing. It is a report, as `diverged` is.

## Why it fits

- It makes delegation more legible: the captain can check the first mate's judgment from the record, not from memory.
- It is a script over durable records, with no agent judgment and no tokens.
- It assumes no consent, since nothing acts on the report. Whether repeated departures should ever feed `data/captain.md` is a separate question, which this does not open.

## Existing state

Checked 2026-11-23 against main `427056c`.
#8147 (open) adds `--rec`, `--option` and the `Rec:` line. This depends on it, or on whatever form the recommendation takes when it lands.
#8152 (open, ready-for-pr) preserves the displayed meaning of an option answer. With it, option answers compare cleanly.
#7733 asks for a task-scoped decision history in Bearings, one task at a time. This is the view across calls.
`fm-captain-hold.sh diverged` reports something else: two records of one call that contradict each other.
Searches across issues and PRs: "recommendation overruled", "recommended pick answer differs", "decision history", "recommendation accuracy", "captain preferences learn decisions".

## Scope

One read-only subcommand and its tests.
No change to `hold`, `answer`, the intake or `AGENTS.md`.
Not proposed: acting on departures, learning from them, or any change of default.

Drafted with Claude.

title: hc backend: doorbell refused as 'blocked (question)' when an omp worker's last answer ends with questions
body:
## What happened

On the hc backend, a steering message to an idle omp worker could not be delivered for about 25 minutes.

The worker was a scout. Its last answer ended with a numbered list of questions for firstmate (its decision request). hc classified the pane as `blocked (question)`, so every doorbell was refused:

```
$ hc send t103 ": Firstmate instruction waiting: ..."
{"error":{"hint":"typing would answer its dialog; read its screen first (hc read t103), or --force","kind":"blocked","message":"t103 is blocked (question)"}}
```

No dialog was open: the pane showed the omp prompt `❯` under the answer text. `fm-send.sh` wrote the inbox record and returned success; the re-ring ladder later escalated with `stale: ... (unread firstmate instruction: ... still unhandled after 3 doorbell delivery attempts with an idle pane; inspect the worker)`.

`bin/fm-control.sh <task> interrupt` and `fm-send.sh --key Enter` did not help; `fm-control.sh relaunch` refuses on hc (no recovery-grade classifier). The only way through was a manual `hc send <t> --force "<doorbell line>"` after reading the screen.

## Why it matters

This happens on the normal path: a scout ends with a `needs-decision` question list, the captain answers, and firstmate sends the answer or a promotion. Every such answer can get stuck. It also hit ship workers that ended a turn with a review-gate question (three more times the same day).

## Expected

- Either hc does not classify an agent's prose answer as a question dialog when the harness prompt is idle, or the hc adapter can tell a harness's own idle prompt from a real dialog and deliver the doorbell.
- At minimum, the escalation reason names the refusal (`hc refused: blocked (question)`) instead of `idle pane`, and `fm-send.sh` surfaces the refusal to its caller.

## Environment

- Firstmate at f6180a0, primary harness omp, worker harness omp, backend hc.
- `bin/backends/hc.sh` `fm_backend_hc_send_text_submit` maps exit 9 to `unknown` and never forces (by design); the false positive is in the classification.

title: Turn-end wakes surface for busy workers after an intentionally aborted no-mistakes run
body:
## What happened

Bare turn-ended wakes kept surfacing every 1 to 2 minutes for workers that were busy, so the primary was woken constantly while three workers ran.

The workers had aborted a no-mistakes run on purpose (a review fix needed a test-file change, which no-mistakes fix rounds do not make), made their own commits, and were working before a fresh run. In that window:

```
$ bin/fm-crew-state.sh <task>
state: failed · source: run-step · run failed · run: <aborted run id>
```

while `state/<task>.busy-state` said `state=busy` and the latest status line was `working: ... run aborted per firstmate; making review fixes test-first`.

So the aborted run's `failed` verdict wins over the busy verdict, the task has no positive work evidence, and every routine turn-end of that worker surfaces. On hc there is also no recovery-grade busy classifier, which removes the other proof.

## Expected

An intentionally aborted run (or any run older than the worker's latest `working:` status or newer commits) should not count as the current state. The busy verdict, or the newer status, should count as positive work evidence so that bare turn-ends are absorbed.

## Workaround

`config/turnend-churn-absorb` (opt-in pane-churn evidence) reduces the noise.

## Environment

Firstmate at f6180a0, primary omp, workers omp on the hc backend, delivery mode no-mistakes.

title: fm-promote.sh prints the next: fm-send command with a wrong fm- task id prefix
body:
## What happened

After a successful scout promotion, `bin/fm-promote.sh` prints a `next:` command with a wrong task id:

```
next: FM_HOME=... bin/fm-send.sh fm-<task-id> "$(cat ...)"
```

The task id has no `fm-` prefix (the branch is `fm/<task-id>`). Copying the command sends to a task that does not exist.

## Where

`bin/fm-promote.sh` at f6180a0:

```
echo "next: FM_HOME=$HOME_Q bin/fm-send.sh fm-$ID \"\$(cat $INSTRUCTIONS_Q)\""
```

## Expected

`bin/fm-send.sh $ID ...` (the real task id).

title: PR-merge poll and contributions check: a stalled forge read times out the whole check and raises a spurious wake
body:
## Behavior

When a forge read stalls (flaky network, a hung TLS connection), `gh` and `glab` can hold for about a minute before their own client gives up.
The watcher's per-check bound (`FM_CHECK_TIMEOUT`, default 30s) then kills the whole check, and supervision gets a `<id>.check.sh: timed out after 30s` wake.

Two checks hit this:

- **PR-merge poll (`bin/fm-pr-poll.sh`).** The GitHub `gh pr view`, the GitLab `glab mr view` and merge-train car reads, the Gerrit `gerrit-axi show`, and the Gitea `tea api` read are all unbounded; only the GitLab detail reads carry their own 5s cap. One stalled read takes the whole poll to the watcher's kill, so each transient stall becomes a supervision wake even though the next sweep usually succeeds.
- **Contributions check (`bin/fm-contributions.sh`).** `poll()` waits on the observation lock without a bound, and the forge-read deadline starts only after the lock is held, so a held lock or a slow pre-read phase pushes the run past the watcher bound. This overlaps #8482, which covers the unbudgeted fixed overhead around the reads.

## Ask

- Give every PR-poll forge read one shared deadline inside `FM_CHECK_TIMEOUT`; a read cut at that deadline reports an explicit "unreachable" result instead of being killed by the watcher.
- Have the watcher retry an unreachable poll quietly and wake once, only after N consecutive unreachable polls; any other result ends the streak, and teardown removes the counter.
- When optional GitLab enrichment (job details, the train-list confirmation) times out, keep an already-known result (failed pipeline, confirmed train drop) rather than turning it into unreachable.
- In the contributions poll, measure the forge-read deadline from the poll's start, bound the lock wait to what is left after the read budget, skip a sweep silently when the lock stays held, and report once after N consecutive lock-busy polls.

## Feasibility

All local to `bin/fm-pr-poll.sh`, `bin/fm-pr-lib.sh` (streak counter and threshold), the watcher's PR-poll branch, `bin/fm-contributions.sh`, and teardown's poll-artifact cleanup.
The perl fork-and-kill process-group bound the GitLab detail reads already use generalizes to every read (Go CLIs ignore SIGALRM), and `fm_lock_acquire_wait_max` already exists for the bounded lock wait.
FIFO-backed fake forge CLIs in `tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh` and `tests/fm-contributions.test.sh` can demonstrate a stalled read deterministically.

title: fix: bound watcher polling and suppress transient timeout wakes
body:
## Intent

Contribute the fork's PR-poll timeout fix upstream to kunchenguid/firstmate (approved option b): the fork merged it as https://github.com/ironerumi/firstmate/pull/140 ("fix: bound watcher polling and suppress transient timeout wakes"). It bounds stalled gh reads in the PR-merge poll and the contributions check, so a hung forge read no longer times the whole check out and raises a spurious timeout wake.

What that fork PR did: bound forge reads to a shared PR-poll deadline, preserving known GitLab degradation results when optional enrichment times out; bound contributions observation-lock waits and notify once after three consecutive lock-busy or PR-read-timeout polls, resetting each streak on recovery; add regression coverage for stalled reads, lock contention, persistent-outage notifications, and teardown cleanup; update watcher documentation.

## What Changed
- Bound PR-poll forge reads to a shared deadline and contributions lock waits to the check budget, preserving known GitLab degradation results when optional enrichment times out.
- Suppress transient timeout and lock-contention wakes; notify once after three consecutive affected polls, reset streaks on recovery, and remove PR timeout state at teardown.
- Add regression coverage for stalled reads, lock contention, outage notifications, recovery, and cleanup; update watcher documentation.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The bounded polling and outage counters are narrowly scoped, preserve existing forge-result semantics, and incorporate the previously requested fixes without a substantiated remaining material defect.

## Testing

Inspected the change, passed focused regressions, and drove real polling, watcher, contribution, and teardown interfaces against disposable local records using real gh/glab. Retained CLI transcripts and request evidence; all children and fixtures were cleaned up. No full suite or lint ran.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 7 of 7 scenarios driven live against the product

title: Operational-inbox path check rejects non-ASCII firstmate home paths
body:
## Symptom

Launching a Claude ship or scout fails with `could not publish the launch brief` when the firstmate home directory path contains non-ASCII characters (for example, a UTF-8 directory name).

## Reproduction

1. Put a firstmate home under a path with non-ASCII characters, e.g. `/home/user/Работа/firstmate`.
2. Dispatch a Claude ship or scout.
3. The spawn fails at launch-brief publication.

## Cause

`bin/fm-operational-input.sh` validates the operational-inbox path under `LC_ALL=C` with `*[![:print:]]*`. Under the C locale every byte >= 0x80 is non-printable, so any path containing a multi-byte UTF-8 character is rejected even though it is a valid path with no control characters.

## Proposed fix

Reject only control characters and the single quote (which the doorbell line uses as a delimiter), using `*[[:cntrl:]]*` in both the record writer and the doorbell parser. Add a regression test covering a non-ASCII home path (it must carry and parse its doorbell) and a control-character path (it must still be refused).

## Possible follow-up

Other places that use the same printable-only check, such as `bin/fm-task-inbox-lib.sh`, may have the same problem. They were left unchanged here because they do not break this launch path; this can be audited separately.

title: Stale and signal branch wakes for hc windows do not name their task
body:
## Symptom

A stale or signal supervision wake for an hc window (`session:terminal`, for example `default:t22`) is handed to the supervision branch with only the raw endpoint.
The branch then has to match that endpoint to a task itself, and it can wrongly conclude that the endpoint has no owner even though the task record carries that window.

## Reproduction

1. Create a task metadata file with `backend=hc`, `hc_session=default`, and `hc_terminal=t22`.
2. Append a `stale: default:t22 (no output for 300s)` wake row for that window.
3. Run the branch dispatch `scope` command, then `wake-prompt` for the same stale message.
4. Observe that the scope resolves the task, but the wake prompt carries only the raw endpoint string and no task line.

## Cause

The branch wake prompt is built from the message alone.
The task resolution already exists in the scope's task index, but it is not passed into the prompt for `signal:` and `stale:` rows.

## Proposed fix

Resolve each signal or stale wake key through the scope's task index, and add a `Task for this wake: <task ids>` line to the wake prompt on both the Pi and off-Pi entries.
The same key resolution is shared with the eligibility offer, so the two stay consistent.

## Related proposal (not in the linked PR)

A ship worker's `done:` status line is currently treated by the supervision branch as a completion event.
For a no-mistakes ship brief, the first `done:` is intentionally the handoff that starts the validation pipeline, so a worker that reports it before a PR exists is not idle.
A possible rule is to report such a `done:` as delivered only when its delivery target is present (a PR URL for no-mistakes and direct-PR, a ready branch for local-only), and otherwise to check the current state and steer the worker onward only when it has stopped with no active run and no PR.
This overlaps with #1033 ("No-mistakes ship briefs instruct workers to report done before validation") and #7118 ("Keep validated ship work in publication state until a PR exists"), and it needs a maintainer decision on the exact handoff contract before it is implemented.

Under `LC_ALL=C` the check treated every byte at or above 0x80 as non-printable, so a Claude ship or scout spawn from such a home failed with `could not publish the launch brief`. The check now rejects only control characters and single quotes, a regression test covers a non-ASCII home path, and a path with control characters is still refused. Fixes #8679. ## What Changed - The operational-input doorbell path checks in `bin/fm-operational-input.sh` (record write and doorbell path parse) and the Calm mod mirror in `.claude/mods/firstmate-calm/lib/fm-operational-input.ts` now reject only control characters and single quotes. title: fix(bin): name the task on stale and signal branch wakes
body:
## Intent Fix supervision-branch wakes for hc (Herdr desktop) tasks. A `stale:` or `signal:` wake names its endpoint, and the branch session had to map that endpoint to a task itself; for an hc address such as `default:t22` it concluded the endpoint belonged to no task, although the task record names that window, so a stalled hc worker was reported as untracked and left idle. The wake prompt now carries the resolved task id for signal and stale wakes, on both the Pi and off-Pi entries, so the branch no longer depends on matching the endpoint string. Closes #8680. ## What Changed - Added `wakeTriggerKeys` and `wakeTaskLine` to `.pi/extensions/lib/fm-branch-dispatch.ts`. They resolve a signal or stale wake's trigger keys to task ids through the scope's `taskByWakeKey` index. `branchOfferForWake` now reuses `wakeTriggerKeys` instead of its own inline copy. `branchWakePrompt` takes an optional `taskLine` and, when it is non-empty, adds a `Task for this wake: ` line after the wake message. - Passed that task line into the wake prompt in both hosts: the Pi extension (`.pi/extensions/fm-branch-supervision.ts`) and the off-Pi `bin/fm-branch-dispatch.mjs` prompt command. The branch no longer has to match the endpoint string to a task itself. - Documented the new line in `docs/supervision-host.md` and added a case to `tests/fm-supervision-host-drain.test.sh`. Closes `#8680` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: This is a small, well-bounded change. It moves trigger-key parsing into one shared helper without changing behaviour, and adds an informational task line to the wake prompt built from the existing read-only scope index. If the task can't be resolved, the line is simply left out (the prompt doesn't fail), and the new test drives the real CLI. ## Testing I ran the targeted host-drain test file, which passed in full, and drove the real dispatch entry (`node bin/fm-branch-dispatch.mjs`) against disposable homes. A stale wake for `default:t22` resolved to `demo-hc` in the scope output and added `Task for this wake: demo-hc` to the prompt. A signal wake naming `demo-hc.status` did the same. A stale wake for an unknown endpoint and a heartbeat produced no task line. title: hc backend: add an opt-in read-only no-mistakes pipeline monitor tab
body:
## Symptom

On the hc runtime backend, a task has no way to show the progress of its no-mistakes pipeline run in the Herdr desktop app.
Users who want to watch a run must attach to it manually.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a firstmate home with the hc backend.
2. Start a ship task whose worktree is `/example/worktrees/task-a`.
3. Start a no-mistakes run on that branch.
4. Observe that no monitor tab showing the run appears in the task's Herdr space.

## Cause

Pipeline monitoring for hc tasks is not implemented, so nothing opens a view of the active run.

## Proposed fix

Add a read-only pipeline monitor for hc tasks, opt-in through a presence flag at `config/hc-pipeline-monitor`, off by default.
When the flag is present and a task has an active no-mistakes run, open one tab named `<task> pipeline monitor` in the task's Herdr space, running `no-mistakes attach --run <run-id>`.
A newer run replaces the tab, and task teardown closes it.
The monitor never receives input and never carries the worker's labels.

title: feat(watch): surface and clean up finished records
body:
## What Changed

Finished work now gets a cleanup owner from disk instead of from a supervisor happening to notice it.
Every watcher heartbeat, in both postures, runs a finished-work review (`bin/fm-finished-record-lib.sh`) over this home's task records.
A record counts as finished when one of these holds:

- **merged** - its recorded `pr=` has the merge-notified record that every merge path writes through `bin/fm-merge-outcome-lib.sh` (`bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` and the merge poll alike), and that record is older than a grace period (default one hour);
- **dead** - its newest crew report is `done:` or `failed:`, the log is older than the grace, and the endpoint's agent reads `dead` or `missing`;
- **unattended** - its newest crew report is `done:` or `failed:` and the log has had no newer status for a day.

The review skips persistent second mates, lanes parked on review or with a pending merged-lane cleanup request, records whose latest event is `captain-held`, and - for the two terminal conditions - records whose merge poll is still armed, because that poll owns a PR awaiting merge.

For each finished record it either raises one `check: finished work: <id> - <why>; clean up with bin/fm-teardown.sh <id>, which refuses unlanded work` notification, or, behind an opt-in, starts the same detached `bin/fm-park.sh land` cleanup the merge poll starts for merged lanes.
The fact it acted on (the merged PR, or the terminal status line) is recorded only after the action is durable, so the same fact never notifies or acts twice, a failure retries next heartbeat, and a new fact on the same record is handled once more.

The review's note about alternating facts does not arise in practice: once a record's current `pr=` has its merge-notified record, the merged condition holds for as long as the record exists, so the terminal condition is reached again only if the record moves to a different PR, which is a genuinely new fact.

## Contract class (split, as triaged)

1. **New default:** counting merged or finished records as actionable in the fleet review.
   It is a new wake reason on the always-on heartbeat and reads only local files plus one endpoint liveness read per terminal candidate.
   It needs no forge read: every merge path already writes the merge-notified record, and a PR merged with no such record is still caught by the terminal conditions.
2. **Opt-in:** running the cleanup automatically.
   A merged record follows the existing `config/auto-land`.
   A finished record without a PR follows the new default-off `config/auto-clean-finished`, and only when its agent is gone or idle, no steering message is waiting, and the record is local.

## How each maintainer constraint is met

- **One notification per record, not a recurring nag:** one `check: finished work:` row per record and fact, keyed `finished-<id>`; an unchanged fact never re-notifies, and the heartbeat backs off as before when nothing is new.
- **Automatic cleanup only behind config:** with neither flag present nothing is ever torn down; the review only notifies.
- **Every teardown refusal stays exactly as it is, never forced:** the cleanup is `bin/fm-park.sh land`, which runs `bin/fm-teardown.sh <id>` without `--force`.
  Unlanded work, a dirty copy, a missing scout report, and the captain-call completion gate all refuse exactly as before.
  `land` additionally refuses to touch a record without a PR whose newest crew line is no longer `done:` or `failed:` (a non-terminal record).
- **A refusal is a finding:** the tick reports `cleanup-refused <id>: finished record; automatic cleanup refused: <reason>` once, and the review never retries that fact.
- **Scripts own the mechanics; restart is a non-event:** all conditions are exact file and endpoint checks, and the handled facts live in `state/.finished-records-surfaced`, so a restarted watcher neither loses nor repeats them.
- **Unlanded work is never torn down:** unchanged teardown gates; the review adds no new teardown path.

## Tests

- `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` drives the real watcher: merged and unattended records each notify once with their cleanup command, an unchanged fact stays silent on the next heartbeat, a new terminal report is a new fact, and records inside the grace, with an armed merge poll, second mates, captain-held records, and working records are skipped; a record whose agent is gone notifies; with both opt-ins the merged and finished records are cleaned up through plain teardowns, a refused teardown is reported and neither retried nor forced, and a record with a waiting steering message only notifies.
- `tests/fm-park.test.sh` covers `land` for a record without a PR: no action without `config/auto-clean-finished`, no teardown once the record reports working again, the refusal wording, and the cleanup wording.

## Live evidence

End-to-end drive in a throwaway second mate home (parent binding to a throwaway parent home), with real git worktrees and a pushed remote, a private tmux server, and the real scripts: the merge outcome recorder, `bin/fm-watch.sh`, `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh`, `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh`, `bin/fm-park.sh`, and `bin/fm-teardown.sh`.
Only the worktree-pool tool was stubbed (it logs the return), so nothing touched a real pool, and the merge itself is recorded with the same `fm_merge_outcome_report ... self` call `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` makes after the forge accepts a merge.

```
=== The mate merges ship1's PR (merge outcome recorded exactly as bin/fm-pr-merge.sh does)
parent channel now holds:
done [key=merged-ship1] [at=…]: merged ship1 https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8399
mate's own wake queue rows for the merge:
0

=== Baseline: before the grace passes, a heartbeat queues no finished-work row (the ordinary handling owns it)
watcher woke with:

(no finished-work or merge rows)

=== After the grace: one heartbeat names both records and their cleanup command
watcher woke with:
check: finished work: scout1 - its last report is done: and its agent is gone (missing); clean up with bin/fm-teardown.sh scout1, which refuses unlanded work; finished work: ship1 - PR https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8399 is merged and its record is still present; clean up with bin/fm-teardown.sh ship1, which refuses unlanded work

=== Next heartbeat: the same facts never notify again
(watcher still polling after 30s: no wake)

(watcher still polling after 30s: no wake)

records left: scout1.meta scout3.meta ship1.meta

=== Next heartbeat: the refused scout3 is neither retried nor forced
(watcher still polling after 30s: no wake)
tick output (empty means nothing new to report):
pending cleanup requests: none
```

<!-- no-mistakes-pr-appendix:v1 sha256=fbf24cb573c7e6c4e7045e3fc872703a3216aecad37f049c57fc520ac1b63ed7 -->
## Intent

Upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8656, filed from the captain's account and labelled ready-for-pr by the maintainer; the captain's standing rule is that a maintainer's acceptance is consent to open that one PR and raise it once green.

Issue text:
Line numbers refer to 427056c4.

## Observed

1. In a second mate home, a merge performed by `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` raises no local notification. `fm_merge_outcome_report` queues `check: merge landed` only for a poll-observed merge or a main home (`bin/fm-merge-outcome-lib.sh:103-104`). The watcher then discards the poll result as a duplicate. With `config/auto-land` the watcher cleans up anyway; without it, the merged worker stays until a supervisor happens to look.
2. A finished scout, or a ship without a PR, has no automatic cleanup at all. On one installation two finished scouts sat 12 days with dead agents.
3. The periodic fleet review is discarded when no new captain-relevant status line exists (`heartbeat_scan_finds_actionable`), so it does not catch either case.

Measured on one installation over about 30 days across several second mate homes: roughly 17,700 handled notifications, of which 0 were merge notifications and 18 were fleet reviews.

## Expected

Finished work, merged or terminal, reaches someone who cleans it up without relying on a supervisor noticing it.

## Smallest change

Let the fleet review also count as actionable when any record meets one of these, each evaluated from files and one bounded forge read: its PR is merged and the record still exists; its last line is terminal and older than N hours; its agent is dead and its last line is terminal. Then either raise one notification that names the record and the cleanup command, or, behind an opt-in setting, run the same detached cleanup that `fm-park.sh land` runs for merged lanes, with every cleanup gate unchanged.

Maintainer acceptance comment (constraints the PR must honour):
Speaking as Kun's firstmate: thanks @Dematom1. The measurements make the gap clear, and I could confirm it on main `427056c4`.

**What I checked:**
- `fm_merge_outcome_report` (`bin/fm-merge-outcome-lib.sh:103-104`) queues the local `check: merge landed` wake only when the merge was seen by a poll or there is no parent destination. A merge performed by `fm-pr-merge.sh` in a second mate home only goes to the parent channel.
- `heartbeat_scan_finds_actionable` (`bin/fm-watch.sh:3580`) counts only captain-relevant status events, so a finished scout or a ship without a PR never trips it.

**Contract-class: split.**
1. Counting finished or merged records as actionable in the fleet review is **new-default**: a new wake reason on the always-on heartbeat, plus one bounded forge read.
2. Running the cleanup automatically is **opt-in**, behind a setting like `config/auto-land`.

**VISION.md, rule by rule:**
- One captain, one interface: aligns, as long as it's one notification per record and not a recurring nag.
- Authority: aligns only behind config for the automatic cleanup. Discarding work needs an explicit grant, so every teardown refusal (unlanded work, a dirty copy) must stay exactly as it is. A refusal is a finding, and must never be forced.
- Scripts own the mechanics: aligns. All three conditions are exact file and forge checks.
- Restart is a non-event: aligns. Finished records get an owner from disk, not from someone remembering.
- Delegation with a spine: aligns. "Unlanded work is never torn down" stays binding.
- Vendor: aligns.
- Scope: aligns.

Labelled `ready-for-pr`. Nothing is waiting on you.

title: feat(bin): add opt-in read-only no-mistakes pipeline monitor for hc tasks
body:
## Intent Add an opt-in, read-only no-mistakes pipeline monitor for hc-backed tasks, so the progress of a task's active no-mistakes run is visible in the Herdr desktop app. When the presence flag config/hc-pipeline-monitor exists, the observe pass opens one Herdr tab per task, named " pipeline monitor", in the task's space, running "no-mistakes attach --run ". A newer run id replaces that tab, and task teardown closes it. The flag is off by default, so existing homes see no change. The monitor never receives input and never carries the worker's task label. The change is documented in docs/configuration.md and linked from docs/hc-backend.md, and the monitor test covers the disabled case. Fixes `#8683`. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-hc-pipeline-monitor.sh` with `observe` and `close` subcommands. When the `config/hc-pipeline-monitor` presence flag exists, `observe` opens one Herdr tab per hc task, named for the task with a "pipeline monitor" suffix, in the task's space. The tab runs `no-mistakes attach --run ` for the task's active run, and a newer run id replaces it. With the flag absent, `observe` opens nothing. `fm-watch.sh` runs the observe pass for every `backend=hc` task on each poll. A failure is only logged and never wakes firstmate. `fm-teardown.sh` closes the monitor for hc tasks; a close failure prints a warning and does not block cleanup. - Documented the flag in `docs/configuration.md`, linked it from `docs/hc-backend.md`, and added the script to the `docs/scripts.md` inventory. - Added `tests/fm-hc-pipeline-monitor.test.sh`, which includes the disabled-flag case. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is opt-in and off by default. The fix round now reads the space from the worker terminal's herdr.space label and falls back to the spawn default. It also reports a failed listing or a failed rm, so the monitor record is kept instead of silently dropped. The docs match the real tab label and the teardown ordering. The new tests exercise the real CLI against a fake hc and would catch a regression to the env-only space or to swallowed failures. ## Testing I ran the focused monitor test (10/10 pass). I then drove the real bin/fm-hc-pipeline-monitor.sh and bin/fm-watch.sh against a real herdr-core 0.1.22 in an isolated fm-hclab session, with a fake no-mistakes on PATH. Without the flag nothing opens. With it, one monitor tab opens in the worker's actual space, running `no-mistakes attach --run <id>`, with no worker label. Re-observing the same run changes nothing, a newer run replaces the monitor, a completed run is left alone, and close removes only the owned monitor. Close reports failures when the listing or the removal fails, and observe refuses to open a second monitor when it cannot list. The watcher opened a monitor on its own in a lab home. The lab teardown could not remove its session directory: the helper's fleet-state tripwire fired because the operator's default core was changing concurrently. My commands were all pinned to the lab socket and no lab processes remain, but the lab directory under /tmp/fm-hc-lab-1000 is still there. - Live validation: ✅ go - 6 of 7 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Flag absent: observe opens no monitor (real hc lab) | ✅ pass | live | pipeline-monitor-live-transcript.txt | | Flag present: one read-only monitor tab in the worker's space running attach --run, no worker label (real hc lab) | ✅ pass | live | pipeline-monitor-live-transcript.txt | | Same run re-observed is idempotent; newer run replaces; completed run is ignored | ✅ pass | live | pipeline-monitor-live-transcript.txt | | Teardown close removes only the owned monitor; foreign worker-label terminal and other-home monitor survive | ✅ pass | live | pipeline-monitor-live-transcript.txt | | Close failure reporting: ls or rm failure makes close exit 1 and keep the record; observe refuses a second monitor when it cannot list | ✅ pass | live | pipeline-monitor-live-transcript.txt | | Watcher integration: fm-watch.sh in a lab home with the flag opens the monitor | ✅ pass | live | watcher-live.out | | fm-teardown.sh end-to-end close warning and the docs change | ⏸️ untested | no | Not run through a real fm-teardown.sh in the time budget; the close command it calls was exercised live, and the docs are static text. |
Evidence: Live transcript summary Source: [Live transcript summary](https://github.com/killthistinker/firstmate/blob/7aca87af41228584167da03b059a589aa70ebdc0/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-up-hc-pipeline-monitor/pipeline-monitor-live-transcript.txt) ```text Real herdr-core (hc 0.1.22) in fm-hclab-* lab session, real bin/fm-hc-pipeline-monitor.sh and bin/fm-watch.sh; fake no-mistakes (status + attach) on PATH. - no flag: observe rc=0, terminals [t1(worker)] only - flag on: observe opens t2 labels {firstmate.monitor=fm-t1, firstmate.home=, herdr.space=proj-x (worker's actual space), herdr.tab="-t1 pipeline monitor"}, argv no-mistakes attach --run run-A, no firstmate.task - re-observe same run x2: terminals unchanged - run-B: old monitor closed, new one argv attach --run run-B, exactly one monitor - run-B completed: no change - close t1: only monitor removed; foreign worker-label terminal and other-home monitor survive - ls failing: close rc=1 "could not list pipeline monitors", record kept; rm failing: rc=1 "could not close"; observe with ls failing refuses to open a second monitor - fm-watch.sh in lab home with flag: opened monitor t9 attach --run run-W in proj-x, record .hc-monitor-t1 written ```
Evidence: Watcher output Source: [Watcher output](https://github.com/killthistinker/firstmate/blob/7aca87af41228584167da03b059a589aa70ebdc0/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-up-hc-pipeline-monitor/watcher-live.out) ```text Завершено sleep "$POLL" ```

✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ⚠️ `bin/fm-hc-pipeline-monitor.sh:133` - The intent says the monitor tab opens "in the task's space". The code instead recomputes the space as `${FM_HC_SPACE:-fm-$home}` from the watcher's own environment. The worker's space is set by fm-spawn from its environment (bin/backends/hc.sh:293) and is not saved in the task meta. Concrete case: the captain spawns a task with FM_HC_SPACE=proj-x, but the long-running watcher was started without it. The monitor then lands in space fm-<hometag>, away from the worker tab, and nothing reports an error. Fix: read the worker terminal's actual `herdr.space` label (`hc get --json <hc_terminal>` using the meta's hc_terminal), the same way monitor_terminal_owned already reads labels, and fall back to the env default only when that label is missing. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-hc-pipeline-monitor.sh:69` - monitor_list throws away the exit status of `hc ls`, so a failed listing looks the same as "no monitors". monitor_close_all also ignores failures from `hc kill`/`hc rm` (lines 86-87, `|| true`). Concrete case: at teardown the hc core is briefly unreachable, so `ls` fails. cmd_close then returns 0 and deletes the .hc-monitor record (lines 150-152). fm-teardown.sh:4151 never prints its "could not be closed" warning, and the monitor terminal is orphaned without any notice, which breaks the documented promise that a monitor that could not be closed is reported. The same gap reaches observe (line 130): if `ls` fails while the record's `hc get` also fails, close_all returns success and a second monitor opens while the first still exists. Fix: make monitor_list return non-zero when `hc ls` or jq fails, and count a failed `rm` (or a terminal still listed afterwards) as a failure in monitor_close_all. - ℹ️ `docs/configuration.md:187` - The docs (and the intent) name the tab `<task> pipeline monitor`. monitor_tab (bin/fm-hc-pipeline-monitor.sh:57) actually produces `<hometag>-<task> pipeline monitor`, for example `firstmate-ab12cd-t1 pipeline monitor`. That follows the hc convention of scoping tab labels by home (the worker tab is `<hometag>-fm-<id>`, docs/hc-backend.md:73), but the configuration doc should state the real label so users can find the tab. Separately, the script header (line 7) says teardown calls close "before the worker close", but fm-teardown.sh:4148 calls it after fm_backend_kill and after the worktree is returned. - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:4064` - With the flag on, every watcher poll runs `no-mistakes axi status` (5s timeout, plus up to 5s for the optional home resolver) and an `hc get` once per hc task, one task after another, in the main loop before the wait. In the default-off case the cost is one small subprocess per hc task. With the flag on and many hc tasks, a slow daemon can stretch each cycle by about 5–10s per task and delay wake detection. Acceptable for an opt-in feature; noted as a tradeoff. 🔧 Fix applied. 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:4064` - With the flag on, every watcher poll runs `no-mistakes axi status` (5s timeout, plus up to 5s for the optional home resolver) and an `hc get` once per hc task, one task after another, in the main loop before the wait. Acceptable for an opt-in feature; noted as a tradeoff.

title: A held call in a secondmate home publishes its own decision key, so the mate's own decision line for the same call stays open after the answer
body:
## Observed

In a secondmate home, `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh hold <task>` publishes `needs-decision [key=captain-hold-<task>-<n>]` on the parent channel (`publish_parent_hold`, `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh` lines 287-300 on `427056c4`).
The key is always derived from the task id and an occurrence count.
The command has no way to publish under a key that already exists.

The same call often already has a keyed decision line: the mate's own `needs-decision [key=<slug>]: ...` on its status log or parent channel, written when it first met the question.
The two records share no key and no recorded link.
`answer` and `answers` close only `captain-hold-<task>-<n>`.
The `<slug>` line stays open in OPEN DECISIONS until someone writes `resolved [key=<slug>]` by hand or names that key in `fm-send --resolve-key`.

The docs accept this shape.
`docs/captain-hold-lifecycle.md` ("Record divergence") says a call "can have two records, and closing one does not close the other."
`bin/fm-captain-hold.sh diverged` reports only the reverse case, a status key closed while its held task stays open.
`docs/secondmate-parent-channel.md` line 39 says "A duplicate line is harmless and a missed one is not, so the mate may still append its own judgement about a delivered outcome".
For a `needs-decision` line, the duplicate is not harmless: it is a second open decision that the answer does not close.

## Expected

One operator call is one open decision.
Answering it through any supported path closes every record the parent reads for that call.

## Consequence

An answered call keeps showing as owed in OPEN DECISIONS and in any list built from it.
The operator is asked again about a settled question, or the supervisor has to find and close the twin key by hand.
Name matching cannot repair this after the fact, because nothing records which status key a held task stands for.

## How to verify a fix

1. In a secondmate home, write `needs-decision [key=api-shape]: REST or gRPC?` to the mate's parent channel, then hold a task for the same question.
2. Answer the held task with `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh answer <task> --decision-file <path>`.
3. Check the parent's OPEN DECISIONS: no open decision for this call should remain.

title: A keyed decision about a pull request stays open after that pull request merges
body:
## Observed

A secondmate often relays a pull request to its parent as a keyed decision, for example `needs-decision [key=pr1234-ready]: PR https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/1234 is ready to merge`.
When that pull request merges, nothing closes the key.

On `427056c4`, none of the paths that see a merge writes a `resolved [key=...]` line: `bin/fm-pr-poll.sh`, `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh`, `bin/fm-teardown.sh`, `bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh` and `bin/fm-contributions.sh` contain no such write.
https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8368 (closed by https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8422) added opt-in settlement of a task held for the operator when its pull request merges or closes.
That settles the held task only.
A keyed `needs-decision` or `blocked` line about the same pull request is a separate record in the status-log fold, and it stays open.

## Expected

Once the pull request a decision asks about has merged or closed, that decision no longer reads as owed, or it is presented with the merge as a fact.

## Consequence

OPEN DECISIONS keeps listing a merge question for a pull request that has already merged.
A supervisor that builds its questions from that list asks the operator to approve a merge that already happened.

## How to verify a fix

1. In a secondmate home, publish `needs-decision [key=pr1-ready]: PR <url> ready to merge` on the parent channel for a task whose `pr=` is that URL.
2. Merge the pull request and let the merge poll report it.
3. Check the parent's OPEN DECISIONS: `pr1-ready` should no longer be listed as owed.

title: Entering away mode holds results that had already finished for the return brief
body:
## Observed

`/afk` entry (`.agents/skills/afk/SKILL.md` "Entering", steps 1-4 on `427056c4`) writes the away-posture record, starts the away session where needed, and announces the read-back.
It does not look at work that is already finished but not yet reported: unread status lines, a worker's ready pull request, or a completed investigation whose report has not been relayed.

Once the record exists, main is parked and the away session takes every wake.
`bin/fm-branch-prompt.sh` line 151 says outcomes with verdict `captain` then "remain unprocessed for the return brief".
So a result that finished a few minutes before `/afk` is presented only at the return.

## Expected

Results that are already finished when the operator types `/afk` are delivered in the entry reply, while the operator is still there to read them.

## Consequence

The operator leaves without a result that was ready, and may wait a whole away period for an answer that existed before they left.
A ready pull request can also sit unmerged for that period, because merge approval needs the operator.

## How to verify a fix

1. Let a worker write `done: PR <url> checks green` and do not handle the wake.
2. Type `/afk` with no words.
3. Check that the entry reply names that pull request as ready.

title: Relaunching a remote secondmate starts it on stale inherited local material
body:
## Observed

A remote secondmate that is relaunched through `bin/fm-remote-secondmate-relaunch.sh` starts its new agent on whatever inherited local material the parent last pushed to that host.
Changes the parent made since then to inherited items such as `data/captain-shared.md` or `config/crew-dispatch.json` do not reach the relaunched agent.

The host-side relaunch says the opposite.
`cmd_relaunch` in `bin/fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh` (around lines 358-370 on `427056c4`) runs the host-local relaunch with `FM_SKIP_SECONDMATE_INHERIT=1` and `FM_SKIP_SECONDMATE_SYNC=1`, and its comment states that "the parent already owns both convergence legs".
No caller of that verb performs either leg first:

- `bin/fm-remote-secondmate-relaunch.sh` runs `fm-on.sh <id> fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh relaunch ...` directly and then republishes the route record.
  It never calls `bin/fm-remote-inherit-push.sh`.
- `bin/fm-secondmate-restart.sh` (`restart_mate`, around line 168) calls that wrapper for every remote mate after `bin/fm-update.sh` has synced tracked files only.
- `bin/fm-update.sh` fast-forwards tracked files and does not propagate inherited local material.

The only senders of inherited material to a remote route are `bin/fm-spawn.sh` at a fresh launch (around line 1527), session-start bootstrap convergence (`bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` around line 696), and a manual `bin/fm-config-push.sh`.
`.agents/skills/secondmate-provisioning/SKILL.md` line 136 says a relaunched secondmate "already reads its files at launch", which is true only of the files already on the host.

## Expected

A relaunched remote secondmate starts on the parent's current inherited local material, the same as a freshly launched one, or the relaunch reports that it could not deliver it.

## Consequence

A restart run by an update, or a profile move documented in `secondmate-provisioning`, can leave a remote mate following an older shared preference file or dispatch configuration until the next session start or a manual push.
Nothing reports the difference, because the relaunch succeeds and the host-side comment treats the push as already done.

## How to verify a fix

1. Launch a remote secondmate, then change a line in the parent's `data/captain-shared.md` without running `bin/fm-config-push.sh`.
2. Relaunch the mate with `bin/fm-remote-secondmate-relaunch.sh <id> <harness> default default`.
3. Read `data/captain-shared.md` in the remote home: it should hold the changed line.
4. Repeat through `bin/fm-secondmate-restart.sh` for a remote mate.

title: The away supervision session never sees what main did while the operator was away
body:
## Observed

On a home that runs the supervision host, an attended wake carries the dialog mirror of main's conversation, and an away wake does not.
`bin/fm-supervision-host.sh` lines 1097-1110 on `427056c4` feed `bin/fm-host-mirror.sh` only when the turn posture is `attended`, with the comment "Away needs none, so an away wake never reads the mirror or moves its cursor."

Main does take turns while the away record exists: in the `/afk` turn itself when the operator gives away words, and on hand-backs such as a declined wake or a park boundary.
Anything main does or says in those turns stays invisible to the away session.

The away session also loses its own corrections.
The host opens a new engine conversation after `FM_SUPERVISION_HOST_ROTATE_TURNS` turns (default 20, line 242, used by `engine_record_resumable` around line 911).
The new conversation starts from the prompt alone, so an outcome the previous conversation recorded or corrected during the same away period is not in its context.

## Expected

The away session's view of the work in progress includes main's own actions during the away period and the outcomes already recorded since the record was written, including after a conversation rotation.

## Consequence

The away session reports work as not started, or as still waiting, after main has already done it.
Those reports become outcome rows with verdict `captain`, so the return brief and the operator receive statements that contradict what main said in chat.

## How to verify a fix

1. Enter away mode on a supervision-host home.
2. Hand a wake back to main and have main steer a worker or merge a pull request.
3. On the next away wake, check that the away session's outcome reflects main's action.
4. Force a conversation rotation with a low `FM_SUPERVISION_HOST_ROTATE_TURNS` and check that the new conversation does not contradict outcomes recorded earlier in the same away period.

title: Completing an investigation attests its open questions but not the work it recommends
body:
## Observed

`bin/fm-captain-hold.sh complete <origin-id> (--none | <task-id>...)` is the completion gate for an investigation, scout report or visual review (`.agents/skills/captain-hold-lifecycle/SKILL.md`, "Operating sequence").
It requires an explicit account of every open question for the operator: held task ids, or `--none` (`command_complete`, `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh` around lines 2099-2155 on `427056c4`).

It asks for no account of the other output of the same report: recommended changes that need no decision.
A report can end with a list of fixes to file or dispatch, and `complete --none` succeeds whether or not any of them became a backlog task.
The origin then reads as handled.

## Expected

Completing a report records what happened to each piece of work it recommends, the same way it already records each open question.

## Consequence

Recommended work that needs no decision has no durable owner after completion.
If the session that read the report is interrupted before filing that work, nothing shows that it was dropped, and the next report finds the same defects again.

## How to verify a fix

1. Write a scout report that recommends two fixes and raises no question for the operator.
2. Run `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh complete <origin> --none` before filing either fix.
3. Check that the completion records the two fixes as filed, or refuses until they are accounted for.

title: A declared wait on an outside party is rechecked every four hours, even when it is known to last days
body:
## Observed

Every `paused:` wait is rechecked on one cadence, `FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS` (default 14400 seconds, `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh` line 124 on `427056c4`).
A worker can name when its wait clears with `until <UTC ISO 8601>`, but `bin/fm-watch.sh` lines 14-16 state that "a declared time beyond FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS cannot extend the ordinary recheck cadence".
The same setting also paces other rechecks in `bin/fm-watch.sh`, so it cannot be raised for long waits without slowing those too.

A wait on a maintainer's review of an outside pull request routinely lasts days.
Each such worker is rechecked six times a day, and each recheck costs a supervisor turn that ends with no action.

## Expected

The recheck cadence for a declared wait can match how long that kind of wait lasts, without changing the cadence of unrelated rechecks.

## Consequence

A home with several workers waiting on outside reviewers spends a steady stream of supervisor turns on rechecks that find nothing.
In one home, nine such workers were reported to produce 79 rechecks in about 33 hours, and none was reported to lead to an action.

## How to verify a fix

1. Have a worker write `paused: waiting for maintainer review of <PR url> until <a date three days ahead>`.
2. Leave the watcher running for more than four hours.
3. Check that the worker is not resurfaced before the declared date, while a worker that declares no date keeps the current cadence.

Related: https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8373 (declared-wait state spread over several marker families) and https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8447 (bare turn-ends of a paused worker); neither changes the recheck cadence.

title: A secondmate's first turn after an outage does not show its unread steering messages
body:
## Observed

A steer to a secondmate is a durable record in its steering inbox plus a doorbell line typed into its terminal (`bin/fm-send.sh`).
If the mate's turn that receives the doorbell fails, for example during an API or sign-in outage, the doorbell is consumed and the record stays unread.
For a remote mate, `bin/fm-send.sh` lines 148-151 on `427056c4` state that "the remote host runs no re-ring ladder of its own" and leave the swallowed doorbell to the parent's pending-reply recovery.

When the mate's next good turn starts from its own wake, it runs `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh`.
The drain has no reference to the steering inbox, so it prints the wake rows, OPEN DECISIONS and UNREAD STATUS but nothing about unread steering records.
The mate goes on with its wake rows and does not read its orders until another doorbell arrives.

## Expected

The first drain a home runs shows that its steering inbox holds unhandled records, so the orders are read on the first good turn.

## Consequence

Orders that arrived during an outage wait until the parent's recovery re-rings or a new message arrives.
A time-bound request in that inbox, such as a request to save work before a restart, can expire unread.

## How to verify a fix

1. In a secondmate home, write a steering record to its inbox without ringing the doorbell.
2. Run `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh` in that home.
3. Check that the output names the unhandled record.

title: A Claude home whose every turn fails keeps re-waking itself every five minutes and tells its parent nothing
body:
## Observed

`bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh` is registered as both a Stop and a StopFailure hook.
After an error-ended turn it delivers one continuation per `FM_CLAUDE_STOPFAILURE_REWAKE_COOLDOWN` window, default 300 seconds (header lines 110-123 on `427056c4`).
Its header says the continuation is "delayed, never dropped, because after an error end it is the only thing that guarantees another hook firing".

That is right for a short API outage.
For a failure that cannot clear by itself, such as an expired sign-in, every continuation fails the same way and the hook schedules the next one.
The loop does not end, and no step of it writes to the home's parent channel, its status log, or any record another home reads.
In a secondmate home, the parent sees only that the mate stopped reporting.

The return brief's supervisor health line also stays green in this state.
It reports the beat of the parent's own watcher (`bin/fm-afk-return.sh`, the "Supervisor health" section), not whether each secondmate is still taking good turns.

## Expected

A home that cannot complete any turn makes that fact visible to whoever supervises it, within a bounded time, and stops spending continuations on a failure that will not clear without the operator.

## Consequence

In one deployment, a sign-in expired on a host that ran three secondmates under one account.
One mate was reported to fail 115 turns over about nine hours, while its parent channel stayed silent and the return brief reported no failures.
Orders sent to the mate in that period were not read until after the operator signed in again.

## How to verify a fix

1. Run a secondmate home on Claude with a sign-in that is revoked.
2. Ring it once so it attempts a turn.
3. Check that the parent receives one blocker naming the failed sign-in, and that the mate does not keep re-waking every five minutes.
4. Check that an ordinary transient API error still gets its continuation.

title: Recovery for an unanswered request to a remote secondmate waits on a read window that may never close empty
body:
## Observed

When a request to a remote secondmate gets no correlated reply, the parent's recovery treats the missing reply as evidence only after the reply channel has caught up.
`fm_pending_reply_missing_report_is_evidence` (`bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh` around lines 940-948 on `427056c4`) returns false for a remote target until the channel's `caught_up_epoch` is at or after the request time.

`bin/fm-procevent-remote-reply.sh` writes that watermark in one case only: a long-poll read window of `FM_REMOTE_REPLY_WAIT_SECONDS` (default 55) that closes with no new line (`WINDOW_CLOSED_EMPTY`, around line 330).
A window that the remote job worker preempts to run another job for the same home returns `JOB_PREEMPTED` and records no watermark (lines 308-315, 332-334).
The comment names the watcher's per-cycle liveness probe as one such job, and that probe runs every `FM_SECONDMATE_LIVENESS_SECS`, default 60 seconds (`bin/fm-watch.sh` line 453).
Any other remote job for the home during a window preempts it too.

So while windows keep being preempted, no watermark is written, the missing reply never counts as evidence, and the recovery and escalation for the request stay held.

## Expected

An unanswered request to a remote mate reaches recovery and escalation within a bounded time, even when the reply channel is busy or preempted.

## Consequence

In one deployment the watermark was reported not to advance for about 7 hours 46 minutes while a remote mate was failing every turn, so the request's repost and escalation were held for that whole time.
Why no window closed empty in that period was not determined.

## How to verify a fix

1. Send a correlated request to a remote secondmate that will not answer.
2. Keep the reply channel's read windows from closing empty, for example by running a remote job for that home more often than every 55 seconds.
3. Check that the request still reaches recovery and escalation within a bounded time.

title: Primary-only guards act inside ship and scout workers that run in a Firstmate worktree
body:
## Observed

Workers that work on the Firstmate repository itself run in linked worktrees of it, so they load its tracked Claude hooks and Pi extensions.
Several of those guards are meant only for the primary supervisor session, and they decide whether they are in the primary from environment variables that a ship or scout worker inherits.

`bin/fm-spawn.sh` (around lines 7739-7742 on `427056c4`) clears `FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE` and the other `*_OVERRIDE` variables only for a secondmate launch.
A ship or scout launch exports `FM_HOME` to the worker and leaves any `FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE` from the spawning environment in place.

Pi: `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-turnend-guard.ts` resolves the home as `process.env.FM_HOME || process.env.FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE || root` (line 20) and has no check that this session is the primary.
In a worker, `FM_HOME` is the supervising home, whose watcher lock belongs to another process, so the guard blocks the worker's turn end with the "TURN WOULD END BLIND" message.

Claude: `bin/fm-cd-pretool-check.sh`, `bin/fm-subagent-pretool-check.sh` and the other hooks that call `fm_primary_scope_matches` set `FM_ROOT=${FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE:-<script checkout>}`.
With an inherited `FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE` naming a plain checkout, the check passes inside a worker's linked worktree.

Reproduction in a scout worktree on `427056c4`, with `FM_HOME` set to the supervising home and `FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE` inherited from the spawning environment:

```
$ printf '%s' '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"cd /tmp"}}' | bin/fm-cd-pretool-check.sh --claude; echo rc=$?
{"hookSpecificOutput":{...,"permissionDecision":"deny"},"systemMessage":"[persistent-cd] a persistent top-level directory change in the primary firstmate checkout is blocked; ..."}
rc=2
$ printf '%s' '...same payload...' | env -u FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE bin/fm-cd-pretool-check.sh --claude; echo rc=$?
rc=0
$ bin/fm-subagent-pretool-check.sh --tool Agent; echo rc=$?
... "[subagent-dispatch] ..." ... (deny)
rc=2
$ env -u FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE bin/fm-subagent-pretool-check.sh --tool Agent; echo rc=$?
rc=0
```

The same scout session also ran the primary's full session-start digest at launch (`bin/fm-sessionstart-run.sh`, which uses the same scope check), reported "another live firstmate session holds the lock" for the supervising home, and printed the supervisor operating instructions into the worker's context.

## Expected

A guard written for the primary session stays inert in a ship or scout worker, whatever the worker inherited from the environment that spawned it.

## Consequence

Workers spend turns arguing with guard messages that do not apply to them.
A Pi worker's turn end is blocked repeatedly, and a Claude worker is refused ordinary actions such as its own subagent tools.
A scout stalled after reading a guard notice about another session's home lock.

## How to verify a fix

1. Spawn a Pi scout on the Firstmate repository from a home whose watcher runs.
2. Let the worker end a turn and check that no turn-end guard message reaches it.
3. Spawn a Claude scout from an environment that has `FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE` set, and check that the pretool hooks allow `cd` and the harness's subagent tool inside the worker.

title: The return brief prints every replaced away-words time as unknown and leaves out main's own actions under the words
body:
## Observed

Two parts of the return brief's account of the away words are wrong on `427056c4`.

1. Replacement time.
   When new `/afk` words replace earlier ones, the old record is archived as `<entered>-superseded-<epoch>.afk-contract` (`fm_afk_contract_archive_target`, `bin/fm-afk-contract.sh` around line 538).
   `render_return_brief` in `bin/fm-afk-return.sh` (lines 571-577) reads the epoch back with `stamp=${stamp%%-*}` before `stamp=${stamp%.afk-contract}`.
   The first step cuts at the hyphen inside `afk-contract`, so the stamp becomes `<epoch>.afk`, fails the digits check, and prints as `unknown`:

   ```
   $ since=1795186100; f=.../1795186100-superseded-1795228251.afk-contract
   $ stamp=${f##*/"$since"-superseded-}; stamp=${stamp%%-*}; stamp=${stamp%.afk-contract}; echo "$stamp"
   1795228251.afk
   ```

   Every replaced set of words is therefore shown as "superseded at unknown".

2. Actions under the words.
   `render_words_account` (line 504) lists only outcome-store rows whose summary starts with the away-action marker, which the away session writes.
   When main itself acts on the words, for example in the `/afk` turn or on a wake handed back to it, it writes no such row.
   The brief then says "the away session took no action under them", although work was done in the operator's name.

## Expected

The brief shows when each set of away words was replaced, and its account of actions taken under the words includes main's own actions.

## Consequence

The operator returns to a brief that hides when their instructions changed and states that nothing was done under them when something was.

## How to verify a fix

1. Enter `/afk` with words, then enter `/afk` again with different words.
2. Return and check that the brief prints the replacement time.
3. While away, have main act on the words, then return and check that the brief lists that action.

title: A child outcome line names one pull request in its text and another in its pr= field
body:
## Observed

When a task in a secondmate home ends, `bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh` relays a line such as `done [key=child-outcome-...]: child <id> done: PR <url-A> ... pr=<url-B>` to the parent channel (`report_child_ledger_locked`, around lines 545-575 on `427056c4`).
The `pr=` value comes from `pr_for_task` (around lines 500-530).
Unless the home has opted into `config/pr-register-scan`, it returns the task's recorded `pr=` metadata first and reads the URL from the terminal line only when no `pr=` is recorded.

A task that delivers more than one pull request, such as a dependency-update task that merges several in turn, keeps whichever URL was registered last in its metadata.
Its final line can then report one pull request in the text and another in `pr=`.

## Expected

The `pr=` field of a relayed outcome line names the pull request that line reports.

## Consequence

`.agents/skills/ship-landing/SKILL.md` and the supervision prompt tell the parent to copy pull request URLs from `pr=` rather than from prose.
Following that rule, the parent can send the operator a link to the wrong pull request, or arm a merge check on it.

## How to verify a fix

1. In a secondmate home, register a task's first pull request with `bin/fm-pr-check.sh <id> <url-A>`.
2. Have the task finish with `done: PR <url-B> checks green` for a second pull request.
3. Check that the relayed child outcome line carries `pr=<url-B>`.

title: A decision raised while the operator is away exists only as a return-brief row, never as a held task
body:
## Observed

While the away-posture record exists, the supervision session reports every event through `bin/fm-branch-report.sh` with a `routine` or `captain` verdict.
`bin/fm-branch-prompt.sh` (lines 115-120 on `427056c4`) tells it to report verdict `captain` for a decision only the operator can make, including ask-user findings, and line 151 says those outcomes "remain unprocessed for the return brief".
The posture rules (line 161) also send every sentence of the away words it cannot act on to the return brief with verdict `captain`.

That outcome row is the only record of the open decision.
No task is held for it through `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh hold`.
After the return, main reads the `BRANCH OUTCOMES` section and marks the rows processed with `bin/fm-branch-outcome.sh mark-processed`.
From then on, the question survives only in chat.

`.agents/skills/captain-hold-lifecycle/SKILL.md` makes a task held for the operator the durable record of an open call: Bearings lists it as an open call, `--until` defers it, `answer` closes it with the operator's words, and the completion gate checks it.
A decision raised while away reaches none of those surfaces.

## Expected

A decision that only the operator can make has the same durable record whether it arises while they are present or away, so it stays listed until it is answered, deferred or reconciled.

## Consequence

An away-time decision that is not answered in the first reply after return drops out of every list once the outcome rows are processed.
Bearings does not show it, the completion gate does not see it, and no reminder or `--until` date can apply to it.

## How to verify a fix

1. Enter away mode, then let the supervision session meet an event it must report with verdict `captain` because only the operator can decide it.
2. Return, read the brief, and process the outcome rows without answering the question.
3. Check that the decision is still listed by Bearings and by `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh` until it is answered or deferred.

title: fix(watch): recheck dead workers and support opt-in relaunch
body:
## What Changed Contract class: split, as the maintainer named it. Naming a dead agent in the declared-wait recheck is new-default; relaunching an ordinary worker is opt-in behind a home setting. - **Declared-wait recheck (new-default).** When `handle_paused_stale` is about to fire a `paused:` recheck for an ordinary worker, it reads `fm_backend_agent_state` once. A `dead` or `missing` verdict replaces "confirm the wait still holds" with `agent dead - , so the declared wait cannot clear on its own; reconcile this record, and check for unlanded work before any cleanup`. A live or inconclusive read keeps the existing wording. The read is paid only on a recheck that will actually fire (the gate is split out of `resurface_absorbed` as `resurface_due`), so ordinary polls cost nothing extra. Captain-held transfers (their agent stops on purpose) and second mates (owned by `secondmate_liveness_tick`) are not probed. - **Worker auto-relaunch (opt-in).** With `config/worker-auto-relaunch` present, a ship or scout whose agent reads `dead` or `missing` at the wedge threshold (`wedge_dead_record`) or at a declared-wait recheck is relaunched through the existing `bin/fm-control.sh relaunch` path with a progress note. Every gate must pass, or the unchanged dead-agent report is sent instead: - the record is a ship or scout; - the last status line is neither captain-relevant (terminal) nor a captain-held transfer, and the lane is not parked on review; - `git status --porcelain` in the recorded local copy is empty (dirty or unreadable means no relaunch); - the shared relaunch ledger (`fm_secondmate_liveness_recent_attempts`, `state/.secondmate-relaunch-`) holds fewer than `FM_SECONDMATE_LIVENESS_MAX_ATTEMPTS` attempts inside `FM_SECONDMATE_LIVENESS_WINDOW_SECS`. Each attempt is ledgered (`attempt`, then `relaunched` or `failed`) and reported as one `check: worker auto-relaunched ...` or `check: worker auto-relaunch failed ...: ` wake, bounded by `FM_SECONDMATE_LIVENESS_TIMEOUT`. Teardown already removes that ledger for every task kind. - Docs: `docs/configuration.md` gains a "Worker auto-relaunch" section, `docs/architecture.md` states the recheck behavior and points at the flag, and the operational-home-layout skill lists the new config file. ### How the maintainer's constraints are met - New-default part: one backend read per recheck that fires, through the backend-neutral `fm_backend_agent_state`, and new wording only when that read is `dead` or `missing`. - Opt-in part: nothing relaunches unless the home creates `config/worker-auto-relaunch`; absent, the watcher never relaunches an ordinary worker. - Clean-copy, non-terminal, and attempt-ledger gates are all enforced as listed above; a dirty copy is never relaunched over, and the relaunch keeps the same local copy, so committed but unlanded work stays where it is. - Reuses `bin/fm-control.sh relaunch` and its own refusals (for example a tmux endpoint it cannot prove stopped, or a recorded copy that is not an isolated task worktree); no new task shape. ### Tests - `tests/fm-watch-triage-pause.test.sh`: a dead and a missing agent are named in the recheck and a live agent keeps its wording; the relaunch runs only when opted in, refuses a dirty copy and a full ledger, ledgers each attempt, and reports a failed relaunch by its error line. Both tests fail on main. - `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh`: at the wedge threshold, a non-terminal dead worker is relaunched and a lane whose last line is terminal is reported, not relaunched. ### Live evidence Driven at this PR's head `ed23881c` in a throwaway home on an isolated tmux server with the real scripts; only the agent binary was a stand-in process. The ship was recorded in a git worktree with last line `paused: waiting on the vendor reply` aged past the recheck cadence, and its window's agent had exited (pane foreground a shell). 1. Default home, declared-wait recheck: `stale: fmdrive:fm-w1 (paused 605s, awaiting external - agent dead - the endpoint is still there with no agent running in it, so the declared wait cannot clear on its own; reconcile this record, and check for unlanded work before any cleanup)` On main the same recheck prints `... declared pause, rechecked on a long cadence not a wedge; confirm the wait still holds`. 2. `config/worker-auto-relaunch` on, untracked file in the local copy: the same agent-dead recheck, triage log `auto-relaunch skipped for w1 (local copy is dirty or unreadable)`, no ledger written, and the file left in place. 3. Flag on, clean local copy: `check: worker w1 auto-relaunched after agent dead (fmdrive:fm-w1)`; ledger `attempt`, `relaunched`; the same window now runs the replacement agent, and the instructions carry fm-control's progress note: `The watcher relaunched this task automatically because its previous agent was found dead (config/worker-auto-relaunch). Its last status line was: paused ...`. 4. Flag on, clean copy, replacement agent exits at once: `check: worker w1 auto-relaunch failed after agent dead: error: w1 was relaunched on grok but no running agent could be confirmed; its work is preserved at `; ledger adds `attempt`, `failed`. Out of scope: the away-mode daemon's own paused recheck wording (`bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh`) is unchanged. ## Intent Upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8657, filed from the captain's account and labelled ready-for-pr by the maintainer; the captain's standing rule is that a maintainer's acceptance is consent to open that one PR and raise it once green. Issue text: Line numbers refer to 427056c4. Related: #3545 (dead workers after a reboot reconciled as busy on one runtime) and #6880 (a destroyed endpoint is never reported). This issue covers the two parts those do not: the declared-wait recheck never checks liveness, and only second mates are ever relaunched. ## Observed 1. `wedge_dead_record` reports a dead or missing agent once per agent incarnation and discards every repeat ("reported once and not re-escalated while it stays that way"). 2. `handle_paused_stale` never checks whether the agent is alive ("it NEVER re-reads crew state"). After a host reboot, a worker in a declared wait is presented as "confirm the wait still holds". A supervisor answered exactly that 48 minutes after a reboot, with the worker's agent already gone. 3. Automatic relaunch exists only for second mates (`bin/fm-secondmate-liveness-lib.sh`). ## Expected A declared-wait recheck says when the agent behind the wait is dead, and an ordinary worker whose agent died mid-task can be brought back without a supervisor noticing first. ## Smallest change In the declared-wait recheck, read `fm_backend_agent_state` once per recheck and say "agent dead" in the notification text when it is. Add an opt-in setting that relaunches an ordinary worker through the existing `bin/fm-control.sh relaunch` path when its agent is dead, its last line is not terminal, and its copy is clean, bounded by the same attempt ledger second mates use. Maintainer acceptance comment (constraints the PR must honour): Speaking as Kun's firstmate: thanks @Dematom1. Both gaps are real on main `427056c4`, and separate from #3545 and #6880. **What I checked:** - `handle_paused_stale` (`bin/fm-watch.sh:2519-2591`) builds its "confirm the wait still holds" text from the status log alone. It never reads `fm_backend_agent_state`, and its own header says it "never re-reads crew state". - `wedge_dead_record` (1906-1927) reports a dead agent "once and not re-escalated". - The only automatic relaunch path is `bin/fm-secondmate-liveness-lib.sh`, which is for second mates only. **Contract-class: split.** 1. Naming a dead agent in the declared-wait recheck is **new-default**: a backend read on every recheck and new wording in the unconfigured notification. 2. Relaunching ordinary workers is **opt-in** only if it stays behind a home setting, as you proposed. **VISION.md, rule by rule:** - One captain, one interface: aligns. "Confirm the wait still holds" for a dead agent is a misleading notification. - Authority: aligns only behind config. Relaunching a worker is autonomy, so it has to be an explicit grant. Keep the clean-copy, non-terminal and attempt-ledger gates you listed, and never relaunch over unlanded or dirty work. - Scripts own the mechanics: aligns. The liveness read and the relaunch gates are exact checks. - Restart is a non-event: aligns directly. This is the reboot case. - Delegation with a spine: aligns. The relaunch reuses `bin/fm-control.sh relaunch` and adds no new task shape. - Vendor: aligns, as long as it goes through the backend-neutral `fm_backend_agent_state`. - Scope: aligns. Labelled `ready-for-pr`. Nothing is waiting on you. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The implementation matches the required default dead-agent recheck wording and opt-in, gated relaunch path; no material source defect or unnecessary introduced component was found. ## Testing Drove seven isolated live scenarios against the real watcher and relaunch flow; each passed, including dead/live agent wording, dirty-copy refusal, successful and failed relaunch, attempt bound, and terminal status. Captured scenario output; no transient worktree artifacts remain. - Live validation: ✅ go - 7 of 7 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Default declared-wait recheck identifies dead agent and removes misleading confirmation | ✅ pass | live | fm-8657-live-scenarios.txt | | Live worker declared-wait recheck preserves confirmation wording | ✅ pass | live | fm-8657-live-scenarios.txt | | Opt-in relaunch refuses dirty worker copy | ✅ pass | live | fm-8657-live-scenarios.txt | | Opt-in relaunch restores a clean dead worker | ✅ pass | live | fm-8657-live-scenarios.txt | | Failed replacement agent records failure and reports control error | ✅ pass | live | fm-8657-live-scenarios.txt | | Three-attempt ledger bound prevents further relaunch | ✅ pass | live | fm-8657-live-scenarios.txt | | Terminal task status is surfaced stale without relaunch | ✅ pass | live | fm-8657-live-scenarios.txt |
Evidence: Seven isolated live scenario outputs Source: [Seven isolated live scenario outputs](https://github.com/Dematom1/firstmate/blob/73f590be4923f85c141d8b6621c0928735e24535/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-8657-dead-wait-recheck/fm-8657-live-scenarios.txt) ```text $ bash .lab-live/fm-live-lab.sh "$PWD" dead-recheck wake: stale: fmlab:fm-w1 (paused 603s, awaiting external - agent dead - the endpoint is still there with no agent running in it, so the declared wait cannot clear on its own; reconcile this record, and check for unlanded work before any cleanup) SCENARIO dead-recheck PASS (24s): declared-wait recheck names the dead agent and drops 'confirm the wait still holds' $ bash .lab-live/fm-live-lab.sh "$PWD" live-recheck pane: sleep; wake: stale: fmlab:fm-w1 (paused 603s, awaiting external - declared pause, rechecked on a long cadence not a wedge; confirm the wait still holds) SCENARIO live-recheck PASS (55s): a live agent keeps 'confirm the wait still holds' and is never called dead $ bash .lab-live/fm-live-lab.sh "$PWD" dirty-copy wake: stale: fmlab:fm-w1 (paused 603s, awaiting external - agent dead - the endpoint is still there with no agent running in it, so the declared wait cannot clear on its own; reconcile this record, and check for unlanded work before any cleanup) SCENARIO dirty-copy PASS (28s): opt-in on + dirty copy: refused, dead-agent recheck kept, no ledger, file intact $ bash .lab-live/fm-live-lab.sh "$PWD" clean-relaunch wake: check: worker w1 auto-relaunched after agent dead (fmlab:fm-w1);
