title: fm-teardown.sh should refuse when the task's most recent merge attempt was refused
body:
### What happens

A supervisor ran a merge script and teardown in one chained command, with the merge output piped, for example:

```
bin/fm-merge-local.sh <task> ... | tail -n 5 && bin/fm-teardown.sh <task>
```

The merge script refused (for example, the local-only branch was no longer a fast-forward of the default branch). The pipe hid the non-zero exit, so `&&` went ahead and teardown ran. Teardown's landed-work check did not stop it, and the task was cleaned up: its task record and backlog item were closed as done while its commit had never reached the default branch. The commit survived only on its task branch, and the change had to be found and re-dispatched by hand as a new "land the finished fix" task.

The same pattern also occurred with `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` during an earlier stretch of about five days, where a refused merge was followed by teardown and the work sat orphaned until it was noticed.

In both cases the operator rule "run the merge script alone, confirm it reports merged, then run teardown; never chain or pipe them" was already written in the home's local notes. It recurred anyway, so a written rule is not enough; it needs a tool-side check.

### Expected

Teardown should know that the task's last merge attempt was refused and refuse cleanup on that basis, independent of how the commands were chained. For example:

- `fm-merge-local.sh` and `fm-pr-merge.sh` record the outcome of each attempt in task metadata (for example `last_merge_attempt=refused <epoch> <reason>` / `last_merge_attempt=merged <epoch>`).
- `fm-teardown.sh` refuses, with a message naming the refusal and its reason, when the most recent recorded attempt is `refused` and no later successful merge or landed proof supersedes it.
- An explicit discard authorization (the existing `--force` path) still overrides, as it does for other refusals.

### Why at the tool level

- A pipe or `&&` chain is an easy and natural way to write the two steps, and the failure is silent when it goes wrong.
- The cost of a false cleanup is high (finished work silently drops out of tracking), while the cost of the check is one metadata field and one comparison.
- The existing landed-work test answers "is this content reachable somewhere"; it does not answer "did the merge this supervisor just asked for actually happen". A recorded refusal is direct evidence for the second question.

### Notes

- I did not reconstruct which branch of the landed-work test let teardown pass in the local-only case; the commit was still present on the task branch afterwards, so no content was destroyed, but the task was closed as landed when it had not been.
- Happy to provide more detail or test a patch.

title: PR health monitor: report any failing check, approved-and-green, who merged or closed, and change requests older than the latest commit
body:
## Observed

On `2f000eb4`, the opt-in PR health monitor (`bin/fm-pr-health.sh`, header lines 36-63) wakes the owning home for a conflict, a failing check, or an author action.
Four useful states never reach the owner:

1. **A failing check that is not required.** Lines 42-44 count a failing context only when it is required, or when no reported context is required. On a repository with required checks, a failing optional check (for example a full suite or a platform job) stays silent, although it often means the PR will not be merged as it stands.
2. **Approved and green.** The monitor records a missing approval (line 51) but never says when a PR becomes approved with every check passing on its latest commit. That is the moment someone with merge rights can act.
3. **Merged or closed, and by whom.** Line 63 treats a merged or closed PR as final and never reads it again. The owner learns of it only through a separate merge poll, which does not say who merged or closed it. A close by a maintainer without a merge is a different outcome from a merge, and the owner should know which it was.
4. **A change request older than the latest commit.** Lines 53-54 report `CHANGES_REQUESTED` once per latest commit, as an author action. After the author pushes a fix, the same review still blocks the PR, but now the next step belongs to the reviewer, not the author. The monitor does not say that the change request predates the latest commit.

## Expected

Each of these is reported once per latest commit, through the same wake line format as the existing conditions:

- Any failing check on the latest commit, required or not. To avoid noise from a check that fails and is rerun at once, a failure is reported only when a second pass still sees it on the same commit.
- Approved and green: the review decision is approved and every reported check on the latest commit has passed.
- Merged or closed, naming the account that merged or closed it, read once when the PR becomes final.
- A change request whose review was submitted before the latest commit, reported as waiting on the reviewer rather than as an author action.

The monitor stays read-only: it never comments on, edits, or fixes a PR.

## Notes

The existing per-commit fingerprints in `state/pr-health.json` already give each condition its own history, so the new conditions can follow the same once-per-commit rule.
Related but different: https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8367 (delivering PR state changes to the captain without a model turn).

title: feat(bin): render markdown and text files to local voiced MP3 briefings
body:
## What Changed - Adds `bin/fm-speak.sh`, an on-demand CLI that turns one markdown or text file into speakable prose, synthesises it with the local Kokoro-82M ONNX voice, encodes mono MP3 with ffmpeg, splits long input into parts under `--max-minutes`, and writes `YYYY-MM-DD-.mp3` files plus an append-only `index.md` to `$HOME/audio-briefings` (or `--out`). It also provides `--setup` to create or repair the local venv/model cache and `--print-text` to emit the cleaned sentences without touching a synthesiser, and refuses output paths that name a Dropbox folder. - Adds `docs/audio-briefings.md` (registered as `operator-current` in `docs/documentation-audiences.json` and linked from `README.md`), documenting engine choice, install and cache layout/sizes, usage, output naming and index behavior, and the tool's explicit non-goals. - Adds `tests/fm-speak-print-text.test.sh`, covering the speakable-text normalisation output, the render report and index row checked against the produced MP3, and the setup/render cache-validity and missing-dependency failure paths using PATH shims. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The change is a self-contained, local-only tool plus one doc and one test (no shared code or existing behavior touched, no network or auth surface in a render), but it is a large new 915-line surface whose remaining defects are all text-pipeline output artifacts worth follow-up fixes. ## Testing Exercised the new audio tooling only through its user-facing CLI: `--print-text` shaping on a deliberately messy report (markup, nested emphasis of mixed delimiter lengths, line-final `vs.`, adjacent `approx.approx.`, `<`/`>` prose that used to be swallowed), ASCII transliteration, the help/flag surface with `--name` refused, the Dropbox refusal and argument validation, a real Kokoro render into the default `$HOME/audio-briefings` (verified as decodable non-silent MP3 by ffprobe/volumedetect with a matching index row), a two-part `--max-minutes 1` render followed by a second run that appended counter-named parts with exactly one index row per file in part order, and the `--setup` story for missing curl, missing python3, a C++-runtime-caused import failure (venv preserved) and an idempotent re-run, plus an strace proof that a render opens no IP socket. Everything ran in a throwaway lab (HOME, cache root and output dirs under a temp root, existing Kokoro files symlinked read-only); the lab was removed and no repository files were modified. There is no UI surface to screenshot — the end-user surface is CLI output plus the rendered MP3 and `index.md`, which are attached as artifacts. `--name fixed` exits 1 with `unk… | | Guards hold: a Dropbox output path is refused without creating it, `--max-minutes 010` is read as decimal ten while `0`/`abc` and an out-of-range `--speed` are rejected, missing/empty inputs fail with… | ✅ pass | live | evidence 03-guards-dropbox-args.txt: `--out <lab>/Dropbox/audio` exits 1 with the Dropbox refusal and creates nothing; Output reported file/duration/size/index/engine/voice/speed/total an… | | A long input with `--max-minutes 1` splits into `-part1.mp3`/`-part2.mp3`, and a second run into the same directory adds counter-named parts with one new index row per file, newest first, deleting not… | ✅ pass | live | evidence 05-render-multipart-index.txt and 05-index-after-run1.md: `--max-minutes 1` produced `...-part1.mp3` (0:49) and `...-part2.mp3` (0:18); a second identical run produced `...-2-part1.mp3`/`...-… | | `--setup` reports missing prerequisites (curl, python3) with an install line instead of a shell error, blames an unimportable-but-installed venv on the C++ runtime without deleting it, and is idempote… | ✅ pass | live | evidence 06-setup-honesty.txt: with a PATH shim lacking curl `--setup` exits 1 naming `curl` and its install line, no shell `command not found`, cache untouched; without python3 it names python3 3.10-… | | A render never uploads: the whole render process tree opens no IP socket and makes no outbound connection | ✅ pass | live | evidence 07-render-no-network.txt: a full render under `strace -f -e trace=connect,socket` completed 0:04 of audio with zero `AF_INET`/`AF_INET6` connects and zero socket() calls in the 177-line trace… |

title: Let a home add a runtime backend without patching core scripts
body:
Thanks for firstmate.

I run my second mates on a runtime firstmate does not ship. It is an agent session held by a long-running local server, with no terminal pane. To make that work, I carry one local commit on top of firstmate. The adapter itself is one new file, `bin/backends/<name>.sh`. Around it, the commit edits 22 shared scripts plus tests and docs (36 files, about 3,000 lines). The list of runtimes, and what each one can do, is written out by name in many places:

- the known and spawn-capable lists in `bin/fm-backend.sh`;
- per-backend `case` branches in `fm-spawn.sh`, `fm-control-lib.sh`, `fm-control.sh`, `fm-teardown.sh`, `fm-busy-lib.sh`, `fm-crew-state.sh`, `fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh` and `fm-remote-doctor.sh` (whether the backend has a pane, how to tell its endpoint is gone, which control verbs it supports);
- the session lock's check for which process owns a session;
- the supervision instructions picker and its protocol docs;
- the test families, timing tables and backend lists in the docs.

About ten of those files conflict on almost every update. Each firstmate update means a manual rebase and a re-test on my two machines, and `/updatefirstmate` correctly refuses on the diverged root until I finish. The backend list has grown since my base commit (tern, hc), so the same edits land on every new runtime too.

## What I would like

A documented way for a home to add a backend that lives outside the core scripts. A local runtime would then be one adapter file plus its own tests.

## The smallest interface I can see

1. Discovery. Core loads extra adapters from one configured folder and adds their names to the known and spawn-capable lists.
2. One capability question instead of name lists. Each adapter answers `fm_backend_<name>_capability <cap>` for the capabilities core already branches on: `pane`, `liveness`, `absence-proof`, `control` (which of interrupt, exit and relaunch it supports, with its own hooks), `session-owner`, `supervision` and `required-tools`. Core calls `fm_backend_capability <backend> <cap>` where it now matches backend names. The built-in backends answer from a built-in table, so their behavior does not change.
3. Tests and docs by filename. Core picks up `tests/fm-backend-<name>.test.sh` and `docs/<name>-backend.md` without a hand-kept list.

Points 1 and 2 for the spawn, control, teardown and session-lock paths alone would remove most of my conflicts.

## Why it may help beyond me

Several runtimes in the tree are marked experimental. With a capability question, each runtime states what it can and cannot do in one file. A new runtime can also be tried locally before anyone asks to upstream it.

I can describe my adapter's needs in more detail or test a branch. If you would rather keep backends in core, that answer helps me too.

title: feat(bin): let a reviewing home merge a routed PR with --routed-review
body:
## Intent Add a supported way for a reviewing firstmate home to merge a pull request whose ship task was dispatched from a different home, so an independent review-and-merge secondmate (shipwright) can actually complete its job instead of needing main firstmate to merge as a workaround. This gap was found by the `shipwright` secondmate reviewing `Denimworld12/Crazyy-Game` PR https://github.com/Denimworld12/Crazyy-Game/pull/2 (its review is recorded at `data/crazyy-game-pr2-review/report.md` in shipwright's own home, `~/.treehouse/firstmate-8bf1b0/1/firstmate`). The review itself was clean - "Clean and in scope. Ready to merge." - but shipwright could not perform the merge: > `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` requires a task record (`state/.meta`) in the merging home. This > shipwright home has no record for `crazyy-game-first-playable-slice` (it lives in the main > home), and there is no supported command to register an externally-dispatched PR here. I did > not hand-write a task record or point the script at the main home's state. > > Options: (a) main firstmate merges from its own home with > `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh crazyy-game-first-playable-slice https://github.com/Denimworld12/Crazyy-Game/pull/2` > (yolo is on for crazyy-game; this review is the clean pass); or (b) a firstmate-repo fix adds a > supported way to register a routed PR in a reviewer home so shipwright can merge itself. > > Recommendation: (a) now; file (b) as follow-up since every future routed PR will hit the same > gap. Main firstmate took option (a) for that specific PR already (it is merged). This task is option (b): close the gap itself so every future routed PR does not hit the same wall. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` gains ` --routed-review --expected-head `, which merges a PR another home dispatched without a task record in the merging home. The gate is this home's own `data//report.md`, which must name the canonical PR URL and the full reviewed commit as whole tokens. The flag is refused when `state/.meta` is a record of any kind other than scout; a scout record is accepted and left untouched. The existing gates (role partition, away posture, captain hold, live pre-merge conditions, head match) still apply. - A routed merge records no `pr=`, arms no merge poll, persists no merge authority and adds no backlog item, so it must be proved landed in the same run. `--attended-override` and `--update-branch` are refused, a GitHub base whose rules do not prove it has no merge queue is refused before anything reaches the forge, a GitLab merge request merges with `--auto-merge=false` and is refused when auto-merge is requested or configured, and an accepted request that reads back queued or unconfirmed exits nonzero. - `bin/fm-pr-check.sh` now refuses to record a PR or arm a merge watch on a scout record. The `ship-landing` skill and `docs/scripts.md` document the routed-review path, and `tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh` and `tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh` add cases for the routed merge, its refusals, the scout-record handling and the GitLab immediate-only behaviour. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: All three round-1 fixes are present and trace correctly through the source (queue preflight now refuses a routed merge before the forge call, only a scout-kind record passes the routed gate and it is rechecked under the control lock, fm-pr-check refuses scout records, the unrequired hint and its test are gone), and I found no new reachable defect; tests were not run in this phase. ## Testing Ran the five routed-review tests from `tests/fm-pr-merge.test.sh` in isolation (mocked forge) and the whole `tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh`; all passed. Then drove the real `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` and `bin/fm-pr-check.sh` in a marked lab home with a placeholder PR URL and the forge CLIs replaced by a guard that logs and fails. That run reproduced the original "task metadata is unavailable" gap on the ordinary path, showed each routed refusal with its exit code and zero forge calls, and showed a valid report passing the gate with no task record and nothing written under `state/`. title: feat(bin): add opt-in reports to the PR health monitor
body:
The opt-in PR health monitor can report four more states.
Each state needs its own config file.
A home that sets none of them keeps the current lines.

`config/pr-health-any-failure` reports any failing check on the latest commit, required or not.
The line prints only when a second pass still sees that failure on the same commit.
`config/pr-health-label-gated` lists checks that stay with the other maintainer-gated CI until the pull request has the named label.
`Full suite` followed by a tab and `full-ci` is the line for this repository.

`config/pr-health-approved-green` reports a non-draft pull request whose review decision is approved and whose reported checks on the latest commit have passed.
That report does not merge, park, or land the pull request.

`config/pr-health-final` reports a merged or closed pull request once and names the account in quotes.
The monitor then does not read that pull request again.

`config/pr-health-stale-review` reports a change request as waiting on the reviewer when `review.commit.oid` is not the latest commit.
It does not use timestamps.
Reviewer names are quoted.
Review text is not printed.

Forgejo pull requests are out of scope.
GitLab merge requests are out of scope.

Related: https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8646 changes the same script, the same docs section, and the same test file.
This change does not include those commits.

title: fix(bin): run remote macOS LaunchAgents with ProcessType=Interactive
body:
## Intent

Option 1 on the laptop timing fix: a Firstmate upstream pull request (github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate) that adds ProcessType=Interactive to the remote LaunchAgents and to the remote doctor's contract, so workers on a remote macOS second mate run at normal timer precision.

Context for that choice: on a remote macOS second mate (a MacBook Pro), workers run under the LaunchAgent dev.firstmate.herdr.fm-remote.plist that bin/fm-remote-doctor.sh writes. It sets no ProcessType, so launchd applies its default light resource limits and short native sleeps oversleep about 5-8x inside that session: python 50x sleep(0.01) took 3.66 s in the session vs 0.68 s over plain ssh on the same laptop (a later run gave 4.33 s with the default vs 0.64 s with ProcessType=Interactive), and a SQLite busy_timeout 500 ms probe took 1.5-1.8 s. A project's timing-sensitive commit-hook test therefore fails every run and build work cannot commit there. `taskpolicy -l 0 -t 0` does not clear it. The doctor exact-matches its plist contract, so a local edit to the plist would break readiness; the fix belongs in the template and the contract. The remote job agent (dev.firstmate.remote-job.plist, written by bin/fm-remote-job-lib.sh) has the same omission. Option 1 was chosen as low risk: the trade-off is that remote worker builds compete with the laptop's own apps at normal priority, only the Firstmate worker service changes, and the change is revertible.

## What Changed

- The Herdr LaunchAgent that `bin/fm-remote-doctor.sh` renders and the remote-job worker LaunchAgent that `bin/fm-remote-job-lib.sh` renders now both set `ProcessType=Interactive`. This lifts launchd's default resource limits, which coarsen timers in worker sessions. The plist contract is an exact match, so the doctor now treats a plist written without the key as stale and rewrites it.
- The doctor's loaded-job checks now also require `spawntype=interactive` in `launchctl print`. If the remote-job worker is loaded but doesn't match the contract, the doctor reports it as fixable ("rerun with --fix to reload") rather than "not loaded". When a manual `--fix` reloads the Herdr agent, the doctor now waits up to about 30 s for launchd to finish removing the label after `bootout`, and only then bootstraps it again. If removal times out, the fix fails cleanly.
- `docs/remote-secondmates.md` and the header comment in `bin/fm-remote-herdr-guard.sh` now describe the new `ProcessType` setting and contract. Tests in `tests/fm-remote-doctor.test.sh` and `tests/fm-remote-job-launchagent.test.sh` cover the new key, the spawn-type check, stale-plist detection, and the reload wait.

Summary of what happened:
1. Read-only (full-1): launchagent=fixable and remote-job-worker=fixable. Both base-written agents read out of contract, and the fix hint names "process type".
2. --fix (full-2): both agents were rewritten with ProcessType=Interactive.

   - The Herdr agent was booted out, but its bootstrap was refused with "Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error", so launchagent-loaded and herdr-server stayed fixable. The doctor's reload_launch_agent runs bootstrap right after bootout, without the bootout-cleanup wait the remote-job library uses.
   - Within seconds the host's own base-code entrypoint reverted the job agent to the base template. The supervising firstmate polls the host every few seconds, and each routed command runs fm_remote_job_ensure_worker against the host's older template.
3. --fix retry (full-3): the job agent was rewritten and reloaded again, and again reverted by the host's own polling-driven ensure. A worker killed mid-start during these competing reloads left only zero-byte temp files (.pid.*, .start.*, .command.*) in worker.lock. The worker's dead-owner reclaim removes pid, start and command but not those temp files, so its rmdir fails and every respawn exits ("cannot acquire or safely reclaim worker ownership"). This is a separate, pre-existing reclaim bug present in base and head.
   Herdr launchagent-loaded and herdr-server were still fixable.
4. Restore with the host's own doctor --fix, routed through fm-on.sh (full-4): the Herdr agent was rewritten to the base template (sha256 identical to before), bootstrapped and started (server running in Aqua). The job worker stayed wedged on the stale lock.
5. Stale lock repair (full-5): after confirming no worker process was running and the three files were zero bytes, they and the lock directory were removed. launchd restarted the worker.
6. Confirmation (full-6): the host's own doctor reports "remote second-mate readiness confirmed on this host". Both agents are byte-identical to their starting files.

What this does and does not show:
- Shown live: base-written agents read out of contract (both), and --fix rewrites both with ProcessType=Interactive. The remote job agent reached ready.
- Not reached live: the Herdr agent reaching ready under this branch. Its bootstrap failed with I/O error 5 immediately after bootout, on both the first pass and the retry, while the job agent was being reloaded concurrently.
- Not representative of a normal upgrade: the competing reloads came from running a newer doctor against a host whose own code root was still older. In a real upgrade the host's code root carries the new template, so its routed ensure agrees with the doctor.
- The host was restored to its starting state afterward.

title: fm-herdr-lab: a timed-out provision orphans its herdr server launch on bash that does not exec the last command
body:
## Problem

When `fm_herdr_lab_provision` times out, `fm_herdr_lab_cancel_provision` (`bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh:452`) signals only `$server_pid`, the `$!` of the backgrounded launch at `bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh:511`. On bash builds that keep a subshell for an async function (macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2, the Linux bash on CI), `$!` is that subshell and `herdr server` is its child, so the cancel leaves the server launch running after the provision has failed and after teardown. Homebrew bash 5.3 execs the last command, which hides it on most Macs.

## Desired

A timed-out or refused provision leaves no `herdr server` process from its launch running on every supported bash, and the test asserts that directly (event-based) right after the provision returns.

## Feasibility

Small and local to `bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh`.
Either make the backgrounded launch exec `herdr` so `$!` is the server process (for example run the launch as `( exec env ... herdr ... ) &` or a raw-exec variant of `fm_herdr_lab_raw`), or have `fm_herdr_lab_cancel_provision` signal the launch's children as well as the launch pid.
The first is simpler and keeps the cancel unchanged.
Happy to send a PR with the fix plus the tightened test assertion if that direction sounds right.

## Details

Repro (no herdr needed; a fake `herdr` blocks on a FIFO and records its pid):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
d=$(mktemp -d); mkfifo "$d/g"
cat > "$d/herdr" <<'H'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo $$ > "$GATED"; read -r _ < "$G"
H
chmod +x "$d/herdr"; export PATH="$d:$PATH" GATED="$d/gated" G="$d/g"
raw() { local name=$1; shift; env -u FOO HERDR_SESSION="$name" herdr "$@" --session "$name"; }
raw lab server > >(exec >/dev/null 2>&1; cat) 2>&1 &
p=$!
while [ ! -s "$d/gated" ]; do sleep 0.05; done
echo "server_pid=$p gated=$(cat $d/gated)"; ps -o pid,ppid,command -p "$p","$(cat $d/gated)"
kill -TERM $p; wait $p; sleep 0.3
kill -0 "$(cat $d/gated)" 2>/dev/null && echo "GATED ALIVE" && kill -KILL "$(cat $d/gated)" || echo "gated dead"
rm -rf "$d"
```

- `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash repro.sh` (bash 5.3): `server_pid` equals the gated pid, prints `gated dead`.
- `/bin/bash repro.sh` (bash 3.2): `server_pid` is the parent of the gated pid, prints `GATED ALIVE`.

The same divergence made a stricter liveness assertion in `tests/fm-herdr-lab.test.sh` (`test_timed_out_provision_cancels_late_launch`) pass on macOS and fail on the Linux CI lane, so the existing test only checks session state after teardown, which a launch that never reaches running cannot fail.

title: feat(bearings): add Ask for more, More answers, and references to board cards
body:
## Intent Build step 2 of the bearings board plan as a pull request to kunchenguid/firstmate: an Ask for more button (a non-choice prompt), a More block (a `more` list, with pages copied beside the board), a `refs` list, and `detail` on decision cards. Maintainer follow-up on https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8776 (comment https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8776#issuecomment-7201563868): raise the PR through no-mistakes, keeping the fork aalexmrt/firstmate as the PR head; record live evidence on a real board in the Test step (click Ask for more, confirm exactly one ask-more prompt is queued and the card stays open, then rebuild with a `more` entry and a page and confirm it renders); and add one docs line that a page named in the payload is copied beside the board and published at the board's origin. ## What Changed - The bearings board template adds an Ask for more button to every Captain's Call card. It queues a Lavish prompt tagged `ask-more` with `fm-bearings-ask-more.v1` context, never a `choice` row, so the card stays open. On `build` it copies each `more` page into `bearings-board-pages/` beside the board under a content-addressed name and rewrites `page` to that relative path. A rebuild can pass that relative path back in, so an open card's `more` carries forward. A page that is missing, unreadable or a symlink stops the build before any page is copied. After the board is published, `build` removes copied pages the board no longer names. The script header notes that a copied page is published at the board's origin. - The bearings skill doc covers `detail`, `refs` and `more`, and says an `ask-more` annotation is a request for more, not an answer. Tests cover payload checks, page copying, refusal and pruning, how the new card parts render (with an updated render harness), and that `fm-procevent-lavish.sh` `answers`/`reconciles` ignore an Ask for more row while `read` still shows it. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is additive and well-bounded: optional payload fields are validated before the board is touched, pages are checked before any copy, the board is published before stale pages are pruned, html pages render in a script-free sandboxed frame, and Ask for more queues a non-choice prompt that the answer intake ignores. title: Session lock: bun-installed omp daemon workers (`bun .../cli.js __omp_worker_*`) are not excluded from anchoring
body:
Speaking as Kun's firstmate: filing a follow-up found while porting #6870 (landed as #8731, dbb3f19679e83bae0259b1424d96da99a9ea2578).

`fm_omp_daemon_worker` in `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh` checks only the first argument after argv0 for `__omp_worker_*`. When omp runs from the bun package (supported on main since #8350), workers spawn as `[bun, <.../dist/cli.js>, __omp_worker_*]` (pi-coding-agent 19.1.1, `src/subprocess/worker-client.ts` `resolveWorkerSpawnCmd`). In `ps` that's `bun .../cli.js __omp_worker_daemon_broker`. The check returns false (the second word is the script), and `fm_omp_process_matches` rejects it too, so `fm_harness_ancestry_pids` walks past the worker to the bun omp that launched it and records that process. This is the #6870 bug, still live for bun installs, and `fm-lock.sh`'s named refusal never fires.

Narrow fix: when argv0's basename is `bun`, check the word after the script for `__omp_worker_*`, and add a bun-shaped row to `test_omp_daemon_worker_is_never_the_session`.

title: fix(bin): reclaim a returned Treehouse pool slot's disk at teardown
body:
## Intent "[...] fare in modo che non ricapiti una situazione simile e che firstmate, quando lavoro su ste cose, elimini da solo eventuali copie" - "niente attivita' automatica, deve essere parte del processo di lavoro (soprattutto questione di copie)". Context: the Mac disk filled up (3.4 GB free of 245 GB). Cause: Treehouse pool worktrees that firstmate's teardown returns to the pool keep all git-ignored build output (node_modules, .next, dist, Electron builds), so each finished task left a 0.5-6 GB slot behind and pools only ever grew (38 GB across pools; one pool held 5 slots at 3-6 GB each, an abandoned pool held 12 idle slots). `treehouse destroy --all --yes` on merged, clean, idle, unleased slots reclaimed ~26 GB. The ask: reclaiming finished copies must be a step of firstmate's own task-completion flow, not a separate scheduled job. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-teardown.sh`: added `teardown_destroy_pool_slot`. After a successful `treehouse return` of a pool slot the task actually held, teardown now runs `treehouse destroy --yes` on that slot. This reclaims the git-ignored build output (`node_modules`, `.next`, `dist`, Electron builds) that `return` leaves behind. A skipped or failed destroy only prints a warning and does not fail teardown. The dirty-return note and the destroy now run only for slots that were pool slots. - Added the `config/keep-pool-slots` presence flag. When it exists, teardown skips the destroy and keeps returned slots pre-warmed in the pool. It is documented in `docs/configuration.md` (new "Pool slot reclaim" section) and listed in the `operational-home-layout` skill. - `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh`: added test coverage for the new teardown behavior. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Il reclaim è limitato allo slot appena restituito, usa il destroy sicuro di default con solo warning in caso di errore, e il release del claim ora avviene prima del destroy come deciso nel round 1. ## Testing The full teardown test file ran too long and was stopped. I then ran only the three pool-slot cases, which drive the real bin/fm-teardown.sh against a stub treehouse binary, and all passed. I did not run a real Treehouse pool or a Herdr lab. The destroy path is therefore proven against a stub of the treehouse CLI, not the real CLI. - Live validation: ✅ go - 3 of 3 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Teardown of a task whose pool slot was returned runs `treehouse destroy <slot> --yes` with no --include-* override | ✅ pass | live | pool-slot-tests.log line 1 | | Adversarial: destroy skips a dirty or unmerged slot, teardown still exits 0, the slot stays and a warning is printed | ✅ pass | live | pool-slot-tests.log line 2 | | config/keep-pool-slots opts the home out, and destroy is never invoked | ✅ pass | live | pool-slot-tests.log line 3 |

title: fix(bin): exec the herdr lab server launch so a timed-out provision cancels it
body:
Fixes #8775 ## Behavior When `fm_herdr_lab_provision` timed out, `fm_herdr_lab_cancel_provision` signalled only `$!` of the backgrounded server launch. On bash builds that keep a subshell for an async function (macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2, the Linux CI bash), `$!` was that subshell, so the `herdr server` launch outlived the failed provision and the teardown. The launch now goes through `fm_herdr_lab_raw_exec`, which execs `env ... herdr`, so `$!` is the herdr server process on every bash. `fm_herdr_lab_cancel_provision` is unchanged. `fm_herdr_lab_raw` now runs `fm_herdr_lab_raw_exec` in a subshell, so the argument and environment handling has one owner. ## Test `test_timed_out_provision_cancels_late_launch` now asserts, right after the timed-out provision returns, that the launch process is gone. The fake herdr server records its own pid and then blocks on a FIFO until it is cancelled, and the provision's status polls wait on that pid file, so the timeout always cancels a launch that is already running (event-based, no fixed sleep or delay that a slow host could outlast). The previous fixed `sleep 1.1` before the late-start check is removed: once the launch is proven dead, nothing can flip the session to running later. ## Evidence (macOS, `tests/fm-herdr-lab.test.sh`) | bash | before the fix | after the fix | |---|---|---| | `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 | fails: `not ok - timed-out provision returned with its herdr server launch (pid 42048) still running` | 26/26 ok | | `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash` 5.3.9 | passes (5.3 execs the last command, which hid the bug) | 26/26 ok | ShellCheck 0.11.0 `--external-sources` is clean on both changed files; the full lint runs in CI on Linux. ## Live Herdr evidence (real Herdr 0.9.5, guarded lab sessions) The timeout was forced with a PATH shim that answers the lab session's `status` as not running while every other call, including the real `herdr server` launch, execs real Herdr. 1. Scenario 1 PASS on fix 11287739 (real Herdr 0.9.5, macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 and bash 5.3.9): the forced 60 s provision timeout killed the `herdr server` launch itself (launch pid 21421 / 74609 gone when provision returned, lab session `running:false`), and teardown left no session, process, or tripwire. 2. Scenario 1 pre-fix control (11287739^ = 4b1d93d2) on `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 reproduces the bug: `$!` was the wrapper subshell (46367, `Terminated: 15`), while the launch pid 46371 survived reparented to pid 1 with the lab session still `running:true` after provision returned 1; on bash 5.3.9 the pre-fix code did not leak (pid 1785 gone), matching the fix's root cause (only bashes that keep an async-function subshell leak). 3. Scenario 2 PASS on the fix under both bashes: normal named-lab provision returned 0 in ~1 s with the launch pid alive as `herdr server --session ` and `status` reporting `server: true`; guarded teardown returned 0, the launch pid exited, and the session disappeared from `session list`. 4. Lab torn down: no `fm-lab-up-fm-8775-*` session, process, session directory, tripwire or server log remains; the fleet `default` session stayed running and every tripwire check passed; no code was changed. ## Intent Open an upstream PR to kunchenguid/firstmate that addresses issue 8775: when `fm_herdr_lab_provision` times out, its cancel signals only `$!` of the backgrounded launch (`bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh:452,511`); on bash builds that keep a subshell for an async function (macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2, Linux CI bash 5.2) `$!` is that subshell, so the `herdr server` launch survives the failed provision and teardown. The maintainer labelled it ready-for-pr and agreed the direction: make the backgrounded launch exec `herdr` so `$!` is the server process, with the cancel unchanged, plus an event-based test assertion right after the timed-out provision returns that the launch process is gone, which must hold on every supported bash. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The bounded exec-based fix preserves session isolation and cancellation behavior while adding a behavioral assertion for the reported orphaned launch. ## Testing Focused helper tests passed after repairing a timing race, and before/after mock-boundary checks reproduced and eliminated the orphan on Bash 3.2 and 5.2. Real CLI scoping and guards passed across three Bash versions, with transcripts retained. Mandatory fleet-tripwire prerequisites blocked real provisioning and teardown, so lifecycle acceptance remains inconclusive. All disposable processes and files were cleaned up. - Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 2 of 4 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Timed-out provisioning kills the launch before returning, and teardown leaves no late server | ⏸️ untested | no | Attempted prepare and provision against real Herdr 0.9.5 with worktree-local XDG configuration. Both refused the missing running fleet tripwire before launch. title: fix(bin): initialize pending-reply id locals and reuse the merge control lock when pinning the local done head

title: `fm_treehouse_spawn_root` lets a missing `TREEHOUSE_ROOT` below a symlink place a secondmate's Treehouse pool inside the home
body:
Affects `2f000eb4` (#8718, the port of #7390) and later until fixed.

## Summary

`fm_treehouse_spawn_root` (`bin/fm-wake-lib.sh`) refuses a pool root equal to, or under, the secondmate home so that a slot's ancestors never include the home's `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`.
It canonicalizes `TREEHOUSE_ROOT` with `cd -P` only when the whole path already exists, then applies a lexical prefix check.
When the path does not exist yet and an existing ancestor is a symlink into the home, the printed path never names the home, the check passes, and Treehouse later creates the pool physically inside the home.

## Reproduction

Run against a checkout of `2f000eb4`. The scratch directory holds a main home, a local secondmate home, and a symlink to the secondmate home.

```bash
t=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$t/main" "$t/mate"
printf 'schema=fm-secondmate-parent.v1\nroute=local\nparent_home=%s\n' "$t/main" > "$t/mate/.fm-secondmate-parent"
ln -s "$t/mate" "$t/alias"
FM_HOME=$t/mate TREEHOUSE_ROOT=$t/alias/not-created HOME=$t/user \
  bash -c '. bin/fm-wake-lib.sh && fm_treehouse_spawn_root "$1"' _ "$t/mate"
echo "rc=$?"
```

Observed: prints `$t/alias/not-created/fm-secondmate/<id>` and `rc=0`.
After Treehouse creates `.treehouse/pool` under that path, `cd -P "$t/alias/not-created"` resolves to `$t/mate/not-created`, which is inside the home.
Expected: refusal (non-zero, nothing printed), the same as for `TREEHOUSE_ROOT=$t/mate/not-created`.

A dangling symlink root (`ln -s "$t/mate/pool" "$t/dangling"`, `TREEHOUSE_ROOT=$t/dangling`) fails the same way, because `[ -d ]` is false and the lexical check sees no home prefix.

## Proposed fix

Resolve the nearest existing ancestor with `cd -P` and re-append the not-yet-existing suffix, then run the existing containment check on that physical path.
Refuse a dangling symlink and a `.` or `..` component in the missing suffix, because neither can be resolved without creating anything.

```bash
anchor=$base
suffix=
while [ ! -d "$anchor" ]; do
  [ ! -L "$anchor" ] || return 1
  part=${anchor##*/}
  case "$part" in .|..) return 1 ;; esac
  anchor=${anchor%/*}
  [ -n "$anchor" ] || anchor=/
  [ -z "$part" ] || suffix=/$part$suffix
done
anchor=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$anchor" && pwd -P) || return 1
base=${anchor%/}$suffix
```

## Regression test

In `tests/fm-spawn-secondmate-pool.test.sh`, assert refusal for: a missing directory below a symlink to the home, the symlink itself, a deep missing suffix below it, a dangling symlink and a missing suffix below it, and a `..` component after a missing directory. Also assert that a missing root below a symlink to a directory outside the home is accepted and printed as its physical path. The first assertion fails on `2f000eb4` and passes with the fix.

title: fm-teardown.sh should refuse when the task's most recent merge attempt was refused
body:
### What happens

A supervisor ran a merge script and teardown in one chained command, with the merge output piped, for example:

```
bin/fm-merge-local.sh <task> ... | tail -n 5 && bin/fm-teardown.sh <task>
```

The merge script refused (for example, the local-only branch was no longer a fast-forward of the default branch). The pipe hid the non-zero exit, so `&&` went ahead and teardown ran. Teardown's landed-work check did not stop it, and the task was cleaned up: its task record and backlog item were closed as done while its commit had never reached the default branch. The commit survived only on its task branch, and the change had to be found and re-dispatched by hand as a new "land the finished fix" task.

The same pattern also occurred with `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh` during an earlier stretch of about five days, and again later in a loop that ran merge then teardown separated by `;` (the merge was refused because the PR conflicted with the default branch; teardown passed because the branch was pushed), where a refused merge was followed by teardown and the work sat orphaned until it was noticed.

In both cases the operator rule "run the merge script alone, confirm it reports merged, then run teardown; never chain or pipe them" was already written in the home's local notes. It recurred anyway, so a written rule is not enough; it needs a tool-side check.

### Expected

Teardown should know that the task's last merge attempt was refused and refuse cleanup on that basis, independent of how the commands were chained. For example:

- `fm-merge-local.sh` and `fm-pr-merge.sh` record the outcome of each attempt in task metadata (for example `last_merge_attempt=refused <epoch> <reason>` / `last_merge_attempt=merged <epoch>`).
- `fm-teardown.sh` refuses, with a message naming the refusal and its reason, when the most recent recorded attempt is `refused` and no later successful merge or landed proof supersedes it.
- An explicit discard authorization (the existing `--force` path) still overrides, as it does for other refusals.

### Why at the tool level

- A pipe or `&&` chain is an easy and natural way to write the two steps, and the failure is silent when it goes wrong.
- The cost of a false cleanup is high (finished work silently drops out of tracking), while the cost of the check is one metadata field and one comparison.
- The existing landed-work test answers "is this content reachable somewhere"; it does not answer "did the merge this supervisor just asked for actually happen". A recorded refusal is direct evidence for the second question.

### Notes

- I did not reconstruct which branch of the landed-work test let teardown pass in the local-only case; the commit was still present on the task branch afterwards, so no content was destroyed, but the task was closed as landed when it had not been.
- Happy to provide more detail or test a patch.

title: refactor(bin): ask backends one capability question instead of matching names
body:
This is step 1 of #8771.

## What it does

I added one question to `bin/fm-backend.sh`: `fm_backend_capability <backend> <cap>`.
Each built-in backend answers it from one table, one row per backend.
Core now asks that question in the places that matched backend names.
Nothing is discovered or loaded from a home. That is step 2.

Contract class: opt-in.
The change is behavior-preserving: every built-in backend gives the same answer as the name list it replaces, and I changed no existing test.

## The interface

- `fm_backend_capability <backend> <cap>` prints the answer and returns 0.
- A flag answers `yes` or `no`. A list answers one or more words.
- Every flag is phrased so that `no` is the cautious answer.
- `fm_backend_capable <backend> <cap> [word]` is the test form. It returns 0 for yes, 1 for no, and 2 for a refusal.
- An unknown backend, an unknown capability, or a missing or malformed answer is refused. The function prints an error on stderr, prints nothing on stdout, and returns 1. There is no default answer.
- Answers are static. None reads runtime state.

## Capabilities and the call sites that moved

| Capability | Kind | Name match it replaces |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `visible-capture` | flag | `FM_BACKEND_VISIBLE_CAPTURE` in `fm-backend.sh` |
| `push` | flag | `herdr\|rex\|t3code` in `fm_backend_has_push` |
| `keys` | list | the case table in `fm_control_backend_supports_key` |
| `state-verified` | flag | `fm_control_backend_state_verified`, and `tmux\|herdr\|rex\|t3code` in `fm-crew-state.sh` |
| `exit` | flag | `fm_control_backend_exit_supported` |
| `relaunch` | flag | `fm_control_backend_relaunch_supported` |
| `secondmate` | flag | five `--secondmate` refusals in `fm-spawn.sh`, now one with the same message |
| `remote-secondmate` | flag | `herdr\|rex` in `fm-spawn.sh`, `fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh`, and `fm-secondmate-liveness-lib.sh` |
| `supervisor` | flag | `FM_SUPERVISOR_SUPPORTED_BACKENDS` in `fm-supervise-daemon.sh`, now built from the table |
| `required-tools` | list | the case table in `fm_backend_required_tools` |

Against the names in #8771: liveness is `state-verified`, control is `keys`, `exit`, and `relaunch`, and supervision is `supervisor` and `push`.
The old helper functions keep their names and now read the table, so their callers did not change.
The `fm-control-lib.sh` helpers load `fm-backend.sh` on first use when a caller has not, so sourcing `fm-control-lib.sh` stays free.

## What I left alone, and why

- `FM_BACKEND_KNOWN` and `FM_BACKEND_SPAWN`. Step 2 extends these lists.
- `pane`. No call site asks a yes-or-no about panes. Each T3 Code branch in spawn, teardown, control, watch, busy, and send runs T3's own alternative, such as a thread launch or a native interrupt. That is an adapter hook, not an answer.
- `absence-proof`. `fm_control_endpoint_absence_verdict` runs each adapter's own recheck, and a yes-or-no would not replace it. The Rex-only `unreadable` rule in `fm_control_absence_recheck_applies` is about how Rex reads.
- `session-owner`. The session lock does not branch on backend names on current main.
- The per-operation dispatch in `fm-backend.sh` (capture, send-key, kill, busy state, composer, agent state, target exists, event wait). Each arm calls that adapter's own function.
- Single-name branches for Orca, T3 Code, Herdr, and Rex in spawn and teardown. Each runs that runtime's own steps, such as Orca's worktree or Herdr's slot lease.
- The `herdr|rex|tern` native-busy rule in `fm-busy-lib.sh`. An earlier branch trusts T3 Code's native state in full, so one yes-or-no would misdescribe T3 Code.
- Harness rules such as "Hermes runs on tmux only". Those lists belong to the harness.
- `fm-remote-doctor.sh`. Its herdr and rex arms run backend-specific checks on the remote host.
- The test-family table in `fm-test-run.sh`. That is step 3.

## One difference for names outside the table

A backend name the table does not know now gets one refusal line on stderr, where some callers were silent before.
The other helpers answered no for such a name, and the refusal still takes their no branch.
`fm_control_backend_exit_supported` used to answer yes for such a name, and now it refuses.
Its callers validate the name or refuse it earlier, so no flow changes.

## Tests

I added two tests to `tests/fm-backend.test.sh`.
One checks every built-in answer against the old name lists.
The other checks the refusals for unknown backends, unknown capabilities, and malformed answers.

Commands I ran on macOS:

- `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-backend.test.sh`: passed, 42 ok, including the old-versus-new conformance diffs for send, peek, spawn, and teardown.
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh` on 41 suites: every backend unit suite, control, control relaunch, crew state, daemon, park, bootstrap, gotmp, watch triage, send, secondmate liveness and restart, the remote secondmate suites, and the harness suites that read the control tables. 39 passed. Two failed on my Mac, `fm-hermes-harness.test.sh` ("NUL argv identity lost when names/ps args are blind") and `fm-spawn-orca-worktree.test.sh` (the interactive `/bin/zsh` pane case). Both fail the same way on the base commit.
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-control.test.sh tests/fm-backend-t3code.test.sh` after the last edit: passed.
- The two new tests under macOS's stock bash 3.2: passed. The new test also asks the table under zsh.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh`, full canonical set with ShellCheck 0.11.0: clean except three findings in `tests/fm-daemon.test.sh` that the base commit has too.
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`: ok.

title: fix(bin): pin secondmate retirement process-event calls to the retiring home's state
body:
Fixes #8634

## Intent

Fix issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8634: three bin/fm-procevent.sh calls in bin/fm-teardown.sh pass only FM_HOME and FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE, while bin/fm-procevent.sh reads FM_STATE_OVERRIDE first, so they can act on the parent's state instead of the retiring home's.
The maintainer named the fix: pin the three calls to the retiring home's state, which restores the documented promise in docs/configuration.md. Add the parent-state regression test and keep the checks that the parent's source file and directory mode are unchanged, as the maintainer's security note asks.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-teardown.sh` now passes `FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$home/state"` on its three `fm-procevent.sh` calls (`sweep-home --preflight`, `sweep-home`, and `reconcile`), so an `FM_STATE_OVERRIDE` inherited from the parent no longer sends them to the parent's state root.
- `docs/configuration.md` now says the sweep matches the home's own `state/` directory and never an inherited `FM_STATE_OVERRIDE`, and the manual recovery command sets `FM_STATE_OVERRIDE=<home>/state`.
- `tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh` replaces the fake-sweep test with a regression test that runs the real `fm-procevent.sh` under a parent `FM_STATE_OVERRIDE` at directory modes 775 and 700. It checks that the retiring home's source is swept, and that the parent's source file and directory mode are unchanged.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change adds FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$home/state" to exactly the three named calls, which equals the path fm-procevent.sh already resolves when no override is inherited, so behavior changes only in the buggy inherited-override case, and the docs and the regression test match the intent.

## Testing

I drove the real bin/fm-teardown.sh and real bin/fm-procevent.sh against disposable parent and child homes in a temp directory, with a fake tmux and fake treehouse from tests/secondmate-helpers.sh as the only stand-ins. On the target commit, all three scenarios passed: normal teardown at parent state modes 775 and 700, the failed-home-return path that restores and rearms registrations, and the documented manual recovery command. On the base commit, the same driver failed the teardown scenario in both modes and deleted the parent's registration at mode 700, which reproduces the reported bug. The repository regression test file tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh also passed on the target commit, including the new parent-state test. No full suite, linter or Herdr lab ran, because this change touches only tmux-backend teardown calls that the disposable homes exercise directly. The change has no UI surface, so there is no screenshot.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Usage: drive.sh <tree> - drives the real bin/fm-teardown.sh and bin/fm-procevent.sh
# from <tree> against disposable homes, with the parent's FM_STATE_OVERRIDE exported.
set -u
TREE=$1
. "$TREE/tests/secondmate-helpers.sh"
T=$(fm_test_tmproot fm-8634-live)
fmode() { stat -c %a "$1"; }
show() { echo "--- $1"; (cd "$2" 2>/dev/null && find . -path ./bin -prune -o -type f -print | sort | grep -v '^./AGENTS.md' ) || echo "(gone)"; }
verdict=0
check() { if eval "$2"; then echo "OK   $1"; else echo "FAIL $1"; verdict=1; fi; }

setup() { # $1=tag $2=mode ; sets home subhome control claims before
  home="$T/$1-parent"; subhome="$T/$1-child"; control="$home/state/parent-route"
  claims="$T/$1-claims"; before="$T/$1.source.before"
  mkdir -p "$control/procevent" "$home/data"
  chmod "$2" "$control"
}
register() {
  mkdir -p "$subhome/state"; chmod 700 "$subhome/state"
  printf 'domain\n' > "$subhome/.fm-secondmate-home"
  cp -R "$ROOT/bin/." "$subhome/bin/"
  FM_HOME="$subhome" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$subhome/state" FM_PROCEVENT_CLAIM_ROOT="$claims" \
    "$subhome/bin/fm-procevent.sh" register lavish source -- "$(command -v true)" >/dev/null || { echo "setup: register failed"; exit 3; }
  cp "$subhome/state/procevent/source.source" "$before"
  cp "$before" "$control/procevent/source.source"   # parent holds a same-named registration
  printf '%s\n' '- domain - design domain (home: '"$subhome"'; scope: design domain; projects: alpha; added 2026-06-22)' > "$home/data/secondmates.md"
}

for mode in 775 700; do
  echo; echo "===== S1 teardown, parent state mode $mode, parent FM_STATE_OVERRIDE exported ====="
  setup "s1-$mode" "$mode"; mark_firstmate_home "$subhome"; register
  fm_write_secondmate_meta "$control/domain.meta" "$subhome"
  fakebin=$(make_fake_tmux "$T/s1-$mode-fake")
  show "parent state before" "$control"; show "child home before" "$subhome"
  out=$(PATH="$fakebin:$PATH" FM_HOME="$home" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$control" FM_PROCEVENT_CLAIM_ROOT="$claims" \
    FM_FAKE_TMUX_LOG="$T/s1-$mode-fake/tmux.log" FM_FAKE_TMUX_CAPTURE="$T/s1-$mode-fake/pane.txt" \
    "$ROOT/bin/fm-teardown.sh" domain 2>&1); rc=$?
  echo "\$ FM_HOME=<parent> FM_STATE_OVERRIDE=<parent>/state/parent-route bin/fm-teardown.sh domain  -> rc=$rc"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed "s#$T#<tmp>#g; s/^/  | /"
  show "parent state after" "$control"; show "child home after" "$subhome"
  check "teardown exits 0" '[ $rc -eq 0 ]'
  check "sweep reports the child registration (attempted=1)" 'printf "%s" "$out" | grep -qF "swept: attempted=1"'
  check "child home removed" '[ ! -d "$subhome" ]'
  check "parent source.source byte-identical" 'cmp -s "$before" "$control/procevent/source.source"'
  check "parent state dir mode still $mode (now $(fmode "$control"))" '[ "$(fmode "$control")" = "$mode" ]'
done

echo; echo "===== S2 failed home return -> restore + reconcile, parent FM_STATE_OVERRIDE exported ====="
setup s2 775; fmroot="$T/s2-fmroot"
make_firstmate_git_root "$fmroot"
git -C "$fmroot" worktree add --quiet --detach "$subhome" HEAD
register
cat > "$control/domain.meta" <<META
window=firstmate:fm-domain
worktree=$subhome
project=$subhome
harness=echo
kind=secondmate
mode=secondmate
yolo=off
home=$subhome
projects=alpha
META
fakebin=$(make_fake_tmux "$T/s2-fake")
show "parent state before" "$control"; show "child state before" "$subhome/state"
out=$(PATH="$fakebin:$PATH" FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$fmroot" FM_HOME="$home" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$control" FM_PROCEVENT_CLAIM_ROOT="$claims" \
  FM_FAKE_TMUX_LOG="$T/s2-fake/tmux.log" FM_FAKE_TMUX_CAPTURE="$T/s2-fake/pane.txt" FM_FAKE_TREEHOUSE_RETURN_FAIL=1 \
  "$ROOT/bin/fm-teardown.sh" domain 2>&1); rc=$?
echo "\$ ... FM_FAKE_TREEHOUSE_RETURN_FAIL=1 bin/fm-teardown.sh domain  -> rc=$rc"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed "s#$T#<tmp>#g; s/^/  | /"
sleep 2
show "parent state after" "$control"; show "child state after" "$subhome/state"
check "teardown refuses (rc != 0)" '[ $rc -ne 0 ]'
check "refusal is the failed home return" 'printf "%s" "$out" | grep -qF "treehouse return failed"'
check "child home retained" '[ -d "$subhome" ]'
check "child registration restored" '[ -f "$subhome/state/procevent/source.source" ]'
check "parent procevent dir holds only its original source" '[ "$(cd "$control/procevent" && ls -A | tr "\n" " ")" = "source.source " ]'
check "parent source.source byte-identical" 'cmp -s "$before" "$control/procevent/source.source"'
check "parent state dir mode still 775 (now $(fmode "$control"))" '[ "$(fmode "$control")" = 775 ]'
FM_HOME="$subhome" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$subhome/state" FM_PROCEVENT_CLAIM_ROOT="$claims" "$subhome/bin/fm-procevent.sh" sweep-home >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

echo; echo "===== S3 documented manual recovery command, run from a shell that exports the parent FM_STATE_OVERRIDE ====="
setup s3 775; mark_firstmate_home "$subhome"; register
export FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$control"
out=$(FM_PROCEVENT_CLAIM_ROOT="$claims" FM_HOME="$subhome" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$subhome/state" "$subhome/bin/fm-procevent.sh" sweep-home 2>&1); rc=$?
unset FM_STATE_OVERRIDE
echo "\$ FM_HOME=<home> FM_STATE_OVERRIDE=<home>/state <home>/bin/fm-procevent.sh sweep-home  -> rc=$rc"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed "s#$T#<tmp>#g; s/^/  | /"
check "sweep exits 0 and retires the child registration" '[ $rc -eq 0 ] && [ ! -e "$subhome/state/procevent/source.source" ]'
check "parent source.source byte-identical" 'cmp -s "$before" "$control/procevent/source.source"'
check "parent state dir mode still 775" '[ "$(fmode "$control")" = 775 ]'

pgrep -af "$T" && echo "WARN: leftover processes" 
rm -rf "$T"
echo; echo "RESULT: $([ $verdict -eq 0 ] && echo ALL-OK || echo HAS-FAILURES)"
exit $verdict

title: fix(bin): read the PR scan past a review wait on the same PR
body:
Fixes #8762 ## Intent Fix issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8762: bin/fm-pr-check.sh scan stops at a paused: line that follows a ready done: line for the same PR. The maintainer wrote the fix and test list: skip back over paused: lines only when they name the same canonical PR URL, keep the draft refusal and replacement rules, and test the three cases the issue names. The three cases the issue names: done then paused on the same PR records the PR and arms its merge poll; done then paused on another PR records nothing; done then working records nothing. A paused: line with no PR or a different PR, and any working:, blocked: or failed: line, still stops the scan. ## What Changed - `pr_check_reported_url` in `bin/fm-pr-check.sh` now walks back over trailing `paused:` lines to the ready `done:` line, and keeps that report only when every `paused:` line names the ready PR at least once and names no other PR. A `paused:` line with no PR or a different PR, and any later `working:`, `blocked:` or `failed:` line, still leaves nothing to record. - When the scan reads a PR URL in a `paused:` line, it ignores punctuation around the URL (a trailing comma or period, enclosing brackets or quotes) and a `#fragment` after it. `docs/configuration.md` and the header comment of `bin/fm-pr-check.sh` describe both rules. - `tests/fm-pr-check-security.test.sh` adds `test_scan_reads_the_ready_line_past_a_wait_on_the_same_pr`. It checks that `done` then `paused` on the same PR (plain and punctuated) records the PR and arms its merge poll, and that `done` then `paused` on another PR, `paused` naming both PRs, and `done` then `paused` then `working` each record nothing. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is confined to one function that fails closed on every path I traced (no done: line, empty note, no PR named, another PR named, a line that cannot be located), and both callers, the draft refusal and the replacement rule are untouched. ## Testing I drove the real bin/fm-pr-check.sh scan, and one real bin/fm-watch.sh sweep, against disposable FM homes with the test suite's local gh emulator and synthetic status files. All 17 scenario runs gave the expected task metadata and merge poll state. The base commit failed the same-PR case, as issue 8762 reports. title: Claude composer readback reads a wrapped doorbell as unknown, so the ring cannot submit it
body:
## Problem

When a steering doorbell line is long enough to wrap in a named Claude worker's composer (a narrow Herdr pane), `bin/fm-composer-lib.sh` classifies the composer as `unknown` instead of `pending`, because it does not read text spanning several glyph rows. The inbox ring (`fm_task_inbox_ring` in `bin/fm-task-inbox-lib.sh`) then cannot recognize and submit the unsubmitted doorbell, so the delivery stays unconfirmed and the worker does not read its inbox until someone presses Enter.

## Desired

A wrapped composer payload that is contiguous, non-blank and within the configured line bound classifies `pending` and extracts completely, so the ring can submit it; blank-gap and overlong regions stay `unknown`.

## Evidence

- Live readback with the fix in https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8501: a wrapped doorbell at width 100 and width 200 classifies `pending` with full extraction, while the blank-gap and overlong guard cases stay `unknown`.
- Related, not the same: #6063 (the doorbell's Enter never lands).

title: fix(bin): name the ready line's PR in a child outcome report
body:
Fixes #8698 Not changed: a non-GitHub ready line without `config/pr-register-scan` still leaves a recorded `pr=` standing, and with `config/pr-register-scan` a recorded PR the status log never named still wins; widening either is a separate change. ## Intent Fix issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8698: the default pr_for_task in bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh returns the recorded pr= even when the terminal ready line names a different PR, so a relayed outcome can name the wrong PR. The maintainer confirmed the path and named the reference: the pr-register-scan path already prefers the ready line. Make pr_for_task prefer the ready line's URL when they differ, test the A-registered, B-reported case, and show that a task with one PR behaves exactly as on main. ## What Changed - `pr_for_task` in `bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh`, on its default path (no `config/pr-register-scan` file), now reads the terminal line even when the task has a recorded `pr=`. A GitHub-shaped `done: PR ` or `done: PR checks green` line names the report's `pr=` over a different recorded one. Any other terminal line leaves the recorded `pr=` standing, so a task whose ready line and recorded `pr=` agree reports the same PR as before. - `tests/fm-inactive-reconcile.test.sh` renames the no-opt-in test to `test_ledger_report_without_scan_opt_in_names_the_ready_pr` and flips two assertions: the `replaced` and `kept` children, each recorded with `pull/1`, now report `pr=` as `pull/22` and `pull/23`, the PRs their ready lines name. The GitLab assertions are unchanged: a GitLab ready line still does not override or fill in `pr=` without the opt-in. - `docs/configuration.md` and the header comment of `bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh` now describe the new precedence with the flag absent: the GitHub-shaped ready line names the PR, and otherwise the recorded `pr=` stands. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a three-line edit to the default branch of pr_for_task with one caller, the PR value is not part of the ledger fingerprint so no report is duplicated, and the round 1 fix only reworded a test comment that now matches the asserted behavior. ## Testing I drove the real `bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh scan` end to end in a disposable secondmate home with ten synthetic child tasks, once from an archive of the base commit and once from the target worktree, with and without config/pr-register-scan, and compared the lines relayed on the parent channel. The base reproduces the wrong-PR report and the target fixes it for the three A-registered, B-reported shapes, while the seven single-PR and guard cases and the whole opt-in path are unchanged. The focused test file tests/fm-inactive-reconcile.test.sh also passed in full on the target. No UI surface is involved, so the evidence is CLI output. The lab tmux primary from the runbook was not used because the changed function is reached only by this script's scan, which I ran directly. - Live validation: ✅ go - 6 of 6 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A-registered, B-reported: a child with recorded pr=pull/101 ends on `done: PR .../pull/202 checks green` (no scan opt-in) and the relayed parent-channel line carries pr=pull/202 | ✅ pass | live | target-default.txt, child a-registered-b-reported: text pull/202, pr=pull/202. base-default.txt shows pr=pull/101 for the same fixture, so the bug reproduces before the fix. | | A-registered, B-reported variants: the status log names PR A then a bare `done: PR B`, and a ready line with an `[at=...]` stamp, both relay pr=B | ✅ pass | live | target-default.txt, children a-then-b-in-log and b-reported-stamped: pr=pull/202. base-vs-target-default.diff shows both were pr=pull/101 on base. | | A task with one PR behaves exactly as on main: ready line names the recorded PR, a plain `done:` with a recorded PR, and a ready line with no recorded PR relay the same line on base and target | ✅ pass | live | base-vs-target-default.diff contains no line for children one-pr, one-pr-plain-done, or no-recorded-pr; target-default.txt shows pr=pull/101, pr=pull/101, and pr=pull/202 respectively. | | Adversarial: a different PR mentioned outside the ready-signal shape (prose mention, ready line with trailing words, `failed:` line) does not replace the recorded PR, and a scout carries no pr= | ✅ pass | live | target-default.txt: prose-mentions-b, ready-shape-with-tail, and failed-names-b keep pr=pull/101; scout-names-b has no pr= field. title: fix(bin): refuse teardown after a task's latest merge attempt was refused
body: ## Intent yes, submit the firstmate fix (The fix is for upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8782, "fm-teardown.sh should refuse when the task's most recent merge attempt was refused", which this home filed. A refused bin/fm-merge-local.sh or bin/fm-pr-merge.sh run, followed by teardown that was chained or piped so the refusal was hidden, let teardown close the task as landed while its work had never reached the default branch. This happened three times. The issue proposes: both merge scripts record each attempt's outcome in task metadata (e.g. last_merge_attempt=refused / merged ); fm-teardown.sh refuses, naming the refusal and reason, when the latest recorded attempt is refused and no later successful merge or landed proof supersedes it; explicit --force discard authorization still overrides. The maintainer's firstmate agent replied on the issue, confirmed it is still real on main, and labelled it ready-for-pr; read its full comment (it states a contract class and possibly constraints) and follow it.) The maintainer comment referenced above says: nothing in bin/ records a merge attempt's outcome in task metadata, so bin/fm-teardown.sh has no way to know the last attempt was refused. Contract class: new-default - teardown would start refusing in a case it allows today, for every home, so the fix needs the maintainer's (Kun's) word before it can merge unless it is gated behind a home-local flag (which would make it opt-in). It also asks whoever picks it up to look at which branch of the landed-work test let the local-only case pass: if that test passes a commit that never reached the default branch, that is a restore-class bug on its own, and fixing it may cover the case without new metadata.
