title: fix: stop false stuck alarms, repeated pane alerts, and silent un-rung messages
body:
## What was wrong

Three defects, observed in one night of monitoring real agent panes. They share
one cause: the monitor could not tell "busy because it is working" from "stuck",
counted one pane's quiet as many incidents, and could skip a due message without
saying so.

1. **A generating agent was treated as stuck.** A busy pane whose composer held
   text was read as an idle unsent draft, so a worker writing a long answer was
   classified as stuck twice and that alert cost it an interruption.
2. **One panel produced twelve identical alarms.** The quiet-pane escalation
   ladder published one escalation every `FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS` for as long as
   the pane sat still, with a counter that grew on every cycle and no bound by
   default.
3. **Three messages sat unread with their doorbell never typed.** The delivery
   attempt was skipped while the pane looked busy, and that skip was recorded
   only in a triage log that nobody reads.

## Fixes

1. **A generating agent is working, and its composer is still not ours to type
   into.** New `fm_busy_working_class` in `bin/fm-busy-lib.sh` resolves a pane's
   turn verdict plus its composer content into
   `working | idle | blocked | unknown`, and the busy-deferral budget
   (`stuck-busy`) is now reserved for a pane whose busy proof has outlived
   `FM_BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS`, so an agent that is generating never spends it.
   The steering-inbox guard uses that classification for stuck-detection only.
   Being busy is not permission to type: `fm_task_inbox_ring` keeps one
   condition, read from the composer content alone, so a proven `pending`
   composer holding anything but our own constant doorbell line is never typed
   into, idle or generating. Text in a composer belongs to whoever typed it -
   the captain, or the worker queueing its own follow-up - never to the turn, so
   our line plus Enter over it would submit their draft with ours appended. The
   skip is recorded in the task status with its reason and the retry ladder keeps
   advancing, while an empty composer or our own stuck doorbell still rings.
2. **One episode, one alarm.** A wedge episode - the window plus the exact stale
   render it is stuck on - now publishes at most `FM_WEDGE_ALARM_MAX`
   (default 2) escalations, the last one naming itself as the last, and then
   stays quiet until that pane renders something different. The budget is keyed
   to the stale render rather than to the poll timer, so a pane that flaps busy
   and back to the same frame is still one episode. It is applied to the
   unconfigured ladder only: an explicitly configured `FM_WEDGE_MAX_ESCALATIONS`
   keeps its own ceiling and its own ladder.
3. **A due message always rings, and a failed ring is visible.** A doorbell that
   was skipped, or that the backend could not confirm, is now written durably
   into the task's own status as a `note` line, once per record and failure,
   instead of disappearing into the log. The retry ladder keeps advancing as
   before.

## What proves each one

- `tests/fm-busy-state.test.sh` - a composer holding text together with an active
  turn classifies as `working` for every trusted busy source, while an idle pane
  holding a draft stays `blocked`, and T3-native uncertainty is not treated as a
  turn.
- `tests/fm-task-inbox.test.sh` - a generating pane rings its due doorbell and is
  never escalated as stuck-busy; the ring never types over composer text that is
  not its own doorbell line, idle or generating, while an empty composer and our
  own stuck line still ring; a ring that cannot be typed is recorded once in the
  task status and the retry ladder advances; and one watcher case drives a real
  generating pane holding the captain's draft - nothing is typed, the skip and
  its reason land in the task status, the record stays durable, and the same pane
  with an empty composer still rings. That watcher case fails against the
  previous commit, which types the doorbell over the draft.
- `tests/fm-watch-wedge-episode-bound.test.sh` (new) - the default bound publishes
  two alarms and then stays quiet with the escalation count frozen, a flapping
  pane stays one episode, a pane that renders something new starts a fresh
  episode, and `FM_WEDGE_ALARM_MAX` validation.
- `tests/fm-watch-wedge-cap.test.sh` - the configured-ceiling contract still holds
  unchanged, including its operator re-engagement path.
- The retired `fm-watch-wedge-cap-unconfigured-parity.test.sh` pinned the old
  unbounded ladder as byte-identical to the previous release, which cannot
  survive an intentional change to that ladder; the episode-bound suite above
  replaces what it proved.

## Not changed here, by the maintainer's decision

Two things this branch deliberately leaves alone, so their absence reads as the
maintainer's call rather than an oversight:

- the default silence after two alarms on a pane that stays stuck;
- the removal of the parity suite that pinned the previous escalation ladder.

## Suites run

`fm-busy-state`, `fm-task-inbox`, `fm-watch-inbox-meta`, `fm-watch-wedge-cap`,
`fm-watch-wedge-episode-bound`, `fm-watch-triage`, `fm-watch-triage-busy`,
`fm-watch-triage-wedge-defer`, `fm-watch-triage-pause`, `fm-send-settle`,
`fm-send-popup-settle`, `fm-daemon` - all green, plus the whole watcher regression
family (994 checks) with two load-related flakes that pass standalone.
`bin/fm-lint.sh` reports nothing for the changed files.
For the doorbell fix itself, the rerun was `fm-task-inbox`, `fm-busy-state`,
`fm-watch-inbox-meta`, `fm-watch-triage`, `fm-watch-triage-busy`,
`fm-watch-triage-wedge-defer`, `fm-watch-wedge-cap`,
`fm-watch-wedge-episode-bound`, `fm-send-inbox`, `fm-inbox` - all green, with
`bin/fm-lint.sh` and `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` clean.

title: supervision-host: open `needs-decision` pins all subsequent task wakes to `main-only`, compounded by unthrottled board-review `stale:` churn, self-merge `rearm-resurface`, and redundant `inactive-outcome` wakes
body:
#### Summary
In a 6.5-hour attended Claude Code primary session with the default Sonnet supervision host active (`389` primary calls, `178` Sonnet host calls, `89` watcher closes), the supervision host worked reliably (`51` handled, `32` silently absorbed, `0` timeouts/latches/mirror failures), yet **`37` closes (`41.6%`) bypassed the host as `pass-through attended main-only`**. Of those `37`, **`31` (`83.8%`)** were avoidable wakes caused by three interactions between `bin/fm-watch.sh`, `.pi/extensions/lib/fm-branch-dispatch.ts`, `bin/fm-merge-outcome-lib.sh`, and `bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh`, adding `66–79` avoidable primary calls (`17%–20%` of turns; `~19%–24%` of total primary cache-read weight via `O(N²)` context growth).

#### Bug 1: Open `needs-decision` forces all subsequent wakes of a task to `main-only` + unthrottled `stale:` churn on idle interactive-review workers

**Observed behavior:**
- On a review scout (`<review-task>`) with an armed Lavish board (`needs-decision [key=board-review]`):
  - While `[key=board-review]` was open, **15 closes** (`10:06–10:37` and `10:48–11:04`) bypassed the supervision host as `pass-through attended main-only` — only 3 carried new `needs-decision` lines; the other 12 were `turn-ended`, `stuck-busy`, `working:`, `paused:`, 6 plain `stale:` ticks, and 2 `possible wedge` escalations.
  - During a 4-minute window in between (`10:43–10:48`) when the worker wrote `resolved [key=board-review]` + `paused:`, the supervision host immediately resumed taking wakes (`2/2` handled) and `fm-watch.sh` absorbed `8` stale polls. As soon as `[key=board-review]` was re-opened, `main-only` pass-throughs immediately resumed (`8/8`).
- On a build ship (`<build-task>`) with an open PR:
  - Before `needs-decision [key=eval-board]` was appended, `6/6` closes were handled by the host (`5/5` idle `stale:` and `stuck-busy` wakes absorbed silently).
  - After `needs-decision [key=eval-board]` was appended — and even **after** the worker later appended `done: PR <url>` — `8/8` subsequent closes (`stuck-busy`, `done:`, `turn-ended`, and 4 idle `stale:` wakes) bypassed the host as `pass-through attended main-only`.
- On a third task (`<other-review-task>`) with an open `needs-decision [key=board-review]` from the prior day, resolving that key with `fm-send.sh --resolve-key board-review` caused the supervision host to absorb its `stale:` wake 3 seconds later.

**Root cause in code:**
1. **Whole-log `openDecisions` pinning for single-task crewmates:** `.pi/extensions/lib/fm-branch-dispatch.ts:485-549` (`scopeForUnreadWake`) already uses `spanIsDecisionOwned` + `.status-presentation-cursor` for second-mate signals (commit `5a9880b4` / `#5879`, specifically so routine updates are not pinned behind an already-presented parked decision). Single-task crewmates (`attendedHost=true`) and `stale:` rows still fold the **entire** status log (`[...open.values()].includes("needs-decision")`), pinning every subsequent `stale:`, `stuck-busy`, `working:`, `paused:`, and `done:` wake to `main-only` for the entire time any `needs-decision` key remains open.
2. **Unthrottled new-hash `stale_is_terminal` wakes on `needs-decision`:** In `bin/fm-watch.sh:4657-4694`, when a worker's newest status line is `needs-decision` (such as an armed Lavish board review) and no backlog captain-hold exists on that exact task ID, `captain_call_stale_bound` returns false. Every idle TUI footer/clock change produces a new `hash_pane` and surfaces a fresh `stale:` wake; and if the worker appends `working:` while the decision key stays open, `stale_is_terminal` flips false and drives the pane into `wedge_timer_check` (`escalation 1`, `escalation 2`). Even `config/wedge-defer-worker-wait` (`fm-watch.sh:1710`) only acts at the wedge timer for a newest `needs-decision`/`blocked` line, not on first-sight new-hash `stale_is_terminal` wakes.

**Suggested fix:**
- Extend the `.status-presentation-cursor` + `spanIsDecisionOwned` rule from `#5879` to single-task crewmate `signal` rows on the attended host so only newly-presented decision lines force `main-only` (keeping the branch actor's `fm-send --resolve-key` refusal intact), and allow the attended host to triage routine `stale:` wakes once the task's open `needs-decision` has already been presented to main.
- Throttle repeated new-hash `stale_is_terminal` wakes in `bin/fm-watch.sh:4657-4694` for an already-surfaced `needs-decision` line (matching `captain_call_stale_bound`'s `FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS` cadence once the first sight has surfaced, reset on any status-log change).

#### Bug 2: `check: rearm-resurface` fires on self-merges and masks branch-eligible / empty queues as `main-only`

_Related: #7761 reports the empty-queue `rearm-resurface` symptom; this section adds two distinct causes (self-merge `check: merge landed:` queueing, and unconditional `main-only` routing of `^check:` closes)._

**Observed behavior:**
- `10` of `37` `pass-through attended main-only` events were `check: rearm-resurface`:
  - `5` fired ~20s after main itself ran `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh`, injecting mid-turn `Stop hook feedback` and forcing extra `fm-wake-drain.sh` + `--ack-through` calls to acknowledge `check: merge landed:` for main's own merge.
  - `1` fired on an empty queue (`--ack-through 0`) immediately after session takeover.
  - `2` fired when a detached successor exited on branch-eligible wakes (`stale:` and `resolved`+`done:`) during a main turn, forcing those branch-eligible rows to `main-only`.

**Root cause in code:**
1. `bin/fm-merge-outcome-lib.sh:103-105` appends `check: merge landed:` to `.wake-queue` whenever `[ "$origin" = poll ] || [ -z "$destination" ]`. In a main home (`destination=""`), even `origin=self` appends a queued `check` wake and publishes `pending:downtime` (`bin/fm-wake-lib.sh:2785`), causing the parked watcher to exit with `check: rearm-resurface`.
2. `.pi/extensions/lib/fm-branch-dispatch.ts:613,628` (`branchOfferForWake`) sets `isCheckTrigger = /^check:/.test(message)` unconditionally, so `check: rearm-resurface` is always forced `main-only` without inspecting whether `.wake-queue` is empty or contains only branch-eligible rows.

**Suggested fix:**
- In `bin/fm-merge-outcome-lib.sh:103`, skip queueing a local `check: merge landed:` wake in a main home when `origin=self` (or when called by `fm-pr-merge.sh` with `FM_SUPERVISION_ACTOR=main`, which already verified the merge synchronously; keep it for `origin=poll` and away-branch merges).
- In `branchOfferForWake`, special-case `check: rearm-resurface` to delegate eligibility to `scopeForUnreadWake` (routing to the host when `.wake-queue` contains branch-eligible rows, and only to main when main-only rows exist or recovery acknowledgement alone is required).

#### Bug 3: Redundant `check: inactive-outcome` wakes on already-presented `done` tasks + duplicate fingerprint when `done:` has trailing prose

**Observed behavior:**
- After `<build-task>` reported `done: PR <url>`, the supervision host handled it and main relayed PR `<url>` to the user (`branch-outcome` marked processed). `17` minutes later, `fm-inactive-reconcile.sh` emitted `check: inactive-outcome` (`pr=<url>`), passing through `main-only`.
- Later, `<build-task>` pushed follow-up fixes and wrote `done [at=...]: PR <url> (<summary prose>)`, which main drained and acknowledged. `36` minutes later, `fm-inactive-reconcile.sh` emitted a **second** `check: inactive-outcome` for the exact same task and `spawn_gen` incarnation, this time with `pr=` empty (`<fp-2>` vs `<fp-1>`).

**Root cause in code:**
1. Ordinary `signal:` presentation (`bin/fm-wake-drain.sh`) and `branch-outcome` acknowledgement (`bin/fm-branch-outcome.sh mark-processed`) never write a `.presented` receipt into `state/terminal-outcomes/`, so `bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh:664-712` treats any still-open `done` lane older than `FM_INACTIVE_RECONCILE_SECS` (`900s`) as unpresented.
2. `terminal_outcome_pr()` (`bin/fm-inactive-reconcile.sh:401`) calls `fm_dod_ready_note_url` (`bin/fm-dod-lib.sh:837-846`), which rejects any text after the URL (even a parenthetical summary), returning empty `pr=""` and producing a distinct SHA-256 fingerprint (`incarnation|id|state|pr`) for the same incarnation and PR.

**Suggested fix:**
- Record (or check) terminal presentation when a `done:`/`failed:` wake is acknowledged by main or a `branch-outcome` covering that status endpoint is marked processed, so `fm-inactive-reconcile.sh` remains a true missed-outcome backstop rather than firing on already-acknowledged PRs.
- In `terminal_outcome_pr()`, fall back to recorded `meta pr=` (when named in the status log) or avoid minting a second `pr=""` receipt for an incarnation that already has a `.presented` `done` receipt with a verified PR.

title: test(fm-control): parse key-gap timestamps under LC_ALL=C
body:
## Intent The fm-control key-gap timestamp test fails under a non-C locale, because awk formats and compares the timestamp gap with the locale's decimal separator. Parse the timestamps under LC_ALL=C so the test is portable. ## What Changed - `first_key_gap` in `tests/fm-control.test.sh` now runs its `awk` under `LC_ALL=C`, so the key-time timestamps are parsed with `.` as the decimal separator whatever the caller's locale. - The `awk` check in `test_devin_interrupt_invalidates_busy` that the second Escape came at least 0.5s after the first also runs under `LC_ALL=C`. This keeps the gap comparison consistent with the parsing above. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Two-line test-only change that prefixes the awk calls with LC_ALL=C, which matches the stated intent. The perl timestamp writer is unaffected by locale. ## Testing I ran test_devin_interrupt_invalidates_busy on its own from the fixed and base versions of the test file, because the full file exceeded the time limit. It passes on the fixed version under de_DE.UTF-8 and C, and on the base version under de_DE.UTF-8. So the original failure did not reproduce at test level here. A direct awk reproduction under de_DE.UTF-8 does show the mechanism: the unpinned parse of the key-times file gave a 0,000 gap, and the pinned C parse gave 0.700. - Live validation: ✅ go - 3 of 3 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Devin interrupt test passes under a comma-decimal locale (de_DE.UTF-8) with the fix | ✅ pass | live | Trimmed run of the fixed fm-control.test.sh under LC_ALL=de_DE.UTF-8 printed 'ok - fm-control Devin interrupt ...' | | Devin interrupt test still passes under LC_ALL=C | ✅ pass | live | Trimmed run of the fixed fm-control.test.sh under LC_ALL=C printed 'ok - fm-control Devin interrupt ...' | | The unpinned awk parse of key-gap timestamps is locale-sensitive and the C pin fixes it | ✅ pass | live | Under de_DE.UTF-8 the unpinned awk printed a gap of 0,000 for timestamps 100.000 and 100.700. title: omp watcher stays disarmed after session_shutdown when the session keeps running
body:
## Summary

On omp, the primary watcher extension (`.omp/extensions/fm-primary-omp-watch.ts`) can be left permanently disarmed in a session that keeps running. After omp emits `session_shutdown` without a following `session_start` in the same process, every `fm_watch_arm_omp` call returns `watcher: not armed - omp session is shutting down`, and the turn-end guard fires `TURN WOULD END BLIND - supervision is off` at the end of every turn. The only recovery is to start a new omp session.

## Environment

- omp 19.2.1 (primary harness)
- firstmate at `aa6c1235` (2026-11-26)

## What happened

- In a long primary session, the conversation was compacted and resumed in the same omp process (earlier history was archived and the session continued).
- From then on, `fm_watch_arm_omp` returned `watcher: not armed - omp session is shutting down` on every call, for more than an hour, across many turns.
- `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh` kept reporting `watcher still down (same stale episode ...)`, and the turn-end guard injected the "TURN WOULD END BLIND" banner after every reply.
- Wakes stayed durable and could be drained by hand, so nothing was lost, but there were no automatic wakes for the rest of the session.

I did not capture the exact omp event sequence; that compaction/resume emitted `session_shutdown` is an inference from the timing.

## Cause (from reading the extension)

- `session_shutdown` calls `stopSessionGeneration(generation, true)`, which sets `generation.stopping = true` (`stopGeneration`).
- `generationIsLive(owner)` requires `!generation.stopping`, and `startArm` / the `fm_watch_arm_omp` tool return `shuttingDownMessage` when it is false.
- A new generation is created only in the `session_start` handler (`if (generation.stopping) generation = createGeneration();`).
- So if omp emits `session_shutdown` for an in-place transition (the header already notes it carries no reason) and the same session keeps taking turns without a new `session_start`, the generation stays stopped for good and nothing can re-arm it.

## Expected

If the session keeps running after `session_shutdown` (a model turn starts, or the arm tool or `/fm-watch-arm-omp` is invoked while the lock is still owned by this process), the extension should start a fresh generation and arm again rather than refuse forever. One option: in the tool/command path, when `generation.stopping` is true and `lockOwnership() === "owned"`, create and activate a new generation, then call `activateOwnedWatch`, replaying any persisted replacement handoff as `session_start` would.

## Workaround

Start a fresh omp session in the home; the watcher arms at `session_start`.

title: pr-health: no read settles when each gh call is slow, and the monitor stays silent
body:
## Observed

On `aa6c1235`, `poll` in `bin/fm-pr-health.sh` starts three `gh` processes per selected PR (REST, GraphQL rollup, GraphQL suites; around lines 334-341). It starts every selected PR in one wave (around lines 562-571), and caps each process at 5 s (`[ "$left" -le 5 ] || left=5`, around line 199).
When one `gh` process costs about 2.5 s (here a credential-broker wrapper around `gh`), 30 or more concurrent processes all pass the cap. Every read fails, the URL goes back to `notifications.pending`, and nothing is printed.
Measured in one home with 64 owned PRs:

| PRs in one wave | gh processes | Settled |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3 | 1/1 |
| 4 | 12 | 4/4 |
| 10 | 30 | 0/10 |
| 64 | 192 | 0/64 |

In that home no PR has settled since 2026-11-24, so every pr-health line (conflicts, failing checks, author action, and the opt-in reports) stopped without any sign.

## Expected

The monitor makes progress when `gh` is slow, and a monitor that cannot settle any read says so.

## Possible fix

- Read at most N PRs per pass in the existing priority order; the rest stay in `pending`, which the code already carries to the next pass.
- Give each process the remaining deadline instead of a fixed 5 s cap.
- Print one line when a PR stays unsettled past a bound, so a total outage is visible.
- A larger option: one aliased GraphQL read for many PRs, since the cost is per `gh` process.

Related: the stale-review field and notifications-cursor fixes are in a separate PR.

title: Codex 0.172: Codex captains silently lose watcher supervision (checkpoint gets backgrounded; Stop park pinned to 0.163 and its codex queue wake isn't consumed)
body:
**What happened**
We upgraded a Codex primary from codex-cli 0.163.0 to 0.172.0 (gpt-6.2-sol, Herdr backend). The home used the foreground-checkpoint protocol. On 0.172 the captain runs `bin/fm-watch-checkpoint.sh --seconds 180` through `tools.exec_command({cmd, yield_time_ms: 1000})`. After the yield, Codex returns a `session_id` and leaves the command running as a background terminal. The model then ends its turn. The checkpoint finishes with no one listening and nothing re-arms the watcher. The captain sat idle for about an hour with about 37 tasks in flight. `fm-guard` printed WATCHER DOWN once, then only one-line reminders. The Codex Stop guard blocks just once per episode, because `stop_hook_active` lets the second stop through.

**The model-free Stop park doesn't cover 0.172 either**
- `fm-codex-stop-park.sh` `verified_cli` accepts only `codex-cli 0.163.0`.
- With 0.172.0 allowed and the session registered, the async Stop hook does fire, and the park arms and watches correctly. But delivery through `codex queue --thread <id> --message ...` returns rc 0 and only writes a row to `~/.codex/queue_1.sqlite` (`queued_items`). The running TUI, which sits on an app-server daemon in 0.172, never consumes it. The park records `delivered` while the wake is lost. A plain test message we queued is also still stuck there.

**Proposed**
1. Docs (small, tested locally): in AGENTS.md section 8 and `codex-checkpoint.md` rule 6, say that a supervision wait the harness moved to a background session (`session_id` returned) is not a live cycle. Keep waiting on it (`write_stdin` with empty input) until it exits, and never end a turn while it runs with work under way. Patch: 2 files, +3 lines.
2. Park on 0.172: find a delivery path the 0.172 TUI actually consumes (perhaps `codex queue --resume`, or the app-server thread API), and verify it before adding 0.172 to the allowlist.
3. Make the gap loud:
   - (a) warn at session start when a Codex primary's CLI is not on the park's verified list;
   - (b) let the Codex Stop guard keep blocking within a bounded budget, as Claude's does, while supervision is needed and no watcher is live;
   - (c) have the park confirm the queued item was consumed before recording `delivered`.

Happy to share logs or the patch.

title: Rex backend still requires REX_SESSION, which Rex stopped setting in 0.1.0-preview.23
body:
## What happens

With Firstmate running directly in a Rex terminal on Rex 0.1.0-preview.25, the Rex backend does not recognise that it is running inside Rex.
Every spawned task tab goes into a separately created per-home Rex session instead of Firstmate's own session.

The terminal environment has `TERM_PROGRAM=rex`, `REX_BLOCK`, `REX_SERVER`, and `REX_BIN_DIR`, but no `REX_SESSION`.

## Why

This is an intentional Rex change.
Since 0.1.0-preview.23, `REX_BLOCK` replaces `REX_SESSION`, and new terminals no longer set `REX_SESSION`.
Anywhere a session is expected, scripts should pass `"$REX_BLOCK"` (for example `-s "$REX_BLOCK"` or `rex session rename "$REX_BLOCK" name`), and Rex resolves it to the session that holds that block.
See https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/automate/cli#command-targets.

Firstmate still gates on `REX_SESSION`:

- `bin/backends/rex.sh` `fm_backend_rex_launcher_session` requires `REX_SESSION`, so it falls through to the per-home session path.
- `bin/backends/rex.sh` places a new secondmate session with `session move --after "$REX_SESSION"`, which is skipped.
- `bin/backends/rex.sh` `fm_backend_rex_retire_session` guards the launcher's own session by comparing against `REX_SESSION`, which is now empty.
- `bin/fm-supervisor-target-lib.sh` `fm_supervisor_in_rex` requires `REX_SESSION` and composes the supervisor target from it, so away and quiet supervision cannot discover a Rex-hosted primary.
- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` forwards `REX_SESSION` to workers, and `bin/fm-osc7501.sh` checks it.
- `docs/rex-backend.md` and `docs/configuration.md` state that Rex exports `REX_SESSION` into every block.

## Repro

1. Run Rex 0.1.0-preview.23 or later and start a Firstmate primary in a Rex terminal.
2. Confirm `env | grep REX_` shows `REX_BLOCK` and no `REX_SESSION`.
3. Spawn any scout or ship.
4. `rex session list` shows a new session labeled with the home tag holding the task tab, instead of the tab opening in the primary's session.

## Expected

Detect Rex from `TERM_PROGRAM=rex` plus `REX_BLOCK` alone, and resolve the launcher session by asking the server which session holds `REX_BLOCK`.
Since `REX_SESSION` is gone, a `REX_SESSION` fallback is not wanted.

## Related observation

Rex's own Claude Code SessionStart hook tells every agent to run `rex session rename <label>` for the session that contains its pane.
A Claude worker in a per-home Rex session followed it and relabeled that session to its task name, after which the backend no longer finds the per-home session by its home-tag label and creates another one.
Once task tabs land in the primary's session as intended, a worker following that hook would relabel the primary's own session instead.

## References

- Rex CLI command targets: https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/automate/cli#command-targets

title: fix(supervision-host): open a new engine conversation when the branch prompt changes
body:
## What Changed
- `bin/fm-supervision-host.sh`: the host now generates the branch prompt before every turn (new `refresh_branch_prompt`) and stores its digest. `choose_conversation` resumes the saved engine conversation only when the digest recorded in `.supervision-host-engine` matches the freshly generated prompt. `write_engine_record` now writes a `prompt_digest` field.
- If prompt generation fails, the host logs `prompt-generation-failed` and does not resume the saved conversation.
- `docs/supervision-host.md`: lists the prompt-digest change as a third case that opens a new conversation. Documents the generation-failure behavior.
- `tests/fm-supervision-host.test.sh`: adds test coverage for this behavior.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is small and bounded. It meets every intent requirement: it compares a digest, replaces the conversation only on a change, logs a generation failure, keeps the reuse test and updates the docs. The prompt generator is byte-stable, so an unchanged prompt does not cause needless rotation. The only gap is a minor warm-compact cost edge.

## Testing

I ran the repo's host tests. They drive the real `fm-supervision-host.sh` with a stub engine, an isolated home and real prompt generation. The three new tests passed on the target commit. Against the base host script, the changed-prompt test failed, so it reproduces the reported bug. The full suite aborted once at `test_return_during_a_failed_turn_still_hands_its_outcomes_to_main`, which does not touch prompt handling. title: fix: read stale PR reviews from latestOpinionatedReviews
body:
## What Changed - `bin/fm-pr-health.sh`: the GraphQL query and the jq step now read `latestOpinionatedReviews` instead of `latestReviews` when they look for stale `CHANGES_REQUESTED` reviews. The header comment matches. - `bin/fm-pr-health.sh`: `read_notifications` keeps the previous `Last-Modified` value (`next_lm=$lm`) when the notifications response has no `Last-Modified` header. - `tests/fm-pr-health.test.sh`: the test fixtures and cases now use `latestOpinionatedReviews`, with added cases for this behavior. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Both fixes are small and do what the intent asks: the review query moves from latestReviews to latestOpinionatedReviews, and a missing Last-Modified now keeps the previous value. Each comes with a regression test that would fail on the base code, and the only finding is a wrong test label. ## Testing I ran the pr-health suite, which runs the real monitor script against a stubbed gh. The stub models the cor3-companion shape: an empty latestReviews, the review held in latestOpinionatedReviews, and the reviewer still in reviewRequests. It also models a `since=` notifications response with no Last-Modified header. On the target commit the stale-review line fires and the stored cursor survives, and the next pass answers 304 with no full sweep. With the base-commit script swapped in, both new tests fail, so they catch the defects. title: fix(bin): skip harness detection on idle wake drains
body:
An idle wake drain can run harness detection twice before returning an empty result. The liveness guard resolves the supervision model before checking whether anything needs supervision, and branch outcome presentation resolves the primary harness before checking whether the outcome file has any records. Check supervision demand before computing watcher health, and check for a nonempty outcome file before resolving its presentation owner. The same watcher health and outcome ownership checks still run when their results are needed. The regression observes detector invocations while running the real drain. It checks that an idle drain returns silently with no probes and that a drain with a stored outcome still detects the harness and presents the outcome. ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

title: fix(bin): fail a request-id replay whose note was never written
body:
Fixes #8716
## Intent

Fix `#8716` within the scope the maintainer triage set there (contract class: restore). In bin/fm-inbox.sh, publish_from_reservation runs inside `id=$(...) || die`, where errexit does not apply, so a failed mktemp, write_note_file or mv still returned 0 and a `note --request-id` replay reported saved:true, acknowledged:true for a note that was never written. Make each of those three steps fail the call: a failed mktemp returns 1, and a failed write_note_file or mv removes the staging file and returns 1, so the replay exits 1 with the reservation kept and a later retry with the same request id writes and announces the note once. Add one case to tests/fm-inbox.test.sh that fails before the fix and passes after. One function, the refusal text of its two callers in queue_note, and one test; nothing else. Not in scope and left unchanged: in write_note_file an earlier printf failure can still be masked by its final command's status; that older gap is in every note write, not only the replay. The pull request body carries `Fixes #8716`.

## What Changed

- `publish_from_reservation` in `bin/fm-inbox.sh` now returns 1 when any of its three write steps fails. A failed `mktemp` returns 1 right away. A failed `write_note_file` or `mv` deletes the staging file and then returns 1. Before this, the function ran inside `id=$(...) || die`, where errexit does not apply, so these failures still returned 0. A `note --request-id` replay then reported `saved:true, acknowledged:true` for a note that had never been written.
- Both `queue_note` callers now refuse with "reserved but its note could not be read or written; retry the same request id". The old message said only "unreadable".
- A new case in `tests/fm-inbox.test.sh` puts a `mktemp` shim on `PATH` that fails only for staging files. It checks that the replay exits 1, prints no replay receipt, publishes no note, appends no wake and keeps the reservation. It then checks that a healthy retry with the same request id publishes the reserved note id and announces it exactly once.

Fixes `#8716`

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is small. It checks the return codes of mktemp, write_note_file and mv inside publish_from_reservation, removes the staging file on failure and updates the refusal text at both queue_note callers. That matches the stated intent exactly, and the new test fails before the fix (the empty tmp led to a missing note, which announce_note reported as rc 2, so the replay came back as acknowledged with exit 0) and passes after it.

## Testing

I ran the real fm-inbox CLI in throwaway homes and made each of the three write steps fail with a PATH stub. In every case the replay is now refused with exit 1: no receipt is printed, no note is written, no wake is added, no staging file is left behind and the reservation is kept. A later retry then publishes and announces the reserved note exactly once. The base commit gives a false receipt (saved:true, acknowledged:true) on the same inputs, and a normal replay is unchanged. The new test passes at the target and fails with the base script at the expected assertion. There is no UI surface, so the evidence is the CLI transcripts.

```text
real_mktemp=$(command -v mktemp); real_mv=$(command -v mv)
mk() { h="$W/$1"; mkdir -p "$h/state/inbox/.requests" "$h/data" "$h/config"; printf '%s\n' "$2" > "$h/state/inbox/.requests/rid"; echo "$h"; }
run() { h=$1; shift; FM_HOME="$h" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$h/state" FM_DATA_OVERRIDE="$h/data" FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$h/config" "$BIN" "$@" </dev/null; }
show() { h=$1; echo "  pending notes: $(ls "$h/state/inbox"/*.note 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')  staging leftovers: $(ls -A "$h/state/inbox" | grep -c '^\.staging-')  reservation kept: $([ -f "$h/state/inbox/.requests/rid" ] && echo yes || echo no)  wakes: $(grep -c inbox: "$h/state/.wake-queue" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"; }
stub() { d="$W/stub-$1"; mkdir -p "$d"; printf '%s\n' "#!/bin/sh" "$2" > "$d/$3"; chmod +x "$d/$3"; echo "$d"; }

echo "=== S1: replay, mktemp of staging file fails ==="
h=$(mk s1 1700000000-sone)
s=$(stub mk 'case "$*" in *.staging-*) exit 1;; esac; exec '"$real_mktemp"' "$@"' mktemp)
out=$(PATH="$s:$PATH" run "$h" note --request-id rid --json "answer" 2>&1); echo "  exit=$? out: $out"; show "$h"

out=$(run "$h" note --request-id rid --json "answer" 2>&1); echo "  exit=$? out: $out"; show "$h"

out=$(run "$h" note --request-id rid --json "answer" 2>&1); echo "  retry exit=$? out: $out"; show "$h"

echo "=== S3: replay, mv of staging into place fails ==="
h=$(mk s3 1700000000-sthree)
s=$(stub mv 'case "$*" in *.staging-*) exit 1;; esac; exec '"$real_mv"' "$@"' mv)
out=$(PATH="$s:$PATH" run "$h" note --request-id rid --json "answer" 2>&1); echo "  exit=$? out: $out"; show "$h"
out=$(run "$h" note --request-id rid --json "answer" 2>&1); echo "  retry exit=$? out: $out"; show "$h"

echo "=== S4: fresh note then replay (happy path unchanged) ==="
h="$W/s4"; mkdir -p "$h/state" "$h/data" "$h/config"
out=$(run "$h" note --request-id fresh --json "first" 2>&1); echo "  exit=$? out: $out"
out=$(run "$h" note --request-id fresh --json "first" 2>&1); echo "  replay exit=$? out: $out"
echo "  pending notes: $(ls "$h/state/inbox"/*.note | wc -l | tr -d ' ') wakes: $(grep -c inbox: "$h/state/.wake-queue")"
rm -rf "$W"
```

title: Arm daily startup growth checks and gate weekly stow wakes
body:
## What changed

- Bootstrap registers the authenticated daily growth check for homes with a startup-memory budget, including secondmates with an inherited budget.
- An actionable overrun can emit one weekly `run the stow pass` wake with `config/record-sweep=on`. Shadow mode records candidates without waking or consuming the live cooldown.
- The internal stow pass includes the exact active Claude project auto-memory index as a read-only fourth input. Unattended and offline reports do not guess a Claude account.

No memory files, Claude account directories, or record-sweep implementation are changed.

## Verification

- `bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-startup-growth-check.test.sh tests/fm-startup-memory-budget.test.sh tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh tests/fm-stow-cascade.test.sh`: 4 passed.

title: fix(bin): let Claude Stop auto-arm rewake on handling-phase and markerless actionable wakes
body:
## Intent

Contribute the fork's narrowed fix for actionable Claude Stop rewakes to the upstream Firstmate repository. When Claude stops while a watcher wake is actionable (a pending or handling recovery marker, or no marker at all), the Stop auto-arm in bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh refuses to re-arm itself, so an actionable wake can go unhandled after a Claude stop. The fork fixed this in commit 1ef3a52a (branch restore/autoarm-actionable-rewake; paths bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh and tests/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.test.sh; 4 production lines and 70 test lines). The captain approved one-task consent to publish this single narrowed contribution to github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate (restore-kit item autoarm-actionable-rewake, classified C narrowed on 2026-11-27).

## What Changed
- `bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh`: when a wake is actionable, `autoarm_commit` now commits a rewake in two cases where it used to return early and skip it. The first is a `pending:handling:*` or `announced:handling:*` recovery marker, allowed only when host mode is off; the epoch records that marker's recovery generation. The second is no recovery marker at all; the epoch records an empty recovery generation. Other marker states still return early as before.
- `tests/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.test.sh`: adds `handling-actionable` and `markerless-actionable` arm fixtures and two tests. Each test checks that the Stop hook exits 2 with the wake banner and the arm's reason line, and that the epoch records `outcome=rewake`. The handling test also checks that the epoch keeps the recovery generation. The markerless test checks that the epoch stays bound to the Claude session that owns the lock and records no recovery generation.
- `docs/watcher-continuity.md`: adds these host-off handling-marker and markerless rewakes to the list of behaviors the tests cover.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: This is a 4-line change to one case statement. It keeps the existing host-mode refusal for handling markers, which the host-mode fallback path and existing tests depend on, and its only downstream consumer (fm_autoarm_midturn_healthy) already treats an empty recovery generation as not healthy. The two new tests run the hook and check its exit code, output and ledger, and they would have failed before the fix.

## Testing

I ran the real Stop hook script, which Claude runs as its Stop hook, from both the base and the target commit inside throwaway fixture homes. The watcher arm and supervision host were small fixture scripts that write each scenario's recovery marker. At the base commit, a pending or announced:handling marker and a missing marker all exited 0, so the actionable wake was silently dropped. That reproduces the reported bug. At the target commit, all three exit 2 and deliver the wake banner plus the reason line. The epoch records outcome=rewake with the lock-owning session_pid, the handling generation is bound, and the markerless case records no recovery generation. Downtime-marker rewakes are unchanged. The adversarial cases still hold: an unknown 'acked:handling' token is refused (exit 0), and a handling marker in supervision-host mode is refused, which ends in outcome=failed with no generation bound. One side effect: in host mode, a markerless wake now rewakes, where the base exited 0. This matches the intent's "or no marker at all" wording. The hook's own test file passed in full (exit 0), including the two new tests. I did not drive a full Claude lab primary: the hook script is the product surface the change touches, and I ran it directly. The hook is a CLI, so there is no UI evidence. The worktree is clean and no temp dirs or background jobs remain.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 7 of 7 scenarios driven live against the product

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude stops while the arm reports an actionable wake with a pending:handling marker: the hook exits 2, delivers the wake banner and reason line, and records outcome=rewake bound to the handling gener… | ✅ pass | live | drive-autoarm.transcript.txt: handling-pending base exit=0 (outcome=arming, wake dropped); HEAD exit=2, outcome=rewake recovery_generation=gen-h1 |
| Claude stops with an announced:handling marker: the hook exits 2 and binds that generation | ✅ pass | live | drive-autoarm.transcript.txt: handling-announced base exit=0; HEAD exit=2, recovery_generation=gen-h2 |
| Claude stops on an actionable wake with no .watcher-down marker: the hook exits 2, records rewake bound to the session lock, and records no recovery generation | ✅ pass | live | drive-autoarm.transcript.txt: markerless base exit=0; HEAD exit=2, outcome=rewake session_pid=<lock pid>, no recovery_generation |
| Regression: a pending:downtime marker still rewakes exactly as before | ✅ pass | live | drive-autoarm.transcript.txt: downtime-regression exit=2 and recovery_generation=gen-d1 at both base and HEAD |
| Adversarial: an unrecognized marker token (acked:handling) is still refused, with exit 0 and no rewake | ✅ pass | live | drive-autoarm.transcript.txt: adversarial-unknown-token HEAD exit=0, outcome=arming |

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Drives the real bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh (base vs target) as a Claude Stop hook
# in disposable fixture homes. Usage: drive-autoarm.sh <worktree> <base-sha>
set -u
WT=$1 BASE=$2
TMP=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fm-autoarm-drive.XXXXXX"); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$TMP/fakebin"; ln -s /bin/bash "$TMP/fakebin/claude"
LIBS="fm-primary-scope-lib.sh fm-supervision-lib.sh fm-wake-lib.sh fm-path-lib.sh fm-session-lock-lib.sh fm-omp-process-lib.sh fm-cursor-lib.sh fm-hook-host-lib.sh fm-lock.sh fm-lease-lib.sh fm-afk-contract.sh fm-classify-lib.sh fm-timeout-lib.sh fm-supervision-engine-lib.sh"
mkhome() { # <dir> <rev> <marker|NONE> <reason-line> <hostmode 0|1>
  local d=$1 rev=$2 marker=$3 reason=$4 host=$5 f
  mkdir -p "$d/state" "$d/config" "$d/bin"; git init -q "$d"; git -C "$d" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@e.invalid commit -q --allow-empty -m init
  : > "$d/AGENTS.md"; : > "$d/state/task.meta"
  [ "$host" = 1 ] || : > "$d/config/supervision-host-off"
  for f in fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh $LIBS; do git -C "$WT" show "$rev:bin/$f" > "$d/bin/$f"; done
  chmod +x "$d/bin/"*.sh
  local writer
  if [ "$marker" = NONE ]; then writer='rm -f "$FM_HOME/state/.watcher-down"'
  else writer="printf '%s\n' '$marker' > \"\$FM_HOME/state/.watcher-down\""; fi
  local script; [ "$host" = 1 ] && script=fm-supervision-host.sh || script=fm-watch-arm.sh
  cat > "$d/bin/$script" <<SH
#!/usr/bin/env bash
$writer
touch "\$FM_HOME/state/.last-watcher-beat"
printf 'watcher: started pid=%s (beacon fresh)\n' "\$\$"
printf '%s\n' '$reason'
exit 0
SH
  chmod +x "$d/bin/$script"
}
run() { # <label> <rev> <marker> <reason> <host>
  local d="$TMP/$1-$2" rc=0 out
  mkhome "$d" "$2" "$3" "$4" "$5"
  out=$(printf '%s\n' '{"session_id":"sess-drive","stop_hook_active":false}' | FM_HOME="$d" "$TMP/fakebin/claude" -c 'printf "%s\n" "$$" > "$FM_HOME/state/.lock"; exec "$FM_HOME/bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh"' 2>&1) || rc=$?
  echo "=== scenario=$1 rev=$2 host_mode=$5 marker=$3"
  echo "exit=$rc"
  echo "--- hook stderr/stdout (delivered to Claude on exit 2):"; printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed 's/^/  | /'
  echo "--- state/.claude-autoarm-epoch:"; sed 's/^/  | /' "$d/state/.claude-autoarm-epoch" 2>/dev/null || echo "  | (absent)"
  echo
}
for rev in "$BASE" HEAD; do
  run handling-pending "$rev" 'pending:handling:gen-h1' 'stale: fixture-win actionable' 0
  run handling-announced "$rev" 'announced:handling:gen-h2' 'signal: fixture actionable' 0
```

title: Scout teardown refusal omits blocking decision keys and actionable recovery command
body:
## Observed
A field inventory found 20 leased work copies and 38 available across eight pools. Every leased copy had a lane record. Exiting an agent left an idle shell and retained the lease; guarded teardown was the release path.

Finished scouts with reports, clean trees, and no commits ahead could remain unsweepable while old status-stream decisions stayed open. The scout completion refusal named the lane but not the blocking decision keys or a concrete recovery command. Fleet views also lacked per-host free-versus-leased counts. These are field observations, not yet a clean-home reproduction of every condition.

## Narrow proposed change
Make the scout teardown refusal identify blocking decision keys and the exact existing command needed to clear the completion requirement, with behavioral coverage. Preserve explicit-answer requirements and all unlanded-work protection. Do not silently resolve old decisions.

## Out of scope for the accompanying fix
Automatic sweeping, new no-agent classification, inventory counts, decision transfer behavior, and local-only revised-head adoption. Those observations are recorded here for separate consideration.

The maintainer confirmed the race and said the suggested fix brings the two branches into line. Keep the old holder's clean-exit assertion. ## What Changed - In `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh`, the `successor_first=0` branch now passes when either `claimed` is 1 or the successor's output contains a `^check: ` line. Before, it required `claimed` to be 1, so the test failed when the successor had already woken and released the lock before the test observed the claim. - This brings the branch into line with the `successor_first=1` branch, which already accepts the `^check: ` line as proof of the claim. - The failure message and the later assertion on the old holder's clean exit are unchanged. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a two-line test-only edit that makes the successor_first=0 branch accept the successor's '^check: ' output exactly as the successor_first=1 branch does, and the old holder's clean-exit assertions are untouched; bin/fm-watch.sh prints only 'watcher: already running' on the stand-down path (line 3784), so a check: line still proves the successor held the lock. ## Testing I ran the full tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh once at the target commit (exit 0, 3m15s), which drives the real bin/fm-watch.sh. title: fix(bin): read owned PRs in bounded waves and report stuck reads
body:
Fixes #8795 ## What Changed - `bin/fm-pr-health.sh` reads owned PRs in waves of `READ_WAVE` (4), in listed order. Each read gets the time left before the check timeout, with a floor of `READ_FLOOR` seconds. PRs the timeout leaves unreached stay pending for the next pass. PRs whose read failed are recorded in `read_failed` and listed after untried PRs, so one stuck PR cannot hold back the rest. - When a pass selects PRs and none of their reads settles, the script prints one line per cause (timeout, or no usable answer) for the PRs that newly fail. A PR prints again only after one of its reads completes. `read_pr` records a `timeout` cause, and `read_failed` entries are pruned when a PR is no longer owned. - `docs/configuration.md` describes the new read order, pending behavior and failure announcements. `tests/fm-pr-health.test.sh` adds coverage for these paths. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The round-2 fix keeps the 'announced' flag apart from demotion, which closes the silent stuck-PR path (A and B are read together, A settles, and B then prints when it fails alone); the updated docs and the new regression test match the code. ## Testing I ran the whole fm-pr-health test file twice. It drives the real bin/fm-pr-health.sh against a stubbed `gh` and a disposable home. Every case passed. That includes the wave, slow-forge, cannot-settle, stuck-PR and ordering cases. The docs match the new behavior. I did not run a real Herdr or Claude primary, because the monitor only talks to `gh`. - Live validation: ✅ go - 5 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Four-PR waves in listed order all settle (local script, stubbed gh) | ✅ pass | live | tests/fm-pr-health.test.sh: 'owned PR reads start together in waves of four and all settle' | | Slow forge settles within the bounded wave (local script, stubbed gh) | ✅ pass | live | 'a load-sensitive forge settles within the bounded wave' | | A pass where no read settles prints one cannot-settle line (local script, stubbed gh) | ✅ pass | live | 'a sweep that cannot settle any read says so once' | | A stuck PR is listed after untried PRs so later PRs are read | ✅ pass | live | 'a PR that cannot finish is listed after the PRs not tried, so later PRs are read' | | A stuck PR prints once, and one that first fails beside a settled PR is still announced | ✅ pass | live | 'a PR stuck on its answer prints once...' and 'a stuck PR first failing beside a settled PR is reported when it fails alone' | ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-health.sh:584` - A slow PR in the first wave can block every later PR on every pass, and the monitor says nothing. Each read now gets the whole remaining deadline (READ_CAP=0, line 574). Each wave waits for all of its PRs (lines 584-587). Example: 8 owned PRs, and PR #2 has a paginated GraphQL or suite read that takes longer than ~20 s. Wave 1 uses up the deadline, the loop breaks at line 576, and PRs 5-8 stay pending. The next pass selects them in the same listed order, with PR #2 still pending ahead of them, so PRs 5-8 are never read. PRs 1, 3 and 4 settle, so settled>0 and the cannot-settle line never prints. Before this change, the 5 s cap let all 8 reads complete. The intent says an unreached PR 'stays pending for the next pass', but without rotation it never makes progress. Possible remedies: put unsettled or pending PRs after fresh ones, rotate the start offset, or keep a per-read cap below the full deadline. Each one changes the accepted ordering design, so the author must choose. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-pr-health.sh:614` - The cannot-settle line repeats, with a wrong cause, when one PR can never settle but the forge is healthy. Examples: the suite list goes past the page bound (the changed test at tests/fm-pr-health.test.sh:820 now expects this line), or the repo returns 404/403 after access is lost. Sequence: pass 1 selects only stuck PR B and prints the line. Pass 2 gets a notification for PR A, A settles, and cannot_settle resets to false. Pass 3 selects only B (it is pending) and prints again. So the line prints again after every pass in which some other PR gets activity. Each time it says 'forge reads are slow or failing', but the reads were fast. That goes against the 'one line per new actionable condition' contract and the 'honest' wording in the intent. Possible remedies: track the stuck state per URL, or use a message that does not name forge slowness for a read that failed on content. Each time it says 'forge reads are slow or failing', but the reads were fast. That goes against the 'one line per new actionable condition' contract and the 'honest' wording in the intent. Possible remedies: track the stuck state per URL, or use a message that does not name forge slowness for a read that failed on content. The author must choose which behavior is correct. - 🚨 `bin/fm-pr-health.sh:634` - The fix round made this regression. A stuck PR whose first failure falls in a pass where another PR settles is never reported. The final jq (lines 643-649) adds every failed URL to `.read_failed`, including in passes where `settled > 0`, and no line prints in those passes. Later, `newly` (lines 635-637) leaves out any URL that is already in `.read_failed`. Sequence: pass 1 is the first or a full sweep and selects A and B. A settles. B fails on the suite page bound, a 403/404, or a timeout. Nothing prints, and `read_failed[B]` is set. Pass 2 selects only B (it is pending). B fails and `settled == 0`, but B is not counted as new, so nothing prints. Every later pass is silent too. The intent requires one honest cannot-settle line when a pass's selected reads all fail, and before the fix round the line printed in pass 2. The same failure happens on a slow forge if one PR in a wave happens to settle. The new test `test_one_stuck_pr_prints_once_across_other_activity` misses this because B fails alone first. Fix: record that the line was printed for a URL separately from the demotion marker. One way is to store `announced: true` in `read_failed[url]` only when a line prints for that URL, and compute `newly` against that field. Demotion can still use `read_failed` as it does now. Add a test where A and B are first read together, A settles and B is stuck, and the next pass then prints for B. - ⚠️ `docs/configuration.md:860` - The user docs still describe the behavior from before the fix round. They say the line 'prints it again only after a pass in which a read completed', and they do not mention demotion. The code now prints one line per cause (timeout, or no usable answer) for each PR that newly fails. A PR prints again only after one of its own reads settles. A PR whose read failed is listed after the PRs that were not tried. The script header comment (bin/fm-pr-health.sh:98-102) was updated, but this doc was not. title: fix(stow-guard): count a /stow command as a stow
body:
## Summary `bin/fm-stow-guard.sh` only recognised a `/stow` that the model started through the Skill tool. A `/stow` run as a slash command (typed, or submitted by a plugin before it compacts) leaves no Skill call in the transcript, so the guard kept an old `last_stow` and its age ask requested another full pass shortly after one had finished. ```diff newest /stow in the transcript tail = an entry with a Skill tool call whose skill is stow + or a /stow command entry: + type == "user" + and not a compaction summary (isCompactSummary) + and message.content is text that starts with a command tag + and carries /stow ``` Both forms feed the same newest-stow timestamp and the same `state/.stow-guard.json`. Text that only quotes the command (a compaction summary, a tool result, a typed prompt, a reply) does not move the clock. The token-line ask is unchanged: it never depended on the last stow. `docs/configuration.md` "Stow guard" does not say what counts, so only the script header changed. Entry shape: read from 37 real `/stow` command entries written by Claude Code 2.1.332 (keys and shape only), 36 submitted by a plugin and 1 typed. All 37 are `type: "user"` with string content made of command tags only. ## Evidence - **Before:** the new test fails on main: a transcript whose newest stow is a `/stow` command, with a stale `last_stow`, gets `{"decision":"block","reason":"fm-stow-guard: the last /stow is older than 24h. ..."}`. **After:** `bash tests/fm-stow-guard.test.sh` 12 of 12 ok; `bin/fm-lint.sh bin/fm-stow-guard.sh tests/fm-stow-guard.test.sh` clean (ShellCheck 0.11.0); `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` ok. New test: - `test_stow_command_sets_the_age_clock` - guards that a `/stow` command is counted as the newest stow, and that four later entries quoting the command (compaction summary, tool result, typed prompt, assistant reply) do not count. Also fixed in the same file: `test_bad_payloads_and_missing_jq_are_silent` failed on a stock macOS bash 3.2, because that shell answers `command -v jq` from its hash table once the test shell has run `jq`. The fixture check now runs after `hash -r` in a subshell. Not included: a live guard for the vendor-written entry shape (the coding guidelines' harness-dependent check rule). The portable test pins the logic; the shape itself was observed on one Claude Code version. If the shape changes, the guard falls back to today's behaviour (an extra age ask), never to a missed one. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way Opt-in hook (`config/stow-guard`), Claude primaries only; reverting restores the previous matching. **Blast Radius:** narrow A home with the guard on sees fewer age asks. No state format change. ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

title: fix(bin): refuse machine-wide pattern kills and slots another task record still names
body:
## Intent

Yes (to: have a worker make the three firstmate fixes).

The fixes, from an investigation of a 2026-11-16 incident (section 2 "Fixes worth shipping"):
1. Take the launch brief out of argv: bin/fm-spawn.sh passes each worker's whole brief as claude's first argument via "$(... encode launch-brief < brief)", so a delegated agent's `pkill -f chrome-devtools-axi` on 2026-11-16 11:57:32 CST SIGTERMed every firstmate-launched worker (only resumed sessions survived).
2. Block machine-wide pattern kills in delegated agents: extend bin/fm-arm-command-policy.mjs (it already refuses pkill aimed at fm-watch) to refuse any `pkill -f` / `killall` style pattern kill by crewmates, and document the matching guard for no-mistakes agents (they run with their own settings).
3. Spawn-side slot exclusivity: fm-spawn hands out a treehouse pool slot that other task records still name (seen live: cim-purchase-flag-review-f2 got cim-bf68b7/6 at 12:17:39 while 5 idle records still named it); refuse or skip a slot any record in any local home still names.

Open the PR. Rebase fixes 2 and 3 onto current upstream main first (drop anything #5664 already covers), rerun tests, then ship to a PR. Do not merge.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-arm-command-policy.mjs` now refuses pattern kills (`killall`, and any `pkill` that selects by pattern or `-f`) with a new `pattern-kill` reason. It still allows a `pkill` aimed at an exact target: only signal options plus `-P`/`-F`/`-g`/`-s`. `bin/fm-arm-pretool-check.sh` now lets `pkill`/`killall` through its prefilter, and `bin/fm-spawn.sh` adds this check as a `PreToolUse` Bash hook for Claude crewmates. `docs/arm-pretool-check.md` covers the guard and how no-mistakes agents can add it.
- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now refuses to hand out a Treehouse pool slot that another task record in any local Firstmate home still names as its `worktree=` or `home=`. If a local home can't be read, spawn warns and scans the homes it can read instead of failing.
- Teardown's record-exclusivity scan moved into a shared `fm_slot_other_record_namer` in `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh`, so spawn and teardown run the same check. `fm_local_firstmate_state_dirs` gained a `best-effort` mode that skips unreadable registries or homes and lists them in the error. Teardown still refuses when a home is unreadable.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The changes are bounded and well tested and they follow the user's earlier decisions, but they add a PreToolUse hook to every Claude crewmate in every project and a new way for spawn to refuse a slot, so it is worth watching after merge.

title: A wake drain piped into a filter can hide the acknowledgement line and wake rows
body:
## Observed

At upstream main `a5225cfa25ab99bac84c1d8fb3794037e99f53c8`, `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh` prints wake rows and UNREAD STATUS (line 450) to stdout, and the `WAKE_ACK_REQUIRED` command (lines 1018 and 1097) to stderr.
`bin/fm-afk-return.sh:771-774` relays the same acknowledgement line.
A call such as `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh | head` or `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh 2>&1 | grep -v ...` can drop rows or the acknowledgement line.
The drain still commits its presentation receipt, so UNREAD STATUS lines dropped by the filter are not printed again.

No pre-tool check stops such a call today.
Both command policies allow it:

```text
$ node bin/fm-cd-command-policy.mjs --home <home> --command 'bin/fm-wake-drain.sh | head -40'  ->  allow
$ node bin/fm-arm-command-policy.mjs --root <home> --home <home> --command 'bin/fm-wake-drain.sh | head -40'  ->  allow
$ node bin/fm-cd-command-policy.mjs --home <home> --command 'bin/fm-afk-return.sh check | grep -v foo'  ->  allow
$ node bin/fm-arm-command-policy.mjs --root <home> --home <home> --command 'bin/fm-afk-return.sh check | grep -v foo'  ->  allow
```

The transport `bin/fm-cd-pretool-check.sh` also allows both before the policy runs, because its prefilter only sends commands that contain `cd`, `pushd` or `popd` to the policy.

## Expected

A shell command that pipes `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh` or `bin/fm-afk-return.sh` into another command is refused before it runs, with a message that names the unfiltered form.
Running either command alone, redirecting it to a file that is then read in full, or feeding it input stays allowed.
The check uses the same PreToolUse transport as the existing cd and arm checks.

## Consequence

A filtered drain consumes status lines that the reader never sees.
The acknowledgement then retires the wake rows, so those results are neither shown nor queued again.
https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8549 shows the same loss with `>/dev/null`.

## How to verify

1. Queue a wake row and a `done:` status line.
2. Submit `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh | head -1` through the PreToolUse check and confirm it is refused with the unfiltered command named.
3. Repeat with `bin/fm-afk-return.sh check | tail` and with `2>&1 |`.
4. Confirm that plain `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh`, its `--ack-through` form, and a redirect to a file are allowed.
5. Confirm that the refused call left the queue and the presentation receipt unchanged.

Related: https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8747 makes the loss visible on the acknowledgement line after it happens.
This check prevents it.

title: UNREAD STATUS lines present pull-request claims without current forge state
body:
## Observed

At upstream main `a5225cfa25ab99bac84c1d8fb3794037e99f53c8`, `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh` prints new worker status lines under UNREAD STATUS (line 450) exactly as written.
A line such as `done: merged https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>` or `working: CI green on <url>` reaches the reader as the worker's claim.
The drain makes no forge read, so nothing beside the line shows whether the PR is still open, merged or failing.

## Expected

For each PR URL in an UNREAD STATUS line, the drain prints the current state (open, closed or merged), the check result summary, and the merge time when merged, beside the original line.
The original line stays unchanged, and the current reading is marked as such.
The read is bounded by a timeout and a per-drain URL cap.
A failed read prints `current state: unknown` and never blocks the drain or its acknowledgement.
Forge text is printed as quoted data, and the reading authorizes no merge or close.

## Consequence

Status lines are written minutes or hours before they are read.
A claim that was true when written can be false when read, and the reader has no current fact to compare it with.

## How to verify

1. Write a status line naming an open PR, then merge or close that PR before the drain.
2. Drain and confirm that the line appears with the current merged or closed state.
3. Put two PR URLs on one line and confirm each gets its own reading.
4. Make the forge unreachable and confirm the line still appears with `current state: unknown`.
5. Confirm that the acknowledgement is unaffected in every case.

Related: https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8748 asks for the same reading for BRANCH OUTCOMES rows.
`bin/fm-pr-poll.sh`, added by https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8598, already reads PR state through the forge CLI and could be reused.

title: `fm-captain-hold.sh hold` accepts a second open hold for the same origin
body:
## Observed

At upstream main `a5225cfa25ab99bac84c1d8fb3794037e99f53c8`, `command_hold` (`bin/fm-captain-hold.sh:1169-1260`) checks only that the task id is not closed and that `--title` matches an existing task.
Running `hold` twice with different task ids and the same `--origin` creates two open holds.
`.agents/skills/captain-hold-lifecycle/SKILL.md:22,28` asks for one held task per genuine gate, but no code enforces it.

## Expected

`hold --origin <origin>` refuses when that origin already has an open captain hold under another task id.
The refusal names the existing task id.
A caller with a real second gate passes an explicit flag that names it as a separate gate, and the hold records that flag.
Re-holding the same task id keeps working as today.

## Consequence

One review can produce two open holds for the same question.
The operator then sees the question twice and has to answer it twice.

## How to verify

1. Hold task `a` with `--origin review-x`.
2. Hold task `b` with `--origin review-x` and confirm it is refused with `a` named.
3. Hold `b` again with the separate-gate flag and confirm both holds are open.
4. Re-hold `a` and confirm it succeeds.
5. Answer `a`, then hold `c` with `--origin review-x`, and confirm it succeeds.

Related: https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/2790 reports the same duplicate and proposes text matching.
https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/7367 covers the opposite case, one hold shared by several origins, and this rule must not block it.
https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/8147 collapses duplicates that share a `--key`.

title: A needs-decision wake can be acknowledged before its decision is held, relayed or resolved
body:
## Observed

At upstream main `a5225cfa25ab99bac84c1d8fb3794037e99f53c8`, `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh --ack-through <n>` consumes every presented wake row up to `n`.
It does not check whether a `needs-decision` row's key has a captain hold, an answer relayed with `--resolve-key`, or a `resolved` status line.
`print_open_decisions_section` (lines 462-523) lists open decisions again on later drains.
The acknowledgement itself records nothing about how the decision was handled.

Reproduction: `state/task1.status` holds `needs-decision [key=api-shape]: pick REST or RPC` and one signal wake row for it.
Nothing resolves or holds the key.

```text
$ bin/fm-wake-drain.sh --ack-through 1 --recovery-generation <generation>
wake drain: acknowledged wakes through 1 (1 row(s) consumed)
```

The command exits 0, and no signal row stays queued.

## Expected

The acknowledgement refuses while a presented `needs-decision` key is neither held through `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh hold`, relayed with `bin/fm-send.sh --resolve-key`, nor closed by a `resolved` line.
The refusal names each unhandled key and the three commands that handle it.
The queue stays unchanged after a refusal.
Other rows in the same drain do not need a new drain to be acknowledged after the keys are handled.

## Consequence

In the reproduction above, the wake for an unanswered decision is consumed with exit 0.
After that, the decision is shown only in chat and in the OPEN DECISIONS list.
It has no `--until`, does not appear on Bearings, and does not reach the completion gate.

## How to verify

1. Queue a `needs-decision [key=k]` status line and drain.
2. Run the printed acknowledgement and confirm it is refused with `k` named.
3. Hold a task for `k` and confirm the same acknowledgement succeeds.
4. Repeat with a `--resolve-key k` relay, and with a `resolved [key=k]` line.
5. Confirm that a drain with no decision rows acknowledges exactly as before.

Related: https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8699 (away-time decisions never held), https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8749 (relay without a declared key), https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8495 (inbox notes lost on acknowledgement).

title: Opt-in: refuse a reply that says it answers from memory without a current read
body:
## Observed

At upstream main `a5225cfa25ab99bac84c1d8fb3794037e99f53c8`, the Claude Stop hooks in `.claude/settings.json` are `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh`, `bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh`, `bin/fm-host-mirror.sh` and `bin/fm-stow-guard.sh`.
Only `bin/fm-host-mirror.sh` reads `last_assistant_message`, and it reads it only to mirror it.
None of them blocks on the reply text.
`VISION.md:45` ("closed by records, not by recollection") and `AGENTS.md:364` (PR URLs "never assembled from memory") are written rules only.

Reproduction: a primary-shaped checkout (`AGENTS.md`, `bin/`, `state/`) gets this Stop payload:

```json
{"session_id":"s1","hook_event_name":"Stop","stop_hook_active":false,"last_assistant_message":"Captain, from memory the PR is already merged and its checks passed."}
```

`printf '%s' "$PAYLOAD" | bin/fm-stow-guard.sh` exits 0 with no block, and no other Stop hook blocks it, so the reply ends the turn.

## Expected

With an opt-in setting, the Stop hook blocks a reply once when the reply says it relies on memory or on no current read for a state claim.
The block message asks for the current read or a plain statement that the read failed.
A second stop of the same turn (`stop_hook_active` true) passes, so the hook cannot loop.
With the setting off, nothing changes.

## Consequence

A reply that admits it answers from memory, as in the payload above, reaches the operator with no prompt to check the source.
The operator cannot tell from the turn end whether the claim was read or recalled.

## How to verify

1. Enable the setting.
2. End a turn whose reply says "from memory" about a PR state and confirm one block with the message.
3. End the same turn again with `stop_hook_active` true and confirm it passes.
4. End a turn with an ordinary reply and confirm no block.
5. Disable the setting and confirm the first reply passes.

Related: https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/6208 was closed partly because a wording filter is easy to evade and can block by mistake.
This proposal is opt-in and blocks only once per turn for that reason.

title: hc smoke test fails teardown whenever a real herdr-core session writes its state during the run
body:
## Observed

At upstream main `a5225cfa25ab99bac84c1d8fb3794037e99f53c8`, `tests/fm-backend-hc-smoke.test.sh` passes all six checks and then fails in teardown on a host that runs a live herdr-core session.
`fm_hclab_fleet_state` (`bin/fm-hc-lab.sh:163-174`) records path, inode, mtime and size for every file under the real herdr-core state roots.
`fm_hclab_check_tripwire` (`bin/fm-hc-lab.sh:183-205`) fails on any difference.
A live session rewrites its own `terminals.json` every few seconds, so the tripwire fires even though the lab did not touch it.

Three runs with herdr-core 0.1.20 all ended like this:

```text
ok - hc smoke: kill closes and removes the terminal
FM_TEST_COMPLETE
fm-hc-lab: FLEET-STATE TRIPWIRE FAILED: real herdr-core state changed during lab work
fm-hc-lab: before: 51 files; after: 51 files
< .../herdr-core/<live-session>/terminals.json 14715286 1795790071 54628
> .../herdr-core/<live-session>/terminals.json 14715286 1795790079 54628
```

In two of the three runs only the mtime changed.
In 20 sequential runs of another smoke test that uses the same lab, 2 failed teardown the same way.

## Expected

The tripwire still fails when the lab writes real herdr-core state.
It does not fail when another session on the host writes its own files during the run.

## Consequence

The test passes on a quiet host and fails on any host that runs herdr-core for real work, so it looks flaky.
Each failure also leaves the lab directory behind for inspection.

## How to verify

1. Start a real herdr-core session that keeps updating its state.
2. Run `bash tests/fm-backend-hc-smoke.test.sh` several times and confirm that it passes.
3. Make the lab write a file under a real state root and confirm the tripwire still fails.
4. Run on a host with no live session and confirm that it passes as before.

title: fix(watch): keep acknowledged recovery closed across planned watcher handoffs
body:
## Problem An acknowledged recovery can reopen when a watcher is restarted, hands off a delivered check, or leaves a stale lock during a verified takeover. If the operator acknowledges a generation between the replacement's startup check and its first poll, an empty recovery wake can take precedence over a new scout completion. A replacement can also signal status history that a previous drain already presented. ## Reproduction Acknowledge an episode, then restart its watcher or let a delivering watcher finish after the acknowledgement. For the takeover race, pause the replacement just before its first poll, append a scout completion, acknowledge the empty recovery, and resume the replacement. For status replay, drain and acknowledge old status signals, append a new decision, and re-arm the watcher. The regression fixtures drive the actual watcher, wake drain, and Stop hook through those sequences. ## Fix Use process identity and verified takeover evidence to keep planned closes from reopening acknowledged episodes, including when the replacement reclaims a retained lock. When recording a planned stop fails, the arm still stops the verified watcher and allows ordinary downtime recovery. Recheck the claimed generation against current queue and marker state before waking, and resume scanning when an empty claim has been acknowledged. Record the file identity and byte endpoint of completed status presentations so a replacement can skip those bytes and still surface later appends. A first re-arm after upgrading can replay history presented by an earlier version. Use a fixed two-second lock wait for park and successor hand-backs. ## Tests The regression cases cover planned restarts, actionable-check exits, verified takeovers with retained locks, genuine outages, and bounded park hand-backs. They also cover late acknowledgements with and without scout work, status replay with later appends and mixed informational lines, and a successor that has already queued its decision before exiting. The focused Stop-hook, park and decision cases passed on macOS and GNU/Linux. The complete watcher-arm and unread-status suites passed on GNU/Linux. The byte-identical re-append fixture also passed on stock macOS Bash after extracting its timestamp before generating the test shim. With the review changes applied, the failed stop-record case passed on macOS and GNU/Linux. The direct-receipt and fixed lock-limit cases also passed on GNU/Linux. Full CI includes the unchanged `tests/fm-daemon.test.sh`, where the same pinned ShellCheck reported `SC2329` and `SC2031` during local validation. ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **Intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ℹ️ `docs/watcher-continuity.md:723` - The doc says the supervision host stops the watcher with `--stop` before it signals any arm, both at the park boundary and when it retires a successor cycle. That is not true on the opt-in acknowledged hand-back path. `acknowledged_handback` (bin/fm-supervision-host.sh:757-764) calls `retire_arm "$ARM_PID"` first, so the arm is signalled before `retire_successor` runs its `--stop`. The arm's TERM handler then stops the watcher with no planned-stop record. There is no behavioral impact, because that path republishes downtime on purpose right afterwards (fm_recovery_marker_publish at line ~771). The doc sentence should be limited to the default boundary and successor paths so it does not mislead future maintainers.
⚠️ **Test** - 1 info - ℹ️ `tests/fm-supervision-host-hook.test.sh` - With four watcher suites running at the same time on this host, the new test_scout_after_late_ack_with_retained_lock failed a fixture setup check ('fixture: the interrupted watcher released its singleton') before it reached the behavior under test. Two older tests failed the same way (fm-watch-arm 'arm did not start a watcher', fm-supervision-host captain outcome). All three pass when run one at a time. This looks like timing sensitivity under heavy load, which the watch-arm suite header already warns about. CI runs suites under its own job layout, so this is only a note. - Live validation: ✅ go - 8 of 9 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A planned host restart (fm-watch-arm --restart) over an acknowledged episode leaves recovery closed | ✅ pass | live | targeted-watch-arm.log: 'a planned host restart leaves an acknowledged episode closed' | | A successful actionable-check handoff keeps the acknowledged episode closed | ✅ pass | live | targeted-watch-arm.log: 'an actionable-check hand-off leaves an acknowledged episode closed' | | A verified takeover with a lock the previous watcher left behind keeps the acknowledgement, while queued, corrupt, interrupted and different-owner evidence still recover | ✅ pass | live | targeted-watch-arm.log: 5 'confirmed takeover with a retained lock' variants ok | | Adversarial: real outages (kill without cleanup, HUP, status 143 with no planned-stop record, stall eviction) still trigger recovery | ✅ pass | live | targeted-watch-arm.log: killed, hangup, 143 and stall-eviction tests ok | | --stop still ends the watcher and publishes downtime when the planned-stop record cannot be written | ✅ pass | live | targeted-watch-arm.log: '--stop ends only this home's watcher and publishes downtime (record-failure)' | | Acknowledgement arriving after the replacement decided on recovery: an empty acknowledged recovery stays quiet and a new scout completion reaches the operator, including with a retained lock | ✅ pass | live | targeted-hook.log: three 'late acknowledgement' tests ok;
