title: fix(bin): handle slow spawns and repeated local-only approvals
body:
## Intent

Fix three firstmate papercuts a fleet hit in daily use, as one upstream PR from a fork, keeping each fix as its own commit.

1. fm-spawn.sh waited a hard-coded 60 seconds for an interactive `treehouse get`. On a loaded host at the pool cap, creating a slot takes minutes, and the pool-cap explanation appears only in the pane, which the refusal then closes. Make the wait configurable through FM_SPAWN_TREEHOUSE_TIMEOUT (default 60; zero or invalid falls back to 60), and include the pane's output after the typed `treehouse get` in the refusal. The pane output is included whether or not treehouse is still running, because no backend offers a common way to read a pane's foreground command.

2. A local-only task records its first accepted done head and refuses any other, so a second round of work could not land after round one merged. When the recorded head is already contained in the project's local default branch, the next done head replaces it. A recorded head that has not landed still refuses any other head, preserving #7782's guarantee that the approved commit is the one that lands.

3. The done head was recorded only when a reader such as fm-crew-state.sh happened to accept the done line, so approving straight from the done notification failed with "missing or malformed local done head". Deliberately not fixed by recording the branch tip at merge time, since that would reopen #7782. Instead the local-only brief's done line names the head (`ready in branch <branch> at <head>`), acceptance refuses a named head that is not the worker copy's HEAD, and fm-merge-local.sh records a head the current done line names when no reader did. A line naming no head refuses as before.

Deliberately out of scope: the teardown refusal after a rebuilt PR (upstream refuses that on purpose; test_squash_merged_same_file_different_content_refuses encodes it) and afk support on the hc backend (needs new daemon backend work). Commits carry no agent co-author trailer, per the repo's rules.

## What Changed

- Add `FM_SPAWN_TREEHOUSE_TIMEOUT` with a 60-second default and fallback for zero or invalid values. Preserve captured pane output in timeout refusals.
- Allow later local-only rounds to replace the recorded done head once the previous head lands on the local default branch. Keep unlanded heads fixed.
- Include full commit IDs in local-only readiness reports and reject mismatches with the worker's `HEAD`. Accept named reports during local merge so direct approval needs no prior reader.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The changes satisfy the stated intent and preserve the unlanded-head safeguard; no material defects or unnecessary components were found.

## Testing

Both targeted test scripts and all live CLI scenarios passed using real Git, Treehouse, and tmux with disposable inputs. Retained CLI transcripts, corrected one setup assertion, and cleaned up all labs and processes.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 8 of 8 scenarios driven live against the product

| An 80-second setting allows a real Treehouse allocation delayed for 65 seconds to succeed. | ✅ pass | live | Allocation beyond 60 seconds |
| Unset, invalid, 0, and 00 timeout values use the 60-second fallback. | ✅ pass | live | Timeout fallback refusals |
| A wrapped treehouse get command preserves the exited pool-cap explanation in the refusal. | ✅ pass | live | Wrapped, noisy, and running Treehouse diagnostics; Wrapped command captured from real tmux |
| A timeout includes pane output while Treehouse is still allocating. | ✅ pass | live | Wrapped, noisy, and running Treehouse diagnostics |
| Later terminal output cannot erase the original pool-cap explanation. | ✅ pass | live | Wrapped, noisy, and running Treehouse diagnostics; Late pane tail after diagnostic displacement |
| Generated instructions name the completed head, and direct approval lands it without a prior reader. | ✅ pass | live | Generated local-only completion instructions; Direct local approval and refusal transcript |
| After one round lands, a later named round replaces its recorded head through direct approval or the public reader. | ✅ pass | live | Direct local approval and refusal transcript; Public done-reader transcript |
| Stale unnamed reports, mismatched heads, and unlanded replacements refuse without changing the approved commit. | ✅ pass | live | Direct local approval and refusal transcript; Public done-reader transcript |

Related changed sites: bin/fm-spawn.sh:5560 discards everything except the last nonblank row; :6158 also produces longer `--root` commands; :6224 consumes the truncated result.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-spawn.sh:5552` - The required criterion is to "include the pane's output after the typed `treehouse get` in the refusal", but the added capture requests only 120 lines after polling finishes. On cmux, Paseo, and Zellij, each directory poll prints begin/path/end markers. When Treehouse immediately reports a full pool, 60 polls produce at least 180 subsequent rows, so the final capture loses both the command and its explanation. Round 1's wrapped-echo fix leaves this sibling failure unresolved. Preserve the diagnostic during waiting instead of relying on the final fixed tail. Related changed sites: bin/fm-spawn.sh:6206 runs the probes and :6226 captures only afterward.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:6202` - The intent requires "zero or invalid falls back to 60", but the new case arm `''|*[!0-9]*|0` only recognizes literal `0`. Setting FM_SPAWN_TREEHOUSE_TIMEOUT=00 passes validation; `seq 1 00` produces no iterations, so spawning immediately refuses without polling. Normalize zero-valued digit strings to the default before constructing the loop. Related sites: bin/fm-spawn.sh:6207 consumes the unchecked value; docs/configuration.md:3785 promises the zero fallback.

🔧 Fix applied.

title: feat(bin): add Droid harness support across Firstmate roles
body:
Speaking as Paul's firstmate:

This replaces #6968 by @delaanthonio, who did the original Droid harness work - their commits are preserved here with authorship intact, rebased onto current main. #6968 was closed as stale only for missing live evidence; see the takeover note (https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/6968#issuecomment-7202237550) and the review findings this PR addresses (https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/6968#issuecomment-7199260922). Thank you, @delaanthonio.

Scope notes and follow-ups:
- Live verification here covered the tmux backend only, against Droid 1.21.1 on macOS (evidence below).
- Herdr away-daemon delivery and SSH remote Droid secondmates are refused for Droid (remote refusal happens locally before any remote call) until authenticated live runs can verify them; they are follow-up work.
- Droid's `[⏱ ...]` composer status-row check is intentionally left ungated, as in #6968; gating it by harness identity across tmux, Herdr, and Zellij is a known follow-up.

## Intent

b take over the PR, comment on the issue for me.

Context: "the PR" is https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/6968 ("feat: add Droid harness support across Firstmate roles", author delaanthonio, fork branch fm/droid-crew-harness-v2 on delaanthonio/firstmate, last head d0386482, 81 files). The maintainer closed it as stale on 2026-11-26 because the author never supplied live evidence for three authenticated scenarios (Droid worker launch/relaunch, Herdr away delivery, remote secondmate recovery); code review, the no-mistakes attestation and Greptile (5/5) were otherwise clean. Option (b) was: take over the PR - bring it up to date with current Firstmate main and add our fixes (co-author line, Claude marker leak, allowlist), produce the worker launch/relaunch test evidence on this machine, trim or defer the two scenarios we cannot test, and contribute it back upstream. The takeover announcement is already posted at https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/6968#issuecomment-7202237550 and the findings at https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/6968#issuecomment-7199260922. An evaluation of the PR is at ~/firstmate/data/prf-3834-droid-adapter-plan/report.md (sections 1.4, 2.3, 4.1 list the gaps and exact live-test commands).

Substance of the referenced findings comment (reviewed d0386482 against droid 1.21.1 on macOS): (1) commit attribution - unless "includeCoAuthoredByDroid": false is set in the Droid settings Firstmate generates, Droid appends a "Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot]" trailer; it should be suppressed unless keep-ai-trailers is configured, and the AI-trailer stripper should also strip factory-droid[bot], matching claude, devin, commandcode and cortex. (2) allowlist - supervision_primary_pin() in bin/fm-harness.sh omits droid, so a Droid primary harness pin fails as an unknown harness. (3) Claude marker leak - Firstmate's Droid worker launch does not unset CLAUDECODE, leaking a parent Claude marker to the Droid worker and its hooks. (4) mid-turn message delivery to a Droid tmux pane cannot observe Droid's busy state (it reads idle mid-turn); wiring Droid's UserPromptSubmit/Stop/SessionEnd hooks into the busy-event path, or otherwise detecting Droid busy, closes it. (5) minor hardening: fm-droid-model.sh gives up immediately on lock contention, which can leave the effective model unknown; the interrupt path has no guard for Droid's Rewind-to-previous-message picker already being open. The evaluation's gaps are the same: missing live evidence for Droid worker launch/relaunch (to be produced here), and Herdr away-delivery and remote-secondmate Droid recovery, which cannot be run authenticated on this machine and so are to be trimmed or deferred rather than claimed.

## What Changed
- Adds Factory Droid as a supported harness for crewmates/scouts, the primary (via `.factory/settings.json` SessionStart, PreToolUse `Execute`/`AskUser`, and Stop hooks) and secondmates. This includes new `bin/fm-droid-trust.sh` (folder trust grant/retire), `bin/fm-droid-model.sh` (exact model resolution and effective-model reconciliation), `bin/fm-droid-afk-askuser-check.sh` and `bin/fm-watch-droid-background.sh`. Droid is also wired into spawn, control/relaunch, teardown, watch-checkpoint, harness detection and dispatch, and the `supervision_primary_pin` allowlist.
- Fixes the issues found in review of #6968:
  - Droid launches unset `CLAUDECODE` and other foreign harness markers.
  - Generated Droid settings set `includeCoAuthoredByDroid: false` unless keep-ai-trailers is configured, and `fm-git-strip-ai-trailers.sh` now strips `factory-droid[bot]`/Factory trailers.
  - Busy detection uses a `droid-hook` adapter (UserPromptSubmit/Stop/SessionEnd) with a rendered-tail regex fallback.
  - The interrupt path recognizes Droid's Rewind picker.
- Herdr away-daemon launch (`fm-afk-launch.sh`) and SSH remote secondmate launch/relaunch (`fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh`) are refused for Droid until authenticated live runs verify them. `docs/verification/droid-primary.md` and `runtime-backends.md` separate older imported evidence from what was verified for this integration. The branch also adds Droid harness docs/skill references and portable plus live-e2e Droid tests.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The fix round correctly applied both user-chosen fixes: the transport table now changes only by adding droid relative to base, and the --primary-only scope check now runs after the fm-watch prefilter fast-allow with an identical decision. The overall branch remains a broad 82-file Droid harness addition across control-plane, hook and supervision paths.

## Testing

This round re-drove both live Droid guards against the real authenticated Droid 1.21.1 CLI in a lab HOME on a private tmux socket, and both passed. The exact native pin now holds at runtime (claude-opus-5-5-fast) despite a conflicting project default. Relaunch, hooks, composer, long-running-tool, busy-signal delivery, interrupt, /quit, trust retirement and Fish-shell ship exit all passed live. The targeted tests for the review fixes all passed (fm-control, fm-arm-pretool-check, fm-droid-harness, fm-droid-primary). The allowlist, trailer stripping, CLAUDECODE scrubbing and the deferred-scenario refusal guards rest on round-1 live transcripts from this unchanged product code. These are CLI/tmux flows with no rendered UI, so the evidence is CLI transcripts rather than screenshots.

title: Reconcile reviewed idle scouts before repeat wedge escalation
body:
## Summary

An idle scout can have a complete report and no remaining captain decision while its old `working:` event remains the last status evidence.
The watcher then repeats wedge escalation even after the report has been reviewed.

The safe reconciliation boundary is narrow.
It must prove the report belongs to the current scout incarnation, has been reviewed with a complete decision inventory, and is strictly newer than both the current work log and the busy generation.

## Expected behavior

Before repeating a wedge escalation, `fm-crew-state.sh` should reconcile an idle scout as done only when all of these conditions hold:

- the task is a scout and the current status event is `working`;
- the report is readable, regular, non-empty, and not a symlink;
- the report's decision inventory has been reviewed;
- the report is strictly newer than both the status log and the current busy generation.

A same-second timestamp tie is not fresh on stock macOS Bash, so it must remain working.
A newer status event, unread instruction, open decision, positive busy event, endpoint loss, or replacement generation must remain visible and must not be suppressed by an older report.

When the authoritative state reader returns the reviewed scout-report completion, the watcher should absorb that repeated wedge episode without changing the existing paths for unfinished, active, unread, unresolved, missing, or replaced work.

## Related work

- #4411 covers the broader durable cleanup obligation for completed scouts and remains wider than this state-reader and watcher boundary.
- #8722 covers a separate launch seed that never starts its brief.
- https://github.com/mehulbhagwani/firstmate/pull/38 contains the fork-only implementation that motivated this focused upstream extraction.

## Done when

The crew-state and watcher behavior is implemented on current upstream `main` with executable regression tests for reviewed idle scouts and negative controls for active work, unread instructions, open decisions, endpoint loss, replacement generations, and exact timestamp ties.

## VISION.md alignment

- **One captain, one interface:** repeated wedge noise must stop only after deterministic state reconciliation proves the report was reviewed.
- **Authority is explicit and never inferred:** a report alone is not completion; the decision inventory and freshness proof are required.
- **Scripts own the mechanics, agents own the judgment:** Bash and the existing captain-hold verifier enforce exact evidence while review remains an explicit attestation.
- **A restart is a non-event:** generation freshness prevents an old scout report from closing a replacement worker.
- **Delegation with a spine:** the watcher reuses the authoritative crew-state result and preserves escalation for evidence it cannot prove.
- **Scope:** this stays a focused scout state and watcher change, without changing ship completion or cleanup ownership.

title: Pi workers remain working after a credential-less initial prompt rejection
body:
## Intent

A Pi or pi-signed worker that rejects its very first prompt because no provider credential is available must not remain classified as an active turn.
The launch should become an unknown, actionable state without reading operator credential files or changing how later turns are classified.

## Behavior

When the untouched `fm-spawn` launch seed is paired with Pi's credential-less initial-prompt diagnostic and its `/login` guidance, `fm-crew-state.sh` should report `unknown` with the reason `launch-auth`.

A trust dialog remains `unknown launch-prompt`.
A real Pi or pi-signed turn that has posted an adapter lifecycle event remains `busy` or `idle` according to that event, even if its rendered tail contains an error-like message.

The focused regression must exercise the public busy-state classifier and the live Pi and pi-signed launch path in a credential-less isolated environment.
It must not read or write operator credential stores, submit a provider request, or answer a trust dialog.

## Evidence

Fork PR https://github.com/mehulbhagwani/firstmate/pull/38 contains an authored preflight implementation and live evidence for this narrow boundary.
The current upstream behavior still reports the untouched Pi launch seed as `working` after the initial credential rejection.
The existing upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/8722 covers aged unconfirmed launches generally, but does not own this immediate Pi credential diagnostic.

## VISION alignment

- **Authority is explicit and never inferred:** a credential rejection is classified from the launch state and Pi's own rendered diagnostic, not treated as proof that a turn started or as permission to inspect credentials.
- **Scripts own the mechanics, agents own the judgment:** the deterministic busy classifier owns the exact predicate; no model or operator decision is introduced.
- **A restart is a non-event:** the classification is bound to the existing generation and untouched launch seed, so stale or replaced turns cannot inherit it.
- **The fleet outlives any vendor:** the predicate is scoped to Pi and pi-signed and preserves the existing trust-dialog and lifecycle contracts for other harnesses and active turns.
- **Scope:** this is a narrow state-classification fix, not account management, credential selection, or a general launch redesign.

title: fix(watch): keep handling-successor recovery and treat superseded omp confirms as delivered
body:
## What Changed - `bin/fm-watch.sh`: `watcher_cleanup` now uses the `release-lock-existing` transition for a `check: rearm-resurface` delivery when the watcher is a handling successor (`FM_WATCH_HANDLING_SUCCESSOR=1`), as well as when recovery is pending. This keeps the recovery episode intact instead of dropping it. - `.omp/extensions/fm-primary-omp-watch.ts`: the omp handoff confirmation now checks against the restoration's own recovery token, not the current arm snapshot, and retries once against that same token. When confirmation exits with status 3, the extension treats it as superseded, so it doesn't retry, report a restoration failure, or retire the successor. - `docs/watcher-continuity.md` now says omp confirms against the restoration token and handles a superseded generation mismatch the same way Pi does. New cases in `tests/fm-omp-harness.test.sh` and `tests/fm-watch-triage-busy.test.sh` cover this behavior. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: This is a small, well-bounded change to the recovery handshake. Exit 3 only means the marker generation moved, other rejections still report FAILED, and the cleanup change applies only to handling successors that delivered a rearm-resurface; both behaviours have new tests that run the real code. ## Testing I ran both changed paths against disposable fixtures. The real `bin/fm-watch.sh` ran as a handling successor on a temporary state directory. The real omp watch extension module ran under node with a stub `pi` API and a fake `fm-watch-arm.sh` that returns confirmation status 3 or 1. On the base commit both new scenarios fail: cleanup republishes the episode as pending downtime, and a superseded confirmation is reported as `watcher: FAILED`. On HEAD both pass, and the five existing omp watch-extension cases still pass. I did not drive a real omp primary in a lab tmux session, because the superseded-confirmation race cannot be triggered on demand there. Full runs of the two test files from a background job failed during setup because `TMP_ROOT` resolved to empty, so they were replaced with the cut-down runs above. None of these runs touched fleet state, and the temporary trees are deleted. - Live validation: ✅ go - 3 of 3 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A handling successor watcher (FM_WATCH_HANDLING_SUCCESSOR=1, temporary state dir with a seeded queued recovery row) resurfaces the row exactly once, its exit cleanup leaves `.watcher-down` as `announc… | ✅ pass | live | head-handling-successor-rearm.tap passes; base-handling-successor-rearm.tap fails with 'cleanup republished recovery episode as pending downtime' | | Adversarial: the omp watch extension gets `--handling-delivered` exit 3 (superseded, synthetic fake arm script).
